title: bug(codex): session stuck 'working' for days — final turn's stop hook never fired, no idle fallback demotes stale active
body:
## Bug
A codex worker session has shown **working / `activity_state=active`** continuously for 2+ days while the agent sat at a chat prompt doing nothing. The last activity transition ever recorded is an `active` at the start of its final turn; the `stop` hook that should have demoted it to `idle` at turn end never arrived, and nothing else in the system corrects a stale `active`.

**Source:** maintainer local report (desktop app, macOS) | **Date:** 2026-07-25 | **Analyzed against:** `dec77c61b` (local) / `12591e1c6` (origin/main) | **Daemon:** app-owned, :3001
**Confidence:** High on evidence and adapter mechanism; Medium on why this specific `stop` was lost
**Priority:** medium-high — "working" is a trust-critical signal; a permanently-working session masks a blocked fleet (and inverts [#2814](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2814)'s kimi idle-while-working)

## Evidence (session `agent-orchestrator-39`, codex)
`change_log` shows healthy hook-driven cycles, then a final transition that never closes:

```
10:19:40 active   10:19:53 idle
10:20:15 active   10:20:29 idle
10:21:15 active   10:21:23 idle
10:21:45 active   10:22:05 idle
10:23:28 active   ← LAST EVENT EVER (2026-07-23); still active on 2026-07-25
```

The agent's final turn ended normally from the user's perspective — it printed a clarifying question and returned to the composer prompt (visible in tmux scrollback). AO's own idle detection even fired worker-idle notifications for this session around the same window, yet the persisted activity state stayed `active`, and `ao session get` reports `status: working` two days later.

## Root Cause
`backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/activity.go` — codex activity is driven by exactly three hook events: `user-prompt-submit`→active, `permission-request`→waiting_input, `stop`→idle. The adapter's own doc comment notes codex has **no SessionEnd/Notification equivalent** and no pre/post-tool-use hooks; runtime exit falls back to the reaper. Consequences:

1. If a single `stop` hook is lost (hook process failed, PATH issue, codex skipped firing it on that turn shape), the session is `active` **forever** — there is no reconciliation that says "no hook events for N minutes + composer prompt visible → demote to idle".
2. The reaper only handles runtime *exit*, not stale *state*; the process is alive, so it never intervenes.
3. Downstream effects compound: `waiting_input`/idle-gated flows behave wrongly for a phantom-active session (e.g. nudge gating in `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go` skips on NeedsInput but not on stale-active; board/status pills show working).

## Fix
Suggested directions:
1. **Staleness reconciliation:** if `activity_state=active` but no hook event has arrived for N minutes, cross-check a cheap liveness/inbox signal (terminal output delta, composer-prompt detection à la `activitystate`) and demote to idle — the generic safety net that would fix this class for every hook-based adapter, not just codex.
2. **Codex-specific:** investigate which turn shapes end without firing the `stop` managed hook (this repro: turn ended with a plain assistant question, no tool use) and harden the hook installation.
3. Emit a diagnostic when a session's last hook event is `active` and older than some threshold — this state is currently invisible until a human squints at the timestamps.

## Impact
- Board/sidebar/status pills show a permanently-working session; the human cannot tell blocked-waiting-on-me from working (this repro sat 2 days awaiting user input the UI never surfaced).
- Automated flows gated on activity state (nudges, idle notifications, completion checks) run against fiction.

## Related
- [#2814](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2814): kimi inverse (idle while working) — same "hook coverage gaps corrupt activity truth" family; fix PR [#2873](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2873) in flight
- [#2047](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2047): claude-code activity misreporting
- [#2802](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2802): IsAlive pane-exists ≠ agent-alive (liveness-vs-inbox split)
- [#2944](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2944) / [#2345](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2345): status presentation locked to PR state

title: Worker escalation/ask-policy is hardcoded in prompt.go — make it user-editable + add real escalation mechanics
body:
## Problem

The rules that govern when a worker **asks the user a question vs. resolves it itself** are **hardcoded strings in `internal/session_manager/prompt.go`** (worker standing instructions: "If you cannot proceed without a decision, ask for that decision instead of guessing"; orchestrator-coord: "Message it only for true blockers, cross-session coordination, or decisions you cannot resolve locally").

There is **no way to configure this policy itself**:
- `--agent-rules` / `--orchestrator-rules` (the `customInstructions` from #1382) can *append* text, but **can't replace or tune the hardcoded baseline** — the escalation policy stays fixed for everyone.
- No `ao user-config` / `ao project set-config` knob for the policy, no UI.
- The policy is not visible to the user at all — it lives in Go source.

This is a real, daily pain point:

1. **Not discoverable for a first-time user.** AO's behavior on "when does my worker ask me vs. decide alone" is invisible — a new user has no idea this policy exists, let alone how to change it.
2. **Rules should be editable through the UI and visible, not buried in source.** A user tuning their agent should see and edit "when to escalate" in the same place they set model/permissions.
3. **Every project is different.** A throwaway prototype tolerates a guess-heavy worker; a production repo needs a strict "ask before any destructive choice" worker. Today both get the same hardcoded policy.

On top of configurability, AO currently has **no real escalation mechanics** — the policy is a single prompt sentence, not a system.

## How this differs from #1382

#1382 (CLOSED, done) added `customInstructions` **appended on top** of the default prompts — that's today's `agent-rules`. This issue is the **next step**: make the escalation **baseline itself** user-editable (not just appendable), and add an actual escalation **mechanism** rather than relying on a single prompt sentence. Related: #2195 (per-role systemPrompt field) covers *what* prompt content to inject per role; this issue is about *the policy that decides ask-vs-decide*.

## Proposal

**A. Make the ask/escalation policy user-configurable** (the core ask):
- Per-project (and user-scope) config field for the worker's escalation policy, editable via `ao project set-config` + the desktop settings form, on equal footing with model/permissions.
- The hardcoded baseline becomes the default, overridable per project.

**B. Add real escalation mechanics** (builds on A, can be phased):

1. **Escalation levels in the prompt**: "try to resolve yourself → after N failed attempts, ask the orchestrator → if unanswered for M minutes, ask the human." Today there is no ladder — a worker flips straight to "ask the human."
2. **FAQ / pattern-book**: accumulate answers to repeated questions so workers (and orchestrator) reuse them instead of re-asking the same thing.
3. **Question filter at the orchestrator**: the orchestrator intercepts a worker's question and decides "trivial — I'll answer / serious — escalate to the human." Today the orchestrator receives the message but there's no explicit "answer on the human's behalf" path — it's emergent LLM behavior, not a wired mechanism.

## Why it matters

The single biggest day-to-day friction with workers is **repetitive low-value questions** that the worker could resolve itself (or the orchestrator could triage). Hardcoding the policy in source means every user is stuck with the same guess/ask tradeoff, with no visibility and no per-project tuning — and there's no mechanical escalation ladder to lean on.

## Out of scope (separate)

- Changing the *content* of the default policy (that's a tuning decision once configurability exists).
- Per-agent-adapter policies (claude-code vs codex may want different defaults) — follow-up.

Ref: `internal/session_manager/prompt.go` (worker standing instructions, orchestrator-coord block). Builds on #1382.

title: fix(codex): recover sessions stuck in active state
body:
Fixes #3115.

## What changed

Codex can occasionally miss its final `stop` hook, which leaves AO showing a session as working even after Codex has returned to the composer.

This adds a small activity observer that:

- checks only stale active sessions whose adapter supports terminal activity detection;
- recognizes Codex's idle composer and footer markers;
- keeps sessions active while the `esc to interrupt` working marker is visible;
- fences terminal observations with the runtime launch and session update timestamp so stale output cannot overwrite a newer prompt;
- uses the normal lifecycle transition, including the durable worker-idle event.

Other agent adapters are left unchanged.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./...`
- `cd backend && go vet ./...`
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- frontend typecheck and E2E typecheck
- 1,084 frontend Vitest tests
- 20 renderer-smoke Playwright tests
- real tmux + SQLite regression test covering both idle recovery and a genuine long-running Codex turn

title: Open session worktree in external IDE (`IDE ↗` + target menu)
body:
## Summary

We are **not** building in-pane file editing right now. Diff review + asking the orchestrator covers most edits. What we want is a quick handoff to open the current session worktree in a real editor (or Finder / Terminal).

## Motivation

- Spawning an agent is overkill for “inspect agent changes” or “change one line.”
- In-pane editing in AO is not a near-term goal (Core Contributor alignment).
- Two proven patterns exist elsewhere:
  - Simple `IDE` + external-link control → open in your preferred IDE
  - App icon + menu → VS Code / Cursor / Finder / Terminal (remembers last target)

## Proposed UX (hybrid)

Session topbar, near the branch chip:

1. **Primary:** `IDE` + external-link icon → one click opens the worktree in the **preferred IDE**
2. **Chevron:** menu to pick **VS Code · Cursor · Finder · Terminal**
3. Choosing VS Code/Cursor updates the preferred IDE; Finder/Terminal open without changing it
4. Preference persisted locally; default IDE = Cursor

### References / mocks

Attach screenshots when reviewing:
- Simple `IDE` + external-link primary control
- Icon + chevron + target list (VS Code, Cursor, Finder, Terminal)
- Menu placement next to the session branch chip

## Scope (v1)

- Open **session worktree root** only
- Desktop launches external apps; daemon only exposes absolute worktree path on a dedicated read endpoint (not on session list/get)
- Clear errors if app missing or workspace unavailable

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Session topbar shows `IDE ↗` (+ optional chevron menu)
- [ ] Primary click opens worktree in preferred IDE
- [ ] Menu can open VS Code, Cursor, Finder/Explorer, Terminal
- [ ] Preferred IDE remembered across launches
- [ ] Session list/get still does not leak `workspacePath`
- [ ] Failures are visible (not silent); works when app launched from Dock

## Open question for reviewers

Prefer **hybrid** (`IDE ↗` + menu), **simple primary only** (no menu), or **menu only** (icon + chevron, no `IDE` label)?

## Follow-up

Open the currently viewed file from Files / diffs with the same control.

title: ci: skip canonical-only workflows on forks
body:
## Problem

Several workflows only make sense on `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` but still run on forks, where they fail red:

1. **Deploy landing to GitHub Pages** — forks copy the workflow, but `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create/enable GitHub Pages (`Resource not accessible by integration`).
2. **Release latest guard** — hourly cron checks `github.repository` for a stable desktop `/releases/latest`; forks have none (`release not found`), so the job fails every hour.

Upstream behavior is fine; the failures are expected off the canonical repo but still noise fork Actions.

## Expected

Deploy/publish/release-state jobs that only make sense on the canonical repo should no-op on forks (skipped). Test CI (Go, Frontend, etc.) should keep running.

## Proposed fix

Gate the jobs with:

```yaml
if: github.repository == 'AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator'
```

in:

- `.github/workflows/deploy-landing.yml` (`build` + `deploy`)
- `.github/workflows/release-latest-guard.yml` (`latest-release`)

## Notes

- Does not change upstream/prod deploy or release-guard behavior.
- Intentional fork desktop test releases (`frontend-release.yml`) stay ungated.

title: ci: skip canonical-only workflows on forks
body:
## Summary
- Gate `Deploy landing to GitHub Pages` build/deploy jobs to `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` so forks skip instead of failing on Pages enablement.
- Gate `Release latest guard` the same way so the hourly schedule does not fail on forks that have no stable desktop release.
- Fixes [#3119](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/3119).

## Test plan
- [ ] On a fork, confirm landing deploy jobs are skipped (not failed) when the workflow runs.
- [ ] On a fork, confirm the next scheduled `Release latest guard` run skips (not `release not found`).
- [ ] On `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`, confirm landing deploy still runs when landing paths change (or via `workflow_dispatch`).
- [ ] On `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`, confirm release-latest guard still runs on schedule/release events.

title: feat(board): revamp task cards with agent logos and cleaner layout
body: ## What Revamps the board / kanban session cards to lead with each agent's real brand logo and a cleaner content hierarchy. ## Changes - **`AgentAvatar`** (new) — renders each harness's real brand logo. 20 agents have assets (codex, claude-code, opencode, aider, grok, droid, amp, crush, cursor, qwen, copilot, goose, continue, devin, cline, kimi, kiro, kilocode, vibe, pi); the few without one (agy, auggie, autohand, fake) fall back to a clean lettered tile. Logos are vendored from the same lobehub set the landing site already uses. - **Card layout** — the title is now the hero; dropped the redundant agent-name text (the logo conveys it). - **Status repositioned** — Working / CI failed / Changes requested etc. moved into the footer at a smaller size, next to a relative timestamp. - **Branch row** gets a git-branch icon; **copy buttons removed** from the card (branch + PR URL). - Only show a PR line when a PR actually exists (removed the "no PR yet" noise). - **Preview data** — varied the mock sessions across agents so the logos show on the `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` board. ## Notes - `agy` / `auggie` / `autohand` stay on the letter tile — no logo asset exists for them in the icon set (didn't want to fabricate a brand mark). - Verified via `tsc --noEmit` and the SessionsBoard unit suite (28 tests). title: fix(sidebar): Linux collapse to icon rail + align rail tiles
body:
## Problems

1. On Linux, collapsing the sidebar made it disappear entirely — including the expand button — with no way to bring it back.
2. In the collapsed icon rail, the tiles didn't line up (search and the new-project button were smaller than the rest).

## Causes

1. `SidebarRoot` used `collapsible="offcanvas"` on every platform, which slides the whole sidebar off-canvas (`w-0`) when collapsed. mac/Windows re-expand from a titlebar toggle (`TitlebarNav` / `WindowTitlebar`), but Linux has no custom titlebar — its only expand control lives inside the sidebar header, so offcanvas hid it.
2. Rail tiles had mismatched box sizes: brand / toggle / project / settings were `size-control-board` (36px), but search was `size-control-form` (32px) and the new-project button was `size-icon-xl` (18px), so their edges never aligned.

## Fixes

1. Linux now uses `collapsible="icon"`, collapsing to the 48px icon rail (the `--size-sidebar-icon` rail the existing `group-data-[collapsible=icon]` styling was already built for), keeping the expand trigger visible. mac/Windows unchanged.
2. Every interactive rail tile is now `size-control-board` (36px), so they share one centered box.

Verified: `tsc` clean, Sidebar suite (38 tests) passes.

title: bug(desktop): Spawn Orchestrator has no recovery when project has no agent configured
body:
## Summary

A valid project registered without an `orchestrator.agent` appears normally in the desktop app and shows an enabled **Spawn Orchestrator** button. Clicking it fails with the raw daemon error:

```text
spawn: session: agent harness required: configure project orchestrator.agent or pass --harness (AGENT_REQUIRED)
```

The desktop action has no harness input, agent picker, or link to project settings, so the user cannot recover from the surface where the error occurs.

Verified on current `main` at `5a587191e` using the Electron development app and its isolated `~/.ao/dev` state.

## Reproduction

1. Create a Git repository with an initial commit.
2. Register it through the supported CLI without agent flags:

   ```bash
   ao project add --path /path/to/repo --name "No Agent Test"
   ```

3. Open that project in the desktop app.
4. Click **Spawn Orchestrator**.

## Actual behavior

- The button is enabled and looks ready to use.
- The spawn request is sent without a harness.
- The board renders the technical `AGENT_REQUIRED` error below the button.
- Retrying produces the same result.
- The error tells the user to pass `--harness`, although the desktop button provides no way to do that.

## Expected behavior

When the project has no configured orchestrator agent, the desktop should provide a recovery path before sending the spawn request. For example:

- open an agent picker and spawn with the selected installed/authorized harness; or
- open Project Settings focused on the missing orchestrator-agent field; or
- disable the button with a clear action to configure an agent.

Configured projects should keep the current one-click spawn behavior.

## Why this state is valid/reachable

`ao project add` intentionally makes `--worker-agent` and `--orchestrator-agent` optional (`backend/internal/cli/project.go`). This can also affect older or externally registered projects whose config lacks role defaults.

The board path currently calls `spawnOrchestrator(projectId, "board")` without checking `workspace.orchestratorAgent` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx`). The failure is only rendered as text after the daemon rejects the request.

## Suggested scope

Frontend-only recovery should be enough; the daemon is correctly rejecting an underspecified spawn.

Add regression coverage for:

- missing `orchestratorAgent`: clicking **Spawn Orchestrator** does not POST an invalid request and opens/directs to an agent-configuration surface;
- configured `orchestratorAgent`: existing one-click spawn still works;
- the same missing-config behavior from every spawn affordance (board empty state, topbar, and sidebar shortcut).

title: Telemetry: validate command-shaped values at the PostHog sink (defense in depth)
body:
Follow-up carved out of #2816, which is being closed as superseded.

## Context

#2829 (merged as `a6d90dfe3`) fixed the reported leak in #2813 at the source: `usageErrorCommand` in `backend/internal/cli/root.go` now walks the live Cobra command tree and stops at the first token that is not a registered subcommand, so raw positional args (URLs, file paths, free text) can no longer reach `command` or `command_path`.

That is the client-side half. #2816 also proposed a **sink-side** defense in depth that is still not on main.

## The gap

The PostHog allowlist gates telemetry *keys*, not *values*. If any future code path writes a command-shaped property, nothing at the sink validates what is actually in it. #2829 fixed today's producer; it did not add a backstop against the next one.

## Proposed change

In the PostHog sink (`sanitizeRemoteValue`), for command-shaped keys (`command`, `command_path`):

- Validate the value against the expected command shape (registered subcommand names joined by spaces).
- If it does not match, replace it with a `sha256:<16 hex>` digest rather than dropping it, so volume and cardinality stay analysable without shipping the raw string.

## Notes

- #2816 has a working implementation of this half if it is useful as a starting point, though it will need rebasing onto post-#2829 main.
- The reviewer on #2816 flagged that there was no end-to-end route test for the sink defense. Worth adding one here.

title: fix(desktop): guard app.dock for Electron 39 types
body:
## Problem

Dependabot's electron 33 to 39 bump (#3123) fails its `test` job on a single typecheck error:

```
src/main.ts(238,3): error TS18048: 'app.dock' is possibly 'undefined'.
```

Electron 39 types `app.dock` as possibly `undefined` because the Dock API is macOS-only. `applyRuntimeAppIcon` already returns early on non-darwin platforms, so the value is always set at that call site, but TypeScript cannot narrow through a `process.platform` check.

## Change

Optional-call the setter, with a comment explaining that the guard is for the type rather than the runtime. No behavior change on any platform.

Landing this separately from #3123 keeps the dependency bump to lockfiles and manifests only, and lets that PR go green on a rebase.

## Verification

Controlled both directions, running the real `npm run typecheck` against each Electron version:

| Config | Result |
| --- | --- |
| This fix + electron 39.8.5 | clean |
| Without this fix + electron 39.8.5 | `TS18048` reproduces at the same line |
| This fix + electron 33.4.11 (current main) | clean, no regression |

Electron 39 was installed with `--no-save` for the check, so no manifest or lockfile is touched by this PR.

## Follow-up

#3123 still deserves a manual smoke test of the Electron surface before merging. Six majors is a wide jump and typecheck only proves compilation, not runtime behavior. This PR only clears the compile blocker.

Refs #3123

title: bug(daemon): failed scratch orchestrator launch leaves workspace state that blocks retries
body: ## Summary A failed initial orchestrator launch in a scratch project can leave AO-created agent hook files in the managed workspace. The spawn seed row is rolled back, so the next attempt reuses the same session ID and workspace path. Scratch workspace creation then refuses the non-empty directory, making the retry fail with an unrelated internal error. Reproduced through the Electron app. I also fetched current `upstream/main` at `4736485cf`; the relevant session-manager and scratch-workspace paths are unchanged there. ## Reproduction 1. Start with a scratch project whose configured orchestrator is unavailable locally (Claude Code in this reproduction). 2. Click **Spawn Orchestrator**. 3. The initial launch fails before a runtime is created because the agent binary cannot be resolved. 4. Click **Spawn Orchestrator** again. ## Actual behavior The retry returns `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`. The daemon reports: ```text spawn scratch-1: workspace: scratch workspace: path ".../worktrees/scratch/orchestrators/scratch-1" already contains files: workspace: uncommitted changes present ``` The preserved directory contains only the workspace-local Claude hook files created during the failed preparation: ```text scratch-1/.claude/settings.local.json scratch-1/.claude/.gitignore ``` The UI exposes only the generic internal error, and subsequent retries remain blocked. ## Why it happens The pre-launch path installs workspace-local agent hooks before validating the launch binary. On failure, `rollbackPreparedSpawnWorkspace` calls workspace destruction first and only calls agent cleanup if destruction succeeds. Scratch `Destroy` correctly preserves every non-empty directory as potential user work. Because the AO-created hook files make the directory non-empty, destruction fails and agent cleanup never runs. The seed session row is still deleted, allowing the next spawn to reuse `scratch-1` and collide with the preserved path. ## Expected behavior A failed pre-runtime launch should leave scratch spawn retryable without risking user files. Possible safe approaches include: - remove only agent-owned preparation artifacts before attempting the normal safe scratch destroy; or - preserve the failed workspace/session identity so the next spawn does not reuse its path. AO should not force-delete arbitrary non-empty scratch directories. ## Suggested tests - Use the real scratch workspace adapter with an agent that writes workspace-local hook files, then fail binary validation. - Verify a second spawn does not fail with `ErrWorkspaceDirty` from the first attempt. - Verify unrelated user-created files are never deleted during rollback. ## Related [#2551](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2551) fixed stale/non-git worktrees during replacement of an existing orchestrator. This reproduction is different: it occurs during rollback of the initial scratch spawn before a live session exists. I’m willing to work on this once the expected rollback approach is confirmed.

pauses on hover, stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`, edges fade via a CSS mask - **~10 visible at a time**: the viewport is capped at `max-w-2xl` and centered, so ~10 logos flow through the window rather than the whole set showing at once - **real logos for every agent (23/23)**: - 20 come from the app's `renderer/assets/agents` (copied into `public/app-icons/agents/`) - `agy` (Google Antigravity), `auggie` (Augment Code), `autohand` (Autohand) use their own brand favicons, whitened where the mark was dark - `goose` / `kilocode` shipped near-black PNGs that vanished on the dark bg — replaced with whitened lobehub marks - **no lazy-load**: marquee items move by `transform`, so their layout position stays off-screen and `loading="lazy"` never fires (logos would blank as they scroll in) — dropped it files: `TrustedBySection.tsx` + the logo assets. ## verification - ran the landing (`next dev`) and rendered the section: 46 track items = 23 agents × 2 copies, `broken: 0` (all load), ~10 visible per frame - confirmed each of the 5 fixed/added marks (goose, kilocode, agy, auggie, autohand) renders visibly on the black background note: the Antigravity mark came from a 16×16 favicon (only source found), so it's slightly softer than the vector logos. --- ### also in this branch: header scroll-to-black fix had *before* its `useState`/`useEffect` hooks — a Rules-of-Hooks violation that broke the client component's hydration, so the scroll listener never attached and the transparent-hero header (`/`, `/design-partners`) stayed transparent instead of turning solid black on scroll. moved the early return after the hooks. verified in a production build: transparent over the hero, `bg-background` once scrolled.

title: fix: preserve failed scratch workspaces for retries
body:
## What

Fixes #3135 by keeping a failed scratch session when its non-empty workspace can't be removed, so retries get a fresh session number instead of colliding with the old path.

## Why

Scratch workspaces intentionally refuse to delete non-empty directories. The old rollback still deleted the seed session row, which made the next spawn reuse `scratch-1` and fail with a dirty-workspace error.

## How

- record the preserved workspace path when rollback cannot remove it
- mark that failed session as terminated
- keep the existing delete-and-cleanup behavior when workspace removal succeeds
- verify the next spawn allocates `scratch-2`

No force deletion or fallback cleanup was added, so user files remain protected.

title: feat(landing): add 0.11.0 changelog entry + restore the detail route
body:
the changelog page showed **"No updates yet."** the site's changelog now builds itself from GitHub Releases, with the curated 0.11.0 entry on top.

## what
- `getChangelogEntries` fetches stable `vX.Y.Z` releases from the GitHub API at build time and merges them with any curated `content/changelog` MDX (curated wins for the same version, so 0.11.0 "The Floor" stays until v0.11.0 is tagged)
- filters out nightlies, per-PR prereleases, package tags, and empty-body releases
- **release bodies render as plain Markdown** (`react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`), never through the MDX compiler — so arbitrary release text (`import`/`export` lines, JSX, `{expressions}`) can't break the static build. curated entries still compile as MDX; a `source` field picks the renderer
- restored the missing `/changelog/[slug]` detail route (`generateStaticParams`); the data fns went async (list page, `[slug]`, sitemap, `changelog.xml` updated)

## refresh mechanism
the changelog is baked in at build, so it updates whenever the landing is **redeployed** (a push to `main`, or a manual dispatch). making a newly published release appear automatically needs a `release: [published]` + `schedule` trigger on `deploy-landing.yml` — that workflow edit can't be pushed from this PR's token (no `workflow` scope), so it's a small follow-up a maintainer applies alongside.

## verification
- `next build` (`output: export`) generates `/changelog` + a detail page per entry (0.11.0 + v0.10.3 → v0.2.0)
- reproduced the reviewer's failing case (`export const metadata = {…}` in a body) through react-markdown: renders clean, text kept literal, no throw

title: feat(web): show a running orchestrator's activity indicator on the board (parity with workers)
body:
## Feature request (UI/UX)

**Wish:** give a running orchestrator session a positive activity indicator on the sessions board / sidebar, comparable to the glowing status dot a worker session shows while it is working.

## Today

- A running **worker** session shows a glowing status dot on the board (the `working`/active tone) while the agent is busy.
- A running **orchestrator** shows **no per-session activity status** on the board. It only surfaces as:
  - A toolbar entry (`Orchestrator` / `Spawn Orchestrator` / `Restarting…` / `Spawning…`) with no live activity state.
  - A health banner that appears only when the orchestrator is `!== "ok"` — i.e. on failure/unhealthy, never a positive "actively working" signal.

By construction the board is worker-centric: the orchestrator is deliberately excluded from the list of sessions that get a `SessionCard` (and therefore the status dot), so it never receives an indicator regardless of its activity state.

## Why it matters

While an orchestrator is actively running there is no at-a-glance signal that it is working (vs. idle vs. done). The user has to open the orchestrator to find out. A small positive indicator — same family of tones the workers already use — would make the orchestrator's state visible from the board without opening it, matching how workers already behave.

## Related (not duplicates)

- #2814 — activity pill shows `Idle` while a worker agent is actively working (Kimi missing mid-turn hooks). That is the *activity-state derivation* layer for workers; this request is about the orchestrator *not being rendered with any indicator at all* on the board.
- #1985 — sidebar dot 5-bucket color scheme. About worker dot semantics; does not cover giving the orchestrator an indicator.
- #1563 — killed orchestrator shown as a stale running card. Opposite direction (stale positive signal); this request is about a *live* positive signal for a genuinely running orchestrator.

## Possible directions (not prescribing the fix)

1. Render a dedicated status indicator beside the orchestrator toolbar entry/banner, driven by the orchestrator's activity/status through the same view-mapping already used for workers (keeps tones/legend consistent).
2. Stop excluding the orchestrator from the board's session list and render a card for it too (with a role badge), giving it the same dot treatment as workers by construction.

Either way the goal is the same: a running orchestrator should have a visible "actively working" signal on the board.

title: feat/pr-merge-button
body: ## What Adds backend support for merging a PR directly from Agent Orchestrator: a MergePR method on the GitHub SCM provider, a new pr.ActionService.Merge that validates PR state before delegating to it, and the daemon wiring to connect the two. ## Why Fixes #3064. Today AO can watch and route PR feedback (CI, reviews) but can't act on the merge itself — users have to leave AO and merge on GitHub. This adds the missing merge action to the backend so a "merge" affordance can be exposed (CLI/API/UI) on top of it. ## How - github.Provider.MergePR calls GitHub's REST PUT /pulls/{number}/merge, mapping 405 → ErrProviderPRNotMergeable and 409 → ErrProviderPRPreconditions so callers get typed errors instead of raw HTTP codes. - pr.ActionService.Merge takes a base64url-encoded PR URL (needed since raw PR URLs contain slashes and can't be a chi path segment), resolves it via PRStore.GetPR, and checks Merged/Closed/Mergeability locally before calling out to the SCM — avoids an unnecessary network round-trip for states we already know about. - Merge method is hardcoded to "squash" for now (see TODO in action_service.go). Intentional omission: no caller-specified method picker yet — deferred until the frontend exposes one, to avoid plumbing an unused parameter through the stack. - startSession now returns the *scmgithub.Provider alongside its existing returns so daemon.Run can wire it into prsvc.NewActionService. Added a typed-nil guard when assigning it to the pr.SCMMerger interface: a nil *scmgithub.Provider is not itself a nil interface value, so without the guard ActionService's s.scm == nil check would never trigger even when GitHub credentials are missing at boot. - Reviewers: please double check whether route registration (an HTTP handler calling PRs.Merge) and any frontend button are expected in this same PR per the issue, or are tracked separately — this diff is backend-only. ## Testing Backend: - go test ./backend/internal/service/pr/... — new action_service_test.go covers: successful merge, PR not found, not mergeable, already merged/closed, nil SCM provider (no credentials), and malformed base64 ID. - go test ./backend/internal/daemon/... — updated wiring_test.go call sites for startSession's new 5-value return signature; confirms existing session-service wiring tests still pass. - go build ./... and gofmt -l clean on touched files. Frontend: Before : After: ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix: close session lifecycle gaps
body:
## Summary

- make agent Resume project-aware so branchless Scratch sessions can resume while repository-backed sessions still require a branch
- serialize Resume, Kill, Restore, replacement retirement, and terminal Cleanup per session, with a re-read before Cleanup destroys resources
- fence the durable Resume commit against concurrent terminal intent and launch-generation changes
- make tmux create/restart transitions cancellation-safe: proven post-respawn probe failures retain ownership, while dispatch-timeout uncertainty is separately typed and compensated instead of being falsely adopted
- keep non-atomic runtime replacement (used by Windows ConPTY) inside one bounded, cancellation-detached Destroy/Create transition, while leaving genuine Create failures exited and retryable
- keep `terminate_on_pr_merge` under its dedicated setter so stale generic lifecycle writes cannot revert user policy
- sort activity history by raw timestamps with deterministic invalid/missing fallbacks
- keep terminated sessions out of command-palette attention actions while retaining them in search

## Root cause

Several lifecycle boundaries treated validation, runtime mutation, and persistence as independent operations. Scratch Resume inherited repository-only branch validation; Resume and Kill could cross each other; a successful tmux respawn followed by a transient probe error was reported as total failure; cancellation could split a destructive runtime command from durable adoption or compensation; Cleanup could act on a stale terminated snapshot after Restore had recreated resources; and generic session updates could overwrite independently owned policy state. The renderer also derived timeline ordering and attention actions from presentation-oriented state instead of the underlying lifecycle facts.

## Concurrency and ownership guarantees

- operations for the same session share one ref-counted lock; different session IDs remain independent
- both Resume-first/Kill-second and Kill-first/Resume-second orderings preserve monotonic terminal intent
- Cleanup re-reads the session under that lock, so it cannot destroy a runtime/workspace recreated by a winning Restore
- caller cancellation is honored before a destructive runtime boundary; after dispatch, bounded detached work reaches a coherent adoption or compensation result
- a confirmed tmux respawn plus failed verification is adoptable, but a dispatch-timeout outcome is never treated as proven success and is compensated using the owned handle
- the test-only post-respawn probe runner is mutex-protected, exact-target-specific, and supports interleaved targets without one probe stealing another target's injected failure

## Impact

Scratch sessions can resume reliably, concurrent lifecycle operations preserve terminal monotonicity, Cleanup cannot tear down freshly restored resources, and cancellation or transient tmux failures cannot silently leave an authoritative generation disagreed with runtime reality. Merge policy and renderer state remain consistent across asynchronous updates.

## Validation

- `GOFLAGS=-p=4 npm run lint` — all backend tests and golangci-lint, 0 issues
- `GOFLAGS=-p=4 go test -race ./... -timeout=10m`
- focused concurrency/cancellation suites under `-race -count=50` for Resume/Kill, Cleanup/Restore, fallback Destroy/Create, tmux Create/Restart, compensation, retry, and target-specific probe injection
- real isolated tmux daemon: race-enabled post-respawn failure integration test passed three consecutive runs
- full frontend Vitest suite: 87 files / 1,086 tests
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck`
- packaged Electron → real daemon/SQLite → real agent process/hooks → real isolated tmux Resume E2E, passed twice
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #3087

title: bug(frontend): hidden collapsed-sidebar Settings button remains keyboard-focusable
body:
## Description

When the sidebar is expanded, the Settings button from the collapsed sidebar rail remains in the keyboard tab order underneath the visible Settings row.

This creates a duplicate invisible focus stop for keyboard and screen-reader users.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Electron app with the sidebar expanded.
2. Navigate to the visible **Settings** button using the keyboard.
3. Press `Tab` once.
4. Focus moves to the hidden Settings button belonging to the collapsed sidebar rail.

## Expected behavior

Only the currently visible Settings control should be focusable and exposed to assistive technologies.

## Actual behavior

The hidden rail button receives keyboard focus even though it is not the active sidebar variant.

Verified on the native Electron renderer from the latest `main`:

- hidden button has `tabIndex=0`
- `aria-hidden` is not set
- visible text is empty
- CSS has `pointer-events: none`
- pressing `Tab` from the visible Settings row focuses this hidden button

## Possible fix

Remove the inactive sidebar variant from the tab order and accessibility tree, for example with `tabIndex={-1}` and `aria-hidden="true"`, while ensuring those attributes switch correctly when the sidebar collapses. A focused keyboard-accessibility test should cover both expanded and collapsed states.

I am willing to work on this issue.

This makes the three most common PR/review actions available directly from `Cmd/Ctrl+K`, with disabled states that explain why an action is unavailable. ## How - New `CommandAction` variants (`open-pr`, `copy-pr-url`, `trigger-review`) in `command-palette.ts`, with three new items emitted per open PR in `buildCommands`. The palette and the Reviews tab now share one fetch path, one React Query cache key, and one copy of the disabled-state logic — no duplicated eligibility math to drift. - `CommandPalette.tsx` fetches review states via `useQueries` for sessions with open PRs **only while the palette is open**; sessions already viewed in the inspector reuse cached data. Unloaded/failed review fetches leave the action enabled — the daemon validates on trigger and the palette's existing error banner surfaces the response. - Disabled states mirror ReviewPanel semantics: session review running → "Review already running"; ineligible or draft PR → "Not eligible for review". The trigger is deliberately session-scoped (same endpoint as the Reviews tab button — one run covers all of a session's eligible open PRs), so multi-PR sessions show one row per PR, all firing the same session trigger with per-PR-accurate labels. - Trigger success invalidates `["session-reviews", id]` + the workspace query, same as ReviewsView. Also adds `copy` to the Copy branch name keywords (the issue's discoverability ask). Intentional omissions: no palette `Cancel review` action — the issue specifies a disabled "review already running" state, so cancel stays in the Reviews tab (possible fast-follow). New coverage: 9 `buildCommands` tests (per-PR action items + URLs, Run vs Re-run labels, "Review already running" / "Not eligible for review" disabled states, enabled-while-unloaded fallback, multi-PR sessions, merged/closed exclusion, `open pr`/`copy pr`/`review` search discoverability, search-only hiding, `copy` keyword on Copy branch) and 6 `CommandPalette` action tests (Open PR fires `openExternal` + closes, Copy PR URL writes clipboard + closes, Run review POSTs the trigger endpoint with the session id + closes, trigger failure keeps the palette open with the daemon error in the alert banner, disabled running/ineligible items never POST). - Full renderer suite `npm test` — 1100 passed (87 files), confirming the SessionInspector extraction is behavior-preserving. - `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` — clean. Screenshots (browser preview, `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1`, mock data; palette opened with `Cmd+K`): Before: After: Highlights: `open pr` goes from plain `#N` navigate rows to 11 direct `Open PR #N` actions; `copy pr` goes from one accidental title match to 11 `Copy PR URL #N` actions; `review` goes from session-name matches only to per-PR `Run review`/`Re-run review` items with "Not eligible for review" shown on the draft PR. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (frontend vitest + typecheck)

title: fix(release): skip blockmap sidecar for macOS zips
body:
## What
Short-term fix for #3034: macOS zips no longer get a `.blockmap` sidecar
file generated or referenced in the feed yml.

## Why
Squirrel.Mac's ShipIt install step runs `ditto` against the extracted
update cache, which fails looking for AppleDouble (`._*`) metadata files
that `@electron-forge/maker-zip`'s output never contains (unlike
`electron-builder`'s ditto-based zips). A blockmap-driven differential
update against that mismatched zip format is the likely corruption path
causing the reported `ditto: ... No such file or directory` errors.

## How
- Added `hashFile` — computes the same `{sha512, size}` shape
  `writeBlockmap` returns, but via plain `node:crypto` hashing, with no
  `.blockmap` sidecar written to disk.
- `generateFeeds` now uses `hashFile` for mac zips specifically and keeps
  `writeBlockmap` unchanged for win/linux.
- Since no sidecar exists for mac, `electron-updater`'s `MacUpdater` will
  always fall back to a full zip download instead of attempting a
  blockmap diff — this doesn't fix the underlying zip-format mismatch, but
  removes the specific failure path from this bug report.

## Scope
This is the **short-term** fix the issue proposes. The **long-term** fix —
generating mac zips via `ditto` (matching `electron-builder`'s format,
preserving AppleDouble metadata) — is a bigger change to the packaging
pipeline (`forge.config.ts` / a custom maker or post-package hook) that I
haven't attempted here, since it needs real macOS build/sign/publish
verification to confirm it actually resolves auto-update end-to-end. This
PR only removes the blockmap-sidecar half of the failure; tracking the
`ditto`-based packaging fix as a separate follow-up.

## Testing
- `npx vitest run scripts/feed.test.mjs` — 19 tests pass, including new
  coverage: `hashFile` unit tests (correct sha512/size, no sidecar
  written) and `generateFeeds` regression tests confirming mac skips
  `writeBlockmap` entirely while win/linux are unchanged.
- Full frontend suite `npx vitest run` — 1089 tests pass across 87 files,
  no regressions.
- `grep` confirms no other script/build step depends on `writeBlockmap`
  running unconditionally for every platform.

**Important caveat**: these tests confirm the *logic* — no blockmap is
produced/referenced for mac — but not that a real macOS auto-update now
succeeds end-to-end. That requires a signed build published through the
real release pipeline, which I don't have access to. Flagging for
@illegalcall / @Pulkit7070 (already assigned to #3034) to confirm on an
actual nightly build before considering this fully verified in
production.

Fixes the short-term portion of #3034.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Long-term fix for #3034: replace maker-zip with ditto-based mac packaging
body:
## Context
Follow-up to #3034. #<short-term-PR-number> ships the short-term fix
(skip the `.blockmap` sidecar for macOS zips, forcing full downloads
instead of a corrupted differential update). This issue tracks the
actual root-cause fix: the macOS zip artifact itself is built in a
format Squirrel.Mac's `ditto`-based install step doesn't fully support.

## Root cause (from #3034)
`@electron-forge/maker-zip` uses a pure-JS zip writer that never
produces AppleDouble (`._*`) companion files or preserves extended
attributes/resource forks — unlike `electron-builder`, which uses
macOS's native `ditto` to build its zips. Squirrel.Mac's ShipIt install
step shells out to `ditto` to extract updates, and `ditto` expects those
companion entries to exist next to their real files. Their absence is
the likely cause of the `ditto: ... No such file or directory` errors
in #3034.

## Proposed direction
Replace `@electron-forge/maker-zip` for the darwin target with a maker
that produces a zip via the same mechanism `electron-builder` uses,
so the artifact format matches what Squirrel.Mac already knows how to
extract.

**Two possible approaches, in order of preference:**

1. **Delegate to `app-builder-lib`** (electron-builder's internals),
   mirroring the existing pattern in `makers/maker-nsis.ts`, which
   already calls `app-builder-lib`'s `buildForge` rather than
   hand-rolling NSIS invocation. Needs research: does `app-builder-lib`
   expose a usable mac zip target that internally uses `ditto`? If so,
   this is the lower-risk option — it reuses code this project already
   trusts for Windows packaging, and may make it possible to safely
   *re-enable* blockmap differential updates for mac (currently
   disabled by #<short-term-PR-number>), since electron-builder's own
   blockmap generator (`blockmap.mjs` already reaches into it) is
   designed for its own zip format.

2. **Hand-roll a `ditto`-based maker** (`execFileSync("ditto", ["-c",
   "-k", "--keepParent", ...])`), if `app-builder-lib` doesn't expose a
   suitable target. Higher risk: reimplements packaging logic instead
   of delegating to a proven library, and needs careful flag selection
   (`--keepParent`, no `--sequesterRsrc`, so AppleDouble entries land
   inline next to their real files — matching the layout in the
   reported ditto errors — rather than in a separate `__MACOSX/`
   folder).

## Why this needs to be a separate PR/issue from the short-term fix
- Touches `forge.config.ts` and the actual release artifact every
  macOS user downloads — much higher blast radius than the short-term
  feed-generation change.
- Cannot be verified without a real macOS build → sign → notarize →
  publish → auto-update cycle. Local `vitest` runs can confirm a maker
  produces *a* zip, but not that Squirrel.Mac's `ShipIt` step correctly
  extracts and installs it end-to-end.
- May interact with codesigning/notarization (`osxSign`/`osxNotarize`
  in `forge.config.ts`) in ways that need real verification, even
  though switching zip tools shouldn't change what's inside the signed
  `.app` bundle itself.

## What's needed to close this
- [ ] Research whether `app-builder-lib` exposes a usable mac zip
      target (approach 1)
- [ ] Prototype maker (either approach), with unit tests mirroring
      `makers/maker-nsis.test.ts`'s style (mock the underlying
      build call, assert on invocation args/output path)
- [ ] Real macOS packaging run confirming the zip contains expected
      AppleDouble entries (`unzip -l` / manual inspection)
- [ ] Real signed build + publish + auto-update verification that a
      client successfully installs an update built this way
- [ ] Decision on whether to re-enable blockmap differential updates
      for mac once the format is confirmed compatible, or leave the
      short-term full-download behavior in place indefinitely

## Related
- #3034 (original bug report)
- #3151 (short-term fix, merged/pending)

title: feat(lifecycle): reap a session's Docker containers on terminal state (#2652)
body: ## What Adds a Docker container reaper that force-removes containers a worker session started when that session is killed / reaches terminal state. ## Why AO tears down a session's runtime and workspace on terminal state, but never touches Docker containers a worker launched (e.g. `docker run postgres` for a local dev database). Nothing ties a container's lifecycle to the session ending, so they accrete indefinitely. This is the container leg of the same "tear down what the worker owns on session end" story #2523 covers for orphan processes and #2608/#2646 cover for worktrees. Fixes #2652 ## How - New `ports.ContainerReaper` interface + `internal/adapters/container/dockerreap` adapter: shells out to `docker ps`/`docker rm -f`, filtered on the `ao.session=` label. A container additionally labeled `ao.spare=true` is never reaped — the opt-out for deliberately shared substrate (a shared postgres, a registry). - Wired into `sessionmanager.Manager.Kill`, called right after runtime destroy, mirroring the existing `cleanupAgentWorkspace` pattern: best-effort, logged on failure, **never returned to the caller** — a reap failure must not block or fail a session kill. - Every failure mode (missing `docker` binary, a probe error, an ambiguous label) resolves to "remove nothing," per the issue's explicit bias toward sparing over guessing — a wrongly-reaped container can cost a live worker its database. - New `ProjectConfig.ContainerReap.Disabled` lets a project opt out of container reaping entirely. - No new AO-side env-injection was needed: `AO_SESSION_ID` is already exported into every worker's environment. A worker that starts its own containers labels them `--label ao.session=$AO_SESSION_ID` (documented at the `EnvSessionID` declaration) for AO to find and reap them. - Intentionally did **not** hook into `session_cleanup_facts` / `ListTerminalCleanupCandidates`: that table was added by #2811/#2853 as schema scaffolding with no consumer yet, so there's no live finalizer to attach to. This lands as a synchronous step in the existing `Kill` path instead, matching how workspace/runtime teardown already works today. ## Testing - `internal/adapters/container/dockerreap/reap_test.go`: table-driven against a fake command runner — labeled removal, spared containers skipped, no containers found, empty session id, missing docker binary, list failure (spares everything), partial removal (one succeeds, one fails). - `internal/session_manager/manager_test.go`: `Kill`-path regression tests — reaper is invoked on kill, a reap failure does not block/fail kill and runtime/workspace teardown still completes, reap is skipped when no reaper is wired and when a project disables it. - Full backend suite: `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` — all green (`openapi.yaml` regenerated via `go generate ./...` to reflect the new `ContainerReapConfig` field). ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` - [x] One focused change; links the related issue - [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for the new behavior - [x] Relevant CI checks pass (`go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`)

title: fix(crush): forward role-specific model config on launch
body: ## What Forwards AO's per-role model config (`agentConfig.Model`) into Crush's `.crush.json` on launch, so a configured worker/orchestrator model actually takes effect instead of silently falling back to Crush's own default. ## Why Fixes #2900. Every adapter must opt in to forwarding `cfg.Config.Model` to its CLI. Claude, Codex, and Kiro already do this; Crush was one of the adapters that silently dropped it. ## How The issue needed a decision between two routes: - **Flag route (rejected):** Crush's `--model`/`-m` flag only exists on the non-interactive `crush run` subcommand — confirmed via Crush's CLI docs (root-only flags are just `--yolo`, `--session`, `--continue`). It's not available on the interactive root command AO actually launches, so a flag fix was never viable. - **Config route (chosen):** `.crush.json`'s `models.large` selection requires both a `model` id and a `provider` id, but AO's `AgentConfig.Model` is a single bare string with no provider. Rather than adding a `Provider` field to AO's schema (which would ripple through the API, UI, and every other adapter), this scopes the fix to the Crush adapter only: it parses `Model` as the convention `"/"` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`) and merges it into `.crush.json`'s `models.large` in `GetAgentHooks`. Implementation notes: - `GetAgentHooks` runs before both Spawn and Restore (via `prepareWorkspace`), so the model override is re-applied on every launch and stays current if the role's config changes. - The merge preserves any other fields already on `models.large` (e.g. a user's `max_tokens`/`temperature`), and any other top-level `.crush.json` config — it only owns the `model`/`provider` identity keys. - If `Config.Model` is empty, nothing is touched, so a model the user picked through Crush's own model picker is left alone. - A model string without a `/` (no provider) returns a clear error rather than silently forwarding something Crush would reject. - `GetConfigSpec` now declares the `model` field and its required `"/"` format, matching the `claude-code`/`codex`/`kiro` pattern. **Intentional omission:** this doesn't add a `provider` field to `domain.AgentConfig`/the API/UI. That was one of the two options raised in the issue; I went with the string-convention approach to keep the change scoped to the Crush adapter. Happy to switch to a schema field if maintainers prefer that route instead. ## Testing Ran the crush adapter's test suite locally: ```bash go build ./internal/adapters/agent/crush/... go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/crush/... gofmt -l internal/adapters/agent/crush/*.go go test ./internal/adapters/agent/crush/... -v ``` All existing tests pass, plus new coverage: - `TestGetConfigSpecReportsModelField` — spec declares the `model` field - `TestGetAgentHooksWritesModelOverride` — provider/model parsed and written into `models.large` - `TestGetAgentHooksPreservesOtherModelFieldsOnOverride` — unrelated keys (e.g. `max_tokens`) survive the merge - `TestGetAgentHooksLeavesModelUntouchedWhenNoOverride` — no override means no write, user's own selection untouched - `TestGetAgentHooksRejectsModelWithoutProvider` — bare model string (no `/`) errors clearly ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(droid): forward role-specific model config via settings file
body:
## What
Droid adapter now forwards `agentConfig.model` into Droid's runtime `--settings`
file instead of silently dropping it.

## Why
Fixes #2898. AO resolves a per-role model into `cfg.Config.Model` and forwards
it to every adapter, but each adapter has to opt in to actually using it.
Claude Code, Codex (#2869), and Kiro already do; Droid didn't — a configured
worker/orchestrator model silently fell back to the CLI's global default.

## How
Interactive `droid` has no `--model` flag (it only exists on `droid exec`), so
model can't be forwarded as an argv flag the way Codex does it. Instead this
folds a top-level `"model"` key into the same runtime settings JSON blob
already used for permission autonomy (`sessionDefaultSettings.autonomyLevel`),
and writes/passes `--settings <path>` whenever *either* value is set (previously
only written for non-default permission modes).

- `permissionSettingsArgs` takes a `model` param, trims it, and sets `model` in
  the settings blob when non-empty.
- `GetLaunchCommand` / `GetRestoreCommand` pass `cfg.Config.Model` through.
- Added `GetConfigSpec` (Droid had none before, so `model` wasn't surfaced as a
  configurable field at all) — mirrors the Codex adapter's spec shape.
- Updated package/function doc comments — the old comments explicitly said
  "only the autonomy level is overridden," which is no longer accurate.

**Intentional omission / open question carried over from the issue:** whether
Droid's `--settings` top-level `model` key actually re-pins the session model
live isn't confirmed by Factory's docs — the issue flags this explicitly as
unverified upstream behavior (see linked Factory issues in #2898). I don't have
a live `droid` binary to confirm against, so this needs a manual smoke test
before merge. If it turns out `--settings`'s `model` key is ignored by Droid in
practice, this PR's mechanism is wrong and option 2 (documented no-op) from the
issue should be taken instead.

## Testing
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/droid/...` — all existing tests pass, plus
  new regression tests: model-only settings write, model+autonomy combined in
  one file, and restore forwarding model.
- `go test ./...` — full backend suite green.
- `go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/droid/...` — clean.
- Grepped `docs/`, `backend/`, `frontend/` for the old "Droid resolves its own
  model" language — none found outside the file itself.
- **Not yet done:** manual verification against a live `droid` binary that the
  settings-file `model` key actually changes the session's model.

## What

Add a provider-free candidate-run observer boundary while keeping Agent Orchestrator as the sole native dispatcher and workspace allocator.

- bind an external, digest-pinned framed-stdio observer sidecar

title: Terminal visibly auto-scrolls from mid-session position on session open
body:
## Bug Description

When opening any worker session, the terminal briefly shows a mid-session position and then visibly auto-scrolls down to the end. This happens every time a session is opened or re-attached, and feels janky/broken to users.

## Root Cause

xterm.js processes large `write()` data **asynchronously in incremental batches** (~15KB write-buffer chunks), rendering intermediate buffer states between batches. The scrollback/handshake replay arrives as a single burst of PTY bytes but xterm splits it into chunks, rendering each chunk before processing the next. The cursor (and viewport) advances through the replay top-to-bottom across multiple animation frames, producing the visible scroll.

The timeline on first session open:

1. **Frontend opens** (`useTerminalSession.ts:195`): `mux.open()` + `mux.resize()` fire immediately
2. **Backend attaches** (`attachment.go:137`): `src.Attach()` spawns `tmux attach-session` (macOS/Linux) or dials the conpty host (Windows)
3. **Runtime replays scrollback**:
   - **tmux**: `tmux attach-session` replays the pane's full screen state
   - **conpty**: `Ring.Snapshot()` (`conpty/ring.go:61`) returns up to **1000 lines** of stored output, sent as the first `MsgTerminalData` frame (`conpty/host.go:253-264`)
4. **`copyOut()`** (`attachment.go:185`) pumps bytes in 32KB chunks → `onData` → WS frames → frontend `terminal.write(bytes)` (`useTerminalSession.ts:212`)
5. **xterm's write buffer** processes the replay in ~15KB batches via `setTimeout` scheduling. Between batches, the renderer draws the current buffer state — the viewport visibly scrolls from mid-replay to the final bottom position.

**Compound effect**: The onRender convergence loop (`XtermTerminal.tsx:550-571`) fires up to 20 re-fits during attach, each sending a backend `Resize` → SIGWINCH → application repaint. These repaint bytes interleave with the initial replay, extending the scroll duration.

## Why No Existing Mitigation Catches This

- **No visual gate during `connecting`**: `TerminalPane` shows `showEmptyState` only when `!handleId` (no terminal handle). Once a session is selected, xterm is immediately visible and receives replay data with no cover overlay (`TerminalPane.tsx:329`).
- **No batch-write API**: `onData` calls `terminal.write(bytes)` per WS frame — no callback signaling when the initial replay is fully processed.
- **`firstAttach` only gates `clear()`** (`useTerminalSession.ts:115`), not visibility.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn a worker session and let it run for a few minutes (accumulate scrollback)
2. Switch away to another session or close the pane
3. Open the worker session again
4. Observe: the terminal shows mid-session content, then visibly scrolls down to the bottom

## Expected Behavior

The terminal should appear already-rendered at the final scroll position. No visible mid-session scroll.


## Key Files

| File | Symbol | Role |
|------|--------|------|
| `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts` | `connect()` L195, `onData` L210 | Attach lifecycle, data handler |
| `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx` | `AttachedTerminal` L223, `showEmptyState` L329 | Overlay gating |
| `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx` | mount effect L272, onRender stabilizer L550 | xterm init + fit convergence loop |
| `backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go` | `copyOut()` L185, `setPTY()` L274 | Replay pump, `onOpen` timing |
| `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/host.go` | `handleConn()` L241 | Scrollback snapshot replay |
| `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/ring.go` | `Snapshot()` L61 | 1000-line scrollback buffer |

## Environment

- All platforms (macOS/Linux via tmux, Windows via conpty)
- Most noticeable on sessions with substantial scrollback (5+ minutes of agent output)

title: Landing analytics banner is misleading and privacy link is broken
body:
## Summary
The landing page cookie/analytics banner currently says:

> We only collect analytics cookies so we can improve your experience.

That wording is misleading for the current deployed site.

## Current behavior
- The `/privacy` link from the banner goes to a 404 page on `https://aoagents.dev/privacy`.
- The live landing page does not appear to send landing events to PostHog right now.
- The page does load Cloudflare Web Analytics / RUM (`static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js`) and posts performance data to `/cdn-cgi/rum`.
- The banner consent controls only the PostHog code path, not Cloudflare RUM.
- The banner stores the local consent value in `localStorage` under `redacted-analytics-consent` after Accept/Opt-out.

## Source notes
- PostHog init is gated behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` in `frontend/src/landing/src/instrumentation-client.ts`.
- The GitHub Pages deploy runs the static build without passing a PostHog key in `.github/workflows/deploy-landing.yml`.
- `frontend/src/landing/next.config.ts` is a static export and says server-backed rewrites/proxy are intentionally omitted, so the configured `/ingest` proxy is not backed by a Next server.
- `frontend/src/landing/src/components/CookieConsent/CookieConsent.tsx` links to `/privacy`.
- `frontend/src/landing/content/legal` is missing, so the privacy page is not generated.

## Expected behavior
- The privacy link should resolve to a real privacy policy page.
- The banner copy should accurately describe what is collected and where it goes.
- If analytics are intended to be consent-based, Cloudflare RUM should not fire before opt-in, or the banner should clearly disclose that Cloudflare performance analytics run independently of the PostHog consent choice.
- If PostHog is later enabled, capture should be gated by explicit opt-in before any pageview/pageleave/exception event is sent.

## Acceptance criteria
- Add or restore a real `/privacy` page.
- Update the banner copy to match the actual analytics behavior.
- Decide whether Cloudflare RUM is allowed before consent; if not, gate/disable it until opt-in.
- Ensure PostHog, if configured, does not capture before opt-in.

title: No cross-session merge-conflict coordination — overlapping PRs cause cascading rebase churn
body:
---

Problem

When multiple worker sessions open PRs that touch the same lines in the same repo (all targeting main), AO detects merge conflicts on each independently and nudges all affected workers simultaneously to rebase and resolve. There is no global ordering or serialization of conflict resolution across sessions.

After one worker's PR merges, main shifts, invalidating the conflict resolutions performed by the other workers. Those workers are then re-detected as conflicting and nudged again. This creates a wasteful cycle:

All PRs ready
→ Merge one
→ Remaining PRs conflict
→ Multiple workers resolve conflicts simultaneously
→ Merge one resolved PR
→ Remaining PRs conflict again
→ repeat


Root cause

The lifecycle manager's world model is per-session. The only conflict-suppression mechanism — prBlockedByOpenParent (reactions.go:309) — checks whether a PR is stacked behind an open parent via ListPRsBySession, which is scoped to a single session ID. When three workers from three different sessions each open independent PRs against main, none are considered "stacked," so none get suppressed. The sendOnce dedup (reactions.go:752) is keyed per-PR and only prevents duplicate nudges for the same PR — it has no cross-PR awareness.

There is no per-repo view of "all open PRs targeting the same base branch," no conflict arbitration to designate one PR as active while holding the rest, and no sequential re-evaluation after a merge shifts main.

Traced code path

| Step | Code location | Behavior |
|------|--------------|----------|
| Observer polls all sessions | observe/scm/observer.go:250 Poll() | Iterates all sessions, dispatches per-PR independently | (1/3)
| Conflict detected per PR | lifecycle/reactions.go:214 | if o.Mergeability == domain.MergeConflicting |
| Stack suppression check | lifecycle/reactions.go:220 → prBlockedByOpenParent | Calls ListPRsBySession(sessionID) — same-session only |
| Rebase nudge queued | lifecycle/reactions.go:225-229 | Message: "Rebase onto the base branch and resolve them" |
| Dedup | lifecycle/reactions.go:752 sendOnce | Keyed "merge-conflict:<prURL>", sig = enum string — no base SHA encoding |
| Post-merge re-evaluation | (none) | No re-sequencing of remaining conflicting PRs |

Impact

Wasted agent compute — multiple workers rebasing against main simultaneously, knowing only one can merge and the rest will re-conflict.
Increased wall-clock time — the cycle length is O(N) merge rounds for N overlapping PRs, where O(1) rounds would suffice with serialization.
Potential for repeated merge-conflict dispatch storms on repos with high PR throughput targeting the same files.

Proposed direction

The existing stack-suppression pattern in service/session/stack.go (buildStacks) and reactions.go:304-326 (prBlockedByOpenParent) is the right template — it already implements "don't nudge a PR that isn't ready to act." The gap is its visibility boundary (one session). Extending it requires:

Cross-session PR query — a store method like ListOpenPRsByRepoAndBaseBranch(repo, baseBranch) to see all sibling PRs across all sessions targeting the same base.
Conflict arbitration — when N PRs conflict against the same base, designate one as "active for resolution" and suppress rebased nudges to the rest (same !blocked gate, broader view).
Sequential re-evaluation — after the active PR merges and main shifts, re-evaluate the queue and promote the next conflicting PR.

Environment

Component: comp/daemon (lifecycle layer) (2/3)
Code path: backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go → ApplyPRObservation → prBlockedByOpenParent
Relevant files: backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go, backend/internal/service/session/stack.go, backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go
Labels: bug, comp/daemon, P1 (3/3)

title: feat: per-role Codex model and reasoning configuration
body:
## What

Lets a project configure the Codex **model** and **reasoning effort** separately for workers and orchestrators — in the project config, the CLI, and the desktop settings UI.

## Why

A common setup is a stronger, higher-reasoning model orchestrating while cheaper, faster workers do the runs (for example a Sol/high orchestrator over Terra/medium workers). Today `agentConfig` only carries a model override and cannot express reasoning effort at all, so per-role tuning is not possible.

Closes #3188.

Note that per-role **model** support for Codex was already handled in #2769; what is missing is reasoning effort, and a picker so model IDs are not typed by hand.

## How

**Backend**

- Add `reasoningEffort` to `domain.AgentConfig`, validated against `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh`.
- `effectiveAgentConfig` merges role overrides over the project-wide defaults, so worker and orchestrator resolve independently. A blank or whitespace-only role value **inherits** the project default rather than clearing it — a blank field in the settings form must read as "inherit", not "override with nothing".
- The Codex adapter advertises `reasoningEffort` in `GetConfigSpec` and forwards the resolved value as `-c model_reasoning_effort="<effort>"` on **both** launch and native resume, mirroring the existing model override.
- The CLI mirrors the new field in its `agentConfig` DTO.
- Regenerated `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.

No `~/.codex/config.toml` writes and no migration: this rides on the existing project configuration.

**Frontend**

- New `ModelOverrideSelect`: GPT-5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna and GPT-5.5, an "Agent default" (inherit) option, and a custom model ID input so unlisted or future model IDs stay reachable.
- `ProjectSettingsForm` gains per-role model and reasoning controls, a resolved effective-configuration summary, and a one-click "Sol orchestrates, Terra works" preset.

**Docs**

- README section on the config shape and the desktop picker.
- New `docs/per-role-agent-config.md`: resolution rules, the Codex argv mapping, the lifecycle caveat below, how to verify a change, Windows testing caveats, and what must be re-derived before extending the pattern to another provider.

**Behaviour reviewers should know:** model and reasoning bind into argv when the agent process starts, so saving new values does not mutate an already-running session. New sessions and resume pick them up; a long-lived orchestrator keeps its original values until it is replaced. This is easy to misread as a bug, so it is written up in the new doc.

**Rebase note:** `ProjectSettingsForm` was rebased across the editable-display-name change (#2970). The per-role controls now save through `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}` with `{displayName, config}`, and the tests assert that contract. The rewritten `ReviewerSelect` from that change is preserved as-is.

**Intentional omissions**

- One commit here is test-only: coverage for a **branchless** session in the command palette. `main` already guards that case in `command-palette.ts`, but nothing exercised it. Say the word and I will drop it to keep this PR strictly to the Codex feature.
- A Windows named-pipe fix for `src/main/supervisor-link.test.ts` and a local `.worktrees/` ignore entry were left out as unrelated; happy to send either separately.

## Testing

- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` — passes.
- `npm --prefix frontend run test` — 1101 passing, including the new `ModelOverrideSelect`, `ProjectSettingsForm`, and command-palette specs.
  - The only failures are 4 pre-existing, Windows-only cases in the unrelated `src/main/supervisor-link.test.ts` (`listen EACCES` on `.sock` paths). That file is untouched here and passes on Linux CI.
- `npm run api:ts` — regenerates `schema.ts` with no drift.
- Backend Go tests were **not run locally** — no Go toolchain in this environment. Backend behaviour is covered by added/updated table tests in `codex_test.go`, `agentconfig` / `projectconfig` tests, `projects_test.go`, `project_test.go`, and `provision_test.go`, and I am relying on the `go` CI workflow to gate them. Please flag anything you want re-verified.

title: fix(agy): honor cfg.Config.Model via --model flag on launch/restore
body:
## What
Forwards the per-role model override (`cfg.Config.Model`) to the `agy` (Antigravity) CLI as a `--model` flag on both session launch and session restore, and declares a `GetConfigSpec` entry for it.

## Why
Fixes #2901.

AO resolves a per-role model and forwards it to every adapter as `cfg.Config.Model`, but each adapter has to opt in to actually passing it to its CLI. The `agy` adapter never did, so a configured worker/orchestrator silently fell back to agy's default model instead of the one set in `agentConfig.model`.

## How
- Verified via `agy --help` that a launch-time flag exists (`--model  Model for the current CLI session`) — this was previously unconfirmed per the issue, so it settles the "does agy even support this" question in favor of applying the mechanical fix.
- Mirrors the pattern from the Codex adapter fix (#2869): an `appendModelFlag(cmd *[]string, cfg ports.AgentConfig)` helper that appends `--model <trimmed value>` only when set, called from both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`.
- Added `GetConfigSpec` (previously inherited empty from `agentbase.Base`), declaring the `model` field with the same shape used by the Codex/Copilot adapters, so the config layer/UI know this adapter now supports a model override.
- Intentional omission worth flagging: unlike the Copilot adapter (#2895), which deliberately does *not* forward `--model` on restore pending verification of `--model` + `--resume` composition, this PR forwards on both launch **and** restore. I found no equivalent warning for `agy` in `--help` or available docs, so I didn't add the same restriction — but a reviewer with a real `agy` install should sanity-check this.

## Testing
```
go build ./...
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/...
golangci-lint run ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/...
```
All pass, 0 lint issues. Covered:
- `TestGetLaunchCommand` — model set, flag appears in the right position.
- `TestGetLaunchCommandNoModel` — model unset, flag omitted entirely.
- `TestGetRestoreCommand` — model set, flag appears alongside `--conversation`.
- `TestGetConfigSpecReportsModelField` — config spec reports the `model` field.

Not yet verified locally: an actual `agy --model <x> --print "..."` run against a real `agy` binary, to confirm the flag changes model selection at runtime rather than just being accepted without erroring.

## Checklist
- [x] Branched from `main` (`fix/agy-model-override`)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue (#2901)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
