Switched to registering the font as a `FontFace` built from decoded bytes on the shadow root's own `FontFaceSet` — no network fetch, so it isn't subject to the page's CSP. ## Test plan - [x] `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts annotate-preload` — 5/5 passing, including new coverage asserting the `FontFace` registration path actually runs with "Geist Variable"/"Geist Mono Variable" - [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean - [x] Manual check in the desktop app: open a project's browser preview, enter annotate mode, select an element, confirm the popup matches the diff viewer's feedback box styling and the font renders as Geist

title: fix(tmux): contain opted-in worker processes after setsid
body:
## What

Add an explicit Linux `AO_PROCESS_CONTAINMENT=systemd` backend for tmux worker processes, and make the contained worker lifecycle generation-specific.

The worker pane command runs in a deterministic transient systemd user scope. Create, Restart, and Destroy report rollback or release only after AO has verified the exact requested worker generation.

## Why

The existing tmux reaper matches the pane's POSIX session ID. A descendant that calls `setsid` leaves that session and can survive tmux teardown (the gap tracked by #2523).

A systemd scope closes that process-ownership gap, but it also introduces a second external lifecycle resource alongside the tmux session. A canceled or ambiguous tmux client result does not prove that `new-session` or `respawn-pane` was not accepted, and a concurrent generation may reuse the stable tmux session name. Cleanup must therefore be fenced to one exact launch; otherwise AO could kill a foreign generation or remove a workspace before runtime release was proven.

Refs #2523

## How

- Keep the existing tmux SID reaper unchanged when `AO_PROCESS_CONTAINMENT` is unset.
- Accept `systemd` only on Linux; fail before creating a tmux session when the explicitly selected user-scope backend is unavailable, with no silent fallback.
- Wrap the existing launch command with `systemd-run --user --scope --collect`, using `KillMode=control-group`, `TimeoutStopSec`, and `SendSIGKILL=yes`.
- Carry the existing worker `RuntimeLaunchID` through the internal runtime config and handle. The same launch ID identifies the supervised worker, tmux generation marker, and deterministic systemd scope.
- Atomically write the tmux generation marker in the same server-side command queue as `new-session` or `respawn-pane`.
- Fence destructive tmux cleanup to the recorded generation. Foreign or unmarked sessions are preserved rather than killed.
- Distinguish rollback-safe Create failures from preserve-required outcomes. Untyped or ambiguous failures preserve the session row, runtime reference, and workspace.
- Release and verify the old exact scope before Restart creates the replacement scope. Failed replacement cleanup restores the old marker only through a generation-fenced operation.
- Remove a worker workspace or claim termination only after exact runtime release succeeds.
- Keep reviewer, standalone shell-terminal, Chat, default-unset, macOS, and Windows ConPTY behavior outside the worker-containment path.
- Record the process-boundary decision in ADR 0003 and the generation-specific lifecycle contract in ADR 0004.

This changes only internal runtime/lifecycle contracts. It does not add a public API, schema, database migration, or production configuration change.

## Cross-platform remediation

The reported macOS/Windows failure was valid: `TestLoadOverrides` unconditionally selected the Linux-only backend while `Load()` correctly rejected it on non-Linux systems.

The current head:

- leaves containment unset in the general override test;
- table-tests containment parsing for Linux, Darwin, and Windows;
- guards the Linux-only `Load()` acceptance test with `runtime.GOOS`; and
- runs `go test -count=1 ./internal/config` in the native Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows GitHub Actions matrix.

## Latest-main resynchronization

The current head merges upstream main snapshot `e5c4c3e8092d1fd3a9374a6c1f9e07410821dc6a` into the exact-generation branch.

Five textual conflicts were resolved by preserving both contracts:

- ConPTY keeps the run-file-scoped registry, protocol negotiation, and styled viewport behavior while carrying typed Create outcomes and `RuntimeLaunchID`.
- Runtime selection and daemon wiring carry both the Windows run-file scope and Unix process-containment option.
- Config retains both GitLab settings and the Linux-only containment setting.
- Session-manager tests retain current-main restart, attachment, model, draft, and recovery coverage together with exact-generation failure preservation.

The earlier dirty random-token proposal was not carried forward because the committed `RuntimeLaunchID` design supersedes it and provides an atomic server-side generation fence.

## Out of scope

This PR intentionally does not include:

- enabling containment by default;
- macOS containment or Windows systemd behavior;
- memory, CPU, or other resource limits;
- durable cleanup-pending storage, migrations, or retry queues;
- daemon-crash recovery for unfinished scope cleanup; or
- production rollout or deployment.

title: fix(frontend): duplicate checkmark on selected agent in New Task modal
body:
## Bug

In the **New Task** modal, the selected agent shows a checkmark icon **twice** — once in the dropdown row and once echoed in the select trigger below it.

**Reported by:** @Dhruv Sharma (bug-triage channel)

## Screenshot

![duplicate-check](https://files.slack.com/files-tmb/placeholder.png)

## Root cause

`RequiredAgentField` (`CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx`) wraps each agent option in a Radix `SelectItem`:

```tsx
<SelectItem key={agent.id} value={agent.id} disabled={agent.disabled}>
    <AgentSelectMenuItem
        agentId={agent.id}
        label={agent.label}
        selected={value === agent.id}   // ← renders a <Check> when true
        status={agent.status}
        statusTone={agent.statusTone}
        disabled={agent.disabled}
    />
</SelectItem>
```

`AgentSelectMenuItem` (`settings/AgentSelectMenuItem.tsx:38`) renders an explicit `<Check>` (lucide-react) when `selected === true`:

```tsx
{selected ? <Check className="size-3 shrink-0 text-settings-label" aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
```

This content lives inside Radix's `SelectPrimitive.ItemText` (see `ui/select.tsx:102`). Radix's `SelectValue` in the trigger **mirrors the full `ItemText` content** of the selected item — including the `<Check>` icon. So the checkmark shows up in both places:

1. **Open dropdown** — the selected agent row renders `AgentSelectMenuItem` with `selected=true` → checkmark ✅
2. **Trigger** (closed select) — `SelectValue` echoes the same `ItemText` content → same checkmark ✅

Result: two visible checkmarks for the same selected agent.

## Affected surfaces

- `NewTaskDialog` → `RequiredAgentField` (default "stacked" variant, using Radix Select)
- Also applies to the Create Project agent sheet which uses the same `RequiredAgentField`

The `"settings-row"` variant (`SettingsOptionMenu`) is **not** affected — it uses a `DropdownMenu` with a custom `renderTrigger` that does not include the check.

## Suggested fix

Do not include the selection check inside `ItemText`. Two approaches:

**Option A (recommended):** Move the check to a Radix `Select.ItemIndicator` slot, which renders only inside the dropdown and is never echoed to the trigger:

```tsx
// select.tsx SelectItem — add an indicator slot
<SelectPrimitive.Item ...>
    <SelectPrimitive.ItemText>{children}</SelectPrimitive.ItemText>
    <SelectPrimitive.ItemIndicator className="absolute right-2">
        {/* rendered only in the dropdown, never in the trigger */}
    </SelectPrimitive.ItemIndicator>
</SelectPrimitive.Item>
```

Then remove the conditional `<Check>` from `AgentSelectMenuItem` and handle selection display via the indicator instead.

**Option B (minimal):** Give `SelectValue` an explicit children render in `RequiredAgentField` that shows avatar + label only (no check), so the trigger stops echoing the check from `ItemText`.

## Severity

**P2** — cosmetic UI issue, no functional impact. Affects every user who opens the New Task modal.

title: Terminal font-size label (12px) visually merges with agent CLI border due to transparent background
body:
## Bug The terminal font-size indicator (`12px`) in the top-right control cluster visually overlaps/merges with the agent CLI's bordered welcome box (e.g. Claude Code's border), making it look like a stray measurement annotation. ## What happens The display controls — `[-] [12px] [+] [⛶]` — float over the terminal's top-right corner with `bg-transparent` and no backing surface (by design, "so they read as part of the terminal itself"). When the agent CLI (Claude Code, etc.) draws its bordered welcome box, the box's **top-right border corner** lands exactly where the `12px` label sits. Since the label has no background, it renders directly on top of the CLI's border line. ## Visual The `12px` text and border line overlap with no separation, making it look like a CSS measurement guide that leaked into the live UI. ## Root cause `frontend/src/renderer/components/CenterPane.tsx` (lines 217–257): ```tsx {/* Display controls float over the terminal's top-right corner with no chrome of their own, so they read as part of the terminal itself. */}
{fontSize}px ← renders "12px" (TERMINAL_FONT_SIZE_DEFAULT = 12)
``` The entire cluster is transparent — when a TUI (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) draws a border at that position, there's nothing to separate the label from the border underneath. ## Fix direction Give the control cluster a subtle backing surface so it sits *above* terminal content instead of blending into it: ```tsx
``` This preserves the "floating over the terminal" intent without overlapping agent TUI borders.

title: docs(frontend): document terminal controls placement, closes #3552
body:
## Summary

Closes #3552

The font-size / fullscreen control cluster (`[-] 12px [+] [⛶]`) was reported in #3552 as visually overlapping with agent TUI box-drawing borders (e.g. Claude Code's bordered UI), giving the appearance of a CSS measurement artifact leaking into the live UI.

## Root cause (already fixed)

The controls were previously floating as an `absolute`-positioned overlay over the terminal surface with no background of their own, causing them to bleed into the terminal content:

```tsx
// OLD — removed by #3480
<div className="absolute right-3 top-2 z-10 flex shrink-0 items-center gap-3 font-mono text-passive/70">
  {/* no background → merged with TUI borders */}
```

## Fix

PR #3480 moved the controls into the session tab bar (`session-topbar-surface`), which provides an opaque `background-color: var(--color-bg-primary)` surface. The controls now sit clearly separated from terminal output, with no floating overlay.

This PR adds an inline comment in `CenterPane.tsx` documenting this intentional design decision so future contributors understand why the controls are not floated.

## Testing

Open a session with Claude Code or any TUI-based agent (Grok, opencode, kilocode). The `[-] 12px [+] [⛶]` controls appear cleanly in the tab bar — they do not overlap the TUI border.

## Related

- Resolves #3552
- Fixed structurally by #3480

title: App must invoke its own bundled ao binary, never whatever is first on PATH
body:
The desktop app (and the sessions it spawns) should always use the bundled binary at `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`, never resolve `ao` from PATH. If another `ao` CLI is installed (e.g. the legacy npm/Homebrew one), the app must still use its own bundled binary.

Real failure this causes: a stale `/opt/homebrew/bin/ao` (npm build from Jun 29, predating the `--name` flag) shadowed the bundled binary in shells that don't prepend the daemon dir, so `ao spawn` appeared to have lost the (required) `--name` flag. Cost a full RCA to discover it was PATH shadowing, not a regression.

Ask:
- Everywhere the app or daemon shells out to `ao` (worker session env, orchestrator sessions, hooks, tmux launch commands), use the absolute bundled path (or prepend the daemon dir to PATH for spawned sessions so `ao` resolves to the bundled binary first).
- Consider `ao doctor` warning when a different `ao` earlier on PATH shadows the bundled one (doctor already prints the resolved path; make the mismatch an explicit WARN).

title: fix(daemon): preserve bundled ao PATH precedence during launches
body:
Partially addresses #3562. The issue remains open for canonical AO-owned callbacks, post-startup shell behavior, and legacy-launcher/update reconciliation.

A stale `ao` installed beside an agent CLI can shadow the bundled daemon binary after launch-time PATH augmentation. Keep the daemon directory first for worker, orchestrator, reviewer, shell-terminal, and Codex Chat launches. Reviewer shim fallback retains the same ordering. Interactive shell startup files can still reorder PATH after launch.

`ao doctor` compares the PATH binary with the running daemon's `/healthz` executable identity, falling back to its own executable when no daemon identity is available. `ao status --json` exposes that identity as `executablePath`.

Updated against upstream main at a merge commit without rewriting the existing PR branch. The shared `agentlaunch` implementation preserves current agent and Node runtime discovery. Codex Chat also retains the pin when it augments the environment a second time. Windows Chat environment merging normalizes case before applying overlays so an inherited `Path` cannot replace the pinned `PATH`; a real `cmd.exe`/`ao.exe` identity test runs in Windows CI.

Validation for head `6b4fd8167f794689c1be0519804ed4101c36077f`:
- Session and reviewer shadowing tests fail with pin restoration removed, and pass with the fix.
- Focused session, reviewer, shell-terminal, doctor, Node runtime, and Codex Chat subprocess regressions pass.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.
- `npm run api` produces no generated artifact drift.
- Native CLI E2E passed locally with inherited AO variables stripped.
- Complete Chat environment and Codex driver packages pass locally with the race detector. The real Windows subprocess identity regression passes in Windows CI.
- All 11 exact-head CI checks pass, including full Go build/vet/race tests, lint, API drift, three-platform CLI E2E, fresh-install container, Windows environment coverage, frontend tests, renderer smoke, and secret scanning.
- Local full race execution hit installer cancellation timing (three isolated retries passed), a Chat timing failure, and 15-minute Chat/SQLite timeouts on this shared host. The clean-runner full race job passes.
- Pinned golangci-lint passes in exact-head CI. Local isolated-cache lint printed zero issues but exceeded its timeout; it is not counted as a final local pass.

Scope: this PR fixes launch-time ordering and daemon-aware diagnostics. It does not override user shell startup files or repair external AO installations.

No replacement PR. Merge requires a clean exact head, green CI, and the repository's required review.

title: feat: one-time interactive tmux auto-install at startup (like pre-rewrite ensureTmux)
body:
## Feature

Implement one-time interactive tmux auto-install in the Go rewrite, mirroring the pre-rewrite TypeScript `ensureTmux()` behavior. When tmux is missing at startup, prompt the user and install it automatically — instead of failing with a bare error at spawn time.

**Source:** Bug triage thread (Praveenkumar K report → team discussion)
**Decision (per @Dhruv Sharma):**
- ❌ **Do NOT bundle/package tmux** with AO — causes version conflicts if user already has tmux, and creates a patching/maintenance burden.
- ✅ **DO implement one-time interactive auto-install** via CLI at startup, like the pre-rewrite TS code did.

Related: [#3434](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3434) (error message improvement — already addressed by [PR #3435](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3435))

## What the old TypeScript code did

The pre-rewrite `ao start` had an `ensureTmux()` function (`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`, ~L1070 in the old codebase) that:

1. Checked if tmux was on PATH (`execSilent("tmux", ["-V"])`)
2. If missing, printed a warning and prompted interactively: `⚠ tmux is required for runtime "tmux". Install tmux now? (Y/n)`
3. If user said yes, ran `tryInstallWithAttempts()` with platform-specific commands:
   - **macOS:** `brew install tmux`
   - **Linux:** `sudo apt-get install -y tmux` → fallback `sudo dnf install -y tmux`
4. Verified the install succeeded by re-checking `tmux -V`
5. If install failed or user declined, printed manual install hints and exited

This covered ALL `ao start` paths (normal, URL start, retry with existing config).

In non-interactive mode, it skipped the prompt and showed the manual instructions only (`start.test.ts` L870: "does not auto-install tmux when missing in non-interactive mode").

## Suggested Implementation (Go rewrite)

**Where:** The daemon startup path or `ao start` CLI command.

**What to build:**
1. A `ensureTmux()` equivalent in the Go CLI (`backend/internal/cli/`) or daemon startup (`backend/internal/daemon/`) that:
   - Runs `exec.LookPath("tmux")` (reuse the existing check in `validateRuntimePrerequisites` at `manager.go:3314`)
   - If missing and interactive: prompt user, run platform-specific install command
   - If missing and non-interactive: show install hints, exit with clear error
2. Platform install commands (same as old TS):
   - **macOS:** `brew install tmux`
   - **Linux:** `sudo apt-get install -y tmux` (fallback: `sudo dnf install -y tmux`)
3. Call this at daemon/startup time — NOT at spawn time — so the user fixes the dependency before configuring a project.

**Key consideration — daemon vs CLI process split:** In the Go rewrite, the daemon is a separate long-lived process. The interactive prompt needs to happen in a context where stdin is available (CLI `ao start`, or the Electron app's onboarding flow), not inside the daemon itself.

## Related

- [#3434](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3434) — original report: tmux prerequisite error gives no install guidance
- [PR #3435](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3435) — Layer 1 fix: actionable error message with install hint (complementary, not a replacement for this)

title: feat: make a missing tmux visible and fixable, in the app and the CLI
body:
Closes #3564. Related: #3434, #3435.

## Problem

A new macOS/Linux user without tmux only finds out at spawn time, via
`RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING: tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH`.
That check runs inside the daemon, which lives inside the desktop app, so it
fires in the one place with no way to tell the user anything and no terminal to
fix it from.

## The desktop app

A non-blocking banner on the board, styled as the project-health banner directly
beneath it:

- **macOS:** an **Install tmux** button that runs `brew install tmux` through the
  daemon, then re-checks PATH. Homebrew needs no password, so it is safe to run
  headless.
- **Linux:** the exact `sudo apt-get install -y tmux` line to copy. The app has
  no terminal to answer a password prompt on, so it does not offer a button it
  cannot honour.
- **Both:** a **Check again** button, so a manual install clears the banner
  without restarting the app.
- An unreachable daemon renders nothing. Not knowing is not the same as knowing
  tmux is absent.

### Why not run the install in an AO terminal pane

That was the first idea and it does not work. `daemon.go:220` wires standalone
shell terminals through the same runtime adapter as session panes, which is
tmux. No tmux means no shell terminal either, so the install cannot be hosted in
one. Hence the split above.

`pkexec` would give Linux a polkit password dialog and close that gap. Left out
deliberately: a second privilege-escalation path deserves its own change, tested
by someone who runs Linux daily.

## The CLI

`ao start` settles the same prerequisite before launching the app, which is what
#3564 asked for and mirrors the pre-rewrite `ensureTmux()`. On an interactive
terminal it prompts and installs (brew, apt-get, dnf, pacman, zypper, apk, first
match on PATH, sudo only where root is needed and reachable). Anything else gets
one warning naming the exact command.

**One deliberate deviation from the issue:** it asks for "show install hints,
exit with clear error". This warns and continues. The old `ensureTmux()` could
exit because `ao start` *was* the daemon; it is now only the app launcher, and
the app is usable without a session runtime. The CLI smoke container proved the
point: it runs `ao start` on a fresh box and asserts the failure is a download
error, and a hard tmux exit broke that check.

Not bundling tmux, per the triage thread: it would conflict with an existing
install and add a version-patching burden.

## Shape

- `internal/prereq` holds the package-manager table, so the CLI and the daemon
  cannot drift on what installs tmux. `Status.NeedsRoot` decides who may run it.
- `GET /api/v1/prerequisites`, `POST /api/v1/prerequisites/tmux/install`. The
  install endpoint refuses anything flagged `NeedsRoot` with
  `PREREQUISITE_NOT_INSTALLABLE`, so the rule holds however the request arrives,
  not just because the UI hides a button.
- A package manager can exit 0 and leave nothing runnable, so success is the PATH
  re-check, not the exit code (`PREREQUISITE_INSTALL_INCOMPLETE`).
- New `Deps.RunInteractive` in the CLI runs the install attached to the real
  terminal so `sudo` can prompt; its stdout goes to stderr so `ao start --json`
  stays a clean JSON document.
- `stdinIsInteractive` excluded `/dev/null`, which is a character device and so
  passed the old "is a terminal" test. `docker run` without `-i` hands a process
  exactly that, which made the confirmation prompt answer itself with its default
  and run an install nobody asked for. This also makes `ao import`'s confirmation
  honest in the same situation. A real tty check needs an ioctl
  (`golang.org/x/term`), which pulled an `x/sys` bump into `go.mod` for one
  boolean; `/dev/null` is the only non-tty character device that turns up as
  stdin in practice.
- `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` regenerated via `npm run api`. Copy added to all
  8 locales.

Complementary to #3435 (better error text at spawn time), which stays the
backstop for anyone who dismisses or ignores the banner.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`; `golangci-lint run` over `internal/{prereq,httpd,daemon,cli}`: 0 issues.
- `go test ./internal/prereq/ ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/cli/`: pass.
- `npx vitest run`: 109/110 test files pass. The one failure,
  `src/landing/scripts/generate-markdown-twins.test.mjs`, is a missing local
  `cheerio` install, untouched here.
- Two pre-existing backend failures
  (`TestWorkspaceFilesIncludeWorkspaceProjectChildRepoDiffs`, and six
  `TestSpawn*`/`TestBrowser*` cases that talk to a live local daemon) reproduce
  identically on `upstream/main` in a clean worktree at the base commit.

Tests added: `prereq` (platform/ordering/root rules), `PrerequisitesController`
(status per platform, install, refusal to run what it cannot, failure and
exit-0-without-tmux), `cli/tmux` (no-ops, warn-without-install per unreachable
case, the `/dev/null` regression, prompt-and-install, decline, failed install,
sudo rules), `PrerequisiteBanner` (present, unreachable daemon, install, copy,
failure, re-check).

**Not done:** I have not seen the banner render in the real app. It only appears
when the daemon reports tmux missing, and this machine has tmux. Worth a look on
a fresh box before merge.

title: fix(storage): heal incomplete chat schema so packaged daemon can start

title: feat(agentstream): ABF-style sequenced agent stream over SSE
body:
## Summary

Ports the **AllBeingsFuture ACP streaming output contract** into the AO daemon as a provider-neutral wire, without a full chat-stack port.

- **Canonical stream events** matching ABF `AgentStreamEvent` (`text_delta`, `thinking_update`, `tool_call`, `tool_update`, `plan`, `status`, `permission_request`, `done`, `error`, `cancelled`)
- **Normalizer** (`BridgeEvent` → sequenced events), modeled on ABF `agent-stream-normalizer` tests
- **ACP v1 mapper** for `session/update` chunks → bridge events (SDK-free; ready for `acp-go-sdk` producers)
- **Hub** with monotonic per-session sequence + short replay buffer
- **SSE path:** `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/agent-stream?after=<seq>`
  - event name: `agent_stream`
  - `id:` = sequence
  - `data:` = `AgentStreamEventResponse` JSON
- Daemon wires `agentstream.NewHub()` into `APIDeps.AgentStream`
- OpenAPI + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated

Intentionally **out of scope** (for follow-up workers): full fenzhi chat/service storage, multi-provider chat drivers, permission-respond HTTP, durable conversation projection.

## Frontend contract

1. Subscribe: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/agent-stream` (or `?after=-1` for full buffer; reconnect with `after=<lastSequence>` / `Last-Event-ID`)
2. Reduce only `AgentStreamEventResponse` types; never import ACP SDK
3. Terminal types (`done` / `error` / `cancelled`) flush the turn
4. Producers call hub `PublishBridge` / `PublishACPSessionUpdate` when ACP drivers land

## Tests

```bash
cd backend && go test ./internal/agentstream/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/ ./internal/httpd/...
```

All green locally.

title: Report a Problem dialog: primary action button text invisible (white-on-white) + footer buttons right-aligned instead of centered
body:
## Bug

**Reported by:** @aditi (Discord #bug-triage)

The "Report a problem" dialog has two visual issues:

### 1. Primary action button text is invisible (white-on-white)

The primary action button (e.g. "Copy & Create GitHub Issue") uses hardcoded `text-white` instead of the design-system foreground token. In dark mode this produces white text on a nearly-white background — making the button text unreadable, and when disabled (`opacity-50`) the entire button becomes an indistinguishable gray blob.

**Root cause:** `ReportProblemDialog.tsx` line 246 uses inline Tailwind classes:
```tsx
className="settings-footer-button border-transparent bg-settings-accent text-white transition-opacity hover:opacity-90 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50"
```

It should use the existing `settings-footer-button-primary` utility class (`styles.css` line 664), which correctly uses `--color-settings-footer-button-primary-fg` → `--primary-foreground` (= `oklch(0.21)` dark in dark mode, giving proper contrast).

**Token chain (dark mode):**
- `bg-settings-accent` → `--primary` → `oklch(0.92 0.004 286.32)` (nearly white)
- `text-white` → `#ffffff` → white text on white background = **invisible**
- Correct: `--primary-foreground` → `oklch(0.21 0.006 285.885)` (nearly black) — already wired in `settings-footer-button-primary`

**Fix:** Replace the inline classes on the primary button (line 244-254) with `settings-footer-button settings-footer-button-primary`.

### 2. Footer buttons right-aligned, user expects centered

The footer uses `justify-end` (`dialog.tsx` line 125):
```
flex shrink-0 flex-wrap items-center justify-end gap-3 border-t ...
```

User expects buttons to be center-aligned (`justify-center`).

**Fix:** Consider changing `settingsDialogFooterClass` to `justify-center` — but verify other dialogs using this class (ConfirmDialog) aren't negatively impacted. Alternatively, this could be a per-dialog override.

## Repro
1. Open Settings → Report a problem
2. Observe the "Copy & Create GitHub Issue" button — text is invisible
3. Fill in title + details → button becomes enabled but text still invisible
4. Buttons are bunched to the right edge, not centered

## Files
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/ReportProblemDialog.tsx` (button classes, line 244-254)
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/dialog.tsx` (footer class, line 124-125)
- `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css` (`settings-footer-button-primary` utility, line 664-680)

title: bug(goose): GetRestoreCommand omits -t/-i/--recipe, restore silently no-ops on Goose 1.45+
body:
## Summary

`goose.Plugin.GetRestoreCommand` builds a restore invocation that omits any of `-i`/`--instructions`, `-t`/`--text`, or `--recipe`, which `goose run` requires unconditionally as of Goose 1.45.0. Every Goose-harness session that survives a daemon/app restart is silently reduced to a zombie: AO's `pty-host` wrapper stays alive and the session is reported as `idle`/restored, but the actual `goose` child process exits immediately with a usage error and no agent is running.

## Where

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/goose/goose.go`, `GetRestoreCommand` (currently ~line 138-169 on `main`):

```go
cmd = append(gooseModeEnvPrefix(cfg.Permissions), binary, "run")
systemPrompt, err := restoreSystemPromptText(cfg)
...
if systemPrompt != "" {
    cmd = append(cmd, "--system", systemPrompt)
}
appendModelFlag(&cmd, cfg.Config)
cmd = append(cmd, "--resume", "--session-id", agentSessionID)
```

This produces:

```
goose run --system "<prompt>" --resume --session-id <agentSessionId>
```

Running that directly against Goose 1.45.0 fails immediately:

```
Must provide either --instructions (-i), --text (-t), or --recipe. Use -i - for stdin.
```

For contrast, `GetLaunchCommand` (the fresh-spawn path) already handles this correctly by appending `-t "" --interactive`, with a doc comment that states the requirement explicitly:

> Goose requires one of --instructions, --text, or --recipe, so AO supplies empty text plus --interactive to land in an input-ready terminal without inventing an initial task.

`GetRestoreCommand` was never given the same treatment.

## History / why this wasn't caught

- `GetRestoreCommand` has never included `-t`/`--interactive` since it was introduced.
- PR #2857 ("fix: restore Goose sessions by native session id") added `--system` to the restore command and explicitly chose *not* to add `-t`, to avoid replaying the original task on resume — a reasonable goal, but it didn't account for Goose's own flag requirement.
- PR #2956 (model-flag forwarding) is the most recent change to this function and didn't touch this either.
- This almost certainly worked on older Goose releases (we were on 1.23.2/1.27.2 before hitting a separate stream-inactivity hang bug fixed by upgrading to 1.45.0 — see the fix in `a345bd22`'s cycle). Something in Goose's own CLI validation tightened between those versions so that `--resume` no longer exempts the invocation from the `-i`/`-t`/`--recipe` requirement. So this is a latent AO bug that a Goose upgrade turned into an active, fleet-wide outage on every restart.

## Repro

1. Spawn any Goose worker/orchestrator session and let it produce at least one `SessionStart` hook (so `agentSessionId` metadata is populated).
2. Restart the AO daemon (or reboot the host).
3. Observe: the session is reported as restored/idle in `ao session get`/the dashboard, but no `goose` process is actually running. Running the exact argv AO used (visible via the OS process command line for the `pty-host` wrapper) reproduces the CLI usage error directly.

## Suggested fix

Append `-t ""` (or `--interactive`, matching whatever the intended non-replaying resume behavior should look like) to `GetRestoreCommand`'s argv alongside `--resume --session-id`, the same way `GetLaunchCommand` does — without reintroducing task replay. Add a regression test asserting the restore command always contains one of `-i`/`-t`/`--recipe` so a future Goose CLI tightening can't silently reintroduce this.

## Impact

Every Goose session (worker or orchestrator) that's alive at the time of an AO daemon restart or app relaunch is silently killed with no error surfaced anywhere in the AO UI/CLI — `ao session get`/`ao session restore` both report success. Discovered because a fleet of in-progress worker sessions all went dark simultaneously after a host reboot.

title: Support Greptile CLI reviews with accurate readiness and output-only UX
body:
resolves #2353 

## What

Adds Greptile CLI as a first-class, reviewer-only integration in AO.

Users can now:

- Select **Greptile CLI** from project settings or the review panel.
- See whether the CLI needs installation or authentication.
- Trigger a one-shot review using `greptile review --json`.
- View readable review progress and findings in an output-only terminal.
- See Greptile's findings in AO and as inline GitHub review comments.
- Receive `changes_requested` feedback through the existing worker review loop.
- Review multiple PRs in one trigger while preserving per-PR run history.
- Recover in-progress Greptile reviews after an AO daemon restart.

The review panel now clearly labels Greptile as **Non-interactive · one-shot** and uses **View output** instead of implying that the terminal accepts commands.

## Why

Greptile is a non-interactive CLI, unlike prompt-driven reviewer agents. Previously, treating it like an interactive reviewer could:

- Make users think they were interacting with another agent.
- Leave an interactive shell behind after the CLI exited.
- Allow confusing terminal input to be sent to a process that cannot use it.
- Report incorrect installation status when the daemon could not see the user's CLI installation.
- Show `Auth unknown` even when the user was authenticated.
- Fail without an actionable install or login message.
- Lose visibility or completion state across daemon restarts.
- Return structured findings without publishing them as inline GitHub comments.

## How

### Greptile adapter and review pipeline

- Adds Greptile to the separate reviewer harness vocabulary and registry.
- Keeps Greptile reviewer-only; it cannot be selected as a worker or orchestrator agent.
- Runs `greptile review --json` once per queued PR, passing the target branch and correct worktree.
- Parses summaries, confidence, security information, findings, locations, severities, and suggestions.
- Normalizes Greptile output into AO review verdicts and inline comments.
- Supports batched review results and existing AO review-run history, retry, cancellation, and worker feedback behavior.

### Installation and authentication readiness

- Adds reviewer-specific binary resolution with support for PATH, npm-managed locations, Windows `.cmd`/`.exe` paths, and GUI daemon environments.
- Uses the same resolved binary for catalog checks and actual launches.
- Adds a bounded, non-interactive `greptile whoami` probe.
- Recognizes explicit signed-in and signed-out responses.
- Falls back to `GREPTILE_API_KEY` and `~/.greptile/auth.json` when the CLI probe cannot complete.
- Treats network or deployment failures as unknown rather than incorrectly reporting the user as unauthenticated.
- Adds reviewer inventory data through `reviewerInstalled` and exposes typed API errors:
  - `REVIEWER_BINARY_NOT_FOUND`
  - `REVIEWER_NOT_AUTHENTICATED`
- Missing installations and unauthenticated runs now provide actionable `greptile login` guidance.

### Output-only terminal behavior

- Adds a durable AO-owned Greptile terminal runner.
- Keeps output scrollable, selectable, and copyable.
- Blocks keyboard, paste, composition, drag/drop, and mouse input from reaching Greptile.
- Does not open a follow-up shell after the CLI exits.
- Applies the output-only behavior consistently to tmux and Windows ConPTY.
- Uses stronger process-liveness checks so retained terminal panes are not mistaken for running CLI processes.
- Preserves the existing interactive behavior for all other agents and reviewers.

### Durability and safety

- Stores versioned request and result sidecars with incremental result updates.
- Recovers active or completed Greptile reviews after daemon restart.
- Fences stale requests and validates worker, batch, task, and result-path ownership.
- Uses restricted file permissions, symlink checks, bounded output, and credential redaction.
- Cleans consumed request/result pairs after the retention period while preserving incomplete work for recovery.
- Cancelling AO stops the local Greptile process; a remote Greptile run that already started may continue remotely.

### GitHub and API/UI integration

- Adds a GitHub review publisher using `gh api` to post inline findings.
- Records the GitHub review ID when publishing succeeds.
- Keeps the AO result recorded and includes a visible warning if GitHub publishing is unavailable.
- Extends review submit/list responses for batched one-shot results and historical runs.
- Updates the reviewer picker, review panel, terminal attachment flow, generated schema, translations, and CLI documentation.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/greptile ./internal/service/agent ./internal/review ./internal/service/review ./internal/httpd/controllers`
- `go vet ./internal/adapters/reviewer/greptile ./internal/service/agent ./internal/review ./internal/service/review ./internal/httpd/controllers`
- Frontend reviewer/session tests: 79 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck`

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` / continued the existing feature branch
- [x] Focused Greptile reviewer integration
- [x] Tests added or updated for backend and frontend behavior
- [x] Focused Go and frontend validation passes

## Summary

- remove padding from the shared topbar surface so connected tabs no longer float above the terminal divider

title: ao session cleanup удаляет worktree активной (нетерминированной) оркестраторской сессии, из которой запущен
body:
## Что произошло

`ao session cleanup` удалил worktree **активной, нетерминированной** оркестраторской сессии, из которой сам же и был запущен.

Команда обещает: «Clean up **terminated** sessions by reclaiming eligible workspaces». Фактически под удаление попал workspace сессии со `status: working`, `terminated: false`.

## Воспроизведение

Из оркестраторской сессии `<project>-114` (роль `orchestrator`, проект `<project>`, worktree `/Users/<user>/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>/orchestrator/<project>-orchestrator`):

```bash
ao session cleanup --project <project> --dry-run   # 178 сессий в списке
ao session cleanup --project <project> --yes       # "Cleanup complete. 178 sessions cleaned."
```

Сразу после этого следующая же bash-команда в той же сессии упала:

```
Working directory "/Users/<user>/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>/orchestrator/<project>-orchestrator"
was deleted; shell cwd recovered to "/Users/<user>"
```

Каталог `orchestrator/` остался пустым:

```
$ ls -la /Users/<user>/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>/orchestrator/
total 0
drwxr-xr-x@ 2 <user> staff 64 Aug 5 10:08 .
drwxr-xr-x@ 6 <user> staff 192 Aug 5 10:08 ..
```

При этом сама сессия по данным демона жива и работает:

```
$ ao session get <project>-114 --project <project>
id: <project>-114
role: orchestrator
status: working
activity: active
terminated: false
created: 2026-07-24T07:16:54Z
updated: 2026-08-05T02:09:09Z
```

## Ожидаемое поведение

`ao session cleanup` не должен удалять workspace сессии, у которой `terminated: false` — тем более сессии, из которой он выполняется. Как минимум:

1. Исключать из выборки все сессии с `terminated: false` независимо от роли.
2. Всегда исключать **текущую** сессию (ту, чей workspace содержит cwd вызывающего процесса) — защита от самоудаления.
3. В `--dry-run` показывать роль сессии (`worker`/`orchestrator`) и признак «current», чтобы такой случай было видно до подтверждения.

## Что сработало правильно

Worktree'ы двух активных воркеров (`<project>-177`, `<project>-182`) очистка **не** тронула — они уцелели и продолжили работу. То есть защита активных сессий существует, но на оркестраторские сессии (или на «текущую» сессию) не распространяется.

## Наблюдение про dry-run

`--dry-run` перечислил 178 сессий, но в списке `<project>-114` **не фигурировал** — при этом его workspace был удалён. Возможно, удаление оркестраторского workspace идёт не по списку сессий, а как «зачистка пустого/родительского каталога» проекта. Стоит проверить эту ветку кода отдельно: dry-run не предсказал фактический эффект, а это отдельная проблема доверия к превью.

## Влияние

- Оркестратор теряет рабочий каталог посреди сессии; последующие команды падают, cwd откатывается в `$HOME`.
- Незакоммиченные изменения в оркестраторском worktree были бы потеряны безвозвратно. В моём случае всё было смёржено заранее, поэтому потерь нет — но это везение, а не гарантия.
- Особенно неприятно тем, что `cleanup` — рутинная операция обслуживания, её запускают без опаски.

## Окружение

- `ao version`: `dev`
- macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon
- Проект `<project>` (`single_repo`), 178 терминированных сессий накопилось к моменту очистки
- Активны на момент запуска: `<project>-114` (orchestrator, current), `<project>-177`, `<project>-182` (workers)

## Возможный фикс

В выборке `cleanup` фильтровать по `terminated == true` и дополнительно исключать сессию, чей workspace является префиксом `os.Getwd()` вызывающего процесса. Плюс покрыть тестом сценарий «cleanup, запущенный изнутри оркестраторского worktree, не удаляет собственный workspace».

title: fix(sqlite): ledger 0043 and repair is_pinned on burned migration histories
body:
## Why

`main` is red on Go / build-test at 3d782c2 ([run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/30976687994)):

```
--- FAIL: TestMigrationVersionLedger
    migration "0043_add_session_pinned.sql" (version 43) is not in the shippedMigrations ledger
--- FAIL: TestSessionListSucceedsOnBurnedMigrationHistory
    insert session mer-1: SQL logic error: table sessions has no column named is_pinned (1)
```

Two PRs, each green on its own base, neither re-run against the other:

- #3511 (merged 2026-08-04 22:09Z) added `0043_add_session_pinned.sql`.
- #3491 (merged 2026-08-05 04:58Z) added the append-only ledger and `schemaRepairs`, both stopping at 42 because the branch predates #3511.

The second failure is not ledger bookkeeping, it is the defect the guard exists to catch. The #3475/#3476 field profiles have `goose_db_version` recording versions 40 through 51 from a foreign build, so goose skips 0043 there entirely. `gen/sessions.sql.go` selects and writes `is_pinned` and `pinned_at` in create, list, get, and update, so on those installs session pinning ships as an opaque 500 on the session list while `/healthz` stays green.

## What

- Append `43: "0043_add_session_pinned.sql"` to `shippedMigrations`.
- Add `sessions.is_pinned` and `sessions.pinned_at` to `schemaRepairs`, and replay 0043's CDC trigger in `postAdd` so pin changes still broadcast on a repaired database.

The trigger replay hangs off `pinned_at`, the second column, because SQLite resolves a trigger body at `CREATE TRIGGER` time and the body references both columns. Hanging it off `is_pinned` would fail with `no such column: NEW.pinned_at`. `postAdd` runs only when the column was just added, so healthy databases are untouched.

## Verification

```
go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/ -run 'TestMigrationVersionLedger|TestSessionListSucceedsOnBurnedMigrationHistory'   ok
go test ./internal/storage/...                                                                                        ok, 88 tests, 3 packages
gofmt -l internal/storage/sqlite/                                                                                     clean
golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/...                                                                              0 issues
```

## Risks and follow-ups

- No schema change and no new migration, so nothing new to burn.
- The repair path is exercised by `TestSessionListSucceedsOnBurnedMigrationHistory`, which seeds versions 40 to 51 as applied and now creates and lists a session successfully.
- Worth considering separately: nothing forces a PR that touches `migrations/` to be re-tested against current `main` before merge, which is exactly how this landed.

Blocks the nightly. Conductor run [30976937971](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/ao-releases/actions/runs/30976937971) was cancelled at the wait step before any publish, so no release was cut from the broken SHA.

## 0.12.0 (`v0.11.2..v0.12.0`, 80 commits, 26 feat, 44 fix, 22 authors)

- i18next foundation with Simplified Chinese, then ja/ko/es/fr/de/pt-BR plus translated READMEs (#3465, #3541)

## 0.12.1 (`v0.12.0..v0.12.1`, 28 commits, 6 feat, 17 fix)

- Nine color themes with Nord, Gruvbox and Solarized, plus the theme-style wiring that had been declared but never applied (#3585, #3620, #3587)
- Adapter-aware model selection with a discovered, cached per-agent catalog (#3386)
- New tasks can be delegated through the project orchestrator (#3443)
- Merge a ready PR from the inspector, with merge blockers explained (#3599, #3589)
- Browser annotation rebuilt, shift to multi-select, and the CSP-blocked font fixed (#3549)
- Sidebar animations, project context menu, reduced-motion respected (#3490)
- The macOS file descriptor leak that prompted the release: the live Files view leaked descriptors and never released them, so the Files view went blank and task creation 500'd after a few hours (fsnotify v1.9.0 kqueue, [postmortem](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/discussions/3646)) (#3624)
- Terminal viewport retained across navigation (#3371), wrong tab content after switching (#3579), authenticated Kimi detection (#3603), the missing 0044 shipped-migrations entry (#3611)

### Why only 0.12.0 and 0.12.1 get curated MDX

`src/lib/changelog.ts` pulls every stable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` release from GitHub at build time and renders its release body, with curated MDX winning for the same version. 0.12.2 through 0.12.6 already list that way, so they need no file here. Only 0.12.0 and 0.12.1 were missing usable bodies.

## Version stamp

`frontend/package.json` has been stuck at `0.10.3` since #2637, through v0.11.0, v0.11.1, v0.11.2 and all of the 0.12.x line. It is now `0.12.6`, which is the current latest release (published 2026-08-16).

This matters beyond cosmetics: `frontend-release.yml` derives the release tag it publishes to from this field rather than from the git tag (`tag="v$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"`), so a `workflow_dispatch` run against the repo as it stands would target `v0.10.3`. The real release path sets the version itself, so shipped assets are named correctly; this brings the checked-in value back in line with them.

The lockfile's root `version` is updated alongside so the two stay in sync. #2637 changed `package.json` alone and let them drift.

## Dates

Both entries carry the release publish timestamp from the GitHub API rather than a bare date (`2026-08-05T06:52:44Z` and `2026-08-05T18:28:27Z`). Both shipped the same day, and the list sorts on that value, so a bare date would have rendered 0.12.1 below 0.12.0.

## Verification

Entry contents were cross-checked against the real ranges rather than taken on trust. Every PR number cited in the 0.12.1 entry (28 of 28) appears in `git log v0.12.0..v0.12.1`; in the 0.12.0 entry, 66 of the 67 numbers appear in `git log v0.11.2..v0.12.0`, and the one that does not, #3475, is cited as the tracking issue for the board-wipe outage, not as a PR.

`npm ci && npm run build` in `frontend/src/landing` passes on the rebased branch, with `NODE_ENV` unset:

```
✓ Generating static pages using 7 workers (89/89) in 3.7s
> node scripts/generate-markdown-twins.mjs
Generated 46 documentation Markdown twins
```

The static export prerenders `agent-orchestrator-0-12-0.html` and `agent-orchestrator-0-12-1.html`, and there is no `v0-12-0.html` or `v0-12-1.html` alongside them, so the dedupe against the GitHub Release body holds. On `/changelog` the order is 0.12.6, 0.12.5, 0.12.4, 0.12.3, 0.12.2, 0.12.1, 0.12.0, 0.11.2, so the new entries slot in correctly.

No em dashes or en dashes in either entry, checked against the rendered HTML (0 matches in both files).

## macOS note

Both entries carry the leak note. 0.12.1 spells out the reboot step, since an attached daemon keeps serving the old binary across an app update. The 0.12.0 entry points macOS readers at 0.12.1 or later, since every 0.12.x patch since then carries the fix.

title: bug(scm): completed checks can remain pending until forced refresh
body:
## Bug

A pull request can continue to show **Checks running** in AO for roughly five minutes after every GitHub check has completed. The card corrects itself only when the SCM observer's unconditional-refresh backstop runs.

**Source:** Live AO review session on 2026-08-05 (no public chat URL)  
**Reported by:** Human reviewer in the AO desktop app  
**Analyzed against:** `c970f0d2436d770cf24bda317785ea5a8313d656`  
**AO version:** `dev` (freshly built Go rewrite; verified installed daemon ready on port 3001)  
**Observed surface:** macOS Electron development app using the same rewrite and real AO data on its development port 3002  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P2 — status is materially misleading, but self-corrects through the bounded-staleness fallback.

## Reproduction

1. Open an AO session whose attributed GitHub pull request has multiple check runs.
2. Push a commit so those checks enter the running state.
3. Keep the PR summary card visible in the session inspector.
4. Wait until every GitHub check completes successfully.
5. Observe that AO can continue to display **Checks running**.
6. Wait for the five-minute forced PR refresh; the card changes to **Checks passing** without user action.

Live instance: PR #3590 had all relevant checks complete by `2026-08-05T07:00:44Z`, while AO did not observe `ci.state: passing` until approximately `2026-08-05T07:06:05Z`. The renderer fetched and displayed the corrected daemon response immediately afterward.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go::CommitChecksGuard` requests:

```text
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs?per_page=1
```

and uses that response's ETag as the fast check-state guard. With multiple check runs, the one returned item can remain unchanged while a different workflow finishes. Since the conditional representation has not changed, GitHub can return `304 Not Modified` even though the aggregate CI state AO displays has changed.

`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go::selectRefreshCandidates` then sees both the repository guard and this single-item check guard as unchanged and skips the full GraphQL PR/check refresh. `DefaultPRMaxAge = 5 * time.Minute` eventually forces the full fetch, which explains the observed delay precisely.

The frontend event transport is not the source of the lag: once SQLite changes from `pending` to `passing`, CDC invalidates the session SCM query and the card updates.

## Suggested Fix

Make the fast check guard represent all check runs that contribute to the aggregate CI state, rather than only one item. A fix should:

- request and condition on the complete relevant check-run representation (including pagination or a better aggregate endpoint where necessary);
- preserve conditional-request savings when none of those runs changes;
- add a provider/observer regression test where the first returned run remains stable while another run transitions from running to passing;
- retain `DefaultPRMaxAge` as a safety backstop for PR metadata changes not represented by check-state guards.

## Impact

- Users can spend up to five minutes believing checks are still running.
- Ready-to-merge status and merge actions are delayed even when GitHub is already green.
- The UI appears unreliable because a later refresh changes the state without any new GitHub activity.

## Related

- [#2656](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2656): tracked PR state could remain stale after merge; established the need for bounded refresh.
- [PR #2678](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2678): added the five-minute forced-refresh backstop that eventually heals this report but does not make CI transitions timely.

title: fix: detect authenticated Kimi installs
body: ## Summary - add Kimi self-managed install path (`~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi`) to binary discovery - recognize Kimi OAuth credential files (`~/.kimi-code/credentials/kimi-code.json`) as authorized when they contain an access or refresh token - prefer valid credential tokens over empty `config.toml` `api_key` placeholders - add focused tests for Kimi binary discovery and credential auth classification ## Issue Kimi was already present in the agents dropdown, but authenticated local installs were still shown as `Needs auth`. The frontend was rendering the daemon catalog correctly; the bad state came from the Kimi adapter's readiness probe. The local Kimi install shape can be: - binary at `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` - `config.toml` containing empty `api_key = ""` placeholders - real OAuth auth stored in `~/.kimi-code/credentials/kimi-code.json` The adapter did not search the self-managed binary path, and its first OAuth credential support still stopped too early when it saw empty `api_key` values in `config.toml`, classifying the install as unauthorized before checking the credential JSON. ## Before ## After ## Fix The Kimi adapter now checks `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` during binary resolution. For auth, it treats a non-empty config API key as authorized, then checks `credentials/kimi-code.json` for an access or refresh token, and only falls back to the empty config-key unauthorized result when no credential token exists. With that, the daemon can classify this local Kimi install as installed/authorized, and the existing agents dropdown can show it as available instead of `Needs auth`. ## Tests - `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/kimi ./internal/service/agent` - `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/registry ./internal/httpd/controllers -run 'Test.*Agent|TestEveryHarnessReportsAuthStatus|TestHarnessed'`\n- `git diff --check`\n\n## Risks\nLow. The change is scoped to Kimi catalog readiness probes and does not alter launch or restore command behavior.

## Summary

When a session is working an issue, there is no way to get from the AO GUI to that issue's page on the forge. The issue reference is already known to AO — sessions can be spawned against an issue id, and the id is carried on the session record — but it is displayed as inert text. Getting to the issue means copying the number, finding the right repo, and navigating by hand.

## Why this matters

Reviewing what a session is actually doing almost always means reading the issue: acceptance criteria, prior comments, linked PRs. That is a per-session, many-times-a-day action, and today every one of them is a manual context switch out of the tool. It is also error-prone in a multi-repo setup — the issue number alone does not say which repo it belongs to, so the operator has to remember, and picking the wrong repo silently shows the wrong issue.

The equivalent affordance already exists elsewhere in the product: PR references deep-link to their forge page, and PR notifications deep-link back to sessions (#2726, #2875). Issue references are the gap.

## Proposed behavior

Make the issue reference on a session a link to the issue on its forge.

- clickable wherever the issue id is already displayed — session list, session detail/header, and anywhere a session is shown with its issue
- resolves against the project's configured repository, so the correct repo is used without the operator having to know it
- opens externally, in the same way existing PR links behave
- degrades quietly: if a session has no issue, or the project has no resolvable repository, render as today rather than producing a dead or wrong link

## Notes / edge cases

- Forge-agnostic: the URL shape should come from whatever the project's remote resolves to rather than being hardcoded to one provider, so self-hosted instances are not excluded.
- A session may have been spawned against an issue in a repository other than the project's default. If AO does not currently store enough to disambiguate that, the honest first cut is to link only when the repository is unambiguous, rather than guessing.
- No new state required as far as I can tell — this is presentation over an id AO already has.

## Scope

Frontend, plus whatever small resolver is needed to turn (project, issue id) into a forge URL. Happy to open a PR if this is wanted and nobody is already on it.

title: bug(runtime): sessions inherit the daemon environment unfiltered, silently changing effective endpoint and model
body:
## Summary

Every agent session inherits the daemon's **entire** environment, unfiltered. The only variables the launch path normalizes are `TERM` and `COLORTERM`. As a result, environment variables that change which backend a session talks to, or which model it resolves, silently apply to every session the daemon spawns — with no signal anywhere that the session's effective configuration differs from its stored configuration.

## Where

`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:134`:

```go
cmd.Env = append(append([]string(nil), os.Environ()...), env...)
```

and the only filtering in that path, `attachEnv` (`tmux.go:520`), which rewrites `TERM` and `COLORTERM` and passes everything else through untouched. There is no allowlist, no denylist, and no diagnostic.

## Why this matters

Agent CLIs take significant configuration from the environment — API base URL, per-tier default models, credentials. Whatever is in the shell that started the daemon becomes ambient policy for every session it will ever spawn.

Concretely: if the daemon is started from a shell configured to point at an alternate API-compatible endpoint (base-URL override plus per-tier default-model overrides), then every session silently runs against that endpoint and that model family, while each project's stored config still reads the originally configured model and looks entirely correct. Inspecting the config proves nothing about what is actually running, and nothing in the session list, logs, or UI reports the divergence.

This is easy to reason yourself out of, because such wrappers are often defined as **shell functions** — which the daemon genuinely cannot invoke, since functions are not inherited by non-interactive spawns. That correctly rules out the wrapper, and incorrectly feels like it rules out the wrapper's environment variables, which leak in whenever the daemon inherits them.

## Interaction with #3218

These compose into a silent failure. #3218 is that the restore path builds its resume argv without a `--model` flag at all, so the CLI resolves the model from its own defaults — which include tier-keyed environment variables. Combined with unfiltered inheritance, a restored session resolves to whatever model family the daemon's environment implies, rather than erroring or warning.

Fixing #3218 alone narrows this but does not close it: it makes the model explicit while leaving base-URL and every other behavioural variable ambient.

## Proposed behavior

Some ordering of, roughly in increasing cost:

1. **Surface it.** At launch, log (and ideally show in `ao doctor`) when the daemon's environment carries variables that override the API endpoint or default models. Cheap, non-breaking, and turns a silent divergence into a visible one.
2. **Declare it.** Make the set of environment variables forwarded to sessions explicit — an allowlist, or a project-level declaration of intended passthrough — so that what a session inherits is a decision rather than an accident of how the daemon was started.
3. **Record it.** Persist the effective endpoint/model a session actually launched with, so after the fact there is something to check that is not the config it was *supposed* to use.

(1) alone would have made this discoverable rather than requiring a code read, so it seems like the right first cut even if the larger question is deferred.

## Notes

I have not proposed a blanket allowlist as the immediate fix — narrowing environment inheritance is a real compatibility risk for anyone relying on ambient configuration today, and that call belongs to maintainers. The reportable defect is that the current behaviour is unbounded and unreported, not that inheritance itself is wrong.

title: fix(frontend): strip macOS nested-radius from Windows/Linux center panel
body:
## Problem

On Windows/Linux, the right side of the app shows curved/rounded corner radii while the left side (flush with the sidebar) stays square — reported by @phylsolver in bug-triage.

## Root cause

`center-panel-surface` uses `border-radius: var(--radius-center-panel)` (= **12px**), derived from a **macOS-specific formula**:

```
inner_radius = window_radius (18px) − inset (6px) = 12px
```

This nested-radius curve only makes sense **inside a rounded macOS window**. On Windows/Linux the frameless window is **rectangular**, and the shell has **asymmetric padding**:

| Edge | Padding | Curve visible? |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Left | `0` (flush to sidebar) | hidden |
| Top  | `0` (overridden by #3083) | hidden |
| Right | `16px` | **visible** |
| Bottom | `14px` | **visible** |

So the rounded corners only show on the right/bottom, making the panel look like a floating rounded card while the left stays square.

PR #3083 (*"flush Windows center panel"*) already dropped the **top** inset on Windows but never stripped the **radius**. This finishes that job.

## Fix

Set `border-radius: 0` on `.platform-windows` / `.platform-linux` `center-panel-surface` so the framed panel has sharp corners, consistent with the flush left edge. macOS is untouched — it keeps the nested-radius curve inside its rounded window.

## Testing

- [x] CSS-only change, no logic/TS affected
- [x] macOS path (`center-panel-shell--mac`) untouched — no regression
- [ ] Manual: verify Windows/Linux center panel now has square corners on right/bottom

title: macOS: an old copy of the app silently overwrites the updated one in /Applications, pinning users to their install version
body:
## Summary

On macOS, launching any second copy of the app that lives outside `/Applications` silently deletes the copy in `/Applications` and replaces it with itself. Users who still have their original download around get pinned to the version they first installed, forever.

Reported by nightly users: "Restart & install" jumps to the new version, the next cold start is back on v0.10.3, which is the version they originally installed.

## Repro

1. Download the macOS zip, unzip it in `~/Downloads`, launch the app from there. It relocates itself to `/Applications` and relaunches.
2. Let it update, or click Settings > Restart & install. `/Applications` is now on the new version.
3. Open the app again from the copy still sitting in `~/Downloads`.
4. `/Applications` is back on the old version.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/main.ts:1492-1498` calls `app.moveToApplicationsFolder()` on every packaged launch, with no conflict handler and no version check.

In Electron 33 that call is destructive by default (`shell/browser/ui/cocoa/electron_bundle_mover.mm` @ v33.0.0):

- `:360` returns early only if the running bundle is already in an Applications dir.
- `:404-434` if something already exists at the destination, it trashes it. The guard is `ShouldContinueMove`, which at `:330-352` defaults to `true` when no `conflictHandler` is passed. We pass nothing, so there is no prompt.
- `:436` copies the running (old) bundle in.
- `:448` `if (diskImageDevice == nil && !DeleteOrTrash(bundlePath))`, so a source on a mounted DMG is never deleted, and the delete is best effort everywhere else (it fails on read-only App Translocation mounts, which is what a quarantined unzipped app runs from).
- `:453` relaunches from `/Applications`, after stripping `com.apple.quarantine`, so the downgrade is completely silent.

Squirrel only ever updates the bundle at the running app's path, so the second copy stays frozen at its install version forever.

**Why "Restart & install" works for exactly one run:** `quitAndInstall` patches the bundle at the running app's path, which is `/Applications`, and relaunches it directly, bypassing whatever the user normally clicks. Confirmed in `ShipItState.plist` (`targetBundleURL = file:///Applications/Agent%20Orchestrator.app/`) and in `ShipIt_stderr.log` ("Installation completed successfully"). The next cold start goes through the user's usual entry point, which is the stale copy.

**Why 0.10.3 specifically:** it was latest stable from 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-28, a 16 day window, where the surrounding stables held 1 to 6 days each. Biggest cohort. The clobber has been firing on every cold start since those users installed, but it was invisible while both copies were the same version. Switching to nightly is what made it visible, not what caused it.

Introduced in `514946fd8` (2026-06-26), which `git tag --contains` confirms is in `desktop-v0.10.3`, so the frozen bundles ship the clobber code themselves.

Not the cause, ruled out: the update feed (latest serves 0.12.0, nightly serves 0.11.2-nightly, neither can produce 0.10.3, so `allowDowngrade` in `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts:72` is not it), ShipIt failing to swap (it succeeds), and the daemon (nothing in the backend launches the app except `ao start`).

## Suggested fix

In `frontend/src/main.ts:1492`:

1. Only relocate on the first launch after the `ao start` bootstrap, which is the case the move was added for. Test: `parseInstalledVia(process.argv)` is set, or `~/.ao/app-state.json` does not exist yet.
2. Pass a `conflictHandler` that returns `false` for `exists`, so an old copy can never trash a newer one. On refusal, `open` the `/Applications` copy and quit, mirroring the mover's own `existsAndRunning` behaviour.

Secondary: `ao start` should prefer `/Applications` over the recorded path in the marker (`backend/internal/cli/start.go:120-130`), so the CLI stops propagating the downgrade once it has happened. Today it is marker-first and by design never compares versions.

## Two follow-ups worth shipping alongside

**1. Ship the DMG on the website.** The DMG maker landed in `0bdfbe6b6` (2026-07-29) and gives users the standard drag-to-Applications window, but the download page never switched to it. `frontend/src/landing/packages/shared/src/constants.ts:40-41` and `frontend/src/landing/src/app/download/page.tsx:101-108` still serve `agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.zip` on both channels. Every macOS download today is still a zip that lands in `~/Downloads` and gets launched from there. Pointing those links at the `.dmg` stops making new victims. Note it does not help anyone already affected, and without the fix above it just swaps a stray copy in Downloads for a frozen copy on a re-mountable disk image, which `:448` never deletes.

**2. Tell users when they are running from the wrong place.** A location check at auto-update opt-in will not fire for affected users: the stale copy relocates itself and relaunches from `/Applications`, so by the time Settings is open the running app *is* in `/Applications`, and they turned auto-update on weeks ago anyway.

The version that does work is to detect the downgrade rather than the location. The app already writes its version to `~/.ao/app-state.json` on every launch (`frontend/src/main/app-state.ts:106-119`). On startup, if the marker records a version newer than `app.getVersion()`, the app was just overwritten. Show a dialog naming the situation and offer to locate the other copy. A few lines, no disk scan, and it reaches every user already stuck on the next launch they do.

## Workaround for affected users

1. Quit the app.
2. `mdfind -name 'Agent Orchestrator.app'` and delete every copy except `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app`. The culprit is usually in `~/Downloads`.
3. Remove the old Dock tile and drag a fresh one in from `/Applications`.
4. Launch from `/Applications` and update once more.

Verify with `defaults read '/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Info.plist' CFBundleShortVersionString`.

title: fix(ptyexec): bound Close wait after the SIGKILL fallback
body:
## Summary

`ptyexec.Spawn` opens a local PTY around a terminal attach client (`tmux attach-session` on Unix, ConPTY on Windows). Its `Close()` tears the attach process down as **SIGTERM → SIGKILL → `<-done`**, where `done` closes when `cmd.Wait()` returns.

That final `<-done` is **unbounded**. A process wedged in an uninterruptible kernel state (`D` — e.g. blocked on a dead NFS/FUSE mount in the workspace) survives **SIGKILL**, so `cmd.Wait()` never returns and `Close()` blocks forever. Because `Close()` runs on daemon shutdown and on session teardown (including via the `Spawn` ctx-cancellation goroutine), a single wedged attach terminal hangs the entire daemon shutdown indefinitely. The Windows `conPTYProcess.Close()` has the identical unbounded wait.

This matters in practice because the attach client here is `tmux attach`, which resolves its session in the workspace tree — exactly the kind of path a hung filesystem can wedge.

## Change

- Add a shared `killGrace` (2s) and a `waitForExit(done, grace)` helper that returns on `done` **or** after the grace.
- Unix `creackPTY.Close()` and Windows `conPTYProcess.Close()` now call `waitForExit(...)` after the SIGKILL fallback, then release the PTY master and return. The `cmd.Wait()` goroutine finishes whenever the kernel eventually reaps the process; `Close` stays idempotent via `closeOnce`.
- Add unit tests (`wait_test.go`) covering both the bounded-timeout escape hatch and the fast path when the process has already exited.

SIGTERM-first behavior is preserved: a cooperative attach client still detaches within `detachGrace` (250ms), and a TERM-ignoring process is still killed via SIGKILL — only the post-Kill wait is now bounded.

## Tests

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/... ./internal/terminal/...` — pass
- `go test ./...` — pass except four pre-existing `internal/cli` spawn tests that fail on a clean `main` checkout too (environment/daemon-404, unrelated to this change).

## Known risks / follow-ups

- Worst-case shutdown now adds up to ~2.25s per genuinely-wedged attach terminal instead of hanging forever (intentional tradeoff).

title: fix(scm): condition commit check guard on all check runs, not just one
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3601 — **completed checks can remain pending until forced refresh**.

`CommitChecksGuard` in `backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go` requested the per-commit check-runs endpoint with `per_page=1` and used that single-item response's ETag as the fast check-state guard. When a PR carries multiple check runs, the one returned item can remain unchanged while a **different** workflow finishes, so GitHub answers `304 Not Modified` even though the aggregate CI state AO displays has changed. `selectRefreshCandidates` then skips the full GraphQL PR/check refresh, leaving the card on **Checks running** until the five-minute `DefaultPRMaxAge` backstop.

## Change

- Request the **complete** check-run representation (`per_page=100`, GitHub's cap) so the ETag covers every run that contributes to the aggregate CI state.
- When a commit carries more than one page of runs (`total_count > 100`), fall back to a stable fingerprint over the **full** run set (paginating), so a transition on a later page still invalidates the guard. Conditional-request savings are preserved: when nothing changed, the guard reports `NotModified` and the observer skips the GraphQL refresh.
- `DefaultPRMaxAge` remains as the safety backstop for PR metadata changes not represented by check-state guards.

## Tests

- `TestCommitChecksGuard_OtherRunTransitionInvalidatesGuard` — regression: first returned run stays stable while another run transitions `in_progress -> completed`; guard must report `NotModified=false`. (Verified this test fails against the old `per_page=1` logic.)
- `TestCommitChecksGuard_PaginatedFingerprintInvalidatesLaterPageRun` — a transition on a page-2 run invalidates the paginated fingerprint guard.
- Ran `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/github/... ./internal/observe/scm/...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and golangci-lint v2.12.2 — all clean.

Pre-existing failures in `internal/cli`, `internal/adapters/agent/fake`, and `internal/adapters/agent/kilocode` reproduce on clean upstream `main` and are unrelated to this change.

## Risks / Follow-ups

None known. The guard change only affects when the fast path forces a full refresh; it can only make CI transitions arrive sooner, never later.
