title: Merge the inspector's two review sections into one list
body:
The session inspector showed AO's own reviewer passes and the reviews left on the PR as two separate sections. A single PR therefore appeared twice, once under each heading, and the reader had to join them up by number to see the whole picture of who had said what about a commit.

They are now one list keyed by PR. Each PR is one expandable row; inside, the groups name their source: **AO codex** against whichever agent actually ran that pass, **On GitHub** for humans and bots. `GithubReviewPanel` is gone.

## Run review

The "This commit has already been reviewed. Push a new commit to run another review." notice was a boxed two-line paragraph. It is feedback about a click, but it outlived the click and kept the rail's width for as long as the panel stayed open.

It is now a one-line `Already reviewed` marker. The sentence is the control's accessible name and shows on hover or focus, so nothing is lost for a screen reader or for anyone who wants the detail, and the resting state costs one line instead of a box.

## Removals

- "No unresolved threads." The unresolved count already rides the PR's own meta line, so the separate sentence only ever appeared when there was nothing to report.
- `inspector.reviewsOnPR` and `inspector.noOneReviewedYet` died with the section that used them.

## Two changes nobody asked for

- Four derivations moved to module level (`openReviewStatesFor`, `runsByPRFrom`, `triggeredReviewStatesFrom`, `aoReviewHarness`). The merged list needs exactly the data `ReviewPanel` was computing privately, and a second copy would have been free to drift from the first.
- `ReviewPanel` loses its `runs` prop, which became dead once the AO list moved out of it.

## i18n

Four keys in, three out, across all eight locales, which `i18n/instance.test.ts` enforces at the type level. `inspector.unresolvedCount` replaces a hardcoded English `` `${unresolved} unresolved` `` in the component, so that string is translatable for the first time.

The seven non-English translations are not from a translator. `inspector.reviewBySource.ao` is deliberately left as `AO {{harness}}` everywhere, since it is a product name plus an agent id.

## Conflicts with #3612

Both changes edit the same few lines of `ReviewsSection`: the auto-inject toggle is inserted immediately after the GitHub section this removes. Whichever lands second resolves by hand.

Separately, #3612 carries migration `0048` while main is at `0079`, so it needs a fresh number regardless of order. If this lands first, the natural resolution is to move the toggle into Run review next to the agent picker, which is arguably where a delivery policy belongs anyway and would give it the section heading it currently lacks.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 87/87 in `SessionInspector.test.tsx` and `i18n/instance.test.ts`, after updating two assertions that named the removed section titles
- exercised in the desktop app against seeded review data

title: fix: stop the session Files diff viewer from freezing on large diffs
body:
## Summary

Opening or scrolling a large file's diff in the session Files panel could block the render thread and spawn redundant git subprocesses per request, making the whole app feel unresponsive. This fixes it end to end, backend and frontend.

**Backend (workspace file/diff serving):**
- Parallelize the independent git subprocess calls in `workspaceChangeMaps`/`workspaceFileSummaries` instead of running them sequentially.
- Add a short-TTL cache for resolved compare/status data (`workspace_cache.go`), invalidated by the workspace filesystem watcher's SSE stream on real changes, so expanding a file right after the list loads doesn't redundantly recompute it.
- Coalesce concurrent cache-miss lookups for the same session/root via `singleflight`, so "Expand All" firing many `GetWorkspaceFile` calls at once shares one computation instead of each spawning its own git calls.
- Fix a misclassification where tracked binary Added files were treated as untracked (`git diff --numstat` omits binary files even when tracked, which isn't the same as being untracked), which produced an incorrect synthetic diff instead of the real one.

**Frontend (`SessionFilesView`):**
- Virtualize the diff row list against the shared scroll container (`@tanstack/react-virtual`) so only rows actually scrolled into view mount, with dynamic per-row measurement for correct heights under line-wrapping at any panel width (docked vs. maximized).
- Memoize per-row rendering and thread the i18n `t` function down instead of every row independently subscribing to the translation context.
- Move diff parsing (`parseUnifiedDiff` + the intra-line LCS highlighting) into a Web Worker for large diffs, with a synchronous fallback if the worker is unavailable; small diffs keep parsing synchronously with no behavior change.
- Reduce the workspace files list's polling interval now that the SSE stream already invalidates it on real changes, cutting redundant backend load.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/httpd/controllers/... ./internal/cli/...` — all pass
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `SessionFilesView.test.tsx` (31 tests, including new coverage for row virtualization and the diff-parser worker fallback path) — all pass
- [x] Production `vite build` — confirms the diff-parser worker bundles correctly as its own same-origin chunk, compatible with the existing CSP
- [ ] Manual verification in the packaged Electron app on a real large diff (recommended before merge)

title: feat(mobile): device roster — see, mute, and remove paired phones
body:
## Problem

There was no way to see which phones can receive push notifications from a desktop, and no way to stop one without hand-editing `~/.ao/data/mobile/push-devices.json`. Hand-editing did not even work: the daemon loads the registry into memory once at startup and rewrites the file from memory on the next mutation, so manual edits were silently reverted.

The registry also accumulated duplicates. Rows were keyed by the Expo push token, which rotates without the app being reinstalled, so one phone became several rows — all of which kept receiving notifications until Expo reported the stale token dead.

To be precise about the scope of the fix: keying on a stable install ID removes duplicates caused by **token rotation**. It does not survive a full uninstall/reinstall — the install ID lives in AsyncStorage, which uninstall wipes — so a reinstalled app does still create a new row. What it can no longer do is leave **two rows holding the same token**, which was the harmful part: that meant every notification delivered twice.

## What this adds

A **Devices** section in the Connect Mobile modal that lists every paired phone with:

- a **live** dot when that phone's app is open and in the foreground, or "last seen X ago" otherwise
- a **mute** switch — the device stays paired but receives no notifications
- **remove**, behind a confirmation

## How it works

**Device identity is decoupled from the push token.** The registry now keys on a stable per-install ID, and the token is an optional attribute. A row means *"a paired phone"*, not *"a push registration"* — so a phone that has not granted notification permission (or whose build cannot mint a token, e.g. an iOS build without the APNs entitlement) still appears, as connected with notifications off. The phone announces its identity on connect with no permission gate; the token attaches to that same row later if permission is granted.

**Liveness comes from the phone's existing 8-second REST poll**, not from a new transport. Every request carries an `X-AO-Install-Id` header, a middleware records the timestamp, and "live" means seen within 20s (two poll intervals plus slack). The mobile app pauses polling on `AppState` background — but deliberately *not* on `inactive`, which iOS reports for Control Centre and the app switcher — so backgrounding goes dark deterministically on both platforms rather than waiting for the OS to suspend the JS timer.

The mux WebSocket was deliberately **not** used: it is only open while the user is on a terminal screen, so it would mean "viewing a terminal", not "app is open".

**Removal writes a tombstone.** A removed phone that re-registers comes back *muted* rather than silently resuming notifications, and the tombstone is consumed on match so a deliberate unmute is never overridden. There is no per-device credential to revoke — every phone shares one bridge password — so fully evicting a device remains "regenerate the password and re-pair the phones you want". The UI says so.

## Security

The management routes (`GET`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/mobile/devices`) are **loopback-only**, mounted under `/api/v1/mobile`, which `lanControlBlockedPrefixes` already blocks on the LAN listener. That gate is enforced by the physical socket the request arrived on, so no header can spoof it, and it required no new gating code. A paired phone cannot enumerate the household's devices, unmute itself, or remove another device.

The phone's own unregister (`DELETE /api/v1/push/devices/{token}`) is unchanged and stays on the shared LAN surface. No new network-facing bind; the loopback listener is untouched.

Registration remains backward compatible: a request without an `installId` gets a server-synthesized `legacy-<uuid>`, which the token-adoption path merges into the real row on the next registration. Phones on older builds keep working — there is no flag day.

## Files worth reviewing

`backend/internal/mobilebridge/pushdevices.go` carries every subtle decision: the three-way `Upsert` resolution (install ID → token adoption → insert), `carryOver` (which preserves mute, created-at and token), tombstone consumption, and the `LoadRegistry` migration.

## Testing

Full suites green: backend (including `-race` on the touched packages), frontend 1976 tests, mobile 337 tests, no OpenAPI/TS drift.

Verified on real hardware (Android + iOS):

- a phone appears as connected with notifications off, before any permission is granted
- granting permission attaches the token to the same row rather than creating a second
- the live dot follows foreground/background, and survives the iOS `inactive` blip
- a notification was received on the device, then **muted and confirmed not delivered** with the device still holding a valid push token
- removing a device, then reopening the app, brings it back muted — and that survives a daemon restart

Not covered: iOS push *delivery*, which needs an EAS build for the APNs entitlement.

## Follow-ups (not blocking)

- `lastSeenAt` is only written on register/announce, so a long foreground session then a background shows a stale "N hours ago". The presence tracker holds the true timestamp; the roster does not read it yet.
- Dead-token pruning deletes the whole row, which contradicts the "a row is a paired phone" model. Clearing the token instead would be model-consistent; today a token death within an hour of a mute can drop that mute.

title: feat(chat): add Codex prompt editing with conversation branches
body:
## Summary

- add Copy and Edit actions to human messages in structured Chat sessions
- support editing for Codex Chat sessions by forking the provider conversation immediately before the selected prompt
- preserve the original conversation as a sibling branch instead of rolling back or deleting later history
- add previous/next branch navigation and persist the active branch across daemon restarts
- keep the existing worktree and its file changes untouched when a conversation branches
- preserve the bottom composer draft while editing inline

## Provider support

- Codex is currently the only provider with targeted conversation-fork support, so Edit is available only for Codex Chat sessions
- the UI is capability-gated; providers without a verified fork implementation do not show Edit
- adding another provider requires a structured fork-or-replay adapter, durable conversation IDs, and reliable resume support
- Copy remains available independently of conversation-fork support

## Architecture

- add a targeted ChatForker provider boundary
- persist conversation branches and active-branch state in SQLite migration 0086
- expose edit/fork and branch-switching operations through the conversation API
- project only the active branch and its ancestry into the rendered timeline
- keep nested lineage cutoffs monotonic and flatten repeated edits into one navigation group

## Behavior and safety

- editing creates a new conversation branch; it does not use provider rollback
- worktree files are never reverted when switching conversation branches
- branch creation is blocked while a turn is active
- failures before branch activation leave the original branch active
- provider send failures leave an empty new branch active and retain the inline draft for a retry on that same branch

title: fix(terminal): stop Windows app menu from stealing Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V in t…
body:
> I think removing the roles is the right approach. The only real alternative would be remapping the accelerators, but that would just steal another shortcut (`Ctrl+Shift+C`) that xterm already uses. Since Electron menu accelerators are static, there's no practical way to enable them only for text inputs.
> I don't see this regressing copy/paste either. Terminals already handle copy/paste themselves, and regular text fields on Windows rely on Chromium rather than Electron menu roles. I'd just do a quick manual check on Windows to confirm copy/paste still works in settings or chat inputs.
> The change is nicely scoped—just removing the two roles and adding a regression test. The only thing still worth verifying before merge is that `Ctrl+C` once again sends `SIGINT` on a real Windows machine, since that's not something the author can test from macOS.

## What

Remove `{ role: "copy" }` and `{ role: "paste" }` from the Windows-only
application menu (`frontend/src/main/menu.ts`), and add a regression test
asserting those roles are never bound (`frontend/src/main/menu.test.ts`).


## Why

On Windows, the Electron app menu installed `role:copy` / `role:paste`, whose
default accelerators are **Ctrl+C** / **Ctrl+V**. Electron resolves application-menu
accelerators in the **main process before** the renderer's `keydown`, so the keystroke
was consumed by the role and never reached xterm.js. As a result `\x03` (ETX → SIGINT)
was never written to the PTY, and a foreground process (`sleep 100`, `ping`) could not
be interrupted with Ctrl+C in a standalone shell terminal (and likewise Ctrl+V paste
was silently dropped).

fixes : #3659

## How

 **Removed `role:copy` / `role:paste`** from `buildWindowsAppMenuTemplate()` (kept
  `undo`/`redo`/`cut`/`selectAll` — they don't collide with terminal SIGINT). With the
  roles gone, Ctrl+C reaches xterm and falls through to `\x03` (SIGINT) when there is no
  selection, and Ctrl+V reaches the existing paste handler.
- **Why remove instead of override the accelerator:** setting
  `{ role: "copy", accelerator: "Ctrl+Shift+C" }` would just move the theft onto
  Ctrl+Shift+C, which xterm already owns for terminal copy (`XtermTerminal.tsx:521`).
  **Gating a menu role on live selection state is not feasible** — Electron menu
  accelerators are static, registered at menu-build time — so removal is the correct fix.
- **Why this is safe for non-terminal text fields:** the "menu must declare copy/paste
  roles for editing shortcuts to work" quirk is **macOS-only**; on Windows/Linux Chromium
  handles copy/paste natively. This menu is `win32`-only (`main.ts:317`) anyway.
- **Copy/paste in terminals is preserved** via: selection auto-copy
  (`XtermTerminal.tsx:550`), Ctrl+Shift+C, Ctrl+Insert, the right-click context menu, and
  Chromium-native in text fields. The visible `WindowTitlebar` Edit menu is a React
  dropdown whose `Ctrl+C`/`Ctrl+V` strings are visual labels only (clicks call
  `act("edit.copy")`, independent of Electron roles) — unaffected.
- **Scope is Windows-only by construction:** `menu.ts` is installed only when
  `process.platform === "win32"`. On macOS/Linux `isTerminalCopyShortcut`
  (`XtermTerminal.tsx:120`) does not match plain Ctrl+C, so SIGINT already worked there;
  this change does not touch those paths.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/main/menu.test.ts src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx`
  → **49/49 pass**. The new guard asserts no `copy`/`paste` role is bound; the existing
  `XtermTerminal.test.tsx:322/343/365` trio still locks the selection-gated copy-vs-SIGINT
  behavior (no renderer change was needed).
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` → no new errors. (Pre-existing, unrelated `code-highlight-engine.ts`
  missing-module errors remain due to stale local `node_modules`; they resolve under CI's fresh install.)
- **Could not reproduce locally** — this machine is macOS, where `menu.ts` is never installed,
  so the bug never reproduces here. Local Ctrl+C working on macOS only proves the non-Windows path
  is untouched.
- ⏳ **Still required before merge (delegated to a Windows machine/VM or the on-call Windows pair
  @illegalcall / @somewherelostt):** in a real Windows build, run `sleep 100` then Ctrl+C in
  (a) a standalone shell and (b) an agent session pane — both must interrupt; plus click-to-focus
  then Ctrl+C (forceSelectionMode) must still send SIGINT; plus copy/paste still works in a normal
  text field.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Linux/AppImage: identity check fails after relaunch-to-update (random /tmp/.mount_agent-* path), app stuck with no sessions and no way to add projects
body:
## Summary

On Linux (AppImage), relaunching the app after an update leaves it permanently stuck on **"AO daemon identity check failed" (`identity_mismatch`)**. The board shows "Could not load sessions." and projects can no longer be added — the app is unusable until the surviving daemon is killed by hand.

The identity check compares the running daemon's `executablePath` against the freshly resolved bundled daemon path. Under an AppImage those paths can never match across two launches, because the AppImage is mounted at a *random* `/tmp/.mount_agent-XXXXXX` path each time it starts.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the Linux AppImage build and let the daemon start (a project was already initialized in my case).
2. Switch the update channel to **nightly**.
3. Click **Relaunch to update**.
4. App comes back up.

## Actual behavior

Error toast, and the app is dead in the water:

```
AO daemon identity check failed                      identity_mismatch

Another AO daemon is already running from
/tmp/.mount_agent-1Qs4N6/resources/daemon/ao; expected
/tmp/.mount_agent-mDQfUL/resources/daemon/ao. Stop the other daemon
before using this app.

Stop the conflicting daemon, then restart the desktop app.
```

Board renders "Could not load sessions." and there is no way to add a project, for as long as the status reads `identity_mismatch`. The toast carries no Restart button in that state: `canRestart` in [DaemonFailureBanner.tsx:21](frontend/src/renderer/components/DaemonFailureBanner.tsx#L21) covers `not_ready`, `spawn_failed`, `exited` and `daemon_unreachable`, but not `identity_mismatch` — so the remediation text ("Stop the conflicting daemon, then restart the desktop app") has nothing behind it.

**It does recover on its own, after a delay.** Worth stating precisely, because it caps the severity:

- The old daemon is only alive because its supervisor grace fires ~5s after the previous Electron process exits ([supervisor.go](backend/internal/daemon/supervisor/supervisor.go)). The relaunch lands inside that window and probes a live daemon at the old mount path.
- `useDaemonStatus` re-polls every 2s while not ready ([useDaemonStatus.ts:8](frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useDaemonStatus.ts#L8)). Once the old daemon exits, `refreshDaemonStatus` finds nothing and — since the prior status was an error carrying a pid/port — rewrites it to `daemon_unreachable` ([main.ts:631](frontend/src/main.ts#L631)).
- `daemon_unreachable` *is* in `canRestart`, so a Restart button appears and clicking it spawns a healthy daemon. Relaunching the app instead works equally well.

So the lived symptom is "relaunch-to-update drops you into a dead app for several seconds, with a misleading and unactionable error, until the banner quietly turns into a different one you can act on" — not a permanent brick. Nothing spawns a daemon automatically: `daemon:start`/`daemon:restart` fire only from that button, plus `void startDaemon()` at boot.

Verified on my machine: the mismatched daemon was gone minutes later and the next launch spawned cleanly from a third mount (`.mount_agent-OgFgtF`).

Note this also means the normal healthy path is being lost: attaching would have worked. The supervisor cancels a pending grace timer on reconnect ([supervisor.go:107](backend/internal/daemon/supervisor/supervisor.go#L107)), and the attach path already re-links app-owned daemons, so the relaunch is *designed* to reattach — the identity check is the only thing preventing it.

## Expected behavior

Relaunching to update should reattach to (or cleanly replace) the daemon it spawned. An AppImage relaunching itself is not a "foreign daemon" and should not be treated as one.

## Root cause

`daemonIdentityError` in [frontend/src/main.ts:540-547](frontend/src/main.ts#L540-L547) for `source === "bundled"`:

```ts
if (launch.source === "bundled") {
    if (!probe.executablePath) { ... }
    if (!samePath(probe.executablePath, launch.command)) {
        return `Another AO daemon is already running from ${probe.executablePath}; expected ${launch.command}. ...`;
    }
}
```

`launch.command` comes from `resolveDaemonLaunch` in [frontend/src/shared/daemon-launch.ts:46-52](frontend/src/shared/daemon-launch.ts#L46-L52), which joins `process.resourcesPath` with `daemon/ao`. On an AppImage, `process.resourcesPath` lives under the squashfs FUSE mount, e.g. `/tmp/.mount_agent-1Qs4N6/resources` — and the `.mount_agent-XXXXXX` suffix is regenerated on every AppImage start.

So the path-equality identity check is structurally guaranteed to fail on Linux/AppImage whenever a daemon from a previous launch is still alive. The two paths in the error above differ *only* in the random mount suffix; they are the same binary from the same install.

## Notes / possible fixes

Not prescribing an approach, but the options seem to be:

- Detect the AppImage case (`APPIMAGE` / `APPDIR` env vars are set by the runtime) and identify the daemon by something stable — the `APPIMAGE` path, an install id, or a build/version fingerprint reported by `/readyz` — rather than by the mount-local executable path.
- Normalize/strip the `/tmp/.mount_*` prefix before comparing, so only the in-package suffix (`resources/daemon/ao`) is matched.
- Independently: when the app is relaunching *itself* for an update, the app-owned daemon should be shut down as part of the relaunch rather than surviving into the new process to be rejected.
- Independently of the root cause, `identity_mismatch` should not be a dead end. Since the state already resolves itself into a restartable one seconds later, the cheapest improvement is to stop presenting it as terminal — either add it to `canRestart`, or soften the copy so it does not read as "you must go kill a process by hand".

## Environment

- Linux, AppImage build (`agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage`)
- Channel: nightly (failure appeared right after switching from the previous channel and clicking "Relaunch to update")

Confirms the 6-character-prefix caveat above: the AppImage filename starts `agent-`, so every channel built under this name mounts as `.mount_agent-XXXXXX` and the mount name alone cannot distinguish them.

title: fix(frontend): clicking project name to switch to kanban board requires two clicks (orchestrator session)
body:
# Bug: Clicking project name to switch to Kanban board requires two clicks (orchestrator session)

## Summary

When viewing an **orchestrator agent session**, clicking the project name in the
topbar to switch to the kanban board requires **two clicks** — the first click
appears to do nothing, the second navigates. This regressed after the separate
"Kanban" button was removed and the project name became the click target for
board navigation.

## Source

**Reported by:** @prateek in Discord `#bug-triage` thread
**Video:** https://drive.google.com/file/d/17qZgkyDBGCP83lf8pBj0yj3QtUzkWDOP/view?usp=sharing
**Analyzed against:** `f17013b53` (origin/main, Aug 7 2026)
**Confidence:** Medium

## Reproduction

1. Open a project and navigate to its **orchestrator session** (`/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId` where the session is the orchestrator)
2. Click the **project name** in the topbar
3. **Expected:** navigates to the kanban board (`/projects/$projectId`)
4. **Actual:** first click does nothing (or the animation swallows it); second click navigates

## Root Cause

PR [#3490](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3490) (sidebar
animations, merged Aug 5 2026) wrapped the topbar project label in a
`motion.span` with a **shared `layoutId="topbar-project-label"`** and
`layout="position"`:

**`frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx`:**

- **Line 183–190** — orchestrator session route label:
  ```tsx
  <motion.span
      layoutId="topbar-project-label"
      layout="position"
      className={topbarProjectLabelClass}
      transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 40 }}
  >
      {projectLabel}
  </motion.span>
  ```

- **Line 213–220** — board route label (same `layoutId`):
  ```tsx
  <motion.span
      layoutId="topbar-project-label"
      layout="position"
      className={topbarProjectLabelClass}
      transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 40 }}
  >
      {projectLabel}
  </motion.span>
  ```

Both labels share the identical `layoutId`. When navigating from the orchestrator
session to the board, Motion's shared-layout animation animates the label's
position from its session-route location to its board-route location. During this
spring animation transition, the first pointer event (click) is consumed by the
layout animation lifecycle rather than reaching the navigation handler. The second
click lands after the animation has settled and successfully navigates.

### Note on navigation wiring

The project label `motion.span` itself has **no `onClick` handler** in the
current code. Navigation to the board is handled by the `openBoard()` function
(line 114–115), which is wired to the separate **"Kanban" `TopbarButton`**
(line 284, `onClick={openBoard}`). This button renders only on the orchestrator
session route (`isSessionRoute && isOrchestrator`).

The reporter indicates the Kanban button was removed in their build and the
project name became the click target. If the project name was given an
`onClick={openBoard}` (or similar) without addressing the `layoutId` animation
conflict, the spring transition would still intercept the first click. The fix
must ensure the click target is not inside an animating `motion.span`, or use
`layout="position"` with `layoutId` disabled during navigation.

## Fix

**Option A (minimal):** Give the project name label a stable wrapper outside the
`motion.span` that handles clicks, so the pointer event isn't captured by the
layout animation. The animation should be purely visual on the inner span.

**Option B:** Remove the shared `layoutId` on the project label when a click
handler is attached — use unique `layoutId`s per route, or drop
`layout="position"` and animate position independently.

**Option C:** Ensure the click target is a sibling `<button>` wrapping the
`motion.span`, so Motion's animation on the inner element doesn't block pointer
events on the outer interactive element.

## Impact

- **Severity:** Core navigation flow broken — users must click twice to return to
  the kanban board from an orchestrator session, every time.
- **Workaround:** Click twice, or use the sidebar project link instead.
- **Frequency:** 100% reproducible per the report.
- **Introduced by:** PR [#3490](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3490) (Aug 5 2026)

## Related

- PR [#3490](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3490) — introduced the shared `layoutId` animation
- PR [#3560](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3560) — topbar layout fix on session page (same area, same author, same day)

title: test(session_manager): fix Windows environment test failures
body:
## What

Fixes environment-specific pathing and mock resolution failures in the `session_manager` test suite that were occurring on Windows. Updates `.github/workflows/go.yml` to include `windows-latest` in the `build-test` matrix.

## Why

Fixes #3681.

Three testing assumptions were breaking `go test ./internal/session_manager/...` for contributors using Windows:
1. `os.UserHomeDir()` mocked exclusively with `HOME` (fails on Windows, which relies on `USERPROFILE`).
2. Hardcoded Unix absolute paths (`/usr/bin`, `/opt/aod`) embedded directly in string assertions.
3. Node `PATH` resolution tests assuming `nodeRuntimeDir` prepended Node binaries to the path, despite the production code correctly short-circuiting and returning an empty string on Windows platforms.

## How

- Extracted a `setHomeEnv(t, home)` helper function in `manager_test.go` and enforced setting both `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` simultaneously to guarantee parity between test setups and OS implementation.
- Replaced all static Unix literals (like `/usr/bin` and `/opt/aod`) with OS-agnostic derivations utilizing `t.TempDir()`.
- Added a `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` guard to `TestSpawnAndRestore_PrependsResolvedBinaryAndNodeDirsToRuntimePATH` to skip the `nodeDir` check on Windows, aligning the test suite's expectations with the production code.

## Testing

Validated via `go test ./internal/session_manager/...` locally on a Windows machine. All tests now cleanly pass (`ok`).

title: fix(desktop): recognise own daemon across AppImage relaunches via stable AO_APPIMAGE identity
body: ## What Fixes the Linux/AppImage daemon identity check so the desktop app recognises its own daemon across launches. The daemon now reports the stable outer `.AppImage` file path (`AO_APPIMAGE`, set by the Electron app at spawn, echoed as `appImagePath` in `/healthz`/`/readyz`), and the app compares that value when running under AppImage instead of the transient `/tmp/.mount_*` executable path. Outside AppImage the exact `executablePath` comparison is unchanged. Also adds a Restart action to the `identity_mismatch` failure banner so a genuine foreign-daemon conflict is actionable instead of a dead end. ## Why Fixes #3679. On Linux/AppImage, every launch mounts the app at a random `/tmp/.mount_agent-XXXXXX` path. After "Relaunch to update", the surviving daemon (kept alive ~5s by the supervisor grace) reported its executable under the *previous* mount, so the exact-path identity check could never match. The app showed `identity_mismatch`, the board rendered "Could not load sessions", and the banner had no recovery action until the old daemon exited and the status degraded into `daemon_unreachable`. ## How - `backend`: `daemonProbePayload` includes `appImagePath` when `AO_APPIMAGE` is set (dedicated env var, matching the `AO_OWNER`/`AO_APP_RUN_ID` family; no OpenAPI impact — health routes are outside the generated spec). - `frontend/main`: passes `AO_APPIMAGE: process.env.APPIMAGE` to the daemon at spawn; the bundled branch of `daemonIdentityError` delegates to a pure, unit-tested helper. - `frontend/shared/daemon-launch.ts`: new `bundledDaemonIdentityError()` — under AppImage compares the probed `appImagePath` against this process's `APPIMAGE`; otherwise falls back to the exact `executablePath` check. Probes that cannot prove identity fail closed, as before. - `frontend/shared/daemon-attach.ts`: `DaemonProbe`/`parseDaemonProbe` carry `appImagePath`. - `DaemonFailureBanner`: `identity_mismatch` added to `canRestart`. Restart only re-runs attach/spawn; it never kills a daemon this process didn't spawn, so a truly foreign daemon simply re-surfaces the error. Trade-off / rejected alternative: stripping the `/tmp/.mount_*` prefix and comparing the in-package suffix was rejected — the suffix is identical across every build and channel, so it would silently attach to a genuinely different install's daemon. Killing the daemon inside `quitAndInstallUpdate` was rejected as racy and insufficient (doesn't cover crash-restart or quick manual relaunch within the grace window). Known one-time limitation: the first update *into* a build with this fix still hits the old behaviour once (a pre-fix daemon doesn't report `appImagePath`), fails closed for the ~5s grace window, then self-resolves — now with a Restart button. ## Testing - `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/shared/daemon-launch.test.ts src/shared/daemon-attach.test.ts src/renderer/lib/daemon-failure.test.ts` — 49 tests pass, incl. new cases: cross-mount reattach (the bug scenario, using the exact paths from the issue), foreign-install mismatch, and fail-closed when identity is unprovable. - `cd backend && go test ./...` — pass (new `TestHealthProbesIncludeAppImageIdentity` covers `/healthz` + `/readyz` with `AO_APPIMAGE` set and unset). - `golangci-lint` v2.12.2 — 0 issues. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean on touched files. - Not yet verified: the real Linux/AppImage relaunch-to-update flow (needs a Linux machine; the bug cannot be reproduced on macOS/Windows). Reviewer smoke test: launch AppImage → switch channel → Relaunch to update → app reattaches with no `identity_mismatch` banner. frontend tests : backend test (added) : ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Workspace import dead-ends on 48 raw errors: origin/worktree validation too strict + no remediation UX
body:
## Bug

Workspace import blocks users behind a wall of 48 raw errors with no path forward except "Cancel." The user picked a legitimate folder (`~/Desktop/AIOS_coding`) containing multiple git repos, and the import modal became a dead-end error screen instead of a usable flow.

**Source:** [Discord #bug-triage](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1535228014290403368) | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `fb0f85fa4`
**Confidence:** High — traced both the frontend pre-scan and backend validation paths.

## What the user sees

Three screenshots were provided in the Discord report. The import modal shows:

> **IMPORT FAILED · WORKSPACE NOT REGISTERED**
> Workspace child repositories must have an origin remote configured (`WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED`)
>
> ❌ `AIOS_HomeServices` — Origin remote is required.
> ❌ `aios-dashboard-slack-step1` — Linked worktree children cannot be ...
> ❌ `wt-ask-chip-fix` — Linked worktree children cannot be ...
> … (scrollable list of **48** failed repos)
>
> Footer: **"Resolve 48 failed repositories to continue"**
> Only action: **Cancel**

This is a UX dead-end — no "import anyway," no "skip failures," no remediation guidance, no explanation of what a linked worktree is.

## Root Cause

Two layers of over-strict validation combine to block the user, and the frontend renders the failure as an unrecoverable wall.

### Layer 1 — Frontend pre-scan (`frontend/src/main/import-folder-scan.ts`)

`scanGitRepo()` (line 126) runs a hard validation on every child directory:

- **`.git` is a file (not a dir) → instant failure** with `"Linked worktree children cannot be imported."` (line 144). This rejects all git linked worktrees — a legitimate workflow (the user clearly uses `wt-*` worktree dirs).
- `scanRepoValidationReason()` (line 192) hard-fails any repo missing an `origin` remote: `if (!hasRemote) return "Origin remote is required."` (line 203). A local-only repo, a fork without a remote, or a freshly `git init`'d experiment all fail here.

The scan result feeds `CreateProjectFolderDialog` (`CreateProjectFlow.tsx:483`):

```tsx
const failedRepos = scan?.repos.filter((repo) => repo.status === "error" || !repo.hasRemote) ?? [];
```

`failedRepos` drives:
- The error banner (shown when `error` is set, lines 544–558)
- The footer: `"Resolve {{count}} failed repositories to continue"` (line 487)
- **No continue/import button exists** — the only action is `Cancel` (line 609).

### Layer 2 — Backend validation (`backend/internal/service/project/workspace_registration.go`)

Even if the frontend didn't block, `validateWorkspaceChild()` (line 186) enforces the same hard constraints server-side:

- `.git` is a file → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_IS_WORKTREE` (line 193) — hard reject.
- No origin URL → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED` (line 217) — hard reject.
- Unborn repo (no HEAD) → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_UNBORN` (line 204).
- No default branch → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNKNOWN` (line 211).

Both layers require **every** child repo to have an `origin` remote and to be a standalone (non-worktree) repo. This is an over-constraint: workspace folders legitimately contain local-only repos, work-in-progress without remotes, and git worktrees.

### Why the UX is a failure (prateek's point)

> "Our UX should never allow users to see such ugly bug messages, it should nudge them towards the right behaviours, and in worst cases, just make decisions for them. They should not be allowed to configure a project in a wrong way in the first place."

1. **Dead-end with no remediation** — 48 errors, only "Cancel." No "import the N valid repos," no "skip failures," no "set up remotes" guidance.
2. **Raw internal error codes** surfaced to end users (`WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED`).
3. **Over-strict validation masquerading as a bug** — a workspace folder with local repos or worktrees is a valid configuration, not an error state.
4. **No prevention at folder-selection time** — the wall appears only after the user has committed to a folder, not as a guided pre-check.

## Proposed Fix

This needs product/UX decisions before implementation. Direction:

### 1. Relax the origin requirement (backend + scan)
Make `origin` optional for workspace children. A child without an origin is included with a `RepoOriginURL` of `""` and flagged as "local only" — SCM operations that need a remote can degrade gracefully. The `WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED` hard reject should become a soft warning.

### 2. Allow worktree children (or auto-detect and skip cleanly)
Git worktrees are a legitimate pattern. Either:
- **(a)** Support them as workspace children (register the worktree path), or
- **(b)** Detect them at scan time and silently exclude from the import set with a non-blocking info note ("N worktrees excluded"), rather than flagging as errors.

### 3. Redesign the failure state as a guided flow, not a wall
Replace the dead-end error modal with actionable UX:
- **"Import N repositories" (primary CTA)** — proceed with the valid repos, showing which are included.
- **"Skip M repositories"** — let the user exclude problematic children and continue.
- **Per-repo remediation hints** — e.g., for missing origin: "Click to set up a remote" (or at minimum, a one-line explanation).
- **Human-readable messages** — replace `WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED` with "This repository doesn't have a remote configured. [Set up origin]"

### 4. Pre-check at folder selection
When the user picks a workspace folder, run the scan immediately and show a summary ("Found 12 valid repos, 48 need attention") before they commit — not after.

## Impact

- **All users** with workspace folders containing local-only repos or worktrees hit this wall.
- The user in the report has **48 of ~50+ repos failing** — the feature is effectively unusable for their (common) setup.
- P1: core workflow (workspace creation) broken with no safe workaround for affected users.

## Related

- [#2222](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2222) — Complete backend support for workspace projects (tracking issue)
- [#2720](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2720) — UI/UX Audit 1

## Reproduction

1. Create a folder with multiple git repos, some without `origin` remotes and some that are git worktrees (`git worktree add`).
2. In the AO desktop app, create a new project → choose "Workspace" → select that folder.
3. Observe: the import modal shows a wall of errors with only a Cancel button.

title: bug(test): dozens of pre-existing test failures on Windows — path assumptions, TempDir cleanup, env var ordering
body:
## Bug

When `windows-latest` was added to the `go test` CI matrix, dozens of pre-existing test failures surfaced across the repository — unrelated to the `session_manager` fix in [#3681](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3681). The failures fall into several categories:

- **Path assumptions** — tests in the chat drivers and elsewhere assume Unix path separators, hardcoded absolute paths (`/tmp`, `/usr/bin`), and `filepath.Join` semantics that don't hold on Windows.
- **TempDir cleanup** — `t.TempDir()` cleanup fails on Windows when files are still locked/open, producing cleanup errors that fail the test.
- **Environment variable sorting** — tests that assert on `os.Environ()` ordering or compare environment slices break because Windows sorts `PATH`/environment differently.

These are **pre-existing** failures — the Go test CI job ([`.github/workflows/go.yml`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/.github/workflows/go.yml)) runs only `ubuntu-latest`, so they've been invisible.

**Source:** Discord #bug-triage | **Reported by:** @Neo
**Analyzed against:** `main` (Aug 7, 2026)
**Confidence:** High — failures directly observed by adding `windows-latest` to the CI matrix

## Context

While fixing [#3681](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3681) (session_manager test failures on Windows), the PR [PR #3684](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3684) temporarily added `windows-latest` to the CI matrix in `go.yml`. This exposed that the session_manager failures were just the tip of the iceberg — dozens of other test files across the repo also fail on Windows for similar but independent reasons.

To unblock the #3681 fix, `windows-latest` was removed from the CI matrix for that PR. This issue tracks the broader Windows test surface that needs fixing before Windows can be permanently added to the `go test` matrix.

## Failure Categories

### 1. Path assumptions (chat drivers and others)

Tests assume Unix path conventions:
- Hardcoded `/` separators instead of `filepath.Join` / `os.PathSeparator`
- Absolute Unix paths (`/usr/bin`, `/tmp`, `/opt`) in test fixtures and assertions
- `filepath.Join` used correctly in setup but compared against string-concatenated Unix paths in assertions

### 2. TempDir cleanup issues

`t.TempDir()` fails on Windows when:
- File handles remain open (file locking — Windows doesn't allow deletion of open files)
- Child processes spawned during tests haven't exited before cleanup
- This produces `RemoveAll` errors that fail the test even when the test logic itself passed

### 3. Environment variable ordering

Tests that:
- Assert on `os.Environ()` output ordering
- Compare environment variable slices
- Assume `PATH`-style ordering semantics

Break on Windows because environment variable enumeration/sorting differs from POSIX.

## Fix Direction

This is a tracking issue. The work should be done incrementally — each category (or affected package) as a separate PR — rather than a single mega-fix:

1. **Audit failing packages** — re-add `windows-latest` to `go.yml` in a throwaway branch, capture the full list of failing packages/tests, and triage by category.
2. **Fix path assumptions** — replace hardcoded Unix paths with `t.TempDir()`-derived paths, use `filepath.Join` consistently, guard Unix-only assertions with `runtime.GOOS`.
3. **Fix TempDir cleanup** — ensure all file handles and child processes are closed/exited before test completion (defer cleanup, `t.Cleanup` with proper teardown ordering).
4. **Fix env var ordering** — sort environment slices before comparison, or compare as maps instead of ordered slices.
5. **Add `windows-latest` to `go.yml` permanently** — once the suite is green on Windows, lock it in to prevent regressions.

## Impact

- **Windows contributors** cannot run `go test ./...` locally — they see dozens of false failures unrelated to their changes.
- **CI gap** — the Go test suite only validates on Linux, so Windows-specific regressions are invisible until a contributor hits them.
- **Product risk** — AO ships a Windows desktop app; untested backend code paths on Windows is a real risk.

## Related

- [#3681](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3681) — session_manager tests fail on Windows (HOME-only mock + hardcoded Unix paths) — the specific fix that exposed this broader issue
- [PR #3684](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3684) — the session_manager fix PR where Windows was temporarily added to CI

## Priority

**P2** — No user-facing runtime breakage (production code is Windows-guarded), but this blocks reliable Windows CI and frustrates Windows contributors. Should be addressed before adding Windows to the permanent CI matrix.

title: fix(session): resolve PR fallback compare base to merge-base
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #3203: the Files tab could report far more changed files than a PR actually has (e.g. 2 files on GitHub vs. 36 in AO).
- Root cause: the PR fallback in `resolveWorkspaceCompare` used the provider's current `pr.BaseSHA` (the target branch's live tip) directly, instead of the merge-base of `HEAD` and that SHA. When the target branch advances after a session forks and no diff base is recorded, the raw-SHA diff also picks up every base-only change in reverse, alongside the session's own edits.
- Fix: resolve `git merge-base HEAD pr.BaseSHA` and use that as `CompareBaseSHA`, keeping the PR's target branch as `CompareBaseRef`. File status, numstat, and per-file diff/patch all read from the same `workspaceCompareTarget`, so this single change fixes all three surfaces.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `TestWorkspaceFilesPRFallbackUsesMergeBaseWhenTargetBranchAdvances`, which reproduces the reported scenario (target branch advances independently after the session forks, no recorded diff base) and asserts base-only files are excluded and only the session's own file shows as added.
- [x] `go test ./internal/service/session/...` — pass, including the existing `TestWorkspaceFilesPRFallbackPrefersDefaultTargetPR` (unaffected).
- [x] `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` — clean.
- [x] `go test ./...` — same 3 pre-existing failures reproduce identically on `main` without this change (Windows PATH-separator formatting in `session_manager`, fsnotify timing in `workspacewatch`); unrelated to this fix.

title: feat(auth): add native WorkOS desktop sign-in
body:
## Summary
- add native WorkOS AuthKit PKCE sign-in through the system browser and return to the desktop app through the registered `ao-app://callback` protocol
- encrypt access and refresh tokens with Electron `safeStorage`, deduplicate refreshes, preserve credentials on retryable failures, and make explicit sign-out authoritative over in-flight refreshes
- add localized sidebar account controls while keeping access and refresh tokens out of renderer IPC
- register Linux deb/rpm protocol metadata and make raw AppImages installed by `ao start` create and verify the freedesktop `ao-app` URL handler
- require the non-secret `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` repository variable in canonical release/artifact workflows so an official build cannot silently ship with sign-in disabled

- sign-out clears the desktop session locally and forces fresh authentication (`maxAge: 0`) next time; it does not open the browser or revoke the WorkOS server session
- when protected OS storage is unavailable, credentials remain memory-only and disappear after restart
- terminal refresh-token failures clear the session; network, rate-limit, timeout, and server failures retain encrypted credentials for retry
- Linux AppImage protocol registration uses the standard XDG applications and MIME-association locations; AO runtime state remains under `~/.ao`

title: bug: opening Settings navigates away from the current session to Board
body:
## Bug
Opening Settings (sidebar footer or Cmd+K → Global settings) leaves the current page and lands on Board behind the modal. Opening settings from a session terminal should keep that session underneath.

## Reproduction
1. Open any session terminal.
2. Click sidebar **Settings**, or open Cmd+K and choose **Global settings**.
3. Observe: settings modal opens, but the page behind switches to **Board**.

## Root Cause
After [#3497](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3497) converted settings to a modal, in-app openers still navigated to `/settings`. The legacy route shim opens the modal then `navigate({ to: "/", replace: true })`, which dumps the user on Board:

- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.settings.tsx` — redirect to `/`
- Callers: `Sidebar`, `CommandPalette`, `_shell` settings shortcut, `WindowTitlebar`, etc.

## Fix
Open the settings modal via `useUiStore.openGlobalSettings()` / `openProjectSettings()` in place (no route change). Keep `/settings` only as a deep-link shim that returns via `history.back()` when possible.

## Impact
- Session/terminal context is lost whenever settings is opened
- Same for project-settings openers that redirected to the project board

## Related
- [#3497](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3497) — settings page → modal conversion that introduced the redirect shim

title: fix(release): stop baking the pre-rename AgentWrapper org into release config
body:
## What

`DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO` in `frontend/forge.config.ts` and `DEFAULT_REPO` in `frontend/src/main/feature-builds.ts` still hardcoded `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` -- the org this repo was renamed away from. Any build path that doesn't set `AO_RELEASE_REPO` explicitly bakes the stale owner into the shipped `app-update.yml`, including `build-artifacts.yml`'s dispatchable unsigned build, which never sets it at all.

Today auto-update only keeps working because GitHub's org-rename redirect (`AgentWrapper` -> `Untrivial-ai`) happens to still resolve. That redirect breaks permanently the moment the still-existing `AgentWrapper` account creates any repo named `agent-orchestrator`, at which point every fleet install baked with the stale owner loses auto-update for good.

## Fix

- `frontend/forge.config.ts`: `DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO` -> `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`.
- `frontend/src/main/feature-builds.ts`: `DEFAULT_REPO` -> `{ owner: "Untrivial-ai", ... }` (kept in sync with the forge default per its own comment).
- `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml`: set `AO_RELEASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}` on the make step, matching the pattern `frontend-release.yml` already uses, so forks and dispatched builds bake their own owner instead of falling through to the production default at all.

## Scope note

This addresses the part of #3523 that lives in this repo. The issue also calls out the external `ao-releases` conductor and a macOS update-e2e regression guard; I don't have access to that conductor repo and don't have a macOS environment to build/verify an e2e guard, so I left both out rather than guess. Happy to take a pass at the e2e guard if someone can point me at how `mac-update-e2e.yml` is normally exercised.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` over the frontend: clean (after `npm ci` to pick up the current lockfile).
- `npx vitest run src/main/feature-builds.test.ts src/main/auto-updater.test.ts`: 61/61 passing, no regressions.
- `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml` parsed with `js-yaml` to confirm the edited step is still valid YAML.
- Grepped the touched files for any remaining `AgentWrapper` reference; only the intentional historical note in the `forge.config.ts` comment remains.

I don't have a way to actually run the Electron packaging step or a macOS/Linux release build in this environment, so I wasn't able to verify the baked `app-update.yml` output end-to-end -- the fix is a straightforward default-value substitution plus an explicit env var mirroring an existing working pattern, but flagging that gap for reviewers.

title: Activity timeline events not sorted chronologically
body:
## Bug

The session inspector's **Activity timeline** does not sort events chronologically. Events are displayed in category-group order (Created → Drafts → Opened → Merged → Done) rather than by timestamp, causing recently-opened PRs to appear below older events.

**Reported by:** @prateek in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1535215769460408392)
**Analyzed against:** `f17013b53`
**Confidence:** High — traced exact code path, fix verified by tests

### Screenshot evidence

The reported session shows:

| Position | Event | Timestamp |
|----------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | Working | (live) |
| 2 | Merged PR #3647 | 18h ago |
| 3 | Opened PR #3647 | 1d ago |
| 4 | **Opened PR #3683** | **53m ago** ← most recent historical event, but buried at position 4 |
| 5 | Created workspace | 1d ago |

"Opened PR #3683" (53m ago) should appear at position 2 (just below Working), not position 4.

## Root Cause

`ActivityTimeline` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx` (line 997):

```typescript
const events = [current, ...history.reverse()];
```

The `history` array is built by pushing events in **category groups**:

1. Created workspace
2. All draft PRs (in PR-number order)
3. All opened PRs (in PR-number order)
4. All merged PRs (in PR-number order)
5. Done (if merged)

`.reverse()` simply flips this category order — it does **not** sort by timestamp. When two PRs are in the same category (e.g. both "opened"), they remain in PR-number order regardless of when they were actually opened. PR #3683 (53m ago) gets placed after PR #3647 (1d ago) because 3683 > 3647 numerically within the "opened" group.

This is invisible when a session has only one PR (the category order happens to be chronological), but breaks for any session with multiple PRs opened/merged at different times.

## Fix

Replace `history.reverse()` with a proper reverse-chronological sort by timestamp:

```typescript
const sortedHistory = [...history].sort((a, b) => b.sortTs - a.sortTs || b.seq - a.seq);
```

Each history entry now carries a `sortTs` (epoch ms parsed from `createdAt`/`stateChangedAt`/`updatedAt`) and a `seq` (push order, used as a tiebreaker when timestamps are equal or missing — preserving the semantic grouping as a fallback).

## Impact

- **Severity:** Medium — confusing UX, not data loss. Users rely on the timeline to understand session history at a glance.
- **Affects:** Any session with multiple PRs where events don't happen in PR-number order.
- **Workaround:** None (users see incorrect ordering).

## Test Coverage

- Updated existing test to use realistic timestamps (previously used artificial equal timestamps that masked the bug).
- Added regression test reproducing the exact reported scenario (PR #3683 opened 53m ago vs PR #3647 opened 1d ago).

title: fix(frontend): sort activity timeline chronologically by timestamp
body:
Fixes #3698

## Summary

The `ActivityTimeline` component in `SessionInspector.tsx` built its history array by pushing events in **category groups** (Created → Drafts → Opened → Merged → Done), then called `.reverse()`. This flipped the category order but did **not** sort by timestamp — so a recently-opened PR (e.g. 53m ago) could appear below an older PR (e.g. 1d ago) when both were in the "opened" group.

**Fix:** Replace `history.reverse()` with a proper reverse-chronological sort:
```typescript
const sortedHistory = [...history].sort((a, b) => b.sortTs - a.sortTs || b.seq - a.seq);
```

Each history entry now carries:
- `sortTs` — epoch ms parsed from `createdAt`/`stateChangedAt`/`updatedAt`
- `seq` — push order, used as a descending tiebreaker when timestamps are equal or missing (preserves the semantic grouping: Done > Merged > Opened > Draft > Created)

## Root Cause

`SessionInspector.tsx:997` — `const events = [current, ...history.reverse()];`

The `.reverse()` call only reversed array push order, not chronological order. Within a category group (e.g. two "opened" PRs), events stayed in PR-number order regardless of their actual timestamps.

## Test

- Updated existing ordering test to use realistic SCM summary timestamps (the original used artificial equal timestamps that masked the bug)
- Added regression test reproducing the exact reported scenario: PR #3683 (53m ago) vs PR #3647 (1d ago)

```
cd frontend && npx vitest run src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx
```

All 76 tests pass.

title: fix(desktop): detect wedged updater network stack and nudge restart
body: ## What Hardens the desktop auto-updater against a wedged Chromium network stack (net::ERR_FAILED on every updater request until app restart): 1. Manual "Check for Updates" failures with a Chromium network error (net::ERR_*) now show restart guidance instead of the raw Chromium string. 2. Consecutive automatic-check failures with network-level errors are counted; after 3 in a row (~3h of hourly checks), the Settings → Updates section shows a non-error warning nudge: "Updates haven't been able to check for a while — restarting the app usually fixes this." ## Why Fixes #3526. A long-running app instance can end up with a wedged Chromium network stack. Every updater request then fails with net::ERR_FAILED until the app is restarted. Two UX problems resulted: - Manual checks surfaced the raw net::ERR_FAILED … string with no guidance. - Automatic (hourly) check failures are deliberately UI-suppressed (telemetry only), so a wedged instance went silently stale — the maintainer's instance missed two published nightlies with no visible signal. ## How - `frontend/src/shared/update-telemetry.ts`: new exported `isNetErrorMessage()` (`/^net::/i`, anchored) — the single definition of the wedge signature. Telemetry bucketing already categorized these as "network"; unchanged. - `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`: - `updateRequestErrorMessage()` swaps the raw `net::` string for restart guidance (original message kept in parentheses for diagnostics), applied in both manual-failure paths: the `checkForUpdatesNow` rejection catch and the error-event fall-through in `wireUpdaterEvents`. Hardcoded English in main, matching the existing manifest-404 message convention. - A module-level streak counter increments on net-level automatic-check failures — in the error handler AND in `runAutomaticUpdateCheck`'s own catch (a wedged stack can reject `checkForUpdates()` without emitting an error event). A per-operation guard prevents double counting when one check surfaces both ways. `update-available` / `update-not-available` / `download-progress` reset the streak, since any of them proves the network works. - `broadcast()` (the single status choke point) stamps `staleCheckNudge: true` on outgoing statuses once the streak reaches `STALE_CHECK_NUDGE_THRESHOLD = 3`. The nudge rides on the normal status object, so it never clobbers state and the automatic-failure UI suppression stays intact. - `frontend/src/main/update-settings.ts`: `UpdateStatus.staleCheckNudge?: boolean`. - Renderer: `UpdatesSection.tsx` renders the nudge as a text-warning line (same pattern as the nightly warning), independent of status state; new i18n key `settings.updates.networkStale` added to all 8 locale files. Intentional omissions: - Issue item (3) — investigating whether the wedge is an Electron network-service crash, attempting session recreation, and sizing via PostHog — is investigation-only and out of scope for this PR. - No automatic remediation (e.g. session recreation); this PR is detect + message only. ## Testing - `npx vitest run src/shared/update-telemetry.test.ts src/main/auto-updater.test.ts src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n/renderer-coverage.test.ts` — 76/76 pass, including new cases: - manual check rejecting with net::ERR_FAILED → friendly restart message (raw string preserved in parentheses), both rejection and error-event paths - non-net errors stay verbatim - 3 consecutive net-failed automatic checks → `staleCheckNudge: true` on the restored status; 2 → no nudge - non-net automatic failures never nudge - one check emitting error AND rejecting counts as a single failure - a successful check clears the nudge - renderer: warning line renders with the normal status still shown - `npm run typecheck` — clean for all touched files (only pre-existing lowlight/highlight.js resolution errors in `code-highlight-engine.ts` from missing node_modules in the local checkout; unrelated). Ui changes (before): Ui changes (after): ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(mobile): make Connect Mobile pairing work over Tailscale, including iOS
body:
## Problem

The Connect Mobile dialog has a LAN/Tailscale segmented control, but the toggle only swapped instruction text — the QR always carried the LAN address. A user who selected **Tailscale** and scanned paired their phone to an address it could not reach, and the resulting error told them to check they were on the same Wi-Fi: the exact opposite of what a Tailscale user is doing.

Fixing that surfaced a second, deeper problem. Even with the correct `100.x` address in the QR, **iOS still could not pair**. App Transport Security permits cleartext HTTP only to RFC 1918 ranges, and Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` is RFC 6598 — so iOS blocked the request before a packet left the device. Confirmed empirically: Safari (exempt from ATS) reached the address fine while the app reported "Reached nothing". Android was unaffected, since `usesCleartextTraffic` is global.

## What this does

**The QR now follows the mode.** LAN encodes the LAN address; Tailscale encodes the Tailscale address.

**A new opt-in "Secure pairing (TLS)" mode** solves iOS. The desktop runs `tailscale serve` to front the bridge with Tailscale's own certificate, and the QR carries the MagicDNS hostname on port 443 with `secure: true`. HTTPS to a cert-backed domain satisfies ATS outright — **no ATS exception, no `app.json` change, nothing to justify at App Store review** — and the traffic becomes genuinely encrypted rather than relying on WireGuard alone, so the "not encrypted" warning is correctly suppressed in that mode.

Two pre-existing bugs are fixed along the way:

- With no address available, the modal used to encode `host: ""`, which the app rejects as *"not an AO pairing code"* — an incoherent error for a QR the desktop generated itself. It now shows an explanatory hint instead.
- A scan overrode host/port/password but **inherited `secure`**, and the `v: 1` payload had no way to clear it. A user who enabled TLS manually and then scanned a LAN QR silently kept `secure: true`, hit the same misleading error, and stayed stuck across restarts because the flag is persisted.

## Compatibility

**The payload stays at `v: 1`, and `secure` is emitted only when true** — every plaintext QR is byte-identical, so no already-installed build regresses. Secure pairing is off by default, so an older build only ever sees a QR it understands.

## The one adoption caveat

Secure pairing needs **HTTPS certificates enabled on the tailnet** (admin console → DNS), which is not on by default, and the `tailscale` CLI on `PATH` (App Store installs of Tailscale don't add it). The feature detects both, plus a missing MagicDNS name and a failed proxy, and shows targeted setup steps rather than a QR that cannot connect. Where it isn't usable, it degrades to today's plaintext behaviour — which still works on Android.

## Design notes worth a reviewer's attention

- **The bridge has no fixed port.** `LANManager.Start` falls back to an ephemeral port when its default is taken (observed: bound `54014` because another instance held `3011`). A `serve` config pinned to a stale port is this feature's primary failure mode, and `serve` config persists inside `tailscaled` across restarts. `Apply` is therefore called with the port `Start` *actually returned*, on every listener start — enable, password rotation, and boot restore. Boot restore routes through `BridgeService` for this reason rather than driving the listener directly.
- **A `serve` failure never takes the bridge down.** It is recorded and surfaced as a reason while the bridge stays up in plaintext mode.
- **`reason` is a fixed enum**, never a raw error string — raw errors are untranslated and can leak filesystem paths to the UI.
- **`serve`, never `funnel`** — the proxy is tailnet-only; nothing is publicly exposed. `/api/v1/mobile` remains 404 on the LAN listener by prefix, so the new route is unreachable from the network with no extra work, and the pairing password never leaves loopback.

## Testing

Automated: backend packages pass with `go vet`/`gofmt` clean; renderer 1448/1448; mobile 349/349; `tsc --noEmit` clean in both TS packages.

Verified on real hardware (macOS + iPhone 13 + Android):

- Secure scan on iPhone **over cellular with Wi-Fi off** — pairs with no typing, including the `/mux` terminal WebSocket.
- Flip back to LAN and re-scan — connects, confirming the stale-`secure` trap is gone.
- Android regression check — both modes still pair.
- Desktop restart with secure pairing on — the proxy re-points at the new bridge port with no re-scan.
- Security: `/api/v1/mobile` returns 404 over the Tailscale address and over the LAN address; unauthenticated data routes 401; authenticated 200.

## Follow-ups, deliberately not here

- Emitting `no_magicdns` distinctly — `tailscale status` cannot distinguish a missing CLI from disabled MagicDNS, so both currently surface as `no_cli`, whose copy covers both.
- Automatic enabling of HTTPS certificates or MagicDNS: both are tailnet-wide administrative changes AO should not make on a user's behalf.

title: CLI actorType is computed but unused — is server-side authorisation on session send in scope?
body:
## Observation

`cliInvocationActorType` (`backend/internal/cli/root.go:241-249`) classifies every CLI invocation as `agent` or `user`, deriving `agent` from a well-formed `AO_SESSION_ID` in the environment:

```go
if sessionIDPattern.MatchString(strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("AO_SESSION_ID"))) {
    return "agent"
}
```

As far as I can tell, that value is only ever used for telemetry sampling (`root.go:237` → `httpd/router.go:187`, `httpd/cli_telemetry_reservoir.go:67-90`). It doesn't appear to reach any authorisation decision.

Meanwhile `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/send` (`httpd/controllers/sessions.go:156`) validates only message content — JSON shape, non-empty, length, control-char sanitisation — and never considers who the caller is. `ao send` stamps `[from <AO_SESSION_ID>]` onto the body (`cli/send.go:44-47`), so the daemon *is* told a session sent it, but treats it as text.

**Net effect:** in a setup where several agent sessions run on one host, any agent with shell access can write a turn into any other session — `ao send --session <peer-id> --message ...`, or a direct POST to the same route.

## This may well be intentional

The trust boundary looks deliberate: the daemon binds loopback only (`config/config.go:20-25`), and `localControlRequest` (`httpd/router.go:275-291`) is explicitly documented as treating any loopback, Origin-less caller as trusted — closing CSRF/DNS-rebinding while leaving the CLI unaffected. The LAN listener is separately gated (`httpd/lan_listener.go:38`, `lanControlBlock`). So this is not network exposure: it's a same-host question about whether agents are peers of the operator.

Some orchestration designs *want* agents messaging each other. If that's AO's intent, this is a docs question, not a bug — and I'd suggest saying so explicitly, since the `agent`/`user` distinction already existing in the code reads as though the groundwork was laid for a policy that isn't there.

## Why it matters for multi-agent setups

For a harness running N concurrent agent sessions on one host with per-session isolation (separate worktrees, scoped file ownership), an unauthenticated same-host `send` is a channel that bypasses the orchestrator: one agent can steer another's work without the supervisor seeing it. Reproducibility suffers before security does — a run's outcome depends on messages nothing recorded as control flow.

## Suggested minimal fix

Config-gated, defaulting to today's behaviour so nothing breaks:

- Pass the already-computed actor type to the daemon on `send` (header or body field), and add a policy setting, e.g. `send.allowAgentToAgent`: `allow` (current behaviour, default) / `deny` / `own-session-only`.
- Under `deny`, reject a `send` whose actor is `agent` and whose target session isn't the caller's own, with a clear error.

A caller can of course spoof or omit the header — this is an accident-and-audit guardrail on a trusted host, not an authentication boundary. If that's too weak to be worth it, an explicit note in the docs that same-host agents can message each other by design would be just as useful to integrators.

## Environment

- Checked against `origin/main` @ `f7e0fe6`.
- Found while auditing a third-party harness that runs multiple concurrent AO sessions; not reporting a live incident.

title: Chat session cannot resume after its controller stops
body:
## Summary

When a Chat-mode agent controller stops, the desktop can show **The agent controller stopped**, but clicking **Resume agent** fails with:

> The agent is still running; only exited agents can be resumed (AGENT_NOT_EXITED)

This leaves the preserved conversation unrecoverable from the advertised recovery action.

![Controller stopped banner and AGENT_NOT_EXITED error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-controller-resume-conflict/docs/issue-assets/chat-controller-resume-conflict.png)

## Source

Reported from the desktop app in a local user session on 2026-08-07/08. No public chat URL is available. The screenshot above is the original report attachment.

Analyzed against `main` at `f7e0fe65bd6fda711f39642798c70b9f0da248df`.

## Reproduction

1. Start and use a Chat-mode agent session.
2. Let the Chat controller stream close without a successfully projected explicit `chat.controller.stopped` event (or let it stop while lifecycle activity is `blocked`).
3. Observe the controller-stopped recovery banner.
4. Click **Resume agent**.

## Expected

The stopped Chat controller is reflected as exited lifecycle activity, and **Resume agent** relaunches the Chat controller using the preserved provider conversation.

## Actual

The durable session may remain `idle`, `active`, or `blocked`, so resume rejects it with `AGENT_NOT_EXITED`. Even if activity is corrected to `exited`, Chat resume then fails because the generic resume path requires a terminal runtime handle, which Chat sessions intentionally do not have.

## Root cause

High confidence, backed by focused failing regression tests:

1. `service/chat.Controller.project` marks only its in-memory controller state stopped when the provider event stream closes; it does not report lifecycle `exited` unless an explicit stopped event was projected first.
2. Lifecycle tool precedence suppresses `chat.controller.stopped` while the current activity is `blocked`, because that event is not classified as a turn boundary.
3. `session_manager.ResumeAgentWithMode` unconditionally requires a `RuntimeHandleID`, even though Chat-mode sessions intentionally launch without terminal runtime handles.
4. Existing sessions already stuck in a non-exited durable state need safe reconciliation: recovery should be permitted only when the Chat controller registry confirms there is no live controller.

## Proposed fix

- Always report lifecycle `exited` when a Chat controller event stream ends.
- Treat `chat.controller.stopped` as a lifecycle turn-boundary event so it can clear `blocked` state.
- Make resume preconditions mode-aware: retain terminal runtime-handle requirements for TUI, but relaunch Chat without one.
- For stale pre-fix records, allow Chat recovery only when no live controller exists; continue returning `AGENT_NOT_EXITED` for a genuinely live controller.
- Add focused tests at the Chat controller, lifecycle, and session-manager boundaries.

## Impact

Affected users cannot recover some Chat sessions from the desktop despite the UI explicitly offering **Resume agent**. The workaround is to abandon the preserved session and start another one or manually open a shell.

## Related, not duplicate

- #3360 — parent structured Chat-mode work
- #3087 — broader remaining session lifecycle correctness gaps

title: fix: recover Chat sessions after controller stops
body:
## What

- report Chat lifecycle `exited` whenever the provider event stream ends, including abrupt disconnects without a final controller-state event
- allow `chat.controller.stopped` to clear sticky `blocked` activity
- make agent resume mode-aware so Chat sessions relaunch their provider conversation without a terminal runtime handle
- recover stale pre-fix Chat activity only when no live controller exists, and wait for a stopped controller's final cleanup before replacement

## Why

The desktop can correctly show **The agent controller stopped** while **Resume agent** fails with `AGENT_NOT_EXITED`. Some sessions remain durably idle/active/blocked after their Chat controller dies; sessions that do reach exited then fail the TUI-only runtime-handle precondition.

Fixes #3710.

## How

The controller's provider-stream closure now emits the same generation-fenced lifecycle signal as an explicit stopped event. Lifecycle treats that event as a turn boundary so a dead controller cannot remain blocked.

Session Manager keeps TUI resume semantics unchanged. For Chat, the in-memory controller registry prevents duplicate recovery of a live controller and permits stale durable rows to recover when no controller remains. The Chat service distinguishes a stopped registry entry from a usable controller and waits for its projector cleanup before launching the replacement generation.

No frontend or API contract changes are required; the existing recovery action works once daemon state and resume semantics agree.
