title: New-task composer discovers TUI-only agents only after failed Chat spawn
body:
## Bug

When Chat is the default session interface and a user selects a TUI-only agent such as Cursor, the new-task composer sends a guaranteed-to-fail Chat request. It then renders the raw SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED backend error and only afterward offers Create as Terminal UI.

AO already knows Cursor is TUI-only before submission, so the composer should choose the supported interface automatically.

![Cursor selected, followed by a raw unsupported-Chat error and delayed Terminal UI fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-proactive-chat-tui-fallback/.issue-assets/proactive-chat-tui-fallback/report.png)

**Source:** local desktop report on 2026-08-08 (no public chat URL)  
**Reported by:** local user  
**Analyzed against:** f7e0fe65bd6fda711f39642798c70b9f0da248df  
**AO version:** dev  
**Platform:** macOS arm64  
**Priority:** medium  
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Set the default session interface to Chat.
2. Open the new-task composer.
3. Select Cursor, which has no Chat driver.
4. Choose Start task.
5. Observe SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED and the delayed Terminal UI retry.

## Root Cause

- The daemon already returns defaultSessionMode and chatHarnesses from GET /api/v1/settings.
- TaskComposer did not consume that capability metadata.
- It only offered TUI after the delegate request returned a typed Chat preflight error.

## Fix

- Resolve the effective interface from defaultSessionMode, chatHarnesses, and the selected agent before submission.
- If Chat is the default but the selected agent has no Chat driver, send the delegate request once with mode tui.
- Keep the ordinary Start task UI; do not show a warning or alternate action.
- Preserve the existing server-error fallback for stale or unavailable capability metadata.

The backend contract remains explicit: the frontend sends mode tui rather than asking the backend to silently reinterpret a Chat request.

## Impact

- Removes a guaranteed failed request and raw backend error.
- Starts TUI-only agents in one click.
- Keeps interface selection out of the way when there is only one supported option.

## Related

- #3360 — Chat and TUI interface architecture
- #3472 — Chat UI and typed post-failure recovery

title: fix(opencode): detect agent exit via AO's process supervisor
body:
## Problem

The `opencode` adapter does not implement `ports.AgentExitDetector`, so it falls back to runtime-only liveness.

AO launches every seat as:

```
bash -c '<agent> ...; exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -i'
```

The trailing interactive shell is deliberate — it keeps the pane usable after the agent finishes. But it means the tmux pane **outlives the agent process**, so `tmux has-session` keeps answering "alive" long after `opencode` has exited or been killed.

Consequences observed on a worker seat whose agent was killed:

- the reaper never observes a dead worker, so the session is never marked terminated;
- `session restore` then refuses the session as not-restorable, because AO still believes it is alive;
- the seat is effectively unrecoverable without manual intervention.

Fixes #2089.

## Fix

Opt `opencode` into `AgentExitDetectionSupervisor`, exactly as the `codex` adapter already does (`adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`). The launch argv is then wrapped in `ao agent-process supervise`, which reports the real process exit back to the daemon, and `RuntimeLaunchID` is populated so the workload-death signal is no longer fenced off.

This is the mechanism AO already ships; the adapter simply was not opted in.

## Verification

Built from this branch and run as an isolated daemon (separate port, data dir, run file and `TMUX_TMPDIR`), against a scratch git repo:

1. Spawned an `opencode` worker seat; confirmed it did real work in its worktree.
2. `kill -9` on the `opencode` process.
3. **Before the patch:** session stayed `running` indefinitely; the tmux pane was still alive, and `has-session` still reported alive.
4. **After the patch:** session moved to `exited` within a few seconds of the kill, while the pane remained (as intended).
5. The seat could then be recovered in place via `POST /sessions/{id}/activity {"state":"exited"}` followed by `POST /sessions/{id}/resume-agent`, and the resumed agent wrote a new file into the preserved worktree — so the session became genuinely restorable, not merely relabelled.

`go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/...` passes, including the added case.

## Notes

- No behaviour change for any other adapter.
- One incidental finding while testing, reported separately rather than folded in here: `respawnPaneArgs` targets `<session>:0.0` unconditionally, so on a machine with `base-index 1` / `pane-base-index 1` in `~/.tmux.conf` the pane is `1.1`, and `resume-agent` fails with `can't find window: 0`. That is independent of this fix and needs its own change (a tmux target that does not assume index 0, e.g. `{start}.{top-left}`); happy to open a separate PR for it.

title: ao project set-config silently discards unspecified config (full replace, no warning)
body:
## Summary

`ao project set-config` is a **full replace**, not a merge. Any field not supplied in the invocation is reset to its zero value, silently discarding config that is already set. Because the command succeeds and prints no warning, the loss is invisible until a later session behaves differently.

This is easy to hit while a project has running sessions: changing one setting (say a model) drops unrelated settings (env, worker config, setup commands) for every session started afterwards.

## Reproduction

```
# 1. establish a config with two independent settings
ao project set-config <project> \
  --config-json '{"agentConfig":{"model":"<model-a>"},"worker":{"agentConfig":{"model":"<model-a>"}}}' \
  --env "SOME_VAR=hello"

ao project get-config <project>     # both present

# 2. later, change only the model
ao project set-config <project> \
  --config-json '{"agentConfig":{"model":"<model-b>"}}'

ao project get-config <project>
```

**Expected:** model updated to `<model-b>`; `SOME_VAR` and the worker block untouched.

**Actual:** model is `<model-b>`, and `SOME_VAR` and the entire `worker` block are gone. Exit code 0, no warning.

## Cause

`buildProjectConfig` (`internal/cli/project.go`) constructs a fresh config object from the flags provided on this invocation and writes it wholesale; there is no read-modify-write against the stored config. The help text does say "Replace a project's per-project config", so the behaviour is intentional — but the failure mode is silent and unbounded, which is what makes it dangerous.

## Impact

The destructive case is not a typo, it is a routine one-setting change. With sessions already running against the project, the operator has no signal that anything else was dropped; the next spawned session simply picks up a different environment. Recovering requires knowing what the config used to be, which nothing records.

## Suggested fix

Any one of these would remove the silent-loss property:

1. **Merge by default**, with an explicit `--replace` flag for the current behaviour. Most consistent with how the command is actually used.
2. Keep replace semantics but **print what is being dropped** and require confirmation (or `--yes`) when the write removes previously-set keys.
3. At minimum, **warn loudly** when a replace discards non-empty fields, and mention the replace semantics in the command's short help rather than only the long description.

Option 1 with 2 as the safety net for `--replace` seems the best balance; happy to send a PR if you have a preference on which way you want it to go.

## Environment

- Reproduced against a local build of `main`.
- Linux, single-repo project.

title: Run Review fails after a second daemon hot-migrates the shared SQLite database
body:
## Bug

Clicking **Run review** can fail with `Review operation failed (REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED)` when a newer daemon has used the same `AO_DATA_DIR` and migrated SQLite while an older daemon remains alive. The failure occurs before AO creates either a `review` or `review_run` row.

**Source:** local AO desktop report | **Reported by:** @illegalcall | **Date:** 2026-08-08  
**Analyzed against:** `f7e0fe65b` (`origin/main`)  
**Running desktop daemon:** `fc5f4ca0219c2b9e11d2982d34598e3d80320d77` with `vcs.modified=true`, `ao version dev`  
**Confidence:** High — the live binary's embedded SQL, the applied schema, migration/daemon timestamps, and SQLite's exact prepare-time failure all line up.

![Run Review shows REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-review-shared-db-migration-20260808/.issue-assets/review-shared-db-migration/run-review-failed.png)

## Environment

- macOS / Darwin 25.5.0, arm64
- Primary daemon healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`, started `2026-08-07T15:11:21Z`
- Claude Code `2.1.225`
- A second daemon was recorded against the same database on port `3012` at `2026-08-08T06:56:16Z`
- Migration `0080_review_per_harness.sql` was recorded as applied at that exact timestamp
- Affected worker: `agent-orchestrator-1-70`, PR [#3711](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3711), selected reviewer `claude-code`

## Reproduction

Use a temporary data directory; do not test this against production data.

1. Start a daemon built before migration 0080 with a temporary `AO_DATA_DIR`, port, and run file.
2. Start a current daemon with the **same** `AO_DATA_DIR` but a different `AO_PORT` and `AO_RUN_FILE`.
3. Let the current daemon apply migration 0080, then stop it while leaving the old daemon alive.
4. In the UI served by the old daemon, select a worker with an open PR and click **Run review**.
5. Observe HTTP 500 / `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED`; no review row or run is persisted.

Observed locally without issuing another review:

- `GET /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-1-70/reviews` returns the PR as `needs_review`.
- The running daemon binary contains:

  ```sql
  INSERT INTO review (...)
  VALUES (...)
  ON CONFLICT (session_id) DO UPDATE SET ...
  ```

- The migrated table now has `UNIQUE(session_id, harness)` and no unique constraint on `session_id` alone.
- Preparing the old statement against the live DB fails deterministically with:

  ```text
  ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint
  ```

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:84-101` guards daemon ownership through the configured run file, then opens/migrates `cfg.DataDir`. A second daemon with a different run file/port but the same data directory can therefore pass the ownership check and mutate the schema underneath the first daemon.

This configuration is reachable in the documented desktop real-data workflow: `.agents/skills/ao-desktop-dev/SKILL.md:14-16,56-65` explicitly runs a separate dev daemon on its own port/run file while pointing `AO_DATA_DIR` at the real database.

Migration `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0080_review_per_harness.sql:13-24` rebuilds `review` with `UNIQUE(session_id, harness)`. Current generated SQL correctly targets that pair (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/review.sql:1-9`), but a live pre-migration daemon continues using `ON CONFLICT (session_id)`. SQLite rejects that statement during review upsert, before a run is created.

Finally, `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/reviews.go:352-361` turns every unexpected service/storage error into the generic `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED` response, so the UI (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx:1187-1196`) has no actionable recovery information.

## Fix

- Acquire and retain an exclusive, **data-directory-scoped** daemon lock before opening or migrating SQLite. The lock must be independent of `AO_PORT` and `AO_RUN_FILE` so two daemons cannot own one database.
- Make the real-data desktop-dev path attach to/restart the owning daemon or refuse to launch against a live data directory; do not run a second migrator over it.
- Add a regression test with two daemon configs sharing `AO_DATA_DIR` but using distinct run files/ports.
- As defense in depth, detect an externally advanced/incompatible schema and stop serving with an actionable restart message. Log the internal review error with the request ID even if the API response remains generic.

## Impact

- The code-review workflow is blocked until the stale daemon is restarted with a schema-compatible binary.
- The same mechanism can break any old query invalidated by a newer migration, so the risk is broader than reviews.
- **Priority: P2** — significant degradation with a restart/workflow-isolation workaround; bounded here to mixed-version daemons sharing one data directory.

## Related

- [#2481](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2481) — concurrent checkout identity errors are masked in the desktop UI; related surface, but that issue assumes the second daemon is rejected.
- [#2845](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2845) — prior dev-daemon port/data isolation decision.
- [PR #3384](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3384) — current interactive-reviewer merge containing migration 0080 on `main`.

title: TUI-to-Chat drain can wait forever after non-submitting terminal input
body:
## Bug

Switching an idle Terminal UI session to Chat UI with the drain policy can remain at **Waiting to switch…** forever when terminal input is newer than the last durable idle activity fact.

**Source:** Interactive report with screenshot on 2026-08-08  
**Analyzed against:** `f7e0fe65bd6f`  
**Priority:** P2 — interface switching is significantly degraded, but Cancel and Stop now remain safe workarounds.  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced with a permanent regression test and traced through the terminal input barrier and session transition loop.

## Reproduction

1. Open an idle Codex session in Terminal UI.
2. Type and erase a character at the composer without submitting a turn, leaving the composer visibly idle.
3. Select **Switch to Chat UI**.
4. Observe the transition remain in the draining phase with **Waiting to switch…** indefinitely.

## Root Cause

`BeginInputDrain` correctly records the newest terminal input accepted before closing the input gate. The TUI drain then rejects an idle activity fact older than that barrier, because buffered PTY input could still be processing.

Codex does not emit a new activity hook for non-submitting input, and same-state idle reconciliation does not refresh the idle timestamp. The drain loop therefore had neither a second authoritative idle signal nor a deadline for this contradictory stale-idle state. Trusting the old row would be unsafe because a just-submitted turn could be destroyed; waiting only for a newer row causes the permanent hang.

## Expected

The transition should either prove the source is quiescent and switch, or fail safely while leaving the source controller available. It must not wait forever or infer runtime death from a failed probe.

## Fix

- Gate terminal input before checking quiescence.
- Preserve the existing path for an idle fact newer than the last accepted input.
- For a contradictory stale-idle row, wait for a post-input quiet window and require three consecutive adapter-confirmed idle samples.
- Use one cumulative five-second deadline for terminal capture and runtime liveness checks.
- On unresolved ambiguity, fail with `DRAIN_QUIESCENCE_UNVERIFIED`, release the input gate, and leave the source running.
- Keep reported active turns and user-paced decisions unbounded and cancellable.

## Intentional Scope

No confirmation dialog or unsent-draft warning is part of this fix. Draft policy remains unchanged.

## Verification

Session-manager tests cover the stale-idle reproduction through the detector port, fresh durable idle facts, unavailable and ambiguous detection, alternating samples, the liveness deadline, confirmed runtime exit, input-gate release, cancellation, source preservation, and Active/WaitingInput/Blocked states. Existing Codex adapter tests continue to cover idle, working, approval, and ambiguous terminal markers.

title: fix(session): prevent stale-idle interface drain hangs
body:
## What

Prevent TUI-to-Chat drain transitions from waiting forever when accepted terminal input is newer than the last durable idle fact.

## Why

The input gate correctly rejects that stale idle row because buffered PTY input might still submit work. Non-submitting Codex input produces no newer hook, however, so the transition previously had no safe proof path and no bound.

Fixes #3718.

## How

- preserve the existing fresh-idle path
- for contradictory stale idle, wait for input to settle and require three consecutive adapter-confirmed idle samples
- give terminal capture and runtime liveness checks one cumulative five-second proof deadline
- fail with `DRAIN_QUIESCENCE_UNVERIFIED` while releasing the input gate and leaving the source controller untouched
- keep Active, WaitingInput, and Blocked drains unbounded and cancellable

The detector stays behind the existing port with a package-local test fake. The only configurable values are the three timings tests need to shorten. There are no frontend, API, storage, or adapter behavior changes.

title: Chat timeline shows image attachments as file paths instead of previews
body:
## Bug

When a PNG is attached to a message in a chat-mode session, the composer stages it successfully and the agent can read it, but the human message in AO's transcript shows AO's generated attachment instruction and workspace-relative file path as literal text. The transcript never renders the image.

**Source:** In-app AO chat report on 2026-08-08  
**Reported by:** AO desktop user  
**Analyzed against:** `f7e0fe65bd6f` (`origin/main`, frontend `0.10.3`, daemon version `dev`)  
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64; verified Go daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P2 — the attachment still reaches the agent, but the visible conversation is degraded and the only workaround is opening the staged path separately.  
**Confidence:** High — a deterministic renderer regression test exercises the exact persisted message shape and fails because the human-message component emits text only.

![Chat message rendering the attachment as a path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-image-attachment-path/.issue-assets/chat-image-attachment-path/attachment-path-in-chat.png)

## Reproduction

1. Open a chat-mode AO session.
2. Paste, drop, or choose a PNG in the chat composer.
3. Send the message.
4. Inspect the human message in the conversation timeline.

### Actual

The bubble contains text like:

```text
Attached files (read these files in the workspace):
- .ao/attachments/attachment-d9014f798f.png
```

No image element is rendered.

### Expected

AO should render staged image references as inline image previews while retaining the file in the worktree for the agent.

## Deterministic repro

```bash
cd frontend
npm test -- src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.test.tsx -t "renders staged image references in human messages as images"
```

The test fails with `Unable to find an accessible element with the role "img"` and shows the generated reference block as the bubble's complete DOM text.

## Root Cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx` intentionally appends staged paths to the outgoing text because worktree files are the provider-neutral delivery mechanism.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` exposes conversation messages with `text` but no structured display attachment metadata.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx` renders `HumanMessage.message.text` verbatim and does not recognize AO's generated attachment suffix.
- The existing workspace-confined `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/preview/files/*` route can serve the bytes, but the packaged renderer CSP currently does not allow loopback image sources.
- Spawned prompts use the closely related header `Attached files (read these files in the workspace for context):`, so both AO-generated variants need coverage.

## Fix

Parse only AO's terminal attachment-reference block in human messages, render supported staged image types through the existing session preview-file route, show non-image attachments as file labels, and preserve malformed or ordinary user text unchanged. Pass the session ID through the timeline and allow the already-trusted loopback daemon origin in `img-src`. Add regression coverage for both generated header variants and URL encoding.

## Impact

- Images still reach agents, so there is no data loss.
- Users cannot visually verify which screenshot/image they sent from the transcript.
- Image-only messages appear as internal implementation instructions rather than the intended content.

## Related

- [#2722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2722) — original task-composer attachment request; adjacent composer behavior, not transcript rendering.
- [#3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — structured Chat/TUI session work that introduced the current chat surface.

title: docs: move README translations into translations/
body:
## What

Moves the seven translated READMEs out of the repo root into a dedicated `translations/` folder, and relocates the language switcher row into the centered header block of every README.

## Why

The repo root carried eight `README*.md` files. On GitHub's file listing they crowd out the actual project directories, and it isn't obvious which one GitHub renders. Grouping the translations under one folder keeps the root to a single `README.md`.

Separately, the language row sat *outside* the `<div align="center">` header, so it rendered left-aligned and orphaned between the hero screenshot and the first `---` — easy for a non-English reader to scroll past.

## How

- `git mv README.<lang>.md translations/` for `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN` (detected as renames, not delete+add).
- Rewrote relative paths inside the moved files: `LICENSE`, `docs/*`, `assets/*`, `frontend/*` links and image `src` attributes are now `../`-prefixed. Sibling language links stay relative within `translations/`.
- Root `README.md` language row now points at `translations/README.<lang>.md`; translated files point back at `../README.md`.
- Moved the language row inside `<div align="center">`, directly under the badge block, so it renders centered and above the fold.
- Dropped the `**Languages:**` label. It was hardcoded English in every localized README; the language names identify themselves without it.

No content translation changes — only paths and placement.

## Testing

- Grepped the repo for references to the moved filenames: only the READMEs themselves referenced them. No workflow, script, `package.json`, or `.gitattributes` entry points at them.
- Verified every relative link and image `src` in the moved files resolves from `translations/`.
- `git diff --numstat` shows 45 changed lines per translated file (link rewrites + header row) and 2 in the root README — no incidental reflow or line-ending churn.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(browser): prevent cancel-frame race from flaking Go CI
body:
## Bug

The race-enabled Go suite can intermittently fail because `TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame` times out waiting for the browser runtime cancel frame. The same race can leave an Electron browser command running after its caller has canceled the request.

**Source:** [failed `main` Go run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/31251765230) after [PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) merged  
**Failure commit:** `b264e7765`  
**Reproduced against:** `a3fbf8850`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P2 — intermittent CI failure and bounded browser-command cancellation leak; rerunning CI is a workaround.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd backend
GOMAXPROCS=1 go test -race ./internal/browserruntime \
  -run '^TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame$' -count=300
```

The original test failed twice in an initial 100-iteration run. Independent 300-iteration runs failed under `GOMAXPROCS=1`, `2`, and `8`. A deterministic `net.Pipe` regression reproduces it by pausing immediately after the runtime receives the command bytes and canceling before the broker's write call returns.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/browserruntime/broker.go` checks `ctx.Err()` after the complete command frame has already been written. If cancellation lands in that narrow interval, `write` reports `context.Canceled`; `Broker.Execute` treats the command as unsent and returns through its early write-error path, so it never emits the required cancel frame.

The write-interrupt `context.AfterFunc` also was not joined before the connection deadline was cleared, allowing its expired deadline to race with the next write.

[PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) did not introduce this code; its merge run exposed the pre-existing race from [PR #3066](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3066).

## Fix

- Treat a fully delivered frame as a successful write even when cancellation arrives concurrently, so `Execute` reaches its cancellation branch and sends the correlated cancel frame.
- Wait for an already-started deadline-interrupt callback before clearing the connection deadline.
- Replace the timing-dependent cancellation test with a deterministic post-delivery interleaving.

## Impact

- Removes a flaky failure from required Go CI.
- Ensures a delivered browser command receives a cancel frame when its request context is canceled.

## Related

- [PR #3066](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3066) — introduced the browser runtime bridge.
- [PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) — unrelated merge whose `main` run exposed the flake.

title: fix(browser): preserve cancel frames after delivered writes
body:
Fixes #3732

## Summary

- preserve a successful browser-runtime write when request cancellation arrives after the complete command frame has been delivered
- wait for an already-started write-deadline interrupt before clearing the connection deadline
- make the cancel-frame regression deterministic by pausing immediately after the fake runtime receives the command bytes

## Root cause

`Broker.write` checked `ctx.Err()` after writing the complete command frame. If cancellation landed between delivery and the write returning, `Execute` treated the command as unsent and exited through its write-error path without emitting a cancel frame. The runtime could keep executing the browser command, and `TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame` intermittently timed out.

[PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) did not introduce the bug; its [`main` Go run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/31251765230) exposed the pre-existing race from the browser bridge.

## Test

```bash
cd backend
go test -race ./internal/browserruntime -run '^TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame$' -count=1000
go test -race ./internal/browserruntime -count=100
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test -race -p 4 -count=1 ./...
cd ..
GOFLAGS=-p=4 npm run lint
```

## Risk

Low. The change is limited to the daemon's serialized browser-runtime write path. Incomplete writes retain the existing context/error behavior; only fully delivered frames are treated as successful so `Execute` can send their correlated cancellation.

title: fix: align Chat recovery with TUI lifecycle
body:
## What

- make Chat controller startup follow TUI's prepare/start/commit/release ordering
- publish connecting-controller ownership before any fallible post-provider work, while gating provider event projection until `MarkSpawned` commits the generation
- distinguish controller liveness from registry ownership so stopped or failed-to-close controllers still prevent duplicate recovery and workspace teardown
- treat every authoritative `ActivityExited` signal as a lifecycle turn boundary, independent of whether TUI or Chat reported it
- align Chat kill, restore, resume, and failed-spawn cleanup with TUI's one-controller and workspace-safety rules

Follow-up to #3711. Fixes parity and rollback gaps found while comparing that recovery path directly with TUI lifecycle behavior. Relates to #3710.

## TUI parity

| Lifecycle invariant | TUI | Chat after this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One controller owns the session | runtime handle and launch generation | controller registry owner and controller generation |
| Signals cannot beat durable launch commit | pending-launch gate | connecting controller plus activation gate |
| Durable launch completion | `MarkSpawned` records runtime metadata | `ControllerReady` calls the same `MarkSpawned` with provider metadata |
| Authoritative death signal | process supervisor/reaper emits `ActivityExited` | provider event-stream closure emits `ActivityExited` |
| Failed stop protects workspace | runtime destroy must succeed before teardown | registry ownership must be released before teardown |
| Duplicate recovery is rejected | live runtime/generation guard | live or cleanup-owning controller guard |

The mechanisms remain adapter-specific: TUI has a terminal runtime and reaper; Chat has a provider process, conversation ID, controller registry, and event stream. The durable lifecycle ordering and safety invariants are now shared.

## Behavior covered

- a provider event emitted immediately at startup cannot overwrite or precede `MarkSpawned`
- commands cannot reach a connecting, uncommitted controller
- an uncommitted generation's buffered provider events are discarded
- a generation-claim or lifecycle-commit failure retains ownership if provider close times out
- a second start/restore cannot create another provider writer while ownership remains
- failed spawn or kill cannot destroy a workspace still owned by a provider
- stream closure clears blocked state through generic exited semantics
- stale pre-#3711 Chat rows remain recoverable when no controller owner exists

## Testing

- `GOFLAGS=-p=1 npm run lint` — pass, 0 issues
- `cd backend && go build ./...` — pass
- `cd backend && go test -race -p 1 ./internal/service/chat ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/session_manager ./internal/daemon` — pass
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — pass

## Checklist

- [x] Based on current `main`
- [x] Focused follow-up to #3711
- [x] Regression tests cover lifecycle ordering, duplicate ownership, failed cleanup, and workspace preservation
- [x] No frontend or API contract changes

title: fix: recover Codex interface switch readiness
body:
## Summary

- invoke Codex lifecycle hooks with the running AO executable's absolute, shell-quoted path, so Codex's login shell cannot redirect callbacks to a stale or foreign `ao`
- recheck only the transient `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` interface status, allowing **Switch to chat UI** to enable as soon as a successful `SessionStart` hook records the thread id
- implement Codex's native-history probe so a reserved UUID with no active rollout starts fresh instead of issuing a doomed `thread/resume`

## RCA

Three independent gaps produced two similar-looking symptoms:

1. **The native id never arrives for some users.** Codex runs command hooks through the user's login shell. AO previously emitted bare `ao hooks codex ...` commands and only prepended the daemon directory to the child process's inherited `PATH`. A login-shell startup file can replace or reorder that `PATH`; the hook then invokes another AO installation (or no AO), exits, and never records the native Codex thread id. This depends on each user's shell setup, which explains why only some users reproduce it indefinitely.
2. **The renderer can cache an early missing-id response.** Even when the hook succeeds, the initial interface-status request can race the asynchronous `SessionStart` callback. The query returned `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`, but idle status queries did not refetch, leaving the button stale until some unrelated remount/refetch.
3. **A UUID is not necessarily resumable history.** Codex app-server can reserve and return a thread UUID before the first user turn writes an active rollout. AO treated every non-empty Codex UUID as resumable, passed an unmaterialized id to `thread/resume`, and surfaced `no rollout found for thread id ...`.

## Why the earlier fixes did not cover this

- #170 prepended AO's daemon directory to the spawned session `PATH`. That helps ordinary child-process lookup, but it does not survive a login shell that reconstructs `PATH` before running a hook.
- #3711 recovers a stopped Chat controller. It does not make a missing Codex rollout resumable and therefore cannot fix `no rollout found`.
- #3719 prevents a stale-idle transition drain from hanging. It is a separate transition-lifecycle failure.
- #3717 changes frontend chat links/text selection and is unrelated.

## Reproduction and evidence

### Real desktop reproduction on `main`

1. Launch the actual AO Electron app against an isolated data directory.
2. Start a Codex 0.147 TUI session and send `Reply with only OK`.
3. Observe Codex return `OK`, while **Switch to chat UI** remains disabled and Activity shows **No Signal**.
4. In the reproduced shell, `zsh -lc 'command -v ao'` resolves a stale package-manager shim; invoking it exits 1 because its old module target no longer exists. Therefore the `SessionStart` callback never reaches this daemon.
5. To isolate the second bug, record the valid native id directly. The daemon then reports `{supported:true,targetMode:"chat"}`, but the already-mounted UI remains disabled because it never refetches the earlier `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` result.

### Real desktop verification on this branch

1. Start the same Codex flow from the fixed app.
2. Inspect the live launch command: every Codex hook contains the absolute daemon executable and the isolated daemon run-file environment.
3. Send the same prompt. The real `SessionStart` callback records the native id, the button becomes enabled, and Activity becomes **Idle**.
4. Click **Switch to chat UI**. The transition completes and Chat UI displays the original `Reply with only OK` prompt and `OK` response. The reverse **Switch to terminal UI** control is enabled.

### Automated regression evidence

- Before the absolute-path implementation, the launch/restore command tests failed because the generated hook command still contained bare `ao hooks ...`; after the change, the same tests pass with the current AO executable embedded.
- The renderer regression test starts at `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`, advances the mocked daemon to `supported: true`, and proves the hook refetches exactly once. A second test proves permanently unsupported harnesses are not polled.
- Session-manager tests prove a missing Codex rollout uses the fresh-conversation sentinel, while a non-empty active `.jsonl` rollout preserves the native id.
- Adapter tests additionally cover missing, zero-byte, archived, active, and compressed active rollout files.

## Change-by-change necessity

| Change | Required? | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Absolute, shell-quoted AO hook executable | Yes | Fixes the indefinite, user-specific failure where no native id is ever recorded. Quoting is required for packaged paths such as `Agent Orchestrator.app`. |
| Error propagation from launch/restore | Yes | A session launched without working tracking hooks recreates the same unrecoverable disabled state. Failing the launch is safer and diagnosable. |
| Targeted one-second `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` poll | Yes | Absolute hooks can still finish after the first HTTP read; polling closes that legitimate async race. It stops immediately when ready and never runs for permanently unsupported harnesses. |
| Codex active-rollout probe | Yes | Prevents `thread/resume` from receiving an id that Codex has reserved but cannot resume. |
| Missing/zero-byte/archived vs active/compressed tests | Yes | These are the exact provider states that decide whether continuity is safe. |
| Frontend permanent-unsupported test | Yes | Guards the UX/performance boundary: Cursor and other unsupported harnesses must not begin background polling. |

No API, schema, storage, or UI-component change is needed.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/codex ./internal/session_manager -count=1`
- `go test ./...` (via the repository lint command)
- focused `golangci-lint` for the changed backend packages: `0 issues`
- `npm test -- --run src/renderer/hooks/useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run package` (production Electron bundles and macOS package)
- actual AO Electron + Codex 0.147 TUI-to-Chat handoff against isolated data

The repository-wide linter process also scanned stale sibling worktrees on this machine and reported pre-existing/generated findings from those other paths. The changed packages themselves lint clean, and CI remains the clean-checkout authority.

title: bug(agent-claude-code): post-Stop `agent_needs_input` notification overwrites Idle with sticky `waiting_input` — sessions freeze indefinitely
body:
## Bug

A Claude Code session that finishes a turn **without asking anything** gets flipped to `waiting_input` roughly 60 seconds later, and — because that state is sticky — stays there forever. The session is then invisible to automated delivery and only a human can free it.

This is **not** the `idle_prompt` conflation of #2525 / #2047. Those describe `idle_prompt` mapping to `waiting_input`, and that remap has landed. The type responsible here is `agent_needs_input`, and the defect survives the #2525 fix.

**Analyzed against:** `66821b3f` (main) · **Confidence:** high — phenomenon measured from persisted activity history; notification type confirmed against the shipped binary.

## Evidence

Across a long-running deployment's activity history:

- **233 distinct sessions** show at least one `idle → waiting_input` transition.
- **737 such transitions** total; **721 (97.8%)** land in a **55–70 s window** after the preceding Stop-derived `idle`, clustered at **60.1–60.2 s** with almost no variance.
- It reproduces on **three different model backends**, including two non-Anthropic ones reached via a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. The trigger is therefore a **client-side timer**, independent of anything the model emitted.

A representative case, reconstructed from the session's own transcript:

```
11:28:53.995  stop hook fires        → activity=idle          (correct)
11:28:53.998  transcript ends on a completion statement — no question asked
11:29:54.1    notification hook      → activity=waiting_input (phantom, +60.12s)
              ... session never moves again
```

The transcript's final entry is a statement that the work is finished. No question, no prompt, no permission dialog.

### Why the notification type is `agent_needs_input`, not `idle_prompt`

The persisted telemetry records only the resulting state, so the type was confirmed against the shipped daemon binary directly:

```
$ for s in idle_prompt agent_needs_input permission_prompt; do \
    echo "$s: $(LC_ALL=C grep -a -o -c "$s" /path/to/ao)"; done
idle_prompt:       0
agent_needs_input: 1
permission_prompt: 1
```

`idle_prompt` does not occur in the binary at all. Since `notificationState()` is a total mapping and only `agent_needs_input` yields `ActivityWaitingInput`, the observed state proves the type received. The same conclusion holds at `66821b3f`, where `idle_prompt` maps to `ActivityIdle`.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/activity.go` — `notificationState()` maps `agent_needs_input` to `ActivityWaitingInput` **unconditionally**, with no reference to what the session was already known to be doing:

```go
case "agent_needs_input":
    return domain.ActivityWaitingInput, true
```

Two properties turn that into a permanent stall:

1. **It is sticky.** `domain/activity.go`, `IsSticky()` returns true for `waiting_input`, so nothing ages it out. `NeedsInput()` also returns true, so the session renders as `needs_input`.
2. **It suppresses automated delivery.** Any lifecycle path that gates on the session being idle before delivering a queued event will refuse to deliver to a `waiting_input` session, so a coordinator session in this state stops receiving the events that would otherwise wake it.

**AO holds strictly more information than the notification carries.** It has already observed the `stop` hook for that turn, and no `user-prompt-submit` has arrived since — so there is no new turn in flight and no question can have been asked. A notification claiming otherwise contradicts AO's own record.

The codebase already has precedence machinery for exactly this class of problem. The comment at `activity.go:23-32` documents that tool events "never demote a sticky state, EXCEPT the post of the exact tool whose permission dialog blocked the session" — a rule added because naive mapping let subagent traffic clear a live `blocked`. The analogous guard is simply missing on the notification path.

## Impact

Beyond cosmetic status noise: on this deployment, **five long-lived coordinator sessions were frozen in phantom `waiting_input` for ~23 hours**, each with an identical signature after a restart —

```
idle → active (+18.4-18.6 s) → waiting_input (+60.2 s) → no further events
```

None of them had done any work. Each booted, took one startup turn, and was frozen 60.2 s later. Work routed through those coordinators silently stopped.

## Reproduction

Deterministic, via the same CLI hook path the harness uses. **Use a throwaway session** — this mutates real session state:

```bash
export AO_SESSION_ID=<throwaway-session-id>

echo '{}' | ao hooks claude-code stop
ao session get "$AO_SESSION_ID" --json | jq -r '.activity.state'   # => idle   (correct)

echo '{"notification_type":"agent_needs_input"}' | ao hooks claude-code notification
ao session get "$AO_SESSION_ID" --json | jq -r '.activity.state'   # => waiting_input
```

**Actual:** `waiting_input`, sticky, with no user prompt in between and no question asked.
**Expected:** the notification is ignored (or recorded non-stickily); the session stays `idle` because AO already knows the turn ended and no new turn began.

Organic equivalent: let any Claude Code session finish a turn without asking a question and sit untouched for ~65 s.

### Acceptance command

Exits 0 when fixed, non-zero while the defect is present:

```bash
export AO_SESSION_ID=<throwaway-session-id>
echo '{}' | ao hooks claude-code stop
echo '{"notification_type":"agent_needs_input"}' | ao hooks claude-code notification
ao session get "$AO_SESSION_ID" --json | jq -e '.activity.state != "waiting_input"'
```

### Field diagnostic

To find affected sessions in an existing deployment (public `change_log` schema only):

```sql
SELECT session_id, count(*) AS flips FROM (
  SELECT session_id,
         LAG(json_extract(payload,'$.activity')) OVER w AS prev,
         json_extract(payload,'$.activity')              AS cur,
         (julianday(created_at) - julianday(LAG(created_at) OVER w)) * 86400 AS gap
  FROM change_log WHERE event_type='session_updated'
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY seq)
)
WHERE prev='idle' AND cur='waiting_input' AND gap BETWEEN 55 AND 70
GROUP BY session_id ORDER BY flips DESC;
```

## Suggested Fix

Apply the precedence rule the tool path already has. A `notification` carrying `agent_needs_input` should not promote a session to a sticky `waiting_input` when AO has recorded a `stop` for the current turn with no subsequent `user-prompt-submit` — in that window the session is known-idle and the notification is a timer artifact, not a question.

Sketch: have the lifecycle layer, which already tracks the last hook event per session, drop or downgrade an `agent_needs_input` notification that arrives after `stop` and before the next `user-prompt-submit`. Keeping the decision in lifecycle (rather than in the pure `DeriveActivityState` mapping) matches how the existing blocked-clear correlation is structured.

A bounded staleness cap on sticky states would limit the blast radius of any future missed clearing event, but it is a backstop, not a substitute — a 23-hour freeze should never have been reachable in the first place.

## Related

- #2525 — `idle_prompt` conflated with `permission_prompt`. Its suggested remap is present in current code; this issue is the surviving sibling on a different notification type.
- #2047 — same family in the pre-Go plugin; also `idle_prompt`.
- #1894 — sticky-state wallclock decay, relevant to the backstop above.

title: fix: sanitize project IDs derived from folder names with dots/special chars

## Summary

When a user runs `ao start` in a directory like `llama.cpp`, the derived project ID would fail validation with:

```

  {
    "validation": "regex",
    "code": "invalid_string",
    "message": "Project ID must match [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ (no dots, slashes, or special characters)",
    "path": [
      "projects",
      "llama.cpp"
    ]
  }
]
```

- Modified `defaultProjectID` in `backend/internal/service/project/service.go` to:
  1. Replace non-alphanumeric characters (except `_` and `-`) with hyphens

fix: reject spawn for closed/cancelled tracker issues
body:
## Summary

Running `ao spawn <issue-number>` on a **closed or cancelled issue** proceeds through the entire spawn pipeline — session ID reservation, worktree creation, tmux pane, and agent launch — without ever checking whether the issue is still open. This spawns a full session on already-resolved work.

## Changes

- **Gate the spawn on issue state** inside `withIssueContext` (`backend/internal/service/session/issue_context.go`), the single funnel for CLI, HTTP and dashboard spawns. When the fetched issue is in a terminal state (`done` or `cancelled`), return `apierr.Conflict` `ISSUE_CLOSED` before any session/worktree/tmux is created.
- **Factor the terminal-state predicate** onto `domain.NormalizedIssueState.IsTerminal()` so `lifecycle` and the session service share one source of truth instead of a duplicated inline check.
- **`Service.Spawn`/spawn** propagate the error instead of proceeding to `manager.Spawn`.

`in_progress` and `review` issues still spawn normally (matches `isTerminalTrackerState` in `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`).

## Test coverage

- `TestSpawnRejectsTerminalIssueState`: done and cancelled issues return `ISSUE_CLOSED` and never reach `manager.Spawn`.
- `TestSpawnAllowsInProgressIssueState`: an in-progress issue still spawns.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `go test ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/lifecycle/...` — pass
- `go vet ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/lifecycle/...` — clean

Fixes #2063

title: Chat UI: MCP tool-server failure banner cannot be dismissed and Reload button is disabled mid-turn
body:
## Bug

The MCP tool-server failure banner in the chat UI (`McpServerBanner`) is a persistent dead-end: it cannot be dismissed, and the only action button ("Reload") is disabled when a turn is in flight — leaving the user staring at an orange warning they can do nothing about.

**Source:** Discord #bug-triage thread (2026-08-09)
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** `2e08699db`
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced

### Two distinct problems

**1. No dismiss option.** The banner renders unconditionally whenever `brokenMcpServers(snapshot)` is non-empty. There is no close/dismiss (X) button. Once an MCP server fails to start, the banner stays above the conversation forever — even after the user has read it, acknowledged it, and decided to deal with it later. It takes up vertical space and draws attention away from the actual conversation.

**2. Reload button disabled mid-turn (by design, but creates a dead-end).** The "Reload" button is `disabled={reloading || turnInFlight}` (`ChatStatusBanners.tsx:218`). When a turn is running or queued (`activeTurn(snapshot)` is truthy), the button is grayed out and unclickable. This is intentional — the daemon refuses a reload mid-turn — but combined with problem #1, the user has **zero agency**: they can't dismiss the banner, and they can't act on it either. They must wait for the turn to finish (or stop it) before they can do anything.

The reporter confirms both symptoms: *"there is no way to dismiss / reload it"* and *"the reload button is also not clickable."*

## Reproduction

1. Start a session with an agent harness that uses MCP servers (e.g. Codex with `figma` and `codex_apps` configured)
2. Ensure at least one MCP server fails to start (timeout, bad config, etc.)
3. Send a message to the agent — the agent starts working (turn is now in flight)
4. Switch to the chat UI
5. Observe: the "N tool servers did not start" banner is displayed with the "Reload" button grayed out / unclickable
6. There is no dismiss (X) button anywhere on the banner
7. The banner remains indefinitely — it does not auto-dismiss, and there is no user action to clear it while the turn is running

## Root Cause

**File:** `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatStatusBanners.tsx:156-235` (`McpServerBanner`)

The component has three states for the action area:
- **No `onReload` prop** → no button rendered at all (harness doesn't support reload)
- **`onReload` + `disabled={reloading || turnInFlight}`** → button rendered but disabled (current case in screenshot)
- **`onReload` + not disabled** → button is clickable

There is **no fourth state**: no dismiss/acknowledge path. The banner's visibility is purely a function of `brokenMcpServers(snapshot)` — if servers are broken, the banner shows, period. There is no "user has acknowledged this" state.

**File:** `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx:363-369`

```tsx
<McpServerBanner
    servers={brokenServers}
    onReload={onReloadMcpServers}
    reloading={reloadingMcpServers}
    turnInFlight={Boolean(turn)}    // ← disables Reload while agent is working
    error={mcpReloadError}
/>
```

**File:** `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/SessionChatSurface.tsx:158-166`

```tsx
onReloadMcpServers={
    !can(snapshot, "mcp_reload") || commands.mcpReloadUnsupported
        ? undefined
        : () => { void commands.reloadMcpServers().catch(() => {}); }
}
```

When the harness doesn't advertise `mcp_reload`, `onReload` is `undefined` and no button renders — but the banner itself still shows with no way to dismiss it.

## Fix

**Dismiss control (primary fix):** Add an acknowledge/dismiss (X) button to `McpServerBanner` that hides the banner for the current session until the MCP server list changes (new failure, or successful reload). The banner is current-state chrome — but "current state the user has already read and cannot act on" is not useful chrome. Options:

1. **Session-scoped dismiss** — track a `dismissedMcpBanner` boolean in component state; reset when the broken-servers set changes (new failure appears). Simplest, no daemon changes.
2. **Persistent dismiss** — store dismissal in the conversation snapshot; daemon tracks it. Heavier, but survives navigation away and back.

Option 1 is likely sufficient — the banner reappears if a *new* server fails, which is the case the user needs to know about.

**Reload button tooltip (secondary):** The disabled button already has a `title` attribute ("Finish or stop the current turn before reloading tool servers"), but it's only visible on hover. Consider surfacing the reason inline (e.g., "Reload available after the current turn finishes") so the user understands *why* it's disabled without hovering.

## Impact

- **Severity:** Medium — UX dead-end, not a functional breakage. The MCP servers remain broken regardless, but the user is trapped with a non-dismissible warning and no actionable control during turns.
- **Frequency:** Every session where MCP servers fail to start and the agent is mid-turn — a common configuration for Codex users with MCP integrations.
- **Workaround:** Finish or stop the current turn, then click Reload. No workaround for the non-dismissible banner itself.

## Related

- The mobile equivalent (`packages/mobile/lib/chat/ChatSessionScreen.tsx:295`) uses an `InlineBanner` with a conditional Reload action — same pattern, likely same issue.

title: bug(chat): "Stop turn" fails with CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN while UI shows a running turn — in-memory/durable turn-state desync
body:
## Bug

Clicking **"Stop turn"** on a chat session that shows a running turn ("Working") returns `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN` — *"there is no turn in flight to interrupt"* — and the turn is **not** stopped. The UI continues showing "Working" indefinitely. The user has no way to stop the turn from the chat interface.

**Source:** [Discord — #bug-triage](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1535762769390080002) | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Date:** 2026-08-09
**Analyzed against:** `b6609ae61` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** High — code path traced end-to-end; the desync mechanism is identifiable in source

### What the screenshot shows

A chat session with:
- Previous turns marked "DONE" and "STOPPED 48.0s"
- A **"Working 3m 0s"** status bar with a spinner and a **"Stop turn"** button
- After clicking "Stop turn": red error `there is no turn in flight to interrupt (CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN)`
- The "Working" bar **remains visible** — the turn is not stopped, the UI does not recover

## Reproduction

1. Start a chat-mode session (any harness with Chat support)
2. Send a message that triggers a long-running turn
3. While the turn is running, click "Stop turn"
4. Observe: error `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN`, turn continues running, UI stays stuck on "Working"

*Note: this is intermittent — it requires the in-memory/durable desync condition (see Root Cause). Most interrupts work. The bug manifests when a `ChatEventTurnCompleted` projection fails mid-transaction.*

## Root Cause

**The in-memory controller state (`pendingTurnID`) and the durable SQLite turn state can diverge**, producing a split where the UI (reads SQLite) shows a running turn but the interrupt path (checks in-memory) finds nothing to cancel.

### The two sources of truth

| Signal | Source | Used by |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `c.pendingTurnID` | In-memory, `Controller` struct | `Interrupt()` → `awaitAcknowledgedTurn()` |
| Turn `state = 'running'` | SQLite `conversation_turns` table | `Snapshot()` → frontend `activeTurn()` → "Working" bar |

### The desync mechanism

`Controller.apply()` (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:1265`) runs **inside** the `ProjectProviderEvent` SQLite transaction as a callback (`controller.go:1262`). For `ChatEventTurnCompleted` (line 1304–1327):

```go
case ports.ChatEventTurnCompleted:
    c.mu.Lock()
    if c.pendingTurnID == event.ProviderTurnID {
        c.pendingTurnID = ""        // ← mutates in-memory state
    }
    // ...
    c.mu.Unlock()
    // ...
    if err := c.store.SettleTurn(   // ← SQLite write, same transaction
        ctx, c.conversation.ID, event.ProviderTurnID, state, message, now); err != nil {
        return err                   // ← transaction rolls back, but pendingTurnID is already ""
    }
```

**If `SettleTurn` (or the archive insert in `ProjectProviderEvent`) fails**, the transaction rolls back — SQLite retains `state = 'running'` — but `c.pendingTurnID` has already been cleared in memory. This is not un-mutated on rollback.

After this:
1. `projectEvent` returns error → `project()` logs and `continue`s (line 1188–1189)
2. `afterProject()` is **skipped** (only called on success, line 1191) → lifecycle never gets the `ActivityIdle` signal → session stays `active`
3. Frontend snapshot reads SQLite → turn still `running` → shows "Working" + "Stop turn"
4. User clicks "Stop turn" → `awaitAcknowledgedTurn()` (line 1068–1077) sees `pendingTurnID == ""` → returns `false` → `ErrNoActiveTurn` (line 1039)

### Why the UI never recovers

The interrupt mutation (`useConversation.ts:208–217`) only calls `invalidate` in `onSuccess`. On error, the conversation query is **not** refetched, so the stale "running" turn persists in the React Query cache. The user is stuck looking at a "Working" bar they cannot dismiss or stop.

## Fix

### Backend (primary): reconcile before refusing

In `Controller.Interrupt()` (`controller.go:1036`), when `awaitAcknowledgedTurn()` returns false, **check the durable SQLite state** before returning `ErrNoActiveTurn`. If SQLite has a turn in `running` state for this conversation, the controller has lost track of it — settle it as `interrupted` and return success (the user's intent was to stop, and the work is stale from AO's perspective).

This mirrors the existing `SettleOrphanedTurns` reconciliation pattern (`conversation_store.go:366`) used on controller start and stream-end cleanup.

### Backend (defense-in-depth): don't mutate in-memory state inside a rollback-able transaction

The deeper fix: `apply()` should not mutate `pendingTurnID` / `ackedTurnID` / `state` inside the `ProjectProviderEvent` transaction callback. These mutations should be deferred to `afterProject()` (which runs only after a successful projection), or applied idempotently outside the transaction scope. This prevents the desync at its source for all event kinds, not just turn completion.

### Frontend (resilience): refetch on interrupt error

In `useConversation.ts`, add an `onError` handler to the `interrupt` mutation that invalidates the conversation query when the error code is `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN`. This ensures the UI refetches and discovers the true turn state, rather than staying stuck on a stale "Working" bar.

## Impact

- **User-facing:** the user's only way to stop a long-running chat turn from the UI silently fails. There is no workaround from the chat interface (the turn continues, the "Working" bar never disappears). The user must kill the session or wait for the provider to finish on its own.
- **Trust:** "Stop turn" is a brake — a brake that appears to work (no visible error until you read the red text) but doesn't actually stop anything erodes trust in the chat surface.
- **Frequency:** intermittent, requiring a projection failure. But projection failures do happen (SQLite constraint errors, disk pressure, WAL contention), and when they hit this path the result is a stuck session with no recovery.

## Related

- [#3115](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3115) — session stuck "working" for days (stale `activity_state=active`, lost `stop` hook). Same "stuck working" symptom, **different mechanism**: that issue is about hook coverage gaps in the lifecycle/activity layer; this issue is about in-memory vs durable turn-state desync in the chat controller. Both produce "permanently working" sessions from different root causes.
- [#2047](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2047) — Claude sessions misreport activity state. Same "status lies" family.

title: Eliminate browser flicker with native view composition and dockable DevTools
body: ## What Rework browser rendering and DevTools integration around Electron’s native view compositor. This PR: - Keeps browser pages running as live native `WebContentsView` surfaces. - Replaces the main `BrowserWindow` composition with a `BaseWindow` containing an explicit transparent shell view. - Adds native compositor ordering for browser tab menus, title-bar menus, and other overlays. - Removes the JPEG screenshot, mirror-frame, parking, and visual-transition paths. - Replaces the custom detached/CDP DevTools window with Chromium’s native DevTools. - Adds DevTools placement options for right, bottom, left, and undocked modes. - Preserves the selected DevTools placement and retargets DevTools when the active browser tab changes. - Synchronizes the toolbar state when DevTools is closed through its native close button. - Handles maximized browser layout, Windows window controls, macOS window behavior, and light/dark native backgrounds. - Removes the old redundant DevTools capability and browser-mirroring code. ## Why The browser flashing, black frames, and apparent freezing came from the previous composition handoff. The browser page is an Electron native `WebContentsView`, while the tabs menu and application menus are rendered inside the React shell. CSS `z-index` cannot place a DOM menu above a separate native child view. The previous implementation worked around that limitation by: 1. Capturing the live browser page as a JPEG/data URL. 2. Decoding and rendering that capture inside React. 3. Parking, hiding, or moving the live native browser view. 4. Reversing the process after the menu closed. Those operations were asynchronous and could not be applied as one atomic frame. Rapidly opening the tabs menu, maximizing the browser, switching tabs, or opening another application menu could expose an intermediate state where: - the live browser view had already moved; - the replacement image had not painted yet; - an opaque shell layer covered the browser; - or a stale captured frame remained visible. That produced the black/blank flash and made the browser appear frozen. This PR fixes the problem at the composition root. The application shell and browser pages now participate in the same explicit native view hierarchy: - During normal browsing, the transparent shell stays below the live browser page. - When a menu or overlay opens, the shell is raised above the browser page by the native compositor. - When the overlay closes, the shell returns below the browser page. The browser itself is never replaced with a JPEG, parked, or hidden during this transition. It remains live and interactive behind the transparent shell, removing the application-side capture and timing race that caused the flicker. For the maximized browser, the normal workspace subtree is hidden while its transparent shell is raised, preventing the terminal, sidebar, or search UI from appearing behind browser menus. ## How ### Native window composition - Introduces `window-composition.ts` to own the explicit shell `WebContentsView`. - Uses `BaseWindow` so there is no implicit renderer competing with the explicitly ordered shell and browser views. - Resizes the shell with the native window and disposes its owned `WebContents` cleanly. - Uses theme-aware native window backgrounds to avoid dark surfaces appearing in light mode. ### Live browser rendering - Removes browser screenshot capture and mirror-frame rendering. - Removes the parked-browser bounds state and transition timers. - Keeps the active browser page at its real bounds while overlays open. - Marks browser and title-bar menus as native overlays so the shell can be reordered consistently. ### Native DevTools - Opens Chromium DevTools directly on the selected browser tab’s `WebContents`. - Supports right, bottom, left, and undocked placement. - Retargets DevTools when the selected tab changes. - Tracks native `devtools-closed` events so the browser toolbar never shows “Close DevTools” after DevTools has already been closed. - Removes the old custom DevTools window, trusted CDP capability, and private DevTools endpoint path. ### Cross-platform behavior - Keeps Windows maximized browser content below the native minimize, maximize, and close controls. - Preserves the existing macOS traffic-light and fullscreen behavior. - Prevents the normal application workspace from showing through a maximized browser overlay. - Keeps native backgrounds consistent with light, dark, and system themes. ## Testing - Manually tested browser tabs and application menus in normal and maximized browser modes on Windows. - Manually tested browser maximize/restore and fullscreen controls. - Manually tested docked and undocked DevTools placement. - Manually tested closing DevTools through its native close button and verified the browser toolbar state updates. - Manually tested browser surfaces in light and dark themes. - `npm run typecheck` — passed. - `npm run typecheck:e2e` — passed. - Focused browser, composition, DevTools, and window tests — 151 passed, 2 skipped. - macOS-focused source tests — 89 passed. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` - [x] One focused browser composition and DevTools change - [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior

title: fix(chat): reconcile turn-state desync when Stop turn fails with CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN
body: Fixes [[#3749](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3749) — "Stop turn" fails with `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN` while the UI shows a running turn. The chat controller kept two sources of truth for "is a turn running?" — an in-memory `pendingTurnID` and a durable SQLite `conversation_turns.state = 'running'` row. They could diverge when `SettleTurn` failed inside the `ProjectProviderEvent` transaction: the rollback discarded the SQLite update but the in-memory mutation had already run, leaving the UI showing "Working" with no way to stop it. ## Root Cause `Controller.apply()` for `ChatEventTurnCompleted` mutated `pendingTurnID = ""` in memory *before* calling `SettleTurn()`, which runs inside a SQLite transaction. If `SettleTurn` failed, the transaction rolled back (SQLite retained `state = 'running'`) but the in-memory `pendingTurnID` was already cleared — not rolled back because it's a Go variable, not SQL. This desync meant `Interrupt()` found nothing to cancel while the UI read SQLite and showed "Working". ## Fix 1. **Reorder `apply()`** — durable write before memory mutation. If `SettleTurn` fails, memory stays intact so `Interrupt()` still works. (`controller.go`) 2. **Disk fallback in `Interrupt()`** — if memory says nothing is running, check SQLite for a stale `running` turn and settle it as `interrupted`. Mirrors the existing `SettleOrphanedTurns` reconciliation pattern. (`controller.go` + `conversation_store.go` + `conversations.sql`) 3. **Frontend resilience** — `onError` handler on the `interrupt` mutation invalidates the conversation query so the UI refetches and unblocks. (`useConversation.ts`) ## Manual Testing ### Test 1: Normal "Stop turn" still works (regression check) 1. Start the daemon: `go run ./cmd/ao daemon` 2. Start the desktop app: `cd frontend && npm run dev` 3. Open a chat session (codex, Chat mode) 4. Send a slow prompt: > Write a comprehensive test suite for a banking application in Go. Include tests for account creation, deposits, withdrawals, transfers, overdrafts, concurrency with goroutines, transaction rollback, audit logging, and edge cases. Cover both unit and integration tests. 5. While it shows "Working Xs", click "Stop turn" 6. **Result:** Turn stops, status shows "Stopped" — no regression ### Test 2: Stale "Working" bar recovers after daemon restart (the bug) 1. Start the daemon standalone: `go run ./cmd/ao daemon` 2. Start the desktop app: `cd frontend && npm run dev` 3. Open a chat session (codex, Chat mode) 4. Send the same slow prompt 5. While it shows "Working Xs", **kill the daemon** (Ctrl+C in the terminal) 6. The UI keeps showing "Working" (stale SQLite state — turn still `running` on disk) 7. **Restart the daemon:** `go run ./cmd/ao daemon` 8. Click "Stop turn" 9. **Before the fix:** Error `there is no turn in flight to interrupt (CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN)`, UI stays stuck on "Working" indefinitely 10. **After the fix:** Turn settles as interrupted, UI unblocks ## Automated Tests - `TestInterruptReconcilesStaleRunningTurnOnDisk` — a turn left `running` on disk while the controller has no `pendingTurnID` is settled as `interrupted` by `Interrupt()`, unblocking the UI. - `TestInterruptReturnsNoActiveTurnWhenNoRunningTurnAnywhere` — the disk fallback does not produce false positives when memory and SQLite agree there is nothing to stop. - `go test ./internal/service/chat/...` — 79/79 pass (77 existing + 2 new) - `go vet ./...` — clean - `npm run typecheck` — clean

title: [Bug]: (chat): "Switch to Chat UI" button disabled on new sessions until first prompt + session switch
body:
### Summary
A newly spawned Codex or Claude Code session (TUI mode) does not enable the "Switch to Chat UI" button until the user sends at least one prompt and then switches away from and back to the session. The button appears disabled with no explanation, making it seem like Chat mode is unavailable.

## Root Cause
The session interface transition status (`GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/interface-transition`) checks whether the session has a "native conversation" (provider thread ID) that can resume in the other interface. For Codex and Claude Code, this native conversation ID is reported asynchronously via a `SessionStart` hook — it is not available immediately after spawn, and only appears after the agent begins its first turn.

The frontend hook `useSessionInterfaceTransition` (`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionInterfaceTransition.ts:50-78`) polls every 1 second while the reason code is `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`. However, the native conversation ID only becomes available after the agent receives and processes its first prompt. The workspace query refetches every 15 seconds and on CDC events, but it does not invalidate the interface transition status query. Only switching sessions (which unmounts and remounts the `SessionView` component) triggers a fresh fetch of the transition status, which then finds the now-available native session.

## Suggested Fix
Add `sessionInterfaceTransitionQueryKey(sessionId)` to the invalidation list in `useConversation.ts` or `event-transport.ts` when a `session_updated` CDC event arrives, so the transition status refetches alongside the workspace.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start AO and open the desktop app
2. Spawn a new Codex or Claude Code session in TUI mode
3. Open the session view — the "Switch to Chat UI" button is disabled
4. Send at least one prompt to the agent
5. Switch to a different session in the sidebar
6. Switch back to the original session
7. The "Switch to Chat UI" button is now enabled and works

### Expected behavior
The "Switch to Chat UI" button should become enabled as soon as the agent's native conversation is available (after the first prompt or turn starts), without requiring the user to switch away and back.

### Actual behavior
The "Switch to Chat UI" button stays disabled until the user manually switches sessions to force a re-fetch of the interface transition status. There is no indication of what's wrong or that the user needs to do anything.

### AO version
586d863b

### Environment
Windows

```shell
```

- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: feat: add Kimchi ACP chat driver binding (working MVP)
body: ## What Binds Kimchi to AO's reusable ACP Chat transport, following the same `nativeacp` pattern as OpenCode and Droid. Users can now spawn Kimchi sessions in chat mode and interact through the mobile/desktop chat UI instead of a terminal. ## Why AO could only supervise Kimchi through TUI mode (terminal scraping). This meant Kimchi was absent from the chat driver list — users who wanted the native chat experience on mobile had to use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or Droid. This PR adds Kimchi to that list. ## How ### Kimchi chat driver binding (`kimchiacp/`) A new `kimchiacp` package delegates to `nativeacp.New()` with four provider-specific functions: - **Harness:** `domain.HarnessKimchi` - **`configure()`:** returns `["--mode", "acp"]`, appends `--append-system-prompt ` when AO provides a system prompt - **`sessionMode()`:** maps `AcceptEdits → "auto"`, `PermissionModeAuto → "auto"` (matching the Kimchi TUI adapter), `BypassPermissions → "yolo"`, `Default → ""` - **`sessionOptions()`:** maps `ChatTurnSettings.Model` to the `"model"` config option ID Binary resolution and auth probing are delegated to the existing Kimchi agent plugin. Registered in the chat driver registry's `Build()` function. ### ACP driver compatibility fixes (`acp/`) Three issues were discovered and fixed during the manual smoke test against a live Kimchi ACP session: 1. **Removed `session/resume` hard gate from `Start()`.** Kimchi's ACP doesn't advertise `session/resume` in its handshake. The driver was hard-rejecting it with `409: ACP agent does not support session/resume`. The fix allows new sessions to start without resume; the resume capability is downgraded to `false`. `Resume()` still returns `ErrChatResumeFailed` if called. 2. **Fixed nil map panic.** `c.capabilities` was only initialized in `start()`, but Kimchi sends `session/update` notifications (with config options) during `NewSession()` — before `start()` runs. This caused `panic: assignment to entry in nil map` in `replaceConfigOptions()`. Fixed by initializing `capabilities` as an empty map in `newConversation()`. 3. **Graceful handling of unsupported ACP methods.** Kimchi's ACP doesn't implement `session/set_mode` (returns JSON-RPC `-32601 Method not found`). The driver was treating this as a fatal error. Added `isACPMethodNotFound()` helper; `applyTurnSettings()` now logs unsupported methods at debug level and continues. Same treatment applied to `session/set_config_option`. ### Mobile logo registration (`packages/mobile/`) Added Kimchi's logo (rasterized from the desktop SVG at 128×128 PNG) to the mobile app's logo registry and test fixtures. ## Testing - `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/...` — all pass (218+ tests across 10 packages) - Binding unit tests (`kimchiacp/driver_test.go`) verify `configure()`, `sessionMode()`, and `sessionOptions()` as pure functions - Registry test (`TestShippedChatDrivers`) asserts `domain.HarnessKimchi` resolves to a non-nil driver - Manual smoke test: spawned a Kimchi chat session from the mobile app against a live AO daemon — Kimchi launched in ACP mode, the session established, streaming messages and tool calls rendered correctly in the chat UI ## ACP compatibility gaps (follow-up work) This is a working MVP.
