title: fix(chat): refresh interface switch readiness from CDC
body:
Fixes [#3753](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3753).

Focused alternative to [#3771](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3771). This PR addresses the reported stale readiness state without changing backend handoff semantics.

## Problem

The daemon already emits `session_updated` when a provider-native session id is captured, but the renderer did not route that event to the interface-transition readiness query. Current polling eventually recovers, but readiness can lag and the event path remains disconnected from the cache it changes.

## Solution

- Route `session_updated` to the exact `sessionInterfaceTransitionQueryKey(sessionId)`.
- Only schedule that invalidation when the mounted query is waiting on `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`.
- Keep the existing one-second poll as a fallback for missed or reordered SSE events.
- Rename the invalidation scheduler to reflect that it now routes workspace, conversation, and transition cache updates.

## Safety

- No backend transition behavior changes.
- No synthetic or hardcoded provider conversation ids.
- No fresh-conversation fallback that could lose TUI context.
- No migration or generated API changes.
- Settled readiness and non-session CDC events do not trigger transition refetches.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/lib/event-transport.test.ts src/renderer/hooks/useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx` — 17 tests passed.
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — passed.
- Native Electron isolated timing check: hook completed at 352 ms, supported readiness refetched at 647 ms, and the button enabled at 751 ms, before the one-second poll fallback.
- Manual dev Electron E2E confirmed: the Switch to Chat button enabled in place after the first Codex prompt without navigating away.

title: Wheel scroll is dead in every terminal pane when tmux reserves screen row 1 (pane-border-status top)
body:
# Wheel scroll is dead in every terminal pane when tmux reserves screen row 1 (`pane-border-status top`)

## Summary

`sgrWheelReport` hardcodes the mouse report's coordinates to cell `1;1`. tmux interprets those coordinates in **client-screen** space, so when the user's tmux config reserves the top screen row — `pane-border-status top`, or `status-position top` — cell `1;1` is the border/status row, not pane content. tmux finds no pane at that cell and discards the report. Wheel scrolling then does nothing in every AO pane, with no error in the app, the daemon, or tmux.

The same session scrolls correctly when attached from a normal terminal emulator, because a real emulator sends the pointer's actual cell rather than a fixed one. That makes the bug look client-side, which is how it was first misfiled locally.

Version: 0.12.2 (macOS 26.5.2, tmux 3.6a, `claude` and `codex` panes both affected).

## Where

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx`

```ts
// line 225
function sgrWheelReport(button: number, count: number): string {
  return `\x1b[<${button};1;1M`.repeat(count);
}
```

emitted by the mouse-tracking branch of the custom wheel handler:

```ts
// line 748
if (term.modes.mouseTrackingMode !== "none") {
  const button = lines < 0 ? SGR_WHEEL_UP : SGR_WHEEL_DOWN;
  emitUserInput(sgrWheelReport(button, Math.abs(lines)), "wheel");
  return false;
}
```

The comment above `sgrWheelReport` states the assumption directly — "reports are 1-based and a single cell is enough for a borderless single pane". The assumption holds only when the pane occupies screen row 1.

## Reproduction

1. In `~/.tmux.conf`: `set -g pane-border-status top`
2. Spawn any AO session (an agent whose TUI requests mouse tracking, e.g. `claude` or `codex`).
3. Scroll the wheel over the terminal pane. Nothing moves.
4. `tmux display -p -t <session> '#{pane_top}'` → `1`. Set `pane-border-status off` (or `bottom`), respawn, and scrolling works; `pane_top` is `0`.

`status-position top` produces the same result by the same mechanism.

## Evidence

Measured rather than inferred, with a harness that drives one real `tmux attach` client on a pty and writes the exact bytes AO writes into its stdin. The pane's app is a sink that enables alt screen + SGR any-event mouse tracking (`\e[?1049h\e[?1002h\e[?1006h`) and echoes what it receives, mirroring an agent TUI. The tmux session is configured as AO configures its own: `mouse on`, `status off`.

| tmux setting                | `pane_top` | bytes written to the client | what the pane's app received |
| --------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `pane-border-status top`    | 1          | `\x1b[<64;1;1M`             | _nothing_                    |
| `pane-border-status bottom` | 0          | `\x1b[<64;1;1M`             | `^[[<64;1;1M`                |
| `pane-border-status off`    | 0          | `\x1b[<64;1;1M`             | `^[[<64;1;1M`                |
| `pane-border-status top`    | 1          | `\x1b[<64;50;15M`           | `^[[<64;50;14M`              |

The last row is the informative one: with row 1 occupied, a report at a real mid-pane coordinate is delivered (with the row translated into pane space), while the hardcoded `1;1` is dropped. Nothing about the transport is broken — only the coordinate.

Note for anyone reproducing this: `tmux send-keys` cannot reproduce or disprove it, because it delivers straight to the pane and skips tmux's mouse handling entirely. The bytes have to enter a real client's stdin.

## Proposed fix

Send the wheel event's actual pointer cell, as a terminal emulator does, instead of a constant. The handler already receives the `WheelEvent`:

```ts
function sgrWheelReport(
  button: number,
  count: number,
  col: number,
  row: number,
): string {
  return `\x1b[<${button};${col};${row}M`.repeat(count);
}

// in the mouse-tracking branch, from the event xterm already hands the handler:
const rect = host.getBoundingClientRect();
const col = clamp(
  Math.floor(((event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * term.cols) + 1,
  1,
  term.cols,
);
const row = clamp(
  Math.floor(((event.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * term.rows) + 1,
  1,
  term.rows,
);
```

SGR (1006) encoding has no 223-column ceiling, so no clamping beyond the grid is needed.

This also fixes a second case that the constant gets wrong regardless of tmux config: if a user splits the pane inside an AO session, every wheel event is reported at `1;1` and therefore scrolls whichever pane sits in the top-left corner, not the one under the pointer.

## Workaround for anyone hitting this before a fix ships

Keep tmux screen row 1 free in AO's sessions. Globally that is `set -g pane-border-status off` (or `bottom`). To keep top border titles in your own sessions and only exempt AO's, hook on session creation and match the pane's start command against AO's worktree path:

```tmux
set -g pane-border-status top
set-hook -g session-created 'run -b "~/bin/ao-pane-border #{hook_session_name}"'
```

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# ~/bin/ao-pane-border
session="${1:-}"
[ -n "$session" ] || exit 0
start_command=$(tmux display -p -t "$session" '#{pane_start_command}' 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
case "$start_command" in
*/.ao/data/worktrees/*) tmux set-option -w -t "$session" pane-border-status off ;;
esac
```

Two caveats found the hard way: a long-running tmux server never re-reads `tmux.conf`, so `tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf` is required before the hook exists; and relaunching AO reattaches to existing tmux sessions rather than creating new ones, so sessions that predate the hook need the script run against them by hand.

## Related, but not duplicates

- #1714 (closed) — same symptom, different cause: the `=` exact-match prefix made `set-option ... mouse on` silently fail, so tmux never had mouse mode. Here `mouse on` is applied correctly (`show-options -t <session> mouse` → `mouse on`); the report is well-formed and simply addressed to a cell that is not pane content.
- #1704 (closed) — mouse mode lost when a late client missed the init handshake. Not this: the handshake arrives, `term.modes.mouseTrackingMode` is non-`none`, and the SGR branch at line 748 is the one that runs.
- #3640 (open) — same file, adjacent mechanism: `forceSelectionMode` suppresses xterm's own mouse **button** reporting. That is arguably why wheel reports have to be synthesized here at all, so a fix to either should keep the other in mind.

title: fix(desktop): authenticate feature-build GitHub requests when a token is available
body:
## What

`frontend/src/main/feature-builds.ts` calls the public GitHub REST API entirely unauthenticated -- capped at 60 requests/hour. Each `listFeatureBuilds()` call fetches the releases list plus one `/pulls/<n>` lookup per unique feature-build PR. On a project with several concurrent feature builds (or just a busy dev machine polling repeatedly), that adds up fast. When the limit is exhausted, `isPrOpen()` deliberately fails open ("On any error keep the entry rather than incorrectly filtering it out"), so the degraded state is a stale/bloated feature-build picker rather than a clean error -- exactly the kind of thing worth avoiding rather than just tolerating.

This was flagged inline in the code itself:
```ts
// ponytail: unauthenticated GitHub API hits the 60 req/hr limit; per-PR-state
// calls are batched/deduped below but could still be exhausted on large lists.
// Upgrade path: pass the app's OAuth token (if one exists) in the Authorization
// header to raise the limit to 5000 req/hr.
```

## Fix

Add an optional `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header to every request `fetchJson()` makes, sourced from:
1. `AO_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an AO-specific override), falling back to
2. `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the ambient env var a dev shell or CI runner commonly already exports).

This mirrors the exact two-name precedence `backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/auth.go`'s `EnvTokenSource` already uses for the daemon's own GitHub calls -- kept in sync here since the Electron main process and the Go daemon are two independent GitHub clients with no shared token plumbing between them (Electron doesn't shell out to `gh`; that's exclusively the daemon's job per this codebase's existing architecture, so I scoped this to env-var-only rather than adding a new `gh auth token` shell-out from the main process).

Purely best-effort and fully backward compatible: when neither env var is set, every request stays unauthenticated exactly as before (60 req/hr). When one is set, requests are authenticated (5000 req/hr).

## Testing

- Added 5 new tests to `feature-builds.test.ts` covering: no token → no header; `GITHUB_TOKEN` set → `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; `AO_GITHUB_TOKEN` takes priority over `GITHUB_TOKEN` when both are set; a blank/whitespace-only token is treated as unset; and that the header reaches the per-PR `/pulls/<n>` lookup too, not just the releases call.
- Proved the new tests are meaningful via a stash-free patch-file round trip: reverse-applied just the implementation change (keeping the new tests), confirmed 3 of them failed against the unpatched code, reapplied and confirmed all 30 tests in the file pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (via `--project tsconfig.json`) is clean.
- Full `feature-builds.test.ts` suite: 30/30 passing, no regressions to the existing 25 tests.

title: feat(chat): expose preventive read-only permission mode for Chat workers
body:
Summary

AO's structured Chat workers currently do not expose a permission mode that allows a worker to inspect a repository while preventively blocking filesystem writes.

For Codex Chat sessions, the current permission mapping is effectively:

default / bypass-permissions
→ approvalPolicy = never
→ sandbox = danger-full-access

accept-edits / auto
→ approvalPolicy = on-request
→ sandbox = workspace-write

This leaves no way for a machine caller to request:

approvalPolicy = never
sandbox = read-only

Codex app-server supports this sandbox profile, and AO already uses enforced read-only Codex execution in its reviewer path.

It would be useful for normal worker / chat / codex sessions to expose an equivalent preventive read-only permission mode.

Use case

A control plane or other automated caller may need to create a Chat worker that can:

inspect repository files;
inspect Git state;
reason about the codebase;
return a structured result;

while being technically unable to modify the workspace.

Prompt instructions such as "do not modify files" and post-run diff checks are useful defense-in-depth, but they are not substitutes for preventive enforcement.

Today a caller that requires a true read-only execution contract has to reject the Chat worker as unsupported even though the underlying Codex sandbox can provide the required isolation.

Suggested behavior

Add a permission profile such as:

read-only

with the Codex Chat mapping:

approvalPolicy = never
sandbox = read-only

The exact public name/API shape is of course up to AO.

Ideally the permission should be represented through AO's normal typed permission/configuration surface rather than as a Codex-specific escape hatch, so callers can capability-check it before creating or delivering work to a session.

Expected behavior

For a Chat worker created with preventive read-only permissions:

the provider cannot modify workspace files;
no approval prompt is required merely to preserve read-only execution;
the mode survives the normal Chat start/resume lifecycle;
unsupported harnesses fail explicitly rather than silently receiving broader permissions;
callers can distinguish supported read-only enforcement from advisory/read-only-by-prompt behavior.
Why this seems to fit AO's existing model

AO already has the relevant pieces:

structured Codex Chat via codex app-server;
typed per-agent permission modes;
preventive Codex read-only execution in the reviewer path.

The missing piece appears to be exposing the equivalent permission profile to ordinary Chat workers.

Related
#3360 — structured Chat/TUI session architecture
#3745 — read-only hardening for reviewer harnesses

This request is specifically about normal structured Chat worker sessions, not reviewer execution.

title: feat: expose shared Cloud runtime and contracts
body:
## Summary
- keep the private `Untrivial-ai/ao-cloud` repository as an optional submodule under `private/ao-cloud`, without breaking unauthenticated public clones or builds
- advance the gitlink to merged private `main` commit `2576c3d1c6dd8863ea495b0e52d210b04d38f495`

- define the complete Cloud worker, turn, credential, SCM, orchestration, terminal, and workspace OpenAPI contract

title: fix(telemetry): retry failed sends; don't disable telemetry after a startup hiccup
body:
## Summary

Two focused fixes so telemetry that fails to send is recovered instead of silently vanishing. Follow-up to the renderer `send_instantly` fix (https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3816). No steady-state event-volume increase, so no impact on the PostHog cap.

**Backend, retry a failed send** (`adapters/telemetry/posthog.go`). The CLI `app.active` day and each `cli.invoked` are marked spent on disk before the event is sent, so a dropped send was a permanent gap. `send` now retries a *failed* attempt (transient network error / HTTP 429 / 5xx), bounded by `postHogSendMaxAttempts`; a permanent 4xx is not retried. A healthy send still makes exactly one request, and a sustained outage gives up rather than blocking the drain goroutine.

**Renderer, don't disable telemetry after a startup hiccup** (`renderer/lib/telemetry.ts`). A thrown (transient) failure in `initTelemetry` was memoized, disabling telemetry for the whole session. It now clears the memoized promise on a thrown error so the next event retries; a deliberate withheld state (no key / not opted in) is still cached and not retried.

## Cost

Neither change raises steady-state volume. Retries only re-send events that already failed (which otherwise sent nothing); bounded attempts cap the worst case during an outage.

## Verification

- **Backend: run at runtime over real sockets.** A live HTTP server that returns 500-then-200 received 2 requests (retried and delivered); a permanent 400 received 1 (no wasted retry); a sustained 500 stopped after the bounded cap. `go test ./internal/adapters/telemetry/` passes incl. `posthog_retry_test.go`.
- **Renderer: run at runtime.** `initTelemetry()` after a thrown bootstrap error returned `false`, and the next call returned `true` (retry works; old behavior returned `false` both times). Executed through the real toolchain with only the posthog/bridge boundaries stubbed.

## Not in this PR (deliberately)

Trimmed out to keep this focused: the `ao.cli.invoked` burst rate-limit tweak, a dev-only warning for unlisted renderer events, and mobile flush-on-background. All real but non-essential; each can ship as a small standalone change. The aggregated-error dimension mis-attribution (5xx-by-endpoint) is still a known follow-up needing a payload redesign.

title: perf: scope CDC refetch fan-out, batch session-list PR facts, stop idle shell re-renders, narrow preview poll
body:
Profiled the live app first (135 sessions, real daemon + real database), then shipped the four highest-impact, well-scoped wins. No behavior changes beyond update timing bounds documented below; every win has a regression test and before/after numbers.

## How the hotspots were found

- Captured the live SSE `/api/v1/events` stream for 60s during agent activity: **187 `session_updated` events/min** (usage-binding + activity CDC), each of which made the renderer refetch the 99KB `/api/v1/sessions` payload, the usage summary, **and every mounted per-session PR summary** (prefix invalidation of `["session-scm-summary"]` = one HTTP request per visible session card).
- Measured `GET /api/v1/sessions` latency and traced its 1+N SQLite query pattern.
- Read-path review of renderer render churn (whole-store zustand subscriptions, per-poll fresh status objects) and daemon polling loops (preview poller reads all 38 session columns at 4Hz).

## Wins and measurements

| # | Change | Metric | Before | After | How measured |
|---|--------|--------|--------|-------|--------------|
| 1 | Scope + rate-bound CDC invalidation (`event-transport.ts`) | Invalidation rounds for 20 `session_updated` events at the live 320ms cadence (workspaces / scm-root / usage) | 20 / 20 / 20 | 7 / **0** / 7 | vitest fake-timer harness run against the old and new implementation |
| 1 | 〃 | Per-session PR summary refetch storms (HTTP requests per round ≈ visible cards) | every round | 0 on session bursts; scoped to the 1 owning session on PR events | same harness |
| 1 | 〃 | Sub-150ms continuous stream (50 events @ 100ms) | 1 starved flush **after** the stream ends (UI frozen while active) | ~1 flush/s while streaming (5 flushes) | same harness |
| 2 | Batch session-list PR facts (kill 1+N) | `Service.List` store cost, 135 sessions / 90 PRs | 2.85ms, 6030 allocs | 0.26ms, 2741 allocs (**10.8×**) | `go test -bench` `BenchmarkListPRFactsPerSession` vs `BenchmarkListAllPRFacts` (Apple M3) |
| 2 | 〃 | Live `GET /api/v1/sessions` (100 reqs, copy of real 135-session DB, before/after daemon binaries) | p50 10.3ms, p90 16.0ms | p50 3.8ms, p90 5.9ms | curl timing against both binaries on identical DB copies |
| 2 | 〃 | SQLite queries per list build | 1 + 135 | 2 | query pattern |
| 3 | Idle shell re-renders (`useDaemonStatus` equality bailout, zustand field selectors, memoized shell context, TrayRuntime stringify) | Consumer re-renders per unchanged 10s status poll (cascades through ShellLayout → Sidebar, board, titlebar, dialogs) | 1 per poll | 0 | render-count regression test (fails on the old hook) |
| 4 | Narrow preview-poller projection (`ListSessionPreviewRows`) | Per-tick cost of the 250ms scan, 135 sessions with ~4KB text columns | 1.62ms, 4.34MB allocs | 0.13ms, 0.12MB (**12× time, 36× bytes**) | `go test -bench` `BenchmarkPreviewPoll*` |

Compound effect during active agent work: the workspace/usage refetch round-trip rate drops ~3× (bounded at 1/s), each round no longer fans out N per-card PR summary requests, and each `/sessions` build costs ~2.6ms less in the daemon — while idle, the app shell stops re-rendering entirely between real changes.

**Update-timing bounds (deliberate):** workspace/scm/usage refetches now flush at most once per second under sustained CDC streams (previously either one round per event, or complete starvation while events arrived faster than the 150ms debounce). Isolated events keep the 150ms latency. Chat/conversation invalidation cadence is unchanged.

## Correctness guards

- `TestListAllPRFactsMatchesPerSessionReads` pins the batch read to the per-session read it replaces (order + fields).
- `TestListSessionPreviewRowsMatchesListAllSessions` pins the narrow poller read to `ListAllSessions` on every field the poller uses, including the terminated-session filter.
- New event-transport tests cover PR-event scoping, `pr_session_changed` root fallback, storm collapse, and no-starvation; the malformed-payload and unknown-event paths conservatively refetch everything, as before.
- Render-count test on `useDaemonStatus` fails against the previous implementation.

## Validation

- `cd backend && go test ./...` — green except pre-existing `internal/cli` failures that also fail on a clean checkout of `main` in this environment (they collide with the real daemon running on this machine).
- `go test -race` on touched packages (`service/session`, `sqlite/store`, `preview`, `httpd/...`) — green.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` — 0 issues.
- `frontend: npm run typecheck` — clean; `npm test` — green except two pre-existing `src/landing/*` suites that fail identically on a clean tree; renderer `vite build` — OK.
- Live daemon A/B: both binaries run against identical copies of the real database (data dir isolated in a scratch directory, separate port/run-file, shut down after measuring).
- No `ao preview` demo: nothing visual changed — the sidebar/board render identically; the change is network/CPU behavior, covered by the measurements above.

## Big-but-risky follow-ups (found while profiling, deliberately not done here)

1. **Reaper fork storm** — 3 subprocess forks per live session every 5s, including a full `ps -axo` process-table dump *per session* (`tmux.go:564`). Batch to one `ps` + one `tmux list-sessions` per tick. Touches liveness semantics, needs care around the "failed probe ≠ dead" rule.
2. **SSE `/api/v1/events` replays the entire `change_log` (29k+ rows, unbounded, no retention) on every connect** since the renderer never passes `?after=`. The client only uses events as invalidation signals and refetches on open anyway. Needs an API-contract decision (tail parameter or retention policy).
3. **Terminal mux emits one JSON+base64 frame per PTY read** with no coalescing; overflow kills the connection (`manager.go:529`). Binary frames + drain-and-concat would cut most of the per-byte cost.
4. **`GET /sessions/{id}/pr` runs 4 queries per PR alias** (checks/threads/reviews/comments) — same batching treatment as this PR's win 2.
5. Missing `(project_id, num)` index on `sessions` (every list sort builds a temp B-tree); `idx_change_log_project` is written on every trigger insert but never read.
6. No `pprof` endpoint in the daemon — worth adding behind a flag before the next perf pass.

title: Windows: selecting a session flashes many Git console windows
body:
## Bug

Selecting a session in the Windows desktop app launches a burst of transient Git console hosts. Users see many shell/Windows Terminal windows flash and immediately exit.

**Source:** local user report in Codex chat | **Reported by:** local Windows user | **Analyzed against:** `cfbefa4cdbd5e8c8e020177e53d105f10e5f44ee`
**AO version:** bundled daemon reports `dev`, loopback daemon verified ready on port `3001`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** medium — routine session navigation is visually disruptive, but sessions and data remain intact

## Reproduction

1. Run the packaged Agent Orchestrator desktop app on Windows.
2. Open a project with two existing worker sessions.
3. Alternate between the two sessions in the sidebar.
4. Observe transient console/Windows Terminal windows appearing and exiting.

A 10 ms process-parent trace while switching sessions reproduced the behavior consistently. The burst contained `git.exe` children whose parent was the AO daemon, followed by `conhost.exe` children and `OpenConsole.exe` instances. Unrelated Docker Desktop console activity was excluded by parent PID.

## Root Cause

Selecting a session mounts the inspector's workspace-file subscription. The frontend opens:

`GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/events`

The controller calls `workspacewatch.Watch`, whose Git discovery and ignore probes in `backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go` use raw `os/exec.CommandContext`. On Windows these non-interactive Git children do not receive AO's `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` / `HideWindow` process attributes, so each Git command receives a console host. Initial discovery runs several Git commands (`rev-parse`, `ls-files`, common-dir and symbolic-ref), which makes one navigation action look like many shells spawning and exiting.

## Fix

Route every background Git command in `workspacewatch` through `backend/internal/process.CommandContext`, and add a Windows regression test that asserts the workspace watcher command factory sets `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and `HideWindow`.

## Impact

- Every session selection can flash multiple console windows on Windows.
- Rapid navigation compounds the burst because each selected session establishes a new workspace watcher.
- The issue is cosmetic/process-launch behavior; no session termination or data loss was observed.

## Related

- [#1565](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1565) — also reports Windows console flashes, but only during ConPTY teardown; this defect occurs during normal session selection and is caused by AO background Git probes.

title: fix(chat): enable Switch to Chat on Windows — fresh-start readiness + .cmd shim resolution
body:
Two fixes that unblock the "Switch to Chat" button on Windows, where the interface transition dead-ends before a Chat session can start.

## Why

Refs [#3753](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3753)

On Windows the SessionStart hook does not fire for Codex (see #3820), so the native conversation id is never reported. The transition status then blocks as `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` and the "Switch to Chat" button stays disabled indefinitely. This is a simpler alternative to #3771 — instead of fabricating a synthetic UUID, it models the fresh-start path in transition readiness using the adapter's existing history probe.

The second fix addresses a separate Windows blocker: Claude Code ships as an npm `.cmd` shim, and Node `child_process.spawn` cannot execute `.cmd` files. Without resolving to the real `.exe`, the Chat spawn fails with `EINVAL` before the transition even begins.

## How

**Commit 1** — `fix(chat): allow fresh-start transition when adapter has history probe`

Commit 1 — fix(chat): allow fresh-start transition when adapter has history probe
If the adapter implements AgentInterfaceHandoffHistoryProbe, an empty native id is allowed through. The history probe distinguishes a real conversation from an empty TUI, and persistedNativeConversationID uses that to decide between resume and fresh start. Adapters without a probe keep the hard block. Two tests cover the new branch: fresh-start allowed with probe, and hard block without probe.

**Commit 2** — `fix(claudeacp): resolve Windows .cmd shim to .exe for Chat spawn`

`resolveClaudeExe` unwraps the npm `.cmd` shim: prefer a sibling `.exe`, else parse the shim's quoted `%dp0%` target path. 7 tests cover pass-through, cancelled context, missing file, sibling `.exe`, quoted `%dp0%` target, malformed shim, and unreadable shim. Windows-gated cases skip on other platforms.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/... -count=1` — 11 pass, 1 skip (live)
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/... -run TestInterfaceTransition -count=1` — pass
- Verified on Windows: Codex "Switch to Chat" button enables, Claude Code Chat launches

title: fix(session): stop stale origin/main ref from inflating workspace diff file count
body:
## Summary
- The session workspace Files tab was showing far more changed files than the PR actually has (e.g. 130 vs. the real 48), and the count would degrade from correct to wrong over a PR's lifetime.
- Root cause: AO never runs `git fetch` against a session worktree, so its `refs/remotes/origin/main` tracking ref can go stale relative to the real upstream. `resolveWorkspaceCompare` recomputes the compare base against that ref on every request; when the branch later merges a newer `main` in (e.g. to resolve a conflict) without the ref moving, the recomputed merge base still "succeeds" but lands earlier than the branch's true fork point, so every unrelated commit that landed on `main` afterward leaks into the diff as if it were part of the PR.
- Fix: prefer the PR's own, independently-synced base commit (`pr.BaseSHA`, re-derived through `git merge-base` as before) whenever it's at least as advanced as the ref-based candidate, since AO's PR sync keeps that current regardless of whether the local tracking ref has been refreshed.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `TestWorkspaceFilesExcludeMainChangesMergedInAfterStaleOriginRef`, which reproduces the bug (fails on the old code, passes with the fix) by simulating a stale `origin/main` tracking ref and a branch that later merges current `main` in.

title: [Feature]: Remote workspaces — run agents on a VM by pointing the desktop app at a daemon over SSH
body:
## Problem

As someone whose laptop is a thin client, I need AO to run agents on my VM,
because that is where the code, the compute, the credentials and the
automations already are. My normal workflow is `ssh vm` and start the agent
there; the laptop is only where I sit.

Today AO can't do that. The desktop app spawns a daemon on the machine it runs
on, and every session runs there. On the laptop the checkouts don't exist, the
build won't run, and the credentials aren't present — so AO is unusable for the
work I actually do, even though a plain `ssh` session is fine.

This isn't only my setup. Anyone with a dev box, a GPU host, or a cloud
workstation hits it, and the current answer is "don't use the desktop app".

Prior art in this repo:

- Discussion #2855 — "Remote access to a headless daemon after the Electron
  rewrite?" — is an unanswered user asking for exactly this.
- Issue #13 listed "Remote session support (SSH + tmux on remote machines)" and
  was closed on 2026-06-24 as rewrite-migration cleanup, with an invitation to
  refile.

## Proposed direction

**A workspace is a machine that runs its own AO daemon.** The laptop is the
`local` workspace and behaves exactly as today. A remote workspace is an SSH
target the desktop app reaches through a loopback port-forward:

```
ssh -N -L <freeLocalPort>:127.0.0.1:<remoteDaemonPort> <target>
```

The supervisor publishes `<freeLocalPort>` as the daemon port. Because the
renderer already addresses the daemon through one mutable base URL handed to it
on `daemon:status` — and the terminal-mux WebSocket and SSE stream both derive
from that base — the entire renderer then works against the remote daemon
**unmodified**. On the far side nothing is remote: the daemon, the git
worktrees, the tmux server and the agent binary are all local to each other, so
none of the usual remote-execution problems arise.

Properties I'd want maintainers to weigh:

- **No bind change and no new listener.** Both daemons stay `127.0.0.1`-only.
  Unlike the LAN listener in ADR-0001, this needs no exception to the
  loopback-only hard rule.
- **Authentication is SSH's, not AO's.** AO shells out to the user's own `ssh`,
  so `~/.ssh/config` (ProxyJump, Match, IdentityAgent) works for free. AO holds
  no key material and never writes `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` is required
  because the supervisor has no tty; `StrictHostKeyChecking` is deliberately
  never set, so an unknown host key is surfaced to the user rather than silently
  accepted, and a *changed* one is reported as the security event it is.
- **AO never installs anything on the remote.** A host without `ao` is reported
  with the command to run — the same answer AO gives for a missing local tmux.
- **The remote daemon outlives the client.** Closing the laptop lid or quitting
  the app closes the tunnel only; sessions keep running and are still there on
  reconnect. A dropped tunnel is reported as reconnecting, never as sessions
  dying.

Scope I'd propose for a first PR series, in order: ADR → registry + SSH
transport → supervisor placement → switcher UI → reconnect. Deliberately **out**
of scope: moving a session between workspaces, a cross-workspace board, and
`ao` CLI parity.

## Alternatives considered

**Session placement — one laptop daemon that places individual sessions on a VM
over SSH.** I designed this in full first, and the design argued against it.
Every consumer that addresses a live session holds only a
`ports.RuntimeHandle{ID string}`, so routing must be a pure function of that
string — which forces the host into the handle id, and that id space is mintable
from project names, so a folder can forge a remote handle and get a healthy
session reaped. On top of that, `gitworktree` bypasses its own command runner in
ten places (so it can't be remoted by swapping the runner), `binaryutil.LookPath`
resolves agent binaries to *laptop* absolute paths that land in the remote pane's
`argv[0]`, hooks and the system-prompt file get written to the local filesystem
at the remote path, and `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` — a live capability token — sits
in the environment that would be exported to a third machine.

Each is solvable, but every one of them exists only because a single daemon is
acting on a filesystem that isn't its own. I think it's the better answer to "run
*this one task* on the big machine while I keep working locally", and it can
layer on later — but it's the wrong first step, because it pays the whole
remote-filesystem cost before delivering the ordinary case.

**Widen the daemon's bind so the app can dial the VM directly.** This is the
obvious reading of #2855, and it's the one thing the codebase forbids by design
(`backend/internal/config`). It would also make AO responsible for
authentication and transport security on a full remote-control API, well beyond
ADR-0001's opt-in, home-network, single-password posture.

**An AO-authored helper service on the VM.** The VM already runs the daemon we
want; a second service to supervise it adds a component without removing one.

**`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` in-process.** Forces AO to own key material,
passphrase prompting with no UI to prompt from, agent forwarding and a
`known_hosts` TOFU policy. AO persists exactly one secret today and doesn't
persist GitHub tokens at all. Shelling out also gets PTY resize and SIGWINCH
propagation for free.

## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

---

I have a working implementation on a branch (~2.5k lines, unit-tested,
`tsc` clean) split into five reviewable commits with the ADR first. Happy to
open it once scope is agreed, or to adjust the shape first — flagging before
opening a PR per CONTRIBUTING.


Branch with the implementation: https://github.com/DeepakSilaych/agent-orchestrator/tree/feat/remote-ssh-sessions

title: fix(mobile): allow cleartext HTTP to Tailscale CGNAT range on iOS
body:
## What

Add an App Transport Security exception for Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` CGNAT range to
`packages/mobile/app.json`, and correct the now-inaccurate cleartext claim in
`packages/mobile/README.md`.

```json
"NSAppTransportSecurity": {
	"NSAllowsLocalNetworking": true,
	"NSExceptionDomains": {
		"100.64.0.0/10": { "NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads": true }
	}
}
```

## Why

Fixes #3852 — the iOS app cannot connect to the desktop daemon over Tailscale. Entering the
Mac's Tailscale IP in manual connect always surfaces the *unreachable* copy, while the same
setup works over a LAN IP and Safari on the same phone reaches `http://<tailscale-ip>:3011/`
fine.

The request never leaves the device:

- RN's `fetch` goes through `NSURLSession`, which is the layer ATS governs.
- As of iOS/tvOS 17, ATS applies to IP-literal connections made through `URLSession` — older
  guidance saying IP addresses are exempt from ATS is outdated. Confirmed by Apple DTS:
  https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/747421
- The app declared only `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`, which exempts *local* destinations (RFC1918,
  link-local, `.local`). Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` is not classified as local, so the cleartext
  connection is refused in-process — which is why LAN works and Safari (exempt from ATS) works.
- Android is unaffected: `usesCleartextTraffic: true` in the Expo build properties permits
  cleartext to any host, with no local/non-local distinction.

Tailscale is an advertised connection method for the mobile app (the manual-connect placeholder
is `192.168.x.x  or  my-pc.tailXXXX.ts.net`, and `config.ts` documents `host` as e.g.
`"100.101.102.103"`), so this is a gap between the shipped config and the intended UX.

## How

iOS 17+ accepts a CIDR block as an `NSExceptionDomains` key, so the exception is scoped to
exactly the CGNAT range instead of loosening ATS globally with `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`. ATS
stays strict for every other destination; `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` is kept as-is for LAN.

Intentional omissions, to keep the diff minimal:

- No change to MagicDNS names (`*.ts.net`). Those resolve into the same range, but the app's
  own manual-connect flow is IP-based; a hostname exception can be added separately if wanted.
- No Android change — not affected.
- No app-code change; this is purely the ATS declaration plus the doc correction.

Note the exception only takes effect in a build that regenerates `Info.plist` (prebuild / EAS
build); it does not change an already-installed binary.

## Testing

- `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('packages/mobile/app.json','utf8'))"` — parses;
  indentation matches the file's existing tabs.

Full verification needs an iOS device on a tailnet, which I could not exercise end-to-end in
this environment. Repro / expected behavior for a reviewer with that setup:

1. Enable **Connect Mobile** on the desktop app (listener on `0.0.0.0:3011`).
2. Put the Mac and an iPhone on the same tailnet (plain Tailscale, no `serve`/funnel).
3. Rebuild the iOS app from this branch so the new `Info.plist` is generated
   (`npx expo run:ios --device` or an EAS build).
4. In manual connect, enter the Mac's Tailscale IP (`100.x.x.x`), port `3011`, **Use TLS** off.

Expected: the connection succeeds, as it already does with a LAN IP. With a deliberately wrong
password, the *auth* error ("Your desktop rejected the password") should appear rather than the
*unreachable* error — that distinction is the tell that the request now leaves the device.
Also worth confirming a LAN IP still connects, i.e. no regression from adding
`NSExceptionDomains` alongside `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue (`Fixes #3852`)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense — n/a, this is a native
      ATS declaration in `app.json` with no JS-testable surface
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched — deferring to CI on this PR; locally I only
      validated that `app.json` still parses (no code paths touched)

title: Cannot start new workers — spawn always fails
body:
# GitHub Issue — AO cannot spawn workers 

**Title:** Cannot start new workers: spawn always fails (Orchestrator: Muse Spark .. Workers: Cline)

**What happens:**
I try to start a new worker with `ao spawn`. The command never creates a worker. It shows an error about connecting to 127.0.0.1:3001 and says operation not permitted. If I try through the API, I get 500 PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Have a project like `aohack` at /Users/rishetmehra/Desktop/aohack
2. Run `ao spawn --project aohack --name test-worker-1 --prompt hello`
3. Or run `ao status` or `curl -x $http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/projects`
4. See error every time

**What I expected:**
A new worker session should start, and `ao session ls` should show it.

**What actually happens:**
- CLI always says: `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:3001: connect: operation not permitted`
- API always says: `500 PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED` or `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`
- Health check via proxy works: `curl -x $http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:3001/healthz` returns ok, so daemon is running but cannot be reached normally.

**Why this happens (plain English):**
Two problems combine.

1. The AO command line tool tries to talk to the daemon on your own computer (127.0.0.1). On this system, direct talk to that address is blocked. The tool is supposed to use a proxy, but Go's helper `ProxyFromEnvironment` skips the proxy for 127.0.0.1 by design. So it never uses the proxy and always gets blocked.

2. Even when we reach the daemon through the proxy, it cannot load projects. It shows PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED for every request. This comes from the project service which hides the real database error. The database file itself is okay, but the daemon needs to write to ~/.ao/data (WAL file) and that write was blocked in sandboxed runs. So the real cause is hidden.

**Environment:**
- AO daemon pid 71197, port 3001, status ok via proxy but unhealthy via direct
- `ao doctor` shows: FAIL data-dir-write and FAIL daemon: unhealthy
- DB `~/.ao/data/ao.db` has 4 projects and 18 sessions, integrity ok

**Suggested fix for maintainers:**
- Make CLI respect proxy for daemon URL, or add a way to force proxy for 127.0.0.1.
- Show the real error behind PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED so users see if it is permission, busy, or migration.


---

# Pull Request — Fix AO spawn blocked 

**Title:** Fix: allow AO CLI to reach daemon and show real project load error

**Summary in plain English:**
Workers could not start at all. The CLI could not talk to the daemon because it bypassed the proxy for localhost. And when the daemon tried to list projects, it hid the real reason it failed. This PR fixes both so spawning works and errors are clear.

**What changed:**

1. CLI now respects proxy for the daemon address (127.0.0.1:3001). It no longer skips proxy for localhost. This lets `ao spawn` and `ao status` reach the daemon even when direct connection is blocked.

2. Project service now includes the real cause when listing projects fails. `PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED` will now show if the database is busy, permission is denied, or a migration is missing.

**How to test:**
1. In a sandboxed shell with `http_proxy` set, run `ao status` — should go from unhealthy to healthy.
2. Run `ao spawn --project aohack --name test-worker-1 --prompt hello` — should create a worker and appear in `ao session ls`.
3. Check `curl -x $http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/projects` returns projects, not 500.

**Technical notes for reviewers:**
- `backend/internal/service/project/service.go:115-128` — `List()` wraps `store.ListProjects` error with `apierr.Internal("PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED", ...)` — now wraps cause with `%w`.
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go` — Open uses `modernc.org/sqlite` WAL mode which needs write to dataDir; add clearer error when pragmas fail.
- CLI HTTP client — `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` bypasses loopback; replace with custom Proxy func that respects AO_DAEMON_PROXY or always uses proxy for daemon URL, or set `NO_PROXY` handling.

**Checklist:**
- [x] Read codebase: `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/projects.go`, `service/project/service.go`, `storage/sqlite/db.go`
- [x] Kept name length <=20 for spawn tests
- [ ] Ran `cd backend && go test ./...` (blocked in sandbox, needs local run)

title: [Bug]: scm-gitlab plugin lacks enrichSessionsPRBatch — ci-failed / changes-requested reactions never fire for GitLab
body:
### Summary

In AO v0.9.2, the GitLab SCM plugin (`@aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-gitlab@0.9.1`) does not implement the `enrichSessionsPRBatch` method, while the GitHub plugin (`@aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-github@0.9.1`) does (line 1124 of its `dist/index.js`). As a result, the lifecycle manager's PR enrichment cache is never populated for GitLab MRs, `pr.reason` never becomes `ci_failing` / `changes_requested`, and the **`ci-failed` and `changes-requested` reactions never dispatch** for GitLab — regardless of pipeline timing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a project with `scm: { plugin: gitlab }` against a self-hosted GitLab instance (glab CLI configured, `GITLAB_TOKEN` set).
2. Spawn a worker session (`ao spawn`) that opens an MR whose pipeline has **already failed** (e.g. commit an intentionally broken YAML file; confirm the pipeline is `failed` both before and after opening the MR).
3. Let the session continue working on that branch — `scm.detect_pr_succeeded` fires and the session reaches `pr_open` with `session.pr` populated (confirmed via `ao status --json`).
4. Keep the session alive (e.g. `sleep 300`) while the MR stays open with the failed pipeline for 10+ minutes.
5. Also tried: `ao spawn --claim-pr <mr-number>` — fails immediately with `SCM plugin "gitlab" does not support claiming existing PRs`.

### Expected behavior

The lifecycle manager should transition the session to `ci_failed` and dispatch the `ci-failed` reaction (default `action: send-to-agent`) with the failure details, the same way it does for GitHub-backed projects.

### Actual behavior

No `ci.failing` event and no `reaction.action_succeeded` for `ci-failed` are ever recorded, even after 10+ minutes with a live session and an MR whose pipeline was already `failed` before the MR was opened. `ao events list` only shows `scm.detect_pr_succeeded` and (in an earlier run, before installing `procps`) `agent.process_probe_failed`.

Root cause (from reading `packages`/vendored `dist` sources):
- `lifecycle-manager.js` derives non-terminal PR states (`ci_failed`, `changes_requested`, etc.) from a batch enrichment cache (`resolvePREnrichmentDecision(cachedData, ...)`). `scm.getPRState()` is only used as a fallback for terminal states (merged/closed).
- The batch enrichment path calls the SCM plugin's `enrichSessionsPRBatch(prs, observer, repos)` — implemented in `ao-plugin-scm-github` but **absent from `ao-plugin-scm-gitlab`** (grepped the built `dist/index.js`: 0 matches for `enrich`).
- Without that cache entry, `pr.reason` is never set to `ci_failing`, so the `ci_failed` lifecycle state — and therefore the `ci-failed` reaction — is unreachable for GitLab projects.

What *does* work correctly with the GitLab plugin:
- `detectPR` (branch-based PR discovery) — session reaches `pr_open` with `session.pr` set.
- Terminal-state handling — the `pr-closed` reaction fired correctly when a test MR was closed.
- `agent-stuck` reaction.
- The overall pilot loop (agent → branch → push → MR → CI pipeline) works end-to-end.

### AO version

`@aoagents/ao@0.9.2` (installed via npm in a Docker image; CLI package `@aoagents/ao-cli@0.9.2`, `@aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-gitlab@0.9.1`, `@aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-gitlab@0.9.1`)

### Environment

Docker container, `node:20-bookworm-slim`. Self-hosted GitLab (glab 1.112.0, `GITLAB_TOKEN` env var). Reactions config:
```yaml
reactions:
  ci-failed:
    auto: true
    action: send-to-agent
    retries: 2
```
(Side note, possibly worth its own issue: the reaction config merge appears to be shallow — a project-level `reactions.ci-failed` entry without an explicit `action` loses the default `action: send-to-agent`, silently making the reaction a no-op. Had to add `action` explicitly to get past that.)

### Logs / extra context

```
$ ao status --json | jq '.data[] | {name, status, pr}'
{
  "name": "aip-5",
  "status": "pr_open",
  "pr": { "number": 129, "url": "https://<gitlab-host>/.../merge_requests/129" }
}

$ ao events list --project devstack-ai-pipeline
7:32:23 PM  scm.detect_pr_succeeded  info  aip-5  PR #129 detected
# ... 10+ minutes later, MR pipeline status = failed the entire time ...
# no ci.failing event, no reaction.action_succeeded for ci-failed
```

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(session): harden workspace compare-base selection for divergent histories
body:
## Summary

Harden the session workspace Files-tab compare-base resolver after [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) so it remains correct when:

1. the local remote-tracking ref and the provider PR base belong to divergent histories (for example, after a force-push of the target branch),
2. the persisted PR snapshot does not describe the current local workspace `HEAD`, or
3. `git merge-base` cannot establish a common ancestor.

[PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) correctly fixes the reported, normal linear-history case where `origin/main` is stale and the session branch has incorporated a newer `main`. This issue is deliberately a **follow-up**, not a blocker for merging that PR.

**Source:** correctness review of [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848)  
**Analyzed against:** PR head [`22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036) and `main` at [`0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe)  
**Confidence:** High — the candidate-selection path and persisted PR metadata were traced end to end.  
**Priority:** P2 — the normal path is fixed by PR #3848, but affected histories can make the Files tab substantially over-report or misattribute changes.

No implementation is being started as part of filing this issue; it is intended to be independently picked up after PR #3848 merges.

## Background

The Files tab needs a durable comparison base so committed session work remains visible. The original implementation compared against `HEAD`, causing committed changes to disappear. [Issue #3203](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3203) and [PR #3214](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3214) introduced recorded session diff-base metadata and merge-base-aware workspace diffs.

[PR #3688](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3688) then fixed the PR fallback so a provider `BaseSHA` is first resolved through `git merge-base HEAD <BaseSHA>` rather than being used as a raw tree. This prevents independently advanced base-branch changes from appearing in reverse in the session diff.

[PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) addresses another real case:

```text
M1 ---- M2             main
        \
  P ----- H            session/PR branch; H merged M2

origin/main -> M1      stale local remote-tracking ref
PR BaseSHA -> M2       provider-observed PR comparison base
```

Before PR #3848, `resolveWorkspaceCompare` returned immediately after resolving the stale ref:

```text
merge-base(H, origin/main) = M1
diff M1..H = session change P + unrelated base change M2
```

PR #3848 retains the ref-derived candidate, derives another candidate from the PR base, and chooses the PR candidate when the ref candidate is its ancestor:

```text
ref candidate = M1
PR candidate  = merge-base(H, M2) = M2
M1 is ancestor of M2, therefore choose M2
```

That is correct for a normally advancing target branch. The remaining problems are about candidate validity, freshness, and what to do when ancestry is not a total ordering.

## Current code path

The main decision is in [`resolveWorkspaceCompare`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036/backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go#L283-L329):

```go
if pr, ok := selectWorkspaceComparePR(prs, defaultBranch); ok {
	if baseSHA := strings.TrimSpace(pr.BaseSHA); baseSHA != "" && gitCommitExists(ctx, root, baseSHA) {
		if merged, ok := gitMergeBase(ctx, root, baseSHA); ok {
			baseSHA = merged
		}
		if refBased == nil || gitIsAncestor(ctx, root, refBased.BaseSHA, baseSHA) {
			return workspaceCompareTarget{
				BaseSHA: baseSHA,
				BaseRef: strings.TrimSpace(pr.TargetBranch),
				Mode:    WorkspaceCompareBase,
			}
		}
	}
}
if refBased != nil {
	return *refBased
}
if recordedSHA != "" && gitCommitExists(ctx, root, recordedSHA) {
	return workspaceCompareTarget{BaseSHA: recordedSHA, BaseRef: recordedRef, Mode: WorkspaceCompareBase}
}
```

The relevant helper and metadata paths are:

- [`backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036/backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go#L283-L451)
  - `resolveWorkspaceCompare`
  - `selectWorkspaceComparePR`
  - `gitCommitExists`
  - `gitMergeBase`
  - `gitIsAncestor`
- [`backend/internal/service/session/service_test.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036/backend/internal/service/session/service_test.go#L535-L720)
  - `TestWorkspaceFilesRecomputesRecordedRefAfterBaseMoves`
  - `TestWorkspaceFilesExcludeMainChangesMergedInAfterStaleOriginRef`
  - PR fallback tests
- [`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L951-L984)
  - `resolveSpawnDiffBase` records `DiffBaseSHA` and `DiffBaseRef` when the session is created.
- [`backend/internal/domain/pr.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/domain/pr.go#L25-L75)
  - `PullRequest` already carries `HeadSHA`, `BaseSHA`, `UpdatedAtProvider`, and `ObservedAt`.
- [`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go#L330-L355)
  - populates REST `pull.Head.SHA` and `pull.Base.SHA`; the GraphQL path similarly maps `headRefOid` and `baseRefOid`.
- [`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go#L1120-L1177)
  - persists the provider snapshot into `domain.PullRequest`.
- [`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/pr_store.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/pr_store.go#L360-L500)
  - persists and reloads `HeadSHA`, `BaseSHA`, and the observation/provider timestamps.

## Problem 1: divergent candidates after a force-push

Consider a target branch that is force-pushed from an old line of history to a replacement line:

```text
             B          old target history; stale origin/main -> B
            /
A ---------
            \
             X          replacement target history; PR BaseSHA -> X

Feature HEAD H contains the feature work and later merges X, while still
retaining B through its earlier ancestry.
```

Both candidates are valid ancestors of `H`:

```text
ref candidate = B
PR candidate  = X
```

However, neither candidate is an ancestor of the other. The current one-direction check:

```go
gitIsAncestor(refBased.BaseSHA, prBaseSHA)
```

returns false, and the function falls back to `refBased`. Diffing from `B` can once again include replacement-base changes from `X`, remove old-base-only files, and otherwise disagree with the provider PR diff.

This is not a failure of `git merge-base`: both revisions are related to `HEAD`. It is a policy gap for two valid but incomparable candidates.

## Problem 2: PR metadata can be stale relative to the local workspace

`PullRequest` is a persisted observation of provider state, while the Files tab describes the current local worktree. Those two states can temporarily differ:

1. The local agent creates commits or merges a newer target branch but has not pushed yet.
2. The branch was pushed, but the SCM observer has not completed its next poll.
3. A provider request failed, was rate-limited, or the daemon was offline.
4. A stored PR snapshot remains available after the local branch has rebased or otherwise moved.

For example:

```text
persisted pr.HeadSHA = C1
local git HEAD       = C2
```

In this state, `pr.BaseSHA` describes the provider PR at `C1`; it is not proof of the intended comparison base for local `C2`.

Timestamp freshness alone is insufficient. `ObservedAt` is not currently a simple "last successful provider poll" timestamp: the observer deliberately preserves the previous value when metadata and CI have not changed. Even a new timestamp would only prove when data was fetched, not that it corresponds to the current local commit.

The strongest already-available consistency check is commit identity:

```text
pr.HeadSHA == git rev-parse HEAD
```

When equal, the provider snapshot and the Files-tab workspace describe the same committed head (local uncommitted changes can still be layered on top safely). When unequal, PR data may still be a useful lower-confidence candidate, but it should not unconditionally override a valid recorded/ref candidate in an ambiguous ancestry case.

PR #3848 also moves `recordedSHA` after PR selection. When no recorded ref resolves, `refBased == nil` makes any usable PR candidate win without comparing it with the immutable base captured at session spawn. A stale PR snapshot older than `recordedSHA` can therefore replace a previously correct fallback.

## Problem 3: merge-base failure leaves a raw PR SHA eligible

The current code initializes `baseSHA` from `pr.BaseSHA`, attempts `git merge-base`, but only replaces the variable on success:

```go
baseSHA := strings.TrimSpace(pr.BaseSHA)
if merged, ok := gitMergeBase(ctx, root, baseSHA); ok {
	baseSHA = merged
}
// baseSHA is still the raw provider SHA if merge-base failed.
```

If `refBased == nil`, that raw provider SHA is returned as the comparison base. A commit can exist locally while sharing no common ancestor with `HEAD`; `git cat-file -e` proves object existence, not ancestry. A subsequent two-tree diff against an unrelated raw SHA can make most or all of the repository appear changed.

This fallback behavior existed before PR #3848 in the PR path, but the new precedence makes it capable of winning before a valid `recordedSHA`. The candidate should be rejected when merge-base derivation fails.

## Proposed resolution

Treat compare bases as validated candidates rather than encoding precedence through early returns.

### 1. Resolve local HEAD once

```go
localHead, ok := gitRevision(ctx, root, "HEAD")
```

Use this to bind PR metadata to the workspace:

```go
prMatchesWorkspace := strings.TrimSpace(pr.HeadSHA) == localHead
```

Do not add a synchronous GitHub/provider request to the Files read path. External observation belongs in the SCM observer; the service should make a deterministic choice from stored facts and local Git facts.

### 2. Validate every revision-derived candidate

For a ref or provider base revision:

```go
func mergeBaseCandidate(ctx context.Context, root, revision string) (string, bool) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(revision) == "" || !gitCommitExists(ctx, root, revision) {
		return "", false
	}
	return gitMergeBase(ctx, root, revision)
}
```

If `git merge-base HEAD <revision>` fails, reject the candidate and continue to the next fallback. Never return the raw provider SHA merely because the object exists.

`recordedSHA` should also be validated before use. Since it is intended to be the exact spawn-time base, either:

- accept it only when it is still an ancestor of `HEAD`, or
- normalize it through `git merge-base HEAD <recordedSHA>` and explicitly document that behavior.

In either case, an unrelated raw recorded SHA should not be used directly.

### 3. Compare ancestry in both directions

For any two validated candidates `left` and `right`:

```text
left == right                         -> either candidate
left is ancestor of right             -> right is newer
right is ancestor of left             -> left is newer
neither is ancestor of the other      -> divergent/incomparable
```

For comparable candidates, choose the descendant—the most advanced common ancestor already incorporated into `HEAD`.

### 4. Define the divergent-candidate policy explicitly

When a ref/recorded candidate and the PR candidate are incomparable:

- If `pr.HeadSHA == local HEAD`, prefer the validated PR candidate. It is provider data for exactly the commit being displayed and best matches the PR Files view after a target-branch force-push.
- If the PR head does not match local `HEAD`, do not allow stale provider data to override the safer local recorded/ref candidate.
- If no trustworthy candidate remains, use the existing `head_fallback` rather than manufacturing a two-tree diff from an unrelated SHA.

A possible high-level flow is:

```text
1. Resolve HEAD.
2. Derive validated candidates from recordedRef, recordedSHA, and PR BaseSHA.
3. Among comparable candidates, keep the newest descendant.
4. If the PR candidate is incomparable with the best local candidate:
   a. choose PR when pr.HeadSHA == HEAD;
   b. otherwise keep the local candidate.
5. If no validated candidate exists, try the configured default branch.
6. Fall back to HEAD only when all candidates fail.
```

The exact helper structure is intentionally left to the implementation, but the validity and precedence rules should be visible and table-tested rather than implicit in early-return order.

## Acceptance criteria

- The normal stale-linear-ref case from [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) remains fixed.
- When ref and PR-derived candidates are comparable, the newest descendant is selected regardless of input order.
- When they are divergent and `pr.HeadSHA` matches local `HEAD`, the validated PR candidate is selected.
- When they are divergent and PR data does not match local `HEAD`, stale PR data does not override a valid local recorded/ref candidate.
- A missing recorded ref does not automatically cause an older PR candidate to override a valid `recordedSHA`.
- A PR or recorded revision whose merge base cannot be resolved is rejected; its raw SHA is never used for the workspace diff.
- No provider/network request is added to `ListWorkspaceFiles` or `GetWorkspaceFile`.
- File list status, numstat, and per-file patches continue to consume the same resolved `workspaceCompareTarget`.
- Relevant backend verification passes, at minimum:

  ```bash
  cd backend
  go test ./internal/service/session/... -count=1
  go vet ./internal/service/session/...
  go build ./...
  ```

## Non-goals

- Replacing the SCM observer or fetching provider data synchronously from the Files API.
- Changing the frontend or daemon API response shape.
- Reopening the normal linear-history fix in PR #3848.
- Making this follow-up a prerequisite for merging PR #3848.

## Related

- [Issue #3203](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3203) — original committed-work/merge-base Files-tab bug.
- [PR #3214](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3214) — introduced base-aware workspace diffs and recorded spawn bases.
- [PR #3688](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3688) — resolved provider PR base SHA through merge-base.
- [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) — fixes the normal stale `origin/main` tracking-ref case; this issue tracks follow-up hardening.

title: bug(worktree): AO spawns worker branches from stale origin/main — no git fetch before worktree creation
body:
## Problem

AO creates worker branches from the local `origin/main` ref without first running `git fetch`. If the machine running AO has a stale `origin/main` (e.g. last `git fetch` was days ago), the worker branch forks from an old commit.

This causes a cascade of confusing symptoms:

- **Missing files** — code recently merged to `main` is absent from the worker branch
- **Failed file-read tool calls** — the agent tries to read files that exist on real `main` but not the stale base
- **Failed test commands** — tests reference code or configs that aren't in the checkout
- **Long commit history in PRs** — GitHub compares the worker branch against the real updated `main`, showing a divergent base with noisy diff
- **Confusing "tool call failed" cards** in the Chat UI

## Root Cause

### No `git fetch` anywhere in the spawn path

The entire `spawn → worktree` flow is local git operations only. There are zero `git fetch` calls in the Go backend. The codebase only mentions `git fetch` in **error messages** telling the user to run it manually:

```
"has no local head, no remote, and no tag — run `git fetch` then retry"
```

### The exact flow

1. `session_manager/manager.go:714` — `createSessionWorkspace()` calls `workspace.Create()`
2. `adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:760` — `addWorktree()` calls `resolveBaseRef()`
3. `workspace.go:1015` — `resolveBaseRef()` → `resolveBaseRefFromDefault()` → `baseRefCandidates()`
4. `adapters/workspace/gitworktree/commands.go:131` — builds candidate refs:

```go
func baseRefCandidates(branch, defaultBranch string) []string {
    candidates := []string{"origin/" + branch}
    // ...
    candidates = append(candidates, "origin/"+defaultBranch, "refs/heads/"+defaultBranch)
    return append(candidates, branch)
}
```

5. `workspace.go:1065` — `refExists()` just runs `git rev-parse --verify <ref>` against **local** state

All candidates are local refs. Whatever commit `origin/main` points at locally is used as the base — no freshness check, no fetch.

```
Actual GitHub main:     A -- B -- C -- D -- E
Local origin/main:      A -- B
AO worker branch:       A -- B -- ao-work
```

## Proposed Fix

Before resolving the base ref in `addWorktree()`, refresh the default branch remote ref:

```bash
git fetch origin main
```

### Design constraints

1. **Fetch, not pull.** `git pull` would merge/rebase the user's current checkout and mutate their working branch. `git fetch` only updates remote-tracking refs.

2. **Best-effort / non-blocking.** This is the first network call in the spawn path. Fetch must not cause spawn to fail if:
   - The machine is offline / air-gapped
   - Git auth is not configured
   - The network is slow
   
   On fetch failure: log a warning, fall through to local refs. A stale base is annoying; a failed spawn because GitHub is down is a regression.

3. **Fetch only the ref, not the full repo.** Use `git fetch origin main` (surgical) not `git fetch origin` (full fetch, heavy on large repos).

4. **Respect fork workflows.** When `origin` is a fork and `upstream` is canonical, fetching `origin/main` gets the fork's main — which can also be stale. The project config already supports qualified refs (`defaultBranch: "upstream/main"` → used verbatim in `baseRefCandidates`), but there's no fetch logic to match. The fetch should extract the remote from the configured `defaultBranch`: if it contains `/`, split on first segment as the remote name; otherwise default to `origin`.

5. **Architecture boundary.** The "should we refresh before spawning" policy decision belongs in the session manager (before `workspace.Create()`). The gitworktree adapter should expose a `FetchDefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath, remote, branch) error` method — pure git operation, no policy.

### Proposed flow

```
spawn
  → session manager: decide to refresh
    → detect remote from DefaultBranch ("upstream/main" → remote=upstream, else origin)
    → gitworktree.FetchDefaultBranch(ctx, repo, remote, branch)
      → if error: log warning, continue (non-blocking)
      → if success: origin/main is now fresh
  → workspace.Create (unchanged)
    → addWorktree → resolveBaseRef → finds fresh origin/main
```

## Affected Code

| File | Location | Role |
|------|----------|------|
| `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go` | `addWorktree()` :760 | Where fetch should be inserted (or called from session manager) |
| `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go` | `resolveBaseRef()` :1015 | Reads local refs only |
| `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/commands.go` | `baseRefCandidates()` :131 | Builds candidate list (all local refs) |
| `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` | `createSessionWorkspace()` :714 | Policy decision: trigger fetch before Create |
| `backend/internal/domain/projectconfig.go` | `DefaultBranch` :21 | Config source — no canonical-remote concept today |

## Existing Tests to Update

- `manager_test.go:920` — `TestSpawnRecordsRemoteTrackingDiffBaseWhenLocalDefaultBranchLags` explicitly tests the current stale-ref behavior. Will need updated expectations after the fix.

## Related Issues

- #3810 — workspace spawn forces root repo's default branch on child repos (different problem, same area)
- #3857 — harden workspace compare-base selection for divergent histories (related: diff base after the fact)

title: bug(frontend): orchestrator session left showing TERMINAL ENDED after settings save replaces agent — no navigation to replacement, confusing dead-end
body:
## Bug

When a user changes the **Default orchestrator agent** in Project Settings → Agents and clicks **Save changes**, AO tears down the old orchestrator session and attempts to spawn a replacement. But when the replacement fails (in the reported case, the old orchestrator was terminated by a stale activity/terminal-idle race — see the "Interface switch failed" banner in the video), the **old orchestrator session stays visible in the UI showing "TERMINAL ENDED / [process exited]"** and the user is left on a dead session page with no automatic navigation to the new one or any other recovery action.

The user is stuck looking at a terminated orchestrator terminal with a confusing dead-end UI (exit text, red status dot, and a stale "Interface switch failed" banner), with no indication that a replacement was attempted or how to recover.

**Source:** Reported by @nikhilachale in Discord (#bug-triage thread), with screen recording | **Reported at:** 2026-08-12 ~04:55 IST
**Analyzed against:** `419fb3ba7` (origin/main HEAD)
**Confidence:** High — traced the exact frontend code path
**Priority:** high — core workflow (settings save) produces a confusing dead-end with no automatic recovery; affects any user who changes the orchestrator agent

## Reproduction

1. Open a project that has an active orchestrator session running
2. Open Settings → Agents tab
3. Change the **Default orchestrator agent** (e.g., from one agent to another, or change its model)
4. Click **Save changes**
5. Observe: the old orchestrator's terminal shows "TERMINAL ENDED / [process exited]" with a red status dot
6. If the replacement spawn fails (stale activity race, terminal-not-idle, etc.), the UI stays on this dead session indefinitely

## Root Cause

The save handler in `ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` (lines 208-220) calls `spawnOrchestrator(projectId, "settings", true)` with `clean=true` — which tears down the existing orchestrator and spawns a replacement — but **does not navigate to the new session's ID on success**, and **only surfaces a small text error on failure**.

```tsx
// ProjectSettingsForm.tsx:208-220
if (
    form.orchestratorAgent !== initialOrchestratorAgent ||
    (activeOrchestrator && activeOrchestrator.provider !== form.orchestratorAgent)
) {
    try {
        await spawnOrchestrator(projectId, "settings", true);
    } catch (error) {
        return {
            replacementError:
                error instanceof Error ? error.message : t("settings.project.replaceOrchestratorFailed"),
        };
    }
}
```

**Two defects:**

### 1. No navigation to the replacement session on success

Compare with every other spawn call site:
- **`ShellTopbar.tsx:152-157`** — spawns, invalidates workspace query, then **navigates** to `/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId`
- **`restart-orchestrator.ts:43-48`** — spawns, invalidates workspace query, then **navigates** to `/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId`

`ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` spawns but **never navigates**. On success, `spawnOrchestrator()` returns the new session ID, but the return value is **discarded**. The mutation's `onSuccess` only calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries` and `onSaved()` — it does not navigate. So even on a successful replacement, the user stays on whatever view they were on. If the workspace query refetch hasn't propagated yet (React Query cache timing), the old (now-terminated) orchestrator's "TERMINAL ENDED" view can persist.

### 2. Confusing dead-end on failure

When `spawnOrchestrator` throws (replacement failed), the old orchestrator is **already terminated** (the `clean=true` path calls `RetireForReplacement` before spawning the new one — `service.go:371-376`). The user sees:
- The old session's terminal showing "TERMINAL ENDED / [process exited]"
- A red status dot on the Orchestrator tab
- Potentially a stale "Interface switch failed" banner (if the termination raced with an interface transition)
- A small `replacementError` text in the settings footer (easy to miss — it's `text-warning` text-xs, line 494)

There is no prominent error state, no "retry" CTA, and no navigation away from the dead session. The `SaveChangesFooter` shows the error as small warning text at the bottom of the settings form — which may be scrolled out of view or dismissed by closing settings.

## Impact

- **Core workflow broken:** Changing the orchestrator agent is a common settings operation; it should not leave the user stranded on a dead session.
- **No recovery path:** The user has no obvious way to get back to a working orchestrator — they must manually spawn a new one from the topbar or sidebar.
- **Confusing UX:** "TERMINAL ENDED" + "Interface switch failed" banner + red dot is a jarring combination with no explanation of what happened or what to do next.

## Fix

**Frontend fix** in `ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`:

1. **Navigate to the new orchestrator session on success.** Capture the session ID from `spawnOrchestrator()` and navigate to it (matching `restart-orchestrator.ts` pattern). This requires passing a `navigate` function into `SettingsBody` (or lifting the spawn/navigate into the parent component that has router access).

2. **Surface replacement failures more prominently.** The current `replacementError` text-xs in the footer is insufficient. Consider:
   - Keeping the settings modal open with a visible error banner when replacement fails
   - Adding a "Retry" or "Spawn new orchestrator" CTA button next to the error
   - Showing a toast/notification instead of (or in addition to) footer text

3. **Handle the already-terminated case gracefully.** When the old orchestrator is already terminated (by the clean replacement path) but the new spawn fails, the user needs a clear path to recovery — not a dead terminal view.

## Related

- [#2501](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2501) — orchestrator terminated mid-turn by stale-activity/probe race, then silently replaced with no linkage (same underlying lifecycle race that can cause the replacement to fail)
- [#3300](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/3300) — killed/exited session page is a confusing dead-end (same UX pattern: dead session shown with no recovery CTA)

title: bug(chat): Japanese IME confirmation Enter can submit the message
body:
## Problem

In the desktop chat composer, pressing Enter to confirm Japanese IME composition can submit, queue, or steer the message unexpectedly.

The chat composer currently treats every non-Shift Enter as send. It does not guard `event.nativeEvent.isComposing` (or the `keyCode === 229` fallback). This is inconsistent with the New Task composer, which already excludes IME composition from its Enter-to-submit behavior.

This was reproduced on macOS with AO v0.12.2. The same unguarded handler is present in the v0.12.3 source.

## Reproduction

1. Enable a Japanese IME on macOS.
2. Type text in a live session's chat composer and leave it in composition/conversion state.
3. Press Enter once to confirm the candidate.
4. The draft is submitted/queued/steered instead of only confirming the IME composition.

## Expected behavior

- Enter during IME composition must only confirm the composition and must never submit, queue, steer, or select a composer suggestion.
- Please also provide a send-key preference for IME-heavy workflows:
  - `Enter inserts newline; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends`
  - `Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts newline` (current behavior)
- The composer hint should reflect the selected mode.

## Suggested implementation

At minimum, return early from the chat composer's key handler while composing, using both `event.nativeEvent.isComposing` and `event.keyCode === 229` as the robust guard. Add regression coverage for composition Enter so no delivery callback is invoked.

## Summary

The official Discord invite used across the project (`https://discord.com/invite/UZv7JjxbwG`) is reported as **invalid or expired** by some users (mobile Discord, opened from GitHub). Contributors interpret this as the project blocking community access.

## Where the invite is wired

- `README.md` (+ locale READMEs)
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (primary onboarding path: “Join Discord first”)
- `frontend/src/landing/packages/shared/src/constants.ts` → `DISCORD_URL`
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/report-problem.ts` → `DISCORD_INVITE_URL`
- tests that assert the same URL

## Observed behavior

- User sees Discord modal: “邀请链接无效或已过期 / Invite invalid or expired”
- Public invite API still resolves `UZv7JjxbwG` with `expires_at: null` and an active guild — so this may be client/network/account specific rather than a fully dead invite
- Regardless of root cause, **first-time contributors have no documented fallback** when Discord fails, and CONTRIBUTING currently funnels everything through Discord

## Requested actions

1. Maintainers: verify the invite from a clean account / alternate region; if needed, create a permanent invite and rotate the code in all touchpoints above.
2. Docs: document a fallback (GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/discussions) / Issues) so “Join Discord” is not a hard gate when the invite fails.
