Document a **GitHub fallback** when the Discord invite shows “invalid or expired”, and fix stale `AgentWrapper` → `Untrivial-ai` links in contributor docs/templates.

## Why

Several users (see #3869 and Discussion #3868) open the official invite from GitHub and get Discord’s **invalid/expired** modal. CONTRIBUTING currently treats Discord as the first onboarding step with no documented alternative, so people assume the project is blocking joins.

The public invite (`UZv7JjxbwG`) still resolves server-side with no expiry, so this is often network/account/client related — but the docs should not hard-gate contribution on Discord access.

## How

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: add “If the Discord invite fails” with workarounds + Discussions/Issues links; note Discord is preferred but not required
- Fix stale org links in CONTRIBUTING, PR template, and issue template contact link

## Testing

- Docs-only change; reviewed rendered markdown via `git diff`

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links #3869 / Discussion #3868
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests N/A (docs)
- [x] Relevant CI N/A (docs)

Related: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/discussions/3868

title: High session spawn failure rate: mostly missing agent binary / runtime and git branch state, not the spawn engine
body:
## Summary

Session spawn has a high failure rate that is concentrated in a few fixable causes, not in the spawn engine itself. From telemetry (PostHog project 475752, last 14 days):

- App-initiated spawns (`ao.renderer.orchestrator_spawn_*`): ~50% of requests end in `failed` (e.g. Aug 11: 700 requested, 358 succeeded, 344 failed).
- All spawns (backend `ao.session.spawned` vs `ao.session.spawn_failed`): ~22% failure (agent-initiated spawns dominate volume and mostly succeed, which pulls the blended rate down).
- Once an agent is actually installed, per-harness failure is low: claude-code 392 failed / 8,832 spawned (~4.5%), codex ~4.8%. So the harnesses themselves are not the problem.

## Failure reasons (backend `ao.session.spawn_failed`, error_kind / error_code, 14d, ~3,030 failures)

| reason | count | approx share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING | 878 | 29% |
| AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND | 531 | 18% |
| internal (unclassified) | 952 | 31% |
| BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED | 313 | 10% |
| BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE | 124 | 4% |
| INVALID_BRANCH | 79 | 3% |
| SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED | 67 | 2% |
| AGENT_REQUIRED | 56 | 2% |
| others (CHAT_AUTH_REQUIRED, WORKSPACE_PROVISION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_HARNESS, ...) | ~30 | 1% |

Session kind of failures: orchestrator 2,271 vs worker 759. Most failures happen before a harness is attached (2,108 of the failures have no `harness`), consistent with failing at validation.

## Root cause

Three buckets account for essentially all of it:

1. Agent / runtime not installed (~47%): `AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND` + `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING`. Users click spawn with an agent whose CLI is not on the machine, or a required runtime is missing. This is a setup/environment gap surfaced as a spawn failure, not a spawn bug.
2. Internal errors (~31%): unclassified. Not covered by the error codes; needs Sentry stack traces to break down.
3. Git branch state (~17%): `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED`, `BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE`, `INVALID_BRANCH`. The branch is not fetched, or already checked out in another worktree.

## Proposed fixes

- Pre-flight the agent before enabling spawn: check the selected harness binary exists (and the runtime prerequisite), and if not, block spawn with a clear "install X" prompt instead of letting it fail. Removes the ~47% agent/runtime bucket.
- Auto-fetch on `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` (fetch the branch, then spawn) instead of failing, and give a clear message for `BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE`. Removes much of the ~17% git bucket.
- Investigate the ~31% `internal` failures in Sentry and give them real error codes so they stop landing in the catch-all bucket.

## Notes

- Data is anonymous, install-based (no per-user identity).
- The renderer `orchestrator_spawn_failed` event does not carry a reason; the reasons above come from the backend `ao.session.spawn_failed` `error_kind`/`error_code`. Consider adding the error code to the renderer event too, so the GUI failure rate is self-describing.

title: bug(orchestrator): fresh orchestrator spawn crashes claude with "invalid session id", leaving an unrecoverable exited/non-terminated session
body:
## Summary Spawning a new **orchestrator** session (`ao spawn --kind orchestrator ...`) for a specific project intermittently fails immediately: the tmux pane shows `invalid session id` and the underlying `claude` process never starts. This has recurred across several days on the same project, and there is no recovery path — `restore` refuses the resulting session, and killing + respawning reproduces the exact same failure. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Have an existing orchestrator session for a project (harness `claude-code`, mode `tui`). 2. At some point the session's activity flips to `exited` while `terminated` stays `false` (observed after a daemon/tmux restart, e.g. Mac sleep — but also reproduced via a **fresh** spawn, see below). 3. `ao session get ` shows: ``` status: exited activity: exited terminated: false ``` 4. `ao session restore ` refuses: ``` Session is not restorable (SESSION_NOT_RESTORABLE) ``` 5. `ao session kill ` succeeds and flips `terminated: true`. 6. `ao spawn --project

--kind orchestrator --branch --name orchestrator --mode tui` creates a **new** session id, but the tmux pane immediately shows: ``` invalid session id ``` and stays there — no `claude` process is running in the pane (`tmux list-panes -F "#{pane_current_command}"` shows a bare `cat`, not `claude`). The corresponding `ao agent-process supervise ... -- claude ...` wrapper process is also gone (it exited alongside the crashed `claude` child), leaving a dead pane with nothing supervising it. 7. The new session is left in the same broken state as step 3 (`status/activity: exited`, `terminated: false`) — no further recovery via CLI. This reproduced on a fresh `ao spawn` (not just `restore`), which rules out a single stale/orphaned resume-id as the sole cause — something about how the `--session-id`/`--resume` value is generated or accepted for this project's orchestrator role is rejected by the `claude` binary outright. For contrast, doing the identical kill+respawn dance on a **different** project's orchestrator (same `claude-code` harness, same `claude` binary version) recovered cleanly — the new session started normally with a live `claude` process in the pane. So this is not a global daemon/tmux issue; it is scoped to specific project/session state. ## Observed ``` $ ao session get status: exited activity: exited terminated: false ``` Pane content: ``` invalid session id ``` No `claude` process; `ao agent-process supervise` wrapper also absent (crashed together with the child). Pane is left running a bare `cat` keep-alive with no supervisor watching it. ## Why this is bad - The session is stuck in a state with no CLI verb to recover it: not `terminated` (so `restore` refuses), not actually alive (so nothing else works either). - The only workaround found is `kill` + respawn, which is destructive and, in this case, **reproduces the identical failure** — there is no way back into a working orchestrator session for the affected project without deeper manual intervention (unclear which project-level state is at fault). - `daemon.log` does not capture this at all — the daemon's own log file was stale (last write far in the past despite the daemon actively serving requests), and grepping it for "invalid session" or the failing session's id returns nothing. There is no first-class signal anywhere (log or `ao session get`) pointing at *why* the harness rejected the id. ## Environment - `ao version dev` (self-built) - `claude` (Claude Code) 2.1.228 - macOS, daemon runs under the desktop app (`Agent Orchestrator.app`) - harness: `claude-code`, role: `orchestrator`, mode: `tui` ## Possibly related - #2702 — restore recreates the tmux session but never relaunches the agent (zombie session). Related but not identical: that issue is about `restore` after a daemon restart; this reproduces on a **fresh spawn** as well, and even kill+respawn doesn't recover it for the affected project. - #1521 — different "Invalid session ID" error (path basename `.` at spawn time, rejected by a regex check in the runtime plugin) — different code path, not orchestrator-specific, doesn't match this symptom (that one fails *at spawn time* with a clear validation error; this one fails *inside the harness process* after the tmux pane is already up). Happy to provide further `ao session get` / `sqlite3` state dumps — keeping project specifics generic since this is from a private setup.

title: fix(cli): allow dots in sessionIDPattern to match projectIDPattern
body:
Code changes: +32 -20  
Tests: +124 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Any project whose id contains a dot (for example `myproject.example`) fails to spawn or restore sessions. The agent process never starts: the terminal runtime is left at its keepalive process and the session lands in `exited` / `is_terminated=false` limbo.

Closes #3875. Also covers the Windows ConPTY boundary reported in #4479.

## Root cause

AO session ids are generated as `{ProjectID}-{num}`. Project ids permit dots, but several downstream session-id validators used a narrower alphabet. The hidden `agent-process supervise` command rejected a dotted id before launching the agent; Windows ConPTY and the headless-review submit allowlist carried equivalent copies of the narrower contract.

## Fix

- Define the canonical AO session-id alphabet in the domain package: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`.
- Reuse that contract in supervisor, hook, telemetry, ConPTY, and reviewer-submit validation.
- Keep runtime launch-id validation separate and narrow.
- Continue rejecting leading dots, slashes, traversal payloads, whitespace, and shell metacharacters.

The supervisor still validates its internal CLI boundary before starting a child, but it no longer maintains an independent definition of a valid session id.

## Testing

- Unit accept/reject coverage for the canonical session-id contract.
- End-to-end supervisor coverage proving `my.project-16` starts its child.
- Traversal rejection coverage for `../evil`, `a/b`, and `.hidden`.
- ConPTY coverage for dotted ids and unsafe inputs.
- Headless-review permission coverage proving a dotted worker id can submit its result.
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...`
- `cd frontend && npm run build`

## Manual verification

Reproduced on the installed `0.13.1-nightly.202609241911` app with project `ao.dotted-repro-test`: spawn initially returned `idle`, then became `exited` with `isTerminated=false`; the terminal contained `invalid session id`.

Re-tested the same repository and project id in the rebased dev Electron app using isolated data. The session remained `idle`, had a live supervisor and Codex child, and successfully completed an `exit-agent` → `resume-agent` cycle. The native dev UI showed `Dotted ID Fixed · Codex · Idle`.

`npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --all` could not run the artifact workflow locally because `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` is unavailable; that job is left to remote CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: bug(chat): nested Codex turns can drain queued automation before the root completes, leaving a permanent phantom Working turn
body:
## Bug summary

AO can permanently show **Working** after the provider is idle and all real work has finished.

This is not merely a stale animation and it is not a long-running tool call. In the captured incident, a nested Codex child turn completed while the root turn was still active. AO treated that child completion as if the whole conversation had become idle, drained a queued automation request too early, and created a second durable AO turn. Codex accepted the automation message into the still-running root transcript rather than starting the provider turn AO had assigned. The assigned AO turn therefore received no provider lifecycle events, remained `running` forever in SQLite, and kept the frontend spinner alive.

**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1  
**Reported/reproduced:** 2026-08-12, from a live packaged AO desktop session  
**Packaged version:** `0.12.1-nightly.202608101434` (bundled daemon reports `dev`)  
**Code inspected:** current `origin/main` at `f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9`  
**Codex CLI:** `0.147.0`  
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64

## User-visible failure

The UI had remained in this state for about 88 minutes when captured and was still stuck afterward:

![Permanent orphaned Working turn after 1h27m](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-nested-turn-orphan-20260812/.issue-assets/chat-nested-turn-orphan/orphan-working-1h27.png)

The visible child-agent review was DONE, there was no new chat activity, and the relevant Codex processes were sleeping at 0% CPU. Restarting/re-rendering the UI cannot repair this because the durable turn row itself is still `running`.

## Observed event timeline

Session: `agent-orchestrator-1-95`  
Conversation: `c1f16460…`

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 05:31:11.935 | Root AO turn `8819be57…` starts; provider turn `019ff474…` |
| 05:32:05.454 | PR review automation is queued while the root is active |
| 05:39:35.091 | Nested child turn `ab357b31…` completes |
| 05:39:35.145 | Only 54 ms later, AO prematurely dispatches queued automation as AO turn `6765ffd1…`, assigning provider ID `019ff47b…` |
| 05:39:37.317 | The automation message appears in the native Codex transcript tagged with the **original root** provider ID `019ff474…`, not the newly assigned ID |
| 05:42:13.774 | The real root turn completes |
| 07:07:48 | Screenshot: assigned automation turn has been `running` for 88.2 minutes with zero activities and zero provider events |

The queued automation was dispatched while the actual root still had another 158.6 seconds of work remaining.

The native Codex transcript ends normally with `task_complete` for `019ff474…`. The orphan provider ID `019ff47b…` never appears anywhere in that transcript.

## Contradictory live state

At the same instant:

| Layer | State |
|---|---|
| SQLite turn row | automation turn = `running` |
| Turn activities | zero |
| Normalized provider events | zero |
| Controller snapshot | `ready` |
| Provider thread state | `idle` |
| Session activity | `idle` |
| Frontend | **Working** indefinitely |
| Codex app-server / code-mode host | sleeping, 0% CPU |

This rules out a live tool call. It is a durable/provider lifecycle split.

## Deterministic code path

The controller models a conversation with one mutable `pendingTurnID` / `ackedTurnID` pair ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L131-L140)).

1. Dispatch creates/binds the queued AO turn and records it as pending ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L750-L762)).
2. **Every** provider `turn.started`, including nested child turns, overwrites `pendingTurnID` and `ackedTurnID` and marks the controller busy ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1315-L1322)).
3. **Every** `turn.completed`, regardless of whether it matches the dispatched root, sets the controller ready ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1350-L1359)).
4. After projection, every completion reports the session idle and drains one queued request ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1697-L1705)).
5. The Codex adapter has the same single-slot assumption: every provider start overwrites `activeTurn` ([conversation.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go#L150-L157)), and interruption targets that value ([conversation.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go#L486-L499)).
6. The frontend considers any durable `running` turn active ([conversation.ts](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/frontend/src/renderer/types/conversation.ts#L746-L750)), so the orphan has no natural recovery path and the Working indicator remains ([ChatWorkspace.tsx](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx#L1848-L1860)).

## Why the other reports looked similar

Two earlier screenshots were not permanent backend freezes:

![Short-lived parent activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-nested-turn-orphan-20260812/.issue-assets/chat-nested-turn-orphan/short-parent-working.png)

![Parent still active after visible child completed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-nested-turn-orphan-20260812/.issue-assets/chat-nested-turn-orphan/overlap-parent-working.png)

In those cases the root was genuinely active and completed shortly afterward. However, `groupByTurn` anchors the entire parent group at its first sequence position ([ChatWorkspace.tsx](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx#L1719-L1785)). Later parent activity can therefore render above completed child cards. At the bottom of the transcript the user sees “DONE” beside “Working,” with no visible evidence of what is still active.

That is an adjacent presentation defect which makes a healthy overlap indistinguishable from this permanent orphan.

## Proposed fix

### Lifecycle correctness

- Track the AO-dispatched **primary/root provider turn** separately from nested provider executions.
- Do not let nested `turn.started` replace primary ownership.
- Do not let nested `turn.completed` set the conversation Ready/Idle or drain the request queue.
- Drain only when the root thread is actually quiescent.
- Add acknowledgement recovery for an AO-dispatched provider ID that never emits `turn.started`.
- Make adapter interruption target the primary AO-dispatched turn, not the most recently started nested turn.
- Reconcile a durable `running` row when the controller is ready and the provider is authoritatively idle, while preserving the rule that failed/unknown probes are not proof of death.

Avoid inferring parentage only from timing or adding a heuristic `parentTurnId` to `ConversationTurn`. The normalizer currently discards provider thread identity, and overlapping events can also be compaction, replay, or resumed work. Codex exposes explicit thread/source metadata; AO should preserve enough of that identity, or model nested provider runs separately from user-request turns.

### UI clarity

- Show the latest activity and age of the active primary turn, with a way to jump to it.
- Keep later parent activity visible after child completion rather than anchoring it entirely above child cards.
- Surface child execution as nested/structured activity.
- If a durable turn has no provider events for a threshold, show an advisory recovery state; do not declare it dead solely from elapsed time.

## Regression coverage / acceptance criteria

- [ ] A nested child start does not replace the primary dispatched turn.
- [ ] A nested child completion does not settle the parent, report the session idle, or drain the queue.
- [ ] Automation queued during root work remains queued until root completion.
- [ ] Root completion dispatches the next request exactly once.
- [ ] A dispatched turn that never acknowledges eventually reaches a recoverable terminal/error state.
- [ ] Stop targets the primary provider turn.
- [ ] Compaction, replay, and resumed-thread flows remain correct.
- [ ] An overlapping parent/child transcript keeps the current parent activity visible.
- [ ] No durable turn remains indefinitely `running` while controller and authoritative provider state are idle.

## Impact

- Misleading multi-hour “Working” state.
- Queued PR-review automation is injected into the wrong provider turn.
- Future queue work may remain blocked behind an orphan.
- Stop/recovery can target the wrong nested turn.
- Users cannot distinguish legitimate hidden parent work from a lifecycle failure.

## Related work

- [Issue #3749](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3749) has the same terminal symptom (durable/in-memory turn-state desync) but a different trigger: projection transaction failure.
- [PR #3752](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3752) adds Stop-time reconciliation and post-commit memory mutation for that path. It can provide manual recovery after Stop, but it does not prevent nested start/completion events from changing primary ownership or prematurely draining the queue.
- [Issue #3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) is the broader structured Chat work.

title: Chat/ACP broken on Intel Macs: bundled acp-runtime Node signed without allow-unsigned-executable-memory → V8 crash (exit 133), "peer disconnected before response"
body:
## Summary

Chat (ACP) is completely broken on Intel Macs: the app-bundled Node runtime in `Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node` is Hardened-Runtime signed **without** `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. On x86_64 that entitlement is required for V8 to make JIT memory executable (`allow-jit`/MAP_JIT only covers the arm64 path), so the ACP adapter process crashes at V8 tier-up before it can answer `initialize`. The daemon surfaces this as:

```
switch interface <session>: resume chat: chat driver incompatible: ACP initialize:
{"code": -32603, "message": "Internal error", "data": {"error": "peer disconnected before response"}}
```

The "chat driver incompatible" label is misleading — no version incompatibility exists; the bundled Node cannot run *any* JavaScript on Intel.

## Environment

- Agent Orchestrator **0.12.3** (`dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`), also reproduced on the previous build (0.12.x, ~2 days earlier)
- macOS **15.7.8**, native **x86_64** Intel Mac (Mac Pro, Xeon W) — no Rosetta involved
- Bundled Node: **v22.23.2** (`Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node`)
- ACP adapter: `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` **0.64.2** (bundled)

## One-line repro (no AO involvement needed)

```console
$ /Applications/Agent\ Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node --version
v22.23.2
$ /Applications/Agent\ Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node -e 'console.log(1)'
# V8 fatal: "Check failed: 12 == (*__error())" in v8::base::OS::SetPermissions
#   -> MemoryAllocator::SetPermissionsOnExecutableMemoryChunk
# stack includes Runtime_BytecodeBudgetInterrupt_Ignition (first JIT tier-up)
$ echo $?
133
```

`--version` works (no JIT reached); any real script dies. Piping an ACP `initialize` request into the bundled adapter under this Node crashes identically with no JSON-RPC response — which is exactly what the daemon reports as "peer disconnected before response". macOS crash reports (`~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/node-*.ips`) show the same signature with parent process `ao`, i.e. the daemon's own spawns hit it, not just manual runs.

## Root cause

Signature of the bundled node (`codesign -d --entitlements -`):

```
CodeDirectory v=20500 flags=0x10000(runtime) TeamIdentifier=X9LNSP8MC2
[Key] com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit                 -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.audio-input           -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.bluetooth             -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.camera                -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.print                 -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.usb                   -> true
```

It looks like the Electron app's entitlements file was reused for the helper. Missing: `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` (official Node.js macOS binaries ship with it in addition to `allow-jit`, precisely because Intel V8 calls `mprotect(RWX)` rather than using MAP_JIT).

Proof the adapter itself is fine: the identical bundled `dist/index.js` run under a system Node (signed with `allow-jit` + `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`) answers `initialize` correctly in under a second (`agentInfo: claude-agent-acp 0.64.2`).

## Impact

- Every chat/ACP interface switch fails on Intel Macs, in ~1.5–3 s, 100% of the time (this machine's DB shows 6/6 failed `tui -> chat` transitions across two builds, zero successes ever).
- Because the failure is wrapped as "chat driver incompatible", users are steered toward version debugging instead of the packaging defect.

## Suggested fix

Sign the bundled `acp-runtime` Node with `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` (matching official Node.js distribution entitlements) for the x64 build — or use the official Node binary untouched. Ideally also make the daemon include the peer's stderr in the ACP initialize error, which would have surfaced the V8 fatal directly.

title: fix(session): harden workspace compare-base selection for divergent histories
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3848 (which fixed the normal stale-linear-`origin/main` case) addressing the three gaps identified in [issue #3857](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3857), a correctness review of that PR:

- **Divergent candidates after a force-push** — the ref-derived and PR-derived compare bases can both be valid ancestors of `HEAD` with neither an ancestor of the other (e.g. after the target branch is force-pushed to a replacement line). The prior one-directional ancestor check silently fell back to the ref candidate here, which can disagree with the provider's PR diff. Candidates are now compared in both directions; when genuinely incomparable, the PR candidate is only trusted when its `HeadSHA` matches the local workspace's actual `HEAD`.
- **Stale PR metadata vs. local workspace** — a persisted PR snapshot can describe an earlier local commit than the one currently checked out. The PR candidate is now weighed against a properly validated local candidate (ref-derived, or the spawn-time `recordedSHA` re-derived through merge-base) instead of unconditionally winning whenever no ref-derived candidate was found.
- **Raw SHA fallback on merge-base failure** — `pr.BaseSHA` was initialized as the candidate and only replaced with the merge-base result on success, so a commit sharing no common ancestor with `HEAD` (object exists locally, but unrelated history) could be returned as a raw, unrelated diff base. Every revision-derived candidate (ref, `recordedSHA`, and PR base) now goes through a single `mergeBaseCandidate()` validator that rejects the candidate outright when merge-base derivation fails.

Fixes #3857

## Test plan
- [x] Added 6 new tests covering each acceptance criterion: divergent force-push histories (PR-head-matches and PR-head-stale), comparable candidates regardless of order, a missing recorded ref not letting a stale PR override a valid `recordedSHA`, and two variants of rejecting a PR base with no common ancestor (with and without a local fallback candidate present). Each new test fails against the pre-fix code and passes with the fix.
- [x] `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/session/... -count=1` (all pass, including every pre-existing workspace-files test)
- [x] `go vet ./internal/service/session/...`
- [x] `go build ./...`

title: feat: add native Android emulator (Track A)
body:
## What

Adds a native, in-app Android emulator: a Settings-gated "Emulator" tab (default off) that boots a real, AO-managed Android device (Google's own SDK/emulator binary, not a from-scratch emulator) directly inside a session, with a live view, tap/swipe/keyboard input, and an agent-facing `ao android emulator` CLI surface (`screenshot`, `inspect-ui`, `tap`/`swipe`/`type`/`press-key`, `find-source`) so the agent can see and drive the device too.

This is **Track A (Android) only** — cross-platform on **Windows, macOS, and Linux**. iOS Simulator support (Track B, macOS-only) is a separate, not-yet-built follow-up.

## Why

Lets an agent build and verify a mobile app end-to-end without leaving AO — install the SDK, boot a device, see the screen, tap through the app, and locate the source behind what's on screen, the same way a developer would with Android Studio's embedded emulator.

## How

- **SDK acquisition** (`androidsdk`): downloads/verifies `platform-tools`, `emulator`, and one pinned system image directly from Google's public repository manifests — no JVM/`sdkmanager` dependency.
- **Device lifecycle** (`androidemulator`): one persistent, shared, headless emulator process with quick-boot snapshots and crash/restart-with-backoff, driven over the loopback `EmulatorController` gRPC service the SDK's own emulator binary exposes (insecure/no-auth by default, confirmed during an earlier spike — no WebRTC in the standard SDK, so the transport is `getScreenshot` polling at ~5fps, not smooth video).
- **Renderer**: new "Emulator" tab in the session inspector (same pattern as Browser/Files), gated behind a Settings toggle so it costs nothing when unused.
- **Agent-facing CLI** (`ao android emulator ...`, surfaced to agents via the `using-ao` skill): screenshot, `uiautomator`-based UI tree inspection, tap/swipe/type/key input, and heuristic identifier→source-file lookup.
- **Env integration**: `ANDROID_HOME`/`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`/`PATH` are injected into session and standalone terminals once the SDK is installed, and `ao doctor` reports SDK/virtualization status.
- **Process supervision fix**: `Kill()` now terminates the whole process tree (`taskkill /T /F` on Windows, process-group kill on Unix), not just the tracked PID — the emulator binary is a launcher whose actual VM backend runs as a separate child process, and a single-PID kill left it orphaned, holding the AVD's lock files and breaking every subsequent boot.

**Known constraint, not a bug**: the emulator needs real host headroom (~3-4GB RAM, a few CPU cores) once booted. On a memory-constrained host it can boot but then show in-guest ANRs ("System UI isn't responding") under contention — expected on any Android emulator (Google's own guidance is 16GB+ RAM for a comfortable experience), not specific to this integration.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` all clean.
- `go test ./...` passes for every android-related package (`androidsdk`, `androidemulator`, `daemon`, `cli`, `session_manager`'s new env-injection tests); a handful of pre-existing, unrelated flakes on this Windows dev box (nvm-version PATH test, a workspace-watcher timing test) are unaffected by this branch — verified they fail identically on `origin/main`.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run` (121 tests across `EmulatorPanel`, `useAndroidDevice`, `android-frame-stream`, `android-stream`, `ui-store`, `GlobalSettingsForm`, `SessionInspector`) all pass.
- Manually exercised end-to-end on Windows: settings toggle → SDK install → device boot → live interactive Pixel home screen → pop-out → tap/swipe/type.

## Testing this PR (Windows / Linux)

1. Check out this branch, `npm install` in `frontend/`.
2. Run the desktop app in dev mode.
3. Settings → toggle on the Android Emulator.
4. Open a session → new "Emulator" tab → Install Android SDK (~2GB download) → Start.
5. On Linux, hardware acceleration needs KVM (`/dev/kvm` readable by your user) — `ao doctor` reports acceleration status if it's unavailable.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change (Android emulator only — no unrelated files)
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass (go build/vet/test, frontend typecheck/test)

title: feat(workspaces): remote workspaces — run agents on a VM over SSH
body:
Closes #3853.

## Problem

If your laptop is a thin client and your VM holds the code, compute and
credentials, AO can't help you: the desktop app spawns a daemon on the machine
it runs on, and every session runs there. Discussion #2855 asks for exactly
this; issue #13 listed it before being closed as rewrite cleanup.

## What this does

A **workspace** is a machine that runs its own AO daemon. `local` is unchanged.
A remote workspace is an SSH target the supervisor reaches through a loopback
port-forward:

```
ssh -N -L <freePort>:127.0.0.1:<remoteDaemonPort> <target>
```

The renderer already addresses the daemon through one mutable base URL handed
to it on `daemon:status`, and the mux WebSocket and SSE derive from that base.
So publishing the forward's local end as the daemon port makes **the entire
renderer work against a remote daemon unmodified**. Pick the machine in
Settings → Workspace; aliases come from your `~/.ssh/config`.

## Why this shape

The alternative — one laptop daemon that *places individual sessions* on a VM —
was designed in full first, and the design argued against it. Routing must be a
pure function of `RuntimeHandle.ID`, which forces the host into the handle id,
and that id space is mintable from project names, so a folder can forge a remote
handle and get a healthy session reaped. Plus `gitworktree` bypasses its own
command runner in ten places, `binaryutil.LookPath` puts *laptop* paths in the
remote pane's `argv[0]`, hooks and the system-prompt file are written locally at
the remote path, and `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` would be exported to a third
machine. All solvable; all existing only because one daemon is acting on a
filesystem that isn't its own. It remains the better answer to "run this one
task on the big machine" and can layer on later — see the ADR.

## Security posture

- **No bind change, no new listener.** Both daemons stay `127.0.0.1`-only, so
  unlike ADR-0001 this needs **no exception** to the loopback-only hard rule.
- **Auth is SSH's.** AO shells out to your `ssh`, holds no key material, writes
  no `known_hosts`. `~/.ssh/config` governs.
- `BatchMode=yes` is load-bearing — the supervisor has no tty and can answer
  neither a passphrase prompt nor an unknown-host-key prompt.
- **`StrictHostKeyChecking` is never set.** An unknown key is surfaced to you
  with the instruction to connect once and see the fingerprint; a *changed* key
  is reported as the security event it is.
- **AO never installs anything remotely.** A host without `ao` is reported with
  the command to run.

## Verification

Verified end to end against a real VM, not just unit tests: the app attaches to
the remote daemon (or starts one), serves the whole UI from it, and upgrades the
terminal-mux WebSocket through the tunnel (HTTP 101).

Real-host testing found **four bugs that unit tests structurally could not**,
each now with a regression test:

| Bug | Why tests missed it |
|---|---|
| `ssh` rejoins argv and the remote shell re-splits it, so `command -v ao` ran the no-op `command` builtin — **preflight passed on a host with no `ao`** | tests asserted the *local* argv, which was correct |
| `ControlMaster`+`ControlPersist` makes `ssh -N` **fork and exit 0**; supervisor read that as "tunnel died" and leaked the forward | a fake child process doesn't fork |
| **Remote port was guessed**; 3001 was taken on the VM so the daemon bound elsewhere and the tunnel hit an unrelated service | no fake reproduces a busy port |
| Concurrent connects each spawned a tunnel | the local path's de-dup guard runs after the remote branch |

1578 tests pass. The 5 failing `landing/generate-markdown-twins` tests fail
identically on a clean `main` and are unrelated.

## Deliberately out of scope

Moving a session between workspaces; a cross-workspace board; `ao` CLI parity
(still local-daemon only); Windows as the client (the failure path is graceful —
a missing `ssh` is reported as such — but it is untested).

## Review order

The commits are meant to be read in order, ADR first.

title: bug(chat): restart recovery deletes image attachments from conversation history
body: ## Bug Chat image attachments are stored only inside the session's disposable Git worktree. When daemon startup recovery recreates a Chat session worktree, `.ao/attachments` is omitted from preservation and deleted. The durable conversation still contains the old workspace-relative paths, so inline previews eventually become broken images and the agent can no longer read those historical attachments. **Source:** Live AO Chat report and two observed restart cycles on 2026-08-11/12 **Reported by:** @illegalcall **Affected build:** `v0.12.1-nightly.202608101434` (nightly commit `2da84a242`) **Analyzed against:** `21fd51acd` (`origin/main` on 2026-08-12; mechanism remains present) **Environment:** macOS 26.5.1, Darwin 25.5.0, arm64, zsh, Go 1.26.5; verified Go daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001` **Priority:** P1 — AO permanently loses attachment content from durable Chat history; no safe in-product recovery exists after the bytes are removed. **Confidence:** High — reproduced across two restart/recovery cycles, traced through the exact storage/lifecycle/preview code path, and verified with filesystem checks plus deterministic cache-busted HTTP requests. ## Reproduction 1. Create or open a non-scratch Chat-mode session. 2. Paste/drop/select an image and send it. 3. Confirm the image renders inline and the daemon preview URL returns `200 image/png`. 4. Restart AO Desktop such that its daemon restarts and startup recovery runs. 5. Reopen the conversation. 6. If the image remains temporarily visible, wait for Chromium to revalidate it or request the preview URL with a unique query parameter. Example request: ```bash curl --path-as-is -i \ 'http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions//preview/files/.ao/attachments/.png?cache_bust=' ``` ### Actual ```http HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 {"error":"not_found","code":"PREVIEW_FILE_NOT_FOUND","message":"Preview file not found",...} ``` The message and attachment path remain in SQLite, but the referenced file no longer exists in the recreated worktree. The inline image is broken, and the agent cannot reopen it. ### Expected Attachments referenced by durable Chat history must survive daemon/app restarts and worktree recreation. The same preview URL should continue returning the original bytes, and the same `.ao/attachments/...` path should remain readable by the resumed agent. ## Observed evidence This was observed twice in the same session, plus once in an older session: | Cycle | Evidence | |---|---| | First restart | Worktree recreated at **2026-08-11 17:12:02 IST**; daemon started at **17:12:05 IST**. Attachments created before recovery were absent and returned `404`. An attachment uploaded at **17:12:53 IST**, after recovery, returned `200`. | | Second restart | Newer images were attached after the first restart. Worktree was recreated again at **2026-08-11 20:07:40 IST**; daemon started at **20:07:43 IST**. Every one of five historical attachment paths was absent on disk and returned `404`; the same cache-busted request returned `404` in three consecutive runs. | | Separate older session | Its durable message predated the next worktree recreation; both referenced attachments were absent afterward and returned `404 PREVIEW_FILE_NOT_FOUND`. | Git reflog for each recreated worktree recorded a reset at the same second as recreation. The installed nightly did not change between the observations. ### Why disappearance can be delayed Chromium may continue painting its cached image after the backing file has already been deleted. In the first observation, an old image remained visible immediately after restart and disappeared later without another restart. Cache-busted requests already returned `404` during that interval. Therefore browser cache timing can mask the loss, but does not cause it. A renderer-only reload or Electron relaunch that leaves the daemon/worktree intact is not sufficient. The destructive trigger is daemon recovery recreating the Chat session worktree. ## Root cause The durable and ephemeral lifetimes are mismatched: 1. [`StageAttachments`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_attachments.go#L50-L76) writes the only copy under `/.ao/attachments` and adds that directory to Git's local exclude list. 2. Conversation persistence retains the generated `.ao/attachments/` reference in message text, but does not retain the attachment bytes or durable attachment metadata. 3. On daemon startup, [`reconcileLive`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1911-L1942) treats every Chat controller as unable to survive the daemon and sends the session through `saveAndTeardownOne`. 4. [`StashUncommitted`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go#L344-L420) intentionally preserves tracked and non-ignored changes only. An attachment-only worktree appears clean, and ignored `.ao/attachments` content is skipped. 5. [`saveAndTeardownOne`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1837-L1885) records the restore marker, then force-removes the worktree. Restore recreates Git-visible state but has no source for the ignored attachment bytes. 6. The preview route [`previewFile`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go#L416-L427) serves only from the current workspace, so historical attachment URLs resolve to `PREVIEW_FILE_NOT_FOUND` after recreation. 7. The renderer added by [PR #3724](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3724) correctly recognizes the durable path and creates an `` URL; it cannot recover bytes the backend deleted. The behavior is cross-platform in principle because it follows shared session-manager and Git-worktree logic, although this reproduction was on macOS. ## Fix direction Introduce a daemon-owned attachment-storage module whose canonical bytes live under AO's durable data directory, for example: ```text $AO_DATA_DIR/attachments// ``` Keep `.ao/attachments/...` as the agent-facing projection so existing prompts and conversations remain compatible. Required behavior: 1. **Stage atomically:** validate the input, atomically write the canonical `0600` copy under `$AO_DATA_DIR`, then materialize it into the session worktree. Return the existing worktree-relative path. 2. **Serve durably:** for strictly validated AO-generated attachment paths, serve the canonical copy rather than relying solely on the disposable worktree. Keep ordinary preview files confined to the worktree as today. 3. **Restore projection:** after recreating a worktree and before relaunching its controller, rematerialize that session's durable attachments into `.ao/attachments` and restore the local exclude entry. 4. **Upgrade safely:** before the first destructive recovery under the fixed build, import legacy worktree-only `.ao/attachments` into durable storage. Otherwise updating to the fix can itself delete attachments created by the affected build. 5. **Tie cleanup to durable ownership:** remove canonical attachments only when the owning session/conversation is permanently deleted—not when its runtime is stopped or its worktree is recycled. 6. **Preserve security properties:** validate generated names, reject traversal and symlink escapes, retain attachment size/type limits, and never expose one session's files through another session ID. Optional SQLite metadata can record attachment identity, MIME type, size, and message/turn ownership, but large binary blobs do not need to live in SQLite. ### Do not fix by - removing `.ao/attachments` from Git exclusion, which would dirty user worktrees; - forcing ignored binary files into Git preserve commits, which would pollute the project object database and blur AO-owned/user-owned state; - changing cache headers or retrying in the renderer, which can only hide a missing-file response; - storing only another ephemeral path without a durable byte owner. ## Regression coverage Add a lifecycle-level test that exercises the real failure seam: ```text start daemon with data dir A → create Chat session → attach an image → assert preview returns 200 and exact bytes → stop/restart daemon using data dir A → allow startup recovery to recreate/restore the session → assert the same preview URL returns 200 and exact bytes → assert the resumed agent can read the same .ao/attachments/... path ``` Also cover: - legacy worktree-only attachment import before teardown; - multiple attachments and collision-free stable names; - image and non-image attachment persistence; - traversal, malformed name, symlink escape, and cross-session access rejection; - permanent session/conversation cleanup; - direct HTTP success after restart without relying on Chromium cache. The existing [`TestChatAttachmentIsStagedIntoTheWorktreeAndReadableByTheAgent`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/e2e/chat_composer_test.go#L87-L152) verifies only immediate readability and clean Git status; it does not cross a daemon restart/recovery boundary. ## Impact - AO loses attachment bytes while retaining apparently valid history references. - Historical screenshots cannot be reviewed by the user or agent after recovery. - Image-only prompts can lose essential context. - Browser caching makes the bug appear intermittent and delays visible failure. - Reattaching is possible only if the user still has the original external file; AO itself cannot recover already-deleted attachments. - The problem affects every attachment type staged under `.ao/attachments`, although images expose it most visibly. ## Related - [Issue #3722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3722) — fixed rendering attachment paths as inline previews; adjacent but not a duplicate. - [PR #3724](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3724) — introduced the renderer path that exposes this underlying lifetime mismatch. - [Issue #2722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2722) — original task-composer attachment capability. - [PR #3691](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3691) — stages delegated-task attachments in worker worktrees. - [Issue #3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) / [PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) — Chat controller persistence and restart architecture.

title: fix(chat): keep nested Codex turns from draining queued work
body:
## Summary

- preserve Codex's provider thread identity on normalized turn lifecycle events
- let only lifecycle events from the AO-owned root thread claim or release the controller's primary turn
- keep nested child turns durable for transcript correlation without reporting the session idle or draining queued work
- apply volatile turn ownership only after the SQLite projection commits
- serialize lifecycle projection, queue dispatch, and handoff quiescence checks at one dispatch boundary
- prevent nested child notifications from replacing the Codex adapter's fallback Stop target

## Root cause

Codex app-server multiplexes child-agent thread lifecycle notifications over the root conversation connection. AO discarded the notification's `threadId`, stored only one mutable active turn, and treated every `turn/completed` as conversation quiescence.

A child completion could therefore release queued automation while the root was still running. Codex accepted the message into that root, while AO had already minted and bound a different durable turn. Because that assigned provider turn never started, the row stayed `running` and a Chat → TUI drain waited indefinitely.

The CI race run also exposed the adjacent quiescence gap: dispatch marks a queued row running in SQLite just before installing its in-memory active-turn ID. A handoff checking those facts without the dispatch lock could briefly see neither queued nor active work and finish early. The handoff now evaluates both facts under the same lock as dispatch.

The added handoff regression covers the complete user-visible sequence: child completion cannot finish the handoff or release its accepted queue; root completion releases that queue; the handoff finishes only after the queue settles.

## Verification

- controller regression passed 50 consecutive times with the race detector
- focused controller/normalizer/adapter regressions passed 20×
- `go test -p 4 ./...`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/service/chat ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver`
- golangci-lint v2.12.2 with fresh Go/lint caches: 0 issues

Related follow-up: #3950 / #3951 durably acknowledge the recovered transition notice so the same historical recovery does not resurface after remounts or restarts.

Fixes #3878

title: fix(chat): persist attachments across restart
body:
## Summary

- store every new chat and spawn attachment canonically under the AO data directory while retaining the worktree-relative path agents read
- import legacy worktree-only attachments before kill, cleanup, replacement, and restart teardown; rematerialize image and non-image files before restored controllers relaunch
- serve strictly validated AO attachment preview URLs from canonical storage so history does not depend on a live worktree or Chromium cache
- remove canonical bytes only with permanent session ownership cleanup, never on runtime stop or worktree recycling

## Review repairs

- anchor canonical and worktree operations with `os.Root`; reject traversal, unsafe generated names, symlink parent escapes, cross-session aliases, empty roots, non-regular files, SVG, and over-limit content
- make canonical creation atomic and no-overwrite, retry randomized chat-name collisions, and preserve historical bytes
- pass `context.Context` through every public attachment-store I/O operation
- restore the Git exclude only when canonical files were materialized, and stop destructive teardown when a present legacy source cannot be imported safely
- add the required real daemon restart/recovery test, including exact cache-busted HTTP bytes and a resumed agent reading the same path

## Root cause

Conversation history persisted only the `.ao/attachments` path. The bytes existed only in an ignored worktree directory, so `StashUncommitted` omitted them and restart reconciliation force-removed the only copy. Chromium cache temporarily made some images appear to survive.

## Verification

- `GOFLAGS=-p=4 npm run lint`
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go vet ./...`
- `cd backend && go test -p=4 ./... -count=1`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/attachmentstore ./internal/session_manager ./internal/httpd/controllers -count=1`
- Windows amd64 cross-compile of `internal/attachmentstore` tests
- `AO_CHAT_E2E=1 go test ./e2e -run ^TestChatAttachmentSurvivesDaemonRestartRecovery$ -v -count=1 -timeout=10m`

## Known limitation

An older build may already have deleted an attachments only copy. This change migrates legacy files that still exist in a live or retained worktree, but cannot reconstruct bytes deleted before upgrade.

Closes #3884

title: fix(desktop): persist daemon output on the piped launch path
body:
## Problem

A desktop-launched daemon writes nothing to disk. The supervisor consumes the child's stdout/stderr pipes and forwards them to the Electron console, so once the app exits there is no record left — a panic stack disappears with it, and the request ID the API returns for log correlation has nothing to correlate against.

Only `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` produced a durable log, because that path redirects stdio to a file at spawn time. The normal packaged launch (`stdio: "pipe"`) has never written one.

Fixes #2689.

## Why not just redirect stdio

The piped path cannot simply point stdio at a file: the supervisor scans both streams for the bound port (`createListenPortScanner`), and port discovery would break. The log therefore has to be a tee — mirror each chunk to disk while leaving the scanners and the Electron console untouched.

## Change

All of it is confined to the `if (!keep)` branch in `frontend/src/main.ts`:

- Mirror stdout/stderr chunks to `~/.ao/daemon.log` (`~/.ao/<dev>/daemon.log` in dev) alongside the existing scanner and console handling.
- Rotate one generation at 8 MiB (`daemon.log` → `daemon.log.1`), checked on open and tracked while writing, so a long-lived install cannot grow it without bound.
- Stamp the exit reason before closing the stream. A bare stack with no terminator is indistinguishable from a truncated log; `[ao] daemon exited with SIGSEGV at <ISO>` names the failure outright.
- Every failure path is best-effort: a stream error clears the writer, an unopenable log warns once, and neither can take the app down. A missing log must never be worse than the current behavior.

Keep-daemon mode is untouched — it already redirects stdio to the same file at spawn time.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npx vitest run src/main/` — 312 passed, 1 skipped (24 files).
- Verified on a packaged build: rebuilt, installed to `/Applications`, and confirmed `~/.ao/daemon.log` receives fresh structured entries within seconds of launch, with the daemon running **without** `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` — the exact path this issue is about. Before the change the file's last write predated the run by three weeks.

title: feat(i18n): add Russian (ru) UI locale
body:
## Summary

The desktop app ships eight UI locales — `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja`, `ko`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, `pt-BR` — but no Russian. Russian-speaking users get English regardless of their system language.

Nothing about the existing implementation excludes it: the localization foundation from #2106 is locale-agnostic, and `ru` is simply one that nobody has contributed yet.

## Current state

`frontend/src/shared/ui-locale.ts`:

```ts
export const APP_LOCALES = ["en", "zh-CN", "ja", "ko", "es", "fr", "de", "pt-BR"] as const;
```

The English catalog (`frontend/src/renderer/i18n/en.json`) currently holds 1071 keys, and each shipped locale carries a full parallel catalog.

## Proposal

Add `ru` as a community locale, following exactly the pattern the seven non-English locales already use:

1. `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/ru.json` — full catalog translated from `en.json`.
2. Register it in `APP_LOCALES` (`frontend/src/shared/ui-locale.ts`), which also widens the `AppLocale` union used across the Electron main/preload/renderer boundaries.
3. Export the catalog from `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/messages.ts` and add it to `appCatalogs` in `instance.ts`.
4. Extend the locale coverage assertions in `instance.test.ts`.

`coerceLocale` and `documentLang` need no change — they derive from `APP_LOCALES`.

## Notes on scope

Following the boundaries #2106 established, this covers display text only. Config keys, schema identifiers, plugin/agent/session ids, branch and status enum values, and agent-facing prompts stay untouched.

Two Russian-specific translation points worth deciding once rather than per-string:

- **Plural forms.** Russian has three (one / few / many), unlike the two-form languages already shipped. Any key whose English form pluralizes with a bare `s` needs i18next plural suffixes rather than a single string.
- **Established technical vocabulary.** Terms like *worker*, *orchestrator*, *session*, and *worktree* are usually left untranslated in Russian developer tooling; translating them tends to make the UI harder to follow, not easier. A short glossary decided up front keeps the catalog internally consistent.

Filing this so the gap is tracked and a contributor picking it up has the integration points and the two decisions above already mapped out.

title: fix(conpty): scope pty-host registry to the daemon instance
body:
## Summary

- The Windows ConPTY runtime's pty-host registry (`~/.ao/windows-pty-hosts.json`) was hardcoded to the default AO home directory via `os.UserHomeDir()`, ignoring the `AO_RUN_FILE`/`AO_DATA_DIR` overrides every other piece of daemon state (`ao.db`, `running.json`) already respects.
- Two AO daemon instances on one machine (e.g. a headless dev daemon at `~/.ao/dev` and the desktop app at `~/.ao`) therefore shared one registry file even though they're otherwise fully isolated.
- Session ids are numbered per-project within each instance's own local DB (`NextSessionNum`), so two instances with the same project can independently mint identical session ids (e.g. `demo-website-2`). The second instance's registration would then silently overwrite the first's pty-host address in the shared registry — attaching that session's terminal to the *wrong* process.
- `ptyregistry.SetRunFilePath` now scopes the registry to the directory containing the calling instance's own `running.json`, wired through `conpty.Options.RunFilePath` and a new `runFilePath` parameter on `runtimeselect.New`, sourced from the daemon's already-resolved `cfg.RunFilePath`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `go test ./...` — new/changed packages pass cleanly; pre-existing failures on this Windows dev environment (`TestStabilizeWorkingDirectoryChdirsToDataDir`, tmux `/tmp`-path tests, `TestWriteAgentHandoffFileIsPrivateAtomicAndImmutable`, `TestSpawn_*` branch-namespace tests, `workspacewatch` watcher timing) reproduce identically on the unmodified base branch and are unrelated (none of those packages import `conpty`/`ptyregistry`/`runtimeselect`)
- [x] New regression test (`TestTwoInstancesWithDifferentRunFilePathsDoNotShareRegistry`) reproduces the exact cross-instance collision and verifies it no longer occurs

title: fix(desktop): preserve Intel Node JIT entitlement
body:
Refs #3879.

## What changed

- Applies a per-file entitlement override only to the bundled ACP Node at `Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node`, and selects it **from the binary content**: the override applies iff the Mach-O header of the file being signed contains an x86_64 slice (a thin x64 binary, or a universal carrying x64). arm64-only binaries keep the default `allow-jit`.
- **The signing host's architecture is never consulted.** `@electron/osx-sign` passes `optionsForFile` only `(filePath)`, and the canonical downstream signer processes both arm64 and x64 artifacts from one host, so `process.arch` was the wrong selector (review follow-up). The new `frontend/makers/macho-archs.ts` parses the Mach-O header (thin `MH_MAGIC_64`, fat `FAT_MAGIC`/`FAT_MAGIC_64`; endianness derived from the magic, cputype-only classification) and `macSignOptionsForFile` keys off it. Tests stub `process.arch` to `x64`, `arm64`, and a nonsense value and pin identical results.
- **Fails closed**: an unreadable or unparseable file at the nested-Node path throws out of `optionsForFile` and aborts the signing pass — no silent fallback to defaults, which is exactly the #3879 crash.
- Preserves `allow-jit` and adds `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`, which x64 V8 needs when Hardened Runtime blocks executable-memory permission changes.
- Leaves every other bundle file on `@electron/osx-sign` defaults.
- Wires the override through both supported Forge signing inputs: `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` and `CSC_LINK`; unsigned local packages remain unsigned.
- Documents the canonical signing contract in `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md` ("macOS signing contract for the bundled ACP runtime"), including pre-publication duties: inspect the nested Node's entitlements in the final artifact and execute the final x64 zip's Node on a native Intel runner, keeping the arm64 verification.
- Extends `frontend/scripts/verify-mac-artifact.sh` to inspect the final nested Node entitlements and execute it only after codesign, Gatekeeper, and stapler all pass. The script is the local diagnostic and the public mac-update-e2e baseline check; the pre-publication gate remains the release conductor's verifier, which now has a documented contract to mirror.

Scope note: the public CI build in `build-artifacts.yml` stays intentionally unsigned, so `osxSign`/`optionsForFile` do not run there — the entitlement decision is enforced wherever signing actually happens (locally signed builds today; the canonical signer once it mirrors the documented contract).

The branch is rebased on current `main`.

## Review follow-up addressed

- Arch selection is keyed off the artifact being signed, not the host (`arch` parameter removed).
- The public verifier is documented as the local diagnostic counterpart, not the publication gate.
- Removed the unrelated `AgentModelCombobox` locale-formatting commit and the net-zero screenshot add/remove pair (tree verified byte-identical apart from the locale file).
- `Closes` demoted to `Refs` until the paired conductor-side change lands (contract in `desktop-release.md`).

## Tests

- Focused suites: 69 passed — new Mach-O parser tests, forge.config signing/postMake, maker-dmg, verify-mac-artifact smoke.
- Mach-O parser coverage: synthetic thin/fat fixtures (incl. `FAT_MAGIC_64`, byte-swapped thin, arm64e cputype-only classification, i386 not masked into x86_64), truncated/garbage/non-Mach-O headers throw, host-arch independence, macOS sanity check against a real Mach-O.
- Frontend typecheck and e2e typecheck: passed. Full frontend suite: 267 files; 3,594 passed, 7 skipped, and 12 failed — all 12 in `browser-profile-import.test.ts`, from a local `better-sqlite3` build carrying the Electron ABI after a local packaged build (environment artifact; neither the module nor that file is touched by this branch).
- Shell syntax and shellcheck: passed.
- Trust-order regression: a mocked untrusted app fails `spctl` and the nested Node sentinel is never executed.
- Real signer A/B (original round): official Node v22.23.2 x64, `@electron/osx-sign` 1.3.3, Hardened Runtime — the entitlement list is unchanged; only the selection mechanism moved from host arch to file content.

## A/B evidence

The screenshots are attached as review evidence and are not part of the PR code diff.

### A — current Forge defaults produce a valid seal but Node crashes

![Before: x64 V8 crashes with exit 133](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-3896/.issue-assets/pr-3896/a-before-intel-node-crash.png)

The final x64 Node has `allow-jit` but not `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. The outer app seal is valid, yet JavaScript hits the reported V8 `SetPermissions` assertion and exits 133.

### B — the selector signs the same Node with the required x64 entitlement

![After: x64 Node executes JavaScript](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-3896/.issue-assets/pr-3896/b-after-intel-node-runs.png)

The same signed Node and command exit 0. This exercises the exact Packager → osx-sign → nested Node/V8 boundary changed by the PR.

## Remaining for #3879

The change that reaches users is the canonical signer's entitlement step in the private release repository. This PR ships the public contract (`desktop-release.md`), the content-based reference implementation (`machoHasX86_64Slice`), and the local diagnostic; `Closes` returns once the conductor side lands:

1. its signing step applies the entitlements per the documented contract (x64-slice predicate, fail-closed);
2. its final-artifact verifier inspects the nested Node and executes the final x64 zip on a native Intel runner.
