body:
## Summary

Clicking a link in a chat message always opened it in the in-app AO Browser panel, and right-click offered nothing — there was no way to get a chat link into the system browser. This adds the standard escape hatches to `MarkdownLink` in `ChatMarkdown.tsx` (the single link surface for all chat prose, including PR/issue URLs agents write in messages):

1. **Plain left-click** — unchanged: opens in the in-app Browser panel via the session link handler.
2. **Right-click** — a context menu (built on the shared shadcn `ContextMenu` primitive already used by the sidebar) with **Open in system browser** and **Copy link address**. Open goes through the existing `app:openExternal` IPC path (main-process `shell.openExternal` behind the URL allowlist); copy uses the native clipboard bridge so it works without document focus.
3. **Cmd+click (macOS) / Ctrl+click (Win/Linux)** — opens directly in the system browser, matching the VS Code/Slack convention. The existing Option/Alt-click path is retained.

Security: the context menu's system-browser item is rendered for http(s) links only (`isWebLink`); non-web schemes (e.g. `mailto:`) get only *Copy link address*. Every open still passes through the main process allowlist in `external-open.ts` — `window.open` is never used.

Out of scope by design: structured PR/issue chips (`ProductExternalLink`) already open in the system browser and are untouched, as are links elsewhere in the app.

## Tests

- 5 new component tests in `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx`: Cmd-click and Ctrl-click route to `openExternal`, right-click menu offers and executes both items, and the mailto menu omits the system-browser item.
- Full frontend suite: 191 files, 2521 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Verified live in the dev Electron app (isolated data mode) on a real chat message: plain click navigated the in-app Browser panel to the URL (confirmed via the native WebContentsView target), Cmd+click and the context-menu item opened the system browser through `shell.openExternal`, and *Copy link address* landed the exact URL on the native clipboard.

## Risks

- Each markdown link now mounts a Radix `ContextMenu` root (same per-item pattern the sidebar uses); no measurable rendering impact observed.
- Chat surface is on the deferred-localization list, so the two menu labels are intentionally hardcoded English like the rest of `ChatMarkdown`.

title: bug(chat): TUI→Chat switch permanently fails with 'settled native conversation history … context deadline exceeded' after a failed chat turn
body:
## Bug

Switching a terminal (TUI) session to the Chat UI fails after ~45s with:

> Interface switch failed — switch interface <session>: resume chat: wait for settled native conversation history: chat conversation history is not settled: context deadline exceeded

Once this state is entered, **every** subsequent switch attempt fails the same way — the session is permanently unable to enter Chat mode.

**Source:** live triage of orchestrator session `agent-orchestrator-88` (project agent-orchestrator), reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-08-19 03:15Z | **Analyzed against:** `4a23d98ca`
**Confidence:** High (root cause reproduced empirically against the live transcript and the real `claude-agent-acp` adapter; regression test reproduces the exact error string and 45s timeout on unfixed code)

## Reproduction (mechanism)

1. Session is in Chat mode; a chat turn **fails** (in the observed incident: `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`, recorded as a terminal `failed` turn with the synthetic assistant error message as its last item).
2. User switches Chat → TUI (succeeds), fixes the problem (e.g. `/login`), and continues working in the terminal. Claude Code forks the next prompt from the **pre-failure** transcript entry, so the failed turn's entries (user prompt + synthetic auth-error assistant message) land on a **dead branch** of the transcript's `parentUuid` tree.
3. User switches TUI → Chat. The resume runs `session/load`; `claude-agent-acp`'s replay walks the parent chain from the last entry — the dead branch is **never replayed** (verified: replay of the live 992-entry transcript contained 183-entry active chain only; the auth-error turn was absent).
4. `captureAOHighWater` (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go`) anchors the settle checkpoint on the **latest terminal turn — including `failed` ones**. The anchor item can never appear in the replay, so `nativeHistoryCheckpoint.reached()` returns false forever; the controller polls the (immutable, cached) ACP replay every 100ms until the 45s `nativeHistorySettleLimit` expires → `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`, rollback to TUI.
5. Terminal-mode turns never write `conversation_turns` rows, so the failed chat turn **remains the latest terminal turn indefinitely** — the switch can never succeed again for that session.

## Root Cause

`captureAOHighWater` filters on `turn.State.Terminal()` (completed | interrupted | failed). A provider only promises to reproduce **completed** work during native history load; failed/interrupted turns commonly end up on abandoned transcript branches (Claude forks from the pre-failure parent), and their synthetic error messages may also be deliberately suppressed on replay (`claude-agent-acp` issue #863 handling). Anchoring the checkpoint on such a turn makes the settle wait unsatisfiable.

## Fix

Anchor the high-water mark only on `TurnStateCompleted` turns. The hook-derived `latestUserPrompt` / `latestAssistantUpdate` checkpoint fields still guard freshness of the newest terminal-side facts. The failed turn's rows stay durable in AO's projection (reconciliation never deletes them) — no history is lost.

## Impact

- Any session whose most recent chat turn failed (auth expiry, API error, interrupt-at-switch) becomes permanently unswitchable to Chat.
- Each attempt also stops the TUI, burns 45s, and rolls back — and the rollback relaunch leaves the switch button disabled with "native conversation id is not confirmed for the current terminal launch" until the next hook fires (separate issue, filed independently).

## Workaround (until fixed)

Complete one more **successful Chat turn** is impossible (chat can't start) — instead, the state self-heals only if AO's chat projection gains a newer completed turn. Practically: none from the UI; the underlying session and terminal keep working normally, and the switch button re-enables for retry after the next prompt/stop hook — but every retry hits the same 45s failure.

title: fix(chat): do not anchor native-history checkpoint on failed turns
body:
Fixes #4120

## Summary

The TUI→Chat interface-switch settle checkpoint (`captureAOHighWater`) anchored on the latest **terminal** turn, including `failed`/`interrupted` ones. A failed turn's items carry no replay guarantee: Claude forks the next prompt from the pre-failure transcript entry, leaving the failed turn (e.g. a synthetic `Failed to authenticate…` assistant message) on a dead `parentUuid` branch that `session/load` never replays. Because terminal-mode turns never update AO's chat projection, the failed turn stayed the anchor forever and **every** switch attempt timed out after 45s with `chat conversation history is not settled: context deadline exceeded`, then rolled back.

This is the root cause of the live incident on orchestrator session `agent-orchestrator-88` (2026-08-19 03:15Z); the mechanism was verified by replaying the live transcript through the real `claude-agent-acp` adapter — the failed turn's items were absent from the replay (dead branch), exactly as the checkpoint required them.

The fix anchors the high-water mark only on `TurnStateCompleted` turns. The hook-derived `latestUserPrompt` / `latestAssistantUpdate` checkpoint fields still guard freshness of the newest terminal-side facts, and the failed turn's rows remain durable in AO's projection (asserted in the test).

## Tests

- New `TestInterfaceHandoffDoesNotAnchorReplayCheckpointOnFailedTurn` models the incident (completed turn + newer failed auth-error turn whose items never replay). On unfixed code it fails with the exact production error after 45.1s; with the fix it passes in 0.13s.
- `go test ./internal/service/chat/ ./internal/session_manager/` — all pass.

## Known risks / follow-ups

- After a failed turn, a stale replay missing that turn's items is now accepted; `latestUserPrompt`/`latestAssistantUpdate` still gate on the newest hook facts, and reconciliation preserves the failed turn's durable rows, so no history is lost.
- Two adjacent defects observed in the same incident are filed separately: the post-rollback "native conversation id is not confirmed" window (SessionStart hook only matches `startup`, not `resume`), and the 45s blind poll over an immutable cached ACP replay.
- `AO_CHAT_E2E=1` real-daemon suite not run (real model calls); covered by the focused unit regression instead.

title: bug(session): switch-to-chat disabled with 'native conversation id is not confirmed' after a relaunch via --resume — SessionStart hook only matches 'startup'
body:
## Bug

After the daemon relaunches a Claude Code TUI with `--resume` (e.g. the rollback of a failed interface switch, or a restore), the switch-to-chat button is disabled with tooltip:

> session: native conversation id is not confirmed for the current terminal launch for claude-code

and stays disabled until the user interacts with the terminal (next `UserPromptSubmit`/`Stop`/tool hook).

**Source:** live triage of `agent-orchestrator-88`, 2026-08-19 03:16–03:18Z (reported by the maintainer) | **Analyzed against:** `4a23d98ca`
**Confidence:** High

## Root cause

`nativeConversationID` (`backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go:520-529`) requires `Metadata.AgentSessionIDLaunchID == Metadata.RuntimeLaunchID` — proof that a hook confirmed the native session id under the **current** terminal launch generation. `CommitControllerEpoch` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:1049`) clears `AgentSessionIDLaunchID` on every mode flip, and a relaunch rotates `RuntimeLaunchID`.

The only hook that fires at TUI startup is `SessionStart`, but AO registers it **exclusively under the `"startup"` matcher** (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/hooks.go:38`). A relaunch via `claude --resume` fires `SessionStart` with source `"resume"` — which the matcher does not cover — so no signal carries the session id + launch id until the user next types. During that window the switch is blocked with the misleading "not confirmed" reason.

Observed live: the interface-switch rollback at 03:16:45Z relaunched the TUI; `agent_session_id_launch_id` stayed empty until the user's next prompt at 03:18:33Z re-confirmed it (verified in the sessions table — the values match again now).

## Fix

Register `SessionStart` under the `"resume"` matcher too (and consider `"compact"`/`"clear"`). A `SessionStart(source=resume)` hook firing from the relaunched process under the new `AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID` is exactly the proof the gate wants; confirming from it closes the window entirely.

## Impact

- P2: self-heals on the next user interaction, but the disabled button + cryptic tooltip right after a failed switch (see #4120) makes the failure look permanent.

## Related
- [#4120](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4120) — the failed-switch rollback that exposes this window

title: chat: settle wait polls an immutable cached ACP replay for the full 45s before failing the interface switch
body:
## Problem

`Controller.importNativeHistory` (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go`) polls `ReadHistory` every 100ms for up to 45s (`nativeHistorySettleLimit`) waiting for the replay to settle / reach the checkpoint.

For ACP drivers (claude, and other `chatdriver/acp` bindings), `ReadHistory` returns a **one-shot cache** captured during `session/load` at Resume time (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/history.go` — `historyLoaded`/`historyEvents`/`historyErr` are set once and never refreshed). If the first read is unsettled or the checkpoint is unreachable, no amount of polling can change the answer — the user just waits 45 seconds for a guaranteed failure, during which the source TUI is already stopped and must be rolled back.

(The Codex app-server driver re-reads live state, so polling is meaningful there — this is ACP-specific.)

**Source:** observed during triage of [#4120](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4120) | **Analyzed against:** `4a23d98ca`
**Confidence:** High (code-traced)

## Suggested fix

Either:
- have the ACP `ReadHistory` (or a capability flag on `ports.ChatHistoryReader`) declare its result immutable so the controller fails fast instead of polling, or
- make the poll re-trigger `session/load` so genuinely-converging histories (transcript flush lag) can actually settle for ACP too.

## Impact

- P2 once #4120 lands: only genuinely unsettled/mismatched replays hit this, but they cost 45s + a TUI stop/rollback cycle instead of an immediate, actionable error.

title: fix: recover supervised sessions after Ctrl+C kills the agent in its pane
body:
## Problem

Ctrl+C in a supervised agent terminal (worker **or** orchestrator) permanently bricked the session with no recovery path:

1. Since #3548, supervised launches park the pane on \`exec cat >/dev/null\` after the agent exits. Ctrl+C kills the agent TUI → the pane silently swallows every keystroke with no banner; it looks hung.
2. Because \`cat\` holds the tmux pane open, \`tmux has-session\` stays true, so the session never becomes \`terminated\` — the supervisor's exit report (and the reaper's workload probe as fallback) flip **activity** to \`exited\`, but \`isTerminated\` stays false, by design.
3. \`TerminalPane\` gated its Restore button on the session being terminated → the button never appeared. The only affordance for an exited-but-live agent was a "Resume agent" control buried in the session inspector's Summary tab — and **orchestrators have no inspector at all** (\`SessionView.tsx\`: \`hasInspector = session && !isOrchestrator\`), so one Ctrl+C in an orchestrator = dead session, zero recovery affordance.
4. \`RestoreUnavailableDialog\` (create-new-orchestrator fallback) was only reachable via a failed restore attempt → also unreachable.

## Triage findings

The backend lifecycle was already sound: the supervisor posts \`process-exited\`, the reaper's supervised-workload probe covers a lost report, and \`ResumeAgentWithMode\` + \`POST /sessions/{id}/resume-agent\` already implement in-place relaunch (native resume, terminal identity and worktree preserved, role-specific system prompt rebuilt). The bricking was a pane-UX + affordance gap, so no backend lifecycle change was needed.

## Fix

- **tmux** (\`buildLaunchCommand\`): supervised panes now print \`[ao] agent exited - restore this session from the app to continue\` before \`exec cat >/dev/null\`. The input-swallowing safety property is unchanged — no interactive shell, stdin still drains into \`cat\`.
- **TerminalPane**: the ended strip now also appears when a live session's activity is \`exited\` (and no agent switch is in flight), with the button routed to \`/resume-agent\`; terminated sessions keep the existing \`/restore\` path. \`SESSION_NOT_RESUMABLE\` from either path opens the existing not-resumable dialog, making the create-new-orchestrator fallback reachable.
- New \`useResumeAgentSession\` hook mirroring \`useRestoreSession\` (shared implementation), including the saved-prompt fallback notification.

## Verification (real repro)

Booted an isolated daemon from this branch with a raw-mode stub \`claude\` binary (emulates a TUI: Ctrl+C arrives as a byte, agent exits cleanly). For **both a worker and an orchestrator**:

- Ctrl+C → pane shows the new banner, \`cat\` holds the pane, session lands in \`status: exited, isTerminated: false\`.
- \`POST /sessions/{id}/resume-agent\` → \`resumeMode: "native"\`, agent relaunched in the same pane with \`--resume <same pinned UUID>\` and the role's rebuilt system prompt; session returns to live status.
- Also confirmed the reaper's workload probe flips the state even when the supervisor's direct exit report fails to land.

## Tests

- \`tmux_test.go\`: new \`TestCreateLaunchCommandSupervisedParksOnBannerAndCat\` (banner precedes the sink; no interactive shell in supervised panes).
- \`TerminalPane.test.tsx\`: live worker/orchestrator with exited activity shows the strip and posts \`/resume-agent\`; no affordance while an agent switch is replacing the agent; existing terminated-session restore tests unchanged.
- \`go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/\`, frontend typecheck, and the full renderer vitest suite pass (pre-existing \`src/landing/**\` failures are an unrelated missing-workspace-install issue in this worktree).

## Risks / follow-ups

- The banner string is asserted in the tmux unit test; changing the copy requires updating both.
- Observation from the repro rig: the supervisor's exit report resolves the daemon from default run-file discovery; in multi-daemon dev setups it can post to the wrong daemon (harmless in production single-daemon installs, and the reaper probe covers it). Possible hardening: pin \`AO_RUN_FILE\` into session env.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(lifecycle): nested claude process inheriting AO_SESSION_ID rewrites the parent session's identity and marks it exited; live chat controller cannot clear the sticky 'exited'
body:
## Bug

Two related defects, observed live on a chat-mode worker session (`agent-orchestrator-143`, 2026-08-19 03:31Z) when a diagnostic script spawned a short-lived Claude process from the session's shell:

**1. Hook attribution is env-only, and chat-mode sessions have no launch-id guard.**
`ao hooks` attributes signals purely by the inherited `AO_SESSION_ID` env var. Any nested `claude` process started from a session's shell — a diagnostic script, a user manually running `claude` in the workspace terminal, an SDK-spawned child — inherits that env, and if its cwd has AO hooks in `.claude/settings.local.json`, its `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd` hooks report **its** `session_id`/`transcript_path` into the **parent** session's row: `agent_session_id`, `native_transcript_path`, and `latest_*` get overwritten, and on quit the parent session is marked `exited` while its real agent keeps running.

The lifecycle launch-id gate (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:506`) only drops mismatched signals when the session has a non-empty `runtime_launch_id`. Chat-mode sessions have none, so every foreign signal passes. Observed impact: the session showed `exited` in the UI while actively working, and `agent_session_id` pointed at a *different session's* native conversation — a later TUI restore would have resumed the wrong conversation.

**2. A live chat controller cannot clear a sticky `exited`.**
Once `activity_state=exited`, only a signal with `Event == "user-prompt-submit"` can resurrect the session (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:524-529`). The chat controller's ongoing activity signals do not carry that event, so a chat session that is demonstrably alive and streaming stays rendered `exited` indefinitely. A live controller generation reporting activity should count as resurrection evidence.

**Analyzed against:** `4a23d98ca` | **Confidence:** High (reproduced + state verified in the sessions table; repaired by replaying a correct `user-prompt-submit` hook payload)

## Suggested fixes

- Gate hook-signal identity updates for chat-mode sessions on the controller generation (or drop `agent_session_id` overwrites whose value disagrees with `provider_conversation_id` while mode is chat), and/or scope hook attribution to the workspace the hook fired from.
- Allow chat-controller signals (matching the current `controller_generation`) to clear `exited`.

## Related
- [#4120](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4120) — discovered while triaging this incident
- [#2604](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2604) — adjacent stale-activity rendering after daemon restart

title: Clarify token usage reporting and avoid apparent cache-token double counting
body:
## Bug

AO presents an inclusive `inputTokens` value alongside cache-read and cache-write token counts, then labels `inputTokens + outputTokens` as **Total tokens**. The arithmetic currently represents all tokens processed, but the terminology makes cache tokens appear duplicated and makes AO difficult to compare with agent-native usage reports.

**Source:** User report in an AO session on 2026-08-18  
**Analyzed against:** `78a1366310c071a5edf5d01f420c162e02e40dec`  
**Confidence:** High — the parser, aggregation query, API DTO, and renderer calculation were traced.  
**Priority:** P2 — reporting is available but materially confusing; underlying token categories are already retained.

The screenshots below are from different sessions and should not be numerically reconciled. They illustrate the terminology problem only.

### AO usage inspector

![AO usage inspector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-token-usage-reporting-20260818/.issue-assets/token-usage-reporting/ao-usage.png)

### Claude Code native usage report

![Claude Code usage report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-token-usage-reporting-20260818/.issue-assets/token-usage-reporting/claude-code-usage.png)

## Current behavior

For Claude transcripts, `backend/internal/observe/usage/parser.go` normalizes:

```text
inputTokens = uncached input + cache reads + cache writes
```

Codex reports inclusive input, so AO derives uncached input by subtracting cache reads/writes.

The inspector (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`) and compact-session query (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/usage.sql`) then calculate:

```text
totalTokens = inputTokens + outputTokens
```

This is a valid **tokens processed** measurement, but the UI shows `inputTokens`, cache reads, and cache writes as if they were independent rows. Reasoning tokens are also shown without explaining that they are included in output.

## Desired reporting contract

Use mutually exclusive user-facing categories:

- **Fresh input** — uncached input tokens
- **Cache reads**
- **Cache writes**
- **Output** — includes reasoning tokens
- **Reasoning (included in output)** — informational subset, never added again

Derive and label the aggregate explicitly:

```text
tokensProcessed = freshInput + cacheReads + cacheWrites + output
```

Do not display the inclusive internal `inputTokens` value as ordinary **Input tokens**.

Suggested summary presentation:

```text
Tokens processed                         2.2M
Estimated cost                              —

Fresh input                              86.5K
Output                                      8K
Cache reads                              2.1M
Cache writes                                 0
Reasoning (included in output)            3.1K
Cache hit rate                              96%
```

Collapsed session/agent/model rows could use `2.2M processed · 96% cached`. Once reliable pricing is available, estimated cost should be the primary comparison metric because token classes have substantially different prices.

## Proposed implementation

1. Add an explicitly named `processedTokens` derived field to detailed and compact usage responses.
2. Present `uncachedInputTokens` as **Fresh input**.
3. Stop presenting inclusive `inputTokens` in the visible breakdown.
4. Rename **Total tokens** to **Tokens processed**.
5. Label reasoning as included in output.
6. Add a cache-hit percentage with a documented denominator.
7. Keep existing API fields temporarily for compatibility and deprecate ambiguous naming rather than silently changing its meaning.
8. Ensure all pricing and telemetry formulas price/count each mutually exclusive category exactly once.

No historical data rewrite should be required: AO already persists uncached input, cache read, cache write, output, and reasoning separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visible token categories are mutually exclusive except reasoning, which is explicitly marked as a subset of output.
- [ ] `processedTokens` equals fresh input + cache reads + cache writes + output at model, harness, session, and compact-card scopes.
- [ ] Cache tokens are not counted twice in any displayed aggregate, cost calculation, or telemetry field.
- [ ] Claude raw `input_tokens` maps to Fresh input; Claude cache fields remain separate.
- [ ] Codex inclusive input is split correctly into fresh/cache categories.
- [ ] Session cards and inspector labels distinguish processed volume from fresh input and cost.
- [ ] OpenAPI and frontend generated types are regenerated together.
- [ ] Parser, aggregation, controller, and renderer tests cover the reporting contract.

## Related

- [PR #4003](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4003) — adds token cost telemetry and should use the same mutually exclusive category contract.
- [PR #2928](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2928) — introduced event-driven session token usage.

title: feat(cli): no supported way to restart all running sessions — needed to pick up a new agent-CLI build
body:
## Problem

There is no supported way to restart every running session — which is exactly what you must
do to pick up a new agent-CLI build.

A running `claude` process holds the inode of its own binary. Updating Claude Code relaunches
nothing: the symlink flips, but every live session keeps executing the old build until it
exits. So "update all my agents" is really "restart all my sessions", and AO offers no verb
for it.

This is not hypothetical. New Claude models shipped, and I currently have **29 live sessions
— 18 of them orchestrators**. Every one of them is pinned to the build it started with.

## Why the existing mechanisms don't cover it

`Manager.RestoreAll` (`session_manager/manager.go:2336`) already does the right thing, but it
is unreachable:

- it is **boot-only**, called from `Reconcile` (`:2256`) via `daemon/daemon.go:352`;
- it has **no HTTP route and no CLI verb**;
- it is **marker-driven** — a session is only picked up if it has `session_worktrees` rows
  with `state='removed'`.

And `Kill` deletes those rows on purpose (`manager.go:1454`, `:1490`, `:1508` — the comment
says it plainly: so the next boot's RestoreAll cannot resurrect a session the user killed).

The consequence is the trap: **"kill everything, then restart the daemon" does not work.**
The markers are gone, so RestoreAll skips them and the sessions simply stay dead.

`ao session cleanup` is not an alternative either — it deletes workspaces, and per #3591 it
does so even for non-terminated sessions.

## What users have to write instead

Every operator ends up hand-rolling the same loop:

```bash
ao session ls --json --all --include-terminated \
| jq -r '.data[] | select(.isTerminated == false) | "\(.id) \(.projectId)"' \
| while read -r id proj; do
    ao session kill    "$id" -p "$proj" || continue
    ao session restore "$id" -p "$proj"
    sleep 3
  done
```

Every part of that is a footgun:

1. **`--all` is mandatory but easy to miss.** Without it orchestrators are hidden
   (`filterAndSortSessions`, `cli/session.go:633`). In my case that silently skips 18 of 29
   sessions — the majority.
2. **Kill/restore is not atomic.** If `kill` succeeds and `restore` fails, the session is
   left terminated. There is no rollback and no report.
3. **Nothing excludes the current session.** Killing the orchestrator you are typing in cuts
   your own connection mid-loop. This is the same class of bug as #3591, where a bulk command
   destroyed the workspace of the very session that invoked it.
4. **The single-live-orchestrator invariant is not enforced on restore.** It is checked on
   spawn only (`service/session/service.go:226-232`, `:384-420`). A partially-failed loop
   re-run can produce duplicates.
5. **No throttling.** Each restore does git-worktree work plus a `tmux new-session`; the
   daemon's own `RestoreAll` is strictly sequential, but a user loop has no such guarantee.
6. **Silent history loss.** Restore degrades to a fresh launch when the transcript JSONL is
   missing (`claudeTranscriptExists`, `claudecode_profile.go:132`). That is reported as
   `restoreMode`, but a shell loop discards it.

## Proposal

Expose the capability that already exists, with the guards a manual loop cannot provide.

**CLI**

```
ao session restart-all [--project <id>] [--include-orchestrators]
                       [--exclude <id>...] [--concurrency N] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

Semantics:

- default target set = all **non-terminated** sessions (restart = kill + restore per session);
- **always exclude the invoking session** (detected via `AO_SESSION_ID`, already exported into
  every supervised process) unless `--force-self` is passed — the #3591 lesson;
- orchestrators require an explicit opt-in flag, given the invariant is unguarded on restore;
- sequential by default, `--concurrency` bounded, mirroring `RestoreAll`;
- per-session result line including `restoreMode`, so `Fresh` (history lost) is visible;
- `--dry-run` prints the plan without touching anything;
- on a failed restore after a successful kill: report loudly, keep going, exit non-zero.

**Ordering matters:** the reap pass must precede relaunch, exactly as `Reconcile` does
(`manager.go:2241-2243`), because tmux session names are deterministic (`tmux.go:902`) and a
leaked session of the same name collides.

**HTTP:** a matching endpoint so the desktop UI can offer "Restart all sessions" — the natural
place for this after an agent-CLI update.

## Alternative considered

Making `Kill` preserve the restore markers so a daemon restart resurrects everything. Rejected:
it would break the deliberate behavior that a user-killed session stays dead, which is exactly
what those code comments protect.

## Related

- #3591 — bulk session command destroyed the workspace of the session that invoked it; the
  same self-exclusion guard is needed here.
- #3265 — orchestrators and workers share one numeric id space, so a bulk loop cannot tell
  roles apart by name alone; this is why `--all` silently hiding orchestrators is dangerous.

## Environment

- 29 live sessions (18 orchestrators, 11 workers) across 20 projects
- macOS, tmux runtime, claude-code harness


---

## Update: implemented and validated locally

I went ahead and built this against the current CLI. It is running on my own fleet; happy to
open a PR if the shape below looks right.

```
ao session restart-all [flags]

  -p, --project string         restart only sessions of this project
      --include-orchestrators  also restart orchestrators (skipped by default)
      --orchestrators-only     restart only orchestrators
      --exclude strings        session ids to leave running
      --self string            id of the calling session (default: AO_SESSION_ID)
      --dry-run                print the plan and exit
  -y, --yes                    skip confirmation
      --json                   machine-readable output
      --settle-delay duration  pause between kill and restore (default 2s)
```

Four files, +644 lines: the command, its tests, one registration line, and one telemetry
classification entry.

### Design decisions worth reviewing

**Workers by default, orchestrators behind a flag.** Killing an orchestrator interrupts the
work it coordinates, while workers are cheap to relaunch. `--orchestrators-only` covers the
opposite case: refreshing the long-lived orchestrators without disturbing workers mid-task.
The two selectors are mutually exclusive.

**Serial, not concurrent.** I dropped the `--concurrency` flag from the original proposal.
Restore recreates the tmux session under a deterministic name, so the previous one has to be
reaped first, and every call also does git-worktree work — the same reasons `RestoreAll` is
serial in the daemon. A `--settle-delay` (default 2s) sits between kill and restore instead.

**Self-exclusion needs more than the env var.** `AO_SESSION_ID` is the right primary source —
it is what `preview`, `hooks`, `claim-pr` and `session switch-agent` already use. But it is not
always present: running the command from a plain shell leaves it unset, and the calling session
then becomes an ordinary target. Rather than inferring identity from the process tree (which
would diverge from every other session-scoped verb), the command takes an explicit `--self` and
warns on stderr when the caller cannot be identified. This is the #3591 guard, made visible
instead of silent.

**Failures are named, not summarized.** A failed restore after a successful kill leaves a
session terminated — the worst outcome here. Those sessions are listed individually and the
command exits non-zero, so a wrapper script can spot what needs a manual restore.

### What I have not done

- No HTTP endpoint yet, so no UI button — the CLI-side loop was the blocking need.
- `restoreMode` is not surfaced per session. The restore response carries it, but the CLI's
  `restoreSessionResponse` does not decode it today; plumbing it through is a separate change
  and would make `Fresh` (history lost) visible, which I still think is worth having.

### Validation

Nine tests covering: the default worker-only selection, the orchestrator-only inverse,
self-exclusion via env and via `--self`, the warning when neither is available, `--dry-run`
mutating nothing, a failed restore being reported with a non-zero exit, the JSON shape, and
the mutually-exclusive selectors. Full backend suite and `golangci-lint` are clean.

Also exercised against a live daemon: `--dry-run` correctly split a running fleet into its
worker and orchestrator sets, and a single-session kill+restore round trip relaunched an
orchestrator natively via `--resume`, keeping a 23 MB transcript intact and picking up the
newer agent binary — which is the whole point of the command.

title: feat(browser): add persistent profiles with cookie and history import
body:
## What

Add opt-in persistent browser profiles to AO.

Users can now:

- Create, rename, clear, and delete named browser profiles from Settings.
- Switch profiles from the browser toolbar.
- Keep cookies and browsing history across AO restarts.
- Import cookies and history from supported Chromium-based browsers, Firefox, and Zen.
- Select one or more detected source profiles and import them into new AO profiles.
- Use imported history as address-bar suggestions.

Temporary profiles remain the default, preserving the existing ephemeral and per-worker-isolated behavior.

## Why

AO browser workers previously used temporary sessions only. This meant authentication and browsing context were lost when the worker or app restarted.

Persistent profiles let users explicitly retain useful browser state without exposing profile selection to agents or changing the default behavior for existing sessions.

## How

- Stores AO-owned profile metadata and imported history under `~/.ao`.
- Uses a dedicated persistent Electron partition for each named AO profile.
- Keeps profile selection user-controlled through Settings and the browser toolbar.
- Reads source browser databases through read-only snapshots without exposing source paths to the renderer.
- Validates source paths, realpath containment, symlinks, database sizes, record counts, and import limits before committing data.
- Creates new destination profiles instead of silently overwriting existing profiles.
- Rolls back newly created profiles and imported state when an import fails.
- Handles Chromium cookie encryption and Firefox database differences, reporting skipped or unsupported data as warnings.
- Preserves browser permission denial, renderer ownership checks, tab isolation, lifecycle cleanup, and the restriction preventing agents from choosing `--profile`.
- Packages the SQLite runtime required by the importer in production builds.

Intentional omissions:

- Bookmarks
- Passwords
- Extensions
- Full browser-profile directory copying
- Signed-in browser account synchronization
- Domain-filtered imports


## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- Focused browser, profile, settings, preload, and IPC tests:
  - 8 test files passed
  - 233 tests passed
- Import, rollback, source-validation, lifecycle, packaging, and Chromium cookie compatibility tests were added during implementation.
- Production packaging and packaged SQLite runtime verification passed before the final upstream merge.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing an existing PR branch
- [x] One focused browser-profile and import feature
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added or updated for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the final pushed commit

title: fix(browser-panel): tabs rail placement, overlay blanking, and URL bar scroll
body:
## Summary
Phase 1 of the AO in-app browser UX overhaul (fix-the-breakages pass, scoped against current `main`):

- Tabs rail now renders on the right in both docked and popped-out/maximized mode (previously it flipped to the left when maximized).
- Fixed the black screen behind any raised overlay (tabs-rail flyout, dialogs, etc.). **Update:** the first attempt only toggled a Tailwind utility class; `.browser-panel__viewport` also carries its own unconditional plain-CSS background in `styles.css`, and unlayered author CSS always beats a Tailwind utility regardless of class presence, so the first fix had no real effect. Fixed properly now by gating the actual CSS rule behind a `data-placeholder` attribute.
- The "Pick element" / agent-activity status no longer sits in the toolbar as permanent on-screen text for the whole duration of picking or agent activity — it's now a small status dot with the detail available on hover (native tooltip) and still announced to screen readers via an sr-only live region.
- Added a stress-test regression guard for the previously-reported "tabs stop closing after a long session" bug, driving the real `closeTab`/`destroyTabView` main-process code through hundreds of open/close/reactivate cycles. It does not currently reproduce on `main` — several stabilization fixes already landed upstream since it was first reported — so no production fix was needed, just the regression guard plus a note on `closeTab`.

title: Windows app takes too long to open because of serial daemon probe timeouts
body:
## Bug

After #4013 fixed the flashing command prompt windows, the Windows app got really slow to open. Like you open the app and it just sits there on the loading screen for 6+ seconds doing nothing before the daemon even starts.

## Why this is happening

In `frontend/src/main.ts`, the `startDaemonInner` function runs three HTTP probes one after another to check if a daemon is already running. Each probe waits 2 seconds to timeout. On a cold start when no daemon is running, all three timeout, so thats 6 seconds of just waiting for nothing.

The thing is, on localhost a refused connection comes back in like 20ms. So waiting 2 seconds each time is just wasting the users time.

This wasnt as noticeable before #4013 because Windows dev mode used to run `go run` which was slow anyway. Now that it uses a prebuilt exe, the probe wait time is the main bottleneck.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, make sure no daemon is running
2. Open the app or run `cd frontend && npm run dev`
3. Watch it sit on the loading screen for a while before anything happens

## Expected

App should open fast. Shouldnt be waiting 6 seconds for localhost connections to tell us nobody is listening.

## Notes

- Only affects Windows, dont touch macOS or Linux
- Got worse after #4013 because Windows now goes through the full probe chain

title: fix(windows): reduce daemon probe timeouts for faster app startup
body:
## What happened

After #4013 fixed the flashing cmd windows on Windows, app startup got noticeably slower. On a cold start (no daemon running), the app just hangs for like 6 seconds before the daemon even starts spawning.

Turns out `startDaemonInner` runs three HTTP probes back to back and each one waits 2 full seconds to timeout. On localhost a refused connection comes back in like 20ms, so 2 seconds per probe is way too much.

## What this PR does

Two small changes, both Windows only:

1. Probe timeout goes from 2000ms to 500ms on Windows. Thats still plenty for localhost, and shaves off ~4.5 seconds on cold start.
2. Skip the orphan probe when theres no run file. If nothing suggests a daemon was ever running, no point burning another timeout checking for one.

macOS and Linux are not touched at all.

Closes #4138

## Test plan

- [x] daemon-launch, daemon-attach, daemon-takeover tests all pass (49 tests)
- [ ] Cold start on Windows should be noticeably faster
- [ ] Warm start (daemon already running) should work same as before
- [ ] macOS/Linux startup unchanged

title: bug(agent-claude-code): session stuck working/active after a turn dies without its Stop hook (login expired) — observer skips claude-code, no TerminalActivityDetector
body:
## Bug

A claude-code worker session (live: `agent-orchestrator-139`) shows **status=working / activity=active** indefinitely while the Claude CLI is provably idle at its composer. The last turn aborted on an expired OAuth login (`Login expired · Please run /login`, `Worked for 0s`), so the turn's Stop hook never fired — and nothing else ever demotes the stale `active`.

**Source:** live observation of session `agent-orchestrator-139` (tmux pane capture) | **Reported by:** maintainer via orchestrator task | **Analyzed against:** `0e472e2b2`
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a claude-code TUI worker; let a turn start (`user-prompt-submit` → activity=active).
2. Kill the turn without a Stop hook — auth expiry mid-stream reproduces it (turn ends with `Login expired · Please run /login`, `✻ Worked for 0s`); a CLI crash or network drop behaves the same.
3. Observe `ao session get`: status stays `working`, activity stays `active` forever. Any further Enter on the logged-out CLI re-fires `user-prompt-submit` and re-asserts `active` (which is why `updated` advances on each retry while nothing runs).

## Root Cause

Claude Code's durable activity is **hook-driven only** (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/activity.go` → `lifecycle.ApplyActivitySignal`). The only transitions out of `active` are the `stop` / `notification(idle_prompt)` / `session-end` hooks. A turn that dies mid-stream emits none of them.

AO already has the exact safety net for this: the activity observer (`backend/internal/observe/activity/observer.go:103-131`) polls every 30s and, for sessions stuck `active` past `DefaultStaleAfter` (2 min), screen-proves the real state via the adapter's `TerminalActivityDetector`. But the claude-code adapter **never implemented `DetectTerminalActivity`**, so `reconcile()` returns at the type assertion (`observer.go:111-114`) and claude-code sessions are exempt from reconciliation entirely. (The adapter has `InspectTerminalSurface` — the classification logic exists — it just isn't wired to the detector port.) The prior test `TestPollLeavesOtherHarnessesUntouched` even pinned claude-code as the example of a skipped harness.

Verified against the live pane: `InspectTerminalSurface` on the stuck screen (login-expired footer, staged draft in the composer, no active chrome) correctly yields `Work=Idle` — the observer would have converged the session within one tick if the detector had been wired.

Hypotheses ruled out: hook/classifier precedence is not involved (there is simply no classifier signal), and nothing refreshes `updated` unconditionally (it stayed frozen at `15:15:56Z` for 6+ minutes of observation; it only advances when the user re-submits on the logged-out CLI).

## Fix

Implement `DetectTerminalActivity` on the claude-code plugin, delegating to `InspectTerminalSurface` — authoritative idle only when the surface positively shows an idle composer (same pattern codex shipped for #3115). Claude stays non-continuous: hooks remain authoritative while they flow; the observer only reconciles a stale `active`.

## Impact

- Users see a phantom "Working" session and wait for output that never comes; the logged-out state is hidden.
- Orchestrators treat the worker as busy and won't dispatch or escalate.
- Class bug: ANY hook turn-death (auth expiry, crash, network) strands claude-code in `working` — until now, permanently.

## Related

- [#3387](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3387) — same class for Kimi; documents that only codex implemented `TerminalActivityDetector` (this issue is the claude-code instance)
- [#3115](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3115) — codex instance (fixed by codex's `terminal_activity.go`)
- [#4048](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4048) — cline instance (fixed via continuous reconciliation)
- [#2047](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2047) — broader claude activity misreporting

title: fix(claude-code): reconcile stuck-active sessions via terminal activity detection
body:
Fixes #4142

## Summary

A Claude Code turn that dies without emitting its Stop hook (expired OAuth login, CLI crash, network loss) left the session's hook-driven activity stuck at `active`, so the app showed **status=working** forever while the CLI sat idle at its composer (live incident: `agent-orchestrator-139`, stranded on `Login expired · Please run /login`).

The activity observer already reconciles exactly this case — a session stale in `active` past 2 minutes is screen-proven against the adapter's `TerminalActivityDetector` — but the claude-code adapter never implemented that capability, so the observer skipped its sessions at the type assertion (`observer.go:111-114`).

This PR implements `DetectTerminalActivity` on the claude-code plugin, same pattern as codex (#3115): delegate to the existing `InspectTerminalSurface` and report an **authoritative idle only** when the current surface positively shows an idle composer with no active spinner/interrupt chrome and no pending decision frame. Anything else fails closed. Claude deliberately stays non-continuous: hooks remain authoritative while they flow; the observer only steps in for a stale `active`.

Scope note: this intentionally fixes claude-code only. The same class bug for other hook-only harnesses is tracked in #3387 (Kimi).

## Changes

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/terminal_activity.go` (new): `DetectTerminalActivity` delegating to `InspectTerminalSurface`, idle-only, fail-closed.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/terminal_activity_test.go` (new): fixtures reproduce the real captured stuck screen (login-expired footer + staged draft, and empty-composer variant) → authoritative idle; active spinner, active footer hint, permission dialog, unrecognizable/empty output → not authoritative.
- `backend/internal/observe/activity/observer_test.go`: `TestPollLeavesOtherHarnessesUntouched` previously pinned claude-code as exempt from reconciliation (encoding the bug) — now uses droid as the detector-less example. Added `TestPollReconcilesStaleClaudeCodeAfterAbortedTurn` (stuck screen → one `terminal-idle` signal with launch/updatedAt fence) and `TestPollKeepsGenuineLongClaudeTurnActive` (real active chrome → no signal).

## Behavior notes

Implementing the `TerminalActivityDetector` port also opts claude-code into the two existing detector consumers beyond the observer, both matching codex's shipped behavior:
- `WaitForMessageDeliveryReady` now screen-proves the composer before injecting (previously: durable idle + first-hook-or-5s fallback) — strictly stronger evidence.
- The interface-transition drain's legacy fallback (only reachable when styled output is unavailable) can now prove idle for claude-code; it additionally requires `ComposerIsEmpty`, which claude-code already implements.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/ ./internal/observe/activity/ ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/lifecycle/` — pass
- Full `go test ./...` — pass (`internal/cli` requires all `AO_*` env unset; failures with leaked env are pre-existing and unrelated)
- Classifier hand-verified against the live stuck pane of `agent-orchestrator-139` (plain `tmux capture-pane`, which is what the observer's `GetOutput` provides): `Work=Idle`, so the observer converges the session within one tick after staleness.

## Risks / follow-ups

- A genuinely active turn whose rendering momentarily lacks both the spinner row and the footer interrupt hint could be sampled as idle; the next tool hook immediately re-asserts `active`, and this is the same trade-off codex has shipped since #3115.
- Follow-up filed separately: surface the `Login expired` screen as a distinct needs-input reason so users know to run `/login` instead of seeing a silent idle.

title: feat: improve update check feedback
body: ## Summary - check automatically on launch and every hour while automatic updates are enabled - make the current update state immediately scannable, with state-specific status, progress, and actions - show the exact running version and its Stable, Nightly, Feature, or Local preview identity separately from the configured update feed - persist the last successful check across launches; failed checks keep the last known-good timestamp - record a real installed/updated timestamp when the running version changes - keep manual checking available, preserve explicit opt-outs, and respect reduced-motion and localization requirements ## UX decisions - **Automatic by default:** installed releases check on launch and hourly, matching the convention used by comparable desktop developer tools. - **Installed build is not the update feed:** the badge describes what is running; the channel selector describes where future updates come from. - **Truthful timestamps:** “Last checked” means the last successful update check. “Updated” is recorded only after a running-version change. - **Exact nightly identity:** nightly builds show the full stamped version instead of collapsing it to a generic “Nightly” label. - **Clear local-build language:** source checkouts are called “Local preview,” with a compact explanation that update checks require an installed release. ## Scenarios ### 1. Stable — up to date A successful check shows the exact installed version, Stable badge, last successful check, and when this build was installed or updated. The configured Stable feed remains visible as a separate setting. ### 2. Checking automatically Installed releases enter this state at launch and on the hourly cadence. The status and action both communicate active work, so the page never looks idle while a request is in flight. ### 3. Update available The available version is named directly and the primary action is unambiguous, while the currently installed version remains visible for comparison. ### 4. Downloading A determinate progress bar and percentage replace the primary action during download, preventing duplicate requests and making background progress visible. ### 5. Ready to restart Once downloaded, the UI says what remains and promotes the conventional final action: restart and install. ### 6. Check failed A failed request gets a visible retry action and an actionable message. The previous successful “Last checked” value remains intact instead of being overwritten by the error. ### 7. Nightly — exact installed build Nightly users see the full stamped semver for the build that is actually running, a Nightly badge, and the pre-release risk warning. This answers both “am I on Nightly?” and “which Nightly exactly?” ### 8. Automatic updates off Explicit opt-outs are preserved. Manual checking stays available, and channel controls are hidden because they have no effect until automatic updates are enabled again. ## Testing - `npm run frontend:typecheck` - `cd frontend && npm test` (2,596 passed, 1 skipped) - `cd backend && go test -p 1 ./...` - `cd frontend && npm run package` - native Electron walkthrough on macOS across every scenario above

title: feat(activity): recognize provider auth-expiry screens as a distinct needs-input state so users know to /login
body:
## Feature

Follow-up to [#4142](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4142) / [PR #4143](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4143).

With #4143, a claude-code session whose turn died on an expired login now converges to **idle** via the activity observer's stale-active reconciliation. That fixes the phantom "Working", but idle still under-communicates: the session cannot make progress until the user runs `/login` in the pane, and nothing in the UI says so. The user's next send just stages in a logged-out composer (that is exactly what happened on `agent-orchestrator-139`: a typed message sat unprocessed for hours).

## Proposal

Recognize the provider's auth-expiry surface explicitly and surface it as a needs-input state with a distinct reason:

- Claude Code renders `Login expired · Please run /login` (and `/login` prompts on startup when logged out). `InspectTerminalSurface`/`DetectTerminalActivity` could classify this as `waiting_input` (or a new `TerminalSurfaceWork` variant) instead of plain idle, carrying an auth-required reason.
- The claude-code adapter already has `AuthStatus()` (`claudecode.go:360`) — the session UI could correlate and show "Login expired — run /login in Terminal" on the session card / needs-input notification, matching how needs-input pings work today.
- Same pattern applies to other harnesses with recognizable auth-error screens (Kimi's `provider.auth_error 401`, see [#3387](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3387)).

## Why it matters

- Idle reads as "ready for work"; orchestrators will happily dispatch to a logged-out worker whose composer silently swallows prompts.
- A needs-input ping is the existing, well-understood channel for "a human must act here".

## Related

- [#4142](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4142) — the stuck-working bug this follows up
- [#3387](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3387) — Kimi auth-error instance of the class

title: fix(browser): non-disruptive preview reveal + reopen closed tabs
body:
## Summary
Phase 2 of the AO in-app browser UX overhaul (calmer, less intrusive UX):

- **Non-disruptive agent browser actions**: a new `ao preview` target used to force-switch the inspector to the Browser tab and pop it open, even if the user was looking at something else entirely (Reviews, chat, a different session). Now it just badges Browser as unseen — same pattern already used for general agent browser activity (fill/click/snapshot) — and lets the user open it when they're ready.
- **Reopen tabs closed by the agent (or you)**: closing a tab was final — the only way back was asking the agent to reopen it. Now the last 5 closed tabs (with title/url/favicon) show as a "Recently closed" section in the tabs rail, in both the popped-out list and the docked hover flyout, click to reopen. The list now survives switching sessions and back (previously renderer-only state, lost on any session switch — unlike live tabs, which are kept alive in the main process).
- **Fixed the automation runtime permanently wedging a session**: `ensureNativeActiveTab`'s convergence loop retried the identical failing `tab-select` forever once the runtime's own tab registry forgot the active tab, wedging every native browser operation for the session — not just close, but tab switching too. It now asks the runtime to refresh its own view before retrying once, and accepts the drift (with a `console.warn` breadcrumb) instead of looping forever if still stale.
- **Fixed a reopen leaving contradictory state**: reopening a closed tab pointed at a dead localhost dev server used to report failure while the tab was actually created and left open — `openTab` threw after already telling the renderer the tab existed. It now matches how navigating an *existing* tab to a dead URL already worked (tab exists, shows an error page, no throw).
- **Fixed the close fallback double-closing an already-closed tab**: the automation runtime's own `Target.closeTarget` handling can close a tab internally before the runtime still reports the overall command as failed. The fallback used to retry AO's own close regardless, throwing `TAB_NOT_FOUND` for a tab that had already, genuinely closed. It now checks whether the tab is already gone and treats that as success. The renderer's close handler also now resyncs tab state from the main process on any failure, instead of leaving a stale "ghost" row that re-fails identically on every retry.
- **Fixed reopening at the 16-tab cap silently losing the closed-tab entry**: gated on the same cap the "+" button respects, with restore-on-failure for races.
- Favicons now render in Recently Closed rows (previously captured but unused). Close/select failures surface a transient notice instead of an unhandled rejection. `closeTab`'s identity no longer churns on every tab update.

## Scope note
The original Phase 2 plan also included a "general smoothness" item (optimistic tab select/close instead of waiting on the IPC round-trip, and/or trimming a MutationObserver's overhead). Left out of this PR — the codebase's own comments show that overhead was already a deliberate, documented trade-off, and reworking tab-selection to be optimistic carries real risk of subtle state bugs that's better done as its own focused pass rather than rushed in here.

The upstream question of *why* the automation runtime's tab registry drifts from `session.tabs` in the first place is still open and deliberately out of scope here — this PR makes AO resilient to it happening, not a fix to the runtime itself. Worth its own follow-up issue.

A separate, pre-existing paper cut was flagged during review: `browser:navigate` silently rejects a URL matching the renderer's own origin (a dev-mode `localhost:517x` port) with no notice surfaced to the user. Confirmed out of scope for this PR by the reviewer.

- [x] `npx vitest run` on `browser-view-host.test.ts`, `BrowserPanel.test.tsx`, `useBrowserView.test.tsx`, `i18n/instance.test.ts` — 163/163 passing, with regression tests for every fix above (each verified to fail against the pre-fix code before being confirmed passing)
- [x] Manual pass in the real Electron app across three rounds of review — tabs opening/closing/switching, Recently Closed (favicons, cap gating, reopen, session-switch persistence), non-disruptive preview reveal

title: fix: isolate ChatUI history by session
body:
## Summary
- prevent ChatUI from rendering a conversation snapshot that belongs to a previously selected session
- remount `ChatWorkspace` when the selected session changes so retained timeline/composer state cannot carry across orchestrators
- hide project conversation pages before the current orchestrator's `ao-context-reset:<session>` boundary, so a replacement orchestrator does not page in the previous orchestrator's history
- filter stale queued/running turns at the same reset boundary so old turn state cannot make the replacement orchestrator appear busy
- persist the fresh-context reset boundary atomically with project conversation rebinds before provider startup
- strengthen regression coverage with a stateful workspace mock and a store-level project conversation rebind/reset test

## Root cause
Project-scoped conversations are intentionally rebound when an orchestrator is replaced. The frontend-only fix reset retained React state, but the paged conversation API could still return rows from before the fresh agent context boundary. That made old orchestrator history visible again after switching/replacing orchestrators.

This PR now treats the context-reset system activity for the current project orchestrator as the first visible sequence for paged ChatUI reads. The boundary activity remains stored as internal metadata, but it is not returned in paged ChatUI reads; older turns, messages, and activities are not returned or pageable from the replacement orchestrator view. The fresh-context boundary is written in the same transaction as the project conversation rebind before provider startup, so provider-start failures do not expose old history under the replacement session.

title: fix(auth): complete WorkOS sign-in locally
body:
## Summary
- use a temporary fixed-port 127.0.0.1 callback during WorkOS PKCE sign-in so the browser receives a final success page
- try WorkOS-configured callback ports in order: 5174, 3000, then 3001
- show "You can close this tab and return to Agent Orchestrator" after the code exchange completes
- trigger a focus-only ao-app://complete handoff from that success page so the browser still shows the native app-open prompt
- keep the existing ao-app://callback handling as a fallback for older in-flight auth redirects
- avoid relaunching WorkOS when a valid cloud session already exists

## Root cause
The sign-in flow used the custom ao-app:// callback as the primary redirect. Browsers present that as an external app launch prompt, and some OS/browser combinations pass the deep-link argument differently or leave the provider tab sitting on a page that keeps trying to hand off to Electron. Switching the token exchange to a local HTTP callback fixes the browser UX, but WorkOS requires the redirect URI to match the application settings exactly, so the callback must use one of the configured loopback ports instead of a random port. A separate ao-app://complete deep link restores the native prompt after the browser has already landed on the close-tab page.

## Validation

- npm run frontend:typecheck

title: Terminal flickers and looks like it reloads while resizing
body:
## What happened

The terminal did not resize smoothly when the app layout changed. Opening or closing the inspector, dragging its edge, or resizing the app window could make the text shake, briefly disappear, and then come back as if the terminal had reloaded.

This was especially noticeable when Claude or Codex was showing a full-screen interface. The session itself was still running and no work was lost, but the repeated flashing made the terminal feel unstable and difficult to follow.

## How to reproduce

1. Open a session that is showing a full-screen terminal interface.
2. Open or close the inspector panel, or drag the divider beside it.
3. You can also slowly resize the app window from its edge.
4. Watch the terminal while its width is changing.

The text may jump around, the terminal may flash black for a moment, and the whole screen may redraw several times before settling.

## What should happen

The terminal should follow the available space without repeatedly flashing or looking like it restarted. Once the resize ends, it should quickly settle on the correct number of rows and columns.

## Why it happened

The app was doing too much work for every tiny movement during a resize.

A single drag can produce many size updates in a very short time. Each update could make the terminal recalculate its layout and ask the program inside it to redraw. On Windows, those redraws are particularly expensive because the terminal program may send most of its screen again after every size change.

There was also a short moment where the old terminal canvas had been cleared but the new content had not been painted yet. That is what caused the black flash. At the same time, the inspector animation kept changing the terminal's available width, creating even more resize work.

These smaller problems happened together, which is why earlier fixes that changed only one resize timer did not fully solve the issue.

## How it was fixed

The terminal now handles resize activity in a more controlled way:

- It avoids repeating expensive layout work when the usable terminal grid has not actually changed.
- It limits how often a new size is sent to the running terminal program during a drag, while still guaranteeing that the final size is sent immediately.
- It keeps the short clear-and-redraw response together so users do not see an empty frame in between.
- The inspector reserves its space in one step and then slides visually, instead of continuously squeezing the terminal throughout the animation.
- The terminal renderer was updated to a version that includes an upstream fix for blank frames during resize.

The full implementation details are documented in [PR #4357](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4357).

## Verification

- 202 focused terminal tests passed.
- Frontend TypeScript checks passed.
- All GitHub CI checks passed, including frontend tests and Windows, macOS, and Linux jobs.

## Related work

- [PR #4156](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4156) was the first attempt and was closed without merging.
- [PR #4357](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4357) contains the complete fix.
- [Issue #2333](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2333) covers other terminal blanking cases that are not caused by resizing.

title: fix(terminal): reduce resize jitter by CSS-scaling during animations
body:
## What happened

The terminal flickers and jitters whenever the container resizes, especially during inspector panel open/close animations. Four things were going wrong at the same time in XtermTerminal.tsx.

## What this PR does

1. **CSS-scale during animations instead of fitting every frame** - When the live-resize attribute is active, we now scale the existing canvas with CSS transform to match the container size. One real fit() happens when the animation ends. This completely avoids the WebGL atlas rebuild storm that was causing the flicker.

2. **Gate the convergence loop behind the debounce** - Added a `debounceInFlight` flag so the onRender convergence loop skips its work while a debounced fit is pending. Before this they could run at the same time and fight over the grid size.

3. **Pin the scrollbar width permanently** - After zeroing `viewport.scrollBarWidth`, we now freeze it with `Object.defineProperty` so FitAddon cant re-read the DOM and bring back the 15px reservation on subsequent fits.

4. **Skip late settle timeouts when ResizeObserver already settled** - The 600ms and 1200ms backstop timeouts now check if the ResizeObserver already produced a stable frame and skip if so. The early 50/250ms ones still run since they help with font loading.

Closes #4155

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles clean (only pre-existing error in product-ui, unrelated)
- [ ] Open/close inspector panel, terminal should resize smoothly without flicker
- [ ] Drag sidebar, terminal should scale during drag and snap to correct grid after

title: feat: nudge SCM polling on agent turn end
body:
## Summary

- reduce agent-driven PR discovery and state-refresh latency from up to the 30-second fallback interval to about 2 seconds after an accepted agent turn-end signal
- cover the full mutation class: PR creation, draft→ready, close, reopen, and pushes to an existing PR branch
- add a concurrent-safe, non-blocking SCM observer nudge channel with a 2-second debounce window
- coalesce concurrent turn-end hooks into one poll and let a regular tick satisfy a pending nudge, avoiding back-to-back provider scans
- wire normalized agent stop hooks through lifecycle after session/generation fencing; terminal command parsing was intentionally avoided because one provider-neutral turn-end signal covers all supported PR mutations
- preserve the independent 30-second scheduled poll as the fallback

## Before / after

Before, a PR created or mutated by an agent could remain stale in the sidebar until the next SCM tick, adding up to about 30 seconds of latency. After, the accepted turn-end hook schedules one debounced poll, so the sidebar normally reflects the mutation in about 2 seconds.

## Tests

- added an end-to-end observer-loop test that establishes a draft PR, changes it to ready, nudges the observer, and verifies the ready state is persisted without waiting for the hourly test ticker
- go test ./... (with all AO_* environment variables unset)
- npm run lint (with all AO_* environment variables unset)
- go test -race ./internal/observe/scm ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/daemon
- repeated focused nudge, draft→ready, debounce, and lifecycle wiring tests (20 runs)

## Risk

The nudge performs the existing full observer poll. Discovery and refresh remain scoped by the observer to tracked sessions, branches, PRs, and repositories; no new provider API path, command parsing, or persisted state was added.

title: feat(cloud): deploy hardened AWS auth foundation
body:
## Summary

This is the hardened hosted-control-plane stack for #4116.

- deploys the PostgreSQL/Google-auth control plane to AWS through API Gateway, an internal ALB, ECS Fargate, and private encrypted RDS
- separates migration, runtime, auth-definer, and SCM-definer database roles; every tenant relation uses forced RLS and startup validation
- adds tenant-scoped PostgreSQL project/session/worktree storage behind the existing AO ports and shared `/api/v1` route classification
- adds the provider-neutral session execution/workspace-observation seams without moving filesystem or runtime logic into Electron
- adds the control-plane OpenAPI/client contract, including async workspace placement, worker operations, and one-time sandbox terminal-ticket redemption
- adds a first-class **AO Cloud** source to the existing desktop Projects `+` flow; tokens and generic fetch remain in Electron main
- adds the GitHub App SCM boundary: OAuth-proven installation ownership, default-deny repository allowlists, fresh scoped clone/push credentials, durable/idempotent webhook processing, and least-privilege PostgreSQL grants

## Load-bearing security properties

- the runtime database role is a separate unprivileged login and never owns tenant tables or SECURITY DEFINER functions
- SCM webhook and observation ledgers have no direct runtime CRUD; the runtime receives only exact function EXECUTE grants
- GitHub setup and user OAuth callbacks are distinct, state-bound phases; spoofed installations and failed ownership checks do not consume the AO-admin state
- credential material is mutable bytes, bounded, zeroed, never cached, and never returned through renderer IPC or persisted in the SCM ledger
- hosted `/api/v1` tenant selection uses authenticated `X-AO-Org`; org-admin routes retain explicit `orgId` membership checks
- the desktop app remains a thin supervisor; hosted filesystem and PTY bytes belong to sandbox adapters, not Electron or the control plane

## Verification

- `npm run cloud:check`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- focused Electron cloud placement/auth/preload/component tests (69 passing)
- focused cloud client tests (10 passing)
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/cloud/... ./cmd/ao-cloud ./cmd/ao-cloud-migrate`
- `cd backend && go vet ./internal/cloud/... ./cmd/ao-cloud ./cmd/ao-cloud-migrate`
- pinned golangci-lint v2.12.2 on changed cloud packages
- real PostgreSQL 16 restricted-role auth/core-storage/SCM installation/webhook conformance, including RLS, replay, lease recovery, and exact grant boundaries
- native dev Electron restarted with the staging Cloud URL and Cloud early-access flag; Projects `+` exposes the AO Cloud source

## Remaining live-staging gates

The desktop discovery/create surface and contracts are present, but this PR is **not claiming end-to-end sandbox provisioning yet**. Before calling the hosted flow production-ready, staging still needs the concrete workspace-placement/compute adapter, sandbox listener/ticket-consume implementation, and a real Daytona clone/session/mux acceptance run. Unsupported hosted application routes continue to fail closed rather than falling back to control-plane filesystem access.

title: fix(browser): keep panel resize handle draggable over the loaded page
body:
## Summary
- The inspector/terminal split's resize handle sits right at the edge of the browser panel. Electron's `WebContentsView` (the native surface that renders the loaded page) is a separate compositor layer stacked above the app's DOM, so once the drag crossed onto the loaded page's screen area, every subsequent `pointermove`/`pointerup` went straight to that native view instead of the app — killing the drag dead. Dragging over any normal DOM area (top bar, terminal, empty inspector) worked fine, matching the reported symptom.
- The codebase already has a mechanism for exactly this class of problem: `useBrowserView.ts` raises a transparent shell view above the live page (`window.ao.browser.setOverlayOpen`) whenever a dialog/menu needs input priority over the page, detected via a `MutationObserver` on `document.body`.
- This change extends that same detection to also treat `useResizable.ts`'s `is-resizing-x` body class (already toggled for the whole duration of any panel drag) as needing the shell raised, via a second lightweight `MutationObserver` scoped to `document.body`'s own `class` attribute (kept separate from the existing subtree/`data-state` observer so it doesn't fire on every className change app-wide).

## Test plan
- [ ] `ao preview <url>` into a session, open the inspector, and drag the resize handle across the loaded page — confirm the panel keeps resizing smoothly instead of the drag stopping dead.
- [ ] Confirm dragging the same handle when the inspector has no page loaded (or a blank tab) still works as before.
- [ ] Confirm opening a dropdown/dialog over the browser panel still works (regression check on the shared overlay mechanism).

title: fix(browser): crash on link click, agent-visible error signals, device-frame presets
body:
## Summary
Phase 3 of the AO in-app browser UX overhaul (agent visibility & frontend-dev ergonomics):

- **Fixed an app-crashing bug**: clicking any link with `target=_blank` (or `window.open()`) inside the browser crashed the whole app with `Invalid webContents. Created window should be connected to webContents passed with options object.` `setWindowOpenHandler`'s `createWindow` callback returned an independently-created `WebContentsView` that Electron's own `openGuestWindow` could never recognize as linked to the guest-window options it computed for that event. Now denies the guest window outright and opens (and actually navigates — it never did before, even before the crash) AO's own tab instead, entirely outside Electron's guest-window machinery.
- **Console errors and failed requests now reach the agent, always-on**: previously only visible via on-demand polling. Watches every tab's native `console-message` event (no CDP/debugger needed, so it can't conflict with agent-browser's own CDP session) and each session's shared `webRequest` for failed/errored XHR+fetch calls. Debounces a burst into one message per ~5s window and posts it through the same `POST /sessions/{id}/send` endpoint the annotation feature already uses — no new data captured beyond what's already visible in DevTools (text, method/url/status — never bodies).
- **Fixed tabs getting permanently stuck open**: reported live from a real long-running session as "Tab t5 not found; run `agent-browser tab` to list open tabs" on close. The external `agent-browser` automation binary keeps its own internal tab registry that can drift from AO's `session.tabs` over a long session; the close handler used to just propagate that failure and give up, leaving the tab stuck forever. Now falls back to AO's own close path (which only depends on `session.tabs` and the real `WebContentsView`, not the runtime's registry) for that specific failure; unrelated automation-runtime errors still surface normally.
- **Device-frame presets, redesigned**: one-click toolbar dropdown for responsive testing. Named real devices (iPhone SE/14 Pro, Pixel 7, Galaxy S22, iPad Mini/Pro) with reference dimensions shown, plus an inline custom-width field — no arbitrary "Mobile/Tablet/Desktop" buckets, no redundant Desktop option. Also fixes the dropdown rendering *behind* the live page (missing the `data-browser-native-overlay` marker that tells the shell to paint above the native view while it's open — the same mechanism the tabs-rail flyout already relies on).
