title: bug(terminal): selection drag does not auto-scroll — alt-buffer/tmux panes never get the drag-scroll the wheel already routes to them
body:
## Bug

Dragging a text selection past the top or bottom edge of an AO terminal does not auto-scroll the pane. The selection stays active and follows the pointer inside the viewport, but the terminal never scrolls, so a selection can never grow past what is already on screen. Ordinary selection and ordinary wheel scrolling both work.

**Reported by:** @whoisasx (in-app report) | **Analyzed against:** `85fab5e29ff718835a098e55ba598f0a2bc91e20` (`origin/main`)
**AO version:** `ao version dev` (worktree build) · desktop app running from `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app`
**OS:** macOS 26.6 (25G70), arm64 · Darwin 25.6.0 · daemon verified listening on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Confidence:** High — traced to specific lines, reproduced in a real Chromium against the shipped xterm build, and confirmed against real `tmux attach` bytes.

## Reproduction

1. Open any AO session terminal (or shell terminal) with more transcript than fits the pane.
2. Press and hold the left mouse button on a line of terminal text.
3. Drag the pointer above the top edge (or below the bottom edge) of the terminal and hold it there.
4. **Expected:** the pane auto-scrolls and the selection keeps extending.
   **Actual:** nothing scrolls. The highlight stops at the viewport edge.

Wheel scrolling in the same pane works, and click-drag selection inside the pane works.

## Root Cause

`XtermTerminal.tsx` routes the **wheel** away from xterm's local viewport for panes whose scrollback lives in the pane, but nothing does the equivalent for xterm's **selection drag**, so the drag falls through to a scroll path that is a no-op for every AO terminal.

**1. AO terminals are always alternate-screen + mouse-tracking panes.**

`tmux.Runtime.Attach` spawns `tmux -u -T RGB attach-session -t <id>` on a PTY with `TERM=xterm-256color` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:702-756`), and the session is created with `mouse on` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/commands.go:41`). Capturing that exact attach stream from a real PTY shows tmux immediately driving the client into the alternate screen with SGR mouse tracking on:

```
head: b'\x1b[?1049h\x1b[22;0;0t\x1b[?1h\x1b=\x1b[H\x1b[2J...'
  ALT SCREEN (smcup 1049h): YES
  mouse X11 1000h: YES
  mouse btn-event 1002h: YES
  SGR mouse 1006h: YES
```

Both the agent session terminal and the standalone shell terminals use this adapter (`backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:300` passes the same `runtimeAdapter` into `startShellTerminals`), so on macOS and Linux every AO terminal is an alt-buffer pane whose scrollback belongs to tmux, not to xterm.

**2. xterm's selection drag-scroll only moves xterm's own scrollback.**

`SelectionService._dragScroll()` (`@xterm/xterm@5.5.0` `src/browser/services/SelectionService.ts:665-690`) fires `onRequestScrollLines`, which `Terminal.ts:526` forwards to `Terminal.scrollLines(amount, suppressScrollEvent)` with the default `ScrollSource.TERMINAL`. That reaches `BufferService.scrollLines`, which begins:

```ts
if (disp < 0) {
  if (buffer.ydisp === 0) {
    return;                      // <-- alt buffer: ydisp is permanently 0
  }
  ...
}
buffer.ydisp = Math.max(Math.min(buffer.ydisp + disp, buffer.ybase), 0);
if (oldYdisp === buffer.ydisp) {
  return;                        // <-- alt buffer: ybase is permanently 0
}
```

In the alternate buffer `ybase === ydisp === 0` forever, so the drag-scroll is a guaranteed no-op. tmux never receives anything, because AO does not forward the drag to the PTY (`forceSelectionMode`, `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:260-268` — the same patch behind [#3640](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3640)).

**3. The wheel already solves this; the drag was never given the same route.**

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:763-805` (`attachCustomWheelEventHandler`) explicitly branches on pane kind: keyboard-scroll panes get `PageUp`/`PageDown`, normal-buffer panes with mouse tracking off get a local `term.scrollLines(lines)`, and mouse-tracking panes get SGR wheel reports that tmux acts on via copy-mode. That is exactly why "normal scrolling works". There is no matching branch anywhere for the selection drag, so it silently keeps using path (2).

### Reproduced in a real Chromium

A harness loading the shipped `@xterm/xterm@5.5.0` build, applying AO's `forceSelectionMode` patch, then synthesizing `mousedown` inside the screen box and `mousemove` 40px above it (held for 600ms, i.e. ~12 of xterm's 50ms drag-scroll ticks):

| case | buffer / mouse tracking | `viewportY` before → after | auto-scrolled |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — plain shell / codex | `normal`, tracking `none` | 377 → 245 | **YES** |
| B — `tmux attach` (every AO terminal on macOS/Linux) | `alternate`, tracking `drag` | 0 → 0 | **NO** |

Case B is set up with the exact sequence tmux sends on attach (`\x1b[?1049h`, `\x1b[?1000h`, `\x1b[?1002h`, `\x1b[?1006h`). Case A proves AO's `forceSelectionMode` patch, the hidden-scrollbar CSS (`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:1449-1464`) and `removeHiddenScrollbarReservation` do **not** break xterm's native drag-scroll — the failure is entirely the alt-buffer/mouse-tracking routing gap.

## Platform Impact

- **macOS / Linux:** always broken. The runtime adapter is tmux, so both agent session terminals and shell terminals are alt-buffer + mouse-tracking panes.
- **Windows:** the runtime adapter is conpty, not tmux (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty`). A plain shell pane there stays in the normal buffer with mouse tracking off, so xterm's native drag-scroll already works (case A). An agent TUI that enters the alternate screen itself, or that enables mouse tracking, hits the same bug.
- **Not Electron-specific.** The mechanism is pure xterm + buffer state and reproduces in stock Chromium outside Electron; no pointer-capture, drag-region or CSS involvement.

## Impact

- A terminal selection can never exceed one screen of text. Copying a full agent response, a long stack trace, or a multi-screen diff out of the terminal is impossible in one gesture.
- Workaround exists but is clumsy: wheel-scroll to the region first, then select only what is visible, repeat.

## Proposed Fix

Mirror the wheel handler for the selection drag in `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx`:

1. Extract the wheel handler's pane-kind decision into a single helper (`local` / `mouseReport` / `pageKeys`) so the two scroll paths cannot drift.
2. While a left-button selection drag is live and the pointer is outside the `.xterm-screen` box, emit the same bytes the wheel would emit for that many lines, on xterm's own 50ms drag-scroll cadence. Skip it entirely for `local` panes — xterm's native drag-scroll already handles those and emitting would double-scroll them.
3. Track the drag with capture-phase `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners: xterm's own document-level `mousemove` listener calls `stopImmediatePropagation()` while a drag is live (`SelectionService.ts:592-601`), which would drop a bubble-phase listener registered after it.

xterm keeps owning the selection model — its `_dragScroll` re-pins `selectionEnd` to the viewport edge on every tick — so the fix only has to supply the scroll the pane never received.

### Known limitation this does not remove

Over a tmux pane the selection still cannot accumulate *beyond one screen*: xterm's selection anchors are buffer rows, and tmux repaints the alternate screen in place, so scrolling changes the text under a fixed anchor rather than adding rows above it. After the fix the pane scrolls under a live drag and the highlight stays WYSIWYG with what is copied, which is as far as xterm-level selection can go while the scrollback lives in tmux. Genuinely unbounded selection needs the pane's native transcript — that is [#3791](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3791).

## Test Plan

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx`: a selection drag past the edge emits SGR wheel reports on a mouse-tracking pane; emits nothing (and does not double-scroll) on a normal-buffer pane; emits page keys on a keyboard-scroll pane; emits nothing while the pointer stays inside the screen box; stops on `mouseup`; direction follows above vs. below the box.
- Existing wheel tests must stay green unchanged — they pin the exact byte sequences the shared helper now produces.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`, `cd frontend && npm test`.
- Manual: drag-select past the top of a real tmux-backed AO terminal and confirm the pane scrolls; confirm ordinary click-selection, wheel scrolling, right-click menu, and typing are unaffected.

## Related

- [#3640](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3640) — `forceSelectionMode` suppresses mouse reporting to the PTY. Same `forceSelectionMode` patch (`XtermTerminal.tsx:260-268`) is what makes AO's local selection possible over a mouse-tracking pane in the first place, so any change there interacts with this.
- [#3791](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3791) — copy full prompt/response from agent TUIs by reading the native transcript. The proper long-term answer to "select more than one screen".
- [#1221](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1221) — terminal selection offset from the overlay scrollbar mismatch (same selection surface).
- [#1280](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1280) — viewport snapped to bottom on drag-start (closed; same drag-selection surface).

title: fix(session): do not apply a role override's model across harnesses
body:
## The bug

A project role override pins a harness and carries an agent config chosen **for that harness**. `effectiveHarness` already honors an explicit spawn harness, but `effectiveAgentConfig` applied the override's agent config unconditionally.

So in a project whose worker role pins `codex` with a codex model id, an explicit `claude-code` spawn inherited that model id and **launched broken**. Found while exercising two concurrent workers on different harnesses in one project.

## The fix

`Model` and `Mode` are applied only when the resolved harness matches the override's pinned harness. An override with no pinned harness keeps its apply-unconditionally behavior, so existing single-harness projects are unaffected.

Every caller now passes the harness actually resolved for that session — the explicit spawn harness, the durable `rec.Harness` on restore and interface transitions, and the target harness on an agent switch.

## Why `Permissions` stays outside the gate

`PermissionMode` is an abstract enum that each adapter maps onto its own agent's native approval flags, so it is not harness-specific. Skipping it on a mismatch would silently substitute the project baseline for the role's permission — and one direction of that substitution, a role pinning `default` over a baseline of `bypass-permissions`, is a **privilege escalation**.

## On the test

The fixture gives the worker override a permission that differs from the base. That detail is load-bearing: with it unset, every permission assertion passes trivially by reading the base value back, whether or not the override was applied at all.

Verified by reverting the function and confirming the test fails; `go build`, `go vet` and `go test ./internal/session_manager/...` (including `-race`) are clean.

title: feat(notifications): tell the user when a TUI worker finishes its turn
body:
## The gap

A TUI worker that finishes its task settles in `ActivityIdle` and **no notification fires**, so nothing tells the user the work is done.

## Why not just map end-of-turn to `waiting_input`

That looks like the one-line fix and it is wrong. `ActivityState.NeedsInput()` gates the automation layer:

- `lifecycle/reactions.go` suppresses `ready_to_merge` while it is true — a finished worker that just opened a PR would never raise `ready_to_merge` until the user messaged it again;
- `cannotNudge` suppresses automated nudges the same way.

Both `claudecode` and `codex` map end-of-turn to idle by documented decision. That stays untouched.

## What this adds

A distinct notification kind, `turn_complete`, emitted on the transition into idle. The predicate is deliberately narrow:

- **`prev` is enumerated** (`active` / `waiting_input` / `blocked`) rather than "not idle". `claudecode` maps *both* `stop` and `Notification(idle_prompt)` to idle, so `idle → idle` must not fire twice; `codex` reaches idle from `waiting_input` after a permission round-trip, which an active-only check would miss.
- **`Kind == worker` and `Mode == TUI`.** Chat sessions are also worker-kind, so gating on kind alone would fire on every chat exchange.
- the session is not terminated.

`turn_complete` needs resolution: resolved when the session leaves idle (the user gave it more work) or terminates, mirroring `needsInputResolutions` from all three lifecycle call sites, plus a reconcile query so a daemon crash between the two writes cannot strand one unresolved.

## Two surfaces worth a reviewer's attention

- The `type IN (...)` lists in `storage/sqlite/queries/notifications.sql` are a **hardcoded SQL mirror** of `NotificationType.NeedsResolution()`. Miss them and the notification is created but never appears in the unresolved list or count.
- `notify/enrich.go` rejects any non-`needs_input` intent without a PR URL, and its title/body switches fall through to a `"Notification"` default that still passes `NotificationRecord.Validate()` — so a missing case ships empty copy with a green suite.

## Renderer

Reuses the `needs_input` toast suppression, so no toast fires while the user is already watching that session, and the row routes to the session on click. Copy goes through `t()` with the English string added to every locale catalog, which is the existing pattern for untranslated keys.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test` and `-race` clean on the changed packages; renderer vitest 156 files / 2274 passed; `npm run api` re-run leaves the tree clean, so the committed `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are genuinely generated.

**Not yet observed in a live session** — this is test-verified only. The thing to watch on first real use is volume: `stop` maps to idle, so an interrupted turn notifies too, at one notification per turn. If the list proves noisy, the natural next step is to dedupe on an existing unresolved `turn_complete` for the session.

## Migration: 0107

This PR includes `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0107_notification_turn_complete.sql`. Adding the `turn_complete` type without widening the `notifications.type` CHECK constraint caused every insert of that type to fail with `CHECK constraint failed` — silently, because notification writes are best-effort by design (a failed notification must never fail the lifecycle write that produced it), so the error only surfaced as a warning log. This was found by live observation, not by tests; live-confirmed firing after the fix (one notification per completed turn).

SQLite cannot alter a CHECK in place, so 0107 uses the standard table-rebuild pattern: create `notifications_new` with the widened constraint, copy all rows, drop the old table, rename. The four indexes from migrations 0031/0041 are recreated verbatim (`DROP TABLE` takes them with it). The down migration deletes `turn_complete` rows first — they are advisory notifications, not durable state — before restoring the narrower constraint.

0107 claims version **107**, not the next free number at branch time, because upstream has since shipped 0104–0106 while this branch predates them; claiming 107 keeps the rebase onto `upstream/main` collision-free. The claim is registered in the append-only ledger in the same change, per `TestMigrationVersionLedger`.

title: bug(desktop): no text outside the terminal can be selected or copied — body { user-select: none } disables every content surface
body:
## Bug

Outside the terminal, no text in the desktop app can be selected or copied. Session details, status text, error messages, PR titles/numbers, branch names, timestamps, and activity-timeline copy are all inert to a mouse drag, so `Cmd/Ctrl+C` has nothing to copy.

**Analyzed against:** `85fab5e29ff718835a098e55ba598f0a2bc91e20` (origin/main) | **AO version:** `ao version dev` (desktop `0.10.3`)
**OS reproduced on:** macOS 26.6 (25G70), arm64 | **Daemon:** running on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Confidence:** High — exact rule, exact lines, exact introducing commit, reproduced with a computed-style read.

## Reproduction

1. `cd frontend && npm run dev:web` (or open the packaged desktop app) and load the board.
2. Open any session so the inspector rail is visible.
3. Drag the mouse across any inspector text — PR row, status, branch, timestamp.
4. No selection highlight appears. `Cmd/Ctrl+C` copies nothing. Right-click offers no Copy for that text.

Measured directly in the renderer (Playwright against `dev:web`):

```
BODY user-select: none
board-session-card user-select: none
```

Selection is available **only** in `input`, `textarea`, `[contenteditable]`, the xterm terminal (which owns its own selection model), and the two surfaces that have since opted back in by hand — the chat transcript and the GitHub review markdown body.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:1393-1394` sets selection off for the whole renderer:

```css
body {
	...
	-webkit-user-select: none;   /* line 1393 */
	user-select: none;           /* line 1394 */
}
```

`user-select` is inherited, so this disables selection on every descendant. The only re-enable is `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:1404-1409`:

```css
input,
textarea,
[contenteditable="true"] {
	-webkit-user-select: text;
	user-select: text;
}
```

Form fields are covered; **read-only content is not**.

Introduced by [PR #3508](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3508) (`b3dcd1eedc55fa53f5853a4c3774703f1299640e`, "fix: disable text selection on app chrome"). That PR's intent was narrow and legitimate — its description says "so sidebar/board chrome text isn't accidentally selectable" and its test plan only covers "sidebar project names / board column headers". The implementation applied that intent to `body`, so it also took out every content surface. Before #3508 the renderer had no `user-select` rule at all, i.e. content was selectable for the app's whole prior history.

### Collateral: a shipped feature is unreachable

The Files-tab diff selection menu (Copy / Explain / Make changes on a selected diff range) is gated entirely on a live DOM selection:

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFilesView.tsx:783-784` — `const selection = window.getSelection(); if (!isSelectionActiveIn(selection, container)) return;`
- The diff container at `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFilesView.tsx:824-827` carries no `select-text`, so it inherits `user-select: none`.

The user can never produce a selection inside that container, so the context menu never opens and `DiffSelectionMenu` is dead code in practice.

## Why a blanket `user-select: text` is the wrong fix

Chrome that the pointer acts on must stay unselectable, or a drag paints a selection instead of doing its job:

- **Board session cards** (`packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.tsx:440-441`) are a `<div onClick={onOpen}>`. A drag that ends inside the card still fires `click`, so making card text selectable turns "drag to select a title" into "open the session".
- **Titlebar / window drag strip** — `.window-titlebar` (`styles.css:2728-2729`) pairs `-webkit-app-region: drag` with its own `user-select: none`.
- **Sidebar and inspector topbar** — the chrome [PR #3508](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3508) was actually about; `.session-inspector__topbar` (`styles.css:3093`) already opts out on its own.
- **Browser tab rail** uses `@dnd-kit` sortable drag (`frontend/src/renderer/components/BrowserTabsRail.tsx:574`).

So the fix has to restore the selectable default **and** keep an explicit non-selectable list for controls and drag surfaces.

## Not affected

- **Terminal** — `@xterm/xterm/css/xterm.css:38-44` sets `.xterm { user-select: none }` itself and `user-select: text` on its accessibility tree, so xterm owns terminal selection regardless of the `body` value. Restoring the default cannot regress it.
- **Clipboard plumbing** — intact on every platform. macOS/Linux use the native Edit menu; Windows installs the equivalent role menu at `frontend/src/main/menu.ts:12-22` (`copy`, `selectAll`). `Cmd/Ctrl+C` already works; it simply has no selection to act on.
- **Resize drags** — `body.is-resizing-x { user-select: none }` (`styles.css:1889-1891`) already suppresses selection for the duration of a sidebar/inspector drag.

## Cross-platform

`user-select` is a Chromium CSS property with identical semantics on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and the rule is unconditional (no platform guard, no `isWindows()` branch). The bug and the fix are platform-independent. Verified on macOS; Windows/Linux need only a confirmation pass.

## Proposed fix

In `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`:

1. Make `body` selectable again (restores the pre-#3508 default).
2. Add an explicit non-selectable rule for interactive controls and drag surfaces, preserving [PR #3508](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3508)'s actual intent — the existing `cursor: pointer` selector list at `styles.css:1411-1424` is already the codebase's canonical "this is a control" set and can be mirrored.
3. Mark the board session card non-selectable so its click-to-open surface keeps working.

Net effect: readable content becomes selectable everywhere; chrome behaves exactly as it does today.

## Impact

- Users cannot copy error messages, session ids, branch names, or PR numbers out of the app — the exact strings needed to file a bug or paste into a terminal.
- The Files-tab diff selection menu is unreachable.
- Accessibility: users who select text to drive a screen reader or magnifier lose that affordance across the whole non-terminal UI.
- Workaround: none in-app.

## Related

- [PR #3508](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3508) — introduced the rule (app chrome).
- [PR #3520](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3520) — applied the same pattern to the marketing site (`frontend/src/landing/src/app/globals.css:11-30`), which additionally opts `.prose` back in. Marketing pages are out of scope here.
- [#4265](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4265) — terminal selection drag auto-scroll. Different subsystem (xterm owns its selection); tracked separately, no shared code with this fix.
- [#3929](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3929) — browser-panel markdown annotations selecting the whole wrapper; adjacent selection behavior in a different surface.

title: fix(session): escape inconclusive agent switch recovery
body:
## Summary

- close an inconclusive `stopping_source` switch as failed while preserving the source owner and runtime handle
- avoid unsafe teardown retries or source relaunches when the runtime adapter cannot prove liveness
- poll asynchronous source-recovery rows and prefer detailed switch history over a stale workspace projection in the dialog

## Independent triage

The durable boundary in `stopping_source` is earlier than target creation: AO cannot have created the target until the source-stopped transaction commits. A failed source liveness probe therefore does **not** make controller ownership ambiguous; the durable session row still owns the original source harness and handle.

Retrying `Destroy` or relaunching the source is unsafe. In particular, #3475 deliberately classifies tmux server-level failures as inconclusive because the provider process can outlive the tmux server. `Destroy` may also treat a missing server as an already-absent tmux session, which still cannot prove that an orphan provider exited. Relaunching at that point can create two controllers. The same ownership rule applies to ConPTY and other adapters.

The dead-end came from retaining a nonterminal switch gate after that probe error. The safe escape is to terminalize the switch without changing source ownership or guessing liveness. This reopens session operations (including termination/retry) and boot reconciliation automatically releases already-persisted rows after upgrade.

The recovery endpoint returns 202 before its worker settles. The UI previously stopped polling recovery rows, and the dialog only read the compact workspace snapshot, so it could keep rendering the old recovery prompt even after switch history changed. Source recovery rows now poll until terminal, and the dialog prefers the detailed history record for the same switch.

## Tests

- `cd backend && go test ./internal/session_manager -run 'Test(RecoverAgentSwitchReleasesSourceWhenProbeRemainsInconclusive|SwitchAgentMarksAndRecoversUnconfirmedSourceStop|ReconcileAgentSwitchesUsesDurableBoundaries)$' -count=1 -v`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/hooks/useAgentSwitches.test.ts src/renderer/components/SwitchAgentDialog.test.tsx src/renderer/components/TerminalSwitchAgentButton.test.tsx src/renderer/components/CenterPane.test.tsx src/renderer/components/chat/SessionChatSurface.test.tsx`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/session_manager -count=1`
- `git diff --check`

## Risk / intentional omission

This does not guess that an unreachable runtime is dead and does not force-kill or relaunch it. If the underlying adapter is still unavailable, the preserved source controller may remain disconnected, but the durable switch fence is released so the user can terminate or retry without risking a duplicate controller.

Closes #4258

title: feat(board): derive a display status per session
body:
Stacked on #4249 (Kanban column). Review that first; this PR targets its branch and only the last commit is mine.

## Summary
Session presentation is now derived in two explicit stages: pick the `kanbanColumn`, then derive a `displayStatus` **within** that column. Both ship on the session read model; the existing `status` is untouched.

The column answers *where in the lifecycle, and whose turn*. The display status answers *what is happening right now at that stage* — so the card can change from "Review scheduled" to "Reviewing" to "Addressing comments" without the card ever moving lane.

`DisplayStatus` values are phrases, not identifiers (`Fixing CI failures`, `Needs human review`, `Closed without merge`). The frontend prints the string; it keeps no mapping table of its own.

## Derivation

`contract.DeriveKanbanPresentation` replaces `DeriveKanbanColumn` as the entry point. Stage one is the reducer #4249 shipped, unchanged in behaviour except where noted below; stage two switches on the chosen column and reads only that column's facts:

| Column | Priority |
| --- | --- |
| **Building** | Working → Blocked → Exited → No signal → Awaiting PR |
| **Validating** | Blocked → Exited → Fixing CI failures / Checks failing → Addressing comments → Needs review → Review scheduled → Reviewing → Needs review (failed pass) → Review pending (cancelled pass) → Draft |
| **In review** | Checks failing → Changes requested → Needs human review |
| **Ready** | Merged → Closed without merge → Mergeable → Checks failing → Approved |
| **Archive** | Terminated |

Two places where the issue's list and the column reducer disagreed, resolved in favour of what the column actually guarantees:

- **A failed or cancelled pass leaves the head unreviewed.** The issue puts "Needs review (failed run)" and "Review pending (cancelled run)" in Validating, but #4249's `!ReviewRun.Present` rule handed such a head to a person as soon as *any* pass existed, so neither phrase was reachable. The column rule is now `!ReviewRun.Outcome` — a pass that produced no verdict does not end AO's validation cycle. New `Outcome` fact, set from `ReviewVerdict.Valid()`.
- **"Addressing comments" belongs to Validating, whichever side asked.** AO fixing *external* feedback is `aoOwnsNextStep`, so the column is already Validating; the In-review branch for it in the issue's list is unreachable by construction and is not implemented. Validating's rule covers AO-side and external changes requests alike.

Ready checks Merged/Closed before merge-readiness: a merged PR's stale `mergeability` must not report "Mergeable" over the merge that actually happened.

`KanbanSessionFacts` now embeds `SessionFacts` rather than re-declaring `IsTerminated`, so Building and Validating read the same worker facts `DeriveStatus` does — including the no-signal rule, extracted to `silentPastGrace` and shared by both reducers instead of written twice.

## Freshness

Review-run currency is enforced in SQL by #4249: `ListCurrentHeadReviewRunsBySession` joins on `target_sha = pr.head_sha`, so a pass recorded for an earlier commit never reaches the reducer, and `Review scheduled` / `Reviewing` / `Needs review` always describe the current head.

**CI needs no equivalent guard.** `pr.ci_state` and `pr.head_sha` are columns of a single `UpsertPR` statement written from one provider observation, and `ClaimPRForSession`'s upsert does not touch `ci_state` — so the stored aggregate cannot describe a commit other than the stored head. An earlier revision of this PR added a `ci_at_current_head` column to defend that case; it was removed as unreachable, and because it cost a correlated subquery per PR on the session-list read.

## Multiple PRs

Unchanged selection: per-PR column, ranked (ready > needs review > validating > building), ties on newest then URL. The display status then reads **the winning PR's** facts, so a merged PR cannot narrate a session whose other PR is still having its CI fixed.

## Frontend

`displayStatus` is plumbed through `useWorkspaceQuery` → `WorkspaceSession` → the board card, which prints it in place of the status badge's label. Precedence is `agent-switch presentation → displayStatus → status badge`: the switch overlay is a transient, more specific state and still wins. A daemon too old to send one falls back to the translated status label, as today.

**Known gap:** `displayStatus` arrives in English from the daemon, which is what the issue's phrase-valued API specifies; the eight renderer locales do not cover it. The fallback keeps older daemons translated, but a current daemon shows English phrases to every locale. Worth a follow-up before the Figma visual treatment lands — either a client-side phrase→key map or identifier values plus a label table.

## Tests
- `go test ./...` (backend, all packages), `golangci-lint run` (0 issues), `gofmt -l .` clean
- `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run src/renderer` in `frontend` (1921 passed); `npm test` in `packages/product-ui`
- New coverage: reducer table tests for every phrase in every column, terminated, multi-PR selection, and "a PR keeps the card out of Building"; column tests for the failed/cancelled-pass rule; a real-SQLite test for `ci_at_current_head` across no-checks / current-head / pushed-since cases; service tests for the derived phrase and for a stale CI aggregate; an API test asserting `displayStatus` on the wire; board and query tests for rendering and hydration.

## Issue
- Closes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4179

title: fix(terminal): auto-scroll the pane while a selection drag is held
body:
Fixes #4265

## Summary

Dragging a text selection past the top/bottom edge of an AO terminal did not auto-scroll the pane, so a selection could never grow past what was already on screen. Ordinary selection and ordinary wheel scrolling both worked.

xterm's built-in selection drag-scroll (`SelectionService._dragScroll`) fires `onRequestScrollLines` → `Terminal.scrollLines` → `BufferService.scrollLines`, which only moves lines xterm holds in its **own** scrollback:

```ts
if (disp < 0) { if (buffer.ydisp === 0) return; }
buffer.ydisp = Math.max(Math.min(buffer.ydisp + disp, buffer.ybase), 0);
if (oldYdisp === buffer.ydisp) return;
```

Every AO terminal on macOS/Linux is a `tmux attach-session` client (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:702`, and `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:300` gives shell terminals the same adapter). Capturing that attach stream from a real PTY shows tmux immediately driving the client into the alternate screen with SGR mouse tracking on:

```
b'\x1b[?1049h\x1b[22;0;0t\x1b[?1h\x1b=\x1b[H\x1b[2J...'
  ALT SCREEN (1049h): YES   mouse 1000h/1002h/1006h: YES
```

In the alternate buffer `ybase === ydisp === 0` forever, so `scrollLines` is a guaranteed no-op and the pane sits still under a live drag. tmux never hears about it either, because AO does not forward the drag to the PTY (`forceSelectionMode`, the patch behind #3640).

The **wheel** already solved exactly this: `attachCustomWheelEventHandler` branches on pane kind and reports to the pane rather than scrolling locally. That is why "normal scrolling works". The selection drag was simply never given the same route.

## What changed

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx`

- Extracted the wheel handler's pane-kind decision into `paneScrollMode()` (`local` / `mouseReport` / `pageKeys`) and its emission into `paneScrollReport()`, so both scroll gestures read one decision and cannot drift apart again. **Wheel behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged** — the existing wheel tests pin those bytes and pass untouched.
- A left-button selection drag held outside the `.xterm-screen` box now emits the same bytes the wheel would for that many lines, on xterm's own 50ms drag cadence.
  - `local` panes (codex, a plain shell, a Windows conpty shell) are **skipped** — xterm's built-in drag-scroll already moves their scrollback, so emitting would scroll them twice.
  - `pageKeys` panes get one page key every 8th tick; one per tick would be twenty screens a second.
  - Distance→speed curve mirrors xterm's own `DRAG_SCROLL_MAX_THRESHOLD`, with the speed cap at 3 instead of 15 because each line becomes a report the *pane* acts on and tmux copy-mode moves 5 lines per report. Measured against a real tmux PTY: 3 reports/tick ≈ 14 lines/tick, i.e. this lands back on xterm's native full-speed drag rate rather than 5× past it.
- Drag tracking uses **capture-phase** `mousemove`/`mouseup` on `window`: xterm's own document-level `mousemove` listener calls `stopImmediatePropagation()` for the whole duration of a drag, which would silently drop a bubble-phase listener.
- Teardown removes the `mousedown` listener and calls `stopSelectionDragScroll()`, so a terminal disposed mid-drag leaves no window listeners or interval behind.

xterm keeps owning the selection model — its `_dragScroll` re-pins `selectionEnd` to the viewport edge every tick — so this only supplies the scroll the pane never received.

## Verification

**Reproduced the bug in a real Chromium** against the shipped `@xterm/xterm@5.5.0` build with AO's `forceSelectionMode` patch applied, synthesizing a held drag 40px above the screen box for 600ms:

| case | buffer / mouse tracking | `viewportY` before → after | auto-scrolled |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — plain shell / codex | `normal`, tracking `none` | 377 → 245 | **YES** |
| B — `tmux attach` (every AO terminal on macOS/Linux) | `alternate`, tracking `drag` | 0 → 0 | **NO** |

Case A proves `forceSelectionMode`, the hidden-scrollbar CSS and `removeHiddenScrollbarReservation` do **not** break xterm's native drag-scroll — the failure was entirely the routing gap. Not Electron-specific.

**Verified the fix's output against a live tmux.** Writing exactly what the fix emits per tick (`\x1b[<64;1;1M` × 3) into a real `tmux attach` PTY, six ticks apart:

```
attached; visible markers: (478, 500)
after 6 drag ticks; markers repainted: (393, 491)
tmux pane_in_mode: 1   scroll_position: 85
```

The pane enters copy-mode and scrolls back 85 lines — the scroll the drag never used to produce.

**Tests** (`npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts`):
- `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` — 64 passed, 7 new: auto-scrolls a mouse-tracking pane on a held drag; correct direction above vs. below the box; keeps ticking while held and stops on `mouseup`; does **not** fire while the pointer stays inside the box; does **not** fire without a selection (click-and-hold never moves the pane); leaves `local` panes to xterm instead of double-scrolling; paces page keys for keyboard-scroll panes.
- `TerminalPane.test.tsx`, `ShellTerminalTab.test.tsx`, `useTerminalSession.test.tsx` — 98 passed, unchanged.
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` — clean on the implementation.

## Known limitation (not introduced here, not removed here)

Over a tmux pane the selection still cannot accumulate *beyond one screen*: xterm's selection anchors are buffer rows and tmux repaints the alternate screen in place, so scrolling changes the text under a fixed anchor rather than adding rows above it. After this change the pane scrolls under a live drag and the highlight stays WYSIWYG with what gets copied — as far as xterm-level selection can go while the scrollback lives in tmux. Genuinely unbounded selection needs the pane's native transcript: #3791.

## Risk / follow-ups

- The minimum drag speed is ~100 lines/s (1 report/tick × tmux's 5 lines) versus xterm's local 20 lines/s, because tmux's lines-per-wheel-report is not something this layer controls. Fine-grained control right at the edge is coarser than on a `local` pane; worth a tuning pass if it feels fast in practice.
- Windows (conpty) is untested on hardware. A plain conpty shell stays a `local` pane and is unaffected by this change; a conpty agent TUI that enables mouse tracking takes the new `mouseReport` path.

## Related

- #3640 — `forceSelectionMode` suppresses mouse reporting to the PTY. Same patch that makes local selection possible over a mouse-tracking pane, so changes there interact with this.
- #3791 — copy full prompt/response by reading the agent's native transcript.
- #1221 — terminal selection offset from the overlay scrollbar mismatch.
- Separate from the non-terminal UI text-selection issue being triaged in parallel; no shared code — that one is app-chrome CSS, this one is xterm scroll routing.

title: fix(desktop): restore text selection outside the terminal
body:
Fixes #4268

## Summary

`body { user-select: none }` — added by [PR #3508](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3508) to stop drags from painting a highlight over sidebar/board chrome — inherits into every descendant. Nothing outside `input`/`textarea`/`[contenteditable]` and the terminal could be selected or copied: session details, status text, error messages, PR metadata. It also left the Files-tab diff selection menu unreachable, since `SessionFilesView` gates that menu on a live DOM selection inside a container that had no `select-text`.

This restores the selectable default and moves #3508's intent into an explicit opt-out list for controls and drag surfaces, so chrome behaves exactly as it does today.

## Changes

- `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css` — drop `user-select: none` from `body`; add an opt-out for `button`, `summary`, `select`, `[role="button"]`, the `data-slot` control set, `[data-slot="resize-handle"]`, and the sidebar menu buttons.
- `packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.tsx` — `select-none` on **interactive** board cards only. The card is the click target and a drag ending inside it still fires `click`, so a drag-select there would open the session. Non-interactive (archive) cards stay selectable.
- `frontend/e2e/text-selection.spec.ts` — new.
- `packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.test.tsx` — card contract test.

`a[href]` is deliberately **not** in the opt-out: links sit inside prose (chat transcript, review markdown), and `user-select: none` on them punches holes in a copied paragraph.

## Deliberately unchanged

- **Terminal** — `xterm.css` sets `.xterm { user-select: none }` itself, so xterm owns terminal selection regardless of the `body` value.
- **Titlebar / drag regions** — `.window-titlebar` and `.session-inspector__topbar` already carry their own `user-select: none`.
- **Resize drags** — `body.is-resizing-x { user-select: none }` still suppresses selection for the duration of a drag.
- **Marketing site** — `frontend/src/landing/.../globals.css` keeps its own rule; out of scope.

One behavior change worth flagging: board **column headers** ("WORKING", counts) are now selectable. They are not interactive, so there is no conflict, but #3508's description mentioned them. Happy to add `select-none` there if reviewers prefer the old look.

## Verification

Run on macOS 26.6 (arm64) against `85fab5e29`.

- `frontend/e2e/text-selection.spec.ts` — **3 passed**. Drives real mouse drags and reads `window.getSelection()`:
  - inspector body copy selects and reaches the clipboard over the ordinary Copy shortcut
  - board card drag selects nothing and navigates nowhere
  - buttons, `[data-sidebar="menu-button"]`, and `[data-slot="resize-handle"]` compute `user-select: none`
  - `.xterm` still computes `user-select: none`
- **Non-vacuous check** — reverted `styles.css` to `origin/main` and reran: the content-selection case fails, the two chrome cases still pass. Restored and reran: all 3 pass.
- `packages/product-ui` — `SessionsBoardView.test.tsx` **7 passed**; `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `frontend` — `tsc --noEmit` clean; `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.e2e.json` clean.
- `SessionsBoard.test.tsx` **38 passed**, `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` + `SessionFilesView.test.tsx` pass (one archive-expansion timeout appeared only under a 3-file parallel run and reproduces on `origin/main` without this change; passes in isolation both with and without it).

## Gaps

- **Windows/Linux unverified.** `user-select` is platform-independent Chromium CSS and the rule has no platform guard, so no divergence is expected — but neither was exercised.
- Verified through the `dev:web` renderer harness, not a packaged Electron build. The `-webkit-app-region` drag strip is untouched by this diff, but a packaged smoke test would confirm the titlebar directly.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: `frontend/e2e/multi-pr.spec.ts` fails on `origin/main` — its "auth stack" fixture is gone from the mock dataset. Not touched here.

## Related

- [#4265](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4265) — terminal selection drag auto-scroll. Separate subsystem (xterm owns its selection); no shared code with this change.

title: feat: allow 120-character session display names with a sliding sidebar label
body:
## What

Session display names were capped at 20 characters — too short to distinguish two sessions working in the same area. This raises the cap to **120** and gives the sidebar a way to actually show a name that long.

Session IDs and prefixes are untouched; this is display names only.

## Backend / API

- **`domain.MaxSessionDisplayNameLen` (120) + `SessionDisplayNameTooLong`** are the single authority. Every boundary counts **runes**, not bytes, so accented/CJK/emoji labels are not cut short by a byte budget.
- **Session service** enforces it on both `Spawn` and `Rename`, so the service is authoritative regardless of transport. `Rename` previously had **no length check at all** — a `PATCH` was the one way to put an unbounded label on a session.
- **HTTP**: spawn and rename handlers both return `DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`, with the message derived from the constant so it cannot go stale.
- **DTO / OpenAPI**: `SpawnSessionRequest.displayName` and `RenameSessionRequest.displayName` are `maxLength: 120`. `npm run api` regenerated `openapi.yaml`; `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` is unchanged (openapi-typescript does not emit `maxLength`).
- **CLI**: `ao spawn --name` and `ao session rename` both reject an oversized label as a usage error (exit 2) before contacting the daemon; help text derives the number from the constant.
- **Agent-facing guidance** (orchestrator prompt, spawn directive, task-title delegation message, `using-ao` skill docs) quotes the cap from the constant.
- `delegatedTaskTitleLimit` stays at **20** on purpose: it is the provisional label cut from a raw brief while the orchestrator picks a real title, and a blind slice of prose reads worse the longer it runs. Commented as such.

Project display names are unrelated and stay at 20.

## Sidebar

- Session names render **in full, clipped rather than ellipsised** — the distinguishing part of a session name is usually its tail.
- **When and only when the name overflows**, hovering the row or focusing its open button slides the text far enough to read the tail, then eases back. Constant travel speed (~100px/s, about reading pace) with a dwell at each end, so a name two characters too wide doesn't crawl and a long one doesn't whip past.
- **Reserved action area, no layout shift.** The pin/rename/kill cluster moved out of flow into reserved padding (`--size-sidebar-session-actions`). It used to grow from zero width on hover, which resized the label track at exactly the moment the label starts moving. Now only opacity changes, and the cluster sits above the moving text (`z-chrome`). Hidden means `pointer-events-none`, so a tap on the row's right edge can't hit an invisible Kill button.
- **Theme-aware edge fade** via a CSS `mask-image`, not a background-coloured gradient. A gradient would have to name a colour, and the row sits on three backgrounds (rest / hover / active) across two themes; the mask fades whatever is actually painted, so nothing is hard-coded.
- **Pauses and resets cleanly** — leaving mid-travel transitions back to rest rather than snapping.
- **Accessible name / tooltip**: the full name is always the row's `title` and its text content.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`**: never animates, in both the component and a CSS backstop. The non-animated readable fallback is the tooltip plus the full accessible name.

## Verification

**Backend** — `go build ./...` and `go vet` clean.
`go test` green for `internal/domain`, `internal/cli`, `internal/httpd/controllers`, `internal/service/session`, `internal/session_manager`, `internal/skillassets`.
(Three `TestSwitchAgent*` tests in `internal/session_manager` fail intermittently under load on this machine — verified they fail identically on the unmodified tree, so pre-existing, not from this change.)

**Frontend** — `npm run typecheck` clean. `Sidebar.test.tsx` 63/63 and `SidebarSessionName.test.tsx` 8/8 pass. A full-suite run showed failures only in files this PR does not touch (e.g. `ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx`), consistent with load-related flakiness in a parallel run.

**Not done:** visual `ao preview` / `ao browser` verification was skipped at the requester's instruction. The marquee's motion has not been eyeballed in the running app.

## Tests added

- `domain`: rune-boundary table (ASCII / 2-byte / 4-byte, at cap and one over).
- `service/session`: spawn and rename cap, trim-before-measure, rejected rename leaves the stored name untouched.
- `httpd/controllers`: spawn and rename each accept exactly-at-cap (multi-byte) and reject one over.
- `cli`: spawn and rename usage errors, and at-cap names forwarded unchanged.
- frontend: overflow detection (including sub-pixel), hover trigger, focus trigger, clean reset, reduced-motion fallback, no-reflow/reserved-strip assertions, constant-speed duration scaling.

## Scope note

Overlaps sidebar DnD and agent-icon work in other sessions — kept independently scoped to the session row's label and action cluster.

title: fix(events): stop a large replay from aborting the mobile app, and clamp future cursors to head
body:
Two commits. The first is the production fix that has shipped; the second is a small daemon-side hardening of the same failure mode.

---

## 1. `fix(mobile)`: stop a large event replay from aborting the app

### Problem

On a fresh install the conversation cursor starts at zero, so connecting asks the daemon for every event it has ever recorded. Against a real 80-session daemon that is **196,658 events / 47MB**, still streaming after 6 seconds.

Read through `expo/fetch`, each chunk emits an event to JS and takes a **JNI global reference** released only once JS consumes it. The reader awaited only already-buffered reads — those stay in the microtask queue — so it never yielded, JS never drained, references accumulated, and the runtime aborted the process on hitting the 51,200 table limit:

```
JNI ERROR (app bug): global reference table overflow (max=51200)
    50472 of java.lang.Object[] (1 elements)
  at expo.modules.fetch.NativeResponse.pumpResponseBodyStream(NativeResponse.kt:199)
Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT)
```

Android reports this as `reason=5 (APP CRASH(NATIVE))` with no dialog, so it presents as the app silently vanishing a few seconds after connecting. Scrolling still worked while it was wedged — that is handled natively — but taps did not, because those need the JS thread.

### Fix

- **Yield a macrotask every 256 frames** inside the frame loop, so consumption keeps up and references are released. One chunk can carry thousands of events, so yielding per chunk is not enough.
- **Persist the cursor by event count** instead of a 500ms debounce. The debounce is a macrotask, so during exactly the drain where progress matters it never ran — every launch restarted from zero.
- **Skip parsing payloads while nothing is subscribed.** Only the chat screen currently open subscribes; during a cold replay none is, so ~196k `JSON.parse` calls were pure waste.

### Verification

- 459 tests, typecheck clean.
- `yields to the event loop while draining a large replay` fails on the pre-fix code — it reproduces the starvation in a unit test and now guards it.
- **On device** (Galaxy M31s, release build, `pm clear` before each run) against the 80-session daemon: baseline aborts at 50,472 references; this build drains cleanly and stays responsive. Relaunch is instant, confirming the cursor persists so catch-up happens once per install.
- **iOS** verified via a fresh TestFlight install against the same daemon — no hang. The JNI ceiling is Android-only, but the JS-thread starvation was not.

---

## 2. `fix(events)`: clamp a future cursor to head instead of replaying from zero

A cursor ahead of head means the `change_log` was truncated or replaced. The stream reset such a client to `0`, which costs it the entire backlog — and because every connected client is reset in the same moment, they stampede together.

It now falls back to head. The gap is recovered from the next snapshot fetch, so the cost is one refetch rather than a full replay.

The existing test asserted the reset-to-zero behaviour; it now asserts the clamp, and additionally that no event at or before head is replayed. `go test ./...` and `go test -race` pass.

---

## Known limitation

Together these make the replay **survivable and one-time — they do not make it smaller**. 47MB still crosses the network on a fresh install, and `pumpResponseBodyStream` has no backpressure.

The real fix is not replaying history at all: the client already loads history through paginated REST snapshots, and the sole stream consumer discards the payload and just refetches. A follow-up covers `from=head`, `maxCatchup`, and replacing the overflow-cancel-then-replay path with a resync signal — deliberately deferred, since the crash is resolved.

title: bug(cli): project set-config silently drops the reviewers config field
body:
## Summary

`ao project set-config --config-json` silently drops the `reviewers` field. The command returns `status: ok` and prints the project back, so the write looks like it succeeded, but the reviewer config is never persisted. `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/config` with the identical body persists it correctly, so this looks like the CLI (or its request struct) not carrying the field through to the daemon.

This is quiet in a way that matters: `reviewers` is what pins cross-family review (Claude reviewing Codex PRs). If it silently goes missing, the review loop just doesn't happen and nothing says so.

## Repro

```bash
ao project set-config work --config-json '{"reviewers":[{"harness":"claude-code"}],"sessionPrefix":"work"}' --json
```

Response (abridged) — no `reviewers`:

```json
{ "project": { "id": "work", "config": {
    "sessionPrefix": "work",
    "agentConfig": {}, "worker": { "agentConfig": {} },
    "orchestrator": { "agentConfig": {} }, "trackerIntake": {} } } }
```

Store confirms it:

```bash
sqlite3 ~/.ao/data/ao.db "select json_extract(config,'\$.reviewers') from projects where id='work';"
# (empty)
```

Same payload through the daemon API persists fine:

```bash
curl -s -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/projects/work/config \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"config":{"reviewers":[{"harness":"claude-code"}],"sessionPrefix":"work"}}'
# -> config.reviewers = [{"harness":"claude-code"}], and it is in ao.db
```

## Expected

Either the field round-trips like every other `ProjectConfig` field, or the CLI rejects it with an explicit error. Silently accepting and discarding is the worst of the three.

## Notes

- `reviewers` is present in `ProjectConfig` in the OpenAPI schema (`items: DomainReviewerConfig`), so this reads as a CLI gap rather than an intentional API-only field.
- `ao project set-config` also has no flag for reviewers, so `--config-json` is the only CLI route to set it today. A `--reviewer` flag would be a natural fix alongside.
- Version: 0.12.6 (bundled daemon reports `ao version` = `dev`), macOS 15 arm64.

title: bug(orchestrator): stale claude-CLI session-id lock survives OOM crash — kill+restore loops on "Session ID ... is already in use"
body:
## Summary

After a hard machine crash (kernel OOM-reboot), an orchestrator session whose
`--session-id`/`--resume` UUID was in flight at the time of the crash can end up
permanently unrecoverable through the normal CLI path. The tmux pane shows:

```
Error: Session ID <uuid> is already in use.
```

`claude` never starts (no process, bare keep-alive shell in the pane), and AO
reports the session as `status: exited`, `activity: exited`, `terminated: false`.

## Root cause (as far as I could trace it)

This message is **not** produced by AO — I grepped the whole `backend/` tree for
`"already in use"` and found only an unrelated preview-server port message. The
string is emitted by the `claude` (Claude Code) CLI itself when it refuses to
start with a `--session-id`/`--resume` value it considers already claimed.

The lock/claim state that causes this rejection does not appear to be file-based
in any location AO manages (no `.lock` next to the session's transcript
`.jsonl`, `lsof` on the transcript showed only AO's own daemon holding a read
fd, not `claude`). So it looks like the claim lives somewhere inside the
`claude` CLI's own state, and it survived the OOM crash even though the
`claude` process itself did not.

## Why AO's existing recovery path doesn't fix it

- `ao session kill <id>` succeeds and flips the session to `terminated: true`.
- `ao session restore <id>` re-launches the *same* session, which reuses the
  *same* `--session-id`/`--resume` UUID — so it hits the identical
  `already in use` rejection again. Kill+restore is not a fix here, it's a
  no-op loop.
- The only way I found to actually recover was to kill the session for good and
  spawn a **brand-new** orchestrator session (`ao spawn --kind orchestrator ...`),
  which allocates a fresh UUID and starts cleanly — at the cost of losing the
  old session's AO session id / transcript continuity from the harness's point
  of view.

## Steps to reproduce (best effort — trigger is a real OOM crash, hard to script)

1. Have AO running an orchestrator session for a project, so its
   `claude --session-id <uuid> --resume <uuid>` is live.
2. Force an abrupt kill of the whole `claude` process tree without a clean
   shutdown (the real-world trigger here was a kernel OOM-reboot of the whole
   machine, which is hard to reproduce deterministically; a `kill -9` on the
   `claude` process while it's mid-turn may reproduce the same claimed-but-dead
   lock state — untested).
3. Let AO's daemon boot-time reconciliation (`RestoreAll`) bring the session
   back.
4. Observe the pane: `Error: Session ID <uuid> is already in use.`
5. `ao session get <id>` → `status: exited`, `activity: exited`,
   `terminated: false`.
6. `ao session kill <id>` → succeeds, `terminated: true`.
7. `ao session restore <id>` → relaunches with the *same* uuid → identical
   error again.

## Expected behavior

- AO's restore path should detect this specific harness-level rejection (or at
  least detect that `claude` exited immediately without ever attaching to the
  pane) and not leave the session stuck in a `kill`+`restore`-loops-forever
  state.
- Ideally, `ao session restore` (or an automatic retry inside `RestoreAll`)
  would fall back to minting a fresh native session id when the harness refuses
  to resume the old one, rather than requiring the operator to manually kill
  the session and spawn an entirely new one to recover.

## Environment

- macOS, AO self-built daemon + Electron app
- harness: `claude-code`, role: `orchestrator`, mode: `tui`
- Trigger: kernel OOM-reboot of the whole machine (not a graceful `ao stop` /
  daemon kill)

## Possibly related

- #3875 — similar unrecoverable `exited`/`terminated:false` orchestrator state
  after a fresh spawn, but with a *different* error text (`invalid session id`,
  not `already in use`) and a different traced root cause (project-id/session-id
  regex mismatch for ids containing dots). That root cause doesn't apply here —
  my project id has no dots. I searched the tracker for the exact string
  `Session ID ... is already in use` and found no existing issue, so filing
  this as a distinct symptom.
- #2702 — restore recreates the tmux session but never relaunches the agent
  after a daemon/tmux restart. Related class of problem (stale runtime state
  surviving a crash) but that issue's pane is a bare idle shell with no error
  message at all, whereas this one has `claude` actively refusing to start with
  an explicit error.

title: Update feedback can remain loading and hide automatic progress
body:
## Bug

Desktop update feedback is misleading in two related situations:

1. A manual **Check for updates** can remain in its loading state after the main process has already published a terminal result. Navigating away and returning remounts the view and reveals the completed result.
2. Automatic checks and downloads produce no sidebar feedback until the update is fully downloaded, making a working automatic update look inactive and leaving users unsure whether they must update manually.

**Source:** Local Codex report with screenshots and a follow-up report from Prateek; no public chat URL  
**Observed:** macOS, AO `0.12.7-nightly.202608221348`  
**Analyzed against:** `858146266`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** Medium — update behavior is degraded, with manual checking as a workaround.

## Reproduction

### Stuck manual loading

1. Open Settings → Updates.
2. Click **Check for updates**.
3. Let the updater publish a matching terminal status such as `not-available` while the IPC invocation remains unsettled.
4. The button and status panel remain in the checking state.
5. Navigate away and return; the completed status appears.

### Missing automatic progress

1. Seed or receive updater status `{ state: "available" }` or `{ state: "downloading" }`.
2. Observe the sidebar footer.
3. No update information is rendered until status becomes `downloaded`, at which point the existing **Restart to update** button appears.

## Root Cause

- `UpdatesSection` owns a renderer-local pending flag whose lifetime is coupled to the IPC promise rather than the updater status event. Electron can publish the terminal event before the invocation settles, so completed state is masked by stale local loading state.
- `Sidebar` explicitly renders its update row only for `status.state === "downloaded"`; `available` and `downloading` return `null`.

## Fix

- Correlate manual update checks with request IDs and clear local pending state when a matching non-checking status arrives, even if the IPC promise remains pending.
- Show informational, non-clickable sidebar states for available updates and download progress; preserve the existing restart/install button only for a staged download.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/main/auto-updater.test.ts`
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`

## Related

- [#2377](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2377) — original downloaded-only restart-row specification.
- [PR #4144](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4144) — update feedback redesign that introduced the renderer-local pending state.
- [#3526](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3526) — automatic updater failures can remain silent; recovery visibility is related but outside this fix.

title: Use review agent hooks to update review status
chore(mobile): upgrade Expo SDK 54 to 57
body:
Moves the mobile app from Expo SDK 54 to 57 — React Native 0.81.5 → 0.86.2, React 19.1.0 → 19.2.3.

SDK 55 and 56 are skipped deliberately. Both carry a Hermes V1 memory regression that inflates memory usage when `react-native-worklets` or `reanimated` is imported; it is fixed in `expo@57.0.9`, and this lands on 57.0.15.

Rebased onto `main` after #4276 merged, so this is a single commit touching only `packages/mobile`.

### Breaking changes the new SDKs required

- **`StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject` was removed.** `absoluteFill` replaces it and has the identical object shape, so the existing spreads behave the same.
- **SDK 56+ forbids importing `@react-navigation/*` directly.** `useTabScrollToTop` now takes `useScrollToTop` from `expo-router/react-navigation`, the supported re-export. Runtime behaviour is unchanged.
- **`splash` is no longer valid at the `app.json` root** and moves into the `expo-splash-screen` plugin. `expo-font` is added because `@expo/vector-icons` requires it as a native peer — expo-doctor flags its absence as a crash risk outside Expo Go.
- **`useColorScheme()` is no longer nullable** and can return `"unspecified"`, so `resolveScheme` accepts it. It falls through to dark exactly as `null` did.

### Other changes

**`expo-speech-recognition` 3.1.3 → 56.0.1.** Worth a look. It is third-party, so `expo install --fix` does not touch it, and its SDK 54 build fails to compile against the new `expo-modules-core` (`promise.resolver` became `legacyResolveBlock(for:)`). Note `56.0.1` is the **SDK 56** release — upstream has not tagged one for SDK 57 (last publish 2026-06-05). Voice input works, but is a version behind by necessity.

**`tsconfig.json` gains an explicit `types` entry.** The Node types the vitest suites rely on used to arrive transitively and no longer do. `"react"` is listed alongside `"node"` because setting `types` at all disables automatic `@types` inclusion.

**`metro.config.js` is deliberately untouched.** The upgrade guide suggests deleting a Metro config that only holds Expo defaults; this one pins `react` and `react-native` to a single copy, and removing it reintroduces the "main has not been registered" launch crash.

**TypeScript 5.9 → 6.0.3** came in via `expo install --fix` as the SDK-aligned version. Everything typechecks on it. Happy to pin back to 5.9 if reviewers would rather not couple a TS major to this.

### Verification

- `expo-doctor` 21/21
- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 475 tests across 56 files passing
- Native iOS build installs and renders on an iOS 26.5 simulator
- Native Android build installs and renders on an Android 15 emulator

The native builds were the only thing that caught the `expo-speech-recognition` breakage — doctor, typecheck, tests, and `expo export` all passed while the iOS build was failing. Worth keeping in mind that CI has no mobile target, so none of the above runs automatically.

### Not yet verified on real devices

Hand-testing so far has been on a simulator and an emulator. Still outstanding:

- **Terminal** — `@fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview` pins React `19.1.0` exactly and we now ship `19.2.3` (installs via the existing `legacy-peer-deps`). Most likely place for a runtime surprise.
- **Chat streaming** — `expo/fetch` and Hermes both changed under the JNI fix from #4276; needs a large Android event replay to exercise properly.
- **Voice input** — see the `expo-speech-recognition` note above.
- **Upgrade-over-install** — `expo-secure-store`, `async-storage`, and `expo-file-system` all jumped major native versions. A fresh install will not reveal migration problems; installing over an existing SDK 54 build is the only way to confirm users stay paired and signed in.

### Follow-ups, not in this PR

- `expo-system-ui` is absent, so `ios.backgroundColor` and `userInterfaceStyle` in `app.json` are silently no-ops. **Pre-existing** — it was missing on SDK 54 too — but worth fixing separately.
- Deprecations left alone: `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` → `expo-sqlite/localStorage`, `@expo/vector-icons` → `expo-symbols`, and enabling React Compiler.

title: bug(desktop): OpenCode terminal drag-select appears to continue into the inspector
body:
﻿## Bug

Click-dragging to select text in an **opencode** worker terminal appears to continue across the terminal's right edge into the session inspector (task list / worktree path).

**Source:** in-session report | **AO version:** v0.12.3 | **OS:** Fedora 43 | **Surface:** Terminal UI, opencode worker
**Analyzed against:** `b48c98c94ca0039ad1bc42bd1b78134d3ff5773d` (tag `v0.12.3`) and `01b4cd61dd4f6d95a86872b20cc560fb2b1f857f` (local #4191 toast branch)
**Confidence:** Medium — traced the mouse/selection path in xterm and AO; not reproduced on Fedora in this checkout.

## Reproduction

1. Open an opencode worker in **Terminal** mode with the right inspector visible.
2. Click-drag to select TUI text, and keep dragging toward the inspector.
3. **Actual:** the highlight looks like it crosses the terminal boundary onto inspector text (task list / worktree path).
4. **Expected:** selection stays inside the terminal (xterm cell highlight only).

Please also answer: when you paste, does the clipboard contain inspector/sidebar strings, or only terminal cells? That distinguishes a visual/TUI-cell effect from native DOM selection.

## Root Cause

This is **not** a clipboard-writer bug and **not** a regression from [#4191](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4191) / [PR #4240](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4240). v0.12.3 already auto-copies via `term.getSelection()`; #4191 only added the toast after a successful write.

Two paths were checked:

**1. Native DOM selection spanning terminal + inspector — ruled out for a drag that starts on `.xterm`.**

- `body { user-select: none }` (`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`) and `.xterm { user-select: none }` (`@xterm/xterm/css/xterm.css`).
- xterm `bindMouse` **always** `preventDefault()`s `mousedown` on `.xterm` *before* mouse-tracking / `shouldForceSelection` (`node_modules/@xterm/xterm/src/browser/Terminal.ts`). A cancelled mousedown must not start a native text selection.
- AO auto-copy writes only `term.getSelection()` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx` `copySelection()`), never `window.getSelection()`.
- Adjacent [#4268](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4268) is the opposite symptom: inspector chrome is *not* selectable because of the body rule.

**2. xterm cell selection clamped to the last column — the remaining explanation.**

- `getCoords()` clamps pointer X/Y to the terminal grid (`@xterm/xterm/src/browser/input/Mouse.ts`). A drag toward the inspector still ends at `cols` / `cols+1`, i.e. the rightmost TUI cells.
- OpenCode (and similar TUIs) paint todos / paths in those columns. The inspector is flush with that edge (`SessionView.tsx` `#terminal` vs `[data-slot="inspector-container"]`).
- `forceSelectionMode()` (`XtermTerminal.tsx`) patches `shouldForceSelection = () => true` so drag-select works while OpenCode has DEC mouse tracking on. OpenCode `CSI ? 1002 h` / `1006 h` later calls `selectionService.disable()` and restores `enable-mouse-events`. The `shouldForceSelection` patch **survives** `disable()`; `mousedown` is still cancelled. That hole does **not** enable native inspector selection.

## Fix

Do not change `copySelection()` / the copy toast unless paste is shown to include inspector strings.

If this is OpenCode TUI chrome being selected as cells, it is expected xterm behavior (same as any terminal). If testers still see a native Chromium highlight on inspector DOM after a drag that started in the terminal, treat that as a browser/`preventDefault` exception and gather a screenshot + paste sample.

No code change proposed until that paste/screenshot check.

## Impact

- Users think AO is selecting the inspector when selecting in OpenCode.
- Auto-copied clipboard should still be terminal cells only; if it is not, this needs reopening as a native-selection bug.

## Related

- [#4191](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4191) / [PR #4240](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4240) — copy toast; same terminal, not this mechanism, not in v0.12.3.
- [#4268](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4268) — inspector text cannot be selected (`user-select: none`); opposite of native spill.
- [#4265](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4265) — selection drag does not auto-scroll alt-buffer panes; related `forceSelectionMode` / mouse-tracking, different symptom.
- [#3640](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3640) — `forceSelectionMode` suppresses mouse reports to the PTY.

title: Update card makes automatic downloads look manual and gives no download-start feedback
body:
## Bug

Settings → Updates presents an automatically discovered update as a required manual action. With long nightly version identifiers, the status column collapses while the full version is repeated in a large button. Clicking that button invokes the updater but does not immediately change, disable, or acknowledge the action, so a working download looks inert.

**Source:** Local Codex report with two screenshots and direct follow-up
**Observed:** macOS, AO v0.12.7-nightly.202608221348, Nightly channel, Automatic Updates enabled
**Analyzed against:** d9cf79178
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** Medium — updates work, but the UI makes them appear broken and invites duplicate clicks.

## Reproduction

1. Enable Automatic Updates and select Nightly.
2. Surface an available update with a long nightly identifier, for example v0.12.7-nightly.202608231350.
3. Open Settings → Updates at the shipped 920px dialog width.
4. Observe that the card still asks for a manual Update action and repeats the full version in that button.
5. Click the update action while updater startup/download remains pending.
6. Observe that the button stays enabled with unchanged copy until a later updater progress event.

## Evidence

A deterministic renderer reproduction at the real 678px card width measured:

- status content width: 113px
- action group width: 453px
- headline: 4 lines
- current version metadata: 3 lines

The click path was also reproduced with a pending updates:download invocation: the bridge was called, but the button stayed enabled and its label did not change.

On the reported machine, the updater cache contained the complete 166,801,038-byte target nightly archive and ShipIt had recorded install requests while waiting for app exit. That confirms the click was not ignored by the updater; the missing part was visible feedback and an explanation of automatic behavior.

Matched before/after screenshots and red/green test output will be attached to the fix PR.

## Root cause

- UpdatesSection.tsx uses the viewport sm breakpoint inside a fixed-width settings card. At this viewport the card is only about 678px wide, but the breakpoint forces status and actions into one row.
- The actions are shrink-0 and contain both the full nightly version and a fixed-width check button, so they take about two thirds of the card.
- The component receives update status but not the Automatic Updates setting, so it cannot distinguish an automatic background download from a manual-only path.
- The download action invokes IPC directly without renderer-local pending state, unlike the manual check flow.

## Expected fix

- Give status content its own row so layout is driven by card width rather than viewport width.
- For automatically discovered updates, explain that download happens in the background and omit redundant manual actions.
- Keep a compact Download now action for manual-only/request-owned updates.
- Optimistically expose downloading state and prevent repeat clicks as soon as that manual action is pressed.
- Add unit coverage for pending download feedback and renderer geometry coverage using the exact long nightly versions.

## Related

- [#3938](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3938) — manual update checks also lacked immediate renderer-owned feedback.
- [#4284](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4284) — request correlation and automatic progress visibility.
- [PR #4144](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4144) — introduced the compact one-row update card.

title: fix(frontend): clarify automatic update feedback
body:
Fixes #4291

## Summary

- let updater status own the card width instead of compressing it beside fixed-width actions
- explain that automatically discovered updates download in the background and remove redundant update/check actions from that state
- keep a compact `Download now` escape hatch for manual/request-owned updates
- show `Downloading… 0%` and disable repeat clicks immediately while a manual download invocation is pending
- add exact nightly-version geometry coverage and extend the renderer bridge fixture for updater state

## Root cause

The fixed 920px Settings dialog leaves a 678px update card, but the card used the viewport `sm` breakpoint to force status and actions into one row. The shrink-proof action group repeated the full nightly version and occupied 453px, leaving only 113px for status copy. Separately, the download button called IPC directly without renderer-local pending state, and the card did not receive the Automatic Updates setting, so it presented an automatic background operation as a required manual step.

## Reproduction evidence

The deterministic renderer reproduction uses the reported versions and the shipped 678px card width. On the pre-fix UI it failed with a four-line headline, three-line current version, 113px status column, and 453px action group.

![Before: reproduced compressed update card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/1c5ef5a2ef734f31fc10c0f9a03c060d4ee13112/update-settings-before.png)

A pending `updates:download` unit reproduction also confirmed that IPC was called while the button remained enabled with unchanged copy. On the reported installed app, the complete 166,801,038-byte target nightly archive was already staged and ShipIt was waiting for app exit, so the updater was working while the UI appeared inert.

## Fix evidence

The same renderer fixture now gives status 584px, keeps both long version strings to one line, explains the automatic background download, and presents no redundant action.

![After: readable automatic-update state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/1c5ef5a2ef734f31fc10c0f9a03c060d4ee13112/update-settings-after.png)

The manual/request-owned path remains available as `Download now`; its pending-state test asserts the button is immediately disabled and both button/status copy change to `Downloading… 0%` before updater progress arrives.

## Native Electron verification

The branch was also launched in the actual Electron app in isolated mode with the real preload bridge and daemon. Settings → Updates rendered at 678px, the daemon reported ready on `127.0.0.1:3002`, and Check for updates returned the expected unpackaged-app status.

![Native Electron Settings verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/1c5ef5a2ef734f31fc10c0f9a03c060d4ee13112/update-settings-native.png)

Electron disables release feeds in unpackaged builds, so the exact available-nightly state is covered by the deterministic renderer fixture; the native run verifies the real settings route, preload, daemon, and card structure.

## Tests

- `cd frontend && npm test` — 209 files passed; 2,748 tests passed, 1 skipped
- `cd frontend && npm test -- GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx` — 30 passed
- `cd frontend && npx playwright test e2e/update-settings-ux.spec.ts --reporter=line` — passed
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — passed
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck:e2e` — passed
- `cd frontend && npm test -- src/renderer/i18n/instance.test.ts` — 12 passed

title: fix(desktop): bundle tmux on macOS and Linux
body:
## Summary
- build tmux 3.5a plus pinned, checksum-verified static libevent/ncurses/utf8proc dependencies during macOS and Linux desktop packaging
- ship the result as `resources/tmux/bin/tmux` and fail packaging if that resource is absent or reports the wrong version
- force packaged desktop daemons to use the bundled binary via `AO_TMUX_BINARY`, with an AO-owned tmux socket so they cannot attach to the machine tmux server
- centralize configured/bundled/system tmux resolution and use it in the runtime, session spawn gate, startup system check, and `ao doctor`
- keep standalone/development daemon behavior backward compatible and cover binary/socket selection with tests

Verified the original gap and rebased this change onto current `upstream/main` (`1880498c8`). This supersedes the bundled-resolution intent of #4164 while also implementing the in-repo macOS/Linux packaging and socket isolation that PR defers elsewhere.

## Verification
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID -u AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY -u AO_PROJECT_ID TMUX_TMPDIR=/tmp/ao-tmux-lint-247 npm run lint`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/tmuxbin ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux ./internal/session_manager ./internal/service/systemcheck ./internal/cli`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run forge.config.test.ts src/shared/bundled-tmux.test.ts src/shared/shell-env.test.ts`
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`
- `cd frontend && npm run build:tmux`
- macOS arm64 linkage check: only `/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib` and `/usr/lib/libresolv.9.dylib`
- packaged the Electron app with Node 22 and smoke-tested the packaged tmux against an empty environment/PATH

## Risk
Linux and macOS Intel native builds are performed on their matching release runners; the package hook now makes either build fail closed if tmux is missing or not runnable.
