title: Codex prompt edit fails because forked thread already has an active writer
body:
## Bug

Editing an earlier human message in a Codex Chat session consistently fails with `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED` instead of creating and activating the edited conversation branch.

**Source:** Reported in AO Chat with an attached screenshot  
**Analyzed against:** `9c1797cde982c0cdf925c74ea4588cf5f3fbcb57`  
**AO daemon:** checkout build (`dev`) on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**Codex CLI:** `0.148.0`  
**OS:** macOS arm64  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1 — the prompt-edit workflow is broken whenever the edited prompt has a preceding provider turn.

![Reported `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED` error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-edit-active-writer/.issue-assets/codex-edit-active-writer/reported-error.png)

## Reproduction

1. Start a Codex session in Chat mode.
2. Complete at least two human/assistant turns.
3. Edit the second human message and submit it.
4. Observe `the stored provider conversation could not be resumed (CHAT_RESUME_FAILED)`.

A minimized live provider harness reproduces the backend boundary directly:

1. Start a real Codex app-server conversation.
2. Complete one turn.
3. Call `thread/fork` through that turn.
4. While the source app-server remains open, start a second app-server and call `thread/resume` for the fork id.

This failed three out of three times with app-server error `-32600: thread <id> already has an active writer`. Waiting two seconds did not change the result. Closing the source connection before resume made the same harness pass twice.

## Root Cause

`Service.EditMessage` calls `ChatForker.Fork`, receives the new provider conversation id, and immediately calls `driver.Resume` for that id on a new app-server process. Codex `thread/fork` already loads the new thread and emits `thread/started`, so the source app-server owns the fork as its active writer. The second process cannot resume it.

AO only closes the source controller after the replacement controller has been created and installed. That point is unreachable because replacement resume fails first.

The existing service fake models `Fork` as returning a passive string and therefore cannot express provider writer ownership. Adapter tests cover fork and resume independently rather than chaining them as the edit flow does.

## Fix

Preserve AO's one-writer and failure-recovery guarantees while changing the edit handoff sequence so a fork is not resumed by a second process while its creating app-server still owns it. Add regression coverage with a writer-aware fake plus an opt-in live Codex fork/resume test.

## Impact

- Editing the first prompt is unaffected because it starts a fresh provider conversation.
- Editing any later prompt is broken for Codex Chat sessions.
- The original conversation and worktree remain intact; the edit is refused rather than silently losing history.

## Related

- [PR #3676](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3676) — introduced Codex prompt editing with conversation branches.

title: fix(files): correctness follow-ups for the markdown Preview tab
body:
Follow-ups for #4251, branched off `feat/github-markdown-render`. Merging this into that branch folds the commits into the PR.

Seven correctness fixes, three cleanups, the first tests for the new code, and a rename plus redesign of the tab pair. One commit per item, each with its reasoning, so anything you disagree with can be dropped on its own.

## Bugs

**Relative images never reloaded after an edit.** `buildWorkspaceBlobUrl` mirrors `ImageDiffView`'s blob route but not its `v=` parameter, and that parameter is why the route works — it serves `no-store`, so as `ImageDiffView`'s own comment puts it, without a changing URL the element never refetches at all. An image an agent rewrote kept rendering from cache indefinitely. Threads the detail's load timestamp through `MarkdownFileContext`.

**A failed image rendered as a broken-image box.** The CSP allows `img-src` from `'self'`, `data:` and the loopback daemon only, so an `https://` image — a shields.io badge, a hosted screenshot, the two most common images in a real README — cannot load here at all. Falls back to alt text, the way `ImageDiffView` already handles its own failures.

**Truncated files rendered as though complete.** The daemon caps content at `maxWorkspaceFileBytes` and reports `contentTruncated`; the diff body respects it, the rendered view ignored it. The rendering is worse than the omission: a cut landing inside a fence leaves it unclosed, swallowing everything after it into one code block, with no signal that anything is missing. Adds the same warning strip behind a new `files.contentTruncated` string, translated for all eight locales.

**Heading links could scroll to the wrong file.** `rehype-slug` guarantees ids unique per rendered file, not per document, and the Files tab expands many cards at once — two open READMEs with `## Overview` put two `id="overview"` in one DOM, and `document.getElementById` answers with whichever is first. Resolves within the file's own container instead. Prefixing the slugs would also have worked but would have broken every hand-written `[link](#overview)`, which is the more common case.

**Clicking a heading overwrote the clipboard.** Silently, with no affordance saying so, and with a bare `#some-heading` that names no file and cannot be pasted anywhere and followed. Scroll only; a deliberate copy-link control can come later.

**The selection guard leaked on tab switch.** `DiffView` reports selection state up so a background refetch cannot re-render rows out from under a live selection, and that effect had no cleanup. Harmless until this PR, since the diff only unmounted with the card. Now: switch tabs with a selection active and `selectionOrMenuActive` stays `true` forever, the detail query stays disabled, and the rendered view sits on a snapshot that never refreshes while the agent keeps writing — with nothing left mounted that could clear it.

**Tab switching lost scroll position.** Not because a scroll position is discarded — an expanded file has no scroll box, the Files panel is one shared scroller. Swapping a 4,000-line diff for its rendered form shortens the column by thousands of pixels, and the browser clamps `scrollTop` to the new maximum; switching back restores the height but not the clamped-away offset.

Worth recording since it is the obvious thing to reach for: **`forceMount` does not fix this.** A hidden `TabsContent` is `display: none`, contributes zero height, and clamps identically — no benefit, and a large diff mounted for as long as the card is open. Instead a small `useViewModeScrollAnchor` records the card's offset from the scroll root when a mode is left and restores it when that mode returns, in a layout effect plus one `requestAnimationFrame`, since virtualized rows settle to their real heights a frame after mounting. No change to `useSharedScrollRowVirtualizer`. (The anchor originally rode the tab strip; the last commit moves that strip into the title row, so it rides the card's own top edge instead — see below.)

## Cleanups

- `textOf` / `fenceOf` / the `language-*` pattern arrived as byte-for-byte copies of `ChatMarkdown`'s. Both feed the same highlighter, so language sniffing had two places to drift. One copy in `lib/markdown-fence.ts`.
- `code-theme.css` had every selector written twice, once per scope. `:is(.chat-code, .markdown-code)` states it once — identical matching, ~60 fewer lines. Also corrects `HighlightedCode`'s comment, which still named `.chat-code` as the only scope.
- Notes in `MarkdownFileView` that the `prefers-color-scheme` argument holds under Electron but not `npm run dev:web`.

## Tests

`markdown-image-resolver` is pure and does the fiddliest work in the feature; it arrived untested. Eleven cases: resolution against the file's directory, a file at the workspace root, `..` walking up, `..` clamping at the root rather than escaping, query/fragment stripping, absolute passthrough, and the version reaching the URL.

The tab pair itself had no coverage at all. Two cases now: the strip renders in the title row as a sibling of the trigger rather than a descendant, and survives the panel swap — which is the `asChild` ref composition actually working at runtime — and it stays off files that cannot render as markdown.

## Rename and redesign

`Source diff` / `Rendered` → **Diff** / **Preview**, strings renamed to `files.diff` / `files.preview` and retranslated for all eight locales.

The control then moved out of the body and into the file's own title row. It had a band to itself under the title, and that band held nothing else — a right-aligned control with the whole width of the card empty to its left. It now sits beside the `+N`/`-N` badges, on the line that already names the file it acts on, and the card is a row shorter.

`AccordionTrigger` already had a `trailing` slot for exactly this: rendered inside the header row but as a sibling of the trigger `<button>`, which is what makes it legal — a `<button>` inside a `<button>` is invalid, and a nested tab would collapse the file on click. The Tabs root moves up to enclose the title row as well as the body it switches; it and `AccordionItem` both take `asChild`, so they compose onto the same single `<li>`: no wrapper element, no change in DOM depth. The strip renders only while the file is expanded.

**This costs the anchoring premise of the scroll-position commit above.** That commit chose the tab strip deliberately, because it sat at the top of the swapped body and was an element the component owned outright, with no ref composition through `asChild` in the way. The strip no longer moves with the body, so the anchor rides the card's own top edge, through a ref composed across both `asChild` roots. Since that is precisely what the earlier commit avoided, it is now covered by tests rather than resting on a typecheck.

Appearance follows the inspector rail's own tab buttons (`session-inspector__tab-button`), which is the tab language of the pane this control lives in: `text-passive` labels, `--color-interactive-*` fills one step apart on the same neutral (foreground at 4% for the track, 7% for the selected tab), and a hairline border — GitHub's segmented-control signature, and what separates this shape from a shadcn pill group. Stock shadcn's palette is dropped, and worth flagging as an actual defect rather than taste: its dark-theme active fill is `bg-input/30`, white at 1.2% over the `bg-muted` track, which is not a visible selection at this size.

Sizing is a 20px track over 16px pills — deliberately under the 20px a standalone control would get. It rides in a 36px row it does not own, beside a 28px button, and reading as the smaller thing there is the point; the labels are wide enough to keep the targets easy despite the height. Narrowing keys off the `inspector` container the shell already declares, at the 350px/300px steps it already breaks at, so the toggle changes on the same drag positions as everything else in the pane. In the centre pane there is no `inspector` container to match, so it keeps full size.

Still a judgement call, and still droppable as its own commit if you disagree.

## Not addressed

- **`github-markdown-css` vs the design system.** `CLAUDE.md` asks for explicit approval before deviating. Your reasoning is sound and I have not touched it — flagging it as the repo owner's call. Side effect worth knowing: AO's nine theme styles (dracula, nord, gruvbox…) do not reach the Preview tab, which stays GitHub-coloured.
- **Lockfile churn.** The `motion` entries under `packages/product-ui` are unrelated to this feature, but they correct a stale lock on `main` (`packages/product-ui/package.json` already lists it there). Harmless — worth a line in the PR body so a reviewer does not stop on it.

## Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Full renderer suite as of the tests commit: **2689 passed, 1 skipped, 204 files** — including your 35 `SessionFilesView` tests unmodified. Each commit typechecks on its own.

For the title-row commit on top I re-ran typecheck and `SessionFilesView` only (**37 passed**, the 35 plus the two new ones), not the full suite.

Manual verification in the Electron app is still worth doing for the scroll anchor and the image reload, which are the two that depend on real layout.

## Demo

Screen recording of the change in the desktop app: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e5T3MbyQTVrNtLqfo2ZLPWgldhwUpDQO/view?usp=sharing

title: fix(chat): keep Codex prompt forks on one writer
body:
Fixes #4299

## Summary

- keep a Codex prompt-edit fork on the app-server connection that created it and already owns its writer lock
- atomically move the live controller to the forked branch without starting a second Codex writer
- preserve the existing resume fallback for providers that do not expose a loaded-fork binding, with unit and live Codex regression coverage

## Root cause

Codex `thread/fork` immediately loads and subscribes the forked thread in the creating app-server process. AO then tried to `thread/resume` that same fork through a second app-server process. Codex correctly rejected the second writer, which AO surfaced in the chat editor as `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED`.

## Local Electron evidence

Both screenshots are from the same isolated local desktop session while editing the second user prompt (the fork path).

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline build: the edit fails with `the stored provider conversation could not be resumed (CHAT_RESUME_FAILED)`. | Fixed build: the edited prompt is accepted and Codex replies `EDITED SECOND RESPONSE`. |
| ![Before: later prompt edit fails with CHAT_RESUME_FAILED](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-edit-active-writer/.issue-assets/codex-edit-active-writer/before-local.png) | ![After: later prompt edit completes successfully](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-edit-active-writer/.issue-assets/codex-edit-active-writer/after-local.png) |

## Verification

- `npm run lint` (clean AO environment): all Go tests and golangci-lint pass
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/service/chat ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver -count=1`
- `AO_CODEX_LIVE=1 go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver -run '^TestLiveCodexAppServer$' -count=1 -v`
- real Electron before/after run against isolated `~/.ao/dev` state

## Risk

The new binding is optional and feature-detected. Non-Codex drivers retain the existing start/resume behavior, and no API, storage schema, or frontend contract changes are included.

title: fix(frontend): detect fresh nightly releases promptly
body:
Fixes #3938

## Summary

- check the Nightly channel every 15 minutes while keeping Stable and feature builds on the existing hourly cadence
- make a user-requested Nightly check resolve the newest completed GitHub release directly instead of depending on the lagging prerelease Atom feed
- require the platform manifest asset before selecting a release, fall back to the existing provider on API/rate-limit/network failures, and restore the normal provider after the check
- reschedule the live timer when the user changes update channels

## Root cause

The reported app launched and checked at about 8:17 PM. `v0.12.7-nightly.202608231517` published at 9:01 PM, but Nightly shared Stable's one-hour timer, so the next automatic check was not due until 9:17 PM. The running app then detected the release on that exact tick and staged its 167,055,860-byte ZIP by 9:18:40 PM. Automatic detection was working, but its policy created a stale window of up to one hour.

Manual prerelease discovery was separately coupled to `electron-updater`'s `releases.atom` path. GitHub can expose a completed release and its manifest through the Releases API before that generated Atom view catches up. The existing issue's proposed missing `Cache-Control` cause is not present in `electron-updater@6.8.9`: `builder-util-runtime` already adds `Cache-Control: no-cache` to GETs, so adding the same header again would not fix server-side feed propagation.

The reported `…1350` build also predates #4285's manual-request status correlation, which explains why the click itself appeared inert. This PR addresses the remaining detection path.

## Reproduction evidence

The scheduling regression test used an enabled Nightly install. Before the fix:

```text
expected 3600000 to be 900000
```

That is the shipped 60-minute timer versus the required 15-minute Nightly timer.

The manual-check regression exposed a completed newer Nightly with the platform manifest. Before the fix, the updater made zero Releases API requests and remained dependent on Atom discovery:

```text
expected fetch mock to have been called
Number of calls: 0
```

Live evidence from the reported machine:

```text
running: 0.12.7-nightly.202608231350
published: 0.12.7-nightly.202608231517 at 21:01 IST
launch/initial check: ~20:17 IST
next hourly check: ~21:17 IST
staged: ~/Library/Caches/agent-orchestrator-updater/pending/Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.7-nightly.202608231517.zip at 21:18:40 IST
```

## Fix evidence

Both deterministic reproductions now pass. The manual fixture also proves an even newer but incomplete release (missing the platform manifest) is ignored.

A real Electron + `electron-updater@6.8.9` check then exercised the fixed direct completed-release route against the public release:

```text
Checking for update
Found version 0.12.7-nightly.202608231517 (url: Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.7-nightly.202608231517.zip, Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-x64-0.12.7-nightly.202608231517.zip)
PASS direct completed release 0.12.7-nightly.202608231350 -> 0.12.7-nightly.202608231517
```

Release: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/releases/tag/v0.12.7-nightly.202608231517

## Tests

- focused updater suite — 58 passed
- frontend CI Vitest suite — 209 files, 2,767 tests passed
- frontend and E2E TypeScript checks — passed
- renderer smoke — passed
- product UI verification — 10 files, 64 tests passed
- gitleaks scan — passed

bug(desktop): macOS Toggle Developer Tools crashes the Electron main process
body:
## Bug

On macOS, invoking the native **View → Toggle Developer Tools** command (or its `Cmd+Option+I` accelerator) can throw an uncaught exception in Electron's main process instead of opening DevTools.

The reporter sees the standard “A JavaScript error occurred in the main process” dialog with:

```text
Uncaught Exception:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toggleDevTools')
    at webContentsMethod (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:31239)
    at Object.execute (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:28651)
    at MenuItem.click (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:35249)
    at a._executeCommand (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:40710)
```

![macOS main-process error after toggling DevTools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-macos-toggle-devtools-crash-20260823/.issue-assets/macos-toggle-devtools-crash-20260823/devtools-crash.png)

**Source:** Direct Codex report on 2026-08-23 (no public chat URL)  
**Reported by:** @illegalcall  
**First observed:** 2026-08-23 on a nightly build; exact regression onset is not established  
**Analyzed against:** `c86b58d04a38ce669be3215ab0834e29cf2c0d30` (`origin/main`)  
**AO desktop version:** `0.12.7-nightly.202608181938` (bundled daemon reports `dev`, healthy on port `3001`)  
**Environment:** macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple Silicon (`arm64`)  
**Priority:** P2 — the action crashes the Electron main process, but the scope is bounded to the native DevTools command and an in-app DevTools path is available  
**Confidence:** High — the stack, platform menu setup, and exact failing mechanism have been traced; an existing tested PR implements the same fix

## Reproduction

1. Launch Agent Orchestrator on macOS.
2. Focus a surface backed by a `WebContentsView` (the Browser panel is the common case).
3. Choose **View → Toggle Developer Tools** from the native macOS application menu, or press `Cmd+Option+I`.
4. Observe the uncaught `toggleDevTools` exception and main-process error dialog.

## Expected

DevTools opens for the focused AO surface, or the shell surface as a safe fallback, without terminating the main process.

## Actual

Electron's native menu command attempts to call `toggleDevTools` through an undefined focused-window target and throws an uncaught exception in the main process.

## Root Cause

`frontend/src/main.ts` installs AO's guarded application menu only on Windows. On macOS, Electron's default application menu remains active, including the built-in `role: "toggleDevTools"` command.

AO composes its window from a `BaseWindow` and `WebContentsView` surfaces. When focus belongs to a `WebContentsView`, Electron's built-in role resolves no focused `BrowserWindow`, then its internal `webContentsMethod` path attempts to access `toggleDevTools` on an undefined target. This matches the `MenuItem.click` stack in the report.

AO's custom titlebar IPC handler and Windows menu already route DevTools through guarded AO logic; the native default macOS menu is the unguarded path.

## Suggested Fix

Install an explicit macOS application menu and replace only the built-in DevTools role with a click handler that:

1. toggles DevTools for the last-focused AO browser surface; and
2. falls back to the shell `webContents` when no browser surface is available.

Keep the standard macOS app roles (About, Services, Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Quit) when replacing Electron's default menu.

## Impact

- A standard macOS menu item and accelerator can crash the Electron main process.
- No data loss was observed in this report.
- Workaround: avoid the native menu/accelerator and use AO's in-app DevTools control where available.

## Related

- [PR #3910](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3910) — open, tested implementation of the traced fix; awaiting review and currently has no closing issue reference.

title: feat(webui): serve the LAN web UI with browser sessions
body:
Serves the existing renderer as a web UI from the opt-in LAN listener, so any
browser that can reach the daemon is a first-class client — board, terminals,
chat, orchestrator — with no Electron. Everything here is off by default;
nothing changes unless the LAN listener is enabled.

### How browsers get in

A browser cannot carry `Authorization: Bearer` on a WebSocket upgrade, an
`EventSource`, or the top-level navigation that loads the app. So browsers log
in once with the **existing connection password** at `/login` and receive a
**session cookie**. Bearer is untouched for native clients.

That works on every network path, with no extra dependencies:

| Deployment | Config |
|---|---|
| Direct on a trusted LAN | nothing beyond enabling the listener (plaintext, same as ADR-0001) |
| Behind a TLS proxy or tunnel (Caddy, nginx, VPN, the ADR-0004 tunnel) | `AO_CONNECT_BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1`, `AO_CONNECT_STRICT_PORT=1` |
| Behind `tailscale serve` | same as above; **optionally** `AO_CONNECT_TRUST_TAILSCALE_IDENTITY=1` + `AO_CONNECT_ALLOWED_LOGINS` to skip the password |

The Tailscale identity option is an opt-in convenience layered on top — it is
not required for anything, and the daemon refuses to start with it enabled on
a non-loopback bind.

### Why this shape

The LAN listener already ships auth, per-source lockout, and control-route
blocking. What was missing was narrow: nothing serves a web UI, and browsers
can't send Bearer. Serving the SPA from that listener makes it same-origin with
the API (no CORS) and inherits every existing protection.

Alternatives rejected:

- **A second listener, or a proxy in front of the loopback listener.**
  `AGENTS.md` allows exactly one network-facing bind, and the loopback listener
  is unauthenticated by design — a proxy would have to re-implement its
  blocklist. This adds no new bind. (A TLS proxy in front of the *LAN* listener
  is supported, per the table above.)
- **Query-parameter tokens for WebSocket/SSE.** They leak into logs, and some
  proxies (including `tailscale serve`) strip them from upgrade requests.
- **A new browser client built on `product-ui`.** The renderer already has a
  bridge abstraction with a browser fallback; a second client would duplicate
  every surface.

### Security rules, each with tests

Recorded in the new `docs/adr/0005-web-ui-on-the-lan-listener.md` (R1–R7):

1. Cookie- and identity-authenticated requests are **CSRF-checked**. Bearer is
   not — native clients have no ambient credential.
2. Cross-origin `/mux` upgrades are **rejected** under cookie or identity auth;
   Bearer keeps its existing skip-verify path.
3. The login route's **lockout can't be evaded** by rotating `X-Forwarded-For`:
   it is trusted only on a loopback bind, where the sole path in is a proxy.
4. **Identity trust requires a loopback bind** and an explicit allowlist; an
   empty allowlist denies everyone.

### Notes for review

- The tracked `backend/internal/httpd/webui/dist/index.html` is deliberately a
  **placeholder**. `dist/` is gitignored; only `index.html` is tracked so
  `//go:embed all:dist` compiles. Run `build:web` to produce a real bundle.
- `AGENTS.md` gains one bullet recording that the LAN listener may also serve
  the web UI, citing ADR-0005, in the same amendment pattern ADR-0001 used.
- Rebased onto current `main`; `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` were regenerated
  via `npm run api` rather than hand-merged.

### Testing

`go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test ./internal/websession/...
./internal/httpd/... ./internal/daemon/...` — all clean, including the OpenAPI
parity test.

The same code was also verified end to end against a real daemon: a browser
with no Electron rendering live data and a streaming PTY over `/mux`, including
from a second device through a TLS proxy (`tailscale serve`). This branch ships
the placeholder `dist/index.html`, so it needs `build:web` before it serves the
SPA itself.

title: Enable interface switching after Codex resumes
body:
## What

Bind exact native Codex resumes to the active runtime generation so restored terminal sessions are immediately eligible for interface switching. Add regression coverage for both restored and restarted supervised sessions.

## Why

Passive Codex resumes may not emit a `SessionStart` hook until the next user turn. AO therefore retained the correct thread ID but treated it as unverified for the new launch, leaving the interface switch disabled.

## How

Only native Codex resume paths establish launch identity immediately. Existing coordinated handoffs retain their behavior, while fresh and fallback launches still require current-generation hook proof.

## Testing

- `cd backend && GOCACHE=/tmp/ao-codex-fix-gocache go test ./...`

title: feat(renderer): gate native-only UI by bridge capability, not Electron presence
body:
Freezes a capability contract on the renderer bridge and gates native-only UI on
the specific capability each surface needs, instead of on whether Electron happens
to be present.

### The problem

Native-only decisions are currently made by testing `window.ao` directly, which
conflates two different questions: *is this Electron?* and *can this surface
work here?* The sharpest example is `TerminalPane.tsx`, where `if (!window.ao)`
early-returns a **static fake terminal** — so terminals are stubbed by
Electron-absence rather than by any real capability, and a caller who has a
working terminal transport but no Electron gets a convincing fake instead of the
real thing.

`BrowserPanel.tsx` had the same shape: a `StaticPreview` component rendering a
mocked-up "Demo app preview" card with invented route counts and latency
whenever the native browser view was unavailable.

### What this does

- Adds an explicit capability set to `aoBridge` and freezes it as a contract, so
  each surface asks for what it needs rather than inferring it.
- Replaces the direct `window.ao` checks in the affected renderer files with
  capability checks against that contract.
- **Deletes `StaticPreview`** and replaces it with an honest "not available here"
  message. Same for the fake terminal path.
- Adds the six locale keys those new states need, in all eight catalogs.

### Alternatives rejected

- **Leaving the `window.ao` checks in place and adding a flag.** The existing
  `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` flag is already overloaded — it unconditionally switches the
  renderer to mock data, so it cannot express "no Electron, but a real daemon."
  Another flag with the same shape would not either.
- **A second renderer built for non-Electron targets.** It would need its own copy
  of the board, terminals, chat and orchestrator surfaces, and would drift.

### Rebase note

Rebased onto current `main`. Upstream's device-preset viewport picker is retained
inside the component this change renames to `NativeBrowserPanelView` — it is
therefore capability-gated by construction, since that component renders only when
the native browser panel is available. The early gate, `aoBridge` access, and the
`StaticPreview` deletion are all preserved, and upstream's new locale keys survive
alongside the six added here.

### Testing

`npm run frontend:typecheck` clean, and the renderer vitest scoped to the affected
files — 11 files, 232 tests passing. The full renderer suite and the e2e suite were
not re-run on this rebased branch.

title: feat(orchestrator): make the project orchestrator a route destination
body:
Makes the project orchestrator a real destination — a route you can navigate to,
link to, and come back to — rather than a topbar shortcut that spawns a session
as a side effect of being clicked.

### Why

The orchestrator is a long-lived, project-scoped thing: it plans and delegates
across a project's workers. Reaching it through a button that both *navigates*
and *spawns* has two costs. There is no address for it, so nothing can link to it
and returning to it means finding the session again. And spawn failures have to
surface in the topbar, which is why the topbar carried its own spawn-in-progress
and spawn-error state.

### What this does

- Adds `/projects/$projectId/orchestrator` as a route, with its own loading,
  not-started, unavailable and restarting states.
- Derives the current session from the route when on that path, so the topbar and
  inspector resolve correctly without a session id in the URL.
- **Removes the topbar's inline spawn path** — `spawnOrchestrator`, the spawning
  flag, and the board-scoped spawn error — since lifecycle now belongs to the
  destination.
- Adds the 22 `orchestratorRoute.*` keys plus `shell.orchestratorOrigin`, in all
  eight catalogs.

### Alternative rejected

Keeping the orchestrator as a shortcut into the existing session surface. That
surface is worker-shaped: it cannot express project-level lifecycle (start,
restart, not-configured) or a stable address, which is most of what makes the
orchestrator useful to return to.

### Rebase note

Rebased onto current `main`. Upstream's `TopbarKillError` → `TopbarActionError`
rename is applied at the two call sites that survive here; the third was inside
the board spawn-error block this change removes, so it is gone rather than
restored. Upstream's `TopbarOpenEditorButton` is retained in the position it was
added.

One follow-up worth flagging: that button is **ungated**. This branch does not
carry a capability contract, so there is nothing here to gate it with. If the
companion renderer-capability change lands, that button will want gating for
non-desktop clients.

### Testing

`npm run frontend:typecheck` clean, and the renderer vitest scoped to the affected
files — 7 files, 128 tests passing. The full renderer suite and the e2e suite were
not re-run on this rebased branch.

title: fix(desktop): prevent macOS DevTools menu crash
body:
Fixes [#4308](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4308).

## Summary

- install an explicit macOS application menu so Electron's unsafe default `toggleDevTools` role is not used
- route the native menu and accelerator through AO's guarded last-focused-browser handler, with the shell web contents as fallback
- preserve Electron's complete standard macOS App, File, Edit, and Window menus through their top-level roles
- add regression coverage proving the DevTools item has a click handler and no `toggleDevTools` role

## Root cause

AO composes its desktop window from a `BaseWindow` and `WebContentsView` children. Electron's default macOS DevTools role assumes focus belongs to a `BrowserWindow`; when focus belongs to an AO child view, Electron resolves no focused window and dereferences `toggleDevTools` on an undefined target in the main process.

## Related

- [PR #3910](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3910) has the same core diagnosis. This implementation preserves the complete Electron-provided macOS menus via `appMenu`, `fileMenu`, `editMenu`, and `windowMenu` instead of reconstructing a subset of their commands.

## Verification

- `npm test -- --run src/main/menu.test.ts` — 4 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck` — passed
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` — passed
- `npx vitest run` — 209 files and 2,767 tests passed
- launched the real Electron checkout in isolated mode with the daemon healthy on `127.0.0.1:3002`
- Electron-native harness installed the generated macOS menu and directly invoked its DevTools item: one handler call, no `toggleDevTools` role, all four standard menu roles present

title: [Bug]: Orchestrator replacement leaves the old agent process running on Windows, worktree cleanup fails
body:
### Summary

Replacing a project's active orchestrator (e.g. after changing its configured agent, or any "clean" re-spawn) can fail on Windows with an internal server error. The previous orchestrator's agent process is left running with its working directory inside the worktree the replacement is trying to delete, so the force-remove fails with a file-in-use error. When this happens mid-flight, the old orchestrator can end up retired with no new one successfully created, leaving the project without a working orchestrator until manually recovered.

### Steps to reproduce

On Windows, start a project's orchestrator (either mode, TUI or chat).

Trigger a clean orchestrator replacement for that project (POST /api/v1/orchestrators with clean: true, e.g. via changing the project's orchestrator agent while a session is active) and observe the response.

### Expected behavior

The old orchestrator's agent process is fully terminated before its worktree is force-removed; replacement succeeds.

### Actual behavior

500 INTERNAL_ERROR, with the daemon log showing: retire replacement <session>: force destroy: gitworktree: force remove path "...\worktrees\<project>\orchestrator\<project>-orchestrator": unlinkat ...: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.

Two independent causes, both in RetireForReplacement (backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go): (1) TUI/conpty sessions: Destroy() killed only the ConPTY's direct child (the "agent-process supervise" wrapper) via TerminateProcess, which does not propagate to that process's own child (the actual claude.exe/codex.exe) so the real agent process was orphaned. (2) Chat-mode sessions: a chat session has no runtime handle at all -- its controller owns an app-server child process directly, not through the runtime port (see the pre-existing, correct branch in Kill, which RetireForReplacement never mirrored) -- so the real agent process was simply never asked to stop.

Fix ready in a PR for both: (1) taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F on Close, matching the same pattern already used in adapters/chatdriver/acp/process_windows.go; (2) branch on session mode in RetireForReplacement (and its workspace-project sibling) the same way Kill already does, calling stopChatBestEffort for chat sessions. Regression test included (fails on old code, passes with the fix). Verified live against a packaged Windows build: reproduced the exact failure on both a TUI and a chat orchestrator, confirmed the old agent process was actually terminated (not just that the API stopped erroring) after each fix.

### AO version

commit ebd56bd (main, 2026-08-23)

### Environment

Windows 11, Go backend

title: fix(session_manager): stop the replaced orchestrator's process on Windows
body:
## What

Orchestrator replacement (`RetireForReplacement` and its workspace-project sibling, `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`) could leave the previous orchestrator's agent process running on Windows, which then holds files open in the worktree the replacement is about to force-remove.

## Why

Fixes #4317. Replacing a project's orchestrator (e.g. via changing its configured agent while a session is active) could fail with:
```
retire replacement <session>: force destroy: gitworktree: force remove path "...":
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
```
When this happens mid-flight the old orchestrator can end up retired with no new one successfully created.

## How

Two independent, unrelated root causes, both fixed here since they produce the same symptom:

1. **TUI/conpty sessions** (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/host_conpty_windows.go`): `Close()` killed only the ConPTY's direct child via `cmd.Process.Kill()` (`TerminateProcess`), which does not propagate to that process's own children (the actual `claude.exe`/`codex.exe`, spawned by the `agent-process supervise` wrapper). Fixed by killing the whole tree with `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` — mirroring the identical, already-established pattern in the sibling `adapters/chatdriver/acp/process_windows.go` (deliberately not a Windows Job Object: that also worked but had no precedent anywhere in this codebase).
2. **Chat-mode sessions**: a chat session has no runtime handle at all — its controller owns an app-server child process directly (`ChatLauncher`/`chatSvc`), not through the runtime port. `RetireForReplacement` never branched on this, unlike `Kill`, which already has the correct `if mode == chat { stopChatBestEffort } else if handle.ID != "" { runtime.Destroy }` pattern (with a comment explicitly calling out the Windows directory-lock risk). Mirrored that branch into `RetireForReplacement` and `retireWorkspaceProjectForReplacement` (3 call sites total).

## Testing

- New regression test `TestRetireForReplacementStopsChatSessionInsteadOfRuntimeDestroy`: fails on the old code (chat.StopChat never called), passes with the fix.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/...` — green except pre-existing, environment-specific failures unrelated to this change (confirmed identical on `main` without it).
- Verified live end-to-end against a packaged Windows build, for both fixes independently and together:
  - Reproduced the original failure on a **chat**-mode orchestrator (the exact repro from #4317), confirmed the fix resolves it and the old agent process is actually gone (`Get-Process` on its PID) after replacement succeeds.
  - Reproduced the same failure on a **TUI**-mode orchestrator, confirmed the fix resolves it and the old process tree (wrapper + agent binary) is actually gone after replacement succeeds.
  - Re-verified after refactoring the conpty fix from a Job Object to `taskkill /T /F` that both repros still pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change (two root causes, one symptom, one issue); closes #4317
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene; conpty fix intentionally mirrors the existing `acp/process_windows.go` pattern rather than introducing a new one
- [x] Tests added for the user-visible behavior
- [ ] CI (not run locally beyond `go test`/`go build`/`go vet` for the touched packages)

## Note for reviewers

This touches session-teardown/process-lifecycle code with real risk if wrong. Flagging for extra scrutiny before merge rather than treating it as routine — happy to split further or add more test coverage if requested.

title: bug(daemon+renderer): SSE streams reconnect with no backoff, amplifying a transient setup 5xx into a request storm
body:
## Summary
The renderer opens Server-Sent-Events streams — `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/events` and `/api/v1/notifications/stream` — with `EventSource`, which reconnects **immediately on any failed connection, with no backoff**. If the daemon returns a transient 5xx while *setting up* the stream, the client reconnects in a tight loop, turning one brief failure into a sustained burst of failed requests and high CPU on both sides.

## Where it happens
- Handler: `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` → `streamWorkspaceChanges` (and the notifications stream controller). These can only return 5xx during setup, before `w.WriteHeader(200)`.
- Setup failure points: `WorkspaceWatchPaths` → `sessionWorkspaceRecord` (its `GetSession` branch wraps the error untyped as `fmt.Errorf("get %s: %w", …)` → 500), and `workspacewatch.Watch` / `watchRoot`.
- Renderer: the `EventSource` consumer for these streams reconnects with no backoff.

## Reproduction
The daemon port is in `~/.ao/running.json`.
1. Healthy stream (baseline): `curl -N http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v1/sessions/<id>/workspace/events` → `200`, stream stays open. ✅ verified
2. Missing workspace: same call for a session whose workspace dir is gone → `404 SESSION_WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (already typed on current `main`). ✅ verified — so the common missing-path case is *not* the culprit.
3. Trigger the amplification: put the daemon under DB-lock contention (see #3963) so `GetSession` intermittently errors → stream setup returns `500` → watch the renderer immediately reconnect and re-fail in a loop (visible in the access log and as CPU spikes). A single stuck stream produces a large, self-sustaining burst.

## Suggested fix
- Renderer: exponential backoff + jitter on SSE reconnect; stop reconnecting when the session is terminated and on any `4xx`.
- Daemon (optional): send `Retry-After` on transient setup failures so clients pace reconnects.

## Related
- #3963 (DB lock contention → the transient 5xx this amplifies)
- #1321 (RFC: remove polling → reactive sync)

title: investigate: reported 502 on /api/v1/* has no matching code path in the current daemon
body:
## Status: needs a captured example before it is actionable

502 responses have been reported on `/api/v1/*`, but on investigation **the current daemon HTTP layer contains no code path that emits 502**:
- `rg -n "StatusBadGateway|502|BadGateway|httputil|ReverseProxy"` over `backend/` returns nothing in the request path.
- When the daemon is down/unreachable, the renderer's `runtimeFetch` returns **503** (`daemon_unavailable`), and a direct loopback call fails with `ECONNREFUSED` (a network error) — neither is a 502.

So my original hypothesis ("client hits the loopback before the daemon is ready") is **not supported by the code** and I've removed it.

## Plausible remaining sources (unconfirmed)
- A **dev-only** intermediary (e.g. the Vite dev server proxy in front of `/api/v1`) returning 502 while the daemon restarts.
- An **older daemon version** that had a proxy/handler since removed.
- An intermediary outside this repo.

## What would make this actionable
A concrete captured 502: the exact request path, method, daemon **version**, and whether it was a dev or packaged build. Without that, there is no reproducible cause to fix in the current code.

If nobody can produce a captured example, this should be **closed** as not-reproducible rather than left open.

title: bug(httpd): transient/DB errors wrapped untyped collapse to 500 INTERNAL_ERROR
body:
## Summary
Handlers and services return raw `fmt.Errorf(...)` for conditions that are **transient or expected**, and `backend/internal/httpd/envelope.go` maps any non-`apierr` error to `INTERNAL_ERROR` / `500`. As a result, transient DB contention (#3963), client-state conditions, and genuine faults all surface as **identical opaque 500s** — the reliability signal is polluted by non-faults, and the real cause is only visible in the daemon log, never in the API response.

## Where
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope.go` — the `INTERNAL_ERROR` fallback for untyped errors.
- Example offender: `backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go` → `sessionWorkspaceRecord` wraps `GetSession` as `fmt.Errorf("get %s: %w", …)` (untyped → 500).

## Reproduction
1. `rg "envelope.WriteError" backend/internal/httpd/controllers` and follow each to the service call it forwards — the ones returning plain `fmt.Errorf` (not `apierr.*`) become opaque 500s.
2. Drive any such handler while the DB is under contention (#3963): the response is a `500` with code `INTERNAL_ERROR` and no specific `error_code`, indistinguishable from a real server fault.

## Suggested fix
- Map transient/contention DB errors to a typed `503` (retryable) with a stable code, and expected states to typed `4xx`, so the 5xx surface reflects only real server faults.
- Land Sentry error capture (PRs #4180 desktop / #4181 mobile) so the remaining genuine 500s carry a grouped stack and root cause.

## Related
- #3963, #3649, #2699, #3408 (instances of the opacity); #4180 / #4181 (visibility)

body:
Code changes: +618 -34  
Tests: +432 -1  
Others: +4 -4  

## What

Adds Qwen token usage observability on current `main`.

- Parses Qwen monthly token usage JSONL and attributes records by bound session ID.
- Resolves usage from Qwen environment settings and each session workspace, including relative runtime output paths.
- Registers every existing monthly usage file and handles rollover and missing source retry.
- Refreshes exact-file watcher roots for Qwen workspaces as session inventory changes.
- Persists and aggregates Qwen usage through the shared collector and SQLite store.
- Accepts provider-reported totals that differ from normalized token buckets.

## Why this PR was recreated

The earlier provider PRs were stacked on one another instead of being based cleanly on `main`. This replaces the earlier Qwen PR #4185 without carrying Pi branch history.

## Related PRs and merge order

1. **Kimi:** #4311
2. **Pi:** #4326
3. **Qwen:** #4327 (this PR)

All three target `main`. Qwen's migration is standalone relative to the usage schema already on `main`; it does not require Pi.

## Implementation

Qwen's shared monthly records are filtered by bound session ID and normalized into the shared token model. The native total remains in `provider_usage_json`. Discovery resolves runtime storage for each AO session's workspace with Qwen's environment and settings precedence. Migration 0178 adds Qwen to the current Claude/Codex/Kimi usage constraints, and its rollback removes only Qwen usage while restoring the predecessor constraints.

The watcher tracks registered files in workspace-specific Qwen roots. A newly created monthly file without a hook is registered on the three-minute safety-net reconciliation tick. Qwen schema version 1 is supported; later versions need a mapping review. AO also requires cached input to be no greater than input so its uncached token bucket stays non-negative.

title: fix(chat): restore navigation to root conversation branches
body:
## What

Fix conversation branch navigation so a user can move from an edited branch (`2 / 2`) back to the root branch (`1 / 2`). Also reset the Chat surface when navigating between sessions so conversation-scoped mutation state cannot leak across tasks.

## Root cause

Root branch IDs use the form `<conversation-id>:root`. The generated frontend client correctly percent-encodes the colon as `%3A`, but Chi exposes that route parameter in encoded form. The controller passed the encoded value directly to the service, so SQLite searched for `<conversation-id>%3Aroot`, did not find it, and returned `CHAT_BRANCH_NOT_FOUND` even though `<conversation-id>:root` existed.

## How

- Decode the branch route parameter at the HTTP controller boundary before the conversation-scoped service lookup.
- Add a router-level regression test proving an encoded `%3Aroot` ID reaches the service as `:root`.
- Key `SessionChatSurface` by `session.id` so changing tasks creates a fresh conversation hook boundary.
- Add a frontend regression test covering that remount.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/httpd/...`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/fake -run TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination -count=1`
- `npm run typecheck` in `frontend/`
- `npm test -- --maxWorkers=1` in `frontend/` — 2,773 passed, 1 skipped
- Rebuilt and launched the isolated AO Electron app, restored the affected scratch session, activated its child branch, then activated the root through the formerly failing `%3Aroot` URL; both requests returned `202 Accepted` and the root response contained the decoded `:root` ID.

The full backend sweep encountered the unrelated timing-sensitive `TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination` failure under concurrent load; it passed immediately when rerun in isolation.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused bug fix
- [x] Regression tests added for the affected HTTP and UI boundaries
- [x] Relevant backend and frontend checks pass

title: bug(cursor): TUI startup MCP approval can consume AO follow-ups before hooks start
body:
## Bug

A Phoenix project configured with worker agent `cursor` and model `composer-2.5-fast` exposed two related spawn failures:

1. A normal prompted spawn failed with `chat mode unsupported for harness: cursor has no chat driver (SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED)` and created no session.
2. Explicit `--mode tui` created `phoenix-10`, but Cursor exited before accepting a follow-up. A disposable reproduction showed the underlying startup race: Cursor stops at its interactive MCP approval screen, while `ao send` returns success and the follow-up is consumed by that screen instead of reaching the agent.

**Source:** AO conversation, session `phoenix-1`, 2026-08-23  
**Reported by:** current AO user  
**Analyzed against:** `6cba6344c7081f2984927ca5f15140f99115c5c0` (`origin/main`)  
**AO CLI version:** `dev`  
**Desktop build:** `0.12.7-nightly.202608231948`  
**Priority:** medium / P2 — spawn is degraded, but manual TUI recovery exists  
**Confidence:** High for the reproduced startup-input loss; Medium for the exact `phoenix-10` exit because the Cursor process had already exited and produced no worker log

## Environment

- macOS Darwin 25.6.0 arm64
- zsh
- bundled binary only: `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`
- healthy daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001`
- Cursor Agent `2026.08.11-e8db854`, authenticated
- Cursor model `composer-2.5-fast`
- tmux 3.7c
- no Go binary in `PATH`

## Reproduction

### Original omitted-mode failure

```sh
AO_BIN="/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao"
"$AO_BIN" status --json # port 3001
"$AO_BIN" spawn \
  --project phoenix \
  --name cursor-chat-repro \
  --prompt "Reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_REPRO_OK and wait for follow-up."
```

Observed:

```text
spawn: chat mode unsupported for harness: cursor has no chat driver (SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED)
```

Exit status was 1 and no session row was created.

### Reproduced TUI startup-input loss

```sh
"$AO_BIN" spawn \
  --project phoenix \
  --name cursor-tui-repro \
  --mode tui \
  --prompt "Reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_TUI_REPRO_OK and wait for follow-up."
```

1. Cursor displays `MCP Server Approval Required` for the project MCP server before it consumes the prompt.
2. While that screen is visible, run:

```sh
"$AO_BIN" send \
  --session phoenix-13 \
  --message "Follow-up: reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_CHAT_FOLLOWUP_OK."
```

3. `ao send` exits 0, but the message is not shown or processed by Cursor.
4. After the MCP gate clears, a second `ao send` is delivered and Cursor replies normally.

For `phoenix-10`, durable state changed from idle to exited about three seconds after spawn. Its tmux shell remained alive, `cursor-agent` was gone, no Cursor native session id was recorded, and no Cursor `worker.log` was created.

## Root Cause

The CLI correctly omits `mode` when `--mode` is not passed (`backend/internal/cli/spawn.go`). The originally running packaged daemon resolved the saved Chat default but had no Cursor Chat driver, producing `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`.

Current `origin/main` already contains both protections:

- inherited Chat preflight failures fall back to TUI in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:771`
- Cursor is registered through `cursor-agent acp` in `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/registry.go:62`

After the daemon restarted, the same omitted-mode reproduction no longer errored and created a TUI session, confirming the original Chat failure was tied to the running packaged build rather than current source.

The remaining TUI race is in current source:

- Cursor TUI launches as `cursor-agent --model composer-2.5-fast -- <prompt>` and does not bypass MCP approval (`backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go:386`).
- AO Cursor hooks begin at `sessionStart` and tool/prompt events (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/hooks.go:57`), so the pre-session MCP dialog emits no blocked activity signal.
- The session therefore remains durably idle. `sessionguard.Deliver` refuses only known blocked decisions, so it permits the write (`backend/internal/sessionguard/guard.go:142`).
- tmux pastes the text and always presses Enter (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:575`). Cursor consumes that input at the approval screen.
- `ao send` has no provider acknowledgement for Cursor and returns success once tmux accepts the keystrokes (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:2887`).

## Suggested Fix

- Add a provider-neutral startup-ready gate for TUI sessions, satisfied by the first native session-start/prompt-ready signal.
- Queue or reject follow-ups with a typed not-ready error until that gate is satisfied.
- Do not auto-approve MCP servers under the default permission policy.
- Add a Cursor regression test where a pre-session dialog is present and verify that no follow-up is reported delivered until Cursor is ready.

## Workaround

- Install/restart into a build containing the merged Cursor ACP driver, then use Chat mode.
- On older builds, use `--mode tui`, answer the Cursor MCP approval screen manually, and resend the follow-up only after the Cursor prompt is visible.

## Verification and PR status

No fix PR was attempted. The machine has no Go toolchain, and repository policy requires `go build ./...` plus `go test ./...` before pushing a backend fix. No system software was installed and no unverified patch was pushed.

Dependency check: Cursor Agent `2026.08.11-e8db854` exposes the hidden `cursor-agent acp` command and matches the minimum version used by the merged Cursor Chat driver. The repository uses `github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk v0.13.5`, which is also the latest published SDK release.

## Related

- [#3712](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3712) — earlier unsupported-Chat Cursor spawn report in the desktop composer
- [PR #3715](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3715) — frontend routing of unsupported Chat agents to TUI
- [PR #4233](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4233) — inherited Chat default falls back to TUI
- [PR #4201](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4201) — merged Cursor ACP Chat driver tested against Cursor `2026.08.11-e8db854`
- [#3634](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3634) — related `ao send` success-versus-delivery semantics

title: fix(httpd): map transient DB-busy/deadline errors to 503, not opaque 500 (#4325)
body:
Fixes #4325.

## Problem
`envelope.WriteError` maps any non-`apierr` error to `INTERNAL_ERROR`/500. So transient SQLite busy/locked contention and server-side deadlines surface as genuine server faults — inflating the 5xx surface and making the true cause indistinguishable from a real bug.

## Change
- `apierr.KindUnavailable` (503) + `apierr.Unavailable(...)`.
- In `WriteError`, before the 500 fallback, detect transient conditions and return a typed **503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`** (retryable):
  - SQLite busy/locked, matched **structurally** via a `Code() int` method (primary code `5`/`6` or extended code low-byte), so `httpd/envelope` takes **no dependency** on the DB driver.
  - server-side `context.DeadlineExceeded`.
  - client `context.Canceled` is **excluded** on purpose (the response never reaches that caller; not retryable).

## Verification
- Real socket: a `database is locked` (Code 5) error returned via the production `WriteError` path yields `HTTP 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` across repeated attempts.
- Unit tests: busy / locked / extended-code / wrapped / deadline / `apierr.Unavailable` -> 503; plain error / non-busy sqlite code (constraint) / `context.Canceled` / `apierr.Internal` -> 500; existing typed kinds (400/404/409/403) unchanged. Run deterministically at `-count=100`.
- Full `internal/httpd/...` suite passes (no spec drift).

## Scope
Pure daemon HTTP classification. No route/DTO changes. Companion to #3963 (the DB contention this reclassifies) and #4323 (the SSE reconnect amplifier); #4180/#4181 (Sentry) give the remaining genuine 500s a grouped stack.

title: bug(daemon): schema drift is swallowed into a WARN while /readyz reports ready, turning ao spawn into an opaque INTERNAL_ERROR
body:
## Summary

When the physical schema drifts from what `goose_db_version` claims is applied, the daemon swallows the failure into a single startup `WARN`, keeps reporting `healthz: ok` / `readyz: ready`, and `ao spawn` — the product's core function — fails with a bare `Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR)` and no path to the cause.

This is not a report about *how* a schema drift happens (that mechanism is #3476). It is about the daemon's reaction to a drift that already exists: three independent design choices compound into an unrecoverable-looking failure with no diagnostic surface.

## Steps to reproduce

Any database where an object is missing while its migration version is recorded as applied reproduces this. On a **copy** of a dev `ao.db`:

1. Drop an object that a later code path depends on, leaving `goose_db_version` untouched:
   ```sql
   DROP TABLE agent_inventory_cache;
   ```
2. Restart the daemon.
3. `ao status` → reports `healthz: ok`, `readyz: ready`.
4. `ao spawn --project <id> --name <name> --kind worker`

The same shape reproduces with any other drifted object; #3476 documents an independent instance on `sessions.diff_base_sha` / `diff_base_ref` reached through migration-version collision rather than a manual drop.

## Expected behavior

A daemon whose schema cannot support its core workflow should either refuse to come up, or report itself as not ready — and the resulting CLI failure should name the actual problem (missing table/column, schema out of sync) rather than `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Actual behavior

The daemon starts, reports healthy, and spawn fails opaquely.

**Startup — the only trace of a broken schema, at WARN level:**

```
level=WARN msg="initial agent catalog refresh failed"
  err="upsert agent inventory cache: SQL logic error: no such table: agent_inventory_cache (1)"
```

**Health probes, after that warning:**

```
AO daemon: ready
  healthz: ok
  readyz: ready
```

**Spawn:**

```
$ ao spawn --project <id> --name <name> --kind worker
Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR) [request <id>]
```

**Daemon log for that request:**

```
method=POST path=/api/v1/agents/refresh status=500
  error="upsert agent inventory cache: SQL logic error: no such table: agent_inventory_cache (1)"
```

Nothing in the CLI output points to the schema; the operator only finds it by correlating a WARN emitted minutes earlier at startup.

### The three contributing defects

**1. A spawn-blocking dependency fails into a fire-and-forget WARN** — `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:275-279`:

```go
go func() {
    if _, err := agentSvc.Refresh(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Warn("initial agent catalog refresh failed", "err", err)
    }
}()
```

The agent catalog is not decorative: `ao spawn` calls `preflightSpawnAgentAuth` → `fetchAgentInventory(ctx, true)` → `POST /api/v1/agents/refresh` (`backend/internal/cli/spawn.go:376`, `:211`). A failure here means spawn cannot work, but nothing records that as a degraded state.

**2. `/readyz` reports readiness without checking anything** — `backend/internal/httpd/router.go:93`:

```go
r.Get("/readyz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
    envelope.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, daemonProbePayload("ready", cfg))
})
```

The shared payload helper states the assumption explicitly (`router.go:317-319`):

> `daemonProbePayload` is shared by `/healthz` and `/readyz`. Dependency initialization happens before the server is constructed, so a listening daemon is ready to answer requests.

That assumption does not hold: initialization already tolerates a failed dependency (defect 1), so "the socket is bound" and "the daemon works" have diverged. This matters beyond triage — #4324 proposes gating client API calls on `/readyz`, which only helps if the probe can distinguish a working daemon from a broken one.

**3. A cache-write failure discards an already-successful probe** — `backend/internal/service/agent/service.go:253-260`:

```go
if s.inventoryCache != nil {
    data, err := json.Marshal(cachedInventory{Installed: next.Installed, Authorized: next.Authorized})
    if err != nil {
        return next, fmt.Errorf("encode agent inventory cache: %w", err)
    }
    if err := s.inventoryCache.UpsertAgentInventoryCache(ctx, string(data), time.Now().UTC()); err != nil {
        return next, err
    }
}
```

At this point `next` is fully computed — every agent has been probed successfully. The result is discarded because a *cache* write failed. The same function already applies the opposite principle to the cache **read** a few lines earlier (`service.go:206-208`):

> A persisted snapshot makes `List` useful immediately after restart. A corrupt or temporarily unavailable cache must not prevent a fresh system probe from repairing it, so `Refresh` deliberately continues when this read fails.

The write path does not honour that same rule.

## AO version

Self-built from upstream `6cba6344c` (`ao version dev`).

## Environment

macOS 26.x arm64.

## Logs / extra context

### Suggested direction

These align with the fix requirements already articulated in #3476, generalized past the specific columns in that report:

1. **Startup schema reconciliation** — verify that the physical objects generated queries depend on actually exist, instead of trusting `goose_db_version` as the sole source of truth. A version marked applied is evidence about a ledger, not about a schema.
2. **Make `/readyz` mean something** — have it reflect that verification rather than the fact that a socket is bound. This is a prerequisite for #4324's proposal to be useful.
3. **Degrade instead of discarding a good result** — in `agents/refresh`, return the computed inventory when only the cache persist fails. A degradation pattern for exactly this situation already exists in the CLI (`agentProbeUnavailable` → warn and continue, `backend/internal/cli/spawn.go:384-389`); the service path can follow it.
4. **Surface schema mismatches as actionable errors** — a missing table or column should produce a message naming it, not `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

### Related

- #3476 — an independent instance of the same failure class (`sessions.diff_base_*` via migration-version collision). Its Impact section notes the misleading `readyz` in passing; this issue is about that behaviour as the defect, and holds regardless of how a given database drifted.
- #4324 — proposes gating clients on `/readyz`, which depends on the probe being meaningful.

title: fix(storage): recreate tables and columns skipped by burned migration versions
body:
## What

`reconcileSchema` (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go`) only verified **columns** from the manual `schemaRepairs` list, via `pragma_table_info`. A whole missing **table** (or a column outside the list) passed the boot check as healthy: the daemon came up green, and the first query against the missing object 500'd — for `agent_inventory_cache` that is every `ao spawn` (`INTERNAL_ERROR`) while `/readyz` stays ready.

This adds:
1. `tableRepairs` — a table-level counterpart to `schemaRepairs`, checked against `sqlite_master` and recreated when absent (idempotent, same as the column path).
2. Repair entries for the two drift casualties found in the field:
   - `0104` `agent_inventory_cache` (whole table missing)
   - `0106` `pr_comment.review_id` (column missing; `preparePRCommentReviewIDMigration` only repaired the mirror case — column present, ledger entry missing)

## Why

Part of #4335: a schema drift must not survive into a green daemon whose core workflow (`ao spawn`) 500s. This is the reconciliation gap, not the WARN/`/readyz` items the issue also lists — those are separate follow-ups.

## Red → green

`TestMigrateReconcilesMissingInventoryCacheTable` and `TestMigrateReconcilesMissingPRCommentReviewIDColumn` simulate the drift by burning the version (`INSERT INTO goose_db_version`) and requiring `migrate()` to leave the object present. Both failed before the fix, pass after. Both are killed by removing their repair entry (mutation check).

title: Orchestrators have no way to learn that a delegated worker finished its turn
body:
Title: Orchestrators have no way to learn that a delegated worker finished its turn

## Use case

Operator delegates a task from the project orchestrator (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`). The spawned worker completes its work — commits sitting on its `ao/<project>/<session>/root` branch — and then nothing happens until a human notices. In our session the orchestrator itself said it had to poll (`ao session get`) to discover its delegate was done. For an orchestration product, the orchestrator being the last to know is the expensive case: the whole point of delegation is that the planner picks the thread back up when the worker stops.

What exists today:

- `turn_complete` notifications reach the **human's** NotificationCenter (#4267). They do not reach any session.
- `DelegateTaskOutcome.OrchestratorID` records which orchestrator spawned the worker — but as far as I can find, **nothing consumes it**. It's bookkeeping metadata.
- W4's orchestrator view lists spawned workers with live state, but only when the human is looking at it.

## Design space

Three shapes this could take, roughly increasing in ambition:

1. **UI-level only.** Surface delegate completion more prominently (badge/ping) on the orchestrator destination view. No daemon semantics change; the orchestrator agent still learns nothing until prompted.
2. **Message injection.** When a delegate goes idle, deliver a system message into the orchestrator session's chat driver (the same path `ao send` uses), e.g. `worker <id> finished: N commits on <branch>`. The orchestrator can then react autonomously — review the diff, ask for a PR, report back. This is what made our workflow feel broken without it: the planner wanted to act on completion but had no event to act on.
3. **Session-addressable notifications.** Generalize the notification model so sessions can be subscribers/route targets. Most flexible, most machinery.

We lean toward **2**: it reuses an existing, proven transport (`ao send` into the chat driver), keeps the notification model untouched, and matches the mental model that the orchestrator is an agent, not just a view. Concerns we'd want the maintainers' read on:

- **Loop safety.** An orchestrator that reacts by delegating again must not create ping-pong; some depth/reentrancy guard seems wise.
- **Terminated/exited delegates.** Should the ping distinguish "finished cleanly" from "process died"? Lifecycle already has both facts.
- **Chat-driver availability.** Orchestrators exist only with a chat driver configured, so transport-2 has no fallback problem — but corrections welcome.

Is there a prior decision here we should know about — e.g. a deliberate choice to keep sessions out of the notification graph? Happy to turn whichever shape you prefer into a spec/PR.

title: fix(renderer): exponential backoff + jitter for workspace SSE reconnect (#4323)
body:
Fixes #4323.

## Problem
`workspace-file-events.ts` retried the SSE stream on a **fixed 5s interval** with no backoff, no ceiling reset, and no cap. A session whose stream keeps failing (e.g. the daemon briefly returns 5xx under DB contention, #3963) reconnected every 5s indefinitely, and many streams reconnected in lockstep — turning a brief hiccup into a sustained reconnect load on the daemon.

## Change (renderer-only, complementary to #4230)
- New dependency-free `sse-backoff.ts` → `computeBackoffDelayMs(failures)`: exponential growth from **5s** to a **60s** ceiling, jitter in `[0.5, 1.0]` of the step (spreads concurrent reconnects), overflow-clamped.
- The stream tracks consecutive failures, backs off per retry, and **resets to a fast first retry on a successful open**.

## Verification
- Ran the actual helper **100×** with invariant checks: monotonic growth to the cap, never exceeds 60s, never below the jitter floor, high-count clamp (no overflow). Sample progression: `4157, 6698, 14280, 39890, 43711, 54303` ms (vs the old flat 5000).
- `sse-backoff.test.ts` (vitest) covers growth, ceiling, jitter band, clamp, and NaN/negative handling.

## Scope / limitation
Native `EventSource` does not expose the HTTP status on error, so "stop reconnecting on 4xx" cannot be done from the client alone — backoff is the client-side mitigation. Daemon-side error classification (transient → 503) is handled separately in #4325. This composes with #4230 (daemon-side SSE replay cap) rather than overlapping it.

title: Desktop startup waits on every agent authentication probe
body:
## Bug
Opening the desktop app can spend 2–10 seconds on the startup requirements screen while AO probes every installed agent CLI and its authentication status, even though startup only needs inexpensive executable-presence checks.

**Source:** [PR #4330](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4330) / teammate report by @ronishrohan
**Introduced by:** [PR #3825](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3825)
**Analyzed against:** `f20411d14`
**Priority:** P2 — significant startup degradation; the app eventually loads.
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction
1. Install several supported agent CLIs, including one whose auth-status command is slow or times out.
2. Start the desktop app.
3. Observe that the startup requirements gate remains pending until the slowest parallel agent/auth probe completes.

## Root Cause
`backend/internal/service/systemcheck/systemcheck.go` implements the startup harness requirement through `agent.Service.RefreshFresh`. That refresh fans out across every registered harness, resolves its binary, and invokes optional auth probes with timeouts up to 10 seconds. The renderer keeps `SessionsBoard` behind the requirements response, so this full catalog refresh is on the first-render critical path.

The daemon and renderer also each trigger eager full catalog refreshes during startup, duplicating work that agent-selection surfaces already know how to request on demand.

## Fix
- Make the startup harness requirement use a bounded executable-presence-only probe, without starting agent CLIs or checking auth.
- Stop eagerly refreshing the full agent inventory during daemon/shell startup.
- Keep full inventory/auth refreshes on the existing agent-selection surfaces (`refreshAgentsIfStale`).

## Impact
- Restores fast first render regardless of slow agent auth commands.
- Preserves install gating for git, tmux, and the presence of at least one supported agent executable.
- Auth remains advisory and refreshes when the user opens a surface where agent choice matters.

## Related
- [PR #3825](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3825) — introduced the startup requirements gate.
- [PR #4330](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4330) — teammate proposal that includes a binary-only startup probe plus broader startup layout/reconciliation changes.

title: fix(desktop): defer agent auth probes until selection
body:

This isolates the auth-probe regression from the broader startup reconciliation and layout changes proposed in #4330.
