title: feat(terminal): add native macOS PTY host
body:
## Summary

- launch new macOS TUI sessions in a detached native PTY host and stream raw terminal bytes over the existing loopback protocol
- preserve every persisted unprefixed macOS runtime handle on tmux; version only newly created direct-host handles
- retain styled viewport reads, process supervision, replay, resize, input, teardown, restart, daemon-restart recovery, and a tmux creation fallback
- serialize registry updates so concurrent host starts cannot lose recovery entries
- show macOS direct-terminal scrollback with a slim app-owned, draggable thumb that is not suppressed by the OS auto-hide preference
- hide the thumb for alternate-screen TUIs, so legacy tmux sessions keep their existing behavior and never gain misleading scrollback chrome

## Compatibility and rollout

- Existing macOS agent sessions are never migrated in place and continue through tmux.
- New macOS sessions use the native PTY host; a host startup failure falls back to tmux with an unprefixed handle.
- Linux remains on tmux and Windows remains on the existing ConPTY host.
- No dependency changes, xterm upgrade, or advanced wheel tuning are included.
- tmux remains available for legacy macOS handles and fallback.

## Verification

- `go test ./...`
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run` — 0 issues
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/runtimeselect`
- `go vet ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/runtimeselect ./internal/terminal`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- `npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx` — 61 passed
- focused Playwright scrollbar test — visible normal-buffer thumb, pointer drag, alternate-screen suppression
- real Electron macOS check — direct shell with 500 output lines, wheel scroll, thumb geometry, and pointer drag
- Windows amd64 cross-compile: conpty and runtimeselect tests
- Linux amd64 cross-compile: conpty tests
- macOS end-to-end host test: detached re-exec, real PTY, env propagation, input/output streaming, resize, request-context independence, and teardown

## Preview bug fix

- Fixes #4538: percent-decodes direct-host shell handles at the HTTP boundary, restoring close-button, Command-W, and rename behavior without changing persisted handles.
- Verified through the generated frontend client and the real isolated Electron UI; closing removes both the tab and its PTY.

## Preview polish follow-up

- Fixes [#4539](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4539): removes a closing terminal tab optimistically while retaining safe rollback when a live PTY fails to close.
- Removes the duplicate chat-terminal wrapper inset so TerminalPane remains the single owner of the left content gutter.
- Makes the macOS overlay thumb appear during scrolling or dragging and fade 700 ms after interaction goes idle; edge hover still exposes the draggable control.
- Adds mutation, idle-fade, and chat-layout regression coverage. The full renderer suite passes: 2,130 tests.
- Native isolated Electron verification measured the tab leaving the DOM before the 204 response and the thumb transitioning from visible during scrolling to fully hidden after idle.
- No dependencies changed.


## Immediate shell UX follow-up

- Publishes the shell returned by the open request directly into the terminal list, eliminating the extra list round trip before a new tab can render.
- Requests keyboard focus whenever an auxiliary shell becomes active, including shells inside Chat sessions.
- Removes a closing shell pill before an in-flight list query finishes cancelling, while preserving rollback for real close failures.
- Keeps replay coalescing and tail reveal intact but makes the replay cover permanently silent, so users never see `Loading latest output...`.
- Preserves native xterm normal-buffer wheel scrolling and the requestAnimationFrame-throttled macOS thumb; no wheel multiplier, xterm upgrade, or dependency change is included.
- Verification: frontend typecheck; focused terminal tests (263 passed); full renderer suite (152 files, 2,173 tests).



## Terminal search follow-up

- Adds an AO-native find overlay backed by the already-installed xterm SearchAddon; no dependency or transport changes.
- Opens from Command/Ctrl+F or the terminal context menu, searches incrementally, reports the active/total match count, and supports case-sensitive and regular-expression modes.
- Enter and Shift+Enter, Command/Ctrl+G and Command/Ctrl+Shift+G, or visible previous/next buttons navigate matches; Escape and the close button clear decorations and return focus to the terminal.
- Validates regular expressions before search and contains the known xterm narrow-grid decoration exception so a search cannot take down the terminal surface.
- Adds localized UI strings for all eight AO locales.
- Verification: frontend typecheck; targeted terminal/i18n tests (81 passed); full renderer suite (152 files, 2,180 tests).

title: feat(mobile): over-the-air JS updates via EAS Update
body:
## What

Adds `expo-updates` + EAS Update so JS-only changes reach installed builds without a store release. Native changes still go through the store.

- Cold start: checks in the background, applies on the next launch. Never blocks the splash.
- Back from 15+ minutes in the background: applies a downloaded update (a JS reload; sessions live in the daemon), otherwise checks silently. Same as Bluesky / CodePush `ON_NEXT_RESUME`. Shorter absences do nothing, so nobody is reloaded mid-prompt. No banner.
- Settings → About → App updates: manual check / restart. Version row and bug reports now carry update id, channel and runtime; the build number is read from the binary (with `appVersionSource: remote` the old row had none).
- Dev builds: `expo-updates` is disabled, so all of this is inert.

## Runtime version

`fingerprint` rather than `appVersion`: native modules have landed on `main` between version stamps, and a fingerprint makes any native change a new runtime automatically, so an update can't reach a build that lacks the native code it calls. `fingerprint.config.js` ignores `google-services.json`, which is gitignored and differs between a laptop, CI and EAS Build; without that the Android hash differs per machine. Verified with `runtimeversion:resolve`.

## Privacy

Each check sends platform, runtime, channel, current update id and a random per-install UUID (`EAS-Client-ID`) to `u.expo.dev`. No user or daemon data. The store privacy policy should name Expo before the next store build.

## Activation

Nothing happens until a build with this config exists. Publishing is a local, deliberate step (`eas update --channel <c> --environment <c> -m "..."`, see the README); there is no CI publish and no Expo token in the repo.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (495, 18 new); `npx expo export` for both platforms
- Release builds on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator, against a local expo-updates protocol server: cold-start download, applied on the next launch, still running after the server reports no update. On iOS a deliberately broken bundle rolled back to the embedded one.
- The Android build's runtime version matched `runtimeversion:resolve` (`2bdcb69b…`) with the placeholder `google-services.json` in place, so the ignore in `fingerprint.config.js` holds end to end
- Debug build: no requests, row reads "Off in development builds"
- Not tried on a device: the 15-minute resume path (unit-tested)

title: fix(observability): drop request-cancellation noise from daemon Sentry
body:
## Why

With daemon Sentry live, `context.Canceled` and `context.DeadlineExceeded` errors are the dominant, un-actionable churn in the issue feed (client/renderer disconnecting mid-request, or a request/op running past its deadline). They are not server bugs, and they bury the real faults.

## What

`CaptureHTTPError` now drops any error that is or wraps `context.Canceled` / `context.DeadlineExceeded` before capture, via a new `IsNoiseError` (`errors.Is`, so wrapped chains like `list prs for x: context canceled` and the bare `context deadlineExceededError` are both caught).

Genuine slow-path/contention stays observable elsewhere: the aggregated `ao.http.5xx` rollup still counts it, and retryable DB contention has the typed 503 path.

## Tests

- `IsNoiseError` over nil / plain fault / canceled / deadline / wrapped / deep-wrapped.
- Recording-transport test: three cancellation errors produce **zero** captured events; a genuine fault (`no such table: ...`) still reaches the wire.

Observed in production feed: `context canceled` / `context deadline exceeded` across `list prs`, `pr facts`, `skills/list`, `conversation`, and bare deadline errors — all now suppressed.

title: bug(workspacewatch): one-fd-per-directory watch exhausts the fd limit on large workspaces, aborting workspace/events with a 500
body:
## Summary

On a workspace with many directories, `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/events` fails with `watch workspace directory "...": open ...: too many open files` and the live-file SSE subscription never starts. The watcher registers one OS watch per directory (one fd on macOS/kqueue, one inotify watch on Linux), so a large tree (node_modules, vendored deps, a monorepo) exhausts the process/system fd limit.

## Root cause

`addInitialDirectories` (`backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go:152-193`) collects **every** directory in the workspace — for a git worktree, the directory of each `git ls-files` entry plus all ancestors; otherwise a full `filepath.WalkDir` — and calls `watcher.Add(dir)` on each with no bound on the count. fsnotify opens an fd per watched directory (kqueue) / consumes an inotify watch, so once the number of directories exceeds `RLIMIT_NOFILE` (or the inotify `max_user_watches`), `watcher.Add` returns `too many open files` (EMFILE/ENFILE). The loop returns on the **first** such failure (`watcher.go:186-192`); the untyped error reaches `streamWorkspaceChanges` (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:622`) -> `envelope.WriteError` -> 500, and the no-backoff EventSource reconnect (#4323) then retries in a loop.

## Reproduction (verified)

Create a git worktree with 400 directories each containing a tracked file, lower `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to 128 to model a daemon already near its ceiling (a real machine hits the macOS default of 256 with a typical `node_modules`), then call `workspacewatch.Watch(ctx, root)`:

```
watch workspace directory ".../pkg264": open .../pkg264: too many open files
```

The endpoint returns 500 and the subscription never establishes.

## Why it matters

Unlike #4414 (a single missing directory, fixable by skip-and-continue), skip-and-continue does **not** help here: the watcher fundamentally registers an unbounded number of per-directory watches, so any sufficiently large workspace fails, and the descriptor pressure can degrade the whole daemon/machine, not just this endpoint.

## Expected / options

- Bound the number of watches, or watch coarsely (watch the root recursively where the platform supports it, or watch a capped/most-relevant set and reconcile) rather than one-per-directory unbounded.
- At minimum, when `watcher.Add` fails with EMFILE/ENFILE, skip that directory and continue (partial coverage) instead of aborting the whole subscription with a 500, and return a typed degraded response rather than an untyped 500.

## Affected code

- `backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go:152-193`
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:622`
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope/envelope.go` (untyped error -> 500)

## Related

- #4414 (same watcher aborts on a single missing directory) — sibling root cause in the same loop.
- #4323 (no-backoff SSE reconnect amplifies a transient setup 5xx).
- #4325 (untyped service errors collapse to 500 INTERNAL_ERROR).

title: bug(observability): Sentry path scrubber leaks local paths containing spaces (e.g. iCloud "Mobile Documents")
body:
## Summary

The daemon Sentry path scrubber (`sentryobs.scrub`) fails to redact local filesystem paths that contain a **space**, so an error message referencing such a path ships the un-redacted tail off the machine. macOS iCloud Drive paths (`.../Library/Mobile Documents/...`) and any user directory with a space are affected.

## Root cause

`scrub` (`backend/internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go`) redacts home paths with `homePath = /(?:Users|home)/[^\s"']+`. The `[^\s"']+` character class stops at the first whitespace, so a path with a space is only partially matched: everything from the space onward survives.

## Reproduction (verified)

```
scrub(`... open /Users/aey/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/vault/rules.md: no such file`)
=> ... open [redacted-path] Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/vault/rules.md: no such file
```

The redaction stops at the space in `Mobile Documents`; the vault path — and implicitly the folder layout and which app the user runs — survives into the event payload.

## Why it matters

It defeats the deny-by-default privacy guarantee for any path containing a space, which is common on macOS (`~/Library/Mobile Documents/...` for iCloud Drive, plus user folders like `My Project`). Usernames, project names, and directory structure can reach the error backend.

## Expected

Redact home/user paths regardless of embedded spaces — anchor on the home/user prefix (and the macOS `.../Library/Mobile Documents/...` form) and consume to a real path boundary rather than the first space. Add scrub test cases for spaced paths.

## Affected code

- `backend/internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go` (the `homePath` / `winPath` regexes and `scrub`).

title: [Bug]: Killing a TUI session whose tmux is already gone returns HTTP 500
body:
## Bug

Closing or killing a TUI session whose tmux runtime is already gone (daemon restart, missing tmux session, inconclusive legacy-socket probe) returns HTTP 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` instead of marking the session terminated.

**Source:** live daemon reproduction (`ao session kill dse_today-6` and `dse_today-2/4/5`) | **Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc`
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Spawn TUI sessions (omp/grok).
2. Restart the daemon so their tmux sessions disappear (`tmux ls` has no matching sessions).
3. `ao session kill <id>` (or close the tab in the desktop UI).

Already-terminated chat sessions kill OK on the same daemon.

## Root Cause

`Manager.Kill` (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`) fails closed on:

- `runtime.Destroy` errors, including `ports.ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` from `tmux.socketForSession` when the private socket lacks the session and the legacy default socket cannot be inspected.
- `terminateNativeSession` errors (stale grok/prime native ids).

Unmapped errors become 500 via `toAPIError`. tmux `Destroy` already treats a missing session / unreachable server as success, but the probe-inconclusive path still 500s the whole kill. The session is never `MarkTerminated`, so the zombie tab stays on the board.

Telemetry fingerprint for `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/kill`: `aad9192f2c617588`.

## Expected

Kill is idempotent. Missing tmux, inconclusive probe, already-dead runtime, or failed native terminate must still `MarkTerminated` and return 200. Closing a zombie tab must never 500.

## Impact

- Users cannot close zombie TUI tabs after a daemon restart.
- Session list stays cluttered with live-looking sessions whose runtimes are gone.
- Chat kill is already best-effort and is not rewritten here.

## Related

- [#2701](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2701) — pre-tmux/legacy handle kill 500s (same symptom, different handle class).
- [#3475](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3475) — probe misreads must not be treated as per-session death for *liveness*; kill teardown is the inverse (user asked to terminate).

title: fix(session): make kill idempotent when runtime is already gone
body:
## What

Make kill, resume-agent, and orchestrator replacement succeed when the TUI runtime is already gone (missing tmux, stale private socket, missing default socket, inconclusive legacy probe, failed native terminate).

Fixes [#4481](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4481).

## Why

After a daemon restart, a project orchestrator (and other TUI sessions) whose tmux server is gone cannot be talked to, resumed, closed, or replaced:

- `POST /sessions/{id}/send` → 409 `AGENT_EXITED`
- `POST /sessions/{id}/resume-agent` → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` (fingerprint `f05be741f335dfad`)
- `POST /sessions/{id}/kill` → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` (fingerprint `aad9192f2c617588`)
- Spawn orchestrator without `clean` returns the zombie; restart (`clean=true`) hits the same Destroy 500.

Live repro: `ao-killfix-2` (grok TUI orchestrator, handle `ao-killfix-2`, no `ptyhost-v1:` prefix). Private socket `/tmp/tmux-501/ao` had no server; default socket was `error connecting ... (No such file or directory)`. `socketForSession` classified that as `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, so resume/kill/replace all 500ed.

## How

- tmux `socketForSession`: a missing legacy default socket (`error connecting ... no such file`) is both-sockets-gone, same as `no server running`. `IsAlive` then reports `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` instead of inconclusive. Transient `connection refused` is unchanged.
- tmux `Destroy` treats `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` / `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` as already-gone.
- `Kill` and `RetireForReplacement` log and continue on native-terminate failure and already-gone runtime Destroy, then still mark terminated.
- User-initiated `restartRuntime` (resume-agent) treats those runtime sentinels as "no existing runtime" and creates a replacement. Boot `reconcileLive` still refuses to recreate on `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`.

## Testing

```bash
cd backend && env -u AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME go test ./internal/session_manager ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux
```

Added/updated:

- `TestIsAliveReportsPrivateServerGoneAndLegacySocketAbsentAsUnavailable`
- `TestDestroyIsIdempotentWhenPrivateServerGoneAndLegacySocketAbsent`
- `TestResumeAgent_InconclusiveRuntimeProbeRecreates`
- `TestRestartRuntime_InconclusiveProbeCreatesReplacement`
- `TestRetireForReplacement_RuntimeProbeInconclusiveStillTerminates`
- `TestRetireForReplacement_NativeTerminationFailureStillTerminates`

Unexpected runtime destroy errors still leave the session active. Chat kill is not rewritten.

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: bug(release): manifest-less feed heads strand desktop update checks
body:
## Bug

A published desktop release can become the updater feed head without its channel manifests. Every installed client selecting that release then fails update checks until a later complete release displaces it. The app correctly surfaced the repeated-failure warning on this machine, but it could not determine whether a newer build existed.

**Observed:** 2026-08-26 19:57 IST (14:27 UTC), local installed AO desktop app  
**Installed app:** `0.12.8-nightly.202608250759`, packaged arm64 macOS app  
**Settings:** automatic updates enabled, `nightly` channel, no feature pin  
**Daemon identity:** bundled `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`, healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**OS:** macOS 27.0 (26A5388g), arm64  
**Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc` (`upstream/main`, 2026-08-26)  
**Root-cause confidence:** **High**

![Settings showing repeated update-check failures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-update-feed-head-missing-manifests-20260826/.issue-assets/update-feed-head-missing-manifests-20260826/update-check-failing.png)

## Reproduction / timeline

1. Install a packaged nightly and enable automatic updates on the `nightly` channel.
2. Publish a newer nightly release without `nightly.yml`, `nightly-mac.yml`, and `nightly-linux.yml`.
3. Leave the app running for at least three scheduled checks.
4. Open Settings → Updates.
5. The warning appears: “Update checks keep failing. The app can't tell whether a newer version is out.”

Concrete incident:

- `v0.12.8-nightly.202608252327` was published at `2026-08-25T23:43:08Z` with installers but **no updater manifests**.
- At screenshot time (`2026-08-26T14:27Z`), that manifest-less release was still the newest published nightly.
- `v0.12.8-nightly.202608261410` uploaded `nightly-mac.yml` at `14:31:41Z` and was published at `14:31:48Z`, about four minutes after the screenshot. The current nightly feed is therefore healthy and the exact incident self-healed when this later complete release displaced the bad head.
- Stable is still affected independently: current latest release `v0.12.7` has installers but no `latest.yml`, `latest-mac.yml`, or `latest-linux.yml`; `/releases/latest/download/latest-mac.yml` redirects to that release and returns 404.

## Root cause

The updater behavior and UI classification match the release state:

- `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts` counts consecutive automatic failures of any kind and stamps `checksFailing: true` after three. Manifest 404s intentionally do not set the separate `staleCheckNudge`, which is reserved for `net::ERR_*` and restart guidance.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx` renders the exact screenshot copy when `checksFailing` is true and `staleCheckNudge` is false.
- Nightly release creation is currently manual after `.github/workflows/frontend-nightly.yml` was removed in `939e0c975` / #3070. Manifest generation/upload is separable from publishing, so a release can be public and selected by clients while incomplete—or remain permanently incomplete.

This is a release-metadata publication failure, not local updater cache corruption, signing/install failure, wrong binary/port, or an auth problem. No updater state was deleted, no app was reinstalled/restarted, and no release state was mutated during triage.

## Impact

- All clients whose selected channel head lacks its platform manifest cannot discover updates.
- Automatic failures accumulate silently until the third failure; users can remain stranded between or beyond releases.
- Nightly recovered only because a later complete release was published. Stable remains unable to resolve its current macOS manifest.
- Workaround is operational rather than user-local: backfill the missing manifests or publish a complete newer release.

## Recommended next action

1. Backfill updater manifests for current stable `v0.12.7` and audit published nightly heads for missing manifests.
2. Merge and enable [PR #4464](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4464), which adds a nightly feed-head guard and already documents this failure class.
3. Make publication atomic from the client’s perspective: keep a release draft/non-discoverable until installers and all channel manifests are present and validated, then publish once.
4. Keep the client-side resolver defensive: skip draft or manifest-less prereleases and select the newest installable release (related [PR #4462](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4462)).
5. Add stable/nightly post-publish probes for every required manifest and alert immediately on 404.

## Related

- [PR #4464](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4464) — open nightly feed-head guard; directly addresses detection of this regression.
- [PR #4462](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4462) — open client hardening around draft/prerelease resolution.
- [#2220](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2220) — closed original absence of updater feed metadata; same user-visible boundary, different current release-process mechanism.
- [#2237](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2237) — closed feed publication blocked after installers were available.
- [#2270](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2270) — closed handling for manifest 404 errors.
- [PR #4397](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4397) — merged UI/failure counter that correctly exposed this incident.

title: bug(delegation): task-title control message pollutes orchestrator conversation and context
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Bug

Direct task delegation injects an internal `AO TASK TITLE UPDATE` instruction into the project orchestrator as an ordinary agent message. The message is visible in the human-facing orchestrator conversation/terminal, becomes provider transcript and context, and can overwrite the session's recorded latest user prompt. Naming a worker is internal coordination and must not consume or perturb the project orchestrator's conversation.

**Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc` (`upstream/main`, 2026-08-26)  
**Introduced by:** `753cacb4c8e980353474996e45a2b4e80d13cc3d` ([PR #3443](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3443), 2026-08-05)  
**Confidence:** **High** — exact construction and both Chat/TUI delivery paths traced; current tests explicitly assert the leaking send.

![AO TASK TITLE UPDATE rendered in the orchestrator conversation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-task-title-control-context-leak/.issue-assets/task-title-control-context-leak/ao-task-title-update-leak.png)

## Reproduction

1. Have a project with a running, exited, or absent orchestrator.
2. Create a direct task through the desktop New Task composer (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`) with a nonblank brief.
3. AO spawns the worker immediately.
4. In the background, AO selects the newest running project orchestrator, resumes the newest exited orchestrator, or spawns a new orchestrator solely for title refinement.
5. Once message delivery is ready, AO sends this into the orchestrator agent:

```text
AO TASK TITLE UPDATE
A worker was already spawned directly with the user's task. Do not spawn another worker or orchestrator, and do not implement the task in this orchestrator session.
Choose a concise task title from the brief and run:

 ao session rename <worker-id> "<title, max 20 chars>"
```

Promptless delegated workers are the exception: an empty brief skips title refinement. Readiness, resume, or send failures can also prevent delivery. Otherwise every direct delegation with a brief attempts this injection.

## Expected behavior

After direct delegation spawns the worker, **that spawned worker** should choose and apply its own concise title with:

```text
ao session rename <its-own-session-id> "<title, max 20 chars>"
```

The project orchestrator must never receive title-control text and must never be spawned, resumed, or woken for naming.

## Actual behavior and source evidence

### Delegation deliberately targets the project orchestrator

`backend/internal/service/session/delegation.go`:

- `DelegateTask` spawns the worker, then calls `refineDelegatedTaskTitleInBackground` for every nonblank prompt (`:44-86`).
- `refineDelegatedTaskTitle` resolves a project orchestrator, waits for its input readiness, and calls `s.manager.Send(ctx, orchestratorID, taskTitleDelegationMessage(...), nil)` (`:89-124`).
- `taskTitleOrchestrator` chooses a running orchestrator, resumes an exited one, or calls `SpawnOrchestrator` when none exists (`:127-161`).
- `taskTitleDelegationMessage` constructs the exact screenshot text (`:175-191`). Git blame attributes that message to `753cacb4c8`; it remains verbatim on current `upstream/main`.

Later commits changed the mechanics but preserved the leak:

- `3934bc86a45ee5c8a2fc4299b9a04aefcae85548` ([PR #3627](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3627)) added the provisional 20-rune display name and made refinement best effort.
- `9c475bf718e81cbf82cc112b3d6aa113c0223623` ([PR #3657](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3657)) made refinement asynchronous and added orchestrator resume/create behavior.

### TUI mode: visible input, transcript/context, and prompt-metadata pollution

`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:2917-2983` routes `Manager.Send` through `prepareOutboundMessage` and `messenger.DeliverWithPostWrite`. `backend/internal/daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go:291-320` resolves the runtime handle and invokes `runtime.SendMessage`, which pastes/submits the text into the live TUI pane.

After delivery, `Manager.send` calls `RecordSessionLatestUserPrompt` with the control message (`manager.go:2971-2978`). This contradicts the domain contract in `backend/internal/domain/session.go:42-45`:

> `LatestUserPrompt` is the latest real user-authored task direction; internal AO coordination messages must not replace it.

Consequences:

- The control message is visible in the terminal transcript.
- The provider treats it as a user turn and includes it in future context.
- It can replace the real `LatestUserPrompt`, contaminating continuation/handoff facts.
- It wakes an otherwise idle orchestrator and spends a provider turn solely on naming.

### Chat mode: persisted visible conversation turn and provider input

`backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go:222-256` routes `Manager.Send` through `RelayChatTurn`. `backend/internal/service/chat/service.go:1175-1210` creates a `ChatUserMessage` with `Origin: automation`, but it remains a **user-role inbound turn**, is stored in the conversation, and is dispatched to the provider.

Automation attribution does not make the message internal or invisible. `TestRelayedMessageIsAttributedToAutomation` (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller_test.go:3181-3205`) explicitly asserts that the message appears in the conversation snapshot and that the provider receives the exact text.

## Current tests protect the leak

`TestDelegateTaskSpawnsWorkerThenRequestsTitleFromNewestActiveOrchestrator` in `backend/internal/service/session/delegation_test.go:14-80` asserts that:

- the title request is sent to `orch-new`;
- delivery readiness is awaited for that orchestrator;
- the sent message contains `AO TASK TITLE UPDATE`;
- it contains “Do not spawn another worker or orchestrator”;
- it instructs `ao session rename mer-9 ...` and includes the worker brief.

Other tests explicitly require the current orchestration side effects:

- `TestDelegateTaskResumesNewestExitedOrchestratorBeforeRequestingTitle`
- `TestDelegateTaskStartsMissingOrchestratorBeforeRequestingTitle`
- readiness/send failure and asynchronous-return tests

These tests need to be inverted around the decided worker-self-rename behavior.

## Decided behavioral boundary

The session service may coordinate naming with the **newly spawned worker only**. It must not use the project orchestrator as a title generator or command executor.

After worker spawn:

1. Ask the spawned worker to derive a concise title from its own task brief.
2. Instruct it to run `ao session rename <its-own-id> "<title, max 20 chars>"`.
3. Keep the existing provisional `delegatedTaskDisplayName` as the immediate/failure-safe label.
4. Treat worker self-rename as best effort and never roll back a successful worker spawn if naming fails.
5. Do not discover, spawn, resume, wake, wait on, or message a project orchestrator for naming.

This boundary belongs in `backend/internal/service/session/delegation.go` and the worker-spawn/prompt handoff. Hiding automation rows in the renderer is not a fix: the provider would still receive and retain the control message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A nonblank direct delegation spawns exactly one worker with the user's task and provisional display name.
- [ ] The spawned worker receives a bounded internal title instruction identifying its own session ID and the 20-character limit.
- [ ] The worker—not a project orchestrator—runs or is asked to run `ao session rename` for itself.
- [ ] No title-control message is sent to any project orchestrator in Chat or TUI mode.
- [ ] Naming does not list/select an orchestrator, call `SpawnOrchestrator`, resume an exited orchestrator, wait for orchestrator message readiness, or wake an idle orchestrator.
- [ ] The human-facing orchestrator conversation, terminal transcript, provider context, and `LatestUserPrompt` remain unchanged after direct delegation.
- [ ] Naming failure remains non-fatal after the worker-spawn commit point; the provisional title remains usable.
- [ ] Promptless worker behavior remains intentional and covered.
- [ ] `OrchestratorID` remains empty on the delegate response unless the wire field is removed through a compatible API change.

## Required tests

- Service test: direct delegation records one worker spawn and **zero** orchestrator spawn/resume/readiness/send calls.
- Targeting test: title instruction references the spawned worker ID and is delivered only through the worker-owned startup/self-rename path.
- TUI regression test: `AO TASK TITLE UPDATE` never reaches the orchestrator runtime messenger and never replaces its `LatestUserPrompt`.
- Chat regression test: no title-control message appears in the orchestrator conversation snapshot and no such text reaches the orchestrator provider.
- Failure test: worker title/self-rename failure does not fail or terminate the successfully spawned worker and leaves the provisional display name intact.
- Promptless test: preserve the explicitly chosen behavior for an empty brief without contacting an orchestrator.

## Impact

- Every ordinary direct delegation can add irrelevant control text to a human conversation and provider transcript.
- The orchestrator may be created or resumed solely to rename another session.
- Provider context and tokens are consumed for internal UI metadata.
- `LatestUserPrompt` can cease to represent the human's latest direction, degrading continuation and agent-switch handoffs.
- The control turn can interrupt or distract subsequent orchestration work.

## Related

- [#3912](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3912) — same naming flow, but tracks ugly provisional titles and silent refinement failure rather than context leakage.
- [#3911](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3911) — missing/invalid worker names on orchestrator-driven `ao spawn`.
- [PR #3443](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3443) — introduced the direct-delegation title message.
- [PR #3627](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3627) — added provisional titles/best-effort refinement.
- [PR #3657](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3657) — moved refinement to background and added orchestrator resume/create.

title: fix(session): keep delegated title control on worker
body:
Fixes #4489

Issue: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4489

## Summary

Direct task delegation now asks the spawned worker to choose and apply its own title through a trusted startup instruction. It no longer selects, wakes, or sends a title-control message to a project orchestrator. The original task brief remains the worker's user-facing prompt, and the provisional display name remains the fallback if self-renaming is unavailable. Promptless and ordinary spawns do not receive this instruction.

The worker uses `ao session rename` with `--if-current-display-name`. The optional `expectedDisplayName` field on the session rename API makes the update conditional, so a delayed worker rename cannot overwrite a title the user has changed. Existing rename requests that omit this field keep their current behavior.

title: feat(onboarding): infer worker and orchestrator defaults from role-specific usage
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Enhancement

New-project onboarding currently defaults both **Worker agent** and **Orchestrator agent** to the same generic authorized-agent choice. It should instead infer each role's default independently from the user's actual AO session history.

**Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc` (`upstream/main`, 2026-08-26)

![Worker and orchestrator agent defaults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-role-aware-agent-defaults/.issue-assets/role-aware-agent-defaults/project-agent-defaults.png)

## Current behavior

When the create-project agent sheet opens, it computes one `defaultAuthorizedAgent(...)` result from the available agent catalog and assigns that same agent to both roles. This commonly produces Claude Code for both fields regardless of which harnesses the user actually uses for workers and orchestrators.

## Desired behavior

Choose defaults independently for the worker and orchestrator roles:

1. Count the harness used by existing sessions of that role.
2. Select the most frequently used eligible harness for that role.
3. If multiple harnesses have the same highest count, select whichever tied harness was used by the most recently spawned session of that role.
4. If no session history exists for that role, default to Claude Code.

Examples:

- Worker history: 5 Codex, 2 Claude Code → default worker to Codex.
- Orchestrator history: 2 Claude Code, 2 Codex, with the newest tied session using Codex → default orchestrator to Codex.
- Orchestrator history: 2 Kimi, 2 Codex, with Codex used more recently → default orchestrator to Codex.
- No orchestrator sessions yet → default orchestrator to Claude Code.

Only installed/authorized agents that can currently be selected should become defaults. If the historical winner is unavailable, continue through the same frequency/recency ordering among eligible agents before using Claude Code as the final fallback.

The inference applies only while the user has not manually changed the field. Existing touched-field behavior must remain: asynchronous catalog/history refreshes must never overwrite an explicit user selection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Worker and orchestrator defaults are inferred independently.
- [ ] The most-used eligible harness wins for each role.
- [ ] Equal counts are broken by the newest spawned session among the tied harnesses.
- [ ] With no eligible history for a role, Claude Code is selected when available.
- [ ] If Claude Code is unavailable, onboarding remains usable by selecting the next valid authorized fallback rather than producing an invalid value.
- [ ] Manual selections are never replaced by a later refresh.
- [ ] Tests cover unequal counts, equal-count recency, separate role histories, unavailable historical winners, empty history, and touched fields.

## Scope

This changes only the initial suggestion shown during new-project onboarding. It does not alter existing project configuration or automatically rewrite saved worker/orchestrator defaults.

title: fix(onboarding): default clones to AO repos and preflight destination collisions
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Bug

Repository cloning has no automatic destination and reports a predictable destination-name collision only after the user advances through setup and attempts the final clone operation.

**Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc` (`upstream/main`, 2026-08-26)  
**Confidence:** High — the frontend destination picker performs no target preflight, while the clone service checks `<parent>/<repository-name>` only during the final clone request.

![Clone destination collision shown after final submission](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-clone-destination-preflight/.issue-assets/clone-destination-preflight/clone-destination-exists.png)

## Current behavior

- Clone onboarding requires the user to choose a destination parent explicitly.
- The UI previews the derived target path but does not check whether it already exists.
- The user can continue to agent selection and invoke the final create/start action.
- Only then does the backend return `CLONE_DESTINATION_EXISTS`: “A folder with this repository name already exists in the selected destination.”

## Desired behavior

### Default destination

When the user does not choose a path, default repository clones to:

```text
~/.ao/repos/<repository-name>
```

Resolve this through AO's shared data/home configuration so supported data-directory overrides and cross-platform path rules are respected; do not hard-code a Unix-only string in the renderer.

### Early collision validation

As soon as both the repository URL and destination parent are known—and especially immediately after the user chooses a destination folder—preflight the derived `<destination>/<repository-name>` target.

If that target already exists:

- Show the collision inline in the clone-details step.
- Identify the exact conflicting target path.
- Keep **Continue** disabled until the URL or destination changes to a valid target.
- Do not make the user continue to agent selection or click the final create/start action to discover the conflict.

The backend must retain its authoritative collision check at clone time to prevent time-of-check/time-of-use races. Early validation improves feedback; it does not replace safe server-side enforcement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening clone onboarding without a previously chosen destination defaults to AO's configured repos directory, normally `~/.ao/repos/`.
- [ ] The default directory is created safely when needed through the daemon/config boundary.
- [ ] URL changes recompute and validate the derived repository target.
- [ ] Choosing a destination immediately validates the derived target before advancing.
- [ ] An existing target produces an inline error with the conflicting path and disables Continue.
- [ ] Changing to a non-conflicting URL or destination clears the error and re-enables Continue.
- [ ] The final backend clone operation still rejects a destination that becomes occupied after preflight.
- [ ] Tests cover the default path, data-directory override, existing target, valid target, URL change, destination change, inaccessible destination, cancellation, and the final race check.

## Scope

This does not overwrite, merge into, rename, delete, or automatically reuse an existing destination folder.

title: fix(scm/github): make rate-limit errors trigger observer cooldown
body:
GitHub `RateLimitError` exposed `ResetAt`/`RetryAfter` as fields but not methods, so the observer's `errors.As` (which needs `GetRetryAfter()`/`GetResetAt()`) never matched for GitHub. Result: a GitHub rate-limit never triggers the bounded cooldown and the daemon keeps polling every 30s, worsening exhaustion. GitLab already implements the interface, so the fleet degrades asymmetrically. Masked in tests by a local double that implements the getters.

Fix: add the two getters mirroring `gitlab/client.go`, plus a regression test that a real `*github.RateLimitError` satisfies the observer's cooldown contract via `errors.As`.

Found in the pre-10k QA audit (finding GH-1).

title: fix(gitworktree): retry worktree removal on macOS/Linux, not only Windows
body:
The bounded worktree-remove retry was gated to Windows (`removeAllRetryEnabled = runtime.GOOS == "windows"`), but the transient race it absorbs is not Windows-only. On macOS/Linux a just-killed agent child can still hold the worktree dir briefly after `ao session kill` destroys its shells, so `os.RemoveAll` fails with a transient `unlinkat` EACCES/ENOTEMPTY/EBUSY. Gated to Windows, that stranded the worktree and returned a 500 on Unix.

Observed in production as `kill X: gitworktree: remove unregistered path: unlinkat ...` and `retire replacement: force destroy` (the two are among the top daemon errors).

Fix: default the retry on for every platform. The ctx-bounded ~7.25s budget and the early ErrNotExist exit are unchanged; a caller that gives up cancels ctx. The var is kept so tests still exercise the disabled path; drops the now-unused `runtime` import; adds a guard test that the default stays enabled.

QA audit finding SESS-1.

title: fix(session): map ErrNoController to a typed 409 on the send path, not a raw 500
body:
A send to a session whose chat controller is not live (daemon just restarted, controller stopped, mid-reconnect) returned `chatsvc.ErrNoController`, which had no case in `toAPIError` and fell through to a raw 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`, shipping `send <id>: no live chat controller for session` to the client and Sentry. The conversation-send path already maps this to 409 `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`; the session-send path (orchestrator relay, `ao send`) diverged.

Fix: add the `ErrNoController` case to `toAPIError` returning the same typed 409, plus a regression test. No import cycle (service/chat does not import service/session).

QA audit finding CHAT-1 (production error AO-DESKTOP-5).

title: bug(terminal): high-output flood tears down the whole terminal WebSocket (crash loop)
body:
## Summary
A high-output command in an attached terminal (a build, `yes`, a verbose test run) tears down the entire terminal WebSocket, then reattaches, replays, floods again, and dies: a crash loop.

## Root cause
`attachment.copyOut` reads 32KB chunks (`backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go:191-204`) into `connState.enqueue` (`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:529-535`) on a 1024-frame channel (`defaultWriteBuffer`, `manager.go:36`). On overflow the `default` branch calls `c.cancel()` (`manager.go:533`), tearing down the whole connection and every pane on it. The PTY read loop never blocks, so there is no upstream backpressure; a flood fills 1024 frames faster than JSON+base64 WS writes drain.

## Expected
Coalesce/drop data frames (the client only needs the latest output), or apply flow control (stop reading the attach PTY so tmux/conpty throttles) instead of killing the connection.

## Suggested fix
On a full buffer, coalesce consecutive `msgData` frames for the same terminal id into the tail rather than cancelling; or batch multiple 32KB reads into one frame in `copyOut` as a stopgap.

## Notes
UNTESTED live (needs a running daemon+renderer); verified from code. QA audit finding TERM-1. Effort: 30-min stopgap, ~2-4h correct. Scaling risk: high.

title: bug(browser-preview): managed preview dev-server crash is invisible in the panel
body:
## Summary
When a managed preview dev-server crashes after launch, the Browser panel keeps showing the stale page with no error; `ao preview status` later reports plain `stopped`.

## Root cause
`waitForExit` flips the run to `StateFailed` (`backend/internal/previewserver/manager.go:499-506`) but does not call `SetPreview("")` and emits no event. The panel's only failure hook, `did-fail-load` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:1828`), fires on navigation, not on an already-rendered page whose backing server dies. After `failedStatusRetention` (5 min) the failed run is deleted (`manager.go:511-518`), so status then reports `stopped` with no error.

## Expected
On a non-stopping exit, clear/mark the session preview so the panel shows a dead-server state.

## Suggested fix
Add an `onExit(sessionID, Status)` callback to `Manager`, call it from `waitForExit` when `!run.stopping`, and wire it to `SetPreview(ctx, id, "")`; SSE already fans session updates to the renderer.

## Notes
UNTESTED live; verified from code. QA audit finding PREV-1. Effort: ~30 min detection, +1-2h for a polished panel state. Scaling risk: high.

title: bug(installer): macOS signing/notarization is fail-open; auto-update zip has no partial-credential guard
body:
## Summary
macOS signing/notarization is fail-open, and the auto-update zip has no partial-credential guard, so a misconfigured secret ships an unsigned, un-notarized update that Gatekeeper blocks on first run.

## Root cause
`osxSign`/`osxNotarize` are set only when Apple env vars are present, else `undefined` (`frontend/forge.config.ts:75-92`), and the build does not fail. The DMG maker refuses partial credentials (`frontend/makers/maker-dmg.ts:150-203`) but the zip path (the auto-update artifact) has no equivalent guard. No `hardenedRuntime`/entitlements are pinned in config (relies on `@electron/osx-sign` defaults).

## Expected
Fail the release build when signing/notarization resolves to `undefined` on the release path; pin `hardenedRuntime` and an entitlements file.

## Suggested fix
Mirror the DMG maker's partial-credential refusal in the zip maker; add `hardenedRuntime: true` plus an entitlements plist.

## Notes
UNTESTED against a produced artifact; verified from config. QA audit finding INST-1. Effort: 0.5-1 day. Scaling risk: critical.

title: bug(installer): Windows builds are entirely unsigned (SmartScreen first-run block)
body:
## Summary
Windows installers ship entirely unsigned, so Defender SmartScreen shows "unknown publisher" on first run and keeps warning until reputation accrues (slow-to-never for unsigned binaries). At 10k users this is a large first-run drop-off.

## Root cause
`frontend/makers/maker-nsis.ts:39-80` has no `certificateFile`/`signtool`/Azure Trusted Signing/sign hook, and neither CI workflow carries Windows signing secrets. Target is NSIS only.

## Expected
Sign the Windows installer (EV certificate or Azure Trusted Signing).

## Suggested fix
Add Windows code signing to the NSIS maker plus the release workflow. Bulk of the effort is certificate procurement.

## Notes
UNTESTED (needs Windows first-run); verified from config. QA audit finding INST-2. Effort: days (mostly procurement). Scaling risk: critical.

title: bug(installer): no DB downgrade protection and /readyz always returns 200
body:
## Summary
There is no schema/app-version downgrade protection on `~/.ao/ao.db`, and `/readyz` always returns 200, so an older app or the frozen npm CLI's daemon can open a DB migrated forward by a newer desktop app and run against a schema it does not fully understand. This is the mechanism behind the schema-drift 500s (#4335, #3476, #4415).

## Root cause
Migrations run with `goose.Up(db, "migrations", goose.WithAllowMissing())` (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go:162`) and nothing stamps or checks an app/schema version. `/readyz` is an unconditional 200 (`backend/internal/httpd/router.go:93-95`) and never probes schema health, so drift is invisible.

## Expected
Stamp an app/schema version in the DB, refuse to open a DB stamped newer than the running binary with a clear error, and make `/readyz` probe schema health.

## Suggested fix
Add a `schema_app_version` row; on open, compare and refuse-newer; add a real schema probe to `/readyz`.

## Notes
UNTESTED against a real downgrade; verified from code. QA audit finding INST-3. Effort: ~1 day. Scaling risk: critical.

title: security(connect-mobile): LAN bridge is plaintext HTTP; bearer password sniffable on shared Wi-Fi
body:
## Summary
The Connect Mobile LAN bridge is plaintext HTTP bound to `0.0.0.0`, and the connection password rides as a `Bearer` header, so on any shared L2 network a passive sniffer captures the password from the first request. That password authorizes terminal input, spawn/kill, and PR actions. The docs say "do not use on public Wi-Fi," and users will.

## Root cause
`backend/internal/httpd/lan_listener.go:138` binds `0.0.0.0:<port>` and serves a plain `http.Server` with no TLS. The password is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <pw>` (`packages/mobile/lib/config.ts:29`), and `packages/mobile/app.json` sets `usesCleartextTraffic: true` / `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`.

## Expected
TLS on the LAN listener (self-signed cert pinned during pairing). Short of that, gate `Enable()` behind an explicit home-network confirmation and surface `mobileUnencryptedWarning` prominently in the mobile app, not only on desktop.

## Suggested fix
Add TLS to the LAN listener with a cert pinned at pairing time; until then make the plaintext warning blocking in the app.

## Notes
UNTESTED as a live capture; verified from code. QA audit finding MOB-1. Effort: warning ~0.5 day, TLS 2-4 days. Scaling risk: critical.

title: feat(windows,shell-terminals): selectable default shell for standalone terminals (Git Bash, PowerShell, cmd)
body:
## Feature Description

On Windows, standalone shell terminals always launch whichever shell the daemon finds first in a **hardcoded probe order** — `pwsh.exe` → `powershell.exe` → `ComSpec` → `cmd.exe`. There is no way for the user to choose a different default shell, and **Git Bash is never considered at all**.

Requested: a user-facing option (app setting and/or per-terminal picker) to select the default shell for standalone terminals, with Git Bash as a first-class choice alongside PowerShell / cmd.

## Current behavior (code anchors)

- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/loginshell.go` — `resolveUserLoginShell()` → `resolveWindowsShell()`: hardcoded candidate list `["pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe"]` then `ComSpec`/`cmd.exe` fallback. No user preference is consulted, no Git Bash probe (e.g. `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`), no override hook.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` — `OpenShellTerminalInput` has no shell/shellPath field, so `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` cannot express a shell choice per open request either.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` (`runLoginShell`, ~line 635) — login-shell env detection runs a shell too; a changed default should be honored consistently there.
- Unix already prefers `$SHELL` (`loginshell.go:24`), which is why this reads as Windows-only — but note the Unix sibling bug with non-POSIX shells: #3788 (fish).

## Motivation

- Reported by a Windows user who lives in Git Bash: **SahilG** in the `#feature-requests` Discord thread *"default terminal option"* — currently the **most upvoted feature request** there.
- Git Bash is a daily-driver shell for many Windows developers; getting PowerShell instead makes the standalone terminal pane a pane they immediately `exit` out of.
- PowerShell-first probe order also surprises cmd users the same way (SahilG perceived "only cmd is supported" — either way, the user loses).

## Proposed Solution

1. **Setting:** add a `shell` preference (e.g. `"auto" | "git-bash" | "pwsh" | "powershell" | "cmd" | custom path`) to app settings, surfaced in the desktop app's Settings UI.
2. **Resolution order:** `resolveUserLoginShell()` should consult the preference first; `"auto"` keeps today's behavior. Git Bash detection: `where git` → `<Git>\bin\bash.exe` (or `bash.exe` on PATH), launched with `--login -i`.
3. **Wire API:** optionally extend `OpenShellTerminalInput` with an optional per-request `shell` override so the UI can offer a per-terminal picker (⊞ new-terminal dropdown) without extra round-trips.
4. **Validation:** reject-with-message or fall back to `auto` when the configured shell path doesn't exist at open time (consistent with the "must not open something unusable" rule in `loginshell.go:17-19`).
5. **Regenerate API artifacts** (`npm run api`) if DTOs change.

## Alternatives Considered

- Environment-variable-only override (e.g. `AO_SHELL`) — cheap but undiscoverable; fine as a power-user extra, not a substitute for a setting.
- Doing nothing / documenting PowerShell-first — rejected: most-upvoted request, and the fix is well-bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Windows user can set Git Bash as the default shell; new standalone terminals launch in Git Bash (`--login -i`)
- [ ] PowerShell (pwsh + Windows PowerShell) and cmd remain selectable; `"auto"` preserves current behavior
- [ ] Custom shell path supported, with clear error/fallback when it's missing
- [ ] Preference honored by the login-shell env detection path (`runLoginShell`), not just terminal spawn
- [ ] Unix behavior unchanged (`$SHELL` still wins)
- [ ] OpenAPI spec + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated if request DTOs change

## Environment

- OS: Windows (feature is Windows-facing; Unix already honors `$SHELL`)
- Surface: standalone shell terminals (`/terminals` screen) — shellterm service → daemon → ConPTY

_Filed from Discord thread "default terminal option" (#feature-requests). Reporter: @SahilG; picked up by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari._

title: fix(observability): harden daemon Sentry capture (re-land #4352)
body:
Re-lands the daemon-Sentry hardening from #4352 that never reached main: a PR-head desync left #4346 merging the pre-hardening commit, so `origin/main` still has the shared-hub capture, double panic-capture, and all-503-suppressed policy. This is the exact verified change from that work, cherry-picked onto current main.

## Fixes
1. **Request-isolated hub.** `CaptureHTTPError`/`CapturePanic` used package-level `sentry.WithScope`/`CaptureException` on the process-global `CurrentHub`, so concurrent requests could interleave scope push/pop and stamp one request's request_id/fingerprint onto another's event. Each capture now resolves a hub from the request context or clones the current hub. Covered by a `-race` test that fails if reverted.
2. **Single panic capture.** The recover middleware captured a panic (fatal, with the Go stack) and the outer 5xx logger then manufactured a second generic `HTTP 500` event with a different fingerprint. Recovery now marks the request via a request-scoped flag and the logger skips its capture when set. Exactly one event, verified through a recording transport.
3. **Code-aware 503.** `ShouldCaptureStatus(status)` dropped every 503, but AO also uses 503 for typed outages (`SCM_UNAVAILABLE`, `BROWSER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`, `DEVICE_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE`). Replaced with `ShouldCapture(status, errorCode)`: only the deliberate `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` backpressure is suppressed.

Adds `Disable()` for shutdown/tests. All tests pass under `go test -race`.

Note: overlaps `internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go` with the noise-filter PR #4475; whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.

title: fix(observability): scrub local paths containing spaces
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4477.

The Sentry path scrubber stopped at whitespace, so local paths such as `~/Library/Mobile Documents/...` could leak the remainder of the path. The scrubber now handles spaces in Unix and Windows paths while preserving the existing error-message suffix behavior.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/observe/sentryobs`
- `gofmt -w internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs_test.go`
- `git diff --check`

The repository-wide `go test ./...` command was also run; it remains red on unrelated Windows/environment-sensitive tests and provider fixtures. `go test -race ./...` cannot start in this environment because CGO is disabled.

title: feat(preview): suggest detected ports in the Browser panel
body: ## What The Browser panel offers the ports a session is actually serving on, next to the address bar. Clicking one opens it the way `ao preview ` does. Same view from the CLI via `ao preview ports [--json]`. ## Why Finding a dev server's port meant reading it out of terminal scrollback and typing it into the address bar. ## How Detection is scoped to a session two ways, and a process qualifies on either: it descends from the session's root process, or its working directory is inside the session's worktree. Both are needed — the root process differs by mode (a tmux pane's shell for terminal sessions, the provider process for chat), and neither survives an agent backgrounding a dev server, since a detached process is reparented to init. The worktree does not move and belongs to one session. `internal/portscan` reads `/proc` on Linux and shells out to `lsof` elsewhere, then credits each port to the deepest process holding it — a server started from a shell is reported by every ancestor that inherited the descriptor. Everything fails open: a missing `lsof`, an unreadable process table, a permission denial, or a session with no live process all yield an empty list, never an error. Windows detects nothing for now (`portscan/windows.go`); its socket enumeration lands separately. `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/preview/ports` carries no capability header — it starts nothing — and is blocked on the LAN listener instead (`httpd/lan_listener.go:84`), so the list never leaves the machine. ## Testing `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test` pass on `internal/portscan`, `internal/cli`, `internal/httpd/...`, `internal/session_manager`. Cross-compiled `portscan` for `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=darwin`. `BrowserPanel.test.tsx` passes 58/58. Not verified in the running desktop app. ## When Server is not Live ## When Server is Live ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Feature]: Custom orchestrator harness
body:
### Problem

## Why this matters

- The orchestrator and worker do different jobs. Workers implement code. The orchestrator should coordinate workers, inspect state, notice collisions, and help the user make decisions.
- A custom harness can ask AO directly for worker state, PR state, review state, changed files, blockers, and dependencies instead of relying on terminal parsing or model inference.
- A dedicated orchestrator runtime gives AO room for differentiated capabilities such as conflict scanning, task graph inspection, shared worker views, and direct worker actions.


### Proposed direction

## Questions to answer

- What should the custom harness own versus what should stay in AO services?
- Should the first version be a thin wrapper over an open-source harness or a more opinionated AO-owned runtime?
- What minimum AO-native tools must exist before the harness becomes meaningfully better than prompt-only orchestration?

## Outcome

Define the first concrete plan for making the orchestrator a real runtime surface rather than a worker with special instructions.


### Alternatives considered

_No response_

- Shared context would let a new worker inherit project facts, recent decisions, rejected approaches, and task boundaries without repeating discovery.
- In team or Cloud settings, several humans and several workers may act in parallel on the same repository, so useful context should survive beyond one chat transcript.
- The orchestrator will make better decisions if it knows what has already been tried, what is blocked, which product decisions are still active, and which codebase areas are already owned.


### Proposed direction

- What information is safe and useful to persist versus too noisy or too risky to store?

title: [Feature]:  Support Artifacts Inside One AO Session
body:
# Session Artifacts

## TL;DR

We want AO sessions to produce a first-class `artifact`, not only a PR.

The design:

- the user starts a session normally
- AO creates a session-owned artifact directory under AO's data directory, outside the git workspace
- AO instructs the worker to write deliverables through that artifact path when producing non-PR outputs
- AO lists session artifacts from that AO-managed artifact directory and from PR facts
- file artifacts may be `markdown`, `html`, or `file`, inferred from extension or MIME type at read time
- a session may show multiple file artifacts without storing one DB row per file
- AO stores the session's current output type as `none`, `pr`, or `artifact`
- HTML artifacts can open in the existing browser preview flow

The main architectural choice is to keep sessions as the primary lifecycle object and add artifacts as a durable session-owned output layer on top.

**How this works with the orchestrator:** the orchestrator (or any caller) will read a session's artifacts the same way it reads PR facts — the existing session read APIs (`GET /sessions/{id}`, `GET /orchestrators/{id}`) return `artifactFiles` alongside `prs`, computed live from the session's artifact directory on every read. This gives the orchestrator listing parity with PRs from day one: it can always see what artifacts a session has produced. Reading an artifact file's *content* is planned as a second delivery on top of that: #5895 will add a dedicated content-read endpoint (and an `ao` CLI command), so the orchestrator — or any caller that isn't co-located with the daemon's filesystem — can fetch artifact bytes the same way it already fetches PR file content via `GET /sessions/{id}/pr/{n}/file`. Until that lands, the orchestrator can still reach artifact bytes through the preview boundary (built for the Browser tab) or, if co-located with the daemon, by reading the artifact directory directly.

**AO Cloud:** in Cloud, an artifact will be shareable through a generated link, restricted to users within the artifact-owning organization — nobody outside that org can open it. The cloud-side technical implementation (link generation, org-scoped access checks, storage) is TBD and out of scope for this issue.

**How this fits `ao report`:** `ao report --artifact <ref>` already exists as a worker-facing CLI flag, but it is an opaque string reference with no connection to the artifact directory this design introduces. It stays that way by design — the same loose coupling `ao report` already has with PRs. `--pr-created <url>` doesn't create the PR; it narrates one that git/GitHub already made. Artifacts follow the same pattern: the artifact directory remains the sole system of record for what artifacts exist (computed live, not trusted from a worker claim), and `ao report --artifact` stays a free-form annotation a worker can optionally add to its report history for a human or orchestrator to read. A natural follow-on, not required for this design, is validating `--artifact <path>` against the session's real artifact directory at report time and surfacing its `Label` as an optional caption on the artifact's card in the UI.

## Competitive Analysis

**Superset** has "Pages" rather than artifacts, and the mental model is meaningfully different from our file-viewer approach: a user clicks "+" to create a page, then prompts an agent to fill it in — the page is the starting point, not an inferred output of a task. Where it does overlap with our direction: users can send feedback on a page back to the worker agent, the same way our solution lets a user leave feedback on an artifact file back to the worker.

**Claude (Code / claude.ai)** follows an approach much closer to ours: nothing is created until the user explicitly asks for it — when a user says "create an artifact" or "create a document," it gets generated, and from there it can be shared and iterated on further.

Building a dedicated page/artifact-creation surface like Superset's — a standing "+" entry point independent of a task — doesn't make sense for AO at this stage; it adds a whole extra creation flow and mental model for users to learn before we've validated the simpler one. The better direction is the one Claude Code already takes: artifacts fall out of what the worker was already asked to do, with no separate creation step, which keeps onboarding easy and fast. This design follows that direction.

## Goal

Let a user start any AO task without declaring in advance whether the outcome should be a PR or some other deliverable. AO should create a session-owned artifact area outside the git workspace, instruct the worker to place non-PR deliverables there, list artifact files from that area, combine them with observed PR facts, and let users open each artifact in the appropriate UI surface.

## High-Level Overview

The system should work like this:

1. user starts a session
2. AO creates the session workspace and a dedicated artifact directory under AO's data directory
3. AO gives the worker instructions for writing non-PR deliverables into that artifact directory
4. the worker produces either:
   - a PR
   - a file inside the artifact directory
5. AO inspects only those durable outputs
6. AO returns a computed artifact list for the session
7. AO updates the session output type to `pr`, `artifact`, or `none`
8. session read APIs return session plus artifact files and existing PR metadata
9. the UI opens HTML artifacts in Browser and other file artifacts in Files

### Mermaid Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User starts a session] --> B[AO creates workspace]
    B --> C[AO creates artifact store outside workspace]
    C --> D[Worker writes file artifact there or opens a PR]
    D --> E[AO inspects PR facts and artifact store]
    E --> F[AO computes artifact list]
    F --> G[AO updates session output type]
    G --> H[Session UI shows artifacts]
    H --> J{Artifact kind?}
    J -->|HTML| K[Open in Browser]
    J -->|Markdown/File| L[Open in Files]
    J -->|PR| M[Open PR surface]
```

## Tech Design

### Model And Schema Changes

#### SQLite Changes Required

This design should not add one DB row per file artifact. Store only the session's artifact folder and a small output summary on `sessions`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN artifact_dir TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '';
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN session_output_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none'
    CHECK (session_output_type IN ('none', 'pr', 'artifact'));
```

`session_output_type` lets Kanban distinguish no output, PR output, and file-artifact output. File artifacts themselves are computed by listing `artifact_dir`.

#### Artifact Directory

`artifact_dir` should point under AO's durable data directory, not inside the git workspace:

```text
$AO_DATA_DIR/artifacts/<session-id>/
```

AO lists files from that folder at read time and derives each file's display kind from extension or MIME type. This keeps generated artifacts outside the workspace so they cannot be accidentally committed.

### Kanban Behavior

For this phase, we should keep the Kanban change deliberately small and leave review behavior out.

Suggested rules:

- if the session has no PR and no artifact files, keep it in `building`
- if the session has artifact files, move it to `validating`
- if the session has PRs, keep using the existing PR-derived Kanban behavior
- do not introduce artifact review states yet
- do not add new artifact-specific display statuses yet

This means artifact availability is enough to move the card out of pure building, but not enough to mark it ready. A generated artifact has not been reviewed or accepted; it is simply available for the user to inspect.

### Code Changes

Implemented in PR #4805 (backend slice #4804 + frontend follow-up, stacked on it).

Backend changes required:

- session spawn flow
  - create or reserve the session artifact directory under AO's data directory
  - persist the artifact directory in session metadata
  - include worker instructions that non-PR deliverable outputs should be written there
- artifact inference flow
  - add daemon-side logic that checks only two sources:
    - session-owned PR facts
    - files inside the AO-managed artifact directory
  - if PRs exist, expose them as PR artifact metadata from existing PR tables
  - inspect the artifact directory for `html`, `markdown`, or generic file artifacts on read
  - do not persist one artifact row per file
  - update `session_output_type` to `pr`, `artifact`, or `none`
- session read flow
  - list artifact files from the artifact directory
  - return artifact files and output type on session APIs
- Kanban derivation
  - feed output type or artifact-file presence into the backend Kanban reducer
  - place sessions with artifact output in `validating`
  - keep sessions with no output in `building`
- preview integration
  - if the artifact is `html`, resolve it into the existing browser preview flow
  - non-HTML artifacts do not go through browser preview by default

**Planned follow-on:** #5895 adds a dedicated content-read endpoint (and `ao` CLI command) for artifact files, so an orchestrator or any non-co-located caller can fetch artifact bytes the same way it already fetches PR file content — this design delivers the artifact *list* first, with content-read landing on top of it.

Frontend changes required (see PR #4805 for the shipped implementation):

- session types extended with `artifactFiles` and `outputType` (`frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts`)
- the session Summary panel shows an **Artifacts** section, one row per file, rendered by `ArtifactSummaryCard` (`SessionInspector.tsx`) — a small pill with a file/globe icon and the artifact's name
- clicking a row:
  - if the artifact `kind` is `html`, it opens in the **Browser** tab via the existing preview flow (`useOpenArtifactPreview` posts the artifact's resolved preview URL to `POST /sessions/{id}/preview`, then switches the inspector to the Browser view) — the same panel and `ao preview` machinery used for regular workspace preview
  - if the artifact `kind` is `markdown` or `file`, it opens in the **Files** tab instead, in a dedicated read-only `ArtifactFileView` component (`frontend/src/renderer/components/ArtifactFileView.tsx`) rendered inside `SessionFileExplorer` — artifacts live outside the git workspace, so they get their own viewer rather than reusing the workspace-diff file view
  - both paths **reuse the existing file-viewer/Browser feedback (commenting) mechanism** — the same `feedbackRequestKey` flow used to leave review feedback on a regular file or preview is passed straight through to `ArtifactFileView`, so a user can leave feedback on an artifact exactly the way they already do on a workspace file or browser preview, with no new UI built for it
- PR artifacts continue using the existing PR presentation

title: bug(agents): goose harness availability detection matches the pressly/goose DB migration tool (name-only binary resolution)
body:
## Bug
The goose **agent harness** availability detection matches the **pressly/goose database migration tool** because both ship a binary named `goose`. On systems that have only the migration tool, AO's agent inventory reports the **Goose AI agent as "installed"** (visible in orchestrator/agent settings), and orchestrators can then pick goose for worker spawns — launching the migration CLI with Block-Goose arguments.

**Source:** Discord `#bug-triage` thread (2026-08-26) | **Reported by:** @Akash
**Analyzed against:** `c4abb3d0e` (origin/main, fetched 2026-08-26 IST)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced; reporter independently confirmed the false "installed" entry in his orchestrator settings.

## Reproduction
1. Install only the DB migration tool: `brew install goose` (pressly/goose) or equivalent, so `goose` on PATH is the migration CLI. Do **not** install Block's Goose agent.
2. Run the desktop app / `ao agent list` (or open orchestrator settings → agents).
3. Goose is listed under **installed** agents.
4. Observed by reporter: the orchestrator attempted to spawn a goose worker (first time ever) and failed/misbehaved, because the launched binary is the migration tool, not the agent.

## Root Cause
Binary resolution for the goose harness is **name-only** — first executable named `goose` wins, with no identity/version probe:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/goose/goose.go:259` — `gooseBinarySpec` lists `Names: []string{"goose"}` plus fallback paths `/usr/local/bin/goose`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/goose`, `~/.cargo/bin/goose`, and npm-global locations. Several of these are exactly where the **migration tool** installs (Homebrew's `goose` formula is the pressly migration tool → `/opt/homebrew/bin/goose`).
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/binaryutil/binaryutil.go:94` — `ResolveBinary` does `exec.LookPath(name)` over the spec names and returns the **first** hit. There is no check that the resolved binary is the Block Goose CLI rather than the migration tool.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/goose/goose.go:276` — `ResolveGooseBinary` is a thin wrapper over that resolver.
- `backend/internal/service/agent/service.go` — the inventory `refresh()` and `FindInstalledBinary()` treat a successful resolve as **installed**. The service's own doc comment (line 23) states this by design: *"only resolves executable paths; it never starts an agent CLI or probes"* — so the false positive is a structural gap, not a regression.
- The inventory is advisory UI metadata, but it is what surfaces Goose as a choice in orchestrator settings, and the orchestrator prompt advertises `--agent <name>` for workers (`backend/internal/session_manager/prompt.go:194`). A name collision therefore propagates from PATH → inventory → "installed" → orchestrator spawn attempt.
- The launch command built for the harness (`goose run [--system ...] -t "" --interactive`, `goose.go:104`) targets Block-Goose CLI semantics and does not exist in the migration tool, so any spawn against the wrong binary is broken by construction.
- The reviewer adapter injects the same resolver (`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/goose/goose.go:54`), so it inherits the same false positive.

## Fix
Add an identity check to goose binary resolution instead of trusting the name:
1. After a candidate path resolves (PATH or fallback), run a bounded probe (e.g. `<binary> version` / `--help` with a short timeout) and require a Block-Goose-specific marker (e.g. `run`/`session`/`recipe` subcommands or the Block version output format). pressly/goose exposes `up`/`down`/`status`/`create` instead — distinguishable.
2. Recommended shape: an optional `ValidateIdentity func(ctx, path) bool` field on `binaryutil.BinarySpec` so the whole resolver fleet can adopt per-harness identity checks; goose opts in first.
3. There is precedent for bounded CLI probes in the daemon: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/authprobe/authprobe.go` (`CLIStatus`) already runs agent CLIs with timeouts for auth status — the same pattern applies to identity.
4. On identity failure, report goose as **not installed** in the inventory (and surface a hint like "found `goose` on PATH but it is the DB migration tool").

## Impact
- False "installed" state for the Goose agent on any machine with the pressly migration tool (common on dev boxes with DB work).
- Orchestrators can select goose for workers based on that false availability, producing broken spawns.
- Desktop startup prerequisite gate (`FindInstalledBinary`) can pass on the migration tool alone, deferring the real "no usable harness" failure to spawn time.
- Generalizes: any harness whose binary name collides with an unrelated CLI is affected by the same name-only resolution (see related codex resolver bug below).

## Related
- [#3409](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3409) — another binary-resolver robustness bug (codex `.cmd` vs `.exe` preference); same resolver class, different failure mode.
