title: fix(desktop): keep update status reactive across settings and sidebar
body:
## Reproduction

1. Open Settings → Updates.
2. Click Check for updates.
3. Let the check complete.
4. The visible Last checked timestamp can retain the mount-time value until Settings is closed and reopened.

The regression test reproduces the ordering directly: a completed-check push arrives first, then the older mount-time IPC snapshot resolves.

## Root cause

Each `useUpdateStatus` caller owned an independent `getStatus` request and `updates:status` listener. Snapshot hydration started before the listener was registered, and a late snapshot was always applied. An older response could therefore overwrite a newer pushed status, including `checkedAt`; Settings and the sidebar could also hydrate divergent local copies.

The renderer now uses one shared external updater store. It subscribes before requesting the initial snapshot and revision-gates that snapshot so a newer push wins. This remains a projection of the existing main-process updater state machine.

## Latest-main relevance audit (2026-09-01)

Rebased onto `main` at `8a88be0c7`.

`main` now includes #4729, which independently added the proactive sidebar update affordance, download/restart/retry states, tests, and per-version dismissal. Those older UI changes from this PR were intentionally dropped during conflict resolution so the newer product behavior remains authoritative.

The underlying reactivity bug is still present on latest `main`: `useUpdateStatus` still creates per-consumer state, starts independent snapshots, and permits a late snapshot to roll back a newer status push. The shared store fix remains relevant and now keeps the existing Settings and #4729 sidebar surfaces synchronized.

## Tests

- `npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx` — 123 passed
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`

## Scope

After the rebase this is a focused two-file change: the shared updater status store plus the immediate Last checked regression test. The current sidebar UX from `main` is unchanged.

title: fix: align session usage costs and card metrics
body:
## Summary

- price fresh provider-native usage when the active catalog has exactly one owner for the reported model, recording the route as `inferred` so later observed Claude routing can still replace attribution and cost
- preserve honest unknowns: unidentified Claude proxy routes and models absent from the catalog remain unpriced
- extend the compact usage API with the canonical token/category totals already used by the detailed session view
- render exactly one Kanban scan metric: reliable dollar cost, otherwise reliable compact tokens, otherwise nothing (including no orphan separator)
- share the detailed token and cost-category breakdown between the developer-mode session inspector and the card's hover/focus tooltip

## Root cause and harness coverage

Fresh Claude Code records can carry native token counters before a billing route is observed. Live ingestion deliberately left those rows unattributed and relied on legacy repair, but repair runs at startup/settle or when route evidence changes. A newly spawned, continuously active worker could therefore accumulate reliable tokens while remaining unpriced until a later repair pass, producing `Unavailable · 5.2M` on its card.

Live ingestion now uses unique catalog ownership as explicitly inferred evidence. This is covered end-to-end for Claude Code, Codex records missing provider metadata, and Kimi wire usage. Provider-specific counters remain intact. Observed routes still win; unknown catalog models and the explicit unidentified-proxy sentinel do not receive fabricated costs.

## UI rules covered

- reliable estimate: `$1.24` only, including reliable `$0.00`
- no estimate + reliable usage: `5.2M` only
- neither: no metric and no separator
- no literal `Unavailable` card placeholder
- hover and keyboard focus disclose fresh input, cache reads, output, cache-hit rate, input/cache/output costs, coverage, and observed/inferred attribution context

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/observe/usage ./internal/service/usage ./internal/storage/sqlite/store ./internal/httpd/...`
- sanitized worker environment: `go test ./...`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` (144 passed)

## Preview evidence

Opened and kept the completed browser-preview target available for human inspection in this AO session with:

`go run ./backend/cmd/ao preview http://127.0.0.1:5174/`

Automated inspection through the AO Browser panel was blocked because this worker was provisioned with an empty browser capability and empty persisted verifier. The capability cannot be safely reconstructed for a running worker, so no direct Browser API fallback or relaunch was attempted.

Separate non-panel visual QA against the same preview build at 1440×1000 reproduced all three branches together: `$1.24`, `5.2M`, and omitted; zero visible `Unavailable` placeholders. Hovering `$1.24` showed the shared token/category and dollar-component breakdown with the provider-pricing explanation.

title: feat(gitlab-tracker): switch List and Get to GraphQL Work Items API
body:
## Summary

Switches the GitLab tracker adapter's `List` and `Get` operations from the REST Issues API to the GraphQL Work Items API (`POST /api/v4/graphql`). Work Items is the superset of Issues — Issues are work items of type "issue" — so the adapter now sees all open work items on the board regardless of type (tasks, objectives, etc.).

Closes ticket 02: Switch GitLab tracker adapter List to GraphQL Work Items.

Depends on ticket 01 (nested-group repo path fix) which preserves the full namespace path for GitLab `fullPath` queries.

### Key changes

- **List**: GraphQL `project(fullPath:)` -> `workItems` connection with cursor-based pagination (`endCursor`/`hasNextPage`). Filters by `state`, `assigneeUsernames`, and `labelName`. `Limit` caps total results, stopping early.
- **Get**: Single work item fetched via `workItem(fullPath:, iid:)` query.
- **Field mapping**: `iid`->Native, `title`->Title, `description`->Body, `state`->State, `webUrl`->URL, assignees from `WorkItemWidgetAssignees`, labels from `WorkItemWidgetLabels`.
- **Error classification**:
  - HTTP 200 with GraphQL `errors` array + `extensions.code: NOT_FOUND` -> `ErrNotFound`
  - HTTP 200 with `data.project == null` -> `ErrNotFound`
  - 401/403 -> `ErrAuthFailed`
  - 429 -> `ErrRateLimited`
- **Preflight** unchanged: REST `GET /user`.
- All sentinel errors preserved (`ErrNotFound`, `ErrAuthFailed`, `ErrRateLimited`, `ErrWrongProvider`, `ErrBadID`, `ErrHostNotAllowed`).
- Host routing unchanged — self-managed hosts use per-host base URL and tokens.

## Tests

All tests rewritten to use `POST /api/v4/graphql` with GraphQL response shapes:

```
go test ./internal/adapters/tracker/gitlab/... -v -count=1
```

37 tests pass covering:
- Happy path (single-page, multi-page cursor pagination)
- Limit stops early
- Nested group paths (full namespace in `fullPath` variable)
- Filter variables (state, assigneeUsernames, labelName)
- Error classification (GraphQL errors, null project, auth failed, rate limited)
- Host routing (self-managed, default, unconfigured rejected, case insensitive)
- Edge cases (no labels, no assignees, no description, empty results)
- Preflight (happy, invalid token, cache, retry)
- Provider/repo validation (unchanged — pre-network)

## Risks

- Work item IIDs share a single per-project sequence across all types — the canonical ID format `gitlab:group/project#iid` remains collision-free.
- No work item type filtering in v1; epics/incidents are included. Can be added later without breaking the query shape.
- GitHub tracker adapter is untouched — no regression risk.

title: feat(mobile): prompt when a newer native build is on the store
body:
## What

OTA covers JS only — with `policy: fingerprint` a native change mints a new runtime, so a build in the field silently stops being offered updates the moment a newer binary ships. This says so and takes the user to the store.

- Cold start, once, after pairing. Android asks Play In-App Updates, so Play compares the installed `versionCode` itself. iOS has no such API, so it queries the iTunes lookup by bundle id against `CFBundleShortVersionString` from the binary — not the JS bundle's version, which OTA can change independently.
- Two tiers: `inAppUpdatePriority >= 4` hands over to Google's updater (still cancellable, so an insistent nudge rather than a lock); everything else is a dismissible sheet, once a day and three dismissals per store version, a swipe counting as one. The first ask waits until Play has known about the update for three days.
- Settings → About → App Store / Play Store checks on demand. Sideloaded, offline or not yet listed all read as "no update"; dev builds are inert.

## Version floor

`EXPO_PUBLIC_AO_MIN_APP_VERSION` and `EXPO_PUBLIC_AO_LATEST_APP_VERSION`, both unset so they ship inert. They are EAS environment variables, so moving one is an `eas update` rather than a store release, and app JS is not a fingerprint input, so it reaches builds already in the field. This exists because iOS cannot be asked at all while unlisted, and because `inAppUpdatePriority` is immutable once a release has rolled out.

**The floor may only escalate an update the store independently confirmed.** It can raise a confirmed update from dismissible to blocking; it can never invent one. So a mistyped floor cannot strand anyone, iOS stays nudge-only while unlisted, and it starts blocking on its own once listed. That is asserted directly in the tests, not left to statement order in `tierOf`. The soft tier needs no confirmation — the only way to surface anything on iOS during TestFlight — and the copy follows the source, so a floor-driven prompt reads "Version 1.3.0 is available." rather than naming a store page that doesn't exist.

`expo-in-app-updates` is **excluded from Apple autolinking**: Android-only code here, and linking the unused pod would put it in the iOS fingerprint, changing the iOS runtime on every dependency bump. It binds via `requireOptionalNativeModule`, which answers `null` on iOS instead of throwing. Play's flexible flow is never started — it calls `completeUpdate()` the moment the download lands and restarts the app unannounced.

## Activation

No CI, no secret, nothing automatic. The floor does nothing until someone creates the two EAS variables with **plaintext** visibility — secret ones aren't readable outside EAS servers and would silently resolve to empty. It is also only as granular as our version stamping: `version` has read `1.2.1` across several commits, and `autoIncrement` moves the build number instead.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` (538, 43 new); `npx expo export` both platforms
- `npx expo-doctor` 20/21 — measured on the base commit too, where it is also 20/21 with the same three packages, so the failure is `main`'s and not this branch's
- `npx expo prebuild --clean` then real native builds on both platforms
- `runtimeversion:resolve` twice per platform, stable. iOS unchanged from base (`e259e922…`) — the autolinking exclusion holding — while Android moves, as a native module must. The floor moves neither, being pure JS
- Lockfile is `main`'s plus one dependency, **zero re-resolutions**, verified by diffing every package version
- On device, both platforms: module linked on Android; `checkStore()` fails open silently on a Play-less emulator; iOS launches with the pod excluded; sheet in light and dark; snooze written, honoured and reset when the version moves. With a floor set, both read "Version 9.9.9 is available." — the value inlined, the store confirming nothing
- Not exercised: the real Play update flow (needs internal app sharing), iOS against a real listing (we have none — the lookup was tested against the live iTunes API with a published bundle id), the stalled-update resume path, and a real `eas update` carrying a floor

title: agy (Antigravity) AuthStatus() is hardcoded to Unknown, never reflects real login state
body:
## Bug

`AuthStatus()` for the Agy (Antigravity) adapter always returns `Unknown` once the binary resolves, regardless of whether the user is actually authenticated. This is a real, live-verified gap distinct from the model-catalog work in [#3385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3385)/[PR #3386](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3386) (merged) and [PR #3960](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3960) (open, fixes an Agy model-discovery pipe-drain bug) — those cover model discovery, not auth detection.

**Source:** live reproduction on a user's machine via Claude Code session | **Analyzed against:** `main` @ current HEAD (fetched directly, confirmed unchanged from the fork checkout) | **Reported by:** @Hendrixx-RE
**Confidence:** High

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/agy/auth.go`:

```go
func (p *Plugin) AuthStatus(ctx context.Context) (ports.AgentAuthStatus, error) {
	if _, err := p.ResolveBinary(ctx); err != nil {
		return ports.AgentAuthStatusUnknown, err
	}
	// Antigravity authenticates through its OS keyring and browser sign-in. The
	// official CLI does not expose a documented non-interactive credential file
	// or status command, so local auth cannot safely be inferred here.
	return ports.AgentAuthStatusUnknown, nil
}
```

The comment's premise is out of date: the real `agy` CLI (confirmed real binary, `agy --version` → `1.1.22`) has a documented `models` subcommand that already IS used for model discovery elsewhere in the codebase (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go`: `"agy": {args: []string{"models"}, parser: parseIDLines}`). Running it directly:

```
$ agy models
Fetching available models...
gemini-3.7-flash-high	Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)
...
claude-opus-4-6-thinking	Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)
```

succeeds non-interactively with no login prompt when the user is authenticated (it fetches live data from a remote service). A successful `agy models` call (which AO already runs for the model catalog) is a usable, already-computed signal of auth state — but `AuthStatus()` doesn't consult it, or any other signal, and unconditionally reports `Unknown`.

## Impact

Every Agy/Antigravity user sees an uninformative "unknown" auth indicator in AO's UI regardless of actual login state, with no way to distinguish "not logged in, spawn will fail" from "logged in and ready." This surfaced in the wild as "AO can't detect my Antigravity auth."

## Suggested Fix

`AuthStatus()` could reuse the model-catalog discovery call (or a cheap equivalent) as a proxy signal: a successful `agy models` call implies authenticated; a failure that looks like an auth/login prompt implies not authenticated. Since the model catalog fetch (`modelcatalog` package) already runs this exact command and caches results, `AuthStatus()` may be able to piggyback on that cache instead of shelling out separately, avoiding duplicate CLI invocations.

## Related

- [#3385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3385) — adapter-aware model selection RFC, merged via [PR #3386](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3386); covers model discovery for Agy, not auth.
- [PR #3960](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3960) — open, fixes an Agy-specific model-discovery pipe-drain timeout bug; same subsystem, different bug.
- [#4031](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4031) — same class of problem for a different adapter ("bug(kimi): OAuth-managed auth is reported unknown or unauthorized").

title: fix(agy): report real auth status instead of always Unknown
body:
Fixes #4639

## Summary

Antigravity's `agy` adapter has no documented status/whoami command, so `AuthStatus()` was hardcoded to always return `Unknown` regardless of actual login state. `agy models` already fetches its catalog from a remote service and only succeeds when the CLI is authenticated — and AO already runs that exact command elsewhere for the model picker (`modelcatalog.Discover`, wired up in `commandSpecs["agy"]` per #3385/PR #3386).

This reuses that same discovery call as a proxy signal:
- success → `Authorized`
- failure → stays `Unknown` (not `Unauthorized` — a failed run could mean "not logged in", "offline", or a transient CLI hiccup, and there's no documented way to tell those apart without guessing at error text, so this only ever turns a `Unknown` into a `Authorized` when it can prove it, never invents a false negative)

## Verification

Reproduced live against the real `agy` CLI (v1.1.22): `agy models` succeeds non-interactively with no login prompt when authenticated, returning a tab-separated `<id>\t<label>` list. Confirmed the fix reports `Authorized` in that case via a table-driven test with an injected `discoverModels` seam (no real subprocess/network call in the test itself, per repo test-hygiene conventions).

The existing test's original intent — unrelated `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (Google ADC) must never be mistaken for Antigravity auth — is preserved as its own subtest.

## Test plan

```
go build ./...
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/... -v
go test ./...
go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/...
gofmt -l internal/adapters/agent/agy/auth.go internal/adapters/agent/agy/agy_test.go
```
All pass; full backend suite green.

## Related

- #4639 — the bug this fixes
- #3385 / PR #3386 — merged model-catalog discovery work that already exercises `agy models`, reused here
- PR #3960 — open, separate fix for a model-discovery pipe-drain timeout bug in the same subsystem; unrelated to this auth-status change

title: Orchestrator killed by tmux/host death has no path back to its own history — only recovery action is a cold, unlinked respawn
body:
## Bug

When a project orchestrator's TUI runtime dies (host reboot, OS kill, tmux server loss), the only recovery actions reachable today discard its conversation history — even though that history is fully intact on disk (confirmed live: a 1.7MB Claude Code transcript survives untouched after the reboot) and the daemon already has a working resume mechanism (`RestoreWithMode` → `GetRestoreCommand` → `RestoreIdentity`) that's simply never invoked by the orchestrator-recovery flow. `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=true)` always spawns a brand-new session with no `AgentSessionID` carried forward from the retired one, and neither the topbar "Orchestrator" button nor `RestoreUnavailableDialog` ever attempt a real restore before discarding.

Basically when I swtiched to  the terminal to talk to the orchastrator  and restarted my pc,the tmux session is cleared  and with that my chat was also gone,so I couldnt go back to the original orchastrator chat

## Reproduction

1. Run a project orchestrator (TUI, Claude Code) with real conversation history.
2. Reboot the host without a graceful `POST /shutdown` (kills the tmux server backing the orchestrator's PTY).
3. On next boot the orchestrator is still `isTerminated: false` but permanently unattachable.
4. `Kill` / clean-respawn (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators {"clean":true}`) both 500 today — tracked in #4481/PR #4482.
5. Even once that's fixed: the only recovery affordances (topbar "Orchestrator" button, `RestoreUnavailableDialog`'s "create new orchestrator") call `spawnOrchestrator(..., clean=true)`, which always creates a new session/conversation id — never attempts `POST /sessions/{id}/restore` against the just-retired orchestrator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a dead-runtime orchestrator is retired via clean respawn, AO attempts to resume its native conversation (the existing `RestoreWithMode`/`GetRestoreCommand` mechanism) before falling back to a fresh spawn.
- [ ] If resume succeeds, the user lands back in the same conversation with full history intact.
- [ ] If resume genuinely fails, the user is explicitly told the respawn started cold (extending the existing `orchestratorRetireNotice` mechanism) instead of silently swapping in a blank coordinator.
- [ ] A "restore instead of replace" action is reachable from the actual orchestrator-recovery UI (topbar button / `RestoreUnavailableDialog`), not only from the Archived Sessions list.

## Related

- #4481 / PR #4482 — prerequisite mechanical fix (Kill/RetireForReplacement 500 on dead runtime).
- #2501 — same underlying gap (orchestrator respawn with no linkage/notification), different trigger (probe race vs. host-level runtime death).

title: fix: GitLab intake observer — nested group repo paths + multi-tracker wiring
body:
## What

Fixes GitLab issue intake: nested group repo paths are now preserved, and the intake observer uses the multi-tracker (GitHub + GitLab) instead of a GitHub-only adapter. Also restores the `gh auth token` CLI fallback for the GitHub tracker that was accidentally dropped during the wiring refactor.

## Why

Two issues prevented GitLab issue intake from working:

1. **Nested group paths truncated** — `cleanRepoPath` took only the last two path segments (same as GitHub), dropping the full namespace for nested groups like `group/subgroup/repo`. GitLab API lookups failed with 404.

2. **Intake observer hardcoded to GitHub** — `startTrackerIntake` wired a `SingleTrackerResolver` with a GitHub-only lazy adapter. Projects with `provider: "gitlab"` always failed with "no adapter for provider gitlab" and entered an endless failure-backoff loop.

## How

- `cleanRepoPath` now takes a `provider` argument. For GitLab it preserves the full namespace path; for GitHub it keeps the last-two-segment behavior.
- `startTrackerIntake` now accepts a `ports.Tracker` and is wired with `newMultiTracker` (GitHub + GitLab), matching the session service's existing pattern. The `SingleTrackerResolver` uses an empty `Provider` so the multi-tracker dispatches by each project's configured provider.
- The GitHub tracker token source restores the full fallback chain (`AO_GITHUB_TOKEN` → `GITHUB_TOKEN` → `gh auth token` CLI with 5-min cache), mirroring the GitLab tracker's `DefaultTokenSource` (env → `glab` CLI).

## Testing

- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go test ./internal/daemon/...` passes
- [x] `go test ./internal/observe/trackerintake/...` passes
- [x] Manual verification: daemon with GitLab intake config successfully polls GitLab API, finds assigned issues, and spawns worker sessions

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: bug(chat): Codex chat controllers can stop together and falsely exit active sessions
body:
## Bug

Multiple live `codex` **chat-mode** sessions were marked `exited` together after their chat controllers emitted `controller.state = stopped`, including the session created from the prompt `Fix the following: 1 ...`. In the UI this looks like the chat session or chat UI suddenly exiting, but the backend evidence shows a shared controller-stop event rather than a renderer-only disappearance.

**Source:** local AO desktop session on this machine (reporter: local user `chauhan`, no public chat URL)
**Date observed:** 2026-08-29
**Installed desktop:** `0.12.10-nightly.202608290454`
**Bundled daemon:** `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao` (`ao version` reports `dev`)
**Analyzed against current main:** `c26f5f1aa14399017e3de54f0522cd18b79e6f9f`
**OS / shell / Go:** macOS 15.6 arm64 (`Darwin 24.6.0`), `/bin/zsh`, `go1.26.3`
**Daemon under test:** healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`, run-file owner `app`, appRunId `apprun-f36fa767-3a50-4806-a1cd-b02c3e606d7c`
**Confidence:** Medium
**Priority:** P1 — active/idle chat workers can all become unusable at once, and at least one in-flight turn is failed.

## What happened

At `2026-08-29 17:25:23Z` to `17:25:24Z`, seven Codex chat sessions emitted `controller.state = stopped` within ~600ms and were then persisted as `activity = exited` / `is_terminated = false`.

Affected sessions observed in the same cluster:

- `agent-orchestrator-154`
- `silentreadingcommunity-1`
- `agent-orchestrator-163`
- `saturday-reads-api-6`
- `agent-orchestrator-153`
- `agent-orchestrator-156`
- `agent-orchestrator-149`

For the user-reported session:

- session id: `agent-orchestrator-163`
- display name: `Fix the following: 1`
- harness: `codex`
- mode: `chat`
- no `runtime_handle_id`
- no `native_transcript_path`
- latest user prompt before failure: `if auto inject review comments is enabled comments are not getting injected why`

The last turn on `agent-orchestrator-163` failed as:

- requested: `2026-08-29 17:24:57.164021Z`
- started: `2026-08-29 17:24:57.181099Z`
- completed/failed: `2026-08-29 17:25:24.114526Z`
- state: `failed`
- error: `controller ended before the turn completed`

## Exact evidence

### Durable session timeline

`agent-orchestrator-163` stayed live in chat mode and accepted user prompts after earlier work completed:

- `2026-08-29 17:16:05.415207Z`: session activity written to `idle`
- `2026-08-29 17:18:02.591334Z`: user prompt accepted while still `idle`
- `2026-08-29 17:20:49.960440Z`: another user prompt accepted while still `idle`
- `2026-08-29 17:24:57.164021Z`: latest user prompt accepted
- `2026-08-29 17:25:24.113570Z`: provider event `controller.state = stopped`
- `2026-08-29 17:25:24.118736Z`: session persisted as `activity = exited`, `is_terminated = false`

### Provider-event cluster

The following `conversation_provider_events` rows all arrived during the same failure window:

- `agent-orchestrator-154` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:23.756869Z`
- `silentreadingcommunity-1` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.044436Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-163` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.113570Z`
- `saturday-reads-api-6` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.174660Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-153` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.238469Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-156` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.298882Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-149` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.360226Z`

This does not look like a single session-specific corruption. It looks like a shared stop/shutdown condition across Codex chat controllers.

## Relevant code path

This failure mode maps directly to the current backend behavior:

1. `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go` emits `ChatEventControllerState{ControllerState: stopped}` whenever the app-server connection ends, explicitly noting that the connection ended rather than leaving the stream quiet.
2. `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` treats that event as authoritative, runs `CleanupOwnedControllerWork(...)`, then reports session activity as `domain.ActivityExited` with event `chat.controller.stopped`.
3. `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go` treats `chat.controller.stopped` as a turn/session boundary event.
4. The renderer then shows the controller/session as stopped or exited. For the failed in-flight turn, `conversation_turns.error_message` becomes `controller ended before the turn completed`.

The code is behaving consistently with the emitted provider event. The bug is that multiple live Codex chat controllers appear to stop together unexpectedly.

## Why this seems distinct from existing tmux/session-exit bugs

This is not the same failure as [#4458](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4458):

- the affected sessions here are all `chat` mode, not TUI
- `agent-orchestrator-163` had no `runtime_handle_id`
- there is no interface-transition row for `agent-orchestrator-163`
- the stop comes from the Codex app-server chat stream closing, not from tmux attach/liveness routing

## Hypothesis

The exact external trigger was not proven during triage, but the evidence suggests one of these shared controller-stop paths:

- a Codex app-server / chat-driver process lifecycle event that propagates across several conversations
- a daemon/app ownership transition or supervision event that closes several chat controller connections together
- a bad restore/reconcile path for existing live chat sessions after AO is launched against real `~/.ao` data

One nearby signal from the same period: another session logged a reconcile failure with `resume chat: chat conversation resume failed: thread/resume: app-server error -32600: no rollout found for thread id ...`, which suggests chat restore/controller ownership around this window may be unstable.

## Reproduction notes

This was observed on a real-data desktop run rather than a reduced e2e reproduction. The sequence on this machine was:

1. Use AO desktop with real `~/.ao` data on macOS.
2. Have several non-terminated Codex chat sessions present.
3. Continue working in `agent-orchestrator-163` and send another prompt.
4. Observe several chat sessions flip to `exited` nearly simultaneously.
5. The in-flight prompt on `agent-orchestrator-163` fails with `controller ended before the turn completed`.

## Expected behavior

- An idle or active Codex chat session should not transition to `exited` unless its own controller actually dies for a local reason the user can act on.
- A shared AO desktop action or daemon reconciliation pass should not silently stop several independent Codex chat controllers.
- If AO detects a recoverable ownership/reconnect condition, the session should surface that explicitly and preserve resumability rather than collapsing multiple sessions into `exited`.

## Suggested investigation

- Trace why multiple `codexappserver` conversation streams closed together in the same second.
- Audit any path where app-owned daemon replacement, supervisor disconnect, or chat restore cleanup can call stop/close on more than one controller.
- Add coverage for multi-session chat survival when a second desktop/dev instance interacts with real data or when the daemon reconciles previously live chat controllers.
- Add a regression test for the in-flight-turn case: one session turn should not fail as `controller ended before the turn completed` because unrelated chat controllers were stopped in a batch.

## Related

- [#4458](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4458) — session false-exit and duplicate-controller issues in TUI/tmux land; related symptom, different subsystem.

title: Expose per-role (worker vs orchestrator) permission mode in Project Settings, not just one shared value
body:
## Problem

Project Settings has exactly one shared "Permission Mode" control (`PermissionModeSelect` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`), which writes only into the project's top-level `agentConfig.permissions`. It's positioned next to the orchestrator agent picker, which reads as "the orchestrator's setting" but actually applies identically to every worker too. There's no way to give workers a different (looser or stricter) permission level than the orchestrator through the UI.

**This is a UI gap, not a backend one — confirmed by code trace, not assumption:**
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`'s `effectiveAgentConfig(kind, cfg)` already merges the shared `cfg.AgentConfig` with a role-specific override (`cfg.Worker.AgentConfig` / `cfg.Orchestrator.AgentConfig`), and `Permissions` is one of the fields that overrides cleanly when set.
- `domain.RoleOverride.AgentConfig.Permissions` is validated today (`projectconfig_test.go`: `{"bad role agent config", ProjectConfig{Worker: RoleOverride{AgentConfig: AgentConfig{Permissions: "nope"}}}, true}`), and `ProjectConfig.Worker`/`.Orchestrator` marshal directly via `json:"worker,omitempty"`/`json:"orchestrator,omitempty"` — no separate DTO stripping the field.
- The frontend's own `buildRoleAgentConfig` helper (used for `config.worker.agentConfig` / `config.orchestrator.agentConfig`) only ever sets `model`/`mode` — never `permissions` — so the working backend field is simply never populated from the settings form.

**Confidence: High** that this is purely a frontend gap; a small addition to `ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` (a second `PermissionModeSelect` per role, wired through `buildRoleAgentConfig`) should be sufficient with no backend/DTO changes needed.

## Real-world motivating case

Hit this directly: a project with the orchestrator on Claude Code and the worker on Codex, one shared "Accept edits" permission level. Assumed both roles had equivalent effective permission — they didn't, because the same domain-level policy maps to very different actual CLI behavior per harness (`backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go`):

```go
// Claude Code
case PermissionAcceptEdits: return []string{"--permission-mode", "acceptEdits"}
// Codex
case PermissionAcceptEdits: return []string{"--ask-for-approval", "on-request"}
```

Claude Code's `acceptEdits` is fairly permissive; Codex's `on-request` means Codex decides for itself when to prompt, so it kept asking. This makes the missing per-role control worse than it might look in the abstract: mixing harnesses across orchestrator/worker (an expected, supported AO configuration) turns one shared slider into genuinely inconsistent real behavior between roles, with no way to compensate short of hand-editing the project config via a raw API call.

## Ask

Add a second permission-mode control for the worker role (or make the existing one explicitly role-aware), writing into `worker.agentConfig.permissions` the same way `buildRoleAgentConfig` already does for `model`/`mode`.

Filing this to gauge interest — curious whether other users have hit the same "workers won't stop asking for permission even though I set it to max" confusion, since the root cause (one shared control, harness-dependent real behavior) isn't obvious from the UI alone.

## Related

- [#2195](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2195) — broader "give workers a full per-role environment profile" RFC (MCP, plugins, system prompt), whose own side-note already flags that per-role `model`/`permissions` are "wired in the Go domain and API schema but only `agent` is exposed per-role in the settings UI." That issue explicitly defers UI work to a follow-up and is additionally gated on resolving #2844's naked-by-default MCP/plugins rollout question. This issue is scoped to just the permissions-UI slice, which has no such rollout blocker and looks independently shippable.
- [#3385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3385) / [PR #3386](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3386) — the same "wired per-role in the backend, not exposed in the UI" pattern, already solved for model selection specifically. This issue asks for the same treatment for permissions.

title: feat(desktop): reveal the collapsed sidebar after a pointer dwell at the left edge
body:
## Feature request

When the desktop sidebar is fully collapsed off-canvas, let the user reveal it by holding the pointer at the far-left screen edge for a deliberate 250 ms dwell. The visible top-left titlebar sidebar button, identified by its Expand tooltip, should open the temporary preview immediately on pointer hover.

The current sidebar has a narrow `SidebarRail` that opens the panel on click. The shell also keeps the sidebar open from the keyboard shortcut. Under Browser workspace pressure, the app can use a separate icon rail, but that is a different state and should keep its current behavior.

This request uses two intentional pointer paths. The far-left edge needs a 250 ms dwell. The visible top-left titlebar button opens on hover without waiting for that dwell.

## Proposed behavior

- Add a narrow activation zone at the far-left screen edge.
- Start a 250 ms dwell timer only when the pointer enters the edge activation zone.
- Cancel the edge timer when the pointer leaves the zone before 250 ms. A quick pass along the edge should not open the sidebar.
- When the pointer hovers the visible top-left titlebar sidebar button, the temporary overlay should open immediately. This button is the control that shows the Expand tooltip.
- After either trigger opens the preview, show the sidebar as a temporary overlay. The overlay must not change the saved sidebar preference, reclaim layout width, or move the center panel.
- Reveal and dismiss the temporary overlay with a short, subtle, smooth slide/fade. Keep the 250 ms edge dwell, immediate titlebar-button hover, and 55 ms dismissal delay unchanged.
- Keep the temporary overlay open while the pointer is over its trigger or the sidebar. Moving from the titlebar button into the overlay must keep it open.
- Keep pointer transfer from either trigger into the overlay independent of animation progress and animated hit bounds. It must not depend on a moving target, so the old race from #3372 cannot recur.
- Leaving both the active trigger area and the overlay should start a 55 ms dismissal delay. Re-entering either area before the overlay closes should cancel the delay.
- Clicking the visible top-left titlebar button or the sidebar expand control while the overlay is open must promote it to the normal pinned-open state. The keyboard shortcut must continue to open the pinned state directly.
- Once pinned open, the sidebar must stay open until the user explicitly collapses it. Pointer movement alone must not collapse it.
- Preserve the existing click, keyboard, resize, and compact icon-rail behavior.

## Accessibility and accidental-trigger requirements

Pointer preview is an optional convenience, not the only way to reach the sidebar.

- Keep the visible titlebar button, its accessible Expand name, and the keyboard shortcut available.
- Do not move keyboard focus into the temporary overlay or add duplicate focus stops for hidden controls.
- Expose the expand/collapse state and accessible names through the existing controls. Screen-reader and keyboard users must have an equivalent path.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences.
- Do not trigger the edge preview from a pointer-down, drag, text selection, or a brief crossing of the edge. The titlebar button's immediate hover preview is intentional, but its click path must remain available.
- Keep the edge activation zone narrow enough that ordinary pointer travel along the left edge does not repeatedly open the sidebar.
- Account for platform chrome, including macOS traffic-light clearance and the Windows titlebar, so the activation targets do not interfere with window controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In the fully collapsed off-canvas state, holding the pointer in the far-left edge activation zone for 250 ms opens a temporary sidebar overlay.
- [ ] In the fully collapsed off-canvas state, hovering the visible top-left titlebar sidebar button, the one with the Expand tooltip, opens the temporary overlay immediately without a dwell.
- [ ] A quick pointer pass across the far-left edge does not open the overlay. The titlebar button remains an intentional immediate-hover trigger.
- [ ] Moving the pointer from the titlebar button into the overlay keeps the preview open.
- [ ] Leaving both the active trigger area and the overlay starts a 55 ms delayed dismissal. Re-entering either area before dismissal keeps the overlay open.
- [ ] Clicking the visible top-left titlebar button or the sidebar expand control while the preview is visible pins the sidebar open. The keyboard shortcut still pins it open.
- [ ] The temporary overlay does not persist the open preference, change the layout gap, or resize the center panel.
- [ ] A pinned-open sidebar remains open until an explicit collapse action.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation, screen-reader naming/state, focus order, and reduced-motion behavior remain correct in both collapsed and temporary-overlay states.
- [ ] The temporary overlay reveals and dismisses with a short, subtle, smooth slide/fade. The 250 ms edge dwell, immediate titlebar-button hover, and 55 ms leave dismissal remain unchanged.
- [ ] With reduced motion enabled, the overlay skips movement or uses a reduced transition while preserving the same trigger, keep-open, and dismissal behavior.
- [ ] Pointer transfer from either trigger into the overlay remains reliable during the transition and does not depend on animated bounds, avoiding the old race in #3372.
- [ ] Pointer drag and text-selection gestures do not cause accidental edge activation.
- [ ] Automated coverage exercises the 250 ms edge dwell, immediate titlebar-button hover, edge dwell cancellation, temporary overlay dismissal, click-to-pin, and the existing keyboard paths on the supported desktop platforms.

## Related history

- [Issue #3372](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3372) documented the old immediate toggle-hover preview race, where the preview closed before the pointer could reach it. This request intentionally uses immediate hover only for the visible top-left titlebar button, while the far-left edge requires a 250 ms dwell. Both paths must keep the preview open as the pointer enters the sidebar and must use delayed dismissal after leaving.
- [PR #4263](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4263) removed the old collapsed-sidebar hover opening from the current frontend. This request brings back immediate preview only for the explicit visible top-left titlebar button and keeps the deliberate 250 ms dwell for the far-left edge.
- [PR #3509](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3509) covered the earlier keep-open zone and click-to-pin interaction.

Inspected against commit `dc1ea86e841e8a879b62f44b67682cce26c26767`.

title: feat(scm): OneDev SCM provider
body:
Code changes: +3230 -61  
Tests: +3626 -1  
Others: +5 -0  

## What

A OneDev SCM provider, so AO can observe and act on pull requests hosted on a self-hosted OneDev instance the way it already does for GitHub and GitLab.

The change includes provider foundation and credential/host resolution, PR and CI observation, build logs, review state, authenticated identity, registration in every SCM constructor, and an `ao doctor` section.

## Why

Fixes #4556.

OneDev is a common self-hosted choice for people who cannot put their code on github.com, and today AO simply has nothing for it — a OneDev repo is invisible to the board, so none of the session/PR/CI lifecycle works.

## How

Points reviewers may want to push back on, stated rather than buried:

- **`MergePullRequest` deliberately returns unsupported.** OneDev's merge API has no compare-and-swap — no expected-head parameter — so a merge cannot be made safe against a racing push the way the GitHub and GitLab paths are. Rather than implement a merge that can silently land the wrong head, the adapter declines and the user merges in the OneDev UI. Automatic merge remains unsupported.
- **Hosts come from configuration, not a fixed base URL.** OneDev is always self-hosted, so there is no public API root to assume. Instances are read from an allowlist and credentials resolved per host. `ebfa1df26` tightened that resolution after a mis-keyed per-host token resolved to the wrong credential; the two `test(scm)` commits are the regression tests for it, including credential *ordering*.
- **`doctor` builds the real adapter rather than re-implementing its checks.** Otherwise doctor can pass while the daemon fails. An unconfigured allowlist and an unreachable instance are WARN (self-hosted instances are commonly on private networks, and most deployments never set the allowlist); a *rejected* credential is a FAIL.
- **`fix(daemon): register OneDev in every SCM constructor`** is a genuine bug in the shape of the wiring: `scm_wiring.go` built providers in three places and only `startSCMObserver` registered OneDev, so `ao session claim-pr` on a OneDev PR failed with `SCM_UNAVAILABLE`. Worth a look as a pattern question — three constructors that must be kept in sync will drift again.
- **`golangci-lint` fixes are folded in, not bolted on.** v2.12.2 flags `gocritic ptrToRefParam` on a `*map` parameter (the pointer existed only so an overflow reset could rebind the map; `clear()` does it in place) and `makezero` on two build-log frame helpers (sizing the frame once and copying into it is lint-clean and one allocation instead of two). Both are fixed in the commits that introduce that code rather than in a trailing cleanup commit. No behaviour change.

Tests are in the same commits as the code they cover. Changes are limited to the OneDev adapter, its wiring, config resolution, doctor, and the status document.

## Review fixes

Truncated PR listings return an error so the observer retains its discovery cursor. A matching first-row hash no longer skips discovery. A full 50-build window reports partial/unknown before commit filtering, preserving durable checks when the current job set may be incomplete. Regression tests cover each case.

## Testing

Rebased onto main at `c9e855943`. Backend build and strict golangci-lint pass. The full backend race suite was run: the installed Codex protocol conformance test fails on both this branch and unchanged upstream. A tmux failure in the full run passed on an isolated retry. These environment findings remain outside this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Full backend suite is green in CI (local protocol mismatch described above)

---

@illegalcall @somewherelostt — tagging you as the on-call pair per your note on #4556. Happy to split this smaller, reorder it, or rework any of the decisions above. #4655 covers #4557 (OneDev issue tracker and multi-provider intake) and is stacked on this branch. Review this PR first; the dependent PR includes these SCM changes until this lands.

title: feat(tracker): OneDev issue tracker, and multi-provider issue intake
body:
Code changes: +4635 -98  
Tests: +4928 -6  
Others: +35 -1  

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Stacked on #4654.** Its SCM changes are included because this cross-fork PR targets main. Review #4654 first; the tracker and intake changes build on it.
>
## What

A OneDev issue-tracker adapter and multi-provider issue intake, with provider selection in the CLI and project forms.

## Why

Fixes #4557.

Issue intake is the part of AO people actually use to drive a fleet from a board. With the SCM provider from #4654 alone, a OneDev user can have their PRs observed but still cannot spawn a worker from an issue — the intake path had no way to reach a third provider.

## How

- **`ports.Tracker` is read-only, and this respects that.** The adapter implements `Get`/`List`/`Preflight` only. AO hydrates a worker's prompt from an issue but never writes status back, so a OneDev board does not reflect what a fleet is doing. That is upstream's port design and I have not widened it here — I mention it because it is the first question a user asks, and the honest answer today is "transition the issue from the worker side".
- **States are not pre-validated.** OneDev issue states are per-instance configuration and no endpoint lists them to a non-administrator. Rather than guess a fixed set, `states.go` surfaces the server's own error plus the states it can observe in use. It is the least-wrong option, but I would take a better one.
- **Provider selection is per project.** An omitted provider is preserved for origin inference. The CLI exposes `--tracker-provider`, and project creation and settings expose the same choice. The OpenAPI and TypeScript schema are regenerated.
- **No behaviour change for existing GitHub or GitLab projects.** A project with no explicit provider resolves from its origin; regression tests retain nested GitLab path coverage alongside explicit OneDev cases.

## Review fixes and scope

An omitted provider stays empty so existing GitHub and GitLab projects retain origin inference, including nested GitLab paths. OneDev remains excluded from the manual spawn request enum: this PR supports OneDev through issue intake. Tracker construction rejects multiple OneDev hosts until workflow state and assignee-field settings are scoped per host.

The UI preserves a selected provider when editing or disabling intake. Choosing Automatic clears the explicit provider.

## Testing

Rebased on the updated #4654. Focused backend race tests, backend build, strict lint, and frontend type checking pass. All 334 frontend test files passed across the full run and a retry of three files after installing their missing native dependencies. Four new UI tests cover selection, preservation, and clearing. An isolated browser fixture verified OneDev selection and preservation when intake is disabled.

The full backend race run on the SCM base found an installed Codex protocol mismatch that also fails on unchanged upstream; a tmux failure passed on an isolated retry. The full backend suite was not repeated on the intake branch.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Full backend suite is green in CI (local protocol mismatch described above)

title: tmux runtime: Restart always fails when base-index or pane-base-index is not 0
body:
### Summary

`respawn-pane` and the pane-pid probe hardcode the tmux target `<session>:0.0`, and nothing in the runtime reads tmux's `base-index` / `pane-base-index`. Both default to `0`, but setting them to `1` is one of the most common tmux customisations there is — so on those machines the session's only pane is `<session>:1.1` and every `<session>:0.0` target misses.

The user-visible effect is that **`Runtime.Restart` always fails**, which is the path session restore uses. It also fails `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` and `TestAttachmentStreamsRealTmuxPane`, so the failure looks like flaky integration tests rather than a runtime bug.

Two sites, both in `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/commands.go`:

```go
// :24  respawnPaneArgs
"respawn-pane", "-k",
"-t", id + ":0.0",

// :61  panePIDArgs
return []string{"display-message", "-p", "-t", id + ":0.0", "#{pane_pid}"}
```

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained, no AO required — it isolates its own server and config:

```sh
CONF=$(mktemp); printf 'set -g base-index 1\nset -gw pane-base-index 1\n' > "$CONF"
export TMUX_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
tmux -f "$CONF" new-session -d -s aorepro 'sleep 300'

tmux list-panes -a -F '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}'   # aorepro:1.1

tmux respawn-pane -k -t aorepro:0.0 -c /tmp sh -c 'sleep 300'   # what AO does today
tmux respawn-pane -k -t aorepro   -c /tmp sh -c 'sleep 300'     # proposed
```

Against AO itself, with `base-index 1` / `pane-base-index 1` in your tmux config:

```
cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/ -run TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell
```

### Expected behavior

`Restart` respawns the session's only pane regardless of the user's `base-index` / `pane-base-index`.

### Actual behavior

```
tmux runtime: restart session <id>: exit status 1: can't find pane: 0
```

The exact message depends on which option is non-zero, because tmux resolves the window before the pane. Measured on tmux 3.7c, single AO-style session, `respawn-pane -k -t <s>:0.0`:

| `base-index` | `pane-base-index` | real target | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | `c:0.0` | ok |
| 0 | 1 | `c:0.1` | `can't find pane: 0` |
| 1 | 0 | `c:1.0` | `can't find window: 0` |
| 1 | 1 | `c:1.1` | `can't find window: 0` |

One wrinkle worth flagging: **`panePIDArgs` does not fail.** `display-message -p -t <s>:0.0 '#{pane_pid}'` silently falls back rather than erroring, and in every single-pane case above it returned the correct pid. So that call site is latent today rather than broken — but it is the same unchecked assumption, and it would stop being harmless the moment a session has more than one pane.

### AO version

`ao version dev`, built from `main` at `759595a9`.

### Environment

- Arch Linux, tmux 3.7c
- `base-index 1`, `pane-base-index 1` set globally in `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`
- Reproduced against `main` with no local patches; the standalone snippet above reproduces with no AO at all

### Logs / extra context

**Suggested fix — target the session name alone.** `respawn-pane -t <session>` and `display-message -t <session>` resolve to the session's current window and active pane, which for AO is the only pane (`respawnPaneArgs`' own comment says "the session's only pane", and there is no `new-window` or `split-window` anywhere in the runtime). Verified working on the `base-index 1` / `pane-base-index 1` server above.

That also matches what this file already does elsewhere — `setStatusOffArgs`, `setMouseOnArgs` and `setWindowSizeLargestArgs` all pass bare `id`, with a comment explaining the targeting choice. So the fix makes the file more internally consistent, not less.

If you would rather keep an explicit pane target, the index-safe form is to resolve it once (`display-message -p -t <session> '#{pane_id}'` gives a stable `%N` that is immune to both options) and target that. I have a preference for the simpler one but no strong opinion — happy to send whichever you prefer as a PR, with the two integration tests as the regression proof.

I did not fold this into #4654 or #4655 (OneDev provider work) since it is unrelated to those.

title: Chat's per-delta SQLite writes make v0.12.9 unusable with the data dir on NFS, and 0105 silently opts existing installs in
body:
## Summary

Upgrading from `v0.12.6` to `v0.12.9` made the first prompt of every new session take **3+ minutes** instead of seconds, on a deployment whose `AO_DATA_DIR` is on NFS.

Two separate things combine:

1. **`0105_default_session_mode_chat.sql` overwrites an explicit preference on existing installs**, silently moving them from TUI to Chat.
2. **Chat persists one row per provider event with no batching**, which is fine on local disk and pathological when `ao.db` is on a network filesystem.

Either alone is defensible. Together they turn a routine upgrade into a severe, silent regression.

---

## 1. Migration 0105 rewrites a preference rather than seeding a default

`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0105_default_session_mode_chat.sql`:

```sql
UPDATE app_settings
SET default_session_mode = 'chat', updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE id = 1;
```

`0067_app_settings.sql` declares `default_session_mode TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'tui'`, so this is not "new installs get Chat" — it rewrites the row on **every** existing database, discarding whatever the operator had chosen. `TestMigrateUpdatesExistingSessionInterfaceDefaultToChat` asserts this is intentional, so I assume it was a deliberate product rollout rather than an oversight.

The problem is that it is unconditional and unannounced. There is no way to distinguish "user never expressed a preference" from "user deliberately chose TUI", and nothing surfaces the change in the UI, so the mode silently flips under an operator who had picked TUI on purpose. Its own `Down` migration takes the opposite position and refuses to clobber:

```sql
-- The previous preference cannot be reconstructed safely. Preserve it rather
-- than replacing a deliberate Chat choice during rollback.
```

That reasoning applies equally to `Up`.

**Suggestions**, roughly in order of preference:
- Only set the value when it is still at the schema default and the install has no sessions — i.e. treat it as seeding, not migrating.
- Or record that the flip happened and surface it once in the UI, so the change is visible rather than silent.
- Or gate it on a new column that records whether the preference was ever explicitly set.

---

## 2. Chat writes per provider event; unusable with the database on NFS

`conversation_provider_events` is written only by `service/chat/controller.go`, so this cost is exclusive to Chat mode — a TUI session writes none of it.

Measured on a fresh database, for **one 200-word reply** (no tool calls):

| Table | Rows |
|---|---|
| `conversation_provider_events` | 110 |
| `change_log` (`session_updated`) | 120 |

Plus one trigger-driven `UPDATE` per inserted event, from `0087_conversation_branches.sql`:

```sql
CREATE TRIGGER conversation_provider_events_branch_insert
AFTER INSERT ON conversation_provider_events
WHEN NEW.branch_id = ''
BEGIN
    UPDATE conversation_provider_events
    SET branch_id = (SELECT active_branch_id FROM conversations WHERE id = NEW.conversation_id)
    WHERE id = NEW.id;
END
```

So a single short reply costs several hundred write operations, each needing WAL locks.

### Why NFS turns that into minutes

Every WAL read transaction takes an `fcntl` lock on the `-shm` index. Over NFS that is a network round trip with multi-second tail latency, and `modernc.org/sqlite` serialises every connection behind one process-global mutex — so one slow lock stalls **every** query in the daemon, not just the chat path.

Goroutine dump taken during a stall (`AO_DEBUG_STACKS`-style `runtime.Stack`), showing a plain `GetSession` blocked:

```
goroutine [sync.Mutex.Lock]:
  modernc.org/libc.Xpthread_mutex_lock
  modernc.org/sqlite/lib._pthreadMutexEnter
  modernc.org/sqlite/lib.Xsqlite3_mutex_enter
  modernc.org/sqlite/lib._unixShmLock
  modernc.org/sqlite/lib._walLockShared
  modernc.org/sqlite/lib._walTryBeginRead
  modernc.org/sqlite/lib._walBeginReadTransaction
  ...storage/sqlite/store.(*Store).GetSession
  ...service/chat.(*Service).requireChatSession
  ...httpd/controllers.(*ConversationsController).configOptions
```

In the same dump, blocked on that one mutex simultaneously: the CDC poller (`EventsAfter`), the preview poller (`ListAllSessions`), the usage collector (`UpdateUsageBin`), a session list (`ListPRFactsForSession`) and the chat controller — while one goroutine sat in `[syscall]` holding it.

### Measurements

Same prompt, same model (`claude-code`), same host, **only the database location differing** (`AO_DB_DIR`):

| | `ao.db` on NFS | `ao.db` on local disk |
|---|---|---|
| turn total | **3 m 17 s** | **9.4 s** |
| delta stream span | 174.8 s | 5.8 s |
| stalls ≥ 1 s | 33, totalling 172.7 s (**99% of the turn stalled**) | 0 |
| `GET …/conversation/config-options` during the turn | 2.1–5.1 s | 0.0005 s |
| `GET /api/v1/settings` during the turn | **60 s timeout** (`context deadline exceeded`) | 1.4 ms |

The second turn in the *same* session was ~21× faster than the first, which is what made this so confusing to diagnose — it reads like a warm-up cost rather than a storage problem.

For contrast: `claude-code` invoked directly, outside AO, produced a comparable 1366-character reply in **17 s**. The agent and the provider were never the bottleneck.

**Suggestions:**
- Batch provider-event persistence (one transaction per turn, or time/size-windowed flushes) instead of one write per delta. Streaming UI updates do not need to be durable per token.
- Consider whether `conversation_provider_events` needs to be durable at all, or whether it could be capped/sampled — it is by far the highest-volume table.
- Avoid bumping the session row (and thus `change_log`) once per delta.
- Fold the `branch_id` assignment into the `INSERT` so the trigger `UPDATE` disappears.

---

## Reproduction

1. Put `AO_DATA_DIR` on an NFS mount (leave `AO_DB_DIR` unset so `ao.db` lands there).
2. Upgrade an install that had `default_session_mode = 'tui'` to `v0.12.9`; observe it is now `chat`.
3. Spawn a worker session and send any prompt that produces a couple of paragraphs.
4. The reply trickles in over minutes; `GET /api/v1/settings` can time out entirely while it does.
5. Set `AO_DB_DIR` to a local directory and repeat: seconds.

## Environment

- AO `v0.12.9`, Linux x86_64
- `AO_DATA_DIR` on NFS; multiple hosts must resolve identical absolute paths under it, so moving the data dir to local disk is not an option — only `AO_DB_DIR` is
- `modernc.org/sqlite` `v1.57.0` (also reproduced with the `v1.51.0` that `v0.12.9` pins)
- Agent: `claude-code`, no tool calls in the measured turns

## Workarounds

`AO_DB_DIR=<local dir>` fixes the performance problem completely and is documented behaviour; a per-install `UPDATE app_settings SET default_session_mode='tui'` (or a follow-on migration) undoes the mode flip. Both are what we have deployed. Filing because the defaults do the wrong thing for network-filesystem installs and the mode change is invisible.

Happy to split this into two issues if you would rather track them separately, and happy to open a PR for the batching or for the seeding-vs-migrating change if you have a preferred direction.

title: bug(reviewer): Claude restore double-hashes session identity
body:
## Bug

A restored Claude Code reviewer can fail immediately with:

> No conversation found with session ID: 03dc146e-e3b6-5d88-a3a3-15fe9f6354bc

The reviewer terminal remains present with no Claude child process, while the associated `review_run` remains durably `running`.

**Source:** AO orchestrator chat report on 2026-08-30  
**Reported by:** AO user (live local observation)  
**Analyzed against:** `d28e46dea577e45f9c995a59f3dfbcfcfe72bb59` (`upstream/main`)  
**AO binary:** packaged rewrite binary, `dev`, verified ready on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64; Claude Code 2.1.251  
**Confidence:** High

![Reviewer terminal showing No conversation found](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-claude-reviewer-double-hash-20260830/.issue-assets/claude-reviewer-double-hash/reviewer-no-conversation.png)

## Reproduction

1. Start a Claude Code reviewer for a worker session.
2. Allow it to create a real Claude conversation/transcript.
3. Restart or otherwise restore the reviewer terminal.
4. Open the Reviewer's terminal tab.
5. Observe `claude --resume <persisted-id>` fail with `No conversation found`.

Observed live instance:

- AO worker: `agent-orchestrator-149` (`pr author avatar`)
- reviewer AO ID: `review-agent-orchestrator-149`
- persisted `review.agent_session_id`: `03dc146e-e3b6-5d88-a3a3-15fe9f6354bc`
- actual Claude transcript ID: `a04d0453-97e8-51ee-84bf-ebe1d2a4a90b`
- persisted-ID transcript: absent
- actual transcript: present and non-empty
- restored pty host invokes `claude --resume 03dc146e-...`, but has no Claude child after the failure
- newest review run `201113cb-b4cf-437a-bb19-e5b0de73a662` has remained `running` since 2026-08-27

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/claudecode/claudecode.go:76-96` first maps the reviewer AO ID to a Claude UUID:

```go
agentSessionID := workeragent.SessionUUID(inv.ReviewerID)
```

It persists that value as `ReviewCommandSpec.AgentSessionID`, but also passes the already-derived UUID as `LaunchConfig.SessionID`.

`backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go:211-221` treats `SessionID` as an AO identity and derives a Claude UUID again:

```go
cmd = append(cmd, "--session-id", ClaudeSessionID(cfg.SessionID))
```

Consequently:

- AO persists `UUIDv5(reviewerID)`
- Claude launches with `UUIDv5(UUIDv5(reviewerID))`
- restore uses the persisted single-hashed ID
- Claude only has a transcript for the double-hashed ID

This mismatch was introduced by commit `d15fd8277c1b63a1a7ebdb55735b9ed6091cf118` in [PR #3484](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3484).

The recent daemon/reconciliation incident triggered a restore and exposed the bug, but did not create the deterministic ID mismatch.

## Fix

1. Make reviewer launch use the exact native ID AO persists. Prefer passing the derived UUID through `LaunchConfig.NativeSessionID`, or pass the raw reviewer AO ID through `SessionID`; do not hash an already-derived native ID.
2. Add an integration-level adapter test asserting the actual emitted `--session-id` equals `ReviewCommandSpec.AgentSessionID`. Existing capture-agent tests only observe the intermediate launch config and therefore missed the second transformation.
3. Preserve existing reviewer conversations created by buggy versions: when the persisted single-hashed transcript is absent but the legacy double-hashed transcript exists, resume the legacy identity and safely migrate/persist it.
4. Ensure a failed reviewer restore transitions its running review run to a failed/retryable state instead of leaving it permanently `running`.

## Impact

- Restored Claude Code reviewers can lose access to their real conversation.
- Automatic review work is blocked until the reviewer is recreated or repaired.
- Review runs may appear active indefinitely despite no reviewer process.
- Every Claude reviewer launched through this path since the regression is potentially affected on restore.

## Related

- [PR #3484](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3484): introduced persisted reviewer-native identity during lifecycle restoration.
- [Issue #2702](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2702): broader runtime restoration/zombie-session failure mode; related subsystem but not this double-hash defect.

title: fix(reviewer): resume Claude after reviewer relaunch
body:
Fixes #4658

## Summary
- pass the persisted Claude reviewer UUID through the explicit native-session field so first launch emits the exact deterministic ID AO owns instead of hashing it twice
- detect and resume both current transcripts and the legacy double-derived transcript, then persist any repaired identity
- when a reviewer pane/process has exited but its durable native ID remains, route the next review launch through `--resume` instead of colliding on `--session-id`
- preserve Claude's read-only tool policy and system prompt on resume, and deliver the new review task as the resume-time user turn
- surface transcript/restore failures without silently fresh-launching; the existing liveness gate continues to notify a genuinely live reviewer rather than starting a duplicate
- fall back to a fresh idle reviewer when native history is unavailable and mark interrupted running review runs failed so they can be retried

## Root cause
Commit `d15fd8277c1b63a1a7ebdb55735b9ed6091cf118` (`fix: align reviewer terminal lifecycle`, PR #3484) introduced deterministic reviewer identity persistence and native restore support, but split ownership incorrectly in two related ways:

1. `ReviewCommand` derived a Claude UUID, persisted it, then passed it as an AO `SessionID`; the worker command builder derived it again. AO therefore persisted the single-derived ID while Claude owned the double-derived transcript, producing `No conversation found` on restore.
2. Ordinary new-review reruns still called `Launcher.Spawn`, whose path always built a fresh command. After cancellation/process exit, `review.agent_session_id` survived while the pane did not, so Claude received `--session-id <existing transcript>` and failed with `Session ID ... is already in use`.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/... ./internal/review/...`
- `go build ./...`
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_TMUX_BINARY -u AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_RUN_FILE go test ./...`
- isolated-cache `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs` (`0 issues`)

## Risk
Low and scoped to reviewer identity/restore selection. A normal review launch attempts native resume only when a durable reviewer-native ID exists; first launch remains fresh and deterministic. Claude only resumes after finding a non-empty transcript. Probe/restore errors are surfaced, and a live reviewer pane is still handled by the existing notify path.

title: bug(send): orchestrator and worker cannot exchange messages while the session is paused on a permission decision
body:
## Bug

When a worker session is paused on a permission decision (`SESSION_AWAITING_DECISION`),
`ao send` is blocked **in both directions**:

- the orchestrator cannot deliver anything to that worker — every `ao send` is rejected;
- the worker's own question never reaches the orchestrator in readable form. The
  orchestrator sees only `status: needs_input` / `activity: blocked` with no indication
  of what was asked.

The session is effectively out of the orchestrator's control until a human opens that
session's terminal and answers the dialog. The orchestrator cannot even tell the worker
"cancel that, here is the answer" — the very channel needed to unblock it is the one
that is blocked.

## Observed

```
$ ao send --session hhru-404 --message "..."
Session is paused on a permission decision; answer it in the session terminal first
(SESSION_AWAITING_DECISION)
```

`ao session get hhru-404` showed only:

```
status: needs_input
activity: blocked
updated: 2026-08-30T05:03:59Z
```

The worker stayed blocked ~35 minutes. Its question — a scope clarification that the
orchestrator could have answered in seconds — was invisible. After the human answered
the dialog in the session terminal, the queued `ao send` messages were delivered and the
worker resumed normally, confirming the messages were queued rather than lost.

## Why this matters

The orchestrator's job is to keep workers unblocked. This defect inverts that: the
moment a worker most needs an answer, the orchestrator is cut off from giving one, and
a human must intervene for a question the orchestrator was fully able to resolve.

With a fleet of parallel workers this scales badly — each permission dialog is a
mandatory human interrupt, and the human has no idea it is waiting unless they watch
the board.

## Expected

At minimum one of:

1. **Surface the question.** `ao session get` / `ao session ls` should expose what the
   session is asking, so the orchestrator (and the human) can see the pending decision
   without opening the session terminal.
2. **Allow delivery while blocked.** Accept `ao send` and queue it (messages already
   queue correctly — they arrived intact after unblocking), or let it answer/cancel the
   pending dialog.
3. **Let the orchestrator respond to the dialog** through a dedicated command, e.g.
   `ao session answer <id> <choice>`, for decisions that do not require the human.

(1) alone would remove most of the pain: knowing what is asked lets the human answer in
one second instead of investigating a silently stalled session.

## Environment

- Orchestrator: Claude Code harness, project with 3-9 parallel workers.
- Worker: Claude Code harness (`hhru-404`), spawned via `ao spawn --issue`.
- Observed 2026-08-30.

## Related, not duplicate

- #3738 — sticky `waiting_input` after a turn where the agent asked **nothing**. Here the
  agent genuinely asked, and the state is correct; the defect is the blocked channel and
  the invisible question.
- #2342 / #3626 — `ao send` multiline delivery problems. Different cause: here delivery
  is refused outright by the awaiting-decision guard, not silently unsubmitted.
- #4333 — Cursor startup MCP approval consuming follow-ups (closed, harness-specific
  startup race).

title: Chat UI shows stale incomplete plan count after worker turn actually completed
body:
## Summary
A completed Chat turn can keep an earlier non-terminal plan snapshot, so the chat UI shows an incomplete plan badge such as `0/3` or `0/4` even though the worker finished all work and posted the final completion message.

## Environment
- Date observed: 2026-08-30
- App build: `ao version` => `dev`
- Daemon/API: local desktop AO on `127.0.0.1:3001`
- Local checkout analyzed: `c26f5f1aa14399017e3de54f0522cd18b79e6f9f`
- Note: local `main` was behind `origin/main` by 2 commits at triage time

## Reported session
- Session: `agent-orchestrator-154`
- Display name: `review agent hooks`
- Mode: `chat`
- Conversation ID: `9c89bcc4-e796-4f4b-b6d3-d50a7f4d47fc`
- Affected turn ID: `0634673f-d5d8-4af6-aeef-fd940fe320b5`
- Provider turn ID: `01a04673-66d8-7a11-8a05-dddefb5f0d72`

## What happened
The final assistant message for the affected turn says the work is done and pushed:
- PR rebased onto `main`
- conflict resolved
- targeted verification run completed
- branch pushed

But the durable turn plan served to the UI still shows the initial plan state:
- step 1: `in_progress`
- steps 2-4: `pending`

Because the frontend plan header counts only steps whose status is `completed`, the UI displays an incomplete badge for a turn that is already `completed`.

## Evidence
### Durable turn record
`conversation_turns.plan_json` for turn `0634673f-d5d8-4af6-aeef-fd940fe320b5`:

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "text": "Fetch `main` and start a rebase of PR #4551 branch onto the latest base branch",
      "status": "in_progress"
    },
    {
      "text": "Inspect each conflict, resolve it in place, and keep the reviewer-hook behavior intact",
      "status": "pending"
    },
    {
      "text": "Run targeted verification for the rebased review-related backend/frontend paths",
      "status": "pending"
    },
    {
      "text": "Push the rebased branch and report the result",
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Final assistant message on the same turn
Stored conversation message sequence `461` on the same turn:

- `PR #4551 is rebased onto the current main and pushed.`
- conflict resolved by renumbering migration to `0117_review_activity_state.sql`
- targeted backend verification run completed
- pushed branch head `40e55caaa`

### Raw provider-event history
For provider turn `01a04673-66d8-7a11-8a05-dddefb5f0d72`, the durable provider event log contains:
- one `turn.plan` at `2026-08-28 03:39:31Z`
- many later `message.completed` events
- `turn.completed` at `2026-08-28 03:42:10Z`
- no later `turn.plan` with completed steps

Method counts for that provider turn include:
- `turn.plan`: `1`
- `turn.completed`: `2` (including one history replay)
- `message.completed`: `13`

So the UI is not inventing stale state; it is rendering the plan AO persisted and served.

## Expected
Once the turn is completed, the plan displayed for that turn should not still read as partially pending if the turn has already produced its final successful completion message.

## Actual
The completed turn still exposes the earlier in-progress plan, so the UI shows an incomplete plan count.

## Likely root cause
This looks like a backend/controller gap rather than a frontend rendering bug.

Relevant code paths:
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnPlan.tsx`
  - counts only `step.status === "completed"`
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go`
  - `ChatEventPlanUpdated` overwrites `conversation_turns.plan_json`
  - `ChatEventTurnCompleted` settles only turn state and does not reconcile/finalize the stored plan
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/conversation_store.go`
  - `SetTurnPlan` only persists what arrived from `turn.plan`

That means if Codex sends an early plan snapshot but never sends a terminal all-completed plan update before `turn.completed`, AO leaves the stale plan in durable state forever.

## Why this seems like the missing test case
Existing plan tests cover the happy path where the provider emits a second `plan_updated` event with all steps completed. They do not appear to cover:
- a turn that completes successfully
- final assistant text is written
- no later terminal `turn.plan` arrives
- stale non-terminal plan remains on the completed turn

## Suggested direction
Either:
1. finalize remaining plan steps when a turn completes successfully and the current stored plan is still non-terminal, or
2. explicitly clear/hide non-terminal plan state for completed turns when no terminal plan revision arrived, or
3. if the provider contract guarantees a terminal plan update, add detection/logging/tests around missing final `turn.plan` events so AO can repair or at least diagnose it.

## Repro confidence
High for the stale-state condition in durable data.

I verified locally that:
- the frontend is reading the snapshot correctly
- the snapshot contains the stale plan
- the turn itself is marked completed
- the provider event log for the same turn has only one `turn.plan` and no terminal plan update
