title: [Cloud][P0] Packaged renderer CSP blocks every cloud terminal WebSocket
body:
## What

In any **packaged/built** desktop app, a cloud session's terminal never connects: the renderer's Content-Security-Policy refuses the direct `wss://` connection to the control plane, so the terminal shows "Connecting…" forever. Dev-mode (`npm run dev`) is unaffected, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Root cause

`frontend/vite.renderer.config.ts` injects a CSP meta tag with `apply: "build"` (built renderers only). Its `connect-src` is:

```
connect-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:* ws://127.0.0.1:* <posthog>
```

The cloud terminal deliberately dials `wss://<control-plane>/api/cloud/v1/terminal?ticket=…` **directly from the renderer** (single-use ticket auth; the WorkOS token stays in the Electron main process — see `frontend/src/renderer/lib/cloud-terminal-mux.ts`). That origin is not in `connect-src`, so Chromium refuses the socket before any packet leaves the machine. Every other CP call rides the main-process proxy and is unaffected — including terminal-**ticket** minting, which keeps succeeding while the attach never happens.

## Evidence (staging, 2026-08-30)

- A dev on a packaged build: 4 sessions (claude-code **and** codex), **2,600+ tickets minted, 0 consumed** (`ao_access_tickets`), zero `GET /api/cloud/v1/terminal` requests reaching the CP.
- Same app via `npm run dev` on another machine: 18 tickets minted, **18 consumed**, terminal works.
- In the packaged app's DevTools, `new WebSocket("wss://echo.websocket.org")` fails instantly with no Network-tab row (classic CSP refusal); the same snippet succeeds in a dev-mode build.

## Fix

Add the cloud control-plane WebSocket origins to `connect-src` in the built CSP (baked defaults `wss://staging-api.aoagents.dev` / `wss://api.aoagents.dev`, extendable via the existing `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` override at build time). PR incoming.

## Follow-up worth considering

Tunneling the terminal WebSocket through the Electron main process (like every other CP call) would remove the renderer-egress requirement entirely, at the cost of a bigger change to the mux.

title: [Bug][Cloud][P1] Cloud terminal WebSockets are severed every ~60s by the ALB idle timeout
body:
## What

Every healthy cloud terminal WebSocket is cut by the staging ALB after exactly ~60 seconds of frame-level idle. The renderer's mux silently reconnects with a fresh ticket and replays, so the terminal *looks* fine, but every idle terminal cycles disconnect/reattach once a minute — visible as a hiccup on slow links, extra ticket/replay load, and a misleading error in the CP logs.

## Evidence (staging, 2026-08-30)

- `GET /api/cloud/v1/terminal` completions with status 101 and durations of **59998–60002 ms**, one per minute per attached terminal, for an actively used session.
- Matching CP warnings once per minute per terminal: `terminal stream ended unexpectedly | failed to get reader: failed to read frame header: EOF` (`cloud/internal/httpapi/terminal_handlers.go:159`), same `terminal_id` each time.

## Cause

The ALB's default idle timeout is 60s and applies per-connection to WebSockets. Neither side sends WebSocket ping/pong keepalives: `connectTerminal` (`cloud/internal/httpapi/terminal_handlers.go:72`) reads/writes only application frames, and the renderer mux (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/cloud-terminal-mux.ts`) writes only on user input. An idle PTY (no output, no input) therefore exchanges zero frames for 60s and gets chopped.

## Fix options

1. Server-side ping every ~20–30s in the terminal WebSocket loop (`websocket.Conn.Ping`) — smallest change, covers all clients including future web/mobile.
2. Additionally or alternatively raise the ALB idle timeout for staging/production (deploy scripts under `cloud/scripts/`).

Option 1 is the right permanent fix; 2 is belt-and-braces.

title: [Bug][Cloud][P1] Failed terminal attach retries forever: ~2 ticket mints/sec, no surfaced error, sandbox never idle-pauses
body:
## What

When the terminal WebSocket cannot attach (CSP block #4666, network/proxy filtering, or any client-side failure), the app retries indefinitely with **no backoff and no user-facing error**: the pane shows "Connecting…" forever while the mux mints a fresh terminal ticket for every attempt (~1–2/sec observed). Two costly side effects:

1. **The sandbox never idle-pauses.** `IssueTerminalTicket` (`cloud/internal/postgres/worker_transport_store.go:324`) deliberately refreshes the sandbox's `interactive_until` lease on every mint — correct for a real viewer, but a broken client turns it into an infinite keep-awake, billing compute indefinitely.
2. **The failure is invisible.** Tickets keep returning 201, so nothing distinguishes "worker still provisioning" from "attach permanently failing client-side".

## Evidence (staging, 2026-08-29/30)

- One dev's 4 sessions: 2,600+ tickets minted / 0 consumed within 45 min (`ao_access_tickets`), sandboxes held awake the whole time; ~840 mints per 10-minute window in the CP access log.
- The same signature ran overnight on 2 sessions, with sandboxes recreated repeatedly (3 provider boxes each) while nothing ever attached.

## Proposed fix

Renderer (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/cloud-terminal-mux.ts` + `useTerminalSession` reattach loop):
- Exponential backoff on attach failures (e.g. 1s → 30s cap), resetting on success.
- After N consecutive *mint-succeeded-but-socket-failed* cycles, surface a distinct terminal state: "Ticket issued but the WebSocket cannot connect — check proxy/firewall/CSP" instead of generic "Connecting…".

Control plane (defense in depth):
- Consider not refreshing `interactive_until` on every mint when the previous N tickets for the session were never consumed, so a broken client cannot hold a sandbox awake forever.

title: fix(frontend): allow cloud control-plane websockets in the packaged CSP
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4666 — in every **packaged** build, the renderer CSP (`connect-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:* ws://127.0.0.1:* <posthog>`) refused the cloud terminal's direct `wss://` connection to the control plane, so cloud terminals stayed on "Connecting…" forever. Dev-mode (`npm run dev`) skips the CSP meta (`apply: "build"`), which is why the bug only reproduced on packaged builds.

This adds the cloud control-plane websocket origins to `connect-src`:
- baked defaults `wss://staging-api.aoagents.dev` and `wss://api.aoagents.dev`, matching the control-plane URL defaults;
- a build-time `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` override (http(s) → ws(s) origin) so a custom control plane keeps a working terminal in packaged builds.

Everything else about the CSP is unchanged. The terminal's direct-dial design is intentional (single-use ticket is the socket's authorization; the WorkOS token never reaches the renderer — `lib/cloud-terminal-mux.ts`), so the CSP must allow the origin rather than the socket moving behind the proxy.

## Evidence

Staging, 2026-08-30: a dev on a packaged build minted **2,600+ terminal tickets with 0 consumed** across 4 sessions (claude-code and codex) — zero `GET /api/cloud/v1/terminal` requests ever reached the control plane; `new WebSocket("wss://echo.websocket.org")` failed instantly in the packaged app's console with no Network-tab row (CSP refusal), while the same dev-mode build on another machine redeemed 18/18 tickets and connected fine.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts` — emitted `index.html` CSP now reads `connect-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:* ws://127.0.0.1:* https://us.i.posthog.com https://us-assets.i.posthog.com wss://staging-api.aoagents.dev wss://api.aoagents.dev`.
- Follow-up issues from the same investigation: #4667 (ALB 60s idle timeout severs terminal websockets — needs server ping/pong), #4668 (attach-failure retry loop mints tickets ~2/s with no surfaced error and keeps sandboxes awake).

## Summary

- Fix the send button stuck on the loading spinner after [#4649](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4649): `editQueuedTurnPendingTurnId === queueEdit?.turnId` evaluated to `true` when both were `undefined`, so `savingQueuedEditPending` was permanently true and the composer could not send.
- Harden dispatch/`busy` handling introduced in [#4457](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4457): only treat `"pending"` dispatch as busy, release the sentinel immediately for queued sends, and refresh conversation snapshots in the background instead of awaiting refetch in mutation `onSuccess` (steer, send, queue ops).
- Surface `sendPending` on the composer send control and show a clear error when a send is blocked by an in-flight message.

## Root cause

| PR | Regression |
|---|---|
| **#4649** | `savingQueuedEditPending={editQueuedTurnPendingTurnId === queueEdit?.turnId}` → `undefined === undefined` → always loading, always blocked |
| **#4457 + #4649** | Accepted dispatch + awaited refetch kept `busy` / mutation pending after the daemon had already accepted work |

title: feat(cloud): orchestrator drives its worker sessions end-to-end (#4574)
body:
## Summary

Implements #4574 in full: a cloud orchestrator can now actually orchestrate — spawn workers, watch them, message them, get reports back, and kill them — and the human can see the whole thing in the app. Everything is gated behind the cloud offering; local sessions are byte-for-byte unchanged.

### Why it didn't work before

The plumbing existed (PR #4434) but the agents were never told about it: no `ao` documentation reached the sandbox, the orchestrator prompt was six lines, and workers had **no** system prompt at all. On top of that, messages to a still-provisioning worker raced the harness TUI, multi-line messages were shredded line-by-line, and there was no channel from a worker back to its orchestrator.

### What this PR does

**Teach the agents (root cause):**
- New `cloud/internal/skillassets` package: a cloud-grammar `using-ao` skill (SKILL.md + orchestration/pull-request guides) embedded in `ao-worker` and materialized into `<dataDir>/skills/using-ao` at boot. Deliberately not the desktop skill — the two CLIs have different grammars.
- Real standing prompts (`cloud/internal/workerexec/prompts.go`): the orchestrator prompt ports the desktop coordination rules (coordination-only, inspect-before-spawn, CI/review routing, ≤20-char labels) onto the cloud `ao` grammar; workers get their first-ever prompt (identity, session branch, `$AO_PULL_REQUEST_HELP`/`$AO_REVIEW_HELP` socket helpers, `ao claim-pr`), with report guidance conditional on having an orchestrator parent. Cursor's builder drops SystemPrompt upstream (known limitation, documented); the on-disk skill still applies.

**Reverse channel (`ao report`):**
- New `worker:report` scope, issued only to sessions with a `parent_session_id` (`issuedWorkerScopes`); `POST /worker/parent/messages` delivers into the parent's conversation with a `[from worker <id8> "<name>"]` provenance prefix. A worker can only ever reach its own parent, enforced twice (scope + SQL parent join).

**Reliable delivery:**
- Queued turns are held until the agent terminal has produced output plus a 2s grace (`workertransport` readiness gate) — no more typing into a TUI that hasn't started.
- Both injection paths encode multi-line text as one bracketed paste (`worker.EncodeTerminalInput`).
- Live terminal-input TTL raised 15s → 60s.

**Orchestrator visibility:**
- `/worker/children` and the new user-facing `GET /orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}/children` share one wire shape (`sessionChildResponse`) carrying `branch` and a full `prs[]` (number, url, state, ci, review, mergeability).
- `ao list` grows `--all` (terminated history, hidden by default), a BRANCH and PR column, and follows pagination cursors.

**Workers view in the app:**
- `OrchestratorChildrenSection` renders first in a cloud orchestrator's Summary tab: status dot + agent avatar + live status per worker, PR chips, terminated history de-emphasized, click-through to the worker session. 5s polling via `useOrchestratorChildren`; preview-mode mock seam for `dev:web`. Additive `workers` slot on `SessionInspectorSummaryView`; i18n in all 8 catalogs.

**Telemetry (main flows only, cloud-scoped, no user content):** `cloud_orchestrator_spawn_succeeded/_failed` (hashed project id), `cloud_workers_viewed` (count), `cloud_worker_opened` (has_pr).

### Tests

First unit tests in the `cloud/` module (previously zero `_test.go`):
- skill install/clobber + desktop-grammar-leak guard; PTY input encoding; turn-forwarding readiness gate (no claim before output+grace, paste-wrapped delivery, loud failure without a terminal); prompt selection per kind/parent; scope narrowing (+non-mutation); handler contracts via an embedded-interface stub store (scope 403s, includeTerminated plumbing, prs mapping, report happy/forbidden/empty, children endpoint happy/bad-UUID).
- Renderer: hook mapping/gating/preview tests + Workers section states/rows/navigation/telemetry tests.
- Docker smoke (`test-cloud-local.sh`) extended: skill file in the sandbox, prompts in harness argv (both kinds), **send-before-boot delivered through the readiness gate**, `ao report` landing in the orchestrator conversation, parentless report rejected, `ao list` branch+prs assertions, kill settling out of the default list but visible with `--all`.
- CI: new `cloud-build-test` job (gofmt/build/vet/test -race) + `cloud/**` path filter in the Go workflow.

### Verification run locally

- `cd cloud && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` — green (5 packages with tests).
- `npm run product-ui:check`, cloud-client typecheck/tests/build — green; `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — green; new renderer tests green (7/7).
- Full renderer vitest: 3106 passed; the 7 failures are pre-existing on this machine (all in `src/landing/**` needing its own npm install, plus two locale-sensitive chat-timestamp tests) — none touch files in this diff.
- Docker smoke + staging E2E: results to be posted as a follow-up comment (Docker daemon unavailable on the dev machine at time of writing).

### Out of scope (per issue)
Push-based child-state events (polling `ao list` stays), batch spawn, cross-worker dependency coordination, cursor SystemPrompt support (upstream `agentruntime` limitation, documented).

Closes #4574.

body:
## Bug

AO accepts a committed, non-bare local Git repository with no remote as a `Git repository` project, stores `defaultBranch: auto`, and then cannot spawn any worker or orchestrator for that project.

Spawn fails with `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` and recommends configuring a remote HEAD—even though this repository deliberately has no remote. The import flow neither asks for a default branch nor warns that the accepted project will be unable to spawn.

**Source:** live AO desktop report on 2026-08-30  
**Reported by:** AO user (local machine reproduction)  
**Analyzed against:** `687038fdb2bf432938e53f3bcf26b7054496b894` (`upstream/main`)  
**AO binary:** packaged Go rewrite, `dev`, verified ready on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, Git 2.39.5  
**Priority:** P2 — a supported import path yields an unusable project, but explicitly configuring `defaultBranch` is a workaround.  
**Confidence:** High

![Spawn failure after importing a remote-less Git repository](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-remoteless-import-default-branch-20260830/.issue-assets/remoteless-import-default-branch/spawn-error.png)

## Live repository evidence

Project: `workspace2`  
Path: `/Users/itrytoohard/AO_TEST/workspace2`

The repository is valid and has a committed local default candidate:

```text
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree  -> true
git symbolic-ref --short HEAD        -> main
git rev-parse refs/heads/main^{commit}
                                      -> a1d8bd354f6d0eb00bafaaf7a8cc1b2b1fbbc0c4
git remote -v                        -> no output
git config --local --get ao.defaultBranch
                                      -> no output
```

AO's project read model is:

```json
{
  "id": "workspace2",
  "kind": "single_repo",
  "path": "/Users/itrytoohard/AO_TEST/workspace2",
  "repo": "",
  "defaultBranch": "auto"
}
```

The folder also contains an unrelated nested `tmux/` repository, but the reported resolver error explicitly targets the `workspace2` root. The root's missing remote/default metadata deterministically explains the failure independently of that nested checkout.

## Reproduction

1. Create a local repository with a commit and no remote:

   ```shell
   mkdir local-only && cd local-only
   git init -b main
   touch README.md
   git add README.md
   git commit -m init
   ```

2. In AO desktop, choose **Add code → Open local repository** and import it as a **Git repository**.
3. AO registers the project successfully with `defaultBranch: auto`; the import UI does not ask for or record a default branch.
4. Try to create a worker task.
5. Observe:

   ```text
   default branch is unresolved: repository ... has no remote or AO-recorded default;
   configure this repository's primary remote and cached HEAD ...
   (DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED)
   ```

## Root Cause

The individual pieces are internally consistent, but the import contract and spawn contract do not meet:

1. `frontend/src/main/import-folder-scan.ts` only resolves cached `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`; otherwise it returns `auto`. A committed remote-less repository is detectable (`hasHead=true`, `hasRemote=false`) but no branch is carried into project creation.
2. `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx` accepts that repository. Its preflight only requests initialization for a missing commit; it does not request/confirm a default branch for a committed remote-less repository.
3. `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx:createProjectConfig` sends worker/orchestrator settings but no `defaultBranch`.
4. `backend/internal/service/project/service.go:Add` validates only that the path is a non-bare repository with a commit, then persists the project even when `defaultBranch:auto` cannot resolve locally.
5. `backend/internal/gitdefault/resolver.go:resolveAOInitialized` intentionally refuses to infer from local `HEAD` for user-created remote-less repositories and returns `no remote or AO-recorded default`.
6. `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:resolveWorktreeRefs` always appends a `git remote set-head` remediation for this unresolved case, even when `git remote` is empty.

The strict spawn behavior was introduced deliberately in [PR #3983](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3983) to avoid choosing a temporary checkout as the repository default. The fix should preserve that safety property rather than silently returning to HEAD inference at spawn time.

## Fix

- During local project import, distinguish a committed remote-less repository from an unborn repository.
- Require or explicitly confirm a default branch before completing import. The UI may prefill the current symbolic branch as a candidate, but the user's confirmation should make it an explicit project `defaultBranch` rather than implicit spawn-time inference.
- Pass the selected branch through project creation and persist it in `ProjectConfig.DefaultBranch`.
- Alternatively, reject registration with a structured, actionable error until a default is supplied; do not register a project that cannot create its first workspace.
- Make `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` remediation state-aware:
  - no remotes: direct the user to Project Settings or `ao project set-config <id> --default-branch <branch>`;
  - remote exists but has no cached/live HEAD: retain the `checkout.defaultRemote` / `git remote set-head` guidance.
- Add frontend preflight/import tests and backend service/workspace tests proving a committed remote-less repository either records an explicit branch or is rejected before registration.

## Workaround

For the live project:

```shell
ao project set-config workspace2 --default-branch main
```

The same setting is available in Project Settings. The local `refs/heads/main` branch is a valid base candidate once the default is explicit.

## Impact

- Local-only Git repositories can be imported but cannot launch agents.
- Users receive remediation that is impossible or inappropriate for repositories intentionally lacking remotes.
- Automatic orchestrator startup after project creation can fail immediately after an apparently successful import.
- The behavior is platform-independent and applies anywhere Git repositories without remotes are supported.

## Related

- [Issue #3981](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3981): automatic default-branch selection previously forced `main` and motivated strict authoritative resolution.
- [PR #3983](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3983): introduced the authoritative remote/AO-recorded resolver and explicit-branch workaround.

title: Interface switch failed: ACP session/load rejected — Claude session already running as background agent (needs attach or --fork-session)
body:
# Bug: "Interface switch failed" — ACP session/load rejects a session running as a background agent

## Environment
- Agent Orchestrator desktop **0.12.3** (`dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`), daemon `dev` on port 3001, macOS 24.6 (Darwin). Reproduced also with Agent Orchestrator desktop **0.12.9** on the same machine.
- Claude Code **2.1.251**
- Harness: claude-code; session `trade-wizz-8` (orchestrator role)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Have a Claude Code session running under AO (the session is launched as a background agent).
2. In the AO desktop UI, switch that session's interface to **chat** (resume chat).
3. AO calls ACP `session/load` with the same Claude session id.

## Actual
Toast **"Interface switch failed"**:

```
switch interface trade-wizz-8: resume chat: chat conversation resume failed: ACP session/load:
{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"Claude Code process exited with code 1.
stderr: Error: Session d0d0953b-7716-4603-afa0-05fba7846ad5 is currently running as a background agent (bg).
Use `claude agents` to find and attach to it, or add --fork-session to branch off a copy."}}
```

## Expected
- The interface switch attaches to the running session, or forks it (`--fork-session`) when the harness refuses to load a session that is already running as a background agent.
- At minimum, a clear message ("session is running in the background — attach or fork?") instead of a raw JSON-RPC internal error.

## Notes
- Claude Code's guard is by design (one live process per session id); AO's switch flow should handle it.
- `ao doctor` is otherwise all PASS (one WARN: 2 hook delivery failures in the last 24h, unrelated).

title: bug(chat): TUI to Chat switch fails outright for ACP (Claude Code) sessions when native history is unsettled - "snapshot is incomplete and cannot be refreshed"
body:
## Bug

Switching a terminal (TUI) session to the Chat UI fails **immediately** for ACP-backed (Claude Code) sessions with:

> Interface switch failed - switch interface `<session>`: resume chat: native conversation history snapshot is incomplete and cannot be refreshed: chat conversation history is not settled

Unlike #4120 (which waited ~45s and failed with "context deadline exceeded", now fixed), this fails right away with no wait. The API surfaces it as `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`.

## Mechanism (from code)

On a TUI to Chat switch, the chat controller rebuilds the structured timeline by reading the provider's native conversation history (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go`, `refreshNativeHistory`) and requires the replay to reach the transition checkpoint:

- If `ReadHistory` errors, or (`required && !checkpoint.reached(events)`), the controller treats the history as unsettled (`ErrChatHistoryUnsettled`) - synthesizing it at `controller.go:542` when `ReadHistory` returned nil but the checkpoint was not reached.
- If the reader implements `ChatHistoryRefresher`, the controller polls/refreshes until it settles or times out.
- If the reader does **not** implement `ChatHistoryRefresher`, it fails immediately at `controller.go:557`: `native conversation history snapshot is incomplete and cannot be refreshed: <unsettled>`.

The ACP chat driver (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/history.go`) implements `ChatHistoryReader` (`ReadHistory`) but **not** `ChatHistoryRefresher` - only `codexappserver` implements `RefreshHistory` (`.../codexappserver/history.go:200`). So for ACP (Claude Code) sessions, any unsettled or checkpoint-incomplete native replay at switch time is a hard, immediate failure with no retry path. Codex sessions do not hit this branch because their reader is refreshable and polls instead.

`backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go:461` maps `ErrChatHistoryUnsettled` to `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` and fails the transition.

## Impact

An ACP (Claude Code) session whose native history is momentarily unsettled, or whose ACP replay does not yet satisfy the switch checkpoint, cannot enter Chat mode at all, and there is no wait/retry for it to settle (the wait path exists only for refreshable readers). The user is stuck in TUI.

## Related (distinct)

- #4120 (closed, fixed): the refreshable/timeout variant - "...context deadline exceeded" after ~45s. Different code path (poll then timeout) and different error string.
- #4123 (closed): settle-wait polled an immutable cached ACP replay for the full 45s before failing. This report is the non-refreshable fast-fail, which may be a side effect of removing ACP from the polling path.
- #4424 (open): unscoped hook checkpoints permanently block TUI-to-Chat recovery - a different blocking cause.

## Suggested direction

Either make the ACP history reader a `ChatHistoryRefresher` so the controller can wait for the replay to settle like Codex, or make the controller degrade gracefully for non-refreshable readers (proceed with the available replay / defer the checkpoint) instead of hard-failing, so a transient unsettled state does not permanently block the switch.

## Source

- Live AO desktop report, 2026-08-30 (session `ao-6`), screenshot of the "Interface switch failed" banner.
- Analyzed against `origin/main` `c13289c1c32afa4acbc2508a4a5402175623cb3e`.
- Confidence: High on the code mechanism (files and lines cited); the specific live trigger (which unsettled turn or checkpoint gap) was not reproduced end to end.

title: fix: keep terminal colors in sync with AO theme
body:
## Summary

Cursor Agent can render its prompt bar with the wrong colors when AO switches between light and dark mode. This PR synchronizes the resolved AO theme with Cursor sessions at startup and while they are running.

## What changed

- Persist the resolved light/dark terminal scheme under AO's data directory.
- Inject `TERM_THEME` and `COLORFGBG` only into Cursor Agent processes.
- Answer Cursor's private color-scheme protocol and OSC 10/11/12 color probes through a dedicated protocol-input path.
- Scope protocol handling to Cursor terminals so shells, Codex, and other TUIs receive no unsolicited control bytes.
- Bound OSC response buffering and avoid duplicate OSC replies.
- Keep terminal theme-hint writes ordered and atomic.
- Prevent theme transitions from flashing terminal/composer chrome.
- Preserve the Cmd+K search query until the palette close animation completes, including reduced-motion environments.

## Root cause

Cursor probes terminal appearance through OSC and private CSI sequences. The renderer previously allowed those replies to be lost or treated like ordinary input, while new theme changes could leave Cursor's prompt bar using stale colors.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/termtheme ./internal/adapters/agent/cursor`
- `vitest run src/renderer/lib/osc-color-report.test.ts src/renderer/lib/cursor-color-scheme.test.ts`
- `npm --prefix frontend test -- src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx src/renderer/components/CommandPalette.test.tsx` — 120 tests passed
- `git diff --check`

The full frontend typecheck is currently blocked by the shared `packages/product-ui` workspace because its React/motion dependencies are unavailable in this checkout.

## Manual test plan

- [ ] Start a Cursor session in light mode; prompt bar is light.
- [ ] Start a Cursor session in dark mode; prompt bar is dark.
- [ ] Toggle the theme with an existing Cursor session open; colors update without restarting.
- [ ] Open a shell or non-Cursor terminal; no unsolicited control bytes or input corruption.
- [ ] Search in Cmd+K, select Toggle theme with Enter, and confirm the query does not flash empty while the palette closes.

title: fix(reviewer): resume Claude after dead-pane relaunch
body:
Fixes #4658
Supersedes #4659

## Summary
- keep first-launch Claude reviewer identity ownership exact: AO persists the same deterministic native UUID emitted through `--session-id`, including migration of the legacy double-derived transcript identity
- when a reviewer pane/process is dead but its native conversation is retained, route a new review launch through the reviewer restore boundary so Claude uses `--resume` instead of colliding on `--session-id`
- detect the existing Claude transcript before resuming, preserve the reviewer read-only tool policy and system prompt, and deliver the new review task as the resume-time user turn
- propagate transcript/restore failures instead of silently fresh-launching; the engine's existing liveness gate still notifies a genuinely live reviewer rather than starting a duplicate
- keep idle restore fallback explicit and mark interrupted running runs retryable when native history is unavailable

## Root cause
Commit `d15fd8277c1b63a1a7ebdb55735b9ed6091cf118` introduced deterministic reviewer identity persistence and a native restore adapter, but ordinary review reruns continued through `Launcher.Spawn`, which hard-coded fresh command construction. After cancellation or process exit, the durable `review.agent_session_id` survived while the pane did not, so the next task launched Claude with `--session-id <existing-id>` and Claude rejected the already-owned transcript.

The related `No conversation found` symptom had the same identity-ownership regression: the first implementation passed an already-derived Claude UUID as an AO `SessionID`, causing the command builder to derive it a second time. AO persisted the single-derived ID while Claude owned the double-derived transcript.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/... ./internal/review/...`
- `go build ./...`
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_TMUX_BINARY -u AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_RUN_FILE go test ./...`
- isolated-cache `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs` (`0 issues`)

## Risk
Low and scoped to reviewer launch/restore selection. A native restore is attempted only when a durable reviewer-native ID exists; first launch remains fresh. Missing transcripts fall back through the existing adapter behavior, while probe/restore errors are surfaced and never converted into a second fresh launch.

title: fix(project import): require explicit defaultBranch for remote-less committed repos (#4679)
body: Closes #4679. ## What this fixes A committed, non-bare local Git repository with no remote could be registered as a project, but its workers failed to spawn because AO had no way to know which branch to base new worktrees on. The strict spawn resolver (added in PR #3983 on upstream main) deliberately refuses to infer from a temporary checkout, so the remediation `git remote set-head` was impossible for the very repos that needed it. ## Implementation (this fork) This fork already has the spawn-side fallback (`baseRefCandidates` falls back to `refs/heads/` when no `origin/<...>` candidate resolves), so the missing piece was the import contract: confirm the base branch at import time rather than at spawn time. 1. `scanImportFolder` exposes `hasCommit` and `checkedOutBranch` on every repo entry (`frontend/src/main/import-folder-scan.ts`). 2. `remotelessDefaultBranchCandidate(repo)` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx` returns the repo's current symbolic HEAD (read from `checkedOutBranch`) iff `hasCommit && !hasRemote`. No hardcoded branch name. 3. The agent sheet (`CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx`) renders an editable "Default branch" field prefilled with the candidate. The user can edit, confirm, or clear. 4. Confirmed value is sent as `config.defaultBranch` and persisted in `ProjectConfig.DefaultBranch`. The existing API contract already accepted this field — no `npm run api` regen needed. 5. The fork's existing `gitworktree` adapter picks the persisted value up via `WorkspaceConfig.BaseBranch` and uses `refs/heads/` as a base candidate, so a remote-less repo with confirmed `trunk` spawns worktrees based on `trunk` instead of `main`. ## Evidence (live AO desktop, AO 0.10.0, this branch) **SCREENSHOT A — import preflight offers trunk** The agent sheet renders an editable "Default branch" field prefilled with `trunk` for committed remote-less repos. (TUI shot from the live AO app showing the prefilled value at submit time.) **SCREENSHOT B — Default branch persisted as `trunk`** Project Settings → Workflow for the imported project shows "Default branch: trunk" — i.e. `config.defaultBranch` round-tripped through the daemon. (Settings panel shot.) **SCREENSHOT C — orchestrator session running from a worktree based on trunk** The live orchestrator session for the `repo` project is active and running `run_commands` in its worktree at `~/.ao/dev/data/worktrees/repo/orchestrator/repo-orchestrator/`. This worktree was created from `refs/heads/trunk` (the user-confirmed default), proving the spawn path that previously failed with `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` is now unblocked for remote-less repos. ## Tests - 3 vitest files, 19 tests, all green (incl. 2 new `import-folder-scan` cases for committed/unborn repos, 5 `remotelessDefaultBranchCandidate` cases, 2 new `_shell-create-project-config` cases for `defaultBranch` propagation). - No new Go test added: `TestWorkspaceIntegrationCreateInRemotelessRepo` already covers the spawn side, and `TestManager_AddDetectsNonMainDefaultBranch` (existing) already asserts that an explicit `Config.DefaultBranch` round-trips through the service to the read model. The new code paths reuse both contracts. - `tsc --noEmit`: clean. ## Notes - The spawn-side state-aware remediation wording described in the upstream fix plan is not applicable to this fork: the `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` code path introduced by upstream PR #3983 does not exist here. The fork's spawn path already accepts any explicit `BaseBranch` and falls back to `refs/heads/` for remote-less repos, which is exactly the behavior the import confirmation is now feeding. - No schema or API regen required. The `defaultBranch` field was already present on the daemon's `ProjectConfig` and the controller's `AddInput`; this PR only sends it from the renderer.

title: test(frontend): 3 vitest specs assume en-US locale for Intl/toLocaleString, fail under any other system locale
body:
## Summary

Three frontend specs call date/number formatting without pinning a locale
(`Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, ...)`, `Number.prototype.toLocaleString()`),
then assert against an English-only shape. Both read the locale from the
process environment at run time, so the assertion is only true when the
machine running `vitest` has an en-US-ish locale (`LANG`/`LC_ALL`). Under any
other system locale (tested with `ru_RU.UTF-8`, but this is not
Russian-specific — any non-English locale changes month names, date order, and
the thousands separator) they fail with no code change involved.

Product code is unaffected — using the viewer's locale there is intentional.
This is a test-isolation gap, not a product bug.

## Repro

```bash
LC_ALL=ru_RU.UTF-8 LANG=ru_RU.UTF-8 npx vitest run \
  src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/components/settings/AgentModelCombobox.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.test.tsx
```

All three fail; the same run under `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` passes cleanly.

## Where

- `src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.test.tsx:310` — expects
  `/^Sent [A-Z][a-z]{2} \d{1,2}, \d{4}$/` (e.g. "Sent Aug 29, 2026"); a
  non-English locale renders a different month abbreviation and date order.
  Source: `dateFormatter` in `ChatTimelineItems.tsx:95`
  (`new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {...})`).
- `src/renderer/components/settings/AgentModelCombobox.test.tsx:71` — expects
  the literal string `"Showing 50 of 1,397 matching models — type to narrow"`;
  a non-English locale uses a different thousands separator (e.g. `1 397`).
  Source: `AgentModelCombobox.tsx:273-274`
  (`visibleModels.length.toLocaleString()`).
- `src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.test.tsx` — same date-format
  dependency as the first file.

## Why this matters

CI presumably runs under an English locale so this stays invisible there, but
any contributor whose machine's system locale isn't English gets spurious
local failures on `npx vitest run` with no connection to the change they're
actually reviewing — easy to misdiagnose as a real regression.

## Suggested fix

Pin a locale explicitly in the failing specs (e.g.
`new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {...})` / `.toLocaleString("en-US")`) rather
than relying on `undefined`/ambient locale, or set `LC_ALL=en-US.UTF-8` (or
equivalent) in the vitest setup/config so all specs run under one fixed
locale regardless of the host machine.

title: feat(files): select between workspace and associated PR diffs
body:
## Feature

The Files explorer currently—and correctly—shows files from the session's live workspace checkout. A session can also own one or more pull requests whose source branches are checked out in separate worktrees or are not checked out locally at all. Add a source selector so users can choose whether the explorer displays the current workspace or a specific associated PR.

## Example

Session `agent-orchestrator-153` owns [PR #4692](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4692), but the two sources are different:

```text
Workspace branch: ao/agent-orchestrator-153/root
Workspace HEAD:   333ae81bb356
Workspace change: private/ao-cloud (deleted)

PR source branch: ao/agent-orchestrator-153/readme-download-section
PR head:          fc60f070fa81
PR change:        README.md
```

The current Files explorer correctly displays the workspace deletion:

![Files explorer showing the current workspace change](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-files-pr-workspace-mismatch-20260830/.issue-assets/files-pr-workspace-mismatch/changed-files-sidebar.png)

To inspect `README.md`, the user currently has to leave AO and open the provider's PR Files view.

## Proposed UX

Add a source dropdown to the Files explorer header, near the existing search and Changed only controls.

Example options:

```text
Workspace · ao/agent-orchestrator-153/root   (default)
PR #4692 · readme-download-section
PR #4701 · follow-up-tests
```

- **Workspace** remains the default and preserves today's behavior. It shows committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked changes from the session worktree using the existing workspace comparison base.
- Add one option for each PR associated with the session. The label should include the PR number and enough branch/title context to distinguish multiple or stacked PRs.
- Selecting a PR displays that PR's exact `base...head` file list and diffs, even when its branch is checked out in another worktree or is not the session's current checkout.
- Switching the display source must be read-only: it must not check out branches, alter the worker's worktree, move HEAD, touch the index, or disturb dirty files.
- Clearly show the active source above the file list and in empty/error states so users know whether they are reviewing Workspace or PR changes.
- Preserve the selected source per session while the inspector remains open; if the selected PR disappears or becomes unavailable, fall back to Workspace with an explanatory message.

## Backend/read-model direction

The existing endpoint `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/files` is intentionally workspace-backed. Keep that semantic intact. Add either a PR-specific endpoint or an explicit source parameter/read model that returns:

- source kind (`workspace` or `pull_request`);
- source identity and display label;
- workspace branch/HEAD or PR number/URL/source branch;
- comparison base SHA/ref and head SHA;
- file summaries and per-file content/diff for that exact source.

PR mode should use the persisted/provider `baseSHA` and `headSHA`, fetching the necessary refs or using isolated temporary review state when objects are not locally available. It must not assume the session worktree HEAD equals the PR head.

File/line feedback sent to the agent should carry the selected source identity so a comment on PR #4692 cannot be mistaken for a workspace-only path or another associated PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- Files explorer defaults to the current Workspace source.
- A session with one associated PR can switch between Workspace and that PR.
- A session with multiple sibling or stacked PRs can select each PR independently.
- PR mode matches the provider's changed-file set for the selected base/head pair.
- PR mode works when the PR branch is in a separate worktree or not checked out.
- Switching sources never mutates the session workspace or dirty state.
- Search, Changed only, unified/split diff, file expansion, and annotations work for every source.
- Empty, missing-ref, deleted-branch, and provider-unavailable states identify the selected source and provide a safe fallback.

## Why this matters

AO deliberately supports multiple PRs per session while each session has one primary workspace checkout. The Files explorer should make both concepts available without conflating them or forcing users out to GitHub/GitLab for PR-specific review.

## Related

- [#2408](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2408) — the same one-workspace/multiple-PR targeting constraint for automated reviewers.
- [#3982](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3982) — broader git-state-aware Files explorer improvements.
- [#3203](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3203) — base-aware workspace diff behavior.

title: bug(desktop): Browser compaction moves the sidebar toggle out of the titlebar
body:
## Bug

Opening the docked Browser in a session can automatically compact the left sidebar. When that happens on macOS/Linux, the sidebar toggle jumps from its stable titlebar position into the icon rail below the AO logo. The control should retain one fixed top-left position across expanded, compact, and hidden sidebar states.

**Source:** AO session report with attached screenshot  
**Reported:** 2026-08-30  
**Analyzed against:** `ed88a86d12027e0e37aa793d2f016165dde18e83` (`origin/main`)  
**Environment:** macOS (Darwin arm64); verified Agent Orchestrator daemon on port 3001  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** Low — visual/interaction consistency regression; the control remains usable

![Compact sidebar with the toggle below the AO logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-sidebar-toggle-jumps-browser-compact/.issue-assets/sidebar-toggle-jumps-browser-compact/compact-sidebar.png)

## Reproduction

1. Open an agent session with the sidebar expanded.
2. Open/select the docked Browser inspector at a window width where the Browser workspace requires more room.
3. Observe that the shell automatically switches the sidebar to its 48 px compact icon rail.
4. Compare the sidebar toggle before and after compaction.

**Actual:** the fixed titlebar toggle disappears and a replacement toggle appears below the AO logo in the rail.  
**Expected:** the same toggle remains in its fixed top-left/titlebar position throughout the transition.

## Root Cause

The Browser pressure path is intentional, but compact mode swaps the control's owning component and layout context:

1. `SessionView.tsx:682-689,714-718` publishes Browser-only workspace demand while the docked Browser is open.
2. `_shell.tsx:132-156` converts that width pressure into `isSidebarAutoCollapsed`; `_shell.tsx:836-847` then passes compact state to `Sidebar`.
3. `TitlebarNav.tsx:53-60` explicitly returns `null` when `sidebarIsCompact` is true, removing the fixed titlebar control.
4. `Sidebar.tsx:638-650,653-720` switches to the icon-collapse variant and renders a separate `PanelLeft` button after the brand/logo inside `SidebarHeader`.

That second button participates in the sidebar's vertical flow and traffic-light/topbar offset, so it necessarily appears lower. This contradicts the shell invariant documented in `_shell.tsx:895-897`: the titlebar cluster is rendered once so the controls never move when the sidebar collapses or expands.

This behavior was introduced by [PR #4409](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4409), merged 2026-08-29. Existing tests codify the swap: `TitlebarNav.test.tsx:64-68` expects the fixed nav to disappear, while `Sidebar.test.tsx:1625-1632` expects the replacement compact toggle inside the sidebar header.

## Suggested Fix

Keep a single sidebar-toggle owner in the fixed titlebar layer for expanded, compact, and off-canvas states. Remove the compact-only duplicate from `SidebarHeader` (or keep only compact history controls there if their vertical rail behavior remains desired). Add regression coverage asserting that the titlebar toggle remains mounted with unchanged positioning classes through Browser-driven compaction.

The fix should separately verify macOS windowed/fullscreen and Linux geometry because `TitlebarNav` has platform-specific offsets.

## Verification Notes

- Source path and regression commit were traced on current `origin/main`.
- The checked-in tests explicitly assert the current component swap.
- Attempted targeted Vitest execution, but this worktree has no installed frontend dependencies (`vitest: command not found`). No code was changed.

## Related

- [PR #4409](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4409) — introduced Browser-only adaptive sidebar compaction and the compact-rail control swap.
- [Issue #3372](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3372) — separate compact/collapsed sidebar interaction bug; not a duplicate.

title: bug(lifecycle): Chat session with stale runtime launch never becomes active
body:
## Bug

A live structured-Chat worker can remain durably `idle` for its entire running turn, so the session sidebar dot never pulses even while the agent is actively producing output.

This was observed live on `readme download cta` (`agent-orchestrator-153`). The provider turn ran from `2026-08-31T03:28:01Z` to `03:31:39Z`, while every session CDC event continued to publish `activity: "idle"`.

**Source:** live AO fleet report  
**Analyzed against:** `ed88a86d12027e0e37aa793d2f016165dde18e83`  
**AO build:** packaged nightly `0.12.10-nightly.202608301738`; bundled CLI reports `dev`; daemon verified healthy on the Go rewrite's loopback port `3001`  
**OS:** macOS  
**Confidence:** High for the activity-signal rejection mechanism; Medium for the original path that reintroduced the stale terminal metadata

## Reproduction

1. Start a worker in TUI mode.
2. Complete a TUI → Chat interface transition. The affected live session completed this transition on 2026-08-26.
3. Reach a state where the Chat session row still or again contains terminal ownership metadata (`runtime_launch_id` and `runtime_handle_id`) while also containing the current Chat `controller_generation`.
4. Send a Chat prompt and allow the provider turn to start.
5. Observe that the conversation turn and provider thread are running, but `sessions.activity_state` remains `idle` and the sidebar dot does not pulse.

Live affected row during the running turn:

```text
session_mode=chat
activity_state=idle
runtime_launch_id=bf9ee0ec-5d39-4c73-8a94-0a5e546f8086
runtime_handle_id=agent-orchestrator-153
controller_generation=3146af78-db54-4fb8-90a1-35d2db5732f6
```

The matching running turn used the same controller generation. Provider events included a root `turn.started`, the durable turn was `running`, and the provider thread state was `active`.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` reports `chat.turn.started` with a valid current `ControllerGeneration`, but intentionally does not attach a terminal `LaunchID` because structured Chat has no terminal runtime generation.

`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go` applies the generic runtime-launch fence first:

```go
if rec.Metadata.RuntimeLaunchID != "" && s.LaunchID != rec.Metadata.RuntimeLaunchID {
    return nil
}
```

For the affected Chat row, `RuntimeLaunchID` is non-empty while the Chat signal's `LaunchID` is empty, so the lifecycle manager silently returns before validating the matching Chat controller generation or writing `ActivityActive`.

The renderer is behaving consistently with the bad durable state: `frontend/src/renderer/lib/session-presentation.ts` only treats raw `activity.state === "active"` as working, and `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx` only adds the pulse animation when that view says to breathe.

A clean Chat spawn intentionally clears `RuntimeHandleID` and `RuntimeLaunchID`, and `CommitControllerEpoch` also clears them during an interface-mode change. The affected row nevertheless regained or retained both fields after its completed transition, so the lifecycle reducer also needs to remain safe if stale TUI metadata is present on a Chat-owned session.

## Expected

A current structured-Chat controller's matching generation is sufficient ownership proof for Chat activity. `turn.started` should set the session to `active`, and `turn.completed` should settle it back to `idle`, regardless of stale terminal launch metadata that is irrelevant to the current Chat owner.

## Suggested Fix

- Make runtime-launch fencing mode/owner aware: terminal `LaunchID` should fence TUI hook signals, while Chat signals should be fenced by the current `ControllerGeneration`.
- Preserve rejection of missing or foreign controller generations for Chat sessions.
- Audit TUI → Chat transition/restart paths so stale `runtime_handle_id` / `runtime_launch_id` cannot be reintroduced after `CommitControllerEpoch` clears them.
- Add regression coverage for a Chat record with stale runtime metadata and a matching controller generation:
  - current generation `turn.started` becomes `active`;
  - current generation completion becomes `idle`;
  - missing/foreign generation remains rejected;
  - sidebar-facing session CDC publishes the updated activity.

## Impact

- Users cannot tell that affected agents are working from the sidebar.
- Any feature consuming durable session activity receives `idle` throughout the turn, not only the renderer.
- The failure is silent because the lifecycle fence returns `nil`; normal session CDC continues, repeatedly carrying the stale state.
- Scope is bounded to Chat rows that retain or regain terminal launch metadata, with TUI → Chat / recovery paths the known trigger class.

## Related

- [#4125](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4125): Chat activity ownership can be corrupted by signals lacking controller-generation attribution.
- [PR #4204](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4204): strengthens Chat activity fencing by controller generation and documents the assumption that Chat sessions have no runtime launch ID.
- [#3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360): introduced structured Chat/TUI session modes and interface transitions.

title: fix(cloud-terminal): stop infinite ticket minting and surface error on WebSocket failure (#4668)
body: ## What When a cloud terminal WebSocket fails (CSP block, proxy, firewall), the app was retrying indefinitely at ~1-2 mints/sec with no user-facing error. This fix adds a circuit-breaker on the frontend and a lease-refresh guard on the backend. ## Why Fixes #4668 Two costly side effects of the infinite loop: 1. The sandbox never idle-paused — IssueTerminalTicket refreshes interactive_until on every mint, so billing ran indefinitely. 2. The failure was invisible — users saw "Connecting…" forever. ## How Frontend (useTerminalSession.ts + TerminalPane.tsx): - Added cloudConnectFailures counter to the runtime object. - In scheduleReattach(), if a cloud session has never attached and the counter hits CLOUD_CONNECT_MAX_FAILURES (8), transition("error") is called and the retry loop stops (~8 seconds of trying). - TerminalPane detects this specific error via isCloudConnectError and renders a CloudConnectError full-screen overlay (not the generic banner) with a "Retry connection" button that resets the counter via attach(). Backend (worker_transport_store.go): - Before refreshing interactive_until, count unconsumed terminal tickets minted in the last 2-minute window. - If the count exceeds unconsumedTicketThreshold (10), the CASE clause skips the lease extension. Sandbox wake (paused → running) still fires. - A slog.Warn is emitted with org_id, session_id, and count for observability without requiring a metrics system change. Intentional omission: no integration test for the backend path — the postgres package has no unit-test infrastructure and the lease suppression SQL is covered by private CI's integration suite. ## Testing Frontend — 4 new Vitest tests in useTerminalSession.test.tsx: npm test -- src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.test.tsx → 50 passed (50) Manual repro (DevTools Network → Offline mode → open cloud terminal): - Before: "Connecting…" forever, ~2 ticket requests/sec in Network tab - After: overlay appears after ~8s, Network tab goes quiet, Retry button reconnects once Network is restored Backend — package compiles and vets clean: go build ./cloud/internal/postgres/... go vet ./cloud/internal/postgres/... ## RESULTS ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Restart can leave a project without a working orchestrator
body:
## What happened

Restart was meant to recover a project whose orchestrator was no longer usable. Instead, AO began shutting down the current orchestrator, waited too long, returned an error, and then finished shutting down the old orchestrator without starting a replacement.

The terminal had already become unusable before Restart was clicked. Restart was an attempted recovery, not the cause of that earlier symptom.

## Why this happens

Restart currently follows this order:

1. Shut down the current orchestrator.
2. Wait for that shutdown to finish.
3. Start a new orchestrator.

The request has a normal time limit.

**If shutdown takes too long, or the new orchestrator fails to start, the old one is already gone. AO has no dependable fallback that restores the old orchestrator or guarantees a replacement.**

## What the user sees

- Restart reports a server error.
- The old orchestrator stops a short time later.
- No new orchestrator appears.
- The project is left without a coordinator for its sessions.

## Expected behavior

Restart should either replace the orchestrator successfully or leave the project with a usable coordinator. A failed replacement should not leave the project without one.

## Suggested fix

- Give orchestrator replacement its own time budget instead of relying only on the normal request timeout.
- Check that the new orchestrator has started before considering the replacement complete.
- If replacement fails, keep or restore the previous orchestrator when possible.
- Add tests for slow shutdowns, failed starts, and recovery after a failed replacement.

## Important distinction

This issue documents a failed Restart attempt. It does not prove that Restart caused the earlier terminal freeze. The terminal was already unhealthy before Restart began.

The separate database and storage reports may explain why the system became unhealthy, but they should not be treated as proven by this issue alone.

## Related issues

- [#2501](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2501): an active orchestrator can be terminated incorrectly.
- [#3862](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3862): the interface can become unusable after a replacement failure triggered by Settings.
- [#4317](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4317): cleanup can fail on Windows during replacement.
- [#4481](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4481): replacement or termination can fail when the terminal runtime is already gone.

## Impact

A Restart intended to recover a broken project can leave that project without any working orchestrator.

title: fix(orchestrator): give replacement a lifecycle timeout
body:
## Summary

- give `POST /api/v1/orchestrators` a dedicated three-minute lifecycle bound while ordinary REST requests retain their configured timeout
- carry the closed renderer source enum into the daemon request and persist a correlated request event locally
- preserve safe source, clean, and mode fields in remote diagnostics and regenerate the API contract

## Why

In [#4700](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4700), a clean replacement began retiring a live Codex coordinator. The ordinary 60-second request deadline returned HTTP 500 after 62 seconds, retirement finished afterward, and that request created no successor orchestrator.

This fixes the exact observed timeout path and makes future initiating UI surfaces attributable. It does not make replacement atomic for every possible teardown or spawn failure; #4700 remains the tracker for that broader recovery path.

## Tests

- `npm run api`
- focused frontend tests: 43 passed
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- product UI checks: 118 tests, typecheck, build passed
- `go test ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/adapters/telemetry -count=1`
- `go vet ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/adapters/telemetry`
- isolated `go test ./...`
- `go build ./...`
- golangci-lint v2.12.2: 0 issues

## Risk

The operation remains synchronous and has a hard three-minute ceiling. Generic recovery after an arbitrary post-retirement failure is intentionally not attempted here because relaunching the predecessor under changed project settings can create a mismatched or duplicate coordinator.

Refs #4700

title: bug(browser): popup tab drift can send agent actions to the wrong authenticated tab
body:
## Summary

After a page opens a popup/new AO browser tab, `ao browser tabs` can report that the new tab is active while `snapshot`, `act`, `click`, `get`, `screenshot`, `errors`, and `dialog` remain attached to the prior tab. IDs returned by `ao browser tabs` can then be rejected by `ao browser tab select`, and queued native commands can appear to stall.

This is a correctness and safety bug: an agent can inspect one authenticated tab in metadata and mutate a different authenticated tab.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31, macOS 14.6 arm64, packaged desktop browser transport `electron-webcontents-debugger`  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Confidence:** High. The exact unsafe fallback remains in current source and explicitly documents that subsequent actions may hit a different tab.

## Sanitized reproduction

1. Open page A in an AO Browser panel.
2. From page A, open page B through `target=_blank` or `window.open()`.
3. Run `ao browser tabs --json`; observe `activeTabId: "t2"`.
4. Run `ao browser snapshot --interactive --json`; observe page A's boundary/content.
5. Run a harmless action whose target exists only on page A; observe page A changes while the tab list still marks t2 active.
6. Run `ao browser tab select t2 --json`; it may fail with:
   `Tab t2 not found; run agent-browser tab to list open tabs (AGENT_BROWSER_COMMAND_FAILED)`.
7. Commands queued behind the popup target-sync operation may fail to return within the caller's 10-second window.

The original report used an authenticated government site. Signed parameters and personal data are intentionally omitted; a local two-page fixture is sufficient.

## Root cause

AO currently has two active-tab registries:

- `session.tabs` / `session.activeTabId` own the Electron `WebContentsView` tabs.
- `agentBrowserRuntime` keeps an independent native tab registry and active target.

In `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`, `ensureNativeActiveTab` tries `tab-select`, refreshes with `tabs`, and retries. If the retry still returns `AGENT_BROWSER_COMMAND_FAILED`, it deliberately logs and **accepts the drift**, then assigns:

```ts
session.nativeActiveTabId = tabId;
```

The adjacent source comment already states the consequence: a later `click/fill/snapshot` can silently land on a different tab. Because the cached field is now equal to AO's active tab, subsequent commands skip synchronization and operate on the runtime's stale target.

Popup activation compounds this through `queueNativeActiveTabSync`, which is fire-and-forget and serialized on `session.nativeOperationQueue`. An unresponsive native select can hold later commands behind the queue; cancellation of a later request does not remove the already-running predecessor.

The unsafe convergence behavior was introduced in `745c26841` and merged through PR #4169. PR #4169 fixed an unbounded retry/stuck-tab problem, but traded it for silent wrong-target execution. Closed issue #3445 is not a duplicate: it concerned visual native-view bleed-through, whereas this report proves automation-target divergence and mutation of the wrong page.

## Expected invariant

One AO tab identity must be authoritative. If AO reports t2 active, every command must either target t2 or fail closed before performing any read or mutation. It must never silently fall back to t1.

## Acceptance criteria

- Remove the path that marks `nativeActiveTabId` synchronized after native selection failed.
- If registries cannot be reconciled, return a stable structured target-mismatch/unavailable error; do not execute the requested action.
- IDs returned by `ao browser tabs` round-trip through select and close.
- Bound and cancel popup target synchronization so it cannot hold unrelated commands indefinitely.
- Do not expose `agent-browser` recovery instructions in AO CLI errors.
- Include target identity in action results (at minimum AO tab ID plus URL/origin after the action) so callers can verify where the action ran.
- Add a regression test with page A opening page B: all read/mutation commands target B, switching back targets A, and forced native registry drift fails closed without mutating A.
- Add a queue/cancellation regression proving a failed popup sync does not wedge later commands.

title: bug(browser): tabs output leaks full signed URLs into agent transcripts
body:
## Summary

`ao browser tabs --json` returns each tab's title and URL verbatim. For signed SSO/handoff links, this emits the full query string—including opaque one-time or credential-like parameters—into agent tool output and retained transcripts. When a page uses the URL as its title, the secret-bearing URL is duplicated.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31 on an authenticated government portal; all secret values are intentionally omitted  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Confidence:** High. Current source returns raw values.

## Sanitized reproduction

1. Open a page whose URL resembles:
   `https://example.test/access?param1=<opaque>&param2=<opaque>&param3=<opaque>`
2. Make the page title equal to that URL (the observed site did this).
3. Run `ao browser tabs --json`.
4. Observe the complete URL and query values in both `tabs[].url` and `tabs[].title`.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts` builds tab results directly from:

- `entry.view.webContents.getURL()`
- `entry.view.webContents.getTitle()`

There is no output-boundary sanitization. The same file already has `sanitizeNetworkURL`, which strips credentials/fragments and redacts query values for captured network metadata, but tab results do not use an equivalent policy.

## Impact

- Signed handoff/SSO material is copied into agent transcripts and diagnostic logs.
- A URL-shaped title duplicates the exposure.
- Long opaque URLs can exhaust tool-output budgets.

No matching open or closed issue was found for browser-tab URL redaction.

## Acceptance criteria

- Default tab output is safe to retain: preserve origin/path while redacting query values, credentials, and fragments.
- Sanitize URL-shaped titles as well as `url`.
- Apply the policy at the trusted Electron/daemon response boundary so text and JSON output are both protected.
- Keep an explicit, clearly unsafe opt-in only if full URL retrieval is genuinely required.
- Cover ordinary URLs, query strings, fragments, embedded credentials, URL-shaped titles, opaque/high-entropy values, and malformed URLs.
- Audit browser errors and other tab metadata paths for the same raw-URL exposure.

title: bug(cli): browser screenshot ignores path with --json and floods output with base64
body:
## Summary

`ao browser screenshot <path> --json` accepts the positional path but silently ignores it. It writes no PNG and prints the entire image as base64 JSON, which can flood and truncate agent tool output.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Confidence:** High; current CLI implementation has this exact branch.

## Reproduction

```sh
ao browser screenshot /tmp/ao-browser-test.png --json
test -f /tmp/ao-browser-test.png
```

Observed:

- command returns a very large `result.data` base64 field;
- the requested file does not exist.

The user report measured roughly 46,000 tokens before truncation.

## Root cause and contract conflict

In `backend/internal/cli/browser.go`, screenshot handling calls the browser action first and then immediately serializes the full response when `jsonOutput` is true. Positional-path handling exists only in the non-JSON branch.

The bundled browser guide currently documents base64 for `--json`, but the Cobra contract says `screenshot [path]` and describes the command as capturing to a PNG file. Accepting a path and silently discarding it is unsafe and surprising even if the behavior was documented elsewhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a path is supplied, write the PNG in both text and JSON modes.
- JSON output for a file write returns compact metadata: resolved path, byte size, width, and height.
- Inline image data requires an explicit opt-in such as `--base64`; it is never the accidental result of combining a path with `--json`.
- Preserve overwrite protections and path-validation behavior.
- Add CLI tests for absolute/relative paths, `--json`, file bytes, compact output, overwrite refusal, and explicit inline mode.
- Update the bundled browser guide and help text so they agree.

title: feat(browser): support action postconditions and report cancelled navigation
body:
## Problem

Browser actions can report that an element was matched and a low-level click/keypress was dispatched while the application produces no observable result. On guarded or authenticated sites, an agent can misread that as the intended action succeeding and may retry a consequential control.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31 on an authenticated Angular application  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Classification:** Product/observability enhancement, not yet a confirmed AO interaction bug.

## Evidence

A visible `Start New Filing` button was present in the snapshot. `act`, `click`, `dblclick`, focus + Enter, and focus + Space all reported a matched/dispatched interaction. The control visibly received focus, but the URL and subsequent snapshots did not change. Chromium also logged a blocked `beforeunload` confirmation.

A physical-click control result was not available, so the report does **not** establish whether AO synthetic input, the site's route guard, or site JavaScript prevented navigation. Current `act.outcome: "matched"` describes deterministic element matching, not application-level success, but that distinction is easy to miss.

## Desired behavior

Allow callers to state an expected postcondition and distinguish:

- element matched;
- input dispatched;
- navigation/dialog/DOM effect observed;
- navigation cancelled, blocked, or timed out;
- no observable effect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add optional postconditions such as expected URL, text, dialog, navigation, or DOM change.
- Include before/after URL and document generation/navigation facts in action results.
- Surface blocked/cancelled navigation and dialog signals in the correlated action response when available.
- Clearly document that `matched` is element-resolution status, not proof of application success.
- Avoid automatic retries of non-idempotent actions after an unknown outcome.
- Add a local integration fixture with `beforeunload`/route-guard behavior and tests for satisfied, unmet, and cancelled postconditions.

title: bug(desktop): Switch agent dialog opens and immediately closes itself
body:
## Bug

Clicking **"Switch agent"** in the session actions dropdown (topbar `...` menu) opens `SwitchAgentDialog`, and it immediately closes again in the same tick — the dialog flashes and disappears instead of staying open.

## Repro

1. Open any active worker session.
2. Click the session actions `...` menu in the terminal topbar.
3. Click **"Switch agent"**.
4. Expected: the switch-agent dialog opens and stays open.
5. Actual: the dialog opens and is dismissed immediately (visible as a brief flash).

## Root cause

Two independent Radix dismissal mechanisms fire on the same click:

1. `TerminalSwitchAgentButton.tsx` renders the menu item as a `DropdownMenuItem` with `onSelect={() => handleOpenChange(true)}`. `onSelect` does not call `event.preventDefault()`, so Radix's default post-`onSelect` behavior closes the parent `DropdownMenu` (`SessionActionsMenu.tsx`) in the same tick `SwitchAgentDialog`'s `open` prop flips to `true`.
2. `SwitchAgentDialog.tsx` renders `<Dialog modal={false} ...>` — intentionally non-modal so it doesn't fight `xterm`'s own focus/keyboard handling underneath it (the dialog is portaled into a container inside the terminal pane, not `document.body`). Because it's non-modal, Radix's `Dialog.Content` relies on `DismissableLayer`'s document-level `pointerdown`/`focusout` listeners for outside-click dismissal instead of a focus trap. The dropdown item is unmounting and returning focus in the very same event cycle the dialog mounts, so `DismissableLayer` treats the residual pointer/focus activity as "outside" and immediately closes the just-opened dialog.

A prior fix (`263ba3b82` / PR #4572, "unify session actions, terminal tabs, and naming") already moved `SwitchAgentDialog`'s render site from inside `TerminalSwitchAgentButton` into `SessionView`, specifically so the closing dropdown wouldn't *unmount* the dialog before it opened. That solved the unmount race but left the `DismissableLayer` outside-click race untouched, which is what's reported here. Possibly related to the closed #4039 ("fills terminal and reanimates on repeated activation") — different symptom, likely same family of dropdown/dialog interaction issues around this control.

## Fix

A PR is attached that adds an `onPointerDownOutside`/`onFocusOutside` guard on `SwitchAgentDialog`'s `DialogContent`, ignoring only outside events whose target is inside the just-dismissed menu/trigger (`[role="menuitem"]`, `[role="menu"]`, `[data-session-actions-trigger]`), so a genuine outside click still closes the dialog normally. Pattern matches the existing `onEscapeKeyDown`/`onPointerDownOutside` guard already used in `InstallDependencyDialog.tsx`.

Covered by a new regression test (`SessionActionsMenu.switch-agent.test.tsx`) that drives the real `DropdownMenuItem` click path — unlike the existing tests, which either mock the button out or open the dialog directly with `open=true` and so don't exercise this race.

title: fix(frontend): prevent switch-agent dialog auto-dismiss race with dropdown menu
body:
Closes #4710.

## Bug

Clicking **"Switch agent"** in the session actions dropdown opened `SwitchAgentDialog` and then immediately closed it again in the same tick — the dialog flashed and disappeared instead of staying open.

## Root cause

Two independent Radix dismissal mechanisms fire on the same click:

1. `TerminalSwitchAgentButton.tsx`'s `DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => handleOpenChange(true)}` doesn't call `event.preventDefault()`, so Radix's default post-`onSelect` behavior closes the parent `DropdownMenu` (`SessionActionsMenu.tsx`) in the same tick the dialog's `open` prop flips to `true`.
2. `SwitchAgentDialog.tsx` renders `<Dialog modal={false} ...>` — intentionally non-modal so it doesn't fight `xterm`'s focus/keyboard handling underneath it. Because it's non-modal, Radix's `Dialog.Content` relies on `DismissableLayer`'s document-level `pointerdown`/`focusout` listeners for outside-click dismissal. The dropdown item unmounts and returns focus in the very same event cycle the dialog mounts, so `DismissableLayer` treats the residual pointer/focus activity as "outside" and immediately dismisses the just-opened dialog.

`263ba3b82` (#4572) already moved `SwitchAgentDialog`'s render site from inside the button into `SessionView` to stop the closing dropdown from *unmounting* the dialog before it opened — that fixed the unmount race but left this `DismissableLayer` outside-click race untouched.

## Fix

Add an `onPointerDownOutside`/`onFocusOutside` guard on `SwitchAgentDialog`'s `DialogContent` that ignores only outside events whose target is inside the just-dismissed menu/trigger (`[role="menuitem"]`, `[role="menu"]`, `[data-session-actions-trigger]`), so a genuine outside click still closes the dialog normally. This mirrors the existing `onEscapeKeyDown`/`onPointerDownOutside` guard pattern already used in `InstallDependencyDialog.tsx`.

## Tests

- **New regression test**: `SessionActionsMenu.switch-agent.test.tsx` drives the real `DropdownMenuItem` click path (`variant="menu-item"` inside a real `SessionActionsMenu`), unlike the existing `SessionView.test.tsx` (mocks the button out) or `SwitchAgentDialog.test.tsx` (opens with `open=true` directly) — neither exercised this race. It fails against `main` with the exact reported symptom before the fix (verified via `git stash`), and passes after.
- A companion assertion in the same test proves a genuine outside click (`document.body`) still dismisses the dialog, so the guard doesn't over-suppress legitimate dismissal.
- Full relevant suite green: `SwitchAgentDialog.test.tsx` + `TerminalSwitchAgentButton.test.tsx` + `SessionView.test.tsx` + the new file — 119/119 passing.
- Full `frontend` vitest suite: 3189 passed / 1 skipped / 4 failed, all 4 pre-existing and unrelated (confirmed via `git stash` — they fail identically with and without this change; they're a known machine-locale `toLocaleString` issue in `AgentModelCombobox`/`ChatTimelineItems`/`ChatWorkspace`).
- `npm run typecheck` — clean.

## Manual verification

- Verified in the real Electron desktop app (dev build on this branch, pointed at real session data) — clicking "Switch agent" from the session actions menu now opens the dialog and it stays open and interactive; a genuine click outside still closes it.
- Verified again against a full self-build of the packaged desktop app + Go daemon (not just the dev harness): this branch merged onto a freshly upstream-synced fork main, `.app` repackaged and daemon restarted, then re-tested live against real session data. Confirmed by the reporting user directly in the rebuilt production app: "все работает, я подтверждаю" ("everything works, confirmed") — the dialog opens and stays open, no more flash-close.

title: fix(terminal): resolve reboot reattach loop and add native auto-resume (#4641)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4641.

This PR addresses two related issues with terminal session persistence and lifecycle:

### 1. Bug Fix: Infinite reattach loop after PC reboot
- **Root Cause**: In `tmux.go`, `IsAlive` classified `serverNotRunningOutput` ("no server running") as `ports.ErrRuntimeUnavailable` (a retryable/transient error) rather than `(false, nil)`. Because it was treated as transient, `attachment.go` retried with linear backoff, but the frontend's 3-second open timeout tore down the socket and reconnected first, resetting the backend's retry counter. This resulted in two retry loops perpetually interrupting each other in an infinite "reattaching" state instead of reaching a clean "session ended" state.
- **Fix**: Reclassified "no server running" as permanent death `(false, nil)`, identical to the "session not found" case. `attachment.go` immediately marks the session as exited. (Darwin native PTY host already uses this classification via `isConnRefused`).
- **Tests**: Updated `TestIsAliveReportsNoServerAsPermanentDeath` and integration test expectations.

### 2. Feature: Auto-resume terminal-only agents into fresh session
- **Behavior**: When a user opens/interacts with a confirmed permanently dead terminal session (`state === "exited"`):
  1. Calls `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/auto-resume-agent` (`AutoResumeAgentWithMode`), which checks if the agent adapter's `GetRestoreCommand` returns `ok=true` (supported for agents like Cline, Claude Code, Goose, etc. that persist native conversation IDs on disk).
  2. If `ok=true`: Launches a fresh terminal process with native resume argv, attaches transparently, and displays a one-line banner: `"Session expired after restart — resumed via <agent>'s native session recovery"`.
  3. If `ok=false`: Returns `SESSION_NO_NATIVE_RESUME` (mapped to HTTP 409), falling back cleanly to the existing "session ended" state with no silent relaunch.
  4. Gated strictly on definitively-dead terminal state, never on transient errors.

## Test Coverage
- `TestIsAliveReportsNoServerAsPermanentDeath` in `tmux_test.go`
- `TestAutoResumeAgent_SucceedsForNativeRestore` in `manager_test.go`
- `TestAutoResumeAgent_FailsWithErrNoNativeResumeWhenNotResumable` in `manager_test.go`
- `TestAutoResumeAgent_RequiresLiveExitedSession` in `manager_test.go`
- `autoResumeAgent` endpoint test in `sessions_test.go`
- Full backend suite passing (`go test ./...`)
