title: fix: support explicit upstream PR claims from fork-backed projects
body:
Fork-backed projects currently reject PRs in their upstream repository. Add an explicit `canonicalRepoURL` project setting so claims can target the origin or one deliberately configured upstream, while checkout/push configuration stays on origin.

- Keep provider, host (including explicit ports), and full namespace checks strict. Never derive claim trust from arbitrary Git remotes. Reject malformed/provider-inconsistent PR URLs before SCM access.
- Resolve numeric references against canonical when set in both `ao session claim-pr` and `ao spawn --claim-pr`, and fetch SCM facts from the actual claimed repository.
- Validate config through daemon project services, persist it in project config JSON, and add migration 0126 preserving existing settings and origin-only defaults. Regenerate the API schema and document config replacement and downgrade behavior.
- Add GitHub and GitLab fork/upstream tests, including self-managed GitLab and nested namespaces, rejected targets, CLI parity, API guidance, config persistence, and migration compatibility.

Validation on the final implementation:

- Full backend suite: `go test -p 2 ./...` with inherited AO runtime variables unset.
- Focused race tests for canonical identity, port handling, and project configuration.
- Full golangci-lint v2.12.2 with an isolated cache: zero issues.
- `npm run api`, HTTP/spec tests, and `npm run frontend:typecheck`.
- All 40 `ProjectSettingsForm` tests, including canonical identity preservation.
- GitHub/GitLab claim and spawn regressions, authenticated origins, custom-port authorities, CLI config read/edit/write preservation, native/legacy import behavior, and migration compatibility.

The initial independent review found custom-port authority loss and CLI config field loss. Both are fixed with reproductions committed, replies posted, and threads resolved. All 11 CI checks pass at `03e35f532b9688652c1bcab52ab121fad8d801e0`. Independent re-review of this exact head is still required; do not merge based on an earlier head's approval.

Scope: canonical identity authorizes PR claims only. It does not change checkout/push remotes, infer fork relationships, retarget tracker intake, or unlink already claimed PRs when config changes.

Closes #4927

title: fix(codex): retry account bootstrap failures
body:
Follow-up to [issue #4908](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4908) and [PR #4924](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4924).

## Summary

- build on the merged safe bootstrap-failure classification and API diagnostics from PR #4924
- replace its demand-driven 1–32 second cooldown with daemon-owned automatic retries after 10 seconds, 20 seconds, 45 seconds, 90 seconds, and then every 3 minutes
- keep exactly one native bootstrap attempt active while concurrent task launches join the same attempt
- keep shared bootstrap work on the daemon context so cancelling one request does not cancel recovery
- invalidate stale retry timers by generation when a caller or another timer has already started an attempt
- cache success permanently and run existing capability, authentication, and capacity warming exactly once
- preserve permanent credential/storage safety failures as fail-closed and non-retryable
- preserve account-switch routes, operation/account-mutation gates, frontend behavior, OpenAPI, and storage schemas

## Context

[PR #4722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4722) originally added a process-lifetime `sync.Once` bootstrap, causing a transient first failure to block every later Codex task launch until daemon restart. PR #4924 removed that terminal latch and added safe reason codes, permanent-vs-transient failure classification, and a real delegate-route regression test.

This PR retains those reviewed protections and changes retry ownership: recovery is scheduled by the daemon rather than requiring a later task-launch request to trigger another attempt.

## Retry behavior

- one native bootstrap attempt may run at a time
- failures remain fail-closed and retain the existing `503 CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` code/message
- only failures already classified as retryable schedule automatic work
- retry delays are 10 seconds, 20 seconds, 45 seconds, 90 seconds, then a 3-minute cap
- calls during backoff receive the safe existing failure immediately
- calls during an active attempt wait for that shared attempt
- daemon shutdown cancels pending timers and prevents further retries

## Verification

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go test -p 1 ./...`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/agent ./internal/session_manager ./internal/integration`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/service/agent ./internal/session_manager`
- `cd backend && go vet ./internal/service/agent ./internal/session_manager ./internal/integration`
- scoped golangci-lint v2.12.2 for the changed packages: `0 issues`
- `git diff --check`

The full suite is run serially because unrelated wall-clock-sensitive adapter fixtures have previously flaked only under repository-wide parallel contention.

title: fix(storage): preserve literal data paths and guard legacy databases
body:
A data directory containing `#`, `?`, or percent escapes was interpolated into a SQLite URI without escaping. SQLite could open a different file, and two distinct data directories could share records. This escapes the filesystem path for both normal and read-only connections.

If the intended database is absent but the old URI points to an existing SQLite database, startup now refuses to create an empty replacement and identifies the legacy file for explicit recovery. Existing intended databases take precedence. No data is moved automatically because multiple directories may have shared the legacy file.

Validation:
- Regression reproduced before the fix: special-character paths opened the wrong database, and two fragment paths shared project records.
- Real SQLite tests cover physical file placement, read-only enforcement, path isolation, legacy-data preservation, and intended-database precedence.
- Windows drive/UNC URI round-trip coverage; focused filesystem regressions added to Windows CI.
- Final focused race suite (54.3s), full SQLite package suite (19.7s), vet, and pinned golangci-lint (0 issues).
- Full SQLite race suite also passed on the initial escaping change (413.3s); the final legacy guard is covered by the final focused race and full non-race suites above.
- Real daemon starts and restarts using an isolated literal `#`/percent data path, serves the projects API, and stops cleanly.
- Independent specification and code-quality reviews passed.

No API, schema, or migration changes. Native Windows results depend on CI; manual recovery of historical misplaced data is intentionally not automated.

Backend-only change. The image is a rendered report of fresh successful Go test output, not a product UI screenshot. The complete captured output is attached.

title: fix(cleanup): stop counting already-gone workspaces as reclaimed
body:
## What

`ao session cleanup` now reports three outcomes instead of two: **cleaned**, **already gone**, and **skipped**. A workspace whose directory was already missing is no longer counted as reclaimed.

## Why

Refs #3219.

The count was derived from a single signal: did `Destroy` return an error. That is not the same question as "was a workspace released".

When a worktree directory is already gone on disk:

1. `git worktree remove` fails, but that error is only ever re-read inside the `findWorktree(records, path)` branch
2. `git worktree prune` succeeds and clears the stale registration
3. `findWorktree` then returns false, so the failure from step 1 is never looked at
4. `os.RemoveAll` returns nil, since it is documented to succeed on a missing path
5. `Destroy` returns nil, and the session is counted as cleaned

Nothing was released, but the run reports otherwise. In a batch that is how a cleanup reports hundreds of sessions cleaned while disk usage does not move, and why running it again never lowers the number.

The scratch adapter had the same shape: `os.Remove` is deliberately tolerated on a missing path, so an absent scratch directory also tore down "successfully" without releasing anything.

## How

`Destroy` keeps its signature and its behaviour. It is in the `ports.Workspace` interface, implemented by three adapters plus test fakes, and changing that contract for a reporting fix would touch every implementation for no functional gain.

Instead this adds an optional capability interface, matching the pattern already used for `AgentInterfaceHandoff`, `TerminalSurfaceInspector` and friends:

```go
type WorkspaceReclaimer interface {
    DestroyReclaim(ctx context.Context, info WorkspaceInfo) (WorkspaceReclaim, error)
}
```

- `gitworktree` and `scratch` implement it; the existing `Destroy` bodies were extracted into a shared `destroy` so there is one code path, not two.
- `router` forwards it, and falls back to `Destroy` for any adapter that does not implement it.
- `Manager.Cleanup` type-asserts for the capability and falls back the same way, so an adapter that does not report reclaim outcomes keeps the previous meaning of a nil error.
- The outcome flows out through `CleanupResult`, `CleanupOutcome`, `CleanupSessionsResponse` and the CLI summary.

Two details worth a reviewer's eye:

- **The path is sampled before any teardown step runs**, not after. Sampling afterwards would always report "absent", because teardown has by then removed it.
- **Only a definite `ErrNotExist` counts as already-absent.** A stat that fails for any other reason (permissions, a racing writer) stays on the removed path, so an unknown is never reported as "there was nothing to do".

API note: `alreadyGone` is added to the cleanup response, so `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated and committed alongside. The field is always serialised as `[]` rather than `null`. No frontend, mobile or packages client calls this endpoint today.

## Testing

`go build ./...`, `go test -race` on the touched packages, `golangci-lint run` (v2.12.2, as CI runs it) reporting 0 issues, `gofmt -l` clean, `npm run frontend:typecheck`, and `npm run api` leaving no spec drift.

The backend suite has 20 pre-existing failures on this machine (`codexappserver` protocol conformance and the Codex account catalog tests). I confirmed they are unrelated by stashing this change and running the same packages on a clean `main`, which reproduces them identically.

New tests: `DestroyReclaim` reporting `already_absent` for a missing worktree and `removed` for a present one (real git repo), the same pair for scratch, `Cleanup` routing an already-absent workspace into its own bucket, and the CLI summary keeping the two apart.

End to end, I built the daemon and CLI from `main` and from this branch and ran each against its own isolated copy of a real data directory, with the project repo cloned locally so nothing touched the original:

```
BEFORE (main)          Cleanup complete. 14 sessions cleaned, 6 skipped.
AFTER (this branch)    Cleanup complete. 6 sessions cleaned, 8 already gone, 6 skipped.

Disk reclaimed in both runs: 11M -> 6.9M
```

Identical teardown work, honest count. Running cleanup a second time on the same data shows the difference more sharply, since by then there is nothing left to reclaim at all:

```
BEFORE, second run     Cleanup complete. 14 sessions cleaned, 6 skipped.
AFTER,  second run     Cleanup complete. 1 session cleaned, 13 already gone, 6 skipped.
```

One detail from that run that shows the accounting working: several terminated sessions shared one orchestrator worktree. The first of them is reported as cleaned because the directory was there, and the rest as already gone. The old code called all of them cleaned.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Bug]: single-user PR stays “Review pending” after AO reviewer approves current head
body:
### Summary

In a single-user GitHub repository, an AO reviewer can complete successfully with
an `approved` verdict, but the PR remains shown as **Review pending** and cannot
be merged through AO.

The worker, PR author, AO daemon, and reviewer all use the same GitHub account.
GitHub does not permit users to approve their own pull requests, so the review
submitted by AO is recorded as `COMMENTED` rather than `APPROVED`.

AO then ignores its own completed `approved` verdict and requires an external
GitHub approval, even when the repository does not require approving reviews.

## Environment

- AO desktop: `0.12.10`
- Platform: macOS, Apple silicon
- SCM: GitHub
- Repository: personal/single-user repository
- Branch protection: no approving review required
- Required CI checks: none
- PR author and authenticated `gh` user: same GitHub account
- Reviewer harness tested: Codex
- The same underlying behavior was also encountered while trying Claude Code


### Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate AO/`gh` as the owner of a personal GitHub repository.
2. Use an AO worker to create a branch and open a pull request.
3. Run **Review PR** from the AO session inspector.
4. Let the reviewer complete with an approved verdict.
5. Open the session Summary pane.

### Expected behavior

AO should provide a viable merge workflow for single-user repositories that do not require GitHub approvals.

Possible expected behaviors include one of the following:

Treat an empty GitHub review decision as “approval not required” when the repository's merge rules require zero approvals.
Allow a completed, current-head AO approved verdict to satisfy AO's own review gate when GitHub does not require an external approval.
Make the external-approval merge gate configurable per project.
Clearly document that AO requires a separate GitHub reviewer identity and provide a supported way to configure reviewer-specific credentials.
At minimum, the UI should distinguish:

“AO review approved”
“GitHub approval required”
“GitHub approval not required”
“Approval impossible because the reviewer is the PR author”
rather than displaying the generic “Review pending” state.

### Actual behavior

AO records the internal review successfully:

```json
{
  "status": "complete",
  "verdict": "approved",
  "targetSha": "<current-pr-head>"
}
```

The target SHA matches the current PR head.

However, GitHub records the submitted review as:

```
{
  "state": "COMMENTED",
  "reviewDecision": ""
}
```
This is expected GitHub behavior because the authenticated reviewer is also the PR author.

AO consequently continues to show:

```
Review status: Review pending
```
The green Merge button is not displayed. ao pr merge <number> also rejects the merge because the backend applies the same approval requirement.

GitHub otherwise reports the PR as open, clean, and mergeable. The repository does not require an approving review.




### Why this matters
The current state is impossible to satisfy in a normal single-user setup:

AO uses the existing gh authentication for GitHub operations.
The same identity authors the PR and submits the review.
GitHub cannot record that review as APPROVED.
AO nevertheless requires APPROVED before exposing or executing its merge action.
Users must leave AO and run gh pr merge even after AO has reviewed and approved the current head.

Creating a second account or approval bot should not be required for a personal repository whose GitHub rules require zero approvals.

### Related issues
#1173 reported that an empty/null GitHub reviewDecision prevented a no-review-required repository from becoming mergeable. Its proposed fix was closed during the ground-up rewrite rather than resolved in the current code.
#2073 proposes configurable merge-gate exclusions, including review_required.
#1275 describes AO review completion as advisory and separate from SCM merge readiness.

### Additional context
This report is specifically about the mismatch between:

AO's internal, current-head reviewer verdict: approved
GitHub's unavoidable same-author review state: COMMENTED
The repository's actual rule: no approval required
AO's derived state: Review pending
It is not a stale-review, merge-conflict, CI, or GitHub authentication issue.

### AO version

AO 0.12.10

### Environment

macOS 26.5.1, Apple silicon, M1 Max

### Logs / extra context

```shell

```

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: bug(chat): Claude OAuth expiry bypasses reauth banner
body:
## Bug

When a Claude Code OAuth session has expired, AO can continue showing Claude Code as authorized while Chat turns appear empty/non-responsive instead of presenting the existing **Sign in again to keep going** banner.

**Source:** live maintainer report in AO Chat, 2026-09-04  
**Observed session:** `agent-orchestrator-296` (`codex chat reauth`)  
**AO:** `0.12.11-nightly.202609041654`, macOS arm64  
**Analyzed against:** `d2c88dae7d968df26c990ac5dd42ed2fc17513b1`  
**Confidence:** High — the live daemon snapshot, stored conversation, provider process, and both relevant code paths agree.

## Reproduction

1. Have Claude Code local account metadata that still identifies an OAuth user/subscription, but whose OAuth refresh session has expired.
2. Spawn a Claude Code worker in Chat mode.
3. Send one or more messages.
4. The live provider returns `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` for every turn.
5. Observe that AO's agent catalog still reports Claude Code `authStatus: authorized`, no reauthentication banner appears, and the turns look empty/non-responsive to the user.

## Live evidence

- `/api/v1/agents` reported `claude-code` as `authorized` throughout the incident.
- The ACP adapter and Claude process stayed alive.
- The conversation snapshot stored the exact authentication sentence as an assistant message for each request.
- Every corresponding turn was recorded as `completed`, with no turn error.
- No account/provider state with `reauthRequiredAt` was present, so `ReauthBanner` had nothing to render.
- The worker performed no repository changes before it was replaced.

No credential contents were inspected or logged.

## Root cause

There are two independent blind spots:

1. **Catalog auth false positive.** `backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/claudecode.go` calls `claudeLocalAuthStatus` before the authoritative `claude auth status` probe. `claudeConfigAuthStatus` returns `authorized` from durable identity markers such as `userID`, `hasAvailableSubscription`, or `oauthAccount.accountUuid`. Those markers survive refresh-token expiry, so AO never asks the CLI whether the session is still usable.

2. **Live ACP failure is shaped differently from AO's detector.** `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go` emits `ChatEventAccountChanged{ReauthRequired:true}` only when `Prompt` returns the typed ACP/JSON-RPC `AuthRequired` error (`-32000`). In this live path, `claude-agent-acp` instead emitted the authentication sentence as an ordinary assistant message and returned a successful prompt completion. AO therefore marked the turns completed and never set `ReauthRequiredAt`. The existing `ReauthBanner` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatStatusBanners.tsx` is correct but unreachable for this provider behavior.

The current test covers the typed `acpsdk.NewAuthRequired` path, not the observed synthetic assistant-message/completed-turn path.

## Expected behavior

- Catalog readiness must not claim `authorized` solely from stale Claude identity metadata when live token freshness is unknown.
- The observed Claude ACP authentication terminal outcome must become structured reauthentication state without broadly matching arbitrary model prose.
- Chat should show the existing sign-in banner, block or clearly fence futile sends, and mark the provider turn failed rather than completed.
- After `claude auth login` and a fresh/recovered controller succeeds, AO should clear the warning through the existing account-state lifecycle.

## Suggested fix

- Prefer or periodically run the authoritative bounded `claude auth status` probe; use local config only as a conservative fallback and never as proof of token freshness.
- Add a Claude-adapter-specific structured signal at the `claude-agent-acp` boundary for its synthetic auth terminal result. Do not add a provider-agnostic substring classifier that could mistake ordinary assistant prose for auth state.
- Add regression coverage for the exact live sequence: assistant auth-failure content + nominal ACP prompt completion, ensuring account reauth state, failed turn semantics, actionable banner, and recovery clearing.

## Impact

A worker can be completely unable to act while AO labels its harness authorized and gives no corrective action. Users repeatedly send prompts, receive what appears to be empty output, and may assume the worker or renderer is frozen.

## Related

- #4296 — analogous stale OAuth recovery for long-lived Codex Chat app-servers.
- #4120 — historical Claude auth-failure turn caused a separate Chat/TUI history-settlement bug; confirms the same provider error shape has appeared before.

title: fix(mobile): Android keyboard inset and orchestrator restart visibility
body:
Two Android-only mobile fixes. Both are pure JS/TS — no native module, config plugin, or `app.json` change.

## 1. Keyboard covered the input dock on every Android device

React Native's Android keyboard event does not report the keyboard's height above the screen bottom. From `ReactRootView.checkForKeyboardEvents`:

```java
Insets barInsets = rootInsets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars());
Insets imeInsets = rootInsets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.ime());
int height = imeInsets.bottom - barInsets.bottom;   // nav bar subtracted
```

So `e.endCoordinates.height` is the keyboard height **with the navigation bar already subtracted**. The terminal, chat and spawn screens padded their root view by exactly that value, but the root view draws edge-to-edge underneath the nav bar, so the keyboard actually covers the full `imeInsets.bottom`.

Every Android device was short by exactly the nav-bar inset:

| Nav mode | Inset | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| Gesture | ~24dp | input row cut in half |
| 3-button | 48dp | input row hidden behind the keyboard |

iOS was unaffected — its event measures from the screen bottom and already spans the home indicator.

New `rootKeyboardPad(platform, height, insetsBottom)` owns that platform difference; `screenKeyboardAvoidance` now takes the inset as a **required** argument so a call site cannot silently reintroduce the bug. `useSafeAreaInsets().bottom` is the correct addend: `react-native-safe-area-context` builds its bottom inset from `statusBars | displayCutout | navigationBars | captionBar` on API 30+ and clamps the IME out on the older path, so it is exactly the `barInsets.bottom` RN subtracted.

Verified on a Pixel 7 emulator (API 35) in both nav modes, and on the terminal and chat docks.

## 2. Orchestrator card offered Restart only when nothing needed restarting

The card rendered Restart when `state === "running"` and hid it otherwise — the inverse. A healthy orchestrator carried a destructive retire-and-replace button, while one that had exited offered "Start orchestrator", which reads as though the app had lost track of a session that has clearly already run.

| State | Footer now |
|---|---|
| running | `Open` only |
| stopped (exited) | `Restart orchestrator` |
| missing (never started) | `Start orchestrator` |

`launchIntent` keeps its running branch: it is still the correct answer to what a launch would do, and the destructive path must keep its confirmation if the card ever offers it again.

Both footer actions are now the shared `Button` rather than a 32x32 `IconButton` and a bespoke 32pt pill, so the tap target is a full-height labelled control. The card itself stays deliberately inert — the zone pills open the board, so a whole-card target would send two taps a few pixels apart to different screens.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — exit 0
- `npx vitest run` — 709 passed (up from 708; new tests written red-first)
- Both changes exercised on a live Pixel 7 / API 35 emulator against a real daemon

The new `launchIntent` test asserts the two labels **exactly** rather than with `/start/i` — "Restart" contains "start", so a loose match passes whichever label is wrong.

## Shipping

JS-only, and this branch's Android fingerprint `bcfb745ef3a294b08d2324b090febfc0a900bc0f` matches production build `ed8bcf7e` (1.3.0, versionCode 8), so this is deliverable over EAS Update on the `production` channel.

## Not verified

The stopped/missing orchestrator footer is covered by unit tests only — every project on the test daemon had a running orchestrator, and staging the state would have meant stopping a live one.

title: fix(tmux): target bare session in respawn-pane and pane-pid probe
body:
Fixes #4656.

## What
`respawn-pane` and the pane-pid probe hardcoded the target `<session>:0.0`, assuming tmux's `base-index` / `pane-base-index` are both `0`. With either set to `1` (a very common customization) the target misses and `Runtime.Restart` — the path session restore uses — always fails with `can't find pane: 0` / `can't find window: 0`.

## How
Target the bare session name instead (`respawn-pane -k -t <session>`, `display-message -p -t <session>`), which resolves to the active window/pane regardless of either option. AO sessions have a single pane, so this is exact. It also matches the file's existing convention: `set-option`, `send-keys`, `capture-pane`, and `paneCurrentPathArgs` already use the bare id. The alternative (resolving a stable `#{pane_id}` first) was left out as unnecessary complexity for single-pane sessions.

`panePIDArgs` was latent rather than broken (`display-message` falls back silently) but carried the same unchecked assumption, so it gets the same fix.

## Tests
- Updated `TestCommandBuilders` (both arg builders) and `TestRestartRespawnsExistingPaneAndPreservesHandle` (restart call-site assertion).
- Targeted tests pass; `go vet` clean; build passes.
- Full `tmux` package run has 4 failures (`TestNewUsesSystemTmuxForLegacyDefaultSocket`, `TestExecRunnerRunsFromStableDir`, `TestExecRunnerFallsBackWhenTempDirMissing`, `TestIsUnsupportedMatcher`) that fail identically on unmodified `main` — pre-existing Windows-environment issues (TempDir/socket preconditions), unrelated to this change.
- The issue's Linux integration tests (`TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell`, `TestAttachmentStreamsRealTmuxPane`) need real tmux and can't run on this Windows box; CI should cover them.

title: claim-pr never checks out the PR branch, and `ao session claim-pr` prints "checkout: already on PR branch" for exactly that case
body:
## Summary

`ClaimPR` never checks out the claimed PR branch — the service layer says so itself in a `TODO` — and the CLI then prints **`checkout: already on PR branch`** for exactly that case. The one code path that checks nothing out is the one that reports the checkout as done.

The `TODO` and the printer disagree, and the printer wins.

## Source, verified on current `main` `95246e9bdb1eeccafe08151b2ab18abc91709a75`

**`backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go`** — the service leaves `BranchChanged` false and states the CLI contract it expects:

```go
// L135-138
// TODO: implement workspace branch checkout. Until then, leave BranchChanged
// false and let CLI output omit the checkout line rather than claiming the
// session was already on the PR branch.
res := ClaimPRResult{PRs: prs, BranchChanged: false, DonorWasTerminated: outcome.OwnerTerminated}
```

**`backend/internal/cli/session.go`**, `writeClaimPRResult` (L427) — does not omit the line; it prints the affirmative wording for the false value:

```go
// L440-444
checkout := "already on PR branch"
if res.BranchChanged {
    checkout = "switched to PR branch"
}
if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(out, "  checkout: %s\n", checkout); err != nil {
```

Since `BranchChanged` is unconditionally `false` at the only place it is set, `"switched to PR branch"` is unreachable and `"already on PR branch"` is printed on every claim — true only by coincidence, when the workspace happened to be on that branch already.

## Reproduction

Observed on a claim of an existing PR whose branch the workspace was **not** on. Sanitized; exit status and output wording are verbatim.

```
$ ao session claim-pr <PR>
session <session-id> claimed PR #<PR>
  pr:       https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<PR>
  checkout: already on PR branch
$ echo $?
0

# read-only, immediately afterward, before any edit:
$ git -C <workspace> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
ao/<session-id>/root          # not the PR branch
$ git -C <workspace> rev-parse HEAD
<live main sha>               # not the PR head
$ git -C <workspace> status --porcelain
                              # empty — nothing was touched
```

The claimed PR's branch existed both locally and on `origin` at the PR head, and was checked out in **no** worktree, so nothing was contending for it. Session metadata was updated correctly; only the workspace claim in the output is false.

## The two CLI forms differ, and both are affected

| Form | Prints a checkout line? | Checks anything out? |
|---|---|---|
| `ao session claim-pr` | **yes — `checkout: already on PR branch`** | no |
| `ao spawn --claim-pr` | no (prints `spawned session … (claimed <url>)`) | no |

`spawn` posts to the same `sessions/{id}/pr/claim` endpoint (`backend/internal/cli/spawn.go` L154) and never calls `writeClaimPRResult`, so it makes no checkout claim — but it also performs no checkout, leaving the new worktree on its root branch while reporting a successful claim. The false *statement* is specific to `ao session claim-pr`; the missing *behavior* is common to both.

## Why it matters

A caller that trusts the successful response can edit the wrong base, overwrite unrelated work, or push a reconstruction that silently omits the current PR head — most dangerously during takeover, recovery, or cross-engine handoff, which is exactly when `--claim-pr` is reached for.

## Expected behavior

Either of these is fine; the present state is neither.

1. **Atomic claim + checkout.** Do not report success until the workspace is actually based on the exact current provider PR head. Session PR-ownership metadata, local `HEAD`, local branch/upstream, and the provider head agree, or the operation fails closed with an actionable error. A provider head that moves during setup aborts rather than silently using stale data. Existing owner/session/worktree content is never deleted or reset as a side effect.
2. **Truthful partial success.** If metadata-only claiming is the intended behavior for now, honor the `TODO`'s own contract: omit the checkout line, or state plainly that the workspace was not changed. The machine-readable `branchChanged` field already carries this correctly — it is only the human-facing line that is false.

Option 2 is a small change and would remove the misleading output immediately, independent of when the checkout lands.

## Tests requested

None currently assert this line. Both CLI forms need coverage:

- `ao session claim-pr` when the workspace is **not** on the PR branch — assert the output does not claim a checkout that did not happen.
- `ao session claim-pr` when the workspace **is** already on the PR branch — the one case the current wording is true for; it should stay distinguishable from the case above.
- `ao spawn --claim-pr` — assert the new session's workspace base against the exact claimed head, or that the command fails closed.
- `branchChanged` in the JSON response stays consistent with whatever the human-readable line says, in both forms.
- Once checkout is implemented: an already-owned PR, takeover, `--no-takeover`, a provider head that moves mid-setup, a dirty preserved prior worktree, and a provider/network failure.

## Related

- **#4890** — `sessions.branch` is never reconciled with the branch the session actually pushed. Related but distinct: that is drift *after* a push; this is a checkout that never happens *at claim time*. Neither causes the other.
- I searched open and closed issues for `BranchChanged`, `already on PR branch`, `claim_pr`, `claim does not check out`, `worktree stays on main`, `claim reports success`, and `session claim checkout` before filing; nothing covers this.

Downstream tracking lives in a private repository, noted for provenance rather than as a reachable link: `menard-software/setup-agent-orchestrator` issue #391, with a read-only pre-flight verifier and its evidence in PR #395. That verifier only *detects* the mismatch before a worker's first edit; the fix belongs here.

## Environment

Source verified by reading this repository at `main` `95246e9b` on 2026-09-05. The reproduction was run against a locally built CLI that self-reports `ao version dev`, so I am not attributing it to a tagged release; the two source locations above are unchanged at `main`, so the behavior follows from current code rather than from that build.

title: feat: add DevEco Code agent adapter
body:
## What

Add DevEco Code as a first-class AO coding-agent adapter on Windows.

- register `deveco` across the backend, API contract, storage validation, and agent selector
- reuse the OpenCode-compatible configuration model while keeping DevEco's own binary and `.deveco` namespace
- install an AO activity plugin and `using-ao` skill under each worker worktree
- support native Windows executable discovery, prompt delivery, session restore, model selection, and permission flags without shell command strings

## Why

DevEco Code is an OpenCode-derived CLI used for HarmonyOS development, but treating it as an alias would mix configuration and session state with OpenCode. This adapter gives each AO worker its own DevEco process and worktree while preserving DevEco's native configuration and plugin conventions.

## How

- extract the small shared system-prompt configuration logic into `opencodefamily`
- resolve `deveco.exe` directly, including npm/native Windows layouts; `.cmd`/`.bat` shims are accepted only to locate their native payload
- pass executable arguments as an argv slice; AO's runtime converts the leading `env` entries to process environment variables on Windows
- write workspace integration to `.deveco/plugins/ao-activity.ts` and `.deveco/skills/using-ao`
- map compatible DevEco/OpenCode lifecycle events to AO activity hooks
- add migration 0126 for the new harness token

Intentional MVP omissions: no automatic DevEco installer and no structured Chat provider; sessions use the native TUI.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/deveco ./internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch`
- `go build ./...`
- `npm run typecheck` in `frontend`
- focused registry, model-catalog, SQLite migration, OpenCode regression, product UI, selector/avatar/settings/terminal tests
- Windows smoke test with DevEco Code 0.1.11:
  - AO detected the native executable
  - two concurrent `deveco.exe` processes launched
  - each process used a distinct Git worktree and AO agent name
  - each received its own `--prompt` argument

The two smoke-test prompts reached separate DevEco TUI processes, but file-generation completion was not asserted because the local CLI remained idle pending its interactive account/model state.

title: fix(import): preserve workspace root branch for orchestrator startup
body:
Workspace import could add a local Git root without saving its branch, then fail to start the orchestrator with `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` for `__root__`. The error incorrectly demanded a remote for a “child repository,” and the imported-project failure was invisible in the Windows/Linux board layout.

This change preserves the checked-out branch for existing workspace roots, while preventing plain nested folders from inheriting an ancestor repository’s branch. Child repositories still resolve their own defaults. Startup errors name the workspace root, retain the underlying diagnostic, and appear in both the macOS and Windows/Linux layouts.

Refs #4679. This covers the workspace-root variant of local import; it does not close the broader remote-less import issue. Existing registered projects can set their intended root default in Project Settings and retry. Remote/authentication failures remain enforced. `AGENTS.md` also records the requested requirement to run complete CI validation locally, report exact local gaps, and verify remote checks before handing over PRs.

Validation:
- 36 scanner/import/error tests passed, including a real Git regression for a plain folder nested inside a repository. The new ancestor-branch regression failed before the guard was added.
- All 61 board unit/integration tests passed after waiting for the loaded board before rendering the Windows/Linux error banner. The full CI suite caught this loading-state race; the existing empty-board regression now passes.
- Real Git integration reproduced unresolved startup without an explicit root default, then successfully created and destroyed root/child orchestrator worktrees with root `trunk` and child `dev`.
- Browser regression passed for macOS, Windows, and Linux platform detection. It exercises real renderer dialogs and the API client with mocked native picker/daemon responses, asserting the saved branch, orchestrator request, and visible actionable error.
- Final commit `56a435fbb`: full frontend CI passed (274 test files, 3,732 tests passed, 6 skipped), both typechecks passed, Cloud client verification passed (21 tests), product UI verification passed (120 tests), and full renderer-smoke CI passed. All 11 GitHub checks passed, including the complete Go build/vet/race suite (17m20s), lint, API drift, Windows workspace tests, CLI smoke on all three OSes, fresh-install container smoke, and secret scanning.
- Local pinned gitleaks scan passed for all six PR commits; no leaks found.
- Local broad verification is not all green: native browser and frontend attempts encountered timing failures under host load; the native Go run also found installed-Codex protocol differences plus process/CLI timing failures outside this change. The first local workflow runner stalled in Node setup and was stopped. A clean Linux renderer run using the pinned Playwright image completed dependency installation and the E2E typecheck, then hit startup timeouts (the page remained on “Connecting to the daemon”) across existing smoke tests and was stopped. The native frontend typecheck also remained unfinished and was stopped; both typechecks passed in CI. title: feat(daemon): add quota-exhaustion and zero-output fallback detectors
body:
Partial slice of #4918 (intake: quota-aware provider/model fallback handoff).

## Summary
Pure domain detectors for acceptance bullets 2-3, decoupled from the switch saga (#3317) and launch gate (#4895):
- `RateLimitsExhausted` — 100% used via existing `WorstUsedPercent`; absent/stale/NaN telemetry reports no signal
- `CodexSnapshotExhausted` — reuses coordinator-derived snapshot `State`, stays consistent with the display surface
- `IsZeroOutputStop` — completed turn + timestamps + no assistant text, diff, plan, or production (command/file_change/plan/mcp_tool) activity

Fail-closed throughout: uncertain input never triggers. Policy (hold, fallback chain, `ao-capacity-gate`) intentionally left for later slices.

Fixes #4918 (partial: detection slice)

## How this helps #3317 and #4895
- **#3317 (switch saga):** the saga executes handoffs but its deferred "automatic quota-based fallback" item has no trigger. These detectors are that trigger — the saga can call them to decide *when* to reassign, without changing its state machine.
- **#4895 / #4897 (launch gate):** the pre-spawn gate decides whether a spawn may proceed. The exhaustion detectors give it a fail-closed quota input: a real 100% reading can HOLD, while absent/stale telemetry stays silent instead of causing a false HOLD or a false GO.
- Both consume these as plain function calls over state they already hold. No shared state, no new dependencies, no coupling — which is also why this PR cannot conflict with either workstream (2 new files, 0 edits to existing code).

## Test
`cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./...` — full suite green (171 packages ok, 0 fail). `golangci-lint v2.12.2`: 0 issues. Race on `internal/domain`: pass.

title: perf(chat): reduce live refresh and rendering overhead
body:
## What and why

Busy chats could wait for event traffic to stop before refreshing, then hold already-received text behind the streaming animation. Large syntax blocks also occupied the main thread, while every scroll repeatedly measured the loaded transcript.

This PR reduces that overhead without changing AO's daemon/API, session lifecycle, persistence, approvals, model selection, Markdown semantics, or chat layout.

- Bound CDC batching to the first event's 150 ms deadline; preserve active requests and catch up after intervening events. Cover reconnect/target overlap and disposal races.
- Memoize grapheme segmentation, append only new text, and flush the animation backlog on the first frame at/after 200 ms, including hidden-tab resumes.
- Cache minimap anchor geometry until content/layout changes; keep every loaded turn mounted for find and selection.
- Tokenize large code blocks in a lazy worker using the existing engine, bounded pending work, and readable plain-code fallback.
- Save the requested local/remote CI validation rule in `AGENTS.md`.

## Live benchmark evidence

Identical real-renderer fixtures on pinned baseline `a96322315` and this branch; three serial repetitions per workload on Apple M5/macOS, Node 24, Chromium 148, 1440×1000. Inputs/bridge are synthetic: these measure AO renderer overhead, **not provider inference latency**.

| Median measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First query fetch starts | 2,070 ms | 152 ms |
| Fetches during continuous event stream | 0 | 10 |
| Received Unicode burst fully visible | 2,857 ms | 213 ms |
| Highlight maximum main-thread callback gap | 65.0 ms | 27.2 ms |
| Anchor measurements over 120 scroll steps | 60,001 | 251 |

**Tradeoff:** first worker highlighting completes in 128.5 ms versus 62.6 ms, including startup/transfer in the development renderer. It leaves the main thread available more often; plain code remains readable. Scroll frame-gap ranges overlap, so no general FPS claim is made.

[Method, commands, ranges, validation details and limitations](https://github.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/blob/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/README.md) · [24 raw measurement records](https://github.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/blob/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/measurements.json)

## Validation

- Full frontend suite: **3,751 passed**, 6 skipped, 275 files.
- Full browser renderer smoke suite: **52 passed**.
- Frontend/E2E types, shared-package generation/drift/tests/build/package checks, pinned browser runtime, production renderer build: passed.
- Baseline and changed-build benchmarks: **12/12 each**, including source-text/copy and 250-mounted-turn integrity checks.
- Native isolated AO startup: real daemon/preload, projects/sessions API 200, actual home screen. Built worker also ran over `app://renderer` with the production CSP and exact Unicode preservation.
- Gitleaks v7.4.0: **9 commits scanned, no leaks** using the workflow config.

The first remote renderer job exposed missing product-ui dependencies when typechecking the new real-component benchmark fixture. The workflow now installs them. A local clean-dependency reproduction failed before this step, passed afterward, and all 52 browser tests passed again.

An initial settings “Saved” timing assertion failed; its full 40-test file passed on baseline and branch, followed by a passing complete frontend rerun. Early resource-contended runs and native ABI setup failures are documented, not counted as passes. The all-workflow wrapper stopped at a missing release-build variable; no publishing job ran. Docker later became unavailable, so the pinned scanner was built and run locally. GitHub runner status is tracked in this PR's Checks tab.

## Screenshots

Same 250-turn chat, before and after; no layout redesign:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before AO chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/assets/baseline-history.png) | ![After AO chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/assets/after-history.png) |

<details><summary>Native isolated AO startup</summary>

![Native AO startup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/assets/native-home.png)

</details>

## Intentional scope

Mermaid remains untouched. Full historical refreshes remain necessary because CDC does not identify changed item ranges; narrowing them can leave old tools stale or skip pagination-boundary items. Transcript virtualization, incremental Markdown parsing, and persistence batching are excluded to preserve behavior. Worker failure/saturation or oversized source leaves plain code; it does not discard source text.

title: [Bug] All project sessions terminated sequentially with no user action; worktrees removed bypassing session_cleanup_facts; sessions left unrestorable
body:
## Environment

- AO daemon: `ao version` → `dev`; binary `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao` (built 2026-09-05 09:54)
- macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), desktop app installed and open, daemon up ~13h (pid 14290)
- Harness: claude-code, 14 sessions in one project (13 workers + 1 orchestrator), TUI mode

## What happened

At 2026-09-05 15:05:46–15:05:55 UTC **all 14 sessions of the project were terminated sequentially with no user action** — a steady mechanical cadence of ~0.68–0.70 s per session, including the orchestrator session record.

Evidence from `ao.db` `change_log` (read-only query, project scoped):

```
seq      created_at                 session_id   event_type        payload
3118052  2026-09-05 15:05:46.586    project-1    session_updated  {"activity":"exited","isTerminated":true,...}
3118054  2026-09-05 15:05:47.311    project-2    session_updated  {"activity":"exited","isTerminated":true,...}
...
3118138  2026-09-05 15:05:55.431    project-14   session_updated  {"activity":"exited","isTerminated":true,...}
```

(14 rows, seq 3118052 → 3118138, one per session in numeric order.)

Within ~2 minutes, all worker worktrees under `~/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>/` were removed as well — **but `session_cleanup_facts` has zero rows for the project**, so the documented cleanup pipeline was not the actor.

## What was NOT happening

- No `ao session kill`, no `ao session cleanup`, no `ao project rm` — none were executed from any terminal (orchestrator session shell history verified).
- The owner states no terminate/cleanup action in the desktop app.
- Preceding daemon calls from the orchestrator (≈15:01–15:04): `ao session claim-pr` twice (failed `PR_NOT_FOUND`, then `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH` — project record holds a stale repo URL), `ao project ls`, `ao project get`, and one `ao project add` upsert on the already-registered path (rejected with `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`). Listing them for completeness; no proven causation.

The orchestrator's CLI client survived (conversation is client-side) and re-registered as a new session id after the sweep killed the old orchestrator record — from the desktop it looked like "all workers disappeared".

## Secondary: the sessions are then unrecoverable

`ao session restore <id>` prints `restored`, recreates the worktree, but the agent immediately exits (`status: exited`, `isTerminated: false`); `ao send` → `AGENT_EXITED`; a second restore → `SESSION_NOT_RESTORABLE`. The agent terminal shows `Error: Session ID <uuid> is already in use.` Same family as #4280 (closed) and #3875 (open) — on a 2026-09-05 dev build. Net effect: a no-user-action sweep + broken restore = permanent loss of 13 sessions mid-flight.

Prior art for probe-failure → bulk-terminate: #1838 (closed), #1735 (closed).

## Impact

13 workers lost mid-task; recovery only via fresh sessions (externalized state — pushed branches, PRs, files outside worktrees — saved us from actual work loss).

## Asks

1. **Attribution**: persist who/what ordered a termination (API caller vs panel vs internal sweep/reaper). Today nothing in the DB can answer "who terminated these sessions", which makes incidents like this undiagnosable.
2. **Guard rails** on bulk termination paths: log the trigger, respect `is_pinned`, and consider requiring explicit intent for sweeps that include the orchestrator.
3. Fix/verify the restore path (#4280 regression, #3875) — it turns any sweep into permanent loss.

title: fix(frontend): recover terminal rendering after WebGL context loss
body:
## What

Keep an xterm terminal rendering after WebGL context loss, even if disposing the WebGL addon throws. Handle repeated loss notifications once.

## Why

Reported on desktop v0.12.10 / Electron 33.4.11 after visiting many sessions in one shell renderer. Chromium logged "Too many active WebGL contexts. Oldest context will be lost." Long-parked terminal panes became blank while their PTY attachments kept working.

The existing loss handler calls `webgl.dispose()` before `loadCanvasFallback()`. A dispose error escapes the handler and prevents the canvas renderer from loading.

## How

Set a per-addon loss flag before disposing. Warn if disposal throws, then call the existing canvas fallback. The flag also prevents repeated or reentrant notifications from disposing or loading the fallback twice. The production call site remains `loadRenderer(term)` in `XtermTerminal`.

Only `XtermTerminal.tsx` and its test file change. This does not change terminal retention, Chromium's context budget, session lifecycle, or the existing behavior if the canvas addon itself cannot load.

## Testing

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `d06b2162d0a84887d67105cae392184255032e21`. Local validation used macOS arm64, Node 24.13.0 and locked dependencies.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx` | 83 passed |
| Mutation proof: restore the upstream handler while retaining the new tests | Exactly the two new tests fail: disposal throws, and repeated loss disposes twice |
| Restore the fix | 83 passed again |
| `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` in frontend | Both pass |
| Complete frontend `npx vitest run` with the pinned agent-browser test binary | 3,734 passed, 6 skipped, zero failures |
| `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer` with an isolated port and the live daemon proxy disabled | 55 passed |
| Cloud client generate, schema drift check, typecheck, tests, pack dry run | All pass; 21 tests |
| Product UI typecheck, tests, pack dry run | All pass; 120 tests |
| Pinned CI gitleaks v7.4 image and configuration | One PR commit scanned; no leaks |

The initial complete-suite attempt lacked the SQLite native binding and Electron test dependency. Preparing those dependencies resolved the failures without source changes. The browser smoke suite passed after installing its pinned Chromium.

The local smoke run uses macOS, not CI's Ubuntu Playwright container. Remote CI remains a separate check. The new context-loss tests simulate addon events and disposal errors; no packaged-app GPU-context eviction or live desktop installation was performed.

## Checklist

- [x] Based on current upstream `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows repository conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Regression tests added and proven to fail without the fix
- [ ] Remote CI checks pass (pending upstream execution)

title: Lifecycle events never start an orchestrator turn — orchestrator sessions stall until a human types
body:
# Lifecycle events never start an orchestrator turn — orchestrator sessions stall until a human types

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| AO desktop app | `0.12.10` (`AO_TELEMETRY_APP_VERSION`) |
| `ao` CLI / daemon binary | `ao version` reports `dev` (bundled at `Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`) |
| DB schema version | goose `118` |
| OS | macOS 26.5, arm64 |
| Orchestrator harness | `pi` 0.85.0, session mode `tui` |
| Worker harnesses | `pi` 0.85.0 (tui) and `claude-code` (chat/ACP) |
| Data dir | `~/.ao/data` (default) |

## Summary

An orchestrator session has no supported way to be re-engaged by AO. Every worker
and PR lifecycle event that AO already observes durably — worker went idle, PR
became mergeable, CI failed, PR merged — updates AO state and the human-facing
notification center, but nothing starts a new orchestrator LLM turn. In a
multi-worker project the orchestrator therefore sits `idle` indefinitely while
workers finish and PRs go green, and only resumes when the human manually types
into it or runs `ao send`.

The effect is that unattended orchestration does not work: AO can supervise
agents, but the supervising agent itself must be hand-cranked.

## Reproduction

1. Register a git project and spawn an orchestrator session (`ao spawn --kind orchestrator`).
2. Spawn one or more worker sessions from it.
3. Let a worker finish its turn and open a PR; let CI go green.
4. Observe AO's own state:

```bash
# worker settles to idle (harness hook fires correctly)
sqlite3 "file:$AO_DATA_DIR/ao.db?mode=ro" \
  "select id,kind,activity_state,activity_last_at from sessions where project_id='<project>';"

# a durable notification is created — attached to the WORKER, never the orchestrator
sqlite3 "file:$AO_DATA_DIR/ao.db?mode=ro" \
  "select session_id,type,status,created_at from notifications order by created_at desc limit 5;"

# the PR fact is broadcast on the durable event stream
curl -sN "http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/events?after=<seq>" | grep -A1 'event: pr_updated'
```

5. Observe the orchestrator: `activity_state` stays `idle`, no new turn, indefinitely.
6. Run `ao send --session <orchestrator-id> --message "..."` — the orchestrator
   immediately flips to `active` and runs a turn.

## Expected

At least one supported mechanism that converts an observed lifecycle event into an
orchestrator turn. Any of:

- a lifecycle reaction that injects into the orchestrator (mirroring
  `auto_inject_ci` / `auto_inject_review`, which today target only the PR-owning
  worker), gated by a per-project or per-session toggle;
- a scheduled/heartbeat message for orchestrator sessions;
- a documented, supported callback/hook contract so an external process can
  subscribe without reverse-engineering internals.

## Actual

Nothing wakes the orchestrator. Concretely, on this build:

1. **Worker completion is observed correctly.** The managed Pi extension
   (`<workspace>/.pi/extensions/ao-activity.ts`) calls `ao hooks pi stop` on
   `agent_settled`, and `sessions.activity_state` becomes `idle`. This layer works.
2. **`ao send` delivery works.** Verified: orchestrator `idle` →
   `ao send --session <orch>` → `active` within ~4s. This layer works.
3. **Durable event/notification state works.** `notifications` rows
   (`ready_to_merge`, `pr_merged`, …) are written and survive restart;
   `GET /api/v1/events` is a durable SSE stream with monotonic `seq`, an `after`
   cursor and `Last-Event-ID` replay, and emits `session_updated`, `pr_created`,
   `pr_updated` (carrying `state`, `ci`, `review`, `mergeability`),
   `pr_check_recorded`. This layer works.
4. **Desktop toast works.** Notification center and push surfaces receive the events.
5. **Orchestrator-turn wake does not exist.** Nothing joins (1)/(3) to (2).
   - Every `notifications` row is keyed to the *worker* session
     (`notifications.session_id`); no row is ever written for the orchestrator.
     The docs confirm this is a human surface: "The notification center keeps
     durable alerts for sessions that need input, pull requests ready to merge,
     merged pull requests, and pull requests closed without merging."
     (https://aoagents.dev/docs/dashboard/)
   - `auto_inject_ci` / `auto_inject_review` (columns on `sessions`, endpoints
     `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/auto-inject-ci|auto-inject-review`) inject into the
     PR-owning worker only.
   - The embedded migration set shows this capability was **built and then
     removed**: `migrations/0038_orchestrator_reengagement.sql` is followed by
     `migrations/0039_drop_orchestrator_reengagement.sql` (leftover index names
     `idx_orchestrator_reengagements_due`, `idx_orchestrator_reengagements_attention`
     remain as strings in the binary). Nothing replaced it.
   - The full embedded OpenAPI surface has no cron, schedule, heartbeat, timer,
     or reaction endpoint. The only orchestrator-directed write paths are
     `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/send`, `/conversation/messages`, `/conversation/steer`
     and `/api/v1/orchestrators/delegate` (orchestrator → worker, not the reverse).
   - Neither https://aoagents.dev/docs/configuration/ nor
     https://aoagents.dev/docs/architecture/ documents any orchestrator
     re-engagement, heartbeat, or scheduling option.

## Impact

Any AO deployment that relies on an orchestrator agent to fan work out and land
PRs requires a human in the loop purely as a clock. Workers are supervised; the
supervisor is not. The workaround is for an external process to subscribe to
`/api/v1/events` and call `ao send` on the orchestrator, which duplicates
lifecycle logic AO already owns and depends on internal event payload shapes.

## Suggested fix

Reinstate orchestrator re-engagement as a first-class, opt-in feature — the
0038 design, with the properties the workaround had to reimplement:

- driven by the existing durable event stream, so it survives daemon restart and
  client reconnect;
- deduplicated by PR/session state signature so an unchanged state is announced once;
- coalesced with a quiet window and a minimum send gap, plus a hard rate cap;
- bounded failure behaviour (never blocks the daemon, never retries unboundedly);
- respects the existing rule that lifecycle messages are not injected while a
  controller is blocked.

## Notes

No secrets are included above. All values are local, non-secret configuration and
schema identifiers. Investigation was read-only against the daemon
(`GET /api/v1/events`, `GET /api/v1/notifications`, read-only SQLite) plus one
documented `ao send`; the daemon was not restarted and no credentials were touched.

## Related

- #4411 (`feat: bring back ao report for worker-to-orchestrator reporting`) covers
  the complementary *worker-initiated* channel. It does not cover this issue: the
  events here (PR became mergeable, CI failed, PR merged, worker died) are observed
  by AO itself, not by the worker, and a worker that has already settled or crashed
  cannot report them. A durable fix likely needs both directions.

The "Worker agent" and "Orchestrator agent" dropdowns in the "Workspace agents" dialog list every agent with a "Needs install" label, even for agents that are installed and working from the terminal. This makes it impossible to create a workspace or start a task. ## Environment - AO version: v0.12.10 Stable - OS: Windows - Install method: - Last version where agents were detected correctly: ### Steps to reproduce 1. error parsing sqlc.yaml: yaml: line 244: found character that cannot start any token
```text
exit status 1
```

The authoritative command in `package.json` pins `github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1`. `AGENTS.md` requires changes to queries/migrations followed by `npm run sqlc` and forbids hand-editing generated files. CI currently has an API-generation drift job but no sqlc regeneration drift job.

## Cause

These entries begin with tabs rather than the surrounding YAML indentation:

```yaml
	          - column: "agent_switch_failure_policy.enabled"
	          - column: "app_settings.cloud_offering"
            go_type: "bool"
```

They also appear to collapse two intended column overrides under one `go_type`. A minimal correction must preserve both boolean overrides and then regenerate with the pinned version. Regeneration currently exposes additional agent-switch query drift, so that output should be reviewed rather than hand-maintained or folded silently into unrelated feature work.

## Expected

`npm run sqlc` succeeds from a clean checkout and `git diff --exit-code -- backend/internal/storage/sqlite/gen` is clean. Consider enforcing that command in CI.

## Related

- #4621: earlier reproducibility report for `app_settings.cloud_offering`
- #4951: durable orchestration outbox work currently blocked from producing an isolated, reproducible generated diff

title: fix(updates): honor saved channels and recover stalled checks
body:
## What and why

Update checks can leave Settings showing “Checking for updates” indefinitely: automatic checks did not settle a returned result when a completion event was absent, and a hung metadata request kept electron-updater's cached check promise and AO's operation queue occupied.

Both automatic and manual checks now settle returned results. A 60-second deadline cancels metadata requests through their cancellation tokens, displays an actionable timeout, and waits for the original check to unwind before allowing a queued retry. The adapter wraps only the updater executor's metadata `request` method during a serialized check and restores it afterward; download cancellation remains separate. This uses electron-updater's internal executor field, verified against the installed library in a real Electron probe. Closing the network session alone did not release the check promise in that probe, so the implementation cancels the requests instead.

The saved channel remains a persistent preference. A user running `0.12.11-nightly.202609051608` who selected Stable is offered stable `0.12.10`, including after restarting or retrying a failed check. That cross-channel downgrade is intended; the original downgrade screenshot alone does not establish a bug. Older releases within the installed channel are rejected. Fresh nightly installs retain Nightly when automatic downloads are declined, existing explicit choices are preserved, and rejected manifests do not redownload the cached staged candidate.

## Validation

- Five new regressions failed before this fix: automatic result settlement and stalled manual, automatic, and return-home checks.
- Updater/settings suite: 117 tests passed, including cancellation/queue ordering and keeping the check deadline away from downloads.
- Real Electron probe of the changed production code against a local stalled manifest: timeout surfaced, followed by a successful retry that discovered version 99.0.0. The probe shortened only the deadline to two seconds; production uses 60 seconds.
- Frontend and E2E typechecks passed. Cloud client generation/typechecks/21 tests/package dry run and product UI typecheck/120 tests/package dry run passed.
- Full local frontend run: all 3,754 assertions passed, but an unexpected HTTP GET hit browser-runtime-link.test.ts's JSON socket and produced an unhandled error. A complete rerun again encountered HTTP socket interference (273 files passed; that file had one failed test and unhandled parse errors). This is **not a clean local full-suite pass**. An earlier interrupted run also had a roughly 14-minute timing jump and UI timeouts; subsequent runs used a temporary sleep inhibitor. The full suite requires verification on the isolated CI runner.
- Local renderer smoke: 53 passed, 2 failed on initial chat/terminal rendering timeouts. A full rerun encountered 6 UI timeouts and was interrupted (4 passed, 1 interrupted, 44 not run). This is **not a clean local renderer-smoke pass**. All three checks passed on final head `5a4ee39d6cbbe8043927f157d55de6abd5efc79c`: frontend tests (5m19s), isolated Linux renderer smoke (2m14s), and gitleaks (20s).

Local checks use Node 24.20.0. Docker is unavailable locally, so the pinned Linux renderer-smoke container and gitleaks also require remote verification. No publishing workflow is used for validation.

## Limits and rollout

This does not cancel an already staged native installer or implement the separate recovery work in #4905. Release manifests, publication schedules, and signing configuration are unchanged. Installed clients need a conductor-built release containing the fix.

title: fix(desktop): improve embedded browser toolbar and import UX
body:
## Problem
The embedded browser toolbar has several related UX inconsistencies:

- Compact URLs are left-aligned while docked, but editing should remain left-aligned and maximized mode should keep the full URL.
- There is no address-bar action to open the current page in the system browser.
- The Browser Controls button appears selected merely because a profile or DevTools is active.
- Closing the Browser Controls menu can queue and display its tooltip even though the pointer is no longer hovering it.
- When a pinned tab rail drops to one tab, the toolbar trigger disappears and Recently Closed becomes unreachable.
- Browser-profile import exposes raw Electron/SQLite errors when a source browser still holds its database.

**Source:** Reported and reproduced during a local AO desktop development session
**Platform:** Windows
**Analyzed against:** `5186c8d7d2069a6a6444a3be0dff172d0b9249bd`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — browser workflows remain usable, but common navigation and import paths are confusing or inaccessible.

## Reproduction
1. Open AO's embedded browser in docked and maximized modes and inspect/focus the address bar.
2. Activate a saved browser profile or DevTools and observe the Browser Controls button.
3. Open Browser Controls, dismiss it outside, and observe focus returning to the trigger.
4. Pin the tab rail, reduce the browser to one tab, and try to access Recently Closed.
5. Attempt to import from a running Chromium-family browser whose profile database is locked.

## Root cause
The browser panel used unconditional input alignment, treated configuration state as a pressed-button state, allowed Radix focus return to reopen the controls tooltip, and hid the tab trigger solely from the pinned flag. Import errors were surfaced directly from the IPC rejection without classifying locked/inaccessible source databases.

## Expected behavior
The address bar should use context-appropriate alignment, expose a system-browser action, keep Browser Controls visually neutral, show its tooltip only from actual hover, preserve access to Recently Closed, and provide browser-agnostic recovery guidance for locked or inaccessible profile databases.

title: bug(daemon): importing a single-repo folder as a workspace tells the user to git init their subdirectories instead of suggesting "Import project"
body:
## Bug

"Import workspace" applied to a folder that is itself a single, fully valid git repository fails with `WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS`, and the error's remediation pushes the user in the wrong direction.

### Repro

1. Have a normal single-repo project (the typical layout of a plain repo — no nested repositories):

```
~/code/my-app/          ← git repo, origin configured, clean main
├── src/
├── dashboard/
├── config/
├── scripts/
└── docs/
```

2. Desktop app → New project → **Import workspace** → pick `~/code/my-app`.
3. Every child directory is listed as `Needs git init`, and the import fails:

> **IMPORT FAILED · WORKSPACE NOT REGISTERED**
> Workspace project must contain at least one fully resolved git repository with an origin remote (`WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS`)
>
> Initialize at least one child repository with a remote origin, then retry.

### What's wrong

- The workspace scan (`detectWorkspaceChildren`) only inspects **direct children** of the picked folder; the root's own `.git` is not counted. That is correct for the workspace model (a container folder + child repos), but it means a single-repo folder can never pass.
- The `suggestedFix` ("Initialize at least one child repository with a remote origin") is actively harmful in this shape: following it means running `git init` inside `src/`, `docs/`, etc. — corrupting the layout of what is actually a perfectly fine single repository.
- Nothing in the error points at the actual right action: this folder should have been imported via **"Import project"** ("Import a single Git repository as one project"). The two modes sit next to each other in the create flow, and this mistake is easy to make.

### Suggested fix

Before emitting `WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS` (`backend/internal/service/project/workspace_registration.go`, the `hasReady` check), detect the "wrong import mode" shape and return a targeted error instead:

- **Condition:** the parent itself is a standalone, non-bare repo with a resolved `HEAD` and an origin remote, **and** none of the children is a git repository.
- **Message:** e.g. `WORKSPACE_PARENT_IS_SINGLE_REPO` — "This folder looks like a single git repository, not a folder containing several repositories. Use 'Import project' to add it."

This combination already fails registration today, so redirecting the message is pure UX — no currently-working configuration changes behavior. A workspace parent that is itself a repo remains legitimate (the `adoptWorkspaceParent` path), because in that case at least one child is a real repo and the new condition doesn't fire.

### Related

- #3686 covered the opposite import failure shape (many child repos failing child-level validation → a wall of errors). This is the zero-children-repos case, where the folder simply isn't a workspace.

Analyzed against `d06b2162d`.

title: Cloud session startup improvement and other bug fixes
body:
# Cloud startup, private GitHub repos, and dynamic orchestrator agent

## What

Improve the Cloud session startup and private-repository experience:

- Start worker transport before repository checkout completes.
- Run checkout and coding-agent initialization in parallel.
- Keep the Cloud terminal on a continuous `Connecting…` state until the agent TUI emits its first output.
- Add encrypted, user-scoped GitHub PAT support for private GitHub repositories.
- Dynamically choose the Cloud orchestrator harness from connected Cloud credentials instead of always using Codex.
- Remove temporary startup timing instrumentation.

## Why

Cloud sessions had unnecessary perceived startup delay and visible blank terminal transitions:

- Repository checkout blocked worker and terminal availability.
- The terminal could attach before Codex had drawn, exposing an empty terminal between loading states.
- Private GitHub repositories could hang or fail without a checkout credential.
- Cloud orchestrators always requested Codex, even when the user had only connected Claude Code or Cursor.

This improves the Cloud parity and startup roadmap. 

Issue #4575 

## How

- Worker transport, heartbeat, checkout renewal, PR bridge, and review bridge start independently from repository preparation.
- Agent input remains queued until checkout completes, preventing work from running in an empty workspace.
- `worker.ready` signals transport availability; `agent.ready` signals coding-agent terminal startup.
- Cloud terminal replay remains covered until the first agent terminal bytes are rendered. Local terminal replay behavior is unchanged.
- GitHub PATs are encrypted in the existing user-scoped provider credential store:
  - no GitHub OAuth flow;
  - no validation request is made when saving;
  - the secret is never returned or logged;
  - only a worker for a session created by that user can retrieve it.
- The orchestrator reads valid organization and personal Cloud credentials, then chooses:
  1. Codex
  2. Claude Code
  3. Cursor

The worker image still intentionally supports only those three installed harnesses. This does not add arbitrary-harness support.

## Testing

Validated locally with:

```bash
cd cloud && go test ./cmd/ao-worker ./internal/reconcile
```

```bash
cd frontend
npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts \
  src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/lib/cloud-orchestrator.test.ts

npm run typecheck
```

Also verified:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Manual scenario validated with the local Docker Cloud control plane:

- Signed in to local Cloud.
- Saved a GitHub PAT in Cloud Settings.
- Created a Cloud project backed by a private repository.
- Confirmed private repository checkout succeeds.
- Confirmed the terminal stays on `Connecting…` until the agent TUI renders.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing the existing `cloud/bug-fix` branch
- [x] Focused Cloud startup/private-repository improvement; no related issue supplied
- [x] Follows [[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md)](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for terminal loading and orchestrator harness selection
- [x] Relevant Cloud Go and frontend checks pass

title: bug(opencode): provider-only model override reaches ACP without actionable validation
body:
## Bug
OpenCode Chat accepts a provider display name as a model override and forwards it to ACP. A reported Windows orchestrator launch sent `TensorMux`, producing `Invalid params: model not found: TensorMux` inside `CHAT_CONTROLLER_FAILED`.

AO should reject an override without the required `provider/model` shape before launching the provider and explain how to recover. The attached report showed `tensormux/glm-4-7-flash` in OpenCode configuration, but `TensorMux` in the AO error. The report does not establish how that override was entered, and this issue does not claim AO converted a valid model ID into a provider name.

## Evidence and reproduction
- Source: user-provided screenshots; reporter and installed AO/OpenCode versions are unavailable.
- Analyzed against main `7e8a66229`.
- Reproduced at the real OpenCode Chat driver boundary with an injected plugin: both Start and Resume with `Model: "TensorMux"` proceed to binary resolution instead of returning a model validation error.
- A valid OpenCode override uses `provider_id/model_id`: [OpenCode model documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/models/#set-a-default).
- Confidence: high for the missing validation; no claim of an end-to-end reproduction on the reporter's Windows machine.

## Scope
Wire an OpenCode-specific `ValidateTurnSettings` callback into the existing ACP lifecycle. Reject missing or empty provider/model parts with `ErrChatConfigOptionInvalid` and recovery guidance. Keep empty overrides (Agent default) and custom, provider-qualified IDs unchanged.

TensorMux credential validity and provider configuration are outside this issue. `opencode auth list` in the report already lists a stored credential; that does not prove it authenticates successfully. No provider settings or credentials need to be modified.

Workaround: select `tensormux/glm-4-7-flash` in AO, or clear AO's model override to let OpenCode choose its configured default.
