title: Kiro auth probe reports unknown: kiro-cli whoami --format json appends non-JSON profile trailer
body:
### Summary
`ao agent ls --refresh` always reports `kiro auth unknown`, even when `kiro-cli whoami` proves a valid, active login. The daemon's Kiro auth probe classifies `kiro-cli whoami --format json` output with the generic keyword matcher in `authprobe.StatusFromText`, but that JSON output never contains any of the recognized keywords (`logged in`, `authenticated`, `"loggedin": true`, etc.), so a signed-in session is always classified as `unknown`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Sign in to Kiro (`kiro-cli login`, or via IAM Identity Center / SSO).
2. Confirm the session is valid: `kiro-cli whoami` prints a "Logged in with..." message and an email.
3. Run `kiro-cli whoami --format json` directly and inspect stdout (see "Actual behavior" below).
4. Run `ao agent ls --refresh` (or open the New Task / agent catalog UI).

### Expected behavior
`ao agent ls --refresh` reports the `kiro` row as `installed` / authorized (or at least not `unknown`) when `kiro-cli whoami` proves an active login.

### Actual behavior
The `kiro` row shows:

```
kiro  Kiro  installed  auth unknown
```

Root cause, reproduced locally with `kiro-cli 2.21.1` on macOS:

`kiro-cli whoami --format json` prints a JSON object followed by a plain-text trailer, so stdout as a whole is not valid JSON (`jq .` on it exits 5):

```
{"accountType":"IamIdentityCenter","email":"<redacted>","region":"eu-west-1","startUrl":"https://d-<redacted>.awsapps.com/start"}

Profile:
KiroProfile-us-east-1
arn:aws:codewhisperer:us-east-1:<redacted>:profile/<redacted>
```

Exit code is 0 in all cases (`--format json`, `--format json-pretty`, and plain format). The plain format instead prints `Logged in with IAM Identity Center (https://...)` then `Email: ...` then the same `Profile:` block.

The probe function `kiro.kiroWhoamiAuthStatus` (in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/auth.go`, called from `kiro.(*Plugin).AuthStatus`) runs `kiro-cli whoami --format json` and hands the raw output straight to `authprobe.StatusFromText` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/authprobe/authprobe.go`), which only recognizes generic phrases like `logged in`, `authenticated`, `"loggedin": true`. None of those appear in the JSON identity object above (its fields are `accountType`, `email`, `region`, `startUrl`), so the probe falls through to `AgentAuthStatusUnknown` even for a fully authenticated session — independent of, and in addition to, the JSON-plus-trailer parsing issue.

### AO version
`dev` (built from `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator@main`, `go run ./cmd/ao`; `ao version` reports `dev` in this build)

### Environment
macOS (darwin/arm64), Go 1.25.4, kiro-cli 2.21.1

### Logs / extra context
No daemon crash or error — this is a silent misclassification. All account identifiers above are redacted placeholders (`<redacted>`), not real values.

---
This issue was generated by Claude Code Agent.

title: fix(kiro): recognize authorized identity in whoami --format json output
body:
## What

Fixes the Kiro auth probe so a valid `kiro-cli` login is reported as authorized instead of `unknown`.

## Why

`ao agent ls --refresh` always shows:

```
kiro  Kiro  installed  auth unknown
```

even when `kiro-cli whoami` proves an active, valid login.

Fixes #5048

## How

`kiro.kiroWhoamiAuthStatus` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/auth.go`) ran `kiro-cli whoami --format json` and handed the raw stdout to the generic `authprobe.StatusFromText` keyword classifier. Two things broke it:

1. `kiro-cli whoami --format json` prints a JSON identity object followed by a plain-text `Profile:` trailer, so stdout as a whole is not valid JSON.
2. Even ignoring the trailer, the JSON object's field names (`accountType`, `email`, `region`, `startUrl`) never match any of the keyword classifier's phrases (`logged in`, `authenticated`, `"loggedin": true`, …), so a signed-in session was always classified `unknown`.

The fix keeps the existing keyword-based "not logged in" detection (unchanged behavior for the logged-out case) but, when that classifier returns `unknown`, decodes only the leading JSON value from stdout with `json.NewDecoder(...).Decode(...)` (which stops at the end of the first JSON value and ignores the trailing text) and treats a non-empty `accountType`, `email`, or `startUrl` as evidence of an authorized session.

## Testing

```
cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/kiro/... -v
```

All tests pass, including two new cases:

- `TestAuthStatusHandlesJSONFormatTrailer` — uses the exact (redacted) `whoami --format json` + `Profile:` trailer output and asserts `authorized`.
- `TestAuthStatusUnknownForEmptyJSONIdentity` — an empty `{}` JSON object still reports `unknown`.

Also ran:

```
gofmt -l backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/auth.go backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/kiro_test.go   # no output
cd backend && go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/kiro/...                                                    # clean

```

title: [Bug](agent-agy): session stuck working/active after turn interrupted (Escape) without Stop hook — observer skips agy, no TerminalActivityDetector
body: ### Summary An agy (Antigravity CLI) session remains permanently stuck in status=working / activity=active (showing a blue dot in the UI) after a tool execution or turn is interrupted with Escape, because the Stop hook never fires and the agy adapter does not implement TerminalActivityDetector. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Spawn an agy worker session (ao spawn --harness agy ...). 2. Start a prompt or turn that runs an in-flight tool or command (e.g. Bash(...) -> activity transitions to active via pre-invocation / post-tool-use hooks). 3. While the tool/command is running, press Escape to interrupt/cancel it. 4. The CLI cancels execution, displays "Interrupted · What should Antigravity CLI do instead?", and sits idle at the prompt (> ). 5. Observe the session in the AO sidebar and inspector: the session remains stuck in "Working" (blue circle dot) indefinitely, even hours or days later. ### Expected behavior When an agy turn is interrupted and the terminal returns to the idle prompt (> ), AO should recognize that execution has stopped and transition the session's activity state back to idle (removing the blue "Working" indicator). ### Actual behavior The session stays permanently in activity_state = active (status = working, blue dot) indefinitely. Inspecting SQLite (~/.ao/data/ao.db) reveals activity_state never changed back to idle because: 1. agy aborted execution without invoking the Stop hook. 2. The background activity observer (backend/internal/observe/activity/observer.go) skips agy because the agy adapter does not implement ports.TerminalActivityDetector. ### AO version 0.12.12 (stable) ### Environment macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Go 1.26.7, Node v24.11.0, agy CLI ### Logs / extra context ```shell ### Database State Query from `~/.ao/data/ao.db`: vexa-3|agy|active|0|tui|2026-09-05 20:46:50.849354 +0000 UTC The session was aborted days ago and is sitting at the prompt, but `activity_state` remains `active`. ### Terminal Output Bash(uv run --directory backend python -c *) (ctrl+o to expand) Interrupted · What should Antigravity CLI do instead? > █ ? for shortcuts accept-edits · Gemini 3.8 Flash · high ### Root Cause 1. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/agy/activity.go`: The `agy` adapter only maps the `stop` hook to `domain.ActivityIdle`. 2. When interrupted via Escape, the `agy` process aborts the turn immediately and does not invoke the `stop` hook. 3. `backend/internal/observe/activity/observer.go:116`: The 30-second activity reconciler checks: detector, ok := agent.(ports.TerminalActivityDetector) if !ok { return // skips agy entirely } Because `agy` does not implement `ports.TerminalActivityDetector`, the background observer cannot screen-detect that `agy` is sitting at `> ` and skips reconciliation. ### Proposed Fix Implement `ports.TerminalActivityDetector` on `agy.Plugin` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/agy/` so that when `agy` is quiet past the staleness threshold and the terminal shows an idle prompt (`> `), the observer screen-proves idle and reconciles `activity_state` back to `idle`. ### Related Issues #4142 — Claude Code instance of this exact bug (`DetectTerminalActivity` added for aborted turns) #3387 — Kimi instance of this bug #3115 — Codex instance of this bug ``` ### Before submitting - [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates - [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(workspace): keep a backslash in a filename on Linux and macOS
body:
## What

Applies the backslash-to-slash normalization in `cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` only on Windows.

Fixes #5044.

## Why

Backslash is a path separator on Windows and an ordinary filename character everywhere else. `cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` folded it unconditionally, so on Linux and macOS a workspace file named `weird\name.txt` could not be read through the workspace-files API — and where a `weird/` directory happened to exist, the request silently returned a *different* file's contents instead of failing.

The file carried no `runtime.GOOS` reference at all, so a Windows-only rule was being applied on every platform.

## How

One conditional around the existing `ReplaceAll`.

The traversal guards are untouched: empty input, absolute paths, `..` and `../`-prefixed paths are still rejected. A second test pins that, so this cannot be read as loosening validation while widening what filenames are accepted.

title: fix(scm/github): stop sending an ignored `since` to the pulls endpoint
body:
## What

Stops sending `since` to the pull-requests endpoint, and applies the incremental watermark client-side instead.

Fixes #5045.

## Why

`ListPRsByRepo` passed `since` to `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`. That endpoint has no such parameter — `since` belongs to the Issues API — and GitHub silently ignores unknown query parameters rather than erroring. The incremental watermark therefore did nothing: every repository with any change re-listed all of its open PRs, and paged through all of them, on every poll.

Nothing surfaced this, which is why it survived: the code reads as though it were filtering.

## How

The filter moves to the client, where it is exact rather than best-effort. The query already asks for `sort=updated&direction=desc`, so the first PR at or before the watermark means every remaining one is older — the loop returns there instead of walking the remaining pages.

An unparseable `updated_at` keeps the PR rather than dropping it. A redundant observation costs one extra comparison; a missed one loses a PR update.

## Testing

`TestListPRsByRepoFiltersOnWatermarkWithoutSinceParam` asserts both halves — that the request carries no `since`, and that only PRs newer than the watermark come back. Without the fix it fails with:

```
request carried since="2026-01-02T00:00:00Z"; the pulls endpoint ignores it
```

`TestListPRsByRepoZeroWatermarkReturnsEverything` pins that a zero watermark still returns a full listing, so the change cannot be read as filtering more than it should. Package tests pass.

title: fix(copilot): exclude session agent profiles with one glob, not one line per session
body:
## What

Excludes AO's Copilot session profiles with one glob instead of one line per session, and prunes the per-session lines earlier versions left behind.

Fixes #5046.

## Why

The adapter writes a role profile to `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` and adds it to the workspace's `.git/info/exclude`. `ignoreCopilotPath` already guards against duplicates:

```go
if pattern == "" || strings.Contains(string(data), pattern) {
    return nil
}
```

but the pattern it receives is the literal profile path, and `copilotAgentName` returns `"ao-" + sessionID`. Every session therefore presents a different pattern, the guard can never match a previous entry, and each session appends another line to a file that belongs to the user rather than to AO. Nothing removes them.

Worth being explicit since the guard looks correct at a glance: the duplicate check works exactly as written — it is the value being checked that makes it ineffective.

## How

Exclude `/.github/agents/ao-*.agent.md` once. One line covers every session, past and future.

The same write also prunes the superseded per-session lines, so existing repositories are repaired rather than merely stopping the growth. Only lines matching the exact shape this package wrote are removed: the regex is anchored and rejects a `*`, so a user's own entry under that directory is left alone. A test pins that unrelated rules in the file survive.

## Testing

- `TestIgnoreCopilotPathWritesOneGlobForAllSessions` — three calls leave exactly one pattern.
- `TestIgnoreCopilotPathPrunesPerSessionLines` — pre-existing `ao-work-1` / `ao-work-2` lines are removed, the glob is present, and the user's own `# user's own rules` / `/build` entries are untouched.

Three existing tests asserted the literal per-session line. They now assert the glob: their intent — "the profile is git-excluded" — is unchanged, and the glob covers the same file. Package tests pass.

title: fix(mobile): apply a saved project filter only when the daemon still lists it
body:
Fixes #4843.

## What

The board's project filter is now derived from the saved choice **and** the project list the daemon returns. A saved filter naming a project the daemon no longer lists applies as **All projects**; Settings and the switcher label the filter honestly while the list cannot name it; the spawn sheet drops a seeded project the list turns out not to have; and when a valid filter hides every session, the board's empty state says so and offers **Show all projects** instead of "No active agents / Spawn a worker".

## Why

`ao.activeProject` was restored from AsyncStorage and never checked. `ao project rm` on the desktop, or pairing the phone with a machine whose projects differ, left it pointing at an id no session carries. The board filtered everything out, the spawn sheet posted the dead id and showed the 404, and nothing said the board was filtered: the switcher hides below two projects, and Settings labelled the stale id "All projects" because its lookup missed. The reporter's way out was clearing app storage.

## Changes

- `lib/projectFilter.ts` (new, pure, RN-free) — owns `ALL_PROJECTS` (moved from `ProjectPickerSheet`, its only user) and three helpers:
  - `resolveActiveProject(id, projects)`: the id when the list names it, `"all"` when it does not. **An empty list is not evidence**: it is the initial state before the first fetch, and `getSessions` substitutes `[]` when `/projects` fails so the board can still render. Judging against either would drop a valid filter on every cold start or every blip. A daemon with no projects has no sessions to filter, so nothing is lost by waiting for a list that names something.
  - `activeProjectLabel(id, projects)`: the name, "All projects", or the raw id while the list cannot name it. The "All projects" fallback is what hid the stale filter from the reporter.
  - `filteredEmptyCopy(label, {live, archived})`: names the filter and counts what Show all projects would put on the board; archived-only gets its own sentence rather than "0 agents".
- `lib/store.tsx` — the saved choice becomes `chosenProjectId`; `activeProjectId`, which every consumer already reads, is `useMemo(resolveActiveProject(chosen, projects))`. **Derived, not reset-and-written-back**, on purpose: the project can disappear while the app is open and the stored value can land after the first list does; storage is only ever written by a tap, as before; a late response from a machine the user just left cannot discard the filter they picked on the new one; and the choice comes back if the project does.
- `app/(tabs)/index.tsx` — a third empty state between the error and "No active agents", rendered only when the filter is not all and the daemon returned sessions for other projects. Live and archived counted apart via the board's own `isArchived`. `errorActions` became `emptyActions` since two empty states now share the row.
- `app/spawn.tsx` — the seed effect re-checks its `projectId` with the same helper and re-seeds when the list does not have it, so a dead id captured before the list landed is not posted. A pick from the picker is always on the list, so a pick is never overridden.
- `app/(tabs)/settings.tsx`, `lib/ProjectSwitcher.tsx` — labels via `activeProjectLabel`; the switcher keeps its colour logic.
- `lib/projectFilter.test.ts` — 10 tests over the three helpers.

## Scenarios

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Cold start, saved filter names a listed project | kept | kept, no storage write |
| Cold start, saved filter names a removed project | board empty, Settings "All projects", spawn 404 | applies as all from the first list; storage untouched |
| Storage read lands after the first list | same as above | same, on that render |
| `ao project rm` while the app is open | board empties at the next poll | the next poll's list makes it all |
| `/projects` fails on a tick (`getSessions` substitutes `[]`) | filter untouched | filter untouched; a stale one shows "Filtered to <id>" with Show all projects until the next good tick |
| Daemon lists no projects | — | filter untouched, nothing to show either way |
| Re-paired to another machine | stale filter from the old machine | validated against the new list on its first fetch; the old machine's choice is kept in storage |
| Late response from the previous machine after re-pairing | transient display glitch | still only that: nothing is written back |
| Spawn sheet opened before the list lands, saved filter dead | dead id posted, 404 | seed dropped when the list lands; re-seeds from the store |
| Filter valid, project has no sessions, others do | "No active agents" | "No agents in this project. Filtered to X. N agents are in other projects." + Show all projects, New agent |
| Same, but the other projects hold only archived sessions | "No active agents" | "… Other projects have only archived sessions." + the same buttons |

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — 719 passed (709 on main + 10)
- `npx expo export --platform ios` — bundles
- iPhone 17 Pro simulator, Debug build, packaged 0.12.11 daemon (one project `scratch`, three live sessions, one terminated session left from a removed project `ao-mobile-pr-test`). Set `ao.activeProject = "ao-mobile-pr-test"` by editing the AsyncStorage manifest with the app closed, launched on `main`, then on this branch:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Board | 0 working · 0 need you · 0 mergeable, Archive 1 | 2 working, both live cards, Archive 8 |
| `ao.activeProject` after launch | `ao-mobile-pr-test` | `ao-mobile-pr-test` — storage untouched, the fallback is derived |

## Not verified

- The filtered empty state and the spawn re-seed on a device: the test daemon has one project, so a valid filter cannot hide anything there and the sheet's seed is always on the list. Both are covered by the helper tests and the walk-through above.
- Android: JS-only, nothing platform-specific.

## Not changed

- `ProjectSwitcher` still hides below two projects. With the fallback in place a stale filter never needs the escape, and a one-project row would show a value that cannot change.
- `getSessions` still folds a failed `/projects` into `[]`, which is why the helper treats an empty list as unknown. Keeping the last good list instead (`catch(() => null)` + `setProjects(prev => next ?? prev)`) would also stop the switcher and Settings flickering to "All projects" on a failed tick, but that changes a shared response shape and is its own issue.

## Known limitation

A stale filter and a permanently failing `/projects` keep the board empty, with the filtered empty state naming the id and offering Show all projects. The daemon cannot say what it has, so the app does not guess.

title: bug(updates): nightly build timestamp is interpreted as local wall time instead of UTC
body:
## Bug

The Updates UI shows the UTC nightly build stamp as if it were already local wall time. Users outside UTC therefore see the wrong instant. The visible clock time stays equal to the UTC digits instead of being converted to the device timezone.

Analyzed against upstream main commit `c8308e64983014ac640f05df87888b7b85a25a2a` on 2026-09-07.

**Confidence:** High. The timestamp producer, parser, every renderer consumer, and current tests were traced.

**Impact:** User facing timestamp correctness only. Stored release metadata and update ordering remain correct. Stable versions and the separate Last checked timestamp are unaffected.

## Reproduction

1. Run AO in a non UTC timezone, for example `Asia/Kolkata`.
2. Install or stage nightly `v0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`.
3. Open Settings, then Updates.
4. Observe that the build time is displayed as Sep 7, 10:35 AM.
5. The embedded stamp is 2026-09-07 10:35 UTC, so the equivalent local time in India is Sep 7, 4:05 PM.

The same input currently renders 10:35 AM in `America/Los_Angeles`; the correct local time is 3:35 AM. Timezones near a date boundary can also receive the wrong calendar day in the sidebar and restart dialog.

## Timestamp source and storage distinction

GitHub release metadata remains an absolute UTC ISO timestamp. For example, the current release API returns `published_at: 2026-09-07T10:56:41Z` for `v0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`. The generated updater feed likewise stores `releaseDate` as `new Date().toISOString()` in `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`.

The affected UI does not currently render `published_at` or `releaseDate` directly. It derives the displayed build time from the `YYYYMMDDHHMM` stamp embedded in the nightly version. That stamp is also UTC:

1. `frontend/scripts/nightly-version.mjs:19-24` creates it with `getUTCFullYear`, `getUTCMonth`, `getUTCDate`, `getUTCHours`, and `getUTCMinutes`.
2. `frontend/src/renderer/lib/build-channel.ts:18-28` extracts those UTC fields but passes them to `new Date(year, month, day, hour, minute)`.
3. That Date constructor interprets its fields in the device local timezone. The represented instant is already shifted before `Intl.DateTimeFormat` receives it.
4. The locale formatter then behaves correctly for the wrong instant, so it reproduces the UTC clock digits instead of converting UTC to local time.

The stored UTC ISO timestamps, UTC nightly stamp, and ordering semantics should remain unchanged. This is an interpretation and presentation bug.

## Affected surfaces

1. Settings, Updates: `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx:394-397,476-485`. This displays the full incorrect local date and time for the installed nightly.
2. Sidebar available or ready update row: `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:2111-2123`. This can display the wrong local calendar day.
3. Restart to update dialog: `frontend/src/renderer/components/RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx:47-57`. This can display the wrong local calendar day.
4. Shared parser tests: `frontend/src/renderer/lib/build-channel.test.ts:24-33` assert local getters and therefore encode the incorrect interpretation. Their result also depends on the test process timezone.

The Last checked value in `UpdatesSection.tsx:418-420` is epoch milliseconds formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`; it already represents an absolute instant and is not part of this bug.

## Root cause

`parseNightlyVersion` parses a UTC encoded version stamp with the local component Date constructor. It should construct the instant from UTC components, for example with `Date.UTC`, and validate against UTC getters. Once the Date represents the right instant, the existing `Intl.DateTimeFormat` calls will render the equivalent time or date in the user local timezone by default.

The defect was introduced with the current nightly presentation in commit `190df05fc21494cdca637a70622a3fbfa6273684` through [PR #4849](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4849).

## Expected behavior

For nightly stamp `202609071035`:

1. The parsed instant is `2026-09-07T10:35:00.000Z`.
2. `Asia/Kolkata` renders Sep 7, 2026 at 4:05 PM.
3. `America/Los_Angeles` renders Sep 7, 2026 at 3:35 AM.
4. All renderer surfaces use the device local timezone and locale.
5. UTC storage, feed metadata, release metadata, and version ordering do not change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Parse the nightly version stamp as UTC, not local wall time.
2. Settings Updates renders the equivalent device local date and time.
3. Sidebar and restart dialog render the correct device local calendar date, including UTC day boundary cases.
4. Existing stable, feature, malformed version, and trailing commit stamp behavior remains unchanged.
5. The separate Last checked display remains unchanged.
6. No UTC timestamp in GitHub metadata, updater feeds, or version strings is rewritten to local time.

## Tests

1. Update `build-channel.test.ts` to assert `builtAt.toISOString()` or `builtAt.getTime()` against `Date.UTC(...)`, not local getters.
2. Add positive offset and negative offset coverage showing the same UTC instant renders to the expected local time.
3. Add a day boundary case for the date only sidebar and restart dialog consumers.
4. Keep coverage for malformed stamps and trailing commit metadata.
5. Add or update component assertions for the Settings full timestamp and the two date only surfaces.

## Related

1. [Issue #2377](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2377): original restart to update and Updates screen specification.
2. [Issue #5041](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5041): recent sidebar update flow work using the shared nightly label.
3. [PR #4849](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4849): introduced the shared nightly parser and current display consumers.

## Duplicate search

Searched all issue and pull request states using: `updates timezone UTC nightly built`, `updates local time timestamp`, `nightly build date timezone`, `GitHub release timestamp UTC`, `parseNightlyVersion`, `nightly timestamp`, `built time`, `local timezone`, and `nightly date wrong`. No exact duplicate was found.

title: fix(agy): reconcile terminal idle on aborted turns
body:
Code changes: +89 -8  
Tests: +125 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Implements `ports.TerminalActivityDetector` for the Agy (Antigravity CLI) adapter so the background activity observer can screen-prove idle state and reconcile sessions whose in-flight turn was interrupted. Also fixes a turn settlement ordering race in the ACP chatdriver where `ChatControllerReady` was emitted before clearing active turn state.

## Why

Fixes #5050

When an in-flight tool invocation or generation in Agy CLI is interrupted via Escape, the CLI aborts execution and returns to its interactive prompt (`> ` with the `? for shortcuts` footer and `⌊ Interrupted · What should Antigravity CLI do instead?`). Because Agy does not emit its `stop` hook upon interruption, the session's activity state in Agent Orchestrator remained permanently stuck in `activity_state = 'active'` (`status = 'working'` with a blue dot).

Previously, `agy.Plugin` lacked an implementation of `ports.TerminalActivityDetector`, causing AO's background `activity.Observer` to skip terminal reconciliation for Agy sessions entirely.

Additionally, in the ACP conversation driver (`internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go`), `finishPrompt` emitted `ChatControllerReady` before acquiring the lock to clear `activeTurn`. Any prompt follow-up reacting immediately to controller readiness raced and failed with `ACP conversation already has a turn in flight`.

## How

- Implemented `DetectTerminalActivity(output string) (domain.ActivityState, bool)` in `internal/adapters/agent/agy/terminal_activity.go`:
  - Scans the candidate frame for active execution markers (`(esc to interrupt)`, `(ctrl+c to cancel)`, `thinking...`) and vetoes idle if any active chrome is present, regardless of whether it appears above or below the footer/prompt (excluding user transcript lines starting with `>`).
  - Requires structural adjacency between the `? for shortcuts` footer and the `>` composer prompt within 2 lines (allowing at most one blank cursor line) so stale transcript prompts separated by output do not satisfy the check.
  - Fails closed on incomplete, ambiguous, or foreign screen captures.
- Added compile-time interface assertion in `internal/adapters/agent/agy/agy.go`.
- Added unit tests in `internal/adapters/agent/agy/terminal_activity_test.go` including busy-screen and stale-prompt regressions.
- Fixed `finishPrompt` in `internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go` to clear `activeTurn` and settling state before emitting `TurnCompleted` and `ChatControllerReady`.

## Testing

- `go test -v ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/...` (PASS - 11/11 subtests)
- `go test -v ./internal/observe/activity/...` (PASS - 13/13 tests)
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... ./internal/observe/activity/...` (PASS)
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp` (PASS)
- `npm run lint` (PASS - 0 issues)
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` (PASS - 0 errors)

title: bug(updater): restored staged update leaves Restart & install waiting for native preparation that never starts
body:
## Bug

On macOS, after reopening AO, both Sidebar Restart to update and Settings / confirmation Restart & install can do nothing while the UI advertises a staged newer nightly.

Reported by the maintainer in AO chat, 2026-09-07, with screenshots. Installed: `0.12.13-nightly.202609070711`; saved and natively extracted candidate: `0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`. No restart or install was triggered during this investigation.

## Live evidence preserved before changing anything

- `~/.ao/staged-update.json` records candidate `0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`.
- Native ShipItState.plist points at an existing extracted app of that candidate version.
- ShipIt log: install request at 04:07:33; installation begins 04:23:03; abort at 04:24:24 because one target app instance is still running, `SQRLInstallerErrorDomain`, code `-9`, `App Still Running Error`.
- The current AO process started at 09:33:48, later than that native attempt. The evidence does not establish why the earlier process remained running.
- Installed bundle remains the 07:11 nightly. AO's native helper is not currently running.

Copies of staged metadata, native state/logs, process start information, a clone of the current native staging directory, and an isolated control-flow probe are preserved locally in `.ao/scratch/restart-noop-evidence/`. These paths are evidence locations, not public attachments. No cache was deleted and no real application was quit.

## Mechanism: saved readiness outlives process-local native readiness

1. `restoreStagedBuild` restores `stagedVersion` and `stagedAtMs` from JSON across process launches.
2. `hasStagedBuild` and same-version checks treat that as staged; the automatic check suppresses another download/handoff for the same candidate.
3. The shared install IPC path calls `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall(false, true)`.
4. In electron-updater 6.8.9, a newly constructed MacUpdater starts with `squirrelDownloadedUpdate = false`. Only a native `update-downloaded` event in that instance sets it true.
5. With that flag false and `autoInstallOnAppQuit = true`, `quitAndInstall` subscribes to native completion but does NOT initiate native checking. If no preparation is running, it waits indefinitely, with no progress/error shown to the user.

A saved JSON record and an extracted app on disk do not initialize the new process's native updater or its localhost handoff.

Confidence: high in this control-flow mechanism; no debugger was attached to the live process, so the individual live click's IPC execution and internal flag values were not directly observed.

## Reproduction evidence

An isolated VM evaluation of the published MacUpdater 6.8.9 source, with fake Electron and a minimal base updater, reproduces the no-op: fresh instance + autoInstallOnAppQuit=true + quitAndInstall => zero native checks and zero quits. Emitting native completion as a control triggers quit. This runs no real Electron application; it verifies the specific library branch, not an end-to-end installed-app reproduction.

A full regression should stage a candidate, restart the desktop process without completing installation, restore AO metadata, then request install. It must re-establish native preparation, show progress and reach native readiness before requesting quit; repeated clicks must not start overlapping native attempts or stack listeners.

## Fix direction and related work

Restore staged JSON as unconfirmed provenance. Re-establish an owned handoff for the remembered candidate before offering/executing installation; do not simply flip the library's internal readiness flag or call native quit against uninitialized state. Surface preparation progress and failure instead of silently accepting the install request.

[PR #5002](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5002) describes re-establishing remembered handoffs and native-ready install ownership; it is broader and still needs integration/review. This issue supplies a concrete live failure case for that work.

[#4254](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4254) concerns signature validation. No new signature rejection was observed here. The previously planned readiness work remains relevant even though [PR #4981](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4981), [PR #5032](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5032), and [PR #5021](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5021) have shipped.

title: fix(review): sanitize reviewer pane handle for dotted session ids
body:
Closes #6303

Related: #4479 — same reject-vs-sanitize class on the conpty/Windows side. The conpty path is intentionally left a validator (it enforces the `Handle.ID == SessionID` ownership invariant at probe/destroy), so #4479 needs id normalization at SessionID mint time rather than this fix; this PR only repairs the tmux-side reviewer path where the raw id reached the validator.

## Summary

Triggering a review for any worker of a project whose id contains a dot failed with `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED`:

```
launch reviewer: reviewer replace stale pane:
tmux runtime: invalid handle id "review-<dotted-id>"
```

The reviewer pane handle was a raw concatenation `"review-" + workerID` (`review/launcher.go`), and the tmux `handleID` validator (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`) **rejects** instead of sanitizing. Worker panes were unaffected because they go through `tmux.SessionName()`, which sanitizes (slug + short hash) — the same asymmetry #4479 documents on the conpty side. The supervised launch path (`agent-process supervise --session <handle>`) has the same rejection (`cli/agent_process.go` activity-id validation), so minting the handle sanitized fixes both consumers.

## Fix

- New `domain.RuntimeHandleName(id)` — the shared sanitizer (conforming id passes through unchanged; otherwise slug + 4-byte sha256 suffix), moved verbatim from the tmux runtime so tmux and the review launcher share one implementation.
- `reviewerHandleID()` routes through it. Conforming ids are unchanged, so existing handles keep working; dotted ids previously never produced a live handle, so there is no migration concern.
- The tmux runtime now delegates to the shared helper (its local copy is deleted); the trivial exported `SessionName` wrapper had no external callers and was removed.

## Tests

- `domain/session_name_test.go`: passthrough for conforming ids, dotted id sanitized to a runtime-safe deterministic name, distinct ids don't collapse.
- `review/launcher_test.go`: regression — `reviewerHandleID` of a dotted id is `review-` prefixed and dot-free, conforming id unchanged.

`go build ./...`, package tests (`domain`, `review`, `adapters/runtime/tmux`), `gofmt -l`, `go vet` all green.

## Live verification (macOS, self-built daemon)

Same project (dotted id, session ids `-34`…`-38`), before and after the fix landed — from the `review_run` table:

```
-- before
...|<project>-34|failed|launch reviewer: reviewer replace stale pane:
   tmux runtime: invalid handle id "review-<project>-34"|...

-- after (fixed daemon, 5 runs in one sweep)
...|<project>-34|complete|Approving. ...|...
...|<project>-35|running|...|...
...|<project>-37|complete|Verdict: approving.|...
...|<project>-36|complete|Approved ✅ — no changes requested.|...
...|<project>-38|complete|## Review: **Approved** ✅ ...|...
```

Reviewer panes now live on sanitized handles and run real reviewers:

```
$ tmux -L ao list-sessions | grep <project>
<project-slug>-33-<hash>: 1 windows ...
<project-slug>-38-<hash>: 1 windows ...

$ pgrep -fl review-
... ao pty-host review-<project-slug>-34-<hash> ... claude --permission-mode auto ...
```

`ao review trigger <project>-38` returns cleanly instead of the 500:

```
reused the existing review for <project>-38
```

title: feat: complete durable worker report delivery
body:
Code changes: +1865 -16
Tests: +1179 -2
Others: +1266 -0

## Summary

- Preserve the reviewed Worker Reports ingestion, validation, storage, restart recovery, and claim-token fencing foundation.
- Instruct project workers in their generated system prompt to persist checkpoints, input requests, stuck states, completion, and outputs with `ao report`.
- Deliver reports durably through Chat and supported TUI semantic boundaries, with a shared fixed one-hour ordinary fallback and a fixed five-minute first-done settlement window.
- Deliver needs-input immediately without interruption. Deliver stuck immediately with durable per-worker three-minute interruption throttling and repeated-report coalescing.
- Resolve the active project orchestrator at each attempt, never auto-spawn one, and recover delivery across daemon and orchestrator replacement.
- Acknowledge only after the target adapter accepts the semantic message. Reuse a durable batch identity so retries are idempotent and reports arriving after a lost response are not silently consumed.
- Piggyback pending reports onto a same-turn human Chat message with one wakeup.
- Expose an independent read-only project report projection for the separate Summary consumer. Summary does not claim or acknowledge delivery.
- Keep outputs independent from state, artifacts opaque, and report claims separate from lifecycle status.

## Runtime boundary

Chat delivery uses the existing semantic Chat send API. Supported TUI adapters wrap each delivery with a durable batch identity and acknowledge only after the native accepted-prompt hook reports that exact identity for the current runtime generation. A raw pane write is never accepted delivery. TUI adapters without that semantic acceptance capability reject submission so reports remain pending. Background consultation remains deferred.

## Verification

title: bug(daemon): workspace projects can never attribute a PR — observer requires /root, ClaimPR ignores WorkspaceRepos
body:
## Bug

A worker session in a `workspace` project can never get a pull request attached to it, by **either** available mechanism:

- the SCM observer cannot match a workspace session's branch shape, and
- `ao session claim-pr` — the documented fallback, and the remediation #4984 relies on — rejects every child-repo PR with `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`.

The PR never appears in the session sidebar and there is no supported way to attach it. `workspace` is a first-class project kind (`domain/project.go:9`, in the storage `CHECK` constraint, backend support closed in #2222), so this is an unhandled kind rather than an unsupported configuration.

**Source:** live report from a worker session that opened two PRs across two child repos of a workspace project
**Date:** 2026-09-07
**Analyzed against:** `4f5c0c899` (`origin/main`)
**Installed:** desktop 0.12.12; daemon binary written 2026-09-06 18:34 UTC; daemon **process** restarted 2026-09-07 10:43 UTC
**Confidence:** High for both root causes (predicates read from source, reproduced against durable SQLite state). Medium for the regression attribution in Root cause 2, which is inferred from behaviour across a dated daemon restart rather than from a recorded version string.

> Org and repository names below are replaced with placeholders (`<org>`, `child-a`, `child-b`) and session ids shortened to `ws-283` / `ws-275`. Happy to share the real identifiers privately — nothing else about the evidence is altered.

## Reproduction

1. Register a workspace project (`kind: workspace`) with child repositories, each with its own GitHub origin. The parent root repo need not have a remote.
2. `ao spawn` a worker. `workspaceProjectBranch` (`adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:1409`) names the session branch `ao/<id>`, disambiguating collisions as `ao/<id>-2`, `-3`, … — **never** `<namespace>/root`.
3. In a child repo, create a PR branch. The child form the worker prompt instructs (`<session-branch>/<topic>`) is impossible here: `refs/heads/ao/<id>-2` exists as a ref, so Git refuses `refs/heads/ao/<id>-2/<topic>`:
   ```
   fatal: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/ao/ws-283-2/topic':
   'refs/heads/ao/ws-283-2' exists; cannot create ...
   ```
   The only available shape is a hyphen sibling: `ao/<id>-2-<topic>`.
4. Open the PR and wait past the observer's poll interval → never attributed.
5. `ao session claim-pr <pr-url>` → `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`.
6. Follow the advice in that error, `ao project set-config <id> --canonical-repo-url <https-url>` → rejected with `canonicalRepoURL: project must have a valid checkout origin repository`.

Durable state after step 4, with a single_repo project on the same daemon for contrast:

```text
session    sessions.branch      PR head branch                 attributed?
ws-283     ao/ws-283-2          ao/ws-283-2-body-887           no
emuil-43   ao/emuil-43/root     ao/emuil-43/triple-ready       yes, within seconds
```

## Root cause 1 — the observer can never match a workspace session's branch

`observe/scm/observer.go:1251` widens attribution to sibling branches only for a `/root` leaf:

```go
func sessionBranchPrefixes(branch string) []string {
	prefixes := []string{branch}
	if namespace, ok := strings.CutSuffix(branch, "/root"); ok && namespace != "" {
		prefixes = append(prefixes, namespace)
	}
	return prefixes
}
```

`matchSession` (`:1227`) then accepts only an exact match or `strings.HasPrefix(sourceBranch, prefix+"/")`. For a workspace session:

```text
sessions.branch : ao/ws-283-2
PR head         : ao/ws-283-2-body-887
```

Not equal, and not prefixed by `ao/ws-283-2/` — the next character is `-`. Both arms fail, deterministically, for every PR the session opens.

The comment above `matchSession` states the intent: *"The default worker branch is a leaf named `<namespace>/root`; for that shape the session also owns sibling branches under `<namespace>/...` so Git can create child PR branches without colliding with the root ref."* Workspace projects never get that leaf, so they get neither the namespace widening nor the ability to use the child form that would satisfy the predicate.

**Relationship to #4984.** Same predicate, different and stricter trigger. #4984 describes a session that *leaves* `/root` and loses its **second** PR; the workspace case never has `/root` at all and loses **every** PR including the first. #4984's fix as scoped (sibling attribution for topic branches) would incidentally cover this half. Naming workspace session branches `<namespace>/root` would too.

## Root cause 2 — `ClaimPR` is not workspace-aware

`service/session/claim_pr.go:62`:

```go
if err := requireSameRepo(prURL, project.RepoOriginURL); err != nil {
    if project.Config.CanonicalRepoURL == "" || requireSameRepo(prURL, project.Config.CanonicalRepoURL) != nil {
        return ClaimPRResult{}, err
    }
}
```

and `:389`:

```go
func requireSameRepo(prURL, repoOrigin string) error {
	if strings.TrimSpace(repoOrigin) == "" {
		return ErrProjectMismatch
	}
```

`project.RepoOriginURL` is the parent root's origin. A workspace project's child remotes live in `WorkspaceRepos` — which the observer already reads (`observer.go:843,846`, via `ListWorkspaceRepos`) and `ClaimPR` never does. `claim_pr.go` contains zero references to `ProjectKindWorkspace` or `WorkspaceRepos`, though it does explicitly special-case another kind at `:86`:

```go
if project.Kind.WithDefault() == domain.ProjectKindScratch {
    return ClaimPRResult{}, ErrSessionNotClaimable
}
```

**This is not limited to a remote-less root.** `requireSameRepo` compares the PR's owner/repo against the root origin, so a workspace rooted at `<org>/parent` still rejects a PR on `<org>/child-a` — different repository. No workspace project can claim a child-repo PR under any configuration. An empty root origin merely fails one line earlier.

**The prescribed escape is a closed loop.** The error tells the user to set `canonicalRepoURL`; `domain/repository_identity.go:83` then refuses one:

```go
checkout, err := ParseRepositoryIdentity(origin)
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("canonicalRepoURL: project must have a valid checkout origin repository")
}
```

— requiring exactly the valid single origin a workspace project does not have. It is also a single URL where a workspace has N children, so it could bless at most one repo even if accepted.

**Regression window.** `requireSameRepo` landed in `d06b2162d` (2026-09-05 12:47 UTC, #4929). The same project, with the same hyphen-sibling branch shape, was attaching PRs the day before:

```text
2026-09-06 18:34 UTC   new daemon binary written to disk
2026-09-06 22:10 UTC   ws-275 attaches child-a PR   (old daemon process still running)
2026-09-07 09:17 UTC   ws-275 attaches child-a PR   (old daemon process still running)
2026-09-07 10:43 UTC   daemon process restarted onto the new binary
2026-09-07 17:12 UTC   ws-283 opens two PRs -> neither attaches, both claims refused
```

Those earlier attachments cannot have come from the observer: the `/root` narrowing is `9ae9f0888` (2026-06-18), long predating them, and `ao/ws-275-warn-on-host` against `sessions.branch = ao/ws-275` fails `matchSession` identically. They were claims. The restart is what removed the fallback that had been quietly carrying this project kind — which is why the breakage looks sudden despite Root cause 1 being three months old.

## Existing coverage gap

`ClaimPR` has a dedicated test for the one kind it does handle — `TestClaimPRRejectsScratchProject` (`service/session/service_test.go:3754`) — and no workspace equivalent. The three `ProjectKindWorkspace` fixtures in that file (`:1849`, `:1928`, `:1983`) are spawn/branch-resolution tests, all well above the `ClaimPR` block. `claim_upstream_test.go` covers the fork-backed single_repo case only.

A regression test asserting that a workspace project can claim a PR on any repo in `ListWorkspaceRepos` would have caught Root cause 2 when `d06b2162d` landed.

## Suggested fix

1. **`ClaimPR`:** for `ProjectKindWorkspace`, validate the PR repo against `ListWorkspaceRepos` (match any child origin) in addition to `RepoOriginURL`, mirroring `workspaceSCMSessionRepos`.
2. **Branch shape:** either have `workspaceProjectBranch` produce `<namespace>/root` (matching `single_repo`), or widen `sessionBranchPrefixes` past the `/root` special case — see #4984.
3. **Error text:** `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH` should not direct users to `--canonical-repo-url` for a project kind whose validator rejects it. Either accept it for workspace projects or say why it does not apply.

Items 1 and 2 are independent; either alone leaves the kind half-broken.

Workspace cleanup can delete a worktree still used by a live session (data loss)
body:
## Problem

`Manager.Cleanup` reclaims the workspaces of terminated sessions. It only checks whether the **session** is terminated. It never checks whether the **workspace path** is still used by another, live session.

When two sessions share one persistent worktree, terminating one of them can destroy the workspace out from under the other. Files and uncommitted work in that worktree are lost.

## Where

- `cleanupOne` passes a workspace to `workspace.Destroy` based on `rec.IsTerminated` alone.
- `ErrWorkspaceDirty` only guards uncommitted changes. It does not protect a worktree that another live session is actively using.

## Repro shape

1. Point two sessions at the same persistent worktree.
2. Terminate one session.
3. Cleanup reaps the shared workspace while the second session is still running.

## Status

Diagnosed by @polymath-orchestrator in PR #2487 (now closed as stale after 62 days of silence, branch remains open to reopen). The guard this PR adds is still missing on main, so the bug is live.

Maintainers: the fix in #2487 is small and is the only known patch for this. Worth picking up or re-triaging.

Credit to @polymath-orchestrator for the diagnosis.

body:
## Report: existing repository shown as “Needs git init”

During a real-project desktop test on 2026-09-08, AO's **Import an existing project** flow (single Git repository mode) displayed `Needs git init` for an existing local repository. A read-only `git -C <selected-folder> rev-parse --verify HEAD` succeeded for the same folder.

## Environment

Native Electron development app associated with [PR #4830](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4830), macOS, isolated daemon/data on port 3002, real project folder. Checkout HEAD `8e808a00cf001a9ddfb20c687426e738a261fbbb` with pre-existing uncommitted changes; not verified against a released build.

## Steps observed

1. Choose **Import an existing project** from the home page.
2. Select a real existing repository through the native folder picker.
3. The dialog explicitly says `Import a single Git repository as one project` and displays the selected folder with `Needs git init`.
4. Verify `.git` exists and `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` succeeds. The notice remained on a subsequent observation.

The user did not proceed with Git initialization; no source-project files were changed.

## Expected

Recognize the existing repository. If another prerequisite is missing (such as origin/default-branch configuration), report that prerequisite instead of suggesting Git initialization. While detection is pending, show a pending state rather than a definitive missing-Git diagnosis.

## Confidence and limits

Medium confidence in the displayed mismatch; low confidence in its cause. Later computer-control accessibility state and screenshots diverged, so this needs confirmation with a fresh pinned build and captured directory-probe response before changing repository detection. Do not treat the later dialog-control problems as separately confirmed AO bugs.

Inspect single-project probe results, loading/error handling and the mapping to `Needs git init` in `CreateProjectFlow.tsx`.

Related but not an exact duplicate: [#4959](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4959) concerns selecting **workspace** mode for a single-repository folder. This observation was explicitly in **single-project** mode. [#4679](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4679) covers remote-less repositories; a missing remote has not been established as this report's cause.

Priority: medium. No fix or reliable cross-project reproduction is claimed yet.

title: bug(codex): Windows ancestor ACL validation rejects valid Codex home
body:
## Bug

On Windows, Codex account bootstrap can fail before any Codex process is launched because the private-directory admission check rejects an otherwise usable Codex home ancestor.

The observed path is:

-  ootstrapInner calls cleanupPendingCredentialHomes before econcileGlobal.
- cleanupPendingCredentialHomes calls ^[nsurePrivateDirectory.
- ^[nsurePrivateDirectory calls alidateCodexDirectoryAncestors before creating or launching the account app-server.
- The validator can reject the volume root (C:\\) based on its owner/ACL checks, producing ^Gccount_storage_unsafe and the public CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE error.

This is a distinct pre-launch failure mode from account app-server environment handoff issues.

## Impact

Users receive the generic account-management error even though Codex itself is installed and authenticated. No Codex process starts, so PATH propagation fixes cannot affect this path.

## Relationship

This is related to #4989 but should be tracked separately because #4989 may include multiple Windows failure modes. Independent reproduction and trace: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4989#issuecomment-5576910008

## Expected

Valid Windows installations should not be rejected solely because an ancestor such as C:\\ has system-managed ownership or non-inherit-only ACL entries. If the directory cannot be safely accepted, the returned diagnostic should expose the specific ancestor and reason.

title: bug(board): idle session card spins a loader next to a green "Mergeable" label
body:
## Bug

A worker session card on the Kanban board renders an animated loader ring next to its status label even though the agent is idle and the label itself reads a settled **Mergeable**. The card sits in the **Ready** lane, so nothing about it is in progress, yet the ring spins continuously at one revolution per second for as long as the card is mounted.

The reporter read the spinner as "this session is Working", which is exactly what it looks like.

**Reported by:** the maintainer, in the AO desktop app (first reported 2026-09-06, still reproducing 2026-09-08)
**Analyzed against:** `ddf1e54f18f9e27dacbfa0d1d90ce37a1c37228e` (origin/main)
**Environment:** AO desktop app, bundled daemon `ao version` = `dev`, daemon healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001` (`readyz: ready`); macOS 14.6 (23G80) arm64
**Confidence:** High — exact lines traced, mechanism explained, reproduced by a deterministic unit test (below)
**Priority:** medium — the board's primary status signal is misleading; workaround is to open the session and read the topbar activity pill

### Screenshots

First report (2026-09-06):

![board card 2026-09-06](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-board-mergeable-spinner/.issue-assets/board-mergeable-spinner/card-2026-09-06.png)

Still present (2026-09-08), same session, still idle:

![board card 2026-09-08](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-board-mergeable-spinner/.issue-assets/board-mergeable-spinner/card-2026-09-08.png)

## Reproduction

Deterministic unit reproduction (no live session needed) — add to `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx`:

```ts
boardSession({
  id: "s-mergeable",
  title: "mergeable-card-task",
  status: "review_pending",
  displayStatus: "Mergeable",
  kanbanColumn: "ready",
  activity: { state: "idle", lastActivityAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" },
})
// expect(within(card).getByTestId("session-status").querySelector(".animate-spin")).toBeNull();
```

Fails on `ddf1e54f`:

```
AssertionError: expected SVGSVGElement{ …(2), …(2) } to be null
+ Received:
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-loader-circle mr-1 size-icon-2xs animate-spin" ...>
  <path d="M21 12a9 9 0 1 1-6.219-8.56" />
</svg>
```

Live reproduction, for reference — a session with several open PRs where at least one is not yet mergeable:

1. Session `analyze Coder PR` has PRs #4624 (`review_required`, `conflicting`), #4787 and #4796 (both `mergeable`), #4434 (merged).
2. `GET /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-211` returns `activity.state: idle`, `status: review_pending`, `scmStatus: review_pending`, `kanbanColumn: ready`, `displayStatus: Mergeable`.
3. The board card shows the Ready lane, a green `Mergeable` label, and a spinning ring.

## Root Cause

`packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.tsx:245-251`:

```ts
const showStatusLoader =
    !needsAttention &&
    session.displayStatus !== "Needs human review" &&
    (session.status === "working" ||
        session.status === "review_pending" ||
        session.displayStatus === "Fixing CI failures" ||
        session.displayStatus === "Addressing comments" ||
        session.displayStatus === "Reviewing");
```

rendered at `SessionsBoardView.tsx:337`:

```tsx
{showStatusLoader ? <LoaderCircleIcon aria-hidden="true" className="mr-1 size-icon-2xs animate-spin" /> : null}
```

Two independent problems meet here:

1. **The loader and the label read different daemon fields.** The label comes from `displayStatus` (`SessionsBoardView.tsx:242`), which the daemon derives from the session's **best** PR — `DeriveKanbanPresentation` picks the highest-ranked column, `ready` first (`backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go:254-266`, `kanbanPriority` at `:167-178`). The loader comes from `status`, which the daemon derives from the session's **worst** open PR (`backend/pkg/contract/status.go:192-215` plus the severity table at `:226-244`). For the session above, #4624 is `review_required` + `conflicting` and yields `review_pending` (severity 3), beating the two mergeable PRs (severity 6). So one card renders the best PR as text and the worst PR as an icon.

2. **The loader never consults agent activity.** `showStatusLoader` has no `session.activity` term at all, so an idle agent cannot switch it off. The card reads activity in only two places, neither reachable here: `boardSessionNeedsAttention` (`:360-373`, which only looks at `activity.state === "blocked"` when `displayStatus` is undefined) and `statusPresentation` (agent-switch, absent). The animation itself is unconditional CSS — `.animate-spin{animation:var(--animate-spin)}` with `--animate-spin: spin 1s linear infinite` — so it has no terminating state.

`review_pending` is also the odd member of that predicate's set. Every other member describes something actively turning (`working` = the agent is running a turn; `Fixing CI failures` / `Addressing comments` / `Reviewing` = AO-driven loops). `review_pending` is a *waiting* state: the app's own taxonomy maps it to the `pending` attention zone, not `working` (`packages/product-ui/src/session-presentation.ts`, `attentionZone`), its own label reads "Review pending", and at the daemon it comes from `prPipelineStatus`'s `case pr.Review == ReviewRequired` (`backend/pkg/contract/status.go:257`) — GitHub reporting that a required human review has not happened.

Introduced in `8162e8da3` (2026-08-26, "feat(board): add active status loaders"), keyed on `session.status` from the start. The only existing test for the loader (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx:501-523`) exercises `status: "working"` with `activity: active` — the genuinely busy case — so the `review_pending` arm shipped untested.

## Fix

Make the loader agree with the label the card actually renders, without touching the multi-PR aggregation in the daemon (that aggregation is deliberate and out of scope here):

- Spin when the agent is genuinely working (`status === "working"`).
- Otherwise spin only when the **rendered `displayStatus`** is itself an in-progress phrase — `Review pending`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Addressing comments`, `Reviewing`.
- Fall back to the old `status === "review_pending"` check only when the daemon sent no `displayStatus` (older daemon against a newer client).

This keeps `Review pending` cards spinning and stops `Mergeable`, `Approved` and `Merged` cards from spinning, which is exactly the behaviour requested in #4725.

## Impact

- Every multi-PR session whose PRs disagree shows a permanent spinner on a settled card.
- The board's most prominent liveness cue is decoupled from agent activity, so users cannot tell from the board whether an agent is running.
- Cosmetic only — no data loss, no incorrect merges.

## Related

- [#4725](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4725) — open design task that already specifies "Mergable should not show a loader / Review pending should show loader / Go over where we show loader". This issue is the concrete bug and evidence behind the first two bullets.
- [#2944](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2944) — closed: sidebar dot + kanban badge locked to PR status, agent working/idle invisible once a PR exists. Same family (PR state masking agent state) on different surfaces, not a duplicate.
- [#2345](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2345) — closed: topbar pill showed a breathing "Working" for `pr_open`/`draft`. Same class of defect on the topbar; this one is the board loader.

title: fix(board): stop spinning a loader on settled session cards
body:
Fixes #5081

## Summary

A board card read its status **label** from `displayStatus` but its **loader** from `status`. The daemon derives those two from opposite ends of a session's PR set — `displayStatus` from the session's best PR (`contract/kanban.go`, `kanbanPriority`, `ready` first), `status` from its worst open PR (`contract/status.go`, `aggregatePRStatus` + severity table). A session with one mergeable PR and one still awaiting review therefore rendered a green **Mergeable** label next to a loader that spun forever. The predicate contained no `session.activity` term, so an idle agent could not switch it off, and `animate-spin` is `spin 1s linear infinite` with no terminating state.

The fix keys the loader off the label the card actually renders:

- keep the loader while the agent is genuinely working (`status === "working"`);
- otherwise show it only when the rendered `displayStatus` is itself an in-progress phrase — `Review pending`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Addressing comments`, `Reviewing`;
- fall back to the old `status === "review_pending"` check only when the daemon sent no `displayStatus`, so an older daemon against a newer client is unaffected.

`Review pending` keeps its loader and `Mergeable` loses it, which is exactly what #4725 specifies ("Mergable should not show a loader / Review pending should show loader").

**The daemon's multi-PR aggregation is deliberate and is unchanged** — this is a presentation-only fix in `packages/product-ui`.

## Test

Three new cases in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx`, covering both directions:

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| idle agent, `status: review_pending`, `displayStatus: "Mergeable"`, `ready` lane | **no** loader (the reported bug) |
| idle agent, `status: review_pending`, `displayStatus: "Review pending"` | loader present (#4725 intent) |
| active agent, `status: working`, `displayStatus: "Mergeable"` | loader present (truly-active still covered) |

The first case fails on `ddf1e54f` with `expected SVGSVGElement … to be null` (the `lucide-loader-circle animate-spin` node) and passes here. The pre-existing `status: "working"` + `activity: active` test is untouched and still passes.

Verification run locally on node 24 (matching `.github/workflows/frontend.yml`):

```
npm --prefix packages/product-ui run typecheck   # clean
npm --prefix packages/product-ui test            # 10 files, 124 tests passed
npm --prefix packages/product-ui run build       # built
npm --prefix frontend run typecheck              # clean
cd frontend && npx vitest run src/renderer       # 197 files, 2828 passed, 6 skipped
```

### Environment limitation, proven not a regression

The full `frontend` suite in this checkout also reports 17 failures across 8 files — all under `src/landing/**` and `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`. None of them import the board or `product-ui`. Two independent checks confirm they are pre-existing environment gaps, not regressions from this change:

1. **Baseline on pristine `origin/main`.** Reverting this PR's two files and re-running *only those 8 files* reproduces the identical 8 files / 17 tests failing. Failure mode is `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and missing native deps.
2. **CI is green on this PR.** The `test` job runs the same full `npx vitest run`, but only after `npm ci --prefix src/landing` and `npm run browser-runtime:prepare` — two setup steps this local checkout never performed. It passed in 5m29s, alongside `renderer-smoke` (2m50s) and `scan` (17s).

So the local failures are missing landing sub-app and browser-runtime dependencies here, and no unrelated code was touched to make anything pass.

title: feat(browser): explicit `ao preview` / `ao browser open` should reveal the Browser panel for the session you are viewing
body:
## Summary

An explicit `ao preview <target>` or `ao browser open <url>` from the session the user is currently viewing succeeds, but the Browser panel is **not** revealed — the inspector only badges the Browser tab as unseen. The user has to notice the badge and click the tab to see the thing they just asked for.

This is **current, intentional behavior**, not an accidental regression. [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) ("non-disruptive preview reveal") deliberately replaced the force-reveal with a badge, and `CLAUDE.md` documents it. This issue asks to narrow that rule, not to revert it.

**Reported by:** @itrytoohard (maintainer), relayed via an AO worker session
**Analyzed against:** `ddf1e54f1`
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced below.

## Current behavior

`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx`

- The preview-target effect (around `SessionView.tsx:1330`) fires when `previewUrl`/`previewRevision` changes. If the Browser panel is already visible it clears the badge; otherwise it calls `setBrowserUnseen(sessionId, true)` and returns. The `setInspectorViewForSession(sessionId, "browser")` + `setInspectorOpenForSession(sessionId, true)` pair was removed by [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) (commit `30a7c20f6`).
- The agent-activity effect (around `SessionView.tsx:1369`) badges on *any* `browserView.agentBrowserActive`, so `ao browser open` is treated identically to a passive `snapshot`, `click`, or `errors` call — badge only, never reveal.

Net effect: the two commands whose entire purpose is "show me this page" are the ones that don't show it.

## Why [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) was right, and what it over-corrected

[PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146)'s rationale — quoted from its own code comment — is that a new preview target used to "force-switch the inspector to the Browser tab and pop it open, even if the user was looking at something else entirely (Reviews, a different session's Files tab, mid-typing in chat)."

The genuinely disruptive case there is a **background** session grabbing the foreground. That is worth preventing and must stay prevented. But the fix was applied to *all* preview targets, including one the user is staring at right now, having just asked for it. Since `SessionView` is mounted only for the routed session (`routes/_shell.projects.$projectId_.sessions.$sessionId.tsx`), "the session whose `SessionView` is mounted" is already exactly "the session the user is viewing" — the disruptive cross-session case and the wanted same-session case are separable with information the renderer already has.

## Requested behavior

| Trigger | Session being viewed | Other session |
|---|---|---|
| `ao preview <target>` (new preview target) | **Reveal** Browser panel | Badge only (unchanged) |
| `ao browser open <url>`, `ao browser tab new` | **Reveal** Browser panel | Badge only (unchanged) |
| `ao browser snapshot` / `click` / `fill` / `act` / `errors` / … | Badge only (unchanged) | Badge only (unchanged) |
| No browser content / terminated session | No badge (unchanged) | No badge (unchanged) |

Revealing means: open the inspector and switch it to the Browser tab for that session. It does **not** mean raising the OS window, changing the routed session, or changing projects — a background worker must never pull the user's navigation to itself.

## Intent contract — already present, no API change needed

The renderer can already tell explicit-open from passive inspection:

- `BrowserAgentActivityState` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:110`) already carries `action` and `phase`, pushed on `browser:agentActivity` and surfaced by `useBrowserView` as `agentBrowserActivity`.
- The action strings come straight from the CLI: `ao browser open` sends `"open"` (`backend/internal/cli/browser.go:91`) and `ao browser tab new` sends `"tab-new"`; every passive command sends its own distinct verb.
- `previewRevision` only changes when someone runs `ao preview`, so a preview-key change is inherently explicit.

So this needs no daemon route, no OpenAPI change, and no contract regeneration — it is a renderer-side policy change over signals the main process already emits.

## Acceptance criteria

1. From the session on screen, `ao preview README.md` opens the inspector on the Browser tab showing the rendered file, with no unseen badge left behind.
2. From the session on screen, `ao browser open http://localhost:5173` does the same.
3. A `ao preview` / `ao browser open` in a **different** session badges that session and does not change what the user is looking at.
4. `ao browser snapshot` / `click` / `fill` / `errors` on the viewed session while the Browser tab is hidden still only badges — no reveal.
5. Revealing never steals OS window focus and never changes the routed session or project.
6. A terminated session's stale `previewUrl` still reveals nothing (existing `hasBrowserContent` guard).

## Reproduction

1. Open a session in the desktop app and park the inspector on Summary (or Reviews).
2. From that session's worker shell, run `ao preview README.md`.
3. Observed: the command reports success; the Browser tab shows an unseen dot; the panel stays on Summary.
4. Expected: the inspector opens on Browser with the rendered README.
5. Repeat with `ao browser open http://localhost:5173` — same observed result.

## Related

- [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) — introduced the current badge-only behavior (the behavior this issue narrows).
- [PR #3359](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3359) — the earlier "open first browser content automatically and badge background activity" split this builds on.
- [#2809](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2809) — agents opening the OS browser instead of the AO in-app preview; same "the preview must actually be seen" goal.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md` currently instructs agents that `ao preview` "does not steal focus or force the Browser tab open" and to tell the user to check the Browser tab. That guidance needs updating alongside the behavior change.

title: fix: serialize mobile bridge state transitions
body:
## What

Serialize Connect Mobile state changes and synchronize the status error snapshot.

## Why

Concurrent Enable/Disable calls could overlap listener operations and overwrite each other's saved settings. Status polling also read `serveErr` while secure-pairing changes wrote it, producing a Go data race.

## How

Use one transition mutex for mutators and short locks for status/connector snapshots, keeping status polling responsive during slow connector work. Share post-start connector setup and restore the previous authentication hash if boot startup fails. Active LAN connection shutdown is a separate follow-up.

## Testing

- Reproduced the data race, overlapping Enable/Disable, and failed-start hash drift against the original implementation.
- Backend: HTTP race regressions; full `go test ./...` and `go test -race -timeout=15m ./...`; `go build ./...`; `go vet ./...`; formatting; golangci-lint v2.12.2.
- Integration: Linux `go test -tags e2e -v ./internal/cli/...`; fresh-install Docker check; `npm ci` and `npm run api` with Node 24, with no generated drift.
- Secret scan: CI-pinned gitleaks v7.4.0 scanned the single PR commit with no leaks.
- Local checks use Go 1.26.5 and an explicit `/bin/sh` for shell-sensitive tests. All nine GitHub CI jobs passed, including native Windows/macOS checks.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Regression tests added for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass

title: fix(cli): use canonical executable in managed login shells
body:
## What

Use the daemon-owned `AO_CLI` executable reference for managed tool commands and Claude hooks, so nested login shells cannot redirect them to an old AO installation.

## Why

A login shell can prepend an incompatible `ao` after the daemon pins PATH. The reproduced Codex worker selected a June 27 CLI without `browser`, despite the current desktop supporting that command.

Related to [#3562](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3562) and its [latest reproduction](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3562#issuecomment-5580034598). This addresses that manifestation without closing every accumulated acceptance item.

## How

- Export protected `AO_CLI` for worker/orchestrator TUI and Chat launches, reviewers, and session shell terminals. Preserve PATH pinning as a convenience; use the explicit reference in managed prompts and the CLI skill, with POSIX and PowerShell syntax.
- Migrate Claude hooks to the quoted reference, preserving user hooks/settings and Claude/Continue switching. Keep legacy managed hooks detectable and removable. Codex hooks already use an absolute executable.
- Correct doctor guidance: login shells can override the session PATH pin. No user shell configuration or installation is modified.

Intentional follow-ups: existing agents need a new launch/restore to receive the reference; stable CLI staging across Linux AppImage mount replacement, desktop startup/update reconciliation of legacy launchers, explicit packaging-time version stamping, and other harness-specific hook formats remain separate work. Inspector-tab selection and existing tmux environment transport are unchanged. No live authenticated Claude/Codex session was started for validation.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...`
- `cd backend && go test -race -timeout=15m ./...` — passed with AO worker environment variables removed from the test runner.
- golangci-lint v2.12.2 — zero findings with a fresh lint cache.
- `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...` — native macOS CLI E2E passed.
- `npm run api` plus generated-file diff check — no drift.
- Linux fresh-install Docker build and smoke test — passed.
- Real nested zsh and tmux create/restart regression tests, hook callback/migration tests, launch/restore propagation tests.
- Live login-shell smoke: bare `ao` still resolved to the legacy launcher while `"$AO_CLI" browser --help` successfully executed the newly built CLI.
- Windows test cross-compilation passed. PowerShell/Git Bash execution is covered by the Windows CI job; not run natively on this macOS host.

## Acceptance handoff for #3562

Verified in this PR:

- [x] Protect daemon-derived `AO_CLI` from configured overrides and propagate it through worker/orchestrator TUI and Chat launches/restores, reviewer launches/restores, and session shell terminals.
- [x] Teach managed prompts and the bundled CLI guide to invoke the explicit executable using POSIX or PowerShell syntax; demonstrate canonical execution after nested login-shell PATH changes, including tmux create/restart and Windows PowerShell/Git Bash tests.
- [x] Route Claude callbacks through the quoted canonical reference and fail closed when it is missing; preserve user hooks/settings and detect/remove legacy managed hooks.
- [x] Preserve Claude/Continue switching and legacy-hook cleanup with regression coverage. This does not claim migration of every Continue callback format.
- [x] Correct only the misleading doctor guidance about PATH pinning; existing doctor checks and the full CLI suite pass. No version-identity implementation is included.

Remaining acceptance work; keep #3562 open:

- [ ] Reconcile legacy launchers at desktop startup/update without overwriting user shell configuration or removing unrelated installations; verify conflicting-install and upgrade cases.
- [ ] Stage a stable canonical CLI for Linux AppImage upgrades and verify that commands survive disappearance/replacement of the old mount.
- [ ] Audit and test other harness-specific hook formats before claiming canonical invocation for all managed callbacks. Codex hooks already use an absolute executable; authenticated live Codex/Claude runs were not performed here.
- [ ] Define and verify explicit packaging-time version identity; do not infer a release identity from an unrelated enclosing Git repository.
- [ ] Validate rollout to existing sessions through relaunch/restore; already-running sessions do not receive the new environment retroactively.

The tmux environment-in-argv behavior predates this PR. Its transport and associated security properties are unchanged; this PR neither introduces that transport nor satisfies the historical environment-secrecy acceptance item. Any transport hardening requires separate work. Inspector Summary selection remains intentionally out of scope.

Validation limits and resolved failures: the initial Windows test harness had PowerShell argument quoting and multi-command identity assertion errors; both were corrected and the native Windows rerun passed. Intermediate prompt-budget/legacy-hook assertions were corrected before the final full race-suite pass. A fresh pinned lint cache avoided stale paths from another worktree; final lint reports zero findings. Windows execution was verified in CI, not on the local macOS host. All ten current CI checks pass on rebased head d296e63e8.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior
- [x] All ten remote CI checks pass on rebased head d296e63e8, including the installed Windows Claude callback fixture

## Review 5173133532 follow-up

Rebased onto main and addressed in 3c67314d6: canonical reviewer submit pipeline, explicit Claude shell selection (PowerShell on Windows, bash on POSIX), combined reviewer diagnostics with daemon logging, and corrected hookBinaryName documentation. See thread replies for tests and the official Claude shell contract. The added Windows fixture runs the installed callback, not an authenticated Claude session; old Claude versions lacking the documented shell field remain unvalidated. Existing adapter AreInstalled/Uninstall coverage intentionally preserves the adapter contract; this PR does not introduce new production callers.
