title: feat(browser): reveal the Browser panel for explicit preview/open commands
body:
Fixes #5083

## Summary

`ao preview` and `ao browser open` succeeded but only badged the Browser tab as unseen, so the two commands whose entire purpose is "show the user this page" were the ones that didn't show it — the user had to notice a dot and click the tab.

[PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) made every preview badge-only, deliberately, to stop a preview grabbing the foreground while the user was looking at something else. **This narrows that rule rather than reverting it.** The disruptive case #4146 was protecting against is a *background* session pulling focus; that protection now comes from `SessionView` being mounted only for the routed session, not from refusing to reveal at all.

- A new `ao preview` target reveals Browser for the session on screen.
- `ao browser open` / `ao browser tab new` reveal too — they are the agent-side equivalents of the same explicit request.
- Every passive agent verb (`snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `act`, `errors`, …) keeps badge-only treatment, as does any preview/open in another session.
- Revealing opens the inspector on Browser and nothing else: no OS window focus, no change to the routed session or project.

The reveal is deduped on `commandId` so a command's `finished` push cannot reopen a panel the user closed mid-command.

## Intent contract — no API change

Explicit-vs-passive was already distinguishable from the existing API, so nothing crosses the daemon boundary and no contracts were regenerated:

- `BrowserAgentActivityState` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`) already ships `action` + `commandId` on `browser:agentActivity`, surfaced by `useBrowserView` as `agentBrowserActivity`.
- The action strings come straight from the CLI — `ao browser open` sends `"open"` (`backend/internal/cli/browser.go:91`), `ao browser tab new` sends `"tab-new"`, every passive command sends its own verb.
- `previewRevision` only changes when someone runs `ao preview`, so a preview-key change is inherently explicit.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `vitest run SessionView.test.tsx BrowserPanel.test.tsx useBrowserView.test.tsx SessionInspector.test.tsx` — 346/346 passing. Three tests that asserted the old badge-only preview behavior were rewritten for the new rule; the `ao preview clear` test keeps its real subject (clearing neither reveals nor badges) with updated surrounding assertions. New coverage: reveal on `open`/`tab-new`, badge-only on `snapshot`/`click`/`fill`/`errors`, no re-reveal on the `finished` push, no reveal on a terminated session.
- [x] **Verified in the real Electron app** (isolated dev profile, driven over CDP; native `WebContentsView` target URLs read as ground truth):
  - Parked on Summary → `ao preview <url>` → Browser tab becomes selected.
  - Parked on Summary → `ao browser open http://127.0.0.1:3007/healthz` → Browser tab selected **and** the native view's target URL is that URL.
  - Parked on Summary → `ao browser snapshot` → stays on Summary, Browser shows the unseen badge.
  - Viewing session B, ran `ao browser open` **and** `ao preview` against background session A → route and tab both unchanged.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md`'s agent guidance said `ao preview` "does not steal focus or force the Browser tab open"; updated to describe the explicit-vs-passive split.

## Known limitations

- Reveal is scoped to the routed session because only that `SessionView` is mounted. If a future change keeps multiple `SessionView`s alive at once, the cross-session guard would need to become an explicit check rather than an emergent property — called out in the comment at the preview effect.
- Unrelated pre-existing behavior seen while testing: on an exited fake-harness session the daemon clears `previewUrl` shortly after `ao preview` sets it (bumping `previewRevision` with an empty URL). That is upstream of this change and left alone.

title: fix: close active LAN connections when mobile access stops
body:
## What

Disabling Connect Mobile now closes active LAN streams and WebSockets before reporting the listener stopped.

## Why

A shutdown timeout could leave HTTP clients connected, and Go's HTTP shutdown does not close hijacked WebSockets. Disable also returned early on a shutdown error without saving the disabled preference, so a stopped bridge could return on the next daemon boot.

## How

Give each listener its own cancellation context and connection registry. Serialize Start/Stop, force-close remaining connections after the grace period, and retain shutdown errors while completing disabled-state persistence. The connection wrapper preserves TCP half-close and efficient response copying.

This is independent of #5084's controller transition locking; their combined HTTP race tests pass. LAN authentication and route boundaries are unchanged.

## Testing

title: fix(scm/github): stop reporting a job that never started as a CI failure
body:
## What

Classifies a GitHub Actions job that never started as `unknown` rather than a failed check.

Addresses **item 3 of #4850**. Deliberately not `Fixes` — that issue tracks three separate defects and the other two are untouched here.

## Why

When a repository hits its Actions spending limit, GitHub reports every job as `conclusion: FAILURE` with no steps recorded, an empty runner and no log to fetch. AO's rollup read that as a red check, moved the owning worker to `ci_failed`, and nudged the agent to go fix a test that never executed.

The reporter measured a refused job retried eight times in about forty minutes, every attempt the identical billing refusal, every one producing a fresh `ci_failed` wake-up until the PR was closed to break the loop.

## How

`steps(first:1){ totalCount }` joins the CheckRun selection so the two cases can be told apart, and a `FAILURE` with a **present-and-zero** step count is classified `unknown`.

Three limits on the rule, each with a test:

- **Only `FAILURE`.** `STARTUP_FAILURE`, `TIMED_OUT` and `ACTION_REQUIRED` still fail with zero steps — an invalid workflow file records no steps and is a real defect the user must see.
- **Present-and-zero only.** A missing `steps` block means the caller did not request it, not that the job did nothing; treating absent as zero would decay every real failure to unknown.
- Unparseable counts fall through to the previous behaviour.

`unknown` is the existing vocabulary for "undetermined", so this needs no new domain status, DTO field or API surface. `ciSummaryFromGraphQL` already treats unknown as neither failing nor passing, so a never-started job stops producing `CIFailing`.

One thing worth a maintainer's eye: `runner_name` is REST-only and not exposed on the GraphQL `CheckRun` type, so the step count is the signal available on this code path. I confirmed against the live schema that `CheckRun.steps` exists and `CheckStepConnection` has `totalCount`.

## Testing

`TestCheckStatusNeverStartedJobIsNotAFailure` and `TestCISummaryNeverStartedJobIsNotFailing` fail without the change:

```
provider_neverstarted_test.go:29: status = "failed", want "unknown"; a job that never started is not a failing test
provider_neverstarted_test.go:70: ci summary = "failing", want anything but CIFailing for a never-started job
```

`TestCheckStatusRealFailuresStillFail` covers the six cases that must keep failing. Package tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

title: fix(lifecycle): do not re-nudge the agent when a failed check is merely re-run
body:
## What

Stops the agent being nudged again when a failing check is merely re-run.

Addresses **item 3 of #4850**, the amplification half. Companion to #5088, which fixes the classification. Deliberately not `Fixes` — #4850 tracks three defects and the other two are untouched.

## Why

`ciFailureSignature` included the check's URL. GitHub mints a new check-run URL for **every attempt**, so re-running an unchanged failing check produced a different signature, the dedupe in `sendOnce` missed, and the agent was nudged again.

During the spending-limit outage in #4850 a refused job was retried eight times in about forty minutes. Every attempt was the identical billing refusal, and every one produced a fresh `ci_failed` wake-up until the PR was closed to break the loop.

Nothing caps this. CI nudges are queued with `maxAttempts: 0`, and `sendOnce` reads `0` as unlimited:

```go
if maxAttempts > 0 && attempts >= maxAttempts {
```

so the signature is the only thing between a retried check and an unbounded stream of injections. (The review-comment path caps at `reviewMaxNudge`; CI has no equivalent. I have not added one here — that is a policy change and belongs in its own PR if you want it.)

## How

The URL is dropped from the signature. Name, commit, status and log tail identify the *failure*, which is what must not repeat.

## Worth stating for review

**AO does not re-run checks.** There is no rerun or rerequest call anywhere in the tree, so this does not stop the retries — it stops AO reacting to each one as though it were new. The issue notes the reporter had not pinned down which component re-ran the job; as far as AO's source goes, it wasn't AO.

## Testing

`TestCIFailureSignatureIgnoresPerAttemptURL` fails without the change:

```
reactions_ci_rerun_test.go:24: signature changed across a re-run of the same failure; the agent would be nudged again
```

`TestCIFailureSignatureStillSeparatesRealChanges` pins that a new commit, a changed log, a different check name and an additional failing check each still produce a distinct signature — the dedupe must not swallow real news. Package tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(landing): reduce eager downloads and size hero before hydration
body:
## What

Reduce unnecessary landing-page downloads and render the hero mockup at the correct mobile size before hydration.

## Why

The live homepage preloaded a tiny Cursor icon that transferred 1.17 MB compressed, plus 376 KB of below-the-fold backgrounds. Its hero board stayed invisible until two JavaScript measurement effects ran; simply revealing the server-rendered board would restore the mobile layout flash.

## How

- Preserve a single hidden-until-measured fallback for older engines. Keep the existing design and animation behavior.
- Add an exported-page browser regression script covering JavaScript-disabled rendering at four widths, delayed hydration, resizing, height constraints, the size cap, and legacy fallback.

title: feat(chat): shared Plan → questions → review → implement flow for Codex and ACP harnesses
body:
## Problem

AO should offer a consistent **Plan → questions → review → implement** flow across Codex and ACP-based harnesses. Today, question handling, planning controls, remembered permissions, and continuation are split across provider adapters, live configuration endpoints, and renderer heuristics.

A user can select Plan without that choice being durable, have it overwritten by a remembered permission setting, or encounter a native question that AO cannot present and answer correctly. Adding a Codex toggle alone would leave those lifecycle problems in place.

**Goal:** one daemon-owned workflow and shared interface, with each adapter translating its provider's native capabilities. Preserve the existing Go service/ports/storage boundaries and keep desktop, mobile, and CLI as clients.

**Source:** user-provided screenshot from anaya, dated 31 August 2026, asking why the question tool is not available for all agents; subsequent investigation requested a generic approach inspired by T3 Code. No source-chat URL was provided.

## Investigation status and existing groundwork

- Rechecked relevant code against main at [`0e8038d7b`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06) before filing.
- Earlier investigation on 7–8 September reproduced two ACP wire-level defects with a scripted provider. These are protocol-boundary reproductions, not a claim that every packaged harness was tested live.
- Main already provides [ChatInputRequest](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/ports/chat.go#L702), structured-input activities, ResolveInput, shared ElicitationCard, Claude ACP forms, and Cursor's [native question extension](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/cursoracp/extensions.go#L70). [PR #4398](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4398) added sequential Claude questions.
- A **local prototype** exists on `codex/shared-agent-questions`, commit `ba33bb5e5132cfd75438f4b5c8274699f0087825`. It adds Codex native question normalization, shared validation, and ordered question groups. It is **not on main and has no published PR**. Review/reuse that work where appropriate; do not count it as shipped.
- The prototype's live round trip passed with Codex CLI **0.153.4**, explicitly starting native Plan mode, answering a structured question, and observing the resumed response. It bypassed the ordinary public turn-settings path, so it does not prove the complete product flow.
- **Confidence: high** in the traced settings/dispatch defects. Cross-harness mode availability and the proposed complete workflow still require live validation. The original screenshot does not establish an exact packaged AO version.

## Concrete gaps

### 1. Working mode is missing from durable settings

[ConversationSettings](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/domain/conversation.go#L465) remembers model, reasoning effort, and approval mode. Planning intent is absent.

[SetConfigOption](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/service/chat/service.go#L1301) changes the live ACP provider first; settingsFromConfigOptions only copies recognized model/effort/permission values into durable state. Restart, queue drain, and non-renderer callers cannot reliably preserve the selected working mode.

### 2. Permission settings can overwrite Plan before the prompt

[ACP applyTurnSettings](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go#L375) translates remembered approval settings into session/set_mode before a turn. For Claude, a nondefault preference such as acceptEdits, auto, or bypass can replace the previously selected Plan mode. Default currently maps to no mode setter, so the overwrite is specifically tied to a nondefault preference.

Scripted reproduction:

1. Advertise native acceptEdits and plan modes, plus the modern mode config option.
2. Select plan through AO's config-option interface.
3. Send a message with the remembered acceptEdits permission preference.
4. Inspect the native mode setter emitted before dispatch.

Observed: `native mode after selecting plan and dispatching = "acceptEdits"; want plan`.

### 3. Modern ACP options lose to legacy routing

[Session setup](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go#L270) enables legacy routing whenever legacy modes/models are present. [SetConfigOption](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/config_options.go#L75) then chooses the legacy setter even when a modern catalog was supplied.

Scripted reproduction: advertise both APIs, select plan, and inspect calls.

Observed: `modern setters = 0; legacy mode = "plan"; want modern setter exclusively`.

ACP recommends that clients supporting config options use that mechanism exclusively when both are offered. [ACP config-options specification](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/session-config-options)

### 4. Presentation currently decides provider semantics

[TurnSettingsBar](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.tsx#L817) identifies Plan/Agent using label/value regexes, synthesizes Agent from Manual, and leaves Plan by choosing another provider value rather than restoring the user's prior execution preference.

Claude-specific permission annotations also live in [the service](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/service/chat/service.go#L1495). Move those semantics into harness bindings; the renderer should consume a shared contract.

### 5. Settings changes and turn dispatch have separate ordering

Configuration uses configMu while dispatch uses sendMu. A live setting can change independently of active work. [Dispatch](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1298) also overwrites message settings from current conversation preferences, so queued messages use settings at dispatch rather than submission.

### 6. Question transport and resolution need a complete contract

Main still classifies [Codex requestUserInput as an approval](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go#L40). The local prototype fixes the native callback bridge, but asynchronous questions require a different continuation route.

There is also a resolution-history race: [ResolveInput](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1663) records action/content after delivery, while input.resolved can first resolve the same activity with only a provider-closure marker. [The SQL update](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/conversations.sql#L1055) accepts pending rows only, preventing the later receipt from enriching the result. Define the accepted disposition and redact secret-marked answers before storing historical details.

## Proposed direction

### Domain concepts

Keep these concepts separate:

| Concept | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Working mode | How the provider approaches the task, such as planning or execution; separate from Chat/TUI interface mode |
| Permission preference | The user's permission policy for execution; some providers couple active permissions to working mode |
| Next-turn settings | Remembered choices used when accepting subsequent work |
| Question | A request for information; answering it does not itself authorize tool execution or leaving Plan |
| Proposed plan | A provider's description of work offered for review |
| Progress plan | A changing checklist of execution steps and status |

### Ownership and public interface

Deepen the existing chat controller. It owns durable intent, submissions, interaction identity, resolution, and continuation. Adapters own wire formats, native mode/permission composition, and capability interpretation. SQLite remains the durable source; the renderer presents the result.

Illustrative operations, extending the existing service rather than adding another manager:

```go
Controls(ctx, conversationID) (Controls, error)
ConfigureNextTurn(ctx, conversationID, expectedRevision, patch) (Controls, error)
Send(ctx, conversationID, message) (Turn, error)
ResolveInput(ctx, conversationID, inputID, response) (Resolution, error)
ContinuePlan(ctx, conversationID, proposalRef, clientMessageID) (Continuation, error)
```

Controls should expose remembered choices, the adapter-described catalog, observed provider values, and actionable configuration problems. Patch semantics distinguish omitted fields from an explicit reset. A revision prevents two clients from overwriting newer choices.

Keep native mode IDs opaque and scoped to the harness. An adapter can annotate a confirmed planning/execution meaning; unknown modes remain usable without forcing them into a binary Agent/Plan model. Preserve generic select/boolean extension controls and make their live/persistent behavior explicit.

### Configuration invariants

- Saving composer settings affects subsequent submissions; it does not mutate the running turn or its questions.
- Resolve the entire working-mode/permission/model/effort tuple once inside the adapter. Avoid independent setters that overwrite one another.
- Apply configuration and prompt dispatch through one ordering boundary.
- If ACP setters partially fail, do not prompt under the accidental mixture. Refresh observed state, retain desired intent, and surface the error.
- Re-read provider catalogs on recovery and revalidate saved choices. Do not persist catalog availability or derived display status.
- On a different-harness handoff, translate only confirmed semantic intent; never blindly copy opaque provider IDs.
- Provider notifications update observed state. An acknowledged user action to leave Plan can update remembered mode with revision checking; arbitrary notifications must not overwrite a newer composer choice.
- Permission changes requiring a restart must be reported honestly.

**Deliberate queue behavior change:** freeze settings when a message is accepted and persist them with its turn. A request submitted in Plan mode must remain Plan even if the composer later switches to Agent. Show the queued mode. Preserve legacy behavior for old rows without snapshots; new rows use snapshots. A deliberate retry can use current composer choices, frozen into the new attempt.

### Provider bindings

| Provider | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | Expose supported collaboration modes; build the complete collaborationMode with effective model/effort; keep approval/sandbox settings independent; explicitly send Default when leaving Plan |
| Claude ACP | Treat native planning and permission modes as one composed configuration; keep execution permission dormant during Plan and restore it when leaving |
| Cursor ACP | Reuse native question IDs/options and plan/approval extensions; discover mode choices; preserve restart constraints |
| Kimchi ACP | Resolve its combined permissions-mode values together so auto/yolo-style preferences do not erase Plan |
| OpenCode, Kimi, Droid, OMP, Pi, future ACP bindings | Respect offered controls and existing launch/admission constraints; annotate planning only where verified; retain generic forms and native option catalogs |

For ACP, use modern config options when supplied, and legacy mode routing for legacy-only sessions. Replace catalogs from authoritative responses/notifications and revalidate dependent choices. Categories support presentation, not correctness. [ACP configuration contract](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/session-config-options)

The installed Codex 0.153.4 experimental schema inspected during the earlier investigation includes collaborationMode, asynchronous agent-message questions, requestUserInput.isBlocking, and proposed plan items. AO's [generator](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0e8038d7b43097e2a531efee591958055863de06/backend/cmd/gencodexproto/main.go#L94) omits --experimental.

Correct generation with recorded provider/schema provenance and focused generator fixtures. Avoid accumulating handwritten experimental payload types. Populate collaboration-mode model/effort from the effective selection because that object takes precedence over separate overrides. Prefer native built-in instructions unless AO needs a specific documented override. Schema presence alone does not establish live availability for every model/build.

### Shared questions, two continuation routes

Reuse ChatInputRequest, ElicitationCard, and the existing activity lifecycle. Bring forward the prototype's shared validation and ordered field groups after review.

Preserve question order, original IDs, option values/descriptions, multiple selection, custom answers, and secret hints. Make choice versus Other explicit so stale custom text cannot silently override a later option selection. Keep arbitrary ACP forms and URL consent intact; do not guess that every schema is a questionnaire. Preserve decoding of historical activities.

The shared card supports two answer routes:

1. **Native reply:** answer a pending provider request. Whether it blocks the turn is a separate fact; respect actual blocking/expiry semantics.
2. **Follow-up message:** record an idempotent answer submission through the existing durable send/queue path. The adapter formats the native input; it must not start an unrecorded turn inside ResolveInput. Use explicit steering only through AO's existing steer action.

Scope AO interaction identity to the owning conversation/branch/provider instance using existing generation fencing. Reject stale cards and duplicate delivery. Reconnecting to a still-live Codex host differs from restarting a dead ACP process; restore callbacks only when they remain live.

Persist one consistent disposition and allow an authoritative receipt to enrich an earlier closure event. Distinguish answered, skipped, cancelled, expired, and uncertain delivery. Redact secret-marked values in AO's historical details. Never automatically replay an uncertain delivery after a crash without evidence it is safe.

### Proposed plans and implementation

Model proposed plans separately from the current progress checklist, reusing existing turn/activity lineage and revisions.

- Render a completed native proposal with **Implement plan** and **Request changes**.
- Request changes submits feedback in Plan mode with the proposal reference.
- ContinuePlan validates branch/revision and creates one idempotent execution submission, restoring the remembered permission preference. Update remembered working mode in the same transaction.
- If an ACP provider is already waiting on a native mode-switch approval, answer its offered decision through the pending request rather than creating a competing turn. Test that execution auto/bypass preferences cannot accidentally skip a review AO presents as explicit. [ACP mode-switch flow](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/session-modes)
- Where no structured proposal is available, offer **Continue in Agent mode** after a completed planning turn. Do not interpret arbitrary prose as a structured approval.

## T3 Code inspiration

T3 demonstrates the useful boundaries:

- [Collaboration-mode construction](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/357b8d5217cd62826767b6ce6d7c47915f2777d2/apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts#L568-L640): mode is separate from runtime permissions.
- [Asynchronous question and proposed-plan normalization](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/357b8d5217cd62826767b6ce6d7c47915f2777d2/apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts#L1668-L1709): common interaction events preserve whether the answer travels as a message, and proposals have a separate event.

Borrow those behaviors into AO's existing controller, queue, and adapters. Copying T3's orchestration framework or instruction text is unnecessary.

## Alternatives considered and scope

- **Only add a Plan toggle:** leaves persistence, permission coupling, queues, and continuation unresolved.
- **Universal generic configuration engine:** handles arbitrary settings but creates more machinery than this workflow needs. Use typed remembered settings plus the existing provider catalog.
- **Separate workflow manager:** duplicates the current controller's lifecycle and ownership.
- **AO-owned MCP question tool:** possible future fallback where a harness can register external tools but cannot emit native questions; still requires per-harness registration. It is not required for the shared native workflow.
- **Prompt-only Plan or parsing questions from prose:** does not establish native capability or dependable semantics.

“All harnesses” means shared contracts and faithful capability handling across all adapters. It does not mean AO can make an unavailable native Plan mode or question tool exist. Planning mode must not be described as an OS-enforced no-write sandbox.

## Implementation sequence

### Phase 1 — Durable mode and correct dispatch

- [ ] Review/reuse local shared-question groundwork; establish the native Codex callback path on main.
- [x] Correct Codex experimental schema generation and provenance.
- [ ] Add durable working mode and submitted settings snapshots with a backwards-compatible migration.
- [ ] Consolidate mode/permission/model/effort resolution in bindings and serialize apply/dispatch.
- [ ] Fix modern ACP precedence and combined Claude/Kimchi mode mappings.
- [ ] Replace renderer mode regexes with adapter metadata and expose current versus next-submission settings.

### Phase 2 — Complete question lifecycle

- [ ] Shared validation and ordered grouping for native questions, with existing generic form/URL compatibility.
- [ ] Codex asynchronous questions through durable message delivery; blocking status independent from reply transport.
- [ ] Consistent resolution receipts, cancellation/expiry behavior, stale-generation handling, and secret-history redaction.
- [ ] Explicit option-versus-custom-answer interaction.

### Phase 3 — Review and continuation

- [ ] Proposed-plan projection separate from progress plans.
- [ ] One idempotent continuation command with branch/revision checks.
- [ ] Implement plan / Request changes, plus capability-appropriate native continuation.
- [ ] Native ACP mode-switch approvals integrated without a second turn or duplicate approval.

Keep implementation PRs focused. Regenerate sqlc from new queries/migrations; regenerate OpenAPI and frontend types together when changing the API. Preserve daemon ownership and existing CDC rules.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

Primary scenario: **Plan → question → answer → review → implement → execution**, exercised through the ordinary product/service path for Codex, modern ACP, and legacy ACP.

- [ ] Selecting Claude Plan after accept-edits/auto/bypass stays in Plan on send; leaving restores the execution preference.
- [ ] Codex Plan/Default dispatch preserves selected model and effort.
- [ ] Modern ACP routing wins when both APIs are advertised; legacy-only providers remain functional.
- [ ] Unknown modes, empty/malformed choices, catalog updates, and dependent settings do not crash the UI or silently substitute execution.
- [ ] Queued Plan messages retain their submitted settings across composer changes and daemon restart.
- [ ] Settings changed while a question is pending affect subsequent work, not its owning turn.
- [ ] Partial configuration failure sends no prompt and exposes desired versus observed values.
- [ ] Native callback answers resume correctly; asynchronous answers create one durable submission.
- [ ] Duplicate clients, stale IDs, provider replacement, expiry, Stop, and uncertain delivery converge to accurate states.
- [ ] Custom-only answers, multiple selection, option identities, and redacted secret history are preserved.
- [ ] Old proposal revisions/branches cannot start implementation; repeated clicks do not create duplicate work.
- [ ] Native ACP continuation resolves its pending approval without an extra turn or unintended review bypass.
- [ ] Existing generic forms, URL consent, progress plans, and mobile/CLI boundaries remain supported.

Use pure binding tests, scripted native transports, and controller tests with real temporary SQLite. Add renderer tests for the shared contract and verify the actual desktop flow. Finish with live supported-provider smoke tests; report exact harness/version and coverage gaps. A generated-schema inspection or mocked provider pass is not certification of every harness.

## Related

- [#4648](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4648) — Cursor plan approval does not automatically continue; related symptom, same root cause not established.
- [#5013](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5013) — OpenCode Plan control disappears after selection; related configuration/UI behavior, root cause still separate.
- [#4420](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4420) — truthful planning-mode copy; Plan must not imply enforced tool containment.
- [PR #4398](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4398) — shipped sequential Claude question presentation.

Existing issues and PRs were searched. This issue tracks the broader shared workflow and does not assert that the related reports have already been fixed.

title: feat(usage): global usage summary API + usage statistics page
body:
## What to build

First vertical slice of the usage statistics dashboard. Add a global (cross-session) usage summary to the daemon and a minimal "Usage Statistics" page in the desktop app that displays it.

Daemon: a summary endpoint that aggregates the existing V1 usage pipeline data (per-model usage events with token metrics and durable nano-USD costs) over an optional time range, returning:

- total tokens consumed (input incl. cached + output), broken into the four display components: uncached ("new") input, cached input ("cache hit"), cache creation (Anthropic), output
- total estimated cost (durable cost totals)
- total request count — semantics: count of usage events for now (token-event granularity); true request-level semantics arrive with the timing pipeline slices
- cache hit rate = cached input / (cached + uncached input)

Frontend: a new "Usage Statistics" route/page showing the summary card (large total-token number, total requests, total cost), the four component cards, and a cache-hit-rate progress bar. Time range defaults to today with simple presets (today / 7d / 30d); source/model filters land in a follow-up slice.

No derived or display state is persisted: all numbers are computed at read time from the usage tables.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Summary endpoint returns totals (token components, cost, event count, cache hit rate) for an optional from/to range; DTOs added to the OpenAPI spec and frontend schema regenerated via `npm run api`, both committed with the Go changes
- [ ] New aggregate queries follow the sqlc flow (new migration/queries only; no edits to already-merged migrations, no hand-editing gen/)
- [ ] "Usage Statistics" page renders the summary card, four component cards, and cache-hit-rate bar from live daemon data (TanStack Query, invalidating via the existing SSE CDC usage invalidation)
- [ ] Nil/unknown token metrics are excluded from totals rather than counted as zero, matching usage domain semantics
- [ ] Tests cover: happy-path aggregation over seeded usage rows, empty range, and controller response shape / CLI-HTTP wire compatibility

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: RFC(usage): request-level timing metrics design for chat and TUI sessions (ADR)
body:
## What to build

Design decision (ADR) for request-level timing metrics across BOTH chat and TUI sessions: per-request/turn first-token latency, LLM elapsed time, tool-call elapsed time, output tok/s, and per-session aggregates (rounds, steps).

Today the usage pipeline certifies token/cost facts only; no timing data is captured anywhere. Chat conversations already persist turn timestamps (requested/started/completed) and tool activities, so chat-mode timing is largely read-model work. TUI/native sessions have no timing facts — the ADR must decide how to derive them (transcript event timestamps vs hook ingress vs both) or scope that explicitly.

The ADR must decide:

1. Data sources per mode: chat turns/activities read-model vs native-transcript derivation for TUI (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi at minimum), consistent with the usage pipeline's "certified usage sources" contract.
2. Storage shape: new timing table(s) vs extending usage events; how rounds/steps are defined; session-level aggregates must be derived at read time unless there is a durable-fact reason to store them (repo rule: no derived/display status persisted).
3. tok/s and first-token definitions (per request; session average) and how unknowns are represented (nil, never zero — match existing usage semantics).
4. Backfill policy: re-scan historical transcripts, or timing starts at deployment.
5. Retention, and interaction with change_log/CDC triggers.

This is a HITL slice: the decision needs a human architecture review before the implementation slices proceed.

Deliverable: an ADR under `docs/adr/` (next number) with the decision and a storage sketch. The "ingest timing metrics", "request log duration columns", and "session runtime stats bar" slices are blocked on this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR merged under docs/adr/ covering all five decisions above
- [ ] Storage sketch reviewed against the durable-facts / derived-status rule
- [ ] Follow-up slices re-scoped (if needed) and unblocked per the decision

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: feat(usage): ingest request-level timing metrics

## What to build

Implement the timing-metrics ingestion decided in the timing ADR (#5099): persist per-request/turn timing facts (first-token latency, LLM elapsed time, tool-call elapsed time, outputs needed for tok/s) for chat and TUI sessions, using the ADR's chosen data sources.

End to end: new migration + sqlc queries for the ADR's storage shape; ingestion wiring into the existing usage pipeline ingress (hook ingress and/or transcript parsing per the ADR); and daemon read paths (service layer) that the request-log duration columns and session runtime stats slices will consume. Semantics follow the ADR: unknown is nil, never zero; session-level aggregates are derived at read time, not persisted.

title: feat(usage): per-session runtime stats bar

title: fix(daemon): bound change log retention
body:
Closes #3963

## Summary
- add a bounded CDC retention janitor with 7-day age and 100,000-row limits
- prune in bounded batches on daemon startup and every 15 minutes
- add a timestamp index and SQLite store queries for efficient cleanup

## Verification
- `npm run sqlc`
- `GOCACHE=/tmp/ao-go-build go test -count=1 ./internal/cdc ./internal/storage/sqlite/...`
- `GOCACHE=/tmp/ao-go-build go test -count=1 ./internal/adapters/agent/fake ./internal/adapters/agent/kilocode ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode`
- full `go test ./...` reached unrelated timing/auth failures in those three adapter packages; rerunning them individually passed

The janitor keeps each delete transaction bounded to avoid turning cleanup into another source of SQLite writer starvation.

title: fix(codex): make Windows Codex account storage usable
body:
Fixes #5080. Very likely related to #4989, though that is not independently confirmed by this change.

## Problem

On stock Windows, Codex account management is unconditionally unavailable. `ensure`
returns:

```
{"error":"unavailable","code":"CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
 "message":"Codex account setup did not complete",
 "details":{"reasonCode":"account_storage_unsafe","retryable":false}}
```

This fires on the very first line of `bootstrapInner` —
`cleanupPendingCredentialHomes` → `ensurePrivateDirectory` →
`validateCodexDirectoryAncestors` — before the Codex binary is ever launched. That also
explains why `~/.ao/data/harnesses/` never gets created on affected machines.

### Bug 1 — the ancestor walk rejects the Windows system drive root

`validateCodexDirectoryAncestors` (`codex_secure_fs_windows.go`) walks from
`%USERPROFILE%\.ao\data\harnesses\codex\pending` up to `C:\` and requires every existing
ancestor to have a trusted owner and no untrusted allow-ACE carrying any bit in
`codexWindowsMutationMask`. Stock Windows `C:\` fails both checks:

| check | stock Windows value | AO's rule |
|---|---|---|
| owner | `NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller` | trusted = {current user, LocalSystem, BUILTIN\Administrators} → false |
| DACL | `NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users:(AD)`, mask `0x00000004` = `FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY` | mask includes `codexWindowsAppendData` → unsafe |

Both of these are Windows defaults (`(Get-Acl C:\).Owner` is `NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller`
on every stock install), so **this reproduces on every stock Windows machine** — not just
misconfigured ones. That matches reports that Codex account management worked prior to
v0.12.11, before this ancestor check was added.

### Bug 2 — POSIX mode-bit check on a managed credential home

Separately, `AccountFactory.Open` gated managed homes on `info.Mode().Perm() != 0o700`.
Windows has no POSIX mode bits: a directory created with `os.Mkdir(path, 0o700)` comes
back from `Lstat` as `0777`, so this comparison can never succeed on Windows. Every
`Managed: true` open therefore failed: opaque-global-credential verification, device
account import, login verification, and switch verification. Bug 1 masks bug 2 today —
but with only bug 1 fixed, account count would still read 0 and adding an account would
still fail.

## Fix

* **`backend/internal/service/agent/codex_windows_security.go`** (new) —
  `codexWindowsAncestorMutationMask`, the vault mask minus `FILE_ADD_FILE` and
  `FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY`, used by a new `codexWindowsAncestorACLIsSafe`. Creating a new
  entry beside the vault chain cannot rename, delete, or redirect an ancestor that
  already exists, so `DELETE`, `FILE_DELETE_CHILD`, `WRITE_DAC`, `WRITE_OWNER`,
  `GENERIC_ALL`, and `GENERIC_WRITE` still disqualify an ancestor. The vault's own mask
  (used for the leaf directory that actually holds credentials) is unchanged.
* **`backend/internal/service/agent/codex_secure_fs_windows.go`** — `NT
  SERVICE\TrustedInstaller` (`S-1-5-80-956008885-…`) added to the trusted-owner and
  trusted-principal sets. It's a service SID that no interactive account can assume
  without already holding SYSTEM, so it's at least as trustworthy as
  `BUILTIN\Administrators` — and it's the unavoidable owner of `C:\` on every stock
  Windows install.
* **`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/account.go`** plus new
  `account_home_unix.go` / `account_home_windows.go` — the `Perm() != 0o700` gate becomes
  a platform-specific `managedHomePrivate(path, info)`. Unix keeps the existing 0700
  comparison. Windows instead verifies what AO actually applies when it creates a managed
  home: the current user owns it, its DACL is protected from inheritance, and no
  untrusted principal holds an effective allow ACE.
* **Regression tests** — `codex_windows_security_test.go`
  (`TestWindowsAncestorACLPolicyAcceptsDefaultSystemDriveRoot`: add-child rights are now
  accepted for ancestors, real mutation rights are still rejected for ancestors, and the
  vault's own (stricter) mask is unchanged) and `account_home_windows_test.go` (asserts
  Windows really reports `0777` on a directory created with `0700`, that a directory with
  an inherited DACL is still rejected, and that an owner-only protected DACL is accepted
  — so the new check isn't a no-op).

## Verification

A/B tested with two separately built binaries (unmodified `v0.12.12` control vs. this
branch), same Go toolchain/flags as `packages/build-binaries.sh`'s `win32-x64` target,
run against an identical sandboxed environment (isolated `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, own
`AO_DATA_DIR`/port, a copy of a real Codex credential):

**Unmodified v0.12.12 (control):**

```
ensure -> CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE, reasonCode=account_storage_unsafe, retryable=false
ao spawn --harness codex ... -> Codex account setup did not complete (CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE)
```

Byte-identical to the reported symptom in #5080 / #4989.

**Patched, identical sandbox:**

```
Codex capability check completed  account_read=supported account_management=supported capacity_read=supported
agent readiness check  harness=codex  outcome=ready
GET /agents/codex/accounts -> 1 account, status valid, authorized, authMethod chatgpt
  capabilities: nativeLogin / resetCreditConsume / globalSwitch all "supported"
ao spawn --harness codex ... -> spawned session (idle)
```

The account was imported through the `Managed: true` path, so bug 2's fix is exercised
too, not just bug 1.

`go vet` is clean on both touched packages. The new targeted tests pass:
`TestWindowsAncestorACLPolicyAcceptsDefaultSystemDriveRoot`,
`TestManagedHomePrivateOnWindows`.

## Honest limitations

* **The package test suites are not green on this test machine, before or after this
  change.** `go test ./backend/internal/service/agent/... ./backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/...`
  reports 95 failures on *both* an unmodified `v0.12.12` build and this branch —
  `comm` over the sorted failure lists shows zero new failures introduced by this change.
  The cause is this machine's environment, not the fix: most `agent` package failures are
  `t.TempDir()` under `%TEMP%`, whose DACL on this machine grants Modify rights to Codex
  CLI sandbox principals — the ancestor check correctly rejects that, since those really
  are mutation rights, unlike `C:\`'s add-subdirectory-only grant. A machine without those
  sandbox groups on `%TEMP%` would not hit this. Several `codexappserver` failures are
  pre-existing hardcoded POSIX paths (`/tmp/ws`) unrelated to this change.
* **The Electron UI was not rebuilt.** Only the Go daemon was built and tested. The
  greyed-out "+ Add account" button reads the same `capabilities` payload that now
  returns `supported`, so it should enable itself, but this was not observed in the
  actual UI.
* **The interactive "+ Add account" browser-OAuth login flow was not exercised.**
  Verification used device-account import instead, which shares the same `Managed: true`
  open path as the OAuth flow, but the OAuth terminal itself was not run end-to-end.

Make local SQLite and PostHog telemetry queues safe when events arrive during or after shutdown.

## Why

Emit could send on a channel that Close had already closed, causing a panic. Both queues date back to [ReverbCode #307](https://github.com/aoagents/ReverbCode/pull/307).

title: fix(updates): parse nightly build stamps as UTC, not local wall time
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5059.

`parseNightlyVersion` read the UTC-encoded nightly stamp (e.g. `202609071035`) with the **local** component `Date` constructor, so the parsed instant shifted by the machine's UTC offset. Every renderer surface that shows the nightly build date — the sidebar update row, the Settings Updates section, and the restart-to-update dialog — then rendered the wrong time (or the wrong calendar day near UTC midnight).

Reproduced against `main` (commit 24e101914): with `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` the stamp `202609071035` parsed to `2026-09-07T05:05:00.000Z` instead of `10:35:00.000Z` (rendered "Sep 7, 10:35 AM" instead of "Sep 7, 4:05 PM"); with `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` it parsed to `17:35:00.000Z`. Under UTC it was correct only by accident. The existing parser tests asserted local getters, so they passed in every timezone and encoded the wrong interpretation.

## Root cause

The stamp digits encode the build time in UTC. `new Date(y, m-1, d, h, min)` interprets them as local wall time; the subsequent validity check also used local getters (`getMonth`).

## Fix

`frontend/src/renderer/lib/build-channel.ts` — two functional lines:

- construct the instant with `Date.UTC(...)`;
- validate the round-trip with `getUTCMonth()` instead of `getMonth()`.

No consumer changes are needed: `Sidebar.tsx`, `settings/UpdatesSection.tsx`, and `RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx` all format through `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, which renders the equivalent device-local time once the `Date` represents the correct instant.

## Tests

- `build-channel.test.ts`: parser assertions rewritten to `builtAt.toISOString()` / `getTime()` against `Date.UTC(...)` (no local getters, timezone-independent), plus new positive/negative offset coverage (`Sep 7, 4:05 PM` in `Asia/Kolkata`, `Sep 7, 3:35 AM` in `America/Los_Angeles`) and a UTC day-boundary case. Malformed/stable/feature and trailing-commit coverage kept.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx`: new staged-nightly case at the UTC day boundary; the expected date-only label is derived from the absolute instant, so the assertion holds in every timezone.
- `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx`: same day-boundary coverage for the dialog label.
- `UpdatesSection.test.tsx` (new): covers the full device-local "Built {{date}}" timestamp for an installed nightly.

All validated locally under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`: build-channel 7/7, RestartToUpdateDialog 6/6, UpdatesSection 1/1, Sidebar 97/97.

## Intentional omissions

- The separate "Last checked" display is untouched: it formats epoch milliseconds and was never affected (per the issue).
- No UTC timestamps in GitHub metadata, updater feeds, or version strings are rewritten anywhere; only the renderer-side parse was wrong, matching the issue's acceptance criteria.

title: perf(ci): Go build-test takes 12 to 19 minutes as SQLite race tests scale
body:
## Bug

The required GitHub Actions check `Go / build-test (pull_request)` now takes roughly 12 to 19 minutes on successful pull requests. The full race-enabled backend test step is the critical path, particularly `backend/internal/storage/sqlite`.

**Reported by:** Harshit Singh Bhandari
**Analyzed against:** `24e101914976a14145d7302f49626db3541ef8b5`
**Confidence:** High. The workflow, job logs, package timings, historical runs, test fixture path, and migration serialization were traced directly.
**Priority:** P1. This delays every backend pull request and has steadily regressed, but does not break correctness.

## Current workflow

`.github/workflows/go.yml` runs this sequence on `ubuntu-latest`:

1. `actions/checkout@v4`
2. `actions/setup-go@v5` using `backend/go.mod`, with `cache: false`
3. Formatting check
4. `go build ./...`
5. `go vet ./...`
6. `go test -race -timeout=15m ./...`

There is no wrapper script, artifact upload, or large log-processing step. The 15 minute package timeout was added in `cf350730` after the SQLite package approached Go's default 10 minute timeout.

## Measured impact

A sample of 17 successful pull request runs from 2026-09-06 17:47 UTC through 2026-09-07 15:15 UTC showed:

| Measurement | Minimum | Median | Approximate p90 | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Whole `build-test` job | 11m40s | 15m13s | 18m01s | 18m40s |
| `Test` step | 10m42s | 14m04s | 16m43s | 17m21s |

The test step consumes about 92 percent of median job time.

Representative runs:

| Run | Started | Job | Setup | Build | Vet | Test | SQLite package |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [Fast successful run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34125339518/job/101752591425) | 2026-09-07 13:04 UTC | 11m40s | 10s | 28s | 9s | 10m42s | 448.732s |
| [Slow successful run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34136321477/job/101788035704) | 2026-09-07 15:03 UTC | 18m40s | 15s | 42s | 14s | 17m21s | 758.741s |
| [Another slow run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34137215212/job/101790865965) | 2026-09-07 15:13 UTC | 17m39s | 12s | 40s | 13s | 16m27s | 714.313s |

This is a sustained regression, not a one-off slow runner:

| Date and run | Whole job | Test step | SQLite package |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [2026-07-07](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/28894351858/job/85714962527) | 2m30s | 1m46s | 3.499s |
| [2026-08-07](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/31204946753/job/92953568067) | 4m23s | 3m27s | 66.263s |
| [2026-08-26](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/33025295371/job/98365045119) | 9m05s | 8m04s | 293.734s |

Across corresponding commits, backend test files grew from 167 to 329 to 444 to 546, SQLite test files from 10 to 20 to 33 to 45, and migrations from 21 to 63 to 93 to about 112. The SQLite package grew much faster than the suite itself.

## Root cause

### 1. Full race instrumentation is the dominant multiplier

On current main, a local comparison of only the two hottest packages with a warm compilation cache produced:

| Command | Wall time | SQLite | Store |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/storage/sqlite ./internal/storage/sqlite/store` | 22.93s | 12.184s | 7.903s |
| `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/storage/sqlite ./internal/storage/sqlite/store` | 597.59s | 577.884s | 399.236s |

Race instrumentation increased wall time by about 26 times and reported package time by roughly 47 to 50 times. Full race coverage is valuable and should be preserved. The suite and fixtures need to make that coverage affordable.

### 2. Test fixtures repeatedly enter serialized migration work

`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go` makes every `sqlite.Open` acquire `gooseMu`, run the migration-history repair and preparation probes, call `goose.Up`, and reconcile schema. Current main contains about 112 migration files.

The SQLite tree has 319 tests, roughly 83 open helper calls, and only 9 `t.Parallel()` calls. Production migration work is intentionally serialized because Goose uses package-level globals.

`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/sqlitetest/sqlitetest.go` builds one migrated database template with `sync.Once`, but each clone still calls `sqlite.Open`. The store suite invokes its test store helper roughly 171 times, so already-current clones repeatedly re-enter Goose and schema repair checks. Dedicated migration compatibility tests also perform many real opens, usually serially.

### 3. Runner variability amplifies the structural cost

Recent fast and slow runs used distinct GitHub-hosted x64 runners but the same `ubuntu-24.04` image version `20260831.293.1`. Build, vet, SQLite, store, chat, usage, controller, and spec generation times all move together by roughly 1.5 to 1.7 times. That is consistent with runner CPU or I/O variability, not one intermittent test.

### 4. Cold caches and duplicate Go toolchain setup add smaller fixed costs

`setup-go` caching is explicitly disabled. A representative build emitted 45 dependency download lines within about 2.46 seconds, then spent most of its 33 seconds compiling.

Setup installs Go 1.25.7 from `backend/go.mod`, but root `go.work` declares Go 1.26.5. `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` then downloads Go 1.26.5 as a second toolchain. This costs roughly 5 to 10 seconds, not the multi-minute regression.

### 5. Actions bookkeeping is negligible

Representative logs are about 469 lines and 55 KB. Post-job cleanup takes 2 to 3 seconds. There are no artifacts.

## Recommended optimization order

1. **Measure individual SQLite costs first.** Capture `go test -race -json` timings and count production `Open` calls per test. Benchmark `-p=1`, `-p=2`, and `-p=4` to determine whether package concurrency is causing runner thrash.

2. **Open known-current cloned test databases without rerunning migrations.** Give `sqlitetest` a test-only path that establishes the normal writer and reader pools against its verified template without running Goose and repair checks again. Keep every migration compatibility test on the production `sqlite.Open` path. Assert the cloned schema version and isolation. Estimated pull request wall-time reduction: 4 to 10 minutes, depending on contention.

3. **Reduce repeated migration setup without reducing coverage.** Reuse immutable historical schema snapshots where multiple cases start from the same version, consolidate compatible table-driven cases, and measure each change. Preserve tests for clean install, supported historical upgrades, burned or renumbered histories, idempotent reopen, rollback where supported, and schema reconciliation.

4. **Preserve full race coverage while parallelizing its delivery.** If fixture work is insufficient, shard stable migration test groups or move the complete race suite into parallel jobs. Do not drop packages from race coverage. Sharding may save 3 to 8 minutes of wall time but increases runner minutes and setup duplication.

5. **Enable correctly keyed Go caching.** Configure `actions/setup-go` with explicit dependency paths for `backend/go.sum` and workspace inputs. Use `-count=1` if all tests must execute while still retaining compilation-cache benefits. Expected warm saving: 30 to 90 seconds. Measure hit rate, restore time, save time, and cache size.

6. **Align the installed toolchain with `go.work`.** Avoid installing 1.25.7 and then automatically downloading 1.26.5. Expected saving: 5 to 10 seconds.

7. **Only then evaluate larger runners.** First use the `-p` measurements to establish whether more CPU improves the critical path enough to justify cost.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Full backend race coverage remains in CI. Optimizing or sharding it must not silently exclude packages.
2. Migration compatibility coverage remains explicit and continues to exercise production `sqlite.Open`.
3. Known-current test clones do not rerun the full migration and repair path.
4. Compare at least 10 successful pull request runs before and after. Report median and p90 `build-test`, `Test`, SQLite, and store timings.
5. Target a median pull request `build-test` time below 5 minutes, with no package approaching the test timeout.

## Related

* [PR #3669](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3669) introduced migrated SQLite test fixtures and reported reducing a full local race run to 2m06s. Continued suite growth has erased that gain, and each cloned fixture still calls `sqlite.Open`.

No open or closed issue, and no open pull request, was found for this exact current slowdown after searches for `build-test`, slow CI, `go test -race`, SQLite fixtures, race detector SQLite, and migration package CI.

title: feat(telemetry): capture project SCM provider and GitHub org for usage ranking
body:
## What

Adds per-project SCM telemetry so we can answer "which providers do our users use" from PostHog, including how many users are on GitLab.

- **`scm_provider`** (new): classifies the project's git remote into a closed vocabulary `github` / `gitlab` / `bitbucket` / `other`, emitted on `ao.projects.created` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added`.
- **`github_org`** (earlier commits on this branch): the GitHub org owner, for attributing/ranking usage by organisation.

## How

- `scmProvider(remote)` + `remoteHost(remote)` in `project/service.go` parse the remote URL (scp-style `git@host:...`, https/http, ssh, git protocol), stripping userinfo and port, and map the host to a provider category.
- Only the category is derived. The host, owner, and repo are never emitted. Self-hosted instances resolve to `other` because the host is not published.
- `scm_provider` is added to the remote payload allowlist in `adapters/telemetry/posthog.go`; without that the sanitizer strips it before it reaches PostHog.

## Testing

- `TestScmProvider` covers github/gitlab/bitbucket across URL forms, self-hosted GitLab -> `other`, gist -> `other`, unknown host -> `other`, empty -> "".
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and gofmt clean.
- `go test ./internal/service/project/ ./internal/adapters/telemetry/` pass.

## Notes / risks

- Not retroactive: only projects added after this ships carry `scm_provider`.
- Self-hosted GitLab/GitHub Enterprise report as `other` by design (host is not shipped). Counting those specifically would require emitting more host detail, which this deliberately avoids.
- The review event's `posted_to_provider` (a boolean) is left unchanged; this PR scopes provider identity to project-add, which is the right signal for per-user provider usage.

Once merged and deployed, GitLab users is:

```sql
SELECT count(DISTINCT person_id) AS gitlab_users
FROM events
WHERE event = 'ao.projects.created' AND properties.scm_provider = 'gitlab'
```

title: fix(workspace): classify signal-killed git probes as transient, not INVALID_BRANCH
body:
## What

`validateBranch` in `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go` mapped **every** `git check-ref-format` failure to `ErrWorkspaceBranchInvalid` → `INVALID_BRANCH`. When the probe process is killed by a signal (e.g. macOS memory pressure / jetsam) or its context is cancelled/times out, git never evaluated the ref name, yet spawn failed with:

```
workspace: workspace: invalid branch name: "ao/agent-orchestrator-291/root" (signal: killed) — INVALID_BRANCH
```

`ao/<session-id>/root` is always a legal ref (`git check-ref-format --branch` exits 0), so this is an **error-classification bug**: "git was killed" was filed under "the branch name is bad". It sends users to check a ref that is fine and pollutes the `INVALID_BRANCH` telemetry bucket (#3942) with environment failures.

## Fix

Classify transient probe failures separately from genuine name rejections:

- New sentinel `ports.ErrWorkspaceProbeFailed` (transient, retryable), surfaced by the service layer as a **503 `WORKSPACE_PROBE_FAILED`** instead of a 400 `INVALID_BRANCH`.
- `validateBranch` now routes context cancellation/deadline **and** signal-killed probes to that sentinel. Signal-kill is detected portably via `(*exec.ExitError).ExitCode() == -1` (the value `os.ProcessState.ExitCode()` reports for a process terminated by a signal) — deliberately avoiding `syscall.WaitStatus.Signaled()`, which does not exist on Windows.
- Genuine git rejections (a real exit code) still map to `INVALID_BRANCH`.

## Scope / intentional omissions

- Surgical to the `INVALID_BRANCH` path named in the issue. The cosmetic `workspace: workspace:` double-prefix and the optional "one cheap retry" mentioned in the issue are left out to keep the diff minimal.
- The sibling `validateBranch` in `internal/gitdefault/resolver.go` wraps its own default-branch message (not `ErrWorkspaceBranchInvalid`) and does not feed the `INVALID_BRANCH` metric, so it is intentionally untouched.
- The signal-kill detection is inherently Unix (the reported failure is macOS jetsam, `signal: killed`). On Windows a killed process yields a real exit code, so `ExitCode() == -1` does not fire there — but the `signal: killed` failure mode also does not occur on Windows, so this is a documented limitation, not a regression. The signal-kill test is skipped on Windows; the context-cancellation branch stays cross-platform.

## Test verification (RED → GREEN)

New unit tests drive the classifier directly (the package already injects a fake `commandRunner`). A real signal-killed child process is used to produce the exact `ExitCode() == -1` shape (Unix-only; skipped on Windows where a killed process yields a real exit code).

**RED — on unmodified `main`** (a temporary test asserting the valid ref must NOT be reported invalid):

```
--- FAIL: TestRED5043/context_cancelled_misclassified_as_invalid_branch
    RED: valid branch reported as INVALID_BRANCH on a cancelled probe:
    workspace: invalid branch name: "ao/agent-orchestrator-291/root" (git wrapper: context canceled)
--- FAIL: TestRED5043/signal-killed_probe_misclassified_as_invalid_branch
    RED: valid branch reported as INVALID_BRANCH on a signal-killed probe:
    workspace: invalid branch name: "ao/agent-orchestrator-291/root" (signal: killed)
FAIL
```

**GREEN — with the fix** (`go test ./internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/...` and the service mapping):

```
--- PASS: TestValidateBranchClassifiesTransientProbeFailures
    --- PASS: .../context_cancelled_maps_to_probe_failure
    --- PASS: .../context_deadline_maps_to_probe_failure
    --- PASS: .../signal-killed_probe_maps_to_probe_failure
    --- PASS: .../genuine_git_rejection_still_maps_to_invalid_branch
ok  	.../internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree	5.9s
--- PASS: TestToAPIErrorMapsWorkspaceBranchSentinels/probe_failed   (WORKSPACE_PROBE_FAILED, 503)
ok  	.../internal/service/session
```

Validated locally against the Go 1.26.5 toolchain: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `go test` + `go test -race` for the touched packages, and `golangci-lint v2.12.2` — all green. Diff-coverage: 100% (18/18) of changed production lines.

Fixes #5043

title: fix(project-settings): allow up to 100-char display names and surface save errors (#3937)
body:
## What

1. Raised project display name maximum length from 20 to 100 runes across backend DTOs, domain service logic, client models, and OpenAPI spec.
2. In `backend/internal/service/project/service.go`:
   - Validates `in.Name` on `Add()`, and truncates auto-derived names from repo folder paths to 100 runes so projects cannot enter the database with an invalid length.
   - In `UpdateSettings()`, allows updating settings for existing projects with unchanged legacy display names exceeding 100 characters.
3. In `packages/product-ui/src/project-models.ts`:
   - Added `name_too_long` code to `validateProjectSettings` for display names exceeding 100 characters.
4. In `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`:
   - Mapped `name_too_long` validation error to localized string.
5. In `frontend/src/renderer/components/SettingsDialog.tsx`:
   - Rendered visible error alert message below the Save button when `projectSaveState.phase === "failed"`.
6. Added localized translation key `settings.project.nameTooLong` across all supported languages (`de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN`).

## Why

Fixes #3937

When a project's repository folder or display name exceeds 20 characters (such as `yandex-direct-mcp-plugin` [24 chars]), saving any project settings (including agent defaults, workflow, intake) failed silently because:
1. `Add()` allowed any folder name to become the display name without length enforcement, while `UpdateSettings()` rejected names > 20 characters with `DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`.
2. `SettingsDialog.tsx` only surfaced the save error in an invisible screen-reader `sr-only` element, leaving the user with a generic "Save failed" button and no visible explanation.

Raising the limit to 100 aligns with GitHub's repository name length limit and prevents valid repositories from becoming un-saveable.

## How

- Raised `maxDisplayNameLen` constant and OpenAPI `maxLength` to 100.
- Preserved backward compatibility by permitting updates to existing projects if `displayName == row.DisplayName`.
- Surface `projectSaveState.error` visually directly below the Save button with `role="alert"`.
- Regenerated OpenAPI specs and client types via `npm run api`.

## Testing

- `npm run product-ui:check` (126/126 tests passed)
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` (clean)
- `npm --prefix frontend test src/renderer/components/SettingsDialog.test.tsx src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n/renderer-coverage.test.ts` (47/47 tests passed)
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/project/... ./internal/httpd/...` (passed)
- `golangci-lint run` (0 issues)
- Manual verification on live Electron app: verified that names <= 100 characters save successfully, and names > 100 characters display visible alert `Project name must be 100 characters or fewer.`

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: fix: improve clone destinations and startup before first push

- Add regression coverage for typed, picker-selected, and saved destinations, missing folders, custom initial-commit messages, non-main branches, and initialization before and after the first push. Exercise real clone → preparation → registration → first-worktree creation.

title: Optimistic project import: load board first, provision in background
body:
## Summary

Importing an existing project no longer blocks on the full setup chain. The board navigates immediately after registration while the orchestrator spawn (git fetch + worktree + runtime) finishes in the background behind a provisioning gate with progress banner, 120s timeout escape, and retry. The pre-submit branch lookup IPC is removed and registration git probes run concurrently.

## Why

Importing an existing project showed 3-4s of blocking latency after agent selection: serial branch lookup, serial registration probes, blocking orchestrator spawn, and a 3x250ms session poll loop. Total work is unchanged; it is moved off the critical path so time-to-board drops to well under a second.

## Tests

- [x] `cd backend && go build ./...`
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/service/project/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/`
- [x] `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- [x] vitest: CreateProjectFlow, Sidebar, SessionsBoard, board-empty-states, shell-new-session-shortcut, ShellTopbar, i18n parity
- [x] live daemon timing run: POST /projects before/after on a 248MB repo

## Files impacted

- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx` — optimistic navigate, background spawn, 120s guard
- `frontend/src/renderer/stores/ui-store.ts` — provisioningProjectIds, gated requestNewTask
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx`, `BoardEmptyStates.tsx`, `ShellTopbar.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx` — banner + gating
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx` — no blocking branch lookup
- `backend/internal/service/project/service.go` — concurrent registration probes
- `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/*.json` — shell.provisioning keys (8 locales)
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.test.tsx`, `__tests__/integration/board-empty-states.test.tsx` — coverage

## Measured numbers

Live daemon (`ao daemon`, isolated data dir) against a 248MB / 3408-file clone, 3 runs each:

| Stage | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| POST /projects | ~28-32ms | ~17-21ms |
| getRepositoryBranch IPC (2 git procs) | ~10ms | removed |
| git worktree add | 1.1s blocking | 1.1s backgrounded |
| git fetch (up-to-date) | 33ms | 33ms backgrounded |
| session poll loop | up to 750ms | single awaited refetch |

Note: per-spawn git costs are ~5ms on fast SSDs and 50-200ms on typical macOS/Windows machines, so slow-hardware savings scale proportionally. Full spawn could not run to completion in the sandbox (no agent binary/tmux); it correctly rejects pre-workspace with AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND.

title: fix(session-manager): don't inherit role model on harness mismatch
body:
## Summary

A spawn that selects a harness other than the project's configured `Worker.Harness`/`Orchestrator.Harness` still inherited that role override's `Model`/`Mode`, leaking a provider-specific model alias onto the wrong agent.

The agent-switch path already guarded against this. This moves that gating into `effectiveAgentConfig` itself so every caller — spawn, restore, chat spawn/restore, interface transition, and switch — shares one rule:

- `Model`/`Mode` are inherited only when the launch harness matches the role's pinned harness (an unset role harness means "not pinned" and matches anything).
- `Permissions` is harness-neutral and is always inherited.

The post-hoc `config.Model = ""` gate in `agent_switching.go` is removed; that path now passes the target harness into `effectiveAgentConfig` instead.

## Tests

- `TestEffectiveHarnessAndAgentConfig` extended: a mismatched harness drops model/mode but keeps permissions; an unpinned role override still applies to any harness.
- New `TestSpawn_DropsRoleModelOnHarnessMismatch`: `Worker.Harness=opencode` with `Model="custom/gpt-5.5"`, spawn with `Harness=codex` → launched model is empty (codex uses its own default), permissions still `auto`.
- `npm run lint` (full `go test ./...` + golangci-lint v2.12.2) passes.

## Risks / notes

- Behavior change beyond the bug itself: in the switch path, a role override with **no** harness pinned previously had its model dropped on every switch; it now applies to any harness, consistent with the new "empty = not pinned" rule. Happy to restore the stricter behavior there if that was intentional.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` was not run — `tsc` is not installed in this worktree. The change is backend-only Go.

title: fix(session-manager): don't inherit role model on harness mismatch
body:
Closes #4873.

## Summary

A spawn that selects a harness other than the project's configured `Worker.Harness`/`Orchestrator.Harness` still inherited that role override's `Model`/`Mode`, leaking a provider-specific model alias onto the wrong agent.

The agent-switch paths already guarded against this with a post-hoc `config.Model = ""` block. This moves the rule into `effectiveAgentConfig` itself so every caller — spawn, restore, chat spawn/restore, interface transition, and both switch paths — shares one definition:

- `Model`/`Mode` are inherited only when the launch harness matches the role's pinned harness (an unset role harness means "not pinned" and matches anything).
- `Permissions` is harness-neutral and is always inherited.

The duplicated gates in `agent_switching.go` and `agent_switching_chat.go` are removed; those paths now pass the *target* harness into `effectiveAgentConfig` instead. Restore keeps pinning `rec.Metadata.Permissions` over the project config, unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestEffectiveHarnessAndAgentConfig` extended: a mismatched harness drops model/mode but keeps permissions; an unpinned role override still applies to any harness.
- New `TestSpawn_DropsRoleModelOnHarnessMismatch`: `Worker.Harness=opencode` with `Model="custom/gpt-5.5"`, spawn with `Harness=codex` → launched model is empty (codex uses its own default), permissions still `auto`.
- Both mandatory gates run locally and pass on this base: `npm run lint` (`go test ./...` + golangci-lint v2.12.2) and `npm run frontend:typecheck`.

## Risks / notes

- The stricter behavior for unpinned overrides is **kept**. An earlier revision of this branch treated a role override with no harness pinned as "applies to any harness"; that reopened the same leak by a second route, since a role `Model`/`Mode` saved without an agent would reach whatever harness launched. The second commit drops model/mode from an unpinned override instead, normalizing in `roleOverride` — the single point both `effectiveHarness` and `effectiveAgentConfig` read through — so the harness-match rule in `effectiveAgentConfig` is unchanged and simply has no model left to inherit. `Permissions` remains harness-neutral and is still inherited.
- The settings form already enforces this (the role agent is required, and changing it clears the role's model/mode). `ProjectConfig.Validate` does not, so a config written through the API, hand-edited, or saved before the agent became required can still carry the shape. Normalizing on read repairs those rather than failing to load them — deliberately not a `Validate` error, which would make existing stored configs fail to load.
- Catalog-based model validation was considered and rejected: codex is `CustomModelEntryDirect` (`modelcatalog/catalog.go`), so `custom/gpt-5.5` is a legitimate free-form value there and a catalog cannot distinguish the leak from a deliberate alias.
