title: fix(telemetry): prune all expired rows and reclaim disk space
body:
Code changes: +117 -11  
Tests: +326 -2  
Others: +14 -4

## What

Prune all expired local telemetry rows, reclaim unused SQLite pages, and make local retention configurable. This changes the local debug copy only; PostHog and remote telemetry are unaffected.

Closes #3321

## Why

The previous sink deleted at most 1,000 expired rows per hour, retained events for a hardcoded 30 days, and never returned freed database pages to disk.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| At most 1,000 expired rows deleted per hour | All expired rows drained in 5,000-row batches with 50 ms pauses |
| Retention fixed at 30 days | `AO_TELEMETRY_RETENTION` accepts a Go duration or day count; default 30 days, minimum 24 hours; overflow rejected |
| Deleted pages stay allocated on disk | Incremental vacuum catches up in 256-page batches with pauses and a no-progress guard |
| No disk-reclamation regression | Real SQLite upgrade test verifies incremental mode and file shrink: 9,830,400 -> 8,781,824 bytes for one 256-page batch |

## How

- Merge current main and replace the conflicting, unshipped `0133` migration with `20261028124744441_telemetry_incremental_vacuum.sql`; preserve every shipped migration ID.
- Enable incremental auto-vacuum with a one-time full `VACUUM`, outside a transaction.
- Recheck the freelist after each incremental batch, stopping below 256 free pages or when SQLite makes no progress. This avoids a fixed 256-page/hour reclamation ceiling.
- Wire retention through daemon configuration and update shutdown-test fakes for the new store methods.

The one-time migration rewrites the database, so large databases require temporary disk space and a longer first startup. Maintenance still runs on the best-effort telemetry worker while local event capture is active. The `ao doctor` database-size warning proposed in #3321 is not implemented in this PR.

## Testing

- Passed: complete telemetry, configuration, and daemon suites with `go test -race -count=1`.
- Passed: real pre-PR SQLite upgrade and physical file-shrink regression with race detection.
- Passed: backend build and vet; pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 (0 issues).
- Passed: `npm run api` and `npm run sqlc`, with no generated drift.

title: feat(mobile-telemetry): tag chat vs tui on spawn, conductor, and handoff
body:
## Why

The mobile app runs a session in one of two interfaces, a native **Chat UI** or the agent's **TUI**, chosen per session via the `mode: "chat" | "tui"` field (`lib/api.ts`). Nothing recorded which one, so "how many sessions run in chat vs TUI, and do people switch" was unanswerable from PostHog. `ao.session.spawned` only carries `client = cli | null`, no surface split.

## What

Adds a single closed-enum `mode` (`chat` | `tui`) to `ao.v2.mobile_app.feature_used` and sets it on every place a mode is chosen:

- **spawn** (`lib/store.tsx`) tags the interface the session is created with.
- **conductor** / orchestrator launch (`lib/store.tsx`) does the same for the second spawn path, so it isn't undercounted.
- **handoff** (new `feature` value): a live in-session Chat<->TUI switch, instrumented once at the hook both call sites funnel through (`lib/session/useInterfaceTransition.ts`). Its `mode` is the target the user switched to, which in a two-mode world also names the direction (to `tui` = from chat).

This lets you separate:
- **what they choose** at creation (spawn/conductor `mode`), from
- **whether chat is carrying the work** (handoff volume and direction).

`trackFeature` gains an optional `context` arg so the `mode` rides on both the success and failure event without touching the action's own result.

## Privacy

`mode` is a closed enum in the allowlist (`lib/telemetry/events.ts`); the mobile contract's "no free-text property" rule is preserved, so no title, path, or prompt can ride along. Sanitisation still iterates the allowlist, and a `mode` outside `chat`/`tui` is dropped (covered by a test).

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit): clean.
- `npm test` (vitest): 787 passed, including new `sanitize.test.ts` cases for `mode` being kept on spawn/handoff and dropped when outside the enum.
- Both are exactly what `.github/workflows/mobile.yml` runs.

## Notes

- Not retroactive: only spawns/handoffs after this ships carry `mode`.
- `feature_used` for `merge`/`kill`/`restore`/`send` stays mode-agnostic (no `mode` passed), by design.

title: fix(lifecycle): honor session toggle when injecting review feedback (#3840)
body:
Fixes #3840

## Problem

Turning off "Automatically send review feedback" (`session.AutoInjectReview = false`) did not reliably stop review feedback from being injected into the worker. Review feedback captured while the toggle was enabled remained marked injectable (`auto_inject_review = true` snapshot) and was still delivered by later observation and delivery passes even after the user explicitly turned the session-level toggle off.

## Root cause

1. In `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`:
   - `ApplyPRObservation` only inspected the per-comment and per-review snapshots (`comment.AutoInjectReview` / `review.AutoInjectReview`) saved when the items were first ingested, without requiring the live `rec.AutoInjectReview` setting.
   - `ApplyReviewBatch` checked `cannotNudge(rec)` but did not check `!rec.AutoInjectReview`.
2. In `backend/internal/service/review/review.go`:
   - `deliverableRuns` only checked `!run.AutoInjectReview` without verifying if the worker session currently has `session.AutoInjectReview` enabled.

## Fix

Treat injection eligibility as the conjunction of both policies (`persisted_feedback.auto_inject_review && current_session.auto_inject_review`):

- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`:
  - Gate both `hasUnresolvedComments` and `ReviewChangesRequest` delivery on `rec.AutoInjectReview && ...`.
  - Gate `ApplyReviewBatch` on `!rec.AutoInjectReview` (returns `ReviewDeliveryNoop, nil`).
- `backend/internal/service/review/review.go`:
  - In `deliverableRuns`, check `session.AutoInjectReview` via `s.store.GetSession` and return empty deliverable runs if disabled.
- Per-feedback snapshots remain intact so re-enabling later does not retroactively inject feedback captured while disabled.

## Testing

Added regression and race tests covering all 4 lifecycle scenarios:
1. `TestPRObservation_ReviewFeedbackNotDeliveredWhenSessionToggleTurnedOff` (`manager_test.go`): captured enabled -> toggle off before lifecycle delivery -> not injected (CI failure nudge still fires independently).
2. `TestPRObservation_ReviewFeedbackNotInjectedWhenDisabled` (`manager_test.go`) & `TestSubmitSnapshotsDisabledPolicyAndNeverDeliversOnRetry` (`review_test.go`): captured disabled -> toggle on later -> not injected.
3. `TestPRObservation_CIFailingAndReviewBothNudge` (`manager_test.go`) & `TestSubmitPersistsThenAppliesThenStampsDelivered` (`review_test.go`): captured enabled and still enabled -> injected.
4. `TestApplyReviewBatchNoopsWhenWorkerCannotBeNudged` (`manager_test.go`) & `TestSubmitDoesNotDeliverWhenSessionToggleTurnedOffAfterRun` / `TestSubmitManyDoesNotDeliverWhenSessionToggleDisabled` (`review_test.go`): AO internal review batch follows the same rules.

Validation passes:
- `go test -race ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/service/review/...` -> PASS
- `go vet ./...` -> PASS
- `npm run lint` -> PASS (0 issues)
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` -> PASS

title: [Feature]: Support Kiro CLI v3 with an opt-in toggle
body:
### Problem

Kiro CLI V3 is available to try with `kiro-cli --v3`, bringing specs, expanded hooks, and a new permissions/trust model. I would like to use it for Kiro sessions managed by Agent Orchestrator, with an easy way to keep using the existing engine while v3 support matures.

The current [Kiro adapter](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/kiro.go) exposes only a model override in `GetConfigSpec`, launches `kiro-cli chat --agent ao`, and maps AO permission modes to legacy trust flags. There is no explicit v3 selection option.

### Proposed direction

Add an optional **Use Kiro CLI v3** toggle in the Kiro agent configuration (or an equivalent engine selector), disabled by default initially.

- Enable the v3 engine using the supported CLI invocation when selected; keep current behavior when disabled.
- Make the selection discoverable in AO's existing configuration surface, ideally per project.
- Check v3 compatibility for generated AO agent configuration, hooks/session status tracking, initial prompt delivery, and permission modes. Kiro documents changes to hooks and replacement of legacy trust flags, so passing `--v3` alone may not be sufficient.
- Preserve the engine choice when restoring a session. Kiro documents that v3 sessions cannot resume in v2; show a clear explanation for incompatible resumes or an installed CLI that cannot run v3.

The initial scope could simply be reliable launch, interaction, status tracking, and resume with either engine. A dedicated AO interface for specs can be considered separately.

Official reference: [What's new in Kiro CLI 3.0](https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3/).

### Alternatives considered

- Run `kiro-cli --v3` manually outside AO, which loses the integrated orchestration workflow.
- Switch all Kiro sessions to v3 automatically, which removes the ability to opt in gradually.

title: bug(browser): stabilize native surface during resize, maximize, and overlays
body:
## Bug

The embedded browser can lag behind its React slot, flicker, or briefly expose a stale/blank native surface when the AO window or inspector is resized quickly, the browser is maximized/restored, or a side panel/renderer-owned overlay opens while the live page is visible.

**Reported by:** @Vaibhaav-Tiwari in an AO implementation session
**Date:** 2026-09-10
**Analyzed against:** `1d89c93dede0`
**Environment:** macOS 26.4, arm64; AO development checkout with Electron 33
**Reproducibility:** intermittent under ordinary use, readily exposed by rapid repeated transitions
**Confidence:** High — the current renderer-to-main geometry and native stacking paths are traced below, and earlier fixes document the same compositor boundary.
**Priority:** P2 — the browser remains recoverable, but a core review/development surface becomes visibly unstable during common layout operations.

## Reproduction

1. Open a session's embedded Browser panel and navigate to a non-blank page.
2. Drag the inspector resize handle quickly back and forth.
3. Maximize and restore the Browser panel or AO window repeatedly.
4. Open/close a side panel, toolbar menu, tooltip, or dialog while the browser is visible.
5. Observe the native page lagging behind its React frame, flickering, or briefly painting stale/blank content.

## Current architecture and root cause

AO correctly keeps the browser page in a live Electron `WebContentsView` owned by the main-process browser registry. The React renderer owns the placeholder/toolbar layout and measures the browser slot with `getBoundingClientRect()`. It sends fire-and-forget `browser:setBounds` messages to main, which scales/clamps the rectangle and calls `view.setBounds()`.

This becomes unstable under fast transitions because:

- React/CSS layout and Electron's native compositor advance independently.
- `ResizeObserver` does not cover every position-only transform; AO compensates with an immediate measurement plus a fixed 280ms settle timer.
- resize/maximize/panel transitions can produce many intermediate bounds with no revision or acknowledgement identifying the final layout.
- the renderer globally observes Radix `data-state` mutations and body resize classes, then reorders the transparent shell above/below the native page. That adds app-wide observation work and exercises a native restacking path with known stale/black-surface behavior.
- maximize/pop-out handoff uses additional frame/timer sequencing, so interrupted or overlapping transitions can temporarily expose the wrong compositor state.

This is presentation drift, not loss of the centralized browser registry or browser/agent lifecycle.

## Proposed fix

- Keep the live browser `webContents`; do not restore the old JPEG/mirror parking implementation removed by PR #3750.
- Add a single revisioned browser-surface coordinator and make Electron main the sole bounds/visibility writer.
- Coalesce intermediate measurements, reject stale layout revisions, and acknowledge the final applied rectangle.
- Drive resize/maximize/dock/overlay phases explicitly rather than relying on a fixed settle timer and document-wide overlay scans.
- Keep native view ordering fixed where possible; use synchronous visibility/interaction handoff only while a renderer overlay actually occludes the browser.
- Preserve the current surface-refresh nudge strictly as recovery, not the normal correctness mechanism.

## Acceptance criteria

- No stale bounds, black/blank flash, or persistent flicker across 200 rapid resize/maximize/overlay cycles.
- Final native bounds match the React slot within one physical pixel.
- Stale layout updates cannot override a newer layout.
- The browser view and `webContents` are never recreated for presentation changes.
- Tabs, profiles, history, annotations, downloads, DevTools, fullscreen, recently closed tabs, and agent browser control continue working.
- Resize handles retain pointer ownership when crossing the native page.
- No document-wide `data-state` overlay query on unrelated UI mutations.
- Verified in the real Electron app, with cross-platform CI coverage and an explicit Windows manual-verification follow-up if a Windows host is unavailable locally.

## Related

- #2491 — earlier stale-position report; closed, with PR #3898 still open and limited to extra remeasurement.
- #2949 — rapid overlay toggle race under the older parking/mirror implementation.
- #4979 — Windows maximized overlay blackout, later addressed by #5001.
- #3750 — introduced the current live native-composition architecture and removed screenshot/mirror parking.
- #4167 — raises the shell while dragging so the resize handle retains input.
- #4136 and #5001 — compositor/opaque-shell fixes around browser overlays and maximized mode.

title: fix(session): defer worktree removal instead of 500 on kill (#3408)
body:
Fixes #3408

## Problem

On Windows, `ao session kill` returned INTERNAL_ERROR (HTTP 500) when the agent
process still held the worktree's cwd. The kill path treated a failed worktree
removal at kill time as a kill failure, even though the session itself was
already terminated.

## Fix

Introduce a `ports.ErrWorkspaceDeferred` sentinel. The gitworktree adapter
returns it (wrapped) when an unregistered-path removal cannot complete past the
async handle-release retry budget. The session manager treats it as a preserved
workspace:

- `Kill` marks the session terminated and returns success — the kill never
  fails because of worktree cleanup trouble at kill time.
- The deferred worktree is retried on a later `Cleanup` pass; while it is still
  in use, cleanup reports the skip reason
  `"worktree is in use; will retry on a later run"` instead of an error, and
  reclaims the worktree on a subsequent pass once the handle releases.

No API or storage contract changes; cleanup status remains derived from the
sessions' durable facts.

## Tests

- Kill still succeeds and the session is terminated even when workspace
  teardown defers (`TestKill_DeferredWorkspaceRemovalPreservesAndTerminates`).
- Deferred workspace-project row removal is defers, not errors
  (`TestKill_WorkspaceProjectDeferredRowDefersRemoval`).
- Cleanup reports the deferred skip reason and later reclaims the same worktree
  once it is removable (`TestCleanup_ReportsDeferredWorkspaceRemoval`).

`go build`/`go vet` clean on touched packages; session-manager, workspace, and
session-controller suites pass on Windows (pre-existing platform failures
unchanged).

title: perf(project): tear down a project's sessions concurrently
body:
## Problem

Removing a project with several live sessions tore the sessions down strictly
one after another, so project-removal wall time grew linearly with the number
of sessions.

## Fix

`service/session.TeardownProject` now fans out one kill goroutine per live
session and waits for all of them, so project sessions are torn down
concurrently and removal time is bounded by the slowest session, not the sum.
The first error (in session order) is still returned, and workspace cleanup
still runs afterwards.

Because concurrent teardown can now touch the same repository at the same time,
the gitworktree adapter serializes git worktree teardown per repository via a
per-repo lock. Lock keys are canonicalized through `physicalAbs`, so relative,
trailing-separator, and symlinked spellings of the same repository share one
mutex. Same-repo Git sequences stay ordered while different repositories
still tear down in parallel.

## Impact

Measured with 16 sessions at 150 ms per kill: ~151 ms vs ~2.4 s sequential
(~16x faster). No API or storage contract changes; derived status, PR/check
facts, and cleanup skip semantics are untouched.

## Tests

- `TestTeardownProjectKillsActiveSessionsConcurrently` — kills are issued
  concurrently; total time approaches max, not sum.
- `TestDestroySerializesGitCommandsPerRepository` — same-repo destroy
  operations never overlap; different repos do run in parallel.
- `TestRepoTeardownLockCanonicalizesRepositoryPath` — equivalent path
  spellings select the same teardown mutex.

All 11 PR checks pass, including native macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows runners,
the Windows workspace suite, build/test, lint, drift checks, container, cloud
build, and scan.

title: fix(chat): hold queued turns when a turn fails instead of draining
body:
Fixes #4861.

## Problem

A terminal provider failure on a busy chat conversation dispatched the next durable queued turn immediately. On a systemic provider outage every queued turn failed in turn and the whole queue drained into failed history. The original report saw one OpenAI incident become 35 failed AO turns in 83 seconds.

## Root cause

`afterProject` called `drainLocked` after every primary `ChatEventTurnCompleted` with no check on terminal state. `drainLocked` only guarded on the pending turn and the Stop cutoff, never on whether the turn that just ended succeeded. So a `failed` or `recovered` completion released the next queued turn into the same broken provider, which failed the same way, and by induction the queue emptied.

The existing sync-dispatch-error guard does not help here: a systemic outage takes the async path (dispatch succeeds and returns a provider turn ID, the failure arrives later as `turn/completed` with `failed`), so the sync guard never runs.

## Fix

`drainLocked` now takes an `allowDispatch` decision:

- `afterProject` passes `true` only for a proven `completed` turn.
- A `failed`, `recovered`, or status-less completion holds the queue at `queued`, durable and retryable.
- The Stop cutoff inside `drainLocked` still re-enables dispatch, so messages typed after an intentional Stop are sent. This is the subtlety a naive "drain only on completed" would break: the Stop path relies on the completion event draining the post-Stop survivors.
- The three explicit drain callers (handoff claim, interface drain, interrupt reconcile) keep dispatching.

## Reproduction

Reproduced on current `main` both as a deterministic unit test and live in the desktop app against a fake 404 provider: a running root turn plus three queued automation messages all drained into the outage and settled `failed`.

## Tests

- New `controller_hold_queue_test.go`: `failed` and `recovered` primary turns hold the queue; the provider receives only the first prompt.
- The existing suite already covers `completed` draining (`TestSendWhileBusyQueuesUntilTheTurnEnds`) and post-Stop delivery (`TestMessageTypedAfterStopIsStillDelivered`, `TestInterruptDurableFallbackPreservesPostStopSend`).
- Full `npm run lint` (`go test ./...` + golangci-lint) is green locally.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The issue also asks for explicit recovery UX. Held automation turns currently re-release only when a later turn completes successfully. An explicit operator resume/retry, plus extending `RetryTurn` to accept automation turns (it rejects them today), is worth a separate issue.

title: [Feature]: Near-duplicate detection before tracker-intake auto-spawns a worker
body:
### Problem

## Problem
Tracker intake (backend/internal/observe/trackerintake/observer.go) polls a
project's issue tracker and spawns one AI worker session per eligible open
issue, autonomously and without human review. It already dedupes exact
repeats: `seenIssueIDs` (observer.go:244) skips an issue ID already present
in the session table, and `pollProject` (observer.go:203) checks that set
before calling Spawn.

What it doesn't do is catch two different issue IDs that describe the same
underlying problem in different words. Nothing in `issueMatchesConfig` or
the spawn loop compares issue content across IDs. So if issue #A ("app
crashes on Windows startup") and issue #B ("Windows: fails to launch, exit
code 1") are both open and both match the intake filter, intake spawns two
independent paid AI sessions to solve the same bug and produces two
competing PRs that a human then has to untangle.

This already happens with human-filed duplicates in this repo: #4407 was
fixed by #4601, and a second, independent fix (#4408) was opened for the
same bug and is still sitting open, unmerged. Tracker intake would hit the
same failure mode on its own, repeatedly, at real compute/API cost, with no
human around to notice.

### Proposed direction

## Proposed direction
Add a near-duplicate check to the intake poll, before Spawn is called:

1. Embed each candidate issue's title and body (any off-the-shelf or local
   embedding model, kept pluggable, similar to the "no mandatory external
   dependency" approach in #3967's reflection design).

2. Compare against embeddings of issues already spawned this poll cycle,
   and ideally against already-open PRs in the repo too.

3. If similarity crosses a threshold, skip the spawn and flag it instead
   (a comment on the issue, or some "needs review" surface in AO). It
   should stay advisory, not silently merge or close anything, since a
   false positive here means a real issue never gets worked. That's the
   same posture as the read-only insights model in #3967.

A reasonable first slice: a standalone comparison function
(`isNearDuplicate(a, b domain.Issue) bool`) wired into `pollProject`'s loop
before the existing `seen[issueID]` check, with the embedding backend
behind an interface so it can start as a no-op (always false) and grow from
there. That way intake's default behavior doesn't change until a backend
is actually configured.

### Alternatives considered

## Alternatives considered
Cheap text-similarity (Jaccard/n-gram) instead of embeddings would be
cheaper and dependency-free, but weaker at catching same-bug-different-words
cases like #4407/#4408, which is the actual failure mode this is meant to
target.

Handling this downstream by deduping PRs instead of issues was another
option, but that just moves the waste later, after two agents have already
run, instead of preventing it.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(cli): report metadata-only PR claims truthfully
body:
Code changes: +36 -21  
Tests: +145 -0  
Others: +16 -0  

## What

When the daemon returned `branchChanged: false`, `ao session claim-pr` said the workspace was already on the PR branch, and `ao spawn --claim-pr` gave no checkout status. Both now report `checkout: not performed; workspace unchanged`. A true response still reports `switched to PR branch`.

## Why

Fixes #4940 using the issue's accepted truthful partial-success approach. A successful metadata claim does not establish that the workspace branch or HEAD matches the current provider PR head.

## How

- Share the checkout formatter between both CLI paths, including responses with no PR facts.
- Preserve `ao session claim-pr --json` and its `branchChanged` field. `spawn` has no JSON mode; its human output now honors the same claim endpoint field.
- Document metadata-only claiming in CLI help and the CLI guide. Automatic checkout and its exact-head, takeover, concurrent-provider-change, and worktree-preservation guarantees remain deferred.
- Cover both CLI paths and JSON consistency, plus real temporary Git repositories whose HEAD is either the PR head or a distinct worker base.

Coordinated with the #5068 worker; repository validation and SCM attribution remain in that issue. #4953 and spawn/takeover lifecycle changes are outside this PR.

## Testing

Passed locally before validation was stopped:
- Focused claim regressions: `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/service/session -run 'ClaimPR|ClaimCommands' -count=1` (including a red/green reproduction of the original CLI output bug).

title: fix(chat): decode percent-encoded ACP approval request ids
body:
## What
Allow and Deny in Electron Chat both failed for Cursor/ACP sessions because the resolve routes did not decode percent-encoded request ids.

## Why
Persistent ACP hosts mint ids such as `acp-request:<host>:<n>`. The Electron client posts through openapi-fetch, which encodes the colons as `%3A`. `chi.URLParam` leaves that encoding in place, so the daemon looked up a different id than the one still pending and returned `CHAT_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING` for every decision.

This is the same trap `ActivateBranch` already handles for `conversation-1:root`.

## How
Unescape `{requestId}` on approval and structured-input resolve, matching the existing branch-id path. Invalid encodings are refused as `CHAT_REQUEST_INVALID`.

## Testing
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers/ -count=1`
- New tests cover escaped ACP ids on both `/approvals/{requestId}/resolve` and `/inputs/{requestId}/resolve`

## Test plan
- [ ] Open AO Electron, import a project, start a Cursor (or other ACP) Chat session in Default approvals
- [ ] Send a prompt that causes a shell/MCP permission card (Allow once / Deny)
- [ ] Click **Allow once** — the command should run and the card should resolve
- [ ] Repeat with **Deny** on a later command — the card should resolve without `this request has already been answered or is no longer waiting`


Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: [Bug]: terminated worker leaves tracked merged/closed GitHub PR open
body:
## Summary

AO can retain a tracked GitHub pull request as `open` after its owning worker
has terminated and the provider has later merged or closed it. Mobile is
faithfully rendering that stale daemon read model rather than serving a stale
client cache.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use AO with a GitHub-backed private repository and let a worker create or
   claim a pull request, so AO persists it as `open` for that worker.
2. Terminate the worker while that pull request is still open. Do not restore
   the worker.
3. Merge or close the pull request on GitHub.
4. Allow normal observer polling, then inspect the AO session or mobile PR
   inventory.

## Expected behavior

Within a bounded normal observer refresh, a persisted, tracked GitHub PR that
is still locally `open` should be eligible to receive its terminal
merged/closed provider state even when its worker is terminated. This should
not restore the worker or alter session lifecycle state; it should only update
the tracked PR facts.

## Actual behavior

The persisted PR remains `open` after the provider transition, and mobile
therefore continues to show it as open. A sanitized observation from
2026-09-07 included both a GitHub-merged PR and a GitHub-closed PR with this
same stale-row shape.

## AO version

Desktop 0.12.12 on macOS; the bundled `ao version` reports `dev`.

The same exclusion is present in the latest nightly source checked on
2026-09-10, so this does not appear limited to the stable build.

## Environment

macOS (Apple Silicon), AO desktop with GitHub SCM authentication.

## Logs / extra context

The current SCM observer docs explicitly say that terminated sessions produce
no subjects and their PRs stop being observed:
https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/docs/scm-observer.md#L113-L115

Both the v0.12.12 release source and the latest nightly source return early
for `sess.IsTerminated` in `discoverSubjects`:

- v0.12.12 release commit `84fb37ce5aa947ceb9b19b0c2435b242ac92ce26`:
  https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/84fb37ce5aa947ceb9b19b0c2435b242ac92ce26/backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go#L726-L739
- latest nightly `v0.12.13-nightly.202609091711`, built from
  `378f9f713b5526eb087c61574b6607ab59807fc7`:
  https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/378f9f713b5526eb087c61574b6607ab59807fc7/backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go#L726-L739

The related live-session stale-state fix is [PR #2678](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2678), merged 2026-07-22, which force-refreshes open PRs after a maximum age. Its linked issue [#2656](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2656) covers an open PR on a live session; it does not cover this terminated-owner exclusion. [#2632](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2632) is also distinct: it concerns PRs that merged or closed before AO ever discovered them.

I searched existing open issues before filing; [#4891](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4891) concerns open PRs stranded by archiving/removing a project, not terminal-state reconciliation for an existing terminated worker row.

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: bug(desktop): saved error-reporting opt-in retries apply-policy every second behind the release gate
body:
## What happens

When AO starts with error reporting already enabled, it keeps asking the daemon to apply that preference once per second. The daemon returns HTTP 200, but reporting stays off because this release has it disabled. The desktop treats that valid response as a failure and retries indefinitely.

Settings then says **“Telemetry is off locally. Daemon cleanup is still pending.”** Nothing is waiting to be cleaned up; reporting is intentionally blocked by the release.

- **Checked against:** latest `main`, `a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6`, September 10.
- **Original reporter:** @notlevi911, as credited in the supplied report. Reproduced there on macOS arm64, Darwin 25.6.0, packaged 0.12.12 and dev `378f9f713`.
- **Local verification:** clean Electron dev build on Windows, isolated data, daemon on `127.0.0.1:3019`. The code mismatch was reproduced in a focused test. The macOS timings below are from the original report.

## Reproduction

On macOS, start with an existing valid `~/.ao/data/telemetry_policy.json` whose `events_enabled` is `true`. The relevant condition is that reporting is still enabled **at startup**.

1. Quit AO completely.
2. Launch the packaged app with its output visible:

   ```sh
   "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/MacOS/agent-orchestrator" 2>&1 \
     | grep --line-buffered apply-policy
   ```

3. Watch `POST /internal/agent-switch-observability/apply-policy` return 200 once per second.
4. Turn reporting off, quit and repeat. The reporter saw one startup call, then no more retries.

The original report measured **60 requests in 60 seconds** on the dev build and **346 in 5m46s** on 0.12.12. All 346 packaged responses were 200, accounting for 346 of 379 daemon HTTP requests in that run.

## Where it goes wrong

[The desktop client](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/frontend/src/main/daemon-telemetry-policy-client.ts#L21-L25) rejects any mismatch:

```ts
if (acknowledgement.eventsEnabled !== eventsEnabled)
  throw new Error("daemon telemetry acknowledgement policy mismatch");
```

But [the controller already allows an off acknowledgement when the release gate is closed](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/frontend/src/main/desktop-telemetry-controller.ts#L206-L210). It never gets to make that decision because the client throws first.

The daemon cannot return enabled here: [the production gate is false](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/backend/internal/domain/agent_switch_observability.go#L17-L19), [authorization requires that gate](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/backend/internal/observe/agentswitch/policy.go#L273-L283), and [the HTTP response uses the authorization value](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/backend/internal/httpd/router.go#L103).

The policy stays `cleanup_pending`, so [the one-second timer](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/frontend/src/main.ts#L2588) keeps retrying. There is no backoff or stopping condition for a permanent restriction.

## Local verification

Tested the actual latest-main controller and client with a simulated HTTP 200 acknowledgement containing the matching generation, `eventsEnabled: false`, `gateDrained: true` and `purgeConfirmed: true`.

| Starting condition | Requests after startup + 60 retry calls | Final state |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Acknowledged preference off | 1 | `applied`, `release_blocked` |
| Acknowledged preference on | 61 | `cleanup_pending`, `daemon_cleanup_pending` |
| Actual Windows policy authority | 0 | `cleanup_failed` |

All three focused checks passed. These were explicit retry calls, not a 60-second wall-clock measurement. Windows fails earlier, before HTTP, because durable policy replacement is unsupported there.

### Windows screenshot

The actual Windows app shows a disabled **Share error events** switch and a permanent cleanup failure message in Settings → General. No reporting preference was changed. This captures the related Windows failure, **not the macOS HTTP loop**.

![Windows Settings: Share error events disabled with a permanent telemetry cleanup failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/423fca22b46dcfbdcc9b4bd76a7bb5fbeee3384d/.issue-assets/telemetry-retry/windows-settings.png)

An additional existing Go check, `go test ./internal/observe/agentswitch -run 'Policy|Production' -count=1`, failed on Windows in `TestPolicyOperationsDoNotOvertakeAtomicApply` with `atomic policy apply did not start`. It is not counted as passing validation.

## Expected behavior

Accept the matching-generation, disabled acknowledgement when the release blocks reporting, as the controller already intends. Settle the policy and show the existing message:

> Error reporting is disabled by this release's safety gate.

Keep the generation check and opt-out drain/purge checks intact. Also stop retrying permanent restrictions such as unsupported Windows durability; backoff alone would still retry forever.

**P2:** unnecessary local requests, log noise and misleading Settings status. At the reported cadence, that is about 86,400 local policy requests per day while the app stays open—not 86,400 PostHog events. Battery impact has not been measured.

## Related

[#5030](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5030) was closed `NOT_PLANNED`. [@i-trytoohard's triage](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5030#issuecomment-5563366293) already identified the Windows retry path.

Filing separately because the release-gate mismatch also affects a supported durable authority. Fixing only Windows would leave this path in place. No matching open issue or fix PR turned up in the duplicate search.

title: fix(review): remove host-trusted reviewers
body:
## Summary

Remove Vibe and Qwen from the supported reviewer set, while retaining them as normal agent harnesses for worker/orchestrator use.

## Why

### Vibe
Vibe cannot provide both properties AO needs from a reviewer: its `plan` agent is read-only but still pauses for confirmation before applying the plan, while its unattended `auto-approve` agent can edit files and run commands. The standalone `--auto-approve` flag approves tool calls but does not bypass the interactive apply-plan transition. Because AO cannot currently configure Vibe as both read-only and fully unattended, Vibe is removed from reviewer selection rather than exposing a reviewer that can stall or modify the checkout.

### Qwen
Qwen does not have auto-approve + read-only access support. These are lesser-used harnesses — if any user requests it in the future, we will implement a custom solution. Not P0.

Continue and Goose remain unavailable for reviewers as they do not meet AO's unattended execution requirement.

All three (Vibe, Qwen, Continue, Goose) remain available as worker/orchestrator agent harnesses.

## Validation

- \`go test ./internal/domain ./internal/adapters/reviewer ./internal/httpd/... -count=1\`
- \`npm run frontend:typecheck\`

title: fix: prevent Windows terminal popups from mobile tunnels
body:
Starting or restoring a Connect Mobile tunnel on Windows opens a standalone cloudflared terminal over the desktop app. The daemon is detached, and the tunnel commands used plain process creation without the Windows console suppression already provided by the shared process helper.

Use that helper for the connector, version probe, and stale-process inspection/cleanup. Add Windows regression tests that launch from a detached parent, assert the child has no console, and verify readiness, cancellation, and PID-file cleanup. Run the tunnel tests in Windows CI.

Hosted CI: all 13 checks passed on commit 7a0ccb6e5, including the full Go race suite, frontend suite, Windows tunnel regression step, native CLI E2E on Windows/macOS/Linux, renderer smoke, container install, lint, generated-file checks, and secret scan.

Validation:
- Both new console tests reproduced the bug before the fix and pass afterward, including with the race detector.
- `go test -race -run 'Cloudflared|Tunnel|Command' ./internal/mobilebridge/ ./internal/process/` passed on Windows.
- Real Windows desktop: startup and mobile disable/re-enable created no terminal popup; disabling removed the connector process and advertised endpoint.
- Real cloudflared: tunnel identity matched the local host; authenticated project access returned 200 and unauthenticated access returned 401.
- Phone verification: paired with the desktop QR, disabled Wi-Fi, and successfully connected and loaded projects over cellular.
- Backend build, frontend/E2E typechecks, shared UI and cloud-client checks, landing icons, and API/SQL regeneration checks passed.

Local validation limitations: the full Windows Go race run completed with existing Unix syscall, path/permission, and other platform-specific failures outside this change; local lint also reports unrelated Windows/line-ending findings. title: feat(ui): inherit Omarchy theme palette
body:
## What

Add an Automatic (Omarchy) color theme that inherits the active Omarchy palette on Linux, updates while AO is running, and applies the palette to application surfaces and xterm terminals.

## Why

AO currently follows only light or dark system appearance. Omarchy users expect applications to inherit the active palette as well as its brightness, while saved AO theme choices must remain authoritative.

No linked issue; this change follows the requested local feature scope.

## How

- Read only allowlisted six-digit hex colors from the active Omarchy `colors.toml` in Electron main, with a 16 KiB limit and regular-file validation.
- Pass normalized palette data through preload; the renderer never accesses the filesystem or evaluates external CSS or scripts.
- Poll the active palette every two seconds to follow file edits, symlink replacement, removal, and recovery.
- Add Automatic (Omarchy) to existing Appearance settings. Saved named styles and explicit Light or Dark choices remain unchanged.
- Apply validated colors through existing UI and terminal tokens, including readable foreground fallback for menus and controls.
- Refresh retained xterm instances in place so scrollback survives palette changes.

Embedded pages and agent TUIs that draw their own true-color interfaces continue to own their colors.

## Testing

- `npm test --prefix frontend -- src/main src/shared src/renderer`
  - 263 files passed; 3,839 tests passed; 7 skipped.
- `npm run typecheck --prefix frontend`
- `npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts` from `frontend`

title: fix: surface Claude subscription errors in chat
body:
## Problem

When a user without an eligible Claude subscription sends a prompt in Agent Orchestrator, chat appears unresponsive instead of showing the subscription/access error returned by Claude.

The reporter investigated the affected account and found that it is currently on Claude's free plan. The supplied screenshot shows repeated short prompts, no visible assistant response or explanatory error, and the session marked **Idle**.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Claude account on the free plan without the subscription/access required for the selected Claude integration.
2. Open a Claude chat session in Agent Orchestrator.
3. Send a prompt.
4. Observe whether Claude's subscription/access failure is surfaced in chat.

## Actual behavior

The user's prompts appear in chat, but no useful response or error is shown. The session remains idle, leaving the user unsure why nothing is happening.

## Expected behavior

- Display the actual subscription/access error returned by Claude when a prompt is rejected for this reason.
- Preserve the provider's explanation and any actionable guidance so the user understands what is required to continue.
- Show the failed prompt outcome clearly rather than leaving an apparently silent, idle session.

## Validation

Reproduce with an account that triggers Claude's subscription/access rejection and confirm the returned error is visible in AO chat. Verify that eligible accounts can still send prompts successfully.

## Investigation notes

The account's free-plan status is reported by the investigator. The exact provider error text and underlying failure path have not yet been captured; verify these during reproduction rather than hard-coding an assumed subscription message.

Related: #4937 covers a similar silent-chat symptom caused by expired OAuth credentials. This report concerns subscription/access rejection.

title: fix(desktop): settle a release-gated telemetry opt-in instead of retrying forever
body: ## What Stops the desktop re-POSTing `/internal/agent-switch-observability/apply-policy` once per second when error reporting is enabled and the release gate is closed, and gives permanently-restricted policies a terminal state instead of an endless retry. Measured on this branch's parent (`a8df5228`), app left idle with no user interaction: **6,716 requests in roughly two hours**. After this change: **1**, at startup. Following review, this PR also: - **Paces retries against an unreachable daemon**: bounded backoff instead of once a second. - **Stops a gated opt-in from carrying into a release that opens the gate.** Accepting the gate's refusal keeps the opt-in on disk, so a future release would otherwise start reporting on consent given while Settings said reporting was disabled. That opt-in is no longer resumed, and the user is **asked again** on launch. ## Why Fixes #5196. `AgentSwitchFailureProductionEnabled` is `false`, so the daemon correctly answers an enable with `eventsEnabled: false` and HTTP 200. `DaemonTelemetryPolicyClient.applyPolicy` threw on *any* difference between the requested and returned `eventsEnabled`: ```ts if (acknowledgement.eventsEnabled !== eventsEnabled) throw new Error("daemon telemetry acknowledgement policy mismatch"); ``` That fired before `DesktopTelemetryController.acknowledges` could run, and `acknowledges` already ends with `return ack.eventsEnabled || !productionEnabled`: it was written to accept exactly this when the gate is closed. So the view never left `cleanup_pending`, and the 1-second timer in `main.ts` re-POSTed for the life of the process. Settings reported "Telemetry is off locally. Daemon cleanup is still pending." when nothing was pending. The follow-ups address both points raised in review ([consent](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5216#discussion_r3984103293), [backoff](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5216#discussion_r3984103685)). ## How ### 1. The retry loop (#5196) - **`daemon-telemetry-policy-client.ts`**: only the unsafe direction throws. Asked to enable and got disabled is the release gate working, so the controller judges it. Asked to disable and got enabled still throws. The generation check and the opt-out drain/purge proof are untouched. - **`telemetryPolicyRetryable()`** plus an early return in `retryPendingCleanup()`: a platform without durable policy replacement is terminal, not retried. It keys on `durabilitySupported`, not on `reason`, which the controller's `catch` rewrites. - **`GeneralSettingsSection.tsx`**: a permanent restriction no longer renders as "Reporting remains disabled while cleanup retries". Reuses existing copy. ### 2. Backoff for an unreachable daemon `retryPendingCleanup` waits 2s, doubling to a 60s ceiling, measured from when the attempt **failed** so a hung daemon burning the client's 2s abort timeout cannot shorten it. It resets when the policy settles and on an explicit toggle. An hour of outage is **64 requests instead of 3,600**, and it still settles within a minute of the daemon returning. No jitter: one desktop process retries its own loopback daemon, so there is nothing to desynchronise. Same shape as `main/supervisor-link.ts`. ### 3. Consent given while the gate was closed - **`telemetry_policy.json` moves to `schema_version: 2`** with `consent_production_enabled`: whether the gate was open when the choice was written. Version 1 records read as `false`, since the gate has never been open in any release. - **Once the gate is open, an opt-in recorded while it was closed is not resumed.** While the gate stays closed, nothing changes. - **This is a backend change too.** The daemon reads the file itself every second and decides enablement from it, so the rule lives on both sides: `telemetryPolicySnapshot` on the desktop, `readAuthority` in `agentswitch`. The Go reader accepts both versions. Changing only the desktop would make the daemon reject every new record as malformed and reject the policy hint as a mismatch, which brings the #5196 loop back. - The policy view gains `consentRenewalRequired`. ### 4. Asking again `TelemetryConsentRenewalDialog`, mounted in the shell, asks on launch when `consentRenewalRequired` is set: - **Keep off** and **Turn on** carry equal weight. This is a consent decision, so neither is styled as the one to pick. - Either answer writes a new choice and the dialog does not come back. Closing it is not an answer, so it asks again on the next launch. - Hidden under an environment veto or without durable policy support, where turning it on would be refused anyway. - Copy added for all 8 locales. Review also turned up a bug in the shared store: two choices sent in the same tick both reached main, and the second, rejected as stale, left `saveError` set after the first succeeded. `setEnabled` now ignores a second choice while one is saving. This affected the Settings toggle too. 34 files, +885 / −75. The design spec's consent-authority section is updated to match. ### Worth knowing - **Every existing packaged install will see the prompt when the gate opens**, not only users who toggled it. Packaged builds write `events_enabled: true` by default on first launch, and all of those records were written while the gate was closed. New installs after the gate opens still default on, with no prompt. - **Downgrading**: an older build rejects a version 2 record and fails closed, so reporting reads as off. Safe for privacy, but not transparent. - **Translations**: only English is verified. de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR and zh-CN follow each locale's existing tone and terminology but need a native check. ### Intentional omissions - No new copy for a failed save in the dialog; it reuses the Settings failure message. - `invalid_authority` from an authority rejected as unsafe at load is also terminal, since `writable` can never flip back, but the view has no field expressing writability, so `telemetryPolicyRetryable` does not claim to handle it. ## Testing ### The retry loop Same starting condition in both clips: `events_enabled: true` on disk, release gate closed, app left idle. Left pane is AO, right pane counts `apply-policy` requests against elapsed seconds. **Before**, `a8df5228`. Requests climb in lockstep with elapsed time. Settings reports a cleanup that is not pending. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2f3883a-48af-40fd-85e8-91b1dee8e6f5 **After**, this branch. Requests stay at zero; the single startup call happened before recording began. Settings names the release gate. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a15d2aa4-65c4-422c-949b-53ffe3329076 | | Before (`a8df5228`) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | --- | | `apply-policy`, idle | 6,716 over ~2h | **1**, at startup | | Policy state | `cleanup_pending` / `daemon_cleanup_pending` | `applied` / `release_blocked` | | Settings → General | "Telemetry is off locally. Daemon cleanup is still pending." | "Error reporting is disabled by this release's safety gate." | ### Asking again What a user whose opt-in was saved while the gate was closed sees on launch, once a release opens the gate. The gate is closed in every current release, so this cannot be reached in a real build yet: it is the real `TelemetryConsentRenewalDialog` rendered in the Playwright renderer harness, fed the policy view the real controller produces for that record. ### Commands run locally - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean - `npx vitest run src/renderer src/shared src/main`: **3,845 passed**. 14 failures, all pre-existing and unrelated: 12 in `browser-profile-import` (`better-sqlite3` built for a different Node ABI) and 2 date-dependent chat tests. - `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 59 passed - `go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages: clean - `go test ./internal/adapters/telemetry/... ./internal/observe/agentswitch/... ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/daemon/...`: ok Each behaviour change had a test that failed before it. A few guards pass either way by design: recovery after an outage, the delay curve, and the closed-gate cases. - **Loop**: a gate-refused startup driven through 60 retries contacts the daemon once, wired to the real `DaemonTelemetryPolicyClient` over a stub fetcher. - **Backoff**: the attempt schedule over an hour of the 1s tick, a hung daemon whose idle gaps must match the schedule, and recovery once the daemon answers. - **Consent**: the parser and Go reader for both versions and every mismatched shape; the rule on both sides; desktop and daemon agreeing on the hint with the gate open and closed; and a real authority and controller across a restart for "asked again", "turned back on" and "declined". - **Dialog**: shown and hidden states, both answers, closing without choosing, a failed save, and the double-save guard. The dialog cannot be exercised in a real build until a release opens the gate. The desktop paths are driven with `productionEnabled: true`, the daemon with `ProductionEnabled: boolPtr(true)`. **Not claimed as passing:** - **Windows**, not run on Windows hardware. The terminal-state path is covered by a test driving the real `TelemetryPolicyAuthority` with `platform: "win32"`, and every branch it touches is a `process.platform` comparison that returns before any filesystem call. Needs CI or a Windows reviewer. - `TestPolicyOperationsDoNotOvertakeAtomicApply`, which #5196 notes failing on Windows, is a pre-existing backend failure unrelated to this change. It passes on macOS. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix: bound terminal scrollback by bytes
body:
## What

Cap terminal scrollback at 1 MiB across completed and unfinished output, while retaining the existing 1,000 completed-line limit. Flushing on exit now enforces both limits.

## Why

Audit AD-01: newline-free terminal repainting accumulated without a byte limit and recopied the entire unfinished line on every append. Flushing after 1,000 completed lines also retained a 1,001st entry.

## How

Use lazily grown circular byte storage and a circular list of completed-line lengths. Appends copy new bytes; eviction updates line boundaries and removes the oldest bytes. Snapshot and Tail still exclude unfinished output, and Replay includes it.

Clipping preserves a raw byte suffix and can start inside a character or escape sequence. Replay remains truncated history; the existing rendered terminal surface remains the screen representation. Live output delivery and the host protocol are unchanged.

title: fix: bound persistent host controller I/O
body:
## What

Bound persistent-host server hellos to one second and controller writes to five seconds. A nonreading controller is detached so another controller can reconnect to the same provider and replay retained output.

## Why

Addresses cleanup finding AD-10 (RUNTIME-3). An incomplete local hello previously kept its handler alive indefinitely. Controller replay and live output also performed unbounded socket writes while holding the shared host mutex, preventing attachment-state changes when a controller stopped reading.

## How

An output mutex orders controller hello, replay, live frames, and local ACP responses. The state mutex is released for controller network I/O, and detachment can close the socket independently. ACP relay changes use the same output ownership so replay cannot race journal truncation or request-state changes.

The complete replay shares one five-second write budget. A failed replay keeps its pending requests and durable ACP journal available for a replacement. Successful authenticated controllers have their hello read deadline cleared, so an idle controller remains attached. Cancellation closes controller connections and wakes a provider waiting for detached replay capacity.

Provider-stdin backpressure remains outside both host mutexes. Frame-size limits and the hello decoder's buffered-frame handling belong to AD-11 and are intentionally omitted. A controller that cannot consume replay within five seconds is disconnected even if it is still making slow progress; provider ownership and retained replay survive.

## Testing

Full local validation covers commit `78152ec4b4e819adf4945ae96a4ddaf9484a1b16`. The original-source regressions fail on the selected base and pass with the fix. Regression coverage includes incomplete hellos, stalled live output and ACP replay, shared-state availability, ordered replacement replay, pending requests, idle controllers, cancellation during a capacity wait and stale generations.

title: fix: keep GitHub validators paired with cached bodies
body:
## What

Keep GitHub REST ETags paired with the body that a conditional request revalidated.

## Why

The remaining GitHub portion of audit AD-05 allows a delayed 304 response to replace the validator after another request has replaced or evicted its cached body. Subsequent requests can then send a validator belonging to a different representation.

## How

Store immutable ETag/body entries and refresh a rotated validator only while the original entry is still current. Return owned body copies so callers cannot change retained representations. Preserve valid empty bodies, retain the sent validator when a 304 omits it, and return an error for an unsolicited 304 without a cached representation.

The existing cache keys, 512-entry FIFO policy, authentication, and HTTP error classification remain in place. The GitLab portion was merged in #5148. GitHub error classification remains outside this change.

## Testing

Full local validation covers commit `0f98a2d9fa0c10c6abc21991e6b65785d3d0b21a`. The original-source regressions fail on the selected base and pass with the fix. Regression coverage includes deterministic replacement, eviction/reinsertion, overlapping rotations, missing validators, empty bodies, unsolicited 304 responses and concurrent caller mutation.

title: fix(review): reclaim worker locks and honor queued cancellation
body:
## What

Allow cancelled review operations to stop waiting for a worker lock, and remove idle lock entries when their last holder or waiter leaves.

## Why

A review trigger waiting behind a slow reviewer spawn previously ignored cancellation until that spawn finished. Every worker ID also kept a mutex for the engine lifetime, including missing IDs. A regression against the original code retained 1,000 locks after 1,000 missing-worker requests.

This addresses the SUP07 backend review lock finding.

## How

Use one channel lease per active worker, with reference counts protected by the lock-map mutex. References cover both the holder and queued callers, so handoffs cannot create separate locks for the same worker. Cancellation releases only the waiter's reference; unlock releases the token and its reference.

Propagate cancellation through all eight operations already using the worker lock. Keep the lock across the trigger's idempotency check and reviewer spawn. Active operations retain their existing context behavior; automatic review policy and previously unlocked methods are outside this change.

## Testing

Full local validation covers commit `b32cf2984664caf68d91a6cab80331f1a6782e6b`. The original-source regressions fail on the selected base and pass with the fix. Regression coverage includes cancelled triggers while launch is blocked, missing worker IDs, queued handoff identity, all eight caller paths, independent workers, deadlines and cancellation/release contention.

title: fix: bound preview log retention by bytes
body:
## What

Bound preview logs to 256 KiB of retained text using a circular completed-line buffer.

## Why

Audit SUP04 found that completed preview log lines had no byte limit. A single completed line could retain its entire large input, and every write into a full 200-line buffer copied the retained string slice. Status reads also copied all lines before selecting the requested tail.

## How

Retain the newest 16 KiB of each completed or partial line, keep the existing 200 completed-line cap, and evict old completed lines as partial text grows beyond the shared budget. Clear evicted string slots and own retained bytes so small suffixes cannot pin giant input strings. Last copies only the requested suffix.

CRLF normalization and chunked writes remain consistent, including eager byte eviction before a trailing CR is removed by LF. Clipping is byte-based. Process management, readiness and API shapes remain unchanged; PTY scrollback changes are separate.

## Testing

Full local validation covers commit `58dadf22e3672df1b1cd708c674a4b9d915a3136`. The original-source regressions fail on the selected base and pass with the fix. Regression coverage includes oversized completed/partial lines, total retained bytes, CRLF/chunk boundaries, circular wrap, tail limits, snapshot ownership and concurrent access.

title: fix(desktop): improve editor handoff guidance UX and add Antigravity IDE support
body:
## Summary

Improves the Editor Handoff user experience by relocating the "no supported editor found" guidance message from an alarming, truncated red alert in the top navigation bar into the options dropdown menu and hover tooltip. Additionally, adds native discovery support and the official brand icon for Antigravity IDE.

## What We Did

- **Topbar Error Cleanup**: Decoupled missing editor guidance from genuine system errors in `TopbarOpenEditorButton`. `<TopbarActionError>` (bright red `role="alert"`) is now reserved exclusively for actual launch failures (`launchError`) and inaccessible workspaces (`!workspaceAvailable`).
- **Dropdown Guidance**: Added a non-destructive informational note (`role="note"`) inside `DropdownMenuContent` below the native fallback options (File Explorer and Terminal), styled with `text-passive text-micro` to match design system tokens.
- **Tooltip Explanation**: Preserved the complete, untruncated guidance in the editor handoff button's hover tooltip.
- **Antigravity IDE Detection**: Added `"antigravity"` to `EDITOR_IDS` and configured candidate detection in `editor-handoff.ts` (`antigravity-ide` and `antigravity` CLI shims, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Antigravity IDE\bin`, `%ProgramFiles%\Antigravity IDE\bin`, and macOS app bundle names).
- **Icon & Branding**: Added the official Antigravity SVG mark and exported `AntigravityIcon` in `icons.tsx` using `BrandGlyph`, registered in `TopbarOpenEditorButton` with its Google Blue `#4285F4` brand color.
- **Tests**: Added Antigravity detection coverage in `editor-handoff.test.ts` and updated `TopbarOpenEditorButton.test.tsx` to assert the clean topbar and dropdown guidance note.

## Before and After Behaviour

- **Before**: When no external editor was installed or detected on PATH, the top navigation bar permanently displayed an alarming, bright red error message truncated with an ellipsis (`"No supported editor found. Use File Explorer or ..."`), crowding out navigation controls and giving the false impression that the workspace or session had crashed. Furthermore, Antigravity IDE was not recognized as an editor even when installed.
- **After**: The top navigation bar remains clean and free of false-alarm red text. The guidance is presented gracefully inside the workspace options dropdown menu (under File Explorer and Terminal) and on hover in the button's tooltip. Additionally, Antigravity IDE is now recognized as a first-class editor with its official brand mark and 1-click launch capability.

## Files Affected

- `frontend/src/shared/editor-handoff.ts` — Added `"antigravity"` to `EDITOR_IDS`
- `frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.ts` — Added Antigravity IDE discovery candidate
- `frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.test.ts` — Added Antigravity IDE win32 discovery test & path normalization
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/icons.tsx` — Extended `BrandGlyph` with optional `viewBox` and added `AntigravityIcon`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/TopbarOpenEditorButton.tsx` — Cleaned up topbar alert, added dropdown note, registered Antigravity icon & color
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/TopbarOpenEditorButton.test.tsx` — Updated test assertions to verify clean topbar and dropdown note

## Tests We Ran

title: feat(cli): attribute created PRs across harnesses through shared gh wrapper
body:
Code changes: +270 -34  
Tests: +507 -6  
Others: +47 -3  

A worker can create a PR on an unexpected branch and stay in Building because polling cannot attribute it. AO now installs a shared `gh` executable wrapper through the common launch PATH, so successful captured `gh pr create` output can attach the PR across harnesses. This replaces the Claude-only hook parser and removes its shell-parser dependency.

- Forward arguments, stdin, stdout, stderr, and exit code to the real gh. Preserve interactive TTY behavior by passing terminal stdout through without capture; relay Unix termination signals. Prevent recursion through inherited/legacy gh wrappers while retaining the pinned ao command.
- Register a single returned github.com PR URL through the existing claim API, with takeover disabled and a five-second deadline. Repository/provider validation, workspace-child support, and derived statuses remain in the daemon.
- Make exactly one registration attempt. No retry queue or automatic retries, including HTTP 5xx. Failures retain gh's successful exit status but print a warning, API code/request ID, and manual claim command, and append to hooks.log. Server faults follow the existing daemon Sentry policy; expected rejections/daemon-unavailable failures remain visible in local diagnostics.

Fixes #2629.

- **All 20 hosted checks passed for `c74cc69fd`**, including all backend race shards, Linux/macOS/Windows native CLI E2E, Windows workspace checks, cloud tests, lint, API/sqlc drift, container smoke, and secret scan. [Go checks](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/37486538534), [CLI E2E](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/37486538484).

- Tests exercise the compiled native alias and common PATH, success/502/single attempt, exact streams and exit codes, Unix termination, interactive passthrough, and legacy-wrapper recursion prevention. The real controller/service/SQLite contract test verifies attachment without changing branch or HEAD.

All other packages passed, including SQLite. The local cloud suite failed only because macOS lacks `sha256sum`; its hosted Linux suite passed. Native Linux/Windows results are CI validation, not local passes. No unrelated code or timeout changes were made.

Scope and live testing: new/restarted sessions using bare gh with captured stdout, github.com PR creation only. Review sessions never auto-claim; draft and already-merged/closed handling retains existing claim rules (merged/closed recovery remains #2632). No live provider PR was created during tests. The [live two-harness/workspace smoke procedure](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c74cc69fd/docs/scm-observer.md#end-to-end-validation) is documented alongside the automated test command.
