title: bug(chat): provider-side failed Codex turns store an empty error_message — timeline shows a bare "The agent ran into a problem"
body:
## Bug

A Codex Chat turn that ends without a `SendTurn` error is settled as `failed` with an **empty** `error_message`, so the timeline renders a bare "The agent ran into a problem" with no detail, no cause, and nothing the user can act on.

**Reported by:** @Ayash-Bera | **Analyzed against:** `15e9ea971`
**Confidence:** High | **Env:** Linux 6.19.6-arch1-1 (Arch), AppImage daemon, node v22.22.0

![failed turn with no detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-switch-recovery-20260912/.issue-assets/codex-switch-recovery-20260912/turn-failed-no-detail.png)

The timeline marker is the entire message. There is no second line, no error activity, and nothing in the turn row to explain it.

## Evidence (live `~/.ao/data/ao.db`)

```
sid                    state   error_message  requested_at          completed_at
agent-orchestrator-13  failed  ''             2026-09-12 09:09:33   2026-09-12 09:13:18
agent-orchestrator-13  failed  ''             2026-09-12 09:06:19   2026-09-12 09:08:35
wailist-agentmesh-4    failed  ''             2026-09-12 09:01:26   2026-09-12 09:13:02
agent-orchestrator-12  failed  "You've hit your usage limit. ..."  2026-09-12 06:23:10
```

Only the last one has a message, and it came from the dispatch-time path. Every provider-side failure stores an empty string.

`conversation_provider_events` for `agent-orchestrator-13`:

```
09:06:19.473  turn.started       providerTurnId 7c2750ab  turnState ""
09:06:19.474  controller.state   busy
09:08:35.782  controller.state   stopped          <-- host gone mid-turn, no error event
09:09:28.765  turn.completed     providerTurnId 7c2750ab  turnState "failed"   <-- no text, no detail
```

## Root Cause

Two paths write a failed turn, and neither reaches `conversation_turns.error_message`.

1. `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go:576-592` — on `err == nil`, `turnState(resp.StopReason)` (line 622) classifies every stop reason that is not `EndTurn`/`Cancelled` as `TurnStateFailed`. That branch emits **no** `ChatEventError` at all, so there is not even an error activity on the timeline.

2. `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go:596-599` — the `ChatEventTurnCompleted` emit never carries `Err`, on either branch:

```go
c.emit(ports.ChatEvent{
    Kind: ports.ChatEventTurnCompleted, ProviderEventID: eventID,
    ProviderTurnID: turnID, TurnState: state,
})
```

`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:2417-2430` derives the stored message from exactly that field:

```go
case ports.ChatEventTurnCompleted:
    message := ""
    if event.Err != nil {
        message = event.Err.Error()
    }
```

`Err` is always nil there, so `message` is always `""`. The `ChatEventError` emitted on the `err != nil` branch (line 574) goes to `UpsertActivity` (`controller.go:2741-2754`), a separate activity row, never the turn.

3. `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx:341` renders `failed` as `"The agent ran into a problem"` with `detail={error}`. Empty error, so the user sees the label alone.

`backend/internal/service/chat/controller_test.go:4700` asserts the crash-recovery state is `failed` but never asserts a message, so the gap is untested.

## Reproduction

1. Run a Codex Chat session and start a long turn.
2. Kill the chat host mid-turn (or let it die), or end a turn on any stop reason other than `end_turn`.
3. Reopen the session. The turn shows "The agent ran into a problem" with no cause.
4. `sqlite3 ~/.ao/data/ao.db "SELECT state, quote(error_message) FROM conversation_turns WHERE state='failed' ORDER BY requested_at DESC LIMIT 5;"` shows `''`.

## Fix

In `acp/conversation.go`, carry the failure onto the turn-completed event and give the stop-reason branch an error of its own:

```go
var state domain.TurnState
var failure error
if err != nil {
    ...
    failure = err
    c.emit(ports.ChatEvent{Kind: ports.ChatEventError, ProviderTurnID: turnID, Err: err})
} else {
    state = turnState(resp.StopReason)
    if state == domain.TurnStateFailed {
        failure = fmt.Errorf("the agent stopped early (%s)", resp.StopReason)
        c.emit(ports.ChatEvent{Kind: ports.ChatEventError, ProviderTurnID: turnID, Err: failure})
    }
    ...
}
c.emit(ports.ChatEvent{
    Kind: ports.ChatEventTurnCompleted, ProviderEventID: eventID,
    ProviderTurnID: turnID, TurnState: state, Err: failure,
})
```

`controller.go` already reads `event.Err`, so no change is needed there. Worth also distinguishing "host died mid-turn" from "provider returned a failing stop reason" in the copy, since the user has no way to tell them apart today.

## Impact

- Every provider-side Codex Chat failure is undiagnosable from the UI.
- Hides real causes (rate limits, auth expiry, host crashes) behind one generic string.
- Users retry blindly because nothing says what to change.

## Related
- [#4296](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4296) — stale OAuth creds after Codex account switch, no auth-failure detection (same blind spot, different trigger)
- [#4937](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4937) — Claude OAuth expiry bypasses reauth banner
- [#4613](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4613) — surface retry and connection state for non-Claude coding agents
- [#5284](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5284) — Codex account switch recovery fence (same session, reported alongside)

title: fix(chat): explain a failed Codex turn instead of settling it empty
body:
Fixes #5289.

## Summary

Failed Chat turns could be stored without an explanation, and native history replay could erase an explanation already recorded. This PR covers the production native Codex adapter as well as ACP.

- Native Codex live completions and history imports share failure handling. Provider messages are preserved; missing details receive an honest fallback that distinguishes failed, unknown, and absent status.
- History reconciliation preserves failure explanations for explicit failed outcomes and recovered outcomes. Incoming provider errors take precedence over stored explanations, which take precedence over synthesized fallbacks. An internal structural error marker avoids comparing display text. Completed and interrupted outcomes do not inherit stale failure text.
- ACP stop-reason failures receive an explanation. An accepted local stop followed by a failing stop reason settles as interrupted. Successful completion races, rejected stops, compaction, and existing separate error activities retain their behavior.

Shared SettleTurn semantics remain unchanged. No new error activity is emitted for a completion fallback.

## Verification

- New native, cancellation and reconciliation regressions reproduced the old behavior before their fixes.
- A SQLite-backed failure/reconnect test checks persisted snapshots and archived completion details, then repeats the history import to prove no duplicate rows. It fails against the pre-fix controller.
- New regressions passed ten repetitions under the race detector.
- Full backend build, vet, non-race tests, race tests, and pinned golangci-lint v2.12.2 passed.
- Cloud build, vet, and race tests passed.
- Linux native CLI end-to-end suite and rebuilt fresh-install container smoke check passed.
- API and sqlc regeneration passed with no drift using Node 24 and pinned generators.
- Formatting and whitespace checks passed. The pinned secret scanner checked all three PR commits and found no leaks.
- All 11 remote CI checks passed for commit 85dda9a208bdde40227ff27bb6ff947eb0d41387, including backend race tests and the Windows/macOS checks.

## Limits and follow-up

- Future handling only. Already-archived empty failures are not backfilled, and deduplicated events are not forcibly reprocessed.
- No HTTP, OpenAPI, database schema, or UI changes. Existing UI rendering consumes the stored explanation.
- No automatic retries or guessed root causes. Missing provider details remain explicitly unknown.
- Root dependency installation reported three existing audit findings. Dependency manifests and lockfiles are unchanged.

title: refactor(httpd): share SSE transport mechanics and bound slow-client writes
body:
## Summary
Extracted a shared SSE transport package (`internal/httpd/sse`) and migrated all 4 server-sent events streaming surfaces in the daemon (CDC events, notifications, workspace changes, and Codex accounts). Standardized header handling, flusher capability validation, framing, and rolling write deadlines across all streams while keeping replay state, sequence cursors, and subscriber ownership resource-specific. Added idle heartbeat pacing to the notifications stream.

## Why We Did It
- **Duplicated Transport Logic**: CDC, notification, workspace, and Codex account streams each repeated header setup, `http.Flusher` assertions, and frame writes independently.
- **Unbounded Slow-Client Writes**: The daemon HTTP servers configure only `ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second` and bypass the REST request timeout for long-lived streams. Neither endpoint configured write deadlines. When a client slowed down, stopped reading, or stalled without closing the TCP connection, `w.Write(...)` and `Flush()` blocked indefinitely. Because handler goroutines were stuck in `Write`, they could never reach `select { case <-ctx.Done(): ... }` or return, retaining live subscriptions (`defer unsubscribe()`) and buffering events in memory.
- **Divergent & Missing Heartbeats**: Heartbeats diverged across endpoints (CDC used 10s, workspace used 15s, Codex used 25s), while notifications had no idle heartbeat at all, leaving idle notification streams susceptible to buffering or silent disconnections by intermediaries/proxies.

## Relevant Files & Changes
- `backend/internal/httpd/sse/writer.go`:
  - Implemented `sse.Upgrade(w, r, opts...)` to validate `http.Flusher` support (answering standard `SSE_UNSUPPORTED` envelope on failure), set standard headers (`text/event-stream`, `no-cache`, `keep-alive`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`), write HTTP 200, and flush initial headers.
  - Implemented `sse.Writer` providing structured framing (`WriteEvent`, `WriteJSON`, `WriteComment`, `Flush`).
  - Configured rolling write deadlines via `http.ResponseController.SetWriteDeadline` before each write/flush and cleared them immediately after completion so idle connections are never erroneously closed between events. Unwraps through middleware wrappers (`chi.middleware.WrapResponseWriter`) and handles `http.ErrNotSupported` cleanly in unit test mocks.
- `backend/internal/httpd/sse/writer_test.go`:
  - Added unit tests for headers, unsupported flusher rejection, event formatting (single and multi-line), JSON serialization, comment frames, middleware unwrapping, and write deadline application and reset.
- `backend/internal/httpd/events.go`:
  - Migrated `EventsController.stream` to `sse.Upgrade` and `sse.Writer`.
  - Retained resource-owned replay cursors, sequence tracking, and live subscription drain. Ensured subscription is active prior to header flush to avoid live event publish race conditions.
  - Bounded stalled writes with write deadline to guarantee prompt handler exit and unsubscription.
- `backend/internal/httpd/events_test.go`:
  - Added `TestEventsStream_BlockedWriterExitsAndUnsubscribesThroughMiddleware` and `TestEventsStream_ContextCancellationUnsubscribes`.
  - Maintained all existing replay, deduplication, and idle heartbeat tests.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/notifications.go`:
  - Migrated `NotificationsController.stream` to `sse.Upgrade` and `sse.Writer`.
  - Added idle heartbeat ticker (`NotificationsHeartbeatInterval = 15 * time.Second`) emitting `: \n\n` comment frames.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/notifications_test.go`:
  - Added `TestNotificationsAPI_StreamHeartbeatsWhileIdle`, `TestNotificationsAPI_StreamBlockedClientExitsAndUnsubscribes`, and `TestNotificationsAPI_StreamContextCancellationUnsubscribes`.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go`:
  - Migrated `SessionsController.streamWorkspaceChanges` to `sse.Upgrade` and `sse.Writer` with keepalive comment frames.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions_test.go`:
  - Added `TestSessionsAPI_StreamWorkspaceChanges_HeartbeatsWhileIdle` and `TestSessionsAPI_StreamWorkspaceChanges_BlockedClientExits`.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/codex_accounts.go`:
  - Migrated `CodexAccountsController.events` to `sse.Upgrade` and `sse.Writer` with heartbeat comment frames.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/codex_accounts_test.go`:
  - Added `TestCodexAccountEventStream_HeartbeatsWhileIdle` and `TestCodexAccountEventStream_BlockedClientExits`.

## Tests Ran
- [x] `go test -v -count=1 ./internal/httpd/sse/...` (all 8 shared SSE transport tests pass)
- [x] `go test -v -count=1 ./internal/httpd/...` (CDC events stream, server lifecycle, router, LAN listener pass)
- [x] `go test -v -count=1 ./internal/cdc/...` (CDC store write, broadcast, and poller tests pass)
- [x] `go test -v -count=1 ./internal/httpd/controllers -run "Test.*Stream"` (all 14 stream tests pass: CDC, Notifications, Workspace, and Codex)
- [x] `go test -v -count=1 ./internal/httpd/apispec/...` (OpenAPI spec drift and route parity pass)
- [x] `go build ./...` (clean repository build across all packages)
- [x] `go vet ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/cdc/...` (zero vet warnings/errors)

title: bug(chat): TUI to Chat switch fails - refresh ACP session history rejected with JSON-RPC -32603 until settle deadline
body:
## Bug

TUI to Chat switch on a Claude Code (ACP) session fails. Toast:

```
resume chat: wait for settled native conversation history: refresh ACP
session history: context deadline exceeded
{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"error":"context deadline exceeded"}}
```

Reported by @Pyasma on Discord. Screenshot: [switch-error.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-acp-refresh-32603/.issue-assets/acp-refresh-32603/switch-error.png)

## Repro

Claude Code session in the Terminal UI, switch to Chat. Provider rejects the history refresh, switch rolls back to Terminal.

## Root cause

The settle wait (`importNativeHistory`, `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:632-668`) polls `RefreshHistory` every 100ms for up to 45s. Each poll is `refreshableConversation.RefreshHistory` (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/history.go:62`): re-send ACP `session/load` to replay the transcript. The provider answers every load with JSON-RPC `-32603 Internal error`, `data: {"error":"context deadline exceeded"}`, so the switch exhausts the 45s budget.

Gaps:

1. `normalizeACPError` (`driver.go:621`) maps only `-32000` and `-32601`. A `-32603` from `session/load` falls through as a generic error at `controller.go:653`.
2. No session-level timeout wraps the load. The deadline the provider hits is its own.

Not covered by #4123 or #4681 (fixed by PR #4770, which made ACP refreshable). The failure is inside that new refresh path.

## Fix direction

Give the `session/load` failure its own transition error code. Cap or back off the retries instead of hammering it for the full 45s.

**Confidence:** Medium on the fix, high that the refresh call fails with the provider's error.

## Related

- [#4681](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4681), fixed by [PR #4770](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4770)
- [#4123](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4123): earlier full-budget burn on an immutable replay

title: feat(scm): add GitCode provider for PR observation and Kanban
body:
## What

Adds a GitCode (gitcode.com) SCM provider so AO can observe GitCode pull requests on the Kanban, alongside GitHub and GitLab.

## Why

GitCode hosts a large share of open-source activity for Chinese communities (Ascend model contests, CANN ecosystem), but AO's PR/CI/review integration currently only supports GitHub and GitLab. A user tracking GitCode-based projects gets no PR column on the board and no `ao session claim-pr` support. This adds first-class GitCode support through the existing multi-provider dispatch (`multi/provider.go` was explicitly designed for "future providers").

## How

- New `backend/internal/adapters/scm/gitcode` package implementing the observer `Provider` contract against GitCode's public **v5 REST API** (`/api/v5/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`). GitCode v5 is Gitee-shaped, so the GitLab adapter cannot be reused.
- **PR states** normalize as `open/merged/closed` (plus `draft`); mergeability maps from GitCode's boolean `mergeable` field; `mergeable=false` reports `MergeBlocked` with a generic blocker (the API does not explain why).
- **Review threads** are derived from PR comments grouped by `discussion_id` (GitCode v5 has no dedicated review/discussion endpoint). Thread-resolved state is not exposed, so threads report `Resolved=false`.
- **CI is intentionally reported as `unknown`** with zero checks: GitCode v5 exposes no pipeline/status endpoints (verified: `/commits/{sha}/status`, `/checks`, `/statuses`, `/pipelines` all 404). `CommitChecksGuard` and `FetchFailedCheckLogTail` are no-ops rather than fabricating a passing state.
- **Pagination** follows the `total_page` response header (GitCode sends no `Link` header); `ListPRsByRepo` stops early at the `updatedAfter` cursor since the listing is `sort=updated&direction=desc`.
- **Guarding**: `RepoPRListGuard` uses a synthetic ETag (`updated:<newest updated_at>`) as the cheapest change signal; v5 sends no ETags.
- **Auth**: `AO_GITCODE_TOKEN` / `GITCODE_TOKEN` env vars (same pattern as `AO_GITLAB_TOKEN`). Anonymous mode reads public repos without an Authorization header; identity resolution uses `GET /user` with the token.
- **URL parsing** is wired through all three layers: `cli/pr_ref.go`, `service/session/claim_pr.go`, and `domain/repository_identity.go` all recognize `gitcode.com` and its `/owner/repo/merge_requests/N` PR path (no `-` segment, unlike GitLab).

## Testing

- Unit tests in `observer_provider_test.go` cover ParseRepository (https/ssh/scp-like + non-GitCode host rejection), pagination + cursor early-stop, positional alignment with `ErrSCMNotFound` placeholders, state normalization, discussion-thread grouping with bot detection, synthetic-ETag guard NotModified, anonymous fallback, error classification, flexTime edge cases, and mergeability mapping.
- End-to-end verified locally against a real GitCode repository: registered a GitCode project → spawned a session → `ao session claim-pr <sid> 4645` → Kanban shows the PR number and 1 review thread from GitCode comments. `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/gitcode/` green; `go vet` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(codex): skip Windows volume root in vault validation
body:
## Summary
- stop private Codex vault ancestor validation before the Windows filesystem volume root
- retain validation of every user-controlled ancestor and the vault itself
- add regression coverage for drive and UNC share root detection

## Why
On a standard Windows installation, the volume root can grant Authenticated Users permission to create entries directly at the root. AO treated that OS-level ACL as an untrusted mutable vault ancestor, which prevented Codex account bootstrap from creating the managed vault and blocked all Codex task creation with ^Gccount_storage_unsafe.

The volume root is not user-controlled vault storage. Skipping that final system-level check preserves the existing security checks for all intervening user-controlled paths.

## Validation
- go test ./internal/service/agent -run '^TestWindowsVolumeRootDetection$' -count=1
- Live Windows verification: Codex account bootstrap completed and AO launched a no-edit Codex worker in an isolated worktree.

title: bug(chat): project-scoped imported conversation edits fail before provider work
body:
## Bug

Editing a Chat message in a project-scoped orchestrator conversation imported from Terminal fails with HTTP 409 `CHAT_EDIT_UNCERTAIN`. No edited branch is created; **Retry edit safely** repeats the error.

**Source:** native QA requested by @illegalcall in [PR #4466](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4466).
**Observed:** 2026-09-12, macOS arm64, Claude Code 2.1.269 / Opus 5, AO checkout `9a34cdad21b6a2567da863b24b13fbf56548f6f6`.
**Priority:** high. **Confidence:** high in the ownership mismatch; regression test pending.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Claude orchestrator in Terminal and complete prompts A/B.
2. Switch to Chat and complete prompts C/D.
3. Edit C and submit.
4. Retry the same saved edit with **Retry edit safely**.

Expected: one edited branch and replacement reply, with idempotent safe retries.
Actual: both requests fail; original eight messages/root branch remain.

## Evidence and cause

![Imported-origin edit fails before provider work](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b91e402-120e-4dc5-8c4a-ba608670ce2b)

The durable delivery remains `reserved`, `provider_work_started=0`. The SQL `BeginConversationEditProviderWork` in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/conversations.sql` joins `sessions.id = conversations.session_id`. For this project-scoped conversation, `session_id` is NULL while `current_session_id` contains the live orchestrator. The same join is present on main `0fae4c289`. Separate session-scoped Chat-start edit controls pass.

This is not evidence that the provider actually received the edit. Unlike [#4454](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4454), the failure occurs before provider work, not after losing an accepted response.

## Acceptance / focused plan

- Gate provider work on the conversation's current owner and exact live Chat generation.
- Cover project/session scopes, project rebinding, stale generations, terminated/TUI owners, and repeated starts with SQLite-backed tests.
- Rerun the original native imported-conversation edit and subsequent TUI/Chat round trip.
- Keep screenshots and local state out of git.

title: perf(mobile): decode PTY frames with atob instead of the hand-rolled loop
body:
## Summary

`base64ToBytes` runs once per PTY frame. It pre-filtered its input by building a new string one character at a time, then accumulated into a boxed `number[]` before copying that into a `Uint8Array` — neither allocation is necessary, since the output length is known up front.

The comment that kept it that way is stale for this app:

```ts
// These helpers avoid depending on atob/btoa (not guaranteed in Hermes).
```

`lib/pairingCode.ts:32` already calls `atob` on the live pair path (reached from `app/pair.tsx:84`), so QR pairing would be broken if Hermes lacked it. The desktop renderer already does this job with `atob` plus a pre-sized `Uint8Array`, at `frontend/src/renderer/lib/terminal-mux.ts:35-42`.

Closes #4876.

## Numbers

Simulator Hermes `250829098.0.17`, one full 32 KiB frame — the daemon's PTY read buffer (`backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go:196`) — 200 iterations after warm-up. All three variants returned byte-identical output:

| variant | ms/frame | vs current |
|---|---|---|
| current | 9.84 | 1.0x |
| pre-sized `Uint8Array`, no prefilter, no atob | 3.56 | 2.8x |
| **`atob` + `charCodeAt` copy (this PR)** | **2.24** | **4.4x** |

Two corrections, because the issue's estimate was wrong and I would rather flag that than repeat it:

- #4876 quoted ~7x for the atob route, from a desktop-class Hermes CLI. On the simulator's Hermes it is 4.4x.
- **These came from a Debug bundle**, where Hermes compiles at runtime without `-O`, so read 4.4x as an upper bound. The direction is still safe: Hermes has no JIT, so optimised bytecode is still interpreted while `atob` is native. The split shows which half is at risk — old → pre-sized (2.8x) is JS-vs-JS and sensitive to compilation quality; pre-sized → atob (1.6x) is interpreted-vs-native and is not.

I did not measure a release build. Doing that properly means putting benchmark code in the app, which does not belong in this PR — say the word if you want the number before merging.

## Changes

- `base64ToBytes` → `atob` plus a pre-sized `Uint8Array`.
- `bytesToBase64` keeps its lookup table. It runs once per input event, not once per frame, so it never sees the sizes that motivate the change; switching it would mean adopting the desktop's chunked `String.fromCharCode` spread, whose argument-count limit is engine-dependent, for no gain on that path.
- Both are exported so they can be tested. `lib/mux.test.ts` is this module's first test.

## The one behaviour change

`atob` throws where the old loop silently pre-filtered. `handle` is called *outside* the `JSON.parse` guard in `ws.onmessage`, so a throw would escape the socket callback — `base64ToBytes` is therefore total, and a payload it cannot read yields an empty frame.

The daemon cannot send one: terminal output has a single encode site (`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:449`, `base64.StdEncoding`), which structurally cannot emit whitespace or line breaks.

It drops silently because the `JSON.parse` guard directly above it is `catch { return; }`, also silent — warning here but not there would be inconsistent, and the case is unreachable from the daemon. Happy to add a `__DEV__` warn if you would rather have the breadcrumb.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx expo export` bundles on **ios and android** — CI runs only `npm ci` → typecheck → `npm test`, so nothing upstream catches a Metro-level break.
- `npx vitest run`, in a clean worktree off `main`: **787 → 802** (+15).
- **Revert test.** Restoring the old decoder (keeping the exports, so the tests still import) fails **1 of 15**: the empty-frame case. The other 14 pass on *both* implementations by design — they pin the wire contract, which must stay byte-identical. Saying so rather than implying all 15 catch the change.
- Fixtures are Go `base64.StdEncoding` output, not `bytesToBase64` output, so the encoder and its test cannot drift together unnoticed.
- **Hermes, not Node.** vitest runs on Node, which proves nothing about the shipping engine, so every `atob` case in the file was re-run on the simulator's Hermes over CDP:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| `typeof atob` | `"function"` |
| `atob("QU\nJD")`, `atob("QU JD")` | `[65,66,67]` — whitespace stripped |
| `atob("not base64!")`, `atob("QQ=")` | both throw |
| `atob("QQ")` unpadded | `[65]` |
| `atob("ABtbMzFt//5/gAo=")` | `[0,27,91,51,49,109,255,254,127,128,10]` |

## Not verified

- **iOS simulator only.** Hermes is pinned once for both platforms in this RN (`sdks/.hermesversion` → `hermes-v0.17.03`, RN 0.86.3), so the `atob` semantics are not iOS-specific — but Android was checked by `expo export`, not by running it.
- **No physical device, no release build** (above).
- **No renderer in `packages/mobile`** — 79 `*.test.ts`, zero `*.test.tsx` — so `handle`'s dispatch to `onTerminalData` is covered by reading, not by running.

# Bug 反馈：Codex 登录成功但在软件中显示“Codex account setup did not complete”

## Summary
Bug 反馈：Codex 登录成功但在软件中显示“Codex account setup did not complete”

## Details
### 1. 现象 (What Happened)

 已通过官方浏览器完成 Codex 登录，本地 codex doctor 均正常，但在 Agent Orchestrator 设置中仍显示 0 个账户，并报错：

 ▏ Codex account setup did not complete（底层错误代码：account_storage_unsafe，HTTP 503）

 ### 2. 期望结果 (Expected)

 软件自动读取本地已有的 Codex 登录凭据（~/.codex/auth.json），正常显示可用账户与额度信息。

 ### 3. 复现步骤 (Reproduction)

 1. 在 Windows 终端运行 codex login，在浏览器完成授权。
 2. 运行 codex doctor，确认本地授权正常（stored ChatGPT tokens: [redacted-secret]
 3. 启动 Agent Orchestrator，打开 Settings -> Accounts。
 4. 观察到界面弹出错误 Codex account setup did not complete，Codex 列表显示 0 个账户。

 ### 4. 根因简述 (Root Cause)

 Windows 权限校验冲突：
 - 官方 Codex 客户端会自动给 ~/.codex 目录添加 CodexSandboxUsers 沙箱用户组。
 - AO 内部的安全策略为强白名单（仅允许当前用户、SYSTEM、Admin），检测到该沙箱组后判定路径“不安全”，直接熔断锁定该模块。

title: fix(reviews): stop probing every reviewer's CLI when the menu opens
body:
Fixes #5307

## What was wrong

`ReviewerSelect` prefetched a model catalog for **every** selectable reviewer harness the moment the menu opened. That read is not free: the daemon answers a cold catalog with the agent's own CLI, so a single menu-open ran the binary of all 21 reviewer harnesses — including agents the user was not choosing and had never signed in to.

For Kiro that discovery command is its **chat entrypoint**:

```go
// backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go:58
"kiro": {args: []string{"chat", "--list-models", "--format", "json"}, parser: parseJSONModels},
```

which is how picking an unrelated reviewer could pop a Kiro OAuth sign-in in the reporter's browser.

## What changed

Only the harness in effect is read up front — the trigger label needs it anyway. Each option now fetches its own catalog if and when its submenu is opened. Clicking a harness that is *not* the current one selects it outright rather than opening its submenu, so the common path needs no extra read at all.

One menu-open goes from 21 catalog reads to 1.

## Tests

New `ReviewerSelect.test.tsx` counts which agents a menu interaction reads catalogs for. Two of the four fail on `main` with exactly the reported shape:

```
× does not read a catalog for harnesses the user is not choosing
× reads a harness catalog once its own submenu is opened
  AssertionError: expected [ 'claude-code', 'codex', …(19) ] to not include 'kiro'
```

All four pass here. The other two guard the reads that *should* still happen (the harness in effect; a submenu the user deliberately opened) so this cannot be "fixed" by removing catalog reads altogether.

Also run: `npm run typecheck` clean; renderer suite `207 passed / 3203 passed`, matching `main` exactly plus the 4 added tests. The one remaining renderer failure (`GlobalSettingsForm > renders the settings sections`) reproduces on unmodified `main`.

## Scope / what this does not do

This narrows what a **passive** menu probes. It does not change what an explicitly chosen or launched agent may do — selecting Kiro as your reviewer still reads its catalog, and so may still trigger a sign-in.

Two deeper questions are left open and written up on the issue rather than guessed at here:

- Kiro's discovery command being `chat` rather than a dedicated subcommand. Fixing that needs someone who can verify `kiro-cli`'s actual surface.
- Gating discovery on the adapter's existing side-effect-free auth probe (`kiro-cli whoami`). That looked attractive but its effectiveness is unproven — [#5048](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5048) documents that probe returning `unknown` for a genuinely signed-in user, so a gate keyed on it may simply not fire.

title: fix(electron): return cancellation results for aborted browser commands
body:
## Summary
- When the Electron browser runtime link reconnects or disposes, emit `BROWSER_COMMAND_CANCELED` result frames for every accepted command (including queued per-session work) before tearing down the socket.
- Handle daemon-initiated `cancel` frames by returning a structured cancellation result instead of silently dropping the response.
- Tear down on socket `end` as well as `close`, and clear `activeCommands` before aborting controllers to avoid duplicate cancellation frames.

## Problem
If the daemon-to-Electron browser bridge dropped while a command was in flight, the frontend aborted locally but never told the daemon the command failed. The broker kept waiting on the pending request until TCP disconnect was detected or the command timed out.

## Test plan
- [x] `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/main/browser-runtime-link.test.ts` (6 tests pass)
- [ ] Verify `ao browser wait` recovers promptly after restarting the desktop app mid-command

title: fix(electron): bound browser profile data operation waits
body:
## Summary
- Add a 60s timeout (`BROWSER_PROFILE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS`) for profile clear/delete work and for browser commands waiting on that queue in `ensureSessionReady()`.
- Wrap Electron `clearStorageData` / `clearCache` with the same bound so a stuck storage call cannot hold the profile operation queue forever.
- Fail with `BROWSER_PROFILE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` instead of leaving automation hung for the session.

## Problem
Before running a browser command, the desktop app waits in a `for (;;)` loop until bound profile clear/delete operations finish. That wait had no timeout. If profile data work stalled (for example on Electron session storage APIs), `ensureSessionReady()` and every subsequent browser command for that session would wait indefinitely.

## Test plan
- [x] `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/main/browser-profile-store.test.ts` (8 tests pass, including new timeout case)
- [x] Added `browser-view-host` regression test for stuck profile-operation wait (runs in CI)
- [ ] Manually start a profile clear, simulate a hang, and confirm `ao browser snapshot` fails within ~60s with `BROWSER_PROFILE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` instead of hanging

title: fix(kiro): never run the model-discovery CLI while signed out
body:
Fixes #5307 · Refs #5048

## The problem

Listing an agent's models executes that agent's own CLI. Kiro's discovery command is its **chat entrypoint**:

```go
// backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go:58
"kiro": {args: []string{"chat", "--list-models", "--format", "json"}, parser: parseJSONModels},
```

With no Kiro session that command starts a browser OAuth sign-in, so simply rendering a picker could open `app.kiro.dev/signin`.

Verified directly against the installed `kiro-cli 2.21.0`, with an isolated `HOME` and a stubbed browser opener (no real browser was launched, no account touched):

```
$ kiro-cli chat --list-models --format json      # signed out
⠿ Opening browser... | Press (^) + C to cancel
```

## Why not just ask Kiro not to open a browser

There is no way to. I checked all three:

| Avenue | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A `--no-browser` flag | `chat --help` has none |
| An env var | Only `KIRO_AUTH_PORTAL_URL` and autosuggest/router vars — no browser or headless switch |
| `--no-interactive` | **Tested — still opens the browser** |

So AO has to decline the run.

## Which needed a working auth probe first

`kiro-cli whoami --format json` reports:

```
signed out:  {"account":null}
signed in:   {"accountType":"IamIdentityCenter","email":"…", …}
             \n\nProfile:\nKiroProfile-…      <- plain text, so the whole payload is not valid JSON
```

Neither contains a phrase `authprobe.StatusFromText` matches, so **both states classified as `unknown`** — the probe could never distinguish them. (The signed-in half of that is [#5048](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5048); the signed-out half is measured here.) This decodes the leading JSON value instead, skipping the trailer.

## The gate

Discovery now skips the command for an agent that positively reports signed out, returning the cached, shared, or manual catalog through the **existing** discovery-failure path — so the fallback behavior is the one already in place and tested — with a warning explaining why and `RefreshRecommended` set.

Only an explicit `Unauthorized` blocks. `unknown` is not a denial: treating it as one would silently disable model listing for every adapter whose probe is imprecise — which, before this change, was Kiro itself in both states.

An explicit `kiro-cli login`, and launching Kiro as a worker or reviewer, are untouched.

## Tests

Both new files fail on `main` with exactly the reported shape:

```
--- FAIL: TestKiroWhoamiAuthStatus/signed_out_reports_unauthorized
        status = "unknown", want "unauthorized"
--- FAIL: TestKiroWhoamiAuthStatus/signed_in_reports_authorized_despite_the_non-JSON_profile_trailer
        status = "unknown", want "authorized"
--- FAIL: TestSignedOutAgentNeverRunsItsDiscoveryCommand
        discovery ran 1 times for a signed-out agent, want 0
```

The probe cases use the verbatim payloads above. The gate tests assert the negative (signed out ⇒ `Discover` never called) **and** both positives (signed in ⇒ called; `unknown` or a failed probe ⇒ still called), so this cannot be satisfied by disabling discovery.

Run locally: `go build ./...` clean; `go vet` clean; `golangci-lint` **0 issues**; `kiro`, `service/agent`, `authprobe`, `modelcatalog` packages all pass.

## Relationship to PR #5310

Independent, and this is the one that closes #5307. [#5310](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5310) stops the reviewer menu probing all 21 harnesses — worth having on its own merits, but it does not prevent the sign-in, since hovering Kiro would still trigger it. This does, whichever route reaches discovery. They do not conflict.

title: fix(terminal): prevent Claude titles from becoming false drafts
body:
Code changes: +95 -1  
Tests: +141 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## Problem and fix

After a Claude Terminal reply, **TUI → Chat could fail with `DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT` even though the composer was empty**.

Claude emits an OSC window-title update containing `✳` (`E2 9C B3`). AO's passive VT parser misreads the UTF-8 byte `9C` as String Terminator and paints the remaining title into the composer. The draft guard then rejects that fake text.

Strip only **OSC 0/1/2 title payloads**, introduced by either `ESC ]` or C1 `0x9D`, from passive capture. Keep escape boundaries, raw PTY replay, the visible terminal, and every draft/history guard unchanged. Real unsent drafts must still block switching. No dependency upgrade or history-recovery changes.

Closes #5301.

## C1 OSC review follow-up — `48d5cbc5f`

Addressed [the review's 8-bit OSC bypass](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5322#discussion_r3999115730). A standalone `0x9D` now enters the same title filter as `ESC ]`. UTF-8 continuation tracking also covers text outside titles, so Unicode containing that byte is not mistaken for OSC.

The new regression failed before the patch: an empty prompt became `Draft`, and a real draft was overwritten by title text. It now passes for OSC 0/1/2, BEL/7-bit ST/8-bit ST, every two-chunk split and byte-at-a-time delivery. Tests also preserve real drafts, UTF-8 text, non-title OSC examples and partial ESC/CSI cancellation.

This follow-up changes only the filter and two test files: **code +30 −19; tests +66 −5**. No dependency, renderer, raw PTY, draft-guard or history-recovery changes.

<summary>Independent code-review results at 671694237</summary>

## Standards

No remaining actionable standards violations or baseline smells against `cadde8c9f`. Preserving OSC boundaries fixes cancellation of preceding partial ESC/CSI sequences; the rendered-state regression and focused filter/surface tests pass.

No remaining actionable spec or correctness findings. The rendered partial ESC/CSI regressions retain the complete draft. Conpty, Claude adapter and terminalui tests pass; raw replay and draft/history gates remain unchanged.

title: feat(daemon): generic Windows .cmd/.bat launch for worker and reviewer harnesses (umbrella)
body:
## Problem

We have no generic way to launch a Windows `.cmd`/`.bat` shim for agent harnesses. Every npm-installed harness ships as a `.cmd` shim, not a `.exe`, so installs that only have the shim fail detection or launch. Each harness PR re-litigates this from scratch; PR #5267 is the latest example: it deliberately excludes `.cmd` shim launching because the launch mechanics don't exist yet.

What's missing:

1. Supervised launch (`pty-host` → `agent-process supervise`) can't spawn a `.cmd` child; it needs the `cmd.exe /d /s /c` wrapping, quoting rules, process ownership, and ConPTY lifecycle done once, generically.
2. Binary resolution and identity validation treat non-`.exe` candidates as unlaunchable, so shim-only installs report "not installed" or stay undetected even when identity checking would confirm them.

## Related work

- #3409: Codex resolver prefers `codex.cmd` over `codex.exe`, and supervise can't launch `.cmd`. Covers the Codex slice plus launch mechanics.
- #3504: reviewer terminals invisible on Windows because ConPTY can't spawn `.cmd` reviewer binaries.
- #5269: closed as completed on Sep 12 by nikhilachale, but no commit or merged PR references it; #5267 is still open. The goose `.cmd` detection gap may not actually be fixed. Needs re-verification.

## Scope

- Build one shared `.cmd`/`.bat` launch path (wrapping, quoting, ownership, ConPTY lifecycle) in the supervised chain.
- Make binary resolution + identity validation accept shim candidates once the launch path can exec them.
- Fold in the Codex-specific work from #3409.
- Re-open or re-verify #5269; re-add `.cmd` candidates per harness (goose, codex, reviewer binaries) with identity validation enabled.

## Non-goals

- Per-harness shell scripting beyond what the shared wrapper provides.
- POSIX changes; macOS/Linux launch already works.

title: [Feature]: Implement Crush native hook support for activity state mapping
body:
### Problem

The `Crush` agent adapter currently lacks support for emitting granular activity states to the UI timeline. Because of this, the dashboard cannot accurately display what the Crush agent is currently doing (e.g. `thinking`, `executing_command`, `idle`) compared to the other supported agents. Users observing a Crush-backed worker session are left without clear contextual awareness of the agent's current background execution state. 

*(Note: There is already an explicit `TODO(crush): Implement activity state mapping once Crush has native hook support.` left in the codebase at `backend/internal/adapters/agent/crush/activity.go:51`).*

### Proposed direction

1. Update the `Crush` adapter to install native lifecycle hooks that tie into the agent's runtime, similarly to how the other adapters handle their internal lifecycle events.
2. Resolve the `TODO` in `activity.go` by mapping the new Crush hook events (e.g., tool execution, prompt generation, waiting for user input) to the standard domain activity states so they broadcast correctly over the WebSocket to the frontend's timeline components.

### Alternatives considered

We could theoretically poll the terminal output or rely on standard `stdout` regex scraping to determine the Crush agent's state. However, this is extremely brittle and inconsistent with the orchestrator's architecture, as most other modern adapters in the codebase are transitioning to (or already use) standard native lifecycle hooks to securely and deterministically broadcast state changes.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

When provisioning an e2e testing pod, the bootstrap script currently has to pull down and install dependencies like `xvfb`, `tmux`, and `@playwright/test` on the fly. This increases cold boot times for testing environments, wastes bandwidth, and makes CI runs more brittle to network flakes.

*(Note: There is a comment tracking this optimization left in the codebase at `test/e2e-pod/boot-real.sh:29`: `# TODO: bake xvfb/tmux/@playwright/test into the Daytona snapshot.`)*

### Proposed direction

1. Update the base Daytona snapshot image configuration used for the e2e-pod to pre-install `xvfb`, `tmux`, and the `@playwright/test` node modules globally.
2. Remove the manual on-the-fly installation steps from `test/e2e-pod/boot-real.sh` to speed up the boot process and ensure environment consistency across runs.

### Alternatives considered

We could leave the script as is and rely on a local pull-through cache for the npm packages and apt dependencies. However, since these dependencies are completely static across e2e runs, baking them directly into the environment snapshot is the standard and most performant approach for Daytona/Devcontainer setups.

title: fix(frontend): offer merge when the provider requires no review
body: ## What In a repository that does not require reviews, a PR authored and reviewed from the same GitHub account showed **Review pending** and **Not mergeable yet** in the session inspector, and AO hid the Merge action. The PR card now reads **No review required**, reports the PR as **Mergeable**, and offers **Merge**, which is what the daemon's merge gate already allowed. ## Why Fixes #4935. GitHub never records a self-review as `APPROVED`, so in a single-user repository the review decision stays empty (`reviewDecision: ""`), which AO stores as `none`. `none` means GitHub requires no review: a branch protection rule or ruleset that requires one makes GitHub return `REVIEW_REQUIRED` and `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` instead. The daemon already treats `none` as satisfied. `domain.MergeReadiness.ReadyToMerge`, which `POST /api/v1/prs/{id}/merge` checks against a fresh fetch, only blocks on requested changes, unresolved human comments, CI and provider mergeability. The renderer did not: - `SessionInspector` offered Merge only for `review.decision === "approved"`. - `prCardPresentation` labelled a PR Mergeable only when approved, otherwise "A required review must be completed before this PR can merge." - `reviewStatusDetail` fell through to **Review pending** for `none`. The "Review pending" in the report is that renderer string, not the backend `review_pending` session status, which only `review_required` produces. ## How - **One rule for the label and the button.** `prCanMerge()` in `lib/pr-display.ts` mirrors `ReadyToMerge`: open, checks passing, provider mergeability `mergeable`, review decision `approved` or `none`, and no unresolved human review comments. `prCardPresentation` and `SessionInspector` both use it. - **`none` reads "No review required"** (new `pr.review.notRequired`, all 8 locales). - **Two consequences of sharing the rule**, both matching what the daemon already enforces: - An approved PR the provider reports as `blocked` or `unstable` is no longer labelled Mergeable. The detail reuses `pr.merge.providerBlocked`. - A PR with unresolved human review threads no longer shows Merge; clicking it used to fail with `PR_PRECONDITIONS_UNMET`. This matters for #4935 specifically: the AO reviewer posts inline comments from the author's own account, so they count as human. The reason is a new `pr.merge.reasonComments`, kept in English in every locale like the other `pr.merge.reason*` strings. - **No backend behaviour change.** `TestActionServiceMerge_MergesAPRThatNeedsNoReview` pins the daemon side so the two cannot drift apart. **Scope.** This does not treat AO's own review verdict as an approval and does not relax any provider blocker. #2073 was closed on the basis that AO should keep respecting required reviews and merge blockers; this change only acts where GitHub itself reports that no review is required. ### Intentional omissions Found while tracing #4935; each is a separate problem: - **`ao pr merge ` cannot succeed.** The CLI posts `{}`, and since #3599 the merge endpoint rejects a body without `prUrl` and `expectedHeadSha` with 400 `INVALID_PR`. That, not an approval check, is why the CLI refused in the report. Fixing it means deciding how the CLI supplies the head SHA it expects to merge. - **A repository with no CI checks never becomes mergeable in AO.** With no status rollup the CI state is `unknown`, which both the card and `ReadyToMerge` treat as a blocker. If the reporter's repository has no workflows at all, this PR alone does not unblock them. - **AO's own inline review comments count as human comments.** `review_comments` in `pr.sql` lacks the `review_run` exclusion that `external_comments` has, so they block merge until resolved. - **Existing copy left as is:** `pr.merge.reasonConflict` says "One approval is sufficient…" whatever the review requirement. ## Testing ### Before and after The same PR state in both: open, checks passing, GitHub mergeable, no review decision. These are the real Session inspector rendered in the renderer harness (`dev:web` with `installFakeAgent`), with the PR summary served for a placeholder `acme/notes-app#7`, not a live GitHub PR. None of the commits on `main` since the before capture touch the PR card. | Before (`main`) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | | | | | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Review status | Review pending | **No review required** | | Readiness | Not mergeable yet: "A required review must be completed before this PR can merge." | **Mergeable**: "No merge conflict, checks are passing, and the review requirement is satisfied." | | Merge button | Hidden | **Shown** | ### New tests Each renderer test below failed before its change. - `pr-display.test.ts`: a `none` PR is Mergeable and reads "No review required"; `blocked` and `unstable` PRs are not Mergeable; `approved` and `none` PRs with unresolved human comments are not Mergeable. `review_required` and `changes_requested` stay not Mergeable (these passed before too and guard the rule). - `SessionInspector.test.tsx`: Merge is offered for a `none` PR without "Review pending"; not offered for `review_required`, `changes_requested`, or unresolved human comments. - `action_service_test.go`: the daemon merges a PR whose decision is `none` with only a `COMMENTED` review (passes on `main` too; it pins existing behaviour). ### CI jobs run locally Run on `f79eca38c`, rebased onto `cadde8c9f`. - **Go** (`golang:1.25.7` container, `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` resolving to go1.26.5 as `go.work` requires): gofmt, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean. `go test -race -timeout=15m ./...`: 167 packages ok, including `internal/service/pr`. 2 packages failed, neither touched here, both explained by the container rather than this change: - `internal/mobilebridge` write-failure tests: the run was as root, which ignores the read-only permissions they rely on. Re-run as uid 1001, the package passes on this branch and on `cadde8c9f`. - `internal/adapters/agent/fake` `TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination` ("read hook log … no such file or directory"): fails identically on `cadde8c9f` in the same `golang` image, so I have not verified it locally; CI is the check for this one. - **golangci-lint** v2.12.2: 0 issues - **sqlc drift** and **api drift** (`npm run sqlc`, `npm run api`): no diff - **gitleaks** v7.4.0 (pinned digest) over the 3 commits in this PR: no leaks - **Frontend test job** (`node:24` container, non-root): cloud-client and product-ui verify, browser-runtime prepare, landing icons check, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, `npx vitest run`: **4,497 passed**, 6 skipped, 0 failed - **Renderer smoke** (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble` container, uid 1001, Node 24.21.0): `npm run typecheck:e2e` clean, `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: **59 passed** ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(cloud): coder and terminal hardening deployed on staging (follow-up to #5023)
body:
## What

The cloud fixes that are deployed and tested on the staging control plane (task-def :102) but were not part of #5023. This lands exactly the deployed CP state on top of #5023.

## Commits (all cloud/ or cloud-gated frontend)

- perf(cloud): launch preinstalled Coder worker, plus make the Coder harness link idempotent (was PR #4795, cherry-picked here).
- fix(cloud): stage the non-empty-workspace checkout inside the workspace (coder checkout-permission fix).
- fix(cloud): three coder UX fixes (terminal reconnect storm, empty-repo race, report fan-in) plus migration 00037 (allow queued fan-in turns).
- fix(cloud): state-driven cloud terminal attach (remove SSE-wait and timeout hacks), plus two earlier terminal iterations that net into it.
- fix(cloud-worker): boot the agent PTY at 80x24 instead of 120x40 so the intro banner never garbles.
- fix(cloud): close a superseded epoch's terminals at retire so stale terminals reconnect state-driven, with no liveness poll.
- fix(cloud): orchestrator inspects before spawn; workers report tersely (see Orchestration fixes below).

## Orchestration fixes (from a live 10-worker run on project l-a, lottie-android)

Two agent-guidance bugs surfaced by the run, fixed in the orchestrator/worker system prompts and the using-ao skill (both compile into ao-worker):

1. Inspect before spawn. The orchestrator invented file names when decomposing a task, so two workers were handed paths that do not exist in the repo (AnimationValueCallback.java, PathInterpolator.java) and blocked with no PR. The orchestrator prompt now requires confirming a file, class, or path exists in the checkout before naming it in a worker prompt.

2. Terse worker reports. Worker ao report messages were multi-paragraph, so a long one landed in the orchestrator conversation looking like an injected prompt. Reports are now constrained to one or two sentences (outcome plus PR number, or the single blocking reason) with no diffs, logs, or file contents.

command_test asserts both rules. Neither touches local-app behavior.

## Testing

Deployed on staging as ao-cloud-staging-api:102 and exercised end to end (coder + nodeops). cloud module gofmt, build, vet, and test are green; no cloud-client codegen drift. The orchestration fixes ride the ao-worker binary, so a CP redeploy propagates them to workers via self-update.

## Notes

- Adds migration 00037.
- Supersedes #4795, which should be closed (its commits are included here).
- All changes are cloud path or cloud-gated; no local-app behavior change.

Follow-up to #5023.


## Resume reliability fixes (added)

Four cloud resume/terminal reliability fixes, cherry-picked as clean commits:

1. Restore terminal 410 (TERMINAL_SESSION_EXITED) handling in the state-driven mux. The state-driven redesign dropped it, so an exited-agent 410 looped the ticket mint (stuck "Connecting"). This restores it.
2. Auto-rebake the coder workspace image on deploy, so the baked ao-worker SHA always matches the control plane and resumes skip the slow PTY upload.
3. Coder HTTP self-heal on a preinstalled-worker miss: fetch the correct worker over HTTP before falling back to the slow PTY upload.
4. Keep a resuming coder box alive through an idle-stop race, so a slow restore is not idle-killed mid bring-up.

Note: the backend false-positive 410 fix is a separate PR (#5477) because it corrects #5350 code that lives in main, not in this branch.

title: bug(docs-site): download page shows Intel button on Apple Silicon Macs
body:
## Bug

On an Apple Silicon Mac the download page's main Desktop button says "Download for macOS (Intel)" and links the x64 dmg. Wrong file for the machine, and the label makes M-series users think there is no native build.

**Source:** [Discord #bug-triage](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1548657412125491401) | **Reported by:** @somewherelostt | **Analyzed against:** `a33d1ac40`
**Confidence:** High on the code path, Medium on the exact trigger (reporter's browser unknown)

![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/main/.issue-assets/download-page-intel-mseries/maaz-download-page.jpeg)

## Reproduction

1. Open the download page on an M-series Mac.
2. The Desktop card button reads "Download for macOS (Intel)" and downloads `agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.dmg`.
3. The correct "Mac (Apple silicon)" dmg is only listed further down under Stable.

## Root cause

`detectMacArch()` in `frontend/src/landing/src/app/hooks/useOS/useOS.ts` picks the arch from one signal: the WebGL `UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL` string. No "apple" in it means the Mac gets classified Intel.

That fails on Apple Silicon whenever the GPU string is missing or masked: Safari with locked-down settings, some privacy extensions, or software rendering. Each of those shows an Intel button on M-series hardware. The fallback direction is also backwards for this audience: when in doubt, arm64 is the safer guess.

## Fix

Treat the WebGL string as a hint, not proof. Add a second signal, e.g. `navigator.userAgentData` high-entropy `architecture` in Chromium or a WebAssembly feature probe, and default to Apple Silicon when signals disagree or are missing. Also consider showing both Mac downloads instead of one best-guess button, so a misdetection can never hand a user the wrong dmg.

## Impact

M-series users get pointed at the x64 dmg, which needs Rosetta or fails to make sense at install time. First impression is "no native build for my Mac".

title: Feature request: ZCode (Z.ai / GLM official coding agent) as a supported harness
body:
## Summary

Please consider adding **ZCode** (Zhipu/Z.ai's official coding agent for GLM models) as a supported harness, alongside Claude Code / Codex / opencode etc.

## Why

- ZCode is the official agent runtime for GLM coding plans (open.bigmodel.cn) — a fast-growing user base, especially among GLM coding-plan subscribers.
- Users running mixed setups (e.g. Claude Code + ZCode) currently can't supervise ZCode sessions on the AO Kanban, since AO only shows sessions it spawned itself.
- Official runtimes usually get better serving/QoS from their own provider, so having the official GLM agent as a first-class harness is attractive for GLM users.

## Current blocker (to be transparent)

As of today ZCode ships as a desktop app (Electron) with a built-in automation/cron system, but **no standalone headless CLI binary** — which harness integration would presumably need (spawn per session, stream turns, resume). So part of this request is also tracking demand so it's ready when Z.ai ships a CLI.

## Ask

1. Any interest / roadmap position for a ZCode harness?
2. If Z.ai ships a headless CLI (or ACP support), would a community PR adding the harness be welcome? Happy to help test.

Thanks for the great project — the live Kanban + worker supervision is a joy.

title: feat(chat): support /compact for Claude Code and ACP providers
body:
## What

Implements `/compact` in Chat UI for Claude Code and all ACP-based providers (`claudeacp`, `cursoracp`, `opencodeacp`, etc.) using the official Agent Client Protocol (ACP) session compaction specification.

## Why

Compaction was previously only available for Codex via its private JSON-RPC method (`thread/compact/start`). For Claude Code and other ACP agents, `/compact` was unavailable in Chat UI.

## How

- **Capability Negotiation**: Negotiates `session.compaction: {}` under `ClientCapabilities.Meta` during ACP initialization per the official ACP Session Compaction specification.
- **Provider Capability Exposure**:
  - `claudeacp` advertises `ports.ChatCapabilityCompaction: true` so the Chat UI exposes the `/compact` command.
  - Generic `acp` driver dynamically enables `ports.ChatCapabilityCompaction: true` when any ACP agent advertises the `compact` available command.
- **Managed Compaction Turn**:
  - Implements `ports.ChatCompactor` on `*conversation`.
  - Dispatches `/compact` asynchronously as a managed prompt turn.
  - Suppresses intermediate `agent_message_chunk` and `agent_thought_chunk` deltas during the compaction turn so the timeline does not get polluted with raw assistant chatter.
  - Calculates token reclaim metrics (`tokensBefore`, `tokensAfter`, `tokensReclaimed`, `contextWindow`) from usage updates and emits `ports.ChatEventCompacted`.

title: feat(onboarding): infer worker and orchestrator defaults from role-specific usage
body:
Fixes #4493.

## Problem
New-project onboarding computed one generic authorized-agent default and assigned it to both Worker and Orchestrator, ignoring role-specific session history. Both fields commonly opened as Claude Code.

## Root cause
The sheet only consulted the agent-readiness catalog. It had no role-filtered usage signal, so both untouched fields received the same catalog-priority result.

## Fix
- Subscribe the sheet to the shared workspace query while open and flatten local session history (this sheet creates local projects only; cloud uses CloudProjectCard).
- Rank eligible agents independently per role by usage count in the last 48 hours (ROLE_HISTORY_WINDOW_MS), then newest matching session, then the existing Claude Code-first priority order. A heavy harness from months ago can no longer outvote current habits; undated sessions are excluded since their age is unknown.
- Role matching reuses isOrchestratorSession, so legacy -orchestrator ids and kind-less sessions behave exactly like the board. Its parameter is widened to a Pick; no caller changes.
- Touched-field protection is unchanged: async refreshes never overwrite a manual selection.
- Removes the now-unused single-default defaultAuthorizedAgent.

## Safety
- Suggestion-only; saved project configuration and session history are untouched.
- Unavailable historical harnesses are never selected; empty or stale history falls back to Claude Code, or the next authorized agent when Claude Code is unavailable.

## Verification
- Targeted suites: 21 passed (agent-select-options, CreateProjectAgentSheet).
- Neighbors (CreateProjectFlow, TaskComposer): 39 passed.
- Full frontend suite: 3589 passed; the only failures are 12 pre-existing better-sqlite3 native-binding errors in src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts, untouched by this change.
- npm run typecheck: clean.
- Perf probe of the real function: 0.014ms at 100 sessions, 0.093ms at 1000, 0.87ms at 10000.

title: fix: preserve session status through daemon restarts
body: Code changes: +282 -40 Tests: +483 -23 Others: +47 -17 ## What Keep session status and board order stable while the daemon reconnects to surviving agents. The board waits for startup recovery; a failed or timed-out check shows **Unable to verify** with **Retry status check**. ## Why A live Chat reconnect reused the fresh-spawn lifecycle transition, which reset activity to idle and advanced `updatedAt`. Claiming a new controller generation also advanced that timestamp. The UI displayed these intermediate records immediately, and its normal attention/recency sort moved cards as the records changed. ## How - Carry the driver's confirmed live-reconnect flag through Chat startup. Validate provider/controller ownership and preserve existing activity, first-signal metadata, and recency for the same surviving provider. Cold launches retain their spawn transition. - Remove the recency write from controller-generation claims and regenerate SQL bindings. - Expose ephemeral `checking` / `ready` / `unavailable` recovery readiness. Fence API snapshots against recovery changes, bound checks to 30 seconds for context-aware dependencies, and offer retry only after the protected recovery path releases session ownership. - Hold the startup board loader while checks are pending, poll until resolved, and show explicit unverified labels and retry actions. The board comparator remains enabled. Subsequent real activity continues to update the board normally. ## Testing **Observed in the real Electron app:** ten disposable sessions, including a running Codex turn, across a daemon replacement. In 518 samples, 486 confirmed the same busy provider turn both before and after reading session status: **zero false Idle samples**. All nine untouched sessions retained their timestamps. The active session changed to Awaiting PR only when its turn completed. The full-board recording was reviewed and approved by the reporter. ### Visual proof **During restart:** the board remains behind the startup screen while session statuses are being verified. **After verification:** the board returns with the original card order and the active session still showing **Working**. Local validation on the PR commit (macOS arm64, Go 1.26.5 from `go.work`, Node 24.14.0): - Frontend and E2E typechecks; full Vitest suite: **313 files, 4,564 passed, 6 skipped**. - Renderer smoke: **59 passed** with `CI=true` and Chromium. - Product UI: typecheck, **128 tests**, build and package dry-run. Cloud client: generated-contract check, typecheck, **21 tests**, build and package dry-run. - Cloud Go: formatting, build, vet and full race suite. - Native macOS helper: configuration/repair tests, x64 and arm64 builds, and Swift state tests. - SQL/API regeneration and generated landing icons: clean. - Backend formatting, build, vet, **full race suite**, native CLI E2E and pinned `golangci-lint` v2.12.2 (**zero issues**). - Review follow-up: full Go suite, build, vet, frontend typecheck, pinned linter (**zero issues**), session-manager and SQLite store race suites, plus the isolated migration race test. The serialized full race run passed all other packages; the complete SQLite migration package exceeded its 10-minute package timeout under race instrumentation, while its timed-out test passed alone in 12.5 seconds. Remote CI: **all 14 checks passed** on the latest review-fix commit, including the Linux Go race suite, full frontend suite, Windows workspace tests, CLI E2E on Linux/macOS/Windows, fresh-install container, renderer smoke, macOS helper, lint, generated contracts, and secret scanning. Local platform gap: Docker's daemon/socket and native Windows/Linux runners were unavailable on this macOS host; the corresponding checks passed in CI. No release or deployment was run. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` - [x] One focused restart-status fix - [x] Follows repository architecture and generated-contract boundaries - [x] Regression coverage for live reconnect, recency, recovery failure/retry, read snapshots, and startup/card UI - [x] Relevant remote CI checks pass (14/14) on the latest commit
