title: [Bug]: File-tab language icon stays hidden after hover or interaction
body:
## What went wrong?

In the session file-tab bar, the language-specific file icon disappears when the tab is hovered. After moving the pointer away, the icon can remain hidden. Clicking or otherwise interacting with the tab also hides the icon, and it does not reappear until focus is moved by clicking elsewhere.

This is reproducible with language-aware file tabs such as `go.mod` and `go.sum`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session.
2. Open a source file so it appears in the file-tab bar.
3. Hover over the file tab and then move the pointer away.
4. Click or otherwise interact with the file tab, then move the pointer away.
5. Observe the language icon in the tab.

## Expected behavior

The language icon should remain visible, or at minimum return when the pointer leaves the tab. Clicking/selecting the tab should not leave the icon hidden.

## Attachments

### Screenshot

<!-- Drag and drop the screenshot here. Do not commit the screenshot to the repository. -->

_[Attach screenshot here]_

### Screen recording

<!-- Drag and drop the video here. Do not commit the recording to the repository. -->

_[Attach screen recording here]_

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected on 2026-09-14 from checkout commit `435f0b48dee3d455c3d2ec0f77446aa93a5a9032` by reviewing the supplied 9.5-second recording and tracing the renderer code.

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFileTabs.tsx` applies `group-hover:opacity-0 group-focus-within:opacity-0` to `WorkspaceEntryIcon`.
- The file tab itself is rendered as a button. A pointer click leaves that button focused, so the outer tab frame continues matching `:focus-within` after the pointer leaves. This explains why the icon remains at zero opacity until focus moves elsewhere.
- The inverse hover/focus classes make the close control visible while the language icon is hidden.
- The behavior was introduced in commit `aee10e0e75febc9a4d262250e2aacfbe1ed83ff9`; before that change, the file icon did not have hover/focus opacity rules.
- `SessionFileTabs.test.tsx` checks only that the icon exists in the DOM. An element with `opacity: 0` still satisfies that assertion, so the persistent-hidden state is not covered.

Duplicate search performed with GitHub issue and PR searches for “language icon tab hover,” “file icon disappears,” “file tab icon hover,” and “language icon disappears.” No matching issue was found.

title: fix: preload session usage before first Kanban render
body:
## Problem

On the first visit to a Kanban board after launching AO, session token/cost badges appear after the cards have already rendered. Navigating away and back does not reproduce the flash.

## Cause

The shell route preloads the workspace/session query, but the board starts `useSessionUsageSummaries(projectId)` only after `SessionsBoard` mounts. On a cold query cache, the board substitutes an empty usage map, renders cards without usage, and rerenders when `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions` completes.

Subsequent visits render cached usage immediately (including while a stale query refetches), which explains why this is first-visit-only.

The endpoint is moderately more expensive than the sessions endpoint because it aggregates persisted usage events by session, but there is no remote pricing lookup or heavy renderer-side calculation. In a representative local database with about 9,900 usage events, the request was typically around 25 ms with cold/contention spikes around 175 ms.

## Proposed fix

Make usage summaries a data dependency of both Kanban routes so the query cache is populated before `SessionsBoard` mounts:

- project board: preload the project-scoped usage summary
- all-sessions board: preload the all-project usage summary

Reuse `sessionUsageQueryOptions` so the route loader and component share the same cache key and query function.

## Acceptance criteria

- Token/cost badges are present on the Kanban's first rendered frame when usage exists.
- Project boards request project-scoped summaries.
- The all-sessions board requests all summaries.
- Later event-driven invalidation and background refresh behavior remains unchanged.

title: fix: show Kanban cost badges on the board's first frame
body:
## Summary

Kanban cards painted before their cost badge (for example `$0.92` next to "Awaiting PR"), and the cost filled in up to ~2s later. This PR makes the cost appear in the same frame as the cards:

- **Warm every board's usage before it's opened, with one request per host.** `warmSessionUsageSummaries` fetches the host-wide `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions` once and splits it into each project's board cache, using the sessions the workspace list already knows.
  - On a normal launch, local boards are warmed from the `_shell` loader, which never waits for it.
  - `ShellLayout` also warms whenever a host's project list becomes known: local once the workspace query succeeds, remote once that host's sessions load. This covers a daemon that becomes ready after the loader returned early, recovery fetches, new projects, and remote hosts. The effect is keyed on the project set, so streamed session updates don't re-run it, and overlapping warm-ups share one in-flight request.
  - Boards that already have data are skipped, including a board that loaded while the warm-up was in flight.
  - Seeded entries keep the response's timestamp, so a board opened later still refreshes once that data is older than 10 s.
  - A failed warm-up is a single attempt; the board's own query fetches (with its usual retry) when it opens.
- **Keep usage summaries cached across board visits** (`gcTime: Infinity` on `sessionUsageQueryOptions`). Before, React Query dropped the entry 5 minutes after the board unmounted, so every later visit painted the cards first again. Freshness is unchanged:
  - Usage writes (`ApplyUsageChunk`, `ApplyUsageCostUpdates`) touch `usage_bindings`, whose CDC trigger emits `session_updated`. The event transport then invalidates `sessionUsageQueryRoot`.
  - An open board refetches right away. A cached board shows its cached cost and refetches when it next mounts.
- **Remove the board route loaders** added earlier in this PR (see "Why the route loader was dropped").

Closes #5399

## Measurements

Real Electron dev app driven over CDP, isolated data: 111 sessions across 2 projects, 13.7k usage events on the measured board's project. "Cards" and "cost" are the first DOM frames with a card and with a `$` amount on the board. Times are ms from navigation, or from reload for cold reloads. Before and after were measured on the same data.

| Scenario | Before (main) | Route loader (previous head) | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| First board visit after launch | cards 368–423, cost **+276–287** | cards **774–796** (blank content until then), cost same frame | cards 367–419, cost **same frame** |
| Cold reload onto the board | cards 970–1037, cost **+385–427** | cards 1186–1358, cost **+320–440** | cards 990–1032, cost **same frame** |
| Revisit after the cache was collected | cards 213–258, cost **+160–270** | cards 170–240, cost **+165–195** | cards 249–338, cost **same frame** |
| Revisit after 5.5 real minutes away | (cache collected, as above) | (cache collected, as above) | entry kept, cost **on first frame** |

The route-loader column was measured earlier on the 91-session single-project lab.

Startup requests (2 projects): this PR sends exactly one `/usage/sessions` request. Opening each board shows its cost on the first frame, then refreshes that project in the background.

Where the gap came from (traced with React Query cache events and CDP network timing):
- **Not request queueing.** Each card's `/sessions/{id}/pr` takes about 2 ms, even on a real 122-session daemon.
- The usage response arrives 30–60 ms after it's sent, but React Query only gets it 200–400 ms later because the main thread is busy rendering 91 cards. A second full render then paints the cost.
- On a real daemon, the endpoint itself often takes 0.35–0.65 s (see Follow-up). That stacks on top of the above and is consistent with the reported ~2s. With this PR it's hidden: the cached cost renders immediately and the refetch runs in the background.

## Why the route loader was dropped

Disabling retries (the earlier review fix) removed the backoff stall, but measurement showed three structural problems:
1. **The first visit waits on the loader.** The router has `defaultPendingMs: 0` and the pending component renders nothing after startup, so the board's content area stays blank until usage resolves (~790 ms vs ~380 ms). That's the wait moved in front of the board, which is what broke the focus smoke spec.
2. **Revisits get nothing.** The router reuses the cached match and reruns the loader in the background, so cards still paint before the cost.
3. **Cold start gets nothing.** Child loaders run in parallel with the `_shell` daemon probe, so the usage loader runs before the API base URL exists and fails instantly with the synthesized 503.

## Tests

- `useSessionUsageSummaries.test.ts`:
  - one host-wide request fills every project board; the standalone workspace is skipped; empty projects get `[]`;
  - seeded entries carry the response's `dataUpdatedAt` (the test uses a ticking clock, and fails if the stamp is dropped);
  - remote hosts are warmed through `clientForHost`;
  - no request when every board is cached;
  - a board that loads mid-warm-up keeps its own data;
  - a failed warm-up is one attempt, leaves boards empty so they fetch themselves, and the board query keeps `retry: 1`;
  - `gcTime` is infinite.
- `shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx` (51/51):
  - the `_shell` loader resolves without waiting for the warm-up (the warm-up never settles in that test);
  - a daemon that becomes ready after the loader ran still warms local boards (fails on the previous shell code);
  - remote boards are warmed only after the host's sessions load, and not again for streamed session updates.
- `useSessionUsageSummaries.test.ts` also covers overlapping warm-ups sharing one request (9/9).
- 264 tests across the shell, board, archive, notification, memory and remote-workspace suites; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run typecheck:e2e`.
- Renderer smoke locally: 73/75 (`cross-platform-focus` 3/3). Both failures are in `chat-composer-text-selection`: the pointer-drag spec fails consistently on macOS and passed in CI on the previous push; the caret spec passes when rerun alone. `smoke-board`'s "narrow card status truncates" (`@BRD`, not in the CI smoke set) also fails locally on the previous head, without this change.
- Real Electron, same lab:
  - Cost updates while the board is open: a new usage event plus binding touch changed `$26.97` → `$31.97` within 3 s.
  - A change made while away shows on revisit.
  - Usage endpoint failing at startup: one warm-up attempt. Once it recovered, opening the board showed the cost 9 ms after the cards.
  - One startup request for two projects; both boards show cost on their first frame.
  - The cache survives 5.5 minutes away.
  - Late daemon: stopped the daemon, reloaded the renderer, then used **Restart daemon**. The previous push warmed nothing and the board's first frame had no cost; this PR warms both boards as soon as the daemon is ready, and the first frame shows the cost.
- Remote warm-up is covered by unit and shell tests only. Exercising it in the app needs a remote host's network listener, which I didn't open on this machine.

## Risks

- Usage summaries are no longer garbage-collected. There's one entry per project and host plus one host-wide entry, and they're small (~25 KB for 120 sessions).
- Seeding relies on the workspace list's session IDs. A session created after that snapshot emits `session_updated`, which marks the seeded entry stale, so the board refetches it on open.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The real daemon's 0.35–0.65 s for `/usage/sessions` is not daemon code. The handler is the SQL plus a JSON map. Sampled every 20 s on a 1.2 GB `ao.db`:
- The same SQL in a fresh `sqlite3` process took 0.40–0.80 s of wall time but only ~20 ms of CPU.
- The daemon, called right afterwards, took 28–115 ms.
- Through modernc (the daemon's driver): 390 ms cold, 21 ms warm.

The time is disk reads. The 13.9k `model_usage_events` rows are scattered across a database dominated by `conversation_provider_events` (~780 MB), and the OS evicts them from its file cache between visits on a memory-pressured machine. Possible backend fixes: a covering index for the compact aggregate, or a per-session usage rollup.

## What

Add a Chat driver for the user's installed GitHub Copilot CLI over native `copilot --acp`, registered alongside the other ACP bindings.

Copilot was TUI-only. Its CLI exposes ACP itself, so it can use the reusable ACP transport without AO bundling or scraping anything.

The generic ACP driver gains `LaunchSessionOptions` for config options fixed for the whole session; they are applied with the per-turn options so a provider that resets them recovers on the next turn.

## Problem

Two daemons pointed at the same data dir would both open the same SQLite database, risking corruption and confusing, hard-to-diagnose failures.

title: feat(attachments): add a lease lifecycle for staged attachments
body:
## Problem

Staged chat attachments had no ownership lifecycle. Files staged for a message that was never delivered were never reclaimed, leaking disk under the data dir over time.

## Fix

Add a lease lifecycle to the attachment store. Staging takes a lease recorded in a `.leases.json` manifest; a successful relay commits the lease; discard releases it; and expired leases (default TTL 24h) are garbage-collected on `RestoreAll`. The manifest access is mutex-guarded and covered by a concurrent race test.

Scope note: immediate frontend release on chip removal is not wired here. The leak is bounded by the 24h TTL plus GC on restart. Wiring an immediate release would need a new DELETE endpoint via the OpenAPI codegen and is left as a follow-up.

## Changes

- Code (+423): `backend/internal/attachmentstore/store.go`, `backend/internal/session_manager/{chat_attachments.go,chat_spawn.go,manager.go}`, `backend/internal/service/session/{attachments.go,service.go}`

title: fix: suppress false exit on planned shutdown and stabilize sidebar order
body:
## Problem

Two issues on daemon restart / controller reconnect: (1) a planned shutdown reported `ActivityExited`, flashing a false "exited" state on sessions that were only being closed normally, and (2) the sidebar sorted by `updatedAt`, which the backend bumps on every controller lifecycle event, so staggered reconnect waves visibly reshuffled the list.

## Fix

Backend: a planned controller `Close` (the only caller is `Service.StopAll`, used for shutdown) sets a `plannedStop` flag so `project()` suppresses the `ActivityExited` report; a genuine stream loss still reports exited. Frontend: the sidebar comparator sorts by the immutable `createdAt` (with `id` tiebreak) instead of `updatedAt`/`lastActivityAt`, so connectivity and activity churn can no longer reorder rows.

Behavior note for review: rows no longer bubble to the top on activity; ordering is now stable by creation. That is intentional per the issue but is a visible UX change.

title: feat(codex): installer-aware Codex CLI update flow
body:
## Problem

AO's "Codex CLI update available" story was not installer-aware. It could not tell whether the `codex` binary came from an npm global, Homebrew, or a standalone install, so it could not offer a correct update action; a generic command risks running the wrong install path and breaking the binary.

## Fix

Backend: a `CodexMaintenanceStatus` advisory resolves the live `codex` binary, classifies its ownership (npm prefix / Homebrew Cellar-Caskroom / standalone) with a pure, unit-tested classifier, compares installed vs latest, and produces an ownership-correct update command (or a manual-only reason). Two new endpoints (`GET /api/v1/agents/codex/maintenance`, `POST .../maintenance/update`) reuse the existing async job pipeline, with a 409 `CODEX_OWNERSHIP_CHANGED` guard against stale advisory state and a 60s server-side cache. Frontend: a `CodexMaintenanceRow` in the Codex settings section shows nothing when up to date, an "Update now" action when supported, live job progress, and a manual-only message otherwise. Localized across all 8 locales.

title: Qwen TUI to Chat handoff (AgentInterfaceHandoff)
body:
Qwen sessions are stuck in the interface they are born in. The tab toggle reports `INTERFACE_HANDOFF_UNSUPPORTED` because the Qwen TUI adapter does not implement `AgentInterfaceHandoff`. Codex, Claude Code, and OMP already do.

## Evidence it is buildable (Qwen 0.23.4, verified live)

- Qwen keeps one session store shared by TUI and ACP: `~/.qwen/projects/<hash>/chats/<uuid>.jsonl`.
- `session/load` with a TUI-created session id over raw ACP replayed the full transcript.
- `session/prompt` on the loaded session streamed a live reply. The adopted session is resumable, not a playback.
- Same shape as Codex, whose handoff works today: same native id on both surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Qwen TUI plugin implements `AgentInterfaceHandoff`: TUI side returns the hook-reported agent session id, Chat side returns the provider conversation id.
- [ ] Optional `NativeConversationExists` probe against `chats/<id>.jsonl` under `QWEN_HOME`, mirroring the Codex rollout walk.
- [ ] Handoff launch path loads (`session/load`) the native id instead of `session/new`.
- [ ] Mode mismatch handled: a yolo-born TUI session loaded into Chat must `set_mode` to the Chat settings and verify it, never silently stay permissive.
- [ ] Trust-gated folders: a silent `set_mode` failure must fail the switch, not leave a permissive session behind.
- [ ] Fresh sessions with no persisted file take the safe-fresh path via the history probe.
- [ ] Chat to TUI reverse (`--resume` on an ACP id) verified or explicitly scoped out.
- [ ] Tests in the Codex handoff style; no changes to generic machinery beyond a narrow load-vs-new option if needed.

## Risks being tracked

Mode mismatch, trust-gate silent failures, unpersisted fresh sessions, unverified reverse direction. Details in the Codex pattern at `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`.

This restores the original empty React root so startup goes directly to the existing React loader. ## Changes - Remove the inline splash CSS, markup, animation, and SVG from `frontend/index.html`. - Restore `

Launch the desktop app from a clean checkout. 2. Confirm no static SVG splash appears before React mounts. 3. title: fix: serialize concurrent TUI deliveries in sessionguard
body:
### Description

**Fixes #4030**

**Description of Changes:**
This PR addresses a race condition where concurrent `ao send` calls targeting the same session resulted in coalesced payloads. When rapidly triggered, multiple messages were written sequentially into the composer before any of the trailing `Enter` commands executed, merging them into a single submission.

**Root Cause:**
Previously, the `InputLease` acquisition in `sessionguard.Guard` only provided concurrency gating against exclusive session mutations (e.g., agent kill, switch). Multiple ordinary `DeliverWithPostWrite` calls on the same session ID were allowed to proceed to `sendAdmittedChecked` concurrently. Consequently, the underlying `tmux` adapter executed multiple `send-keys` chunks into the pane before its 300ms trailing `Enter` delay (`defaultEnterDelay`) expired for the first caller.

**Implementation Details:**
- Introduced a `deliveryMu` mutex and a `deliveryLocks` map to `sessionguard.Guard` that dispenses per-session locks (via a buffered channel).
- `sendThen` (the choke point for `Send`, `Deliver`, `Nudge`, and `DeliverWithPostWrite`) now acquires this per-session delivery lock *before* acquiring the `InputLease` and checking the session state.
- This guarantees that for a given session, the full `read -> chunked paste -> delay -> Enter` transaction is entirely serialized.
- Agent mutations (which write directly via `DeliverUnderMutation` or `CoordinationUnderMutation`) remain safe and bypass this lock because they inherently hold the exclusive `agentOpMu` fence and wait for the `InputLease` queue to drain prior to executing.
- Added `TestGuard_ConcurrentDeliverSerializesWrites` to verify that concurrent deliveries never overlap inside the messenger.

title: bug(daemon,desktop): Finder/Dock launch inherits launchd's generic $SHELL=/bin/sh, breaking session shells and hooks that need the real login shell
body:
## Bug

When AO Desktop is launched from Finder/Dock (macOS) rather than a Terminal, the process is started by `launchd`, which does not export the user's real login shell in `$SHELL` — it leaves it unset or sets the generic `/bin/sh`. AO trusts that value as-is wherever it is non-empty, so:

- Agent sessions (Claude Code, etc.) spawned inside AO's tmux panes run their shell as `/bin/sh` instead of the user's actual shell (e.g. `/bin/zsh`).
- Standalone shell terminals opened from the AO desktop app do the same.
- Because `/bin/sh` never sources `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`, anything only on `PATH` via an interactive-shell init (nvm, mise, etc.) is invisible inside AO — e.g. `node: command not found` even though `node` works fine in a normal Terminal window.

Running the same AO build/session **launched from a Terminal** does not show the problem, because the Terminal's own shell already has a correct `$SHELL`, and that correct value is what gets inherited — confirming this is specifically about the Finder/Dock launch path, not AO's shell-handling logic in general.

**Analyzed against:** `d6fd5e5f` (`origin/main`)
**AO version:** `dev` (local build)
**OS:** macOS 15 (Darwin 25.2.0), arm64
**Confidence:** High — traced to exact call sites, and independently confirmed that `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell` returns the correct `/bin/zsh` on the affected machine even while the AO-inherited `$SHELL` is `/bin/sh`.

## Reproduction

1. On macOS, install/build AO Desktop and launch it via Finder or the Dock (not from a Terminal).
2. Open a standalone shell terminal, or start any agent session (e.g. Claude Code).
3. Inside that shell/session, check the shell in use (e.g. via a Stop/session hook that shells out, or `ps -p $$`) — it resolves to `/bin/sh`, not the user's configured login shell.
4. Anything that depends on interactive-shell PATH setup (nvm-managed `node`, mise shims, etc.) fails with "command not found," even though the same command works in a normal Terminal window on the same machine.

## Root Cause

`$SHELL` is read and trusted directly, with no correction for the launchd GUI-launch case, in at least these places:

- `frontend/src/shared/shell-env.ts:149-151` — `resolveShellPath()` only falls back to `/bin/zsh` when `env.SHELL` is *empty*; a non-empty `/bin/sh` from launchd is accepted as-is.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` → `buildDaemonEnv()` (`frontend/src/shared/shell-env.ts:183-192`) — merges `{ ...shellEnv, ...processEnv }`, so Electron's own `process.env.SHELL` (the launchd-supplied `/bin/sh`) wins over any recovered login-shell env, and this becomes the `SHELL` the Go daemon inherits.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:290-296` (`New()`) — `shellPath = getenv("SHELL")`, falling back to `/bin/sh` only when empty. This is the shell used for agent-session tmux panes.
- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/loginshell.go:22-35` (`resolveUserLoginShell()`) — same pattern for standalone shell terminals; PATH-based `zsh`/`bash`/`sh` lookup only triggers when `$SHELL` is empty, not when it's the generic `/bin/sh`.

None of these distinguish "the user's real shell happens to be `/bin/sh`" (rare) from "launchd assigned the generic default because this was a GUI launch" (common), so the second case is silently treated as the first.

## Fix

Prototyped and locally verified: added a small `backend/internal/usershell` package with `PreferOverGeneric(envShell string) string`, which only acts when `envShell == "/bin/sh"` — on macOS it consults Directory Services (`dscl . -read <home> UserShell`), the same source Terminal.app and the login window use, and returns that value when it differs from the generic default; otherwise it returns `envShell` unchanged. Wired into `tmux.go`'s and `loginshell.go`'s shell-resolution call sites. Verified on the affected machine that `PreferOverGeneric("/bin/sh")` correctly returns `/bin/zsh`. All existing tests in the touched packages still pass; new tests cover the `usershell` package.

Not yet opened as a PR — happy to push it if a maintainer confirms this is the right approach (vs. e.g. fixing the frontend's `buildDaemonEnv` merge order instead/also, which would fix it at the source before it ever reaches the Go daemon).

## Related

- [#3788](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3788) — same `tmux.go` shell-resolution area (`$SHELL` trusted directly), different symptom: `fish` breaks the POSIX prelude script. Worth reconciling any fix together, since that issue's suggested fix (force `/bin/sh` for the internal prelude) and this one (avoid an incorrect `/bin/sh` for the interactive shell) touch the same code but pull in different directions.
- [#2812](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2812) — same root class of bug ("Electron has a PATH floor, Go daemon does not"): the daemon inherits a GUI launcher's minimal environment and doesn't correct for it, there for `tmux` binary lookup rather than `$SHELL`.
- [#2832](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2832) (closed) — explicitly documents the same trigger ("the daemon runs inside the Electron process and inherits a minimal PATH from the GUI launcher — it does not source shell rc files") for nvm-installed agent binaries specifically.
- [#4505](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4505) (closed) — added a selectable default shell for standalone terminals, but Windows-only (`git-bash`/`pwsh`/`powershell`/`cmd`); macOS has no equivalent override today, so this class of bug currently has no user-facing workaround on macOS either.

title: fix/5365: Agents peer of Projects
body:
## Summary

Part of #5365. Also hides SCM/PR controls for standalone sessions.

title: Feature request: per-session effort/reasoning-level flag for ao spawn
body:
### Feature request

`ao spawn --model <id>` exists, but there is no equivalent flag for the agent's effort / reasoning level (e.g. Claude Code's `/effort` setting).

**Problem**

When spawning workers with `--model`, there is no way to also control the effort/reasoning level for that session only. Effort is a harness-level setting (e.g. Claude Code's `/effort max`), so today the only options are:

- manually setting effort inside each spawned session, or
- changing the harness-wide default in settings, which affects all sessions, not just AO workers.

**Proposal**

Add an effort-style override to `ao spawn`, mirroring `--model`:

```bash
ao spawn --project my-proj --name "fix-bug" --model glm-4.7 --effort max
```

Semantics could match `--model`: a per-session override that does not change project/role config. A corresponding project/role-level config key (e.g. `worker.effort`) would also be useful as a default.

**Why**

Workers doing hard implementation or review tasks benefit from a higher effort level, while routine workers don't need to pay the token cost — the same reason `--model` exists as a per-session override.

title: fix(pi): detect OAuth logins in auth probe
body:
Code changes: +17 -2
Tests: +34 -0
Others: +0 -0

Fixes [#5265](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5265)

## Bug
Pi shows as not logged in after `/login`, even though the user authenticated.

**Reported by:** @jfoley13 (AO 0.12.12, packaged, MacIntel) | **Analyzed against:** `2bc5a88`

## Root Cause
Pi's `/login` flow stores OAuth credentials in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` as
`{"provider": {"type": "oauth", "access": "...", "refresh": "...", "expires": N}}`,
but `piAuthEntry` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/pi/auth.go` only
deserialized `type` + `key`. OAuth entries have no `key`, so
`piAuthKeyIsResolved("")` returned false and the probe reported `unknown` —
only `api_key` entries (or env vars) were ever detected.

## Fix
- Extended `piAuthEntry` with `access`/`refresh`/`expires` and added
  `piAuthEntryIsOAuth()`: an `oauth` entry with a non-empty access token
  reports `authorized`. Expiry is ignored since Pi auto-refreshes tokens,
  so an expired token still indicates a login.
- Added `TestPiAuthJSONStatusAuthorizedWithOAuth` (fresh, expired,
  access-only tokens) and `TestPiAuthJSONStatusUnknownWithOAuthMissingAccess`.

## Test
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/adapters/agent/pi/...` — pass (new tests fail
  on the pre-fix code with `("unknown", false)`, reproducing the issue).
- `go test ./internal/service/agentauth/... ./internal/adapters/agent/registry/... ./internal/adapters/agent/omp/...` — pass; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Manual: real daemon on scratch `AO_DATA_DIR` + fixture `auth.json` —
  `POST /api/v1/agents/pi/probe` returns `unknown` for `{}` and `authorized`
  for an OAuth entry with the fix, `unknown` without it.

## Impact
- Pi users who authenticated via OAuth (`/login`) are now correctly shown as
  signed in; API-key detection is unchanged.

## Screenshots
Manual verification with a real daemon on scratch data (`AO_DATA_DIR` +
`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` fixtures; tokens shown are fake test values).
No login — probe reports `unknown`:

![pi probe with empty auth.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohitGoyal09/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-pi-login-5434/.issue-assets/pi-login-5434/pi_probe_empty.png)

OAuth login present — probe reports `authorized`:

![pi probe with OAuth auth.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohitGoyal09/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-pi-login-5434/.issue-assets/pi-login-5434/pi_probe_oauth.png)

`ao agent ls --refresh` shows Pi as `installed / authorized`:

![ao agent ls pi row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohitGoyal09/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-pi-login-5434/.issue-assets/pi-login-5434/pi_agent_ls.png)


## `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` structure
Map of provider id to credential (verified against live file + upstream
`auth-storage.ts`; secrets redacted). The probe previously only understood
`api_key` entries — `oauth` entries like the one below were invisible:

```json
{
  "anthropic": {
    "type": "oauth",
    "access": "<access-token>",
    "refresh": "<refresh-token>",
    "expires": 9999999999999
  },
  "openai": {
    "type": "api_key",
    "key": "sk-..."
  }
}
```

title: fix: stop session file tab icon from sticking hidden after click
body:
## What

Stop the language icon in a session's file-tab bar from getting stuck hidden after a tab is clicked.

## Why

`WorkspaceEntryIcon` hid on both `group-hover` and `group-focus-within`. Hover clears when the pointer leaves, but `focus-within` stays true as long as the tab's activation button holds focus, which it does after a click since nothing moves focus elsewhere afterward. That left the language icon hidden indefinitely once a tab was clicked, and it only came back once the user clicked something else entirely.

Fixes #5398

## How

Dropped the `group-focus-within:opacity-0` trigger from the icon's classes, keeping only `group-hover:opacity-0`. Hover-driven hiding self-corrects the moment the pointer leaves, so the icon's visibility no longer depends on sticky focus state. The icon's existing `dirty && "opacity-0"` behavior (hidden in favor of the unsaved-change dot) is unchanged.

Added a regression test that clicks the tab, confirms it retains focus (reproducing the exact precondition for the bug), and asserts the icon is never tied to that sticky focus-within state, closing the coverage gap where the previous test only checked the icon existed in the DOM, not that it stayed visible.

## Testing

- Reproduced the bug live in the AO desktop app (isolated dev data): reverted just this fix in a running dev session, confirmed the icon stuck hidden after clicking a file tab and moving the mouse away, then restored the fix via hot reload and confirmed the icon stayed visible on the same click-and-move-away sequence.
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend)

- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable

- persists `fx` sessions through the daemon/API/CLI contract
- exposes `fx` in desktop and mobile agent selectors with official branding
- adds an **Install** action in Global Settings → Agents using the official `https://fx.sh/setup.sh` installer
- documents setup, expected binary location, and current limitations

## Why

AO could not previously create, restore, monitor, switch to, or install `fx` sessions. This change makes `fx` available through the same daemon-backed workflows as the existing TUI harnesses while preserving the rewrite architecture and keeping the frontend a thin API client.

## How

- Introduces a dedicated Go adapter for command construction, model discovery, provider credential detection, and native resume.
- Adds a Herdr-compatible local lifecycle socket with per-launch generation fencing so stale processes cannot overwrite current activity.
- Extends the harness domain, readiness catalog, installer plans, API schemas, CLI validation, session switching, and SQLite constraints.
- Uses the shared Global Settings harness controls for installation, documentation, refresh, retry, and verification. The automatic installer downloads the official setup script and expects `~/.local/bin/fx`.
- Delivers switch prompts only after the replacement fx process starts and wraps standing instructions for interactive sessions.

### Intentional omission

`fx` Chat/ACP mode remains unavailable. The current upstream `fx` release ignores AO standing instructions in ordinary ACP sessions and exposes `ask`/`code` behavior rather than the planned `inspect`/`apply` contract. This PR therefore limits support to the Terminal UI instead of presenting an unreliable Chat experience.

title: Bug: ao browser screenshot always fails with SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE while other ao browser commands work
body:
### Bug report

`ao browser screenshot` consistently fails with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, while all other `ao browser` commands work fine against the same session target.

**Environment**

- Platform: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), AO desktop app
- Browser runtime: connected (`electron-webcontents-debugger`)
- Session: an orchestrator session with a static file opened via `ao preview index.html` (AO preview origin, `http://ao-preview.<id>.localhost:3001/index.html`)

**Observed behavior**

Every `ao browser screenshot` call returns:

```
The service is momentarily unavailable, please retry. (SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)
```

with a request id. Attempts spanned ~10 minutes, so this is not a momentary blip:

- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-022151`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-022458`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-022774`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-023066`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-024650`

Both variants fail identically: `ao browser screenshot <path>` and `ao browser screenshot <path> --json`.

**What works fine on the same target (so the runtime/page are healthy)**

- `ao browser status` → connected
- `ao browser get url`
- `ao browser snapshot --interactive`
- `ao preview` open/clear

**Expected behavior**

`screenshot` writes a PNG of the current tab, or returns a meaningful error if capture is genuinely unavailable.

**Notes**

Looks like the daemon-side capture/screenshot service is down or misrouted while the rest of the browser control plane is healthy. A clearer error distinguishing "capture service unavailable" from transient unavailability would also help.

title: Deduplicate transcript-existence probes behind one agentbase helper
body:
## What is the issue?

- Four adapters answer the same question: does this session id have a saved transcript on disk?
- Claude (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/claudecode.go:303`), Codex (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`, below `:197`), OMP (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/omp/omp.go:117`), and Qwen (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/qwen.go`, below `:172`) each wrote their own version of the check.
- The `NativeConversationID` function is also copied three times word for word (Claude, Codex, Qwen).
- Only small details differ per provider: home folder name, file name pattern, and whether empty files count.
- Contract: `backend/internal/ports/agent.go:108-135` (`AgentInterfaceHandoff` plus the history probe).
- Analyzed against `2bc5a88b4`. Related: [#5420](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5420) (Qwen handoff), [#5036](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5036) (OMP resume with unpersisted UUID).

## Why is this a problem?

- The copies already disagree. OMP counts empty files, the other three do not. Nothing says whether that is intentional, so nobody knows if it is a bug.
- Three of the four walk whole directory trees on every switch-status check. Those folders grow forever. Claude checks files directly without walking, which stays fast.
- Every new handoff-capable adapter copies the same ~40 lines again, bugs included.

## How to solve it

Two helpers in `agentbase`, where shared adapter bits already live:

```go
// Home resolution: env override, process env, then ~/.<dotDir>.
func ProviderHomeDir(env map[string]string, envName, dotDir string) (string, error)

// Bounded check: one ReadDir plus one stat per project dir, require non-empty.
func TranscriptInProjects(ctx context.Context, projectsDir, relPath string) (bool, error)
// claude: TranscriptInProjects(<cfg>/projects, id+".jsonl")
// qwen:   TranscriptInProjects(<home>/projects, "chats/"+id+".jsonl")
```

Plus `HookOrProviderConversationID` for the three identical `NativeConversationID` bodies (Claude keeps its one extra deterministic-UUID fallback line).

Order: helper plus unit tests first. Qwen adoption second (new code, no excuse for a fourth copy). Claude and OMP migration third, guarded by their existing tests. Codex stays separate: dated subdirs plus compression plus the archival-exclusion rule genuinely differ, and bending the helper to fit would add the branching KISS forbids. OMP gains the non-empty rule as a tested drive-by. Deliberately excluded: replacing probes with attempt-based load (side effects inside a readiness check), and doing it inside PR #5019 (keeps that PR small).

## Who does this help?

- The next adapter author: two lines instead of forty.
- The next performance hunt: one code path to measure instead of four.
- The next provider format change: one place to update per layout instead of hoping all copies get the edit.

## Open question

Is OMP skipping the non-empty check intentional or a bug? Nothing in code or history says. Proposed answer: treat it as a bug and unify, covered by a test stating the rule.

title: fix(runtime): replay negotiated terminal modes to late attachers on the PTY host
body:
Code changes: +420 -25  
Tests: +631 -15  
Others: +0 -0  

Fixes #5039

## Problem

On 0.12.12 the mobile app can't scroll a TUI (Qwen Code, Claude Code, …) once the session has produced more than ~1000 lines. A desktop pane that re-attaches after a relaunch has the same problem.

New Linux sessions moved to the native pty-host in 0.12.12 (#4727; macOS got it in #4473). The host replays its ring buffer to every new attach, and the ring keeps the last 1000 lines, so the alt-screen / mouse-tracking / bracketed-paste handshake a TUI prints once at startup is the first thing to fall out of it. A client that attaches after that renders everything in the normal buffer with mouse reporting off, and its scroll gestures never reach the program. tmux re-sends those modes on every attach, which is why 0.12.10 works and sessions created before the upgrade (still on tmux) keep working. `internal/terminal/attachment.go` already describes this exact failure as the reason the mux relies on the runtime re-sending the modes.

## Fix

`conpty/modes.go` tracks the DEC private modes as output flows through the host. On attach the replay is prefixed with the modes it no longer contains. The state model follows xterm.js 5.5, which is what both the desktop pane and the phone's WebView run: one mouse protocol, one mouse encoding, one alt buffer, the keyboard/paste/focus flags, and the two default-on modes (auto-wrap, cursor visible). DECSTR and RIS reset what xterm's soft/full reset reset.

The prefix is diffed against a second pass over the replay bytes, so a client that attaches while the ring still holds the handshake gets the bare ring exactly as before, and shell output from before the TUI started stays in its normal buffer.

Left out on purpose: modes 6 and 45 only affect how the replay paints and the next repaint corrects them; 12, 1048 and 2026 aren't state in xterm.js; 1005 and 1015 are no-ops there.

## Testing

- `TestLateAttachReceivesNegotiatedModes` fails without the `Restore` call in `handleConn` and passes with it. Early attach and attach-after-exit cases pin the no-prefix behaviour.
- Tracker unit tests plus a fuzz test: never panics on arbitrary bytes, byte-at-a-time writes match a single write, and prefix + replay ends in the same state as the full stream at any split point. Benchmark: 0 allocs/op, ~400 MB/s; this is the only per-byte work added to the pump.
- `go test ./...` green, the package also under `-race`.
- Reproduced and verified end to end on an isolated daemon with Qwen Code 0.23 and the iOS simulator: before, a drag on the phone's terminal left the screen unchanged; after, the same drag scrolled Qwen's history. Feeding the captured attach frames to headless xterm.js confirms the client state (normal buffer / no mouse before, alternate / drag after).

Prasad's attach-race review is covered by deterministic `TestOutputWaitsForAnAttachInProgress` and `TestOutputDuringAttachIsDeliveredOnce`: ring append, mode update, and broadcast now share the attach-ordering lock, so a chunk is either in the snapshot or delivered afterward, exactly once. Both tests passed repeatedly under `-race`.

Not run: Windows ConPTY (same host code), a desktop relaunch.

title: fix(mobile): tolerate sessions without a projectId
body:
Code: +13 −6
Tests: +13 −0
Files removed: 0

## What

The 1.3.1 store build crashes on the board as soon as the daemon lists a standalone agent session.

## Why

Standalone sessions (#4851) omit `projectId` on the wire. `SessionCard` passed the missing value to `shortLabel()`, which reads `.length` of `undefined` inside render, so the whole board unmounts. Reproduced from a MIUI bug-report trace: `shortLabel@1:1078216 / SessionCard@1:1200331`.

## How

- `packages/mobile/lib/api.ts:146` — I made `WireSession.projectId` optional to match the daemon, and default it to `""` in `mapSession`/`mapOrchestrator`. Making the type honest is what surfaced three more unsafe callers in the orchestrator dedupe; I skip project-less orchestrators there since one cannot exist.
- `SessionCard.tsx:68`, `PRCard.tsx:62` — cards show `Standalone` instead of throwing.

title: [Bug]: Security: SQL Injection Vulnerability in `migrate_conversation_branches_test.go`
body:
### What went wrong?

```markdown
## Security: Prevent SQL Injection Pattern in Test Queries

### Description
In `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrate_conversation_branches_test.go` (lines 67, 112), table names are directly interpolated using `fmt.Sprintf`:

```go
if err := db.QueryRow(fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT branch_id FROM %s LIMIT 1`, table)).Scan(&branchID); err != nil {
    t.Fatalf("read %s branch: %v", table, err)
}

```

Although isolated to test code, this establishes an unsafe pattern that risks being copied into production.

---

### Proposed Fixes

#### Option 1: Whitelist Table Names (Recommended)

Validate table identifiers against an allowlist before formatting the query:

```go
validTables := map[string]bool{
    "conversation_turns":           true,
    "conversation_messages":        true,
    "conversation_activities":     true,
    "conversation_provider_events":true,
}

for _, table := range []string{
    "conversation_turns", "conversation_messages", "conversation_activities", "conversation_provider_events",
} {
    if !validTables[table] {
        t.Fatalf("invalid table name: %s", table)
    }
    var branchID string
    if err := db.QueryRow(fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT branch_id FROM %s LIMIT 1`, table)).Scan(&branchID); err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("read %s branch: %v", table, err)
    }
    if branchID != activeBranchID {
        t.Errorf("%s branch = %q, want %q", table, branchID, activeBranchID)
    }
}

```

#### Option 2: Regex Identifier Validation

Ensure table names conform strictly to safe identifier patterns (`^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`):

```go
func safeTableName(table string) error {
    if matched, _ := regexp.MatchString(`^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`, table); !matched {
        return fmt.Errorf("invalid table name: %s", table)
    }
    return nil
}

```

#### Option 3: Static UNION Query

Eliminate dynamic SQL entirely using static queries:

```go
var branchID string
query := `
    SELECT branch_id FROM conversation_turns WHERE branch_id = ? LIMIT 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT branch_id FROM conversation_messages WHERE branch_id = ? LIMIT 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT branch_id FROM conversation_activities WHERE branch_id = ? LIMIT 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT branch_id FROM conversation_provider_events WHERE branch_id = ? LIMIT 1
`
if err := db.QueryRow(query, activeBranchID, activeBranchID, activeBranchID, activeBranchID).Scan(&branchID); err != nil {
    t.Fatalf("read branch: %v", err)
}

```

---

### Action Items

* **Immediate:** Apply Option 1 to `migrate_conversation_branches_test.go`.
* **Short-term:** Audit codebase using `rg "fmt\.Sprintf.*(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE)" --type go`.
* **Long-term:** Add linter rules to flag dynamic SQL generation.

```

```

title: Fix/files changed only toggle resets on navigation
body:
## What

Stop the "Changed Only" toggle in a session's Files view from silently resetting to on whenever the user navigates away from the Files tab and back.

## Why

`SessionInspector`'s generic tab-switch handler (`setView`) unconditionally called `onOpenFiles` whenever the destination tab was Files, forcing the changed-only toggle back on every time, even for a plain rail-click switch with no chat or review context involved. Since switching to another tab and back is an ordinary navigation action, the user's toggle choice was getting clobbered on essentially every visit to the Files tab, not just when returning to a specific file.

Fixes #5431

## How

Removed the automatic `onOpenFiles` call from `setView`, so tab switching only switches which tab is visible and no longer triggers a content-level preference reset as a side effect.

This is safe because the two flows that genuinely want the changed-only reset don't depend on that side effect:
- Opening a file or a turn's review from chat already calls `setFilesChangedOnly(sessionId, true)` explicitly via `handleOpenFiles`/`handleOpenReviewFile`/`handleOpenFile` in `SessionView.tsx`, unaffected by this change.
- The "Show Files" call-to-action button in the empty Files state calls `onOpenFiles` directly on click, independent of `setView`,  also unaffected.

So the reset stays intact for its original intended purpose (landing on the changed-files diff view when reviewing what an agent just did), and is only removed from plain tab navigation, which never had a legitimate reason to touch it.

## Testing

- Updated the existing "Files tab opens" test to drop the outdated assertion that clicking the tab calls `onOpenFiles` (that assertion encoded the bug).
- Added a regression test: click Files, click Summary, click Files again, assert `onOpenFiles` was never called.
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend), clean, including after merging in latest `main`

title: fix: stop worker processes on desktop app quit
body:
## Summary

Closing the desktop IDE left every agent worker process behind: 9 `ao` processes + 8 worker processes eating ~1.4 GB RAM, surviving indefinitely with no UI and no owner. This PR makes orderly app quit put all sessions away (work stashed, worker processes stopped, one-shot restore markers written) so the next launch restores sessions cleanly via the existing `RestoreAll`/`reconcileLive` path.

Relates to #3537, #2523, #4317, #4850.

## Problem

Three compounding causes:

1. **Quit never tore anything down.** Both daemon shutdown paths (`SIGTERM` and `POST /shutdown`) deliberately preserved sessions for next-boot adoption — correct for restarts, wrong for IDE quit, where no next boot adopts them.
2. **Chat-mode workers were unkillable.** `saveAndTeardownOne` only destroyed runtime handles, but chat sessions (opencode as worker/orchestrator) own an app-server child process — never stopped, leaked every time.
3. **Windows TUI kills orphaned the real agent.** conpty used bare `Process.Kill()` on the `agent-process supervise` wrapper; the real agent (`opencode.exe`/`claude.exe`) survived as an orphan (same mechanism as #4317).

## Fixes applied

- **Quit-time teardown wiring:** `POST /shutdown` accepts optional `{"teardownSessions": true\}`. Empty body (how `ao stop`, daemon replace, and the supervisor watchdog shut down) preserves adopt-on-restart behavior. The flag is first-wins and read by the daemon after `Run` returns, which then runs `TeardownForAppQuit` bounded by `ShutdownTimeout`.
- **Chat gap closed:** `saveAndTeardownOne` now stops chat controllers (same split as `Kill`); new `TeardownForAppQuit` adds a best-effort second pass for branchless/scratch sessions the save path skips — workers stopped, rows left live, worktrees untouched.
- **Windows tree-kill:** conpty force-kill and pty close now use `taskkill /PID /T /F` with direct-kill fallback; Unix unchanged (Linux session sweep + Darwin group signal already reap trees). Includes a fail-closed self-PID guard and a swappable `killTree` seam for tests.
- **Desktop hook:** `before-quit` POSTs teardown for app-owned daemons only; headless `ao start` and `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` daemons stay persistent. Best-effort, 3s cap, never blocks quit.

Deliberately unchanged: restart/update adopt behavior, `ao stop` semantics, crash/SIGKILL fallback (adopts on next boot; the external guardian from #3537 remains future work).

## Files affected

- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` — chat stop in `saveAndTeardownOne`; new `TeardownForAppQuit` + `teardownQuitSkippedSession` (incl. shell-terminal drain).
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager_test.go` — 2 new regression tests + shell-terminal assertions.
- `backend/internal/httpd/router.go`, `server.go` — `ShutdownRequest`, body decode (fail-closed to plain shutdown), first-wins flag.
- `backend/internal/httpd/control_test.go` — 6 teardown-flag cases + flag-gating test.
- `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go`, `lifecycle_wiring.go` — quit-only teardown hook + interface entry; `wiring_test.go` fake + dispatch assertions.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/runtime.go`, `host_conpty_windows.go` — tree-kill in `Destroy` force path and pty close.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/killtree{,_windows,_unix}.go` (new) — OS tree-kill + self-PID guard; `killtree_test.go`, `killtree_windows_test.go` (new) — live tree-kill test.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/runtime_test.go` — stubbed `killTree` seam in force-path tests.
- `frontend/src/main/quit-teardown.ts` (new), `quit-teardown.test.ts` (new) — testable quit module (7 tests); `frontend/src/main.ts` — before-quit hook + updated teardown comments.

## Tests ran

- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] `go vet` on session_manager, httpd, daemon, conpty — clean
- [x] New Go tests: `TestSaveAndTeardownOne_StopsChatController`, `TestTeardownForAppQuit_StopsSkippedBranchlessSessions`, `TestShutdownTeardownSessionsFlag` (6 cases), `TestTeardownSessionsRequestedFirstWins`, `TestKillProcessTreeRejectsNonPositivePID`, `TestKillProcessTreeRefusesOwnPID`, `TestKillProcessTreeKillsChildTree` (live tree-kill on Windows) — all pass
- [x] Wiring dispatch test extended for `TeardownForAppQuit` — passes
- [x] Save/teardown/kill subset (53 tests), full `httpd`, `cli`, `runtimeselect`, conpty (3 consecutive full runs) — pass
- [x] Frontend vitest `quit-teardown.test.ts` (7/7) + related main tests (36 total) — pass; `tsc` shows zero errors in touched files
- [x] Full-package runs diffed against HEAD via `git stash` — remaining failures (file-mode, missing tmux, TempDir locks, missing `@pierre/diffs` dep) are identical pre-existing Windows-environment issues, none caused by this change

title: [Feature]: Let AO's embedded Browser panel remember a default browser profile
body:
## Problem

As a user of AO's in-app Browser panel, I need opening a link (e.g. a GitHub PR/issue link) to reuse a browser profile I've already chosen, because right now every new AO session starts with the profile unbound — the panel shows "Temporary" and I have to pick my profile again before signed-in sites like GitHub work. With many sessions per day, re-selecting a profile every single time is a real workflow tax.

## Root cause (from investigation)

`browser-view-host.ts`'s `ensureSession()` resolves a new session's profile only via `browserProfileStore.getSessionProfileId(sessionId)` (a per-AO-session binding). When that lookup misses — which it always does for a brand new session — `profileId` is `null` and the view gets a throwaway `ao-browser-${randomUUID()}` partition. There is currently no concept of a default/preferred profile in `BrowserProfileRegistry` (`shared/browser-profiles.ts`) for a new session to fall back to.

## Proposed direction

Add a global default browser profile:
- `BrowserProfileRegistry` gains a `defaultProfileId: BrowserProfileId | null` field (additive, no registry version bump needed).
- `BrowserProfileStore` gains `getDefaultProfileId()` / `setDefaultProfileId()`, clearing the default when that profile is deleted.
- `ensureSession()`'s fallback order becomes: session-specific binding → global default → temporary.
- Expose "set as default" in the existing Manage Browser Profiles settings UI.

A per-project (per-workspace) default was also discussed, but needs new plumbing (Electron main currently has no notion of `workspaceId`/project, only `sessionId`) — proposed as a possible follow-up, not part of this first pass.

## Alternatives considered

None — this is purely an AO-side behavior; it's unrelated to OS/Chrome default-browser-profile settings (confirmed `shell.openExternal` isn't involved here, since this is about AO's own embedded Browser panel, not system browser links).

title: [Bug]: ao session kill fails permanently when the workspace is already gone, and cleanup cannot recover it
body:
## Summary

A session whose worktree has already been removed can never be terminated. `ao session kill` fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR`, which means the session's `terminated` flag is never set — and `ao session cleanup` only processes **terminated** sessions, so it skips it forever. The two code paths disagree about whether a missing workspace is an error, and the session is stuck visible in the sidebar permanently.

## Reproduction

1. Have a worker session with a git worktree.
2. Kill it once. In my case the first kill returned `INTERNAL_ERROR` but *did* remove the worktree and set `status: exited`.
3. Retry `ao session kill <id>` — it fails every time thereafter:

```
Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR) [request EID-.../...]
```

4. `ao session get <id>` shows the contradictory state:

```
status: exited
activity: exited
terminated: false
```

5. `ao session cleanup --project <project>` never offers it. Other sessions in the same state *are* offered and report `Already gone: <id> (workspace was missing; nothing reclaimed)` — so cleanup handles a missing workspace gracefully.

## Expected

Either:
- `kill` should treat an already-missing workspace as success (idempotent) and set `terminated`, **or**
- `cleanup` should be able to reclaim sessions that are `exited` but not `terminated`.

Right now neither is true, so the session is unreachable by any path.

## Actual

Permanently stuck. The only observable difference between this session and its siblings that cleaned up fine is that its `terminated` flag is `false`.

## Notes

- Reproducible on Windows 11, ao daemon healthy (`ao doctor` all green), the rest of the session lifecycle working normally.
- `ao session cleanup` output confirms the graceful path exists — `Already gone: ... (workspace was missing; nothing reclaimed)` — it just isn't reachable for a session that never got marked terminated.
- I have not read the kill path's source, so the above is observed behavior rather than a diagnosed root cause. The asymmetry between the two paths' handling of a missing workspace looks like the likely culprit.

title: [Bug]: Windows installer does not add the ao CLI to PATH, so the CLI is unusable outside AO-spawned sessions
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the installer places `ao.exe` at `C:\Program Files\agent-orchestrator\resources\daemon\ao.exe` but never persists that directory to either the Machine or User `PATH`. The CLI therefore works *inside* sessions AO spawns (which get it injected into their environment) but is not found in a normal PowerShell or cmd window.

## Reproduction

Open a fresh PowerShell window:

```powershell
ao session cleanup --dry-run --project <project>
```

```
ao : The term 'ao' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program.
```

Confirm nothing was persisted:

```powershell
([Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") -split ';') | Where-Object { $_ -like "*agent-orchestrator*" }
([Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")    -split ';') | Where-Object { $_ -like "*agent-orchestrator*" }
```

Both return nothing.

## Expected

After install, `ao` resolves in a new terminal without manual setup.

## Actual

`CommandNotFoundException`. Reopening the terminal does not help, because there is nothing in persisted PATH to pick up.

## Two things that make this more confusing than it needs to be

1. The binary is **not** directly in `C:\Program Files\agent-orchestrator\` — it is nested under `resources\daemon\`. Someone who navigates to the install folder looking for it will not find it there.
2. PowerShell does not search the current directory, so `cd`-ing into the install folder and running `ao` still fails (unlike cmd).

## Workarounds

Call it directly (the `&` is required because of the space in `Program Files`):

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\agent-orchestrator\resources\daemon\ao.exe" session cleanup --dry-run --project <project>
```

Or add it to the User PATH manually:

```powershell
$dir = "C:\Program Files\agent-orchestrator\resources\daemon"
$cur = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
if ($cur -notlike "*$dir*") {
  [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", ($cur.TrimEnd(';') + ";$dir"), "User")
}
```

## Impact

Low severity but high friction: every CLI example in the docs fails for a Windows user until they discover this, and the failure mode (`command not recognized`) gives no hint that the binary is installed and simply unreachable.

title: [Bug]: --reviewer is documented as repeatable but only the first value is ever used
body:
## Summary

`ao project set-config --reviewer` advertises itself as repeatable:

```
--reviewer stringArray   Reviewer harness that reviews worker PRs (repeatable; e.g. claude-code)
```

Additional values are accepted, validated and stored, but **never consumed**. Every reader takes index 0 only, so configuring two reviewers silently behaves identically to configuring one.

## Evidence

`backend/internal/domain/projectconfig.go:102-105`:

```go
func (c ProjectConfig) ResolveReviewerHarness(worker AgentHarness) ReviewerHarness {
	if len(c.Reviewers) > 0 {
		return c.Reviewers[0].Harness
	}
	...
```

`backend/internal/review/review.go:1351`:

```go
	return cfg.Reviewers[0].Harness, cfg.Reviewers[0].AgentConfig, nil
```

The only place that iterates the slice is the validation loop at `projectconfig.go:203` (`for i, rv := range c.Reviewers`), which checks the extra entries and then discards them. Nothing else ranges over `Reviewers`.

## Expected

Either:
- multiple reviewers actually run (the behavior the help text implies), **or**
- the flag is documented as single-valued, and supplying more than one is rejected at config time rather than silently ignored.

## Actual

Silent no-op for every entry after the first. A user who configures two reviewers reasonably believes they have two and has one.

## Why this matters beyond the docs bug

The natural reason to want multiple reviewers is diversity — e.g. having a change reviewed by a model from a different vendor than the one that authored it, to avoid correlated blind spots. That use case reads directly off the help text and does not work. Worse, it fails *quietly*: there is no warning, and the config round-trips showing both entries.

Related: when no reviewer is configured at all, `ResolveReviewerHarness` falls back to the **worker's own harness** (the `switch worker` block above). So the default is same-vendor self-review, and the one documented knob that looks like it would fix that doesn't. Worth at least calling out in the docs.

## Version

Observed against `main` at commit `87cb4b6`.

title: Codex account card jumps while metadata refreshes
body:
## Report

In the production app, expanding a Codex account's metadata card makes the account row and surrounding list visibly jump/flicker before the usage details settle.

Steps shown in the recording:

1. Open **Settings > Subscriptions**.
2. Expand the active Codex account row to view its plan and usage details.
3. The active row briefly loses its stable position/state, then moves back while the card opens.

Expected: the card expands in place. The `In use` state and row order stay stable while that account's metadata refreshes.

Actual: the active row/list visibly jumps during the expansion.

Production recording: https://screen.studio/share/vDypfkWI

## Agent-collected evidence

Checked against `main` at `d6c7d6018`.

- Expanding a row calls `ensureAccount(account.id)`.
- That targeted request asks for authentication/capacity/usage for one saved account.
- The backend currently starts device-global reconciliation for every ensure request, including this targeted metadata refresh.
- Reconciliation publishes a temporary `checking` snapshot with no verified active account.
- The frontend correctly hides `In use` for that unverified snapshot and sorts active rows first, so the row briefly loses its badge and position. The following `verified` snapshot restores both, producing the visible jump.
- The transition is more visible when the packaged/native request takes longer.

No matching open or closed issue/PR was found using the account-card jitter/flicker symptom.

## Proposed fix

Keep device reconciliation and account metadata refresh as separate operations:

- A targeted ensure request with explicit account IDs should refresh only those saved accounts' authentication/capacity/usage data.
- It should not start device-global reconciliation unless reconciliation is explicitly forced.
- Full account refreshes (no explicit account IDs), Settings-open/focus refreshes, and explicit reconciliation retries should continue reconciling the global credential.
- Keep the current truthful frontend rule: during a real reconciliation, no stale account is shown as `In use`.

Add a regression test proving that a targeted metadata refresh does not start reconciliation, while a full or forced refresh still does.

title: feat(telemetry): classify project repo owners as user or organization
body:
Code changes: +305 -33
Tests: +506 -6
Others: +7 -0 (docs)

## Why

`github_org` has never distinguished a personal GitHub account from an organisation. It is just the first path segment of a project's git remote, so the name asserts a distinction the code never makes and org-vs-person is unknowable in the exported data.

This is the **non-PII half** of that fix. It adds a classification and an honest name. It does not change what identity data AO sends, does not touch consent, and does not touch the privacy page.

## What changed

**`repo_owner_type` — new property, `User` or `Organization`.** Resolved from GitHub's public `GET /users/{owner}`. The new `internal/adapters/repoowner` adapter reads only the `type` field from the response; the rest of the `/users` payload (name, email, company, avatar) is never decoded, so it cannot reach a payload by accident. Any value other than the two known account types is rejected rather than forwarded, so a future GitHub account kind cannot silently widen the property's value space in a dashboard.

**The lookup never sits on the project-add path.** `Add` returns without waiting; the classification runs off-thread under a 5s bounded context and emits when it settles. `OccurredAt` is stamped at add time, so a delayed send still reports when the project was actually added. Every failure mode — offline, rate limited, unknown owner, unexpected type, invalid owner — omits the property and changes nothing else.

**`github_org` → `repo_owner`, with `github_org` still shipping.** Both are emitted in parallel for one release so existing PostHog queries and dashboards keep resolving. `github_org` is marked deprecated at the emit site and in the allowlist.

**Allowlist.** Both `ao.projects.created` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added` gain `repo_owner` and `repo_owner_type`. Payloads are strictly allowlisted, so a property missing here is dropped silently — there is now a test asserting both entries carry exactly the expected key set, and a second asserting neither ever allowlists repository-identifying keys.

**Buffered sinks no longer panic on a late `Emit`.** Emitting after the originating call has returned makes an `Emit` racing `Close` reachable; both `LocalSQLiteSink` and `PostHogSink` would have panicked on a send to a closed channel and taken the daemon down during shutdown. They now drop the event. Verified as a real regression: reverting the guard makes the new test panic.

## Deliberate decisions

**The GitHub call carries no credentials.** The brief anticipated an authenticated lookup degrading to omission when unauthenticated. `GET /users/{owner}` is public, so this ships unauthenticated instead. That is both simpler and better coverage: the installs currently missing owner attribution are disproportionately the ones with no GitHub token, and they get classified just as well. It also keeps this PR completely free of credential handling, which is the point of the split. The trade is GitHub's 60 req/hour unauthenticated budget per IP; exceeding it degrades to an omitted property, the same as any other failure.

**No call at all when telemetry is off.** The classifier is wired from the consent-resolved config, so a user who declined telemetry never has their machine call GitHub for a property that would never be exported. `Deps.RepoOwners` left nil keeps the previous inline-emit behaviour exactly.

**The owner is validated before it reaches a request path.** It is a path segment of a remote URL AO did not author, so it is checked against GitHub's login grammar rather than trusted; a crafted remote cannot steer the request off `/users/{login}`.

**Still only the owner segment.** Never the repo name, never the full URL. Asserted in the service test and in the allowlist test.

## Tests

Narrow first, then the CI-equivalent suites.

- `internal/adapters/repoowner` — account-type mapping, unknown-type rejection, 404 / rate-limit / 5xx / malformed-body degradation, owner validation (traversal, spaces, over-length, leading/trailing hyphen), context cancellation, and an assertion that no `Authorization` header is sent.
- `internal/service/project` — `repo_owner` + deprecated `github_org` emitted together; `repo_owner_type` stamped for both User and Organization; omitted on classifier failure without losing `repo_owner`; **`Add` returns while the classifier is still blocked** and the events land after it answers; no lookup at all for a non-GitHub remote.
- `internal/adapters/telemetry` — allowlist coverage and rejection of repository-identifying keys on both project events; sanitizer keeps the new keys and drops a remote URL; `Emit` after `Close` drops instead of panicking on both buffered sinks.
- `go test -race` clean on `internal/service/project`, `internal/adapters/repoowner`, `internal/adapters/telemetry`, `internal/daemon`.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` (the CI-pinned version): 0 issues across the touched packages.
- Full `go test -race ./...`: green except `internal/session_manager`'s four `TestSpawn_*Binary*` tests, which **fail identically on unmodified `origin/main`** on this machine (environment-dependent agent-binary probe). Unrelated to this change; verified in a clean worktree at `d6c7d60`.

## Scope

Deliberately out of scope, and split into a follow-up precisely because it cannot ship without privacy and consent work in the same PR: capturing the authenticated user's `github_login`. `distinct_id` remains the anonymous `ins_<uuid>` install ID and `$process_person_profile: false` is untouched here.

Note for reviewers: `docs/telemetry.md` already discloses that the owner segment is sent and that for a personal repository it is the user's own GitHub username. The landing privacy page does not yet mention it at all — a pre-existing gap that belongs to the follow-up, not to this PR.

title: feat(telemetry): derive workspace GitHub owner from child repos
body:
> **Stacked on #5473, which is stacked on #5471.** Base is `ao/agent-orchestrator-342/repo-owner-parser`. This PR's diff contains only PR B; merge #5471, then #5473, then this one. Draft until both land.

## Problem

The project-added payload derives the repo owner from the project's own `RepoOriginURL`. For a **workspace** project that field is the *workspace root*, which is normally a plain container directory holding several repos — AO initializes it as a git repo with no origin. So the owner was essentially never captured:

| Project kind | Root has git remote | Owner captured | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspace | yes | 36 / 110 | 32.7% |
| workspace | no | 0 / 1,168 | 0% |

Workspace overall: **36 / 1,278 = 2.8%**.

Meanwhile `prepareWorkspaceProject` has already enumerated the child repos, and `workspace_registration.go` sets `RepoOriginURL` on every child record. Those records are in scope at the emit call site. The data was simply never consulted — no new git subprocesses and no new plumbing are needed.

## What this changes

`emitProjectAdded` now takes the workspace child records (nil for single-repo projects) and, for workspaces, derives the owner from them.

**`RepoOriginURL` is deliberately untouched.** It is load-bearing well beyond telemetry — `session_manager` feeds it into session spawn context, and tracker intake uses it for provider inference, repo parsing, and host resolution. Repointing a workspace project's `RepoOriginURL` at one of its children would silently change which issues get polled and what repo context sessions spawn with. This change is purely additive on the telemetry payload.

### Multi-repo owner policy

A multi-repo workspace has no single owner, so rather than invent one:

1. The **root's own remote still wins** when it has one — no behaviour change for the 36 workspaces already attributed.
2. Otherwise, **exactly one distinct owner** across the children populates `repo_owner`.
3. Children with **different owners leave `repo_owner` unset**. Picking the most common owner would attribute a workspace to an owner of only part of it; omission is the honest answer.
4. A new **`repo_owner_count`** property (distinct owner count, workspace events only) keeps the mixed-owner and no-owner cases countable, so case 3 is visible in analytics instead of looking identical to "no data".

A derived owner is an owner like any other, so it flows into #5471's `repo_owner_type` classification and into the deprecated `github_org` alias exactly as a root-derived owner does. Neither behaviour changes, and the one-release `github_org` compatibility now covers workspaces too.

Only owner *segments* are ever emitted — never repository names or remote URLs. `repo_owner_count` is a bare integer with no identifying content, allowlisted on both `ao.projects.created` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added`.

## Tests

- `TestWorkspaceRepoOwners` — no children, same-owner dedupe, mixed owners sorted, missing/non-GitHub remotes ignored, no-GitHub-remotes.
- `TestWorkspaceRepoOwnersIsOrderIndependent` — enumeration order cannot leak into the payload.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceDerivesRepoOwnerFromChildren` — end-to-end through `Add`; asserts `repo_owner` **and** the `github_org` alias, and that the stored `RepoOriginURL` is still empty.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceOmitsRepoOwnerWhenChildrenDisagree` — both `repo_owner` and `github_org` omitted.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceIgnoresChildrenWithoutGitHubRemotes` — a child with no remote plus a GitLab child.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceWithoutGitHubChildrenReportsZeroOwners`
- `TestManager_AddSingleRepoOwnerPayloadUnchanged` — single-repo payload unchanged, no `repo_owner_count`.
- `TestSanitizeRemotePayloadKeepsWorkspaceOwnerCount` — the new property survives the allowlist while repo name / origin URL still do not.
- #5471's own `repo_owner` / `repo_owner_type` tests all still pass on this branch.

Ran locally after the rebase, with the telemetry env stripped: `go test ./backend/internal/service/project/ -run 'Workspace|Owner|Telemetry|RepoOwner'` (32 tests) and `go test ./backend/internal/adapters/telemetry/ -run 'Sanitize|Allowlist|RepoOwner|Owner'` — both pass. Local `golangci-lint` is built against Go 1.24 and refuses this module's 1.25.7 target, so lint is left to CI.

## Notes

- `docs/telemetry.md` said the owner segment was "the one GitHub-derived value AO does send". That was already understated by #5471's `repo_owner_type`, and `repo_owner_count` makes a third, so the privacy doc now names all three.
- Linearized above the parser-coverage PR #5473 (previously a sibling). #5473 moves `githubOwner` out of `service.go` into `owner.go`, so `workspaceRepoOwners` now lives in `owner.go` beside the parser it calls — the workspace owner is derived through #5473's widened parser, not the old five-prefix one.
- `docs/telemetry.md` keeps every statement from all three PRs: #5471's owner-type bullet, #5473's GitHub Enterprise and token-in-remote limits, and this PR's workspace sentences. Nothing was taken wholesale from one side.
- Does not touch consent (#5264). Non-PII either way.

## Risks

- Behaviour change is confined to the telemetry payload for workspace projects. No storage, API, or spawn path is affected.
- Workspace projects that previously made no owner-classification request may now make one, since a derived owner feeds #5471's lookup. That lookup is already off the `Add` path and bounded by its own timeout.
- `repo_owner_count` counts *GitHub* owners only; a workspace of GitLab repos reports 0.
