title: fix(telemetry): recognise the GitHub remote forms the owner parser missed
body:
Stacked on #5471 — **base is `ao/agent-orchestrator-341/repo-owner-type`, not `main`.** Retarget to `main` once #5471 merges. `githubOwner`'s body is byte-identical on #5471, but #5471 rewrites the enclosing hunk (`emitProjectAdded` through `githubOwner`) and the function's doc comment and call site, so developing this against bare `main` would conflict in exactly the region it needs to edit. Review this PR's own commit only.

## Problem

`githubOwner` matched five literal prefixes — `git@github.com:`, `https://github.com/`, `http://github.com/`, `ssh://git@github.com/`, `git://github.com/`. Anything else returned `""`, so the project-added event shipped no owner at all. Verified against the old implementation, every one of these yielded nothing:

| Remote | Old |
|---|---|
| `https://ghp_…@github.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `https://octocat@github.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `git@github.com-work:aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `ssh://git@github.com-work/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `ssh://git@github.com:22/octocat/hello.git` | `""` |
| `https://github.com:443/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `https://GitHub.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `git@GITHUB.COM:aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `HTTPS://github.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `github.com:aoagents/x.git` | `""` |

The token-embedded and SSH-alias forms matter disproportionately: they are what credential helpers and multi-account setups write, i.e. exactly the developers worth attributing.

It also emitted junk from malformed paths — `https://github.com/../x.git` returned `".."`, `https://github.com/-aoagents/x.git` returned `"-aoagents"`.

## Change

Parse the remote's structure instead of prefix-matching it, in a new `owner.go` (moved out of `service.go` unchanged in behaviour apart from the fix):

- Split both the URL form (`scheme://[userinfo@]host[:port]/path`) and the SCP-like form (`[user@]host:path`).
- **Discard userinfo without inspecting it** — it routinely carries a token, which must never leave the function.
- Drop an explicit port; compare scheme and host case-insensitively; the owner segment keeps the case git recorded.
- Accept `github.com`, `www.github.com`, and SSH config aliases of the shape `github.com-<name>`. A hyphen suffix is the documented multi-account convention; a dot suffix (`github.com.evil.example`, `git@github.com.work:`) is **not** accepted.
- Require the first path segment to look like a GitHub login (≤39 chars, alphanumeric plus `-`/`_`, no leading/trailing hyphen), so path noise is no longer exported as an owner.

## GitHub Enterprise is deliberately out of scope

A GHE host (`github.mycompany.com`) is **not** matched, and there are tests asserting that. An owner there is a different, private namespace from a github.com org; folding the two into one `repo_owner` would make the property ambiguous and unqueryable. Capturing GHE at all would need a distinct signal (a separate property, or a hashed host) and its own decision — raising it here rather than deciding it silently.

## The privacy rule is unchanged

Only the owner segment ever comes out — never the repo name, the host, or the URL. `TestGithubOwnerNeverLeaksBeyondTheOwner` pins that against remotes that embed a token and a private repo name. **No raw remote URL or repo name was added to telemetry**, which is also why the cause split behind the missing-owner gap cannot be measured from PostHog: the candidate causes above are reasoned from the parser, not a measured breakdown.

## Scope

Pure telemetry. `githubOwner` has exactly one caller — the `ao.projects.created` payload. Nothing outside the event changes: no `RepoOriginURL` behaviour, no tracker intake, no session spawn, no consent (that is #5264, untouched). `docs/telemetry.md` gains the github.com-only / GHE-excluded statement.

## Tests

`backend/internal/service/project/owner_internal_test.go` is table-driven over every accepted and rejected form: default git forms, six credential-embedded variants, four SSH-alias variants, four port variants, five case variants, shape tolerances, non-github hosts, lookalike hosts, three GHE forms, local/relative/Windows paths, unsupported schemes, and six malformed-owner rejections, plus the 39-character boundary and the no-leak test.

```
go vet ./internal/service/project/
go test ./internal/service/project/ -count=1   # ok, 109s (full package)
```

Local `golangci-lint` is built against go1.24 and cannot load this repo's go1.25 config, so lint is left to CI.

title: fix(cloud): stop false-positive agent-exited 410 on resumed terminals
body:
Code changes: +32 -2  
Tests: +14 -12  
Others: +0 -0

## What
Fixes a false-positive "agent terminal has exited" (HTTP 410 TERMINAL_SESSION_EXITED) on any resumed cloud session.

## Why
`IssueTerminalTicket` decided the agent had exited if ANY agent terminal for the session was `closed` or `failed`. But every resume closes the previous agent terminal and opens a fresh one, so a session that has been paused and resumed even once always carries a closed terminal. The result: the browser terminal-ticket mint returned 410 in a loop for a live session, and the UI showed "Connected" with no terminal. This came in with #5350 and only surfaces once a session has been resumed.

## How
The agent is treated as exited only when a dead terminal exists AND no live one does. Both occurrences of the check in `worker_transport_store.go` now require `NOT EXISTS` an `opening`/`open` agent terminal, so a resumed session with a live open terminal is no longer misreported.

## Testing
cloud gofmt, build, vet, and `go test ./internal/httpapi/` pass. Verified against the l-a run where a resumed orchestrator with a live open terminal was being 410-blocked.

title: fix: prevent orphaned worktrees and ghost sessions when spawn context cancels
body:
### Summary


Fixes #3649 

This PR addresses issue #3649 where `ao spawn` occasionally fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR` (e.g., from a timeout or client disconnect), leaving behind orphaned git worktrees (e.g., `ao/projects-14`) and ghost session rows in the DB marked as `no_signal` but without active handlers.

### Root Cause & Fix

The `Manager.Spawn` pipeline previously propagated the incoming HTTP request context directly into the fallback/rollback routines. When the spawn request was interrupted by a timeout or client cancellation (like an abrupt TCP closure), the context became `context.Canceled`. The downstream rollback methods (`rollbackSeedSpawnWorkspace`, `markSpawnFailedTerminated`, etc.) would receive this canceled context and immediately abort their internal operations (e.g., SQLite updates and git worktree destruction) returning context errors instead of executing cleanup.

This fix injects `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` at the start of all relevant rollback and cleanup paths in `manager.go` and `chat_spawn.go`. This guarantees the cleanup logic (such as `destroySpawnWorkspace`, `store.DeleteSession`, and `lcm.MarkTerminated`) executes independently of the inbound request's lifecycle state. 

### Verification Done

- Added `TestSpawn_ContextCancellationCleansUpWorkspace` to `spawn_timeout_test.go` utilizing a custom blocking mock runtime that triggers mid-flight cancellation and verifies that the workspace destruction count reaches 1.
- Verified local tests (`go test -v ./internal/session_manager/`) pass successfully.
- Verified entire backend test suite (`go test ./...`) passes.

title: fix(updater): progress-based macOS staging watchdog with retry
body:
## Problem

macOS updates could fail with "macOS stopped responding while preparing the update" on slow machines, and with a cryptic ditto pkzip error when the disk was low. Two root causes:

1. Native staging (Squirrel.Mac: ditto extract, code-signature verify, swap prep) was bounded by a fixed 3-minute wall-clock deadline. Squirrel exposes no progress event and no cancel API, so a slow disk that was still making progress got killed at 180s. The only recovery was a manual quit-and-reopen.
2. A full disk hit a separate path and surfaced ditto's raw "No space left on device" text (report in https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5170).

## Change

- Replace the fixed timeout with a progress watchdog that polls the ShipIt staging directory for growth and only gives up after a stretch of no progress (90s inactivity). Fixed caps remain as a fallback when the growth signal cannot be read at all (6-minute no-signal, 15-minute absolute). All reads are read-only against the OS updater cache under `~/Library/Caches/*.ShipIt` and fail open to the fixed caps, so a stat failure never trips the watchdog. AO writes nothing there and keeps no AO state there.
- Add a free-space preflight before handing off to ditto, so a full disk stops early with a short actionable message instead of a partway pkzip failure.
- Surface short, user-readable messages; the full ditto/pkzip/codesign detail is logged, never shown. The remap is deliberately narrow: only known extraction/verification failures are rewritten, and any other error (for example a restart-handoff failure) passes through unchanged so its own recovery and messaging stay intact.
- Retry now restarts AO (`updates:relaunch`) instead of re-invoking `install()` against a Squirrel that cannot be reset in-process. A fresh process re-checks the feed and re-stages cleanly. This is a plain restart, not an install, so it does not touch the post-update relaunch marker.

## Size (for review)

16 files, +225 / -36.

- Production code: +179 / -20 across 5 files. The bulk is `auto-updater.ts` (+152): the watchdog, the staging-dir and free-space probes, and the short-message mapping. The rest is small: the `updates:relaunch` IPC handler (`main.ts`), its preload/bridge wiring (1 line each), and the dialog's Retry action (`RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx`).
- Tests: +38 / -16 across 3 files. Existing timeout tests were rewritten to drive the watchdog deterministically through a filesystem test seam (`__setStagingProbesForTesting`) rather than the real disk, plus the dialog's retry-by-relaunch and hide-install-on-quit cases.
- i18n: +8 / 0. One `update.restart.retry` key added to each of the 8 locale files.

## Verification

Run on this branch checked out clean off `main`, not on the development branch:

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `vitest run` for `auto-updater.test.ts`, `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx`, and `i18n/instance.test.ts`: 204 passing. The i18n test confirms the new key exists in every locale.

The disk-full and slow-disk staging paths themselves are macOS-native (Squirrel) and cannot be exercised in unit tests; those are covered by the deterministic test seam plus the free-space and message-mapping logic, not by a live staging run.

title: fix(chat): surface silent native ACP turns and record outage support
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4613. The Codex slice landed on `main` via https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5227; this covers the non-Codex behavior AO can own.

When a provider connection drops mid-turn, native ACP agents behave inconsistently. The worst case is OpenCode: it leaves the `session/prompt` call open and emits nothing, so AO's turn stays `Working` indefinitely with no explanation. The shared ACP driver had no idle watchdog: `runTurn` created the turn context with `context.WithCancel` and no deadline, so nothing settled a silent turn.

## Fix

- **Idle watchdog (surface-only).** A per-turn watchdog surfaces one non-terminal, turn-scoped "waiting for the agent" system row after a bounded silence (default 3m, `idleActivityTimeout`) and settles it on recovery or turn completion. It never cancels the turn, so a slow but legitimate turn that simply is not streaming is unaffected. Any session update resets the idle clock, and a turn-state guard closes the race between a watchdog tick and turn settlement.
- **Outage support matrix.** Each shipped chat harness is recorded as `handled` (Codex, Claude, OpenCode), `upstream-blocked` (Cursor, Droid: they surface terminal failures faithfully but emit no retry telemetry AO could display), or `unverified` (Pi, Kimi, Kimchi, OMP). A guard test fails if a registered driver has no entry, so an agent cannot be silently claimed as supported.

Deliberately not done: AO does not invent retry counts or backoff for agents that never emit them (the issue forbids it). Existing `sessionFailure` rendering is unchanged and already covered by `prompt_failure_test.go`.

## Changes

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/idle_watchdog.go` (new): watchdog, activity tracking, idle row emit/settle.
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go`, `client.go`: start/stop the watchdog per turn, note activity on session updates, settle the row on completion.
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/network_resilience.go` (new) + guard test.
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/idle_watchdog_test.go` (new): surface+settle, stays-quiet-while-streaming.

## Validation (run locally, not inferred)

- `go build ./...` clean; `go vet` clean; `gofmt -l` empty
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/... ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/... -race` passes, including the new cases
- `go test ./internal/service/chat/...` passes (the controller consumes these events)

Refs https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4613

title: feat(cloud): PR tracking for cloud workers and PR details in the sidebar
body: > **Stacked on #5379.** This branch is built on `fix/cloud-pr-tracking-and-workspace-checkout`, so the diff includes #5379's two commits until that merges. The new work is the last three commits: `feat(cloud): track worker pull requests…`, `feat(desktop): show cloud session pull requests…`, and `fix(cloud): build against the pinned backend contract`. ## What Cloud sessions now get the pull request tracking and sidebar PR details that local sessions have. Ported the local implementation to cloud sessions - **Control plane:** a PAT-backed tracker finds the PRs a worker opens from its session branch and keeps each one's CI, review, and mergeability current. - **Session list/get responses:** now include each session's `prs` and `scmStatus`. - **Desktop:** the sidebar, board and inspector show cloud PRs the same way they show local ones. ## Why On a deployment without a GitHub App (the setup #5379 fixes raise/claim for), cloud PR tracking stopped at `ao claim-pr`: - `prstatus.Scanner` only runs with an App. PRs raised or claimed with a PAT stayed at their initial state and never got CI, review or mergeability updates. - A PR the agent opened any other way (`gh api`, the browser, an MCP tool, or `gh pr create` output the wrapper couldn't parse) was never attached to the session. The local daemon's SCM observer finds these PRs by matching the session branch. - The desktop mapped cloud sessions with `prs: []`, and the inspector always asked the **local daemon** (`/api/v1/sessions/{id}/pr`) for PR detail. So the sidebar and inspector never showed a cloud PR, even when the control plane had one. ## How **Control plane (`cloud/`)** - `githubapp.PATPullRequestTracker` works through every live session (sandbox not deleted or terminated): - **Finding PRs:** only for running sandboxes. It lists `pulls?head=owner:&state=all` and claims any PR that no session in the org tracks yet (`PullRequestTracked`), so it never reassigns a PR another session already has. - **Refreshing PRs:** for each of the session's open PRs, it records CI, review and mergeability through `UpdatePullRequestObservation`. - It authenticates with the session creator's PAT, the same credential worker checkout and push already use. Sessions without a PAT, or on a non-github.com remote, make no GitHub calls. - **Wiring:** it only runs when no GitHub App is configured (`githubService == nil`). App deployments keep the existing scanner, unchanged. It reuses the scanner loop through the new `prstatus.NewFunc`, and polls at `max(AO_CLOUD_PR_STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL, 1m)` because each call counts against the user's own GitHub rate limit. - **Shared code:** - `observePullRequest` is used by both the App refresh and the PAT tracker. - `sessionGitHubPAT` is used by both `WorkerGitHubPAT` and the new `SessionGitHubPAT`. - `httpapi.GitHubPATAssociatedData` exposes the PAT's encryption associated data so the tracker can decrypt it. - **Database access:** the cross-org session scan reads only `ao_sandboxes`, which the service context can already read. Session rows are then read with `withOrg`, so no new RLS policy or migration is needed. - **Response shape:** `GET /sessions` and `GET /sessions/{id}` now return the same shape as the children listing (`sessionChildResponse`). The additions are `prs` and `scmStatus` (derived with the same `contract.DeriveSCMStatus` the local daemon uses). Kanban column and display status are not sent: the cloud module builds against a pinned `backend` version (the Docker build has no `go.work`) that predates the Kanban reducers, so the desktop places the card from the session status, as it already does when the daemon omits a column. The change is additive; existing fields are unchanged. **Desktop (`frontend/`)** - **Board:** cloud sessions map `prs` and `scmStatus`, and derive their board column from the session status, so status dots, board columns and PR chips follow the same rules as local sessions. - **Inspector:** `useSessionScmSummary(session)` reads cloud PR detail from the control plane's `/sessions/{id}/pull-requests` route and maps it to the daemon's `SessionPRSummary` shape. It polls every 15s because no daemon event stream invalidates it. The control-plane URL is read from the settings cache when fetching (as `useTerminateSession` does), so local-only renders don't subscribe to the cloud auth hooks. - **Local-only actions:** the local-daemon merge button is hidden for cloud PRs, and the local reviewer query is skipped for cloud sessions. **Intentional omissions** - The control plane doesn't track review threads, failing-check logs, or CI/review auto-inject yet; those fields take empty defaults. - No server-side Kanban column/display status until the cloud module's `backend` pin is bumped to a version with the Kanban reducers. - PR discovery through the App path (branch matching with an installation token) is not added; App deployments behave exactly as before. - Like the existing scanner, the tracker runs on every replica, and claims are idempotent upserts. ## Testing - `cd cloud && gofmt -l . && GOWORK=off go build ./... && GOWORK=off go vet ./... && GOWORK=off go test ./...`: all pass, both standalone (the pinned `backend`, as the Docker build uses) and through `go.work`. `docker build --target control-plane` succeeds. `go test -race` passes for `githubapp`, `httpapi` and `prstatus`. - New Go tests: - `pat_tracker_test.go`: finds and refreshes a PR; skips PRs already tracked; paused sessions only refresh; no GitHub calls without a usable PAT. - `resource_handlers_test.go`: PRs and SCM status on the response. - New SQL checked against a throwaway `postgres:17` with migrations applied, run as the non-privileged `ao_cloud_app` role under RLS: - `PullRequestTrackingSessions` excludes deleted sandboxes and marks paused ones inactive. - `SessionGitHubPAT` resolves the credential. - Claim, then `PullRequestTracked`, `OpenPullRequestRefsForSession` and `UpdatePullRequestObservation` all behave as expected. - `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`: passes. - New and updated vitest: `useSessionScmSummary.test.tsx` (local vs cloud source, shape mapping, unconfigured control plane) and `useWorkspaceQuery.test.tsx` (cloud PRs and SCM status). - Full `npx vitest run`: **18 failures remain, and they fail identically on the base branch** (landing analytics/download tests, `browser-history-store`, `browser-profile-import`). `GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx` fails only under full-suite load and passes on its own, both with and without this change. - **Not verified end to end:** I didn't run this against a live control plane with a real GitHub PAT, and I didn't take UI screenshots; the sidebar/inspector rendering code itself is unchanged, only its data source. ## Checklist - [x] Continuing an existing PR branch (stacked on #5379) - [x] One focused change - [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (pending remote CI)

title: fix(mobile): advertise the secure-pairing proxy so iPhones can pair over Tailscale
body:
Code changes: +120 -32  
Tests: +252 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

Fixes #3852

## Problem

An iPhone on the tailnet can't pair with the daemon, or reconnect to it, unless the Cloudflare tunnel is up. iOS refuses cleartext HTTP to `100.64.0.0/10` (`NSAllowsLocalNetworking` covers only local ranges), so the plaintext Tailscale entry in the pairing code can never win the race on iOS.

#3707's secure pairing already solves the transport — `tailscale serve` fronts the bridge on the MagicDNS name, and the desktop turns it on by itself when Connect Mobile is opened on a machine with a tailnet address — but the endpoint list, in the v2 code and on the phone's refresh route, comes from `mobilebridge.Endpoints`, which only knows LAN addresses, the plaintext Tailscale address and the tunnel (#4615 lists this under "not covered"). The proxy is never advertised. The documented workaround, typing `<magicdns>:443` with TLS on, erases itself on the first successful connect, because `mergeEndpoints` lets the daemon's list replace every kind it mentions.

## Fix

`Endpoints` takes the state of secure pairing and advertises the tailnet as at most one candidate: the plaintext address while the mode is off; the proxy (`tailscale` kind, MagicDNS name, `:443`, `secure: true`) in its place while the mode is on and `SecurePairing.Active`; nothing while the mode is on but unverified.

One candidate rather than both because the phone keeps whichever of two same-ranked answers arrives first and re-races once a minute off the LAN, so plaintext and TLS side by side would flip the config on packet timing and tear down the streams keyed on it; #3707's QR replaced the address the same way. Nothing while unverified because "unverified" includes a CLI call that timed out and the moment between the listener binding and `serve` being applied: the phone keeps a kind the list omits, whereas a plaintext entry would replace the stored TLS one and strand an iPhone off the LAN.

`Status()` and `AdvertisedEndpoints()` build from one `endpointInputs`, so the QR and the refresh can't drift, and already-paired phones pick the proxy up on their next connect. No wire-shape, `app.json` or mobile change. With the mode on, the refresh route makes the same two bounded, read-only `tailscale` calls `Status()` makes — about once a minute per phone away from the LAN. They now run concurrently, so even if both calls stall for their 3 s bound, the refresh remains inside the phone's 5 s request timeout.

## Testing

- Regression tests for the endpoint and refresh behavior. Reverted to `main`'s behaviour, the positive and omission tests fail; reverted to "plaintext whenever unverified", exactly the omission tests fail. `go test ./...` green; `openapi.yaml` regenerates with no diff.
- Isolated daemon from this branch with a fake `tailscale` on `PATH`: mode off → `lan`; mode on → `lan` + `tailscale <name>:443 secure` in both the status list and the refresh route; serve state edited to another port, or the CLI failing → `lan`; restored → proxy back; mode off → gone, `serve off` called.
- Phone side, against the unmodified modules with a probe that fails the plaintext entry in-process like ATS: the iPhone's race is won by the TLS entry; a hand-typed TLS entry survives the refresh; a refresh landing while the proxy is unverified keeps it, whereas the plaintext-fallback variant stores the plaintext entry and the next race off the LAN reports `none-reachable`; an Android phone paired on plaintext moves to TLS once and stays.

Later regression checks: a deterministic test forces both Tailscale reads to overlap and verifies that the TLS proxy is advertised; the focused controller tests passed under `-race`, `go vet ./internal/httpd/controllers` passed, and all Go packages compiled. The full controller suite could not run in this local sandbox because loopback binds are blocked; the complete backend CI suite passed on this head.

Not run: a real tailnet (Tailscale is stopped here, no cert domains); #3707 verified the `serve` → iPhone hop on hardware, and the tunnel exercises the same `secure: true` path on the phone. SSE through `tailscale serve` is reasoned, not measured: Go's `ReverseProxy` flushes `text/event-stream` immediately.

Limitations: #3707's prerequisites still apply (CLI on `PATH`, HTTPS certificates on the tailnet) and the desktop shows which is missing; a phone with Tailscale DNS off won't resolve the MagicDNS name and falls back to the LAN or the tunnel; a bare `100.x` typed by hand with TLS off on iOS gets a Tailscale reachability message that does not explain iOS's plain-HTTP restriction — app-side, for a follow-up.

Claude Code 2.1.273 paints provider-owned non-dim content into that region: a bare `Claude Code` product label on the prompt row between the rules, and a multi-line statusline below the lower rule (which the footer-free fallback scans when rule geometry does not match). One transient frame permanently failed the switch. Fixes: the draft refusal now requires the same repeated stable samples as the idle decision; a horizontal rule below the prompt closes the footer-free composer scan; adapters can name provider chrome labels that never read as a draft.

2. **`NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` from a never-messaged Chat session.** Entering Chat reserves a provider conversation id, but the durable conversation row is materialized only when the Chat controller starts (first turn). The chat→Terminal freshness proof demanded that row, so a session that had never been messaged — nothing to resume, nothing to discard — could never reach Terminal. Fix: the Chat emptiness proof accepts `domain.ErrNoConversation`; generic history read failures and every other guard (prompts, checkpoint facts, transcript evidence, turns) stay fail-closed.

title: Chat default fails instead of falling back to Terminal UI for unsupported harnesses
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Summary

When Chat UI is configured as the default interface and a project is launched with a harness that Chat UI does not support, such as Kimi, AO attempts to start it in Chat and surfaces an error.

AO should detect that the selected harness is not supported by Chat UI and automatically launch the project in Terminal UI instead.

This appears to be a regression or an uncovered launch path related to #3712, which implemented proactive Terminal UI fallback for TUI-only agents in the new-task composer.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set the default interface to Chat UI.
2. Launch a project using a harness that Chat UI does not support, such as Kimi.
3. Observe that launch fails with an unsupported interface error.

## Expected behavior

AO checks the selected harness capabilities before launch. If Chat UI is unsupported, it automatically starts the project in Terminal UI without first sending a guaranteed-to-fail Chat request.

## Actual behavior

AO attempts to use the configured Chat UI default and displays an error instead of falling back to Terminal UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Harness capability is resolved before the launch request is sent.
- A harness unsupported by Chat UI launches directly in Terminal UI when Chat UI is the configured default.
- Chat-capable harnesses continue to respect the configured Chat UI default.
- The existing explicit interface behavior remains unchanged when the user has selected a supported interface.

## Related

- #3712

title: fix(mobile): allow plain HTTP to the tailnet on iOS so iPhones can pair over Tailscale
body:
Fixes #3852

## Problem

Since iOS 17, App Transport Security applies to IP addresses, and `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` only exempts the local ranges (RFC 1918, link-local, `.local`). Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` is RFC 6598, so a plain-HTTP connection to the daemon's tailnet address is refused before a packet is sent. The pairing code carries exactly that address, so an iPhone off the LAN can't pair or reconnect over Tailscale.

#5485 makes the daemon advertise the TLS proxy from #3707 instead, which fixes it wherever secure pairing can run. That still needs the `tailscale` CLI on the Mac's `PATH` and HTTPS certificates enabled on the tailnet, and a `100.x` address typed by hand with TLS off keeps failing. Android already allows it (`usesCleartextTraffic`).

## Fix

Two `NSExceptionDomains` entries in `app.json`, and nothing wider:

- `100.64.0.0/10` — CIDR keys are accepted from iOS 17, the same release that started blocking. On iOS 16 and earlier ATS never applied to IP addresses, so nothing changes there.
- `ts.net` with `NSIncludesSubdomains` — the MagicDNS name, for the same daemon reached by name instead of by address.

Not `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`. The exception only reaches hosts inside the user's own tailnet, where the link is already WireGuard-encrypted; any other `http://` host stays blocked. The daemon still advertises the `tailscale serve` proxy when secure pairing is active (#5485); this is for the tailnets where it isn't, and for the manual entry. `lib/ats.test.ts` pins the two entries and asserts nothing else is waived, so the block can't drift back or widen. README and the desktop's TLS comment updated to match (the frontend change is a comment).

This changes the native fingerprint (runtime version `ad3999c7` → `8685992b`), so it ships with the next store build, not over the air; builds before it keep needing #5485's TLS path. App Review may ask for a justification for `NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads`; one that fits: "The app connects to a daemon on the user's own computer over the user's Tailscale VPN (`100.64.0.0/10`, `*.ts.net`). That link is WireGuard-encrypted, and the daemon has no public hostname to hold a CA certificate for."

## Testing

- Native build from this branch on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5), `fetch()` from inside the app over the Hermes debugger, against a plain-HTTP server bound to a `100.100.100.100` loopback alias: `http://100.100.100.100:3099/api/v1/identity` → 401 from the server, request logged server-side. `http://1.1.1.1/` → still "App Transport Security policy requires the use of a secure connection", so the exception is targeted. LAN address unchanged. On `main`'s build the same probe to `1.1.1.1` is refused the same way; the `100.x` probe was only run on this branch's build. The built `Info.plist` carries both entries; the `ts.net` one wasn't exercised (no DNS for a fake name here).
- `ats.test.ts`: both tests fail with `app.json` reverted. 860 → 862 vitest, `tsc` clean, `expo export --platform ios` bundles.

Not run: a physical iPhone on a real tailnet (Tailscale is stopped on this Mac, no cert domains). ATS is enforced the same way in the simulator.

title: ao spawn: SPAWN_TIMEOUT leaves session started but initial prompt never delivered
body:
## Summary

`ao spawn --project <project> --name <name> --claim-pr <N> --no-takeover --prompt "..."` timed out client-side with `SPAWN_TIMEOUT`, but the session was actually created and started. The initial prompt was never delivered to the agent, so the session sat idle and had to be manually recovered with `ao session claim-pr` + `ao send`.

## Observed behavior

Two spawns were issued back to back for the same project, different PRs. Both CLI calls failed with:

```
Session spawn timed out before the agent could start (SPAWN_TIMEOUT) [request <host>/<req-id>]
```

After the timeout, `ao session ls` showed both sessions existed and were idle, but:
- They were on the default `ao/<session-id>/root` branch, not the requested PR branch
- The `--name` flag did not appear to be applied
- No PR was claimed (so `--claim-pr` / `--no-takeover` did not take effect)
- The agent had received no prompt

Manual recovery worked: `ao session claim-pr <session-id> <pr>` succeeded (printed `checkout: already on PR branch` and `taking over from <old-session>`) and `ao send --session <id> --message ...` delivered the task.

## Expected behavior

Either the spawn succeeds end to end (session created, branch/name/PR claim applied, prompt delivered), or it fails atomically with no partially-initialized session left behind.

## Suspected area

Timeout path in the spawn flow: the daemon appears to create and start the session before the CLI gives up waiting, and the prompt delivery (plus name/branch/claim application) never happens afterward. Observed with the kimi harness; may be harness-specific startup slowness exceeding the client timeout.

## Environment

- AO CLI/daemon: local dev build, macOS (arm64), 2026-09-16
- Harness: kimi
- Impact: 2/2 spawns failed this way in one batch; sessions silently idle until manually noticed

title: fix(acp): report rejected session/load and back off history settle polling
body:
Code: +104 −9
Tests: +284 −0
Files removed: 0

## What happened
Switching a Claude Code session from Terminal to Chat hung for 45 seconds, then failed with a vague "resume failed" toast.

## Issue solved
Fixes #5292. The second history load (`session/load`) ran inside the 45 s settle window with no bound of its own, so one slow load ate the whole budget. The `-32603 "context deadline exceeded"` in the report is the SDK echoing AO's own expired deadline, not a provider refusal.

## What we did
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` — each refresh load gets its own 30 s deadline; a bound hit returns `ErrChatHistoryLoadFailed` right away. Retry wait now grows 100 ms → 2 s.
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/driver.go`, `history.go` — a `-32603` from `session/load` maps to `ErrChatHistoryLoadFailed` only when AO's context is still live; AO's own deadline keeps its context error.
- `backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go` — the switch reports `TARGET_HISTORY_LOAD_FAILED` and does not restart the target a second time.
- Tests: stalled load returns within the attempt bound; provider `-32603` vs AO deadline classified apart; backoff schedule; transition code. Touched packages pass `go test`; I did not run the full `-race` suite or `golangci-lint` locally (lint crashes on go1.27 here).

title: fix(update): stop restart dialog jittering on workspace refetch
body:
## What

Stop the restart-to-update dialog from jumping every ~15 seconds while it is open.

## Why

The dialog renders a "Current worker state could not be confirmed…" line whenever `workspace.isFetching` is true. The workspace query polls the daemon on a 15s `refetchInterval`, so `isFetching` flips true during every background poll even though the last-known session list is still in hand. The line inserts and removes on each poll, and Radix re-centers the dialog on any height change, so the whole dialog bounces every 15 seconds while a build is staged.

`isFetching` is the wrong signal: on a background refetch the worker list is not actually unknown. The genuinely-unknown cases are already covered by `!workspace.data` (first load, nothing yet) and `isError` (fetch failed).

## How

title: Open agent reports reliably and improve dark-mode output readability
body:
## What

Fixes several usability issues in agent chat output and the AO Browser:

- Makes code comments and quoted syntax readable on dark backgrounds.
- Opens local report links inside AO instead of sending unusable filesystem paths to the external browser.
- Adds right click actions for opening verified workspace files in Files.
- Makes link behavior consistent between AO Browser and the system browser.
- Adds a compact Copy URL button to the AO Browser address bar.

## Why

Agent-generated reports could be difficult or impossible to open:

- Windows absolute paths could be removed by Markdown URL sanitization because drive letters resemble URL schemes.
- Local paths that had not yet appeared in the workspace file index were treated as external links.
- Absolute workspace paths did not receive the normal link context menu.
- Filesystem paths passed directly to Chromium produced empty or unusable tabs.
- Some syntax-highlighted comments used the passive text color, which had insufficient contrast on the dark code-block surface.
- The Browser address bar displayed a shortened hostname but had no direct way to copy the complete URL.

## How

### Report and workspace links

- Normalizes relative, POSIX, Windows, encoded, and `file://` workspace paths.
- Resolves known files to their workspace-relative paths.
- Sends newly created or not-yet-indexed report paths through the existing session preview resolver.
- Keeps filesystem access confined by the backend workspace validation.
- Opens normal HTTP and localhost links in AO Browser by default.
- Preserves explicit system-browser behavior for web links through modifier-click and the context menu.

### Link context menu

- Shows **Open in AO Browser** for browser-compatible links.
- Shows **Open in Files** only when the link resolves to a verified workspace file.
- Shows **Open in external browser** only for HTTP(S) links.
- Keeps **Copy link** available without automatically opening the link.

### Browser URL copying

- Adds a Copy URL control beside the existing external-browser button.
- Uses the same compact `23×23px` styling with a 4px gap.
- Copies the complete underlying URL, including path and query parameters.
- Replaces the copy icon with a checkmark briefly after success instead of showing a global toast.
- Retains an error notification if copying fails.

### Output readability

- Uses the normal muted-text token for highlighted comments and quotes instead of the much darker passive-text token.

## Testing

title: fix(scm): keep UNSTABLE PRs mergeable instead of downgrading to blocked
body:
## What

Move the `UNSTABLE` check above the draft / CI / review blockers in the SCM observer's two mergeability derivers, so an `UNSTABLE` PR is recorded as `Mergeability = unstable` rather than `blocked`.

## Why

Fixes #2401.

`mergeabilityObservation` (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go`) and its byte-identical twin `mergeabilityFromProviderFacts` (`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`) checked `draft` / `ci == failing` / changes-requested, set `MergeBlocked`, and returned — before ever reaching the `UNSTABLE` branch at the bottom.

Because an `UNSTABLE` PR's status rollup aggregate is `FAILURE` (→ `ci = failing`), that bottom branch was effectively dead for the common case, and a genuinely mergeable PR was persisted as `blocked` with blocker `ci_failing`.

`UNSTABLE` means the PR *is* mergeable but a non-required check failed or is pending (a *required* failure yields `BLOCKED` instead). `doc.go` in the same package spells out the priority — rule (3) `UNSTABLE` outranks (5) changes-requested and (6) CI-failing — and the sibling `mergeabilityFromGraphQL` in `provider.go` already implements that order. The two observer functions didn't, and the `UNSTABLE` observer path was untested, which is how the divergence slipped in.

## How

- `UNSTABLE` now returns `MergeUnstable` immediately after the `DIRTY` / `BEHIND` / `BLOCKED` handling, matching `doc.go` and the GraphQL sibling.
- **Deliberate deviation from the issue's suggested fix:** the `BLOCKED` branch keeps falling through instead of returning early. `BLOCKED` and `UNSTABLE` read the same `state` field so they are mutually exclusive anyway, and an early return there would truncate a blocked PR's blocker list to just `blocked_by_provider`, dropping `draft` / `ci_failing` / `changes_requested` detail — a regression the issue didn't ask for.

Reviewers may want to focus on the downstream consumers of `MergeUnstable`, which this change makes reachable for the first time in the common case:

- `lifecycle/reactions.go:405` (`mergeabilityClearsConflict`) already documents `unstable` as a definitive non-conflicting state.
- `service/session/pr_summary.go:404` (`mergeabilityReasons`) already handles `MergeUnstable` and derives reasons from the PR's own fields, so the UI still surfaces `ci_failing` for an unstable PR even though the observation's `Blockers` list is now empty.
- No auto-merge gate keys on `Mergeability`.

## Testing

Added table tests for the previously untested `UNSTABLE` observer path in both packages, covering the issue's repro (optional check fails, rollup `FAILURE`, review approved) plus guard rows for the paths that must not change: conflicting still wins, blocked still collects every blocker, `CLEAN` + failing CI still blocks, `CLEAN` + approved still mergeable.

- Verified the new tests **fail without** the source fix (`State = "blocked", want "unstable"`) and pass with it, so they aren't vacuous.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/adapters/scm/... ./internal/observe/...` clean.
- Full `go test ./...` across the backend passes. The first run showed two failures in `adapters/agent/fake` and `adapters/agent/pi` — both timing-sensitive, unrelated to SCM, and both passed on a clean re-run.

title: fix(tabs): pin the tab overflow action to the tab's right edge
body: ## Problem In a session tab, the `⋮` overflow menu sat immediately after the end of the title text instead of at the tab's right edge. With a short title like `hii`, the button floated in the middle of the tab. ## Cause `TerminalTabFrame` renders its trailing action as an overlay positioned `right-1` inside the tab's inner row. title: fix(session): require consecutive dead probes for orchestrators and notice on replace
body:
## What

Requires two consecutive `ProbeDead` runtime reaper observations before terminating orchestrator-kind sessions, and sends a durable continuity notice with predecessor ID and transcript path when `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=false)` replaces an unexpectedly terminated predecessor.

## Why

Fixes #2501.
Orchestrators are long-running and execute unhooked sub-agent/tool operations where intermediate activity hooks are not fired. A single transient probe jitter or lag meeting the stale-activity window was enough to terminate them prematurely. Subsequently, navigating back or refreshing in the UI triggered `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=false)`, which found no active session and spawned a replacement with a blank transcript, leaving the user with no explanation of what occurred or where the previous transcript was.

## How

1. **Consecutive dead probe gate (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go`)**:
   - Track `consecutiveDeadProbes map[domain.SessionID]int` guarded under `m.mu` in `m.mutate`.
   - Require `orchestratorDeadProbeThreshold = 2` before `KindOrchestrator` sessions transition to `IsTerminated = true`.
   - Reset the counter on any non-dead probe, activity signal, or launch mismatch.
   - Workers and other session kinds retain historical single-sample termination so short-lived tasks are not prolonged.
2. **Predecessor continuity notice (`backend/internal/service/session/service.go`)**:
   - When `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=false)` finds no active orchestrator, look up the most recent terminated orchestrator within `orchestratorPredecessorStaleWindow` (30 minutes).
   - If found, inject a plain-text continuity message into the newly spawned session referencing the predecessor ID, termination timestamp, and `NativeTranscriptPath`.
   - Best-effort delivery mirroring `sendRetireNotice`.

### Intentional Omissions
- Did not touch worker termination threshold: workers need fast failure detection to avoid hanging task queues.
- Did not alert on predecessors older than 30 minutes: projects reopened days or weeks later are deliberate fresh starts, not silent reaper races.

## Testing

- Added `TestRuntimeObservation_OrchestratorRequiresConsecutiveDeadProbes` in `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager_test.go` covering 1-sample non-kill, 2-sample kill, counter resets on alive probes, and worker single-sample kill.
- Added `TestSpawnOrchestratorNoCleanSendsContinuityNotice` in `backend/internal/service/session/service_test.go` covering cold spawn without predecessor, recent predecessor notice, ancient predecessor bypass, and newest predecessor selection.
- Added `TestSpawnOrchestratorNoCleanIdempotentDoesNotDoubleNotice` verifying no duplicate notices on re-render/retry.
- Full test suites passed:
  - `go test ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/service/session`
  - `go test -race ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/service/session`
  - `go vet ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/service/session`

title: feat: add zcode harness adapter
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5341

Adds zcode (Z.AI GLM terminal coding agent) as a first-class harness adapter, following the grok adapter pattern:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/zcode/` — clean-room adapter (launch, restore, readiness hints, auth checker, config spec, table tests)
- Migration `0148_allow_zcode_harness.sql` — admits `'zcode'` in `sessions.harness` CHECK, handling both the normal and the legacy `'qm'` schema variants from the 0095 era
- Registration chain: `registry.go`, `harness.go`, `dto.go` enums, `openapi.yaml` + `schema.ts` regenerated and committed together
- Frontend: `zcode` added to product-ui `AGENT_OPTIONS`/`AGENT_LABELS`

## Design notes

- **Interactive TUI + after-start prompt delivery** (not `--prompt`): zcode's `--prompt` is a headless single-turn path; workers need the interactive composer. Prompt is injected once `PromptReadinessHints` match.
- **Auth checker reads `~/.zcode/v2/credentials.json`** (OAuth access token JWT) and decodes `exp` locally — structural `apiKey` presence in `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` cannot distinguish logged-in from OAuth-expired (observed live).
- **Restore falls back to a fresh launch** when no native `agentSessionId` was captured; `-c/--continue` deliberately rejected as a resume fallback.

## Intentional omissions

- No `doctor.go` probe spec, `systeminstall.go` targets, `agentauth/plans.go` login plan, or `activitydispatch.Derivers` for zcode: `CoverageForHarness` returns `SignalCoverageNone` and `agentSessionId` is not captured — self-consistent with the no-AO-managed-hooks stance and the fresh-launch restore fallback.
- No AO-managed workspace hooks: zcode gates workspace-scoped hook files (`zcode.json`, `.zcode/config.json`) behind an interactive trust review an orchestrator cannot complete unattended.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `domain.AgentConfig.Validate()` hardcodes Amp's mode vocabulary (`low|medium|high|ultra`), so project-config validation rejects the modes zcode's own `GetConfigSpec` advertises (`build|edit|plan|yolo`). The adapter validates modes itself at argv-build time, but the domain validator contradiction remains.
- Resumed sessions may not mount the welcome banner, so readiness hints can time out (best-effort 10s, delivery proceeds anyway).

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet` (zcode, sqlite, httpd), `go test -count=1` on zcode, storage/sqlite, registry, httpd/... — all green
- Live end-to-end: daemon spawned a real zcode worker in a worktree, TUI booted `--mode build`, prompt injected, permission dialog approved, file created; kill/restore round-trip verified
- Binary surface audited against the real zcode 0.16.5 CLI (no invented flags; the `--prompt` headless path deliberately avoided)

## Verification gap

- Frontend `npm run typecheck` and the api-drift CI job could not run locally (`node_modules` not installed in this worktree; `openapi-typescript` unavailable). Spec regen was verified drift-free via `npm run api:spec` (zero changes), and schema.ts changes were regenerated earlier in the branch. Please let CI confirm the TS side.

title: fix(updater): quiet automatic checks and hide the normal install window
body:
## Problem

Two dogfooding reports on a nightly build:

1. A red "Update check timed out. The update service did not respond in time." error appeared on launch, after the app had been idle for a day. A manual "Check for updates" then worked. The error was for a background check the user never asked for.
2. An "Installing and reopening AO" window appeared during the update install/restart. It is not needed on a normal update; the app should just reopen to its own loader.

## Change

Three focused fixes. All build on the already-merged staging watchdog (https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5479); none of that work is touched here.

- **Suppress the check-timeout error for automatic checks.** The deadline timer in `checkForUpdatesWithDeadline` broadcast a red error to the Settings panel even for a background launch check. On a cold network that stranded a failure the user could not act on. The timeout now surfaces only for user-initiated checks (manual and return-home); automatic timeouts still route through the existing UI suppression and the failing-checks nudge, so a persistent problem is still reported, just not as a startup banner.

- **Collapse the automatic re-check cadence to once a day on every channel.** The 15-minute nightly and hourly stable polling were redundant background work: a fresh check already runs on every launch, so the interval only governs sessions left open for a long stretch. Frequent polling on a cold network was also a source of the launch-time check errors above.

- **Keep the macOS progress helper hidden on a normal update.** `UpdateProgressState.stage()` previously surfaced a window after 30s of a slow-but-healthy quit and kept it up through install. It now stays hidden (accessory, no window) for the full three-minute budget and only presents a recovery window if the update is genuinely stuck (no close or no reopen after three minutes). The normal path is: AO closes, macOS installs silently, AO reopens to its own loader.

## Verification

Run on this branch checked out clean off `main`:

- `vitest run src/main/auto-updater.test.ts`: 176 passing, including the rewritten interval/cadence tests and the split automatic-vs-manual timeout assertion.
- Swift `StateTests` compiled and run: passing, including the new slow-but-healthy close/reopen cases and the three-minute recovery deadlines. The helper `main.swift` still compiles against the changed state module.
- Full-project `tsc --noEmit` could not be run to completion in the sandbox used here; CI runs it on this PR. The changes are type-local: a renamed numeric constant, an underscore-prefixed unused param, and an added guard on an existing module variable.

The slow-disk and disk-full staging paths are macOS-native (Squirrel) and are covered by 5479's test seam, not by a live run here.

title: feat(cli): ao ps — read-only process/RSS viewer for the AO footprint (daemon, tmux server, per-session trees, orphans)
body:
## Problem

When the machine gets slow or loud, there is no AO-native way to answer "how much is AO actually eating right now?" The only option is hand-grepping `ps`, and even then attribution is guesswork: the daemon, the Electron app, the tmux server, and the per-session worker trees (`ao pty-host` → `agent-process supervise` → agent) are indistinguishable without knowing the internal process topology.

This bites especially during the orphan accumulation described in #3537 / #2523: 63 orphaned processes (~3.6 GB idle RSS) piled up over 3 days on a 24 GB machine here, and the only way to find out was manual `ps` forensics. Swap was full, the memory-pressure guardian was killing unrelated dev servers — and `ao session ls` looked perfectly normal, because RSS is simply not surfaced anywhere.

## Proposal

A read-only `ao ps` command (optionally mirrored as a dashboard panel) that lists AO-owned processes with RSS, grouped and totaled:

| group | what | example |
|---|---|---|
| control plane | daemon itself, desktop app helpers | daemon: 90 MB, app: 310 MB |
| tmux server | the AO tmux server process | 45 MB |
| sessions | per-session tree totals, by session name | `worker-7`: pty-host 7 MB + supervise 6 MB + claude 180 MB |
| orphans | worker trees with PPID=1 / not in the daemon's live task set | 21 trees, 3.6 GB — candidates for reaping (see #2523) |

Deliberately minimal scope: **visibility only** — no caps, no killing. Enforcement belongs to #2523; attribution is the missing primitive both that and the reaper work can build on. A per-session RSS column in `ao session ls` (already floated as a nice-to-have in #2523) would be a natural companion.

## Why it matters

- "Is AO eating my memory, and which part — the daemon, tmux, or workers?" is currently unanswerable without expert `ps` usage.
- It makes the orphan problem visible days earlier: the fan-noise/swap phase of #3537 would show up as a fat "orphans" row instead of mysterious system-wide slowdown.
- The data is already known to the daemon (it owns the tmux server, session names, and spawn topology); this is mostly presentation.

title: fix(storage): write SQLite timestamps in UTC so non-UTC zones can read them back
body:
## Problem

In time zones whose abbreviation is numeric, AO cannot read back timestamps it wrote to SQLite. Asia/Colombo is one example: its abbreviation is `+0530`.

Unless `_timezone` is set, the modernc driver writes a `time.Time` as `t.String()` in the caller's zone:

```
2026-09-11 20:39:10.511227327 +0530 +0530 m=+73.186830353
```

The driver's parser reads the second `+0530` with the layout `-0700 MST`, and parsing fails. Every later `Scan` of that row errors with `unsupported Scan, storing driver.Value type string into type *time.Time`.

**Impact:**
- **Projects:** `ListProjects` fails as soon as one project is registered. In releases that seeded Scratch at boot, the daemon exited 1 on every start (`seed scratch project: Failed to load projects`).
- **Other code paths:** the same bug appears elsewhere. On current `main`, with the machine's zone set to Asia/Colombo, these existing store tests fail, and they pass with `TZ=UTC`:
  - `TestNativeCheckpointEvidenceRoundTripCASAndEpoch`
  - `TestPRChecksCDC_EmitsOnInsertAndStatusUpdate`
  - `TestWritePR_PersistsScalarsChecksAndComments`
  - `TestFreshInterfaceEpochReleasesOnlyUntouchedRootProvider`

CI runs in UTC, so it never sees these failures.

## Fix

- **Connection setting:** add `_timezone=UTC` to both the read-write and read-only DSNs in `storage/sqlite/db.go`. The driver then converts every time to UTC before writing it, which also drops the monotonic reading, and returns UTC on read. New rows use the same `... +0000 UTC` format that rows written from UTC machines already have, so stored values stay in one consistent format.
- **Migration `0148_repair_local_zone_project_timestamps.sql`:** rewrites `projects.registered_at` and `projects.archived_at` values that were stored with a local offset. Each value becomes the same instant in UTC, in the format the driver writes. Rows already in UTC, and values without a readable offset, are left unchanged. The down migration deliberately does nothing, because the original zone can't be recovered.

## Intentional omissions

The migration repairs only `projects`. Before this change, a tainted project row broke the project list, and in older releases stopped the daemon from starting, so affected installs couldn't build up tainted rows in other tables. I also scanned two affected real databases, and all their other timestamp columns were clean. If someone reports tainted values in other tables, a follow-up can extend the repair to them.

## Tests

- **`TestManager_AddPersistsRegisteredAtInUTC`:** registers a project with a clock in a `+0530` fixed zone, then reads it back through `GetProject` and `List`. Without the DSN change it fails with the scan error above.
- **`TestProjectTimestampRepairNormalizesLocalZoneValues`:** migrates tainted rows (IST with a monotonic suffix, a negative offset, an already-UTC row) and checks that every value scans back to the right instant. It fails if 0148 is removed.
- **Migration list:** 0148 is registered in `shippedMigrations`.

## Local validation

- **With the Asia/Colombo system zone:** `go test ./internal/storage/... ./internal/service/project/` passes, including the four store tests listed above that fail on `main`.
- **Full backend suite:** `TZ=UTC go test ./...` passes except `internal/integration` and `internal/service/agent`. Those two fail the same way on unmodified `main` on this machine: the Codex credential tests report "codex directory has a writable ancestor" from the environment.
- **Not run locally**, so these need CI:
  - `-race`: this machine has no C toolchain, so cgo is unavailable.
  - `golangci-lint`: not installed. `go vet` passes on the touched packages.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(chat): Resume agent returns 500 forever when a Codex thread was never materialized
body:
## Bug
If a Codex Chat session stops before its first user turn, "Resume agent" fails every time with a bare "Internal server error". Codex reserves a thread id on `thread/start` but writes no rollout until the first message. AO saves that reserved id as `provider_conversation_id`, and every resume sends `thread/resume` for it, which Codex rejects. The session can't be recovered from the UI: you can't send a message while the controller is stopped, and you can't restart the controller without a message. A project Orchestrator stuck this way blocks the whole project's coordinator.

**Reported by:** @Ayash-Bera | **Analyzed against:** `f006182a5` (origin/main), reproduced on desktop `0.13.1-nightly.202609170454`, codex-cli `0.153.4`, Linux
**Confidence:** High

## Evidence
Banner in the Orchestrator chat: "The agent controller stopped" / "Internal server error", and Resume agent fails on every click.

Daemon log for `POST /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-1/resume-agent` (captured with a scratch daemon on a copy of the same database, because the desktop app sends daemon output to `/dev/null`):

```text
status=500 error="resume agent agent-orchestrator-1: resume chat: chat conversation resume failed:
thread/resume: app-server error -32600: no rollout found for thread id 01a07f69-d0ce-7790-91e5-9922da24e81b"
```

Session and conversation state:

```text
sessions.agent-orchestrator-1: kind=orchestrator mode=chat harness=codex activity=exited
  provider_conversation_id=01a07f69-d0ce-7790-91e5-9922da24e81b
conversation 2a5645d1 (scope=project): conversation_turns=0, conversation_messages=0, provider_events=68
```

No rollout file exists for that id. `~/.codex/sessions/2026/09/08/` has rollouts on both sides of it (`01a07f53…` at 10:12, `01a07f9a…` at 11:30) and nothing for `01a07f69…`, and no archived copy exists. That fits a thread that was reserved and never materialized, since zero turns were ever sent.

## Reproduction
1. Create a Codex Chat session or project Orchestrator (chat mode).
2. Don't send a message. Stop the controller, for example by quitting or updating the desktop app.
3. Reopen the chat and click Resume agent.
4. HTTP 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`, and it fails again on every retry.

## Root Cause
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` `restoreArgv` (TUI) already guards this case: `conversationLost := ok && nativeConversationMissing(...)`, then falls back to `freshLaunchArgv`. Its comment describes this exact situation ("a session torn down before its first turn").
- The Chat path has no such guard. `relaunchSessionWithPolicyAndGeneration` only rejects an empty `ProviderConversationID`, and `resumeChatController` (`chat_spawn.go`) passes the saved id straight to `StartChat` with no `nativeConversationMissing` check.
- `codex.Plugin.NativeConversationExists` (`adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`) was written for this case too. Its doc says `thread/resume` "rejects that reserved-only UUID with 'no rollout found for thread id'".
- The error is not mapped to an API error, so the client only sees "Internal server error".

## Fix
In the Chat resume path, when native history is not required (`requireNativeHistory == false`) and the harness probe reports the native conversation missing, drop the dead provider id and start a fresh provider thread. That matches the TUI path. For orchestrators, `chat.Service` already records an "Agent context reset" boundary when `ProviderConversationID` is empty. Callers that require native history (account switch, interface transitions) should keep failing, with a mapped error instead of a 500.

## Impact
- A chat session or project Orchestrator stuck this way stays unusable until someone edits the database by hand or replaces the orchestrator.
- The message "Internal server error" gives no clue about the cause.

## Related
- [#5174](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5174): same Orchestrator chat, stale tool-server failures
- [#4481](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4481): kill on a missing tmux returned HTTP 500 (same unmapped-error pattern)
- [#5228](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5228): Codex Chat provider handle mismatch permanently blocking a session

title: [Bug]: Notification sound never plays on Linux — shell.beep() is a silent no-op for desktop-launched apps
body:
## Bug

With **Sound notifications** enabled (the default), the desktop app plays no sound on Linux when an agent needs input or a PR is ready to merge. Toasts and taskbar flashing still work; only the audible signal is missing.

**Source:** local observation (Arch Linux, Hyprland/Wayland, packaged AppImage 0.13.0) | **Reported by:** @Pyasma | **Analyzed against:** `f006182a5` (main)
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Linux desktop (tested: Arch, Hyprland, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`), launch the AO desktop app from the launcher / AppImage (i.e. not from a terminal).
2. Settings → General → leave **Sound notifications** on.
3. Unfocus the AO window and trigger a `needs_input` notification (any agent asking a question), or in a dev build call `__testNotif("needs_input")` from the renderer devtools.
4. Toast appears, window flashes, **no sound**.

## Root Cause

The only sound path is `shell.beep()`:

- `frontend/src/main.ts:2447-2449` — `notifications:show` handler
- `frontend/src/main.ts:2468-2470` — dev-only `notifications:devBounce`

Electron's Linux implementation of `shell.beep()` (`shell/common/platform_util_linux.cc`, v33) is:

```cpp
void Beep() {
  // echo '\a' > /dev/console
  FILE* fp = fopen("/dev/console", "a");
  if (fp == nullptr) {
    fp = fopen("/dev/tty", "a");
  }
  if (fp != nullptr) {
    fprintf(fp, "\a");
    fclose(fp);
  }
}
```

For a normal desktop launch both opens fail, so the call returns without doing anything and without reporting an error:

- `/dev/console` is `crw------- root root` — not writable by the user.
- `/dev/tty` needs a controlling terminal; the app has none when launched from a launcher/AppImage (`ps -o tty` shows `?`, stdin/stdout are `/dev/null`).

Even in the rare case one of the opens succeeds, `\a` is the PC-speaker/TTY bell, not audio output — on most modern desktops (Wayland especially) that is inaudible as well. So on Linux the "Sound notifications" toggle is effectively a no-op, and `soundNotificationsEnabled` defaults to `true`, so users expect a sound that can never arrive.

The beep was introduced in [PR #4051](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4051) and behaves as intended on macOS (`NSBeep`) and Windows (`MessageBeep`); the Linux branch is what is broken.

## Fix

Play a real audio asset instead of relying on `shell.beep()` on Linux (or on all platforms, for consistency):

- Bundle a short default sound in the app resources and play it from the renderer via an `<audio>` element / `Audio` — main cannot play audio itself, so `notifications:show` would send a `notifications:playSound` message back to the shell webContents (the same mechanism the closed custom-sound [PR #5282](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5282) used for user-supplied files).
- Alternatively, on Linux only, shell out to a system player (`canberra-gtk-play -i bell`, `paplay`, `pw-play`) as a fallback — heavier and less portable, so the renderer approach is preferred.
- Keep `shell.beep()` for macOS/Windows if a native beep is desired there.

The custom-sound work in [PR #5282](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5282) already contains the renderer playback plumbing; a minimal fix could land just the "bundled default sound played by the renderer" part without the file-picker UI.

## Impact

- Every Linux user: the sound toggle does nothing, so agents blocked on input are missed unless the user notices the toast / taskbar flash.
- The toggle is on by default, so this reads as "notifications are broken" rather than "feature unavailable".
- No error is logged anywhere, which makes it hard to diagnose.

## Related

- [PR #4051](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4051) — introduced `shell.beep()` for `needs_input` / `ready_to_merge`
- [#5035](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5035) / [PR #5282](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5282) — custom notification sound (closed); contains renderer-side audio playback that would also fix this

title: feat(session): worker watchdog with switch_recovery_pending
body:
Code changes: +849 -29  
Tests: +977 -3  
Others: +241 -0 (generated: openapi.yaml, schema.ts, sqlc gen)

## What

Adds a read-time worker watchdog that surfaces sessions needing a human, derived from durable facts only (never persisted), plus a new `switch_recovery_pending` verdict for agent switches wedged on an ambiguous ownership boundary.

- `AttentionReason` vocabulary extended with `switch_recovery_pending`; `domain/watchdog.go` owns the reason and the project-resolvable thresholds (`stalled`, `questionPending`, `consecutiveInfraErrors`).
- Derivation order: terminated (never flags) → pause states (decision/question) → wedged switch → consecutive provider-error rules → active-quiet stall catch-all.
- **Switch verdict** fires immediately once `AgentSwitch.RequiresRecovery()` matches — exactly the three retained markers `source_stop_unconfirmed`, `target_start_unconfirmed`, `source_restore_unconfirmed`. Healthy mid-switch sagas stay silent; terminated sessions never flag; the verdict auto-clears on the first read after the row clears.
- Detail names the harness pair, the stable error code, and how long the saga has been wedged, with the Restore affordance; `lastWorkerErrorAt` anchors on the switch's `UpdatedAt` (falling back to `RequestedAt`).
- `List`/`Get` load the active switch once and reuse it for both the `ActiveAgentSwitch` projection and the verdict — no new query, no migration for the switch path.
- Worker-error classification: TLS/certificate handshake failures (`certificate`, `cert`, `tls`, `ssl`) now classify as transient retryable errors instead of unknown.
- Durable worker-error log: migration `0148_session_worker_errors.sql`, sqlc queries + store, recorded from `SettleTurn`/`SettleTurnByID`, bounded per session.

## Tests

- `go build ./...` clean; `go vet ./...` clean.
- `go test ./internal/domain/... ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/httpd/...` pass.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` → **0 issues** (clean cache, serial run).
- Full `go test ./...`: only the repo's pre-existing environment-dependent failures (tmux binary / `gh` / agent-binary packages: `runtime/tmux`, `session_manager`, `systemcheck`, `cli`, `agent/fake`, `agent/goose`, `agent/pi`). No touched package fails.
- New coverage: switch-recovery table tests for all three retained markers, healthy mid-switch silence, terminated-never-flags, pause-state and error-rule precedence, detail contents, auto-clear; classifier cases for TLS/certificate; service fake-store `List`/`Get` verdict + projection + clear cases.

## Notes

- `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated in the same commit for the new enum value.
- Frontend typecheck was not run locally (`node_modules` absent in this worktree); CI covers it.
- Continues the watchdog work started on `ao/agent-orchestrator-10/watchdog`.

title: fix(chat): swallow settled-turn 409 on Stop instead of trapping the composer
body:
Code changes: +14 -2
Tests: +40 -0
Others: +0 -0

## What
Pressing Stop on a Chat turn that already settled returned red 409 CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN ('there is no turn in flight to interrupt') and left it as a persistent red composer banner. Since the backend 409s only when in-memory tracking AND SQLite agree no turn is running, the rendered 'running' row is necessarily stale — the end state the user wanted is already true, and the mutation's onError refetch reconciles the view. Surfacing the 409 as an error traps the user into pressing Stop into the same 409.

This filters CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN out of the interrupt error surfaced in commands.error (genuine failures — network, provider refusal — still surface; the onError snapshot refetch is unchanged).

## Tests
- frontend: useConversation.test.tsx 45/45 pass, incl. 2 new tests (409 swallowed with refetch triggered and no error; non-settlement interrupt failures still surface)
- ChatComposer / TaskComposer / event-transport suites: 175/175 pass
- frontend typecheck: 0 errors under src/ (only pre-existing missing-module errors under ../packages/product-ui from the partial monorepo install)
- No backend changes; live-checked the running daemon to confirm the 409-vs-snapshot invariant (snapshot running rows match durable running rows outside the reported stuck state)

## Risks
- If a snapshot refetch itself fails, Stop stays visible with no error shown until the next press surfaces the real failure. Acceptable: the alternative (today) is a guaranteed-misleading red 409.
- No API, migration, or generated-file changes.

title: cloud: robust worker self-heal so a stale baked binary is a non-event (nodeops helper-path mismatch + coder PTY-stream reliability)
body:
## Problem

Every control-plane deploy that changes the `ao-worker` / `ao` binary silently breaks cloud sessions until the provider templates are manually rebaked, because the worker's baked-in copies go stale and the self-heal does not actually land the fresh binary where the runtime uses it. This has recurred on both providers (nodeops capture breakage; coder worker-bootstrap failures) and is currently worked around with manual `publish-nodeops-template.sh` / `publish-coder-workspace.sh` rebakes per deploy.

Goal: a stale bake becomes a **non-event** — the worker self-heals the current binaries to the exact paths the harness, hooks, and bootstrap invoke — so no template rebake is required for a worker change.

## Root cause 1 — nodeops helper-path mismatch (breaks event-based capture)

- The claude Stop hook (and the other activity hooks) invoke a **hardcoded absolute path**: `cloudHookBinary = "/usr/local/bin/ao"` (`cloud/internal/workerexec/activity_hooks.go:9`, used at :45 and :88).
- `healHelper` heals the current `ao` helper **only into `$AO_DATA_DIR/bin/ao`** and depends on it shadowing the baked copy *on PATH* (`cloud/cmd/ao-worker/selfupdate.go`, `healHelper`). It never writes `/usr/local/bin/ao`.
- The worker runs as `ao-worker` (uid 1001) and cannot overwrite `/usr/local/bin` (root-owned), so the baked helper stays stale.
- Result: the Stop hook runs the **stale baked** `/usr/local/bin/ao`, which lacks `pokeCheckpoint`, so durable-restore capture never fires. (Observed on staging: baked helper `20dd1ba…` vs CP-expected `cd4149b7…`; capture produced 0 rows until a manual per-sandbox overwrite + template rebake.)

### Fix options
- (Preferred, no elevated perms) Stop pointing the hook at `/usr/local/bin/ao`. Point `cloudHookBinary` and `AO_WORKER_HELPER_PATH` at the **healed** path (`$AO_DATA_DIR/bin/ao`), which the worker owns and self-heal keeps current. The bootstrap already sets `AO_WORKER_HELPER_PATH`; make the hook use it (or the healed override) instead of a hardcoded absolute path.
- (Alternative) Have the bootstrap install the healed helper to `/usr/local/bin/ao` using the elevated perms it already has (it runs the launch via `sudo`), so the absolute path everything uses is always current.

## Root cause 2 — coder PTY-stream fallback is unreliable (breaks worker bootstrap)

- #5329 added preinstalled-miss detection (`__AO_PREINSTALLED_MISS__`, `errPreinstalledWorkerDoesNotMatch`) and a `bootstrapWorkerThroughPTY` fallback in `cloud/internal/sandbox/coder/client.go`.
- When the baked worker is stale, the fast path correctly misses, but the fallback fails with `coder: read workspace PTY before worker upload: EOF` and `AO worker exited during startup __AO_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED__` — so a stale coder bake fails to bootstrap instead of cleanly streaming the current worker. (Observed on staging: coder workspace baked worker `d6ce491…` vs CP-expected `0eea515…`; sessions could not connect until the workspace image was reseeded.)

### Fix
- Make `bootstrapWorkerThroughPTY` robust to the PTY read (retry/handle the EOF, ensure the launch/upload handshake completes) so the streamed worker path reliably delivers the current binary whenever the baked SHA does not match `AO_WORKER_EXPECTED_SHA256`.

## Acceptance

- Deploy a CP with a changed `ao-worker`/`ao` **without** rebaking either template. A fresh nodeops session auto-captures on turn completion (Stop hook runs the current helper), and a fresh coder session bootstraps its worker via the stream fallback. No manual `publish-*-template` step required for correctness (rebakes remain a pure launch-speed optimization).

## Context / related
Documented in prior debugging: the nodeops rebake process gap and the coder reseed. Deploys that change the worker currently MUST go through `deploy-staging.sh` (which rebakes both templates) — this issue removes that hard dependency for correctness.

title: feat(cloud): session delete and restore, with terminal-epoch reconnect, first-click delete, and worker self-heal (#5518)
body:
Cloud session delete and restore, plus the reliability fixes surfaced while validating it end to end on staging.

## Feature
- Delete a cloud session (or project) and restore it later under the same session_id: the conversation and uncommitted work are captured to `ao_session_transcripts` (durable transcript blob + a preserved git ref) and rehydrated into a fresh sandbox on restore. Capture is event driven off the harness Stop hook. Provider agnostic (nodeops + coder).
- Migration `00039_session_restore` (renumbered from `00037` to avoid the collision with `00037_turns_allow_queued_fanin`).

## Reliability fixes (found and fixed during E2E)
- Terminal reconnect on the worker epoch: the cloud terminal is now keyed on the session's `workerEpoch`, so a resume from idle-pause, a restore, or any re-provision re-mints the terminal against the live agent instead of clinging to the dead epoch's exited terminal. Fixes the "connected but TERMINAL ENDED / can't type" loop, where nothing attached and the session then idle-paused again.
- Delete terminates the session on the first click: `deleteSession` now sets `is_terminated=true` and requests the sandbox teardown atomically (new `TerminateSession`, the inverse of `RestoreSession`), instead of only setting the sandbox `desired_state` and racing the idle scanner. The board archives it immediately; no more repeated clicks.
- Robust worker self-heal so a stale baked binary is a non-event (Closes #5518, part 1): the harness hooks now invoke the self-healed helper at `<dataDir>/bin/ao` instead of a hardcoded `/usr/local/bin/ao`, and `healHelper` always keeps that path current. This stops the recurring stale-bake breakage where the Stop hook ran the stale baked helper (no `pokeCheckpoint`) and durable capture silently stopped until a manual template rebake. Coder PTY-stream reliability (part 2 of #5518) remains open.

## Testing
Validated on staging: capture on turn completion, delete then restore round trip (conversation + uncommitted work returned), resume from idle-pause reconnects, delete archives on first click. Cloud module `go build/vet/test` green; renderer typecheck + vitest green.

Closes #5518
