title: feat: reveal tab close button in the icon slot on hover
body:
Code changes: +47 -70
Tests: +10 -15
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Shell terminal tabs and session file tabs previously revealed their close button on the **trailing** edge of the tab on hover. Now, matching common browser/editor tab behavior:

- **Terminal tabs** (connected session strip): hovering or keyboard-focusing a tab fades the terminal glyph out and reveals the × in the icon's slot on the left.
- **File tabs**: same treatment — the × overlays the file icon's slot and appears on hover/focus. Dirty files keep the always-visible unsaved dot in that slot, which swaps to the × on hover.
- **Removed the per-tab "+" (add feedback) button** from file tabs. Whole-file feedback remains available from the file workspace header; the unused `files.addFileFeedback` i18n key is removed from all locales.

## Implementation notes

- Both tabs reuse `TerminalTabFrame`'s existing `actionLayout="overlay"` / `actionPosition="leading"` path — no new chrome was added; the close control stays a sibling button (never nested inside the tab button), so keyboard traversal and aria roles are unchanged.
- The glyph only fades when a close action actually exists (not while renaming or for optimistic terminals).

## Testing

- `SessionFileTabs.test.tsx`: asserts the icon hides on hover, the close button sits in the leading overlay, and the dirty dot swaps to the × on hover.
- `ShellTerminalTab.test.tsx`: "reveals close in the terminal glyph's slot on hover" replaces the old trailing-position assertions.
- `SessionView.test.tsx`: the tab-feedback test now toggles the composer via the workspace header (the tab "+" entry point is gone).
- Verified locally: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, and the renderer vitest suites for the touched areas all pass. Manually verified in a dev Electron instance (isolated mode) by hovering both tab types.

**Local validation gap:** the `src/landing` vitest files cannot run in this worktree because `@ao/shared` has no resolvable package content here; those tests are untouched by this diff and are left to CI.

title: perf(landing): cut first-load weight from 2.8 MB to 0.96 MB
body: ## Why `https://orchestrator.inc/` shipped **2.8 MB** on first load, **2.2 MB of it images**, and almost all of those images were fetched at preload priority *before* the hero could paint. Root causes, in order of weight: 1. **`public/app-icons/cursor.svg` was 1.5 MB** — a 36×36 icon wrapping a 2000×2000 base64 PNG (1.17 MB gzipped over the wire). It was preloaded in ``, so it competed with the LCP image on every visit. Two lines in `FleetBoardDemo` referenced it; an identical **542 B** vector mark already existed at `app-icons/agents/cursor.svg`. 2. **47 image preloads in ``.** React 19 hoists a `` for every non-lazy `` rendered on the server, so every agent mark in every below-the-fold demo was fetched at top priority. 3. **`layout.tsx` preloaded five feature backgrounds on every route** — 374 KB downloaded on `/blog`, `/docs`, `/privacy`, where they are never rendered. 4. **No responsive delivery.** `output: "export"` forces `images.unoptimized`, so `next/image` emitted a single fixed-width source: phones downloaded the same 1440–1600 px art as desktops. 5. **Oversized icons**: agent marks at 384 px and 128 px rendered at 12–32 px; `ao-logo.svg` a 57 KB path blob for a 20 px mark. 6. **Duplicated libraries**: `framer-motion` *and* `motion` both installed and both imported; `geist/font/mono` (71 KB) preloaded for two below-the-fold demos next to the IBM Plex Mono the rest of the site uses. Separately, `public/` held **43 MB of PNG masters no page references**. `output: "export"` copies `public/` verbatim, so all of it was deployed. ## What changed - `app-icons/cursor.svg` deleted; `FleetBoardDemo` uses the vector mark. - `loading="lazy"` + `decoding="async"` on below-the-fold ``s. Preloads in the served HTML: **47 → 10**, and all 10 are hero elements. - Route-wide preloads removed from `layout.tsx`; the hero preloads itself through its own ``. - Hero: single-format WebP `srcset` (720/1080/1440). Single-format on purpose — with a `` the preload scanner and the element can pick different candidates and download the hero twice. - Feature backgrounds: `` with AVIF + WebP fallback at 640/960/1280, lazy. - Icons regenerated at 64 px; `ao-logo.svg` run through SVGO. - Source art moved to `assets/` (outside `public/`); `scripts/optimize-images.mjs` (`npm run images:optimize`) regenerates every shipped variant from it. - `framer-motion` removed (12 files now import `motion/react`); Geist Mono dropped for the site's IBM Plex Mono; `@sentry/nextjs` loads only if the error boundary fires. - `DEPLOYMENT.md` documents the Cloudflare cache rules for `/_next/static/*` (GitHub Pages serves everything `max-age=14400`, including content-hashed chunks, and Actions-based Pages deploys ignore `_headers`). ## Benchmarks Headless Chrome over CDP against both builds served from the same local static server (brotli for text, cold cache, fresh profile per run). **Runs are interleaved before/after per iteration**, so machine drift lands on both variants. Medians; LCP range in brackets. Harness and raw output: see "Reproducing" below. ### Desktop — 1440×900, 30 Mbps / 10 ms, no CPU throttle, median of 6 | Metric | Before | After | Δ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **LCP** | 336 ms [332–444] | **200 ms** [196–316] | **−40%** | | FCP | 144 ms | 116 ms | −19% | | `load` | 799 ms | 254 ms | −68% | | **Transfer** | 2820 KB | **959 KB** | **−66%** | | — images | 2224 KB | 452 KB | −80% | | — fonts | 168 KB | 98 KB | −42% | | — JS | 337 KB | 320 KB | −5% | | Requests | 100 | 73 | −27% | | CLS | 0.0007 | 0.0003 | — | ### Mobile — 390×844 @2x, Slow 4G (1.6 Mbps / 150 ms), 4× CPU, median of 5 | Metric | Before | After | Δ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **LCP** | 6080 ms [6068–6112] | **1652 ms** [1644–1696] | **−73%** | | FCP | 1028 ms | 988 ms | −4% | | `load` | 12764 ms | 3245 ms | −75% | | **Transfer** | 2486 KB | **648 KB** | **−74%** | | — images | 1906 KB | 154 KB | −92% | | Requests | 85 | 58 | −32% | | Total blocking time | 42 ms | 7 ms | −83% | | CLS | 0.0082 | 0.0029 | −65% | The run-to-run spread is ±2% on mobile and ±1% on desktop except for first-iteration warm-up, which is why the ranges are printed. ### Per asset (bytes on disk) | Asset | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `app-icons/cursor.svg` | 1,575,673 | **removed** | | hero background | 221,118 (1 size) | 152,500 @1440 / 87,232 @1080 / 37,304 @720 | | `feature3` | 143,680 | 69,808 webp / 40,283 avif @1280 · 6,688 avif @640 | | `agents/aider.png` | 93,930 | 4,132 | | `agents/agy.png` | 25,278 | 3,026 | | `agents/muse.png` | 20,037 | 3,189 | | `ao-logo.svg` | 57,373 | 22,540 | | `app-icons/terminal.png`, `coverage-aider.png` | 150,000 | **removed** (unreferenced) | | **Deployed `out/`** | **62.8 MB** | **17.6 MB** | ### Visual verification Full-page screenshots of both builds at 1440 px, captured after a stepped scroll so lazy art loads: - Page height identical: **7572 px → 7572 px** (no layout shift from the markup change). - Mean per-pixel difference across 8 horizontal bands: **≤ 2.4/255**, concentrated in the animated demo panels and attributable to re-encoding plus the mono-font swap. - Re-encoded art vs the old files at matched size: mean difference 2.5–2.7/255. - `ao-logo.svg` rasterized at 128 px before vs after SVGO: **max channel difference 1/255**. ## Honest caveats - **The Sentry change is hygiene, not 60 KB.** `@sentry/nextjs` was already mostly code-split; the eagerly-loaded chunk containing SDK code was 16 KB raw (~5 KB br). After the change no chunk on the landing page's initial graph contains it. My original estimate for this item was wrong; the measured first-load JS saving is ~2 KB, and the rest of the −17 KB JS is the `framer-motion`/`motion` de-duplication. - **Cache rules are documented, not applied.** They are Cloudflare dashboard config; repeat-visit gains are therefore not measured here. - **Lazy feature art can pop in** if a visitor scrolls faster than Chrome's ~1250 px lazy threshold loads. This is the trade for taking 374 KB out of the critical path. - The two terminal demos now render in IBM Plex Mono rather than Geist Mono. This is the one intentional visual change. - Benchmarks run against a local static server, not GitHub Pages behind Cloudflare; they isolate this diff rather than predicting absolute field numbers. - `sharp` was already a devDependency; `svgo` is added as one. Neither ships to visitors. ## Reproducing ```bash cd frontend/src/landing && npm ci && npm run build # out/ # serve out/ with brotli, drive headless Chrome over CDP, interleave A/B, # report medians (harness kept out of the diff; happy to add it if useful) ``` `npm run images:optimize` regenerates every asset under `public/optimized`, `public/app-icons` and `public/ao-logo.svg` from `assets/`. ## Verification run - `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean (only the pre-existing `Cannot find module 'vitest'` errors in test files, unchanged by this PR). - `npm run build`: succeeds. - `npm run icons:check`: passes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(lifecycle): an agent's own review-thread reply is nudge-eligible - AO delivers the agent's own comment back to it as review work
body:
## Bug

An agent's **own** review-thread reply is nudge-eligible, so AO delivers the agent's words back to it as review feedback to "address and push fixes" for. Nothing in the nudge path checks whether the comment author is the identity the session itself comments and pushes with.

**Source:** maintainer local report (desktop app, macOS, this machine) | **Reported by:** maintainer | **Analyzed against:** `3e46ad3b4` (origin/main), observed on branch `8c4285c62`
**AO version:** `dev` | **Confidence:** High for the self-nudge mechanism; Medium for the resolved-state disagreement in Secondary below
**Priority:** medium - wastes agent turns, and becomes a feedback loop for any agent that replies to a review thread without resolving it

## Reproduction

1. Give a session a PR and set `sessions.auto_inject_review = 1`.
2. Have any reviewer (here: React Doctor, a GitHub App) open inline review threads.
3. From the session, reply on those threads using the same account AO pushes with (`gh api graphql addPullRequestReviewThreadReply`).
4. Wait for the next SCM poll.

The session receives a nudge whose body is its own reply, prefixed with *"The following 1 unresolved review comment(s) are on PR ... Address each comment and push fixes."*

## Live evidence

Session `agent-orchestrator-9`, [PR #5573](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5573):

| Time (UTC) | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 06:31:13 | React Doctor opens 12 inline threads (all `github-actions`, `__typename: Bot`) |
| 06:50:16 | Agent replies on all 12 threads as `AgentWrapper` (`__typename: User`) and resolves each via `resolveReviewThread` |
| 06:50:42 | SCM observer writes 12 threads `resolved=1, is_bot=0`, 12 bot comments `is_bot=1, resolved=1`, 12 agent replies `is_bot=0, resolved=1` |
| 06:50:42 | One nudge fires, keyed to the agent's own reply |

`pr.last_nudge_signature` recorded one attempt whose `seen` value is the pair
`PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6jpPWf` + `PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7xEbOT` (thread and comment IDs, NUL-separated).
`PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7xEbOT` is the agent's own reply on `RoadmapSlideshow.tsx:3`; the delivered
message quoted it back verbatim and told the agent to address it and push.

## Root Cause

Bot-ness is computed per *thread* as "every comment is a bot comment", so one reply declassifies the thread:

```go
// backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go - scmThreadFromGraphQL
allCommentsBot := len(commentNodes) > 0
for _, cn := range commentNodes {
    if !isBotAuthor(author) { allCommentsBot = false }
    ...
}
out.IsBot = allCommentsBot
```

Persistence inherits that down onto comments, so the agent's reply lands as `is_bot=0`:

```go
// backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go:1830
comments = append(comments, domain.PullRequestComment{..., Resolved: th.Resolved, IsBot: c.IsBot || th.IsBot, ...})
```

And the nudge filter only knows about `Resolved` and `IsBot` - never about who AO itself is:

```go
// backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:642 - prCommentObservations
if comment.Resolved || comment.IsBot { continue }
```

`backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:265-283` then emits one nudge per surviving comment, so every self-authored reply is one more nudge (bounded only by `reviewMaxNudge`).

### Secondary, lower confidence

The delivered message asserted the comment was **unresolved**, yet every persisted row for that PR reads `resolved=1`, and the `resolveReviewThread` mutations completed 26 s before `pr.review_observed_at`. Either GitHub's GraphQL returned a stale `isResolved` for that one thread immediately after the mutation, or nudge evaluation and the resolved write disagree within a single poll. Pinning this needs daemon logs from the poll at `06:50:42Z`, which were not available locally; treating it as a separate, smaller defect is reasonable.

## Fix

Skip comments authored by the session's own provider identity when selecting nudge candidates. The identity is already available - `pr.author` is `AgentWrapper` on the PR row, and the SCM adapter authenticates as that account - so the filter can sit next to the existing one:

```go
// prCommentObservations
if comment.Resolved || comment.IsBot || isSelfAuthored(comment.Author, prAuthor) { continue }
```

Sourcing it from the SCM auth identity (a `whoami`-style lookup, cached per provider) is more correct than `pr.author`, since a human can also open a PR that a session later claims. Either way the check belongs in the lifecycle, not the adapter.

No fix pushed: choosing where the session's provider identity comes from is a design call, and getting it wrong would silently drop legitimate human feedback. Worth spawning an agent once that decision is made.

## Impact

- Agents burn turns "addressing" their own comments, and an agent that replies without resolving can be re-nudged up to `reviewMaxNudge` times with its own text.
- Interacts badly with [#2827](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2827): today bot review comments are dropped entirely, so agents rarely reply to bot threads. Fixing #2827 means agents *will* reply to them, turning every reply into a fresh nudge unless this is fixed first or alongside.

title: bug(updater): Linux quitAndInstall has no relaunch verification, app can go silently dead after nightly update
body:
## Bug

On Linux, an auto-update relaunch (either the "Restart to update" button or an automatic install-on-quit) can leave the desktop app completely dead: no Electron process, no bundled daemon, nothing, indefinitely, with no error surfaced to the user. Only discovered because the previous session's `daemon.log` stopped abruptly and `~/.ao/staged-update.json` plus `~/.ao/update-restart/relaunch-flag.json` were both present on disk with a `fromPID` for a process that no longer existed. No new process of any kind was running until the app was manually relaunched from its AppImage over 5 hours later.

**Source:** local occurrence, self-diagnosed | **Reported by:** @Ayash-Bera | **Analyzed against:** `3e46ad3b4` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** Medium

## Reproduction

1. Run the Linux AppImage build with the nightly channel enabled and auto-update on.
2. Let the app detect and stage a new nightly (`staged-update.json` written via `stagedUpdateFile()` in `auto-updater.ts`).
3. Let it call `quitAndInstallUpdate()`, which invokes `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall(false, true)`, either via the "Restart to update" button or an automatic install-on-quit.
4. If electron-updater's `AppImageUpdater` install/relaunch step fails for any reason (the outer AppImage path not matching what `process.env.APPIMAGE` reports, a `--appimage-extract-and-run` temp mount getting cleaned up mid-flight, a transient install error, etc), the old process has already quit and no new process is spawned.
5. Result: `~/.ao/staged-update.json` and `~/.ao/update-restart/relaunch-flag.json` are left on disk referencing a dead PID, and the app is simply gone. Nothing running, nothing visible, no dialog, no crash report.

Not consistently reproducible on demand (I could not force step 4 to fail synthetically without patching electron-updater). This is a report of a real occurrence with full forensic detail from the state left behind, not a lab repro.

## Root Cause

`frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`'s `quitAndInstallUpdate()` (around L2094-2114) calls `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall(false, true)` unconditionally on non-darwin platforms. Compare to the macOS path:

- `getMacInstallBlocker()` (around L2035-2068) checks the running bundle's location is writable before letting the click proceed, and shows a blocking dialog if not.
- `applyInstallOnQuitPolicy()` (around L2076-2090) disables `autoInstallOnAppQuit` when that blocker fires, so a bad install-on-quit never fires silently.
- The native macOS helper (`mac-update-progress.ts`) additionally watches for the install to actually complete via its own `update-restart/active.json` marker and terminate handshake.

There is no equivalent for Linux (or Windows): no preflight check that the install can succeed from the app's current location, and per `frontend/src/main/update-relaunch-flag.ts`'s own doc comment, "here it is the only such signal (no native helper)" for non-darwin, meaning nothing on Linux confirms the relaunch actually happened. If `quitAndInstall()`'s underlying install/relaunch fails on Linux, the app quits anyway and there is no watchdog, no retry, and no user-facing error.

This is adjacent to but distinct from [#3679](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3679) (identity-mismatch after relaunch, which does self-recover within seconds via the `daemon_unreachable` fallback path). In my case there was no self-recovery at all, for over 5 hours, because no new process of any kind ever started.

It is also distinct from [PR #5206](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5206)'s "No update filepath provided" fix, which addresses a specific electron-updater in-memory-state gap on quit-and-install and clears stale `staged-update.json` after 3 failed automatic checks, but nothing there retries or verifies that a successful `quitAndInstall()` call actually produced a running process.

## Fix

Add a Linux equivalent of the macOS relaunch-verification pattern:

- Preflight: verify the AppImage path (`process.env.APPIMAGE`) is writable before calling `quitAndInstall()`, mirroring the macOS bundle/parent-writable check.
- Post-install watchdog: some independent, minimal mechanism (a small detached watcher process spawned right before quit, checked on a short timer) that can tell if the relaunch never happened and either retry or surface an error, since `markUpdateRelaunch()`'s flag in `update-relaunch-flag.ts` is currently only ever consumed by the app itself on its next boot, which never comes if the boot never happens.
- At minimum: do not leave `staged-update.json` pointing at a version that was never actually reached, so the next manual launch does not inherit confusing state.

## Impact

- The app can go from fully working to completely unresponsive and invisible with zero error surfaced, indistinguishable from "did I break my install" for the user.
- Manual recovery requires knowing to inspect `~/.ao/*.json` and relaunch the AppImage directly. Not discoverable by an average user.

## Related

- [#3679](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3679): relaunch-to-update identity mismatch, same subsystem, but self-recovers; this does not.
- [PR #5206](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5206): related non-darwin quitAndInstall hardening, does not cover this path.
- [#3528](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3528): same silent-failure pattern on Windows/Squirrel (ENOSPC), different platform and mechanism.

title: fix(updater): publish AppImage blockMapSize so Linux updates diff
body:
Code changes: +72 -20
Tests: +291 -2
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #5576. Linux AppImage updates always attempted a differential download: AppImageUpdater reads the new build's blockmap from the AppImage's own embedded tail at `size - (blockMapSize + 4)`, and AO's feed never published blockMapSize, so the offset was NaN, every attempt died with ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE before fetching a byte, and each update fell back to a full ~186MB download.

The maker already appends an embedded blockmap (deflate + 4-byte big-endian size footer) to every AppImage at build time (makers/maker-appimage.ts -> app-builder-lib appendBlockmap, both build paths). The feed now reads that footer via readEmbeddedBlockMapSize, validates it (blockmap v2 whose chunk sizes cover the file exactly: sum(sizes) + blockMapSize + 4 === file size), and emits blockMapSize on linux feed entries. A corrupt or absent tail publishes nothing and the updater falls back to a full download, same as pre-fix clients.

With blockMapSize published, AppImageUpdater range-reads only the new tail (a few hundred KB), diffs against the running AppImage's embedded map, and downloads just the changed chunks. The new appimage-differential-reconstruction.test.mjs drives the real electron-updater against a loopback server: a 512,683-byte fixture AppImage is reconstructed byte-identically (digest-validated by the updater) after transferring 98,875 bytes, plus fallback coverage for a missing old tail, servers rejecting ranges, legacy feeds without blockMapSize, and digest corruption. Win feeds deliberately stay without blockMapSize so the NSIS sidecar path keeps working; mac feeds are untouched.

Per the maintainer review on this PR, disabling differential downloads was only a workaround; this replaces it with the metadata fix that makes embedded AppImage differential actually work.

The linux .blockmap sidecars remain generated but are consumed by nothing; removing them is tracked on #3288 workstream 3.

No visual behavior changes, so no screenshots are applicable.

Validation: full frontend suite passes (324 files, 4935 tests, 7 skipped), typecheck passes, targeted auto-updater/feed/blockmap/AppImage-reconstruction suites pass on the rebased base. The mac-differential-v2 and blockmap-reconstruction suites require a system `zip` binary (cross-zip); installed via nix shell locally to run them.

- Detached relaunch watchdog (`linux-update-watchdog.ts`): armed before the explicit install and at quit when install-on-quit is active. Waits for the old process to die, confirms the next build came up (a running process holding the AppImage path, or the relaunch marker consumed), respawns the newest AppImage when nothing does, and on total failure retires the update state and writes a one-shot failure marker.

title: refactor(tmux): run the launch prelude under /bin/sh and drop the dead $SHELL launcher-shell plumbing
body:
### Problem

The tmux adapter resolves `$SHELL` and uses it as the interpreter for AO's own POSIX launch prelude:

```
tmux new-session ... <shellPath> -c '<cd ...; export ...; <agent argv>; exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -i>'
```

`buildLaunchCommand` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go`) emits pure POSIX (`cd`, `unset`, `export`, `exec`), so the interpreter choice is invisible for bash/zsh and only matters when `$SHELL` is a non-POSIX shell — where it breaks the launch outright (fish exits 127 on `export VAR=VAL`, see #3788).

Since the native PTY host landed (#4473 macOS, #4727 Linux), new sessions on macOS/Linux exec their argv directly and never touch this code. The `$SHELL -c` path is now only reachable via:

- the tmux fallback when the direct PTY host fails to spawn (`runtimeselect/hybrid.go`), and
- pre-rollout handles without the `ptyhost-v1:` prefix, which route to tmux permanently (`runtimeselect/runtimeselect.go`).

That is exactly the path that has to work when the primary host is unavailable, and today it fails for fish/nushell/tcsh users.

### Proposed direction

1. Pass `/bin/sh` as the `-c` interpreter in `Create` and `Restart` (`tmux.go`), instead of `r.shell`.
2. Delete the plumbing that only exists to feed it: `Options.Shell`, `Runtime.shell`, the `$SHELL`/`/bin/sh` resolution in `New`, and the test fixtures that set `Shell:` explicitly (`tmux_test.go`, `shellterm/tmux_integration_test.go`).
3. Drop `TestNewDefaultsToPortableShell` / `TestNewPicksUpShellFromEnv`; the prelude interpreter is no longer configurable.
4. Leave `exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -i` in the prelude alone — that is the user's interactive shell after the agent exits, and it works fine under fish.

This also resolves #3788 on the tmux path.

### Alternatives considered

- **PR #3789** adds `launcherShell()` with a denylist (fish, nu, csh, tcsh, elvish, xonsh). It works, but it is a list to maintain, it keeps the `$SHELL` plumbing alive, and the prelude never needs anything but POSIX sh. If #3789 lands first, that function becomes dead code too.
- **Keep `$SHELL` for POSIX shells, fall back otherwise**: same behavior as always using `/bin/sh`, with more code.
- **Remove the tmux runtime entirely**: out of scope here. It is still the fallback and the legacy-handle route, and `frontend/forge.config.ts` still ships bundled tmux.

title: fix(cloud/terminal): ignore zero-dimension resize instead of closing the socket
body:
## Problem

A cloud agent terminal in the browser connects, then flashes blank and reconnects in a loop (reported as "connected, then Connecting, then a glitch, then the terminal again", and "connected, blank screen, then the terminal"). Each cycle the user sees the screen wiped and repainted.

## Root cause (confirmed on staging with per-close diagnostics, not inferred)

The browser's first frame after every attach was a `resize` with `columns=0, rows=0`. A pane that fits while its element is not yet laid out (hidden behind the connecting cover, or mounted before layout) proposes a 0x0 grid.

The control plane treated a zero-dimension resize as invalid and closed the socket (`connection.Close(StatusPolicyViolation, "invalid terminal size")`). readTerminalInput returning ended the stream, so the client reconnected, which replays from sequence 0 with a screen reset (the blank flash), whereupon the pane fit at 0x0 again and the socket was closed again. An endless reconnect+flash loop.

Evidence from staging logs while the loop was live:
- Every looping socket died with `close_source=read`, nil error, `connected_ms` around 550 to 720ms.
- The first frame on those sockets was `type=resize columns=0 rows=0`.
- The one terminal in the same window that sent a valid `102x37` first frame never looped.
- After this fix, those exact terminal ids attached once more and held a stable open socket with no further closes.

## Fix

Ignore a zero-dimension resize (`continue`) instead of closing the socket. The frame carries no size to apply; the PTY keeps whatever size it already had, and the next real fit sends valid dimensions. This makes the control plane resilient to any client (a stale build, a parked or off-screen pane, a third party) rather than amplifying a benign client hiccup into a session-killing loop.

The renderer already guards `sendResize` against 0x0 in `cloud-terminal-mux.ts`; this closes the gap on the server side so the control plane never turns a 0x0 frame into a dropped session.

Also logs one line per socket close (`close_source`, `ws_close_status`, `connected_ms`) so a future terminal drop names its own cause without a redeploy. That is how this root cause was pinned.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/httpapi/`, `go test ./internal/httpapi/` all pass.
- Deployed to staging (surgical task-def swap, control plane only, no worker change). Verified in live logs: the two terminals that had been looping every ~2.5s each attached once more and then held an open socket with zero further closes; no short-lived (<2s) closes appeared after cutover. Deployment reached steady state on the fixed image.

## Scope

Control plane only. No migration. No worker binary change (no nodeops rebake needed). The renderer needs only a reload to pick up its existing 0x0 guard; no renderer code change is required for this fix.

title: fix(tmux): run the launch prelude under /bin/sh and stop treating tmux as required
body:
Code changes: +38 -105  
Tests: +79 -165  
Others: +35 -59 (generated `openapi.yaml` + `schema.ts`, landing docs, i18n catalogs)

## What

Two changes to the tmux path:

**1. Run the launch prelude under `/bin/sh`** (fixes #3788, closes #5582). Deletes the `$SHELL` plumbing that only existed to feed it: `Options.Shell`, `Runtime.shell`, the `$SHELL` resolution in `New`, and the `shellPath` parameter on `newSessionArgs`/`respawnPaneArgs`.

**2. Stop treating tmux as a required runtime.** New macOS/Linux sessions run on the native PTY host; tmux only serves handles created before that host existed and the fallback path when the direct spawn fails. Removed the code and copy that still claimed tmux was required to start a session:

- the macOS spawn gate (`validateRuntimePrerequisites`), the `ports.ErrRuntimePrerequisite` sentinel, and its `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` API mapping
- the `tmux` install target from `systeminstall`, the `/system/install/{target}` enum, and the frontend install dialog
- the tmux `systemcheck` row and `ao doctor` are now advisory: warn, never block
- landing docs that told users to install tmux

## Why

**Prelude.** `buildLaunchCommand` emits a POSIX prelude (`cd`, `unset`, `export`, `exec`), but the pane was started as `$SHELL -c <prelude>`. A non-POSIX `$SHELL` (fish, nushell, tcsh) rejects `export VAR=VAL`, so the pane exited immediately at creation and the session never came up (#3788).

**Required runtime.** Since the native PTY host landed (#4473, #4727), new sessions on macOS/Linux exec their argv directly and never touch tmux. What remains is the fallback and pre-rollout handles — real, but not something a user has to install. The old macOS spawn gate failed sessions when tmux was missing, the startup dialog offered a tmux install, and the docs said tmux was required; all three were wrong for the current runtime.

## How

- `launcherShellPath = "/bin/sh"` in `commands.go`, used by both `newSessionArgs` and `respawnPaneArgs`. The prelude only ever needed POSIX sh, so the interpreter is no longer configurable and the `shellPath` parameter is gone.
- Deleted `Options.Shell`, `Runtime.shell`, and the `$SHELL`/`/bin/sh` resolution in `New`; the two `New` tests that asserted `$SHELL` pickup went with them.
- Left `exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -i` in the prelude alone: that is the user's interactive shell after the agent exits, and it works fine under fish. This also fixes standalone shell terminals on the tmux path, which pass the user's shell as argv.
- New regression test `TestCreateLaunchesPreludeUnderPOSIXShellRegardlessOfEnv` sets `SHELL=/usr/bin/fish` and asserts the pane is still launched with `/bin/sh`.
- tmux stays as the legacy/fallback runtime: the tmux adapter, `runtimeselect` routing, `tmuxbin` resolution, bundled tmux, and pre-rollout handle paths are untouched.
- `systemcheck` still reports a tmux row and `ao doctor` still probes tmux — both now advisory (`Required: false`, `doctorWarn`), so a missing tmux never blocks startup or fails the doctor run.
- Deliberately left alone: `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` in the frontend/mobile observability catalogs (a client-side classification table that tolerates codes the daemon no longer emits), and the internal architecture docs (`docs/architecture.md`, `docs/daemon-environment.md`) that describe the tmux runtime layer, which still exists.

Supersedes #3789, which adds a `launcherShell()` denylist (fish, nu, csh, tcsh, elvish, xonsh) for the same bug. The denylist works, but it is a list to maintain and it keeps the `$SHELL` plumbing alive; the prelude only ever needed POSIX sh.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go test ./...` — pass.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs` (fresh cache) — 0 issues.
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` — pass.
- `cd frontend && npx vitest run` — 4915 passed; a handful of unrelated component suites (`GlobalSettingsForm`, `ProjectSettingsForm`, `CreateProjectFlow`, `browser-history-store`) timed out under local load and pass in isolation (137/137). CI is the authority.
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/... ./internal/service/shellterm/... ./internal/daemon/...` — pass (the shellterm suite drives a real tmux binary).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] Two related tmux changes; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene

title: feat: limit OMP model picker to providers with configured credentials
body:
Code changes: +265 -12
Tests: +202 -0
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

`omp models --json` lists every model in OMP's registry — including providers the user never authenticated — so the AO model picker offered choices that could only fail at launch (on a typical install: 321 models across 3 providers, only 2 configured).

Discovery now filters the parsed catalog against OMP's own credential stores — the same stores the adapter's auth probe (`omp/auth.go`) reads:

- `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` → `auth_credentials.provider` where `data` is non-empty and `disabled_cause IS NULL`
- fallback `auth.json` → entries with a non-empty `key`
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (project env, then process env) overrides the config dir, matching the auth probe

The configured provider set is folded into the catalog fingerprint, so enabling or disabling a credential invalidates the cached picker without a manual refresh.

Edge semantics:

- **No credential store at all** → fail open with the full catalog (covers env-var-only API-key setups AO cannot enumerate)
- **Store exists, every credential disabled** → empty catalog with a warning
- **Store unreadable** → unfiltered catalog plus a warning (never empties the picker on a probe error)
- Models without provider attribution are kept (fail-open if OMP changes its output shape)

Implementation: `modelcatalog` keeps ownership of per-agent discovery config reading (same pattern as claude/qwen/goose); the generic command-runner was extracted as `runModelCommand` with unchanged behavior for all other agents. No frontend or API contract changes — the picker consumes the same `GET /api/v1/agents/omp/models` response.

## Tests

- 10 new unit tests in `omp_test.go`: agent.db / auth.json / merged / disabled / empty / missing store cases, filter behavior (unattributed models kept), fingerprint stability + invalidation on provider-set change, binary-missing dispatch. All pass.
- Real-binary smoke check on a machine with `kimi-code` + `vercel-ai-gateway` configured and `moonshot` unconfigured: catalog filtered 321 → 304 models, all 17 `moonshot` entries removed, fingerprint populated (throwaway test, removed after passing).
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, gofmt clean; `omp` adapter package tests pass.

## Known gaps / risks

- Full `go test ./...` could not be validated on this Windows dev host: ~90 pre-existing failures at baseline (confirmed identical via `git stash`) from environment issues (temp-file ACLs, codex account sandbox expectations, git URL validation) plus 2 env-dependent modelcatalog tests (autohand/continue read the real home dir). These must be verified in CI.
- `golangci-lint` is not installed locally; the pinned v2.12.2 was run via `go run` on the changed package and reported only CRLF line-ending artifacts (untouched baseline files flagged identically; git normalizes to LF on commit).
- Providers authenticated purely via environment variables (e.g. `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`) with no credential-store entry cannot be enumerated; the filter fails open in that case by design.

Model discovery for `opencode` and `kilocode` now reads the agent's own configuration first and only falls back to the CLI model registry when no usable config exists.

- **Paths** (`config.go` → `modelConfigPaths`): OpenCode reads the inherited or project-overridden `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, XDG/global `config.json` and `opencode.json[c]`, ancestor project `opencode.json[c]`, `.opencode` config directories, and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. Kilo Code reads the corresponding `KILO_CONFIG`, XDG/global files, ancestor `kilo.json[c]` and legacy `opencode.json[c]`, `.kilo`/`.kilocode` config directories, and `KILO_CONFIG_DIR`. Relative explicit config paths resolve from the project working directory.
- **Parser** (`parseOpenCodeModels`): strips `//` and `/* */` comments (JSONC), enumerates `provider.<id>.models` map keys as `provider/model` IDs, skips providers without a `models` map (they resolve registry defaults themselves), and marks the top-level `model` key as default—appending it when it isn't declared under any provider (mirrors the Claude configured-default behavior).
- **Fallback** (`catalog.go` → `Discover`): config-first, CLI-fallback for opencode/kilocode only. A missing config, an unparsable one, or one that pins no provider models falls through to the existing `opencode --pure models` / `kilocode models` commands, so the picker never shows a dead empty list. Other config-discovered agents keep their config-only behavior.
- **Fingerprint**: `configDiscoveryFingerprint` hashes every resolved config path and its contents, so edits to inherited overrides, XDG/global files, ancestor project files, and config-directory files invalidate cached catalogs automatically.
- No frontend changes: the picker consumes `AgentModelCatalog` generically, and opencode keeps `CustomModelEntryDirect` so manual ID entry still works.

## Tests

- Added modelcatalog coverage for provider/models extraction, JSONC comments, undeclared defaults, empty provider models, malformed JSON, config-first discovery, CLI fallback, fingerprint invalidation, inherited config overrides, project-over-environment precedence, XDG and legacy global config, ancestor discovery, and Kilo's `.kilocode` directory.
- Per request, the latest follow-up commit was not tested locally; validation is delegated to this PR's CI checks.

## Known gaps / risks

- Behavior matrix: config with providers+models → narrowed picker with default preselected; config without provider models or no config → full registry via CLI; editing a config file changes the discovery fingerprint and refreshes the picker.

title: diag(cloud/worker): report bootstrap phase timing to the control plane
body:
## Why

A cloud worker session's terminal can take much longer than expected to appear after the sandbox is provisioned. In one case it was ~3.5 minutes between "worker connected" and the agent terminal opening, and we had no way to see where that time went: ao-worker logs its bootstrap phases to stdout inside the Firecracker microVM (/var/log/ao-worker.log), which nodeops does not ship and which dies with the ephemeral VM. The structured worker events it did report were not persisted as queryable phase markers either, so the intra-sandbox stretch (clone, git setup, harness start) was invisible.

## What

ao-worker now emits a best-effort `worker.phase` event at each bootstrap boundary, and the control plane logs it (not persisted, no schema change) so the breakdown reaches CloudWatch per session:

- `connected` (baseline, elapsed 0)
- `checkout_grant` (checkout grant obtained)
- `checkout_done` (git clone finished)
- `git_configured` (git tooling in place)
- `rehydrate_done` (delete/restore rehydration, near zero for a fresh session)
- `credential_loaded` (harness credential fetched)
- `harness_built` (harness command built)
- `agent_terminal_ready` (agent PTY up, browser can attach)
- `scratch_ready` (scratch-workspace path)

Each event carries `elapsedMs` (since `connected`) and `deltaMs` (time spent in that phase). Elapsed is measured from `connected`, so the per-sandbox self-update and provisioning, which happen before that point and are already visible in the control plane's own logs, do not skew the phase deltas. Reports fire in the background with a short timeout so they never delay the phases they measure.

## Result

With this deployed on staging, fresh sessions broke down as: post-connect bootstrap 2 to 6 seconds, dominated by the git clone (1.5 to 5.3s), with git config plus rehydrate plus credential plus harness build plus agent terminal all under 0.5s combined. Provisioning was usually about 0.1 to 0.2s but one session hit a 12s provisioning (createos microVM variance). So the earlier 3.5-minute case was an outlier (a pathologically slow clone), not the normal path, and if it recurs the `checkout_done` delta now names it directly.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/ao-worker/ ./internal/httpapi/`, `go test ./internal/httpapi/` all pass.
- Deployed to staging and verified live: five fresh sessions each logged the full phase sequence with per-phase deltas; the instrumented worker is served and re-exec'd via the existing self-update path (no template rebake required).

## Scope and stacking

Control plane plus ao-worker. No migration. Diagnostic instrumentation, low overhead (a handful of log lines plus best-effort events per session). Opened on top of `fix/cloud-terminal-resize-noop` (#5584), which is what the diag build was deployed against; the two changes touch different files (this one does not touch `terminal_handlers.go`). Rebase onto main once #5584 merges, or retarget to main if #5584 lands first.

title: fix(workspace): render untracked child-repo diffs in the Files inspector
body:
Code changes: +77 -18
Tests: +132 -1
Others: +8 -0 (i18n catalogs, one new key)

Closes #5363

## Root cause

Not a race or a slow request. A workspace-project session leaves every git-state section and the commit list zero-valued, so the Files review pane can only ask for the `combined` scope. That scope resolves diffs with `git diff <base> -- <path>`, which reports **nothing for an untracked file** — and a file an agent has just created is untracked.

So `/workspace/diffs` answered HTTP 200 with an empty patch. The renderer found no metadata for that path and fell through to a fallback card whose caption had no state that could ever replace `Loading diff...`. That is why every backing request succeeded while the visible render state never advanced, and why the reporter's audit saw healthy responses throughout.

The **File** action worked in the reported screenshot because the single-file `GetWorkspaceFile` endpoint already synthesizes this patch. Only the batch endpoint did not.

## Changes

**`workspace_review.go`** — the combined scope now synthesizes the added-file patch for untracked targets, exactly as `GetWorkspaceFile` already does. Tracked paths still go through `git diff` unchanged. git's own output is concatenated first so the 2 MB group cap drops synthesized content before anything git already reported.

Scoped deliberately to `combined`: it is the only scope that compares base..worktree, where an untracked file is a genuine addition. `staged`, `unstaged` and `committed` have no untracked side by definition and are untouched.

**`WorkspaceReviewPane.tsx`** — the fallback card now distinguishes a batch still in flight from one that settled without a diff. A settled miss reaches `Unable to load this diff.` with a **Retry** action beside the existing **File** action, so a future gap here is visible and actionable instead of an indefinite spinner. `Load diff` and `Retry` are mutually exclusive by construction, so the card never grows a third button.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A changed file in a multi-repository workspace renders its diff
- [x] Rendering reaches success or a retryable error — the card resolves the moment its batch settles (~350 ms in the reported audit) rather than hanging
- [x] The error state includes Retry and Open file actions
- [x] A two-repository integration test verifies this path

## Tests

`TestGetWorkspaceDiffsIncludesUntrackedChildRepoFile` builds a root workspace repo plus `alpha` and `beta` child repos, creates an untracked file in one and a tracked modification in the other, and asserts both patches arrive. `TestGetWorkspaceDiffsCombinesUntrackedAndTrackedPathsInOneRepo` covers the mixed single-repo case. The renderer test covers a two-repository group response: one group renders, the other settles empty and offers Retry.

Both new backend tests were confirmed to fail against the unfixed code before the fix was written.

## Validation

Backend, post-rebase, on an idle machine: `go test ./...` 169 packages green, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `go build`/`go vet` clean. Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean post-rebase; the full renderer sweep (147 files, 2521 tests) was green pre-rebase and the remaining post-rebase sweep is left to CI.

## Intentional omissions

- **No client-side timeout.** The state resolves when the request settles. An artificial abort risks false failures on slow large workspaces, where the server's own budget is 15 s.
- **No `diff_rendered` / `diff_render_failed` telemetry.** Requested in an issue comment but not in the acceptance criteria, and framed there as instrumentation to size production impact. It needs session kind and workspace kind plumbed into a component that does not receive them today — better as its own PR.

## No API contract change

`dto.go` and `openapi.yaml` are untouched, so no regeneration is needed. The only consumer of `GetWorkspaceDiffs` is the `/workspace/diffs` controller.

title: fix(board): keep a crowded PR row inside the card
body:
## The bug

A session with many open PRs renders them as one row per state. On a board card
with ten open PRs the numbers ran into each other and past the card's right edge,
clipping the trailing ones:

`#5146#5147#5148#5149#5217#5218#5219#5221#5223#5290`

## Why it still happened

#5565 let that row wrap, which fixed the common case. But wrapping was only the
row's *preference*, not its floor: every entry kept `min-w-0` and the default
`flex-shrink: 1`, so any layout that put more entries on a line than fit still
compressed them — and the PR number is a bare `<span>` with nothing to clip it,
so its glyphs painted straight over the neighbouring entry and out past the card.

Measured on the pre-fix row, ten open PRs overflowed their own links by 43px and
escaped a 237px card.

## The fix

Make wrapping the only way a crowded row can resolve.

- `shrink-0` on each entry, so a row that runs out of width wraps instead of
  squeezing its entries into each other.
- `max-w-full` plus a truncating number for the one case wrapping cannot fix —
  a single entry wider than the whole row — which now ellipsizes inside the card
  rather than escaping it.

## No visual change where the board actually renders

Board lanes are `>=256px`, and at every width from 200px up the rendered layout
and the card's measured height are identical to `main`. The change only takes
effect in the states that were already broken.

## Verification

- New regression test in `SessionsBoardView.test.tsx`; it fails on `main` and
  passes here.
- `packages/product-ui`: typecheck clean, 129 tests pass.
- `frontend`: typecheck clean, `SessionsBoard.test.tsx` 48 tests pass.
- Checked in the running renderer with a ten-PR and a twelve-PR card (mixed
  states, a 7-digit number, review comments): zero overflow, zero overlap.

title: fix(cloud/ui): cloud task composer + terminal connecting/connected UX, and the fresh-session blank flash
body:
## What

Cloud project UI/UX fixes for the New Task composer and the agent terminal's connecting/connected surface, plus the fix for the fresh-session terminal blank flash. Frontend only: 16 files, zero control-plane or Go changes. This is the branch that has been running on staging for review.

## Fixes

**Task composer (cloud projects)**
- The harness dropdown on New Task now lists only the harnesses a cloud project actually supports (claude-code, codex, cursor), instead of the full local catalog.
- The model selector no longer shows a spinner when no harness is selected; it shows a static placeholder until a harness is chosen, then the real model combobox.

**Terminal connecting / connected surface**
- A connected agent terminal shows a single small status dot, not the full "Connected" button.
- After a terminal is revealed there is no dot at all (no lingering green dot top-right).
- While connecting, the pane shows ONE centered "Connecting" cover and ONE elapsed timer (top-right), replacing the three overlapping loaders that used to stack.
- The connecting cover no longer flashes back over an already-visible terminal on a transient reattach (it is latched on first reveal).

**Fresh-session blank flash (worker-epoch flip)**
- A fresh cloud worker attaches optimistically before its sandbox is up, when the worker epoch is still unknown; the moment the worker comes online the polled epoch flips from undefined to its first value. That value was folded into the terminal cache key, the reconcile-loop dispose test, and the connecting-cover identity, so the flip tore down the just-attached pane and remounted it: a from-0 replay with a screen reset that the user saw as connected then blank then terminal.
- Fix: treat the unknown to first-known transition as the worker coming online for the SAME terminal and adopt the epoch in place. The worker cache key no longer carries the epoch (only handle plus restore nonce); a change BETWEEN two known epochs (idle-resume or restore) still re-mints via the reset nonce (new advanceEpoch action); the connecting-cover latch keys on the handle only. Restore and idle-resume re-mint are preserved.
- Confirmed on staging: each fresh session logged exactly one browser attach to the same terminal id and epoch (before the fix, two attaches with a clean close between).

## CP dependency

The blank-flash fix has a small control-plane half that is already deployed on staging: a zero-dimension terminal resize is ignored instead of closing the socket (see #5584). This renderer change is independent of it (different files) and does not require any further CP deploy; the shared staging CP already carries it.

## Testing

- Component tests updated and passing: TerminalPane (retained-cache remount and connecting-cover behavior, plus a new regression test that the first-epoch flip does not remount), SessionView, XtermTerminal, terminal-reset-store.
- i18n keys added or updated across all 8 catalogs (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, zh-CN).
- typecheck clean for the changed files.

## Scope

Frontend only. No migration. No control-plane change. i18n coverage updated.

title: Prevent browser profile tab freezes and stale target errors
body:
Code changes: +276 -108\
Tests: +293 -27\
Others: +0 -0

## Issue

Browser profiles could become unresponsive when several tabs were open because profile replacement waited for tab initialization and page restoration to complete sequentially. A slow or stalled page could therefore block the browser operation queue until the runtime timeout.

Tab selection could also drift between the visible Electron `BrowserView` and the automation runtime’s cached active target. This created two failure modes:

- Agent commands or screenshots could target a stale tab.
- A surface refresh during profile replacement could access a temporarily unavailable active tab, producing the uncaught `Active browser tab is unavailable` error.

The lifecycle and targeting logic is shared across platforms. The reported uncaught-error dialog was observed through the macOS surface-refresh path.

## Fix

- Apply user tab selections immediately without waiting for runtime synchronization.
- Synchronize the automation runtime at the next command boundary and fail safely if the requested target cannot be confirmed.
- Preserve newer user selections when delayed runtime callbacks complete.
- Use a stable target provider that matches the runtime’s provider-caching behavior.
- Serialize screenshots behind tab synchronization and readiness checks.
- Complete the structural profile swap without waiting for every page to reload.
- Restore tabs concurrently, starting with the active tab, while retaining per-tab readiness barriers for automation.
- Preserve pending restore URLs when another profile switch supersedes an in-progress restoration.
- Prevent profile replacement from overlapping destructive browser operations.
- Ignore surface refreshes during profile replacement and reject stale deferred refresh callbacks.

## Files affected

- `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`
  - Updates tab targeting, profile restoration, operation coordination, and stale surface-refresh handling.
- `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts`
  - Adds regression coverage for delayed selection callbacks, cached providers, screenshot targeting, stalled tab restoration, repeated profile switches, and stale refreshes.

## Validation

- `npm test -- src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts`
  - 1 test file passed.
  - 138 tests passed.
- `git diff --check`
  - Passed.

title: feat(orchestrator): let an orchestrator read a worker session's output
body:
## Problem

An orchestrator can spawn workers and message them, but it cannot see what they produced. `ao orchestrator` implements only `ls` (`backend/internal/cli/orchestrator.go`), and no CLI path reaches a worker's conversation. When a worker stalls, contradicts itself, or reports a success the orchestrator cannot verify, the only recourse is `ao send` asking the worker to describe its own state — the source already in doubt, and it fails exactly when the worker is confused. In practice the orchestrator either respawns work that was fine or relays an unverified claim to the human.

The data already exists server-side: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/conversation` returns a snapshot built from `ConversationTurnResponse` / `ConversationMessageResponse`, alongside the SSE stream and terminal mux. The gap is consumption, not capture.

This affects orchestrator-driven fleets, CI/review follow-up routing, and headless/API consumers that have no desktop UI to read.

## Proposed contract

- Add `ao session output <session-id>` reading the existing session conversation snapshot; no new capture path.
- `--tail N` bounds how many recent turns are returned, defaulting to a small number. Pull with an explicit bound is deliberate: the orchestrator decides how much enters its context, so worker output cannot flood it unrequested.
- Default rendering is the recent assistant and tool turns in readable form; `--json` emits the structured turns for programmatic use, matching existing CLI JSON conventions.
- Reuse the existing conversation route and service operation as the single implementation; no orchestrator-specific server path.
- Preserve daemon error envelopes and request IDs, and return the standard not-found envelope for an unknown session id.
- No DTO change expected. If a harness turns out not to populate the snapshot fields the command needs, that is reported before extending `dto.go`, since it pulls in OpenAPI/TS regeneration (`npm run api`).
- `--follow` over the existing SSE stream is explicitly out of scope here and remains possible later.

## Verification

Cover CLI happy path, `--tail` bounding and `--json` shape against a fake daemon; unknown-session and daemon-error envelope propagation; and one end-to-end check that the command returns real turns from a live session, since the main risk is the snapshot-payload assumption rather than command logic.

Happy to implement this if maintainers agree on the shape.

title: test(browser): pin wedged-runtime broker behavior for #5369
body:
## Summary

Regression tests for the browser-runtime wedge behind #5369: a desktop (Electron) main process that is busy, asleep, or network-wedged keeps its broker socket attached, so every `POST /api/v1/browser/commands` waits for the caller's context while `GET /api/v1/browser/status` keeps reporting `connected: true`. The deterministic repro (`kill -STOP` / `-CONT` of the Electron main process) and the fingerprint proposal were posted in [#5369 (comment)](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5369#issuecomment-5734580482); this PR turns that scenario into Go test coverage.

Test-only, complementing the open #5484 (reconnect wait + typed codes) and #5552 (command timeout reporting): the attached-but-unresponsive runtime path is not covered there.

## What is covered (new `broker_wedge_test.go`)

- **Bounded deadline failure with a silent runtime** — `Execute` with an attached runtime that never answers returns `context.DeadlineExceeded`, emits a `cancel` frame on the wire for the expired request id, and leaves the pending registry empty. The deadline path had no coverage; cancel frames were only exercised for explicit `context.Canceled` (#3732).
- **Next command after a wedge stays bounded** — fresh request id, same typed deadline failure, and a late result for the expired request is ignored without disturbing the registry; the broker keeps serving commands afterwards.
- **Status during a wedge** — `Status()` reports `Connected: true` while a command is in flight unanswered. Pinned as the documented current contract; surfacing a degraded state remains up to the #5369 fix.
- **Replacement connection recovers the broker** — a second runtime handshake fails stale in-flight commands with `ErrUnavailable` and then carries new commands end to end.

## Testing

```
go test ./internal/browserruntime -count=1        # pass
go test ./internal/browserruntime -count=1 -race  # pass
gofmt -l .                                        # clean
```

New tests complete in ~0.3 s total; all existing package tests pass unchanged.

Refs #5369

title: fix(browser): detect wedged runtime via ping/pong liveness (#5369)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root cause of the 503 storms from #5369: the daemon had no way to detect a wedged browser runtime. A desktop main process that stops scheduling (busy event loop, system sleep, wedged network stack) keeps its broker socket attached, so every `POST /api/v1/browser/commands` burned the full 60s request timeout and `GET /api/v1/browser/status` kept reporting `connected: true` the whole time. Deterministic repro and fingerprint analysis: [#5369 (comment)](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5369#issuecomment-5734580482); regression coverage for the pre-fix behavior landed in #5601 (included here as its base commit).

## What changed

**Broker liveness (protocol v3).** The broker now heartbeats the runtime: pings every 5s, and if no pong arrives for 15s the connection is torn down as unresponsive. Tearing down is what activates the existing recovery machinery — pending and queued commands fail fast with the typed `BROWSER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` error (503), and `status` reports `connected: false` instead of a lie. Hellos carry `version: 3`; v2 hellos are still accepted for mixed-version deployments and are simply not probed.

**Desktop link answers pings.** `browser-runtime-link.ts` replies to ping frames outside the per-session command chains, so a wedged operation can never starve the heartbeat. The link's existing reconnect backoff re-establishes the connection once the process unwedges, making recovery deterministic instead of accidental.

**Tab readiness is bounded.** The initial `about:blank` load that every CDP command awaits (`entry.ready`) could hang forever and wedge the session's whole native operation queue; it now fails with a typed `BROWSER_DEVTOOLS_UNAVAILABLE` error after 60s (above the 55s wait-action ceiling).

## Behavior change

| Scenario (desktop process wedged) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detection latency | never | ~15–20s |
| In-flight command | hangs 60s → 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | fails ≤ ~20s → 503 `BROWSER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` |
| Subsequent commands | hang 60s each, back-to-back | fail immediately, typed |
| `browser/status` | `connected: true` (lie) | `connected: false` |
| Recovery on unwedge | accidental (sleep/wake timing) | deterministic (link reconnect backoff) |

## Testing

```
go test ./internal/browserruntime -count=1        # pass (new liveness suite: unresponsive detection, responsive survives, v2/v3 negotiation, legacy gets no pings)
go test ./internal/browserruntime -count=1 -race  # pass
npm --prefix frontend test -- --run src/main/browser-runtime-link.test.ts src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts  # 139 pass (new: ping→pong, readiness bound)
gofmt -l .                                        # clean
```

End-to-end on an isolated dev instance: `kill -STOP` of the Electron main process → within ~20s `browser/status` flips to `disconnected` and commands fail immediately with `BROWSER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`; `kill -CONT` → the link reconnects on its own and commands work again.

Complements #5484 (reconnect wait and typed codes compose cleanly on top) and #5552.

Refs #5369

title: feat(chat): ACP Chat bindings for Auggie, Autohand, Cline, Goose, Kilo Code, Kiro, and Vibe
body:
Code changes: +782 -53  
Tests: +955 -39  
Others: +111 -6  

## Summary

Closes the Chat gap for seven harnesses that were TUI-only. Each binding launches the exact executable resolved by that harness's existing agent plugin over AO's reusable ACP transport — AO never downloads, packages, or substitutes a provider CLI, and the existing agent plugin stays the single answer to "is this agent installed and logged in".

| Harness | Launch | Model | Permissions | Standing instructions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Auggie | `auggie --acp` | `--model` at launch and `session/set_model` | ACP requests | session-private `--rules` file |
| Autohand | `autohand-acp` | session-advertised | `AUTOHAND_PERMISSION_MODE=external` | not injectable |
| Cline | `cline --acp` | `CLINE_MODEL` env | `--auto-approve true` for auto/bypass | not injectable |
| Goose | `goose acp` | session-advertised | `GOOSE_MODE` env | not injectable |
| Kilo Code | `kilocode acp` | `session/set_config_option` (`model`, `effort`) | `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` permission map | `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` generated agent |
| Kiro | `kiro-cli acp --agent ao` | `session/set_model` | ACP requests | workspace-local `ao` custom agent |
| Vibe | `vibe-acp` | `session/set_config_option` (`model`) | ACP requests; `auto`/`bypass` use per-call approval, `accept-edits` prompts | not injectable |

Registration in `chatdriver/registry` remains the whole capability gate, so a harness without a driver fails with `ErrChatUnsupported` rather than quietly producing a TUI session.

`docs/harnesses/acp-bindings.md` records each binding's launch shape, deliberate limitations, and the blocker matrix for TUI-only harnesses. Prime Agent remains TUI-only: its ACP server has neither permission requests nor `session/load`; bypass can waive approvals but cannot waive AO's resumability floor.

## Verification

Every shipped binding except Kiro was probed against the provider's real ACP server on macOS arm64; Kiro's CLI was unavailable in this environment and its row says so.

| Binding | Version | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auggie | 0.18.1 | `initialize` ok, `loadSession: true`; `session/new` requires `auggie login` |
| Autohand | adapter 0.2.1 | `initialize` ok, `loadSession: true`, `list`/`resume`/`fork`; `AUTOHAND_PERMISSION_MODE` present in the shipped adapter |
| Cline | 3.0.62 | `initialize` ok, `loadSession: true`; `--acp` and `--auto-approve <boolean>` in `--help`, `CLINE_MODEL` present in the shipped binary |
| Kilo Code | 7.7.5 | full `session/new`; config option ids confirmed; `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` present in the shipped binary |
| Kiro | not installed | launch shape derived from the published `kiro-cli acp --agent <name>` surface; covered by unit tests only |
| Goose | 1.51.0 | `initialize` ok, `loadSession: true`; `--help` confirms no model or system-prompt launch flag; `session/new` requires `GOOSE_PROVIDER` |
| Vibe | 2.25.5 | `initialize` ok, `loadSession: true`; `request_permission` supplies no tool kind, so `accept-edits` safely prompts; AO selects `allow_once` for `auto`/`bypass` so a later permission downgrade takes effect |

The probes and review passes found and fixed these behavioral gaps:

- Kilo's effort choice was dropped, and its generated default agent needed `mode: "primary"` to avoid silently falling back to the read-only `ask` agent.
- Kiro Chat skipped TUI workspace preparation, so ACP configure now materializes the workspace-local agent and standing prompt before start/resume.
- Vibe's cached grant could survive a permission downgrade, so automatic approvals now use `allow_once`; its model is mapped through the advertised config option.
- Prime Agent 0.7.2 advertises `loadSession: false`; its unreachable Chat binding was removed and the registry test now requires `ErrChatUnsupported`.

Every shipped binding has focused unit tests over launch argv, environment, permission mapping, and turn-setting validation. Only Auggie ships a live test; it is env-gated with `AO_LIVE_AUGGIE_ACP=1`, so CI never depends on a provider being installed.

Local: `go test -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry ./internal/service/chat` and `go vet ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/... ./internal/service/chat` pass. The broader local Chat suite reaches an unrelated Codex conformance check against a newer installed provider; CI runs the repository's pinned environment.

## Risks

- Kiro's launch shape is unit-tested but not confirmed against a live binary; a wrong argv there affects Kiro only.
- Approval changes fixed at process launch return `ErrACPSetterUnsupported` and require a Chat restart by design.

title: fix(desktop): offer Resume agent when an agent exits but its session lives
body:
Code changes: +245 -81  
Tests: +421 -8  
Others: +0 -0  

Fixes the "no way to spin it back" dead end: an agent that exits without terminating its session (`/exit`, Ctrl+C, a provider usage limit) left the pane showing **TERMINAL ENDED — "This terminal process ended, but the session is not marked terminated yet."** with no control anywhere.

Refs #4936, #3875.

## The bug is in the UI, not the daemon

`POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/resume-agent` already recovers this state perfectly — it returns `resumeMode: "native"`, i.e. a real `codex resume` of the original conversation. Worktree, branch, and history are all intact. `ao session resume-agent <id>` has always worked.

What broke is that every recovery affordance was gated on `sessionIsActive`, which reports **row** liveness:

```ts
sessionIsActive = session.isTerminated !== true && session.status !== "terminated"
```

A Ctrl+C'd session is *not* terminated, so that returns `true`, so `canRestoreSession` is `false`, so the strip renders the message and no button.

**Orchestrators had no path at all.** `ResumeAgentControl` was the one surface with the correct gate (`activity?.state !== "exited"`), but it lives on the inspector's Summary view — and `SessionInspector.tsx:207` filters the view list down to `["browser"]` for orchestrator sessions, so it can never be reached. Workers had one escape hatch via the rail; orchestrators had zero.

## Changes

- **Extract `ResumeAgentControl`** and mount it on the terminal-ended strip — where you are standing when the agent dies. It self-gates, so the strip needs no knowledge of when resume applies. The inspector's wrapper `div` moved to its call site so the component is layout-free and usable in both.
- **`sessionAgentExited`** added beside `sessionIsActive` in `types/workspace.ts`, naming process liveness as distinct from row liveness.
- **`showEndedState` now includes it.** An agent can exit while its tmux pane survives on a `cat` keep-alive (#3875), so the mux never reports `exited` and the strip — carrying the only recovery control — stayed hidden in exactly the state it exists for. Without this the fix only covers harnesses that happen to close their PTY.
- **Clicking Orchestrator resumes an exited orchestrator** instead of navigating to a dead terminal. `newestActiveOrchestrator` counts an exited-but-alive orchestrator as active, so the button routed you straight back into the dead pane.
- **Auxiliary terminals ignore the worker exit state.** The keep-alive fallback now applies only to the worker target, so an attached shell or reviewer terminal stays unobscured when the worker agent exits.
- **Active agent switches keep ownership.** Both orchestrator launchers open the existing session instead of calling `resume-agent` while `activeAgentSwitch` is present.
- **Resume failures stay visible and in place.** The shared launcher returns mutation errors through its existing board/topbar feedback; the sidebar uses the existing error toast and does not navigate into the dead terminal.

Restore (terminated rows) and Resume (live row, dead agent) are now both reachable and mutually exclusive — they never both render.

## Why click-driven and not automatic

Auto-relaunching on the exit event was considered and rejected. `cli/agent_process.go:74` does `_ = child.Wait()` — **the exit code is discarded**, so `/exit`, Ctrl+C, OOM, and a usage limit all post the identical `{state: "exited", event: "process-exited"}`. There is no signal to branch on, and auto-restarting the usage-limit case (the original report) is a hot loop against a metered API; #3875 is the same shape, where every relaunch reproduces the identical failure.

This also matches the boundary the daemon already draws: `reconcileLive` auto-relaunches when the *runtime* died (reboot, tmux server killed) but adopts and stops when only the agent exited. A click is the intent signal.

## Tests

Regression coverage includes:

| Test | Regression it catches |
|---|---|
| posts resume-agent from the strip for a worker / orchestrator | wrong endpoint or hidden button |
| shows the strip even when the mux never reported an exit | the `showEndedState` hole |
| keeps attached shell/reviewer terminals unobscured after worker exit | false ended strip over a live auxiliary terminal |
| opens a switching orchestrator without resuming from either launcher | guaranteed `resume-agent` conflict during agent handoff |
| surfaces rejected orchestrator resume requests from both launchers | silent board/topbar failure or sidebar navigation into the dead terminal |
| offers restore and not resume once the row is terminated | the two actions colliding |

The auxiliary-terminal regression fails for both targets without the worker-target guard; both launcher regressions fail without the switch guard, and rejected-request coverage verifies both visible feedback and no dead-terminal navigation.

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` — clean
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.test.tsx` — 55 passed
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx` — 147 passed

Two renderer tests (`SettingsDialog`, `TopbarOpenEditorButton`) fail only under full-suite parallel load and pass in isolation; both are timing-sensitive and untouched by this diff. `src/landing/**` failures are local-only — `@ao/shared` is not installed in this worktree, and CI installs it.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Ceiling: the strip still needs to mount, so a harness that neither closes its PTY nor reports an exit is out of reach. That's the supervisor-side half — PR #5014 is raising it for OMP.
- The strip's copy (`terminal.sessionEndedNotTerminated`) still narrates the dead end. Left alone deliberately: it reads fine beside a button, and rewording it stales 8 locale files.
- Not touched: the command palette's resume item (still excludes orchestrators and calls `/restore`), and the orchestrator inspector's Browser-only filter. Both are separate calls.

**#4936 is assigned to @ronishrohan** — flagging so this doesn't collide with work already in progress.

title: [Bug]: persistenthost package fails to compile on Windows — host_race_test.go uses syscall.Kill with no build tag
body:
### What went wrong?

Went to run the backend suite on Windows and it dies before any test runs:

```
# github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost [.test]
internal\adapters\chatdriver\persistenthost\host_race_test.go:86:33: undefined: syscall.Kill
internal\adapters\chatdriver\persistenthost\host_race_test.go:95:34: undefined: syscall.Kill
FAIL	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost [build failed]
```

`host_race_test.go` uses `syscall.Kill(-pid, syscall.SIGKILL)` in two `t.Cleanup` calls to tear down the spawned hosts. That's POSIX-only — killing a process group via negative PID doesn't exist on Windows.

The file just has no build constraint on it. Looks like an oversight rather than intent, since everything else platform-specific in that package is already split properly (`child_unix.go`/`child_windows.go`, `spawn_unix.go`/`spawn_windows.go`). Came in with #4766 by the looks of the history.

Sticking `//go:build unix` at the top fixes it and keeps the tests running everywhere they currently pass.

Couple of things that make this more annoying than a normal platform-skipped test:

- It's a *build* error, not a test failure, so `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` both blow up on Windows regardless of what you touched. Took me a while to convince myself it wasn't my own change.
- persistenthost is the detached host layer behind Codex and the ACP chat providers, so none of the restart/reconnect behavior has any Windows coverage right now, and a real regression there would be hidden behind this.

Doesn't look like a dupe of #3687 — that one's about tests that run and fail on Windows (path assumptions, TempDir cleanup). This one won't compile at all.

Probably worth flagging on #5416 too, since that turns on Windows Go tests in CI and will hit this straight away.

One thought for later: those two tests cover genuinely cross-platform behaviour (stale descriptor handling, the `O_EXCL` launch lock), so a Windows equivalent would be better than just excluding them. The build tag is enough to unblock though.

Windows 11, go1.26.5, on main @ 8e486821.

## Why

## How

Add `//go:build !windows` at the top of the file, matching `child_unix.go` / `spawn_unix.go` in the same package. The concurrent stale-probe race test still runs on Unix.

## Testing

## Checklist
