title: fix(workspace): serialize concurrent spawns per repo and surface WORKSPACE_CREATE_FAILED
body:
Code changes: +78 -4  
Tests: +134 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

Concurrent `ao spawn` calls against one repo race `git fetch` + `git worktree add`, each writing `.git/config` via Git's `config.lock`; the loser exits 255 ("could not lock config file") and surfaces as an opaque 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` (Untrivial-ai#4350).

### Changes

1. **Serialize Git mutations per repository**:
   - Add per-repo mutex (`repoSpawnLock`) mirroring `repoTeardownLock`, held across both `addWorktree` and `FetchDefaultBranch` so concurrent fetches and worktree adds do not collide on `.git/config.lock` or `packed-refs.lock`.
   - Hold `repoSpawnLock` in `createWorkspaceProjectRepo` so multi-repo workspace projects (`ProjectKindWorkspace`) are serialized across child worktree creations.
   - Independent repositories stay unlocked and spawn in parallel.

2. **Type the error (Prevent opaque 500 collapse)**:
   - Introduce `ports.ErrWorkspaceCreateFailed` and wrap `git worktree add` failure paths in `gitworktree`.
   - Map `ports.ErrWorkspaceCreateFailed` in `session/service.go` (`mapSessionError`) to HTTP 409 Conflict with code `WORKSPACE_CREATE_FAILED`.

3. **Regression Tests**:
   - Update `TestWorkspace_ConcurrentSpawnsOnSameRepoAllSucceed` to run 15 parallel goroutines firing both `FetchDefaultBranch` and `Create` against a real Git repository.
   - Add `TestCreate_WrapsErrWorkspaceCreateFailedOnWorktreeAddFailure` verifying worktree creation errors wrap `ErrWorkspaceCreateFailed`.
   - Add test case in `TestToAPIErrorMapsWorkspaceBranchSentinels` to verify error mapping to `WORKSPACE_CREATE_FAILED`.

Closes Untrivial-ai#4350

title: fix(chat): keep the skills catalog across a restart, and stop truncating it at fifty
body:
Code changes: +149 -7  
Tests: +182 -0  
Others: +24 -4 (generated sqlc)  

## Code change summary

- Emit ACP command-catalog pushes as chat skill events, archive each full payload, and project each replacement into durable conversation state.
- Add migration 0149 and sqlc support for `skills_json`, preserving an explicit empty catalog so uninstalling every skill clears stale entries.
- Fall back to the stored catalog when a reattached ACP provider cannot replay it, while preferring live results; clear it atomically whenever provider branch ownership changes so commands cannot cross agents or branches.
- Remove the 50-item cap from skill suggestions while retaining the existing cap for file suggestions.

Two defects that both ended with skills missing from the chat composer.

## 1. Every ACP session reported zero skills after a daemon restart

Measured on a live daemon mid-investigation:

| session | created | skills |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-orchestrator-1-182` | after the restart | **248** |
| every other claude-code session | before the restart | **0** |
| every codex session | before the restart | **105-108** |

ACP has no request that asks for the catalog. The agent pushes
`available_commands_update` on `session/new` and again on `commands_changed`, and
nothing re-sends it when AO reattaches to a provider that outlived the daemon. The
driver held that push in memory only (`acp/skills.go`), so a replacement controller
started empty with no way to ask and stayed empty for the rest of the session.

An empty catalog is not renderable as "not known yet": the composer reads `[]` as an
agent with no skills, so `/` stops opening a menu entirely. Codex escaped because
`skills/list` is a request its driver can re-issue at any time.

**Fix.** Persist the push in `conversations.skills_json`, following `mcp_servers_json`
from migration 0073. Every push replaces the whole catalog, so the latest payload is
the complete answer; an empty list is stored as an empty array so "the provider says
there are none" stays distinguishable from "the provider has never said". `Skills()`
falls back to the stored catalog only when the live conversation answers empty, so a
provider that can still enumerate always wins and staleness is bounded by one push.

Shared by all nine ACP drivers: claude, cursor, opencode, pi, droid, kimi, kimchi,
omp, native.

## 2. The `/` menu showed at most fifty skills

`rankSkills` capped ranked rows at `MAX_SUGGESTIONS = 50`. An empty query scores every
skill equally, so the menu sorted by name and showed the first fifty alphabetically --
with 247 installed, everything past roughly the letter "d" was invisible with nothing
to suggest it existed. Codex users hit this too at 107 skills; it only looked fine
because typing narrows the list below the cap.

The cap's own rationale is a file concern (a five-thousand-file worktree must not
render itself into the menu), so `rankFiles` keeps it and `rankSkills` returns
everything. The menu already scrolls.

## Tests

- `TestSkillsSurviveARestartThroughTheStoredCatalog` -- provider pushes, then answers
  empty as a reattached conversation does; the stored catalog is served.
- `TestAnEmptyPushClearsTheStoredCatalog` -- an empty push overwrites, so uninstalling
  every skill does not leave a stale menu.
- `TestSkillsDoNotCrossProviderOwnershipBranches` -- an empty answer from a new owner
  cannot resurrect the previous owner’s catalog.
- `TestACPDriverEmitsTheCommandCatalogAsAnEvent` -- the catalog leaves the driver as an
  event, not only as in-memory state.
- `does not cap a large catalog` -- 250 skills in, 250 out, for both an empty and a
  typed query.

Run locally: `go test ./internal/service/chat/... ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/...
./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/httpd/...` green; renderer chat suite 680
passed; `npm run frontend:typecheck` clean. `npm run lint` was still running when this
PR was opened -- see the comments for the result.

## Risks

- One new migration (0149), additive column, registered in the shipped-migration ledger.
- No API surface change: the HTTP DTO already had `ConversationSkillResponse`, and the
  spec/drift tests pass unchanged.
- The fallback serves a catalog up to one push stale within one ownership branch. It is
  cleared atomically when the active provider branch changes.

title: feat(mobile): pull request reviews are not available on the phone
body:
### What happens

On mobile there is no way to see a pull request's reviews. `packages/mobile` has no caller of
any review route, and no screen that shows review content — so a PR that has feedback on it
gives you a single "Unresolved comments" chip (`lib/prView.ts:240`) and nothing behind it.

Reported in Discord `#dev-chat` by @illegalcall: *"On mobile 1. Links dont open in AO browser
2. Review is not available"*. The first half is #5646.

### What desktop does

The session inspector has a Reviews tab (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`)
with two halves:

- **Review controls** — reviewer agent picker, Auto review toggle, Run / Re-run / Stop, kill.
- **The reviews themselves** — each reviewer's verdict and summary, their inline comments at
  `file:line`, Resolve, Request another review.

### Why this is mostly a client gap, not a daemon one

The phone already fetches the data for the second half. `GET /sessions/{id}/pr` is called on the
PRs tab (`lib/api.ts` → `lib/usePRSummaries.ts`), and the daemon's response already carries
`review.reviews[]` (reviewer, verdict, body), `review.resolvedBy[]` and
`review.unresolvedBy[].links[]` with file, line and body — see `SessionPRReviewSummary` in
`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go`. The mobile client type models only `decision`,
`hasUnresolvedHumanComments` and `unresolvedBy[].count`, so all of it is discarded on arrival.
Desktop's entire "External reviews" half is built from that same response.

The controls need `GET /sessions/{id}/reviews` plus the trigger / cancel / auto-review /
comments-resolve / rerequest routes. None of those are blocked on the LAN listener
(`lanControlBlockedPrefixes` in `backend/internal/httpd/lan_listener.go` covers `/api/v1/mobile`
and other loopback-only prefixes, not `/api/v1/sessions/…`), so they are reachable from a paired
phone today.

### Expected

A pull request's reviews are readable on the phone, and AO's own reviewer can be run or stopped
from there — the same things the desktop Reviews tab offers, in a shape that suits a phone.

### Notes

- Mobile-only change: no daemon change and no wire-contract change.
- Reported by @illegalcall.

title: fix(mobile): show pull request reviews and let AO review from the phone
body:
## Summary

On mobile there was no way to read a pull request's reviews. `packages/mobile` had no review
screen and no caller of any review route, so a PR with feedback showed one "Unresolved comments"
chip and nothing behind it. Reported in Discord `#dev-chat` by @illegalcall.

This adds a Reviews screen, reached from a new row on the PR card.

Most of the data was already reaching the phone. `GET /sessions/{id}/pr` — which the PRs tab
already fetches — carries `review.reviews[]`, `review.resolvedBy[]` and
`review.unresolvedBy[].links[]` with file, line and body. The mobile client type stopped at
`count`, so all of it was discarded on arrival. Widening the type is most of the read half;
the controls come from `GET /sessions/{id}/reviews` and the trigger / cancel / auto-review /
resolve / rerequest routes, none of which are blocked on the LAN listener.

No daemon change and no wire-contract change.

## Changes

| File | |
|---|---|
| `lib/api.ts` | `PRReviewCommentLink`, `PRReviewEntry`, `PRUnresolvedReviewer.links`, `review.reviews`/`resolvedBy`; `autoReviewEnabled` off the board poll; `getSessionReviews`, `triggerReview`, `cancelReview`, `setAutoReview`, `resolveReviewComment`, `requestRereview` |
| `lib/reviewsView.ts` (new) | Pure grouping, wording and ordering |
| `lib/reviewsView.test.ts` (new) | 23 tests |
| `app/pr/[number].tsx` (new) | The screen |
| `lib/PRCard.tsx` | The row that opens it |
| `app/_layout.tsx` | `headerShown: false`, like `project/[id]` |
| `lib/RouteErrorBoundary.test.ts` | Registers the route on the screen-fallback list |

## Decisions worth a look

**One list, not desktop's Agent/External split.** That split needs `GET /sessions/{id}/reviews`
to know which GitHub review id AO's reviewer produced. AO's reviewer submits through GitHub like
anyone else, so its pass is already in `review.reviews[]` — one list keyed by reviewer loses the
label, not the content.

title: [Bug]: terminal panes go blank for parked sessions — WebGL context-loss fix (#4949) is stalled and terminal retention is still unbounded
body:
## What went wrong?

On the desktop app, individual agent sessions sometimes show a blank terminal pane. The session itself is fine — the agent keeps working, the PTY stays attached, and tmux still holds the content — but the pane renders nothing. Switching away and back does not repaint it; restarting the app does. It hits *some* sessions and not others, which makes it feel intermittent.

Observed on AO **v0.13.0** (macOS). I noticed it most when a session's conversation had grown long, though see the caveat at the bottom — I have not verified that conversation size is what actually triggers it.

## This is already diagnosed, and there is already a fix open

PR **#4949 — "fix(frontend): recover terminal rendering after WebGL context loss"** describes this exact symptom:

> Reported on desktop v0.12.10 / Electron 33.4.11 after visiting many sessions in one shell renderer. Chromium logged "Too many active WebGL contexts. Oldest context will be lost." **Long-parked terminal panes became blank while their PTY attachments kept working.**

The earlier root-cause analysis is in **#2333**, which found that panes go black in *visit order* — earliest-visited first — once enough sessions have been opened in one renderer process, matching Chromium evicting the oldest WebGL contexts.

## Status: the fix is stalled, and the bug is still on `main`

**#4949** (opened 2026-09-05, last touched 2026-09-06 — 14 days idle):
- `mergeable: CONFLICTING`
- `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`, zero reviews
- no CI checks recorded on the head commit

The defect it fixes is still present on `main` today — `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:118-121`:

```ts
webgl.onContextLoss(() => {
    webgl.dispose();
    loadCanvasFallback();
});
```

If `dispose()` throws, the error escapes the handler and `loadCanvasFallback()` never runs, so the pane has no renderer at all and stays blank.

## #4949 is necessary but not sufficient

#4949 is deliberately scoped to *recovery* from context loss. Its own description says:

> This does not change terminal retention, Chromium's context budget, session lifecycle, or the existing behavior if the canvas addon itself cannot load.

The *accumulation* that causes the loss is untouched:

- `MAX_RETAINED_TERMINALS` (previously 6) no longer exists anywhere in the repo — removed in `4986af7d0` ("fix: retain terminals without eviction"). Every visited session keeps a mounted xterm, with its WebGL context, for the renderer process's whole lifetime.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx:512` states the current design explicitly: *"Project/session teardown is an ownership boundary, not an LRU event."* There is no size bound on the retained-terminal cache.
- **#3901** ("fix(terminal): bound retained terminals and stop black-pane latches") addressed exactly this accumulation, plus five paths that could leave a pane latched at `visibility: hidden` over a healthy session. It was **closed without being merged.**

So the two halves of the fix are currently: one stalled (#4949, recovery) and one abandoned (#3901, accumulation). Landing only #4949 should make the blanking recoverable rather than terminal, but sessions will still keep losing their contexts as the pane count grows.

## Tracking gap

**#2333** carried the root-cause analysis for this symptom and was closed as *completed* on 2026-08-27, but no PR that fixes it was ever merged — #3901 was closed unmerged, and #4949 is still open. That leaves the symptom with no open issue tracking it. The only open, terminal-blanking issue is **#4155**, which is scoped to blanking *during resize* and is covered by a different PR (#4357).

Filing this so the symptom has a live tracking issue again.

## Asks

1. Review and land **#4949** (it needs a rebase — it currently conflicts).
2. Decide whether to revive **#3901**, or otherwise re-bound the retained-terminal cache, so contexts stop accumulating past Chromium's per-page cap.
3. Consider reopening or linking **#2333** rather than leaving it closed-as-completed against an unmerged fix.

## Caveat on my own report

I hit this with long-running sessions and assumed conversation length was the trigger, but the established cause above is *session count* in one renderer, not conversation size. A large scrollback does mean more GPU memory per context, so it is plausible that a long conversation just makes eviction arrive sooner — but I have not measured that, and I would not want it treated as a second, separate cause without evidence.

title: bug(spawn): workspace + OpenCode fails chat start (ACP additionalDirectories unsupported)
body:
## Summary

`ao spawn` on a **workspace** project can create the git worktrees, then fail when starting the worker chat:

```text
chat controller: ACP agent does not support additional workspace directories (CHAT_CONTROLLER_FAILED)
```

Seen on AgentLab (`agentlab-in`, kind `workspace`, default worker harness **OpenCode**) while spawning a new worker (`agentlab-in-11`) on 2026-09-19. Retry failed the same way. Existing workers on that project (`agentlab-in-9`, `agentlab-in-10`) already had a chat controller and kept running.

## Why it happens

Workspace spawn does not only set cwd to the session root. It passes every **child worktree path** (except the root) as ACP `additionalDirectories`.

- `workspaceProjectDirectories` in `backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go` (collects `project.Worktrees` whose path is not the session root)
- `ChatStart.AdditionalDirectories` on the chat controller
- ACP driver `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/driver.go` calls `normalizeAdditionalDirectories`
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/session_setup.go`: if `directories` is non-empty and `init.AgentCapabilities.SessionCapabilities.AdditionalDirectories == nil`, return that error

OpenCode’s ACP initialize does not advertise `sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories`. AO fails closed. The session is then a failed spawn even though worktree add may have already run.

This is **not** a bad `ao spawn` invocation. It is workspace project + ACP harness without that capability + at least one child worktree.

## Repro

1. Workspace project with multiple registered children (e.g. six git children).
2. Default worker agent: OpenCode (ACP).
3. `ao spawn --project <id> --name test --prompt "ping"`
4. Observe `CHAT_CONTROLLER_FAILED` / `ACP agent does not support additional workspace directories`.

Single-repo projects should not hit this path (`workspaceProjectDirectories` returns nil when `project` is nil / not workspace).

## Expected

Either:

- Skip `additionalDirectories` when the agent does not advertise the capability, and still start chat with cwd = workspace root (children remain on disk under that root), **or**
- Fail earlier with a harness/capability error **before** creating worktrees, **or**
- Document that workspace workers require a harness that advertises additional directories (e.g. Claude Code) and refuse OpenCode at spawn validation.

Failing closed after worktree create leaves a half-made session.

## Non-goals

- Auto-registering unregistered clones on disk as workspace children (that is #5644).
- Changing the “all children in one worktree” workspace model.

Unregistered extra checkouts (we had cloned `alab-cli` into the workspace folder without registering it) are **not** in `workspaceRepos` and should not be the dirs AO sends. The dirs that trigger this are the **registered** child worktrees.

## Related

- #5644 workspace CLI lifecycle (list/add/rm/sync). Different bug; same area.
- #5643 add-repo CLI only.

## Environment

- AO CLI + daemon, 2026-09-19
- Project kind: workspace (`agentlab-in`)
- Worker harness: OpenCode
- Error code: `CHAT_CONTROLLER_FAILED`

title: bug(codex): cached executable path survives install/reinstall until daemon restart
body:
## Problem

`codex.Plugin` resolves the Codex executable once and caches the path in `resolvedBinary` for the life of the daemon. Nothing clears it when the user installs or reinstalls Codex from Settings, so the daemon keeps launching, probing, and listing models from the old executable until it is restarted.

## Reproduction

1. Start the daemon with Codex installed at path A.
2. Open any Codex Chat or model picker so the path is resolved and cached.
3. Reinstall or upgrade Codex so the executable now lives at path B, or path A is removed.
4. Trigger readiness, model discovery, or a launch. The daemon still uses path A.

## Why

`qwenBinary`/`codexBinary`-style resolvers guard the cache with a mutex but expose no way to reset it. `InvalidateAgentInstallation` in the readiness service only marks the readiness observation stale; the adapter's cached path survives.

## Fix direction

Give adapters that cache the path an optional invalidation capability and have `InvalidateAgentInstallation` call it, so the next operation re-resolves the current installation. The Qwen adapter caches the same way and needs the same treatment.

## History

A version of this fix shipped inside #5019 (Qwen Chat) as commit `c2ce82804`, bundled with a Reinstall button in Harness settings. That was out of scope for a Qwen PR and is being reverted (see the linked revert issue) so the fix can land on its own, aligned with #5003 and #5194, which own the installer-aware Codex update flow.

title: Blocker/non-blocker review findings — merge gate counts only blocking threads; reviewer must not resolve threads on behalf of the worker
body:
AO treats every unresolved review thread as a merge blocker and provides no way to mark a finding as non-blocking. This forces reviewers to resolve their own threads on behalf of the worker.

**Case:** the reviewer left two inline findings on a PR, explicitly marked as non-blocking observations deferred to the live run. The merge gate showed "Not mergeable yet — Unresolved review comments must be resolved", so the reviewer had to resolve his own threads just to clear it — breaking the rule that resolution belongs to the worker who applies the fixes.

## Proposal

1. **`blocking: true|false` on inline findings** — a field in the `comments` array of `ao review submit --reviews -` (default `true`). GitHub has no native flag on review threads, so store it in AO (the review already arrives as full JSON with `githubReviewId`) and optionally duplicate it as a `[non-blocking]` marker in the comment body.
2. **Merge gate counts only unresolved blocking threads.** Non-blocking ones stay open as the live-run checklist without gating the merge.
3. **Reviewer-task rule: the reviewer never resolves threads.** The reviewer files findings and replies on the merits; resolution is always the worker's job. With (1)–(2) in place this rule no longer conflicts with the gate.

## Open questions on the role model

- **Reviewer-merges:** in some configurations the reviewer also performs the merge — review, thread resolution and merge in one pair of hands. What compensators does AO intend (e.g. blocking threads resolvable only by the worker; self-merge blocked when reviewer and branch author share one account)?
- **Follow-up issues from review:** may the reviewer file issues (deferred observations, side bugs) instead of leaving them as inline threads that collide with the merge gate?
- **Role matrix:** an explicit action x role table (review / reply / resolve / merge / create issue / push) across {worker, reviewer, orchestrator, user} — today the rules live in task prompts and behavior is defined by whatever the gate blocks at the moment.

## Acceptance

- `blocking: false` findings do not affect mergeability; unresolved blocking threads still do;
- the reviewer-task template explicitly forbids resolving threads on behalf of the worker;
- blocking status is visible in the AO UI (and via marker in the GitHub comment body).

title: feat(cli): attach and detach workspace child repos via CLI
body:
Slice 2 of #5644. Closes #5643.

## What

Attach and detach workspace child repos from the CLI, so a workspace can gain or lose a child without re-running `project add --as-workspace`.

**Daemon**

* `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/repos` attaches one on-disk child to the registry. Name defaults to the directory basename. Origin and branch are inferred, and an explicit `defaultBranch` in the body wins. Unborn or origin-less children register as `needs_init`, same as add-time behavior.
* `DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}/repos/{name}` drops the row. Pass `?deleteFiles=true` to also delete the directory.
* New sqlc query `DeleteWorkspaceRepo`. No migration, no schema change.
* Root `.gitignore` is extended and committed on add through the extracted `commitWorkspaceGitignore` helper. Remove keeps the ignore line. The sync slice will reconcile stale entries.
* New error codes: `REPO_ALREADY_REGISTERED` (409), `REPO_NOT_FOUND` (404), `NOT_A_WORKSPACE_PROJECT` (400).
* No spawn changes. The session manager already reads `ListWorkspaceRepos` at spawn time, so the next spawn worktrees an added child automatically.

**CLI**

* `ao project repo add --project <id> --path <dir> [--name] [--default-branch] [--json]`
* `ao project repo rm --project <id> <name> [--delete-files] [--json]`
* `--project` falls back to `AO_PROJECT_ID` and the current directory, like spawn.
* Plain remove is registry only and needs no confirmation. `--delete-files` asks for the repo name before deleting anything on disk.

title: fix(chat): reap detached chat hosts after shutdown
body:
Detached chat hosts are started with Setsid but remain children of the long-lived AO daemon. Calling Process.Release() discards the handle without waiting, so an explicitly shut down chat-host can remain as a zombie owned by the daemon.

This replaces Process.Release() with an asynchronous Wait(), preserving detached/session restart behavior while ensuring the parent reaps the host when it exits.

The regression test starts a detached host, shuts it down, and asserts that its PID fully disappears from the process table rather than remaining as a zombie.

Observed live on Linux with AO commit 7e876efa1a947b41ff1284cb3da87bd74a2ab2f6: provider exited, session became terminated, but chat-host remained Z/defunct under the daemon; repeated runs accumulated zombies.

title: fix(browser): preserve host only cookies during profile import
body: Code changes: +4 -1 Tests: +15 -2 Others: +0 -0 ## What Preserve host-only cookie scope when importing browser profiles, including cookies using the `__Host-` prefix. ## Why The importer always supplied a `domain` to Electron, which converted host-only cookies into domain cookies. title: fix(workspace): lock orchestrator worktree to prevent deletion during worker cleanup (#5598)
body:
Fixes #5598

### Summary of Changes

During multi-agent orchestration, an orchestrator session can inadvertently delete its own active worktree and branch when executing cleanup instructions aimed at worker sessions. Because the orchestrator process remains running without a backing worktree, subsequent turns fail with provider/service failures.

This change:
- Uses \git worktree lock\ upon creation (\Create\ and \CreateWorkspaceProject\) for orchestrator sessions (\domain.KindOrchestrator\) with a distinct lock reason (\^Gctive AO orchestrator workspace\) so that accidental \git worktree remove\ (or worker cleanup commands) cannot delete the orchestrator's own worktree.
- Parses \LockReason\ from \git worktree list --porcelain\ and ensures \destroy()\ only unlocks worktrees locked by AO with \orchestratorLockReason\ during legitimate teardown, while preserving user/external locked worktrees and refusing removal.
- Unlocks the worktree during forced teardown paths (\ForceDestroy()\, \ orceDestroyPath()\).
- Updates the orchestrator system prompt rules in \session_manager/prompt.go\ to explicitly instruct orchestrator agents never to delete their own worktree or branch, and directs them to use \^Go session kill\ and \^Go session cleanup\ for worker sessions.
- Adds an integration test \TestWorkspaceIntegrationOrchestratorWorktreeLockedAndProtected\ verifying worktree locking, resistance to \git worktree remove\, and successful cleanup during authorized destruction.
- Updates unit tests in \gitworktree\ and \session_manager\.

## Summary

- release a parked terminal pane's WebGL context via `WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext()` instead of relying on `dispose()` alone, which only detaches the canvas and leaves the GPU slot counted against Chromium's ~16-context cap until GC
- gate the release on `loseContext()` succeeding — degrade to the 2D-canvas renderer if the slot can't be provably freed, rather than marking the pane parked and risking the accounting drifting from Chromium's live count

- harden the existing forced-loss handler so a throwing `dispose()` can't block the canvas fallback from loading
- add regression coverage for the renderer lifecycle: force-free on park + reload on unpark, context-lost panes staying on canvas, degrade-to-canvas when the slot can't be freed, canvas fallback surviving a throwing dispose, and construct-failure fallback

title: feat(cloud): ECS-on-EC2 (Graviton) self-hosted sandbox provider
body:
## What

Adds a self-hosted sandbox provider that runs each cloud session's worker as an ECS task on a Graviton (arm64) EC2 fleet, so sandboxed sessions run on our own AWS infra instead of paying NodeOps for dogfooding. It runs alongside coder (kept for 11x, which needs no isolation) and is additive: existing providers are untouched. New sessions default to ecs; coder and nodeops remain selectable.

## How it works

- Mirrors the docker provider: the worker is baked into the arm64 task image as its entrypoint; the per-session bootstrap environment rides as a RunTask container override; tasks are correlated by `startedBy` plus ownership tags; networking is bridge (no per-task ENI, so one host packs many sessions). Implements `Provider` + `Recreator`, not `Bootstrapper`.
- No idle-pause (users terminate sessions manually): the idle scanner skips ECS, `Stop`/`Delete` are StopTask, a stopped task maps to `StateDeleted` (it is terminal and its filesystem does not survive), and `Start` errors on a stopped task so the reconciler recreates with a fresh single-use ticket.
- Cross-architecture: sandboxes are arm64 while the control plane and the worker binary it serves are amd64, so the reconciler never advertises the self-update hash to an ECS session. The baked arm64 worker is authoritative and rebuilt from the same commit on every deploy.
- No provider secrets: the control-plane task role carries the `ecs:RunTask/StopTask/DescribeTasks/ListTasks/TagResource` and scoped `iam:PassRole` permissions.

## Provider selection and default

- The Settings provider picker is already data-driven from `/me`, so `ecs` appears automatically once the control plane advertises it; it gets a clearer `ECS (self-hosted)` label to set our own infra apart from the external NodeOps and Coder options.
- New `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` sets the default the control plane advertises and the provider a session with no explicit choice provisions on, separate from `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDER` (which stays the secret-plumbing primary, coder, so 11x keeps working). `deploy-staging.sh` sets the default to `ecs` when `AO_CLOUD_ECS_ENABLED=1`.

## Config

Enabled via `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS` (for example `coder,ecs`), defaulted via `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=ecs`, plus non-secret `AO_CLOUD_ECS_*` env. `deploy-staging.sh` injects these when `AO_CLOUD_ECS_ENABLED=1`.

## Tooling and docs

- `scripts/provision-ecs-sandbox.sh` (idempotent cluster, Graviton ASG, capacity provider, IAM, SG, task-def)
- `scripts/build-ecs-sandbox-image.sh` and `scripts/verify-ecs-sandbox-image.sh` (arm64 build + verify)
- `deploy-staging.sh` opt-in hook
- `cloud/ecs/README.md`

## Verification

- `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, full `cloud` test suite: green (provider, config, resolver, reconciler tests, including the ECS-default resolution and the no-self-update-hash-for-ECS invariant).
- Live on staging AWS (eu-north-1): cluster + Graviton c7g.2xlarge ASG + capacity provider + IAM + task-def provisioned; a Graviton instance registered, a smoke RunTask placed via the capacity provider, the arm64 worker pulled and executed on the host and exited on the expected missing-bootstrap-token error (no arch or pull error). ASG then scaled back to 0.

## Contract note (pre-existing)

The provider-selection wire fields (`provider` on create-session, `sandboxProviders` on `/me`) already ship via the hand-written desktop client but are not yet in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` / the generated `packages/cloud-client`. Left as pre-existing contract debt, out of scope for this PR.

title: [Bug]: lastInputAt map in terminal manager never pruned, leaks one entry per terminal id
body:
## Bug

`lastInputAt` in the terminal manager is never pruned, leaking one entry per terminal id for the daemon's lifetime.

Source: self-triage | Analyzed against: current `main` | Confidence: High (reproduced with a failing unit test locally, Go 1.27.1, macOS)

## Reproduction

Temporary/permanent test — `TestServeLastInputMapPrunedAfterClose` (`backend/internal/terminal/manager_test.go`):

1. Open 8 terminals on one connection through the real attach path (`msgOpen` → wait for `msgOpened`).
2. Type into each (`msgData`) — every accepted write runs `writeInput`, which sets `lastInputAt[terminalID]` at `manager.go:175`.
3. Wait until `len(mgr.lastInputAt) == 8` (confirms population).
4. Close each terminal through the normal path (`msgClose` → `closeTerminal` → `leaveTerminal` → `a.close()`).
5. Wait until `len(mgr.attachments) == 0` (confirms teardown actually completed).
6. Assert `len(mgr.lastInputAt) == 0`.

Actual: assertion fails — all 8 entries survive teardown.

Failure output:
```
--- FAIL: TestServeLastInputMapPrunedAfterClose (0.01s)
manager_test.go:162: lastInputAt not pruned after closing all 8 terminals: len = 8, want 0
(map leaks one entry per terminal id for the daemon's lifetime)
```

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:175` (`writeInput`): every keystroke sets `m.lastInputAt[terminalID] = time.Now()`. Nothing ever deletes from this map. Its sibling map, `inputBlocked`, *is* correctly cleaned up on drain release (`manager.go:160`), but `lastInputAt` has no equivalent teardown hook.

The correct prune point is `leaveTerminal`, not any earlier per-connection close: `leaveTerminal` already refcounts viewers of a shared terminal id and deletes `shared[id]` only when the last viewer leaves. `closeTerminal`, connection cleanup, and the `onExit` callback all funnel through it, so it's the universal teardown hook — and pruning any earlier would be wrong while another client still has the pane open.

## Fix

In `leaveTerminal`, when `len(s.members) == 0` and `shared[id]` is deleted, also `delete(m.lastInputAt, id)` under `inputMu`. Do **not** prune `inputBlocked` from this same hook — it's owned by the `BeginInputDrain`/release refcount and must not be cleared out from under an in-flight drain.

Verified locally:
- `TestServeLastInputMapPrunedAfterClose` — FAIL before the fix (`len = 8, want 0`), PASS after (one-line delete under the existing lock).
- Full `internal/terminal` package under `-race` — ok.
- `go vet ./internal/terminal/` — clean.

## Impact

Slow, unbounded memory leak: a long-running daemon where the user creates/destroys many terminal sessions accumulates one permanent `time.Time` entry per distinct terminal id ever typed into, for the process's entire lifetime. No workaround short of restarting the daemon.

title: fix: prune lastInputAt when a terminal's last viewer leaves
body:
## Summary

- `lastInputAt` in the terminal manager is set on every keystroke (`writeInput`, `manager.go:175`) but never pruned, leaking one `time.Time` entry per terminal id for the daemon's entire lifetime
- prune it in `leaveTerminal`, when `len(s.members) == 0` and `shared[id]` is deleted — this is the universal teardown hook (`closeTerminal`, connection cleanup, and `onExit` all funnel through it) and refcounts viewers, so a shared pane's entry survives while any client still has it open
- deliberately does **not** prune `inputBlocked` from the same hook — that map is owned by the `BeginInputDrain`/release refcount and must not be cleared out from under an in-flight drain
- add `TestServeLastInputMapPrunedAfterClose`, which drives the real attach/write/close paths through the existing fake harness and asserts the map is empty after all terminals close

Closes #5691.

## Testing

title: fix(gitworktree): remove worktrees with owner read-only dirs on Linux
body:
Code: +81 −5
Tests: +124 −0
Files removed: 0

## What

On Linux, AO could not delete its own worktree when a folder inside it was read-only for the owner (mode `0500`) and held a symlink. `renv` sandboxes create exactly this. Cleanup stopped with `openfdat ...: permission denied` and the worktree stayed on disk.

## Why

Deleting a file needs write permission on its parent folder, not on the file. A `0500` folder blocks that, and `removeAllWithRetry` gave up on the first error. Fixes #3807

## How

- `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/remove.go:92` — on a permission error, I repair the tree once and retry once.
- `remove_repair_other.go` — walks the worktree and gives owner `rwx` back to real folders only. It never calls `os.Chmod` on a symlink, so targets outside the worktree keep their contents and mode.
- Windows keeps its existing retry loop; the repair is a no-op there.

## Testing

- Added the issue's repro plus two more cases (read-only nested files, `0000` folder) in `remove_repair_other_test.go`. All three fail on `main` and pass here.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree -count=1` passes; `GOOS=windows go vet` passes.

title: fix(cloud): make deploy tooling safe for a multi-provider control plane
body:
Two fixes so `deploy-staging.sh` / `promote-production.sh` work correctly on the staging control plane, which serves **multiple** sandbox providers (`AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS=nodeops,coder`; eleven_x runs on coder).

## 1. Preserve secrets for every sandbox provider (the important one)

The renderer plumbed only the single active `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDER`'s secrets and pruned the rest. On a `nodeops`-primary deploy that **dropped all 8 `AO_CLOUD_CODER_*` secrets** (28 -> 20) and would have broken coder sandboxing for eleven_x. (Found live: a `deploy-staging.sh` render produced a 20-secret task-def vs the 28 the running CP carries.)

Now the tooling plumbs and preserves secrets for **every** provider in `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS`:
- `deployment.py`: `resolve_sandbox_providers` + `build_task_definition` prune only providers **not** in the available set, require the **union** of all available providers' secrets, and stamp `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS`. `validate_task_artifacts` derives the set from that env and rejects only non-served providers' secrets.
- `render-task-definition.py`: new `--sandbox-providers` (comma list; defaults to the single `--sandbox-provider`, so single-provider deploys are unchanged).
- `deploy-staging.sh` / `promote-production.sh`: resolve every provider in `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS`, validate and plumb each one's secret block (`providers_has` gating), pass `--sandbox-providers`, and rebake the coder workspace whenever coder is served.

Single-provider deploys render byte-identically to before. **23 deployment tests pass** (19 existing + 4 new for the multi-provider paths).

## 2. Allowlist four unpatched base-OS CVEs

Adds `CVE-2026-8927`, `CVE-2026-8924`, `CVE-2026-8286` (curl) and `CVE-2026-85091` (zlib) to `SCAN_CVE_ALLOWLIST` in both scripts (kept in sync). All four are CRITICAL/HIGH findings in base-OS packages with no Debian fix yet, in the same class as the existing entries, and the worker exercises none of their vulnerable code paths (no proxy/cookie/STARTTLS curl use; git uses zlib inflate/deflate, not the gz file API). Already present in the running worker image; each clears on its own once Debian ships the backport.

Sources: [8927](https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-8927.html) · [8924](https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-8924.html) · [8286](https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-8286.html) · [85091](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2026-85091)

## Related infra fix (done out-of-band, not in this PR)

The staging migrate task-def's container was named `migrate` while the codebase and production use `migration` (so `deploy-staging.sh`'s migration step would `StopIteration`). Fixed by re-registering `ao-cloud-staging-migrate` (rev 84) with container `migration` to match prod. That is a staging infra change, not code.

title: ci: run the SQLite package first so it stops starting last
body:
Code changes: +0 -0
Tests: +0 -0
Others: +22 -1

Part of #5116. **Stacked on #5632** — base is that branch, so the only variable in this diff is the package ordering.

## Summary

`go test` launches packages in import-path order, four at a time on `ubuntu-latest`. `internal/storage/sqlite` sorts 161st of 170 and is the longest package in the suite by a wide margin, so it starts last and then finishes alone.

Measured in [35435481761](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/35435481761), the warm-cache run on #5632:

| | |
| --- | ---: |
| packages listed before it | 160 (1358 package-seconds) |
| its start, into the Test step | 229s |
| its own runtime | 556.4s |
| Test step | 785s |
| work bound, 2091 package-seconds on 4 cores | 523s |

The 262s gap is the tail: three cores idle while the longest package runs by itself. Compilation is not the cause — with the cache restored by #5632 the first package result lands 2s into the step.

Listing it first should let the other 180 packages fill the slots behind it. Expected step near 560-600s, roughly 3 minutes.

## Why not a separate job

Giving the package its own job reaches about the same place — `max(556s, 1535/4)` — but renames the required check, which is a branch-protection change, and adds a second runner paying its own checkout and toolchain setup. One line of ordering is worth trying first.

## The list is asserted, not trusted

The obvious failure mode is a silent subset: if `go list` returns nothing, the command runs the SQLite package alone and the required check goes green having skipped the suite. That is the same class of bug as the test-result caching #5632 had to close, so the step counts what it is about to run:

```
want=$(printf '%s\n' "$all" | wc -l)
got=$(( $(printf '%s\n' "$rest" | wc -l) + 1 ))
```

Verified locally against all three paths:

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| normal | 181 packages, sqlite first, exit 0 |
| `go list` unavailable | exit 127 |
| filter over-matches | `package list mismatch: go list found 181, about to test 9`, exit 1 |

The `$` anchor keeps the subpackages — `sqlite/gen`, `sqlite/sqlitetest`, `sqlite/store` — in the second group where they belong.

## Validation

This PR's own CI run is the measurement. If the Test step does not drop, the revert is one line, and the fallback is the separate job described above.

title: feat(tracker-intake): support label-based eligibility filter alongside assignee
body:
## Summary

`TrackerIntakeConfig` only supports an `Assignee` eligibility rule for issue-driven worker spawning (`backend/internal/domain/tracker.go`). There is no way to additionally scope intake by label, even though the underlying `domain.ListFilter.Labels` field already exists and `Issue.Labels` is already surfaced into the worker prompt.

This makes intake all-or-nothing per assignee: any open issue assigned to the configured user gets a worker, regardless of whether it's actually ready for agent work (e.g. still triaging, needs design, blocked on another team).

## Background

- Label eligibility was in the original scope for issue intake (#2324: "Define explicit eligibility through a configured label, assignee, or both").
- PR #2325 (the v1 implementation) deliberately dropped labels from the shipped config during review, to keep v1's product/API surface to assignee-only: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2325#discussion_r3520579177 (review comment: "For v1, intake was supposed to be assignee-only... Can we remove labels from v1 intake end-to-end?"). The `ListFilter.Labels` type was intentionally retained for this follow-up.
- Two follow-up attempts were made and both were closed unmerged after the observer's tracker-resolution plumbing was reworked out from under them (first in #2325 itself, then again in #4644 for multi-tracker/GitLab support):
  - #2527 "bind GitHub intake to user and labels" — closed as superseded by the #4644 rework.
  - #2468 "add label filters and concurrency cap" — closed as stale for the same reason.
- Multi-tracker (GitHub + GitLab) intake landed via #4644, so any new implementation should filter through the current `ports.Tracker` / `ListFilter` seam rather than a GitHub-only adapter.

## Proposal

- Add an optional `Labels []string` field to `TrackerIntakeConfig`, additive to the existing required `Assignee` rule (not a replacement).
- Pass `Labels` into `ListFilter` in `trackerintake.Observer.pollProject`, and extend `issueMatchesConfig` to require all (or any — needs a decision, see open question) configured labels to be present on the issue.
- Surface the field through project config API/schema, CLI (`project set-config --tracker-labels`), and the dashboard's Tracker Intake settings (ideally as a multi-select against the repo's actual label catalog, as #2527 prototyped).

## Open questions

- AND vs OR semantics for multiple labels — #2468 used AND-for-include with an additional exclude list; #2527 used OR (flagged by a reviewer as surprising vs. GitHub's own filter UI, which is AND). Worth deciding explicitly before implementing rather than repeating the ambiguity.
- Whether to also support an exclude-labels list, or keep this slice include-only and follow up separately.

## Non-goals

- Reworking assignee semantics (`*`, `none`, explicit user) — out of scope here.
- Non-GitHub/GitLab providers.

title: Reviewer agent loops on dozens of consecutive no-op Bash true calls
body:
### Problem

Read-only reviewers cannot use `Write`/`Edit`, but the current reporting instructions require embedding review Markdown inside shell-quoted JSON for both GitHub publication and AO bookkeeping.

Reviewers can attempt to write a temporary payload, fall back to emitting it as ordinary response text—which AO does not consume—and enter the tool-call loops analyzed below (measured evidence preserved in the thread of closed PR #5863).

Fix the reporting contract rather than adding a loop detector or enabling file writes.

### Root cause (verified)

Verified from transcript re-analysis and the reviewer launch code:

- The reviewer is launched **read-only** (`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/claudecode/claudecode.go`): allowlist is Read/Grep/Glob plus narrow Bash (`printf`, `gh`, read-only `git`, `ao review submit`); `Write`/`Edit`/`NotebookEdit`/`git push`/`git commit` are hard-denied, headless — nothing outside the allowlist can be approved. The payload-file workaround is blocked by the Write ban (upstream #4810).
- The review prompt (`backend/internal/review/prompt.go`) allows exactly one hand-off: inline the entire review Markdown as a JSON string literal inside a shell-quoted `printf`, piped into `gh api` (publication) and into `ao review submit --reviews -` (bookkeeping).
- Long reviews full of quotes, backticks and newlines must be hand-escaped into shell-quoted JSON. When escaping fails, submission fails while the review text is already composed. The model then probes the only remaining channel (trivial Bash commands) and/or emits the JSON payload as plain assistant text, which a headless run never consumes — until a human intervenes.
- Two loop forms confirmed across hung reviewer transcripts: **probe storms** (fresh trivial command each time, commonly non-empty output; worst measured: 176 calls / 44 min / ~26M input tokens) and **identical repeats** (dozens of same-file `Read` calls with identical offset/limit). In every series the finished review was already present in the preceding assistant text. Loops also occur with thinking enabled.
- Any repetition guard must tolerate legitimate retry streaks (observed: 5 consecutive `git rebase --continue` retries is normal operation).

### Decision: one submission to AO, breaking change

The reviewer submits only to AO through the existing `ao review submit` command:

```bash
printf '%s' 'Review summary in Markdown' | ao review submit \
  --session worker-1 \
  --run run-1 \
  --verdict changes_requested \
  --body - \
  --comment-path src/auth.go \
  --comment-line 42 \
  --comment-body 'Missing authorization check.'
```

(`--session` is the canonical form for reviewer invocations; the positional form remains for interactive use.)

- Read the review body as plain Markdown from stdin.
- Accept inline findings through repeatable `--comment-path`, `--comment-line`, and `--comment-body` flags. Pair values by occurrence; reject incomplete groups. Omit these flags when there are no inline findings.
- **Finding bodies are single-line by contract.** Multi-line prose belongs in the review body, not in flag values; the CLI rejects multi-line `--comment-body` values with a clear error instead of inviting fragile shell quoting again.
- Do not parse findings out of Markdown or require model-authored JSON, temporary files, or JSON escaping in shell commands.
- The CLI performs internal serialization.

**This replaces the old workflow, rather than adding another optional mode.**

- No `--publish` flag: submission always includes publication.
- Remove legacy JSON/file submission through `--reviews` and file-valued `--body`.
- Remove caller-supplied `--review-id`; GitHub review IDs are outputs, not inputs.
- Reject obsolete inputs clearly. Update prompts, help, documentation, and reviewer adapters to the new contract.

### Daemon responsibilities

Use the existing submission endpoint and GitHub integration.

The daemon validates the run, persists the submitted content, publishes one GitHub `COMMENT` review containing the summary and inline findings, and records the returned review ID. Resolve the PR and target commit from the run.

Return the publication result through the same CLI invocation. Preserve findings in AO bookkeeping and worker feedback.

Repeated identical submissions must not create duplicate GitHub reviews. Persist publication-attempt state before the external request; report uncertain outcomes explicitly rather than blindly reposting.

Remove direct GitHub publication permissions from reviewers while retaining required read operations and AO submission. Keep `Write`/`Edit` prohibited.

No new MCP server, publication command, HTTP endpoint, generic JSON editor, or transcript-output parser.

### Open question for whoever designed the review flow

This contract is a stopgap: the issue author patched the broken hand-off from the outside, as best they could, without access to the original design intent. Properly, this should be addressed to whoever designed the review submission flow itself: **how do you want this to work for all users and harnesses?** The day-to-day review loop in agent-orchestrator is genuinely good — the goal is to make it better, not to redefine it unilaterally. Input from the original designer or maintainers on the shape of this contract is explicitly requested before any upstream PR.

### Acceptance and rollout

- Reviews with zero, one, and multiple inline findings reach GitHub and AO.
- Quotes, multiline Markdown, and code blocks survive unchanged.
- Multi-line `--comment-body` values are rejected with a clear error.
- Obsolete inputs fail clearly.
- Retries, concurrent submissions, daemon restarts, and GitHub failures do not lose results or silently duplicate publication.
- Verify the previously failing workflow with `Write` disabled, including another supported harness.
- Validate on the fork and collect before/after evidence before opening an upstream PR. Do not claim this eliminates every possible model loop.

## What

- Adds provider-neutral pull-request reviews to cloud sessions across Docker, NodeOps/CreateOS, and Coder.

title: ci: scope the Go build cache to build-test, and trim the snapshot helper
body:
Code changes: +0 -0
Tests: +7 -16
Others: +11 -18

Follow-up to #5632, which merged while these cuts were still local. No behaviour change.

## Cache only where compilation is on the critical path

#5632 enabled the Go build cache on three jobs. Only one of them needed it:

| job | duration | cache worth it |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `build-test` | 13m40s | yes — this is the regression in #5116 |
| `windows-workspace` | 4m46s | no, and a second large cache competes for the repository's 10 GB quota against the one that matters |
| `cloud-build-test` | 25s | no |

Both revert to `cache: false`. The seven `-count=1` flags that existed only to stop those restored caches replaying test results go with them — `build-test` keeps its own, which is load-bearing and stays.

## Trim the snapshot helper

- `sync.Mutex` on the cache: the package has no `t.Parallel` and no `go func` anywhere, so it guards concurrency that does not exist. It also runs under `-race`, so whoever adds `t.Parallel` gets a loud map race rather than silence.
- Lazy nil-map init: the `var` can initialise its own map.
- `noForeignKeysDSN`: one use, inlined.
- `migratedDatabaseSnapshot` and `buildMigrationSnapshots` duplicated a copy between them; the cache-hit check folds into the accessor and the builder stops returning a value.

## Validation

- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/storage/sqlite`: 78/78 pass, 423.3s — faster than the 463.6s measured on #5632, since the cuts remove a mutex and a redundant copy
- `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, and `golangci-lint v2.12.2`: clean, 0 issues

title: [Bug]: Cursor reviewer pane stalls on Cursor's MCP approval prompt — nobody is there to approve it
body:
## What went wrong?

A Cursor reviewer pane stops on Cursor's `MCP Server Approval Required` screen and the review never starts. Nobody is sitting at a reviewer pane, so there is no one to answer the prompt — the review just stays queued until a human notices the pane and clicks through by hand.

**Environment**

- AO desktop `0.13.1-nightly.202609191635` (nightly channel), macOS arm64
- `cursor-agent 2026.09.18-9a7762b`
- Reviewer harness `cursor`, configured via project config `reviewers: [{ harness: cursor, agentConfig: { model: <model> } }]`, with `autoReview` enabled

**Reproduction**

1. Use a repository that declares an MCP server in a checked-in `.cursor/mcp.json` (in my case one stdio server launched through the project's own CLI).
2. Let AO trigger an auto-review on a PR with the Cursor reviewer harness.
3. The reviewer pane opens and Cursor renders `MCP Server Approval Required` for the project server.
4. The review stays at `needs_review`, `cursor-agent` is alive, and no verdict is ever recorded. Approving by hand in the pane lets that one review proceed normally.

I saw this on two concurrent reviews: the one whose profile had no recorded approval stalled, the one that already had an approval from an earlier manual click ran to completion. That difference is what pointed at the profile rather than the harness.

**Why it recurs for every new session**

`reviewerProfileDir()` in `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/config.go` keys the AO-owned Cursor profile on `sha256(inv.ReviewerID)[:8]`, and Cursor records approvals per profile at `<CURSOR_DATA_DIR>/projects/<workspace-slug>/mcp-approvals.json`. So a manual approval is scoped to that one reviewer's profile; the next session gets a fresh profile and prompts again.

## Exact current launch behaviour

`(*Reviewer).ReviewCommand` (`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/cursor.go`) takes the argv from `agent.GetLaunchCommand` and splices the reviewer flags in ahead of the `--` separator:

```
cursor-agent --model <model> --trust --add-dir <ao-prompt-root> -- <task prompt>
```

with `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` pointed at the isolated AO reviewer profile. `--trust` trusts the workspace, but Cursor still gates repo-declared MCP servers behind the interactive approval screen. `ReviewRestoreCommand` delegates to `ReviewCommand`, so a restored pane hits the same screen.

## This is not the worker-path problem

#4333 / #4404 / #4495 covered the *worker* TUI path, where the fix was to stop losing sends while the approval screen is up (gate sends until the first agent hook arrives). That is a transport/ordering fix, and it is the right one for a worker, because a human is present and a follow-up is coming.

A reviewer pane has neither: there is no follow-up to gate and no one to approve. This issue is about **reviewer trust policy**, not send ordering, and I don't think the worker fix generalises to it.

## What I tested locally

I have a local one-line change that adds `--approve-mcps` to the reviewer flags:

```go
flags := []string{"--trust", "--approve-mcps"}
```

`insertBeforePrompt` already handles placement, so it lands before `--` and leaves `--model`, `--trust`, `--add-dir`, prompt delivery and the profile env untouched. Because `ReviewRestoreCommand` delegates to `ReviewCommand`, fresh and restore launches are both covered by that single site.

I added five argv regression tests in `cursor_test.go` — full fresh argv; ordering relative to `--trust` / `--add-dir` / `--`; the `insertBeforePrompt` no-separator fallback; restore argv identical to fresh; flag retained when `--add-dir` is omitted — each verified to fail with the change reverted and pass with it. `gofmt` and `go vet` clean, `go build ./...` passes, and `go test -race` passes across all reviewer adapters plus `internal/adapters/agent/cursor` and `pkg/agentruntime`. The worker path (`pkg/agentruntime.buildCursorLaunch`, which owns the `--force` / `--yolo` mapping) is untouched.

**I am not assuming that is the fix you want.** See the tradeoff below — I'd rather you pick the direction than have me land a permissive default.

## The tradeoff, stated plainly

`--approve-mcps` auto-approves the MCP servers **the reviewed checkout declares**. A `.cursor/mcp.json` specifies an arbitrary `command`, so on a branch from an untrusted contributor this means AO spawns a repo-controlled process during review without asking. Today the prompt is what stops that: it is a deadlock for AO, but it is also a real gate.

That sits awkwardly next to #2844 (least-privilege workers, "naked" unless opted in) and #3745 (enforce read-only tool access for reviewer harnesses). Options I can see, roughly least to most permissive:

1. **Disabled by default.** `installReviewerConfig` already owns the reviewer profile; it could write `mcp-disabled.json` alongside the config it writes today, so reviewers run with no MCP at all. No new CLI flag, no new trust, removes the stall, and it matches the direction in #2844. Cursor supports this — `cursor-agent mcp disable <id>` is what writes that file.
2. **Restricted / allowlisted.** Approve only servers the AO user has explicitly allowed for reviewers, rather than whatever the checkout happens to declare.
3. **Opt-in.** A per-project or per-reviewer setting that enables auto-approval, defaulting to off, so the permissive behaviour is a deliberate choice.
4. **Always approve** — the `--approve-mcps` change above. Simplest, and defensible if reviewing a branch is already treated as trusting it, but the most permissive.

My own preference is (1) or (3); I implemented (4) only because it was the smallest thing that unblocked me locally, and I'm happy to rework it into whichever direction you prefer, or to leave it with you entirely.

Either way the stall itself seems worth fixing: right now an auto-review on any repository with a checked-in `.cursor/mcp.json` silently never completes.

---

Investigated with agent assistance; the reproduction, environment and test results above are from my own machine.

title: feat(cloud): provision the coder flow on Azure (CP + DB stay on AWS)
body:
## What

Stand up the **coder flow on Azure** so cloud sessions with `provider=coder` run on Azure VMs/containers, while the control plane and its database stay on AWS. Goal: dogfood internally and demo to eleven_x on Azure credits without moving the CP or data.

## Why it needs no AO code change

The coder provider (`cloud/internal/sandbox/coder/`) already targets a Coder API endpoint (`AO_CLOUD_CODER_URL`), and `cloud/coder/main.tf` is a **Docker** template (workspace = a container via a Docker socket). So it already runs on any Docker host. "Coder on Azure" is therefore infra plus a one-line config repoint. The same `main.tf` and `Sandbox.Dockerfile` are reused verbatim.

## Contents

- `cloud/scripts/provision-coder-azure.sh` - one Azure VM running Docker + Coder + Postgres, plus a long-lived admin API token. Parameterized (region, VM size, names) and idempotent; retries the transient VM-create NIC race.
- `cloud/scripts/provision-coder-azure-template.sh` - builds the workspace image on the VM (bakes the release-matched `ao-worker` from the control-plane image; amd64, so no cross-arch worker gymnastics) and publishes the `ao-linux-docker` template.
- `cloud/coder/AZURE.md` - architecture, provisioning, CP wiring, the shared-CP guardrail, region guidance (Sweden Central next to `eu-north-1`), and teardown.

## Guardrail

Do not repoint the **shared staging CP** at the Azure Coder (it would move eleven_x's workspaces). Dogfooding uses a separate/dev CP; the coder config is a single endpoint per CP.

## Validation

Provisioned live in `swedencentral`: Coder healthy, template published, and a test workspace spun up a container on the Azure VM with the agent **connected**. Then torn down.

## Notes / follow-ups (in AZURE.md)

title: bug(send): a message delivered into a TUI session concatenates with the operator's half-typed draft and submits both as one prompt
body:
## Bug

A message delivered by `ao send` / `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` is written into a TUI
session's composer without checking whether a human is in the middle of typing there. The
inbound text is appended to the operator's half-written draft and the trailing Enter submits
the concatenation as a single prompt.

The operator loses their draft and the agent receives a garbled prompt that mixes two
unrelated intents.

Reported while typing into an orchestrator's Terminal while a worker sent a status update;
it is not orchestrator- or worker-specific.

## Reproduction (verified)

Environment: macOS 26.2, `ao version dev`, upstream/main `99a79364`, claude-code harness,
ConPTY (pty-host) runtime, session mode `tui`.

1. Open a TUI-mode session on its Terminal.
2. Type a partial message into the composer; do not press Enter.
3. From another session: `ao send --session <id> --message "<text>"`.

Observed — the durable prompt recorded by the provider for that submission:

```
2026-09-20T23:52:04.200Z
'I have written this far[from agent-orchestrator-7] [repro-2] terminal draft mixing probe - this is a test, no work needed.'
```

`I have written this far` is the operator's unsubmitted draft. Everything from
`[from agent-orchestrator-7]` on is the delivered message (`ao send` prefixes the payload with
`[from <sender session>] `). The two run together with no separator, and the trailing Enter
submitted them as one prompt. Draft and payload text are translated from the original
Japanese; the structure is verbatim.

**Chat mode is not affected** (control run): the same `ao send` into a chat-mode session
landed as its own `automation` turn with no draft mixed in. Chat delivery goes through
`sendChat` -> `RelayChatTurn` -> `Controller.Send`, which appends exactly one user message
and never touches the renderer's composer state.

`ao send` is only the easiest trigger. The same `/send` endpoint is called straight from the
renderer, so these UI actions can concatenate into a draft the same way:

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/DiffSelectionMenu.tsx:105` (send a diff selection)
- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useFileAnnotation.ts:61` (send a file annotation)
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/BrowserPanel.tsx:244`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx:1784,1791` (send review comments)

## Root cause

The delivery path has no notion of composer occupancy:

- `sessionguard.Guard.Deliver` (`backend/internal/sessionguard/guard.go:195-200`) documents
  `waiting_input` as a safe write target: "an agent sitting at an idle prompt is exactly where
  a user message ... belongs". The policy never considers that the prompt may hold a human
  draft. `Guard.Nudge` does refuse `waiting_input`, so AO-initiated messages are protected; a
  user-initiated `ao send` is not.
- The runtime writers just type and press Enter, without reading the screen:
  `tmux.Runtime.SendMessage` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:751`) and
  `conpty.Runtime.SendMessage` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/runtime.go:478`).
  Both runtimes share the defect, so the guard belongs above them in the Deliver path.
- The fact needed for a guard already exists and is unused here:
  `ports.TerminalComposerDraft` (`backend/internal/ports/terminal_surface.go:25`), with
  `InspectTerminalSurface` implementations in claudecode and codex. Its only consumer is the
  interface-transition drain (`interface_transition.go:983`), which *does* protect operator
  drafts when switching Terminal <-> Chat.
- `WaitForMessageDeliveryReady` consults `ComposerIsEmpty`, but it is reached only from the
  delegation path (`service/session/delegation.go:129`), and that check is skipped whenever the
  activity detector is authoritative — which it is for an idle session holding a draft.

## Expected

A send into a TUI session whose composer holds a human draft must not concatenate. Either
refuse with a typed retryable outcome (the caller retries, as with the existing `Suppressed*`
outcomes), or hold the message until the composer is empty.

## Suggested fix direction

Two signals already exist; either can gate the Deliver path:

1. `TerminalInputGate.BeginInputDrain(terminalID) (lastInputAt, release)`
   (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:283-289`, implemented at
   `backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:148`) atomically blocks later terminal writes and
   returns the timestamp of the newest accepted human keystroke. Holding it across the pane
   write closes the check-then-write race as well.
2. `InspectTerminalSurface(...).Composer == TerminalComposerDraft`, the same fact the
   interface-transition drain uses.

Fail open on `TerminalComposerUnknown` and on adapters/runtimes without the capability, so
delivery is preserved where the draft state cannot be proven. Note #5482: over-eager draft
detection misreads provider chrome as a draft, which here would silently block delivery — the
transition drain requires repeated samples before trusting a draft observation.

## Related

- #4030 — concurrent `ao send` calls coalesce into one submission. Same write boundary, but
  AO-authored text colliding with AO-authored text; PR #5428 (serialize deliveries in
  sessionguard) does not consider a human draft. That serialization would be a natural place
  to add this check.
- #3221 (fixed) — a stranded AO message flushed by the next send.
- #5482 / #5301 — draft detection on the interface-switch path, the opposite failure direction.

title: fix: refuse sends into a TUI composer holding an unsent human draft
body:
Code changes: +650 -58  
Tests: +1037 -8  
Others: +0 -0  

## Summary

When a Terminal UI session's composer holds a half-typed human message, an AO delivery (`ao send`, a relay, or a worker report) is pasted after that text, and the runtime's trailing Enter submits both as one prompt. The operator loses their draft, and the agent gets a garbled instruction.

AO now refuses to write into a composer that holds an unsent draft, and returns a retryable `409 SESSION_COMPOSER_BUSY` instead.

Fixes #5711.

## Root cause

The guard's `refuseDeliver` checked only startup readiness and `ActivityBlocked`. An idle, `waiting_input` or active session with a draft in its composer went straight to the pane write. Nothing looked at the composer, and nothing stopped a keystroke from landing between a check and the paste.

## Changes

**Draft check before the write (`send_composer_guard.go`, `sessionguard`)**
- Every non-empty TUI send runs a composer check under the guard's input lease, right before the pane write. This covers `ao send`, relays, worker reports and messages delivered after an agent switch.
- An empty message, the deliberate Enter that submits an existing draft, is not checked.
- The check reads the screen with the existing `InspectTerminalSurface`, which the draft-preservation drain (#3953, #5482, #5486) already uses:
  - A draft must show on 3 captures in a row before a send is refused.
  - Sampling waits for the last keystroke to render.
  - Idle, `waiting_input` and active sessions are all inspected.
  - Provider approval and input screens are not drafts.
- Anything it can't prove fails open and delivers. That covers a non-TUI session, a harness or runtime that can't read the screen, a capture error, and a probe that runs past 5 s.
- A proven draft returns a new `SuppressedComposerBusy` outcome. It maps to `ErrComposerBusy` and then `409 SESSION_COMPOSER_BUSY`, and nothing is written.

**No keystroke between the check and the paste (`terminal.Manager.HoldInput`)**
- Once the probe reads an empty composer, the guard holds that terminal's input fence. It waits for the newest keystroke to render, repeats the three-sample draft proof, and keeps the fence held through the paste.
- A keystroke typed meanwhile waits until the paste is done. It is not dropped.
- Input buffered while a client is still attaching waits on the same fence.
- The fence is per terminal, so other terminals keep typing.

**Other terminals stay responsive (`terminal/manager.go`)**
- The desktop app sends every terminal over one WebSocket, and keystrokes were written on that connection's read loop. A keystroke waiting on the fence froze typing, resizes and pings in every terminal.
- Each connection now writes a terminal's input through its own ordered queue.
- Input received during a drain is still refused, and keys typed just before a terminal is closed are still written.
- A terminal's queue is retired once it closes.

**No retry Enter on the operator's typing (`confirmActive`)**
- For claude-code and its delegators, AO presses Enter again if the session doesn't go active. Each retry now holds the terminal input fence across the latest-input timestamp check and the Enter write.
- It is skipped once the operator has typed since the send. The send reports `ErrDeliveryUnconfirmed`, unless this delivery's acceptance evidence is already there.

**Refused reports don't block other projects (`report.Coordinator`)**
- A report refused for a draft is now deferred 30 s (`ErrOrchestratorBusy` → `DeferReportBatch`).
- Releasing it kept it the earliest due report. `RunDue` then stopped on it every 5 s, so no other project's reports were delivered.

## Review updates

This PR incorporated four rounds of review feedback:

1. **First review (axisrow):**
   - Rebased onto main, so `DeliverUnderMutationChecked` (#5436) compiles and is never composer-gated.
   - Removed the recency shortcut that skipped the screen when the agent had acted after the last keystroke.
   - Provider waiting and approval screens are treated as not-a-draft.
   - Added a settle window after the last keystroke, a probe deadline, a read-only `LastInputAt` (the drain used to drop keystrokes), logged fail-open paths, and a `ctx.Err()` check before the write.
   - Added the end-to-end 409 test and coverage for `composerBusyCheck`.
2. **Second review (ronishrohan):**
   - Worker reports now run the check.
   - Active turns are inspected.
   - Terminal input is fenced across the final check and the paste.
3. **Third review (ronishrohan):**
   - Typing buffered during attach now waits on the fence.
   - The fenced re-check waits for the newest keystroke to render before capturing.
   - The fence is per terminal instead of manager-wide.

4. **Fourth review (ronishrohan):**
   - Fenced each confirmation Enter from the latest-input check through the actual write.
   - Refreshed the human-input timestamp after buffered replay reaches the PTY, while holding its fence, so a slow attach cannot bypass the render settle window. Terminal reports do not refresh this timestamp.
   - Reused the repeated-sample draft proof under the fence so one transient frame cannot cause a false 409.
   - Added regression tests that failed before each fix and pass with `-race` afterward.

After the third review I also added the following, each with a test that fails without it:
- The per-terminal keystroke queue. A per-terminal fence alone still froze every terminal sharing the desktop app's connection.
- The retry-Enter check.
- The report back-off.

## Testing

New tests:
- **`sessionguard`:** the composer check runs while the input lease is held and before the write, the fence is released only after the write, and a cancelled context never writes.
- **`TestComposerHoldsDraft`:**
  - Drafts are refused in idle, `waiting_input` and active sessions, even when the agent acted after the last keystroke.
  - Provider screens are not drafts, and a draft that clears mid-sequence delivers.
  - Sampling waits for the last keystroke.
  - Every unprovable case fails open, including a hung capture.
- **Fenced re-check:** catches a keystroke that renders late and a stable draft that appears after the probe, permits a transient draft-shaped frame, and hands the fence back still held for the write.
- **Send path:**
  - A draft is refused, an empty composer delivers, the Enter-only resubmit is unchecked, and a worker report is refused.
  - The retry Enter is skipped once the operator types, including typing accepted while retry admission is acquired; retries retain the input fence through the write and still run when nobody types.
- **`terminal`:**
  - A held fence queues keystrokes without dropping them or stalling the connection's other terminals and pings.
  - Typing buffered during attach waits on the fence and refreshes the render-settle timestamp when replayed; automatic terminal reports leave that timestamp unchanged.
  - Queued keys survive a close, closed terminals don't keep writers, and a reopened terminal's writer waits for the retired one.
  - Input received during a drain is refused.
- **`service/report` and `daemon`:** a busy orchestrator is deferred while other projects' reports are delivered, and the daemon reports a draft refusal as busy.

Every new test for the last round failed before its fix.

Local runs (from `backend/`):
- `go build ./...`: ok · `go vet`: ok · `gofmt`: clean
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/sessionguard/ ./internal/terminal/ ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/service/report/ ./internal/daemon/`: pass
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on the touched packages: only `session_manager/manager.go` `time-naming: scriptStepMinute`, which is existing code on `main`

Follow-up validation for `4964d09279` (2026-10-24, macOS / Go 1.27.1):
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`: pass.
- Focused composer, confirmation-Enter, buffered-replay and terminal-fence tests with `-race -count=1`: pass. All four new regression tests failed before the fixes.
- Full `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./...`: attempted, not a local pass. It encountered adapter failures also reproduced on main, then missing shared Go-cache import files; the invalidated run was stopped. Complete affected-package suites subsequently passed with an isolated cache and `SHELL=/bin/sh` (matching CI); the inherited fish shell caused the earlier terminal integration failures.
- Complete affected-package `-race -count=1` suites: pass for `sessionguard`, `terminal`, `session_manager`, `service/report`, `service/session`, and `daemon`.
- Pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 locally: only the existing `scriptStepMinute` time-naming warning; no findings in the follow-up changes. The remote lint check passed.
- Docker-based local workflow validation is unavailable because the Docker daemon socket is absent. The new macOS, Windows, Linux and container CLI checks all passed remotely.
- All 20 remote checks passed for `4964d0927955bea24e003f573f1aa5d64acf3415`, including all backend race-test shards, the build gate, lint, API/SQL drift, native macOS/Linux/Windows CLI checks, and the container check.

## Limitations

- After an `ErrDeliveryUnconfirmed`, AO's own unsubmitted prompt reads as a draft. Later sends get a 409 until someone clears it, and reports to that orchestrator retry every 30 s.
- Two AO sends to the same session at once can give the second a spurious 409, because it sees the first send's paste before its Enter. #5428, which serializes deliveries, would cover this.
- Waiting for the fence has no timeout, so a keystroke write stuck on a full PTY stalls a send to that session.
- Keys typed through a direct `tmux attach` are not fenced.

- [X] Branched from main (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [X] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [X] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [X] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
