title: style(review): quiet and flatten the review tab
body:
## What

A UI-only pass over the session inspector's **Reviews** tab, in two commits: the controls at the top, then the expanded review card below them. No behaviour is added or removed — every control, disclosure and action still does what it did.

## Why

The tab read as a settings form bolted onto a panel. The controls used ALL CAPS section labels, rows ruled off from one another, and labels written as instructions rather than names. The expanded review below them was a stack of same-weight parts: three filled surfaces nested inside each other, two disclosures styled identically despite doing different things, and four levels of nesting rendered flat.

One label was also simply wrong: the row keyed `inspector.review.session` rendered as "Trigger review" while holding the reviewer-session controls and restating the "Review latest commit" button beside it.

## How

**Controls**

- Row card loses its horizontal padding, so control rows share a left edge with their section heading and the review cards below. The tab keeps its own gutter.
- Section headings in sentence case, per [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) ("Never use ALL CAPS labels"), and matched to each other — "Review summary" had been a size larger than "Review controls".
- Row labels name the thing, following onboarding's `Coding agent` / `Credential type` pattern: "Select reviewer agent" → **Reviewer agent**, "Trigger review" → **Reviewer session**.
- The ⓘ beside "Auto review" is gone; the toggle and label already say what it does. That orphaned `inspector.autoReviewDescription`, dropped from all 8 locales.
- Dividers replaced by spacing; the agent dropdown sizes to its label instead of clipping at `11rem`.
- The reviewer session row is hidden while auto review is **idle**, where its controls are all disabled anyway. It deliberately returns while a review is **in flight** — stopping one is reachable from nowhere else, and `shows reviewing status and cancel action while auto-review is running` covers that path.

**Expanded review card**

- One surface instead of three; a hairline replaces the nested fill.
- Card header is a single centre line: avatar, reviewer and timing left, verdict and actions right. Name and timing wrap as a pair so a narrow rail drops the timing rather than clipping the reviewer's name to `cod…`.
- "Show more" no longer mimics the "Resolved comments" disclosure — no chevron, no underline, 10px, and positioned where the clamped text actually stops.
- The clamp's fade is gone; it half-erased a live line and read as a bug.
- Resolved comments are nested under their heading by a rule, with quieter bodies.

**Worth a reviewer's attention:** `useClampedTextEnd` is the one piece of real machinery here. `line-clamp` hides overflow without reporting where it cut, so anything pinned to an edge drifts away from text ending mid-line. The hook walks the rendered text with a `Range` to find the last character still inside the clamp box and positions the control there, re-measuring on resize. It falls back to the bottom-right corner when it cannot measure — which is what happens in jsdom, where rects are zero-sized. **That fallback is why the suite stays green, so the positioning path itself is not covered by tests**; it was verified by measuring in the running app.

Two smaller findings while doing this: `--color-bg-settings-row` resolves to `transparent`, so an overlay using it let text run straight through (the painted surface is `bg-background`); and `tailwind-merge` cannot distinguish `text-micro` (a size) from `text-passive` (a colour) and silently drops one, so the size now sits on a wrapper.

## Testing

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` — clean.
- `packages/product-ui` — 129/129 pass.
- `SessionInspector.test.tsx` — 119/119 pass, including the updated auto-review assertions.
- Measured in the running app (`dev:web`, mock data): control rows, section headings and review cards share one left edge inside the panel gutter, with no horizontal overflow; header items share one centre line across differing heights; the expander sits 0px from the end of the truncated text, on the same line, 221px clear of the right edge.
- Runs showing failures in `ProjectViews` / `TaskComposerView` / `SessionsBoardView` were 5s timeouts from a background typecheck competing for CPU, in files this PR does not touch; they pass once it is cleared.

**Not verified:** the `frontend/e2e` spec edits are string updates made by inspection — that suite needs a running app and was not executed. The resolved-comments indent is confirmed structurally (the rule is applied when open) but never seen rendered, as no preview fixture produces resolved comments.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) — frontend typecheck and unit suites pass locally; CI not yet run

title: Mobile UI touch-up: type, icons, keyboard and board fixes
body: A pass over the mobile app after driving it on a real iPhone for a few days. Three things drove everything here: it did not look like the desktop app, it fought the keyboard, and a few screens broke outright. SCREENSHOTS: @Prasad-D-Ware mostly just quality of life changes, improving parity with desktop app, and some ux improvements ## Type now comes from the renderer The app was drawing SF Pro because no family was bundled at all, and its own ramp used weight 700 and 800 for every title. The renderer stops at `--font-weight-semibold`, so the same screen looked heavier on the phone than on the desktop. Geist and Geist Mono are bundled and loaded before the first paint. Weights are 400, 500 and 600 only; 92 bold usages were normalised to semibold. Tracking follows the renderer's scale instead of SF Pro's optical values, which run positive at large sizes and were pulling the other way. A weight is a font file here, not a number: iOS draws whichever face the family name points at and ignores `fontWeight`, so every style that sets a weight names its face. `fontForWeight` in `lib/tokens.ts` is that mapping, and 310 inline styles were updated to use it. ## Icons come from the desktop's set The desktop draws from Lucide. The app drew from Feather, which is Lucide's ancestor, so most glyphs looked close enough and a few did not. `lib/icons.tsx` now imports `lucide-react-native` at the same version as the renderer (1.47.0) and maps the names the call sites already use, which keeps the diff to one file plus the import lines. MaterialCommunityIcons is gone from the pin rail and the sidebar destinations; pinning uses the desktop's Pin and PinOff. The native SwiftUI chrome keeps SF Symbols. Those are real SwiftUI views inside an `@expo/ui` Host and Lucide glyphs cannot be drawn there. ## The keyboard The composer snapped because we positioned it from `keyboardVisible`, a flag that turns over when the keyboard has finished moving. The dock did the same thing, which left its buttons hanging where the keyboard had been and then snapping back. Both now hold their resting position and ride the keyboard's own progress, so they travel with the keys. Two related bugs: the composer dismissed the keyboard after the send resolved rather than on the tap, which tied its exit to the network, and the dock's lift was computed from the library's animated `height`, which is the keyboard frame origin and negative while the keyboard is up, so the lift was always zero and the search field sat under the keys. The composer is one borderless capsule now, with Liquid Glass drawn behind the row. Its size comes from constants, not from layout: three attempts at a growing pill each ended with the material drawn at a different size than the pill it sat behind, because every one of them read that size at runtime while the keyboard was still moving. ## Board and session fixes Switching project filters showed two lists at once, recycled cells of the old grouping under the new data with the empty state on top. The list is now mounted per filter. The worker dock's menus open upward, and SwiftUI reverses an upward menu's items under its default order, which put "All projects" last. Both menus pin their order, and the projects row shows the selection alone rather than a prefix that wrapped. On iOS 26 the session header's actions button was drawing the system's shared bar-button background under our own glass, so it came out with two outlines and a squarer shape than the back button beside it. Glass controls in native headers are declared as header items with the shared background hidden. Page transitions showed a white seam between the outgoing and incoming screens, from the navigator's own container colour, which comes from the navigation theme and defaults to white. The theme now carries the palette. The seam is gone in the 93 frames I captured across pushes and pops. Also in here: the conversation start label and the message bubble border are gone, the session screen renders its content while it is still sliding in rather than after, and its header title is set on the first commit instead of a frame later. One crash fix that is not cosmetic. `expo-web-browser` arrived with an earlier branch and its native module was never added to this worktree's Pods project, so any tap that opens a GitHub link threw while the module was being imported and took the screen down. The dependency is now installed properly, and the import is guarded so a build without the pod falls back to the system browser the way this function used to. ## Since this was written Review turned up three things, each now fixed: the font load had no error path and kept no splash, so a face that failed to load left the app on a blank root forever; the header buttons lost the `isButton` trait when the glass surface moved from a `Button` to a `Group`; and the icon and font barrels were shipping their whole sets — a production iOS export carried 4,330 modules against 2,480 on main, and registered all 36 Geist faces for the four the app draws. Per-glyph and per-weight imports bring that export to 2,563 modules, four faces, and 5.38 MB against 8.46 MB. More days of driving it after that turned up the rest of what is in this branch: - **Merged has its own hue.** It was drawing the same muted grey as a session that had merely switched off, under the green that had just said "mergeable". The palette had a deliberate "no purple" rule enforced by a test — purple is in now, meaning exactly that one state, and the legend and the test were updated to say so rather than being left contradicting the code. - **"Needs you" and "Pinned" never fold.** Both could be hidden behind a chevron, so the board could show a clean, quiet screen with work waiting inside it. The rest still fold and stay folded. - **A row without a pull request names its branch.** Dropping the branch outright had left the second line blank on exactly the rows where the branch was the only thing naming the worktree. - **Back no longer dead-ends.** `router.back()` on an empty stack is an unhandled `GO_BACK`, and a screen with no other exit had no way out — a deep link or a notification tap that cold-starts the app is how a screen gets there. One `backOr` now covers all fourteen exits, with a source test that fails on an unguarded one. - **A working row's circle breathes.** It was drawn as a bare glyph, so the one status that means "still going" was the only one that never moved, while the same word breathed on the project cards. - **The spawn sheet stopped naming a model the provider will not run.** It showed the catalog's `isDefault` entry, and codex's is wrong — `gpt-6-astra` advertised while a new thread comes up on `gpt-5.6-sol` — and picking that value sent no model at all, so the session recorded nothing and the chat displayed whatever the thread happened to be running. - **The composer footer's label no longer draws over its neighbours** — the context meter, or the "sent after this" note when a message is queued. - **The Android swipe rail's buttons sit in the row's centre.** The rail spans the row's full height while its buttons are a fixed 76pt block, so they were top-pinned and would drift high on any row taller than the minimum. ## Checking it `tsc` is clean and the suite passes at 130 files and 1228 tests. Most of the visual work was checked by capturing the simulator while driving it, including frame-by-frame captures for the transition seam and the keyboard geometry. Two things I could not verify and would like a second pair of eyes on: the simulator's software keyboard refuses to appear on this machine, so the keyboard travel is verified by construction and by its endpoints rather than by watching it, and menus need a tap I cannot perform, so the menu order rests on the documented SwiftUI behaviour. ## Known gaps The Android drawer still uses FontAwesome for its two items, and the native SwiftUI chrome uses SF Symbols. Both would need shipped image assets to match Lucide exactly.

title: refactor(ui): converge the app on one design language
body:
Retargeted onto `main`. This branch used to sit on top of #5566; the only thing it needed from there was the onboarding button's radius and weight, which is `--radius-topbar-control: var(--radius-md)` here.

## What

Several parts of the app had competing implementations of the same thing. This pulls them onto one vocabulary. No layout changes.

**Focus** — one treatment (`outline-2` + `--ring`), replacing eight: 2px rings, 1px rings, brand-coloured rings, inset rings, and a width-less one, across 26 files.

**Colour naming** — `text-settings-muted`, `text-settings-label`, `settings-accent` and `color-text-import-title` were all aliases of existing roles *in the same context*; collapsed onto the roles themselves. `error` and `danger` resolve to the same hue as `destructive` in every theme, so 126 classes moved to the documented name — `DESIGN.md` uses "destructive" throughout, and the emitted values are byte-identical.

**Inputs** — `Input` (`default` | `field` | `bare`), a new `Textarea`, and `SearchField` (`field` | `menu`). Three CSS utilities that each re-spelled the same bordered field are deleted.

**Buttons** — gained the variants the app was already hand-rolling: `quiet`, `danger`, `rail`, `link`, `link-quiet`, `icon-xs`, `icon-lg`. Neutral hovers now share one wash, press uses the `scale-press` token, and the primitive honours `prefers-reduced-motion` — the hand-rolled copies did, the primitive didn't.

**Hover** — the sidebar's growing fill is now the default for every transparent button: `ghost`/`quiet` Buttons, the transparent topbar variants, and the inspector tabs. Chip triggers opt in through a new `highlight` prop; the composer's selectors also drop their carets.

**Chat composer** — 16px radius, and a border that no longer changes in any state.

## Verification

- Every touched module compiles through the Vite dev server.
- Run against a real database alongside several live instances. That caught a genuine regression — a converted `<Button>` with no import in `Sidebar.tsx` — which neither tag balance nor the transform detects, only running it.
- Token moves were checked value-exact rather than assumed: `text-error` and `text-destructive` both emit `color: var(--bridge-danger)`.
- After the move to `main`, the sweep was re-run across the whole tree: no remaining reference to a collapsed token, and the two dangling vars the re-base re-exposed are fixed (`--color-text-muted-foreground` → `--muted-foreground`, `--color-text-import-title` → `text-foreground`). The `packages/product-ui` views that the first pass missed now speak the same vocabulary as the renderer.
- **Not run:** the frontend test suite. Class-name assertions were updated where they were coupled (`TopbarButton.test.tsx`, `Sidebar.test.tsx`, `SessionInspectorView.test.tsx`).

## Deliberately left, and why

- `text-passive` measures **2.41:1** against a 4.5:1 requirement, and it's a chart-ramp step used as a text colour. Repainting it is a design call.
- Dialog widths have six vocabularies; converging them moves geometry by 8–72px, which is layout, not polish.
- ~178 raw `<button>` remain — many are rows, tabs and menu items that legitimately aren't Buttons — plus the sidebar's own focus wash, the last place not speaking the unified focus language.

title: feat(landing): add weekly changelog publishing flow
body:
## Summary

- Publish a concise weekly product changelog with individual permalinks and RSS.
- Cover every completed week from the repository's first commit: 32 continuous weekly windows.
- Use one editorial structure throughout: customer-focused major features, grouped improvements, grouped fixes, and learn-more links.
- Keep detailed version release notes accessible without mixing their different structure into the weekly feed.
- Rewrite historical feature headings in plain customer language instead of copying raw PR titles.
- Link every displayed PR number, including references preserved in detailed release write-ups.
- Reserve screenshots for substantial user-facing workflows, with at most one image per weekly entry and none under routine improvements or fixes.
- Exclude raw commit dumps, internal-only work, repeated items, and routine contributor roll calls.
- Keep contributor credit exceptional and explicit through the `changelog:credit` label.
- Automatically draft future weekly updates as reviewable pull requests; publishing still requires human review and merge.

## Human workflow

1. Read every merged PR collected for the week.
2. Remove internal, reverted, duplicated, superseded, or unavailable work.
3. Combine related PRs under one customer-facing feature.
4. Rewrite the headline, summary, and major features around what users can do.
5. Group smaller improvements and fixes by product area.
6. Add one real screenshot or demo only when a major workflow materially benefits from it.
7. Credit a contributor only for a genuinely exceptional contribution explicitly marked for credit.
8. Preview desktop and mobile layouts, verify links, wait for CI, and merge when ready.

## Validation

- `npm run changelog:test` — 8 passing
- `npm run changelog:validate` — passed
- `npm run changelog:ui-test` — passed against all 32 weekly feed entries
- `npm run build` — passed; 138 static pages generated
- Browser verification — 32 weekly articles rendered with no error overlay
- Detailed 0.11.0, 0.12.0, and 0.13.0 release pages remain directly accessible
- Continuous coverage verified from 2026-02-13 through 2026-09-20
- Validation prevents more than one image per week or media below the major-feature section
- No repeated PR badges within an entry
- No raw commit links in weekly entries
- No unlinked PR references in detailed release write-ups
- All required checks pass on the current head

## Review reminders

- Generated weekly changelog pull requests open as GitHub Draft PRs.
- `@somewherelostt`, `@illegalcall`, and `@AgentWrapper` are added as assignees and reviewers.
- One initial comment tags all three people with the editorial checklist.
- An hourly monitor posts a tagged reminder only after six elapsed hours, then every six hours while the PR remains open.
- Reminders stop automatically when the PR is merged or closed, and hidden markers prevent duplicate initial notifications or early reminders.

Validation: both workflows pass YAML parsing, actionlint, shell syntax checks, and current-head CI.

title: feat(cloud): gate sandbox providers on WorkOS org capabilities
body:
## Summary

Gate a sandbox provider (starting with `coder`) to specific organizations, using a per-org capability seeded from WorkOS organization metadata. Reuses AO's existing WorkOS org identity rather than a bespoke table, and is default-off so shipping it changes nothing until an operator opts in.

## How it works

- The WorkOS org resolver now also reads `metadata.capabilities` (a comma-separated list) and returns it; `auth.Verify` carries it on `Principal.OrgCapabilities`. This rides the existing cached (5-minute) org fetch, so there is no token/RBAC change and no extra per-request WorkOS call.
- A provider is gated only if it is listed in `AO_CLOUD_CAPABILITY_GATED_PROVIDERS` (comma-separated, default EMPTY). A gated provider then requires the active org to hold a capability of the same name. Empty set = every provider ungated = current behavior.
- `GET /me` filters the advertised providers by the org's entitlement, so the provider toggle is driven entirely by the server: a non-entitled org gets `coder` filtered out of `available`, and the frontend (which renders options from `available` and collapses the selector when only one remains) shows no coder toggle. No frontend change.
- `createSession` enforces the same check server-side (403 `provider_forbidden`) so the gate holds even against the raw API.

## Rollout (no lockout)

1. Merge + deploy: gate off, zero behavior change.
2. Flag entitled orgs in WorkOS: set org metadata `capabilities = coder` and add the members.
3. Set `AO_CLOUD_CAPABILITY_GATED_PROVIDERS=coder` on the control plane. `coder` is then offered and allowed only to entitled orgs; everyone else silently gets the default provider.

Extensible: `capabilities` is a list, so future providers or features gate the same way by adding a capability string.

## Tests

- `parseOrganizationCapabilities` (metadata parsing: trim / lowercase / dedupe / empty).

title: feat(telemetry): resolve GitHub handle via credential-helper, SSH, and noreply fallbacks
body:
## What

Broadens operator GitHub-handle resolution for product telemetry beyond an env token and `gh auth token`, so operators who never configured either are still counted. Builds on the merged base feature (#5521).

`githubActor` now resolves in two tiers, stopping at the first that yields a username:

**Authoritative** (API-verified via `GET /user`, also feeds the SCM observer):
1. env token (`AO_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`)
2. HTTPS credential helper (`git credential fill`) — new `CredentialHelperTokenSource`
4. `gh auth token`

**Best-effort** (local signals, telemetry-only, not API-verified):
3. SSH auth greeting (`ssh -T git@github.com` -> "Hi \<user>!")
5. git noreply commit email (`<id>+<handle>@users.noreply.github.com`)

## Why the best-effort tier is separated

`AuthenticatedIdentity` also drives the SCM observer's PR attribution (`resolveIdentities`), which must only trust API-verified, human logins. Feeding it unverified SSH/email handles would risk mis-attributing PRs. So the SSH/email probes live behind a new telemetry-only port, `ports.ScopedBestEffortIdentityResolver`, and `githubActor` consults them only after the authoritative tier returns nothing.

## Privacy

Only the resolved handle is sent (event property `github_actor` and the PostHog person property). The token and SSH key never leave the machine; only the derived username does. The whole thing is gated by the existing telemetry opt-out: turning telemetry off stops the carrying event entirely. `docs/telemetry.md` is updated to disclose the two-tier resolution honestly.

## Hot-path safety

`emitSpawned` runs synchronously on session spawn, so:
- SSH probe runs non-interactively (`BatchMode=yes`), mutates nothing (`UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null`), 4s timeout.
- Credential helper runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so a missing credential errors instead of prompting.
- Both best-effort probes and the credential read are memoized (including the empty result), so repeat spawns are not delayed.

All prior failure modes still degrade to anonymous.

## Change size

13 files changed, +726 / -16.

| Category | Files | Added | Deleted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Production Go | 8 | 389 | 8 |
| Tests | 4 | 311 | 0 |
| Docs | 1 | 26 | 8 |
| **Total** | **13** | **726** | **16** |

Production Go: `scm/github/auth.go` (+117), `scm/github/besteffort.go` (+163, new), `scm/github/provider.go` (+27/-1), `scm/multi/provider.go` (+24), `daemon/scm_wiring.go` (+6), `ports/scm_actions.go` (+6), `ports/scm_observations.go` (+11), `service/session/service.go` (+35/-7).
Tests: `scm/github/besteffort_test.go` (+171, new), `scm/github/provider_test.go` (+17), `scm/multi/provider_test.go` (+47), `service/session/github_actor_test.go` (+76).
Docs: `docs/telemetry.md` (+26/-8).

## Tests

- `CredentialHelperTokenSource`: password parse, caching, invalidation, host override, empty -> `ErrNoToken`
- `BestEffortLoginResolver`: SSH-then-email ordering, empty-result caching, regex parsing of the SSH greeting and noreply email
- multi provider: `BestEffortLoginForProvider` delegation, unsupported-provider -> `("", nil)`, unknown-provider error
- session service: `githubActor` tier precedence (authoritative wins, fallback on failure/non-human, anonymous when both empty or best-effort errors)

Verified: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, package tests, and `-race` on the GitHub/multi packages all pass on top of current `main`.

title: bug(usage): long-running session undercounted ~100x — inspector showed 3.6M tokens processed, transcript shows ~342M
body:
## Bug

SessionInspector → USAGE & COST massively undercounts a long-running session — by ~100x.

Observed on a real ~10-hour Claude-harness session (model `glm-5.3-flash` via the claude harness, ~2,190 assistant turns, transcript activity 17:00–02:59 UTC). The inspector showed:

| Metric | Inspector | Ground truth (transcript) |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens processed | 3.6M | **≈ 342M** |
| Fresh input | 207.2K | 0.76M |
| Cache reads | 3.4M | **341.4M** |
| Output | 32.2K | 0.19M |
| Estimated cost | $0.15 | (off by the same factor) |

Ground truth = summing `message.usage` over all assistant records in the session's Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/<worktree-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`): fresh input 757,393 + cache reads 340,699,328 + output 193,726 ≈ **341.65M** (plus 9.8M in the pre-resume transcript file). Hourly buckets of cache reads: 17:xx UTC alone is 3.16M — i.e. the inspector's 3.4M matches only the **first hour** of the session; ingestion stopped after that.

**Source:** live observation | **Reported by:** @axisrow | **Analyzed against:** `1c888193c` (origin/main, 2026-09-22; daemon self-built from that tree — the fork delta does not touch `internal/observe/usage`)
**Confidence:** Medium — mechanism localized to ingestion, exact break point not yet pinned.

## What the code says

- `backend/internal/observe/usage/parser.go`, `normalizeAnthropicUsage()` (~L765–780): `InputTokens = cache_read + (input + cache_creation)` — cache reads are included.
- `backend/internal/service/usage/summary.go`, `usageTotals()` (~L115–118): `ProcessedTokens = InputTokens + OutputTokens`.

So with full ingestion the UI would have shown ~342M. It shows 3.6M ⇒ this is not a formula error: the vast majority of usage events never reached the DB.

## Reproduction

1. Run a long-lived claude-harness session (hours, thousands of turns).
2. Let the daemon / usage collector restart at least once during the session (collector `restart-all` also triggers this).
3. Open SessionInspector → USAGE & COST: totals match only a small early slice of the session. Compare with a `jq` sum of `message.usage` over the transcript jsonl — off by orders of magnitude.

## Suspected root cause

The ingestor stops following the transcript early in the session's life. Candidates:

- watcher loses the file on transcript rotation (resume creates a new session-id file) and never re-scans;
- after a daemon restart the collector attaches by tailing new lines only, without replaying what it missed;
- related to the recent collector `restart-all` path (mutex contention fix era).

## Impact

- "Tokens processed" and estimated cost are wrong by orders of magnitude on long sessions — the sessions where spend matters most.
- The cost figure cannot be trusted for budgeting.

## Related

- [#5232](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5232) — same ingestion pipeline, different symptom (missing provider attribution → cost unavailable)
- [#4126](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4126) — earlier clarification of cache-token counting semantics

## Request

Add two derived metrics to the SessionInspector **USAGE & COST** panel:

1. **Turns** — number of assistant turns in the session. The usage pipeline already ingests one usage event per assistant message, so this is a `count(*)` over ingested events — no new collection needed.
2. **Throughput (tok/s)** — processed tokens per second of active session time, e.g. `ProcessedTokens / (last_usage_event_ts − first_usage_event_ts)`, shown alongside "Tokens processed".

Both are derivable from data the pipeline already stores; the panel already shows the components (fresh input, cache reads, output, hit rate, cost).

## Why

- Turns is the most intuitive "how much work happened here" counter; today it is not visible anywhere in the inspector.
- Throughput makes session comparisons meaningful (a 10h session and a 10min session with the same token count are not the same thing) and surfaces wedged sessions (throughput → 0).
- Concretely motivating case: a ~10h session processed ~342M tokens across ~2,190 turns — a turns/throughput row would have made the usage undercount from [#5745](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5745) (inspector showed 3.6M) obvious at a glance.

title: fix(usage): ingest resume continuation transcripts missing a hook
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5745 — the usage pipeline never followed resume continuations, so every resumed claude session silently lost all post-resume usage.

**Root cause (from the production incident):** `claude --resume` continues a conversation in a new native session file in the same project directory, with no back-reference to the old id. Discovery keyed only on the stored native id ([`discoverPath`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/backend/internal/service/usage/collector.go) globs `<ClaudeProjects>/*/<nativeID>.jsonl`), and the only intake for a new native id was a hook — which resume flows may never send (guard drops / daemon unreachable). fsnotify watches exact files, never directories, and the pipeline had no periodic backstop. In the incident session the pre-resume transcript was ingested fully and correctly (UI = DB = 3.6M), while the post-resume transcript (~342M across 2,249 assistant turns) had no binding and no source; schema-wide, no `claude_main` binding had ever followed more than one native id.

**Fix:**
- `ReconcileSources` now scans the current source's project directory for unregistered `*.jsonl` files, reads `sessionId`+`cwd` from a bounded window of leading records, and when `cwd` matches the session workspace (AO worktrees are per-session by design) registers the continuation binding + source through the same validated path hooks use. The write-once `(binding_id, source_event_key)` dedup keeps replay idempotent.
- A 3-minute safety-net tick fans into the coordinator refresh, healing both hookless resumes and silently lost fsnotify watches.
- The two silent hook guard drops (launch-id mismatch, session not live) now log a warning; behavior unchanged.

**Known limit:** bindings already in `complete` state are not reconciled, so a resume after finalization is still only recovered by a hook — noted for a future eligibility widening.

## Test

- New: `TestCollectorDiscoversClaudeContinuationInWorkspaceDir` (incident repro), `...IsIdempotent`, `...IgnoresCwdMismatch`, `...IgnoresPathBoundToAnotherSession`, `TestReadClaudeTranscriptMetaSkipsRecordsWithoutCwd`, and pipeline-level `TestPipelineIngestsDiscoveredClaudeContinuation` (aggregate = old + continuation, replay does not double count).
- `gofmt -l .` clean; `go test ./...` green for touched packages; `go test -race` and `golangci-lint run` clean on touched packages. Note: `internal/adapters/agent/crush` has a pre-existing local-env failure on clean `main`; `claudecode`/`goose` were flaky only under full-suite parallel load and pass in isolation.

## Live verification plan

On the incident machine, rebuilding the daemon from this branch and restarting it should: log `usage continuation source registered` for the orphaned transcript, register the missing binding/source (offset 0 → file size), and converge the session total to ~352M (from the previously shown 3.6M). Will be confirmed on the reporter's deployment; unit and pipeline-level repro are in the test suite.

title: dashboard: no_signal paints live sessions red forever — mass false alarms for never-prompted sessions
body:
## Bug / UX

`no_signal` paints live sessions in the attention ("Needs you", `#f06445`) tone **permanently**, and it triggers for sessions whose silence is the *expected* state — so a normal machine shows half the project rows in alarming red for days, and real "hooks are broken" cases drown in noise.

**Source:** live observation on a long-running install | **Reported by:** @axisrow | **Analyzed against:** `1c888193c` (origin/main, 2026-09-22)
**Confidence:** High — full code path traced plus production data.

## What happens on a real install

Project-row dots in the sidebar (production data, 2026-09-22):

| population | sessions | state |
|---|---|---|
| red since a bulk relaunch 9 days ago | `direct-cli-17`, `wordstat-1`, `tg_content_factory-86`, `wordstat-trends-11`, `yandex-direct-mcp-plugin-25`, `stocks_momento_bot-44` | live, `first_signal_at` empty, `updated_at` frozen at one bulk-relaunch instant (2026-09-13 16:14 UTC, identical to the second) |
| red from birth | a freshly created orchestrator never yet given a first prompt | live, idle, no hook signal expected until the user types |
| grey (for contrast) | `claude-devtools-1`, `tg-use-1`, `srouter-191` | same idle, but `first_signal_at` is set from an older session — "confident idle" |

The stuck sessions are genuinely live processes (relaunched claude TUIs idling in their tmux panes for 9 days), so this is not stale-data rendering — the status is recomputed on every read and the condition never un-satisfies itself for an unprompted relaunch.

The fresh-orchestrator case reproduces 100%: create a project, open the orchestrator, do nothing → red dot at T+90s.

## Root cause

`DeriveStatus` ([`backend/pkg/contract/status.go:102`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/backend/pkg/contract/status.go)) downgrades idle → `no_signal` when `SignalExpected && !HasSignal && now.Sub(LastActivityAt) > noSignalGrace` (90 s, `service/session/status.go:17`). Two problems:

1. **Silence before the first prompt is normal, not anomalous.** Orchestrators are promptless by design (`session_manager/manager.go:60-64`): spawn delivers no prompt, so no state-carrying hook can ever fire until the user types. The 90 s downgrade fires anyway, and there is **no TTL** — `silentPastGrace` has no upper bound, so the attention tone is sticky for days. The 9-day-old cluster came from one daemon-restart bulk relaunch (`reconcileLive → relaunch → MarkSpawned` stamps `LastActivityAt` and clears `FirstSignalAt`, `manager.go:1524`) after which nobody ever prompted those sessions.
2. **The discriminating fact already exists but is unused.** `Metadata.LatestUserPromptAt` is persisted (set on prompted spawns and advanced by prompt checkpoints, `manager.go:1142-1144`, `:764-767`) and already shipped over the API as `lastUserMessageAt` — but `contract.SessionFacts` doesn't receive it. "Never prompted" (normal) and "prompted but hook-silent" (the broken-pipeline case the orange was designed for, cf. #3410) are conflated into one alarming tone.

Frontend mapping: `attentionZone` includes `no_signal` in the action zone (`packages/product-ui/src/session-presentation.ts`), painted `--color-status-needs-you`; the sidebar dot routes it there via `getOrchestratorStatusDotView`/`getSessionStatusDotView`.

## Suggested fix

**Goal split.** `no_signal` should mean *"prompted after the current spawn/restore, live, and still hook-silent → the hook pipeline is probably broken"* (real alarm, keep the orange). *"Never prompted since the current spawn/restore"* is the expected state for a promptless orchestrator and should render as confident `idle` (grey), like every other not-yet-working session.

**Concrete change — one fact, no schema churn.** `MarkSpawned` already resets the per-spawn proof (`FirstSignalAt`, `manager.go:1524`). The spawn stamp is exactly what `Activity.LastActivityAt` holds for a silent session. So in `toContractSessionFacts` (`service/session/status.go`) derive:

```go
PromptedSinceSpawn: rec.Metadata.LatestUserPromptAt.After(rec.Activity.LastActivityAt)
```

add it to `contract.SessionFacts`, and change `DeriveStatus` condition 6 (`pkg/contract/status.go:128-130`) to downgrade only when `PromptedSinceSpawn` is true:

- never prompted since spawn → `idle` (grey) — nothing is broken, nothing to alarm about;
- prompted but hook-silent past the 90 s grace → `no_signal` (orange) — the original watchdog case (e.g. #3410) keeps firing.

Any valid activity signal still flips the session out of both states exactly as today (`manager.go:955-957`).

**Why not tone-only.** Dropping `no_signal` from the attention zone (frontend-only) would also silence the genuinely-broken-hook case; the backend split above keeps the alarm where it is real. An optional extra: cap the `no_signal` attention tone with a long TTL as defense in depth, but with the prompt gate it should be unnecessary in practice.

**Edge worth deciding.** A session prompted *before* a relaunch (my `direct-cli-17`/`wordstat-1` cases — prompted Sep 6/10, relaunched Sep 13; note their `lastUserMessageAt` is non-zero) will read grey-idle after this change until prompted again. A plain "`lastUserMessageAt` non-zero" gate is therefore **not** enough — the comparison has to be against the current spawn/restore stamp, otherwise restored sessions that were prompted once in an earlier lifetime stay red forever. That matches the "each spawn must re-prove its hook pipeline" contract already encoded in `MarkSpawned`, but it is a visible behavior change — flagging it deliberately.

## Reproduction

1. `ao` → create a project → open the orchestrator, don't type anything.
2. ~90 s later the project dot turns needs-you red, display status "No signal".
3. It stays red until you either type a prompt into that session or kill it — potentially forever.

## Related

- #3909 — board conflating technical recovery states with human "Needs you" (closed as outdated; this is the current-board incarnation)
- #2604 — transient no_signal right after daemon restart (same tone problem, earlier window)
- #3410 — a case where the no_signal alarm is genuinely correct (Windows: every hook dies)
- #3315 — receipt-only SessionStart signals

@khovan123 (sidebar dot lane alignment, #4026) @ashish921998 (no_signal watchdog, #170) — you both own halves of this (the tone mapping and the watchdog semantics); does the split above fit the original intent, or would you rather keep `no_signal` and only change its zone/tone? Happy to push a PR in whichever direction you prefer.

Keep a project-pinned Codex model visible in the new-task picker when the account-scoped app-server catalog does not list it, and allow an explicit effort to reach Codex for that off-catalog model.

## Why

Codex accepts direct model IDs beyond its account catalog. AO already supports direct Codex model entry, but the task picker omitted a project pin that was absent from the global catalog, and session provisioning rejected its effort before Codex could validate it.

## How

* Overlay the selected project's pinned Codex model in the task picker's display catalog without mutating or project-scoping the global durable catalog cache.
* Treat a missing Codex catalog entry as capabilities unknown during provisioning, preserve the requested effort, and let Codex perform the authoritative validation.
* Continue strict AO validation for provider-listed models with known effort capabilities.
* Continue failing closed for stale catalog capabilities when the selected model is provider-listed.
* Avoid reintroducing the superseded project-scoped discovery/fingerprint and generated session-effort contract changes from the pre-rebase patch.

title: fix(review): tighten reviewer prompt and surface prior verdicts
body:
Code changes: +87 -20  
Tests: +133 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

The reviewer task prompt (`backend/internal/review/prompt.go`) spent nearly all of its length on submission plumbing and repeated itself in places, while giving almost no guidance on how to review. This PR removes the objective redundancies and mistakes, then adds the guidance the existing plumbing already supports.

### Redundancies and mistakes removed

- The provider-failure rule ("leave the id empty") was stated in both step 1 and the closing paragraph. It is now stated once, in the bookkeeping step.
- The system prompt repeated the posting step ("Post your review as a comment... with inline comments") that the task prompt spells out with the exact command. The system prompt now carries only the review criteria and safety boundaries.
- The multi-PR autonomy paragraph ("do not stop after the first PR") was emitted for single-PR queues. It now only renders when the queue has more than one task, alongside the queue header that was already conditional.
- Step 2 restated its own ordering three ways ("After every PR has its own GitHub review from step 1, record... for those already-posted reviews"). Now: "Record AO's bookkeeping for every PR in the queue with one command."
- The prohibition list enumerated nine actions and then ended in "or otherwise modify the checkout". Trimmed to a short list plus the catch-all.
- Step 1 said "For each PR below" while the queue is listed above it.
- One bullet carried a stray tab from the Go raw string.

### Improvements added

- **PR context from the provider, not the worktree.** The reviewer now runs `gh pr view --json title,body,baseRefName,headRefOid,files` and `gh pr diff`, reviews the queued head commit, and uses the checkout only to read surrounding code. The checkout is the worker's live worktree and may hold uncommitted or newer work that is not part of the PR.
- **Verdict threshold.** `changes_requested` only when a finding would block a merge (correctness bug, security issue, behaviour-breaking missing error handling, changed behaviour with no test). Otherwise approve, even with non-blocking comments. The GitHub body verdict line must match the AO verdict.
- **Fixed review-body shape.** Verdict line first, then numbered findings with file, line, and blocking/non-blocking marker, then PR-description claims the reviewer could not verify (it cannot run tests).
- **Inline-comment constraint and fallback.** `line` must be on the new side of the diff; GitHub 422s otherwise. Findings on unchanged lines go in the body, and a rejected post is retried once without `comments` rather than dropping the review.
- **JSON escaping.** The prompt previously only mentioned shell-escaping single quotes. It now also calls for JSON-escaping newlines and double quotes in the review text.
- **Prior verdict on re-review.** `LaunchSpec.PreviousRuns` existed but was only populated on terminal restore. `Trigger` now passes this harness's runs, and the prompt surfaces the latest completed verdict on an earlier commit of each queued PR (body truncated to 1200 chars), asking the reviewer to say which findings the new commit addressed instead of repeating them.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/review/` — pass (4 new prompt tests, 1 new trigger test)
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/review/...` — 0 issues
- `npm run lint` (full backend `go test ./...`) — all packages pass except four `session_manager` tests (`TestSpawn_RejectsMissingAgentBinary` and siblings) that fail locally with "tmux required on macOS but ... was not found". These do not touch the review package and are an environment gap on this machine; verifying in CI.

## Risks and follow-ups

- The prompt text is behavioural, not functional: harnesses will follow it to varying degrees. Assertions cover the presence and placement of each instruction, not reviewer behaviour.
- Prior-verdict text is also injected when a live reviewer with native history is notified of a new commit. It is redundant there but bounded and harmless.
- Base branch and PR title are still fetched by the reviewer rather than embedded in the prompt, since `ReviewRun` does not carry them. Plumbing them through the store is a possible follow-up.

title: fix(ci): rename reserved GraphQL variable in review leaderboard
body:
Code changes: +4 -4  
Tests: +5 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Every run of the "Post trailing 7-day review stats" job has failed since #5750 merged, with:

```
Error: [@octokit/graphql] "query" cannot be used as variable name
```

`@octokit/graphql` reserves `query`, `method`, and `url` as option names, so passing `{ query, cursor }` as GraphQL variables throws before the request is sent. This renames the search variable to `searchQuery` in both the query document and the call site.

The test's fake `graphql` client now rejects those reserved names, so the workflow's "Test leaderboard calculation" step catches this class of mistake. Against main's script the new assertion fails with the same message; with the rename it passes.

The workflow runs on `pull_request_target` and checks out the default branch, so this fix only takes effect once merged. It cannot be verified by this PR's own leaderboard run. First observed on #5753.

## Tests

- `node --test .github/scripts/pr-review-leaderboard.test.mjs` — 4 pass
- Same command with main's script and the new assertion — 1 fail, confirming the guard reproduces the CI error

## Risks

- None beyond the rename. The fake client guard mirrors octokit's documented reserved names and does not affect production behaviour.

title: [Bug]: Settings shows raw electron-updater errors (stack, headers, HTML) on check failure
body:
### What went wrong?

## Summary

When "Check for updates" fails (e.g. GitHub returns a 504), Settings → Updates renders the full raw `electron-updater` error string instead of a short user-facing message. That includes HTML response bodies, HTTP headers (including `set-cookie`), and a JS stack with local `app.asar` paths.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Settings → Updates on an installed desktop build.
2. Click **Check for updates** while the GitHub releases feed is unreachable or returns an HTTP 5xx (e.g. gateway timeout on `/releases/latest`).
3. Observe the Updates status / error notice.

## Expected

A short, actionable message, e.g.:

> Couldn't check for updates — the update server timed out. Try again in a few minutes.

(or equivalent localized copy), with full detail logged in the main process only.

## Actual

The UI shows the full error dump, for example:
    
## Why this happens

- Main process `errorMessage()` in `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts` passes through `err.message` unchanged.
- Only some cases are rewritten today (manifest 404 → friendly string; Chromium `net::` failures → `netError` + localized guidance; some macOS staging failures → `shortStagingMessage()`).
- HTTP 5xx / "Unable to find latest version on GitHub" / "Cannot parse releases feed" fall through and are broadcast as `UpdateStatus.message`.
- The renderer (`UpdatesSection`) displays `status.message` (and IPC catch `error.message` / `checkError`) directly.

## Proposed fix

- Map known updater/GitHub feed / HTTP errors to short user-facing messages in the main process (same pattern as manifest 404).
- Keep the full error in `console.error` / telemetry only.
- Optionally harden the renderer with a length / content guard so a raw dump can never fill Settings even if a new error shape escapes.

## Environment

- Desktop app (packaged), Windows NSIS updater path observed.
- Version shown in UI: v0.13.0 Stable.

title: fix(updates): hide raw updater errors in Settings
body:
Three code paths bypassed errorMessage() and passed raw Error.message directly to the renderer, allowing HTML bodies, HTTP headers, and stack traces to reach Settings -> Updates.

## Changes

**Main process error rewriting (auto-updater.ts)**
- Added UpdateErrorPhase to distinguish check/download/install operations
- Rewrote errorMessage() to accept an explicit phase parameter
- Applied errorMessage() with correct phase to all error paths
- Reordered regex checks in userFacingUpdateError(): 5xx/Gateway first, then generic HttpError, then phrase matches
- Moved looksLikeTechnicalUpdateDump() to shared update-telemetry.ts

**Renderer last-resort guard (UpdatesSection.tsx)**
- Added guardUpdateText() using the shared looksLikeTechnicalUpdateDump() to sanitize all status text
- Applied guard to both status.message and status.checkError before render
- Changed IPC rejection fallback to use check-specific shell.updateCheckFailed

**Shared helper (update-telemetry.ts)**

title: bug(chat): Claude ACP turn remains Working after final response without terminal event
body:
## Human report

In the **Review Prompt Audit** Claude Code chat session, AO showed **Working for 30m** even though the agent was no longer doing useful work. The session status and chat indicator were confusing and did not reflect whether work was actually progressing. The expected behavior is for the turn and session to leave Working when the provider response finishes or the provider stream becomes unusable.

Observed on macOS in the packaged AO desktop app on 2026-09-22.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected read-only from the affected daemon and `~/.ao/data/ao.db` on 2026-09-22. The running checkout used for code comparison was `28c68a08a39266760e58168c6f060114ea4bbf0a`; the packaged daemon reports version `dev`.

- Session `agent-orchestrator-54` was non-terminated and reported `activity_state=active`, with its last session activity timestamp stuck at `2026-09-22T06:39:14.75926Z`.
- Durable turn `45616119-7043-4b0e-b06a-ebf5661dff8d` / provider turn `d043ae35-571b-477f-b8f0-f03cfbc1ec04` started at `06:39:14Z` and remained `running` with no completion timestamp.
- Claude continued producing command and message events through `07:00:59Z`. The final persisted assistant message reads like a completed answer, but remains `streaming=1`.
- After that final answer, there is no matching `message.completed`, `turn.completed`, or `controller.state=ready` provider event.
- The Claude, ACP runtime, and AO chat-host processes remained alive, but no additional useful activity arrived.
- The frontend derives the inline Working timer from a durable `running` conversation turn, so the missing terminal boundary keeps it visible indefinitely.

This confirms the immediate failure mode: AO has no terminal provider event and no recovery path settles the abandoned durable turn while the persistent provider processes remain alive. It does **not** yet prove whether the terminal event was omitted by Claude Agent ACP, lost during reconnect/relay handling, or received but not projected.

## Related issues

- #3749 had the same durable/in-memory stale Working symptom after a projection rollback, but a different observed trigger.
- #3878 covered a Codex nested-turn orphan, also with a different provider and trigger.
- #4016 previously fixed another stuck chat Working path.

This appears to be a regression/new Claude ACP variant rather than an exact duplicate.

title: bug(inspector): merged PR failure keeps CI Failed timeline badge
body:
## Human report

In the **Review Prompt Audit** session, the Activity timeline showed **CI Failed** beside Working even though the session's current open PR had passing CI. The expected behavior is for the sidebar/inspector to reflect actionable CI on current open PRs, not a historical failure from a PR that has already merged.

Observed on macOS in the packaged AO desktop app on 2026-09-22.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected read-only from the affected daemon, GitHub, and `~/.ao/data/ao.db` on 2026-09-22. Code was inspected at `28c68a08a39266760e58168c6f060114ea4bbf0a`.

- Open PR #5753 has eleven completed checks, all successful. AO's daemon reports its CI state as `passing`.
- PR #5754 is already merged. Its historical `Post trailing 7-day review stats` check failed before merge, and AO retains `ci_state=failing` for that merged PR.
- The daemon's SCM derivation correctly filters to open PRs through `openPRs()`.
- The inspector timeline's `scmTimelineStates()` independently iterates every `session.prs` entry and adds `ci_failed` whenever `pr.ci === "failing"`, without excluding `merged` or `closed` PRs.
- Therefore the visible red badge is sourced from merged PR #5754, not from current open PR #5753.

The screenshot supplied with the report is retained locally at `.ao/attachments/attachment-95f136075164d0dcec5afe827730589e.png`; it was not uploaded because the CLI issue API does not provide a safe local attachment upload path.

No exact duplicate was found in open or closed issue/PR searches.

title: fix(updater): pick up nightly/hotfix builds within 15 min and surface API-discovered builds when the CDN check stalls
body:
## Problem

Two separate gaps kept published nightly/hotfix builds from reaching users:

1. The automatic re-check interval had been raised to 24h, so a session left open picked up a newly published nightly or hotfix build up to a day late. This is the regression reported in https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5510.
2. On the nightly/feature channel the automatic check runs in two hops. First it hits api.github.com to list releases, verify the channel manifest asset exists, and point the feed at the matching release. That host answers reliably. Then electron-updater fetches the manifest yml, which 302-redirects to release-assets.githubusercontent.com, a separate CDN host. For users whose network reaches the GitHub API but not that CDN (HTTPS-inspecting AV or VPN, ISP/DNS blocking of githubusercontent, a dead anycast route, or MTU packet drops), that second hop stalls. The socket-inactivity timeout is 60s, and retryOnServerError only retries 5xx and EPIPE, never a hang, so the check takes one shot and gives up. These users never see an "update available" notification even though the API discovery already told us a newer build exists.

## Fix

Two independent changes:

**Re-check interval back to 15 minutes.** The periodic re-check was lowered from 24h to 15 min. A fresh check still runs on every launch, so this only governs sessions left open for a long stretch: a newly published nightly or hotfix is now picked up within minutes instead of after a day.

**Surface the API-discovered build when the CDN hop stalls.** During direct-prerelease feed setup we already fetch the release list from the API and know the newest completed prerelease tag and its notes. This records that discovery when the tag is strictly newer than the running version, and, in the automatic check's finally block, surfaces it as "available" if the electron-updater manifest fetch did not already settle to a more advanced state (available, downloading, preparing, downloaded). The user still gets a truthful "update available" notification when the CDN hop hangs.

No second checker, no new polling, and no new push channel. The CDN change reuses the result the existing check already produced. Both stay on the automatic path only, so the manual "check now" and remembered-update paths are untouched.

## Tests

Adds a test that stubs the API to return one nightly release with the platform manifest asset, forces autoUpdater.checkForUpdates to reject as if the manifest fetch timed out, and asserts the last status broadcast is "available" with the discovered version. Disabling the new call makes the test fail. The interval change updates the tests that pinned the 24h cadence to 15 min. Full auto-updater suite passes (189).

## Line changes

| Category | Added | Removed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Code | 56 | 11 |
| Tests | 91 | 24 |
| Other | 0 | 0 |
| Total | 147 | 35 |

title: bug(lifecycle): PR-wide review nudge budget duplicates old comments and suppresses new feedback
body:
## Bug

AO keys review-comment delivery deduplication and its attempt budget to the whole PR rather than to an individual comment/thread or feedback signature. Multiple unresolved comments therefore compete for one remembered signature and one three-send budget.

This produces two failure modes:

1. Different comment signatures overwrite one another, so a previously delivered comment can look new on a later poll and be injected again.
2. Once the shared attempt counter reaches `reviewMaxNudge`, a genuinely new comment on the same PR is silently suppressed.

**Source:** maintainer report while dogfooding PR #5742
**Analyzed against:** `bfaa1aa61f142b306beca4149d790f82915d7284`
**AO version:** `dev`
**Confidence:** High; confirmed from GitHub state, AO's persisted PR/comment rows, and the lifecycle delivery state.

## Concrete incident

PR: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742

AO successfully observed and persisted the new unresolved human comment:

- Comment: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742#discussion_r4069029633
- Comment ID: `PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7yiHcB`
- Thread ID: `PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6kn0Nt`
- GitHub review state: `COMMENTED`
- AO policy snapshot: `auto_inject_review = true`

But the comment was not delivered to the worker. The persisted reaction state for the PR was:

```json
{
  "seen": {
    "comment:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742": "PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6kndp6 + PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7yhl_I"
  },
  "attempts": {
    "comment:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742": 3
  }
}
```

The new comment has a different signature, but `sendOnce` checks the already exhausted attempt count for the shared `comment:<PR URL>` key and returns without sending it.

## Root cause

`ApplyPRObservation` creates one pending nudge per unresolved comment, but every one uses the same key:

```go
key: "comment:" + o.URL
```

Each comment's signature is independently derived from its thread/comment IDs. `sendOnce` stores only one `seen[key]` value and one `attempts[key]` counter.

With comments A and B, delivery can behave like:

```text
send A -> seen[key] = A
send B -> seen[key] = B
next poll sees A -> A differs from B, so A is sent again
```

The three-attempt budget eventually stops this ping-pong, but it also prevents later comment C from being delivered.

Relevant code:

- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`, review-comment nudge construction
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`, `sendOnce`

## Expected behavior

- Each newly observed actionable comment/thread is delivered once.
- An unchanged comment is not repeatedly injected on later polls.
- A new comment remains eligible even if older comments on the PR exhausted their own retry or safety budget.
- Resolution stops further delivery for that comment.
- Deduplication remains durable across daemon restarts.
- A broader rate limit may protect against comment storms, but it must not permanently discard later feedback.

## Acceptance criteria

- Scope the delivery identity and attempt accounting to the actionable feedback rather than only the PR URL.
- Add a regression test with two simultaneously unresolved comments proving they do not alternate/replay.
- Add a regression test where comment A exhausts its budget, then newly observed comment B is still delivered.
- Preserve identical-comment deduplication across repeated polls and daemon restarts.
- Make a budget-exhaustion suppression observable enough to diagnose without querying SQLite directly.

## Related

- #5574 — self-authored review-thread replies are nudge-eligible; adjacent selection/delivery bug, not a duplicate.
- #1943 — old pre-rewrite review dispatch observability report; similar symptom, different implementation and cause.

title: bug(UX): review feedback is mislabeled as Changes Requested and disappears while agents work
body:
## Bug

AO conflates two independent dimensions — agent activity and SCM/review state — into one primary session status. It also maps any unresolved review comment to `changes_requested`, even when GitHub has no formal changes-requested review.

This produces misleading and unstable UI:

```text
Idle · Changes Requested
        ↓ agent starts working
Working
        ↓ agent becomes idle, comment still unresolved
Idle · Changes Requested
```

The review feedback never disappeared. Its tag vanishes solely because active agent state has higher precedence than SCM state.

**Source:** maintainer report and screenshot while dogfooding PR #5742
**Analyzed against:** `bfaa1aa61f142b306beca4149d790f82915d7284`
**AO version:** `dev`
**Confidence:** High; confirmed from GitHub, AO's stored state/event history, backend status derivation, and frontend timeline logic.

## Concrete incident

PR: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742

GitHub reported:

```text
reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED
```

AO stored:

```text
review_decision: review_required
reviewComments: true
```

AO's SCM event history never recorded `changes_requested` for this PR. The outstanding thread came from a `COMMENTED` review and was explicitly described by its author as an optional, non-blocking nit:

https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742#discussion_r4069029633

Despite that, the inspector showed `Idle · Changes Requested`. When the agent became active, it showed only `Working`.

## Root causes

### 1. Unresolved comments are treated as a formal changes-requested decision

`backend/pkg/contract/status.go` derives the PR pipeline status using:

```go
case pr.Review == ReviewChangesRequest || pr.ReviewComments:
    return StatusChangesRequested
```

This collapses these distinct facts:

- GitHub formally reports `CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
- A PR merely has one or more unresolved inline comments from a `COMMENTED` review.

### 2. Active agent state replaces SCM state

Session status derivation returns `working` immediately for an active agent, before evaluating SCM status. This is reasonable for a primary activity label, but it becomes lossy because the UI relies on that same primary status to recover the unresolved-comment signal.

### 3. The frontend cannot independently reconstruct review feedback

`scmTimelineStates()` adds the tag only when:

```text
session.status == changes_requested
or
pr.review == changes_requested
```

When the agent is active:

- `session.status` becomes `working`.
- `pr.review` correctly remains `review_required`.
- The unresolved-comment fact is therefore no longer represented by either condition.

Relevant code:

- `backend/pkg/contract/status.go`, `DeriveStatus` and `prPipelineStatus`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`, `scmTimelineStates`

## Expected behavior

Activity and SCM feedback should remain independently visible because both can be true simultaneously:

```text
Idle · Review feedback
Working · Review feedback
```

Reserve `Changes Requested` for a formal provider `CHANGES_REQUESTED` decision. An unresolved comment from a `COMMENTED` review should use distinct language such as `Review feedback` or `Comments to address`.

The feedback indicator should remain visible until the underlying feedback is resolved, regardless of whether the agent is currently working, idle, or waiting.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Changes Requested` is displayed only for a formal changes-requested review decision.
- Unresolved actionable review comments have a distinct presentation.
- Activity state and SCM/review feedback can be rendered concurrently.
- Starting work does not hide an unresolved-feedback indicator.
- Resolving all applicable comments removes the feedback indicator.
- Add backend coverage for `review_required + reviewComments = true` without deriving the formal `changes_requested` meaning.
- Add frontend coverage for an active/working session that still has unresolved review feedback.
- Keep multi-PR and stacked-PR aggregation behavior explicit and covered.

## Impact

- Optional, non-blocking feedback appears as a formal blocking review.
- The same PR condition appears and disappears as agent activity changes.
- Users cannot reliably tell whether feedback was resolved or merely hidden because the agent started working.

title: feat(desktop): desktop app optimisation pass v1
body:
Code changes: +1011 -218  
Tests: +569 -145  
Others: +0 -0

## Opening the app

You quit from a session. Next time you open the app, the old screen shows a loader until the daemon is up and the project list comes back.

Now you see that session's title and the composer immediately. You can type. Send stays off until the daemon says the session is real, and what you typed is still there. If you quit from the board instead of a session, you still get the loader.

## Starting a task

You hit Send on a new task. The old app waits for a git fetch to finish before the agent can talk.

Now the folder is ready first, the agent starts, and the fetch runs after that. The agent can talk while git is still fetching.

## Saving a long answer

The agent writes a long answer as many small saves. The old app wrote the database once per save. A 96-save answer was 96 writes, and any other open session waited behind them.

Now those saves are written together, about every 32 of them, or every 8 KB, or every 40 ms. That same 96-save answer is 3 writes. If the app crashes in that short gap, the agent can replay the unsaved tail.

The finished answer takes the same space on disk. The saving is how many times SQLite is written while the answer is still coming in.

## Disk cleanup

This pull request does not clean the disk. Nothing new labels ~/.ao, and nothing new deletes cache, prompts, or worktrees. That work was left out.

## A long chat that is already open

A page is one fetch of up to 200 rows, messages and tool rows together. Opening a long chat already loaded only the newest 200. Scroll up and the older 200s load. That part did not change.

What changed is a chat where you have already scrolled, so several of those chunks are open. You send a message and the reply streams in. Before, each save fetched every chunk you had open. Four chunks open, and one sentence that lands as one refresh, meant all four chunks came back. Now only the newest chunk is fetched again. The ones above it stay as they are.

If a save skips a row, or changes a row up in an older chunk, every loaded chunk is fetched again, once.

## Several sessions in one sitting

You open ten sessions. The old window kept a full chat copy for each of them.

Now it keeps the one you are looking at and the one you just left. Go back to an older one and that chat loads again. The agent is still running. That drop is not the session ending. Terminals keep their text.

## How a burst shows up

A sentence can arrive as one lump. The old playback typed for a moment, then gave up after 200 ms and dumped the rest, so it looked smooth and then jumped.

Now the lump stays buffered and comes out one word every 10 ms. A word with no space after it waits until the space arrives, or until the reply ends. Text that was already on screen when you opened the session is not played back from the start. [REFERENCED VERCEL'S SMOOTH STREAM FOR THIS]

## Summary

Accounts Manager adds an AO-owned account inventory, encrypted credential lifecycle, explicit session bindings, and coordinated account controls around the embedded CLIProxyAPI `v7.3.8` runner.

Draft checkpoint. Exact descendant retirement/deletion recovery, pending-switch restart, model compatibility, native-platform acceptance and current-main integration remain open. The user chooses accounts; the service must never silently choose a replacement or fall back.

Device-global credentials and the existing Subscriptions and native account-switching surfaces remain unchanged. Routing is disabled by default.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[Settings and session controls] --> API[AO loopback API]
    CLI[Thin HTTP CLI] --> API
    API --> Service[Account control service]
    Service --> DB[(Bindings and operation journals)]
    Service --> Runner[Embedded accounts runner]
    Runner --> Vault[Encrypted credential store]
    Runner --> Engine[CLIProxyAPI engine]
    Launch[Session launch] --> Service
    Service --> Child[Explicitly bound child runtime]
    Child --> Runner
    Runner --> Selector[Exact account selector]
    Selector --> Engine
```

## What is included

### Embedded runner and lifecycle

- Vendors the MIT-licensed engine with a bounded SDK callback listener/address extension documented in `accounts-manager/UPSTREAM.md`.
- Bundles the runner and supervises it from the daemon with authenticated reattachment, lease expiry, bounded restart backoff, and safe status reporting.
- Keeps management, lifecycle, data-plane and routing credentials separate. Listeners and callback transport remain loopback-only.

### Account lifecycle

- Browser and device login, API-key and credential import, verification, refresh/reconnect, enable/disable, models, and safe inventory projections.
- Encrypted durable storage with admission checks and refresh shutdown joining. Invalid credential verification does not become successful account authorization.
- Durable removal journals, impact/confirmation, stop/revoke acknowledgements, retry/cancel boundaries, tombstones and recovery. Exact retirement of escaped descendants is still a blocking defect.
- Only public-safe account/operation IDs and redacted errors cross the public boundary. Credentials, raw provider responses and private endpoints remain private.

### Accounts UI

- Dedicated Accounts settings alongside the existing Subscriptions page, inline login/import, verification, account details and provider-reported usage.
- Per-session selection, pending versus committed state, policy/revision/operation/request IDs, and switch retry/cancel controls.
- Removal impact preview with exact revision and confirmation. Unavailable service or usage remains explicit; no optimistic completion or invented quota.

### Routing and strict session pinning

- Explicit managed-account or native selection, with durable per-session/provider bindings.
- Reuses the selected binding for launch, restore and switch. No automatic fallback or silent repinning.
- Journals switch progress, preserves pending queues, fences runtime ownership and authorization revisions, and supports restart recovery.
- Selected-account failures remain actionable failures. Unrelated sessions must continue unchanged.

### Provider launch integration

- Child-scoped Responses API routing for the supported terminal integration and gateway environment routing for the supported CLI/ACP integration.
- Conflicting credentials are removed only from the routed child's environment.
- The app-server Chat integration remains on its native device account. Device-global auth/config files are not rewritten.
- Setup-token classification, usage eligibility, native Harness status integration, and the supported subscription-authentication design remain incomplete.

## Security and failure behavior

- Runner binds only to `127.0.0.1`; account control routes remain unavailable through Connect Mobile.
- Route capabilities are opaque, authenticated-encrypted, session/account scoped, and backed by a private persistent key.
- Credentials and route tokens stay out of public DTOs, logs, argv and persisted runtime metadata. Public errors preserve request IDs without provider bodies.
- Runner failure degrades account controls without failing daemon readiness. Native routing-off behavior remains available.
- Release HOLD: strict retirement refusal prevents unsafe completion, but five positive recovery cases across three groups still fail. Linux containment primitives remain unwired. This checkpoint must not be treated as complete teardown safety.

## Storage and API

- Routing migration `0165` plus `0166` through `0172` add bindings, switch/removal journals, ownership, history decisions and queue obligations after reconciling the branch with main. The obsolete duplicate `0148` from the original remote series was not reintroduced.
- SQLite stores public-safe account IDs and durable operation facts, not raw credentials.
- Public account/session controls delegate through service/port boundaries; the CLI remains a thin HTTP client.
- sqlc, OpenAPI and frontend API types are regenerated and checked for drift.

## Validation performed

- Backend and runner build/vet/pinned full lint pass on the preserved source snapshot.
- Complete backend ordinary suite: 10,882 passing, 10 failing, 75 skipped cases. Complete race suite: 10,887 passing, five failing, 75 skipped cases. Five retirement failures remain reproducible; intermittent descriptor-publication failures are documented separately.
- Complete runner ordinary and race: 297 passing cases each, no failures/skips.
- Complete engine ordinary: 10,043 passing cases, eight skips. Complete engine race: 10,038 passing, one media-relay failure reproduced on unchanged control source, 11 skips.
- Complete frontend on Node 22 and Node 24: 5,626 passing cases, six existing skips; both typechecks pass.
- API/SQL generation has no drift. All 91 protected paths, 33 generated entries and five guest-design/evidence entries retain their hashes.
- Linux package builds and the no-network installation smoke pass with the documented isolated packaging tools. Native installation/update and Windows/Mac certification are not claimed.
- Fresh pinned offline scans of the current changed source and all 71 PR-selected commits found no credential leaks under the repository rules.
- Real-account tests establish the bounded outcomes above, not permanent deletion, full runner/vault cold recovery or provider-side billing attribution for every request.

See [the current checkpoint](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/d6ff87eebd9d0e78d438ddcf00e79cb399435c4f/docs/plans/accounts-manager-completion/PUBLISH-2026-09-29.md) for full commands, retained failures, scope and native/live-provider gaps. Historical slice clearances apply only to their sealed snapshots.

## Desktop evidence (earlier checkpoint)

Real Electron app, isolated data, real provider catalog. Personal labels are masked at capture; application state and responses are not mocked. The second account's unavailable usage remains visible.

![Account inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/04e12ca3dc78ba96674a63c2039ac6b0b271b52f/docs/plans/accounts-manager-completion/evidence/accounts-overview.png)

## Intentionally deferred and remaining gates

- Correct production switch execution and escaped-descendant retirement, complete the remaining cancellation/recovery schedules, and re-review the integrated snapshot.
- Complete managed/default model compatibility, session email/status presentation and explicit setup-token migration/reconnect. Initial explicit session choice is implemented; it does not close the remaining isolation and identity-display gaps.
- Implement and prove the macOS containment boundary on native arm64/x64; run the Windows ownership/recovery matrix on native Windows.
- Extend the observed real A/B replies, switching and cancellation to permanent in-use removal, cold recovery, provider revocation, unrelated native coexistence and measured desktop responsiveness. Correct the pending-switch daemon-restart failure.
- Complete current-main integration, obtain fully passing integrated suites, independent review and native desktop/platform acceptance. The current source passes pinned full lint, but this does not close the remaining test failures.

Automatic fallback, routing non-AO shells, and removing Subscriptions are outside the requested design. The app-server Chat route remains native.

title: fix(frontend): make dev:web work on Windows
body:
## What

- replace the POSIX-only environment prefix in `dev:web` with a small Node launcher
- set `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1` in the child process while preserving Vite's normal `development` mode
- forward Vite arguments and resolve the frontend paths independently of the caller's working directory
- add focused launcher and process-start regression tests

Fixes #2589.

## Why

npm runs scripts through `cmd.exe` on Windows, where `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite ...` is treated as an executable name. The command therefore exits before Vite starts, blocking both the renderer-only development loop and Playwright's renderer web server.

The launcher uses Node's process environment API, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux without adding a dependency or changing the lockfile. Unlike a custom Vite mode, it preserves the existing `import.meta.env.MODE === "development"` behavior and does not introduce `.env.web` loading.

## Packaged Windows app

The packaged `.exe` is unaffected by this bug: `dev:web` is a source-development npm script and is not referenced by the Electron development, packaging, or runtime paths. `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` is set only inside the new launcher, so packaged renderers continue to leave the preview flag undefined and use the real daemon.

## Testing

Windows 11, Node 24.12.0, npm 10.9.1:

- `npx vitest run scripts/dev-web.test.mjs` — 2 passed
- `npm run typecheck` — passed
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` — passed
- `npm.cmd run dev:web -- --port 5199 --host 127.0.0.1 --strictPort` — Vite started successfully and forwarded the arguments
- fetched the served preview module — confirmed `MODE: "development"` and `VITE_NO_ELECTRON: "1"`
- packaged-path audit — no Electron development, packaging, or runtime path invokes `dev:web` or the launcher

The previous revision's remote frontend test, renderer-smoke, mac-update-helper, and secret-scan jobs all passed. The updated revision reruns them.
