title: feat(settings): UI to configure Anthropic-compatible gateway providers (base URL, token, model)
body:
## Problem

AO already supports Anthropic-compatible gateway providers (any `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`-fronted endpoint — e.g. z.ai/GLM, MiniMax): the backend resolves base URL + token + model from env vars and Claude settings files, validates the credential, surfaces the provider's own model list in the picker, and prices it via the catalog. #2614 tracked this and was closed as completed.

But configuration is files/env only. A user who opens Settings finds no screen for it — the UI only displays the *result* (auth badge, model picker entries). Discoverability is zero: unless you already know which files AO reads, gateway setup looks unsupported.

## Request

A Settings screen to add and manage gateway providers:

- fields: base URL, auth token (masked), default model
- two scopes: app-wide and per-project override (mirroring the existing resolution precedence)
- writes through the same resolution chain AO already reads, so the UI and a hand-edited settings file never disagree
- on save, run the existing credential probe so the screen can say "works / rejected" immediately

## Context

- Follow-up to #2614 (closed completed; covered the resolution/validation plumbing, not the UI).
- Backend already has everything needed: provider detection, credential validation, provider-scoped model discovery. This is purely a frontend + settings-persistence feature.

title: feat(agents): apply provider-profile switch to running sessions (exit-agent + resume-agent)
body:
Follow-up to #6095 (provider profiles + settings). That issue covers configuration and new sessions; this one covers applying a provider switch to **already-running** sessions.

## User story

I switch the default provider (or a role assignment) in Settings — and my running sessions keep chatting on the old provider until I restart them by hand. I want AO to offer applying the switch to running sessions, preserving their context.

## Design

The machinery already exists — this is orchestration + UX:

- `ExitAgent` (session manager) stops only the agent controller; the session, its worktree, and the native conversation survive.
- `ResumeAgentWithMode` re-launches through the full env re-assembly path, so once #6095's profile injection lands, every resume picks up the new provider for free. TUI resumes via `claude --resume <native-id>`; chat sessions via the chat resume path preserving the provider conversation id.
- New: `POST /api/v1/provider-profiles/apply` with `{sessionIds?: []}` — empty = all running claude-code sessions whose stamped profile differs from the newly effective one; per-session result `{state: applied|failed|skipped, error}`; bounded concurrency.
- UI: after saving assignments, if stale running sessions exist, a dialog offers "apply now" with a per-session result toast. (Requires the session metadata provider stamp from #6095 to detect staleness.)

## Stated risk

Cross-provider `--resume` is best-effort: the local transcript exists, but model ids from provider A may not resolve on provider B. If the resume is rejected, the session must stay exited-and-restorable (`/restore`) with the error surfaced — never a lost session. The existing force-fresh relaunch policy is the documented fallback for unreliable provider pairs.

## Acceptance criteria

- running TUI worker on z.ai → switch default to Anthropic → apply → pane relaunches without `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, prior transcript visible (resume worked);
- a chat session continues the same conversation after apply;
- a failing resume leaves the session restorable and reports the error without affecting other sessions in the batch;
- gofmt / `go test -race` / vitest clean.

title: feat(settings): per-role effort selector never renders for gateway providers (no advertised capabilities)
feat(modelcatalog): gateway-served models arrive with no effort levels — enrich catalogs so effort pickers light up
body:
Follow-up to #3188 (per-role effort UI, shipped) and the entry point for the effort work — #6097 (UI fallback when efforts are unknown) comes after this one.

## Problem

First-party Anthropic model discovery returns `capabilities.effort`, and AO's gateway parser already reads that field **when the gateway returns it** — but Anthropic-compatible gateways (z.ai/GLM and most others) omit the field from their `/v1/models` response entirely. So every gateway-served model arrives in the catalog with `efforts: []`, and every effort control gated on advertised efforts (per-role pickers in project settings, the per-turn chat picker) never renders — even though the models do support reasoning levels and the backend plumbs `--effort` end-to-end into the agent launch.

In other words: the capability exists in the product; the data just never arrives, so the UI stays dark for gateway users.

## Request (implementation starts here)

1. **Probe and record**: hit a live gateway's `/v1/models` (z.ai) and document whether any capabilities come back — decides whether this is purely a data-absence problem or also a parsing gap.
2. **Seed known effort levels** for common gateway model families (`glm-*`, `deepseek-*`, `qwen-*`) in the static/fallback catalog layer — same place `claudeFallbackModels` lives (`modelcatalog/catalog.go`). Provider-discovered lists should merge seeds for models the provider did not annotate.
3. **Persist user-set effort overrides** per model id in the existing `agent_model_catalog` cache, so off-seed and custom models stay tunable; overrides should survive catalog refreshes.
4. #6097's UI fallback remains as defense-in-depth for models where nothing is known.

## Acceptance criteria

- a gateway-backed project (e.g. z.ai) shows the effort selector with correct levels for glm models **without** the #6097 fallback being needed;
- a user-set effort override on an unseeded model survives a catalog refresh;
- first-party Anthropic discovery is unchanged (advertised efforts still win);
- the discovery fingerprint accounts for seeds/overrides so stale cached catalogs refresh;
- Go tests for seeding merge and override persistence.

title: bug(tmux): "no such session" (tmux >=3.5) not recognized as session-absent — auto review always fails; errors should carry the tmux version
body:
## Observed failure

Auto review fails on every launch with:

```
Auto review Failed: launch reviewer: reviewer replace stale pane: tmux runtime: set detach-on-destroy review-ccstatusline-28: exit status 1: no such session: =review-ccstatusline-28
```

Context: Review Controls → Auto review for worker session `ccstatusline-28`, claude-code reviewer, macOS, **tmux 3.6b**.

## Root cause

Before every reviewer launch, AO idempotently destroys any stale reviewer pane (`review/launcher.go:540`) — a missing pane is the normal first-launch case and must succeed silently.

The failure happens inside `Destroy`: the pre-kill `detach-on-destroy` re-assertion (`tmux/tmux.go:537`, `set-option -t =id: detach-on-destroy on`) fails when the session does not exist, and the "already gone" detector does **not** recognize the error text modern tmux emits:

- `confirmedAbsentOutput` (`tmux/tmux.go:1360`) gates on `sessionMissingOutput` (`tmux/tmux.go:1317`), which matches only `can't find session` and `session not found`.
- tmux ≥ ~3.5 changed the message to **`no such session: <target>`**. Verified on tmux 3.6b:

```
$ tmux -L probe -f /dev/null new-session -d -s s
$ tmux -L probe set-option -t "=missing:" detach-on-destroy on
no such session: =missing:      # exit 1
```

So on modern tmux the idempotent path is broken: "session absent" reads as a hard failure, the wrapper turns it into `reviewer replace stale pane`, and the whole auto review fails.

`sessionMissingOutput` / `confirmedAbsentOutput` are the single absence-vocabulary for the tmux runtime — all of these silently degrade on modern tmux, not just the reviewer path:

- `Destroy`'s kill-session result handling (`tmux/tmux.go:558`),
- the legacy-socket migration probe in `socketForSession` (`tmux/tmux.go:1056`),
- `enforceDetachOnDestroy` legacy adoption (`tmux/tmux.go:1377`).

## Fix

1. Add `no such session` to `sessionMissingOutput` (case-insensitive `Contains`; the `=` exact-match target prefix needs no special handling).
2. Regression tests with a fake runner: the exact string `exit status 1: no such session: =review-x:` makes `Destroy` a no-op success; transient texts (`error connecting`, `protocol version mismatch`, …) must still **not** be treated as absent — the fail-closed behavior from #4223 must be preserved.
3. **Error diagnostics — carry the tmux version.** This failure shipped as an opaque string with no hint which tmux produced it. When building these command errors, include the tmux version (resolve `tmux -V` once per process/socket and cache it; do not shell out on the hot path), e.g.:

```
tmux runtime: set detach-on-destroy review-x (tmux 3.6b): exit status 1: no such session: =review-x:
```

so the next message-vocabulary drift across tmux versions is diagnosable from the error alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- on tmux ≥ 3.5, re-launching a reviewer with a dead/stale pane succeeds and auto review starts;
- transient tmux failures still fail closed (no session/worktree deletion on an unconfirmed state);
- the tmux version appears in tmux runtime command errors;
- `gofmt` clean, `go test -race ./...` green (unit tests cover all three absence texts + transient negatives).

title: [Feature]: Add Hermes Agent to the current supported-agent registry
body:
## Problem

I want to run a heterogeneous local agent team in Agent Orchestrator, using Hermes Agent alongside Pi, Goose, and Codex.

AO currently lists Pi and Goose among its 32 supported coding agents, but Hermes is not in the current supported-agent registry. This leaves Hermes sessions outside AO's project-level task, worktree, lifecycle, and review workflow.

There was earlier Hermes work in #1406, and #1405 records a prior process-runtime lifecycle problem. Issue #1406 was closed because Hermes support did not appear relevant or needed at that point, with an invitation to open a new issue if the need remained. The current use case is specifically a mixed-agent local team, not only controlling AO from Hermes through Discord or Telegram.

Is first-class Hermes Agent support still planned or something the maintainers would accept?

## Proposed direction

If this fits AO's roadmap, add Hermes as a first-class worker adapter with a deliberately small initial scope:

- detect an installed `hermes` CLI;
- launch the native interactive Hermes TUI inside an AO worker and bind it to that worker's repository/worktree;
- map process lifecycle into AO status so the worker does not appear completed while Hermes is still active;
- support stop/restart and conversation resume where Hermes exposes a stable session interface;
- document local setup for the platforms AO and Hermes both support.

Hermes messaging gateways, cross-platform conversation routing, memory synchronization, and Hermes-to-AO remote control could remain separate follow-ups. The initial goal would only be reliable worker execution inside AO.

## Alternatives considered

Running Hermes manually in another terminal or terminal-session manager works for process organization, but it loses AO's shared project context, task ownership, worktree isolation, pull-request/CI state, and orchestrator supervision.

## References

- Previous Hermes plugin request: #1406
- Previous Hermes worker lifecycle report: #1405
- Hermes Agent: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent
- Current AO supported-agent list: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#supported-agents

## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: [Feature]: Expose the bundled using-ao skill to external controller agents such as Hermes
body:
## Problem

I want to use Hermes as a personal/messaging control plane above Agent Orchestrator: Hermes receives a request from its CLI, Discord, or Telegram surface, then uses the `ao` CLI to create and supervise AO workers such as Codex, Pi, or Goose.

This appears to fit the current product boundaries better than registering Hermes as another coding-agent worker (#1406 and #6100):

- AO already ships a version-matched `using-ao` skill that documents `ao spawn`, `ao session`, `ao send`, `ao report`, and the other machine-readable CLI flows.
- However, AO currently materializes that skill under its own data directory and points AO-launched sessions at the absolute path from their system prompt.
- An independently running personal agent therefore has no documented, stable install/sync path for the same skill. Copying it out of AO's internal data directory is undiscoverable and couples the integration to an implementation detail.
- Hermes already supports standard `SKILL.md` skills, external skill directories, and direct GitHub/URL skill installation, so the missing piece is distribution/discovery rather than a new Hermes runtime adapter.

Could AO expose the bundled `using-ao` skill as a supported integration surface for external controller agents, with Hermes as the first documented example?

## Proposed direction

Any one of these would solve the core problem; the exact mechanism is up to maintainers:

1. Publish `using-ao` at a stable repository path that external agents can install directly; or
2. Add an AO command such as `ao skill path` / `ao skill export <dir>`; or
3. Document the stable materialized path and an external-skill-directory configuration, if that path is intended to be public API.

A small Hermes integration guide could then show:

- how to make `using-ao` discoverable from a Hermes profile;
- that `ao` must be on `PATH` and the AO daemon must be reachable;
- how Hermes should prefer `--json` for reads and preserve AO's normal confirmation/permission boundaries for mutations;
- one end-to-end example: user asks Hermes to start a coding task, Hermes calls `ao spawn`, observes the session, and reports status back through the originating messaging channel;
- how the installed skill stays in sync when AO is upgraded.

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- From a fresh Hermes profile, one documented command or configuration makes AO's current `using-ao` skill available.
- The skill version follows the installed AO version or has an explicit update mechanism.
- The documented smoke test covers spawn, status/session lookup, send, and stop/kill behavior.
- Windows, macOS, and Linux path handling is documented or tested where AO supports those platforms.

## Non-goals

- Do not register Hermes as a coding-worker runtime.
- Do not embed the Hermes TUI inside an AO worker.
- Do not synchronize Hermes memory with AO session state.
- Do not make AO responsible for Hermes messaging gateways or cron jobs.
- Do not add nested delegation: Hermes controls AO; AO remains the owner of project tasks, worktrees, worker lifecycle, PRs, CI, and review.

## Alternatives considered

- **Hermes as an AO worker:** this creates overlapping orchestration, lifecycle, session-identity, permission, and memory semantics; #1405 also records the earlier process-runtime lifecycle failure.
- **Hand-copy the skill from AO's data directory:** workable locally, but not discoverable, portable, or safely updateable.
- **Teach Hermes the CLI ad hoc in every prompt:** duplicates the versioned catalog AO already maintains and will drift as commands change.
- **Build a separate protocol/plugin immediately:** unnecessary for the MVP because the existing CLI and its JSON output already provide a narrow control surface.

## References

- Built-in `using-ao` skill: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/tree/main/backend/internal/skillassets/using-ao
- Skill installation/materialization code: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/backend/internal/skillassets/skillassets.go
- Completed internal AO skill request: #1473

title: ao report exits 0 with no output — no queued/placed confirmation and no pending-batch indicator; agents treat silence as loss
body:
confirmation and no pending-batch indicator; agents treat silence as
loss

Environment: Agent Orchestrator desktop 0.13.1 on macOS; CLI reports
"ao version dev". Same behavior on current main: report() in
backend/internal/cli/report.go posts the report to the daemon, decodes
a response that contains the report id (reportAPIResponse{ID}), then
discards it and prints nothing.

What happens:

- `ao report <text>` exits 0 with zero output: no "queued", no id, no
  delivery hint.
- Delivery to the orchestrator is batched at the orchestrator's next
  turn boundary; the receiving side sees them as
  <ao-report-delivery id="report-batch:...">. Until that boundary
  there is no observable sign the report is pending.
- Real failure mode (observed 2026-10-01, multi-agent setup): two
  reviewer agents, seeing no confirmation for five submitted reports,
  re-sent their verdicts via `ao send`; when the batch then arrived
  whole, the channel held duplicates and extra turns were spent
  deciding whether verdicts had been lost.

Related but distinct: #3634 documents the same turn-boundary delay
for `ao send` — but ao send's output at least confirms acceptance
immediately. `ao report` has no confirmation at all, and unlike a
chat message a report gets no reply that would ever confirm receipt.

Request: on `ao report`, print the queued report id and state (e.g.
"report <id> queued; delivered at the orchestrator's next turn"),
and/or expose the pending-batch state via `ao status` /
`ao session get`, so agents can distinguish "queued" from "lost".

title: Worker isn't notified of merge conflicts on its PR, while the sidebar shows "Merge Conflicts"
body:
## Report

Reported by @AgentWrapper:

The right sidebar showed "Merge Conflicts" for PR #6061, but the worker session that owns it (`agent-orchestrator-87`) wasn't notified by the lifecycle manager. I expected the worker to get the merge-conflict notice so it could rebase.

## Agent-collected evidence

*Collected 2026-10-01 ~08:43 UTC. Installed app 0.13.3-nightly.202610010256; daemon `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao` (PID 66139, port 3001, data dir `~/.ao/data`).*

**Timeline for PR #6061:**
- 09-30: the PR became conflicting and the worker **did** get the nudge ("There are merge conflicts on PR #6061 … Rebase onto the base branch and resolve them.").
- The worker rebased it. GitHub then reported `mergeable=MERGEABLE` with `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`, because a required review is pending.
- 10-01: three new commits on `main` made the PR conflicting again. No nudge was delivered.

**Persisted state.** Read-only query, taken after the worker resolved the second conflict:
`sqlite3 -readonly ~/.ao/data/ao.db "select mergeability, provider_mergeable, last_nudge_signature from pr where url like '%/pull/6061'"`
```
blocked | MERGEABLE | {"seen":{"merge-conflict:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6061":"conflicting"},"attempts":{"merge-conflict:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6061":1}}
```
The `conflicting` dedup entry from 09-30 is still there, even though GitHub has said `MERGEABLE` since the first rebase.

**Same pattern elsewhere:** `select count(*) from pr where mergeability='blocked' and provider_mergeable='MERGEABLE' and last_nudge_signature like '%merge-conflict:%conflicting%'` returns **2** on this install.

**Hypothesis from reading the code (not confirmed by a reproduction):**
- The re-arm added for #4528 only fires on `mergeable` or `unstable` (`mergeabilityClearsConflict`, `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:436-438`) and deliberately skips `blocked`.
- The observer turns GitHub's `BLOCKED` into AO's `blocked` even when GitHub's own `mergeable` is `MERGEABLE` (`mergeabilityFromProviderFacts`, `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go:1938-1941`).
- So a PR that's clean but waiting on a required review never re-arms, and its next conflict matches the old signature and is dropped as a duplicate. That looks like #4528's symptom persisting for PRs awaiting review.

**Related:**
- #4528 (closed): same symptom; its fix doesn't cover the `BLOCKED` case.
- #5833 (open): a different nudge-delivery problem. There, nudges are queued and never drained; here, nothing was queued.

title: bug(review): manual review trigger failure hides the persisted error — UI shows only "Review operation failed"
body:
## Observed failure

Triggering a review from Review Controls fails fast with only a generic toast: **"Review operation failed"**. No reason is shown anywhere in the UI for manually triggered reviews, and the daemon logs nothing useful (stdout goes to the Electron pipes).

## What the data shows

The reason is **already persisted** — `review_run.body` carries the full error text (written by the engine's `failRuns` helper in `internal/review/review.go` via `UpdateReviewRunResult`), e.g.:

```
launch reviewer: reviewer replace stale pane: tmux runtime: set detach-on-destroy review-<worker>: exit status 1: no such session: =review-<worker>:
```

(that specific root cause is #6099). So the failure loop was: error lands in `review_run.body` → trigger returns the same error → `writeReviewError` (`internal/httpd/controllers/reviews.go`) collapses it into the `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED` default with the message `"Review operation failed"` and `details: nil` → the renderer toast has nothing to show.

The renderer only surfaces a failed run's `body` for **auto** reviews (`SessionInspector.tsx` filters on `triggerSource === "auto" && autoReviewEnabled`); a failed **manual** trigger shows no persisted reason anywhere.

## Fixes

1. **Backend (small, no API break):** in `writeReviewError`'s default branch, pass the underlying error through the envelope `details`, e.g. `{"detail": err.Error()}`, instead of `nil`. The text is already persisted in `review_run.body`, so repeating it leaks nothing new, and the toast becomes diagnosable without a DB query.
2. **Renderer:** surface the failed run's `body` for manual triggers too (same affordance the auto-failure notice already uses), or render `error.details.detail` from the trigger mutation in the Review Controls error area.

Optional hygiene: `review_run` has no dedicated error column — the reason rides in `body`, which doubles as the review text. A dedicated `error` column (or at least a documented convention) would make "failed run → reason" queryable instead of convention-dependent.

title: bug(linux): systemd-oomd kills AO during startup reconciliation
body: ## Summary On Linux, the AO desktop/daemon was terminated during startup/recovery activity after systemd-oomd selected the AO app scope under sustained user-session memory pressure. Before the first kill, AO logged an ACP Chat-session resume failure (initialize timed out with JSON-RPC -32603 Internal error). A later oomd event killed the scope again at a higher measured scope memory use. The evidence confirms oomd as the proximate termination mechanism; it does not identify one process or session as the sole pressure source. This is Linux evidence consistent with, but distinct from, the macOS eager Chat restore resource-spike report in [#4608](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4608). **Confidence:** - **High** — `systemd-oomd` killed the AO application scope after sustained user-session memory pressure. - **Medium** — AO startup/recovery restoration was a significant contributor to the memory pressure. - **Low** — Any claim that a specific AO child process or session was the initiating cause of the pressure. ## Environment - **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS - **AO version:** 0.13.1 - **Incident:** 2026-09-27 (local time) - **Corroborating checkout:** `0c60f21360f1718c75394649e8e3634c0b690e65` (2026-08-11); not confirmed as the incident revision. ## Evidence timeline - **22:36:52** — During startup reconciliation, AO logged a live-pass failure while resuming Chat session `repo-ana-6`: ACP `initialize` returned `context deadline exceeded`, with JSON-RPC `-32603 Internal error`. - **22:37:21** — `systemd-oomd` selected the AO app scope at **1.4 GiB**. User-session memory pressure was **63.09%** against a **50%** limit for more than 20 seconds, with reclaim activity. systemd recorded **34 processes killed** and scope result `oom-kill`. - **22:45:31** — AO logged reconciliation errors for two sessions because `git config extensions.worktreeConfig` could not lock `.git/config` while a lock file existed. This is evidence of recovery/reconciliation activity, but does not establish the cause of the oomd event. - **About 22:45:45** — Attached screenshot shows load average **5.57**, high CPU and I/O wait, about **188 MiB free**, **1.1 GiB available**, and **283 MiB** swap in use. - **22:46:17** — `systemd-oomd` selected the AO app scope again, now at **2.1 GiB**. User-session pressure was **71.94%** against the **50%** limit for more than 20 seconds, with reclaim activity; **37 processes were killed** and the scope again failed with `oom-kill`. Several OpenCode scopes were each around **140–206 MiB**; Chromium was another oomd candidate at about **313 MiB**. The available evidence does not identify which process or workload initiated the memory pressure. ## RCA **Confirmed:** systemd-oomd selected and killed the AO app scope after user-session memory pressure remained above its configured 50% threshold for more than 20 seconds while reclaim was active. The evidence points to memory pressure, **not disk exhaustion**. **Likely AO-side contributor:** eager boot-time reconciliation/restoration of non-terminated Chat sessions may have contributed additional process and memory load. On the inspected checkout, `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` has `Reconcile` run `reconcileLive` for non-terminated records and then call `RestoreAll`; Chat controllers are daemon child processes and cannot be adopted after daemon restart, so eligible saved sessions are restored. The ACP timeout precedes the first oomd kill, but chronology alone does not prove it increased memory use or caused the kill. The inspected revision is only code-path corroboration, not proof of the incident binary's implementation. ## Impact The AO app scope was killed during startup and again during recovery, interrupting the desktop/daemon and its processes. With several concurrently restored Chat sessions and other workloads, startup recovery may contend for memory and CPU/I/O and trigger oomd termination. The evidence does not establish data loss or that every AO process was killed in either event. ## Investigation findings The following observations were reproduced during investigation: - The most noticeable resource pressure and lag were observed during app launch/relaunch and session restoration when Chat/OpenCode sessions were present. - Restart/relaunch/reinstall scenarios using only TUI sessions did not reproduce the same lag. - After adding Chat/OpenCode sessions, subsequent launch/relaunch tests showed increased memory usage, swap activity, and noticeable lag. - A startup/recovery scenario involving restored Chat/OpenCode sessions produced severe system lag that required a forced shutdown. - During a later reproduction, OpenCode processes were observed consuming substantial memory while swap usage increased. - These observations are consistent with Chat/OpenCode restoration contributing to resource pressure, but do not establish that Chat restoration was the sole cause of the original freeze. ## Related issue - [#4608](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4608) — macOS report of eager startup Chat restoration causing a resource spike and desktop lag. This report adds Linux oomd evidence; the two incidents have similar suspected contributors but different platforms and confirmed outcomes.

title: [Feature]: feat(settings): make Shortcuts search match IDs, default keys, key aliases, and multi-word queries
body:
### Problem

Description:
Current behavior
The Shortcuts search bar (settings panel KeyboardShortcutsContent.tsx:155-164, duplicated in KeyboardShortcutsSettingsDialog.tsx:169-178) does a single substring match over exactly three fields:
1. the localized shortcut label (e.g. "Toggle sidebar")
2. the localized category (General / Navigation / Session)
3. the current binding label (e.g. "Ctrl+B" or "⌘B")
Anything outside those three strings finds nothing, which leads to several "why can't I find it?" cases:
Problems
- IDs aren't searchable. Typing toggle-sidebar or focus-terminal returns no results, even though those are the shortcuts' stable identifiers — and the only locale-independent way to name them.
- Factory-default keys disappear after remapping. Once a user rebinds "New session", its default Ctrl+Shift+N no longer matches any query, so users can't find a shortcut by the keys they remember from the docs/cheat sheet.
- Key queries must match the exact rendered string. ctrl b (space) fails against Ctrl+B. On macOS the label renders as ⌘B, so typing cmd, command, or option never matches.
- Multi-word queries require the exact phrase. tab next finds nothing because the filter looks for one contiguous substring; it should match all tokens (AND) regardless of order.
- No synonym/locale-independent words. There's no way to search by alternate terms ("palette", "sidebar", "devtools"), and in a non-English UI, English words like "terminal" won't match translated labels at all.
- No status filters. The list shows a "Modified" badge, but typing modified doesn't filter to changed shortcuts; same for unassigned / fixed (non-customizable) rows.
- The read-only cheat-sheet dialog has no search at all (KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx), despite listing the same 15 shortcuts.
Proposed
Extend the filter to match, case-insensitively:
- shortcut id (AppShortcutId from frontend/src/shared/shortcuts.ts)
- default bindings in addition to effective bindings (defaultShortcutBindings)
- tokenized binding matching with modifier aliases: split Ctrl+Shift+N into tokens; accept ctrl/control, cmd/command/⌘, opt/option/⌥, win/super; allow ctrl b and cmd b style input
- whitespace-split AND matching for the whole query (every token must match somewhere in the row)
- optional keywords?: string[] field on ShortcutDefinition for synonyms + English terms usable in any UI language (requires adding entries across the 8 locale files)
- status tokens: modified, unassigned, fixed
- a search input in KeyboardShortcutsDialog using the same matcher
Notes
- The filter logic is copy-pasted in two components today — extract one shared helper so the two search bars can't drift apart.
- No API/daemon changes; pure renderer filter logic.
- Nice-to-have follow-up: unit-test the matcher in the style of frontend/src/shared/shortcuts.test.ts.

### Proposed direction

_No response_

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: [Feature]: support durable ao report delivery to Qwen TUI with post-admission acceptance
body:
## Problem

Durable worker reports cannot currently be delivered to a Qwen Code orchestrator running in TUI mode.

The worker side succeeds: `ao report --done --note ...` is persisted durably. Delivery then reaches `SessionManager.SendSemantic`, which refuses Qwen TUI with:

```
session: semantic message acceptance unsupported
```

This is correct fail-closed behavior today: Qwen TUI does not currently expose a post-admission signal that satisfies AO's semantic-delivery contract.

### Environment / target baseline

- AO observed: v0.13.1 / `460d9c45f7bf5503808254e0cb02ee52bf537349`
- AO current main also lacks Qwen TUI semantic acceptance
- Qwen Code target baseline investigated: **v0.24.7**
- Linux
- Qwen TUI orchestrator

## What AO's semantic-delivery contract requires

AO's current contract is intentionally stronger than “text was written to the terminal.”

`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` documents `SendSemantic` as:

> returns only after the target agent has accepted that exact message

and explicitly says:

> a successful pane write alone never satisfies this method

For TUI adapters, `ports.SemanticMessageAcceptanceSignaler` is reserved for adapters that can correlate a specific AO-authored message with **provider acceptance**.

This distinction is deliberate. Current main has a regression test for OpenCode v2 that requires:

```
OpenCode 2 must not advertise semantic acceptance without a post-admission signal
```

So Qwen should not simply opt into `EmitsSemanticMessageAcceptance()` unless it can provide equivalent post-admission evidence.

## Qwen Code 0.24.7 findings

### 1. `UserPromptSubmit` is pre-admission, not an acceptance acknowledgement

Qwen 0.24.7 fires `UserPromptSubmit` before the user content is committed to the chat/history send path.

In `packages/core/src/core/client.ts`, Qwen runs the hook first. A blocking hook returns before the history push; the code explicitly notes:

```
A blocked send never reaches the history push
```

Only later does the request reach `turn.run(...)` / `chat.sendMessageStream(...)`.

Therefore Qwen's `UserPromptSubmit` cannot by itself satisfy AO's post-admission semantic-acceptance contract.

### 2. `submitted_prompt` is useful provenance, but not acceptance

Qwen 0.24.7 documents `submitted_prompt` in:

`docs/design/submitted-prompt-provenance.md`

It is the original supported submission before Qwen expansion and is useful for identifying the exact AO envelope.

However Qwen explicitly says provenance-sensitive consumers must treat a missing `submitted_prompt` as unavailable and **must not fall back to `prompt`**.

So AO may use `submitted_prompt` to identify the exact report envelope, but the presence of that field still does not prove admission.

### 3. Qwen's structured `--json-file` user event is also too early

Qwen 0.24.7 Dual Output emits a structured `type:"user"` event before calling `llmClient.sendMessageStream(...)`.

That event is useful for observation, but it also represents submission intent rather than post-admission acceptance.

The current stream-json / dual-output envelope also does not expose Qwen's `prompt_id` as a stable correlation field on assistant stream events, so AO cannot safely pair an early user event with a later provider event by exact turn identity.

### 4. Qwen already computes the correct acceptance boundary internally

Qwen 0.24.7 already maintains:

```ts
let modelRequestAccepted = false;
```

and sets it only after receiving the first substantive model event:

```ts
const acceptsModelInput =
  event.type === LlmEventType.Content ||
  event.type === LlmEventType.Thought ||
  event.type === LlmEventType.ToolCallRequest ||
  event.type === LlmEventType.Finished ||
  event.type === LlmEventType.Citation;

if (acceptsModelInput && !modelRequestAccepted) {
  modelRequestAccepted = true;
}
```

Qwen also uses the same area to settle queued/steer input because by then:

```
the user-content push has landed by now
```

This is the semantic boundary AO needs.

## Correct path forward

The safest design is to expose Qwen's existing post-admission boundary as a small observational signal, then wire AO to it using its existing report-delivery machinery.

### Qwen side

Add a non-blocking/post-admission event for a fresh `UserQuery`, for example `UserPromptAccepted` (exact naming is up to Qwen maintainers).

It should fire exactly once when Qwen first flips `modelRequestAccepted` for that user turn and include at least:

- `session_id`
- `prompt_id`
- `submitted_prompt` when the original supported TUI submission provenance is available

Preferably it should reuse Qwen's existing hook transport and be observational/fire-and-forget, not a blocking decision hook.

The critical guarantee should be:

> this event is emitted only after the user content has landed and Qwen has observed provider/model acceptance for this turn.

Do **not** move the existing `UserPromptSubmit` event later; its current pre-send/blocking semantics are useful and changing them would be a compatibility break.

### AO side

Once such a Qwen post-admission event exists:

1. Install the new Qwen hook alongside AO's existing Qwen hooks.
2. Parse **`submitted_prompt` only** for AO report-delivery envelopes; do not fall back to `prompt` when provenance is absent.
3. Extract the existing `domain.ReportDeliveryID(...)`.
4. Persist the normal coordination checkpoint only from this post-admission event.
5. Make the Qwen adapter implement `ports.SemanticMessageAcceptanceSignaler` and return true.
6. Leave `SessionManager.SendSemantic` and report acknowledgement semantics unchanged.

That gives Qwen the same effective contract AO expects from other supported TUI adapters:

```
AO SendSemantic
  -> write <ao-report-delivery id="..."> into Qwen TUI
  -> Qwen UserPromptSubmit (pre-admission; NOT acknowledgement)
  -> Qwen history/model request is actually admitted
  -> Qwen post-admission acceptance event
  -> AO extracts exact delivery id
  -> coordination checkpoint
  -> SendSemantic succeeds
  -> report batch acknowledged
```

## Why not synthesize acceptance from existing later hooks?

Qwen 0.24.7 later hooks such as `MessageDisplay`, `PreToolUse`, and `Stop` carry `prompt_id` and could theoretically participate in a two-phase correlation scheme.

That is less robust than exposing Qwen's existing acceptance boundary directly:

- `MessageDisplay` only covers displayed assistant text.
- `PreToolUse` only covers tool-producing turns.
- `Stop` can arrive far later than AO's semantic-delivery timeout.
- Qwen treats `Thought` as valid model acceptance, and long reasoning can precede both visible text and tool use.
- Implementing durable pending correlation in AO would add substantially more lifecycle state solely to reconstruct a fact Qwen already knows exactly.

A dedicated post-admission Qwen signal is therefore both simpler and closer to AO's existing fail-closed contract.

## Tests

### Qwen

- `UserPromptSubmit` fires before admission as today.
- New acceptance event does not fire when `UserPromptSubmit` blocks.
- New acceptance event fires once after the user-content push/provider acceptance.
- It fires for first accepted `Thought`, text, tool-call, finished, or citation paths.
- It carries the same `prompt_id` for the turn.
- `submitted_prompt` is preserved when supported provenance exists and omitted otherwise.
- Retries/fallbacks do not create ambiguous duplicate acceptance for the same logical submission.

### AO

- Qwen does not advertise semantic acceptance without the post-admission hook capability.
- Matching Qwen acceptance event + report delivery id acknowledges `SendSemantic`.
- Pre-admission `UserPromptSubmit` alone never acknowledges.
- Missing `submitted_prompt` fails closed.
- Wrong delivery id / wrong launch / stale native session does not acknowledge.
- Duplicate acceptance is idempotent.
- Existing report retry semantics remain unchanged.

## Scope

This issue is specifically about enabling Qwen **TUI** to meet AO's existing semantic-delivery contract. It should not weaken `SendSemantic` to treat a terminal write or pre-admission hook as success.

Qwen ACP/Chat already has a native accepted-turn boundary and is a separate path.

Related: #6119 tracks report-scheduler starvation when an undeliverable report remains permanently at the head of the pending queue.

title: fix(cloud): stop desktop sign-in tab freezing on the provider page
body:
## Problem
After a successful desktop AO Cloud sign-in, the browser tab stays on Google's dimmed account chooser with a progress bar forever. WorkOS redirects straight to `ao-app://callback`; the browser hands that URL to the OS without committing a page, so the tab keeps showing the last thing it drew.

## Fix
- **Control plane:** new unauthenticated `GET /api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback`. It renders a plain "Finishing sign-in" page (same styling and security headers as the GitHub callback pages), forwards only `code`/`state`/`error`/`error_description` to the fixed `ao-app://callback` target via meta refresh, and adds an "Open Agent Orchestrator" button as a fallback. Nothing is exchanged or stored. The code is useless without the PKCE verifier held by the desktop app. An incomplete callback gets a 400 page and is not forwarded.
- **Desktop:** packaged builds use `${AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL || https://api.aoagents.dev}/api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback` as the WorkOS redirect URI. The loopback callback server now only starts for `http://127.0.0.1|localhost` redirects (it previously matched any http(s) URL). Dev builds are unchanged.
- Docs updated (`cloud/docs/deployment.md`, `cloud/README.md`).

## Rollout (order matters)
1. Deploy the control plane to staging and production.
2. Register `https://staging-api.aoagents.dev/api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback` and `https://api.aoagents.dev/api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback` in WorkOS. Staging and prod share one WorkOS environment.
3. Only then ship a desktop release. Keep `ao-app://callback` registered so older desktop builds can still sign in.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/httpapi -run DesktopAuth`: param allowlist (no open redirect), HTML escaping of provider errors, error forwarding, 400 on incomplete callbacks, no-store/no-referrer headers.
- `vitest src/main/cloud-auth.test.ts`: 15/15, with the redirect URI assertion updated.
- Not yet verified in a real browser end to end. That happens on staging before the desktop release.

## Risks
- Some browsers may hold the meta-refresh protocol hand-off behind a click. The button covers that case, and staging verification will show how Chrome and Safari behave.

## Summary

Stream the desktop-owned browser into AO Mobile's Preview screen by default. When browser sharing is disabled or unsupported by the desktop and a selected app preview exists, open Mobile view automatically unless the user has explicitly chosen a view. A top-right **Mobile view** toggle opens the session's selected app preview at the phone's viewport size, with a persistent phone icon and a blue enabled state.

Desktop browser sharing requires a separate explicit opt-in in Connect Mobile. An authenticated mobile WebSocket connects through the daemon to Electron's private browser-stream link; Electron alone owns Chromium, capture, and remote input. The loopback listener and mobile authentication boundaries are preserved.

## Behavior

- Keep JPEG frames latest-value under backpressure and preserve ordered state/control events separately. A stalled control subscriber closes rather than silently losing state transitions.
- Coalesce `BROWSER_REMOTE_READ_ONLY` input rejections to one per stream per 500 ms so dragging while an agent drives the browser cannot flood the control queue during a frame write. Fatal errors and state updates remain unthrottled; stream lifecycle changes clear the limiter. Regression coverage includes a 120-command burst, independent streams, fatal errors, and restart/reconnect handling.
- Stream only the session's explicitly selected preview without first opening its desktop Browser panel. Do not discover unrelated repository HTML when the selection is empty; resolve selected workspace/artifact files against their own root and the current daemon address. Seed only the initial unused tab, preserving user-created blank tabs and explicit clears across mobile reconnects.
- Keep hidden streamed views outside the desktop window, with native bounds verification. Use bounded screenshot fallback only for hidden/minimized surfaces; suppress identical JPEGs and back off unchanged captures up to five seconds. Visible static pages do not initiate fallback captures.
- Preserve frame aspect ratio and translate mobile taps/swipes into normalized browser input, including wheel direction independent of desktop focus.
- Load App preview from the authoritative session selection rather than a repository's unrelated `index.html`. Serve selected workspace files and artifacts through their distinct confined authenticated routes on the paired endpoint; preserve relative assets and guard host changes.
- Identify disabled browser sharing through an authenticated HTTP check after a native WebSocket handshake failure (which hides the response body). Both `BROWSER_REMOTE_DISABLED` and a 404 from an older desktop without the stream route trigger Mobile view fallback; other failures retain the browser error. Unsupported desktops show “Update the desktop app to view its browser from your phone” when the user chooses Browser or has no selected app preview. HTTP checks do not reserve a browser lease or start capture. Preserve explicit view choices and ignore stale checks after closing or changing sessions.
- Keep explicit preview mode and the disabled-sharing fallback scoped to the stable host/session identity, so switching between LAN and tunnel endpoints preserves the selected view. While fetching a new endpoint URL, retain Mobile view with a loading indicator; the previous endpoint URL is never rendered with new credentials.
- Keep browser URL/navigation chrome in its dedicated workstream (#6070).

## Main integration

Merged current `main` (`4d175a54`) in `de2a72bb1`. Resolved the Connect Mobile settings conflict by preserving main's shared Stay Awake hook alongside the browser-sharing mutation, including its pending, error, and reset handling. GitHub reports the PR as mergeable.

The supplied Prasad read-only-error, selection-only browser-seeding, and disabled-sharing preview UX review threads are addressed and resolved. The latest general-review note about config identity resetting the chosen preview mode is also addressed.

- Mobile typecheck and full suite: 220 files / 2,234 tests passed, including disabled-sharing fallback, delayed preview selection, explicit view choices, and late handshake-check handling, and view preservation across endpoint switches, and OTA compatibility with older desktops (404 fallback, update copy, other HTTP failures, and late-probe guards).

title: CI: build-test flaky 20m timeout in internal/storage/sqlite migration tests (blocks unrelated PRs)
body:
## Summary

The Go CI pipeline (`build-test` job) intermittently fails with a 20-minute package timeout in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite`, where an individual migration test appears hung until the package-wide `panic: test timed out after 20m0s` kills the run. Observed three consecutive Go runs in a row — including a run triggered by the default branch itself with no related changes — so it blocks unrelated PRs.

## Evidence

Three runs with the same signature (different hung test each time, same package):

| Run | Trigger | Test running at panic |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PR branch | `TestMigrateRepairsRenumberedUsageCostHistory/all_usage_migrations_applied_at_0109_through_0112` |
| 2 | PR branch | `TestOpenPreMigratedSucceedsForMigratedDatabase` |
| 3 | **default branch** (after an unrelated merge) | `TestOpenPreMigratedSucceedsForMigratedDatabase` |

- The hung test differs each time — this does not look like a deterministic bug in one migration test; the whole test binary appears to wedge (e.g. a leaked lock/connection from an earlier migration test starving the next one, or a load-dependent deadlock).
- The same tests pass locally (`go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/` completes normally on macOS).
- A second, separate flake appeared in the same runs: `internal/service/shellterm` `TestCueCommandDoesNotSendWhenCanceledDuringReadiness` failed once and passes on rerun.
- None of the affected PRs touched `internal/storage/sqlite`, migrations, or `shellterm`.

## What I think is going on

The sqlite package runs many migration tests in one binary; any single hang burns the entire 20m package budget, and `go test` reports only whichever test was running at panic time — which changes between runs. That pattern (arbitrary test "hung", local runs green, CI-only) is consistent with contention or a deadlock under the CI runner's parallel package load rather than a specific migration defect.

## Suggested directions

1. Mine the goroutine dump already present in the failing CI logs for the blocked goroutine's stack — that should name the actual contended resource.
2. Reproduce under load locally: `go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/ -count=5` alongside other packages, or with `-p`/GOMAXPROCS matched to CI.
3. Split the slowest migration suites (or adjust `t.Parallel` boundaries) so one hang doesn't burn the 20m package budget and the failing test is identifiable.
4. Consider a per-package `-timeout` with panic-profile artifact upload so every CI failure directly yields the blocked stack.

body:
Code changes: +197 -57  
Tests: +203 -43  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary
- keep files reachable when switching between the terminal, agent, and file surfaces
- open chat file references at their requested line and consume each line-navigation request exactly once, including across file-viewer remounts
- preserve file scroll position across agent navigation, retry restoration after asynchronously loaded content becomes scrollable, and finish at the reachable offset when content dimensions change
- display clicked files directly in the center pane without forcing the file-directory sidebar open
- remove the redundant Return to panel browser menu action when the maximize/minimize control already provides that path

## Regression provenance
- #5119 introduced the terminal/file center-surface switching regression while adding the extra terminal surface.
- #5243 introduced line-aware file links, but the center-pane path dropped the requested line before reaching the viewer.
- #5575 introduced session-scoped file workspaces; its remount behavior reset file scroll state when navigating through an agent.
- #5837 routed file clicks through the sidebar workspace, which forced the right-side file directory open.
- #6062 added browser maximize/minimize controls, making the Return to panel dropdown action redundant.

## Testing
- `cd frontend && npm test -- ReadOnlyFileView.test.tsx SessionFileWorkspace.test.tsx FileContentPane.test.tsx SessionView.test.tsx ChatMarkdown.test.tsx workspace-file-path.test.ts BrowserPanel.test.tsx` (402 tests passed)
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`
- manual verification in the latest AO Electron development instance

## Notes
- Line reveals are enforced by request identity and remain consumed across viewer remounts.
- Scroll restoration remains pending while content is not yet scrollable, then clamps to the available range once content is ready so later user scrolling is remembered.

title: bug(ui): orchestrator session keeps pulsing blue 'Working' dot while factually idle — stale active activity state
body:
### Summary

An **orchestrator** session (the project's own orchestrator pane, e.g. a GLM/claude-code harness) keeps flashing the blue "Working" activity dot in the sidebar project tree even though the orchestrator agent is idle at the prompt and has produced no output for hours. The indicator suggests the orchestrator is actively working when it is not.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a project with a long-lived orchestrator session (here: harness = claude-code backed by a GLM gateway model).
2. Let the orchestrator finish its turn and return to the idle prompt (no queued work, no in-flight tools).
3. Watch the project's dot in the sidebar: it keeps pulsing blue as if a turn were running, indefinitely.

### Expected behavior

When the orchestrator's turn has ended and the terminal sits at the idle prompt, the activity state should demote to idle and the blue pulsing dot should stop.

### Actual behavior

The session stays in activity_state = active / status = working (pulsing blue dot) while the agent is factually idle.

### Related — the same "wrong activity/status indicator" family

- #5050 — agy: stuck working after a turn is interrupted without its Stop hook (observer skips harness, no TerminalActivityDetector) — **template for this issue**
- #4142 — claude-code: stuck working after a turn dies without its Stop hook (closed)
- #3387 — Kimi: 'Working' indefinitely after provider.auth_error (401)
- #4048 — cline: completed turns stay working/active at the idle prompt (closed)
- #3115 — codex: stuck 'working' for days, stop hook never fired, no idle fallback demotes stale active (closed)
- #4213 — feat(web): orchestrator activity dot in the sidebar project tree — the indicator itself; orchestrator sessions seem especially prone to a stale active state
- #5751 — the inverse false-positive: fresh/live sessions mass-reported red (no_signal) by the LatestUserPromptAt discriminator

Common root cause across the family: activity state is set by hooks (pre/post tool-use, Stop) but nothing reliably demotes it when a turn ends without its Stop hook — the background observer only demotes harnesses implementing TerminalActivityDetector.

### AO version

Nightly 0.13.3 (Oct 2)

### Environment

macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Electron desktop app, harness claude-code + GLM gateway model

title: bug(ui): Review Summary hides review runs for earlier PRs of the same session (multi-PR sessions)
body:
### Summary

A session that produced **multiple PRs over its lifetime** (here: worker opened PR #51 — merged — then a follow-up bugfix PR #53) keeps review runs for **all** of them in the daemon DB, but the inspector's **Review Summary only shows runs for the session's current PR**. The three review passes for the merged PR #51 (changes_requested → approved → approved, distinct head SHAs, all auto-triggered, published) are invisible in the UI — only the #53 run is listed.

### Evidence (daemon DB, `review_run` for one session)

```
01:38  pull/51  changes_requested  delivered
01:53  pull/51  approved           complete
02:01  pull/51  approved           complete
03:03  pull/53  approved           complete   ← the only one shown in Review Summary
```

### Root cause (likely)

The review model is keyed `UNIQUE(session_id, harness)` — one review per session — and the summary binds to the session's currently attached PR. Runs belonging to earlier PRs of the same session have no surface in the UI.

### Expected

Review Summary should cover the session's whole review history: per-PR sections (or a PR selector), including merged/closed PRs, each with its runs, verdicts and SHAs. This is the review-side twin of #6132 (PR panel assumes one PR per session); both should be considered in the same inspector-rail rework.

title: [Feature]: Renderer crash screen has no app identity or error details — a screenshot can't tell what crashed
body:
### Problem

As a desktop user, when the renderer hits an unexpected error the whole window is replaced by a bare crash screen: a `Something went wrong!` heading, a `Hide Error` toggle, and a red box with the raw error message. Nothing on that screen says which app it is.

What I observed on 2026-10-02: the window went blank except for that screen showing `CancelledError`, with no way to tell what crashed, where, or why.

- No app name or logo — a screenshot of the window is indistinguishable from any other app's crash. I screenshotted it and sent it to an LLM, and it could not tell this was agent-orchestrator.
- No route/surface, no error details beyond the one-line message, no stack.
- No "Reload" or "Copy error details" buttons — the only way out is restarting the app.
- It happens even for benign errors: a cancelled in-flight request (`CancelledError`) killed the entire window instead of being swallowed.

### Proposed direction

A first-party crash screen whose screenshot is self-sufficient:

1. App name and icon, so any screenshot identifies the app on its own.
2. States that the renderer crashed, plus the route/surface where it happened.
3. Collapsible details: error name, message, stack (visible without DevTools).
4. "Copy error details" and "Reload" buttons.
5. Report the error to failure telemetry so these crashes are counted.
6. Do not replace the whole window for a mere request cancellation during navigation/teardown.

### Alternatives considered

Telling users to open DevTools and copy the console output — not realistic for a non-developer, and the common support path is a screenshot, which today carries no identifying information.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar

title: fix(frontend): swallow query cancellation in the router error boundary
body:
## Summary

A TanStack Query `CancelledError` losing its race against route teardown landed in the router's default `ErrorComponent` and replaced the entire window with the stock `Something went wrong!` screen — for a benign cancellation (observed in the desktop app: a cancelled workspace query blanked the whole UI).

Register `RouteErrorFallback` as the router's `defaultErrorComponent`: `CancelledError`/`AbortError` render nothing (the boundary's resetKey clears the state on the next navigation), every real error keeps the existing stock screen unchanged.

Part of #6134 (the branded crash screen with identity/details/telemetry is that issue's remaining scope).

## Red → green

- New `frontend/src/renderer/test/router-cancelled-error.test.tsx` (5 tests): default-error-component wiring, cancelled → no crash screen, abort → no crash screen, real error → stock screen preserved, end-to-end through a router boundary.
- Red before the fix (no component wired, crash screen shown for a cancelled query), green after; both manual mutants (guard removed / guard always-true) are killed by the suite.

## Gates

title: fix(lifecycle): re-arm merge-conflict nudge when a clean PR is policy-blocked
body:
Fixes #6104

## TL;DR

A worker was never told about a returning merge conflict when its PR went
conflicting -> rebased clean but still blocked (for example, waiting on a
required review) -> conflicting again. The `blocked` state alone cannot prove
the conflict went away, so the dedup never re-armed. Providers now report the
positive "no conflicts" signal out of band (`ConflictsCleared`), and the
lifecycle re-arm gate honors it.

## What was happening

1. PR conflicts -> worker gets a merge-conflict nudge (and AO remembers a
   durable "conflicting" signature in `pr.last_nudge_signature`).
2. Author rebases. The PR is clean but still blocked — GitHub reports
   `mergeable=MERGEABLE` with `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`; GitLab typically
   lands on `detailed_merge_status=not_approved` (rebase reset approvals) or
   `ci_still_running` (pipeline re-running).
3. Because the state reads `blocked`, not `mergeable`, the re-arm gate stayed
   shut and the old "conflicting" signature survived — across restarts too.
4. When a base-branch advance reintroduced a real conflict, the nudge was
   swallowed as a duplicate. The worker stayed silent while the sidebar showed
   "Merge Conflicts".

## The fix

The provider's own merge rollup already knows conflicts are gone, so it now
travels out of band alongside the derived state:

```go
mergeabilityClearsConflict(o.Mergeability) || o.ConflictsCleared
```

- `backend/internal/ports/scm_observations.go` — new `ConflictsCleared` flag
  on `SCMMergeabilityObservation` (plus a mirror on `PRObservation`).
- `backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go` — set from the
  `MERGEABLE` rollup, even when policy/CI/draft/review forces `blocked`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/scm/gitlab/observer_provider.go` — set from
  every computed non-conflict `detailed_merge_status` (see table below), even
  when the MR is blocked for an unrelated reason. New
  `gitlabMergeStatusRulesOutConflicts` helper computes it once above the
  switch and threads it into every return.
- `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go` — local recompute
  (`mergeabilityFromProviderFacts`) is now provider-neutral
  (`MERGEABLE` / `CAN_BE_MERGED` / merge-state `mergeable`), and the
  persisted-state override carries the flag so a review-only refresh cannot
  drop it.
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go` — the re-arm gate ORs the flag in.

### Which GitLab statuses set the flag

| Flag | Statuses |
| --- | --- |
| `true` — GitLab computed the merge, no conflict | `mergeable`, `can_be_merged`, `ci_must_pass`, `ci_still_running`, `discussions_not_resolved`, `draft_status`, `requested_changes`, `not_approved`, and the provider-blocked set (`not_open`, `locked_paths`, ...) |
| `false` — not proof the conflict is gone | `conflict` / `cannot_be_merged*`, not-yet-computed (`checking`, `preparing`, `unchecked`, `approvals_syncing`, `""`), unknown future statuses, and `need_rebase` (documented boundary: behind-base alone does not prove conflict-free) |

## Review feedback addressed

The review noted the first version only fixed GitHub: `mergeabilityFromMR`
set the flag solely on the unblocked `mergeable` return (which adds nothing —
`MergeMergeable` already re-armed), and the local recompute only recognized
GitHub's `MERGEABLE` enum while GitLab persists `can_be_merged` /
`mergeable`. This update:

1. Threads the flag through every `mergeabilityFromMR` return via the new
   helper, so `not_approved` / `ci_still_running` after a rebase re-arm.
2. Makes `mergeabilityFromProviderFacts` (and the GitHub live path for
   consistency) provider-neutral, so the live and replay paths agree.
3. Closes the test gaps: GitLab-shaped rows in both observer tests,
   `ci_still_running` / `not_approved` (+ the full blocked set, unknown-status
   boundary) in the GitLab provider test, and a GitLab-shaped wiring leg
   matching real `mergeabilityFromMR` output.

## Verification

Focused suites pass:

```text
ok  backend/internal/observe/scm
ok  backend/internal/adapters/scm/github
ok  backend/internal/adapters/scm/gitlab
```

`go vet` is clean on the touched packages. Broader regression coverage for the
re-arm lives at every layer: provider mapping (GitHub + GitLab), local
projection + persisted-state override (`internal/observe/scm`), re-arm gate
(`internal/lifecycle`), and end-to-end over the real sqlite store including
restart replay (`internal/daemon`).

### What went wrong?

Terminal users expect that any focus on terminal makes input field editable. While in AO input field requires specific focus.

title: feat(chat): add Command Code ACP Chat driver (v1.74.0 ships cmd acp)
body:
﻿### Problem

Command Code ships a first-party ACP agent but AO has no Chat driver for it, so Command Code sessions are TUI-only and the desktop never offers the TUI ⇄ Chat toggle.

Earlier discussion (#5781, #5958) assumed Command Code exposed no machine protocol. That assumption is now stale: `cmd --help` on v1.74.0 lists

```
cmd acp   Run as an ACP agent over stdio (for Zed, etc.)
```

### Verified capability surface

Probed against a live `cmd acp` handshake on Windows, Command Code v1.74.0 (2026-10-02):

```json
{"protocolVersion":1,
 "agentCapabilities":{
   "loadSession":true,
   "promptCapabilities":{"audio":false,"image":true,"embeddedContext":true},
   "mcpCapabilities":{"http":true,"sse":false},
   "sessionCapabilities":{"list":{},"resume":{},"close":{}}},
 "authMethods":[{"id":"command-code-cli","name":"Command Code CLI login"}],
 "agentInfo":{"name":"Command Code","version":"1.74.0"}}
```

This clears AO `chatProductionFloor` (streaming, approvals, interrupt, resume) because `loadSession: true` provides resume and ACP carries real `session/request_permission` approvals.

`session/new` advertises five modes and two live config options:

| id | name |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Standard |
| `auto-accept` | Accept Edits |
| `plan` | Plan |
| `dont-ask` | Don'"'"'t Ask |
| `bypass` | Bypass Permissions |

Config options: `model` (category `model`, 85 entries) and `effort` (category `thought_level`: off/high/max). Both are provider-owned, so AO needs no hardcoded model list.

### Proposed direction

Add `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/commandcodeacp/`, built with `nativeacp.New` against the existing Command Code agent plugin, and register it in `chatdriver/registry`. Mapping:

| AO permission mode | Command Code mode id |
| --- | --- |
| default | `default` |
| accept-edits / auto | `auto-accept` |
| bypass-permissions | `bypass` |

`plan` and `dont-ask` have no AO equivalent and would stay reachable only through Command Code'"'"'s own UI.

Launch is `cmd acp --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update --trust [--model …] [--permission-mode …]`; the existing plugin still owns binary resolution and auth.

Refs #5781, #5958, and the TUI work in #5959.

### Verification status

Handshake and `session/new` probed directly against v1.74.0 on Windows. A full `session/prompt` round trip was **not** exercised, so streaming deltas, tool-call updates, and permission round-trips still need end-to-end confirmation against a logged-in account.

title: fix(modelcatalog): Command Code TUI picker shows descriptions instead of model names
body:
### Problem

In TUI mode the Command Code model picker shows model *descriptions* where names should be, so the list reads as marketing copy rather than a set of models.

`cmd --list-models` prints an id and a description, with no friendly name:

```text
deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    hybrid-attention long-context reasoning
deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash   fast hybrid-attention reasoning (default)
minimaxai/minimax-m3        600B sparse-MoE agentic coding with 1M context
```

#5959 wires `command-code` to the shared `parseAgyModels` in `adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go`, which treats everything after the id as the label:

```go
label := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, fields[0]))
if label == "" {
    label = id
}
```

That is correct for Agy'"'"'s format, where the trailing text is a display name, but for Command Code it is the description. The picker therefore offers entries like "balances intelligence and cost" and "agentic coding & reasoning" as if they were model names.

Chat mode is unaffected. The ACP catalog supplies real names (`Claude Sonnet 5.5`, `DeepSeek V4 Pro (latest)`) and the correct value/description split.

### Proposed direction

Give `command-code` a parser that prefers the model id as the label, or one that derives a readable name from the id and keeps the trailing text as a description. The id alone is unambiguous and matches what the user passes to `--model`.

Refs #5959.

### Notes

The two `TestResolveBinary*` failures in the same package are unrelated and tracked separately.

title: feat(chat): Command Code ACP Chat driver, and fix TUI model labels
body:
Code changes: +779 -147  
Tests: +1135 -7  
Others: +246 -7 (generated OpenAPI spec and frontend TS types)

## Summary

Two fixes for the Command Code harness, both verified against a real Command Code v1.74.0 install.

Closes Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#6141
Closes Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#6142

> **Stacking.** This branch is built on `feat/commandcode-tui-5958` (#5959), which is still open and whose branch lives in the fork rather than in this repository. GitHub therefore cannot use that branch as this PR's base, so this PR targets `main` and its diff also contains #5959. The counts above are the full diff against `main`; reviewers should read the two commits on top of #5959 as the actual change.

### 1. Chat mode was missing because the premise was stale

Earlier Command Code discussion assumed it exposed no machine protocol. That is no longer true — v1.74.0 ships a first-party ACP agent:

```text
cmd acp   Run as an ACP agent over stdio (for Zed and other ACP clients)
```

Probed against a live handshake:

| Capability | Value | Effect in AO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loadSession` | `true` | clears the resume requirement of `chatProductionFloor` |
| `promptCapabilities` | `image`, `embeddedContext` | image and embedded-context prompts |
| `mcpCapabilities` | `http` | MCP over HTTP |
| `sessionCapabilities` | `list`, `resume`, `close` | enumeration and resume |

Because ACP carries real `session/request_permission`, approvals are first-class in Chat mode — unlike the TUI path, where Command Code's hook surface has no permission-request event and cannot distinguish an approval from other in-turn work.

`session/new` advertises five modes, so every AO permission mode maps exactly:

| AO mode | Command Code mode id |
| --- | --- |
| default | `default` |
| accept-edits | `auto-accept` |
| auto | `auto-accept` |
| bypass-permissions | `bypass` |

`plan` and `dont-ask` have no AO equivalent and are deliberately left unexposed.

Model and effort come from the provider's own catalog (`model`, 85 entries; `effort`, category `thought_level`), so AO keeps no hardcoded model list. Verified against a running daemon:

```text
id=model  cat=model  n=85   value=claude-sonnet-5-5  name='Claude Sonnet 5.5'
id=effort cat=thought_level n=3  off / high / max
```

The binding launches `cmd acp --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update --trust` through `nativeacp.New`, reusing the existing Command Code agent plugin for binary resolution and auth. Registration in `chatdriver/registry` is the whole capability gate, which is what makes the desktop render the TUI ↔ Chat toggle.

### 2. The TUI model picker offered descriptions as models

```text
fast hybrid-attention reasoning
600B sparse-MoE agentic coding with 1M c...
balances intelligence and cost
```

`cmd --list-models` prints `<id>  <description>`, and the trailing text is marketing copy, not a display name. #5959 wired `command-code` to the shared `parseAgyModels`, which reads everything after the id as the label — correct for Agy, wrong here.

Command Code publishes no friendly name in this listing, so the id is the only label that cannot misdescribe a model, and it is exactly what `--model` accepts.

`TestCommandCodeCatalogParsesTabularModelList` asserted a fabricated format:

```text
anthropic/claude-opus-4-1  Claude Opus 4.1
```

Real v1.74.0 emits bare ids (`claude-opus-5-5`) plus descriptions, with no `anthropic/` prefix. The invented fixture made the wrong behavior look like an intentional contract; it is replaced with real output.

## Validation

Both changes build clean and were exercised against a live Command Code v1.74.0 install on Windows.

Model catalog, run against the real 85-row listing:

```text
parsed 86 models
default model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
every label equals its id
no heading or boilerplate parsed as a model
```

The 86th row is `typesafe/jev`, listed under a separate "Decision models (headless only)" section; the banner's "85" does not count it.

Daemon, run against an isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`:

```text
GET /api/v1/settings   -> 14 chatHarnesses including command-code
GET /api/v1/agents     -> command-code, authStatus authorized
GET .../conversation/config-options -> 85 models + 3 effort levels, correct names
```

Tests:

```text
ok  internal/adapters/chatdriver/commandcodeacp
ok  internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry        (TestShippedChatDrivers)
ok  internal/domain
ok  internal/service/chat                        (run separately, 101s)
```

`go build ./cmd/ao` clean, `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean.

### Known failures not introduced here

Confirmed identical on the untouched base:

```text
modelcatalog: TestAutoHandDiscoveryReadsConfigurationWithoutRunningBinary  (autohand not installed)
modelcatalog: TestConfigCatalogDiscoveryAndFingerprint                   (continue not installed)
commandcode:  TestResolveBinaryFindsCommandCodeOnPath
commandcode:  TestResolveBinaryMissingReturnsErrAgentBinaryNotFound
```

The two `commandcode` failures appear only when Command Code is installed locally, which is why CI is green. They are test-isolation gaps in #5959's adapter: the first sets `PATH` but `binaryutil` also searches fixed `WinPaths`, so the real `cmdc.cmd` wins; the second skips on `UnixPaths` being present but never clears the Windows paths.

### Not verified

A full `session/prompt` round trip was not exercised end to end. Streaming deltas, tool-call updates, and the approval round trip against a logged-in account still need manual confirmation.

## Merge status: up to date with `main`

`main` has been merged into this branch, so the PR is no longer `CONFLICTING`. Two things were fixed in the process:

- The harness migration originally claimed number `0171`, which `main` had already taken with `0171_shell_preview_capability.sql`. Two files claiming one version makes goose refuse to build its history, which would have failed daemon startup on every existing install. It is now renumbered to `0179`, past everything currently on `main`, with the ledger, the reconcile comment and the migration tests following. (`main` claimed the intermediate numbers 0172-0178 while this PR was open, so the file moved more than once.)
- The Command Code ACP binding registered a `ValidateTurnSettings` that rejected every real approval change with "restart Chat", even though Command Code implements `session/set_mode`. The transport calls the validator before the runtime setter, so no approval change could ever reach a live session. The validator is gone; `session/set_mode` applies the change, and a provider answering `-32601` still surfaces as `ErrACPSetterUnsupported`.

## Screenshots

<!-- Add evidence images here before requesting review. -->

- [ ] Composer showing Command Code selected and the Chat interface available
- [ ] Chat session with streamed assistant output
- [ ] Model picker before this PR (descriptions as labels)
- [ ] Model picker after this PR (ids as labels)

## Risks

- `cmd acp` is recent. The binding pins no minimum version because `ValidateInitialize` is preferable to a version flag that many stdio agents do not implement. `TestVerifiedModeVocabulary` pins the five mode ids read from a live handshake so a future rename is visible rather than silent.
- The five mode ids come from a live v1.74.0 handshake, not from documentation.
- The model-label change alters what users see for this harness only; no other harness shares `parseCommandCodeModels`.

title: perf(files): eliminate blocking file viewer scans
body:
Code changes: +1216 -234  
Tests: +697 -40  
Others: +816 -140

## Summary

- add a compact, versioned workspace manifest backed by a bounded stale-while-refresh index
- reconcile missed edits when the workspace event stream reconnects, before announcing readiness
- coalesce refreshes, publish versioned workspace events, and lazy-load commit history
- migrate the file tree to `@pierre/trees` and prioritize initial diff batches
- align prefetching with the viewer's combined 24-file batches and keep content caches fresh across metadata-equivalent edits
- add opt-in, path-free file-viewer performance measurements and operational documentation

## Verification

- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- focused Vitest suite: 4 files, 56 tests
- `go test ./internal/service/session ./internal/httpd/controllers ./internal/httpd/apispec/...`
- `go test -race ./internal/service/session -run 'WorkspaceManifest|WorkspaceCache|WorkspaceDiffStats'`
- manual native Electron review using fresh isolated AO data

## Performance

- warm cached manifest benchmark: 264 ns/op, 0 B/op, 0 allocs/op

title: fix(lifecycle): ignore phantom post-Stop agent_needs_input notification
body:
Fixes #3738.

## Summary

Claude Code fires `Notification(agent_needs_input)` on a ~60s **client-side idle timer** even when the finished turn asked no question. `notificationState()` maps that type to `ActivityWaitingInput` unconditionally, so a session that had already gone `idle` (Stop observed, no `user-prompt-submit` since) was promoted into sticky `waiting_input` — which suppresses automated delivery until a human intervenes. On the reporting deployment this froze five coordinator sessions for ~23 hours.

The fix applies the precedence rule the tool path already has (see the blocked-clear correlation in `applyToolPrecedenceLocked`): a `waiting_input` signal derived from a `notification` is suppressed while the durable state is `idle`. In that window AO's own record — Stop landed, no new prompt — contradicts the notification, so it is a timer artifact, not a question. A genuine `agent_needs_input` arrives mid-turn (state `active`) and still lands; re-assertions over `waiting_input` remain same-state no-ops.

The suppression is scoped to the harnesses that speak the Claude Code hook contract (`claude-code`, `grok`, `continue`, `kimchi`) — the same family whose derivers share `claudecode.DeriveActivityState`'s notification mapping. Harnesses whose `notification → waiting_input` is genuine keep it: aider's completion notification is its only activity signal, and droid deliberately upgrades its post-Stop idle Notification to sticky `waiting_input` to suppress nudges. The decision lives in lifecycle, not in the pure `DeriveActivityState` mapping, matching how the existing blocked-clear correlation is structured.

## Reproduction (measured locally, macOS, real daemon, CLI 2.1.287)

- Throwaway claude-code session, trivial turn with no question: `stop` → `idle` at 21:55:41.830, phantom `POST /activity` at **+60.04s** (21:56:41.872) — the client-side timer is real and OS-independent, matching the issue's 60.1–60.2s cluster.
- The unit test demonstrates the flip on current code: red before the guard (`state after phantom agent_needs_input = "waiting_input"`), green after.

## Tests

- `TestToolPrecedence_PostStopNeedsInputNotificationStaysIdle` — table over `claude-code` and `grok`: phantom post-Stop notification keeps `idle`; genuine mid-turn notification still lands `waiting_input`.
- `TestToolPrecedence_PostStopNeedsInputNotificationOnlySuppressedForClaudeFamily` — pins that aider, droid, and an unknown harness keep their genuine post-idle notification (the aider regression shape: only signal + idle seeding; droid's documented upgrade).
- `go test -race ./internal/lifecycle/` — ok; gofmt clean.

## Risks

- A claude-family harness that reports a genuine needs-input question **after** its turn's Stop (no such producer exists today — question tools hold the turn open) would keep the session at `idle`; the next prompt/turn boundary restores normal flow.

### Summary

Gateway provider support (#6095 / #6096) is **one active gateway per scope** (app or project): a single `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` written to settings, inherited by every role. There is no way to say "Worker on the gateway, Orchestrator/Reviewer on Anthropic" — all roles silently share whatever the Gateway providers section resolves.

In Settings → Agents each role (Worker / Orchestrator / Reviewer) has an Agent picker, a model override and a reasoning effort — but no provider dimension. Models from the active gateway's catalog are offered for every role, which makes it look like a per-role choice exists when it doesn't.

Add a per-role provider selector in Settings → Agents:

- per role (Worker / Orchestrator / Reviewer): provider = "default (Gateway providers resolution)" | any configured gateway entry | "direct Anthropic (no gateway)";
- when a role pins a provider, its model list should come from that provider's catalog (the probe in #6095 already returns the gateway's model list);
- sessions already stamp `provider_base_url`/`provider_model` (#6096) — extend the staleness/apply flow to per-role overrides so a role switch can relaunch affected sessions the same way;
- resolution precedence should mirror the existing app→project override pattern and show the effective source.

### Related

- #6096 — apply provider switch to running sessions
