title: fix(chat): guard IME Enter and persist send-key preference
body:
## What

Guards the chat composer's Enter handler against IME composition, and adds 
a persistent send-key preference for IME-heavy workflows.

## Why

Fixes #3863.

Confirming a Japanese (or other IME) candidate with Enter was treated the 
same as a plain Enter — submitting, queueing, or steering the message 
instead of only confirming the composition. The chat composer checked 
`event.nativeEvent.isComposing` inconsistently with the New Task composer, 
and neither guarded the `event.keyCode === 229` fallback some browsers/IMEs 
rely on since `isComposing` isn't always reliable on the exact key-up that 
confirms composition.

## How

**IME guard, at both points Enter is actually handled:**
- `ChatComposer.tsx:1313` — the outer React keydown handler.
- `ComposerEditor.tsx:335` — Lexical's own internal completion handling, 
  which runs separately from the outer handler. Missing this second point 
  would have left a real gap: Lexical can process Enter for its own 
  completion semantics before the outer handler ever sees it.

Both locations check `event.nativeEvent.isComposing || event.keyCode === 229`. 
The guard blocks every delivery path, not just plain submit: send, queue, 
steer, promoting a queued message, and composer suggestion selection are 
all covered.

New Task's composer (`TaskComposerView.tsx:204`) was used as the reference 
pattern and left unchanged — it already checks `isComposing` (lacking the 
`229` fallback itself, but out of scope here per the issue, which only 
asked for Chat composer parity).

**Send-key preference**, added per the issue's request:
- Two modes: *Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts newline* (current/default) 
  and *Enter inserts newline; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends*.
- Lives in `Settings → General → Sessions → Chat send key`, following the 
  existing Zustand + localStorage pattern already used for settings like 
  terminal copy-on-select — not a new state mechanism.
- The composer hint text updates immediately when the mode changes.
- The IME guard applies identically in both modes — composing never 
  submits, regardless of which send-key mode is active.
- Translated across all existing locales (de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, 
  zh-CN).

## Testing

- 36 new regression tests, covering both composition signals 
  (`isComposing` and `keyCode === 229`) independently, across both 
  send-key modes, against every delivery path: send, queue, steer, queued- 
  message promotion, and suggestion selection (including `/compact`).
- Full suite validated on a clean, freshly-fetched `upstream/main` baseline 
  (detached HEAD, matching worker configuration) against the rebased 
  branch:

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Passed | 6,100 | 6,151 |
  | Failed | 0 | 0 |
  | Skipped | 6 | 6 |

  The +51 matches the added tests exactly — zero regressions, zero 
  pre-existing failures carried forward.
- Frontend and E2E typechecks both pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: Validate release lockfiles with the same Node and npm toolchain used to build artifacts
body:
## What happened
The [October 4 artifact build](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/37173088836) failed during npm ci with:
```
Missing: @pierre/theme@1.1.0 from lock file
```

#6214 restored the missing nested optional-peer entry and the later nightly shipped. That repairs this lockfile, but leaves the condition that caused the failure.

## Cause
On current main, .github/workflows/frontend.yml uses Node 24 while the frontend install in .github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml uses Node 22. The PR documents npm 11 accepting a lockfile that release npm 10 rejects after #6145 added @pierre/trees. Regenerating with the newer npm can remove the compatibility entry again.

This is a desktop artifact-build issue, separate from the private landing repository's missing weekly changelog run.

## Fix
Pick and pin a tested Node/npm toolchain for both PR validation and artifact builds. If both runtimes must remain supported, add a required clean-install matrix that checks the committed lockfile with the actual release npm version. Keep signing/publishing out of this validation job.

## Done when
- [ ] Document and pin the supported Node and npm versions.
- [ ] A clean PR install reproduces the artifact-build dependency resolution.
- [ ] The pre-#6214 lockfile fails the added release-toolchain regression check.
- [ ] Current lockfile passes all supported install environments.
- [ ] Verify unsigned artifact builds on Windows, Linux and both macOS architectures.
- [ ] Do not treat the one-entry lockfile repair alone as the permanent fix.

Related bootstrap work: #4396. This issue is specifically the release/PR validation mismatch.

title: fix(cloud): bump backend pin so the CP image builds with agentruntime.Effort
body:
## Problem

The control-plane Docker image does not build from current main. `#6163` added cloud code that uses `agentruntime.Effort` (in `agentruntime.RestoreConfig` and `agentruntime.LaunchConfig`), a backend field introduced on 2026-09-24 by `#5208`. But the `#6163` merge did not bump `cloud/go.mod`'s backend `replace` pin, which still points at an Aug-12 commit (`...20260812094327-5da0ce157982`) that predates the field.

Local and CI builds pass because the repo `go.work` makes them use the in-repo `backend/` (which has `Effort`). The control-plane Docker build has no `go.work` and compiles `cloud/` against the pinned backend, so it fails:

```
cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go:150: unknown field Effort in struct literal of type agentruntime.RestoreConfig
cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go:167: unknown field Effort in struct literal of type agentruntime.LaunchConfig
```

This affects both the official `deploy-staging.sh` / `promote-production.sh` flow and any manual CP build, so main is currently not deployable.

## Fix

Bump the `cloud/go.mod` backend `replace` pin to the backend module at main HEAD (`168f09b74`), which is exactly what `go.work` and CI already build against. `go mod tidy` pulled the three transitive `golang.org/x/*` minor bumps the newer backend requires.

## Verification

Compiled every binary the control-plane Dockerfile builds with `go.work` disabled (`GOWORK=off`), which is the same module resolution the Docker build uses:


Two features plus a follow-up fix, from a request to (1) make terminal-based provider authentication work for every harness and (2) be able to run several models on one task.

### 1. fix(agentauth): refresh harness readiness when a login terminal completes
Previously only Codex's login terminal had a daemon-side completion watcher. For every other harness, a finished sign-in was only noticed if the Settings panel happened to be polling, so the harness could stay "needs auth" after a successful login. Now the daemon watches the login command of **any** harness and, on exit, invalidates + re-checks that harness's readiness. New `POST /api/v1/sessions/council` and `ao council` fan one brief out to 2-8 harness/model members, each its own worker session, all tagged with a shared `councilGroupId` so clients can compare the cohort side by side. Best-effort: each member returns its session or its spawn error.

- Frontend: `useSpawnCouncil` hook.

### 3. fix(sessions): keep council group id through spawn/restore metadata rebuilds
The TUI spawn, Chat spawn, and restore paths rebuild `SessionMetadata` from a fixed field list, which dropped `CouncilGroupID` — found via live testing (council members lost their cohort link after launch). Carried over in all three paths, with a test.

title: Shell tab close: bound hung close requests and restore only the failed tab on error
body:
Follow-up to #6196, from the review comment https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6196#issuecomment-5981479029. Both findings were verified against `main`. Both are low severity: each needs a close request that fails or hangs.

## 1. A close request that never settles keeps a live shell tab hidden

`useCloseShellTerminal` (`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useShellTerminals.ts`) works like this:
- `onMutate` adds the handle to `closingShellHandles`;
- `fetchListedShellTerminals` filters marked handles out of every list refetch;
- the marker is removed only in `onSettled`.

`closeShellTerminal` sends the `DELETE` with no `signal`, and the renderer's fetch transport has no timeout. A request that hangs therefore keeps a still-live shell hidden from every refetch, with no way to retry.

Realistic trigger: a stalled connection to a remote host. Waiting on a session teardown's gate is benign, because the teardown destroys the shell anyway.

**Fix:** bound the request, e.g. `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` on the `DELETE`. A timeout isn't `SHELL_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND`, so it takes the existing `onError` path: the tab returns and the user can retry. `onSettled` then clears the marker and refetches.

## 2. A failed close restores a stale snapshot and resurrects sibling tabs

On any close error other than `SHELL_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND` (e.g. the daemon's 409 `SHELL_TERMINAL_STILL_RUNNING`, or a network error), `onError` writes the whole `onMutate` snapshot back. With two quick closes (A, then B), a failing A restores `[A, B]`, so B reappears while its own close is in flight, or after it already succeeded.

This predates #6196, but #6196's rapid-close flow makes it reachable. It self-corrects on the settle refetch unless the network is also failing.

**Fix:** on error, re-insert only the failed tab at its previous position (from the snapshot) instead of restoring the whole list. Other tabs' removals then stand.

## Done when

- [ ] A hung close times out and the tab comes back for retry (test with a never-resolving `DELETE` and fake timers).
- [ ] A failed close of A while B is closing (or closed) restores only A, in its original position (test).
- [ ] Existing `useShellTerminals` tests pass.
- [ ] Reply on the review comment linking the fix PR.

title: [Bug]: ao start launches the Linux AppImage with stdout/stderr closed, AppImage runtime then spins at 100% CPU
body:
### What went wrong?

On Linux with the AppImage install, every app launched by `ao start` leaves the AppImage runtime process (`~/.ao/agent-orchestrator.AppImage --installed-via=npm-bootstrap`) burning 100% of one CPU core for as long as the app runs, and after the app quits too.

**Root cause: `ao start` starts the app with stdout and stderr closed.** `backend/internal/cli/process.go` (at a34094e):

```go
type processStartConfig struct {
	...
	Stdout *os.File
	Stderr *os.File
}

func startProcess(cfg processStartConfig) error {
	cmd := exec.Command(cfg.Path, cfg.Args...)
	cmd.Env = cfg.Env
	cmd.Stdout = cfg.Stdout
	cmd.Stderr = cfg.Stderr
	...
```

`openApp` leaves `Stdout`/`Stderr` unset. Assigning a nil `*os.File` to the `io.Writer` fields gives a non-nil interface holding a nil pointer, which `os/exec` passes as "no file". The child therefore starts with **fd 1 and fd 2 closed**. Stdin is untouched, so it correctly gets `/dev/null`. A minimal Go 1.27.1 program with the same assignment shows `fd0=open fd1=CLOSED fd2=CLOSED` in the child.

**Why that costs a core:** the AppImage type2 runtime (here `AppImage/type2-runtime@dd6cebe`) creates its keepalive pipe with `pipe()`, so with 1 and 2 free the pipe lands on fd 1/2. When the FUSE side daemonizes, it redirects 0-2 to `/dev/null`, which silently replaces the pipe's write end. `write_pipe_thread` then loops `write()` "until we block", and writes to `/dev/null` never block, so it spins in the kernel. It also never sees the `EPIPE` that should end it when the app exits.

**Observed on the running app:**
- The runtime process has fds `0,1,2 -> /dev/null`, the AppImage and `/dev/fuse`, and **no pipe**.
- One thread spends about 75% of its time in the kernel, with 0 voluntary context switches.
- The Electron main process has `fd 2 -> /tmp/.mount_agent-*/AppRun`: stderr was closed at start, and a later `open()` reused the number.

**Minimal repro without AO:**

```sh
A=~/.ao/agent-orchestrator.AppImage
setsid sh -c "exec $A --appimage-mount" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &     # busiest runtime thread: 0% CPU
setsid sh -c "exec 0<&- 1>&- 2>&-; exec $A --appimage-mount" &          # busiest runtime thread: 100% CPU
```

**Also affected:**
- A second-instance `ao start` that only focuses the existing window also leaves a spinning runtime behind.
- Killing the spinning runtime unmounts `/tmp/.mount_agent-*`. Running daemon, pty-host and chat-host processes execute from that mount, so they break. The only clean way out is restarting AO.
- The `.deb` install isn't affected, since it has no FUSE runtime.

**Suggested fix** (one place, covers every caller): only set the writers when a file was given, so an unset stream falls back to `os/exec`'s default, `/dev/null`:

```go
if cfg.Stdout != nil {
	cmd.Stdout = cfg.Stdout
}
if cfg.Stderr != nil {
	cmd.Stderr = cfg.Stderr
}
```

**Workaround:** launch the AppImage yourself with `/dev/null` stdio instead of `ao start`:

```sh
setsid ~/.ao/agent-orchestrator.AppImage --installed-via=npm-bootstrap </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
```

**Environment:** AO 0.13.3 AppImage at `~/.ao/agent-orchestrator.AppImage`, Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 7.0), XFCE, `libfuse2t64` 2.9.9.

title: feat(review): let agents request AO native review of their own PRs
body:
Code changes: +982 -410  
Tests: +1339 -459  
Others: +155 -37 (generated OpenAPI/TS schema, i18n, docs, skill text)

## Why

A worker (worker100, PR #6258) repeatedly asked the orchestrator for an independent review. The orchestrator spawned a generic worker (worker106) instead of using AO's native reviewer, and the conversation then drifted to GitHub's "authors can't approve their own PR" rule, which is a separate boundary. PR #6258 sat at `needs_review` with **zero** native review runs.

The native reviewer was mature. The gaps were in how agents reach it:

1. The worker prompt never mentioned native review and sent "review help" to the orchestrator.
2. The orchestrator prompt said to spawn a worker for *every* code-review task.
3. `ao review trigger` required an explicit session id.
4. A review reached the worker twice: once as AO's verdict message and once as the reviewer's GitHub comments, which turned optional suggestions into required work.
5. Agent-requested passes were labelled `manual`, the same as a person's click.
6. Only per-adapter allowlists stopped a reviewer from triggering reviews.

## What

Behavior agreed with the user before implementation:

- **The worker reviews its own PR.** `ao review trigger`, `ao review ls` and `ao review cancel` default to the calling session (`AO_SESSION_ID`).
  - `trigger` takes `--agent/--harness`, `--model` and `--effort` per pass.
  - Runs are recorded with the new trigger source `agent`; the inspector labels them "Requested by agent".
  - The command refuses to run inside a reviewer pane (`AO_REVIEW_SESSION_ID`), so reviewers never start reviews.
- **Same-commit policy.** If a head already has a review, or a review is still running on it, `trigger` exits 1 with `409 REVIEW_HEAD_ALREADY_REVIEWED` or `REVIEW_ALREADY_RUNNING`, and the message says what to do next.
  - `--rerun` really reviews the same commit again. #6118's migration 0177 narrows the unique key to *running* passes; the #242 double-spawn guard is kept and tested.
  - There is no cap on review rounds. The desktop Run review button keeps its existing reuse behavior.
- **Parallel reviewers.** Reviewers with different agents can run on the same head at once (e.g. `--agent opencode --rerun` while Claude Code is running).
  - Trigger and worker restore no longer tear down a reviewer that is still working; only idle panes are released.
  - Stale-pane cleanup is scoped to one reviewer, and cancel stops every reviewer.
  - The list API exposes `activeReviewers`, and the inspector offers Open for each live reviewer.
- **Feedback loop (one channel).** AO's reviewer reaches the worker the same way any reviewer does: the SCM observer forwards its inline GitHub review comments. AO no longer sends a separate verdict message. This removes the pre-existing changes-requested verdict delivery (lifecycle `ApplyReviewBatch` and the review service's delivery step). Results are still recorded in AO and shown by `ao review ls` and the inspector.
  - The reviewer prompt requires an inline comment for every finding that needs a change, design-level ones included, and keeps optional suggestions in the summary only. Inline comments are all the worker receives, and it treats each as required.
  - Auto-inject stays a session setting. `ao review trigger` turns it on, since it controls review-comment forwarding, unless you pass `--no-inject`. Auto-review and the UI's Run review never change it.
  - An approval adds no comments, so the worker checks `ao review ls` for the verdict before reporting done.
- **Policy.** New project setting **Workers request AO review** (`workersRequestReview`, off by default), with a Settings toggle and a CLI `set-config` round-trip.
  - On: workers request a review once their PR is ready, and again after each fix.
  - Off: workers are taught the feature but ask the user or orchestrator first.
  - Either way, workers are told never to spawn a reviewer worker.
- **Orchestrator.** It never spawns workers to review code. It runs `ao review trigger <worker>`. For a PR that no AO session owns, it asks the human how to proceed.
- **Reviewer defaults.** Session reviewer choice, then the project reviewer config, then the project's **default worker agent with its model and effort**. Worker permissions are never inherited. Settings shows the inherited model truthfully.
- **Unchanged.** Merge rules, branch protection and GitHub credentials are untouched. The reviewer still posts `COMMENT` reviews from the author's account.

No provider issue backs this task (it is a freeform task from the user), so nothing is linked.

## Rebased onto main with #6118 and #6291

- **Migration:** #6118 shipped the identical approved-head migration as `0177_review_run_rerun_same_head.sql` (same blob). This PR no longer adds its own; `TestMigration0177AllowsRepeatApprovalsButNotDoubleRunning` now covers up/down for `0177`.
- **Trigger contract unified:** #6118's `TriggerOptions{Harness, Config, Source, InterfaceMode, Rerun}` gains `RejectReviewedHead`. All HTTP triggers go through one service path (`TriggerRequested`); `TriggerWithMode`/`TriggerWithOptions` stay as wrappers.
- **Rerun policy:** a person's rerun (`manual`) keeps #6118's behavior and reuses an active pass from the same reviewer (200). An agent's rerun (`agent`) gets `409 REVIEW_ALREADY_RUNNING` instead, so it knows nothing new started. Agents may now rerun; #6118 allowed only manual.
- **#6291 archive:** an archived reviewer is never listed in `activeReviewers`, and worker restore still skips it.

## Changed after real-agent testing on the rebased build

- **One feedback channel (decided with the user):** see "Feedback loop" above. It fixes a review being delivered twice and optional suggestions being escalated to required work.

- **Fresh PR facts on trigger:** a requested review (manual or agent) fetches the worker's open PRs from the provider first, through the session claim path, and then decides what is due. It is bounded at 10s and best effort for tracked PRs; on failure it falls back to stored facts. Auto-review does not refresh. Right after a push the provider itself can lag 1 to 2 seconds, so the already-reviewed message says to retry after a few seconds.
- **`ao review trigger --pr <url>` (`prUrl`, same names as #6136):** reviews only that PR. A PR AO doesn't track yet is attached first and never taken over from another active session (`409 REVIEW_PR_OWNED_BY_OTHER_SESSION`). With no tracked PR, the error points at `--pr`.
- **Failed or cancelled runs:** nothing reports these to the worker, so its instructions say to re-trigger when `ao review ls` shows `failed` or `cancelled`.

## Follow-ups found testing with real agents (included)

- The inspector refreshes a session's reviews on `review_run_created`/`review_run_updated`. Before, a review an agent started, or a reviewer finished, stayed invisible until something else refreshed.
- When the selected reviewer is idle and another is working (an agent used `--agent codex`), the inspector offers to open the working one and the Reviewer tab shows it. The selected-reviewer fields in the API keep meaning the selected reviewer; clients read `activeReviewers`.
- Worker restore no longer cancels a running Chat reviewer for having no pane; Chat reviewers are recovered by `RecoverChatReviewers`.

Verified in a dev Electron build with real Claude Code and Codex agents on a private playground repo. The worker requested its own review; Claude and Codex reviewers approved and posted COMMENT reviews; verdicts were delivered to the worker (that build still had verdict delivery; see the change above); same-commit re-trigger was refused; the inspector updated live.

Then, on the head with the forced refresh and `--pr`, against the same playground:
- Push, wait until GitHub reported the new head, then trigger at once, with AO's stored head still on the old commit: the run reviewed the new commit (`b745ebe`).
- A trigger within about a second of the push saw the old head, because GitHub's API had not updated yet; it reported the new head 1 to 2 seconds later. That build answered with a local-git probe (`REVIEW_HEAD_NOT_OBSERVED`); AO's review then showed the probe misfires when the provider is ahead of the local ref, so it was removed and the already-reviewed message says to retry after a few seconds.
- `ao review trigger --pr <url>` right after `gh pr create` (PR #4, untracked by AO) attached the PR and started its review within 1 second; the reviewer posted an inline comment.


## Changed after AO's own review of this PR

- Removed the local-git pushed-head probe and `REVIEW_HEAD_NOT_OBSERVED`; the provider refresh covers it.
- `List` keeps the selected-reviewer fields meaning the selected reviewer; the client picks a working reviewer from `activeReviewers`.
- Removed trigger entry points with no production callers (service `Trigger`/`TriggerWithMode`/`TriggerWithOptions`, engine `Trigger`/`TriggerWithSource`/`TriggerWithSourceAndMode`) and the unused `MarkReviewRunDelivered` writer. The `delivered` status stays for existing rows.
- `Engine.Cancel` cancels legacy harness-less runs once.

## Verification

Local runs used the CI commands. The Go suites ran with the AO session environment unset, as on CI:

- Backend: `gofmt`, `go build`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint v2.13.2` (0 issues), `npm run sqlc` (no drift), `npm run api` (spec and `schema.ts` regenerated, no further drift).
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`: 187 packages ok. Three unrelated failures, each checked:
  - `codexappserver/TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` also fails on clean `origin/main`; it compares against this machine's installed `codex`.
  - `goose` and `conpty` failed once under heavy concurrent load and passed `-race -count=3` on this branch (and on main).
- Frontend: `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`, full `vitest run` (383 files, 6136 tests passed), `test:browser-postcondition-integration`, docs build, and the product-ui and cloud-client checks all pass.
- **Isolated daemon end-to-end run** (scratch `AO_DATA_DIR`, lab pty host, fake `claude`/`opencode`/`gh` binaries, so no model spend and no GitHub writes in this phase). With a real spawned worker and a seeded PR:
  - The worker's system prompt contained the opt-in section.
  - `ao review trigger` from the worker started a Claude Code run labelled `agent` and turned on inject.
  - A repeat trigger was rejected with `REVIEW_ALREADY_RUNNING`.
  - An OpenCode reviewer ran **in parallel** without cancelling the first.
  - Submitted verdicts were delivered into the worker's pane on that pre-change build. Verdict delivery has since been replaced by PR-comment delivery (see above).
  - The reviewed head was rejected with `REVIEW_HEAD_ALREADY_REVIEWED`; a simulated push started a new review; cancel stopped both reviewers.
  - `--rerun` on an approved head started a new run (the real index).
  - The reviewer pane's environment carries `AO_REVIEW_SESSION_ID` and no `AO_SESSION_ID`, and the CLI refusal fires there.
- **Isolated Electron run** (dev build of this branch, separate profile and run file, the same scratch data): the inspector listed two live reviewers with Open (opening OpenCode switched the reviewer tab), the run showed "Approved · Requested by agent", and Settings showed **Workers request AO review** on.

### Not verified locally

- Windows, macOS-update and Docker CLI e2e jobs.
- Local Node is 22; CI uses 24.

Remote checks on the previous head all passed, including the Windows, macOS and Linux native jobs, which cover the gaps above.

## Risks and follow-ups

- **Overlap with open review PRs.**
  - #6118 touches `service/review` and `review/review.go`.
  - #5571 adds sequential multi-reviewer aggregation. This PR keeps "latest run wins, but running has priority" per head and does not aggregate verdicts.
  - #6136 adds per-PR targeting.

- **Parallel reviewers share one reviewer tab.** The tab follows the reviewer you open; it is not one tab per reviewer.
- **Pre-existing crash found during the Electron run (not fixed here).** `SessionPRMergeabilitySummary.Reasons` serialises as `null` for an open PR whose mergeability is unknown/mergeable, and `pr-display.ts` calls `.includes` on it. The inspector crashes for a PR the SCM observer can't read. Worth a separate fix.

## Why

Opening the session inspector for **any open PR that is mergeable** crashes the desktop session view with:

title: fix(chat): settle Claude turns stuck after background-task cycles
body:
Code changes: +369 -26
Tests: +441 -0
Others: +0 -0

## What

Build-time patches to the pinned `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0, added to `frontend/scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.mjs` and applied by `build-acp-runtime.mjs` next to the existing retry/context patches, plus a persistent chat-host watchdog.

- `patchClaudeFoldedPromptSettlement`: a `task-notification` result that names a pending prompt in `user_message_uuid(s)` now settles that prompt. Port of agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp#1233 for issue agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp#1145.
- `patchClaudeStaleIdleDebt`: drops the adapter's unpaid trailing-idle debt on an idle→running transition. Port of the sweep upstream shipped in claude-agent-acp 0.79.
- `patchClaudeSteerSettlement` (new): a result naming a steered message in `user_message_uuid(s)` retires the steer lane and settles through the ordinary result path. Port of the exact-result acknowledgement path upstream in claude-agent-acp#1166.
- `patchClaudeSteerIdleGuard` (new): the idle-debt absorption branch no longer consumes the one coalesced terminal idle of a *completed* steer sequence (echo replayed and steered result recorded). Incomplete steer sequences keep absorbing, so their terminal idle is still ahead.
- `patchClaudeSteerDebt` (new): steering a turn that recorded a held result hands that result's trailer to the steer lane's idle, and an autonomous result the pending steer aborted shares the steered sequence's single idle instead of owing its own. When the settlement patch has already retired the lane, a steer-answering result owes no fresh trailer.
- Persistent chat-host watchdog (new): an in-flight `session/prompt` that has heard nothing from the adapter for 15 minutes gets a terminal `-32603` error instead of hanging the session's Working indicator until restart. This is a backstop for adapter state losses this PR does not (yet) settle, e.g. a lost subagent task-end bookend.

## Why

Claude chat sessions keep showing "Working for N min" long after the agent has finished, until the user presses Stop or sends another message. There are three triggers:

1. A message sent while Claude is handling a background-task notification gets folded into that cycle. The cycle's result keeps `origin: task-notification`, so the adapter treats it as autonomous and never answers `session/prompt`, and the AO turn stays `running`. Reproduction steps are in a comment below.
2. When a background task's notification arrives before the turn that started it ends, Claude Code emits a single idle for both. One owed idle is never paid, and it later swallows the idle a steered turn settles on, so that steered turn hangs.
3. Even with fixes 1 and 2 installed, a live session still hung "Working forever": a human result held open for a background subagent, steered during the subagent's hand-back cycle, ends with the steered answer recorded in the steer lane — and the single idle the SDK emits for the whole wake+steer+steered sequence was absorbed as owed trailing-idle debt *before* the steer lane could run. The debt reset from `patchClaudeStaleIdleDebt` cannot help because there is no idle→running transition anywhere inside that stretch. This PR fixes that live case end-to-end.

No upstream release fixes #1145 yet (latest is 0.85.1). These patches should be removed once we bump to a release that includes all of the fixes.

## How

- All patches use the same tripwire style as the existing ones: an exact anchor match, so packaging fails instead of silently skipping the patch if upstream code changes.
- The fold patch sends a result down the ordinary user-turn path only when it names an unsettled turn that isn't held open for background subagents. Results without the uuid stamp behave exactly as before; Claude Code older than 2.1.268 doesn't stamp them, so that case still hangs, with no regression.
- The debt reset fires only on a real transition into `running`. An idle that arrives late for the previous turn is still absorbed, so the adapter's #825 stuck-turn detection is unaffected.
- The steer settlement patch tracks injected steer UUIDs separately from the replay-echo bookkeeping, so a stamped result retires the lane even when its echo frame was lost. Cancelled turns are untouched, and unstamped results keep the prior idle behavior (covered by the idle guard and debt accounting instead).
- The watchdog stamps the last adapter output on every frame, runs on a 30s check under the host mutex (never racing `forwardProvider`), resolves only same-generation prompts (reconnect-recovery owns earlier ones), and stays terminal — it cannot fire twice, and the session accepts a new prompt once the controller acknowledges the synthetic completion.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.test.mjs`: 36 passed. The tests run the patched code itself, not just string checks.
- The upstream 0.70.0 adapter suite run against the patched dist: 812 passed, 0 failed. A 9-case steer-into-held-turn regression suite (replaying the captured live frame sequences) passes 9/9 on this patch set; the pre-steer-fix composition failed 3 of its 9 cases.
- Real end-to-end with Claude Code 2.1.292 on an isolated daemon: the exact trigger (async subagent, held human result, steer during the hand-back cycle) hung 2/2 against the previously-installed patches (3 results + 1 idle, turn running forever, queued message undelivered); with these commits the same choreography settles in milliseconds and the queued message is delivered. Plain-steer, folded-prompt, held-turn-no-steer, and followup-at-turn-end controls all settle with no failed turns.
- The `no-task-notification` sequence (lost task-end bookend) still stalls the adapter and is intentionally not fixed here; the watchdog converts that hang into a terminal error after 15 minutes instead.
- `npm run build:acp-runtime` applies all patches to the real 0.70.0 adapter, and the result passes `node --check`. Backend: `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/...` passes (watchdog paths).

title: fix: Claude Code shows signed-out on expired OAuth; stuck session can't be deleted
body:
Code changes: +105 -0
Tests: +106 -0
Others: +0 -0

## Why

Two bugs that together made Claude unusable in AO and left a session stuck and undeletable:

1. **Auth false-negative.** The Claude auth ladder's network probe reads the short-lived OAuth access token from the keychain and calls `GET /v1/models`. A Claude Max subscription access token expires routinely while the user stays signed in — Claude Code refreshes it from the refresh token, so `claude auth status` keeps reporting `loggedIn`. AO saw the `401 "OAuth access token has expired"` and classified the credential as Invalid, rendering a working, signed-in user as **"Signed out"** and blocking Claude launches.

2. **Undeletable wedged session.** A switch stuck at `source_restore_unconfirmed` ("Codex could not be restored") can be neither recovered (the source relaunch keeps failing) nor auto-failed (its retained recovery marker must never sit on a failed row), so it holds the switch/input gate forever. `Kill` acquires that gate first, so it refused with `ErrSwitchInProgress` — the session could never be removed and its terminal stayed locked.

## What

1. Treat an **expired-but-refreshable** OAuth access token as inconclusive (`StateUnknown`) instead of a decisive rejection (mirrors the existing `IsResolverBug` downgrade). The ladder then defers to the CLI/local rungs → "Configured", and launch is allowed (Claude refreshes the token on start). A revoked token ("... is invalid") does not match and stays a decisive rejection.
2. `Kill` now finalizes a retained stuck switch (`source_session_terminated`) and releases its gate before acquiring the kill gate, so a wedged session is removable. It acts only when the gate is held as a retained recovery fence, never racing a live switch worker. `reconcileAgentSwitch` gains the same terminated-session handling so a reaper-terminated session self-heals on boot instead of re-quarantining.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test` on the touched packages: green. New unit tests for both fixes (`TestValidateResolvedLocalTreatsExpiredOAuthAsRefreshable`, `TestValidateResolvedLocalKeepsRevokedOAuthInvalid`, `TestIsRefreshableOAuthExpiry`, `TestAbandonRetainedAgentSwitchForTerminationReleasesStuckGate`).
- Verified live in the real Electron app: Claude Code flipped from "Signed out" to "Configured", a Claude Code session launched (ACP connected, all start stages OK), and it responded correctly in-session.

title: fix: unify the effort picker and select a default effort
body:
Code changes: +354 -105  
Tests: +328 -19  
Others: +80 -0 (translations)

## Summary

Extract the effort picker UI from #6236 into an independent PR targeting `main`, and make sure a model that offers effort levels never shows an unselected effort.

- Share effort menu rendering across New Task, project settings, and native/ACP chat.
- Show only concrete, localized effort names (Medium, High, Extra high, ...) in menus and selectors. No Default, Use agent effort, or Effort not reported rows. Levels a provider reports that AO does not know are shown as reported.
- Use consistent effort row typography and short, compact menus; remove explanatory fallback paragraphs.
- Hide empty effort controls; retain saved values and an explicit Clear effort action for unavailable saved selections.
- Select an effort when the model reports levels but no usable default (see below).

## Default effort when the provider reports none

When a model offers levels but the provider names no default for them, AO picks the middle level (`fallbackEffort` in `lib/effort.ts`) and treats it as the real selection, so the level a picker shows is the level the run uses. A provider that reports a default among its levels is always left in charge, and a level the user picks always wins.

| Surface | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| New Task | Shown as selected and sent when the task starts. |
| Project settings | Shown as selected and saved when the user chooses a model. Opening settings does not write anything. |
| Chat (ACP and native menu) | Set when the user switches model, and on open only for a conversation with no turns yet. Reopening an existing local conversation does not change the effort it was running with (cloud chat has a known gap, see below). Nothing is set while the chat controls are disabled (controller stopped, connecting or provisioning, or a config change in flight). |

Selecting the provider's reported default level behaves differently by surface: on ACP chat pickers that expose a reset choice it sends the provider reset token; on New Task, project settings, and the native chat menu it clears the explicit choice so the agent default applies.

Also in this PR: a saved effort for a model missing from a loaded catalog is flagged invalid again, while a listed model whose provider reports no efforts keeps its saved effort.

## Scope

Frontend only. Model fetching, caching, account handling, model catalog ordering, additional models, and backend effort transport remain in the existing PR stack. This PR can merge directly into `main`; it does not require #6234, #6236, or #6251.

## Validation

Run on the current head, after merging the latest `main`:

- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- 54 affected test files (effort picker, composer, project settings, chat, i18n): 1,197 passing.
- Full renderer suite on the previous head: 6,150 passing, 22 failing. All 22 are in `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch, and come from a `better-sqlite3` native-module ABI mismatch (built for Electron, not the test runner).

title: fix(chat): recover untouched Chat sessions across interface switch, rollback, and resume
body:
Code changes: +252 -33  
Tests: +688 -1  
Others: +64 -3 (generated sqlc)

## What

Fixes three defects that together left an untouched Chat session (no messages sent) stuck with "The agent controller stopped" and an "Internal server error" on **Resume agent**:

1. Switching an untouched **orchestrator** Chat to Terminal always failed with `empty root proof changed`.
2. The rollback of that failed switch failed with `session controller ownership changed before browser capability rotation`, leaving the transition in `recovery_required`.
3. Resuming an untouched Chat whose persistent provider host had died failed with ACP `session/load` `-32002 Resource not found`.

## Why

Fixes #6267

- **Switch:** orchestrator conversations are project-scoped (`conversations.session_id` is NULL, the active orchestrator is `current_session_id`), but `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider` (added in #5053) required `session_id` to match.
- **Rollback:** when the controller epoch never committed, rollback relaunched with `fresh=true`, which clears the provider id only in memory. The database still held it, so the expected controller owner mismatched during browser capability rotation.
- **Resume:** Claude Code reserves a session id when a Chat opens but writes no transcript until the first prompt. With the host gone, reloading that id can never succeed.

## How

One commit per defect:

- **`fix(chat): release untouched orchestrator Chat…`**: the release predicate accepts a project-scoped conversation currently bound to the session. The empty-history guards (`latest_sequence = 0`, no turns) are unchanged, so a conversation with history, another session's conversation, or a reviewer conversation is still never released.
- **`fix(chat): start fresh when resuming an untouched Chat…`**: a surviving host still holds the session in memory and must be reattached, and only the driver knows whether it is alive. So the fallback lives where a reload actually fails:
  - Session Manager always offers the stored id. It sets `FreshIfProviderConversationMissing` only for an ordinary resume with durable proof the conversation never started (the adapter finds no persisted history, and AO recorded no turns or messages). This reuses `persistedNativeConversationID` / `nativeConversationNotStarted`.
  - The ACP driver opens a new session on the freshly spawned connection only when the reload returns `-32002` and the flag is set. Other errors and non-ACP drivers are unchanged.
  - The Chat service accepts the different provider id only with the flag and without a live reconnect, and skips native-history import.
  - `ControllerReady` moves the session and its untouched root branch to the new id in one guarded transaction (`ReplaceUnpersistedChatProvider`). The root **keeps its provider scope**, which is part of the persistent host's ownership fingerprint. The `conversation_branch_root_provider_update` trigger only fires for `'' → id`, so the root update is explicit.
- **`fix(chat): restore the durable Chat owner when a switch rolls back…`**: rollback starts fresh only if the epoch committed or the source is not Chat. TUI sources and committed rollbacks are unchanged.
- Compatible with #6254's reconnect-only startup health check: the fresh-start fallback is disabled when `ReconnectOnly` is set (driver and Session Manager), so a health check never opens a new provider session.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- Clearing the stored id before resuming broke reattach to a live host ("fresh ACP start found an existing initialized session").
- Rotating the root's provider scope broke the host fingerprint ("provider launch configuration changed").

**Known limitation (pre-existing, not addressed):** if a still-untouched project conversation is rebound to a *second* orchestrator, the next Chat→Terminal switch is refused cleanly at the same release check. It ends in `failed`, not stuck. Tracking as a follow-up.

## Testing

From `backend/`:

    GOWORK=off go vet ./...
    GOWORK=off go test -race -count=1 ./...

New tests, each of which fails without its fix:

- `store`: `TestFreshInterfaceEpochReleasesUntouchedProjectConversation`, `TestReplaceUnpersistedChatProviderMovesSessionAndRoot`
- `acp`: `TestACPDriverResumeStartsFreshOnlyForMissingSessionWhenAllowed`
- `service/chat`: `TestResumeAcceptsFreshProviderOnlyWhenAllowed`
- `session_manager`: `TestResumeUntouchedChatStartsFreshWhenProviderNeverPersisted`, `TestInterfaceTransitionRollbackRestoresUncommittedChatSource`

Manual, in the desktop app (isolated dev data, macOS):

- Untouched orchestrator Chat → Terminal: the switch completes.
- Claude Code, host alive: quit and relaunch, then Resume. The session reattaches with the same provider id.
- Claude Code, host killed: Resume returns 200, the log shows `ACP session missing; started fresh`, and the session and root move to the new id with the same scope and no child branch.
- Codex orchestrator start: unaffected.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat: add CLIProxyAPI account management and routing
body:
Code changes: +6021 -10234\
Tests: +10479 -8419\
Others: +3743 -5045

## What

Account Manager: several Claude and Codex accounts in AO, with each session's model requests sent to that session's account through a small helper process built on the CLIProxyAPI SDK. It replaces the Codex subscription management, which this PR removes.

The daemon owns accounts, per-provider defaults and session routes. The detached helper (`ao-proxy-host`) holds the sign-ins, forwards requests and counts what passes through each account; it knows no provider response shape.

Started by @whoisasx. After review the PR was taken over; [Changes after review](#changes-after-review) lists what changed since.

## What a user gets

- Sign in to Claude and Codex accounts inside AO: browser sign-in, Codex device code, API key, or credential JSON import. A browser sign-in opens the provider's page, and the page it returns to says whether the sign-in worked. A label typed with an API key names its account. AO copies nothing from the computer. An agent whose provider has no account in AO keeps the computer's own setup (its login, an API key, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, `apiKeyHelper`, a custom Codex `model_provider`), as on `main`.
- Settings > Accounts, a list beside a detail:
  - plan, limits with reset times, resets and extra usage, a default per provider, rename, renew sign-in, sign out, remove, move sessions; the list shows each account's limit with the least left;
  - what AO sent through the account: tokens per day for 14 days, today, 7 days and since counting began, the share of each model, and the models the account can use, newest first;
  - health: the last refused request, refusals by kind, and the typical time to the first word;
  - the account's sessions by name with today's tokens, each one openable or movable, and an estimated cost of those sessions;
  - three settings: keep the account in reserve, switch its sessions to another account when its limit is reached, and warn when little is left;
  - a link to the provider's own plan page.
- "Device" marks the AO account with the same email as the computer's own login.
- On the harness pages, an agent whose provider has AO accounts shows them and a button to the Accounts page, instead of its own login and logout.
- Pick an account when starting a task; switch a session's account from the session menu. An account in reserve is not offered for a new task.
- Model pickers list the models of the session's account. A Codex sign-in lists only the models OpenAI offers that account.
- "Switch agent" between Claude and Codex keeps working. The session goes on its account for the target provider (the default the first time), and a switch back returns it to the account it had.
- A Codex session moves only between accounts of one kind, ChatGPT plan to plan or API key to key: Codex sends its earlier encrypted reasoning back on every turn, and the other kind cannot read it.
- Signing an account out moves its sessions to the replacement when they can go there. The others wait, and go on when the account signs in again. The sessions of a removed account go on the next sign-in they can move to.
- Sessions that predate Account Manager move onto their provider's default once it has one, chats and terminals alike, within about 30 seconds of the first sign-in. A session is moved when it is idle, never while it works or waits for an answer. A terminal is moved once nobody types in it, on screen or not: no text typed for 30 seconds and none typed since its turn ended. Its agent exits and is resumed on the account, with keystrokes held back for those seconds.
- Chats, side chats, terminals, background tasks and reviews all run on their session's account.

## How

- **One source of truth.** Account state is one JSON document in SQLite (`0199_provider_accounts.sql`). A change asks the helper first, then saves; the daemon re-sends the whole route table to the helper at start and every 10 seconds.
- **Managed providers.** AO manages a provider once it holds an account for it, signed in or not. Until then its agents run as on `main`, and old sessions are moved only onto a default account.
- **Routes and tickets.** A session has one route per provider it uses: its own agent's under the session's id, any other as `id/provider`. Each has a ticket derived from the session and the provider (an HMAC under the helper's ticket key), so an agent switch renames routes but moves no ticket, and an agent still running on the provider the session left keeps its account. Related work (a reviewer, a side chat, a background task) runs on the session's route for its own provider and never moves the session's own route. A terminal switch prepares the target's account without moving the route, and moves it only after the source agent has stopped.
- **One busy rule.** The helper refuses a sign-out or removal while one of that account's requests is in flight. A sign-out between two requests of a turn is accepted and the turn continues on the replacement account.
- **One helper interface.** `ports.AccountHelper`, implemented by `adapters/proxyhost.Client`. Usage, plan and reset shaping live in the daemon only.
- **Helper updates.** The daemon starts the helper with a build id (a hash of its binary), and `/ao/status` reports it. A running helper of another build is asked to stop (`POST /ao/stop`, refused with 409 while a request is in flight) and replaced once idle. The identity is kept in `run/host.json` and in `host.json`. A lost or broken copy is restored from the other, so a running helper and its sessions carry on. With both copies gone, AO starts on a new identity, and a helper whose identity was replaced stops by itself once idle.
- **Security boundary.** Control key and session tickets are separate; a ticket reaches only the inference paths and the model list; the helper selects exactly the session's account with no fallback; credential files are owner-only; account routes refuse foreign web origins and are absent on the LAN listener. The helper sets no management secret, so the SDK's management routes and its Redis-protocol listener are off, and AO registers the management handlers it needs behind its own boundary. Every request with an `Upgrade` header gets 501. The helper runs with umask 077, and at start it makes sign-ins saved earlier 0600.
- **Refusals.** A model the provider refuses (400, 404 or 422 that is not about the credential) returns the provider's own answer for that request and leaves the account available. A session whose account is signed out or removed gets one answer its CLI does not retry (403 for Claude Code, 400 for Codex), saying to sign in on the Accounts page.
- **Resets.** A reset whose answer was lost or unknown is sent again with the same request ID, so the provider answers `already_redeemed` and does not spend a second one.
- **Counting in the helper.** A usage plugin on the SDK counts tokens per account, model, day and session, and refusals by kind. Daily counts are kept across a restart in `run/activity.json`, keyed by a hash of the account; nothing but hashes and numbers is stored.
- **Readings are paced.** An account's limits are read every five minutes. A reading that fails is retried after a minute and the last good one stands for half an hour. What the helper counted itself is read on every request.
- **Moving old sessions.** At most four at once; a move starts when a turn ends and again at a check every 30 seconds. The sessions are listed again whenever the providers with a default account change, so a sign-in reaches sessions started while their provider had none.
- **Reports missed while closed.** At start the daemon applies the last end-of-turn report each session made while it was down, so a terminal that finished meanwhile reads as idle and can be moved.
- **Typing.** The terminal mux records when it last took input that carries text. Reports a terminal sends by itself (focus, theme, colour replies) and keys that only move or edit do not count, so they do not hold a move back. The resumed agent is reported idle, so it does not read as "No signal".
- **Six API operations** under `/api/v1/provider-accounts`, including one `actions` endpoint for per-account changes.

## Changes after review

Each item answers a review thread or a test report on this PR.

- AO no longer copies the computer's logins or keys, so renewing an account no longer signs the computer's `claude` or `codex` out; providers with no account in AO keep their own setup (6bb1ad169, af3564edc).
- A broken `host.json` gets a new identity (b93004960); an AO update replaces a running helper once it is idle (21a0b0370, 549d4a1b0).
- Every Claude and Codex launch runs on its session's account: side chats, reviewers on the other provider, and a switch into Claude or Codex (33992a1a9). Switching between Claude and Codex works again (33992a1a9, 7a39fbfe3), and background tasks no longer move a route (ec0426b3b).
- The helper refuses every upgrade request (d3c0cb460) and no longer runs the Redis-protocol listener (a07863e0f).
- Codex sessions move only between accounts of one kind, in the daemon and on the page (2fa074cb2, b96b3a56c); waiting sessions keep their kind (7a39fbfe3, f1d65f9df). A retried reset spends nothing twice (2fa074cb2).
- A refused model gets the provider's answer, not a retried 503 (30194de30); a Codex sign-in offers only the models OpenAI lists for it (435090450), newest first (bab05076b); calls made as a Codex account carry its account id and originator (ebbaa22a0).
- The account row shows the limit with the least left (661741ecb).
- Remote hosts can log in to Codex again (c5916f15f); the headless host bundle ships the helper (fedd5a28e).
- Any signed-in account can replace the default, and sessions it cannot take wait (d6349d8c1); the session menu asks for a sign-in while the session's account is signed out (6f698c42e); moving a session from the account page moves its route for that account's provider (347dd99d8).
- A desktop run with real accounts found nine more issues. Eight are fixed:
  - A browser sign-in opens the provider's page. The page it returns to waits for the outcome and says it, also after Deny. (0062a0da2, 878c8621a)
  - "Managed sessions need you to sign in again" shows only when all of a provider's accounts are signed out. Only the sessions an account serves now count as using it. (0062a0da2)
  - Request counts are live. A key's label names its account. A Codex kind refusal names the kind. (c3a522f32)
  - The helper identity is kept twice and restored, and a replaced helper stops. Sign-in files are 0600. (bfb667494)
  - A session waiting for a sign-in gets one clear answer instead of ten retried 401s. (682f6a7d9)

  New accounts keep their generated names for now.
- A test of moving existing chat and terminal sessions (matrix in the QA comment) found these, now fixed:
  - Signing in the first account of a provider moved no idle session until its next turn or an app restart. It now moves them within about 30 seconds, and a chat whose turn-end move was skipped is tried again. (c1a05c737)
  - A terminal on screen sometimes restarted in front of the user, and text typed but not sent was lost. A terminal now moves once nobody types in it, as above. (c1a05c737)
  - A moved terminal showed "No signal" until its next message. (c1a05c737)
  - A chat waiting on a question or an approval during an app restart stopped ("The agent controller stopped") and could not be resumed: the replayed request broke its unique key. This also happened on `main`. (e92740161)
  - A side chat of a session that had not moved listed the session under the account. (c1a05c737)
  - The first sign-in said saved sessions "can use it again". It now says the sessions on this computer's own sign-in move to the account. (c1a05c737)

  A moved Codex terminal's footer drops "fast", but its requests keep the priority tier: Codex sends `service_tier` to the helper, and the helper forwards it.
- `main` took 0197 and then 0198 meanwhile, so the account migration is now 0199. `main`'s new harness pages show a managed agent's AO accounts in place of its own login.

## Known limits

- New Account strings are English in the seven other languages (two labels outside the page are translated).
- A terminal moved while it is on screen shows "Terminal ended" for about a second and is blank for about a second more, then shows its conversation again.
- Text typed into a terminal before an app restart and not sent is lost when that terminal is moved: the daemon sees typing only from its own start.
- Claude Code on an AO account shows "API Usage Billing" and turns off claude.ai connectors; both come from Claude Code when it runs on a routed token.
- Helper counting starts when this ships; today's tokens per session are held in the helper's memory and start again when it restarts.
- The low-limit warning and the "sessions moved" notice are desktop notices, not entries in AO's notification list.
- "In reserve" is applied by the app when it offers accounts; the daemon accepts an explicit choice of such an account.
- Once Claude has accounts in AO, a session runs on its AO account, also over a project's own `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. That key can be added as an API-key account.
- If both copies of the helper's identity are lost while it runs, the sessions running then need their agent restarted, because their tickets were made with keys no daemon knows anymore.
- A database that ran an earlier build of this branch: press "Make default" once per provider; accounts copied from the computer stay as accounts, so remove them and sign in inside AO; sessions started on such a build need a restart, because session tickets changed.

## Testing

On `c3eb123f2`, which merges `main`:
- Backend: `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean, and `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 reports 0 issues. `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=30m ./...` passes in every package but one. `opencodev2` fails only on this Mac: its test picks up a real OpenCode 1.19 from `~/.opencode/bin`, and its code is the same as on `main`. Three packages failed under the full run's load and pass when run alone: `claudecode` (a child that times out at 3 s), `fake` (a timing check) and `service/agent`. `service/agent` failed because of the managed catalogue test that the merge adapted.
- Helper (`GOWORK=off`): `gofmt`, build and vet are clean, it also builds for Windows, and `go test -race -p 1 -count=1 ./...` passes.
- `npm run sqlc` and `npm run api` leave no drift.
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass. `npx vitest run` passes 469 of 470 files (7,938 tests). The last file, `useBrowserView.test.tsx`, failed once under the full run's load and passes 3 of 3 when run alone; this branch does not touch it. `packages/product-ui` type-checks and its 161 tests pass.

On the final commit (`2e7a42050`, which merges `main` again): `go build ./...` and `go vet` are clean, `golangci-lint` reports 0 issues, and `go test` passes in `session_manager`, `terminal`, `service/provideraccounts`, `storage/sqlite/store`, `service/chat`, `lifecycle`, `daemon` and `domain`. `npm run sqlc` leaves no drift, `npm run typecheck` passes, and the 24 settings and terminal test files pass (432 tests). The fixes were checked again in the desktop app on old sessions made by `main`: a first sign-in in a fresh lab moved both old sessions about 20 seconds later; a terminal on screen moved; a terminal with unsent text was not moved until the text was sent; moved terminals stayed idle past the 90-second "No signal" mark; and a chat waiting on a question through a restart kept working, as did one that `main` had left stopped.

Before the review, on earlier code: 106 manual checks in the desktop app against two Claude and two Codex accounts; moving old sessions in two runs of 20 and one of 4; 49 account checks against three Claude and three Codex accounts; a real Codex reset spent from the page; and a user test run on 11 and 12 Oct (34 scenarios pass, results in the checklist comment). After review, the desktop app was run again on this branch with two Claude and two Codex accounts. The results and the issues it found are in the desktop-run comment; every fix was checked again in the app.

No release, deployment, or publish was performed.

title: feat(files): add ask in chat for selected lines
body:
Code changes: +577 -2\
Tests: +597 -0\
Others: +8 -0 (i18n strings)

## What

Highlight one or more lines in the Files review list, a file opened in the centre, or a diff opened in the centre, and an **Ask in chat** button appears at the end of the selection (also **Cmd/Ctrl+L**). It puts a `file#L2-L4` chip into the session's chat box; when sent, the chip expands to the selected code with its language tag (```` ```ts ````) or diff markers (```` ```diff ````). The user types their question after it.

The button appears only in Chat sessions (TUI sessions have no chat box).

## Why

Requested on Discord by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari: "ask questions by highlighting a line or several lines, that context is automatically sent to the agent so that we can ask questions about that line in the chat UI". Today the only line action is the gutter **+ → Send feedback**, which covers one line and sends a change request, not a question.

## How

- **Selection tracking** (`diffs/useCodeSelection.ts`): reads the selection inside Pierre's shadow root and maps it to rows. In split diffs, old-side rows keep old line numbers. It keeps the state in a small store that only the button subscribes to, because re-rendering the surface would redraw Pierre's rows and drop the selection.
- **Electron 33:** its Chromium reports a shadow-root selection as collapsed even while it holds text, so the range is built from the selection's anchor/focus points instead of `isCollapsed`/`getRangeAt`. Without this the button never appears in the desktop app.
- **Button** (`diffs/SelectionAskButton.tsx`): sits just past the selected text and follows a drag in progress, ignoring the pointer until release so it doesn't disturb the selection. It uses AO's menu surface tokens (`bg-card`, `border-border`, `shadow-md`).
- **Chip** (`lib/chat-context-bus.ts`, `ChatComposer`, `ComposerEditor`): a small bus hands the reference to the session's Chat composer, keyed by the host-scoped session key so remote AO machines work. `SessionView` brings Chat forward when asked from a file tab.
- **Gutter +:** behaviour unchanged, but it now sits beside the line number instead of 12px over the start of the code. Otherwise a drag starting at column 0 presses the + instead of selecting text. This is the only change to existing UI.

**Intentional omissions (possible follow-ups, happy to add any):**
1. An **Explain** button that sends "explain these lines" straight to the agent.
2. **Modify…** for ranges: the existing feedback box, for several lines.
3. Hiding the gutter + while text is selected, or folding it into a selection toolbar.
4. Persistent review comments that stay on the diff (bigger change).

**Notes: previous related work**
- #3492 added inline file feedback: the gutter + and **Send feedback**, modelled on GitHub PR review comments (one line, a change request sent to the agent as a message; nothing stays on the diff).
- #4252 kept that "GitHub-PR-style review flow" alongside the new file explorer.
- #5175 rebuilt the viewer on Pierre and removed the older floating selection menu (Copy / Explain / Make changes); this PR brings back selection-based asking in the Pierre viewer, scoped to Ask in chat.
- #5921 (multiple AO machines) introduced host-scoped session keys; the chip is routed through them.

## Testing

Ran the Frontend workflow's steps locally (Node 24), after installing `product-ui` and `cloud-client` dependencies as CI does:

- `product-ui`: typecheck, tests (134), pack. `cloud-client`: generate (no schema drift), typecheck, tests (26), pack. Docs build.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean.
- `npx vitest run` (full suite, 6154 tests): all pass except `browser-history-store` "caps entry count…", which times out at 20 s only under the full-suite load. It passes on its own and fails the same way on `main`.
- `npm run test:browser-postcondition-integration`: passes.
- `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 73/73 in two consecutive runs on a clean checkout.
- New e2e `e2e/files-ask-in-chat.spec.ts` (10 scenarios), run in **Chromium** and in **AO's own Electron 33** (`AO_E2E_ELECTRON=1`), ×3 in two rounds, all passing:
  - review list, file, and diff in the centre;
  - Cmd/Ctrl+L;
  - removed + added lines;
  - split-diff old side;
  - button following a drag;
  - hiding on Escape, scroll-away, and redraw;
  - plain click shows nothing;
  - gutter + still opens feedback and sits clear of the code;
  - TUI sessions show no button.
- New unit tests: chip format (language tag, diff markers, old side, fence safety, long selections), remote-host routing, selection reading (including Electron 33's collapsed selection), and the button.
- No backend changes, so the Go workflow isn't affected.

title: [Bug]: Generic tool hooks can leave Summary Activity stuck on Input needed after approval
body:
## Bug

In Summary → Activity, a session can remain **Input needed** for many minutes after a tool approval, and some harnesses can enter that status for ordinary tool use that does not require user input. `waiting_input` and `blocked` are intentionally sticky; `blocked` has a correlated-tool completion path, but generic pre-tool callbacks are classified as `waiting_input`, which does not clear on ordinary post-tool activity. For adapters without a distinct approval-resolution signal, the state may persist until a recognized resume or turn-boundary event.

**Code-path confidence:** High - the callback mappings and sticky-state behavior are present in current upstream source.

**Priority:** P2 - session status and related automated behavior can be misleading or degraded, but the session can continue and a later recognized signal can clear it.

## Reproduction

The source-level path to check is:

1. Start a session using Copilot, Cline, or Kiro etc and ask it to run a tool.
2. Observe Summary → Activity when the harness emits its pre-tool callback; those adapters route it to AO's `permission-request` event.
3. Allow the tool (or use a tool invocation that does not require an approval decision), then let the agent continue without ending the turn.
4. Check whether Activity remains **Input needed** after work resumes, until a later recognized resume/turn signal arrives.

Droid is a related potential false-positive path: its `Notification` hook has no type discriminator, so every notification maps to `waiting_input`, including its idle notification. Exact occurrence may vary by harness and approval mode.

**Expected:** Input needed is shown only while user input or a pending approval is genuinely required, and an observed approval/resumption clears it without waiting for the whole turn to finish.

**Actual:** The reported status can remain after approval, and broad pre-tool/notification callbacks can classify work as waiting for user input even when no user decision is needed.

## Root Cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitystate/activitystate.go:11-35` maps `permission-request` to `ActivityWaitingInput` without examining the hook payload.
- Copilot maps every `preToolUse` to `permission-request` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/copilot/hooks.go:76-86`). Cline does the same for `PreToolUse` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/hooks.go:60-74`), as does Kiro for `preToolUse` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/hooks.go:58-71`). Thus the event may describe an approval *opportunity*, not proof that user approval is required.
- `backend/internal/domain/activity.go:28-40` makes both `waiting_input` and `blocked` sticky and maps both to the `needs_input` status. In `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:1385-1388`, generic tool-use activity cannot demote a sticky state; blocked additionally requires a correlated completed tool or safe turn boundary (`manager.go:1244-1249,1349-1382`).
- Droid maps every `notification` to `waiting_input` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/droid/activity.go:20-38`) because the payload does not distinguish permission-needed from idle notifications.
- Cursor is **not** currently the same generic mapping: current upstream installs before/after execution hooks and evaluates permission mode (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/hooks.go:113-125`; `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/activity.go:41-66`). Its prior sticky-activity report was #3306 and was addressed by #4495.

## Fix

Audit each hook contract so an event meaning “tool is about to run” does not imply a user decision is pending. Preserve `blocked` for confirmed approval dialogs and its fail-closed correlated-tool/turn-boundary clearing. Add or use explicit approval-resolution/resume signals where the harness provides them; for harnesses without those signals, choose a state/mapping that does not falsely claim user input is required and define a safe fallback that cannot clear a genuine pending decision.

## Impact

- Summary Activity can mislead users about whether an agent is waiting or still working.
- Sticky state can remain visible well beyond approval and until a recognized clearing callback arrives.
- Code paths that suppress automation while a session needs input can delay otherwise safe automated delivery.
- Over-classifying routine tool events as user decisions can create repeated false-positive notifications.

## Related

- [#6224](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/6224) — Codex Auto-review raises `needs_input` for approvals it handles itself; adjacent harness-specific false positive.
- [#3738](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3738) — Claude Code post-Stop `agent_needs_input` notification creates sticky stale state.
- [PR #6154](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6154) — proposed fix for the Claude post-Stop notification in #3738.
- [#3306](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3306) and [PR #4495](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4495) — prior Cursor sticky-state issue and fix; current Cursor implementation uses a permission-aware path.

title: fix(chat): improve chat ui ux overall
body:
Code changes: +1349 -601  
Tests: +858 -188  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Makes chat message submission optimistic and stabilizes streaming reconciliation, so a sent message appears once, stays in place, and doesn't flicker between composer, queue and timeline states.

- Inserts user messages immediately and reconciles them in place with server state.
- Keeps queued attachments, send journals and drafts stable across remounts and session transitions.
- Preserves final assistant component identity across live-to-settled transitions and main's 50 ms streaming delay limit.
- Restores attachment-only drafts without exposing the wire payload; scopes optimistic recovery to the correct host.
- Stabilizes Working/Worked rows, timeline ordering, scrolling, composer menus and action controls.
- Workspace-unavailable recovery distinguishes definitive missing-worktree errors from transient probe failures.
- MCP startup failures are informational and shown once per session; the manual MCP Reload action is removed.
- Exposes `clientMessageId` on `ConversationMessageResponse` (`openapi.yaml`, `dto.go`, `conversations.go`, `schema.ts`) so optimistic prompts can be matched to persisted ones.

## Why

Optimistic sends flickered and could duplicate across composer, queue and timeline. This is a standalone rebuild of #6048 on current `main`, using it as the reference. It does not depend on the #6047/#6049 stack: only the `clientMessageId` API exposure is taken from #6047.

## How

- Core logic is in `useConversation.ts`, `ChatWorkspace.tsx` and `ChatComposer.tsx`.
- If renderer draft storage is unavailable, `ChatWorkspace` now mounts an in-memory composer instead of blocking the session behind a retry screen.
- `validation_error` stays in the definitive send-rejection set (now in `lib/chat-send-errors.ts`).
- Intentionally omitted from #6047: session-manager/driver recovery changes, `CHAT_RECOVERY_INCONCLUSIVE`, resume-without-history.
- `schema.ts` was edited by hand to match the generator output; CI's api-drift job regenerates it.

## Testing

Not run locally for this PR creation; relying on CI. Earlier local runs on this branch before the last rebase onto main: frontend typecheck clean for `frontend/src`, chat component and hook suites passing, `go test ./internal/httpd/...` passing.

body:

Tests: +19202 -342  
Others: +3980 -462  

## Summary

- Combine multiple paired Local hosts and Cloud on mobile, with source-qualified project/session routes, filters, badges, and actions.
- Bring Cloud sign-in, repository/project creation, orchestrator and worker spawning, Chat, Terminal, Files, notifications, PR/review actions, and the native live agent browser onto the current desktop/API boundaries.
- Preserve Local behavior, drafts, grouping, release app data, and explicit session lifecycle actions. Cloud routes never borrow a selected Local host's credentials.
- Reconcile desktop Cloud provider defaults and typed API contracts. Checkpoint the previously implemented isolated Claude/Codex native sign-in backend and phone settings; real provider approval from a phone is still unverified.
- Cloud attachments and responsive App/Mobile previews remain unavailable because the existing desktop/main Cloud contract does not support the required transport. This work does not invent or deploy those features. Existing Local attachments/previews remain supported.

## Current checkpoint — 2026-10-24

Six focused checkpoints preserve the accumulated work: organization provider defaults, deterministic setup-log test fixture, isolated native agent login, typed Cloud capabilities, Expo 57 scene compatibility, and the atomic mobile workflow integration. No local implementation plan, credentials, build outputs, run state, or unrelated `PRODUCT.md` were added.

Independent reviews covered personal Disconnect/recovery, scoped PR/review ownership, reviewer terminal targeting, browser protocol/auth/input/crop handling, account replacement, and Local regressions. All reported P2 findings were reproduced and corrected, including StrictMode load cancellation, Local-only feedback actions on a resolved Cloud route, sliding cache expiry, missing terminal browser navigation, and stale terminal callbacks. No automatic session archive/delete was introduced.

## Current validation

- Mobile: complete TypeScript check and **335 files / 3,806 tests passed**, independently run under Node 24.16.0 and Mobile CI's Node 20.20.2.
- Cloud client: deterministic contract generation, typecheck, build, package dry run, and **92 tests passed**.
- Cloud Go: formatting, build, vet, and complete `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passed. The setup-heartbeat fixture initially failed intermittently because its final newline completed the line being asserted unfinished; only the fixture changed, then 20 repeated regressions and the full suite passed.
- Native sign-in: **12 PostgreSQL integration tests passed** on the authorized disposable `ao_login_test` database, including RLS, expiry, atomic credential promotion, cancellation and shared capacity. The separate phone test database and production were untouched.
- Desktop: TypeScript and E2E TypeScript checks; **523 files / 8,963 tests passed, 7 skipped**; guarded-navigation integration and **17 native helper tests passed**. The user desktop app was not launched.
- Product UI: typecheck, build, package dry run, and **161 tests passed**.
- Whitespace and staged-artifact checks passed. Remote checks must be evaluated for this new head, not the historical results below.

## Known validation gaps — draft, not merge-ready

- The full backend suite was run twice. Build/vet and 207 packages passed, but the untouched OpenCode v2 `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects/malformed_version` fixture falls through to this Mac's installed OpenCode 1.19.2 and fails its expected error assertion. It reproduces in isolation; no implementation in that package was changed here.
- Pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 flags the existing `scriptStepMinute` duration variable name in untouched `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`. This checkpoint does not silently change unrelated main behavior to conceal the failure.
- Physical iPhone/Android testing and real Claude/Codex provider approval are deferred at the user's request. Automated tests do not prove live GitHub merge/install timing or a phone's native browser/terminal rendering.
- Windows/Linux-specific jobs, signed desktop/native packaging, clean hosted dependency installs, all real-provider/sandbox integration, and current remote CI results are not claimed locally passed. No publishing or production deployment was performed.
