title: feat: import local agent sessions with native resume
body:
Code changes: +13304 -148\
Tests: +12129 -12\
Others: +940 -0

## What

Chats you already had with coding agents on this computer can be imported into Orchestrator. An imported chat is an idle session; opening it continues the agent's own conversation in an Orchestrator worktree.

**Where to import**
- **Home, while there are no projects:** "Bring your earlier chats into AO" → **Choose folders**. The picker lists folders with chats (path, agent logos, chat count, last activity). Folders with 3 or more chats from a ready agent are preselected; the rest sit under "Other folders". Each picked folder becomes a project, and its chats are imported.
- **An empty project board:** "N earlier chats in this folder" with Review, Import and dismiss.
- **Project settings:** "Import chats…".
- **Settings > Harness > Import:** one list per agent, for picking single chats.

**Agents:** Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot, OMP, Kimchi, Qwen, Gemini, Aider, Cline, Cursor, Grok and OpenCode 1. Droid and Kimi are not offered (see Limits).

**Which chats are listed**
- Only chats active in the last 30 days. Files not modified in that window are skipped before they are read.
- A chat lands in its registered project (including linked worktrees and other clones of it), or in Standalone (chats started in the home folder or in Codex Desktop's per-chat folders). A chat from a Git repository that no project holds is listed as "<folder> (new project)"; importing it adds that folder as a project first.
- Hidden: missing, unreadable and malformed transcripts, plain (non-Git) folders, bare repositories, Orchestrator's own sessions and worktrees, deleted folders, archived Codex threads and Codex subagent rollouts.

**Importing**
- Creates idle sessions without starting an agent or creating a workspace. Imports survive daemon restarts, and never-opened imports stay off the board's lanes.
- The list shows at most the 100 newest not-yet-imported chats of each project or folder; the next 100 appear once those are imported.
- Each chat keeps all of its conversation text up to 32 MiB. Above that, the first prompt and the newest messages are kept and the chat is marked "Some text in this chat is too large to import". Agent log files up to 4 GiB are read.

**First open**
- Opening an imported chat resumes it; there is no Resume button. If its agent is signed out or not installed, a sign-in or install line replaces the composer and nothing starts.
- The workspace is created in the registered repository from the source's HEAD (a commit that exists only in another clone is fetched) and receives only what Git shows as changed: staged, unstaged and untracked files that are not ignored. The source folder is never changed. Ignored files such as `.env` come from the project's symlinks and Setup, as for any session. Standalone chats get an empty folder. If the original folder was deleted, the chat continues from the project checkout.
- The agent resumes its native conversation with the original identity, or with a verified private copy for agents that key chats by folder. Claude and Pi keep the model the chat last used (Pi also keeps its thinking level).
- The timeline shows the imported messages with their original times in place of the agent's partial replay (Claude replays only from its latest compaction).
- A chat still open in another app shows "This is open elsewhere / Close it there to continue here" with Retry, and rechecks every 30 seconds.
- Every resume-agent request now gets a 10-minute budget, because reading a large native history can take over a minute.

**Telemetry** (documented in `docs/telemetry.md`): import offer shown and scan completed (each at most once per app launch), import completed (source, counts, agents) and first open (agent, outcome, duration, error code). Only closed-vocabulary values, counts and durations are sent; no titles, paths or message text.

## Why

People already have weeks of chats with these agents on their computer. Moving to Orchestrator should not mean starting over or switching back to the agent's own app to continue one.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Earlier agent chats on this computer are invisible to Orchestrator | Listed by folder from Home, the empty board, project settings and Settings > Harness > Import |
| Continuing an old chat means going back to that agent's app | Opening the imported chat resumes the agent's own conversation in an Orchestrator worktree that carries the source's uncommitted changes |
| A chat with a 2.1 GB Codex log (tool output and screenshots) could not be read | Logs up to 4 GiB are read; the 2.1 GB one reads in 5.5 s at 96 MB peak memory |

Screenshots have not been refreshed for the current head.

## How

**Backend**
- `service/sessionimport`: discovery plus one streaming reader per agent. A scan reads each file modified in the last 30 days once per daemon run and caches the result by size and modification time. The Aider, Cursor and OpenCode readers also fingerprint the history they read; if it changed between the scan and the import, that chat fails with "scan again". Readers keep visible text only; oversized records are skimmed, and tool output and images are dropped.
- `storage/sqlite`: imported sessions and their message archive (`session_import_messages`, migration `20261103000000000`). The archive is only displayed; the agent always resumes from its own transcript.
- Session manager: adoption on first open. Agents that key chats by folder implement `AgentImportedSessionRelocator`, which prepares a private, validated transcript copy once (`importcopy.CopyOnce`); `AgentImportedSessionPreparer` lets OpenCode use its own export/import and lets Cursor publish its copy into the ACP layout for Chat. The launch folder is saved as `ImportSource.ResumeCwd`, and the workspace starts from `StartRef`.
- `service/chat/session_import.go`: shows the archive below the first Orchestrator turn.
- Ownership evidence: Codex's per-thread writer lock, Claude Code's live-session registry, then a writable transcript handle.

**Frontend**
- `lib/session-import.ts`: the scan query, batched imports and the telemetry helpers.
- `SessionImportOffer` (Home), `ProjectImportOffer` (empty board), `SessionImportDialog` (folder and project dialogs) and `SessionImportPanel` (Settings).

## Testing

- CI passes on `711051cdf1` ([run 42704679717](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42704679717)).
- Real local histories (878 chats active in the last 30 days, 6.4 GB of logs): a full scan takes 14 s and 21 s of CPU, down from 17.6 s and 38 s before files older than 30 days were skipped, and lists the same 303 chats. The largest chat held about 1.1 MiB of conversation text.
- End to end with real Claude Code 2.1.301 and Codex 0.162.1 on an isolated daemon and in the Electron app (earlier heads; the 30-day window and size limits came later):

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Claude, dirty repo: staged, unstaged, untracked, relative symlink | Follow-up recalls the code word; all files carried; source unchanged; native ID kept |
| Claude chat from a 13 GB checkout (`node_modules`, worktrees, a submodule) | Resumes in 20 s into a 738 MB worktree whose `git status` matches the source |
| Codex, plain and `.jsonl.zst` rollouts | Follow-up recalls the code word |
| Chat from a linked worktree, from a second clone, from the home folder | Lands in the project, in the registered repository, and in Standalone |
| Re-import | `already_imported`, no duplicate |
| Daemon restart before opening | Imports stay idle and readable |
| `claude --resume` / `codex resume` holding the chat | "This is open elsewhere"; connects after it closes |
| Transcript moved away after import | History stays readable with a clear error; restoring it and retrying works |
| Three concurrent opens | One workspace; the others report resume in progress |
| Largest real histories (Claude with 24 compactions, 1,772 messages; Codex in two `.zst` segments) | All messages kept with original times; both open first time |

- Live provider checks on earlier heads: Pi resumed on its original model; OpenCode recalled its first question; Cursor opened in Chat through ACP and answered from the original conversation with the source unchanged; Copilot resumed in a second folder and its tools ran there.

## Limits

- The imported history shows messages only, not the tool calls between them.
- The first scan after the app starts reads every log modified in the last 30 days (14 s for 6.4 GB here); later scans read only changed files. A chat still in use is read again on each scan.
- Codex's background app-server can keep a closed chat locked for a while (28 minutes in one test). The chat shows "open elsewhere" and resumes once Codex lets go.
- Ownership checks depend on the agent: Pi and OpenCode expose no reliable per-chat owner. On Windows, Codex's writer lock is not probed; Codex itself refuses a second writer.
- Droid is not offered: its tool folder on resume is unverified. Kimi is not offered: it runs tools in the chat's saved folder, ignoring the one Orchestrator asks for.
- A failed native resume keeps the imported history and shows the error; there is no automatic fresh-session fallback.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing the existing PR branch; history preserved with normal merges
- [x] One feature end to end
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions
- [ ] Before / After screenshots refreshed for the current head
- [x] Tests added or updated for the import behavior
- [x] CI passes on the current head
- [ ] AO review of the commits after `3e286bd1`
- [ ] Human approval, and clearing the older CHANGES_REQUESTED review

title: fix: protect setup ownership and condition project config updates
body:
Code changes: +330 -72  
Tests: +1691 -54  
Others: +101 -4 (generated sqlc/API and documentation)

## What

Pass protected session and actual workspace context to `postCreate`, and publish the returned workspace identity before setup queries its owning session.

Keep uncertain pre-controller workspaces intact after daemon failure. Replay, resume, restoration, retirement and cleanup refuse when prior setup-writer stop is unproven. Established controllers retain normal recovery.

Add a database-owned project revision and config-only conditional update so a setup/routing consumer cannot overwrite a concurrent project edit. GET exposes `revision`; config PUT accepts optional `expectedRevision` and returns `409 PROJECT_REVISION_CONFLICT` when stale. Existing clients keep their request shape; all config updates compare the validated snapshot revision atomically.

## Why

A setup hook currently receives project variables without the owning session context, and ordinary synchronous startup publishes workspace identity after the hook. A strict hook cannot verify its owner through the daemon.

Publishing earlier creates an additional recovery window. A real daemon-PID-only kill test showed that a clean, registered setup hook can survive its parent and write afterward. Clean Git status and a returned shell are not proof that prior descendants stopped.

Related work: https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6092 adds project setup configuration. This contribution addresses setup identity and early-publication recovery rather than the settings UI.

## How

- Use Manager-owned protected `AO_SESSION_ID`, `AO_PROJECT_ID`, `AO_ISSUE_ID`, `AO_DATA_DIR`, `AO_RUN_FILE` and `AO_WORKSPACE_PATH`, overriding project and inherited identity values.
- Publish the actual adapter-returned branch/path/repository with a controller-free ready-seed SQL fence. A reserved Chat generation is not established controller publication.
- Reuse durable setup/agent progress to distinguish workspace existence, unfinished setup and completed controller launch. Retry known failures without using a saved path as completion evidence.
- Preserve uncertain crash state. A narrow no-setup synchronous runtime failure is eligible for later safe cleanup only when the existing runtime-effect contract proves no external effect or successful cleanup.
- Do not convert an unowned published provisioning row into a known cancellation. Only the current Manager’s cancel-and-join can supply that completion evidence, even when startup settlement previously failed.

The conditional-update extension adds one project-revision migration using the existing revision-trigger pattern. Config SQL updates only config and reads its committed revision inside the write transaction. Explicit revision rollback/jumps refuse, including with recursive triggers enabled. CLI JSON preserves absence when talking to older daemons.

No new supervisor, native lease, auth mechanism or automatic orphan cleanup is added. Manual prior-writer identification and data preservation remain required for uncertain setup. This is a source contribution, not a released or locally deployed AO build.

## Testing

Regression evidence covers the actual Spawn/shell/SQLite path, inherited/project identity spoofing, prepared branch suffixes, failed publication, durable setup checkpoints, live-hook/background-health overlap, reserved-generation-before-publication, known-failure cleanup retries and normal recovery compatibility.

The daemon-only `SIGKILL` test independently checks the retained row, actual directory, exact Git registration, surviving hook, post-crash dirty payload, refused replay/resume/cleanup and zero provider launches. Established pending-approval recovery remains covered.

Validation on the final integrated head is recorded below before publication. Full backend runs use clean provider credential inputs, real Codex 0.146.0 matching the generated protocol and the real app-bundled tmux on PATH; no package/test exclusions. Linux/Windows remote CI remains separate from local macOS evidence.

- Integrated-head full backend suite: 193 tested packages passed, 15 packages without tests, no exclusions (`go test ./... -p 1 -count=1`). The validation context masks inherited provider keys, uses real pinned Codex/tmux, and selects Bedrock without credentials to avoid an upstream fixture probing personal first-party authentication.
- Pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2: 0 issues.
- Integrated-head `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, changed-file `gofmt`, whitespace checks, and pinned sqlc parity passed.
- Final-head focused ownership/preservation race checks and the complete session-manager race suite passed (`-timeout=30m`, no exclusions), together with the actual daemon-only preservation end-to-end test. The test harness builds its child daemon normally; no race-instrumented child-daemon claim is made. Local macOS evidence does not replace Linux/Windows CI.
- One extra full SQLite-package race run hit the default 10-minute timeout in an unchanged migration test and is not represented as green. The complete non-race backend suite and SQLite-store race checks passed.
- Independent whole-branch review and correction re-reviews found no remaining publication blocker on the final cancellation correction.
- Final CAS source: complete backend suite passed all 193 tested packages and 15 no-test packages without exclusions. The unsanitized first attempt failed inherited-credential/native-tool fixtures; the supported credential-cleared, pinned Codex/tmux rerun passed.
- Final CAS source: backend build/vet and pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 passed with 0 issues. Frontend typecheck passed after provisioning its existing locked dependencies.
- CAS regression RED/GREEN covers equal-revision concurrent writers, stale revisions after unrelated edits/archive/ABA, explicit revision resets, missing trigger startup refusal, malformed/null body preconditions, trailing JSON, committed-row reads, legacy omission, and old-daemon CLI revision absence.
- Affected project/SQLite/HTTP/CLI module and race checks passed after the monotonic-trigger/CLI corrections. The broad affected race run needed a 25-minute timeout; no module was excluded.
- Focused producer and consumer correction reviews are PASS/READY. The producer remains an unreleased source contribution; no installed application, live database, or infrastructure was changed.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from main and merged the current base without rewriting history.
- [x] One setup identity/recovery boundary; related setup UI work linked above.
- [x] Tests cover observed behavior and physical data preservation.
- [x] Final integrated validation evidence read and recorded before opening.

title: fix(session): let interface switches proceed past unsent TUI text
body:
Code changes: +20 -98\
Tests: +32 -234\
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Switching a Codex session from Terminal to Chat failed on an **empty** composer:

> AO found unsent text in the terminal composer. The source interface was left untouched; submit or clear the draft and retry, or choose Discard draft and switch

The `Ask Codex to do anything` placeholder is unchanged (bold `›` marker, SGR-dim text). The footer changed. Codex now draws two footer rows, and both contain ` · `:

```
› Ask Codex to do anything                          ← dim placeholder
  GPT-6.1-Sol ultra · Context 94% left · …          ← model/status row (truecolor, not dim)
  ? for shortcuts         ⚠ 3 warnings · f2 to view ← new hint row
```

#6041 already treats the exact `Ask Codex to do anything` text as chrome, but `codexComposerFrame` took the bottom-most ` · ` row as the footer. That put the status row inside the composer region, where it read as a human draft. #5486 fixed the earlier version of this false positive, which assumed a single footer row.

Reproduced by recording a real Codex 0.160.1 PTY stream and replaying it through the pty-host's `renderedSurface` (vt-go): the empty composer classified as `TerminalComposerDraft`. Under tmux the same screen happened to pass, because of the second bug below.

## Changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `codex/terminal_activity.go` | The composer frame ends above the whole contiguous ` · ` footer block, not just its last row. |
| `terminalui/composer.go` | Dim and bold are parsed by one `applySGR` that skips extended-colour payloads. Previously the `2` in `38;2;R;G;B` was read as SGR dim, which could make truecolor draft text look like a placeholder to message delivery. |
| `session_manager/interface_transition.go` | The `drain` policy no longer inspects the composer. An idle provider is enough to switch, and unsent terminal text is discarded. Removes `errDrainDraftPresent` / `DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT`, plus the composer-empty gate on the unstyled-runtime fallback. |
| Desktop `SessionInterfaceSwitch.tsx`, mobile `terminalInterfaceRecovery.ts` | Removes the "Discard draft and switch" recovery. "Cancel request and switch" for `DRAIN_DECISION_PENDING` and main's "Terminate and then switch" for an unverifiable source both stay. |

Product decision: a user who chooses to switch interfaces should not be blocked by text left in the TUI composer. Draft detection was a recurring source of false positives (#5486 and this one) that made the switch fail, so the drain no longer reads it.

## Intentional omissions

- Composer-draft detection stays for **message delivery** (`message_delivery.go`, `agent_switching.go`), so AO still never types into a half-written prompt. Only the interface-switch drain ignores it.
- `DRAIN_QUIESCENCE_UNVERIFIED` ("could not verify that the terminal was idle") is unchanged. It still fires when AO cannot recognise the TUI screen at all. One report showed a purple `»` prompt on Codex 0.159.1 that the Codex inspector does not match. That is a separate follow-up.
- Older persisted `DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT` transitions still show their stored error text, without the discard button. Retrying the switch now succeeds.

## Testing

- New tests: two-row Codex footer (empty → `Empty`, draft → `Draft`); truecolor draft text (semicolon and colon forms) stays `Draft`.
- Transition tests now assert that an idle draft completes the switch on both the styled path and the unstyled fallback path. Removed the four tests that only existed for draft blocking.
- Real Codex captures after the fix: pty-host surface → `Empty`; tmux capture → `Empty`; typed text → `Draft`.

**Local CI** (the machine ran out of disk mid-run: about 4 GB free, so the full suites could not complete locally):

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| Go: gofmt, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` | ✅ whole module |
| Go: `go test -race` on `codex`, `terminalui`, `session_manager` | ✅ (see flake note) |
| Desktop vitest `SessionInterfaceSwitch.test.tsx` | ✅ 23/23 |
| Mobile vitest `terminalInterfaceRecovery.test.ts` | ✅ 2/2 |
| Full `go test -race ./...`, golangci-lint v2.12.2, frontend typecheck + full vitest, mobile typecheck + test | Not run locally (no disk space). ✅ All 24 PR CI checks pass on `31e9cba`. |

Flake note: `TestInterfaceTransitionUnpromptedChatRoundTrip` hit its 3 s `awaitTransition` limit once in a `-count=5` race run of the whole package, while other race suites were running on the same machine. It passed 20/20 in isolation (`-race -count=20`). Its terminal surfaces are empty composers, and this change only lets drain accept idle sooner, never later.

title: fix(desktop): spawn AO_DAEMON_COMMAND from a real directory in packaged builds
body:
Code changes: +4 -2  
Tests: +19 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Spawn an `AO_DAEMON_COMMAND` daemon from `~/.ao` in packaged builds instead of from `app.getAppPath()`.

## Why

In a packaged build, `app.getAppPath()` returns the `app.asar` archive path. `main.ts` already notes this near its macOS bundle lookup. `resolveDaemonLaunch` passes that value as the spawn `cwd` for a configured daemon. Electron does not allow an archive path as a working directory ([asar archives: "Working Directory Can Not Be Set to Directories in Archive"](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/docs/tutorial/asar-archives.md)). So `spawn` throws `ENOTDIR` before the shell starts, and the packaged app ends up with no daemon whenever `AO_DAEMON_COMMAND` is set.

Reproduced with the app's Electron (33.4.11, `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`), using the same spawn options as `startDaemonInner` (`shell: true, detached: true`):

- `cwd` = `…/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar` → synchronous `ENOTDIR`. A wrapper script given as the command never runs.
- `cwd` = `~/.ao` → spawns normally.

Dev builds are unaffected: their `getAppPath()` is the real `frontend/` directory.

## How

- `resolveDaemonLaunch`: a configured daemon in a packaged build uses `<home>/.ao`, the same working directory as the bundled daemon. Dev keeps `appPath`.
- `startDaemonInner`: creates that directory first for a packaged configured daemon, as the bundled path already does. Without this, a fresh install could hit the same `ENOTDIR`/`ENOENT` failure.
- Identity checks are unchanged. `configured` daemons keep their existing behavior.

## Testing

- New `daemon-launch.test.ts` case: a packaged `AO_DAEMON_COMMAND` resolves `cwd` to `/Users/alice/.ao`, and the result never contains `.asar`. Test file 12/12 pass.
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` passes.
- Full `npx vitest run`: the only failures are in `browser-profile-import`/`browser-view-host`/`provider-auth-flow`. They also fail on unmodified `main` in my environment (`better-sqlite3` native bindings not built). One `browser-history-store` timeout passed 3/3 when run alone on both `main` and this branch.
- I have not exercised this in a signed packaged build.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene

title: feat: let AO workers delegate bounded work to native subagents
body:
Code changes: +15 -5  
Tests: +79 -2  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Let AO worker sessions delegate bounded parts of their assigned task to their harness's native subagents or task-delegation tools. The change applies to the desktop worker prompt and the AO Cloud worker prompt. Orchestrator prompts are unchanged.

## Why

The worker prompt currently forbids native subagents outright ("Do not use the agent runtime's built-in subagent or task-delegation tools"). The CI/review follow-up line also tells workers to ask for more AO workers *instead of* native delegation. Harnesses such as Claude Code can run several read-only lookups or disjoint sub-tasks concurrently inside one session. The blanket ban blocks that, even when the work genuinely splits. The only alternative is spawning extra AO worker sessions, which is heavier and needs an orchestrator.

## How

Desktop worker (`session_manager/prompt.go`) and cloud worker (`workerexec/prompts.go`) replace the ban with three rules:
- The worker may delegate bounded portions of its assigned task when the harness supports it. It delegates only work that actually splits, with no fan-out of serial work and no activity for its own sake.
- The worker stays responsible for integrating results, testing, reporting, and its PR/MR. Subagents get no broader authority than the session: the same scope, ownership, execution guards and approval boundaries apply.
- Parallel subagents must be read-only or own disjoint files. No two agents edit the same file concurrently.

The CI/review parallel-help lines now ask for extra AO workers only when the work needs more capacity than bounded subagent delegation provides. The no-orchestrator fallback (continue serially, report to the human) is unchanged.

Intentionally unchanged: the orchestrator templates. Their "AO workers only" lines govern the orchestrator's own implementation delegation, and an orchestrator still delegates implementation to AO workers. Standalone workers had no ban.

## Testing

- `prompt_test.go`: a new positive test for the permission rules.
- A conflict check renders every worker variant (repo + orchestrator, `WorkersRequestReview`, no repo, no repo + orchestrator, standalone) and asserts that no ban phrase remains, including "AO workers only".
- `workerexec/prompts_test.go`: the same checks for the cloud worker prompt, with and without an orchestrator.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run 'TestBuildSystemPrompt|TestSpawnWorker_IncludesReviewCIAndPlanningInstructions|TestSystemPromptGuard'` passes.
- `go test ./internal/workerexec/ -run 'TestWorkerSystemPrompt|TestBuildInteractiveInjectsSystemPrompt'` passes.
- gofmt, `go vet` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 are clean for `session_manager`. golangci-lint reports nothing in the touched `workerexec` files. Its pre-existing findings elsewhere in that package are unchanged.

title: fix(codex): find node for npm Codex during login and auth probe
body:
Fixes #6370

## Summary
When a user logs in to Codex from **Subscriptions**, AO runs `ao codex-login --executable <adapter-resolved codex>`, and that command execs codex with the daemon's inherited PATH. The Codex auth probe (`codex login status`) runs codex the same way. If codex is the npm launcher (`#!/usr/bin/env node`) and `node` isn't on the daemon PATH, login exits with `env: node: No such file or directory` (exit 127). The probe output then can't be parsed, so the status shows **Unknown**. This happens with nvm/fnm/volta node or a Finder launch, where the adapter resolver still finds codex outside PATH.

Normal sessions, the Codex app-server, and the reviewer already avoid this through `agentlaunch.AugmentRuntimePATHForLaunchBinary`. This PR applies that same augmentation to the two code paths that skipped it:

- `agentlaunch.ProcessEnvForLaunchBinary`: a small helper that returns the process environment with PATH augmented for a given binary.
- `cli.runInteractiveCommand`, used by the `codex-login` child. The managed-account "Add Codex account" terminal and `claude-login` share this helper, so they get the same fix.
- `codex.Plugin.AuthStatus` (`codex login status`).

There's no new hardcoded node path and no retry. Node discovery is the existing shared logic.

## Tests
- New: `TestProcessEnvForLaunchBinaryAddsNodeForNPMLauncher`, `TestRunInteractiveCommandFindsNodeForNPMLauncherOutsidePATH`, `TestAuthStatusFindsNodeForNPMLauncherOutsidePATH`. Each uses an npm-style launcher with node only under a fake `~/.nvm`. With the fix removed, the two end-to-end tests fail with `env: node: No such file or directory`.
- Manual: `printf '1\n' | env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ao codex-login --executable <node-shebang codex>` failed with exit 127 before the change and printed `Codex sign-in complete.` after it.
- `go test -race ./internal/agentlaunch/... ./internal/adapters/agent/codex/... ./internal/service/agentauth/...` passes. `go test ./internal/cli/...` passes once the worker's `AO_*` env is unset; `TestSpawnResolvesProjectFromCWD` fails locally only because of the inherited `AO_SESSION_ID`. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 reports 0 issues.
- `codexappserver`'s `TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` fails locally against my installed Codex version. That package isn't touched by this PR.

## Risks / follow-ups
- The fix only affects these child processes' PATH, and the change mirrors what session launches already do.
- Other harness login plans launch the agent directly in the auth terminal, without the `ao *-login` menu, and don't get this augmentation. I left them out to keep the fix scoped to the reported bug.

title: Codex sessions fail to launch when effort is set to `ultra` (Codex rejects unknown variant)
body:
## Bug

Spawning a Codex session with effort `ultra` kills the agent at launch. Codex refuses its config and exits immediately:

```
Error loading config.toml: unknown variant `ultra`, expected one of `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`
in `model_reasoning_effort`
[process exited]
```

The session page then shows the generic "TERMINAL ENDED — this terminal process ended, but the session is not marked terminated yet" strip with a Resume button. Resuming relaunches with the same bad effort and dies the same way, so the session is stuck dead.

**Source:** Discord DM report (screenshot, 2026-10-06) | **Reported by:** @nikhilachale | **Analyzed against:** `cecf04fe9` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** High — full code path traced below

## Root Cause

AO lets `ultra` through its own validation and passes it verbatim to Codex, which rejects it. Two layers, mismatched vocabularies:

1. **AO's config layer accepts `ultra`** — `backend/internal/domain/agentconfig.go:63` validates `AgentConfig.Mode` against `{"", low, medium, high, ultra}`. That enum exists for **Amp**, whose effort scale is `low|medium|high|ultra` (see `backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp.go:67`). The comment on the field says "currently Amp", but the value is stored agent-agnostically and `Effort` is not validated against the target harness at all.

2. **AO forwards it to Codex unchecked** — `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go:192` (`appendReasoningEffortFlag`) passes any non-empty effort straight through: `-c model_reasoning_effort='ultra'`. Codex only accepts `none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh` and treats the unknown variant as a fatal config error, so the process exits before doing anything.

Net effect: a value that AO's own UI/validation admits (or that a user sets via project config for an Amp project, or copies across projects) bricks every Codex spawn that inherits it, with an error that only appears in the terminal — nothing in the daemon blocks it or surfaces a clear message in the UI.

## Fix

Validate effort against the **target harness's** advertised enum at spawn/restore time:

- Reject (or remap) an effort the target adapter doesn't advertise, with a clear API/UI error: "effort `ultra` is not supported by Codex (valid: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh)".
- The model catalog already knows per-model efforts (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/claude_provider_test.go:270` shows the shape); the codex adapter should consult it or its own enum before emitting the flag.
- Alternatively, clamp to the harness default when the value isn't advertised — but an explicit error is better than silent substitution.

## Impact

- Any Codex session launched with `ultra` effort (set for Amp, or hand-edited config) exits instantly; Resume loops on the same failure.
- Reporter-facing workaround today: clear the effort override in the composer (the "Use agent effort" option) or set it to a Codex-valid value, then resume.

## Related

- [#6272](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6272) — unified effort picker (frontend-only, merged Oct 5; did not touch the Go validation or codex adapter, so it neither causes nor fixes this)
- [#6236](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6236) — open PR reworking effort pickers/persistence; worth folding the harness-aware validation into it

Code changes: +210 -24  
Tests: +563 -16  
Others: +39 -7 (generated sqlc)

## What

Keep report deliveries acknowledged when Claude Code wraps pasted input, including mixed prompts. Add regressions for the wrapper shapes and receipt handling.

## Why

Claude Code's leading `<pasted_content id="eead">` wrapper hides the `<ao-report-delivery>` envelope from the strict hook parsers. The hook records human origin without the delivery ID. Semantic acceptance then times out, the coordinator releases the claim, and the same stuck-report batch returns about every three minutes.

The open and closed issue/PR audit found no existing fix for this wrapper bug. The old Untrivial-ai repository redirects to OrchestratorInc. Current main at `30723c0be55edde1a012a4cd3d25039c43002e26` still lacks report-wrapper parsing. The original replay baseline was `6942e179517f23c490d6ef0bbbc0d96c99408426`. Related #6119 concerns Qwen batch starvation and has a different cause.

Investigated baseline `70813e6687dd9870e79b1a772961f65a893c8686`. The tests retain paste boundaries from native transcript lines 1538, 687, 659, and 1303, with unrelated report text shortened.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A prompt with a pasted report and human text kept the human checkpoint but lost the report's acceptance, so delivery timed out and retried. | The hook keeps the human checkpoint and records the report's delivery ID on the session for that runtime launch. Delivery returns once that ID is recorded. |

## How

- Normalize only a known leading Claude paste wrapper before authorship and delivery-ID parsing. Require its closing tag and preserve text after the pasted segment, including the rest of a split report envelope.
- Keep the raw prompt as the human checkpoint. Human text before or after the report keeps the turn classified as human. Record acceptance in two `sessions` columns, `accepted_delivery_id` and `accepted_delivery_launch_id`, in the same fenced activity update. Only a prompt with a delivery ID writes them, so a later human prompt can't clear them. Main's checkpoint check stays as a fallback for batches accepted before upgrade.
- Preserve main's `CoordinationDeliveryID` path and leave `ReportDeliveryID` strict. Test malformed wrappers, invalid IDs, mixed human prompts, and another agent.

Terminated-worker filtering and coordinator retry policy remain outside this fix.

title: fix(browser): block downloads until the user allows them
body:
Code changes: +191 -16\
Tests: +334 -5\
Others: +40 -0

## What

Downloads in the Browser panel are blocked until the user allows them from the Downloads list.

- **Blocked by default.** The download is cancelled before any bytes are written and shows up in the Downloads list as "Blocked · from <site>".
- **Explicit allow.** Clicking **Download** on the entry requests the file again and saves it to `~/Downloads` as before. The X dismisses the entry.
- **Single-use approval.** An approval covers one request for that URL and expires after 60 seconds, so a later automatic request is blocked again.

## Why

The Browser panel saved every download Chromium started straight to `~/Downloads`. A link opened by an agent (`ao browser open`), a page popup, or a stray click on a file URL therefore put a file on disk without the user asking for it. The reported case was a Go module zip (`v1.54.0.zip`) landing in Downloads while an agent was working on a PR.

## How

- The gate lives in the `will-download` handler in `frontend/src/main/browser-download-manager.ts`, so it does not depend on what triggered the navigation.
- A blocked request is cancelled with `preventDefault()`, not paused, so nothing touches disk. Allowing it calls `downloadURL` on the originating tab, or on its session if the tab is gone, and the approval matches only a request that starts from the approved URL (`getURLChain()[0]`), not one that merely redirects through it. It is also bound to the session, and to the tab when replayed through one, so another profile or tab requesting the same URL cannot use it.
- A repeat request is merged into an existing blocked row only when it comes from the same session and tab; another profile or tab gets its own row. An allowed download is saved under the filename shown on the approved row.
- Blocked entries have their own cap of 20 (oldest dropped first) and never evict real download history.
- Blocked entries are not written to download history, since they cannot be replayed after a restart. The toolbar's Downloads button shows its indicator dot while one is waiting.

Trade-offs for reviewers:

- A download link the user clicks themselves inside the panel also needs the extra **Download** click. Agent-driven clicks and real clicks are indistinguishable to Chromium, so exempting user gestures would reopen the hole.
- Because an allowed download is re-requested, downloads that come from a form POST or a very short-lived URL may fail after approval and need the link opened again.
- The new strings in the seven non-English locales are machine-written and would benefit from a native review.

## Testing

- `vitest`: `browser-download-manager`, `BrowserDownloadsList`, `useBrowserDownloads`, `BrowserPanel`, `preload`, `browser-view-host`, and the i18n suites pass. New cases cover block-without-saving, allow, single-use approval, redirect matching, redirect-through rejection, approval expiry, session fallback, the blocked-entry cap, and the blocked row UI.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean for `frontend/src`.
- Ran the manager in a real Electron 33 process against a local server that redirects to a zip attachment: navigating wrote nothing, allowing saved the file, navigating again was blocked again.
- Not checked visually inside the full AO desktop app; no screenshot of the blocked row.

title: feat(files): send several inline comments in one message
body:
Code changes: +354 -147  
Tests: +394 -50  
Others: +24 -0 (locale strings)

## Summary

File feedback could only hold one inline comment at a time: opening a box on another line discarded the one being written. Now each line or file picked for feedback keeps its own box open, across files, and the comments can be sent one at a time or all together as a single message.

- **Opening:** boxes with text stay open as you move to other lines or files. A box left empty still closes when another is started, so writing a single comment behaves as before.
- **Sending:** a box's send button delivers that comment only and leaves the others open. ⌘/Ctrl+Enter in any box delivers every written comment in one message, in the order they were opened, and so does the bar that appears under the files view once two or more are written ("Discard all · Send all 3"). Whole-file comments are included.
- **Cancelling:** Cancel or Esc closes only that box.
- **Failures:** comments stay open for a retry; any that already reached the agent close.

The comment box itself is unchanged; the bar is the only new element, and it stays hidden while fewer than two comments are written. New strings are in all eight locales.

## Implementation notes

- `useFileAnnotation` holds a list of open comments instead of a single target; `FileAnnotationModel` exposes `targets`, `draftFor`, and per-target `setDraft` / `cancel` / `submit`.
- Every consumer of the model renders one box per open comment: the review list, the focused diff and file views, the legacy diff rows, and the cloud equivalents.
- A box hands its text to the model on blur, and tells it when it starts or stops having text, so the bar counts and sends it without re-rendering the diffs on each keystroke.
- `formatFileAnnotationMessages` batches comments. A single comment produces the same message as before. The daemon caps a message at 4096 characters, so a batch that exceeds it spills into consecutive messages marked "message 1 of 2" rather than dropping comments. The cap is not raised here, since that is an API contract change.

## Behaviour to be aware of

- In the single-file viewer, a comment written on one file stays pending when another file is opened and goes out with the next "Send all". The number on the bar's button is the only sign of it there.
- Switching review scope or commit, or collapsing a file, still discards the comments in that view, as before.

## Tests

- New Playwright spec `e2e/files-multi-feedback.spec.ts`: three comments across two files in real Chromium; one is sent from its own box, the other two with the shortcut as one message. Passes, along with the existing `files-narrow-inspector` spec.
- Unit tests added for the batched formatter, the hook (multi-file send, empty-box closing, single cancel, retry after failure), the comment box, and the review list.
- `npm test` in `frontend`: 6230 passed. Two suites (`src/main/*`) could not load locally because the Electron binary was not installed in the worktree, and one `CreateProjectFlow` test failed in the full run and passed when run alone. Both need confirming in CI.
- `tsc --noEmit` in `frontend`: no errors in frontend sources. Local errors were limited to `packages/product-ui`, whose own dependencies were not installed.

## Known gaps

- Not exercised in the packaged desktop app.
- Cloud-session views are covered by unit tests only.
- Backend, Go lint, and the Docker-based workflow validation were not run locally; this change touches only `frontend/`.

title: fix(opencode): one configuration overlay for Terminal and Chat, and enable interface switching
body:
Code changes: +161 -61
Tests: +801 -54
Others: +4 -4 (docs)

Supersedes #3703, which @illegalcall closed with two required changes: symmetric configuration preservation, and both transition directions tested. Both are addressed here.

## What

Gives opencode a single configuration overlay shared by Terminal and Chat, and opts its adapter into `ports.AgentInterfaceHandoff` so opencode sessions can switch between the two interfaces.

## Why

An opencode session resolved **different configuration depending on which interface it ran in**. Chat applied AO's settings as an inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` overlay and left the user's own `OPENCODE_CONFIG` alone; Terminal pointed `OPENCODE_CONFIG` at a file AO generated, evicting whatever the user had selected there. opencode merges configuration rather than replacing it, and those two variables sit in different layers of that merge, so switching interfaces could silently change the provider, model, MCP servers, plugins, or permission rules a session resolved. That is the configuration-continuity break #3703 was closed for.

Separately, opencode sessions were stuck in the interface they were born in: the tab toggle reported `INTERFACE_HANDOFF_UNSUPPORTED` because the adapter never declared the handoff capability.

## How

**One overlay, built in one place.** Both surfaces now call `PrepareACPConfigContent` and deliver the result through `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`. AO no longer assigns `OPENCODE_CONFIG` at all, so a custom config path survives in both interfaces. `TestTerminalAndChatOverlaysMatch` asserts the two overlays are byte-identical across all four permission modes, so the guarantee holds by construction rather than by two call sites agreeing.

**Handoff opt-in.** `NativeConversationID` reports the plugin-observed id for a Terminal source and the persisted provider id for a Chat source. A Terminal session with no reported id yields `ok=false`, so Session Manager fails the switch closed: without that report AO cannot prove which native session the visible pane owns.

Two consequences worth reviewer attention:

- **The overlay carries standing instructions inline, so a launch no longer needs `SystemPromptFile` to exist.** That also unblocks interface-transition preflight, which builds a terminal target from the recomputed prompt with no file and previously hit a hard error. Reviewer launches still pass only the file, so the adapter reads it — mirroring `kilocodeSystemPromptText` in the Kilo adapter that bridges the same opencode-derived CLI.
- **The reviewer policy moved from `ReviewCommandSpec.Env` into the same overlay.** This widens the change into `adapters/reviewer/opencode`, which I would otherwise have left alone. It is not optional: the runtime applies an argv `env` assignment *after* the spec environment, so once both sources used `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, leaving them split would let the agent's overlay silently replace the policy that keeps a reviewer read-only.

**Not included:** `NativeConversationExists`. Unlike Claude and Codex, AO never reserves an opencode id — the plugin reports one only after opencode has created the session — so a reported id always has a conversation behind it. Adding a fourth copy of that probe would also cut against #5439, which tracks folding the existing three behind one `agentbase` helper.

## Testing

**Both handoff directions, live against OpenCode 1.18.31** (`AO_LIVE_OPENCODE_ACP=1`, gated exactly like the existing live test so CI never depends on a local install):

- `TestLiveOpenCodeTUIToChatHandoff` — launches the adapter-produced interactive command on AO's shared PTY path, reads the native session id opencode persisted, resumes it through the ACP driver, and asserts both halves that separate an adoption from a playback: `session/load` replays the terminal turn, and a follow-up prompt answers from the terminal-era context.
- `TestLiveOpenCodeChatToTUIHandoff` — the forward direction, recovered from #3703's `assertLiveTUIRestore` (that branch proved this direction but not its reverse).
- `TestOpenCodeDeclaresInterfaceHandoff` guards the capability itself, mirroring the `piacp` test that asserts Pi's deliberate absence; losing the type assertion would disable switching silently rather than fail a build.

**Manual verification in the desktop app** (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`): the in-session switch is offered, a Chat→TUI transition reaches `phase: "completed"`, the conversation carries across, and with a custom `OPENCODE_CONFIG` exported the custom file is loaded in **both** modes — confirmed in opencode's own log (`message=loading path=…`), not just inferred from UI behaviour.

**Suites:**

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` — clean for the touched packages.
- `go test ./...` — the set of failing packages is **identical to `main`** on the same machine (pre-existing environment failures: missing agent binaries, shell fixtures, file-mode assertions). I captured a `main` baseline and diffed it rather than reading the failures as new.
- `go test -race` on the three touched packages — **passes on Linux**, which is the platform the `go` workflow actually runs. It cannot run on my Windows checkout (`-race requires cgo` with no C compiler), so I verified it in WSL rather than claiming a Windows pass.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` — no findings in the touched packages. Its `goimports` complaints on this checkout are a `core.autocrlf` artifact and absent from the committed LF content.
- Frontend suites not run: no frontend files are touched.

## Note for reviewers

**#5559 changes `opencodeConfigEnvPrefix`'s signature and so does this PR** — whichever lands second will need to reconcile the permission-config work with the overlay unification. Happy to rebase onto it.

Also worth flagging: this change moves AO's overlay from opencode's custom-path layer to its inline layer, which sits *above* project config. AO only writes a session-id-namespaced `agent` entry plus `default_agent`, so a collision with a repository `opencode.json` is practically impossible — but #5559's comment reasons explicitly about repository policy staying authoritative, so I would rather you judge that than assume it.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; supersedes #3703
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (with the `-race`-on-Windows gap reported above rather than claimed)

title: Protect Changes view from huge merge-generated diffs
body:
## Summary

The desktop Changes view can become extremely slow when a branch is temporarily merged with an up-to-date `main` branch. During PR #5552 conflict resolution, the workspace Changes view displayed **2,826 files**, with approximately **+282,573 / -75,410 lines**. The UI became noticeably slow while loading and rendering the diff.

This was not an accidental 2,826-file product change. The merge commit (`7d929b589`) brought the latest `main` tree into the PR branch. GitHub correctly calculated the PR as only 9 changed files against `main`, but the workspace viewer compared the merged worktree against the old PR baseline and treated the upstream sync as a giant local diff.

## User impact

- High CPU and memory usage while scanning and rendering thousands of files.
- Significant disk I/O and file-stat work.
- Slow or unresponsive Changes view while diff contents and syntax highlighting are loaded.
- A confusing presentation: upstream/merge synchronization appears as user-authored workspace edits.

## Proposed fix

1. Detect unusually large diffs before loading file contents (for example, a file/line threshold).
2. Show a clear warning and summary instead of eagerly rendering the entire diff.
3. Load file metadata first; fetch and syntax-highlight contents only when a file is opened.
4. Virtualize the file list so only visible rows are rendered.
5. Allow an explicit “Load all” action for intentional large-diff inspection.
6. Distinguish workspace changes from PR base-to-head changes so syncing with `main` does not appear as thousands of user edits.
7. Cancel or replace stale diff scans when the workspace changes.

The highest-value safeguards are the size guard, lazy content loading, and correct separation of upstream/merge changes from actual workspace edits.

## Evidence

- Screenshot: workspace Changes showed `+282573 -75410`, `0 of 2826 viewed`.
- Merge commit: `7d929b589` (parents: original PR head `3ce4d9a78` and updated `main` `bf5550d15`).
- Final GitHub PR comparison: 9 changed files, confirming the large count was a workspace diff/visualization problem rather than the PR scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- A merge/rebase producing thousands of upstream changes does not make the app eagerly load every diff.
- The Changes view remains responsive and explains why the diff is large.
- Users can inspect individual files and intentionally opt into loading the complete diff.
- PR changes and workspace changes are clearly differentiated.

title: fix(chat): stream agent text smoothly with a per-character fade
body:
Code changes: +125 -39  
Tests: +148 -35  
Others: +3 -1

Agent text in chat arrived in blocks. This makes it stream smoothly and fade in as it appears.

## Why it was blocky

`useSmoothStreamingText` flushed its whole backlog 50 ms after each snapshot. Snapshots arrive about every 100 to 150 ms, so every burst was dumped at once and the smoothing never had time to play.

## What changed

- **Smoother drain.** Each update reveals a share of the backlog that decays over about 140 ms, at most about 30 updates a second (each update re-parses the markdown). A hidden tab, or one that skipped frames for over a second, shows the current text at once.
- **Per-character fade.** A small rehype plugin (`rehype-stream-fade.ts`) wraps newly revealed characters in a span that fades in once on mount. The spans are dropped 450 ms after the stream settles, so a finished reply is plain markdown again.
- **Bounds.** The plugin only wraps the last block, leaves a block over 4,000 characters plain, skips code, and leaves emoji as text so the emoji spacing still applies. Any error leaves the reply untouched. Reduced motion gets plain text.

## Behavior change to know about

This replaces the "burst fully visible in about 200 ms" limit from #4947. A very large burst now takes about a second or more to finish revealing. The streaming tests were rewritten for the new pacing, and the responsiveness README notes that its old burst number is superseded.

## Known limits

- When markdown restructures mid-stream (`**bo` becoming bold, a paragraph turning into a list), the affected characters fade a second time.
- I could not run the opt-in burst benchmark (`AO_PERF_BENCH`), so the new reveal time is not measured.

## Validation

Run locally on this branch: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, the full `npx vitest run`, and the renderer smoke suite (`test:e2e:renderer`).

- Two failures are not from this change. `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts` (22 tests) fails locally because `better-sqlite3` is built for a different Node ABI. The `chat-composer-text-selection` e2e test fails the same way on a clean `origin/main`.

title: bug(chat): OpenCode image input is refused through ACP but works through CLI
body:
### What went wrong?

Summary

An image attached in AO’s OpenCode Chat displays correctly, but the agent responds that its model does not support image input.

The same model identifies the same image correctly through direct OpenCode CLI. A direct ACP test also reproduces the refusal, so this has not been isolated to AO.

Agent-collected evidence

Environment

  • AO: development checkout at d7369626b58b5ffd0eb3dba3b54c33bc15063eed
  • OpenCode: 1.18.18
  • Model: omniroute/antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-low
  • OS: macOS
  • Test image: a solid red, 128 × 128 PNG
  • Tested October 7–8, 2026

Reproduction

  1. Open an OpenCode session in AO Chat using the model above.
  2. Attach the red PNG.
  3. Send: “Without using tools, what solid color is the attached image? Reply with the color only.”
  4. Compare the response with direct OpenCode CLI and direct ACP using the same model and image.

Expected

The agent identifies the image as red, consistently with the CLI result.

Actual

Path | Result -- | -- AO Chat | Reports that image input is unsupported Direct OpenCode CLI | Answers “Red” Direct OpenCode ACP | Reports that image input is unsupported

AO’s attachment preview loads correctly, including after reloading the conversation.

The direct ACP session advertises image support during initialization, but responds:

I cannot read the attached image because this model does not support image input.

Verification limits

  • AO Chat reproduced the refusal twice on October 7.
  • Direct CLI and ACP controls reproduced the difference again on October 8.
  • AO’s UI interaction was not repeated on October 8 because its browser debugging connection was unavailable.
  • This was tested with one model and provider configuration.
  • The exact cause remains unconfirmed. The direct ACP reproduction means this is not established as an AO-specific attachment bug.

Related

  • #4427 covers attachment delivery presentation and filename handling. This report concerns the different image-input results between OpenCode CLI and ACP.

title: fix(coder): require an explicit template for BYO Coder + action logging for RCA
body:
## Why

Diagnosing why **ahmad@11x** could not start a BYO-Coder session, two problems surfaced:

1. **No template could be chosen, so every session 422'd.** For a bring-your-own-Coder org, session start requires a concrete Coder template (`coder_template_required`); there is no implicit org-default. But the project-create picker (a) pre-selected an **"Organization workspace"** option (empty `templateId`) and (b) curated the list with a hard-coded `startsWith("ao-devkit")` allowlist, which **hid every BYO org's own templates** (they are not named `ao-*`). Result: the only pickable option was the empty default, the project was created with no template, and the session failed later with an opaque 422. The user deleted-and-retried 4×.
2. **The stuck tenant was nearly impossible to trace.** The access log carried only `method/route/status` — no `org_id`/`user_id` — so you could not filter the log down to one org/user to see what they did.

## What

**Commit 1 — require an explicit coder template (FE).**
- Drop the "Organization workspace" (empty) option; the picker starts unselected ("Select a template").
- Replace the `ao-devkit` allowlist with a minimal **internal-plumbing blocklist** (`ao-azure-vm*`, `ao-linux-docker*`) so a BYO org sees its own templates; exported `visibleCoderTemplates` so the gate and picker share one rule.
- Block project creation until a template is chosen: **Create disabled + hint**, plus a submit-time guard. Only applies when coder is active and templates exist.
- Tests: picker offers no default option; create is gated and the chosen `templateId` is sent on `config.coder`.

**Commit 2 — action logging for RCA (CP).**
- Stamp `org_id` (URL-scoped) on every `HTTP request complete` line → the access log is greppable by tenant.
- Structured action logs with `org_id` + `user_id` + resource id: session created, session rejected (coder-template-required), github project created, project created, provider connection saved (covers harness login and coder connect).
- Logging only; no behavior change.

## Verification

- `go build` + `go test ./internal/httpapi/...` pass.
- FE typecheck clean; `CoderTemplatePicker` + `CreateProjectFlow` suites pass (incl. new gating/no-default tests); i18n coverage + parity pass.

## Notes for review

- The internal-template blocklist is name-based and AO-specific; the cleaner long-term home for "which templates are offerable" is the backend lister (follow-up). This change unblocks BYO without regressing AO's own picker.
- Per-org BYO Coder itself is already implemented on main/prod (#6165); this only fixes the template-selection UX and adds logging — **no provisioning changes**. Worth a staging smoke-test against a real BYO Coder before relying on it in prod.

title: fix(coder): restore codex + cursor-agent harnesses on the dev-kit template
body:
## Problem

Codex (and cursor) sessions on the Coder **dev-kit** template hang at "Preparing your repository and agent." Worker log from an SSH'd workspace:

```
codex harness binary "codex" is unavailable: exec: "codex": executable file not found in $PATH
```

The dev-kit image (`cloud/coder/Sandbox.Dockerfile` -> `ao-coder-workspace:local`) baked only claude-code + claude-agent-acp + opencode. codex and cursor-agent were never installed, so those harnesses had no binary. (`coder-azure-vm` bakes all four, which is why codex works there.)

While verifying the fix, opencode also turned up intermittently missing from fresh dev-kit workspaces, confirming the host-local image is unreliable (known image-pipeline gap), so the startup now guarantees every harness rather than trusting the baked image.

## Fix

Covers all four supported harnesses plus the ChatUI path:

- **`coder/main.tf` startup_script** - install `codex`, `cursor-agent`, and `opencode` at workspace start when the image lacks them, and ensure `claude-agent-acp` (the ChatUI ACP bridge for claude - the only harness whose ACP is a separate npm package; opencode and cursor speak ACP via their own CLIs). Each install is idempotent (skipped when present) and non-fatal (a failed optional install never blocks the workspace). Deployable without an image rebuild because the dev-kit templates reuse the existing approved host-local image.
- **`Sandbox.Dockerfile`** - also bake codex + cursor-agent (versions in lockstep with `scripts/bake-coder-azure-image.sh`) so the next image rebuild carries all four permanently and the startup installs become no-ops.

## Verification

Throwaway dev-kit workspaces, all four resolve on PATH:

```
claude:        2.1.228 (Claude Code)
codex:         codex-cli 0.147.0
cursor-agent:  2026.08.11-e8db854
opencode:      opencode v2.0.24
```

Both templates (`ao-devkit`, `ao-devkit-large`) re-pushed to prod Coder with the startup installs live.

## Scope note

This is a Coder-template change (deployed via `coder templates push`), not a control-plane change - there are zero `cloud/internal` edits. The control plane already supports all four harnesses (registered in `workerexec`, credential types in `httpapi/harness_spec.go`); the only gap was the dev-kit workspace binaries.

title: fix(chat): stop queue flashes, bubble replays and scroll jumps on send
body:
## What users saw

- Send a message to an idle agent and it briefly showed up in the queue dock, then came back to the chat.
- The user bubble played its send animation twice.
- Sending from the bottom of a long chat snapped the view up and left it short of the end.
- Queuing behind a running turn looked like a normal send first, then jumped to the dock.

## Causes and fixes

**Queue flash.** The daemon saves every send as `queued` and moves it to `running` 25 to 130 ms later. A snapshot in that gap made an idle send look queued. I reproduced it: 5 of 5 sends showed a `queued` snapshot. Snapshots (session and review chats) now report the turn being dispatched as `running`. A turn that really waits behind another stays `queued`. The marker is cleared on any send that does not dispatch, so a failed dispatch cannot leave a turn stuck as running.

**Replayed bubble.** The renderer dropped `clientMessageId` when it mapped daemon messages, so the optimistic echo and the daemon row never shared a key and the row remounted. The daemon now returns `clientMessageId` (one optional field in `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`). The item, group and run keys use it, and the enter animation is tracked by that key.

**Scroll jump.** A new turn in a long chat is measured in steps. For a moment the rendered content still carried the 600px estimate, the prompt spacer was sized from it and collapsed to 0, and the browser clamped `scrollTop`. The scroll handler then read that as the reader leaving and cancelled the glide. The spacer now waits until the rendered height matches the virtualizer total. This bug was already on `main`: I reproduced it with all of my renderer changes reverted.

**Queued sends.** A send made behind a running turn is tagged queued and goes straight to the dock as an inert row (no steer, edit, delete or drag until it has a turn id). It hands over to the real row under the same key.

Smaller changes:
- The draft is hidden while a plain send is in flight and comes back after 3 seconds if the daemon has not answered. The send request has no timeout, so this keeps a stuck send from looking like a lost draft.
- The "Sending" note on the optimistic bubble is gone.
- The send animation rises from 16px below instead of scaling.
- The first send in an empty chat no longer makes the composer jump. The welcome heading used to vanish at once while the dock kept its place, so the composer lost 64 px in one frame (409 to 345) before sliding down. The slide now starts from the composer's own position and the heading fades out in place over 150 ms.
- Two log lines in the controller: one when a send is queued behind a busy controller, one when a turn-completed event is ignored because its provider turn id does not match. I could not reproduce the "queued while idle" report from the busy path, so these are for the next time it happens.

## How I checked it

I drove the real Electron window over CDP and traced each symptom before and after.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Idle send shows a `queued` snapshot | 5 of 5 sends | 0 of 10 sends |
| Scroll after a send from the bottom | view jumps up 222 to 240 px, ends 420 to 438 px short | never moves backwards, ends at the end (gap 0 px) |
| Queued send | chat bubble at 111 ms, dock at 394 ms | dock row at 70 to 80 ms, no chat bubble |
| Message sent mid-turn | queued | still queued |
| Spacer while a long reply streams | n/a | shrinks 400 to 0, view stays pinned |
| Composer top on the first send of an empty chat | 409, then 345 in the next frame, then slides to 711 | 409, then slides smoothly to 711 |

Tests added:
- Go: four tests on the real `Service` that take a snapshot in the gap right after the row is saved as `queued`. They cover an idle send reading `running`, a send behind a running turn staying `queued`, and the marker lifecycle (kept after a good send, ignored for duplicates, cleared on a failed dispatch). A DTO test checks `clientMessageId` is returned. I checked that breaking the overlay or the cleanup makes the right test fail.
- Frontend: echo and durable row share one node, queued send shows in the dock and not the chat, `toSnapshot` keeps `clientMessageId`, the draft hides and comes back on failure and on a stalled send.

`go test` for `service/chat` and `httpd/...` passes. Frontend chat and conversation suites pass (921 tests). `tsc` is clean for `frontend/src`.

## Review notes

Five independent reviews of this diff (daemon concurrency, frontend identity and queue, scroll and composer, API consumers, test quality) found no P0. The two P1s are fixed in this PR: the stuck marker after a failed dispatch, and the hidden draft on a stalled send.

Known and left alone, all cosmetic or narrow:
- A queued message plays its entrance animation when it is queued instead of when it joins the chat.
- Older remote daemons that do not send `clientMessageId` fall back to the old matching and remount once.
- A duplicate-send response can release the echo a moment before the real row is cached.
- With more than one queued message, a collapsed dock hides a just-sent pending row.

Mobile and the `ao` CLI do not use the changed fields. I read both, did not run them.

title: fix(settings): load cloud project settings from the control plane
body:
## Problem

Opening **Project settings** for a cloud project hangs on "Loading project settings…" and surfaces "Unknown project". A customer using bring-your-own Coder reported it, and I reproduced it on the released nightly `0.13.5-nightly.202610072244` (which includes #6401).

The cause: the settings dialog always reads the project from the local daemon (`ProjectSettingsForm` → `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}`). Cloud projects live only in the control plane, so the daemon answers `404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND – "Unknown project"`.

This also left template-less cloud projects (created before #6401) without a visible explanation. Their sessions are rejected with `coder_template_required`, and the one place you'd look at the project wouldn't open.

## Fix

- **`SettingsDialog`** identifies a cloud project the same way task creation already does: no remote host, and the ID appears in `useCloudProjectsQuery`. It then renders a cloud settings view. Only the General section is shown; Agents, Environment and Cues are local-daemon features. While the cloud project list is loading, the dialog shows the loading state instead of falling through to the daemon. The local form is used only for a project the local daemon actually lists. If the cloud lookup fails for any other project, the dialog shows the error with a Retry action instead of a misleading "Unknown project". Local and remote projects are unchanged.
- **New `CloudProjectSettingsForm`**, built from the shared `@aoagents/product-ui` settings rows:
  - Project name and default branch are editable and autosaved via `PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/projects/{projectId}`. It uses the same 650 ms debounce, validation and rail save state as local projects.
  - Type and repository are shown read-only.
  - The **Coder template** is shown read-only, resolved to its display name, plus machine size when set. With no project template, the row shows **"Default template"** (the deployment or org default applies; non-Coder providers need none). It shows a blocking warning only for a bring-your-own-Coder org with no org-default template, the one case the control plane rejects with `coder_template_required`.
- Six new strings, added to all 8 locales.

## Not in scope

- Changing the template of an existing cloud project. The control plane's `PATCH` only accepts `displayName` and `defaultBranch`, so this would need a CP change and deploy. It's left as a follow-up.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- New `CloudProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx` covers:
  - details and the template name
  - the missing-template warning
  - the rename autosave call
  - that an empty branch is not saved
- `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` covers:
  - a cloud project renders the cloud form, with only General
  - the loading state while the cloud list resolves
- Targeted run, `vitest` on Node 24: 4 files, 48/48 pass, i18n parity and literal coverage included.
- Full frontend suite: the only failures are in `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`. They're environmental (the `better-sqlite3` native ABI was built under Node 22, tests ran on Node 24) and unrelated to this change.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Verified in a running app:** a dev Electron build of this branch, signed into production, opened Project settings for a real cloud project (`ao-landing`). Before the fix the same dialog hung on "Loading project settings…". It showed name, type (Cloud project), repository, default branch, Coder template (`ao-azure-vm-staging`) and machine size, with only the General section. Renaming in the UI autosaved to the control plane (confirmed via `GET /projects`), then I reverted it. The missing-template warning is covered by unit tests only.
- Note: staging could not be used. On `main` the CP allows the GitHub App only in production (`cloud/internal/config/config.go:552`), so staging exposes no `/github/*` routes and no cloud project can be created there. That's pre-existing and out of scope.
- If a user is signed into cloud, project settings for local projects briefly show the loading state until the cloud project list resolves. The list is usually already cached by the sidebar.
- Follow-up: let users set or change the Coder template on an existing cloud project (CP `PATCH` plus UI).

title: [Bug]: AO sessions create claude.ai Docs artifacts instead of local AO artifacts
body:
## Summary

When a user asks an AO session to "create a document", the agent creates a **claude.ai Docs artifact** (via the Claude Docs MCP connector) instead of a **local AO artifact** under the session's artifact directory (`~/.ao/data/artifacts/<session-id>`). This violates AO's "Session Artifacts" rule, which requires non-PR deliverables to be written as local files in the AO artifact directory.

## Root Cause

Two instruction sources conflict, and the connector instructions win:

1. **AO worker standing instructions ("Session Artifacts")** say every non-PR deliverable must be a local file under `~/.ao/data/artifacts/<session-id>`. This assumes the deliverable *is a local file* and only governs *where the file goes*.
2. **The Claude Docs MCP connector instructions** (injected as "MCP Server Instructions") aggressively say to make a doc there "not a local file, even when coding" when the user asks for one, and to make it FIRST — "a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan."

The word "document" triggers the connector reflex, which explicitly overrides "local file" before AO's rule is even considered. The AO prompt never says "do not use the Claude Docs connector / do not create claude.ai artifacts," so there is nothing to out-rank the connector.

## Impact

- AO deliverables leak to claude.ai instead of staying local under `~/.ao`, breaking the artifact model and the publishing-scope / local-only guarantees.
- The gap is **not just in the top-level worker**: spawned subagents (Plan, Explore, general-purpose, etc.) start with fresh system prompts that do **not** include the "Session Artifacts" rule but **do** load the same MCP connectors — so the Claude Docs reflex fires there too, with no AO guardrail at all.

## Proposed Fixes (strongest first)

1. **Disable the Claude Docs connector for AO execution contexts.** Don't load `mcp__claude_ai_Claude_Docs__*` when `AO_SESSION_ID` is set, for workers *and* all spawned subagents. If the connector isn't present, the reflex cannot fire — no instruction-precedence battle. Most reliable.
2. **Inject an AO context header into every agent's system prompt** (worker + subagents) explicitly redefining "document" as a local file under the AO artifact dir and forbidding external document connectors (Claude Docs, Google Drive) for AO deliverables. Flexible, but still subject to instruction-precedence against the aggressive connector reflex.
3. **MCP context detection at the tool layer:** when a connector detects `AO_SESSION_ID`, refuse to create external artifacts (or redirect to the AO dir). Most robust but needs harness support.

Recommended: ship (1) as the real fix; optionally add (2) as defense in depth. (2) alone is fragile because the connector instructions are written to beat competing guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In an AO session, asking the agent to "create a document" produces a local file under `~/.ao/data/artifacts/<session-id>`, never a claude.ai Docs artifact.
- The same holds for subagents spawned within the AO session.

title: bug(chat): OpenCode command activity does not show nonzero exit codes
body:
### What went wrong?

### What went wrong?

In an OpenCode Chat session, a shell command exiting with code `7` is shown as completed without an exit-code indicator.

The command output is available, and the agent can explain the failure, but the activity card does not show the nonzero result.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an OpenCode session in AO Chat.
2. Ask the agent to run only `printf AO_TEST_ERROR; exit 7`.
3. Inspect the command activity card.

### Expected behavior

The command activity shows `exit 7`, distinguishing successful execution from a command that finished with a nonzero exit code.

### Environment

- AO: development build at `d7369626b`
- OpenCode: `1.18.18`
- Model: `gemini-3.1-pro-low`
- macOS

### Notes

Verified that OpenCode sends the exit code through ACP in `rawOutput.metadata.exit`. AO preserves the output text but drops the exit code when building the command activity details.

A focused fix and regression coverage are prepared. The regression fails against the original implementation and passes with the fix.

title: fix(chat): preserve OpenCode command exit codes
