title: [Bug]: Cline PreToolUse maps to sticky Input needed (false/inverted after upstream #7446)
body:
## Bug

Cline TUI sessions can show Summary → Activity as **Input needed** for ordinary tool use, or remain sticky after the user already approved. AO installs Cline `PreToolUse` as `permission-request`, and `StandardDeriveActivityState` maps that to sticky `waiting_input`.

**Related:** parent family bug [#6280](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6280) (Copilot / Cline / Kiro). Copilot will be fixed separately via observe-hooks . This issue tracks **Cline-only** follow-up.

**Code-path confidence:** High on current main (hook install + mapping). No separate live TUI recording attached here; behavior follows from the same path called out in #6280.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Cline TUI session and run a tool (interactive approval or auto-approve).
2. Observe Activity when AO’s `PreToolUse` wrapper runs (`ao hooks cline permission-request`).
3. After Approve (interactive) or while tools run under auto-approve, check whether Activity is **Input needed** and stays until `TaskComplete`/`TaskCancel` (`stop`) or the next `UserPromptSubmit`.

**Expected:** Input needed only while a human decision is actually pending; clear when work resumes after approval.

**Actual:** Every managed `PreToolUse` enters sticky `waiting_input`. After upstream [cline/cline#7446](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/7446) (**merged** 2025-11-13), when approval is required `PreToolUse` runs *after* Approve — so the AO mapping is **inverted** for that path. With auto-approve, `PreToolUse` still fires with no human prompt → ordinary false positive. #7446 fixed Cline’s hook UX; it does not break Cline, but it makes AO’s mapping worse for interactive sessions.

## Root cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/hooks.go` — `PreToolUse` → `permission-request`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitystate/activitystate.go` — `permission-request` → `waiting_input` (sticky; `NeedsInput`).
- AO does not install a Cline post-tool clear for this path; clear is mainly `TaskComplete`/`TaskCancel` → `stop` or next `UserPromptSubmit`.
- Terminal detector exists (`DetectTerminalActivity`) but deliberately ignores the approval fixture (`tool_approval.txt`), so it does not recover genuine approval UI today.
- Copilot-style (`notification.permission_prompt` / typed `permissionRequest`) does **not** transfer: Cline’s hook contract is cancel-oriented, not Copilot’s ask/allow + typed permission notification shape.

## Fix direction

1. Stop mapping `PreToolUse` → `permission-request` / `waiting_input` (treat as active / tool-use).
2. Restore real Input needed ,teach the terminal detector to recognize approval chrome, and/or use ACP Chat approval events if/when Cline Chat is available ([#5604](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/5604)).
3. Remap-only without (2) would hide pending approvals in TUI until observation exists - same tradeoff as closed AO PR #2594 for the family.

title: [Bug]: Kiro preToolUse maps to sticky Input needed with no approval observation path
body:
## Bug

Kiro TUI sessions can show Summary → Activity as **Input needed** for ordinary tool use and keep that status sticky until a turn-boundary-style clear. AO installs Kiro `preToolUse` as `permission-request`, and `StandardDeriveActivityState` maps that to sticky `waiting_input`.

**Related:** parent family bug [#6280](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6280) (Copilot / Cline / Kiro). Copilot will be fixed separately via observe-hooks . This issue tracks **Kiro-only** follow-up.

**Code-path confidence:** High on current main (hook install + mapping). No separate live TUI recording attached here; behavior follows from the same path called out in #6280.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Kiro TUI session and invoke a tool (interactive approval via Kiro’s permission UI, or an auto/trust path).
2. Observe Activity when AO’s `preToolUse` hook runs (`ao hooks kiro permission-request`).
3. After the tool is allowed / while tools continue, check whether Activity remains **Input needed** until `stop` or the next `userPromptSubmit`.

**Expected:** Input needed only while a human decision is actually pending; clear when work resumes after approval.

**Actual:** Every managed `preToolUse` enters sticky `waiting_input`, including tools that never need a human decision. There is no AO terminal waiting-recovery path for Kiro today.

## Root cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/hooks.go` — `preToolUse` → `permission-request` (`ActivityWaitingInput`).
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitystate/activitystate.go` — name-only sticky `waiting_input`.
- Managed hooks are `agentSpawn`, `userPromptSubmit`, `preToolUse`, `stop` — no post-tool clear; no typed permission-notification hook like Copilot’s `notification.permission_prompt`.
- No `DetectTerminalActivity` implementation for Kiro.
- Real approvals are owned by Kiro’s `permissions.yaml` / interactive UI (and PreToolUse can block via exit `2`); AO’s install does not expose a Copilot-like ask/allow observe contract.

## Fix direction 

1. Stop mapping `preToolUse` → `permission-request` / `waiting_input` (treat as active / tool-use).
2. Restore real Input needed ,add terminal approval detection, and/or use ACP Chat approval events if/when Kiro Chat is available ([#5604](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/5604)).
3. Remap-only without (2) would hide pending TUI approvals until observation exists — same family tradeoff as closed AO PR #2594.

title: fix(cloud): drain the GitHub webhook queue with workers and drop untracked repos
body:
Code changes: +122 -6  
Tests: +242 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

On production, PR status in cloud sessions could stay **"Status unavailable / Checks unavailable" for ~40 minutes** after AO opened a PR (observed on `Pritom14/BusinessManagement` #3: created 21:02 UTC, first refresh 21:43 UTC).

The webhook was delivered and accepted (HTTP 202) but sat in the queue:

- GitHub sends SCM events for **every repository an installation can see**. An install with "All repositories" delivers push / check_run / status / review traffic for dozens of repos that have no AO project or PR, and every one was queued.
- The queue was drained by **one worker processing at most one delivery per second** (`time.NewTicker(time.Second)` around a single `processNext`). Production received ~1–2 deliveries/s, so the backlog grew and a new PR's events waited behind unrelated traffic.

## Fix

Two changes, cloud SCM only:

1. **Filter before queueing** — `EnqueueVerifiedWebhook` drops SCM events (`push`, `check_run`, `check_suite`, `status`, `pull_request*`) for repositories that no organization routed through the installation tracks: no project on the repo, no recorded pull request in it, and no worker branch refs for it (`GitHubRepositoryTracked`). The receiver acknowledges them with 200 and stores nothing.
   - Installation events (`installation`, `installation_repositories`) always queue.
   - A failed tracking lookup **queues the event anyway**, so a database hiccup can never drop an event that matters.
2. **More workers** — `Run` starts 8 workers that drain the queue back to back and pause (1s) only when it is empty. `ClaimGitHubWebhook` already leases rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and keeps installation events in receipt order, so workers never share a delivery or reorder routing changes.

Not changed: GitHub API usage per event (the same refresh runs, just sooner), migrations, config, frontend, or the local daemon.

## Testing

- New unit tests (`githubapp/webhook_queue_test.go`): untracked repos are dropped for every SCM event type; tracked repos queue; installation events queue without a lookup; a failed lookup still queues; a 24-delivery backlog drains concurrently in ~0.16s (24s with the old loop); an empty queue does not spin.
- New PostgreSQL integration test (`postgres/github_webhook_tracking_test.go`, run with `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL`): a project's repository is tracked; a repository with no project and an unrouted installation are not.
- Full `cloud` `go test ./...` passes. With a real database, two pre-existing `internal/postgres` tests fail identically on unmodified `main` (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestMigrateInterfaceHandoffFromMainVersion`) and are unrelated.
- Live check against a local control plane built from this branch, fresh database, signed with the real GitHub App webhook secret:
  - 40 webhooks for an untracked repo → HTTP 200, **0 queued**
  - 6 webhooks for a tracked repo → queued and **processed within 3s**
  - installation event → queued
  - burst of 150 tracked-repo webhooks → **all processed 0.75s after the first send**, no errors

`gofmt` and `go vet` are clean; `golangci-lint` was not available locally, so CI's lint job is the first lint run.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Refresh a PR immediately after AO opens it, and don't treat the insert-time `observed_at` default as an observation (the false "unavailable" window before the first refresh).
- Coalesce repeated refreshes for the same PR, reuse installation tokens, and back off per installation on GitHub rate-limit headers.

title: fix(agentauth): open Pi's login picker automatically
body:
## Summary
Pi has no `login` subcommand, so Settings → Harness → Log in to Pi launched the bare Pi TUI and held `/login` behind an **Open login** button in the terminal header. Users saw only Pi running in the PTY and no login flow.

This switches Pi to the daemon-side auto-input path Kimi already uses: the auth terminal launches `pi`, and the daemon types `/login` once Pi renders a ready marker:
- Pi's footer context stat `0.0%/` (primary). A fresh Pi session always renders it, with or without a selected model and with `quietStartup` on.
- Pi's startup onboarding line `Pi can explain its own features` (secondary).

If neither marker appears within the 10 s ready wait, the daemon still sends `/login` as long as the terminal is alive (new opt-in `SendInitialInputOnReadyTimeout`, used only by Pi). Pi no longer returns `terminalInput`, so the Open login button doesn't render for Pi. Droid, OMP, Prime Agent, Gemini, and Qwen keep the button flow. Kimi keeps marker-only behavior.

## Changes
- `agentauth/plans.go`: `piLoginPlan()` with `initialInput`, ready states, and the timeout fallback
- `agentauth/service.go`: pass the fallback flag to the terminal opener
- `shellterm`: `MatchInitialInputReadyState` (exported matcher used by the ready loop), an opt-in send-on-timeout fallback that skips exited terminals, and an injectable ready timeout for tests
- Tests:
  - Pi markers matched against captured Pi 0.85.1 screens: default startup, `quietStartup` with and without a model, still loading
  - shellterm fallback: opt-in, default-off, and exited-terminal paths
  - the button-flow service test moved from Pi to Droid

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/service/agentauth/ ./internal/service/shellterm/` passes. On Windows, the Kimi trust test fails on unchanged `main` too (HOME isolation), and it's unrelated.
- Verified end to end against a dev daemon with Pi 0.85.1:
  - default startup, model selected: the login picker opened automatically
  - `quietStartup: true` with a model selected (no header): the login picker opened automatically

## Risks
- Pi accepts typing during startup but ignores Enter until startup finishes, and the markers render slightly before that. AO relies on the runtime's ~300 ms pause before Enter. On a very slow first run, while Pi downloads `fd`/`rg`, `/login` can stay in the editor unsubmitted, and the user presses Enter.

title: fix(agentauth): open Copilot's native /login account picker
body:
Code changes: +146 -1  
Tests: +172 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary
Clicking **Login** for GitHub Copilot ran `copilot login`, which always starts the GitHub.com browser flow. Copilot's account picker (GitHub.com / GitHub Enterprise Cloud `*.ghe.com` / Microsoft Entra) only exists behind `/login` in the interactive TUI, so users on GHE or Entra could not pick their account type.

This follows the same pattern as the Kimi fix (#5651):
- **`agentauth/plans.go`**: the Copilot plan now launches the `copilot` TUI and injects `/login` once the composer footer renders. If slow hook and skill loading delays that footer beyond the bounded readiness wait, AO verifies that the PTY is still alive and sends `/login` through the existing timeout fallback.
- **`adapters/agent/copilot/trust.go`** (new): Copilot's "Confirm folder trust" dialog would swallow the injected input in AO's private auth workspace, so the workspace's symlink-resolved path is added to `trustedFolders` in `$COPILOT_HOME/config.json` (default `~/.copilot/config.json`), which is what Copilot records for "Yes, and remember this folder". The `//` comment header and other keys are preserved, the write is idempotent, and unsupported config shapes are left untouched (Copilot then asks for trust interactively).
- **`shellterm/service.go`**: full-screen TUI readiness checks now fall back to AO's rendered terminal surface and normalize ANSI styling before matching. This is required on the native PTY host, where Copilot renders the visible `/ commands` footer with styling that splits the raw byte sequence.

## Testing
- Manual, isolated Electron PR lab: clicking Copilot Login automatically opened the three-option picker (`GitHub.com`, `GitHub Enterprise Cloud (*.ghe.com)`, and `Your organization (Microsoft Entra)`) in both live PTYs, including after startup exceeded the readiness wait.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/copilot ./internal/service/agentauth -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/service/shellterm -run 'Test(OpenCommandTerminal|MatchInitialInputReadyState)' -count=1`
- `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.13.2 run --path-mode=abs --timeout=10m` (`0 issues`)
- `go build ./...`

The full `npm run lint` test phase was also attempted locally, but this machine's highly parallel run hit unrelated CLI-probe timeouts plus environment-dependent tmux and installed-Codex protocol conformance failures before reaching the lint phase. The affected packages above pass independently, and the linter passes when run separately; remote CI remains authoritative for the complete suite.

## Notes / risks
- The timeout fallback uses the existing terminal-alive guard, so it does not inject `/login` into a PTY that exited during startup.
- Not addressed here: `copilotConfigAuthStatus` parses `config.json` without stripping Copilot's `//` header, so that auth-status check likely never succeeds and falls back to `gh auth`.

On the Harness settings page, Qwen's setup flow showed the **Connect a Provider** heading, but its three options (Alibaba ModelStudio, Third-party Providers, Custom Provider) and the next-step provider list didn't render. It happened in both dark and light mode.

title: fix(chat): stop opening turn-diff files outside the session workspace
body:
Fixes #6422

## Summary
Claude Code reports absolute paths in turn diffs, including files it writes outside the session workspace (for example its auto-memory notes under `~/.claude/projects/…`). Clicking one of those rows in the turn's **Files Changed** card opened a file tab that could never load. The tab showed only "workspace path must be relative".

- **Daemon:** the conversation snapshot now checks each absolute turn-diff path against the session's real workspace root (`Metadata.WorkspacePath`):
  - A path inside the workspace gets a new `workspacePath` field with its workspace-relative form.
  - A path outside it gets `outsideWorkspace: true`.
  - Relative paths, and snapshots where the root is unknown (reviewer chats), are unchanged.
  - Nothing new is persisted, and the daemon's workspace confinement is unchanged.
- **Renderer:**
  - The Files Changed card opens `workspacePath` directly when it's present.
  - Rows flagged `outsideWorkspace` stay readable but aren't offered as a click. They are `aria-disabled` and still focusable, and their tooltip shows the full path plus "Outside this session's workspace".
  - Older daemons and cloud sessions keep the current behaviour.

## Not included (follow-up)
A chat markdown link to an absolute path that isn't in the workspace file list goes through `explicitWorkspaceFilePath` and can still open the same kind of broken tab. That path deliberately accepts link-shaped paths for new files that aren't yet in the catalog (#5119), so changing it is a separate decision. Evidence is on the issue.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers/ ./internal/service/chat/`: these cover inside, outside, sibling-prefix and relative paths, and check that the snapshot carries the session's workspace root.
- `vitest` across `components/chat`, `hooks/useConversation` and `lib/turn-file-open-path`: 923 tests pass. New cases check that the relative path opens and that outside rows are inert and show the tooltip.
- Typecheck shows no errors in the touched files.
- **Real Electron app**, run in isolated mode with a daemon built from this branch and driven over CDP. A real Claude Code chat session wrote `/tmp/…` and `notes/inside-note.md`:
  - The snapshot returned `outsideWorkspace: true` and `workspacePath: "notes/inside-note.md"`.
  - Clicking the outside row opened no tab and showed no raw error.
  - Hovering it showed the path and "Outside this session's workspace".
  - Clicking the inside row opened `notes/inside-note.md` with its content.

## Risks
- The prefix check is purely lexical (`filepath.Rel` + `IsLocal`). If a provider reports a path through a symlinked alias of the workspace, the file would be flagged as outside. In that case the row is inert, which is the same result users get today.

title: feat(telemetry): identify on AO Cloud sign-in, identity on every event, in-app opt-out
body:
Code changes: +1645 -64  
Tests: +2245 -22  
Others: +206 -30

## What

Implements "Minimal changes" 1-6 from the telemetry audit, plus the opt-out the identity rules require.

- **Identify on AO Cloud sign-in.** Desktop calls `posthog.identify(<AO Cloud user ID>, { email, ao_cloud_user_id, github_login })`. An unbound install starts with its anonymous `ins_` ID and joins that history on first sign-in. A previously bound install starts with a fresh anonymous ID to avoid merging another account. Signed-in daemon events use the AO Cloud user ID directly. Only the production WorkOS provider is identified, not the dev-only local one.
- **Email only from the signed-in AO Cloud account**, set as a person property on sign-in and later signed-in launches. It is never stamped on events, read from git config, or sent to the daemon or phone (they get only the opaque user ID). Tests assert this at each layer.
- **GitHub login at daemon start.** Background resolver (bounded retries) stores the authenticated human login on the daemon's telemetry identity. The renderer reads it from the daemon with bounded retries.
- **`github_actor` + `ao_cloud_user_id` on every daemon and renderer event** (daemon event properties, renderer super properties).
- **Mobile adopts the desktop identity.** New authenticated `GET /api/v1/telemetry/identity` (outside `/api/v1/mobile`, so reachable over the LAN socket). The phone identifies only a signed-in AO Cloud user ID. It keeps an anonymous install ID anonymous and honors the opt-out. Mobile switches to `personProfiles: "identified_only"`.
- **Version on every daemon event.** The daemon receives its binary build version explicitly and uses it when `AO_TELEMETRY_APP_VERSION` is unset. See risks: release tooling does not stamp `cli.Version` yet.
- **New events:** `ao.app.installed` (daemon, first run of a fresh install only), `ao.onboarding.step_viewed|completed|abandoned` (desktop, steps `welcome` and `github_auth`, once per install each), `invite.sent` (cloud, role + hashed org id, never the invitee email).
- **Opt-out toggle** in Settings > General > Privacy ("Share usage analytics", all 8 locales). One marker file (`telemetry_opt_out`) in the data dir: the daemon drops everything, the renderer calls `opt_out_capturing()` + `posthog.reset()` (and a launch that starts opted out never builds a client), and the phone resets and persists the opt-out. Separate from the existing agent-switch "Event reporting" consent, which is untouched.
- **Docs:** `docs/telemetry.md`, FAQ, README now state exactly what is sent (including email for signed-in AO Cloud users) and how to opt out.

## Not done (flagging, not hiding)

`pricing.viewed`, `checkout.started`, `subscription.created`: the repo has no pricing page, checkout, or subscription code (`pricing/` is the LLM token-cost catalog). I defined the cloud sink, event names and property allowlists (tests included) so wiring them later cannot widen what is sent, but nothing emits them yet. They need the billing surface first.

## Rollout note

- **Cost:** identified events bill at a higher rate. Anonymous installs stay anonymous. A person profile is now created (a) once a GitHub login resolves (same as before, but now at daemon start instead of first spawn, so far more installs), and (b) on AO Cloud sign-in, after which that user's desktop, daemon and paired-phone events are all identified. A signed-out paired phone remains anonymous. Expect the identified share to rise; watch PostHog usage after release.
- **Cloud server-side events** are off unless `AO_CLOUD_POSTHOG_KEY` (and optionally `AO_CLOUD_POSTHOG_HOST`) is set. They are not covered by the desktop opt-out; the docs say so.
- **Opt-out semantics:** in-session opt-in leaves the renderer on a fresh anonymous ID until restart; sign-out does the same (documented in code as `ponytail:` notes). A phone's opt-out is sticky until a paired opted-in desktop lifts it. An old daemon without the new route simply leaves the phone anonymous.
- **Version fallback** only helps once release builds stamp `cli.Version` (ldflags); today they do not, so `ao start`-launched daemons still report no version. Separate small release-tooling change.

## Follow-up (required before release)

- **Update the privacy policy** (orchestrator.inc/privacy) to cover collecting the AO Cloud email, user ID and GitHub username in PostHog, the mobile identity linkage, and the new opt-out.

## Validation at 73e30e74a

title: fix(chat): settle ACP steer method-not-found as refusal
body:
Code changes: +178 -1\
Tests: +160 -0\
Others: +18 -1

## What

Treat ACP `_session/steering` JSON-RPC method-not-found (`-32601`) as a definite provider refusal so steer delivery handles settle as rejected instead of remaining `reserved` / `CHAT_STEER_UNCERTAIN`.

## Why

Fixes #6188.

OpenCode answers steering probes with a received `-32601` response. AO reserved the client delivery handle before dispatch, then classified the wrapped error as uncertain transport failure. Recovery kept replaying uncertainty without settling and without another provider call—correct for real transport ambiguity, wrong for a definite unsupported-extension response.

Analyzed against canonical `main` at `6763832d4e8afe13950ab7e4ed33195fb136e962`. No competing fix PR found.

## How

- In `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/steer.go`, reuse existing `isACPMethodNotFound` and wrap `-32601` in an ACP `providerRefusal` that implements `ChatRefusal()`.
- Leave non-`-32601` CallExtension failures as ordinary errors so the service still returns `ErrSteerDeliveryUncertain` and does not auto-resend.
- Service classification already maps `ChatRefusal()` → `ErrProviderRefused` → durable `RejectSteerDelivery` / `provider_refused`.

Intentional omission: no capability-advertisement rewrite and no rewriting of already-reserved historical uncertain rows without evidence.

## Testing

title: fix(chat): keep the Working row below the newest work of a running turn
body:
Fixes #6426

## What

While a turn is running, the "Working for …" row now sits below the turn's newest work (just above the composer when you're at the bottom). Before, it sat directly under the prompt that opened the turn. Once the turn settles, the "Worked for" row still takes over at the top of the turn, as before.

## Why

#6298 merged the turn's two Working rows into one and put it directly under the opening prompt. In a long turn the view follows the newest work, so that row scrolls out of view. Nothing near the work the user is watching then says the agent is still running (reported on a Claude Code scratchpad session in a long video-render step; see #6426).

## How

`TurnGroup` builds the live row the same way as before, but adds it to the end of the turn body instead of between the opening prompt and the work. The settling row (440 ms spinner fade) stays in the same bottom spot. Startup is unchanged: with no work yet, the setup checklist is in the same place either way.

## Testing

- New `ChatWorkspace` test: in a running turn with tool runs and a progress message, the Working label comes after the prompt, the progress message and the latest tool run. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- Updated the mid-turn steer ordering test, which encoded the old placement.
- `vitest` on `src/renderer/components/chat/`: 868 passed. `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `frontend/src`.
- Real Electron lab (this branch; isolated data under `~/.ao/dev/lab-122`, daemon :3012, driven over CDP) with a Claude Code standalone session. During a ~90 s Bash call, "Working for 20s" showed under the newest "Ran command" row, right above the composer. After the turn settled, "Worked for 1m" folded the work at the top of the turn and the final answer sat below it.

## Known follow-up (not in this PR)

Claude ACP leaves a Bash tool call in `pending` until its first update. The lab's 90 s ping stayed `pending` for its whole run, and standalone-9's render call stayed `pending` for 35 s. `ActivityRun` only counts `running` for its spinner, so a long tool row shows no spinner of its own during that time. With this fix the turn-level Working row covers the gap. Treating `pending` as live inside a running turn could be a separate change.

title: feat: detect cached Gemini credentials
body:
Code changes: +227 -57  
Tests: +438 -10  
Others: +17 -3

## What

Adds local Gemini CLI authentication detection for `GEMINI_API_KEY`, cached OAuth credentials, and Gemini's saved `gemini-api-key` selection (whose secret may live in the OS keychain). Gemini settings.json comments are accepted, including when falling back to cached OAuth credentials. `GOOGLE_API_KEY` alone remains unknown. Missing credentials remain unknown, while unexpected home-resolution, settings, or credential-file errors are returned to the caller.

## Why

Deliberate difference from #7118: this PR uses `Configured` for setup-style harnesses in the `configured` state, including **Gemini and Unreal Agent**. #7118's neutral `Installed` label remains for generic configured harnesses whose auth action is not `setup`. For setup flows, `Configured` distinguishes locally detected configuration from unavailable setup status; it does not mean credentials were validated or a provider request succeeded. Existing provider-diagnostic and token-renewal rules still take precedence.

Configured setup results complete and close the auth terminal, including readiness recovery. Setup-style harnesses show Configured for unverified local evidence and retain Open setup; authorized results show Connected. Unknown setup status offers Set up without blocking Update, marking the row as an auth failure, or blocking its model catalog. Main's provider diagnostics, token-renewal display, and separate CLI-account completion handling are preserved.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Gemini's local key, saved API-key selection, or cached OAuth credentials are not detected by this adapter. | Supported local evidence yields `configured`; `GOOGLE_API_KEY` alone stays `unknown`. |
| Gemini settings do not contribute local auth evidence. | Saved API-key selection is detected in settings with JSON comments, including with cached OAuth fallback. |
| #7118 labels setup-style harnesses with local configuration as `Installed`, including Unreal Agent. | Setup-style `configured` harnesses deliberately show `Configured`, including Unreal Agent and Gemini. Generic non-setup `configured` harnesses retain `Installed`. |
| Unknown setup status has no setup entry point. | `Set up` is available while Update, neutral row status, and the model catalog remain available. |
| A detected `configured` setup result can leave the auth terminal unverified and open. | Both completion and readiness recovery close a successfully configured setup terminal. |
| Gemini setup can submit `/auth` before command readiness or reopen an existing picker. | AO skips an open native picker and otherwise waits for the editor and command completion with separate timeout budgets. |

## How

Gemini setup launches the normal TUI. If its native authentication dialog is already open, AO skips injection. Otherwise AO types `/auth` after the editor appears, waits for the `Manage authentication` completion, then presses Enter. Startup and completion have independent bounded waits. Without completion, `/auth` remains unsubmitted and guidance explains manual submission after completion appears. This avoids `--prompt-interactive` and early-submit races that treated `/auth` as a model prompt.

Merged canonical main `f7c037f736a0e65a3c3fa855857a98d4683514e3` in `7ce06c050aeaeed9c32b51da6a207951872aaf9d`. Resolved adjacent additions in `agentauth/plans.go` and `agentauth/service_test.go` by retaining both Gemini’s setup/readiness flow and main’s OMP native provider setup, including both sets of regression tests. Newer Claude setup-token guidance and auth-workspace data-directory handling are preserved.

## Testing

Validation for merge head `7ce06c050aeaeed9c32b51da6a207951872aaf9d`: all 30 GitHub Actions checks passed, including [Go](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41027735773) (build, vet, formatting, lint, all backend/Chat/SQLite/session-store race suites, Windows coverage, API/sqlc drift), [Frontend](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41027735657) (all four Vitest shards, typechecks, renderer smoke, browser boundaries, macOS helper/DMG checks), [CLI E2E](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41027735609) (Linux, macOS, Windows, container), secret scanning, and public-boundary checks.

Local validation was limited to repository-wide Go formatting, `git diff --check`, clean/unmerged-index checks, the public-boundary script, and changed locale JSON parsing. No local test suite executed: pinned Go 1.27.1 and locked frontend dependencies were unavailable; their incomplete downloads were stopped. Docker was not running, and native Linux/Windows runners were unavailable on this macOS host. All executed test validation listed above ran in GitHub Actions on this merge head.

Regression source covers Google-key-only detection; commented settings/OAuth fallback and I/O errors; setup button/update/model-catalog independence; configured Gemini completion and readiness recovery; separate completion deadlines; native picker skip; and leaving `/auth` unsubmitted without its completion marker.

title: [Bug]: Reviewer model selector shows the pinned Claude alias (Opus), not the gateway model actually running
body:
### What went wrong?

**Summary:** when a Claude Code reviewer runs against an Anthropic-compatible gateway, the model shown in the reviewer selector ("Claude Code · Opus") is the pinned alias from the static Claude catalog, while the process actually runs a gateway model (glm-5.3-flash). The UI label and the runtime model are two disjoint id spaces with no resolution feedback.

**Reproduction:**

1. Configure an Anthropic-compatible gateway (z.ai `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic`) and run a PR-review reviewer session with the claude-code harness.
2. The reviewer picker shows the agent and model as "Claude Code · Opus" — model id `opus` comes from the static Claude catalog entry (`Label: "Opus"`).
3. The same reviewer pane's statusline reports `glm-5.3-flash`, and the spawn env confirms the resolution:

```
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=glm-5.3-flash
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=glm-5.3-flash
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=glm-5.3-flash
```

So the pinned alias `opus` is silently remapped to a gateway model, and everything the UI shows ("Opus") disagrees with what is actually running.

**Why it happens:** the per-session model pin stores an id from one catalog (static Claude families), while the actual model is resolved at spawn through another (the gateway catalog / `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` mapping). Nothing validates that the pinned id exists in the active provider's catalog, and no surface (reviewer select, inspector, review controls) shows the resolved value.

**Expected:** wherever AO displays a session's model, show the resolved model actually passed to the provider (the gateway-catalog id), or at least visibly mark a pinned alias as unresolved/translated (e.g. "Opus → glm-5.3-flash"). Ideally, when a role's provider is a gateway, the pin should store the gateway-catalog model id so selector, config, and runtime all agree.

**Environment:**

- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon), desktop app
- Build: local self-build from fork main (synced with upstream main 2026-10-08)
- Harness: claude-code reviewer against a z.ai Anthropic-compatible gateway
- Model catalogs in play: static Claude families + gateway-seeded glm-* entries

title: fix(cline): stop PreToolUse pinning sessions to needs_input
body:
Code changes: +111 -4
Tests: +161 -3
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #6414.

Cline PreToolUse fires after approval since upstream cline/cline#7446, or with no prompt at all under auto-approve, so mapping it to permission-request pinned every tool invocation to sticky waiting_input (inverted for interactive sessions, false positive otherwise).

What:
- PreToolUse installs as permission-resolved (active) instead of permission-request. The event name matters as much as the state: permission-resolved is a turn boundary, so the post-approval hook also clears a waiting_input the terminal detector wrote while the approval dialog was on screen. A plain pre-tool-use mapping cannot do that — lifecycle suppresses tool-use events against sticky waiting_input — so an approved session would keep showing Input needed until some unrelated marker arrived.
- New cline.DeriveActivityState: permission-resolved, pre-tool-use (hook scripts from the intermediate install), and legacy permission-request (hook scripts installed before this fix) all derive active.
- Genuine approval dialogs carry no hook and are observed via DetectTerminalActivity, which now recognizes the Approve tool call dialog as waiting_input. It only accepts the dialog's own structure — a question line plus both `[y] approve` and `[n] deny` controls — so quoted approval text, prose mentioning approve/deny, and the "Auto-approve all disabled" footer never read as a pending decision.
- Shared StandardDeriveActivityState learns pre-tool-use / post-tool-use / permission-resolved as active (tool traffic is work; lifecycle precedence still protects sticky states).

Testing:
- go build ./...
- go test ./internal/adapters/agent/cline/ ./internal/adapters/agent/activitystate/ ./internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch/ ./internal/lifecycle/ ./internal/observe/activity/ -count=1
- go test ./internal/cli/ -run Cline -count=1
- go vet + golangci-lint on the touched packages
- New lifecycle regression test covers the full observer-writes-waiting_input → PreToolUse → persisted active sequence, plus a pin that a plain pre-tool-use signal cannot clear it.

Tradeoff: remap-only would hide real approvals; the terminal detector covers the TUI approval dialog so pending decisions still surface as Input needed.

title: feat(telemetry): report the automation create funnel
body:
Code changes: +64 -9  
Tests: +94 -1  
Others: +38 -1  

## What changed

Automations shipped with no telemetry on any surface. The page reported as route surface `other`, and nothing recorded whether anyone opened the create dialog, completed it, or abandoned it at the empty prompt textarea. There was no way to tell which recurring tasks people actually set up, which is the input for deciding which preset templates to offer.

This adds the create funnel in the renderer, where abandonment is visible: `ao.renderer.automation_create_opened` on dialog open, then `_requested` and `_succeeded` or `_failed` around the mutation. Editing an existing automation emits nothing. The automations route now reports surface `automations`.

Only closed vocabularies leave the machine. The prompt never does: a byte-size band stands in for it, so the promise in `docs/telemetry.md` that prompts are never transmitted is unchanged. The project id goes through the existing hashing sanitizer. `docs/telemetry.md` now discloses automation page visits, the four creation events, the allowed properties, UTF-8 prompt-size bands, and the existing opt-out controls.

Incidental behavior change, called out because it is not pure telemetry: a failed create used to let its rejection escape to the global handler, reporting the same failure a second time as an unhandled renderer exception. The dialog already renders that error, so the escape is dropped in favour of the explicit failed event. The edit path still has this duplication. That is pre-existing and left for its own change.

## How to test

1. `cd frontend && npm ci`
2. `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/AutomationsView.test.tsx src/renderer/lib/telemetry.test.ts`
3. `npm run typecheck`
4. `npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts`
5. To see the real events, launch with a local sink and the dev opt-in, then create an automation:

```
cd frontend && env AO_PORT=3012 \
  AO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.ao/dev/telemetry-verify/data" \
  AO_RUN_FILE="$HOME/.ao/dev/telemetry-verify/running.json" \
  AO_TELEMETRY_RENDERER=on \
  VITE_AO_POSTHOG_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:9898 \
  npm run dev
```

## Useful code paths

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/AutomationsView.tsx`, the funnel inside `AutomationFormDialog`
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts`, the sanitizer cases, the `/automations` route branch, and `automationPromptLengthBucket`

## Proof

Static checks, all run: full renderer suite 405 files / 6504 passed / 7 skipped, exit 0. Type check clean across `frontend/src`. Production renderer build exit 0.

Live run against a real daemon and a real renderer, observed as decompressed HTTP POST bodies leaving posthog-js, with nothing mocked inside the renderer:

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| Dialog open emits `opened` with no event properties | Confirmed, context keys only |
| Submit emits `requested` then `succeeded` | Confirmed, 1 ms apart, `{project_id_hash, schedule_preset, prompt_length_bucket}` |
| `project_id_hash` is a real hash | Confirmed, 64 hex, matches `sha256` of the daemon's project id |
| Prompt size band | Confirmed, a 103-byte prompt banded `s` (81-240) |
| No user content on the wire | Confirmed, 0 hits for the display name, prompt text, or raw project id across every request of the session |
| Editing emits nothing | Confirmed, zero events of any name during an edit and save |
| Route surface | Confirmed, `route_viewed` with `surface: automations` |
| Failed create | Confirmed against a genuine daemon `404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND`: `failed` fires, no `succeeded`, no `$exception`, dialog stays open with the error |

The automation was really created, not optimistically rendered: `GET /api/v1/automations` returned it with the expected RRULE and next run time. All app state stayed under the isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`; nothing was written to `~/Library/Application Support`.

A fresh-context adversarial review drove the real `captureRendererEvent` with a hostile payload carrying a prompt, display name, RRULE and a filesystem path as the project id. Only the three expected properties reached `posthog.capture`. An unregistered event name carrying a prompt emitted nothing, since the sanitizer has no default case.

That review also caught a test of mine that could not fail: the expected object read its own hash back out of the actual value, so deleting the hashing from the sanitizer kept all 57 tests green. It is rewritten to assert the exact key set and a 64-hex hash, and re-mutating the sanitizer now fails it. It caught a real bug too: the size bands counted UTF-16 units while the daemon's 4096 cap counts bytes, so non-Latin prompts banded two steps low. Now measured with `TextEncoder`, with a non-Latin case in the test.

### Confidence

| Area | Confidence | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| No user content transmitted | High | Wire-level capture plus a hostile-payload probe |
| Funnel fires correctly | High | Driven in the real app, all five paths |
| Unpackaged dev build | High | That is what was run |
| Packaged build gate | Unverified | Gated on `app.isPackaged`, read but not run |
| Delivery to the real PostHog project | Unverified | Host was redirected to a local sink on purpose, so a verification run would not pollute production analytics |

### Not fixed here

`hashedTelemetryID` is an unsalted `sha256` of the project id, and project ids derive from directory names, so a common repo name is recoverable from a dictionary. Pre-existing at `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts:383`, but this change routes project ids from a new surface through it. Worth its own decision.

## Documentation follow-up validation

The follow-up commit changes only `docs/telemetry.md`. Local checks passed with Node 24.21.0: the full frontend suite with 6,505 tests and 6 skipped, frontend and E2E type checks, the docs production build, Cloud client and product UI package checks, and the guarded-navigation browser integration. The lockfile dry-run passed with CI's Node 22.23.2. Both macOS helper architectures compiled, passed architecture verification, and passed the native state tests.

The local macOS renderer smoke run passed 73 tests and failed three: `e2e/chat-agent-switch.spec.ts` and `e2e/chat-interface-refusal.spec.ts` timed out waiting for the Chat region, and `e2e/chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts` reported a collapsed pointer-drag selection. The documentation follow-up changes no frontend code. Docker is unavailable locally, so the pinned Linux Playwright and gitleaks containers were not run locally. The local Mac is arm64 rather than CI's Intel runner. Remote checks provide the CI-environment results.

This PR adds a MiMo-specific parser that extracts the model ID before the details and adds a regression test.

Tests:
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog -run 'Test(ParseMiMoModelsAcceptsInlineDetails|MiMoCodeDiscoveryUsesNativeModelsCommand)'`

title: feat(mobile): enable partial agent response selection
body:
Code changes: +605 -145  
Tests: +552 -63  
Others: +408 -0  

## Summary

- Make each agent reply one native selectable text surface in the conversation. A range can cross headings, paragraphs, numbered and bulleted lists, quotes, code, tables, and image captions on iOS and Android. Remove the separate Select text sheet.
- Preserve tappable inline links and add native attributed-link semantics for iOS VoiceOver inside the selectable text view. Keep the neutral gray selection color.
- Keep image previews below the selectable reply text. The response text includes their captions; code and tables use readable text styling inside the single selection surface.
- Keep Android's natural-order timeline and mirrored jump positioning, which prevent selection gestures from fighting the inverted list. Merged PR #6513 changes turn folding in the same timeline, but leaves the agent response row in place. The quote action uses conversation context and does not modify the folding path.

- Add native **Add to chat** actions to the iOS and Android text-selection menus. The native selection is passed directly into a removable text preview inside the composer, preserving the typed reply. Each selection retains its conversation ID, source message ID and revision. Send uses the same `excerpts` request envelope as desktop, so the daemon verifies the selected text and supplies the paired user/assistant turn as background context. No message is sent by selecting or adding a quote.
- Match the supplied composer sketch: selected text and its remove control sit above the input inside one rounded panel. Reuse the native iOS glass backdrop and the established Android surface; keep multiple snippets scrollable and inset from the rounded corners. Tighten the quote top spacing and vertically center its larger remove control.
- Save and restore source references with the per-host/session draft and exact retry record; preserve a newer draft if an earlier send completes. Older saved quotes without provenance must be reselected.
- Render server-verified excerpt summaries as readable quote text above the sent user reply on mobile, including messages sent from desktop. Use a subtle quote mark, prose spacing and a fine divider within the existing message bubble. Give quoted messages enough width for full selections; omit desktop annotation chips.
- Verify native list/task markers, code language labels, table separators and image captions against the durable Markdown source, through the existing excerpt validation path. Complete turns only; stale sources remain rejected.
- Design references: [ChatGPT quoted reply composer](https://mobbin.com/screens/7126f028-6eb0-4003-8f4b-b204e726c330) and [Claude mobile composer](https://mobbin.com/screens/25841e2c-ae18-4bdc-8ac7-c1707513118f) from Mobbin.

## Validation

- Node 20.20.2 mobile typecheck passed; complete mobile suite passed: **173 files, 1,609 tests**. Tests cover the exact API envelope, native source callback, selected Unicode/bullets, draft/reference persistence, retries and sent-message rendering.
- Complete backend chat suite passed with Go 1.27.1, including the exact partial paragraph/bullet selection reproduced from the physical iPhone failure. Delivery tests exercise desktop and native excerpts through the same verifier and assert selected text plus the full paired turn in the provider prompt. Invalid/stale sources remain rejected.
- Backend build and vet completed locally before the final accessor cleanup; focused verification and full chat tests pass on the final changes. The attempted complete repository race suite was interrupted by disk exhaustion and installed-provider conformance differences (local OpenCode 1 fallback and a newer Codex protocol). Docker is unavailable locally; Linux, native-platform, container and full race gates are being verified in CI.
- All **21 CI checks pass** on exact current head `7b1f67a8b6cd411ab29fdf81505ca55634ab8854`, including full backend/race shards, API/sqlc drift, lint, mobile, native platforms and container checks.
- Android Release build succeeded and is installed as Selector. Physical screenshot verification of the existing desktop “and these?” message shows its selected excerpt as highlighted text above the reply. No real message was sent for this check.
- iPhone and Android Release builds succeeded at `58c21275c`. The quote polish was rebundled into those signed test installers, preserving native binaries/assets, and installed as Selector on both connected devices. Physical screenshots verify the full selection above the reply on both platforms. No real chat message was sent by this worker.
- Native AO review approved the full PR at `58c21275c` and then approved the quote-presentation follow-up at exact current head `7b1f67a8b`. No blocking findings; physical VoiceOver and iOS 15 checks remain follow-ups.
- Merged current main, including #6513 and desktop excerpt support, before implementing transport parity.

## Risk

- The single selectable surface presents code and tables as styled text instead of their previous interactive cards; image previews follow the selectable text. This keeps one continuous selection range across the full reply.
- VoiceOver link attributes compile and link callbacks are covered in component tests. A hands-on VoiceOver navigation pass is still needed. The iOS 15 legacy responder menu compiles but has not been exercised on an iOS 15 device.


- Hands-on full-response sends require the AO host to run this PR’s backend for native marker verification. The live daemon was not restarted.

title: fix(settings): auto-focus harness login terminal inside Settings dialog
body:
## Summary
- Clicking **Login** on a harness in Settings → Harness opens an inline terminal (`HarnessAuthTerminalPanel`) running the CLI's own login command, but it never gained keyboard focus — users had to click into the terminal manually before they could type/interact.
- Root cause: `canAutoFocusTerminal()` in `XtermTerminal.tsx` bailed out whenever `isDialogOrMenuOpen()` was true, on the assumption that an open dialog is always an *unrelated* overlay stealing focus. But the harness login terminal is rendered *inside* the open Settings dialog itself, so this guard always blocked its auto-focus.
- Added `isDialogOrMenuOpenOutside(host)` in `dom-selectors.ts`, which only blocks auto-focus when a dialog/menu *not containing* the terminal's host element is open, and swapped it in for the blanket check in `canAutoFocusTerminal`.

## Test plan
- [x] Reviewed the existing `data-terminal-focus-handoff="true"` marker already present on the harness login button (`HarnessSettingsSection.tsx`), confirming this auto-focus hookup was already intended but broken by the dialog guard.
- [ ] Manually verify in the running app: Settings → Harness → Local tab → Login → terminal should gain focus immediately without an extra click.
- Note: full `npm run typecheck` surfaces unrelated pre-existing errors in `packages/product-ui` (missing `react`/`motion` type declarations in that workspace package); no errors were introduced in the two files touched here.
