title: perf(terminal): WebGL past 16 terminals, batched output frames, faster terminal open
body:
## Summary

Terminal performance pass. Each change was profiled first and then measured A/B against `main` (d26270f84) on the same machine and the same seed data.

1. **WebGL contexts stay under Chromium's cap** (`fix`). Chromium keeps at most 16 live WebGL contexts per renderer and kills the oldest beyond that. Every cached terminal held a context forever, and a lost context was never re-created. As a result, older terminals stayed stuck on the slow DOM renderer once you had about 16 open.
   - A small pool (`lib/terminal-webgl-pool.ts`) keeps WebGL for the 8 most recently shown terminals.
   - It parks older hidden terminals on the DOM renderer.
   - A terminal gets a fresh context when it is shown again, including after a real context loss.
2. **Streaming output leaves the daemon as a few large frames.** The mux writer sent every PTY read as its own WebSocket message. `seq 1 100000` reached the renderer as about 2,300 messages, each costing an event, a JSON parse and a base64 decode on the thread that also parses and draws the terminal.
   - A frame queued after a quiet period is still written immediately, so keystroke echo is never delayed.
   - While output keeps streaming, writes are spaced 4 ms apart, so queued output merges into fewer frames.
3. **The scrollbar follows scrolling once per frame.** xterm fires a scroll event per line feed, so the overlay scrollbar's reveal ran 100,000 times per `seq 1 100000` (about 9 ms of renderer time).
4. **A new terminal's create request goes out before its tab renders.** There were three causes:
   - The click's state updates render synchronously in a microtask, so the POST queued behind the optimistic tab's render.
   - The shared API client rebased every request from its placeholder base URL by buffering the body asynchronously. It now builds requests against the daemon's current address. A request built before the address changed is still rebased.
   - The list refetch after a create also ran twice. Removed the duplicate.
5. **Unchanged shell tabs skip session-view re-renders.** Shell tabs are now memoized with stable handlers.

## Results

All numbers are from the same machine on the same day, `main` (d26270f84) against this PR, each build on fresh copies of the same seed data.

**Screen capture** (real keystrokes, ScreenCaptureKit frames, medians). The command is typed inside the timed window, so typing time adds the same amount to both builds:

| Metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `seq 1 100000` until fully drawn | 238 ms | 227 ms |
| Full-screen redraw ×200 | 670 ms | 635 ms |
| Typing lag | 19.5 ms | 20.2 ms (no change) |
| Open → prompt | 206 ms | 195 ms |
| Close | 57.5 ms | 57.9 ms (no change) |

**In-app** (CPU profiler, debugger network tracking off, 5 runs each):

| Metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| WebSocket messages for `seq 1 100000` | ~2,300 | ~24 |
| First → last xterm parse of that output | ~136 ms | ~95 ms |
| Renderer CPU during that run (JS + native) | ~123 ms | ~90 ms |
| Create request sent after the "New terminal" click | ~19 ms | ~1 ms |
| WebGL contexts lost with ~27 terminals open | 22 | 0 |

An earlier version of this description reported ~256 → ~100 ms for `seq` delivery. That came from timestamping every WebSocket frame over CDP, whose per-event overhead inflated `main`'s ~2,300-frame run. The numbers above replace it.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/terminal/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/...` passes, `-race` on `internal/terminal`. Added `TestWriteLoopPacesBurstsButNotIsolatedFrames`.
- `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean. `golangci-lint` isn't installed locally, so CI will run it.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- The full renderer `vitest` run passes (6,642 tests), apart from 23 `src/main` failures this PR doesn't touch:
  - 22 are `better-sqlite3` built for Electron's ABI locally.
  - 1 is a timeout that passes when run alone.
- New tests: the WebGL pool, the scrollbar following scrolling once per frame, and the API client calling `fetch` in the same task.
- Terminal Playwright specs show identical results on `main` and this branch locally (4 pass, 8 fail on both because of the local dev:web environment).

## Risks

- **Burst pacing** can delay output that arrives within 4 ms of the previous write by up to 4 ms. An isolated chunk, such as a keystroke's echo, is unaffected.
- **API client:** the local client now stamps the current daemon base URL on every request, which affects every API call. Tests that spy on `apiClient` methods are unaffected because the methods are plain properties.
- **WebGL pool:** a terminal shown after being parked rebuilds its WebGL renderer on activation. In testing this caused no long tasks, and tab switches stayed around 67 ms either way.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- **Faster open needs a design decision.** Creating a shell waits for the daemon to start a pty-host process (17–50 ms). The service deliberately spawns the runtime before writing the row and issues a per-shell preview capability during that launch window. A pre-warmed host or asynchronous spawn would change that contract, so it should be decided separately.
- **Binary WebSocket frames:** after the pacing change, base64 and JSON costs about 2–5 ms per 1 MB, so the remaining win is small.
- **Ghostty renderer:** tracked in #6238.
- **Browser runtime link reconnect loop:** if the daemon rejects the handshake (for example a token mismatch after the app restarts against a surviving daemon), the client resets its backoff on TCP connect, so it reconnects every 200 ms. That loop re-renders the whole session view about 10 times a second. Found while profiling; not fixed here.

title: Browser runtime link reconnects every 200 ms when the daemon rejects its handshake, re-rendering SessionView ~10x/s
body:
## Problem

When the daemon rejects the desktop app's browser runtime link handshake, the app reconnects every 200 ms forever. Each attempt flips `browserRuntimeConnected` from true to false. That state lives in `useBrowserView`, which is called from `SessionView`, so the whole session view re-renders about 10 times a second while the app is idle. That is roughly 120 ms of React work every 2.5 s, around 5% of a CPU core, and it competes with terminal output and typing.

## Cause

`frontend/src/main/browser-runtime-link.ts`:
- On TCP `connect`, the client calls `setConnected(true)` and resets `backoff = BACKOFF_INIT_MS` (200 ms), then sends `hello`.
- The daemon (`backend/internal/browserruntime/broker.go`) closes the connection when the hello is invalid, for example on a token mismatch.
- The close tears the link down, which calls `setConnected(false)` and `scheduleReconnect()` with the backoff that was just reset to 200 ms.

The result is a connect/close loop at about 5 Hz with no backoff growth. Every state change is broadcast as `browser:runtimeState` to the renderer.

## Repro

1. Start the dev Electron app with an isolated data dir.
2. Kill only the Electron process, so the daemon survives (`ppid` 1), then relaunch the app. The new app generates a new `browserRuntimeToken`, but it adopts the surviving daemon, which still holds the old token.
3. `/tmp/<log>` fills with `browser-runtime-link: connected` (about 2,800 lines in a few minutes).
4. A React commit hook shows about 20 commits a second while idle, with `SessionView` re-rendering because `useBrowserView`'s `browserRuntimeConnected` toggles.

I found this while profiling terminal performance for #6465. After a clean restart (daemon and app together), idle renderer work drops from ~120 ms to ~3 ms per 2.5 s.

## Suggested fix

- Only treat the link as connected, and reset the backoff, once the daemon has accepted the hello. Alternatively, reset the backoff only after the connection has stayed up for some time.
- Consider surfacing a persistent handshake rejection as a visible error instead of retrying silently.
- Separately, `browserRuntimeConnected` should not re-render the whole `SessionView` when the browser panel isn't shown.

title: fix(claude): don't adopt another data dir's transcript when an AO session id is reused
body:
## Problem
A new orchestrator replayed an unrelated prompt from an old conversation ("This turn was recovered from an earlier session").

Claude's legacy session id is `uuidv5(AO session id)`, but Claude keeps every transcript in one global config dir. When a second or wiped data dir reuses an id (`flash-1`), the id maps onto the old transcript, and `--session-id` then continued it. The chat host was launched with `--resume=<old uuid>` and the old turn was imported.

## Fix
`GetLaunchCommand` checks, on a fresh launch with no caller-assigned id, whether the derived id already has a transcript. If so it uses a new random id; hooks capture whichever id Claude ends up with.

## Scope
Restore of pre-hook sessions still falls back to the derived id; that path is unchanged.

## Test
`go test ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/ ./pkg/agentruntime/`; new test covers the reused-id case.

title: feat(testing): agent-driven PR testing in the real desktop app
body:
Code changes: +7248 -64  
Tests: +8502 -5  
Others: +4153 -572  

## What this does

Lets an AO worker test a pull request in the real desktop app and review it.

Give a worker a PR URL. It reads the PR, launches the PR's version of AO next to yours, uses the app like a person would (screenshots, clicks, typing), records what happens, and drafts a GitHub review with the screenshots and clips attached. Nothing is posted until you approve the preview.

Your own AO is never touched: the test app runs with its own data folder, port and Electron profile.

## How a run works

1. **Read the PR.** `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`, the changed files and their callers, existing reviews and `gh pr checks`. The worker writes down what changed, what triggers the bug, and how to reach it in the UI. It never runs the repo's build, test or lint suites; CI status comes from `gh pr checks`.
2. **Before (base).** AO checks out the PR's base in a reusable target folder, launches it with private state, and the worker runs its steps, taking screenshots and recording. Exact numbered steps and inputs are saved in retained evidence.
3. **After (head).** Same folder, switched to the PR head, the saved steps and inputs replayed verbatim.
4. **Review.** One draft review: inline file:line findings (or "no issues found" plus what was checked), and before/after screenshots and clips (15 s max each). The verdict is `REQUEST_CHANGES`, `COMMENT` or `APPROVE`.
5. **Approve, then post.** You see the exact preview first. After approval the worker uploads the media, posts the review, and re-reads it on GitHub to confirm it landed as previewed.
6. **Cleanup.** Cleanup stops the test's owned processes and deletes private app data only after verified shutdown. Screenshots, video, logs and the report are kept.

If the worker never reaches the PR's actual trigger, the result says **partial**. It does not claim a fix it didn't see.

## What's in the code

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| `adapters/testingdesktop/cua` | Screenshot, click, type, keys and recording, locked to the test app's window |
| `adapters/testingtarget/local` | Launches the PR's AO with private state, reuses one checkout and the normal Go/npm caches, installs dependencies only when the lockfile changes, and kills everything it started |
| `adapters/testingevidence` | Keeps screenshots, video and logs after cleanup |
| `service/testing` | Runs each attempt: start, deadline, action log, report, cleanup |
| `cli`, `httpd/controllers` | `ao testing ...` commands and HTTP routes used by the worker |
| `storage/sqlite` | Tables for runs and attempts (migration `0194`) |
| `skillassets/testing/SKILL.md` | The instructions the worker follows (the steps above) |
| daemon / session_manager | Wiring, plus a daemon shutdown fix needed for clean teardown |

Generated files account for +3787/-571 lines of Others. The rest is docs, config and a dependency license. Counts use GitHub's per-file diff; local Git also counts 216 license lines that GitHub omits.

## Limits

- Requires Cua Driver 0.34+ installed (/Applications/CuaDriver.app) with macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions; AO does not install it.
- macOS host only. No cloud VMs or Windows/Linux targets yet.
- Posting always needs approval.
- Base and head are two sequential attempts, not one live session switching revisions.

## Verified so far

- On the rebased head, root `npm run api` using cached `openapi-typescript@7.4.4` and `go build ./...` passed. API generation produced no drift. Full testing service, desktop, evidence, target and skill suites passed, along with testing-focused CLI, session, daemon, API, chat and storage checks and migration upgrade/downgrade/version checks.
- Previous head `8e5edc131` passed all 23 CI checks; earlier validation also passed sqlc generation, pinned lint and Windows CLI/target cross-compiles.
- Earlier live runs on PRs #6300, #6387 and #6418 launched the app, typed into the real UI and recorded video. #6300 used assisted setup and publication. The #6387 comparison remained blocked or unverified; #6418 ended **partial** because the investigator didn't reach its timing-dependent trigger.

**Not yet verified:** full CI on the rebased head and a full live run of this version: before/after, review draft, approved posting, and warm-run setup time.

title: [Bug]: Renamed orchestrator name is not reflected in the UI
body:
### What went wrong?

When an orchestrator is renamed, the operation succeeds, but the updated name is not reflected in the UI. The orchestrator continues to display its previous name, making it unclear whether the rename was successful.

Expected behavior: After a successful rename, the new orchestrator name should immediately appear in the UI without requiring a page refresh.

Actual behavior: The orchestrator is successfully renamed, but the UI continues to display the old name.

Possible cause: The frontend state or cache is not updated after the rename operation completes.

Suggested fix: Update the local state/cache with the new orchestrator name after a successful response, or refetch the updated orchestrator to keep the UI synchronized with the backend.

title: feat: add a project session switcher
body:
Code changes: +515 -22
Tests: +469 -22
Others: +40 -8

## Summary

Adds a project-scoped session switcher, rebased onto the keyboard-shortcut catalog from #6531.

- Hold Ctrl and press ` (backquote) on every platform, including macOS. Shift moves backward. Release Ctrl to open the highlighted session.
- Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab stay the in-session tab shortcuts (chat, reviewer, terminal) on every platform.
- Ctrl+` was also Toggle terminal, and Ctrl+Shift+` was the Windows new-terminal chord that still works while a terminal is focused. Those moved so both features remain: Toggle terminal is Cmd+J on macOS and Ctrl+J on Windows/Linux. A new terminal while one is focused on Windows/Linux is Ctrl+Shift+J. Ctrl+T is unchanged.
- The first press opens a vertical list and highlights the current session. It does not advance. On the project board, that highlight is the live orchestrator.
- Further presses cycle. Releasing Ctrl opens the highlighted session.
- Escape dismisses the list and stays on the current session. The later modifier release does not navigate. If the window blurs before that release, the cancelled gesture is cleared so the next chord opens the switcher again.
- Losing the window also dismisses without navigating.
- Scope is the current project, including a remote host or cloud project open in the shell. Other projects and the scratchpad are not included.
- The live orchestrator is always first. Workers use the sidebar rule: not terminated, ordered by last interaction, then last user message, then creation. Manual sidebar drag order is not used.
- At most seven workers. If the current worker is outside that seven, the list is that worker plus the six most recently active, still in activity order. The orchestrator does not consume a worker slot.
- The list is frozen while it is open. A session that becomes ineligible before release is not opened. A project change closes the list without navigating.
- The orchestrator row title is Orchestrator. Selected row text stays white.
- Commit uses the same navigation as a sidebar row, a kanban card, and a canonical session link (`useNavigateToSession`), including the remote host id. A worker open records the same manual-open identity as the sidebar.

The chord is taken in the main process, including when focus is in xterm, the chat composer, or the embedded browser. The popup does not move DOM focus. While it is open it marks itself as a native browser overlay so the shell paints above the browser view.

Commit happens only when Ctrl itself comes up, including a Control keyUp whose ctrl flag is still true. The backquote keyup is not a commit. With Shift held, Electron reports key "~" and code Backquote, and that still steps backward.

Shortcut conflict search prefers the fixed switcher over an earlier customizable row.

## Tests

- Selection cap, activity order, orchestrator precedence, cancel, and vanished-session commit.
- Ctrl+Tab still sends next-tab on macOS and on Windows/Linux. Ctrl+` steps the switcher. Alt+Tab and Option+Tab do not.
- Release order: backquote then Ctrl, and Ctrl then backquote, each commit once. Backquote and Shift keyup while Ctrl is held do not commit.
- Escape followed by blur, then a fresh Ctrl+`, opens the switcher again.
- Popup render: initial highlight, cycle, release, escape, orchestrator label, and no focus move.
- Frontend `tsc --noEmit` and the shortcut, preload, switcher, and keyboard-help vitest files passed locally. No live Electron pass.

## Risks

- Not exercised against a live Electron window in this session.
- Sidebar drag order is intentionally not followed.
- Windows and Linux Toggle terminal is no longer Ctrl+`. It is Ctrl+J. The from-terminal new-terminal chord is Ctrl+Shift+J.

title: feat(cloud): Freestyle sandbox provider and Stripe billing for AO Cloud
body:
Code changes: +5454 -180
Tests: +3528 -6
Others: +419 -8 (i18n strings) ## Summary Adds [Freestyle](https://freestyle.sh) as an AO Cloud sandbox provider for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions, built for fast session start and for wakes that keep the running agent alive. **Provider and startup** - Freestyle VMs boot from per-harness snapshots (`publish-freestyle-snapshot.sh` bakes Claude Code, Codex and Cursor images and records them in the deployment secret). - Each repository gets a prepared snapshot with the repo already cloned, built in a throwaway VM so no session credentials or conversation are captured. Sessions boot from it and only `git fetch`. - Snapshots are keyed by GitHub repository id, shared by every project on that repository, and kept when a project is deleted; a collector removes snapshots unused for 7 days. A snapshot is only used while the project still names the `owner/name` it was cloned from, because the worker rejects a mismatched origin. - Startup waits removed: the first heartbeat, transcript, credential and checkout grant run beside startup instead of in sequence; the reconciler is woken through `pg_notify`; the control plane holds an agent terminal ticket request until the terminal is live, instead of the browser polling 409s. **Wake keeps the agent running** - On Freestyle the agent runs under `dtach`, so pausing and resuming the VM (memory included) and restarting the worker re-attaches to the same agent process instead of starting a new one. A Chat handoff still stops it. **Deployment and config** - Hosted environments accept `freestyle` as a sandbox provider; migration 00073 extends the existing provider constraint rather than replacing it. - Staging and production scripts, task-definition rendering and hosted-settings validation carry the Freestyle secret. **Frontend** - The cloud startup loader stays until the terminal has content, removing the flash of an empty pane between "connected" and the first output. **Billing (Stripe)** - AO Cloud is a paid feature. Plans and their limits are Stripe product metadata (`ao_plan`, `ao_max_active_sandboxes`, `ao_orchestrator_slots`, `ao_window_hours`, `ao_window_session_hours`, `ao_weekly_session_hours`, `ao_manual_resets_per_month`), cached on the organization by a signed, idempotent webhook that re-reads the subscription from Stripe. - Session creation checks the plan inside the transaction that already locks the organization: one reserved orchestrator slot, the rest for workers (including orchestrator-spawned sessions), an entitled subscription (active, trialing, or past_due within 7 days), and usage under a rolling 5-hour window and a weekly limit. - Usage is a ledger of running session-minutes. The weekly window resets automatically; an admin may reset it manually once per billing period. Over-limit organizations cannot start or wake sessions, and running sessions pause between turns. - Settings gains a Billing page: plans priced from Stripe, Checkout and Customer Portal in the system browser, usage meters, slots in use, and the manual reset. - Organizations with plan `internal`, or created before `AO_CLOUD_BILLING_EXEMPT_ORGS_CREATED_BEFORE`, are exempt. Billing is off unless `AO_CLOUD_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is set; staging reads `ao-cloud/staging/stripe` (a Stripe sandbox). - Idle pause counts terminal input and a presence heartbeat from visible sessions, and its default drops from 1h to 15m. ## Measured (staging, eu-north-1) | Session | Created → terminal ready | |---|---| | Large repo, first session (full clone) | ~9.6 s | | Same repo, from the repository snapshot | **4.0 s** | | VM create from snapshot | 0.5–0.6 s | The three latest commits (ticket long-poll, checkout-grant prefetch, per-repository snapshots) are not yet measured on staging; the expected saving is ~0.3–0.8 s per session, and a deleted-and-re-added repository starts at ~4 s instead of a full clone. ## Migrations - `00073` adds `freestyle` to the sandbox provider constraint. - `00074` / `00076` project snapshot table, re-keyed by repository in `00076`. `00076` carries existing rows over; the migration role is subject to forced RLS, so it lifts `FORCE` for its own statements and restores it before commit (covered by a test that runs the migration as a non-bypass role and fails without that step). - `00075` notifies the reconciler when a sandbox is asked to run. - `00077` adds billing: organization subscription columns, the Stripe customer map and processed events, the usage ledger, manual resets, and `last_interaction_at` for idle pause. ## Testing - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` in `cloud/`: all pass. - PostgreSQL integration tests for the new store code and migration pass against Postgres 17. - Frontend: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, and the touched test files pass. **Known local failures, not from this branch** (identical on unmodified `main` in the same environment): - `go test ./internal/postgres` with a database: `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`. - `npx vitest run`: 43 failures in `auto-updater`, `browser-profile-import`, `ChatWorkspace`, `ContextMeter`. **Not run locally:** the `docker build --target expat-build` CI step and the renderer smoke job; relying on CI for those. **Not yet exercised end to end:** Codex and Cursor sessions on Freestyle (snapshots are baked and selected per harness, but only Claude Code was run on staging). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat: add independent side chats in the inspector
body:
Code changes: +6250 -62  
Tests: +3416 -3  
Others: +5133 -2075  

## Summary

Add independent side conversations in the right inspector, with browser-style tabs, independent drafts, settings, queues, streaming, approvals, interruption, retry, and launch-scoped daemon recovery. Opening the panel creates nothing; users create, rename, and confirm closing individual sides.

Each side freezes main-chat context at its latest completed, non-rolled-back turn. Codex uses an exact isolated native fork; Claude Code and OpenCode use a fresh provider conversation reconstructed from completed visible history. Later main messages are never synchronized automatically. Main and same-side excerpts supply selected text and its complete paired turn without moving the fork point; cross-side and side-to-main references are rejected.

Insert the canonical side-conversation boundary after inherited history and before the first side request, with delivery receipts and recovery checks protecting against duplicate first sends and uncertain boundary placement. Preserve the shared workspace, Git state, MCP configuration, and inherited permissions. Read-only defaults and the prohibition on sub-agent interaction are behavioral instructions, not a filesystem sandbox or technical removal of tools.

## User behavior

- Side chat sits immediately after Browser; + creates a separate conversation. `/btw` and `/side` always create a new side and send the question there; retrying the same submission reuses its receipt. Add to side chat continues to use the active side.

- Numbered default names use currently open tabs, with inline, F2, double-click, and context-menu renaming.

- Compact annotation counts support removal and navigation to source text with visibility-aware scrolling and gray highlighting.

- Independent FIFO queues skip stale excerpt turns after marking them failed. Accepted excerpt context and delivery receipts survive retries and daemon replacement.

- Sides are local-desktop only and ephemeral across desktop launches. Unsupported harnesses and unverifiable recovery fail visibly.

## Earlier validation (before this refinement)

Historical results from the earlier implementation; the current refinement results are recorded below:

- Focused side-chat service/controller and Codex tests.

- Relevant Linux backend race suites: chat service, Codex, ACP, Claude ACP, OpenCode ACP, HTTP, and CLI.

- Complete HTTP/API package suite on Linux as a non-root user.

- Frontend typecheck, E2E typecheck, focused renderer/annotation tests, and disclosure tests.

- API regeneration with unchanged generated artifacts; changed-code golangci-lint v2.13.2 and relevant go vet.

- Real isolated Electron verification with scratch data: Codex native forks, configured read-only MCP exploration, OpenCode reconstruction, two independent sides, post-fork excerpt isolation, shared-file visibility after an explicit side-local mutation request, source navigation, and daemon recovery.

Known validation limits:

- The full Windows frontend suite is not green: 6,537 passed, 159 failed, 8 skipped, across 415 files. Failures include macOS packaging/update tests and existing locale expectations (Indian digit grouping in ContextMeter/ChatWorkspace).

- Windows backend checks encounter existing POSIX path assumptions and installed-Codex protocol drift; relevant Linux suites passed.

- Claude Code was not installed, so its adapter paths have automated coverage but no live-provider verification.

- Native macOS signing/update checks and the complete hosted CI environment are unavailable locally. CI results must be reviewed before marking this draft ready.

- Full Linux backend rerun failed in fake-agent lifecycle (missing hook log), systemexec process-group cancellation, usage pricing catalog hash validation, and Claude session-manager transitions (container home/config permission errors).

- Full Windows golangci-lint v2.13.2 reported 1,440 findings, including 1,385 goimports findings and Windows-specific diagnostics; changed-code lint passed. This is not a clean repository lint result.

- Shared package checks passed: cloud client typecheck, 29 tests, and build; product UI typecheck, 158 tests, and build.

- Hosted browser/CLI end-to-end jobs, native macOS checks, complete CI backend race shards, and docs builds were not all reproduced locally. These remain CI validation gaps.

## Review follow-up

Commit `013e02174` addresses the three review findings:

- Preserve registered forks while their side tabs remain open, including after daemon recovery; delete them after closure or retirement.

- Acknowledge ACP compaction completion receipts before releasing queued work, and show acknowledgement failures instead of dispatching another prompt.

- Merge refreshed side snapshots by ID so new turns cannot leave gaps above loaded history; retain updated messages without duplicates.

Added regression tests for created/recovered fork cleanup, compaction acknowledgement ordering and failure, and pagination before/after new turns arrive.

Earlier follow-up validation (before the current Windows refinement):

- Passed: full Linux chat-service race suite; focused backend cleanup/compaction tests; 37 focused side-chat renderer tests; pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 on Linux with zero findings; Linux and Windows native CLI E2E; frontend typecheck and E2E typecheck; guarded-navigation browser integration; shared package typechecks, 29 cloud-client tests, 158 product-UI tests, both shared builds; docs production build.

- Full Linux frontend run: 410 files passed and 5 failed (6,582 tests passed, 118 failed, 6 skipped). All five failing files subsequently passed on rerun: four packaging files after correcting archive line endings/installing missing zip, and browser-history after a timeout under concurrent load. This is full-suite coverage plus successful affected-file reruns, not a single clean full-suite run.

- Full Windows frontend run: 394 files passed and 21 failed (6,539 tests passed, 159 failed, 8 skipped), including platform-specific packaging and locale expectations; the changed side-chat suites passed.

- Linux Go build and vet passed. The full backend race run passed every package except the fake-agent lifecycle test described below; chat, SQLite, session manager, and SQLite store all passed. Linux native CLI E2E also passed.

- The fake-agent lifecycle hook-log failure also reproduces on the original PR head, before this follow-up.

- Native macOS jobs, renderer Playwright smoke, fresh-install CLI container, remaining Windows matrix jobs, cloud/API/sqlc regeneration jobs, and the complete hosted CI environment are not locally verified in this follow-up. The CI connector requests a GitHub account connection, so hosted check results remain unverified.

## Integration status

Rebased onto upstream main `c087cb02ee016620d5e9dcfe7dd9487c0b1b12c1` (11 October 2026). The PR remains draft; all 23 hosted checks pass on the latest head. Local Windows validation limitations are listed below.

## Scope

No automatic worktrees, filesystem permission changes, main-history synchronization, cross-side annotations, remote side chats, or additional harnesses. Reconstruction includes completed visible transcript context, not hidden provider state. Sub-agent restrictions intentionally rely on the boundary instructions.

## Attached Video Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d34027d-d778-4d27-8895-6067e418863f

## Side-chat refinement and illegalcall review fixes

- Reuse the browser tab row's padding, shrinking tab widths, hidden scrollbar, edge fades and wheel scrolling; keep only side tabs and the existing new-tab button.
- Ask “Delete side chat?” with Cancel and a neutral Delete button.
- Share the main chat's live elapsed-time status, completed-work divider and activity disclosure. Match the queue placeholder and preserve drafts while delivery is pending.

No P0 findings were left by illegalcall. All five findings are addressed:

| Priority | Finding | Fix and reason in plain language |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | [Restored running turn can wait forever](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6481#discussion_r4239115427) | Read fresh Codex history before restoring ownership and reconcile a completed result. Fail visibly if the outcome cannot be verified, preserving queued messages. A saved “working” label may be stale after a crash; it must not block the chat forever. ACP cached replay is not treated as a fresh outcome. |
| P1 | [New /btw question can resend an older question](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6481#discussion_r4239115434) | Both commands force a new side for a new submission. Keep stable creation/message IDs and the exact handoff receipt for retries. A new question now reaches its own chat instead of disappearing after an old question is resent. |
| P2 | [Closing a tab can orphan its provider](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6481#discussion_r4239115429) | Retain cleanup records across shutdown failures and daemon recovery; retry stopping the host before deleting the fork. Closing the visible tab no longer loses track of the process that still needs to stop. |
| P2 | [Autosave can erase a send receipt](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6481#discussion_r4239115431) | Order draft reads and every write per side across remounts, including autosave, replacement and receipt writes. An old save cannot arrive late and cause a previously accepted question to run twice. |
| P2 | [Older messages can land in another side](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6481#discussion_r4239115437) | Guard pagination results, errors and loading cleanup by side/session and request generation. Switching tabs while an older-page request is pending cannot mix their history or cursors. |

Regression coverage includes fresh command handoffs and retry keys, serialized draft I/O/remounts, delayed pagination across tabs, terminal-history reconciliation and cleanup recovery.

## Earlier refinement validation (Windows, 11 October 2026)

- Passed: all 81 focused side-chat, handoff, draft-ordering and localization regression tests; backend side-chat tests; Go build and vet; API spec checks; shared cloud-client and product-UI typechecks, tests and builds; docs production build; frontend and E2E TypeScript checks.
- Renderer Playwright smoke: 74 passed, 2 failed (composer pointer-drag text selection and the settings Help button). Chromium was installed and the suite ran on a separate port from the local desktop app.
- Full frontend suite: 6,739 passed, 183 failed, 8 skipped across 429 files. The changed side-chat suites and localization coverage pass. Failures include native packaging/platform and locale expectations; this is not a clean full-suite pass.
- Full Windows backend and HTTP suites encounter POSIX path, symlink-privilege and file-mode failures. The full lint run reports 1,682 findings, dominated by goimports line-ending findings; the final changed-line lint rerun passed with zero findings after correcting recovery errors and import formatting. Go race testing is unavailable because this Windows setup has CGO disabled.
- Desktop app rebuilt and launched against isolated scratch data. Visual inspection caught and corrected the tab-row wrapper; complete interactive overflow/dialog verification was interrupted when the user took over testing.
- Native macOS, Linux container/fresh-install and remaining hosted matrix jobs are not locally verified in this refinement. Hosted checks must be verified separately; no publishing or production deployment was used for validation.

That earlier hosted run completed with all checks passing except two locale assertions: the five new side-chat labels were missing from all seven translated catalogs. The correction and latest validation are below.

title: bug(scm): worker PR on an ao/<session>/ branch stays unattached ("Awaiting PR") even after ao report --pr-created
body:
Environment for all five: AO desktop 0.13.5 on macOS (Darwin 27); `ao --version` prints `dev`, so the bundled build is identified by the app version. Two hosts (MacBook and Mac mini), each with its own daemon. Workers and reviewers: codex, claude-code (Claude Code 2.1.295) and others. Projects set `env.GH_CONFIG_DIR` to a dedicated GitHub bot identity. Searches ran 2026-10-09.

**Related:** [#4984](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/4984) (sibling PRs missed once the session branch leaves `/root`; same symptom, manual `claim-pr` fixes it), [#5986](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/5986) (design says `ao report --pr-created <url>` should make the PR visible immediately; open). Worth cross-linking rather than duplicating #4984.

### Version info

AO desktop 0.13.5, macOS, daemon bundled with the app. Workers are codex and claude-code TUI sessions. PRs are opened with a dedicated GitHub bot identity (`GH_CONFIG_DIR` in the project env), not the identity of the person who runs AO.

### Minimal repro

1. Register a GitHub project. Spawn a worker; its branch is `ao/<session>/root`.
2. In the worker, push a branch under the session namespace (`ao/<session>/root` itself, or a sibling like `ao/<session>/<topic>`) and open a PR with `gh pr create` (author is the bot account).
3. Run `ao report --pr-created <pr-url>` (or `ao report --done --pr-created <pr-url>`).
4. Wait several poll intervals. Look at `ao session ls` (PR column shows `-`) and the session card.

### Expected

The PR attaches to the session: via branch-namespace discovery, and certainly after the worker explicitly reports it with `--pr-created`. The card moves off "Awaiting PR" and CI/review state populates.

### Actual

The card stays on "Awaiting PR" and the `pr` table has no row for the session. It happens on `ao/<session>/<topic>` branches and after `ao report --pr-created`. We observed it repeatedly across 2026-10-07..09 on both hosts, which is why our merge watcher runs `ao session claim-pr <session> <pr-url>` for every open PR whose head branch starts with `ao/<session>/`. `ao session claim-pr` attaches immediately every time.

Not reproduced in this session (the probe session had no PR yet). Currently attached PRs on the MacBook (for example a worker PR from `ao/<session>/root`) did attach, so the failure is intermittent or depends on something we have not isolated. Candidate factors, unverified: PR opened by a bot identity different from the daemon's `gh` login; sibling branch under `/root` (#4984); poll timing around the first push. We have no daemon log excerpt to attach; if upstream wants one, we can capture `daemon.log` around the next occurrence.

### Workaround

`ao session claim-pr <session> <pr-url>` (a merge watcher does it automatically). In 0.13.5, `ao review trigger --pr <url>` also attaches an untracked PR before reviewing.

### Suggested ask

Make `ao report --pr-created <url>` an authoritative association (as #5986 proposes) and log (or surface in the card) why branch discovery skipped a PR whose head branch is under the session namespace.

title: bug(updater): daemon relaunched after auto-update loses env from the original launch (GH_CONFIG_DIR); SCM sync silently stops
body:
Environment for all five: AO desktop 0.13.5 on macOS (Darwin 27); `ao --version` prints `dev`, so the bundled build is identified by the app version. Two hosts (MacBook and Mac mini), each with its own daemon. Workers and reviewers: codex, claude-code (Claude Code 2.1.295) and others. Projects set `env.GH_CONFIG_DIR` to a dedicated GitHub bot identity. Searches ran 2026-10-09.

**Related:** [#5575](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/5575) (Linux: relaunch after update can leave the app dead with no error surfaced; same "no error surfaced" theme, different platform and failure), [#3562](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/3562) (environment handling around the bundled binary). No existing issue covers env loss on macOS relaunch.

### Version info

AO desktop 0.13.5 (and the nightlies before it) on macOS. The app was started from a shell that exported `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, which `gh` needs to find the bot account's token. The same applies to any variable exported only at launch (we also use `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`).

### Minimal repro

1. Quit AO. Start it from a shell with `GH_CONFIG_DIR=<dir with a gh login>` exported, so the daemon inherits it. Verify with `ps eww -p <daemon pid>`: `GH_CONFIG_DIR=` is present.
2. Register a GitHub project whose PRs only the `GH_CONFIG_DIR` login can read. Confirm `sqlite3 -readonly ~/.ao/data/ao.db "select max(observed_at) from pr"` advances every poll.
3. Let the app auto-update and restart itself (or click "Restart to update"). The relaunch happens through the updater, so the new process does not get the original shell environment.
4. Check the daemon: `ps eww -p <new daemon pid>` no longer shows `GH_CONFIG_DIR`.
5. Push to an open PR. Watch `pr.head_sha` and `pr.observed_at`.

### Expected

Either the relaunched daemon keeps the environment it was launched with, or AO has a supported place to persist it (project env is already configured for sessions, but the daemon's own `gh` calls evidently do not use it). If SCM polling cannot authenticate, AO surfaces an error (card badge, `ao doctor`, daemon status).

### Actual

The daemon comes back up and looks healthy. PR sync silently stops: `pr.observed_at` freezes, `pr.head_sha` falls behind GitHub, CI and review state go stale, and AO reviews run against old heads. No error appears in the UI or `ao session ls`. We noticed only because our merge watcher kept failing reviews at stale heads ("Opus failed 3x"), hours later. The restart evidence is the mtime of `~/.ao/update-restart/` and a daemon start time that differs from the app's.

Observed in practice on one of our two hosts during 2026-10-07..09 (our notes do not record which). Not reproduced live in this probe: on 2026-10-09 both daemons were started with `GH_CONFIG_DIR` present (verified value-free with `ps eww`), `observed_at` was within a few minutes of now on both hosts, and live PR heads matched `pr.head_sha`. The claim "the relaunch drops env" is our diagnosis from the pattern (stale `observed_at` plus a missing variable on the daemon process, fixed by relaunching with the variable), not a captured updater trace.

### Workaround

A wrapper (`ao-relaunch --ensure`) relaunches AO with the required variables and strips SSH variables. After any auto-update, check that `max(observed_at)` in the `pr` table is recent; if not, relaunch.

### Suggested ask

(1) Preserve the launch environment across updater relaunches, or document where daemon-level env belongs. (2) Treat repeated SCM auth/poll failures as a visible state (card badge or `ao doctor` finding), since a frozen `observed_at` is currently the only signal.

title: bug(delivery): review feedback and /send return ok but are dropped when the worker's agent process has exited; session not marked exited
body:
Environment for all five: AO desktop 0.13.5 on macOS (Darwin 27); `ao --version` prints `dev`, so the bundled build is identified by the app version. Two hosts (MacBook and Mac mini), each with its own daemon. Workers and reviewers: codex, claude-code (Claude Code 2.1.295) and others. Projects set `env.GH_CONFIG_DIR` to a dedicated GitHub bot identity. Searches ran 2026-10-09.

**Related:** [#6064](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6064) (reviewer pane dead-ends when the controller stops), [#5790](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/5790) (session shows Exited while the agent still runs: the reverse state mismatch), [#6454](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6454) (session marked exited while TUI is live), [#2170](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/2170) (stale-head suppression; closed). None covers delivery to an exited agent.

### Version info

AO desktop 0.13.5, macOS. Observed with codex and claude-code TUI workers whose agent finished and exited after `ao report --done`; the supervisor process (`ao agent-process supervise`) stays alive.

### Minimal repro

1. Spawn a TUI worker. Let it open a PR and run `ao report --done`; the agent exits (`pgrep -P <supervise pid>` shows no child).
2. Run `ao review trigger <session>` on its PR with `changes_requested` as the verdict (or wait for auto-review to produce one).
3. Wait. Then also `POST /api/v1/sessions/<id>/send {"message":"..."}`.
4. Inspect the worker's transcript/rollout for the message, and `review_run.delivered_at` for the run.

### Expected

Either delivery fails with an error (the session is exited; resume the agent first), or AO resumes the agent (`ao session resume-agent <id>` exists) and delivers. `delivered_at` stays NULL until delivery really happens, and the card shows "feedback not delivered".

### Actual

`/send` returns ok, but nothing lands in the worker rollout or transcript. Review findings never reach the worker; the card sits on "Needs review"/"changes requested" for hours with no new push. We detect it only by checking the supervisor for a live child process or searching the transcript for our message. `ao send` on TUI sessions can also exit 0 with nothing delivered.

Supporting data (read-only counts from `review_run`, 2026-10-09): `changes_requested` runs with `delivered_at` set vs NULL. MacBook: 6 auto-triggered (all delivered), 36 manual delivered, 16 manual not delivered. Mac mini: 9 auto (all delivered), 4 manual delivered, 18 manual not delivered. Many NULLs are runs superseded by a newer head or relayed by hand, so this is indicative, not a measured drop rate. All runs had `auto_inject_review = 1`.

We did not re-run a destructive probe for this report (it would mutate a live session). The AGENT_EXITED/ok mismatch is from operational history; a one-off probe on a throwaway project would give exact response bodies.

### Workaround

Check the supervisor for a child before relying on delivery. If the agent is gone, kill the session and spawn a fresh worker with `--claim-pr <url>` and the review body (`select body from review_run where ... verdict='changes_requested'`) in the prompt. We plan to try `ao session resume-agent <id>` then re-deliver (our internal tracking).

### Suggested ask

Return a clear error (or `AGENT_EXITED`) from `/send` and review delivery when no agent process is attached, keep the review undelivered, and optionally auto-resume the agent before delivery.

title: feat(session): switch Chat and Terminal interfaces instantly
body:
## What changes for the user

Switching an orchestrator between Chat and Terminal now shows the destination on the click itself. The daemon still does the handoff behind it.

- **Terminal to Chat.** The chat page appears at once with the composer docked at the bottom (or centered if the chat has no messages yet), the startup shimmer and a placeholder that follows the controller. Messages fade in once they load. The old transcript no longer flashes, hides and reappears.
- **Chat to Terminal.** The terminal appears at once with a one-character spinner (`| / - \`) and a short line that changes ("Preparing the orchestrator", "Warming up the agent", ...). The "Terminal ended" strip no longer shows while the new terminal starts.
- **Opening an orchestrator whose agent has exited.** The button opens the chat immediately and the resume runs in the background, instead of waiting about 2s for `resume-agent` to return.
- **Plain navigation is quiet.** Opening a session whose last handoff had already finished no longer replays the shimmer or the fade. A handoff counts as in progress only if this view saw it running or started it.

## How it works

- `useSessionInterfaceSwitch` keeps a click-time `switchIntent` and derives `optimisticTarget` / `renderedMode` from it. A running turn that has to drain keeps the old surface, cloud sessions are unchanged, and a failed or cancelled switch falls back to the committed mode.
- `SessionChatSurface` renders a starting snapshot for the whole arrival (over any cached transcript). `ChatWorkspace` docks or centers the composer from `session.lastUserMessageAt`.
- `TerminalPane` takes a `booting` prop and shows the spinner status instead of the ended or empty chrome.
- Local resume shares one in-flight request per session (`resumeOnce`), so the session page's resume-on-open joins the click's resume.

## Behavior changes worth a look

- A failed resume now leaves you on the chat page with the error shown, instead of staying on the previous page. Two tests were updated.
- A remote-host terminal to chat switch now leaves the terminal at once instead of keeping it up with input fenced. One test was updated.

## Not in this PR

- The reused-session-id fix that stopped a stale prompt replaying is #6471.
- A dotted project name (for example `ronish.dev`) still breaks terminal start with `invalid activity id`. It predates this change.
- The terminal loader text is English only.

## Verification

- Typecheck clean. Full frontend suite: only failures in `browser-profile-import` (22), `ContextMeter` (2) and the `ChatWorkspace` context-usage test (1), all untouched by this PR.
- Checked live in the desktop app: instant switches in both directions, spinner visible, no ended strip, no animation on board to orchestrator navigation.

title: feat(mobile): add phone-mediated Watch inbox and complication
body:
Code changes: +360 -0\
Tests: +116 -0\
Others: +786 -0 (mostly `package-lock.json`, plus README, plists, target config)

Stack 1/2. The follow-up with wrist actions is stacked on this PR.

## What

Adds a read-only Apple Watch companion to the mobile app: an **AOWatch** inbox (list and detail of Needs-you items) and an **AOAttention** WidgetKit complication / Smart Stack widget that shows the attention count. The phone sends the data. The Watch has no network client and no credentials.

## Why

Users should be able to see that an agent needs them without taking out their phone, and the count must never claim "0" when the real count is unknown.

## How

- **Targets:** `@bacons/apple-targets` (pinned) generates the `watch` and `watch-widget` targets from `targets/`. Shared Foundation model in `watch-model/` (a SwiftPM package that is symlinked into both targets). Local iOS Expo module `modules/ao-watch/` wraps WatchConnectivity. Generated `ios/` is never edited. These source dirs are explicit `fingerprint.config.js` inputs, because this needs a new native binary and can't ship over the air (OTA). Requires watchOS 10+. Android is a no-op.
- **Snapshot (`lib/watch/snapshot.ts`, `WatchManager.tsx`):** while AO is in the foreground, the phone publishes a bounded, sanitized Needs-you snapshot every 30s. It reuses the existing multi-host polling and `agentsView` semantics, including pinned workers. Limits: 8 hosts and 8 rows per host. Counts include hidden rows, and hosts that were left out are marked explicitly. Each snapshot goes through `updateApplicationContext` and replaces the previous one.
- **Freshness:** freshness comes from the timestamp of the original successful poll, not from when the bridge delivered it. Data is treated as stale after more than 2 minutes, after failures, or when host coverage is partial. Stale data shows as **N+** (known attention) or **—** (unknown), never a fresh-looking zero. Disconnected hosts keep their last-known rows. The Watch caches the snapshot in a Watch-only App Group shared with the widget. The widget timeline schedules a stale entry at expiry, and its refresh rate is set by the OS budget, so it is not real-time.
- "Open on iPhone" is an instruction to the user. The Watch does not remote-launch iOS.

Reviewers should focus on the snapshot bounds and sanitization, how unknown vs. zero is handled, and the fingerprint/target config.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test` pass on this branch (211 files / 1,894 tests, Node 22.22.2) on `main` `c3e17362a`. CI `check` and `scan` pass. The original worker ran this commit on Node 20: 167 files / 1,567 tests passed. *Local Node 20.12.2 can't run Vitest here because it is below rolldown's `^20.19` engine floor, so npm skips the native binding. CI's Node 20 resolves to a newer 20.x.*
- Snapshot contract written test-first (`lib/watch/snapshot.test.ts`).
- Swift Foundation model assertions pass (`./scripts/test-watch-model.sh`): freshness and count display.
- `npx expo prebuild --clean --platform ios --no-install` is clean. The generated target embeddings, autolinking and fingerprint coverage were inspected.
- Rebased onto `main` `c3e17362a` (first `33569b9fb`, then again after #6558). The only conflict was in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, against main's new `@ao/response-selection` / `@bsky.app/react-native-uitextview` deps. Both sides are kept, and the lockfile was regenerated from main's (+644 lines, the same as before).
- **CI fix (`9fd47d95a`):** main's new `lib/settings-sheet.test.tsx` renders `app/_layout`, which now mounts `WatchManager`. Its bridge imports `expo`, and `expo` needs the RN `__DEV__` global that Vitest lacks. The test now mocks `./watch/WatchManager` alongside the other root managers.
- **Native build (Xcode 27.0, 27A266a), at `c652c2446` on `33569b9fb`.** The same native sources were rebuilt as part of the stacked #6488 tip on `c3e17362a`, with the same results. Steps: `npx expo prebuild -p ios --clean`, `pod install`, then `xcodebuild … CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build`:
  - `-scheme AOWatch`, watchOS 27.0 Simulator, Apple Watch Series 12 (46mm): **BUILD SUCCEEDED**
  - `-scheme AO`, iOS 27.1 Simulator, iPhone Duo: **BUILD SUCCEEDED**
  - Products: `AO.app/Watch/AOWatch.app`, which embeds `AOWatch.app/PlugIns/AOAttention.appex`.
- **Native QA fix (`e72727d16`):** the Expo module pod was named `AOWatch`, the same name as the apple-targets Watch app. That gave the workspace two `AOWatch` schemes, and the watchOS build failed with `watchOS Simulator platform doesn't match libAOWatch.a's supported platforms`. The pod and native module are renamed to `AOWatchBridge` (podspec, `Name()`, `requireOptionalNativeModule`), so the schemes are now `AO`, `AOWatch` and `AOWatchBridge`.

**Pending:** the sanitized empty/busy/stale/blocked screenshots, signing, and the physical-device QA below. Simulator builds are not evidence of WatchConnectivity delivery. Mobile CI does not compile iOS/watchOS or run Swift checks, so a green CI here is TS-only evidence.

### Physical paired-device QA checklist (merge gate)

- [ ] **Notification mirroring:** with iOS/Watch notification permissions on, cause a needs-input transition. Apple routes it normally (not to both devices). Check Focus behavior and the real notification haptics.
- [ ] **Locked phone:** lock, suspend, then force-quit phone AO. The Watch cache stays readable, the age keeps growing, and the stale/unavailable state is explicit. Reopening the phone recovers.
- [ ] **Daemon offline:** disconnect the daemon, then the phone, then start with no cache. Unknown is never shown as zero. Partial host coverage shows partial counts with correct host labels.
- [ ] **Revoked credentials:** rotate or revoke the daemon password through the normal desktop flow. Failure is safe, and things recover after re-pairing.
- [ ] **Duplicate/expired approval:** N/A for this read-only PR. Covered in the stacked PR.
- [ ] **Complication freshness:** add each complication family and a Smart Stack widget. Check after 2 min, after a day, and after reconnecting. The last-known count and age match the inbox. Check wrist-down privacy and VoiceOver.
- [ ] **Haptics:** only system notification haptics. No custom or guaranteed-immediate haptics are promised.
- [ ] Two daemon hosts with overlapping session IDs: no host mix-ups. Forgetting a host removes its rows on the next delivered snapshot.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(mobile): add confirmed Watch permissions and replies
body:
Stacked on #6487

Code changes: +445 -19\
Tests: +254 -0\
Others: +53 -3

*(Counts are for this PR's own commits only. This is a cross-repo PR from a fork, so it targets `main`, and until #6487 merges the diff here also shows that PR's commit. Review only the commits after `feat(mobile): add phone-mediated Watch inbox and complication`.)*

## What

Stack 2/2. Adds confirmed wrist actions to the Watch companion: one-time approve/deny for a deliberately small set of permission requests, and reviewed replies (canned or dictated) to pending input or chat. Every action is reviewed on the wrist, and the phone carries it out over the existing Chat routes.

## Why

The simplest prompts (a read-only command approval, a short reply) should be answerable from the wrist. That must not create a second, weaker path for approvals.

## How

- **Transport:** reachable `WCSession.sendMessage` only. The native bridge (`AOWatchModule.swift`) accepts one live request, and only while phone AO and its JS listener are foreground-ready. It fails closed otherwise. Timeouts are 20s on the bridge and 25s on the Watch. If the response is lost after a write, the result is **Delivery unknown**, not success or failure. There is no background action service, `transferUserInfo`, deferred decision, automatic retry, or Watch-to-daemon network path.
- **Binding (`lib/watch/actions.ts`):** action tokens live only in phone memory and are bound to identity and config: host, session and request. They expire after 60s. The phone re-fetches the current pending context before any write. Duplicate and already-handled requests map to typed outcomes: HTTP 409 `CHAT_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING` becomes **Already handled**, and HTTP 400 `CHAT_DECISION_NOT_OFFERED` is preserved.
- **Approvals:** the provider must have offered a semantic `allow_once` / `reject_once` decision, matched by its exact offered ID. Decisions are never inferred from labels. The Codex adapter (`backend/.../codexappserver/conversation.go`) marks the detail `scopeComplete` only when its projection dropped no request field (network context, environment, network policy amendments, approval callbacks or unknown fields), and the Watch requires that flag. Partial projections and older daemons defer to iPhone. The initial allow-list covers Codex approvals for the literal commands `pwd`, `git status`, `git status --short`, `git status --short --branch` and `git log -1 --oneline`, with cwd and reason shown in full. Wrapped, destructive or unknown commands, broad grants, TUI prompts and non-command permissions are deferred to the iPhone.
- **Replies:** a single plain-string input property, or an ordinary message only when a full read proves nothing is pending. Max 500 Unicode scalars. Each reviewed draft gets a stable `clientMessageId` (`lib/chat/api.ts`, `types.ts`) so a repeated delivery creates one message.
- **Watch UI (`WatchActionsView.swift`, `WatchActionState.swift`):** explicit **Confirm and send**, a 60s review window, and no merge/spawn/kill/terminal controls.

Reviewers should focus on the allow-list and binding logic in `actions.ts`, plus the fail-closed paths in the native bridge.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test` pass on this branch tip (213 files / 1,912 tests, Node 22.22.2) on `main` `c3e17362a`. The original worker's Node 20 run passed on the pre-review commit (168 files / 1,583 tests). *Local Node 20.12.2 can't run Vitest here because it is below rolldown's `^20.19` engine floor. CI's Node 20 resolves to a newer 20.x.*
- Review follow-up (883414cb0): Go `TestParseApprovalMarksOnlyCompleteCommandScope` exercises the real `parseApproval` projection. The `codexappserver` package passes with `-skip TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider`. That test compares the generated protocol with the locally installed Codex binary, and the binary has drifted on this machine; the change touches neither. `lib/watch/AOWatchModule.source.test.ts` guards readiness across a paired-Watch switch.
- Action boundaries written test-first: `lib/watch/actions.test.ts` covers binding, expiry, offered-decision checks, dedup and typed errors. `lib/chatModeApi.test.ts` covers `clientMessageId`.
- Swift Foundation review-state assertions pass (`ActionTests.swift`, via `./scripts/test-watch-model.sh`).
- `npx expo prebuild --clean --platform ios --no-install` is clean.
- **Rebased** onto #6487's tip `9fd47d95a` (`main` `c3e17362a` + the `AOWatchBridge` rename + the CI test mock). The `Name()` conflict is resolved to `AOWatchBridge`, and `bridge.ts` uses `requireOptionalNativeModule("AOWatchBridge")`. `f1eeff416` gives each mocked Watch Chat API call a fresh `Response`, because main's API boundary (#6558) now reads every body.
- **Native build (Xcode 27.0, 27A266a), at `6f370c2a3` on `c3e17362a`** (the only later commit changes a test): `npx expo prebuild -p ios --clean`, `pod install` (127 pods), then `xcodebuild … CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build`:
  - `-scheme AOWatch`, watchOS 27.0 Simulator, Apple Watch Series 12 (46mm): **BUILD SUCCEEDED**
  - `-scheme AO`, iOS 27.1 Simulator, iPhone Duo: **BUILD SUCCEEDED**
  - Products: `AO.app/Watch/AOWatch.app`, which embeds `PlugIns/AOAttention.appex`.

**Pending:** sanitized screenshots, signing, and the physical-device QA below. Node and Swift Foundation tests are not evidence of WatchConnectivity delivery, SwiftUI or dictation behavior, and Mobile CI does not compile iOS/watchOS.

### Physical paired-device QA checklist (merge gate)

- [ ] **Notification mirroring:** a needs-input notification routes normally, and acting from the Watch inbox opens the same request the phone shows.
- [ ] **Locked phone:** with the phone locked, suspended or force-quit, actions show **Open on iPhone** and never queue for later. Reopen AO in the foreground and retry only after reviewing the current context.
- [ ] **Daemon offline:** the action is rejected or shows explicit uncertainty, with no deferred approval after reconnecting.
- [ ] **Revoked credentials:** an authorization failure shows clearly, with no success haptic.
- [ ] **Duplicate/expired approval:** answer on the phone first, then confirm on the Watch, and expect **Already handled**. Change the offered decisions or scope, or let the 60s review expire: no write. Repeated delivery of a reply creates one message. An unoffered decision keeps HTTP 400 `CHAT_DECISION_NOT_OFFERED`.

title: fix(tmux): deliver sends as bracketed paste so codex submits them
body:
Code changes: +52 -35  
Tests: +117 -66  
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #3626

## Root cause
Every `ao send` is **multiline**: the message is wrapped in the `<ao-session-delivery id="…">\n…\n</ao-session-delivery>` envelope. The tmux runtime typed the text into the pane with `send-keys -l`. That gives the TUI a burst of keystrokes, not a paste. Codex's paste-burst heuristic then sometimes treats the trailing Enter, 300ms later, as a newline inside the burst, and the prompt sits unsubmitted. That's why single-paragraph ~900-char orchestrator messages also got stuck. The problem was never that the text was multiline. The real issue was that the text arrived as keystrokes.

I reproduced this on a live codex 0.161 TUI in tmux, using AO's exact sequence (envelope plus a ~900-char single-line body, `send-keys -l`, 300ms, `Enter`): the old path left the draft unsubmitted in 3 of 4 runs.

## Fix
- The text is staged in a uniquely named tmux buffer (`set-buffer`, chunked as before to stay under tmux's command-size limit).
- It is then delivered with a single `paste-buffer -p -r -d`:
  - `-p`: tmux adds bracketed-paste markers only if the pane's app enabled bracketed paste. Codex, claude-code and other TUIs get exactly one paste event.
  - `-r`: newlines stay LF, so apps that did *not* enable bracketed paste (shells) get byte-for-byte what `send-keys -l` used to send.
  - `-d`: the buffer is deleted after the paste.
- There is still **exactly one Enter**, with no retries and no new nudge path. Codex's permission safety (#2357/#3231, `EmitsBlockedActivity=false`) is unchanged, so this can never answer an approval dialog.
- Cancellation got simpler and safer. A caller cancel while staging leaves nothing in the pane (the partial buffer is deleted). From the paste onward, paste, pause and Enter are detached as before, so a draft is never stranded.

## Why not #3741
#3741, closed as stale, only lengthened the paste→Enter delay. That narrows the race but keeps the timing heuristic (on a loaded machine, chunks and Enter can still land in one read). This PR removes the race: the bracketed paste tells codex exactly where the pasted text ends. No `confirmActive` change was needed.

## Tests
- New `TestSendMessageUsesBracketedPasteIntegration` (real tmux): a stand-in TUI enables bracketed paste and records the raw bytes it receives. It **failed before the fix** (`"line one\nline two\r"`) and passes after (`"\x1b[200~line one\nline two\x1b[201~\r"`).
- Unit tests updated or added for the command sequence (`set-buffer` chunks → `paste-buffer -p -r -d` → `Enter`), cancel-while-staging, and Enter surviving a caller cancel after the paste.
- Live check against codex 0.161 using the new sequence at the default 300ms delay: 6 of 6 submitted (envelope plus ~900-char single line, a 25-line message, ~3k chars), compared with 1 of 4 on the old path.
- `go test -race` on `internal/adapters/runtime/...`, `internal/session_manager`, `internal/sessionguard`: pass. The full `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes except `codexappserver` `TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider`, which compares against the locally installed codex binary (0.161) and doesn't involve this change. `go vet ./...` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 on the runtime packages: clean.

## Not covered
- **ConPTY (Windows)** is unchanged. It writes chunks straight into the PTY and doesn't expose whether the app enabled bracketed paste. Wrapping blindly would inject literal escape sequences into apps that didn't ask for them. I can't verify codex-on-Windows input handling here, so that should be a follow-up if Windows users hit this.

title: bug(remote-hosts): desktop connects to its own account-synced host
body:
## Bug

A macOS AO host paired from a second signed-in desktop is synced back to its own desktop as a remote host. The sidebar then lists the same local project and session twice: once locally and once with its own host badge.

Reported by Dhruv Sharma in this chat on 2026-10-10, using nightly v0.13.6-nightly.202610092159. Reproduced with real remote-host, registry, local workspace, and remote workspace hooks against main c72956ae6, with synthetic account/transport fixtures. Confidence: high.

## Reproduction

1. Open current AO on Macs A and B with the same AO account and remote-host connections enabled.
2. Enable remote hosting on A and pair A from B.
3. Allow the account host directory to sync on A.
4. Observe A's local project/session again under A's remote host badge.

## Root cause and fix

`useRemoteHosts` imports all account host records and connects every saved host without excluding the current daemon's stable `/api/v1/identity` host ID. Filter the local host from connections/sidebar data while retaining the saved and cloud records for other clients. Do not deduplicate by project name or delete the account host.

## Evidence and scope

The same-host fixture failed deterministically before the fix with two copies of its one project and one session. Separate macOS Mobile QR behavior under tunnel-only hosting is not part of this issue. Screenshots are not republished because they include account/project information.

title: feat: add Letta Code terminal harness
body:
Code changes: +463 -23  
Tests: +459 -2  
Others: +51 -3  

Withdrawn after independent source review: Letta Code v0.34.9 (`cbf9026030c74e60432c246aec2bb0ec08fd49bc`) cannot safely support the private instruction and lifecycle boundaries claimed by this prototype. This PR is closed without merging; no replacement gate-only PR is proposed.

Four concrete blockers in the pinned upstream source:

- **Private instructions can leak into the visible transcript.** `src/hooks/executor.ts:429` accumulates successful UserPromptSubmit stdout; `src/cli/app/use-submit-handler.ts:662-675` prints all accumulated feedback if a later hook blocks. `quiet` suppresses executor logging but not this rendering.
- **UserPromptSubmit is not acceptance.** Later hooks and pending approvals can reject submission (`use-submit-handler.ts:652-712`), so acknowledging an AO delivery there is premature.
- **Stop is not settled idle.** Stop hooks may veto completion and subsequent turn_end mods may continue the conversation (`src/cli/app/use-conversation-loop.ts:1490-1582`).
- **Permission state cannot be reliably correlated.** PermissionRequest omits tool_call_id (`src/hooks/index.ts:179-190`), while permission checking precedes PreToolUse for client tools (`src/tools/manager.ts:2192`); AO cannot reliably clear that blocked observation.

Before closure, the branch removed raw private-context output and unsupported submit, semantic-acceptance, permission-blocked and Stop-idle signals. It retains an unmerged prototype for reference. Native mods were investigated, but the released API has no additive per-process mod file flag, turn_start remains cancellable, turn_end still allows continuation, and llm_start is local-only. A future integration needs a proven common contract that preserves native settings and mods.

The prototype included dedicated conversations, exact conv-* restore, explicit permission mapping, model/install/setup surfaces, API/product registration and migration 0196. These changes are not shipping.

title: feat(chat): batch pending messages and flush the queue alongside steering
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Summary

For Chat-mode agent sessions, deliver all pending messages together at the next delivery opportunity instead of starting a separate agent turn and waiting for a response for each queued message. If a steer arrives while messages are queued, deliver the queued messages alongside that steer.

This applies to all message sources, not only agent-to-agent messages. Terminal UI sessions are explicitly out of scope.

## Flow 1: Drain the queue as one delivery after the current turn

1. An agent is working in Chat mode.
2. Multiple ordinary messages arrive from one or more agents while it works. These messages do not use `--steer`.
3. The current agent turn finishes.
4. Deliver every message already waiting together in the next provider input, so the agent can consider them together and respond in one turn.

Do not send message A, wait for the agent's response, send message B, wait again, and repeat. Messages arriving during that next turn form the next pending batch.

## Flow 2: Steer also flushes pending messages

1. An agent is working in Chat mode and ordinary messages are waiting.
2. A steer message arrives.
3. Deliver the steer and the already-pending messages together through the active-turn steering path, rather than steering with only the new message and leaving the rest queued.

If the turn finishes during this operation, preserve the existing steer-to-normal-turn semantics and deliver the batch once. Do not drop or duplicate messages because of the transition.

## All message sources follow the same rule

Include ordinary agent messages, review comments, changes-requested notifications, merge-conflict messages, and other AO-delivered messages addressed to the agent. Do not introduce a separate sequential delivery behavior for review or lifecycle notifications.

Batching is a delivery behavior, not permission to reclassify messages. Preserve each message's content, origin, sender metadata, and safe display-name session link. Keep individual provenance visible in the Chat transcript, even if the provider receives one combined input. Preserve existing hidden-context rules for piggybacked worker reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- Multiple queued messages are delivered in one next-turn input, without waiting for a response between messages.
- A steer includes all messages already pending at the delivery boundary.
- Queue order is deterministic and preserves enqueue order; the new steer must remain identifiable as the steer rather than being disguised as an ordinary sender message.
- Messages from different senders retain distinct provenance and content.
- Review comments, merge-conflict notifications, changes-requested notices, and ordinary messages use the same batching behavior.
- Queue draining and steer flushing use a consistent delivery boundary so concurrent arrivals, turn completion, and retries cannot lose or duplicate messages.
- Messages are not reported as delivered merely because they were enqueued. Existing delivery handles and recovery behavior remain meaningful for each included message.
- Failed or uncertain provider delivery preserves recoverability rather than silently discarding the pending batch or blindly replaying accepted content.
- Preserve message boundaries and disclose any provider input-size limit. Do not silently truncate, summarize, or drop content to build a batch.
- No behavior change for Terminal UI sessions.

## Regression coverage

- One queued message and multiple queued messages, from one and multiple senders.
- An active turn finishing with several pending messages.
- Steer arrival with an empty queue and with several pending messages.
- Concurrent enqueue during queue draining and steer delivery.
- Turn completion racing with steer delivery.
- Mixed ordinary, review-comment, changes-requested, and merge-conflict messages.
- Delivery failure, uncertain outcomes, retry/recovery, and duplicate delivery handles.
- Transcript attribution, safe sender links, and hidden worker-report context remain intact.
- Terminal UI behavior remains unchanged.

## Related issues

- #5833 tracks queued PR nudges incorrectly reported as delivered behind a stale turn. This request defines batching behavior, rather than only stale-turn recovery.
- #6299 tracks Claude background-task overlap leaving a queued turn working indefinitely. This request should not regress that lifecycle behavior.

title: bug(mobile): tunnel-only host has no pairing QR despite ready endpoint
body:
## Bug

Connect Mobile shows “No network address found for this computer” and no QR code after `ao remote-host enable --tunnel-only`, even when the daemon advertises a ready HTTPS tunnel.

Reported by Dhruv Sharma in this Codex chat on macOS with the latest nightly. Analyzed and reproduced against `4273bec7c638ea078fbead68090286315bc1b90a`.

**Confidence:** High. Rendered regression tests reproduce the exact message with a valid HTTPS endpoint and empty legacy LAN fields.
**Priority:** Medium. Manual address/password pairing is a workaround.

## Reproduction

1. Open a remote-capable AO nightly on macOS.
2. Enable remote access with the bundled CLI: `ao remote-host enable --tunnel-only`.
3. Wait for `ao remote-host status` to advertise a ready HTTPS address.
4. Open Settings → Mobile / Connect Mobile.

Expected: the v2 QR contains the daemon's stable host ID, existing pairing token, and advertised HTTPS endpoint. While the tunnel starts, show a pending state.

Actual: a LAN-address requirement suppresses the QR and shows an unrelated Wi-Fi/Ethernet/Tailscale hint.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/ConnectMobileContent.tsx` already builds the v2 pairing payload from the daemon's `endpoints` list. A second `activeHost` check still requires the legacy `status.host` LAN field. Tunnel-only intentionally leaves that field empty while advertising ready HTTPS endpoints.

Two rendered regressions fail on current main with `npm test -- src/renderer/components/ConnectMobileModal.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2 -t 'tunnel-only'`: the ready QR is absent and the starting state shows the wrong hint.

## Fix

Use the daemon's canonical advertised endpoints for QR readiness and connection presentation. Preserve existing LAN behavior, secure-pairing restrictions, host identity, and credentials. Do not change transport or enable new network listeners.

## Related

- #6491 and #6495 concern this machine appearing as its own remote connection.
- #5485 concerns advertising the Tailscale HTTPS proxy in the daemon. This issue concerns the renderer rejecting already-advertised tunnel endpoints.

## Summary

Chat records daemon-confirmed AO session mutations as `ao_action` activities. The collapsed label is a short verb. Expansion holds the target, prior value, link, and status. Replay of the same operation settles one row. A write failure does not change the mutation result. A new UTC migration admits the activity kind on existing SQLite databases.

Desktop Archive calls `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/kill`. Kanban archive is derived from `isTerminated`. The daemon emits `session.terminated` for that kill. There is no separate archive mutation.

There is no daemon pull-request creation path (`CreatePullRequest` does not exist). `pull_request.created` is renderer vocabulary only. A shell `ao spawn` or an MCP `create_pull_request` stays an ordinary command or tool activity. This PR does not claim end-to-end capture of pull request creation.

## Changes

- Kind `ao_action` with `detail.action` (no `detail.event`, so existing run batching stays intact). Actions: `session.spawned`, `session.terminated`, `session.renamed`, `session.restored`, `pull_request.claimed`, plus render-only `session.agent_switched` and `pull_request.created`.
- Stable `providerItemId` `ao-action:{action}:{operationID}`. Spawn success uses the child session id and is written on the parent conversation when `ParentSessionID` is set. Failures and cancellations use the pre-wrap error so `context.Canceled` stays cancelled. A successful rename includes a fresh id, so repeating the same rename writes a new row. Replay settles one row for spawn, kill, restore, and claim.
- Rename skips an unchanged name and does not record the orchestrator-rename refusal. Claim keeps https hrefs and drops `javascript:` and other non-allowlisted links. Text is capped at 160 runes.
