All eight new AO action count keys lacked the CLDR `many` form in Spanish, French, and Brazilian Portuguese. Head `22cebc81553db6c7ad78734c95ea2a2ad5f84218` adds those 24 translations and a regression that resolves each key at 1,000,000, where those locales select `many`. Pre-merge head `559d2dfb528a81466faf8d19e41276e509d35109` passed frontend typecheck, the focused i18n suite (21 of 21), and the combined locale and action rendering set (34 of 34). The complete local renderer run was stopped after unrelated tests broadly timed out under host load. Required CI will validate the full suite on its runner.

## Earlier main reconciliation

Merged main `0c11049ce0bc1613428e67cc28bfc6fb09c68acd` into the existing PR at `57392138d7cbe3157d5d9baffd947088ce087459`. The three textual conflicts retain main's spawn-budget fake fields, auto-resume SQL query, and two usage-limit migrations alongside the AO action fake observer and migration ledger entry. Current Chat question/outcome/usage-limit behavior and AO action rendering remain in the merged tree. Pinned sqlc and API regeneration yielded no drift.

On the merged head, the complete affected Go session, SQLite, store, and HTTP suites passed. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and the session and SQLite store race suites passed. The focused AO action, timeline, and locale renderer set passed 67 of 67.

## Claim review follow-up

Head `a7cc2169c8d5391e18b8a53a4dc3155b6c271f8d` gives failed PR re-claims a request-scoped operation ID even when the PR URL is known. A later failed claim therefore cannot settle an earlier confirmed claim. `TestFailedReclaimKeepsConfirmedClaim` covers success followed by failure for the same URL. On this head, the full session service and SQLite store suites passed, and the new test passed under the race detector.

## Provider item lookup review follow-up

Head `2c3f361c810b29fec345acc242a3eb584095ce9f` adds migration `20261021142844923_index_conversation_activity_provider_item_lookup.sql`, a partial index on nonempty `provider_item_id`, and the matching predicate in `SelectSessionForActivityProviderItem`. A real migrated SQLite regression checks that `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` searches through the index and that rollback removes it. Pinned sqlc generation updated the generated query. The complete SQLite, SQLite store, and session service suites passed; the migration/ledger race check, `go build ./...`, and `go vet ./...` passed.

## Pending cleanup review follow-up

Head `e4068a23c6f1b6e03dcf20dc122d1b7fc320d933` records a Completed terminate action from `RequestKill` only when cleanup has finished synchronously. A request that returns `CleanupPending` emits no confirmed terminate action, since its background cleanup may still fail. `TestRequestKillDoesNotConfirmPendingCleanup` covers both pending and confirmed outcomes. The full session service suite and focused service/manager cleanup race tests passed. The full session manager suite has four unrelated macOS spawn failures because tmux is unavailable on this host.

## Switch failure message review follow-up

Head `dda0ac4d845eca86b248a3f2a72a559f6bf94233` uses the existing typed switch error translation map when expanding a failed AO action. Persisted switch activities now show a readable localized reason. An unfamiliar code shows the localized generic switch failure; errors from other actions retain their original messages. The focused chat activity and timeline suites passed, 45 of 45. Local full frontend typecheck was stopped after prolonged host resource contention. The complete renderer run reached unrelated main-process identity-probe timeouts and browser bridge failures, then was stopped without a complete result. Required exact-head CI remains the full-suite gate.

## Claim admission review follow-up

Head `3cb5fcac9ee79d56328addd3cab00698c325635e` omits claim actions for repository validation failures and missing SCM dependencies, before any claim attempt starts. Failures after the SCM lookup begins still record a failed action, preserving the earlier failed re-claim behavior. `TestClaimAdmissionRejectionsWriteNoAction` covers both preflight cases and an attempted lookup failure. The complete session service suite, focused claim race tests, `go build ./...`, and service `go vet` passed.

## Action detail key review follow-up

Head `5a25cc4ad8882c3652a46a31c74346278f1ac27d` uses the stable index for each static expanded action detail line, avoiding duplicate React keys when two lines have the same text. The affected chat activity and timeline suites passed, 45 of 45. GitHub's net diff counts remain unchanged.

## Current main reconciliation

Merged `main` at `9e347ec0268647cc58f2c4bfdfdb79832a5a32c7` into this PR at `470d2d0d6fdfc830230159dc97b6761e6f750cc4`, preserving both histories. Main replaced the old durable agent-switch saga with a new provider-switch path. Its Chat switch commits a confirmed `provider_switch` system activity with the branch, source, target, and settings. This PR removes the obsolete switch callback and race tests rather than emitting a duplicate AO switch row. The renderer keeps the `session.agent_switched` vocabulary for any earlier stored AO action and shows the current localized generic failure message without exposing a raw error code. Main's commit-selection cache, migration ledger entries, Chat timeline changes, and provider-switch marker remain intact alongside AO action recording for spawn, termination, rename, restore, and claim.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, mobile typecheck, the SQLite and SQLite store suites, API spec tests, focused provider-switch tests, AO action race tests, and the focused action/timeline/locale renderer set (67 of 67) passed. Pinned sqlc and API regeneration produced no drift.

Local full-suite gaps on this head: the session suite failed in an unrelated macOS scratch-index test because `xcrun_db` appeared in its temporary directory. The Chat suite failed starting a persistent ACP host in `TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts`. HTTP and controller suites could not bind loopback test ports under this sandbox. The complete renderer run reached unrelated main-process identity-probe and browser bridge failures, then was stopped without a final summary. Frontend typecheck remained silent for two minutes and was stopped. Exact-head CI must verify the complete suites and typecheck.

## Failed switch replay review follow-up

Head `a64674591e2d2057f5cbc7b13c0197d51feab0dc` adds a real SQLite regression for a failed Chat provider switch replayed with the same idempotency key. The current provider switch architecture commits an activity only with a successful target branch. Both failed attempts therefore leave no confirmed switch row to overwrite. The provider switch test group and its race checked run passed. The complete local Chat suite still fails in `TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts` because its persistent ACP host does not start on this host.

## AO action rollback review follow-up

Head `c980dec3a449d242f3e7d6abe6cd69c81fabaae4` keeps the widened conversation activity kind constraint when migration `20261020090353460` is rolled back, matching the earlier additive activity kind migrations. A real SQLite regression inserts an `ao_action`, rolls back, checks the row and schema, and requires `PRAGMA integrity_check` to return `ok`. The test failed against the previous Down migration. The full SQLite and SQLite store suites, plus the race checked rollback regression, pass.

## Mobile action summary review follow-up

Head `9600d022511d874001e7c702e21d60f2e5e23a86` counts `ao_action` separately in the mobile activity run summary. Consecutive actions now read `Performed 2 actions`; a mixed command and action run keeps separate counts. The pure summary moved into the timeline model for behavior regression coverage. The focused mobile model test passed 31 of 31, the complete mobile suite passed 2,442 of 2,442, and mobile typecheck passed.

## Lint CI recovery

The completed lint job for head `9600d022511d874001e7c702e21d60f2e5e23a86` reported one `sqlclosecheck` finding in `migrate_ao_action_activity_test.go`: the provider item query closed its rows manually. Head `9c35ea8b5ec02e30376119f88571fe6743713aac` scopes that query and defers its close before the rollback step. The full SQLite and SQLite store suites pass, and pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports zero issues for `./internal/storage/sqlite/...`. The complete local pinned lint run additionally reports `revive` time-naming for `scriptStepMinute` in `internal/session_manager/manager.go`; that source is identical on `origin/main` and has no diff in this PR. The separate main lint regression has been sent to the project orchestrator. Exact-head CI remains the required gate.

## Rollout

Ships with the desktop app and daemon together. Existing conversations gain activities only for mutations after this build. Migration `20261020090353460_allow_ao_action_activity.sql` expands the SQLite activity kind check while preserving existing rows, indexes, and triggers.

## Omissions

- No daemon emitter for `pull_request.created`.
- No actor HTTP header and no success inferred from command or tool prose.
- No PR merge and no release dispatch.

title: feat: add harness integration and lifecycle audit skill
body:
Code changes: +2519 -0 Tests: +1869 -0 Others: +1591 -0 Adds an AO contributor skill for assessing coding harnesses, implementing supported integration surfaces, and auditing native CLI/AO lifecycle behavior. The API-first runner preserves failed, blocked and not-run gates, including fresh instruction delivery, cancellation and exact restore. Harness-specific audit reports, JSON receipts, screenshots and provenance must be published in comments and GitHub attachments on each harness's integration PR; new evidence files must not be committed. This PR contains reusable skill guidance, the runner, fixtures and CI wiring. Version-specific investigation narratives and the dated session index are excluded from its file diff; general integration and evidence requirements remain. [Historical index and per-harness evidence](https://github.com/nikhilachale/agent-orchestrator/blob/def16c285aaab59e396c774c7dc3c8c9bfdf184d/docs/research/ao-agent-harness-session-2026-10-10.md) remain preserved at the pre-cleanup revision and through the respective integration PRs; existing evidence-file migration requires verified attachments before removal. Operational guidance now includes a compact Prepare/Launch/Doctor/Drive/Evidence/Cleanup checklist and a [journey map](https://github.com/nikhilachale/agent-orchestrator/blob/78d01a4cf93b911ee10626d19c3310a8107b39bf/.agents/skills/ao-agent-harness/references/audit-journeys.md). It maps actions to proof prerequisites and observed results, adds read-only instance checks, identifies separate UI/Chat and independent-instruction coverage, and requires evidence to survive teardown. The [ACP/shared-Chat-UI guide](https://github.com/nikhilachale/agent-orchestrator/blob/78d01a4cf93b911ee10626d19c3310a8107b39bf/.agents/skills/ao-agent-harness/references/chat-integration.md) maps the native binding, registry, typed contracts, daemon events and shared renderer. Its focused Chat checklist covers real UI creation, streaming, history/load, decisions, cancellation, reconnect, daemon recovery and exact restore. Chat Doctor uses controller/snapshot readiness rather than TUI composer cues; this adds guidance, not Chat automation to the runner. A full integration now starts by reading AO/upstream docs and existing PRs, then planning each native capability and AO gap. Supported TUI, Chat and reviewer surfaces must be qualified independently. AO Account login/setup, both model lists, persisted model enable/disable preferences and applicable picker effects, and provider/account configuration with effective native routing are explicit requirements. Reviewer registration/picker, review execution and correlated result/cancel/rerun have separate evidence checkpoints. Unsupported native behavior needs proof; unfinished AO wiring keeps the full integration incomplete. Integration handoff now requires a completion matrix covering product registration/UI, model lists/visibility, provider management, setup, OS/config readiness, branding, TUI/Chat, reviewer, permissions/instructions, lifecycle, evidence and current CI/merge state. Each row records supported scope, verification status, and proof or an omission reason. Current-status receipts separate runtime-tested builds from the current CI head, preserve sanitized reproduction inputs and distinct attempts, and reconcile stale claims/counts before handoff. These are contributor review gates; the runner schema and automation are unchanged. The skill now requires a per-harness, per-attempt screenshot index for every meaningful UI action and result: Agent Harness listing, install offer/progress/result, login/configuration or stored-credential state, Agent Harness models, New Task agent/model selection, running/output, follow-up and active-command cancellation, Kill/archive confirmation, archived entry, exact restore, and the same card back in Kanban with a fresh continuation. Supported Chat also requires real shared-UI streaming, decisions, cancellation, reconnect and recovery evidence. Each checkpoint links actual images and functional receipts with build, identity and capture provenance; failures retain original screenshots or explicit capture-unavailable reasons plus sanitized logs. Images are embedded in journey order with durable, verified links on the harness integration PR. Already installed/connected does not prove a fresh install/login. The accepted saved-credential route can qualify after fresh verified authorization and a successful provider turn; its unexercised fresh-login alternative remains explicitly labelled without blocking that route. Manual-only plans retain an explicit unexercised in-page step and can qualify only agreed manual scope. A planned/absent Agent Harness model panel remains `NOT_RUN / NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; New Task models cannot substitute. Real credentials must not be deleted to stage captures. Later reproductions cannot replace originals. Screenshots prove visible states, while native identity, provider authorization, cancellation and restored continuation require independent functional proof. These are contributor gates; the API-first runner still captures failures only and does not automate successful-step screenshots. Detailed evidence belongs in PR comments/attachments; the description links to them. Existing committed evidence is removed only after its originals and published destinations are verified; source logos/licenses and synthetic fixtures remain source files. Isolated candidate registration enables real Chat qualification before production registration. Validation: whitespace and 53 local documentation links/anchors passed, along with independent baseline/forward capability exercises and focused review. This update changes four Markdown files; runner/tests/workflow are unchanged. Current-head CI is pending. [Detailed verification and prior failure history](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6509#issuecomment-6213144479) are in the PR comment. No live harness/UI qualification is claimed. Historical run details and failures remain in the linked integration reports and earlier discussion. This contributor tooling does not add a desktop scheduler, automatic login or automatic PR publisher. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Read the skill
SKILL.md and reference guides"] B["Prepare the agent integration
and its audit configuration"] C["Run the audit
audit_ao.mjs"] D["Check startup, instructions,
cancellation and restore"] E["Save results and evidence
audit_ao.mjs + audit_evidence.mjs"] F["Review passed, failed
and blocked checks"] T["Tests + GitHub Actions
Check that the audit tools work"] A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F T -. validates .-> C T -. validates .-> E ``` Repository docs point contributors to the skill. The historical index above links to each agent's detailed evidence outside this PR's file diff. Tests validate the audit tools; a live audit checks the actual agent.

title: fix(desktop): hide Dock presence when quitting to tray
body:
Code changes: +63 -36  
Tests: +118 -1  
Others: +6 -4

## Problem

After #6472, desktop Quit/Cmd+Q closes AO's window but keeps Electron alive for the tray, daemon, and remote access. The quit path never hides the Dock, so AO still appears as a running Dock application. The requested behavior is tray-only background operation.

## Changes

- Hide the macOS Dock only after the native window successfully closes, preserving canceled unsaved-draft warnings.
- Restore the Dock before reopening; share the focus path across tray, app activation, second-instance/folder launches, sign-in callbacks, and existing-window notification clicks.
- Retry an ignored hide once after 1.1 seconds: Electron 33 ignores Dock hides for one second after a show. Cancel that retry on reopen/full quit/update; recheck tray and quit eligibility before it runs.
- Preserve startup initialization, full tray Quit, updater/system shutdown, and Windows/Linux quit behavior.

User-pinned Dock shortcuts are intentionally not removed. No daemon, mobile API, remote credentials, or installation changes are included.

## Verification

- Red → green native macOS Electron 33.4.11 check using the real lifecycle controller and an isolated BaseWindow/Tray: canceled close retains the window/Dock; desktop Quit leaves zero windows, Dock hidden, tray alive, and the same Electron PID; two rapid reopen/quit cycles restore and hide the Dock; explicit full Quit exits 0.
- 69 focused tests pass: desktop quit, tray, tray lifecycle, draft close/unload guards, window composition, supervisor link, and update quit.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass on Node 24.14.0.
- `git diff --check` passes; independent lifecycle review found no actionable issues.

The native check exercises the controller against Electron/macOS, not the complete AO desktop/daemon/mobile composition. A signed nightly upgrade and a fresh two-Mac run were not tested. Existing AO processes and real user data were left untouched.

title: feat(testing): add agentic testing investigations
body:
Code changes: +7323 -67\
Tests: +8231 -5\
Others: +4057 -631 (generated sqlc, openapi.yaml, schema.ts, docs, skill asset)

## What

Adds the agentic testing feature: an investigator that drives the real AO desktop app against an isolated local AO target and records what it observes. Includes the Cua desktop adapter (guarded window control and recording), the isolated local target launcher, native investigation attempts persisted and served over HTTP, stdio MCP testing tools with a management CLI, investigator chat tools, and the testing skill.

Also includes a small daemon fix (`fix(daemon): preserve signal handling during shutdown cleanup`, `retain signals through final cleanup`) that the testing target shutdown depends on.

## Why

Lets an agent verify a change in the running app instead of relying only on unit tests. No linked issue.

## How

- Stack is 25 non-merge commits on top of current `origin/main`. Commits are grouped by checkpoint (`checkpoint0`, `checkpoint1-host`), so reviewing by commit is the easiest path.
- Rebased onto `origin/main` to clear merge conflicts. Conflicts resolved:
  - Testing migration renumbered from `0179_testing.sql` to `0195_testing.sql` (main now uses up to 0194). Its test now opens at 194 and migrates to 195.
  - `startSession` keeps main's `reviewerRecoveryDone` parameter and returns the concrete `*sessionmanager.Manager` that testing wiring needs.
  - Chat launch and resume append the `ao-testing` server to main's `aoMCPServers` list instead of replacing it.
- Post-rebase follow-up: testing subprocesses now go through `internal/process` (main's forbidigo rule). Testing-profile test assertions select the `ao-testing` server by name, since chat sessions now also carry the general `ao` tool server.
- Reviewers should focus on: process identity checks, shutdown and reaping of owned providers, the Cua input mapping, and the chat MCP composition above.
- The `wip: checkpoint0 + checkpoint1-host (pre-cloud baseline)` commit is a WIP-labeled checkpoint and is included as-is. Squash or reword before merge if that is not wanted.
- Intentional omissions: not assessed in this pass against any older behavior.

## Testing

Run locally on the rebased branch (observed):

- `go build ./...`: pass
- `go vet ./...`: pass
- `golangci-lint run ./...` (v2.13.2): 0 issues
- `npm run api` (OpenAPI spec and TS types) and `npm run sqlc`: no generated-file drift
- `go test ./...` (full backend): 12 packages fail on this machine.
  - Also failing on a clean `origin/main` export, environmental (opencode/crush/goose version probes timing out, tmux prerequisites, installed Codex protocol drift, git import behavior): `agent/crush`, `agent/goose`, `agent/opencode`, `agent/opencodev2`, `chatdriver/codexappserver`, `chatdriver/opencodev2acp`, `runtime/tmux`, `cli`, `service/importer`, `service/systemcheck`.

- Earlier in this PR's life, `session_manager` had three testing-profile failures from the MCP composition. Fixed in the follow-up commit; the testing-focused subset passes.
- Local commits used `--no-verify`. The pre-commit hook runs the full `npm run lint`, which is blocked by the environmental failures above. Remote CI is the real gate for those packages.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` (before rebase): 54 errors, all in `packages/product-ui`, which this branch does not touch. Not re-run after rebase.

Not run: `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --all` (needs Docker).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [ ] One focused change; this is a multi-commit feature stack, not a single issue

title: chore(cloud): retire the NodeOps sandbox provider
body:
Code changes: +3163 -1527  
Tests: +2690 -177  
Others: +82 -76 (docs, config, generated schema, i18n)

> **Stacks on #6478 (Freestyle provider).** Merge after #6478. Until it lands, this diff includes #6478's changes, so the counts above include them. This PR's own commit (`b7c82c1fc`) is: code +245 -1452, tests +417 -189, others +50 -100 (66 files, +712 -1741).

## Summary

Retires the NodeOps (CreateOS) sandbox provider and the dangling `ecs`, `daytona` and `lambda-microvms` provider names from AO Cloud. Old sandbox rows on those providers are now settled safely and no longer retry forever.

## Removed

- `cloud/internal/sandbox/createos/client.go` (CreateOS client)
- `cloud/scripts/publish-nodeops-template.sh` and `cloud/nodeops/Sandbox.Dockerfile` (legacy all-agents image)
- `sandbox.ProviderNodeOps`, `ProviderECS`, `ProviderDaytona`, `NodeOpsConfig`, `rootFSForHarness`, the NodeOps plan branch, and `Spec.Shape` / `Spec.Ingress` (only CreateOS read them)
- NodeOps config fields, env vars, validation and hosted allowlist entries in `config.go`. `ecs` and `daytona` are no longer accepted for `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDER(S)`.
- NodeOps wiring in `cmd/ao-cloud/main.go`, including `readSSHPubKeys`, which only NodeOps used
- The `nodeOps` argument of `sandboxresolve.New` and `providerProfile.NodeOps` in the reconciler
- NodeOps parts of the deploy tooling: `lib/deployment.py`, `deploy-staging.sh`, `promote-production.sh`, `render-task-definition.py`, `validate-hosted-settings.py`, `.env.example`
- `nodeops` and `daytona` from the `ProviderName` enum in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, with `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` regenerated (`npm --prefix packages/cloud-client run generate`)
- The `createProject.sandboxProvider.{nodeops,ecs,daytona}` labels in all 8 locales

## Moved

- `cloud/nodeops/Sandbox.base.Dockerfile` and `cloud/nodeops/harness/*.Dockerfile` now live in `cloud/sandbox-image/`. `publish-freestyle-snapshot.sh` replays their RUN steps for the Freestyle snapshots, so its default paths, comments and docs are updated. The base `FROM` (ignored by the bake) now reads `debian:bookworm` instead of the NodeOps image.

## Changed defaults

- `defaultSandboxProvider(hosted)` returns `coder` (it returned `nodeops`). `deploy-staging.sh` defaults to `coder`, and the Python renderer and validator default to `coder` too.
- `providersRequireWorkerHome` now covers `docker`, `coder` and `freestyle`. It used to list `nodeops` but not `freestyle`.
- `deploy-dev.sh` inherits the `coder` default, which means it reads the staging Coder secret unless `AO_CLOUD_CODER_SECRET_ID` is set. Its header comment now says this.

## Kept on purpose

- The non-Coder `/workspace` layout in `workspaceLayout`, `Spec.RootFS`, `Spec.AutoPauseSeconds`, the restoring state, the deletion deadline, worker self-update and `DefaultWorkerTokenTTL` (Freestyle and Docker use them).
- The provider CHECK constraint still allows `nodeops`. Historical rows exist (19 prod, 350 staging), migrations are immutable, and no new migration is needed.
- `RETIRED_PROVIDER_ENV_PREFIX = "AO_CLOUD_NODEOPS_"` in `deployment.py`. The renderer always prunes these names from an older task definition, and `validate_task_artifacts` rejects a task that still has them. This is what makes it safe to delete the nodeops secrets after the first deploy.

## Retired-provider behavior

`sandbox.IsRetiredProvider` covers `nodeops`, `ecs`, `daytona` and `lambda-microvms`.

- **Reconciler.** `reconcileSandbox` checks the retired set before `Resolve`. Before this, `Resolve` failed first, so these rows never reached the deletion path or the terminated parking and retried every 5 minutes. That covers the 4 live prod NodeOps sessions failing with 401 for 2 weeks, and the staging `ecs` and `lambda-microvms` rows stuck at `desired=deleted`. Now:
  - `desired=deleted`: calls `CompleteSandboxDeletion` with no provider call and logs any leftover provider id for manual cleanup.
  - Anything else: disconnects workers, records a `provider_retired` startup error ("This session ran on a sandbox provider AO no longer supports. Start a new session to continue.") and parks the row as `terminated`, with a quiet 24h no-op re-check. An already parked row is not re-recorded.
  - The desktop renders this with existing states: `runtimeState=terminated` plus a startup error shows the "This session couldn't start" pane with the reason. Session lists and history still render the old rows.
- **`SessionPlanForProvider`** returns `ErrProviderRetired` for a retired provider and an error for an unknown one. It no longer builds a provider-only plan.
- **Restore** (`RestoreSession`) and **startup retry** (`RetrySessionStartup`) check the sandbox provider first and return `ErrProviderRetired`. `writeStoreError` maps that to `409 provider_retired`. A rejected restore leaves the session terminated.
- **Child spawn.** An orchestrator on a retired provider gets `409 provider_retired` from `createWorkerChild` and no child row is created. Before, this was a 500 "misconfigured" error.
- The OpenAPI startup error code list and the retry endpoint description now document `provider_retired`.

## Tests

Fixtures that used `nodeops` now use `freestyle`, `coder` or `docker`: `worker_orchestration_handlers_test.go`, `resource_handlers_autolink_test.go`, `providers_test.go`, `provider_capabilities_test.go`, `workspace*_handlers_test.go`, `reconciler_test.go`, `test_deployment.py`, and 4 frontend fixtures.

New tests:
- Reconciler: retired deletion completes, a live retired row parks as terminated with `provider_retired`, an already parked row stays quiet. A failing resolver proves `Resolve` is never called.
- Resolver: retired versus unsupported errors.
- `SessionPlanForProvider`: rejects retired and unknown providers.
- Child spawn: `409 provider_retired`.
- Postgres: retry and restore are rejected and the session is left unchanged.
- Config: retired providers rejected, hosted default is `coder`, worker-home set.
- Deploy tooling: retired names are pruned from an older task, a task that keeps them is rejected, retired overrides are rejected, retired provider rejected by the validator.

## Test results (local)

- `cd cloud && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./...`: clean
- `GOWORK=off go build ./cmd/...` in `cloud/`: OK
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` with `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointing at a throwaway `postgres:16-alpine`: every package passes except 4 postgres tests that already fail on main (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`). The new `TestRetiredProviderSessionRejectsRetryAndRestore` passes.
- `cd cloud/scripts && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 34 tests OK
- `bash -n` on `deploy-staging.sh`, `promote-production.sh` and `publish-freestyle-snapshot.sh`: OK
- `packages/cloud-client`: regenerating is a no-op against the committed schema; typecheck, tests (29) and build pass
- `frontend`: `tsc --noEmit` is clean. The touched tests and i18n tests pass (6 files, 127 tests). The full renderer suite has 25 failures in 5 files, all from the local environment and unrelated to this change: en-IN number grouping in `ContextMeter`/`ChatWorkspace`, and the Electron binary and native modules being absent after `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (`browser-profile-import`, `browser-view-host`, `provider-auth-flow`).
- golangci-lint: the CI lint job only covers `backend/`, which this PR does not touch, so it was not run.

## Remaining `nodeops` / `createos` references

`git grep -i 'nodeops\|createos'` still matches the following, each on purpose:
- Migrations `00004`, `00028`, `00031`, `00036`, `00040`, `00041` (immutable history and the CHECK constraint)
- The retired-provider set, its tests, and the deploy `RETIRED_PROVIDER_ENV_PREFIX` pruning plus its tests
- Docs that name NodeOps as retired (`deployment.md`, `execution-readiness.md`)
- `docs/superpowers/*` dated plans and specs (history)
- `createOscColorReportForwarder` in the frontend (case-insensitive false positive)

## Ops follow-ups

- At the next production deploy, drop `nodeops` from production `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS` / `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDER`. The deploy scripts now reject it, and `promote-production.sh` mirrors staging, so deploy staging first.

title: feat(mobile): fold a settled turn's work behind a Worked for row
body:
## Summary

Brings desktop's "Working for → Worked for" turn accordion to mobile. Mobile already received all the data it needs (turn state, timestamps, `turnId` on each item), so this is a client-only regrouping of the conversation snapshot. It doesn't depend on the harness: every agent that works on desktop gets the same behavior.

- **While running:** the prompt, then a "Working · 12s" row with a spinner, then the work streaming in below it. This row used to sit at the bottom of the turn.
- **Once settled:** tool calls, interim messages, and approval and question cards fold behind a tappable "Worked for 20s ›" row, closed by default. The final reply, errors and system notices stay visible below. Failed and stopped turns fold too, and keep their "Failed after…" and "Stopped after…" labels.
- **Nothing to fold:** a turn with no work shows a plain, non-tappable "Worked for…" row.
- **Open state** is kept above the `FlatList`, so it survives row recycling.
- **Animation (Reanimated, using the durations in `motion.ts`):** the chevron rotates, the folded work fades in and out, and the content below slides. On the Working → Worked change, the spinner fades out and the label slides into its place. With Reduce Motion on, all of this is skipped.

### Changes
- `lib/chat/timelineModel.ts`: a new `partitionTurnItems` splits a turn into the opening prompt, the folded work, the notices and the final reply, using the same rules as desktop's `ChatWorkspace`. A running or queued turn stays unfolded, so the answer never jumps out of the stream.
- `lib/chat/ChatTimeline.tsx`: a new `TurnStatusRow`, kept as one stable `Pressable` so the handoff animation isn't remounted. Also the fold wiring in `ConversationTurnGroup`, and the open/closed state in `ChatTimeline`.
- `lib/chat/TurnFoldMotion.tsx`: the Reanimated pieces (`FoldBody`, `FoldLayout`, `StatusSpinner`, `StatusLabel`, `FoldChevron`).
- The rollback button now sits on its own row at the bottom of the turn.

## Testing
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `npx vitest run`: all 1568 tests pass, including new unit tests for `partitionTurnItems` and source tests for the status row.
- On the iOS simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, fresh native build, paired to a local daemon), a settled Claude Code turn renders the prompt, a closed "Worked for 18s ›" row, then the final answer.

## Known risks / follow-ups
- **Partly checked on the simulator.** Only the closed settled state was seen. Opening the fold, the animations, and the live "Working" row still need checking by hand, and so does the approval/question fix.
- The slide animates the content inside the list cell, but the cell's own height changes at once. On the inverted `FlatList`, the surrounding rows may jump slightly.
- Unlike desktop, there's no shimmer and no 440ms delay before "Worked for". Reasoning stays hidden on mobile, as before.

title: fix(chat): prevent ACP replay overflow and preserve reconnect ownership
body:
Code changes: +109 -26  
Tests: +614 -7  
Others: +0 -0  

After AO restarts during an ACP Chat turn, retained updates can overflow the SDK’s 1,024-notification queue. AO stops reading but leaves the TCP socket open. The persistent host then blocks replay while holding its ownership lock. Resume times out, and AO fails the unfinished turn although its provider remains alive.

Deliver validated chat updates and host receipts in wire order, so a full AO event queue slows socket reads. Keep JSON-RPC requests, responses, and permission requests in the SDK. Close failed attachment sockets without terminating the persistent host. Preserve unfinished turns and queued messages for recovery. A definitive terminal receipt still settles its turn when a disconnect races the response.

### Before and after evidence

The process test uses real `ao` daemon executables, loopback HTTP, the persistent TCP host, and SQLite with a synthetic ACP provider. Each case uses isolated data. Send a prompt, save one seed delta, stop the daemon, emit 20,543 updates while detached, and restart the daemon. SQLite projection consumes immediately, without an artificial pause.

| Before: main `4273bec7c638` | After: this PR |
|---|---|
| Turn incorrectly becomes `failed`. | Original turn becomes `completed`. |
| Only 3,847 of 20,544 assistant bytes reach SQLite. | Exact 20,544-byte output reaches SQLite once. |
| Archive contains 3,847 deltas and no completion. | Archive contains 20,544 unique deltas and one completion. |
| Provider remains alive behind a failed controller. | Same host survives, with one provider launch. |
| Subsequent attachment can time out behind the leaked socket. | Terminal ACK clears the journal, and a third daemon restart retains the ready conversation. |

Actual daemon process results:

```text
before: turn=failed error="controller ended before the turn completed"
        assistant_bytes=3847 archived_deltas=3847 archived_completions=0
        same_host=true provider_launches=1

after:  turn=completed assistant_bytes=20544 archived_deltas=20544 archived_completions=1
        same_host=true provider_launches=1 journal_cleared=true third_restart_ready=true
        completion after restart=11.138s
        assistant_sha256=fa6c253b7b33ae9d37fbba8fbccf1c2972f403f5b7223bfd8942a9d752f0057f
```

The committed regression exercises the real ACP adapter, persistent host, Chat service, and SQLite. It checks every byte, unique durable event, terminal ACK, and third restart. Against unchanged main, it reproduces the queue overflow:

```text
host journaled 20543 detached updates plus one already projected seed
ACP replay overflowed while the real SQLite projector was consuming
failed to queue notification; closing connection
err="notification queue overflow" capacity=1024 queued=1024
--- FAIL: TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts (3.67s)
```

A baseline diagnostic also reproduced the blocked next attachment:

```text
chat conversation recovery is inconclusive: persistent ACP host:
chat host ownership is inconclusive: context deadline exceeded
```

With this PR:

```text
same host committed exactly 20544 unique deltas, 20544 assistant bytes and one completion; terminal ACK cleared journal
third daemon-style restart reattached ready to the same native conversation
--- PASS: TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts (13.33s)

# Same assertions with the race detector and concurrent suite load:
replay completed after 3m42.964s
--- PASS: TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts (249.71s)
```

Run the committed regression:

```bash
cd backend
go test -race -count=1 -v -run '^TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts$' ./internal/service/chat
```

For the failing baseline, copy `backend/internal/service/chat/controller_acp_replay_test.go` into a separate checkout of `4273bec7c638ea078fbead68090286315bc1b90a`. Run the same command against that implementation. Use scratch databases and synthetic provider processes only.

### Validation

- Go 1.27.1: full backend build and vet, complete backend race-package coverage, and full reruns of affected packages.
- All 395 Chat tests pass across both CI-style race shards: 354.889s and 179.014s. The complete ACP and persistent-host race suites pass.
- Complete SQLite race suite passes in 1120.191s. Session-manager and SQLite-store race suites also pass.
- Complete macOS CLI E2E suite passes. Cloud build, vet, format, and complete race suite pass.
- Golangci-lint v2.13.2: zero issues. Gofmt and whitespace checks pass. Gitleaks v7.4.0 scans both commits with no leaks.
- SQLc v1.31.1 and API generation under Node 24.14.0 produce no drift. Trusted leaderboard tests pass.

The initial backend sweep found two installed-provider checks that also fail on unchanged main. The OpenCode fixture finds an installed 1.18.35 binary. Codex protocol conformance compares installed CLI 0.162.0 against protocol 0.146.0. Both complete packages pass in a clean environment matching CI. Installed-provider protocol conformance is not claimed as passed.

The initial replay fixture also exceeded its two-minute deadline under the race detector while projection continued. The final fixture uses a measured five-minute bound and cheaper indexed polling. Both complete Chat shards and the focused race reproduction pass with every content, ACK, and restart assertion intact.

All **21 remote checks pass** on `d1af9046a2f221b639c2725bdb72170920862bbe`, including both Chat race shards and all four SQLite shards.

- [Go CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38045190949): complete backend suites, Windows workspace recovery, cloud Docker Expat validation, lint, SQLc drift, and API drift pass.
- [CLI E2E CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38045190928): native Linux, macOS, Windows, and the fresh-install container pass.
- [Gitleaks CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38045191083): the pinned Linux scanner passes.

Docker and native Linux/Windows execution were unavailable locally. The successful remote jobs close those validation gaps.

Additional regressions cover replay order, socket release, full-buffer teardown, preservation of running/queued work, and terminal receipts racing a disconnect.

Related proposed fixes: #6215 and #6027. This PR includes the immediate-SQLite regression and unfinished-work preservation. It does not rewrite turns that previous versions already marked failed. Those sessions need separate recovery.

These controlled-provider tests do not exercise the packaged Electron updater or authenticated vendor behavior. The real OpenCode validation is linked below. The original production SDK exception was not durably stored. Production attribution rests on live socket/journal state and the reproduced failure chain. The controlled-provider evidence above contains synthetic data only. The real OpenCode evidence is linked below.

## Continuous restart proof and repeatable evidence

Run `20261011T120114Z-85b0ee40` repeats the complete failure and recovery test with actual before/after daemon executables, HTTP, the persistent TCP host, and SQLite. The synthetic provider emits 20,544 distinct numbered updates, `[000000]` through `[020543]`, totaling 164,352 bytes. Each case starts with fresh isolated data; projection consumes immediately.

| Before: main `4273bec7c638` | After: this PR implementation |
| --- | --- |
| SDK reports `notification queue overflow`, capacity 1,024. | All 20,544 updates reach SQLite in wire order. |
| Only 3,994 updates survive as an ordered prefix; turn incorrectly fails. | The original turn completes once; transcript equals all 164,352 expected bytes. |
| Two actual Resume POSTs return HTTP 409, `CHAT_RECOVERY_INCONCLUSIVE`, after 1.038s and 1.018s. | Automatic reattachment succeeds with the original host, conversation, provider turn, and one provider launch. |
| Failed reader retains an ESTABLISHED socket with 608,200 unread bytes; host journal retains 6,706,782 bytes. | Terminal ACK clears the journal; a third daemon start retains the completed conversation and ready controller. |

The **42.667-second continuous recording** includes the complete 39.109-second test. It shows a live process-log viewer while the real processes run. All 435 captured frames and wall-clock intervals are retained, with a maximum sample gap of 445 ms. There are no cuts, speed changes, inserted cards, or omitted restart intervals. This is a process test recording; the separate native Electron clip below remains a companion demonstration.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5aa98bfe-fc63-4bf0-bd5a-bf41a9ba9f44

[Download the repeatable test and complete raw evidence](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33302528/ao-acp-replay-proof.zip). The archive includes build provenance, the exact executed harness and synthetic provider, all five scoped daemon logs, event exports, transcripts, assertion results, capture timestamps, and a file hash manifest. The README gives exact build and run commands. Tokens and workstation paths are removed; private databases and binaries are excluded.

```text
expected and fixed transcript SHA-256:
b8f03508562e6e0e9bceac1c8d89b310f04912a70a8c7be3f63f96407054420d
video SHA-256:
76a70581c4e28673ee0ecd5c9a49ff80a7820dd36e41fdff9d939633cbcbfcca
ZIP SHA-256:
89c9aa4401f9481572b5751fa4cc1d00560bdec9e550534169bdbdc6469182b7
```

A separate check verifies every payload, provider event ID, contiguous persistent event ordinal, one original completion, unchanged host PID/start time and conversation identity, and the third restart. A full video decode and archive integrity/hash check pass. These results establish prevention for the reproduced restart/replay failure. They do not test updater installation, authenticated vendor APIs, or repair of sessions already marked failed by an old build.

## Desktop screen recording

A separate run in the real Electron app reproduced the same controller-stopped banner and ownership timeout. The fixed build reopened the preserved chat with an idle controller.

| Before fix | After fix |
| --- | --- |
| 4,155 of 20,544 unique deltas saved; turn failed | All 20,544 unique deltas saved; one completion |
| Replay journal retained: 5,864,478 bytes | Completion acknowledged; journal cleared |

The video contains native AO window captures at recorded speed, with labeled cuts. The app restart and elapsed gaps are omitted; the completed chat is opened after replay finishes. Both runs use isolated data and a synthetic ACP provider, with mock Keychain for the test app; no production session data is included. This does not exercise the updater installation or a real model API.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ee20c4c-a53d-44ab-9581-698567f54743


## Matched real OpenCode restart comparison

[Uncut native AO recording and independent before/after audit](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6514#issuecomment-6115000817). The same real OpenCode chat and GLM-4.7 model replay the same 18,885 retained updates from an identical initial AO checkpoint. The baseline overflows its notification queue, fails the original turn and cannot Resume; the patch completes that turn, archives every update once and in order, clears the journal and completes a real-model follow-up. All 54 prior messages are preserved.

This local comparison restores only the private AO DB/WAL/SHM between cases; native chat, model, host, provider and journal remain unchanged. It proves prevention/recovery from the initial running checkpoint, not in-place repair of baseline-failed turn state or operation of the packaged updater. The requesting user’s regular app and complete native history are restored after recording.

title: fix(mobile): make the Settings notifications switch respond instantly
body:
## Summary

The notifications switch in mobile Settings took ~3s (sometimes more) to toggle. The switch was replaced by a spinner until everything below finished, one after another:

1. **Retrying old turn-off requests.** Turn-off requests for earlier machines that couldn't be reached are queued (up to 10). Each toggle retried all of them first, and each one checks the machine with a 3s timeout (`PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`). One unreachable old machine added 3s to every tap.
2. **The current daemon.** Turning off waited on an identity probe plus the DELETE; turning on waited on the Expo token and the register POST.
3. **A queued status read.** The row re-read status afterwards, and that read waited behind the re-registration of every connected machine that follows turning push on. The switch often snapped back to its old position before settling.

### Changes

- `lib/push.ts`
  - The pending-unregister retry is queued after `registerForPush` / `unregisterFromPush` resolve instead of inside them.
  - `unregisterFromPush` resolves once this machine's registration is moved into the durable pending-unregister queue (queued first, then cleared), so an app suspended or killed right after the switch shows "off" still retries the DELETE on next launch. Draining that queue (probe + DELETE) is queued at call time right behind it, so a quick re-enable still runs after the DELETE, and the existing flush drops the entry when the same token was registered again.
- `app/settings.tsx`
  - The switch shows the new position the moment it's tapped (disabled while the change applies) and goes back if registration fails. The outcome is applied directly instead of waiting on the queued status read; a refresh still runs afterwards.
  - Renamed "Agent notifications" to "Notifications".
- `lib/push.test.ts`
  - New tests: turning off resolves without waiting on the daemon and with the unregister already recorded as pending; off-then-on sends the DELETE before the register POST and leaves nothing owed.
  - Retry tests now wait for the queue instead of depending on microtask timing.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npx vitest run`: 166 files, 1565 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- On a physical iPhone 13, using a side-by-side Release build (separate bundle ID, no push entitlement):
  - The label reads "Notifications".
  - The switch moves the instant it's tapped.
  - A failed turn-on (no token in that build) puts the switch back and shows the alert.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Not yet tried on a build with working push, so the on/off timing against a real daemon is only covered by the unit tests.
- Turning on still waits ~1–2s for the Expo token and the register POST. That's intentional, since it can fail and needs to report why. The switch shows "on" but stays disabled until then.
- The "This build can't receive push notifications" alert repeats its title in the message. That copy was already there and isn't changed here.

Renaming appears to be broken for both sessions and orchestrators in the Cloud environment.

The rename functionality works correctly for normal sessions in local projects, but the corresponding behavior seems broken on Cloud. The desktop app's rename behavior is separate and should not be confused with the Cloud implementation.

Expected Behavior

Users should be able to rename sessions on Cloud.

Users should be able to rename orchestrators on Cloud.

The UI should not suggest that an item can be renamed when the action is unsupported.

Actual Behavior

Renaming sessions on Cloud appears to be broken.

Renaming orchestrators on Cloud also appears to be broken.

Local session renaming works as expected.

Scope

Investigate and fix rename behavior for both sessions and orchestrators on Cloud.

Verify that the UI correctly reflects rename availability.

Test the fix against both session and orchestrator workflows.

Collaboration

Assigned to: Anirban Ghosh and Anaya.

Note: The exact failure mechanism on Cloud still needs to be investigated.

title: fix(chat): preserve orchestrator conversation scope during provisioning
body:
Code changes: +6 -1  
Tests: +58 -35  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keep an orchestrator's opening prompt in the project-scoped conversation that its controller uses. A prompt queued before the controller starts now drains after startup instead of remaining stranded in a second, session-scoped conversation.

## Why

Related to #6523. In the reported desktop session, the orchestrator chat was blank and showed a message as queued even though the live controller had already replied.

Agent-assisted diagnosis found two conversation rows with the same current session: a session-scoped row containing the original queued prompt, and a project-scoped row containing the active transcript. `ensureConversation` unconditionally created the former during provisioning, while `Start` correctly created/reused the latter. Snapshot lookup by session could then return the wrong row. The regression test reproduces the stranded opening prompt with the real SQLite store and a fake provider, without account credentials or external services.

## How

Select project scope for orchestrators during provisioning, matching `Start`; retain session scope for workers. Extend the existing queued-prompt lifecycle test across both roles and assert the queued turn starts, the conversation ID is preserved, and the scope is correct.

Intentional omission: this prevents new split histories; it does not migrate already-split conversations or automatically replay their stale prompts. Repairing existing history needs an explicit policy to avoid duplicating work. No schema, generated API, frontend, or installed-app changes.

## Testing

- Regression red/green: worker passed and orchestrator failed on the original implementation (opening prompt remained queued); both pass with this fix.
- Focused race checks: passed for queued-prompt draining (both roles), first-controller startup, ordered provisioning messages and worker-report piggybacking (`go test -race -count=1 -timeout=90s ./internal/service/chat -run 'Test(DrainWithoutControllerKeepsOpeningPromptForLaterStart|FirstControllerAfterQueuedPromptIsNotFencedAsResume|SendWhileProvisioningQueuesInOrder|ProvisioningSendPiggybacksReportsOnlyOnRecordedTurn)$'`).
