title: Switch agent dialog offers only unversioned Claude aliases (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) instead of models like Opus 5.5 when the Claude login has expired
body:
Switching a session from Codex to Claude Code, the model dropdown in the **Switch agent** dialog only lists **Fable 5.1, Haiku, Opus, Opus (1M context), Sonnet**. It doesn't show the actual Claude models with versions, such as **Opus 5.5**, so I can't tell or pick which version I'm getting. The dialog also showed the "saved Claude Code login token expired" warning at the same time (that warning text is tracked separately in #6658).

Reported by: @somewherelostt (Windows 11, AO desktop app)

---

**Agent-collected evidence** (collected 2026-10-13 ~22:55 IST)

- **Reproduced on latest `main` (`ae6aef2ea`)** with a dev daemon from a clean `origin/main` worktree in isolated mode (`AO_PORT=3012`, separate data dir). This is not the reporter's installed app. Claude Code CLI `2.1.296`. On this machine the saved Claude OAuth token's `expiresAt` is 2026-10-11, so it really is expired.
  ```
  POST /api/v1/agents/claude-code/models/refresh  -> 200
  GET  /api/v1/agents/claude-code/models
    source=catalog  stale=true  warningCode=auth_expired
    models: fable "Fable 5.1" | haiku "Haiku" | opus "Opus" | opus[1m] "Opus (1M context)" | sonnet "Sonnet"
  ```
  That is exactly the list in the screenshot.
- The list matches the static fallback `claudeCodeModels()` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go:320-328`. `discoverClaudeCatalog` returns that fallback whenever the provider model list call fails (`catalog.go:355-358`), and here it fails because of the expired token. Only `fable` carries a version in its label. `opus`, `sonnet` and `haiku` are bare aliases with no resolved version, and no versioned IDs such as `claude-opus-5-5` are offered.
- The isolated data dir had no last-known-good provider catalog to fall back on. The reporter's installed app showed the same alias list, which suggests it had none either (not verified).
- I did not drive the dialog in the dev Electron window. The UI evidence is the reporter's screenshot from their installed app, and the `main` reproduction is at the daemon API level.
- **Hypothesis (unconfirmed):** once a saved Claude login expires and there's no cached provider catalog, every Claude picker (Switch agent, New Task, settings) shows only the unversioned alias list until Claude Code runs and refreshes the token.

Related: #6658 (raw token-expired warning in the same dialog), #5989 (chat composer folds Opus 5.5 into the "Opus" alias), #5834 (resolve vague labels to concrete values), draft PR #6251 (extra Claude models via provider discovery, which still needs a working login).

title: [Feature]: Run local agents in a Docker sandbox (shared or per-agent, with prebuilt images)
body:
### Problem

Local workers run directly on the host: the daemon spawns the harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, …) in a tmux/ConPTY runtime against a git worktree under `~/.ao`. That gives an agent the same reach as the user. It can read `~/.ssh`, global credentials, and other projects, install packages globally, and leave processes and containers behind (#3537, #2523). Harness permission modes reduce this, but they are policy inside the agent, not a boundary around it (#4840, #3280).

Teams also need repeatable environments. Each worker ends up installing the same toolchain (language runtimes, CLIs, browsers, system packages) on every run, or depends on whatever happens to be installed on the host. Cloud sessions already have sandbox providers, including a Docker provider in `cloud/internal/sandbox/docker`, and snapshot baking is being discussed for Daytona (#5327). The local desktop daemon has nothing equivalent.

### Proposed direction

Add an opt-in **Docker sandbox** for local sessions. The agent process runs inside a container; the daemon, UI, and worktree management stay on the host.

**1. Sandbox modes (per project, overridable per role)**

| Mode | Behavior | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| `off` (default) | Current behavior, agent runs on the host. | Existing projects |
| `shared` | One long-lived container per project. Every worker in the project runs inside it, each in its own worktree. | Fast startup, shared caches and services, low overhead |
| `per-agent` | One container per session, created at spawn and removed at kill. | Isolation between workers, clean state per task |

Mode should be selectable per role (for example, orchestrator `off`, workers `per-agent`), building on the `RoleOverride` direction in #2195.

**2. Prebuilt sandboxes**

Users can prepare an image with the software a project needs, so workers start ready to go:

- Project config points at either an image reference (`image: ghcr.io/org/app-dev:latest`) or a build context (`dockerfile: .ao/sandbox/Dockerfile`). Consider accepting `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` as a source too.
- `ao sandbox build` (and a button in project settings) builds the image and tags it by a content hash of the build inputs. The daemon reuses the cached image until the inputs change, and rebuilds or warns when they do.
- An optional `setup` step (script or command list) runs once per container after creation, for work that can't be baked into the image, such as `npm ci` against the worktree.
- AO layers in what it needs on top of the user image (the `ao` CLI and hook shims, harness binaries if missing), so a user image doesn't have to know about AO internals. This needs a base image or an install step that works on common distros.

**3. Runtime integration**

- New runtime option alongside `tmux` / `conpty` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime`, picked in `runtimeselect`): the PTY runs `docker exec -it <container> <harness …>`, so terminal attach, scrollback, and liveness keep working through the existing `ports.Runtime` contract.
- Worktrees are bind-mounted at the **same absolute path** inside the container, so paths in transcripts, diffs, and the file panel match on both sides.
- In-container hooks and the `ao` CLI must reach the daemon. Mount the daemon socket or expose the HTTP endpoint, and forward `AO_SESSION_ID` and related env.
- Harness auth: forward only what the selected harness needs (specific env vars, or read-only mounts of its auth file). Never mount the whole home directory.
- Container labels reuse the existing scheme (`ao.session`, plus a project label for shared containers) so `dockerreap` cleans up per-agent containers on kill. A shared container must be exempt from per-session reaping and gets its own lifecycle: start on first worker, stop when idle or when the project closes.
- Resource limits (CPU, memory, pids) come from project config and line up with #2523.
- All sandbox state (build cache metadata, container records) lives under `~/.ao` per the repo's app-state rule.

**4. UI**

- Project settings: sandbox mode, image or Dockerfile, setup command, resource limits, and a build/rebuild action with build logs.
- Session view: show that a session is sandboxed and which image or container it uses.
- Clear errors when Docker isn't installed or running, or the image build fails, with a fallback offer to run unsandboxed.

### Scope suggestion

1. `per-agent` mode with a user-supplied image reference, Claude Code only, macOS and Linux.
2. `shared` mode and the shared-container lifecycle.
3. Prebuild: Dockerfile build, content-hash caching, setup step, settings UI.
4. Other harnesses, devcontainer.json support, Windows (Docker Desktop and WSL2).

### Open questions

- Reuse or extract the Docker Engine client in `cloud/internal/sandbox/docker` instead of shelling out to the `docker` CLI like `dockerreap` does?
- Network policy: full egress by default, or an allowlist option?
- Shared mode: how should concurrent workers avoid fighting over global state inside the container (package caches, ports, `~/.claude`)?
- Should prebuilt images be shareable across machines (push to a registry) or local only to start with?
- Browser and preview features (`ao preview`, CDP) when the dev server runs inside the container: port publishing, related to #4582.

### Alternatives considered

- **Harness-native sandboxes** (Codex sandbox, Claude Code permission modes): per-harness, inconsistent, and they don't give a reproducible toolchain.
- **Cloud sandboxes** (#4911): strong isolation, but they need a control plane and a network round trip, and they don't cover offline or local-only use.
- **Devcontainers only**: a good image source, but they don't solve runtime integration, lifecycle, or shared vs per-agent placement on their own.

Related: #2195, #2844, #2523, #3537, #4911, #4575, #5327, #4582

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar

title: fix(cloud): bring-your-own Coder sessions work in the template's checkout; cloud projects get Setup/Cleanup scripts
body:
## Why

A customer with their own Coder (11x) reported that cloud sessions "work but are janky". Their template prepares everything under `~/work/<repo>`: the checkout, a mode-600 `.env` and a Docker stack. It only reports Ready once that is done.

AO ignored all of it:
- **Started too early.** AO launched its own worker before the template had finished setting up.
- **Separate clone.** It cloned the repository again into `~/repository`.
- **Different user.** It ran the agent as a separate `ao-worker` user, so `make` targets got "Permission denied" on the template's `.env`.
- **Wrong path in the agent's instructions.** It told the agent the project lives at `/workspace/repository`, which does not exist on Coder.
- **Unreadable workspace names.** Workspaces were named `ao-<hash>`.

The customer also asked for:
- startup/shutdown scripts,
- a way to set where the agent lands,
- a guide for templates,
- and Claude kept away from `.env`.

All of this reproduced on staging with a replica of their template (`ao-11x-replica`, their `main.tf`).

## What

**Bring-your-own Coder connection (Settings > Coder > Workspace setup).** The options that already existed but were hidden from the UI are now visible, along with two new ones:
- **Run the agent as the workspace user** (`workerUser: workspace`), so it has the same access as the template's user.
- **Use the template's existing checkout** (`reuseExistingCheckout`).
- **Working directory** (new, `workingDirectory`, for example `~/work/{repo}`). AO adopts the checkout there: it switches to the session branch and stashes any local changes. If the directory is missing, AO clones into it. If it holds something else, the checkout fails with a clear message.
- **Ready check** (`readyProbe`), which waits for the template's own "Ready" signal.
- **Keep the agent out of secret files** (new, `protectSecretFiles`, on by default), for Claude Code and Codex:
  - AO writes Claude Code `permissions.deny` rules for `.env` and `.env.*`. They hold even in `bypassPermissions` and also stop the file commands Claude recognizes in Bash (`cat`, `head`, `grep`, `cp`).
  - `ao-worker secret-file-guard` runs as a `PreToolUse` hook on the shell tool for Claude Code (Terminal and Chat) and Codex (Terminal, exec and Chat). It blocks commands that name a `.env` file, such as `python3 -c "open('.env')"` or `. ./.env`, which the deny rules miss. For Codex `apply_patch`, only the files a patch touches count. Codex Chat's app-server records the hook's trust hash (`hooks/list` + `config/batchWrite`), since it has no `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`.
  - Commands and `make` targets that load `.env` without naming it still work. `.env.example`, `.env.sample` and `.env.template` stay readable. Cursor and OpenCode are not covered, and the docs say this is not a hard boundary.

**Project Setup/Cleanup scripts for cloud projects.** These reuse the local Project settings > Scripts feature (`postCreate`/`preRemove`) with the same semantics:
- **Setup** runs in the session's working directory after checkout and before the agent starts. Each step has a 10 minute limit. A failed step keeps the agent from starting.
- **Cleanup** runs before the session's workspace is deleted, never on stop or pause. It currently runs on Coder only; the UI says so for other providers.
- **Environment.** Scripts get `AO_WORKTREE_PATH`, `AO_SOURCE_TREE_PATH`, `AO_SESSION_ID`, `AO_SESSION_KIND`, `AO_SESSION_BRANCH`, `AO_PROJECT_ID`, `AO_PROJECT_NAME` and `AO_REPOSITORY_URL`.
- **Retrying Setup.** A failed Setup shows on the session's startup screen (`project_setup_failed`) with the step, exit code and output. Retry, or reopening the session, re-reads the project's current Setup commands.
- **Current Cleanup.** At deletion, Cleanup uses the project's current commands.

**Other fixes**
- **Instructions path.** The agent's instructions now name the real working directory instead of `/workspace/repository`.
- **Readable workspace names.** Bring-your-own Coder workspaces now default to a project-named prefix, for example `alice-e0f014617de5`. Existing sessions keep their names. The session top bar shows the workspace name with a link to it.
- **Late `claude` install.** The worker now waits for a `claude` binary that the template installs late. Before, it never launched the agent.
- **Checkout failures.** Repository checkout and working-directory failures now also show on the startup screen instead of an endless spinner. This gap existed on main.
- **Deletion stall.** A running worker's heartbeat no longer postpones a sandbox deletion.
- **Clearing Workspace setup settings.** The control plane keeps any Coder setting a save leaves out, so the form now sends every Workspace setup field to a control plane that knows them. Before, a saved ready check or working directory could not be cleared and the workspace user could not be turned off.
- **Clean `git status`.** The Claude and Cursor hook files AO writes into the checkout (`.claude/settings.local.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`) are added to the checkout's own `info/exclude`, scoped to the working directory. A working directory that is the user's checkout no longer shows an untracked `.claude/`.

**Docs.** New `cloud/docs/bring-your-own-coder.md` covers:
- the template requirements and what belongs in the template versus Setup;
- readiness;
- working directory and secret-file protection;
- per-session Docker stacks with `AO_SESSION_ID`;
- troubleshooting.

## Compatibility

- **Existing connections and sessions.** Connections that set none of the new options behave as before. The one exception is `protectSecretFiles`, which defaults to on for new sessions. Sessions keep the profile they were created with.
- **Old workers.** An older worker never sends the new `workspace.startup` / `workspace.setup` events and behaves as before.
- **New worker, old control plane.** The control plane rejects the new event with a 400; the worker only logs a warning.
- **No migration.** The new project keys live in the existing config JSON.

## Testing

**Unit tests**
- `go test -race` passes on sandbox, sandbox/coder, worker, workerexec, httpapi, domain, roleprompt, reconcile, cmd/ao-worker and postgres. The postgres run used a throwaway database. Four postgres tests fail identically on main:
  - `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`
  - `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`
  - `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`
  - `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`
- `packages/cloud-client` regenerates with no diff; its typecheck and tests pass.
- Frontend: vitest passes on the touched files (257 tests), and tsc is clean on the touched files.

**Staging (td:245, our Coder, template `ao-11x-replica`).** I reproduced each problem on main first, then repeated the same steps with the fix:

| Check | Main | This PR |

title: bug(project): derived project ID from folder names with commas/spaces fails INVALID_PROJECT_ID
body:
## Summary
Registering/opening a git repo whose folder name contains commas and spaces fails, because the project ID AO derives from the folder name is then rejected by its own storage-path validation.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Have a valid git repo at a path like `/home/<user>/<dir>/Some Folder Name, 12`
2. Run `ao project add --path "/home/<user>/<dir>/Some Folder Name, 12"` (or open the folder in the desktop app)

## Actual
```
Project id failed storage-path validation (INVALID_PROJECT_ID)
```
The desktop app fails to open the folder as well, with no actionable hint.

## Expected
The derived ID is slugified into a valid ID (e.g. `some-folder-name-12`). Failing that, the error should explain the cause and suggest `--id`.

## Workaround
Pass an explicit ID: `ao project add --path "..." --id some-folder-name-12 --name "Some Folder Name, 12"`

## Environment
Linux, `ao version dev`

title: perf(desktop): show the board sooner on launch
body:
Code changes: +101 -120\
Tests: +120 -33\
Others: +0 -48 (i18n strings)

## What

The board shows up sooner when the desktop app launches or reloads.

- **Reload to usable board:** about 600 ms down to about 115 ms (5 runs each).
- **Cold launch:** about 1.9 s down to roughly 0.6 to 0.8 s on a data dir with 600 sessions. The machine was busy during these runs, so treat the cold launch number as an estimate.

The startup loader now shows only the AO icon, without the text under it.

## Why

Most of the wait on launch was not real work:

- The first workspace fetch ran before the daemon was ready, failed, and then sat out a retry backoff even after the daemon came up.
- TanStack Router holds a pending screen for at least 500 ms by default (`defaultPendingMinMs`), so the startup screen stayed up half a second after the data arrived.
- The daemon only started after the window finished opening, and it then waited for the login shell probe (0.2 to 2 s).
- The daemon ran `cloudflared --version` before it started listening (27 to 117 ms, 5 s timeout).

## How

- **`useWorkspaceQuery.ts`:** a fetch made before the daemon is ready throws `DaemonNotReadyError` and does not retry. The existing ready triggers (status change, SSE open, the `_shell` startup fetch) fetch right away instead.
- **`router.tsx`:** `defaultPendingMinMs: 0`. This only affects first-time route matches. Session switching is unchanged: session routes have no loader, and the `_shell` loader refreshes in the background.
- **`main.ts`:**
  - On macOS and Linux, the login shell probe starts with the process, and the daemon boots alongside the window instead of after it. `createWindow` already links the browser runtime when the daemon is ready first.
  - If the early probe failed under launch load, the daemon start probes once more before falling back to a bare PATH.
  - Windows keeps the old order. Its probe depends on the terminal shell from UI settings, which are not loaded that early, and nothing in CI launches the desktop app on Windows.
- **`daemon.go`, `mobile.go`:** the cloudflared lookup runs in the background after the daemon listens. Mobile status and enable wait for it, so Connect Mobile never sees an early "remote access unavailable". If the boot lookup finds nothing, enabling looks again, as before.
- **Startup loader:** icon only. I removed the rotating phrases, their styles and their i18n keys. The `updates:isPostUpdateRelaunch` IPC is now unused by the loader and is left in place.

I left `ReconcileStartupSafety` (about 50 ms of daemon boot) alone because it is what stops sessions from being started twice after a crash.

## Testing

- `useWorkspaceQuery.test.tsx`: a new test checks that the fetch happens as soon as the daemon is ready. It fails without the fix.
- `mobile_tunnel_boot_test.go`: new tests check that status and enable wait for the boot lookup, and that an empty lookup looks again later. The first two fail without the wait.
- `npx vitest run` (full suite): 7560 passed, 3 failed. The failures are in `ContextMeter.test.tsx` and `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`, and they fail the same way on unchanged main on my machine.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: no errors outside the known local `packages/product-ui` dependency errors.
- `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 75 passed, 1 failed (`chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts`). That test passed 3 out of 3 on rerun, so it looks flaky.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass. `go test -race` passes for `internal/httpd/...`, `internal/daemon/...` and `internal/mobilebridge/...`. The OpenCode adapter tests fail locally because they read my own `~/.local/share/opencode`, and they fail the same way on main.
- **Manual testing:**
  - Ran built bundles on a throwaway data dir with 600 sessions.
  - Ran them on a real data dir, with the installed app stopped.
  - Booted the daemon and called `/api/v1/mobile/status` the moment it was listening: 200, with `tunnel.supported=true`.
- **Windows:** a teammate ran this branch on Windows and it worked. Windows keeps the old startup order, so that run covered the other changes.
- **Not tested:** a desktop launch on Linux, which gets the new startup order.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Bug]: Home relative times follow the OS locale instead of the app language (mixed-language UI)
body:
### What went wrong?

On an English-language app running under a non-English OS locale, the Home screen's recent-project timestamps render in the **OS language** while the rest of the UI is English — and the project board renders the same kind of timestamps in **English** at the same time. Two surfaces, two languages in one app.

Reproduced with environment locale `ru-RU` and default app language (English):

- Home: heading "Jump back right in" (en) next to «2 часа назад» / «3 часа назад» (ru) on the recent-project rows.
- Project board (same app, same locale): card times render "18m ago", "46m ago" (en).

### Cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/HomePage.tsx` (`relativeProjectTime`) formats with `new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(undefined, …)` → resolves to the environment/OS locale, not the app's i18n language.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionLinkPreviewCard.tsx` has the same pattern for `shell.updatedAt`.
- Every other relative-time surface goes through the i18n catalog: `renderer/lib/format-time.ts` → `@aoagents/product-ui` `formatTimeCompact` with `time.minutesAgo` / `time.hoursAgo` / `time.daysAgo` keys.

So the app language is ignored by exactly these call sites, and any user whose OS language differs from the app language sees mixed-language timestamps. Also relevant to the pending ru locale (#3893): with the app language set to ru on an English OS, Home would render English times inside a Russian UI.

### Suggested fix

Pass the app's resolved i18n locale to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (or reuse `formatTimeCompact` for the Home rows) in both `HomePage.tsx` and `SessionLinkPreviewCard.tsx`.

### Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon); both the packaged desktop app and the plain-browser renderer are affected.
- Verified the code is present on current `main` before filing.
- Locales tested: `ru-RU` (leaks Russian) vs `en-US` (no leak) — deterministic, no console errors.

title: [Bug]: Artifact viewer shows "Binary file preview is not available." for PNGs although markdown artifacts can embed the same images
body: ### What went wrong? In the Artifacts list, selecting a `.png` file renders the placeholder **"Binary file preview is not available."** in the content pane. The same image renders fine when it is **embedded in a markdown artifact** (e.g. a `report.md` with `![](shots/01.png)` shows the image inline), so the bytes are servable from the artifact preview origin — the image viewer just isn't wired for the artifact source. Repro: 1. A session writes artifacts containing a markdown report plus PNG screenshots (e.g. `report.md`, `shots/01.png`). 2. Open the session's artifact list, select the `.png` file → content pane shows "Binary file preview is not available." 3. Select `report.md` → rendered markdown shows the same PNGs inline. ### Cause (current `main`) - `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionWorkspaceFiles.ts` → `fetchSessionArtifactFile` builds the artifact `WorkspaceFileDetail` with `binary: true` for non-text bytes but **never sets `imageMediaType`**. - `ReadOnlyFileView` only renders the `` branch when `detail.binary && detail.imageMediaType`, otherwise it falls back to the "Binary file preview is not available." message. - Even when that branch fires, it builds the image URL with `workspaceRawImageUrl(...)` — a **workspace** endpoint. Artifact bytes live on the **artifact preview origin**; their raw URL is already known (`rawUrl`, passed from `ArtifactFileView` into `FileContentPane` as `source.rawUrl`) but is never used for image rendering. So PNG artifacts are detectably binary, displayable bytes, and the app itself proves it by rendering them inside markdown — but the direct file view can't. ### Suggested fix Detect an image media type for artifact responses (response `Content-Type` header or file extension), set `imageMediaType` on the artifact detail, and render the `` from the artifact `rawUrl` instead of `workspaceRawImageUrl` when `source.kind === "artifact"`. ### Environment - macOS (Apple Silicon); packaged desktop app and browser renderer, both show the placeholder; no console errors. - Verified the code path is present on current `main` before filing.

title: [Bug]: session spawn timeout surfaces only "timed out" — per-step failure causes stay in daemon.log
body:
### What went wrong?

Creating a new task in a project whose origin is GitHub failed with:

> Session spawn timed out before the agent could start

That message reports only the consequence. The actual causes were logged by the daemon (visible in daemon.log) but never reach the user:

```
level=WARN msg="spawn: default branch refresh failed; continuing with local refs" error="gitworktree: fetch origin main: git -C ~/Projects/<project> fetch origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main: signal: killed: error: RPC failed; curl 35 LibreSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to github.com:443"
level=WARN msg="spawn: default branch resolution failed; continuing with adapter fallback" error="gitworktree: resolve repository default for \"~/Projects/<project>\": context deadline exceeded"
level=WARN msg="claimed task preparation cleanup failed" error="context deadline exceeded"
```

In my case GitHub was unreachable from the machine (broken egress), so the spawn steps that talk to the origin hung until the spawn deadline, and every retry surfaced as the same opaque "timed out" message.

Expected: the user-facing spawn-timeout error should aggregate the per-step failure reasons the spawn pipeline already logs, e.g. "spawn timed out: default branch resolution: context deadline exceeded; base ref refresh: git fetch …: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL" — so a user can tell "network to origin is down" apart from "daemon is broken" or "worktree is locked" without reading daemon.log.

### Environment

- OS: macOS (arm64); daemon self-built from `main`
- Spawn path: desktop app "Create task" dialog → daemon session spawn
- Origin host: `https://github.com` (unreachable at the time; reproducible by blocking egress to github.com and creating a task)

title: [Bug]: workspace cleanup deadlocks when the cleanup loop runs under the project's workspace gate (cleanupOne re-acquires it)
body:
### What went wrong?

`Manager.Cleanup` can deadlock itself against `cleanupOne` through the per-project workspace gate when the cleanup loop runs with that gate already held.

`cleanupOne` is written on the assumption that the caller does **not** hold the project's workspace gate: it acquires the same per-project mutex twice internally (once for its `isWorkspaceInUse` ownership recheck, once around the actual teardown, both via `acquireWorkspaceGate`). But nothing documents or enforces that contract, so any caller that wraps the loop in the gate deadlocks on the first re-entrant acquire:

```
goroutine N [sync.Mutex.Lock, minutes]:
session_manager.(*Manager).acquireWorkspaceGate(...)
session_manager.(*Manager).cleanupOne(...)          <- manager.go, re-entrant acquire
session_manager.(*Manager).Cleanup.func1(...)       <- caller holds the gate around the loop
session_manager.(*Manager).Cleanup(...)
TestKillCleanupScriptFailurePreservesWorkspaceForRetry
```

We hit this on a downstream fork that batches `Cleanup` per project and holds the gate around the whole loop (the workspace-ownership freshness check), so every `Cleanup` for a project with a terminated session hung forever; the suite test `TestKillCleanupScriptFailurePreservesWorkspaceForRetry` reproduces it deterministically once the loop is gated (it passes on upstream `main`, where `Cleanup` does not hold the gate, but the hazard is one refactor away).

Suggested directions, in increasing strictness:

1. Document the contract on `cleanupOne` / `acquireWorkspaceGate`: "must be called without holding the project's workspace gate; it acquires it internally."
2. Make the recheck explicit at the `Cleanup` call site: hold the gate only around the freshness list (`cleanupRecords`), release before the `cleanupOne` loop — the internal recheck under the gate already closes the spawn race. This is what our fork now does.
3. Optionally guard against regressions with a debug-mode re-entrancy check (e.g. gate holder ID) or a test that runs `Cleanup` under a held gate.

Happy to send the change if maintainers point at the preferred option.

### Environment

- OS: macOS (arm64); daemon self-built
- Deterministic repro: gate the `Cleanup` per-project loop (as a per-project batching optimization would) and run `TestKillCleanupScriptFailurePreservesWorkspaceForRetry` — the test hangs until the go test timeout kills the binary; the dump shows the test goroutine blocked in `acquireWorkspaceGate` from `cleanupOne`, with no other holder alive
- Affected surface: project workspace cleanup (`POST`-cleanup path), both the synchronous `Cleanup` API and the Kill-spawned background cleanup job pattern

title: bug(send): `ao send` to an idle claude-code TUI worker exits 0, but the message never reaches the agent
body:
## Observed

1. A worker session (claude-code harness, TUI interface) ends its turn with `ao report --needs-input` and waits for an answer.
2. About a minute later the project's orchestrator session runs `ao send --session <worker> --message "<answer>"`. The command exits 0 and prints nothing.
3. The message never reaches the worker: its Claude transcript gets no `<ao-session-delivery id="session-send:…">` entry and no new user turn, and the worker stays idle.
4. Twenty minutes later a second `ao send` to the same session is delivered at once, and the worker continues.

Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-13): 13:50:49 the worker runs `ao report --needs-input`; 13:51:00 its turn ends; 13:51:48 the orchestrator's `ao send` exits 0; nothing is delivered; 14:11:44 a resend is delivered.

Other deliveries to the same worker in that hour (CI-failure notices) arrived fine. The same evening a message sent to the orchestrator session itself took effect only after it was sent a second time.

## Expected

`ao send` either delivers the message (queues it and submits it once the agent is idle) or fails with a non-zero exit code or a visible delivery state, so the sender can retry. A delivery id that can be checked later would also do.

## Impact

The worker waited 20 minutes on a question that had already been answered, and nothing in AO showed that the answer was lost.

## Environment

- Agent Orchestrator desktop 0.13.7 (macOS, Apple Silicon), daemon owned by the app
- Claude Code CLI 2.1.296, worker and orchestrator harness `claude-code`, TUI interface

title: Unauthenticated Loopback Shell-Terminal Spawn and `/mux` Command Injection in Agent Orchestrator Lead to Remote Code Execution
body:
# Unauthenticated Loopback Shell-Terminal Spawn and `/mux` Command Injection in Agent Orchestrator Lead to Remote Code Execution

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project | [Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator) |
| Vulnerability Type | Missing Authorization (CWE-862) leading to OS Command Injection (CWE-78) |
| Severity | High — CVSS 3.1 Base Score: 8.3 |
| CVSS Vector | `AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` |
| Affected Versions | <= 0.13.7 (verified on 0.13.7, latest release as of 2026-10-14; commit `4273bec`) |
| Authentication | None (browser content on a trusted preview origin) |

---

## Summary

Agent Orchestrator's backend is an unauthenticated loopback daemon (bound to `127.0.0.1:3001`) whose only browser boundary is CORS. That boundary explicitly admits workspace-preview origins: `isLoopbackOrigin` (`backend/internal/httpd/cors.go:131`) unconditionally accepts any `localhost` / `*.localhost` origin, and the sessions controller serves arbitrary workspace HTML/Markdown (Goldmark `WithUnsafe` raw HTML passthrough) at exactly such origins (`http://<sessionID>.localhost:3001`). Any file an attacker lands inside a workspace — via cloning an external repository (a core workflow) or via prompt injection writing a booby-trapped `.md` — therefore runs its JavaScript as trusted loopback content once the user opens the preview.

`POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/shell_terminals.go:57-81`) has no capability check, origin restriction, or authorization of any kind: an empty body spawns a real login-shell PTY and returns its `handleId`. The attacker page then attaches via `ws://127.0.0.1:3001/mux` (accepted with `InsecureSkipVerify: true`, `terminal_mux.go:36-43`) and streams base64 keystrokes into the PTY — arbitrary command execution as the Agent Orchestrator user. The project's own threat model treats same-machine browser content as hostile (the `codexAccountOriginMiddleware` exists precisely to fence credential routes off from it), so this endpoint is a missing piece of that same fence.

## Details

`shell_terminals.go` — the create handler documents that an empty body is valid and performs no authorization:

```go
// An empty body is a valid request: it means "open a shell with no project
// context", which the service resolves to the daemon data dir.
var req OpenShellTerminalRequest
if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) { ... }
terminal, err := c.Svc.OpenShellTerminal(r.Context(), ...)
envelope.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, ShellTerminalEnvelope{ShellTerminal: shellTerminalResponse(terminal)})
```

`terminal_mux.go` — the WebSocket transport skips same-origin verification entirely:

```go
// InsecureSkipVerify disables coder/websocket's same-origin check: the
// daemon binds loopback only and the desktop renderer's origin differs
// from the loopback host, mirroring the legacy Node mux server.
c, err := websocket.Accept(w, r, &websocket.AcceptOptions{InsecureSkipVerify: true})
```

The mux protocol (`internal/terminal/protocol.go`) then lets the client open any handle and write input: `{"ch":"terminal","type":"open","id":<handleId>}` followed by `{"ch":"terminal","type":"data","data":"<base64 keystrokes>"}`.

## PoC

Verified against the release 0.13.7 backend (built from the `v0.13.7` tag, commit `4273bec`) running with its default configuration (daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001`). The PoC client is stdlib-only and speaks exactly as injected preview-page JavaScript would: plain HTTP + WebSocket with `Origin: http://standalone-1.localhost:3001`.

**Step 1: the preview-origin boundary check**

```
-- [0] CORS boundary --
    preview-origin preflight -> HTTP 405, ACAO: 'http://standalone-1.localhost:3001'
    foreign-origin preflight -> HTTP 403, ACAO: None
```

A `*.localhost` origin is reflected back (browser content there may read responses); a foreign origin is refused — confirming the design intends to exclude hostile content while admitting preview content.

**Step 2: spawn the shell**

```
-- [1] POST /api/v1/shell-terminals (empty body) --
    HTTP 201 {"shellTerminal":{"handleId":"shellterm-6eb1f1bc19da79b4",
              "workingDir":"/Users/0xgenesi/.ao/data","title":"Terminal 1",...}}
```

**Step 3: attach and inject a command**

```
-- [2] ws /mux: open handle, inject command, read output --
    upgrade: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
    opened: True  output excerpt: ...terminal framebuffer bytes...
    [VULN] marker file exists: Mac-Mini.local
```

The injected command `(id; uname -srm; hostname) > /tmp/AO_RCE_PROOF.txt` executed in the spawned PTY and wrote the marker file.

**Real-environment reproduction** (the product itself, run for this test): the transcript is a live run against the 0.13.7 daemon — shell created over unauthenticated HTTP from a preview origin, attached over `/mux`, keystrokes injected, and command execution confirmed by the marker file on disk.

![Real-environment verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xGenesi/CVE/main/agentorchestrator_shell_terminal_spawn_rce.png)

---

## Impact

An attacker who can place one HTML-bearing file in any Agent Orchestrator workspace (cloned repository content, prompt-injected agent output) gains arbitrary command execution as the local user the moment the victim previews that file — with no vulnerability in the preview renderer itself required. From there: source-code and credential theft (`~/.ao` state, SCM tokens), lateral movement, and persistence. Combined with the `/mux` attachment and mobile-enable issues reported separately, this also compounds into persistent remote access.

### Remediation

1. Require an explicit capability token (as `authorizePreviewServer` already does for preview/server endpoints) for `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` and every other privileged loopback route, minted per desktop window — not per origin.
2. Stop treating all `*.localhost` origins as trusted in `isLoopbackOrigin`; preview origins serve attacker-influenced workspace content by design and must be treated as untrusted for state-changing routes.
3. Bind terminal handles to the connection/session that created them, and have `/mux` reject opens of handles it did not create (see the companion report on `/mux` ownership).
4. Render workspace previews with raw HTML/JavaScript disabled or sandboxed (`WithUnsafe` off, CSP'd iframe on a distinct non-loopback-trusted origin).

title: `/mux` Terminal WebSocket Accepts Any Origin and Any Terminal ID in Agent Orchestrator, Allowing Hijack of Existing Agent Session PTYs
body:
# `/mux` Terminal WebSocket Accepts Any Origin and Any Terminal ID in Agent Orchestrator, Allowing Hijack of Existing Agent Session PTYs

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project | [Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator) |
| Vulnerability Type | Missing Origin / Authorization Check on WebSocket (CWE-346, CWE-862) |
| Severity | High — CVSS 3.1 Base Score: 7.5 |
| CVSS Vector | `AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` |
| Affected Versions | <= 0.13.7 (verified on 0.13.7, latest release as of 2026-10-14; commit `4273bec`) |
| Authentication | None (browser content on a trusted preview origin) |

---

## Summary

`GET /mux` upgrades to a WebSocket with `websocket.AcceptOptions{InsecureSkipVerify: true}` (`backend/internal/httpd/terminal_mux.go:36-43`), disabling coder/websocket's same-origin verification, while the CORS middleware admits `*.localhost` preview origins. The mux protocol's `open` frame takes a client-supplied terminal id and attaches to it without any ownership check (`newAttachment` → `runtimeAdapter.Attach` with `ports.RuntimeHandle{ID: id}`, `internal/terminal/manager.go`), and subsequent `data` frames write base64 keystrokes straight into the shared PTY with output echoed back on the same connection.

Under the same precondition as the shell-terminal issue — attacker-controlled JavaScript running on a workspace preview origin — this gives two capabilities without creating anything new: silently reading the live terminal stream of existing agent sessions (source code, tokens, credentials, internal dialogue), and injecting keystrokes to drive an agent mid-task: approving dangerous commands it proposed, or interrupting with Ctrl+C and typing shell commands directly. Session ids are predictable (`<lowercased projectID>-<counter>` or `standalone-<N>`), so no information leak is needed to find targets. This bypasses the product's entire approval workflow, which is an equivalent of code execution with the user's authority.

## Details

`terminal_mux.go`:

```go
// InsecureSkipVerify disables coder/websocket's same-origin check: the
// daemon binds loopback only and the desktop renderer's origin differs
// from the loopback host, mirroring the legacy Node mux server.
c, err := websocket.Accept(w, r, &websocket.AcceptOptions{InsecureSkipVerify: true})
```

`internal/terminal/manager.go` — the open path trusts the client's id:

```go
case msgOpen:
    c.openTerminal(msg.ID, msg.Rows, msg.Cols, msg.Role)
case msgData:
    raw, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(msg.Data)
    ...
    if a := c.lookup(msg.ID); a != nil {
        c.mgr.writeInput(msg.ID, a, raw, release)
    }
```

There is no mapping between a WebSocket connection and the terminal handles it may address; every connected client may open and write to every handle. Contrast the codex-account middleware (`cors.go:89-105`), which rejects origins not in an exact allow-list — the same treatment is absent here.

## PoC

Verified against the release 0.13.7 backend (commit `4273bec`, default configuration). The stdlib PoC client connects as preview-origin browser content. (The transcript below is the same live run reported in the companion shell-terminal advisory — it demonstrates the `/mux` protocol exactly as this issue describes.)

**Step 1: the WebSocket accepts a preview origin with no verification**

```
-- [2] ws /mux: open handle, inject command, read output --
    upgrade: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
    opened: True  output excerpt: ...live PTY framebuffer bytes...
```

**Step 2: keystroke injection into the opened PTY**

```
    [VULN] marker file exists: Mac-Mini.local
```

The `open` frame addressed a handle the connection had no relationship to, and the `data` frame's keystrokes executed in that PTY. Against an existing agent-session terminal the same frames read the live output stream (returned as `data` messages on the same socket) and inject approvals or shell commands.

**Real-environment reproduction** (the product itself, run for this test): live 0.13.7 daemon, real `101 Switching Protocols` upgrade from a `*.localhost` origin, real PTY attachment and keystroke injection captured in the transcript.

![Real-environment verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xGenesi/CVE/main/agentorchestrator_mux_terminal_no_ownership.png)

---

## Impact

From hostile preview content:

- **Session eavesdropping** — continuous capture of agent/user terminal output: proprietary source, secrets, API tokens, and internal agent dialogue leave the machine through the attacker's page
- **Approval-workflow bypass** — injected keystrokes can accept dangerous tool calls an agent is waiting on, or hijack the terminal after interrupting the agent, achieving user-privileged execution without touching the shell-terminal route
- **Chaining** — independent of the shell-spawn issue; fixing either one alone leaves this path open

### Remediation

1. Re-enable origin verification on the `/mux` upgrade, or replace it with a per-connection capability minted by the desktop app (token in the query string/header at upgrade time).
2. Bind terminal handles to the creating connection or window session; `open`/`data` on foreign handles must be rejected.
3. Make session ids non-enumerable (random rather than `<project>-<n>`), and require an explicit user gesture for attaching to an already-running terminal.
4. Log and alert on terminal attachments from connections that did not create the terminal.

title: Unauthenticated Mobile Enable Endpoint in Agent Orchestrator Returns the Plaintext Connection Password to Browser Content and Opens Remote Access
body:
# Unauthenticated Mobile Enable Endpoint in Agent Orchestrator Returns the Plaintext Connection Password to Browser Content and Opens Remote Access

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project | [Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator) |
| Vulnerability Type | Missing Authorization (CWE-862) / Cleartext Transmission of Credentials (CWE-319) |
| Severity | High — CVSS 3.1 Base Score: 8.0 |
| CVSS Vector | `AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N` |
| Affected Versions | <= 0.13.7 (verified on 0.13.7, latest release as of 2026-10-14; commit `4273bec`) |
| Authentication | None (browser content on a trusted preview origin) |

---

## Summary

`POST /api/v1/mobile/enable` (and `/regenerate`) is mounted on the loopback face without the browser-boundary protections that other sensitive surfaces have (`backend/internal/httpd/router.go:203-212` notes the mobile routes are deliberately not covered by `localControlRequest`; the LAN face 404s the prefix but the loopback face does not). On success, the `MobileStatusResponse` carries the **plaintext connection password** (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go:2128-2155` documents that the `Password` field is populated only in enable/regenerate responses), together with LAN listener endpoints and — when `cloudflared` is present — a public `trycloudflare.com` tunnel URL.

Hostile preview-origin JavaScript (same precondition as the companion shell-terminal report) can therefore call this endpoint with no user interaction, exfiltrate the password and endpoints, and switch on a NAT/firewall-traversing tunnel initiated by the victim's own machine. Afterwards the attacker connects from the internet through the tunnel (or from the LAN), authenticates with the stolen Bearer password — the only check the LAN listener's `authMiddleware` performs — and reaches the full data-plane API and the `/mux` terminal path. The password is also persisted in cleartext at `~/.ao/mobile/config.json`, so the access survives until the user regenerates it, and the plaintext grant happens with zero clicks.

## Details

`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/mobile.go` — enable needs no body and no authorization:

```go
func (c *MobileController) Enable(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ...
}
```

`dto.go` — the response model:

```go
// Password plaintext exists only transiently in the response.
Password string `json:"password,omitempty"`
```

`router.go` — the mount deliberately excludes these routes from the local-control guard that protects other routes from browser content; only the LAN socket blocks the prefix (`lanControlBlockedPrefixes`), so the loopback face — reachable by every `*.localhost` preview origin — is unprotected.

## PoC

Verified against the release 0.13.7 backend (commit `4273bec`, default configuration; `cloudflared` is not installed in the test environment, so the tunnel shows as supported-but-not-running — the password disclosure is unaffected).

**Step 1: enable mobile access as browser content**

```
-- [3] POST /api/v1/mobile/enable --
    HTTP 200 {"enabled":true,"loopbackOnly":false,
              "endpoints":[{"kind":"lan","host":"10.0.1.12","port":3011,"secure":false},
                           {"kind":"lan","host":"192.168.3.198","port":3011,"secure":false}],
              "tunnel":{"supported":false,"running":false,...}}
    [VULN] plaintext connection password returned to browser content: 'DciXg1HR'
```

The eight-character password is returned in the same unauthenticated response that turns the remote-access listener on. With `cloudflared` installed, the response additionally contains the public `trycloudflare.com` hostname; the listener was disabled immediately after evidence collection in this test.

**Real-environment reproduction** (the product itself, run for this test): a live POST to the 0.13.7 daemon from a preview origin enabled the mobile listener and returned the plaintext password in the response body, exactly as the model documents.

![Real-environment verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xGenesi/CVE/main/agentorchestrator_mobile_password_tunnel.png)

---

## Impact

- **Persistent remote access** — the attacker keeps working after the victim closes the page: the LAN listener (or the public tunnel when cloudflared exists) accepts the stolen password as its only authentication, unlocking sessions, files, and the `/mux` terminal path (chaining the companion reports into full remote code execution)
- **Zero-interaction escalation** — enabling and exfiltration require no click beyond opening the hostile preview; the tunnel egress originates from the victim machine and defeats NAT/firewall filtering
- **Long-lived credential** — the password persists in cleartext on disk until manually regenerated

### Remediation

1. Require a user-issued capability token or an explicit desktop-app confirmation before enable/regenerate; never expose the password to any origin admitted by the loopback CORS policy.
2. Show the password only inside the desktop UI (out-of-band from the HTTP API), or deliver it via a first-run QR/pairing flow that never renders it in a response body.
3. Do not persist the password in cleartext (`~/.ao/mobile/config.json`); store a verifier instead, and rotate automatically on a configurable interval.
4. Default the mobile listener to off, require re-authorization after restart, and gate tunnel creation behind an explicit user action with a visible indicator.

title: [Bug]: Qwen ACP treats ask_user_question as permission approval instead of interactive user input (including YOLO mode)
body:
### What went wrong?

Qwen ACP ask_user_question displays approval but loses answers

## What went wrong?

In AO Chat mode with Qwen Code 0.25.1 via ACP, the built-in `ask_user_question` tool appears as a generic **Submit / Cancel** approval prompt rather than an interactive question form.

Clicking Submit produces:

`No valid answers were provided.`

The user cannot provide answers through AO. Asking questions as plain chat text works as a workaround.

### Reproduction

1. Start Qwen Code in AO Chat mode (`qwen --acp`).
2. Have Qwen invoke its built-in `ask_user_question` tool with multiple-choice questions.
3. Observe that AO displays an approval prompt, without the questions or answer options.
4. Click Submit.
5. Qwen receives no answers and reports `No valid answers were provided.`

### Expected behavior

AO should display the questions, including choices, multi-select options and free-text answers, and return the selected answers to Qwen.

### Verified root cause

Qwen sends `ask_user_question` through ACP `session/request_permission`, embedding the questions in:

- `toolCall.rawInput.questions`
- `toolCall._meta.qwenInteractionKind = "user_question"`
- `toolCall._meta.qwenQuestions`

Qwen expects an extended permission response containing `answers` in addition to the selected `optionId`.

AO's generic ACP client (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/client.go`) returns a permission response containing only `Outcome`.

The Qwen ACP adapter (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/qwenacp/driver.go`) does not implement question-specific handling.

Consequently, AO shows an approval but does not collect or transmit answers.

This was verified against installed Qwen Code 0.25.1 and AO's implementation. The full local investigation is `ask-user-question-approval-prompt-root-cause.md`, in orchestrator session `premiumizearr-nova-164` artifacts.

### Suggested fix

Detect Qwen's `user_question` metadata, use AO's existing structured-input UI to collect answers, and return Qwen-compatible `answers` alongside the permission outcome.

Important: YOLO mode is not an exception.
Qwen Code intentionally sets canAutoApproveOnAllow() = false for ask_user_question, because it requires actual user input rather than permission to execute a tool.
Even with --approval-mode yolo, AO must present the interactive questionnaire, not a generic approval dialog. It must neither bypass the question nor automatically submit an empty answer.
This behavior should be independent of the configured approval mode.

Add regression tests for single-choice, multi-select, free-text, cancellation and ordinary approvals.

### Environment

- Linux AO AppImage, Qwen ACP Chat
- AO telemetry version 0.13.7 (CLI reports `dev`)
- Qwen Code 0.25.1

Related: #5093 — shared cross-provider question handling.

title: [Bug]: forge package silently exits 0 with an empty out/ under Node 26 — CI safe on 24 today; one-line override available
body:
### What went wrong?

`electron-forge package` under Node.js 26 exits with code 0 a fraction of a second into packaging, leaving `frontend/out/` empty. Nothing in the build output indicates a failure — instead, the next step that consumes the bundle fails with an error pointing at the missing output path rather than at the actual cause. (In a local rebuild script this also defeats `set -e`: packaging "succeeds" green, and the copy step crashes on the missing `.app`.)

The root cause is upstream and already tracked: electron/forge#4277 — `extract-zip → yauzl@2` is broken on Node 24.16–24.17 and across the 26.x line (reported there on 26.7.0 and 26.9.0; reproduced on 26.11.1). Node 24.18 reverted the breaking Node change, but 26.x is consistently affected, so this will not self-heal. The fix only shipped in Forge 8; this repo pins `@electron-forge/cli: ^7.8.0`, which resolves to 7.11.2 — the last 7.x release, frozen without the fix.

CI is currently safe: workflows pin `node-version: 24` (one job on 22.23.2). The trap arms itself the next time someone bumps a workflow to 26 — and the failure will be silent, as described above. Local builds are exposed today: any contributor whose toolchain delivers Node 26 (e.g. Homebrew auto-updates) hits this with no signal of what broke.

Evidence from a debug run (`DEBUG=electron-packager,electron-forge:*`): the Electron zip starts extracting into the packager template dir, and ~8 ms later the whole forge process exits 0 before any copy work is scheduled — `out/` stays empty. The same tree under Node 20.20.0 packages all the way through postPackage.

### Suggested fix

Cheap insurance now, maintainer-endorsed in electron/forge#4277 — one line in `frontend/package.json`:

```json
"overrides": {
  "extract-zip": "npm:@electron-internal/extract-zip@1.0.3"
}
```

`@electron-internal/extract-zip` is Electron's own drop-in replacement for `extract-zip` (1.0.5 is current). With it, packaging works on every Node version and the CI pins stop being load-bearing.

Longer term, the Forge 8 migration solves this properly, whenever that upgrade gets scheduled.

### Environment

- OS: macOS (arm64), daemon/desktop self-built from `main`
- Toolchain: Node 26.11.1 (fails silently) vs Node 20.20.0 (packages fine); npm 11.20.0
- Dependencies: `@electron-forge/cli` 7.11.2, `@electron/packager` 18.4.4, `electron` 33.4.11 (`extract-zip` 2.0.1 → `yauzl` 2.10.0)
- Upstream tracking: electron/forge#4277

title: feat(chat): add Cline to Chat UI via native cline --acp
body:
## Enhancement
Cline is currently TUI-only: `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/registry.go` has no driver for `domain.HarnessCline`, so `Driver(cline)` returns `ports.ErrChatUnsupported`, Cline is absent from the daemon `chatHarnesses` capability list, and the desktop never renders the TUI ⇄ Chat toggle for it. `ao send --steer` cannot target Cline either.

**Source:** local dev session | **Reported by:** @ApexYash11 | **Analyzed against:** `untrivial/main` @ `70d62ce9e`
**Confidence:** High (traced exact gate + verified first-party protocol on the installed CLI)

## Why now
- Cline 3.x ships a first-party `--acp` stdio surface (verified on 3.0.70: `cline --help` lists `--acp`, "Run in Agent Client Protocol (ACP) mode for editor integration"). This clears the blocker-matrix rule in `docs/chat-mode.md` §10 (AO requires a first-party protocol).
- The reusable ACP transport means the binding is a ~80-line package copying `ompacp`/`qwenacp`/`kimchiacp`, reusing the existing `agent/cline` plugin for binary resolution (`ResolveBinary`) and auth (`AuthStatus`), per the `nativeacp.Plugin` invariant (no second CLI, no download path).
- Known launch shape (consistent with open PR #5604 notes): `cline --acp`, model via `--model` flag + `CLINE_MODEL` env, permissions mirroring the TUI adapter (`--auto-approve true` for accept-edits/auto, `--yolo` for bypass), no launch-time standing-instruction surface in ACP mode. Approval changes are launch-fixed, so the binding needs `ValidateTurnSettings` (same as `ompacp`).

## Acceptance criteria
1. New `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/clineacp/` binding (`Configure`, `SessionOptions`, `ValidateTurnSettings`, `VersionProbe` for the 3.x CLI line).
2. Registered in `registry.Build` (+ pinned in `registry_test.go`); Cline appears in `GET /api/v1/settings → chatHarnesses`.
3. Unit tests over argv/env/permission mapping + turn-setting validation; env-gated live test (`AO_LIVE_CLINE_ACP=1`, skipped in CI).
4. No frontend harness list to edit (Chat UI is capability-driven); verify the TUI ⇄ Chat toggle, steer vs steer_restart labeling, and `ao send --steer` against Cline.
5. Doc note for the binding's launch shape and deliberate limitations (no standing instructions in ACP mode).

## Related
- `docs/chat-mode.md` §10–11 (blocker matrix + adding-a-harness checklist)
- PR #5604 notes (pending ACP bindings incl. Cline row)
- Verified locally: dev daemon on this checkout already serves `"cline"` in `chatHarnesses` with the binding applied (screenshot shared in chat: Cline chat session rendering with model/approval pickers).

**Priority:** P2 — feature gap with a workaround (TUI mode works); **Labels:** enhancement, needs-triage, comp/daemon

title: feat(sandbox): run local Claude Code agents in a Docker sandbox (#6663)
body:
Code changes: +3536 -228  
Tests: +5216 -12  
Others: +2552 -1  



## What

Opt-in Docker sandbox for local Claude Code agents. It covers scope items 1 and 2 of #6663: `per-agent` and `shared` modes, configured per project and overridable per role, with a user-supplied image.

- **Config.** `sandbox: { mode: off|shared|per-agent, image, cpus, memory, pidsLimit }` on the project. Roles can override it. Workers inherit the project block. The orchestrator runs on the host unless `orchestrator.sandbox` is set explicitly.
- **`dockersandbox` adapter.** `Ensure`, `Exec`, `Release` and `Discard` manage containers with labels `dockerreap` understands.
  - Worktrees are bind-mounted at the same absolute path inside the container.
  - The agent runs as the host uid, with `no-new-privileges` and resource limits.
- **In-container `ao`.** A small relay client passes requests through a file spool, which `ao agent-process supervise --sandbox-relay` serves on the host.
  - The host side is confined with `os.Root`.
  - Only these requests are allowed: hooks, report, status, version, and preview with http(s) URLs.
- **Claude Code.** `PrepareSandbox` sets up per-project Claude state. Credentials are passed via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (from `claude setup-token`). The home directory is never mounted.
- **Session manager.** Spawn and restore run inside the sandbox. Chat spawn, restore and switch are refused for sandboxed roles. Failed launches discard their container, and kill removes per-agent containers.
- **Docs.** `configuration/sandbox.mdx` (setup, modes, network, limits, troubleshooting) and `docs/STATUS.md`.

Closes #6663 (items 1 and 2). Prebuild, the settings UI and other harnesses are follow-ups; see below.

## Why

Local workers currently run with the user's full reach. This gives teams a container boundary against accidental damage, and a repeatable toolchain per project.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Local Claude Code workers run on the host. | Projects can opt into shared or per-agent Docker sandboxes; unsupported Chat launches are refused. |
| PR #6693 conflicts with current `main`. | Merged `main` at `c8be3cbd`, preserving native resume/refresh behavior and sandbox hardening, including workspace revision and snapshot views. |

## How: security model and hardening

Threat model: the agent controls every read-write mount. No host-side code may follow anything the agent planted there. The docs describe the sandbox as protection against accidental damage, not as a complete boundary against a hostile agent, and list the remaining limits.

- **Git metadata.**
  - The git common dir is mounted read-only. Only `objects/` and `refs/` are writable.
  - `logs/` is container-local tmpfs, so reflog symlinks never reach host git.
  - In per-agent mode, the session's own worktree admin dir is writable. Its `commondir`, `gitdir`, `config.worktree` and the worktree's `.git` file are read-only.
  - The trusted git dir is resolved from the project's repository path, never from the worktree's `.git` file.
  - Without this, an agent could plant a `commondir` that makes `git status` in the user's own main checkout run its command.
- **AO's own host git on sandboxed worktrees.** Status and diff use `--ignore-submodules=all`, plus `core.fsmonitor=false`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `submodule.recurse=false`. This stops a committed nested repo with a malicious filter or fsmonitor from running in the changes panel or the Destroy dirty check.
  - A session counts as sandboxed if its sandbox state dir exists or its config says so. Unknown sessions fail closed.
  - Unsandboxed sessions are unchanged.
- **Host network.** Sandboxes run on a dedicated `ao-sandbox` network. A pinned `alpine:3.22` helper with NET_ADMIN, which shares the container's network namespace, blackholes the Docker host aliases and their /24, including Docker Desktop's HTTP proxy at `192.168.65.7:3128`.
  - It then probes the daemon's bound port directly and through the proxy, and refuses to start if either is reachable.
  - The agent itself has no NET_ADMIN.
  - No change to the daemon or its loopback listener, per AGENTS.md.
  - Services bound to `0.0.0.0` stay reachable through the host's LAN IP. This is documented.
- **Host file writes.**
  - `.claude.json`, the env file, relay spool dirs, hook settings (`hooksjson`) and the shared `.gitignore` helper all go through `os.Root`, with Lstat checks, O_NONBLOCK opens and temp-plus-rename.
  - The last two also fix pre-existing issues on `main`: a symlinked `.claude/settings.local.json` was followed, and a planted FIFO could hang Install.
- **Refused setups.**
  - Multi-repo workspace projects, because their child `.git` files are outside the read-only binds.
  - Per-agent sessions on the main checkout.
  - Images missing `/bin/sh` or the harness binary.

**Known limits** (documented in Limits):
- `shared` mode lets sessions tamper with each other's git metadata.
- Reviewers and `preRemove` commands run on the host in the agent's worktree, so don't enable `autoReview` for untrusted sandboxed sessions.
- Running git yourself in a sandboxed worktree can run code the agent planted.
- Internet egress is unrestricted.
- Only Docker Desktop on macOS is tested; other engines are best effort, with the fail-closed probe as backstop.
- Ref deletion and `git gc` inside the sandbox fail, because `packed-refs.lock` is read-only. Commits print a harmless `packed-refs.lock` error.

**Intentional omissions** (follow-up plans for #6663):
- No settings UI.
- No Dockerfile build, image caching or setup step.
- Claude Code is the only harness.
- No chat mode, agent switching, sandboxed reviewers, Windows or `ao mcp` in the sandbox.
- No Docker-in-Docker.

**Follow-ups to file:**
- About 25 other harness installers still make their own unconfined writes inside the worktree. They aren't sandbox-capable yet.
- Optionally refuse `autoReview` for sandboxed workers.

## Testing

### Merge resolution validation (2026-10-28)

Merged current `main` (`c8be3cbd`) without rewriting PR history. Resolved the source conflicts, adapted native restore/terminal refresh and workspace revision/snapshot callers, and added sandbox-context regression coverage. GitHub reports head `77f998a25` as mergeable.

- Fixed a semantic merge issue caught by the full CLI suite: the newly added `browser-host` command is now explicitly denied by the sandbox relay policy and its regression test.
- Full backend race and renderer suites are not locally green. The first backend run hit timing/auth-probe failures, installed OpenCode model-catalog/version failures, and inherited AO/tmux environment interference. Full CLI and Claude adapter reruns now pass. Other affected-package reruns use limited concurrency and unset inherited tmux settings; they are still running. The renderer run reports failures in unchanged browser-profile import tests; local frontend dependencies were installed with `--ignore-scripts`, so native-module validation is incomplete.
- GitHub Go, Frontend, CLI E2E, and gitleaks runs for the final head were approved and are pending/queued. Native Windows/Linux CI and Docker smoke checks have not been reproduced locally on this macOS host. Local Node is v26.8.2; CI pins v24.

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `GOOS=windows go build ./...` pass.
- `golangci-lint run ./...` (local 2.14.0; CI pins 2.13.2): 5 `gocritic sprintfQuotedString` issues in the reviewer adapters, which already exist on `main`.
- `go test ./...`: everything passes except the `opencode`, `opencodev2` and `chatdriver/opencodev2acp` packages. They fail locally only because OpenCode 1.18.30 is on PATH, and this branch doesn't touch them.

  - In-container commit reaches the host with the host identity.

  - The host listener is unreachable directly, via `host.docker.internal`, and via the Docker Desktop proxy, including after `docker restart` plus `Ensure`. Internet still works.
- Adversarial review passes reproduced each escape before its fix: commondir RCE, reflog symlink write, proxy bypass, nested-repo filter, workspace child `.git`. Each was confirmed closed after its fix (about 30 network bypass routes tried).
- **End-to-end run against a real daemon.** The setup: this branch's `ao daemon`, isolated on port 3011 with its own data dir and tmux socket; an image built `FROM node:22-bookworm-slim` with `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`; Docker Desktop 29.8.0; a per-agent project; and workers spawned with `ao spawn --harness claude-code --mode tui`.

title: [Feature]: Switch between multiple Claude Code accounts/subscriptions
body:
### Problem

As a user with more than one Claude subscription (for example a personal and a work account), I need to switch which Claude account AO uses without breaking the Claude Code login.

AO has no way to switch Claude accounts today. When I switch between Claude subscriptions/accounts, macOS ends up with two Claude Code credential entries in the Keychain, and AO reads the wrong one. That is the cause of #6076: Settings → Harness → Claude Code → Login completes in the inline terminal, but AO keeps showing the Login button. The only fix I found was to delete one of the Keychain entries by hand.

### Proposed direction

- Save more than one Claude Code subscription account in Settings → Harness → Claude Code, and pick which one is active.
- Switching leaves exactly one credential for Claude Code to read, so the login never ends up with a duplicate Keychain entry.
- Settings shows which account is active (email and plan).
- Adding a new account does not sign out or break the current one.

AO already manages multiple Codex accounts, so this would bring Claude Code up to the same level.

Prior work: #4813 (`feat(claude): add account management and hot switching`) was closed without being merged. #4875, #4881 and #4884 are open follow-ups written against that PR.

### Alternatives considered

Deleting the duplicate Keychain entry by hand. It works, but the only symptom is a Login button that never changes, so it is hard to find out that the Keychain is the cause.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

Related: #6076

title: feat(inspector): give Artifacts its own tab with Finder/Terminal shortcuts
body:
## Summary

- **Artifacts is a regular inspector tab.** It sits after Files and uses the same `FileText` icon as the sidebar's Artifacts entry. The ⋮ menu that used to hold it is gone, because Artifacts was its only item. The tab shows only when the session has artifact files; otherwise the inspector falls back to Summary. It checks the same `artifactFiles` list the Artifacts view and chat artifact links use, so those links still open correctly. Artifact rows in the Summary card, the Artifacts list and board cards now use `FileText` instead of `Shapes`.
- **Open the artifacts folder in Finder or Terminal.** The Artifacts header has two icon buttons that reuse the existing "open workspace" launcher. Labels follow the platform: File Explorer / Command Prompt on Windows, File Manager / Terminal on Linux. The main process gets the session's artifact folder from a new loopback-only daemon route, `GET /api/v1/desktop/sessions/{sessionId}/artifacts`, so it matches the daemon's `AO_DATA_DIR`. If opening fails, the reason shows in the header for 5 seconds. The buttons appear only for local sessions that have at least one artifact.
- **Welcome-screen prompt suggestions sit above the composer.** The order is now heading, suggestions, composer. The suggestions still fold away once you start typing.
- The Browser and Files tabs reserve space so their topbar field doesn't overlap the tabs. That reserve now follows the actual tab count (`--inspector-tab-count`) instead of assuming four tabs.
- **One header row for an open artifact.** It used to have two rows that both named the file. Now one row holds the back button, the file name as a dropdown, and the viewer's source/rendered/feedback buttons. The back button stays visible while the file loads or fails. `FileContentPane` gained a `toolbarHost` prop so it can render its buttons into a header the host owns, following the pattern the Files and Browser topbars already use.
- **File-name dropdown.** It has three items: "Show in Finder" (File Explorer / File Manager on other platforms) reveals the file; "Show in Terminal" opens a terminal in the file's folder; the third item reads "Copy as Markdown" for `.md` files and "Copy contents" for anything else. The first two appear only for local sessions. In the main process, `openArtifacts` takes an optional `path` and rejects paths that resolve outside the session's artifact directory, comparing them after `realpath` so symlinks can't escape it.
- **Delete artifact.** The file-name dropdown ends with a destructive "Delete artifact" item that opens a confirm dialog. On failure the dialog stays open and shows the reason. It's available for local and remote-host sessions, not cloud sessions. The backend side is a new daemon route, `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/artifact-files?path=`. It deletes only a regular file that appears in the session's artifact list, and it opens the directory through `os.Root`, so `..` paths and symlinks can't reach anything outside. The response is the session with its refreshed artifact list. `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck` (frontend): clean
- Frontend vitest: `SessionInspector`, `SessionArtifactsView`, `editor-handoff`, `ChatWorkspace`, 397/397 passed
- product-ui `SessionInspectorView`: 19/19 passed
- `go test ./internal/httpd/...` passes, including spec drift and route parity; new controller tests cover deleting a listed file and refusing unlisted, missing, directory, symlink and `..` paths.
- e2e typecheck (`tsconfig.e2e.json`): clean. The e2e fake bridge was missing `openArtifacts`, which failed both `test` and `renderer-smoke`.
- New tests cover the header dropdown (reveal/terminal with the file path, copy as Markdown vs. copy contents, remote host, delete confirm/failure/cloud), path-escape rejection in the handoff, and also the hidden Artifacts tab, the folder buttons and their error path, and the artifacts-folder handoff in the main process.

title: feat(artifacts): show HTML artifacts in the live app theme
body:
Code changes: +150 -31\
Tests: +182 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

- An HTML artifact opened in the Browser panel now shows in the app theme and restyles live when the theme or light/dark mode changes.
- An inline page in the chat thread no longer paints its own background, so macOS window transparency shows through it.

## Why

Pages in the chat thread already followed the app theme. The same page saved as an artifact and opened in the Browser panel did not get the theme at all. With window transparency on, an inline page also drew a solid box over the blurred window.

## How

- **Backend:** the artifact preview origin serves `.html` files with the theme bootstrap a chat render gets. `?raw=true`, other file types, and workspace previews are served as before. The ETag includes `renderpage.Version`, so a bootstrap change is not served from cache.
- **First paint:** the Browser panel opens an artifact URL with the theme in its `#ao-theme=` fragment, so the page paints in the right colors from the start. History stores the URL without the fragment.
- **Live changes:** the shell watches its theme (`useRenderTheme`, moved out of `RenderFrame`) and sends it to main over `browser:artifactTheme`. Main checks the shape, keeps the last theme, and posts it to open artifact tabs on every change and every load. The page's bootstrap already listens for that message.
- **Transparency:** the bootstrap marks where the page shows (`data-ao-display`: inline, fullscreen, or page). The base stylesheet leaves an inline page's background clear. An expanded or standalone page keeps the solid theme background, since nothing sits behind it. The html tool description and `ao render --help` now tell agents not to paint html or body.

Agents still style pages freely with the theme variables, as before.

title: fix(chat): TUI-to-chat switch fails with 'context deadline exceeded' after an interrupted Claude turn
body:
## Bug
Switching a Claude Code session from Terminal UI to Chat fails with `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` when the last turn was interrupted. The UI shows the raw Go error chain ending in "context deadline exceeded". The switch rolls back, so the terminal keeps working while the chat view has nothing to show.

**Reported by:** Aditi Chauhan (session `agent-orchestrator-246`) | **Analyzed against:** `032ed6f10` (origin/main) | **Date:** 2026-10-14
**Confidence:** Medium (mechanism traced; the relative contribution of the two causes below is not separated)

## Observed
- `GET /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-246/conversation` returns `409 SESSION_MODE_MISMATCH` ("created in Terminal UI mode and has no chat conversation").
- `GET /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-246/interface-transition` shows a failed `tui -> chat` transition that ran about 6s (11:09:18Z to 11:09:24Z), so it was not the 45s step limit:
  - `errorCode: TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`
  - `errorDetail: switch interface agent-orchestrator-246: resume chat: wait for native checkpoint: claude native checkpoint: observed native turn not completed: chat conversation history is not settled: checkpoint mismatches [unsettled_turn_boundary]: context deadline exceeded`

## Root cause
1. `backend/internal/service/chat/native_checkpoint.go:14` (`verifyNativeCheckpoint`) polls the provider transcript under a hard `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second)`. When it expires, the wrapped error ends in `context deadline exceeded`.
2. `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/checkpoint.go:232` only marks a turn complete when `record.Message.StopReason == "end_turn"`. Line 266 then returns `observed native turn not completed`.
3. In the ao-246 Claude transcript, the interrupted turn ends with a `[Request interrupted by user for tool use]` marker followed by a synthetic assistant message, "No response requested.", with `model: <synthetic>` and `stop_reason: "stop_sequence"`. That message was written at 11:09:25.5Z, about 1.4s after the switch had already failed.

So two issues combine:
- The fixed 3s window races Claude's asynchronous transcript flush.
- Even with more time, an interrupted turn ends in `stop_sequence` rather than `end_turn`, so it may never count as settled.

## UX defect
`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInterfaceSwitch.tsx:352` renders the raw `errorDetail`, so the user sees "context deadline exceeded" instead of an actionable message.

## Reproduction
1. In a Terminal UI Claude Code session, interrupt a turn mid tool use (Esc).
2. Switch the session interface to Chat.
3. Switch fails with `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`; the session stays in Terminal mode; the chat view returns 409.

(Not reproduced end to end; derived from the live session state and transcript above.)

## Suggested fix
1. In `claudeacp/checkpoint.go`, treat Claude's synthetic `stop_sequence` / "No response requested." tail after an interrupt marker as a completed turn. Confirm with a fixture from a real interrupted transcript.
2. Lengthen the 3s budget in `native_checkpoint.go`, or tie it to the observed hook event.
3. Map `ErrChatHistoryUnsettled` to a readable message in the switch UI.

## Workaround
Let the agent finish a normal turn (it ends with `end_turn`), then retry the switch.

## Impact
- TUI to Chat switch is blocked after any interrupted turn.
- The error text is misleading.
- No data loss; the rollback to the terminal is clean.

## Related
No existing issues found for `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`, `unsettled_turn_boundary` or the native checkpoint timeout. History-recovery code came in with [PR #4466](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4466).

body:
Code changes: +0 -0  
Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +129 -0

## What

Document the failed ACP gate for #6657 and the upstream change needed before AO can replace its existing prompt delivery.

## Why

Command Code 1.79.2 and 1.82.1 accept session `--mod` paths in ACP mode but do not load them. Both flag positions initialize and create a session, then send a model request without the sentinel instructions. Print mode loads the same generated mod and puts the sentinel in the system message.

## How
