title: Browser profile: explicit Temporary bindings are retained forever and count toward the 1,024 limit
body:
Follow-up from #5453 (review by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari, "Smaller concern"):

An explicit Temporary choice for a worker session is stored in the browser profile registry as a binding with `profileId: null`, and it is never removed.

Current behavior (`frontend/src/main/browser-profile-store.ts`, `bindSession`):

- `bindSession(sessionId, null)` writes `{ profileId: null, updatedAt }` into `registry.bindings`.
- The entry counts toward `BROWSER_PROFILE_MAX_BINDINGS` (1,024, `frontend/src/shared/browser-profiles.ts`). Once the limit is reached, a new binding fails with `BROWSER_PROFILE_BINDING_LIMIT`, so switching a new worker to Temporary can fail.
- Nothing deletes bindings. The only write path is `bindSession`, so entries for sessions that no longer exist stay in the registry.

Why the null binding is stored at all: `getSessionProfileId` treats `undefined` (no binding, use the default profile) and `null` (explicitly Temporary, do not use the default) differently. The `null` entry is what keeps an explicit Temporary choice from being overridden once a default profile is set.

Options:

- A. Do not persist the null choice. Keep it in the in-memory `explicitTemporarySessionIds` set only. Trade-off: after an app restart, a worker that chose Temporary falls back to the default profile.
- B. Do not store a null binding while no default profile is set. With no default, `null` and "no binding" behave the same after the #5453 fallback fix, so the entry can be dropped. Still stored while a default exists.
- C. Remove a session's binding when that AO session ends or is deleted. This bounds growth for all bindings, but needs a session lifecycle hook.

Suggested direction: B for the limit problem in the common case, and C for cleanup. Pick after confirming which AO session lifecycle events are available to the browser profile store.

Acceptance:

- A worker that explicitly chose Temporary stays Temporary when a default profile is set (existing test coverage should keep passing).
- Bindings do not grow without bound, and a Temporary switch does not fail because of the binding limit.

title: fix(claude-code): start tasks on an expired login Claude Code can renew
body:
Code changes: +42 -27  
Tests: +66 -3  
Others: +0 -16

## Summary

Claude Code's subscription access token expires every ~8 hours and is renewed from the refresh token only when Claude Code itself runs. After a few idle hours (typically overnight) AO saw the expired token, marked the Claude model catalog stale with `auth_expired`, showed "Claude Code's saved login has expired", and refused to start Claude Code tasks with `spawn: model capabilities unavailable for model "claude-sonnet-5-5": catalog is stale`. Since no task could start, nothing renewed the token. Users hit this roughly once a day, on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

This change lets Claude Code renew the token itself instead of blocking:

- **`agentcreds`** now reads `refreshTokenExpiresAt` next to the stored login (file and macOS Keychain). `ExpiredButRenewable` is true only while the refresh token is still in date.
- **Spawn (`resolveAgentConfig`)**: a catalog that is stale *only* because of `auth_expired` no longer blocks a Claude Code launch. Models and efforts the last-known catalog lists are still validated. Models it doesn't list are left to the CLI only when the catalog has no account-scoped list; otherwise they are rejected as before.
- **Composer**: no "expired" notice for a renewable login, because the user has nothing to do. The unused `newTask.modelNotice.expired` / `loginAgain` strings are removed from all locales.
- **Refresh token past its expiry** (applies only when Claude Code records `refreshTokenExpiresAt`; not yet confirmed against a real credential file): AO probes the provider as before, gets a rejection (`auth_required`), and the composer offers **Log in** before any session starts.

AO still never refreshes the token itself and never runs Claude Code to do so. Claude Code serializes refresh behind its own lock and rotates the refresh token, so a second writer could sign the user out.

## Tests

- `go test ./pkg/agentcreds/ ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/`: pass
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run TestResolve`: pass, including the new `TestResolveClaudeModelAllowsCatalogStaleFromExpiredLogin`
- New `TestExpiredLoginIsRenewableOnlyWhileItsRefreshTokenIsInDate`
- `vitest` `TaskComposer.test.tsx` and `useAgentModelsQuery.test.ts`: 81 pass. The updated composer test fails if the expired notice is shown again.
- The full `session_manager`, `service/agent` and `modelcatalog` packages have Windows-only failures (Codex ACL, path tests). The same failures occur on unchanged `main` on this machine.

## Risks

- A refresh token revoked server-side before its recorded expiry (logout elsewhere, password change) can't be detected locally. That session would prompt `/login` in Claude Code. This is rare, and the user has to sign in again anyway.
- Older Claude Code versions that don't record `refreshTokenExpiresAt` keep the previous assumption that the refresh token is usable.

title: feat(desktop): switch agents mid-chat from the model menu
body:
Stacked on #6733.

## What

The agent row stays at the top of the model menu inside a session, not only on the new chat page. Switching agents works like t3code: picking one is local and instant, and the next send does the switch.

- **Pick:** the bar shows the new agent, its default model, and effort at once. Once the pick holds for 400ms the daemon starts the agent's process (no session) so the send can take it over; picking something else drops it.
- **Send:** your message shows at once and reads as Working. It becomes the new agent's first turn. There is no separate activation turn anymore.
- **During the switch:** no composer shimmer, and a progress card only if the switch takes over 10s. Messages you send meanwhile wait in the queue dock, survive a reload, and go to the new agent once that switch completes. If the switch is refused or fails, the text comes back to the composer after anything you typed since.
- **After:** a "Switched from [logo] X to [logo] Y" row sits above the message that made the switch. The working timer counts from the send, not from when the new agent took it.
- **New chat page:** it reserves the session's worktree on open and starts the picked agent there, so the first message skips the agent's startup too.
- **Every chat agent** can be switched to and from: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Droid, Cursor, Grok, fx, pi, and omp. Main allowed only Claude Code and Codex. Grok and fx get new ACP Chat drivers.

## Results against main

Headless daemon, one macOS machine. Each run starts a fresh chat, plants context over two turns (fact A plus a real shell command, then fact B), then switches with a five-part quiz the target must answer from the handoff alone. "Ready" is send to the target running that message. On main the switch runs an activation turn first and the quiz is sent after, so main's number covers both.

Main refuses every agent except Claude Code and Codex. For the others, the baseline is main's protocol run on this branch (switch with no message, wait for the activation turn, then send the quiz). That baseline already includes this branch's startup fixes, so it understates main: it measured 7.44s to Codex where real main took 11.57s.

| Switch from Claude Code to | main | main's protocol | This PR | Speedup | Quiz |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | 11.57s | 7.44s | 0.36s | 32× vs main | 5/5 |
| Grok | refused | 19.91s | 0.70s | 28× | 5/5 |
| pi | refused | 7.92s | 0.76s | 10× | 5/5 |
| omp | refused | 8.39s | 1.09s | 7.7× | 5/5 |
| fx | refused | 5.97s | 1.61s | 3.7× | 5/5 |
| opencode | refused | 11.34s | 1.72s | 6.6× | 5/5 |
| Droid, picked ≥1s before send | refused | 7.33 to 7.82s (4 runs) | 1.32 to 1.68s (8 runs) | ≥4.4× | 5/5 |
| Droid, cold | refused | 7.53s (median) | 2.63s (median of 5) | 2.9× | 5/5 |
| Cursor, picked 6s before send | refused | 13.27 to 21.27s (4 runs) | 1.04 to 1.90s (4 runs) | ≥7× | 5/5 |
| Cursor, picked 3s before send | refused | 13.27 to 21.27s | 2.34 to 3.51s (3 runs) | ≥3.8× | 5/5 |
| Cursor, picked 1s before send, or cold | refused | 14.15s (median) | 4.94s (median of 8, 4.3 to 7.0s) | 2.9× | 5/5 |

Codex -> Claude Code: main 8.85s, this PR 2.03s (4.4×), 5/5. "≥" compares this PR's slowest run with the fastest baseline run.

A chain through all nine agents and back to Claude Code, telling each a new fact, recalled 9/9 facts at the end in each of three runs.

AO's own steps take 10 to 30ms. The rest is stopping the source and starting the target.

- **Stopping the source.** Cursor and Grok ignore stdin closing or exit slowly, so every switch away from them waited out the host's 3s kill deadline. The host now sends SIGTERM to the provider's process group 1s after closing stdin, or 300ms after when the provider answered `session/close`. Cursor (no `session/close`, exits 50ms after SIGTERM) and Grok (saves after every turn; verified by killing it without a close and resuming) set `QuickStop` for a 500ms close wait and the 300ms grace. Cursor's stop went from 3.0s to 0.32s, Grok's from about 3s to 1.4 to 1.7s.
- **opencode was slow because of AO.** AO writes its plugin into each worktree's `.opencode/`, and opencode npm-installed `@opencode-ai/plugin` there on every first launch (4 to 7s). AO's plugin only imports that package as a type, so `GetAgentHooks` now seeds an empty `node_modules` and a stub lock file, only when `.opencode` holds nothing but AO's files.
- **opencode-v2 failed to start** for anyone who had used an opencode language server: the data migration refused the symlinks in opencode's `bin/` tool cache. It now leaves that cache behind.
- **Cursor closed every API connection.** Its CLI bootstraps `global-agent`, whose HTTPS agent declares no keep-alive, so each of the dozen calls a new session makes paid a new TCP and TLS handshake. The Cursor driver now loads a small preload through `NODE_OPTIONS` that, with no proxy configured, marks that agent keep-alive and opens three TLS connections up front. It removes itself from `NODE_OPTIONS`, so commands Cursor runs never load it. A switch to Cursor went from about 6s to a 4.94s median. What remains is Cursor's own server time, which the pick-time start above takes off the switch when the pick comes a few seconds before the send.
- **Starting the target on pick.** `POST /sessions/{id}/switch-agent/prewarm` prepares the target's workspace files, instructions, and environment as the switch would and starts the provider in a persistent host under a one-off `<session>.standby-<random>` key, because the current agent still owns the session's host. It runs `initialize`, and for Cursor `cursor/list_available_models`, which loads its services without creating a session. The process's browser bearer is inert until the switch stores its verifier after the source stops, where a cold switch rotates it. On send, a standby whose target, model, effort, approval mode, environment, and instructions match is rekeyed onto the session (`persistenthost.Rekey`) and opens the session; anything else, re-picking, or two idle minutes drops it. A send that arrives while it is still starting waits up to 10s, then starts the agent itself, and a standby that lands later shuts down without touching the workspace. Every ACP Chat driver opts in; Codex starts in 0.3s and does not.
- **New chat.** `POST /task-preparations` reserves the id, branch, and worktree (or a scratch directory with no project) when the page opens, and `POST /task-preparations/{token}/agent` starts the picked agent there. `POST /sessions` takes `taskPreparation`. Picked 6s before send: Cursor 1.24s (cold 5.67s), Droid 1.64s (cold 2.96s), Claude Code 1.01s (cold 1.83s).
- **Readiness.** `POST /agents/{agent}/chat/prewarm` runs the Chat readiness check in the background. Picking an agent calls it, so the first switch to an agent no longer waits up to ~1.3s on it.

Details: `docs/performance/agent-switching.md`.

## Context across switches

- The handoff carries AO's own transcript of the chat: every agent's messages in order, plus a compact line per action (commands with exit codes and a failed command's output tail, file changes, MCP tools, plans, errors, approvals, questions). It fills a 96 KiB budget from the newest end. A provider's own transcript only has its own turns, so after a few switches it dropped what the agents in between said.
- The target always starts a fresh native session. A resumed Claude or Codex session keeps its original instructions and ignores the handoff, so an agent coming back knew only its own earlier turns.
- Cursor ignores the system prompt, so its handoff goes in as a text block ahead of the first message. Its quiz score went from 0/5 to 5/5.
- fx dropped AO's standing instructions, handoff included, because they came with an `ao://` URI ("unsafe target"; fx wants a readable local file). The fx driver now writes them to the session's prompt directory and sends a `file://` URI. fx also wrote its own diagnostics (`[context] ...`, skill discovery warnings) into the reply; the driver drops them while they lead a turn. Quiz 5/5 from Claude Code and Codex.
- The chat's approval mode carries over to the target.

## Robustness

A pass aimed at "never worse than main":

- Held messages are stored with the switch they wait for and sent only when that switch completes toward the chat's current agent. Refused, failed, and never-recorded switches return them to the composer. They show in the dock again after a reload and leave storage one by one as they are sent.
- A failed switch clears the picked agent once, so the next send does not retry the switch quietly.
- A switch or launch that stops waiting for a standby moves an epoch on, so the late standby cannot write workspace files or register itself. Launches take the standby before writing workspace files. A terminal launch that claims a prepared worktree drops its standby.
- Adopting a standby requires the exact standing instructions; a provider that exits during warm-up fails the standby instead of hanging it.
- The handoff redacts secrets in commands, tool calls, errors, and failed output, keeps switch markers, and falls back to the source's native transcript tail if AO's excerpt is unavailable. A resumed agent gets a resume note, not a stale handoff.
- The Cursor preload never blocks a launch, steps aside for more proxy variables, checks the TLS identity of handed-over sockets, and removes stale copies.
- The opencode stub sits under an AO-managed `.gitignore` (the registry's footprint test caught that it did not).
- Discarding a prepared scratch directory only removes the session's own directory.

Rerun on the final build, picked 6s before send: pi 0.43s, Claude Code 1.04s, opencode 1.18s, Droid 1.56 to 1.70s, Cursor 1.11 to 4.92s (Cursor's own startup ranged 3.6 to 9.5s that day), all 5/5. The nine-agent chain recalled 9/9.

## How

- **Backend:**
  - `POST /sessions/{id}/switch-agent` takes an optional `message` (the same shape as a conversation send) and `reasoningEffort`. The chat switch saga delivers the message as a human turn in place of the activation prompt, and tells the target to answer it.
  - Chat-mode switches accept any agent with a Chat driver. Terminal switches keep the old list.
  - `TranscriptExcerpt` on the chat service builds the handoff's conversation section.
  - New `grokacp` and `fxacp` Chat drivers.
  - Standbys: `ports.ChatStandbyDriver`, `acp.StandbyConfig` (Cursor and Droid opt in), `persistenthost.StandbyKey`/`Rekey`, and `Manager.PrewarmChatSwitch`.
  - Each switch logs `agent switch timing` with one duration per step.
- **Frontend:**
  - `useSessionAgentSwitch` and a small draft store hold the picked agent per session, and prewarm the switch once the model the send will carry is known.
  - `useSwitchAgent` sends the message and seeds a local echo.
  - `ChatWorkspace` gains `agentMenu`, `switchingEcho`, `agentSwitching`, and `agentSwitchMarkers`.
  - The held launch bar keeps the agent icon, so the new chat page hands over without the bar changing.

## Not done

- The standby has backend tests (host rekey, driver adoption and mismatch, session takeover, bounded wait, late arrival). The in-chat prewarm call has no frontend test; the new chat page's does.
- Text restored to the composer after a failed switch drops images and excerpts that were attached to it.
- The "Switched from X to Y" divider is English only.
- A switch awaiting recovery shows its card again; the branch had hidden it along with the progress card.
- On this machine `ContextMeter`, one `ChatWorkspace` context test, and three `TurnSettingsBar` long-menu tests fail on the base branch too (Indian-locale number grouping, and a menu click reaching the composer).
- pi needs `pi-acp` installed (`npm i -g @victor-software-house/pi-acp`).
- The agent menu still offers agents that cannot run under the chat's permission mode (unreal-agent is refused on send).
- On my machine `TestResolveBinaryForMajor` and `TestWrongOpenCodeMajorIsRejectedBeforeACPProcessLaunch` fail because a real `opencode` 1.x on PATH wins over the test fakes. This PR does not touch that code.

title: [Feature]: style transcript links like a browser — persistent underline and distinct link color instead of hover-only
body:
## Summary

In the desktop chat/transcript, links (URLs, forge references) currently reveal themselves only on hover: an underline appears and a preview popover opens (see #6479). At rest, links are visually indistinguishable from surrounding text, so there is no way to tell a link is clickable without mousing over it.

## Proposed behavior

Style links at rest the way browsers do:

- persistent underline (not only on hover);
- a distinct link color (e.g. the app accent / a blue link tone), in both light and dark themes;
- keep the existing hover preview popover as-is — this request is only about the resting visual state;
- apply the same treatment to autolinks and inline markdown links in the transcript so all clickable text is consistent.

## Why it matters

- Discoverability: without hover there is currently no signal that text is clickable — this matters for trackpad users scanning long transcripts, and for keyboard-only navigation.
- Convention: every browser, chat app, and markdown renderer underlines and colors links; the current hover-only affordance reads as plain text until touched.
- Consistency with #6479: the hover preview already treats this text as a link; the resting state should say the same thing.

**Priority:** low — pure visual affordance, no functional gap.

**Confidence:** High — behavior verified on the current desktop build (underline + preview appear only on hover).

## Related

- #6479 — hover preview for markdown frontmatter / links (the popover this request complements).

## Environment

- OS: macOS (darwin 25.6.0), arm64
- Build: desktop app self-built from a recent upstream `main`
- Surface: session chat/transcript message rendering (autolinks and markdown links)

title: fix(session): let Restore retry a source restore that failed once
body:
Code changes: +37 -4  
Tests: +118 -15  
Others: +0 -0

Part of #6741

Builds on #6743. This PR was rebased onto `main` and cut down to the one part #6743 doesn't cover. The undeletable-session, Chat→Terminal, and rollback fixes that were originally here are already on `main` via #6743.

## Problem
**"Restore <agent>" can never recover a switch parked on `source_restore_unconfirmed`.** The Restore action (`POST …/agent-switches/{id}/recover`) is accepted, but `reconcileAgentSwitch` returns "source restoration remains unconfirmed" before trying anything, even after the source agent is healthy again. Startup already labels this state "source agent is stopped; explicit recovery is required" (`failRecoveredSwitchWithSourceRollback`), yet explicit recovery is blocked too.

After #6743, Kill can end such a session, and new Chat switches no longer park there because of a leftover target host. A session that is already parked, or that parks for another reason (for example the source agent genuinely failing to restart), can still only be deleted, not recovered. That's the reporter's situation after upgrading.

Reproduced on v0.14.0 with real Claude Code and Codex: the target failed after Claude Code stopped, Claude Code's restart failed, and the switch parked. After Claude Code was healthy again, Restore was accepted, but the log showed `agent switch recovery failed … source restoration remains unconfirmed` and nothing restarted.

## Fix
- Only the user's Restore action (`RecoverAgentSwitch`) may retry a restore that already failed once. Boot reconciliation and a new switch request on a retained session still never retry on their own.
- `retrySourceRestore` compensates the source directly. It stops any target runtime the switch recorded, clears target workspace state, then runs the existing `failRecoveredSwitchWithSourceRollback`, which restarts the source and settles the switch. It never probes or adopts the target. So a TUI `starting_target` row with no target handle isn't reclassified as `target_start_unconfirmed` (found by the AO review), and a live target can't be adopted.
- If the restart fails again, the switch stays parked on `source_restore_unconfirmed`, so both Restore and #6743's Kill takeover still apply.

## Tests
These fail on `main` and pass here:
- `TestSwitchAgentRetainsRecoveryWhenSourceRollbackFails` (updated). It used to assert that Restore had no effect. Now it checks that Restore retries and stays parked while the source can't start, then restores the source, settles the switch, and reopens the session once the source can start.
- `TestRestoreRetriesSourceForStartingTargetWithoutHandle`, successful-restore case: a TUI `starting_target` row with no target handle.

Passes before and after:
- The same test's failed-restore case: the switch stays restorable and Kill still works through #6743.
- `TestReconcileSourceRestoreUnconfirmedIsSideEffectFreeAndIdempotent`: boot/retained reconciliation still never retries.
- #6743's `TestKillTerminatesSessionQuarantinedOnSourceRestore`, `TestKillStillRefusesSwitchWithUnconfirmedSourceStop`, and `TestSwitchAgentChatTargetFailureStopsTargetHostBeforeRestoringSource`.

Suites:
- `go test -race` on the switch, restore, and kill tests passes.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/` passes except four `TestSpawn_*Binary*` tests that fail identically on `main` on this machine (`tmux required on macOS … not found`).
- `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

## Real-app verification
Before the rebase, in the Electron lab with isolated data and a real Claude Code Chat: I forced the parked state for real (Codex target launch and `claude` restart failing via PATH wrappers). The sidebar showed "Claude Code needs restoration". With Claude healthy again, I clicked **Restore Claude Code** in the Switch agent dialog: `source restored`, `resolved=true`, switch settled, sidebar cleared, and a follow-up message got the reply "restored". On v0.14.0 the same click did nothing. The Restore code path is unchanged by the rebase. I haven't re-run the lab on top of #6743.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- In a Chat session, the "Claude Code could not be restored" card has no Restore button. It's reachable only from the session menu's "Claude Code needs restoration" item.
- After a successful restore, the dialog's history line reads "Recovery failed after source shutdown" (the existing label for `daemon_restart_post_stop`).

title: fix(session): unstick sessions left locked by failed interface and agent switches
body:
## Part 1: stuck Chat-to-Terminal switch

### Problem

A customer on v0.14.0 (local, single-repo project) reported an orchestrator stuck with:

> Interface switch needs attention: release untouched Chat provider for 11x-3: empty root proof changed; source restore: switch interface 11x-3: session: incomplete teardown handle

Every retry of the Terminal switch fails the same way, Resume agent returns 409 "Session is missing runtime or workspace handles", and reinstalling the app changes nothing because the state lives in `~/.ao`.

### Root cause

It happens when a Chat session whose controller never started (for example its start failed) is switched to the Terminal UI.

1. That Chat has no conversation row. The Chat-to-Terminal freshness proof (`nativeConversationNotStarted`) accepts "no conversation row" as an untouched Chat, so the switch proceeds with an empty native id.
2. The controller epoch commit (`commitSessionControllerEpoch`) then requires `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider` to update exactly one root branch. There is none, so it fails with "empty root proof changed" and the mode stays Chat.
3. Rollback resumes the Chat source because the epoch did not commit (#6273). The session holds no provider conversation id, so the relaunch fails with `ErrIncompleteHandle` and the switch ends in `recovery_required` with no controller.

### Which PRs

- #5053 (`09effe55b`) added the "exactly one released root" requirement to the commit.
- #5486 (`974a5d06b`) made "no conversation row" satisfy the freshness proof without changing the commit, so the two disagree. Its tests used a fake store, so the real SQL never ran.
- #6273 (`0ca80cfc3`, v0.13.5) fixed the same error for orchestrators that do have an empty row, and changed rollback to resume an uncommitted Chat source. That turned this case into the permanent recovery state.

### Fix

- **Store:** commit the fresh Terminal epoch when the session has no conversation row at all. A conversation with history still fails closed.
- **Rollback:** start Chat fresh when the Chat source holds no provider conversation id, instead of failing with an incomplete handle.
- **Up-front guard:** when a session's start failed before its workspace existed, refuse the switch with reason `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE` ("Retry start before switching interfaces"). Neither controller can run without a workspace, so the switch could only fail into recovery. Sessions still provisioning are not refused. The desktop status poll rechecks this reason, so the switch enables once Retry start succeeds.

Already-stuck sessions recover after upgrading: the Terminal switch now completes, and a session without a workspace shows Retry start, which brings it back.

### Testing

**Unit tests (real SQLite store and controller epoch):**
- `TestInterfaceTransitionNeverStartedChatSwitchesToTerminal`: fails on main with the customer's exact error, passes here.
- `TestInterfaceTransitionRollbackStartsNeverStartedChatFresh`: fails on main with "incomplete teardown handle", passes here.
- `TestInterfaceTransitionRefusesSessionWithoutWorkspace`: covers start failed, no provisioning record, and still provisioning (not refused).
- `TestCommitSessionControllerEpochFreshTerminalWithoutConversation`: fails on main, passes here.
- `TestCommitSessionControllerEpochFreshTerminalRefusesTouchedConversation`: guard that history still fails closed.
- `useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx`: `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE` is polled until the switch is supported.

**Suites:**
- `go test` for session_manager, storage/..., lifecycle, service/session and httpd/... all pass.
- `go test -race` on the InterfaceTransition tests passes.
- `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Live in the desktop app, isolated data, main vs this branch:**

| Scenario | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator whose Chat start failed, then Switch to terminal UI | stuck, exact customer banner | switch disabled with "Retry start before switching interfaces"; no transition created |
| Orchestrator with a workspace and no conversation row, then Switch to terminal UI | stuck, exact customer banner; Resume agent 409 | switch completes, Claude Code running in Terminal |
| Upgrade: open both sessions stuck by main in this build | | the session with a workspace switches to Terminal. The other recovers via Retry start (200, Chat ready), then switches. Remove project returns 200 |
| Control: healthy untouched Chat, then Switch to terminal UI | completes | completes |

## Part 2: "This session already has an agent switch in progress" (delete blocked)

The same customer could not archive the session or remove the project. Their worker row read "Claude Code needs restoration", which is the agent-switch quarantine state.

### Root cause

1. A worker's Chat agent switch (Claude Code ↔ Codex) whose target fails to start leaves the target's provider host behind. Each session has one persistent host (`persistenthost`, keyed by session id).
2. Rollback reopens the source, and `ConnectOrStart` refuses it because the descriptor still names the target's protocol while that host is alive: `chat host incompatible: host protocol="acp" requested=""`.
3. The switch parks on `starting_target` / `source_restore_unconfirmed` and retains the session's switch gate. Recover deliberately does not retry a source restore (`TestSwitchAgentRetainsRecoveryWhenSourceRollbackFails`), and startup quarantines the session again on every launch.
4. Kill hits the retained gate and returns 409 `AGENT_SWITCH_IN_PROGRESS`. Archive fails, and Remove project fails because it kills every session. Reinstalling changes nothing.

### Fix

- **Rollback:** stop the failed target's controller and host before restoring the Chat source. The source comes back and the switch ends `failed` instead of quarantined.
- **Archive takes over the quarantine:** Kill may take over the gate of a switch parked on `source_restore_unconfirmed`, where the source is stopped, the target never took ownership, and nothing runs. Kill stops every controller the session has, then the switch closes as `source_session_terminated`, the same settlement as a kill that wins the source-stop race. Any other retained switch (for example unconfirmed source stop, where a live process may exist) still refuses.

### Testing

**Unit tests:**
- `TestSwitchAgentChatTargetFailureStopsTargetHostBeforeRestoringSource`: fails on main (`starting_target / source_restore_unconfirmed`), passes here.
- `TestKillTerminatesSessionQuarantinedOnSourceRestore`: fails on main ("switch already in progress"), passes here.
- `TestKillStillRefusesSwitchWithUnconfirmedSourceStop`: the guard, passes on both.

**Suites:**
- session_manager, service/..., storage/..., lifecycle, httpd/... and daemon all pass.
- `-race` on the switch and kill tests passes.
- `go vet` is clean.

**Live in the desktop app, main vs this branch, same steps:**
1. Worker in Chat on Claude Code, then Switch agent to Codex (completes).
2. Relaunch with a Claude Chat runtime whose adapter exits on start.
3. Switch agent back to Claude Code.
4. Remove project.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Step 3 | switch parked `source_restore_unconfirmed`, worker shows "Codex needs restoration" | "source restored after target failure", switch `failed`, worker back on Codex and idle |
| Step 4 | 409 "This session already has an agent switch in progress" (also Archive, also after restart with a healthy runtime) | 200 |
| Upgrade: data locked by main, opened in this build | | still loads quarantined. Remove project returns 200, switch closes `failed / source_session_terminated`, all sessions terminated |

title: feat(artifacts): full-screen, editable artifact viewer with selection feedback
body:
## Summary

The Artifacts inspector viewer becomes one combined surface, modelled on Claude artifacts:

- **Full screen**: an expand icon in the viewer header covers the whole app window (the window itself is not made full screen). Escape or the shrink icon returns it to the inspector. The viewer moves between the two places instead of remounting, so an edit in progress survives the switch. Markdown is centred at GitHub's 980px reading width; on macOS the header clears the traffic lights unless the window is natively full screen.
- **One view per artifact**: the File/Rendered mode switch is removed for artifacts. Markdown renders; other text files show as code.
- **Edit in place**: the pencil swaps the same pane to the existing markdown editor. Save returns to the preview with the saved content. Hidden for cloud sessions and for truncated or binary files.
- **Selection feedback**: artifact text is now selectable (the app shell is `user-select: none`). Selecting rendered text opens the app's standard feedback composer (`FileAnnotationComposer`) under the selection, and the comment goes to the worker with the selected text. It shares the artifact's feedback model, so several comments go out together through the existing send-all bar.

### Backend

New `PUT /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/artifact-files` (`UpdateArtifactFileRequest` → `ArtifactFileResponse`):
- writes only a listed, regular file inside the artifact directory (`os.Root`; symlinks and `..` refused → 404)
- requires `expectedFileFingerprint` (hex SHA-256 of the content the edit started from) and returns **409 `ARTIFACT_FILE_STALE`** if the file changed underneath, so a save never clobbers a worker's write
- rejects non-UTF-8 or NUL content (400)

`openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated.

### Other changes
- `FileAnnotationTarget` gains an optional `quote`, which is part of its key, its label ("selected text"), and the message ("Location: Selected text").
- Artifact text reads now compute a SHA-256 fingerprint and mark complete text files editable.
- New i18n string `files.selectionFeedbackTarget` and the full-screen labels, in all 8 locales.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/httpd/...` passes, with new tests for a successful save, a stale-fingerprint 409, and unlisted/symlink/outside/directory paths plus bad content.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Vitest for the artifact viewer, file content pane, diff/annotation components, and i18n: 118 passing. New tests cover: no mode switch, edit and save with the fingerprint, read-only and truncated artifacts, the selection composer sending with the quote, a click-away closing an empty composer, full screen keeping the same viewer, and Escape/back exiting it.
- Full renderer suite: the only failures are `src/main` browser-import/history-store tests, caused by `better-sqlite3` being built for Electron in the local worktree. They are unrelated to this change.

## Risks / follow-ups
- HTML artifacts still open in the Browser panel, so they don't get full screen or editing here.
- The selection composer covers rendered markdown. Code artifacts keep the existing "Ask in chat" selection button.
- Saving rewrites the file in place; a UTF-8 BOM, if present, is not preserved.

title: feat(harness): update harnesses while sessions run (all phases)
body:
Code changes: +5828 -248  
Tests: +4963 -62  
Others: +1126 -9

## Latest-head OMP verification — `ea290627a8`

**PASS at current PR head `ea290627a83bf07ccd09edeebac42ff74dcc47fb`**, superseding the earlier exact-head rerun gap. Fresh backend built with Go1.27.1; embedded VCS revision matched this commit and `vcs.modified=false`. No source changes/new commit were needed.

- **TUI + Chat automatic migration 18.11.3 → 18.12.1: PASS.** Real private Bun baseline, then AO's actual managed Update API with two live sessions and a safe advisory. Same native conversation IDs; new launch/controller generations; stale state cleared; new release's actual native modules mapped in both processes. Their OS process cwd matched native history cwd. Model `zai/glm-5.2`, TUI thinking `high`, and Chat settings were preserved. Fresh post-upgrade replies recalled each fixture's distinct code-word.
- **Unsent-input safety: PASS.** An actual TUI draft remained visible and blocked migration after idle Chat had already moved; old release remained available. After clearing the draft, a harmless completed turn supplied the fresh native idle hook required by OMP, then TUI migrated automatically.
- **Reconnect after private backend restart: PASS for both TUI and Chat.** Same native IDs and fresh exact code-word replies after restart/reattach; durable `v2` leases rechecked. Chat had exactly3 durable user messages with all turns completed; TUI native history had exactly4 user turns (initial memory, harmless idle proof, migration recall, reconnect recall). Challenge prompts never included the code-word.
- **Isolation/cleanup: PASS.** Only the existing approved Z.AI credential and onboarding/model metadata were copied privately; no original conversation was copied. No input, stop, resume or model change was sent to the user's original sessions. Original session metadata and AO PID/start time matched before/after. Owned fixture sessions/backend and detached children were closed, zero private file references verified, then the private tree including credentials was deleted. Global harness installs unchanged.

OMP limitation remains: clearing a draft alone emits no new native idle event and there is no AO empty-composer inspector for OMP; migration safely waits for a subsequent completed turn. Private fixture used `AO_VERSION_REFRESH_IDLE=2s`; normal default unchanged. This was a macOS run, not native Windows validation.

Exact focused regression command (both packages PASS):
```sh
cd backend
GOCACHE=/private/tmp/ao-harness-gocache go test -race ./internal/adapters/agent/omp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/ompacp -run 'Test(RefreshRestore|GetLaunchCommand|GetRestoreCommand|NativeConversationExists|OMP|ConfigureUsesNativeACP|SessionOptionsUseAdvertisedModelOption|ValidateTurnSettings|Driver|ValidateVersionOutput)' -count=1
```
Build: `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/ao-harness-gocache go build -buildvcs=true -o /private/tmp/ao-6745-omp-latest/ao ./cmd/ao` (from `backend`). Actual old/new CLI help verified `--resume`, `--model`, `--thinking` and extension arguments. `git diff --check` passed; worktree clean. No full suite or full frontend typecheck ran.

## Summary

Harness updates now install while sessions run. Running agent processes are left alone and keep the release they loaded. AO tracks every session still on the old release and restarts it on the new one once it is idle.

### How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  U["Update starts"] --> P["Installer runs as its own process"]
  P --> B{"Install method"}
  B -->|"npm, Bun, uv, pipx"| C["Install into versions/vN"]
  C --> D{"vN --version works?"}
  D -->|"yes"| E["Switch current to vN, under the harness lock"]
  D -->|"no"| F["Delete vN, keep the current release"]
  B -->|"Homebrew formula"| G["brew upgrade, keep the old keg"]
  B -->|"Windows, in-place method"| H["Wait for idle sessions, stop, install, resume"]
  E --> R["Running agent processes are left alone and keep their release"]
  G --> R
  E --> N["Every new launch runs the new release"]
  G --> N
  R --> I["Mark those sessions stale"]
  I --> J{"Idle, no pending work, quiet 10m?"}
  J -->|"Chat"| K["Stop the provider and start it again at once on the new release"]
  J -->|"Terminal: off screen, no running command"| L["Resume in place"]
  K --> M["Old release deleted once no session or reviewer runs it"]
  L --> M
```

**Symlink switch (macOS and Linux):**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph before["Before the update"]
    L1["bin/codex (launcher symlink)"] --> C1["codex/current (symlink)"] --> V1a["versions/v1"]
    S1["Running session"] -.->|"loaded from"| V1a
  end
  subgraph install["Update"]
    I1["npm install --prefix versions/v2"] --> I2["versions/v2/bin/codex --version"]
    I2 --> I3["Create temp symlink .current-v2 to versions/v2"]
    I3 --> I4["rename .current-v2 over current (atomic)"]
  end
  subgraph after["After the update"]
    L2["bin/codex (unchanged)"] --> C2["codex/current"] --> V2["versions/v2"]
    N2["New session"] --> L2
    S2["Session started before"] -.->|"still runs"| V1b["versions/v1 (kept)"]
  end
  before --> install --> after
  after --> X["Idle move restarts the old session through the launcher, so it lands on v2"]
  X --> Y["v1 deleted once no session or reviewer runs it"]
```

On Windows `current` is a junction and the launcher is a `.cmd` file; on macOS and Linux both are symlinks. The launcher is created once and never changes, so harness resolvers can cache its path; only `current` moves.

### Behaviour
- **Install safely.** Managed side-by-side and versioned installers can update while sessions use the old release. Unmanaged installers that overwrite files in place wait until dependent live processes exit (or use the existing Windows idle-update flow).
  - Homebrew formulas keep their old keg until no session needs it; then `brew cleanup` runs.
  - **Windows** cannot replace a running executable. There the update waits for idle sessions, stops them, installs, and resumes them; a failed install resumes them on the old release. The wait can be cancelled.
- **No new sessions during the update.** While a harness is being installed or updated, no session of that harness starts. A launch waits for the update (up to 45s) instead of failing.
- **Track old-binary sessions.** A successful update marks every live launch of the harness as stale.
  - Migration 0201. The mark is tied to the launch, so any relaunch reads as current with no extra write.
  - API: `Session.staleBinary`.
- **Move them when idle.** A stale session restarts on the new release once quiet for `AO_VERSION_REFRESH_IDLE` (10m).
  - **Chat:** the provider is stopped and started again at once on the new release, with native resume, in the background. The user never restarts anything, and this does not depend on the developer hibernation setting. A message sent meanwhile is queued and delivered once, on the new release. If the background move has not happened yet, the next message moves it first.
  - **Terminal:** the Resume action runs in place. The session is never terminated. Running commands are read from the process tree under both tmux and the native PTY runtime (ConPTY on Windows).
  - **Never moved while:** a turn, queued message or approval is pending, the terminal is on screen, there is typed input, a shell command or dev server is running, or the conversation has no native resume.
- **UI:**
  - Update, or "View sessions (n)" only when update-while-running is off.
  - "Switching to vX…" in chat.
  - Settings → General: "Move open sessions to new versions automatically" (migration 0202).
  - Windows: "Updating when sessions are idle · Cancel".

### Managed versioned installs (npm, Bun, uv, pipx)
These package managers rewrite a package in place, which can break a running session on its next lazy load (and fails on Windows). AO now installs their updates side by side:
- **Layout:** `~/.ao/data/harnesses/<agent>/versions/vN/`, with `current → vN` and a stable launcher at `~/.ao/data/harnesses/bin/<cli>`.
- **Flow:** install into a fresh directory → run its `--version` → switch `current` atomically (a junction on Windows, under the harness lock) → harness resolvers prefer the launcher → old sessions restart once idle → the old release is deleted once none use it.
- **Delete only when unused:** every launch records the release it runs (`session_harness_releases`, filled by a trigger on new controller generations and terminal launch ids; migration 0203). A live Chat reconnect after a daemon restart carries its old release over. Cleanup deletes a release only when it is neither current nor run by a live session, and deletes nothing if that can't be read. It reads the current release under the harness lock, and keeps every release while a reviewer runs the harness (reviewers are not sessions, so no row records their release).
- **Reinstall** repairs the managed copy (the same release, installed fresh beside it), not the global one.
- **Windows Claude Chat** resolves the native `claude.exe` inside the current managed release behind the `.cmd` launcher.
- **Effect:** these updates are `safe` on every platform, Windows included. The user's own global install is untouched; login and config are shared.
- **Adapters:** every adapter can now drop its cached binary path, so the first managed install is picked up without a restart.
- **Flag:** `AO_MANAGED_HARNESS_INSTALLS` (on).

### Reused from Account Manager (#6274)
- **Chat restart:** the same stop-then-start-at-once move Account Manager uses (`HibernateChatForRestart` + `WakeChat` there); a moved chat is never left asleep.
- **Turn-end trigger:** a move is checked when a turn ends (`SessionTurnEnded` from the lifecycle manager), as well as on the sweep.
- **Concurrency:** at most four sessions restart at once.
- **Retry:** a session a move stopped but could not start again is resumed on every sweep, up to ten tries. A Chat counts as stopped while no controller runs it; its queued messages are delivered by the resume, not failed.
- **`TerminalOnScreen`:** a terminal counts as shown only while an app window holds its grid. The app parks hidden panes and windows with a 0x0 resize (ported `parkOffScreen`).

### Flags (all on by default)
| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `AO_UPDATE_WHILE_RUNNING` | `off`: every update waits for sessions to end |
| `AO_VERSION_REFRESH` | `off`: sessions are never moved (the Settings toggle applies on top) |
| `AO_VERSION_REFRESH_IDLE` | Quiet time before a move (default 10m) |
| `AO_TUI_VERSION_REFRESH` | `off`: terminals are not moved |
| `AO_WINDOWS_UPDATE_WHEN_IDLE` | `off`: Windows updates are refused while sessions run |

### Metrics
`ao.harness.update`, `ao.harness.version_switch`, `ao.harness.stale_sessions` and `ao.harness.update_idle_wait`, all allowlisted for PostHog.

## Known gaps
- **Unmanaged in-place installers** are blocked while live processes depend on their files; managed npm/Bun/uv/pipx and versioned installers preserve the old release.
- **Harness coverage:** all 36 adapters explicitly declare refresh capability. 32 support exact-native resume, including OpenCode v1/v2, Pi and Grok; Aider, Continue, DeepSeek Harness and Chat-only Unreal remain excluded for the verified limitations in [the support matrix](docs/harness-version-refresh.md). Registry fixtures verify native arguments/options; authenticated conversation-memory and arbitrary historical cross-version compatibility are not claimed.
- **No retry on the old binary:** a failed restart resumes on the installed release. AO cannot launch an older binary.
- **Reconnect carry-over:** release carry-over is transactional with the live generation claim; a failed database operation does not publish the new claim or permit cleanup of its old reference.
- **Minimized window on reconnect:** a terminal that reconnects while its window is minimized publishes its real size, so it counts as on screen until the window is shown and hidden again. This only delays that terminal's restart.
- **Native PTY on Windows:** an MCP server an agent starts through `cmd /c` counts as a running command, so such a session can keep a Windows idle update waiting until it times out.
- **Native Windows verification:** startup repair is covered by a forced-crash remove/mklink regression with junction fixtures on macOS. The managed Codex native-executable version/app-server launch still needs a real Windows host before merging; its review thread remains open.
- **Startup proof:** automatic terminal migration requires a surviving exact child and preserves recoverable state on failure; it does not provide a provider-protocol conversation-loaded acknowledgement. Existing unsupervised processes are skipped until a manual native resume supplies workload proof.

## Terminal refresh coverage

- Explicit capabilities replace the Claude/Codex name restriction. Native restore builders preserve the captured ID; strict migration and automatic retries never fall back to a fresh task.
- Corrected Amp, Goose, FX and Auggie passive-resume arguments against installed CLI help; preserved model/thinking options for Pi, OMP, Prime, Kimchi and Kimi.
- OpenCode v1/v2, Kilo, MiMo and Kimi verify exact local native history before stopping; OpenCode majors use separate managed launchers.
- In-use advisories use the actual managed recipe so safe updates remain available; disabled/unmanaged/rejected-capability controls stay blocked. Proven-dead replacement startup failures reconcile stopped state for immediate native retry without an old exit hook; unknown liveness retains retry intent.
- Retried moves share the four-start semaphore through provider startup. Missing Windows `current` after a crash is repaired from durable intent or reported as a recovery failure.
- Full matrix, command evidence and limitations: [docs/harness-version-refresh.md](docs/harness-version-refresh.md).

## Test plan

Passed locally through `78ffa64aca` using focused selections only:
- Native restore/identity/option regressions across agent adapters, including all 32 enabled builders.
- Session-manager eligibility, active/typing protection, shared concurrency, failed native startup/retry and release-store retention regressions.

No full local suites, frontend typecheck, global harness installation changes or AO app restart were run. CI at `645903df9a` found two obsolete Amp direct-argv assertions; both were reproduced and fixed in `b08a0c5ba6`. CI at `b08a0c5ba6` had 19 passing checks and no failures when superseded by the reviewed corrections. title: fix(mobile): keep selected text readable on Android
body: ## Summary On Android, selecting text in a text field showed a solid block with no visible text. This happened in the Environments host editor, the "Name this machine" sheet, the connect sheet, and most other inputs in the app. **Cause:** Android paints a `TextInput`'s `selectionColor` as the highlight itself, at full opacity. The inputs passed `t.accent`, which is the same color as the text (near-white in dark mode, near-black in light mode), so the selected characters disappeared into the highlight. iOS adds its own transparency to the highlight, so it was only broken on Android. **Fix:** a shared `textSelectionColors(t)` helper (`lib/textSelection.ts`), spread into every React Native `TextInput`: - **Android:** a translucent accent (`accentBorder`) for the highlight, plus the solid accent for `cursorColor` and `selectionHandleColor`. Without those, the cursor and handles would take on the translucent color. - **iOS:** the solid accent, unchanged. `spawn-prompt-input.android.tsx` already used this split, and so did the selectable chat text (`ChatMarkdown`, `HighlightedCodeText`, #6441). All of them now go through the helper. **Inputs fixed:** - **Opaque highlight (the bug):** Environments host editor (`EnvironmentMachineRow`), `sheets/machine-name`, `ManualConnectSheet`, worker search, worker rename, elicitation text field (also used by conversation rename), terminal session composer. - **No colors set (stock Material teal):** chat composer, reviewer reply, request card answer, model picker custom field, skills/files search, worker search fallback, iOS spawn prompt (same colors as before). ## Screenshots Android emulator, dark mode, long-press to select a word. **Environments → Edit machine → Host** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | **Name this machine sheet** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | ## Testing - `lib/textSelection.test.ts`: - Checks that the Android highlight is translucent in both themes, the cursor and handles stay solid, and iOS gets the solid accent. - Source guard: fails if any `TextInput` under `app/` or `lib/` skips the helper, or if a selection color is set directly from a `t.*` token. - `ChatComposer.quotes.test.tsx`: added `Platform` to its `react-native` mock, since the composer now reads `Platform.OS` through the helper. - `packages/mobile`: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vitest run` 1912/1912 passing. - Built a fresh debug app from this branch, installed it on an Android emulator, and captured the screenshots above. Each "before" uses the `upstream/main` version of that one file, cold-started the same way. ## Notes - JS only, no native changes. - Light mode was not captured. It uses the same split (`rgba(20,21,25,0.24)` highlight on near-black text), and the unit test covers both themes.

title: feat(modelcatalog): role-scoped model catalog queries — "models as this role would see them"
body:
### Summary

Per-role model pickers don't see what the role will actually run with. Today `GET /api/v1/agents/{agent}/models` resolves the catalog from the default settings resolution (project env + app-level Claude settings). If a role is pointed at a different provider (e.g. #6156 per-role provider pins, or a gateway configured in #6095), the picker still shows the models of the *default* resolution, not the models the role's launch env would discover. The user picks a model that either isn't offered by the role's provider or misses the ones that are.

### Proposal

Add an optional `role` query parameter to the model catalog endpoints:

- `GET /api/v1/agents/{agent}/models?projectId=...&role=reviewer` and the matching `POST .../models/refresh`;
- allowed values: `worker`, `orchestrator`, `reviewer`; `role` requires `projectId` (400 `PROJECT_REQUIRED` without it, 400 `INVALID_ROLE` for unknown values);
- semantics: build the discovery request with the same launch env the role's launch path would apply (role provider pin from project config overlaid on project env, mirroring `session_manager` / reviewer launcher), so the returned catalog is "models as this role would see them";
- cache scoping needs no schema change: encode the role into the existing project scope key (`proj@role:reviewer`), the same trick already used for credential scopes (`@cred:`);
- frontend: role-aware pickers (reviewer selector, per-role settings rows) pass the role; react-query keys distinguish roles so catalogs don't collide.

No new tables, no migrations — it is a query-parameter + scope-key extension of the existing discovery pipeline.

We run this in a local fork today: reviewer model selector and per-role settings rows request role-scoped catalogs, with the same validation and scope-key approach described above. Covered by HTTP validation tests (role without projectId / unknown role), service-level tests for scope parsing and role-pin-to-env folding, and a frontend test asserting the role-scoped cache key. Happy to send a PR if there's interest.

### Related

- #6156 — per-role provider selector (role pins are what make role-scoped catalogs meaningful)
- #6095 — gateway provider settings (gateway catalogs are the main case where the default resolution differs from the role's)
- #5848 — shared model catalogs / discovery rework this builds on

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15 (arm64), self-built from a fork tracking origin/main
- Feature is frontend + API surface; observed on the desktop app and daemon

title: feat(artifacts): version history menu with restore
body: ## What Slice 2 of #6573. Version capture (#6583) records every artifact version but nothing could read them back. This adds the read and restore API and a History menu in the artifact viewer. ## Backend - `session_artifact_versions` gets `source` (agent or user), `harness` (which agent was running) and `restored_from`. Migration 0200. - Saving in the app records a user version right away, while the edit lock is still held. - `GET /sessions/{id}/artifact-versions?path=` lists a file's versions, newest first. It only reads. - `POST .../artifact-versions/sync` records any settled edit the observer has not seen yet, then returns the same list. The menu calls it when it opens. - `GET .../artifact-versions/{version}?path=` reads one version's text. Content over 256 KiB is cut short and marked `truncated`. - `POST .../artifact-versions/restore` writes an earlier version back. It first keeps the current content as a version and then writes only while the file still holds that content: - If the content cannot be kept, nothing is written. That covers the agent still writing (409 `ARTIFACT_FILE_STALE`), a file over the 50 MiB version limit (400 `ARTIFACT_FILE_TOO_LARGE`), and a blob store error (500). - If the agent writes between the snapshot and the write, the restore gets 409 `ARTIFACT_FILE_STALE` instead of overwriting it. - The restore is stored as a new version, so history is never rewritten and a restore can be undone. - A save first records any settled agent edit that has no version yet. Its own fingerprint check still guards the write. - `GET /github/status` also returns `login`, the GitHub username AO is signed in as. It comes from the SCM provider (`AO_GITHUB_TOKEN`, then `gh auth token`) and is empty when unknown. The lookup is capped at 2s and a miss is remembered for 30s. ## Frontend - A History button in the viewer header opens the same dropdown menu the file name uses. Versions are listed newest first, eight at a time with Show more. The first is marked Current. - Each row shows the agent's logo, or your GitHub avatar for a save made in the app. - Choosing an older version previews it in the viewer with Restore and Back to current. An edit in progress is kept. Markdown renders; other files, HTML included for now, show as source. A truncated version says so. - History is hidden for cloud sessions and for binary files such as images. - Strings are in all 8 locales. ## How to test 1. Start a session whose agent writes a markdown artifact, then ask it to edit the file. 2. Open the artifact, edit and save it once yourself. 3. Click the clock icon in the viewer header. You should see three versions: yours as Current with your avatar, then the agent's two with its logo. 4. Click an older one to preview it, then Restore. The file goes back and a new Current version appears. 5. Open an image artifact. There is no clock icon. ## Notes - `harness` is best effort: it is the agent running when the version was recorded, so an edit made before an agent switch but recorded after it shows the new agent. Versions recorded before this change have no `harness`, so the menu shows the session's current agent for them. - Not covered by tests yet: the preview and restore flow end to end in the UI, and the 2s timeout of the GitHub username lookup. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_015RmYFdH4Ww1hyoFWSg8tv3

title: bound ResolveDefaultBranch live lookup + daemon proxy support
body:
## Summary `ao spawn` reproducibly hangs: the CLI never gets a response from the daemon, times out, and exits 1 — but the session **does** appear in the desktop app sidebar as a stuck red-dot entry whose pane shows an infinite spinner (`/ Almost there`). The daemon never surfaces an error, and the zombie sessions can't be retried from the UI. So a batch launch leaves silent garbage that must be cleaned via CLI. ## Environment - Agent Orchestrator desktop app daemon (`ao version dev`), macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64) - Daemon healthy at the time: `healthz: ok`, `readyz: ready`, 5h uptime (pid checked live) - `ao doctor`: all checks PASS except `github-token` — which fails with the **same** `context deadline exceeded`, while `curl https://api.github.com/zen` from the same machine returns `200` in 1.8 s. ## Repro 1. `ao spawn --project

--name "" --issue --prompt "..."` 2. CLI prints `warning: agent "claude-code" auth status is unknown; continuing and letting spawn validate runtime readiness`, then after ~2 min: ``` call daemon: Post "http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers) ``` exit code 1. 3. Desktop app: the session shows up in the project sidebar (red dot), opening it shows `/ Almost there` forever. No error, no failed state, no retry affordance. Observed 6/6 times when launching six spawns in parallel, and again on a single sequential spawn — not a concurrency artifact. Same signature reproduced ~2 weeks earlier on a different daemon uptime, so it is persistent, not transient. `ao session restore` of an existing terminated session works fine during the same period, so the daemon is alive — it is the **create-session path** that never answers. --- ## Debug data (follow-up investigation) **Root cause chain (confirmed by measurement):** the machine's *direct* route to GitHub is degraded (works, but 3–6 s per request, historically flapping to full timeouts). Shell tools survive via env proxy. The daemon is a GUI app: it has **no proxy env vars** and **no macOS system proxy** configured, so every daemon-side GitHub call (agent auth / `gh` token validation during spawn) goes direct, exceeds its deadline, and stalls session creation past the CLI client timeout. ### Routing matrix (same machine, same minute) | Host | Direct (`--noproxy '*'`) | Privoxy `127.0.0.1:8118` (shell env proxy) | |---|---|---| | `api.github.com` | 200, **3.1 s** | 200, **0.85 s** | | `github.com` | 200, **5.7 s** | 200, **4.8 s** | Additional path: global git config forces `http.https://github.com.proxy = socks5h://127.0.0.1:10808` — that SOCKS endpoint is currently **stalling**: `curl -x socks5h://127.0.0.1:10808 https://github.com` timed out at 10 s after receiving ~290 KB. So git-over-https pushes flap for the same underlying reason (degraded direct egress + half-dead secondary proxies), while `gh` in the shell looks "always fine" because it rides the healthy Privoxy env proxy. This matches the machine's long history of *selective, per-host, bidirectional* GitHub flapping (api OK / git push dead, and the reverse, by moment). ### Daemon has no proxy, by two independent proofs 1. Process env of the live daemon (pid 43594) inspected via `ps eww`: `PATH`/`HOME`/`USER` are visible (env IS readable) and there are **no** `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`ALL_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` entries — GUI apps don't inherit shell env. 2. `scutil --proxy` shows **no system-wide proxy** (only `FTPPassive: 1`) — so the GUI process also picks nothing from macOS system network settings. Shell for comparison (any terminal): `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8118`, `http_proxy`/`https_proxy` set the same way. ### DNS is NOT the culprit today `dig +short api.github.com` → `140.82.121.5` instantly; `/etc/hosts` has no GitHub pins. Resolution is clean; the degradation is at the connection/egress layer. ### Timeline / symptom mapping - Daemon-side `gh token validation` (`ao doctor`, and the same validation inside spawn's "runtime readiness" step): direct HTTPS to `api.github.com` at 3–6 s/req × several calls → blows the check's deadline → `context deadline exceeded`. - `POST /api/v1/sessions` (spawn): provisioning blocks on that same validation; the CLI's fixed client timeout (~2 min) fires first → CLI exits 1, daemon keeps waiting → session row already persisted in the sidebar, provisioning never completes → permanent `/ Almost there`. - Same CLI/daemon timeout mismatch on `ao session cleanup` with large terminated batches: daemon continues committing work after the CLI reported `context deadline exceeded` (observed; idempotent re-runs required to finish). ### Addendum: repo-level git config made it look repo-specific (found and fixed) One affected repo (`tg_content_factory`) had local `.git/config` entries that silently overrode the global proxy rule for all its git operations — a month of "why does git flake in this repo while gh is fine": - empty overrides `http.proxy = ""`, `https.proxy = ""`, `http.https://github.com.proxy = ""` — empty values **beat** the global `http.https://github.com.proxy = socks5h://127.0.0.1:10808`, forcing everything direct onto the degraded route; - stale `http.curloptresolve` pins (`github.com:443:140.82.121.3`, `codeload.github.com:443:140.82.121.9`) — July-era Fastly edge IPs; GitHub rotates these, so traffic was pinned to dead/blocked addresses ("Connection reset"). Removing all five keys restored the global socks path; `git ls-remote origin HEAD` answered instantly afterwards. Comparison point: a healthy sibling repo had a working local `http.proxy` instead. Two takeaways for this issue: (1) proxy-dependent machines break in layered ways — per-repo git config is one layer, the daemon's missing proxy support is another, and they mask each other during triage; (2) after the config fix the daemon's spawn hang **remained** (POST /api/v1/sessions still times out even in a good-network window, single spawn, route at ~1.5 s) — consistent with provisioning being wedged behind yesterday's never-completed spawns, i.e., the stuck `/ Almost there` sessions are not just cosmetic: a daemon restart was needed to clear the jam. This strengthens the "fail fast + mark failed" recommendation: a hung spawn must not be able to block subsequent ones. ## 2026-10-16 reproduction: SPAWN_TIMEOUT leaves a live zombie row (and a duplicate on retry) Same machine, daemon healthy (`healthz: ok`), same degraded-direct-route conditions: 1. `ao spawn --project --name "

title: feat(settings): gateway provider configuration with write-through Claude settings persistence
body:
Fixes #6095

## What

Adds Anthropic-compatible gateway configuration (any `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`-fronted endpoint) as a settings feature, at the scope #6095 describes:

- **API**: `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/gateway` (+ `POST .../gateway/probe`). `GET` accepts `?projectId=` and returns the app-scope entry, the project-scope entry, and the effective merge. `PUT` validates the scope and applies tri-state key updates. The probe reuses the existing `agentcreds` validator and returns its verdict plus the gateway's reported models.
- **Persistence: write-through.** There is no new store. Entries are written into the same Claude settings files the daemon's resolution chain already reads: app scope → `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (or `~/.claude`) `settings.json` `env` block, project scope → `<project>/.claude/settings.json`. A hand-edited file and a UI save can never disagree, and model discovery picks gateway models up with no changes on our side.
- **UI**: a "Gateway providers" section in global settings, and a Gateway tab in local project settings showing the project override next to the inherited app-wide values, with an effective line. The probe's model list feeds a datalist on the model input. Translations for all eight locales.

## Design decisions

- **Concurrency with the CLI**: last-writer-wins, saved atomically (temp file + rename; Windows falls back to remove+rename). Files are re-read on every write, so external edits between saves are not clobbered beyond the usual last-writer-wins window.
- **Foreign keys survive**: the file is parsed as raw JSON and only the three known keys inside `env` are mutated; formatting is normalized (2-space JSON + trailing newline) on first write.
- **`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` respected**: the writer resolves the app-scope path through the same exported `agentcreds.ClaudeConfigDir` helper the reader uses, so writer and reader cannot drift.
- **Empty string = delete.** Writing `""` into these env keys would shadow inherited values (the resolution chain treats empty as set), so clearing a field removes the key instead.
- **`settings.local.json`**: the UI writes only `settings.json`; `settings.local.json` is still read and wins in the effective merge. One open question for maintainers: a project-scope token lands in `<project>/.claude/settings.json`, which is typically committed — should the project-scope write target `settings.local.json` instead (or split base URL and token across the two files)?
- **Known gaps, proposed as follow-ups**: the model catalog cache isn't invalidated when an entry is saved (gateway models appear after the next discovery refresh), and config that lives only in process env is invisible to the UI — the effective line could gain an `env` source in ~8 lines if wanted.

## Testing

- `backend/internal/service/gateway`: tri-state persistence, project-over-app effective merge, `settings.local.json` winning in effective, foreign keys and file mode preserved, validation rejects bad scopes/URLs.
- `controllers`: 501 when unwired, scope/project validation, query propagation, error mapping.
- `frontend`: section renders stored entries, tri-state PUT bodies, probe verdict + model datalist, project override editor.

title: [Bug]: Browser panel cannot scroll or click pages that declare `app-region: drag` (e.g. Linear)
body:
### What went wrong?

In the Browser panel, some pages cannot be scrolled with the mouse wheel or trackpad, and clicks on parts of the page do nothing, while the same page works normally in Chrome. Linear's narrow layout is a reliable example: open any Linear page in the Browser panel with the panel at a narrow width, and wheel/trackpad scrolling and clicks are ignored. An agent driving the same tab with `ao browser` can still scroll it, which made it look like a human-only problem.

### Expected

Pages in the Browser panel accept wheel, click and scrollbar input the same way they do in a normal browser.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon)

### Analysis (agent-collected, separate from the observation)

Linear declares `app-region: drag` on a full-viewport container for its own Electron desktop build. Chrome ignores the property, but inside AO's embedded `WebContentsView` Electron honours it: native hit-testing returns no view for those regions, so real input never reaches the page while CDP/`sendInputEvent` scrolling still works. Injecting a user-origin `app-region: no-drag !important` rule into browser pages fixes it; a PR with that change and a test follows.

title: [Bug]: usage sources stuck on source_event_conflict re-finalize every 2 s and flood change_log with session_updated
body:
### What went wrong?

After a reboot, several Claude sessions' usage sources got stuck. For each of them the daemon flipped the `usage_bindings` row between `partial` and `finalizing` every two seconds, forever. Each flip wrote two `usage_bindings` updates and therefore two `session_updated` rows into `change_log`, so the renderer kept receiving `session_updated` events for idle sessions and `change_log` grew continuously. The sources' `last_error_code` was `source_event_conflict`.

### Expected

A source whose replay conflicts with what is already stored should stop retrying (or retry on a sane schedule), and an idle session should not produce a steady stream of `session_updated` events.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon); the stuck sources appeared after a reboot that renumbered the volume, so every transcript's `unix:dev:ino` identity changed and every source replayed from byte zero

### Analysis (agent-collected, separate from the observation)

Two things combine:

1. The replay of a transcript whose stored rows the legacy repairer had attributed by inference arrives unattributed (live parsing never infers a billing provider), so `ApplyUsageChunk` compares `"anthropic"` with `""` and reports `source_event_conflict`.
2. On that conflict the ingestor keeps the cursor in front of the rejected chunk, returns the finalization `RetryAt` computed earlier in the pass, and `MarkUsageSourceState` clears `next_retry_at`, so the quiet period never settles and the binding is reopened two seconds later.

Related to #6219, which measured the `usage_bindings_cdc_update` write rate on a different machine; part of that rate comes from this loop. A PR that makes an unattributed replay match the stored attribution and parks conflicting sources follows.

title: [Bug]: Connect Mobile quick tunnel never registers on networks that drop UDP (cloudflared stays on QUIC)
body:
### What went wrong?

Connect Mobile's managed quick tunnel never became ready on my Mac while a VPN/proxy in TUN mode was active. The daemon log showed cloudflared redialing over and over without ever printing "Registered tunnel connection", and the Connect Mobile panel never showed a tunnel endpoint. With the proxy off, the tunnel registered within seconds.

### Expected

The quick tunnel registers on networks that drop UDP, or at least falls back to a TCP transport.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon); a VPN/proxy in TUN mode that drops UDP to Cloudflare's edge

### Analysis (agent-collected, separate from the observation)

cloudflared starts a quick tunnel on QUIC and does not fall back on its own. On a network that drops UDP it never registers; its own precheck even suggests http2. Starting the connector with `--protocol http2` registered about a second after the hostname was issued on the same network, and works on networks where QUIC also works. A PR that pins the connector to HTTP/2 follows.

title: [Bug]: a quick tunnel whose edge connection dropped is still advertised as ready to the phone and the Connect Mobile panel
body:
### What went wrong?

While the quick tunnel's connection to Cloudflare's edge was down, AO kept advertising the tunnel endpoint as ready: the Connect Mobile panel still showed it, and the phone kept trying it and failing, until cloudflared re-registered (sometimes minutes later). On one flapping link I counted 18 edge disconnects in three hours. Nothing about those disconnects appeared in the daemon log at the normal level, so it was hard to tell what the phone was fighting.

### Expected

A tunnel endpoint is only advertised while the connector actually has a live edge connection, and edge connects/disconnects are visible in the daemon log.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon); a link behind a TUN-mode proxy that flaps

### Analysis (agent-collected, separate from the observation)

cloudflared outlives an edge disconnect and re-registers on the same hostname, but `TunnelLog` only counts registrations, so a tunnel whose only edge connection dropped still reads as ready. The raw connector output is debug-only. Tracking live connections by `connIndex` from cloudflared's own "Registered tunnel connection" / "Lost connection with the edge" / "Connection terminated" lines, withdrawing the endpoint while no connection is up, and logging each transition at INFO fixes both parts. A PR with that change and tests follows.

title: [Bug]: after the shell renderer process crashes, AO shows a blank white window until quit; tray Show and notification clicks re-show it
body:
### What went wrong?

After a few hours of use the AO window suddenly went completely white: no sidebar, no content, nothing reacting to clicks. The daemon and the sessions were still running (the tray menu listed them). Clicking the tray's "Show", clicking a notification, or launching AO again just brought the same white window to the front. The only way back was to quit from the tray and start AO again. The Electron log showed the shell renderer process had gone away (an out-of-memory crash of the renderer).

### Expected

When the renderer process dies, AO rebuilds the window (or at least offers to), instead of leaving a dead white window that every entry point re-shows.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon), long-running session with many active workers

### Analysis (agent-collected, separate from the observation)

`main.ts` handles `render-process-gone` only by resetting a few flags; the `BaseWindow` keeps its transparent shell view with nothing painting into it. Tray "Show", notification clicks, second-instance and Dock activate all call `show()` on that window. Rebuilding the window after `render-process-gone` (restoring bounds and window state, not taking focus for an automatic rebuild, with a crash-loop guard that asks in a native dialog after repeated crashes), and making the other entry points rebuild a dead window instead of showing it, fixes it. Related to the crash-screen discussion in #6134, but this is the process-level crash rather than a React error boundary. A PR with that change and tests follows.

title: [Bug]: id-only or repeated session_updated events refetch the whole workspace every 150 ms during long agent runs
body:
### What went wrong?

With a few long-running agent sessions open, the desktop renderer refetched `/api/v1/sessions` (the whole workspace) continuously, about every 150 ms, for hours. Most of the `session_updated` events that triggered those refetches carried only a session id, or repeated a status the session already had; nothing visible on the board changed. The renderer's memory kept growing during such runs, and in one case it ended with the renderer crash described in the issue about the blank window.

### Expected

Events that do not change what the board shows should not refetch the whole workspace at the maximum rate; real status changes should still refresh immediately.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon), several Claude sessions with subagents (high usage-event rate)

### Analysis (agent-collected, separate from the observation)

`event-transport.ts` coalesces CDC events into a 150 ms window, but every `session_updated` invalidates the workspace query regardless of whether the session's status changed. Routing id-only updates and updates that repeat the session's last status through a slower background lane (one flush per five seconds) while keeping status changes and new sessions on the immediate path removes the storm. A PR with that change and tests follows.

title: [Bug]: a phone on the quick tunnel re-requests its whole event backlog every ~30 s because Quick Tunnels cut SSE streams
body:
### What went wrong?

A phone connected through the managed quick tunnel became very slow after the app had been in the background for a while. The daemon log showed the phone opening `/api/v1/events` with an old cursor, the daemon replaying the whole backlog (about 12 MB in my case), the stream being cut after roughly 30 seconds, and the phone reconnecting and asking for the same backlog again: seven times in six minutes. Every other request the phone made was starved meanwhile.

### Expected

A client coming back through the tunnel should not have to download the full retained change log before it gets live events, especially since the mobile app already re-reads the board and the open conversation on reconnect.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon) with Connect Mobile's managed cloudflared quick tunnel; iPhone on a different network

### Analysis and proposed change (agent-collected)

Cloudflare Quick Tunnels do not support long-lived SSE, so the edge closes each stream after about 30 s, and a large replay never finishes. The mobile app already adopts the `X-AO-Event-After` header as its cursor, so the daemon can replay at most one batch for streams that reach the LAN listener from loopback (the managed cloudflared or another local connector) and report the jump in that header. Direct LAN clients and the loopback desktop listener would keep the full replay. Logging each stream's transport, cursor, backlog and skipped count on open and its replayed/live counts and end reason on close would make this visible.

I have this implemented with tests (four cases: capped through cloudflared, capped through any local connector, full replay for direct LAN clients, small backlog replayed in full) and can open a PR if this direction is acceptable. It builds on the transport classification from the LAN-listener gzip/rejection-log proposal, so it would come after that one.
