title: fix(usage): stop conflicting sources from looping session_updated events
body:
Code changes: +44 -2\
Tests: +496 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A usage source whose replay is rejected as `source_event_conflict` no longer flips its binding between `partial` and `finalizing` every two seconds.

- A replay that names no billing route now matches a stored attribution and keeps it, the same way a stored NULL attribution already matches.
- A source that hits a conflict is parked in memory at that cursor: no retry is scheduled and later passes return before reopening the binding. Reactivation, a replaced transcript's new generation, or a daemon restart earns another attempt, so sources parked by an older build heal once this ships.

## Why

Fixes #6757. Related: #6219 (part of the `usage_bindings_cdc_update` write rate measured there comes from this loop).

A source whose replay `ApplyUsageChunk` rejects keeps its cursor in front of the rejected chunk, so its transcript always looks longer than what was ingested. The conflict path also returned the finalization `RetryAt` computed earlier in the pass, and `MarkUsageSourceState` cleared `next_retry_at`, so the quiet period never settled. Every two seconds the ingestor reopened the idle partial binding to `finalizing`, hit the same conflict, and settled it back to `partial`: two `usage_bindings` updates and two `session_updated` change_log rows, forever, per source.

The conflicts came from replays of transcripts whose stored rows the legacy repairer had attributed by inference. Live parsing never infers a billing provider, so the replay arrived unattributed and the disposition compared `"anthropic"` with `""` and called it a conflict. A reboot that renumbers the volume changes every file identity (`unix:dev:ino`) and replays every source from byte zero, which is how a whole machine's worth of sources got stuck at once.

## How

- `usage_store.go`: an unattributed replay event matches any stored attribution (one more case in the replay disposition).
- `ingestor.go`: a per-source in-memory park set, checked before the binding is reopened and cleared on reactivation or a new generation.
- No migration. `usage_bindings_cdc_update` cannot tell a meaningful update from a no-op one, because `TouchUsageBinding` is an `updated_at`-only UPDATE that relies on the trigger to publish real usage changes.
- Intentional omission: no retention or janitor change; that is #6219's scope.

## Testing

- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/observe/usage/...`: ok. New: `TestIngestorParksConflictingSourceInsteadOfReopeningItsBinding`, `TestIngestorRetriesParkedConflictAfterReactivation`, `TestIngestorReplayAfterIdentityChangeKeepsRepairedAttribution`, `TestIngestorHealsSourceParkedByEarlierBuild`, `TestIngestorStopsRetryingConflictingNativeEvent`.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/storage/sqlite/store/` (usage/replay/attribution tests): ok. New: `TestApplyUsageChunkUnattributedReplayKeepsStoredAttribution`.

title: feat(cloud): store cloud session artifacts in S3 behind AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS (1/3)
body:
Code changes: +2496 -50  
Tests: +1775 -1  
Others: +886 -2 (contract, generated cloud-client schema, go.mod/go.sum, compose/env)

Stack: **#6769 control plane (this PR)** → #6779 worker → #6809 desktop and docs.

## Summary

PR 1 of 3 for **cloud session artifacts**: the control plane, shipped dark behind `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS` (default off). With the flag off nothing changes. The artifact routes are not registered (404), `requestedOutput: "artifact"` is rejected (422), and no S3 client is constructed. Migration `00084` runs either way; it is safe to run again, so it can be renumbered after reaching an environment. #6844 renumbers above `00086` (#6929); this PR merges first.

When the flag is on:
- **Storage**: workers relay files through the control plane into a versioned S3 bucket at `orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}/{path}`. Postgres keeps one row per file (`ao_session_artifacts`) with the S3 key, the committed `version_id` and the sha256. It never stores file bytes.
- **Worker routes**: these use worker-token auth and epoch fencing, like `/worker/transcript`.
  - `POST /worker/artifacts/manifest` compares `(path, size, sha)` against the stored rows and returns the paths that changed.
  - `PUT /worker/artifacts/blob/{path}` streams the body to S3 with `ChecksumSHA256` and requires `Content-Length`, with a 5-minute read deadline. A checksum mismatch returns 422, and S3 creates no version. Each upload is recorded in `ao_artifact_object_versions`; a session can hold at most 400 uncommitted uploads or 1000 MiB.
  - `POST /worker/artifacts/commit` checks each `(path, versionId)` with `HeadObject` (size and sha), then, in **one transaction** under the session row lock and only from the worker's current connection: claims each version as an open upload, upserts and deletes rows, queues the versions it replaced or deleted, recomputes `output_type` and appends an `artifact.changed` event. The 200-file / 500 MiB per-session caps are enforced inside that transaction, and a commit that changes nothing appends no event.
- **Cleanup**: a sweeper deletes, by version, uploads not committed within 24 hours and replaced or deleted versions one hour after their commit. A version the sweeper has claimed can no longer be committed.
- **Tenant routes**:
  - `GET /orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}/artifacts` reads Postgres only and never calls `ResumeSession`.
  - `POST …/artifacts/access` returns a 10-minute HMAC-signed path prefix bound to one user, org and session. The signing key is derived from `AO_CLOUD_PROVIDER_SECRET_KEY`.
  - `GET /artifact-files/{token}/{path}` checks that the user is still an active member of an active org, reads the row, fetches the **committed** version from S3 and streams it (HEAD reads metadata only). Every file response sets a CSP `sandbox` without `allow-same-origin` or popups and with `connect-src 'none'`, plus `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, Content-Type from the extension and an ETag from the sha (304 is supported). If the row exists but the object is gone, it returns 404 with code `artifact_unavailable`.
- **Session fields**:
  - `requestedOutput` is accepted on create and passed to the worker in `LaunchContext`.
  - `outputType` is in every session projection; every session read counts the session's pull requests into it.
  - The session list carries `artifactCount`; session get carries `artifactCount` and `artifactFiles`.
  - `/me` gains `offering.artifacts`, so the desktop can gate its UI (unverified item 2).
- **Isolation**:
  - Object keys come only from claims or from Postgres rows read under the org's RLS context. The client never supplies a key.
  - The key builder refuses an empty org or session.
  - Paths are NFC-normalised. Paths that are absolute, contain backslashes or drive letters, contain `.`/`..`/empty segments, control or invisible format characters, or Windows device names, sit under `.versions/` in any letter case, or push the key past 1024 bytes are rejected. Content-Type comes from a fixed list.
- **Config and deploy**:
  - `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS`, `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_BUCKET`, `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_REGION` and the optional `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_ENDPOINT` (for MinIO). Startup fails when the flag is on without bucket, region or provider key.
  - Staging and production offering files set the flag to `0` with the decided buckets `ao-cloud-{staging,production}-tenant-artifacts` (region `eu-north-1`).
  - `validate-hosted-settings.py` and the task renderer reject a bad flag, a missing bucket or region, the worker-binary bucket (`ao-cloud-<env>-artifacts`), and any endpoint override in hosted tasks. The control plane refuses an unparseable `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS`.
  - With the flag at `1`, `deploy-staging.sh` and `promote-production.sh` stop unless the bucket exists with versioning enabled, and production needs staging to serve artifacts first.
- **Local**: `compose.yaml` adds MinIO (pinned by digest, running as the invoking user) plus a one-shot `minio-init`, bounded to a minute, that creates `ao-cloud-local-tenant-artifacts` with versioning on. Data lives under `~/.ao/cloud/minio`, and `cloud-local-reset.sh` removes it after resolving the path.
- **Contract**: `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` is edited (it is the source), and `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated with `npm run generate`.

## Unverified items from the brief

1. **Streamed checksum upload: resolved, the design holds, with one constraint.** I checked with aws-sdk-go-v2 (`service/s3` v1.114.3) against MinIO:
   - A non-seekable body needs SigV4 `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD`; otherwise the SDK cannot hash the payload.
   - With `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD`, `ChecksumSHA256` and a known `Content-Length`, a mismatch is rejected (`XAmzContentChecksumMismatch`) and **no version is created**.
   - An unknown length is rejected with 411. The blob route therefore requires `Content-Length`, which the worker always knows.
   - No trailing checksums or multipart upload are needed.
   - Not yet run against real AWS S3.
2. **How the desktop learns artifacts are enabled: resolved.** `/me` already returns `offering` per org and for the active org, so this PR adds `offering.artifacts`.
3. **MinIO versioning: resolved.** `VersionId` is returned, and `GetObject`/`HeadObject` by version work, both on the cached `minio/minio` image and on the `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio` image compose now uses. A made-up version id returns 404.

## Tests run

Re-run after the review (2026-10-19), on the merged branch:
- `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `GOWORK=off go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`: clean.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` with a scratch Postgres: everything passes except four `internal/postgres` tests and the two `internal/workerexec` Claude tests, which fail the same way on a clean `origin/main` checkout.
- New tests: upload cap; commit needs an open upload and queues replaced versions; empty and no-op commits append no event; replaced worker rejected; sweeper claim/forget; disabled member cannot read; two racing 150-file commits give exactly one success; PR-derived output type on read; migration runs twice; idempotency payload; path rules; fixed Content-Type list; sweeper against the fake S3; unparseable flag refused; membership revocation, HEAD without `GetObject`, and pending cap through the router.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 85 pass. Cloud client: typecheck and tests pass.
- Live on `npm run cloud:local`: see the follow-up table below.

Original run:
- `cd cloud && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./...`: clean.
- `cd cloud && go test -race -count=1 ./...` (the CI job) passes except `internal/workerexec` `TestCloudClaude{ProviderModelsReachAdapter,DiscoversProviderCatalogWithLaunchCredentials}`. Those two **fail identically on `origin/main`** in this environment and are not touched here.
- Postgres integration, with `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL` on a scratch `postgres:17`, under a role without RLS bypass:
  - New tests for the artifact store: commit, list and output type (including `pr_artifact` and a delete back to `pr`); the manifest diff; file-count and byte caps rejected with no rows and no event; a commit that fails mid-way leaves no rows, no event and no output-type change; isolation between two orgs (list, read, batch read, commit and manifest all fail across orgs).
  - The rest of `internal/postgres` passes except four tests that also fail on `origin/main` with a fresh database.
- Handler tests through the full router, with the in-process fake S3:
  - Flag off returns 404 everywhere, and `/me` reports `artifacts:false`.
  - Missing, stale-epoch and wrong-scope worker tokens are rejected.
  - Checksum mismatch returns 422 with no version; over-cap returns 413; unknown length returns 411; bad paths and traversal attempts are rejected.
  - A commit naming a missing or mismatched version returns 409, and nothing is stored.
  - Listing artifacts never calls `ResumeSession`.
  - Files are served with the right headers, relative assets resolve, and 304 works.
  - A newer **uncommitted** upload is never served.
  - A missing object returns `artifact_unavailable`.
  - Forged and expired tokens return 401.
  - Cross-tenant requests return 404 or 403, and a worker of session B cannot write into session A's prefix.
- `artifactstore` against the fake S3 and against real MinIO (`TestStoreAgainstMinIO`, gated on env vars).
- Compose `minio` + `minio-init` brought up in a throwaway project: the bucket is created with versioning on, and re-running init is idempotent.
- `cd cloud && python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 85 tests pass.
- `npm run cloud:check` steps (`generate`, the schema diff, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`) all pass.

## Re-review follow-up (2026-10-22)

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| 1. Migration order with #6844 | Back to `00084` (re-runnable; it also applies cleanly where `00085` ran) with a 5 s `lock_timeout`. Asked #6844 to renumber above #6929's `00086`. This PR should merge before #6844. |
| 2. Rebase onto #6425 | `main` merged: `analytics` and `artifactstore` imports kept, `Analytics`/`Activity`/`SupportToken` and `Artifacts`/`ArtifactAccessSecret` options kept. |
| 3. Commit loop bypasses the cap | The pending cap now counts every queued version (open uploads and replaced versions not yet swept). Postgres test: an upload-and-commit loop on one path hits the limit after about 400 rounds. |
| 4. Deploy check skips the task role | `check_artifact_bucket` resolves the service's task role and runs `iam simulate-principal-policy` for the object and bucket actions; it stops the deploy and names what is denied. Five script tests with a stubbed `aws_cli`. |
| 5. AWS state | Still to do on the AWS side; the staging test plan has the commands (bucket policy, lifecycle, task-role policy). |
| 6. Lock timeout | `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` in the migration. |

Also for #6809's re-review: the session list and get carry `artifactsUpdatedAt` (newest commit time) so the desktop can key file lists on it, and a frame navigating with an expired link gets a short sandboxed page instead of JSON.

Checks: `go build`, `GOWORK=off go build`, `go vet` clean; `go test -race ./...` passes apart from the four `internal/postgres` tests and one `internal/workerexec` test that also fail on `main` (a Coder sandbox test failed once under load and passes 3/3 alone); 92 deploy-script tests pass.

## Pre-merge review follow-up

Addressed (Pritom14's review, plus axisrow's optional notes):

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Blocker: migration number | Every statement made re-runnable (now `00084` again, see the re-review below) (`IF NOT EXISTS`, `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS`); a test runs it twice. Applied cleanly on a local database that already had the old `00084`. |
| Merge with main | `main` merged in; `$17` stays the branch override and `requested_output` is `$18`; the test uses `launchCapabilities`. |
| Major 3: idempotency payload | `RequestedOutput` is `json:",omitempty"`, with a test. |
| Major 4: unbounded uploads, no cleanup | Upload accounting, per-session pending cap, open-upload check at commit, and the sweeper (above). Tested against Postgres and the fake S3, and live on MinIO: a replaced version was deleted, the current one kept. |
| Major 5: token outlives membership | User claim, membership and org-status check on every read, 10-minute links, CSP comment reworded, popups dropped from the served sandbox. Live: disabling the membership turned the same link into a 404 at once. |

| Minors 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 21, 23, 24, 25 | `outputType` from PR existence in every read; list sends a count; `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`; empty commits append nothing; epoch re-checked in the commit; requested output reaches the worker only while artifacts are on; stricter paths; fixed Content-Type list; HEAD uses `HeadObject`; 5-minute upload read deadline; `updatedAt` is the commit time; existence check for access; `go mod tidy`; racing-commit, empty-commit and payload tests; staging-first rule for production; compose fixes; reset path resolution; `.env.example` note. |

Not in this round (follow-ups):
- **Bucket, IAM and lifecycle in AWS** (checklist items 2–4): infrastructure for whoever owns the AWS account; the runbook and the deploy check cover what to create.

title: fix(mobile): pin the quick tunnel connector to HTTP/2
body:
Code changes: +9 -0\
Tests: +4 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Start the managed cloudflared quick tunnel with `--protocol http2`.

## Why

Fixes #6760.

A quick tunnel starts on QUIC and never falls back, so behind a VPN or proxy in TUN mode that drops UDP to the edge it redials forever and never registers. HTTP/2 runs over TCP and registers on both kinds of network. Measured on such a network: QUIC had not registered after fifty seconds (cloudflared's own precheck suggested http2), while HTTP/2 registered about a second after the hostname was issued.

## How

One extra argument in `CloudflaredArgs`, with a comment explaining why, and the existing argument test extended to pin it. Intentional omission: no runtime fallback from QUIC to HTTP/2, since cloudflared does not expose a reliable signal for "QUIC is blocked" before it gives up.

- `gofmt -l`, `go vet` clean. `golangci-lint` not available locally; verified in CI.

title: fix(mobile): withdraw the tunnel endpoint while its edge connection is down
body:
Code changes: +88 -12\
Tests: +150 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Track the quick tunnel's live edge connections by `connIndex` from cloudflared's own log lines, withdraw the tunnel endpoint while no edge connection is up, and log each edge connect and disconnect at INFO.

## Why

Fixes #6761.

cloudflared outlives an edge disconnect and re-registers on the same hostname, but `TunnelLog` only counted registrations, so a tunnel whose only edge connection had dropped still read as ready and kept being advertised to phones and the Connect Mobile panel. The raw connector output is debug-only, so a flapping tunnel (measured: 18 drops in three hours on one link) left no trace in a normal log.

## How

- `tunnel.go`: `TunnelLog` keeps a set of live connections keyed by `connIndex`, fed by "Registered tunnel connection", "Lost connection with the edge", "Connection terminated" and "Serve tunnel error" lines; readiness requires at least one live connection. Each transition is reported as an `EdgeChange` with the edge's location, protocol and, for a drop, cloudflared's reason.
- `tunnel_runner.go`: the runtime withdraws the endpoint on the last connection dropping and re-advertises on the next registration, and logs the transitions.

title: perf(renderer): refresh repeated session_updated events through a background lane
body:
Code changes: +81 -6\
Tests: +97 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Route `session_updated` CDC events that carry only a session id, or repeat the status the session already had, through a background refresh lane that flushes at most once per five seconds. A status change or a session seen for the first time still refreshes immediately through the existing 150 ms window.

## Why

Fixes #6763.

Every `session_updated` event invalidated the workspace query within the 150 ms coalescing window, whether or not anything the board shows had changed. During a long agent run with several sessions emitting usage/activity updates that meant a full `/api/v1/sessions` refetch every 150 ms for hours; on one machine that ended in the renderer OOM handled by the PR for #6762.

## How

- `event-transport.ts` remembers the last status each session's update carried. An update that repeats it, or carries no status, marks the workspace (and the open conversation / editor handoff for that session) as pending on the background lane instead of the immediate one.
- The background lane flushes on its own timer (`BACKGROUND_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000`), and an immediate flush also drains it, so nothing is ever refreshed later than it would have been before when a real change arrives.
- Intentional omission: no change to which queries are invalidated or to the 150 ms window itself. The `after=latest` cursor that `main` already uses is untouched.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/event-transport.test.ts src/renderer/hooks/useConversationConnecting.test.tsx`: 53 passed. New cases cover: an id-only `session_updated` does not refetch within the window but does within the background interval; a repeated status joins the background lane; a changed status refreshes immediately; a new session refreshes immediately; an immediate flush drains the background lane.
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors under `frontend/src`.
- The change has been running in the reporter's desktop build since 2026-10-14.

title: fix(desktop): rebuild the window when the shell renderer dies
body:
Code changes: +330 -15\
Tests: +237 -0\
Others: +82 -10 (i18n JSON, generated main-process catalog)

## What

When the shell renderer process dies, rebuild the window instead of leaving a blank one, and make every entry point that would show a dead window rebuild it instead.

- Rebuild after `render-process-gone` (any reason but `clean-exit`, not while quitting or closing), restoring bounds, maximized, full-screen and minimized state. An automatic rebuild does not take focus. A crash-loop guard allows three automatic rebuilds per ten minutes, then asks once in a native dialog.
- Tray "Show", notification clicks, a second launch and Dock activate rebuild a window whose renderer has died. Tray session targets wait for the replacement renderer.
- A dead renderer's chat drafts no longer block the close, and a rebuild is not treated as the close a background quit waits for.
- Log shell unresponsive/responsive, main-frame load failures, helper `child-process-gone`, and a per-process memory summary every five minutes. Start a local-only crash reporter with dumps under the Electron `userData` directory (which `main.ts` already pins under the AO data dir).

## Why

Fixes #6762. Related: #6134 (crash screen for renderer-side errors; this PR is about the renderer *process* dying).

When the shell renderer crashed (a PartitionAlloc OOM after a few hours, see #6763), Electron kept the window but nothing painted into its transparent shell view, so AO showed a blank white window until the user quit from the tray and relaunched. Tray "Show", notification clicks and a second launch all just re-showed the dead window.

## How

- `main/shell-recovery.ts` holds the pure decision logic (should this `render-process-gone` trigger a rebuild, crash-loop accounting, snapshot/restore of window state) so it is unit-testable without Electron. `main.ts` wires it to `BrowserWindow` events and to the existing tray/notification/second-instance paths.
- `main/process-diagnostics.ts` formats the periodic `app.getAppMetrics()` summary and resolves the crash dump directory.
- The dialog copy ships through the generated main-process catalog (`scripts/sync-tray-catalog.mjs`, which already carries the tray and zone strings), so `main.js` still does not import the renderer locale files (#6611). The four `desktopRecovery.*` keys are added to all eight locale JSONs and the catalog is regenerated.
- The rebuild creates the window hidden and shows it inactive, so it composes with `showWhenRendererLoaded`: the window is already visible when the renderer finishes loading, and no focus is stolen.
- Intentional omission: no renderer-side changes. The refetch rate that led to the OOM is addressed separately in the PR for #6763.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/shell-recovery.test.ts src/main/process-diagnostics.test.ts src/main/tray-lifecycle.test.ts src/main/tray-catalog.test.ts src/main/tray.test.ts`: 57 passed (`tray-catalog.test.ts` pins the regenerated catalog against the JSON).

title: bug(desktop): no "Link ao command" row in Settings on Linux .deb with Developer Mode on; ao version prints "dev"
body:
**What happens**
On Linux (.deb install), Developer Mode is on, but the "link the global `ao` command" row never appears in Settings → General. The macOS app has that button, and the source (`frontend/src/shared/cli-link.ts`) says .deb/.rpm installs are supported, so I expected it here.

`ao` isn't on the normal `PATH` after installing the package. The only command it adds is `/usr/bin/agent-orchestrator`, which starts the app. The CLI is at `/usr/lib/agent-orchestrator/resources/daemon/ao` and is on `PATH` only inside AO sessions. I worked around it with `ln -s /usr/lib/agent-orchestrator/resources/daemon/ao ~/.local/bin/ao`.

**Also noticed**
`ao version` prints just `dev`. I don't know if that's related, since the link feature checks the bundled CLI's version, but it looks off for a packaged release.

**Environment**
- Package `agent-orchestrator` 0.13.7 (amd64), installed from the .deb, not an AppImage (`AO_APPIMAGE` unset)
- Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS, Wayland
- Developer Mode: on

**Expected**
Either the CLI link row shows up in Settings → General, or the package puts `ao` on `PATH` (e.g. a `/usr/bin/ao` symlink).

**Not verified**
I haven't confirmed which setting controls whether the row is shown, so Developer Mode may not be the right toggle on Linux.

title: fix(chat): handle Qwen ask_user_question as interactive input in ACP
body:
Code changes: +343 -8  
Tests: +305 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Route Qwen Code’s `ask_user_question` tool invocations from ACP `session/request_permission` into AO’s interactive input flow (`ElicitationDock` / mobile) and inject the user's answers back into the JSON-RPC wire response.

In YOLO mode (`--approval-mode yolo`), questions bypass permission auto-approval so the agent never receives an empty response or gets stuck.

Fixes #6690.

- Detect `ask_user_question` tool calls via `_meta.qwenInteractionKind`, `_meta.toolName`, `tool.Kind`, or title heuristics.

- Track incoming `session/request_permission` RPC IDs and intercept outgoing JSON-RPC responses on the transport writer to inject `"answers": { "0": "...", ... }` into the `result` object.
- Map user cancel/decline actions to a `cancelled` permission outcome.

No API, schema, or frontend changes are required.

title: feat(cloud): sync the worker's artifact directory to the control plane (2/3)
body:
Code changes: +919 -117  
Tests: +858 -76  
Others: +9 -0 (contract and generated cloud-client schema)

Stack: #6769 control plane → **#6779 worker (this PR)** → #6809 desktop and docs. Base is `ao/agent-orchestrator-251/cloud-artifacts-control-plane`; review #6769 first, this diff is only the worker slice.

## Summary

PR 2 of 3 for cloud session artifacts: the **worker**. It still ships dark, because the control plane only sets `launch.artifacts` while `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS` is on and the worker advertises `session.artifacts`. With the flag off, the worker creates no directory, runs no scanner and adds no prompt section.

When `launch.artifacts` is set:
- **Directory and prompt.** The worker creates `<AO_DATA_DIR>/artifacts/<sessionId>`, outside the git checkout, passes its path to the agent as `AO_SESSION_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, and adds it to the directories the harness may write (Claude `--add-dir` and settings, Codex writable roots, Chat sandboxes). It adds a "Session Artifacts" section to the worker prompt, modelled on the local `artifactPrompt`. Workers created with `requestedOutput: "artifact"` also get the "Artifact Output" section, modelled on `artifactOutputPrompt`. Reviewers get neither.
- **Scanner** (`cmd/ao-worker/artifacts.go`):
  - Walks the directory through `os.Root`.
  - Skips symlinks, `.versions`, `.git` and `node_modules`, non-regular files, paths that cannot be stored or do not fit a bucket key, unreadable files and directories, and files beyond the 25 MiB / 200-file / 500 MiB caps (checked in path order). Each skipped file is logged once. A file that keeps changing stops scheduling settle rescans after 15 scans.
  - Hashes a file only after two scans saw the same size and mtime, and caches the hash.
- **Sync.** The worker sends a manifest of settled files that differ from what it last confirmed, uploads only the paths the control plane reports as changed (streamed, with `Content-Length` and the sha header), then commits.
  - A failed request backs off from 10 s, doubling to 5 min; a failed commit is then retried **reusing the uploaded version**. A request failure never schedules the 2 s settle rescan.
  - A request refused with a client error (for example a 413 at commit) waits until the files change.
  - A `409` drops the cached versions so the files are re-uploaded; a `422` on upload re-hashes the file.
  - A `404` from the control plane (no artifacts there) pauses syncing for 10 minutes; a replaced worker stops syncing.
  - Empty files upload with `http.NoBody`, so they carry `Content-Length: 0`.
  - The syncer never blocks the agent; failures are logged.
- **Triggers:**
  - the agent's Stop hook, through the existing checkpoint bridge;
  - a 30 s rescan, matching the checkpoint safety net (a rescan with no change makes no request);
  - a **2 s settle rescan** whenever a file was still changing;
  - a final flush, bounded to 20 s, when the worker shuts down.
- **Decision (brief item 3):** a Stop-hook sync follows the same settle rule as every other trigger: it waits for a second scan. The 2 s settle rescan keeps a file written at the end of a turn visible within seconds.
- **Deletes** are sent only for files this worker process has synced and that are gone from the directory: a file over a limit, unreadable, or under an unreadable directory is never reported as deleted. An empty directory after a restore onto a fresh disk therefore never clears the stored list.
- **Capability.** The worker advertises `session.artifacts`, and the control plane sets `launch.artifacts` only for workers that do. If the directory cannot be created, the worker turns artifacts off for the agent.

Control-plane follow-ups found while building the worker:
- **Deleted files.** The control plane's sweeper (#6769) deletes the versions a commit replaces or deletes, so commits put no delete markers.
- **Path validation moved to `domain`** (`CleanArtifactPath`), so the worker binary doesn't link the AWS SDK.
- The worker artifact wire types moved to `internal/worker` and are shared by both sides.

## Not included: hard-delete cleanup

The brief's hard-delete slice cleans up S3 on **hard delete** of a session. Cloud has no hard delete today: `DELETE /sessions/{id}` archives the session, and nothing removes `ao_sessions` rows. I left that slice out rather than add an unused job. If a hard delete (or org purge) is planned, the cleanup would hook in there.

## Tests run

Re-run after the review (2026-10-19): `go vet` clean; `go test -race ./cmd/ao-worker/ ./internal/...` passes apart from the known `main` failures; new syncer tests for backoff, refusal until change, a replaced worker, empty files, checksum re-hash, cap-driven and unreadable-directory deletes, skipped tool directories, the path-length limit and endless changes; `agentDirectories` and the reconnect capability gate are tested. Live on `npm run cloud:local`: the agent environment and `--add-dir`, an empty file and `.git` skipped (see the table above).

Original run:

- `cd cloud && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./...`: clean.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes except the two `internal/workerexec` Claude model tests, which also fail on `origin/main` in this environment.
- New worker tests (`cmd/ao-worker/artifacts_test.go`, run against an in-memory control plane):
  - settling, including a file that changes between scans;
  - symlink, `.versions` and oversize skips;
  - unchanged files send no request, and a restart sends no upload;
  - deletes, and a restart on a fresh disk deleting nothing;
  - a failed commit retried without re-upload;
  - stopping on `404`;
  - the final flush on shutdown;
  - path escaping.
- Prompt tests: the sections appear only when they apply.
- Control-plane tests: the delete marker is placed and the version is kept, and `/worker/reconnect` reports `launch.artifacts` according to the flag.
- **Live run.** The real syncer ran against the real control plane and compose MinIO on an isolated stack:
  - paths with spaces and `#` round-trip;
  - a changed file got a second version;
  - a deleted file got a `DEL` marker with its old version kept;
  - the files are served through the access prefix.

## Re-review follow-up (2026-10-22)

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Major 1: over the cap stops all syncing | Files this worker synced keep their slots first (including ones it can no longer send); new files fill what is left in path order. Test: 200 synced files plus `a.md`, which sorts first: `a.md` waits, an edit to a synced file still syncs. |
| Medium 2: refusal bypassed | The refusal fingerprint covers settled files only. Tests: a growing log and an unreadable file no longer resend a refused request. |
| Medium 3: final flush skipped in a backoff | The shutdown flush ignores `retryAt` (a refusal and a stopped syncer still apply). Test included. |
| Minor 1: Chat turns | `Supervisor.TurnEnded` pokes the syncer after each Chat turn. |
| Minor 2: CLAUDE.md as instructions | The `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD` decision uses the repository checkouts only. With several repositories it is still on, and then also covers the artifact directory, because Claude applies it to every added directory. |
| Minor 5: results capacity | 7. |
| Tests missing | Added the above, the directory in Claude and Codex commands from `BuildInteractive` and `Build` (including parent start), and a Postgres test that the branch and requested output bind to their own columns. |

Not changed: minor 3 (a working folder that contains the durable root, which already exposes all of `.ao`), minor 4 (Cursor in its default mode; not checked live), minor 7 (an old worker drops an artifact request silently) and minor 8 (seeding from the control plane at startup). A restore onto a fresh disk at the cap still waits until the files change; seeding (minor 8) would fix it.

## Pre-merge review follow-up

Addressed (Pritom14's review):

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Major 1: persistent failure retries every 2 s | Exponential backoff (10 s to 5 min); client errors wait until the files change; failures never re-arm the settle rescan. |
| Major 2: empty files never upload | `http.NoBody` for zero-byte files, with a test. Live: an empty `empty.md` synced. |
| Major 3: agent cannot write the directory | The directory joins the harness's extra directories (Claude `--add-dir`, Codex writable roots, Chat). Live: the Claude command line has `--add-dir=/workspace/.ao/worker/artifacts/<session>`. |
| Major 4: capped files deleted | Present-but-unsyncable files and files under unreadable directories are never deleted, with tests. |
| Major 5: 30 s read timeout | The control plane's upload route gets a 5-minute read deadline (#6769). |
| Merge with main | Both capabilities, both env blocks, both prompt sections kept; `$18` from #6769. |
| Minors 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 | 404 pauses 10 minutes; failed mkdir turns artifacts off; over-long paths skipped; endless changes stop rescanning; 422 re-hashes; uncommitted uploads are swept (#6769); `launch.artifacts` gated on the capability; `.git` and `node_modules` skipped; `STALE_WORKER_TOKEN` stops the syncer; variable renamed to `AO_SESSION_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, which no repo script uses. |

Not in this round (follow-ups):
- Minor 8: seed `synced` from the control plane's list at startup, so a restart on the same disk notices files deleted while the worker was down, and a restore onto a fresh disk could put the committed files back.
- Minor 10 (reviewer env): reviewer launches use their own `HarnessBuilder` without the worker's env, so they do not inherit the variable; nothing to change.

## Known risks and follow-ups

- Resolved by #6769's sweeper: an upload that is never committed (for example, the sandbox dies between upload and commit) is deleted by version after 24 hours, which makes the committed version current again before the 30-day noncurrent rule could expire it.
- The worker's 25 s checkpoint safety-net timer also pokes the syncer, so with a 30 s rescan as well there can be two scans per 30 s. Neither makes a request unless something changed.
- Desktop UI, docs and the local end-to-end steps are in #6809.

title: fix(artifacts): read local content through loopback API
body:
Code changes: +21 -10  
Tests: +227 -8  
Others: +0 -0  

A local artifact URL can resolve to IPv6 `::1`, where another application owns the same port as AO's IPv4 daemon. The viewer reaches that application's 404 and shows “Failed to fetch.”

Read local artifact text through the currently trusted daemon API with `source=artifact&raw=true`. Preserve artifact-directory confinement and remote/cloud content URLs. Reject absolute/dot-segment paths before URL normalization and fail closed while the daemon address is unavailable.

title: fix(chat): stop snap-to-bottom jitter when scrolling near the end
body:
Code changes: +7 -1\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Scrolling down the chat toward the bottom no longer jitters and snaps to the end.

## Why

Inside the 64px band at the bottom, `onScroll` re-pins the chat to the live end. That re-pin runs `syncScrollLayout`, which does a follow pass and writes `scrollTop` to the very bottom while the reader is still scrolling. Even a few pixels away, the view jumped.

## How

The re-pin sets `skipRelatchFollow`, and the next layout pass skips that one follow. The reader is already at the end, so there is nothing to catch up to. New content still follows once pinned. Requested glides (send, jump to latest) are unaffected. The change is in `ChatWorkspace.tsx`.

## Testing

Chat workspace tests pass, including the existing re-latch test. One test, "shows live provider context usage", fails on number grouping (`2,58,400`), a locale issue on my machine that this change doesn't touch.

title: fix(mobile): keep the worker board on screen across a quick background
body: ## Summary Opening the Workers board, backgrounding the app, and coming back within a second showed the full-screen loader again instead of the workers that were already loaded. **Cause:** on background, `store.tsx` drops the connection on purpose, because a LAN address can point at a different machine after the phone wakes. The cached rows were kept, but `sessionRowsForMachine` only shows rows for the connected machine. With `config` null that machine was `""`, so the board was empty. Loading was on while the endpoint race ran, and empty plus loading shows the loader. Once the race finished, `reloadConfig` compared the selected host against the cleared `cfgRef` and wiped the rows as if the user had switched machines. **Fix:** - On background, remember the machine and host id the board was showing (`heldMachine` / `heldHostIdRef`). While `config` is null, that machine stands in, so the cached rows stay visible during the reconnect. - `reloadConfig` checks for a host change against the held host id, so resuming on the same machine no longer clears the board. - The held machine is released when the user switches hosts, when the host is version-incompatible, and once a config resolves. - The bearer connection is still never reused after waking. Only what's displayed changed. If the machine is unreachable on resume, the board shows the cached rows with the stale banner (same as a dead poll on a populated board) instead of a spinner. ## Before / after Recorded on the iOS simulator, paired to a local daemon over loopback: open the Workers board, press Home, and reopen the app about a second later. Loopback is the fastest possible reconnect, so the loader shows here for only ~250 ms. Over LAN or the tunnel on a real phone it stays up longer. | Same moment after returning | | --- | | | **Real speed** **Slowed 4x around the return** The "Open debugger to view warnings" toast comes from the dev build and isn't related to this change. ## Tests - `npx tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `store.tsx`. - `npx vitest run`: 1907/1908 pass. The one failure (`uitextview-selection-color.test.ts`) needs the `patch-package` patches applied and isn't related to this change. - `store.tsx` can't be imported by vitest (React Native), so there's no new unit test. ## Risks - After a wake, the rows shown are from the previous connection until the first poll lands. They are still keyed to the same host id, so another machine's rows are never shown. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(command-code vendor): cmd acp accepts --mod but silently ignores it
body:
## Problem

Command Code's Chat mode accepts `--mod` and then ignores it. There is no error, no warning, and the ACP agent starts and runs normally — so a caller that relies on a mod gets a silently inert mod.

This is a vendor bug in `CommandCodeAI/command-code`, not in AO. Filed here because AO is blocked on it and because the failure is invisible.

## Evidence

Tested on **v1.79.2** and again on **v1.82.3**.

A mod whose factory writes a log line at load time, at `appendSystemPrompt` invocation, and at `onRunEnd`:

| Mode | Declaration | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| print (`cmd -p`) | `--mod ./mod.ts` | ✅ `factory:ran`, `hooks:registered`, `appendSystemPrompt:invoked`, `onRunEnd:fired` |
| ACP (`cmd acp`) | `--mod ./mod.ts` | ❌ **no log at all — mod never loaded** |
| ACP | `settings.mods.paths` (absolute) | ❌ never loaded |
| ACP | `settings.mods.paths` (relative) | ❌ never loaded |
| ACP | `<project>/.commandcode/mods/` | ❌ never loaded |

The print-mode result rules out an invalid mod file: the same file loads and its hooks execute there. The ACP session itself starts cleanly and answers prompts, so the failure is isolated to mod loading.

## Why this matters beyond AO

The same gap appears to disable **shell hooks** on the ACP path. `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` and `Stop` are documented to fire, and they do in practice — but `SessionStart` is the one hook never fired under ACP across every test. A consumer relying on `SessionStart` under `cmd acp` gets nothing, again silently.

## Reproduction

```bash
# sentinel.ts
import { appendFileSync } from "node:fs";
appendFileSync("/tmp/mod-events.log", "factory:ran\n");
export default function (cmd) {
  cmd.hooks({
    appendSystemPrompt: () => { appendFileSync("/tmp/mod-events.log", "appendSystemPrompt\n"); return "X"; },
  });
}
```

```bash
cmd -p "hi" --mod ./sentinel.ts   # /tmp/mod-events.log  -> "factory:ran", "appendSystemPrompt"
cmd acp --mod ./sentinel.ts       # /tmp/mod-events.log  -> does not exist
```

Driving the ACP session over stdio requires only `initialize`, `session/new`, then `session/prompt`.

## Requested behaviour

Either:

- load `--mod` / configured mods on the ACP path, matching print mode, **or**
- reject the flag on `cmd acp` with a clear error instead of accepting and ignoring it.

The second is far less useful but would at least make the limitation visible to integrators. The mod API is documented as experimental, so treating this as a known gap is also reasonable — but it should be stated in the ACP documentation rather than discovered by trial.

## Upstream

https://github.com/CommandCodeAI/command-code

Docs: <https://commandcode.ai/docs/mods>

Not filed upstream yet — say the word and I'll open it there with this reproduction.

title: test(command-code): Chat-mode activity tracking and native session-id capture never verified end-to-end
body:
## Problem

AO's Command Code **Chat** activity tracking has never been verified end-to-end. We know the underlying hooks fire under `cmd acp`, but we have not observed AO's `activity` field actually updating during a real Chat session.

This is a verification gap, not a reported bug — nothing is known to be broken.

## What is established

**Hooks fire under ACP.** Tested with a live `cmd acp` session against a workspace `.commandcode/settings.json` carrying all four hooks, logging each invocation:

| Hook | ACP |
| --- | --- |
| `SessionStart` | ❌ does not fire (TUI-only) |
| `PreToolUse` | ✅ fires |
| `PostToolUse` | ✅ fires |
| `Stop` | ✅ fires |

**Terminal mode works.** A live spawned Command Code worker reported:

```
status: working
activity: active
```

So Terminal activity is confirmed.

## What is not established

- Whether a Chat session's `activity` transitions to `active` during a turn and back to `idle` afterwards.
- Whether AO captures Command Code's native `session_id` in Chat. In Terminal this comes from the `SessionStart` hook, which never fires under ACP, so the Chat native-id capture path may be silently empty.
- Whether restore works for a Chat session as a consequence.

That last two matter beyond cosmetics: if native-id capture is empty in Chat, `session/load` restore has no identity to resume against.

## Why it was worth separating

An earlier pass in #6778 claimed all hooks were dead under ACP and that Chat activity tracking was broken. **That claim was wrong** — it came from a probe whose ACP session had timed out, so the hooks were never given a chance to run. The correction is recorded in #6657. This issue exists so the remaining *unverified* surface is tracked rather than assumed either way.

## Suggested verification

1. Register a project with `command-code` as both orchestrator and worker agent.
2. Spawn a **Chat** session (not Terminal) and send a prompt that forces a tool call.
3. Watch `ao session get <id>` during the turn — expect `activity: active`, then `idle` after.
4. Inspect session metadata for `agentSessionId` and confirm it is non-empty.
5. Confirm the Activity column moves in the desktop app for that session.

## Notes

- Terminal-mode activity is unaffected by any of this and is covered by existing tests.
- No code change is proposed here; this is a verification task. If step 4 shows an empty native id, the fix is a separate change — the ACP path has no hook to capture it from, so it would need `session/new`'s response id.

title: fix(cloud): let capabilities=coder orgs buy Freestyle again

## What

Restores the rule agreed for #6651:

| WorkOS `capabilities` | Default sandbox | Coder | Freestyle | Upgrade page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `coder` | Coder | Free, plus its own Coder deployment | On a plan | Shown |
| not set (everyone else) | Freestyle | On a plan | On a plan | Shown |

## Why

Before #6651 merged, a coder-only exception was added (`coderOnlyCustomer`, commit `c417106e2b`). It hid Freestyle from organizations tagged `capabilities=coder` without `freestyle`, so those organizations:
- lost the Upgrade page;
- couldn't buy Freestyle at all.

Almost every WorkOS organization is tagged `coder`, including the team's, so in practice nobody on Coder could buy Freestyle.

## How

  - both providers, with Coder as the default and plans shown;

  - a Freestyle session can be created;

title: fix(cloud): start a cloud Claude terminal on the upgraded Claude Code
body:
## Problem

Found live on prod after #6587 shipped. On a fresh Coder workspace the first cloud terminal (TUI) session runs the Claude Code the image ships (2.1.228), and current models refuse it:

> API Error: 400 Claude Code 2.1.228 does not support this model; version 2.1.280 or newer is required.

#6587 upgrades Claude Code into `~/.ao/tools` at worker boot. Chat turns wait for that upgrade (`claudeCodeTurnWait`, 90s), but the terminal launch picks the binary with `defaultClaudeCode.current()`, which never waits, so it starts the old install while the upgrade is still running.

## Fix

`workerexec.AwaitClaudeCodeUpgrade(ctx)` waits for an upgrade in progress with the same 90s bound Chat turns use. The worker calls it before building the interactive Claude command and the reviewer command. It returns at once when nothing is pending (the workspace's own Claude Code is current, or the upgrade already finished) or when an earlier upgrade failed (retries run in the background, see #6587's backoff).

Cost: the first terminal start on a fresh workspace can wait for the npm install, up to 90s, instead of starting a CLI that fails its first turn.

## Tests

`TestClaudeCodeAwaitRunsTheTerminalOnTheUpgrade`: a pending upgrade is waited for and the launch uses the upgraded binary; a stuck upgrade is bounded by the wait and falls back to the existing install. `workerexec`, `cmd/ao-worker`, `worker` pass; `-race -count=3` on the Claude Code tests.

title: fix(harness): stop false "update did not reach" failures for Kimi, Crush and silent self-updaters
body:
Code changes: +205 -42\
Tests: +201 -8\
Others: +0 -8 (locale strings)

## What

Fixes three ways a harness update shows a red failure when nothing is actually broken, or without saying why:

1. **Kimi**: `the update finished, but the installed version 2.0.2 did not reach the requested version 2.2.0`. Two users reported this, one at 2.0.2 and one at 0.41.0.
2. **Any vendor self-updater that exits 0 without updating** (Droid seen in the field: `0.159.1 → 0.242.0`): the error never said what the updater printed.
3. **Crush** (and other harnesses that release often): `v0.98.1 is now the latest release. Select Update again to install it.`

This PR covers all three on purpose, at the reporter's request. They share one cause: the update flow treats an exit code or a cached advisory as proof of the outcome.

## Why

**Kimi.** AO ran `kimi upgrade -y`. Reading Kimi Code's bundled updater (2.0.2 and 2.2.0, `handleUpgrade`), that command exits **0 without replacing the binary** in three cases:
- Its own rollout channel says nothing is newer: `Kimi Code is already up to date (…)`. AO reads `code.kimi.com/kimi-code/latest`, which can be ahead of that channel.
- The install source is Homebrew or unsupported: it prints `To update manually, run: …`.
- On native installs it runs `__update_download`, which only **stages** the new binary. The swap happens on a later launch, and that launch skips the swap if another instance holds the swap lock or the smoke check fails.

AO's `--version` check then still sees the old version, and every retry fails the same way.

**Error text.** The updater's output was already kept in the job's output, but the card only showed the generic message, so users and maintainers couldn't tell which case happened.

**Crush.** A card's latest version comes from the cached advisory, which the periodic pass refreshes every 6 h by default. The click-time `refresh=true` check often finds a newer release for fast-moving harnesses, and `useStartHarnessUpdate` then refused and asked the user to click again.

## How

- **Kimi re-runs its official installer on every OS** (`installerUpdateTargets`): `install.sh`, or `install.ps1` on Windows. `bindKimiInstallerUpdate` binds the run to the copy sessions use:
  - It applies only to Kimi Code's default native install, `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` (`kimi.exe` on Windows). The match is exact on macOS and Linux, and case-insensitive with either separator on Windows. A `kimi` anywhere else (`~/.local`, `~/.cargo`, `/usr/local`, a legacy Python `kimi-cli` entry point, a uv-copied `kimi.exe`) may belong to another tool, so it is refused with "update it manually" rather than replaced.
  - `KIMI_INSTALL_DIR=<root>` and `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`, so shell rc files are not edited.
  - `PATH` without `<root>/bin`. Both installers skip their legacy-shim migration (which renames the first legacy `kimi` on PATH to `kimi-legacy` and deletes the rest) only when `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH` is set **and** their own bin directory is off PATH. With this, an AO update replaces only `<root>/bin/kimi`, plus the installer's `kimi.bak`.
  - `KIMI_VERSION=<approved release>` through `pinVendorUpdate`, so the installer and AO's verification agree on the target.
  - The update advisory applies the same check (`vendorMaintainable`), so a `kimi` outside `~/.kimi-code` gets manual-update guidance instead of an **Update** button that is always refused.
  - A staged binary left by an earlier `kimi upgrade` can't downgrade this install. On startup, Kimi's `maybeRelaunchWithStagedNativeUpdate` discards a staged update that is not newer than the running version (`if (!semver.gt(staged.version, currentVersion)) discard`), in both 2.0.2 and 2.2.0.

  `vendorMaintainable` counts installer-updated targets, so Kimi stays updatable from AO. Grok's Windows destination override now shares the new `withInstallerEnv` helper (behaviour unchanged, still covered by the existing Grok tests).
- **Failed updates quote the updater's last line** (`lastOutputLine`). It is shown as a terminal would show it: ANSI CSI/OSC sequences removed, only the text after a line's last `\r`, and capped at 200 runes. This applies only to command-based updates, not installer scripts. Example: `…did not reach the requested version 0.242.0; the update command reported: "Droid is already up to date."`
- **Click-time newer release.** `useStartHarnessUpdate` no longer takes `latestVersion`. When the fresh advisory is still `behind_latest` through the same maintenance method, it installs `fresh.latestVersion`, which it already sent as `expectedVersion`. The daemon still refuses a target at or below the installed version (`ErrUpdateVersion`). A changed method is still refused (`updateMethodChanged`). The hook returns the advisory it acted on, so a failed update in `HarnessUpdateNotice` keeps showing the release it actually tried. The unused `settings.harness.updateTargetChanged` string is removed from all locales.

### Similar problems in other harnesses (audit, follow-ups not in this PR)

I read each vendor self-update command in `vendorUpdateCommands` from its shipped bundle or source, without running them. Almost all can exit 0 while the next `--version` still shows the old release:

| Harness | Exit-0 no-op cases | Suggested follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| Droid | `Auto-update is not available for npm installations.`, `✓ Already up to date!`, `Update to X was skipped.` (directory not writable). Its latest comes from `downloads.factory.ai/factory-cli/LATEST`, not npm `droid`. | Re-run `app.factory.ai/cli`, as for Kimi |
| Autohand | Runs `curl … \| sh` without pipefail, so it prints `Successfully updated` even when curl failed. Its installer defaults to `~/.local/bin`. | Re-run `install.sh` with install dir and version, as Windows already does |
| OpenCode | `Upgrade failed` still exits 0. The installer only writes `~/.opencode/bin`. | Refuse other locations, and treat `Upgrade failed` as a failure |
| Claude Code | `stable`-channel users get "up to date" (2.1.292) while AO compares to `latest` (2.1.301). Also exits 0 when another Claude process is running or updates are disabled. | Respect `autoUpdatesChannel` when choosing the latest version |
| OMP, Cursor, FX, Pi, Grok, Prime Agent | Each "already up to date" against its own channel or feed, which differs from AO's source | Align AO's latest-version source per harness |
| Goose | GitHub's `stable` tag can lag a new release by minutes | Retry later |
| Qwen, Kimchi | "update with brew/npm" messages | Covered by the quoted-updater message |
| Codex, Amp | Effectively safe | — |

The quoted-updater message in this PR already turns every one of these from a generic failure into a self-explaining one.

## Testing

Per the reporter's request, validation runs in this PR's CI. Locally, only `go test ./internal/service/systeminstall/` was run (passing). The full repo suites, the frontend typecheck and the vitest run were not run locally.

New or updated tests:
- `TestKimiUpdateReinstallsAdvisoryReleaseIntoConfirmedDirectory`: an end-to-end update runs the installer, never `kimi upgrade`, with `KIMI_INSTALL_DIR`, `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`, `KIMI_VERSION` and a PATH without `<root>/bin`, and verifies success.
- `TestKimiUpdateBindsOnlyKimiCodeDefaultInstall`: `~/.kimi-code` is accepted on macOS, Linux and Windows. Other tools' `~/.local`, `~/.cargo` and `/usr/local` copies are refused, as are a case-mismatched `BIN` or `kimi.exe` outside Windows, and an empty path or home. Homebrew plans are untouched, and the original plan is not mutated.
- `TestKimiUpdateAdvisoryOffersUpdateOnlyForDefaultInstall`: the advisory's maintenance method is `official-installer` for `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` and empty for `~/.local` and `~/.cargo` copies.
- `TestKimiUpdateKeepsItsBinDirectoryOffInstallerPath`: `<root>/bin` is removed from PATH (Unix exact, Windows case-insensitive) and other entries are kept.
- `TestLastOutputLineShowsWhatTheTerminalWouldShow`: covers empty output, blank lines, ANSI colour, OSC title, `\r` progress (including a trailing bare `\r`) and 200-rune truncation.
- `HarnessUpdateNotice.test.tsx`: a failed update keeps the card on the newer release the click-time check chose.
- `TestFailedUpdateQuotesWhatTheUpdaterReported`: the exact failure text includes the updater's last line.

title: feat(files): branch reviews with full file browsing and direct actions
body:
Code changes: +4858 -1021  
Tests: +3853 -493  
Others: +1359 -72

## What

The Files panel supports reviewing work by scope, selected commits, and source branch, with complete repository browsing and direct file controls.

- **Changes:** Uncommitted, Staged, Unstaged, and a directly accessible commits list. Ticking several commits reviews those commits together. Untracked files are included in Uncommitted and Unstaged.
- **Branch:** local branches, known remote-tracking branches, and associated PRs whose source branch is not local. Reading a source never checks it out or changes the worktree or real index. Branch menus render an initial page of 50 rows and retain search and pagination.
- **Direct controls:** unified/split layout and collapse/expand-all sit in the toolbar. Per-file collapse remains in the file header and preserves feedback drafts.
- **Consistent file actions:** Open full file and Open diff in center remain inline in narrow panes and work for branch, PR, and combined-commit reviews. From the maximized viewer, center navigation closes the overlay in the same action. Full source and rendered preview remain separate modes.
- **Complete source trees:** Changes and All files work across review sources. All files lazily lists the selected snapshot, includes unchanged files, and supports path filtering. Snapshot navigation does not read same-named live workspace files.
- **Separate tabs per source:** a workspace file and historical copies of the same path coexist. Local file panes remain mounted when switching tabs so workspace drafts survive, and inactive/covered editors cannot intercept Save shortcuts. Snapshot labels, scroll state, display mode, feedback, assets, and expanded diff context retain their source.
- **Read-only historical views:** snapshots show an explained editing restriction. Deleted files open their previous contents. Relative Markdown images and raster previews use snapshot-aware blob reads.

## How

- The daemon retains the existing uncommitted scope, `GET /workspace/branches`, read-only view history, and `POST /workspace/history/selection`.
- Adjacent commit selections resolve to a revision range. Gapped selections replay through a scratch `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, leaving HEAD, refs, the real index, and worktree untouched. Conflicts offer Include commits in between or Show all commits.
- Snapshot file, tree, blob, and revision reads reuse validated branch/associated-PR selection logic and resolved revision pairs, including synthetic combined trees. Paths, refs, commit membership, output sizes, and read deadlines stay bounded.
- Pinned snapshots survive ordinary source advances while their anchor remains reachable. A force-push or unavailable source produces an explicit error rather than substituting newer or live content.
- Local and remote-tracking refs have distinct identities. PR folding continues to require repository identity, and a capped branch list cannot establish that a selected branch was deleted.
- Explicit historical response markers prevent older remote daemons from silently answering a snapshot request with live workspace data. Such hosts receive an update-required explanation.
- OpenAPI and frontend schema types are regenerated from the Go contract. No storage migration is needed.

## Intentional limits

- Historical views contain tracked repository paths; Workspace retains its tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored behavior. Snapshot editing and automatic checkout are outside this change.
- Cloud-session branch APIs are unchanged.
- Media and large-file previews retain explicit capability/size limits. Raster snapshot blobs are bounded; unsupported content shows an unavailable state.
- Gapped commit replay uses `git apply --cached` and can report a conflict that a three-way merge might resolve.
- No Last agent turn or Commit & Push flow is added.

## Validation

Passed locally on macOS with Go 1.27.1 and Node 24:

- 498 viewer/selection/tab regressions across 14 test files, followed by passing affected suites for the added keyboard-focus regression and deleted-file old-side context. These cover historical context expansion, same-path source isolation, and maximized preview navigation.
- Both narrow-inspector browser tests, including primary-action bounds at the minimum width.
- Complete session-service and HTTP/controller/API suites with race detection, plus the final added snapshot cases (unchanged files, PR and remote sources, combined commits, deleted files, source movement, and dirty-workspace preservation).
- Backend build, vet, and pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 (zero issues).
- Full frontend TypeScript check, E2E TypeScript check, and changed-file semantic diagnostics (zero errors).
- API regeneration and clean diff/format checks.

The full frontend run completed with 8,481 tests passed, 7 skipped, and 3 failures from outdated selection-hook assertions. Those assertions are corrected and all 19 tests in that file now pass; the entire frontend suite was not repeated afterward. The broad backend run encountered installed-harness/provider assumptions and an inherited tmux setting pointing to a missing bundle. Complete session/HTTP race suites and the focused checks above pass. Full-suite and final CI success are not claimed; remaining CI results can be reviewed on this PR.

The implementation is ready for manual testing. No native Electron manual verification or menu-latency percentile is claimed.



## Review follow-up

- **P1:** PR rows fold into local branches only after matching the workspace origin's repository identity (provider host and namespace), even when branch names and tip SHAs are identical. Fork, child-repository, and unknown-origin cases retain distinct PR rows. Existing same-repository folding and remote-tip matching remain covered.
- **P2:** The existing `truncated` guard keeps a selected branch when the capped list omits it. The strengthened regression confirms no branch-change callback occurs until the history endpoint explicitly reports deletion.
- Follow-up validation: complete session-service suite with race detection, final branch-list regression group, all 19 selection-hook tests, and pinned backend lint pass. The earlier full-suite limitations above still apply.



## Manual-testing feedback fixes

- Whole-file feedback opens from collapsed headers and remains open, with its draft intact, when a file or all files are collapsed or expanded.
- Explicit commit selections stay selected even when they include every listed commit. Selecting a branch's only commit now visibly checks its row instead of immediately returning to All commits.
- Collapse-all and expand-all show distinct inward/outward chevron icons according to the current file state, including changes made through individual headers.
- The circular-arrow control refreshes the selected snapshot source; it never checks out a branch or writes workspace files.
- Validation for this follow-up: all 136 focused tests across five files, all three narrow-layout/feedback browser tests, changed-file TypeScript diagnostics, E2E TypeScript check, and diff checks pass. The full application suite was not rerun for this follow-up.

title: fix(cursor): mark inline resource exhaustion as a failed turn
body:
Code changes: +27 -0  
Tests: +60 -1  
Others: +0 -0  

## Problem

Cursor Agent can stream `Error: RetriableError: [resource_exhausted] Error` as ordinary assistant text and then return a successful ACP `end_turn`. AO consequently marks the request completed even though the provider failed. This was observed with Cursor Agent 2026.10.14-0f9edde. The same error-channel behavior has also been reported on [Cursor's forum](https://forum.cursor.com/t/acp-error-responses-not-being-passed-through-correct-error-channels/163218).

## Change

Add a provider-owned assistant-message failure callback alongside the existing prompt-response callback. Cursor opts in and recognizes the observed resource-exhaustion prefix on the final nonempty message line. A nominally completed turn then emits the existing failed-turn result with the provider's error text. Other providers and cancelled turns retain their existing behavior.

This is a narrow status-reporting fix. The match is deliberately limited to the observed Cursor error form; it does not resolve the provider's underlying capacity or quota condition. Tests cover ordinary text, prefixed quotations, fenced examples, and a subsequent recovery line.

## Validation

Passed on Windows amd64 with Go 1.27.1:

```sh
go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/nativeacp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/cursoracp -run '^(TestPromptMessageFailureMarksTurnFailed|TestACPDriverPromptResponseFailure|TestPromptResponseFailureIgnoresNonErrors|TestBindingLaunchesExactUserInstalledBinary|TestCursorPromptMessageFailure)$' -count=1
```

Changed Go files pass gofmt and `git diff --check`. Full suites and native Linux/macOS validation were not run locally; upstream CI remains pending.

title: fix(cursor): use native parameterized ACP model controls
body:
Code changes: +61 -25  
Tests: +56 -5  
Others: +0 -0  

## Problem

AO does not advertise Cursor's `clientCapabilities._meta.parameterizedModelPicker` extension. Cursor therefore exposes opaque parameterized model variants rather than its native family picker with Context, Effort, and Fast controls. Selecting a persisted variant can reapply parameters embedded in that value instead of using the user's current Cursor family preferences.

Cursor can also return both modern `configOptions` and legacy `models`. AO currently chooses the legacy model setter whenever the latter exists, even when the modern model control is present, losing the parameter-control behavior.

## Change

- Forward binding-owned client capability metadata while preserving existing ACP extensions. Enable `parameterizedModelPicker` for Cursor chat sessions and model discovery.
- Prefer the advertised modern model control when both model protocols are present. Legacy-only agents keep their existing setter.
- Resolve saved bracketed Cursor selections to their model family; Context, Effort, and Fast remain controlled through Cursor's native parameter options and preferences.
- Discover task-creation models through the same native ACP capability and invalidate old Cursor CLI catalog snapshots through the existing fingerprint.

No user-specific context size, effort, or fast setting is hardcoded. This introduces no new frontend components: existing conversation settings already render the native options. The extension is also used by [Zed's ACP client](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/agent_servers/src/acp.rs).

## Existing Cursor cache boundary

Cursor Agent 2026.10.14-0f9edde can migrate its own previously selected ACP variant into CLI preferences the first time parameterized mode is initialized. This PR follows Cursor's native initialization behavior; it does not edit or clear external Cursor configuration files. A local repair of that stale external cache was performed separately before live verification and is not part of this patch. Afterward, the native resumed session advertised the family `grok-4.7` and Context `500k`, Effort `xhigh`, Fast `true`, matching the user's configured preferences.

## Validation

Passed on Windows amd64 with Go 1.27.1:

```sh
go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/nativeacp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/cursoracp ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/deepseekharnessacp ./internal/daemon -run '^(TestACPDriverNegotiatesRichClientCapabilitiesAndNativePromptContent|TestBindingLaunchesExactUserInstalledBinary|TestSessionOptionsPreserveCursorFamilyPreferences|TestSessionPrefersModernModelConfiguration|TestDiscoverConfigOptionsReadsSessionCatalogWithoutPrompt|TestCursorCatalogFingerprintTracksParameterizedACPSource|TestConfigureBootsTheACPProfile|TestReviewerAgentAuthUsesLaunchReadinessAndPreservesStrictStates)$' -count=1
```

Changed Go files pass gofmt and `git diff --check`. Full suites and native Linux/macOS validation were not run locally; upstream CI remains pending.
