title: feat(desktop): show cloud session artifacts and document cloud artifacts (3/3)
body:
Code changes: +561 -81  
Tests: +414 -12  
Others: +166 -0 (docs and locale strings)

Stack: #6769 control plane → #6779 worker → **#6809 desktop and docs (this PR)**. Base is `ao/agent-orchestrator-251/cloud-artifacts-worker`; review those first, this diff covers only the desktop and docs.

## Summary

PR 3 of 3 for cloud session artifacts: the **desktop** plus the **docs**. As before, everything is gated on the deployment. Cloud sessions carry artifact files only while the control plane reports `offering.artifacts`. With it off, no cloud artifact surface renders: the Artifacts tab, Summary section and page are all driven by the file list.

- **Data.** The cloud session list carries only `artifactCount`. `useCloudSessionsQuery` reads each session's files with `listSessionArtifacts` once per session version (every commit changes the session's `updatedAt`) and fills in `artifactFiles`, which `toCloudWorkspaceSession` maps centrally (per the repo rule). File URLs are not built at list time. When the Artifacts view opens, `useCloudArtifactAccess` asks for the short-lived access prefix (it lasts 10 minutes) and replaces it two minutes before it expires, and on window focus near expiry. Each file URL carries the file's `updatedAt` as `?v=`, so an open file reloads when the agent rewrites it; it keeps its URL across a prefix refresh, and a refused read takes a fresh prefix and reopens once.
- **Viewer** (`SessionArtifactsView`):
  - A cloud HTML file opens in `CloudArtifactFrame`, an iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"`: **no `allow-same-origin` and no popups**, loaded from the control plane. That control plane also sends a sandbox CSP with `connect-src 'none'`, and the main process holds the frame to its session's access prefix.
  - Other files render through `main`'s `ArtifactViewerBody`, read-only, fetched through the cloud bridge (`cloudCpFetch`; the control plane has no CORS). Relative Markdown images resolve against the access prefix. Images, audio and video use `main`'s media viewers streamed from the control plane; media and other non-text files are read with HEAD only.
  - A row whose object is gone shows **"This file is no longer available."** rather than an error page; any other failure shows a message. A failed access request shows its own message with a retry button.
  - Local-only actions (folder buttons, delete) stay hidden for cloud.
- **Renderer CSP.** `frame-src` and `media-src` now list the cloud control-plane origins: staging, production, and `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`. Without this the frame and cloud media would be blocked. The websocket list is derived from the same origins.
- **Artifacts page.**
  - The cloud skip in `groupArtifactsByProject` is removed (remote hosts are still skipped).
  - The page loads cloud workspaces only when `offering.artifacts` is on.
  - "New artifact" lists cloud projects and starts a cloud session with `requestedOutput: "artifact"`, using the project's worker agent and falling back to Claude Code. It stays available for cloud projects when no local agent is ready.
  - Cloud groups use the Cloud icon; the sidebar counts cloud artifacts only while the offering has them.
- **Live updates.** The existing 5 s cloud session poll picks up a commit through the session's `updatedAt`; there is no separate event stream.
- **Clients.** `packages/cloud-client` gains `listArtifacts` and `getArtifactAccess`. The renderer client gains `createSessionArtifactAccess` and `listSessionArtifacts`. The offering resolver exposes `artifacts`.
- **Strings** in all 8 locales.
- **Docs:**
  - `cloud/docs/control-plane.md` gets a "Session artifacts" section covering the worker, storage, upload accounting, the sweeper, commit, reads and isolation.
  - `cloud/docs/deployment.md` gets the bucket (TLS-only policy, encryption, ownership, versioning, lifecycle backstop), task-role IAM including `s3:ListBucket`, settings, the deploy checks, rollout by committing `staging.env`, the build-time `frame-src` note, and local MinIO.
  - The Cloud user guide gets an "Artifacts" section: only the artifacts folder is copied, and pages cannot fetch, open windows or follow links.

## Tests run

Re-run after the review (2026-10-19): full `npm run typecheck` in `frontend/` passes with 0 errors (after `npm ci` for `main`'s new dependencies). The affected vitest suites pass, including `src/renderer/hooks`, the artifact views and page, the sidebar, the CSP, and the frame guard: 87 files, 1,109 tests. New tests cover the session-list file hydration, the pinned URL across a prefix refresh, recovery after a refused link, the access retry button, the cloud branch of `useCreateArtifactSession` and the frame-navigation guard.

Original run:

- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`: 0 errors, with `packages/product-ui` dependencies installed as CI does.
- New and updated vitest suites pass:
  - cloud cases in `SessionArtifactsView.test.tsx`: an HTML file opens the sandboxed frame at the access URL and not the Browser panel; an open HTML file gets a new URL when the file changes; Markdown opens with the cloud fetch and the right raw URL; an access error shows; no local folder or delete actions appear;
  - `useCloudArtifacts.test.ts`: URL escaping, the session mapping, and an older control plane;
  - `artifacts.test.ts`: cloud projects are included and remote hosts excluded;
  - `cloud-offering.test.ts`: `artifacts` resolves for server, legacy and missing values;
  - `vite.renderer.config.test.ts`: `frame-src` and the websocket origins;
  - `packages/cloud-client`: 30 tests, including the new artifact routes.
- Full `npx vitest run` in `frontend/`: 7846 passed, 2 failed, plus 2 files that failed to load.
  - The two failures (`browser-history-store`, `HarnessSettingsSection`) were timeouts under load; both pass when run on their own.
  - The two files that didn't load (`browser-view-host`, `provider-auth-flow`) need the Electron binary, which this machine's install did not download (install scripts were skipped). CI installs it.
- `npm run build --prefix src/docs` succeeds.
- The control-plane serving this view depends on was checked in Chromium on an isolated compose stack in PR 1's test plan: the sandboxed page rendered with its relative CSS and PNG, inline script ran, and `fetch` was blocked.

## Test locally (Docker, all three PRs)

From the repository root on this branch:

```bash
AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1 npm run cloud:local     # Postgres, MinIO + versioned bucket, control plane on :8081
cd frontend
D="$HOME/.ao/dev/cloud-artifacts"
env -u AO_PORT AO_DEV_ELECTRON_DIR="$D/electron" AO_RUN_FILE="$D/running.json" AO_DATA_DIR="$D/data" \
  AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 npm run dev
```

`AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` must be set at launch: it adds the local control plane to the renderer's `frame-src`. The desktop's own daemon always uses a local SQLite database; the separate `D` directories give this branch a fresh one. The shared `~/.ao/dev/data` may already be migrated by another branch and fail with `duplicate column name: artifact_dir`.

1. Sign in to Cloud as `dev@local.test` / `localdevpass123`.
2. **Settings → Harness → Cloud**: add a GitHub personal access token (the local stack has no GitHub App) and a coding-agent credential. Credential validation is skipped locally, but the agent needs a working key to write files.
3. **Clone to the cloud** with a test repo URL.
4. **Artifacts → New artifact** on that project; ask for an HTML page with a CSS file and a Markdown file.
5. In the session's **Artifacts** tab: files appear within ~30 s; HTML opens sandboxed with its CSS; Markdown opens read-only; edits and deletes show up after the next sync; after **Archive session** the files still open.
6. Restart with `npm run cloud:local` (flag off): no cloud artifact UI appears.

Without an agent key, write files into the worker directly: `docker exec <worker> sh -c '…'` into `<AO_DATA_DIR>/artifacts/<sessionId>`. Check with `curl …/me` that `offering.artifacts` is `true`.

All of these steps were run on 2026-10-16; the results are below.

## End-to-end results (local Docker stack)

These results are from 2026-10-16, before the review changes below. For this round the API and storage behaviour was re-checked live (see the follow-up section); the desktop window was not driven again.

Run on 2026-10-16 against `npm run cloud:local` with `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1` (Postgres 17, MinIO, control plane, Docker workers running Claude Code v2.1.287). The desktop was a dev build of this branch, driven through its real Electron window with Playwright over the Chrome DevTools Protocol; storage was checked in Postgres and MinIO after each step.

| # | Scenario | What was done | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Artifacts page lists cloud projects | Opened **Artifacts** in the sidebar | ✅ `px0` (Cloud) listed with its file and session title |
| B | New artifact on a cloud project | **New artifact** → `px0` | ✅ Cloud session created with `requested_output = artifact`; the menu offered Scratchpad and `px0` |
| C | Agent writes files | Typed a task into the session terminal; the agent wrote `report.html`, `styles.css`, `logo.svg`, `notes.md` | ✅ Written 09:53:31, committed 09:53:34 (3 s); the Artifacts tab and sidebar count (1 → 5) updated without a reload |
| D | HTML in the sandboxed frame | Opened `report.html` | ✅ Relative CSS and SVG image loaded; inline script ran; its `fetch` to the control plane was blocked; `document.cookie`/`localStorage` threw; frame origin `null`; iframe sandbox has no `allow-same-origin` |

The URL now carries the file's `updatedAt` as `?v=`. After the fix the open HTML view updated in 10 s and Markdown in 19 s. Each edit added an S3 version; the row points at the newest |

Archived board cards can't be opened (existing app behaviour), so the files reappear in the app after **Restore**; they then open with the latest edit, and the restored worker left the stored files untouched. The user guide is corrected to say this |
| I | Flag off | Restarted with `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=0`, reloaded the app | ✅ `/me` `artifacts: false`; artifact routes 404; `requestedOutput: "artifact"` rejected (422); no `artifactFiles` on sessions. App: Artifacts page shows its empty state, **New artifact** offers only Scratchpad, no Artifacts tab on the session |
| J | Ordinary task | Session "can you create a document summarising the project" (not an artifact session) | ✅ The agent wrote `px0-project-summary.md` to the artifacts folder; it synced, listed and opened |

Storage and access checks on the same stack:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Every Postgres row vs. its MinIO object | ✅ Committed version exists and its SHA-256 matches, for every file in both sessions |
| One `artifact.changed` event per commit | ✅ 5 events for session `1a8156c7`, matching the writes, edits and delete |
| 26 MiB file (over the 25 MiB cap) | ✅ Skipped with "file is over the per-file limit"; a small file written alongside it synced |
| Another org's user: list / access on this org's session | ✅ 403 / 403 |
| Another org's user: own org path with this session's ID | ✅ 404 / 404 |
| Access link for session A used for a session B file | ✅ 404 |
| Tampered access link / path traversal / not signed in | ✅ 401 / 404 / 401 |

Found while testing, not changed here:
- A restored worker's artifacts folder starts empty, so the agent can't see its earlier files on disk. They remain stored and readable in Cloud.
- A message sent through the session messages API did not reach the agent in this terminal-mode session, so the task was typed into the terminal. Not investigated; it doesn't involve artifacts.
- The Artifacts page hides archived sessions' files, for local sessions too (since #6567).

## Re-review follow-up (2026-10-22)

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Conflict with `main` | Merged; `useSessionWorkspaceFiles` keeps both import sets and passes `source.cloud`. |
| Major 1: pinned link expires | Full screen (which reloads the frame) takes a current link; a cloud image or video that fails to load asks for a fresh link and loads again. A frame that navigates to a sibling file with an expired link now gets a short "link expired" page from the control plane instead of JSON (#6769). |
| Major 2: reads inside the session poll | The list query fetches the list only. Each live session's files are read in their own query, at most four at a time, keyed on the artifact version (count and `artifactsUpdatedAt`), so activity does not re-read them and the list never waits. A session keeps its last good list while a new one loads or after a failed read. Archived sessions are not read. |
| Major 3: New artifact bypasses `createCloudSession` | Now created through it, with the user's default session interface and its retry for older control planes. |
| Minors 1, 2, 5, 6 | Copy hidden for cloud files that are not text; Markdown images use the pinned root; the New artifact menu says why local items are disabled; viewer tests for a cloud image and video. Earlier minors 2, 5, 13: cloud file reads never go stale (no re-read on focus), retries use the action slot (also on the HTML error state), the control-plane doc no longer says pages can open windows. |

Not changed: minor 3 (no Range support when serving files, so a cloud video cannot seek past what has loaded), minor 4 (hover cards for cloud artifact links show no preview), minor 7 (the frame guard matches the path on any origin), and the earlier deferred items. The desktop click-through is still open.

Checks: the affected vitest suites pass (2,549 tests; two unrelated tests failed once under load and pass alone). Full `tsc` was still running locally at push time; CI runs it.

## Pre-merge review follow-up

Addressed (Pritom14's review, plus axisrow's optional notes):

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Blocker: conflicts with `main` | Merged; cloud files go through `main`'s `ArtifactViewerBody` with the cloud bridge and access prefix passed down; cloud HTML keeps `CloudArtifactFrame`; `media-src` gains the control-plane origins. |
| Major 2: frame can open any URL | `allow-popups` and `allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` removed here and from the control plane's CSP (#6769); the main process holds a cloud artifact frame to its access prefix. User guide corrected. |
| Major 3: token expires while a file is open | Refresh from `expiresAt` minus two minutes, on focus near expiry; a 401/403 takes a fresh prefix and reopens once; HTML shows a message instead of the error body. |
| Major 4: every refresh reloads the open file | The open file keeps the URL it opened with until the file changes. |
| Major 5: polling and control-plane load | The list sends a count; files are read once per session version; the per-view event stream (and its replay from 0 and clock-skew filter) is gone. |
| Minors 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14 | Navigation pinned; non-text cloud files not carried over IPC; cloud New artifact without a local agent; retry button; no retries for missing files or refused links; event filter removed with the stream; sidebar gated on the offering; Cloud icon; docs corrected; tests for the cloud branch of `useCreateArtifactSession`. |

Not in this round (follow-ups):
- Opening links from a cloud HTML artifact (and minor 8, plain links hitting the CSP block page): needs the control plane to serve the link-request script, or another bridge.
- Major 5 (part): one timer owner for the cloud session poll, as `useWorkspacePolling` is for local.
- Minor 4: full screen moves the iframe node, which reloads it.
- Minor 9: `frame-src` is fixed at build time (documented in the runbook).
- Minor 10: only the first 100 cloud sessions are fetched, so older cloud artifacts are missing from the Artifacts page.
- The desktop click-through was not repeated after these changes; unit tests cover the new paths.

## Known risks and follow-ups

- Cloud HTML runs in an opaque origin, so module scripts and runtime `fetch` calls in an artifact page don't work. That is the security trade-off left to you in setup doc A6.
- Links in a cloud HTML artifact do not open: the frame has no popups, and `main`'s link-request protocol relies on a script the local daemon injects into its pages. Follow-up below.
- A cloud artifact session can only be started from the Artifacts page. The New Task composer has no artifact option for local projects either.

title: bug(review): --no-inject still delivers reviewer comment threads to the worker session
body:
## Summary

A worker session triggered reviews on external (not-its-own) PRs, always with `ao review trigger <session> --pr <url> --no-inject`. Despite that, an unresolved reviewer thread from the AO native review was still **forwarded into the worker session** as a task with the template instruction "fix + push + resolve the thread".

For sessions that only *trigger* reviews of other people's PRs (review-only workers), such a delivery is at best noise and at worst a prompt injection-shaped instruction to modify someone else's PR. The session must refuse it manually, and each delivery still wakes the session and burns tokens.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** `--no-inject` means no review output is forwarded into the session — or, read strictly ("leave the session's review auto-inject setting unchanged"), the session's auto-inject state is never silently ON to begin with.
- **Actual:** the thread delivery arrived anyway. Two plausible causes, both worth checking:
  1. the session's auto-inject birth-state is ON (e.g. inherited from project-level `autoReview`), so "leave unchanged" preserves an ON state the operator never set;
  2. the review-comment forwarding path does not consult the session's auto-inject flag at all.

## Requests

1. Make `--no-inject` a hard guarantee: no reviewer comments/threads are forwarded into the session for runs triggered with it, regardless of prior session state.
2. Expose the current auto-inject state in `ao review ls --json` and/or `ao session get` (today it is invisible, so operators cannot tell why a delivery arrived).
3. Provide a CLI way to turn auto-inject off for an existing session (currently the only lever is a trigger-time flag that merely "leaves unchanged").

## Notes

- The docs describe the default as "auto-inject is turned on" and `--no-inject` as "leave unchanged" — the semantic gap between those two is what bites: a session that was never explicitly opted in can still be opted in by birth-state.
- Delivery of review comments is otherwise a great feature for worker-owns-PR flows; this request is only about honoring the opt-out.

**Priority:** high for review-pipeline automations — forwarded "fix+push+resolve" instructions into sessions that must never edit those PRs; each delivery also wakes the session.

**Confidence:** High — reproduced across multiple triggers in one session, all with `--no-inject`; delivery observed with the full template text.

## Environment

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64), desktop daemon `ao version dev`, self-built from a recent upstream `main`
- Flow: dedicated review-only worker session; all runs triggered via `ao review trigger <session> --pr <external-pr-url> --no-inject`

body: Code changes: +1046 -40 Tests: +1404 -12 Others: +129 -4 ## What Name new Git worker branches and worktrees from the initial task prompt across desktop, CLI/API, and orchestrator-created sessions. For example, “redesign the website in vaporwave theme” becomes `ao/vaporwave-site/root` and a `vaporwave-site` worktree. Session IDs stay unchanged. The naming prompt prefers two short words, permits a third only when needed, and enforces three words / 24 characters. Pending names use a shimmer with one of five short translated labels; temporary session-ID branches are hidden from branch summaries and copy commands. ## How - Reuse the selected harness’s background title call to generate title and slug together, overlapping workspace preparation. Limit concurrency to four calls and fall back to a local slug after 20 seconds, invalid output, unsupported providers, or capacity overflow. - Use atomic no-replace worktree moves on macOS, Linux, and Windows, and check local/cached remote refs and Git registrations. Collisions get matching numeric suffixes for the branch and directory. Never force a branch rename or overwrite an existing directory. - Finalize names before setup or agent launch. Persist actual paths after partial failures, retain durable recovery stages, and repair interrupted Git registrations on retry. Workspace projects update each registered repository. - Keep explicit branches and existing sessions unchanged. Shared daemon naming supports Chat and TUI for desktop, CLI/API, and orchestrator-created workers. Explicit CLI/API session titles are preserved while their workspaces receive generated names; scratch/cloud sessions retain their workspace behavior. ## Review Reviewed against repository standards and the requested behavior. title: fix(desktop): stop refetching the whole workspace for events that change nothing on the board
body:
Code changes: +61 -20\
Tests: +101 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## Impact

| | before | after | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `GET /api/v1/sessions` during a 10 s streaming turn, id-only updates at 10 Hz | 64 | 4 | **-94%** |
| All renderer API requests in that turn | 324 | 83 | -74% |
| Replay of the busiest real 120 s: `GET /api/v1/sessions` | 38 | 16 | -58% |
| Same replay: all renderer API requests | 202 | 118 | -42% |
| 120 s at 10 Hz: `GET /api/v1/sessions` | 758 | 24 | -97% |
| 120 s at 10 Hz: JS heap growth after a forced GC | 5.84 MB | 1.65 MB | -72% |
| 120 s at 10 Hz: peak JS heap | 104 MB | 69 MB | -34% |

## What

A `session_updated` event that carries only the session id no longer refetches the whole workspace (`GET /api/v1/projects` + `GET /api/v1/sessions`) within the 150 ms window. It refreshes the workspace at most once per 5 s: at once when the workspace is already 5 s old, otherwise once when it gets there, and not at all when another workspace refresh covers it first. The session's own conversation and editor-handoff caches still refresh at once. Status changes, sessions-row updates, new sessions and PR events keep the 150 ms path.

## Why

Fixes #6763.

`event-transport.ts` coalesces CDC events into a 150 ms window, and every `session_updated` without a `conversationId` invalidated the workspace. Usage bookkeeping emits exactly that: `usage_bindings_cdc_update` fires on every update of a binding, including `TouchUsageBinding`'s `updated_at`-only one, with the payload `{"id": <session>}`.

How often these rows arrive depends on the workload:

- **#6763 reports a sustained rate:** with several Claude sessions and subagents, the renderer refetched the workspace about every 150 ms for hours.
- **Real databases show bursts:**
  - In a 3.9 GB database, 93,829 of the 100,446 retained `change_log` rows (93%) are id-only, nearly all from usage (the whole database has 31 agent-switch rows and 14 PR report outputs). They came in bursts: at most 30 rows in one second and 73 in one minute; no minute reached one row per 150 ms.
  - In two smaller real databases, one usage pass writes 2-5 rows with a single timestamp (median 2 and 4, p90 5, max 24). Passes come about every 30 s; in the more recent database, one pass in ten follows the previous one within 3.4 s.

For an isolated burst, `main` and this branch both fetch the workspace about twice: `main` at once and once per 150 ms window the burst spans; this branch at once and 5 s later. The branch saves when id-only rows keep arriving within 5 s, as in the issue's report and in closely spaced passes.

Measured with the real renderer attached to a lab daemon (Evidence):

| Workload | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| The issue's sustained rate (10 Hz) during a 10 s turn | 64 fetches | 4 |
| The busiest real 120 s, replayed with its original timing | 38 | 16 |

The 10 Hz scenario models the issue's report; it is about 8 times the busiest real minute above. At 10 Hz for 120 s, the renderer's JS heap after a forced GC grew 5.8 MB on `main` and 1.7 MB on this branch.

Streamed chat deltas are not the cause: their rows carry a `conversationId`, which `main` already routes to the open chat only (a streaming turn alone: 3 workspace fetches on `main`, 2 here).

#6773 proposes a similar lane. This PR differs in two places, both on purpose (How): it does not defer sessions-row updates whose fields repeat, and it keeps the session's own chat and editor-handoff refresh immediate.

## How

- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/event-transport.ts`:
  - An id-only `session_updated` (payload keys only `id`/`sessionId`; per the CDC triggers that is usage bindings and usage sources, agent switches, cleanup facts and reported PRs) queues the workspace refresh instead of flushing it, until `ID_ONLY_WORKSPACE_REFRESH_MS = 5_000` after the last workspace refresh, with one timer. When the timer fires it checks again, because another refresh may have moved that point; any workspace refresh (a status change, a new session, a reconnect) covers and clears the queued one. Disconnect clears the timer.
  - The caches refreshed with the workspace (agent switches, SCM summary including the session's linked PR, usage summaries) wait with it, as before.
  - The session's conversation and editor-handoff refresh stays on the 150 ms path: an id-only update can be what tells an open chat that its start-up finished (`useConversationConnecting.test.tsx`), and the chat does not poll.
  - `scheduleFlush` is the existing 150 ms window code moved into a function, unchanged, so the id-only timer uses the same pacing.
- **Repeated status: not deferred, on purpose.** The `session_updated` payloads that carry a status are:
  - chat activity, message, turn and account rows: they carry a `conversationId` and already skip the workspace refresh on `main`;
  - the sessions-row trigger: it fires only when a session column changed, and its payload omits board-visible columns (title, start-up checklist, branch state, pin and prompt times), so fields that match the board do not mean the board is current;
  - interface-transition rows: they coincide with provider changes that the session list reports without any CDC event (`chatProviderPreserved`).

  Deferring the last two would delay visible changes, and sessions-row updates are 0.09% of the rows in the 3.9 GB database above.
- **Reconnect: unchanged.** Every stream open still refreshes the workspace, because `Last-Event-ID` replay is not provably complete:
  - A new `EventSource` (first connect, a new daemon port, a rebuild after `CLOSED`) opens with `?after=latest` and no `Last-Event-ID`, so it starts at head and nothing replays the gap.
  - On the browser's own reconnect the daemon replays `seq > cursor` (`ReadChangeLogAfter`), but the retention janitor (7 days or 100,000 rows) may have pruned part of the gap, and the daemon neither detects nor reports that. A streaming turn writes about 200 rows per second, so 100,000 rows is about 8 minutes of streaming. A cursor ahead of head is clamped to head and reported only in `X-AO-Event-After`, which `EventSource` cannot read.
  - The stream has no project events, and the session list has live fields (`statusReadiness`, `chatProviderPreserved`) that no CDC event announces.

## Evidence

All counts are median (min-max) over 3 repetitions per side. Base and branch differ only in `event-transport.ts` and alternate.

The issue's sustained rate, during one streaming turn (base 7dceb0ec7d):

| During a ~10 s streaming turn | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Id-only rows at 10 Hz: `GET /api/v1/sessions` | 64 (64-65) | 4 (4-4) |
| Id-only rows at 10 Hz: `GET /api/v1/projects` | 64 (64-65) | 4 (4-4) |
| Id-only rows at 10 Hz: all renderer API requests | 324 (322-325) | 83 (82-87) |
| No id-only rows (turn only): `GET /api/v1/sessions` | 3 (1-3) | 2 (1-2) |

On `main` the fetches come about every 150 ms for the whole turn. On this branch they come at the prompt, at about 5.3 s and at about 10.2 s.

The real pattern, without a turn (base 5418c4631b): the busiest 120 s of id-only rows in the more recent real database (97 rows in 13 bursts of 2-16 rows, each within 252 ms, 1.0-30.3 s apart), replayed with the original offsets:

| In the 122 s window | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| `GET /api/v1/sessions` | 38 (37-38) | 16 (15-17) |
| All renderer API requests | 202 (198-205) | 118 (112-121) |

Both counts include the workspace's own 15 s poll.

Renderer memory at the issue's rate, without a turn (base 5418c4631b): id-only rows at 10 Hz for 120 s, heap read over CDP at the start and the end:

| Over 120 s | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| `GET /api/v1/sessions` | 758 (737-792) | 24 (23-25) |
| JS heap growth after a forced GC (`Runtime.getHeapUsage`), MB | 5.84 (5.06-7.31) | 1.65 (0.70-1.80) |
| Peak `JSHeapUsedSize` in 10 s samples, MB | 104 (91-109) | 69 (69-73) |

How it was measured:

- **Daemon:** built from the merge-base, run under the shared perf lab's sandbox with a fresh database and the scripted Claude ACP agent. The turn is its `reasoning` scenario (2,000 streamed chunks at 200/s, about 10 s).
- **Renderer:** this worktree's real renderer from the Vite dev server in headless Chromium 148, opened on the session's chat route. The preload is the repo's e2e `installFakeBridge`; `EventSource`, the API client and the workspace query are real.
- **Counting:** a proxy in front of the daemon logs every renderer request. The browser can reach only Vite and the proxy (0 requests blocked, 0 console errors in every run).

title: fix(browser): keep dialogs and notices above the native browser view
body:
Code changes: +209 -49\
Tests: +122 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keeps dialogs and floating notices, such as the "Agent updates available" notice and the New task dialog, above the native browser page instead of underneath it.

It also stops the update notice from blocking the browser: before, you couldn't click or scroll the page while the notice was showing.

## Why

The browser page is a separate native `WebContentsView`. When an overlay opens, the main process raises the transparent shell above it. Two problems broke that:

1. **New tabs were added above the raised shell.** `browser-view-host` calls `contentView.addChildView(view)` with no index for each new tab, which puts the view on top. Any tab created while an overlay was open (from the user, `ao preview`, or an agent's `ao browser` action) covered the overlay until the overlay closed and reopened. The update notice stays mounted with `data-state="open"`, so it was hit most often.
2. **Overlay tracking was per hook, not per document.** `SessionView` and `BrowserPanel` can each have a `useBrowserView` instance mounted at the same time. Each kept its own `overlayOpenRef` and sent `setOverlayOpen(false)` on cleanup, so unmounting one lowered the shell while another still saw an overlay as open and never re-raised it.

3. **The update notice blocked all browser input.** The notice is long-lived and flagged as a native overlay, so the shell stayed raised over the page the whole time it was showing. A raised shell covers the full window and receives every click and scroll, and Electron can't make a single view click-through for just one region.

## How

- `window-composition.ts`: new `restackShell()` raises the shell back to the top when an overlay is open, and does nothing otherwise. Ordering is shared with `setOverlayOpen` through `placeShell`, so the macOS surface refresh still applies.
- `browser-view-host.ts`: optional `onNativeViewAdded` callback, called right after each page view is appended. `main.ts` wires it to `windowComposition.restackShell()`.
- `renderer/lib/browser-overlay-sync.ts`: a single ref-counted `MutationObserver` for the whole document, using the same selectors and `data-state` filtering as before. `useBrowserView` subscribes to it instead of running its own observer. The shell is lowered only when the last subscriber unmounts.

- `HarnessUpdateNotice`: no longer flagged as a native overlay. A new `useLiveBrowserViewportRect` hook measures the live browser viewport, which is exactly the native view's bounds. `noticePlacement` then keeps the notice in its corner, moves it beside the page if it would overlap, or hides it while the page leaves no room (maximized browser, or a very wide inspector rail). The notice comes back when the browser is restored.

The stacking fix covers every surface that already matches `OPEN_BROWSER_OVERLAY_SELECTOR`, so individual dialogs or notices don't need changes.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/browser-overlay-sync.test.ts src/main/window-composition.test.ts src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.test.tsx src/renderer/native-composition-cascade.test.ts`: all pass.
- New tests:
  - `restackShell` raises the shell only while an overlay is open.
  - The host calls `onNativeViewAdded` after each `addChildView`.
  - With two overlay subscribers, unmounting one does not lower the shell.
  - An overlay that is already open when the tracker subscribes raises the shell.
  - The notice never sets `data-browser-native-overlay`.
  - `noticePlacement`: default corner, page elsewhere, move beside a docked page, hide when there's no room.
- `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `frontend/src`.
- Manual check in the Electron desktop dev app (macOS) on this branch: the update notice and the New task dialog stay above the live browser page. The notice-input change (second commit) still needs a manual check.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

The Harness settings page stopped scrolling after #6699.

That PR wrapped every settings section's toolbar and body in a new `div`. The Harness page turns off the page scroll and lets the harness list and the open harness scroll on their own. title: fix(harness): turn Droid's own auto-update switch back on for its update
body:
## Problem

Updating Droid from AO could fail like this, even for the copy at the official installer's location (`~/.local/bin/droid`):

```
Error: the update finished, but the installed version 0.159.1 did not reach the requested version 0.242.1
Output:
Auto-update is not available for npm installations.
Run: npm update -g @factory/cli
```

`droid update` checks Droid's own auto-update switch. When `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED` is `false`/`0`, or the build turns auto-update off (as Droid's npm build does), it prints that message and exits 0 without updating. The message is misleading: an official-installer copy prints it too. Reproduced with `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false droid update` on Droid 0.242.0, installed with the official installer.

## Fix

When the user asks AO to update Droid through the official installer, `droid update` now runs with `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=true`, which overrides that switch (Droid reads a truthy value before its build default). This applies only to vendor self-update commands, through a small per-target `vendorUpdateEnv` map, so another vendor with the same kind of switch can be added there.

## Tests

- `TestDroidUpdateTurnsDroidsAutoUpdateBackOn`: the update command runs with `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=true`.

title: perf(sessions): list sessions without a query per archived session
body:
Code changes: +67 -14  
Tests: +493 -3  
Others: +46 -0 (generated sqlc)

## Impact

| `GET /api/v1/sessions`, real database (300 sessions, 269 archived) | before | after | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SQL statements per call | 273 | **5** | **-98%** |
| Daemon CPU per call, median / p95 | 36.2 / 46.8 ms | 29.8 / 37.8 ms | -18% / -19% |
| Latency, median / p95 | 34.0 / 69.1 ms | 30.4 / 56.7 ms | -11% / -18% |

The statement count is exact; the timings are noisy, but lower in 5 or 6 of 6 interleaved pairs.

## What

`GET /api/v1/sessions` now loads the workspace-cleanup facts of all listed archived sessions with one query, instead of one query per archived session. The response is unchanged.

- New batched query `ListSessionCleanupFactsBySessions` (`json_each` over the id list, the same shape `ListPRFactsBySessions` and `ListCurrentHeadReviewRunsBySessions` already use) and `Store.ListSessionCleanupFactsForSessions`.
- `Service.List` collects the archived ids, makes one call, and hands each session its disposition. `Get` keeps its single-session read.
- A session still exposes its `workspaceCleanup` only when its facts row belongs to its current `cleanupGeneration`; the rule moved into one helper (`currentWorkspaceCleanup`) used by both paths.

## Why

A list read made one `GetSessionCleanupFacts` query for every archived session (a comment in the code marked it "batch if archive reads become a bottleneck"). On a 302-session board with 269 archived sessions that is 273 SQL statements per call (`4 + archived`), and the renderer refetches this list every 15 s, every 300 ms while any session is "checking", after most CDC events, and on every event-stream reopen. No tracking issue.

## How

- `queries/cleanup.sql` + `npm run sqlc` (ASCII only); `store/session_cleanup_store.go` wraps it and returns a map of the sessions that have a row.
- `service/session/service.go`: `Store` interface gains the batched method; `toSessionWithFacts` takes the disposition as an argument instead of querying; `toSession` (single-session path) loads it itself.
- A list with no archived session makes no cleanup-facts call.

Deliberately not changed, and why:

- **Artifact folder walk.** Every listed session still walks its artifact folder. `artifactFiles` (path, size, mtime, URLs) is part of each list response and comes from that walk; the persisted `session_output_type` only says whether any artifact exists, so it cannot replace the file list without changing response values. The walk is about 10% of an in-process list call on the clone.
- **Output-type self-repair.** Unchanged. It runs synchronously inside the list read, per session whose persisted type disagrees with the disk (or whose `artifact_dir` is empty), through `ReconcileSessionOutputType`, which re-walks the folder and writes through `UpdateSessionArtifactOutput` on the single writer connection. It is a one-time heal per session, so a settled board never reaches the writer (0 `change_log` rows during the lab calls).

## Evidence

Lab: `ao-perf-lab`, clone mode, APFS clone of a 3.88 GB real database (300 sessions listed, 3 with artifact files; 269 archived in the database, 270 in every lab daemon's response because a daemon boot flips one more session to terminated, cause not confirmed; the statement count above was taken on the 269 state, so base would run 274 at 270 archived by the same formula). Base `5418c4631b` against this change, 6 interleaved runs per binary, 20 timed calls each after warm-up; Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.5.1, go1.27.1, Low Power Mode on, shared machine (so absolute times are noisy; compare within the table).

| | Base | This change | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SQL statements per list call (exact, counting driver) | 273 | **5** | -98% |
| Latency, median (HTTP, 120 calls) | 34.0 ms | 30.4 ms | -11% |
| Latency, p95 | 69.1 ms | 56.7 ms | -18% |
| Daemon CPU per call, median | 36.2 ms | 29.8 ms | -18% |
| Daemon CPU per call, p95 | 46.8 ms | 37.8 ms | -19% |
| In-process `List` median / p95 (200 calls, no HTTP) | 23.2 / 36.9 ms | 17.7 / 30.5 ms | -24% / -17% |

CPU per call was lower in 6 of 6 interleaved pairs, latency in 5 of 6; run-to-run spread (18 to 40 ms) is larger than the gain, so read the latency as "about 10%, consistent direction". The statement count is exact. In the CPU profile the cleanup-facts reads fell from 16% of a list call to 1.5%.

Measured by `lab.py clone` plus a driver that does one clone and one daemon per run, 3 warm-up calls and 20 timed calls, with daemon CPU from `proc_pid_rusage` around each call. Not measured: the clone has no `session_cleanup_facts` rows, so the lab only exercises the "no row" branch; row mapping is covered by tests below.

## Testing

Commits: `578e2ddb51` is the head before rebasing; `e3ba35c649` is the same change rebased onto `5afd868cc7`; `e52ff75110` is the same change rebased onto `645f7f560c` (the final-round results below were measured there); `a977e403ac` is the final head, rebased onto origin/main `43a4b02645` whose new commits touch only frontend files, so the backend tree is identical (gofmt, build, vet, sqlc, api:spec and service/session + sqlite/store tests re-run there, ok). All rebases were conflict-free.

- RED on base `5418c4631b` (new tests + test-side fake additions, production code untouched): `TestListLoadsCleanupFactsInOneBatchedQuery` reads = 1, 7, 60 (want 0); `TestListIssuesTheSameStatementsForAnySessionCount` 9 vs 44 statements for 8 vs 64 sessions; store test does not build (method missing).
- GREEN on `578e2ddb51`: the same tests pass; 5 statements for 8 and for 64 sessions.
- Equality of results: `TestListMatchesGetForEverySessionShape` (real SQLite, 11 session shapes including archived with current, stale, missing and preserved-dirty facts, PRs, artifacts and three self-repair cases) asserts `List` equals `Get` per session and that the repair fires for exactly the mismatching sessions; it passes on base and on the branch. A cross-commit golden (20 shapes x 8 filters, full JSON per session) is byte-identical between base and branch (sha256 `d159032e...c2ab`). Live lab responses: 10 of 11 full responses (300 sessions) identical after removing per-daemon fields; the 11th differs in one live chat orchestrator's `statusReadiness`, which is boot-time recovery state outside this change's path.
- `TestListSessionCleanupFactsForSessionsMatchesSingleReads`: batch equals single reads, absent rows omitted, 2,000+ ids in one call, empty request.
- `gofmt -l`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`: clean on `578e2ddb51`, `e3ba35c649` and `e52ff75110`.
- `golangci-lint run ./...` v2.13.2: 0 issues on `578e2ddb51`, `e3ba35c649` and `e52ff75110` (whole backend each time).
- `npm run sqlc` and `npm run api:spec`: no drift on `578e2ddb51`, `e3ba35c649` and `e52ff75110`.
- `go test -race -p 4 ./internal/service/session ./internal/storage/sqlite/store ./internal/artifactversions` on final head `e52ff75110`: ok (227 s, 550 s, 71 s). Earlier: ok on `578e2ddb51` (service/session, sqlite/store) and on `e3ba35c649` (all three).
- `go test -p 4 ./...` once on final head `e52ff75110`: 195 packages ok, 7 failed, none of which can see the changed code (`opencode`, `opencodev2`, `chatdriver/acp`, `runtime/conpty`, `runtime/tmux`, `integration`, `terminal`). Re-run on `e52ff75110` and on origin/main `645f7f560c` the same minute: `opencodev2`, `conpty` and `integration` fail identically on `645f7f560c`; `tmux` and `acp` fail intermittently on both (acp alone x6: 2 and 4 of 6 pass on each); `opencode` and `terminal` pass on re-run (`terminal` failed twice on the branch and 0 of 4 times on base, a small sample). An earlier full run on `578e2ddb51`: 197 ok, 4 failed, all four also fail or flake on base.

## Not covered

- `npm run api:ts`, frontend jobs, Windows and other CI-only jobs were not run locally (no frontend or API-shape change; `openapi.yaml` regenerates with no diff).
- The per-session artifact folder walk remains; avoiding it needs a persisted file index and would change when the list shows new files, so it is a separate change. A walk of a session holding a very large artifact tree (up to 1,000 files) costs far more than the typical few-file folder; only a micro-benchmark under load, not a lab number.
- The self-repair still runs on the writer during a list read when a session needs healing.

title: fix(auth): keep unpackaged builds from taking ao-app:// from the installed app
body:
## Summary

Cloud sign-in from the installed app could open a blank stock **Electron** window instead of returning to AO. The browser showed "You're signed in", but the app never received the session.

**Root cause:** `registerCloudProtocol()` ran on every launch, including dev builds. On macOS, `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(protocol, path, args)` ignores `path`/`args` and binds the scheme to the running bundle. For a dev build, that bundle is `frontend/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app` (`com.github.Electron`, shared by every checkout). Every `npm run dev` therefore took `ao-app://` away from `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app`. On Windows, a dev build wrote `HKCU\Software\Classes\ao-app` pointing at the dev `electron.exe` and a worktree script.

## The rule

Whether a build holds `ao-app://` depends on how it signs in, not on the platform:

| Build | `ao-app://` |
|---|---|
| Packaged app (any redirect) | claims it, as before |
| Dev build, loopback sign-in (the default) | never claims it, and releases a claim an earlier dev run left behind |
| Dev build with `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT` set to a bounce page or `ao-app://callback` | claims it while it runs, and gives it back when it quits |

**What releasing does, per platform** (checked against Electron 44's `browser_mac.mm`, `browser_win.cc`, `browser_linux.cc`):
- **macOS:** the scheme goes back to the installed app at once. Electron picks the first other handler, and stable and nightly share `dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`.
- **Windows:** the stale dev entry is deleted. The installed app takes the scheme again the next time it starts (it registers on every launch).
- **Linux:** Electron's removal is a no-op, and a dev build registers the installed app's own `.desktop` entry, so there is nothing to release and the check is skipped.

**Only the single instance claims or releases.** `registerCloudProtocol()` now runs after `requestSingleInstanceLock()` succeeds, so a second launch that is about to exit can't drop a running build's claim. On macOS any dev checkout would otherwise match it.

Dev builds still sign in: unpackaged builds default to the loopback redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:3000/callback`). A loopback dev build no longer receives `ao-app://billing`; that link opens the installed app, and it only opens Settings → Billing.

`cloud/README.md` and `cloud/docs/deployment.md` said dev and staging builds sign in through `ao-app://callback`. They now say dev builds use the loopback callback, and the installed app goes through the `/app/auth/return` bounce page.

## Tests

- `cloud-auth.test.ts` (33 tests) pins `process.platform`, since CI runs on Linux. Cases:
  - packaged app, including with a loopback override and when launched with a deep link in `argv`;
  - loopback dev build;
  - release on macOS and Windows, with the exact executable and script Windows matches on;
  - no release on Linux;
  - a dev build with no app path;
  - a localhost override;
  - bounce-page and `ao-app://` overrides, including the release on quit and Linux without one.
- **Mutation check:** each of 8 deliberate breaks of the logic fails at least one test (ignoring `isPackaged`, dropping the `defaultApp` or `argv` guards, releasing on Linux, never releasing, no release on quit, releasing without the ownership check, a quit hook for packaged builds). Passes under shuffled order.
- `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in the changed files.

**Live on macOS (Electron 44.7.0)**, reading the `ao-app` handler with `LSCopyDefaultHandlerForURLScheme`:
1. The machine started affected: the handler was `com.github.Electron`. A loopback dev build from this branch moved it to `dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`, so links open `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app`.
2. A dev build with a bounce-page override claimed it (`com.github.Electron`). A second launch sharing its profile lost the single-instance lock and exited in 2 s, and the claim stayed.
3. Firing `will-quit` in that build gave the scheme back to `dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`.

A full quit of this dev setup (no local daemon built) doesn't finish, with or without this change, so step 3 fires `will-quit` directly instead.

Not run live: Windows and Linux. They're covered by the unit tests and the Electron source.

title: feat(agents): per-folder Claude Code and Codex accounts
body:
Code changes: +3637 -126  
Tests: +1184 -2  
Others: +1818 -17 (generated sqlc, OpenAPI spec and TS schema; 8 locale catalogs)

## Summary

**Developer-mode preview.** Turn on Settings → General → Developer mode to see it. Accounts are managed on Harness → Claude Code (or Codex) → Account, and each session's Summary shows its account. Without developer mode nothing changes from `main`: Settings keeps its Subscriptions page with the Codex account switcher, and no account UI appears. Not gated, on purpose: the two general fixes below (Codex v0.162 terminals, graceful chat stop) apply to everyone; migrations 0210–0212 run for everyone but stay inert until an account is added; accounts added in developer mode stay in effect if it is turned off later (the daemon does not see that renderer setting).

Adds Claude Code and Codex **subscription accounts that are plain CLI config folders**. AO launches the unmodified `claude` / `codex` binary with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` pointing at the account's folder. Sign-in is each CLI's own (`claude auth login`, `codex login --device-auth`). There is no proxy, no service to run, and AO never reads or stores a token.

- **Your CLI's own login is an account.** The login your CLI already has shows up by its email, tagged "CLI login", with no setup. AO launches it with the CLI's own folder untouched. Accounts are named by their email everywhere; a Claude CLI login that reports no email (a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` login) is "OAuth token"; AO does not read the token to tell tokens apart.
- **Add more accounts in AO.** Switching in AO never changes the CLI outside AO.
- **Each task runs on an account.** New tasks use the provider's default. Sessions on different accounts run side by side.
- **Move a session after its turn.** Chat and terminal both work. The move is a transaction: B's agent resumes the same native conversation before the session is rebound, and a failure leaves the session on A. A turn that is still working, for example one waiting for the old account's limit to reset, can be stopped and moved after a confirmation.
- **Every limit of every account.** Claude's 5-hour, weekly and per-model windows plus extra usage come from the CLI's own `get_usage` control request. Codex windows and reset credits come from its app-server. They appear on each CLI's Harness Account tab and in each session's Summary.
- **Statistics.** Tokens each account used in AO over the last 30 days. Usage is attributed through a time-stamped session→account binding history, so a moved session's usage splits correctly.
- **The right account.** Each folder is checked against the login it was added with. Credential env vars (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, …) are cleared for account launches. A login that already exists is refused, the computer's own included. A picked account must be signed in.

- **Upgrades keep old sessions where they are.** Migration `0210` binds every existing session to the computer's own login at its creation time. No running agent restarts.
- **Also fixed: Codex v0.162 terminals.** Codex v0.162 draws its composer as `»`; AO's screen reader knew only `›`, so no idle Codex terminal could be switched (Terminal → Chat on `main` too) or moved. Separate commit `c9316cf`, easy to split out.
- **Also fixed: a stopped chat agent no longer leaves its command running.** AO stopped chat agents with SIGKILL at once; Claude Code stops the commands it runs only on SIGTERM or SIGHUP, so a dev server or build kept running with no agent. Chat stops now send SIGTERM, wait up to 2 s, then SIGKILL (`process.TerminateGroup`), as terminal sessions already do. Commit `c0e9cd5`; `837b824` widens the daemon's wait for the chat host to exit from 5 s to 10 s to cover the longer shutdown (on a loaded machine a move otherwise ended in `SOURCE_STOP_UNCERTAIN`).

- **Changes made on an account stay there.** Settings and MCP servers are shared key by key (`env` and `mcpServers` entry by entry). A key follows This computer until it is changed on the account; from then on the account's value stays. A small `.ao-shared.json` in each folder records what AO last wrote.
- **A folder that cannot link is refused.** If an account folder cannot link to this computer's history, sign-in, binding and moves refuse it (`AGENT_ACCOUNT_UNSHARED`) instead of letting the CLI start history of its own there. On Windows the links need Developer Mode.

History stays shared, so a resume works across accounts. Each folder keeps only its own login, settings copy and app-server daemon state. Everything a conversation needs (`projects`, `sessions`, history, skills, plugins, …) is a link back to the computer's own folder, recreated at every launch.

## How it works (two-minute version)

An account is a separate config folder for the CLI. AO picks the folder per session, and moves a live session between folders with the same durable handoff the Chat ↔ Terminal switch uses.

1. **Accounts are folders.** Claude Code reads `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and Codex reads `CODEX_HOME`. Each extra account is a folder under `~/.ao`, signed in by the CLI's own login in an embedded terminal. AO never reads or stores a token; it asks the CLI who is signed in and what the limits are. The computer's own login is the implicit "device" account.
2. **Shared history, private login.** Each account folder links the device folder's history and project data, so every account sees the same conversations. `settings.json` and MCP servers are shared key by key through a ledger (`.ao-shared.json`), so an edit made on one account stays there. Login files stay private to each folder.
3. **Binding.** `session_agent_accounts` records which account a session uses, with history for usage attribution. `runtimeEnv()` applies that account's env on every launch path (spawn, restore, resume, chat, terminal). The migration binds existing sessions to the device login.
4. **Moving a live session** reuses `session_interface_transitions`, same mode, different account:

   ```
   preflight B (A still running) -> drain or interrupt -> prove A stopped -> start B -> commit binding
                    failure before commit -> stop B, restart A on A;  daemon crash -> boot recovery
   ```

   The binding is the commit point, and only one writer per conversation runs at any time.
5. **UI (developer mode).** Harness → Account lists accounts and limits; the session Summary shows the session's account and switches it.
6. **Fixes found on the way (for everyone).** Chat agents get SIGTERM before SIGKILL; `exit-agent` keeps terminal sessions live (`runtime_released_launch_id`); the Codex `»` composer.

## Design: an account move is a transaction

**Problem.** The first version moved a session by stopping the agent, rebinding it, then resuming it. During that gap the session was saved as *Exited*, so the chat screen showed "The agent controller stopped" for about 20 s. A failed resume left the session stopped and already rebound.

**Constraint.** A provider allows one live writer per conversation (Codex `thread-writer-locks`, Claude's single transcript file). So B's agent cannot start while A's still runs: the gap can be shortened and made safe, but not removed.

**Design.** A move uses the durable handoff saga that the Chat ↔ Terminal switch already uses (`session_interface_transitions`). It names a source and a target account, and the mode stays the same. Everything that can fail runs first; the binding is the commit point.

| Phase | What happens | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| preflight | A keeps running. AO checks B's login, launch auth in B's environment, and that B's folder can see the conversation. | Abort. Nothing was touched. |
| drain | The current turn finishes, or is interrupted after the user confirms. | Abort. Nothing was touched. |
| source stop | A stops, and the stop must be proven. | Unproven stop → `recovery_required`; AO never starts a second writer. |
| target start | The conversation resumes with B's environment (an in-memory override); the binding still names A. | Stop B, restart A on A. |
| commit | The session is bound to B. | Same rollback. |

**Continuity.** Preflight proves that B's folder can see the conversation. If the provider still cannot resume it when B starts, a terminal follows the [ordinary Terminal restore policy](docs/architecture.md) and starts fresh, as any terminal restore on `main` does; Chat rows stay intact.

If the daemon exits mid-move before the commit, recovery stops anything started under B, and the binding still names A. If the binding already names B, recovery keeps B's agent.

**Why this shape.** There is one state machine for every controller replacement: the interface switch, the account move, and later auto-switch at a limit. The move inherits its message queueing and input fences, cancellation before the stop, rollback, crash recovery, and the UI's in-progress state. Every client shows "Switching to B…" instead of the stopped-controller banner.

**Schema and API.**
- Migration `0211` adds `source_account_id` and `target_account_id`, and widens `CHECK (source_mode <> target_mode)` to `… OR target_account_id <> ''`.
- `PUT /api/v1/agents/accounts/sessions/{id}` starts the move and answers `202` with the transition.
- Progress uses the existing `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/interface-transition`.

## Terminal sessions stay live after their agent exits (`3967cbd`)

**Problem (also on `main`).** `ExitAgent` (used by `ao session exit-agent` and by account removal) destroys a terminal agent's runtime and keeps the session. The reaper then probed the dead runtime and the lifecycle read it as a crash: an exited agent never counts as recent activity. The session was terminated and dropped out of the sidebar.

**Fix.** `ExitAgent` records the launch it releases (`sessions.runtime_released_launch_id`, migration `0212`) before it stops the terminal, inside its agent operation, so no reaper tick lands in between. The lifecycle leaves an exited session whose *current* launch was released live. The marker names one launch: a new launch has a new id, so a crash of any later launch still ends the session. That includes the existing race where the dying agent's exit hook lands before the reaper (`TestRuntimeObservation_RetriesAfterRevisionChangesDuringFinalization` still passes unchanged). A general "exited sessions are never terminated" rule broke that crash case, so it was not used.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove an account bound to a live Claude terminal | `exited`, `is_terminated=0` through five reaper ticks (25 s); terminal gone; still in the sidebar |
| Open that session | Resumed on the default account and replied `STILL-EXITED-THEN-BACK` |
| `exit-agent` on a Codex terminal, three ticks, `resume-agent` | `exited|0`, then replied `CODEX-RESUMED` |
| `kill -9` a live terminal's host (a crash) | Still terminated (`exited|1`) |

## "Stop and move" shows the switch, not a failure (`7af5b77`, `33ec910`)

Moving an agent mid-turn stopped the turn, and the chat then showed "The agent ran into a problem" (or "interrupted by you"). The old agent's reply to the cancel races its shutdown, so the turn could settle as failed. When the move commits, the stopped turn now settles as interrupted and carries an `account.switched` notice: "Switched to <account>. The agent stopped here for the switch. Press Continue to resume this turn, or send a new message." The turn stays continuable. The confirmation says what the agent is doing (still working, or waiting for your decision) instead of guessing at a usage limit.

Without it, account transcripts already land in `~/.claude/projects` through the shared links, so per-account statistics were unaffected; the lab ran with a custom config folder. |
| **L9** | Kept as is, deliberately. Claude's home mixes per-account state into top-level entries (`backups/` with copies of the login's `.claude.json`, `policy-limits.json`, `remote-settings.json`, `telemetry/`, auth caches), so Claude shares an allow-list; an unknown new entry stays per account rather than carrying one account's state into another. Codex keeps its private state separate and shares by default. |
| **L2/L3/L5** | Out of scope: the matrix's own "PR as is" expectation. Merging an account's existing private history is a possible follow-up. |
| **Cold Claude move** | Not reproduced. Six chat moves timed by phase right after a cold daemon start, including a 2 MB conversation, took 3.8 to 10 s end to end, with 0.8 to 7 s in `target_starting`, against the 45 s step limit. The chat start log now times `session/load` and `session/resume`, so a slow move shows where its time went. |
| S2, S3, R5 | Covered: the Claude browser duplicate refusal ran for real in the lab when B was first added, and unit tests cover duplicate cleanup and a different login on sign in again. |
| S7 | API-key sign-in: out of scope by decision. |

## Design notes

- `domain` / `ports`: `AgentAccount`, limits and usage types; the `AgentAccountProviderCLI` port, with one adapter per provider in `adapters/agentaccount`; `AgentAccountStore`; `AgentAccountLaunchEnv`, which is the only thing Session Manager depends on.
- `service/agentaccounts`: the catalog (device accounts plus saved ones), cached readings (5 min), the sign-in flow in an embedded terminal, defaults, bindings, usage and the right-account checks.
- Session Manager: account env is applied in `runtimeEnv`, so every launch path picks it up (spawn, restore, resume, chat, terminal). It wins over project env. A session is bound at spawn (rolled back on failure). `StartAccountTransition` runs the move as a controller transition (see the design above). Claude workspace trust (`PreLaunch`) writes to the account folder's `.claude.json`, and the setup-token injector stays out of account launches.
- Storage: migration `0210_agent_accounts.sql` adds `agent_accounts`, `agent_account_defaults`, and `session_agent_accounts`, a binding history that cascades with sessions.
- HTTP: `/api/v1/agents/accounts…`, under the same strict-origin CORS gate as the Codex account routes and blocked on the LAN listener.
- UI (developer mode): a Subscriptions group on Harness → Claude Code / Codex → Account, next to the CLI's own login. The session Summary shows the session's account, its limits, and the switch. In developer mode the Settings Subscriptions page is hidden.

## Validation

Run locally on macOS (Go 1.27.1, Node 26; CI runs Linux with Node 24). The machine was shared with other heavy suites, with a load average of 60–100.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` | pass |
| `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 (whole module; touched packages again after the move commit) | pass |
| sqlc drift, API drift (`openapi.yaml` + `schema.ts`) | pass |
| `go test -race` on every touched package (`agentaccount`, `agentaccounts`, `httpd/...`, `session_manager/...`, `sqlite/store`, `service/session`, `daemon`, `claudecode`, `ports`, `domain`) | pass |
| After the move commit: `go test` on `codex`, `agentaccount`, `agentaccounts`, `service/session`, `session_manager`, `storage/sqlite/...`, `httpd/...`, `domain`, `ports`, `daemon/...`; the account-move tests 3× under `-race` | pass |
| After the move commit: frontend `typecheck`, `SessionInterfaceSwitch`, `SessionInspector`, i18n catalog tests | pass |
| `go test -race ./internal/storage/sqlite` and `./internal/service/chat`, run alone as CI shards them | pass |
| Frontend `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`, `test:browser-postcondition-integration` | pass |
| Vitest | 8066 passed; see the notes below |
| Renderer e2e (`@T0\|@P0`) | see the notes below |
| After `8cb67ce`: `golangci-lint` on touched packages (0 issues); `go test` on `agentaccount`, `agentaccounts`, `usage`, `chatdriver/...`, `service/agent`, `session_manager`, `daemon` (32 packages); frontend `typecheck` and the accounts panel tests | pass |
| After `93c7003`: `go build ./...`, `golangci-lint` on touched packages (0 issues); `go test` on `service/agent`, `agentaccounts`, `service/session`, `service/chat`, `session_manager`, `storage/sqlite/...`, `daemon`, `agentaccount`, `lifecycle`, `httpd/...`, `domain` (18 packages) | pass |
| After `d53a948`: `go build ./...`, `golangci-lint` on touched packages; `go test` on `agentaccounts`, `service/session`, `service/chat`, `session_manager`, `storage/sqlite/...`, `daemon`, `lifecycle`, `httpd/...`; sqlc regenerated | pass |
| After `3967cbd`: `go build ./...`, `golangci-lint` on `lifecycle`, `session_manager`, `storage`, `domain`; `go test` on `lifecycle/...`, `session_manager/...`, `observe/...`, `storage/sqlite/...`, `daemon/...`, `httpd/...`, `service/session/...`, `domain/...`; sqlc regenerated; accounts panel and i18n tests | pass |
| After `b511133`: `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `golangci-lint` on touched packages; `go test` on `session_manager/...`, `agentaccounts`, `httpd/...`, `daemon/...`, `service/session/...`; API drift regenerated; frontend `typecheck`, the accounts panel and i18n tests | pass |
| After the review fixes: `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` on touched packages; `go test` on `session_manager`, `agentaccounts`, `agentaccount`, `chatdriver/...`, `process`, `httpd/...`, `storage/sqlite/...`, `codex`, `daemon/...`; frontend `typecheck`, `SessionInspector`, `HarnessSettingsSection` | pass |

New tests:
- The store attributes usage through the binding history: one session moved between accounts splits its tokens correctly.
- Folder sharing for Claude and Codex: history and config are linked, login and app-server daemon files stay private, and the code is idempotent.
- Credential env vars are cleared for account launches.
- Changes made on an account stay, entry by entry, while untouched keys keep following This computer; a value set back to the computer's follows again.
- A folder that cannot link is refused at sign-in, at bind (default or picked) and at a move; This computer is never refused.
- The service refuses duplicate logins and signed-out or mismatched picks, and binds default accounts.
- The account move: phase order for chat and terminal, rollback on a failed start or bind, a failed preflight leaves the agent running, refusals, boot recovery of an uncommitted target, and boot recovery that keeps a committed one.
- The preflight resolves the target account's env without changing what a concurrent launch of the running agent gets.
- Migration `0210`/`0211`/`0212`: old sessions bound to the computer's login at creation; the widened `CHECK`.
- Lifecycle: a released launch's runtime death keeps an exited session live; an earlier released launch, or none, still terminates. The store writes the release only for the current launch, and a full-row update leaves it. `ExitAgent` records the release before the runtime is destroyed.
- Removal exits only the running agents bound to the account, and a stop that fails keeps the account signed in; a move of an exited agent restarts it on the new account (chat and terminal).
- Sign in again: refused for This computer, cancel keeps the folder, another login is `mismatch` and signed out, the same login comes back on the same account.
- The accounts panel: "Sign in again" only on a signed-out saved account, a closed sign-in is not checked again, and the remove dialog starts without an old error.
- Codex: the history probe follows a linked sessions folder; v0.162 `»` frames read as idle, draft, active and not-started.

Failures I saw locally that are **not caused by this PR**. CI needs to confirm them:
- `opencodev2` `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects` and `integration` `TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch` fail identically on a clean `main` checkout on this machine.
- These are load timeouts that pass when run alone: `claudecode` `TestClaudeAuthReportIgnoresStderrJSON` (5/5 alone), `fake` `TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination`, Vitest `GlobalSettingsForm` and `SessionMemoryPanel` (`SessionMemoryPanel` compares "38s" against a `Date.now()` offset).
- 40 Vitest failures in `src/main/browser-profile-import` and `browser-history-store` (files this PR does not touch). `better-sqlite3` is built for Electron's ABI 130, and local Node 26 needs 147.
- 24 renderer e2e specs failed under load. All re-passed with `--workers=2` except `chat-composer-text-selection` › "visibly selected". That one also fails in this worktree with `main`'s `frontend/src` checked out, so it is environmental here.
- Windows, mobile, cloud module and docs jobs were not run locally.

## Intentional omissions and follow-ups

- **No account picker in the New Task dialog.** Use "Make default" before starting a task.
- **No automatic switch when an account hits its limit.** It was out of scope for this PR.
- **Main's legacy global Codex account switch is not removed.** Without developer mode it is still the Settings Subscriptions page; in developer mode that page is hidden. Removing or adopting the old code is a follow-up.
- **A move still has a short gap with no live agent.** Providers allow one writer per conversation, so B starts only after A stops. Messages sent during the gap are queued and delivered after the move.
- **MCP OAuth is per account folder.** Claude asks to authenticate MCP servers again on a new account.
- **No sweep of unsaved sign-in folders.** If the daemon restarts mid-sign-in, the unsaved folder under the state dir stays behind.
- **The server's window labels are English** ("Session (5h)", "Weekly · Opus").

This PR is independent of #6274 and does not build on it.

title: perf(desktop): run browser-profile import off the main process thread
body:
Code changes: +175 -33\
Tests: +370 -0\
Others: +4 -1

## Impact

| Importing a large Chrome profile (258 MB `History`) | before | after | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Longest freeze of the Electron main thread (every AO window) | 2,720 ms | 44.8 ms | **-98%** |
| Main-thread stalls over 50 ms per import | 2-4 | 0-1 | |
| Import wall time | 6.30 s | 6.19 s | unchanged |

Measured on Electron 33.4.11, before main moved to Electron 44 (#6462). Not re-measured on 44.

## What

Browser-profile import now reads the source browser's databases in an Electron utility
process instead of on the Electron main thread. A large Chrome, Firefox or Safari
profile no longer freezes every AO window while it is read.

## Why

`frontend/src/main/browser-profile-import.ts` ran `better-sqlite3` synchronously in the
main process: `backup()` of source databases up to 256 MB, `COUNT`/`ORDER BY` queries
over the whole `urls`/`cookies` tables, up to 20,000 cookies with one PBKDF2 derivation
each for Chromium on macOS, and Safari's binary cookie parse. On a near-cap synthetic
Chrome profile the main thread was blocked for 2.6-2.9 s at a time, so every window,
IPC call and timer stalled. Import is user-triggered, but it is the slowest thing the
main process does.

Related: #6380 touches the same file (the Firefox visited-history filter). This PR does
not change any query, and `git merge-tree` of this branch's head with #6380's head
(`db85f9f5d7`) still merges cleanly.

## How

- The two reads that open browser databases, `readProfileData` and the Safari
  profile-name lookup, now take and return structured-clone-safe data. Read data takes
  one request object: the import's size budget travels as a number and comes back
  updated, and the Chromium cookie key is passed as `{ platform, key }` and rebuilt in
  the reader.
- `BrowserProfileImportService` sends those reads through an injectable `readSource`.
  It defaults to running in-process, so the existing tests run the same code unchanged.
  The desktop app passes `processSourceReader`, which forks a fresh utility process
  (`AO browser import`) per read from a new Forge Vite entry,
  `src/main/browser-profile-import-worker.ts`, and kills it when the read settles.
  Canceling an import (app quit) now stops a read in progress instead of waiting for it.
  The process has exited before the read settles, so staging cleanup cannot race it.
- Discovery, request validation, the macOS keychain / Windows DPAPI key lookup, path
  redaction and the Electron session cookie and history writes stay in the main process.
  The browser-import rules are unchanged: the reader opens only validated, contained
  source files read-only (`query_only`, `backup()` into staging), writes only under the
  AO state dir's `browser-import-staging`, and source paths never reach the renderer.
- The packaged app keeps the `RunAsNode` fuse off (#6462). Utility processes do not use
  it; the fuse comment in `forge.config.ts` now says so instead of "no utilityProcess".

Why a utility process and not `worker_threads`: both load the Electron-ABI
`better-sqlite3` from `app.asar` (checked with the unpacked `.node`), but a worker
thread runs at default thread priority. On a loaded Mac it made the import about 5x
slower (51.5 s vs 10.1 s median), while a utility process kept main-thread speed. A utility
process also inherits the app's macOS responsible process, so Safari's Full Disk Access
grant still applies (checked with `responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid`).

## Evidence

Real desktop app (`electron-forge start`, own `npm ci`) on isolated lab state, with a
synthetic Chrome profile near the import caps: `History` 258 MB (500,000 URLs,
1,500,000 visits) and `Cookies` 9.7 MB (30,000 v10-encrypted cookies, synthetic Safe
Storage key via a stub `security`). Base and branch apps ran side by side and the
imports were interleaved, 3 measured repetitions each after a warm-up. The event-loop
delay was recorded in the main process with `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay`
(1 ms resolution) through the inspector, and wall time around
`window.ao.browserProfiles.import()` in the renderer.

| Median [min-max] | base `5418c4631b` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Main event-loop delay, max during import | **2,720 ms** [2,636-2,863] | **44.8 ms** [42.0-55.9] |
| Main event-loop delay, p99 during import | 14.7 ms [14.1-23.0] | 9.8 ms [8.0-10.9] |
| Main-loop stalls > 50 ms per import | 2-4 | 0-1 |
| Import wall time | 6.30 s [5.91-6.39] | 6.19 s [6.16-6.55] |
| Idle noise floor (max, 3 s before each import) | 17.3 ms [12.5-46.8] | 22.4 ms [11.4-22.7] |

Both variants imported identical results in every run (18,916 cookies, 5,000 history
entries, same warnings). Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.5.1, Electron 33.4.11; the machine was
shared with other jobs (load average 34-37 during the final runs).

## Testing

- The final head `ee86de90d9` is rebased onto `7d2165ef5c` (main with Electron 44.7.0 and
  #6930) and was not re-run locally; CI (typecheck, typecheck:e2e, full vitest) covers it.
  The only rebase conflict was the `main.ts` import line next to #6826's
  `registerChatImageIpc`; the change itself is the same as before.
- Before the rebase, on `6b97d50505` (on `9e4196cf30`, Electron 33.4.11), Node 24.14.0: `npx vitest run forge.config.test.ts src/main/browser-profile-import-worker.test.ts src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts src/main/browser-profile-ipc.test.ts src/main/browser-profile-store.test.ts src/main/browser-history-store.test.ts src/renderer/components/settings/BrowserImportDialog.test.tsx --testTimeout=180000`: 7 files, 133 tests passed, and `npm run typecheck` passed.
- New `browser-profile-import-worker.test.ts` (14 tests): reading a near-real Chromium profile from a structured-cloned request without changing the source; budget carry-over; error message and code; the reader client against real child processes (result, failure response, crash, exit without answer, cancel mid-read, cancel before spawn, already-canceled import); the service sending only cloneable reads with its abort signal, rolling back on cancel, and keeping default Safari names when the names read fails.
- New `forge.config.test.ts` assertion: the Vite build list contains `src/main/browser-profile-import-worker.ts` as a `main` target, the file `main.ts` forks. It fails with that entry removed.
- On `c68b4f2de8` (same change on an older base): `npm run typecheck:e2e` passed; full `npx vitest run --testTimeout=180000`: 474 of 476 files, 8,065 tests passed, 7 skipped, 3 failed in `ProjectEnvironmentSettings.test.tsx` and `HarnessSettingsSection.test.tsx`, which this change does not touch. Both files pass when rerun alone (118/118); they flaked at load average 50-65.
- Packaged layout, Electron 33.4.11 only: the production build of the new entry ran from inside `app.asar` with the unpacked `.node` and read the full lab profile.

## Not covered

- Not verified on Electron 44: the utility process loading `better-sqlite3` in a packaged
  app with #6462's fuses on (`EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation`,
  `OnlyLoadAppFromAsar`, `RunAsNode` off). That needs a packaged build and one real
  import; PR CI does not package the app, and the dispatchable "Desktop build artifacts"
  workflow builds an unsigned one. The dev path (`electron-forge start`) on Electron 44
  was not run either.
- No signed or notarized build was produced. The utility process runs in the plain Helper app, which gets the same entitlements as the main app (which already loads this `.node`); library validation under hardened runtime is not verified.
- Safari and Firefox imports were not exercised in the desktop lab, and Windows and Linux were not run; their read code is unchanged and covered by the existing tests through the in-process reader.
- The Chromium-on-macOS decryption still derives the PBKDF2 key once per cookie. It now runs off the main thread, but deriving it once per import would cut the read time; left for a follow-up.
- The docs build, the Cloud client and product UI package checks, and the browser postcondition integration job were not run locally; this change does not touch them.
