title: fix(send): fail on unconfirmed delivery and adapt multiline paste delay
body:
Code changes: +172 -33
Tests: +237 -3

## Summary

Fixes an issue where `ao send` targeting an idle `claude-code` TUI worker returned HTTP 200 / exit code 0 even when the message's trailing Enter was absorbed by the terminal during large/multiline paste bursts, causing the worker to stay idle indefinitely without starting a turn.

`ao send` now **fails honestly** when delivery cannot be confirmed (HTTP 409 `SESSION_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED`) instead of silently reporting success — while recognizing durable acceptance evidence so a prompt that was genuinely accepted is never reported as a false failure.

Fixes #6685.

## Changes

- **Adaptive Paste Delay (`inputdelay`):**
  - Dynamically scales the pre-Enter delay for terminal text input based on message size and newline count:
    - Empty messages (Enter-only nudges): immediate (`0ms`).
    - Single-line messages (≤ 512 runes): standard configured delay (`300ms`).
    - Multiline or large pastes (> 512 runes): starts at `1s` plus `150ms` per additional 512-rune chunk, capped at `2s`.
    - Preserves any explicitly configured longer delay.
  - Applied to Unix `tmux` runtime (with adjusted `sendCompletionBudget`) and Windows `conpty`.

- **Delivery Confirmation Contract Enforcement:**
  - Introduces the `sessionmanager.ErrDeliveryUnconfirmed` sentinel error.
  - `confirmActive` / `confirmActiveWithNudge` return `ErrDeliveryUnconfirmed` when the confirmation budget is exhausted without the session becoming active, rather than silently returning `nil`.
  - `Manager.send` propagates the failure; `service/session` maps it to HTTP 409 `SESSION_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED`, so `ao send` exits nonzero and the caller can retry instead of hanging.

- **Durable acceptance evidence (`deliveryEvidence`):**
  - A prompt can be accepted and finish *between* the ~300ms activity polls, leaving the session idle with `Active` never observed. Confirmation now honors this delivery's durable acceptance marker instead of returning a false 409:
    - **User-authored send:** `LatestUserPromptAt` advancing past the delivery instant (`options.InteractionAt`). The baseline is pinned to the delivery instant — not read from the store after delivery — so the `UserPromptSubmit` hook cannot land in the read gap and hide inside the baseline.
    - **Coordination send (`ao send` / worker report):** the coordination checkpoint for this exact delivery ID, scoped to the current runtime launch (`semanticMessageAccepted`: `ConversationCheckpointState == Coordination`, `ConversationCheckpointGeneration == RuntimeLaunchID`, `ConversationCheckpointTurnID == deliveryID`). Keying on the delivery ID means an unrelated concurrent prompt cannot falsely confirm it. The delivery ID is symmetric by construction — `send()` and the live `UserPromptSubmit` hook both derive it from the `<ao-session-delivery>` wrapper via `domain.CoordinationDeliveryID`.
  - `SendSemantic` no longer treats `ErrDeliveryUnconfirmed` as fatal: its own durable acceptance loop is authoritative.

## Review updates

This PR incorporated three rounds of review feedback (@Vaibhaav-Tiwari):

1. **Successful delivery reported as failure** — added the retained-submission-evidence check above.
2. **Baseline captured after delivery** — pinned the baseline to the delivery instant (`options.InteractionAt`) to close the hook-vs-read race.
3. **Coordination sends false-failing** — replaced disabling evidence for coordination with the coordination acceptance marker (delivery-ID + launch scoped) via the `deliveryEvidence` descriptor.
   Also fixed a stale `sendConfirmConfig` doc comment that still claimed confirmation "never fails the send".

## Testing

- **`inputdelay`** unit suite: empty nudges, short lines, multiline, chunk boundaries, burst caps, custom overrides.
- **Session manager confirmation tests:**
  - `TestSend_ConfirmAcceptsRetainedSubmissionEvidence` — user prompt whose hook lands after the delivery instant, turn finishes between polls → confirmed, not a false 409.
  - `TestSend_CoordinationDeliveryIgnoresPromptEvidence` — a prompt-timestamp advance must not confirm a coordination send.
  - `TestSend_CoordinationAcceptanceMarker_RealStore` — real sqlite store driven by the real lifecycle hook emission records the coordination marker, then a real coordination `send()` is confirmed through it.
  - Existing nudge/decision-safety tests continue to pass.
- **API & service error mapping:** `ErrDeliveryUnconfirmed` → HTTP 409 `SESSION_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED`.

Passed locally (incl. the race detector):

- `go test ./backend/internal/adapters/runtime/inputdelay/...`
- `go test ./backend/internal/session_manager/...` and `go test -race ./backend/internal/session_manager/...`

## Summary
The Linux x64 desktop artifact build has failed since the Electron 33 → 44 upgrade (#6462). That blocks every nightly, because the release conductor needs all four platforms. Today's nightly (ao-releases run 39017499597, building `5a1ba26a9`) failed in `build (ubuntu-22.04, linux-x64, linux)`. macOS and Windows built fine.

When node-gyp rebuilds `better-sqlite3` against Electron 44's headers on `ubuntu-22.04`, it hits two problems:
1. **GCC 11 can't parse the headers.** `v8-primitive.h:658` declares `class [[deprecated(...)]] __attribute__((visibility)) Value`, and GCC 11 rejects a GNU attribute after a C++11 attribute in a class head (`expected identifier before '__attribute__'`).
2. **clang 14 (the runner's default `clang++`) is too old.** It fixes (1) but fails on `v8-source-location.h`. The 22.04 libstdc++ 11 only provides `std::source_location` when the compiler has `__builtin_source_location`, which arrived in clang 15.

The Linux job now sets `CXX=clang++-15`, which is preinstalled on the 22.04 image. Only C++ changes:
- tmux, ncurses (`--without-cxx`), libevent and the C half of better-sqlite3 still build with GCC.
- The job stays on `ubuntu-22.04` for the glibc baseline (#4616).

## Verification
- `frontend/release-workflows.test.ts`: 6/6 pass.
- Real runner: I dispatched `Desktop build artifacts` from this branch (run 39018823637, version `0.14.3-cxxcheck.2`, no release created). The Linux build succeeded. The first attempt with plain `clang++` (run 39018530045) failed on `std::source_location`, which is why this pins clang 15.
- I downloaded the Linux `.deb` from that run. Its `better_sqlite3.node` requires at most `GLIBC_2.34` and `GLIBCXX_3.4.29`. Ubuntu 22.04 provides glibc 2.35 and `GLIBCXX_3.4.30`, so the Linux floor doesn't move.

## Risks
- If a future runner image drops `clang++-15`, the step fails immediately at `command -v clang++-15` rather than producing a different build.
- I haven't launched the Linux app itself. I only checked the native module's symbol requirements.

title: feat(browser): consistent Chromium identity, and Chrome mode for agents in the user's own Chrome
body:
Code changes: +6326 -79\
Tests: +3036 -1\
Others: +534 -7\

## What

Two parts, both aimed at sites that challenge or block AO's browser.

**1. A consistent Chromium identity for the Browser panel** (first commit)

Browser tabs now present the Chromium build they really are, consistently:
- a Chrome-shaped, reduced user agent;
- Chromium's low-entropy `Sec-CH-UA*` client hints;
- an `Accept-Language` that matches `navigator.languages`.

**2. Chrome mode: agents in the user's own Chrome** (approved proposal, D1–D4)

A session can drive the user's real Google Chrome through a new MV3 extension, the **AO Browser Bridge**, instead of the panel:

```bash
ao browser target chrome   # this session now drives the user's Chrome
ao browser target panel    # back to AO's Browser panel (default)
ao browser chrome setup|status|remove
```

The agent gets a genuine Chrome fingerprint and the user's real sign-ins, with no remote-debugging port. Every `ao browser` command keeps its name and result shape.

## Why

The panel is Electron: Chromium's content layer without Chrome's browser layer. Measured on httpbin, browserleaks, bot.sannysoft, pixelscan, the reCAPTCHA v3 demo and nowsecure:

| Signal | Before | After part 1 |
|---|---|---|
| User-Agent | `… Orchestrator.inc/<ver> Chrome/152.0.7977.130 Electron/44.7.0 …` | `… Chrome/152.0.0.0 Safari/537.36` |
| `Sec-CH-UA*` headers | never sent (while JS exposes `userAgentData`) | sent, matching `navigator.userAgentData` |
| `Accept-Language` vs `navigator.languages` | `en-GB` vs `en-GB,en-IN` | identical lists |
| reCAPTCHA v3 / Cloudflare challenge | — | 0.9 / passes |

Two problems remain that Electron can't fix honestly:
- **Fingerprint tools still flag it.** pixelscan flags *any* Electron window ("inconsistent", "automated"), even a bare one with no AO code. Real Safari and the Codex app pass. Codex passes because it ships a custom Chromium (`Codex Framework.framework`, Chromium 154, with Chrome's browser layer).
- **Google blocks sign-in** in embedded browsers ("This browser or app may not be secure").

Driving the user's real Chrome solves both without spoofing anything.

## How

**Panel identity**
- `frontend/src/main/browser-identity.ts` runs per Browser partition, before the first page exists. Chromium reads the session user agent when a WebContents is created.
- The brand list reproduces Chromium's seeded GREASE algorithm, so the header matches `navigator.userAgentData.brands` exactly.

**Chrome mode, daemon side**
- **Session routing:** `service/browser` routes each session to the panel runtime or a second `browserruntime.Broker` (`chrome-extension` transport). The choice persists in `<data>/browser-targets.json`, and session teardown reaches both runtimes.
- **Connecting the extension:** the extension reaches AO through Chrome Native Messaging. Chrome launches `ao browser-host`, which relays frames to an owner-only socket.
  - The broker accepts a host only if it runs as the daemon's user and is the daemon's own executable (`LOCAL_PEERPID`/`SO_PEERCRED`), and presents the token from the owner-only `<data>/browser-chrome/endpoint.json`.
  - The first connected Chrome profile keeps the bridge (exclusive mode), so two profiles can't keep displacing each other.
- **Setup/remove:** `ao browser chrome setup|remove` and `GET/POST/DELETE /api/v1/browser/chrome` install the unpacked extension and host wrapper under `~/.ao`. Setup registers the host manifest with each Chrome channel in use (the registry on Windows).
  - **D1:** that manifest is the one approved file outside `~/.ao`. It's written only on explicit setup and removed by remove; `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` document the exception.

**Chrome mode, extension side (`frontend/src/browser-extension`)**
- **Consent and scoping:**
  - The first command from a session opens an AO consent window that only a person can answer.
  - Each session works only in its own tab group, "AO · <session>" (**D3**).
  - A user-editable site policy applies: denied sites (sign-in, payment and password-manager sites by default) fail with `BROWSER_SITE_BLOCKED`. There's also an optional allow list.
  - Kill switch: the toolbar popup's "Stop all agents".
- **Snapshots:** an isolated-world builder, invisible to page JavaScript, emits agent-browser's `- role "name" [ref=eN]` format and refs map. So `act` uses the existing deterministic matcher (shared from `src/main/browser-act-matcher.ts`), and deltas, waits, `get` and frames work the same way.
- **Input (D2):** trusted input by default, through a *transient* `chrome.debugger` attachment.
  - Only the `Input` and `Page` domains are used, attached for one action, never `Runtime`.
  - The agent's tab is brought to the front of its window first, because Chrome drops input to hidden pages.
  - A click that opens `alert`/`confirm`/`prompt` returns at once, and the attachment stays only until `ao browser dialog` answers it.
  - Per-site synthetic (T0) input is available for sites that should never see the debugging bar.
- **Other commands:** screenshots (with `--annotate`), network metadata via `webRequest`, and console/errors (Chrome's kept messages, read on request). `devtools` is panel-only.
- **Shipping:** built by `scripts/build-browser-extension.mjs` into `frontend/browser-extension`, which Forge ships beside `daemon/`. The fixed manifest `key` pins the extension ID to `eefgahhblbmjpccfcnpkhkadgcccnibg`, which the host manifest allows.
- **Shared code:** URL/title sanitizers moved to `src/shared/browser-sanitize.ts`, so both runtimes redact the same way.
- **Chrome only (D4):** Chrome, Beta, Dev, Canary and Chrome for Testing.

**Desktop UI:** Settings → Browser → "Agents in your Chrome" sets up or removes Chrome mode, shows registered channels, and gives the extension folder and ID to load. Strings are in all 8 locales.

**Deviation from the proposal:** site access and `debugger` are install-time permissions, not optional ones. Optional permissions made each session show two prompts, AO's consent window and then Chrome's own permission dialog, and nothing could automate Chrome's dialog. A session still does nothing until the user allows it in AO's consent window.

## Review follow-up (20 October)

Addressed all three remaining review findings in `6e2b51cfb`:
- Validate the selected iframe and its ancestors before trusted keyboard input.
- Move held mouse input outside the viewport before cancellation releases it; a real Chromium regression checks that the pressed form receives no click or submit after cancellation.
- Preserve detachment semantics for `selector-gone`, while keeping visibility checks for positive selector waits.

Merged current main and preserved published branch history. Focused extension tests (62), Chromium browser integration on Node 24, extension build, backend build/vet, browser/daemon/API package tests and isolated CLI suite pass. All 23 remote CI checks pass at `70defeca6`, including the complete frontend suite, Chromium integration, backend race shards, lint, API/SQLC drift, renderer smoke, and native platform checks.

Local validation limits: the full Node 24 frontend run encounters a pre-existing Electron/Node ABI mismatch in the installed `better-sqlite3` binding (147 vs 137), affecting profile-import tests. The full backend run reports external model-catalog discovery failures; the OpenCode discovery failure also reproduces on clean main. The local full TypeScript check was interrupted after a long run without diagnostics, and local lint reported zero issues but reached its time limit. Their CI counterparts passed. Redundant local full-suite runs were stopped after CI completed.

## Pointer-capture follow-up (23 October)

Fixed the remaining cancellation activation bug in `fb6c36194`, included in final head `20e56c21f`:
- Track the actual trusted mouse pointer ID in each frame's isolated extension world, including held movement entering another frame, then release active capture before moving outside and sending mouseup. Traverse closed shadow roots using Chrome's extension DOM API.
- If capture cleanup cannot be verified, skip a potentially activating release. Add a failure-path test for this guard.
- Extend the real Chromium regression with a Submit button that captures on pointerdown: ordinary clicks still submit, cancellation produces no target click or submit, and a later normal click still works.
- Merge current main, preserving both browser identity and its new readiness/liveness behavior. Answer broker heartbeat pings in the extension to keep Chrome mode connected.

Validation on final head `20e56c21f`:
- Full local frontend suite: **538 files passed; 9,103 tests passed, 9 skipped** (Node 24, two workers). An earlier run under machine contention had timing failures in three UI files; all 423 tests in those files passed alone, followed by the complete green repeat.
- Strict extension TypeScript check, E2E typecheck, extension build, complete Chromium browser integration, and the real-Electron terminal-origin/browser-boundary suites pass locally.
- Backend build and browser/CLI/daemon/API suites pass; browser broker, native host, and routing race suites pass.
- CI project and E2E typechecks pass. At the latest check, **13 CI checks pass**, the frontend test job is running, and **8 backend checks are queued for runners**; no failing checks are reported. The full local compiler and backend/lint attempts were interrupted under contention; their completed scoped checks are listed above. Do not treat the queued full CI jobs as passed.

Frontend dependencies were reinstalled under Node 24 and its native SQLite binding restored for this run.

## Testing

- **Go:** new tests for the broker (peer verifier, exclusive mode, hello metadata), `browserchrome` (ID derivation, endpoint permissions, setup/remove/refresh incl. foreign-manifest safety, registry path, host relay through a real broker, protocol mismatch, missing daemon, wrong token, busy rejection, executable pinning on a real Unix socket), router/target store/lifecycle, and CLI commands. `golangci-lint` on touched packages: 0 issues.
- **Frontend:** full vitest run, 501 files / 8,340 tests passing; `tsc --noEmit` clean. The extension has 51 tests: snapshot builder, deltas, policy, keys, pointer paths, URL rules, content ops on jsdom, consent races, manifest identity, and executor behaviour against a fake Chrome (consent, policy, tab-group scoping, trusted vs synthetic input, act, tabs, teardown, screenshots).
- **Real Chrome (`TestChromeE2E`, opt-in):** drives the real extension in Chrome for Testing 155 through a real broker and native host. Covers consent, open, snapshot, `act` fill, trusted click with a text postcondition, Enter, deltas, acting inside an iframe, annotated screenshot, network capture, console replay, a `confirm()` dialog, tabs, site-policy and file-URL blocks, devtools refusal, and teardown. Passes in about 5 s. It found four bugs that unit tests missed, all fixed:
  - the consent-close race;
  - input dropped on hidden tabs;
  - clicks blocking on dialogs;
  - a group-event race when creating tabs.
- **Panel identity:** live checks against httpbin and browserleaks on Electron 33 and 44.
- **CI:** all 23 checks pass at `70defeca6`. See the review follow-up above for local environment limitations.

## Follow-ups

- Publish the extension to the Chrome Web Store (unlisted). After that, add the store ID to the host manifest's `allowed_origins` alongside the pinned unpacked ID. Until then, setup asks the user to "Load unpacked".
- Accept-CH high-entropy hints for the panel.
- Edge, Brave and Arc support (D4 later phase).
- Chrome mode is local-daemon only; cloud and remote sessions aren't supported.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

### Review follow-up (26 October)

Pushed `e36861bf5` addresses all seven latest review threads. Network capture stops as soon as tab ownership ends. Revoking a session aborts its admitted commands before removing approval. Cancelled mouse cleanup collects observed pointer IDs and sweeps every frame, including children whose observers were suppressed, before sending cleanup input. Navigation checks cancellation after asynchronous setup and before updating the tab. Synthetic typing skips unsupported selection APIs, srcdoc children can be selected, and Meta/Control+Shift+Z dispatches redo.

Validation: all 78 extension tests pass; the complete Chromium postcondition integration passes, including a captured drag into a child whose early listener suppresses the local observer. Merged current main without rewriting history to resolve the CI-blocking package.json conflict, preserving extension packaging and the native TypeScript compiler. Final head: `6fd1ffad2`. Project/E2E typechecks, extension build, browser backend suites, API spec tests and regenerated API drift checks pass. Full frontend run: 553 files passed; one file had one failed assertion (9,342 tests passed, one failed, nine skipped). The sole failure was the existing ChatWorkspace scroll assertion at line 539; all 215 tests in that unchanged file passed in an isolated rerun. This full run is not reported as all green. A prior sandboxed attempt timed out in three loopback-server tests; all 34 tests in that file passed outside the sandbox before the complete unrestricted run. Remote CI currently has seven passing checks and 15 pending, with no failures. Full backend/lint and native-platform jobs were not rerun locally in this follow-up and remain subject to remote CI. All seven review threads are resolved. The earlier unmerged full-suite and legacy compiler attempts were stopped before merging main; they are not reported as passes.

title: feat(cloud): let ao spawn start a worker on an existing branch
body:
Code changes: +160 -51  
Tests: +387 -4  
Others: +23 -3 (cloud contract, generated cloud-client schema, using-ao skill doc)

## Why

A Coder customer asked to start a worker on an existing branch. The main case is resuming after a worker stops partway: its branch is already pushed, and a new worker should continue on it. Today every cloud session gets a generated `<prefix>/<short id>` branch cut from the default branch, and the cloud `ao spawn` has no way to name one. Local `ao spawn` already has `--branch`. The agreed direction is to ask the orchestrator rather than add a field to the new-task form.

## What changed

- **`ao spawn --branch <name>`** (`cloud/cmd/ao-cloud-agent`). The branch is sent only when given, so other spawns are unchanged.
- **Control plane.** `POST /worker/children` passes `branch` into `domain.CreateSession.Branch`, which is `omitempty` so the idempotency payload of every other create is unchanged. `createSessionTx` enforces `domain.ValidSessionBranch` on every create path. It refuses names that break git's branch-name rules, the project's default branch (a worker would push to it directly), and the session prefix (its ref would conflict with every generated `<prefix>/<short id>`). The API reports `invalid_branch`.
- **Worker checkout.** A branch that already exists on the remote is continued from its commits instead of being cut from the default branch:
  - Fresh clone (`ConfigureWorkerGit`): `checkout --no-track -B <branch> origin/<branch>` when there is no local branch yet. If local files block that switch, the worker cuts the branch at HEAD as before instead of failing startup. A restarted worker keeps its local branch.
  - Adopted template checkout (reuse existing checkout, or the connection's working directory): adoption bases the branch on `origin/<branch>` when present, and stashes tracked changes even when the checkout is already on the requested branch. Adoption reports whether it created the branch. After the fetch, a branch it created (so with no work of its own) moves onto `origin/<branch>`. That covers a template that cloned before the branch was pushed and a branch rebased since. Any other branch only fast-forwards.
- **PR attribution.** A pull request whose head is in a fork is never auto-claimed for a session, even when its branch name matches a session branch.
- **Contract and docs.** `CreateWorkerChildInput.branch` is in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` (client regenerated). The flag is documented in the `using-ao` skill, the CLI usage text, and the orchestrator prompt. To resume another worker's branch, kill that worker first and have the new one run `ao claim-pr <number>` if a PR exists.

Side effect: if a session's sandbox is re-created after the session already pushed its generated branch, the session now resumes from those commits instead of restarting from the default branch.

## Intentionally not included

- No new field in the desktop new-task form. This is orchestrator-only, per the agreed direction.
- Booting the Coder workspace itself from the branch (passing it into template parameters) is left out. It is only needed for testing template changes and depends on each template's parameter names.
- No guard against two live sessions on one branch. The docs tell the orchestrator to kill the old worker first; enforcement was deliberately left to the user.
- `AdoptedNow` is still not persisted. A worker that restarts between adoption and the post-fetch advance keeps the adopted base. This predates this PR, and the outcome is non-destructive: a push of a diverged branch is rejected.
- The branch length limit counts bytes, like the existing `defaultBranch` validation.
- Extra repos keep their configured branch.

## Validation

- `cloud`: `gofmt -l .` clean, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` all pass (32 packages).
- Each new test failed when its code change was removed: continuing a remote branch on a fresh clone and on an adopted checkout; moving onto a branch pushed after the template cloned, or rebased since; stashing on an already-checked-out requested branch; startup falling back when local files block the switch; not claiming fork PRs; the `invalid_branch` mapping; the CLI request body; and the branch rules (domain table test).
- Postgres store (CI skips these tests): ran `internal/postgres` against a local PostgreSQL 15. 220 tests pass, including `TestCreateSessionKeepsRequestedBranch` (keeps a requested branch, generates one when absent, and refuses the default branch, the prefix and invalid names). Four other tests fail in the same way on unmodified `origin/main` in this environment (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`), so they are unrelated to this change.
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` leaves no diff after commit; `typecheck`, `npm test` (29) and `npm pack --dry-run` pass.
- Not run locally: the cloud job's Docker-based "Test Expat security backport" step, because no Docker daemon was available. Left to CI.

title: fix: bound spawn remote lookup and detach seed-row rollback
body:
## Summary

Two defects together turned a stalled git remote into a silent spawn zombie: the session row appeared in the UI and sat on "Almost there" forever, with no error ever reaching the CLI or any log.

- `gitworktree.Workspace.ResolveDefaultBranch` ran the live `ls-remote` with the raw request context — the only remote call in the spawn path without its own budget (the other two use 5s). A stalled route wedged the whole spawn until the outer REST deadline. Give the lookup the same `defaultBranchResolutionBudget` and fall back to the cached remote HEAD.
- `Manager.rollbackSpawnSeedRow` unwound on the already-canceled context after that deadline fired: both `DeleteSession` and the `markSpawnFailedTerminated` fallback failed silently (`context canceled`), stranding the seed row as a phantom. Run the rollback with the sibling `spawnRollbackContext` helper (detached + `spawnRollbackBudget`), so cleanup survives the deadline and a wedged store write cannot hang the rollback goroutine.

Fixes #6754 — the reported failure mode (spawn wedged on a stalled remote, eternal "Almost there" phantom rows, no error surfaced). Measured reproduction and the code-level anatomy are in the issue. Follow-up scope from that report, intentionally out of this PR: daemon proxy support, the UI failed-state surface (`provision_error` rendering), and the timeout-path error envelope.

## Tests

- `TestResolveDefaultBranchBoundsStalledRemoteLookup` (new): a `git ls-remote` shim that stalls 30s must not hang resolution — the resolver must fall back to the cached `origin/HEAD` within the budget. Fails on the old code (30s > 9s assertion).
- `TestRollbackSpawnSeedRow_SurvivesCanceledContext` (new): rollback on a canceled context must still delete the seed row. `fakeStore.DeleteSession` now mirrors the sqlite driver and fails on a dead context, so this pins the fix.
- `go test -race` on `internal/session_manager`, `internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree`, `internal/gitdefault` — ok. `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` — clean.

## Known risks

- The rollback now completes even when the request is gone; sessions that previously leaked as phantom rows will now be properly deleted (or parked terminated if they progressed past seed state). That is the intended behavior, but if anything downstream depended on seeing phantom rows, it will notice.
- The 5s budget on the default-branch lookup matches the two existing remote budgets; repos on very slow but working remotes now resolve from cache instead of waiting longer than 5s for a live HEAD.

title: feat(review): stage reviewer payloads via base64 files instead of inline JSON
body:
## Why

Fixes #6021.

A reviewer model that cannot reliably emit a multi-KB single shell argument (GLM-5.3-flash collapsing to literal `PLACEHOLDER`) could never submit: the only sanctioned channel carried the whole review as one single-quoted JSON literal with `'\''` escaping on top, and every alternative was closed by design (no Write/Edit, heredocs banned, hook auto-allow limited to the exact printf pipe). The review existed only inside the model's head.

## What

- Review task template (`internal/review/prompt.go`): payloads are staged via base64 — `printf '%s' '<BASE64>' | base64 -d > /tmp/ao-review-<worker-session>-{post,results}.json` — then posted (`gh api --input <file>`) or submitted (`ao review submit --session <worker-session> --reviews <file>`). Base64's alphabet cannot quote, expand, or terminate a shell literal, so the whole quoting/escaping class disappears regardless of body content. The template also states explicitly that the sandbox auto-allows these shapes and inherited "no long inline arguments" hygiene rules do not apply there (in #6021's session the model routed around the sanctioned shape because of inherited operator rules, then collapsed on an improvised workaround).
- Permission hook (`internal/cli/hooks.go`): the staged shapes get their own strict allow regexes — per-worker /tmp paths (parallel reviewers cannot stage over or consume each other's payloads), base64-only payload charset (an embedded quote, `$`, or `(` breaks the match), and every captured session id — the submit flag and the file name — checked against `AO_REVIEW_WORKER_SESSION_ID`. The legacy printf shapes stay allowed so in-flight reviewers with old persisted task prompts can drain. Deny message points at the new shapes.
- Invariants kept: single submission (no chunked protocol), the body never passes through shell quoting as raw text, publication stays daemon-owned (`gh api` shape unchanged apart from `--input <file>`), resubmission stays idempotent, the hook stays deny-by-default.
- Kimchi tool policy: `bash(base64:*)` so its classifier recognizes the new segment.

`ao review submit --body <path>` / `--reviews <path>` already accept files (existing flags and tests) — the task template now actually uses that channel; `-` still works.

## Tests

- `TestReviewTextsIncludesMultiPRQueue`: pins the exact staged command lines and rejects the stale inline `--reviews -` and apostrophe-escaping shapes.
- `TestHooks_ReviewerPermissionRequestAnswersInsteadOfBlocking`: staged staging/post/submit allow cases; deny for embedded quotes, command substitution, foreign staging paths and foreign worker sessions.
- `TestReviewSubmitBatchReadsReviewsFile`: batch results from a file with apostrophes, double quotes, unicode, and newlines round-trip untouched.
- Gates: `gofmt -l backend` clean; `go test -race ./internal/cli/... ./internal/review/... ./internal/adapters/reviewer/kimchi/...` green (run locally with a scrubbed environment — the cli suite is not hermetic to an AO session's env on this base; a scrubbing fix exists on a fork and can be proposed separately).

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- opencodev2's shell policy still allowlists only the legacy shapes, so its reviewers would stall at the staging command until the reviewer tool-policy layer is reworked for the staged shapes; kiro carries its own base64-piped prompt and is unaffected.
- The model must base64-encode its own payload correctly; the emission ceiling for that is unmeasured (same honesty as #6021's unmeasured 2 KB–20 KB gap). The failure mode is a failed decode at submit time, not a silently corrupted review.

title: feat(files): add audio/video previews and fit media to panes
body:
Code changes: +123 -58  
Tests: +446 -4  
Others: +2 -1  

Includes one binary test fixture: an 11,770-byte WebM clip.

## What

Add native audio/video players in Artifacts and current workspace Files, and fit raster image/video previews to the available pane with vertical centering.

## Why

Opening a recording currently shows a binary-file placeholder. Small media also stays at its original dimensions near the top of large file tabs.

## How

Reuse the existing confined streaming routes and native playback/seek controls. Read media headers with GET and immediately cancel the body instead of applying text-file limits, and share the explicit loopback artifact URL between metadata and playback.

Workspace binary fingerprints include nanosecond file modification times from the existing stat result, so equal-size replacements refresh without restarting unchanged playback or reading the whole recording.

Streaming responses include an ETag based on file size and nanosecond modification time. Browser clients can read the header, and private, no-cache responses require revalidation; rapid artifact replacements update the media URL while native range streaming stays intact.

SVG keeps main's rendered/source views. Historical/staged audio/video and cloud-workspace media transport are outside this change; playback depends on Chromium's supported codecs.

## Testing

- Artifact regression: actual preview/files route tests failed before the fix and pass for PNG, WebM and MP3. They cover same-size rewrites one millisecond apart, size-only changes, browser-readable ETags, cache revalidation, unchanged 304s and If-Range seeking. All 34 ArtifactFileView tests passed, including ETag-only replacement refresh and uninterrupted unchanged playback.
- Workspace regression: equal-size binary rewrites change the fingerprint in untracked and scratch workspaces, including writes one millisecond apart. All 39 FileContentPane tests passed, covering replacement refresh and unchanged playback.
- Local frontend: the complete suite passed 8,304 tests across 489 files (six skipped), and both typechecks passed on Node 24.14.0.
- Local backend: Go build, vet and pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 passed; the complete final HTTP race suite passed, including controllers (101.562s). The broader backend race run completed, including SQLite (1,181.917s), chat (773.797s), session manager (294.852s) and session service (121.540s). The remaining local failure is the unchanged OpenCode v2 fixture selecting the user-installed OpenCode v1 binary; the corresponding complete CI backend suite passed. CLI and tmux full race suites passed on rerun after clearing the inherited browser capability and retrying a timing failure.
- CI: [all 23 checks passed on 02c2a28e3b](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6880/checks), including Go core/race suites, lint, API/sqlc drift, frontend unit tests, renderer smoke, both typechecks, browser integration, native macOS helpers, cross-platform/container CLI smoke and secret scan.
- Other local gaps: the earlier broad renderer smoke run encountered UI timeouts; all six media tests passed on rerun and the complete smoke suite passed in CI. Docker and native Windows validation ran in CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from main and integrated current main
- [x] One focused change; no provider issue is associated with this request
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior

title: feat(chat): add wrapping for HTML chat content
body:
Code changes: +58 -32  
Tests: +255 -4  
Others: +8 -0  

## Summary

Wide tables inside HTML chat pages can force readers to scroll horizontally. Add a default-off **Wrap content** toggle beside Expand for HTML renders and artifacts, sharing the per-page choice between inline, expanded, and external views.

title: feat(chat): give turns one ending, follow live work, redesign the plan panel
body:
Code changes: +1075 -362\
Tests: +557 -29\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Restructures how an agent turn reads in Chat. UI only; no workflow or API changes.

- **Turn header:** the divider rule under "Worked for" is gone.
- **Live turn, bottom row:** the words "Working for" are gone. The row at the end of a live turn is orb, current step, timer: `◌ Search 12s`, or just `◌ 12s` between steps. The step is named the way its own activity row names it (Search, Read file, Ran command, Thinking). The row follows the work down as it grows.
- **Live turn, work window:** tool calls and interim notes scroll inside a 240px window that follows the newest step and fades older steps out at the top edge. The reply being written stays outside the window at full size. Scrolling up or clicking inside the window stops the follow until the reader returns to the bottom.
- **Settling:** the bottom row fades where it is while `Worked for ›` opens at the top over the same beat the window folds, animating in from zero height, so the top of the turn reads as the work collapsing into its summary and nothing appears to travel. The old 440ms settle delay and label slide are removed. Copy and roll back appear only once the turn settles, in the spot the bottom row held, so nothing shifts. The live window and the streaming reply open from zero height instead of popping in.
- **Working mark:** `LatticeLoader.tsx`, a 4×4 grid of small dots with a short bright trail running clockwise round the outer twelve while the inner four rest. Pure CSS (`.chat-lattice` in `styles.css`), inked in the element's own colour so it follows the theme, and held still under reduced motion. The setup checklist's running step uses the same mark. No new dependency.
- **Provider retries:** while the provider retries, the same row shows a neutral chip, `Reconnecting… 4/5` (hairline, surface fill, muted text, small amber dot), with the reason in one muted line beneath. The chip is keyed by kind, not text, so the attempt count ticks in place instead of remounting on every attempt. Settled retry notes split the same way: the count as the label, the error as muted detail.
- **One ending per turn:** stopped, failed and recovered turns end on a status row (icon, title) followed by the same action row a finished answer uses: Retry, copy, roll back. A failed turn's provider text sits in a full-width mono block under the title, like command output. The lone undo above the outcome and the rule through it are gone.
- **Scroll follow:** a reader who nudges the view up a little while a turn streams has paused, not left: after 1.8s with no further input, while the turn is live and they are within 320px (or 40% of the viewport) of the end, the follow resumes with a glide. Scrolling further up, or opening a disclosure, never pulls them back.
- **Plan panel:** redesigned as a transparent card with a hairline border and a full-row header (icon, "Plan", count, chevron) that turns into a success tick once every step is done, naming the current step while folded. Steps use body-size text and outline marks (dashed ring, neutral turning ring, a check that draws itself in). Long plans scroll in a window that keeps the active step centred and fades its edges; the plan folds when the last step is ticked and reopens if the agent re-plans.
- **Setup checklist:** a step not yet started uses the same dashed ring as the plan.
- **Scroll fix:** when content at the end of a pinned chat shrinks on its own (a plan folding, the live window fading out), the view is restored in the same frame instead of gliding back from where the browser clamped it.

## Why

The agent response had no consistent outline: a rule under the header, actions in different places per ending, and error states that broke the layout. Long live runs pushed the reply off screen. The "Working for" label travelled from the bottom of the turn to the top when it settled. Provider retries re-rendered a warning card on every attempt, and a small upward nudge during streaming stranded the reader below the live edge. The live-activity follow and fade and the plan panel behaviour were requested product changes.

## How

- `TurnActions` (`ChatTimelineItems.tsx`) is the one action row: `AssistantMessage`, tool-only turns, and `TurnOutcome` all render it. A stopped or failed turn hands its answer's copy and undo down to the outcome's row.
- `LiveResponseStatus` is the bottom row: orb, label slot (current step / retry chip / setup label, keyed by kind), timer. `liveTaskLabel` reuses the activity rows' label derivation; `reconnectCopy` splits a retry into count and reason (Codex puts the whole error in the summary; Claude keeps the reason in `detail.text`).
- `LiveActivityWindow.tsx` wraps the live turn's work runs and reuses `hooks/useScrollFollow` (already on `main`, from #6304) for its follow. `TurnGroup` keeps the tail assistant message, the reply being streamed, outside the window.
- `edge-fade.ts` plus `.edge-fade-viewport` (`styles.css`) is a shared edge-fade mask, used by the live window and the plan.
- `ChatWorkspace`: `syncStreamedGrowth` restores `scrollTop` before paint when the observer sees a clamp; `onScroll` arms a relatch timer (`RELATCH_AFTER_MS`, `relatchBand`) on a scroll within the band that follows the reader's own wheel, touch, key or scrollbar-drag input (a marker or prompt jump never arms it), re-arms on each further scroll, and drops it past the band or on a disclosure click.
- The plan's in-progress mark used `text-accent`, a surface grey here, and pending dots were 4% white; both were effectively invisible. They're replaced as part of the redesign.

Reviewers: the scroll changes in `ChatWorkspace` (`syncStreamedGrowth`, the relatch in `onScroll`) are the only behaviour outside rendering.

Intentional omissions, found while testing and kept out of this UI-only PR:
- A chat send waits behind an in-flight composer prompt suggestion. In the daemon, the prompt-suggestion fork holds the session's controller gate, including its host cleanup. Measured 3.6–6.2 s per send. Backend; separate change.
- Claude Code sessions never feed the plan panel: in AO's launch the agent gets no to-do tool (TodoWrite/TaskCreate). The bundled ACP adapter already maps both to plan updates. Backend; separate change.

## Testing

Local, macOS, Node 22.23 (CI pins 24):
- `npm run typecheck` ✅ on the final commit; `npm run typecheck:e2e` ✅ earlier on the branch (no e2e types touched since).
- `npx vitest run` across `src/renderer/components/chat`: 41 files, 1131 tests ✅ on the final commit, except `IndependentSideChatDelivery.test.tsx`, which times out only when run while typecheck and a dev server share the CPU and passes alone (33/33) every time.
- New and updated tests cover: the one action row (retry, copy, undo; the refusal alert; no row when nothing to act on); a stopped answer handing its actions to the outcome; the live row (step label and timer; the retry chip keeping its node while the attempt count climbs; Claude's retry named in the row with the backoff beneath); the live window holding work but not the streaming reply, and no window once settled; the plan (fold/reopen, folded header naming the current step, the window centring the active step, `aria-busy`); pause-then-resume following within the band and staying put beyond it.
- Visual checks used a temporary harness that is not committed, rendering the real `ChatWorkspace` in headless Chrome in dark and light themes: live row states (step, idle, retry), the settle handoff with scroll position logged (no movement), failed and stopped endings, the plan's tick/fold/reopen, the orb at 4× against the reference, the setup checklist, narrow widths.

**Gaps, verify in CI:**
- **Renderer smoke (`test:e2e:renderer`):** couldn't be run reliably on this machine (load average about 30 during runs). In this checkout 80/88 passed; the 8 failures re-run alone gave 23/25, and the remaining `chat-composer-text-selection` drag test fails identically on unmodified `upstream/main` in this checkout while passing for both in a clean checkout, so it's environmental here.
- **Other jobs not run locally (areas untouched):** `mac-update-helper`, the cloud-client and product-ui package checks, the docs build, the browser postcondition integration.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.): pending CI, see gaps above

title: fix(report): isolate undeliverable batches from the delivery schedule
body:
Code changes: +43 -16  
Tests: +144 -15  
Others: +0 -0

## What

A report batch with no active orchestrator, a failed interruption, or a refused submission now backs off so other due batches can deliver in the same cycle. The retry delay doubles after each failure, up to 64 times the configured retry delay.

## Why

Fixes #6119. An undeliverable oldest batch kept newer reports from receiving a delivery attempt.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A project with no active orchestrator stops the delivery cycle before claiming its report | The batch records an attempt and `last_error`, backs off, and the next due project delivers in the same cycle |
| An interrupt failure releases the batch and stops the cycle | The batch backs off and the next due project delivers in the same cycle |
| A refused submission retries at a fixed delay | The delay grows through 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x, 32x and 64x, then stays at 64x |

## How

Claim failed batches and defer them with capped exponential backoff. Deferral records the failure reason and lets scheduling continue. A failed deferral or lost claim token still returns an error.

Keep claim-token fencing and stable batch identity. Preserve the fixed 30-second busy-orchestrator retry and #7435's protection against interrupting terminal orchestrators. Piggyback release behavior stays the same.

## Testing

- Local: `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/service/report` passes.
- Fail-before: the dead-project starvation, interrupt-failure isolation, and growing-backoff tests fail on main at `a8451c437ca79408e2d5029e97e802be121e44b1` and pass on this branch.
- Backoff assertions cover nine attempts: 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x, 32x, 64x, 64x, 64x. Tests check the stored failure reason and fenced-out deferrals.
- Full backend suites, storage race tests, lint, code-generation drift, Linux native CLI and fresh-install CLI checks pass in [CI run 43641006923](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/43641006923) on `f5e99c5996a888c976c7a71991156f26158cc8a2`. Public-boundary, secret-scan, and CodeRabbit checks also pass.

## Regression risk

Risk tier: NORMAL (score 0).
Could break: report scheduling, terminal report delivery, busy retry, or piggyback acceptance.
Checked: focused race tests pass for those paths, including terminal protection, refused submissions, and claim-token fencing.
Changed test expectations: the no-orchestrator test now expects durable deferral instead of an immediate error; retry assertions extend through the cap.
Regression from: none identified; the bug is present on the tested main commit.
Not verified: live daemon delivery. Full suites ran in CI.

## Related work

#6584 also addresses #6119 with fixed deferral and additional storage integration tests. #8225 changes `activeOrchestrator` to select exited agents and avoids interrupting an exited target. Those changes are outside this PR.

- [x] One focused change linked to #6119
- [x] Before / After records observable behavior
- [x] Focused regression tests fail before and pass after
- [x] CI passes for the pushed head

title: Desktop: typing lag and slow pane switching when a session has a large event history (renderer main-thread saturation)
body:
## Summary

Typing in the desktop app's prompt input lags, and switching between session panes is sometimes very slow. Evidence captured live from a running instance points to the Electron renderer's main thread being saturated by rendering large conversation event histories, compounded by concurrent streaming from multiple sessions.

## Environment

- Desktop app `0.14.3-nightly.202610161732+local`, macOS 26.7 (ARM64)
- ~15 live sessions, several actively streaming

## Evidence

**1. Renderer CPU is disproportionate to daemon load.** Over ~2h of uptime the renderer accumulated ~68 min of CPU time (≈60% of one core sustained); the daemon used ~5% in the same window. Sampling the renderer (`sample`, 5s) showed main-thread time split between JS execution and Skia font shaping (`fontations` frames on the main thread, Compositor, and thread-pool workers) — i.e., large volumes of text being re-laid-out, not I/O or daemon stalls.

**2. Lag correlates with per-session event count.** Two sessions compared from the same instance:

| | session A (small) | session B ("laggy" one) |
|---|---|---|
| provider events | 806 | 8,031 |
| of which streaming deltas | small | 7,030 (`message.delta`) |
| event payload volume | ~0.8 MB | 7.1 MB |
| tool/command activities | few | 154 (120 commands) |

Typing in a fresh/new-chat prompt (small history) was fine; switching to the session with the 10× larger event history was slow, and typing inside it lagged.

**3. Concurrent streaming multiplies the load.** In a 10-minute window, six different sessions emitted deltas concurrently (up to 517 `message.delta` from one). Globally the store held 1.76M `conversation_provider_events` (819k `reasoning.delta`, 663k `message.delta`). Every delta is a candidate UI update, so with many sessions live the renderer re-renders many times per second and keystrokes queue behind those frames.

**4. Long sessions dominate the store.** The heaviest sessions hold up to ~158k provider events each. If any view touches conversation history on activation (replay, diffing, layout), activation cost scales with event count.

## Suspected causes

- `message.delta`/`reasoning.delta` events appear to drive per-event UI updates rather than being batched (e.g., rAF-chunked flush).
- Long conversation views appear to render the full history rather than a virtualized window, making pane activation and re-layout O(event count).
- Font/text shaping cost scales with the amount of visible text, so both problems compound.

## Suggested directions

- Batch streaming deltas into one flush per animation frame instead of per-event renders.
- Virtualize long message/activity lists in the conversation view.
- Consider cheap-to-render placeholders while a heavy pane hydrates on switch.
- Optionally cap or page the delta history loaded into the view.

## Reproduction

1. Run several sessions; let one accumulate thousands of streaming deltas in a long tool-heavy run.
2. Type in a new-chat prompt (should be fine), then switch to the heavy session pane and type there.
3. Observe input lag in the heavy pane and elevated renderer CPU (~20–35% sustained) while the small-history pane stays responsive.

title: Hibernated chat worker deadlocks on SCM lifecycle notification: resume waits on the guard's own input lease (send 503, kill 409 AGENT_SWITCH_IN_PROGRESS)
body:
### What went wrong?

With chat hibernation enabled, a hibernated **chat-mode worker** that receives an SCM lifecycle notification (for example new review comments on its PR) deadlocks for 60 s on every observer cycle. While this lasts, the worker cannot be reached or killed:

- `ao send --session <id>` returns 503 after up to ~60 s: `send <id>: resume agent <id>: context deadline exceeded`
- the daemon log repeats, about every 62-63 s: `level=ERROR msg="scm observer: lifecycle notification failed" session=<id> pr=<url> err="guard <id>: send: send <id>: resume agent <id>: context deadline exceeded"`
- `ao session kill <id>` returns 409 `AGENT_SWITCH_IN_PROGRESS`, although no agent switch exists (the operation in progress is the stuck `resume`)

We saw it twice in one day on v0.13.5 (Linux, claude-code workers in chat mode). In one case the cycle lasted ~45 min (44 consecutive observer failures); in the other ~10 min. `kill` only succeeded once the retries stopped, or by chance in the ~2-3 s gap between cycles. Workers that were mid-turn (process alive, not hibernated) were never affected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable chat hibernation (in our case the web UI enables it on load when Developer mode is on).
2. Let a chat-mode worker with an open PR finish its turn and get hibernated.
3. Have a reviewer post review comments on that PR, so the SCM observer sends a lifecycle notification to the hibernated worker.
4. Observe the log line above every ~60 s, `ao send` failing with 503, and `kill` failing with `AGENT_SWITCH_IN_PROGRESS`.

### Analysis (v0.13.5 source)

1. `observe/scm/observer.go` calls `lifecycle.ApplySCMObservation`, which writes to the worker through `sessionguard.Guard.send` → `sendThen`.
2. `sendThen` acquires an input lease (`AcquireSessionInput`, `sessionguard/guard.go` ~L369, `defer release()`) and holds it across `messenger.Send` (~L417). Acquiring the first lease creates `inputDrained[id]` (`session_manager/session_input.go` ~L44).
3. For chat sessions the send goes to `Manager.send` → `sendChat` → `RelaySessionChatTurn` → `wakeHibernated` (`service/chat/hibernate.go`) → `WakeHibernatedChat` → `ResumeAgentWithMode` → `beginAgentResume` (60 s window).
4. `beginAgentOperation(resume)` waits for all input leases to drain (`session_input.go` ~L127-135, `<-m.inputDrained[id]`). The only open lease is the one held by `sendThen`, higher up in the same call stack, which is released only after the send returns. Result: deadlock until the context deadline.
5. The observer retries on the next cycle, so the `resume` operation is held ~60 s of every ~63 s. The API `/send` path does not hold a lease, but it joins the in-flight wake (`hibernate.go`, `case <-run.done`) and inherits its error. `Kill` sees the active operation and returns `errAgentOperationInProgress`, which is mapped to `ErrSwitchInProgress` (`manager.go` ~L2384, `service/session/service.go` ~L1343).

The relevant code in v0.14.2 and current `main` looks unchanged.

### Suggested fix (untested)

- Do not acquire the pane-input lease for chat-mode sessions (they have no pane to write to), or release it before waking a hibernated chat.
- Map `errAgentOperationInProgress` in `Kill` to a message that names the actual operation (e.g. "resume in progress"), instead of `AGENT_SWITCH_IN_PROGRESS`.

### Workaround

Disable chat hibernation: `PATCH /api/v1/settings/chat-hibernation` with `{"enabled":false}`, and turn off Developer mode in the UI so it is not re-enabled on load.

### Environment

AO v0.13.5 (daemon), Linux, workers on claude-code in chat mode. Possibly related, different symptom: #6700, #6870 (`context deadline exceeded` on resume after TUI-to-chat switch).

title: fix: retain Codex completion until durable projection
body:
Code changes: +1581 -210  
Tests: +3875 -32  
Others: +94 -0  

## What

Prevent a completed Codex turn from leaving AO busy with later messages permanently queued. The original update/restart failure and a separate five-second queue-saturation loss both reproduce locally.

## How

The AO-owned Codex host journals conversation notifications before delivery and retains the turn until AO acknowledges successful SQLite projection. Stable source-frame and derived-event IDs make replay idempotent even if commit succeeds but its acknowledgement is lost. All events derived from one frame commit before its single receipt is acknowledged; database failure or controller-generation fencing detaches without discarding pending delivery.

A dedicated host writer keeps replay from blocking acknowledgements. Hosted adapters apply cancellation-aware backpressure instead of dropping queued output. Retained turn prefixes rebuild within-turn citation/retry state, while host thread facts exclude proven child turns from root ownership; unknown work keeps its busy gate.

This reuses the existing provider acknowledgement and journal seams, adds no dependency, database migration, public API or frontend protocol, and keeps the history reconciliation fallback for legacy raw-host live attachments. Fresh native resumes retain their existing history-import path. Startup verification continues to use the existing connecting presentation.

### Delivery boundary

The host protects daemon replacement while the same native provider/host survives. It does not add upstream Codex protocol ACKs or promise recovery of this journal after host death/power loss. Retained output is bounded at 256 MiB; quota exhaustion fails explicitly instead of silently evicting events. Account/auth/capacity traffic is excluded from the conversation journal.

## Reuse and local T3 comparison

Codex now uses the existing ACP/raw host attachment reader, provider forwarding, error handling and detach paths. Its adapter also uses the existing `ChatProviderEventAcknowledger(ProviderEventID)` contract: only the last semantic event from a source frame maps to that frame's host receipt. The shared event model no longer needs `ProviderReceiptID`. Thread/turn ownership uses native pair keys instead of encoded strings. Retention, replay activation, separate ordered output, stable IDs and per-frame ACK validation remain unchanged.

Compared the clean local T3 source checkout at `c77a7b7eeb` (server `0.0.45`), including its [production runtime wiring](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/c77a7b7eebd6ea8a3a63bbcaaa7c1707fe65c86e/apps/server/src/server.ts#L483): [completion handling](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/c77a7b7eebd6ea8a3a63bbcaaa7c1707fe65c86e/apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters/CodexAdapterV2.ts#L5972) enqueues normalized events in memory; [ingestion](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/c77a7b7eebd6ea8a3a63bbcaaa7c1707fe65c86e/apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/RunExecutionService.ts#L1208) commits downstream. Its [event sink](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/c77a7b7eebd6ea8a3a63bbcaaa7c1707fe65c86e/apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EventSink.ts#L240) publishes after transaction commit, and [command commits](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/c77a7b7eebd6ea8a3a63bbcaaa7c1707fe65c86e/apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EventSink.ts#L527) include projections, receipts and the effect outbox atomically. Its [startup recovery](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/c77a7b7eebd6ea8a3a63bbcaaa7c1707fe65c86e/apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts#L300) settles abandoned runs and can schedule a new continuation. This inspected path has no producer source-frame ACK tied to SQLite ingestion, so its memory-queue design cannot replace AO's retained delivery without weakening the guarantee. AO already reuses its existing transactional event archive/projection; no T3 code, dependency, outbox or schema is added.

## Holistic follow-up review

The follow-up review found and reproduced three additional boundaries in this delivery path:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |

## Review regression: committed completion with a lost ACK

[The review finding](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6889#discussion_r4315478010) is real. On `665d377`, the exact failure sequence is:

1. AO accepts a follow-up into its durable queue while the original turn runs.
2. SQLite commits the original `turn.completed`.
3. The provider ACK socket fails before `afterProject` can mark Idle and release queued work.
4. Replacement attachment deduplicates that saved completion; no post-projection effect runs.
5. The original answer is saved, but the follow-up stays queued indefinitely.

The existing actual-host fixture called `DrainQueued` explicitly after reconnect, hiding this gap. That call is removed; the regression now requires recovery without it. The service/SQLite regression fails on the previous production source, and the actual-host commit/ACK-loss case also fails without the manual drain.

| Before: `665d377` | After: `c2b3ee8` |
| --- | --- |
| Real Electron app remains **Working** with one preaccepted queued message after ordinary Resume. | The **same queued turn** automatically starts and completes once when the fixed daemon reconnects; tab is **Idle**. |
| Resume has already acknowledged the original completion, leaving an empty host journal. | Recovery also works without a replayed completion: it reads committed facts before consuming new events. |
| Queue release depends on an in-memory post-ACK callback. | Shared live reconnect uses the existing `afterProject` / serialized drain path after checking the latest primary turn and current owner generation. |

[Native before/after screenshots and evidence](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6889#issuecomment-6272420686): real Codex `0.162.1`, synthetic session `standalone-2`, same host `92421` and Codex `92422`. Original completion remains `16:36:16Z`; the previously queued turn completes at `16:44:57Z`. Both answers and both terminal archive records occur exactly once. No Send or Drain API call triggers the fixed recovery, and no database rows are hand-edited.

The native fault was injected with a one-shot local JSONL proxy: briefly hold only the scratch database's writer lock, deliver the completed native frame, reset the daemon attachment, then release the lock. SQLite saves completion after the socket is gone. Ordinary Resume on the old binary reproduces the stuck queue; starting the fixed binary recovers that existing queue. The proxy restores the scratch host descriptor's address and leaves its credential unchanged.

The normal path remains **commit → ACK → post-projection effects**; ACP requires ACK before accepting its next prompt. Recovery only runs for a verified live attachment with no active/pending turn, compaction, pending interaction, Close, Stop or handoff. It rechecks admission after database reads and uses the existing controller-generation fencing. A read failure preserves the host and stops recovery rather than declaring it idle.

The latest primary turn is ordered by the existing provider archive, not turn-row creation order: queued messages can be reordered. One small `turn.dispatching` record is saved through the existing transactional projection before provider preparation/send, including deferred ACP preparation. This prevents a newer failed or unbound dispatch from being hidden by an older completed turn. No schema, outbox, dependency or additional ACK protocol is added. Tests cover replay and suppressed replay, reordered queues, later bound/unbound failures, deferred preparation failure, child turns, stale owners/branches, pending interactions and actual Stop/Close during the database read.

title: fix(autohand): deliver AO role prompts on the session-start hook
body:
Code changes: +22 -7
Tests: +86 -0
Others: +0 -0

Slice of #6752 — Autohand role prompts on the session-start hook.

## What changed after review

Both review comments were correct, and I verified each against the upstream sources you linked before changing anything.

### 1. Autohand: wrong response shape (your second comment)

Confirmed against `HookManager.parseHookResponse` (`JSON.parse(trimmed) as HookResponse`) and `HookResponse` in `src/types.ts`:

```ts
export interface HookResponse {
  decision?: 'allow' | 'deny' | 'ask' | 'block';
  ...
  /** Additional context to add to conversation */
  additionalContext?: string;
}
```

Autohand is a flat `JSON.parse` of stdout with no `hookSpecificOutput` envelope, so AO's nested shape was silently dropped. Autohand now shares OpenHands' top-level branch, and `openHandsContextHookOutput` is renamed `topLevelContextHookOutput` since it no longer serves one harness. `TestHooks_AutohandSessionStartInjectsTopLevelSystemPromptContext` asserts the top-level field is populated **and** that `hookSpecificOutput` is absent, so a regression back to the nested shape fails the test.

This also confirms the fix reaches the reported case: `HookContext.sessionType` is `'startup' | 'resume' | 'clear'`, AO installs the hook with no `matcher`, so it fires on `autohand resume` too — which is where `--sys-prompt` is unavailable.

### 2. Kimi: dropped from this PR (your first comment)

Confirmed against both sources. `runHook.ts` parses only:

```ts
const HookJsonOutputSchema = z.looseObject({
  message: OptionalStringSchema,
  hookSpecificOutput: HookSpecificOutputSchema,  // { message, permissionDecision, permissionDecisionReason }
});
```

and `SessionExternalHooksService.triggerSessionStart` is `Promise<void>` — it awaits `this.runner.trigger('SessionStart', ...)` and returns nothing. There is no field in that schema that reaches Kimi's model context, and the result is discarded anyway, so AO cannot inject standing instructions through a Kimi `SessionStart` hook at all. My change would have printed the asserted JSON while both fresh and restored Kimi sessions still received no instructions — exactly the "tests validate AO's emitted JSON, neither consumer accepts it" failure you described.

Kimi is therefore removed from this PR entirely, including the `systemPromptFileRequired` entry. Kimi has no working context channel in AO today: `.kimi/AGENTS.md` is not read by the current loader, and the hook channel is dead upstream. I traced its `sessionAgentProfileCatalog` but stopped short of guessing at the on-disk profile shape, since a wrong guess is another no-op. Kimi needs its own investigation — I'll track it separately rather than ship another unverified change.

## What the PR now does

`autohand/hooks.go:113-118` already installs `{Event: "session-start", Subcommand: "session-start"}` into `~/.autohand/config.json`. `shouldEmitSessionStartContext` now serves it. Nothing else changes: no adapter argv, no hook schema, no new event name.

`systemPromptFileRequired` gains Autohand. The hook reads `<dataDir>/prompts/<session>/system.md`, so a silent write failure would drop the role prompt rather than degrade to a fallback this CLI does not accept — matching gemini, agy, command-code, devin and openhands.

## Verification

```text
$ go build ./...
$ go test ./internal/cli/ -run "TestHooks_" -count=1
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/cli	19.056s

$ go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run "TestSystemPromptFileRequired" -count=1 -v
--- PASS: TestSystemPromptFileRequiredCoversHookDeliveredHarnesses (0.00s)

$ go test ./internal/adapters/agent/autohand/... ./internal/adapters/reviewer/autohand/... -count=1
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/autohand	1.838s
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/autohand	1.171s
```

New tests:

- `TestHooks_AutohandSessionStartInjectsTopLevelSystemPromptContext` — the exact flat contract, with an explicit negative assertion on `hookSpecificOutput`.
- `TestHooks_AutohandSessionStartWithoutSystemPromptFileStaysSilent` — a missing `system.md` must not emit an empty context block.

`golangci-lint` on `./internal/cli/... ./internal/session_manager/...` reports the same 19 pre-existing issues as on a clean `canonical/main` checkout, none in the files this PR touches. The 13 `session_manager` and 2 `kimi` package failures on this Windows machine are also identical with the change stashed.

## Intentional omissions

- **No live `autohand` run.** Autohand is not installed here. The wire contract is taken from the upstream source at commit `3b840ca` that you cited, not from a live session — the same basis as your own review, so a maintainer with Autohand installed would still be the one to confirm end to end.
- **Kimi is out of scope** for the reason above. Cursor and Copilot CLI are in the companion PR (#6896).
- **AGY and Command Code remain unaddressed**, as in the earlier note.

title: fix(cursor,copilot): make AO's generated instruction file actually load
body:
Code changes: +182 -13
Tests: +271 -1
Others: +0 -0

Slice of #6752 — Cursor and GitHub Copilot CLI role prompts.

Both harnesses deliver AO's role prompt through a file AO writes into the session worktree. In both cases the file could exist and still never reach the agent. Same root cause, same fix shape: make the generated file authoritative.

## Cursor — Terminal UI, fresh start and resume

`cursor.go` already documented that Cursor has no inline or file system-prompt flag and reads workspace rule files (`AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules`, `CLAUDE.md`) — then delivered nothing at all. Every managed Cursor session started with no AO role prompt.

`GetAgentHooks` now installs an always-applied rule:

```text
.cursor/rules/ao-agent-orchestrator.mdc
---
description: Agent Orchestrator standing instructions for this managed session
alwaysApply: true
---

<!-- agent-orchestrator: managed cursor standing instructions -->

<AO standing instructions>
```

That frontmatter is not new guesswork: `chatdriver/cursoracp` already ships the identical `.mdc` shape and Cursor already loads it from AO's plugin directory on the Chat path. The Terminal UI path simply never wrote one.

`prepareWorkspace` calls `GetAgentHooks` before every launch *and* every restore, and the rule lives in the worktree, so both fresh start and `--resume` are covered. The rule is gitignored via `hookutil.EnsureWorkspaceGitignore` so it never becomes the untracked file that blocks `git worktree remove`. A non-AO file at the generated path is refused with an actionable error rather than overwritten — the same choice the Crush adapter makes for its generated context file. `UninstallHooks` removes the rule only when it carries AO's marker.

Cursor is deliberately **not** added to `systemPromptFileRequired`: unlike the hook-delivered harnesses, this path resolves the instructions from the file *or* the inline text, so an unwritable prompt file degrades cleanly to inline instead of failing the launch.

## GitHub Copilot CLI — Terminal UI, name collision

`installCopilotAgent` silently returned without writing when a non-AO file already occupied the generated path:

```go
if err == nil && !strings.Contains(string(existing), hookutil.CopilotAgentProfileSentinel) {
    return nil
}
```

But `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` still passed `--agent=ao-<session>`, and that is exactly the path Copilot resolves. The session ran the **project's** agent with no AO role prompt at all — the case the issue reports.

The name is now resolved from the workspace in one place, so install, launch, restore and Chat all agree:

```text
.github/agents/ao-<session>.agent.md                  # free path, unchanged behavior
.github/agents/ao-<session>-<8 hex of workspace path> # a foreign file owns the base name
```

The resolution is deterministic, so a restore re-selects the profile AO actually wrote. The residual case — a foreign file that also owns the digest name, 8 hex chars of a path hash — now returns an error instead of skipping silently.

## Verification

```text
$ go build ./...
$ go test ./internal/adapters/agent/cursor/... -count=1
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor	2.239s

$ go test ./internal/adapters/agent/copilot/... ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/copilotacp/... -count=1
--- FAIL: TestEnsureWorkspaceTrustedCreatesConfig (0.01s)
    trust_test.go:23: read config: open ...\.copilot\config.json: The system cannot find the path specified.
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/copilotacp	2.116s
```

New tests:

| Test | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `TestGetAgentHooksInstallsStandingRule` | rule written with `alwaysApply: true`, AO marker and the instructions; idempotent on re-install; gitignored |
| `TestGetAgentHooksReadsStandingInstructionsFromThePromptFile` | prompt-file path, not just inline |
| `TestGetAgentHooksWithoutStandingInstructionsWritesNoRule` | no prompt, no file |
| `TestGetAgentHooksRefusesToOverwriteAForeignRule` | user rule is byte-identical after the refusal |
| `TestUninstallHooksRemovesOnlyTheAOManagedStandingRule` | AO's rule is removed, a user rule is not |
| `TestCopilotAgentNameIsStableAndSharedByLaunchAndRestore` | install writes the profile; launch *and* restore select that same name |
| `TestCopilotAgentNameIgnoresAForeignFileWhenNoneExists` | the common, uncollided case is unchanged |
| `TestLaunchSessionOptionsMovesAsideWhenProjectOwnsTheProfileName` | the Chat/ACP path disambiguates too |

`TestInstallAgentProfilePreservesUserOwnedProfile` already covered the collision; it is extended to assert AO now installs its own profile *as well* as preserving the project's file.

`golangci-lint run` on the three touched packages reports only `cursor/install.go` and `copilot/install.go` goimports findings. Neither file is in this diff; both are pre-existing CRLF artifacts of this Windows checkout.

### Pre-existing failures on this Windows machine, not caused by this PR

`TestEnsureWorkspaceTrustedCreatesConfig` (copilot), `TestVersionProbeUsesStandardInstallerSymlinkWithoutLaunchingCLI` (cursoracp), `TestCrushLocalAuthStatusDoesNotUseProviderCatalog` (crush), and 13 `session_manager` / `review` / `reviewer` failures. I confirmed the identical failure set with this change stashed, so they are environmental (POSIX file modes, hardcoded `/` in paths, symlinks) and untouched here.

## Intentional omissions

- **No live harness run.** `cursor-agent` and `copilot` are not installed on this machine, so the end-to-end behavior — that `cursor-agent` TUI reads `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` on a fresh launch and on `--resume`, and that Copilot honors the disambiguated `--agent=` value — is not verified against a real binary. The `.mdc` shape is copied from a Cursor path AO already ships and Cursor already loads; the Copilot change only alters which profile name is selected, not how Copilot resolves `--agent`.
- **No `docs/harnesses/` page.** Neither harness has one today, so there was nothing to bring up to date. Writing them is separate work and would need a `docs/README.md` row.
- **The remaining #6752 harnesses.** Kimi and Autohand are in the companion PR. AGY and Command Code are deliberately excluded: AGY's managed hook registers only `PreInvocation`/`PostToolUse`/`Stop`, and adding an unverified `SessionStart` key risks AGY rejecting the whole hook file and regressing Kanban activity tracking (#4085); Command Code's plan-mode gap needs a live `cmd` in plan mode to diagnose.

title: fix(models): show cached catalogs while refreshing in background
body:
Code changes: +152 -60  
Tests: +369 -23  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keep model pickers visible while the daemon reads or refreshes its catalog. Restore a saved frontend catalog immediately, read the backend DB catalog before session-history enrichment, and update the choices in place. The shared renderer covers Windows and macOS.

## Why

New Task and project model settings showed a blocking "Loading models" placeholder even when a catalog was already cached in the daemon.

## How

- Persist advisory frontend snapshots by host, agent, and project; keep at most 10 snapshots within a 1 MiB budget, evicting the least recently written entries. Hydrate synchronously and re-read the daemon in the background. The daemon DB remains authoritative.
- Keep cached models visible after read failures, retain recency for surviving models while history is pending, clear saved catalogs after login changes, and prevent late DB or recency responses from overwriting newer refresh results in memory or saved storage.
- Cancel task and inactive catalog reads on login invalidation, and discard aborted responses before publishing or persisting them.
- Respect the ten-minute validation window for fresh in-memory catalogs on remount; restored snapshots still revalidate immediately after app restart.
- Remove blocking model loaders and the unused shared model loading property. With no saved catalog, the picker stays visible and fills when its DB response arrives.

## Testing

- Current PR head renderer suite: 386 files passed, 6,375 tests passed, 6 skipped. Before the recency follow-up, the complete Windows frontend run had 8,212 tests pass, 181 fail in 23 platform-dependent files, and 7 skip; no renderer file failed.
- Full frontend TypeScript check passed on the current PR head (Node 24, 6 GiB heap); strict checking of the changed files also passed.
