title: [Bug]: Claude Code sessions never get a to-do tool, so the plan panel is always empty for Claude
body:
### What went wrong?

Claude Code chat sessions never show the plan (to-do) panel, because the agent has no to-do tool to call in AO's launch of it. Codex and Cursor sessions get the panel; Claude sessions never do, even when the user asks for a to-do list in so many words.

**Repro** (AO desktop from `main`, Claude Code 2.1.296 via the bundled `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0):

1. Open a Claude Code chat session.
2. Send: *"Use your to-do list tool for this. Create a to-do list with these 10 items, then work through them one at a time, marking each in progress and completed."* (any 10 trivial read-only steps).
3. Watch the turn.

**What happens**

- The agent runs `ToolSearch` for `todo list task create update` (three times in one turn) and gets back unrelated tools (Docs, Drive, Cron); no `TodoWrite`, `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate` or `TaskList`.
- It then falls back to narrating in prose: `[done] 5. … [in progress] 6. …`, and on a second run says outright: *"I still don't have a to-do list tool. I looked for TodoWrite, TaskCreate and TaskUpdate and none exist in this session."*
- `conversation_turns.plan_json` stays empty for the turn, so the chat's plan panel has nothing to render.

**What should happen**

Claude Code has a to-do tool available (`TodoWrite`, or the newer `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`), its calls reach AO as plan updates, `plan_json` fills in, and the plan panel renders and ticks along like it does for Codex.

**What's already in place**

- The bundled adapter maps both `TodoWrite` and `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskList` to ACP `plan` session updates (`frontend/resources/acp-runtime/node_modules/@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp/dist/acp-agent.js` around lines 1078 and 6560; `dist/tools.js` `case "TodoWrite"` / `applyTaskCreate`).
- AO turns an ACP `plan` update into `ChatEventPlanUpdated` (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/client.go:694`), which is what the panel reads.

So the missing piece is only that the agent process never has the tool.

**Observed launch**

The `claude` child is started as `claude --output-format stream-json --verbose --input-format stream-json --permission-prompt-tool stdio --tools default --mcp-config …` with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-ts`. AO's `claudeacp` driver sets no tool-related flags of its own; the flags come from the adapter/SDK. Claude Code 2.1.296 gates these tools behind `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS` (on unless explicitly `false`) and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS`.

**Things to check for the fix**

- Whether the adapter or SDK passes `disallowedTools`/`allowedTools` that drop the to-do tools, or whether `--tools default` excludes them under the SDK entrypoint.
- Whether `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS` needs to be set for SDK sessions, and whether the SDK sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=false`.
- Whether the deferred tool catalog (what `ToolSearch` can find) simply omits `Task*` tools in SDK mode.

A small headless run that prints the agent's `init` tool list would settle it. A Go test around the launch env/options would keep it from regressing.

**Impact**

Every Claude Code session in AO: no plan panel, and no way for the agent to track multi-step work the way the other harnesses do. The UI work on the panel itself (#6884) is independent of this.

title: fix(cloud): feedback round: live Setup/Cleanup logs, PR opener, error idle, auto-mode dialog, and bugs
body:
## Summary

Tests : 20,541 LOC


This PR fixes the feedback from 11x and our own prod testing after #6828: the PR author, Setup failure logging, a wrong label, an unpinned Save button, copyable variables, and six bugs. Each fix has a root cause and tests, and every fix was verified live on staging on Coder (11x-style template) and Freestyle, with Claude and Codex.

| # | Problem | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The PR sidebar names the bot (`ao-by-untrivial`) instead of the person | AO's GitHub App opens every cloud PR, so GitHub records the bot as author | The sidebar shows "**<person> via AO**": the creator of the session that opened that PR, with their GitHub login and avatar when they have connected GitHub. On GitHub the App still opens the PR, exactly as today. Only org members see the name; share-link viewers see the plain author. Only the AO App's own account counts, so a claimed dependabot PR keeps its author. |
| 2 | Setup or Cleanup fails and nobody can tell why (hackmad) | A failed step reported only its number, exit code and an output tail; the full output was never kept | A failed step now reports its command, folder, the Linux user and groups it ran as, and the path of its full log (`<data>/setup-logs/step-N.log`, mode 0600, 4 MiB cap per step). It adds a hint for the common cases: Docker socket, sudo, permission denied, SSH key, command not found. The command is redacted before it is shown. The error card and the chat setup row show the same details. |
| 3 | The review switcher labels the main repo "repository" | It showed the checkout folder name, which is always `repository` on Coder and Freestyle | The worker sends the main repo's real name as `label`. |
| 4 | The Save button on the Scripts page scrolls out of view | Save sat in a plain row at the end of the form | The pinned Save bar from Repositories/Instructions is now one shared `SettingsSaveFooter`, used by Scripts too. |
| 5 | Variable names can't be copied without typos | The app sets `user-select: none` everywhere | The variables list is selectable, and each name has a copy button. Setup and Cleanup also get `$AO_REPOS_ROOT` (the folder that holds every checkout). It is listed only for multi-repo projects. |
| 6 | A Codex terminal stays "working" after a turn fails (usage limit, unsupported model, expired login) | Codex only fires its Stop hook when a turn succeeds, and has no error hook. Claude fires `StopFailure`, which AO never installed. | The worker follows the terminal's Codex session log and treats a turn that ended on an error as a stop. It writes the same stop proof, dated when the turn ended, so the session goes idle within about 2 s and "Finish work, then switch" completes. It reads only what is appended after it starts, so a resumed terminal never replays old failures. It follows the resumed conversation even when that conversation started in Chat. Claude gets the `StopFailure` hook. A failed turn is also checkpointed. |
| 7 | A bad `--branch` in a full org gets the quota error | Create checked the sandbox quota before the branch | The branch is validated first, on every create path. |
| 8 | `ao kill` / `ao send` on a session the orchestrator didn't spawn says "You do not have access to this organization" | A generic forbidden mapped to the org-access message | It now returns 404 `not_orchestrator_child`: "That session is not one this orchestrator started. An orchestrator can only kill or message the sessions it spawned." An unknown session, another org's session and a non-child all get the same 404, so it reveals nothing. Killing your own child that has no sandbox left now succeeds. |
| 9 | Agent-browser requests return 502 (77 of 103 on prod, 1488 of 1676 on staging in 48 h) | Coder images don't have the browser yet (the shared template was never rebaked after #6652), so there is never a relay | With no browser connected the CP answers 409 `AGENT_BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After: 30`, and the desktop waits that out per session. A connected relay that fails still returns 502. |

Example of the new Setup failure, captured on staging (Coder, `ls /root`; hint wording updated afterwards in a1081f504):
```
Setup step 3 failed: exit status 2. This step ran as ubuntu, which was refused access to a file or directory:
check that ubuntu owns or can write the path in the step's output. Fix the project's Setup script
(Project settings > Scripts), then reopen this session to retry.

Step 3: ls /root
Ran as ubuntu (groups: ubuntu adm cdrom sudo dip lxd docker) in /home/ubuntu/repository
Full output: /home/ubuntu/.ao/worker/setup-logs/step-3.log

ls: cannot open directory '/root': Permission denied
```

## Added after the first review round

### Live Setup and Cleanup logs (self-serve, for 11x)
Customers can now see what their scripts are doing without asking us for logs.
- **Live step panel:** while Setup runs, each step shows its status, command, repo, duration and live output. It uses GitHub Actions-style chevron rows that expand, with selectable output and a copy button. The running step and failed steps open by default.
- **Where it shows:** in the chat timeline, in the terminal "Preparing your repository and agent" screen, as collapsed "Setup"/"Cleanup" sections in the Summary sidebar, and on the startup failure card.
- **Worker:** publishes `workspace.script.step` events. It sends only complete lines, every 2 s (every 5 s after two minutes), with a 16 KiB redacted tail per step. Earlier `running` rows are deleted when a step's final event lands. Final events are sent on a detached, bounded context, and a step is never slowed by publishing.
- **Cleanup on delete:**
  - Now runs on Freestyle and Docker as well as Coder (Freestyle and Docker never ran Cleanup before).
  - Results are parsed per step and stored on the deleted session.
  - Freestyle resumes a paused VM, stops the session's worker and agent processes, then runs the hook as `ao-worker` (never root) in a background exec that keeps the 10-minute budget.
  - At most 4 runs per provider and 2 per org at a time. A VM paused for billing is skipped with a reason.
  - A Cleanup the provider could not run shows each step as skipped with the reason.
- **Secrets:**
  - One redactor is shared by Setup and Cleanup, on both the worker and the CP. It masks `NAME=value`, `NAME: value` and JSON values for secret-looking names, plus token shapes (GitHub, OpenAI, Slack, AWS, npm, Google, SendGrid, GitLab, JWTs and private key blocks).
  - Script output is returned to org members only; share-link grantees get the step list with `outputHidden: true`.
  - **Redaction hardening.** Values a step assigns to secret-named variables are masked even when printed bare. Multi-line commands are redacted before they are flattened. Password flags are matched only for commands that take a password and per shell segment (quote-aware), so `ssh -p 22` and `docker run -p 8080:80` stay visible.
  - **Covered shapes:** `curl -u`, tokens as URL users, Azure SAS `sig=`, Kubernetes Secret data, YAML block scalars, JSON argument lists, `hf_` and `rk_live_` tokens, and colour codes between a name and its value.
  - **Installed Cleanup commands.** The Cleanup commands a worker was given are stored in `bootstrap_context.installedCleanup` (no migration), so Cleanup output stays masked even after the project's scripts change.
  - **Tests.** 79 leak cases run through all 10 output paths, plus a linear-time test.
  - A `types=` filter on `chat-events` lets the desktop fetch only script events.

### More fixes
- **Claude's "Make auto mode your default permission mode?" dialog** (Claude Code 2.1.287+) swallowed AO's injected messages. Enter picked "Yes" and switched the session to auto mode.
  - Cloud marks the dialog seen in AO's own config.
  - Local passes a per-session `--settings` for explicit modes. For AO's default mode, it marks the dialog seen only when the user's settings would trigger it, in the directory Claude actually reads (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` aware).
- **Local desktop: a Claude or Codex terminal turn that fails no longer stays "working".**
  - Claude: AO installs the `StopFailure` hook.
  - Codex: a watcher reads the session's rollout file and only queries live Codex terminal sessions. It reports each failure once and ignores records without a readable timestamp.
- **"Finish work, then switch" through the API could wait forever.** If no turn is running and the worker can't prove the terminal idle, the drain now ends after 30 s with `SOURCE_DRAIN_FAILED`, and the desktop shows a short notice.
- **"Model choices unavailable" after deleting and restoring a session:** models now reload for the restored worker. Resuming a deleted session returns 409 `SESSION_TERMINATED` ("This session was deleted. Restore it to continue.").
- **Failed Coder builds** (e.g. `VcpuLimitExceeded`) used to leave sessions on "provisioning" for up to 25 min, and Retry started no new build.
  - A failed or canceled build now parks the session with `workspace_build_failed`. On a BYO workspace the message is the redacted Coder `Error:` line. On AO-managed compute it is only the cloud error code, so AO's infrastructure stays hidden.
  - Retry starts exactly one new build. Each failed build is acted on once, keyed by build ID in `bootstrap_context` (no migration).
  - AO never starts a build on its own, and never on a customer's BYO workspace. A parked session stays parked on wake, but AO-managed compute that was restarted is still stopped.
  - A workspace that can never be created now parks with `workspace_create_failed` after the startup budget.
- **Esc in a terminal turn now ends it within about 2 s, cloud and local, Claude and Codex.**
  - Claude fires no hook on Esc and Codex 0.147 has no Interrupt hook. Both write the interrupt to their transcript, which AO now follows.
  - The Claude transcript is followed by the terminal's own conversation, including across `/clear` and `/resume`.
  - An interrupt older than the latest prompt is ignored, and a typed marker or terminal replies never count.
  - Locally, hooks are applied only from the session's own Claude process.
  - Before this, a message sent after Esc waited for a 5-minute fallback.
- **Chat switch after an Esc-interrupted Claude turn.** The local checkpoint treated the interrupted turn as unfinished forever, so the session could never switch to Chat. The interrupt marker now settles that turn; a turn that is genuinely still running is still refused.
- **Archive or restore of a Chat-mode session** no longer leaves a stuck "Connecting your terminal" loader.
- **A session created elsewhere** (for example via the API) now connects on first open.
- **A project created elsewhere** shows in the sidebar without a reload.
- **The startup card's "Copied"** resets after 2 s and never carries over to another session.
- **A retried Setup that failed again** left the failure card on "Retrying...". The CP now refreshes `startupError.at` on every failure, and the card also leaves the retrying state when the retry's run ends.

## Added for the second 11x feedback round

- **Repo picker no longer closes Settings.** Picking a repo in the project settings popover kept the dialog open. Project rename via General, Name works and is covered by a test.
- **Readable Coder workspace names, at creation only.** Orchestrators are `<prefix>-o-<id12>` and workers `<prefix>-w-<first word of the task>-<id12>`, with one retry on a name clash. Existing workspaces and chats are never renamed. Behind `AO_CLOUD_CODER_READABLE_NAMES` (on in staging, off in prod for now).
- **Per-step time limits for Setup and Cleanup**, 1 to 120 minutes, default 10. Stored as a leading `# ao-timeout: Nm` line in the step, so no migration. The Cleanup budget is the sum of its steps (capped at 2 h). A small "No output for 3 minutes" banner shows on a running step. Local has the same limits, and a local worker spawn is no longer cut at the daemon's 60 s request limit.
- **Cloud follows the global Default session interface**, like local, for Claude and Codex. Orchestrators start in Chat when the harness supports it. The worker installs `claude-agent-acp` itself, so no image change is needed. A session that cannot start in Chat falls back to the terminal with a quiet notice.
- **Chat honors trusted and standard mode.** A trusted Claude Chat session no longer asks before every command: a turn without its own choice follows the session mode, the same way the terminal does. The composer's starting choice follows it too.
- **Template options:** clearer labels and a warning when the template already clones the repo (duplicate checkout).
- **ao-worker working folder:** in ao-worker mode AO's checkout lives at `~/work/<repo>` and nothing is cloned into `~/repository`. A folder that is not durable, or already used by someone else, is refused with a clear message and Cleanup is skipped there. Behind `AO_CLOUD_CODER_WORKER_WORKING_FOLDER` (on in staging, off in prod for now).
- **Fair Cleanup slots:** 16 at once overall, 2 per org.
- **UX polish from the staging UI pass:** "+ Add a repository" opens its picker right away and an unpicked row goes away; a backdrop click with a picker open closes only the picker; the save bar error stays on the Save row; the duplicate-clone notice is a muted heads-up; content stays clear of the harness update notice; a session's start Setup shows above its first prompt in Chat.
- **Status while Setup runs:** the session reads as working (API, sidebar, board) while a Setup step runs on a connected worker. Only the read changes; idle pause and message delivery are untouched.

**Verified on staging `:290`:** trusted Claude Chat runs `whoami`, file writes and `curl` with 0 approval prompts on Freestyle and Coder; standard mode prompts for `curl` only; an explicit "default" choice still prompts; Codex trusted Chat unchanged. Setup reads working for the whole run and idle after, a failed step does not stay working. All picker, save bar, notice and Setup-order checks pass in the desktop app. Locally, a 75 s Setup step with a 2 minute limit now succeeds on a stock daemon (it used to die at 60 s).

Items 8 (task button tooltip) and 9 (Branch field in New Task) are waiting on 11x and are not in this PR.

## Not in this PR (on purpose)
- **Opening PRs as the user on GitHub.** We built it and then removed it. Anyone who can prompt a session (a teammate, or a prompt injection) would open PRs under the creator's GitHub identity, and creators could no longer approve their own PRs. That needs its own product decision.
- **Rebaking the managed Coder image with the agent browser.** The template is shared by staging and prod, so it needs a planned window. Bring-your-own Coder templates need an optional browser install, which we will document.

## Compatibility
- **New CP, old worker:** unchanged behavior.
- **New worker, old CP:** an old CP rejects the new `stop-failure` activity event (400). The stop proof is written on the worker first, so the Chat switch still unblocks, and the session shows idle once the CP is updated. The new Setup fields are dropped.
- **No migrations.** Rollback is a plain task-definition switch.
- `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` gains the Setup failure fields, `stop-failure`, `openedBy` (`PullRequestOpener`) and `WorkspaceRepository.label`, and `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated.

## Tests
- **Cloud:**
  - `gofmt` and `go vet ./...` are clean, and `GOWORK=off go build ./...` passes.
  - `go test -race` passes for httpapi, worker, workertransport, workerexec, githubapp and `cmd/...`.
  - Postgres tests ran on postgres:16. The new tests pass: opener lookup, members-only, per-PR session, branch before quota, non-child kill. 4 other tests fail the same way on main (`TestCIFailureNotification...`, `TestQueuedTurn...`, `TestReviewsSnapshot...`, `TestDisconnectSettles...`).
  - New tests for the Codex watcher:
    - an old failure plus a new `task_started` does not stop;
    - the stop proof uses the turn's own timestamp;
    - a Chat-then-terminal thread is followed;
    - a record over 4 MiB is skipped;
    - a failed turn triggers a checkpoint.
- **Desktop:** `tsc` is clean, vitest passes (41 files, 698 tests, including i18n coverage), and the new strings are in all 8 locales.
- **Reviews:** an adversarial review of the combined diff found 4 majors and several minors, all fixed here.

## Verified live on staging (`:276`, this branch)

| Check | Coder (11x-style template) | Freestyle |
|---|---|---|
| "Pritom Mazumdar via AO" in the API and sidebar; GitHub author still `app/aoagentsdev123` | Pass | Pass |
| Setup failure: step, command, user, groups, folder, log path (file exists, 0600), hint | Pass | Pass |
| `$AO_REPOS_ROOT` is the folder holding every checkout (`/home/ubuntu`, `/workspace`) | Pass | Pass |
| `ao spawn --branch master` gets the branch error; valid spawns work | Pass | |
| `ao kill` / `ao send` on a non-child get the new message; killing own child works | Pass | |
| Agent browser: 409 + `Retry-After: 30`, 0 x 502 in 45 min of CP logs | Pass | Pass (connects) |
| Codex terminal on gpt-5.6-sol (400): active to idle in about 2 s, switch to Chat proceeds | Pass | Pass |
| Claude with an invalid model: idle in about 1.8 s via `StopFailure` | Pass | |
| Successful Codex turn still goes idle | Pass | Pass |
| Review switcher shows the real repo name | Pass | Pass |
| Scripts: Save pinned with 4 steps, variables selectable, copy works, `AO_REPOS_ROOT` only for multi-repo | Pass | |
| Regression: single-repo first turn and PR, Chat round trip, standalone | Pass | Pass |

## Staging status

Staging runs the head of this branch (`:283`). Final live results:

- **Coder and Freestyle:**
  - Live Setup logs: expand, copy, failure and Retry, Summary sidebar.
  - Cleanup on delete, including a paused Freestyle VM, running as `ao-worker` (not root).
  - The full secret suite: 0 leaks across UI, Copy, events, startup detail and Cleanup.
- **Freestyle:**
  - Cleanup after a Scripts edit.
  - Esc interrupt, then a message, then a quick re-prompt.
  - Chat switch after Esc.
  - Restore in Chat mode, and API-created sessions.
  - Every original fix.
- **Local daemon:**
  - Esc and failed turns go idle (Claude and Codex).
  - Hooks from other Claude processes are ignored.
  - Chat switch after Esc.

**Not testable live:** the share-link view needs a non-member account. Its Postgres test passes.

**Known pre-existing failing tests**, which also fail on main:
- 4 Postgres tests;
- 3 vitest (`ContextMeter`, `ChatWorkspace` context usage);
- 40 environment-dependent main-process vitest;
- a few backend tests that only time out under parallel load.

title: fix(chat): enable Claude Code's to-do tools in Claude chat sessions
body:
Code changes: +11 -0\
Tests: +26 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Claude Code chat sessions now get Claude Code's to-do tools, so the chat's plan panel fills in for Claude like it does for Codex and Cursor.

## Why

Fixes #6900.

Claude Code withholds its to-do tools (`TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList`, `TaskUpdate`) from SDK-driven sessions unless `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS` is set. AO never set it, so the agent had nothing to call when asked for a to-do list, narrated progress in prose, and `conversation_turns.plan_json` stayed empty.

I checked this against the `claude` CLI directly (2.1.302), launched with AO's flags and reading the tool list from the `init` message:

| Environment | Tools | To-do tools |
|---|---|---|
| default | 26 | none |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-ts` | 26 | none |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=true` | 26 | none |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` | 30 | `TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList`, `TaskUpdate` |

`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS` alone does not enable them, and the `sdk-ts` entrypoint is not the cause.

## How

- `claudeACPLaunchEnv` (`claudeacp/driver.go`) sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`.
- A value the user already chose wins: it is not set when the project env (`input`) has the key or the daemon's own environment has a non-empty value. This is the same pattern the function uses for `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION`.
- The variable is not part of Claude Code's documented settings as far as I know, so it may change between Claude Code versions. I tested 2.1.302; the issue reports 2.1.296.
- Intentional omission: no frontend change. The plan panel already renders plan updates; the issue notes the panel redesign (#6884) is independent.

## Testing

- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/`: ok. New: `TestClaudeACPLaunchEnvEnablesTodoToolsByDefault`, `TestClaudeACPLaunchEnvKeepsConfiguredTodoToolsChoice` (project env and daemon env cases).
- In the desktop app (isolated dev data), the same 10-step to-do prompt on a Claude Code chat session:
  - `main`, variable unset: agent says it has no to-do tool; `plan_json` empty.
  - this branch, variable unset in the shell and daemon: `plan_json` filled with all 10 steps, each `completed`.
- Mirrored the Go CI job locally: `gofmt -l` clean, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -race -count=1` over all packages, including the chat, session manager, SQLite and SQLite store packages that CI shards. All passed.
- Gap: `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 does not run on my machine. It fails with a `typecheck` error ("export data version 5 is greater than maximum supported version 4") at `backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go:3`, and fails identically on a clean `main`. Lint is not verified locally; I am relying on the remote check.
- Frontend jobs were not run; this change touches only Go files.

title: feat(awake): move Stay Awake to a sidebar toggle shared with Connect Mobile

## What
Stay Awake moves out of the topbar, right sidebar and settings into one square coffee toggle next to the sidebar Settings row, and it now shares state with the Connect Mobile **Keep awake** switch.

- Removed the control from the topbar, sessions board, archive view and session inspector.
- Removed the Stay Awake settings page (`StayAwakeSection` and its tests).
- New macOS coffee toggle in the expanded sidebar. Its fill means the desktop or mobile backend actually holds wake. Configured but inactive requests show an attention icon and accessible tooltip, including the daemon stop reason. Pressed state tracks configured requests so they remain clearable; actual wake display waits for daemon facts.

The mobile Keep awake flag and the Stay Awake session are still two separate backends (both reuse the same `caffeinate`/lid code). This PR keeps them in step from the UI rather than merging them in the daemon.

title: fix(accounts): read limits again soon after an answer with no windows
body:
Code changes: +13 -1\
Tests: +39 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

An account's limits answer with no windows is now kept for 30 seconds instead of the 5-minute cache window, so the next one-minute poll reads the account again.

## Why

After adding a Claude account (a Team login), the session's Account panel showed no limits. The first read ran right after sign-in and Claude's `get_usage` came back with no windows; that is not an error, so the daemon kept it as fresh for 5 minutes. A forced refresh a few minutes later returned Session (5h) 1% and Weekly · Fable 3%. Worst case before this change: about 6 minutes with no limits (5-minute cache plus the 60-second poll). After it: about 1 minute.

## How

- `needsReading` uses a 30-second window when the last reading has limits with no windows; readings with windows keep the 5-minute window.
- Identity checks (`DefaultSignIn`, `pick`) are unchanged: they care about sign-in, not limits.
- Trade-off: a plan that never reports windows is read on every poll, one CLI call a minute while the panel is open.

## Testing

- `TestLimitsWithNoWindowsAreReadAgainSoon`: an empty answer is read again a minute later; an answer with windows is kept. Fails without the fix, passes with it.
- `go test ./internal/service/agentaccounts/`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run ./internal/service/agentaccounts/...` (0 issues).

title: fix(daemon): keep product telemetry independent of the error-sharing consent
body: ## What One deletion in `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go`. The daemon no longer overwrites `cfg.Telemetry.Events` with `policyCoordinator.EventsEnabled()` before building the product telemetry sink. ## Why `policyCoordinator` is the agent-switch failure-reporting consent, surfaced in settings as "Share error events" with the description "Share bounded, privacy-filtered error diagnostics". `docs/telemetry.md` says the env vars, not this switch, govern product telemetry, and the renderer deliberately ignores the policy for PostHog (`telemetry.ts` `applyRendererTelemetryPolicy` is a no-op). On the daemon the switch did more than that. `Coordinator.EventsEnabled()` is `stored toggle && AO_TELEMETRY_EVENTS`, and an unreadable or malformed `telemetry_policy.json` makes it `false` too. Feeding that into `newTelemetrySink` installed a `NoopSink`, so the install stopped sending `ao.session.spawned`, `spawn_failed`, `ao.cli.invoked`, the CLI `ao.app.active`, `ao.http.5xx`, onboarding, project and review events. Nothing is recorded locally either. Windows never writes the policy file (`telemetry-policy-file.ts` `durabilitySupported`), so Windows daemons were unaffected. That is visible in PostHog over the last 14 days as the share of installs that send window events but no daemon events: | platform | window-event installs | window only | |---|---|---| | win32 | 1,481 | 2.6% | | darwin | 1,754 | 7.4% | | linux | 506 | 8.2% | The excess on mac and linux is about 90 installs in two weeks. There is also a latent cliff. `policy.go` `readAuthority` computes `storedEnabled = EventsEnabled && (!productionEnabled || ConsentProductionEnabled)`. When `AgentSwitchFailureProductionEnabled` flips to true, every existing consent record evaluates as off until the user answers the renewal dialog, and with this line in place daemon product telemetry would have gone dark for the whole installed base. ## What still uses the consent - Sentry failure capture, via `OnEventsChanged: sentryobs.SetPolicyEnabled`. - The agent-switch dispatcher, which reads the coordinator directly in `telemetry_wiring.go`. Neither path is touched. ## Testing - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/daemon/` - `go test ./internal/daemon/ ./internal/observe/agentswitch/ ./internal/adapters/telemetry/` pass. - No existing test drives `run()` with a policy file, so there is no regression test for this line. `newTelemetrySink` has its own tests for the `Events` flag and they are unchanged. ## Not in this PR The renderer-side wipe of the PostHog daily-gate keys in `telemetry-policy-store.ts`, which is driven by the same consent and inflates heartbeat counts on Windows. Separate change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(renderer): stop the error-sharing consent from resetting PostHog daily gates
body:
## What

Removes four lines from `frontend/src/renderer/stores/telemetry-policy-store.ts`. The failure-reporting policy listener no longer deletes `ao.telemetry.activeSlotsByDate` and `ao.telemetry.routeViewsByDate` from `localStorage` when the policy arrives with `eventsEnabled = false`.

## Why

Those two keys are the once-per-UTC-day gates for the PostHog heartbeat (`ao.v2.app.active`) and route views (`ao.v2.renderer.route_viewed`) in `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts`. The policy being listened to is the "Share error events" consent for Sentry, which `applyRendererTelemetryPolicy` documents as having no effect on PostHog analytics.

The wipe fired far more often than "when the user opts out":

- On Windows the policy file is never read (`telemetry-policy-file.ts`, `durabilitySupported = false`), so the view is always `eventsEnabled = false`.
- Main broadcasts the view on every `publish()`, and `retryPendingCleanup` republishes about once a second until the daemon applies the policy.
- After a wipe, the next `focus`, `visibilitychange`, `pointerdown` or `keydown` reserves the day again and captures another heartbeat. The heartbeat calls `posthog.capture` directly and skips `reserveCapture`, so the 5/min and 200/day caps don't apply.

Measured in PostHog over 30 days, share of desktop install-days with more than one heartbeat:

| builds | install-days | more than one heartbeat |
|---|---|---|
| up to v0.12.10 (before the wipe) | 957 | 2.1% |
| v0.12.11 and later (`cf350730b5`) | 17,832 | 18.3% |

Over the last 7 days: 557 of the 642 duplicate days are win32. One install (0.12.12, win32) sent 4,302 heartbeats in one day. Route views duplicate per surface on 590 of those 642 days and on 2 of 2,285 clean days, which is what you'd expect if the two keys are cleared together.

Unique-install counts (DAU) were never affected, since PostHog counts each `distinct_id` once per day. Raw event counts, per-install "events per day" tiles, and ingestion volume were.

## Testing

- `vitest run src/renderer/stores src/renderer/lib/telemetry.test.ts src/renderer/lib/telemetry.init.test.ts`: 8 files, 111 tests pass.
- No test asserted the removed behaviour.
- `tsc --noEmit` in the fresh worktree reports only missing types under `packages/product-ui` (workspace deps not installed there), nothing in `frontend/src`.

## Not in this PR

- Routing the heartbeat through `reserveCapture` so a future gate failure is capped like every other event. Worth doing, but it's a behaviour change in `telemetry.ts` rather than a removal, so it's separate.
- The daemon-side half of the same consent problem is #6905.

title: fix(pr): record an in-app merge as merged right away
body:
Code changes: +168 -36  
Tests: +160 -0  
Others: +0 -0

Part of #6555.

## Problem

After merging a PR with the in-app **Merge** button (session inspector → Pull request card), the card kept showing **open / Mergeable** with the Merge button for minutes.

Seen on PR #59 in `OrchestratorInc/ao-landing`: GitHub reported it merged at 00:52:53Z, but AO still showed it open at 00:55:37Z.

## Cause

- `POST /api/v1/prs/{id}/merge` → `pr.ActionService.Merge` returned success once GitHub's merge API said `merged: true`, but **wrote nothing locally** and ran no lifecycle.
- The renderer already invalidates the PR summary and workspace queries on success. The refetch just read the still-open row.
- The only path to `merged` was the SCM observer's next poll. That poll is one serial pass over every repo, with all writes at the end. The nominal cadence is 30s, but on the affected machine one tick took about 2m14s:
  - Tick starts: 00:53:57 → 00:56:11.
  - The tick that saw the merge committed its write about 3m18s after the merge.

This is not a regression: the merge route has never recorded its result (#88, extended in #3599).

## Fix

- New `scm.MergeRecorder` (`backend/internal/observe/scm/merge_recorder.go`) persists a merged observation through the **same write + lifecycle path the observer uses**. That path is extracted from `Observer.Poll` into `persistObservation` with no behaviour change. So the in-app merge produces:
  - the `pr` row update, and the `pr_updated` CDC event that drives live UI;
  - notifications;
  - terminate-on-merge.
- `ActionService.Merge` builds that observation from the provider observation it already re-fetched just before merging, then marks it merged:
  - merge commit SHA from the merge response;
  - merged/closed timestamps;
  - mergeability `unknown`, matching GitHub after a merge.
- It records the merge **before** returning, using a non-cancelling context, so the renderer's existing invalidation refetch sees `merged`.
- Review rows and the review decision are preserved. The next poll still refreshes everything and agrees with this write.
- A recording failure is logged, not returned: the merge did happen, and the next poll still catches it.
- Wired in `daemon.go`.

## Tests

- `internal/integration/pr_merge_test.go`, run against a real sqlite store and the real lifecycle manager:
  - a tracked open PR is merged through `ActionService` while the provider still reports it open (no poll in between);
  - asserts the row is merged with the merge commit SHA, mergeability is unknown, the review decision is preserved, and the terminate-on-merge session is terminated;
  - a following poll doesn't undo it.
  - **On `origin/main` (same scenario, main's wiring) it fails with the reported symptom:** `merged:false mergeability:"mergeable"`.
- `internal/service/pr` unit tests: the recorder gets the merged observation for the tracked URL; a recorder failure doesn't fail the merge; a failed merge records nothing.
- `go test` passes for `./internal/{daemon,observe,service/pr,httpd,lifecycle}/...`. `golangci-lint v2.13.2` reports 0 issues on the changed packages.
- `internal/integration` has one failure, `TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch`. It **fails on `origin/main` too** and is unrelated to this change.

## Verified in the real Electron app

- Setup: isolated data dir, dev daemon from this branch, and a throwaway private repo with one PR carrying a success commit status.
- Before: the inspector card showed open / Checks passing / Mergeable / Merge, the same as the report.
- Clicked **Merge** over CDP. The card showed the **merged** badge 3.4s after the click (most of that is the pre-merge refresh plus GitHub's merge call).
- GitHub `mergedAt` was 01:13:37Z. AO wrote `pr_state=merged` with the merge commit SHA at 01:13:38.2Z.
- Activity showed "Merged PR #1" and "Done" right away.

## Not in this PR (follow-up)

- Merges made **outside** AO (on GitHub) still wait for the observer, whose tick ran about 2m14s on the reporter's machine against a 30s cadence. No daemon log was persisted, so the slow step isn't identified yet. That needs its own investigation (per-phase tick timing) rather than a guess here.
- Narrow race: a poll that started before the merge and observed an unrelated change could briefly write `open` back. The following tick corrects it. In the reported case nothing else changed, so that poll wrote nothing.

title: fix(inspector): stop offering Create PR for work a merged PR shipped
body:
Code changes: +17 -4  
Tests: +57 -2  
Others: +3 -0 (generated openapi.yaml, schema.ts)

Part of #6555 (Case 1). Follow-up to #6908; same user report.

## Problem

After a session's PR is merged, the inspector's git row still offers **Create PR** (with "2 commits pushed"). Seen on `OrchestratorInc/ao-landing` PR #59, which was squash-merged as `f6e2f6d4f7` (1 parent).

Pressing Create PR asks the agent to open a duplicate PR of already-shipped work.

## Cause

`gitActionPlan()` in `SessionBranchSummary.tsx` (#6323) only knows about an *open* PR. Once the PR merges, `openPRNumber` is undefined and the plan falls through to `createPR` whenever `branch.commits > 0`.

Squash and rebase merges leave the branch's own commits outside the base. A merge commit does too, until the local base ref is fetched. So the branch still counts its commits as ahead of the base, and commit counts alone can't tell shipped work from new work.

## Fix

- **Daemon:** the branch-state pass already reads the branch tip. It now stores it as `SessionBranchState.headSha` (optional API field; `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` regenerated).
- **Renderer:** when there is **no open PR**, the tree is **clean**, and **HEAD equals the head SHA of a merged PR**, the row offers no create-PR action.
  - Commits made after the merge move HEAD past that SHA, so **Create PR** comes back whether or not they're pushed.
  - Uncommitted changes still offer it too.
  - The open-PR path (Commit & push / Push to #N) is unchanged.

## Tests

- New `SessionBranchSummary.test.ts`:
  - HEAD at the merged head gives no action, for squash, rebase and merge-commit merges (with the base fetched and not yet fetched).
  - Commits pushed after the merge → Create PR.
  - Unpushed commits after the merge → Push & create PR.
  - Dirty tree → Create PR.
  - Unknown HEAD keeps today's behaviour.
  - An open PR still wins.
  - On `origin/main` the three merged-head cases fail; the other six pass.
- `branch_state_test.go` now also asserts the recorded HEAD SHA.
- Local runs:
  - `go test ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/domain/...` passes, and `golangci-lint v2.13.2` reports 0 issues.
  - `npm run typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` are clean.
  - Full `vitest run`: 8382 passed, 19 failed. All 19 are in `src/main/auto-updater.test.ts` and `src/main/remote-proxy.test.ts`, which this PR doesn't touch, and they fail identically on `origin/main` with the same `node_modules`. CI is the reference for those.

## Verified in the real Electron app

Isolated data dir, dev daemon from this branch, throwaway private repo:

1. Session worktree at PR #1's head `6963a42`; PR #1 was squash-merged as `0daf770`. The inspector showed the **merged** card and "1 commit pushed", with **no Create PR**.
2. Committed and pushed one more commit (`48672f0`). The row showed "2 commits pushed" and **Create PR**.

## Not covered

#6555 Case 2 is not covered: a squash-merged branch **with no upstream of its own**, whose HEAD isn't the merged PR head (for example, the work was pushed under a different branch name). That needs a daemon-side content check ("is this tree already in the base?").

title: [Bug]: Continue fails with "interrupted task is no longer available" after stopping a Codex thread-goal turn
body:
## Bug

In a Codex chat, clicking **Continue** after stopping a turn fails with *"the interrupted task is no longer available to continue; send a new instruction"*. This happens when the stopped turn was started by Codex itself to keep working on a **thread goal**. Typing "continue" as a normal message works.

**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma (nightly, macOS, Codex local, GPT-6.1-Sol Ultra, Bypass permissions) | **Reproduced on:** `6f2990140` (origin/main), Codex CLI 0.162.1 | **Date:** 2026-10-19
**Confidence:** High (reproduced end to end in the dev app; fix verified on the same session)

## Observed

- The chat shows two "Worked for …" blocks in a row. The second has no user message above it, and both say "interrupted by you".
- The Continue button is shown. Clicking it sends `POST /api/v1/sessions/<id>/conversation/messages`, which returns **409 `CHAT_CONTINUATION_UNAVAILABLE`**.
- In the repro session, the turn Codex started (`1c336aa2`) is stored with **0 user messages**.

## Root cause

- Codex **Goals** is on by default (`codex features list` → `goals stable true`). The model can call `create_goal`. When a turn ends with the goal still active, Codex starts a new turn **without AO asking for it**, with the prompt "Continue working toward the active thread goal".
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` (~2992): when `dispatchingTurnID` is empty, `apply()` adopts the turn with `AdoptProviderTurn`. This creates a turn row with **no user message**.
- `backend/internal/service/chat/continuation.go`: `ContinuableTurnID` returns this interrupted turn, so the frontend shows Continue. But `stoppedContinuationContext` looks for a user message with `TurnID == stoppedID`, doesn't find one, and returns `""`. `prepareContinuation` then returns `ErrContinuationUnavailable` and the request fails with a 409 (`conversations.go:1042`).
- AO ignores `thread/goal/*` notifications (`codexappserver/normalize.go:678`), so it can't tell that these turns come from the goal.

## Reproduction

1. Open a Codex chat and send: *"Use your create_goal tool to set this goal: 'Run the shell commands sleep 3 && echo g1 through sleep 3 && echo g12, one at a time as separate command calls, and then write a final summary.' After creating the goal, run only g1 and g2, then end this turn."*
2. The turn completes. Codex then starts a new turn by itself, with no user message above it.
3. Stop that turn and click **Continue**.
4. The error appears and the POST returns 409.

Reproduced end to end. Quick Stop/Continue, Ultra effort, daemon reconnect, compaction and background terminals were also tried (~70 trials) and none of them caused it.

## Suggested fix

- In `stoppedContinuationContext`, if the stopped turn has no user message, fall back to the latest real user request in the visible history, and keep the partial output from the provider-started turn. The fix is ready locally with the regression test `TestStoppedContinuationContextProviderStartedTurn`. Verified in the dev app: Continue now shows "Continued", and the agent finishes g1–g12 and marks the goal complete.
- Follow-up: handle `thread/goal/*` notifications and pause the goal on Stop.

## Workaround

Type "continue" (or any instruction) as a normal message instead of clicking Continue.

## Impact

- Continue is broken for any Codex chat whose goal started a turn on its own. This is common on long research or multi-step tasks.
- The error wrongly suggests the task is gone.
- No data loss.

## Related

- Feature PR: #6328 (continue stopped conversation turn).
- Also found during the investigation, to file separately:
  - Stop sends only `turn/interrupt`, so the Codex goal stays active.
  - After Stop, background commands show as "cancelled" but keep running, and their later output isn't recorded.

title: fix(chat): continue a stopped provider-started Codex goal turn
body:
Code changes: +10 -0  
Tests: +13 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Fixes an issue where clicking **Continue** after stopping a Codex turn failed with "the interrupted task is no longer available to continue; send a new instruction" (HTTP 409 `CHAT_CONTINUATION_UNAVAILABLE`), while typing "continue" as a normal message worked.

The stopped turn was started by Codex itself through its **thread goals** feature (on by default). When a turn ends with a goal still active, Codex starts a new turn with no prompt from AO ("Continue working toward the active thread goal"). AO adopts that turn with no user message. `ContinuableTurnID` still offers it for Continue, but `stoppedContinuationContext` needs a user message on the stopped turn, so the continuation was refused.

Fixes #6910.

## Changes

- **Continuation context (`service/chat/continuation.go`):**
  - When the stopped turn has no user message (a provider-started turn), use the latest visible message as the cutoff instead of returning no context.
  - The existing logic then picks up the latest real (non-continuation) user request as the original task. The provider-started turn's partial output stays in the response tail.
  - Withdrawn, cancelled and queued-but-undispatched turns are still excluded, as before.

Out of scope (tracked in #6910): pausing the Codex goal on Stop, and handling `thread/goal/*` notifications.

## Testing

- **New regression test:** `TestStoppedContinuationContextProviderStartedTurn` covers a completed task followed by a stopped turn that Codex started, with no user message. It checks that the context includes the original request and the goal turn's progress, and excludes older unrelated tasks.
- **Manual (dev app, Codex CLI 0.162.1):**
  - Asked the agent to `create_goal`. Codex then started a turn by itself, which I stopped. Clicking Continue returned 409 (reproduced).
  - With the fix, on the same session, Continue showed "Continued". The agent finished the remaining goal steps (g1–g12) and marked the goal complete. Screenshots are on #6910.

Passed locally:

title: fix(daemon): keep telemetry export settings out of child environments
body:
## What

After `config.Load()` the daemon removes the telemetry export variables from its own process environment (`config.ScrubTelemetryEnv`, one call in `daemon.go`). The settings stay in `Config`, so the daemon itself still exports. Every child it starts now inherits an environment without them. The two Go e2e harnesses also set `AO_TELEMETRY_REMOTE=off` explicitly.

## Why

The desktop stamps `AO_TELEMETRY_REMOTE=posthog`, the PostHog key, `AO_TELEMETRY_APP_VERSION` and friends onto the daemon's environment (`frontend/src/main.ts` `telemetryOverrides`). Every child the daemon starts begins from `os.Environ()`: tmux and pty shells, ACP agents via `processenv.Merge`, git. So the settings reach every agent session.

When an agent working on the AO repo boots a test daemon the way the harnesses do (scratch `AO_DATA_DIR`, free port, `append(os.Environ(), ...)`, no telemetry override), that daemon inherits production export and the host app's version, mints a fresh install id, and reports to PostHog as a brand-new install that then adds a project and spawns a session, because that's what the tests do.

Observed on a dev machine: the session host (`ao chat-host`) and the agent process carry all five `AO_TELEMETRY_*` variables inherited from the daemon. Reproduced end to end with the PostHog host pointed at a local capture server: a daemon started from that environment with a scratch data dir minted a new `ins_…` id and sent `ao.daemon.started` with `app_version: "0.13.7"` and an ephemeral port.

Measured in PostHog over 7 days:

- 145 installs with daemon events and no window events, ever.
- 176 of their 335 daemon starts on ephemeral ports (49152+), 130 on other non-default ports, 29 on 3001. Normal installs: 6,978 on 3001, 1 ephemeral.
- All at tenure day 0; 106 of 145 ran add-project then spawn-worker.
- All traceable to a dozen GitHub handles, each of which also has one or two real desktop installs on port 3001 with window events. One handle produced 22 fake installs in a week.

That is about 140 fake new installs a week in "first project added", "first session spawned", sessions and spawn failures. DAU is unaffected since they never send the heartbeat.

## Why scrub at the source rather than at each launch site

Twenty-odd places in the daemon start children from `os.Environ()`. `config.Load` is the only reader of these variables, it runs once, and the daemon never re-execs itself (`grep` for `syscall.Exec`, `os.Executable`, `os.Args[0]` in `daemon` and `cli` finds nothing). Unsetting after `Load` covers every present and future launch site.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet` on config, daemon, cli, e2e.
- `go test ./internal/config/ ./internal/daemon/ ./internal/cli/` pass.
- New `TestScrubTelemetryEnvKeepsLoadedConfigAndClearsProcessEnv`: loads config with the variables set, scrubs, asserts the loaded config kept them, asserts `os.Environ()` no longer has them, then execs `env` as a real child process and asserts the child does not see them while still seeing unrelated `AO_*` variables.
- Note for reviewers: `ps eww` on macOS shows a process's exec-time environment, not its live one, so it cannot be used to confirm this. The child-process test is the proof.

## Related

- #6905 and #6906 fix the two other ways the error-sharing consent distorted telemetry.

title: feat: per-role agent assignment (Design, QA, Architect, etc.) + bug: OpenCode worker delegates to Codex exhausting quota
body:
## Feature Request: Per-Role Agent Assignment

Currently AO assigns a single worker agent per session. In real workflows, different roles need different specialized agents:

| Role | Ideal Agent | Why |
|------|-------------|-----|
| **Design** | `opencode-v2` / `kilocode` / `agy` | UI/UX, pixel art, mockup-to-prototype skills |
| **QA** | `opencode-v2` / `codex` | Test generation, e2e, contract testing |
| **Architect** | `opencode-v2` / `claude-code` | System design, ADR, tech decisions |
| **Implementation** | `opencode-v2` / `kilocode` | Feature coding, refactoring |
| **Code Review** | `codex` / `copilot` | PR review, security audit |

**Proposed:** Allow project/session config to map roles → agents:
```yaml
# .ao/config.yaml or project config
agents:
  design: opencode-v2
  qa: opencode-v2
  architect: opencode-v2
  implementation: kilocode
  review: codex
```

Orchestrator would spawn the correct agent when a task with that role is queued.

---

## Bug: OpenCode Worker Delegates to Codex (Quota Exhaustion)

**Environment:**
- AO version: 0.14.2
- Project: registered with `ao project add`
- Worker agent configured: `opencode-v2` (via `--worker-agent opencode-v2` or project config)
- Actual behavior: Tasks delegated to Codex, hitting 5-hour rate limit

**Expected:** When worker agent is `opencode-v2`, the spawned session should run OpenCode, not Codex.

**Observed:** 
- `ao agent ls` shows `opencode-v2: authorized`
- Spawn command: `ao spawn --project test --worker-agent opencode-v2 --name "feat-xyz"`
- Session starts but actual work done by Codex (visible in token usage / model name)
- Codex free tier quota exhausted in < 1 hour

**Suspected causes:**
1. Harness resolution falling back to Codex when OpenCode server not ready
2. `--worker-agent` ignored, defaulting to project `orchestrator.agent` or global default
3. Agent switch happening mid-session without user consent

**Logs to check:** `ao hooks` output, session `agent_switches` table, daemon logs.

---

## Impact
- Cannot use OpenCode for implementation (main use case)
- Forced to wait 5 hours for Codex quota reset
- No way to assign specialized agents per role

## Suggested Priority
1. **Bug fix** (P0): Ensure `--worker-agent` / project config is respected
2. **Per-role agent config** (P1): Enable multi-agent workflows

title: bug(daemon): stale AO worktree registration permanently blocks orchestrator spawn; replacement dialog surfaces one project at a time
body:
Split out of #6443 after verifying every part against `main` (`3b442275a`, 2026-10-19). Parts 1, 2, 4 and 5 of that issue are resolved or already have a PR; these are the two that remain.

---

# Part A (P2, launch-blocking) - a worktree registration under an old AO data root permanently blocks the orchestrator

## Symptom

Every orchestrator spawn for one project fails with HTTP 409, and the board shows the generic *"No orchestrator is running for this project."* There is no AO-side recovery, and no setting the user can change.

```
POST /api/v1/orchestrators  {"projectId":"<redacted>"}
409 {"error":"conflict","code":"BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE",
     "message":"spawn <id>: workspace: workspace: branch is already checked out in another worktree:
                \"ao/<project>-orchestrator\" is checked out at \"D:/ao-cc-lab-data/worktrees/<project>/orchestrator/<project>-orchestrator\""}
```

## Cause

Each project has one **fixed-name** orchestrator branch, so its worktree path is deterministic - `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:2178-2182`:

```go
path = filepath.Join(w.managedRoot, string(cfg.ProjectID), "orchestrator", prefix+"-orchestrator")
```

Before adding, `addWorktree` lists **every** worktree git knows about for the repo - `listRecords` runs `git worktree list --porcelain` with no filter against AO's managed root - and refuses if any other worktree holds that branch (`workspace.go:1563`):

```go
if conflict, ok := findWorktreeByBranch(records, branch); ok && filepath.Clean(conflict.Path) != filepath.Clean(path) {
    return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q is checked out at %q", ErrBranchCheckedOutElsewhere, branch, conflict.Path)
}
```

AO cannot distinguish "another live AO session legitimately holds this branch" from "a registration from a previous AO install still points at a path that exists". Both hit the same branch, because the branch name is fixed per project.

The only recovery AO implements is `staleRegistrationForPath` / `registeredWorktreeDirMissing`: a registration **at the same path** whose directory is gone. A registration at a *different* path that still exists on disk is not recovered, and `git worktree prune` cannot remove it (prune only drops registrations whose directories are missing). The refusal is deliberately pinned by `TestAddWorktreeRefusesBranchCheckedOutElsewhere` (`workspace_test.go:951`).

The sentinel is mapped to the 409 in `backend/internal/service/session/service.go:908`.

## Reproduction

```powershell
git -C <project> worktree list
# a registration under a data dir AO no longer manages, still holding ao/<project>-orchestrator:
#   D:/ao-cc-lab-data/worktrees/<project>/orchestrator/<project>-orchestrator  refs/heads/ao/<project>-orchestrator

# the directory exists, so prune is a no-op:
git -C <project> worktree prune

# any AO orchestrator spawn for that project now 409s
```

Triggers whenever an AO data dir is moved, renamed, or cleaned up out of band while a worktree registration survives - not platform-specific.

## Workaround (verified applicable)

```powershell
git -C <project> worktree remove D:/ao-cc-lab-data/worktrees/<project>/orchestrator/<project>-orchestrator
```

## Not the same as

- **#3942** - asks for a clearer message for `BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE`. The message is already accurate; the missing behaviour is adopting or offering cleanup of AO's own stale registrations.
- **#1641** (closed May 2026) - the TypeScript-era "adopt an orphaned orchestrator worktree instead of failing startup" fix. The Go rewrite does not carry that adoption path; `addWorktree` refuses outright.

## Suggested direction

Not prescribing a fix, but the decision has to be made somewhere:

1. **Offer cleanup instead of refusing.** When the conflicting registration looks like a prior AO layout for this same project (matches the project's orchestrator worktree shape but sits outside the current managed root), surface an actionable error - or a confirmation - naming the path and the `git worktree remove` command, instead of an opaque conflict.
2. **Adopt on demand.** If the registration is otherwise safe (clean tree, correct branch, matching project), reuse the path rather than refusing. This is what the TypeScript implementation did.
3. **Show it in `ao doctor`.** A registration holding a project's canonical orchestrator branch with no live orchestrator session behind it is a detectable dead state and is currently invisible.

Whatever the shape, the safety rule that already exists should be preserved: never force-delete a dirty registered worktree, and never treat a registered-but-locked worktree as recoverable.

---

# Part B (P3, cosmetic) - a failed orchestrator replacement surfaces one project at a time

The rest of #6443 Part 4 is fixed: the mutation now returns a typed `SettingsSaveResult`, a failure closes Settings, records a typed `OrchestratorReplacementFailure`, and renders `OrchestratorReplacementDialog` with Retry / Retry as TUI / Open current. The latching `replacementAttemptedRef` / `replacementFailedRef` are gone.

What remains is the display side. The store holds every failure keyed by project - `frontend/src/renderer/stores/ui-store.ts:58`:

```ts
orchestratorReplacementErrors: Record<string, OrchestratorReplacementFailure>;
```

but `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx:200` picks exactly one:

```ts
const replacementErrorProjectId = Object.keys(orchestratorReplacementErrors)[0] ?? null;
```

and `OrchestratorReplacementDialog` accepts a single `projectId` / `error` pair.

## Correction to #6443 Part 4(c)

The original claim that "a second project's error queues behind the first and is never shown" no longer holds. The queue does drain: dismissing clears that project's entry (`_shell.tsx:812-814`), and `restart-orchestrator.ts:41` clears the entry *before* spawning, so a successful retry promotes the next queued failure. Both paths were verified in the current code.

## What is actually left

When several projects fail replacement at once, the user repairs them one dialog at a time with no indication of how many are still pending. Low-value polish rather than a defect - filed here only so it is not lost, and safe to close as wontfix.

If it is picked up: render the pending count on the dialog, or list the affected projects in one dialog with per-project actions.

title: feat(browser): hand off Google auth and checkout to the system browser (#6622)
body:
Code changes: +386 -3  
Tests: +576 -7  
Others: +65 -0 (+1 binary image)

## Summary

Google sign-in and Google Workspace checkout refuse to run inside the embedded
AO Browser panel because Google blocks those flows in webviews, and the panel
also advertised itself as one (UA contained `Electron/` and app tokens). This
PR implements the P0 + P1 user-agent parts of #6622:

- **System-browser handoff.** Any navigation to `accounts.google.com`,
  `myaccount.google.com`, `pay.google.com`, `checkout.google.com`, Google
  sign-in/checkout paths on `*.google.com`, Stripe/PayPal checkout hosts, any
  OAuth `authorize` endpoint, or a user-configured host now continues in the
  user's own browser via `shell.openExternal`. The panel keeps the page it
  already had and shows a "Sign-in and checkout pages open in your browser"
  notice with an **Open again** button. Coverage spans the three entry points
  that reach a URL: typed/agent navigation, in-page clicks and redirects, and
  popups.
- **Chromium-style UA.** The panel session now runs with a user agent that
  drops only the `Electron/` and app tokens, leaving Chromium's real version
  in place so `Sec-CH-UA*` client hints still agree. It does not claim to be
  Google Chrome.
- **Configurable host list.** A new Settings > Browser "Sign-in handoff"
  section persists extra hosts (built-in hosts always hand off).
- **Docs.** `docs/cli/README.md` explains which sites hand off and that agents
  must not retry or work around them.

## Out of scope

Notification permission prompts, persistent-profile defaults, codecs/Widevine,
passkeys, and the P2 CDP scoping item, which are separate follow-ups. The
Electron upgrade to 44 already shipped (#6462), and named persistent profiles
already exist.


## Screenshot

Dev Electron build (`Orchestrator.inc (dev)`, isolated data): after a typed
`accounts.google.com` navigation, the panel keeps `example.com` on screen and shows
the handoff notice with **Open again**. The white area is the BrowserView surface,
which is not part of the renderer paint captured here.

![Sign-in handoff notice in the AO Browser panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/72e80ae0ce/docs/assets/pr-6919-signin-handoff.png)
## Test plan

- `src/shared/browser-external-handoff.test.ts` (host matching, OAuth paths,
  Google paths, look-alike hosts, user-configured hosts)
- `src/main/browser-user-agent.test.ts` (token removal, no Chrome rebrand)
- `src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts` (typed/click/redirect/popup handoff,
  user-host handoff, agent open handoff, nested-URL redaction, popup
  denial, first-tab UA)
- `src/renderer/stores/browser-handoff-hosts-store.test.ts`
- `src/shared/ui-locale.test.ts` (host-list coercion)
- Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, and the guarded-navigation postcondition integration pass. Full vitest and renderer smoke runs add no new failures versus the merge base; every remaining local failure reproduces on base too (Windows-only environment issues; CI runs Linux).

Rebased onto main at 8fbec7895 and pushed head 5b1e85ef0. The test-setup conflict preserves both the window-visibility mock and the external-browser mock. All 425 tests across seven affected suites and the native Electron integration pass locally after the rebase. The final diff check also passes. Full CI must rerun on this head.

title: feat(mobile): show a live setup checklist while a Chat session starts
body: Code changes: +548 -19 Tests: +210 -1 Others: +0 -0 (12 binary screenshots on a separate branch, not in this diff) ## Summary Brings the desktop's session start-up checklist (`SessionStartup`) to mobile Chat sessions. Before, a starting session on mobile showed: - a yellow "Starting the agent…" warning banner; - an empty "Connecting to the agent…" screen; - the opening prompt parked above the composer as a queued chip that could be discarded. There was no progress information at all. **Now** - **Checklist under the brief.** The opening brief reads as sent, with the daemon's start-up stages under it: - Fetch base branch, Create worktree, Run setup script, Start ; - pending / running / done status for each stage, with live elapsed times formatted like the desktop's; - the desktop's branch-naming phrase on the worktree row, then the real branch. - **Divider.** A full-width rule under the "Setting up session" header sets the checklist apart from the brief. The turn's Working / Worked row gets the same rule, as on the desktop, so the line stays in place through the handoff. - **Handoff.** Once the agent is up, the checklist hands over to the turn's "Working · Ns" row. - **Failure.** A failed start keeps its failed stage (red ✗), the daemon's reason, "Your messages are saved…" and **Retry start**, in place of the failure banner. - **Promptless starts.** They show the checklist alone, then "Start with a task" once the agent connects. - **Composer.** It reads " is starting…" during setup. - **Haptics.** A light tap as each stage finishes, and a success tap when the agent is up. - **Loading state.** A starting session shows the checklist instead of "Loading conversation…". **How it works** - **Data.** `DashboardSession` now carries the daemon's `provisionSteps`; no backend change. The board poll (8s direct, 2s tunnel) skips whole stages, so `useStartupSession` re-reads the session every 1s. It only polls while the session is provisioning, its screen is focused and the app is active. It overlays only the provisioning fields, and a board-side change (for example Retry) drops the overlay. - **Logic.** `lib/session/sessionStartup.ts` is a pure, unit-tested port of the desktop rules: - which turn is the opening one, ignoring paged history; - when the checklist hands off; - which stage failed; - duration formatting; - keeping the branch private until the worktree stage lands. - **Timeline.** The opening turn stays in the timeline instead of the composer's queued list. - **Agent ready after a promptless start.** Over the direct link this produces no conversation event, so after provisioning the screen re-reads the conversation until it reports the agent connected. The reads run serially (`startSerialPoll`), each paced from the previous one's completion, so a slow link never has its responses superseded by the refresh's latest-request gate. Previously a promptless start stayed on "Connecting to the agent…" indefinitely; the existing refresh path looks affected too, but this wasn't confirmed against `main`. - **Failed opening turn.** While a start is in progress or failed, the first turn hosts the checklist whatever its state, as on the desktop, so a provider rejection that fails both the turn and provisioning still shows the failure and **Retry start**. If no loaded turn can host a visible checklist, it renders on its own at the live edge. - **Agent label.** Reuses `agentLabel` from `packages/product-ui`, imported by relative path the same way mobile already imports `packages/shared`. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `packages/mobile`: 217 files, 2194 tests pass. New unit tests cover the startup model and the opening-brief timeline rules, and source assertions cover the screen wiring. - Run on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator (light and dark) against an isolated daemon (`AO_DATA_DIR` under `~/.ao/scratch`) with a slow Setup script. Cases covered: - a normal start; - Setup failing, then **Retry start** recovering into Working; - a promptless start: 40 frames captured through the handoff, none showing the banner. The poll stopped after 2 conversation reads. ## Screenshots **Before (iOS)** | Starting: banner, empty "Connecting…", prompt as a queued chip | Prompt only appears once the agent is up | | --- | --- | | | | **After (iOS)**: the rule under the header holds from setup through Working to Worked for | Naming the branch | Branch shown, setup running | Hands off to Working | Settled: Worked for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | **Failure and promptless start (iOS)** | Setup failed, reason + Retry start | Promptless: checklist alone | Agent connected: Start with a task | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | **After (Android)** | Naming the branch | Branch shown, setup running | Settled: Worked for | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | ## Known gaps / follow-ups - Orchestrator sessions (`OrchestratorLink`) don't carry provisioning fields on mobile, so they are unchanged. - Standalone spawns still use the synchronous spawn path, so they land on a ready session without a checklist. - Terminal-mode sessions are unchanged.

title: feat(mobile): add a session Files screen with a diff viewer and line feedback
body: Code changes: +2894 -393 Tests: +388 -1 Others: +107 -0 (generated file-type icons) ## Summary The mobile app can now review a session's changes the way desktop does. Until now it showed a turn's changed paths with +/− counts and pointed you at the worktree shell for the diff. - **Files screen** (`app/files/[sessionId]`) with two tabs: - **Changes:** uncommitted work vs. what's already committed on the branch, totals against the base branch, refreshed every 5s while open. - **All files:** folder browser with breadcrumbs, change dots, and search. - **File viewer** (`app/files/[sessionId]/file`): - Unified diff with word-level highlights and syntax colours. - Hidden context expands 20 lines at a time. - Wrap toggle, and previous/next across changed files. - A File tab: highlighted source, Markdown preview, image before/after. - **Feedback to the agent:** tap a line, or select a range the way you select text: hold a line and drag, or drag the line numbers. The list scrolls at the edges, and a drag that starts on an end of the selection adjusts it. Then Comment (queue it), Send now, or Copy. Comments queue across files and send as one message through `POST /sessions/{id}/send` with `userAuthored: true`, formatted exactly as desktop formats them. - **Inline comments:** each comment is drawn under the line it's about, GitHub-style, in the app's card: "You · Lines …", the text, and Pending or Sent. Pending ones can be deleted; sent ones stay as a record and can be dismissed. - **File icons:** each file shows its type's logo, using the same `@react-symbols/icons` set desktop draws in `WorkspaceEntryIcon`, with desktop's status letter (A, M, D, R in desktop's colours) at its bottom right. Folders get desktop's folder icons. `scripts/generate-file-icons.mjs` renders them to SVG in `lib/files/fileTypeIcons.generated.ts`. - **No Explain / Make change:** desktop no longer renders its old selection menu (`DiffSelectionMenu`), so mobile offers what desktop's diff view does: line feedback (Comment, Send) and Copy. `diff-selection.ts` stays where it was on desktop. - **Entry points:** - A changes pill in the composer's meta row. It uses git totals, appears only once the session changed files, and takes the place of the "Sent after this" note; the placeholder still says the message waits, and the steer action is kept. - "Review changes" in the conversation actions menu. - The per-turn changed-files card: a Review button, and every row opens its diff. - The terminal session header, which has no actions menu. - **Shared code:** the diff parser and both feedback formatters (`diff-selection`, `file-annotations`) move to `packages/shared/files/`, so both apps build identical rows and messages. The old desktop paths re-export them; desktop behaviour is unchanged. - **Accessibility:** every diff line has a VoiceOver/TalkBack label (for example "Added 793: …"), and screen-reader users get an "Extend selection to this line" action instead of long-press. No daemon or API changes: everything uses the existing workspace routes (`manifest`, `file`, `file/blob`, `tree`, `search`, `send`). ## Screenshots Final build on Android (emulator, dark theme), reading this session's real worktree. | Changes pill (composer) | ⋯ menu | Changes | All files | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | Diff | Drag to select | Comments on lines | Review sheet | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | Markdown preview | | --- | | | ## Testing - **Mobile** (`packages/mobile`, as in `mobile.yml`): `npm run typecheck` is clean; `npm test` passes 219 files, 2,208 tests. New tests cover: - the change grouping, diff rows and folds, and selection labels and annotation targets; - the send path (batching, partial failure, the 4 KiB `/send` limit); - a check that every Lucide icon import resolves to a shipped module; - entry-point placement. - **Desktop** (`frontend`, as in `frontend.yml`): `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` are clean; `npx vitest run` passes 499 files, 8,392 tests. - **Renderer e2e:** `test:e2e:renderer` passed 95 of 96 locally on macOS. `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts` ("typed chat composer text is visibly selected with a pointer drag") fails here even when run alone. This branch changes nothing in the desktop chat components or the e2e specs, so I'm relying on the Linux Playwright container in CI to confirm. - **Device follow-up:** after testing on a Pixel 10a and an iPhone 13, the follow-up commit replaces long-press-to-extend with drag selection, draws comments inline, fixes the Android review sheet drawing under the status bar, and swaps the status letters for icons. I verified drag selection (holding a line, and dragging the line numbers), quick-swipe scrolling, edge auto-scroll, inline queued and sent cards, and the sheet inset on the Android emulator with real touch events; the line-number drag was also verified on the iOS simulator. - **Simulator walkthrough** (iOS, Debug build): the Changes list, a diff, folds, range selection, queueing and sending a review, All files, a Markdown preview, the composer pill, and the actions menu. The send was captured before reaching any agent and matches desktop's annotation format. ## Known gaps / follow-ups - Android is not tested yet. - Image before/after wasn't tried with a real changed image. - The Changes list refreshes every 5s instead of using desktop's `workspace/events` stream. - Not in this PR: editing files, commit history, and showing a PR's files from the Review screen.

title: fix(files): restore image review scrolling and collapse controls
body:
Code changes: +97 -53  
Tests: +331 -19  
Others: +0 -0  

Image previews in workspace reviews were outside the text diff scroller and ignored collapse state. Render fallback cards inside CodeView’s measured footer, mount the viewer for image-only reviews, and use accessible file headers backed by the existing collapse state. Image-only and mixed reviews now scroll through every preview and support individual collapse, collapse-all, and re-expansion.

Deferred lockfiles and large text files now load on individual expansion, matching Expand all. Each loaded deferred path has a separate batch, so existing text diff queries stay cached and mounted during loading. Binary files are exempt from text deferral in both the pane and prefetch helper, keeping large image previews expanded by default. The first individual expansion follows the diff when its loaded row moves from the footer into file order. Reopening an already loaded deferred file preserves the scroll position. Collapsing and re-expanding reuses the loaded diff without an extra request. Regression tests separately cover a small lockfile and a file over 512 KB.

Image and binary fallback rows also expose the same saved Viewed checkbox as text rows. Marking a file viewed collapses its preview. Headers use the same 36px row height, ghost open-file icon and status label immediately after the filename as text rows; image panes no longer sit inside a second bordered card. Tests cover marking every file, persistence, and unmarking in image-only and mixed reviews.

The changed-files rail brings fallback rows into view, including collapsed images. Regression tests exercise 600 KB image summaries, real image decoding and mouse-wheel scrolling at 400px and 650px, plus rail reveal and individual/global collapse behavior. Text diff virtualization stays with CodeView.

Rebased onto current main, retaining the target-based review API, parent toolbar collapse controls, historical-source image guard, and file navigation. The regression fixtures use the same collapse request/callback contract as the Files toolbar.

Validation on follow-up commit `7cec1bf9c`:
- Focused file-review/image-preview suite: all 52 tests passed, including reopening loaded lockfiles after both individual expansion and Expand all, with no extra scroll or request. The new cases failed before the fix.
- The preceding head passed all 9,031 local unit tests, project and E2E typechecks, and the production renderer build. Local renderer smoke had 116 passes and the previously documented macOS composer-selection failure.

title: fix(chat): settle Claude checkpoints with input queued mid-turn
body:
Code changes: +29 -2
  Tests: +38 -0
  Others: +0 -0

  ## What

  Fixes Terminal → Chat switches for Claude Code sessions that fail with `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED … native submission attachment not flushed` when a message was sent while Claude was busy. Retries failed the same way.

  ## Why

  Fixes #6870.

  When AO delivers a message while Claude is mid-turn, Claude Code does not write a new `user` record. It writes a `queued_command` attachment inside the running turn, followed by the `UserPromptSubmit` hook attachment that carries AO's correlation ID. `verifyCheckpointTranscript` matched that submission to the running turn and compared the queued message's text with the turn's original prompt. Those never match, so the checkpoint could never settle and the switch was blocked for good.

  ## How

## How

**Claude native checkpoint (`claudeacp/checkpoint.go`)**
- Read the `prompt` of a `queued_command` attachment and remember it for the submission hook that immediately follows.
- Match a queued submission's text against its queued prompt instead of the running turn's prompt.
- Submissions without a preceding `queued_command` take the same path as before.
- Nothing is relaxed: a queued text that doesn't match is still rejected, and the turn must still complete with `end_turn`.

## Testing

**New regression test:** `TestNativeCheckpointQueuedCommandInsideTurn` uses the real transcript shape: a prompt, a tool call, two `queued_command` + hook pairs, then `end_turn`.
- Without the fix it fails with `native submission attachment not flushed`. With the fix it settles on the original user boundary.
- A queued text that doesn't match its submission is still rejected.

**Manual (dev app, Claude Code 2.1.303):**
- **Before:** in a Terminal UI session, I sent two `ao send` messages while Claude was making tool calls, then switched to Chat. The switch failed with the exact error from the issue, and Retry failed the same way.
- **After:** on the same session and transcript, the switch completed. The conversation carried over, and a follow-up message in Chat was answered correctly.

Passed locally:

- `go test ./backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/ -run QueuedCommandInsideTurn -v`
- `go test ./backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/...`
- `go vet ./backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/`

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
