title: feat(chat): add shared path menu and native editor actions
body:
Code changes: +385 -109  
Tests: +603 -7  
Others: +54 -9  

## Summary

Chat filesystem paths now share a right-click menu with **Open in AO**, **Copy path**, **Reveal in Finder / file manager**, and installed supported editors. Existing clicks, artifact navigation and line references are preserved. Cursor and VS Code file handoffs open a new window.

- Keep remote/cloud paths out of local native actions. Validate paths, relative-path workspace confinement and launcher arguments behind trusted Electron IPC.
- Share AO’s existing symbols between chat and the topbar, with automatic native app icons for editors without a built-in symbol.
- Show a compact, centered **Copied to clipboard** confirmation with a green checkmark after successful copies, retaining the existing dismissal duration.

## Validation

- Requester manually tested the real Electron dev app and approved the feature and appearance.
- Complete frontend suite on `b1941719d`: **539 files passed; 9,313 tests passed, nine skipped** (Node 24).
- All 258 focused tests and both project/E2E typechecks passed.
- Cloud contract generation, drift check, typecheck, 30 tests and package dry run passed. Product UI typecheck, 161 tests and package dry run passed. Docs translations, seven tests and production build passed.
- Guarded-navigation integration and real Electron terminal-origin/daemon-browser boundary tests passed.
- Node 22.23.2 lockfile compatibility, macOS helper configuration tests, arm64/x64 builds, and native Swift policy/state tests passed. Original Electron SQLite binary restored after validation.
- Linux renderer smoke passed in CI. Locally on macOS, **127 passed, one failed**: the previously documented composer pointer-drag selection test. No selection behavior was changed.
- Current-head CI: renderer smoke, macOS native helpers and security scan passed; the main frontend job is still running.

No dependency, daemon API, storage or migration changes.

## Review follow-up

Native actions retain symlink/parent component order before containment checks, and inline/Markdown menus use the normalized displayed path rather than a basename-matched catalog entry. Existing Files clicks remain unchanged.

`b1941719d` fixes missing copy targets by resolving the nearest existing ancestor before checking containment. Tests cover missing/present controls, missing directory suffixes, symlinked workspaces, escaping paths, Windows paths and non-missing resolution errors. All supplied review threads are resolved.

Rebased onto `main` (`e65b57b0c`) to clear conflicts, retaining upstream navigation guards, Markdown link styles, and toast borders alongside this PR’s path menu and compact centered copy confirmation. The PR remains unmerged.

## October 28 conflict resolution

Merged `main` (`c8be3cbd4`) into this branch in `7b2a7071f`. Kept the new editor-preference APIs, shared icon export, inline-file link behavior and translation additions alongside the existing path-menu and symlink fixes. No new user-visible behavior was introduced by this merge. All 276 focused tests and both typechecks pass. CI on `7b2a7071f` was fully green: all four Vitest shards, typechecks, docs/package/integration checks, macOS helpers, renderer smoke and security scan. Local native helpers, all three Electron origin-boundary tests, Node 22.23.2 lockfile checks and Cloud/product/docs checks also pass. The full local unit run completed with 9,966 passing, six skipped and six timing/assertion failures across four files; the 158-test Sidebar file passes separately. Topbar and memory tests pass separately as well; the three IndependentSideChatDelivery assertions still fail locally (75 other tests pass in that rerun), while all four complete CI shards pass. title: feat(cloud): public share links for local artifacts behind AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_SHARES
body:
Code changes: +860 -14
Tests: +713
Others: +340 (contract, generated cloud-client schema) and +15 (compose/env)

Stack: #6769 control plane → **this PR**. The base is `ao/agent-orchestrator-251/cloud-artifacts-control-plane`, so this diff covers only share links. It needs only the control plane's artifact store, sweeper queue and migration `00084`, not the worker (#6779) or desktop (#6809) PRs.

## Summary

A signed-in user can publish **one file from a local session** to a public link. This PR adds the control-plane side. The desktop Share button and a daemon endpoint come in follow-up PRs. It is **development-only** and off by default: `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_SHARES` is refused in staging and production and requires `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS`.

- **Link:** `<project>-<feature>-<email>.<share origin>`, for example `http://agent-orchestrator-login-page-aditi1178-gmail-com.share.localhost:8081/`.
  - Lowercase; every run of characters outside `a–z0–9` becomes `-`.
  - Project and feature are shortened so the label, including a collision suffix, fits the 63-character DNS limit.
  - A taken name gets `-2`, `-3`, and so on.
  - The email comes from the signed-in principal, never from the request.
- **Limit:** 3 active links per user (`AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_SHARE_LIMIT`).
  - A new link takes a per-user advisory lock, counts the user's links, and inserts in one transaction, so concurrent requests cannot pass the limit.
  - Going over returns `409 artifact_share_limit_reached` with "Upgrade to AO Cloud to share more."
  - A cheap count before the upload means a request over the limit never reaches S3.
- **Same document, new version:** a document is identified by its project, feature and file name (`document_key`, unique per user). `POST` for a document that already has a link replaces the version that link serves and returns `200` with `replaced: true`. The URL and slot stay, and the earlier version is no longer served and is queued for the sweeper. A different file or feature is a new document and needs a free slot.
- **Republish** (`PUT`) keeps the URL and does not use another slot. The replaced S3 version is deleted.
- **Revoke** (`DELETE`) stops the link serving at once and queues its stored version for the sweeper. The row stays with `revoked_at` set, so **a revoked link still uses its slot**: revoking cannot make room for a new document. Publishing the revoked document again restores its link. A second revoke, and a `PUT` on a revoked link, return 404. `GET` lists revoked links with `revokedAt`, and `used` counts them.
- **Routes** (authenticated, registered only when the flag is on):
  - `GET /me/artifact-shares` lists links with `used` and `limit`.
  - `POST /me/artifact-shares?name=&project=&feature=` publishes the body. It requires `Content-Length` and `X-AO-Artifact-SHA256`, and caps a file at 10 MiB.
  - `PUT /me/artifact-shares/{id}` republishes; `DELETE /me/artifact-shares/{id}` revokes.
- **Serving:** a middleware matches hosts that are a single label directly under the share origin's host and serves that share's file at `/` only, for GET and HEAD. Every other host passes through to the normal routes.
- **Storage:** one object per link at `shares/{shareId}` in the existing artifact bucket. The row records the live `version_id`, as session artifacts do.
- **Data:** migration `00085` adds `ao_artifact_shares`.
  - An owner RLS policy (`user_id = ao_current_user_id()`) covers the account routes.
  - A service policy covers lookup by slug for public serving.
- **Reuse from the stack:**
  - `artifactstore` for put, get, delete and content types.
  - The sandbox `artifactFileCSP` and the SHA-256 header and validation.
  - The upload and the streamed, sandboxed serve are now shared helpers (`putArtifactObject`, `writeArtifactObject`) that both session artifacts and share links call.
  - The only visible change to session artifacts: log messages renamed from "blob" to "object".
- Markdown is served as `text/plain` so browsers show it instead of downloading it.
- **Contract:** `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` adds the three routes. `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated with `npm run generate`.
- **Local:** `compose.yaml` passes the three settings. The origin defaults to `http://share.localhost:${AO_CLOUD_PORT}`, and `*.localhost` resolves to loopback without DNS changes.

## Tests run

- `cd cloud && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./...`: clean.
- **Unit:** slug rules (DNS-label validity with suffix, budget split, empty parts) and config (off by default, required settings, refused when hosted).
- **Handlers**, through the full router with the in-process fake S3:
  - Flag off returns 404 everywhere and nothing reaches S3.
  - Publish and serve, with headers: sandbox CSP without `allow-same-origin`, `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, ETag/304, no `Set-Cookie`.
  - Markdown is served as text.
  - Slug collisions get a suffix.
  - Republish keeps the link and leaves exactly one stored version.
  - The limit, with no S3 write over it.
  - Another user's republish or revoke returns 404.
  - Revoke frees a slot and removes the object.
  - Upload validation returns 400, 413, 422 and 401 as expected.
  - Host routing: other paths, POST, an unknown slug, the bare domain, a nested subdomain, an uppercase host, and the API host still working.
  - A missing object returns `artifact_unavailable`.
  - The existing session artifact tests pass after the refactor.
- **Postgres**, with `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL` on a scratch `postgres:17`:
  - 8 concurrent creates against a limit of 3 make exactly 3 links, with `-2` and `-3` suffixes.
  - Ownership isolation for get, update, delete and list.
  - Update returns the replaced version.
  - Lookup by slug runs under the service context.
  - Delete frees a slot.
- `go test ./...` with the Postgres URL: everything passes except `internal/postgres` `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`, and `internal/workerexec` `TestCloudClaude{ProviderModelsReachAdapter,DiscoversProviderCatalogWithLaunchCredentials}`. All six **fail identically on this PR's base** (`ce2c31cba`).
- `npm --prefix packages/cloud-client run generate` and `typecheck`: clean.
- **End to end on Docker Compose** (Postgres, MinIO, control plane, `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1 AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_SHARES=1`), using local auth and curl:
  - Publish, open the link, hit the limit, a second user, republish, cross-user 404s, and revoke freeing a slot.
  - MinIO holds exactly one version per live link and none for revoked ones.
  - A real artifact was read through the running AO daemon (`artifactFiles[].rawUrl`) and published; the link serves the identical bytes.
  - In a browser, an HTML link runs its script inside the sandbox, and its `fetch` is blocked by `connect-src 'none'`.

## Known risks and follow-ups

- **Desktop and daemon:** the Share button and sign-in prompt, plus a local record of each artifact's share ID so the desktop republishes instead of creating a new link, are the next PRs.
- **Production:** wildcard DNS and TLS for `*.orchestrator.inc`, then lift the hosted refusal.
- **Separate domain:** user HTML served on subdomains of the main domain shares its registrable domain. Before production, never set cookies on the parent domain, and preferably serve shares from a separate domain.
- **First-boot compose race:** on a brand-new Postgres data directory, `migrate` can hit "connection refused" once, because Postgres restarts at the end of initialisation. Re-running `docker compose up` succeeds. This happens on the base too and is not touched here.

title: [Bug]: delivered worker reports stay 'claimed' and re-deliver to a live orchestrator every turn
body:
Worker reports stay in `delivery_state = 'claimed'` after delivery and never move to `acknowledged`. The daemon then re-delivers the same `report-batch:<id>` to the orchestrator on every turn. One report reached 51 deliveries.

Related, different mechanism: #6119 (undeliverable batch starves newer reports, rows stay `pending`), #6639 (retry storm against a dead controller). Here the orchestrator is live, delivery succeeds, `last_error` is empty, and the row stays `claimed`.

## Impact

- The orchestrator gets the same report on every turn, which hides new reports and wastes turns.
- A daemon restart (`ao stop`, `ao start`) does not clear it. The claim is persisted and re-claimed on start.
- No CLI command acknowledges a report. The only fix is a manual `UPDATE` on `ao.db`.

## Evidence (`ao.db`, `reports` table)

| Report | Worker | State | Attempts | Acknowledged by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | worker A | checkpoint | 2 | daemon |
| 2 | worker B | done | 14 | daemon |
| 3 | worker C | done | 14 | daemon |
| 4 | worker B | done | 51 | manual SQL |
| 5 | worker B | needs_input | 6 | manual SQL |
| 6 | worker B | done | 4 | manual SQL |
| 7 | worker B | done | 4 | manual SQL |

Totals: 5 of 21 `done`, 1 of 6 `needs_input` and 1 of 30 `checkpoint` reports needed more than one delivery. On the latest day, 4 of the last 5 reports looped.

Reports 2 and 3 came from different workers and were acknowledged in the same transaction (identical `acknowledged_at`).

## Repro

1. A worker in a Terminal UI session runs `ao report --done --note "..."` (or `--needs-input`).
2. The orchestrator (claude-code harness) receives the `<ao-report-delivery>` block and replies.
3. The next orchestrator turn receives the same batch id again. Repeats until the row is set to `acknowledged`.

Not verified: what event should acknowledge a report. An `ao send` to the worker after delivery did not acknowledge it.

## Workaround

```sql
UPDATE reports
SET delivery_state = 'acknowledged',
    acknowledged_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%f +0000 UTC', 'now')
WHERE id = '<report id>' AND delivery_state = 'claimed';
```

Works with the daemon running. Back up `ao.db` first.

## Environment

- `ao version`: dev
- macOS
- Orchestrator harness: claude-code. Worker harness: claude-code, Terminal UI mode.

title: fix: update PR cards immediately after merge
body:
Code changes: +225 -22  
Tests: +242 -8  
Others: +80 -12 (generated sqlc, OpenAPI, and TypeScript API artifacts)

## What

Update local PR state and the inspector card as soon as GitHub confirms a merge. Persist the authoritative merge result, emit the existing PR CDC event, return `state` and `stateChangedAt` from the merge endpoint, and update the React Query cache from that response.

Also prevent an in-flight pre-merge observation from writing stale `open` state over a confirmed merge, and add poll/provider timing diagnostics for future slow-refresh investigations.

## Why

The 30-second SCM poll checks the repository open-PR-list ETag and the head commit's check-runs ETag. Those guards can remain unchanged after the PR itself merges, so AO may skip the actual PR detail fetch until the five-minute bounded-staleness refresh. This produced a reported delay of roughly three minutes even though the merge request itself had succeeded.

The merge response is already authoritative, so the card should not wait for a later observation cycle.

## How

- Persist `merged`, the merge commit SHA, and merge timestamps immediately after provider success.
- Run lifecycle reactions only after the merged state is durable.
- Keep returning the remote success if local persistence fails, while logging the failure for observer reconciliation; retrying the already-completed remote merge would be incorrect.
- Treat merged state as irreversible in PR upserts so an older in-flight observation cannot regress it to open.
- Return only the response fields needed by the UI and update the cached PR summary immediately.
- Log full poll and provider-request durations, warning when either exceeds the polling cadence.

## Testing

- `env GOCACHE=/private/tmp/reverb-merge-cleanup-go-cache go test ./internal/service/pr ./internal/storage/sqlite/store ./internal/observe/scm`
- `env GOCACHE=/private/tmp/reverb-merge-cleanup-go-cache go test ./internal/httpd/controllers -run '^TestPRsRoutes_Merge_200$' -count=1`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx` — 168 tests passed

title: fix(terminal): open ao:// session links on a plain click
body:
## Summary

A plain click on an `ao://sessions/...` link in the terminal did nothing. Only Cmd-click (Ctrl-click on Windows/Linux) navigated. This removes the modifier gate, so session links open on a plain click, like web links in the same terminal already do.

## Root cause

`activateLink` in `XtermTerminal.tsx` dropped plain clicks on `ao:` links whenever the pane tracked the mouse:

```ts
if (term.modes.mouseTrackingMode !== "none" && !modifierPressed) return;
```

In practice, mouse tracking is almost always on:
- Legacy tmux sessions run `set-option mouse on` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go`), so they always track the mouse.
- Fullscreen TUIs track it too. Claude Code's fullscreen renderer is the case from the report.

xterm still fires link `activate` on a plain mouseup while tracking is on, so only AO's gate blocked the click. The click then went to the TUI. Claude Code refuses `ao:` URLs, and its copy-on-select copies text on a small drag or a double-click. That is the "it just copies to clipboard" in the report.

When this gate was added in #4606, the review described it as matching the web-link behaviour. The web-link handler never had a gate, so session links were the only links that needed a modifier.

## Evidence

Real Electron dev build from this branch, isolated lab data, Claude Code 2.1.303 in fullscreen mode (`CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1`). The clicks are real CDP mouse events on the rendered link.

| Before (plain click ignored, only Cmd-click navigates) | After (plain click navigates) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7523dc3531a8c8119a042c44a2b1e830033dab1b/before-plain-click.gif) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7523dc3531a8c8119a042c44a2b1e830033dab1b/after-plain-click.gif) |

Full-quality MP4s: [before](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7523dc3531a8c8119a042c44a2b1e830033dab1b/before-plain-click.mp4) and [after](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7523dc3531a8c8119a042c44a2b1e830033dab1b/after-plain-click.mp4). The red ring marks the click point and is drawn into the page for the recording.

## Tests

- `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`: the old test asserted that a plain click is ignored while the mouse is captured. It now asserts that the plain click opens the session link. It failed before the fix and passes after; the full file passes (149 tests).
- Manual, in the dev build: 3 of 3 plain clicks on `ao://sessions/repo/repo-1` opened the target session. Before the fix, a plain click did nothing and only Cmd-click navigated.

## Risks

- While a TUI captures the mouse, the click on a session link still reaches the TUI too. Web links already work this way. Claude Code ignores `ao:` links, so the only side effect is a possible text selection.
- Cmd-click and Ctrl-click still open the link.

title: feat(harness): update official-installer and single-binary cask harnesses beside running sessions
body:
## Problem

Since #6745, an update runs while sessions use the harness only when AO can keep the running release: managed npm/Bun/uv/pipx copies, Homebrew formulae, and Claude Code / Cursor / Grok. Harnesses installed with their vendor's `curl | sh` installer are blocked while a session runs (`warn` → `blocked`), because the installer writes one file in place and AO cannot keep the old release. This includes Codex, OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Kimi, Goose, Memcode, fx, OMP, Qwen, Amp, Autohand, Agy and Droid, and Homebrew casks (`warn` → `blocked` too), so the user has to end their sessions before updating them.

## After this PR

**Updates while sessions run (macOS and Linux)**, by how the harness is installed:

| Installed with | Harnesses |
| --- | --- |
| npm / Bun / uv / pipx | Every harness installed this way (unchanged since #6745) |
| Homebrew formula | Kimi, Amp, Crush, Qwen, Autohand, Kimchi, OMP, OpenCode, OpenCode 2 (unchanged since #6745) |
| Homebrew cask | Claude Code, Copilot and Droid (single binary); Codex (through its official installer). **New** |
| Official installer | Claude Code, Cursor and Grok (unchanged since #6745). **New:** Codex, OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Kimi, Goose, Memcode, fx, OMP, Qwen, Amp, Autohand, Agy and Droid |

**Everything else updates when idle, on every platform.** Before this PR, macOS and Linux showed **View sessions (N)** for these and refused the update even when every session was idle. Now the update starts at once: AO stops the idle sessions, updates, and resumes them on the new release. A session that is mid-turn is waited for. `AO_UPDATE_WHEN_IDLE=off` restores the refusal; the older `AO_WINDOWS_UPDATE_WHEN_IDLE` is still read.

**The update notice only offers Update.** View sessions, the session list and the idle-wait details are gone from the notice. An update waiting for idle sessions shows as **Updating…**. If the daemon refuses, for example with update-when-idle off, the card says why.

**These cannot update beside running sessions, only when installed with their official installer, so they update when idle.** Installed any other way, they update while sessions run.

| Harness | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Prime Agent | Its installer stops prime-agent daemons, busy ones included. |
| Kimchi | At runtime it reads data from the real `$XDG_DATA_HOME/kimchi`, which a per-release copy would not update. |
| Muse | No version pin, and its launcher updates itself hourly in its own folder. |
| Devin, Aider, Pi, Kiro, OpenHands | No managed recipe yet. Each installer has to be read before it can run into a release of its own. |

**Windows:** unchanged. Every update there waits for idle sessions.

## Change

AO now runs the vendor's **own installer** into a release directory of its own (`<data>/harnesses/<target>/versions/vN`), pinned to the release the update picked, then switches `current` and its launcher, the way it already does for npm. Sessions keep running the old release, and they move to the new one once idle, like every other managed harness.

Each recipe (`managed_official.go`) was read from the vendor's script:

| Harness | Install dir | Version pin | Other |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode | `$HOME/.opencode/bin` | `VERSION` | `--no-modify-path` |
| Kimi | `KIMI_INSTALL_DIR` | `KIMI_VERSION` | `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`; `KIMI_CODE_HOME` inside the release |
| Goose | `GOOSE_BIN_DIR` | `GOOSE_VERSION` | `CONFIGURE=false` |
| Memcode | `MEMCODE_INSTALL_DIR` | `MEMCODE_VERSION` (tag) | no TTY, so no sudo or first-run exec |
| fx | `FX_INSTALL_DIR` | tag as first argument | |
| OMP | `PI_INSTALL_DIR` | `--binary --ref v<ver>` | `--binary` avoids a bun source build |
| Qwen | `QWEN_INSTALL_LIB_DIR` / `QWEN_INSTALL_BIN_DIR` | `QWEN_INSTALL_VERSION` | `QWEN_INSTALL_METHOD=standalone`, `QWEN_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` |
| Codex | `CODEX_INSTALL_DIR` + private `CODEX_HOME` | `CODEX_RELEASE` | `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1`; the user's config, auth and own installs stay out |
| OpenCode 2 | `$HOME/.opencode/bin` | `VERSION` | `--no-modify-path`; keeps its own `opencode-v2` launcher |
| Amp | `AMP_HOME` | `AMP_VERSION` | its `~/.local/bin` link lands in the private HOME |
| Autohand | `AUTOHAND_INSTALL_DIR` | `AUTOHAND_VERSION` | skips zit, computer control, first run and local AI |
| Agy | `--dir` | none (latest) | the installed version is still checked against the release the update picked |
| Droid | AO downloads it | release path | its script runs `pkill -KILL droid`, so AO fetches `downloads.factory.ai/factory-cli/releases/<ver>/<os>/<arch>/droid` and verifies its published `.sha256` itself |

Every installer runs with:
- **A private `HOME` inside the release.** Any shell profile or config it writes stays in the release, not in the user's files. Sessions still run with the user's real `HOME`.
- **A system-only `PATH`** (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`). Several installers check the `opencode`/`kimi` already on `PATH`, to skip an install they think is current or to migrate or replace it. They must see neither the user's own copy nor AO's current release.
- **`SHELL=/bin/sh`.** Installers pick the profile they append `PATH` to from `SHELL`. fx, for one, writes `$HOME/.config/fish/config.fish` for fish users without creating its folder, and fails under `set -e`.

`InstallScriptCommand` gains `Args`, passed after the downloaded script, because some pins and opt-outs are flags only. The update advisory now reports these updates as `safe` while sessions run.

**The update keeps being offered.** Once AO runs its own release, sessions resolve AO's launcher, which is nowhere the vendor's installer puts the CLI. The advisory takes the maintenance method from the managed record (`official-installer`) instead of re-deriving it from the path, so the second and later updates are offered too. A recipe harness without an update command of its own (Memcode, OpenCode 2, Agy) is offered its managed recipe for the first update as well.

**Each recipe is pinned to the release its installer would install**, read where the installer reads it:

| Harness | Release source |
| --- | --- |
| OpenCode | npm `opencode-ai` (OpenCode 1 only; a 2.x there is refused). GitHub's Latest may be OpenCode 2, which `opencode.ai/install` exits on. |
| OpenCode 2 | `opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/npm`, as `opencode.ai/v2/install` reads it |
| Memcode | GitHub `memcode-ai/memcode` latest (`memcode.ai/dl` redirects there) |
| Qwen | npm `@qwen-code/qwen-code` latest, stable releases only. GitHub's Latest for the repository can be an SDK or desktop release, and the Aliyun pointer the installer reads is unreachable from some networks. npm publishes minutes after each release's standalone assets. |

**Reinstall repairs AO's release**, with the vendor's installer at the recorded release. For a managed Codex cask install that is Codex's installer, not `brew reinstall --cask codex`.

macOS and Linux only. Windows keeps update-when-idle, which now also covers every update on macOS and Linux that cannot run beside sessions. A terminal stopped for the update now exits the way **Exit agent** exits it: its launch is recorded as released before the runtime goes, and the session as exited after. The reaper therefore never ends it while the installer runs, and the batch's last check before installing no longer counts it as running. Before, a TUI session made the batch resume the old release and try again every poll, or was terminated by the reaper mid-install.

### Homebrew casks

Casks that ship one self-contained executable (**Claude Code, Copilot, Droid**) now update while sessions run. `brew upgrade --cask` deletes the old version folder, but a running process keeps the file it already opened and loads nothing else from there.

The **Codex** cask also ships `codex-resources`, which a running session can load after `brew upgrade --cask` deletes them. AO therefore updates a Codex cask install with Codex's official installer, into a release of its own. The install is pinned to the cask's latest version and the cask is left untouched. Sessions move to the managed release; the user's cask stays where it was until they upgrade it themselves.

The installers run in isolation:

- A managed official installer gets only its recipe's environment, plus locale, temp, proxy and TLS settings. An exported `KIMI_CODE_HOME` or `OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR` therefore cannot redirect the install into the user's files.
- Every downloaded installer runs from its private job directory.
- A cask counts as single-binary only when the exact audited cask (`claude-code`, `copilot-cli`, `droid`) owns the binary.

## Tests

- `TestOfficialManagedRecipesInstallInsideTheRelease`: each of the 13 recipes pins the release, installs inside the release directory, isolates `HOME` and `PATH`, and names a relative binary path.
- `TestOfficialInstallerUpdatesBesideARunningSession`: an OpenCode official-installer update with a live session succeeds instead of being refused. The installer runs with `HOME` inside `versions/v1` and `VERSION` set to the advisory's release, and the launcher resolves to the new release.

- `TestDroidDownloadsThePinnedReleaseWithoutItsScript`: Droid's download URL and checksum, the baseline build on Intel, and a refusal without a pinned release.
- `TestUpdateWhileRunningLevelMatrix`: only the audited single-binary casks are safe. Another cask for the same target stays `warn`, and so does a raw Codex cask upgrade.
- `TestCodexCaskUpdatesWithItsInstallerBesideARunningSession`: a Codex cask update with a live session runs no `brew` command. It runs one isolated Codex installer into `versions/v1`, pinned to the advisory's release, and the launcher resolves to the new release.
- `TestUpdatesThatCannotRunBesideSessionsWaitForIdleOnEveryPlatform`: on darwin, linux and windows, `warn` and `blocked` become `idle` when update-when-idle is on, and `blocked` when it is off.
- `TestRunInstallIsolatedKeepsUserVariablesOut`: an isolated installer runs in its given directory. An inherited `KIMI_CODE_HOME` does not reach it; a proxy setting does; the given `SHELL` wins over an inherited fish.
- `TestManagedOfficialReleaseStaysUpdatable`: Kimi is updated twice from its official install. Both advisories name `official-installer`, the installer is pinned to each release, and the launcher ends on `versions/v2`.
- `TestOfficialInstallsOfferTheirManagedRecipe`: Memcode, OpenCode 2, Qwen and Agy official installs get `official-installer` and their own release lookup. Without managed installs, only a harness with its own update command keeps a method.
- `TestOfficialManagedRecipesHaveAReleaseSource`: every recipe has a release source on darwin and linux, amd64 and arm64.
- `TestOpencodeOneNeverPinsAnOpencodeTwoRelease`: OpenCode 1 reads npm only, and refuses a 2.x there.
- `TestCodexCaskReinstallRepairsTheManagedRelease`: reinstalling a managed Codex cask release runs Codex's installer pinned to the recorded release and no `brew` command.
- `TestTerminalStoppedForUpdateSurvivesTheReaperAndResumes`: the real session manager, lifecycle and SQLite store stop an idle terminal, a reaper tick runs while the installer would be running, and the session is still live (exited, its launch released) and then restarts on a new launch.
- `TestIdleUpdateRunsAfterStoppingTerminalSessions` / `TestIdleUpdateNeverRunsBesideASessionThatWasNotStopped`: a stopped (exited) terminal does not keep the installer out; a live session that was not stopped still does.
- `TestQwenAdvisoryReadsTheCLIRelease`: with GitHub's Latest on an SDK release, an installed Qwen 0.26.0 is `behind_latest` 0.26.1, and a preview on npm is never offered.

Not yet run against the real vendor installers: CI covers the fixtures. A manual pass is needed for each installer on macOS: update with a session open, check that the session keeps the old release, and check that the user's own copy and shell files are untouched.

title: perf(pty-host): bound replay retention and stop probing replays
body:
Code changes: +424 -71\
Tests: +660 -6\
Others: +196 -0 (docs)

## What

Bound the pty-host replay ring by bytes and stop sending scrollback replay to probe and input-only connections, so status/get-output probes and fire-and-forget input sends no longer re-read and discard multi-megabyte session history.

## Why

On a live session the pty-host read 233 KB / 20 s from the agent PTY but wrote **31.7 MB / 20 s** to the daemon (~215x amplification, 7.8 GB lifetime), and the daemon read 89 MB / 20 s and discarded nearly all of it. Root cause: the ring retained 1000 "lines" with no byte bound, and full-screen TUIs produce megabyte-scale partial lines; every new connection got the entire ring replay, while probes open a fresh connection per poll. CPU cost scaled with history size x probe frequency.

Related: #6259 (unbounded partial line in the pty-host ring). This PR addresses that root cause but does not claim the issue, which is assigned.

## How

1. **Byte-bounded ring** (`ring.go`): `MaxRingBytes = 4 MiB`, partial lines split at `MaxRingLineBytes = 64 KiB`, head eviction, and `Replay()` still returns the retained byte stream unchanged, while `Tail(n)` counts completed logical lines (a chunked line is reassembled before it is counted) and `Snapshot()` excludes the in-progress line, including its chunks, exactly as `partialLine` did before the PR. Probe response tails are capped at `MaxTailBytes = 128 KiB` by the host handlers (`capTailBytes`), and replay is sent in `MaxReplayChunk = 256 KiB` frames instead of one multi-megabyte write.
2. **Connection classification** (`host.go`, `proto.go`, `attach.go`): new `MsgAttach = 0x0b` hello with `{cols, rows, replay}`, protocol v2 -> v3. The first frame classifies a connection as viewer (`MsgAttach` / `MsgResize` -> replay), input-only (`MsgTerminalInput` -> dispatched to the PTY, no replay, never broadcast to) or probe (status/get-output/kill -> no replay, skipped by broadcast). Silent connections and status-first legacy viewers upgrade after short graces; a later resize upgrades a probe, but a later input never does. `attach.go` sends the hello first and keeps `Resize` + `StatusReq` for old-host compatibility.

The design, cross-version compatibility matrix, and rollback are documented in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-pty-host-replay-cpu-and-quota-removal.md`. Old hosts ignore the unknown hello and replay on connect as before; old clients are classified from their first frame. Reverting the host restores v2 behavior. Old pty-host processes keep replaying to old daemons until sessions restart after an upgrade -- self-healing.

Accepted compatibility boundary: a hypothetical third-party client that sends `MsgTerminalInput` first without any hello/resize no longer receives a replay; every in-repo client sends the hello (new attach) or `MsgResize`/`MsgStatusReq` first (pre-hello attach) before any input.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/ -count=5`
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/`, plus a full `go test -race ./...` with **0 data races**
- Terminal/runtime adapter and session-manager suites
- New regression tests: `TestInputFirstConnectionIsInputOnly` (an input-first connection's bytes reach the PTY, and the connection receives no replay and no broadcast), plus the ring's logical-line suite: `TestRingTailReassemblesAChunkedCompletedLine`, `TestRingSnapshotExcludesAChunkedPartialLine`, `TestRingTailCountsLogicalLinesAcrossChunks`, `TestRingFlushPartialCompletesAChunkedLine`, `TestRingChunkBoundaryEdgeCases`
- Full backend `go test ./...`: only pre-existing failures reproduced identically on `main` (agent adapter/credential packages and `internal/integration`, all failing on this NTFS mount's writable-ancestor checks)
- `golangci-lint v2.13.2` with `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.1`: **0 issues**
- Lab run with a real `ao pty-host` and real PTY, 10 MB newline-free burst, 60 connections / 11 MB written, host CPU 0.2 s: 20 get-output probes = 2.62 MB total (payload capped at 131,072 B each), 20 status probes = 1.06 KB, viewer replay = 4.17 MB (ring cap), hello replay=false = 65 KB. Before: full ring replay per probe.

**Gaps:** macOS/Windows CI jobs and the Docker-based `agent-ci` e2e were not run locally (Linux-only environment, no Docker socket). No frontend files changed; the renderer/GPU trace is a separate follow-up.

title: fix(tmux): treat an absent legacy socket as missing without system tmux
body:
Code changes: +20 -0\
Tests: +61 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Reviewer launch no longer fails on Linux hosts that have no system tmux installed.

## Why

Fixes #6649

When AO uses its private tmux socket and no system tmux is on PATH, `socketForSession` had no client to probe the legacy default socket. Any session missing from the private socket was reported as an inconclusive probe. Reviewer launch destroys the stale reviewer pane first, so that error aborted every `ao review trigger` with `reviewer replace stale pane: tmux runtime: set detach-on-destroy ...`.

## How

Without a system tmux, check whether the legacy default socket file exists, resolved the same way tmux does (`$TMUX_TMPDIR` or `/tmp`, then `tmux-<uid>/default`).

- File missing: no legacy server can exist, so the private socket is used and a missing session is handled normally (Destroy treats it as already gone).
- File present: still returns `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, since a live legacy server could be behind it and only a matching client can ask it. This keeps the rule that an unknown probe is never treated as proof a session is dead.

Overlap note: #5587 edits the same file (the constructor near `legacyBinary`) but not `socketForSession`.

## Testing

Run on Fedora 44 x86_64.

- New `TestIsAliveTreatsAbsentLegacySocketAsMissingWithoutSystemTmux` and `TestDestroyMissingSessionSucceedsWithoutSystemTmux`. Both fail on main with the error from the issue and pass with this change.
- `TestIsAliveReportsMissingLegacyClientAsProbeInconclusive` now creates the socket file so it keeps covering the inconclusive case.
- `go vet` on the tmux and review packages.
- `go test -race` on `internal/adapters/runtime/tmux`, `internal/review`, `internal/terminal`, `internal/service/shellterm`.

body:
Code changes: +1180 -106  
Tests: +1404 -83

## What and why

Unify file selections and chat excerpts under Add to chat, with shared annotation previews in drafts and sent messages. Save captured code separately from the written question and preserve it through reload, queues and retry. Source checks explain changed/unavailable files without navigation in this PR.

Fixes the four P2 findings in [Ronish's earlier review](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6939#pullrequestreview-5620384743):
- Queued promotion formats annotations before steering; durable activity retains the original structured context.
- Native history matching reconstructs the dispatched prompt from saved captures/excerpts, including annotation-only messages and opaque provider-ID changes. Continuation context and malformed-history fallback remain compatible.
- Cloud uses the shared draft annotations and a renderer-only text-delivery mode. Captures become inline provider text once at the request boundary, without clipping again. Retries preserve saved code and client identity; cloud previews do not query the local daemon. Older local daemons retain unsupported drafts visibly.
- Current-workspace and supported PR single-commit views capture their immutable SHA and source through a shared helper. Other-branch, all-commit and composite snapshots remain unsupported because this reference contract cannot represent their comparison identity.

The earlier approximate-replay fix is retained: editing a later turn includes earlier captured code once before the replay budget, without reading current files. No additional public API, database or draft-format change was introduced for these review fixes.

## Implementation stages

1. Phase 1: shared annotations, delivery/history/cloud/single-commit fixes and regressions.
2. Phase 2: advisory source checks, with captured-only cloud previews.
3. Review hardening: early capture/ownership validation, bounded tolerant replay, quoted prompt paths, and throttled source checks.

title: fix(chat): keep answered questions and feedback in chat history
body:
Code changes: +111 -18  
Tests: +223 -5  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keep answered agent questions and submitted replies, including “Other” feedback, readable in chat history after the next question, a reload, and turn completion. Reset each new request’s form so previous answers do not carry over.

## Why

Answered questions currently disappear from the transcript, so users cannot review what the agent asked or the feedback they submitted. Consecutive questions can also inherit the previous selection and free-text reply.

Related: #6936

## How

Render the daemon’s existing persisted input resolutions as read-only history. Keep those records outside a completed turn’s collapsed work, and reset the question dock when its activity ID changes. Reuse the full-prompt selection used by the pending form.

The main regression risks are unusual provider form schemas, long-card scrolling, and draft retention during updates to the same pending question. Answer submission and daemon persistence use their existing paths. Model-output parity between terminal and chat remains unverified.

## Testing

- Added coverage for question/reply history during running and completed turns, consecutive questions, free-text feedback, multiple questions, selected option labels/descriptions, multi-select, false/zero values, skip/cancel, expired requests, and URL consent.
- Browser regression exercises submission, a second question with empty fields, reload, and completed-turn history.
- Passed locally: Node 22.23.2 lockfile compatibility, Node 24 E2E typecheck, the question-history browser regression and isolated switch-agent retry, renderer/docs builds, cloud-client checks (29 tests), product UI checks (160 tests), and macOS helper tests plus both architecture builds.
- Full Node 24 unit suite: 8,445 passed, 6 skipped across 501 files. Scoped changed-file/import typecheck and E2E typecheck passed. The full-project typecheck passed locally on Node 24 and in CI.
- Wider renderer smoke: 97/99 passed initially. The switch-agent startup timeout passed when rerun in isolation. The pointer-drag selection failure also reproduces on unchanged base `d1f210d9e7`.
- The guarded-navigation browser integration fails its drag-region assertion on both this branch and unchanged base `d1f210d9e7` on this macOS host.
- All five remote checks passed on `99af553ff3`: frontend test (including full-project typecheck, unit suite, docs/package checks, and guarded-navigation integration), renderer smoke, Intel macOS helper, secret scan, and review stats. [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/39292549055). Local container validation was unavailable because the Docker socket was missing; the corresponding Linux checks passed in CI.
- Tested the actual Electron app against an isolated scratch daemon/data/profile with live Claude Code: two separate structured requests, full question text, option labels/descriptions, Other feedback, empty second form, reload while pending, completed-turn reload with routine work collapsed, multi-question/multi-select, Back/Next draft retention, Skip, Cancel, navigating away/back, and long-text wrapping with the inspector open and enlarged text. Restored zoom after testing. Verified the saved input contents through the scratch daemon API. The lab used `AO_DISABLE_GPU=1` after its initial window failed to repaint; no GPU setting or product code was changed.

Manual test in a Claude Code chat running this branch:

1. Send: “This is a UI test. Do not run commands or modify files. Use AskUserQuestion to ask which fictional worktree I prefer, with options fix/login and fix/settings. After I answer, ask a second structured question, then summarize both replies and stop.”
2. Verify the full prompt is visible. Choose an option, type “Show me the names first” in Other, and continue.
3. Verify the first prompt, choice, and Other text remain visible while the second question appears. The second form must have no inherited selection or text.
4. Answer the second question, let the turn finish, collapse its work, then navigate away/back and reload. Both exchanges must remain readable.
5. Repeat with a multi-question/multi-select request and with Skip or Cancel. Verify answers match their prompts and skipped/cancelled requests are not shown as answered. Check a long prompt in a narrow window for wrapping and scrolling.

title: feat(session): refuse ao send to one-shot terminal harnesses
body:
Code changes: +81 -15\
Tests: +163 -0\
Others: +0 -0

Base: `main` (`f86a8c56e`). Branch `pr/send-gate` (`e4d211c5b`), one commit:
`feat(session): refuse ao send to one-shot terminal harnesses`.

## What

`ao send` to a TUI-mode session whose harness declares one-shot terminal
messaging is refused with 409 `HARNESS_ONE_SHOT` before anything is written to
the pane. The refusal names the harness and points at `ao spawn`. Chat-mode
sessions are relayed as before, and adapters that do not declare keep the
existing paste+Enter delivery.

The gate is harness-agnostic: this PR adds the optional
`ports.AgentTerminalMessagingDeclarer` capability (`TerminalMessaging()`
returning `ports.AgentTerminalMessagingOneShot`, wire value `one_shot`) and
the manager check; no shipped adapter declares it yet. The first declarer is the ZCode harness, which follows in a separate PR
stacked on this branch.

## Why

Some harnesses run their terminal launch as a one-shot turn (`<cli> -p
<prompt>`): the reply streams on the pane and the process exits into AO's
keep-alive shell. For such a session AO's message channel (tmux `send-keys`
of the text plus Enter at the foreground process) is wrong on both sides of
the exit: typing into the running one-shot CLI is undefined, and after it
exits, until the reaper's next tick flips the row to `exited`, the message is
typed at a live shell prompt and executed as a shell command in the
worktree. The session manager has no fact today that tells it apart, so it
needs the adapter to say so.

## How

- `ports/agent.go`: the `AgentTerminalMessaging` value type, its
  `AgentTerminalMessagingOneShot` constant and the
  `AgentTerminalMessagingDeclarer` interface, documented as a per-harness
  declaration, not a per-runtime-generation one: a restored generation of
  the same harness (for example an interactive `-c` resume) is refused too,
  because the session record carries nothing that distinguishes it from
  the one-shot launch.
- `session_manager/manager.go`: `Manager.send` reads the session row once
  (the same read now also feeds the existing Copilot orchestrator framing,
  extracted into `prepareOutboundMessage`) and, for a non-terminated row
  whose normalized mode is TUI and whose harness declares one-shot
  (`harnessTerminalOneShot`), returns the new `ErrHarnessOneShot` before
  the runtime guard and before any pane write. A terminated row falls
  through to the runtime guard and keeps the more precise
  `SESSION_TERMINATED`. An exited row is refused as `HARNESS_ONE_SHOT`:
  `AGENT_EXITED`'s "relaunch it" advice would not help for a harness whose
  relaunch is refused again.
- `service/session/service.go`: maps `ErrHarnessOneShot` to 409
  `HARNESS_ONE_SHOT` in the API error envelope.
- Tests: `TestSend_OneShotHarnessRefusesTerminalDelivery` (no pane write),
  `TestSend_OneShotHarnessDeadRowRefusals` (exited vs terminated rows),
  `TestSend_OneShotHarnessChatModeIsRelayed`,
  `TestSend_ConversationalHarnessUnaffected` and
  `TestSendSemantic_OneShotHarnessRefuses` in `manager_test.go`; the
  error-code mapping row in `service_test.go`.

Intentional omissions: no CLI change (the existing `ao send` surfaces the
daemon's error envelope and code unchanged), no DTO or OpenAPI change (the
error envelope shape is unchanged; only a new code value), and no adapter
declares the capability here.

## Testing

Rebased onto `main` `f86a8c56e` (the original commit was written against
`671b75f18`; the cherry-pick applied cleanly, only hunk offsets moved).
Validated on macOS (Go 1.27.2, darwin/arm64), mirroring `go.yml`:

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `gofmt -l .` | clean |
| `go build ./...` | exit 0 |
| `go vet ./...` | exit 0 |
| `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/session_manager ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/ports/... ./internal/httpd/...` | all ok (session_manager 184 s, service/session 45 s, httpd + apispec + specgen + controllers + envelope ok: route/spec parity unchanged) |

The full repo-wide `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` were run on the
stacked ZCode harness branch, which contains this commit unchanged (see that
PR's Testing section).

Not run locally: the `windows-workspace` job (no Windows runner), the
`lint` job as CI runs it (the pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 cannot read Go
1.27 export data on the validation machine; the touched packages were linted
clean with golangci-lint v2.15.0 under the repo config as part of the stacked
harness branch's `--new-from-rev=main` run), the
Docker-based `cloud-build-test` Expat step, and the GitHub Actions matrix
sharding itself. Please rely on CI for those.

The stacked ZCode harness PR adds the first declarer and pins it in the
agent registry test. Its live e2e runs confirm the chat-mode side of the
gate (`ao send` to a chat-mode zcode session is relayed into the
conversation, never gated); the TUI-mode refusal itself is covered by the
unit tests here, not by a live run.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change (no linked issue; groundwork for the ZCode harness PR)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: feat(zcode): add the ZCode harness (one-shot TUI and app-server chat driver)
body:
Code changes: +6373 -25\
Tests: +6525 -9\
Others: +206 -8

Base: `main` (`f86a8c56e`). This PR depends on the harness-agnostic `ao send`
gate in OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator#6944 and carries that one commit as
its first commit, because a cross-fork pull request cannot be based on a branch
in the fork. Once #6944 merges, this branch rebases to the eight zcode commits.
The counts above are against `main` and include that commit. Branch
`pr/zcode-harness` (`8ce600007`), nine commits:

0. `feat(session): refuse ao send to one-shot terminal harnesses` (= #6944)
1. `feat(zcode): add the ZCode harness adapter, registrations and migration`
2. `feat(zcode): declare one-shot terminal messaging so ao send is refused`
3. `feat(zcode): API-key provider config and hidden ao zcode-login`
4. `feat(zcode): zcodeproto wire types, methods and provenance catalog`
5. `docs(ports): ChatDeferredTurnStarter also covers ack-first protocols`
6. `feat(zcode): app-server chat driver`
7. `fix(chat): drop the cached probe when Start reports auth required`
8. `docs(zcode): harness documentation`

## What

Adds **ZCode** (Z.AI's GLM coding CLI, binary `zcode`, currently 0.16.9) as a
harness in both session modes:

- **TUI mode**: a one-shot `zcode -p <prompt> --cwd <worktree>` turn per spawn.
  The reply streams in the pane and the process exits into AO's keep-alive
  shell. Standing instructions are prepended to the prompt (zcode has no
  system-prompt flag), the permission mode is pinned to `--mode edit` instead
  of zcode's flagless `yolo` default for `--prompt` runs, and restore is the
  cwd-scoped `zcode -c` with the same mode flags re-applied. The adapter
  declares one-shot terminal messaging, so `ao send` to a TUI zcode session is
  refused with 409 `HARNESS_ONE_SHOT` (the gate from the base PR) instead of
  being typed into the exiting CLI or executed by the keep-alive shell.
- **Chat mode** (the default for a non-standalone spawn): the new
  `zcodeappserver` chat driver runs a persistent `zcode app-server --stdio
  --cwd <worktree>` behind AO's detached chat host (`ProtocolRaw`, NDJSON over
  stdin/stdout) and maps the app-server protocol onto AO's chat events:
  streaming text and reasoning, tool activity, approvals
  (`interaction/requestPermission`, answered on every re-announced frame id),
  user questions (`requestUserInput`), interrupts (`session/stop`), per-turn
  model and reasoning-level selection validated against the advertised
  catalog, usage and context occupancy, history import through `session/read`
  after a restart or TUI handoff, `session/resume` in a replacement process
  when the host is gone, hibernate/resume, and live reconnect that adopts the
  durable running turn. The wire vocabulary lives in `zcodeproto`, hand-written
  (zcode ships no schema generator) with a provenance catalog: every method
  the driver sends or reads is either PROVEN by a Phase 1 capture (the
  `testdata/*.ndjson` fixtures are extracted verbatim from those captures) or
  STATIC from the bundle and kept behind fail-closed branches.

Everything a harness needs to be enumerable is wired: domain enum, agent and
chat-driver registries, model catalog, agentauth login plan, systeminstall
target (an explicit not-installable entry: zcode ships inside the ZCode desktop
app, which installs no CLI launcher, so the `zcode` launcher is user-provided;
see the reviewer note), spawn CLI/skill help, DTO enums (`openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`
regenerated with `npm run api`), the product-ui agent list and a renderer
avatar.

## Why

Lets an AO board run GLM workers next to Claude/Codex ones: a Claude
orchestrator spawning a zcode worker with `ao spawn --agent zcode --mode chat`,
sending it follow-ups with `ao send`, and seeing it die when its process does
(GLM's duo test below). No linked issue; feature work done on the integration
branch of this fork and brought to `main` here.

## How

### Credentials

Two credential routes exist; chat mode is built for the first.

- **Coding-plan API key (recommended).** The agentauth plan for zcode is a
  login-menu plan that launches the hidden `ao zcode-login --executable
  <zcode> --provider-config <path>`: option 1 runs the CLI's own `zcode login
  zai` browser flow, option 2 reads a Z.AI Coding Plan API key without echo,
  trims it, and writes an AO-owned personal provider config to `<AO data
  dir>/harnesses/zcode/provider_config.json` (atomic write, mode `0600`,
  directory chmodded to `0700` after `MkdirAll` because the zcode CLI creates
  it first with its own umask). The file names the `zai-api` template provider
  `zai-api-ao` with `GLM-5.3` and `GLM-5.3-Flash`. The auth probe reports
  `authorized` while that file holds a key (the absent file is the normal
  state for OAuth-only users and records no diagnostic; an unparseable or
  blank-key file is `credential_file_invalid`), and every launch (TUI and
  chat) exports `ZCODE_PERSONAL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE` only under the same
  predicate. Only the path is ever exported or printed; the key is never
  logged, returned or echoed.
- **OAuth login (still offered).** `zcode login zai` against AO's isolated
  credential store at `<AO data dir>/harnesses/zcode` (exported as
  `ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR`). The raw z.ai token lives one hour with no refresh
  flow, so the probe reports `needs auth` once it expires. It works for the
  TUI path.
- **Why the app server cannot use the OAuth account.** In app-server mode the
  CLI asks its host, per turn, for `interaction/requestProviderRuntimeHeaders`
  and expects the host to mint the runtime credential: raw OAuth token ->
  `POST https://api.z.ai/api/auth/z/login` -> business token -> project
  lookup -> project access token, plus an `accountScope` hash (all private
  surface of the desktop app; details in the fork's HANDOFF.md, Phase 1
  findings). Unanswered, the request times out and blocks the serial request
  queue. AO does not play that host role, so chat mode requires a provider
  that needs no runtime headers: the coding-plan API key route, on which the
  app server never sent that request in any capture. `docs/harnesses/zcode.md`
  states this.
- An operator-set `ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR` or `ZCODE_PERSONAL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE`
  in the daemon environment wins over AO's values on every path.
- `fix(chat)`: when `Start` reports auth required after a successful
  capability probe (a credential that lapsed), the cached probe is dropped so
  the next spawn is refused up front by the preflight check instead of after
  a worktree exists. This is in `service/chat` and applies to every driver.

### Migration

The sessions.harness `CHECK` is widened by a new migration. On the integration
branch it was `0207_allow_zcode_harness.sql`; `main` has since used 0210-0215
and switched new migrations to UTC ids (`npm run migration:create`, #6640), so
it is now `20261019154945497_allow_zcode_harness.sql`, with the matching
`shippedMigrations` ledger entry in `migrate_burned_versions_test.go` (kept in
its own alignment block so gofmt does not reflow the whole map). The SQL is
unchanged: it anchors on the retained `'fake'` tail of the constraint
(`replace(sql, "'fake'))", "'zcode', 'fake'))")`) like the Command Code and
Memcode migrations, so it composes with whichever constraint shape a database
arrives with. `reconcileHarnessConstraint` in `sqlite/db.go` gets the
`needsZcode` arm beside `needsMemcode`/`needsCommandCode`, plus the
post-repair check, for databases that skipped the migration.

### Context cost and the mcpServers trim

Every app-server session loads the CLI's configured MCP servers and plugins
into the model context. On the development machine, with a large global MCP
server in `~/.zcode/cli/config.json`, that was ~270k input tokens per turn in
the Phase 1 probes. Chat mode therefore passes AO's own tool servers as
`session/create.mcpServers`, which replaces the operator's global
`config.mcp.servers` for the session (plugin-provided servers are still merged
in), and disables the CLI's own title generation on create. Measured per-turn
cost in the e2e runs: ~30.4k input tokens (mostly cache reads after the first
turn), 3-37 output tokens for one-word replies.

### Rebase notes

Rebuilt as a linear series on top of `main`'s 23 new commits. Conflicts were
all "add zcode beside memcode": `domain/harness.go`, `dto.go` enums,
`spawn.go` help, `systeminstall.go` targets and enum, `product-ui/agents.ts`,
`openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` (then regenerated: no drift), `sqlite/db.go`
(arm order: Memcode, then ZCode) and the migration ledger. The chat-driver
registry's new `add(driver, plugin)` shape registers the zcode plugin as a
binary-resolution invalidator. Two small adaptations to upstream's
harness-update work (#6745) live in the adapter: `InvalidateBinaryResolution`
(the adapter caches its executable path) and
`SupportsTerminalVersionRefresh() == false` (the terminal restore is the
cwd-scoped `zcode -c`, not an exact native conversation id, and there is no
installer AO could run), which `TestEveryRefreshHarnessResumesExactConversation`
now requires of every shipped adapter. Two upstream tests that enumerate every
harness are adjusted: the systeminstall plan count (37 -> 38) and
`TestTerminalRefreshSupportMatrix`, where zcode joins the explicit opt-out
list beside memcode.

### Reviewer notes

- **Avatar**: `zcode-light.svg`/`zcode-dark.svg` are a preliminary "Z"
  monogram, not Z.AI's mark. Happy to swap for whatever the project prefers.
- **Dev-built daemon and Claude chat mode**: the duo test below spawns a
  claude-code orchestrator from a daemon built with `go build ./cmd/ao`. That
  binary looks for AO's ACP runtime beside itself and fails the spawn with
  `CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE` without it; symlinking the installed app's
  `Contents/Resources/acp-runtime` next to the binary, or setting
  `AO_ACP_RUNTIME_DIR` on the daemon, fixes it. Not a zcode matter, but worth
  a line in the dev docs eventually.
- **The launcher is user-provided**: the ZCode desktop app installs no CLI
  launcher; nothing named `zcode` lands on `PATH`. The CLI is
  `Contents/Resources/glm/zcode.cjs` inside the app and only reaches its
  provider with the environment the desktop app would give it, so AO resolves
  a `zcode` executable (`PATH`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`,
  `~/.local/bin`) and never a bare `zcode.cjs`, and `docs/harnesses/zcode.md`
  carries the wrapper script verbatim: it exports `ZCODE_BASE_URL` and
  `ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE`, keeps a preset
  `ZCODE_PERSONAL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE` and `ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR` (the
  `[ -n "$X" ] || export X=...` guards are load-bearing: AO presets both, and
  an unconditional export would silently replace AO's provider config and
  credential store with the wrapper's own), then `exec node .../zcode.cjs "$@"`.
  The systeminstall entry's reason text says the same. Every run in the
  evidence below used exactly that wrapper. Letting the adapter launch `node
  <bundle>` with that environment itself would remove the dependency; listed
  under follow-ups.
- **Permissions**: chat-mode approvals are proven under `edit` only (`build`,
  AO's `auto` mapping, is untested). Read-only sessions are refused: zcode's
  `plan` is a planning mode, not a provider-enforced sandbox.
- **stderr**: the app server's stderr is discarded; the CLI's credential
  logger writes there.

### Intentional omissions and follow-ups

- The auto-title side task asks the driver for a read-only session, which
  `validateStart` refuses, so zcode sessions get no generated title (an INFO
  line per spawn, `generated=false`). Follow-up: map ReadOnly onto zcode's
  `plan` mode for tool-less side tasks, or skip task naming for drivers
  without a read-only mode.
- Per-worktree `.zcode/config.json` with `plugins.enabled:false` would also
  drop the plugin servers and the skills index from the context; the one-shot
  path has no per-session parameters, so the same trim would apply there.
- `aoDataDir` documents that a relative `AO_DATA_DIR` is unsupported for the
  zcode probes until daemon startup re-exports `cfg.DataDir`.
- No "forget API key" action: the provider config is removed by deleting the
  file under `<AO data dir>/harnesses/zcode/`.
- The adapter could launch `node .../zcode.cjs` with the provider environment
  itself (a `binaryutil` spec for the bundle path plus the exports in
  `AugmentRuntimeLaunchEnv`) and drop the user-provided launcher; not done
  here, since the resolution contract (an executable on `PATH`) is what every
  other harness uses.
- Other one-shot terminal harnesses (auggie, deepseek) could declare
  `AgentTerminalMessagingOneShot` too; not done here, one harness per PR.
- TUI mode has no workspace hooks in v1 (zcode hooks live in per-plugin
  `hooks.json` manifests), so a TUI session's active work reads as idle; the
  reaper flips it to exited within one tick of `zcode -p` returning. Chat mode
  reports activity from the protocol.
- No steer, compaction, fork or rollback through the app server yet; tool
  output is not streamed by the app server; tool parts of the native
  transcript are not imported (no capture covered one).
- Mid-session agent switching (upstream #6588, merged into this branch on
  2026-10-21) scopes its targets to the lists in
  `frontend/src/renderer/lib/agent-switch-targets.ts`; zcode is not added.
  The chat driver carries a system prompt as a first-message preamble, so a
  handoff note would reach it, but that file admits an agent only after a
  real switch passes and none has been run to or from zcode. The picker
  always lists the running agent, so a zcode chat is unaffected.

Reference: `docs/harnesses/zcode.md`.

## Testing

Validated on macOS (Go 1.27.2, darwin/arm64, Node 24.21.0), mirroring
`go.yml`, `frontend.yml` and the drift jobs as far as one machine allows. The
full runs below were made on the series before the two review amendments
(`2b2431b12`: lint directives, the launcher wording and the harness listings
are the only differences); the affected gates were rerun on the final head
`8ce600007` and are listed after the table.

| gate (CI job) | result |
|---|---|
| `gofmt -l .` (backend-core) | clean |
| `go build ./...` (backend-core) | exit 0 |
| `go vet ./...` (backend-core) | exit 0 |
| `go test -count=1 -timeout=20m ./...` | 204 packages ok; 4 FAIL under full-suite load, all pre-existing load-flaky integration tests unrelated to this change: acp `TestACPReplayLoadLargeHistoryThroughSDK`, conpty `TestDarwinPTYCloseDoesNotWaitOutAShellThatIgnoresSIGTERM`, tmux `TestRuntimeIntegrationLegacyDefaultSocketDestroyEnforcesDetachOnDestroy` and `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell`, observe/activity `TestObserverIntegrationReconcilesRealTmuxOutputIntoSQLite`. acp, both tmux tests and observe/activity each pass when rerun alone with `-count=1`. conpty `TestDarwinPTYCloseDoesNotWaitOutAShellThatIgnoresSIGTERM` is a darwin-only timing test (500 ms grace, observed 502-504 ms): it failed twice more when rerun alone on the loaded machine, fails identically 3/3 on `main` `f86a8c56e` on the same machine, passed 3/3 with `-count=3` once the machine was idle, and is not part of CI's Linux matrix. |

title: [Feature]: Pool of models/harnesses per role, with quota failover
body:
### Problem

As someone running AO with more than one subscription, I want to  attach several models/harnesses to a project under Workers, Reviewers, and Orchestrator. Today each role gets one agent and one model. When that subscription hits its limit, that role stops. I have other paid capacity sitting unused.

I want two things from the pool:
1. Spread work across the list so one subscription does not take every call.
2. When a model hits its subscription limit, keep going on the next one in the list instead of waiting for reset.

This applies to workers, reviewers, and the orchestrator.  Potentially the orchestrator is only for fallback, not for load sharing.


### Proposed direction

In project settings, let each role (Worker, Reviewer, Orchestrator) have an ordered list of harness + model pairs, not a single pick.
 
- New sessions / new turns take the next available entry so load spreads across subscriptions.
- If the current entry is exhausted, AO continues on the next one that still has quota.
- Same job, same branch/worktree/PR when the switch happens mid-session.

### Alternatives considered

Alternatives considered:                                         
- Commenting on #4918 and waiting. That issue is failover for one primary, not a pool I can assign under each role.
- Switching the project default by hand when a quota dies. This works, but I have to notice.
- Waiting for reset (#6241). Leaves the other subscriptions idle.

Related open issues:              
- #4918 is the closest. It asks for an ordered fallback list and a quota handoff (Claude → Codex Terra). It does not add a pool per role or spread new work across several subscriptions.
- #6156 pins one provider per role.
- #6696 switches Claude accounts by hand.
- #6241 waits for the same quota to reset.
- #3802 is manual failover on a paused session.
- #6917 maps extra roles (Design, QA, Architect) to different agents. That is a different problem. 



### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix: refresh existing Claude chats for task tools
body:
Code changes: +233 -18  
Tests: +534 -7  
Others: +51 -1

## What

Existing Claude chats can pick up AO's task-tool settings after an app update while keeping their native conversation history.

## Why

Surviving provider processes skip launch setup when AO adopts them. They can therefore keep task tools disabled even after the app updates.

Related: #6902

## How

- Adopt live hosts first and compare an additive launch revision. Refresh through the existing native-resume path only when the session has no running or queued turn, pending decision, or active/unknown background work.
- Sweep idle, unviewed chats even with optional hibernation disabled; a send can refresh a viewed idle chat. Include orchestrators while retaining their ordinary hibernation exclusion. Honor explicit task-tool opt-outs.
- Persist refresh recovery intent atomically with shutdown intent. Sends queue before their own wake; pending refresh intent also admits concurrent sends after another failed wake clears the sleep marker. Accepted messages stay queued through failed shutdown, failed resume, and daemon restart. Clear the intent after compatible provider admission or explicit Stop.

title: fix(sidebar): match session dots to board cards and surface sessions that need input
body:
## What

The sidebar session dots used the old attention-zone colours (purple, yellow, green, grey). The kanban cards show none of that: they colour by lane. This makes the sidebar say the same thing as the card.

## Changes

- **Dot colour follows the card's lane.** Building is blue, Validating is yellow, In review is amber, Ready is green, Archive is grey. A merged PR in Ready is purple, matching the card's "Merged" text.
- **Needs-you override.** Needs input, Blocked, "CI failing" and "Changes requested" show the orange-red dot, the same states the card flags. It beats the lane colour, so a session waiting on you with an open PR no longer looks calm.
- **Needs input gets a red alert icon** in place of the dot, and those sessions sit at the top of their project list (and the standalone list). Manual order and recency order still hold inside each group.
- **Merged and closed PRs hold still.** The dot no longer pulses and the card no longer shows a loader when the PR is merged or closed, even if the agent keeps running. The card's "Merged" text is now purple instead of the lane's green.

- **Validating is cyan, not yellow.** Yellow and the amber of In review were close to indistinguishable on an 8px dot (colour distance 26 in dark, 17 in light). Validating is now `#22d3ee` in dark and `#0891b2` in light, which lifts the closest pair of lane colours to about 42. The column header, card status text and sidebar dot all use the one token, so they change together. Themes derive Validating as a teal between their own blue and green, because Dracula and Monokai use the same hex for cyan and blue, and Rosé Pine uses the same hex for cyan and green. `DESIGN.md` is updated.

## Notes

- In themes, needs-you and In review are still close (In review is a mix of orange and yellow). That predates this PR and is not changed here.

- `Mergeable` and `Approved` still show the loader while the agent works. An existing test keeps that on purpose, because the work has not landed.
- Idle sessions with no PR are now blue, since the card puts them in Building.
- The `needsInput` flag is exposed on `getSessionStatusDotView`. The child-session list and link preview card only read the colour, so they show the orange-red dot for needs-input.

## Testing

- `vitest`: Sidebar, SessionsBoard and session-presentation suites pass (290 tests). New cases cover each lane colour, the needs-you override, the alert icon, ordering, and the merged/closed no-pulse and no-loader rules.
- Checked in the dev app against a fresh daemon with a project of 17 seeded sessions covering building, validating, in review, ready and archive, plus edge cases (needs input with an open PR, CI failing with the agent idle, a merged and a failing PR on one session).
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean outside `packages/product-ui`, which has no `node_modules` in my worktree.

title: feat(sidebar): preview the board card when hovering a session row
body:
Stacked on #6951 (the sidebar status fix). Merge that first; this PR's diff is only the hover preview.

## What

Hovering a session row in the sidebar shows its board card to the right of the row, so you can read a session's state without opening it.

## Behaviour

- **The real card.** It renders the same board card component, not a copy, so it stays in sync. It is static: no click target, no archive button, and no attention pulse (a needs-input card keeps its tint and border).
- **First hover.** Opens after about 350ms and fades in with a small slide. It does not zoom, and closing is instant.
- **Sweeping.** Once a preview is showing, moving to another row swaps it instantly with no animation. After the pointer has been off every row for about 300ms, the next hover is delayed and animated again.
- **Stays out of the way.** The preview ignores the pointer, never opens for touch, closes while you drag a row, and does not open on the inline rename editor.

## Implementation

- `useSessionPreviewHover` owns the open state and the delay. The rows share one "warm" flag. Each row handles its own pointer and focus events so leaving a row always cancels a pending open. A controlled Radix hover card never reports a close for a card that has not opened yet, so relying on its callback left delayed opens running and stacked cards after a quick sweep. There is a test for that sweep.
- `HoverCardContent` gets an `animation` option (`"full"` default, `"enter"`, `"none"`). Other hover cards keep their current animation.
- `SessionCardView` gets a `still` prop that drops the attention pulse and the list role.

## Testing

- `vitest`: Sidebar, SessionsBoard, session-presentation and AppLink suites pass (300 tests). New tests cover the delayed first open, the instant swap, the quick sweep across cold rows (only the last card shows), and going cold again.
