title: fix(review): find a just-opened PR when ao review trigger runs
body:
Code changes: +380 -21\
Tests: +569 -4\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When a worker tracks no open PR yet and no `--pr` is given, `ao review trigger` now looks up open PRs from the worker's branch and reviews the one the signed-in account opened. A PR another author opened on the same branch is never attached automatically; the error names it and gives the `--pr` override. If it cannot, the error names the branch and gives the exact retry command:

> AO is not tracking an open PR for worker "mer-1" yet and found no open PR from its branch "ao/mer-1/fix"; if you just opened one, run `ao review trigger mer-1 --pr <url>` with that PR's URL

## Why

Closes #7302

The first trigger right after `gh pr create` failed with `REVIEW_INVALID` until the SCM observer's next poll discovered the PR.

## How

- `session.Service.FindBranchPRs` (`backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go:549`) asks the SCM provider for the open PRs from the session's branch, through a new `ListOpenPRsByBranch` (GitHub `pulls?head=<owner>:<branch>&state=open`, GitLab `merge_requests?source_branch=<branch>&state=opened`, multi provider delegates). It looks in the project's canonical/origin repository and, for a workspace project, in every child repository from `ListWorkspaceRepos` with a parseable origin: the same repositories `ClaimPR` accepts, with the same branch name, as the SCM observer does. A repository whose provider cannot list by branch is skipped; any other listing error fails the lookup. The provider filters on the server in one request, so a repository's other open PRs are never paged through. GitHub reads one page of 100 on purpose: it allows one open PR per head and base. GitHub's `head=<owner>:<branch>` excludes forks; GitLab drops MRs whose source project differs from the target project and reports the project as both head and base. Results are still checked for the exact branch, and forks (head repo ≠ base repo) and closed/merged PRs are skipped. The method is optional on the session service's SCM dependency, so claim-only fakes keep working.
- Authorship: the lookup applies the SCM observer's discovery rule, now shared as `ports.SCMIdentity.Authored` (`backend/internal/ports/scm_observations.go:112`, used by the observer at `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go:1196`): a PR counts as the worker's own only when its author matches the signed-in human account's login (case-insensitive). `FindBranchPRs` returns own and other-author PRs separately (`BranchPRs{Own, OtherAuthor}`). The account is resolved once per provider/host, only when a candidate PR exists; if it cannot be resolved, or is not a user account, the lookup fails rather than guess.
- `review.Service.refreshPRs` → `attachBranchPR` (`backend/internal/service/review/review.go:548,606`) runs when the worker has no open tracked PR (none tracked, or only closed/merged ones):
  - exactly one own match: attached through the existing claim path (`RefreshPR` → `ClaimPR`, never a takeover), then reviewed. If the attach fails (e.g. the PR closed in between), the error says the PR was found on the branch but could not be attached, keeps the claim's error class, and gives the exact retry command.
  - another author's PR(s) only: `REVIEW_INVALID` saying a PR from another author was found on the branch and is not attached automatically, with `ao review trigger <worker> --pr <url>` for each as the override. Naming a PR with `--pr` is unchanged and skips the branch lookup.
  - several own matches: `REVIEW_INVALID` listing `ao review trigger <worker> --pr <url>` for each.
  - lookup failure: `REVIEW_INVALID` saying AO could not look up the branch's PRs, with the exact retry command.
  - no match: the trigger tells the engine through `TriggerOptions.BranchPRLookupFoundNone`.
- Engine error (`backend/internal/review/review.go:788`) gives the exact retry command with the worker id, so it also works for an orchestrator triggering a worker's review. It says the worker's branch has no open PR only when a lookup ran and found none; otherwise (auto-review, no branch lookup) it says only that AO is not tracking an open PR. A worker whose tracked PRs are all closed or merged gets the same error instead of `no open PR head to review`.
- Auto-review is unchanged: it does not refresh PRs.

Exact branch match only. A PR on a child branch of the session namespace is still found by the observer's prefix matching on its next poll, or attached with `--pr`.

Separate PR from the "review done" message (#6955): a different problem in a different code path (trigger-time PR attachment vs. end-of-run delivery). The two branches merge cleanly with each other, #6831 and #6821.

## Testing

Clean env (all `AO_*` unset):
- `go test ./...`: all pass except `internal/integration` `TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch`, which fails the same way on `origin/main` locally.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2 (Go 1.27.1): 0 issues.
- `go test -race` for `internal/review`, `internal/service/review`, `internal/service/session`, `internal/daemon`, `internal/ports`, `internal/observe/scm`, `internal/adapters/scm/...`: pass.
- New/updated tests:
  - session: matches only the open same-repo PR from the session branch, queried for the canonical repo and the session branch; a workspace project also looks in each child repository (root listed once, an unsupported child skipped, a failing child named in the error); no branch or no listing capability finds nothing; another author's PR (or one with no author) is returned apart from the own PR, with the account resolved once; a bot account, an account without a login, or a failed identity lookup fails the lookup naming the PR, and no identity is needed when nothing matches; a child repository's other-author PR is kept apart too.
  - review service: one branch PR is attached before planning, also when only a closed PR is tracked; a lookup error reports the failure with the exact retry; an attach failure after the lookup says the PR was found, keeps the error class and gives the retry; several PRs fail with an exact command per PR and nothing attached; the engine is told the lookup found none only when it ran and found nothing; another author's PR is not attached and the error names it with the `--pr` override; the own PR is still attached beside another author's; a named `--pr` is attached without a branch lookup.
  - engine: the error names the branch and `ao review trigger mer-1 --pr <url>` after a lookup that found none, does not claim the branch has no PR without one, and a session with only a closed tracked PR gets the same retry command.
  - ports: `SCMIdentity.Authored` matches a human account's login case- and space-insensitively and never matches for a bot or empty login.
  - providers: GitHub sends `head=<owner>:<branch>` in one request; GitLab sends `source_branch` and drops a fork MR with the same branch name; both keep the PR author; multi delegates or reports unsupported.
  - daemon: the wired SCM provider implements `ListOpenPRsByBranch` and `ScopedIdentityResolver`; the review refresher keeps own and other-author PRs apart.

## Checklist

title: [Bug]: Release latest guard has skipped every run since 10-05; main's frontend/package.json (0.13.0) is behind v0.14.3
body:
The "Release latest guard" workflow has skipped both of its jobs (`latest-release` and `package-version`) on every run since 2026-10-05. That is roughly 400 hourly and release runs so far. The last run that executed the jobs, on 2026-10-05, failed `package-version`, and the condition it flagged is still true today: `frontend/package.json` on `main` is `0.13.0`, while the latest stable release is `v0.14.3`.

### Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-10-19 around 21:20 UTC, with `main` at 4f5117479760.

- **Run history** (`gh run list -R OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator --workflow release-latest-guard.yml`):
  - Runs succeeded through 2026-09-26.
  - `package-version` then failed on every run up to [37256614665](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/37256614665) (2026-10-05 02:45 UTC).
  - All 408 runs from [37260303427](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/37260303427) (2026-10-05 03:39 UTC) onward are `skipped`. In the latest, [39319395033](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/39319395033), both jobs show `skipped` with no steps.
- **Job condition.** Both jobs still have `if: github.repository == 'Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator'` ([L17](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/4f5117479760482a2ba58e9d12239f627a791a00/.github/workflows/release-latest-guard.yml#L17), [L67](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/4f5117479760482a2ba58e9d12239f627a791a00/.github/workflows/release-latest-guard.yml#L67)). `gh api repos/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator --jq .full_name` now returns `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`. This is the only workflow that hard-codes a repository name. `deploy-docs.yml` and `harness-release-feeds.yml` skip forks with `!github.event.repository.fork` instead. #3236 changed the same line after the previous rename (AgentWrapper → Untrivial-ai).
- **Job script.** I ran the `package-version` step script unchanged, with `REPO=OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`, against `main`'s `frontend/package.json`. Two runs gave the same output:

title: fix(cloud): wait for the user after a failed Setup instead of re-running it
body:
Code changes: +12 -0\
Tests: +14 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

After a cloud session's Setup step (or checkout) fails, the worker now waits for the user to retry or reopen the session. It no longer re-runs Setup on its own a second later and starts the agent when that re-run passes.

## Why

A tester's Setup step timed out after 10 minutes, and the chat showed "Setup step 1 timed out" immediately followed by "Setup finished in 1m 6s"; the agent then worked on an environment whose setup had just failed. Worker log:

```
15:59:36 WARN project setup: a step did not succeed; the agent will not start status=timed_out step=1
16:00:43 INFO project setup: finished status=succeeded duration_ms=66243
```

Opening a cloud session sends a workspace request to the worker (`SessionView` → `requestWorkspaceCheckout`). While Setup runs, the worker saves one such request (`RequestCheckout`, a one-slot channel). After a failure, the Setup loop waits on that channel for the reopen that should trigger a retry, and the request saved during the failed attempt satisfied it at once. The re-run started about one second after the failure; it passed in the tester's case because containers started by the timed-out step kept running.

## How

`dropPendingReopen` discards a reopen request saved while the failed attempt ran, right before the failure is reported. A retry the user asks for after seeing the failure is never dropped. It is called at both failure points that wait for a reopen: the checkout loop and the Setup loop in `ao-worker/main.go`.

The Setup success row now says "Setup passed" instead of "Setup finished" (all locales). After a failure and a Retry, "Setup step 1 failed" followed by "Setup finished in 0s" read as Setup being skipped and the agent starting anyway.

Not in this change: the 10-minute per-step Setup timeout and a "still running, keep waiting or cancel" prompt.

## Testing

**End to end on the local cloud stack** (`npm run cloud:local`, Docker sandbox provider), same scenario against a worker image built from `main` and one built from this branch. A project's Setup step fails on its first run and passes on its second:

```sh
if [ -f /tmp/ao-setup-once ]; then echo "second run: passing"; else touch /tmp/ao-setup-once; echo "first run: failing in 60s"; sleep 60; exit 1; fi
```

A driver made the desktop's calls over the control-plane API: create the task, `POST /sessions/{id}/workspace/checkout` at +5 s, +20 s and +40 s into Setup (what opening the session sends; each returned `requested: true`), wait 45 s after the failure, then one more checkout (Retry). Session events (`/chat-events`):

| | Worker from `main` | Worker from this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Setup step 1 fails (+61 s) | yes | yes |
| Right after the failure | `workspace.setup succeeded` and `agent.ready` in the same second, no retry | nothing for 45 s |
| After Retry | n/a | `workspace.setup succeeded` (8 ms), then `agent.ready` |

```
main     01:56:17 workspace.setup failed (step 1, exit 1, 60012 ms)
         01:56:17 workspace.setup succeeded (1 ms)        <- no retry was requested
         01:56:17 agent.ready
branch   01:51:34 workspace.setup failed (step 1, exit 1, 60020 ms)
         ...      no events for 45 s
         01:52:20 workspace/checkout (Retry)
         01:52:21 workspace.setup succeeded (8 ms)
         01:52:21 agent.ready
```

The branch image's `/ao-worker` contains `dropPendingReopen`; the `main` image's does not.

**A Setup step that always fails never starts the agent**, Retry included (local stack, this branch's worker; step `echo "this step always fails"; exit 1`, two Retries 10 s apart):

```
+1.1s   workspace.setup failed exit=1
+11.1s  Retry 1 → +12.2s workspace.setup failed exit=1
+22.2s  Retry 2 → +23.2s workspace.setup failed exit=1
+43.2s  no agent.ready; no claude process in the worker container
```

**Production, before the fix:** the same Setup step in two sessions opened during Setup shows `workspace.setup failed` and then `workspace.setup succeeded` 1-2 s later with no retry, and the agent started.

**Unit and checks** (in `cloud/`): `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/ao-worker/`, `gofmt -l`, `go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/ao-worker/` pass, including the new `TestAnOpenSavedBeforeAFailedStartIsNotARetry`. Frontend: `vitest run` on `ChatTimelineItems`, `CloudSessionChatSurface` and `i18n` (80 tests) passes.

Takes effect for users once a new ao-worker image is deployed.

title: fix(billing): say Free connects from anywhere via Tailscale or the tunnel
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #6963, under the founder's "don't undersell" directive. The Free plan card said "Same-network connectivity (no cloud relay)". That suggests Free users can reach their computer only on the same network, but Connect Mobile on every plan also offers the computer's Tailscale address and a managed HTTPS tunnel (`cloudflared`). This PR changes `settings.billing.freeNetwork` in all 8 locales to match the docs (#6912 and #6915):

| Locale | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| en | Same-network connectivity (no cloud relay) | Connect on the same network, or from anywhere with Tailscale or the HTTPS tunnel |
| de | Verbindung im selben Netzwerk (kein Cloud-Relay) | Verbindung im selben Netzwerk oder von überall über Tailscale oder den HTTPS-Tunnel |
| es | Conexión en la misma red (sin relay en la nube) | Conexión en la misma red, o desde cualquier lugar con Tailscale o el túnel HTTPS |
| fr | Connexion sur le même réseau (sans relais cloud) | Connexion sur le même réseau, ou de n'importe où via Tailscale ou le tunnel HTTPS |
| ja | 同一ネットワーク内での接続（クラウドリレーなし） | 同一ネットワークで接続、または Tailscale か HTTPS トンネルでどこからでも接続 |
| ko | 같은 네트워크 연결 (클라우드 릴레이 없음) | 같은 네트워크에서 연결하거나, Tailscale 또는 HTTPS 터널로 어디서든 연결 |
| pt-BR | Conexão na mesma rede (sem relay na nuvem) | Conexão na mesma rede, ou de qualquer lugar pelo Tailscale ou pelo túnel HTTPS |
| zh-CN | 同一网络内连接（无云端中继） | 在同一网络内连接，或通过 Tailscale 或 HTTPS 隧道随时随地连接 |

The translations reuse each catalog's existing "tunnel" term from the Connect Mobile strings (Tunnel, túnel, tunnel, トンネル, 터널, 隧道).

**Deliberately unchanged:** "2 devices logged in at once" (`settings.billing.freeDevices`). Whether to enforce or drop it is part of the founder's open plan-card decision. Nothing else on the plan cards changes.

- `backend/internal/mobilebridge/endpoints.go` advertises `lan`, `tailscale` (the computer's `100.x` address when it's on a tailnet) and `tunnel` (managed `cloudflared`, `secure: true`, port 443) endpoints. There's no plan or billing check in the mobile bridge or the daemon.

body:

Tests: +90 -0  
Others: +5914 -134 (17 PO catalogs, lockfiles, config, CI)

## Summary

Translates the docs site's interface into 17 languages: en, ja, zh-CN, zh-TW, ko, fr, es, de, pt-BR, it, ru, tr, pl, nl, id, cs, vi. The articles stay in English.

- **Choosing a language.** Every page keeps its one URL and is prerendered in English. The language switcher sits in the sidebar footer and names each language in its own language.
  - Picking a language saves it in an `ao_locale` cookie and changes the interface in place, with no reload or redirect.
  - On later visits, an inline script sets `<html lang>` from the cookie before first paint, and the interface switches once the page hydrates.
  - Nothing reads Accept-Language. A reader with no saved choice sees English.
- **What gets translated.**
  - Site nav ("Orchestrator Docs", "Main site").
  - Sidebar section and folder titles.
  - The docs framework's own strings: table of contents, search, pagination, sidebar controls, code-block copy, language switcher.
  - The tab title and the 404 page.
  - A one-line notice that the article is shown in English.
  - Product names stay untranslated.
- **What stays English.**
  - The article bodies. They are marked `lang="en"` so the page still identifies them as English. Code blocks take the interface language on their frame, so the copy button is announced in the reader's language, while the code inside stays `lang="en"`. Each language in the switcher is marked with its own `lang`.
  - Sidebar page titles and table-of-contents entries, which come from the articles.
- **Lingui 6.**
  - `@lingui/core`/`@lingui/react` 6.8.0 and `@lingui/swc-plugin` 6.6.0 are pinned exactly. `next` is now pinned exactly to 16.2.11 too, because the SWC plugin only loads with the `swc_core` of that Next version.
  - Catalogs are PO files that use the English text as the message id. `npm run build` runs `lingui compile --strict` first.
  - The compiled catalogs are gitignored. They are a few dozen strings each, so all of them ship with the page.
  - A new step in the docs job of `frontend.yml` runs `npm run check:i18n`. It re-extracts the strings and fails when any locale is missing a translation.
- **SEO.** There is one URL per page with a self-referencing canonical and no hreflang. The new `sitemap.xml` lists each page once.
- **Search.** Search still uses the English index, since that is the language of the articles.

## Notes

- Because the site is a static export, the HTML is English. On a first load in another language, the interface shows English briefly until hydration finishes.
- The "Main site" link still points to the bare marketing URL.
- The site renders no page actions, edit-on-GitHub link, or last-updated date, so those strings are not included.

## Verification

- `npm ci && npm run build` in `frontend/src/docs` passes. This matches the docs job in `frontend.yml` and the steps in `deploy-docs.yml`. The build produces 51 static pages, the same set as before.
- Checked in a browser against the static export:
  - On `/cli/`, choosing 日本語 keeps the URL. It sets `ao_locale=ja`, `lang="ja"`, and the title "CLI reference | Agent Orchestrator ドキュメント", and translates the header, search, sidebar sections, and table of contents.
  - After a full reload of `/quickstart/`, the sidebar sections show はじめに, Orchestrator の使い方, リファレンス, ヘルプ, and the title stays Japanese.
  - Navigating within the site keeps the title Japanese.
  - `/nope/` shows the 404 page in Japanese.
  - Choosing English restores the English title, sidebar, and `lang` and removes the notice.
- Checked all 47 pages in Japanese. Each has `lang="ja"`, a Japanese title and sidebar sections, the English-article notice, a translated table-of-contents label, and its own canonical URL. There were no script errors.
- Checked `/quickstart/` and the 404 page in each of the 17 languages: `lang`, title, nav, sidebar sections and switcher label are right, with no errors.
- A malformed `ao_locale` cookie falls back to English. `<html lang>` goes straight to the saved language without flipping back to English, and the language menu closes after a choice.
- `npm run check:i18n` fails when a translation is blanked out.
- `npm test` (new, Vitest + jsdom, run in the docs CI job) covers the language boundaries. Inside an English-marked article, the code-block copy button follows the interface language while the code stays English, and the current language and every menu choice carry their own `lang`. The test fails if either fix is reverted.
- I did not run the rest of the frontend CI locally (Electron, Go). This PR doesn't touch those areas.

title: docs: add robots.txt pointing to the sitemap
body:
## Problem

docs.orchestrator.inc has no `robots.txt`. Today https://docs.orchestrator.inc/robots.txt returns 404.

#6967 adds `sitemap.xml` to the docs site, but crawlers have no standard way to discover it unless someone submits it by hand in each search console.

## Proposal

Add `frontend/src/docs/src/app/robots.ts` with `export const dynamic = "force-static"`, so the static export writes `out/robots.txt`. It should:

- allow all crawlers
- point to `https://docs.orchestrator.inc/sitemap.xml`

```
User-agent: *
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://docs.orchestrator.inc/sitemap.xml
```

## Done when

- `npm run build` in `frontend/src/docs` produces `out/robots.txt` with the content above.
- After deploy, https://docs.orchestrator.inc/robots.txt returns 200.

title: docs: make translated docs visible to search engines and AI crawlers
body:
## Background

#6967 translates the docs site's interface into 16 languages besides English: nav, sidebar sections, table of contents, search, 404 page and tab title. Every page keeps a single URL. The reader's choice is stored in an `ao_locale` cookie and applied in the browser after the page loads. The articles stay in English.

## Problem

Crawlers never see the translated versions:

- The static HTML is prerendered in English, and crawlers don't send the `ao_locale` cookie.
- Googlebot runs JavaScript but has no cookie, so it renders English.
- Most AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) don't run JavaScript at all.

As a result, the docs can't rank for searches in other languages, and AI assistants only ever quote the English pages. Today that costs little, since the only translated text is interface chrome with no search value. It starts to matter as soon as any article is translated.

## What it would take

Both of these are needed. Neither is enough alone.

1. **Translated articles.** The loader already supports per-locale files such as `cli.ja.mdx`. Start with the pages new users read first: Introduction, Installation, Quickstart. Each translation also has to be kept in step with the English page.
2. **A crawlable URL per language** for translated pages, e.g. `/ja/quickstart/`, prerendered at build time with:
   - `<html lang>` for that language
   - a canonical pointing to itself
   - hreflang alternates plus `x-default`
   - an entry for each language in the sitemap

   The cookie should only decide which version a reader lands on. It must not be the only way to reach a translated page.

## Open questions

- Is there enough non-English traffic to justify translating and maintaining the articles?
- Who reviews translations for technical accuracy (commands, flags, config keys)?

title: Support --effort for the Kiro harness
body:
**Problem**

`ao spawn --effort` is rejected for the Kiro harness, but Kiro CLI supports an effort flag (`kiro-cli chat --effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max>`, since CLI 2.6). There is no way to give AO Kiro workers different effort levels.

**Reproduce**

```
ao spawn --project <project> --agent kiro --effort low --name "effort test" --prompt "Reply ok."
```

**Actual**

```
spawn: unsupported model effort for harness "kiro": effort is only supported for codex, claude-code, and command-code agents (UNSUPPORTED_EFFORT)
```

No session starts.

**Expected**

AO passes the effort to Kiro, e.g. `kiro-cli chat --agent ao --effort low --trust-all-tools`, the same way it does for codex, claude-code and command-code. Project/worker/orchestrator/reviewer `agentConfig.effort` should apply to Kiro too.

**Why the workaround doesn't work**

AO launches Kiro as `kiro-cli chat --agent ao --trust-all-tools` with a generated `.kiro/agents/ao.json` that pins `"model"`. Kiro's `chat.modelDefaults` effort setting does not reliably apply when the agent config pins the model (see kirodotdev/Kiro#8754), and Kiro agent configs have no `effort` field yet. So Kiro workers run at the model's default effort.

**Use case**

Different workers need different depth: e.g. builder on high effort, docs and quick checks on low.

**Versions**

- AO: `dev` (desktop app daemon)
- kiro-cli: 2.32.0
- macOS 26.7.1

The task composer showed `FX could not list models for: codex, grok` for users who never set up Grok. title: fix(awake): unify sidebar and mobile settings wake toggles
body:
Code changes: +159 -43  
Tests: +651 -51  
Others: +72 -32 (localization catalogs)  

## What

The sidebar coffee button and the main Keep awake switch in Connect Mobile now call the same shared operation. On supported Macs, either enables desktop-owned closed-lid wake; Macs without closed-lid support use the same idle-only fallback. Either control turns the shared feature off.

Stacked on #6972: merge the startup-confirmation fix first. This PR targets its branch so the diff contains only the wake-control changes.

## Behavior

- Wake ownership and the configured battery cutoff are independent of mobile access. Turning off mobile connection does not cancel wake started from either control.
- The separate closed-lid switch uses desktop ownership too. Without an enabled automatic lid rule, turning it off preserves unrelated timed/session owners and establishes indefinite AO idle wake before ending lid owners. If an automatic lid rule is enabled, the existing daemon stop-all operation ends **all** sessions and pauses **all** rules before starting indefinite AO idle wake; unrelated owners are not preserved in this case.
- On daemon startup, transfer saved legacy mobile wake intent to desktop ownership and retire the legacy flags before restoring the bridge, preventing an independent mobile lease from bypassing the configured cutoff. The shared controls also retire legacy ownership after establishing desktop wake. Turning off the shared feature attempts both releases.
- Use the existing daemon start/setup/stop APIs and native coordinator. Preserve the configured battery cutoff (10% by default), critical-heat stop, and explicit safety rearm.
- Wait for closed-lid acknowledgement, not just an idle assertion, before leaving Starting. Show attention and the daemon failure reason if closed-lid wake fails.
- Reflect shared wake state in both controls with mobile access on or off. Keep the ventilation/battery tooltips and all eight locale catalogs.
- No native, API contract, or mobile-listener changes.

## Validation

- Final focused control/settings/localization suites: 151 passed, 6 skipped with Node 24. Coverage exercises either control enabling wake and the other disabling it, mobile access on/off, unsupported-host fallback, pending acknowledgement, safety failures and legacy-owner cleanup.
- Cloud contract/client generation, typecheck, tests and package dry-run passed. Docs production build passed. Product UI validation was also run.
- Native helper build/packaging tests, both helper architecture builds and Swift wake/effects/power/update state tests passed.
- Existing awake/mobile/controller Go suites passed; daemon migration validation is recorded below.
- Physical closed-lid/battery/thermal behavior is not locally verified. Isolated data cannot join the production native coordinator.
- Local macOS guarded-navigation integration fails the drag-region assertion on both this commit and the unchanged PR head (305fbe9a01). The full local renderer run had 63 passes and 35 failures, including focus/Chat fixture timeouts; a representative Chat test passes when run alone on the unchanged head. Linux-container CI remains the required renderer verification.
- TypeScript check of all changed code/tests and renderer globals passed after explicitly typing the mobile-request test mock. E2E typecheck passed. Whole-project local checking did not finish: the initial run was stopped after roughly eight minutes, and the final retry after roughly seven minutes. No full-project local pass claimed; the GitHub frontend job must verify it.
- Final full Vitest retry: all 498 files passed; 8,491 tests passed, 7 skipped. The pinned agent-browser runtime suite also passed all 26 tests with its conditional native check explicitly enabled. The initial full run had one CreateProjectFlow disabled-button failure; its full 85-test suite and the subsequent full frontend retry both passed.
- GitHub checks rerun after each push. The latest daemon migration requires the complete Linux backend and renderer CI gates; prior UI-only validation does not substitute for those checks.

## Helper setup fallback follow-up

- Exclude structured `helper_upgrade_required` / `setup_failed` states from default closed-lid availability, even if the capability still advertises `available: true`.
- If the first default start discovers one of those setup failures, refresh daemon state and retry idle-only wake. Both main switches retain the same behavior. Explicit closed-lid opt-ins and safety pauses do not silently downgrade; a failed idle retry remains an error.
- Mark closed-lid support unavailable in the off tooltip after the fallback, rather than claiming it is active.
- Ten added regressions cover known/discovered setup failures, both main controls, explicit opt-ins, safety pauses, and failed idle fallback.
- Latest validation: full frontend Vitest 498 files / 8,501 tests passed, 7 skipped; complete affected control/mobile/sidebar suites 291 passed, 6 skipped; changed-file TypeScript and backend awake suite passed. A bounded full-project TypeScript attempt is not claimed as passing; CI must verify the complete check.
- Supplied thread PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6uXtIO resolved after pushing c74977a81.

## Legacy mobile wake migration

On upgraded daemon startup, migrate the saved mobile wake opt-in into desktop ownership **before** restoring the mobile bridge. This runs even when mobile access is off; opening a view or toggling off/on is unnecessary. Preserve the saved lid choice and pairing settings, then clear both legacy wake fields durably so a later bridge restart cannot bring back independent ownership.

Migration never resumes a safety pause. If desktop wake is refused or unavailable, retire the legacy flags and log the failure rather than restoring a hold that bypasses desktop policy. If retirement cannot be saved, do not restore the bridge with the old flags. Old-helper upgrade errors can retain idle-only wake. A saved lid preference with keep-awake off is cleared without starting anything.

Validation for 67fff8b18:
- Startup migration regressions passed (bridge on/off, lid opt-in on/off, one-time transfer, pairing preservation, safety pause/refusal, unavailable service, old helper and persistence failure).
- Complete race-enabled suites passed: `./internal/daemon ./internal/service/awake ./internal/httpd/controllers ./internal/mobilebridge`.

A retry without inherited AO worker environment passed Claude auth, tmux and CLI; live OpenCode credential/model discovery still failed against the installed binary. No full backend race-suite pass is claimed; CI must verify the complete Linux suite.
- No frontend, API DTO, or native helper changes in this migration follow-up; physical lid/battery/thermal validation remains unverified locally.
- Supplied thread PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6uXtIW resolved directly after the successful push.

## Persistent idle wake after disabling lid wake

Turning off closed-lid wake reuses only an open, indefinite AO idle owner. If only timed or session-scoped idle owners remain, establish a new indefinite AO idle hold before ending lid owners. When no automatic lid rule is enabled, temporary owners continue normally, and their later completion no longer removes the user's persistent Keep awake hold.

Validation for 3fca711a7:
- Regression tests cover timed and session-bound owners ending after the transition, replacement-before-release ordering, and reuse of an existing indefinite AO idle owner.
- Focused frontend tests: 293 passed, 6 skipped.

## Persistent ownership when enabling wake

`ensureDesktop` now reuses only an open indefinite AO session whose lid setting matches the request. Session-scoped/timed owners and automatic lid rules cannot substitute for the user's persistent wake setting.

Validation for 68b23e16d:
- Added regressions for session-scoped and timed lid owners, an idle owner with a lid rule, mismatched and ended owners, idle-only requests, and reuse of matching indefinite AO owners. Lid wake remains active after previous owners/rules finish.

## Review clarification and UI consistency

Closed-lid wake by default on supported Macs is intentional: the requested behavior is for the coffee button to keep the laptop working after lid closure, using the same native capability as Connect Mobile. This changes the previous separate-opt-in behavior. The tooltip discloses lid wake, ventilation, battery use, and the configured safety cutoff; unsupported or failed helper setup retains the documented idle-only fallback.

The automatic-lid-rule exception is now explicit above. Keep the existing daemon stop-all boundary so automatic lid rules cannot immediately rearm; there is no narrower rule-disable implementation in this follow-up. A regression verifies that all sessions end and all rules are paused before replacement idle wake starts.

Lid diagnostics now accept known lid reasons only, with the lid capability reason as a fallback when an unrelated overall persistence/observation/recovery error masks it. Otherwise the UI reports the known fact that closed-lid wake is inactive without assigning an unrelated cause. Low-battery lid warnings now interpolate the configured cutoff in both controls and all eight locales.

## Follow-up on the three earlier review findings

- Persistent orange warning after mobile activation: already addressed. Both controls start desktop-owned wake, wait for native closed-lid acknowledgement for up to 10 seconds, and use the shared awake status query for subsequent updates. No independent mobile enable POST remains in either control.
- Advertised cutoff differing from the mobile lease: already addressed. Both controls use desktop ownership and its configured safety policy. Startup migration retires saved independent mobile flags before restoring the bridge; cutoff text in both controls and all locales uses the configured value.
- Lid-off release loop: now attempts every cached lid owner even if an earlier end request fails, alongside the mobile release. After failures it refreshes authoritative daemon status and ignores an error only when that owner is confirmed ended or absent. Still-live or unverifiable failures remain visible; replacement indefinite idle ownership is preserved. Regressions cover expired, live and unavailable-status cases.

title: feat(remote-hosts): let this computer link itself to your AO account
body:
Code changes: +202 -0\
Tests: +329 -1\
Others: +67 -1

## What

Adds **This computer → Allow access from your devices** to Settings → Remote hosts. Turning it on makes this computer appear on every device signed in to the same AO account, with no address or password to copy. Turning it off stops remote access and removes the computer from the account.

## Why

Using one desktop from another today means running `ao remote-host enable` and `ao remote-host status` on the host, then copying its HTTPS address and password into **Add host** on the other machine. Connect Mobile shows only the LAN address, so access from another network needs the CLI. Account discovery (#6204) already syncs a linked host to every signed-in device and follows its tunnel address; the only manual step left was that first link.

## How

- **On:** if the bridge is off, `POST /api/v1/mobile/enable`. If it is already on (a phone paired through Connect Mobile), `POST /api/v1/mobile/remote-access` instead, which keeps the password. Then poll `/api/v1/mobile/status` every 2 s until the tunnel endpoint is advertised (90 s limit), take a host token from `POST /api/v1/remote-host/account-token` (pairing password + account ID), and save `{hostId, label, url, token}` with the existing `PUT /api/cloud/v1/me/hosts/{hostId}`.
- The saved URL uses the same `https://<host>:443` form as the daemon's address publisher, so its first publish does not rewrite the record and reconnect every device.
- **Label:** the macOS Computer Name (`scutil --get ComputerName`, new `remotes:computerName` IPC), else the host name; trimmed to AO Cloud's 64-byte limit.
- **Off:** `POST /api/v1/mobile/disable` first, so access is cut even when AO Cloud is unreachable, then `DELETE /api/cloud/v1/me/hosts/{hostId}`.
- **State is derived, not stored:** on = listener enabled, public tunnel allowed, and this host ID listed in the account.
- **Failed turn-on:** anything short of a saved link puts remote access back as it was: disabled if it was off, LAN-only with the same password if a phone was paired that way (`POST /api/v1/mobile/enable-lan-only`), untouched if remote access was already on. Otherwise the switch would show off while this computer stayed reachable.
- No `cloudflared`: remote access is put back, the row offers **Install cloudflared**, and turning on runs again after the install. A linked computer whose tunnel failed shows the connector error instead of "Starting remote access…".
- No backend, API or AO Cloud changes.

Known limits, deliberately out of scope:

- Remote hosts stays behind Developer mode on both machines.
- Two machines on the same network still connect through Cloudflare, which terminates TLS.
- Turning the switch off also disconnects phones paired through Connect Mobile, because they share the listener. The remote-access docs page says so.
- Turning on takes about 20 s, mostly the daemon's fixed 12 s DNS settle wait for a new quick tunnel.

## Testing

- `ThisComputerAccess.test.tsx`, 13 tests. Only the two network edges are faked (daemon API, AO Cloud bridge request); the account-sync code between them is real. Cases: links at the tunnel address; keeps a paired phone's password; waits for the tunnel before linking; times out with an error; turns off (disable, then delete); still cuts access when the AO Cloud delete fails; offers the cloudflared install; stays off when only the account lists the computer; reports a failed link; shows a failed tunnel; trims long names. The timeout, failed-link and no-connector cases assert remote access ends up off; two more cover a failed turn-on restoring LAN-only access with the same password and leaving already-on remote access running. Breaking each restore branch on purpose fails its test.
- `remotes-main.test.ts`: Computer Name preference and host-name fallback.
- Focused run on the rebased branch: 6 files, 102 tests pass (`ThisComputerAccess`, `RemoteHostsSettings`, `remotes-main`, `preload`, i18n coverage and completeness).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` on the rebased head: 0 errors each, with `packages/product-ui` and `packages/cloud-client` installed as CI does.
- Full `npm test`: the only failures were in unrelated files (SessionsBoard, GlobalSettingsForm, chat panels and others); those files pass when re-run with less parallel load.
- Manual, macOS, this branch's desktop app on isolated data: turned the switch on. Daemon log: listener up at +0 s, tunnel registered at +6.2 s, advertised at +18.5 s, account token issued at +20.1 s. A second machine importing the host was not exercised.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(chat): make agent question dock scrollable and bound height (#6942)
body:
## Code Changes

- **Code:** +20 / −12
- **Tests:** +64 / −0
- **Other:** +0 / −0

## What

Make the agent input question dock (`ElicitationDock`) scrollable and limit its maximum height. Forms with multiple questions, many options, or custom write-in fields can now scroll instead of expanding beyond the viewport.

Fixes #6942.

## Why

`ElicitationDock` previously had an unconstrained height, `overflow-hidden` on its root container, and no internal scroll container for its fields. When an agent or harness—such as OpenCode or a generic MCP server—presented a multi-question form or questions with multiple choices and descriptions:

- The dock could grow to around 500–600 px, collapse the timeline, and extend upward beneath the workspace top bar (`.workspace-topbar-container`), hiding the `DockHeader` and first question.
- Wheel and touch scrolling did not work because the form had no scroll container.

## How

title: fix: show a failed Setup the same way in cloud and local, say what went wrong, and allow 30 minutes per step
body:
Code changes: +131 -39\
Tests: +174 -14\
Others: +26 -25

## What

A failed project Setup script now looks, reads and behaves the same in cloud and local. Where cloud has to differ, it follows local as closely as cloud allows:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud, Chat mode | Full-screen "The project's Setup script failed" panel; the conversation is hidden | Local's failed-start checklist under your messages: ✓ Create worktree · ✗ Run setup script · ○ Start Claude Code, the error, "Your messages are saved here and will be sent if you retry.", **Retry start**. Composer: "The controller is not connected", no model controls |
| Cloud, a message sent while Setup is failed | Failed at once with the startup error | Stays queued and is sent once a retry passes, as in local. While it waits it does not keep the sandbox running (idle pause still applies) |
| Cloud, Setup history in Chat | Every failed attempt stays as a red row | Failed attempts are left out while the checklist shows the failure and once a retry passes; the Setup that passed stays (duration and output) |
| Cloud, Terminal mode | Panel | Panel (cloud-only: the session exists before Setup runs, so there is no create box to show the error in) |
| Error text, local Terminal (create-task error), local Chat and cloud (checklist, panel) | Local: `spawn ao-6959-repo-3: provision: setup step 1 failed: exit status 1: installing dependencies... error: could not reach registry`; cloud: `Setup step 1 failed: exit status 1. Fix the project's Setup script (Project settings > Scripts), then reopen this session to retry.` | Both: `The project's Setup script failed at step 1 (exit status 1), so the agent did not start. Fix the script in Project settings > Scripts, then try again. Output: installing dependencies... error: could not reach registry` (or "stopped at step 1 after 10 minutes") |
| Cloud Retry when Setup fails the same way again | Stays on "Retrying" | Shows Setup running, then the new failure |
| Time limit per Setup step, local and cloud | 10 minutes (and local Chat starts cut at 10 minutes in total) | 30 minutes; a local Chat start's budget adds 30 minutes per Setup step (cloud Cleanup stays at 10 minutes per step) |

## Why

A tester found cloud and local Setup failures confusing. Cloud Chat hid the conversation behind a panel local Chat doesn't have and failed the messages sent meanwhile, and the local error was the internal spawn error chain, which doesn't say that the project's Setup script failed or where to fix it.

## How

**Cloud Chat reuses local's failed start** (`CloudSessionChatSurface`). When the worker reports a checkout or Setup failure (`isWorkspaceStartupError`), `ChatWorkspace` gets what a failed local start gives it:
- `provisionState`, `provisionSteps`, `provisionError` on the session, so `ChatWorkspace` draws the existing checklist. No new UI.
- A `stopped` controller and `settingsReady={false}`, so the composer and settings read as local's do. While a retry runs, both stay as they are, so messages can queue as in a local start.
- Retry sends the request the panel's Retry already sends (`requestWorkspaceCheckout`).

`SessionView` shows `CloudSessionStartupError` for these errors only outside Chat.

**A waiting message doesn't keep a cloud sandbox up.** `keep_alive` (`ClaimSandboxes`) and the billed running sessions query count `queued` turns as activity. A turn queued behind a failed checkout or Setup (`startup_error_code` in `domain.WorkspaceStartupErrorCodes()`) is now skipped, so the sandbox can idle-pause and isn't treated as busy for running slots. Once the worker reports the workspace ready, the same turn counts again.

**The cloud worker keeps queued messages** (`workerexec.Supervisor.Run`). While the workspace start is failed it does not claim turns. Before, it claimed each one and failed it (`FailTurn`). Turns now wait in the queue and run once a retry clears the failure, which makes "Your messages are saved…" true for cloud.

**One wording** (`backend` `SetupStepError`, `cloud` `SetupEvent.Summary`). Local's `runPostCreate` returns a `SetupStepError` whose text is what the user reads. The spawn API error (`toSpawnAPIError`) and the failed async Chat start (`failAsyncChatSpawn`) use that text instead of the `spawn <id>: provision:` chain; the error code stays `WORKSPACE_PROVISION_FAILED`. The worker's summary, documented as "in the local daemon's words", now uses the same sentence. Cloud's own wording changes when a new ao-worker image is deployed.

**30-minute Setup steps.** Local Chat starts run under `asyncChatSpawnBudget` (10 minutes for the whole start). The budget now adds `setupStepTimeout` per Setup step, so a long step isn't killed at 10 minutes and misreported as a script failure.

**30-minute Setup steps, the constants.** A tester's step (installing dependencies, starting containers) ran past the 10-minute limit and was killed. Local uses one `setupStepTimeout` for the limit and its message. Cloud splits its shared constant: `ProjectSetupStepTimeout` (30 minutes) for Setup, and `ProjectCleanupStepTimeout` (10 minutes) for each Cleanup command, which also has the provider's 10-minute deletion budget. The project settings hints (all locales), `docs/configuration/projects`, `cloud/docs/bring-your-own-coder.md`, and the cloud API description (`contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, regenerated `schema.ts` line) say 30 minutes.

**Retry staying on "Retrying"** (this bug was already in the Terminal panel). The desktop treats a retry as finished when the failure time changes. `RecordWorkspaceStartupError` kept the first time for an identical failure; every worker report is a new attempt, so it now records `now()`.

Not in this change:
- Cloud tasks start in Terminal even when Chat is the default.
- A session switched to Chat while its Setup is failed also starts the Terminal agent once Setup passes, because the worker reads the interface it was given at connect.
- The desktop shows "Creating the workspace" indefinitely when the control plane gives up starting a sandbox without recording a startup error.

## Testing

Desktop dev build against the local cloud stack (`npm run cloud:local`, Docker sandboxes; control plane built from this branch, worker image from this branch plus #6961):

- **Messages kept through a failure**, driven over the control-plane API. A session with a failing Setup is switched to Chat, and "are you there?" is sent while Setup is failed: no turn events for 15 s. Setup is then changed to `echo ok` and retried:

  ```
  13:43:08 workspace.setup succeeded, agent.ready
  13:43:09 chat.turn_started  (the message sent while Setup was failed)
  13:43:12 chat.assistant_delta "Invalid API key · Fix external API key"   <- stack uses a placeholder key
  ```

- **Cloud Chat in the app**, Setup step `echo "installing dependencies..."; echo "error: could not reach registry"; exit 1`:
  - Your messages, then the checklist with the error above, "Your messages are saved here and will be sent if you retry.", **Retry start**.
  - Composer "The controller is not connected", no model controls, no red Setup rows.
  - With a 10 s failing step, **Retry start** shows "Setting up session" with Run setup script running, then the failed checklist again with the new failure time.
  - With Setup fixed, **Retry start** sends the saved message, the composer returns, and only the passed Setup row remains.
- **Cloud Terminal**: the same failure still shows the full-screen panel with Retry and the output.
- **Local Terminal** (`ao spawn --mode tui`) and **local Chat** (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`, the desktop's background start), same failing step: both report the new sentence.

Checks:
- `backend`: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/service/session/` pass, including the new `TestRunPostCreateFailureSaysWhatFailedAndWhereToFixIt`.
- `cloud`: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race ./internal/workerexec/ ./internal/worker/ ./cmd/ao-worker/ ./internal/httpapi/ ./internal/sandbox/...` pass.
  - The new `TestQueuedChatTurnsWaitWhileTheWorkspaceStartFailed` fails on the previous claim loop (42 claims while failed).
  - `TestWorkspaceStartupErrorSurvivesHeartbeatsUntilReady` (PostgreSQL) passes with its new repeated-failure check, which fails on the previous SQL.
  - New `TestQueuedTurnBehindAFailedWorkspaceStartDoesNotKeepTheSandboxUp` (PostgreSQL): a queued turn keeps the sandbox up, stops doing so while Setup is failed, and does again once the workspace is ready. It fails on the previous query. The sandbox, claim and billing store tests (23) pass.
- `frontend`: `tsc --noEmit` passes. Vitest passes 557 tests across `CloudSessionChatSurface` (new: checklist, stopped composer, Retry; only the passed Setup row stays), `ChatWorkspace`, `SessionView` and `CloudSessionStartupError`.

title: fix(cloud): start a cloud task in the default session mode
body:
Code changes: +68 -16\
Tests: +142 -0\
Others: +16 -0

## What

A cloud task now starts in the user's default session mode, as a local task does: with Chat as the default it opens in Chat instead of always in the terminal. Every decision on the way follows what the local daemon and desktop do.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud task, default session mode Chat | Starts in the terminal (`interfaceMode: tui`); the user has to switch | Starts in Chat (`interfaceMode: chat`); the opening prompt runs as the first Chat turn |
| Cloud task, default Terminal | Terminal | Terminal (unchanged) |
| Cloud task with an agent that has no Chat in the cloud | Terminal | The composer starts it in the terminal, as local does for an agent without Chat (it reads the cloud's list, as it reads the daemon's for local) |
| A create that asks for Chat with such an agent | n/a | Refused with `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`, the local daemon's code; the composer offers "Create as Terminal UI", as for local |

## Why

A tester reported that their Chat default was ignored in cloud: every cloud session opened in the terminal. Local tasks honor the setting because the daemon applies it when the create request has none. The control plane has no such setting, and its create-session API had no field for the interface, so the desktop could not pass it.

## How

- **Control plane** (`createSessionRequest`): new optional `interfaceMode` ("chat" | "tui"), passed to `domain.CreateSession.Interface`, which the store already persisted and the worker bootstrap already read (`ao_sessions.interface` → `WorkerLaunch.Interface`).
  - Omitted keeps the terminal default.
  - Chat for a harness without a Chat controller is refused with 409 `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`, as the daemon refuses it.
  - Any other value is refused with 422.
- **One list of Chat harnesses**: `chatHarnesses` (claude-code, codex, cursor) backs create, interface switching (`chatControllerSupported`), and a new `/me` `chatHarnesses` field. That field is the cloud counterpart of the daemon's settings `chatHarnesses`.
- **Opening prompt** (`createSessionTx`): a terminal session gets the prompt on the agent's command line, so only the `chat.user_message` event is written, as before.
  - A Chat session's controller runs queued turns, so its prompt is queued as a turn (`appendUserMessage`). Without this, a Chat session would show the prompt but never run it.
  - Its terminal launch prompt (`ao_sessions.prompt`, read only by the worker launch spec) is left empty. A later switch to the terminal then starts the agent without the prompt, as a local Chat session does (`freshLaunchArgv` with no prompt), instead of running it again.
- **Desktop** (`TaskComposer`): a cloud task sends `interfaceMode` from the default session mode (or the composer's explicit choice). The local path is unchanged; the daemon still applies the default itself.
  - "Does this agent have Chat?" (`requiresTuiFallback`) reads the cloud list from `/me` (`useCloudOffering`) for a cloud project, and the daemon's list for a local one.
  - A control-plane error keeps its code (`TaskCreateError`), so `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` brings up the same "Create as Terminal UI" fallback as a local create.
- **Contract**: `CreateSessionInput.interfaceMode` and `CurrentAccount.chatHarnesses` in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, with `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` regenerated (`npm run generate`).

Not in this change: the project orchestrator and `ao spawn` children created inside a cloud session still start in the terminal.

## Testing

Local cloud stack (`npm run cloud:local`, Docker sandboxes), desktop dev build with the default session mode set to Chat:

- **From the app's composer**: a new task in a cloud project is created with `interfaceMode: chat` and opens in Chat.
- **Over the API**:
  - `/me` returns `chatHarnesses: [claude-code, codex, cursor]`.
  - `interfaceMode: "chat"` with `aider` → 409 `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` ("aider can't run in Chat in AO Cloud. Start it in the terminal.").
  - `interfaceMode: "gui"` → 422.
  - `interfaceMode: "chat"` → the session reports `interfaceMode: chat`. The opening prompt's `chat.user_message` carries a `turnId`. After Setup, `chat.turn_started` runs it through the Chat controller, and no terminal agent starts (no `agent.ready`).
- **With #6976 (failed Setup)**: a Chat task's opening prompt waits while Setup is failed (no turn for 12 s). After fixing Setup and retrying, it runs (`workspace.setup succeeded` and `chat.turn_started` in the same second).

Checks:
- `cloud`: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test ./internal/httpapi/` pass.
  - New `TestCreateSessionInterfaceMode` covers chat, omitted, no Chat controller → 409 `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`, and unknown → 422.
  - New `TestMeListsChatHarnesses` checks the `/me` list.
  - New PostgreSQL test `TestCreateSessionStartsInTheRequestedInterface` checks that a Chat session launches in Chat with one queued turn and no launch prompt, and a terminal session has the launch prompt and no turn. It passes.
  - The full `internal/postgres` package has four failures that also fail on `main` against the same local PostgreSQL (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`).
- `frontend`: `tsc --noEmit` passes. `TaskComposer` tests (88) pass, including three new ones:
  - starts a cloud task in the default session mode;
  - starts it in the terminal when the control plane has no Chat for its agent;
  - offers "Create as Terminal UI" when the control plane refuses Chat.

  The offering and cloud client tests (45) pass.
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` leaves no diff.

title: fix(telemetry): reduce duplicate and noisy product events
body:
Code changes: +728 -91
Tests: +639 -103
Others: +39 -6

## Summary

Reduce duplicate and noisy product analytics while preserving local diagnostics and functional error handling.

Remote `ao.http.5xx` is no longer sampled. The minute rollup and the 1,500 per day cap are the remote limit. A real HTTP 500 still reaches the existing gated daemon Sentry once. Expected `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` (account management is not wired in this process) is not an analytics or Sentry event. Login terminal failures are `CODEX_LOGIN_TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE`. Setup that did not finish is `CODEX_ACCOUNT_SETUP_INCOMPLETE`. Both of those report. The Codex account stream stays open while management is unavailable and retries subscribe every 30 seconds. The retry interval is settable in tests, and a later successful subscribe continues the event loop. Automatic desktop ensure backs off on account management unavailable and on incomplete account setup, until the daemon base URL changes or a later ensure succeeds. That reset lives in the accounts hook. Explicit user retries are not gated.

`ao.cli.usage_errors` is one event per command path and error kind per install per UTC day, capped at 20. `command_path` is its own property and `count` is a number. No raw arguments or error text. The event is stamped at the end of that UTC day. Full local events stay unsampled. Opt out remains ahead of the daily summary and aggregation.

Renderer `ao.v2.renderer.api_error` is not sampled. It drops startup `daemon_unavailable` 503s while the daemon is still starting, and HTTP 409 only for `POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/workspace/diffs`, `GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/conversation/config-options`, `GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/conversation/models`, and `GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/conversation/skills`. It also drops `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` and `SHELL_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND`. `GITHUB_AUTH_INVALID` reports again. Other 401 and 404 responses still report.

`ao.renderer.update_failed` emits once per open failure streak (phase, category, target version). The daily total is a separate event, `ao.renderer.update_failures_daily`, with `day` and `failure_count`, so a streak insight does not count the daily summary. A rejected or thrown streak capture releases the claim so the retry is not swallowed. Restart keeps the open streak. A successful download of that target clears it.

The named requested UI events stay removed where a succeeded or failed pair exists. `ao.renderer.project_add_failed` and `ao.renderer.project_clone_failed` carry the error code. Foreign event names are not filtered in this daemon. `ao.mobile.device_connected` stays: it is the host's first authenticated request per transport, not the phone's `ao.v2.mobile_app.connected`.

`ao.review.triggered` no longer sends `reused`. `ao.renderer.session_management_summary` is back on main's 45 minute flush plus jitter. `ao.renderer.cloud_offering_resolved` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added` are unchanged by this PR.

## Verification

On `823b6ac6f3`: api-client vitest passed (36 tests), including a 409 on `GET /api/v1/agents/:id/models` that still reports and a 409 on the session skills probe that does not.

On `03cee8d5c2`: focused Go tests passed for telemetry, daemon wiring, the Codex account stream (including a later subscribe that continues the loop), and review payloads. Focused vitest passed for api-client, telemetry, telemetry init, the Codex accounts query, and Codex account settings (153 tests).

Earlier on `3122127b92`: race tests passed for `internal/adapters/telemetry`, `internal/daemon`, `internal/httpd`, and `internal/httpd/controllers` (1287 tests). Pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2 reported 0 issues on those packages. Frontend typecheck passed. Those were not rerun on this commit.

`openapi.yaml` and sqlc output are not in this diff.

The complete local `go test ./...` was not clean. OpenCode v2 malformed version selected the installed OpenCode binary. tmux tests called the real tmux. CLI hook and spawn tests inherited this worker's `AO_SESSION_ID`. Those packages are outside this diff. The whole-backend golangci run and the full frontend suite were not rerun in this pass.

## Review follow-up and reconciliation

Updater failure capture still releases its reservation when PostHog rejects or throws, now on the streak claim instead of the old 24 hour key. This branch keeps a4fc51a18, which contains 22df5877dc, so that retry behavior is included. Merged identity PR #6425 stays in the base. The daemon opt out gate sits ahead of the daily summary and aggregation. Consent based email remains a person property only.

Saved PostHog insights `tOrAiPWP`, `j3p0y1yN`, and `6RLSde7F` still use `*_requested` as a denominator. They were not rewritten: this environment has no PostHog credentials. Ronish can update them now that `error_code` is kept on the project failure events.

## Rollout and compatibility

HTTP 5xx allowlist still includes `sample_rate` for older clients. New CLI usage events carry `command_path`, `error_kind`, `count`, and `day`. Old packed `command_counts` batches stop. The reported v1 renderer names still map to v2 names, with no parallel v1 capture calls. `ao.renderer.update_failures_daily` is a new name. `ao.review.triggered` drops `reused`, which breaks that property's series against #4665.

## Explicit exclusions

Identity and install fixes are owned by merged PR #6425. There is no authoritative durable session outcome and end time, shared first success fact, or agent creation provenance for PR observations, so this PR does not emit guessed session ended, first success, or agent PR lifecycle events. An offline client cannot emit its own 14 day absence or OS uninstall. Website `web.*` emitters live in ao landing and were handed to the project orchestrator. PostHog internal install filters, project rename, and timezone require a verified target project and user choices. No production test error was sent. Daemon `ao.mobile.device_connected` was kept because it is not the same action as phone `ao.v2.mobile_app.connected`.

body: Code changes: +825 -1 Tests: +559 -0 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary Pages an agent publishes with `html_render` / `ao render` (screenshot grids, charts, mockups) show inline in desktop chat, but the mobile app showed nothing for them. The daemon records each page as a `system` activity row (`detail.event: "render"`) and serves it, images inlined, from `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/renders/{renderId}`. Mobile had no handling for that row. - **Inline render** (`lib/chat/RenderFrame.tsx`): a WebView loads the render route with the pairing's bearer headers, so it works over LAN, Tailscale and the tunnel, and for sessions on any paired machine (`HostScope` supplies that machine's config). It opens at the daemon's measured height for its width, then fits the height the page reports, and doesn't scroll on its own. The page gets the app's palette and system fonts through the bootstrap's `#ao-theme` fragment, and later theme changes are posted to it without a reload. - **Tap to expand**: tapping anywhere on the render opens a full-screen viewer with the title and a close button. The page scrolls there, and pinch or double-tap zooms. The viewer also lifts any page-set zoom lock (`user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`) up to 5×. The WebView runs edge to edge and the page carries the thread's gutter itself (injected before first paint), so zoomed content pans to the screen edges. Scrollbars are hidden. The viewer's state resets when it closes, not in Modal `onShow`: iOS fires that after the fade-in, and a reset there remounted a page that was already showing, which flashed blank and reloaded. - **Only pages near the screen hold a WebView**: a page can carry megabytes of inlined images, and the chat list keeps several turns mounted at once. Each frame measures itself as the thread scrolls (on the list's existing throttled `onScroll`). It holds a WebView only within half a screen of view and lets it go past a screen and a half; the gap stops it flickering at the edge. Checks coalesce to one per frame, since a streaming reply grows the list many times a second. A screen pushed over the session (a PR, a file) leaves the frames laid out "in view", so they let their pages go there too and reload them on return. A page coming back revalidates with `If-None-Match` and gets a 304, so it isn't downloaded again. - **Loading skeleton** (`lib/chat/RenderSkeleton.tsx`): while a page is out of range or still loading, the frame shows a skeleton at the page's remembered height, so the thread doesn't jump. It has a content block, plus two caption lines when the frame is tall enough, with a highlight band sweeping across (an `react-native-svg` gradient on the native-driver `Animated` loop the spinner uses; 1.3s sweep, 0.4s rest). The band is lighter than the block in both themes, and Reduce Motion leaves the blocks still. The expanded viewer shows the same skeleton until its page loads. - **Exact page heights**: the WebView reports the page's content box. It uses `scrollHeight` only when that beats the viewport, which means real overflow. `scrollHeight` never drops below the viewport, and Android's WebView viewport rounds a pixel taller than the frame (327dp at 2.625x is 858.4px), so trusting it reported "frame + 1" forever: frames sat ~18px too tall over 309px of content and grew each launch. The report also waits for images to decode and fonts to load, then for the height to hold still for 80ms (1.5s cap), because an earlier report caught a reloaded page at 92px of its 309px. A page that fills its viewport (`min-height: 100vh`, `height: 100%`) has no height of its own, so it keeps the frame's height. A report that only follows the frame's own growth (`100vh` plus a margin) is held, so such a page can't grow the frame step by step to the 2000px cap. - **No height shifts**: the skeleton stays until a page's first settled height, so a page appears at its size. For a page this device has already sized, the skeleton waits 250ms and only shows for a slower load, so the viewer and pages scrolled back into view don't flash one. Heights are saved to app storage, keyed by render and frame width, capped at 200 pages, and written within a second and when the app leaves the foreground. A frame opens at its saved height, so a relaunch opens at the right size: one page used to go 520 → 312 → 319. A page this device has never measured loads two screens out and stays until measured, so it's sized before it reaches the screen. The Android list anchors on-screen content again (`maintainVisibleContentPosition`, dropped when that list stopped inverting in #6441), so an off-screen resize, or earlier history loading in, doesn't move what's on screen; iOS already had it. - **Recovers a killed page**: the OS can kill a WebView's page process under memory pressure, which leaves the frame blank with no error. The frame remounts the page (`onContentProcessDidTerminate` / `onRenderProcessGone`) and falls back to "Tap to retry" after two deaths. - **Locked down**: the frame only ever loads the page itself. Links open in the browser only right after a touch in the expanded viewer, so a page can't open one on its own by posting to the bridge. The daemon's CSP sandbox still keeps the page on an opaque origin. - **No re-renders from chat updates**: the frame is memoized on the render it shows, and its WebView source is stable. - **Model** (`lib/chat/renderFrameModel.ts`): ports desktop's `readRenderRef` and measured-height logic from `frontend/src/renderer/lib/render-frame.ts`, plus the theme mapping, the WebView bridge scripts, viewport ranges and the saved-height cache. JS only: `react-native-webview` and `react-native-svg` are already dependencies, and there's no native change. ## Screenshots Session `agent-orchestrator-mo-215`, paired through a read-only proxy to a real daemon. For the skeleton shots the proxy held each page back a few seconds. **iOS**: the same turn as the desktop report, inline with the expand icon, expanded, zoomed **Android**: inline, expanded, after a two-finger pinch, panned while zoomed **Loading skeleton, iOS**: expanded viewer in dark and light, inline in light **Loading skeleton, Android**: expanded viewer in dark and light ## Testing - `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 2280 tests pass, including new `renderFrameModel.test.ts` (ref validation, measured heights, theme fragment and live theme message, bridge message parsing, navigation lockdown, zoom-lock removal, viewport ranges including measure-ahead, per-frame coalescing of viewport checks, saved heights across a simulated relaunch, the height reporter against Android-style viewport rounding, half-laid-out pages, bursts of layout changes, viewport-filling pages and pages that follow the viewport plus a margin, the viewer's page styles, skeleton lines). - **Physical devices**: Release builds of this branch installed next to the existing AO apps, as "AO Renders" (`com.prasadware.ao.mobile.renders` on an iPhone 13 running iOS 27.2, `aoagents.dev.renders` on a Pixel 10a). Over-the-air updates were off, and each was paired to a real daemon through Connect Mobile. Manual testing: - Renders show inline in a real session, and tapping one opens the full-screen viewer on both phones. Two-finger pinch zoom works on the iPhone (not testable on the simulator). - The first round found two problems, both fixed in `0bb36fe`: the viewer's side inset cut a zoomed page off at the left edge, and a scrollbar showed. Opening the viewer also flashed the skeleton for a page that had already loaded. - The second round: Android's viewer opened immediately and cleanly. iOS still showed image → blank → image on open, which was the `onShow` reset above, fixed in `fa87563` and confirmed on the iPhone. The simulator never showed it (there the page loads after the fade). - iOS simulator: renders load and fit their height, light and dark themes and a live theme switch work, and expand, close, double-tap zoom and pan work. The skeleton shows inline and in the viewer in both themes, and the band reads as a highlight in each. - Android emulator (`worli`): inline render, expand, real two-finger pinch zoom (injected multi-touch), pan and close work. - Android, on a separate `ao216-lab` emulator: tapping the middle of a render opens the viewer, and the skeleton sweeps in dark and light. - Heights, on a separate `ao216-lab` emulator and the iOS simulator. The lab proxy trimmed the conversation so a chosen render opened on screen, and a temporary log recorded every resize and where it happened: - Android relaunch: a frame opened at its saved 309 and the page reported 309, so it stayed. With the old reporter the same page crept 316 → 319 → 320 → 321 → 324 → 327 across launches. - First view after clearing saved heights: the render on screen at open sized 312 → 309 on Android (312 → 303 on iOS) under its skeleton, then appeared at that size. Renders further up were measured off screen, 1.5–1.8 screens above. - Scrolling away and back: remounts reported the same height, with no 309 → 92 → 309 dip. - Android anchor: on-screen text stayed in place while renders above resized by up to 39px. Following a live conversation at the bottom still followed it. - Saved heights survive the app being backgrounded half a second after a measurement and then killed. - A `min-height: 100vh` page with a 16px paragraph margin (the review's repro): with the earlier reporter it grew 325 → 341 → … → 2016 in 16px steps, 107 reports in 30s. Now it reports 328 once and holds. - Jump-to-message from the conversation history sheet lands on the chosen exchange and stays put while renders below it load. - Viewport gating, checked through the proxy's request log and a temporary live-state log: - iOS: on opening the session, FlatList had 3 render rows mounted but only the one near the screen fetched its page. Scrolling loaded each page as it neared, and coming back to a page returned 304s. - Android: across 14 swipes of history, pages mounted at about half a screen below view and unmounted past 1.5 screens above, with at most two live at once. ## Risks and follow-ups - **Android list anchoring is back for all of chat.** It's verified on the emulator for off-screen resizes, following a live conversation, and loading earlier history (on-screen text stays put; that check also found renders reloading through the layout in between, fixed in `5ef72b1`). Jump-to-message from the conversation history sheet was checked with it too. - **A render on screen at open, never measured on this device,** opens at the daemon's estimate (measured in the desktop app) and settles once, a few pixels in testing, while still a skeleton. The page itself never moves. Other content in view can move by that amount once. - **Viewport-sized pages take the frame's height.** A page that only fills its viewport has nothing else to measure, so it shows at the daemon's estimate or this device's saved height for it. - **First load costs data.** A page downloads in full the first time it nears the screen, now up to two screens out if it's never been measured. Pages in this session ran 0.1–1 MB; the daemon allows up to 25 MiB. Later visits revalidate with a 304. There's no "only on Wi-Fi" setting. - **Accessibility.** Inline, a render is one "Expand " button. VoiceOver and TalkBack can read the page's content only in the expanded viewer. - **Fonts.** Pages get system fonts, not Geist as on desktop. - **Follow-up: HTML artifacts** (`detail.event: "artifact"`) still don't show inline on mobile. The phone's auth cookie only covers `/preview/files/`, so an artifact page's sibling files under `/artifact-files/` can't authenticate. The desktop's same-origin artifact host is a `.localhost` name the phone can't reach. This needs a daemon change. Resolved since the first draft: per-WebView memory (now gated to the viewport), blank frames after a killed page process (now remounted), the height shift on every launch (heights now saved), the Android height creep (root-caused and fixed, so no tolerance or clipping), shifts when a page first scrolls into view (measured ahead, list anchored), and the skeleton on Android (checked on a separate emulator), and the iOS viewer flicker (confirmed fixed on the iPhone). Checked and not a risk: sessions on a second paired machine, whose renders load from that machine.

title: fix(cloud): rename a cloud chat, as a local one is renamed
body:
Code changes: +111 -4\
Tests: +143 -0\
Others: +71 -1

## What

A cloud chat can be renamed the same way a local one can, from the sidebar or from its Chat tab.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar ▸ Rename on a cloud session | The name snaps back. The request went to the local daemon, which doesn't know the session, and the error only reached the console. | The session is renamed on the control plane, and the sidebar shows the new name. |
| Double-click / F2 on a cloud Chat tab | Not renamable | Renamable, as a local Chat tab is |
| Renaming a project orchestrator | n/a | Refused, as locally (`ORCHESTRATOR_RENAME_UNSUPPORTED`) |

## Why

A tester reported they could not rename chats in AO Cloud. The sidebar offers Rename for cloud sessions, but `useSessionRename` always called the local daemon's `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/{id}`, and the control plane had no way to rename a session.

## How

Each rule follows the local daemon's `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/{id}`.

**Control plane: `PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}` with `{displayName}`** (`updateSession`, `Store.RenameSession`).
- The name is trimmed and must be 1 to 100 characters. Errors use the daemon's codes: `DISPLAY_NAME_REQUIRED`, `DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`.
- Unknown fields are refused.
- Anyone who may edit the session can rename it, whatever its agent's permission mode; viewers cannot. This is why it is not part of `PATCH .../preferences`, which refuses read-only sessions.
- The project orchestrator can't be renamed (`ORCHESTRATOR_RENAME_UNSUPPORTED`), because the desktop always shows it by its role.
- A rename is recorded as a `session.renamed` audit event, the same way a project rename is.

**Desktop.**
- `useSessionRename` sends a cloud session to its control plane and a local one to the daemon, as before. It reads the control plane URL when the rename is committed, as archiving a cloud session does (`useTerminateSession`), so sidebar rows don't each subscribe to cloud state.
- The sidebar refreshes the list a session comes from: the cloud session list or the local workspace.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface` passes `onSessionRenamed`, which makes its Chat tab renamable, as `SessionView` does for a local Chat tab.

**Contract.** `updateSession` and `UpdateSessionInput` are added to `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, and `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated.

## Testing

Desktop dev build against the local cloud stack (`npm run cloud:local`, control plane built from this branch):
- Sidebar ▸ right-click a cloud session ▸ Rename ▸ type ▸ Enter. The sidebar shows the new name, the control plane logs `PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}` 200, and `GET` returns the new `displayName`. Renaming it back works the same way.
- Over the API: an unknown field returns 400, and a blank name returns `DISPLAY_NAME_REQUIRED`.

Checks:
- `cloud`: `go build ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean, and `go test ./internal/httpapi/` passes.
  - New `TestUpdateSessionRenames` covers a trimmed rename, empty, missing, too long, an unknown field and the orchestrator.
  - New PostgreSQL test `TestRenameSession`: a session in read-only mode can still be renamed, the audit event is written, and the orchestrator is refused.
- `frontend`:
  - `tsc --noEmit` passes.
  - Vitest passes 556 tests across `useSessionRename` (new: cloud to the control plane, no control plane configured, local to the daemon), `Sidebar`, `CloudSessionChatSurface`, `ChatWorkspace`, `CenterPane` and the cloud client.
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` leaves no diff, and its typecheck passes.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
