title: feat: Report a problem starts a bug-report agent (ao triage)
body: Code changes: +1855 -477 Tests: +2441 -311 Others: +299 -114 ## What "Report a problem" now starts an agent that writes the bug report with the user, instead of showing a form. 1. The user picks Report a problem from Cmd+K, Settings, or the background service failure banner. All three call the same function. 2. If the background service is running, the app opens a new chat on Scratchpad with the prompt already in the message box. The project picker is locked on that page, so the report always runs as a standalone agent. The user's usual harness, model and mode stay as they were. The user can add a line about the problem, then presses Send. The session is named Report a problem. 3. If the background service is down, the system terminal opens and runs `ao triage`, which starts `claude` or `codex` directly. With neither installed, it leaves a prompt to paste into any coding agent, and that agent asks for the yes and posts. On Linux the window waits for Enter at the end, so the result stays readable. 4. The agent asks what went wrong, checks for an existing issue, and fills in a draft of about 120 words. 5. It shows the final text and posts to GitHub only after the user says yes. If the user leaves that page without sending and starts a normal new chat, the prompt line is removed and anything they typed stays. Normal new chats keep the project picker. Videos from the real desktop app at `aac4300d75`, using isolated data. Nothing was sent or filed. Each clip shows the full app window. Built-in draft instructions are covered with a labeled redaction. Cmd+K: choose "Report a problem". The report page opens with "What went wrong?". https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d64bdf08-1786-4c3f-ba1e-f0e84e5b4884 Settings: Help, then "Report a problem". It opens the same report page. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50491633-04b7-434a-a6d6-3008e15d2193 ## Why Most bug reports arrive without logs, a version, or a duplicate check, so a maintainer has to ask for them. The program can collect those facts itself. An agent handles the part that needs judgment: asking one or two questions and deciding whether an existing issue is the same bug. This replaces #6946, which ran chat without the background service by building a separate support host and publisher (22k lines, 5k after cutting it down). Opening a terminal covers that case with no extra host. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Settings, Help shows a form with a title, details, and Copy & Create GitHub Issue, Copy & Open Discord and Copy & Open Email buttons | Settings, Help shows one Report a problem button. GitHub, Discord and Email stay as plain links | | In Cmd+K, a Report a problem row opens Settings, Help. Enter on "bug" opens Developer mode | One Report a problem row. Enter on "bug" or "report" starts the agent, same as clicking it. Cmd+K itself still shows only in dev and nightly builds | | Enter on "review" opens New sidebar design, because "hover preview" contains the word. "code" and "keys" have the same problem | Enter on "review" opens the diff and "keys" opens the shortcuts. "code" opens Pairing code or password, whose title (renamed on main in #8081) names it; Open in editor still ranks above the Mobile rows' "qr code" | | The failure banner has no report action | The failure banner has a Report a problem button | | No `ao triage` command | `ao triage` collects evidence, redacts it, and starts an agent. `--no-launch` only writes the files | | The user writes the whole report alone | | The two recordings for the new flow are under What. ## How The program does the fixed steps and the agent does the judgment. **`ao triage`** (`backend/internal/cli/triage*.go`) - Collects version, OS, background service status, log tails, agent CLI versions and recent sessions, capped at 10 s. - Checks that `gh` is installed and logged in, and that the `needs-triage` label exists. - Searches open and closed issues for at most five likely duplicates. - Redacts tokens, auth headers and the home path, then writes `context.md`, `bug-report.md`, `SKILL.md` and `prompt.md` to a scratch folder in the app's data folder. Folders are 0700, files 0600, and they are pruned after 7 days. - Pins every `gh` call to github.com and this repo. - Asks the agent to keep the human sections to about 120 words. Logs and versions go in the evidence comment. **In-app path** (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/report-problem.ts`). `startProblemReport` writes a short prompt into the new chat draft and opens the new chat page on Scratchpad with a `report` flag. With the flag set, `NewChatPage` turns the project picker off and moves back to Scratchpad if it lands on a project. The one exception is a retry after a lost response: that send stays pinned to the project it started on. Without the flag, the page removes the prompt line from the shared draft and keeps the rest. `sessionNameFromBrief` names the session Report a problem instead of using the first 100 characters of the prompt. The prompt tells the agent to use the bug-triage skill and run `ao triage --no-launch`. If the user already has a draft, the prompt goes above it, and a second click does not add it twice. A new draft revision makes an open message box reload it. The session's `ao` is the daemon's own binary, so triage files land in the right data folder. **Cmd+K ranking** (`matchScore` in `frontend/src/renderer/lib/command-palette.ts`). Developer mode has the keyword "debug", which contains "bug". That tied with the real "bug" keyword at 500, and the Settings group won the tie. Now a keyword equal to the query scores 650, a whole word inside a keyword 600, and letters inside a longer word stay at 500. I also removed the Settings row titled Report a problem, because it only opened the Help page and beat the real action on "report". A title match still beats any keyword, so since #8081 renamed a remote-host setting to "Pairing code or password", Enter on "code" opens that setting rather than the editor. **Terminal path.** The agent runs in the scratch folder. When it exits, `ao triage` prints the exact title and body and asks `[y/N]`. Yes runs `gh issue create` or `gh issue comment`, adds the evidence as a separate comment, and writes `result.json`. It never retries a create that may have gone through. If `gh` was missing or signed out when triage started, it checks again after the agent exits. The issue body and evidence comment are both written to disk before the first GitHub write. The terminal command holds only the binary path, `triage`, `AO_DATA_DIR` and `AO_RUN_FILE`. **Instructions.** `.agents/skills/bug-triage/SKILL.md` on main is the one source. The binary embeds a byte-identical copy, and a test fails if they drift. The daemon installs it beside `using-ao` when it starts, and every agent's system prompt gives its path in one short sentence, so the skill is there before `ao triage` runs. That sentence replaces "do not load unrelated command guides", which repeated "only the relevant file", so the always-on prompt stays at its 260 word limit. OpenCode, OpenCode v2 and MiMo Code also get a copy in their workspace skill folders. That copy writes its ownership marker first and never clears the folder, so an interrupted install repairs itself, and a project's own `bug-triage` folder is still left alone. Claude Code and Codex read it through the system prompt, the same way they read `using-ao`, so it does not appear in their own skill lists. **Logs.** Includes the two commits from #6210 so the daemon log lives under the data dir, where the snapshot reads it. The daemon opens `daemon.log` only after it holds the data-dir lock, so a predecessor still shutting down cannot rotate the file under it, and one record never exceeds the 16 MiB cap. Electron main now writes `desktop.log` (5 MiB, one backup). A Go panic never reaches `daemon.log`, so the snapshot also reads `logs/daemon-crash.log` beside `running.json` (added on main in #8194). It keeps only crash sections from daemon runs that started in the last 7 days and tags each panic `[daemon started ]`. **Windows.** The agent gets a one-line pointer to `prompt.md`, because batch shims drop newlines in arguments. **Left out on purpose.** - Cmd+K stays behind `isCommandPaletteEnabled`, so stable builds reach the report through Settings. - There is no model picker. - The Settings group still ranks above Global when two rows tie exactly. "copy" opens Copy on select, not Copy session path. Swapping the groups would send "import" to Go home, so I left the order alone. - A session or project with "bug" or "report" in its title still ranks above Report a problem, because a title match beats a keyword. - There is no hard approval lock in the app. The agent has the user's `gh` login and is told to ask first, but nothing stops it. The terminal path blocks until `y`. ## Testing **Takeover follow-up, final head `df7dd4a143`.** Main was merged in twice with normal merges (`5cac73d268` up to `34c77c20cc`, then `5929279e8e` for #8248); no rebase or force-push. Six files conflicted: `daemon.go`, `telemetrymeta/cli.go`, `ui-store.ts`, `NewTaskNavigator.tsx`, `NewChatPage.tsx` and `ReportProblemContent.tsx`. On a report page, main's new redirect away from Cloud agent projects stands aside, so the page keeps its Scratchpad lock and report flag. After the merge, the PR also adds the crash-log evidence, the daemon log, payload, redaction and skill install fixes above (the skill install now also removes temp files left by an interrupted write, found by listing the folder rather than globbing the path), and one corrected palette case. Eleven review threads opened during the takeover (three from native reviews, eight from CodeRabbit) were fixed, answered and resolved. - No local tests, typecheck, builds or app runs were done for these commits. They rely on CI. No new screenshots or recordings; the videos above are from `aac4300d75`, before the takeover. - CI at `df7dd4a143`: 21 checks passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending (run 43405354189; no checks are marked required on this branch, `ci-ok` aggregates them). `frontend / vitest (2)` needed two reruns: the first attempt failed in `ShareSessionDialog.people.test.tsx` ("Unable to find … Change access"), the second in `src/main/artifact-snapshots.test.ts:128` (newest snapshot ordering). Neither file is touched by this PR, and the frontend is identical to `cb098dd261`, which passed; only the two `hookutil` Go files changed since. `go / backend-core (1)` failed once in the copilot package (`TestFinalAssistantMessageWaitsForTheLogToCatchUp`, no copilot changes here) and passed on rerun. - Earlier heads: `7727b168da` and `cb098dd261` passed all CI checks. On `c8a6840376`, typecheck and `vitest (1)` failed on a duplicate import left by the merge, fixed in `7727b168da`, and `vitest (2)` failed on the "code" palette case, fixed in `fd3c813051`. `renderer-smoke (2)` failed there in `e2e/session-switch-held.spec.ts` ("the hold outlasted its limit"); main failed the same assertion at `8892282f0b`, and it passed on `7727b168da`. - Orchestrator's built-in review: approved at `df7dd4a143` with no required changes (earlier passes also approved `7727b168da`, `9df14ed949` and `e9cddae578`). One optional note was left as is: two installs running at the same moment in the same workspace could remove each other's temp file; no path that shares a workspace that way was found. This is Orchestrator's internal review, not a GitHub approval. - Not tested: a real GitHub post, the daemon takeover log handoff, a real daemon panic, and the app flow after the merges. The report page, picker lock and Cmd+K should be checked by hand. - `36ade2985e`: diagnostic collection now accepts the desktop logger's `[uncaught]` level. `TestTriageSnapshotIncludesUncaughtDesktopErrors` failed on `aac4300d75` and passed after the fix, checking both the snapshot and report draft. The nearby log tests and CLI build passed. - `aac4300d75`, real desktop app on macOS with isolated data: Cmd+K and Settings, Help, Report a problem both open the page headed "What went wrong?". The command palette entry reads "Report a problem". - `aac4300d75`: the report label test passed all 17 cases (`src/renderer/i18n/report-problem.test.ts`). The desktop daemon, main process, preload and renderer built successfully. - Full suite results are in [CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42703736859). Earlier validation, retained from the existing description: - Go: `internal/cli`, `internal/config`, `internal/daemon`, `internal/skillassets` and `internal/telemetrymeta` pass. Three `internal/cli` tests read the session's own `AO_*` variables, so they need those unset when run inside an Orchestrator session. - Frontend: the 7 test files for this flow pass (361 tests). Typecheck and e2e typecheck pass. - New Cmd+K tests failed before the fix (12 failures, with Enter on "bug" picking `setting:developer-mode`) and pass after it. Two press Enter in the real `CommandPalette` component. The rest check the Enter target for "bug", "report", "issue", "feedback", "keys", "code" and "review". - I compared the Enter target before and after for 326 queries (every row title and keyword). 16 changed. Beyond the report queries and the three above: "dark" and "light" now toggle the theme instead of opening Settings, "cloud" opens a shared link, "cli" opens the CLI setting, "upgrade" opens Updates, and "browser profile" opens Create profile. - Real dev app on an isolated data dir, on fabf0dc978: Cmd+K, "bug", Enter and Settings, Help, Report a problem both land on a new chat on Scratchpad with the prompt filled in once. The picker is off and a real mouse click opens no menu. - fabf0dc978: after leaving without sending, a normal new chat in a project shows only the typed words, and its picker lists Scratchpad, demo-app and Create new. - fabf0dc978: sent a report on Claude Code with Haiku 5.5. The session is named Report a problem and has no project. - 6cd8500e6d, before the last merge of main: the same send ran to the end. The agent ran triage and showed a 98-word draft with the title, body, label and evidence comment, then asked for a yes. I did not say yes and nothing was filed. - 6cd8500e6d: a file pasted on Scratchpad before starting the report reached the agent, which described it correctly. A file pasted on a project page stays on the report page, but I did not send that one. - Earlier build, real dev app: harness, model and mode stayed unchanged, text already in the message box stayed under the prompt, and "report" and Enter landed the same way as "bug". - `e2e/chat-turn-settle.spec.ts` from #7806 failed `renderer-smoke` twice here. The real `ao triage` binary with no agents on PATH wrote the in-app prompt. The Linux wait command, run with `/bin/sh` on macOS, stayed open until Enter and kept exit status 3. - Not tested: a Codex agent finding the skill (the picker would not open through the debug port, and Codex gets the same system prompt text), the OpenCode and MiMo Code skill folders with a real agent (unit tests only), a real GitHub post, sending a file pasted on a project page, the terminal launch on Windows and Linux, the packaged app, and modes other than Auto-approve (a stricter mode may ask for approval before `ao triage` runs). - ef3726e5ad, real dev app on an isolated data dir: the daemon wrote the skill at start, byte-identical to the source. Its transcript has that one read and nothing else. The skill install changes nothing on screen, so the videos stand. - 44dbd02f08 merges main and resolves a conflict in `editor-handoff.ts`. The editor, launch and palette tests, typecheck and the Go build pass on it. The earlier app runs were not repeated. - The background service stopped path has unit tests on this build. Its launch was not rerun here. - The earlier Litmus runs and instruction scores covered the old hidden prompt, so they are dropped from this description. ## Regression risk Risk tier: HIGH (score 6). The guard found no blockers. The review follow-up adds one accepted log level and a snapshot regression test. Could break: the Settings Help screen, the failure banner, the Cmd+K list and what Enter picks there, new chat drafts, the project picker on the new chat page, session names for standalone agents, daemon log location, terminal launch from the app, skill install at daemon start, OpenCode and MiMo Code workspace skill folders.\ Checked: Settings, Cmd+K, the locked picker and the normal new chat in the real dev app, all work. `matchScore` has no callers outside the palette, and the 326-query comparison covers its Enter targets. The removed Settings row had no other users, and Settings, Help still has the button. Draft handling has unit tests and a dev app check. Banner and terminal launch have unit tests only on this build. `reportProblemDestinationUrl` is unchanged, and its caller still works. The `prepare` bridge is gone from the Electron main process, preload and tests, and the dictation bridge beside it is kept.\ Changed test expectations: one palette case changed. Enter on "code" now expects `setting:connection-password`, because main renamed that row to "Pairing code or password"; the case still checks that Open in editor outranks the Mobile rows' "qr code". `editor-handoff.test.ts`: the Windows file open test from #6927 now expects `start` instead of `/k`, because this PR sends every terminal launch through one helper. The launcher has no stdio, so a direct `cmd.exe` gets no console. `GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx`, `smoke-t0.spec.ts` and the report tests expected the old form or the hidden prompt, and both are removed on purpose.\ Regression from: none Other notes: - The Settings button, the banner, Cmd+K and `ao triage` form one report flow. - The 4 new test skips are conditional: POSIX shell fixtures on Windows, or a missing fixture. - Both `nolint` annotations have reasons beside them. `daemon/log_file.go` opens a path rooted in the data dir; `hookutil.go` reads from the caller-owned skill directory. - "Opening..." matches 25 existing strings on main, and the DESIGN rule on ellipses is about search fields. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable (#6946, #6210, #6721) - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.): see the checks on this PR ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added “Report a problem” actions in Settings, the command palette, and the daemon-failure banner. title: feat(cloud): name a project orchestrator's Coder workspace <prefix>-orch-<id>
body:
Code changes: +60 -3\
Tests: +98 -29\
Others: +19 -17

## What

A project orchestrator's Coder workspace is now named `<prefix>-orch-<id>`, so in Coder it can be told apart from the project's worker workspaces (`<prefix>-<id>`).

| Session | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Worker | `todo-app-6d1f3b9a2c4e` | `todo-app-6d1f3b9a2c4e` (unchanged) |
| Project orchestrator | `todo-app-1b2c3d4e5f60` | `todo-app-orch-1b2c3d4e5f60` |
| Orchestrator, no prefix (deployment Coder) | `ao-<hash>` | `ao-orch-<id>` |
| GitHub scratch project's orchestrator on a bring-your-own Coder | `ao-<hash>` | `<project>-orch-<id>` |

Existing sessions keep the names they were created with.

## Why

A tester running AO Cloud on their own Coder could not tell which workspace was the orchestrator's: every session's workspace was `<prefix>-<id>`.

## How

- **Where the name is chosen**: when the session's plan is made.
  - `domain.CoderOrchestratorWorkspaceNamePrefix` turns the project prefix into `<prefix>-orch`, or `ao-orch` with no prefix.
  - `Plan.ForOrchestrator` stores that prefix in the plan's Coder profile (`coder.workspaceNamePrefix`). It follows `WithFreestyleSnapshot`'s rewrite and validates the result.
  - Both places that make an orchestrator's plan call it: `createSession` for kind orchestrator, and `scratchSessionPlan` (GitHub scratch projects).
  - Children from `ao spawn` are workers and are unchanged.
- **Why existing sessions keep their names**: the stored profile drives every later step. That covers workspace creation, `FindBySession`, the bootstrap identity check and the workspace link (`WorkspaceURL`). It is written once, when the session is created, and restore and resume reuse it.
- **Limits**: the project prefix is shortened to 15 characters before `-orch` is added. The stored prefix therefore stays a valid prefix of at most 20 characters, and the name stays within Coder's 32.
- **Scratch projects**: `scratchSessionPlan` now also passes the project name as the default prefix on a bring-your-own Coder, as `createSession` does, so a scratch project's orchestrator is named after the project.
- **Wording**: the "Workspace name prefix" hints (all locales) and `cloud/docs/bring-your-own-coder.md` describe the orchestrator's name.

Not in this change:
- Reserving `-orch` in project prefixes. That would invalidate existing projects whose prefix already ends in it; names stay unique anyway, because they include the session ID.

## Testing

Checks:
- `cloud`: `go build ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean. `go test ./...` passes; the PostgreSQL tests skip without a test database. New and updated tests:
  - `TestPlanForOrchestratorNamesTheWorkspace`: no prefix → `ao-orch`, `todo-app` → `todo-app-orch`, and a 20-character prefix is shortened. The stored profile stays valid, and a Docker plan is unchanged.
  - `TestOrchestratorWorkspaceNameFitsCoder`: the name keeps `-orch-` and stays within 32 characters for the longest prefix.
  - `TestCreateSessionStampsBYOStartupPolicyAndPrefix` checks both kinds: an orchestrator gets `ahmad-orch` and a worker keeps `ahmad`.
  - `TestScratchSessionPlanUsesOrgDefaultAndBYOConnection`: the scratch orchestrator gets `todo-app-orch`.
- `frontend`: vitest passes for `CreateProjectFlow`, `CloudProjectSettingsForm`, `CoderTemplateOptions`, settings and i18n (589 tests).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(mobile): swipe to merge a pull request from the review screen
body: Code changes: +343 -13 Tests: +142 -0 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary On the mobile review screen, the **Merge** pill and its "Merge PR #N?" alert are replaced by a full-width **swipe-to-merge** slider docked at the bottom of the screen: a footer under the scroll view, within thumb reach and clear of the home indicator, like a checkout's slide-to-pay. Carrying the knob to the end of the track is the confirmation. - **Look:** light glass in GitHub's merge-button green (`#238636` / `#2ea043`; `#1f883d` on light). A faint green wash, a top sheen, and a green border that brightens as the knob travels. - **Drag:** solid green floods in behind the knob, only as far as it has gone. The knob turns solid green with a white merge icon and a faint white rim so it stays distinct from the fill. The label dims as it's covered. - **Commit:** past 85% of the track, the knob snaps to the end and shows "Merging…" with a spinner. A failed merge springs it back with an error haptic and shows the existing error text. A successful merge keeps the slider on screen. - **Merged:** the bar stays full with the knob at the end, fades from merge green to GitHub's merged purple (`#8957e5`; `#8250df` on light) over 700ms, reads "Merged PR #N", and locks. A PR that was already merged when the screen opens shows the purple bar without the fade. - **Cross-platform:** drawn with plain React Native `experimental_backgroundImage` gradients and `boxShadow`, so iOS and Android render the same. Light and dark palettes. - **Accessibility:** the slider is one accessible button. Screen-reader users get an `activate` action that keeps the original confirmation alert, since they can't drag. - **Haptics:** the drag feels like a physical slider. - A light tap when you grab the knob. - A selection tick for each of ten detents the knob passes. - A rigid bump when it crosses the commit point, in place of that step's tick. - A medium impact on release into the merge. - The existing success and error haptics still mark the outcome. - **Safety:** commits are distance-based, not velocity-based, so a horizontal flick while scrolling can't merge. Reduced motion removes the chevron pulse and the springs. ## Android fast-swipe fix On Android, gesture-handler reports a pan's `translationX` from where the pan *activated*, not where the finger went down. A fast flick's first event can already be 50–70dp along, so that distance was lost and the knob stopped short of the commit point. Before the fix, quick swipes merged only 2 of 10 times on the emulator. The drag is now measured from the touch-down `absoluteX` (captured in `onBegin`), and the lift position counts in `onEnd`. `SwipeToMerge.test.tsx` reproduces the Android event sequence. ## Screenshots On a physical Pixel 10a, merging a real pull request (#6989) through the slider: rest, dragging, merging, merged. Simulator and emulator, light and dark: Screenshots show the slider itself; it now sits in the bottom footer rather than under the PR row. | | Rest | Dragging | Merging | |---|---|---|---| | iOS dark | | | | | iOS light | | | | | Android dark | | | | | Android light | | | | After a successful merge (iOS dark), mid-fade and settled: ## Testing - Ran the mobile CI job locally on Node 20.20.2 (CI's pinned runtime) in `packages/mobile`: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm test` all pass, with 2280/2280 tests. - New tests: - `swipe-to-merge-model.test.ts`: travel, bounds, and the commit threshold. - `SwipeToMerge.test.tsx`: a fast flick whose `translationX` lags still commits, a short drag doesn't, the haptic sequence (grab, detents, armed bump, release) fires in order, and a merged slider reads "Merged PR #N" with no merge action. - Manual checks on an iOS 26.5 simulator and an Android emulator (`worli`), in light and dark mode, on a temporary test screen with a fake merge handler (not committed): - Partial drags spring back. - Full drags commit. - A failed merge resets to the glass state. - After the fix, quick 0.2–0.25s swipes committed 5/5 on iOS and 15/15 on Android, and half-way drags never committed. - Installed as a side-by-side Release build ("AO Swipe", OTA off) on a physical iPhone 13 (iOS 27) and Pixel 10a. Both launch cleanly. - On the Pixel 10a, merged a real pull request (#6989) end to end through the docked slider. It went from rest to the drag fill, then "Merging…", then the purple "Merged PR #6989" bar, and the screen's PR row updated to **Merged**. ## Not verified - **iPhone:** the real merge flow was exercised on the Pixel 10a only. The iPhone 13 build launches cleanly but hasn't been taken through a merge.

title: fix(chat): reconnect chats after a restart instead of asking for Resume
body:
Code changes: +142 -8
Tests: +244 -0
Others: +0 -0 ## Problem After AO restarts (every nightly update does this), a Chat can show **"The agent controller stopped"** with a Resume button even though its agent process is still running. Clicking Resume fixes it in under a second, but the user has to do it for each chat, after every restart. Three gaps cause it: 1. **No retry.** On startup the daemon gets one 30 s attempt to reconnect each Chat to its surviving provider host. A failure is only logged (`reconcile: live pass failed, skipping`). 2. **Resume offered too early.** While the daemon is still checking a session (before the startup pass reaches it, or during a retry), the chat already shows the red banner and offers Resume. 3. **No refresh.** When a background reconnect succeeds, nothing tells an open window. A live reattach writes no change event, so the chat keeps showing the stale `stopped` state. Captured on a real desktop restart (nightly `0.14.4-nightly.202610200854`, daemon log saved). Three chats on three harnesses failed at the same instant, 30 s into the startup pass: ``` reconcile: live pass failed, skipping sessionID=…-280 error="check session …-280: resume chat: reconcile conversation authentication: context deadline exceeded" (Claude) reconcile: live pass failed, skipping sessionID=…-260 error="… reconcile conversation authentication: context deadline exceeded" (OpenCode) reconcile: live pass failed, skipping sessionID=…-249 error="… reconcile conversation authentication: context deadline exceeded" (Codex) ``` The check spent its whole budget waiting on the store's single writer. Resume then reconnected each chat to the same host in 0.06–0.7 s. ## Fix - **Retry (`session_manager`).** When a Chat's startup check fails with the check's deadline (`context.DeadlineExceeded`) or an inconclusive host owner (`ErrChatRecoveryInconclusive`), retry the reconnect in the background after 2 s, 5 s, 10 s, 20 s, 30 s, 1 m and 1 m. Each retry: - is reconnect-only, so it never launches a provider or restores a worktree; - waits if a user operation holds the session, and tries again on the next delay; - stops once the Chat is live, hibernated, or terminated. The session stays `checking` until a retry settles it. Success reads `ready`. Only the last failed attempt, or a failure that isn't retryable, reads `unavailable` and brings Resume back. - **Say it's reconnecting (`ChatWorkspace`).** While a stopped chat's session is `checking`, the banner and composer show "Reconnecting to the agent…" and "AO restarted. History is kept." The red alert and its Resume and Open shell buttons are hidden. This also covers the window before the startup pass reaches the session. - **Refresh (`SessionChatSurface`).** Refetch the conversation snapshot when the session's readiness turns `ready`. The workspace query already polls every 300 ms while any session is `checking`, so the chat clears as soon as the reconnect lands. ## Before / after | Before (`main`): the chat stays stopped | After (this PR): it reconnects on its own | |---|---| | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/dcf75bb51a907814738c8d99568c085ae74b0272/before.gif) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/dcf75bb51a907814738c8d99568c085ae74b0272/after.gif) | Previews run at 2× speed. Full-speed MP4s: [before.mp4](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dcf75bb51a907814738c8d99568c085ae74b0272/before.mp4) · [after.mp4](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dcf75bb51a907814738c8d99568c085ae74b0272/after.mp4) | | startup check | host free again | what the chat shows | chat back | |---|---|---|---|---| | before | failed at 21.7 s, logged once | 27.5 s | red "stopped" + Resume, start to end | never: still stopped at 83 s | | after | failed at 24.6 s, retry failed at 36.8 s | 44.5 s | "Reconnecting to the agent…", no buttons | 44.5 s (`reconcile: chat reattached on retry`), window ≈0.5 s later | No red banner appears in any frame of the after recording; I checked every second for the banner's red text. ## How the recordings were made - **Setup:** an isolated lab with its own data dir, run file, and Electron profile, and one Codex chat that has finished a turn. - **Restart:** quit the app completely, then start it again, as an update does. The after clip cuts 16 s of the black screen while the dev app rebuilt. - **Before:** the nightly's UI (unpackaged from its `app.asar`) with a daemon built from `main`. - **After:** this branch's UI and daemon (`electron-forge start`). - **Trigger:** to make the startup check fail on demand, a script attaches to the chat's host as a stale client and holds it after the new daemon is ready. It holds for 14 s before and 30 s after, so the retry visibly takes two attempts. This is the "replaced daemon has not detached yet" case `persistenthost` already anticipates (`chat host already has a controller`), and it takes the same path as the production deadline. Both errors are covered by unit tests. ## Tests - New `session_manager` tests, using the production error text: - transient failures (deadline and inconclusive) retry until reconnected; - the session stays `checking` while a retry is pending; - a permanent failure does not retry and reads `unavailable`; - the retry settles a chat reattached by something else as `ready`; - the retry gives up after its schedule and reads `unavailable`. - New renderer tests: - a stopped chat whose session is `checking` shows "Reconnecting to the agent…" with no alert or Resume, and gets them back when `unavailable`; - the chat refreshes when readiness settles, and not for a session that was ready from the start. - Each new main-path test fails with its fix removed and passes with it. - `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./internal/session_manager ./internal/storage/sqlite/store` (the CI command): pass. - `golangci-lint run ./internal/session_manager/...` (v2.13.2): 0 issues. - `npx vitest run` on `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` and `SessionChatSurface.test.tsx`: 272 passed. - Earlier commits on this branch also passed: - frontend `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e`; - the full `npx vitest run`, apart from one file that fails only with a local `better-sqlite3` built for Electron's ABI and passes 47 of 47 after `npm rebuild`. - **After rebasing onto `main`** (one import conflict in `SessionChatSurface.tsx`), rerun on head `465fc7c9d1`: - `go vet`, `go build ./...`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), and the CI race command for `session_manager` and `store`: pass. - Both chat test files: 276 passed. - Frontend `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e`: pass. - Full `npx vitest run`: 514 of 516 files passed. The 2 failures (a 20 s timeout in `browser-history-store.test.ts` and a missed "Load earlier messages" in `IndependentSideChatDelivery.test.tsx`) came at load average 80–130 from other work on this machine. Rerun alone, both files passed 36 of 36. - CI's Frontend job passed all of these on this head. ## Not in this PR - **Why the writer is busy for 30 s at startup.** #6848 makes the wait cancellable, and #6804 and #6846 cut the contention. - **The ~67 s before the startup pass begins**, measured on the same real restart. Reconnects still wait for it, but chats now say "Reconnecting to the agent…" during it instead of offering Resume. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(mobile): connect on the first scan after allowing Local Network access
body: Code changes: +370 -57 Tests: +301 -10 Others: +0 -0 ## Problem On a fresh iOS install, the first pairing scan always failed. The first request to a LAN address raises the Local Network prompt and fails instantly; the request never leaves the phone. The pair screen showed a red error. It had also stopped reading the camera after that one attempt. After tapping **Allow**, scanning again did nothing until the user found **Try again** or reopened the screen. The error itself told them to "scan it again". Measured on an iPhone 13 (iOS 27.2) against a lab machine on the LAN: - While the prompt is pending, every LAN request fails in 3–40 ms with "The Internet connection appears to be offline". - Answering the prompt sends the app inactive and back to active within 8 ms. That's before the grant applies, so a single retry on returning to the foreground also failed. - On a different network (mobile hotspot), iOS shows **no** prompt but fails requests with the same instant error, so the two cases can't be told apart from JS. ## Change - **No error while iOS asks.** A LAN code that reached nothing keeps retrying silently, once a second, while local network access is unconfirmed. Meanwhile the screen shows "Connecting… If asked, allow access to your local network." The retries stop 10 s after the scan, or 3 s after the prompt is answered. If the prompt is answered after the error appears, the code is retried once on its own. (`lib/localNetworkWait.ts`) - **Remember access.** After the first successful LAN pairing (QR or manual), later scans skip the Local Network wait. (`lib/localNetworkStore.ts`) - **Scanner re-arms after a failure.** Pointing at the code again, or at a new code, starts a new attempt. A code held in view doesn't retry every frame. (`lib/scanGate.ts`) - **Feedback from the first moment.** "Connecting…" shows as soon as a scan starts, because the first attempt alone can take ~20 s when a code's tunnel is down. The Local Network line appears only during the Local Network wait. An attempt that throws shows "Couldn't pair" instead of stopping silently. - **Quieter UI.** The connecting and failure states sit inline under the viewfinder with no tinted box or border. Try again and Open settings use the same text-action style as "Enter details manually". - **Shorter copy.** Unreachable-code messages are one actionable line each, and the Local Network hint is one line. These strings are used only on the pair screen; the hint is also used by the manual-connect sheet. - **Haptic.** A light tap when a scanned code starts connecting. | Before | Connecting | Error (light) | Error (dark) | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 2297 passed. `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. New tests cover the scan gate, the wait and retry timing, and the copy, including a length cap. - iPhone 13, iOS 27.2, Release builds side by side, against a lab machine logging every request: | Scenario | `main` | This PR | |---|---|---| | Fresh install, same Wi-Fi | Error; Allow does nothing; Try again needed | "Connecting…", connects 0.06–0.7 s after Allow | | Mobile hotspot (wrong network) | — | "This code only works nearby" after ~10 s | | Back on the right Wi-Fi, Try again | — | Prompt appears; connects after Allow, no error | | Haptic on scan | — | Felt on device | Independently verified by @ronishrohan on an iPhone 16 (iOS 27.2) at `5023933`. That covers the late answer (Allow after 15+ s connects on its own), a failed code held in view (no per-frame retry), pointing away and back, already-confirmed access with an unreachable machine (no 10 s wait), offline, and the focus guard behind the manual sheet. ## Risks and follow-ups - **Off-network wait.** On the wrong network, the first scans wait up to 10 s before the error, because iOS gives no way to distinguish that from a pending prompt. A follow-up will add `expo-network` to compare the phone's Wi-Fi address with the code's LAN address and skip the wait. That's a native change, so it needs a store build, not an OTA. - **Denied users.** Someone who denied the prompt earlier also waits 10 s per scan before the error and its Open settings action. - **Slow tunnel failures.** A code whose tunnel is unreachable still takes up to ~20 s to fail, because `probeEndpoint` retries tunnels for `TUNNEL_PROBE_WINDOW_MS`. Connecting is now shown throughout. A follow-up could skip that retry when the failure is the instant "offline" error rather than DNS. - **Local test builds only.** To launch iOS 27 SDK builds on iOS 27, the local test builds needed UIScene adoption in the generated, gitignored `ios/` project. That isn't part of this PR, but local Xcode 27 builds of `main` will crash on launch until the template adopts UIScene.

title: fix(mobile): match reviewer chat to sessions and keep chat composers keyboard-aware
body: Code changes: +327 -115 Tests: +181 -24 Others: +0 -0 (screenshots live on `ao/reviewer-chat-ui/reviewer-chat-keyboard-screenshots`) ## What this fixes Three mobile chat issues, all reproduced on an Android emulator: 1. **Reviewer chat didn't match session chat, and the keyboard covered it on Android.** The reviewer screen had its own flat composer and React Native's `KeyboardAvoidingView` with no Android behaviour and a hard-coded `keyboardVerticalOffset={88}`. With the keyboard open, the composer was completely hidden. 2. **A keyboard-sized empty gap with no keyboard (session chat).** keyboard-controller only learns about the keyboard from its window-insets animation callback, and some transitions never reach it. Reproduced by focusing the composer, then holding the mic the first time: the system's microphone permission dialog takes focus and hides the keyboard, keyboard-controller never reports the close, and the root keeps its keyboard padding with nothing under it. The same desync can also leave the composer *under* a keyboard it never saw. 3. **Review actions (the ⋯ sheet on the review page) only sometimes closed on swipe down (Android).** With two detents, Material's `BottomSheetBehavior` treats the 60% detent as "collapsed". Once the sheet content scrolls, a downward drag from the content did not hide it: 0 of 3 attempts on the emulator, including an 800px drag. Short content still closed, which is why it felt random. ## Changes - **`useChatKeyboard`** (new) gives the session and reviewer chats the same keyboard handling. It keeps keyboard-controller's early events for the animation and reconciles them with React Native's `Keyboard` events, which compare the real window insets on every layout pass. When the two disagree, the later report wins and the composer dock is pinned instead of riding a stuck progress value (`reduceChatKeyboard` / `chatDockRiseOverride` in `keyboardInset.ts`). - **Android keyboard pad:** keyboard-controller's height already includes the navigation bar on edge-to-edge Android (it reported 336 where React Native reported 312 on a 24dp gesture bar). The old code added the nav bar on top, so the session composer sat ~32dp above the keyboard instead of the intended 8dp. Only React Native's height gets the nav bar added back now. - **`ReviewerComposer`** reuses `ChatComposer`'s dock, glass pill (`ComposerGlass`), metrics, mic key and growing field. It keeps only send / attach / interrupt, with no turn settings or queue. - **Review actions** gets one detent on Android (`androidDetents: [0.6]`, the same treatment conversation actions already had), so Material skips the collapsed state and closes on a normal swipe. iOS keeps `[0.6, 0.95]`; UIKit's sheet already dismisses from the lower detent. The per-route `androidDetents` field replaces the hard-coded conversation-actions branch in `_layout.tsx`. - Removed `screenKeyboardAvoidance`, which no longer has callers. ### Review follow-up (12cbb32) - React Native's keyboard reports are held for `PLATFORM_KEYBOARD_SETTLE_MS` (500ms) and applied only if keyboard-controller still disagrees and React Native's own record hasn't moved on. On Android its `keyboardDidHide` fires as the close *starts* (logged on the emulator: React Native `didHide` at 91195, keyboard-controller `willHide` at 91199), which dropped the pad at once and snapped the composer. - A pinned dock stays pinned until keyboard-controller reports the close; the reducer no longer reacts to `keyboardWillHide`. - Keyboard heights compare with a 1dp tolerance. - `MicKey` takes `disabled`. Both composers pass `stopped || submitting`, so dictation can't write into a read-only field. title: bug(desktop): harness "Update all" shows a bare Updating… spinner for minutes with no progress, elapsed time, or output
body:
## Bug
Harness updates started from "Update all" show a bare `Updating…` spinner for 4+ minutes with no progress, elapsed time, or output. It looks hung, but the updates are working: the installers are downloading slowly. On a slow connection, nothing in the UI tells the user anything is happening.

**Source:** live report from the founder (desktop app, 2026-10-20) | **Reported by:** maintainer | **Analyzed against:** `30723c0be` (main)
**Confidence:** High (live process inspection plus code trace)
**Priority:** medium (feature works and finishes; the UX makes it look broken)

## Observed live (macOS, Surfshark WireGuard VPN active)
"Update all" started 3 updates at the same moment, all as children of the daemon (PID 24814):

| Harness | Command | Download growth over 10s | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kimchi v1.16.0 → v1.17.0 | `kimchi update self --force` | ~90 KB/s, tarball to `$TMPDIR/kimchi-update-*/` | finished after ~4m45s |
| Droid v0.244.0 → v0.245.0 | `droid update` | ~88 KB/s, writing `~/.factory/updates/droid` (≈50 MB at 4m30s) | still running at 4m47s |
| Copilot v1.0.98 → v1.0.101 | `npm install @github/copilot@1.0.101` | ~395 KB/s, writing the ~100 MB `copilot-darwin-arm64/copilot` binary | still running at 4m47s |

All processes were in state `S`, had stdin on a pipe (not waiting for a prompt), held established HTTPS connections, and their files were growing steadily. Nothing was deadlocked.

## Root cause
- `backend/internal/service/systeminstall/systeminstall.go`: each run is bounded only by `defaultInstallTimeout = 15 * time.Minute` (l.305). The job exposes `StartedAt`/`Output`, but no progress or bytes.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/HarnessUpdateNotice.tsx:301` and `components/settings/harness/describe-harness.ts:123` render a static `settings.harness.updating` ("Updating…") label with a spinner. No elapsed time, no live output, and no "taking longer than usual / slow network" hint.
- "Update all" starts every outdated harness at once, so the downloads share bandwidth. Each one finishes later than it would alone, and all the rows sit on a spinner for the same long stretch.

## Suggested fix
1. Show elapsed time on the busy button/row, e.g. "Updating… 2:41", from `job.startedAt`.
2. After about 60s, show a secondary line: "Still downloading, which can take a few minutes on slow networks", with a "Show output" disclosure that streams the job's `Output` (already captured).
3. Optional: run "Update all" with limited concurrency (for example 2 at a time) so each row finishes and turns green sooner, instead of every row crawling together.
4. Optional: a Cancel action that kills the job's process tree.

## Reproduction
1. Throttle the network (VPN or Network Link Conditioner at ~1 Mbps).
2. Settings → Harnesses (or the harness update notice) → "Update all" with 3+ outdated harnesses (Droid, Copilot, Kimchi).
3. All rows show `Updating…` with no change for several minutes.

## Related
- [#3938](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/3938): Updates settings, missing loading spinner (closed; same surface)

title: bug(harness): Copilot npm update always fails: managed install looks for bin/copilot-darwin-arm64 instead of bin/copilot (regression from #6745)
body:
## Bug
Updating GitHub Copilot (npm install) always fails with a raw internal error:

> the install finished but /Users/<user>/.ao/data/harnesses/copilot/versions/v1/bin/copilot-darwin-arm64 is missing

The npm install succeeds (the ~100 MB native binary downloads), then AO looks for the wrong executable name, deletes the new release and reports failure. Every Copilot npm update hits this, so Retry can't succeed.

**Source:** live report from the founder (desktop app, 2026-10-20) | **Reported by:** maintainer | **Analyzed against:** `30723c0be` (main)
**Confidence:** High (exact code path traced and matched to the live filesystem)
**Priority:** high (harness updates for Copilot are broken with no workaround inside AO; regression)
**Regression from:** [PR #6745](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6745), "update harnesses while sessions run" (2026-10-19), which added managed side-by-side npm installs.

## Root cause
1. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/copilot/copilot.go:180-277`: the Copilot resolver deliberately skips the `npm-loader.js` shim and returns the platform-native binary `.../@github/copilot/node_modules/.bin/copilot-<os>-<arch>` (here `copilot-darwin-arm64`).
2. `backend/internal/service/systeminstall/managed.go`: `managedCLIName(baseline)` uses `filepath.Base(baseline.path)`, giving `copilot-darwin-arm64`.
3. `managedBinRel` then expects `<release>/bin/copilot-darwin-arm64`, but `npm install -g --prefix <release>` creates `bin/copilot` (the package's `bin` entry). The `os.Stat` at managed.go:~254 fails, the deferred `RemoveAll` deletes `versions/v1`, and the update fails.

Live state confirms this: `~/.ao/data/harnesses/copilot/versions/` is empty after the failure. The user's own `~/.local/bin/copilot`, a symlink to `npm-loader.js`, is untouched and still reports 1.0.98. Rollback is correct and nothing is lost.

Other harnesses whose resolvers return a platform-native or renamed binary instead of the package's bin name are probably affected the same way. Audit every adapter whose resolved basename differs from the npm/bun/uv/pipx bin name.

## Fix
- Take the managed CLI name from the package's declared bin (for npm, read `package.json` `bin` in the installed release, or keep a per-target bin name), not from the basename of the resolved executable. Or, for Copilot, map the resolved native path back to `copilot`. Keep the native-binary preference only for launching.
- After the managed install, resolve the launch binary through the same adapter logic (loader → native) when that matters.
- **UX:** don't show raw absolute paths as the headline error. Say something like "Copilot updated, but AO couldn't find its executable. Your current version is unchanged," and put the path under "Show diagnostics".
- Test: a managed npm update for Copilot where the baseline resolves to `node_modules/.bin/copilot-darwin-arm64` must end with `current` → the new release and the launcher pointing at a working binary.

## Reproduction
1. Have Copilot installed with npm (`~/.local/bin/copilot` → `npm-loader.js`), at an outdated version.
2. AO desktop → harness updates → Update (or Update all) on GitHub Copilot.
3. After the download, the row shows the error above. Retry gives the same result.

## Related
- [#6990](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6990): Update all spinner shows no progress (same flow, same session)
- [#2832](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/2832): npm binary detection gap across adapters (closed; same subsystem)
- [PR #6934](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6934): open follow-up to managed installs; check for overlap

title: fix(harness): list the bin directory when a managed install's executable is missing
body:

## What happened to this PR
It originally fixed the Copilot managed-npm-update failure, but main landed the same fixes first:
- #7005 added the `managedCLINames` table (`copilot`, `opencode`) plus the Copilot resolver work and the regression test `TestManagedCopilotInstallsTheLauncherNotThePlatformBinary`.

That listing is exactly what would have made #6991 obvious from a user's diagnostics: `…/bin/copilot-darwin-arm64 is missing; …/bin contains: copilot`.

The detail goes through the existing `installFailure` channel, so the headline stays short ("Installed, but copilot was not found.") and the listing lands under Show diagnostics.

title: fix(desktop): show elapsed time and live output for slow harness updates
body:
Fixes #6990

## Summary
A harness update on a slow network sat on a bare **Updating…** spinner for minutes and looked hung. Now:

- **Elapsed time** on every busy install/update state, counted from `job.startedAt`: the update notice button (`Updating… 2:41`), the Harness detail button, and the Harness list row. The ticking text is `aria-hidden` so the status region doesn't announce every second.
- **After 60s**, a secondary line reads *"Still downloading. This can take a few minutes on slow networks."* (announced once via `role=status`), plus a **Show output** disclosure (shadcn `Button`, `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`). The disclosure shows what the installer has printed so far, with ANSI escapes stripped and `\r` progress redraws collapsed to the last frame, and it follows new output unless the reader scrolls up. While verifying, the hint goes away and the output stays available.
- **Daemon:** before this change, `Job.Output` was only filled in when the command finished, so a running job always reported empty output. A running job now keeps its live capture buffer (unexported `Job.live`, guarded by `s.mu`), and `Status`/`AgentJobs`/`Start`/`Cancel` snapshots include the output so far. The existing 1s install-jobs poll streams it to the UI. The `output` OpenAPI description was updated, and `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` were regenerated.
- 5 new i18n keys, translated in all 8 locales.

New shared component: `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/harness/HarnessJobProgress.tsx` (`useJobElapsed`, `JobElapsed`, `HarnessJobSlowDetail`, `formatElapsed`, `terminalText`).

**Not done (optional item 3):** capping "Update all" at 2 concurrent updates. The batch would have to wait on job completion and show a new *Queued* state on the waiting rows, so it isn't a small, safe change. I suggest a follow-up.

## Demo
I rendered the real `HarnessUpdateNotice` and `HarnessSettingsSection` against stubbed jobs modeled on the issue (Droid, Copilot and Kimchi started together). The notice cards count up (`Updating… 5:05`, `Updating… 4:57`) with the slow-network hint. The Droid detail page shows `Working… 5:05` with the hint and the expanded live output (`Downloading droid 0.245.0 … 50% (26.8 MB of 52.4 MB)`).

## Tests
- `go test -race ./internal/service/systeminstall/`: passes, including the new `TestRunningAgentJobShowsOutputSoFar` (running job exposes output through `Status` and `AgentJobs`, snapshots don't leak the writer, and the final output isn't duplicated).
- vitest: new `HarnessJobProgress.test.tsx` (6 tests); new cases in `HarnessUpdateNotice.test.tsx` and `HarnessSettingsSection.test.tsx`; i18n suites pass. Two existing progress tests now pin `Date` near their fixture's fixed `startedAt`, so they still exercise a just-started job.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.

## Risks
- Job snapshots are now taken under `s.mu` while copying up to ~4 KB of output, which is negligible.
- The elapsed time uses the client clock against the daemon's `startedAt`. For a remote host with clock skew it is clamped at 0:00.

## Follow-ups from review
- **`runStartedAt`:** an update that waited for idle sessions is now timed from when its command started, not from when the wait began.
- **Notice layout:** the version pair (`v0.244.0 → v0.245.0`) keeps its width. If the busy button's timer no longer fits beside it (a classic scrollbar, or a timer past 10:00), the button moves to its own line instead of breaking the versions. The busy button also uses `gap-1` for more room.
- **`operation`:** jobs now report `install`/`reinstall`/`update` (in memory, absent after a daemon restart), so Settings says **Updating…** instead of **Working…** for an update started from the notice.

title: fix(updates): keep release-note links when the feed sends HTML
body:
Code changes: +40 -8 Tests: +84 -5 Others: +0 -0 ## Problem The Restart to update dialog sometimes shows nightly notes as plain text: no bullets, `#6972` not linked, and `by @user` left in. For example, Nightly 0.14.4 (Oct 20) showed `Avoid inactive warning while native wake starts by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari in #6972`. The published release body is correct Markdown. electron-updater's GitHub provider reads `releases.atom`, which delivers the same body as HTML. `normalizeReleaseNotes` stripped every tag, which deleted the `` links and `
  • ` bullets. Provider notes take priority over the API's Markdown body (`normalizeReleaseNotes(info.releaseNotes) ?? directFeedReleaseNotes`), so whenever an atom-feed check reported the build, its flattened copy replaced the good notes. Because the attribution cleanup in `prepareDesktopReleaseNotes` only matches a Markdown `[#N](url)` link, the GitHub handle stayed visible as well. ## Fix `normalizeReleaseNotes` now rewrites the HTML it receives into the Markdown that `DesktopReleaseNotes` already renders: - `text` becomes `[text](url)`. User-mention anchors (`@name`) and links that aren't https keep only their text, so the existing attribution cleanup still removes `by @user`. - `
  • ` becomes `- `, and the list stays tight. `

    `–`

    ` become `### ` headings. - Mention text such as `@dependabot[bot]` is left unescaped, so the attribution cleanup still matches it. Brackets are escaped only in real link labels. - ``/`` becomes `**…**`, and `` becomes backticks. - All other tags are still stripped. The renderer's existing `urlTransform` allowlist still limits which links render. The rewrite runs only when the notes contain HTML block tags (`

    `, `

      `, `
    • `, …), so Markdown notes from the API path pass through exactly as before. `prepareDesktopReleaseNotes` also drops the `**Full Changelog**: [v1...v2](url)` footer form that GitHub's HTML (`v1...v2`) converts to, as well as the bare-URL form from the Markdown body. Nested `
    • ` items each get their own line, and anchors are matched quote-aware (single or double quotes, `>` inside other attributes). Not handled (none occur in GitHub's generated notes): `
        ` numbering becomes `-` bullets, `
        ` becomes a plain paragraph, and a backtick inside `` is not escaped. ## Tests - New `update-telemetry` tests use a trimmed copy of the real `releases.atom` HTML for this nightly. They also cover unsafe or non-https links, nested lists, quote-aware `href` parsing, and confirm Markdown input (including loose lists) is left unchanged. - A `DesktopReleaseNotes` test runs the HTML and Markdown forms of the same notes through `normalizeReleaseNotes` and then `prepareDesktopReleaseNotes`, and checks that they produce identical output (bot attribution and changelog footer included). - Updated two `auto-updater` expectations: HTML list items now come out as `- ` bullets instead of bare lines. ## Validation Run locally on Windows 11 with Node from the repo toolchain: - `npm run typecheck` (frontend): passed. - Focused suites (`update-telemetry`, `auto-updater`, `DesktopReleaseNotes`, `RestartToUpdateDialog`, `UpdatesSection`): all pass except 5 `auto-updater` macOS install-location tests. Those same 5 fail on `main` on Windows. - Full `npx vitest run`: 157 failures on both `main` and this branch, the identical set. They are macOS and Unix-only scripts and tests that don't run on Windows. This branch adds 6 passing tests and introduces no new failures. (One `useBrowserView` test failed once during a full run and passed 58/58 when run alone; that file isn't touched here.) **Not verified locally:** the Linux CI runner, `typecheck:e2e`, the e2e renderer suite, and the browser-postcondition integration. These need verification in CI.

title: feat(ci): sync open issues to a contributor Project with suggested areas and owners
body:
Code changes: +1902 -0  
Tests: +2004 -0  
Others: +1477 -0  

## What

Adds a workflow that keeps a private org GitHub Project of every open issue. Each issue gets a suggested product area and up to three suggested owners. Core contributors filter the board by area, or by their own name, to find work.

## Why

About 500 issues are open and nothing says who should look at which one. This gives every issue a starting owner, based on who actually works in that part of the code.

## How

The sync runs every 15 minutes and manually. Issue events are reconciled on the next scheduled run.

1. It adds open issues that are missing from the Project and archives closed ones. If an issue the bot archived gets reopened, it comes back.
2. It picks an area. First match wins:
   - a hand-reviewed route in `data/issue-areas.json` (about 490 issues)
   - a single `area:<id>` label on the issue
   - a text match against the hand-reviewed issues, used only when confident (82% correct in leave-one-out testing, covers 11% of issues)
   - otherwise `Needs area review`
3. It writes the area's top 3 core contributors into `Suggested owner`.

Owners rebuild once a day in a separate job with its own concurrency group, and the result is cached by source/data hash and UTC date. Per area, each person scores:

| Signal | Weight |
|---|---|
| Merged PRs touching the area, last 90 days | 60% |
| Lines changed there, older work counting less | 25% |
| Reviews on those PRs | 10% |
| Current lines they wrote, from a blame snapshot (`data/blame-lines.json`) | 5% |

Core means 10+ merged PRs in 90 days. `data/core-overrides.json` adds or drops people.

Human edits win. A `Sync record` field stores what the bot last wrote, and the bot only changes a field that is blank or still holds its own value.

It never assigns, adds labels, comments, or touches items from other repos. The App token is limited to this repo, org Projects write and Issues read.

Review focus: `apply_plan` in `sync_project.py` (the write path) and the cache steps in the workflow.

Left out on purpose:
- No `area:*` labels exist yet. A labelling rule for the repo bot is drafted but not enabled, so most new issues land in `Needs area review` until it is.
- Blame is a snapshot from 2026-10-21, refreshed by hand (`scripts/blame_snapshot.py`, see README). Live blame took over 15 minutes per run.
- Removed 10 path rules for agent-switch code that is gone from `main`.

## Scaling and recovery

- Each run allows at most 100 mutation attempts, paced at least one second apart, and reserves enough budget to finish an item before starting another. Scheduled runs allow at most 400 attempts per hour. Retries count against the budget.
- Pending field targets are recorded before writes. A later run finalizes confirmed values and resumes unfinished updates while preserving human edits. Deferred syncs emit `complete: false`, a reason and remaining-item count, and exit 3. The workflow shows the JSON summary and a warning. A deferred run that wrote nothing exits 4 and fails the job, so a stalled backlog is visible; other errors also fail the job. A rate-limit wait that would run past 30 minutes defers instead of sleeping into the 45-minute job timeout.
- Normal scans read active items and archived open items, leaving closed archive history out of the scan. A separate total count warns at 40,000 items. At GitHub's 50,000-item limit, new issues are skipped, existing items still update, and the job fails with an error until the board is rotated. Rotation to a new private Project is an explicit administrator step; old history is retained and never automatically deleted.
- Owner extraction reuses historical PR evidence, refreshes a seven-day overlap, and expires evidence older than 540 days. Full refreshes run every 30 days or on request. Interrupted attempts retain a pinned capture time and completed API pages; inconsistent pagination is discarded and fetched again. The last complete evidence file and successful owners survive failed attempts.
- Owner refreshes and sync use independent jobs and concurrency groups. Owner caches hash the owner scripts and data files, excluding `sync_project.py`, so sync-only edits keep today's owners and generated bytecode cannot change the key between restore and save. PR evidence is saved only when a failed extraction made progress, owners built, or nothing was cached yet, so a failing build does not save a new cache every 15 minutes.

## Setup after merge (admin)

Nothing runs until step 1 is done.

1. Create a private org Project and set the repo variable `AO_CONTRIBUTOR_PROJECT_URL`.
2. Create a GitHub App with org Projects write and repo Issues read, installed on this repo. Set `AO_CONTRIBUTOR_APP_CLIENT_ID` and the secret `AO_CONTRIBUTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
3. Run the workflow by hand and check its progress summary. The initial backfill continues over scheduled runs; owner suggestions arrive after the separate owner build succeeds.

If the owner build fails or the owners are more than 7 days old, the run shows a warning annotation.

## Testing

- All 137 Python tests pass, including fault injection before/after each field-write phase, preservation of human edits, cached-page resume, pagination invalidation, and stable cache keys.
- A stateful 512-issue backfill completes over 26 runs, each limited to 100 writes. Every completed item has its suggestions and finalized record.
- All 19 live GitHub scenarios pass on the [private QA Project](https://github.com/orgs/OrchestratorInc/projects/13) with [disposable issues](https://github.com/ronishrohan/ao-pr-6995-manual-qa-20261025/issues/5). This includes a real 10-write stop/resume and recovery from staged partial updates. The Project is closed and the fixture repository archived after testing.
- Cold extraction took 370.62 seconds; the first incremental refresh took 29.89 seconds. Both owner builds succeeded.
- On `8d1e69ba7f`, all 137 Python tests, area-map validation and workflow lint pass. Six further live checks pass: dry-run, the 10-write limit, resume, existing-item updates while a lowered test capacity blocks additions, a later addition after that threshold clears, and a zero-write rerun. The real API was used for reads and writes; the capacity threshold alone was lowered in process. The private QA Project is closed and the fixture repository archived again.
- All GitHub checks pass on this head: [frontend tests, Linux browser integration, renderer smoke and Mac helpers](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40134756246), [contributor tests](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40134756256), and [Gitleaks](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40134756262). The privileged owner/sync jobs correctly skip PR runs.
- Native validation also passed the full frontend suite on retry, package checks, docs build and helper builds. The local workflow emulator failed on worktree/Git transport and its Playwright image loader. The native macOS browser integration has the same drag-region failure on this head and unchanged `fc43317`; the corresponding Linux integration passed in GitHub CI.

The narrowed App installation token and hosted Actions cache restore/save path have not been exercised live. The live sync checks used the authorized CLI OAuth token. Production Project settings and existing issues were untouched.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for the new behavior
- [x] CI passes

title: bug(desktop): "Commit & push to #N" names the first open PR, not the PR for the checked-out branch, when a session has several PRs
body:
## Bug
In the Pull requests panel, the primary git action reads "Commit & push to #N", where N is the **first open or draft PR in the session's list**, not the PR whose head branch is checked out. When a session owns several PRs (for example a stacked pair), the label can name a different PR from the one the commit will update.

**Source:** ao-landing worker ao-landing-4, relaying a user report from the desktop app (2026-10-20) | **Analyzed against:** `30723c0be` (main)
**Confidence:** High (code traced)
**Priority:** medium (misleading label on a commit/push action; the user can check the branch with git)

## Observed
Session `ao-landing-4` (repo OrchestratorInc/ao-landing) owns:
- PR #52 `ao/ao-landing-4/stripe-policies → main` (checked out)
- PR #66 (draft) `ao/ao-landing-4/legal-terms-privacy → ao/ao-landing-4/stripe-policies`, stacked on #52

The panel shows "Commit & push to #52". It happens to be right here because the stripe-policies branch is checked out, but only because #52 is listed first. If `legal-terms-privacy` were checked out, the label would still say #52 while the push updates #66.

## Root cause
`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx:422`:
```ts
const openPRNumber = prSummaries.find((pr) => pr.state === "open" || pr.state === "draft")?.number;
```
This is passed to `SessionBranchSummary.tsx` (`gitActionPlan`/`primaryLabel`, l.318–365), which builds the "Commit & push to #N" label and message from it. Nothing compares it with the worktree's current branch.

## Fix
- Pick the PR whose `headRef` equals the worktree's current branch. If none matches, fall back to a neutral "Commit & push to <branch>" instead of naming a PR.
- With several PRs, make the target explicit in the button or the dropdown.
- Test: a session with two open PRs where the checked-out branch is the second PR's head must label the second PR.

## Related
- [#6636](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6636): panel header shows the session root branch instead of the attached PR head (same panel, same session)
- [#6637](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6637): `.ao/launch.json` counted as an uncommitted file that drives "Commit & push" (same panel)
- [#6555](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6555): inspector git actions ignore merged PRs (same component)

title: fix(kanban): show Interrupted on a card after the agent is stopped
body:
## Problem

When you stop a chat agent, its card on the board keeps saying "Awaiting PR". Stopping the agent only makes the session idle, and the board treats an idle session with no PR as finished work waiting for a PR. The chat already knows the turn was interrupted, but the board never read that.

## Fix

The board now reads how the session's latest chat turn ended. If it was interrupted and the agent is idle, the card says **Interrupted** and stays in its current column, usually Building. A session with only artifact output stays in Validating.

- Sending a new message clears it, and the card goes back to "Working".
- A queued message you withdrew does not clear it.
- If the agent exited, the card says "Exited" as before.
- Cards with a PR still show their PR status (CI, review), because that tells you more.

The interrupted check is one database query per board load, covering every session at once. A single-session read runs the same query for that one session. The query uses the existing indexes on conversations and turns.

## Changes

- `backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go`: new `Interrupted` session fact and new `Interrupted` display status, used in the Building and artifact states.
- `queries/conversations.sql` + `conversation_store.go`: `ListInterruptedSessions` picks each session's conversation the same way `SelectConversationBySession` does. It ignores cancelled, rolled-back and promoted turns.
- `service/session`: the session list and single-session reads pass the fact to the board.
- API spec and `schema.ts` regenerated. The frontend label is added in all 8 languages. Mobile shows the daemon's `displayStatus` text as-is, so it needs no change.

## Not covered

Terminal (TUI) sessions. When you press Esc in one, the agent's hooks may not report anything, so the card could keep saying "Working". That is a separate problem in how terminal sessions report activity.

## Testing

- `go test ./pkg/contract/ ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/httpd/...` pass.
- New tests: how the status is chosen (idle, active, exited, artifact output); the store query (interrupt, withdrawn queued prompt, new turn); the service list and single-session reads.
- Frontend: the translation files and `SessionsBoard` tests pass.
- To test by hand: start a chat session with no PR, stop it mid-turn, and check the card says Interrupted. Send a message and check it goes back to Working.

title: [Bug]: managed npm update always fails for packages whose CLI comes from an optional dependency (@github/copilot)
body:
## Bug

Managed side-by-side updates (`backend/internal/service/systeminstall/managed.go`) verify a freshly installed release by stat-ing `<release>/bin/<cli>`, where `cli` is the basename of the executable AO resolved before the update (`managedCLIName`). For the `npm` method the install is `npm install -g --prefix <release> pkg@ver`, and npm links only the **root package's own `bin` entries** into `<release>/bin`. Bins contributed by (optional) dependencies are linked only into the package's nested `node_modules/.bin/`.

`@github/copilot` declares `bin: { "copilot": "npm-loader.js" }`; the native `copilot-darwin-arm64` is the bin of the optional dependency `@github/copilot-darwin-arm64`. When AO's baseline resolves to the native binary (a user's own `npm -g` install exposes it as `.../node_modules/.bin/copilot-darwin-arm64`), `cli` becomes `copilot-darwin-arm64`, and the post-install verification (`managedBinRel` → `bin/copilot-darwin-arm64`) always fails:

```
Method: npm
Error: the install finished but <root>/harnesses/copilot/versions/v1/bin/copilot-darwin-arm64 is missing
Output:
Installing @github/copilot into <root>/harnesses/copilot/versions/v1
added 3 packages in 23s
```

The failed release directory is then removed by the failure cleanup, so **every managed update attempt for this harness fails the same way** and the harness stays behind latest indefinitely. Health keeps reporting the user's own global install (which AO correctly leaves alone), so the UI shows `behind_latest` with no way to converge.

## Expected

The managed installer should locate the executable inside the release directory the way the package manager actually lays it out. Suggested search order for npm:

1. `<release>/bin/<cli>` — current behavior, correct for root-bin CLIs;
2. `<release>/lib/node_modules/**/node_modules/.bin/<cli>` — bins contributed by dependencies (bounded glob; `@scope` packages nest one level deeper).

The found relative path should be recorded in `managed.json` (the `BinRel` field already exists) and reused for the version probe and the release launcher. The current all-or-nothing `bin/<cli>` stat then only stays the fast path, not the sole path.

## Notes

- Affects any npm package whose session executable is a dependency bin rather than the root bin: `@github/copilot` today; the same shape applies to `bun`, where `BUN_INSTALL_BIN` similarly only receives root bins.
- Not a regression from a recent change; the managed installer never handled this layout.

## Environment

- AO 0.14.x nightly line, macOS (Apple Silicon), harness update method `npm`, package `@github/copilot` 1.0.100 → 1.0.101 (Homebrew Node/npm for the user-owned install).
- Reproduces on every managed update attempt of this harness; observed 2026-10-21.

title: fix(models): keep project model lists in step with Settings
body:
## What users saw

A user switched on 42 OpenCode 2 models in Settings ("42 of 733 shown in model pickers"). New Task offered only one.

## Why

Settings and the pickers read different model lists. Settings reads the device-wide list. New Task and chat read a separate list for each project. The Settings switches only save which model IDs are off, and pickers apply that to the project list. If the project list is missing the models you switched on, you see whatever is left, which is often just the one model Disable all keeps.

Two things leave project lists behind.

1. Project lists refresh once a day or when the discovery fingerprint changes. For OpenCode 2, a provider connected inside OpenCode lives in its own database, which the fingerprint ignores. So the device-wide list can gain a provider's models (for example when Settings refreshes it) while project lists keep the old ones until tomorrow.
2. OpenCode 2.0.14 exits 0 with no output the first time `models` runs in a new folder. The second run lists everything (3 of 3 fresh folders: first=0, second=208). OpenCode 1.18.35 doesn't do this. So every new project started with an empty, failed OpenCode 2 list waiting out a retry.

## Fix

- When a successful discovery saves device-wide models that differ from the cached ones, the daemon rediscovers any project list for that harness whose models differ. This covers every refresh path: Settings, picker refresh buttons, and the background daily check.
- Each drifted project row is requeued the way login invalidation already does, so retry backoff doesn't block it. That reset now lives in one helper, `requeueCatalog`, shared by all three callers.
- Rows for cloud credential scopes, missing projects and archived projects are skipped.
- When OpenCode 2's `models` exits cleanly with empty output, discovery runs it once more, with its own timeout.

The first version of this PR ran the pass on every forced Settings refresh. Review showed that reran discovery for every project whose list legitimately differs (its own config or env) each time Settings opened a harness. It also showed retry backoff silently blocked the rediscovery. Both are fixed in the last commit.

## Testing

The failing tests land in their own commits before the fix.

- `TestGlobalRefreshRediscoversProjectScopesThatDiffer`: a project list built before a provider connected picks up the new models.
- `TestGlobalModelChangeRediscoversProjectInRetryBackoff`: a project left failed by the empty first run is rediscovered without waiting out its retry. It fails if the requeue is removed.
- `TestUnchangedGlobalRefreshLeavesDifferingProjectAlone`: three forced refreshes with no model change run only the 3 global discoveries.
- `TestOpenCodeV2RetriesEmptyFirstRunInNewFolder`: a fake `opencode2` that prints nothing on first sight of a folder still yields its models.
- `go test -race`, `go vet` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 pass on both changed packages.
- `go test ./...`: 203 packages pass. 4 fail the same way on `main` (`adapters/agent/opencode`, `adapters/agent/opencodev2`, `adapters/chatdriver/opencodev2acp`, `adapters/reviewer/opencodev2`). They resolve the installed OpenCode binaries by major version, and none of them touch code in this PR.

In the isolated dev app with the real `opencode2` binary. Both lists were seeded without the 20 `anthropic/*` models, as they would be before a provider connects, and 5 of those were switched on plus the model Disable all keeps (6 of 183).

- Before opening Settings: New Task offered one model, `baai/bge-m3`.
- Opening Settings → Harness → OpenCode 2 → Models refreshed the device-wide list (163 to 183 models). Both project lists were rebuilt within 0.2s.
- New Task then offered all 6.
- Reopening Settings with no model change refreshed only the device-wide list. The project lists were not touched.
- A new project's first OpenCode 2 read returned 208 models. Before the fix it returned 0 with "opencode-v2 model discovery returned no models".

## Notes for reviewers

- OpenCode's GitHub Copilot model list varies between runs (13 vs 25 models here), so lists built at different times can differ. This PR brings project lists back in line when the device-wide list changes. Models that exist only in a project list are still offered, because Settings never saw them to switch off. That's existing behavior.
- Without `--standalone`, `opencode2 models` talks to the user's OpenCode 2 background service, which ignores the `XDG_DATA_HOME` AO sets. So that isolation doesn't hold while the service is running. This PR leaves that alone.
