title: feat(desktop): ship cloudflared in the macOS app
body:
## What

The packaged macOS app now includes `cloudflared`, so turning on remote access (Connect Mobile, or **Settings → Remote hosts → Allow access from your devices**) never stops at **Install cloudflared**.

## Why

On macOS that install runs `brew install cloudflared`. On a Mac without Homebrew it fails, and remote access cannot start at all. The app already ships its other helper programs (tmux, the wake and update helpers, the ACP runtime's Node), so cloudflared follows the same path.

## How

- `scripts/prepare-cloudflared.mjs` fetches cloudflared **2026.10.2** for the build Mac's architecture. It checks the archive's SHA-256 before `tar` reads it and the extracted binary's SHA-256 after; the binary checksum is the one Cloudflare lists in the release notes. It also saves Cloudflare's Apache-2.0 license. A rerun with a matching binary skips the download. On Windows and Linux the script does nothing.
- `prepackage`, `premake` and `publish` run it, next to `browser-runtime:prepare`.
- `extraResourcesForPlatform("darwin")` adds `cloudflared`. `postPackage` fails the build if `Resources/cloudflared/cloudflared` is missing or `--version` does not exit 0, so a release can't silently fall back to asking for an install.
- The packaged macOS desktop passes `AO_CLOUDFLARED_PATH=<Resources>/cloudflared/cloudflared` to the daemon. The daemon already treats that variable as an override (`ResolveCloudflared`), so the backend is unchanged. A user-set `AO_CLOUDFLARED_PATH` still wins.
- Docs: **Install cloudflared** is now described as Windows and Linux only.

Cost: about 38 MB per architecture (arm64 binary 39.4 MB, x64 42.4 MB). The arm64 app went from 565 MB to 602 MB.

Out of scope: Windows and Linux keep the winget/apt install. Bundling there, plus copying the binary into AO's data dir (which the Linux AppImage needs), is tracked in #7003. A headless `ao daemon` started outside the desktop does not get the variable and resolves cloudflared as before.

## Testing

- `forge.config.test.ts`: 24 pass, including two new tests (cloudflared ships only on macOS; packaging fails when the packaged copy is missing). Both failed before the change.
- `prepare-cloudflared.mjs`: ran clean, then a rerun skipped the download (0.3 s). A copy with one wrong archive checksum fails with `cloudflared archive checksum mismatch` and leaves nothing behind.
- Real package, macOS arm64, unsigned (`npm run package` prepare steps, then `electron-forge package` on Node 24 as CI uses): `postPackage` passed, and `Resources/cloudflared/cloudflared --version` prints `2026.10.2`.
- The packaged `Resources/daemon/ao daemon`, on separate test data with the variable the desktop now sets, logged `mobile remote access available ... Resources/cloudflared/cloudflared source=env`, and `/api/v1/mobile/status` reported `tunnel.supported: true`.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.
- Not tested: launching the packaged app itself (it shares `~/.ao/electron` with the installed app), and a signed or notarized build. `osx-sign` signs every nested Mach-O file, and `verify-mac-artifact.sh`'s `codesign --deep --strict` covers the new binary.

Local note: under Node 26, `electron-forge package` exits 0 partway through unzipping Electron and leaves no `out/`. CI packages on Node 24.

title: Bundle cloudflared on Windows and Linux, matching macOS
body:
## Problem

#7002 ships `cloudflared` inside the macOS app, so turning on remote access (Connect Mobile, or **Settings → Remote hosts → Allow access from your devices**) starts without an install. Windows and Linux still stop at **Install cloudflared**, which runs `winget install Cloudflare.cloudflared` or the distro package manager (`backend/internal/service/systeminstall/systeminstall.go`, `planCloudflared`). If that install fails or the user skips it, remote access cannot start. Every platform AO releases should behave the same way.

## What to do

1. **Bundle cloudflared for the other release targets.** AO releases `darwin-arm64`, `darwin-x64`, `win32-x64` and `linux-x64` (`.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml`). Add pinned targets to `frontend/scripts/prepare-cloudflared.mjs` for the same version #7002 pins (2026.10.2), or a newer one:

   | Target | Asset | Asset SHA-256 | Size |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `win32-x64` | `cloudflared-windows-amd64.exe` | `12c7c887f8aaab779aef1dfa9b60673530a5adb88ecc55dd6df8f56e0b70f199` | 55 MB |
   | `linux-x64` | `cloudflared-linux-amd64` | `35fbdd2beb378436c7da377d7358cea8e33f9c94a6705d1d8036bf9b0d6d8005` | 40 MB |

   Both are plain binaries, not archives. Check them against the checksums in Cloudflare's release notes too. Add `cloudflared` to `extraResourcesForPlatform` for `win32` and `linux`, and extend the `postPackage` check that runs `cloudflared --version`.

2. **Copy the bundled binary into AO's data dir, per app version, like tmux.** On Linux the AppImage's resources live on a temporary FUSE mount that disappears when Electron exits, but the daemon can keep running (see `frontend/src/shared/bundled-tmux.ts`, `stableBundledTmuxBinaryPath`). A daemon pointed into the bundle then has no cloudflared the next time the tunnel restarts. The same copy protects a long-running daemon on macOS while an update replaces the app, and on Windows when an update changes the install folder. Point `AO_CLOUDFLARED_PATH` at the copied file on every platform, replacing the macOS-only bundle path that #7002 sets in `frontend/src/main.ts`.

3. **Docs:** drop the "On Windows and Linux" wording around **Install cloudflared** in `frontend/src/docs/content/configuration/remote-access.mdx`.

Out of scope: Windows on ARM and Linux on ARM have no AO builds. Headless `ao daemon` started outside the desktop keeps resolving cloudflared from `PATH`.

## How to verify

- Run **Desktop build artifacts** (`workflow_dispatch`, `ref` = the branch) so all four platforms package. Each `postPackage` run of the bundled `cloudflared --version` must pass. This also covers the Intel Mac build, which #7002 did not package.
- On each OS, the packaged app's daemon logs `mobile remote access available ... source=env` with the copied path under AO's data dir, and `GET /api/v1/mobile/status` reports `tunnel.supported: true`. No **Install cloudflared** prompt appears.
- Linux AppImage: quit the app with the daemon kept alive, then turn remote access off and on through `ao remote-host`. The tunnel must restart.
- After merge, the first signed nightly: turn on remote access on each OS and reach it from another device.

title: fix(models): name the provider on every compact model row
body:
Code changes: +21 -2\
Tests: +206 -3\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The New Task and chat model menus use the compact picker, which rendered the
model label alone. A label carries no provider: the daemon strips the provider
prefix when it splits a provider/model ID, so OpenCode's
`openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5` reads as `anthropic/claude-opus-5`.

- A compact row now names its provider when the catalog has more than one.
- The compact menu now shows the "Showing X of Y matching models — type to
  narrow" line, which it suppressed while the grouped menu showed it.

## Why

A user with OpenCode 2 saw `openrouter/` models in Settings → Harness → Models
but not in the Task dialog's model dropdown.

Two things hid them:

1. Settings groups the catalog by provider and names the provider (and the
   grouped picker prints the machine ID under the label), so the provider is
   visible there. The compact picker used by New Task and chat printed neither.
   OpenCode 2 lists every OpenRouter model twice, once under `openrouter/` and
   once under `console-openrouter/`, so the compact menu showed each name twice
   with nothing to tell the rows apart.

2. The compact menu caps the list at 50 entries and hid the line that says so.
   On the reported machine `opencode models` reports 734 models (352
   `openrouter/`, 340 `console-openrouter/`, 42 `opencode/`), so 684 of them —
   including 327 of the 352 `openrouter/` ones — were not in the list, and
   nothing told the user the list was truncated.

The catalogs themselves were fine: the device-wide and per-project caches held
the same 734 models in the same order.

## How

- `AgentModelCombobox` derives the provider set from the search index, the same
  place the rows read their provider from, and names it on a compact row when
  more than one provider is present. A single-provider catalog is unchanged.
- The count line loses its `!compact` gate. It only renders when the menu
  already shows a search box, so a small catalog still reads as a plain list.

`frontend/e2e/task-model-picker-catalog.spec.ts` covers the picker against a
catalog shaped like OpenCode 2's (120 models, two providers listing the same
names): each row names its provider, the picker says how many models it left
out, a model past the row cap is found by search and picked, and Settings and
the picker count the same catalog.

This is the picker half of the report. The other half — Settings reads the
device-wide catalog while the pickers read a per-project one, and OpenCode 2's
in-app provider connections do not change the discovery fingerprint — is fixed
in #7001, which has since landed on `main`.

## Testing

- `cd frontend && npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/settings/AgentModelCombobox.test.tsx` — 38 passed.
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck:e2e` — clean.
- `cd frontend && npm test` — 8855 passed, 7 skipped, 1 failed:
  `src/main/remote-proxy.test.ts > startRemoteProxy over HTTP/2 > verifies the
  host once per upstream session, before the credential`. That test fails the
  same way on a pristine `main` checkout and does not touch this change.

New unit tests cover the provider on a compact row, its absence for a
single-provider catalog, and the truncation line. The three Playwright specs
fail against the picker as it was and pass with it.

`npm run test:e2e:renderer` (the suite CI runs): 109 passed, 1 failed —
`e2e/chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts` "typed chat composer text is
visibly selected with a pointer drag". That spec fails the same way on a
pristine `main` checkout (two of its tests fail there) and touches neither
the picker nor the chat composer.

Rendered against the live OpenCode 2 catalog from the reported machine (734
models):

```
catalog size: 734 | rows rendered: 50
ROW: "aion-labs/aion-2.0console-openrouter"
ROW: "aion-labs/aion-2.0openrouter"
FOOTER: "Showing 50 of 734 matching models — type to narrow"
```

Before the change the two rows read identically and there was no footer.

## Rebased onto `main`

This branch was rebased onto `main` after #7001 landed and after the Cursor
model-variant work changed `AgentModelCombobox`. The conflict was in the
compact row, where `main` had renamed `effectiveModel` to `shownModel`; the
resolution keeps `main`'s rename and adds the provider span. The change is the
same shape as before the rebase: a compact row names its provider, and the
count line shows in compact mode.

## CI note

This branch is pushed from a fork (`siliconsenthil`), because the account used
for this work has `push: false` on `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`. GitHub
holds the `Frontend` and `gitleaks` runs in `action_required` until a
maintainer approves them for the fork. The commands those jobs run
(`npm run typecheck` and the vitest suite) were run locally and pass, apart
from the one pre-existing failure noted above. The Go jobs are untouched by
this frontend-only change.

title: fix(harness): install the copilot launcher, not its platform binary
body:
## Problem

Updating an npm-installed GitHub Copilot beside running sessions fails after npm finishes:

> the install finished but ~/.ao/data/harnesses/copilot/versions/v1/bin/copilot-darwin-arm64 is missing

The Copilot resolver follows the npm loader (`npm-loader.js`) to the platform binary at `node_modules/.bin/copilot-darwin-arm64`. The managed update took the executable name from that path, so it looked for `bin/copilot-darwin-arm64`. npm installs `bin/copilot`, and the resolver looks up the managed launcher as `copilot`.

Homebrew installs are not affected, because the cask's binary is already named `copilot`.

## Fix

- `managedCLINames` fixes the executable name for targets whose resolved binary is named differently: OpenCode v2 uses `opencode`, and Copilot uses `copilot`.
- `ResolveCopilotBinary` follows the managed launcher (the npm loader) to the native binary, through `copilot/current`. Managed sessions don't need `node` on PATH, and the path still follows updates.
- On Windows, release cleanup also counts an opaque `<cli>-*.exe` process, such as `copilot-win32-x64.exe`.

## Tests

- `TestManagedCopilotInstallsTheLauncherNotThePlatformBinary` builds the real npm symlink layout. It checks that `managed.json` records `copilot` and that the launcher runs.
- `TestResolveCopilotBinaryRunsTheManagedNativeBinary` checks that the resolver returns the native binary through `current`.

title: fix(harness): keep harness update failures short in the notice
body:
Harness update failures put install paths and command output in the update notice. The notice now shows a short message, and the full detail goes to **Show diagnostics**.

**Side-by-side (managed) updates**

| When | Notice |
| --- | --- |
| Folder can't be created | Could not create the install folder. |
| Install command fails | The install command failed. |
| Executable missing after install | Installed, but `<cli>` was not found. |
| `--version` fails to run / prints no version | The new `<cli>` did not start. / The new `<cli>` did not report its version. |
| Below the pinned version | The new `<cli>` reports X, not Y. |
| Switch or release record fails | Installed, but could not switch to it. |
| Record and restore both fail | Switched to the new version, but could not record it. |
| Launcher or `managed.json` fails after the switch | Switched to the new version, but could not finish setting it up. |

**Every update, after verification**

Each message starts with "The update finished, but …", shows only versions, and quotes at most 80 characters of the updater's last line. For example: `The update finished, but it reports 0.159.1, not the requested version 0.242.0. The updater said: "Droid is already up to date."` The binary path and the different-installation hint go to diagnostics.

`installFailure` holds the short summary and the detail. `failureSummary` writes the detail to the job output. Errors that were already short (`exit status 1`) are unchanged. The notice clamps any error to three lines.

title: fix(agents): follow the default account in readiness and list the CLI login with the others
body:
## Summary

With a saved account as the default for new tasks, the harness **Account** card described the CLI's own login, and its **Log in again** / **Log out** acted on that login. Claude readiness also ignored the saved default (Codex already followed it), so the agent picker could block Claude while tasks would start fine, or show it ready while they would fail.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Claude readiness with a saved default | The CLI's own login | The saved default, named by email and plan (as Codex) |
| Harness → Account with accounts listed | A card for the CLI login, plus the list | Only the list; the CLI login row has **Sign in again** and **Log out** |
| Saved default, developer mode off | The card only | The list |
| CLI login sign-in/out check, saved default | Readiness, which now describes the default | The CLI login's row in the accounts list |
| "Log in" shortcut (update notice), saved default | Starts the CLI login | Opens the Account tab |
| "CLI login" tag on that row | Shown | Removed |

## How

- `agentaccounts.DefaultSignIn` returns the default account's identity. The agent service's saved-default check covers Claude Code and Codex, sets `account`, and adds a `saved_default_account` diagnostic, which the renderer uses to tell that readiness is not about the CLI login. No API change.
- For a saved Claude default, "authorized" comes from `claude auth status` in the account's folder, the evidence Codex's saved default already uses. AO's own credential reader reads the CLI's default Keychain entry, not the per-folder one.

## Tests

- `go test` for `service/agent`, `service/agentaccounts`, `domain`; `go build ./cmd/...`; `tsc --noEmit`; vitest for the accounts panel (new CLI login row cases), harness settings and i18n.
- Isolated desktop lab with a real saved Claude default: readiness named that account; the Account tab showed only the list, with developer mode off; Codex kept its card until developer mode was on.

Not run end to end: finishing a sign-in or sign-out from the CLI login row, which would have changed the machine's real CLI login.

title: feat(docs): crawlable URLs for translated articles
body:
Code changes: +833 -153  
Tests: +62 -0  
Others: +1073 -4 (translated articles, message catalogs, config)

Closes #6969. Builds on #6967, which is now merged into `main`.

## What changes

Translated articles now have their own URLs that crawlers can read. Untranslated pages are unchanged.

- **Storage:** a translation sits beside its English article as `page.<locale>.mdx`. The loader has no fallback, so a page counts as translated in a language only when that file exists.
- **URLs:** each translated article is prerendered at `/<locale>/<path>/`, e.g. `/ja/quickstart/`. The static HTML has the article, sidebar and interface in that language.
- **SEO tags, translated articles only (English and translated URLs):** `<html lang>`, a self canonical, hreflang alternates for every language plus `x-default` (English), and one sitemap entry per language with the same alternates.
- **Untranslated pages:** one English URL, self canonical, no hreflang, one sitemap entry. The interface still switches in place from the `ao_locale` cookie.
- **Cookie and switcher:**
  - On a translated URL, the URL decides the language. Visiting it does not change the saved choice.
  - The switcher saves the cookie. It then goes to that language's URL if one exists, or otherwise to the English URL with the chosen interface language.
  - On an English page, a saved language that has a translation of the page sends the reader there. A head script handles page loads; an effect handles links inside the site.
  - Crawlers send no cookie, so they always get the URL they asked for.
- **Search:** stays English-only.

## How it is built

- **Route groups:** English pages and each translated language have their own root layout, in `app/(en)` and `app/(<locale>)/<locale>`. That is what lets `<html lang>` be correct in the static HTML.
- **Why not one route with a dynamic language segment:** a dynamic `[lang]` segment beside the English catch-all would capture English URLs in `next dev`, and a root layout inside the catch-all would remount on every navigation.
- **Per-language files:** each language with translations needs two small files, a layout and a page.
- **404 page:** there is no top-level layout any more, so the 404 page renders its own `<html>` through `global-not-found`. This needs `experimental.globalNotFound`.
- **New check:** `npm run check:i18n` now also runs `check:translations`. It **fails** when a translation has no English article, no `translatedFrom` hash, or no route folder, or when a route folder has no translations. It **warns** when the English article changed since the translation, by comparing the `translatedFrom` hash.

## Translations

Introduction, Installation and Quickstart are translated into Japanese (`ja`) and Simplified Chinese (`zh-CN`).
- Commands, flags, config keys, code blocks, anchors, product names and in-app UI labels stay in English.
- These are machine translations that a native speaker has not reviewed yet.
- The download table component (`<InstallDownloads />`) is still English on the translated Installation pages.

## Review fixes

- **Sections survive a language move.** The saved-language redirect, links inside the site and the language menu all keep the query and the section, e.g. `/installation/?from=review#where-ao-stores-data` with Japanese saved opens `/ja/installation/?from=review#where-ao-stores-data` at that section. Each such move changes the root layout, so it is a full page load and the browser scrolls to the section.
- **English section ids on translated pages.** Every translated heading also carries its English id, so existing links such as `/installation/#common-installation-problems` reach the section on `/ja/installation/` and `/zh-CN/installation/`. `check:translations` now fails when a translation is missing an id the English article has.
- **Paths with spaces.** `check:translations` resolves its own location with `fileURLToPath`, so it works from paths with spaces and on Windows.
- **Rebased** onto the latest #6967, keeping its newer fixes. #7014 and #7015 are carried over on top.
- **Markdown export from paths with spaces.** The post-build `move-markdown.mjs` step converts its output URL with `fileURLToPath`. `scripts/move-markdown.test.ts` runs it from a checkout named `AO review` and from one without a space.
- **Saved-language redirect test.** `saved-locale-script.test.tsx` covers keeping the query and section on the redirect.

## Verification

- **Checks:** `npm run check:i18n` and `npm run build` pass. `/ja` and `/zh-CN` each prerender 3 pages.
- **Translated pages:** `out/ja/quickstart/index.html` has `<html lang="ja">`, a canonical `https://docs.orchestrator.inc/ja/quickstart/`, alternates for `en`, `ja` and `zh-CN`, and `x-default` pointing to `/quickstart/`. The title is `クイックスタート | Agent Orchestrator ドキュメント`.
- **Unchanged pages:** I compared every HTML page with a build of `ao/localisation-in-docs`. The 47 untranslated pages and `404.html` match in head tags, visible text and links. The only change to the 3 English pages that have translations is the added hreflang links. The search index has the same 1,582 English entries.
- **Browser, against the static export:**
  - `/ja/quickstart/` with no cookie renders Japanese.
  - Switching to 简体中文 goes to `/zh-CN/quickstart/`.
  - Switching to Français goes to `/quickstart/` with a French interface and the "not translated yet" notice.
  - With `ja` saved, `/installation/` goes to `/ja/installation/`, and the sidebar link from `/cli/` to Quickstart lands on `/ja/quickstart/`.
  - Switching to English goes back to `/quickstart/`.
  - Navigation between English pages stays client-side.
  - `/ja/cli/` returns the 404 page.
  - After the review fixes: the redirect, the menu (ja → zh-CN → fr) and a link from `/troubleshooting/` all keep `?from=review` and the section, and land on it. `check:translations` fails when the `common-installation-problems` alias is removed, and runs from a folder with a space in its path.
  - After the rebase: every page's head tags match the previous PR head, except the 404 title, which now uses #6967's "Page not found".

title: docs: make the docs readable by AI tools (llms.txt, Markdown pages, page actions)
body:
## Problem

AI assistants and coding agents read docs as plain text. docs.orchestrator.inc only serves rendered HTML, so tools have to scrape the pages, and there is no index that tells an agent what pages exist.

## Proposal

Generate these at build time, so they work with the static export on GitHub Pages:

- `/llms.txt`: a short summary of Agent Orchestrator, then every docs page grouped by section as `- [Title](https://docs.orchestrator.inc/<path>.md): description`, and a pointer to `llms-full.txt`.
- `/llms-full.txt`: every page's processed Markdown in one file, each page headed by its title, URL and description.
- A Markdown copy of every page at `/<path>.md` (for example `/quickstart.md`), generated from the MDX source.
- Page actions on each docs page: **Copy Markdown** (copies the page's Markdown) and an **Open in** menu that opens ChatGPT or Claude with a prompt pointing at the page's `.md` URL, plus **View on GitHub** linking to the source file.

English only; translated pages can be added later.

## Done when

- `npm run build` in `frontend/src/docs` writes `out/llms.txt`, `out/llms-full.txt` and one `.md` per docs page.
- Every link in `llms.txt` resolves to a file in `out/`.
- The page actions render on every docs page and work in the built site.

title: docs: add Open Graph tags, preview images and structured data
body:
## Problem

Docs pages have a title and a description, and nothing else for search engines or link previews: no Open Graph or Twitter tags, no preview image, and no structured data. A docs link shared in Slack, X or LinkedIn shows a bare text preview, and search results have no breadcrumbs.

## Proposal

- **Open Graph and Twitter tags on every page:** `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:site_name`, `og:type`, `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, set per page from frontmatter.
- **A generated preview image for every page** (title and description on a branded background, 1200x630), built at build time with `next/og` so it works with the static export, at a stable URL such as `/og/<path>/image.png`.
- **Structured data (JSON-LD)** on each docs page: `TechArticle` (headline, description, url, publisher) and `BreadcrumbList` following the sidebar sections; `Organization` and `WebSite` on the docs home.
- **Search snippet settings:** `robots` with `max-image-preview:large` and `max-snippet:-1`.
- A canonical URL on every page if the base branch does not have one yet.

## Done when

- `npm run build` in `frontend/src/docs` passes and every docs page in `out/` has the tags above.
- Every page's preview image exists in `out/` and is 1200x630.
- The JSON-LD on a sample page passes the Schema.org validator.

title: docs: add real lastModified dates to the sitemap
body:
## Problem

The docs sitemap added in #6967 lists every page but no `lastModified` date, so search engines cannot tell which pages changed and recrawl them all at the same rate.

## Proposal

- Set `lastModified` for each sitemap entry from the git history of the page's source file (the last commit that touched the `.mdx`, or its translation for translated URLs).
- The docs deploy workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml`) checks out with the default shallow clone, where every file reports the same date. Fetch full history there (`fetch-depth: 0`).
- Fall back to the build time when git history is unavailable, so local builds still work.

## Done when

- `npm run build` in `frontend/src/docs` writes `out/sitemap.xml` with a `<lastmod>` per URL that matches `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <file>`.
- Pages edited at different times have different dates.

title: feat(docs): add lastModified dates to the sitemap
body:
Code changes: +44 -2

title: feat(docs): add llms.txt, Markdown pages and page actions
body:
Code changes: +232 -0  
Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +325 -2 (translation catalogs, docs content, package.json)

Closes #7011. Builds on #7010 (`ao/docs-crawlable-i18n`), so this PR targets that branch.

## What changes

- **`/llms.txt`**: a short product summary, then every English docs page grouped by sidebar section as `- [Title](https://docs.orchestrator.inc/<path>.md): description`, and a link to `llms-full.txt`. Pages left out of the sidebar (legacy plugin URLs) are listed under "Other pages", so every published page is covered.
- **`/llms-full.txt`**: every page's processed Markdown in sidebar order, each headed by its title, URL and description. Uses fumadocs' `includeProcessedMarkdown` / `getText("processed")`.
- **`/<path>.md`** for every English page, e.g. `/quickstart.md`, `/configuration/projects.md`. The home page is `/index.md`.
- **Page actions** on every docs page: Copy Markdown, an Open in menu (ChatGPT, Claude) with a prompt that points at the page's `.md` URL, and View on GitHub linking to the source `.mdx`. The new strings are translated in all 16 non-English catalogs.

## How the `.md` files get to the site root

All three outputs are route handlers with `dynamic = "force-static"`, so they work with `output: "export"`. Route handlers are written under their exact path; `trailingSlash` doesn't change their file names (`out/llms.txt`, not `out/llms.txt/index.html`).

`/quickstart.md` can't be a route handler at the root, though: the English article route `app/(en)/[[...slug]]` already owns every root path, and Next rejects another catch-all beside it. So the handler builds the copies at `/markdown/<path>.md`, and `npm run build` then runs `scripts/move-markdown.mjs`, which moves them to `out/<path>.md`. GitHub Pages serves that file for `/quickstart.md`, next to `/quickstart/`. The deploy workflow already runs `npm run build`, so it needs no change. Under `next dev`, the copies stay at `/markdown/<path>.md`, and Copy Markdown reads them from there.

## Notes

- Drops a third-party name from the list of unsupported legacy notifiers in `plugins/notifiers`, so it no longer appears in the docs or the generated Markdown.
- `llms.txt` is headed "Orchestrator.inc Docs", and its summary names the product Orchestrator, also known as Agent Orchestrator or AO. Page descriptions keep the article text as written, including "Agent Orchestrator" and "AO", rather than the shortened name the site shows.
- Markdown is English only, as the issue says. On a translated article, the actions use the English `.md`. View on GitHub links to the translated source file (e.g. `quickstart.ja.mdx`).
- Copy Markdown hands the clipboard a pending `ClipboardItem`, so Safari keeps the click's permission while the file loads.

## Testing

- `npm ci && npm run build` in `frontend/src/docs` passes. `out/` has `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and 47 `.md` files, one per English page. All 47 links in `llms.txt` point to a file in `out/`.
- Served `out/` statically and checked in a browser: `/quickstart.md`, `/index.md` and `/configuration/projects.md` return Markdown. Copy Markdown copies the page (button switches to "Copied"; checked with the clipboard stubbed, since the test browser blocks clipboard access). The Open in menu opens with both links, and View on GitHub points at the `.mdx`. Labels follow the interface language (checked `ja` on `/ja/quickstart/` and German via the saved language), and the row wraps at phone width.

title: fix(chat): retry transient agent resumes after restart
body:
Code changes: +42 -11  
Tests: +558 -8  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Recover an opened local session after a transient agent-initialization timeout. Opening recovery now makes at most three attempts, with 2- and 5-second backoffs, while preserving readable history and suppressing the stopped banner during recovery. Permanent failures stop immediately and retain their error details.

## Why

After a reboot, a slow Codex initialization was reported as protocol incompatibility and the controller stayed stopped after one attempt. This is a human-reported startup bug; there is no associated provider issue. The original machine freeze/memory pressure has not been attributed conclusively to AO, and this change does not claim to fix a system-wide memory problem.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| An initialize deadline is reported as `409 CHAT_DRIVER_INCOMPATIBLE`; opening makes one attempt and leaves the controller stopped. | Context failures retain their cause and return `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; opening can recover automatically, with at most three total attempts. |
| ![Before: stopped controller after timeout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2d3de41-d2e6-4fb7-853e-cc910e998354) | ![After: controller automatically ready](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b8d1a24-08ff-4003-a2c2-a3d54dcd077f) |

These are **historical native fixture captures**: baseline `474962e31` and fixed `ba053d07b`, using the actual isolated Electron/daemon path and a delayed local fake Codex provider. They are not fresh captures of the rebased base/head, an OS reboot, or genuine live-provider recovery. [Original capture scope and observations](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7017#issuecomment-6315219328).

## How

Preserve initialization context errors instead of wrapping them as driver incompatibility. The existing service/HTTP contract then returns 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE; a genuine incompatible handshake remains 409. The resume helper retains error code, status, and request ID, including bodyless HTTP failures. Automatic opening retries only explicit SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE or HTTP 504 responses.

Each delayed attempt rechecks the opening identity, mounted state, current session eligibility, and daemon readiness. Navigation, termination, manual recovery, and interface/agent changes fence delayed launches. Existing hover/manual callers still share an in-flight request. This adds no eager bulk restore and submits no turn.

## Testing

**Rebase update — 2 November 2026:** rebased onto fixed `main` base `e8e3342d3fff2112ca64764a7254000f2d637f68`; current head `4edcdbf1af0ec8c5df42736a852ead09432c7ea5`. GitHub now reports the branch mergeable. No dependency/lockfile, API DTO/schema/OpenAPI, SQL/sqlc or migration changes were introduced by this PR.

Conflict resolution preserves main's translated resume guidance, request deduplication, current interface-transition checks, conversation invalidation and unchanged-toast assertions while retaining the structured failure metadata, bodyless-504 handling and original bounded retries. Added an authentication guidance/metadata assertion, updated the renderer's auth expectation, and extended HTTP tests to cover main's `RelaunchError` wrapper without changing its specific-error precedence.

- Current local checks: `git diff --check` passed. A genuine own `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` passed in 118.83s without source/lock/config changes. Both complete affected frontend unit files passed **304/304 tests**, with zero skipped/failed tests or unhandled errors; complete E2E TypeScript (`tsgo`) also passed. These ran sequentially under Node 24.22.0/npm 11.19.1, one worker and a 1536 MiB heap limit; common UI phase 26.01s, all owned process groups confirmed empty. No local Go tests or compilation, native app or browser phase has run on the rebased head. A separate module-only `go mod download` in a new private cache reached its administrative time cap after 276.60s (SIGTERM/exit -15, 0.957 GiB retained, 49/62 required module directories extracted). This setup is **INCOMPLETE**, not a test/product failure or pass; source/go.mod/go.sum/config hashes stayed unchanged, owned groups were confirmed empty, and no retry or unready Go test was started. Backend coverage is verified in exact-head CI below.
- **Current-head [Frontend CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41352455042) passed:** all four Vitest shards completed with **613 files passed, 10,571 tests passed and 6 skipped (10,577 total)**, zero failed files/tests and no reported unhandled errors. Renderer smoke passed **145/145**. Main and E2E TypeScript, shared-package/docs checks, Electron boundary checks, guarded navigation, and macOS helper/layout checks passed. These totals were read from the completed same-head logs. **All 30 current-head checks completed SUCCESS**, with no skipped, cancelled or stale job counted as a pass. title: feat(computer-use): install Cua Driver from Settings and give chat agents computer-use tools over MCP
body:
## Summary

Adds computer use to AO through [Cua Driver](https://cua.ai):
- **Settings → Computer use agents**, a new page that installs and manages the driver.
- **Computer-use tools** for chat agents. They let an agent see the screen and operate desktop apps, and they come from the session's existing `ao mcp` tool server.

Each action returns the window afterwards, the way Cua's own MCP server does: a text summary plus the window's screenshot as a real image. A terminal command can only return text, so there is no shell path: computer use is MCP-only.

### Settings → Computer use agents
- **Install / Update.** `cua-driver` is a new fixed target on the existing system-install route. It runs Cua's official installer through the same hardened `RunInstallScript` runner the agent CLIs already use (HTTPS only, size-capped, private scratch dir, SHA-256 recorded in the job output):
  - macOS and Linux: `install.sh` with bash.
  - Windows: `install.ps1` with PowerShell.
  - When bash or PowerShell is missing from the daemon's PATH, the page shows the reason and a copy button for Cua's own one-line install command (`curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh | bash`, or `irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows). It doesn't show an Install button that would fail the same way.
- **Install check.** A resolver probes the installer's destinations (`~/.local/bin`, `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cua`), because a Dock-launched daemon's PATH rarely includes `~/.local/bin`.
- **Status rows:**
  - Version, with "Update to X" when Cua's release channel has a newer one.
  - Background service (running/stopped), with **Start**.
  - macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording, with **Grant**. Grant runs `cua-driver permissions grant`, so macOS attributes the prompts to CuaDriver.app rather than AO.
  - Details: executable, screenshots folder, and **Run doctor**. When an update is available, a "Latest version" row with a release-notes link appears too.
- Built from `SettingsSection` and `SettingsRow` per `DESIGN.md`, and translated for all 8 locales.

### "Let agents use this computer"
- A switch at the top of the page, stored in `app_settings.computer_use` (new migration, **off by default**) and exposed as `PATCH /api/v1/settings/computer-use` plus `computerUse` in the settings response.
- While it's on, each **new chat session**:
  - gets `AO_COMPUTER_USE=1` on its `ao mcp` server, which then offers the computer-use tools;
  - gets a short **Computer use** prompt section: read the guide (`commands/cua.md`) first, send setup problems back to Settings, use `ao browser` for web pages, treat screen contents as untrusted, and confirm before anything destructive or outward-facing.
- The setting is read when a chat starts or restores, like the rest of the system prompt. Terminal sessions have no tool server, so they get no computer use.
- The switch needs Cua Driver installed before it can be turned on, and can always be turned off.

### The tools
`ao mcp` offers 8 tools, short on purpose because every definition sits in the agent's context on every request (about 7k tokens):

`list_windows`, `launch_app`, `bring_to_front`, `get_window_state`, `click`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `run_steps`

- **Schemas from the installed driver.** Each description and input schema is read from `cua-driver describe`, once per driver version, so arguments can't drift from the driver. Inputs AO sets itself or refuses are removed: `session`, `scope`, screenshot paths, `capture_mode`.
- **`hotkey`, `scroll`, `set_value`, `drag`** run as `run_steps` steps. `run_steps` types a step's args as any object, so its description lists their arguments, read from the driver's schemas.
- **Results** have a text block in Cua's MCP layout, plus one image block per screenshot:
  - the action's summary;
  - the window line (`window_id … pid … snapshot_id=…`);
  - the tree, or the diff since the last read;
  - which snapshots went stale.

### What AO does around each call
- **A read after every action.** `click`, `type_text` and `press_key` are followed by a `get_window_state` read of their window (`since:"latest"`, so only the changed rows), with a screenshot. `run_steps` gets the same through its `observe`, as one screenshot after the last step. A token names a snapshot, not a window, so AO remembers each snapshot's window.
- **One driver session per AO session.** Every call names `ao-<session id>`, so tokens and pixel-click context carry across calls. When an idle driver session has ended, AO revives it with `start_session` and retries once.
- **Refuses actions that would land wherever the user is working.** These checks run before the driver, on direct calls and on every `run_steps` step:
  - `scope: "desktop"` or a desktop `target`: `COMPUTER_USE_DESKTOP_SCOPE_DISABLED`.
  - Pixel `x`/`y` without the window's `pid` and `window_id`: `COMPUTER_USE_WINDOW_REQUIRED`.
  - `type_text` with no field: `COMPUTER_USE_TEXT_TARGET_REQUIRED`. This is the case that typed into the wrong WhatsApp chat in testing.

  The driver's own `desktop_scope_disabled` refusal gets AO's advice added, because the driver suggests `scope="desktop"`.
- **A failed `run_steps`** returns its per-step report (`2. click failed (find): …`) and the window, not an error.
- **Screenshots** are saved under `<data dir>/computer-use/<session>/`, newest 200 kept, and sent to the agent as images. Inline base64 from the driver is decoded to files and never passed through.
- **No foreground input.** `delivery_mode: "foreground"` (on an action, a `run_steps` step or the batch) and `foreground_fallback` are refused with `COMPUTER_USE_FOREGROUND_DISABLED` and hidden from the schemas, because they raise the window and send real input to whatever has focus. When the driver suggests foreground, AO adds its own advice instead.
- **`bring_to_front`** raises a window that stopped drawing because it was behind others (Chromium-based apps, on Windows especially). It sends no keys or clicks, and is followed by a read. Because it takes focus, the agent asks the user first.
- **Web pages** go through `ao browser`. The user's own browser is used only when they explicitly ask; then the agent checks the signed-in account and, if it starts the browser, passes Chromium's no-background-throttling flags.
- **Calls run only while "Let agents use this computer" is on, and only the 8 offered tools.** `POST /computer-use/call` checks the setting on every call. While it's off, the call is refused with `COMPUTER_USE_DISABLED`, which also cuts off chats that already list the tools. Any other driver tool is refused with `COMPUTER_USE_TOOL_NOT_OFFERED` before the driver runs: browser tools (which conflict with `ao browser`), `run_script`, whole-screen capture, and step-only actions called directly. That matters because the route is loopback-only but any local process can reach it.
- **Paired phones can't reach computer use.** The computer-use routes and the "Let agents use this computer" switch are both blocked on the LAN listener.

### API
These are new loopback-only routes. They are added to the LAN listener's blocked prefixes, so a paired phone can't drive the desktop:

| Route | Used by |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/computer-use/status` | Settings |
| `POST /api/v1/computer-use/daemon/start` | Settings |
| `POST /api/v1/computer-use/permissions/grant` | Settings |
| `GET /api/v1/computer-use/doctor` | Settings |
| `GET /api/v1/computer-use/agent-tools` | `ao mcp`: the 8 tools with their schemas |
| `POST /api/v1/computer-use/call` | `ao mcp`: runs one tool |

The OpenAPI spec and `schema.ts` are regenerated.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test` on every touched package: `systeminstall`, `computeruse`, `cli`, `httpd` (spec drift, LAN block), `session_manager`, `settings`, `storage`, `skillassets`, `telemetrymeta`. The `computeruse` and `cli` tests cover:
  - the action checks, including `run_steps` steps;
  - the read after each action, and token-to-window lookup;
  - session sharing and revival;
  - failed-batch reports;
  - agent-tool schemas and the step-argument summary;
  - MCP text and image blocks, and tools hidden while computer use is off.
- [x] `go vet`, `gofmt`, `go build`. Frontend `tsc`, and `vitest` for `ComputerUseSection` and i18n coverage.
- [x] Live on macOS with Cua Driver 0.37.0, through a lab daemon from this branch (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` and port), speaking MCP to its `ao mcp`:
  - `tools/list` returned the 7 tools;
  - reading Calculator, clicking a button by token, and `run_steps` each returned the text plus a PNG image block, and the image matched the tree;
  - a pixel click with no window was refused.
- [x] Live against the real driver: ended-session revival, the failed `run_steps` report, and screenshots after each action.
- [ ] Install and update on a clean machine. Not clicked locally, to avoid modifying the existing install; covered by unit tests.
- [ ] Linux and Windows on real machines.
- [ ] Windows **Start** fallback: when `autostart kick` fails, AO starts `cua-driver serve` itself, at the daemon's (non-elevated) integrity level, not as the installer's elevated logon task. Confirm it drives ordinary apps the same, and check what it can't reach: Windows (UIPI) blocks input to elevated windows.
- [ ] A real chat session (Claude Code and Codex) using the tools end to end. Image blocks in MCP tool results depend on each harness.

## Notes and risks
- **Remote script.** Installing runs Cua's vendor script, the same policy as the agent-CLI official installers (goose, devin, openhands). `install.sh` fetches a second Cua script itself, which AO does not fingerprint.
- **Windows.** The installer shows one UAC prompt to register Cua's logon auto-start task, which may run the service elevated. If AO has to fall back to starting `serve` itself, the service runs non-elevated and can't send input to elevated windows. The status row doesn't tell the two apart yet.
- **Terminal sessions** have no computer use.
- **Context.** Each action's screenshot is an image in the agent's context, roughly 1–1.5k tokens at the 1366 px cap.
- **Windows on another macOS Space** can't be read by the driver: `ax_window_unresolved`. AO shows the driver's reason in the result.
- **Lint.** golangci-lint v2.13.2 can't run on the local Go 1.27 toolchain, so CI is the first lint run.

## Follow-ups
- Optionally scope the toggle per project.
- Show the agent's latest screenshot in the session inspector.

title: fix(onboarding): recover clone and project setup failures

Code changes: +401 -101

## What

Make clone onboarding recover from URL formatting, destination conflicts, connection failures, cancellation, and project setup failures. A normal GitHub repository page URL works without adding `.git`; an existing destination offers reuse only when it is the same repository.

## Why

Cloning could hang and finish with a generic error, leaving users without a useful next step. Setup failures could also discard a successful checkout or leave the flow stuck after a lost registration response.

## How

- Normalize GitHub repository URLs and inspect destinations in the daemon without a network precheck.
- Retry temporary Git connection failures up to three attempts, show elapsed activity, and cancel the Git process tree on request cancellation.
- Retain successful clones for validation and registration retries. Back and Close always preserve completed checkouts; current daemons release the ownership marker, while legacy daemons receive no destructive cleanup request. A later flow must explicitly reuse an existing checkout rather than reclaim ownership from its marker.
- Resume local and remote project provisioning when registration succeeded but its response was lost; daemon project locks reuse active orchestrators. Failed existing-checkout validation keeps the clone dialog, inputs, and retry controls visible.

Credential setup and missing Git/agent installation remain intentionally deferred.

title: feat(chat): explain provider failures and offer the fix
body:
## Problem

When a provider refuses a turn, chat shows "The agent ran into a problem" followed by the raw JSON-RPC error, for example:

```
ACP session/prompt: {"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: Upstream request failed: Insufficient account funds","data":{...}}
```

Users can't tell whether AO, the harness, or the provider failed, or what to do. Separately, reopening a session could erase the error entirely, leaving the generic title with no text.

## What changed

**Daemon**
- `domain.ClassifyConversationFailure` sorts a failed turn's error into one of: out of credit, bad credentials, rate limited, overloaded, context too long, model unavailable, can't reach provider. OpenCode 2's `providerData.errorName` (`provider.quota`, `provider.auth`) is trusted first, then text patterns. HTTP status digits only match where they read as a status, so ports and line numbers don't.
- It strips transport framing down to the provider's sentence: JSON-RPC wrapping, `Internal error:`, `stream disconnected before completion:`, `unexpected status 401 ...:`, trailing `url:`, `cf-ray`, request ids, and Bun's `pass verbose: true` hint.
- Turns carry a new optional `failure: { kind, detail }`, derived on read, so existing history is classified too. The usage-limit notice still wins when it applies. Unknown errors return nothing and keep today's display.
- `SettleTurn` keeps the stored error when a turn is settled again into the same state with no message. Reattaching a controller replayed the completion without its error and wiped it.

**Chat card**
- Plain title, the provider's sentence, a short hint, then the action that can fix it: Sign in (opens the harness login), Switch model (opens the composer model picker, shared with the shortcut), or Retry for transient faults.
- The raw error sits behind "Error details" with a copy button.
- A failed turn with no work no longer shows "Worked for" and a lone rollback row above the card; rollback moves into the card.
- Retry is a real button and its strings are translated. New copy is in all 8 locales.

## Testing

- Classifier tests include every distinct failed-turn message found across 88 local AO databases (Codex, Pi, OpenCode), plus messages captured from live OpenCode 2 sessions.
- Ran 7 real OpenCode 2 chat sessions in an isolated dev app against a mock provider (402 funds, 401, 429, 529, context length, 404 model, dropped connection). All 7 classified correctly, and the errors survived a daemon restart and controller reattach after the `SettleTurn` fix.
- Earlier in the work: `go test` for domain, store, controllers, and chat service passed; frontend chat and i18n tests passed except three ContextMeter tests that fail on machines using Indian digit grouping (`2,58,400`), unrelated to this change.
- Not run on the final commit: tests and typechecks after the last two changes (rollback moved into the card, "Error details" rename).

## Notes

- OpenCode retries 429, 529, and dropped connections for about 3 to 4 minutes before failing, so those cards appear late. Not changed here.

title: 0.14.4: daemon/session API fail — native_identity_observed_at stored as text, cannot scan into time.Time
body:
**Daemon fails to start / session API returns INTERNAL_ERROR after update to 0.14.4: `native_identity_observed_at` stored as text that cannot be scanned into time.Time**

**Version:** AO desktop 0.14.4 (macOS, Apple silicon), auto-updated 21 Oct 2026 via ShipIt. Harness: codex (codex-cli 0.163.0). Previous version worked.

**What happens**
1. After the auto-update and restart, the daemon exits with code 1:
   `reconcile sessions on boot: reconcile: agent-switch pass: list all sessions: sql: Scan error on column index 14, name "native_identity_observed_at": unsupported Scan, storing driver.Value type string into type *time.Time`
2. Setting that column to NULL for the affected session lets the daemon start (`ao doctor` all PASS), but as soon as AO starts a Codex session it writes the value again as text, e.g.
   `2026-10-21 18:15:40.647754 +0200 CEST` (Go `time.Time.String()` format; an earlier write was `2026-10-21 18:10:29.118562 +0200 +0200`).
3. From then on, `ao send`, `ao session resume-agent` and session listing fail with `INTERNAL_ERROR` / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; a session left in `AGENT_RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` never resumes.

**Expected:** the column is written in a format the SQLite driver can scan back into `time.Time` (e.g. RFC 3339 / the driver's timestamp format), or it is declared/handled as TIMESTAMP so the read path does not fail.

**Notes**
- `sqlite3 ao.db "select typeof(native_identity_observed_at), count(*) from sessions group by 1"` shows one `text` row (the session AO just started); the other rows are `null`.
- Sessions whose chat-host processes predate the restart also stay unreachable after the update.
- Workaround we use: stop using AO for now.

title: fix(cli): ignore hooks from Claude background sessions
body:
Code changes: +33 -0\
Tests: +86 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Hooks that run inside a Claude Code background session no longer report to AO, so a background conversation can no longer take over an AO session's conversation id.

## Why

Addresses #6585. This covers the identity rebinding; the `AO_*` scrub and the delivery-side change the issue also suggests are not in this PR.

Claude Code's background daemon starts on demand (`/bg`, `claude --bg`, agent view) and inherits the environment of the process that first started it. When that process is an AO terminal session, the daemon and every background conversation it runs carry that session's `AO_SESSION_ID` and `AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID`. Their `ao hooks claude-code ...` calls therefore look like the AO session itself, with a valid launch id. The daemon accepts the new conversation id as an in-launch identity change (like `/clear`), and the next relaunch runs `claude --resume <background id>`, which Claude refuses because its daemon owns that conversation.

Reproduced on Claude Code 2.1.303 and 2.1.306 in the desktop app (isolated dev data, terminal-mode worker):

| Step | `sessions.agent_session_id` |
|---|---|
| baseline | `19f9aef9…` |
| after `/bg` in the pane | `19f9aef9…` |
| after a second `claude --bg` in the worker's folder | `2fc812d8…` (the background conversation) |
| after `ao session resume-agent` | `2fc812d8…`, and the pane prints "That session is running in the background (2fc812d8)…" |

The daemon's environment held `AO_SESSION_ID`, `AO_PROJECT_ID` and the worker's `AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID`.

## How

`runHook` (`backend/internal/cli/hooks.go`) now returns early for `claude-code` hook calls that come from a background session, before it reads stdin or reports anything.

- A background session is recognised by `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` (its job directory) or `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_KIND=bg`. Hooks do not see `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_KIND`: I logged the environment inside real background hooks on 2.1.303, 2.1.304 and 2.1.306 and only `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` is present, so the job directory is the marker that works in practice.
- A session with `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=1` is never treated as background. An interactive session started from inside a background job inherits those variables, and it must keep reporting. Background sessions have `attended=0`, including while a person is attached to them.
- Other harnesses are unaffected.

Not in this PR:

- Scrubbing `AO_*` from the environment Claude's daemon inherits (the issue also notes that `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` leaks into the long-lived daemon).
- Keeping a delivery pending when the relaunch fails with "running in the background", instead of marking the batch acknowledged.
- The reviewer hook path (`AO_REVIEW_SESSION_ID`).

Known limits:

- While a person is attached to a background conversation, AO does not see its activity. Before this change AO would rebind to that conversation and the next relaunch would fail.
- An AO daemon that was itself started inside a Claude background job would pass a stale `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` to unattended (Chat) Claude processes, and their hooks would be skipped.
- The markers are Claude Code details and could change in a later version.

## Testing

- Real flow (Claude Code 2.1.306, terminal worker, daemon and hooks built from this branch merged with `main` at 7c83bd68c): `/bg` in the pane, then a second `claude --bg` in the worker's folder. `agent_session_id` stayed `24c0f324…` and `ao session resume-agent` relaunched `claude --resume 24c0f324…` normally. The same steps without the change moved the id and broke the relaunch.
- Hook environment logged in real sessions on 2.1.303, 2.1.304 and 2.1.306: background hooks have `attended=0` and a job directory, foreground ones `attended=1` and none. This held for a foreground session spawning a subagent, and for a background session someone attached to. A Chat-mode worker's hooks still reach the daemon.
- `TestClaudeHookIgnoresBackgroundSessions` and `TestClaudeHookStillReportsForegroundSessions` cover the markers above, inherited markers on an attended session, and other harnesses. The first fails without the change.
- Mirrored the Go CI job locally on the merged tree (gofmt, build, vet, `go test -race` over all packages, including the sharded chat, session manager and SQLite ones). All passed except `TestDarwinPTYCloseDoesNotWaitOutAShellThatIgnoresSIGTERM` in `adapters/runtime/conpty`, which missed its 500 ms limit by 1.5 ms while the machine was busy, then passed 3 of 3 package runs and 10 of 10 single runs. This change does not touch that package.
- `golangci-lint` does not run on my machine (a `typecheck` error at `backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go:3`, identical on a clean `main`), so lint is left to CI. Frontend jobs were not run; only Go files changed.
- Not tested: Windows and Linux, Claude Code versions outside 2.1.303 to 2.1.306, several background sessions at once.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): show the saved model instead of a loader when opening a chat

## What changed

Opening a chat showed "Loading models…" with a spinner in the model picker until the agent reported its live settings. Since #6588 this happened on every chat you hadn't opened yet, and on any chat that was waking up.

The picker now names a model right away, picking the first one it knows:

1. The model saved on the chat.
2. The model this chat's agent last reported running. The renderer now remembers it per chat in local storage, capped at 500 chats. This covers agents that report their model only while running, like Cursor, OpenCode and Aider.
3. The agent's default model from its shared model list. This covers Claude Code chats on Claude's default model, which save no model.

While the chat starts, the model menu lists the agent's models from that same shared list, with the saved model checked. The rows are greyed out until the agent reports its own settings, then the menu switches to them. Before, the menu was empty until then.

The spinner only shows when none of these are known. That is a chat with no saved model, never seen running since this change, whose agent's list marks no default.

- `recordedModelName` moved from `ChatTimelineItems.tsx` to `lib/agent-model-choices.ts`, so the handoff line and the picker name models the same way.

title: fix(chat): show a zero context reading as 0% instead of "?"
body:
## What

The chat composer showed a "?" with "Context unknown / 1M" whenever the provider reported 0 tokens used next to a real context window. This draws that case as an empty 0% ring instead.

## Why it happens

The bundled Claude adapter (`claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0) sends `used: 0` in two cases:

- A turn fails. Claude Code writes its own stand-in reply (API error, usage limit, prompt too long) that never went through the API, so its token counts are all 0. The adapter reports that as the context used.
- A compaction finishes but the follow-up "how much is left" check fails, so the adapter falls back to 0.

AO keeps the latest report, so the 0 replaces the last good reading until the next turn reports a real number.

## Change

- `ContextMeter.tsx`: a known window with 0 used now renders the normal ring at 0%, with an empty track rather than the small sliver used for nearly-empty chats.
- A provider that reports used tokens but no window still gets the used-only readout. Nothing changes there.
- Tests updated for the 0-used case.

Keeping the previous reading instead of accepting the 0 is a backend change in `mergeUsage` and is left for a follow-up.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/`: 46 files, 1230 tests pass
- `npm run typecheck` passes

title: fix(report): deliver TUI reports whole and slow down unacknowledged retries
body:
Code changes: +263 -23\
Tests: +532 -0\
Others: +2 -3 (generated sqlc)

## What

Long messages that AO types into a Terminal UI agent now arrive whole, and AO stops re-sending a report every few seconds when it doesn't arrive. The bug was reported with Claude Code; Codex is affected too (see Testing).

## Why

Fixes #6931.

AO typed each report batch into the orchestrator's terminal, then waited for Claude Code's prompt hook to confirm it. Three problems combined into a loop:

1. **The text arrived broken.** AO typed long prompts as 512-character chunks. When the agent was slow to read its terminal, macOS joined the chunks into 1022-byte pieces. Claude Code treated each piece as a separate paste and dropped or reordered some of them. File paths ending in `.png` also became image attachments, with an `[Image #N]` placeholder placed in front of the text.
2. **AO only accepted a report if it came first.** If anything was in front of AO's envelope (a broken piece, an image placeholder, or the user's unsent draft), AO treated the delivery as failed.
3. **Failed deliveries were retried every 15 seconds, forever.** Each retry typed the whole batch again, and the reason for the failure was erased on each try.

The full investigation and a reproduction are in [this comment on #6931](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6931#issuecomment-6325616828).

## How

- **Send a prompt as one paste.** The pty-host has a new `MsgPasteInput` message. The host still writes the text in 512-character pieces, 15 ms apart. If the program has turned on bracketed paste, the first and last pieces also carry the paste markers, so the program reads all of it as one paste. The runtime uses this only with hosts that report protocol version 3. Hosts started by an older AO keep the old keystroke path.
- **Check that the report arrived whole.** The envelope now starts with a check line, `<ao-delivery-check sum="…"/>`: a short hash of the body with whitespace removed. AO pastes the envelope last, so it now accepts an envelope at the end of the prompt, even with other text in front of it, if the hash matches. It rejects one where text was lost, reordered, or added. A report quoted in the middle of a human prompt is still treated as human text. Envelopes without a check (written before this change) keep the old rule.
  - The opening tag is unchanged, so a hook from an older AO still reads the new envelope. This matters when agents keep calling the installed app's `ao` while a newer daemon runs, for example when testing a checkout against real AO data, or after a rollback.
  - Side effect: Copilot orchestrators get an AO directive in front of every message, so their reports could never be acknowledged before. Now they can.
- **Wait longer after each failed try.** When AO typed a batch but never got a confirmation, it now waits 15 s, then 30 s, 1 min, and so on, up to 10 min. Only those tries count toward the wait. Other failures, where nothing was typed (for example, an open permission dialog), still retry quickly. The count lives in memory, so a daemon restart starts again at 15 s. `last_error` now stays until the batch is acknowledged.
  - This growing wait is new and local to the report coordinator. Other AO retries, such as the handoff outbox, keep the message and retry without one. It is kept local because there is only one caller; it can move to a shared helper if reviewers prefer.
- **Keep file paths as text.** Output references, and words in report notes that end in an image extension, are put in backticks. Claude Code then leaves them as plain text.

Reviewers may want to look closely at `deliveryID` in `domain/report.go` and `MsgPasteInput` in the pty-host.

**Left out on purpose (follow-ups):**
- **tmux runtime:** it still types text with `send-keys`. The checksum and slower retries protect it, but it still needs a paste-buffer change and its own test.
- **Typing over a user's draft:** AO still writes into a composer that already holds text. That is a separate bug, already tracked in #5711.
- **A "stalled" state and a manual acknowledge command** for batches that never get through.
- **The coordinator lock is held while waiting for a confirmation,** which still delays other projects for up to 10 s.
- **A send queued during an interface switch** is counted as typed, so it waits like a failed try. It is acknowledged without being typed again if it lands before the next try.

## Testing

New tests, each written first and seen failing before the fix:

| Test | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `domain`: `TestReportDeliveryAcceptedBehindOtherText` | A whole report behind a user's draft is accepted |
| `domain`: `TestReportDeliveryRejectedWhenBodyChanged` | Lost, reordered, or added text is rejected (before the fix, all of these were accepted) |
| `domain`: `TestReportDeliveryCheckIgnoresWhitespace` and `TestLegacyReportEnvelopeStillAcceptedOnlyAtStart` | Harmless changes still match; old envelopes keep the old rule |
| `domain`: 6 more | A doubled envelope and a body that quotes AO's tags still match; a report quoted inside a human prompt does not; a checked envelope that lost its end is rejected; the old parser still reads the new envelope |
| `cli`: `TestHookConversationFactsCorrelatesReportBehindDraft` | The prompt hook reports the batch id in that case |
| `store`: `TestReportBatchKeepsLastFailureUntilAcknowledged` | `last_error` is no longer erased on retry |
| `report`: `TestCoordinatorWaitsLongerAfterEachUnacknowledgedDelivery` and three others | The wait doubles and is capped; other failures retry quickly and don't add to the wait |
| `report`: `TestRenderPutsOutputReferencesInBackticks` and `TestQuoteImagePathsInNoteText` | Paths stay plain text |
| `session_manager`: `TestSendSemanticTUITimeoutSaysTheMessageWasWritten` | A timeout says the text was typed |
| `conpty`: 6 tests | One bracketed paste when asked for, plain text otherwise, same 512-character pacing, old hosts unchanged |

**Reproduction with real Claude Code** (2.1.292, macOS). A small harness sent AO's exact keystroke pattern while pausing the Claude Code process for 150 ms, which forces the slow-reader case every time:

| Input | Old way (512-char chunks) | One bracketed paste |
|---|---|---|
| A real 1434-byte report batch | first 1022 bytes lost, exactly as in the bug | arrived whole |
| 2.9 KB text with a `.png` path | text reordered, `[Image #1]` in front | `[Image #1] [Image #2]` in front |
| Same, path in backticks | — | arrived whole |

That is why the fix uses both one paste and backticks. The unit tests show AO now sends exactly what the harness proved works.

**Other agents.** Eleven harnesses confirm delivery through a prompt hook, so all of them can loop the same way when text arrives broken. The same harness, with the same stall, was run against the other agents installed on the test machine:

| Agent | Old way (512-char chunks) | One bracketed paste |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code 2.1.292 | text lost or reordered; `.png` paths become images in front | whole once paths are in backticks |
| Codex 0.163.0 | the whole text sits **unsent** in the prompt box; Enter is taken as part of the paste (the symptom in #3626) | whole, `.png` paths included |
| Grok 1.0.62 | whole | whole |
| Pi 1.3.0 | whole | whole |

This PR doesn't claim to fix #3626: that report is on tmux, which this PR doesn't change, and #6490 takes a different approach there. On pty-host, one bracketed paste was enough for Codex to submit.

The host only adds paste markers when the agent has turned on bracketed paste, so an agent that never asks for it gets plain text as before. Not tested, because they weren't installed on the test machine: Amp, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Continue, Mimo Code, OMP, Prime Agent.

Side finding, not fixed here: Pi can drop a bracketed paste when the third-party `pi-auto-mode` package (0.1.3) is loaded. Typed keystrokes still arrive. In tests with Pi 1.4.0 the loss followed that package, not the "package updates available" notice: a paste was lost with the notice off, and arrived with the notice on and the package absent. I do not know why the package drops it. Users with `pi-auto-mode` could lose messages to Pi after this PR, because it moves Pi from keystrokes to one paste.

**CI jobs run locally** (macOS, Go 1.27.3; lint with Go 1.27.1 as in CI):

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| `gofmt`, `go build`, `go vet` | pass |
| `sqlc-drift` (pinned sqlc 1.31.1) | pass |
| `api-drift` | pass |
| `cli-e2e` Go tests (`-tags e2e`) | pass |
| `lint` (golangci-lint 2.13.2) | 1 finding, `scriptStepMinute` in `session_manager/manager.go`. It is already on `main` and not from this change. |
| `backend-core` + `chat-race` + `session-store-race` + `sqlite-race` (`go test -race ./...`) | pass, except 3 tests in packages this PR doesn't touch (below) |
| `cloud-build-test` | pass, except 1 timing test (below) |

The tests that failed in the full local run, and why they appear unrelated:
- `crush` `TestCrushLocalAuthStatusDoesNotUseProviderCatalog`: fails on `main` too on the test machine, because it finds that machine's real Crush login.
- `chatdriver/acp` `TestACPReplayLoadLargeHistoryThroughSDK` and cloud `TestSetupStepEventsHeartbeatWhileOutputKeepsArriving`: timing tests that failed only under full parallel load. Each passes when run on its own, on this branch and on `main`.

title: fix(projects): let large repositories finish cloning
body: Code changes: +23 -5 Tests: +75 -0 Others: +16 -0 (translations) ## Problem Cloning `https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator` from the Clone dialog hung for about a minute, then showed "Could not clone repository". A retry with a `.git` suffix sometimes worked, so it looked like a URL problem. It was a timeout. `git clone` runs inside the `POST /api/v1/projects/clone/prepare` request, and every `/api/v1` request is capped at 60 seconds (`config.DefaultRequestTimeout`). This repository is about 590 MB, and a clone took 86 seconds on a fast connection. At 60 seconds the request context was cancelled, git was killed, and the daemon returned `GIT_CLONE_CANCELLED`, which the dialog shows as the generic error. Both URL forms resolve the same way (`git ls-remote` takes about 2 seconds for each). The `.git` retry worked only when it happened to finish in under 60 seconds. The dialog also gave no sign that a clone was running. The inputs went grey and nothing else changed. ## Changes - `POST /api/v1/projects/clone` and `POST /api/v1/projects/clone/prepare` get a 30-minute budget. Other routes keep the configured budget. - A clone that runs out of time returns `GIT_CLONE_TIMED_OUT` instead of `GIT_CLONE_CANCELLED`. - The dialog shows its own message for `GIT_CLONE_TIMED_OUT`. While a clone runs, the button shows a spinner and "Cloning...", and the text under "Clone into" reads "Cloning into . Large repositories can take a few minutes." The new strings are translated in all 8 locales. ## Before / after Real desktop app with isolated data, cloning `https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator` (no `.git`) into an empty folder. Before is `origin/main` at f691e1d244. After is this branch. | | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | 45 s after Continue | | | | Result | | | | `clone/prepare` response | `400 GIT_CLONE_CANCELLED` after 60.0 s | `200` after 133.7 s | The timeout message (`GIT_CLONE_TIMED_OUT`) is covered by tests and isn't shown here, because reaching it takes 30 minutes. ## Not in this PR - Live clone progress (streaming `git clone --progress`). - A way to cancel a running clone. Close and back stay disabled during a clone, as before. - Renaming the "Repository URL" label. URLs with and without `.git` both work. ## Testing - `TestCloneRoutesUseExtendedTimeout`: fails before the fix (the clone routes got the 250 ms test budget). - `TestManager_PrepareCloneReportsRequestTimeout`: a deadline returns `GIT_CLONE_TIMED_OUT`. - Frontend tests for the cloning state and the timeout message. - Local CI: Go `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), `go test -race` on `internal/httpd/...` and `internal/service/project/...`; frontend `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, `npx vitest run` (516 files, 8,863 passed, 7 skipped). The full sharded Go suite and the other workflows are left to CI. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(storage): index provider events by session so restarts don't stall chats
body:
## Problem

After a restart, existing chats returned `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY` for 30 s or more, and some stayed `unavailable` until a manual Resume.

`conversation_provider_events.session_id` cascades from `sessions` but has no index, so every session delete scans the whole table on the only writer connection. The startup check deletes leftover spawn seed rows. At 2.4M events that delete took 28.5 s, and the other sessions' reattach checks timed out at their 30 s limit.

## Fix

Add `idx_conversation_provider_events_session`. The delete drops from 28.5 s to 0.08 s.

Restart until the first send is accepted, on a copy of an affected 4.1 GB database:

| build | send accepted |
|---|---|
| main | +26-32 s |
| this PR | +1.0-1.2 s |

The index build is a one-time cost on first launch: 17-61 s on that database.

## Tests

- `TestProviderEventsSessionLookupUsesIndex` fails without the migration (`SCAN conversation_provider_events`).
- `go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/...` passes.
- `npm run sqlc` produces no drift.
