title: bug(desktop): main-process crash ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION in JSStreamSocket: remote proxy runs HTTP/2 over a WebSocket Duplex (regression from #6652)
body:
## Bug
The desktop app repeatedly shows a native "A JavaScript error occurred in the main process" dialog:

```
Uncaught Exception:
Error [ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION]: This is caused by either a bug in Node.js or incorrect usage of Node.js internals.
    at assert (node:internal/assert:11:11)
    at JSStreamSocket.doWrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:176:5)
    at JSStream.onwrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:35:57)
    at ClientHttp2Stream.submitRstStream (node:internal/http2/core:501:19)
    at ClientHttp2Stream.finishCloseStream (node:internal/http2/core:2109:3)
    at closeStream (node:internal/http2/core:2085:7)
    at ClientHttp2Stream._destroy (node:internal/http2/core:2512:7)
    at _destroy (node:internal/streams/destroy:122:10)
    at ClientHttp2Stream.destroy (node:internal/streams/destroy:84:5)
    at Writable.destroy (node:internal/streams/writable:1124:11)
```

**Source:** live report from the maintainer (desktop app `0.14.5-nightly.202610212020`, macOS, 2026-10-21) | **Analyzed against:** `origin/main`
**Confidence:** Medium-high. The code path is traced and matches the stack exactly; the exact Node race wasn't reproduced in a harness.
**Priority:** high (uncaught main-process exception with a modal dialog, recurring; the main process continues in an undefined state)
**Regression from:** [PR #6652](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6652) (2026-10-16), which added the WebSocket tunnel transport to the remote proxy.

## Root cause
`frontend/src/main/remote-proxy.ts`:
- For `https` remotes, `openTunnel()` (≈l.270) opens a WebSocket to `/api/v1/tunnel` and wraps it with `ws.createWebSocketStream`, a JS `Duplex`.
- `openUpstreamSession()` (≈l.347) passes it to `http2.connect({ createConnection: () => tunnel })`. A non-native Duplex makes Node wrap it in an internal **`JSStreamSocket`**, which is exactly the frame in the stack.
- When a client stream is destroyed (a request cancelled, `stream.close(NGHTTP2_CANCEL)`, a client disconnect, keep-alive retiring the session, or the tunnel itself closing), http2 sends RST_STREAM via `submitRstStream` → `JSStreamSocket.doWrite`. That trips Node's internal assertion when a write is already pending or the wrapped Duplex is closing. This is a long-standing fragility of http2 over JSStreamSocket in Node/Electron. Because it's thrown synchronously inside `destroy()`, none of the `on("error")` handlers catch it, so it's an uncaught exception.

**Why this machine hits it:** `~/.ao/remotes.json` has 2 remotes, both `https://*.trycloudflare.com`. Quick tunnels take the WebSocket-tunnel path (see the comment above `tunnelRetryAt`) and drop or recycle connections often. The machine is also on a VPN (Surfshark WireGuard). Both mean frequent tunnel closes with streams still in flight.

## Fix (suggested)
1. **Don't hand http2 a JS Duplex.** Bridge the WebSocket tunnel through a loopback TCP pair: a one-shot `net` server on 127.0.0.1, `pipe` the ws stream to the accepted socket, and give `http2.connect` a real `net.Socket` via `createConnection`. Native sockets don't go through JSStreamSocket.
2. Belt and braces: when the tunnel emits `close`/`end`, `session.destroy()` the http2 session before Node tries to RST individual streams, and avoid `stream.close(NGHTTP2_CANCEL)` on a session whose tunnel is already closing.
3. A main-process `uncaughtException` handler should log and recover from errors that come from the remote proxy, instead of showing a native modal that leaves the app in an unknown state. Don't swallow everything globally.
4. Regression test: an http2 session over the tunnel with several in-flight streams, then the WebSocket is closed abruptly, or streams are cancelled while writes are pending. Must not throw.

## Reproduction
1. Add a remote host that is served through a Cloudflare quick tunnel (`https://*.trycloudflare.com`).
2. Use it (open remote sessions, previews or the agent browser), ideally on a flaky network or a VPN.
3. After a tunnel drop or request cancellation, the main-process error dialog appears, and keeps reappearing.

## Related
- [PR #6652](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6652): introduced the WebSocket tunnel transport

title: [Bug]: PR panel merge-readiness indicator hangs gray forever when repo Actions are disabled (no checks exist)
body:
### Bug description

On the PR panel, the merge-readiness indicator stays gray **"Checking merge readiness — Waiting for the latest checks and review state"** forever when the repository's GitHub Actions are disabled at the platform level (e.g., GitHub auto-disables Actions on a fork). In that state the checks rollup is permanently empty — the checks API returns `total_count: 0`, nothing is pending, no result will ever arrive — but the panel renders this absence as "checks in progress" and never resolves the indicator to any terminal state (green / red / neutral).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take a repository (in my case a private fork of this project) where GitHub Actions is disabled by the platform — `POST /dispatches` returns `HTTP 422 "Actions has been disabled for this repository"`, while `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions` misleadingly reports `enabled: true`.
2. Open any of its PRs in the AO desktop app PR panel.
3. Observe the merge-readiness rows: two gray "Checking…" indicators that never resolve, no matter how long you wait or how often the panel refreshes.

### Expected behavior

- Zero checks (`total_count: 0`, no in-progress runs) should resolve to a terminal/neutral state immediately — e.g., "No checks configured" — not be rendered as an eternal "checking" wait.
- The UI should distinguish "checks exist and are running" from "no checks exist at all".

### Actual behavior

Gray "Checking merge readiness — Waiting for the latest checks and review state" hangs indefinitely; merge-readiness never resolves for any PR in the repo.

### Environment

- AO desktop app, macOS (Apple Silicon), 0.14.x line.
- Repository with GitHub Actions disabled by the platform (fork).
- Panel data at the time: checks rollup `total_count: 0`, all rollup entries `pending` — i.e., an empty set drawn as "waiting".

Happy to provide more diagnostics if useful. Not planning to work on the fix myself — filing for triage.

title: feat(accounts): sign an expired account in again from chat, and start new tasks on another account
body:
Code changes: +255 -27\
Tests: +245 -16\
Others: +40 -0 (translations)

## Problem

When Anthropic refuses a saved Claude account's refresh token (`invalid_grant`), Claude Code clears that account folder's login. The chat turn fails with "Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed", and then:

- AO keeps reading the account as signed in until its 5-minute cached reading expires.
- The sign-in banner says to run `claude auth login`. That command signs in this computer's own login, not the account's folder, so following it does not help.
- Every new task keeps starting on the dead default account.

## What changes

**The failure is noticed at once.** When a session's agent is refused for its credentials, the daemon re-reads that session's account in the background (`RecheckSessionAccount`). Claude has already cleared the folder's login by then, so the account reads as signed out immediately in Settings and for new tasks. This works for saved accounts and for this computer's own login.

**New tasks skip an account that is known to be signed out.**
- A new task starts on the default, unless the default is known to be signed out or to now hold another login. Then it starts on the first other signed-in account.
- A signed-out reading of the default that is older than the cache window is read again first.
- The task is refused only when no account is signed in.
- Readiness (`DefaultSignIn`, which #7007 extended to Claude) describes the account new sessions actually start on. A dead default no longer blocks the picker when another account works, and readiness reports "signed out" only when no account is signed in.

**The chat banner offers the fix.**
- It names the signed-out account ("dhruv@example.com is signed out").
- **Sign in again** runs that account's own sign-in in the same embedded terminal Settings uses, shown in a dialog.
- **Continue on <other account>** moves the chat to another signed-in account, using the existing move.
- Both end with a note to retry the last message.
- A chat on this computer's own login keeps the `claude auth login` / `codex login` hint and still gets the Continue button.

## Behavior change

`BindSession` used to refuse a new task on a known-bad default rather than "quietly on another account, which bills someone else". This PR reverses that on purpose: a dead default now falls back to a signed-in account. It is not silent, because the session's Account field shows which account the task started on.

## Intentional omissions

- The first chat on a newly expired login still fails. Nothing local can know the refresh token is dead until a refresh is attempted. From that failure on, the banner and the fallback take over.
- There is no in-chat sign-in button for this computer's own login. Its sign-in runs through the harness login flow in Settings.
- There is no automatic retry after signing in or moving. The banner asks the user to retry.

## Tests

- `agentaccounts`:
  - A bad default falls back to the computer's login and the other way round, and is refused when nothing is signed in.
  - A stale signed-out default is re-read before falling back.
  - `RecheckSessionAccount` marks a dead login signed out, and new tasks then move off it.
  - `DefaultSignIn` follows the fallback and names the account it falls back to.
- `ReauthBanner`:
  - Sign in again runs the account's sign-in and verifies it.
  - A sign-in that isn't finished stays open, and closing it cancels the login.
  - Continue moves the session.
  - A chat on this computer's login gets the Continue button.
  - The existing 8 banner tests are kept.

## Local verification

- **Go:** gofmt, `go build`, `go vet` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 (0 issues) are clean.
  - The full `go test -race -count=1 ./...` run: 199 packages pass, including the accounts, agent, session, daemon and chat packages. After rebasing onto #7007, I reran agentaccounts, agent and daemon with `-race`; they pass.
  - Two failures in the full run pass when rerun alone, so they were load flakes: `e2e` `TestFirstTaskStartupRetryAfterDaemonSIGKILL` and the two `claudecode` auth tests.
  - Six failures fail identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout on this machine. They come from the locally installed agent binaries: `fake`, `modelcatalog`, `opencode`, `opencodev2`, `reviewer/opencodev2` and `integration`.
- **Frontend:** `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e` and the full `npx vitest run` before the #7007 rebase. 8,866 tests pass once the 4 `ChatWorkspaceProviderState` tests that this PR broke are fixed; the fix stubs the new account reads.
  - After the rebase, the affected vitest files pass (39 files, 554 tests).
  - After the rebase, `tsc --noEmit` is clean too.
- **Not run locally:** the Windows jobs, the docs build, the cloud-client and product-ui package checks (untouched), and the browser integration job.
- **Not verified in the running desktop app:** the banner and the sign-in dialog are covered by component tests only.

title: fix(models): cache agent model catalogs per device, not per project
body:
Code changes: +370 -283  
Tests: +542 -332  
Others: +14 -8

## What

Model catalogs are now cached once per agent per device instead of once per (agent, project). The only scopes left are the device catalog and cloud credential scopes (`@cred:<type>`).

## Why

The cache was split by project. Opening a model picker in a project with no row of its own blocked on a full CLI discovery, even when the device already had an identical catalog cached for another project. Measured on a real daemon: cached reads take ~11 ms, while the first read in a new project took ~1 s for codex, ~15 s for cursor and ~23 s for opencode. In practice the per-project lists were the same everywhere (27 of 30 agents had byte-identical model lists across projects), yet each project needed its own discovery, revalidation and drift-repair pass (#7001).

## Flow

How a picker gets its models (New Task, chat, project settings, Settings > Harness):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant UI as Picker / Chat / Settings
    participant LS as Browser snapshot
    participant API as Daemon models API
    participant DB as agent_model_catalog (one row per agent)
    participant RD as Agent readiness
    participant CLI as Agent CLI discovery

    UI->>LS: read saved snapshot
    LS-->>UI: render instantly
    UI->>API: GET /agents/{agent}/models (no project)
    API->>DB: read device row
    alt row exists
        DB-->>API: saved catalog
        API-->>UI: list in ~10-200 ms, no readiness wait
    else never discovered
        API->>CLI: start discovery in background
        API-->>UI: within 500 ms: real list, or fallback marked refreshing
    end
    Note over API,CLI: Updates run in the background, only after readiness
    API->>RD: wait for startup readiness pass (max 30 s)
    alt agent not installed
        RD-->>API: skip update, keep saved row
    else installed or unknown
        API->>CLI: discover models
        CLI-->>API: models
        API->>DB: save row
        DB-->>UI: model_catalog CDC event
        UI->>API: refetch every view of this agent
        API-->>UI: new list replaces the old one
    end
```

Where each request goes in the daemon:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Models request: agent and optional scope] --> B{Cloud credential scope?}
    B -->|yes| C[Cloud credential catalog]
    B -->|no: project ID or empty| D[Device catalog for this agent]
    C --> E{Saved row?}
    D --> E
    E -->|yes| F[Return saved list at once]
    F --> G{Due, inputs changed or invalidated?}
    G -->|no| Z[Done]
    G -->|yes| U[Background update]
    E -->|no| H[Start discovery, wait up to 500 ms]
    H --> I{Finished in time?}
    I -->|yes| J[Return discovered list]
    I -->|no| K[Return fallback marked refreshing, UI polls]
    H --> U
    U --> R[Wait for startup readiness pass, max 30 s]
    R --> N{Agent not installed?}
    N -->|yes| S[Skip and keep saved list]
    N -->|no| P[Discover with agent CLI]
    P --> Q[Save device row]
    Q --> T[CDC event refreshes open pickers, chat and Settings]
```

Chat and spawn use the same saved catalog first:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Chat
      C1[Chat opens] --> C2[Show saved catalog]
      C2 --> C3{Live session list answered?}
      C3 -->|models or error| C4[Live answer decides]
    end
    subgraph Spawn
      S1[Launch with model or effort] --> S2{Saved catalog lists the model?}
      S2 -->|yes| S3[Validate, no discovery]
      S2 -->|no, stale or empty| S4[One live rediscovery, then validate]
    end
```

## How

**Backend (`service/agent`)**
- `modelCatalogScope` is now pure. It keeps a `@cred:` credential scope and maps everything else, including a project ID, to the device scope. Discovery never reads a project's path or env, so it always uses the AO model-discovery directory.
- Removed `ProjectLookup`, `rediscoverDriftedProjectCatalogs` and `InvalidateProjectModelCatalogs`, plus the project service's `OnModelScopeChanged` hook that fed it. With one catalog there is nothing per-project to repair or invalidate.
- Startup prefetch and `InvalidateModelCatalogs` skip legacy per-project rows.
- A read with no cached catalog never blocks the picker. It waits at most 500 ms for discovery; slower agents immediately get their capability fallback marked `refreshing`, discovery finishes and persists in the background, and open views (which already poll refreshing catalogs) pick up the real list. Explicit refreshes still wait.
- Saved catalogs list without waiting on agent readiness; background catalog updates wait for the startup readiness pass (bounded at 30 s); explicit refreshes bypass that wait, including a background load joined by spawn and skips agents readiness found not installed, keeping their saved catalog. Settings > Harness models shows the saved list before install/login are confirmed; the install/login notice only appears when nothing is saved.
- Session spawn validates model and effort against the saved catalog first and rediscovers only when the saved list cannot answer (stale, empty, failed, or missing the requested model). Previously every Claude Code or Codex launch with a model or effort set waited on a live discovery.
- Model recency stamps (`lastUsedAt`) now use sessions from every project, so the shared catalog response is the same everywhere.
- Migration `20261022054735000_device_model_catalogs.sql` deletes legacy per-project rows and the retired `@browse:all` rows. Device and `@cred:` rows are kept. It is forward-only because the rows are a cache.

**Frontend**

- Local callers (`TaskComposer`, `ProjectSettingsForm`, the shell prefetch) pass the device scope. Cloud opencode keeps its credential scope.

After any live answer (models or error) the live list decides, so entitlements still win and agents that cannot list models never offer saved choices. title: fix(desktop): give the remote proxy's HTTP/2 session a native socket over the tunnel
body:
Fixes #7043

## Summary
The remote proxy passed the WebSocket tunnel's JS `Duplex` (`ws.createWebSocketStream`) to `http2.connect` via `createConnection` (#6652). Node wraps any non-native Duplex in an internal `JSStreamSocket`.

When the tunnel's TCP connection resets (a Cloudflare quick tunnel dropping, a VPN), `ws` closes without the socket ever reaching `finish`. The `JSStreamSocket` then starts a shutdown that never completes, and the HTTP/2 session stays open on it. The next frame the session writes trips `assert(this[kCurrentShutdownRequest] === null)` at `js_stream_socket:176`, uncaught, in the main process. That frame can be RST_STREAM for a cancelled preview or EventSource, the keep-alive PING, or the GOAWAY on destroy.

**Fix:** `openTunnel()` now relays the tunnel through a loopback `net` socket pair, using a one-shot listener on `127.0.0.1:0`, so http2 gets a native `net.Socket` and never goes through `JSStreamSocket`.
- The listener accepts only the proxy's own connection, matched by its local port. Any other local dialer is dropped, and the listener closes once the pair exists.
- If the tunnel, either loopback end, or the session's socket ends or closes, all three are torn down. A dead tunnel closes the session at once, and the next request opens a fresh tunnel.

## Regression test
`survives streams cancelled after the tunnel reset, then opens a new tunnel` in `remote-proxy.test.ts`:
1. Opens 4 preview streams through a tunnelled host.
2. Resets the tunnel's TCP connection (`resetAndDestroy`).
3. Cancels the streams and waits through a keep-alive ping.
4. Asserts that no `uncaughtException` was raised and that the next request goes over a new tunnel.

- **Before the fix:** fails with 6 × `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION` captured.
- **After the fix:** passes.

## Tests run
- `vitest run src/main/remote-proxy.test.ts`: 65/65 pass.
- `vitest run src/main/remote*`: 148/148 pass.
- Tunnel tests run 10× in a row with no flakes.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean for `frontend/src`. The only errors are pre-existing ones in `packages/product-ui`, from its uninstalled workspace dependencies.
- Run on Node 24.20. A standalone repro (http2 over `createWebSocketStream`, tunnel reset, then a stream cancel or session destroy) also reproduces the assertion on Node 22.11.

## Not included: a main-process `uncaughtException` guard
I considered one and left it out. Electron shows its "A JavaScript error occurred in the main process" modal only when it is the sole `uncaughtException` listener, and Sentry's integration decides the same way (`listenerCount <= 2`). So any listener we add, however narrow its match, suppresses the modal for every main-process error, and we would have to re-implement it. With this change the remote proxy no longer hands http2 a JS stream at all, so this error class can't come from here. Happy to add a narrowly matched guard (`ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION` with a `js_stream_socket` frame, everything else re-shown) as a follow-up if wanted.

## Risks
- One extra loopback hop per tunnelled session: a local copy only, negligible next to the tunnel.
- When the session ends, the tunnel is destroyed rather than given a WebSocket close handshake. The host already treats a dropped tunnel as a closed session.

title: fix(scm): resolve a PR with no checks instead of waiting on them
body:
Code changes: +199 -10\
Tests: +286 -0\
Others: +28 -2 (generated OpenAPI spec and schema, translations)

## What

A PR whose head commit has no checks now has its own CI state, `none`, so the PR panel shows "No checks configured" and resolves from the provider's merge state instead of sitting on "Checking merge readiness" forever.

## Why

Addresses #7044.

When a commit has no check runs and no commit statuses (a repository with no workflows, or with Actions disabled), GitHub returns a null `statusCheckRollup`. `ciSummaryFromRollupState` mapped that to `unknown`, the same value as "not observed yet", and `pr-display.ts` treats `unknown` as "checks still loading". Nothing is ever going to arrive, so the panel never resolved.

Reproduced on current `main` in the desktop app with a real PR in a fork with Actions disabled: GitHub reports it `CLEAN`, `MERGEABLE` and 0 checks; `ao session ls` shows `CI unknown`, the API returns `ci: "unknown"` next to `mergeability: "mergeable"`, and the panel stays on "Checking merge readiness / Waiting for the latest checks and review state." more than a minute and several SCM polls later.

## How

- `github/provider.go`: `noRollupCIState` is shared by both rollup mappers. A null rollup on a PR that has a head commit is `none`; with no head commit it stays `unknown`. A rollup that is present keeps its existing mapping, including `unknown` for a state GitHub did not decide.
- `contract/status.go`, `domain/pr.go`: new `CINone`. `ReadyToMerge` does not treat it as a blocker, so the provider's own merge state (`Mergeability`) decides, as it does for `passing`. `unknown`, `pending` and `failing` still block.
- `pr.ci_state` has a CHECK constraint, so `20261022051758732_pr_ci_none_state.sql` widens it with the same `sqlite_master` rewrite the harness migrations use (RESET, shape guards in both directions, and a down that refuses while `none` rows exist). The id is added to `shippedMigrations`.
- `dto.go`, `openapi.yaml`, `schema.ts`: the `ci` and `ci.state` enums gain `none` (regenerated, no other drift).
- `pr-display.ts`: `none` is not "checking"; it gets a "No checks configured" row and "No checks" in the summary, `prCanMerge` accepts it when the PR is mergeable, and the ready detail no longer says "checks are passing" for it. A merge state that is still `unknown` keeps showing "Checking merge readiness".
- Three strings in the eight locale catalogs (`pr.card.checksNone`, `pr.ci.none`, and `pr.merge.reasonReadyNoChecks`, which is English in every locale like the existing `pr.merge.reasonReady`).

Not in this PR:

- GitLab has the same gap (a merge request with no pipeline stays `unknown`). Left alone; it is a different adapter and I did not test it.
- `cloud-cp/types.ts` has its own copy of the state union for the cloud API and is unchanged.

Known limits:

- GitHub also returns a null rollup for a moment right after a push, before it creates the checks. That PR reads as `none` until the next poll. GitHub's own merge state is still required, and repositories that require checks report `BLOCKED` in that window, but one that does not can briefly show "Mergeable".
- A PR already stored as `unknown` is re-observed and updated within `DefaultPRMaxAge` (5 minutes) after upgrading.
- Rolling back past the migration needs the `none` rows cleared first; the down migration refuses otherwise.

## Testing

- Real app (fix built from this branch, isolated data, throwaway PR in a fork with Actions disabled, closed afterwards): `ao session ls` shows `CI none`, the API returns `ci: "none"`, and the panel shows "No checks configured", "Mergeable" with "No merge conflict, no checks are configured, and the review requirement is satisfied.", and a Merge button. The daemon applied the new migration to an existing database (schema now allows `none`, existing rows kept).
- New tests: null rollup is `none` for both mappers (and `unknown` without a head commit, `passing`/`pending`/`failing` for a present rollup); a blocked PR with no checks stays blocked; `ReadyToMerge` across CI states and merge states; the store round trip `unknown` to `none` to `pending`; the migration up and down on a real schema, an unrecognized constraint refused, rollback refused with `none` rows, integrity and foreign-key checks; and the panel for `none` (mergeable, blocked, merge state unknown, review required, `prCanMerge`) plus `unknown` still waiting.
- Reverting each production change in turn (null rollup back to `unknown`, `none` blocking `ReadyToMerge`, the panel counting `none` as checking, `prCanMerge` ignoring `none`, no migration file) makes the matching tests fail.
- Mirrored the Go CI job locally on this branch (gofmt, build, vet, `go test -race` over all packages, including the sharded chat, session manager and SQLite ones). All passed. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 under Go 1.27.1 reports one finding, a `revive` `time-naming` warning in `session_manager/manager.go` that is on `main` and not touched here (CI did not flag it on my other PR).
- Regenerating the OpenAPI spec and `schema.ts` leaves no diff. `tsc --noEmit` reports the same 57 errors as an unchanged checkout, all in `packages/product-ui` (`react` does not resolve here) and none in files this PR touches. Frontend renderer suite: 8830 passed, 40 failed, 7 skipped. The failures are `browser-profile-import.test.ts` (39; the `better-sqlite3` native module does not match this Node version, identical without my change), `annotate-preload.test.ts` (a Vite "Denied ID" error from my `node_modules` symlink) and one `HarnessUpdateNotice` test, which fails the same way on an unmodified upstream `main`. None involve this change.
- Not tested: GitLab, Windows and Linux.

- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: bug(updater): macOS 'could not prepare the update' when the Mac sleeps mid-preparation: watchdog counts sleep as stall, and Retry can never succeed
body:
## Bug
On macOS, "Restart to update" fails with **"AO could not prepare the update… Couldn't finish preparing the update. AO stayed open, so nothing changed. Retry to try again."** when the Mac sleeps while the update is being prepared. **Retry can never succeed in the same app process.** The native update was in fact staged correctly.

**Source:** live report from the maintainer (2026-10-21, macOS, running `0.14.5-nightly.202610212020`, target `0.14.5-nightly.202610220502`) | **Analyzed against:** `origin/main`
**Confidence:** High. The timeline is proven from power logs and the ShipIt cache, and the code path is traced. This confirms the hypothesis from the 2026-10-16 occurrence.
**Priority:** high (every nightly update on a laptop that sleeps mid-preparation fails; the in-app Retry is a dead end)

## Evidence (read-only, nothing clicked or changed)
| Time (PDT) | Event |
|---|---|
| 22:35:08 | DarkWake (maintenance) |
| 22:35:12.198 | AO records the download (`~/.ao/staged-update.json` `stagedAt`); ShipIt cache `update.dT6Nr6J` is born the same second |
| **22:35:14** | **System sleeps ("Maintenance Sleep") for 987 s** |
| **22:51:41** | **Wake (lid/HID)** |
| 22:51:48 | `update.dT6Nr6J` finished: a complete 603 MB `Agent Orchestrator.app` at `0.14.5-nightly.202610220502` |
| 22:51:50 | `ShipIt_stderr.log`: "Detected this as an install request"; ShipIt PID 46557 is still armed and waiting |

Disk: 14 GiB free (97% used) on the data volume. The disk check passed.

The 2026-10-16 occurrence had the same shape: an 8m41s sleep ending exactly when the staging dir appeared. See `artifacts/agent-orchestrator-399/updater-triage.md`.

## Root cause
`frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`, `beginNativePreparation()` (≈l.322–400):
- The watchdog measures elapsed time with **`Date.now()`**: `startedAt`, `lastProgressAt`, and `now - startedAt` against `STAGE_NO_SIGNAL_CAP_MS` (6 min) and `STAGE_ABSOLUTE_CAP_MS` (15 min). Wall-clock time includes system sleep.
- On the first 10 s tick after waking, `now - startedAt` is ~16.5 min, which is over both caps, so `trip()` runs before the native ready event arrives about 9 s later.
- `trip()` calls `blockNativePreparation(STAGE_STALL_MESSAGE)`. `nativePreparationBlocked` is **never cleared** for the life of the process: `beginNativePreparation` returns immediately when it's set ("recovery is a clean relaunch"). So the dialog's **Retry button can never work**, and the late native ready event is ignored. That matches "retry failed again".

## Fix
1. **Don't count sleep.** Use a monotonic clock that excludes suspend, or subscribe to `powerMonitor` `suspend`/`resume`: pause the watchdog on suspend, and on resume reset `lastProgressAt` and push `startedAt` forward by the time spent asleep. Re-check `macShipItDir()` before deciding.
2. **Accept late success.** If the native `update-downloaded`/ready event or a completed `update.*` bundle for the target version arrives after a trip, clear the block and offer "Restart to update" instead of ignoring it.
3. **Make Retry honest.** Retry should either truly re-arm, or the dialog should say "Quit and reopen AO to finish updating" (or offer a Relaunch button) instead of a Retry that can't succeed in this process.
4. Merge or rebase onto [PR #6856](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6856), which persists updater diagnostics including suspend/resume events.
5. Tests: a fake clock with a simulated 16-minute suspend mid-preparation followed by the native ready event must end in "ready to restart". Retry after a real stall must re-arm, or must not be offered.

## Workaround
ShipIt is armed with a valid staged bundle, so **quit AO (Cmd-Q) and reopen it**. That should install 0.14.5-nightly.202610220502. Not verified, but it's the same armed state the 2026-10-16 occurrence was in.

## Related
- [PR #6856](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6856): persist local preparation diagnostics (open; adds suspend/resume logging)
- [PR #5479](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/5479): introduced the progress-based staging watchdog
- [PR #5907](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/5907), [PR #6609](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6609): other open updater fixes
- [#4175](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/4175): macOS ShipIt ditto staging failures (different native failure, same dialog text)
- [#6911](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6911): macOS update popup hangs on install (different symptom)

title: fix(chat): move idle orchestrators to a new harness release
body:
## Summary

After a Claude Code update to 2.1.308, two orchestrator Chat sessions (`agent-orchestrator-117`, `ao-landing-3`) kept showing **"Switching to v2.1.308… Happens when the agent is idle or with your next message."** and never switched, even after sitting idle for a long time.

**Cause.** Every trigger that moves a Chat session to a new release skipped orchestrators:

- **Sweep:** `ListVersionRefreshChatCandidates` had `AND kind <> 'orchestrator'`.
- **Turn-end timer and next message:** both go through `hibernateOptions.eligible` → `EligibleForChatHibernation`, which rejects `KindOrchestrator`.

The exclusion comes from idle hibernation keeping orchestrators awake (#6386). #6745 reused that filter for version moves, but a version move stops the provider only to start it again right away. The installer stop (`forUpdate`) already lifts the exclusion for the same reason. The banner, meanwhile, renders for any session with the stale mark.

**Changes**

- `hibernate.go`: a version move (`versionRefresh`) lifts the orchestrator exclusion, as `forUpdate` does. Turn, queue, approval, background-work and view checks are unchanged. Idle hibernation still keeps orchestrators awake (`TestHibernateChatKeepsOrchestratorAwake` still passes).
- `sessions.sql` (+ sqlc): the chat sweep candidate query no longer excludes orchestrators. The TUI query is unchanged; terminal moves are a separate opt-in.
- Banner: the sweep can't move a session whose agent controller **stopped** (the `ao-landing-3` case); only a resume starts it, on the new release. In that state the banner now reads "v2.1.308 installed · Resume the agent to start it on the new version." instead of "Switching…". The existing controller banner beside it carries the Resume action. Strings added for all 8 locales.

The usage-limit error turn seen on `ao-landing-3` is not a blocker: a failed turn counts as settled.

The `ao-landing-3` resume failure (provider-handle mismatch) is a separate problem and is being triaged elsewhere; it is not addressed here.

## Evidence

Read-only query of the live DB (2026-10-22 06:36 UTC): both affected sessions are `kind=orchestrator`, `chat`, `idle`, `ready`, marked stale on their current `controller_generation`, with `stale_binary_switch_failed_at` NULL. They meet every sweep condition except the `kind` filter. A worker on the same update (`agent-orchestrator-147`) did move.

## Tests

New tests, each failing on main and passing here:

- `TestVersionRefreshChatCandidatesIncludeOrchestrators` (store)
- `TestVersionRefreshMovesQuietStaleOrchestrator` (chat; checks idle hibernation still refuses the orchestrator)
- `TestSendMovesQuietStaleOrchestratorToNewRelease` (chat, next-message path)
- `VersionSwitchBanner` › asks for a resume instead of promising a switch when the agent stopped (frontend)

Also ran:

- `go test ./internal/service/chat/... ./internal/storage/...`: pass.
- `./internal/session_manager/`: pass except four `TestSpawn_*Binary` tests, which fail the same way on main in this environment.
- `go vet`, `npm run typecheck`, and the `ChatStatusBanners` and i18n vitest suites: pass.

**Isolated lab** (headless daemon, separate data dir and port, `AO_VERSION_REFRESH_IDLE=20s`, a real Claude Code Chat orchestrator in a throwaway repo, stale mark written to the lab DB only):

- Main build: idle about 8 minutes across three sweep ticks; same chat-host, same generation, no move.
- This branch: after a daemon restart the old chat-host reconnected with the mark carried over. On the first sweep tick the log showed `chat session stopped to move to a new harness release`, a new chat-host from the new binary started, the generation changed, `staleBinary` cleared, and the session stayed awake (`hibernated_at` NULL).

The lab was shut down and removed afterwards.

## Risks

- Orchestrators now restart once after an update when quiet for `AO_VERSION_REFRESH_IDLE` (10m default), or right before the next message after that quiet period. Messages that arrive meanwhile queue and are delivered on the new release, as for workers. A failed start records `switchFailedAt` and keeps the queued messages.
- Terminal (TUI) orchestrators are still excluded from terminal moves. That path is a separate opt-in (`AO_TUI_VERSION_REFRESH`) and was left unchanged.

title: [Feature]: Choose native subagents or AO workers based on the task
body:
## Problem

AO's desktop and cloud standing prompts prohibit native subagents for both orchestrators and workers, routing all parallel help through separate AO worker sessions (introduced in #3817).

That blanket restriction makes bounded read-only work such as code searches, log investigation, summaries, and second looks at a diff require a whole AO session. Workers without an orchestrator cannot obtain that help through the suggested route. Agents without native subagents also need guidance on when a separate AO session is appropriate.

## Proposed direction

Choose delegation based on the work, while honoring explicit user requests:

- Small or step-by-step work: handle it directly within the agent's role.
- Bounded read-only side tasks that report back: use native subagents when available; otherwise handle the task directly.
- Work that edits files alongside the current task, needs its own branch/PR, should outlive the task, or should be visible on the board: use a separate AO worker. Workers ask their orchestrator to spawn it, or tell the human if there is no orchestrator.
- Native subagents share the workspace: never let one edit while the parent or another subagent is editing.
- An explicit user choice of native subagents or AO sessions takes precedence, while preserving role boundaries.
- Orchestrators remain coordination-only. Native subagents may assist with read-only investigation; implementation, fixes, and tests go to AO workers.
- Native subagents are not AO worker sessions and must never be reported as started AO workers.

Update all four standing prompts together:

- Desktop orchestrator and worker: `backend/internal/session_manager/prompt.go`.
- Cloud orchestrator and worker: `cloud/internal/workerexec/prompts.go`.

## Acceptance criteria

- All four prompts consistently express the work-based choice and explicit-user-preference rule, without the blanket native-subagent ban.
- Worker guidance works both with and without an attached orchestrator.
- The orchestrator implementation restriction and native-subagent/AO-session distinction remain explicit.

title: GitHub reviews, comments and merges take minutes to reach AO (SCM observer ticks run ~2 minutes)
body:
### What went wrong?

GitHub changes take minutes to reach AO. That is too slow, and not acceptable by design: new reviews and comments, CI state, and merges/closes should show up in AO within about 30–60 seconds.

Two cases from one day (2026-10-19, macOS, installed app, dozens of sessions across two repos):

- An AO native review comment was posted on #6907 at 02:13:25Z. AO first recorded it at 02:17:01Z. Injection into the worker followed promptly after that.
- OrchestratorInc/ao-landing#59 was merged on GitHub at 00:52:53Z. AO's next observer tick started at 00:53:57 but only committed at about 00:56:11, so one tick took ~2m14s against a 30s target. (#6932 now records in-app merges right away; external merges still wait on the observer.)

Related, same area: the review feedback delivered to the worker listed thread `PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6txAz0` as unresolved, even though it was resolved by the time the message arrived.

### Expected

GitHub changes reach AO within ~30–60s at a realistic fleet size, and observer ticks never stretch to minutes.

title: feat(review): refresh a PR's review threads as soon as an AO review is submitted
body:
Code changes: +128 -15\
Tests: +141 -4\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When AO's native reviewer submits a review it posted to GitHub (`ao review submit --review-id …`), the daemon immediately asks the SCM observer to fetch **that PR's** metadata and review threads, then runs the normal ingest and auto-inject path. It no longer waits for the next poll to notice the PR changed. This is the review-side counterpart of #6932, which did the same for in-app merges.

## Why

Part of #7057.

AO's own review on #6907 was posted at 02:13:25Z and recorded at 02:17:01Z. Most of that delay was the stalled poll fixed separately in #7058. Even with polls healthy, a review still waits for the next scheduled tick and for the repo guard to notice the PR's `updated_at` change.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A provider-posted AO review waits for scheduled SCM polling and review cadence. | Submission requests an immediate poll and thread refresh; provider cooldowns still apply. |

## How

- `Observer.RequestReviewRefresh(prURL)` records a one-shot request and kicks the poll loop through a new `observe.StartTriggeredPollLoop`. `StartPollLoop` is unchanged for other observers.
- The next poll treats that PR as a refresh candidate and bypasses the review cadence for it. It then goes through the **same** persist → lifecycle → acknowledgement pipeline as any other change, so the injected message is built from the threads fetched at that moment.
- One attempt, no retry loop. The request is consumed by exactly one poll whatever its outcome. Fetch failures are logged by the existing poll paths (`review refresh failed`, `GraphQL PR batch failed`), and the regular cadence remains the fallback. Rate-limit cooldowns still apply: while a provider is cooling down, neither the PR batch nor the review-thread fetch is sent, forced or not (thread fetches previously ignored the cooldown).
- `review.Service` calls it only on the real `running → complete` transition and only when a provider review id was supplied. Re-submitting an already complete run doesn't trigger another fetch.
- The daemon builds the review service before the observer, so it holds a late-bound `scmReviewRefresher`. Until the observer is bound, or when no SCM provider exists, a request is a no-op and polling picks the review up.

On the stale "unresolved" thread from #7057: that message came from a snapshot that was ~2 minutes old by the time it was delivered (see the evidence on #7057). On this path the threads are fetched at submit time and the nudge is built from the rows just written, so that staleness window doesn't exist here.

## Testing

Rebased onto `main` at `2c58085c`; current head is `7378a8abf`. The rebased source tree is byte-for-byte identical (same Git tree ID) to `a33ff8002`, for which all 20 CI checks passed. The three PR commits are retained with the verified daemon-wiring conflict resolution; fresh CI is rerunning for the new commit IDs.

### Merge-conflict resolution validation (`a33ff8002`)

Merged `main` at `2c58085c` without rewriting the PR history. The single conflict in daemon wiring preserves both the combined browser lifecycle and the late-bound review refresher.

- Local build, vet, focused race suites (`./internal/observe/... ./internal/service/review ./internal/daemon`), an isolated daemon race rerun, and clean-environment native CLI E2E passed. Pinned lint reported zero issues.
- Broad local backend/cloud runs were not clean: they encountered adapter/probe/timing failures in unmodified packages. The CommandCode conditional-include and installed-OpenCode catalog failures also reproduced on unmodified `main`. These local runs are not claimed as passing.
- All 20 fresh GitHub checks passed for `a33ff8002`, including the full backend suites, cloud, native CLI on all OSes, Windows-specific checks, container install, lint, and API/SQL drift. Docker was unavailable locally; the container job was verified in CI.

- `TestPoll_RequestedReviewRefreshFetchesThreadsOnce`:
  - With the repo guard at 304 and the PR fresh, a normal poll fetches nothing.
  - After `RequestReviewRefresh`, the trigger fires and the next poll fetches the PR and its threads once, persists the comment in replace mode, and notifies lifecycle.
  - A following poll does not fetch again.
- `TestPoll_RequestedReviewRefreshRespectsRateLimitCooldown`: a forced refresh during a provider cooldown makes no thread or PR fetch. Without the guard it fails with `reviews=1 batches=0`.
- `TestSubmitRequestsReviewRefreshForProviderPostedReview`: exactly one request for a provider-posted review, none on retry, none without a review id.
- `TestStartTriggeredPollLoopPollsOnTriggerBeforeTick`.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test ./internal/observe/... ./internal/service/review/ ./internal/daemon/` pass.
- **Isolated daemon lab.** Setup: own data dir and port, a hibernated Claude chat worker with an open PR on a private test repo. A review run was created by `ao review trigger`; I then did what the reviewer does: posted a GitHub review with an inline comment, then ran `ao review submit --run … --review-id …`. The post was timed 3s after a poll finished, so the scheduled path has to wait for the next tick. Both builds include #7058, so the hibernated-worker stall doesn't skew the numbers.

| | #7058 only | #7058 + this branch |
|---|---|---|
| inline comment posted → in AO's DB | 26.9s | 1.4s, 1.6s |
| delivered to the worker | via the next scheduled poll | immediately; the worker's conversation received the "1 unresolved review comment" nudge |

## Risks / follow-ups

- A triggered poll is a full poll (all tracked repos), not a single-PR fetch. At the fleet size measured on #7057 that is ~8–14s of GitHub calls, mostly 304s. Reviews are infrequent, so the extra poll is cheap compared with tick cadence.

title: fix(updater): exclude macOS sleep from preparation watchdog
body:
Code changes: +129 -24  
Tests: +206 -11  
Others: +12 -3  


## What

Fix macOS update preparation failing across system sleep and restore installation when the owned native update succeeds late.

Builds on #6856, which is now merged. This PR now targets `main` and contains only the sleep/recovery fix.

## Why

Fixes #7053.

The issue's power-log timeline proves a 16-minute suspend between download and native readiness. The previous `Date.now()` watchdog counted that interval against its 15-minute absolute cap, blocked preparation, and ignored native success nine seconds after wake. Fake-clock regressions reproduce and prevent this failure.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The preparation failure dialog labels its process-relaunch action **Retry** and says nothing changed. | The same error state says **Relaunch AO** and removes the misleading “nothing changed” claim. |
| A 16-minute suspend counts toward the 15-minute wall-clock watchdog cap and fails on wake. | Power events and a timer-gap fallback exclude suspended time; native readiness nine seconds after wake is accepted even with either or both power events missing. Active-time caps remain intact. |
| Native success after the watchdog trip is ignored for the rest of the process. | A matching owned target/channel recovers readiness and offers explicit install confirmation. |
| A failed install request can resume when its uncancellable transfer settles. A native error after readiness can also leave it waiting for the progress helper. | Failed requests stay abandoned, including during helper startup; another explicit confirmation is required. |
| A missed resume can freeze the preparation clock indefinitely. | A running watchdog tick clears stale suspension; ordinary ticks still reach the active-time limits. |
| The disk error says “retry” beside a process-relaunch action. | It says “Free up space, then try again,” compatible with the dialog and Settings recovery paths. |

Native desktop captures: `updater-before.png` and `updater-after.png`, attached to the AO session report for manual GitHub attachment. Both use the real Electron app, the same 1080 × 780 window, empty scratch data, version 2.0.0 and a controlled IPC preparation-error fixture. They verify UI wording, not an actual native update failure. Additional review-follow-up captures: `updater-disk-before.png` and `updater-disk-after.png` show the disk error with the same controlled IPC fixture and window. Both isolated labs were stopped and their temporary worktree removed. Browser attachment upload is blocked by the ChatGPT extension's file-URL permission; the four PNGs are supplied through AO artifacts for manual attachment.

## How

- Pause the macOS native-preparation clock on `powerMonitor` suspend. A running tick clears stale suspension when resume is missing. Gaps above 30 seconds count as one 10-second poll and refresh inactivity, so missing suspend/resume events cannot recreate the reported failure. Re-resolve staging on wake; preserve the existing active-time caps. Backwards clock gaps also avoid extending the budget.
- Accept a late native ready event only for the still-owned timed-out target and channel. A native error or discarded target invalidates recovery. No filesystem bundle alone is treated as verification success.
- Keep failed install requests abandoned even if their uncancellable cache transfer or progress-helper handshake later settles. Native errors reject the active install after readiness as well; post-wait guards prevent quitting. Recovery restores an explicit install confirmation.
- Label the existing relaunch action **Relaunch AO** in all supported locales and let an open dialog recover when native readiness arrives before or after the failed IPC reply.

### Limits

The timer-gap fallback treats a long event-loop pause like sleep, since those signals are indistinguishable here. Every gap still credits a normal poll toward the absolute cap. No assumption that Electron emits power events for Maintenance Sleep/DarkWake is required.

The maintainer confirmed that quit-and-reopen installed `0.14.5-nightly.202610220502`, validating the workaround. This worker did not touch the live installed app, ShipIt processes/cache, or staged update. No live update hop or release/publish was attempted. Native failure recovery deliberately requires a fresh process unless a matching native success arrives; the new Relaunch label states that action explicitly.

## Testing

### Review follow-up (2026-10-30)

Head `88b24bf876` addresses review [5712679157](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7061#pullrequestreview-5712679157): missing-event timer fallback, bounded stale suspension, repeated-gap active cap, backwards-clock regression, native failure while the progress helper is starting, and neutral disk-space recovery wording. The progress-helper regression failed against the old error handler, then passed with active-operation rejection and post-wait guards.

- 251 focused updater/dialog/diagnostics/i18n tests passed, including confirmation of a newer remembered target after an earlier native error. Both frontend TypeScript checks passed.

- Native helper configuration (17 tests), both architecture builds/lipo, Swift policy/effects/low-power/update-state tests, three real Electron boundary tests and browser integration passed.
- Final local full Vitest rerun with two workers: all **593 files / 9,937 assertions passed**, 9 skipped, but the command exited nonzero for one asynchronous Radix/jsdom focus-scope teardown exception attributed to `SettingsDialog.popovers.test.tsx`. The initial highly concurrent run hit an unrelated browser-history timeout and was stopped before this full rerun. An isolated rerun of `SettingsDialog.popovers.test.tsx` passed all 7 tests without the exception. This is not a clean local full-suite pass.
- Local macOS renderer rerun with one worker: **131/133 passed**; composer-selection failures at `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts:111` and `:139`. The first concurrent run passed 126/133. No updater assertions failed.

Docker is unavailable locally; the Linux renderer container and newer main's `mac-dmg-layout` job were verified in CI. Historical validation below is for earlier heads.

title: [Feature]: Update open artifacts in real time as agents edit them
body:
### Problem

Open artifacts do not update in real time when an agent edits the underlying file. A user watching an artifact cannot follow the document as it is being written.

Reported in the Oct 22 discussion with Aditi: Claude sometimes creates a document outline first, then fills in and edits sections while the document is open. We want that same ability to watch an AO artifact take shape.

### Proposed direction

Keep the open artifact viewer in sync with agent changes as they happen. Support the flow where an agent creates a document or outline, the user opens it, and subsequent edits appear without closing, reopening, or manually refreshing the artifact.

Acceptance criteria:
- An artifact already open in the viewer updates automatically when its underlying content changes.
- Multiple successive agent edits continue appearing while the artifact stays open.
- Updates preserve the user's reading position where possible.
- Incoming updates do not silently overwrite unsaved user edits; handle that state explicitly.
- Verify the behavior for local artifacts and cloud artifacts when cloud artifact support is enabled.

### Alternatives considered

Closing and reopening the artifact interrupts reading and makes it difficult to follow the agent's progress.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar.

title: Native reviewer can't reliably submit: whole review must fit in one single-quoted shell argument, loops and burns tokens
body:
## Bug
AO's native reviewer can write a review but often can't **submit** it. The prompt gives exactly one way to submit: put the whole review into a single shell command as one big single-quoted JSON string (`printf '%s' '<json>' | gh api ...` and then `printf '%s' '<json>' | ao review submit ... --reviews -`). Every other route is blocked. When the review is long, or the text contains an apostrophe the model doesn't escape as `'\''`, the command fails or gets denied. The reviewer then has no other way to submit, has nothing else it can do, and loops. One observed run burned **~235k tokens** without posting anything.

**Analyzed against:** `a95139bb0d` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** High (code path traced; the loop itself was reported, not reproduced locally)

## Reproduction
1. Run `ao review trigger` on a PR with a non-trivial diff, using the default Claude Code reviewer.
2. The reviewer produces a long review (many inline comments and/or prose with apostrophes, e.g. "doesn't", "worker's").
3. Step 1 (`printf '%s' '<json>' | gh api --method POST .../reviews ...`) fails because the quoting breaks or the generated argument is malformed. If the model tries a heredoc or a temp file, the call is denied.
4. The reviewer retries or echoes and never reaches a successful submit. No GitHub review and no `ao review submit` record are produced.

## Root Cause
Several constraints together leave a single fragile submit path:

1. **The prompt requires one-line, single-quoted JSON and forbids heredocs.** See `backend/internal/review/prompt.go:29` and `:38`:
   > Keep the JSON on one line and shell-escape any single quotes in review text before passing it to printf; do not use a heredoc because reviewer panes run through an interactive PTY.

   The *entire* review (summary plus every inline comment) is sent this way. Step 2 sends the full markdown body a **second** time, the same way.
2. **The permission hook accepts only that exact shape.** `backend/internal/cli/hooks.go:536-540`: `reviewerSubmitCommandPattern` matches `^printf '%s' '<single-quoted literal with '\'' escapes>' | (gh api ... --input - --jq '.id' | ao review submit --session X --reviews -)$`. A heredoc, a file, `--body-file`, a stray unescaped `'`, or anything else gets `reviewerPermissionDenyMessage`.
3. **File writes are blocked.** `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/claudecode/claudecode.go:82-85` disallows `Edit`/`Write`. Codex runs with `--sandbox read-only` (`codex/codex.go:123`). So `ao review submit --reviews <path>` / `--body <path>` (`cli/review.go:208-210`), which already exist, can't be used.
4. **Models are bad at producing very large, escape-heavy tool arguments.** One missed `'\''` ends the quote early. The command then either fails the regex (denied) or becomes a malformed shell command. The deny message says to use "the exact single-line printf command", so the model tries the same fragile thing again, which produces the loop.

The bug is in the design rather than in one line: the whole review payload is pushed through shell quoting in a channel where one wrong character fails the submit.

## Fix (suggested; needs a design decision, not a one-line patch)
Take review content out of shell arguments entirely. Options, roughly in order of preference:

- **A. Let the reviewer write to an AO-owned scratch path outside the worktree.** Example: `~/.ao/data/reviews/<run-id>/review.json`. On Claude Code, allow `Write(<that dir>/**)` while keeping the general `Write` deny. On other harnesses, use the equivalent rule. Then submit with `ao review submit --session X --reviews <path>`, which is a short, static, regex-friendly command. Have the **daemon** post the GitHub review (it already has the PR and SCM adapter), so step 1 and step 2 become one call and the reviewer never builds `gh api` JSON. This also removes the duplicate body.
- **B. Add an AO-provided MCP/tool for submitting** (structured `reviews[]` arguments, no shell). This is the cleanest for harnesses that support MCP, but it's more work for each harness.
- **C. (Stopgap)** Make submit incremental: one `ao review comment --run X --path F --line N` per inline finding, with the body on stdin, then a short final submit. Each argument stays small. This is still quoting-based, so it only reduces the failure rate.

Also worth doing regardless:
- Cap retries: after N denied or failed submit attempts, the reviewer should call `ao review submit` with an empty `githubReviewId` and a short body (or AO should mark the run failed) instead of looping.
- Have the daemon detect a reviewer that has gone idle or is looping with no submit and fail the run, so tokens aren't burned without limit.

## Impact
- The native review feature silently produces nothing on exactly the PRs where a review matters most (large diffs, many findings).
- Unbounded token spend (~235k observed on one run) with no output.
- The worker never gets the review comments, so the review → fix loop stalls.
- Affects every harness, because the prompt is shared. Harnesses without a permission hook may also run a half-quoted command.

## Related
- `e74fb65a85` feat(review): support additional reviewer harnesses (#2306): introduced the single-line printf/no-heredoc submit instruction.
- `ff8d490ebc` feat(review): let agents request AO native review of their own PRs (#6262)

title: fix(opencode-v2): install OpenCode 2 beside OpenCode 1 with every method
body:
Code changes: +397 -45  
Tests: +701 -33  
Others: +0 -8  

## Problem

OpenCode 1 and 2 both ship an executable named `opencode`. Only AO's npm method installed OpenCode 2 into a private prefix. The other two methods wrote it over OpenCode 1:

- **Official installer** (`opencode.ai/v2/install`) always writes `$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode`, the same file OpenCode 1's installer uses, and edits shell profiles.
- **Homebrew** (`anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2`) links it into `<prefix>/bin/opencode`. The formula also declares `conflicts_with "opencode"`.

When that happens, the OpenCode 1 harness reports "not installed" and existing OpenCode 1 sessions can't resume. One user hit exactly this: v2 at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`, v1 gone, and the panel said only "OpenCode is not installed."

## Changes

**Every OpenCode 2 install method now stays out of OpenCode 1's path**
- Official installer: runs with `HOME=<opencode-v2-home>/installer` and `--no-modify-path`, so it writes only `~/.local/share/opencode-v2-home/installer/.opencode/bin/opencode`. If that home can't be resolved, the method is unsupported rather than falling back to the default path.
- Homebrew: after install, update or reinstall, runs `brew unlink opencode-v2`, and v2 is resolved through `<prefix>/opt/opencode-v2/bin/opencode`. If OpenCode 1's `opencode` formula is linked, it's unlinked first (otherwise the formula conflict blocks the install) and linked again afterwards.
- `Plan` gains `Cleanup` steps. They run after `Command` whether or not it succeeded (bounded by their own timeout, even after an install timeout), so OpenCode 1's link is always restored. They also appear in the displayed command.
- The resolver probes the installer bin dir and the `opencode-v2` opt links. It still checks the major version, so OpenCode 1 sessions never pick up v2.
- Removed the "installing OpenCode 2 replaces OpenCode 1" notice, the install dialog's fallback text, and its i18n key in all 8 locales, since no method replaces OpenCode 1 anymore.

**Explain an existing replacement**
- When the OpenCode 1 check finds only OpenCode 2 at a default (non-AO) location, the health panel now says which executable is OpenCode 2, that it replaced OpenCode 1, and the repair order: reinstall OpenCode 2 from AO first, then OpenCode 1. The `not_installed` state and reason code are unchanged. OpenCode 2 found only in AO's private folders still reads "not installed".

- The resolver also checks for the unlinked `opencode-v2` formula under `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` and under the prefix of the `brew` on PATH, so a Homebrew install under a custom prefix verifies instead of failing as "not found".
- If OpenCode 1's default `opencode` is Homebrew's link into the `opencode-v2` keg, the message says to run `brew unlink opencode-v2` first. That link also blocks linking OpenCode 1's formula, and reinstalling OpenCode 2 with npm would leave it in place.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| OpenCode 2 official/Homebrew installs can overwrite OpenCode 1's executable. | AO isolates OpenCode 2 and restores OpenCode 1's Homebrew link after the operation. |
| A v1 check finding v2 at the default path only says v1 is not installed. | The message identifies the executable and gives repair steps. |
| Replacement daemon waits 108 seconds by default while installer draining can take 284 seconds, then can exit 75 before cleanup finishes. | Takeover includes the shared installer shutdown budget and waits 382 seconds by default, allowing bounded cleanup before refusing startup. |
| A second automatic SIGTERM during shutdown can terminate the daemon before OpenCode 1 is relinked. | Worker cancellation leaves signal handling registered through restoration and the remaining shutdown stages. |

## Review follow-up

- Daemon shutdown separates worker cancellation from deferred SIGINT/SIGTERM unregistration, so a second automatic signal cannot interrupt restoration.
- Every v2 Homebrew run reserves v1 before inspecting its linked marker, including when planning overlaps a v1 reinstall or a deferred operation starts later.
- Normal daemon shutdown allows both cleanup deadlines, command termination and persistence to finish before exiting. Replacement-daemon takeover uses that same installer budget instead of timing out during cleanup.
- AO-managed v2 launchers no longer produce a false v1 replacement warning. Resolver test fixtures exclude host Homebrew installs and drain cancellation workers before cleanup.

## Tests

- Native CI follow-up: `TestE2E_SecondDaemonOnSameDataDir` derives its expected refusal message and outer timeout from the expanded installer drain budget (302.8 seconds plus a 15-second test margin with its 100ms shutdown setting). Exit 75, no second run-file, first-daemon health and takeover after owner shutdown remain covered. This adds roughly five minutes of lock waiting to the native suite; validation runs only in GitHub Actions.
- Repeated-signal follow-up: added a Unix subprocess regression for both SIGTERM-initiated and cancellation-initiated shutdown, with SIGTERM during simulated restoration. Not run locally; GitHub Actions only.
- Takeover follow-up: added duration cases and a scaled data-directory lock regression for installer cleanup beyond the previous takeover deadline. Not run locally; GitHub Actions only.
- Updated: OpenCode 2 recipe test (all methods isolated, no replacement notice), legacy install route test, readiness mismatch test.
- New: installer private HOME and `--no-modify-path` (and unsupported without a home), Homebrew unlink/relink order for install and update, cleanup running after a failed install, and the replacement message for default vs. private locations.
- Rebased onto `main` (`e8e3342d3f`); resolved installer dependency and plan-field conflicts by retaining main’s managed-binary, download and migration fields alongside the PR’s private installer homes and harness reservations. Main’s live installer progress output is retained. Validation for the rebase and review follow-ups runs only in GitHub Actions. No on-device checks, tests, builds, lint, typechecks, generation or benchmarks were run.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Homebrew may print "keg not linked" hints after install. Running `brew link opencode-v2` by hand would bring the clash back; that's the vendor's formula and can't be changed from AO.
- Installs done outside AO (running the vendor installer or `brew install` in a terminal) still overwrite OpenCode 1. AO can now only explain that and give repair steps.
- Updating an installer-based OpenCode 2 install from AO was already unsupported and still is.
- The Homebrew and installer flows haven't been exercised end to end on a real machine.

title: feat(search): search file contents and chats from the command palette
body:
Code changes: +4083 -71  
Tests: +1614 -34  
Others: +721 -1 (generated OpenAPI spec, `schema.ts` and sqlc; `go.mod`/`go.sum`; i18n catalogs)

## What this does, in one sentence

⌘K can now search **inside files and inside chats**, not just names, and it ranks everything (settings, actions, sessions, file names, code passages, chat messages) in one list, so the thing you meant is what Enter opens.

## What you'll notice

| You type… | You get |
|---|---|
| `dark mode` | **Theme** setting first (Enter opens Settings scrolled to the Theme row, highlighted) |
| `hide sidebar`, `toggle sidbar` (typo) | **Toggle sidebar** runs |
| `where do we close the palette` | **In files** → `CommandPalette.tsx:389  closePalette();` (Enter opens the file at that line, highlighted) |
| a sentence you remember from a chat | **In chats** → the conversation, scrolled to that message |
| `resolveDataDir` | the file that **defines** it, above files that only call it |
| `tokens.css` | that exact file |

Other changes:
- About 50 settings rows and 21 shortcut actions are now searchable. Before, ⌘K had only "Global settings".
- File passages show the matched line with the matched words in bold.
- Chat messages that an edit replaced are labelled **Earlier version** and ranked lower.
- While a session's files are being indexed for the first time, the palette says **Indexing files…**.

## How it works (simple version)

There are no AI models and no vectors anywhere. It is keyword search done carefully.

1. **Names are matched in memory, in the renderer.** These are small lists (settings, actions, sessions), so the match takes under a millisecond with no network call. It tolerates typos ("sidbar"), word forms ("closing" = "close"), abbreviations ("tgl term") and synonyms through keywords ("dark mode" → Theme).
2. **Files and chats are searched by the daemon with [Bleve](https://github.com/blevesearch/bleve)**, a Go keyword-index library.
   - **Files:** each session gets an index of its worktree, cut into 40-line pieces. A search finds the right *spot* (and line), not just the right file.
   - **Chats:** one index for all chat messages. It only contains finished messages, never half-streamed ones.
3. **One scoring scale for everything.**
   - Rare words count more than common ones.
   - Exact phrases, matched words sitting close together, and code that *defines* what you typed all earn bonuses.
   - Tests, generated code, lockfiles and translation files rank lower unless you ask for them.
   - A misspelled word the project has never seen is corrected to the closest real word ("did you mean").
4. **Names first.** If what you typed clearly names a setting or action, that wins Enter. File and chat hits still list below it. They only take the top spot with strong evidence: a quoted or code-like query, an exact phrase of 3+ words, or a full file name like `tokens.css`. Without this rule, a file that merely mentioned "dark mode" beat the Theme setting.

## Performance

Measured on this repo (5,611 files, 55 MB of text) and a real chat history of about 2,000 messages, on an M4 Pro:

| What | Number |
|---|---|
| Name matching (settings, actions, sessions) | **< 1 ms**, in the renderer |
| Search over files + chats | **2–10 ms** (median) per query |
| Building a session's file index the first time | **about 9 s**, in the background; file *names* are searchable immediately |
| Keeping it fresh after edits | only changed files are re-read, detected by size + modified time; a search checks for edits at most every 2 s and waits at most 250 ms |
| Catching up on new chat messages | every 2 s, from the last checkpoint |
| File index on disk | about **42 MB** for this repo, under `~/.ao/data/search` (no word positions, which saves about 2/3) |
| Memory | build is batched; the index is memory-mapped by the OS |
| Limits | at most 8 session indexes open at once, at most 24 kept on disk (least recently used are removed), files over 512 KB are found by name only, binaries and minified files are skipped |

All indexes are **derived data**. Deleting `~/.ao/data/search` is always safe; they rebuild.

## Quality (did it find the right thing?)

These numbers come from the real code in this PR, on this repo and a real chat history:

| Search | Right result at #1 | In top 5 |
|---|---|---|
| Exact code / identifiers (`matchScore`, `PALETTE_FILE_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`) | 100% | 100% |
| File names (`cmdpal`, `uiStore`, `tokens.css`) | 100% | 100% |
| Plain-English questions about code | 75% | 100% |
| New plain-English questions it was never tuned on | 67% | 83% |
| A sentence you remember from a chat | **100%** | 100% |
| The same sentence with a typo | **95%** | 95% |
| A few words from a chat, in any order | 96% | 100% |

For app controls in the full palette (names and content mixed), the right control opened on Enter 91% of the time with the names-first rule, versus 40% without it.

**Honest limit:** without vectors, a question that shares *no* words (or synonyms) with the code can miss. For example, "in sync with settings" won't find code that says "in step".

## What changed

**Backend**
- `internal/service/search` (new):
  - the file and chat indexes
  - query parsing, retrieval and the reranker
  - spelling correction
  - fuzzy file-name matching
- `GET /api/v1/search`:
  - parameters `q`, `sessionId`, `kinds` (`fileNames,fileContent,messages`); at most 20 hits per group
  - the response carries only what the palette reads: hits and whether the session's file index is still building
  - highlight offsets are UTF-16, so JavaScript can slice them directly
- Wiring in `daemon.go`:
  - the daemon starts the chat catch-up loop and closes indexes on shutdown
  - if the index can't open, the route answers 501 and nothing else is affected
- Storage:
  - migration `20261022080719423` adds an index on `conversation_messages(updated_at, id)`, so catching up is cheap
  - new sqlc queries and store methods
  - chat hits use the **same visibility rule as the transcript** (active edit branch, rolled-back turns hidden)
- `SessionService.SearchWorkspace` lists the same files the workspace browser shows, without the git status work.

**Frontend**
- `lib/palette-search.ts` (new): the name scorer and the names-first rule.
- `lib/palette-registry.ts` (new): searchable settings rows and shortcut actions, which follow the same visibility rules as Settings.
- `CommandPalette.tsx`: "In files" and "In chats" groups, matched lines with bold words, and the indexing status row.
- Opening results:
  - a file opens at its line, which is highlighted for 2 seconds (`ui-store`, `SessionView`, `ReadOnlyFileView`)
  - a chat opens scrolled to the message, with the matched text highlighted (`ui-store`, `SessionChatSurface`, `ChatWorkspace`)
  - a settings row opens its page scrolled to that row, highlighted for 2 seconds (`lib/settings-focus.ts`, `SettingsDialog`)
  - shortcut actions run after the palette closes (`useAppShortcut` now has an in-renderer dispatcher)
- New labels are translated into all 8 languages.

**Dependency:** `github.com/blevesearch/bleve/v2` v2.6.1 (pure Go, no CGO). Bleve requires cobra v1.10.2, a patch bump from v1.10.1.

## Testing

- **Backend:**
  - new unit tests for analysis, query parsing, scoring, spelling, file-name matching and snippets
  - service tests for indexing, edits, deletes, reopening, chat streaming/settling/editing/deletion, older edit branches and phrase search
  - store tests on real SQLite, including edit-branch visibility
  - controller tests

title: fix(sessions): start tasks before the generated name arrives
body:
Code changes: +187 -719\
Tests: +255 -768\
Others: +50 -59 (generated sqlc, docs, CI test filter)

## What

New tasks no longer wait for their generated name. The worktree stays in its `<session-id>` folder, setup and the agent start straight away, and after launch a background step renames only the branch to `ao/<slug>/root` and applies the title. Until that lands (at most 30 s), the desktop keeps showing the existing naming shimmer, so only the generated branch name is ever shown. The folder move, its journal, recovery and repair, and the pre-launch setup checkpoint they needed are removed.

## Why

#6811 renamed the branch **and moved the folder** before setup or the agent could run. That caused two problems:

1. **Starts fail.** Clicking **Create task** before the speculative worktree finishes fails the start with `workspace: task naming session no longer accepts this workspace`. `nameTaskWorkspace` passed a copy of the session row read before `awaitTaskPreparation` as the expected path. The preparation then published the real path, so the guarded save matched no row. On one maintainer machine, 3 of the 11 named chat starts since Oct 18 failed this way. The lab reproduces it 5/5.

   ```
   1.  dialog opens   speculative worktree starts (git fetch + worktree add)
   2.  Create task    row promoted; spawn copies it        -> copy.workspace_path = ''
   3.  preparation    publishes workspace_path = .../<session-id>
   4.  naming         moves folder -> .../<slug>
   5.  save           WHERE workspace_path IN ('', copy '', new) -> 0 rows -> start fails
   ```

2. **Every start waits for a model call.** Setup and the agent waited for naming: 6.9 s median on Opus 5.5 in the lab, and the full 20 s deadline when the call stalls.

## How

- `session_manager`: naming runs under the daemon context. `nameTaskBranchLater` runs after the controller launches, on both the sync and async paths. It waits for the name, renames, compare-and-swaps the branch (`SetSessionTaskBranch`), then writes the title. The title write fires the session change event, so the UI refetch already sees the new branch.
- `gitworktree.RenameTaskBranch`: `git branch -m` in every repository of the task, all-or-nothing, with a numeric suffix on collision. It refuses once the checkout has left the temporary branch, pushed it, or created refs under its namespace. AO attributes PRs by that namespace (`sessionBranchPrefixes`), so a later rename would orphan them.
- If the row no longer carries the temporary branch, the Git rename is put back.
- `session-branch.ts` (second commit): keeps a young session's temporary branch behind the naming shimmer, bounded at 30 s so a skipped rename never shimmers forever.
- Deleted: the folder move (4 per-OS files), the move journal, `RecoverTaskWorkspace` / `RepairTaskWorkspace`, the retry and reconcile recovery passes, `SetSessionNamedWorkspace`, and the setup checkpoint with its `interruptedClientSetup` startup cleanup.

### Behaviour changes to review

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Worktree folder | `<slug>` | `<session-id>`; only the branch is short |
| Branch in the first seconds | hidden behind the naming shimmer | still hidden behind the naming shimmer until the rename lands (at most 30 s) |
| Agent and setup wait for naming | yes (up to 20 s) | no |
| Naming fails or times out | fallback slug; start waited | fallback slug; start did not wait |
| Daemon restarts before the name arrives | journal finishes the move | temporary branch kept |
| Agent already branched from or pushed the temporary branch | n/a (named before launch) | temporary branch kept |
| Retry of a failed start | recovers the naming | keeps the temporary branch |
| "Run setup script" row | every named task | only projects with setup commands |

Known gaps:
- The naming call boots its own provider host alongside the agent's. On a heavily loaded machine this slowed the agent boot in 2 of 3 recording takes (9.7–10.8 s against about 5 s). Possible follow-up: start naming once the controller is up, or use a lighter naming call.
- A full-row `UpdateSession` landing in the same millisecond as the branch write could revert it. All 15 lab sessions ended with the DB branch equal to the checkout's HEAD.
- A branch-only change does not fire `sessions_cdc_update`. A session that keeps an explicit title (CLI `--name`) shows the new branch on its next session event.

## Testing

### Recordings: desktop dev app, same UI code, `main` daemon on the left

Both apps ran side by side under the same machine load (load average about 96). Each clip shows the median take per build, and every take is listed. The timer starts at the **Create task** click. The GIFs play at 2x; the MP4s are real time.

**Typical start: type the task, then Create task** ([MP4](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/8ea785ce8abf97f42586e1076a4d279d82007414/typical.mp4))

![typical start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/8ea785ce8abf97f42586e1076a4d279d82007414/typical.gif)

| Take | Before: agent running | After: agent running | After: branch renamed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 19.4 s | 13.4 s | 18.1 s |
| 2 | 23.8 s | **12.6 s** (shown) | 17.3 s |
| 3 | 17.2 s | 5.7 s | 10.0 s |

Take 1 is the one shown for "before". In every take "before" waited 11.4–13.2 s for naming; "after" waited 0 s.

**Create task right after opening the dialog: the reported failure** ([MP4](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/8ea785ce8abf97f42586e1076a4d279d82007414/immediate.mp4))

| 2 | failed at 13.0 s, same error | agent running at 17.1 s on `ao/dark-mode-2/root` |

The recordings above predate this commit, so they still show `ao/repo-after-4/root` in the checklist for a few seconds.

### Headless A/B: 30 real starts

Claude Code with Opus 5.5 on a fresh clone of this repo, with a real `git fetch` from GitHub, interleaving the two builds. Median time from Create to the agent running with the prompt (min–max):

| Start | Before | After |

| Worktree prepared while typing | 10.3 s (9.2–11.0) | **3.0 s** (2.9–3.2) |
| Cold, nothing prepared | 9.9 s (9.4–11.8) | **8.3 s** (7.8–8.6) |
| Create right after opening | **0/5 started** | 5/5 started, 10.4 s |

- All 15 "after" sessions were renamed, kept their `<session-id>` folder, and had the DB branch equal to the checkout's HEAD.

### Edge cases on a live daemon

- **Agent branched before the name arrived:** rename skipped, temporary branch kept, title still applied.
- **Session killed while naming:** no rename and no stray branch.
- **Daemon restarted while naming:** temporary branch kept, session came back ready, DB and Git agree.

### Automated

- New or updated tests:
  - `TestTaskNamingAfterAgentLaunch`: chat async, chat sync and TUI, each prepared and cold.
  - `TestTaskNamingAfterLatePreparedWorkspace`: regression test for the failure above.
