title: fix(mobile): load chat render pages on iOS over the tunnel
body: Code changes: +18 -1\ Tests: +19 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What On iOS, html_render pages in chat (#6982) stayed on their loading skeleton when the phone reached the desktop through the tunnel. They now load. Android was not affected. | Before (iOS) | After (iOS) | |---|---| | | | ## Why The frame's WebView only lets the render page itself load (`isRenderPageLoad` in `onShouldStartLoadWithRequest`), and it compared URLs as exact strings. `httpBase` always writes the port, so over the tunnel the page URL is `https://.trycloudflare.com:443/api/v1/sessions/…/renders/…`. iOS asks `onShouldStartLoadWithRequest` about the **initial** load too, and passes the URL as WebKit canonicalized it: default port dropped, host lowercased. That no longer matched, so the guard refused the page. WebKit cancels a refused navigation without an error. react-native-webview reports neither `onLoadEnd` nor `onError` for it, so the frame never left its skeleton and never fell back to "Couldn't load · Tap to retry". Android doesn't consult `onShouldStartLoadWithRequest` for the initial load, so it always worked. LAN and Tailscale IPs on port 3011 also worked on iOS, because nothing in that URL changes when canonicalized. ## How `isRenderPageLoad` now compares both URLs in canonical form: scheme and host lowercased, `:80`/`:443` dropped for http/https, fragment ignored. The path still has to match exactly, so a different origin, scheme, port, or path is refused as before. It parses by hand because React Native's `URL` doesn't expose host and port. Not included: the frame still has no timeout for a load that never reports an outcome. With this fix the known cause is gone; a timeout that switches to "Couldn't load" would be a separate safeguard. ## Testing - `renderFrameModel.test.ts`: new cases for the tunnel URL with `:443`, `:80`, mixed-case hosts, and a Tailscale MagicDNS name; plus refusal cases (other scheme, port, host, path, path case). The canonicalization case failed before the fix. - Reproduced on an iOS 26.5 simulator (Debug build, paired through a read-only loopback proxy) by pairing with host `LocalHost`. Logging showed iOS asking about `http://localhost:3226/…`, the guard returning `false` for both renders, no `onLoadEnd`/`onError`, and the on-screen frame stuck on its skeleton (Before). With the fix, the same setup allows the load, both pages report their heights, and they paint (After). - Mobile CI locally on Node 20: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (233 files, 2385 tests) all pass. - Not tested: a physical iPhone over the actual tunnel. The simulator repro uses host lowercasing, which goes through the same WebKit canonicalization step as the dropped `:443`. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(desktop): confirm Cmd+Q with a "Quit AO?" dialog on macOS
body:
## Summary

A stray ⌘Q no longer quits AO straight away. It opens a **"Quit AO?"** dialog first.

- **Quit ⏎** (focused by default, so Return confirms) quits. **Cancel / Esc** dismisses.
- When the menu bar icon is up (the normal macOS case), Quit only closes the window and AO keeps running there, so the dialog says: *"AO will keep running in the background. You can reopen it from the menu bar."* Without the tray it asks *"Are you sure you want to quit AO?"* instead. Main sends `keepsRunning` with the request, computed the same way `desktopQuit` decides to keep the app alive.
- Pressing ⌘Q again while the dialog is open also quits.
- These still quit at once: choosing **Quit** from the app menu with the mouse, Dock → Quit, tray → Quit, and ⌘Q when the window is hidden or minimised (there's nowhere to show the dialog).
- The red close button is unchanged. On macOS it only closes the window and AO keeps running.

### Design
`QuitConfirmDialog` is built on the shared settings-dialog frame and tokens (`settingsDialogContentClass`, `settingsDialogFooterClass`, `footer-primary`), the same family as `ConfirmDialog`. It follows light/dark and every style theme: Quit takes each theme's accent. The layout is the title and question, then a hairline above a right-aligned footer with a quiet **Cancel Esc** and an accent **Quit ⏎**. Focus returns to where it was when the dialog closes.

### How
- `frontend/src/main/menu.ts`: the macOS app menu no longer uses Electron's `quit` role, which maps to `NSApp terminate:` and can't be intercepted. It has a plain `Command+Q` item that reports whether the accelerator fired it.
- `frontend/src/main/quit-confirm.ts`: a small controller. ⌘Q requests a confirm, a second ⌘Q while one is pending quits, and the shell's answer resolves it. A shell reload or window close clears the pending state.
- IPC: `app:quit-confirm-request` (main → shell) and `app:quit-confirm-result` (shell → main, sender-checked). They're exposed as `onQuitConfirmRequest` / `resolveQuitConfirm` on the bridge.
- Strings are added in all 8 locales.

The existing quit flow is unchanged: the unsaved-draft prompt, macOS tray "close window and leave the Dock", and cleanup.

## Tests
- `quit-confirm.test.ts`, `QuitConfirmDialog.test.tsx` (focus, Return/Esc/Cancel), a menu test for the Quit item, and a shell integration test (open → Quit/Cancel → result sent to main).
- `tsc --noEmit` and `typecheck:e2e`: no errors in `frontend`.
- Full frontend vitest: 8912 passed. Two files fail locally for environment reasons only (`browser-profile-import`: better-sqlite3 bindings not built under Node 23; `remote-proxy`: hook timeout). Both passed in CI on the previous push.
- Visual check: a throwaway Playwright script opened the dialog in the renderer across all 9 style themes in dark and light. Quit was focused and the theme was applied in each one.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Not yet tried in the packaged desktop app. Worth a manual ⌘Q → Return / Esc / second ⌘Q check.
- Windows/Linux menus are untouched.

title: fix(cloud): load Chat model choices once the worker connects, not on a timer
body:
## Problem

On a new or resumed Coder session, cloud Chat shows **"Model choices unavailable: The session worker is not connected."** under the composer, even though the chat itself works.

The composer asked the worker for its model catalog as soon as Chat opened. A session still starting has no worker yet, so the request returned `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The composer then woke the session and retried every 500 ms, 20 times (about 10 s), gave up, and never asked again. Freestyle wakes within that window. A Coder workspace takes 1 to 3 minutes to boot, so the error stayed until the user left the session and came back.

Seen on staging, session `47f69d09` (Coder, Claude Chat):

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:42:48 | Session created |
| 13:42:49 to 13:43:09 | 21 `chat-models` requests, all 409; the picker gives up |
| 13:45:10 | Worker connected |
| 13:52 | User reopened the session; `chat-models` returned 200 |

## Fix

The composer now waits for the worker instead of a timer:

- **Fetch only while connected.** The catalog is requested only while the session reports `runtimeConnected`. That flag is the same live `ao_worker_connections` row the request needs, and the session list polls it every 5 s. The catalog loads as soon as a worker connects, however long the boot takes. A reconnect the session list sees refreshes it, since the query is always stale.
- **Codex catalog before the first turn (worker).** `chat.models` ran a bare `codex app-server` without the session's Codex credential or `CODEX_HOME`, which only a turn's command sets up. On Freestyle that failed with `WORKER_OPERATION_FAILED` until the first turn. Codex discovery now uses the same agent command as Claude discovery: the running agent's, or one built by `AgentCommandFactory` with the credential (`Supervisor.modelDiscoveryCommand`). It also runs from the worker's own directory while the checkout does not exist yet.
- **A slow first catalog read.** A worker's first Claude catalog read can outlast the 12 s request expiry (`TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT`) while it prepares the agent's tools. The composer asks again up to three times before reporting it.
- **A worker leaving mid-request is not an error.** The request is retried with backoff only while the list still reports the worker connected. This covers a quick pause and resume that a poll missed. Once the list reports it gone, retrying stops and the query waits for the next connection. `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE` is never shown under the composer.
- **Wake once.** Opening Chat wakes an idle-paused session once, as before. An open Chat tab no longer wakes a session again after it idle-pauses, so leaving Chat open does not defeat idle pause.
- **A model picked during boot is kept if the worker can run it.** The composer adopts the worker's native model when the catalog arrives, unless the user picked one since the catalog was last read. That baseline used to be "when the request started". The request now starts at connect, so it is "when the catalog was last read", and a model picked while a Coder session boots is no longer replaced. A pick from the local list that the worker's catalog does not have is replaced by the worker's model, so the next turn does not fail.
- **No stale errors.** A model error is shown only while a worker is connected, so an error kept from an earlier worker does not reappear on a remount.
- **Deleted sessions.** A session deleted under the composer still says "This session was deleted. Restore it to continue."

The change is in the renderer (`CloudSessionChatSurface.tsx`) and in worker model discovery. There is no control-plane or API change. It works the same on every sandbox provider, because it depends only on the connection flag.

## Tests

- `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx` (55 of 55). The new cases are:
  - waits for the worker, with no error and no request until it connects;
  - does not wake a connected session, or one that pauses while Chat is open;
  - retries a worker that left mid-request only while it is still reported connected, then stops;
  - retries a timed-out first read three times, then reports it;
  - hides an error kept from a worker that is gone;
  - deleted then restored, and deleted under the composer;
  - a model picked during boot is kept if the worker has it, and replaced if it does not.
- Worker:
  - `TestDiscoverCodexModelsRunsWithTheAgentsCodexHome`
  - `TestDiscoverCodexModelsBeforeTheCheckoutExists`
  - `TestModelDiscoveryCommand*`
  - `go test ./internal/workerexec/ ./internal/workertransport/` passes.
- Each new test was checked against the code without its fix and fails there.

## Staging validation

Passed on staging (control plane :301) for Freestyle and Coder, Claude and Codex: new sessions, boot-time model picks, pause while open, idle-paused sessions, Terminal to Chat, delete and restore, failed Setup. Details: https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7075#issuecomment-6347020370

title: [Bug]: Fail closed when Cursor rejects an explicit Fast setting
body:
### What went wrong?

When an explicitly parameterized Cursor model includes `fast=false`, AO currently marks the `fast` session option optional. The ACP driver treats an `InvalidParams` response for optional settings as a reason to continue startup, so a provider rejection can leave its default Fast setting active without telling the user.

**Expected:** An explicit `fast` setting is required. If Cursor rejects it, AO fails startup with the provider error instead of silently continuing under another setting.

**Actual:** Cursor `fast` is currently optional, so an invalid-params response can be swallowed.

**Scope:** Separate from [#6797](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6797), which addresses native parameterized model controls and Cursor preference precedence.

**Evidence:** Live ACP inspection showed Cursor accepts the string-valued `ValueId` `false` and returns current `fast: "false"`; the wire encoding already works on the verified provider. Source inspection found explicit `fast` is marked optional, and the ACP driver intentionally swallows invalid-params errors for optional settings. This issue is limited to making explicit Fast fail closed when rejected. The earlier source-only assumption that the ACP Boolean request field was needed was incorrect and has been removed from the patch.

title: fix(httpd): reject untrusted browser access to terminals and APIs
body:
Code changes: +187 -82  
Tests: +635 -19  
Others: +26 -0  

## Problem and fix

Fixes #6687.

Workspace previews and unrelated loopback pages could create a shell and attach to the terminal mux. Reject untrusted browser requests before REST handlers or WebSocket upgrades, using exact configured renderer origins instead of blanket loopback trust. The primary listener stays bound to loopback and unauthenticated for native clients.

- Preserve packaged/development renderer access, CLI access, and the React Native mux Origin only after successful bearer authentication on the authenticated listener. Preview cookies grant only preview-file reads.
- Sandbox legacy API-origin documents without same-origin authority. Keep ordinary isolated previews interactive and preserve application-supplied CSP when the remote proxy removes the host-added API sandbox on its separate preview origins.
- Check browser origins before the remote proxy strips Origin or injects credentials. Static preview hosts cannot fall back to token-prefixed daemon sockets, even with a known token.
- Add real-router shell/mux regressions, authenticated mobile-listener echo/reconnect/two-viewer checks, an HTTPS static-preview fallback test, and actual Electron/Chromium transport verification wired into CI.

## Review follow-up

Addressed both P1 findings from @ronishrohan in `f0dea9043` (rebased from `e4624f4fc`):

- Protected local/proxied media requests now use anonymous CORS so Chromium supplies the trusted renderer Origin. Covered file media (image/audio/video), chat thumbnails/full-size images, Markdown images, image diffs, read-only file images, and artifact image cards. External image URLs retain their existing loading mode.
- Permit no-Origin GET/HEAD only for the exact sandboxed render-document route in both the daemon and the remote control proxy. Render publishing/check/artifact APIs, workspace blobs and terminal access keep the browser guard.
- Expanded the actual Electron fixture to exercise media elements, sandboxed iframe navigation and render-check window navigation through the real router and production remote proxy. It also verifies foreign and no-CORS media rejection and that loaded renders cannot create terminals. This remains a transport regression fixture, not a complete viewer GUI walkthrough.

## Rebase onto current main

Rebased onto `b087ce794`, which includes #7105. Preserve its separate, stricter terminal mux policy and reuse the validated LAN bearer context for both REST and mux. Keep the proxy's validated native WebSocket forwarding, HTTPS static-preview token fallback regression, both Electron CI checks, and the renderer media/render fixes requested in review. Explicitly install Electron before capturing its executable path so lazy-download diagnostics cannot corrupt the command.

Post-rebase validation: complete HTTP/terminal/mobile-bridge race suites, all 68 proxy tests, both real Electron regressions, backend build/vet, E2E typecheck, workflow YAML and diff checks pass. Complete frontend suite passes: 520 files, 8,985 tests passed, seven skipped. Pinned new-change lint passes with zero issues. Full production TypeScript checking also passes locally. Fresh remote checks were started; Linux/Xvfb, Docker/native-platform coverage and the broader baseline gaps below remain separate verification requirements.

## Verified locally

- **Exploit baseline:** unchanged main allows hostile preview/loopback origins to create a fake shell and attach an existing fake terminal. Candidate rejects both with zero service/attachment effects. All terminals are in memory; no OS payload is executed.
- Complete affected HTTP/preview race suites pass after the review follow-up. New-change pinned lint and E2E TypeScript checking pass. The complete frontend suite passes locally: **519 files, 8,959 tests passed, six skipped**. All **67 remote-proxy tests** pass, including the actual HTTPS static-preview token-path regression.

- Mobile typecheck and the **complete mobile suite pass: 2,385 tests across 233 files**, using a clean environment.

title: fix(chat): publish a replacement orchestrator's provider handle to the inherited branch
body:
Code changes: +7 -1\
Tests: +317 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A replacement orchestrator that is still provisioning when it starts now publishes its own provider handle to the project conversation it inherits, so the session can be resumed after a daemon restart.

## Why

Addresses #6606.

`Service.Start` does not reserve a provider boundary for a session's first controller (`queuedBeforeFirstController`). That is right for a new conversation, which has no provider history to fence off. A replacement orchestrator inherits the project conversation instead, and its active branch still holds the previous orchestrator's session and provider handle. With no boundary reserved, the controller-ready step records the new handle on the session (`MarkSpawned`) but never on the branch. Nothing notices while the controller is live, because the handle check only runs on resume. After a restart, resume compares the branch's handle with the session's and refuses: `active conversation branch provider handle "…" does not match session handle "…"`.

Reproduced on current `main` with a real daemon (isolated data dir, real Claude Code orchestrators): after a replacement that was provisioning, the active branch belonged to an earlier orchestrator, and after a restart startup reconcile failed with the error above, the session showed `exited`, and `ao session resume-agent` returned the 500.

## How

- `service/chat/service.go`: `branchHoldsAnotherSessionsHandle` is true when the active branch carries a provider handle owned by a different session. The first-controller exemption no longer applies then, so `Start` reserves the boundary and `CommitChatSpawn` publishes the new session's handle on a child branch, as it already does for a replacement that is not on its first start. The strict handle check on resume is unchanged.

Not in this PR:

- A database that is already in this state is not repaired. Its sessions still fail the resume check. The workaround in the issue (fix the branch row, or terminate the session and create a new orchestrator) still applies.
- #6639 and #6695 describe sessions that cannot resume after a restart through different mechanisms. This does not address them.

## Testing

- Real daemon, built from `main` and from this branch, each with its own data dir: spawn an orchestrator and let it finish a turn, slow provisioning with a `post-create` hook, replace the orchestrator and send a message while the replacement is provisioning (accepted as `queued`), then restart the daemon.
  - `main`: the active branch stays on an earlier orchestrator's session and handle. After the restart reconcile fails with the mismatch, the session is `exited`, and `resume-agent` returns 500.
  - This branch: the active branch belongs to the replacement with its own handle. After the restart the session comes back `active` with no mismatch in the logs, and the queued turn is preserved (2 completed, 1 running).
- New tests in `orchestrator_replacement_handle_test.go`: the replacement publishes its handle and resumes after a restart; its queued opening prompt survives; an inherited conversation with no history still starts on the root without a boundary; a failed provider start leaves the inherited head alone and a retry publishes the handle.
- Reverting the fix makes three of the four fail with the error from the issue. Forcing `branchHoldsAnotherSessionsHandle` to always be true does not fail any test, so the "owned by another session" condition is not pinned by a test of its own.
- Mirrored the Go CI job locally on this branch: gofmt, build, vet, and `go test -race` over all packages including the sharded chat, session manager and SQLite ones. All passed except `TestDarwinPTYCloseDoesNotWaitOutAShellThatIgnoresSIGTERM` in the `conpty` package, a macOS timing test (`Close took 500.5ms` against a 500ms grace) that is unrelated, failed the same way on an earlier branch of mine, and passes when run alone. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 under Go 1.27.1 reports one `revive` `time-naming` finding in `session_manager/manager.go` that is on `main` and not touched here.
- Not tested: the exact claude-code to opencode switch from the issue (only claude-code and codex were available), Windows and Linux, and TUI-mode orchestrators.

## What

A skill (`.agents/skills/ao-agent-harness/`) that takes any coding-agent CLI from a link to an integrated, audited AO harness. Nothing in it is specific to one harness: everything harness-specific lives in one contract entry per harness (`assets/local-contracts.json`). Codex and Claude Code are the worked examples.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | The workflow: intake → compatibility → build → contract → live audit → UI audit → fix and hand off |
| `scripts/harness_intake.mjs` | Given a link: already in AO? open PR? upstream OS/installer facts and the local `--help` |
| `scripts/harness_touchpoints.mjs` | Every AO file a harness must be wired into, and where a similar harness did it (`--like`). This includes its own `GetAgentHooks` and the `activitydispatch` mapping, without which session status is never reported |
| `scripts/audit.mjs` | Builds AO from the checkout, runs an isolated daemon, and audits each harness live |
| `scripts/ui_audit.mjs` | Drives the desktop app (via CDP) with a screenshot at every step: Harness page, install, health, models, login, New Task, spawn TUI/Chat |
| `scripts/run_local.sh` | `doctor`, `audit`, `ui` launcher |
| `assets/contract-template.json`, `assets/local-contracts.json` | The per-harness contract |
| `references/integration-guide.md` | Compatibility table, build order, and the mistakes that failed earlier harness PRs |

`.gitignore` un-ignores the skill folder; `AGENTS.md` gets a one-line pointer.

### The audit

Checks, per harness:

| Area | Checks |
|---|---|
| CLI | Installed, version, login, model list |
| AO | Registered, installed, login verified, models |
| TUI | Spawn, first prompt once in the worktree, AO system prompt, AGENTS.md, session status tracked by hooks, session ID, follow-up, usage, Kill stops a running command, native restore, history after restore |
| Chat | Spawn, first prompt, system prompt, AGENTS.md, follow-up, models and switching, Kill/restore of the same conversation, history |
| Roles | A worker and an orchestrator each name their own role |

Output:
- `report.md`
- per-check evidence JSON
- daemon and run logs

The report's **Fix** section sorts every failure into four groups:
- **AO implementation**, with the source folders to open
- **Contract or upstream CLI**
- **Machine setup**
- **Needs the user**

This replaces #6509, which grew to 39 files and ~11k lines. The tests, the fix-loop machinery and most of the references are dropped.

## Verification

No test files are included; the skill is verified by running it. A live run of `audit.mjs` against Codex on this branch (stopped part-way) passed:
- every CLI check
- every AO check
- TUI: spawn, prompt, worktree, system prompt, AGENTS.md, activity, session ID, follow-up and usage

It found one AO implementation failure: `tui_stop`. After Kill, the command Codex was running kept going and wrote its delayed file, so AO does not stop the agent's child processes. That's an existing AO bug, not part of this PR.

title: fix(lifecycle): terminate sessions whose runtime is dead while paused
body:
Code changes: +9 -2\
Tests: +102 -0\

## What

A session whose runtime probe comes back conclusively dead is now terminated even while its activity is paused in `blocked` or `waiting_input`.

## Why

Fixes #6726. `runtimeClearlyDead` treated a sticky activity state as recent activity, so a session that died while paused was never cleaned up: the agent that would have cleared the pause is gone, and nothing else moves it out of the sticky state.

## How

- `runtimeClearlyDead` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/runtime.go`): a `ProbeDead` result now outranks stickiness. Stickiness still only stops *time* from demoting a paused agent.
- Failed and alive probes never override a sticky state, so the "failed probes are not proof of death" principle is unchanged.
- One sentence added to the key principle in `docs/architecture.md`.

title: fix(review): use a fresh session id when a reviewer conversation exists
body:
Code changes: +40 -4\
Tests: +260 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A fresh claude-code reviewer launch no longer reuses a session id that already has a Claude conversation behind it.

## Why

Fixes #6642. When a review is re-triggered with an override (`--harness`, `--model`, `--agent`), AO starts a fresh reviewer and pins `--session-id` to the reviewer's deterministic id, the same id the first round used. Claude refuses to start a new session on an id that is already in use, so the second round never starts. A plain re-trigger without overrides already resumes the existing conversation and is unaffected.

## How

- `ports.ReviewInvocation` gains `LaunchID`, filled from `spec.LaunchID` in `review/launcher.go`.
- `claudecode.Reviewer.freshSessionID` keeps the deterministic id unless `NativeConversationExists` reports a conversation for it; then it uses `SessionUUID(reviewerID + "/" + launchID)`. That id is returned as `AgentSessionID`, persisted as before, and later rounds resume it.
- Preflight calls (no launch id) skip the history probe.
- `review.go` is untouched, so this does not overlap with #6891.
- Out of scope: marking a reviewer that dies at launch as `failed`.
- Known limitation: if a project overrides `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, the probe looks in the default config directory. The existing resume path has the same limitation.

## Testing

- `claudecode_test.go`: `TestReviewCommandStartsNewConversationWhenReviewerIDIsTaken`, `TestReviewCommandKeepsReviewerConversationForFirstLaunch`, `TestReviewCommandWithoutLaunchSkipsHistoryProbe`, `TestReviewRestoreCommandResumesFreshLaunchConversation`, `TestReviewCommandEmitsFreshSessionIDWhenTranscriptExists`.
- `review/override_test.go`: `TestSecondClaudeReviewRoundDoesNotReuseExistingConversation` drives a second override round end to end through the real launcher with a stub `claude`.

title: fix(sessions): harden background task branch naming
body:
Code changes: +492 -134 (115 of the additions are the migration, mostly the recreated change trigger)\
Tests: +648 -62\
Others: +109 -27 (generated sqlc and OpenAPI, `schema.ts`, docs)

## What

Follow-ups from two reviews of #7069, which renames a task's branch in the background after launch. The first review's 15 findings were reproduced on `main` with scratch tests before fixing; F5 and F10 were already in #6811. The second review (R1–R15) found that the first round's fixes were built on two things that did not hold: a fake `branch` provision step, and a lifecycle-lock write that guarded only the lifecycle's own row rewrites.

The design now has two facts on the session row:
- `branch_naming`: set from the start of naming until the rename lands or is skipped. Clients hide the temporary branch while it is set. It is written only by its own narrow setter.
- `temporary_branch`: the branch that the rename replaced. A full-row write from an older read never puts it back, and the PR observer still attributes refs under it.

## Why and how

First review (of #7069):

| # | Problem on `main` | Fix | Regression test |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Another start holding the project gate past the 30 s rename deadline dropped both the rename and the generated title | The deadline starts once the gate is held. The title is written before the gate, which it does not need | `TestTaskNamingWaitsForGateBeforeDeadline` |
| F2 | A full-row write from a read taken before the rename wrote the temporary branch back | `UpdateSession` keeps the current branch when asked to write the recorded `temporary_branch`. It covers every full-row writer: lifecycle, provider switch, controller commit | `TestTaskRenameSurvivesStaleRowWrites` |
| F3, F11 | A PR from a branch the agent made or remembered under the temporary name (`ao/<id>/fix`, workspace `ao/<id>-fix`) stopped being attributed after the rename | `matchSession` also owns the session's recorded temporary branch. With that, only an already-pushed temporary branch still blocks the rename, because the agent's next plain `git push` would name another remote branch | `TestMatchSession_RenamedTaskKeepsTemporaryNamespace`, `TestRenameTaskBranchGuard`, `TestTaskNamingRenamesBesideAgentBranches` |
| F4 | The undo after a rejected row write reused the expired deadline, or went through the suffixing rename and landed on `ao/<id>-2/root` | New exact `RevertTaskBranch`, which restores each repository's own original branch | `TestTaskNamingUndoesRenameTheRowRejects`, `TestRevertTaskBranchIsExact` |
| F5 | A fallback slug equal to the session ID collided with the task's own branch and got a `-2` suffix (also in #6811) | A rename to the current name is a no-op | `TestTaskNamingKeepsMatchingTemporaryName`, `TestRenameTaskBranchToItsOwnName` |
| F6, F7, F14, F15 | The desktop guessed "name pending" from the branch shape and a 30 s clock started at creation. It showed the temporary branch on slow starts, did not re-render when the window ended, and shimmered for sessions that are never renamed. The test file also had a formatting slip | The desktop and mobile app read the daemon's `branchNaming` flag | `TestTaskNamingBranchNamingFlag`, `command-palette.test.ts`, `sessionStartup.test.ts` |
| F8 | A branch-only rename emitted no change event, so the UI kept the temporary branch whenever no title was written (every fallback name) | `sessions_cdc_update` now also fires on `branch` and `branch_naming` changes | `TestTaskRenameSurvivesStaleRowWrites` |
| F9 | The session row and the child `session_worktrees` rows were updated separately | `SetSessionTaskBranch` updates both in one transaction | `TestSetSessionTaskBranchMovesWorktreeRows`, `TestTaskNamingRenamesEveryRepository` |
| F10 | A daemon shutdown could kill `git branch -m` partway through renaming a live agent's branch (also in #6811) | Git renames run without a cancellable context, and a stopping daemon skips the rename | (reasoned; the rename path checks the daemon context first) |
| F12 | When undoing a partial multi-repository rename also failed, the result claimed the old branches | The result reports the branches Git holds, and the row records them | `TestRenameTaskBranchReportsFailedUndo` |
| F13 | No upgrade path for state left by #6811 builds | A retry recreates a saved worktree that no longer exists. Startup again rolls back synchronous starts that a #6811 build checkpointed mid-setup (marked as a legacy path to delete later) | `TestRetryRecreatesMissingWorktree`, `TestStartupHealthCleansOnlyUncommittedSetup` |

Second review (of the first version of this PR):

| # | Problem | Fix | Regression test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Full-row writers other than the lifecycle (TUI provider switch, controller commit) could still put back the temporary branch or the old title | The store guard (F2) covers them. `UpdateSession` no longer writes `display_name`, which only narrow writes change. The lifecycle-lock method is removed | `TestTaskRenameSurvivesStaleRowWrites` |
| R2 | When the undo failed, the row kept the temporary branch while Git held the new one | A partial rename records the root branch Git holds, and a failed undo retries the row write | `TestTaskNamingRecordsSplitBranches` |
| R3 | The temporary branch showed between the worktree step and the post-launch branch step | `branchNaming` is set when naming starts | `TestTaskNamingBranchNamingFlag` |
| R4 | The branch stayed hidden for as long as another start held the project gate | If the rename has to wait for the gate, it clears the flag first; the rename still lands after | `TestTaskNamingWaitsForGateBeforeDeadline` |
| R5, R10, R12, R13 | The fake `branch` step raced checklist writes, fired an extra mobile haptic, broke a memo, and needed special cases in every checklist consumer | The step is gone: one narrow flag | (by design) |
| R6 | A workspace project's bare `ao/<id>` branch, named after its own ID, became `ao/<id>-2/root` | The own-name check compares namespaces | `TestRenameTaskBranchToItsOwnName` |
| R7 | The async start held the project gate through the first-turn dispatch | The gate is released right after launch | `TestAsyncStartNamesOnlyAfterSuccess` |
| R8 | A retry that recreated a missing worktree showed no worktree or setup steps | The retry shows the whole checklist | `TestRetryRecreatesMissingWorktree` |
| R9 | A start that failed after launch was still renamed, and its checklist showed the naming shimmer | Naming is handed off only after a successful start, and clients ignore the flag on a failed start | `TestAsyncStartNamesOnlyAfterSuccess`, `command-palette.test.ts`, `sessionStartup.test.ts` |
| R11 | A later task named after a renamed task's old temporary branch made PR matching ambiguous | Temporary-branch matches rank below current-branch matches | `TestMatchSession_RenamedTaskKeepsTemporaryNamespace` |
| R14 | Two copies of the rename-back loop | One `moveBranches` helper | existing adapter tests |
| R15 | The observer guessed the temporary branch from the branch shape, and the orchestrator guard was untested | The observer reads the recorded `temporary_branch`, so the guess and its guard are gone | `TestMatchSession_RenamedTaskKeepsTemporaryNamespace` |

Third review (of `1449935`):

| # | Problem | Fix | Regression test |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | After a rejected row write, an undo that put the root back but failed on a child recorded the generated name for the root | `RevertTaskBranch` reports the branches Git holds, and that is what gets recorded | `TestTaskNamingRecordsSplitBranches`, `TestRevertTaskBranchReportsFailedUndo` |
| T2 | A partial rename recorded the root's branch on every repository row | `SetSessionTaskBranch` writes each repository row's own branch | `TestTaskNamingRecordsSplitBranches`, `TestSetSessionTaskBranchMovesWorktreeRows` |
| T3 | The new failed-start assertion had no finished worktree step, so it failed | The fixture has the finished worktree step that a start failing after launch has | `command-palette.test.ts` |

Other changes:
- Migration `20261022172135175_session_branch_naming` adds both columns and recreates `sessions_cdc_update`.
- `branchNaming` is in the session view (`openapi.yaml`, `schema.ts`).
- Store tests that used the title as a generic full-row change now use the model.

## Testing

- The regression tests above, plus the full `store`, `session_manager`, `lifecycle`, `observe/scm` and workspace adapter packages, ran locally.
- Frontend, mobile, typecheck and the full suites are left to CI.
- `schema.ts` was edited by hand to match the `openapi-typescript` output (one optional field), because the generator is not installed here. The `api-drift` job checks it.

title: fix(settings): show readable local time and UTC in problem reports
body:
## Summary

The **Generated** line in Report a Problem drafts (email, GitHub, Discord) printed a raw ISO timestamp:

```
Generated: 2026-10-21T20:50:24.025Z
```

It now shows the reporter's local time with its timezone, plus a UTC reference so support can line reports up without converting:

```
Generated: Oct 22, 2026, 2:20:24 AM GMT+5:30 (2026-10-21 20:50:24 UTC)
```

- New `formatReportTimestamp()` in `frontend/src/renderer/lib/report-problem.ts`; only the rendered line changes, `generatedAt` stays ISO.

title: fix(artifacts): delete a file's version history when the user deletes it
body:
## Summary

Clicking **Delete artifact** removed only the file. Its version rows in `session_artifact_versions` and the `.versions/blobs` copies of its earlier contents stayed on disk until the whole session's artifacts were deleted on archive. A user who deletes an artifact expects every copy to be gone, which is different from archiving the session.

The single-file delete now removes the file's history too:

- **New query** `DeleteSessionArtifactPathVersions`: deletes one path's version rows and returns their hashes. Includes the store method and sqlc-generated code (v1.31.1).
- **`Capturer.DeleteVersions`** (`artifactversions/delete.go`): drops the path's rows, then removes each blob no other version in the session still uses. A blob shared with another file that has identical content is kept.
- **`DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}/artifact-files`** calls `DeleteVersions` after removing the file. If that step fails, the request returns an error instead of reporting success.

`DeleteVersions` holds the capture lock. A capture that read the file before it was removed records its version first, and that version is then deleted. A capture that starts later finds no file, so nothing comes back.

Archive-time "Delete N artifacts" (`DeleteSession`) is unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestDeleteVersionsRemovesOnePathAndKeepsSharedBlobs` (real SQLite): checks that the deleted file's own blobs are removed, a blob another file still uses is kept, the other file's versions are untouched, and a later capture records nothing.
- `TestDeleteArtifactFileDeletesItsVersions`: the endpoint removes the file and its versions.
- `go test ./internal/artifactversions/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/...` passes, and `gofmt -l` is clean.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Not yet exercised by hand in the desktop app.
- If deleting the versions fails after the file was removed, the file is gone but its history remains. The request reports an error, but the UI has no listed file left to retry from.

title: feat(mobile): talk to the project orchestrator from the session list
body:
Code changes: +95 -16
Tests: +138 -0

## Bug

The mobile board's session fetch dropped every orchestrator-kind session client-side: `getSessions`
in `packages/mobile/lib/api.ts` filtered `kind !== "orchestrator"`, so a project's orchestrator was
reachable only through the project card and could not be opened from the session list where workers
live. Compounding it, `mapSession` did not carry `kind` onto `DashboardSession`, so the UI could not
have distinguished an orchestrator row if it had one.

Everything else already existed: the daemon serves orchestrator sessions on the same endpoints the
desktop board uses, `/orchestrators` is fetched separately for the project card, the chat route can
resolve orchestrator sessions, and `ChatSessionScreen` already applies orchestrator guards (the
daemon refuses renaming it).

## What changed

- `getSessions` now lists the project's one **live** orchestrator among its sessions, carrying the
  wire `kind` (`worker | orchestrator`) — reusing the field the session already has, no new API
  field. Historical orchestrator sessions (one per past kill/respawn) and terminated rows stay off
  the board: a stopped orchestrator is the project card's Start/Restart job, not a board row.
- The row is visually distinct: a small purple "Orchestrator" badge in the eyebrow line, matching
  the orchestrator's color across the app.
- Chat works end to end exactly like a worker: tap opens the conversation — streaming replies,
  approvals, compose, all existing machinery. The chat route now resolves orchestrators **before**
  sessions so `ChatSessionScreen` keeps its orchestrator guards (no rename/delete/pin) instead of
  mistaking the row for a worker.
- Row actions degrade to open/resume: the daemon refuses orchestrator renames, and Archive (a
  destructive `killSession`) has no business on a swipe rail. Pin/openPr/rename/delete are fenced
  off in `workerContextActions`.
- `workersOf` and `projectPageStats` skip orchestrator-kind rows so project card pills and project
  page counts do not double-count the orchestrator (it is already counted from its link).
- **Spawn untouched:** mobile still sends `kind: "worker"` when spawning new tasks (fenced by a
  source test).

## Tests

- `lib/api.orchestrator-board.test.ts` — orchestrator appears in the board list with its kind, dead
  history stays off, the link is still mapped for the project card.
- `lib/worker-action-model.test.ts` — orchestrator gets open (+resume when stopped) and never
  pin/rename/openPr/delete/restore.
- `lib/worker-list-row.test.tsx` — badge renders on the orchestrator row only; no swipe pin/archive
  actions on it.
- `lib/orchestrator-board.source.test.ts` — wiring fences: the live orchestrator reaches the board,

## Gates

- `npm test` (mobile vitest): 235 files, 2395 tests, all green.

title: fix(mobile): show the streaming cursor only on the newest reply
body: Code changes: +16 -2 Tests: +28 -1 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary During a long Claude Code turn, mobile chat showed a typing cursor after every text block, not only at the end of the reply being written. **Cause:** the ACP driver settles a turn's assistant messages only when the turn ends (`settleOpenItems`), so every earlier text block in a running turn still arrives with `streaming: true`. Mobile appended the `▍` glyph to each of them. Desktop never draws a glyph, so the stale flags aren't visible there. **Fix:** `streamingCursorMessageId` (in `timelineModel.ts`) picks the turn's newest item when it is a streaming assistant reply, and only that message draws the cursor. While a tool call runs after a block, no cursor shows; the Working row already says the agent is busy. ## Screenshots The same frozen running turn on the iOS simulator: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | ## Tests - `packages/mobile`: `npx vitest run`, 2389 tests pass; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. - New unit tests for `streamingCursorMessageId`; the `ChatTimeline` source test now pins the new cursor condition. - Checked in the iOS simulator against a copy of a running Claude turn served by a read-only proxy (screenshots above). ## Risks / follow-ups - Earlier blocks still carry `streaming: true` until the turn ends, so their copy button stays hidden until then. Settling each block when the next tool call starts (in the ACP driver) would fix that for every client.

title: fix(desktop): PR panel targets the checked-out branch and sets AO config apart
body:
Code changes: +119 -35  
Tests: +97 -19  
Others: +39 -0 (generated OpenAPI/TS schema, i18n strings)

Fixes #6997
Fixes #6636
Fixes #6637

## Summary

Three bugs in the inspector's **Pull requests** panel, all seen in session `ao-landing-4` (PR #52, plus draft #66 stacked on it; the checkout is `ao/ao-landing-4/stripe-policies`; the only change is an untracked `.ao/launch.json`).

- **#6636: stale root branch in the header and `ao session ls`.** The branch-state reconcile already reads the worktree's HEAD for commit and push facts. It now also records that branch as `SessionBranchState.branch`. The branch name is part of the reconcile fingerprint, so checking out a stacked branch at the same commit is still observed. `ao session ls` (BRANCH), `ao session get` and the renderer's `sessionBranchPresentation` prefer it over the recorded root, which also covers board cards, the chat header and the command palette. In the panel header, the base comes from the checked-out branch's PR, so a stacked PR reads `legal-terms-privacy → stripe-policies`. The JSON shape is additive, and the stored `branch_state` column is JSON, so no migration is needed.
- **#6997: "Commit & push to #N" named the first open PR.** `SessionInspector` now passes every open or draft PR to the panel, and the panel targets the one whose `sourceBranch` is the checked-out branch. If the session has open PRs but none for this branch, the action names the branch instead: "Commit & push to `<branch>`" / "Push to `<branch>`". The agent message then omits a PR number.
- **#6637 (middle ground only): `.ao/` files alone no longer drive Commit & push.** When *every* uncommitted file is under `.ao/`, the panel shows them as a separate **AO config · not part of the PR** row (same `GitStatusRow` primitive; Lucide `FileCog`; muted note) and offers no commit action. If project changes are present too, `.ao/` files stay in the uncommitted count and commit with them, because a launch config may be intended. `launch.json` is **not** hidden from git.

## Screenshots

Each image shows the real `SessionInspector` at the base commit (left) and on this branch (right), with ao-landing-4's PR, branch and file facts replayed through a stubbed daemon API. The harness itself is not part of the PR. The PR titles and per-PR stats (#52: 8 files +454 −4; #66: 6 files +848 −500) are copied from GitHub. The session's activity is a fixed "Idle". An earlier capture showed "Unknown" in Activity and identical stats on both cards; those came from the harness fixture, not from this change.

**ao-landing-4 as it is today** (#6636, #6637): the header shows the checked-out branch, and `.ao/launch.json` moves to the AO config row with no "Commit & push to #52".
![live](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/cedac64881611277ae1c63751ab663555f91bdf0/pr-panel-live.png?raw=true)

**Stacked branch checked out** (#6997, #6636): the action targets #66, and the header base is #66's base.
![stacked](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/cedac64881611277ae1c63751ab663555f91bdf0/pr-panel-stacked.png?raw=true)

**A branch with no PR of its own** (#6997): the action names the branch, not #52.
![unmatched](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/cedac64881611277ae1c63751ab663555f91bdf0/pr-panel-unmatched.png?raw=true)

## Tests

- New inspector tests: target the checked-out PR (#66, not #52); header shows the checked-out branch with its PR's base and no root; branch-named fallback with no `PR #` in the message; AO-only changes show the row with no commit button; mixed changes still commit.
- `branch_state_test.go`: `Branch` is recorded, and checking out a new branch at the same commit is re-observed. CLI: `ls` shows the checked-out branch, and `formatBranchState` falls back to the recorded branch.
- Local: `go test` for `cli`, `service/session`, `httpd/...`, `domain` passes. golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports 0 issues on the touched packages. `npm run typecheck` is clean. Vitest: 157 files and 2,899 tests pass.
- Full `go test ./...` has two failures that also fail on the untouched base commit on this machine: `opencodev2 TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects` (local OpenCode is 1.x) and `integration TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch`. CI is the check for those.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Until the SCM summary loads, PR facts fall back to the recorded branch as `sourceBranch`. A session on a child branch may briefly show "Commit & push to `<branch>`" before switching to its PR number. This is neutral, never a wrong PR.
- Multi-repo workspace projects are not branch-reconciled, so they keep today's behaviour (recorded branch, first matching PR).
- The rest of #6637 (an ephemeral remote-preview route that needs no launch.json) is out of scope.

title: feat: add Stakpak Agent TUI harness
body:
## What

Adds [Stakpak Agent](https://github.com/stakpak/agent) (qualified on 0.3.88) as a **Terminal UI** harness. This is a new integration; it replaces the closed #6550.

| Area | How |
|---|---|
| Launch | `stakpak --system-prompt-file <file> [--model <m>]`. The TUI ignores a positional prompt, so AO types the first task once the composer footer (`$ shell \| / commands`) is drawn. Keys typed during Stakpak's ~3 s startup are lost, Enter included. |
| Status | No external hooks exist, so status comes from the rendered screen. A footer with `esc cancel` means active, the idle footer means idle, and an `Approval Required` box means blocked. |
| Session ID | Read from `stakpak sessions list --json`, matched by worktree (symlink-resolved) and launch time. |
| Restore | `--session <id>` after `stakpak sessions show` confirms the conversation still exists; otherwise a fresh launch. Instructions the conversation already stores are not re-sent, because Stakpak re-inserts `--system-prompt-file` on every resume. |
| Permissions | `.stakpak/session/auto_approve.json`, with a `.gitignore` and an AO marker. accept-edits approves `create`/`str_replace`/`remove`; auto and bypass approve every non-shell tool. A manual launch removes AO's file, and a policy file the user wrote is left alone. |
| Auth | Verified with a provider round-trip. A Stakpak key is checked by `stakpak auth status`'s API check. Bring-your-own-key profiles are checked by asking each provider of the active profile whether it accepts its key, without spending tokens: `GET /models` for OpenAI-compatible and custom endpoints, an empty Messages request for Anthropic-compatible ones. |
| Install / update / login | Homebrew tap `stakpak/stakpak/stakpak` or the official `install.sh` on macOS/Linux; manual release zip on Windows. Update with `stakpak update`, log in with `stakpak auth login`. |
| Models | Free text, forwarded as `--model`. |
| Wiring | Domain constant, registry, migration `20261108105252617_allow_stakpak_harness` plus schema repair, DTO/OpenAPI/schema enums, doctor probe, spawn help, avatar (Apache-2.0 mark), docs. |

### Not supported, with proof

- **Chat.** Stakpak's ACP `session/load` only records the session id; it never reloads or replays the stored messages (`cli/src/commands/acp/server.rs`, `load_session`), so a restored Chat would continue without its history. The ACP model list also omits custom providers, and a profile model without an `anthropic/`, `openai/` or `google/` prefix is routed to the Stakpak API.
- **Unattended shell commands.** Stakpak always prompts before `run_command`: it forces the base rule back to `Prompt` when loading the policy, and scoped rules match only by command name. In every AO mode shell commands wait for a human, and AO reports the session as blocked.
- **Unattended version refresh.** Off, because the session id is inferred rather than reported by a hook.

## Live audit (ao-agent-harness skill, #7081)

Run against this branch, using Z.ai GLM through Z.ai's Anthropic-compatible endpoint:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| cli_installed, cli_version, cli_login | PASS |
| ao_registered, ao_installed | PASS |
| ao_authenticated | PASS (authorized, not just configured) |
| ao_models | PASS (free-form) |
| tui_spawn | PASS |
| role_worker, role_orchestrator | PASS (AO's system prompt reaches Stakpak) |
| tui_prompt | FAIL: the task was delivered and the agent started, then stopped at Stakpak's approval for `pwd`. AO showed the session as `blocked`. This is the upstream shell-approval behaviour above. |
| tui_worktree … tui_restore_history | SKIP (depend on tui_prompt) |

Done by hand in tmux, not through AO: resume by id keeps history and follows the instructions; Esc cancels a running command; frames captured for idle, draft, working, approval and side panel (used in the unit tests).

Found by the audit and fixed here: the first task was typed before the TUI was ready. `waitForPromptReadiness` sends immediately when an adapter gives no text pattern, despite what the port comment says.

Known upstream behaviour: Stakpak redacts token-like strings in prompts, and by default appends `.stakpak/session*` to the worktree `.gitignore` (`auto_append_gitignore`).

## Verification

No local test run; CI verifies. New tests: `adapters/agent/stakpak` (terminal frames, launch/restore argv, session matching, auth probes against `httptest`, permission file), the migration, the install plan, auth plan and registry/wiring entries.

body: Code changes: +142 -25 Tests: +189 -4 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary Brings the mobile Notifications screen in line with the desktop notification panel. - **Mark read on open.** Opening the screen marks the unread rows it has loaded as read. Like desktop, it sends only those concrete ids to `POST /notifications/read-all`, so unread rows on pages not loaded yet stay unread until you scroll to them. Each machine's bell badge is refreshed after a successful ack. It only acks while the screen has focus: a reload while you are in a session opened from it (for example a host reconnecting) leaves new rows unread, and they are acked and highlighted when you come back. - **Highlight for the visit.** Rows that were unread keep their unread dot and colour until the screen loses focus. Tapping into a session and coming back shows them as read, like reopening the desktop panel. - **Clear all replaces Mark all read.** The top-right header button is now a trash icon that calls `DELETE /notifications` on every connected machine, including pages that aren't loaded. Offline machines are skipped and named in a short notice. Unlike desktop, it asks for confirmation first (a destructive alert), because the header circle is easy to hit on a phone and the clear can't be undone. The button is hidden when the list is empty. If a machine's delete fails, its previously loaded rows are put back even when the recovery reload also fails. This is skipped only if a reload has already replaced them. - **Failure handling.** If an ack fails, those rows go back to unread and a short notice names the machine. It isn't retried in a loop; pull-to-refresh retries. Each row remembers which request last tried to mark it read, so an older request that fails late only rolls back rows it still owns. It can't undo a newer request that succeeded. A failed badge refresh never rolls anything back. `markAllNotificationsRead` in `lib/api.ts` takes optional ids (the daemon already accepts them; desktop sends them), and there is a new `clearAllNotifications`. The native header button gains a `trash` icon (SF Symbol `trash` on iOS, Feather `trash-2` on Android). ## Screenshots Verified against a local lab proxy serving fake notifications. No real notifications were read or cleared. | | Opened (loaded unread marked read, still highlighted) | Back from a session | Clear all confirmation | After Clear all | |---|---|---|---|---| | iOS | | | | | | Android | | | | | ## Testing - `packages/mobile`: `npx vitest run` passes (2394 tests); `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. - New tests in `lib/notifications-screen.test.tsx` cover: acking the loaded unread ids on open, keeping them highlighted until blur, not acking rows that load while blurred and acking them on refocus, a failed ack restoring unread without a retry loop, an older ack failing after a newer overlapping one succeeded (rows stay read, no notice), a failed badge refresh leaving rows read, and pull-to-refresh retrying. They also cover Clear all after confirming across both machines, skipping an offline machine with a notice, restoring a machine's rows when both its delete and the recovery reload fail, and hiding the button when the list is empty. - Manual check on the iOS simulator (Debug build) and an Android emulator (debug build), with these results: - Opening sent `read-all` with exactly the 3 loaded unread ids. - Rows stayed highlighted, then showed as read after visiting a session and coming back. - Cancel in the confirmation sent nothing, and Clear all sent one `DELETE` and showed the empty state. - On iOS, the bell badge cleared afterwards. ## Risks - Against an older daemon that ignores `ids`, opening the screen marks every notification on that machine read, not just the loaded ones. - The confirmation prompt is a deliberate difference from desktop.

title: feat(chat): show worker updates as rows in the orchestrator chat
body:
Code changes: +614 -18\
Tests: +272 -0\
Others: +24 -0

## What

In the orchestrator chat, worker traffic is now compact rows instead of full message cards:

- **Worker rows.** Each worker message, report entry or mid-turn worker steer is one row: agent avatar, worker name, state (`needs you` / `stuck` / `done`), a headline and the time. The row expands to the full text.
- **Name link.** The name opens the worker's session, as the `[from …]` label does today. Hovering it shows the session card with live status and PR state.
- **Artifact link.** A report's `artifact:` output becomes a link under its row, with the artifact hover preview. Relative and absolute artifact paths both resolve.
- **Quiet replies.** When a settled worker turn's answer asks the user nothing, it draws as one line under the rows. The line is markdown, and it keeps the reply's copy and rollback controls (shown on hover or focus). It also opens the turn's work, replacing "Worked for".
- **Normal turns.** Every other turn renders as before: a reply that asks something, a tool-only turn, or a failed turn. A worker turn the orchestrator only read, with no work and no reply, shows just its rows.
- **Tight spacing.** Consecutive quiet turns with nothing else in them (no notices, plan, diff or spawned list) sit tight together, so they read as one list.
- **Folded reports.** Reports folded into a user message while the orchestrator was busy show as rows above that message.
- **Spawned list.** A turn that ran `ao spawn` lists the workers it started. Each line shows the worker's current state: PR (with "ready to merge" as text), done, needs input, stuck, or its latest checkpoint.
- **Older messages.** Three older formats also become rows:
  - report batches that link the session as a bare `ao://sessions/…` with no name;
  - worker messages from before AO stored the sender, which carry only the `[from <session>]` prefix;
  - AO's old task-naming prompt, which shows as "New task named <title>".
- **Stale states.** A `needs you` or `stuck` state is only highlighted while it is that worker's latest update.

Worker sessions and non-orchestrator chats are unchanged.

## Why

The orchestrator chat is where the user talks to AO and delegates work. Today each worker message and report batch draws as a full-width card, and the orchestrator often repeats the same update back in prose. A busy session becomes a log of worker traffic, and the few questions that need the user get lost in it.

## How

- `WorkerUpdates.tsx` holds the parsing and the components. `ChatWorkspace` uses them only when `sessionRole === "orchestrator"`.
- Reports are parsed from the text that `report.PreparedBatch.Render` writes. Direct messages and steers use the existing `senderSessionId` metadata.
- Parsing is cached per item and per group. The worker index keeps its identity until some worker's newest update changes, so streamed deltas don't re-render settled rows.
- Worker sessions resolve through the chat's link source (local daemon, remote host or Cloud), the same source the session and artifact links use.
- `ArtifactPathCode` and a `useChatLinkWorkspaces` hook are exported from `ChatMarkdown`. `SessionLabelLink` accepts a `className`.
- Known limits, marked in the code:
  - A question is detected from punctuation (`?` / `？`, ignoring code, links and `a?.b`).
  - The report text can be mimicked by a worker's note.
  - The spawned list reads `ao spawn` output.

  Structured report and spawn data from the daemon would remove all three; #6507's `session.spawned` rows cover the last.

## Testing

- `WorkerUpdates.test.ts` covers:
  - report parsing, and a malformed session link
  - sender-prefix stripping for messages and steers
  - folded reports
  - headlines
  - question detection
  - real `ao spawn` output
  - quiet-reply selection
- `ChatWorkspaceWorkerUpdates.test.tsx` renders an orchestrator timeline and checks three cases:
  - A quiet reply keeps copy, opens its work, and rolls back the right turn.
  - A reply that asks something stays a full reply.
  - A tool-only turn still shows its work.
- The real `ChatWorkspace` was rendered in a local dev page over a fixture built from real orchestrator transcripts. In it I checked:
  - the rows and the name and artifact links with their hover previews
  - the quiet reply's hover controls and its work disclosure
  - the spawned list

  Dark theme only.

title: feat(mobile): edit an earlier message in place, as on the desktop
body:
Code changes: +687 -71
Tests: +545 -5
Others: +0 -0 ## Summary Brings the desktop's "edit an earlier message" to the mobile app. - **Long-press a sent message** to get **Edit** and **Copy**. Edit appears only when the desktop would offer it: an idle agent, a finished turn, and either the first prompt, a native fork point, or replayable history. Otherwise the menu offers only Copy. - **Edit happens in place.** The bubble becomes an editor drawn as the composer's own pill (Liquid Glass on iOS 26+), with ✕ and send. While editing, the composer steps aside (still mounted, so its draft and attachments are kept), the prompt scrolls back into view as the keyboard opens, and leaving the screen closes the edit first. - **Sending** posts to the existing `POST /sessions/{id}/conversation/turns/{turnId}/edit` route, the same request the desktop sends. Each edit carries one `clientMessageId`, so retrying an uncertain send can't branch twice; a definitive refusal (`CHAT_EDIT_REJECTED`, `_BUSY`, …) gets a fresh id. Attachments and quotes stay with the message: only the written text is editable, and AO's staged-file block is re-appended on send. - **Copy** copies the written text, matching the reply's copy button. Sent-message text is no longer selectable, so a long-press opens the menu instead of starting a selection. - **Menus:** iOS uses the system context menu. Android's native popup can't be styled to match, so Android draws the same interaction: the conversation dims, the bubble lifts, and a rounded Edit/Copy card opens under it. No API changes: the snapshot already carries `editAvailable`, `nativeForkAvailableAfterSequence`, and `activeBranchId`. **Daemon fix, found while testing repeated edits:** editing an already edited prompt failed with `CHAT_EDIT_UNCERTAIN` on any client. A branch install made the session's `agent_session_id` durable as the new provider conversation, but the chat service's cached expected controller owner kept the old value. The next browser-credential rotation then failed Session Manager's ownership fence, and the source restore failed the same way, leaving the session stopped. `installStartedBranchController` now mirrors those fields. Reproduced and confirmed fixed against a real daemon running Claude Code. ## Screenshots | iOS: long-press | iOS: editing | iOS: after a change | iOS: not editable | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | Android: long-press | Android: editing | Android: not editable | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | Captured on an iOS 26.5 simulator and an Android emulator against live sessions, through a read-only proxy that stubbed every write. The iOS simulator was headless, so no keyboard is drawn there. ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 2404 tests pass. New tests cover the edit gate (`editableHumanTurns`), text/attachment splitting, `CHAT_EDIT_*` error copy, the editor's delivery-id rule, and the Android menu. - `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. - Manually on iOS and Android: the menu opens, Edit appears only when editable, cancel works, and send issues `{"text": …, "clientMessageId": …}` to `/turns/{turnId}/edit`. On Android the keyboard rises with the editor in view, and the header Back closes an open edit before leaving. ## Risks and follow-ups - **Not verified:** the full mobile UI against a live daemon (the daemon edit path was verified directly over HTTP: three consecutive edits of one prompt, all accepted); the iOS keyboard; Android hardware/gesture back (on the test build, back from a conversation leaves the app even without this change). - **Branches:** mobile shows only the active branch. Desktop's branch navigator isn't ported. - **Recovery:** desktop persists an in-flight edit across restarts. On mobile, the draft lives only while the screen is open. - **Worker reports:** mobile still shows the `` block inside orchestrator prompts (desktop hides it), so editing such a prompt includes that block.

body:
Stacked on #6364. Merge that first; this PR's diff is only the change below.

## Why

Other agent apps offer to bring earlier chats in once, at first launch, and keep the import in settings after that. #6364 added an always-visible sidebar button behind Developer Mode instead.

## What changes

- **Home:** a one-time card with one "Import <agent> chats" button for each agent that is installed and signed in on this computer (Claude Code, Codex). - **New folders:** the scan now also lists chats from Git folders that are not AO projects yet, as "<folder> (new project)". The folder is the repository's main checkout, so chats from its linked worktrees share one entry. On import, those folders are added as projects first, then the scan runs again and the chats import into them. Plain folders and bare repositories stay hidden, as before. New projects do not start an orchestrator; the usual spawn button does that.

## Tests

- `sessionimport`: destination table covers unregistered repos, linked worktrees of them, bare repos and plain folders; a scan → add project → rescan → import test.
- Renderer: the Import tab (agent filter, new-folder flow, stop when a folder cannot be added, results kept across the rescan); the Home card (one button per signed-in agent, none when no agent is set up, "Not now"); the Harness page opening on the Import tab, and no Import tab for other agents.

title: fix(httpd): restrict terminal mux access to trusted clients
body:
Code changes: +71 -9  
Tests: +280 -4  
Others: +10 -0  

Fixes #6688.

Workspace/loopback browser content could attach an existing agent terminal and read/write its PTY. Require exact configured renderer origins before the `/mux` upgrade. React Native's `http://localhost` compatibility Origin is accepted only after successful bearer validation on the authenticated listener; a header or preview cookie cannot establish that trust. Reject originless browser metadata and preview-host mux requests.

Check control WebSocket origins in the remote proxy before stripping Origin/injecting credentials, and prevent static/artifact preview hosts from falling through to a token-prefixed control socket. Managed app/agent preview sockets keep their confined path.

## CI recovery

Commit `1b7c944c8` addresses the cloud job's `ETXTBSY` failure in `TestCleanupSkipsTheStepsOfARepositoryFolderThatIsNotAOs`. The two ownership-behavior tests invoke the generated hook via its declared `sh` interpreter instead of asking Linux to exec a freshly written fixture. All ownership/skip assertions remain; separate direct executable-hook contract tests are unchanged. No production hook or terminal behavior changes.

- 50 repeated runs of the ownership and direct-hook tests pass with the race detector; cloud build, vet and formatting pass. Commit `8f64bdd86` also corrects a heartbeat fixture that completed its progress line with a final `echo` while asserting it stayed unfinished. That failure reproduced repeatedly on unchanged main; after removing only the final newline, all 50 race-enabled repetitions pass. No assertions were removed.
- Full cloud-module race runs still hit local `TestWorkspaceUserLaunchScriptStartsWorker` startup timing failures. The complete Coder package passes when retried separately; no Coder implementation change is included. The final complete worker-package race suite passes (`go test -race -count=1 ./internal/worker`). Docker is unavailable locally, so the Expat build remains for CI.

## Verification

- Unchanged main reproduces hostile existing-handle attachment and bidirectional input/output using an in-memory terminal; candidate rejects it with zero attachments. No OS command payload runs.
- Full HTTP/preview/terminal race suites pass. Desktop/development/native clients and a real authenticated loopback mobile listener pass echo, reconnect, two-viewer and retired-password checks.
- Real Electron tests trusted renderer echo and hostile document rejection through both the real Go router and production remote proxy. Enabled in Linux frontend CI.
- Complete frontend suite: 520 files passed; 8,959 tests passed, six skipped. All 65 remote-proxy tests, production TypeScript check, final E2E TypeScript check and pinned new-change lint pass. Full unchanged mobile-client suite and typecheck pass: 2,439 tests across 237 files.

- The two standalone issue branches merge without conflict; combined HTTP/mobile-bridge/terminal race suites pass in a clean environment.

## Gaps and scope

- Full backend race validation is not clean: installed-OpenCode discovery/version failures reproduce on unchanged main. Full pinned lint also fails on unchanged `scriptStepMinute` in `internal/session_manager/manager.go`; no unrelated rename is included. Fresh remote CI must be assessed independently. The original cloud fixture failure is addressed above; fresh-head Linux CI is pending.
- No physical phone, complete desktop GUI journey, public tunnel, signed package or Linux/Windows local runtime was exercised. Electron transport checks run on macOS with CI flags; Linux runs in CI. Docker-dependent jobs are unavailable locally.
- Native local processes remain trusted by design. Terminal handles remain shared for reconnect/multiple authorized viewers; no connection-owned handles, random session IDs or daemon-wide authentication is introduced.
- Related #7077 supplies the broader API/preview boundary. This PR is independently based on main; it does not require #7077. Their overlapping mux/proxy edits need reconciliation when integrating both.
An initial combined race run returned 404 in existing `TestLANManagerStartWaitsForPreviousStop`; the complete combined rerun with inherited AO variables removed passed. No lifecycle change was made for that result.

Reuse the exact-origin control proxy guard and validated native forwarding now merged in #7077; this PR adds mobile-specific regressions, including encoded mobile paths. Trusted media/render transports retain main's browser policy. The phone-facing listener continues to hide its own control routes.

Resolved workflow/proxy/test conflicts against `c2722b7e7`. Keep the merged broad proxy guard, the dedicated mobile daemon policy and no-store responses, and all three Electron CI checks. Updated the media regression to send the trusted renderer Origin required by main.

Complete HTTP/terminal/mobile-bridge races and the full frontend suite also pass (520 files, 8,986 tests passed, seven skipped). Full production TypeScript checking also passes locally. Fresh remote CI has started; Linux/Xvfb and the platform gaps below remain unverified locally.

## Verification

- CI recovery: install Electron explicitly before capturing its executable path, preventing lazy-download stdout from corrupting the path. Reproduced the original failure with an isolated missing runtime, then verified the corrected fresh-runtime bootstrap. Real Electron regression passes on macOS both normally and with CI Chromium flags; complete HTTP/mobile-bridge race suites pass again. Workflow YAML parses and diff checks pass. - Historical exploit baseline (`44d71b5c3`, before #7077/#7105): hostile preview POST enables the real pairing service's fake listener/tunnel and returns a generated test password. Candidate rejects all tested enable/rotation/control/preflight/status requests with no listener/tunnel/config effects.

title: fix(cloud): rebuild Brotli with the upstream decoder fix for the worker image
body:
## Summary

ECR reports **CVE-2026-111497 (CRITICAL, CVSS 4.0 9.2)** on the worker image, against Debian's `libbrotli1` `1.1.0-2+b7`, and Debian hasn't shipped a fix for trixie. This PR rebuilds Debian's package with upstream's fix and installs it over the stock one. It follows the same pattern as the existing Expat stage.

## Issue

Brotli streams are split into blocks, and the stream says when to switch to the next "block type". Upstream commit [`google/brotli@0ed4268a44`](https://github.com/google/brotli/commit/0ed4268a4401abcb4472096340477cf4af7d1a2b) ("Detect and report invalid stream earlier") fixes how the decoder handles a block switch that can't be valid, because only one block type exists:

- **Fast decode path:** `DecodeLiteralBlockSwitch`, `DecodeCommandBlockSwitch` and `DecodeDistanceBlockSwitch` returned `void`. When a switch was invalid they quietly did nothing, and decoding carried on with stale state, including a block length of 0 that is then decremented.
- **Careful decode path** (used near the end of the input): the same failure came back as `BROTLI_FALSE`, which the decoder reads as "needs more input". A corrupt stream looked like one that was only incomplete.

The fix makes these functions return a real status. An invalid switch now fails at once with the new `BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH` (-17) error. Upstream 1.1.1 is exactly 1.1.0 plus this commit and a version bump.

The severity comes from the scanner's CVSS data (`AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N`, high C/I/A). I haven't seen a public advisory or proof-of-concept.

## Impact on AO

- **Exposed:** anything in the worker image that decodes Brotli through Debian's `libbrotli1`, which means libcurl:
  - `git` over HTTPS turns on every encoding libcurl supports, so a hostile or compromised HTTPS remote could send a crafted `Content-Encoding: br` response.
  - `curl --compressed`, which agents often run against arbitrary, possibly attacker-controlled URLs.
- **Not exposed:**
  - Node-based agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) use Node's bundled Brotli, which Node v22.23.4 in the base image already fixes.
  - Chromium has its own copy and is only installed when `AGENT_BROWSER=1`, so it isn't in the published image.
- **How far it reaches:** at worst, code runs inside one session's worker sandbox, which holds that session's git token and coding-agent credential. Each session has its own worker. TLS prevents a network attacker from injecting the payload, so exploiting this needs a malicious or compromised server.
- **Operational:** the CRITICAL finding currently fails the ECR scan on every new worker image.

## Changes

- **New `brotli-build` stage** in `cloud/Dockerfile`:
  - Downloads Debian trixie's `brotli` 1.1.0-2 source package and the upstream patch, each pinned by SHA-256. The patch is fetched with `?full_index=1`, so its bytes, and therefore the pin, don't change when GitHub's short hashes get longer.
  - Appends the patch to `debian/patches/series` and builds with `-Pnopython`.
  - Versions the package **`1.1.1-0+ao1`**. Debian marks every 1.1.0 build as unfixed, so the 1.1.1 version is what lets the scanner see the fix.
  - Runs Brotli's ctest suite during the build.
- **Worker stage:** installs the patched `libbrotli1` with `dpkg -i`, checks the installed version, and checks that `curl` still reports brotli support.
- **CI:** a new `Test Brotli security backport` step builds the `brotli-build` stage, next to the Expat one.
- The stage carries a "remove once Trixie's libbrotli1 includes the upstream fix" note.

## Testing

All builds are linux/amd64 under emulation on arm64.

- **Patch and build:** the patch applies cleanly on top of Debian's `0001-build-static-libraries-by-default.patch`. All **14 ctest tests passed**, and `dpkg-gensymbols` reported no symbol changes.
- **The patched code is what runs:**
  - The new `_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH` string is present in the worker image's `libbrotlidec.so.1.1.0` and absent from stock trixie `libbrotli1 1.1.0-2+b7`.
  - It's the only `libbrotlidec` in the image, and `curl` and `libcurl.so.4` resolve to it.
- **Runtime:**
  - The installed `libbrotli1` is `1.1.1-0+ao1`.
  - `curl --compressed -H 'Accept-Encoding: br'` works.
  - `git`, `node v22.23.4` and Expat `2.9.0-1` are unchanged.
- **ECR scan:** I pushed the image as `ao-cloud-worker:libbrotli-patch-test-linux-amd64` and scanned its amd64 manifest (`sha256:9bce0b6b…`). It has **no brotli findings**. Compared with the current `7dd0334…-linux-amd64` image, the only change is that CVE-2026-111497 is gone; the other 17 findings (glibc, zlib, nghttp2, cyrus-sasl2) are the same in both.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **No regression test for the bug itself yet.** The scan is version-based, and Brotli's tests only decode valid streams. A follow-up should add a test like `cloud/test/expat-buffer-bounds.c` that feeds a crafted invalid-block-switch stream and expects `BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH`. It's waiting on a reproducer.
- The `brotli-build` stage adds about 2.5 minutes under amd64 emulation; it should be faster on native CI runners.
- Only `libbrotli1` is replaced. `libbrotli-dev` and the `brotli` CLI aren't installed in the worker image.
- Remove the stage once trixie ships a fixed `libbrotli1`.

title: fix(chat): a steer starts a new visual turn and stays visible
body:
## Summary
A steer is the user speaking, but it was drawn as a bordered bubble inside the same turn, and once the turn settled the "Worked for" fold swallowed it.

- A steer now starts a new visual turn. The work before it settles into its own "Worked for" row, and the steer gets a fresh Working row, timer and reply. It is still one real turn: only the last segment carries the live state, outcome, diff and plan.
- Steers and later user messages stay outside the fold once a turn settles, in order, so the reply never answers a message the reader can no longer see.
- The steer bubble is a plain user bubble, labelled "↳ Steered" instead of "Steered into the running turn".
- The copy action on a reply shows as soon as its text has fully arrived, not after the turn ends and the typing animation catches up. While a turn runs it only shows when the reply is the newest item. Rollback still waits for the turn to settle.

Overlaps #6627, which fixes the folded-steer part only and conflicts with `main`. This supersedes it.

## Testing

I did not run the test suite for this PR. I updated the steer-order test, added one for a steer in a settled turn, and updated three steer-label checks.

## Risks
- Visual only, no daemon or data changes.
- Duplicate `turnId` across the segments of one turn; nothing that acts on a turn (rollback, retry) is attached to the earlier segments.
