title: fix(mobile): open GitHub PR links on the PR in the iOS GitHub app
body:
Code changes: +33 -15\
Tests: +39 -25\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When the GitHub app is installed, tapping a PR, issue or repo link in AO mobile now opens the `https://github.com/...` URL with `Linking.openURL` instead of a `github://repo/...` URL. iOS treats that https URL as a universal link, so the GitHub app opens on the PR itself.

## Why

A user reported that tapping a PR link on iOS brings up the GitHub app but leaves it on whatever page it was last showing. `githubAppUrl()` rewrote `https://github.com/o/r/pull/N` to `github://repo/o/r/pull/N`. That scheme's paths are undocumented (our own comment already noted they "have changed across app releases"). The app opens for the scheme but evidently doesn't route that path.

github.com's `apple-app-site-association` claims `/<owner>/<repo>/pull/*` and `/issues/*` for the GitHub app (`com.github.stormbreaker.prod`), so the https URL is the supported way in.

## How

- `githubLink.ts`: `githubAppUrl` → `githubAppLink`. It applies the same conservative shape filter (repo root, `pull/<n>` and `issues/<n>` only; `issues/new?body=` and deeper paths stay null), but returns the canonical https URL. The query string is dropped and `http`/`www.` are normalised.
- `openGitHub.ts`: probes `canOpenURL("github://")` only to detect the app, then opens the https link. This must go through `Linking.openURL`, because the in-app browser (SFSafariViewController) never hands a universal link to an app. Everything else is unchanged: the fallbacks, `fromSheet`, and non-web schemes such as the `x-safari-https://` bug report.
- If a user has told iOS to open github.com links in Safari, the link now opens the right page in Safari rather than the wrong screen in the app.
- Android: in practice nothing changes. The app declares no `<queries>` entry for `github`, so the app check is expected to answer false there and links keep going to the Custom Tab, as before.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 237 files / 2441 tests pass. `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- Updated the `githubLink` tests for the https output. In the `openGitHub` tests, the app path now asserts the `github://` probe and the https open, and never opens `github:`. A new case keeps `/pull/N/files` in the in-app browser.
- The updated `openGitHub` app-path test fails against the old implementation.
- **Not verified on a device.** The simulator can't install the GitHub app, and no physical iPhone was reachable. Someone with the GitHub app on an iPhone should tap a PR link (PR card, or the review screen's open-in-GitHub button) and confirm it lands on the PR.

title: fix(terminal): split large paste into bounded messages
body:
Code changes: +7 -1  
Tests: +78 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Why

An 800 KiB terminal paste exceeds the daemon’s 1 MiB WebSocket message limit after base64 encoding. The socket closes and the paste is lost. Split input into 32 KiB byte chunks before framing each message.

## What changed

- Encode input once and send bounded messages in the existing FIFO order.
- Cover large bracketed pastes, UTF-8 across chunk boundaries, queued input, empty input, and disposal.

## Scope

This fixes the local daemon terminal transport. Cloud terminal transport uses a separate protocol and remains outside this change.

## Blast Radius

All local terminal input passes through this path. Small input retains its existing wire format; large input remains one ordered byte stream. The daemon message limit and API stay unchanged.

## Verification

- Targeted Vitest suite: 23/23 pass. The regression fails before the fix because the encoded message exceeds 1 MiB.
- Native Electron: reproduced the disconnect before the fix; the reporter confirmed the paste works with the fix. Focused review found no P0, P1, or important P2 issues.

title: fix(browser): discover and select newly opened tabs
body:
Code changes: +112 -13\
Tests: +748 -20\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Make page-opened tabs available to browser automation. Agents can interact with the popup, switch back to the opener, reselect the popup, and close the requested tab.

## Why

AO showed new tabs while the native browser daemon retained an older target registry. Selecting the popup failed with `BROWSER_TARGET_MISMATCH` and blocked later commands.

Source review also found a P1 identity bug. AO target IDs and native tab numbers have independent lifetimes. After a short-lived popup disappeared, AO `t3` could refer to a different page than native `t3`.

Related to #4705.

## How

- Reconcile AO-owned targets before native commands and publish discovery changes independently to subscribed CDP clients.
- Resolve selection through stable `targetId`, verify the returned identity, and invalidate cached selection before an explicit switch.
- Close the exact AO-owned target through its provider so native renumbering cannot redirect a close to another page.
- Update AO selection only when no newer selection occurred during the native command.
- Cover popup discovery, isolation, numbering gaps, failed-selection recovery, queued renderer selection, exact closure, and native daemon restart recovery.

The Electron fixture uses AO's real renderer bounds event and asserts that the selected view is visible while inactive views are hidden. Text waits observe the result of one native click without retrying input. Restoring the old forced-visible fixture fails the new inactive-tab assertion.

Existing fail-closed behavior and worker isolation remain. Hidden-panel clicks that create no popup are outside this change.

title: fix(chat): restore background title and branch generation
body:
Code changes: +24 -3\
Tests: +144 -3\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Restore generated session titles and branch slugs for background calls that were answering the original task instead of naming it.

## Why

With the prompt `what is in this repo`, Claude inspected the empty scratch directory and returned a repository answer. The selected Codex model, `gpt-6-luna`, also answered the question instead of returning naming JSON. Both results were rejected by the naming parser, leaving the title and branch on prompt-based fallbacks.

## How

Every fresh background call now includes the generation instructions in its actual turn, followed by the original prompt as a JSON string. The provider still receives the standing instructions through its existing system/developer channel.

Background calls also request `DisableTools`. Claude ACP enforces this with an empty built-in tool list, strict MCP configuration, and an MCP-tool deny rule. It omits to-do guidance for those calls and preserves the compaction environment. Other providers keep their native tool/sandbox policy and receive the shared request-format fix.

## Testing

- Regression tests failed before the fix and pass afterward. They cover the instructions/input boundary for Claude, Codex, and Kimi; tool-policy propagation through ACP; and Claude metadata with and without a compaction setting.
- Live tests through the background service pass for Claude and Codex `gpt-6-luna`. A separate run using the production naming prompt confirmed Luna changes from a non-JSON repository answer to `{"title":"Inspect repository contents","slug":"repo-contents"}`.
- Backend and cloud build/vet pass with Go 1.27.1. The full cloud race suite and native macOS CLI E2E suite pass.
- API generation with Node 24 / openapi-typescript 7.4.4 and sqlc generation have no drift. Gitleaks 7.4.0 scans the commit without findings.

- The final full race runs for `service/chat`, `chatdriver/acp`, `chatdriver/claudeacp`, and `chatdriver/codexappserver` pass. SQLite, store, and session-manager race suites also pass.
- The full backend race run is **not green on this host**: the OpenCode probe/major-version packages, tmux runtime, activity observer, and terminal integration packages fail on both this branch and unchanged `main` (`b087ce794d`). The initial ACP replay failure also reproduces on the baseline; its final full-package rerun passes. An agent-catalog coalescing failure passes on full-package rerun.
- Full golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports the same pre-existing `scriptStepMinute` / `revive time-naming` warning at `session_manager/manager.go:6307` on this branch and unchanged `main`.
- Docker is unavailable locally, so the CLI container smoke test and cloud Expat image check require CI. Windows and Linux-native matrix jobs also require CI. Remote checks are pending.

title: fix(artifacts): skip OS metadata files and keep helper code out of the artifact dir
body:
## Summary

Session artifact directories were surfacing junk: Finder's `.DS_Store` and agent helper scripts/source files.

**OS metadata files.** `sessionartifacts.List` returned every regular file in the artifact directory, so a `.DS_Store` written when someone opened the folder in Finder was listed as an artifact, captured as versions, and flipped the session's output type to "artifact". `List` now skips known OS metadata and tool entries, matched case-insensitively at any depth:

- macOS: `.DS_Store`, `._*`, `.Spotlight-V100`, `.Trashes`, `.fseventsd`
- Windows: `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini`
- Tooling: `.git`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`

Since the artifact list, output-type reconcile (`lifecycle/output_type.go`), and version capture (`artifactversions`) all go through `List`, the fix applies to all three. A list of names is used rather than skipping all dotfiles because user content in dot-directories (e.g. a nested `.versions/`) is intentionally kept.

**Helper code.** The Session Artifacts prompt says any non-PR file must go in the artifact directory, "never into the git workspace, even temporarily", which led agents to write their generator scripts there too. The prompt now tells agents to keep scripts, source code, and other helper files in the system temp directory unless the user asked for that code as the deliverable.

## Tests

- New `TestList_SkipsOSMetadataAndToolFiles` covers top-level and nested junk alongside real deliverables.
- `go test` passes for `sessionartifacts`, `artifactversions`, `lifecycle`, `observe/artifacts`, `service/session`.
- `session_manager`: 4 `TestSpawn_*MissingBinary*` tests fail locally because tmux isn't installed; they fail identically on `main`.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Junk versions already captured stay in the database; they just stop growing.
- The prompt change only applies to newly spawned sessions, and is guidance — an agent can still write code into the directory.

title: fix(mobile): keep an open Archive cheap with read-only archived rows
body: Code changes: +243 -15\ Tests: +242 -6\ Others: +0 -0 ## Why Opening **Archive** on the Workers board lagged badly on iOS and Android and could crash the app. The archive is most of a long-running board: on the test machine, 340 of 381 workers. The archive only rendered once expanded, but then every archived session was added to the list as a full live row: - **iOS:** each row mounted a native `MenuView`, which in `@expo/ui` is a whole SwiftUI host (`Host` + `ContextMenu` + `RNHostView`), plus an RNGH `Swipeable`. - **Android:** each row mounted a three-gesture `GestureDetector` race and an always-built swipe rail (two ripple buttons and SVG icons), even at rest. - **List:** `FlatList` ran with its default window (21 viewports), so roughly 200 of these rows were built within about a second of the tap. ## What changed Archived sessions now match desktop's archive card, which is non-interactive and has Restore as its only action. - **`ArchivedWorkerRow`** (new): a read-only row with the same text layout as a live row and a trailing Restore control. It has no tap-to-open, context menu, swipe, or copy branch. It's used in Archive and for archived matches in search results. - **Restore:** one restore at a time. A successful restore opens the session, unless you've left the board for another tab or session by the time it finishes. A failure shows the error under that row, with retry available. The button is disabled while the session's machine is offline, as on desktop. - **Android swipe rail:** the action controls mount when a drag starts and unmount once the row settles closed, as iOS already does. - **List window:** `windowSize` 7, `maxToRenderPerBatch` 8, `initialNumToRender` 12. A test pinned the old defaults without a stated reason; it now asserts the bounded window. Live rows are otherwise unchanged. ## Before / after **Setup:** - **Data:** the real daemon's 381 workers (340 archived), served through a read-only loopback proxy with writes stubbed. - **Builds:** the same native binaries before and after, an iOS Debug build on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator and an Android debug build on a Pixel 7 emulator (API 35, 2 GB). Both loaded a production, minified JS bundle (`dev=false&minify=true`). - **Steps:** cold launch, scroll to Archive, tap it, sample for 20 s, then 30 fast flings. - **Spinners:** live "Working" spinners were frozen in both runs, so that `uiautomator` could reach an idle UI. | | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | **iOS:** main thread blocked after tap | 10.9 s | **3.4 s** | | **iOS:** CPU in the 20 s after tap | 7.5 s | **1.8 s** | | **iOS:** native views when expanded | 10,522 | **6,421** | | **iOS:** SwiftUI hosting views when expanded / deep in archive | 288 / 240 | **102 / 36** | | **iOS:** memory when expanded / peak while flinging | 636 / 862 MB | **552 / 682 MB** | | **iOS:** 30 flings, wall time / CPU | 665 s / 112 s | **71 s / 31 s** | | **Android:** UI thread busy after tap | 6.8 s | **2.5 s** | | **Android:** CPU in the 20 s after tap | 9.3 s | **1.9 s** | | **Android:** views when expanded / after flinging | 5,277 / 7,327 | **2,343 / 2,533** | | **Android:** PSS when expanded / after flinging | 759 / 939 MB | **638 / 776 MB** | | **Android:** janky frames expanding / flinging | 74% / 85% | **23% / 0.7%** | | **Android:** p90 frame time while flinging | 150 ms | **31 ms** | Archive just opened: | iOS before | iOS after | Android before | Android after | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | After 30 flings into the archive: | iOS before | iOS after | Android before | Android after | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | ## New behaviour | Restoring (iOS) | Failed restore (Android) | Machine offline (Android) | Live row swipe (Android) | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | | The icon spins and the other Restore buttons are disabled. On success the session opens (checked on iOS and Android). | The error shows under its row; retry stays available. | With two machines paired, the offline machine's Restore buttons are disabled and the online one's stay enabled. They re-enable on reconnect. | The rail now mounts on drag: no rail buttons at rest, two while open. | ## Testing - **CI steps** (`npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`): run on Node 20 in a clean copy. Typecheck is clean and 2451/2451 tests pass. npm was 11.13 there, while CI's Node 20 ships npm 10. - **New tests:** - archived rows are read-only with only Restore, in Archive and in search; - restore goes to the session's own machine, then opens the session; - a failure shows inline and doesn't navigate; - one restore runs at a time; - Restore is disabled while that row's machine is offline, using the board's own connection for rows without a host id; - the bounded list window; - the Android rail mounts on drag and releases once settled, including when the close is interrupted. - **Fail-before check:** the Android rail tests fail against the previous implementation. - **Manual (simulator and emulator):** - tapping an archived row's body does nothing (iOS); - restore opens the session (iOS and Android); - a failed restore shows inline (Android); - the offline machine's Restore is disabled, then re-enabled on reconnect (Android, two paired machines); - live-row swipe still works (Android). - **Restore after leaving the board:** a test starts a restore, blurs the board without unmounting it (tabs keep visited screens mounted), then resolves the restore. It checks there is no navigation and that Restore is usable again. It fails on the commit before the fix. The mobile suite now passes 2452/2452 locally. ## Risks and follow-ups - **Behavior change:** archived workers can no longer be opened, pinned, renamed, or archived from the board. This matches desktop. - **Offline, single machine:** if your only paired machine goes offline, the board already shows "No machines connected". The disabled state therefore only shows when another machine is still connected. - **Not tested on hardware:** these numbers are from a simulator and an emulator. Neither crashed before the change; the before build froze instead (30 flings took 11 minutes on iOS). - **Not covered:** iOS long-press on live rows wasn't retested. That code path is unchanged. - **Follow-up:** the sessions poll still downloads the full history every tick. Paging the archive on the server is a separate change. - **Side finding:** on a fresh install, a successful Manual connect leaves the onboarding screen up until the app is relaunched, on both platforms. This wasn't investigated here.

title: Orchestrator shows "The agent controller stopped" after a restart and Resume agent never brings it back
body:
The ao-landing project's orchestrator (Chat mode, Claude Code) showed "The agent controller stopped. History is kept. Resume the agent or open a shell in the same worktree" with Resume agent / Open shell. I didn't stop it, and Resume agent doesn't bring it back.

Screenshot (shared locally): the orchestrator tab with the red "The agent controller stopped" banner above "Reports since your previous turn".

---

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 by an AO worker session on the reporter's Mac (macOS 26.5). The live data was only read, never written. Installed app 0.14.3-nightly.202610182020 (daemon `vcs.revision=6e8d6e4e0`) at the time of the incident and 0.14.5-nightly.202610220502 (`18315f063`) on 10-23. Code read at `origin/main` `fd7be1b7c`.

**Why the agent process went away.** The Mac kernel-panicked at about 19:56 PDT on 2026-10-18 (`/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/panic-full-2026-10-18-195753.0002.panic`: `watchdog timeout: no checkins from watchdogd in 94 seconds`; `Compressor Info: ... 100% of segments limit (BAD) with 14 swapfiles and LOW swap space`). The reboot killed the orchestrator's chat host (`chat-hosts/ao-landing-3/host.json` pid 68368, never cleaned up). There was no hibernation (`hibernated_at` NULL) and nothing relayed to it after the reboot. The last worker report was acknowledged at 01:46:07Z, before the panic.

**Why it can't come back.** The session and the project conversation it inherited name different Claude threads:

```
sessions.ao-landing-3.provider_conversation_id                     = 48272083-…   (its own thread, first prompt 2026-10-18T22:50Z)
conversation_branches[5dfe305b…:root].provider_conversation_id     = 250f03c6-…   (the previous orchestrator ao-landing-1's thread, last used 2026-10-07)
conversation_branches for that conversation                        = 1 (root only)
```

On daemon boot, `checkSessionHealth` and every Resume stop at `service/chat/service.go`:

```
reconcile: live pass failed ... error="check session ao-landing-3: resume chat: active conversation branch provider handle \"250f03c6-…\" does not match session handle \"48272083-…\""
POST /api/v1/sessions/ao-landing-3/resume-agent → 500
```

This was reproduced against an isolated daemon at `6e8d6e4e0` using a trimmed copy of the DB. Because this isn't `ErrChatHostNotRunning`, boot never recorded `exited`. The row stayed `idle` with no controller, which the UI renders as "controller stopped". On 10-23 at 09:31:13Z a failed Resume moved it to `exited` (`preserveFailedReconcileRelaunch`).

**How the mismatch is created (code reading + lab).** When a new orchestrator's first controller starts, `Start` rebinds the existing project conversation. `queuedBeforeFirstController` is true for every first start, and since #5626 it also blocks reserving a new provider boundary, even when the active branch already holds the previous orchestrator's thread. The fresh thread then reaches only the session row. The root-branch trigger fills an empty branch handle only, so the branch keeps the old one. Everything works until the first daemon restart or reboot, and after that the orchestrator can never be resumed.

Fresh reproduction on `origin/main` (isolated headless daemon, real Claude Chat orchestrators): spawn orchestrator 1 → one turn → kill it → spawn orchestrator 2 → one turn → SIGKILL daemon and host → restart:

```
before crash: branch=fb3f289e… session=b0bd8220… branches=1
after restart: idle   (reconcile: ... does not match session handle ...)
resume-agent: Internal server error → state exited
```

**Related.** #6606 has the same failing check and permanent 500, but the mismatch there comes from agent-switch handoff. Open PR #6709 heals an already-rebound orchestrator's stale branch identity, but it doesn't stop new ones being created. #6695 is a different error (`CHAT_RECOVERY_INCONCLUSIVE`). Searched OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator issues and PRs for "does not match session handle", "provider handle", "controller stopped", "orchestrator resume project conversation" and "queuedBeforeFirstController".

title: fix(chat): give a replacement orchestrator its own provider boundary
body:
## What

A replacement Chat orchestrator now records its fresh provider thread on its own conversation branch. Previously that thread reached only the session row. After the first daemon restart or reboot, such an orchestrator showed "The agent controller stopped", and Resume agent failed with 500 every time.

Fixes #7123

## Why

When a new orchestrator's first controller starts, `Start` rebinds the existing project conversation. That conversation's active branch still names the previous orchestrator's provider thread. `queuedBeforeFirstController` is true for every first start, and since #5626 it vetoes reserving a new provider boundary. So the new thread was written only to `sessions.provider_conversation_id`, and the root-branch trigger fills an empty branch handle only. Every later reconnect or Resume passes the session's handle and is refused:

```
active conversation branch provider handle "<previous thread>" does not match session handle "<new thread>"
```

That error isn't `ErrChatHostNotRunning`, so startup leaves the row `idle` with no controller, which the UI renders as the stopped banner.

## How

One condition in `service/chat/service.go`. The queued-intake case is already excluded by `!preserveUndispatchedQueue` on the `LatestSequence` clause, so `!queuedBeforeFirstController` is dropped from the boundary decision. Inherited provider history (`activeBranch.ProviderConversationID != ""`) reserves a boundary again, as it did before #5626. A brand-new session's first start is unchanged because it has no branch thread.

Undispatched intake moves with the boundary. Queue adoption has already placed the replacement's opening turn on the predecessor's branch, and native replay only correlates turns inside the active provider scope. So `CommitChatSpawn` now moves the session's queued, never-dispatched turns, together with their messages and activities, onto the new branch in the same transaction that activates it. Without this, the prompt was imported a second time after a restart, as found in review.

This prevents new mismatches. Orchestrators already in this state still need #6709 (healing) or a manual repair.

## Testing

- `TestReplacementOrchestratorFirstStartReservesBoundaryForInheritedThread` covers queue → start → complete → restart → native replay. The replay uses reconstructed turn ids, as ACP does, and the test asserts a fresh-thread boundary plus one opening prompt on one completed turn. It fails on `main` (no boundary) and with the boundary change alone (2 prompts).
- `TestCommitChatSpawnMovesOnlyUndispatchedIntakeToProviderBoundary`: queued intake moves to the boundary, and an already-dispatched turn keeps its branch. It fails without the store change.
- `go test ./internal/service/chat/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/lifecycle/` (full), and the chat/orchestrator/spawn/resume subset of `./internal/session_manager/` all pass. The only failures are 4 `TestSpawn_*MissingBinary*` tests that need the tmux lookup; they fail identically on unmodified `main` on this machine. `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean; sqlc was regenerated with the pinned version.
- Isolated headless daemons (real Claude Chat orchestrators): spawn orchestrator 1 → one turn → kill → spawn orchestrator 2 → one turn → SIGKILL daemon and host → restart → Resume.
  - `main`: branch `fb3f289e…` ≠ session `b0bd8220…`, 1 branch; after restart the row is `idle` with the mismatch error; Resume returns 500 and the row becomes `exited`.
  - this branch: branch and session both `f7d8960b…`, 2 branches; after restart the row is `exited`; Resume succeeds in native mode and the row is `idle`. A rerun at the second commit found one copy of the opening prompt after restart and resume, on one completed turn on the replacement's branch.
  - The labs were shut down and deleted afterwards.

## Risks / follow-ups

- A replacement orchestrator's first start now creates a child branch, which is the same mechanism a provisioning retry with prior provider history already uses. Its undispatched intake moves onto that branch; row IDs don't change.
- Related: #6606 is the same failing check reached through agent-switch handoff, a different trigger that isn't fixed here.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode 2 model discovery times out while copying legacy data store on macOS
body:
### Environment

- Agent Orchestrator 0.14.5, local macOS installation (OS version not recorded).
- Adapter: `opencode-v2`.
- Native PATH OpenCode: `~/.local/bin/opencode`, version 2.0.25.
- AO-selected OpenCode: `~/.ao/data/harnesses/bin/opencode-v2`, version 2.1.3.

### Observed behavior

The native PATH CLI's `opencode models` succeeds and lists the existing Solheim and DeepInfra providers/models. AO's OpenCode 2 catalog has zero usable entries and reports:

```text
opencode-v2 model catalog: prepare data home: opencode: copy legacy data store: context deadline exceeded
```

The failure occurs during data-home preparation, before model discovery. No model-ID rejection was observed. Authentication and inference remain untested.

The two binary versions differ, but a version mismatch has not been established as the cause. The directly observed failure is the legacy-store copy timeout. The separate OpenCode 1 adapter remains usable and unaffected. No destructive workaround, credential-store copy, reinstall or migration retry was attempted.

### Minimal reproduction

With an existing OpenCode 2 installation and provider connections:

1. Select OpenCode 2 in AO's model picker and refresh models.
2. Inspect the resulting catalog.
3. Observe the preparation error above and zero usable catalog entries, while the native PATH CLI's model list succeeds.

### Expected behavior

AO should discover models using the existing installation and provider connections, or provide an actionable migration error explaining what failed and how to proceed safely.

Is there a documented, scoped binary/data-home override for `opencode-v2` that preserves OpenCode 1? Otherwise, could data-home preparation handle this copy timeout robustly and provide an actionable recovery path?

### Related

Related: #6009 describes a `--pure` / empty-catalog symptom. This report has a distinct failure during data-home preparation and legacy-store copying. A common cause has not been established.

title: feat(chat): ship agent switching without Developer mode
body:
## Summary
Mid-session agent switching (reworked in #6588) is no longer gated on Developer mode, so it reaches every user in the next stable release.

Removed Developer-mode gates:
- `chat/AgentSwitchPicker.tsx`: the **Agent** row and other-agent targets/favorites were hidden unless Developer mode was on.
- `chat/SessionChatSurface.tsx`: a pending pick was dropped while Developer mode was off.
- `TerminalAgentControls.tsx`: the terminal **Session actions → Agent** picker required Developer mode.

No backend, CLI, or mobile gate existed (the daemon's `provider-switch` endpoint never checked it).

Kept, since they don't depend on Developer mode:
- Cloud sessions can't switch agents (`SessionView`, `SessionChatSurface` `!session.cloud`).
- `newWorkDisabled` still hides the chat picker.
- Targets that aren't installed or ready, or lack Chat support (`/agents/chat/unavailable`), aren't offered. One-shot agents stay greyed out in a terminal.
- The terminal picker shows only in Terminal UI (`switchTarget === "chat"`). Chat switches from the composer.
- Daemon refusals still apply: busy, pending approval/question, terminated session, unsupported target.
- Orchestrators were never excluded and still aren't.

Docs: added a "Switch agents mid-session" section to `guides/per-role-agents.mdx`.

## Tests
- `vitest`: AgentSwitchPicker, SessionChatSurface, SessionView, TurnSettingsBar: 467 passed. The suites now default to Developer mode **off**. The old "hidden outside Developer Mode" and "pick lapses when Developer Mode turns off" tests now check the reverse.

A complete tmux-package rerun with no AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME and a fresh private TMUX_TMPDIR passed all 131 leaf cases in 9.218s, without source changes or shared-socket access. The capped broad command remains **incomplete**, not a full local pass; remaining local packages were not rerun. Current-head full Go CI passed. Full-backend race, full frontend suite/typechecks/build/native packaging, Linux/Windows/container and API/sqlc generation were not all rerun locally; their applicable new-head CI results are verified successful. Historical results are not relabeled as current passes. No new AO static-review approval, merge or ready-state change is claimed.

## What

The daemon's network-facing listener, which phones and remote desktops reach directly or through a Cloudflare tunnel, now gzips `application/json` responses for clients that send `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. The loopback listener is unchanged.

## Why

Every response left the machine uncompressed. Behind a tunnel, `cloudflared` carries those bytes to Cloudflare as they are, and Cloudflare compresses only on the way to the phone. The board poll (`GET /api/v1/sessions`) is about 260–320 KB on a real board, and a phone on a tunnel polls it every 2 seconds.

A load test of simulated phones through a named tunnel levelled off at about 9 board polls per second. Small requests through the same tunnel kept climbing past 60 req/s and the machine's uplink had room to spare, so the limit was the board's size, not the request count.

## How

- `remoteJSONCompression` negotiates exact gzip/deflate tokens and their quality values before using chi's `middleware.NewCompressor(flate.BestSpeed, "application/json")` with a zlib-framed deflate encoder inside the LAN auth chain. Explicit `q=0` rejects a coding; mixed preferences and wildcard overrides are honored. The inner handler retains the original request headers. BestSpeed matches the preview response compression level.
- Only JSON is compressed. `text/event-stream` stays unencoded so events flush immediately.
- Remote responses preserve `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, including identity/range responses and 304 revalidation. The desktop proxy merges its CORS `Origin` variant with upstream Vary fields instead of overwriting them.
- Responses that already set `Content-Encoding`, such as gzipped preview files, pass through untouched.
- WebSocket upgrades pass through, because chi's writer delegates `Hijack` and `Unwrap` before any header is written.
- The HTTP/2 requests carried inside the `/api/v1/tunnel` WebSocket go through the same handler, so remote desktops get the compression too.
- Clients need no change. iOS and Android `fetch`, Chromium, and Node's HTTP/2 proxy path decode gzip themselves, and none of them strips `Content-Encoding`.

## Testing

- New `TestLANManagerGzipsJSONButNotEventStreams`: a JSON response comes back gzipped and round-trips, and an event stream comes back unencoded. `go vet ./internal/httpd/` is clean.
- A/B load test, run back to back on the same machine and network with the same 320-session seeded board, through a named Cloudflare tunnel served from BOM. Each simulated phone polls `/sessions`, `/orchestrators` and `/projects` every 2 s:

| Simulated phones | Without gzip, p50 / p95 per poll | With gzip, p50 / p95 per poll |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 541 / 1,942 ms | **335 / 492 ms** |
| 10 | 1,326 / 2,377 ms | **305 / 562 ms** |
| 40 | 7,654 / 10,187 ms (16.8 req/s) | **285 / 522 ms (60 req/s)** |
| 80 | 14,447 / 14,817 ms (20.2 req/s) | **324 / 713 ms (119 req/s)** |
| 150 | 25,769 / 26,175 ms (30 req/s) | 2,329 / 3,349 ms (185 req/s) |

- Phones held within the 2 s poll (p95 ≤ 2 s, ≥ 99% OK) went from **1 to 80**. There were no errors in either run.
- Against the listener directly, without a tunnel, latency and CPU were unchanged at 20, 40 and 60 phones: p95 17–21 ms on both builds, daemon CPU 54% vs 57% at 60 phones.

## Accept-Encoding review follow-up (#7267)

Fixed the review finding at `ba543dafaa538ee172033e1ae9a134ce3ff5e4ae`: `gzip;q=0` and `gzip;q=0, identity;q=1` now return identity encoding. Supported positive weights select the highest preferred supported encoding; malformed weights and ambiguous duplicate rejections do not permit compression. Existing encodings, loopback behavior and authentication boundaries remain covered.

Local validation on macOS arm64 with pinned Go 1.27.1, private scratch state/cache, `GOMAXPROCS=2`, `-p=1` and `CGO_ENABLED=0`:

- Independently reproduced the pinned chi 5.1.0 defect before changing source (12-case probe: 4 passed, 8 failed).
- PASS: `go test -mod=readonly -count=1 -timeout=30s -v internal/httpd/remote_compression.go internal/httpd/remote_compression_test.go` — 3 top-level tests, 37 negotiation subcases (39 leaf cases), including q=0/mixed preferences, wildcard/duplicate/malformed values, encoded passthrough and SSE flush.
- PASS: `go test -mod=readonly -count=1 -timeout=45s -run '^TestLANManagerCompression' -v ./internal/httpd` — 3 top-level tests and 10 router subcases (12 leaf cases). Actual ephemeral loopback sockets verify SSE flush while the handler is open and WebSocket-carried HTTP/2 unauthorized/q=0/gzip responses; recorder-based actual-router checks cover loopback/auth/identity/control/error envelopes.
- `git diff --check` passed. Full local backend/race/lint/API/sqlc suites were not run under the bounded shared-resource admission. Full HTTP package compilation succeeded, but only the named integration tests ran. The current-head remote CI result is recorded above; the author's original load measurements do not constitute validation of the review follow-ups. No external tunnel or native-app test was performed for this change.

- CI lint follow-up `aefd439e4b6e2bf37523d215e9b3fb8375638faf`: corrected Staticcheck QF1011 in the integration fixture by inferring the existing `http.Handler` type. This one-line correction was pushed separately; lint now passes on the final head. The deflate-framing correction was subsequently validated and pushed as described below.

## Deflate framing review follow-up

Fixed in `37809725127c3301870b91ab3c35a95c215affe6`: the chi compressor now overrides its default raw-DEFLATE encoder with `zlib.NewWriterLevel` for HTTP `Content-Encoding: deflate`. The negotiation regressions now decode with `zlib.NewReader`, including plain `deflate`, `gzip;q=0, deflate;q=1`, higher deflate quality, wildcard and repeated-header cases.

- PASS on the corrected source: pinned Go1.27.1 `go test -mod=readonly -count=1 -timeout=30s -v internal/httpd/remote_compression.go internal/httpd/remote_compression_test.go` — 3 top-level tests plus 37 subcases (39 leaf cases), including encoded passthrough and SSE flushing. Private warmed cache, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOMAXPROCS=2, -p=1, CGO_ENABLED=0; common phase32.303s, Go test2.260s. All frozen source hashes stayed unchanged, owned process group empty.
- This was a two-file test invocation. The full httpd package, updated integration fixture, race/lint/API/sqlc/full suites and real wire integration were not rerun locally for this correction. The earlier 12 integration leaf passes above belong to `ba543dafaa` before this encoder correction. All20 remote CI checks and AO native static review subsequently passed on this correction; full local suite gaps remain as listed.

## Range and ETag review follow-up

Addresses [review 5697866020](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7128#pullrequestreview-5697866020):

- Requests carrying `Range` bypass compression, including when `If-Range` makes the file handler return the whole file. A206 response also bypasses compression when no Range header was supplied, preserving its bytes, Content-Range, Content-Length and ETag.
- A strong ETag becomes weak only when the middleware applies gzip/deflate to previously unencoded JSON. Existing weak validators, identity/non-JSON responses and pre-encoded responses remain unchanged.
- The real artifact route is exercised through the authenticated remote handler on an ephemeral loopback socket with a scratch `.json` file. Regressions cover gzip/deflate decoding,100-byte ranges, matching/stale/weak If-Range and weak If-None-Match revalidation. Existing SSE-flush and WebSocket-carried HTTP/2 checks also pass.
- Local pinned Go1.27.1, private state/cache, GOMAXPROCS2/-p1:48 focused middleware leaf cases;69 combined focused leaf cases; full `./internal/httpd/...` race run1,135 leaf cases across five packages (360.152s). After the test-only lint correction, the full affected controller race suite passed again:846 leaf cases (106.765s). No full-backend race/Windows/native-client pass is claimed locally for this follow-up.

## 304 revalidation review follow-up

Addresses [review 5699316469](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7128#pullrequestreview-5699316469) in `712ef57e0b117ce9babb2099018328dc8654ac55`:

- With gzip or deflate negotiated, a 304 keeps the weak validator used for the compressed JSON representation. Since Go removes Content-Type before ServeContent writes a 304, the middleware conservatively weakens a strong ETag when that type is unavailable. Known non-JSON types, identity/rejected-compression requests, Range requests and pre-encoded responses preserve their existing policy.
- A 304 bypasses the encoder and remains bodyless, including when a handler retains its JSON Content-Type.
- The real authenticated scratch JSON-artifact regression now expects a weak ETag for gzip/deflate revalidation. It also covers strong/list/wildcard If-None-Match and identity/q=0/range revalidation; middleware cases cover missing/retained types, existing weak tags and encodings.
- The review has no associated inline thread to resolve. No review dismissal or approval is claimed.

## Vary and variant-cache review follow-up

Addresses [review 5712164208](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7128#pullrequestreview-5712164208) in `0dcc1fd55a7ad0755c2bad95f3e3281a5cda9c3b`:

- A final response-header boundary adds Accept-Encoding to Vary when missing. It runs after handler/encoder header changes, so 304, identity/q=0 and partial-response paths retain the same variant key. Existing Vary fields, case-insensitive Accept-Encoding and wildcard are preserved.
- Both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 desktop-proxy relays merge the CORS Origin token with upstream Vary, retaining other tokens and wildcard. Authentication, SSE flushing and WebSocket-carried HTTP/2 behavior remain covered by the existing tests.
- Regressions exercise real authenticated JSON-artifact responses, 200/206/304 negotiation cases, existing Vary values and actual proxy sockets. The separate Chrome comparison verifies that changed encodings contact upstream after a 304 instead of silently reusing a fresh cached variant.
- CI typecheck follow-up in `22a2ab4fde3a97c5b1f248267b8a8815f479bc95`: use `setHeader` for the multi-value HTTP/2 fixture before `writeHead`. This corrects TS2769 without changing production code or weakening the assertion; the complete proxy file passed 74/74 again. Full new-head typecheck subsequently passed in CI.
- This review is body-only: no inline thread IDs are associated with its review ID, so no thread-resolution mutation is available.

title: feat(desktop): combine mobile wake controls and add menu bar status
body:
Code changes: +278 -140  
Tests: +476 -67  
Others: +83 -11  

## What

Shows AO’s active Stay Awake status in the macOS menu bar and combines mobile wake controls into one closed-lid-capable switch. Includes Ronish’s independent-wake follow-up and supersedes #7143.

## Why

Wake changes the Mac’s sleep behavior beyond the AO window. Its active state should stay visible, and the mobile switch should clearly include closed-lid operation.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The menu bar does not show an active wake hold. | AO’s icon includes the same Coffee symbol as the sidebar while wake is active; attention counts remain visible. |
| Mobile settings has separate idle and closed-lid wake controls. | One **Keep this Mac awake** switch requests closed-lid mode, with explicit help and safety details. |
| Saved mobile wake depends on the mobile listener. | Wake starts and restores independently of mobile access; explicit wake-off releases it. |

Actual-app before/after captures remain unavailable: the native-control service rejects Electron access despite the user’s renewed approval. No screenshots or physical lid-close pass are claimed.

## How

Shows a coffee indicator beside AO’s macOS menu bar icon while a local desktop or Connect Mobile wake hold is active. It stays visible when the AO window is closed, and disappears when the hold ends.

Uses the same outlined Lucide Coffee symbol as the sidebar, with Retina assets, localized hover/menu status, and a 36px sidebar button and 14px icon matching Settings. Attention counts remain visible; failed status reads preserve the last active indication with a question mark.

The main process uses native Node HTTP fetches so daemon browser-origin checks do not reject its status polls. It observes the local daemon independently of the renderer, with request timeouts, overlapping-poll prevention, stale-response guards, and shutdown cleanup. Includes two binary icon assets and their Lucide license.

Mobile settings now has one **Keep this Mac awake** switch. Enabling it requests closed-lid wakefulness through the native recovery helper; disabling it releases both wake modes. The separate lid switch is removed.

Wake is independent of Connect Mobile: it starts immediately with mobile access off, survives mobile enable/disable, and restores on daemon boot even with mobile off or a failed listener bind. Wake restoration does not start listeners, connectors, or change credentials. Explicit wake-off and full daemon shutdown release the hold. Failed awake startup restores the previous saved preference.

The row now says **Keep your Mac running, even with the lid closed.** Battery, ventilation, and below-10%-battery/critical-heat details are in an accessible info tooltip. Helper/recovery status stays inline; the isolated-data explanation is available in the info tooltip. Copy is localized in all nine locales.

Existing idle-only holds are not presented as closed-lid-enabled; the single switch can explicitly upgrade them. There is no idle-only fallback: older daemons, isolated data directories, or unsupported hardware show an unavailable reason and cannot enable the combined control. Saved closed-lid requests remain clearable when support is lost. The remembered loading state includes the lid preference so the switch does not change meaning while status loads.

Closed-lid registration completes before creating or resuming desktop awake ownership. A failed registration leaves existing or paused ownership untouched. If desktop startup fails afterward, the saved mobile request remains visible and clearable. Regression coverage uses both real controls with their shared hook.

Includes all commits and fixes from #7143, which is superseded by this combined PR. Uses the existing wake service/API, native power policy, and safety limits.


The inline default-data-folder status is removed; its explanation remains in the info tooltip and the power isolation checks are unchanged.

Chat fixtures use main's shared QueryClientProvider helper with an empty workspace cache and background refreshes disabled, keeping fixture reads local. Existing test assertions remain in place.

Rebased onto current `main` at `b303d2fe6`, preserving the upstream Connect mobile switch, connector installation state, and locale/plural handling. Added the new Russian locale to the wake copy and generated tray catalog. Adapted regression tests to the new switch and loading-row replacement. The quick-tunnel test now waits for the connector startup record before cancellation, avoiding a reproducible scheduling race.

The cancelled native-helper job passed on retry. Both update-helper architecture builds and its standalone state tests also passed locally (cross-compiled on Apple silicon; Intel execution verified by CI).

Previous-head local validation (`6d64f9d89`, retained for history):

- Complete renderer smoke rerun passed: 143 tests. The initial run with five workers hit nine startup/visibility timeouts; the complete rerun with two workers passed.

title: fix(session): stop the Chat controller and bound the retire notice when replacing an orchestrator
body:
Code changes: +41 -3  
Tests: +176 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Restarting a project orchestrator (a clean replacement) had two problems with Chat orchestrators.

1. `RetireForReplacement` never stopped the Chat controller, although `Kill` does. After every Restart, the old `ao chat-host` and its provider kept running with their working directory inside the worktree that Restart deletes.
2. Restart sends a retire notice to the old orchestrator first, and it waited on that notice without a limit. If the old provider stopped responding, Restart hung and no replacement started.

Refs #6449. I suspect the leftover process is what blocks the worktree removal on Windows and produces the 500 in that report, but I haven't verified it there (see "Not covered").

## Changes

`RetireForReplacement` now stops the Chat controller before it removes the worktree, on both retire paths. The stop gets 15 seconds. If it fails, the error is logged and the replacement continues.

`sendRetireNotice` gives the notice 10 seconds. It waits on a goroutine instead of relying on the context alone, because the provider call can run past its context.

## Verification

I ran these live on macOS against an isolated daemon with a real Chat orchestrator, using the request Restart sends (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators` with `clean: true`).

| Scenario | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code at its real usage limit, Restart to Codex | 201, old Chat processes still running (2 of 2) | 201, none left |
| Same, on the `v0.13.5` tag | 201, old process still running (1 of 1) | not run |
| Terminal-mode orchestrator at the usage limit | 201, none left | unchanged |
| Provider frozen with `SIGSTOP`, message in flight | no response after 420 s | 201 in 20 s, old processes gone |

These tests fail on `main` and pass on this branch:

- `TestRetireForReplacementStopsChatController`, with and without a workspace. It checks that the controller stops and that this happens before `ForceDestroy`.
- `TestSpawnOrchestratorCleanDoesNotWaitForUnresponsiveOrchestrator`.
- `TestRetireForReplacementBoundsAHangingChatStop`, which also fails if the 15 second limit is removed.

`TestRetireForReplacementDoesNotStopChatForTUISession` passes on both. It guards Terminal sessions.

Locally, gofmt, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass, and the API spec and sqlc generators show no drift. The race tests for the two changed packages pass. A full local `go test -race ./...` was not usable: the machine was under heavy load and many test binaries were killed. I'm leaving the full suite to CI. Three tests failed locally in packages this PR does not touch. The Crush auth test also fails on unmodified `main`. A conpty PTY test and a browserruntime liveness test pass on `main` when run alone.

golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports one revive `time-naming` finding locally, on `scriptStepMinute` in `session_manager/manager.go`. That line is already on `main` (from #6901), and this PR doesn't change it. CI lint passes on `main` with a restored lint cache, so I expect it to pass here too. If it doesn't, this PR isn't the cause.

## Not covered

The report describes "Internal server error" on Windows after Codex hit its usage limit. On macOS a real usage limit doesn't reproduce the failure: Restart succeeds and only leaves the processes behind. The connection to this PR is my guess that, on Windows, the leftover process stops the worktree from being deleted. I haven't tested that, and the hang fix on its own ends in a 503 or no response, not a 500. I also haven't tested a Codex usage limit.

title: fix(hermes): accept Homebrew bottles whose banner reads vunknown
body:
Code changes: +69 -2  
Tests: +92 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Installing Hermes from **Settings → Harness → Hermes Agent → Install** on macOS runs `brew install hermes-agent`. The install succeeds, but AO then rejects the binary it just installed:

```
resolve installed hermes binary: hermes: /opt/homebrew/bin/hermes: version banner
"Hermes Agent vunknown (2026.9.24)" is not a Hermes release line AO has qualified:
agent: binary identity unknown
```

Hermes is then unusable in both Terminal UI and Chat, through AO's own default install path.

## Root cause

Homebrew builds `hermes-agent` from the release **tarball** (`archive/refs/tags/v0.22.4.tar.gz`), which has no git metadata. Hermes derives its banner version from git, so the bottle prints `Hermes Agent vunknown (…)`. The identity probe (`probeNativeVersion`) accepts only a `vX.Y.Z` banner on a qualified line (`0.21`, `0.22`) or a `vgit.<sha>` banner resolved through the source checkout. `vunknown` matches neither, so a genuine 0.22.4 install is rejected.

## Changes

- `probeNativeVersion` gains one fallback, `qualifiedHomebrewKeg`, mirroring the existing `vgit.<sha>` fallback. It applies only when **all** of these hold:
  - the banner is exactly `Hermes Agent vunknown[ …]`;
  - the launcher resolves into a `Cellar/hermes-agent/<version>[_<revision>]/…` keg;
  - the keg's `INSTALL_RECEIPT.json` records the same `source.versions.stable`;
  - that version is on a qualified line.
- Every other unrecognised banner stays rejected (other formulae, `HEAD-<sha>` kegs, missing or mismatched receipts, unqualified lines, `vunknown` outside a keg).
- This matches `installedVersionText` in `systeminstall`, which already takes a Homebrew install's version from its keg for display and update checks. The admission check now agrees with it.
- Tests: the system install locations `ResolveBinary` probes are now a package variable (`systemLaunchers`, same values). `fakeNativeBinary` clears it so a qualified Homebrew Hermes on the developer's machine no longer takes precedence over the fixture. Without this, `TestFreshLaunchTitlesNewNativeConversation` and `TestRestoreResumesTitledConversationWithoutCreating` fail on a Mac that has Homebrew Hermes installed.

## Testing

New tests:
- `TestHomebrewUnknownBannerQualifiesFromKeg`: table covering the accepted cases (qualified keg, banner without date, revised formula `0.21.6_1`) and the rejected ones (unqualified line, receipt mismatch, no receipt, another formula's keg, `HEAD-` keg, other unrecognised banner, non-Hermes banner, `vunknown` outside a keg).
- `TestProbeAcceptsHomebrewBottleWithUnknownBanner`: end to end through `probeNativeVersion` with a fake keg binary printing the real banner; a keg without a receipt is still rejected with the existing reason.

Against a real install (macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Homebrew `hermes-agent` 0.22.4) with a clean `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, via a throwaway local test that was not committed: banner `Hermes Agent vunknown (2026.9.24)` → keg version `0.22.4` → `probeNativeVersion` **accepts** (rejected on `main`).

Local runs (Go 1.27.1, from `backend/`):
- `gofmt -l .`: clean · `go build ./...`: ok · `go vet ./...`: ok · `GOOS=windows go vet` (hermes, systeminstall): ok
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/adapters/agent/hermes/ ./internal/service/systeminstall/`: pass
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on `./internal/adapters/agent/hermes/...`: 0 issues
- Full `backend-core` package set (`go test -race -count=1`, CI's package list), run before the final test-isolation commit: 199 packages ok. The remaining failures are **pre-existing on `main` on this machine** (verified on a clean `main` worktree at the same base) and come from real installs on the host: `crush` (local auth), `opencode`, `opencodev2`, `opencodev2acp` (a real `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`), `tmux` (supervised-exit integration). CI runners do not have these installs; I'm relying on CI for those jobs.
- Full-repo `golangci-lint` also reports `session_manager/manager.go:6307` (`time-naming: scriptStepMinute`). That's existing code on `main`, untouched here; the lint job does not use `only-new-issues`, so it may show on this PR.

## Not in this PR

- Homebrew's `hermes-agent` bottle printing `vunknown` is an upstream packaging issue; to be reported to the formula/Hermes separately.
- Install progress visibility (the install job publishes no output until it finishes) is a separate issue.

## Checklist

- [X] Branched from main (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [X] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [X] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [X] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: feat: add local harness troubleshooting with helper terminals
body:
Code changes: +884 -15  
Tests: +357 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Adds a Troubleshoot tab to every local harness so users whose installation or login disagrees with AO detection can collect fresh diagnostics, review them, and start an embedded helper terminal.

## Why

Users need a local way to investigate detection mismatches, verify whether a repair worked, and prepare evidence for an AO bug report without automatically sharing credentials or filing an issue.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| An installation or login mismatch requires manual investigation outside the harness page. | Each local harness has fresh installation/authentication checks, sanitized evidence, and an optional embedded helper. |
| Users assemble reproduction details and detection results themselves. | An editable, copy-only issue draft separates user observations from initial and fresh AO evidence. |
| Users interpret diagnostic codes and manually find installation/login settings. | Plain-language results explain missing installation, rejected or unconfirmed sign-in, incomplete checks, or successful checks, with direct setup actions and a usable no-helper fallback. |
| There is no helper launch or recovery flow on this page. | Launch retries preserve the exact request and ID; a stopped or exited helper can be replaced with a new request. |
| A parked terminal with stale appearance props can switch the entire app between dark and light. | Parked terminals preserve the app appearance and refresh their palette when revealed, retaining the terminal and scrollback. |

Native before/after evidence was captured and inspected in an isolated Electron checkout using the same Codex harness, scratch data and 1320x862 window. The base Health screen and final guided result screen are available as `troubleshooting-base-health.png` and `troubleshooting-guided-results-dark.png`; `troubleshooting-guided-results-light-narrow.png` shows the 700px light-mode viewport. These files were provided locally for manual attachment because the available GitHub tools do not upload image attachments. Real installation/sign-in checks and fresh rechecks preserved both dark and light mode. Helper provider launches and every failure-state layout were not re-exercised natively in this update.

## How

- Make the flow understandable without reading JSON: Check installation and sign-in, see the current installation/authentication/results phase, then read a plain-language outcome and recommended next step.
- Open the affected agent setup directly for missing installation or rejected sign-in. When no helper is ready, offer direct Codex/Claude Code setup actions and make the copy-prompt fallback usable instead of showing an unavailable launch button.
- Explain that AO keeps the report local until the user starts a helper. Keep technical evidence and error details collapsed, preserve draft edits and exact launch retry payloads, and distinguish unconfirmed sign-in from being signed out. New copy is translated in all nine supported locales.

- Export classified installation/authentication observations; omit identities, credential contents, paths, raw errors, and installer output.
- Launch a standalone Codex or Claude Code helper with explicit Accept Edits permissions and a pending request whose ID and exact payload survive retries and rechecks. Keep the terminal accessible across Settings visits, provide a Stop helper action, and allow a replacement with a new request after stop or exit. Ignore terminal events from superseded sessions.
- Wait for installation verification to finish, then explicitly probe authentication. Preserve initial evidence separately and never treat helper messages or failed rechecks as verification success.
- Guide users through setup checks and investigation with compact status summaries, check timestamps, expandable details, a sticky terminal toolbar, contextual progress/copy feedback, and protected draft edits.
- Provide a copyable troubleshooting prompt when no supported helper is ready, plus an editable issue draft. Nothing is submitted automatically.
- Rebase onto main `63581129a`, retaining all existing fixes and every upstream translation. Add all 44 troubleshooting strings for Russian, which main now supports.
- Prevent hidden/parked terminals from applying stale appearance props to the global document. Reapply their palette on visibility changes without recreating the terminal or losing scrollback.

First-version limits: local harnesses only; embedded helpers are Codex and Claude Code, with a copy-prompt fallback for other agents. Diagnostics describe observed checks rather than a new complete detection-rule registry. Accept Edits uses native harness permission controls and permits scratch-workspace edits; it is not an additional AO sandbox. Troubleshooting controls are translated in all nine supported locales; diagnostic evidence and helper prompts stay in English. Issue submission remains manual.

Regression tests reproduce a hidden terminal overwriting the app's dark/light mode and named palette. The guard now prevents those global writes while parked, and both dark-to-light and light-to-dark cases pass. The collection handler itself does not change the theme. Native collection and rechecking on the guided flow preserved dark and light mode.

## Testing

- Final guided-flow validation: all five troubleshooting, local/remote harness and localization suites passed (176 tests); frontend and E2E TypeScript checks passed. Coverage includes stage transitions, missing installation, rejected/unconfirmed sign-in, no-helper setup and copy fallback, failed rechecks, exact launch retries and edited drafts. The preceding terminal appearance update passed all 412 affected tests, including the two regressions that failed before that fix.
- Cloud client: generation produces no contract drift; typechecks, all 31 tests, build, and pack dry-run passed. No daemon API contract changes were required.
- Product UI: typecheck, all 162 tests, build, and pack dry-run passed.
- Docs: catalog extraction/compilation passed. Translation validation passed after LF-normalizing the nine relevant source files to match Linux checkout behavior. The production build passed. Local docs tests encounter the Windows alias-resolution failure for `@/i18n/locales`.
- The full frontend Vitest suite was started locally and has failures outside this PR's files, including macOS updater and Windows filesystem/CLI-link assumptions. A full local pass is not claimed.
- Exact-head hosted validation for `676426f28e4e39defef615e095c911eb711e69c8` is tracked in [PR checks](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7133/checks). This Windows host cannot reproduce Ubuntu's pinned Playwright container or Linux Electron boundary jobs; those are verified in hosted CI. macOS jobs are skipped by the workflow's UI-only PR policy, so no current-head native macOS validation is claimed.

No publishing, deployment, or merge is part of validation. The pre-existing ScriptRunPanel snapshot is preserved outside the PR.

title: docs: add pr-approach-note skill
body:
Code changes: +0 -0  
Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +111 -0

A PR description here usually reads like a changelog: a restatement of the issue, some adjectives, then a file-by-file summary. The reviewer already has the diff open, so that mostly tells them what they can see. What they cannot see is why the change took this shape, which alternative got rejected, and what the author is still unsure about.

So this adds a skill for writing that note in first person, with a before/after example built from #7125. It also spells out what not to write, because the banned list is the part that actually keeps the machine register out: no "robust", no em-dash clause joins, no three-adjective bullets, no closing paragraph that repeats the note.

`.agents/skills/*` is ignored on purpose, so the new skill is whitelisted in `.gitignore` next to `ao-desktop-dev`, `bug-triage`, and `pr-description`. I left `.claude/skills` alone because `pr-description` is not mirrored there either.

I also installed the same file under `~/.config/opencode/skills/pr-approach-note/`, which is how it can be used across worktrees before this merges. That copy is local and not part of the PR.

title: feat(claude): gate models the installed Claude Code is too old for
body:
Code changes: +578 -9  
Tests: +270 -3  
Others: +6 -0 (OpenAPI spec + generated schema.ts)

## What

Gate Claude models that the installed Claude Code CLI is too old to use, instead of letting the user pick one and fail on the first turn.

## Why

The Claude model picker lists models from the provider's `/v1/models`. That list says what the account may use, not what the local CLI can drive. A user on an older Claude Code could select e.g. `claude-opus-5-5` and get a raw `API Error: 400 {...}`.

A version × model matrix (Claude Code 2.0.67, 2.1.101, 2.1.172, 2.1.239, 2.1.309) showed:

- The API itself rejects too-new models with `error_code: claude_code_version_too_old` and names the minimum version: `claude-opus-5-5` needs 2.1.280+, `claude-fable-5-1` needs 2.1.251+.
- Not every newer model is gated: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5` work on 2.0.67. So AO must not infer requirements; it records what the API reports.
- Aliases (`opus`, `sonnet`, `opus[1m]`) never fail. They silently resolve to an older model on an older CLI, e.g. `opus` → `claude-opus-4-5` on 2.0.67 and `claude-opus-4-8` on 2.1.172. `fable` fails outright on CLIs that predate the alias.

## How

- **Learn from the API** (`claudeacp/driver.go`). The Claude prompt-failure classifier recognizes `claude_code_version_too_old`. It replaces the raw error with "Claude Code X does not support <model>; version Y or newer is required. Run `claude update`…", attaches the new `ports.ErrAgentVersionTooOld`, and records the minimum for that concrete model ID.
  - The ACP failure hook now receives the session's selected model.
  - Aliases are not recorded, because they resolve per CLI version.
- **Persist minimums** (`claudecode/model_versions.go`). The minimum version per model is stored in `<StateDir>/harnesses/claude-code/model-versions.json`. It is seeded with the two observed requirements so users see the gate before their first failure.
- **Gate on read** (`service/agent`, `daemon`). A new optional `Deps.ModelGate` runs on every `Models`/`ModelCatalog` read, so the durable catalog cache stays the raw discovered list.
  - The Claude gate compares against `claude --version`, cached by the executable's path, size and mtime, so `claude update` lifts the gate automatically.
  - A too-new model gets `requiresVersion` + `unavailableReason` and loses `isDefault`.
  - An unknown installed version gates nothing.
- **Picker** (`AgentModelCombobox`). Gated models render disabled, with the reason and remedy shown under the label.
- **Spawn** (`session_manager`). Spawning on a gated model fails up front with `UNSUPPORTED_MODEL` and the same explanation.
- **Alias resolution.** After a successful turn, the Claude binding reads the answering model from Claude's own session transcript (tail-read, skipping `<synthetic>` entries).
  - If the selected model is an alias, it emits the existing `ChatEventModelRerouted` once per (selection, served) pair, so the existing reroute indicator shows e.g. "opus → claude-opus-4-8".
  - The chat workspace now hides a recorded reroute once the user selects a different model.

### Intentional limits

- Terminal (non-chat) Claude sessions don't learn new minimums, because the rejection appears only in the TUI. They are still covered by the seeded and previously learned requirements, and by the spawn check.
- After a turn records a new requirement, an open picker reflects it on its next catalog fetch. No push invalidation is added.
- Alias resolution assumes the ACP session id is Claude's transcript UUID (true for `claude-agent-acp`). If the transcript isn't found, nothing is reported.

## Testing

Per my workflow, nothing was run locally; CI validates this PR. New tests:

- `claudecode/model_versions_test.go`:
  - parsing both error forms
  - persistence, and learned values overriding seeds
  - gating (only too-new models, input not mutated, unknown version is a no-op)
  - version caching by executable fingerprint
  - transcript model extraction
- `claudeacp/driver_test.go`: version-too-old classification, recording (not for aliases), and alias-only served-model reporting.
- `service/agent/catalog_test.go`: the gate applies on read and the cache keeps the raw catalog.
- `AgentModelCombobox.test.tsx`: a gated model is disabled, shows its reason, and can't be selected.

The version × model behavior above was verified manually against real CLI installs before implementation.

title: perf(sessions): cut repeated work out of board polls
body:
Code changes: +80 -6\
Tests: +120 -1\
Others: +206 -0 (sqlc-generated `gen/sessions.sql.go`)

## What

Two cuts to the work each phone poll makes the daemon do. A phone polls `/sessions`, `/orchestrators` and `/projects` every 2 seconds on a tunnel:

1. `GET /api/v1/orchestrators` now reads only orchestrator rows, through a new `ListOrchestratorSessions` query. Before, it read every session row and then dropped the workers.
2. The output-type repair that a board read runs for stale rows now runs once per row revision instead of once per row per concurrent read.

## Why

Profiling the daemon under simulated phone load (320-session board) found:

- **`/orchestrators` was about a third of each poll's server cost.** It decoded all 320 rows (about 4 ms) to return an empty list.
- **A cold board queued every poll behind one lock.** When rows need the repair (an empty `artifact_dir` after upgrade or import), every concurrent `/sessions` read called `ReconcileSessionOutputType` for every stale row, and each call takes the lifecycle `reconcileMu`. With 20 concurrent first reads, each took about 2.3 s.

## How

- `listRecords` takes the whole `ListFilter`. With no project and `OrchestratorOnly`, it uses the new query, which is the same column list as `ListAllSessions` plus `WHERE kind = 'orchestrator'` and the same ordering. The response bodies are byte-identical.
- `claimOutputReconcile(id, revision)` is a `sync.Map` from session to the row revision whose repair was claimed. The first read of a stale revision claims and repairs; other reads of that revision skip the call.
  - Skipping readers still return the corrected output type, because the read sets it on the response before the repair call, as before.
  - The repair's write bumps `revision` (trigger), so a later mismatch is claimed afresh.
  - A failed repair releases the claim, so the next read retries.
- The query file was regenerated with `npm run sqlc` (sqlc v1.31.1). The generated diff only adds the new query.

## Testing

- **New tests:**
  - `TestListRunsEachRepairOncePerRevision`: 8 concurrent lists run one repair per stale row, and a failing repair is retried on the next list. With the dedupe disabled it fails with "8 concurrent lists ran 24 repairs, want 3".
  - `TestListOrchestratorSessionsSkipsWorkers`
  - `TestClaimOutputReconcileOncePerRevision`
- **Changed test:** `TestListMatchesGetForEverySessionShape` now runs its `Get` pass on a fresh service. The fake reconciler never writes, so the list's claim would otherwise make the same service skip those repairs.
- **Test runs:** `go test ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/...` passes; the new tests also pass under `-race`. `go vet ./...` is clean.
- **Load A/B** against the daemon's LAN listener, `main` vs this branch, same machine and same 320-session board. Each simulated phone polls the three endpoints every 2 s:

| Scenario | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Cold start, rows need repair, 60 phones: p95 / p99 | 749 / 1,222 ms, CPU 89% | **388 / 806 ms, CPU 58%** |
| Steady, 60 phones: p95, CPU | 26 ms, 72% | **21 ms, 52%** |
| Steady, 200 phones: p95, CPU | 101 ms, 211% | **25 ms, 151%** |
| Steady, 400 phones: CPU % per req/s (2 runs each) | 0.65, 0.69 | **0.54, 0.49** |

At 400 phones, latency on this shared machine swung between about 0.5 s and 5 s p95 on both builds from run to run, so I compare CPU per request there. That is about 22–25% lower on this branch. There were no errors at any step.

title: fix(opencode-v2): let model discovery finish the data-home migration
body:
Code changes: +38 -3  
Tests: +174 -0  
Others: +0 -0

Model discovery for OpenCode 2 failed at 30 seconds with `opencode: copy legacy data store: context deadline exceeded`. The copy is a one-time migration of the pre-isolation data store. On a store that needs more than 30 seconds it never finished: the timeout deleted the staging directory, and the next refresh started the copy again from zero.

The copy was not new work. Readiness already runs `PrepareV2DataHome` under `opencodeV2MigrationTimeout` (30 minutes). Discovery called the same function through `modelcatalog.Discover`, but under the generic `modelCatalogLoadTimeout`, so it was abandoning a copy the rest of the daemon was still working on. `modelCatalogLoadBudget` now gives `opencode-v2` the migration budget plus the CLI timeout. Every other harness still gets 30 seconds.

I considered taking discovery out of the migration entirely: readiness owns the copy, and discovery returns a "preparing" catalog instead of waiting on the lock. That is the better shape, but discovery has to know the data home before it can run the CLI, so it would change that contract inside a timeout fix. The cost of what I shipped is that an explicit refresh on the very first run can wait for the copy instead of failing at 30 seconds. Passive catalog reads do not wait: they return the persisted catalog and refresh in the background, and a scope with no catalog returns after 500 ms with a refreshing placeholder.

Two smaller changes came out of the same trace. A legacy database locked by a running OpenCode 1 now fails after 10 seconds with "quit OpenCode 1 and retry" instead of sitting inside the budget. A timeout now says the legacy store was left unchanged and retrying is safe.

Evidence: the regression test fails on the old one-line budget with the same `context deadline exceeded`, and passes now. I ran the whole path on Windows against a fake `opencode.exe`. The committed end-to-end test is POSIX-only and skips on Windows, so it has only run in CI. The two catalog tests that also fail here (directory mode 777, qwen config fixture) reproduce on unmodified `main`, and the other Windows failures are the known symlink and Codex ACL ones. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and the two touched package suites passed locally; `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --all` needs Docker, which is not installed here.

`#7066` also edits `v2home.go`, but it adds installer helpers above this code and does not touch `PrepareV2DataHome`.

Fixes #7125.

title: fix(chat): treat a chat host whose pid was reused as dead
body:
Code changes: +113 -10\
Tests: +60 -0\
Others: +5 -3

## What

Resume works again for a Chat whose persistent host died and whose pid the OS gave to another process. AO now launches a new host and natively resumes the conversation. Before, it showed this error on every Resume:

```
AO could not safely reconnect to the session's still-running chat process: resume agent agent-orchestrator-223: resume chat: chat conversation recovery is inconclusive: persistent host: chat host ownership is inconclusive: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:51390: connectex: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it.
```

## Why

Fixes #6695. Same failure on Windows: #6639.

When an update or reboot kills a host, its `host.json` and `host.lock` stay in `~/.ao/data/chat-hosts/<session>/`. `ConnectOrStart` treats the host as alive while `processalive.Alive(pid)` is true, and it never launches a second provider over a live owner. Once the OS gives that pid to an unrelated process, the check is true forever. Resume fails, and so does every startup reattach retry from #6987. #6695 has the live evidence: the recorded pid belonged to `AppleAccountIntents`, which started after the restart, and nothing listened on the port. Windows reuses pids especially quickly.

## How

- `processalive.AliveSince(pid, recordedAt)` is `Alive` plus one more rule: the process must have started no later than the record naming its pid, with 1 s of slack for coarse timestamps. A process that started later holds a reused pid, so the recorded owner is dead.
- **Windows** reads creation times from the system process list (`NtQuerySystemInformation`). The list covers every process without opening it. This matters because a reused pid often belongs to a service that a normal user can't open (`ACCESS_DENIED`, which `Alive` counts as alive).
- **macOS** reads the kernel's fork time (`kern.proc.pid`). A later clock step doesn't move it.
- **Linux** keeps bare-pid liveness. Its start times are ticks since boot, and their wall-clock value moves when the clock steps, so a live host could read as newer than its own record. Recording boot id + start ticks, as `previewserver` does, is the upgrade path if reuse shows up there.
- `persistenthost` uses `AliveSince` wherever it decides whether a recorded host is alive:
  - the descriptor checks in `ConnectOrStart`, compared with `StartedAt`;
  - `Reconcile`, `Shutdown` and `HostPID`;
  - the launch-lock reclaim, compared with the lock file's mtime. The pid and mtime are read from one open file, so a lock replaced mid-check can't pair one owner's pid with another's time.
- Existing stuck descriptors already record `startedAt`, so they recover on the next Resume without manual cleanup.
- The design note (`docs/adr/0003`) records the new rule.

Intentionally unchanged:
- the `ErrAttached` wait loop, because the host itself just answered;
- the host's check on its own provider child;
- other `processalive.Alive` callers (daemon run-file takeover, ConPTY). The wider #6718 covers those; this PR fixes only the Chat recovery bug.

## Testing

- New `TestReusedHostPIDIsNotALiveOwner` checks both directions:
  - **reused:** a pid recorded before its process started gives `ErrNotRunning` and a reclaimable lock;
  - **live:** a pid recorded after its process started stays `ErrOwnershipInconclusive` with `ErrHostExists`.
- Without the fix, the reused case fails with the production error: `chat host ownership is inconclusive: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:…: connect: connection refused`.
- The test is added to the Windows CI job, because CI otherwise runs it on Linux only, where it skips.
- Local macOS run: the new test and the related `persistenthost` tests pass with `-race` (ConnectOrStart, Shutdown, Reconcile, AcquireHostLock, HostLaunchLock, ReconnectOnly). `./internal/processalive` passes too.
- `go vet` is clean for darwin, windows and linux.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports 0 issues for darwin and linux.
- Windows lint, which CI doesn't run, flags the same gosec patterns (unsafe pointer, integer conversion) on the new lines as on the existing lines in `process_windows.go` and `child_windows.go`.

### Manual check on Windows

An unsigned test build is coming from the Desktop build artifacts workflow (version `0.14.6-pidfix.1`). To reproduce the bug on the current nightly first, then confirm the fix:

```powershell
# Quit AO completely from the tray first.
$s   = '<chat-session-id>'   # a chat session that has finished a turn
$dir = "$HOME\.ao\data\chat-hosts\$s"
$old = Get-Content "$dir\host.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
Stop-Process -Id $old.pid -Force                 # kill the host; its files stay behind
$lockTime = (Get-Item "$dir\host.lock").LastWriteTime
# ping stands in for an unrelated process that got the host's pid
$squatter = Start-Process ping -ArgumentList '-t','127.0.0.1' -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru
(Get-Content "$dir\host.json" -Raw) -replace '"pid":\d+', "`"pid`":$($squatter.Id)" |
  Set-Content "$dir\host.json" -NoNewline
Set-Content "$dir\host.lock" "$($squatter.Id)`n" -NoNewline
(Get-Item "$dir\host.lock").LastWriteTime = $lockTime   # keep the lock's original time
```

1. Start AO and open the session. On the nightly you should see the banner above, and Resume should fail the same way.
2. Install the test build and open the session again. It should come back, on its own or after one Resume, with its history.
3. Clean up with `Stop-Process -Id $squatter.Id`.
