Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Updates `baseline-browser-mapping` from 2.10.35 to 2.11.35
Release notes

Sourced from baseline-browser-mapping's releases.

v2.11.0

What's Changed in 2.11.0

  • feat: Adds a new getTimeline() method for getting the series of minimum browser changes, either grouped by date or by browser.
  • refactor: Substantial refactoring of the data compression process that replaces the full list of browsers from @mdn/browser-compat-data and downstream-browsers.json and features from web-features (in their very pared down form) with a change-list timeline that reflects which versions supported Baseline (newly available) on a given date. Thanks to @​swwind for the idea!
  • refactor: Some common functions have been moved to a util.ts module for use in other scripts.
  • fix: Removes process.exit() calls when unsupported option combinations are passed to getCompatibleVersions() and getAllVersions() in favour of throwing an Error. There is a small security risk with process.exit() calls that sites accepting unsanitised inputs could be the subject of attacks. Unsupported config options now throw and Error which should allow for more graceful handling. Thanks to @​bnbdr for flagging this as vulnerability CVE-2026-45819 .

Fixes #134

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

title: feat(mobile): combine keep-awake and closed-lid controls
body:
Code changes: +52 -71  
Tests: +150 -39  
Others: +0 -0  

Consolidated into #7130, which includes all commits and fixes from this PR. Please review and merge #7130.

Mobile settings now has one **Keep this Mac awake** switch. Enabling it requests closed-lid wakefulness through the native recovery helper; disabling it releases both wake modes. The separate lid switch is removed.

The row explicitly says the Mac keeps running with the lid closed and explains phone reachability, operation while mobile access is on even after the phone disconnects, battery use, ventilation, and the existing below-10%-battery/critical-heat stops. Existing helper/recovery status stays inline. Copy is localized in all eight locales.

Existing idle-only holds are not presented as closed-lid-enabled; the single switch can explicitly upgrade them. There is no idle-only fallback: older daemons, isolated data directories, or unsupported hardware show an unavailable reason and cannot enable the combined control. Saved closed-lid requests remain clearable when support is lost. The remembered loading state includes the lid preference so the switch does not change meaning while status loads.

Closed-lid registration completes before creating or resuming desktop awake ownership. A failed registration leaves existing or paused ownership untouched. If desktop startup fails afterward, the saved mobile request remains visible and clearable. Regression coverage uses both real controls with their shared hook.

Independent follow-up to #7130; no backend power policy or safety limits change.

title: fix: preserve Codex effort when retrying failed task startup
body:
Code changes: +21 -28  
Tests: +238 -8  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Preserve the model, effort, and permissions resolved at session creation across failed-start Retry and Chat/TUI restore or resume. Explicit High and Extra High choices remain selected.

An omitted effort inherits the initial project or role default when present. For example, Medium remains pinned after the project default changes to Low. When the saved resolved effort is empty, Retry keeps the provider default instead.

## Why

The retry reconstructed agent settings from project defaults and restored the saved model, but omitted Codex's saved effort. This let a retried task run with the project's or Codex's default instead of the effort selected in New Task.

Other restore paths previously honored only non-empty saved effort, so an empty saved effort could inherit a changed project default on resume. The shared helper now gives empty model and effort the same meaning across all restore paths.

## How

Restore saved model, effort, and permissions in the shared restoredAgentConfig helper used by Retry and Chat/TUI resume. Empty saved model and effort values mean provider defaults for every harness; changed project defaults cannot replace them. Validate Codex tuning against the current catalog before launch without merging changed project defaults; an unsupported effort falls back to the model's provider default, while catalog lookup errors return early. Existing provider conversations continue to resume from their durable Chat settings, so later Chat effort changes are not overwritten by the original launch choice.

Eight Retry cases cover High, Extra High, omitted effort without an initial project default, and omitted effort inheriting Medium, each with unchanged defaults and with defaults changed to Low. Add eight cases covering empty saved models, compatible/incompatible ChatUI model changes, provider-default/saved-model catalog drift, and catalog errors, plus an existing-provider-conversation bypass test. Retry reuses the session and delivers the opening prompt once.

## Testing

- Passed: retry-focused session-manager tests and Chat-service persisted-settings/resume tests.
- Passed on Go 1.27.1: backend-wide build and vet, API regeneration/drift check, sqlc regeneration/drift check, and diff whitespace check.
- Full backend unit run on Windows completed: 153 packages passed and 54 failed. This run inherited worker environment variables and includes platform/context-dependent failures; it is not a pass or a substitute for Linux CI. The session-manager failures reported during focused validation were also reproduced on unchanged source.
- Native CLI E2E command completed with 812 passing cases and four failing fixtures. Three failing fixtures pass when inherited AO session variables are removed; the remaining fixture requires Windows symlink privileges unavailable here.
- Full pinned golangci-lint 2.13.2 run on Windows failed with repository-wide findings and a timeout; a diff-scoped run reported zero issues but also timed out, so neither is claimed as passed. The Linux CI lint check remains required.
- Linux/macOS runners and container checks cannot run locally: this host has neither WSL nor Docker. The CI race command cannot run locally because CGO is disabled and no C compiler is installed. These checks require CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched/rebased from upstream main; one focused change.
- [x] Regression tests added for the reported failure followed by Retry.
- [x] Existing-provider resume logic intentionally unchanged.
- [x] All 20 CI checks pass on 1b6947793; local platform gaps are listed above.

## Review follow-up validation

- All six new tuning-validation cases failed before the fix and pass afterward. Focused retry/catalog tests also cover existing-provider-conversation resumption and retain the original High/Extra High/unspecified cases.
- Passed locally: backend-wide build and vet, API and sqlc generation/drift checks, gofmt, and whitespace checks.
- Full backend unit suite rerun on Windows with AO worker environment variables removed: 153 packages passed, 54 failed. Four packages (gitworktree, project service, session service, and session manager) hit the 10-minute package timeout. This is not a local full-suite pass.
- Full pinned Windows lint reported repository-wide findings and timed out. A separate Linux-target lint attempt hit local disk exhaustion/typechecking errors. Neither local lint attempt is claimed as passed.
- The exact CI session/store race command cannot run locally because CGO is disabled and no C compiler is available.
- All 20 remote CI checks passed on 739a49ea7, including full backend race shards, session/store race, Chat and SQLite race shards, Linux lint, Windows workspace checks, API/sqlc drift, native CLI tests on Linux/macOS/Windows, container tests, and the aggregate backend gate.


## Shared restore follow-up

- Removed duplicated metadata overrides from failed-start Retry, terminal relaunch, and Chat resume. Existing provider conversation resumption and retry catalog validation remain covered.
- Expanded SQLite/reopened-store persistence coverage to 300 cases across Codex, Claude Code, Command Code, and Hermes, worker/orchestrator sessions, and six restore/resume paths. Coverage includes High, Codex Extra High, empty saved effort/model, changed project/role defaults, saved permissions, and native conversation identity. All cases passed locally, along with failed-start Retry regressions.
- Confirmed failures before the fix: all six Codex provider-default restore paths inherited the changed project model; a separate native resume with a saved model inherited the changed project effort instead of preserving empty effort.
- Passed locally: backend-wide build and vet. The full Windows unit run with a three-minute package timeout finished with 151 packages passed and 56 failed; eight packages timed out. Full pinned Windows lint reported repository-wide findings and timed out. These local full-suite/lint attempts are not passes. The exact local race command remains unavailable because CGO is disabled and no C compiler is installed.


- All 20 remote CI checks passed on e920ef655, including the full session/store race suite, both backend-core shards, all Chat and SQLite race shards, Windows workspace checks, Linux lint, API/sqlc drift, native CLI tests on Linux/macOS/Windows, container tests, and the aggregate backend gate.


## Omitted-effort coverage

The intended rule is to preserve the resolved creation snapshot. Omitting effort with a project default of Medium saves Medium in session metadata; a later project-default change to Low does not alter the retry effort. Omitting effort when no default exists saves an empty effort, retaining provider-default behavior on Retry.

The renamed TestResumeFailedAsyncChatSpawnPreservesResolvedEffort covers both meanings explicitly. All eight cases passed locally, including checks of failed-start metadata, launched effort, ready-session metadata, session reuse, and one opening-prompt delivery. All failed-start Retry regressions also passed. The complete local SQLite-store suite passed. The complete local session-manager suite finished in 138 seconds with seven previously observed Windows failures; none were in the Retry regressions. ## Retry model/effort combinations

TestResumeFailedAsyncChatSpawnRevalidatesSavedTuning explicitly records each starting model and asserts the failed session saved that exact model plus xhigh before changing project defaults. The empty-model case changes the project model to small, which only supports low/medium; Retry preserves the empty provider-default model with xhigh instead of combining small with xhigh.

PersistChatModel cases verify that changing the saved model leaves xhigh intact before Retry. Added both compatible and incompatible Chat model selections starting from an empty model, alongside the existing explicit-model selections. Successful retries assert the launched and persisted pair: unsupported xhigh clears to provider default, while supported xhigh remains. Session reuse and single-prompt delivery remain covered.

All eight revalidation cases and all failed-start Retry regressions passed locally. The complete local SQLite-store suite passed. The complete local session-manager suite finished with the same seven previously observed Windows failures; none were in the Retry regressions. title: fix(cloud): index the GitHub webhook claim and prune finished deliveries (P0 DB CPU)
body:
## Problem (P0)

The production database (`ao-cloud-production-storage`, db.t4g.medium) sat at 99% CPU. That is what broke 11x's sessions on 2026-10-22: the control plane timed out, failed its health check and was replaced 10 times, and workers stranded with `worker_never_started`.

Nearly all of that CPU came from one query, `ClaimGitHubWebhook`:

- It ran **two full scans** of `ao_github_webhook_deliveries` per claim:
  - The OR'd `status = 'processing'` branch kept the planner off the pending/retry index, which had 0 scans since stats began.
  - The installation-order `NOT EXISTS` scanned the table once per waiting delivery.
- The table **never shrank**: 353k rows, 99.96% already processed, 1.9 GB.
- **Eight workers** claim every second (#6416, Oct 8). Database CPU stepped from 10% to 19% at that deploy, then climbed with the table to 44% daily average and daily 100% peaks.

Scale of it:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Share of all rows the database read (2.41T since Sep 23) | 99.5% |
| Claims per second at the time of the incident | 29 |
| Rows scanned per second | about 10M |

## Fix

1. **Migration 00086 adds two partial indexes that only hold in-flight rows,** so they stay tiny as the table grows:
   - `ao_github_webhook_install_order_idx`: `(github_installation_id, received_at, github_delivery_id)`, only installation events that are pending, retry or processing.
   - `ao_github_webhook_processing_idx`: `(lease_until)`, only processing rows.
   - They are built `CONCURRENTLY` (`-- +goose NO TRANSACTION`), so writes keep flowing. `IF NOT EXISTS` makes the migration a no-op on production, which already has them (see below).
2. **Retention:** an hourly pruner deletes finished (processed or failed) deliveries older than 8 days, in batches of 1000. 8 days covers GitHub redelivery and the 7-day look-back of `RecentOpenedPullRequestWebhooks`. Pending, retry and processing rows are never touched.

The claim query itself is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Local copy shaped like prod** (352k processed rows, 96 queued):
  - Before: a claim takes 75 ms, with two full scans.
  - After the indexes: 0.2 ms, with a BitmapOr over the pending/retry and processing indexes, and an index scan for the ordering check.
  - The same 0.2 ms with an empty queue.
- **Production:** the two indexes were created by hand on 2026-10-23 at 16:30 UTC (approved P0 mitigation, `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` as the table owner).

  | Measure | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Database CPU | 99.5% (16:29 UTC) | 8.1% (16:32 UTC) |
  | 5xx since 16:31:30 UTC | n/a | 0 |
  | Queued deliveries | 95 | 0 |

  The live plan on production uses both new indexes.

## Tests

- `TestPruneGitHubWebhooksKeepsRecentAndInFlightDeliveries` (Postgres): old processed and failed rows are deleted; recent ones and pending, retry and processing rows are kept.
- `TestGitHubWebhookClaimIndexesExist` (Postgres): both indexes exist and are valid after migrating a fresh database. That also exercises the non-transactional goose migration.
- `TestPruneWebhooksDeletesInBatchesUntilAShortOne` and `TestWebhookRetentionCoversTheOpenedPullRequestLookBack` (unit tests).
- Existing webhook queue and migration tests pass, including `TestMigrationVersionsAreUnique`.

## Notes

- **Migration number:** #6844 still carries `00084_session_task_naming.sql`, which collides with main's 84. Whichever of #6844 and this PR merges second must take the next free number.
- **Not in this PR:** follow-ups from the same investigation.
  - The one-time bootstrap token is used up before the slow part of the handler, so a slow request strands the worker. That is in a separate PR.
  - `/readyz` pings the database with a 5 s timeout, so a slow database gets the only control-plane task replaced, which makes it worse.
  - Cloud ACP drops tool-call updates (`acp_runner.go`), so Chat shows no tool activity.
  - `pg_stat_statements` and Performance Insights are off on production.

title: feat(desktop): share a local artifact as a public link, behind a flag
body:
Code changes: +330
Tests: +390
Others: +90 (locale strings in 8 languages)

## Summary

The desktop side of artifact share links. The control-plane side merged in #6929. **Everything here is behind `ARTIFACT_SHARING_ENABLED = false`**, so nothing appears until the share-links control plane is deployed and a later PR flips the flag.

- **Share button.** An icon-and-label **Share** button in the open artifact's header (`SessionArtifactsView`), next to the feedback action. It appears only for local sessions (not cloud or remote hosts), with the flag on and cloud sign-in configured. `VITE_AO_ARTIFACT_SHARES=1` turns it on in a build without the flag change, for testing against a local control plane.
- **Share panel** (`ArtifactShare.tsx`, a popover under the button):
  - **Signed in:** opening the panel publishes the file and shows the link in a read-only field with **Copy link**, which shows "Copied" for 2 seconds. A hint says anyone with the link can view it, or, when publishing replaced an existing link, that the link now shows the latest version.
  - **Signed out:** the panel says "Sign in to AO Cloud to create a shareable link for this artifact" with a **Sign in** button. Sign-in starts only on that click, using the local email/password dialog in dev and WorkOS otherwise. When sign-in brings a new session, the panel reopens and creates the link. Closing the local sign-in dialog returns to the prompt.
  - **A session the control plane refuses** is asked to sign in once. The share continues only when a *different* session arrives (keyed by user id and `storedAt`), so a stale session can't reopen sign-in in a loop.
  - **At the link limit** (`409 artifact_share_limit_reached`): the limit message and **Upgrade to AO Cloud**, which opens Upgrade in Settings.
  - **A control plane without share links**, which answers this route with a plain-text 404: "Sharing isn't available on this AO Cloud server". Other failures show the server's message with **Try again**.
- **Publishing** (`lib/artifact-share.ts`): reads the file's exact bytes through the daemon's loopback artifact route (`artifactContentUrl`) and computes its SHA-256 with `crypto.subtle`. It then `POST`s `/api/cloud/v1/me/artifact-shares?name=&project=<workspaceName>&feature=<session title>` with `X-AO-Artifact-SHA256`.
- **Control-plane bridge:** `CloudCpProxyRequestInit` gains an optional `bodyBase64`, so binary artifacts (images, PDFs) cross IPC intact. Main decodes it to a `Buffer`. It is mutually exclusive with `body` and validated like the other fields. `cloudCpUpload` in `renderer-client.ts` sends it.
- **Strings** in all 8 locales.

## Tests run

- `vitest`: `ArtifactShare.test.tsx` covers:
  - signed-in create and copy
  - the replaced hint
  - the signed-out prompt, then sign-in, then create
  - a refused session asking only once over re-renders, then creating after a new session
  - closing the local sign-in dialog
  - the limit, with Upgrade opening billing settings
  - an unavailable server, with Try again
- `vitest`: `artifact-share.test.ts` covers exact bytes and SHA-256 on upload, the replaced flag, the typed limit, auth and unavailable (plain 404) errors, and server or fallback messages.
- `vitest`: `SessionArtifactsView.test.tsx` checks Share is hidden with the flag off, and shown for a local session but not a remote or cloud one with the flag on.
- `vitest`: `cloud-cp-proxy.test.ts` (new) checks a base64 body is sent as raw bytes, a string body is unchanged, and both-or-invalid bodies are refused.
- 50 tests in those files pass. `src/renderer/i18n` passes (22 tests), including locale key coverage and the hard-coded-English check.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors outside `packages/product-ui`, which cannot resolve its own dependencies in this worktree. Re-run on this head (`49274eabcb`): clean.
- **Not yet verified end to end in the native Electron window.** The control-plane side was verified against a local Docker stack (publish, link, limit, republish, revoke). Clicking through the panel in Electron against that stack is still to do.

## Known risks and follow-ups

- Turning sharing on in production needs, in one later PR:
  - `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS` enabled in the hosted environments
  - the development-only refusal in `validateArtifactShares` removed
  - `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_SHARES` and the share origin set
  - wildcard DNS and TLS for `*.orchestrator.inc`
  - flipping `ARTIFACT_SHARING_ENABLED`
- Sharing cloud-session artifacts (a server-side copy route), plan-based limits, and an `offering.artifactShares` gate are follow-ups.

title: feat(chat): calm expired-login banner that opens the Harness page
body:
## Problem

On a session running on a remote host, the "Provider authentication needs attention" banner read and moved accounts through **this computer's** daemon. That daemon doesn't know the session, so:

- it answered the account read with its own default account, and the banner offered this computer's accounts;
- "Continue on …" sent `PUT /api/v1/agents/accounts/sessions/{id}` to the local daemon → `404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, shown as **"Unknown session"**.

Sending those calls to the host instead doesn't fix it: the host's remote listener keeps `/api/v1/agents/accounts` loopback-only (since #6822), so a desktop can't read or move accounts on another machine.

## Change

The banner is now one calm line with one action:

> Your Claude Code login on Macbook Air M1 has expired. Log in again to keep using this chat. **[Log in again]**

- **Log in again** opens Settings → Harness for that agent on the session's host (the cloud view for a cloud session) and starts its login there, the same shortcut the task composer's "Log in" uses. A local session on a saved account lands on that account list.
- Neutral row style, `role="status"`; the raw provider error stays in the timeline only.
- The in-banner sign-in dialog, the "Continue on" move, and their 5 strings are removed. Moving a local session to another account stays in the session inspector.
- New strings `chat.reauth.expired`, `chat.reauth.expiredOnHost`, `chat.reauth.logInAgain` in all 8 locales.

## Tests

- `ChatStatusBanners.test.tsx`: plain message without the provider error; "Log in again" opens the Harness page for local, remote (with `hostId`, host named), and cloud sessions; dismissal; silent cases.
- `ChatWorkspaceProviderState.test.tsx`: updated for the new notice.
- Desktop E2E on a local build against a second daemon paired as a remote host: before/after screenshots are in a PR comment.

## Risks / follow-ups

- On the remote host's Harness page, "Log in again" signs in that host's CLI login. A remote session bound to one of the host's *saved* accounts still has to be fixed on that machine, because account routes stay loopback-only there.

title: feat(usage): add a Usage page with cost, tokens and subscription limits
body:
Code changes: +10343 -576\
Tests: +5964 -458\
Others: +3302 -47 (generated sqlc, OpenAPI and TypeScript types, regenerated pricing catalog, locale strings)

## What

A **Usage** page that shows what AO's agent sessions cost and use, and how much of each subscription is left. Open it from the sidebar or from the command palette ("Open usage"). For now the whole page is shown only with Developer Mode on.

![Spend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/507038447a325ab2ab47567f4caf843ef15dc628/pr-7148-v2-spend-dark.png)

- **Spend**, measured in cost or tokens (a menu on the total):
  - The period's total and each agent's share and sessions. An agent with no priced usage reads "Not priced", not $0.00 and 0% of cost.
  - A stacked bar per day, or per hour for the past 24 hours.
  - Totals, including what the cache saved.
  - Cost or tokens by type: input, cache read, cache write and output.
  - Cost or tokens by speed, with the premium paid for fast processing.
  - A breakdown grouped by model (with cache hit rate and cost per 1M tokens), day, project or session, picked from a "Group by" menu. The first ten rows show, with Show more for the rest. A model run by two agents is two rows, since each agent bills it apart. Session rows open the session.
- **Limits:** every signed-in Codex and Claude Code account, listed under its provider with its plan, default mark and reset credits, then its own windows with a reset countdown. Meters use the provider's colour and turn to a warning at 25% left or less. Sign-in problems show on the account's line, and this computer's own login is marked as such. Each window carries its pace since it opened to the reset: a tick on the meter marks what is left then, and a line says about how much, or when it runs out.
- **Windows** (Experimental): each login, named with its plan, has its five-hour windows over the week on a timeline and each weekly limit in use with its pace since it opened. The open window shows a dashed projection to its reset. Windows come only from limit readings AO took; nothing is inferred from activity, and each section says in one line how to read it.
- Periods: the last 24 hours, 7, 30 or 90 days, from a menu. Previous and next step through earlier periods, which are named by their dates. Filter to one project or see all of them.
- Each agent has its own colour: Claude Code orange, Codex purple, and a hue for every other agent AO runs. It colours the agent rows, the chart and its legend, the share bars and the limit meters.
- Usage priced at fast or priority rates is now priced correctly. Before this change, every turn was priced at the standard rate.
- Prices come straight from LiteLLM's live price table, so a model LiteLLM prices is priced within a day, with no AO release or catalog commit in between.
- When a provider's rates change, costs AO already stored are repriced to the new rates. Old Codex and Claude turns also recover their speed tier, so past fast turns now cost their fast price. A cost an agent reported is never repriced.
- **Model prices:** give a model your own rates per million tokens, or price it as a catalog model. A "Not priced" model opens the dialog, and a model with your price is marked. Your price covers every cost AO estimates for that model, and a cost the agent reported stays as reported. Removing a price returns the model to the catalog's.
- More agents are counted: Pi, OMP, Kimchi, Qwen Code, Goose, OpenCode, Kilo Code, prime-agent, Grok Build, DeepSeek Harness and Antigravity sessions. They are priced against every provider LiteLLM prices, not only Anthropic, OpenAI and Z.ai. Where an agent reports its own cost (Pi and its forks, Goose, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Grok Build), that cost is kept, including $0 for calls through the agent's own gateway.
- Usage is read when it is shown. An agent's writes no longer parse its transcript or hold the database writer; the Usage page, the session usage in the Resources panel and account usage read whatever changed first, waiting at most 5 seconds. A session that ends is still read at once, so its last usage is kept.
- Counts are fixed where AO missed or doubled usage: old Codex turns with no time now land on their day, Codex input past 272k tokens is priced at its long-context rate, a Claude message copied into a fork is counted once, a Claude message with no final record is still counted, and AO's own Claude calls for titles and prompt suggestions are counted against their session.

Usage covers AO sessions only. Costs are API-equivalent estimates, not a subscription bill, and the page says so.

## Why

AO already ingests every agent turn's tokens and prices them, but nothing showed the totals. There was also no single place to see how much of each subscription is left.

The pricing was also wrong for fast mode. Codex priority and Claude fast requests bill at a multiple of standard rates (2x for gpt-6.1-sol priority, 2.5x for gpt-5.5 priority, 2x for claude-opus-5-5 fast), and AO priced them all as standard. On one developer machine, 31,791 of 42,211 priced Codex turns over 7 days ran at priority: $1,331.63 at standard rates against $2,233.60 at their tier's rates.

## How

**Service-tier pricing**
- A new nullable `model_usage_events.service_tier` column holds the provider's own word for the tier:
  - Codex: `thread_settings_applied.thread_settings.service_tier`, carried in parser state to the token count it prices.
  - Claude: `usage.speed`, read leniently so a value of an unexpected type cannot drop the event.

  It is a column because a stored provider usage object is immutable. Adding a key to that object would turn every replay of an older event into a source event conflict, which stops ingestion of the source.
- The catalog gains `model#tier` rows such as `gpt-6.1-sol#priority` and `claude-opus-5-5#fast`, built from LiteLLM's `*_priority`, `*_flex` and `*_ultrafast` rates and its `provider_specific_entry.fast` multiple.
  - The v1 schema does not change. Released daemons decode the repository catalog strictly, so new rate fields would make them reject every later catalog. Extra rows are only models they never look up.
  - A tier row ships only when it carries every rate its standard row does.
- Pricing:
  - An unreported tier prices at standard, as before.
  - A tier word with no rule, or a model with no row for its tier, prices as unknown rather than at standard.
- The cost backfiller carries the tier, with a CAS guard. Legacy repair and inferred-provider promotion fill a NULL tier from the replayed event they re-cost.

**Pricing source**
- The daemon downloads LiteLLM's `model_prices_and_context_window.json` itself and builds the catalog in-process, with the same builder that writes the repository catalog. It refreshes every 24 hours with the table's ETag and keeps the last good catalog under `~/.ao/data/pricing`, as before. A new provider version re-prices events that have no cost yet, as before.
- Before, it downloaded AO's catalog from `main`, so a new model or tier row priced nothing until a catalog commit landed there. On this branch that left every Codex fast-mode turn unpriced, since `main`'s catalog has no tier rows yet, and `gpt-6.1-terra` was unpriced everywhere.
- The table is live and nobody reviews it first, so an entry the builder cannot read, or two entries pricing one model differently, drops that model instead of failing the whole table.
- The repository catalog and its generator stay for released builds, which still download it. The manifest fetcher had no other caller and is removed.

**Reading on demand**
- File events, hook registrations and inventory refreshes only mark a source unread. `Pipeline.Flush` hands the unread sources to the workers and returns when the queue is empty, or after 5 seconds; work it started keeps running.
- The report, session usage and account usage readers are wrapped in the daemon to flush first. Nothing else reads usage events.
- Sources of a finalizing binding (the session ended or its process exited) and timed retries still run at once, so finalization settles without a reader.
- Deleting a session flushes first, so usage written since the last read is stored and folded into account totals before the record and its usage rows go.
- While a flush waits, new changes are read too, so a child transcript found mid-flush is in the same read.
- The 15-second SQLite poll is removed. The watcher reports a write to any registered source file: transcripts, a database's `-wal`, and the Grok and DeepSeek snapshot files. The 3-minute reconcile tick marks every live source unread, which covers a missed event at the next read.
- The in-memory skip for an unchanged snapshot file went with the poll. An unchanged file is read again only after that tick or while its session finalizes, and it writes nothing.

**Report API:** `GET /api/v1/usage/report?days=&offset=&tz=&projectId=`
- Reads timestamped events in the window. The window is local days, or the last 24 local hours by hour, in the caller's IANA zone. The hour boundaries are built locally, so half-hour zones such as Asia/Kolkata bucket correctly.
- Each row is one period × harness × model × speed tier, with disjoint token counts.
- The stored cost is split into input, cache write, cache read and output, plus the speed premium and cache savings. The split ratios come from the catalog for each price key and are applied to the stored totals, so the parts always add up to what was stored.
- A per-session list feeds the project and session breakdowns.
- `offset` steps back whole periods: 1 with 7 days is the week before this one.

**Page**
- A new `/usage` route with its own `PageTopbar` (title and the period, project and refresh controls), a sidebar entry and a command palette item. The sidebar entry and palette item show only in Developer Mode, and the route sends everyone else Home.
- The chart is plain markup with stacked bars and round-number ticks. No charting dependency was added.
- Limits are grouped per provider in a pure function, default account first. One grid per provider keeps bars aligned across accounts.
- Spend, Limits and Windows are underlined page tabs in the harness settings' tab style, pinned above the scrolling view. Cost or tokens, the period and the grouping are the Settings dropdown.
- Pace is one rule everywhere (`paceToReset`): use so far since the window opened, carried on to its reset. Limit windows report their length, so a live reading has a start. No projection while nothing is used, at the limit, or before a tenth of the window (at most an hour).
- Agent colours: one hue per agent id in `lib/agent-tone.ts`, at a lightness and chroma set per theme in `tokens.css`, so every agent holds the same contrast in light and dark. Agents whose mark is black and white read as neutral.
- Spend lists each agent's share beside its value on one line, in a list that scrolls beside the chart. The estimate note is a tooltip on the total.
- Every string is in all nine locales, Russian included.

**More agents**
- Schema: `usage_bindings` and `usage_sources` are rebuilt once more with only non-empty checks on harness and kind; `model_usage_events` is untouched. The store guards both instead: a binding needs a known `AgentHarness`, a source a kind in `domain.AllUsageSourceKinds`. A new usage harness needs no migration. It is the branch's only rebuild of those tables; its rollback restores `main`'s checks (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi) and removes only the rows they cannot hold.
- The Codex-profile renumber repair counts the open schema as migration 0117's effect. It took the missing `kimi` literal as proof 0117 was the old collided migration, re-ran it on the second start, and put back a CHECK that rejects every newer harness.
- Sources, one per agent:
  - Pi, OMP, Kimchi and prime-agent write Pi-format session JSONL and share one parser with a dialect per fork. AO launches Pi with `--session-dir` under its data dir and passes the transcript path through Pi's hooks. OMP and Kimchi are read from their agent dirs. prime-agent has no hook, so its transcript binds to the one live prime-agent session in the transcript's workspace.
  - Qwen Code: monthly `token-usage-*.jsonl`, attributed by native session ID. Its log names only an auth type, so the billing route is resolved from Qwen's settings for the session and kept on the binding. Reasoning is counted once, by auth type.
  - Goose: the per-call `usage_ledger` in `sessions.db`, never the session totals.
  - OpenCode and Kilo Code: the per-call `step-finish` parts in `opencode.db` and `kilo.db` (or a release-channel `<app>-<channel>.db`), including sub-agent sessions. The cursor is the part's creation time plus low row-id bits, because OpenCode undo deletes rows and SQLite reuses their ids.
  - Grok Build: `usage.json`, rewritten after each turn, read as a snapshot with the turn number as the cursor.
  - DeepSeek Harness: the zstd `session.v4` log, with the record sequence as the cursor. Terminal sessions have no hook, so they bind to the one live session in the log's workspace.
  - Antigravity: the per-call protobuf rows in each conversation's `gen_metadata` table.
- SQLite sources are opened strictly read-only (modernc, `mode=ro`, `query_only`, busy timeout), and marked changed by writes to the database's `-wal`.
- Reported costs: an agent's own figure is stored with a pricing version naming it (`pi:reported`, `opencode:reported`, ...), and the ingestor leaves it alone. A $0 through the agent's own gateway (Kimchi, OpenCode Zen, the Kilo gateway) is kept as charged; a zero through any other provider goes to the catalog. The report counts a stored total even when the agent gives no input, cache and output split.
- Cache writes: each agent names its cache-write count differently (`cacheWrite`, `cache_write_tokens`, `tokens.cache.write`, ...), so every parser also stores it under AO's `ao_derived_cache_write_input_tokens` key beside the agent's own usage object, plus `ao_derived_cache_write_1h_input_tokens` when Pi reports the 1-hour split. Pricing and the report query read that key after Claude's and Codex's own fields, so the Spend view's cache-write cost and tokens cover every agent, not only Claude and Codex.
- Every provider: the live build keeps every LiteLLM provider with chat or responses rates. Vertex's per-publisher providers fold into `vertex_ai`, and `bedrock_converse` into `bedrock`. Anthropic, OpenAI and Z.ai stay required, and the repository copy still holds exactly those three for released builds. `CanonicalProviderID` maps harness spellings (`google`, `amazon-bedrock`, `github-copilot`, ...) onto LiteLLM's. Inferring a provider from a model name still looks only at the required three, because resellers reuse first-party model names. A table row whose key keeps a provider prefix is skipped alone.

**Repricing and old tiers**
- A new catalog version for a provider now reprices every row an older version of that provider priced, found by `pricing_version` through a new partial index, not only rows with no cost. A row the new catalog can no longer price keeps its cost. Rows an agent priced (`pi:reported`, ...) are never selected.
- Old speed tiers: the migration queues, in `usage_tier_repairs`, every Claude and Codex source that has an untiered event. The legacy repairer rereads each source once and fills the tier its transcript reports. That clears the row's cost, and the backfiller prices it at the tier's rates. The queue exists because a NULL tier also means "none reported", so without it a reread could never know it was done.

**Model prices**
- `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/usage/prices` read and replace the whole set, stored in `usage_price_overrides`. A row holds either input and output rates as decimal USD per 1M tokens (cache read and cache write default to input), or a catalog model to price as (`provider/model`).
- Overrides live in the pricing snapshot, so new usage, the backfill and the report all use them, and a catalog refresh keeps them. Own rates price with an `ao-override:sha256:…` version; price-as prices at the target's catalog row and version.
- Saving reprices only the models whose override changed, through a new `(model_id, id)` index. Removing an override returns its rows to the catalog price.
- An agent's reported cost is never replaced. The agent's figure is what it billed, and replacing it would lose that figure for good.

**Limit readings and windows (Experimental)**
- All of it is off unless Developer Mode is on. A new app setting, `app_settings.limit_history` (off by default), tells the daemon; `PUT /api/v1/usage/limit-history` sets it, and the app sends Developer Mode there whenever it syncs it to the daemon, next to chat hibernation. With it off, no reading is kept and nothing reads limits in the background.
- While it is on, every successful limits read is kept in a new `agent_limit_readings` table for 14 days, with the login the account was signed in as. Limit windows now report their length (`durationMinutes`).
- A daemon loop re-reads each account once its last reading is five minutes old, so the history continues while no screen asks for limits.
- `GET /api/v1/usage/limit-windows?days=` groups readings into windows per login, limit and reset time (resets within two minutes are one window):
  - final: read within six minutes of its reset;
  - partial: readings stopped earlier, so it got at least that full;
  - open: not reset yet;
  - a window replaced before its reset (Codex restarting a week early) ends when the next begins.
- Two accounts on the same login are one login; the computer's own login splits when it changes accounts.

**Accurate counts**
- Times for old events: rows written before the parser read record times have no `created_at`, and the report windows by time, so they were in no period. On each start the legacy repairer rereads those sources once, including the `.zst` copy Codex leaves when it compresses an old rollout, and fills each time from the event with the same source event key. A stored time is never replaced. This adds a direct dependency on `github.com/klauspost/compress` (already in the module graph) for zstd.
- Long context: the catalog gains `model#above272k` rows (and `model#tier#above272k`) from LiteLLM's `*_above_272k_tokens` rates, only when complete. An event whose input is past the size prices at that row. A migration clears the cost of stored OpenAI rows past 272k so the backfiller reprices them.
- Fork copies: a new `provider_message_id` column with a unique index on (provider, message id). A Claude fork or resume opens with copies of its parent's messages; the insert now skips a message another source already stored, so it is counted once.
- Unfinished messages: Claude writes a message's usage on its records as it streams. A message whose last record has no `stop_reason` (the turn was interrupted) was dropped; the parser now holds it, carried in parser state, and counts it when the next message or user record arrives.
- Background calls: titles and prompt suggestions run as separate Claude calls in a temporary workspace no session claims. After the call returns, and before the workspace is removed, the session manager hands its path to the collector, which finds the transcript in the matching Claude project folder and records it under a new `background-task` hook event. That event drains only the call's own binding, on the worker's route; it never finalizes the worker.

**Intentional omissions**
- The Windows tab draws no inferred windows and no next-week projection. Both would come from activity timing, not readings.
- Old Codex rows with no billing provider (4,030 on one machine, Jul 29 – Aug 10) stay Not priced, even with a model price. AO cannot tell who billed them.
- Old Claude events whose transcripts were deleted keep no time; nothing is left to read it from.
- Codex background calls are not counted. Titles run ephemeral, so Codex writes no rollout for them. A prompt-suggestion fork does write one, but it holds no usage of its own: its one token count repeats the parent's last count, and AO stops the turn before Codex reports the fork's usage. Reading it would count the parent's last turn twice.
- Regional and plan endpoints (`minimax-cn`, `zai-coding-cn`, Alibaba's Coding and Token plans) and local servers stay unpriced instead of borrowing a provider's list price.
- Antigravity bills by quota, so its cost is a list-price estimate.
- Codex 0.162.x wrote the tier line only on a settings change, so earlier turns from those versions price at standard. Codex 0.163 writes it when a thread starts.

## Testing

Backend:
- `go build ./...`, and `go vet` on the changed packages.
- `npm run api` regenerates `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`; the committed versions match (checked by `api-drift`).
- New tests cover:
  - Limit readings round trip, ignore a repeated read, and expire after 14 days.
  - Readings into windows: jittered resets merged, final/partial/open, a login change, two accounts on one login, a week restarted early, hourly points.
  - Report windows in a half-hour time zone.
  - Stepping back one week with `offset`, and rejecting a negative one.
  - The premium, the cache-write split and unpriced events.
  - Time-range and cache-write extraction against stored rows.
  - The time repair, run through the repairer's `Start` as the daemon runs it, filling times from a `.zst` rollout (fails if the repair is not wired in).
  - Long-context rows emitted only when complete, and priced past their size.
  - A fork copy counted once across two transcripts of one session.
  - A message with no final record counted, with state carried across chunks.
  - A background call counted on the worker's route, leaving the worker binding active.
  - The live build matches the generator's provider versions, survives the cache, and answers a 304 only when a cached catalog exists. CI runs the same test on the LiteLLM table it downloads.
  - A conflicting or unreadable table entry drops only that model.
  - An agent's priced-event count, which decides "Not priced".
  - Each added agent's parser and collector: Pi (normalization across every pi-ai API family), OMP, Kimchi, prime-agent, Qwen (routes and reasoning), Goose, OpenCode and Kilo (cursor, sub-agents, release-channel databases), Grok Build, DeepSeek Harness and Antigravity.
  - The open-kinds migration from `main`'s schema, with rollback, and the renumber repair keeping 0117 applied after a second start.

title: bug(review): a reviewer turn that fails with a provider error leaves `review_run.body` as "reviewer Chat turn ended without submitting a result"; `ao review ls` shows no provider error class or message
body:
## What went wrong?

When a native reviewer turn fails because the provider rejects the request, the real error is stored only on the `conversation_turns` row (`error_message`). The review run it belongs to gets a generic body, and `ao review ls` / the review controls show nothing that identifies the provider error. An operator has to open the SQLite database to learn that the cause was a provider-side 400 (a model not supported for the account), which is not discoverable from the CLI or the UI.

There is a second, related path: a manual review trigger on a worker session of a remote host returns only `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED` with the message "Review operation failed" and no detail. This looks like the same family as #6107; adding the occurrences here so they can be matched.

**Expected:** a failed reviewer turn exposes the provider error class and message (for example `invalid_request_error`, HTTP 400, and the provider's message) in `review_run.body` (or a dedicated error field), and `ao review ls` prints it. A failed trigger returns the underlying error in the error `details` (the fix proposed in #6107).

**Actual:** `ao review ls` shows the run as `failed` with body `reviewer Chat turn ended without submitting a result`; the trigger API returns `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED`, "Review operation failed".

## Evidence (redacted)

AO desktop build 0.14.4 (daemon reports `ao version dev`), macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64). Reviewer harness: `codex`. Review runs started by an agent (`trigger_source = agent`).

Three failed review runs, 2026-10-18, each with a single failed reviewer turn:

| review_run id | created (UTC) | status | body | matching `conversation_turns` row (failed, same second) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a758c199-c2f3-477a-932c-c8af67935aaa | 14:13:05 | failed | `reviewer Chat turn ended without submitting a result` | turn aa81c53f…, 14:13:05 to 14:13:09 |
| c4af8df4-e611-47da-bd65-24e57d332467 | 14:13:26 | failed | same | turn c5321967…, 14:13:26 to 14:13:27 |
| c9960f0c-8de5-45c7-b081-6f72864c864c | 14:13:39 | failed | same | turn 61a6cac0…, 14:13:39 to 14:13:41 |

The three turns have the same `error_message` (nothing else is stored there):

```
{"type":"error","status":400,"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The 'gpt-5.5' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
```

So the cause was a provider-side configuration error that could have been fixed in minutes (switch the reviewer model), but the review run and `ao review ls` only said the turn "ended without submitting a result".

Manual trigger failures on a worker session of a second Mac, 2026-10-19, with the remote host's AO transport healthy:

- `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED`, request `<lan-host>/KvUin1noZb-113051`
- `REVIEW_OPERATION_FAILED`, request `<lan-host>/KvUin1noZb-113630`

No reason was visible to the client; we could not tell whether the cause was the same provider error, a tmux issue (#6099) or something else.

## Repro conditions

1. Configure the native reviewer for a harness/model that the provider rejects for the signed-in account (here: Codex with a ChatGPT account and model `gpt-5.5`).
2. Let an agent trigger a review on a worker's PR.
3. `ao review ls`: the run is `failed` with body `reviewer Chat turn ended without submitting a result`; no provider error class or message appears. The message is only in `conversation_turns.error_message` for the turn handled by the review.

## Suggested direction (from #6107, applies here too)

- Copy the turn's `error_message` (or its parsed `error.type` and `error.message`) into `review_run.body` when a reviewer turn fails with a provider error, instead of the generic text.
- In `writeReviewError`, pass the underlying error through the envelope `details` rather than `nil`.
- Show the failed run's body for manual triggers in the UI, and print it in `ao review ls`.

No secrets, tokens, transcripts, repository names, PR URLs or addresses are included; the only host reference is the placeholder `<lan-host>`.

title: fix(cloud): 11x feedback: stranded worker bootstrap, standalone working folder, live tool calls in Chat
body:
## Summary

Fixes for three problems 11x reported on their Coder workspaces. The root causes come from the prod CP logs (`/ao-cloud/production/control-plane`) and RDS metrics for 2026-10-22.

| # | Problem | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Task stuck on "Connecting to the worker", then `worker_never_started` (ahmad's org, and two sessions in jeson's org) | Prod Postgres hit 99% CPU from 17:44 to 17:55 UTC, so CP requests took 20–60 s. The CPU went to `ClaimGitHubWebhook` full table scans (fixed by #7145 and the indexes added on prod 2026-10-23); the instance runs in unlimited credit mode, so the zero credit balance was a cost signal, not throttling. The worker's `POST /worker/bootstrap` timed out at 30 s **after** the CP had already spent the single-use ticket. The retry got 401 "already used", the worker exited, and nothing relaunched it. The session sat until the 30-min ceiling parked it. Retry worked at once because it issues a fresh ticket. | **CP:** a ticket redeemed within 10 min can be redeemed again for the same epoch until a worker checks in on it, the epoch is fenced or superseded, or a newer ticket replaces it. **Worker:** bootstrap retries transport errors and 5xx for up to 8 min (backoff capped at 15 s), instead of about 4 s of transport-only retries. |
| 2 | Agent starts in `~/repository` although the connection's working directory is `~/work/{repo}` | The project is standalone (no repository), so `{repo}` has nothing to fill in. The worker logged a warning and fell back to an empty `~/repository`. | A standalone session starts in the folder above `{repo}` (`~/work`), as the existing code comment intended. A `{repo}` directly under home or `/` keeps the old default. |
| 3 | A long prompt shows only "Working for 5m", with no tool calls to steer by | Since #6901, Coder sessions follow the Default session interface and open in Chat. For Claude and Cursor, the cloud ACP runner dropped every tool call and update (`cloudACPClient.SessionUpdate` published only assistant text), so there were no tool rows at all: no `chat.activity` events in any prod org since Oct 15. Codex already emitted activity. Separately, Chat collapses each run of tool calls into one summary line during the turn. | **Worker:** Claude and Cursor tool calls (`tool_call` / `tool_call_update`) and thoughts are now forwarded as chat activity, mapped as local Chat maps ACP tools (command, file change, reasoning, tool row), bounded under the CP's event limit, best effort. **Frontend:** while a turn runs, the run the agent is working in stays **open** (with its subgroups and working subagents), so each call shows as its own row as it happens; earlier runs in the turn fold to their summary. Each row still expands to its command, output or diff. When the turn settles everything folds back into "Worked for", as before. A reader's click always wins over the live default. |

### Incident timeline (session `73693168`, UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 17:27:20 | Workspace created |
| 17:31 → 17:49 | Template ready check failing (17.5 min of the 30-min budget) |
| 17:50:58 | Worker launched; bootstrap → 500 after 29.4 s (worker timeout) |
| 17:51:48 | Retry → 401 "already used"; the worker exits |
| 17:57:27 | Ceiling → `worker_never_started` |
| 18:05:36 | User clicks Retry → connected in 2 s |

The six failed bootstrap requests on prod in that window belong to three workers: this one, plus two reinstalled workers in jeson's org that were disconnected by the slowdown and stranded the same way. They were parked an hour later.

## Needs a decision (not in this PR)

1. **Reconciler never reinstalls a worker that launched but didn't check in (BYO Coder).** Both the repair timer and the give-up ceiling run from workspace creation. With a long connection startup timeout they expire together, and the ceiling is checked first, so `startup_attempts` stays 0. Proposal: reinstall when a worker hasn't checked in **10 min after launch** (matching the CP's ticket retry window, above the worker's 8-min retry budget), and give up no sooner than **launch + 20 min**, so there's room for exactly one reinstall. This keeps a customer's workspace running up to about 20 min past launch, which is why it needs sign-off.
2. ~~**Prod Postgres sizing.**~~ Not needed: the CPU was the webhook claim query, fixed by #7145. Original text: `ao-cloud-production-storage` is a burstable `db.t4g.medium` with **0 CPU credits since Oct 15**. Average CPU has gone from 28% to 53% in a week, against a 20% baseline, and it hits 100% about once a day (again at 18:13 on Oct 22). Every route degrades while it does. Proposal: move to a fixed-performance instance (for example `db.m7g.large`) and turn on Performance Insights to find the query behind the spikes. This is an infra change with a brief failover.
3. **Chat by default for Coder sessions.** This PR makes Chat show live tool calls, but the Default session interface still decides whether 11x lands in Chat or Terminal. Decide whether cloud should keep following it or default to Terminal.
4. Ahmad's org has had 13 `terminal_unavailable` failures since Oct 13. That's a separate issue and isn't investigated here.

## Review fixes (d009ce897f)

- **Retry window from first redemption:** a redeemed ticket can be redeemed again for 10 min from its first redemption, even past its own expiry. In the incident the worker install took 117 s, so a ticket could expire inside the worker's 8 min retry budget.
- **Bootstrap request timeout 90 s** (bootstrap only; other requests keep 30 s), so a slow but working CP is waited out instead of retried against.
- **Standalone folder guard:** the folder above `{repo}` is refused when it is the home directory spelled out (`/home/<user>/{repo}`), the root, or AO's worker folder.
- **Live Chat:** only the run in progress stays open, so a long turn does not keep every call mounted.
- **Index:** the `ao_access_tickets (org_id, session_id, purpose)` index this retry check needs is in #7145's migration 00086 (keeps this PR migration-free).

## Still open (not in this PR)

- `/readyz` pings the DB with a 5 s timeout, so a slow DB gets the only CP task replaced (10 times on Oct 22), which makes the outage worse.
- Reconciler relaunch of a worker that launched but never checked in (Needs a decision 1).

## Compatibility

- No migration.
- New worker, old CP: a retried spent ticket gets 401, same as today.
- Old worker, new CP: better than before. Old workers already retry transport errors (including their 30 s client timeout) a few times, so the CP change alone fixes the incident pattern; worker self-update then brings the longer retry.
- Replay exposure: within 10 min of redemption, a holder of the bootstrap ticket can get a token for the same epoch, but only until the real worker's first heartbeat. The ticket lives only in the worker's env file, which the launcher deletes.

## Tests

- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean.
- `go test` passes for `cmd/ao-worker`, `internal/worker`, `internal/httpapi` and `internal/reconcile`.
- New Postgres tests (`bootstrap_ticket_retry_test.go`) cover:
  - retry before and after registration;
  - refusal after a heartbeat, past the window, after a newer ticket, for a ticket invalidated before it was redeemed, and for a fenced epoch.
- The retry test fails on `main` and passes here.
- The full `internal/postgres` suite on a fresh postgres:16 database fails only the 4 tests that already fail on main (`TestCIFailureNotification…`, `TestQueuedTurn…`, `TestReviewsSnapshot…`, `TestDisconnectSettles…`).
- New worker tests: 5xx retried with the same ticket; retries stop at the budget; 4xx still not retried.
- `TestStandaloneWorkingDirectory` covers `~/work/{repo}` → `~/work` plus the error cases.
- Frontend: new `ActivityRun` tests cover a live run showing each call, folding on settle, a reader's choice sticking, and a working subagent opening. They fail on `main`.
- The chat test folder passes 1269 of 1271. The 2 failures (`ContextMeter`, `ChatWorkspace` context usage) fail the same way on `main`. Frontend `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- New: `TestBootstrapTicketRetryIsRefusedAfterCheckInUnderRLS` (runs as a non-bypass role; fails without the org scoping), `TestBootstrapTicketRetryOutlivesTheTicketExpiry`, `TestBootstrapWaitsLongerThanOtherRequests`, the standalone refusals, the ACP activity tests (`acp_activity_test.go`), and the ChatWorkspace live-run test. Each fails without its change.
- **Staging:** passed; see the staging validation comment.

title: feat(cloud): shareable cloud sessions with live presence and a hard lock
body:
Code changes: +5395 -262  
Tests: +5123 -10  
Others: +2058 -35  

## What this does

Several people can work in one cloud session at once, the way people share a Google Doc. The owner shares a link. Anyone who opens it sees who else is there and watches the current writer type live. Only one person at a time can talk to the agent.

- **Share links.** A link covers a project or a single session, with a role: editor or viewer. `ao-app://share/...` links open in the desktop app, and so does **Open shared link** in the command palette. Opening a link from inside the owning org takes you straight to the session.
- **Presence.** Each open session lists who has it open.
- **Hard lock (composer lease).** Whoever types first holds the chat box. Everyone else's box is locked, and they can ask for a turn and wait in line. The session creator and org owners/admins can take over.
  - The lease lasts 15 s, renews while you type, and is released after 45 s idle.
  - When the holder lets go, the lease passes to the next person in line who is still in the session.
  - Every grant carries an epoch. A send with an old epoch is refused with `COMPOSER_LOCKED`. Terminal keystrokes, stops and approvals go through the same check.
- **Live draft.** Others see the holder's draft as it's typed, with the holder's name on their cursor.
- **Prompt attribution.** Each prompt records and shows who sent it.
- **Owner-set model.** The session owner (or an org admin) sets the model, effort, mode and approval mode. Everyone else sees these read-only. The server applies the owner's settings to every turn, whatever the sender asked for.

## How it works

- Postgres holds the shared state, in migrations `00086`–`00091`:
  - `ao_session_viewers` (who has the session open)
  - `ao_composer_leases` and `ao_composer_waitlist` (who holds the chat box, who is in line, and the holder's draft)
  - `ao_sessions.chat_settings` (the owner's model settings)
- Triggers call `pg_notify` on every change. The session event stream wakes on NOTIFY instead of polling.
- A live feed (`/events?live=1&types=session.live`) pushes the session's live state to every open stream. The state includes viewers, holder, line, draft, `chatSettings`, `canTakeOver`, `canConfigure`, and `you`, the server's view of who you are.
- The desktop app takes identity from `you`, never from a local guess. Each app instance keeps its Cloud sign-in in its own `AO_DATA_DIR`.

New routes:
- `POST /sessions/{id}/composer/{acquire,renew,release,queue,takeover,draft}`
- `DELETE /sessions/{id}/composer/queue`
- `PUT /sessions/{id}/chat-settings`

Sends and steers accept `composerEpoch`. The OpenAPI contract and `packages/cloud-client` are regenerated.

## Tests

- **Go store and HTTP tests** cover the lease (epoch fencing, row locking, handoff, idle release, take-over rules), presence, drafts, share redemption and owner-set settings.
- **`cloud/scripts/test-shared-session.sh`** is a 45-check end-to-end run against a local stack with three users: an owner, a guest editor and a viewer. It passed 45/45 before the merge with main.
- **Vitest** covers the shared chat surface, `useComposerLease`, the live stream bridge and the share dialogs.

After merging main, the shared session and Chat surface vitest suites pass and the Go backend builds. The full suites were not rerun. Two vitest failures (the ChatWorkspace context-usage test and a ContextMeter test) also fail on main.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Session header and startup fixes

- Share uses the same compact toolbar sizing as Orchestrator, with the standard 4px action gap. Browser verification measures both buttons at 28px tall.
- Cloud orchestrator creation uses the standard Chat startup view in shell and board entry paths. Cloud Chat retains its own startup checklist instead of also showing the terminal workspace/worker/attachment loader. Terminal startup and reconnect loaders remain intact.
- The five affected suites pass across reruns (477 tests); production renderer build and E2E typecheck pass. Cloud client (30), product-ui (161), packaging helpers (17), and docs (7) tests pass, as do docs translations and build. Renderer smoke: 122/124 pass; both failures reproduce on the original PR head (chat pointer selection and macOS Cmd+K focus).

## CI follow-up

Fixed the reported remote-board boundary failure: sharing hooks only read local Cloud settings when the local board has eligible Cloud sessions, and remote boards disable participant lookup. Completed shared-chat model fixtures with their required display name, eliminating the unhandled `split` error in the original CI log.

Validation at `b5d17f3dd`:
- All 97 focused tests pass (remote board, board, shared status, and shared Chat).
- Production renderer build passes. Supplemental native TypeScript checking passes with an equivalent temporary import-path configuration; the standard compiler is not claimed as passed after its earlier 16-minute run was stopped without a result.
- The complete frontend suite finishes with **9,239 passed, 6 skipped, 1 failed**, with no unhandled shared-chat error. The remaining failure is the unrelated harness-settings update-indicator test, which passes when the settings suite is rerun alone. That isolated suite instead exposes its concurrent-install spinner failure, which also reproduces on the original PR head.

The conflicts reported during this earlier verification are resolved by the rebase below, and remote CI is running on the rebased head. Linux Electron boundary checks and the Intel macOS native-helper matrix remain CI verification gaps. The guarded-navigation integration has an unrelated page drag-region assertion failure.

## Review fixes and verification

All four findings in [review 5643050590](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7151#pullrequestreview-5643050590) are addressed:

- `d2d5406a9`: idempotent commands retain the guest's requested settings; the message uses the owner's effective settings. Retrying still matches after the owner changes settings.
- `e8d880fc4`: creator checks use null-safe comparisons, preserving authorized access for sessions without `created_by_user_id`.
- `28de5c3a2`: an owner shares drafts when the only other participants are viewers, and draft publication is throttled every 120ms rather than postponed by each keystroke.
- `6bfb3f68d`: strengthens null-creator owner/editor/viewer permissions coverage and verifies that turn authors and org owners can stop turns, while unrelated participants get `ErrForbidden` instead of a SQL NULL scan error.

Verification: 38 frontend sharing tests pass. Guest-retry, nullable-creator, composer lease, live-state, and turn-permission regressions pass against disposable PostgreSQL 17 with race detection. Cloud build and vet pass; every non-PostgreSQL package passes the complete Cloud race run, and the PostgreSQL package passes in CI's default no-database configuration. The complete real-database store suite exposes four unrelated failures, all reproduced on the original PR head: CI notification recipient RLS, idle status with queued turns, reviewer credential selection, and retired-worker activity settlement. The temporary database was removed after testing.

There are no inline review threads to resolve. The rebase below resolves the branch conflicts that blocked remote CI.


## Rebase onto current main

Rebased all 36 commits onto `fefa2e8bebb485d5900f487d6c9b5c212b883b7e` and pushed head `6bfb3f68d093e362ed819c589b99cb2ea2a151a1` with an explicit lease. GitHub reports **MERGEABLE**. Conflict resolutions preserve main's terminal resize delivery, startup guard, catalog synchronization, command palette, settings navigation and protocol tests, alongside the sharing changes. Locale catalogs retain both sets of keys.

Validation on the rebased head:
- Frontend and E2E typechecks, production renderer build, and 1,021 targeted frontend tests pass.
- Cloud HTTP tests, build and vet pass. Cloud client generation produces no drift; its typecheck and all 30 tests pass.
- Product UI typecheck, all 161 tests, and package dry-run pass.
- Docs translation validation, all 7 docs tests and the docs production build pass.
