title: feat(chat): show subagents as a team and open each one in a Subagents panel
body:
Code changes: +1603 -15\
Tests: +1326 -0\
Others: +318 -0

## What

Subagents now render in Chat as a team where the agent launched them, and each one opens into its own read-only conversation in the inspector.

**Team card in the chat**
- **Header:** the agents' marks, then "3 subagents  2 working · 1 done" on one line, with the chevron right after it. The marks overlap, each cut back short of the one over it, so several agents read as several marks. Every state is counted, "1 no report" included, so the parts add up to the team.
- **One row per subagent:** its task name, its agent type when it is a specialized one (`Explore`, `Plan`, a project's own agent; Claude's default `general-purpose` is not shown), what it is doing right now ("Running `grep -rn …`"), or the first line of its report once it finishes, its elapsed time, and its state: Working, Failed with the provider's reason, Stopped, or No report. Done shows no mark: the report line and the header count already say it. A child that ended before recording any step says "No steps recorded". The mark, the time and the chevron sit centred on the row's two lines.
- **Plain rows, working or finished:** no box and no dividers, the names lined up under the team's, brightening on hover. Only the spinner and the live line set a working child apart, so nothing changes shape as it ends.
- **While any child works**, the team stays in the turn's flow, open.
- **Once every child is done**, the team folds into "Worked for" with the rest of the turn's work, closed until opened. A child still working after the turn ends keeps the team in view.

**Subagents tab in the inspector** (new, beside Side chat)
- Clicking a row opens that subagent's conversation:
  - the parent's instructions as a "Sent by the parent agent" bubble (long ones fold)
  - everything it said and ran, in order, drawn with the chat's own parts
  - the live row while it works, naming its current step
  - its report
- It is read-only: a subagent answers to its parent agent. It ends in the side chat's composer, switched off: "Read-only: a subagent works on its own and reports back to this chat." sits where "Message the agent…" would, over the same tools (attach, the model control, send), each disabled. The model control always reads "Choose a model", since which model a child ran is not recorded. Escape inside the panel does not stop the parent's turn.
- A back arrow leads to the chat's subagents, listed the way the Summary tab lists its rows: its collapsible "Working" and "Finished" sections, then one 32px row per child (mark, name and type, state, time), newest first. Past ten, a section's last two rows fade into a centred "Show N more agents"; opened, it reads "Show fewer agents". The list follows the conversation live, and each child opens fresh at its start.
- The tab shows only while the chat has subagents, an orchestrator's rail (Summary, Browser, Artifacts) included. Opening a row from the Browser resizes the inspector the way a tab click does.
- Coming back to a session left on its Subagents tab shows Summary until the chat reports its subagents, then the tab returns selected.
- Chats with no inspector panel (cloud sessions, side chats, the reviewer chat) keep expanding a row inline, and draw the same conversation there.

Motion follows DESIGN.md:
- Rows fade in as each agent launches.
- The live line uses `chat-working-shimmer`.
- The spinner crossfades away when a child finishes.
- Expand and collapse animate.
- The timer ticks only while a child works.
- Reduced motion turns all of it off.

## Why

Claude's ACP adapter files a subagent launch (the `Agent` tool, `Task` before it was renamed) as `reasoning`, and `readableItems` drops every reasoning row. So the launch vanished. The child's commands, which point back to it through `parentProviderItemId`, surfaced as loose "Ran N tool calls" rows in the parent's turn. Nothing said which agent ran them, whether it finished, or what it found.

## How

**`subagent-team.ts`** (pure, unit tested)
- `isSubagentLaunch` recognizes a launch.
- `partitionSubagentSteps` moves each step under the outermost launch above it. A grandchild stays with the chain, a step whose launch is not in the list stays where it was, and malformed parent cycles are handled.
- `readSubagent` derives state only from recorded facts:
  - A completed `SubagentHandback` addressed to this launch means done, and its message is the report.
  - A running step, or a background launch while any AO turn holding the child is still running, means working.
  - A failed or cancelled launch means failed or stopped, with the provider's reason (code fence stripped).
  - A child that never reported back is "No report", never assumed done.
  - The "Async agent launched… agentId" note to the model is never shown.
- `stepSections` breaks the child's tool calls into runs at what it wrote.

**`ChatWorkspace.tsx`**
- `readableItems` keeps launches.
- `runsOf` groups back-to-back launches into a `subagents` run.
- `groupByTurn` partitions steps over the whole conversation, in sequence order, before any turn is split at its steers. A child whose steps or report land after a steer, in a later turn, or outside any turn keeps them under its launch. A part left holding only moved steps is not drawn, unless its turn ended other than completed: a failure stays on the timeline.
- Live state is read per launch: a child can still be working while any AO turn holding its launch or one of its steps runs.
- A settled turn keeps a team out of its "Worked for" fold only while a child is still working; otherwise the team folds with the turn's other work.
- `Timeline` derives the panel's list from every turn group (it is virtualized), provides `OpenSubagentContext` to the team rows, and portals `SubagentPanel` into the inspector tab: the same route side chats take, so no new data path.
- The parent's live row no longer names a child's running step as its own.
- The chat's Escape handler ignores keys from the portaled panel, as its click handler already did, so Escape there does not interrupt the parent turn.

**Plumbing**
- `SessionView` owns the tab's container, and reveals the tab through `transitionInspectorView`, so the inspector resizes as it does on a tab click.
- `SessionChatSurface` passes the container, that reveal and the chat's model catalog to the chat (through `SubagentPanelHost`), and reports availability.
- `SessionInspector` and the product-ui shell gain a `subagents` view. While a requested Subagents view waits for the chat to report, the inspector shows Summary without writing it back.
- `ui-store` gains a per-session `subagentsAvailable` flag, set the same way as `setBrowserUnseen`.

**UI**
- `SubagentTeam.tsx`, `SubagentPanel.tsx` and `SubagentTranscript.tsx` are built from existing pieces: `ActivityRun`, `ChatMarkdown`, `LiveResponseStatus` with `liveTaskLabel`, `AgentAvatar`, app-icons, product-ui's `InspectorSection`, `TurnSettingsBar`, `ui/button`, `ui/pressable` and `ui/tooltip`.
- The transcript is one shared component, used by the panel and the inline fallback.
- State is never shown by color alone.
- The chat draws no focus rings, so the team header and the folded rows show keyboard focus with a fill.
- A child's name carries no native `title` tooltip.
- **Strings:** new strings are added to all 9 locales, with the plural forms each needs (Russian's one/few/many/other included). The fold reuses the sidebar's "Show {{count}} more agents" and "Show fewer agents".

Nothing existing is removed. Every child step still renders, under its agent. Other reasoning rows are still dropped. This changes Claude/ACP runs only: AO's Codex driver does not record Codex's own subagent spawns yet, and mobile shows the same rows as before. The components read a neutral `Subagent`; only `subagent-team.ts` knows Claude's records.

## Testing

- **Unit and component tests:**
  - `subagent-team.test.ts`: detection, partition, every state, and step sections.
  - `SubagentTeam.test.tsx`: rows, states, per-child live state, header counts, the inline fallback, opening in the panel, and "No steps recorded" for a child that ended before any step.
  - `SubagentPanel.test.tsx`: the Summary-style sections and their order, the newest ten with the faded, counted fold, the read-only conversation and its disabled composer, the live row, the prompt fold, another child opening fresh, long-path wrapping, a failed launch, and the fallback when the open child is gone.
  - `ChatWorkspaceSubagents.test.tsx`: one team and no loose rows, steers, a child's steps and report landing in a later turn or in none, the finished team folding into "Worked for" closed, a later failed turn keeping its failure, Escape in the panel, and the panel opening on the clicked child and following it live.
  - `SessionInspector`: the tab normally, on an orchestrator's rail, and kept through the gap before the chat reports.
  - `SessionView`: the Browser to Subagents resize.
  - `ui-store`: the availability flag.
  - The product-ui shell slot.
- **Each regression test fails without its fix:**
  - live state across a steer
  - the parent row not claiming a child's step
  - Escape in the panel not interrupting the parent turn
  - a child picked up in a later turn staying Working until its report arrives
  - a later turn that held only a child's steps keeping its failure
- **Current head:** `tsgo` passes for the frontend, and the subagent suites (`SubagentTeam`, `SubagentPanel`, `ChatWorkspaceSubagents`) pass (34 tests).
- **Earlier heads in this round:** `SessionChatSurface` (82 tests) after the composer change; the subagent, `SessionInspector` and `ui-store` suites (281) after merging `main` at `ea5d35adb9`; `ChatWorkspace` (262), `SessionView` (307), the product-ui shell (22) and product-ui `tsgo` before that.
- **Full renderer suite,** on an earlier head: 9972 passed. The only 2 failures are desktop main-process tests this PR does not touch, and both fail on this Mac on `main` too: `browser-history-store` (a 20s timeout under full-suite load) and `remote-proxy` (an HTTP/2 hook timeout).
- **Visual:** the working and folded team, hover, the header's mark cut-out, the panel's sections, fold and read-only composer were checked by rendering the real components in a browser, and in the dev app on real data.
- **Real app,** on real dev data, on an earlier head:
  - an orchestrator chat with dozens of subagents
  - a subagent running live in the panel: the live row, steps appearing, then the report
  - long paths wrapping in the prompt bubble, with no scroll track painted

title: fix(cli): route ao browser to the configured remote agent browser
body:
﻿Code changes: +230 -4
Tests: +229 -0
Others: +40 -0

## What

On a daemon configured with `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL`/`AO_AGENT_BROWSER_TOKEN`, `ao browser <args>` now forwards to that remote agent-browser service instead of the desktop browser bridge, and agents get matching remote-browser instructions.

## Why

Fixes #7166. The remote-browser feature (PR #6652) left `ao browser` wired to the desktop bridge only. On a self-hosted host every browser command failed with `BROWSER_RUNTIME_RECONNECTING` while the configured remote Chromium worked fine through its own client. The injected skill pointer and installed guide still described the desktop command set (`status`, `act`, `--delta`, per-session isolation), so agents following their instructions used the wrong interface and retried it. A shell alias cannot fix this because AO pins its own executable first on session PATHs.

I reproduced the full failure locally before the fix: a real daemon with `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL` set, a working remote Chromium (rbhost + agent-browser serving `https://example.com`), and a real spawned agent session whose `ao browser snapshot --interactive` returned exactly `BROWSER_RUNTIME_RECONNECTING` while the remote service received zero requests; its system prompt and installed `commands/browser.md` were the desktop variants.

## Reproduction evidence

Before the fix, on a daemon started with `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080` and a live remote Chromium (rbhost + agent-browser, already serving `https://example.com` through its own client), a spawned agent session ran the commands its injected instructions told it to:

```text
$ ao browser status
Browser runtime: disconnected (electron-webcontents-debugger)        # exit 0

$ ao browser snapshot --interactive
Desktop browser runtime is reconnecting; retry shortly
(BROWSER_RUNTIME_RECONNECTING) [request YASH/vccj247vha-000072]       # exit 1

$ ao browser act "example"
Desktop browser runtime is reconnecting; retry shortly
(BROWSER_RUNTIME_RECONNECTING) [request YASH/vccj247vha-000076]       # exit 1
```

The remote service logged zero incoming command requests during all three — `ao browser` never contacted it. The session's on-disk `system.md` contained the "AO desktop Browser panel" section pointing at the desktop guide, and the installed `commands/browser.md` was the desktop variant ("The desktop app must be open", "isolated profiles"), with no remote guide present.
## How

- **CLI routing** (`browser_remote.go`, `root.go`): before Cobra parses anything, `ao browser <args...>` with both env vars set POSTs `{args, files}` to `<url>/agent` with the bearer token — the same command contract the shipped `experiments/remote-browser-poc/browser` client speaks — and relays output, writes returned files (screenshots), and surfaces service errors. This intentionally forwards the remote command interface verbatim rather than re-implementing desktop subcommands: remote syntax differs (`tab list`, `get url`), so desktop-only parsing would reject it. Clear errors for missing token or unreachable service; desktop hosts are untouched.
- **Session env** (`manager.go`, `lifecycle_wiring.go`): the daemon exports `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL`/`AO_AGENT_BROWSER_TOKEN` into session processes only when it was itself configured with them (protected from project-env overrides, absent on desktop hosts), so the routing works inside AO sessions where PATH resolves to the pinned `ao` binary first.
- **Instructions** (`manager.go`, skill assets): on remote hosts the system prompt points at a new `commands/browser-remote.md` (installed for every host) and states that the host shares one browser across sessions — tabs, cookies, logins included. `SKILL.md` and the quick reference gained remote rows. Desktop text is byte-identical to before.

Intentional omissions: no per-session remote browser, no desktop/remote command parity, and no packaging of a separate client binary — the CLI speaks the service contract directly, so nothing new needs to be on PATH. The `agent-browser` daemon-side relay behavior is unchanged.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestBrowserRemote` — forwarding (method/path/bearer/args), returned-file writes, service error relay, missing-token and unreachable-service errors, and that only `browser` is intercepted.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run 'TestRuntimeEnvInjectsAgentBrowser|TestRuntimeEnvOmitsAgentBrowser|TestAOSkillPointerRemote|TestAOSkillPointerDesktop'` — env injection/protection on remote hosts, absence on desktop hosts, and both prompt variants.
- `go test ./internal/skillassets/` — remote guide content and materialization.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet` on touched packages, gofmt clean.
- Live end-to-end reproduction of the failure before the fix (daemon + rbhost + agent-browser + spawned agent session), as described under Why.

Pre-existing failures verified unrelated by re-running them on a stashed tree: Windows symlink privilege (`TestRenderCheckReplacesItsEarlierScreenshot`) and unix-path absoluteness (`TestChatStartsPassTheAOToolServerWithOnlyDaemonCoordinates` and neighbors) fail identically on unmodified `main` on this Windows host; CI runs them on Linux.

- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene

- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (all 20 checks green: lint, backend-core, chat-race, sqlite-race, session-store-race, cloud-build-test, windows-workspace, native macos/ubuntu/windows, container, scan, api-drift, sqlc-drift)

title: fix: stop agent processes when the desktop exits
body:
Code changes: +264 -29  
Tests: +298 -0  
Others: +12 -4  

## What

Stop agent processes when an app-owned desktop fully exits, including unexpected Electron termination. Keep session history and worktrees available for resume.

## Why

Workers currently remain alive after both Electron and its daemon exit. An isolated baseline run with idle Claude and Codex Chat workers left ten host, provider, and MCP processes running after full desktop exit.

This intentionally changes the existing background-work policy: full desktop exit interrupts agent work. The previous proposal to stop workers on quit was declined on policy grounds; this PR makes that decision explicit for review.

Related: #2523, #5948, #5451.

## How

- Full quit requests agent shutdown through the existing loopback-only control route. The daemon validates app ownership before accepting it and stops session agents, reviewer terminals, session shells, and remaining Chat controllers.
- Losing the desktop supervisor connection requests the same cleanup after its five-second grace period. An already-requested daemon replacement wins, so updates and planned relaunches preserve providers.
- Ordinary macOS window close keeps its existing tray behavior. Headless and keep-alive daemons remain outside desktop-owned cleanup.
- Session records and worktrees remain available. Killing both Electron and the daemon still bypasses this cleanup; this does not implement general ownership of dev apps launched by an outer Claude/Codex CLI.

## Testing

Focused local validation passed, run serially at lowered scheduling priority:

- Go HTTP shutdown endpoint, desktop-exit policy, app ownership, and replacement preservation tests.
- Go session-manager tests for stopping agents while retaining worktrees and resumable session identity.
- Go Chat tests for explicit termination versus daemon-replacement detach.
- Daemon wiring compiled with no daemon tests executed.
- 21 frontend tests across desktop quit and daemon shutdown policy passed in 1.49 seconds.
- Isolated TypeScript checking for the shutdown helper and its tests passed; Electron main-process syntax transpilation passed.
- Whitespace validation passed.

Go commands used GOMAXPROCS=2, a 768 MiB soft memory limit, package parallelism 1, and 30-second test deadlines. Frontend tests used one worker and a 512 MiB Node heap cap. That earlier focused run reused existing frontend tooling without installing dependencies.

Post-change manual verification used the actual Electron app from this branch, a fresh local dependency install, a built daemon/ACP runtime, isolated scratch data, and real authenticated Claude and Codex workers. No written tests were rerun during this manual verification.

- User-assisted **Quit AO Completely** from the actual lab tray: Electron requested `/shutdown`, the daemon logged a clean stop, and all 21 tracked app/agent processes were gone about 1.1 seconds after observed desktop exit. The three session records remained resumable, uncommitted files survived, and lab ports were closed.
- Force Quit of Electron with idle Claude, then with both idle Claude and Codex: desktop, daemon, hosts, providers, and MCP children stopped within about 6.2 seconds.
- Force Quit while Claude ran a real `sleep 120` command, with Codex Chat, a Claude TUI session, and a session shell also live: all 22 tracked processes stopped within 8.2 seconds, including the running command.
- Claude and Codex resumed natively afterward with unchanged conversation IDs and retained messages. The interrupted turn was recorded as failed. All three sessions stayed resumable and all worktrees retained uncommitted sentinel files. TUI native resume also returned successfully.
- Closing/reopening the desktop window preserved the worker host PIDs and worktree files.
- Wrong/missing app-run ownership returned HTTP 409, and a disallowed Origin returned HTTP 403; the daemon and workers remained running.
- A plain replacement `/shutdown` preserved both provider host PIDs; after desktop/daemon restart, the same hosts were adopted.

Real installer update/relaunch, Windows/Linux manual behavior, and simultaneous SIGKILL of both desktop and daemon were not exercised. Normal macOS SIGTERM did not fully exit the app, consistent with its background/tray quit behavior; it is not counted as a full-quit cleanup pass.

Full local suites, race tests, lint, and full frontend typechecking/builds were intentionally skipped to limit local resource use. Automatic commit/push hooks were skipped for the same reason. At the initial submission's remote inspection, all 22 completed CI jobs passed; a separate `build-test` job was queued. Manual validation required no additional source changes. All lab workers and launchers exited; the unrelated running dev app was left untouched.

## Latest rebase and manual workspace fix

Rebased onto main `2339cbb41f5d22fa9d74863eac0fe0d65fe871aa`; current head `b916314292d7b239f209f5a2b402ec1f04f09617`. All four PR patches remain unchanged. This includes the already-merged desktop daemon-request fix #7271, which resolves the workspace `403 ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN` observed during the five-harness manual run. No duplicate fix or daemon origin-guard exemption was added.

On this head, restarted the actual Electron app against the same isolated scratch data, opened the saved Pi session, and used Open workspace options → Finder. Finder opened the correct session directory and showed the retained sentinel and lifecycle files. The app's workspace requests returned HTTP 200; the telemetry identity hand-off returned 204. Stopped the idle Pi agent afterward.

Only dependency installation, launch builds, and actual manual app operations were performed for this rebase, per the user's instruction. No automated test suites, lint, or typechecks were run. Fresh GitHub CI is pending; validation recorded below belongs to earlier heads.

## Previous rebase validation

Rebased all four commits onto `97d18e3d0565608738e2ddb10636e84ddc81b4b9` without conflicts. Current PR head: `0eabca44e6`. `git range-diff` verified all four patches are unchanged.

Post-rebase local checks passed: frontend and E2E typechecking, all 226 focused updater/desktop quit tests, shutdown-policy/ownership/endpoint and session/provider preservation tests under Go's race detector, backend `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`, and Cloud client/product UI typechecks. Full suites were not rerun locally for this unchanged-patch rebase; fresh CI is pending. The broader validation results below belong to the pre-rebase head and are retained as history.

## Update restart follow-up

Commits `e7b357a586` and `0146a5c8df` fix the Windows/Linux update shutdown regression identified in review. Installer handoff sets restart intent on every platform before Electron can quit, preserving agents during updates. Canceled quits, thrown installer failures, and non-macOS updater error events clear that intent so a later ordinary full quit stops agents normally. Canceling a macOS restart permits a fresh retry; clearing an ordinary quit before installer handoff retains the preparation already in progress and prevents duplicate handoffs.

Regression coverage connects the actual updater restart getter to `requestDesktopShutdown` on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and covers cancellation/retry, synchronous/asynchronous installer failures, rejected installs, and preserving pending macOS preparation.

Follow-up local validation used Node 24.22.1 and Go 1.27.1:

- 226 focused updater/desktop quit tests passed, including the final cancellation guard. Focused updater typechecking passed again on the final head.
- Full frontend and E2E typechecking passed. The complete frontend Vitest suite passed: 533 files, 9,149 tests passed, six skipped.
- `npm run build` passed and produced the macOS ARM64 desktop package, including production main/preload/renderer bundles and native dependency preparation. No publishing or production deployment was run.
- Backend build/vet and the complete Chat-service, session-manager, HTTP, SQLite, and store race suites passed. Native CLI E2E and real Electron HTTP origin/boundary tests passed.
- Cloud Go build/vet/race suites, Cloud client and product UI typechecks/tests/package dry-runs, docs translations/tests/build, 17 native-helper configuration tests, and SQL/API regeneration drift checks passed.

The full local backend race command did **not** pass overall: nine packages failed in unchanged adapter/terminal/observer paths (`commandcode`, `opencode`, `opencodev2`, `chatdriver/acp`, `chatdriver/opencodev2acp`, `reviewer/opencodev2`, `runtime/tmux`, `observe/activity`, `terminal`). The first three failures reproduced on original PR head `0561069f91`; the OpenCode tests pick up a host Homebrew binary. No Go files changed in this follow-up. Local pinned golangci-lint also reports an existing `revive/time-naming` warning at `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:6475`.

The local Chromium renderer suite passed 121/122 tests, with a pointer-drag text-selection failure in unchanged renderer code. The real-Electron browser postcondition integration failed its page drag-region assertion. These are not counted as local passes. Docker is not running locally, and this macOS ARM64 host cannot reproduce the exact Ubuntu/Windows/macOS Intel runners. The final head's corresponding backend, frontend, renderer, lint, and container CI jobs passed. Real packaged installer update/relaunch behavior remains unperformed.

Pre-rebase CI at `0146a5c8df`: 22 checks passed, including full frontend, renderer, all backend/race suites, Windows workspace, CLI on all three operating systems, container smoke, lint, and generated-contract drift. The remaining [macOS update-helper job](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40235935060/job/121297436175) is stuck at “Compile and test wake helper” beyond its configured 15-minute timeout. GitHub accepted a force-cancel request, but the job remains in progress and GitHub refused its retry until cancellation completes. It is **not** counted as passed. The native wake policy/effects/low-power and update-helper state test programs all compiled and passed locally on macOS ARM64. This follow-up supersedes the initial submission's narrower validation notes above.

title: feat(search): search file contents and chats from the command palette
body:
Code changes: +1393 -28  
Tests: +899 -42  
Others: +374 -0  

A smaller take on #7068: same features, about a third of the code (+2,314 vs +6,730), no Bleve and no new Go dependencies.

## What you get in ⌘K

- **In files**: lines inside the current session's files. Enter opens the file at that line.
- **In chats**: messages from any chat on this machine. Enter opens the chat scrolled to the message.
- **Settings and actions**: about 50 settings rows and 21 shortcut actions are now searchable. "dark mode" finds Theme, "toggle sidbar" runs Toggle sidebar.
- A control whose name holds every typed word stays above file and chat hits, so Enter runs the control, not a file that mentions it.

## How it works

- **Files**: `git grep` per query over tracked and untracked, non-ignored files, retaining the first three matching lines per file before ranking. Every word must be on the line (any order, case-insensitive). If no line has them all, lines with the most words win. Ranking favors declarations, word starts and matching file names, and ranks tests, generated code, lockfiles and translations lower. No index, so an edit is searchable on the next keystroke.
- **Chats**: an SQLite FTS5 index on finished messages (`conversation_messages_fts`), kept in sync by triggers. Search uses the current Chat transcript's visibility rule, so detached conversations, Terminal-only histories, edited-away and rolled-back messages never show. The palette hides hits whose session is not loaded locally.
- **Settings, actions and deep links** reuse the pieces from #7068 (`palette-registry`, `settings-focus`, `useChatMessageFocus`, open-at-line).

New routes: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/search/content` and `GET /api/v1/conversations/search`. Matches come back wrapped in U+0002/U+0003 inside the text.

## Performance vs #7068

Original measurements before review fixes, using the same queries on this repo (5.7k files) and a real chat database (2.7k messages, plus a 20x copy). These have not been rerun after the review changes.

| | This PR | #7068 |
|---|---|---|
| File search, p50 / p95 | 88 / 110 ms | 5.5 / 12 ms |
| First build before file search works | none | 9 s, 119 MB peak heap |
| File index on disk | none | 49 MB per session |
| Edit visible in search | 80 ms | 700 ms |
| Chat search p50, real / 20x | 0.6 / 14 ms | 2.6 / 20.5 ms |
| Chat index on disk, real / 20x | 0.5 / 9.4 MB | 3.5 / 82 MB |

File search is slower per query, but well under the palette's 200 ms debounce, and needs no build, disk or memory.

## Review follow-up

Addressed @MohamedKamran's feedback: generated sqlc model, bounded per-file grep output, reachable current Chat results, and visible search errors. Resolved conflicts with `main` and aligned Remote hosts search visibility. GitHub smoke CI also exposed stale maximize labels in the newly merged Cloud review tests; updated their selectors to the current UI labels. Local checks and tests are intentionally skipped at the requester's instruction; validation runs on GitHub.

## Test plan

1. Open a session with a worktree, press ⌘K, type `where do we close the palette` (or any function name in that repo). Check the "In files" row and that Enter opens the file at that line.
2. Type a sentence you remember from a chat. Check that Enter opens the chat scrolled to that message.
3. Type `dark mode`. Theme comes first; Enter opens Settings at the Theme row.
4. Type `toggle sidbar`. Toggle sidebar comes first and runs on Enter.

title: fix(chat): support Codex structured user input
body:

Tests: +831 -0

## What

Fixes #7121. Handle Codex `item/tool/requestUserInput` through typed input events and native answers instead of approval prompts. Preserve structured choices/free text, reject stale or duplicate answers, and retain accepted content when an immediate `serverRequest/resolved` ACK arrives before persistence.

## Why

Valid Codex questions should remain answerable across additive protocol fields, omitted headers and fast server acknowledgments.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Native questions are not represented as typed user input. | Choices/free text produce native Codex answers and remain in history. |

title: fix(chat): isolate replacements from empty provider branches
body:
Code changes: +7 -7  
Tests: +152 -15  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Give a replacement project orchestrator its own provider branch even when the previous agent never recorded a thread ID. This also covers removing a project and adding the same project ID again. Stored project history remains available.

## Why

The previous fix detects an inherited provider thread, but an empty branch can still belong to the retired session. Branch ownership must also establish that a fresh provider needs a new branch.

Related: #7124

## How

- Treat an active branch owned by another session as inherited state, independently of its provider thread ID.
- Cover all four combinations of a saved/missing predecessor thread and queued/no opening prompt. Check fresh ownership, unchanged predecessor history, and cold resume.
- Make the older orchestrator test helper publish reserved branches through the same atomic store operation as production.
- Rename the existing script timeout test hook to satisfy the full lint check. Its value and timeout behavior are unchanged.

This prevents new ownership drift; it does not repair already-corrupted sessions or change history-retention behavior.

title: fix(mobile): keep the comment composer's glass full height above the keyboard
body: Code changes: +6 -1 Tests: +11 -0 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary On iOS, with the keyboard up, the file diff's line-comment composer drew its Liquid Glass as a thin bar above the field instead of behind it, so the input looked collapsed. **Cause:** `SelectionComposer` rises above the keyboard through `KeyboardStickyView`, which applies a `translateY` transform. Its layout frame stays at the bottom of the screen, under the keyboard. The glass is a SwiftUI `Host`, and its `UIHostingController` insets content for the keyboard by default. It treated almost the whole pill as keyboard safe area, so the material shrank to the `Spacer`'s ~8pt minimum, pinned to the top-leading corner. The session chat composer moves by real layout (`KeyboardAvoidingView`), so it never overlapped the keyboard and never showed this. **Fix:** `ComposerGlass`'s `Host` now sets `ignoreSafeArea="all"`. The glass is only a backdrop and should always fill its pill. This matches the existing `Host` in `ChatTurnSettingsControl.ios.tsx`, and it covers every composer that layers `ComposerGlass`. ## Screenshots | Before (device, keyboard up) | After (iOS 26.5 sim) | | --- | --- | | | | The "after" capture comes from a headless simulator, which can't show the software keyboard. It confirms the composer still draws normally at rest. The keyboard-up case itself still needs a check on a device. ## Testing - New `composer-glass.ios.source.test.ts` checks the prop stays in place. It and the existing `ChatComposer` source and quotes tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` passes for `packages/mobile`. - Ran the branch in an iOS 26.5 simulator against a read-only lab proxy. I checked a single line, a dragged range, a focused field, light and dark theme, and the composer forced 300pt up with a static offset. Every one of these drew correctly even before the fix, which ruled out the transform alone and left the keyboard safe area as the cause. ## Risks - Low. The only behaviour change is that the glass host no longer insets for the keyboard or container safe areas, and a backdrop that fills its RN frame should never inset for either.

title: fix(mobile): stop spawn photo thumbnails jumping to the sheet's top-left and blocking the prompt
body: Code changes: +40 -32 Tests: +7 -1 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary Fixes the spawn sheet's photo thumbnails on iOS. After you attached a photo, the thumbnail first showed up above the selectors, then jumped to the sheet's top-left corner. After opening and closing the image viewer, the prompt also stopped accepting taps and scrolls, so you couldn't keep editing it. ## Root cause On iOS 26, react-native-screens (4.26) searches a form sheet's direct native children for a `ScrollView` and resizes it to fill the sheet (`RNSScreen applyFrameCorrectionForDescendantScrollView`). Fabric flattens layout-only Views, so the attachment row's horizontal `ScrollView` becomes a direct child, third after the background and the prompt. For anything past the second child, `coerceChildScrollViewComponentSizeToSize` gives up and the legacy fallback runs `[scrollView setFrame:self.frame]`. Every sheet resize therefore put the row at **(0, 0) and stretched it to the full sheet (440×808pt)**. The keyboard hiding or returning around the photo picker or the image viewer counts as a resize, and so does dragging between detents. Yoga's layout stayed correct: the slot above the selectors stayed empty. The stretched scroll view was transparent and sat above the prompt `TextInput`, so it swallowed taps and scrolls. That is why the prompt looked clipped and couldn't be edited. Confirmed with `lldb` `recursiveDescription` on the simulator: before the fix, `RCTScrollViewComponentView` frame = `(0 0; 440 808)`. After the fix it is `(0 0; 408 62)` inside its wrapper. The same code path also logs a react-native-screens dev warning ("FormSheet with ScrollView expects at most 2 subviews"). ## Fix Wrap the row's `ScrollView` in `` (`packages/mobile/lib/spawn-attachment-row.tsx`). The scroll view is then no longer a direct child, so react-native-screens leaves its frame alone. The Android spawn sheet doesn't use this form sheet, so it is unaffected. ## Before / after (iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator, iOS 26.5) | Before: photo attached | Before: after a sheet resize | After: after a detent resize | After: viewer closed, prompt edited | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | In the second "before" shot, tapping the thumbnail dismissed the keyboard and resized the sheet. The thumbnail jumped to the top-left, and taps on the prompt no longer focused it. After the fix, the row stays above the selectors through detent drags and viewer open/close. Tapping the prompt after closing the viewer focuses it, and typing appends (" now"). ## Tests - New `spawn-attachment-row.test.tsx` case: the row's `ScrollView` sits inside a non-collapsable `View`. It fails without the fix and passes with it. - Updated the `spawn.source.test.ts` assertion that pinned the old markup. - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 239 files, 2498 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. - Manual check on the simulator: attach a photo → drag the sheet to half and back → open/close the viewer → tap the prompt and type. ## Risks / follow-ups - After the fix I didn't re-check with the software keyboard: the simulator switched to hardware-keyboard mode. The detent drag goes through the same react-native-screens resize path the keyboard triggers. - Any other `ScrollView` that becomes a direct native child of an iOS form sheet hits the same trap. I didn't find another one on the spawn sheet.

Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.2 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

Updates `undici` from 6.27.0 to 6.29.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v6.29.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 · GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

Release notes

Sourced from seroval's releases.

seroval-plugins@1.7.1

Patch Changes

  • 2d03651: serialize, toJSON, crossSerialize and toCrossJSON now throw when the value contains an async iterable or a ReadableStream, as they do for a promise. Before, they sent a stream that never got its values. Use an async or streaming function to send them.

seroval@1.7.1

Patch Changes

  • b703710: createCrossDeserializer no longer causes unhandled rejections. This covers a rejected promise that the caller never reads, and a pending promise that abort rejects. Code that awaits the promise still gets the rejection.
  • 2d03651: serialize, toJSON, crossSerialize and toCrossJSON now throw when the value contains an async iterable or a ReadableStream, as they do for a promise. Before, they sent a stream that never got its values. Use an async or streaming function to send them.
  • 2c25bf3: serialize, toJSON, crossSerialize and toCrossJSON now send a createStream stream that has ended with all its events. A stream that is still open, or a live stream, now throws. Before, they sent an empty stream that never ended.

seroval-plugins@1.7.0

Minor Changes

  • 4c0008f: Add createLiveStream(), a single-consumer stream that holds one event at a time and resolves each producer write only after the serialized record is accepted. crossSerializeStream and toCrossJSONStream callbacks may now return a promise; the next record, and the acceptance of the source event behind it, wait for it to settle. Records discovered while parsing an event are emitted after the record that introduces them, one callback runs at a time, onDone waits for the last callback and is not called after an output failure, and cleanup runs every callback once. Async iterables and ReadableStream values read their next chunk only after the previous record is accepted. Existing streaming plugin lifecycle hooks remain available; parsing a live stream is the preferred way to connect an incremental source.
  • f2b7d0c: Raise the supported Node.js floor from >=10 to >=20 in engines, remove the no-op typesVersions from seroval, give seroval-plugins main, module and types fields plus a typesVersions entry that points at the emitted web declarations, and link the plugins package to the workspace copy of seroval.
  • 5ab601f: Add plugin context hooks for parsing an async iterable as a stream source. Use them in the ReadableStream plugin to avoid a separate live-stream producer while keeping backpressure, cancellation, and wire format intact.   • 90e8f73: The web plugins that match instances of a built-in class, such as URL, Blob and Headers, now set skipPlainObjects. With a seroval version that supports it, serializing plain objects with these plugins is faster.

Minor Changes

  • 9a75aae: Add the assignSharedRefsOnly option to crossSerialize and crossSerializeAsync. It stores only the values the output reads more than once in $R, which makes shorter output when no later script refers back to it.

Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.6 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

title: fix(session): name exclusive-operation holders and reap stale ones
body:
Code changes: +31972 -122717
Tests: +23073 -107431
Others: +5924 -16639

When a harness switch (e.g. TUI→Chat) is refused because another exclusive holder exists, the refusal now names the holder, and holders that are provably dead (their session exited) are reaped instead of blocking every future switch until restart.

Reproduced before the fix: a worker that died while holding the exclusive handle blocked all harness updates on that harness indefinitely (`ListLiveReviewerHandles`-style ghost). Regression tests cover naming, reap-on-exited, and keep-alive for live holders.

Provenance: shipped on our fork as PR #30 (merged), running in production on our install since 2026-10-22.

Evidence from the fork PR: https://github.com/wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator/pull/30

title: fix(chat): keep reasoning rows on the timeline and make thinking-block collapse per-conversation
body:
Code changes: +32019 -122731
Tests: +23071 -107382
Others: +5924 -16639

Two related chat-timeline behaviors:

- A reasoning row that has content stays on the timeline (default visible) instead of disappearing when the next turn starts.
- Thinking-block collapse is remembered per conversation: collapsing one thinking block hides later thinking blocks in the same conversation until re-expanded, and other conversations are unaffected. Outside a conversation scope the preference stays in-memory.

Provenance: shipped on our fork (PRs #29/#33 line), in daily use since 2026-10-22. Frontend-only.

title: feat(chat): Steer action on a queued message — cut the running turn and send it now
body:
Code changes: +32078 -122810
Tests: +23199 -107630
Others: +5925 -16640

When a turn is running, a plain send is queued. The queue dock's cards now offer **Steer** next to **Edit**: Steer cancels the running turn (marked interrupted in the timeline), waits for it to settle, and promotes the addressed queued message to a running turn immediately.

- Harness-agnostic: uses the session cancel seam plus queued-turn promotion — no per-harness steering protocol required. On drivers that advertise no steer support the button still works via cut-and-resend (pinned by test).
- The interrupted turn keeps its partial output visible; nothing silently vanishes.
- Plain send keeps today's queue behavior; Steer is explicit.

title: fix: make terminal backgrounds follow window transparency
body:
Code changes: +37 -13  
Tests: +41 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Terminal backgrounds now follow macOS window transparency, including terminals that are already open.

## Why

Terminals kept an opaque background when the rest of the window was transparent. Making the canvas transparent also exposed black rectangles behind dimmed text and artwork in Codex and Claude Code.

## How

Clear the terminal canvas, gutters, and resize cover when window transparency is enabled. Use xterm's DOM renderer in that mode because the WebGL renderer forces some cell backgrounds opaque. Restore WebGL when transparency is disabled, retaining the terminal buffer across toggles.

Text, cursor colors, and terminal color-protocol replies retain their solid theme colors. Transparent mode trades WebGL acceleration for correct alpha rendering.

## Testing

- The user manually tried the updated isolated Electron app and confirmed the fix works after reporting the black rectangles in Codex and Claude Code.
- Added coverage for live transparency toggles in light and dark themes, retained terminal buffers, and opaque backgrounds outside macOS.
- CI passed: frontend tests and typechecks, macOS helper checks, and the complete renderer smoke suite. The smoke suite passed on rerun after an intermittent chat-composer caret-position failure; no code changes were needed for the rerun.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions; initial local validation was deferred at the user's request and CI results were subsequently verified
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(shortcuts): improve settings and help dialog usability
body:
Code changes: +637 -789  
Tests: +39 -16  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Make shortcut settings easier to scan and customize using the Harness page layout and readable, separate key badges. The ⌘/ help modal uses the same badges in a compact three-column layout, showing one binding per command with a styled +N pill for alternatives. Customize opens Settings → Shortcuts.

## Why

The previous screen repeated category labels, compressed key combinations into small text, and exposed competing edit/remove/add icons on every row.

## How

- Keep the heading, search, and filters stationary while the command list scrolls inside the available pane height.

title: fix(lifecycle): stop holding the input lease across PR reaction sends
body:
Code changes: +25 -12  
Tests: +142 -28  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Follow-up to #7209 (merged), which fixed the deadlock that left hibernated Chat workers unable to wake ("could not wake the agent: resume agent <id>: context deadline exceeded"). This PR hardens the lifecycle side so the same class of bug cannot come back:

- Lifecycle reactions (CI, review and merge-conflict nudges) no longer hold Session Manager's input lease while they deliver.
- Each open PR's lifecycle reaction is bounded by 30s, so one wedged session cannot hold up every other session's PR status. Merged and closed PRs are exempt.

## Why

Lifecycle's guard held the input lease across the whole reaction send. A send that has to wait on an exclusive operation for the same session, such as waking a hibernated Chat session (the resume waits for admitted input to drain), deadlocked on that lease:

```
observe/scm.(*Observer).Poll
 lifecycle.ApplySCMObservation → sendOnce
  sessionguard.NudgeUrgent → sendThenChecked            ← held Session Manager's input lease
   session_manager.Send → sendChat → chat.relayChatTurn → workingController → wakeHibernated
    session_manager.WakeHibernatedChat → ResumeAgentWithMode → beginAgentResume
     beginAgentOperation                                ← waited 60s for that lease to drain
```

#7209 fixed the delivery side: a relay into a sleeping session now queues and wakes in the background. This PR removes the other half. No lifecycle reaction holds the lease, so a future delivery path that waits on an exclusive operation cannot recreate the deadlock. It also stops nudges from being dropped silently during a kill, switch or restore.

## How

**Lease removal.** `daemon.go` no longer wires `lifecycle.SetSessionInputLease`, and that method and its test are removed. Reactions reach the agent through `sessMgr.Send`:

- **TUI sessions:** Session Manager's own guard still holds the lease across the pane write (`m.messenger.SetInputLease(m)`), so a kill, switch or restore still keeps a nudge out of the pane. That guard maps `SuppressedInputGated` to `ErrOperationInProgress`. The error travels through `sendOnce` and `ApplySCMObservation` to the observer, which leaves the PR's hashes unacknowledged and retries on the next poll. Before, lifecycle's own guard suppressed the nudge silently, and it was not sent again until the PR changed.
- **Chat sessions:** they get the same admission as a user's send. An interface transition queues the nudge; a controller handoff returns `ErrControllerHandoff` (retried next poll); a hibernated session queues it and wakes in the background (#7209).

**Timeout.** `DefaultLifecycleTimeout = 30s` bounds `ApplySCMObservation` for open PRs; a timed-out reaction is retried on the next poll.

- It only cuts work that honors cancellation. A chat wake and a session teardown run on their own budgets.
- One TUI nudge with its delivery confirmation takes at most ~6s (3 Enters × 2s), so 30s leaves headroom.
- If the deadline cuts a send after the pane write, the result matches the existing `ErrDeliveryUnconfirmed` path: the error is accounted and the dedup signature is not recorded, so the nudge may be sent once more.
- Merged and closed PRs are exempt. They are not selected again after a failed reaction, so a teardown or final notification cut at 30s would otherwise stay undone until restart.

**Known costs.** While an exclusive operation keeps refusing a nudge (for example a long agent switch), each poll:

- re-lists that repo's open PRs (a failed reaction marks the repo refresh incomplete, which is what drives the retry);
- logs `scm observer: lifecycle notification failed` at Error.

Both stop when the operation ends. Logging `ErrOperationInProgress` / `ErrControllerHandoff` at Info is an optional follow-up if the log proves noisy.

## Testing

- `TestLifecycleNudgeDuringExclusiveOperationIsRetryable`: a lifecycle guard without the lease nudges a TUI session during a kill and gets `ErrOperationInProgress` with no pane write. The retry after the kill is delivered. With the old wiring (lease on the lifecycle guard) the same nudge returned `nil`, a silent drop.
- `TestPoll_TerminalPRLifecycleIsNotTimeBounded`: a merged PR's reaction runs without a deadline and completes; an open PR's reaction in the same poll is cut at the timeout. It fails if the timeout is applied to every PR.
- `TestPoll_StalledLifecycleDoesNotBlockOtherSessions`: one stalled open-PR reaction does not block other sessions.
- `TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat` (from #7209) still passes on this branch.
- `go test` for `observe/scm`, `lifecycle`, `sessionguard`, `daemon` and `session_manager` passes locally. The exceptions are four `TestSpawn_*Binary*` tests that need tmux on macOS, and one spawn test that flaked once under load and passes alone. CI is green.

Lab, measured before #7209 merged: an isolated daemon with 8 hibernated Claude Code chat sessions, 6 of their PRs made conflicting, and the other 2 pushed every 30s for 12 minutes.

| build | polls during 12 min of conflicts | slowest poll | failed reactions |
|---|---|---|---|
| main before #7209 | 2 | 374.8s | 11 |
| timeout only (first revision of this PR) | 2 | 367.8s | 11 |
| lease removal + timeout | 25 | 23.1s | 0 |

With #7209 on `main` the deadlock no longer reproduces there, so this table shows what the lease removal fixed on its own, not a gain over today's `main`.

title: fix(desktop): keep a Cloud Chat session's shell tab on the Cloud surface
body:
Code changes: +27 -1  
Tests: +36 -2  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

A production user had a Cloud session's Chat view replaced by a red **"session not found"** screen. This happened right after they opened a shell tab, with the new-terminal shortcut, in a Cloud session that was in Chat mode. The sandbox, worker and conversation were all healthy: every control-plane request in that window returned 2xx, and the shell itself attached.

Cause: `SessionView` keeps the Chat surface mounted for `worker`, `reviewer` **and** `shell` targets, but only used `CloudSessionChatSurface` for `worker`/`reviewer`. A Cloud session with a shell target fell through to the local `SessionChatSurface`. That surface fetches `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation` from this machine's daemon, which has never heard of a Cloud session and answers `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` ("session not found").

## Fix

- `SessionView`: every Cloud Chat target stays on `CloudSessionChatSurface`.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface`: passes the session's shells (list, selected target, select/close/rename) through to `ChatWorkspace`. `ChatWorkspace` already renders them as tabs, as for local sessions, and `TerminalPane` already dials Cloud shells through the control plane (`workspace` terminal tickets).

Not included: a visible "+" new-terminal button in the Cloud Chat tab strip. Cloud Chat never had one, and the shortcut remains the way to open a shell there. That can follow separately.

## Testing

- New `SessionView` test: a Cloud Chat session with a selected shell stays on the Cloud surface, shows the shell, and switches back to chat. It fails on `main` (the Cloud surface disappears) and passes with this change.
- `SessionView.test.tsx` and `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx` pass.
- Full frontend suite (`vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts`): 9048 passed, 52 failed in 7 files. The same 52 tests fail on `main` at 2782e4d7f6 on this machine (`forge.config`, `annotate-preload`, `browser-profile-import`, `cloud-agent-proxy`, `remote-proxy`, `ChatWorkspace` context meter, `ContextMeter`), so none is caused by this change.
- `tsc --noEmit`: the same 8 errors with and without this change, all in Electron main-process files untouched here, so they come from the local install.

title: fix(ui): give overlays one faint edge and make pickers match dropdown menus
body:
Code changes: +105 -88\
Tests: +7 -7\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Modals, menus, pickers and popovers now share one faint edge and one light shadow. The model, permission and settings pickers now look like the regular dropdown menus. Hovering a theme in Settings only previews it now.

## Why

Overlay edges made the app look sloppy. Each overlay primitive had its own border and shadow, so there were about nine border styles and eight shadow styles. In dark mode no shadow showed at all, because every elevation shadow was tinted with the background color. Some specific problems:

- Dialogs and the side sheet used a bare `border`. In Tailwind v4 that is `currentColor`, so they had a near-white edge.
- Picker menus used `border-settings-menu`. That class also matched Tailwind's theme color `--color-settings-menu`, which is the menu fill, so their edge was invisible and they had no shadow. The three-dot menu next to them had a visible edge.
- Settings menus mixed 40% of the text color into their edge, so it looked bright.
- There were double edges in the Add a project list, the update toast stack and toasts that had both a ring and a border.
- Pickers used their own row padding, height, radius, text size and highlight, so they did not match the dropdown menus.
- Hovering a theme and then moving off the options left the hovered theme applied until the menu closed.

## How

- **Tokens.** Two tokens carry the look:
  - `--color-border-overlay` is 2% of the foreground.
  - `--shadow-popover` is `0 4px 12px -4px` at 14% black in dark and at 5% of the foreground in light.
  - The settings menu, settings dialog, command palette and toast tokens point at these two.
  - Both are built from `--foreground` or black, so the derived themes and translucent window mode need no changes.
- **Shared primitives** use the overlay edge and shadow, plus the elevated fill (`bg-overlay`): `menu-styles`, `select`, `popover`, `hover-card`, `dialog`, `sheet` and `option-menu`. Tooltips stay borderless and only get the shadow.
- **Custom overlays.** About a dozen had their own border or shadow, and those overrides are removed. They include the notification menu, toasts, the onboarding dialogs and the composer suggest menu.
- **Picker rows.** Picker and settings menu rows use the action menu's rhythm: rows `px-2 py-1.5 rounded-md text-control`, `interactive-hover` highlight and micro labels. The selected row gets `interactive-active` instead of an outlined row. Per-picker padding overrides in the composer are removed.
- **Theme preview.** `SettingsOptionMenu` ends the preview on blur unless focus moves to another option.
- **Keeping old values.** `--color-border-settings-input` keeps its old value, so non-overlay inputs don't change.

Settings dropdowns get the same denser rows, because they share the picker style.

Not in this PR:
- Pointing `--color-popover` at `--color-bg-elevated`.
- The settings dialog's corner radius, which is 24px or 10px depending on how it is opened.
- The z-20 notices and the terminal find bar going see-through in translucent mode.
- Borders that are not on overlays.

## Testing

I checked it by hand in the desktop app, in dark and light, on a copy of real data. The surfaces were dropdown and right-click menus, the model, permission and settings pickers, the notification menu, dialogs, the command palette, tooltips and the theme menu. I did not run tests, typecheck or lint locally. Six tests that assert exact class strings were updated to the new classes and are left for CI.

title: fix(cloud): keep the model picker inside the control plane's wait
body:
Found while testing the #7164 release on staging before promoting it to prod.

## The problem

On Freestyle, 3 of 10 model catalog requests (`GET .../chat-models`) returned 504 `WORKER_TIMEOUT`, averaging about 11 s.

- The worker builds the catalog from scratch on every request: it starts the Claude ACP adapter and opens a session.
- #7164 added a per-model approval-mode probe with a 5 s budget on top of that.
- That took Freestyle to 11 to 15 s, past the control plane's 12 s wait for any worker request.
- The desktop retries a timeout 3 times, so users mostly see a picker that takes 12 to 36 s, and occasionally "Model choices unavailable".

Coder was not affected (about 8 to 9 s).

## The fix

- **Worker:** remembers each model's probed options for its lifetime, keyed by the adapter and Claude Code that served them. Only a worker's first catalog request probes; every later one costs what it did before probing existed. A new adapter (an upgraded Claude Code) is probed afresh.
- **Control plane:** a catalog request waits 25 s for the worker instead of 12 s, or the configured request wait if that is longer. The worker's own discovery budget is 20 s, so the wait now covers a cold worker plus delivery. Other worker requests keep their 12 s wait.

## Tests

- `TestClaudeCatalogReportsApprovalModesPerModelFromACPOptions` now also checks that a repeat request switches no models and returns the same modes, and that a different adapter is probed again.
- `TestChatModelsRequestWaitsForColdDiscovery` checks the 25 s floor and that a longer configured wait wins.
- `go build` with `GOWORK=off`; `httpapi`, `workerexec` and `workertransport` packages pass.

Staging results will follow in a comment.

title: fix(scm): dedupe PRs reported under a renamed repository's old name
body:
## Summary

After a repository is renamed or transferred, the session inspector shows the same PR twice: the tracked card, plus a "Reported by worker" card for the same number under the old repository name.

**Root cause**
- The project origin still uses the old name, and GitHub redirects it.
- Discovery lists PRs under the old name but stores GitHub's canonical URL.
- A worker that builds the PR link from the origin reports the old-name URL.
- `ListPRListing` dedupes by `owner/repo#number`, so the two URLs never match.

**Fix (reuses the existing `pr_url_alias` table, no schema or query changes)**
- `observe/scm/observer.go`: when a listing under one repository name returns a PR URL under another name, discovery saves the listed-name URL as `URLAlias`, normalized with `ParseChangeRequestURL`. The store already writes that to `pr_url_alias`. Same-name PRs and fork PRs get no alias, because a PR's URL always uses its base repository.
- `store/report_store.go`: `ListReportedPRURLs` resolves each reported URL through `GetPRByURLOrAlias`, first as typed (claim-time aliases are stored that way), then normalized. Any spelling of the old name (case, `www.`, `http://`, trailing `/`) therefore maps to the tracked PR, and the existing key dedupe removes the duplicate card.

This also covers GitLab, because the alias is built from `domain.ParseChangeRequestURL` and not from provider-specific URL formats.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/observe/scm/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/store/ ./internal/service/session/`: pass.
- New: `TestReportedPRURLResolvesStoredURLAlias` (real SQLite: an old-name report, and an `http://www.` / mixed-case / trailing-slash spelling of it, both resolve to the canonical URL; an unrelated reported URL is unchanged).
- New: `TestListedRepoAliasIsNormalized` (the discovery alias is written in normalized form).
- Extended: `TestPoll_DiscoversSameRepoPRAfterRename` now also checks that discovery records the old-name alias.

## Known limits

- PRs discovered before this change have no alias, so an existing duplicate stays until that PR closes. Backfilling would mean writing on every poll, so this change does not do it.
- `ao session claim-pr` still rejects the canonical URL when the origin uses the old name (`PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`). Setting the project's `canonicalRepoURL` already fixes that, so this PR does not change it.

title: feat(cloud): ~3 s Freestyle session start: repository snapshots at connect and after deploys, warmed snapshots, prewarmed agent, in-place start
body:
Code changes: +1279 -137\
Tests: +1017 -17\
Others: +8 -0

## What

New **Freestyle** sessions are ready in about **3 s instead of 7–10 s**, and the desktop no longer blocks on a loading screen while they start or wake. Coder and every other provider start exactly as on `main`: every change is gated on the Freestyle provider.

- **Repository snapshots that are always there and always warm.** A project's snapshot (the harness snapshot with the repository cloned) is now built when the repository is connected and rebuilt right after each deploy, instead of on the first session. Each new snapshot is booted once and discarded ("warmed") before a real session uses it.
- **Orchestrator-spawned workers boot from the repository snapshot.** Before, only sessions created from the app did; workers an orchestrator spawned always cloned.
- **Claude starts ahead of the turn** (from the first version of this PR): during the checkout, and after each turn for the next one.
- **Desktop:** a new or waking Freestyle Chat session stays on its conversation. No startup checklist or full-screen loader: the composer shimmers and queues messages until the worker connects, and a waking session keeps its Paused badge.
- **Fallback when there is no snapshot:** the clone fetches only branch tips first, and the history arrives in the background.
- **Measurement:** `workspace.ready` (in-VM startup breakdown) and a fixed `sandbox.ready` (wakes were reported as `phase=create`, timed from the session's creation).

## Why

A new Freestyle Chat session took about 6 s in production before its agent could answer, behind a 4–5 s full-screen loader. On staging the breakdown showed where the rest went:

- the first session on a repository, and the first after every deploy, cloned (each deploy rebakes the harness snapshots, which made every repository snapshot unusable);
- workers spawned by an orchestrator never used the repository snapshot;
- the first boots from a freshly made snapshot are several seconds slower than later ones (VM 2–3 s and worker start 1.3–2.6 s, then 0.5 s and 0.7 s).

## Before / After

Measured on staging (`workspace.ready` / `sandbox.ready`, seconds from the create request):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Worker created from the app: ready at **9.6 s** (cold repository snapshot) | **3.1 s** (warm repository snapshot) |
| Worker spawned by the orchestrator: **7.3 s**, clones the repository | **~3.0 s**, boots from the repository snapshot |
| Worker connected: 4.7–7.5 s | **1.4–1.5 s** |
| First session after a deploy: clones on a cold snapshot | Snapshots rebuilt and warmed within ~1 min of the rollout (4 rebuilt in 2.4–3.7 s each on staging) |
| New Freestyle Chat session: full-screen loader, then a startup checklist | Opens on its conversation; the composer shimmers and queues messages |
| Opening an idle-paused Freestyle Chat session: full-screen loader while it wakes | Conversation stays, with its Paused badge until the worker is back |
| `sandbox.ready` for a wake: `phase=create`, `ttr` of minutes to days | `phase=resume`, timed from the wake |
| Coder session start | **Unchanged** (startup screen, steps, workspace link) |

Screenshots of the desktop states to follow.

## How

**Repository snapshots (`internal/projectsnapshot`, `internal/httpapi`)**
- `createProject` / `createGitHubProject` start the snapshot build for the project's orchestrator and worker harnesses when it runs on Freestyle.
- `RunRefresher` (control-plane start, then hourly) rebuilds snapshots used within the idle retention that sit on an older harness snapshot. Snapshots are listed under the service context and each project is looked up inside its own organization (`ao_projects` has no service-context read policy).
- `createWorkerChild` and `createSession` share `bootFromProjectSnapshot`; a spawned child boots from the snapshot and keeps it fresh (`Ensure`).
- Warming: one throwaway VM per new snapshot (repository snapshots after their build, harness snapshots at control-plane start) reads the worker, the agent CLIs and the repository, then is deleted. No extra snapshots are kept.

**A new token path: `IssueProjectCheckoutGrant` (please review)**
Builds at connect and after a deploy have no session, so they clone with a token issued for the **project**:
- Same checks as the session grant: installation active, grant not revoked, repository not archived or disabled, user-scoped access re-checked live on GitHub. Archived projects and other organizations' projects are refused.
- Read-only, primary repository only, ≤2 h, never exposed through an API. It only reaches the builder VM through one command's environment, and the clone script fails if the token is found on disk.
- Every issuance writes an `ao_audit_events` record (`github.checkout_grant.project_issued`). The token is handed out only once that record is written.
- The store's checkout-context queries now take a session or a project scope.

**Builder and warming VMs are never left behind**
- These VMs hold a clone of a private repository. They are named after the snapshot they serve (Freestyle slug, from `sandbox.Spec.Name` when the VM has no session) and labelled with org and project.
- A failed delete is retried. A VM still left behind is found by name and deleted before the next VM of that name and by the collector's hourly sweep.

**Worker**
- Prestarted Claude agent with a launch-key check (credential env, model env, directory, instructions, conversation); a mismatch discards it, so a shared session never runs one user's turn on another's credentials. Opt-in via `AO_WORKER_PREWARM_AGENT=1`, which only Freestyle's launch sets.
- No-snapshot clone: `--depth=1 --no-single-branch` plus `--filter=blob:none`, then `CompleteShallowClone` in the background through the credential helper (Freestyle only, `AO_WORKER_PARTIAL_CLONE`).

**Desktop**
- `cloudChatStartingInPlace` (Freestyle Chat, not paused, worker not connected) decides both the in-place start and the in-place wake.
