title: fix(chat): queue relays to a sleeping Chat session instead of waking inline
body:
Code changes: +134 -12  
Tests: +309 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Sending a message to a sleeping (hibernated) Chat worker could fail with:

```
could not wake the agent: resume agent <id>: context deadline exceeded
```

Root cause: a lifecycle nudge deadlocks with the wake it triggers. Lifecycle nudges are the failing-CI note, the merge-conflict note, and review feedback. They reach a Chat worker through `sessionguard`, which holds the session's **input lease** for the whole write. `relayChatTurn` then wakes the hibernated session **synchronously**, and the resume that wakes it (`beginAgentResume`) waits for that same lease to drain:

```
SCM observer tick → lifecycle sendOnce → sessionguard.Nudge / NudgeUrgent
  AcquireSessionInput(id)                                   ← lease held for the write
  → Manager.Send → sendChat → chat.relayChatTurn
    → workingController → wakeHibernated (synchronous)
      → WakeHibernatedChat → ResumeAgentWithMode → beginAgentResume
        → waits for the session's input leases to drain     ← the lease above
60s later: "resume agent <id>: context deadline exceeded" → nudge fails → next tick repeats
```

The nudge is never recorded as delivered, so every SCM tick retries it and deadlocks again. Any user send or chat view that joins the in-flight wake fails with that wake's error. The SCM observer also stalls for 60s per tick, which delays PR/CI updates for every session.

## Changes

- **Fix** (`service/chat/service.go`): when the target session is hibernated, `relayChatTurn` queues the turn durably and wakes in the background, which is what a user's send already does (`queueWithoutController` + `startBackgroundWake`). If the store refuses the queued append because the session woke after the read, the message goes to the live controller.
- **Race with hibernation** (review follow-up): a relay that read the session just before hibernation wrote its marker used to wait on the gate and then wake inline. `switchBeforeSend` hibernates during a user's send without an agent operation fencing input leases, so a lifecycle nudge can hit this window. `admitController(ctx, id, wakeAsleep=false)` now returns `errAsleep` for a session found asleep, and the relay loops back to the queue and background wake. `workingController`'s other callers are unchanged.
- `service/chat/provisioning_queue.go`: queued messages keep sender attribution (`SenderSessionID`, `SenderProjectID`, `SenderDisplayName`) and `InteractionAt`, matching the live send path, so a queued relay still shows who sent it.
- **Diagnostics** (separate commit), added because the incident left no trace:
  - Chat wake start (with the caller chain), join, and result.
  - A warning when an exclusive operation gives up waiting for input to drain, with the lease count and the oldest lease's age, or for hibernation to finish.
  - A log line before a failed background wake fails queued messages.
- **Tests:**
  - `TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat` (new) uses the real Chat service, Session Manager, session guard and SQLite store, wired as in `daemon.go`; only the provider is faked. It covers both the routine nudge (`Nudge`, failing CI) and the urgent one (`NudgeUrgent`, merge conflict), and checks that a user's message sent during the wake does not fail.
  - `TestRelayChatTurnWithIDWakesHibernatedSession` now asserts that the relay returns while the wake is still blocked, and that the message is delivered once it finishes.
  - `TestRelayRacingHibernationQueuesInsteadOfWakingInline` (new): the relay's first read returns the pre-marker record, and hibernation is blocked between the marker write and the provider stop with the gate held. The relay must return a queued turn while the wake callback is still blocked. It fails on the previous relay (`relay waited on the wake instead of queueing`) and passes now (3/3 under `-race`).

## Before / after evidence

Same regression test on this branch. Before = `service.go` and `provisioning_queue.go` reverted to `main`; after = this PR.

| | Before | After (`-race`) |
|---|---|---|
| `ci-failure nudge` | FAIL after 60.8s | PASS |
| `merge-conflict urgent nudge` | FAIL after 60.2s | PASS |
| Nudge returns in | `1m0.005s` / `1m0.003s`, error `resume agent mer-1: context deadline exceeded` | 39ms / 54ms, no error |
| User message sent during the wake | `failed: could not wake the agent: resume agent mer-1: context deadline exceeded` | not failed |
| Worker | never resumed | woke in 123ms / 81ms and received the nudge first |

<details><summary>Before: diagnostic log (ci-failure subtest)</summary>

```
22:04:06.359 INFO "chat wake started" callers="chat.(*Service).workingController < chat.(*Service).relayChatTurn < chat.(*Service).RelaySessionChatTurn < … < session_manager.(*Manager).sendChat < session_manager.(*Manager).send < … < sessionguard.(*Guard).sendAdmittedChecked < sessionguard.(*Guard).sendAdmitted < sessionguard.(*Guard).sendThenChecked < sessionguard.(*Guard).send < sessionguard.(*Guard).Nudge"
22:04:07.363 INFO "chat wake joined an in-flight wake" wakeRunningFor=1.003s
22:05:06.361 WARN "agent operation gave up waiting for session input to drain" operation=resume waited=1m0.001s inputLeases=1 oldestLeaseHeldFor=1m0.002s error="context deadline exceeded"
22:05:06.363 WARN "chat wake failed" took=1m0.004s err="resume agent mer-1: context deadline exceeded"
22:05:06.364 WARN "joined chat wake failed" waited=59.001s err="resume agent mer-1: context deadline exceeded"
22:05:06.364 WARN "chat session could not wake; failing its queued messages" err="resume agent mer-1: context deadline exceeded"
--- FAIL: TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat (121.01s)
    --- FAIL: TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat/ci-failure_nudge (60.84s)
    --- FAIL: TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat/merge-conflict_urgent_nudge (60.17s)
```
</details>

<details><summary>After: log (-race)</summary>

```
=== RUN   TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat/ci-failure_nudge
INFO "chat wake started" callers="chat.(*Service).startBackgroundWake.func1 < runtime.goexit"
INFO "chat wake finished" took=123ms
nudge took=39ms err=<nil>; user turn state=queued error=""
=== RUN   TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat/merge-conflict_urgent_nudge
INFO "chat wake started" callers="chat.(*Service).startBackgroundWake.func1 < runtime.goexit"
INFO "chat wake finished" took=81ms
nudge took=54ms err=<nil>; user turn state=queued error=""
--- PASS: TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat (31.85s)
    --- PASS: TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat/ci-failure_nudge (28.35s)
    --- PASS: TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat/merge-conflict_urgent_nudge (3.50s)
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/session_manager	33.977s
```

(The first subtest's 28s under `-race` is mostly SQLite setup; without `-race` the whole test runs in ~4s per subtest.)
</details>

### Production occurrences (read from `ao.db`; packaged-app daemon logs go to `/dev/null`)

Both match the deadlock's timing: a failing user turn joined a wake that started 60s before the failure. The hibernation marker was never cleared, and no provider events were recorded after the session went to sleep.

| Session | Trigger | User turn queued → failed | Other evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| worker on #7152 | failing CI nudge (`test` failed 18:40:54Z) | 18:57:55.2Z → 18:58:28.8Z (33.6s) | chat-view 503 after 16.6s at 18:57:12.0Z (joined the previous doomed wake); `last_nudge_signature` empty; #7152 `observed_at` gaps 75.8s / 86.8s against a 30s tick |
| worker on #7147 | merge-conflict nudge (CI green, `CONFLICTING`, base `main`) | 14:36:40.3Z → 14:36:57.6Z (17.3s) | chat-view 503s at 14:35:40.1Z and 14:41:05.9Z; no `merge-conflict:` key in `last_nudge_signature`; #7147 `observed_at` gaps 92.6s / 76.9s / 76.0s |

The daemon itself was not stalled during the first incident: another session's 30s heartbeat events were stamped on time to the millisecond throughout.

## Tests run

- `go test ./internal/sessionguard/ ./internal/service/chat/ ./internal/lifecycle/`: pass. `go test -race ./internal/service/chat/ -run 'Hibernat|Wake|Relay'`: pass.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/`: pass except `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingAgentBinary`, `TestSpawn_MissingBinaryPreservesNonEmptyScratchWorkspaceForRetry`, `TestSpawn_ValidatesBinaryAfterEnvPrefix` and `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingBinaryAfterEnvPrefix`. These fail identically on the clean base on macOS (`tmux required on macOS … not found` under the tests' scrubbed `PATH`) and are unrelated.
- `go test -race -run TestLifecycleNudgeWakesHibernatedChat ./internal/session_manager/`: pass.
- `go vet` on the touched packages: clean.
- Not run locally: the full CI workflow suites (frontend, other backend packages, other OS runners). CI verifies those.

## Behavior change / risk

A relay to a sleeping session now returns once the message is durably queued. If the background wake then fails, the queued turn is marked failed in the chat timeline, as for a user's send. The relaying caller (lifecycle nudge, `ao send`, report delivery) no longer gets the wake error synchronously, so a lifecycle nudge is recorded as sent once it is queued. Messages queued while a session is stopped for a harness update are still kept for the post-update resume, and a failed version switch still keeps queued messages.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The packaged app sends daemon output to `/dev/null`, so the new diagnostics are only visible in dev and keep-daemon runs. Persisting daemon output to a rotated file under `~/.ao` would make them useful for field incidents.

title: bug(windows): Project Settings Scripts steps with double quotes fail because cmd.exe receives \" escaping
body:
**Environment:** AO CLI `ao version` prints `dev` (desktop build from the v0.13.x line), Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26300).

## Problem
In Project Settings > Scripts on Windows, a step that contains double quotes, e.g. `git -C "%AO_WORKTREE_PATH%" status`, fails with:

```
fatal: cannot change to '"C:\Users\<user>\.ao\data\worktrees\<project>\<session>"': Invalid argument
```

The command line handed to `cmd.exe` has its double quotes escaped as `\"` (Go / CommandLineToArgv-style escaping). `cmd.exe` does not understand `\"`, so the quotes reach `git` literally as part of the path.

## Minimal repro (no AO needed, shows the escaping effect)
```python
import subprocess
step = 'git -C "C:\Windows" status'
r = subprocess.run(['cmd', '/c', step], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(r.stderr)
# fatal: cannot change to '"C:\Windows"': Invalid argument
```
`subprocess.run` with a list applies the same `\"` escaping, matching what AO's script runner does.

## Expected
Script steps run the way they would when typed into `cmd.exe` (e.g. pass the raw string via `SysProcAttr.CmdLine` / `/s /c "..."` without re-escaping), so quoted paths work.

## Actual
Quoted arguments break. Workarounds: avoid double quotes (fails for paths with spaces), or `powershell -EncodedCommand <base64>`.

title: bug(codex,windows): codex.cmd shim re-parses AO's -c hooks.* flags (exit 255); doctor warns codex-launch-flags and sessions run without hooks
body:
**Environment:** AO CLI `ao version` prints `dev` (desktop build from the v0.13.x line), Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26300), Codex `codex-cli 0.163.0` installed via npm (`%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd`).

## Problem
When Codex is launched through the npm shim `codex.cmd`, `cmd.exe` re-parses AO's `-c hooks.*=...` arguments. The `\"`, `&` and `|` characters in the hook command values are interpreted by cmd, and codex exits with status 255. Result: `ao doctor` reports

```
WARN codex-launch-flags: codex rejected AO's launch flags (`codex features list -c check_for_update_on_startup=false ... -c hooks.SessionStart=[{hooks=[{type="command",command="& \"C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\agent-orchestrator\resources\daemon\ao.exe\" hooks codex session-start",timeout=5}]}] ...`: exit status 255) — codex sessions may spawn without activity hooks
```

and Codex sessions run without activity hooks (no activity/needs-input tracking).

With `codex.exe` first on PATH instead of the shim, both doctor checks (`codex` and `codex-launch-flags`) pass, so the flags themselves are valid; the shim layer is what breaks them.

## Expected
Hook flags reach codex unchanged regardless of how codex was installed.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the shim to the vendored binary (`...\node_modules\@openai\codex\...\codex.exe`) or launch `node <...>\codex.js` directly, bypassing `cmd.exe`. Related but distinct from #5323 / #3409, which are about being able to spawn `.cmd` at all; this one is about argument mangling when a `.cmd` is used.

title: [Bug](agent-agy): model backend errors (503 no capacity, 429 quota) in agy's own log are never surfaced; session just shows idle with no turns
body:
### Summary

The `agy` harness does not surface model backend failures. When Antigravity's model backend returns an error (for example `503 No capacity available` or `429 quota reached`), the AO session just shows `idle` with no turns and no report. The only trace is a line in agy's own CLI log, so a worker can stay silent for hours without anyone knowing it failed.

This is different from #4995 (quota error shown opaquely in the New Task UI) and #5050 (session stuck `active` after an interrupt): here the session is `idle`/`working` in AO, the turn silently ended with an error, and AO never reads it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Spawn an agy worker with a model that is currently at capacity or out of quota, for example `ao spawn --agent agy --model gpt-oss-120b-medium --prompt "..."`.
2. Let the worker run until the backend fails.
3. Run `ao session get <id> --json` and `ao session history <id>`.

### Actual behavior

AO shows `activity: idle` (or `working`) and no turn carries an error. The worker never sends `ao report`. `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-<date>_<time>.log` contains the failure:

```
E1025 23:13:48.481574  995 errorreport.go:224] agent executor error: generating and executing: UNAVAILABLE (code 503): No capacity available for model gpt-oss-120b-medium on the server
E1025 22:37:46.779532  741 errorreport.go:224] agent executor error: generating and executing: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429): Individual quota reached. Please upgrade your subscription to increase your limits. Resets in 117h48m41s.
```

Unrelated errors in the same log (for example `GetProject: failed to read standalone project file`, or `You are not logged into Antigravity` during startup) must not count, only lines containing `agent executor error:`.

### Expected behavior

AO reads the agy CLI log of each running agy session and, on an `agent executor error`, marks the session `errored` or `blocked` with the code and message (and the reset time for 429), so the orchestrator and the UI show it instead of a silent idle session. The log of a session can be found from the startup line `Creating CLI server backend: ... workspaceDirs=[<session worktree> ...]`, which names the session's worktree folder.

### AO version

`ao --version` prints `dev` (desktop build), Windows x64, agy language server 1.4.7

### Logs / extra context

The agy log line format is shown above; it contains no secrets.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates (closest: #4995, #5050)
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs

title: perf(chat): trim Claude chat start and park idle providers longer
body:
## What

Cuts about a second off a cold Claude chat start and stops idle chats from paying a full cold start on their next message.

- **Launch auth reuses a verified verdict** within the existing 5-minute cache instead of running `claude auth status` plus an HTTP probe on every start. The `claude auth status` report itself is cached too (keyed by binary, credential env and the workspace's `.claude/settings*.json`), so model discovery no longer runs the CLI a second time. A live provider rejection drops both caches, as before.
- **Idle hibernation waits 90 s** instead of 30 s before stopping a quiet provider. Version-refresh and update stops are unchanged.
- **Branch naming starts after the session's provider is up**, so its throwaway provider process no longer competes with the real one for CPU during boot. The branch is marked private from the start of provisioning, as before.
- A repeat fetch of the same base ref within 30 s is skipped; the fetch was already best effort.
- The packaged Node version check runs once per daemon; the chat-host descriptor poll is 5 ms instead of 20 ms.
- The task composer no longer blocks submit on the advisory readiness check; it refreshes the snapshot in the background. The project-aware launch path stays authoritative.

## Measured

Same machine, interleaved A/B against main, Claude Code / Sonnet, first assistant text after the create call:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Cold new chat (3 runs) | 5.84 / 3.95 / 3.72 s | 3.01 / 3.29 / 3.71 s |
| Follow-up after 100 s idle | 3.13 s (hibernated) | 1.39 s (still parked) |
| Launch prep inside controller start | 0.77–0.96 s | 0.06–0.19 s |

Immediate follow-ups are unchanged (1.1–2.0 s). The rest of the cold start is claude-agent-acp's `session/new` (claude boot plus its control round trips), which this PR does not touch.

## Risk

The one behavioural change worth a look is trusting the cached auth verdict at launch: a revoked credential now reaches the session's first request (which fails and invalidates the cache) instead of being refused before launch, for at most 5 minutes. Parked providers hold memory 3× longer (90 s instead of 30 s). Everything else is timing.

No tests or typecheck were run locally; relying on CI.

title: fix(frontend): teach cn() the app's custom text sizes
body:
Code changes: +12 -1\
Tests: +22 -8\
Others: +0 -0

## What

`cn()` in `frontend/src/renderer/lib/utils.ts` now knows the app's custom font sizes: `text-micro`, `text-2xs`, `text-caption`, `text-sm-md`, `text-md-sm`, `text-control`, `text-brand`, `text-subtitle`, `text-heading-sm`, `text-heading`, `text-heading-lg`. It is built on `extendTailwindMerge` with those names added to the `text` theme scale.

Visible effect: the ScriptRunPanel step labels now render at the caption size the component already asked for (previously `cn()` dropped it).

## Why

These sizes are defined in the `@theme` block of `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`, but tailwind-merge only knows Tailwind's default sizes. It read the custom ones as text colours. Two things went wrong as a result:

- `cn("text-xs", "text-caption")` kept both classes, so which size won depended on CSS order, not on the caller.
- A custom size and a colour in the same call were treated as two colours, so one of them could be dropped.

Any component that takes a `className` and has a default size was affected when a caller passed one of these sizes.

## How

The list matches the `--text-*` entries in `styles.css` on main. If a size is added there later, it needs to be added here too.

The `ScriptRunPanel` snapshots change as a direct result. The step command span calls `cn("min-w-0 flex-1 truncate font-mono text-caption", reached ? "text-foreground" : "text-muted-foreground")`. Before this change the rendered class had no `text-caption`, so the step name fell back to the inherited size. The updated snapshots now include `text-caption`.

## Testing

No local checks were run; CI runs the new test file `frontend/src/renderer/lib/utils.test.ts`.

To check by hand, in a Node REPL from `frontend/` or a scratch test:

- `cn("text-xs", "text-caption")` returned `"text-xs text-caption"` before, and returns `"text-caption"` now.

title: fix: scrub dynamic context from daemon Sentry error titles
body:
Code changes: +405 -95  
Tests: +328 -36  
Others: +20 -7  

## What

Fix IDP-10 at the live daemon Sentry capture boundary. Events use fixed safe failure or panic titles, allowlisted codes, and runtime-derived AO failure function frames and fingerprints for HTTP faults. `user.id` comes from the authoritative installation ID, and every captured event has bounded release and environment values. Area tags are added only for supported git, SQLite, agent, or network evidence. Canceled errors and marked upstream link-preview 502 responses do not create Sentry issues. File path errors do not receive a network title.

The current main branch also captures failed agent relaunches answered as 409 `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED`. This PR keeps that capture through the same safe boundary with fixed operation and code labels, grouped by operation and failure step with a bounded step tag and no HTTP route tag. Raw project and session names, IDs, repository names or paths, request data, panic values, and dynamic exception text stay out of outbound events. Existing consent and opt-out gates remain in place.

## Why

Dynamic error text could become a Sentry issue title or exception value, breaking the privacy promise in `docs/telemetry.md`. The direct agent relaunch capture added on main needed the same outbound scrubber after this branch rebased.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A daemon failure could place a project name, session name, repository path, or panic value in Sentry title-generating fields. | Fixed operation labels and allowlisted codes replace dynamic text. Safe AO function and line information remains. |
| Agent relaunch failures could bypass the HTTP logger's capture path. | The direct 409 relaunch capture uses the gated, scrubbed Sentry boundary with static operation and code labels. |
| Canceled requests and expected link-preview upstream 502 responses could create Sentry noise. | Those cases do not create Sentry issues. |
| A file path error could be titled as a network fault. | Only concrete network error types receive the network title. |
| A direct 5xx `WriteAPIError` response grouped at the request logger. | Its controller caller site is retained for Sentry grouping. |

## How

The final outbound event is scrubbed before transport. HTTP error capture records a runtime-derived AO function frame; registered route templates, bounded tags, installation identity, release, and environment survive final validation. Static routes are retained, while relaunch events have no route tag. Agent relaunch failures use an adapter to the same capture function. Direct 5xx API responses record their caller site without overwriting a previously captured error. In-memory transport tests marshal outbound events and check synthetic sensitive values do not survive. The telemetry documentation now covers 5xx, 409 relaunch, and panic capture.

## Testing

- Focused capture, request logger, link preview, telemetry metadata, and relaunch regressions passed.
- The complete non-race tests for all changed packages passed within `go test ./...`; full HTTP and envelope suites passed again after the direct 5xx fix.
- `go build ./...`, affected `go vet`, and golangci-lint v2.13.2 passed with zero lint issues.
- Race tests passed for Sentry, HTTP, controllers, and telemetry metadata, including the final direct 5xx regression. The session race suite failed only in unchanged `TestSearchWorkspaceContentCommonTermReachesLaterFiles` with `context deadline exceeded`.
- The full backend `go test ./...` did not pass. Failures were in untouched `commandcode`, `opencodev2`, `tmux`, `cli`, `systemcheck`, and `session_manager` packages under this machine's tool and session environment. The changed packages passed.
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check` passed. Remote CI was not polled.

No frontend files changed. The previous frontend typecheck attempt produced no result before it was stopped.

## Checklist

- [x] Kept this PR scoped to daemon Sentry privacy and capture correctness.
- [x] Preserved consent, opt-out, and installation identity behavior.
- [x] Added real outbound capture tests with synthetic sensitive values.
- [x] Updated telemetry documentation and verified the published change counts.
- [ ] SEN-7 database scan remains unclaimed. The tracker provides no stored value, full exception, or reproduction path. Supported migrated rows and current writer paths do not reproduce it. The speculative blank-string scanner and fixture were removed; a database fix needs the failing representation or read path.

Desktop, mobile, and Cloud Sentry transports remain outside this PR. No production events or account settings were touched.

title: feat(chat): highlight paths and session ids in agent-to-agent messages
body:
Code changes: +97 -16\
Tests: +53 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Messages agents send each other now highlight what they reference:

- Bare file paths render as inline code. This covers absolute paths, `~/`, `./` and `../` paths, and relative paths with two or more slashes or a file extension, such as `src/a.tsx:42`. They get the usual inline-code behavior: a path inside the workspace opens in Files, and a listed artifact path links to its preview.
- A word that matches the ID of a known session becomes an `ao://sessions/…` link, with the usual hover card.

This applies to two places:

- a message from another agent (its orchestrator or a sibling worker) in a worker chat (`FromAgent`)
- an expanded worker row in the orchestrator chat (`WorkerUpdateRow`)

## Why

Orchestrators and workers write plain prose through `ao send` and `ao report`, without backticks or links. A 150-character attachment path and the session IDs around it rendered as one undifferentiated wall of text, so it was hard to see what the message pointed at.

## How

- `remarkPlainReferences` in `lib/session-links.ts` works on markdown text nodes only, so code spans, fences and authored links (inline or by reference) are left alone. It reuses the text-node walker that `remarkSessionLinks` already had; that walker now takes a matcher.
- The stored text is not rewritten, so "copy as markdown" still copies exactly what the agent sent.
- A session ID becomes a link only when it matches a session in the chat's link source (local daemon, remote host or Cloud).
- These rules are deliberately left as prose:
  - one-slash words with no file extension, such as `and/or` or `CI/CD` (`src/App.test.tsx` and `config/.env.local` are paths)
  - single-segment `/word`, which usually means a slash command
  - `#123`, which could mean a PR or a session
- `ChatMarkdown` has a new optional `remarkPlugins` prop, appended after the built-in plugins (with or without math) and passed to every streamed markdown chunk. Other callers keep the module-level plugin list and are unchanged.
- `usePlainReferences` builds the plugin list once per workspace list and shares it across messages. It keeps the same list until a session is added or removed, so status and PR events do not re-parse messages. Only rendered agent prose (`AgentProse`) reads it, so chats without agent messages never touch the workspace query.
- The messages stay `safeOrigin`, so external links in them are still inert.

## Testing

- `vitest`: `session-links`, `ChatWorkspaceWorkerUpdates`, `ChatMarkdown` and `WorkerUpdates` pass, 140 tests in total. New tests cover path and session detection, punctuation and prose edge cases, and both rendered views.
- Real dev Electron app, built from this branch, running against a snapshot of a real AO database. The lab daemon ran inside a `sandbox-exec` profile that blocks writes to real state, outbound network and signals to real processes.

Worker chat: an orchestrator message, expanded. Before this change, the path and the session ID were plain prose.

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

DOMPurify 3.4.17

  • Fixed an issue with IN_PLACE, SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES and shadow roots, thanks @​manus-pi

  • Fixed the SMIL attributeName guard in XHTML mode, thanks @​Koukyosyumei
  • Hardened several smaller edge cases (namespaces, literal-text elements, isValidAttribute()), thanks @​artiphishell
  • Added a purify-edge test runner as a compatibility check, thanks @​anzal1
  • Clarified the IN_PLACE documentation in the README about possible risks
  • Updated several dependencies

DOMPurify 3.4.16

  • Fixed a problem with IN_PLACE node removal when working with hooks, thanks @​manus-pi
  • Fixed a problem with IN_PLACE sanitization and raw-text roots, thanks @​h-t-m

Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.2 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

Updates `undici` from 6.27.0 to 6.29.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v6.29.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 · GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

seroval-plugins@1.7.1

Patch Changes

  • 2d03651: serialize, toJSON, crossSerialize and toCrossJSON now throw when the value contains an async iterable or a ReadableStream, as they do for a promise. Before, they sent a stream that never got its values. Use an async or streaming function to send them.

seroval@1.7.1

Patch Changes

  • b703710: createCrossDeserializer no longer causes unhandled rejections. This covers a rejected promise that the caller never reads, and a pending promise that abort rejects. Code that awaits the promise still gets the rejection.
  • 2d03651: serialize, toJSON, crossSerialize and toCrossJSON now throw when the value contains an async iterable or a ReadableStream, as they do for a promise. Before, they sent a stream that never got its values. Use an async or streaming function to send them.
  • 2c25bf3: serialize, toJSON, crossSerialize and toCrossJSON now send a createStream stream that has ended with all its events. A stream that is still open, or a live stream, now throws. Before, they sent an empty stream that never ended.

seroval-plugins@1.7.0

Minor Changes

  • 4c0008f: Add createLiveStream(), a single-consumer stream that holds one event at a time and resolves each producer write only after the serialized record is accepted. crossSerializeStream and toCrossJSONStream callbacks may now return a promise; the next record, and the acceptance of the source event behind it, wait for it to settle. Records discovered while parsing an event are emitted after the record that introduces them, one callback runs at a time, onDone waits for the last callback and is not called after an output failure, and cleanup runs every callback once. Async iterables and ReadableStream values read their next chunk only after the previous record is accepted. Existing streaming plugin lifecycle hooks remain available; parsing a live stream is the preferred way to connect an incremental source.
  • f2b7d0c: Raise the supported Node.js floor from >=10 to >=20 in engines, remove the no-op typesVersions from seroval, give seroval-plugins main, module and types fields plus a typesVersions entry that points at the emitted web declarations, and link the plugins package to the workspace copy of seroval.
  • 5ab601f: Add plugin context hooks for parsing an async iterable as a stream source. Use them in the ReadableStream plugin to avoid a separate live-stream producer while keeping backpressure, cancellation, and wire format intact. v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

title: perf(chat): reuse completed markdown blocks while streaming
body:
Code changes: +213 -57  
Tests: +229 -0  
Others: +12 -0

## What

Keep completed markdown blocks stable as a reply streams, and progressively highlight completed code lines. Preserve code source and nested syntax-token scopes.

## Why

Each streamed update currently reparses the whole reply. Long replies repeatedly process prose that has already finished arriving.

## How

- Reuse the existing GFM parser to split each message, retaining two unstable blocks and freezing only at a blank-line boundary. Reference definitions and footnotes retain a single document so links resolve and footnote IDs stay unique.
- Repair incomplete prose with `remend`; bypass code, including code nested in lists and quotes. History that mounts settled keeps the original single-parser path.
- Coalesce worker requests into completed-prefix snapshots, without adding partial snapshots to the settled-code cache. Lowlight does not expose a supported continuation API, so tokenization still receives the complete prefix; line rendering is memoized and preserves nested CSS scopes. Live snapshots above 100,000 characters retain readable plain text beyond the last highlighted prefix.
- Keep the existing renderer, lowlight, class-based themes, CSP, Mermaid, links, and image components.

## Testing

Earlier focused tests passed (111 tests) before the final review fixes. The full frontend suite and typechecks were stopped at the author's request; the suite had reported a remote-proxy GOAWAY test failure, which was not investigated. Tests, typechecks, and builds have **not** been rerun on the final patch, as requested.

Added regression cases for incremental GFM boundaries, references/footnotes, fade offsets, literal fenced/indented/nested code, token-scope nesting, worker coalescing, stale results, and transient-cache behavior.

A production browser benchmark before the final review fixes streamed a reply from 100 to 125 paragraphs (93 updates, 18,390 source characters), with five alternating runs per version:

| Render work per update | Previous renderer | Block renderer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 6.3 ms | 0.9 ms |
| 95th percentile | 13.6 ms | 2.0 ms |

All measured runs preserved the expected prose and reported no browser errors. This was a synthetic prose workload on a busy local machine, not a measurement of code-heavy replies or the final patch.

The real Electron app was launched from this branch against isolated scratch data and subsequently closed. No additional manual retest is requested.

title: feature: project default (and ao spawn flag) for "Archive on merge"; every new session starts with it off
body:
## Summary
"Archive on merge" (Session controls) is a per-session toggle stored as `sessions.terminate_on_pr_merge`, and every new session starts with it off. There is no project-level default and no `ao spawn` flag for it, so an owner who wants merged workers archived must switch it on in every session by hand.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- AO: `ao version` prints `ao version dev`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Switch "Archive on merge" on in one worker session.
2. Spawn another worker with `ao spawn`.
3. Open its Session controls, or read `sessions.terminate_on_pr_merge` in `ao.db`.

## Actual
- The new session has the toggle off (`terminate_on_pr_merge = 0`). In our project, 8 of 8 recent sessions were 0.
- `ao spawn --help` has no option for it.
- `ao project set-config` has no key for it.

## Expected
One or both of these:
- a project setting "Archive on merge by default" that new sessions inherit;
- an `ao spawn --archive-on-merge` flag.
"Automatically fix CI failures" and "Automatically fix review comments" (`auto_inject_ci`, `auto_inject_review`) would benefit from the same project default.

## Workaround
Our merge script calls `ao session kill <worker>` after a merge when the worktree is clean.

At minimum, it warns before dropping fields it does not manage.

title: feat(chat): draw AO's automation messages as what they are
body:
Code changes: +520 -88\
Tests: +202 -11\
Others: +126 -0

Follows #7096 and #7154.

## What

Every message AO sends an agent for the user, or relays from GitHub, drew as the same bordered "automation" card: an info icon, the full agent-facing text dimmed and clamped to three lines, and **Show full report**. Each kind is now drawn for what it is.

**What you did through AO** is drawn as your own message:

| Kind | Written by | Now shows |
|---|---|---|
| File inline feedback (one or a batch) | `packages/shared/files/file-annotations.ts` | your words under a file chip (`guard.go:131`, opens the file at the line), plus the commented code when there is one. Workspace version, fingerprint and agent instructions are hidden. |
| Instruction on lines picked in a diff | `shared/diff-selection.ts` | file and line range, then the instruction |
| Git buttons | `SessionBranchSummary.tsx` | `Create PR › main`, `Create draft PR`, `Commit`, `Commit & push`, `Push` |
| Browser annotations | `shared/browser-annotations.ts` | page, each comment with its target, screenshot count (replaces their own card) |

**What GitHub reported on the session's PR** is a row in the PR glyph, tinted by meaning, with the PR linked and its title beside it:

| Kind | Written by | Now shows |
|---|---|---|
| CI failing | `lifecycle/reactions.go` | each failed check, linked to its run, with its log tail one click away |
| Unresolved review comment | `lifecycle/reactions.go` | `@author commented on #N`, the file and line, the comment (folded after 5 lines) |
| Changes-requested review | `lifecycle/reactions.go` | `@author requested changes on #N`, the review (folded) |
| Merge conflicts | `lifecycle/reactions.go` | `Merge conflicts on #N` |
| Old AO reviewer findings | no longer sent | a changes-requested row from "AO reviewer" |

**AO's notices** are one quiet line:
- the orchestrator being replaced;
- an agent switch carrying context over (only in old history);
- a reviewer receiving its review task.

**Another agent's message in a worker chat** now names any sender session, not only the orchestrator (#7154). A sibling worker shows as its task name.

## Why

These messages carry what the agent needs, but the user reading the chat needs something different: what they asked for, or what GitHub said. The single card showed the agent's version every time:
- 40-line CI log tails;
- thread IDs;
- workspace fingerprints;
- "Apply this feedback in the current workspace".

All of it labelled a "report", even when it was the user's own comment.

## How

- `AutomationMessage.tsx` reads each kind back from the fixed text AO writes for it.
  - Renderer-side templates are tested through their real formatters, so changing one fails the reader it breaks. The daemon's are tested with samples of `lifecycle/reactions.go` output.
  - Text that matches no kind keeps the card, and so does a PR nudge without a PR number.
- `TimelineItem` now draws `FromAgent` → `AutomationMessage` → `OriginMessage` (the card is the fallback).
- Shared pieces:
  - The five-line fold from #7154 is now a shared `Folded`.
  - `FileReference` (in `ChatMarkdown`) opens a workspace file at a line, the way inline code paths already do.
- Review comment and review bodies render with `safeOrigin`, as they do today, because their text comes from whoever commented on the PR.
- Strings are in all 8 locales, including plural forms.

## Testing

- `AutomationMessage.test.tsx` covers:
  - reading every kind;
  - drawing file feedback, failing CI (including opening a log), and a review comment;
  - the fallback to the card.
- `ChatWorkspaceWorkerUpdates.test.tsx` covers:
  - a sibling worker named by its task;
  - an unknown sender keeping its card.
- Browser annotation tests are updated for the new look.
- Checked in the desktop app on a copy of real AO data:
  - file feedback;
  - failing CI, with its log;
  - a review comment;
  - a changes-requested review;
  - an old AO reviewer finding;
  - the "Create PR" button;

title: perf(chat): stream code tokens incrementally with shiki
body:
Code changes: +286 -133  
Tests: +198 -58  
Others: +201 -51

## What

Continue the streaming-renderer work in #7226 by replacing repeated full-prefix code tokenization with incremental Shiki highlighting. Each live fence retains its grammar state in a worker, sends only appended complete lines, and receives only newly highlighted lines.

## Why

Block memoization avoids reprocessing completed prose, but lowlight still tokenizes an increasingly large completed code prefix for each live snapshot. Shiki's streaming tokenizer can reuse the state of the preceding line, including inside multiline comments and strings.

## How

- Use Shiki 4.5.0 and `@shikijs/stream` with the JavaScript regex engine and fine-grained bundled grammars. No WASM, runtime grammar fetches, raw highlighted HTML, or CSP changes.
- Keep settled-tree caching and AO's syntax-class/color contract shared by chat, Markdown previews, and word diffs. JSON/CSS property names retain the red palette. JSX, TSX, HTML, and JSONC use their dedicated grammars. Remove lowlight.
- Coalesce work per fence. Reset on edits or language changes, ignore results after disposal, prevent replay after cleanup, and replay once after worker-state eviction. Worker state is capped at 16 streams, 100,000 source characters per stream, and 1,000,000 retained source characters overall.
- Keep completed React line tokens and their signatures unchanged as new lines arrive. The unfinished line remains readable plain text until completed; larger unsupported live snapshots preserve the highlighted prefix and plain remainder.

## Related

Related: #7226 (merged). This PR now targets `main` and contains only the Shiki migration.

## Testing

Source/API review performed. Manually tested in the real Electron app (author-reported), using isolated scratch data. Automated tests, typechecks, and benchmarks were not run locally at the author's request; final review fixes passed GitHub CI. No measured Shiki speedup is claimed.

GitHub CI passed on `b7cef5dd91`: frontend tests (including the new regressions), renderer smoke tests, macOS helper, and secret scanning. The disposal/replay race and JSON/CSS property-color findings from static review are fixed in that commit.

Added or updated regression coverage for grammar continuation, multiline strings/comments, exact Unicode and line endings, independent fence state, append-only worker messages, replay after eviction, edits/language changes, disposal, worker failures/timeouts, alias mapping, and reusable completed-line tokens. These cases have not been run locally.

title: feature(review): forward all comments of a review run in one message (+ verdict event); per-comment delivery causes fix-push-retrigger loops
body:
## Summary
When an AO review run finishes with N inline comments, AO forwards them to the worker one message at a time ("The following 1 unresolved review comment ..."). Agents read "1 unresolved" as the whole review, so they fix, commit, push and re-trigger a review per comment. Each push supersedes the review that just started, and the cycle repeats N times.

## Data (one project, 2026-10-25, about 9 h)
- 177 forwarded review messages. Every one had N=1; none were batched.
- 162 of 177 (92%) were followed by `git push` within 10 minutes (median 28 s).
- Example: the reviewer posted 6 inline comments within 1 s (17:12:38-39Z). AO forwarded them as 6 messages over 4 minutes (17:12:58 ... 17:16:54). The worker made 6 commits and 6 triggers, and 5 runs were "superseded by a review trigger for a newer commit".
- In total 71 of 173 review runs (41%) failed as superseded or were cancelled. That is about 17% of review spend.
- Written rules in AGENTS.md ("fix all comments in one push") did not reduce it (36% -> 44%).

## Expected
Forward all unresolved comments of a completed review run in ONE message, after the run reaches `complete`: "The following N unresolved review comments from review run <id> ...". The message format already has a count. Optionally, include the verdict in the same message.

## Related
Agents also have no event when a run ends approved, failed or cancelled; the `ao review` docs say "nothing else reports it". So they write sleep-poll loops on `ao review ls`. A verdict message to the worker would remove those loops.

title: fix(composer): allow dragging and dropping text into prompt input
body:
Code changes: +154 -7\
Tests: +95 -0\
Others: 0

## What

Allow dragging and dropping plain text into the main prompt input field (chat composer) and task prompt textarea.

## Why

Previously, dragging and dropping text into the main prompt composer did not work:
1. `ChatComposer` treated all dragover events as file attachment attempts (`setDragging(true)` and `preventDefault()`), suppressing the native editable drop behavior for text drags while showing an attachment drop border.
2. `ComposerEditor` did not handle `DROP_COMMAND` for external text drops, causing dropped text to be ignored.
3. In `TaskComposerView`, `handleDrop` unconditionally called `preventDefault()` even when no files were present, and `TaskPrompt` did not handle dropped text into its controlled textarea.

## How

- In `ComposerEditor`:
  - Registered `DRAGOVER_COMMAND` and `DROP_COMMAND` to handle plain text drags and drops.
  - Resolved drop caret position at event coordinates (`caretRangeFromPoint` / `caretPositionFromPoint`) and inserted raw text (`selection.insertRawText(text)`).
  - Exposed `insertText` in `ComposerEditorHandle` to allow programmatic insertion.
- In `ChatComposer`:
  - Differentiated between file drags and text drags in `onDragOver` so text drags are not treated as attachment drops and do not toggle `data-dragging`.
  - Added fallback text drop handler (`onFormDrop`) on the composer form surface to insert dropped text even if dropped on the padding around the editor.
- In `TaskComposerView`:
  - Handled text drops on `TaskPrompt` textarea to insert text at cursor/selection and update state.
  - Avoided preventing default in `handleDrop` when no files are present, allowing text drops to proceed.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `ChatComposer.test.tsx` and `TaskComposerView.test.tsx`.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.test.tsx` (167 passed)

title: fix(mobile): keep attachments picked on Android and type images by their bytes
body: Code changes: +182 -80 Tests: +165 -11 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary On Android, attaching a photo or a file in a mobile chat silently did nothing: you pick it, return to the chat, and no attachment chip appears and no error shows. iOS was unaffected. This PR fixes that, and also fixes image types: both pickers send JPEG data under the original file's type, so iOS camera photos (HEIC) were rejected in chat, and PNG screenshots went out as JPEG data labelled `image/png`. ## Root cause - **Lost attachments (Android only).** The system photo picker and file picker are separate activities, so opening one backgrounds the app. React Native's Android AppState has no `inactive`, so it reports `background`, and the store tears the connection down (`lib/store.tsx`: `setConfig(null)`, `setConfigResolved(false)`). `sessionRouteView` checks `configured === null` before `listed`, so the session screen swaps the chat for a spinner and unmounts `ChatSessionScreen`. The pick then resolves into the composer that was unmounted, and the rebuilt composer starts with no attachments. iOS pickers run in-process and only report `inactive`, which `shouldPoll` treats as active. This has been the case since #5921. - **Wrong image types (both platforms).** With `quality < 1`, expo-image-picker re-encodes base64 as JPEG on Android and always exports JPEG base64 on iOS, but `mimeType` describes the source file. The composer trusted the label. As a result, iOS HEIC camera photos hit "Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, and BMP images are supported", and PNG screenshots were sent as JPEG data labelled `image/png`. The daemon forwards that label unchanged to the agent and names the staged file from it. ## Changes - `lib/chat/composerAttachments.ts` (new): unsent attachments, and the last picker error, live in a store keyed like the text draft (machine + session). Pickers capture the key when they open and read the stored list when they resolve, so a pick that outlives the composer still lands, and a second pick can't overwrite the first. - `ChatComposer` and `ReviewerComposer` use the store and type each image by its bytes, falling back to the picker's label. The reviewer is keyed `reviewer..`. Its resource attachments now carry `bytes` so the two composers share one attachment type. - `sniffImageMimeType` moves unchanged from `spawn-attachments.ts` to `lib/imageMime.ts`, so the spawn sheet and both composers share it. ## Verification All runs used latest-main JS against an isolated scratch daemon with a Claude Code chat session. Test images contained distinctive text so the agent's replies prove it received each image. Android runs used a side-by-side Release build (separate app id, OTA off) on a **Pixel 10a (Android 17)**. iOS runs used a Debug build from this branch on an **iPhone 17 Pro simulator**. | Entry point | Android (Pixel 10a) | iOS (simulator) | |---|---|---| | Chat: photo | ✅ PNG and JPEG survive the picker; agent read "PNG BANANA 42" / "JPEG MANGO 17" | ✅ PNG and HEIC attached; agent read both | | Chat: file | ✅ text file survives the picker; agent read its contents | not run (no files on the simulator); same code as Android plus unit tests | | Chat: edge cases | ✅ cancel adds nothing; oversized-file error still shows after the remount; a new pick clears it; an attachment stays when you leave and come back; ✕ removes it | n/a | | Spawn sheet: photo | ✅ PNG and JPEG reached the agent | ✅ HEIC and PNG reached the agent | | Reviewer chat | unit test only (no device run) | unit test only | The daemon staged every image with an extension that matches its bytes (e.g. the Android PNG pick is now a real `.jpg`). **Android: before (shipped 2.1.0) → after** Before: picked a photo and no chip appears. After: the chip is kept, the agent reads the image, and an oversized-file error survives the remount. **iOS: main rejects a HEIC camera photo → fixed** I also screen-recorded the original Android bug on the Pixel. On returning from the picker, the chat shows a full-screen spinner for about a second and then re-renders empty. ## Tests - `npm run typecheck` clean; `npx vitest run`: 2507/2507 pass (`packages/mobile`). - New regression tests, each confirmed to **fail on main** and pass with this change: - chat: a pick that resolves after the composer unmounts is still attached on remount and sent as `image/jpeg`; - chat: an iPhone pick labelled `image/heic` with JPEG bytes is accepted; - reviewer: the same remount + type check. - both composers: a send that finishes after the conversation was left and reopened removes only what it submitted, keeping a photo the reopened composer attached meanwhile (from review). - Store unit tests; the sniffer test moved to `imageMime.test.ts`. ## Behaviour changes and risks - Unsent attachments now stay in memory when you leave a chat and come back, matching draft text. They're cleared on send and don't survive the app being killed. They aren't evicted otherwise; each session's images are capped at 25 MB. - A picker error now stays visible until the next pick or send, including after leaving and returning. - Image types come from the bytes. Both pickers always export JPEG base64 for `mediaTypes: ["images"]`, so this only corrects labels and can't newly reject an image. - The reviewer screen may not actually unmount on Android: `currentHostId` survives backgrounding. The store change there is defensive. The type fix applies either way. The reviewer path was not run on a device. - The underlying store teardown on background is unchanged. Anything else that awaits an external activity from inside the chat screen has the same exposure.

title: fix: consolidate session failures into one recovery banner
body:
Code changes: +114 -87  
Tests: +74 -11  
Others: +200 -8  

## What

When a Chat agent stops or a resume fails, show one clear recovery banner with technical diagnostics collapsed behind **Details**. Keep the raw diagnostics selectable and copyable, and show **Reconnect** after a failed resume.

## Why

Controller and resume failures could repeat raw driver JSON across the banner and latest failed turn, making the recovery action hard to find.

## How

- Combine and deduplicate controller, resume, and shell diagnostics in the banner.
- Hide an exact matching error on the latest turn only while the banner owns it. Preserve distinct errors, usage-limit recovery, and historical failures; restore the turn's failure row after the controller recovers.
- Explain the stopped composer's state and point to the banner's recovery action.
- Keep existing resume/shell callbacks and startup/handoff suppression. No daemon or API changes, and no other UI-audit changes included.

## Testing

- Added coverage for collapsed/copyable diagnostics, failed-resume recovery, matching latest-turn failures, and distinct turn errors. Updated existing banner assertions.
- Local test suites and typechecks were not run at the user's explicit request; manual review is pending.

title: fix(cli): fail stop when daemon process lingers
body:
Code changes: +6 -12  
Tests: +10 -10  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary
- make `ao stop` fail when the verified daemon PID remains alive past the requested timeout, even after `running.json` is removed
- retain the existing successful path when the PID actually exits and add a regression test for the false-success/orphan path

## Root cause
`waitForStopped` treated removal of `running.json` as a successful stop once the timeout elapsed. The run file disappears while shutdown is still in progress, so a daemon that never exits could be reported as stopped. If its desktop parent subsequently exits, that live process is an orphan even though its loopback listener is gone.

## Verification
- Red regression: before this change, `TestWaitForStoppedFailsWhenRunFileGoneButProcessLingers` failed because `waitForStopped` returned success while `ProcessAlive` stayed true.
- `go test -race -mod=readonly -count=1 ./internal/cli` — pass
- `go vet ./internal/cli` — pass
- `go test -mod=readonly -tags e2e -count=1 -run '^TestE2E_Lifecycle$' ./internal/cli` — pass
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -mod=readonly -o /tmp/ao-windows-amd64.exe ./cmd/ao` — pass

## Applicability
The false-success behavior was introduced by 77f33c28646d81f76c5f55362fae94316d1d7304 (`fix(cli): treat run-file removal as stopped in ao stop`, 2026-06-27). It is present in released v0.10.0 and later release tags, including v0.14.7. This change does not force-kill a daemon or alter data/lock cleanup; it reports the lingering verified PID as a failed stop so recovery can be handled explicitly.

title: fix(sessions): accept the suffixed branch when replacing an orchestrator
body:
## Problem

Replacing an orchestrator from project settings returns "Internal server error" while the new orchestrator is actually running. PostHog: `POST /api/v1/orchestrators` → 500, 371 times for 92 users in the last 7 days (Error Tracking issues `01a13033…` and `01a16c43…`, plus the per-release copies).

The cause:
1. Another worktree has `ao/<prefix>-orchestrator` checked out.
2. The spawn intentionally falls back to `ao/<prefix>-orchestrator-N` (`session_manager/manager.go`, added in #6383).
3. `verifyOrchestratorReplacement` still requires the exact branch, so it returns a plain error, which becomes an untyped 500.
4. The settings form re-runs the replacement on every later save once one has failed, so the same failure keeps repeating.

This only happens for TUI-mode orchestrators. Chat mode creates the worktree after the request returns.

Reproduced on a local daemon: a TUI orchestrator, with its branch checked out in another worktree, then `POST /api/v1/orchestrators {"clean":true}`:

```
status=500 error="orchestrator replacement verification failed: new session …-4 uses branch \"ao/longnameproj-orchestrator-3\", want \"ao/longnameproj-orchestrator\""
```

## Change

- `verifyOrchestratorReplacement` accepts `<branch>-N` as well as the exact branch.
- Its remaining failures (session terminated, wrong kind, wrong agent, unrelated branch) return `ORCHESTRATOR_REPLACEMENT_UNVERIFIED` instead of an untyped `INTERNAL_ERROR`, so telemetry can tell them apart.

Nothing else depends on the exact orchestrator branch name.

## Testing

Focused unit test `TestVerifyOrchestratorReplacementBranch`: accepted branches (canonical, `-2`, `-13`, empty) and rejected ones (`-`, `-x`, no dash, another prefix, `main`).

```
cd backend && go test ./internal/service/session/ -run '^TestVerifyOrchestratorReplacementBranch$' -count=1
```

I didn't run any other tests or checks locally; CI covers the rest.

To check by hand: open a project with a TUI orchestrator. In a terminal, run `git worktree add ../elsewhere ao/<prefix>-orchestrator` inside the project repo, then change the orchestrator agent in project settings and save. Before this change the save shows "Internal server error". After it, the save succeeds and the new orchestrator opens.

## Why

`Frontend / test` is the slowest PR check: about 13 min median and 21 min p90, measured over 59 PR runs on 25–26 Oct. It runs the vitest suite (about 9 min) and `tsc` (about 5.6 min) one after the other in a single job, so the Frontend workflow takes about 16 min median and 23 min p90.

- `vitest`: a new 4-shard matrix job (`npx vitest run --shard=N/4`). It installs frontend and product-ui deps plus the agent-browser runtime, the same as the old job.
- `typecheck`: a new job for `npm run typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e`. It sets `ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1` because `tsc` needs Electron's types but not its binary, so this job never hits the flaky Electron download.

Not included: rebalancing the Go race shards. That would mean 13 more jobs per push for about 2 min less time, and it would split `session_manager` and `sqlite/store` for the first time.

title: fix(scm): never latch a merge conflict the provider no longer reports
body:
Code changes: +45 -2
Tests: +173 -2
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

A session could stay flagged **Conflict** even though its PR had no conflict — in the reported case the PR was already merged and the red Conflict badge hung indefinitely. The verdict was latched on the first DIRTY/CONFLICTING observation and nothing retracted it:

1. **Force-push transitional window** — GitHub recomputes mergeability asynchronously after a push and serves the value cached for the *previous* head in the meantime. A CONFLICTING verdict observed in that window was persisted, and for an already-exited session nothing ever re-observed the PR to clear it.
2. **Merged PRs** — a merged PR has no mergeability, but every derivation happily mapped GitHub's stale cached `mergeable`/`mergeStateStatus` to `conflicting`.
3. **Frozen rows** — sessions whose agent exited are dropped from observation, so a conflicting row frozen before the merge was displayed forever.

## Changes

- `mergeabilityObservation` (github batch path), `mergeabilityFromGraphQL` (github REST/legacy path) and `mergeabilityFromMR` (gitlab): a merged PR answers `unknown` — the DIRTY/CONFLICTING branch is unreachable, so a merged PR can never be persisted as conflicting.
- SCM observer (`prepareForPersistence`): a CONFLICTING verdict observed against a head the local row has never seen is demoted to `unknown` for that tick; the next observation of the same head is a settled provider answer and persists as-is. A real conflict surfaces one poll (~30 s) late instead of a phantom one latching until the row freezes. Nudge dedup is unaffected: the demoted `unknown` deliberately does not re-arm (`mergeabilityClearsConflict` already excludes it).
- `mergeabilityObservationFromLocal` (review-only local recompute) and read-side `summarizeMergeability`: terminal (merged/closed) PRs answer `unknown` with no reasons, so already-frozen rows stop reporting a conflict that cannot exist.

## Tests

- github: `mergeabilityObservation` table gains merged cases (stale CONFLICTING/DIRTY cache → unknown; clean signals → unknown); batch observation and `mergeabilityFromGraphQL` pinned for merged PRs.
- gitlab: `mergeabilityFromMR` merged case pinned.
- observe/scm: `TestPoll_FreshHeadConflictingDemotedUntilConfirmed` — poll 1 demotes fresh-head conflicting to unknown, poll 2 (same head) confirms conflicting; `mergeabilityObservationFromLocal` merged case.
- service/session: `TestSummarizeMergeabilityTerminalPRsAreUnknown` — merged/closed rows answer unknown with no reasons, open conflicting rows unchanged.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/github ./internal/adapters/scm/gitlab ./internal/observe/scm ./internal/service/session` — pass, including `-race`.
- Full `go test ./...` on this machine shows pre-existing environment-shaped failures in packages this PR does not touch (`agent/commandcode` git include-headers, `agent/crush` provider catalog, `agent/fake` hook log, `opencode` credential scope) — all reproduce without this change and are ambient-env dependent (git global config / ambient credentials / machine locale).
- `golangci-lint@latest` (pinned v2.13.2 cannot read Go 1.27 stdlib export data locally) — 0 issues on all touched packages.

## Notes

- No API contract change: `PullRequestMergeabilitySummary` shape is unchanged, only the values for terminal PRs, so no spec/types regeneration is needed.
- Task source is the session assignment (issue #149 in the tracker is an unrelated closed Codex issue; no tracker issue is linked deliberately).

title: feat(markdown): render LaTeX math in chat and Markdown previews
body:
## Summary

Agent replies and Markdown previews show formulas as raw TeX, and Markdown mangles them: `_` turns into emphasis and `\(` loses its backslash. This PR typesets math with KaTeX in chat replies and in the Markdown file preview.

- ```` ```math ```` fences always typeset, the same way ```` ```mermaid ```` fences render as diagrams.
- `$…$`, `$$…$$`, `\(…\)` and `\[…\]` typeset behind a new opt-in setting, **Settings → Appearance → Render math**. It is off by default, translated into all 8 locales, and listed in settings search.
- KaTeX loads lazily on the first formula. It runs with `trust: false`, so `\href` and `\htmlClass` emit nothing active. TeX it cannot parse (an unsupported command, or a formula still streaming) stays as source.
- Copying a selection that includes a formula copies its TeX, not the glyphs twice. The plain text is the browser's own `innerText` of the selection with each formula swapped for its source, so paragraph, list and table breaks survive, including across a streamed reply's chunks.
- The streaming chunker now cuts blocks in the renderer's math dialect. A display formula with a `- 2ab` line or a blank line therefore stays in one chunk, and formulas skip the prose repair pass, which would otherwise rewrite TeX such as `$a~b$` into `$a\~b$`. Turning the setting on or off re-cuts a streaming reply, so a paused stream decides its repair again.
- KaTeX 0.16.47 is the copy `mermaid` already ships. The new packages are `micromark-extension-llm-math` (the standard math tokenizer plus `\(…\)` / `\[…\]`) and `mdast-util-math`.

### Why opt-in

A lone `$` is also currency and shell syntax. With the setting on, `The Pro plan costs $20 and Max costs $100` renders `20 and Max costs ` as a formula (see the second screenshot). The setting's description says so.

## Screenshots

Render math **off**. Only the ```` ```math ```` fence typesets; the rest is how replies look today:

![Render math off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/2e6a280f77a3fd5c067150444c1d928ebfc8c957/math-off.png)

Render math **on**, chat reply (left) and Markdown file preview (right):

![Render math on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/2e6a280f77a3fd5c067150444c1d928ebfc8c957/math-on.png)

## Tests

- `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx`, 5 new tests:
  - setting off leaves `$` as text
  - all four delimiters typeset
  - ```` ```math ```` typesets without the setting
  - unparseable TeX stays as source
  - turning math on mid-stream keeps `$a~b$` from reaching KaTeX as `$a\~b$` (fails without the fix)
- `e2e/chat-math-copy.spec.ts` (`@T0`, runs in `renderer-smoke`) copies a settled and a streamed reply in real Chromium and checks the TeX and the block breaks. Copy is tested here because jsdom has no `innerText`. It fails on KaTeX's `copy-tex`, which this PR replaced.
- `streaming-markdown.test.ts`: the every-character "chunks parse the same as the whole message" property now also runs in the math dialect. The 2 display-formula cases and the repair test fail on the old splitter.
- The affected suites and both typechecks (`typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`) pass locally, and CI is green.

## Known limits

- `$$ x $$` written on one line renders inline, not as a display block.
- A `|` inside a formula in a table cell splits the cell, because GFM splits cells before inline parsing.
- With the setting on, `\[WIP\]` renders as a formula.
- There is no math preview in the composer. The mobile app is unchanged because it has no Markdown renderer.
