title: fix(sessions): report agent relaunch failures as 409 AGENT_RESUME_FAILED and keep them in telemetry
body:
Code changes: +126 -26  
Tests: +82 -0  
Others: +4 -2

## Problem

Opening a session whose agent has exited auto-calls `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/resume-agent`. When the relaunch fails at any step (runtime create/restart, agent hooks, system prompt, launch preparation, chat start, …) the manager returns a plain `fmt.Errorf`. `mapSessionError` falls through to `default`, and the envelope answers **500 INTERNAL_ERROR**. This is the top user-facing error in PostHog (~200 users/week, ~1,220 hits). Telemetry only records `error_kind=internal`, so it cannot tell which step fails.

## Change

- `session_manager`: a `RelaunchError{Step, Err}` wraps every untyped failure in `relaunchSessionWithPolicyAndGeneration` and `resumeChatController`: agent adapter, system prompt (+file), browser capability, model configuration, agent hooks, launch command, after-start prompt, agent binary, supervisor, runtime preparation, prepare launch, controller admission, runtime, agent start check, record launch, native initialization, deliver prompt, workspace roots, provider ownership, chat start. Returns that already carry a typed sentinel (incomplete handle, auth required, not resumable, chat unsupported, recovery inconclusive) keep their own 4xx codes, and the store read after a successful launch is not a relaunch step. It keeps `Error()` text and `Unwrap`, so existing `errors.Is` sentinel mappings still win. `resumeAgentWithMode` (every return path, including the failed-chat-spawn retry) and `RestoreWithMode` log `<operation>: relaunch failed` with session id, step and raw error. The access log only records errors for 5xx, so without this the 409's cause would be missing from the daemon log.
- `service/session`: `mapSessionError` maps it to **409 `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED`**. The message names only the step (`details.step`), so no raw error or env text reaches the client. The new case comes after every specific sentinel. `context.DeadlineExceeded` stays unmapped and keeps its 503.
- **Telemetry is kept.** These failures leave `ao.http.5xx`, so `ResumeAgent` and `Restore` emit `ao.session.relaunch_failed` with `operation`, `step`, `cause_type` (Go type of the root error only, never its text), `harness`, `kind`, `error_code` and `fingerprint`. It fires only when the response is actually `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED`, so 503s are not double-counted and typed 4xx errors are not mislabeled. A relaunch canceled because the client left is not counted. The event is allowlisted in the PostHog sink and listed in `docs/posthog-cost-controls.md`.
- **Sentry is kept.** The request logger only sends 5xx to Sentry, and the 409 envelope no longer carries the raw cause. So the service sends the raw relaunch error to Sentry itself (`sentryobs.CaptureHTTPError`, which scrubs events), with the same fingerprint as the PostHog event. It respects the existing "Share error events" consent; `docs/telemetry.md` now lists it. In the renderer, `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED` gets a P1/ours code override in `classifyError`; otherwise the 409 would drop from a reported issue to a P3 breadcrumb.

Before (real manager + SQLite store + service + envelope, runtime create failing):
```
HTTP 500 {"error":"internal","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal server error"}
```
After:
```
HTTP 409 {"error":"conflict","code":"AGENT_RESUME_FAILED","message":"AO could not relaunch the agent (step: runtime). Check the daemon log for details.","details":{"step":"runtime"}}
```

## Notes / intentional omissions

- **The drop in resume-agent 5xx after release is a reclassification, not a reliability win.** The same failures move to `ao.session.relaunch_failed` and to Sentry under a new fingerprint. Track those for the real rate.
- A 409 is not a perfect fit for "the agent failed to relaunch". It was chosen so the client gets a readable message while telemetry and Sentry keep the failure.
- This does not make the relaunch itself succeed. It turns an opaque 500 into a classified failure, so the dominant step can be identified from `ao.session.relaunch_failed` and fixed next.
- `Restore` uses the same mapping, so a restore relaunch failure also becomes 409 `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED` and is recorded with `operation=restore_session`.
- The frontend is unchanged. Resume and restore callers already show the envelope `message` and only special-case other codes (`AGENT_NOT_EXITED`, `SESSION_NOT_RESUMABLE`).
- A `SQLITE_BUSY` during the "record launch" step now answers 409 instead of 503. Nothing retries resume or restore on 503 today, so the user-visible effect is only the wording.
- PostHog ingestion rules for project 475752 must keep `ao.session.relaunch_failed` (doc updated; the live rule is configured in PostHog).

## Validation

Focused tests only:
- `go test ./internal/service/session/ -run 'TestResumeAgent|TestRestore|APIError'` (new `TestResumeAgentMapsRelaunchFailureToConflict`: 409 mapping, no raw-error leak in message or PostHog payload, one PostHog event and one Sentry capture with the raw error per operation, nothing for the 503 deadline path)
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run 'TestResumeAgent_|Restore'` (new `TestResumeAgent_RuntimeFailureNamesRelaunchStep` against the real manager)
- `go test ./internal/adapters/telemetry/ -run 'PostHog|Allowlist'`
- `npx vitest run src/shared/observability.test.ts` (new case: a 409 `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED` is P1 and reported)

The full CI suites, `golangci-lint`, `go vet` and `-race` were not run locally; CI covers them.

title: feat(review): run the Claude reviewer in Chat, read-only, and close the pane's auto-mode write gap
body:
Code changes: +267 -86\ Tests: +411 -24\ Others: +0 -0 ## What - The Claude Code reviewer can run in **Chat** (typed ACP transport), like the Codex reviewer, and that Chat is **read-only**. - The Claude reviewer **terminal pane** now starts in Claude's `default` mode instead of `auto`. In `auto`, shell writes in the worker's checkout were not blocked. ## Why The Claude reviewer only ran in a terminal pane because Claude's ACP driver ignored `ChatStartConfig.ReadOnly`. ACP has no read-only primitive: modes mean whatever the agent says, and the client fs capability is not a sandbox. So the Chat has to enforce read-only through Claude Code's own permission engine. While checking that, a live test of the existing pane showed a real hole. The pane launched with `--permission-mode auto`, and in `auto` Claude's classifier approves shell commands that no allow rule names, such as `touch b.txt` or `printf hi > d.txt`. Those calls never reach the PermissionRequest hook that is supposed to deny them, so a reviewer could write to the worker's branch. ## Before / After Captured in the real desktop app (isolated lab data dir) and in a real tmux pane. Before is `main` at 4d7c9cf; after is this PR at 1de80c0b26. Reviews were posted to a throwaway repo. | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | | Claude reviewer opens as a terminal pane in `auto mode on`; every command, including a compound `git fetch …; git diff …`, is `Allowed by auto mode`
![Before: Claude reviewer pane in auto mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/before-app-reviewer-pane-main.png) | Claude reviewer runs in Chat and posts its review (GitHub review 5864448249, `changes_requested`)
![After: Claude reviewer in Chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/app-reviewer-chat.png) | | No Chat reviewer for Claude. The live test with `ReadOnly` off lets all 10 writes through, including `git commit` and `git diff --output=e.txt` ([log](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/live-control-readonly-off.log)) | Asked from the app to write four files under `/tmp`, the Chat reviewer is refused on every call (`4 exited`); no files appear, checkout unchanged
![After: four writes refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/app-reviewer-writes-refused.png) | | Terminal pane in `auto`: `touch b.txt` and `printf hi > d.txt` create files; the PermissionRequest hook is never called
![Before: pane writes go through](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/pane-before-main-auto.png) | Terminal pane in `default`: AO's PermissionRequest hook denies every shell write; checkout clean
![After: pane writes denied](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/pane-after-pr-default.png) | | Terminal reviewer submits under `auto mode on` | Terminal reviewer (still selectable) runs in `manual mode on`; only the two exact submit commands are `Allowed by PermissionRequest hook` (GitHub review 5864556501, approved)
![After: terminal reviewer in default mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/app-reviewer-pane-tui.png) | Chat review on PR head, then the `/tmp` write probe (2x): ![Chat review and write probe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/review-in-chat.gif) https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/review-in-chat.mp4?raw=true Posted reviews: [changes requested from Chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/github-review-5864448249.png), [approval from the terminal pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/github-review-5864556501.png). ## How - **ACP driver** (`chatdriver/acp`): - `LaunchConfig` carries `ReadOnly` on start and resume. - A binding's `Config.ReadOnly` hook supplies the provider mode to pin, which wins over the turn's approval setting, and the permission policy that answers requests in place of a human. - A read-only launch that has tools, on a binding without that hook, is refused instead of silently running writable. - A policy can return `CancelPermission`, so a request with no usable reject option is cancelled instead of waiting for a human. - **Claude Chat binding** (`claudeacp`), for read-only sessions: - Sends the reviewer allow/deny tool lists through `_meta.claudeCode.options`; claude-agent-acp passes them to Claude Code as `--allowedTools` / `--disallowedTools`. - Pins mode `default`. Not `auto` (its classifier approves unnamed shell commands) and not `dontAsk` (it would also block the review POST, and newer adapters drop that mode). - Rejects every permission request except the exact submit commands, which are allowed once, never "always". - **One shared rule** in `adapters/agent/claudecode`: the reviewer tool lists and the submit-command matcher, used by the pane, its PermissionRequest hook and the Chat. - No prefix allow rules for `git diff/log/show` (their `--output=` writes a file) or `ao review submit` (a prefix would skip the worker-session pin). Claude Code's own read-only check still approves plain `git log`/`git diff` in `default` mode and prompts on `--output`, which AO denies. - `mcp__*` and `AskUserQuestion` are denied. A reviewer needs no MCP tool, and a headless reviewer would wait forever on a question. - The matcher accepts apostrophes escaped as `'"'"'` and dotted worker ids (`acme.dev-2`); a test covers a `$(…)` injection attempt. - **Review prompt**: one added line asks for each submit command as its own shell call, with no `cd`, `&&`, `;` or redirection. In a live run the model prefixed `cd &&`, the matcher refused it, and ACP's bare "User refused permission" gave it no hint to retry. - **Claude reviewer adapter**: - Implements `ReviewChatHarness()`. - Launch and restore pin `--permission-mode default`, plus a flag-settings `defaultMode: "default"` merged into any existing `--settings`, which also keeps Claude's one-time auto-mode dialog out of the pane. Orchestrator's own `default` setting can't do this: it passes no flag, so the user's `defaultMode` (often `auto`) would apply. Behaviour change: when the Claude chat runtime is available, new Claude reviews start in Chat. Existing reviews keep their recorded interface. ## Testing On 1de80c0b26, with Claude Code 2.1.322 and a user `defaultMode` of `auto`: - **Desktop app**: the PR build in an isolated data dir with a real worker and a real PR on a throwaway repo. - The Chat review posted with verdict `changes_requested`. The worker fixed both findings, and a terminal-pane review of the new head approved. - The `/tmp` write probe was refused. The reviewer never changed the worker checkout; only the worker's own fix commits landed. - The same flow on `main` produced the before captures. - **Live test** `TestLiveClaudeACPReadOnlyRejectsWrites` (`AO_LIVE_CLAUDE_ACP=1`): passes. Edit/Write/`touch`/`bash -c`/`printf >`/`sed -i`/`git commit`/`git diff --output` are refused, and `git status` and `git log` run ([log](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/live-readonly.log)). With `ReadOnly: false` the same test fails because all 10 writes land, so the test tells the two cases apart ([log](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7eed50b4a0fcba16c35943da657ce6995f938abe/1de80c0/live-control-readonly-off.log)). - **Terminal pane in tmux**, using the exact reviewer argv from `ReviewCommand` and the hooks installed by `PreLaunch`: on `main`, 2 of the shell writes created files and the PermissionRequest hook was called 0 times. On this PR, every write was denied by the hook. - **Unit tests**: new and updated tests in `adapters/agent/claudecode`, `chatdriver/acp`, `chatdriver/claudeacp`, `adapters/reviewer/claudecode` and `review`; CI is green on 1de80c0b26. Not covered: - `ForkIntoHost` doesn't pass `ReadOnly`. Reviewers never fork, but the new guard doesn't cover that path. - The hook's deny message still names `git diff/log/show` as allowlisted. Plain reads do still run through Claude's own read-only check, so the guidance holds, but the wording is stale. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Security** * Review sessions now run in read-only mode, blocking file changes, Git writes, and other unapproved actions. * Review submissions are permitted only for approved commands tied to the current worker session; chained or modified commands are rejected. * Read-only sessions that require tools are refused when the required permission policy is unavailable. * **Improvements** * Review instructions now require specified commands to run individually, without chaining or redirection.

title: fix(sessions): retry transient 503 on orchestrator open and tag ao.http.5xx with transient cause
body:
Code changes: +54 -30  
Tests: +80 -3  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Opening an orchestrator can fail with "The service is momentarily unavailable, please retry." (503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, ~39 users/week). The envelope maps a raw SQLite BUSY/LOCKED or `context.DeadlineExceeded` from the pre-spawn reads/writes in `SpawnOrchestrator` to 503, but the renderer never retried. Telemetry recorded these as `error_kind=internal` with no code, so busy vs deadline could not be told apart.

## Change

- `spawnOrchestrator` (renderer) retries a 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` after 500 ms and 1500 ms, **only for non-clean spawns**. A non-clean spawn holds the per-project orchestrator lock and returns the existing orchestrator if one is live, so a retry cannot start a second one. A clean (replacing) spawn is never replayed.
- `telemetrymeta.TransientCause` (`sqlite_busy` | `sqlite_locked` | `deadline`) replaces the envelope's private `isTransient`, with the same matching rules. The 503 mapping is unchanged.
- `ao.http.5xx` carries `transient_cause`, which is added to the PostHog allowlist so export does not strip it.

## Notes / intentional omissions

- Which DB condition dominates in the field is inferred, not confirmed. The new `transient_cause` field plus the existing `duration` (about 5 s means busy_timeout, about 60 s means request deadline) should settle it.
- `ao.http.5xx` is rolled up per minute; the rollup keeps the last sample's `transient_cause`.
- The retry wait is not abortable; at most 2 s of extra wait.

## Validation

Focused tests only (pass after rebase onto `main`):
- `go test ./internal/telemetrymeta/ -run TransientCause`
- `go test ./internal/httpd/envelope/ -run TestWriteError_`
- `go test ./internal/httpd/ -run TestRequestLogger`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/telemetry/ -run TestHTTP5xxAllowlistExportsTransientCause`
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/spawn-orchestrator.test.ts` (retries 503 then succeeds; clean spawn never replayed)

The full CI suites, `golangci-lint`, `go vet` and `-race` were not run locally; CI covers them.

title: fix(projects): log remove failures and archive after teardown outlives the request budget
body:
Code changes: +5 -1  
Tests: +39 -0

## Problem

"Failed to remove project" (~24 users/week) comes only from `project.Service.Remove`. Both store-error sites replaced the real error with a generic `apierr.Internal` and logged nothing. When teardown finished but had used up the 60 s request budget, the final `ArchiveProject` ran on an expired context, failed, and left a fully torn-down project listed.

## Notes / intentional omissions

- This covers teardown that **succeeds** after spending the budget. If teardown itself fails or times out, `Remove` still returns that error before archiving (unchanged, fail-closed).
- The response is still 500 with the same message, so `ao.http.5xx` and Sentry are unchanged; the cause is now in the daemon log. Mapping busy errors to 503 is a possible follow-up.

title: fix(frontend): report remote host list failure once and keep polling
body:
Code changes: +12 -2  
Tests: +19 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Remote host polling is the most frequent renderer error (1,429 hits, ~48 users/week), though users never see it. `useRemoteHosts` refreshes every 30 s with `void refresh()`, and `await aoBridge.remotes.list()` sat outside any try/catch. When main rejects (main is signed out of AO Cloud while the renderer still has a cached session, or `remotes.json` cannot be read), every poll produced an unhandled rejection.

## Change

- Catch the `remotes.list()` failure and return, keeping the current hosts state so the next poll retries (no destructive disconnect on an unknown list).
- Report the failure once per app session per class (`list_saved_hosts_signed_out` / `list_saved_hosts`) via `captureRendererException`, so it stays visible without repeating every 30 s.
- Catch rejections from disconnecting hosts that were removed.
- Test: one report across repeated failed polls, polling continues, no unhandled rejection.

## Notes / intentional omissions

- The underlying renderer/main sign-in mismatch is not fixed here; the per-class report will show how often it happens.
- Two other `void disconnectHost(...)` call sites (account change, disabled) are outside the poll path and unchanged.

## Validation

Focused tests only (pass after rebase onto `main`):
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/hooks/useRemoteHosts.test.tsx`

title: fix(chat): treat a reused pid as a dead chat host instead of an inconclusive reconnect
body:
Code changes: +128 -10  
Tests: +115 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Chat reconnect fails with "inconclusive" for ~27 users/week. `persistenthost.ConnectOrStart` returns `ErrOwnershipInconclusive` when attaching fails but `processalive.Alive(pid)` is true, and `Alive` checks only the pid. After a crash or reboot, a stale `host.json` (or launch lock) whose pid was reused by an unrelated process stays "inconclusive" forever.

## Change

- `processalive.AliveSince(pid, since)`: the process is alive and did not start more than 1 minute after `since`. The start time comes from `ps -o lstart=` on unix and `GetProcessTimes` on Windows. The 1-minute tolerance absorbs `ps` boot-time drift.
- The host descriptor (`StartedAt`, written by the host process itself) and the launch lock (now `pid unixSeconds`) use it. A reused pid falls through to `ErrNotRunning`, which leads to the normal resume path.
- `ErrOwnershipInconclusive` is kept for attach timeouts, `ErrAttached` and a genuinely live host.
- Warn logs record pid, address and attach error kind (`refused`/`timeout`/`attached`/…).
- The `ErrAttached` wait loop checks identity once and then polls the cheap `Alive`, so it does not spawn `ps` every 20 ms.

## Notes / intentional omissions

- Fail-closed by design: zero `StartedAt`, legacy pid-only lock files, and an unreadable start time all keep today's pid-only behaviour. Reconcile still claims the lock before deleting a descriptor. A reused pid is never signalled.
- The Windows start-time path is compile-checked only (`GOOS=windows`).
- Clock steps of more than 1 minute between host start and the check could still misjudge a live host as reused.

## Validation

Focused tests only (pass after rebase onto `main`):
- `go test ./internal/processalive/ -run 'TestAliveSince|TestAliveReportsZombieAsDead'`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/ -run 'TestConnectOrStartReusedPID|TestAcquireHostLockReclaims|TestConnectOrStartTimesOutSilentLiveHost|TestConnectOrStartConcurrentStaleProbe|Attached'`

title: perf(chat): measure and cut render time when opening large chats
body:
**Priority: P0** (ordered for developers on Macs working against their local daemon)

## Problem

Opening a large chat on a Mac is limited by rendering, not by data transfer. Before #7165, the biggest chat (`agent-orchestrator-1-254`, 4.9 MB first page) took about 0.82 s from click to its last message on screen over loopback, and cutting its payload from 5.3 MB to 0.4 MB did not change that time (822 ms vs 843 ms). Parsing the JSON took under 7 ms.

#7165 now puts whole turns on the first page, so a page can carry up to about 1,850 tool rows (first-page p90 went from 1.03 MB to 2.74 MB on the same data). Open time on current `main` has not been measured, and it is likely worse.

## What to do

1. Measure on current `main` with the five largest chats on a real database:
   - time from navigation to the last message being visible;
   - long tasks (PerformanceObserver `longtask`): count, longest, total;
   - React commit time for the chat timeline (React Profiler);
   - JS heap after the open.
2. Find where the time goes. Candidates to check first: rows inside collapsed turns ("Worked for …") that mount even though they are hidden, per-row markdown and code highlighting, and re-renders of the whole timeline when one row changes.
3. Fix the largest cost. Likely shapes: do not mount collapsed turn bodies until opened, virtualize rows inside a long turn, memoize rows by id and revision.

## How to verify it is done

- A before/after table on the same database for the five chats: open time, longest long task, total long-task time, heap.
- Proposed targets: the largest chat shows its last message in under 400 ms, with no long task over 200 ms.
- No visual change: the timeline looks the same with every turn collapsed and with every turn opened (compare the rendered text of opened turns before and after).
- Scrolling up and "Load earlier messages" still work, and a running turn still streams.

---
Measurement setup: a sandboxed copy of a real `ao.db` (337 sessions, 236 chats), daemon builds from `main`, loopback plus a throttling proxy (400 kbps each way, 400 ms round trip, a new connection per request) for the slow-network numbers, and the dev desktop app driven over CDP for the desktop numbers. Lab scripts: `~/.ao/dev/perf-lab`.

title: perf(chat): load tool bodies when a row is opened, not with every chat page
body:
**Priority: P0** (ordered for developers on Macs working against their local daemon)

## Problem

Every chat page carries the full body of every tool call: command output, MCP results (including base64 images, often twice), file patches and reasoning text. The timeline shows none of it until someone opens the row. Since #7165 a first page holds whole turns, so it carries even more.

First page of all 236 chats on current `main`:

| | p50 | p90 | largest | all chats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Today | 487 KB | 2.74 MB | 5.5 MB | 230 MB |
| With this change (512-byte previews) | 116 KB | 811 KB | 1.77 MB | 66 MB |
| With 128-byte previews | ~85 KB | ~597 KB | ~1.48 MB | ~53 MB |

On the desktop (measured before #7165): about 8 MB less renderer memory after four opens, and the largest chat opened in 747 ms instead of 822 ms. On a slow network the largest chat went from 99 s to 8 s.

About 10% of all page bytes are a second copy of the same body:
- `mcp_tool` rows repeat `content` in `output`, and the timeline renders only `content`;
- `command` rows repeat `output` in `content`, and the timeline renders only `output`;
- `rawCommand` often equals `command`.

## What to do

Server (`GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/conversation`, opt-in so old clients get the same bytes):
- `compactDetails=1`: for settled rows (status not `running` or `pending`) of kinds `command`, `mcp_tool`, `file_change` and `reasoning`, cut every string in `detail` longer than 128 bytes to a 128-byte preview (for `progress`, keep the last 128 bytes, because the collapsed row shows its last line) and set `detailOmitted: true` on the row. Never compact `system` rows: a steer shows its images inline.
- `dedupeBodies=1`: drop the copy the timeline does not render (rules above) and mark it (`outputOmitted: "content"`, `contentOmitted: "output"`). Only drop a copy whose long strings all appear in the kept field.
- Add a single-row read, for example `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/conversation/activities/{activityId}`, that returns one activity with its full (deduped) detail. Since #7165, `limit` counts messages only, so a page read with `limit=1` no longer returns just one row.

Client:
- Request pages with both flags.
- When a row with `detailOmitted` is opened (command and file rows, MCP rows, and reasoning blocks while reasoning is shown), read the row whole and render that. Cache it by session, row id and revision.
- Running rows are never compacted, so live command output keeps streaming.

Test: add a byte-budget test that builds a snapshot with a 5 MB command output and a duplicated 660 KB image and asserts the compacted response stays under 64 KiB, running rows keep their full output, and short fields (`command`, `exitCode`) stay whole.

A local prototype of the server half (`conversation_compact.go` with tests) applies cleanly on current `main`.

## How to verify it is done

- For every chat on a real database, a compacted page has the same message and activity ids, in the same order, as an uncompacted page.
- Open every row in a few large turns, with and without the flags: the rendered text and images are identical. (In the lab this was checked on two turns of 6 KB and 1.8 MB of rendered text; 17 row reads happened only when rows were opened.)

title: perf(chat): live updates should fetch only what changed, not every loaded page
body:
**Priority: P1** (ordered for developers on Macs working against their local daemon)

## Problem

When the open chat changes, the client invalidates the conversation query in `event-transport.ts`, and TanStack Query then refetches every loaded page of the infinite query. #7165 stopped reloads for id-only updates while a chat is ready or busy, but every real change (a new message, a tool row, a finished command) still re-downloads, re-parses and re-renders every page the chat has loaded. Since #7165 those pages are larger (first-page p90 2.74 MB).

Measured before #7165: one live event on the open largest chat downloaded 10.2 MB (the 4.9 MB page twice plus the 343 KB session list). Fetching only the rows that can still change: 101 KB in total, of which the conversation part was 13 KB. On a slow network a live update went from 99 s to 1.1 s.

## What to do

Server:
- Add an opt-in `afterSequence=N` to the newest-page read: return only messages and activities with `sequence >= N`, plus the header and turns as today, and echo `afterSequence` in the response.
- If the page does not reach back to `N` (`hasMoreBefore` and `oldestSequence > N`), return the full page without `afterSequence`, so the client knows to replace instead of merge.
- Rows are rewritten in place: their `sequence` never changes and only `revision` grows. The exact fix is a per-row "changed at" sequence (a column bumped on every write, plus an index), so the server can return every row changed after a cursor. Prefer this. The cheaper alternative used in the prototype: the client sends the sequence of its earliest row that can still change (a `running` or `pending` activity or a streaming message), else `latestSequence + 1`. That relies on settled rows never changing, which needs to be confirmed for every adapter.

Client:
- For an open local chat, a conversation event refreshes only the live page with `afterSequence` (single-flight per chat, like the existing remote refresh) and merges the rows into it by id with `mergeConversationPages([delta, livePage])`.
- Fall back to the current invalidation when there is no cached page, when the response has no `afterSequence`, or when `conversationId` or `activeBranchId` changed (edits, rollbacks, branch switches).

## How to verify it is done

- Run a real agent turn with several commands, including one that prints for 30 s or more. In the network log, each refresh during the turn carries `afterSequence` and is a few KB, not a full page.
- After the turn ends, the timeline equals a fresh reload of the same chat: same row ids and revisions, same rendered text.
- Edit a message, roll back a turn, and switch branches: the timeline is correct afterwards (full refresh path).
- Approvals and input requests appear and resolve as before.
- Report bytes per live event and the number of conversation requests during a 5-minute turn, before and after.

---
Measurement setup: a sandboxed copy of a real `ao.db` (337 sessions, 236 chats), daemon builds from `main`, loopback plus a throttling proxy (400 kbps each way, 400 ms round trip, a new connection per request) for the slow-network numbers, and the dev desktop app driven over CDP for the desktop numbers. Lab scripts: `~/.ao/dev/perf-lab`.

title: perf(chat): opening a stopped chat reloads its history and the whole session list
body:
**Priority: P1** (ordered for developers on Macs working against their local daemon)

## Problem

Opening a chat registers its view (`POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/chat-view`) in `SessionView.tsx`. After the registration succeeds, the client:
- invalidates the conversation when the chat is not settled (stopped or waking), which refetches every loaded page; most chats people reopen are stopped;
- always invalidates the whole session list (`/api/v1/sessions`, about 343 KB on a real machine), on every chat open.

Measured before #7165: opening the largest stopped chat downloaded 5.26 MB (4.9 MB conversation plus 343 KB list). When the conversation had already been fetched (for example by a hover prefetch), the registration triggered a second full download of the same page.

## What to do

- A stopped chat does not change while it is stopped, so do not reload it after registration. Waking emits its own events, which refresh the chat.
- For a waking chat, refresh only the live page (see the issue on live updates fetching only what changed), not every loaded page.
- Replace the session-list invalidation with a read of this one session (`GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}`) patched into the workspace cache.

## How to verify it is done

- Open five stopped chats one after another: each makes exactly one conversation request, and no `/api/v1/sessions` list request is made.
- Open a hibernated chat and send a message: it wakes, the state moves to ready, and new rows appear without a manual refresh.
- Opening a chat that was hover-prefetched makes no second conversation request.
- Report requests and bytes per chat open, before and after.

---

title: perf(desktop): refresh one session row on id-only updates, and read the session list once at startup
body:
**Priority: P1** (ordered for developers on Macs working against their local daemon)

## Problem

1. A `session_updated` event that carries only the session id (usage bookkeeping, cleanup facts) refetches the whole session list, at most once every 5 s since #6813. While agents run, these keep coming, and each refetch is about 343 KB on a real machine (335 sessions), then parsed and diffed. Lifecycle sweeps emit them in bursts: 20 to 23 sessions within one second, seen both on a real daemon and in the lab.
2. On a cold start the desktop requests `/api/v1/sessions` twice (687 KB instead of 343 KB). The cause has not been traced.

## What to do

- In `event-transport.ts`, collect the session ids of id-only updates during a flush window. If there are 3 or fewer, read each with `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}` and patch that row into the workspace cache (replace it by id in its project, add it when missing, keep pending optimistic kills applied). With more than 3, fall back to the existing throttled list refresh, because one list read is cheaper than twenty row reads.
- Single-flight per session: one row read in flight plus at most one queued.
- Find and remove the duplicate `/api/v1/sessions` request at startup.

## How to verify it is done

- One id-only update costs one row read (about 1.3 KB) instead of a list read (343 KB).
- With one agent working for 5 minutes, count full `/api/v1/sessions` reads before and after.
- A burst of more than 3 sessions causes one list read, not one read per session.
- Status changes on the sidebar and board still show within a second.
- The startup network log shows one `/api/v1/sessions` request.

---
Measurement setup: a sandboxed copy of a real `ao.db` (337 sessions, 236 chats), daemon builds from `main`, loopback plus a throttling proxy (400 kbps each way, 400 ms round trip, a new connection per request) for the slow-network numbers, and the dev desktop app driven over CDP for the desktop numbers. title: perf(desktop): load archived sessions on demand instead of with every session-list read
body:
**Priority: P2** (ordered for developers on Macs working against their local daemon)

## Problem

The desktop reads every session the machine has ever run on each session-list read (polling, events, chat opens). On a real machine that is 335 rows and 343 KB, of which 301 rows (87% of the bytes) are ended sessions that only show when someone opens an archive.

The daemon already supports what is needed (#7155, used by mobile): `GET /api/v1/sessions?active=true` returns only live sessions and reports `archived: {total, byProject}`, and `active=false&limit=&cursor=` pages the archive in board order.

A naive version was tried in the lab: live sessions plus the newest 25 ended sessions across all projects. The list read dropped from 343 KB to 75 KB, but project boards lost their Archive column: `todo-app` showed "No worker sessions yet" instead of "Archive 6", and the sessions board archive dropped from 3 to 2 entries.

## What to do

- Read live sessions with `active=true` for the workspace list, and keep the `archived` summary.
- Archive columns and counts (project boards, the sessions board) use `archived.byProject` and load archive pages only when the archive is opened or searched.
- An ended session opened by URL, notification or link already falls back to `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}`. That serializes the conversation read behind the session read (+177 ms measured), so start the conversation read in the session route loader at the same time.
- Check every place that reads ended sessions from the workspace list: orchestrator children, session search, artifacts, notifications.

## How to verify it is done

- A session-list read is about 75 KB instead of 343 KB on the same machine.
- Every project board shows the same Archive count as before, and opening the archive lists the same sessions in the same order.
- An ended session opened from a link or notification opens without extra delay.
- Orchestrator children, search and notifications show ended sessions as before.

---
Measurement setup: a sandboxed copy of a real `ao.db` (337 sessions, 236 chats), daemon builds from `main`, loopback plus a throttling proxy (400 kbps each way, 400 ms round trip, a new connection per request) for the slow-network numbers, and the dev desktop app driven over CDP for the desktop numbers. title: perf(remote): gzip JSON responses on the remote listener
body:
**Priority: P3 (remote clients only)** (ordered for developers on Macs working against their local daemon)

## Problem

JSON responses from the daemon are not compressed. This matters only for clients that are not on the same machine (phones, remote desktops, tunnels). On the loopback listener compression is a cost with no benefit: in the lab, gzip raised server time for a 4.9 MB chat page from about 30 ms to about 80 ms.

On a slow-network model: the session list goes from 343 KB to 36 KB (7.8 s to 1.6 s). A chat page with tool bodies loaded on expand goes from 363 KB to 60 KB (8.2 s to 2.1 s). Base64 images in tool bodies barely compress, so without that change gzip saves only about 30% on large chats.

## What to do

#7128 gzips `application/json` on the remote listener only. Review and land it. Keep the loopback listener uncompressed and event streams unencoded.

## How to verify it is done

- On the remote listener, a JSON response requested with `Accept-Encoding: gzip` comes back gzipped and decodes; an event stream does not.
- On loopback, responses are not compressed.
- Phone board polls and chat opens over a tunnel are faster (see #7128's load test).

---

title: feat(desktop): rework the agent update notice
body:
Code changes: +522 -208  
Tests: +103 -82  
Others: +51 -0 (i18n strings, 8 locales)

## Why

The agent (harness) update notice was rough to look at and use:

- Its position followed each page's top bar, so it jumped when switching pages.
- The dismiss × rendered at 32px instead of the authored 20px (tailwind-merge kept Button's `size-control-form` over `size-5`), floated over the card's corner, and sat 2.5px above Update.
- Timestamped versions were middle-truncated into `v0.0.177…cd91 → v0.0.179…a0d4`, which reads like two patch releases for a ~6-month gap.
- Several updates showed as separate floating cards with a toggle row that floated over page content, with Show all and Show less on different sides and buttons that did not line up.
- A finished update just vanished, the same as a dismissal.

This PR is UI only: when the notice appears and how dismissal works are unchanged (dismissing hides that release; a newer release shows it again).

## What changes

- **Placement:** top-right of the framed center panel: 12px from its top without a top bar, and just below the page's top bar when it has one (`useCenterPanelBox` reports how far a `.workspace-topbar-container` across the panel's top edge reaches in). It slides between the two (`translate`, 200ms) instead of jumping, and never covers a page's own actions. A fixed box that tracks `.center-panel-surface` clips it (matching the panel's radius). It is still portaled to `<body>` for Electron drag-region ordering. While the live native browser page overlaps it, it stays mounted but invisible and inert (and publishes no rect), so its measured rect drives the overlap check. It still publishes its rect for `useHarnessUpdateNoticeClearance`.
- **One card layout** for one update, several (collapsed) and the expanded list: a header with the agent mark(s) (several overlap, each cut out with a halo in the card colour), a short helper line on why to update, the list toggle on the left and Update / Update all on the right (same 28px height and right edge). The expanded list is one panel with rows; it animates its height and stays mounted while closed, so opening does not stall on building rows.
- **Swipe to dismiss:** two-finger horizontal trackpad swipe (same native scroll-phase handling as `SwipeNavigation`) or a pointer drag. Past 35% of the width or on a flick, the card or row slides out, then closes its gap; shorter swipes spring back. The in-flow 20px × uses the same exit. Mostly vertical gestures are ignored. Dismissal itself is unchanged.
- **Readable versions:** builds stamped `0.0.<unix seconds>-g<sha>` show their build date (`May 6 → Oct 26`), full version in the hover title.
- **Success state:** an update started from the notice that succeeds shows "Amp updated · Now on Oct 26" for 4s.
- **Surface:** the chat model selector's menu surface (`--color-bg-settings-menu`, `--color-border-settings-menu`, `--radius-settings-panel`, `--shadow-popover`), so it does not blend into cards and the composer beneath it.
- Removes `useWorkspaceTopbarBottom`, whose only user was the old notice.

## Intentionally not changed

- When the notice shows and how dismissal works. Agents that publish several builds a day (Amp) still bring it back with each new build; that is a separate behaviour change.
- The tailwind-merge config in `lib/utils.ts` still does not know the `control-*` size keys, so other `<Button size=…>` call sites that override height/size keep the same bug. That is app-wide and belongs in its own PR; this notice no longer depends on it.
- The notice can sit over page content in the panel's top-right corner (for example the end of a chat message) while it is shown; it never covers a top bar.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck`: pass.
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/HarnessUpdateNotice.test.tsx src/renderer/components/GlobalToast.test.tsx src/renderer/components/SessionInterfaceSwitch.test.tsx src/renderer/components/ScriptRunPanel.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n`: 141/141 pass (the notice tests add top-bar offset, swipe, vertical-gesture, build-date and success-state cases; post-dismiss assertions wait for the exit animation).
- On the previous head, the full frontend vitest suite and `npm run typecheck:e2e` passed locally, except `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`, which fails on this machine only (`better-sqlite3` built for Electron's Node ABI) and is untouched here. Renderer smoke could not run locally (no Playwright browser installed); CI covers it.
- Checked by hand in the dev Electron app (isolated data): the position on the home page (no top bar) and a session page (below its top bar), clipping by the center panel, swipe and × exits, collapsed/expanded with 3–4 real and 10–11 updates (extra ones were stubbed in the renderer only), button alignment measured, surface computed styles matching the model menu.

title: perf(models): avoid duplicate OpenCode catalog downloads
body:
Code changes: +111 -4  
Tests: +507 -1  
Others: +10 -0

Refs #7266.

OpenCode session opens currently fetch the full provider-cache catalog twice: first for catalog facts, then again for usage. Use one device/host/credential-scope read, deduplicate pending reads across observer remounts, and discard pending reads when login changes. Existing Settings catalog data remains visible while the read is pending.

Catalog invalidation also stops pending reads from being shared, including reads detached by observer teardown:

- The event transport evicts matching pending reads for **every** `agent-models` invalidation: CDC, resync, remote events and remote fallback polls. This runs before its per-key coalescing return. It uses TanStack's own prefix matching against each read's query key, so hosts, agents and credential scopes stay isolated.
- This does not depend on TanStack's `invalidate` event. TanStack 5.101.0 emits no event while a query is already marked invalidated, which happens after an earlier invalidation or a failed read.
- Eviction only removes a read from sharing. Every unsettled read stays tracked until it settles, so a later catalog change still reaches it.
- An actual catalog change marks every matching tracked read invalidated, whether or not it was evicted. That means a local `model_catalog` CDC event, or a remote host's typed `model_catalog` event (scoped to that host and agent). Any queryFn still awaiting such a read then reads again before publishing; this includes an observerless `prefetchQuery`, which gets no cancellation and no transport catch-up. Catalog row writes are finite, so these restarts end.
- Remote polls, other remote events and resyncs repeat without naming a catalog change, so they only stop sharing. A read slower than the 2 s remote polling interval still finishes and publishes.
- A remount after any invalidation issues a fresh read instead of reusing a pre-event response. An older read that settles later cannot write the query cache or saved snapshot, or remove the newer pending read.
- The transport's existing catch-up for active fetches is unchanged. An active read overtaken by a catalog event may therefore read once more before that catch-up runs. Ordinary remounts with no invalidation still share one pending read.
- **Known residuals:** both concern an observerless prefetch whose query was already invalidated.
  - A remote host in polling fallback delivers no typed events. The prefetch can publish a pre-change catalog, and the next 2 s poll invalidates it.
  - A catalog change whose event is lost in an SSE gap is followed only by a generic resync. Making resyncs restart reads could livelock a slow read while SSE flaps. The pre-change catalog can stay until the next catalog event, the 10-minute stale time, or about 3 s after mount when the response reports a refresh in progress.
  - `main` never restarts an observerless enriched read, even for delivered events.

Picker responses preserve every model ID, label, provider, default, effort/fast control and usage timestamp. Context windows, input modalities and discovery metadata remain available through the existing Settings `catalogOnly=true` read. No schema, persisted discovery catalog, provider-selection policy, gzip behavior or persistent-cache size limit changes.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| An OpenCode picker downloads the browsing catalog before the catalog with usage. | The picker uses one response and shares pending reads across remounts. |

### Evidence and proposed target

- **Measured synthetic fixture:** 10,000 model records, decoded JSON **2,296,163 → 1,806,030 bytes** (21.35% smaller). Full Settings response: 2,296,164 bytes including encoder newline. Selectable option count is preserved: **10,000 → 10,000**. Tests compare every retained model/control field and verify the shared catalog is not mutated.
- **Proposed target:** under 100 KB. This fixture remains above that target. The existing project/task pickers expose unconfigured-provider entries too, so all those options are preserved.
- **Actual configured-machine evidence unavailable:** the issue's approved `~/.ao/dev/perf-lab` directory is absent here and OpenCode is not on PATH. No personal credentials, live AO database, private transcripts or global harness install were used.
- **Persistence limit unchanged:** catalogs above the existing 1 MiB snapshot budget still rely on the per-device in-memory query cache.

### Validation

- **Current head `3e6a5b4e54933db4fdb31025ac276a6135dc0fbf`:** Rebased onto `main` at `16146672aea233ba44aabb7c9de43c4346e2f928`. Conflict resolutions retain the API error helper and shell-terminal imports. Remote catalog invalidation uses the current event router and remains scoped by host and agent.
- **Local frontend:** Both project and E2E TypeScript checks passed under Node 24.22.3. The complete related Vitest run passed: 4,687 tests across 117 files. The SQLite addon was rebuilt for Node 24 before this run.
- **Local backend:** HTTP package tests passed with race detection under Go 1.27.4. Build, vet, and the public boundary check passed. The local Go version differs from the CI module pin, Go 1.27.1.
- **Remote CI:** `ci-ok`, Public boundary, and gitleaks passed on the new head. The draft PR skips the Go, Frontend, and CLI E2E lanes.
- **Remaining checks:** Full backend suites, golangci-lint, generated-code drift, CLI E2E, Electron boundary tests, browser integration, and renderer smoke were not run locally. The configured-OpenCode and desktop measurement gaps below remain.
- **Previous rebase head `15db753f33793a1b7a07beb2c8a793bda097ce83`:** `335b446a17` rebased onto `main` at `fe0550a4e8` (94 commits newer). `git range-diff` shows commits 2–7 unchanged; commit 1 differs only in `docs/harnesses/model-catalogs.md`, where this PR's OpenCode paragraph now precedes `main`'s new `## Cloud tasks` section. All six code and test files have the same net patch as before, and `main` did not touch them. **Previous-head remote CI: all 30 checks passed.** Frontend passed 10/10 jobs, Go 14/14, CLI E2E 4/4, gitleaks 1/1 and Public boundary 1/1. The Vitest shard logs show `useAgentModelsQuery.test.ts` 43, `lib/event-transport.test.ts` 52 and `TaskComposer.test.tsx` 135 passed; the last includes `main`'s new Cloud catalog tests. **AO native review:** approved this head with no actionable findings. It is an internal static review, not a GitHub approval, and does not satisfy branch protection. Not run locally: `main` changed `frontend/package.json` and its lockfile, so the installed dependencies no longer match.
- **Pre-rebase head `335b446a17e773122741d42b91bfc2b298f0d7a6` (`fix: keep evicted OpenCode reads trackable for catalog changes`), focused local run.** Dependencies came from an install-only `npm ci --ignore-scripts` of `packages/product-ui` (124 packages) and `frontend` (1459 packages) on Node 24.22.0. No install scripts ran, so native modules and Electron are unverified locally. The two changed test files then ran with `vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/hooks/useAgentModelsQuery.test.ts src/renderer/lib/event-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism --bail=1`. **Both files passed, 95/95 tests (`useAgentModelsQuery.test.ts` 43, `lib/event-transport.test.ts` 52), with none skipped or failed** (Vitest 11.0 s). No local typecheck, build, other test files, Go, native or E2E run. Regressions in this head:
  - Both `opencode` and `opencode-v2` go through two inactive catalog-event/remount cycles. The test asserts the query is still marked invalidated before the second event and that each event triggers a fresh read. An older read that settles before the replacement must keep it shared; one that settles after must not overwrite the query data or the saved snapshot.
  - For both IDs: a failed read, then one catalog event between unmount and remount.
  - For both IDs: an observerless `prefetchQuery` starts while the query is already invalidated. **New in this head:** a generic resync evicts the read, then a catalog change arrives during its GET. The test asserts there is no active fetch, that a second GET follows, and that the seed stays until the post-event catalog is published and saved.
  - **New in this head:** two already-invalidated observerless prefetches (`opencode`, `opencode-v2`) are evicted by a generic resync, then a catalog change arrives for `opencode` only. Only `opencode` re-reads and saves the new catalog; `opencode-v2` publishes its own read; 3 GETs in total.
  - For both IDs, a slow read outlasts six fallback polls. The first poll's invalidate event restarts it once; later polls must not. It must publish and save after 2 GETs.
  - Transport:
    - A second catalog event that only marks the running refresh dirty still restarts pending reads before the early return; the catch-up only evicts.
    - Remote fallback polling evicts on each 2 s poll without restarting reads.
    - **New in this head:** a generic remote event does not restart reads. A remote typed `model_catalog` event restarts exactly `["agent-models", "box-a", "opencode"]` and nothing on `box-b`, while the generic eviction still runs.
- **Remote CI on the pre-rebase head `335b446a17`: all 29 checks passed.** Frontend passed 9/9 jobs (`typecheck`, all four Vitest shards, `checks`, renderer smoke, `test`, `mac-update-helper`); the shard logs show `useAgentModelsQuery.test.ts` 43 and `lib/event-transport.test.ts` 52 passed. Go passed 15/15, including `windows-workspace`. CLI E2E passed 4/4 and gitleaks 1/1.
- **AO native review:** approved for the pre-rebase head `335b446a17`. It is an internal static review, not a GitHub approval, and does not satisfy branch protection.

title: fix(desktop): reach the daemon with Node fetch from the main process
body:
## Problem

Since #7077, the daemon refuses any request that carries browser fetch metadata (`Sec-Fetch-Site`) without an allowlisted `Origin`. Electron's main-process `net.fetch` uses Chromium's network stack and sends `Sec-Fetch-Site: none` / `Sec-Fetch-Mode: no-cors` with no `Origin`, so these main-process daemon calls get `403 ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN` ("Origin is not allowed to access this daemon"):

- `fetchDesktopSessionPath`: **Show in Finder / Show in Terminal** for artifacts, the artifacts-folder buttons, and the workspace **Open in…** menu (editors, Finder, terminals)
- `TelemetryIdentityController`: analytics opt-out and AO Cloud user hand-off
- `createAwakeDownloadBridge`: awake-download requests

## Fix

Use Node's `fetch` for these three calls. It sends no fetch metadata, so the daemon treats it as a native client. The daemon health probe already does this (#6525). The daemon's boundary from #7077 is unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestBrowserBoundaryElectron` (real Electron 44 against the Go router; runs in frontend CI): the fixture now checks from the Electron main process that Node `fetch` gets 200 and `net.fetch` gets 403. Passes locally on macOS.
- `vitest`: `telemetry-identity`, `awake-download-bridge`, and `editor-handoff` (96 tests) pass.
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in frontend sources. Errors remain only in `packages/product-ui`, whose dependencies weren't installed locally.

## Risks / notes

- The fixture checks the transport contract, not `main.ts` wiring directly. If a `net.fetch` daemon call is reintroduced, the fixture won't catch it, but its 403 assertion documents why it must not be used.
- I did not do a manual click-through in the packaged app.

Refs #7077

title: perf(desktop): batch session row refreshes and share startup snapshot
body:
Code changes: +232 -24  
Tests: +434 -91  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

**INCOMPLETE DRAFT: review source fixes and regressions pass current-head remote CI; fresh native review, complete local validation, and desktop performance measurements remain pending.**

Batch unique id-only session updates over 150 ms. Read and patch up to three session rows; larger bursts retain the five-second throttled list fallback. Each row has one in-flight request and one queued catch-up. Failed or unpatchable reads return to the list fallback. Small batches also refresh usage and SCM summary caches, which do not poll locally.

The shared row patch preserves optimistic kills, handles project and standalone rows, respects active-only archive membership, and updates existing direct-session detail cache entries from the same response. Small batches also invalidate archive views.

Fixes #7264.

## Why

Id-only usage updates currently refresh every session. The source also contains a forced fresh shell-mount fetch after its loader has already read the workspace list. The transport then opens after that snapshot and needs another refresh to cover the gap. This is source diagnosis, not a measured desktop network result.

## How

Start the app-owned event transport before route loading. The loader waits up to one second for SSE readiness before taking its snapshot; initial shell mount reuses the fresh loader result. Events arriving while the initial inactive REST snapshot is in flight wait for that read and queue a catch-up; startup without an event still reads once. Later daemon transitions and reconnects retain their catch-up refreshes. If SSE misses the readiness timeout, REST startup proceeds and a later stream open still refreshes the gap; this fallback can legitimately read the list again.

Workspace polling has a single hook-owned clock, independent of row-cache writes. It retains the normal 15-second fallback for changes without CDC (such as project names), switches to 300 ms while statuses are checking, and stops when disabled.

Scope is 12 frontend implementation/test files. No daemon/API changes, archive UI, or conversation refresh changes are included. The helper contract is `patchWorkspaceSession(QueryClient, ControllersSessionView): boolean` in `hooks/useWorkspaceQuery.ts`. Coordinated additive boundaries with #7262, #7263, and #7265; this PR targets main and does not import their unmerged code.

Neither fixture is a real-agent or native network benchmark.

title: perf(chat): load settled activity details on demand
body:
Code changes: +433 -24  
Tests: +638 -4  
Others: +258 -0

## What

Load settled activity bodies on expansion through a dedicated full-activity endpoint, with opt-in compact conversation pages and conservative duplicate omission.

## Why

Conversation pages eagerly shipped multi-megabyte tool bodies hidden behind collapsed rows. Keep essential navigation metadata complete while deferring those bodies until needed. Fixes #7260.

## Before / After

Numeric measurements below are from prior head `927a06ccd4fccda912d840c70078ff7c173a0484`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Pages include complete settled command/MCP/file/reasoning bodies even when rows are collapsed. | With both opt-in flags, body strings use UTF-8-safe 128-byte previews, progress retains its tail, and essential navigation paths stay complete. |
| Large command/MCP bodies can repeat in two fields. | Proven duplicate bodies are omitted with explicit source markers. |
| Expansion already has full bodies from the page. | An omitted body is fetched as one full stored activity and cached by host/session/id/revision; previews never render as full images. |
| **Measured prior-927 synthetic fixture:** 11,838,126 response bytes. | **Measured prior-927 fixture:** 989 response bytes; target <65,536 bytes. New-head bytes are not measured. |

Real-desktop before/after captures are not available.

## How

- `compactDetails=1` previews only settled command, MCP, file-change, and reasoning detail strings; progress keeps its tail. Essential navigation addresses (`detail.cwd` and file-change `files[].path`/`oldPath`) remain whole for collapsed turn-level file links. System content, running/pending rows, approvals, and input requests stay whole.
- `dedupeBodies=1` removes only provable large-string copies and records their source fields. Full-row reads preserve retained bodies and are scoped to the session's active lineage and context-reset boundary.
- `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/conversation/activities/{activityId}` returns exactly one full activity; it does not use message-counted pagination.
- The client opts into both flags, waits for full detail before mounting expanded bodies (including image data), and caches by host/session/id/revision with 64 entries per mounted chat. Visible reasoning uses the same path. Old daemons ignore flags and send rows without omission markers, so no new endpoint read is needed.
- Incremental reads use both compact flags. Explicit full-output reads omit them. Grouped activities and AO tool summaries fetch full details on expansion.

## Testing

Rebased onto `main` at `3cb3366d20c45257798898ef514995e979e317ed`. API and sqlc files were regenerated. All eight locales preserve every base key and value.

- Passed: 134 focused frontend tests; focused Go regressions; both frontend typechecks with Node 24; Go build and vet; API/sqlc generation with no drift; locale preservation checks.
- Passed with the race detector: HTTP controllers, API-spec packages, SQLite store, and the isolated CLI suite. The four-file frontend rerun covering ChatWorkspace, ChatMarkdown, remote SessionView, and browser-profile imports exited successfully after preparing the native SQLite dependency.
- The complete Go race run did not pass. Installed OpenCode discovery and version-selection tests failed; terminal and HTTP tests had failures or timeouts; chat, session-manager, and SQLite suites reached the 10-minute local timeout. Removing inherited session settings fixed the CLI and PTY failures, but terminal and HTTP timing failures remained.
- The broader CI-selected frontend run was stopped after native-dependency and timing failures under heavy host load. The full frontend suite is not verified. Lint reported zero issues but exited on timeout, so it is not a pass.
- Linux container fresh-install, tagged CLI E2E, Electron boundary, browser postcondition, and renderer smoke jobs were not run locally. The shared host could not complete the broader validation reliably.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/43183745649) passed its gate, but skipped the test lanes because this PR is draft. The separate secret scan and check jobs passed. GitHub reports this head as mergeable.

The endpoint restores data retained in storage. It cannot reconstruct images stripped by an adapter before storage. Native desktop captures and real-database performance measurements remain unavailable.

## Checklist

- [x] Fixes #7260 with compact pages and full activity reads.
- [x] Regression tests cover body budgets, cache isolation, images, navigation metadata, grouped details, and incremental page flags.
- [ ] Real-desktop before/after captures.
- [ ] Real-database performance measurements.

The PR remains draft.

title: perf(mobile): load faster and stay usable on slow networks
body:
Code changes: +407 -195  
Tests: +540 -146  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

On a slow link the phone app makes too many serial round trips. It replays the whole event backlog on resume. It reloads a chat page once per event while an agent streams. And it treats a slow download as an unreachable host, which triggers a re-race and a full reload. This PR fixes those paths in `packages/mobile` only. There are no daemon or API changes, and it works against older daemons.

The rule for this PR: in every scenario, behaviour must be equal to or better than `main` for latency, staleness, missed updates and failed auth attempts. The Risks table lists each scenario against `main`, including the two that are still worse.

## Changes

**Board poll** (`api.ts getSessions`, `store.tsx`, `otherHosts.ts`)
- `/sessions` still goes first, alone. `/orchestrators`, `/projects` and the unread count go out as soon as the `/sessions` headers accept the credential (2xx or 304), without waiting for its body. A tick is 2 serial steps instead of 3, and a bad credential still costs exactly 1 failed attempt per tick, on every daemon version. There is no remembered "accepted credential" any more.
- The board publishes without waiting for the unread count. The badge updates when `/notifications` answers, as on `main`.
- The next tick waits as long as this tick's requests would have taken one after another (each measured on its own). So ticks per minute are never above `main`'s, while each board arrives sooner.
- On an older daemon, the unfiltered `/sessions` already holds the orchestrators, so `/orchestrators` is skipped there.
- Other paired machines poll at the same rate as on `main` (8 s direct, 2 s tunnel), with the same batching and pacing.

**Revalidation** (`api.ts req`, moved here from #7281)
- GETs keep the last body and ETag per URL and send `If-None-Match`. A 304 is handed to callers as the cached 200 body. Daemons without ETags behave as before. With #7281's daemon side, an unchanged board poll downloads only headers.

**Timeouts** (`api.ts req`)
- A request fails at the later of: 12 s from the start (or the caller's own timeout), as on `main`; or 8 s after the last body byte of a successful response. A slow body that keeps arriving is never cut off, so it is no longer reported as unreachable (which re-raced and reloaded everything). There is no overall cap.
- 8 s outlasts 2-3 back-to-back TCP retransmission timeouts on a phone (about 1 s, then doubling).
- Error responses, and a fetch without a readable body, keep the plain timeout.
- The streamed body is decoded with `String.fromCharCode` plus `decodeURIComponent` on non-ASCII runs (native string code), instead of Expo's JS `TextDecoder` loop.

**Event stream on resume** (`chat/conversationEvents.ts`, `chat/useConversation.ts`)
- Every stream start (launch, resume, new endpoint) opens at head. There is no backlog replay, and the persisted cursor is gone (old keys are still removed on unpair). Reconnects within one start resume from the in-memory cursor.
- An opening chat loads once its machine's stream is open, not before. The daemon fixes the head before it answers, so that load holds every change up to the head, and the stream delivers every change after it: one load, no replay, no gap.
- If the stream's first attempt fails, or it has not opened within 5 s, the chat loads anyway (as on `main`) and reloads once when the stream opens. While the stream is already open, for example when moving between screens, a chat loads at once.

**Chat page loads** (`chat/useConversation.ts`)
- Event-driven reloads coalesce: one load in flight plus one queued follow-up. An explicit refresh aborts the superseded download.
- On a tunnel, the chat poll starts a load at most 2 s after the previous load, whatever started it. Loads that events already started save polls; a page is never older than with `main`'s fixed 2 s interval.

**Connect** (`connect.ts`, `hosts.ts`)
- `GET /endpoints` no longer blocks connect. The first board load overlaps it. The merge runs inside the storage write, against the endpoints stored at that moment.

## Measurements

Modeled from payload sizes in a copy of a real AO database. The 3G **model** is 400 ms RTT and a 50 KB/s shared link. It was not measured on a radio.

| Scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Board refresh, 3G model | 3 serial steps, ~2.0 s | 2 serial steps, ~1.2 s |
| Board ticks per minute (2 s tunnel, 3G model) | 14.9 | ≤ 14.9 (13.5 by the pacing rule) |
| Connect → first board, 3G model | `/endpoints` then board, ~2.4 s | board ∥ `/endpoints`, ~1.2 s |
| Resume after 1 h | 952 KB SSE replay, ~19 s | 388 B |
| Resume after 8 h | 5.7 MB, ~115 s | 388 B |
| Resume with a chat open | replay + 1 page load | 1 page load, no replay |
| Agent streaming into a 311 KB chat: event → screen | 156 s mean (375 s max) | 8.8 s (13.2 s max) |
| Agent streaming into an 89 KB chat: event → screen | 13.0 s mean | 2.8 s mean |
| Unchanged board poll, daemon with #7281 | full bodies (41.7 KB) | headers only |
| Decode of a 2.2 MB body, Hermes 0.12 CLI / V8 | native `text()`: not measurable in Hermes / 1.2-1.5 ms | 20 ms / 6-7 ms (Expo's `TextDecoder`: 31-33 ms / 6-8 ms) |

## Compatibility

- Old daemons: no ETag means plain 200s. An unfiltered `/sessions` means `/orchestrators` is skipped. A missing `/notifications` gives no unread count.
- No wire or API change. The `If-None-Match` header is ignored by daemons without #7281.

## Risks

| Scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Failed auth attempts per tick with a dead credential (any host) | 1 | 1. The rest of the board is sent only after `/sessions` accepted this tick's credential. |
| Board staleness | 3 serial steps, then the interval | Board lands sooner. Period is set by the measured serial time, which errs long under contention by at most the small requests' transfer time (~0.2 s on 3G). A tick still lands a round trip or more earlier, so the oldest board on screen is younger than on `main`. |
| Board data per minute | baseline | ≤ `main` |
| Other machines' rows | 8 s direct / 2 s tunnel | same rate |
| Tunnel chat poll | a load every 2 s | a load at most 2 s after the previous load |
| Resume: bytes | whole backlog since backgrounding + 1 page load | 1 page load |
| **Resume with a chat open: when the load starts (later than `main`)** | at once, competing with the replay | after the board's first poll and the stream's open (1 RTT more), at most 5 s. On a fast link that is tens of ms later than `main`. On a slow link the replay `main` downloads alongside makes `main` finish later anyway (bench: 7.9 s on weak 4G). The cached page stays on screen meanwhile. |
| Resume with a chat open: changes missed | none (replay) | none: the load starts after the head is fixed, later changes arrive as events |
| Stream fails to open | chat loads at once | chat loads at once, plus one reload when the stream opens later |
| Slow but alive body | fails at 12 s, then re-race + full reload | never fails while bytes keep arriving |
| Dead download | detected 12 s after the start | same, **except** if bytes arrived in the 8 s before the 12 s mark: then up to 8 s later. `main` would have failed that download at 12 s even if it was alive. |
| **CPU to decode a body (worse than `main`)** | native `text()` | JS decoding, about 9 ms/MB in Hermes 0.12 on an M-series Mac (more on a low-end phone). Reason: the native `text()` reports no progress, so stall detection needs the stream. Coalescing cuts the number of page loads while an agent streams (143 → 46-109 in 5 min), so total decode work there is lower than `main`'s. Not measured on a device. |
| **Event during an in-flight chat load (worse than `main` in one corner)** | starts another load at once | queued until the current load lands. On a bandwidth-bound link that lands about when a concurrent load would. On a latency-bound link it can be up to one page-load time later. In exchange, a streaming agent no longer starves the page (156 s → 8.8 s mean above). |
| Endpoint refresh | finished before connect returned | runs in the background. Right after connect, the endpoint list used to explain a failure can be the previous one until the next resolution. The next race reads storage fresh. |

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) passes. `npm test` (vitest, `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`) passes: 245 files, 2523 tests.
- New or changed tests:
  - `chatModeApi.test.ts`: the rest of the board is sent after the `/sessions` headers, before its body; a rejected credential sends nothing else on every tick; the board does not wait for `/notifications`; poll pacing; a real stream with cursor and heartbeat frames.
  - `api.request-lifecycle.test.ts`: no timeout sooner than 12 s; stall after the last byte; a body that keeps arriving for 10 minutes; no-body responses keep the plain timeout; UTF-8 split across chunks and invalid bytes; ETag revalidation; every board request cancels with its lifecycle.
  - `conversationEvents.test.tsx`: opens at head with a chat open and no stored cursor read; open/failed/stopped stream state; reconnect resumes from the in-memory cursor and stays open.
  - `useConversation.refresh.test.tsx`: coalescing, abort on explicit refresh, tunnel poll timed from the last load; one load after the stream opens and an event after it reloads once; a stream that fails to open loads at once and reloads once when it opens; the 5 s fallback.
  - `connect.test.ts`, `hosts.test.ts`: endpoint merge against the stored list.
- Under the `en_IN` locale, the existing `conversationChrome.test.ts` fails on number formatting. This PR does not touch it.
- Not run locally: the other CI jobs. CI will cover them.

## Related

The daemon side of slow-network loading comes in separate PRs: gzip JSON, ETag/304 on polled lists (#7281), fixing the idle `session_updated` churn, and counting repeated attempts with the same wrong password once (#7285). The mobile `If-None-Match` commit now lives in this PR, not #7281.

title: fix(chat): resume a replacement orchestrator after a restart
body:
## What Changing a project's orchestrator agent and then restarting AO no longer leaves the new orchestrator stuck on "The agent controller stopped". A resume that can never succeed now answers 409 with a readable message instead of a 500 "Internal server error". ## Why Two user reports on 0.14.3 (Linux and Windows) describe the orchestrator showing "The agent controller stopped" with "Internal server error" on every Resume click. Both happened after switching the orchestrator agent (OpenCode and Codex; Claude Code and Codex) and restarting. Related: #7123 (fixed by #7124), #6560, #5513, #5922, #6606. #7124 gives a replacement orchestrator its own provider boundary, so new replacements no longer hit the handle mismatch. Two gaps remained: 1. **Unprompted replacement.** If nobody wrote to the new orchestrator before the restart, its provider never saved the thread: Codex writes no rollout before the first message, and Claude Code writes no transcript. Every Resume after the restart failed with `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED`. The "never started" proof that permits a fresh start only covered a root branch, and since #7124 a replacement runs on its own child boundary. 2. **Already broken orchestrators.** Sessions that broke before #7124 still fail the active-branch vs session handle check. That error was unmapped, so it surfaced as a bare 500. ## How - `service/chat/service.go`: `switchBranchUnanswered` becomes `branchUnanswered`. Besides agent-switch branches, it accepts a provider boundary the session reserved for itself that never had a turn. Resume then sets `FreshIfMissing`, so the provider starts fresh in place only when it reports the stored thread missing, and `rebindBranchOnReady` moves the branch to the fresh thread. A boundary that answered a turn is unaffected. - The handle mismatch now wraps `ports.ErrChatResumeFailed`, which maps to 409 `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED`. - `service/chat/history.go`: restoring a source controller after a failed native edit uses the same rule. ## Evidence **Setup:** - The dev Electron app runs from this branch and from `origin/main`. Each points at a trimmed copy of a real AO database: one project, a cloned repo, and an isolated data dir. - The agents are real Claude Code and Codex. - "Restart" means a cold restart: the daemon and every agent process are killed, then the app is relaunched. | Flow | `main` | This branch | |---|---|---| | Change the orchestrator agent to Codex, send nothing, restart, Resume | Stuck: 409 "could not resume", every click
| Resumed (200), then answered a prompt
| | Orchestrator that broke before #7124, Resume | 500 "Internal server error"
| 409 with a readable message
| Also on this branch: - **Claude Code replacement:** works both unprompted and prompted, across cold restarts. - **Orchestrator broken before #7124:** recovers after one agent change plus a restart.
Daemon log excerpt ``` # main, orchestrator broken before #7124 reconcile: live pass failed sessionID=todo-app-11 retrying=false error="check session todo-app-11: resume chat: active conversation branch provider handle \"75de4916-…\" does not match session handle \"f3701a0e-…\"" POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/resume-agent status=500 (x3) # this branch, same database reconcile: live pass failed sessionID=todo-app-11 retrying=false error="check session todo-app-11: resume chat: chat conversation resume failed: active conversation branch provider handle \"75de4916-…\" does not match session handle \"f3701a0e-…\"" POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/resume-agent status=409 (x3) # main, unprompted Codex replacement after a cold restart POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-10/resume-agent status=409 (x2, CHAT_RESUME_FAILED) # this branch, same flow on a fresh copy POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-10/resume-agent status=200 (Codex, unprompted) POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/resume-agent status=200 (Claude Code, unprompted) POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/resume-agent status=200 (Claude Code, prompted) POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-12/resume-agent status=200 (broken orchestrator replaced) ``` After the fresh start, the session and its active branch name the same new thread, so the next restart resumes it normally.
## Testing - `go test ./internal/service/chat/` passes locally (without `-race`). - New: `TestUnansweredReplacementOrchestratorStartsFreshAfterRestart`. It fails without this change with "resumed provider conversation handle … does not match requested handle". - `TestReplacementOrchestratorFirstStartReservesBoundaryForInheritedThread` now also asserts that a boundary which answered a turn never starts fresh. - `TestOrdinaryResumeRejectsProviderHandleOutsideActiveBranch` asserts that the mismatch is `ErrChatResumeFailed`. ## Not in this PR - Orchestrators that broke before #7124 are not repaired automatically.
