## What

Related to #7262. Fetch durable live-conversation deltas and merge by row ID/revision while retaining loaded history. **Draft: corrected head `0fc2223fad6e9334b6d9e4220ad0b110ead1f187` has approved fresh internal code review and all29 current CI checks successful after one targeted remote rerun; desktop/real-agent measurements remain incomplete. Keep the issue open.**

## Why

Conversation events previously invalidated every loaded infinite-query page. Mutable settled rows also require a durable write cursor; timeline sequence alone cannot identify their rewrites.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Source audit: each open-chat change invalidated the whole infinite query. | An opted-in marked delta updates one live page and preserves loaded history. The synthetic store fixture serializes **1,650 bytes** for its full page versus **1,375 bytes** for its changed-row delta; these are measured fixture JSON sizes, not real event/network results. |
| Source audit: sequence-only delta filtering hid a promoted batched prompt even though a full snapshot retained it. | Real SQLite regression verifies marked `afterSequence=11` and `12` responses, without `afterChange`, equal the corresponding fresh-snapshot messages after batch dispatch. |
| Source audit: an old delta could trigger a refetch during a pending model choice and restore stale settings. | Regression holds model B's PATCH open, resolves an old model-A delta, then verifies the effort PATCH retains model B without an interim refetch; latest mutation settlement still refreshes. |
| A rejected delta bypassed the settings guard via transport invalidation; a session-specific mutation key also lost its pending indicator during navigation (observed CI failure on `4614703bcb`). | Real transport rejection and resolved/rejected model/effort regressions preserve optimistic B; the unchanged settings-navigation regression passes with a host-stable mutation key filtered by target session. |
| Pagination could commit pre-delta pages after the final live event. | Real infinite-query observer regressions cover both completion orders and retain the final row/revision/text and older history. |

No visual layout change is introduced. The timing-sensitive picker/desktop flows still lack real-app before/after recordings; synthetic regressions are not substitutes, and this acceptance gap remains open.

## How

- SQLite triggers maintain a durable indexed per-row change cursor for messages, activities, and turns, including settled rewrites. A new migration leaves shipped migrations intact.
- Newest-page `afterSequence` is inclusive; optional `afterChange` is exclusive. A matching response echo marks a complete delta. Coverage limits, removals/resets, unsupported responses, cache absence, and conversation/branch/visibility changes retain full-refresh fallback.
- Per-chat single-flight refreshes merge highest revisions by ID, retain earlier pages, wait for concurrent pagination writes, and defer reads/fallbacks, including GET errors, while settings mutations own optimistic state. The transport never adds an unguarded error invalidation. A host-stable mutation key retains navigation state while a target-session predicate scopes coordination. Mutation settlement catches up normally.
- Delta visibility now matches main's batched-source predicate. Genuine pinned sqlc regeneration also incorporates main's `batched_input` / `provider_input_text` turn fields.
- Compact-body (#7260), registration (#7263), and workspace batching (#7264) remain independent work with additive interfaces; no neighbor source or stack was imported.

The server still reads the bounded newest page for metadata; no server CPU/read reduction or measured write-overhead claim is made.

title: feat(artifacts): preview PDF, CSV/TSV and Mermaid artifacts
body:
## Summary

Adds previews for artifact types that currently fall through to the binary placeholder or raw source.

### PDF
- PDF artifacts (and binary PDFs in the workspace Files view) render with pdf.js, which is lazy-loaded on first use: a separate chunk plus its worker asset.
- Pages fit the pane width (up to 2×) and draw as they scroll near the viewport.
- Each page has a pdf.js text layer, so selected text opens the existing artifact feedback composer, the same as rendered markdown. Whole-file feedback from the toolbar keeps working.
- Cloud-session PDFs keep the binary placeholder: the cloud control-plane bridge only carries text bodies, and CSP `connect-src` doesn't allow direct control-plane fetches.

### CSV/TSV
- `.csv`/`.tsv` files get a rendered table view (shadcn `Table`). The first row is the header, ragged rows are padded, and numeric columns right-align with tabular figures.
- Clicking a header cycles the sort: ascending, descending, then file order (numeric-aware collation, `aria-sort` set).
- Text selected in the table opens the artifact feedback composer.
- Parser: `lib/delimited-text.ts` handles quoted fields with delimiters, newlines and `""`, plus CRLF and a BOM.

### Mermaid (`.mmd`, `.mermaid`)
- Rendered through the shared `MermaidBlock` (strict mode + DOMPurify, theme-aware, source toggle).
- Cloud sessions now read `.mmd`/`.mermaid` artifacts as text so they can render.

CSV/TSV and Mermaid artifacts open in rendered mode by default, like markdown and SVG. In the workspace Files view they gain a Rendered toggle.

## Tests
- `ArtifactFileView.test.tsx`: a PDF artifact renders its pages, and text selected on a page is sent as feedback with the quote and path.
- `FileMediaPreview.test.tsx`: a PDF that fails to load shows Retry.
- `ArtifactFileView.test.tsx`: a CSV opens as a table and sorts by a clicked column; a selected cell is sent as feedback; a `.mmd` file renders as a diagram.
- `delimited-text.test.ts`: quoting, CRLF, TSV, BOM, empty file.
- Typecheck clean; related artifact/file suites pass.
- Ran the real pdf.js calls the component makes (`getDocument`, `page.render`, `TextLayer`, worker) in headless Chromium against a real PDF: the canvas draws, text is extracted, and a mouse drag selects the expected line.

## Risks / follow-ups
- New dependency: `pdfjs-dist@^6.4.299`. The lockfile diff is limited to it and its optional `@napi-rs/canvas` binaries.
- PDF memory: pages far from the viewport release their canvas, text layer and parsed page data, and a PDF over 100 MiB isn't read (it shows the file-size message instead).
- Follow-ups (not in this PR):
  - Standard-font, CMap and wasm decoder assets aren't bundled, so PDFs with non-embedded or CJK fonts render with substitute fonts, and JBIG2/JPX images may not render.
  - A modified PDF in a diff shows only the current file, with no before/after view like images have.
- Table rendering is not virtualized; artifact reads are capped at 256 KiB, which bounds row count.
- New i18n key `files.emptyTable`, added to all locales.
- Not yet clicked through in the packaged Electron app.

title: fix(usage): stop idle usage bindings from emitting session_updated every pass
body:
Code changes: +85 -13\
Tests: +223 -3\
Others: +18 -4

## What

Stops usage binding writes that change nothing, and stops re-ingesting conflicted transcripts that haven't changed. An idle daemon no longer emits a `session_updated` event on every reconcile pass.

## Why

An idle daemon kept writing `usage_bindings` rows. The `usage_bindings_cdc_update` trigger turns each write into a `session_updated` event, and every connected client refetches on those events. On a real database this loop made 43% of the last 10k `change_log` rows.

This PR stops the writes at the writer, with no migration.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Idle reconciliations rewrite unchanged bindings and emit `session_updated` | The SQL writer skips writes that change neither state nor error code |
| A conflicted transcript is re-read and re-marked on every pass | It is skipped while its file size and modification time are unchanged |
| A conflicted transcript corrected in place stays quarantined | A changed file is ingested again and can recover |
| Discovery rotates through bindings only because of the no-op writes | Discovery pages by id with a cursor and wraps around |

## How

- `queries/usage.sql` `UpdateUsageBinding`: a WHERE guard writes only when the state or error code would actually change. It mirrors the SET clause, including the sticky `codex_source_budget_exceeded` code. sqlc regenerated with the pinned v1.31.1.
- `observe/usage/ingestor.go`:
  - A `complete` source with `source_event_conflict` is skipped while its saved file size and modification time still match and its binding is not finalizing.
  - Identity changes, truncation and checkpoint mismatches are checked before that skip, so a rewritten transcript still gets a new generation.
  - The conflict snapshot is saved at the original cursor through `ApplyUsageChunk`, with the same revision check as a normal chunk. It writes no events, so it does not touch the binding.
  - A conflict no longer schedules the finalization retry, since retrying an unchanged file cannot resolve it.
- `ListUsageDiscoveryBindings` now pages by `id` with an `after_id` cursor. `Collector` keeps the cursor in memory and wraps around to the start. The old `ORDER BY updated_at` rotation only advanced because of the no-op writes, so without this change discovery would stay on the same first 64 bindings. A negative limit visits every eligible binding from id 0 and resets the cursor.
- No trigger migration: a trigger cannot tell a no-op reconcile write from `TouchUsageBinding`, which is the real "new usage landed" signal.

## Measurements

Two sandboxed daemons ran side by side on copies of a real DB, over a 4 min window starting 2 min after start-up. Before = main at the time (`e81912c11a`).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `change_log` rows/min (all) | 130.5 | 23.2 |
| rows/min excluding the 2 live sessions | 101.5 | **0.0** |
| looping session rows/min | 56.5 | **0** |
| reconcile no-op rows/min | ~45 | 0 |
| start-up burst (first 90 s) | 328 | 192 |

The two remaining sessions had transcripts that really grew during the run.

The desktop renderer already limits these id-only `session_updated` events to one workspace refresh every 5 s (#6763). An idle desktop goes from up to ~12 of those refreshes a minute to about none. Clients on slow or remote links save more per refresh.

This does not lower usage-pipeline CPU. Reconcile still runs every 30 s and still does discovery work; it just stops writing.

## Testing

- `TestIngestorConflictedSourceLeavesSettledBindingAlone`: fails on main. It rebuilds the ingestor between passes to check that the snapshot persists.
- `TestIngestorCorrectedConflictCanRecover`: same-size corrections, appended events, and a committed prefix.
- `TestCollectorReconcileLeavesUnchangedBindingsAlone`: fails without the SQL guard.
- `TestCollectorUnlimitedPassIncludesEarlierBinding`: a bounded pass followed by an unlimited one.
- `TestCollectorDiscoveryLimitRotatesPendingBindings`: now runs a third `limit=1` pass that has to wrap to the first binding. It fails with the wrap disabled.

Focused runs, all passing:

```
go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/store/ -run 'Usage|Kimi'
go test ./internal/service/usage/ -run 'Collector|Reconcile|Binding|Finalize|Reactivate|Continuation|Budget'
go test ./internal/observe/usage/ -run 'Ingest|Coordinator|Codex|Pipeline|Conflict'
```

Broad checks (`go vet`, golangci-lint, full `go test ./...`) are left to CI.

## Compatibility

- No wire or schema change.
- `UpdateUsageBindingState` / `UpdateUsageBindingErrorCode` now return false for writes that change nothing. No caller reads that value.
- Parser state gains an optional `conflict_snapshot` field. An older daemon rejects unknown parser fields, so after a downgrade it cannot decode sources stuck in a conflict. #4160 and #4168 added parser fields the same way.

## Risks

- Discovery order changes from "least recently updated" to round-robin by id. Every eligible binding is still visited within ceil(N/64) passes. The cursor resets on restart.
- Conflict suppression keys on file size and modification time. On a filesystem with one-second timestamps, a same-size correction within the same second stays skipped until the file changes again. APFS and ext4 record nanoseconds.
- Conflicted sources written before this change have no snapshot. Each is re-evaluated once to save one.
- Not fixed here: exited sessions keep `finalizing` bindings that never settle, so the 30 s reconcile poll keeps running. It no longer writes, but it still does discovery work. Repeated transcript discovery is a separate issue.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing the existing PR branch, based on `main`
- [x] One focused change to usage ingestion and discovery
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions
- [x] Regression tests added for the no-op writes, conflict recovery, unlimited discovery and wraparound
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go` jobs pending)

title: feat(httpd): gzip JSON responses over 1 KB for clients that accept it
body:
Code changes: +152 -2  
Tests: +150 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary
The daemon sent every JSON body uncompressed. This adds a `compressJSON` middleware: gzip at BestSpeed for JSON responses of 1 KB or more, only when the client accepts gzip. Mobile and the desktop remote path (HTTP/2 inside a WebSocket, where edge compression cannot help) gain the most.

## Changes
- `httpd/compress.go` (new): the middleware.
  - It compresses only when all of these hold: `Accept-Encoding` admits gzip (`q=0` counts as a refusal); no HEAD, `Range` or `Upgrade` (WebSockets and the terminal mux are skipped); not a preview or agent-browser route (those keep their own gzip); the response is `application/json` with no `Content-Encoding` already set; the body reaches 1 KB.
  - It sets `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, uses pooled writers, and keeps `Flush` and `Unwrap` working. SSE (`text/event-stream`) is never compressed.
- `httpd/router.go`: mounts it after `previewOriginMiddleware`.
- `controllers/sessions.go`: exports `AcceptsGzip`, so both gzip paths share one Accept-Encoding parser.
- The LAN listener, cloudflared/Tailscale and the `/api/v1/tunnel` path all use the same router, so they are compressed per response.

## Measurements (measured)
Loopback, httpx, sandboxed daemons on a copy of a real DB, median of 15-50.

| path | before wire | after wire (gzip) | after server time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| /api/v1/sessions | 72,152 B | **10,138 B** (7.1x) | 5.6 ms (5.8 ms identity) |
| biggest chat /conversation | 1,019,845 B | **156,799 B** (6.5x) | 13.2 ms (10.0 ms identity) |
| /api/v1/agents/readiness | 29,877 B | 4,465 B (6.7x) | 3.6 ms |
| /api/v1/projects (886 B) | 886 B | 886 B (below 1 KB) | 0.7 ms |

- Modeled at 50 KB/s: the biggest page goes from about 20 s to 3.1 s, and `/sessions` from 1.4 s to 0.2 s.
- Level choice: BestSpeed costs about +3 ms on a 1 MB page, and its output is about 19% larger than level 6. Full table in the commit notes.

## Compatibility
- Only clients that send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` get gzip. Renderer (Chromium), Electron main `fetch`, the Go CLI and RN fetch all decode it.
- Raw `node:http` / `http2` calls in `remote-proxy.ts` send no Accept-Encoding, so they still get identity.

## Risks
- Loopback CPU: about +3 ms per 1 MB page for the local renderer, which gains nothing from fewer bytes on loopback.
- A JSON handler that flushes before 1 KB is sent uncompressed.
- The preview exclusion is a path-prefix check.

## Testing
- New `TestCompressJSON` (7 cases), `TestCompressJSONLeavesEventStreamsStreaming` and `TestCompressJSONThroughTheLANTunnel`.
- `go test ./internal/httpd/ -run 'TestCompressJSON|TestLANTunnel|Events|TestServer|TestRouter'` and `./internal/httpd/controllers/ -run 'TestSessionsAPI_ManagedPreview|TestSessionsAPI_Preview'`: pass.
- Manual: SSE and the `/mux` WebSocket upgrade still work with `Accept-Encoding: gzip`.

Run locally:
- `go build ./...`; `go vet` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 on `./internal/httpd/...`: clean.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/httpd/...`: pass.
- `go test ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/integration/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/previewserver/... ./internal/mobilebridge/...`: pass, except `mobilebridge` `TestTunnelRunnerKeepsTheQuickTunnelUntilAReplacementIsMade`, which fails the same way on main locally.

## Review notes
- The Electron remote proxy (`frontend/src/main/remote-proxy.ts`) relays response bodies and `Content-Encoding` unchanged, so the renderer decodes them; the proxy's own identity probe sends no `Accept-Encoding` and stays uncompressed.
- `Range`, `HEAD`, upgrades and preview/agent-browser routes are skipped, so 206 responses and preview ETags are untouched.

title: perf(httpd): revalidate polled list reads with ETag/304 and refetch after opening Chat only on a wake
body:
Code changes: +73 -23  
Tests: +88 -31  
Others: +21 -5 (generated: openapi.yaml, schema.ts)

## Summary
Two fixes for repeated downloads:
- Polled list reads (`/sessions`, `/orchestrators`, `/projects`, `/notifications`, `/settings`) now answer with a weak ETag and `304` when nothing changed.
- `POST /sessions/{id}/chat-view` now says whether it woke the agent. Desktop refetches the board and conversation after opening Chat only on a wake.

Mobile revalidation (`If-None-Match` on the mobile board poll) ships separately in #7275.

## Changes
- `envelope.WriteRevalidatedJSON`:
  - The ETag is a hash of the encoded body, so it is exact by construction, including read-time derived fields.
  - It sends `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and answers a matching `If-None-Match` (weak compare, lists, `*`) with a bodyless `304`.
  - It is used by the five list controllers.
- `chat.Service.SetChatView` returns `(woke, err)`. The route answers `200 {"woke": bool}` instead of `204` (dto + specgen; openapi.yaml and schema.ts regenerated).
- `SessionView.tsx`: after the chat-view registration, refresh only when `data?.woke ?? true`.
  - An older daemon (204) keeps today's behaviour.
  - Inside that, #7165's rule still applies: a ready or busy cached chat is not reloaded.
  - The board refetch now also waits for a wake.
- Desktop needs no client code for the ETag. Chromium stores `no-cache` + ETag responses and revalidates them itself. This was checked in real Electron: `200 72374 B`, then `304 0 B`.

## Measurements (measured, before #7165 landed)
Real renderer in headless Chrome, sandboxed daemon, copy of a real DB, against e81912c11a. #7165 has since removed the second conversation fetch on open for ready chats, so the conversation column now overlaps with it. The list-byte savings are this PR's alone.

| run | boot list bytes | open: list bytes | open: conversation reqs / bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| warm, before | 368,525 | 221,115 | 2 / 2,040,156 |
| warm, after | 76,180 | 928 | 1 / 1,020,078 |
| cold, before | 294,820-442,236 | 221,115 | 2 / 2,040,156 |
| cold, after | 75,254-149,100 | 928-1,392 | 1 / 1,020,078 |

- An unchanged list fetch is now 232 B of headers. Server time for `/sessions` stays about 6 ms either way.
- Mobile board poll with #7275's `If-None-Match`, 8 ticks at 2 s: body bytes went from 333,931 to 41,729 (28 of 32 were 304s).

## Compatibility
- Old clients ignore the ETag and keep getting `200` bodies.
- The `204` → `200 {woke}` change: the desktop client treats a missing body as "refresh as before". Mobile does not read the response.

## Risks
- The server still builds the list in order to hash it. Only wire bytes go away.
- `woke` is true only when this call resumed a hibernated provider. Any other change still arrives through events.

## Testing
- `go test ./internal/httpd/envelope/ ./internal/service/chat/ -run 'TestWriteRevalidatedJSON|Hibernat|ChatView|VersionSwitch|Nudge'`, `./internal/httpd/controllers/ -run 'TestChatViewRoute|List|Project|Notification|Setting|Orchestrator'`, `./internal/session_manager/ -run 'Hibernated|Nudge'` and `./internal/httpd/apispec/...`: pass.
- vitest `SessionView.test.tsx` (270): pass.

Broad checks were not run locally, per the maintainer's standing preference: `go vet`, golangci-lint, full `go test ./...`, frontend `npm run typecheck`, full vitest, and e2e. CI covers them. On the stack tip only, `cd backend && go build ./...` and the renderer `vite build` both passed.

1. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7280 `perf/gzip-json-responses`: feat(httpd): gzip JSON responses over 1 KB for clients that accept it
2. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7281 `perf/session-list-etag`: perf(httpd): revalidate polled list reads with ETag/304 and refetch after opening Chat only on a wake ← this PR
3. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7282 `perf/lean-activity-previews`: perf(chat): send activity previews on conversation pages and load a row's full body when it opens
4. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7283 `perf/live-sync-deltas`: perf(chat): refresh only changed rows of live chats and poll only while the event stream is down

title: perf(chat): send activity previews on conversation pages and load a row's full body when it opens
body:
Code changes: +425 -47  
Tests: +369 -1  
Others: +231 -0 (generated: openapi.yaml, schema.ts, sqlc gen)

## Summary
Conversation pages carried every tool row's full body (command output, patches, inputs), even though only opened rows show them. With `?activityDetail=preview` the daemon sends settled tool rows as previews, and desktop fetches a row's full body when the user opens it. The default stays `full`, byte-identical to today.

## Changes
- **Daemon**
  - `controllers/conversation_activity_preview.go` (new):
    - Every row: a `rawCommand` equal to `detail.command` is dropped, and a summary equal to it is sent empty.
    - Settled `command` / `mcp_tool` / `file_change` / `auto_review` rows: long bodies keep a 300-byte head or are dropped, marked `detailOmitted` + `detailBytes`.
    - Running and pending rows and all other kinds are untouched.
  - `GET /sessions/{id}/conversation?activityDetail=full|preview`. An invalid value returns 400 `CONVERSATION_ACTIVITY_DETAIL_INVALID`.
  - The preview runs in the controller after `SnapshotPage`, so it covers #7165's message-based page, including rows pulled in by reach-back.
  - New `GET /sessions/{id}/conversation/activities/{activityId}` returns the full row (404 `CHAT_ACTIVITY_NOT_FOUND`).
  - `Service.Activity`, store `ConversationActivity`, new query `SelectConversationActivityByID` (sqlc regenerated), openapi.yaml and schema.ts regenerated.
- **Desktop**
  - The page fetch sends `activityDetail=preview`.
  - `FullActivityBody` mounts only inside an opened row body and reads the full row with `conversationActivityQueryOptions` (keyed by revision, `staleTime: Infinity`). It keeps the last full copy while a held-open row settles.
  - `ChatTimelineItems` command/file/MCP/auto-review bodies render from the full row, with loading and retry states. Headers still read the preview.
- **Mobile is not opted in.** It has its own expanded bodies and no query cache, so it stays on `full` with today's bytes.

## Measurements (measured)
Newest page, `limit=200`, sandboxed daemon on a copy of a real DB, gzip -6 computed locally.

| chat | full raw | preview raw | full gzip | preview gzip |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| del-video-2 (biggest) | 1,020 KB | 217 KB (4.7x) | 131 KB | 49 KB (2.7x) |
| del-video-5 | 687 KB | 156 KB (4.4x) | 104 KB | 34 KB (3.0x) |
| del-3 | 617 KB | 168 KB (3.7x) | 118 KB | 33 KB (3.6x) |

- All 66 chat first pages: 8,299 KB → 2,629 KB raw. Server time is unchanged.
- Opening a preview row costs one GET (about 0.7 ms server; median 7.7 KB).

These numbers were measured on the 200-row pages from before #7165. #7165's message-based pages carry more activity rows per page, so the share that previews remove is, if anything, larger.

## Compatibility

- A new desktop against an older daemon gets full rows. Rows without `detailOmitted` never call the activity route.

## Risks
- Anything that reads a cut field without opening the row would see the head only. The eager readers were audited (summary/category, spawned-session parsing in the 300-byte head, minimap hover, diff totals, exit codes, MCP headers).

title: perf(chat): refresh only changed rows of live chats and poll only while the event stream is down
body:
Code changes: +493 -118  
Tests: +484 -97  
Others: +21 -0 (generated: openapi.yaml, schema.ts)

## Summary
Every conversation event refetched the open chat's whole newest page (about 620 KB for a large chat), and refetching an infinite query reloaded every older page too. This PR has three parts:
- **W2:** live updates read only the rows that changed, checked by a page digest.
- **W4:** remote and catalog polls run only while the event stream is down.
- **W5:** a resumed SSE reconnect trusts the daemon's replay instead of refetching everything, unless the daemon says it reset.

It builds on #7165's refresh rules and keeps them.

## Changes
- **Daemon**
  - The newest page of `GET /sessions/{id}/conversation` carries an opaque `changeCursor`: conversation, branch, edit floor, latestSequence and the read time.
  - `?changedSince=<cursor>` returns the same page with `changesOnly: true`. Rows are sent only if `sequence > cursor` or they were updated since the read (2 s overlap). Turns and metadata are always complete. `pageDigest` is FNV-1a over `kind:id:revision` for the full page.
  - A cursor from another conversation, branch or edit floor returns the full page. A bad cursor returns 400 `CONVERSATION_CURSOR_INVALID`.
  - The change filter runs before the activity preview from the previous PR, so delta reads are previews too.
  - `/events`: the first cursor frame says `{"resets":true}`. A resume whose cursor is ahead of head, or whose gap was pruned, starts with `event: reset`.
- **Desktop**
  - `refreshLiveConversation()` replaces `refreshRemoteConversation()` for local and remote chats.
    - It reads page 0 only, using `changedSince` when the page has a cursor, and checks the merged page against `pageDigest`. On a mismatch it reads the full page.
    - At most one read is in flight plus one catch-up per chat. A busy stream never aborts a slow read.
  - `event-transport.ts`: a loaded, observed chat refreshes page 0 in place. Anything else is only invalidated.
  - #7165's rule still decides whether a chat is refreshed at all: an id-only `session_updated` skips ready or busy chats.
  - The chat-view refresh after a wake (`SessionView`) also goes through `refreshLiveConversation`.
  - Remote 2 s polls (live chat page, 12 query families) run only until the host's stream proves delivery. A dropped stream is re-probed with SSE backoff. Remote workspace 15 s polls stop while the stream is healthy. The config-options poll slows from 5 s to 30 s.
  - A resumed `onopen` skips the global refresh when this source announced resets. `event: reset` runs it.

**With #7165's message-based pages:** the cursor does not encode page boundaries.
- Page 0 moving forward is handled: slid-out rows leave the digest set and stay on screen.
- Page 0 reaching back to an older prompt causes a digest mismatch and one full page-0 read.
- Streaming inside a turn keeps page 0's start fixed, so deltas apply.

## Measurements (measured)
Real renderer, 10 s of simulated streaming into a chat plus 5 s of settle, one run per profile, against e81912c11a.

| profile | metric | before | after |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| local | conversation GET bytes | 30,315,146 (49 reads) | 408,441 (53 reads) |
| local | renderer JSON decoded | 30.6 MB | 0.70 MB |
| 3G | conversation GET bytes | 1,240,482 (only 2 reads) | 117,446 (13 reads) |
| 3G | final text lag | 30,861 ms | 894 ms |

- Modeled from payload sizes: an idle open remote chat goes from about 310-500 KB/s of polling to 0 while its host's stream delivers.
- A resumed reconnect against a daemon that announces resets sends nothing beyond the replayed events. Verified on an isolated daemon.
- The stack-level benchmark is in the bottom PR.

## Compatibility
- All wire changes are additive. Old clients ignore `changeCursor`, `changesOnly`, `pageDigest`, `resets` and the named `reset` event.
- New clients against old daemons get no cursor, so they never send `changedSince`, and get no `resets`, so they keep the refresh on every reopen.
- Mobile does not read any of it.

## Risks
- `changedSince` relies on `updated_at` moving on every row change, and on one host clock. A miss is caught by the digest, which falls back to a full read.
- After a trusted replay, rows deep in older pages that changed during the gap stay stale until the next full load.
- No `maxPages`: in TanStack 5 it evicts the live page when fetching older pages.
- Local command follow-ups (send/retry/edit/stop) still invalidate all loaded pages.

## Testing
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers/ -run 'ChangedSince|Preview|Conversation|Snapshot|Activity|ChatView'`, `./internal/httpd/ -run 'TestEventsStream|TestWriteSSE'` and `./internal/httpd/apispec/...`: pass.
  - New tests: changed rows only, invalid cursors, changedSince with previews, and resume after a pruned gap.
- vitest `event-transport`, `useConversation`, `useConversation.live`, `useWorkspaceQuery`, `useConversationConnecting`, `SessionView` and `FullActivity`: 430 pass.

Broad checks were not run locally, per the maintainer's standing preference: `go vet`, golangci-lint, full `go test ./...`, frontend `npm run typecheck`, full vitest, and e2e. CI covers them. On the stack tip only, `cd backend && go build ./...` and the renderer `vite build` both passed.

## Stack
Merge in order, bottom first. Each PR is based on the one before it; #7280 is based on main. (#7279, the usage fix that used to sit at the bottom, is independent and merges on its own.)

1. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7280 `perf/gzip-json-responses`: feat(httpd): gzip JSON responses over 1 KB for clients that accept it
2. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7281 `perf/session-list-etag`: perf(httpd): revalidate polled list reads with ETag/304 and refetch after opening Chat only on a wake
3. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7282 `perf/lean-activity-previews`: perf(chat): send activity previews on conversation pages and load a row's full body when it opens
4. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7283 `perf/live-sync-deltas`: perf(chat): refresh only changed rows of live chats and poll only while the event stream is down ← this PR
5. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7284 `perf/persist-query-cache`: feat(desktop): show the cached session list and transcript on launch

The mobile counterpart is #7275, which is separate and based on main.

title: feat(desktop): show the cached session list and transcript on launch
body:
Code changes: +357 -13  
Tests: +185 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary
Nothing survived a reload, so every launch waited for the full session list and the full first conversation page before painting. Desktop now persists the local workspace list and page 0 of the 10 most recently opened chats in IndexedDB. It shows them at once, refetches them right away, and never acts on them until live data arrives. This follows t3 code's "cached shell first, then revalidate".

## Changes
- `lib/query-persistence.ts` (new): a small IndexedDB persister with no new dependency.
  - **Keyed by** the daemon's host id from `GET /api/v1/identity`. That id is stored in the daemon's data dir, so another data dir or machine gets its own cache. No id means no cache.
  - **Busted by** schema version, app version and git commit.
  - **Bounds:** 10 chats, 2 M chars per entry, 8 M total, oldest evicted first.
  - **Restore:** chats are restored lazily when their query is created. Restored data carries `dataUpdatedAt 0`.
  - **Writes:** throttled to 2 s and skipped when unchanged. Only data fetched live from this daemon is written. Remote hosts and cloud queries are never persisted.
- `lib/restored-query.ts`: `isRestoredQueryData`.
- `routes/_shell.tsx`: the loader returns at once when the list was restored, and the live fetch keeps running.
- **No action on restored data:**
  - `SessionChatSurface` fences new work, hides the agent switch and prompt suggestions, reports no work state, and auto-opens no links.
  - `SessionView` waits for the live list before resume-on-open.
- `useConversation.ts`: #7165 keeps local chats fresh forever (`staleTime: Infinity`), which would leave a restored page stale forever. A restored page now counts as stale at once, and live cached pages still need no request. Covered by a new test.
- IndexedDB lives in Electron `userData`, which `main.ts` pins under `~/.ao`.

## Measurements (measured)
Production renderer build in headless Chrome, sandboxed daemon, copy of a real DB, biggest chat open, reloaded repeatedly. 3G = CDP throttling of daemon requests (400 ms, 50 KB/s).

| reload, biggest chat open | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| local: time to session list | 116.5 ms | 114 ms |
| local: time to transcript | 207.5 ms | 184 ms (-11%) |
| 3G: time to session list | 5,519 ms | 3,591 ms (-35%) |
| 3G: time to transcript | 42,987 ms | 3,652 ms (11.8x) |

Wire bytes and request counts do not change: restored data is always refetched in full. The earlier PRs in this stack make that refetch cheap.

## Compatibility
- Desktop only, with no API change.
- A daemon without `/api/v1/identity` gets no cache.

## Risks
- One identity round trip before restore (about 1 ms locally).
- A user click during the restore window acts on cached list data. Mutations stay daemon-validated.
- A shape change to `ConversationSnapshot` or `WorkspaceSummary` needs `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped. App version and commit are already in the buster.

## Testing
- vitest `query-persistence`, `SessionChatSurface`, `useConversation` (including the new restored-page test), `SessionView` and `event-transport`: 447 pass.

Broad checks were not run locally, per the maintainer's standing preference: `go vet`, golangci-lint, full `go test ./...`, frontend `npm run typecheck`, full vitest, and e2e. CI covers them. On the stack tip only, `cd backend && go build ./...` and the renderer `vite build` both passed.

Merge in order, bottom first. Each PR is based on the one before it; #7280 is based on main. (#7279, the usage fix that used to sit at the bottom, is independent and merges on its own.)

1. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7280 `perf/gzip-json-responses`: feat(httpd): gzip JSON responses over 1 KB for clients that accept it
2. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7281 `perf/session-list-etag`: perf(httpd): revalidate polled list reads with ETag/304 and refetch after opening Chat only on a wake
3. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7282 `perf/lean-activity-previews`: perf(chat): send activity previews on conversation pages and load a row's full body when it opens
4. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7283 `perf/live-sync-deltas`: perf(chat): refresh only changed rows of live chats and poll only while the event stream is down
5. https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7284 `perf/persist-query-cache`: feat(desktop): show the cached session list and transcript on launch ← this PR

The mobile counterpart is #7275, which is separate and based on main.

title: fix(httpd): count repeated attempts with the same wrong password once in the lockout
body:
Code changes: +20 -8  
Tests: +81 -14  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

The LAN/tunnel auth lockout now counts distinct wrong passwords per source, not failed requests. A source that sends the same wrong password many times in one window has made one guess. Five distinct wrong passwords in a sliding one-minute window still block the source with 429, as before.

- `lockout` keeps, per source, up to 5 keyed hashes (`hash/maphash` with a per-process random seed) of the wrong tokens it has seen. It never stores raw tokens.
- A token already in the set does not count again. It still extends the window, like any failure today.
- A missing or empty token counts as one distinct value.
- Window expiry, `reset` on success, `resetAll` on password rotation, and the retired-password exemption are unchanged.
- `authMiddleware` is the only production caller of `lock.fail`. The tunnel and the preview-cookie path go through it, so both get the same behavior. Mobile control routes are loopback-only and have no lockout.

## Why

Retired passwords already do not count, but the retired list lives in memory only. After a password change and a daemon restart, a phone that still holds the old password fails every concurrent request (batched board polls, SSE reconnects, chat reloads). Five of those inside a minute locked the phone out, even though it had made one guess. Any client making parallel requests with a stale credential hits the same problem. The motivating case is the batched mobile polling in #7275.

## Security note

Brute-force protection is unchanged. Guessing a password requires trying different values, and every different value still counts. An attacker still gets at most 4 distinct guesses per source per window before a 429. Repeating a value that already failed gives the attacker no new information. The per-source set is capped at 5 entries, so memory per source stays bounded even when concurrent requests race past `blocked`. The hashes are keyed with a random per-process seed and kept in memory only.

`docs/adr/0001-lan-listener-for-mobile.md` still says "after 5 failed attempts". I left the ADR as written; this change narrows what counts as an attempt.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go test ./internal/httpd/ -run 'Lock|Auth'`: pass. This includes the new table test `TestAuthLockoutCountsDistinctWrongPasswords`: same wrong password repeated, 5 distinct, 4 distinct, mixed repeats and distinct, missing password, window expiry, reset on success, per-source isolation, and retired password not counted.
- `go test ./internal/httpd/ -run 'LANTunnel|LANManager|Rotat|Retired|Spoof|TunnelClient|LANListener'`: pass.
- Existing lockout tests that sent the same wrong password 5 times now send 5 distinct ones.
- I ran focused tests only. CI covers the full suite and lint.

title: perf: cut idle daemon CPU, streaming render cost and pty replay growth
body:
Five low-risk fixes found by profiling the daemon and the renderer against a copy of a real AO database (72 sessions). One commit per fix, so each can be reverted on its own.

## Before / after

Sandboxed daemon on a copy of a real DB, production renderer in headless Chrome, A/B runs alternated, 2 runs each.

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Daemon CPU, app idle on the board | 7.8% | 2.9% |
| Daemon CPU, no client attached | ~5.0% | ~1.9% |
| Daemon requests from an idle renderer | 158/min | 76/min |
| Renderer main-thread time while a chat streams (per 14 s) | 8.3 s | 4.9 s |
| Pty ring, 3,000 full-screen repaints | 1.2 s CPU, 26.9 GB allocated | 78 ms, 24 MB |
| Terminal replay sent on attach | 17.9 MB, unbounded | 3.2 MB, capped at 4 MB |
| Session switch / scroll p95 | 54 ms / 16.8 ms | 55 ms / 16.7 ms (unchanged) |

## Changes

| Commit | Cause |
|---|---|
| `perf(chat)`: stream fade | `.stream-char` used `animation: … both`. A filling animation never ends, so a long reply kept ~1,000 finished animations alive and Chrome re-layerized them every frame. The animation has no delay and ends at the element's normal opacity, so it looks identical without the fill mode. |
| `perf(daemon)`: Claude transcript discovery | `filepath.Glob(projects/*/<id>.jsonl)` opens and lists every project directory. With ~1,800 projects that was ~25 ms per live Claude session on every reconcile pass, 43% of idle daemon CPU. Now: one `ReadDir` of the root and one `Stat` per project (~3 ms). Same result: newest match, 128-match cap. |
| `perf(daemon)`: preview poller | The 250 ms poll decoded every column of every session. A new `ListPreviewPollSessions` query reads the 5 columns it uses, for live workers only. |
| `perf(pty)`: ring partial line | Full-screen agents rarely print a newline, so output piled up in the partial line and was re-copied on every chunk (quadratic; plan item TB-1). The partial line now grows by append. Past 64 KB everything before the latest screen clear (`ESC[2J`, `ESC c`) is dropped, since replay paints the same screen from there. Programs that never clear are cut to the newest 2 MB at an escape boundary once they pass 4 MB. Modes from the dropped part are re-sent by `modeTracker.Restore`. |
| `perf(desktop)`: switch-readiness poll | The sidebar checks each project's orchestrator. When an orchestrator's native transcript is gone (Claude prunes them after 30 days by default) it polled `/interface-transition` every second, forever. The poll is now 1 s for the first 30 s of a readiness wait, then 15 s. |

## Trade-offs

- A switch whose native session appears more than 30 s after the wait started can take up to 15 s to enable. The usual case, where the session-start hook arrives within seconds, still gets 1 s rechecks.
- If a program prints over 64 KB without a newline (wrapping and scrolling) and then clears the screen, the scrolled-off part is not replayed. The visible screen is unaffected.

## Test plan

New tests: ring trim (clear split across chunks, small partial kept whole, hard cap starts on ESC) and readiness backoff. Tests were not run locally; CI verifies.

Manual:
1. Run the desktop app from this branch and open a chat session.
2. Ask the agent for a long reply (1,000+ words).
3. Confirm each new character still fades in as it streams.
4. Open a terminal session with a full-screen agent, switch away, then come back. Confirm the screen redraws correctly.

title: perf(chat): let finished stream-fade animations end
body:
Streamed chat text fades in one character at a time (`.stream-char`, added by `rehype-stream-fade`). The CSS used `animation: stream-char-in 300ms ease both;`. With a fill mode an animation never ends: it holds its last frame forever. Partway through a long reply about 1,150 of these animations were alive at once (976 finished, 181 running), and Chrome re-layerized and repainted all of them on every frame.

This drops the fill mode. Each character still fades in over 300 ms. The animation has no delay and ends at the element's normal opacity, so it looks the same, and Chrome now drops each animation when it finishes.

## Before / after

Production renderer in headless Chrome against a sandboxed daemon on a copy of a real database, streaming 12 s into a long chat. Two runs each, alternated.

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Renderer main-thread time while streaming (per 14 s) | 8.3 s (58% busy) | 4.9 s (34% busy) |
| Live animations partway through a long reply | ~1,150 | ~180 (only the ones still fading) |

## Test plan

1. Run the desktop app from this branch and open a chat session.
2. Ask the agent for a long reply (1,000+ words).
3. Confirm each new character still fades in as it streams, and that settled text looks unchanged.

title: fix(files): bound large reviews and guide safe PR checkouts
body:
Code changes: +60 -15  
Tests: +283 -1  
Others: +42 -0  

## What

Keep large Files reviews responsive by loading at most 96 files per page, and guide existing-PR work through verified commit SHAs.

## Why

A branch named `FETCH_HEAD` can collide with the fetch pseudo-ref: a failed Git switch can replace the index and working files while leaving HEAD unchanged. The resulting thousands of staged changes caused the review pane to progressively fetch every patch and render all unloaded fallback rows.

## How

- Bound diff queries, parsed patches, fallback rows, and prefetch to the current 96-file page. Preserve the complete file count and direct navigation to distant files.
- Preserve other pages’ collapsed, viewed, and loaded deferred-diff state when using Collapse all or Expand all on the current page.
- Reset pagination when the filter, session, or review selection changes; preserve the current page across workspace manifest refreshes and clamp it when the list shrinks. Cancel abandoned diff requests.
- Add safe-checkout guidance to claim output, worker prompts, and the bundled skill. Claiming remains metadata-only; existing dirty worktrees are not repaired or switched automatically.
- Add Git collision, pagination, cancellation, and 5,123-file real-renderer regressions, plus a reusable performance fixture.

## Testing

title: fix(mobile): render chat tables as aligned grids
body: Code changes: +73 -24\ Tests: +45 -7\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Markdown tables in agent replies on mobile now render as real grids instead of `cell | cell` text. Columns line up across rows, long cells wrap, cells show inline Markdown, and wide tables scroll sideways. | Before (iOS, current app) | After · iOS | After · Android | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | Wide tables scroll sideways inside the reply, and the page still scrolls vertically: | After · iOS, swiped to Notes | After · Android, swiped to Notes | | --- | --- | | | | ## Why Agent replies render through `ChatMarkdown`'s `continuousSelection` mode: the whole reply sits in one native text view so a selection can span headings, lists and code. A table can't live inside a text view, so `SelectableResponseText` flattened it into `a | b` lines. The grid component (`MarkdownTable`) existed, but only on the non-continuous path, and there its columns didn't line up and cells showed raw `**` and backticks. ## How - **Split replies at tables.** In continuous mode the blocks are cut into runs; each text run is still one selectable surface (Add to chat works per run), and each table renders as a grid between them. Trade-off: one selection can no longer cross a table. - **Aligned columns.** React Native has no grid layout, so each column gets one width for every row, estimated from its longest cell (72–220pt). Columns then grow in proportion to fill narrow tables and scroll when wide. This has to be `width`, not `flexBasis`: inside a horizontal `ScrollView` the row width is undefined, and Yoga then ignores a numeric basis and sizes each cell to its own content. - **Cells** render inline Markdown (bold, code, links) via `SelectableInlineText` at footnote size, with code at caption size so it doesn't outgrow the cell text. - **Parser** (`markdownBlocks.ts`): reads `:--` / `:-:` / `--:` alignment, accepts short dividers like `|-|-|`, requires the divider to match the header's column count (otherwise the text stays prose), and unescapes `\|` in cells. No lookbehind regex, for Hermes. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 2510 tests pass. - New tests: alignment, short dividers, escaped pipes and mismatched dividers in the parser; a continuous-mode reply renders text / grid / text with matching column widths in every row. - Real devices: side-by-side Release builds (embedded JS, OTA off) on an iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 27.2) and a Pixel 10a, paired to a real machine and checked on live conversations. The Android screenshots are from the Pixel. The iOS ones are from an iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator rendering the same reply text, light and dark mode both checked. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): keep usage limits intact across account moves, and continue on another account
body:
## Problem

A Claude chat hit its account's usage limit, the user moved it to a second account, and four things went wrong (two real sessions, 2026-10-26; the database shows exactly these writes):

1. **Red error after the move.** A move restarts the agent and ACP `session/load` replays the transcript. The replayed completion has no failure text; settling the turn with it erased the recorded error (`SettleConversationTurn` sets `error_message = ?`). The usage limit is parsed from that error, so "Usage limit reached" became "The agent ran into a problem / Retry", and the replay's restored limit (`provider.failure` activity) appeared as a second red row.
2. **Duplicate "recovered" turn for prompts with images.** ACP replays attachments as `[Image]` / `[File: …]` / `[Embedded context]` after the text; AO stores only the typed text, so the prompt never matched and came back as a second turn: "outcome unknown", "This turn was recovered from an earlier session", text ending `[Image][Image]`.
3. **The limit still waited for the old account's reset.** After a move the notice counted down to the old account's reset and offered only "Auto-resume at reset", which AO refuses once the account changed (`ErrAgentAccountChanged`).
4. **Other chats stayed stuck.** Moves are per session and a new default doesn't move existing sessions, so the next message in another chat failed on the same limit with no way forward. (It looked like a "switch back"; the session had never moved.)

## Change

- `reconcileNativeHistory` keeps AO's recorded error on a replayed completion, drops a replayed provider failure that repeats the turn's error, and also matches a replayed prompt against its attachment placeholders (plain text still matches, so agents that replay without placeholders are unaffected).
- The snapshot marks a usage limit `accountChanged` when the session's account changed after the failed turn (reusing `SessionAgentAccountChangedSince`); spec and `schema.ts` regenerated. The notice then says "This chat now uses another account. You can resume now." with Resume.
- When another signed-in account of the same provider still has quota, the usage-limit notice offers **Continue on <account>**: it moves the session there and, once the move completes, sends the failed prompt again (`useUsageLimitContinue`). Local sessions only; if the chat closes mid-move, the limit falls back to the Resume state above.
- New strings in all 8 locales.

## Reproduce, then prove the fix

Each change is a failing test commit followed by the commit that makes it pass:

| Commit | Account-move scenarios (Go: real ACP adapter + SQLite store + fake `claude-agent-acp` speaking the same frames) | `UsageLimitNotice` after a move | Continue on another account |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 `test(chat): reproduce the account-move replay bugs` | **FAIL**: error `""` + extra `system/failed` limit row; turns `[failed recovered]` with `[Image][Image]`; limit gone | **FAIL** | n/a |
| 2 `fix(chat): keep usage limits intact…` | PASS | PASS | n/a |
| 3 `test(chat): reproduce the stuck chat…` | PASS | PASS | **FAIL**: no "Continue on" button |
| 4 `feat(chat): continue a chat stuck…` | PASS | PASS | PASS |

Commit 1 also fails `lint` on a redundant conversion in the new test helper; commit 2 fixes it. Desktop before/after screenshots from the real app (isolated lab, two accounts, one out of quota) are in the comments.

## Tests

- New: `account_move_replay_test.go` (3 scenarios), `UsageLimitNotice.test.tsx` (moved limit), `ChatWorkspaceUsageLimitContinue.test.tsx` (2 cases).
- Locally also green: chat replay/reconcile/checkpoint/continuation/retry/auto-resume tests, store/controller/domain usage-limit and snapshot tests, `ChatWorkspaceRetry`, i18n parity and coverage, golangci-lint on the touched packages.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Placeholder matching mirrors the ACP adapter's `historicalUserContent`; if that rendering changes, attachment prompts fall back to today's behaviour.
- "Continue on" retries only after the move reports `completed`; a failed move shows its error and leaves the chat on the old account.

title: fix(chat): keep usage-limit refusals through wake replay, and let a new chat switch account
body:
## Evidence: before vs after, in the desktop app

Recorded in the real desktop app against a lab daemon built from each commit: **before** is `a2a981122f` (main) and **after** is `3ecafd1513` (this PR). Each animation plays before, then after, at 1.5× speed, with waits sped up further and labelled with their real time. Full-resolution videos: [account switch, 1:46](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/account-switch.mp4) · [usage limit, 2:29](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/usage-limit-auto-resume.mp4).

### 1. Switching account on a chat with no messages yet

![Account switch: before fails with the ownership error, after switches and the agent answers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/account-switch.webp)

**Before (main):** "Account switch failed" with the ownership error; the chat stays on the old account.

![Before: Account switch failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/account-switch-base-end.jpg)

**After (this PR):** the switch completes and the first message is answered on the new account.

![After: switched, the agent answered on the new account](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/account-switch-head-end.jpg)

### 2. Usage limit and auto-resume across sleep and wake

![Usage limit: before, the wake erases the refusal and auto-resume stops; after, the notice survives and auto-resume runs at the reset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/usage-limit-auto-resume.webp)

**Before (main):** reopening the sleeping chat wakes it, and the notice becomes "The agent ran into a problem".

![Before: after the wake the notice became The agent ran into a problem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/usage-limit-auto-resume-base-after-wake.jpg)

**Before (main), end:** auto-resume has already stopped, before the reset, without retrying.

![Before: auto-resume stopped without retrying](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/usage-limit-auto-resume-base-end.jpg)

**After (this PR):** after the wake, the usage-limit notice and the scheduled auto-resume are still there.

![After: the notice and auto-resume survive the wake](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/usage-limit-auto-resume-head-after-wake.jpg)

**After (this PR), end:** at the reset, auto-resume runs and the agent answers.

![After: auto-resume ran at the reset and the agent answered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c319bf3033b7454aeaaf1b0f3d0549341e153271/usage-limit-auto-resume-head-end.jpg)

The refusal itself is simulated: the turn is settled with Claude's refusal text and a reset 5 minutes out. Everything after that is real: the click on "Auto-resume at reset", idle hibernation, the wake on reopening, the ACP history replay, and the scheduler. The lab used the dark theme and Developer Mode, which shows the inspector's Account selector.

## Problem

Two bugs, both seen on 2026-10-26 in real sessions that hit the Claude 5-hour limit.

**1. The usage-limit notice turns into "The agent ran into a problem", and auto-resume stops.** A chat session that hit its limit showed "Usage limit reached" with auto-resume. Once the session hibernated and woke, the same turn showed a generic failure with Retry. Auto-resume armed on another session never fired at the reset.

Cause: waking a hibernated chat runs ACP `session/load`, which replays every turn. ACP history carries no turn error, so the replayed `turn.completed` re-settled the failed turn with an empty message (`SettleConversationTurn` overwrites `error_message`). The usage limit is classified from that message, so the turn stopped reading as a usage limit:

```
11:50:01  live    turn.completed  error="You've hit your session limit · resets 12pm (Asia/Calcutta)"
11:50:37  session hibernates
11:54:47  wake -> acp-history turn.completed, turnState=failed, no error -> error_message=''
```

The scheduled auto-resume wakes the session itself, so this hit every hibernated session: the wake erased the refusal, the retry's own check then saw no usage limit, and the scheduler stopped with "Auto-resume stopped: usage-limit auto-resume is unavailable". The UI never showed that message either, because it lives under the usage limit that no longer parsed.

**2. Switching account on a chat with no messages yet always fails.**

```
Account switch failed
switch interface …: resume chat: chat driver unavailable: persistent ACP host: prepare chat
controller environment: persist browser capability verifier: session controller ownership
changed before browser capability rotation
```

Cause: an account move skips `CommitControllerEpoch`, but `runInterfaceTransition` still started the target fresh whenever no native conversation existed. That is the case for a new chat, because Claude has not persisted its provider conversation yet. The fresh relaunch blanks `ProviderConversationID` only on the in-memory record. That record becomes `ExpectedControllerOwner`, so the browser-capability fence compared `""` with the handle still in the session row and refused the target. The transition then rolled back. The rollback path already had the right rule ("a fresh relaunch drops the provider id only in memory…"), which is why it succeeded.

The other account's sign-in was not the cause: AO read it as signed in.

## Change

- `Store.SettleTurn`: re-settling a turn in the state it already has, with an empty message, keeps the recorded error. A replay can no longer erase a refusal. A real change of state still writes its own message.
- `runInterfaceTransition`: the forward path uses the rollback's predicate. A Chat that durably holds its provider id resumes it, and the ordinary resume (`providerNeverPersisted` → `FreshIfProviderConversationMissing` → `replaceUnpersistedChatProvider`) replaces a never-messaged provider in place. Interface switches (TUI ↔ Chat) and Terminal account moves are unchanged.

## Verification: PR base vs PR head

Isolated lab daemon per build (own `AO_DATA_DIR`, port, chat hosts), real Claude Code ACP runtime, real Claude accounts. Base `a2a981122f` (main), head `3ecafd1513`.

**Account switch on a never-messaged chat**, both directions:

| | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| device login → saved account | `failed TARGET_RESUME_FAILED … session controller ownership changed before browser capability rotation`, binding unchanged | `completed`; binding moved; provider runs with the saved account's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` |
| saved account → device login | same failure, binding unchanged | `completed`; binding moved; first message replies `ok` |

(In the first head run the saved account had just hit its own real 5-hour limit, so that first message got a genuine refusal from the new account. The reverse run shows a clean reply.)

**Usage-limited turn, auto-resume armed, idle hibernation on.** The turn was settled as the live refusal leaves it (`You've hit your session limit · resets <4 min ahead>`), auto-resume armed through the API, and the session left to hibernate before the reset:

```
                 Base                                          Head
hibernates       16:17:36                                      16:21:58
reset, wake      history replay runs (1)                       history replay runs (1)
source error     erased                                        kept
auto-resume      "Auto-resume stopped: usage-limit             retry turn created -> completed
                 auto-resume is unavailable", no retry
API usageLimit   null (notice gone)                            {resetsAt, autoResume:false}
```

## Tests

- `TestSettleTurnReplayKeepsUsageLimitRefusal`: live refusal, then a replay settle; fails on main (`ErrorMessage:""`, `UsageLimit:nil`).
- `TestAccountTransitionMovesANeverMessagedChat`: account move on a never-messaged chat with the capability fence active; fails on main with the production error.
- Locally: `go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/store/` and the `service/chat` history/replay/usage-limit tests pass. `./internal/session_manager/` passes except `TestSpawn_*` tests that fail identically on main here (tmux lookup, and a 100 ms deadline flake in `TestSpawn_AfterStartPromptReservesCallerDeadlineForFallbackDelivery`).

## Risks

- `SettleTurn` now treats "same state, empty message" as a replay. Every caller that settles a failed turn for real passes its own message, so none relies on clearing it.
- Turns already wiped in existing databases stay wiped; the fix stops new erasures only.

title: feat(remote): give linked machines fixed addresses from AO Cloud
body:
Code changes: +1671 -195  
Tests: +2095 -49  
Others: +38 -7 (docs, locale strings, generated API spec)

## What this changes

A signed-in machine keeps one remote address, `https://h-<hash>.<zone>`, across restarts and sleep. Paired phones and desktops keep working without scanning a new code. AO Cloud owns the machine's tunnel. The machine only ever receives its own tunnel's run token.

Anyone without a fixed address keeps `main`'s behaviour: signed-out desktops, headless hosts, AO Clouds without fixed addresses (including today's), and accounts that use all of their fixed addresses all run the quick tunnel as before.

| Who | Remote access before | Remote access now |
|---|---|---|
| Signed-in desktop, AO Cloud gives fixed addresses | Quick tunnel; the address changes on restart | Fixed address |
| Signed-in desktop, AO Cloud gives none, or the account has none left | Quick tunnel | Quick tunnel, as before |
| Signed-out desktop | Quick tunnel | Quick tunnel, as before. Connect Mobile adds a note that signing in keeps the address |
| Headless host (`ao remote-host enable --tunnel`) | Quick tunnel | Quick tunnel until a desktop links it, then the fixed address |
| Linked machine while AO Cloud cannot answer | n/a | Cached fixed tunnel. With none cached, a quick tunnel until AO Cloud answers |

## Split

This PR is the desktop and daemon part. The rest is in other PRs:

- #7410: the Cloud API contract and the regenerated `packages/cloud-client`.
- AO Cloud's side, in the private control-plane repository.
- #7411: the phone.

Merge order:

1. #7410.
2. AO Cloud's side, deployed.
3. This PR. It also works against an AO Cloud without fixed addresses: such an AO Cloud answers 404 or 503, and the machine runs the quick tunnel, as on `main`.
4. #7411, at any time.

## The Cloud API it uses (from #7410)

- `PUT /me/hosts/{hostId}` without `url`: AO Cloud makes the machine's tunnel and lists the machine at its fixed address. 409 `fixed_address_limit_reached` means the account has no fixed address left. A registration with `url` succeeds as before.
- `GET /me/hosts` returns `fixedAddresses`. The desktop leaves out `url` only when it is true.
- `POST /remote-hosts/{hostId}/tunnel` (host digest) returns the hostname, the run token and `since`, the time the DNS record was made. `{"repair":true}` replaces the tunnel under the same name, and the answer says `"repaired":true` when it did. It answers 401 when the machine is not linked, 404 or 503 when AO Cloud gives no fixed addresses, 409 at the limit, 429 when rate-limited and 502 when Cloudflare failed.
- A registration with a new host token (a new pairing password) replaces the tunnel, so a run token fetched with the old credential stops working.

## How it works

**Daemon**
- **Fixed tunnel:** a linked machine fetches its tunnel from AO Cloud on every start. While AO Cloud cannot answer, it starts the cached token. With none cached, or while AO Cloud cannot make the tunnel (429, 502), a quick tunnel serves and the machine keeps asking. If AO Cloud gives no fixed addresses (404, 503) or the account has none left (409), the machine runs a quick tunnel. The cache is keyed by AO Cloud, host and account link, written atomically, and removed once the link is gone.
- **Moving off the quick tunnel:** a machine on a quick tunnel moves to the fixed address once AO Cloud gives it one. It checks every 30 s, and remote access nudges it to check at once.
- **New DNS name:** the address is held back until 12 s after AO Cloud made its DNS record (`since`), so a record made seconds ago is not advertised early.
- **Losing the address:** while fixed, the machine checks AO Cloud every 30 minutes and drops an address it no longer gets. A new account token (another account's link) nudges it to check at once. A new pairing password revokes the link. The connector then keeps serving and asking for up to 2 minutes, until the signed-in desktop's new link reaches AO Cloud. It gives the address up only if no link arrives. A refusal gets the same grace, since a new link is written on the machine before it reaches AO Cloud. Within the grace, only a link on its way or an unreachable AO Cloud is asked again; an answer such as 429 waits for the next check, and so does a "no fixed addresses" answer. A bare 404, from a proxy during an AO Cloud deploy or an AO Cloud that predates the route, keeps the cached tunnel. AO Cloud with fixed addresses off answers `404 fixed_addresses_unavailable` (#7500), so linked machines do not count as server errors there. A start that has just asked AO Cloud drops an earlier nudge.
- **Coming back:** once all its connections stay down for 10 s, the machine asks AO Cloud again. If AO Cloud gives it a new tunnel, it restarts on that tunnel. An edge restart reconnects within seconds and asks nothing.
- **Replacement:** the daemon reads cloudflared's output. The next start asks AO Cloud for a replacement when the connector exits, has no live edge connection for 3 minutes, or is refused four times in a row. It asks at most every 2 minutes, doubling up to an hour for each replacement that did not help, so a connector that keeps crashing cannot use up the account's tunnel writes. The address stays. A tunnel that served owes no replacement. While AO Cloud cannot make the replacement, the machine serves a quick tunnel instead of the failed one, and moves back only onto a replacement AO Cloud made. Meanwhile it asks at least every 5 minutes. The machine sends no requests to its own address.
- **Restarts:** a planned restart (moving to the fixed address, or onto a new tunnel) reads as starting in the status, never as an error.
- **cloudflared:** when no usable copy exists, the daemon downloads pinned 2026.10.2, the release the macOS app bundles. A test keeps the two pins together. The daemon checks the SHA-256 and installs the copy into `<data>/bin`, fsynced before the rename. A managed copy that reports another version is downloaded again; one whose version cannot be read is kept. A download that sends nothing for a minute is given up. A failed download is tried again after 5 s, 30 s and 2 min within one install timeout, and again the next time remote access starts; wrong bytes are not downloaded again until the daemon restarts. Homebrew, winget or the Linux command is offered only after that, and that install starts the connector by itself too.
- **Address publish:** the daemon republishes its address every 10 minutes. After AO Cloud refuses it (a 401 with code `unauthorized`), it backs off from 1 to 30 minutes.
- **Status:** `tunnel.fixed` says whether the address is fixed. `tunnel.installing` says a cloudflared download is running. `ao remote-host` uses both.

**Desktop**
- **Signed in:** Connect Mobile and **Allow access from your devices** link the computer before starting the tunnel, so the code holds the fixed address from the start. So does Connect Mobile's cloudflared install.
- **No fixed address:** when AO Cloud gives none, or the link fails, **Allow access** lists the computer at its quick tunnel's address once the tunnel is up, as on `main`.
- **New pairing password:** when the account still lists the computer, the desktop links it again, at the fixed address or, on an AO Cloud without fixed addresses, at the quick tunnel's address. On `main`, nothing links again.
- **Signed out:** Connect Mobile pairs with a quick tunnel, as on `main`, and adds a note that signing in gives the computer an address that stays the same.
- **Taking back:** a turn-on that fails after linking removes only a listing it added itself.
- **Offline machine:** a fixed address keeps its DNS record while its machine is offline, so Cloudflare answers 530. The desktop rechecks the host on 530, as on 502 and 503, and shows it offline. On `main`, an offline quick tunnel stops resolving instead.
- **Allow access switch:** it waits for a running cloudflared download instead of turning off, and the download does not count against its 90 s wait.

## Testing

- **CI:** backend packages (`mobilebridge`, `daemon`, `httpd/controllers`, `cli`, `systeminstall`, `systemexec`), the frontend vitest suite and `tsc`.
- **Lint:** `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on every changed backend package, 0 issues (on the head before the quick-tunnel fallbacks).
- **Live, on earlier heads:** these ran before the quick-tunnel fallbacks for anyone without a fixed address. The fixed-address path they exercise is unchanged.
  - **Linking:** linking a running machine moved it to its fixed address in 4.1 s. After a restart, the address was shown at 1.5 s and answered publicly at 7.0 s.
  - **Sleep:** after a 90 s sleep the machine kept its tunnel and answered 7.8 s after waking. After a long sleep it got a new tunnel at the same address and answered 16.8 s after waking.
  - **cloudflared:** with no cloudflared on `PATH`, the download's hash matched, the connector started at 32 s, and a restart reused the copy.
- **Not tested:** the quick-tunnel fallbacks against a live AO Cloud (unit tests cover them), a real phone scanning a fixed-address code, Windows and Linux runs, and a staging deployment with fixed addresses on.

## Intentionally left out

- **Duplicate host IDs:** two machines with one host ID (a copied `~/.ao`) serve one address, with no warning yet.
- **Address row:** Connect Mobile still shows the LAN address in its Address row. The fixed address is in the QR code and in the account's host list.
- **Account devices and the run token:** any device of the account can fetch the machine's run token and run a second connector for its tunnel. This is accepted, since those devices can already reach the machine. A new pairing password ends it, because the registration with the new host token replaces the tunnel.
- **`~/.cloudflared/config.yml`:** it still applies to the connectors the daemon runs, as on `main`. A catch-all ingress rule there answers at the machine's address instead of the daemon, on quick and fixed tunnels alike.
- **Account link status:** paths that make a new pairing password without the desktop (a signed-out Connect Mobile, `ao remote-host enable`) still clear the account link, as on `main`, and **Share this computer** does not yet show that the link is gone. A follow-up adds the link state to the mobile status and lets the desktop link again (#7412).
- **Phone access follow-ups** (per-phone revoke, keeping the password when Connect Mobile is turned on again) go in a separate issue and PR.

title: test(chat): add opt-in large-chat profiling harness (partial #7259)
body:
Code changes: +0 -0  
Tests: +637 -5  
Others: +152 -0

## What this adds

Two developer tools for investigating slow chat rendering:

- **Measure a large chat:** render a generated chat with 1,850 tool rows and save how long its last message takes to become visible, browser freezes (long tasks), React rendering work, and JavaScript memory use. A separate check expands collapsed work and verifies that its content is present.
- **Compare before and after:** read saved results from two revisions and show median values, percentage changes, sample ranges, and a verdict: helped in these samples, regression observed, no clear improvement, or inconclusive.

These use the real renderer with generated data. They do not require a daemon or your private chats, and they do not change the app’s runtime behavior.

## How to use it

From `frontend/`, with the checkout’s Node version, dependencies, and Playwright Chromium installed, collect at least three samples before your change:

```sh
AO_PERF_BENCH=1 AO_E2E_PORT=5199 AO_PERF_LABEL=before \
  AO_PERF_DIR="$HOME/.ao/dev/chat-perf/before" \
  NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1536 \
  npm run test:e2e -- --grep 'largeTurn' --workers=1 --retries=0 --repeat-each=3
```

Apply your rendering change, then repeat that command with `AO_PERF_LABEL=after` and `AO_PERF_DIR="$HOME/.ao/dev/chat-perf/after"`. Use fresh output directories and the same machine, browser, viewport, launch settings, and cache/warm-up policy.

Compare the saved results:

```sh
node e2e/performance/compare-results.mjs \
  "$HOME/.ao/dev/chat-perf/before" "$HOME/.ao/dev/chat-perf/after"
```

The comparison rejects mismatched workloads or environments, mixed revisions within one side, duplicate samples, and diagnostic captures. Missing metrics or fewer than three samples per side produce an inconclusive result.

“Helped in these samples” means the median visibility time fell by more than 5%, with no supporting metric worsening by more than 5%. This is a simple reporting rule, not statistical proof. Check the sample ranges and repeat on a quiet machine. React rendering time is not commit-phase wall time, and memory readings are not normalized by forced garbage collection.

More details: [measurement and comparison README](frontend/e2e/performance/README.md).

## Why this is useful

It gives developers a repeatable workload and an easy before/after report, so future rendering changes can be judged using measurements instead of impressions. Saved results include the revision, workload identity, and environment settings to help catch invalid comparisons.

## What is still missing

**This PR does not fix slow chat opening and does not complete #7259.** No production optimization is included. Two local optimization approaches were rejected because they changed behavior.

The original safe five-chat sandbox and scripts are unavailable. We still need measurements on those real chats, a behavior-preserving fix, and a matched before/after comparison. The proposed under-400ms opening and no-over-200ms long-task targets have not been achieved or verified. Generated-chat results do not satisfy that acceptance. This PR remains draft.

## Validation

- All 14 dependency-free Node24 tests passed on rebased head `8a26b79121c1e9a091ef9aac59456ea2ef10ec0e` (1.835s).
- Historical check before this rebase: all 8 comparison tests also passed from a directory containing spaces.
