- Historical CI: all 10 reported checks passed at `2f3bae851cb35203735fdf1be36b87bc5174cbdf`, including typecheck, four component-test shards, renderer smoke, macOS helpers, general checks, and secret scanning. [CI run](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40514612237).

Full local frontend/native/browser suites were not rerun for the final test-launcher fix; Windows was not tested locally. The Node tests above ran locally; ordinary CI does not run the opt-in measurement/comparison contracts. Historical browser measurements and internal reviews apply to their recorded revisions, not the current head.

Rebased onto `main` at `55ed9b5ba07f8465b42a0d87e2c179011d288700`. The conflict resolution preserves main’s history-virtualization and `chatRenderCost` assertions alongside these disclosure checks. New-head scheduled checks passed: change selection, PR check, secret scan and CI aggregate. Current CI skips validation lanes for draft PRs, so the frontend suite did not run on this head; that skip is not a frontend validation pass. Historical CI, reviews and measurements do not qualify this rebased head. No production changes or new browser measurements.

title: [Bug]: Cursor reviewer runs under the user's `~/.cursor` permission rules instead of AO's reviewer profile
body:
I ran `cursor-agent` with the environment AO gives the Cursor reviewer (`CURSOR_DATA_DIR` pointing at AO's reviewer profile) and asked it to run `ls` and then `git status`. `ls` ran without asking; my personal `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` allows only `Shell(ls)`. `git status` stopped at `Not in allowlist: git status`, although AO's reviewer profile allows `Shell(git)`. When I also set `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` to the same profile folder, it reversed: `ls` stopped at `Not in allowlist: ls`. Expected: the Cursor reviewer runs under AO's reviewer profile, not under whatever I allowed in `~/.cursor`. **Before / after** (left: AO's reviewer environment; right: with `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` also set)
Agent-collected evidence Tested on cursor-agent `2026.10.22-27dcf5f`, against the reviewer profile AO generates on `main` at `a00ef3c770`. Each run starts a fresh `cursor-agent --trust` in a scratch repository and asks it to run one command. Two rule files are involved: | File | Allows | | --- | --- | | `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` (personal) | `Shell(ls)` | | AO reviewer profile `cli-config.json` | `Read(**)`, `Shell(git)`, `Shell(gh)`, `Shell(ao)`, `Shell(printf)` | Cursor sometimes runs a command without asking even when no rule file allows it: `uname -s`, allowed by neither file, ran without a prompt in 1 of 3 runs. So a run without a prompt does not show which rules applied. A **prompt** for a command does: it means that command is not on the active allowlist. | Environment | Command | Allowed by | Runs | Prompted | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` only (AO today) | `git status` | AO profile | 5 | 3 (`Not in allowlist: git status`) | | `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` only (AO today) | `ao --version` | AO profile | 3 | 1 (`Not in allowlist: ao`) | | `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` only (AO today) | `ls` | personal file | 2 | 0 | | `+ CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` | `git status` | AO profile | 3 | 0 | | `+ CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` | `ao --version` | AO profile | 3 | 0 | | `+ CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` | `ls` | personal file | 2 | 2 (`Not in allowlist: ls`) | | `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` only (control) | `uname -s` | neither | 3 | 2 | With only `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`, Cursor prompted for commands AO's profile allows, so the profile was not the active allowlist. With `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` set, it never prompted for those, and prompted for `ls`, which only the personal file allows. **Where AO sets it**: `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/config.go` (added in #3384, reused by #5782): ```go cursorDataDirEnv = "CURSOR_DATA_DIR" ... return map[string]string{cursorDataDirEnv: profileDir} ``` `installReviewerConfig` writes `cli-config.json` into `profileDir`. **Where Cursor reads it**: the installed CLI's bundled JS (minified, identifiers as shipped): ```js function o(){const t=process.env.CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR;if(t?.trim())return t; const e=process.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME;return e?.trim()?(0,i.join)(e,"cursor"):(0,i.join)((0,s.homedir)(),".cursor")} function m(){return(0,i.join)(o(),"cli-config.json")} function c(){const t=process.env.CURSOR_DATA_DIR;return t?.trim()?t:(0,i.join)((0,s.homedir)(),".cursor")} function u(){return(0,i.join)(c(),"projects")} ``` `cli-config.json` comes from `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` (then `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cursor`, then `~/.cursor`). `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` only sets the `projects` data path. **Related:** once the profile is applied, its whole-tool rules (`Shell(git)`, `Shell(printf)`) let `git push` and `printf x > file` run without a prompt. **Not checked:** whether older Cursor CLI versions read `cli-config.json` from `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`; a live AO review run (the profile file and binary were used directly). **Related issues:** #6752 / #6896 (Cursor worker role prompt not loading; a different file). #5235 plans `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` + `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` for Cursor account isolation. No duplicate found for "cursor reviewer", "CURSOR_DATA_DIR", "CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR", "cursor reviewer profile" or "cli-config.json" in open and closed issues and PRs.

title: feat(api): raise the task size cap to 100 KiB
body:
Code changes: +23 -16\
Tests: +70 -10\
Others: +2 -2 (generated OpenAPI)

## What

Raises the new-task and spawn prompt cap from 16 KiB to 100 KiB, and makes Qwen workers launch with a 100 KiB task on Linux.

- `maxPromptLen` 16 KiB → 100 KiB (`sessions.go`), covering `TASK_TOO_LONG` (delegate) and `PROMPT_TOO_LONG` (spawn), with the error text updated.
- `maxLength` on `SpawnSessionRequest.prompt` and `DelegateTaskRequest.brief` 16384 → 102400, with `openapi.yaml` regenerated. `schema.ts` doesn't emit `maxLength`, so it is unchanged.
- Mobile `PROMPT_TOO_LONG` copy now says 100 KiB.
- Qwen workers on macOS/Linux: the task is written to `<key>.submit.jsonl`, and the launch wrapper `mv`s it into Qwen's input file. The wrapper's `sh -c` script now carries only paths.

## Why

Long tasks, such as a pasted compaction summary, failed in the composer with "Task must be 16 KiB or fewer". The 16 KiB cap protected tmux launches, which new sessions no longer use (see How).

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Delegate with a 16,385-byte brief → `400 TASK_TOO_LONG` "Task must be 16 KiB or fewer", shown in the composer | Accepted up to 102,400 bytes; 102,401 → `400 TASK_TOO_LONG` "Task must be 100 KiB or fewer" |
| Spawn with a prompt over 16,384 bytes → `400 PROMPT_TOO_LONG` | Limit 102,400 bytes; message "Prompt must be 100 KiB or fewer" |
| Qwen wrapper inlines the escaped task twice: a 34,373-byte argument at 16 KiB, and 206,405–718,733 bytes at 100 KiB, which Linux rejects with `fork/exec /usr/bin/sh: argument list too long` | Script argument holds only paths; a worst-case 100 KiB Qwen task launches on Linux |
| Mobile: "Keep it to 16 KiB or fewer" | "Keep it to 100 KiB or fewer" |

No UI code changed; the composer shows the API's message.

## How

The 16 KiB cap kept tmux launches safe. TUI agents get the task as a command-line argument, and tmux refuses a `new-session` command over about 16 KiB (tmux 3.6a: 16,200 bytes worked, 16,400 failed with `command too long`).

New sessions no longer launch through tmux:

| Path | How the task reaches the agent | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| Chat | Normal turn (`chat_spawn.go`) | None from the launch command |
| New TUI, macOS/Linux | Native PTY host, one `execve` argument (`runtimeselect/hybrid.go`, `conpty/spawn_unix.go`) | macOS 1 MiB total (`ARG_MAX`); Linux 128 KiB per argument |
| tmux | Older tmux handles, or fallback when the PTY host fails to start | About 13 KiB of task |

100 KiB stays under the Linux per-argument limit, with headroom for the issue context that `prompt.go` appends to the task.

Qwen was the one adapter that put the task inside a shell script: the remote-input wrapper embedded the JSON- and shell-escaped submit line twice. Staging the line in a file removes the task from argv. `mv` within one directory is a single rename, so Qwen's input watcher never reads a partial line.

## Testing

- `TestSessionsAPI_DelegateTaskAcceptsLongBrief` sends exactly 100 KiB; `...RejectsBriefPastLaunchSafeLimit` sends 100 KiB + 1 and checks the new message.
- `spawn.source.test.ts` asserts the new mobile copy.
- `TestRemoteInputWorkerLaunchesMaxSizeTask` launches a worst-case 102,400-byte task (`<'"` and newlines) through the real Qwen wrapper with a stub `qwen`, checks the input file byte for byte, and keeps every argv element under 128 KiB. On Linux (Debian bookworm, kernel 6.10, 4 KiB pages) the old code fails with `argument list too long`; the fix passes.
- Lab runs on macOS with an isolated AO daemon, each task carrying a mid and a final marker code:
  - Claude Code and Codex, TUI and Chat: 100 KiB ASCII, multibyte and shell-hostile tasks arrived intact.
  - Real Qwen Code 0.26.6 against a recording fake OpenAI endpoint: 15 KiB and 100 KiB ASCII, multibyte and shell-hostile tasks reached the worker's model request intact.
- Full CI suites not run locally; CI is the gate.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **tmux fallback:** a TUI task over about 13 KiB that lands on tmux (PTY host failed to start, or restart of an older tmux session) fails at launch with `command too long` instead of the composer's clear message. Measured: 13,344 bytes worked, 13,568 failed; env exports and flags share tmux's limit.
- **Windows TUI:** a task over the 32,767 UTF-16 command-line limit fails at launch with the existing `WINDOWS_COMMAND_LINE_TOO_LONG` error.
- **Still at 16 KiB:** agent cue prompts (`domain/cue.go` `MaxCuePromptLength`) and tracker-intake prompts (`trackerintake` `maxIntakePromptLen`). Both stay spawnable because they are under the new cap, but their "matches the spawn cap" comments are now stale. Raise them separately if wanted.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [ ] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene (full CI suites not run locally)
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: fix(cursor): apply the reviewer profile Cursor actually reads
body:
Code changes: +24 -6
Tests: +35 -1
Others: +0 -0

## What

The Cursor reviewer now runs with AO's reviewer permission profile instead of the user's personal `~/.cursor` rules, and that profile is narrowed so it can't push or write files.

## Why

Fixes #7297.

AO writes the reviewer's `cli-config.json` to its own profile folder, but only sets `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` to point at it. Cursor CLI (2026.10.22) reads `cli-config.json` from `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR`, then `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cursor`, then `~/.cursor`. `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` only sets the `projects` path. So every Cursor review ran under whatever the user had allowed in `~/.cursor`.

## How

- `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/config.go`: `reviewerEnv` now sets both `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` and `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` to the profile folder.
- Same file, narrower rules. The old profile allowed whole tools (`Shell(git)`, `Shell(gh)`, `Shell(ao)`, `Shell(printf)`), so once it was actually applied, `git push` and `printf x > file` ran without a prompt. The allowlist is now `Read(**)`, `git status/diff/log/show`, `gh pr view/diff/checks` and `ao review submit`; `git push`, `git commit` and `ao spawn/send/stop` are denied. Anything else prompts.

Cursor sometimes runs commands without asking even when no rule allows them, so this profile is a guard, not a hard boundary. AO's daemon also refuses session-management requests from reviewers (#6842, separate PR).

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/` (new `TestReviewerProfileIsActuallyReadAndNarrow` checks both env vars point at the profile and the allow/deny lists).
- Live, cursor-agent `2026.10.22-27dcf5f`: with only `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`, Cursor prompted for `git status` (allowed by AO's profile) and ran `ls` (allowed only in my `~/.cursor`). With `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` set, it reversed. Full table and screenshot in #7297.
  Not checked: older Cursor CLI versions; a full AO review run end to end; the narrowed rules were checked by the unit test, not in a live run.

title: [Bug]: `ao review trigger` right after `gh pr create` fails until AO discovers the PR
body:
### What went wrong?

A worker opened a PR with `gh pr create` and then ran `ao review trigger`. It failed with `REVIEW_INVALID`:

> AO is not tracking a PR for worker "<worker>" yet; if you just opened one, run `ao review trigger --pr <url>`

Running `ao review trigger --pr <url>` worked.

AO attaches a session's PRs when the SCM observer discovers them on its next poll. Until then, a trigger without `--pr` finds no PR. The PR is already open on the session's own branch, which AO can look up when the trigger runs. The error also does not name the worker or its branch, so the suggested command only works from inside the worker session.

Expected: the trigger finds the open PR on the worker's branch and reviews it. If it cannot, the error should print the exact retry command.

## What

- Add a random, persisted project telemetry UUID scoped to each local installation and project. Usage events contain no repository names, paths, PR URLs or titles, message content, or raw local project and session IDs.
- Count newly accepted direct human project Chat messages once at the durable insert boundary. Exclude standalone sessions and all spawn opening prompts. Store bounded pending counts per session and flush about every 30 minutes, after archive, at desktop exit, and at daemon stop.
- Count each provider PR associated with an AO worker once, plus its first merged outcome once. Existing worker PR associations are backfilled once, including already merged outcomes marked historical. Later ownership changes do not erase the recorded worker association.
- Apply opt-out and remote property allowlists. Document exact counting and privacy scope in `docs/telemetry.md` and add storage, migration, HTTP, daemon, and telemetry regression tests.
- Keep local usage facts pending through temporary identity or remote setup failures, wait for remote queue capacity, and move the initial flush off the startup path.
- Retry a transient Windows sharing violation whenever a persistent host reads `host.json`, addressing the reported `windows-workspace` ACP hibernate failure.

## Why

AO needs project usage and worker PR outcome counts that remain stable across restarts without sending repository identity or message content. Review follow-up also prevents one standalone summary from blocking all exports and keeps telemetry failures from failing core PR writes.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| No stable project usage grouping ID was emitted. | Usage summaries carry an opaque random UUID per local installation and project. |
| Direct human project Chat messages had no batched usage count. | One durable per-session count is flushed about every 30 minutes and after archive, at desktop exit, or at daemon stop. |
| A standalone count could stop every message and PR flush. | Standalone messages are not counted, and earlier standalone summaries are skipped while project batches drain. |
| An asynchronous delegated opening prompt could be counted as a direct Chat message. | Queued opening prompts stay uncounted; a later direct message counts once. |
| Worker PR associations and merged outcomes had no deduplicated measurement. | Each provider PR contributes one worker association and one first merged outcome per project, including after reassignment; historical associations are labeled. |
| A telemetry write error could fail a successful PR merge or observation. | The PR write succeeds and logs the telemetry error. |
| A burst above PostHog buffer capacity silently lost reserved usage batches. | Usage events wait for queue capacity. |
| An identity write failure discarded counts, and a missing PostHog sink drained them locally. | Identity write failures pause draining; missing remote setup keeps new facts pending. |
| The first historical flush delayed daemon startup. | It runs in the background, and shutdown has a five-second flush deadline. |

## How

- The message count increments in the same transaction as a newly accepted direct human project Chat message. The asynchronous provisioning queue preserves the opening prompt marker through storage. Opening prompts, worker automation, reviewer Chat, retries, replays, tool calls, active turn steering, and TUI input are excluded. Pending counts survive restart. A batch is reserved before export. Usage events wait for PostHog queue capacity, while a crash, cancellation, daily cap, or send failure after reservation can still lose that batch without replaying it.
- The worker association is recorded in a local table keyed by provider PR identity. Polls and worker takeovers do not add counts. Orchestrator-only PRs are excluded. Historical backfill is eligible when events are first enabled if its rows were not discarded during a disabled observation. Explicit opt-out discards pending rows before export.
- Opt-out discard scans merged PRs once and updates only pending measurement flags. An identity persistence failure pauses draining but retains pending counts. Archive requests signal the flusher without waiting for export. The Electron opt-out request also returns without waiting for the daemon flush. The initial flush runs in the background and shutdown uses a five-second deadline. The minute pass skips the PR scan; full passes run about every 30 minutes and on close. Usage events keep a 100,000 per-name rolling 24-hour emergency cap per daemon process, with no minute cap. Counts beyond the cap are dropped after reservation.
- Every persistent host descriptor read retries Windows `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` for at most one second, including startup, reconciliation, PID lookup, and shutdown.
- Rebasing onto main `dbeaf19c8a9decc2330fc1fac8c36f22b417dabd` preserves the already merged telemetry cleanup, retention migration, and Sentry privacy changes. No extra events were removed. Harshit owns the PostHog inventory and keep/drop decisions. This PR adds no dashboard, cohort, tier, email, replay, policy, website, or ingestion changes.

## Testing

- Complete daemon, telemetry, persistent host, SQLite, HTTP, and Chat package suites passed on the review fix. The full daemon suite passed again after the final remote setup fix.
- Focused regressions passed for remote buffer backpressure, identity persistence failure, unavailable remote setup retaining a message count, and standalone PR exclusion. The Windows descriptor package cross compiled; its Windows-only regression requires the Windows CI runner.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `npm run frontend:typecheck`, `gofmt`, and `git diff --check` passed. Pinned `sqlc v1.31.1` regenerated the query artifact.
- A complete `go test ./...` run on the rebased base failed in unrelated host-dependent commandcode, OpenCode, tmux, CLI, systemcheck, and session manager tests. The pinned local golangci-lint previously could not typecheck Go 1.27.3 export data. These are validation gaps, not passes. Remote CI was not polled after this push.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` and rebased the existing PR branch onto current main
- [x] One usage measurement PR with a targeted fix for its reported Windows CI job
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in with observable nonvisual behavior
- [x] Regression tests cover privacy, counts, deduplication, persistence, flush, and opt-out
- [ ] Relevant remote CI checks pass

title: fix(chat): end Claude turns without waiting for the context usage snapshot
body:
Code changes: +93 -31  
Tests: +80 -34  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

In Claude Code chat sessions, the session stayed **Working** for up to 2 s after the answer had finished. AO's patch to `claude-agent-acp` (added in #5829 for the context meter) awaited `session.query.getContextUsage()` (2 s timeout) inside the `result` handler, *before* the turn settled. On large conversations that call takes about 1 s, so every consumer of turn end was late: the Working indicator, the idle state, notifications, queued message delivery, and agents or scripts waiting on the session.

Measured on real sessions: under 200k tokens of context, 8% of turns were delayed; above 300k tokens, about 60% were, with a median of 0.9 s and a maximum of 2.0 s (the timeout). Claude Code's own Stop hooks had already finished about 25 ms after the answer; nothing else was in flight during the gap.

## Change

`patchClaudeContextUsage` now replaces the result's usage block. The turn settles immediately, and the same `usage_update` (snapshot `used`/`size`, cost, origin) is published in the background once the snapshot arrives:

- Same fallback as before: if the snapshot fails, returns zero, or takes over 2 s, the update uses the last message's usage.
- The snapshot only updates the turn's usage value while that turn is still current, so it can't change the next turn's value.
- It doesn't overwrite the context window if the model was switched while the snapshot was pending.
- A failed send is logged instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.
- The patch requires an exact (whitespace-normalized) match of the upstream 0.70.0 block and fails the build otherwise.

AO already accepts usage updates when no turn is running: usage is stored per conversation and overwritten, and cost is a running total. The persistent host forwards (or buffers) notifications that arrive outside a prompt.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.test.mjs`: 31 passed (4 new: the result settles before the snapshot arrives, fallback, model switch while pending, failed send).
- `node scripts/build-acp-runtime.mjs`: the patch applies to the real pinned 0.70.0 adapter alongside the other five patches; `node --check` passes.
- `AO_LIVE_CLAUDE_ACP=1 go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp -run '^TestLiveClaudeACP$'`: passes against the patched runtime.
- Live ACP comparison on a copy of a ~460k-token conversation, shipped adapter vs this patch:
  - Turn with a slow snapshot: the turn ended **884 ms** after the last answer text on the shipped adapter, **81 ms** with this patch (usage update followed 796 ms later). Same usage values.
  - Model switch right after a turn: no hang (13 ms). New prompt plus interrupt right after a turn: cancelled in 2 ms, and the next turn was normal.
  - Back-to-back turns: usage and cost updates arrive in order and never regress.

Lint, typecheck and full suites were not run locally; relying on CI for those.

## Tradeoffs

- The context meter can update up to about 2 s after the turn ends instead of at the same moment.
- A compaction started within about 1 s of a turn ending may compute its "freed X tokens" summary from the previous turn's message usage rather than the snapshot. The compaction itself is unaffected.
- SDK control requests are serialized, so a model switch or interrupt issued while a slow snapshot is still pending may queue behind it (up to about 1 s). This was possible before too (during the held turn); it was not reproduced in the live run, where the switch happened after a fast snapshot.

title: feat(mobile): paste images into the chat composer
body:
Code changes: +697 -51  
Tests: +130 -1  
Others: +64 -0

## Summary

On mobile, pasting an image into the chat composer now attaches it, as it does in other chat apps. Long-press the field, tap **Paste**, and the image shows up as an attachment chip: the same thumbnail, ×, and send path as a photo picked from the library, labelled "Pasted image". On Android, tapping the copied image in Gboard's clipboard strip attaches it too. Text pastes behave exactly as before.

Both the session chat composer and the reviewer reply composer get this.

## How it works

- **`native/image-paste`**: a new local RN module, autolinked the same way as `response-selection`. JS attaches it to the composer field's react tag on layout, so no other text field in the app changes.
  - **Android**: an `OnReceiveContentListener` for `image/*` on the composer's `EditText`. It handles both the Paste menu item and keyboard image insertion (commit-content). Any text in the same paste is left to the field. Because an image paste doesn't change the text, the floating Paste toolbar would stay open, so RN's insertion and selection toolbar callbacks are wrapped to close it. Reads run on a background thread, which holds the accepted payload until they finish. For a keyboard insertion, that payload owns the IME's temporary read grant; the grant is released afterwards. Only clip URIs from other apps' content providers are read. `file://` URIs and the app's own provider authorities are never opened, because reads run with the app's permissions; they show as "couldn't be read".
  - **iOS**: overrides `RCTUITextView`'s own `paste:` and `canPerformAction:withSender:`, but only for attached views. The image path runs only when the clipboard holds just an image: no strings, and either `hasImages` or a type conforming to `public.image` (`hasImages` misses HEIC). Paste is offered for it, and the pasteboard images are sent to JS. Spreadsheet cells and rich copies carry an image rendering beside their text, so they still paste as text. The pasteboard data is read inside the user's Paste action, so iOS doesn't show the "Allow Paste" prompt. Decoding, re-encoding and base64 then run on a background queue.
  - Both platforms pass PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP through unchanged and re-encode anything else (HEIC, TIFF) as JPEG. Images over 10 MB are reported by size and not sent across the bridge. Each batch is also capped natively at the composer's 8 images and 25 MB: images past either limit are never read or encoded, and the event's `overflow` (`count`/`size`) becomes the matching notice. On iOS, an item's representations are read on demand in the pasteboard's own order, stopping at the first pass-through one that fits. If one is over 10 MB (a PNG of a photo), the next one that fits is used; otherwise that oversized one is re-encoded as JPEG. Other types, such as a Retina TIFF over Universal Clipboard, are never fetched unless nothing else can be used.
- **`useImagePaste`** turns the native event into picker-shaped assets.
- **`composerImages.acceptImageAssets`**, with its `attachComposerImages` store helper, is the one image gate now used by the photo picker and paste in both composers. It covers supported types (detected from the bytes, as #7237 does), the 10 MB / 25 MB limits and the 8-item cap. Results are written to the per-session attachment store, so behaviour on Android chat remounts is unchanged.

## Release note

This adds native code, so it changes the fingerprint runtime and **needs a new store build**. It can't ship as an OTA update.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) and the full mobile `vitest` suite pass (245 files, 2518 tests). New tests cover the gate and its store helper, the hook's tag scoping and attach/detach, a composer paste → chip → oversized notice → send flow, the reviewer composer's `attachmentsEnabled` paste gate, and how native overflow reaches the notice.
- Manual tests on Debug builds of the earlier base (no RN/Expo version changes since), using a temporary lab route that rendered the reviewer composer:
  - **iOS 26.5 simulator:** with an image on the clipboard, Paste appears and attaches a chip, with no permission prompt. Text paste still inserts text. A mixed text + PNG clipboard (like copied spreadsheet cells) pastes its text and attaches nothing. A HEIC-only clipboard attaches a JPEG. With a temporary read log, a small PNG next to a 17 MB TIFF read only the PNG, and a 17 MB PNG next to a 17 MB TIFF read only the PNG and re-encoded it. Ten pasted PNGs read only the first 8 and attached 8 with "You can attach up to 8 items.". Four 8.3 MB PNGs attached 3 (25 MB) with "Images must total under 25 MB.". A 17 MB PNG listed before a 4.3 MB JPEG sends the JPEG, and the 17 MB PNG alone is re-encoded to a JPEG that fits. Sending delivers the text plus `image/png`.
  - **Android emulator:**
    - Paste attaches a chip and inserts no `content://` text, and the toolbar closes afterwards.
    - Gboard's clipboard "Image" chip, which uses Gboard's own content provider, attaches the image.
    - A clip pointing at the app's own `FileProvider` shows "couldn't be read" and attaches nothing.
    - Text paste still inserts text.
    - Sending delivers the original PNG bytes.

## Not covered

- iOS keyboard stickers and Genmoji.
- Physical devices.

title: fix(chat): keep OpenCode Go model routes selectable
body:
Code changes: +19 -4  
Tests: +98 -2  
Others: +0 -0  

## Summary

Keep OpenCode Go models selectable in Chat when OpenCode advertises the same model name through another provider. For example, `opencode/deepseek-v4-flash` and `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` now remain separate choices and selecting Go sends its exact provider/model ID.

## Cause and change

OpenCode ACP advertises provider-qualified IDs and names. Chat removes the name prefix, but its generic group-label helper treats both `opencode` and `opencode-go` as the harness's own group and suppresses them. Name deduplication then folds the two routes into aliases of one row. Which route remains depends on the current selection, so a model enabled in Settings can disappear from the running Chat menu.

Preserve the explicit provider ID as the group for OpenCode 1 and 2 before name deduplication, including releases that send bare model labels. Readable `groupName` headings accompany the stable provider keys, so menus show labels such as “OpenCode Go” and “Z.ai Coding Plan”. Existing provider grouping stays intact. Other harness model-selection logic and Claude alias handling keep their existing behavior.

A shared `readableProviderName` formats display labels independently of harness-specific group suppression; neither OpenCode call site relies on an empty harness argument. Provider headings intentionally remain visible for single-provider OpenCode menus, keeping their route identity explicit and the menu layout consistent. Regression coverage includes this case.

This fixes choices already advertised by the live agent; it does not add unadvertised catalog models or change authentication. It is separate from DeepSeek recovery PR #7303.

## Validation

- GitHub Actions [tests-only baseline](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40410822764), commit `c785606c70`: the new OpenCode regression failed with **expected 2 model rows, received 1**, in both current-route selections. The unified picker also lost a route.
- Regression coverage includes both OpenCode majors, exact route IDs, standalone and unified Chat pickers, existing explicit grouping, and provider-prefixed/bare names.
- Original-fix GitHub Actions [Frontend run](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40420105056), commit `3e6e9b5ecc`: all four Vitest shards, typecheck, frontend checks, renderer smoke, macOS helper, and the aggregate frontend gate passed. The new regression tests pass after failing on the tests-only commit.
- Per user instruction, no local tests, builds, lint, typechecks, smoke checks, or live UI/provider verification were run. Validation is exclusively in GitHub Actions.

- Review follow-up `d3243392cf`: preserve raw deduplication keys while adding readable headings; helper and both picker assertions updated. GitHub Actions [Frontend run 41276324622](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41276324622) passed on this commit: all four Vitest shards, typecheck, checks, renderer smoke, macOS helper/layout, and the aggregate frontend gate. The live consolidated review thread is resolved.

- Brand-casing follow-up `cb3f547e01`: shared provider labels now spell OpenCode, OpenCode Go, OpenCode Zen, and Z.ai Coding Plan correctly. Updated picker assertions also cover unknown-provider fallback formatting. The supplied thread is resolved; Validation is superseded by the formatter follow-up below.

- Formatter/single-provider follow-up `3dd3da4102`: extracted explicit shared display-name formatting, preserved generic own-group suppression, added single-provider heading coverage, and resolved both remaining live threads. Final GitHub Actions [Frontend run 41286891975](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41286891975) passed for this commit: all four Vitest shards, frontend typecheck/checks, renderer smoke, macOS helper/layout, and the aggregate frontend gate.

title: fix(chat): keep the composer pickers in place and responsive
body:
## What changed

- **Permission menu** opens upward, lined up with its button's right edge (it sits next to Send), 20rem wide. Long descriptions wrap instead of stretching the panel across the window.
- **Agent/model menu** lines up with the button's left edge, which doesn't move when the label changes width. When rows disappear, the menu shrinks from the bottom: the top edge and every row stay where they are, and the lost height becomes margin outside the panel.
- **Effort** shows a disabled "Default" row when the selected model has no effort choices, instead of leaving a hole in the menu.
- **The agent picker stays usable while a setting is being saved.** Saves for model, effort and fast mode are queued: each one waits for the one before it, the picker shows the new choice immediately, and only the newest response is applied. Before, every row was disabled until the agent confirmed. The "Loading settings…" row now only appears when there's nothing to show yet.
- **Less style recalculation.** In a trace of the installed app, opening, closing and hovering menus each restyled about 2,200–2,900 elements (30–40 ms each):
  - `OptionMenu` and `DropdownMenu` are now non-modal by default. A modal menu locks scrolling and turns off pointer events on `<body>`.
  - Hovering from one row to the next row in the same menu changes focus once instead of twice.
  - The model list no longer reads `scrollTop` when it first opens.

## Non-modal, without click-through

`OptionMenu` and `DropdownMenu` are now non-modal unless `modal` is passed. An outside click still only closes the menu: the click that follows the outside pointerdown is swallowed. The pointerdown itself does reach the page, so another menu's trigger opens on the first click. Menus that pass `modal={false}` explicitly (the agent picker, Cmd+K, the terminal context menu, the title bar) keep letting the click through.

## Overlapping saves

- Saving the agent's settings times out after 60 s, the same as other option writes, so a hung save can't hold later picks in the queue.
- A pick that was queued behind an earlier one is checked against the options the agent returned for that earlier pick. It's dropped if that option or value no longer exists, for example an effort level the new model doesn't offer.
- If an earlier pick fails while later ones are still saving, only that option is reverted, unless a later pick changed the same option.
- A menu that shrank settles back onto its trigger once the pointer leaves it, unless the pointer moved into a submenu.

## How to test

1. Open a chat and click the permission button next to Send. The menu should open upward, with its right edge lined up with the button. Long descriptions wrap onto a second line.
2. Open the agent/model picker. Change the effort, toggle Fast mode, and switch to a model without effort choices. Rows shouldn't slide sideways or drop under the cursor, and no gap should appear inside the menu.
3. With OpenCode and a model that has no effort choices, Effort shows a greyed "Default".
4. Change the model, then change the effort straight away. Both should apply, and the rows should stay clickable while the first change saves.
5. Open and close a few ⋯ menus and composer menus. Hovering rows and opening and closing menus should feel lighter.
6. With a ⋯ menu open, click a button elsewhere on the page. The menu should close, and the button should not activate.

title: Warn when another ao on PATH shadows the app's bundled CLI
body:
## Problem

A user turned on **Settings → Remote hosts → Allow access from your devices** and then ran `ao remote-host status` in an AO terminal to get the connection details. The command failed with:

```
unknown command "remote-host" for "ao"
```

The cause was an older `ao` that came before the app's bundled CLI on `PATH`. AO starts terminals with `…/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon` first on `PATH`. The user's `~/.zshrc` and `~/.zprofile` then unconditionally prepend `~/.local/bin`, which held a symlink to a local dev build from June that predates `remote-host`. A broken `npm link` of `@aoagents/ao` (it failed with "no prebuilt binary for darwin-arm64") was also on `PATH`.

Nothing told the user their `ao` was not the app's `ao`. The error looked like an AO bug.

## What already exists

- `ao doctor` has a `checkAOBinary` check (`backend/internal/cli/doctor.go`) that flags an `ao` on `PATH` shadowing the daemon's binary. However:
  - it only runs when someone asks for it;
  - when a shadow exists, typing `ao doctor` runs the **shadowing** binary, which may be too old to have the check.
- The desktop CLI link status (`frontend/src/shared/cli-link.ts`, `pathIssue`) is Developer Mode only.

## Proposal

Warn proactively when the `ao` a user's shell resolves is not the bundled CLI:

1. **Desktop app:** on startup (and maybe when Settings opens), resolve `ao` through the user's login and interactive shell env (the same `shell-env` probe the app already uses). If it does not resolve to the bundled binary, show a non-blocking notice. The notice should give the shadowing path and version, the bundled path, and the fix: remove or reorder the shadowing install. Never edit the shell rc files automatically.
2. **CLI:** when the bundled CLI is invoked by full path or by the daemon, it could cheaply note a shadow. Item 1 is the main fix, though, because the stale binary can't warn about itself.
3. Optionally, make docs and settings copy that tells users to run `ao …` mention the full bundled path as a fallback.

## Acceptance

- With a different `ao` first on the interactive shell's `PATH`, the desktop app shows a warning naming both paths.
- With the bundled `ao` first (or a symlink to it, such as the Developer Mode CLI link), no warning appears.
- No shell startup files are modified.

title: feat: configure provider keys across supported harnesses
body:
Code changes: +4805 -119  
Tests: +2473 -28  
Others: +1878 -9

## Summary
- **Account panel for every supported harness:** reviewed native sign-in methods plus provider keys, with the terminal login kept as a fallback.
  - Account sign-ins and API keys are listed separately.
  - A key row shows only its own state ("Not set" or "Saved, ending 1234"), and the note about AO-launched sessions appears once under the key list.
- **API keys settings page:** set each provider key once, and AO-launched sessions get it (see the one exception under limitations).
  - Keys are shown masked (last four characters).
  - A key can be checked against the provider's models endpoint before it is saved, so a mistyped key is never stored.
  - Keys read by several harnesses are listed first, with search and a count of saved keys.
- **Provider catalogs:** where a harness supports many providers, its Account panel offers one searchable "Provider API key" picker over that harness's own catalog, and saves the key in the harness's own credential store, where it outranks environment variables.
- **Device environment is opt-in, and session-scoped.** "Share with other apps" publishes a key to the current OS user's login session: macOS launchd and Linux's systemd user manager, reapplied when AO starts. Nothing is written outside `~/.ao`, so Windows doesn't offer it yet (`deviceAvailable: false`).
  - A value the user set themselves is never replaced. Turning sharing off, or removing the key, unsets only AO's own copy, best effort.
  - AO-launched sessions receive saved keys either way.
- **Native stores:**
  - Continue gets a model route in `~/.continue/config.yaml` and a key in `~/.continue/.env`.
  - Qwen gets a provider/model route in its user settings.
  - OpenHands gets `LLM_API_KEY` and a LiteLLM `LLM_MODEL`.
  - DeepSeek Harness gets `refs.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`, the record its Models page writes. AO takes its `<file>.lock` (holder PID), writes a 0600 temp file and renames it, and keeps comments and other entries.
- **Model ID where a key alone can't select a working provider:** Qwen and Continue (plus OpenHands, which needs a LiteLLM ID) can now fill a model picker from the provider.
- **Claude Code:** the panel warns that an Anthropic key can replace the Claude subscription and bill the API account.
- **OMP sign-in probe fix:** `agent.db` uses WAL, so a read-only open fails while OMP is not running. The probe now falls back to an immutable read when no `-wal` file exists.

## Provider catalogs: done and remaining
Of AO's 38 harnesses:

| Status | Count | Harnesses |
|---|---|---|
| Done, provider picker | 6 | OpenCode (219), Kilo Code (219), MiMo Code (208), Crush (36), Pi (34), OMP (62) |
| Remaining candidates | 6 | Cline, Hermes, Autohand, Aider, Goose, OpenCode 2 |
| Blocked | 1 | Prime Agent: its compiled binary carries no provider table AO can rely on |
| Provider key + model through fixed lists | 3 | Qwen, Continue, OpenHands |
| Single vendor or account sign-in (no picker needed) | 22 | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Grok, Amp, Auggie, Droid, Devin, Kiro, Muse, Agy, Command Code, Gemini CLI, Kimi, Vibe, DeepSeek Harness, Kimchi, fx, CodeWhale, memcode, Unreal Agent |

How each finished harness saves a key:
- **OpenCode, Kilo Code, MiMo Code:**
  - Provider list: the models.dev cache each one keeps (`~/.cache/<harness>/models.json`).
  - Key saved as `{"type":"api","key"}` in that harness's `auth.json`. MiMo's data directory comes from `mimo debug paths`.
- **Crush:**
  - Provider list: the Catwalk catalog it caches (`providers.json`).
  - Key goes in `providers.<id>.api_key` in the `crush.json` beside it, under Crush's `crush.json.lock`, keeping every other setting. The data directory follows Crush's `GlobalConfigData()` (`CRUSH_GLOBAL_DATA`, then `XDG_DATA_HOME`). Keys containing `` $`\'" `` are rejected because Crush passes them to its shell expander, and the sign-in fields Crush itself drops on a key save are removed.
- **Pi:**
  - Provider list: a table generated from `@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.4.0.
  - Key goes in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` under Pi's proper-lockfile lock, written atomically, with `$` and a leading `!` escaped for Pi's config-value templates.
- **OMP:**
  - Provider list: a table generated from oh-my-pi v18.13.3 `rules.json`.
  - Key is imported through `omp auth import -` as a login-sourced key, which replaces that provider's earlier API keys. A key starting with `!` is rejected because OMP would run it as a shell command.
- **All of them:** providers that need more than a key (a region, an account, an endpoint, or OAuth only) stay with each harness's native sign-in. The Pi and OMP tables are pinned to those releases and need regenerating when new providers ship.

## Account sign-in without the terminal `/login`
Nine harnesses sign in by typing `/login` (or `/auth`) into a hidden terminal.

**Now driven by AO's own background login (2)**
- Their documented non-interactive commands run in the background, and only the reviewed login link and device code are published, as for Codex and Claude Code.
- **Copilot:**
  - GitHub in the browser (`copilot login --web-flow`).
  - A device code (`--device-code`, at `github.com/login/device`).
  - A GitHub token piped into `copilot login --with-token`, which keeps it in Copilot's own credential store. This replaces the AO-injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` row.
  - GitHub Enterprise and Entra stay in Copilot's own picker.
- **Kimi:** Kimi Code's device flow for either region (`kimi login --region global|mainland-cn`).

**Still in the terminal (7)**
- Pi, OMP, Kimchi, Droid, Prime Agent, Gemini CLI and Qwen expose no non-interactive account login: Pi's `auth` command only checks and prints, and OMP's only imports and exports.
- Their OAuth sign-in stays in the terminal. Each already takes a key from the panel.

## Fixes from code review
- **Numbered native menus:**
  - They accept Enter, so a CLI that reads a line can finish.
  - Only the latest menu in the scrollback is read, and a cursor-marked entry counts.
  - Each choice sends the digit the CLI printed rather than its position in the list.
- **No slow save stalls other logins:** key saves (`omp auth import`, `mimo debug paths`, the Pi lock, `launchctl`, `systemctl`) run under the harness's own login reservation. The service-wide lock is taken only to record the result, and menu keystrokes are sent outside it.
- **No untracked device key:** publishing to the OS user environment records the key as AO-published first, and rolls back only the keys that call newly published if publishing or saving fails.
- **Startup and large catalogs:** opted-in keys are republished at startup in the background, and the model-list response cap rises from 4 to 32 MiB.

## Second review round
- **Held-back keys stay held back everywhere:** `providerkeys.Withheld` applies the per-harness rule to sessions, reviewers, Claude Code's probe and account check, and (via `WithheldForSignIn`) every login command and terminal. It fails closed when the store can't be read.
- **Native sign-in:** an exit counts only when the harness's probe confirms it; only then is the API-key claim released. Answered menus in scrollback are ignored, a numbered choice is refused if the menu changed, and Droid, Qwen and Prime Agent no longer offer a guided sign-in they can't open.
- **Key form:** `device` is optional and keeps the current setting; the panel waits for the saved keys (with Retry) before saving; menu actions go through the main-process IPC.
- **Locks:** the Pi and DeepSeek Harness locks never spin on a lock they can't remove; DeepSeek ports dsh-atomic-write 0.2.2's takeover protocol exactly.
- **Native config writers:** Continue (CONTINUE_GLOBAL_DIR, legacy config.json, YAML anchors), Crush (see above), Gemini (`GEMINI_CLI_HOME`, key also in session env) and Qwen edit their files in place, keeping comments, trailing commas, BOM and layout.
- **Key check:** Gemini and xAI 400s read as invalid, redirects are never followed, regional Moonshot/DashScope rejections read as unverified. **OMP:** Windows-safe SQLite URI for the immutable fallback.

## Validation
- Parent #7163 was squash-merged; this PR now targets `main`, merged against the parent's final head so only real conflicts with later `main` changes needed resolving (Settings catalog, LocalHarnessContent, locales).
- The second review round was validated in CI only: per the owner's instruction, nothing was run on the Windows workstation.
- Passed locally: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, full agentauth and providerkeys packages, focused controller and session-manager tests, API-spec tests, and 60 Account/IPC/localization frontend tests. All 98 new strings are present in the parent's Russian locale.
- The full Windows Go suite was attempted; broader adapter tests hit filesystem, path, and permission failures and the run was stopped after progress ceased. Frontend typecheck and 236 focused tests pass locally. A full Windows Vitest run had broad platform and sandbox failures; CI uses a clean Linux install.
- **Checked by hand in the desktop app (macOS):**
  - The provider-catalog routes return the counts above.
  - A Z.ai key saved through the picker for OpenCode (`zai-coding-plan`), Pi (`zai`) and OMP (`zai`) landed in each native store with mode 0600.
  - All three then reported as signed in.
  - The Copilot and Kimi methods appear in the running app, but no sign-in was completed through them.

## Scope and limitations
- **Device-wide** means the current OS user's login session, not every user account.
  - Already-running apps keep their old environment and need restarting.
  - Linux propagation reaches processes started by the systemd user manager.
  - macOS propagation reaches future launchd children and is reapplied, for opted-in keys only, when AO starts in a new login session.
- `launchctl setenv` briefly exposes the key as a process argument, and processes inheriting a shared environment can read it.
- Persistent sharing on Linux (`environment.d`) and Windows (`HKCU\Environment`) would need an explicit exception to the `~/.ao` hard rule; a shell-profile helper (`eval "$(ao provider-keys env)"`) is the follow-up that avoids one.
- A key saved without a check proves local configuration, not provider acceptance.
- Removing a key from the API keys page leaves copies that a harness wrote into its own settings.
- AO passes saved keys to the sessions it starts, with one exception: a variable that would override how a harness signs in reaches that harness only when its own panel saved it. That covers `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for Claude Code, `OPENAI_API_KEY` for Codex, `GEMINI_API_KEY` for Gemini CLI, and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` for DeepSeek Harness, which ranks its launch environment above its own store.
  - Because runtimes start from the daemon's environment, a withheld key's inherited copy is blanked, but only when it holds AO's value.
  - A variable you exported yourself before starting AO is passed through unchanged.
- A key saved through a provider picker is device-wide for that harness, inside and outside AO.
- Antigravity CLI and Auggie use their documented account flows.
- Qwen's DashScope button targets the China endpoint; other regions remain available through native setup.
- A previously selected Continue config can take precedence over `~/.continue/config.yaml`.
- Saving a key for Crush's OpenAI, xAI or Anthropic provider removes that provider's stored sign-in, as Crush's own key save does.
- The held-back-key rule is applied to Claude Code's probe; the Codex, Gemini and DeepSeek Harness probes still read the daemon environment.

title: feat(desktop): let the new chat page take pasted images and files
body:
Code changes: +114 -70\
Tests: +71 -3\
Others: +0 -8

## What

The new chat page (`/new`) now takes pasted, dropped, and picked images and files before the task's session exists, including in Scratchpad. They are uploaded with the create request on the first send.

## Why

Attachments on the new chat page only worked once the project's prepared worktree was ready, and never in Scratchpad, which has no prepared worktree. Until then the composer showed a disabled "Files can be attached once the task has started" button, and paste and drop did nothing.

## How

- `ChatComposer` has a new `holdAttachments` prop. With it set, files that have no workspace to stage into stay in the composer with their bytes. On send they are passed to `onSend` as `FileAttachmentPayload`s next to any native image payloads. `ChatWorkspace` passes the prop through, gated by `newWorkDisabled` the same way `onStageAttachments` is.
- `NewChatPage` sets `holdAttachments` and forwards the payloads to `useTaskLaunch().launch` through a new `attachments` option. That option replaces the hook's own (unused here) attachment list.
- No backend change. `POST /sessions` and `POST /orchestrators/delegate` already accept `attachments`, write them into the new session's worktree, and add their paths to the opening prompt. This holds for async Chat spawns and for prepared worktrees too.
- Once the prepared worktree is ready, files are still staged into it as before. Files held before that are sent with the create request.
- The `attachLater` prop, the disabled button it drew, and its `chat.composer.attachLater` strings in every locale are removed. Nothing else used them.

Known limits:
- Held files live in memory only, so a reload before sending drops them. The text draft is kept.
- If the page reloads while a send's response was lost, the retry carries no files. Its request fingerprint then differs from the original, so the daemon refuses it rather than starting a session without them.
- Cloud projects still redirect to the New Task dialog, which reports that attachments aren't supported for cloud tasks.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` (frontend) passes.
- `npx vitest run` passes for `NewChatPage`, `ChatComposer`, `ChatComposer.optimistic`, `ChatWorkspace`, `TaskComposer`, and the i18n tests: 519 tests.
- New tests:
  - `ChatComposer`: with no workspace, pasting an image and a text file shows the attach control and both chips, and the send carries both files' bytes with the message.
  - `NewChatPage`: the page sets `holdAttachments` and passes the sent files to `launch`.
- Not checked in the real desktop app.

title: fix(tmux): treat tmux 3.5 "no such session" as a missing session
body:
Code changes: +4 -2\
Tests: +135 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The tmux runtime now treats tmux 3.5's `no such session: <target>` as "session is gone", the same as `can't find session` and `session not found`. Auto review no longer fails when it removes a stale reviewer session on tmux 3.5+.

## Why

Fixes #6099. On tmux 3.5a, `set-option -t =<id>: detach-on-destroy on` against a missing session prints `no such session: =<id>:` (exit 1), while `has-session` and `kill-session` still print `can't find session`. `sessionMissingOutput` didn't match the new wording, so `Destroy`'s pre-kill `set-option` step returned an error instead of treating the session as already gone, and every auto review failed with `exit status 1: no such session: =review-x:`.

## How

- `runtime/tmux/tmux.go`: `sessionMissingOutput` also matches `no such session`. Every caller goes through it, directly or through `confirmedAbsentOutput`: `Destroy` (the set-option step and the kill-session result), `IsAlive`, `ProcessRootPIDs`, `enforceDetachOnDestroy` and the legacy-socket probes in `socketForSession`. So they all pick up the new wording.
- The transient-failure helpers are unchanged, so connection errors, protocol mismatches and unexpected server exits still fail closed, as #4223 requires.

Thanks to @axisrow for the root-cause analysis and the reproduction in the issue. Their fork fix (axisrow/agent-orchestrator#46) takes the same one-line approach. I left out the optional tmux-version-in-errors part.

## Testing

New tests in `tmux_test.go`:

- `TestSessionMissingOutputRecognizesTmux35Wording`: a table over `sessionMissingOutput` and `confirmedAbsentOutput`, covering all three missing-session wordings, plus transient errors that must not count as gone.
- `TestDestroyIsIdempotentWhenSessionMissingTmux35Wording`: `Destroy` returns nil on the issue's exact output.
- `TestDestroyFailsClosedOnTransientFailuresAlongsideTmux35Wording`: transient failures at the set-option or kill-session step still return an error, and kill-session never runs after a failed set-option.
- `TestIsAliveReturnsFalseNilOnTmux35NoSuchSession`, `TestProcessRootPIDsTreatsTmux35NoSuchSessionAsNoPIDs` and `TestIsAliveAdoptsLegacySessionWhenPrivateSocketReportsTmux35NoSuchSession`.

Five of the six fail without the fix. For example, `Destroy` fails with `set detach-on-destroy review-x: <nil>: no such session: =review-x:`. The fail-closed test already passed, as expected.

- `go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/...`: 118 passed, including the integration tests against a local tmux 3.5a.
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/... ./internal/review/...`: ok.
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/...`: 0 issues. `go vet`, `gofmt` and `go build ./...` are clean.
- Not run locally: the full backend suite with `-race`, the frontend jobs and agent-ci. Only macOS with tmux 3.5a was tested.

title: fix(cli): keep effort and preRemove in project set-config
body:
Code changes: +80 -30\
Tests: +212 -1\
Others: +20 -19

## What

`ao project set-config` no longer drops worker, orchestrator or reviewer `effort` or `preRemove`.

- Field flags now change only the fields they name and keep the rest of the saved config.
- `--config-json` now carries `effort` and `preRemove` through.
- `--clear` and `--config-json` are still full replacements.

## Why

Fixes #7229. Two problems combined:

1. **The CLI's copy of the config was missing fields.** `cli/project.go` keeps its own copy of `domain.ProjectConfig`, which had no `effort` on `agentConfig` and no `preRemove`. `set-config` decodes into that copy and PUTs it back, so both were lost, even with `--config-json`. `project get --json` couldn't show effort either.
2. **Flag mode replaced everything.** It built a new config from the flags alone, and the config PUT replaces the stored config, so a single `--session-prefix` erased everything else, including effort set in the app.

## How

- `agentConfig` gains `Effort` and `projectConfig` gains `PreRemove`, with the domain's JSON tags.
- `TestProjectConfigMirrorsDomainJSONKeys` compares the two types by reflection, including nested structs, pointers and slices, so a future domain field the CLI doesn't model fails a test instead of being dropped silently.
- **Flag mode** in `buildProjectConfig`:
  - It still requires at least one config flag, checked with `Flags().Changed` before any request, so a call with none is still a usage error with no API call.
  - It reads the current config (`GET /projects/{id}`), overwrites only the fields whose flags were passed, and PUTs the result.
  - A flag given with an empty value (for example `--session-prefix=`) now clears that field.
  - Repeatable flags (`--env`, `--symlink`, `--post-create`, `--reviewer`) replace that whole map or list.
  - `--tracker-intake` sets only `enabled`, so a saved tracker provider is kept.
- If the project reports `status: "degraded"`, there is no config to merge into, so flag mode returns an error and points to `--config-json`. The help text and `configuration/projects.mdx` say so.
- **Docs:** the `set-config` help text, the `using-ao` skill page, `docs/cli/README.md` and six docs pages said flags replace the whole config and that effort is dropped. They now describe the new behaviour, and still warn that `--config-json` replaces everything.

## Testing

- **New tests:**
  - `TestProjectConfigMirrorsDomainJSONKeys`
  - `TestProjectSetConfig_FlagsUpdateOnlyChangedFields`. Two cases: changing the prefix and model keeps effort at every level, `preRemove`, `env` and `workersRequestReview`; and `--session-prefix=` clears just that field. Each case checks the requests are exactly GET then PUT.
  - `TestProjectSetConfig_ConfigJSONKeepsEffortAndPreRemove`
  - `TestProjectSetConfig_NoConfigFlagIsUsageErrorWithoutRequests` (guards existing behaviour)
  - `TestProjectSetConfig_FlagsRefuseDegradedProject`
  - `TestProjectConfigFlagsListsEveryFieldFlag`: every registered field flag is in `projectConfigFlags`, and every listed name is registered.
- **Before the fix**, the drift test reports `CLI projectConfig is missing domain key "preRemove"` and `"worker.agentConfig.effort"`, and the flag tests show a PUT with no GET that drops effort.
- **Commands:**
  - `go test -race ./internal/cli/...`: ok.
  - `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...`: ok.
  - `go test -race ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/skillassets/...`: ok.
  - `golangci-lint run ./internal/cli/...`: 0 issues. `go vet`, `gofmt` and `go build ./...` are clean.
- **Not run locally:** the Windows workspace job, the CLI fresh-install container, and the docs build (`npm run build --prefix src/docs`), which covers the MDX edits.

## Notes

- **Overwrite window:** flag mode reads then writes, so an edit made in the app between the two calls is overwritten. #6365 adds `expectedRevision` to the config PUT; once it lands, a small follow-up can pass the revision read here and close that window.
- **#6834** (reject unknown keys in `--config-json`) adds `PreRemove` to the same struct, so the two PRs will conflict on that line. It doesn't add `effort`, so with only #6834 a `--config-json` containing `effort` would be rejected. The two changes work together, and the drift test would catch any further gaps. The docs edits overlap too.
- **#6325** (`ao project update` via PATCH) is a separate command. Once it lands, flag mode could use PATCH instead of GET then PUT.
- **Repeatable flags replace, not add.** For example, `--env A=1` replaces the whole env map. Happy to change that to merging keys if you'd prefer.

title: fix(terminal): forget a terminal's input timestamp once its runtime is destroyed
body:
Code changes: +49 -8\
Tests: +229 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The terminal manager's `lastInputAt` map no longer keeps one entry for every terminal ever typed into. When Session Manager has successfully destroyed a session's runtime, it now tells the terminal manager to drop that terminal's input timestamp.

## Why

Fixes #5691. `recordInputAt` sets `lastInputAt[id]` on every keystroke, and nothing ever deleted it.

The earlier PRs (#5692, #5724) deleted the entry in `leaveTerminal` when the last viewer left. That isn't safe, because the timestamp has to outlive its viewers:

- **Idle check:** `tuiIdleAfterInput` (`session_manager/interface_transition.go`) treats a missing timestamp as idle.
- **Restart check:** `terminalIdleForRestart` (`tui_version_refresh.go`) relies on the timestamp to tell whether the operator typed something.
- **Retry check:** `confirmActive` compares it with the delivery baseline before pressing Enter.

If an operator types a draft without pressing Enter and switches tabs, dropping the entry on detach lets AO treat the TUI as idle and restart it, or press Enter on the draft. A new test pins this. It fails if that delete is added back.

## How

- **`terminal`:** `(*Manager).ForgetTerminalInput(terminalID)` deletes `lastInputAt[id]`. It takes the terminal's write fence first, then `inputMu`, so a keystroke write that's already in flight finishes before the entry goes. It leaves `inputBlocked` alone, because that count belongs to whoever holds the drain.
- **`session_manager`:** a new optional capability, `TerminalInputForgetter`, sits next to `TerminalInputObserver` and `TerminalInputFencer`. A new helper, `destroySessionRuntime`, calls `runtime.Destroy` and, only if Destroy succeeded, calls `ForgetTerminalInput(handle.ID)`. A failed Destroy may leave the runtime, and the draft in it, alive, so the timestamp stays.
- The paths where a session's runtime is torn down as it leaves its live lifecycle now use it: Kill, RetireForReplacement (two places), workspace retire, both save-and-teardown paths, reconcileReap, and Cleanup.
- Restart and rollback destroys are unchanged. Handle IDs are stable per session, so they don't add new keys, and the idle checks around those transitions keep their timestamp.
- **`daemon`:** the compile-time assertion on `*terminal.Manager` now includes `TerminalInputForgetter`.
- The map key is the runtime handle ID, which is the same ID the session manager already passes to `BeginInputDrain`, `LastInputAt` and `HoldInput`.

**Known gap:** an agent that exits on its own, with no Kill, retire, reconcile reap or Cleanup, keeps its entry until one of those runs for that session. Keys are per session and stable, so this is at most one entry per such session, not unbounded growth.

## Alternative for reviewers

I'd like your input on which design you prefer. I built and tested a second version that keeps the pruning entirely inside the terminal manager:

- **How it works:** when an attachment sees its runtime exit, it forgets that terminal's timestamp. A background sweep, at most once a minute and started when a viewer leaves, also probes every terminal that still has a timestamp but no viewer. It drops the ones whose runtime is confirmed gone; a failed or inconclusive probe never counts as gone.
- **Advantage:** because it watches runtime liveness directly, it also covers agents that exit on their own while nobody is viewing them, which is the gap above.
- **Cost:**
  - about 86 lines of code, against 49 here;
  - a long-lived goroutine;
  - up to one `IsAlive` probe (`tmux has-session`) per unviewed terminal per minute;
  - more locking to reason about.

This PR uses the destroy-driven version because it needs no goroutines or probes and only drops an entry once Session Manager has proven the runtime destroyed. If you'd rather close the self-exit gap, I can switch to the sweep version, or add a forget call at the point where the session is marked terminated.

## Testing

- **`terminal`** (`manager_test.go`):
  - `TestServeKeepsLastInputAtWhenTheLastViewerCloses`: both viewers close and the timestamp is still reported. It fails if a #5692-style delete is added to `leaveTerminal`; I checked by adding that delete temporarily.
  - `TestForgetTerminalInputDropsTheTimestamp`
  - `TestForgetTerminalInputIgnoresUnknownTerminals`
  - `TestForgetTerminalInputWaitsForTheWriteFence`
  - `TestForgetTerminalInputIsSafeAlongsideInputAndReaders`: a `-race` stress test with keystrokes, readers and forgets running at once.
- **`session_manager`** (`manager_test.go`):
  - `TestKill_ForgetsTerminalInputAfterRuntimeDestroy`: forgets only after Destroy ran.
  - `TestKill_KeepsTerminalInputWhenRuntimeDestroyFails`
  - `TestCleanup_ForgetsTerminalInputOfTerminatedSessions`
- **Before the change:** `ForgetTerminalInput` doesn't exist, and the Kill and Cleanup tests fail with `forgotten terminals = [], want [h1]`.
- **Commands:**
  - `go test -race ./internal/terminal/... ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/daemon/...`: all pass (terminal 65, session_manager 1417, daemon 126).
  - `golangci-lint run ./internal/terminal/... ./internal/session_manager/...`: 0 issues. `go vet`, `gofmt` and `go build ./...` are clean.
- **Not run locally:** the full backend suite, the frontend jobs and agent-ci.

## Notes

- Open PR #5649 rewrites `RetireForReplacement` and `Cleanup` and adds new `runtime.Destroy` calls. Whichever lands second should route those through `destroySessionRuntime`.
- #5525 adds a forced-cleanup Destroy, which should do the same.
- @Meraj-08, thanks for #5692, which this builds on.

title: fix(new-chat): stop the Scratchpad composer showing a project-ID validation error
body:
Fixes #7319

## Summary
The Scratchpad composer ("What do you want to work on?") showed a red **"Project id failed storage-path validation"** before anything was sent.

**Cause:** #7032 added a `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}` read to `useRememberProjectPermissions`. Every chat uses that hook, and its only guard is `enabled: Boolean(projectId)`, so a Scratchpad chat requests `GET /api/v1/projects/__standalone__`. The daemon's `validateProjectID` rejects that ID with `INVALID_PROJECT_ID`. The read is cached under `["project", "__standalone__"]`. `useTaskLaunch` in `TaskComposer.tsx` uses the same key. Its query is disabled for Scratchpad, but a disabled TanStack query still reads the cached entry, and `remoteLoadError` passed `projectQuery.error` through without checking `isStandalone`. So after you viewed any Scratchpad chat, the composer showed the error.

**Fix (frontend only, 3 small source edits):**
- `useRememberProjectPermissions`: don't read a project for the standalone sentinel.
- `SessionChatSurface`: Scratchpad chats no longer offer "Remember for this project". Turning it on would have sent `PATCH /api/v1/projects/__standalone__/permissions` and hit the same validation error.
- `TaskComposer`: ignore the project query's error for Scratchpad and cloud targets, which never read a local project. Errors for real projects still show.

The backend correctly keeps rejecting `__standalone__` as a project ID, as in #5993 (#5898). That earlier fix covered a different caller, the Switch agent dialog, so this is a new caller and not a regression of it.

## Tests
- New: `TaskComposer.test.tsx`: "does not show another view's failed lookup of the standalone sentinel as a Scratchpad error". It seeds the shared cache entry with the daemon's rejection, as a Scratchpad chat does.
- New: `useRememberProjectPermissions.test.tsx`: "does not read a project for a Scratchpad session".
- Both new tests **fail on `main`** and pass with this change.
- `vitest run` on useRememberProjectPermissions, TaskComposer, NewChatPage, SessionChatSurface, TurnSettingsBar and SwitchAgentDialog: all pass.
- `tsgo --noEmit`: no errors under `src/`. The local environment can't resolve deps for `packages/product-ui`; that's unrelated.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Not checked in the Electron app because disk space on the dev machine is limited. Tests cover the shared-cache mechanism directly.
- Other hooks share the `["project", id]` key with different query functions and data shapes. That's a broader cleanup and is out of scope here.

title: fix(desktop): revert the cloud startup changes that hid the Coder loader
body:
## Problem
Two commits from the `cloud/share-session` branch, both shipped to main in #7151, broke the cloud startup flow:

- `c24a882ec2` "keep cloud startup inside chat" added `expectsTerminal &&` to `showLifecycleLoader` and `showCompletedLoader` in `SessionView.tsx`. That hid the full-screen startup loader for every Chat-mode session.
- `efd1f75d9b` "use chat startup view for cloud orchestrator creation" replaced the cloud startup loader with the local "starting" chat while a cloud orchestrator is created (`OrchestratorStartingChat`, `SessionsBoard`, `_shell.tsx`).

Together they meant a Coder session showed a chat first and the loader only later, or not at all, with no startup steps and no Coder workspace link. `stable` (2026-10-24) has the original behaviour; `release/stable-2026-10-27` has the regression.

## Fix
This reverts the startup parts of both commits, back to how `stable` works:
- `efd1f75d9b` is fully reverted.
- From `c24a882ec2`, the loader conditions, the comment and the original "keeps the restored Chat-mode session's loader" test are reverted. Its sharing-action alignment (`workspace-topbar-actions`) and the `subscribeSessionLiveBridged` test mock stay, because #7151's sharing features need them.

Coder Chat regression tests are added: the loader shows while the workspace is `requested`, `provisioning` or `bootstrapping`, and goes away once it connects.

## Tests
- SessionView, SessionsBoard and the shell shortcut tests: 421 passed.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- The new Coder tests fail on main without this change.
- Two tests in `ContextMeter`/`ChatWorkspace` (context-usage tooltip) fail on main without this change too; they're unrelated.

## Also: "Model choices unavailable" after a worker connects
A worker that has just connected fails its first model-list reads while it still gets the agent ready: a Coder workspace finishing its tool installs, or Claude Code upgrading. The control plane reports those failures as `422 WORKER_OPERATION_FAILED`. The chat showed that at once as "Model choices unavailable" and never retried, so the error stayed until the view remounted (switching tabs and back cleared it).

`CloudSessionChatSurface.tsx` now retries that failure up to 6 times, waiting 2, 4, 8, then 15 s between tries (about a minute in total), and shows the error only if every retry fails. Timeouts and `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE` are handled as before. In production on 2026-10-27, Claude sessions recovered within about a minute of connecting. All 58 CloudSessionChatSurface tests and `npm run typecheck` pass.

title: fix(mobile): shrink the Settings notifications toggle
body: Code changes: +38 -2 Tests: +0 -0 Others: +0 -0 ## Summary The Notifications toggle in mobile Settings looked oversized on some phones. It is the platform's native switch, drawn at a fixed size that ignores the row's 15pt type: - **Android:** Material 3's switch is a fixed 52×32dp with a thick track. - **iOS 26:** the switch is 63×28pt, and an empty-label SwiftUI `Toggle` reserves about 8pt more for its label. Inside the old 54pt `Host` it hung about 10pt past the row's trailing edge, so it also misaligned with the values and chevrons in the other rows. This draws the switch at 0.8 on both platforms and sizes the `Host` so the pill's trailing edge lines up with the other rows: - `lib/settings-switch.android.ts`: Compose `graphicsLayer` scale. The Host is the scaled width. - `lib/settings-switch.ios.ts`: `labelsHidden()` and `scaleEffect`. The Host keeps the native width (63pt on iOS 26, 51pt before), with a negative trailing margin for the space the scale leaves. - `lib/settings-switch.ts`: fallback, unchanged size. The Host stays 44 tall, so the touch target doesn't shrink. ## Screenshots Same screen, before (current main) and after, both cold-started. **iOS 26.5, iPhone 17 Pro simulator:** 60×27pt on screen → 48×21pt, now flush with "Check now" **Android 15, Pixel 7 emulator:** 52×32dp → 41.5×25dp Simulators always report push as unsupported, so the toggle normally renders disabled and off there. For these shots only, a local, uncommitted one-line override forced it on and enabled, applied the same way to both before and after. ## Testing - `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 243 files, 2510 tests pass. - Ran Debug builds of this branch on both simulators. With a temporary log in `onToggle`, taps on the scaled pill's centre and its trailing end reached the handler on both platforms. ## Risks - The iOS native width is keyed on the OS major version (≥ 26 → 63pt, else 51pt). Not checked on an iOS 18 device or simulator. If the width there is off, only the trailing alignment moves, by a point or two. - Not checked on a physical device.

title: fix: keep selection actions visible and responsive
body:
Code changes: +560 -136  
Tests: +749 -35  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Keep selection controls available during background updates and dismiss them before an Escape can interrupt an agent. Chat, file and diff toolbars now follow the same first-line placement rule. Rebased onto main after #7489 merged; side-creation recovery is split into #7560.

## Why

Background content replacement and passive composer focus could discard a native selection. Escape dismissal could reopen on an unrelated key release, and toolbar placement differed between chat and files.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Background file/diff refresh replaces selected content | Retain selected content until selection clears; theme, editing, annotations and callbacks remain live |
| Escape dismisses controls, then Shift reopens them | Keep the same native range dismissed; held Escape cannot also interrupt |
| Mouse selections leave keyboard events targeted at the document body | Escape handles document/body targets while preserving editors, terminals, menus and browser input |
| Chat and file toolbars anchor differently | Follow the first highlighted line, flip below when there is no room above, and pin at the pane top when it scrolls above |
| Side-chat availability changes the action label | Keep **Add to side chat**, disabled while checking or processing |

[Manual desktop QA with uploaded screenshots](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7327#issuecomment-6541724683) predates this rebase; final-head renderer-fixture validation is recorded below. Review images and the process log have been removed from the repository.

## How

- Reuse #7489's placement behavior through a shared geometry function; preserve its Ctrl/Cmd+L shortcut, repeat protection and target scoping.
- Snapshot content/diff data only, including delayed hydration. Stable callbacks keep Pierre's presentation and interaction props current.
- Remember dismissed ranges and scope Escape to a matching live selection; selection changes do not resubscribe the six-listener effect.
- No backend, creation receipts, API, database or persisted-format changes. Recovery and its alias/primary-key tests are in #7560.

## Testing

Current head: `feb128cfb`.

title: fix(chat): stop showing Claude compaction summaries as user messages
body:
## Summary

When Claude Code compacts a conversation that ran out of context, it writes the summary into its transcript as a user record that starts with "This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context." The live stream never shows that record. The `session/load` replay that runs when a hibernated chat wakes does show it, and `getSessionMessages` drops the record's `isCompactSummary` flag on the way. AO had no stored row for the summary, so it imported it as a new human message at the end of the chat. The result was a long "you sent this" bubble the next time the user opened the chat.

This change adds the summary's fixed opening sentence to `claudeTranscriptNotice`, next to task notifications and interrupt markers, so replay skips the summary. Checkpoint verification already treats any compacted transcript as unsettled, so this change only affects the replay filter.

## Evidence

Sandboxed lab with two daemons built from identical sources (`origin/main` at `fdea8d15a5`, plus or minus this change). Both used the same flow on a real Claude Code 2.1.311 chat: one prompt, `/compact` through `POST /conversation/compact`, idle hibernation, then a wake through `POST /chat-view` (`session_load` ok in both).

| Daemon | Summary records in the Claude transcript | Chat messages after the wake | Summary bubbles |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 1 (`isCompactSummary`) | prompt, reply, then seq 4 `user`/`human` with the 2,770-character summary | 1 |
| main + this change | 1 (`isCompactSummary`) | prompt, reply | 0 |

The same bubble appeared in a real chat after it auto-compacted at 967K of 1M tokens and later woke from hibernation.

## Tests

- `claudeTranscriptNotice` table: both summary forms Claude Code 2.1.311 writes return true, and a prompt that only quotes the sentence returns false.
- The replay wiring (a notice starts no turn and adds no user message) is already covered by `TestACPReplayDrainReconstructsTurnsInOrder`.

## Risks and follow-ups

- This is a text match, the same kind as the existing notices. A human prompt that starts with that exact sentence would be hidden from replay. The exact fix is for `getSessionMessages` to drop `isCompactSummary` records the way it drops `isMeta`.
- Summary bubbles that were already imported stay in existing chats. This change only stops new ones.
