title: fix(cloud): run any Coder template's first Chat start without errors
body:
Follows #7322 (merged as a81f681475), which brought the startup loader back. Together they fix the first start of a Coder Chat session on a bring-your-own template that installs its own tools in its startup script, such as `ao-11x-replica` and 11x's own.

## What went wrong

| Problem | Cause |
|---|---|
| A Chat task moves to the terminal on its first start | The Claude ACP adapter's install can only start once the template has npm and takes about 20 s; the worker waited 15 s (`claudeChatAdapterWait`). Measured on `ao-11x-replica`: the install finished 5 s after the fallback. |
| "Model choices unavailable: The worker could not complete the operation." | The model list is asked before the template has installed the agent. A missing binary fell through to the generic `WORKER_OPERATION_FAILED`. Seen on prod in 3 Codex Chat sessions on this template today. |
| Codex runs an unpinned release | The template ships Codex `0.164.0`; AO's templates install `0.147.0` (`cloud/coder/main.tf`), the release the app-server protocol was built for. The worker pins Claude Code but not Codex. |

## Fix

- **Pinned Codex:** the worker installs and runs `CodexVersion` (`0.147.0`) in `~/.ao/tools`, reusing the Claude Code pin machinery (retry, backoff, durable reuse). Exact match, because the app-server protocol changes between releases. It installs at boot (`WarmCodex`), also when the template has no Codex yet. The terminal launch, Chat turns (`runCodex`) and model discovery wait for an install in progress. The harness gate accepts the worker's own install of Claude Code or Codex, so a template need not ship them.
- **Model list while the agent installs:** a missing agent binary is `CHAT_AGENT_INSTALLING`. The app asks again quietly every 5 s, for up to 3 minutes, for it and `CHAT_ADAPTER_INSTALLING`, on top of #7322's retry of `WORKER_OPERATION_FAILED`.
- **Claude Chat stays in Chat:** `claudeChatAdapterWait` 15 s to 90 s. The loader from #7322 covers the wait.

## Tests

- New `codex_cli_test.go`: keeps a workspace install of the pinned release, installs over a newer one, installs when there is none, falls back without npm, parses `codex-cli 0.147.0`.
- `TestMissingAgentBinaryIsReportedAsInstalling` (`workertransport`).
- `TestSettleClaudeChatStartWaitsForAnInstall` replaces the test that pinned the 15 s window.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface`: the catalog is asked again quietly while the agent or adapter installs. It fails without this change.
- Rebased onto main after #7322 merged: full `go test ./...` passes (36 packages). Frontend typecheck is clean. Full renderer suite: 7360 pass, 2 fail (`ContextMeter`, `ChatWorkspace` context usage); both fail the same way on main with this PR's frontend change removed.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface` keeps #7322's retry of `WORKER_OPERATION_FAILED` and adds the quiet retry for `CHAT_AGENT_INSTALLING` / `CHAT_ADAPTER_INSTALLING`.
- The commits main gained since the staging deploy change no `cloud/` files, so the worker and control plane code here is exactly what staging `:322` runs.

## Staging (`:322`, main + #7322 + this), template `ao-11x-replica`, workspace-user connection

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Codex Chat task from the New task page | Loader through the build, stays in Chat, worker runs its own Codex `0.147.0` (template has `0.164.0`). The model list failed once while Codex installed, then the quiet retry got 200 three seconds later; no error shown. The turn reached Codex, whose account on the staging org is out of quota (a credential limit, not this change). |
| Claude Chat task | Stays in Chat (adapter installed 11 s after the worker connected), live tool calls, DONE. Model list 200 on the first request. |
| Orchestrator in Chat | Loader from 4 s through creation and startup, then Chat with the model picker loaded, ORCH-OK. |

Deploying this to prod needs a control plane deploy; workers pick it up when they start.

title: feat(mobile): draw AO's automation messages and worker reports as desktop does
body:
Code changes: +1559 -81\
Tests: +615 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The mobile chat now draws AO's automation messages, worker reports and session links the way the desktop does since #7230. Before, it showed one generic "AUTOMATION" card, raw report text and raw `ao://` URLs.

- **Worker reports** are quiet rows: the worker's harness logo, its task, its state ("needs you" in amber while it is that worker's latest report), a headline and the time.
  - Tap anywhere on a row to open the full report beneath it, with headings, lists and code drawn, safe links live, and **Open chat**.
  - Reported artifacts open in a new artifact viewer (`app/artifact/[sessionId].tsx`). It loads the daemon's `preview/artifacts` page, the same rendered Markdown the desktop shows.
- **A human message with reports folded in** shows only what the user typed. The reports draw as rows above it, and Copy and Edit leave them out.
- **PR events** are rows in the PR glyph, tinted by meaning, with the PR linked:
  - review comments, with a file chip and the comment folded after five lines;
  - failing CI, listing each check with its log one tap away;
  - changes requested;
  - merge conflicts.
- **What the user did through AO** (the git buttons, file feedback, diff selections, browser annotations) draws as the user's own bubble. AO's notices are one quiet line.
- **Messages from other agents**, including steers sent mid-turn, name their sender.
- **`ao://sessions/…` links** in any chat (the orchestrator's own replies included) open that session's chat on the conversation's machine. A bare link reads as the session's name, which is read from the daemon when the session is archived.

Anything that matches none of these keeps the old card.

## Why

Mobile showed AO's agent-facing instructions verbatim in a dimmed card, printed `<ao-worker-reports>` envelopes inside the user's bubble, and left session links as unclickable `ao://` text. The desktop has drawn all of these as what they are since #7230.

## Before / After

Each cell is iOS 26.5 (left) and Android 15 (right) in the real `ChatTimeline`, with the same data on both sides. "Before" runs this PR's base code.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: worker reports printed as raw text inside the user's bubble](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/reports-before.jpg) | ![After: one row per worker report above the user's own words](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/reports-after.jpg) |
| ![Before: review comment, CI failure and Create PR as generic AUTOMATION cards](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/pr-before.jpg) | ![After: PR event rows and a Create PR bubble](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/pr-after.jpg) |
| ![Before: ao:// session links in an orchestrator reply printed as raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/links-before.jpg) | ![After: the same links drawn as links, a bare one named for its session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/links-after.jpg) |
| `ao://` text could not be tapped | ![After: tapping a session link opens that session's chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/link-opened.jpg) |
| A report's full text sat raw in the bubble, with nothing to open | ![After: tapping a row opens the full report with links and Open chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/row-opened.jpg) |
| An artifact path was plain text | ![After: tapping an artifact opens the daemon's rendered page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/7d6a60a7d1b370b9e6e435b099afdfba609f28a6/artifact-opened.jpg) |

## How

- **Readers.** `lib/chat/automationMessages.ts` ports the desktop's readers (`AutomationMessage.tsx`, `WorkerUpdates.tsx`). Like the desktop, it reads AO's fixed message templates, so **a template change needs its reader changed on both clients**. A message an agent sent is never read as AO's.
- **Rows.** `lib/chat/AutomationMessage.tsx` draws the rows. `ChatTimeline` hands every non-human user message to it, with the old card as the fallback.
- **Links in text an agent or a reviewer wrote** (worker reports, agent messages, review comments, changes-requested bodies) are held to `safeLink`: only `ao://sessions/…` and github.com/gitlab.com pages stay links, and a forge link whose label isn't its URL names its host. In the Markdown paths, `safeMarkdown` rewrites the text before `ChatMarkdown` sees it, as the desktop's `safeOrigin` does:
  - any other link keeps its words;
  - a bare URL becomes code;
  - images, including ones nested in links, become their alt text;
  - code is left as written.
- **Session links.** `ChatMarkdown` recognizes `ao://` links. Only the chat screen knows the machine, so it routes them (`hostId` = the conversation's) and names bare ones. Elsewhere they stay words, rather than becoming links that would land on "belongs to another machine".
- **Harness logo and names.** The board list can leave out archived workers, which send most reports. A missing session is read once with `getSession` through `sessionLookup`, a cache shared by rows and links. Failures are retried and the cache is capped. Until a read lands, a row shows the chat's own agent, never a generic glyph.
- **Rendering cost.** Rows read the sessions and pairing from one `WorkerSessionsProvider`, whose value changes only when a field a row shows changes. A poll or notification no longer redraws every row.
- **Folding.** The fold is five whole prose lines. Android clips rather than ellipsizes, and the first version cut a line in half there. The fold is measured only while unclipped, and again after a width change.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` passes, and `npx vitest run` passes 2551 tests. New tests cover:
  - the readers, run on the desktop's samples;
  - artifact paths, `safeLink`, `safeMarkdown` (nested images, code) and `reportBlocks`;
  - rows: logo lookup, retry, opening a row, links, Open chat, artifacts, and not redrawing on an unrelated store update. I checked this test fails without the memo.
  - the real `ChatMarkdown`: unsafe links in agent and review text are not drawn as links (checked to fail without `safeMarkdown`), and `ao://` links are named, open, and ask once for an unknown session's name;
  - Edit opening without folded-in reports.
- Run on an iOS 26.5 simulator and an Android 15 emulator against real sessions and artifacts, through a read-only loopback proxy that stubbed every write.
  - The `ao://` row adds one reply with two session links to a real orchestrator conversation, inside the proxy, since none of the 57 orchestrator chats had one.
  - Tapping each link opened the real session, including an archived one shown by name.

- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior

title: feat(integrations): add Grok Bot skill pack for running AO from chat
body:
Code changes: +589 -0 (seven skill files and the manifest script)\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +125 -0 (README and generated manifest)

## What

Adds `integrations/grok-bot/`: seven skills that turn a Grok Bot into a chat remote for AO, on one or more computers.

| Skill | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `ao-rules` | Shared rules: AO hosts, the `aoapi` helper (local, or remote over AO's password-protected remote access), orchestrator-first routing, who may answer, secrets |
| `ao-setup` | Finds AO on each connected computer, adds a remote host (password typed in a local Terminal window, never in chat), turns on routines |
| `ao-status` | What's running and waiting, ready-to-merge PRs, review news (each reported once), daily digest |
| `ao-orchestrator` | Passes the user's request to the project orchestrator, waits for its reply, relays it; starts an orchestrator with the request as its prompt when there is none |
| `ao-answer` | Finds questions, approvals and plain-text questions; shows them as cards; sends the user's pick back; away mode |
| `ao-actions` | Interrupt, kill, restore, resume, merge (pinned to the head SHA shown), review, screenshot, files, keep-awake, automations |
| `ao-update` | Self-update: downloads changed skills from the newest `main` commit, checks each sha256 against `manifest.json`, rewrites them |

## Why

Lets people run AO from the chat they already use (the Grok Bot app on a phone), across several computers, and gives AO a shareable Grok Bot template. The bot talks to the project orchestrator for anything that needs judgement, so there is one manager, not two.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| No way to check or steer AO from Grok Bot | "status" in Grok Bot lists sessions on every connected computer, labelled `<host>/<session id>` |
| A worker's question or approval waits until the user opens AO | "what's waiting on me" shows it as a card; the pick goes straight to the worker |
| — | "catch me up on <project>" is sent to the project orchestrator, tagged `[via Grok Bot #…]`, and its reply comes back to chat |
| `ao-update` check before this merges: `DOWNLOAD_FAILED … integrations/grok-bot/manifest.json 404` | After merge it reads the manifest from `main` and lists changed skills |

## How

- No daemon or CLI changes. Every command is the AO REST API that already exists, called through a small `curl` helper; JSON is parsed with `python3`.
- Remote hosts use AO's existing remote-access listener with the pairing password as a Bearer header read from a mode-600 file (`curl -H @file`), so it never appears in chat or command lines.
- Away mode accepts only one-time approvals (`allow_once`), never `allow_always`, and never anything high-risk.
- Updates download from one commit SHA, so the manifest and skills always match; any hash mismatch writes nothing.
- Intentional omissions: Windows is not supported (POSIX shell); no push from AO to the bot yet, so questions reach chat on a 30-minute routine (the AO mobile app stays instant).
- Found while testing, not fixed here: an orchestrator can't be created when an untracked folder is left at its worktree path (`provisionState: failed`); `POST /sessions/<id>/send` returns a bare 500 when the agent controller is stopped (`steer-or-send` returns `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`); `ao pr merge <n>` posts an empty body and always fails with `INVALID_PR`.

## Testing

Every skill's commands were run as written against a live AO daemon, in zsh and bash, with throwaway sessions in demo projects (removed afterwards):

- Question (AskUserQuestion) answered by option and by typed "Other"; approval answered Allow Once; answering twice returns `409 CHAT_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING`
- Plain-text question detection on idle sessions
- Orchestrator: find, start with prompt, send, wait (`ROUNDTRIP OK`, `START OK`), steer (`STEER OK`), send to a broken orchestrator (error shown, one retry)
- Interrupt (turn state `interrupted`), kill, restore, resume; merge details and request shape (fake PR, no real merge); review trigger, screenshot and files error paths; automation create and delete
- Remote mode through the real password-protected LAN listener, setup probe, password window, connection test
- `ao-update`: first install, no change, one change, tampered file (`HASH_MISMATCH`, nothing written), GitHub before publishing
- Syntax check of all 20 shell blocks in zsh and bash
- In Grok Bot itself: skills loaded with UpdateSkill; status, waiting, and an orchestrator catch-up worked on two Macs

Not covered: Linux, and Grok Bot routines over a full day.

title: fix(performance): bound conversation reads and large chat rendering
body:
Code changes: +82 -15  
Tests: +219 -2  
Others: +56 -16 (generated sqlc)

## What

Bound conversation payload reads and expensive chat rendering so large histories and long streaming replies consume less CPU and daemon memory. Oversized command logs now show a bounded tail with a short truncation notice instead of laying out the entire log.

## Why

Four local sessions with large saved histories caused excessive memory use, slow typing, and sustained CPU load. A 5.44 MB / 160,000-line command output could also hang the desktop renderer when expanded. These fixes address the measured storage and renderer costs; they do not claim to solve every source of AO memory use.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Storage materializes up to 200 full message/activity payloads before the snapshot byte budget can apply | SQL budgets payload bytes before returning full rows; oversized first row remains readable and pagination advances |
| Long replies continue grapheme smoothing and intermediate Markdown renders | Above 4,000 UTF-16 code units, snapshots coalesce at 100 ms; completion displays immediately |
| Expanded command output lays out the full text, including multi-megabyte logs | Preview retains at most 64 Ki UTF-16 code units and 400 lines; a short notice identifies omitted earlier output |
| Four-session streaming: average AO process CPU **143.3%** | **92.2%** (36% lower; 100% = one core) |
| Peak daemon physical footprint **462.8 MiB** | **129.3 MiB** (72% lower) |
| Peak renderer physical footprint **1,683.1 MiB** | **1,576.4 MiB** (6% lower) |
| Peak summed lab-process footprint **2,534.5 MiB** | **2,112.1 MiB** (17% lower; not unique physical system RAM) |
| Draft typing latency p95 **3,143.5 ms** | **218.7 ms** |
| Stop-turn latency **1,498.4 ms** | **930.6 ms** |
| Median / peak CPU chip temperature **74.4 / 80.6°C** | **60.1 / 78.0°C** |

Native before/after replay screenshots and the oversized-output capture are retained locally for attachment; screenshot upload is unavailable through the CLI. They are not committed to the repository. Measurements/captures were taken on the original benchmark base `fc0b92a9059d1480e700ce275c58bd4fb0bcf494` plus these fixes, before rebasing onto current `main`; the benchmark was not repeated after rebase.

## How

- Apply the existing 4 MiB page budget inside generated SQLite message/activity reads, counting UTF-8 payload bytes. Permit one oversized first row so cursors cannot stall; treat only an empty fetch as EOF because a byte-limited chunk can be shorter than its row limit.
- Preserve smoothing for short messages and reduced-motion behavior; cancel pending long-message updates on completion, replacement, or unmount.
- Bound only the rendered command-output preview, avoiding a split surrogate pair. Keep the full stored text unchanged. The preview shows a truncation notice without a download action; existing storage-truncation warnings remain separate.
- Add tests for every budgeted payload column, multibyte byte counting, oversized-row pagination, streaming boundaries/cancellation, growing output previews, and preview truncation notices.

## Testing

**2026-11-02 follow-up (`6a72e0498b`):** Removed the full-output download button after manual UI review; bounded previews and the notice that earlier output is hidden remain. In the isolated native Electron lab, the reviewer confirmed long-reply responsiveness, the 1,200-line command preview through `END_LOG`, and stopping a long reply followed by a new message. The updated UI was inspected with the download button removed. Updated the preview assertion and removed the obsolete download test. No local automated tests or checks were run for this follow-up, as requested. All 30 current-head CI checks passed on `6a72e0498b`, including backend race suites, frontend tests/typechecking, renderer smoke, cross-platform CLI checks, and both result-aggregation gates. Additional manual pagination review used a separate scratch database in the native Electron app: a 125-turn fixture loaded all 250 messages across byte-bounded pages (190 newer messages, then 60 older messages), and a second fixture paged through two complete 5 MiB replies and a 3 MiB UTF-8 reply to the first message without a cursor stall. This was manual app/API inspection; no local automated test suite was run. The benchmark and validation reports below describe earlier commits, including the former download action.

**2026-11-01 rebase:** Rebased onto `main` at `7690e4e7e` (head `0e947717a`). Regenerated the only conflicted sqlc file from merged SQL, preserving upstream `authored_by_user`/batched-input behavior and this PR’s byte budget. Post-rebase validation passed: all four SQLite race shards, both chat race shards, complete session-manager/store race suites, 608 frontend test files (10,373 passed / 6 skipped), all 140 renderer smoke tests, both TypeScript checks, build/vet, pinned lint (10-minute local timeout), CLI E2E, generation/drift/format checks, shared/docs/native helper/DMG/Electron/browser checks. Both broad backend-core shards fail only eight unchanged test functions (OpenCode/model discovery, Git conditional includes, Cue EOF shell behavior, and tunnel replacement); all eight also fail on untouched `7690e4e7e` on this Mac. The full local backend suite is therefore not claimed green. New-head CI: 25 successful checks, 4 pending, no failures. Docker/cross-OS/Node 22 parity is checked in CI, not claimed locally. The historical manual benchmark and earlier validation counts below describe the original tested build; that benchmark was not repeated for this rebase.

### Native desktop manual scenarios completed

Used real Electron main/preload, daemon, SQLite, and conversation SSE with isolated data. Replayed four local Codex-protocol agents concurrently for 180 seconds; no live model or MCP/tool calls.

- Cloned the same starting history DB for both builds. Verified all four initial histories and completed 3,600-line replies by SHA-256; same 1320×847 viewport at DPR 2.
- Opened four large histories, used **Load earlier messages** three times, and switched between sessions repeatedly.
- Measured 18 draft-typing interactions at ten-second intervals, stopped a subsequent turn, and verified the interrupted state.
- Observed 20 seconds of post-run idle memory; no renderer exceptions in either run.
- Expanded the 5,440,027-byte / 160,000-line log in the patched native app: bounded preview remained responsive and preserved its latest marker. Downloaded output matched the full fixture byte-for-byte (SHA-256 `537f8783c6789115e105a730345fe2e1da41b4f6f4eb6ecc2cc3de14716e632f`).
- Recorded daemon, renderer, agent, main, and GPU/utility memory separately using `proc_pid_rusage`; sampled chip temperature and battery/power state. Charger remained disconnected throughout. Starting CPU temperatures were 51.2 / 50.1°C with nominal thermal state. Reason and Minimi were temporarily closed and restored; Claude and installed AO remained open.

**Limits / follow-ups:** one A/B pair with background activity explicitly allowed. Background-app CPU medians were 33.4% / 47.9% of one core, so neither run satisfies the original quiet-load criterion. Temperature and whole-laptop power cannot be attributed solely to AO, and this is not a battery-life or case-temperature test. Both runs reached fair thermal state. Four lightweight replay agents peaked at 88.4 / 87.3 MiB; real agents/MCP/tools may use substantially more.

**Observed regressions to investigate:** cold history navigation median 455 → 840 ms (only four first opens, different byte-bounded page contents); renderer peak RSS 1,730 → 1,842 MiB despite lower physical footprint. Cached switching median improved 82 → 66 ms (20 repeated switches). A longer real-agent soak and repeated cold-navigation measurements remain follow-up work.

### Automated validation

- Frontend and E2E TypeScript checks passed.
- Complete frontend Vitest suite passed after rebase: **576 files, 9,657 tests passed, 9 skipped** (`npm test -- --maxWorkers=2`).
- Cloud client generation/typecheck/tests/package dry-run and product UI typecheck/tests/package dry-run passed.
- Docs translation checks, tests, and production build passed.
- Native Electron terminal-origin, browser-boundary, and mobile-control tests passed; guarded-navigation/native popup integration passed.
- macOS helper Node tests, x64/arm64 builds with `lipo` verification, and all Swift policy/effects/low-power/update-state tests passed.
- Renderer smoke suite: **132 passed, 1 failed**. The unchanged pointer-drag selection test fails identically on untouched `main` on this Mac.
- Complete store race suite passed; all four CI-style SQLite race shards passed (129 top-level tests total). Complete chat and session-manager race suites passed in the broader run.
- Backend build, vet, pinned golangci-lint v2.13.2, and native CLI E2E suite passed.
- Repository Go formatting and sqlc/OpenAPI/frontend-type/shared-client generation drift checks passed.

**Local full-suite limits/failures outside this diff:** the initial all-package backend race wrapper hit its 40-minute local limit; SQLite was then rerun successfully in CI’s four-shard layout, and the complete store suite was rerun separately. The broader run reports adapter failures in CommandCode, modelcatalog, OMP and OpenCode adapters. CommandCode conditional-include failure and model-discovery failure also reproduce on untouched `main`; OMP passes in isolation. Cloud race suite fails `TestWorkspaceUserLaunchScriptStartsWorker` and `TestClaudeACPConversationRestore` in unchanged worker packages. These suites are not claimed green; remote CI must resolve whether remaining failures are specific to this Mac/environment.

**Local gaps:** Docker daemon unavailable (container CLI install and cloud image backport checks not run); Linux/Windows runner parity, Node 22.23.2 lockfile compatibility and the pinned Linux gitleaks scan require CI. Native helper tests ran on Apple Silicon, not the workflow’s Intel runner.

## Checklist

- [x] Rebased onto `main` at `7690e4e7e`; one focused performance fix across storage and renderer boundaries
- [x] Tests cover changed behavior
- [x] Before / After includes measured behavior and explicit benchmark limits
- [x] Relevant remote CI checks pass

title: feat(mobile): tell a bad phone connection apart from an unreachable machine
body: Code changes: +419 -43\ Tests: +318 -5\ Others: +12 -0 (expo-network in package.json and lockfile) ## What The mobile app now tells "your phone has a bad or no connection" apart from "your machine is down", and only says the machine is down when it really is. - Adds `expo-network` and a pure classifier, `lib/linkHealth.ts`, with these states: `ok`, `slow`, `reconnecting`, `phone-offline`, `unreachable`. - A single unanswered poll now shows amber **"Reconnecting to …"**. Red "Can't reach" / "Your machine is offline" needs 3 unanswered polls over at least 15 s. - When the phone has no network: **"You're offline. Check this phone's Wi-Fi or mobile data."** No Retry button, and the worker rows stay. - When the phone comes back online or switches networks, the app races the endpoints and polls immediately instead of waiting for a poll to fail. - Repeated slow (over 4 s) or timed-out polls show **"Slow connection. Updates may lag."** - The new states also apply to the board banner and empty states, the project and chat screens, the per-machine view, and the Settings status row. ## Why People saw "Your machine is offline" whenever one poll failed. A dropped packet, a radio waking up or a weak signal all looked like a dead machine, and the next successful poll quietly took the message back. The app also had no view of the phone's own network, so having no signal, or leaving Wi-Fi, was blamed on the machine ("check you're on the same Wi-Fi"). `lib/reRace.ts` said so directly: *"There is no network-change listener on this platform build."* ## Before / After Android 15 emulator, the same debug binary with the same data. The app was paired to a scratch daemon through a fault proxy that dropped, hung or delayed requests. "Phone offline" was Android airplane mode. Before = the base JS, after = this branch's JS. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | **Short blip** (no answer for 13 s): red "Your machine is offline" after about 7 s | Amber "Reconnecting to lab-mac…" throughout, never red. Clears on its own | | | | | **Real outage** (requests hang for 60 s): red after about 15 s | Amber until about 40 s, then red "Can't reach your machine". Real outages are still reported | | | | | **Phone offline:** "Your machine is offline. Check you're on the same Wi-Fi." and the rows disappear | "You're offline. Check this phone's Wi-Fi or mobile data." Rows stay, no Retry | | | | | **Back online:** board back after about 8 s | Board back within about 3 s | | | | | **Slow connection** (+5 s per request): nothing shown | "Slow connection. Updates may lag." after two slow polls (about 35 s) | The "before" JS came from `6e8d6e4e04`, the commit this branch started from. It was rebased onto current `main` afterwards, and current `main` doesn't change this behaviour. ## How - **`lib/linkHealth.ts`** is free of native imports. `recordPoll` folds each poll outcome (`ok`, `slow`, `timeout`, `no-answer`, `answered-error`) into a small tracker. `classifyLink` combines that with the phone's network. An answered error (401, 429, 5xx) keeps its existing copy. Only "nothing answered" gets the softer handling. - **`lib/store.tsx`** subscribes to `expo-network`, records an outcome for every poll and every failed endpoint race, and exposes `linkHealth` and `phoneOffline`. `unreachable` is now `linkHealth === "unreachable" && isDesktopUnreachable(...)`. Re-racing and the 15 s reconnect timer are skipped while the phone is offline. A network change resets the race cooldown path by calling `reloadConfig()` and then `fetchAll()`. - **Other paired machines** get the same treatment. Each background runner in `lib/otherHosts.ts` records its poll and race outcomes in a `linkTracker` on its snapshot. `HostScope` (their chat and project views) and the board's per-machine card classify that tracker against the phone's network, which the store keeps as `phoneNetwork`. - Being on a network without internet only counts as "phone offline" while polls are also failing, so a LAN-only setup with no internet keeps working. - **Reviewers:** `expo-network` is a native module. It changes the fingerprint runtime, so this needs a **new store build** and can't go out as an OTA. ## Testing - `cd packages/mobile && npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test`: 246 files, 2547 tests pass after the rebase. The new tests cover `linkHealth`, six store-level scenarios (a blip shows reconnecting, an outage turns unreachable, phone offline then back online races and polls, a request stuck on the old link is replaced when the network returns while the poll loop keeps running, an incompatible-version race clears "reconnecting", and no upgrade race runs while the phone is offline, so the rows are kept). Further tests cover another machine's runner (a blip reads as reconnecting; a sustained failure turns unreachable), the same through `HostScope`, and the board's per-machine card showing "Reconnecting…" and the Settings status row. - `npx expo install --check` doesn't flag `expo-network`. - Manually on an Android 15 emulator, with the five scenarios above on both builds. - Not covered: switching Wi-Fi to cellular on a real phone, iOS (the simulator shares the Mac's network), and a release build. - Seen once and not reproduced in three later runs on either build: a debug red box, `updateRootConstraints called while measuring`, from `@expo/ui` `HostView.onMeasure` re-entered through Reanimated. It came about 11 s after airplane mode turned on during the first branch run. - Existing behaviour on both builds, not changed here: when every endpoint race fails, the active machine's rows are dropped, as in the blip screenshots. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

The chat drew them as: - the generic "automation" card, for a plain `send`; - the user's own bubble, for session create and `steer-or-send`, which store the message as origin `human`; - the user's steer, for a steer into a running turn. It folds after five lines and shows the Queued note while it waits. - A message an AO session sent keeps its sender, whatever its text says. - The orchestrator's answer to the tool stays a full reply. These messages are not worker leads, so the answer is not folded. - Reports the daemon appends to a busy orchestrator's message still draw as their own rows. title: fix(mobile): keep the model picker on chats that were hibernated
body: Code changes: +250 -45\ Tests: +443 -18\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Opening a hibernated Chat session on mobile no longer drops the model from the composer. The turn-settings line shows the model, effort and permission mode, for example "Opus 5.5 · Medium · Auto", instead of only "Ask when unsure". The full settings menu or sheet is available again. This also fixes the Android turn-settings sheet letting the chat hibernate while it is open. ## Why The composer kept switching between the full settings line and "Ask when unsure". Most chats are hibernated when you open them from the phone, because a chat with no viewer sleeps after about a minute once Chat hibernation is on. - A hibernated chat's snapshot reports no capabilities, so the screen asked `/models` instead of `/config-options`. Claude has no model list there, so it got `[]`. - That empty catalog was cached for 30 seconds and loaded only once per screen. Opening the chat wakes the agent through the view lease, but the daemon reports the wake no other way, so the screen never asked again. - Re-opening didn't help either. The screen chose the endpoint from the page cached on the previous visit, which still said "no capabilities". - Each chat sheet is its own route, and the view lease followed screen focus. Opening turn settings on Android therefore released the lease, and the chat hibernated about 80 seconds later behind the open sheet. ## Before / After Captured on the same simulator, emulator and scratch daemon, with real Claude Code chats. Before is `main`; after is this branch, with the same native builds. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Refresh in the sheet calls `/models` again and gets 0 models | Refresh calls `/config-options` and gets the full catalog | | Android sheet left open: the lease is released when it opens, and the chat hibernates about 80 s later | Android sheet left open: the lease renews every 15 s and the chat is still awake after 84 s | ## How - **Which list to ask for** (`turnOptionsCatalog.ts`): ask `/config-options` first and fall back to `/models` only when it is empty. Drivers without provider controls already answer `[]` there, so the snapshot's `config_options` capability no longer decides. A failure, such as `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`, is passed on rather than read as "no controls". - **No caching of an empty catalog** (`useConversation.ts`): an empty result is dropped from the 30 s cache, so the next open or Refresh asks again. - **Last catalog kept per chat:** the last non-empty catalog for each machine and session is kept in memory (up to 32 chats). It seeds a newly mounted screen and stays shown while a reload fails or comes back empty, so the model doesn't flicker while the agent wakes. It's empty on the first open after the app launches; there the line fills in once the wake finishes, about 2 s in testing. - **Reload on wake** (`ChatSessionScreen.tsx`, `useChatViewLease.ts`): the daemon wakes a hibernated chat before answering the `chat-view` POST and publishes no conversation event for it. The lease hook now calls `onViewing` once each registration is answered, which re-reads the chat. The screen reloads the catalog when the provider becomes live (`ready` or `busy`), skipping the cache on that transition. - **Lease while a sheet is open:** the lease follows "focused, or only `sheets/*` routes above this chat in its stack" instead of focus alone. It reads `navigation.getState()` on `state`, `focus` and `blur` events; `useRootNavigationState` doesn't re-render on changes. A screen opened from a sheet, such as the shell, still releases the lease. iOS's turn-settings control is a native menu, so there this only affected the other chat sheets. The daemon is unchanged. JS only; `package.json` is untouched, so this ships over the air. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) is clean, and `npx vitest run` passes: 247 files, 2550 tests. - New tests in `useConversation.turnOptions.test.tsx` cover asking `/config-options` while the snapshot is hibernated, not caching an empty catalog, and keeping the last catalog through a `409`. `useChatViewLease.test.tsx` covers keeping the lease under a sheet, releasing it for a screen opened from a sheet, and announcing each registration once. Three of the four new catalog tests and the sheet-lease test fail on the old code. - Review follow-up: `turnOptionsCatalog.test.ts` covers the reload-on-wake decision (`turnOptionsLoadFor`). `useChatViewLease.test.tsx` covers a failed registration followed by a successful renewal, and a late answer from before backgrounding. `asyncValueCache.test.ts` covers the `keep` predicate, and `turnSettingsModel.test.ts` covers a remembered catalog shown alone while the snapshot reports no capabilities. - Second review follow-up: `useConversation.turnOptions.test.tsx` covers retrying a catalog that failed during the wake (`ifMissing`), and the remembered catalog on a screen that mounted before it was remembered. `useChatViewLease.test.tsx` covers a render that sees the chat blurred before the stack listeners run, and a registration answered after the chat stopped being viewed. - Third review follow-up: `useConversation.turnOptions.test.tsx` covers a lease retry waiting for a load in flight, and an older load that fails or lands late not undoing a newer one. `lastTurnOptions.test.ts` covers the remembered-catalog store, and `disconnect.storage.test.ts` covers dropping it when a machine is forgotten. - Manual check on an iOS 26.5 simulator and an Android 35 emulator, with Debug builds against a scratch daemon built from this branch, two real Claude Code chats and hibernation on. A logging proxy recorded every catalog request. Scenarios: open a hibernated chat; open its menu or sheet; tap Refresh; keep the sheet open 80 s; re-open a chat that went back to sleep with the wake held back 10 s (the model stays shown throughout). ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(cloud): delete a cloud session's artifacts on archive, and retune artifact limits (100 MiB files, 50 per session)
body:
Code changes: +137 -23\
Tests: +220 -13\
Others: +20 -6 (cloud OpenAPI contract, generated cloud-client schema, control-plane docs)

## What

Archiving a cloud session now offers the same unchecked **Delete N artifacts** box that local sessions already have. Checking it turns Confirm destructive and deletes the session's artifact files along with the archive.

It also changes the cloud artifact limits:

| Limit | Before | After | Constant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Size of one artifact file | 25 MiB | 100 MiB | `domain.MaxArtifactFileBytes` |
| Files per session | 200 | 50 | `domain.MaxSessionArtifactFiles` |
| Total size per session | 500 MiB | 500 MiB (unchanged) | `domain.MaxSessionArtifactBytes` |
| File versions waiting for cleanup per session (uploaded but not yet committed, or replaced in the last hour) | 400 versions / 1,000 MiB | 100 versions (twice the files limit) / 1,000 MiB | `domain.MaxPendingArtifactUploads` / `MaxPendingArtifactBytes` |

## Why

Cloud artifacts are among the remaining pieces of the cloud artifacts work (#6769). Until now the archive dialog hid the box for cloud sessions, and the control plane's session delete couldn't remove artifacts. So a cloud session's files stayed in S3 with no way to clear them on archive, unlike local mode.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Archive dialog for a cloud session with artifacts shows no delete box | Shows the unchecked "Delete N artifacts" box with the "can't be undone" hint, same as local |
| `DELETE /api/cloud/v1/orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}` always keeps the session's artifacts | `?deleteArtifacts=true` deletes them in the same transaction and responds `"artifactsDeleted": true` |
| — | Without the flag, or with cloud artifacts off, artifacts are kept and the response has `"artifactsDeleted": false` |
| Worker uploads a 75 MiB artifact file: skipped as oversized | Uploaded and shown (cap is 100 MiB) |
| Commit taking a session to 51 files: accepted (cap was 200) | Refused with `413`; the limit message reads "100 MiB per file, 50 files and 500 MiB per session" |

Screenshots still needed: I couldn't capture the dialog from the real app because this session has no signed-in cloud org with artifacts enabled. The dialog markup is the existing local-mode box, unchanged.

## How

- **Store:** `TerminateSession` takes a `deleteArtifacts` flag. When set, the new `deleteSessionArtifactsTx` (a session-scoped sibling of `deleteProjectArtifactsTx`) runs in the same tenant transaction. It removes the session's `ao_session_artifacts` rows and queues every object version (committed, replaced, or still uploading) with `collect_after = now()` so the sweeper deletes them. It also updates the output type and appends one `artifact.changed` event with the removed paths.
- **Late uploads:** an archive with `deleteArtifacts` also sets `ao_sessions.artifacts_deleted_at` (migration `00095`), and `RestoreSession` clears it. `RecordArtifactUpload` and `CommitSessionArtifacts` lock the session row (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`) and return `ErrNotFound` (404) while it is set. Because the archive updates the same row, an upload or commit from a worker that is still connected either lands before that archive (and is deleted with it) or is refused. The blob route deletes the S3 version when recording fails, and the worker treats the 404 as a refusal and waits instead of retrying. A plain archive doesn't set the column, so the worker's final sync still saves the last files written before it.
- **Handler:** `deleteSession` reads `?deleteArtifacts=true` only while cloud artifacts are enabled. It's a query param because the route is a bodyless `DELETE`.
- **Renderer:** `SessionArchiveDialog` no longer excludes cloud sessions. `useTerminateSession` passes `{ deleteArtifacts: true }` to the cloud-cp client and reports the response's `artifactsDeleted`. The existing "artifacts kept" toast fires when the control plane doesn't confirm the delete.

- **Limits:** only the two constants in `cloud/internal/domain/artifacts.go` change. The pending-version cap is already `2 * MaxSessionArtifactFiles`, so it drops to 100 on its own. The worker scan, the commit and upload checks, the limit error message and the agent prompt all read the constants. Hard-coded copies were updated: the contract's file `size` maximum (52428800), the desktop's cloud artifact download cap (`MAX_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_BYTES`), and `cloud/docs/control-plane.md`. Tests that hard-coded 200 files, 26 MiB or 150-file batches now derive their values from the constants. Artifact shares keep their own separate `MaxArtifactShareBytes`.

Reviewer notes:
- The fallback toast says the files are "still on disk", which is slightly off for cloud. It only shows on a control plane that predates this flag or has artifacts off, so I didn't add a new string to every language file.
- The box appears once the cloud session's artifact list has loaded, since that list is read per session after the session list.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/httpapi ./internal/postgres -count=1` against a disposable Postgres 17:
  - new `TestDeletingASessionCanDeleteItsArtifacts` (route: default, on request, artifacts off) passes
  - new store tests `TestDeletingASessionCanDeleteItsArtifacts` and `TestDeletingASessionKeepsItsArtifactsByDefault` pass; they check the files are gone, every version is queued and due, the output type, the event, and that a late commit is rejected
  - new `TestArchivingWithDeletedArtifactsRefusesLateUploads`: after an archive with deletion, recording and committing a late upload both return `ErrNotFound`, the list stays empty, and after a restore a commit works again
  - new `TestAPlainArchiveStillSavesLateArtifacts`: after a plain archive, a late upload records and commits, and the session lists both files
  - all existing artifact tests pass
  - four unrelated tests fail identically on a clean `main` checkout: `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`
- `go test ./internal/domain ./internal/httpapi ./cmd/ao-worker ./cmd/ao-cloud-agent -count=1`: pass, including the cap, oversized-file and concurrent-commit tests against the new limits
- `go test ./internal/workerexec`: two Claude model-catalog tests (`TestCloudClaudeProviderModelsReachAdapter`, `TestCloudClaudeDiscoversProviderCatalogWithLaunchCredentials`) fail identically on `origin/main`; unrelated to artifacts
- `npx vitest run src/main/cloud-artifact-ipc.test.ts`: 4 passed
- `npx vitest run` on `SessionArchiveDialog.test.tsx` (new), `useTerminateSession.test.tsx`, `ShellTopbar.test.tsx`, `cloud-telemetry.test.ts`: 87 passed
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend): no errors in changed files
- `gofmt -l` clean; `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` regenerated with openapi-typescript 7.4.4

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: chore(cloud): turn on session artifacts in the staging and production offerings
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +2 -2 (staging and production offering config)

## What

Sets `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1` in `cloud/scripts/offering/staging.env` and `cloud/scripts/offering/production.env`, so both environments serve cloud session artifacts. These are the "turn staging on" and "repeat for production" steps of the artifacts rollout in `cloud/docs/deployment.md`.

## Why

- **Staging** already serves artifacts, but only through a value set in the deploying shell. The running task definition (`ao-cloud-staging-api:325`) has `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1`, and the bucket holds artifact versions from Oct 23 and Oct 26. The committed offering still says `0`, so the next deploy from `main` would turn artifacts off for every staging org.
- **Production** runs with artifacts off (`ao-cloud-production-api:73`, `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=0`). The next `promote-production.sh` turns them on. Its existing gate refuses that unless staging's running task has `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1`, which it does.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `staging.env`: `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=0`; a plain `deploy-staging.sh` turns artifacts off | `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1`; every staging deploy keeps them on and runs the bucket check first |
| `production.env`: `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=0`; production has no session artifacts | `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACTS=1`; the next promote checks the bucket and role, then turns artifacts on |

## How

Prerequisites checked read-only against AWS (eu-north-1) before the flip. Both environments are configured the same way:

| Check | Staging | Production |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bucket exists, versioning `Enabled` | `ao-cloud-staging-tenant-artifacts` ✓ | `ao-cloud-production-tenant-artifacts` ✓ |
| Public access blocked, `BucketOwnerEnforced`, policy denies non-TLS | ✓ | ✓ |
| SSE-KMS with the key pinned in the bucket policy | key `eeb248dc-…` ✓ | key `d7aae827-…` ✓ |
| Task role allowed all nine S3 actions `check_artifact_bucket` and the docs list (`iam simulate-principal-policy`) | `ao-cloud-staging-task-role` ✓ | `ao-cloud-production-task-role` ✓ |
| Task role `kms:GenerateDataKey`/`kms:Decrypt` on its key, via `kms:ViaService = s3.eu-north-1.amazonaws.com` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `AO_CLOUD_PROVIDER_SECRET_KEY` on the running task (signs artifact links) | ✓ | ✓ |
| Lifecycle rule (docs' backstop to the sweeper) | **missing** | **missing** |

Follow-up outside this PR: neither bucket has a lifecycle configuration. The docs require one as a backstop to the sweeper: expire noncurrent versions after 30 days, remove orphaned delete markers, abort incomplete multipart uploads after a day. It isn't needed for artifacts to work, but both buckets should get it.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest scripts/tests/test_deploy_scripts.py` (from `cloud/`): 22 passed
- After merge, run the docs' rollout checks on staging, then again on production after the next promote: an artifact session's HTML file and the image it references open, an edit adds a version, and an archived then restored session's files open again.

title: fix(daemon): find Homebrew tmux when a macOS daemon's PATH omits it
body:
Code changes: +33 -1\
Tests: +169 -5\
Others: +6 -3 (docs)

## What

When the daemon's own `PATH` has no tmux, the shared tmux resolver (`backend/internal/tmuxbin`) now also checks the fixed macOS install paths: `/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux` (Homebrew on Apple silicon), `/usr/local/bin/tmux` (Homebrew on Intel) and `/opt/local/bin/tmux` (MacPorts). The existing lookup order is unchanged and comes first.

## Why

Fixes #2812, scoped to the remaining standalone/headless macOS case as asked in https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/2812#issuecomment-6447275278.

A daemon started outside the desktop app (launchd, cron, `env -i`, automation wrappers) inherits a minimal `PATH` without `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `/usr/local/bin`. `tmuxbin.ResolveWith` checked `AO_TMUX_BINARY`, then the bundled resource, then `lookPath("tmux")` on that `PATH` only. So an installed Homebrew tmux was invisible: every TUI spawn failed with `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING`, and `ao doctor` reported tmux as missing instead of pointing at the cause.

## Before / After

Real `ao daemon` started with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, with real tmux 3.5a at Intel Homebrew's `/usr/local/bin/tmux` and not on that `PATH`:

| Before (upstream `main` 37951c2c1b) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| `ao doctor`: `WARN tmux: no configured, bundled, or system tmux found for this ao process` | `ao doctor`: `PASS tmux: /usr/local/bin/tmux (system for this ao process; tmux 3.5a)` |
| `ao spawn --mode tui`: `spawn: runtime: prerequisite missing: tmux required on macOS but AO's configured, bundled, or system tmux was not found (RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING)`, no session row | `spawned session demo-1 "tmux-probe" (idle)`; `GET /api/v1/sessions` shows it live |
| `AO_TMUX_BINARY=/nonexistent/ao/tmux`: refused | Still refused: a broken configured path never falls back to a machine tmux |

## How

- Lookup order: `AO_TMUX_BINARY` (fail-closed, unchanged) → packaged `resources/tmux/bin/tmux` (unchanged) → `PATH` (unchanged) → on macOS only, the three install paths above, in that order. The bundled binary and a tmux on `PATH` keep priority over the fixed paths.
- The install-path probe uses the same injected `lookPath` as the other steps, so production uses `exec.LookPath` (which skips missing or non-executable files) and tests stay hermetic on machines that have Homebrew tmux. A hit keeps the Homebrew symlink path rather than the versioned Cellar path, so it survives `brew upgrade`.
- The spawn gate, the tmux runtime default binary, `ao doctor` and the startup system check all call this resolver, so they agree on one binary.
- Earlier attempts (#2815, #2870) changed the daemon's process-wide `PATH` at startup. This PR only touches tmux discovery: no `os.Setenv("PATH")`, no login-shell probe, and nothing else in the daemon changes.
- Intentional omissions:
  - Linux is unchanged: it no longer gates spawns on tmux, and its packaged tmux is bundled.
  - Nix and other custom prefixes are not probed. `PATH` or `AO_TMUX_BINARY` still cover them.
  - The legacy default-socket client lookup in the tmux runtime is unchanged. It is only used when the desktop sets `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME`, and the desktop already provides a full `PATH`.
- `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingTmuxBeforeSessionRow` stubbed only the bare name `tmux` as missing. It now treats any `…/tmux` as missing so it keeps meaning "tmux is not installed".

## Testing

- **Real server (macOS, Intel):** built `ao` from upstream `main` and from this branch. Each daemon ran under `env -i` with the minimal `PATH`, a scratch `HOME`/`AO_DATA_DIR`, a scratch git repo and a stub `aider` harness. Each run did `ao project add`, `ao doctor`, `ao spawn --mode tui`, and checked `GET /api/v1/sessions` (results in the table above).
  - With no tmux anywhere, both builds refuse the spawn, so there is no false positive.
  - Not run on a real machine: the Apple-silicon `/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux` path. Unit tests cover it, and the new doctor test runs on `macos-latest` in `cli-e2e`.
- **Regression tests (red on `main`, green here):**
  - `tmuxbin`: each install path found with a minimal `PATH`; the real `exec.LookPath` skips missing or non-executable candidates. These call the macOS path list directly, so they run in Linux CI too.
  - `session_manager` (macOS): a spawn succeeds with Homebrew tmux off `PATH`.
  - `cli` (macOS): `ao doctor` reports Homebrew tmux as PASS.
  - Precedence guards (pass before and after): `AO_TMUX_BINARY` never falls back; the bundled binary beats install paths; `PATH` beats install paths; no install paths outside macOS.
- **Local CI mirror (Go 1.27.1):**
  - `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`
  - both `backend-core` shard commands, and `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./internal/session_manager ./internal/storage/sqlite/store`
  - `go test -tags e2e -v ./internal/cli/...`
  - golangci-lint v2.13.2 (`0 issues`), sqlc v1.31.1 and `api:spec` regeneration (no drift)
  - gitleaks v7.4.0 in `debian:bookworm-slim` (`No leaks found`)
  - `cli-e2e` fresh-install container (`fresh-install check: OK`)
  - Results: everything passes except tests that also fail on `main` on this machine. The full parallel `-race` shards hit agent-adapter CLI-probe timeouts on this Intel Mac, and 18 of the 22 failing tests pass when rerun alone (`-p 1`). The other 4 fail identically on upstream `main`:
    - `TestSpawn_EarlyFailurePreservesNonEmptyScratchWorkspace`: no tmux on `PATH` here; passes with tmux on `PATH`.
    - `opencodev2/malformed_version`: finds the real OpenCode installed on this Mac.
    - `TestSearchWorkspaceContentCommonTermReachesLaterFiles`: hits its 5 s deadline on this machine.
    - `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders`: depends on this machine's git conditional-include behavior.
- **Left to remote CI:** `chat-race` and the `sqlite` shards (`go list -deps` shows none of their packages import `tmuxbin`), the Windows job (no Windows runner here), and `api-drift`'s `schema.ts` step (the spec is unchanged).

title: Mobile: reconnecting an id-less legacy machine by QR adds a second entry instead of replacing it
body:
## What happens

A machine migrated from the old single-server config is saved with `id: ""` (`packages/mobile/lib/hosts.ts:50`). It adopts its daemon-issued id only on its first successful connect, so a pairing that has been unreachable since the migration stays id-less.

That is the machine a user tries to fix with **Reconnect** / **Scan new code**. Every current pairing code carries a `hostId`, so the scanned code never matches the saved `""` id:

- **Before the reconnect-scan fix:** the scan was rejected as "That code belongs to a different machine", even when it came from the same computer.
- **After it:** `pairFromCode` treats the code as a different machine and saves it as a new entry. The old id-less entry stays in the list, still offline, with no identity to match it again.

## Expected

When the repair target has no identity yet, a code that answers from one of the same addresses should replace that entry. The scanned machine would take over its name and appearance, and the `""` entry (plus its keystore token) would be removed.

## Notes

- Matching on endpoints alone is not an identity check. A private LAN address is a different machine on each network (see `lib/race.ts`), so the match should require the user to have chosen this entry explicitly (the repair path), not happen on a generic scan.
- Follow-up to the mobile change that lets a reconnect scan for another machine connect that machine instead of rejecting it.

title: fix(mobile): connect the scanned machine instead of rejecting it during reconnect
body: Code changes: +97 -30\ Tests: +96 -5\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Scanning a pairing code always connects the machine that code belongs to: - **Reconnect / Scan new code, another machine's code:** that machine is connected. If it's already saved, it's refreshed in place with its name kept. If it's new, it goes through the normal naming step. The machine you started from is left untouched. - The pair screen now says what a scan did before it closes, using the existing in-place notice slot for about 2 s (VoiceOver gets an explicit announcement on iOS; Android reads the live region): - **Reconnected *A*** (reconnect matched) - **_B_ is already paired** / *Connection details refreshed.* ("Add a machine" with a saved machine's code) - **Connected to *B*** / *That code was for B. A still needs a new code.* (reconnect with another machine's code) - A machine you have just named shows nothing new, same as before. ## Why Users reported that scanning a machine they already have, to switch to it, stopped on "That code belongs to a different machine". Generic **Add a machine** already refreshed a saved machine in place. But Settings shows **Scan new code** (the repair path for the selected machine) right above **Add a machine** whenever the selected machine is offline, and the repair path rejected any code that wasn't for that machine, before even probing it. Successful scans of a saved machine also closed the scanner silently, so nobody could tell whether it had re-paired, switched, or added anything. Follow-up for id-less legacy pairings: #7346. ## Before / After Android release builds of the PR base and this branch on an emulator. The emulator's virtual camera is fed a QR image, and two scratch daemons (*Work Laptop* = A, frozen to be unreachable, and *Studio Mac* = B) provide the codes. The QR viewfinder is blurred, and the daemons and their tokens have been deleted. | Before (base `83bb06c`) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | | | | | Settings → **Scan new code** on offline *Work Laptop*, scan *Studio Mac* → "Different machine: That code belongs to a different machine. Scan the code from Work Laptop." | *Studio Mac* is named, saved and made active; the notice "Connected to Studio Mac" shows before the screen closes. *Work Laptop* stays saved and unchanged (Environments: 2 machines). | | **Add a machine**, scan saved *B* → the screen closes with no message | | | **Reconnect** *A*, scan *A* → the screen closes with no message | "Reconnected A" then the screen closes (covered by `pairFlow` / `pairedNotice` tests; not recorded) | ## How - `lib/pairFlow.ts`: `pairFromCode` no longer rejects a mismatch before the race. After verifying, it picks the saved pairing by the identity being saved (`offer.hostId || outcome.hostId`). The repair target counts only when its id is that identity, so another machine's token is never written under the repair target's entry, and an id-less legacy pairing never "matches" an id-less code on `""`. A new `findHost` dependency replaces the lookup the screen used to do before calling. The result now carries `kind` (`added` / `reconnected` / `existing`) and, on a mismatched repair, `instead`. The `wrong-machine` reason is gone. - `pairedNotice(result)` is pure copy selection, kept in `lib` so the suite covers it (the package has no screen tests). - `app/pair.tsx`: `finish(notice)` shows the notice, runs the reconnect while it's on screen, and then navigates. A throw while finishing clears the notice. Leaving the screen early skips only the plain back navigation (so it can't pop another screen); finishing onboarding always runs once a machine is saved, as before. - Probing order is unchanged: the code's endpoints are still raced against the code's own `hostId`, so identity is checked before the token is presented. **Intentional omission:** reconnecting a legacy pairing with no id (`id: ""`) by QR adds the scanned machine as a new entry, and the notice says the old one still needs a code. Replacing the id-less entry is tracked in #7346. ## Testing - `packages/mobile`: `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` (245 files, 2527 tests) pass on Node 20.20.2 (CI's version). - `lib/pairFlow.test.ts` covers: a different machine during repair is added as itself; a saved different machine during repair keeps its name and appearance; a generic scan of a saved machine refreshes in place without the name sheet; a matching repair reports `reconnected`; an id-less legacy repair is not reported as reconnected (fails against the previous match); plus `pairedNotice` copy for each outcome. - On an Android emulator (release builds, base vs head), verified as recorded above. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(cloud): raise the artifact file cap to 100 MiB
body:
Code changes: +3 -3\
Tests: +2 -2\
Others: +3 -3 (cloud OpenAPI contract, control-plane docs)

> Stacked on #7340, which raised this cap from 25 to 50 MiB. This PR targets #7340's branch; retarget it to `main` once #7340 merges.

## What

Raises the size cap for one cloud session artifact file from 50 MiB to 100 MiB.

| Limit | Before (#7340) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Size of one artifact file (`domain.MaxArtifactFileBytes`) | 50 MiB | **100 MiB** |
| Files per session (`domain.MaxSessionArtifactFiles`) | 50 | 50 (unchanged) |
| Total size per session (`domain.MaxSessionArtifactBytes`) | 500 MiB | 500 MiB (unchanged) |
| File versions waiting for cleanup per session | 100 versions / 1,000 MiB | unchanged |

## Why

Allow larger single deliverables, such as videos, datasets and exports, as session artifacts.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Agent saves a 75 MiB file: the worker skips it ("file is over the per-file limit") and it never appears in Artifacts | Uploaded and shown in Artifacts |
| Upload or commit over the cap: `413` "Artifacts are limited to 50 MiB per file, 50 files and 500 MiB per session" | Same refusal above 100 MiB, with "100 MiB per file" |
| Desktop refuses to save a cloud artifact over 50 MiB | Refuses over 100 MiB |
| Agent prompt: "up to 50 MiB per file" | "up to 100 MiB per file" |

## How

- One constant changes in `cloud/internal/domain/artifacts.go`. Everything else reads it: the worker scan, the upload and commit checks, the limit error message and the agent prompt.
- Copies that had the number written in were updated by hand:
  - the contract's file `size` maximum (`104857600`, both schemas)
  - the desktop's `MAX_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_BYTES`
  - `cloud/docs/control-plane.md`
  - the CLI listing test's maximum-size fixtures
- **What a 100 MiB file stresses:**
  - The control plane streams each upload straight to S3 in one `PutObject` without buffering. S3 accepts single PUTs up to 5 GB.
  - Both the worker's upload timeout and the control plane's upload read deadline are 5 minutes, so a 100 MiB upload needs about 0.35 MiB/s.
  - The desktop's save path holds the file in memory, which is fine at 100 MiB.
- **Reviewer notes:**
  - Two shorter worker timeouts depend on the session total (still 500 MiB), not the file size: the 30-second restore before the agent starts, and the 20-second final flush at shutdown. A single 100 MiB file is more likely than a 50 MiB one to miss the final flush on a slow link. In that case the file isn't saved, the same as any file written too late.
  - Shared artifact links keep their own 10 MiB cap (`MaxArtifactShareBytes`).

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/domain ./internal/httpapi ./cmd/ao-worker ./cmd/ao-cloud-agent -count=1`: pass, including the oversized-file test (derived from the constant) and the CLI listing test, which checks a full page of maximum-size entries still fits the CLI's response limit
- `go test ./internal/postgres -run 'Artifact|DeletingA|ArchivedSession'` against a fresh Postgres 17: pass
- `npx vitest run src/main/cloud-artifact-ipc.test.ts`: 4 passed
- `gofmt -l` clean; `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is unchanged (openapi-typescript doesn't emit `maximum`)

title: feat(integrations): install and onboard Orchestrator.inc from Orchestrator Bot
body:
Code changes: +105 -11 (one skill file)\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +4 -4 (README and generated manifest)

## What

Orchestrator Bot's `ao-setup` now takes a user from "no Orchestrator.inc" to a working first orchestrator.

**Install and open** (new "Missing pieces" section):

| Probe shows | Next step the bot takes |
| --- | --- |
| `python=missing` (including the macOS python3 stub) | Fix first: `xcode-select --install` on macOS, package manager line on Linux |
| `daemon=not running`, `app=missing` (macOS) | Offers to install; on yes runs "Install on a Mac" |
| `daemon=not running`, `app=<path>` | Opens that app, then waits up to 2 minutes for the daemon |
| `daemon=not running` on Linux | Open it if installed, else the AppImage, .deb or .rpm link |
| `projects=` empty | Runs "First run" |
| `ao=missing` with projects | Says which three actions need the CLI |

**Install on a Mac:** runs detached in the background (its own session) and logs to `~/.ao-grok/install.log`, which the bot polls. Picks the chip with `sysctl hw.optional.arm64`, downloads the latest DMG from GitHub releases, verifies the app's code signature and Developer ID team `X9LNSP8MC2`, copies it to `/Applications` (or `~/Applications` if that isn't writable), opens it, and always detaches the image. Ends in `INSTALLED <path>`, `INSTALLED_NOT_OPENED <path>`, `DOWNLOAD_FAILED`, `BAD_SIGNATURE` or `INSTALL_FAILED`.

**First run** (once the app is running):

1. **A coding agent:** lists readiness from `GET agents/readiness`. Uses a ready agent (asks which if several), starts sign-in for an installed one (`POST agents/<id>/auth`, relays `guidance`, rechecks with `agents/refresh`), or installs Claude Code or Codex through Orchestrator.inc's installer (`POST agents/<id>/install`, polls the job).
2. **A project:** suggests the 10 git clones with the most recent git activity (worktrees left out) and registers the pick with that agent as worker and orchestrator (`POST projects`). Reports `NOT_A_GIT_REPO` and `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED <id>`.
3. **The first orchestrator:** offers to start it with the user's first request.

Also: "install Orchestrator" trigger, onboarding in the skill description and README, manifest `2026.10.28.1`.

## Why

Anyone can add the public template (https://x.ai/bot/1WTqU5Ql7Ysftsg4KpWjW), but setup used to stop at "AO not found". Now the bot onboards people who don't have Orchestrator.inc yet, from chat.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Probe on a computer with the daemon stopped: Python traceback | `daemon=not running` |
| Computer without Orchestrator.inc: listed as not found | "Want me to install it?" → `INSTALLED <path>`, app open |
| App running with no projects: "open it and add a repo" | Bot checks the coding agent, suggests repos, registers the pick, offers to start the orchestrator |

## How

- Every install, sign-in and project change needs the user's yes. Sign-in happens in Orchestrator.inc's own terminal (it may open the browser).
- Downloads come only from the official `releases/latest/download` URLs; the app is installed only if its signature verifies with team `X9LNSP8MC2`.
- Existing users (projects already registered) skip "First run", so they aren't asked to pick an agent again.
- Intentional omissions: Linux installs stay manual (they need `sudo`); Windows stays unsupported by the skills.

## Testing

All against the live daemon on macOS, in zsh and bash, with throwaway data removed afterwards:

- Probe: running → app path, 5 projects, 33 live sessions; daemon unreachable → `daemon=not running`, no traceback.
- Install, with the real 295 MB arm64 DMG: system Applications made read-only → fell back to `~/Applications`, logged `INSTALLED <path>`; same DMG with a wrong team ID → `BAD_SIGNATURE`; no image left mounted. The detached job runs in its own process group and finishes after the starting shell returns. The generated script passes `sh -n`.
- First run: agent list shows readiness and sign-in state; repo finder returns clones ranked by git activity; registering a throwaway repo → `added`, again → `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED <id>`, a plain folder → `NOT_A_GIT_REPO`; test project deleted (200), project list back to five.
- All 7 shell blocks parse in zsh and bash; manifest hashes match; `ao-update`'s fetcher with the published `2026.10.27.3` as installed: only `ao-setup` changes and its frontmatter parses.
- Not run: a real agent install or sign-in (would change this machine's agents), Linux, and a fresh Grok account.

title: chore: move the AO Cloud control plane to its own private repository
body:
Code changes: +54 -114264\
Tests: +1 -76140\
Others: +30 -7604 (docs, CI, go.work, package.json)

> **Draft: do not merge before the cutover.** Merging this removes the control plane from this repository. The private `OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane` repository must be caught up, and deploys moved to it, first. See **Cutover** below.

## What

Moves the AO Cloud control plane out of this public repository into the private `OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane`. This follows the "Tailscale model" from the 2026-10-24 security review: an open client and a proprietary hosted service.

- **Stays public:** everything a user installs. That is the desktop app (including its Cloud UI), the local daemon and CLI, the mobile app, `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, and the `@aoagents/cloud-client` SDK.
- **Moves private:** all of `cloud/`. That is the control plane, worker, migrations, sandbox providers, billing, deploy and promote scripts, infrastructure, Coder templates and operator runbooks.
- **Where they meet:** only at the versioned contract and at the public Go packages the control plane imports (`backend/pkg/contract`, `pkg/agentruntime`, `pkg/agentcreds`).

This PR:

- deletes `cloud/` (786 files), plus the cloud developer guide and cloud design notes from `docs/`, which now live in the private repo's `docs/`;
- changes `go.work` to `use ./backend`. Without this, every backend job, and the `ao-releases` pricing-catalog job, would fail on the missing module;
- drops the `cloud-build-test` job and the `cloud/**` trigger from the Go workflow, and the `npm run cloud:local*` / `cloud:staging` scripts. `cloud:check` stays; it builds the public client;
- adds `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh` and a `Public boundary` workflow. This is the Bitwarden lesson: the public app must build from public code alone. The check fails if `go.work` uses a missing directory, `cloud/` reappears, Go code imports the control plane module, or an npm script runs something from `cloud/`;
- points the few comments that named `cloud/` files at the private repository, and removes `cloud/*` from the contributor path-area map.

## Why

The whole paid control plane, with its billing, auth, providers, deploy scripts and runbooks, has been public under Apache-2.0 since 2026-08-28. The security review recommended keeping future work, ops tooling and runbooks private, and having the two sides meet only at a versioned API contract.

This does **not** rewrite public history. Copies already taken stay under Apache-2.0, and leaked resource names are treated as known.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `cloud/` (control plane, worker, deploy scripts, runbooks) in this public repo | In private `OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane`, 72 commits of history kept via `git filter-repo` |
| `go.work`: `use ( ./backend ./cloud )` | `use ./backend` |
| Go workflow runs `cloud-build-test` | Runs in the private repo's CI: build, vet, `-race` tests, script tests, contract integrity, image backports |
| Nothing stops a private import or path from creeping in | `Public boundary` workflow: `public boundary: ok` on this branch; on `main` it fails ("cloud/ is tracked", "Go files import the control plane module", "package.json: scripts cloud:local… reference cloud/") |
| Control plane image built against a backend pin from 2026-10-05, while CI built against HEAD via `go.work` | Private repo pins public main (`83bb06c741`); CI and the image build the same thing with `GOWORK=off` |

## How

**The private repository** (`OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane`, private) was made like this:

```sh
git clone --no-local --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator ao-control-plane
cd ao-control-plane
git filter-repo --path cloud/ --path-rename cloud/:
```

Then one stand-up commit:

- a proprietary `LICENSE` that notes the prior Apache-2.0 publication;
- `go.mod` pinning `github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend` to public main through the canonical `OrchestratorInc` path, with `scripts/bump-public-backend.sh`;
- vendored copies of the two public contract files its tests read (`contracts/`), with `scripts/sync-public-contracts.sh [--check]`;
- path fixes where code assumed a `cloud/` subdirectory: two Go tests, the monitoring test, and the staging desktop launcher, which now uses a sibling public checkout;
- a `package.json` that keeps `npm run cloud:*`;
- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the README's "Working across the two repositories" section;
- CI:
  - `CI`: gofmt, build, vet, race tests, 93 script tests, contract integrity, Expat/Brotli backports;
  - `gitleaks`: every PR and push, plus a weekly full-history scan of every branch;
  - `Public main compatibility`: nightly against the tip of public main, to catch a public change that would break the control plane.

Two helper scripts are there for the transition: `scripts/import-public-cloud-commits.sh` replays any public commits that touch `cloud/` after the split point, and `scripts/port-public-pr.sh` moves the `cloud/` part of an open public PR onto a private branch.

**Cutover** (needs an owner and a freeze window):

1. Freeze `cloud/` here: no new merges that touch it.
2. In the private repo, run `scripts/import-public-cloud-commits.sh <public checkout>` to catch up to public main, and push.
3. For the 10 open PRs touching `cloud/` (#7201, #7208, #7294, #7340, #7341, #7059, #6719, #6844, #7041, #6983), either merge them before the freeze or port them with `scripts/port-public-pr.sh <n>`. The public part stays in the original PR.
4. Deploy staging from the private repo (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) and run the usual smoke tests. Production promotes from staging as before.
5. Rebase this PR on main, regenerate the change counts, mark it ready, and merge.
6. Afterwards, add CODEOWNERS for `contracts/` and `backend/pkg/`, the packages the control plane imports. Contract changes stay additive.

## Testing

**Public, on this branch:**

- `cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...` passes.
- `go test -count=1 ./...` matches `main`: the same two tests fail on unmodified `main` too (`TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders`, `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects`, both tied to the local environment). Five more failed only under full-suite load and pass when run alone, on both trees.
- `go build ./cmd/pricingcatalog` passes; this is the job `ao-releases` runs.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok here, fails on `main` for the expected reasons.
- Contributor-project tests: 137 passed.
- Nothing in `frontend/`, `packages/` or `mobile` imports or builds anything from `cloud/` (audited). `ao-releases` never references `cloud/` or `contracts/` (audited).

**Private (`ao-control-plane` at `49819a4`):**

- GitHub Actions `CI` and `gitleaks` both passed on the first push.
- Locally: `GOWORK=off go build`, `vet`, and `go test -race ./...` all pass. `TestWorkspaceUserLaunchScriptStartsWorker` flaked once under load and passed 3 of 3 alone. 93 script tests pass.
- gitleaks v7.4.0 (the pinned CI binary) found no leaks over the full 72-commit history.
- The `ao-cloud` binary built from the private repo has the same dependency set as the one the current `cloud/Dockerfile` builds. Only the backend pin moved, to public main.
- The import script reproduced the private repo's own #7329 commit byte for byte. The port script turned #7041 and #7340 into building private branches.

**Not done yet:** a staging deploy from the private repository, which is step 4 of the cutover.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense (no user-visible change; the boundary check is the new test)
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) (pending on this draft)
