title: fix(cloud): serve artifact byte ranges so video and audio can seek
body:
Code changes: +92 -8\
Tests: +57 -6\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The cloud artifact file route now serves HTTP byte ranges, so video and audio artifacts can be seeked. It also serves audio, video and image artifacts with their real media types.

## Why

In a cloud session a video artifact played, but the seek bar did nothing. The route ignored `Range` and always answered `200` with the whole file and no `Accept-Ranges`, so Chrome reported nothing seekable. `.mov`, `.m4v`, `.ogv`, audio (`.m4a`, `.aac`, `.flac`, `.ogg`, `.oga`, `.opus`) and some images (`.avif`, `.apng`, `.bmp`, `.ico`) were served as `application/octet-stream`, although the viewer treats them as media.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `GET` with `Range: bytes=1000-1999` returns `200`, full body, no `Accept-Ranges`. Chrome: seekable range 0, seeking to 15s snaps back to the start. | Returns `206`, `Content-Range: bytes 1000-1999/N`, `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. Chrome seeks to 15s. |
| `.mov` is `application/octet-stream` | `.mov` is `video/quicktime` |

Checked against the local cloud stack (MinIO): a real 2.8 MiB `.mp4` returned `206` with `Content-Range: bytes 0-99/2839045`, and the desktop app seeked it.

## How

- `artifactstore.GetRange` passes one byte range to the S3 `GetObject`. `Get` calls it with no range, so other callers are unchanged. A range past the end becomes `ErrRangeNotSatisfiable`.
- `writeArtifactObject` accepts only a single `bytes=a-b`, `a-` or `-n` range. Several ranges, another unit, or an `If-Range` that does not match the served ETag are served as the whole file with `200`. A range past the end returns `416` with `Content-Range: bytes */size`.
- The S3 fake now uses `http.ServeContent`, so it honors `Range` like S3.
- Content types stay a fixed list in `artifactstore.ContentType`. It also feeds share links.

Not changed: files over 25 MiB are still skipped by the worker, and the viewer does not keep the playback position when a link is refreshed.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet` and `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/artifactstore/... ./internal/httpapi` in `cloud/` pass.
- New tests cover closed, open-ended and suffix ranges, several ranges, a stale and a matching `If-Range`, a range past the end, and the media types.
- Not run locally: the full `cloud` suite (`go test -race ./...`) and `golangci-lint` (not installed). Those need CI.
- Seeked a real `.mp4` in the desktop app against the local cloud stack.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions
- [x] Before / After filled in
- [x] Tests added for the new behavior
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (run in CI; see Testing for what ran locally)

title: fix(cloud): load cloud artifact media without a CORS request
body:
Code changes: +5 -3\
Tests: +6 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The file viewer no longer sets `crossorigin="anonymous"` on images, video and audio that come from a cloud session.

## Why

`mediaCrossOrigin` sets `crossorigin="anonymous"` for localhost URLs so the local daemon sees the renderer Origin. It was applied to cloud artifact URLs too. The cloud control plane sends no CORS headers on `/artifact-files`, so with the control plane on localhost (the `npm run cloud:local` dev stack) the browser refused the file and the viewer showed "Unable to load this file". Retry failed the same way.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud video on a localhost control plane: "Unable to load this file" (`MEDIA_ELEMENT_ERROR: Format error`) | The video loads and plays |

Checked in Chrome against a real cloud artifact: without `crossorigin` the video loaded and seeked; with `crossorigin="anonymous"` it failed.

## How

`FileMediaPreview` passes no `crossOrigin` when the source is a cloud artifact. Daemon and remote host files keep it. Production uses an https control plane, so it was probably not affected; this fixes local and dev cloud setups.

Not changed: other components that call `mediaCrossOrigin` (chat images, markdown images, link preview cards) were not checked for the same problem.

## Testing

- `vitest run src/renderer/components/FileMediaPreview.test.tsx` passes (14 tests, 1 new).
- Not run locally: the frontend typecheck and the rest of the frontend CI jobs. Those need CI.
- Opened a cloud `.mp4` in the desktop app against the local cloud stack.

title: feat(mobile): browse, comment on and restore a session's artifacts
body: Code changes: +2355 -97\ Tests: +590 -3\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Mobile can now show a session's artifacts: the pages, documents and images an agent writes to the session's artifact folder. Desktop shows them in the inspector's Artifacts tab; until now the phone had no way to see them. - **Entry points:** an **Artifacts** row (with the file count) in a chat session's ⋯ menu, under Review changes. Terminal sessions have no ⋯ menu, so they get a header button after Files, shown only once the session has artifacts. - **Gallery:** a two-column grid (three on wide screens), newest first. Each card shows a peek at the file, as the desktop gallery does: the picture for an image, the page itself drawn small for HTML, the document drawn small for markdown, and the opening lines for text. Other files get a per-kind icon and file type. Every card also shows the name, age and size. Pull to refresh. - **Tap opens a viewer:** markdown renders natively (with its images, from the artifact folder), code and text are highlighted (a long file shows its first 200k characters, with a note), images fit and pinch-zoom, HTML pages render as the desktop frames them (AO's theme, a phone-width viewport, and the files they link), and SVG, video and (on iOS) PDF open in a WebView; Android's WebView has no PDF renderer, so a PDF there says to open it on the machine. A file that reads as binary says it isn't text; one with an unknown extension is read and shown if it is text, as on desktop. The viewer reloads when the agent rewrites the file. - **Long-press (or the viewer's ⋯):** Open, Ask the agent, Copy contents and Version history (not for known binary formats: archives, office documents, databases) and Delete artifact, which asks first. iOS uses the native action sheet; Android uses an in-app list styled like the worker row's options. - **Version history** (text artifacts only: markdown, code, HTML; the daemon reads versions back as text, so images and media have none, as on desktop): a clock button in the viewer header and **Version history** in both menus open a sheet listing every kept version, newest first, the first marked **Current**. Each row has a time ("Today, 8:31 PM", "Yesterday, …", "Oct 11, …"), "Restored from …" for a restore, and who wrote it (the agent's logo, or a person icon for a save or restore made in the app). Tapping a version opens it read-only (an HTML version drawn as its page, markdown rendered, anything else as source) with **Back to current** and **Restore this version**; the daemon keeps the replaced content as a version first, so a restore can itself be undone. - **Ask the agent:** select text in a markdown or code artifact and choose **Add to chat** in the selection menu to comment on that text, or pick **Ask the agent** in the ⋯ or long-press menu to comment on the whole file (any artifact, HTML and images included). The comment is sent now or added to the session's review, the same one the Files screen keeps, and reaches the agent as the message the desktop artifact viewer sends ("Selected text: …", or "Entire file"). - **Reported pages in chat:** an HTML page a chat agent reports with `ao report --artifact` now shows in its turn, in the same frame as `html_render` pages (#6982), instead of a one-line row with its name. A tap opens it in the artifact viewer. ## Why Agents increasingly hand back artifacts rather than PRs (plans, reports, HTML pages, screenshots). On the phone those were invisible: the only way to read one was to go back to the desktop. Agents also rewrite artifacts as they go; the daemon keeps up to 50 versions of each, but the phone had no way to see an earlier one or roll back a bad rewrite. ## Before / After Android emulator, same session and data on both sides. The gallery and chat rows compare against `main`; the later rows (version history, Ask, images, card previews, HTML versions) compare against this branch before each was added. The image rows use a markdown file the test proxy served (linking two real screenshots) and real HTML artifacts. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | No artifacts screen | | | No artifacts screen | | | No artifact viewer | | | No artifact viewer | | | | | | | | | No version history on mobile | | | No version history on mobile | | | No version history on mobile | | | | | | | | | No way to comment on an artifact | | | No way to comment on an artifact | | | No way to comment on an artifact | | | No way to comment on an artifact | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | On iOS, the rest of the features, from the same run: | Gallery | Action sheet | Add to chat | History | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | Version | Review tray | Markdown images | Card previews | HTML version | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | ## How - **No backend changes.** History uses the existing `artifact-versions` list, sync, read and restore routes, and `artifactFiles` was already on every session read; `mapSession` now keeps it (only path, name, kind, size and time: the daemon's `rawUrl`/`previewUrl` use its own request host and aren't reachable from the phone). - **File routes.** Reads the app makes with the Bearer header (text, a page's inlined files, gallery and markdown images) use the `artifact-files` route, which serves the artifact folder only, a page with AO's bootstrap and anything else as its bytes. The legacy `preview/files/__ao_artifacts__/` form is kept only where it is needed: a URL a WebView loads by itself (SVG, video, oversized text, an unlisted file, the chat frame's fallback), whose auth is the preview cookie scoped to that route, and a page's raw HTML for Copy. - **Markdown source** comes back raw from `artifact-files`; a page's raw HTML is read from the preview route with `raw=true`, since `artifact-files` writes the bootstrap into pages. - **One viewer with #7331.** #7331 added a screen at the same route, `/artifact/[sessionId]`, for files a worker report links to; it loads `/preview/artifacts/`. This viewer now serves both: a file the session lists gets the native viewer and its menu, and anything else (the session's list is capped) opens as the daemon-rendered page, as #7331's did, with "The worker no longer has this file." on a 404. The report row now passes `path` instead of `entry`. It goes through `preview/files/__ao_artifacts__/` rather than `/preview/artifacts/` because the `ao_conn` cookie is scoped to `/preview/files/`: over a password-protected connection, a page from the other route cannot load its own images. - **Delete** calls the existing `DELETE /artifact-files` and hides the card at once rather than waiting for the next poll. - **Android menu:** an Android `Alert` holds at most three buttons, so Open/Copy/Delete/Cancel silently lost Cancel. The menu is an in-app modal there, which also fits Version history and Ask the agent, and leaves room for Share. - Pure logic lives in `lib/artifacts.ts` (parsing, ordering, path safety, which viewer and which menu actions apply) with unit tests. - **Opening is instant:** the sheet shows the stored list from `GET`, then replaces it with the `sync` result. Sync records any edit the daemon's 30-second observer has not picked up, but waits up to two seconds for the file to settle, so showing only its answer meant a spinner every time. The desktop menu does the same. - **Time labels are written out** rather than built with `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, which Hermes does not have. Times and dates still use the device locale. - Opened from a gallery card, **Current** opens the live file; from the viewer, it just closes the sheet. - **An HTML version shows as its page**, so versions can be told apart at a glance (desktop still shows source, "for now" in `ArtifactVersionPreview`). Versions are stored raw and the daemon writes its theme bootstrap only into the current file, so `versionPageHtml` writes in the same theme variables (the app's), base style and viewport after the doctype; the page's linked files are inlined as for the live page (today's files, not the version's), and the WebView does not navigate. A truncated version still shows as source, since a cut-off page would render broken. - Parsing, time labels, restore notes and authorship live in `lib/artifactVersions.ts`, with unit tests. The base page style there is a copy of the daemon's `baseCSS`; a test reads the Go constant and fails if they drift. - **A session the board does not list** (an orchestrator) is read again when its screen regains focus and every 10 s while it is up, so a restore or an agent's rewrite shows in the viewer. - **Comments reuse the Files screen's pieces** (#6922): `SelectionComposer`, the review store and tray, and `sendFileFeedback` with the shared formatter. The target matches the desktop's `ArtifactSelectionAsk`: `{ source: name, path, side: "file", quote }`. Artifact comments join the session's one review, so they batch with file comments. A selection of only whitespace quotes nothing. - **"Add to chat"** is the native selection item chat already uses (patched `UITextView` on iOS, `AOResponseSelection` on Android). Its label is native, so it stays "Add to chat" without a new app build. `ChatMarkdown` and `HighlightedCodeText` gain an `onAddSelection` prop that turns it on outside a conversation; chat's own rule (only a finished message can be quoted) is unchanged. A markdown artifact now renders in `continuousSelection` mode, like a chat reply, so a selection can span paragraphs. - **Chat frames:** `readArtifactRef` reads `{ event: "artifact", artifact: { path, name } }` and the frame loads the page as the viewer does (inlined, below). It stays at the desktop's 400 px opening height rather than the page's measured one: most artifacts have no mobile viewport, so the WebView scales them down and their measured height left an empty band. - **HTML artifacts load inlined, with AO's theme, on both platforms** (`lib/artifactPageInliner.ts`, `useInlinedArtifactPage`). The page is read from the `artifact-files` route, the one the desktop frames artifacts from, which writes in AO's theme bootstrap (the variables pages style against, the font, a viewport tag). Read from the preview route, a page styled for AO fell back to the browser's serif font at desktop width. The files the page links are then read with the Bearer header and written in (images as `data:` URIs, stylesheets and scripts as inline blocks), within a budget that depends on where the page shows: the viewer and version screen use `ao render`'s limits (10 MiB per image, 25 MiB per page); a chat frame keeps 2 MiB images in 6 MiB; a gallery card keeps 300 KiB images in 2 MiB, so a full-size screenshot stays out of a card's preview. An image over the budget is not downloaded when its size is declared. The result loads from memory with no base URL. Two reasons. First, since #7077 preview pages on the API host carry `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms`, so the page has an opaque origin, and Android's Chromium withholds the `SameSite=Lax` `ao_conn` cookie from its own requests, so every image, stylesheet and script failed there. Second, an image an agent links by its absolute path into the artifact folder (which `ao render` accepts) never loads from a URL, on any platform. The inlined page needs no cookie and has no origin to reach the daemon from, so the sandbox is not loosened. Script elements are set aside while the markup passes run, so code that mentions `src=` or `srcset` is never rewritten, and linked files load side by side, four at a time, one load per file. The app's theme is written into the bootstrap's `#ao-theme` style before the page loads, so it never paints in the system theme first. References that are missing, too large or outside the folder stay as written; if inlining fails, the page loads from its URL as before. The viewer posts the app's live theme into the page, as a chat frame does; the chat frame inlines only while it is in view. - **Images:** an artifact image's source carries the auth header as an array source on Android (React Native 0.86 forwards headers only that way); the viewer had relied on a cookie left by an earlier request. A markdown artifact's `![alt](path)` lines resolve against its folder, or by an absolute path into it as a page's do, and carry the image's listed time so a regenerated image reloads; `parseBlocks` reads relative image lines only when asked, so chat replies keep to web images. - **Card previews** follow the desktop's `ArtifactThumbnail` (`lib/ArtifactThumbnail.tsx`, `lib/artifactThumbnailModel.ts`). An HTML card loads the same inlined, themed page as the viewer into a WebView laid out at 420 points (a phone page) and scaled down to the card as a view, the way the desktop scales a 1000×625 iframe. A CSS `zoom` instead left the page's window at the card's width, so a canvas sized from `innerWidth` filled only a corner. A markdown card renders the first 4,000 characters through `ChatMarkdown` at twice the card's width, drawn at half size, with its relative images; text shows its opening lines. Text over 256 KB keeps the icon. Previews load only while the card is on screen (`onViewableItemsChanged`), and an off-screen card releases its WebView; pages and text are cached per file version (`lib/artifactPageCache.ts`, `cachedThumbnailText`); the page cache holds at most 12 pages and 24M characters in total, oldest dropped first. Only a completed read is kept: a failed one is tried again on the next mount, and pulling to refresh retries a card that fell back to its icon. A page whose version the phone cannot know (a page reported in an orchestrator's thread, whose files it has no list of, or a file the session does not list) is read afresh on every mount rather than shared, so a rewrite always shows. A preview takes no touches, so tap and long-press still reach the card. While a preview loads the card shows a plain tile (its kind icon only if the preview fails), and a pressed card dims under a veil rather than by opacity: an Android WebView does not follow its parent's opacity and can blank for a frame when it changes. **Not fixed here:** the daemon-side cookie cause still affects the mobile Preview screen on Android, which loads workspace pages through the same route and cookie. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) and `npm test` in `packages/mobile`: 256 files, 2656 tests pass. - Android emulator (debug build, this branch's JS), against the real daemon through a read-only proxy that forwards reads and stubs every write: gallery, markdown/PNG/HTML viewers, long-press menu, Copy (raw read), Delete (request sent, card removed, file untouched), and the terminal header button on a session shown in terminal mode. - Version history on the Android emulator, this branch's JS, against the real daemon through a read-only proxy. Every real artifact had a single version, so the proxy served a three-version history for one markdown file, built from its real content, and answered restore by adding a version, as the daemon does. Checked: header button, both menus, the sheet (labels, Current, restore note, agent and user marks), version screen, restore returning to the file, the new version appearing in History, and Current from the gallery opening the live file. `sync` on real sessions was answered with the read-only list, so nothing was recorded or restored on the real daemon. - Ask the agent and chat frames on the Android emulator (debug build of this branch), through the same read-only proxy, which captured each `/send` instead of delivering it. Checked: Add to chat in markdown and code artifacts; the composer on selected text and on a whole HTML file; Send now and queue-then-send from the tray, each producing the desktop's message (`Location: Selected text` with the quote, or `Entire file`); and a real reported HTML artifact (session 237's) drawn in its turn, opening the viewer on tap. - Images on the Android emulator (debug build of this branch), through the read-only proxy, on a fresh emulator with no stored cookies: gallery thumbnails; a markdown artifact linking two screenshots by relative path (served by the proxy, since no real artifact does); session 252's `iphone-duo.html` with all its relative images (no 401s, where every one failed before); session 237's chat frame with images linked by absolute path. - iOS simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5), a Release build of this branch through the same read-only proxy, every feature: the menu row and count, gallery with thumbnails, the native action sheet (Open, Ask the agent, Copy, Version history, Delete), markdown with relative images, Add to chat in markdown and code (each message checked), Ask the agent on a whole file queued to the review and sent from the tray, history, a version, restore, the image viewer, HTML pages and the chat frame, Copy to the clipboard, Delete, and the terminal header. Found and fixed on iOS: absolute-path images in HTML artifacts (broken before), the unthemed serif pages, and the terminal header's Artifacts button not reading as a button. title: ci: fail PRs that make a breaking change to the cloud contract
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +49 -0 (CI workflow)

## What

Adds a `Cloud contract compatibility` workflow. On any PR that changes `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, it runs `oasdiff breaking` against the base branch's copy and fails if the change removes or narrows anything. If a breaking change is intended and coordinated with the control plane, the `contract-breaking-change` label lets it through, with a warning.

## Why

The control plane is moving to a separate private repository (draft #7352), so `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` becomes the only interface between the public apps (desktop, mobile, `@aoagents/cloud-client`) and a service that is developed and deployed on its own schedule. An older desktop has to keep working against a newer control plane and the other way round, so contract changes need to stay additive. This is the "contract breaking-change gate" step of the split plan. It is useful before the split too.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A PR can drop or narrow a contract route or field unnoticed | `oasdiff` fails the PR, for example: `error [api-path-removed-without-deprecation] in API GET /api/cloud/v1/orgs/{orgId}/agents` |
| (n/a) | An additive change passes: "No breaking changes to report, but the specs are different." |

## How

- `oasdiff` v1.34.1 is installed with `go install` and pinned. It is not pulled from Docker Hub, which has been unreliable from our runners and this network.
- The base copy comes from `git show origin/$BASE_REF:contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`.
- `--fail-on ERR`, so warnings such as deprecations don't fail the PR.

## Testing

Local runs of `oasdiff breaking` against the current contract:

- same file: exit 0, "No changes detected";
- with an added route: exit 0;
- with `GET /orgs/{orgId}/agents` removed: exit 1, with the error above.

This PR touches the workflow file, so the workflow runs on itself and passes, because the contract is unchanged.

title: feat(mobile): browse and restore an artifact's version history
body: Code changes: +460 -10\ Tests: +74 -5\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Stacked on #7355 (the artifacts gallery); review that first. This PR adds version history to mobile artifacts, matching the desktop viewer's History menu. - **Where:** a clock button in the artifact viewer's header, and **Version history** in the long-press and ⋯ menus. Text artifacts only (markdown, code, HTML): the daemon reads versions back as text, so images and other media have none, as on desktop. - **History sheet:** every kept version, newest first, the first marked **Current**. Each row has a time ("Today, 8:31 PM", "Yesterday, …", "Oct 11, …"), "Restored from …" for a restore, and who wrote it: the agent's logo, or a person icon for a save or restore made in the app. - **Version screen:** tapping a version opens it read-only, with a "Viewing the version from …" banner, a notice when it is cut to its first 256 KiB, and **Back to current** / **Restore this version**. Markdown renders; anything else, HTML included, shows as source, as on desktop. - **Restore** rewrites the file and returns to it. The daemon keeps the replaced content as a version first, so a restore can itself be undone from History. ## Why Agents rewrite artifacts as they go, and the daemon already keeps up to 50 versions of each. On the phone there was no way to see an earlier version or roll back a bad rewrite. ## Before / After Android emulator, same session and data. Before is #7355's branch. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | No version history on mobile | | | No version history on mobile | | | No version history on mobile | | ## How - **No backend changes.** Uses the existing `GET /artifact-versions`, `POST /artifact-versions/sync`, `GET /artifact-versions/{version}` and `POST /artifact-versions/restore`. - **Opening is instant:** the sheet shows the stored list from `GET`, then replaces it with the `sync` result. Sync records any edit the daemon's 30-second observer has not picked up, but waits up to two seconds for the file to settle, so showing only its answer meant a spinner every time. The desktop menu does the same. - **Time labels are written out** rather than built with `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, which Hermes does not have. Times and dates still use the device locale. - Opened from a gallery card, **Current** opens the live file; from the viewer, it just closes the sheet. - Parsing, time labels, restore notes and authorship live in `lib/artifactVersions.ts`, with unit tests. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) and `npm test` in `packages/mobile`: 248 files, 2571 tests pass. - Android emulator, this branch's JS, against the real daemon through a read-only proxy. Every real artifact had a single version, so the proxy served a three-version history for one markdown file, built from its real content, and answered restore by adding a version, as the daemon does. Checked: header button, both menus, the sheet (labels, Current, restore note, agent and user marks), version screen, restore returning to the file, the new version appearing in History, and Current from the gallery opening the live file. `sync` on real sessions was answered with the read-only list, so nothing was recorded or restored on the real daemon. - Not covered: iOS (this worktree's iOS build predates two native modules on `main`; Phase 1 was checked on iOS before the rebase), a physical device, a truncated (256 KiB+) version. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Orchestrator never starts when a leftover folder sits at the project's orchestrator worktree path
body:
Starting an orchestrator for one project fails every time. The session is created, but its `provisionState` is `failed`, the agent never starts, and every message sent to it fails. A worktree folder from that project's earlier orchestrator (created in August) is still on disk at the orchestrator worktree path, but git no longer tracks it as a worktree.

Expected: AO reuses or clears the leftover folder (or tells the user how to), and the orchestrator starts.

Seen on macOS 26.5.1, on both attempts (2 of 2). Found while testing the Orchestrator Bot skills (`integrations/grok-bot`).

---

### Agent-collected evidence

**Environment:** local daemon (pid 58927, started 2026-10-27T06:17Z) run by `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator 2.app`. That app now reports `0.14.7-nightly.202610271258`; the exact daemon build at collection time wasn't recorded. Source references are to `main` at `0b7d96c67b`.

**Repro** (2026-10-27, about 14:23 UTC):

```
POST /api/v1/sessions {"projectId":"todo-app","kind":"orchestrator","mode":"chat","displayName":"Orchestrator"}
→ todo-app-11 created; provisionState=failed; conversation controller "stopped", 0 turns

POST /api/v1/sessions {... same, plus "prompt": "..."}
→ todo-app-12 created; provisionState=failed, provisionError:
spawn todo-app-12: workspace: gitworktree: worktree add existing branch "ao/todo-app-orchestrator":
git -C ~/Development/todo-app worktree add ~/.ao/data/worktrees/todo-app/orchestrator/todo-app-orchestrator ao/todo-app-orchestrator:
exit status 128: Preparing worktree (checking out 'ao/todo-app-orchestrator')
fatal: '~/.ao/data/worktrees/todo-app/orchestrator/todo-app-orchestrator' already exists
```

**State of the leftover folder** (read-only, 2026-10-27T20:40Z):

```
$ ls -ld ~/.ao/data/worktrees/todo-app/orchestrator/todo-app-orchestrator
drwxr-xr-x@ 17 <user> staff 544 Aug 16 13:27 …/todo-app-orchestrator
$ git -C ~/Development/todo-app worktree list
~/Development/todo-app  a2bdc64 [main]                # the folder is not listed
$ git -C ~/.ao/data/worktrees/todo-app/orchestrator/todo-app-orchestrator rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree
fatal: not a git repository: ~/Development/todo-app/.git/worktrees/todo-app-orchestrator
```

The folder's `.git` file points to a worktree admin entry that no longer exists (pruned), so `git worktree add` refuses the path.

**What this supports (hypothesis):** the orchestrator worktree path is fixed per project, so one leftover folder blocks every later orchestrator for that project: `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:2182`:

```go
path = filepath.Join(w.managedRoot, string(cfg.ProjectID), "orchestrator", prefix+"-orchestrator")
```

How the folder came to outlive its registration isn't known (it dates from August).

**Related:** #6918 (closed) is the inverse case: a stale *registration* blocked the branch (`BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE`). Here the *folder* survives without a registration. The failed session's later `send` behavior is filed separately.

**Duplicate search:** `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`, open and closed issues, for "worktree add already exists orchestrator", "provisionState failed orchestrator", "git worktree add", "worktree directory already exists", "stale orchestrator worktree". Considered #6918, #3220, #4350, #4590; none matches this case. Daemon logs weren't available (the packaged app doesn't persist daemon stderr).

title: `POST /sessions/{id}/send` returns a bare 500 when the agent controller isn't running
body:
Sending a message to a session whose agent controller isn't running fails with a bare `500 Internal server error`. For the same session, `steer-or-send` returns a clear `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY` ("the agent controller for this session is not running").

Expected: `send` returns that same clear error, so the CLI, scripts and bots can tell the user to resume or reopen the agent instead of showing an internal error.

Seen on macOS 26.5.1, on every attempt. Found while testing the Orchestrator Bot skills (`integrations/grok-bot`), which send through this route.

---

### Agent-collected evidence

**Environment:** local daemon (pid 58927, started 2026-10-27T06:17Z) run by `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator 2.app`. That app now reports `0.14.7-nightly.202610271258`; the exact daemon build at collection time wasn't recorded. Collected 2026-10-27, about 14:25 UTC.

**Session:** `todo-app-11`, a chat orchestrator whose provisioning failed (see #7358). `GET /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/conversation` showed `"controller": "stopped"` and 0 turns; the session's activity state was `idle`.

**Same session, two routes:**

```
POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/send
{"message":"[via Grok Bot #manual] ...","userAuthored":true}
→ HTTP 500
{"error":"internal","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal server error","requestId":"<host>/19r8TmJzZS-043089","reporting_owner":"http"}

POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/conversation/steer-or-send
{"text":"[via Grok Bot #manual2] ...","clientMessageId":"<uuid>"}
→ HTTP 409
{"error":"conflict","code":"CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY","message":"the agent controller for this session is not running","requestId":"<host>/19r8TmJzZS-043117"}
```

`POST /api/v1/sessions/todo-app-11/resume-agent` then returned `200 {"ok":true,"resumeMode":"saved_prompt"}`, but the controller stayed `stopped` and `send` kept returning 500. A second orchestrator in the same state (`todo-app-12`) gave the same 500 on two more `send` attempts.

**Limits:** shown only for a controller that never started because provisioning failed; not checked for a controller that stopped after running. Daemon logs weren't available (the packaged app doesn't persist daemon stderr), so the 500's underlying error isn't known.

**Related, not the same:** #5922 and #5513 (Resume agent returns "Internal server error"), #6639 (send/resume fail after daemon restart on Windows). Those are about resuming; this is the error `send` returns.

**Duplicate search:** `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`, open and closed issues, for "send 500 INTERNAL_ERROR", "CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY", "controller stopped send". Considered #5922, #5513, #6639, #6110, #6064; none reports `send` returning 500 where `steer-or-send` returns 409.

title: fix(sessions): reject spawn prompts with unexpanded shell variables
body:
Code changes: +33 -0\
Tests: +57 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

`POST /api/v1/sessions` now rejects a spawn prompt that still contains an unexpanded shell variable. It returns
400 `PROMPT_UNEXPANDED_VARIABLE`, and the message names the token it found.

## Why

The spawn handler checks only the prompt's length, and `ao spawn` passes the prompt through verbatim. When the
caller does not expand a variable (single quotes, a shell such as `cmd.exe` that does not expand `$`, a prompt built
from a template or a JSON file), a prompt like `Read $env:BRIEF` or `Work from ${TASK_FILE}` reaches the
agent as literal text. The agent then starts work from a placeholder instead of the real instructions, and nothing
tells the caller that anything went wrong.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/sessions` with `"prompt": "Read $env:BRIEF and start"` returns 201, and the agent receives the literal text `$env:BRIEF`. | The same request returns 400 with code `PROMPT_UNEXPANDED_VARIABLE` and the message `Prompt contains $env:BRIEF, which looks like a shell variable that was never expanded; expand it before spawning, or put it in a fenced code block`. No session is spawned. |
| `ao spawn` with the same prompt starts a session. | `ao spawn` prints the server error as it does for any other API error: `<message> (PROMPT_UNEXPANDED_VARIABLE) [request <id>]`. |

## How

The check sits in the spawn handler, right after the existing prompt-length check. It flags three shapes:

- `$env:NAME`: PowerShell environment variables. The `env:` prefix is matched case-insensitively, as PowerShell does.
- `${NAME}`: POSIX braced form.
- `$NAME`: POSIX bare form.

For the braced and bare forms, NAME must be all caps, as environment variables are by convention: `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`,
with at least one letter.

These pass through unchanged:

- prices such as `$5` and `$1.50`, because a name cannot start with a digit;
- a `$` on its own;
- lower-case names such as `$foo`, which are common in code samples;
- PowerShell's pipeline variable `$_`, because it has no letter.

**Rule for code blocks.** Lines inside a fenced code block (opened by a line starting with ```` ``` ```` or `~~~`)
are exempt. That way a prompt can still quote a shell or PowerShell script that uses `$HOME`, `${TASK_FILE}` or
`$env:USERPROFILE`. An unclosed fence exempts everything after it. Inline code spans (single backticks) are **not**
exempt: an inline `` `$TASK_FILE` `` is the shape an unexpanded variable usually takes in a one-line prompt. Someone
who really means to send the literal text can put it in a fenced block, and the error message says so.

The CLI needs no change: it already renders API errors as `message (CODE) [request id]`.

Reviewer focus: whether the all-caps rule is the right balance. It catches the common case (environment variables)
and leaves prose and lower-case code alone. It will still reject an all-caps `$WORD` written on purpose outside a
fence.

## Testing

New table tests in `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions_test.go`:

- `TestSessionsAPI_SpawnRejectsUnexpandedShellVariable`: `$env:BRIEF`, `${TASK_FILE}`, `$TASK_BRIEF`, and a
  variable that comes after a closed fenced block. Each returns 400 `PROMPT_UNEXPANDED_VARIABLE`, the body names the
  token, and nothing is spawned.
- `TestSessionsAPI_SpawnAcceptsPromptsWithoutShellVariables`: plain text, `$5` and `$1.50`, a lone `$`, `$foo` and
  `$bar`, `$_`, a ```` ```sh ```` block with `${TASK_FILE}`, `$HOME` and `$env:USERPROFILE`, and a `~~~` block with
  `$PATH`. Each returns 201 with the prompt unchanged.

Local CI, on a Windows x64 host with Go 1.27.1 (no C compiler, so every step ran without `-race`):

- `gofmt -l` (backend and cloud), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`: clean.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 with `GOOS=linux`: 0 issues.
- sqlc drift and API schema drift (`npm run sqlc`, `npm run api:spec` plus `openapi-typescript@7.4.4`): no diff.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/httpd/...`:
  - `httpd`, `apispec`, `specgen` and `envelope` pass.
  - In `controllers`, the new tests pass. The same four existing tests fail at this commit and at its parent. All
    four depend on the host: Windows file-vs-directory status, file locking, symlink privilege and file URLs.
- Full `go test ./...`: 152 packages pass. Every package that fails also fails at the parent commit, with the same
  tests apart from timing flakes. None of them import the changed package.
- The Windows CI job's test steps: same results at this commit and its parent, apart from timing-sensitive flakes.
- `cloud`: `GOOS=linux go build` and `go vet` pass.

Not run locally:

- `-race` (needs cgo);
- the Linux test suites as such;
- the `cloud` tests and its docker builds;
- the macOS frontend helper jobs;
- the frontend Ubuntu jobs. No frontend file changed, and the schema drift check is clean.

These need the CI run.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(search): search every past session from Cmd+K and ao search
body:
Code changes: +8734 -69\
Tests: +8450 -3\
Others: +653 -9 (generated sqlc, OpenAPI and `schema.ts`, 9 locale catalogs, `go.sum`)

Three commits: the index (`search.db`, readers, query language), the API, daemon wiring and `ao search`, and the desktop (Cmd+K, opening at the match).

## What

Search across every past AO session, live, hibernated or terminated, from two places:

- **Cmd+K.** Type two or more characters and matching past sessions appear above the commands.
  - One row per session, showing its best-matching message with the typed words marked, plus "you · 7 matches · project · agent".
  - Enter opens the session scrolled to that message; ⌘↵ copies its resume command.
  - With nothing typed, recent sessions sit below the commands.
- **`ao search`.** For people and agents, as a table or `--json`, with flags that mirror the query operators, `--index-status`, and `--reindex` to rebuild the index.

**Opening a result** scrolls the Chat transcript to the message and marks the matched word. When the match is in a user or assistant message, it also opens `main`'s find in chat (#7684) on that word, starting at that message, so Enter and Shift+Enter step through its other occurrences across the whole history. Both wait until the session's conversation has loaded. A long prompt that `main` folds behind Show more opens when the match is below its fold.

## Why

There was no way to find something said in a past session. Orca ships the closest equivalent, Agent Session Search, with an `orca search` CLI. Main's palette "Messages" search (#7185) covers AO Chat message text only: not tool or command output, file changes, reviewer chats, or terminal sessions' own transcripts.

## Before / After

| Before (`main`) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- |
| Cmd+K, `flaky login`: only AO Chat messages whose text contains the words, one row per message | One row per session at its best match, across messages, tool calls and output, file changes and terminal transcripts, with a match count |
| No way to search past sessions by project, agent or date | Type `project:`, `harness:`, `after:`/`before:` or `sort:recent` in ⌘K or `ao search` |
| A Messages row opens that one message | It opens at the session's best message, with find in chat open on the matched word |
| `ao search` does not exist | `ao search "flaky login" --json` returns session id, best message id, snippet and match count |

Recorded in the real desktop app (this branch, on a fenced copy of this Mac's data, 13 Nov): Cmd+K recents, a typed search with marked snippets and match counts, Enter opening the session at the matched reply with find in chat on 14/16, stepping to 16/16, and a command-output match opening its folded row.

## How

- **Index.** SQLite FTS5 in its own database file, `search.db` beside `ao.db` (`storage/sqlite/search_db.go`). SQLite allows one writer per file, so index writes never make chat or session writes wait.
  - Search queries run on their own small reader pool, whose connections attach `search.db` so queries still join documents to sessions. The app's other readers never attach it.
  - **Search is optional.** If `search.db` can't be opened (permissions, a lock, a full disk), the daemon still starts and everything else works; search answers `503 SESSION_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE`, `--index-status` says `unavailable`, and ⌘K says so instead of showing an empty result.
  - **`ao search --reindex`** (`POST /api/v1/search/reindex`) empties the index in place and rebuilds it in the background, without a restart; index status says `backfilling` until it ends. Repeated requests collapse into one rebuild.
  - **`AO_SESSION_SEARCH=off`** makes the daemon skip search entirely, without opening `search.db`: a support lever, not a user setting.
  - Its schema is versioned with `user_version` and tied to the `ao.db` it indexes; a mismatch clears it and the indexer rebuilds. A file SQLite reports as corrupt or not a database is removed and rebuilt the same way, so a damaged index never keeps the daemon from starting.
  - `ao.db` keeps only `session_search_deleted` and the owner token. A trigger on `sessions` records a deleted session's id (one row); search excludes it at once and the next sweep removes its documents.
  - A pass writes only documents whose fingerprint changed, and reads a conversation again only when its stamp moved.
  - A backfill starts by comparing the sessions the index holds with the `sessions` table and recording any the database does not have as deleted. That covers an older backup of `ao.db` restored beside a newer index, which keeps the same token.
  - The ranking query leaves the documents of deleted sessions out before it keeps its best 2,000 candidates, so documents waiting for the sweep can't crowd a live match out of them.
  - A backfill on start, then a sweep every 30 s. Transcripts are prepared on up to three goroutines and written in order by one.
  - Read-only toward session data.
- **What is indexed** (`sessionsearch/coverage.go`, the same for every source, following Orca):
  - user and assistant messages, plans, session names, prompts, branches and file paths;
  - a tool call as `name: argument`, the argument being the first of `command`, `cmd`, `file_path`, `path`, `pattern`, `query`, `description`, up to 2,000 characters;
  - a tool's output, its first 3,072 characters;
  - not reasoning, edit or write contents, or diffs;
  - a message longer than 8 KiB as up to 8 chunks. Each chunk repeats the last 256 bytes of the one before it, so a quoted phrase across a chunk break is still found.
- **Sources.** AO Chat conversations of every agent (including reviewer chats), and the transcripts of Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode v1/v2 terminal sessions. Other agents' sessions are found by name and prompt.
- **Ranking.**
  - BM25 over an unstemmed index; each typed word also matches its English stem (Snowball/Porter2, `kljensen/snowball`) as a prefix, ranked below the word as typed.
  - Identifiers are split (`handleSubmit` → `submit`).
  - Field weights: name > your words > paths > replies > tool output.
  - A session scores as its best match plus a quarter of its next five, so a long session can't win on volume alone.
  - Sessions whose name holds every typed word come first.
- **Find in chat.** A result hands `ChatWorkspace` a find request, and `useChatFind.openWith` (added to `main`'s hook) opens find already searching, anchored at the result's message. The surface holds the match until the chat is rendering the daemon's conversation, not the placeholder an orchestrator shows first, and drops the request once the chat applied it. This PR has no find bar of its own.
- **Cmd+K** is built on the redesigned palette: rows render through `PaletteRow`, "Copy resume command" is ⌘↵, and a Messages row for a session the search group already lists is not repeated.

**Reviewers might focus on:**
- `service/sessionsearch/service.go` and `native.go`: incremental indexing, the parallel preparation, the transcript readers.
- `storage/sqlite/search_db.go` and `store/session_search_store.go`: the separate file and the ranking SQL.
- `CommandPalette.tsx`; `useChatFind.tsx` (`openWith`) and `SessionChatSurface.tsx` for opening find.
- Search adds one migration to `ao.db`, `20261113173435236_session_search.sql`: the deleted-session table, its trigger and the owner token. The index's own schema is in `search_db.go`. A dev database that ran an earlier build of this branch needs a fresh copy.

**Intentional omissions:**
- **Session delete is `main`'s.** An earlier head of this PR also changed how a session is deleted; that is removed, so deletes are exactly what `main` has (#7928). The only thing this PR adds to a delete is the trigger that records the deleted id for search.
- **No semantic search.** A word, or a form of it, must appear.
- **Words only in reasoning, edits or long output past 3,072 characters are not found.** Same as Orca; chosen for index size and build time.
- **A quoted phrase with more than about 256 bytes before a chunk break of a long message is missed**; shorter ones across a break are found.
- **Find steps through the matched word, not the whole query.** For `flaky login` it opens on the word the best message marked first. The row's "7 matches" counts matching messages, tool output included; find counts one word's occurrences in message text, so the numbers can differ.
- **A match in tool or command output, a path or the name opens without find**, because find in chat searches message text only and would say "No results".
- **Terminal sessions** open without find in chat; the terminal has its own (Cmd+F).
- **Only this machine.** Searching every saved AO machine is #7378.

## Evidence

Measured on 9 Nov on `b581900603` (on `main` `d25418c4a2`), on this 8 GB MacBook Air. This head is that branch rebased onto `main` `e5368cf4e6`, plus the switch to `main`'s find in chat, renumbered migrations, and the four review fixes of 10 Nov (the chunk overlap for long messages among them). The public-dataset benchmark was last run after those fixes (10 Nov, on `3153e82ed8`) with the same numbers; its harness has since been removed from this PR (see below). The last of those fixes changes the ranking query: on a synthetic 60,000-document index a broad search with nothing deleted takes 31 ms against 34 ms before it. The index size and build time were not remeasured; the overlap adds at most 320 bytes per chunk after the first, for messages over 8 KiB only.

**Search quality.**

| Suite | This branch | Orca, same datasets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LongMemEval-S, 470 questions | R@1 88.3, R@5 96.6, R@10 98.1 | R@1 86.8 |
| LoCoMo, 1,536 questions | R@1 62.6, R@5 87.8, R@10 94.1 | R@1 61.6 |
| Agentic, 43 searches written from AO sessions | R@1 93.0, R@5 95.3 | R@1 81.4 |
| Real transcripts, 321 rare-word searches | R@1 72.0 | R@1 71.0 |

- The first three rows were measured with a benchmark harness that is no longer in this PR, so they can't be reproduced from this branch. It was a measurement tool, not part of the feature. The public-dataset suites are in commit `249195792c`; the 43-search suite, last run at R@1 93.0, is in `9cc7e040d2`.
- What still guards ranking in this PR: the 13-case ranking test (`benchmark_test.go`) and the regression tests for each ranking bug found.
- The options those measurements switched (a hard order by kind, an all-words-first tier, strict AND, the other typo rules) are gone too, so the query and the parser hold only the shipped behaviour. The last commit with them is `8cab2470a4`.
- Orca's numbers are its own engine, run unmodified from a full checkout and graded by the same scorer.
- The real-transcript suite was built to probe content Orca does not index. Messages, replies, short output and long messages all score as before. Words found only in reasoning, edit contents or output past 3,072 characters are now missed, as in Orca.

**End to end on a real daemon.** This branch's `ao daemon` on a fenced copy of this Mac's archive (63 sessions, 30,144 documents, with copies of its Claude, Codex and OpenCode transcripts), 226 graded searches over HTTP:
- 186 pass (right session in the top 3), 2 soft (top 8), 38 fail.
- 35 of the failures are cases whose data is gone: since they were written, main's retention deleted the sessions 30 of them look for, 4 depend on those or on a session that has since been terminated, and 1 is pinned to this Mac's old hostname.
- Of the 191 cases that still apply: 186 pass, 2 soft, and 3 fail by design (the word is only in reasoning, or past 3,072 characters of a command's output).
- Warm Cmd+K latency over 127 queries: p50 55 ms, p95 214 ms. 115 of 118 top results opened on their message; 3 had none and opened the session.

**No app write waits for search.** A copy of the archive, with a tiny app write every 5 ms while search works:

| While search is… | Worst app-write wait |
| --- | --- |
| Building the whole index (30,143 documents) | 10.7 ms |
| Clearing and rebuilding it | 1.5 ms (mean 0.13 ms) |
| Re-indexing an edit, or an idle sweep | under 6 ms |

`TestAppWritesAndSearchesDoNotWaitForTheIndexWriter` holds the index's write lock and checks that an app write and a search both go through.

**Index cost.** The commit before Orca's coverage and the parallel build (`8ba46b336a`) against this head, alternated on the 126 real transcripts (667 MB) used for the Orca comparison:

| | Before | This head | Orca |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Index file | 49.7 MB | **18.1 MB** | 29 MB |
| Build, machine busy | 21–25 s | **9 s** | – |
| Build, machine idle (same commits, earlier today) | 8.3 s | **3.1 s** | 2.9 s |
| Peak memory | 84–85 MB | **75–79 MB** | 229 MB |
| Search p50, machine busy | 5.6 ms | 4.3–4.7 ms | – |

## Testing

- **Backend:** `go build ./...`; golangci-lint v2.14.0 on every Go package this PR touches, 0 issues. `go test` on `cli`, `daemon`, `domain`, `httpd`, `httpd/apispec/...`, `httpd/controllers`, `sessionsearch`, `storage/sqlite`, `searchtext`, `store` and `telemetrymeta`: all pass. Each of the three commits builds on its own.
- **Generated code:** the OpenAPI spec and `schema.ts` regenerate with no diff.
- **Frontend:** `typecheck` clean; every test file this PR adds or changes plus the i18n coverage check pass. Five tests failed once while this Mac's load average was 44–63 and pass on rerun; none are in files this PR changes except `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`'s "scroll away from a find result", which is `main`'s and passes alone.
- **A damaged `search.db`** (overwritten with garbage) is rebuilt on open; the test fails without the fix with "file is not a database (26)".
- **Search is optional (13 Nov).** New tests: the store opens and app reads and writes work when `search.db` can't be opened, app reads keep working when it breaks after start, `AO_SESSION_SEARCH=off` never creates it, and reindex rebuilds in place. The first two fail on the previous wiring ("unable to open database file", "attach session search database").
- **On a real daemon** (this branch, fenced copy of this Mac's data, 69 sessions): `ao search --reindex` rebuilt all 36,288 documents in 25 s with identical results for the same query; with a directory in place of `search.db` the daemon started, served all 69 sessions and its projects, and search and reindex answered `SESSION_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE`.
- **Real desktop app:** run from this branch on a fenced copy of this Mac's data and recorded (see above). The dev build needed `better-sqlite3` rebuilt with the SDK's libc++ headers.

**Not verified here:**
- **The full Vitest suite and the renderer Playwright gate** were not rerun locally; CI runs both.
- **`go test -race`** on `store` was not rerun locally (12 minutes here); CI's `go / storage-race` runs it.

**CI on this head:** green on `3e2ea965f2`, on `main` `72c1d3c44d` (19 checks pass, 9 skipped).

title: [Feature]: Add read-only Linear issue intake
body:
### Problem

I plan and track my work in Linear. I would like AO to pick up assignee-scoped Linear issues through the same opt-in intake it offers for GitHub and GitLab. Linear is currently listed as unsupported.

### Proposed direction

A Linear adapter at `backend/internal/adapters/tracker/linear` implementing `ports.Tracker` and mapping issues to `domain.Issue`, registered as a `trackermulti.NamedTracker` in `backend/internal/daemon/tracker_wiring.go`. It would also need a Linear `domain.TrackerProvider`, provider validation in `TrackerIntakeConfig.Validate` and `ao spawn --tracker-provider`, and an explicit Linear team or project scope per AO project, since there is no repo URL to infer it from.

Scope and safeguards for v1:
- Same project opt-in, daemon-wide gate and required assignee rule as today. Read-only: no comments, transitions or sync.
- A dedicated read-only Linear key held by the daemon, kept out of project config, worker environments and logs.
- A fixed official API origin; issue content never selects an endpoint.
- Issue title and body handled as untrusted input, the same as GitHub intake.
- Any spawn limits from #2344 apply once they land.

I know intake is not a current focus. I am offering to build and maintain the adapter if this shape is welcome.

### Alternatives considered

I could mirror Linear issues into GitHub or start workers by hand. Both add a separate step and a second source of truth.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: [Feature]: Optional external selector for worker and reviewer agents
body:
### Problem

I use coding agents from several vendors and pick the agent and model per task: by task type, by remaining plan usage, and with the reviewer from a different vendor than the author. Today an explicit `--agent` wins, otherwise the project role default applies (`effectiveHarness`). I can ask the orchestrator to follow my policy through `orchestratorRules`, but that depends on the agent complying, and reviewer selection follows its own chain.

#6947 asks for ordered pools with quota failover inside AO. This asks for a complementary hook so the policy can live outside AO; a pool could be one such policy.

### Proposed direction

An optional project setting naming a local executable that AO consults when no agent was chosen explicitly, before starting a worker and before selecting a reviewer. It receives JSON on stdin (task title and summary, project, ready harnesses, and the author's harness for reviews) and returns JSON with an agent and optional model and effort. Explicit choices always win. `effectiveHarness`, `RoleOverride` and the reviewer selection in `review.go` look like the boundaries.

Safeguards:
- Enabling or changing the executable needs explicit user approval, stored outside repository config.
- Run by absolute path with argv and JSON stdin, no shell, a minimal environment, a timeout that ends the process tree, and output size limits.
- Strict parsing of one JSON object; results checked against user-approved worker and reviewer allowlists, never widening permissions.
- On failure, stop with a clear error unless the user opted into falling back to the role default.
- Off by default.

### Alternatives considered

`orchestratorRules` asking the orchestrator to run my selector, which relies on prompt compliance and does not cover reviewers. A fixed project default, which cannot vary per task.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: new left sidebar design
body:
Code changes: +683 -95\
Tests: +407 -31\
Others: +17 -1 (i18n strings, DESIGN.md)

## What

A redesign of the left sidebar. It builds on #6952 (board-card hover preview on session rows), which this branch includes.

- **Status icons instead of dots.** A session row shows an icon only when there is something to read: a spinner while the agent works, red alert for needs input / CI failing / changes requested, review alerts, a pull-request icon when ready to merge, a merge icon when merged. Idle and exited rows show no icon.
- **Every session listed.** Projects and the Scratchpad list every non-archived session.
- **Repo avatars for projects (optional).** The folder icon becomes the GitHub (or GitLab/Bitbucket) owner avatar of the project's repo, as a 4px-radius squircle. Settings → Appearance → Project avatars turns it off (default on). Avatars are cached as data URLs in localStorage, so a launch paints them before any request, and refreshed once per launch. The folder shows until an avatar loads and stays for cloud, remote-host, avatar-less, or failed projects.
- **Scratchpad rows are plain.** Each row shows only the harness logo and the title, in the same 14px slot and inset as project avatars.

## Feature flag

The whole design sits behind **Settings → General → Advanced → New sidebar design**, shown only in Developer mode and **on by default**. Turning it off brings back the previous sidebar exactly: folder icons, plain status dots, no hover preview, no Scratchpad logo rows, no needs-you ordering. It also restores the yellow Validating colour and the board card's old loader and Merged tone, and hides the Repository avatars setting. The switch only takes effect in Developer mode, so turning Developer mode off always gives the new design.

- `newSidebarDesign` (`ao.newSidebarDesign`) in the UI store; read it through `selectNewSidebarDesign`.
- Colours: themes emit `--color-status-validating-new` and `-legacy`; `:root[data-legacy-status-colors]` picks the old one.
- Board: `SessionCardView` takes `legacyStatus`.

## Why

The coloured dot on every row carried little signal. Rows now flag only what needs reading, and projects are recognisable at a glance.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Every session row has a coloured status dot | Rows show an icon only for working or a board-column state; idle/exited rows have none |
| Projects show a folder icon | Projects show the repo owner's avatar (4px radius) |
| Scratchpad rows show status dot and age | Scratchpad rows show harness logo + title only |

Screenshots to be attached.

## How

- `repositoryOwnerAvatar` moved from `NewTaskDialog.tsx` to `lib/repository-avatar.ts` so the dialog and the sidebar share it. GitHub avatars now come from `avatars.githubusercontent.com/<owner>`, which serves the image with CORS; `github.com/<owner>.png` is an uncached redirect.
- `useProjectAvatars` reads project details through the existing `["project", id]` query key and keeps the image cache in `ao.projectAvatarCache`. The setting is `ao.projectAvatars` in the UI store.
- Scratchpad rows pass a `harnessOnly` flag down `SessionReorderList` → `SessionRow`, which drops the status icon, spinner, shimmer, and age.
- Frontend only; no daemon or API change.

## Testing

Exercised in the desktop app (`npm run dev`) against real local data.

Not run: local CI suites (frontend typecheck/vitest, Go). Sidebar tests may need updating for the icon changes.

title: fix(desktop): mouse-drag dismiss and fade-out for harness update notice

Code changes: +17 -10\

## What

Harness update notice cards: make the mouse drag swipe more reliable, and give the × button a quick fade-out instead of the swipe-away slide.

title: feat(ui): swipe or drag notification panel rows right to clear them
body:
Code changes: +95 -20\
Tests: +75 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Notification panel rows can now be cleared by swiping them right, either with two fingers on the trackpad or by dragging with the mouse. This is the same gesture the harness update notice already uses. The × button still works as before.

The shared `useSwipeToDismiss` hook also gets three fixes, which the harness update notice picks up too:

- A fast trackpad swipe dismisses as soon as the fingers lift, instead of after the momentum ends.
- The momentum left over from that swipe no longer swipes away the next row that moves under the pointer.
- The click that ends a mouse drag no longer also activates the element. In the panel, that click would otherwise open the row's session.
- `onDismiss` may resolve to `false` to say the dismissal failed. The element then comes back instead of staying hidden.

## Why

The harness update notice can be swiped away, but panel notifications could only be cleared one × at a time.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Panel rows clear only with the × button | Swiping a row right (trackpad or mouse drag) clears it; a short swipe springs back |
| After a fast trackpad swipe, the row waited for the momentum to end (up to about 1 s) before clearing | The row clears once the fingers lift |
| Mouse-dragging a row and letting go also clicked it | The click after a drag is ignored |
| A hard swipe's leftover momentum could swipe the next row too | One swipe clears one row |
| (new) | If the clear request fails, the swiped row comes back and the panel shows the error |

Recording to be attached by the author.

## How

- `NotificationItem` and `CloudNotificationItem` attach `useSwipeToDismiss` to their list item. Swiping calls the same `onClear` as the × button. `handleClear` and `handleClearCloud` now resolve to whether the clear worked, so a failed swipe-clear brings the row back. Swiping is turned off while that row's clear is disabled (the row is already clearing, or Clear all is running).
- The list gets `overflow-x-hidden`, so a row sliding out does not cause a sideways scrollbar.
- Rows get `select-none touch-pan-y`, as the harness card has, so a drag never selects text.
- Chromium reports the end of a trackpad scroll only after the momentum finishes. The hook now uses the same approach as `SwipeNavigation`: a fast swipe whose speed then drops 4 events in a row has been released. It only acts on this once the element is already past the dismiss point, where lifting would dismiss it anyway. That way, fingers that slow down early in a swipe are never mistaken for a release.
- After that early release, every swipeable element ignores the rest of the scroll (a module-level flag). The next scroll-phase signal clears it. Without native phases it clears after `IDLE_MS` without wheel events, and it also clears once no swipeable element is mounted.

## Testing

- The author tried it manually in the desktop dev app, using isolated data and seeded notifications: slow, hard and short trackpad swipes, mouse drags, and hard swipes on rows one after another.
- New tests: swiping a row clears it without opening its session; a failed swipe-clear brings the row back; the click ending a drag does not open the session; a hard swipe dismisses once it decays into momentum, and that momentum does not swipe the next card (`useSwipeToDismiss.test.tsx`).
- The tests were not run locally. CI is the check.

title: perf(frontend): use Pierre's WASM highlighter and skip layout for hidden file tabs
body:
Code changes: +24 -13\
Tests: +1 -1\
Others: +16 -77 (lockfile, package.json)

## What

Two changes to the desktop file and diff views:

1. Highlight files and diffs with `@pierre/diffs`' WASM engine (`preferredHighlighter: "highlights"`) instead of `shiki-js`. Bumps `@pierre/diffs` 1.4.1 → 1.6.1 (pinned). Adds `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` to the renderer CSP `script-src`.
2. Skip layout for inactive center file tabs with `[content-visibility:hidden]`, so a large file kept open in a background tab no longer slows tab switches and the rest of the app.

## Why

Large files and diffs take seconds to colour on the main thread with `shiki-js`, and a big file in a hidden tab made the whole app laggy because `visibility: hidden` still lays out the hidden DOM.

Inspired by pingdotgg/t3code#23178, which made the same engine switch.

## Before / After

Highlighting call only, run in a real Electron window with the CSP change, median of 7 runs, `github-dark` theme, real AO files and the last 40 commits touching `frontend/` (354 file diffs):

| Case | Before (`shiki-js`) | After (`highlights`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `browser-view-host.ts` (235 KB) | 1814 ms | 10 ms |
| `SessionView.test.tsx` (254 KB) | 3145 ms | 9 ms |
| `styles.css` (175 KB) | 161 ms | 6 ms |
| `ja.json` (191 KB) | 74 ms | 3 ms |
| 354 file diffs, total | 7915 ms | 133 ms |
| Slowest single diff | 399 ms | 9 ms |
| Switching tabs / resizing with a big file open in a hidden tab | laggy | smooth (manually verified) |
| `.prisma`, `.env`, ini, cobol, ansi files | coloured | plain text (known gap, see below) |

Screenshots and a short recording of the tab switch: to be attached by the author.

## How

- One constant, `PIERRE_HIGHLIGHTER`, in `diffs/pierreTheme.ts`, used by `AoDiffFile`, `ReadOnlyFileView`, `CloudDiffFile`, `WorkspaceReviewPane` and the preload hook. Pierre allows one engine per page, so every render site must pass the same value. The constant lives in `pierreTheme.ts` (not the hook) so components do not import the real `@pierre/diffs`, which would break test mocks that rely on the `diffs-container` element.
- Pierre 1.6 changed `CodeView`'s `renderAnnotation` to `(annotation, file, item)`. `WorkspaceReviewPane` and its test mock are updated.
- CSP: `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` allows WebAssembly compilation only, not JS `eval`. Highlights compiles its module synchronously from inline bytes; without the directive Electron throws `CompileError`. Reviewers should confirm this loosening is acceptable. The stale comment in `mermaid-diagram.ts` that said the CSP has no `wasm-unsafe-eval` is updated.
- Chat code blocks use AO's own Shiki core engine (`code-highlight-engine.ts`) and are unchanged.
- Hidden tabs: one Tailwind arbitrary property on the inactive file-tab wrapper. Scroll position is preserved across hide/show (checked in a standalone Electron page).

## Known trade-offs

- Highlights has no lexer for about 146 languages Shiki supports (prisma, ini, dotenv, cobol, ansi; upstream issue pierrecomputer/pierre#1228). Those files render as plain text.
- Colours differ from Shiki for some tokens, and Highlights emits about 45% more styled tokens on a large TS file (more DOM nodes).
- Files over `tokenizeMaxLength` (200,000 characters) still render as plain text. Raising it is left for a separate change.
- A file tab opened in the background and never shown has no layout while hidden, so its remembered scroll position may restore to 0 on first show.

## Testing

Manually in the real desktop app against scratch data (`AO_DATA_DIR`), local session with 9 modified files and sample files in py, sh, yaml, rs, go, css, json, md, Dockerfile, prisma and env:

- Large file open, diffs (split and unified), review pane scrolling, edit mode, line comments / Ask in chat, light and dark themes, coloured vs plain-text languages: all behave as expected.
- Switching file tabs and resizing with a large file in a hidden tab: no lag.
- DevTools console: no CSP or WebAssembly errors.

Also ran focused vitest files (CSP config, `ReadOnlyFileView`, `usePierreFileHighlight`, diffs and cloud-workspace components) and a frontend `tsc` before the last rebase onto `main`.

The full local CI suite was not run, as requested by the author. Relying on the PR's CI checks for that, and a packaged-build run has not been done.

title: fix(models): stop Claude listing "Opus 5.5" twice in the agent picker
body:
## Summary

Users report the Claude Code model picker sometimes lists **"Opus 5.5" twice**, the second right under the first. Two changes:

1. **`fix(modelcatalog)`: keep a configured context alias distinct.** When Claude Code's configured model is a context alias (`opus[1m]`) the catalog appends it labeled with its own ID, and `LabelClaudeAliasVersions` rebuilt the label from the family alone, so it read "Opus 5.5", a twin of the concrete `claude-opus-5-5` row. Its `[1m]` gives it its own slot in `splitClaudeModels`, which is exactly why it sat directly under the real one. It now reads **"Opus 5.5 (1M context)"**. The Claude catalog fingerprint is tagged so saved catalogs refresh once.
2. **`fix(chat)`: merge same-named Claude rows in the agent picker.** Claude can offer one model under several ids (for example AO's `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION` makes the adapter advertise both `opus` and `claude-opus-5-5`, both named "Opus 5.5"). The chat options are already deduped by name (#6588), but the agent picker's Model menu and search draw from other sources too (catalog, saved settings template). Before ordering, Claude rows with the same name in the same group are now merged: the chosen model's row stays and the others' ids become its aliases, so favourites still show as starred. Context variants and other agents are untouched; the ids sent to Claude are unchanged.

## Root-cause notes

- Anthropic's `/v1/models` returns one Opus 5.5; the doubling comes from AO's own sources.
- Couldn't reproduce on the reporting device (no configured model, clean catalog), so (2) is deliberately defensive: whatever source produces a same-named twin, the picker shows it once.
- Leaving `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION` alone on purpose: removing it risks the adapter rejecting concrete ids (#6399).

## Tests

- Go: `TestLabelClaudeAliasVersionsKeepsConfiguredContextVariant`.
- Vitest: `mergeSameNamedModels` (keeps the chosen id, keeps a row an alias already folded into, leaves distinct names / context variants / groups apart).
- Not run locally; relying on CI.

title: fix: unify the session pane tab strip
body:
Code changes: +322 -414\
Tests: +66 -41\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The tab strip at the top of the session page is now one list with one look. The session tab, reviewer, shell terminals and open files all use the same tab chrome (`TerminalTabFrame`), and the toolbar on the right sits on the same center line.

- One width rule: each tab fits its title between 64px and 140px, and long titles truncate with a tooltip. The session tab no longer has a fixed 148px width, and the reviewer tab no longer has dead space.
- One icon slot: every icon is 13px in a 16px slot, and every label starts at the same x. All labels use regular weight.
- One control slot: the session `⋮` menu and the shell/file close buttons replace the tab icon on hover or keyboard focus. The control takes clicks only while revealed (hover, focus, open menu, drag or pinned); a tap or a click on a faded slot selects the tab instead. The cloud interface-switch control is resized in the slot to match: a 16px box, 13px glyph and 28px hit area. They share one control (16px visual, 28px hit area, hover surface). An unsaved file's dot and a running interface switch stay visible.
- The session tab is part of the list in both the terminal and chat strips. It sits in the same scroll row and stays first; it is not draggable. Chat mode's hand-built reviewer and no-session tabs now use the shared tab.
- Keyboard focus: focus rings are off app-wide, so a focused tab shows the hover wash and its hidden control appears.
- The `+` new-terminal button now uses the same toolbar rules as its neighbours (7px radius, no-drag, press scale).
- Drag reorder: a dragged tab stays inside the reorderable group, so it never covers the session tab, `+` or the toolbar. It also keeps its hover look while dragged, even if the pointer leaves it vertically.
- Wheel scrolling works from every point over the tabs, including the 1px separators.

## Why

Feedback from the person who uses the app: the session tab and the other tabs at the top of the session page looked misaligned and random, and the session tab did not share characteristics with the other tabs. Testing the change live turned up three follow-up bugs, all fixed here:
- Dragging the last tab made it jump.
- Dragging a tab dropped its hover look when the pointer left it.
- Wheel scrolling did not work over the borders between tabs.

## Before / After

Same mock data, 1440x900. Captures are from `npm run dev:web` with a temporary mock patch (reviewer, 2 files, 2 shells) that is not committed. Before = `origin/main`, After = this branch. The screenshots are attached below.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Session tab fixed 148px (`Resolve revi…` + `⋮`), reviewer 148px with empty space, file tabs medium weight, mixed icon sizes (11/13/16px) | Every tab fits its title, 13px icons in one slot, one weight, labels and toolbar centered on y=24.5 |
| Shell active: close X at the left, the session `⋮` always shown at the right edge | Shell active: same strip, the session `⋮` hidden until hover, like the close buttons |
| Hover on a file: rounded close pill; shell close has no hover surface | One shared close/menu control with a hover surface |
| Keyboard focus on a tab: no visible change (rings are off app-wide) | The focused tab shows the hover wash and its close X |
| Dragging the last tab of a scrolled strip jumped from x=577 to 371 and stuck there | The tab follows the pointer and stops at the group edges; it keeps its hover look with the pointer off it |
| Wheel over a tab border did nothing (macOS window-drag region) | The strip scrolls from every point over the tabs |

## How

- `TerminalTabFrame` is the only tab chrome. It takes `icon`, `label`, an optional `action` that takes the icon's slot on hover/focus, and `actionPinned` to keep the action shown. Unused variants are removed: `appearance`, `actionLayout`, `actionPosition`, `trailingAction`, `contentClassName`, `data-terminal-role`, and the always-false `sessionTabActionWide`, which becomes `sessionTabActionPinned` while an interface switch runs.
- `DraggableWorkspaceTab` (exported from `CenterPane`, also used by `ChatWorkspace`) derives the dragged tab's `x` from the pointer and the group's current box, clamped to the group. It recomputes on every `x` write, every strip scroll and every commit. Framer's ref-based `dragConstraints` measured the group without the strip's scroll offset (the jump). Framer also rebases the drag offset a frame after Reorder's edge auto-scroll or a reorder moves the layout (the lag). It sets `data-dragging`, and the frame mirrors its hover classes with `in-data-dragging:`.
- The reveal-active-tab scroll is keyed on the set of tabs, not their order, so a reorder does not scroll the strip under the pointer.
- Scrolling has two causes:
  - On macOS the header is a `-webkit-app-region: drag` area where only buttons and tabs opt out. The tab row now opts out as a whole (`[-webkit-app-region:no-drag]`). The empty header space after the last tab stays draggable.
  - `useTabScrollEdges` attached its listeners only if the strip existed on the owner's first render. The strip mounts through the topbar portal later, so the hook now uses a callback ref.
- Tailwind only. `styles.css` and `tokens.css` only lose now-unused rules and tokens (`.session-tab-icon-floor*`, `--size-shell-tab-connected`, `--size-terminal-agent-icon`).

Review findings that were declined:
- The chat session tab now scrolls with the list instead of staying pinned outside it. This matches the terminal strip; it still stays first and is never dragged.
- The session `⋮` menu is hover/focus-revealed like the close buttons on purpose: the request was for the session tab to share the other tabs' traits.

## Testing

Per the requester's rule, local validation ran focused tests only. CI runs the full suites.

- Focused vitest (Node 24, `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`): `CenterPane`, `SessionFileTabs`, `ShellTerminalTab`, `chat/ChatWorkspace`, `chat/ChatWorkspaceRollback`, `SessionView`, `SessionView.remote`, `chat/SessionChatSurface`, `ShellTerminalsView`, `chat/IndependentSideChats`, `BrowserPanel`, `XtermTerminal`, `SessionInterfaceSwitch`, and the new `hooks/useTabScrollEdges.test.tsx`. All passed: 14 files, 963 tests.
- Focused e2e (`AO_E2E_PORT=5397`): `e2e/chat-interface-refusal.spec.ts` (@T0) passes. It now hovers the session tab before `Session actions`, as a pointer user does. `e2e/shell-terminal-tabs.spec.ts` hovers a shell tab before its close button. 2 untagged specs in that file still fail, as they do on `main`, and they are not in the CI smoke grep. One waits for `getByTestId("terminal")`, which does not exist on `main`. The other waits for a `New terminal` button on the project board.
- One `ChatWorkspace` test formats `258,400` as `2,58,400` on an en-IN host. That is the host locale; it passes with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`.
- Manual, `npm run dev:web` (terminal strip):
  - Measured every tab's geometry: same icon x, label x and center line.
  - Hit-tested 7 points per tab, including edges and separators: no dead zones.
  - Dragged the first, middle and last tabs in both directions, with and without overflow, scrolled to the start and to the end. A per-frame trace while auto-scrolling both ways keeps the tab within 0.5px of pointer minus grab offset, and it stops exactly at the group edges.
  - Simulated the macOS drag region: no drag points over the tabs.
  - Dispatched a wheel event at every 0.5px: every point over the tabs scrolls. The 5 points that do not are the center panel's rounded corner, which is outside the strip.

Gaps:
- The chat-mode strip cannot render in `dev:web` ("Electron preload is not available"). It shares the same components, but it was not checked visually.
- The `⋮` menu-open and switch-spinner states were not captured.
