title: feat: add more sidebar and board context menu actions
body:
Code changes: +420 -65\
Tests: +61 -2\
Others: +24 -0 (i18n catalogs)

## What

Adds right-click actions to the left sidebar and the kanban board:

- **Session rows** (project sessions, Pinned, Scratchpad) and **kanban session cards**: Open in <default editor>, Copy path, Rename, Pin/Unpin, Resume agent, Open PR #N, Copy PR URL, Copy branch name, Archive session.
- **Project rows**: New task, Open/Spawn orchestrator, Open dashboard, Copy path, Project settings, Remove project.
- **Scratchpad header**: Open a new agent, Archived sessions.

## Why

The sidebar's right-click menu only offered Rename for sessions and three items for projects. Common actions (open the worktree in an editor, copy the branch or PR link, pin, archive) needed the session open first or a hover target.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Session right-click menu: Rename only | Open in <default editor>, Copy path, Rename, Pin session, Copy branch name, Archive session (plus Resume agent / Open PR / Copy PR URL when they apply) |
| Kanban card: no right-click menu | Same session menu; Rename opens a small dialog because a card has no inline title editor |
| Project right-click menu: New task, Project settings, Remove project | Adds Open/Spawn orchestrator, Open dashboard, Copy path |
| Scratchpad header: no right-click menu | Open a new agent, Archived sessions |
| Right-clicking an open session menu also opened the project menu behind it | Right-clicks on menus, dropdowns and confirm dialogs stay there |

Screenshots to be attached.

## How

- The session items live in `SessionContextMenuItems.tsx`, shared by `Sidebar.tsx` and `SessionsBoardAdapters.tsx`. Radix mounts menu content only while open, so the editor handoff lookup runs on demand, not once per row. The editor row shows a disabled "Preparing workspace…" placeholder until the lookup resolves, so the menu does not jump.
- Open in editor and Copy path reuse the Electron editor handoff (`aoBridge.editorHandoff`) behind the session topbar button, and appear only for local sessions. Rename and Pin are hidden for Cloud sessions because both requests go to the daemon that owns the session.
- The archive confirm state moved from `SessionActions` up to `SessionRow`, so the hover button and the menu open the same dialog.
- Open in editor reports failure through `mutateAsync`: the menu unmounts as soon as an item is picked, and TanStack skips per-call `mutate` callbacks after unmount.
- Portaled React events bubble up the component tree, so a right-click on a session menu reached the project row's trigger. `ContextMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuContent` and `ConfirmDialog` (content and overlay) now stop `contextmenu` propagation. `ConfirmDialog` already did the same for clicks.
- Copy actions show a short toast. 3 new i18n keys in all 8 locales.

## Testing

- Updated the Sidebar session-menu test for the new item list. Added tests for archive from the menu, for not opening the project menu on a right-click inside the session menu, and for renaming from a board card.
- Per the requester, no tests or checks were run locally; CI is the first run.

## What

## What

The session menu's editor row becomes **Open in ›**. Hovering it opens a submenu listing every target that can open the session's worktree: the default editor first, then other installed editors, then the file manager and terminals.

title: ci: run race, macOS and Windows checks on main instead of every PR
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +179 -124 (CI workflows)

## What

Trims the PR checks that cost the most and caught nothing, per step 1 of #7181:

- `go test` runs without `-race` on PRs for backend-core, session-store, sqlite and windows-workspace. Race stays on for every push to `main`. `chat-race` keeps `-race` on PRs.
- The sqlite job uses 2 shards instead of 4. The `-race` suffix is dropped from the sqlite and session-store job names, since they no longer always run race.
- `go vet` is removed from backend-core. golangci-lint already runs govet.
- `cloud-build-test` moves to a new `cloud.yml` that runs only when `cloud/**` changes. `cloud/go.mod` pins backend to a fixed commit, so backend changes cannot affect it.
- `mac-update-helper` moves to a new `mac-native-helpers.yml` that runs only when `frontend/native/**` or the helper/repair-installer build scripts change.
- CLI E2E runs Linux only on PRs. macOS and Windows run on `main`. setup-go caching is now on, which removes the `proxy.golang.org` fetch flake.
- The Frontend `typecheck` job no longer runs `typecheck:e2e`, because renderer-smoke already runs it.

## Why

Part of #7181. In 80 failed PR runs, race detection caught nothing. macOS jobs were about 59 of the ~165 runner minutes a backend+frontend PR costs. Numbers are in the [audit](https://gist.github.com/ronishrohan/5fb3ea649e9b78a113fb23fd7e330017).

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Every backend PR runs 4 race-instrumented sqlite shards, race session-store, race windows-workspace | 2 plain sqlite shards, plain session-store and windows-workspace; race runs on `main` |
| Every frontend PR runs `mac-update-helper` on macOS (~38 min equivalent) | Runs only when native helpers or their build scripts change |
| Every backend PR runs CLI E2E on Linux, macOS and Windows | Linux on PRs; all three on `main` |
| Every backend PR runs `cloud-build-test` | Runs only when `cloud/**` changes |
| `typecheck:e2e` runs twice per frontend PR | Runs once, in renderer-smoke |

## How

- One workflow-level `RACE` env var expands to `-race=true` on `main` and `-race=false` on PRs. An explicit bool flag works the same in bash and PowerShell, while an empty value would not.
- The CLI E2E matrix is picked from the event, so PRs never queue macOS or Windows runners.
- No status checks are required by the `main` ruleset, so renamed jobs and the new workflows do not block merging.
- Not done here (follow-ups on #7181): a Postgres service for the cloud tests, the flaky tests, and a nightly schedule. Every push to `main` already runs the full race and OS matrix.

## Testing

No local runs. These are workflow-only changes, and `agent-ci` needs Docker. This PR's own run checks the PR path. The first `main` run after merge checks the race and macOS/Windows path.

title: ci: run cloud Postgres integration tests against a service container
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +15 -0 (CI workflow)

Stacked on #7375 (base `ci/trim-pr-checks`). Retarget to `main` after #7375 merges.

## What

Add a PostgreSQL 17 service container to the `cloud-build-test` job in `.github/workflows/cloud.yml` and set `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL` for the `go test` step.

## Why

Part of #7181. The audit found about 160 Postgres tests in `cloud/internal/postgres` (RLS, migrations, billing) that never run in CI. Their fixtures (`openNotificationTestStore`, `openGitHubMultiOrgStore`, and the migration tests) call `t.Skip` when `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is empty, and the job had no database.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `cloud-build-test` has no database; every test in `cloud/internal/postgres` that needs one skips | The job starts `postgres:17-bookworm`, and those tests run against it |

## How

- Image: `mirror.gcr.io/library/postgres:17-bookworm`. This is the same version as `cloud/compose.yaml`, pulled from the GCR mirror that this workflow already uses for its Docker builds.
- The test URL connects as the image's default `postgres` superuser. The tests expect this: they create their own `NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS` roles (`openAppRoleStore`, `openRLSStore`), schemas, and the `pgcrypto` extension. They also run `Migrate` themselves, which takes an advisory lock. The job needs no init SQL.
- Only `cloud/internal/postgres` reads the variable, so other packages are unchanged.

## Testing

- Nothing was run locally. These tests need Docker, and the user asked not to run broad builds or suites.
- Not run: `go build`, `go vet`, `go test`, lint.
- Validation is this PR's Cloud workflow run, which now runs the Postgres tests.
- Run [40647590160](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40647590160): the service container started, all 94 migrations applied, and the RLS role fixtures worked. Every other cloud package passed. Four tests in `cloud/internal/postgres` fail. None of them is a setup problem: each fails on product behavior, so this PR does not change them and does not skip them:
  - `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`: `ci_feedback_store_test.go:92: failing notification = []`. No `ci_failed` notification is created for a failing CI snapshot.
  - `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity/{queued,running}`: `project_session_store_test.go:266: status = "working", want idle despite queued/running turn`.
  - `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`: `project_settings_store_test.go:199: review credential provider= err=not found`.
  - `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`: `worker_activity_settlement_test.go:162: activity = "active", want "idle"`.
- The job stays red until those four failures are fixed in separate PRs.

| `cloud/internal/worker` `TestSetupStepEventsHeartbeatWhileOutputKeepsArriving` | Already fixed on `main` by b087ce794d (#7105). The trailing `echo` was removed. Every CI failure (`an unfinished line was published: "start\nprogress 11"`) ran on a commit from before that fix. |
| `cloud/internal/worker` `TestCleanupSkipsTheStepsOfARepositoryFolderThatIsNotAOs` (`text file busy`) | Already fixed on `main` by b087ce794d. The test now runs the hook with `sh <hook>` instead of exec'ing a file that was just written. |
| `chatdriver/acp` `TestACPDriverDeliversSessionPreambleOncePerSession` | Already fixed on `main` by 484932e075 (#6769). The driver now releases the turn before it emits `ChatControllerReady`, and `runOneTurn` waits for that event. |
| `systeminstall` `TestAgentVendorScriptInstallPersistsInstallVerifySuccessLifecycle` | Fixed here. Its twin, `TestAgentInstallPersistsInstallVerifySuccessLifecycle`, had the same race and is fixed too. |
| Renderer smoke `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts:111` | Fixed here. |

## Why

Part of #7181.

- **systeminstall:** `finishAgentJob` sets the in-memory job to `succeeded` before it writes that state to the job store. The tests waited on `Status()`, which reads the in-memory job, and then read the store history. Sometimes they read the history before the last write landed. CI failed with `statuses = [installing verifying]`.
- **composer e2e:** the padding-click step pressed `ArrowLeft` right after the log click, whose focus restore makes Lexical write the DOM selection. After its own write, Lexical skips the next `selectionchange` (`isSelectionChangeFromDOMUpdate`). If the key arrived before that event fired, Chrome merged the two into one event and Lexical skipped it. The DOM caret was at 4, but the editor still had 5. The padding click calls `editor.focus()`, which applies the editor's selection, so the caret went back to 5. CI failed at line 134 with `Expected: 4, Received: 5`.

## Before / After

No user-visible change. Only test code changes.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A 50 ms delay on the fake store's `succeeded` write makes both systeminstall lifecycle tests fail with `statuses = [installing verifying]` | Same delay: both pass. The tests wait for the success callback, which runs after the write |
| Setting Lexical's `isSelectionChangeFromDOMUpdate` before `ArrowLeft` gives the CI failure: `Expected: 4, Received: 5` at the padding click | No arrow key follows a Lexical selection write. The caret stays where typing put it (offset 5, mid-text). Setting the flag before the typing and before the padding click still passes 10/10 |

## How

- `systeminstall_test.go`: the two lifecycle tests register `SetOnSucceeded` and wait for it with a new `waitForPersistedSuccess` helper (used twice). `finishAgentJob` calls the callback only after `persistJobBestEffort` succeeds, so this waits for the write itself.
- `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts`: removed the `ArrowLeft` before the padding click. The test now checks that the click keeps offset 5, where typing `X` left the caret, and that `Y` goes in there (`abcdXYef`). The test still checks a mid-text caret, so it can still tell "keep the caret" apart from "select end" (offset 7).
- The code is unchanged. The DOM selection running ahead of Lexical's needs a key that arrives before a queued `selectionchange` task. That happens to Playwright input, which arrives back to back, but is very unlikely when a person types.
- Not changed: the first half of that test (`fill` then two `ArrowLeft`s) could in theory hit the same Lexical skip. It has not failed in CI, so I left it alone.
- Not in scope: the CLI E2E `proxy.golang.org` flake from the audit. That is a CI caching change, not a test fix.

## Testing

Run:
- `go test -run '^(TestAgentVendorScriptInstallPersistsInstallVerifySuccessLifecycle|TestAgentInstallPersistsInstallVerifySuccessLifecycle)$' -count=200 ./internal/service/systeminstall`: pass. A temporary 50 ms delay on the fake store's `succeeded` write made the old tests fail every time and the new ones pass. The delay was not committed.
- `npx playwright test e2e/chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts:111 --repeat-each=20 --workers=4`: 20/20 pass. A temporary, uncommitted copy of the spec that set Lexical's skip flag gave the CI failure on the old steps and passed 10/10 on the new ones.
- For the already-fixed tests, I checked the CI failure logs with `gh run view --log-failed`. I also confirmed that each failing run's commit predates the fixing commit.

Not run: full Go or frontend suites, `go build ./...`, `go vet`, golangci-lint, typecheck (including `typecheck:e2e`), or the rest of the renderer smoke suite. CI covers those.

title: fix(session): re-create a missing workspace before resume-agent relaunches
body:
Code changes: +140 -33  
Tests: +211 -3  
Others: +0 -0

## What

`resume-agent` restores a missing worktree on its saved branch, finishes the project's Setup, and then relaunches the exited agent. It retries an interrupted or failed Setup even when the checkout already exists. The request uses the project's Setup budget and reports a structured error if provisioning fails.

## Why

An exited (not terminated) session keeps its row, branch and history, but its worktree directory can disappear. Typical causes are a user or a disk-cleanup job running `git worktree remove` on a finished session to reclaim space, or someone deleting the directory by hand. Today `resumeAgentRecordWithReservedGeneration` passes `Metadata.WorkspacePath` straight to the relaunch without checking it:

- in chat mode the harness is launched with a missing working directory, so the launch fails with an opaque error;
- or the agent's hook installation (`MkdirAll(<workspace>/.claude)`) first creates an empty, non-git directory, and the agent then starts and works in a directory with no checkout.

The desktop app calls `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/resume-agent` automatically when a session is opened, and when the pointer rests on a sidebar row, so the user hits this just by opening an old session.

`Restore` (terminated sessions), retry-start (`chat_spawn_async.go`: "A saved worktree that no longer exists … is created again") and daemon-restart recovery already re-create a missing workspace. Only the exited-agent resume path did not.

I did not find an existing issue for this. Happy to open one and link it if you prefer.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| On main, resuming an exited agent whose worktree was removed failed with HTTP 409 and left the checkout missing. | Resume recreates the saved checkout and completes Setup before relaunch. |
| On the previous PR code, a 75-second Setup exceeded the ordinary 60-second request limit. | A route test completes 75 seconds of virtual time and returns HTTP 200. A separate real 65-second Setup completes before runtime relaunch with a 60-second base request budget. |
| On the previous PR code, a failed Setup returned a generic 500. A second resume could start the agent in the incomplete checkout. | Each failed attempt returns HTTP 409 with `WORKSPACE_PROVISION_FAILED` and a safe step diagnostic. The session stays exited until Setup succeeds. |

## How

- Include the resume route in the existing Setup budget middleware.
- Record pending Setup in AO's data directory before restoring a checkout. The shared restore path clears the marker after successful provisioning. A pending restore can reuse a dirty registered worktree through the existing Git adapter.
- Report the failed step and an exit status or timeout when available. The response excludes raw errors and script output.
- Merge upstream main at `2cc4111357bd`.

**Regression risk:** A retry runs the current Setup from its first step in the same checkout, so scripts may encounter files or other side effects from a partial run. Existing checkouts without a marker keep the ordinary resume path, including older checkouts for which there is no durable Setup history.

## Testing

- WSL2 with Go 1.27.1. Formatting, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and focused race tests in `internal/httpd`, `internal/session_manager`, and `internal/service/session` passed.
- The new route, timeout, HTTP error, and Setup retry regressions failed on the synchronized previous PR code and passed with the fix.
- The Git worktree regression verifies two failed attempts, including a retry with a fresh manager, preserve a dirty tracked file and block runtime launch. It then checks successful Setup before launch and a subsequent resume that skips Setup.
- The full session-manager race suite passed on the final revision, including the existing Restore prompt-file fallback tests. The SQLite, SQLite store, and HTTP race suites and the public-boundary check also passed locally.
- A real shell Setup ran for 65.04 seconds with a 60-second request budget. The fake runtime checked for its completion file before relaunch.
- The broader local race run surfaced environment failures that also reproduce on upstream main (installed Codex protocol schema, WSL login-shell output, process-group shutdown, and missing zsh and fish). GitHub reports [`action_required` for the Go workflow](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42050334709) on the final commit.

title: feat(desktop): sign a release build pointed at staging in to staging's WorkOS
body:
Code changes: +67 -11\
Tests: +67 -0\
Others: none

## What

A release build (nightly or stable) launched against staging now signs in to staging:

```sh
AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=https://staging-api.aoagents.dev \
  "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/MacOS/agent-orchestrator"
```

When the control plane is `https://staging-api.aoagents.dev`, on any port, the app:

- signs in with staging's AuthKit client (`client_01KZ3VRKC374…`, the public client id already baked as the default);
- returns through staging's bounce page (`https://staging-api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return`);
- keeps that sign-in in `cloud-auth-staging.bin`, so it never mixes with the production sign-in in `cloud-auth.bin`.

A normal launch is unchanged. `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT` still overrides the return page. Development builds still use the loopback callback.

## Why

Production moved to its own WorkOS environment on 2026-10-07, while staging stayed on the old one. Release builds bake production's AuthKit client through `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`. So a nightly pointed at staging:

- signed in to production's WorkOS;
- had every staging request answered with 401 (`/me`, projects, hosts);
- went back to WorkOS on "Connect repository", which only produced another production token.

Contributors could no longer test staging with a nightly.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Nightly + `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=https://staging-api.aoagents.dev`: staging returns 401 to every request, and sign-in loops | Signs in to staging's WorkOS and works against staging |
| One sign-in file shared by every launch, so a production token was sent to staging | Staging keeps its own `cloud-auth-staging.bin`; switching back to production keeps the production sign-in |
| Normal launch: production WorkOS, `api.aoagents.dev` return page | Unchanged |

## How

- New pure module `frontend/src/main/cloud-auth-environment.ts`. It decides the client id, return page and sign-in file from `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT`, `app.isPackaged` and the build's client id.
- `cloud-auth.ts` reads those three values from it once at startup, instead of hard-coding them.
- Only the HTTPS staging host matches. Production, local and look-alike hosts keep the build's settings.

## Testing

- New `cloud-auth-environment.test.ts`:
  - normal packaged launch;
  - packaged launch pointed at staging;
  - production, local and look-alike hosts;
  - a development build pointed at staging;
  - the `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT` override.
- `cloud-auth.test.ts` and `cloud-auth-local.test.ts` pass: 51 tests across the three files.
- `tsgo --noEmit` passes.
- `src/main`: 1552 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `remote-proxy.test.ts > startRemoteProxy over HTTP/2 > verifies the host once per upstream session`, which also fails on unmodified `main` on this machine.
- Live test with a locally packaged macOS build that bakes production's client id (`VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_01KZ3VRKTDKBZ…`), as a release does. It ran from `~/Applications` under a temporary bundle id, so it never touched the installed nightly, with its own `AO_DATA_DIR`:

  | Launch | Signed in through | Result |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=https://staging-api.aoagents.dev` | staging WorkOS, `staging-api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return`, `ao-app://callback` | staging `GET /me` 200 (401 before this change); GitHub installations, repositories and projects 200 |
  | normal launch | production WorkOS, `api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return`, `ao-app://callback` | production `GET /me` 200 |
  | that production session sent to staging | | 401, so the two sign-ins stay separate |

  - Staging's WorkOS environment lists `https://staging-api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return` as a redirect URI, so nothing needs to change there.
  - The unsigned test build could not read the app's Keychain key, so it kept each sign-in in memory. The separate file names (`cloud-auth.bin`, `cloud-auth-staging.bin`) are covered by the unit tests, not the live run.

title: Sentry: full error coverage for daemon + Electron
body:
Code changes: +382 -78  
Tests: +548 -10  
Others: +39 -5

## What

Split daemon and Electron Sentry projects, implement consented Electron main capture behind a closed production release gate, route renderer exceptions to Sentry through the preload bridge, report daemon background panics, and group daemon HTTP errors by registered route and safe error code. This builds on merged #7221.

The production release gate remains closed. The privacy policy must name Sentry and describe the data it receives before a separate activation change ships.

## Why

The shared old desktop DSN mixed process errors. Electron main had no active sender, renderer exceptions went to PostHog, daemon goroutine panics escaped HTTP recovery, and function-site grouping split equivalent workspace Git failures.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The packaged app handed the old desktop DSN to the daemon. | The daemon receives its own project DSN and keeps `AO_SENTRY_DSN`. Electron main uses `AO_ELECTRON_SENTRY_DSN`; development defaults to an empty DSN on both processes. Explicit overrides retain precedence. |
| Electron main had no active Sentry sender and renderer exceptions went to PostHog. | Once the release gate opens, a consent-gated main sender captures main crashes, renderer and child process exits, and sanitized renderer exceptions. Renderer exceptions no longer enter PostHog. The remote `$exception` deny list also stops renderer forwarding. |
| Renderer errors shared a generic issue, and nightly Electron builds were labeled stable. | Safe exception type and top function separate issues while keeping messages private; Electron and daemon use the same version channel for Sentry environment. |
| An app exit after persisting opt-out could leave an offline event for a later opt-in. | Startup with sharing off purges the queue before a sender can open it. A failed purge blocks opt-in until cleanup succeeds. Opt-out also gates offline retries and waits for any active network send before queue deletion. |
| Background daemon goroutine panics were outside handler recovery. | Daemon-owned goroutine entry points log the stack, call consent-gated `sentryobs.CapturePanic` with a fixed label, then rethrow so a fatal panic still stops the daemon. |
| HTTP failures could split by recording function. | Registered route plus allowlisted error code groups equivalent Sentry failures; status separates errors without a captured cause. Existing PostHog fingerprints retain their old values. |

No UI change. Share error events remains the user-facing consent and opt-out control.

## How

When enabled, Electron uses the `@sentry/electron` main offline transport with its queue pinned under AO's Electron `userData` directory. Opt-out gates further retries and requeues, drains any active network send, and deletes that queue before completion. On restart with sharing off, the controller purges any queue left by an interrupted opt-out before publishing the policy. A purge failure keeps cleanup pending and blocks a later opt-in. The renderer has no direct Sentry transport or independent DSN override. Electron events use fixed titles, allowlisted tags, an installation ID user, exception type and top safe function fingerprints, and sanitized function and line number frames. Raw stack paths and exception messages are removed before sending. Electron and daemon environments use the same version channel mapping, including the daemon's `AO_TELEMETRY_APP_VERSION` override. Expected abort, network change, and daemon startup noise is dropped. The daemon reuses #7221 privacy and identity rules, reports background panics before rethrowing, and preserves stable fingerprints. Electron removes SDK process crash listeners after consent closes so a later opt-in adds one fresh set. The SDK marks uncaught exceptions with a fatal `generic` mechanism, which is classified separately from other main errors. Startup `daemon_unavailable` and 4xx probe routes stay out of Sentry. Mobile DSN is unchanged. No live Sentry or PostHog event was injected.

For a prior opt-in recorded while the release gate was closed, renderer startup loads the policy and the shell opens the "Share error events?" renewal dialog with "Turn on" and "Keep off" choices. Sending stays off until the user chooses "Turn on". Dismissing the dialog does not record consent, so it appears again on the next app start.

The earlier activation commit is offset by this review fix: `AGENT_SWITCH_FAILURE_PRODUCTION_ENABLED` remains false in the final diff. A separate activation change must follow the privacy policy update.

The model probe suppression already requires status 409 and an exact normalized operation. The link-preview 502 mapping and supervisor package dependency are unchanged cleanup follow-ups.

## Testing

- Focused review regressions passed: 67 frontend tests, 61 tests in the two initially flaky frontend files, and both changed Go packages.
- Frontend `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` passed.
- Full frontend Vitest was run twice. The parallel run had 2 failures in untouched browser history and settings tests; the isolated rerun passed all 61 tests. The second full run had 1 browser history timeout, with 10,003 passed and 9 skipped. Focused changed tests passed.
- Changed Go packages with `go test -race -count=1`: passed on this head.
- Go `build ./...` and `vet ./...`: passed on this head.
- Full local Go suite failed in seven untouched packages: commandcode, opencodev2, tmux, CLI, service/session, systemcheck, and session_manager. Changed packages passed, including race tests.
- Pinned `golangci-lint` is unavailable locally. Docker daemon is not running, so the Docker-backed local CI runner is unavailable. Remote checks on this new head remain to be verified.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from merged `main` containing #7221
- [x] Before / After filled in
- [x] Process boundary, consent lifecycle, queue purge, scrub, fingerprint, and goroutine recovery tests added
- [x] Mobile DSN unchanged; Electron production gate closed pending privacy policy
- [ ] Relevant remote CI checks pass

title: fix(sessions): say "orchestrator replaced" when restoring an old orchestrator
body:
## Problem

Restoring or resuming an orchestrator after a newer one was created for the same project fails with `project conversation <id> is no longer owned by session <id>`. Sentry: [AO-DESKTOP-42](https://untrivial-x0.sentry.io/issues/AO-DESKTOP-42), plus about 10 similar groups in 30 days. Since #7252 it answers a generic 409 `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED` (step `chat start`). The project's orchestrator conversation belongs to the newest orchestrator, so the old one cannot reattach to it.

## Change

- `ports.ErrProjectConversationReplaced`, wrapped by the store at the `preserveOwner` check in `conversation_store.go`, only when another session owns the conversation. When the owner row was deleted (`current_session_id` is NULL), nothing replaced it, so the plain error stays.
- Chat start, coordinator-reserved restore (provider id and scope set): `ConversationForSession` finds nothing for an old orchestrator. If the project conversation is owned by another session, the error now wraps the same sentinel.
- `mapSessionError` maps it, before the generic relaunch case, to **409 `ORCHESTRATOR_REPLACED`**: "This orchestrator was replaced by a newer one for the project. Open the newer orchestrator instead."
- `emitRelaunchFailed` also reports `ORCHESTRATOR_REPLACED` with its real code, so `ao.session.relaunch_failed` and Sentry still see it. Restore and resume-agent share the path.
- Renderer `classifyError`: `ORCHESTRATOR_REPLACED` is P2 / user, so it is still reported.

## Which restores are covered

| Restore path in chat `Start` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Native resume (provider id, no scope): `OpenNativeConversation` | generic 409 | `ORCHESTRATOR_REPLACED` |
| Coordinator-reserved boundary (provider id and scope) | generic 409 | `ORCHESTRATOR_REPLACED` |
| Fresh context (no provider id) | rebinds the conversation to the old orchestrator | unchanged |

The fresh-context path is left alone on purpose. It is how a new orchestrator takes over, and it is also how a user gets an old orchestrator back after the newer one was killed. Refusing it would break that.

## Notes / intentional omissions

- Behaviour stays "refuse" on the two covered paths. A takeover could steal a live orchestrator's conversation.
- The UI still offers restore on a replaced orchestrator. It is offered from several places and the UI does not know about replacement; hiding it is a follow-up.
- `CommitChatSpawn` has a similar plain "no longer owned" error; it is unchanged.

## Validation

No local builds or tests were run for the review fixes; CI runs them.

- `TestStartReplacedOrchestratorReportsReplacement` (chat service): restores an old orchestrator through `Start` on both covered paths, asserts the sentinel, and checks the newer orchestrator keeps the conversation.
- `TestOpenNativeConversationRejectsReplacedOrchestrator` and `TestOpenNativeConversationWithDeletedOwnerIsNotReplaced` (store).
- `TestRestoreReplacedOrchestratorAnswersTypedConflictAndStaysInTelemetry` (session service mapping and telemetry).
- `src/shared/observability.test.ts` case for the new code.

title: fix(sessions): destroy a terminated session's leftover runtime before restoring it
body:
Code changes: +17 -0  
Tests: +47 -5  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Restoring a terminated session fails with `conpty: session "<id>" already exists; destroy before re-creating`. Sentry: [AO-DESKTOP-44](https://untrivial-x0.sentry.io/issues/AO-DESKTOP-44), plus about 10 similar groups in 30 days, on Windows conpty and the macOS direct PTY host. Since #7252 it answers 409 `AGENT_RESUME_FAILED` with step `runtime`. Retrying never recovers: one user retried 5 times in 8 minutes.

`RestoreWithMode` relaunches with no restart handle, so it calls `runtime.Create`. conpty `Create` refuses an id it still has in memory or in its pty-host registry. A session can be terminated without its runtime being destroyed (its agent exited on its own), so the dead host's registry entry stays until something calls `Destroy`.

## Change

- `RestoreWithMode` destroys the terminated session's own runtime handle before relaunching. A destroy failure returns `RelaunchError` step `runtime cleanup`, so it stays a 409 that is still reported to PostHog and Sentry.
- `restartRuntime` (resume path) destroys a runtime the probe reports as definitively not alive before `Create`. The "runtime unavailable" outage branch is unchanged.

## Why this is safe (fail-closed)

- The session is durably terminated, so its runtime is AO's to reap. `Manager.Reconcile` already destroys a terminated session's leftover runtime.
- conpty `Destroy` returns nil only when the registry proves the host is gone. It returns an error for an inconclusive scan or unresolved ownership, and then restore stops instead of starting a competing host.
- tmux `Destroy` treats only confirmed session/server absence as already gone.

## Notes / intentional omissions

- Spawn uses fresh ids and is not changed.
- Other nil-handle relaunch callers (TUI provider switch, `reconcileLive` relaunch) are follow-ups.
- Two existing tests counted every `Destroy` call. They now assert that the runtime the failed restore created is the one rolled back, which is the same property, checked by handle.
- Not verified on a real Windows/macOS conpty host.

## Validation

Focused tests only (pass after rebase onto `main`):
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run 'Restore|Resume|Restart|Reconcile|Interactive|Native'`
- The 3 new tests (`TestRestore_DestroysLeftover…`, `TestRestore_LeftoverRuntime…`, `TestRestartRuntime_Destroys…`) fail without the `manager.go` change.

The full CI suites, `golangci-lint`, `go vet` and `-race` were not run locally; CI covers them.

title: fix(mobile): send terminal-composer messages as the user's own words
body: Code changes: +12 -5\ Tests: +48 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Text sent from the mobile terminal composer (the "Message the agent…" box under a terminal session) now reaches the agent as a plain user prompt. Before, it was typed into the agent wrapped in `…`. The same applies to the review screens' **Send to worker** actions, which now match desktop. ## Why `sendMessage` in `packages/mobile/lib/api.ts` posted `{ message }` to `POST /sessions/{id}/send` with no `userAuthored`. Without that flag the daemon treats the text as AO coordination (an `ao send` from another session). `manager.send` then wraps it with `WrapSessionDelivery` and types the envelope into the pane. Every place desktop sends text the user wrote already passes `userAuthored: true`, and so does mobile's own file-review send (`lib/files/api.ts`). What the user saw: - **Every terminal-mode harness got the envelope**, because delivery doesn't depend on the harness. Codex echoes it verbatim. Claude Code v2.1.312 does too now; older versions folded it into a pasted-text block, which hid it. - **The agent read the user's words as an AO coordination message**, not as a user prompt. - **The prompt hooks marked the turn as coordination** (`isAOCoordinationMessage`), so the message never became the session's latest user prompt. ## Before / After Same scratch daemon (`ao daemon` built from this branch, its own data dir), fresh terminal-mode sessions, same Debug app binary. Only `TerminalSessionScreen.tsx` changed between captures: `main` → this branch. Each shot is "Hi" typed into the composer and sent. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | | | | | Rows: iOS 26.5 simulator and Android emulator, each with Codex v0.162.1 and Claude Code v2.1.312. **Not fixed here:** the yellow "Message not sent… the agent did not start a turn" banner on the Claude Code shots shows on **both** sides. That's a separate daemon issue: `/send` returns 409 `SESSION_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED` for a Claude Code terminal session even though Claude took the prompt and replied. It reproduces from plain `curl` with `{"message":"Hi","userAuthored":true}` (the desktop path). In that run Claude's activity hooks post 200, but the session's activity state never leaves `idle` and nothing moves `latest_user_prompt_at` past the send's own baseline. So `confirmActive` runs out its attempts. I'll follow up separately. ## How - `sendMessage` takes an optional `{ userAuthored }` and sends `userAuthored: true` only when asked. This is safe with older daemons: `/send` decodes leniently and ignores unknown fields. - Three user actions opt in: the terminal composer, **Send to worker** for a review summary (`app/review/[sessionId].tsx`), and for an inline review comment (`app/sheets/review-actions.tsx`). Desktop's `SessionInspector` `sendMessageToWorker` already sends those same formatted review messages as `userAuthored`; thanks to the review for catching the gap. - The only change to the composer is the flag. The 409 `SESSION_AWAITING_DECISION` → PTY reroute is unchanged. ## Testing - `npx vitest run lib/api.send.test.ts`: the new tests check the request body with and without the flag, and pin all three user-initiated call sites. title: Windows app gets stuck on “Agent Orchestrator is starting” because ao.exe is blocked
body:
## What happened

The official Windows `v0.14.7` release is installed on my PC. The app opens, but stays on **“Agent Orchestrator is starting”** and does not reach the main screen.

Windows is blocking the bundled `ao.exe` background process. Running `ao.exe version` directly gives an Application Control error. The app cannot finish loading without it.

I also extracted a fresh copy of the official installer and ran it with separate AO data. It had the same problem. I did not change any Windows security settings.

## What I checked

- Windows Code Integrity logged events **3077** and **3033** for `ao.exe`, saying it did not meet the required signing level.
- Windows reports **NotSigned** for both the desktop app and the bundled `ao.exe`.
- The installed files match the files from the official `v0.14.7` release. Their SHA-256 hashes are:
  - `agent-orchestrator.exe`: `88bf900045a26f1dceb8620d2d749297d0cd3a94dbb763a7d858f9aee88bb51b`
  - `resources/daemon/ao.exe`: `b100652ce3e426f45a177743dbf0482e1884fa2aa2eeee0771500de0696f78d9`

## What should happen

The Windows release should include a signed desktop app and bundled `ao.exe` so it can run on PCs that require signed software. If Windows blocks `ao.exe`, the app should show an error instead of staying on the loading screen.

Related: #7232 covers the unsigned installer, and #7157 covers Bitdefender blocking `ao.exe`. This report confirms the startup failure with the **unmodified official `v0.14.7` files**.

title: feat(inspector): PR details, actions, comments and activity in the session inspector
body:
Code changes: +8361 -429\ Tests: +5685 -174\ Others: +2822 -29 (generated OpenAPI, schema.ts and sqlc; 8 locale files) ## What A PR can now be read, reviewed, merged and stacked without leaving AO: - **PR tab.** Each PR opens in its own tab beside the chat. The header holds the state pill, title, branches, Open on GitHub and Merge. Below it, **Summary** shows the full description and **Comments** shows the conversation. Reviewers, checks and the stack sit in a side column that folds under the title when the pane is narrow. A tab keeps its section, scroll position and any half-written comment when you switch away. - **Sidebar card.** One PR at a time. A session with several PRs gets chips over the card (open first, then drafts, newest first); merged and closed PRs wait under "+N earlier". The row has an **Open tab** pill, which hides when that tab is already in front, and the GitHub logo is the way out to GitHub. - **Description**: a short preview that fades out, a line counting its images and tables, and **Read full description**, which opens the PR tab. Images open in a **gallery**: full size, arrows, arrow keys, thumbnails, "n of m", Open original, and a clear message for images a private repository only serves to a signed-in browser. - **Merge status** as one line that opens to the rest. The line shows the worst fact: a failure or conflict, then a warning, then review, then checks. Failed check names, conflicts and reviews sit in the dropdown. "No reviews yet" is gone because it decides nothing. "Not mergeable yet" appears only when no fact explains the block, for example a branch rule on GitHub. - **Merge** sits in the tab header in both layouts, as a split button with squash, merge commit and rebase. When GitHub won't allow it, it greys out with the reason, such as "1 check failing". - **One action button** at the card's foot. It does the next step: the branch's work first (Commit & push, Push, Update from main, Resolve conflicts), then what the PR waits for (Ready for review, Reopen, or merge). Its menu holds the other branch steps, the merge method and Close (asks first). Draft, Open and Closed change from the state pill. - **Branch rows** ("6 commits · 6 not pushed", "2 commits behind main · conflicts") open in place to their files: name, folder, +/−, change letter. A file opens its diff; View all changes opens the Files tab. - **Comments** as cards, bots included: reviews, top-level comments and review threads (file and line shown). The tab reads oldest first, and the sidebar previews the newest few. **Reply** opens the same box as a new comment, and replies post to GitHub. **Resolve** folds a thread into the Resolved group at the bottom. **+ Comment** takes attachments (picked, pasted or dropped). Each card's ⋯ menu has Add to chat, View in diff, Send to agent, Open on GitHub and Copy link. - **Stacks** (GitHub): the tab lists the whole GitHub stack, top first, with this PR marked and its base underneath. **Merge through #N · k PRs** lands every layer up to this one, all or nothing, after a confirmation that names each PR. **New task on this PR** starts an agent from that PR's branch, and **Add to stack** joins a PR to the one it's based on. - **No PR yet**: Commit & push, then Push, then Create PR once everything is pushed (and no Create PR for work that already shipped). - **Artifacts** in the Summary tab: newest 4 first, then Show more (from #6669). The Reviews tab and its Review controls are `main`'s, unchanged. ## Why Today the PR description, its comments, why a PR can't merge, and how far the branch is behind main all need a trip to GitHub, and so does merging with anything but squash, closing a PR or marking it ready. With the sidebar closed there is no way to merge at all. "Merge blocked" doesn't say why, and AO can't show a stack, merge one or start an agent on top of one. Review on this PR asked for the detail to live in its own tab and for the sidebar to stay light. This also carries over the agreed parts of #6669 (Ronish is credited as co-author on those commits) and adds what T3 Code, Paseo, Orca and Emdash show for a PR. The git panel follows as a stacked PR. ## Before / After The clips are the running app on a real GitHub test repository: real CI, real replies, real merges and a real agent run. The merge status images use substituted data to reach each state. The Before column is `main`'s behaviour in words. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | PR details only on the sidebar card or on GitHub | **Each PR opens in its own tab**
| | No way to open a PR inside AO | **Open tab stays in AO, the GitHub logo leaves it**
| | Several PRs stack as full cards | **One PR at a time, with chips.** Why it can't merge is one click away
| | Readiness rows always open, "Checking merge readiness" twice, "No review required" | **One line, worst fact first, the rest behind one click**
| | Same | Checks failing
| | Same | Merge conflict
| | Same | All passing
| | Same | Approved, with unresolved comments
| | Same | Blocked by GitHub for another reason
| | No PR description in AO | **The full description in the tab**, with images, tables and code
| | PR images only on GitHub | **A gallery**, with arrow keys and thumbnails
| | Merge only on the sidebar card, so closing the sidebar removes it | **Merge in the tab header**, with the method in its menu
| | Closing the sidebar loses the PR's details and Merge | **They move to a column beside the PR**, and Merge stays
| | Merge is squash only; draft, ready, close and reopen need GitHub | **One action button**, with the rest in its menu
| | "4 commits pushed" only | **Branch rows** with "behind", "not pushed" and conflicts, each opening to its files
| | Same, for a branch with no PR yet | **Create PR** once everything is pushed, with a draft option
| | Same | Its menu
| | PR comments only on GitHub | **Pass a comment to the agent**, then come back to the tab as you left it
| | Same | **Reply and resolve**, on the real GitHub thread
| | Same | **+ Comment**, with attachments
| | Same | **View in diff** opens the commented line. Off the PR's branch, it opens the comment on GitHub's Files tab
| | No way to start work on top of a PR | **New task on this PR** starts an agent from its branch. This run opened #38
| | Stacks not shown | **Add to stack**, and a failing layer holds back the ones above it
| | A stack can't be merged from AO | **Merge through #35** lands #34 and #35 together, and the rest stay open
| ## How - **PR details:** the GitHub observer's existing batch query also reads the PR body (capped at 64 KB), labels, requested reviewers, commits and the last 50 conversation comments (8 KB each), stored in `pr_details` (migrations `20261028180000000` and `20261101102149555`) and returned with `detailsObservedAt`, so the view can tell "not loaded yet" from "none". `SessionPRSummary` gains `threads` (stored review comments grouped by thread) and `conversation`. Reading any of it makes no provider call. - **PR tab:** `lib/pr-tabs.ts` is a small per-session store of open PR tabs, the one in front and the section asked for. `PRTabPane` draws the tab and keeps Summary and Comments mounted, so a half-written comment survives a look at the description. - **PR actions** (`POST /api/v1/prs/{id}/…`): - `merge` takes an optional `method` (`squash` by default, so existing clients keep working); the head-SHA guard is unchanged. A plain merge of a stack layer with unmerged layers below it is refused (`ErrPRStacked`), because it would land on its parent's branch. - `state` (`close`, `reopen`, `ready`, `draft`) checks the move against the stored state and updates it at once, so lifecycle sees a close the observer would never poll again. Closing a draft keeps it a draft, as the providers do. - `comments` posts a top-level comment, or a reply in a review thread that must belong to this PR, stores it at once, and asks the observer to reconcile. - `attachments` uploads a comment attachment, since GitHub's API cannot attach media to a comment: it checks the file (10 MiB; images, video, pdf, text, json, csv, zip; the bytes must match the declared type, never SVG or HTML) and commits it to an `ao-attachments` branch in the PR's repository (an orphan branch with a README saying not to merge it), returning the markdown that embeds it. GitLab uses its own uploads API. - GitLab: merge commit, close and reopen, comments and thread replies work; rebase merge and draft toggling return 501. - **Stacks:** `SCMStacker` reads a PR's stack, adds a PR to one, and merges every layer up to a chosen PR through GitHub's stacks API (`/api/v1/prs/{id}/stack`, `/stack/merge`). Sessions can start from a PR's branch with a base branch, and the agent's prompt says which branch its own PR should target. - **CI log tails:** a PR action re-reads the PR, which could drop stored CI log tails. `ApplyStoredLogTails` keeps them. - **Resolve** now marks the whole thread and its comments resolved locally (`MarkPRReviewThreadResolved`), so the card updates at once instead of after the next review poll. - **Branch state** gains `conflicts` (an in-memory `git merge-tree --write-tree`, run only when both the branch and its base moved, once per new tip) and `head`. - **Description:** images and tables are counted from the parsed markdown (the renderer's own tree), so code never counts and an image's URL is exactly what the renderer loads. React-markdown never renders raw HTML, and only http(s) images load. - **Merge status:** `readinessExplained` says whether a fact on the card explains the block. If not, the verdict shows. Access-lost paths leave it unset, so the verdict shows there too. - **One PR at a time:** `InspectorPullRequestCardView` takes `headerless` so a host header row can stand in for its title; `PRSummaryCard` takes `layout="focus"` in the inspector and keeps the full card elsewhere (the shared project panel). The pick is remembered per session. - **Sending to the agent** goes through one `useSendToSessionWorker` hook that the Reviews tab now shares. - Cloud and shared sessions keep their own merge flow and get no new write actions. - **Not included:** lineage (a later PR); Rebase stack; Mermaid in PR descriptions; a Changes tab inside the PR tab; #6669's compact rows outside the PR card, last-commit row, hidden Activity, overlay scrollbars and the header "More" menu; #6670's Reviews list. The Activity section is `main`'s, unchanged. ## Testing - `go test` passes for every changed backend package, and each of the latest commits builds and typechecks on its own in a clean checkout - `npm run api:spec` and `openapi-typescript@7.4.4`: no drift - Frontend: `npm run typecheck`; `packages/product-ui` `npm test` (166 pass); PR view tests (633 pass in a clean checkout) - Full renderer `npx vitest run`: 7,705 pass and 3 fail, in files this round didn't change. Two are number formatting in `ContextMeter` and `ChatWorkspace`, not yet confirmed on `main`. `ReadOnlyFileView` failed in the full run and passes alone - A self-review pass over the whole diff fixed 11 bugs, each with a regression test that fails without the fix, and removed dead code and tests that could not fail - Checked in the desktop app on a real GitHub test repository: one PR, several PRs, no PR, a real squash merge, a real reply and resolve, a four-PR stack with a partial merge, and a task started by a real agent. 18 merge status states were checked with substituted data - CI: GitHub reports no checks on this branch yet. It conflicts with `main` and needs a merge first ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a richer pull-request view with descriptions, checks, reviewers, commits, comments, and review threads. * Added controls to comment, reply, attach files, change pull-request state, and choose supported merge strategies. * Added stacked pull-request workflows, including stack management, merging, and starting tasks from a stack. * Added an optional base branch when starting sessions or delegated tasks. * Added branch status details, conflict detection, and related Git actions. * Added pull-request tabs and a Developer Mode toggle for the new view. * Added a changed-files summary with quick access to individual files. * **Improvements** * Pull-request summaries now include richer details and review timestamps, with clearer merge-readiness information. * Added localized labels and messages for pull-request and branch features.

title: fix(persistenthost): Windows shutdown wait must cover the serialized stop chain
body:
Code changes: +96 -10
Tests: +74 -3
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

`TestPersistentClaudeACPHibernateAndNativeResume` fails intermittently on the `windows-workspace` shard with `Hibernate: wait for chat host shutdown: context deadline exceeded` (observed twice in a row on PR #6635's head, then passing on attempt 3 of the same SHA).

## Root cause

`persistenthost.Shutdown`'s process-exit wait is a hard-coded **10 s** budget, but the host's own stop sequence on Windows is serialized and can take up to ~8 s before the descriptor and launch lock are released:

- `providerStdinGrace` 1 s + `providerStopDeadline` 3 s + reap wait 1 s (Windows `terminateProviderProcess` is a no-op; the kill is an external `taskkill /T /F` with a 3 s context)

That leaves < 2 s of margin, which a loaded `-race` Windows runner routinely consumes. The pass/fail line sits exactly at the wait budget: on PR #6635's head, attempts 1–2 failed and attempt 3 — same SHA — passed. `acp/process.go` already carries the same lesson in a comment ("on a loaded machine 5 s ran out first and failed a provider switch"); this is that failure mode recurring at 10 s on Windows.

## Fix

- `persistenthost/host.go`: the 10 s literal becomes `shutdownWaitBudget` (var, default 10 s) + `WaitBudget()` accessor; the stop-sequence durations get names.
- `child_windows.go`: `init()` raises the budget to **30 s on Windows only**, documented against the serialized stop chain.
- Caller clamps that would have defeated the raise follow the accessor: `acp/process.go` `persistentTerminate` (10 s), `codexappserver` terminate (10 s), and `unrealagent` `Terminate` (5 s — the known-bad magnitude).

## Tests (Windows-gated, `child_windows_test.go`)

- `TestWindowsShutdownWaitBudgetCoversStopSequence` — invariant: budget ≥ grace + stop deadline + reap + kill + 5 s margin. Fails on the old constant (10 s < 13 s required), passes with the fix.
- `TestWindowsShutdownToleratesSlowHostCleanup` — behavioral: a host that ACKs shutdown but releases its descriptor/lock after 12 s (> old budget, < new) cleans up without a deadline error.

Windows validation happens in this PR's `windows-workspace` shard (the new tests are `//go:build windows`).

title: chore(mobile): bump app version to 2.2.0 and keep package.json scripts out of the fingerprint
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +10 -1 (app config, fingerprint config)

## What

- Bump the mobile app version from 2.1.0 to 2.2.0 for the next iOS and Android store builds. Build numbers keep coming from EAS remote versioning with auto-increment.
- Add `sourceSkips: ["PackageJsonScriptsAll"]` to `packages/mobile/fingerprint.config.js`, so the `scripts` section of `package.json` is no longer an input to the fingerprint runtime version.

## Why

The app uses `runtimeVersion.policy: "fingerprint"`, and the fingerprint hashed `package.json` scripts. #7047 changed only the `typecheck` script (`tsc` → `tsgo`), and that alone moved the runtime: from then on, no update published from `main` could reach the 2.1.0 store builds. The #7237 OTA had to be published from a branch off the previous OTA commit.

Scripts never end up in the binary. Native inputs are still covered by their own sources: patch-package patches (`patches`), autolinked native module directories, config plugins and `package:react-native`.

This takes effect from the 2.2.0 build on. It changes the runtime hash, which a new store build sets anyway.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Resolved app version `2.1.0` | Resolved app version `2.2.0` (bundle `aoagents.ao`, package `aoagents.dev` unchanged) |
| Fingerprint sources include `packageJson:scripts` | `packageJson:scripts` is the only source removed; no other source changed on either platform |
| Changing `"typecheck": "tsgo --noEmit"` → `"tsc --noEmit"` moves the iOS runtime `02eeb23e…` → `05a55a77…` | The same edit leaves the runtime unchanged: iOS `97aacc2d…`, Android `3b257c42…` |

## How

`sourceSkips` in the config file replaces the library default (`PackageJsonAndroidAndIosScriptsIfNotContainRun`) instead of adding to it. `PackageJsonScriptsAll` returns before any script is read, so it covers the default's case too. Checked against the installed `@expo/fingerprint` 0.20.11.

Intentionally left out of this PR:
- No EAS image pin. With no `image` set, EAS uses `auto`; the 2.1.0 iOS build ran on `macos-tahoe-26.5-xcode-26.6`, the `sdk-57` image. Xcode 27 builds need the UIKit scene lifecycle to launch on iOS 27, which is follow-up work.
- No other native or dependency changes.

## Testing

All under Node 20.20.2, the version `mobile.yml` uses, after `CI=true npm ci` in `packages/mobile`:
- `CI=true npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `CI=true npm test`: 252 files, 2,634 tests passed.

title: refactor: share one top bar frame across every page
body:
Code changes: +993 -1335\
Tests: +328 -416\
Others: +4 -4

## What

Gives every page one shared top bar. Boards, the session tab strip, chat, settings, artifacts, automations and the new-chat page all use the same `PageTopbar` frame. That frame has one height, one edge inset and one style for primary and utility buttons. Notifications show in the shared top bar on every page.

- One `PageTopbar` frame for every page and the session tab strip. `ShellTopbar` becomes `SessionTopbarActions`.
- Removes unused top bar variants and legacy header CSS. The session top bar host is sized with the shared toolbar token.
- Primary top bar actions get one filled 28px style, one per region (Orchestrator on the board). Utility controls rest muted and use the sidebar hover highlight.
- Removes the board title icon, the orchestrator button status dot and the settings page close button.

## Why

Each page's top bar had drifted apart in height, padding and button style. This puts them all on one frame so they match and only one place needs to change.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Pages and the session tab strip each have their own header frame, height and button styles | Every page uses one shared top bar with matching height, inset and button styles |

No screenshots attached. A Windows 11 review compared `main` and this branch on the same seeded data, page by page (see the review on this PR).

## How

This is the original `feat/unify-topbar` branch, rebased again onto current `main` on 2026-11-01. #7398 was built on the earlier version of this branch plus two follow-up commits (the header-band portal and the new-chat drag region), so it is now behind this one. **The two PRs cover the same changes, so only one should merge.**

Conflict resolutions in this rebase:
- `CenterPane` and `ChatWorkspace`: took the shared `SessionTabsTopbar`. Main's new `tabStripAction` was already carried into it; its wrapper keeps the `workspace-topbar-actions` class so the button stays no-drag on macOS.
- `SessionsBoard`: kept main's cloud-project orchestrator auto-start next to the "open orchestrator" shortcut this branch moved there.
- `styles.css`: kept main's framed sidebar-closed panel on macOS (#7509) and dropped the drag strip and legacy topbar CSS as this branch intended.

Fixes on top of the rebase:
- Repaired imports left dangling by the refactor: `ArtifactsView` (`topbarProjectLabelClass`), `NewChatPage` (deleted `ShellTopbar`), `SessionView` (`Globe2` → `BrowserIcon`), plus stale test mocks.
- The old `ShellTopbar` identity block is gone, so main's `SessionOwnerTag` now leads the session topbar actions instead of being dropped. Board cards still show it too.
- The notification bell shows on every page, Settings included, except the welcome start page. It is first in tab order.

Review follow-ups:
- The welcome page and cloud startup loader have no header. On macOS an invisible strip keeps the top edge draggable.
- The new-chat page holds its place with the shared session frame, so the bar doesn't change at handoff.
- Window drag regions are macOS-only, as on `main`. Linux keeps its native frame.

title: fix(kimi): install mid-turn tool and permission hooks so working sessions are not shown Idle
body:
Code changes: +162 -8\
Tests: +597 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Install Kimi's native `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, and `PermissionResult` callbacks alongside its existing four hooks. Tool callbacks report Working through the shared mapper; `PermissionResult` uses canonical `permission-resolved`. Kimi-only lifecycle tracking retains completed approval identities so an early result followed by its delayed request cannot re-arm stale Waiting.

## Why

Fixes #2814. The managed config omitted mid-turn tool activity and permission-result callbacks. Independent hook processes also make callback delivery order unreliable: clearing every approval on any result, or forgetting a result before its request arrives, produces incorrect activity.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Kimi tools execute without reporting mid-turn activity | Tool callbacks report Working |
| Answering an approval supplies no explicit resume signal | PermissionResult reports resumed activity once all known approvals resolve |
| One result can clear another pending approval; an early result can be forgotten | Scoped identities resolve only their own approval; retained completion suppresses late requests and duplicates within the cache bound |

No frontend changes or screenshot. A separately authorized isolated daemon/status smoke reached Kimi startup but was blocked by rejected Kimi credentials before tool execution; the full pill flow remains unverified.

## How

- Rewrite only AO's sentinel-managed block, preserving user hooks and installation idempotence. A migration regression starts with the legacy four-hook config.
- Keep the shared activity mapper and non-Kimi permission semantics unchanged. Only Kimi permission callbacks use a 78-byte SHA-256 key of **native session ID, agent ID, turn ID, and approval UUID** on the existing opaque `toolUseId` wire slot. Tool-call identity alone is insufficient; incomplete approval identity uses ID-less compatibility. No new API fields, persisted display status, terminal scraping, or correlation ports.
- Reuse per-session `toolFlight` and its optimistic-projection deep copy. Record results even before requests. One result cannot clear another known pending approval. ID-less results cannot clear tracked pending approvals or overflow uncertainty; all-ID-less installs keep their legacy clear.
- Bound both map and FIFO to **128 identities/session**. Evict the oldest completed identity by first observation, never a pending approval; duplicates do not refresh order. If all slots are pending, latch overflow and retain Waiting until an existing turn boundary resets it.
- Completion evidence survives an empty pending set, Stop and new prompts. Existing turn boundaries settle observed pending identities and reset overflow while retaining completed identities. Process exit, termination and controller replacement release the whole flight; a successful Kimi spawn also resets it after committing the new process generation. Daemon restart loses it too.

Authoritative source is pinned to **MoonshotAI/kimi-code `0c63065fbd7386132b3b8c914de37adfff4c8daf`**, without assuming Claude-compatible behavior:

- [Hook definitions](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/0c63065fbd7386132b3b8c914de37adfff4c8daf/packages/agent-core-v2/src/features/externalHooks/internal/types.ts) include the installed event names.
- [Approval service](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/0c63065fbd7386132b3b8c914de37adfff4c8daf/packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/toolApproval/toolApprovalService.ts) creates `approval_${randomUUID()}` and carries session/agent/turn scope into the same result context. Different approvals can share a tool-call ID.
- [Permission bridge](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/0c63065fbd7386132b3b8c914de37adfff4c8daf/packages/agent-core-v2/src/features/externalHooks/agent/agentExternalHooksService.ts) fire-and-forgets both permission events; the [runner](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/0c63065fbd7386132b3b8c914de37adfff4c8daf/packages/agent-core-v2/src/features/externalHooks/app/externalHooksRunnerService.ts) starts independent trigger promises. Result-before-own-request delivery is therefore possible.
- [Payload conversion](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/0c63065fbd7386132b3b8c914de37adfff4c8daf/packages/agent-core-v2/src/features/externalHooks/internal/matchHooks.ts) converts fields to snake_case. The [interaction facade](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/0c63065fbd7386132b3b8c914de37adfff4c8daf/packages/agent-core-v2/src/human/interaction/facade.ts) supports multiple unresolved interactions scoped by session and agent, without one-approval-per-AO-session serialization.

**Explicit limits:** this is bounded correlation, not durable ordered delivery. Eviction, daemon restart/process reset, dropped/incomplete callbacks, and requests first observed only after a boundary cannot receive complete ordering protection. Stop/new prompts retain their existing authority to settle observed requests, including callbacks from different native agents; global main/background turn ordering is not established here. The same complete native identity is a duplicate while retained; different UUIDs/turns/agents/native sessions yield different keys. Overflow may intentionally retain Waiting until a boundary. The original assertion that Stop fires after every tool step remains unverified and is not assumed by this fix. No arbitrary-order or live end-to-end correctness claim is made.

## Testing

Full regression validation remains in **GitHub Actions**. No local test suites, lint, formatting, generation or installations were run. Separately, on November 2 the user authorized a daemon/status-only smoke: prior head `cc01a8f279` was built from cached dependencies and an isolated Kimi 2.4.1 session was launched. Kimi rejected its stored login before running tools. Startup Idle → Working was observed; tool/approval/resume/final-Idle transitions remain unverified. The rebase used Git and source inspection only.

- Regression-only head `0ce1f2abfa` failed in both backend-core Actions shards for expected missing identity, early-result, duplicate, interleaved-result, retention and bound/overflow behavior. An unsupported interrupt fixture was removed after inspecting the unchanged mapper.
- Rebased head **`66e3f44c8313544f938b2cf9964de69f99009b00`**, based on canonical `main` **`1c3022d6dac0226126aa86f7d3610bc51bfefc3e`**: current-head Actions validation pending. All seven commits were replayed; the only manual resolution retained both main's PR-change detection helper and the Kimi approval helper in `cli/hooks.go`. Prior head `cc01a8f279` passed all 20 Actions checks; those results are historical, not validation of this rebased head.
- Coverage: eight-hook config, legacy migration/user-hook preservation/idempotence; shared derivation and CLI activity wire; scoped approval identity, reused tool calls and incomplete identity; Working → Waiting → Working → Idle; result-before-own-request; duplicates; request A/request B/result A/result B; result A before request A while B pending; ID-less guard; FIFO eviction/overflow; completion retention across Stop/new prompts; teardown, successful-spawn reset/old-launch fencing and daemon-restart limit; unchanged non-Kimi behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] Continued the existing feature branch and PR for #2814
- [x] Focused change with pinned native-source evidence and explicit limits
- [x] Before / After describes behavior; live execution gap disclosed
- [x] Regression coverage added
- [ ] Current-head GitHub Actions checks pass

title: feat(desktop): share cloud sessions with a short link
body:
Code changes: +50 -18\
Tests: +36 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The desktop shares a cloud session with a short link, `https://<cp>/s/<code>`, which opens `ao-app://share/<code>`. Today's link is `https://<cp>/app/share#<org-uuid>/<43-char token>`. Opening or pasting a short link redeems it by its code.

## Why

The current share link exposes the organization UUID and a long token, and is unwieldy to paste into chats and email. The control plane now mints a 12-character code per link (OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#15), so the desktop can share one short value instead.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Share → copies `https://api.aoagents.dev/app/share#<org-uuid>/<43-char token>` | Share → copies `https://api.aoagents.dev/s/k7Hq2x9PmB4w` (example code) |
| Opening a link redeems `{orgId, token}` | a code link (`…/s/<code>`, `ao-app://share/<code>`) redeems `{code}`; token links redeem as before |

Against a control plane without codes (no `code` in the create response), the dialog copies the token link exactly as before.

## How

- **`lib/share-links.ts`:**
  - `ShareLinkTarget` is now `{ code } | { orgId, token }`.
  - New `shareCodeLinkUrl(cp, code)`.
  - `parseShareLink` accepts `https://<cp>/s/<code>` and `ao-app://share/<code>`, where the code must be 12 letters or digits. Existing token forms still parse.
- **`ShareSessionDialog.tsx`:** new `createdShareLinkUrl` prefers the code and falls back to the token. It shows the existing "no token" error only when the response carries neither.
- **`OpenShareLinkDialog.tsx`:** new `redeemShareTarget` calls `redeemShareLinkCode(code)` or `redeemShareLink(orgId, token)`.
- **`lib/cloud-cp`:** `CloudCpShareLink.code?` and `redeemShareLinkCode`, which POSTs `{ code }` to the existing `/share-links/redeem`.
- **No main-process change:** `main.ts` already forwards any `ao-app://share…` URL to the renderer unchanged.
- **No contract change:** the project share endpoints aren't in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`; the control plane lists them as routes outside the contract.
- **Not changed:** the access model. A code is a bearer link like the token: roles, mode caps, expiry and revocation apply as before.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` (frontend): pass.
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/share-links.test.ts src/renderer/components/ShareSessionDialog.test.tsx src/renderer/components/OpenShareLinkDialog.test.ts src/renderer/test/shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx`: 86 passed. New cases:
  - code links build and parse (web and deep link, trailing slash, whitespace);
  - malformed codes are rejected;
  - the dialog copies the short link when there's a code and the token link otherwise;
  - redeem picks the code or token call.
- Not yet run end to end: needs ao-control-plane#15 deployed. Against production today the desktop falls back to the token link, which the tests above cover.

title: feat(testing): test PRs and reproduce issues in the real desktop app with ao testing
body:
Code changes: +11455 -23
Tests: +14666 -0
Others: +156 -0 (agent instructions, recipe, README) ## What this does Run `ao testing start ` and an AO agent tests it in the real desktop app, the way a person would. It clicks through the app, saves a screenshot after every action, and writes up what it found with pictures and short clips. - **PR:** builds the app before and after the change, then tries the new behavior. Result: pass, fail, partial or blocked. - **Issue:** builds today's main and tries to make the bug happen. Result: reproduced, not reproduced or blocked. ## Why A diff can't tell you whether a desktop change works, and most open issues never get re-checked by hand. This gives every PR and issue a real click-through test with proof attached. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart TD A["ao testing start + PR or issue link"] --> B["AO reads the PR or issue
and pins the exact commits"] B --> C["Builds the app twice:
before the change and after it"] C --> D["Opens each build with its own
private app data"] D --> E["Testing agent uses the app like a person:
clicks, types, changes settings and themes"] E --> F["Each action saves a screenshot
and the console log"] F --> G["Agent writes the verdict.
AO rejects findings with no screenshot behind them"] G --> H["Draft comment with pictures and clips"] H --> I{"Someone approves?"} I -- "yes: ao testing post" --> J["Posted on the PR or issue"] I -- no --> K["Nothing is posted"] ``` ## Example #7092 says the PR panel should follow whichever branch is checked out. The agent made its own test repo, switched branches, added `.ao/`-only and mixed changes, and checked the panel after each step. Verdict: pass, with a screenshot for every check. ## Rules the testing agent follows - Never runs the project's test suites, pushes code, or posts to GitHub by itself. - Never signs in, signs out or changes accounts, and stays off billing pages. - The builds AO made are read-only. Test repos it creates itself are fair game. - If the Mac sleeps mid-test, the time limit moves forward instead of failing the run. ## How it was checked 70+ runs on real open AO PRs and issues. A separate model graded each verdict against its screenshots; recent runs had two graders. ## Status Draft. Replaces #6568 and #6473 with a much smaller design. Rebased onto main on 2026-10-29.

title: feat(contract): describe the remote-host routes, with fixed addresses
body:
Code changes: +0 -0
Tests: +0 -0
Others: +536 -1 (contract, generated client types)

## What this changes

`contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` now describes AO Cloud's remote-host routes, which the desktop, the daemon and the phone already call:

| Route | Caller | New in this change |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/cloud/v1/me/hosts` | desktop, phone | `fixedAddresses` on the list |
| `PUT /api/cloud/v1/me/hosts/{hostId}` | desktop, phone | `url` may be left out; `409 fixed_address_limit_reached`, `429 tunnel_rate_limited`, `502 tunnel_unavailable` |
| `DELETE /api/cloud/v1/me/hosts/{hostId}` | desktop | — |
| `POST /api/cloud/v1/remote-hosts/{hostId}/address` | daemon | — |
| `POST /api/cloud/v1/remote-hosts/{hostId}/tunnel` | daemon | the whole route (`ensureRemoteHostTunnel`) |

The two machine routes use a new `hostDigest` scheme: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the machine's account token, hashed as its 64-character hex text. It is a bearer credential with no expiry, as strong on these routes as the account token, and not an account session. `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated with the pinned `openapi-typescript` 7.4.4.

## Why

Fixed remote-access addresses (#7294) add a route and fields between the apps and AO Cloud. The contract is the interface the control plane implements, so it lands first.

## Compatibility

Additive only: no route, field or status code an older client uses is removed or changed in shape. An older desktop keeps working against a newer control plane, and a newer desktop against an older one: it reads a missing `fixedAddresses` as false and links with `url` as before.

Two things an older client can now see:
- **New errors on a registration with `url`:** `429` and `502` when a new `token` retires a machine's fixed tunnel. Older clients show them as a failed link and can try again.
- **Fixed host names in `RemoteHost.url`:** older phones label such an address as a LAN address but put it first, so they still connect. #7411 labels it correctly.

## Testing

- The `breaking-changes` gate (`oasdiff` against `main`) runs in CI.
- The client types are regenerated with the pinned `openapi-typescript` 7.4.4, which `npm run cloud:check` verifies in CI.
- Each route's request body, status codes and headers were checked against the control-plane handlers. The empty-body 400 on `/tunnel` and the strict decoding on `PUT` and `/address` are now described.

## Merge order

1. This PR.
2. The control-plane PR that implements it, after `npm run contracts:sync` there.
3. #7294 (desktop and daemon) and the phone PR, in either order.

title: feat(mobile): treat AO Cloud's fixed addresses as stable tunnels
body:
Code changes: +40 -14
Tests: +54 -7
Others: +0 -0

## What this changes

AO Cloud can now give a signed-in computer a fixed address, `h-<hash>.<zone>`, that stays the same after restarts and sleep (#7294). This is the phone's half:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Account address `h-<hash>.useao.dev` | Filed as a LAN address, kept beside a pairing's dead quick address | Filed as a tunnel: it replaces the pairing's quick address |
| Account address on a LAN name, Tailscale, an IP literal or a custom domain | Filed as LAN (Tailscale IPs too) | Kept beside the pairing's tunnel; Tailscale IPs filed as Tailscale |
| A fixed address that fails | "Scan the new code" | "Offline", since only quick addresses rotate |
| Poll interval on a fixed address | The slower tunnel interval | The normal interval: fixed tunnels deliver the event stream |

Quick tunnels, LAN pairing, Tailscale and the account sync of manual pairings work as before.

## Why its own PR

The phone app is moving to its own repository. Keeping its changes apart from #7294 lets them move as one piece.

## Compatibility

Nothing here depends on a newer desktop or AO Cloud: with neither, the phone never sees an `h-` address, and every other address is handled as before. An older phone keeps working with a newer desktop: it tries every address it is given.

## Testing

- `accountHosts`, `staleTunnel`, `pollInterval` and `conversationPoll` tests cover the new classification and messages. The Mobile CI check runs them; the phone's dependencies are not installed on this machine.

## Merge order
