title: fix(chat): show one current Plan card and stop its spinner once the turn ends
body:
Code changes: +142 -36  
Tests: +277 -2  
Others: +49 -0 (generated sqlc query code, OpenAPI spec, `schema.ts`; hand-written, see Testing)

## What

Shows one Plan card per list at its newest state, and stops the step spinner once a turn has ended, failed or been stopped.

Part of #7159

## Why

Follow-up to #7173 from two new reports:

- **standalone-26 (Claude, idle).** The chat showed a 7/8 Plan card with a live spinner, then two 8/8 cards. Read-only DB check of conversation `d39e388c`: turn `a53b31f3` ended at 22:42:11 with a render running in the background. At 22:49 Claude resumed on its own, outside any AO turn, so its items (two tool calls, two `TaskUpdate` plan updates, the final answer) have no `turn_id`.
  1. `planItemID("")` returned `""`, so each plan update with no turn inserted a new row. Two updates gave two 8/8 cards.
  2. #7173's "latest copy wins" rule only compared turn plans, so the turn's 7/8 copy was never replaced by the later rows.
  3. `TurnPlan`'s step mark (#6884) spins any `in_progress` step whether or not the turn is still running.
- **agent-orchestrator-150.** A failed turn's 2/4 card kept spinning on an unfinished step (defect 3).

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Two plan updates outside any turn write two rows: two 8/8 cards, plus the turn's stale 7/8 card | One run of turnless updates rewrites one row in place: one card, at its newest state |
| A failed, stopped or finished turn's unfinished step keeps spinning | The step shows a still, faint ring; the arc shows only while the turn runs |

Screenshots from the desktop lab to follow.

## How

- **Backend: which copy is current.** When a list that spans turns is written, `SupersedeSpanningPlans` marks every other copy `superseded`, on turns (`plan_json`) and on plan rows (`detail_json`), in the same projection transaction. The copy just written is rewritten whole, so it is never marked. `ConversationPlanResponse` gains `superseded`.
- **Backend: turnless keys.** `planItemID` keys a plan with no turn per run of turnless work (`ao-plan-run-<id>`), held in the controller. The run ends when an event names a turn. One run's revisions rewrite one row, which keeps its place and id. `planDetail` writes `spansTurns` into the row.
- **Desktop and mobile** only read the flag: they hide a superseded plan row and a superseded turn checklist. The client-side dating of copies is gone. Plan rows without `spansTurns` (for example from provider turns AO never correlated) are separate plans and all show.
- **`TurnPlan`.** The arc shows only while the turn is live. It keeps turning while it fades out. On a settled turn an unfinished step shows the faint ring alone. A plan row no turn holds never spins: chat reports activity only around AO turns, so AO cannot tell when work outside a turn stops.

## Testing

- Go:
  - `TestTurnlessPlanRevisionsRewriteOneRowPerRun`: one run of turnless updates rewrites one row, including an update sent after the user dispatched B but before B started. A run after B gets its own row after B's reply. Only the newer row is current.
  - `TestSpanningPlanCopyWrittenLastIsCurrent`: a turnless copy supersedes turn A's copy. Turn B's copy then supersedes the turnless row, and A stays superseded.
  - `TestSuccessfulCompletionKeepsPlanThatSpansTurns` also checks the flag on the turn's row.
- Desktop vitest (`ChatWorkspaceProviderState.test.tsx`, `TurnPlan.test.tsx`): a superseded turn copy and a superseded row are hidden; the standalone-26 case shows one 4/4 card; unflagged rows all show; the arc is hidden on failed, interrupted and completed turns and shown while a turn runs.
- Mobile vitest (`timelineModel.test.ts`): superseded rows are hidden, unflagged rows are kept.
- The generated sqlc code, `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` were written by hand to match the generators, because the local disk was full. The api-drift and sqlc CI jobs verify them.
- The Go, desktop and mobile test suites were **not run locally**; CI verifies them.

## Branches and rollback

The current copy is decided over the active path only, using the timeline's branch and discarded-turn filters. Each cross-turn plan row records `writtenAt`, because one run's revisions rewrite one row in place. `ReconcileSpanningPlans` recomputes the marks after each plan write, when a branch is activated, and on rollback. Copies on other branches keep their marks until their branch becomes active again. Switching back to a branch shows its own current copy, and rolling back the turn holding the current copy makes the previous copy current.

## Known limits

- Copies stored before this change are repaired on upgrade by migration `20261103094403671_backfill_spanning_plan_copies`. It sets `spansTurns` on Claude's old plan rows and turn plans, using durable evidence: a turn plan the Claude driver already flagged, or Claude Code as the harness at the row's position (from `provider_switch` markers, falling back to the session's harness). It then marks every copy on each conversation's active path, except the latest, `superseded`. The latest copy is dated by when its content was written (a turnless row's `created_at`, a turn's `completed_at`), not `updated_at`, because settling and recovery also touch rows. Old plans from other agents are left alone. Review conversations are flagged only through the first rule. For legacy data, this ordering is a best guess. If a turnless row was written during a turn, after that turn's last plan revision, the turn's copy still wins, because it is dated at the turn's completion.
- AO gets no signal when Claude's work outside a turn stops. Two such runs with no turn between them share one row, at the first run's position.
- A current row that clears the list renders as a plain activity row on desktop and as an empty card on mobile, as before.

title: feat(onboarding): ask how new installs heard about Orchestrator and fix the onboarding funnel
body:
## Summary

Adds an optional first-run **"How did you hear about Orchestrator?"** step so we can see which channels bring installs. Also fixes the onboarding funnel telemetry: `welcome` had 0 `step_viewed` events because the home page, which is the real first-run landing, never reported it. Implements L4 from the telemetry audit (§3.2) and the onboarding rows in §4.2.

### What changed
- **Question step** (`components/onboarding/AttributionQuestion.tsx`) renders on the empty home page (and on the board welcome), after the welcome actions and before the GitHub sign-in notice. It is single-select: one click answers. **Skip** dismisses. There is no free-text box and nothing blocks. Options come from a closed enum (`shared/acquisition-channel.ts`): `x_twitter, youtube, friend_colleague, github, hacker_news, reddit, search, ai_assistant, newsletter_blog, conference_event, other`.
- **Persistence**: `~/.ao/app-state.json` gains `acq_channel_self_reported`.
  - Only a marker **created** by this build starts as `"pending"`. That means first-run installs are asked and existing installs (field absent) are never interrupted.
  - The value becomes the channel or `"skipped"` and is preserved on every launch write, so it is never asked again, including after updates.
  - New main-process IPC: `appState:getAcquisitionChannel` and `appState:recordAcquisitionChannel`. Recording validates against the enum and only succeeds while the value is still `pending`.
  - The Go `ao start` reader ignores the extra key.
- **Funnel fix**:
  - `HomePage` now reports the `welcome` step while it shows the no-projects Get started state. It completes the step when a project is added or a standalone agent starts, mirroring `BoardWelcome`.
  - `attribution` joins the step vocabulary.
  - A new `step_skipped` phase exists. Completed and skipped exclude each other, a finished step is never abandoned, and abandoning on one launch still allows a later completion.
- **Opt-out**: answering or skipping still works and is stored, but `captureRendererEvent` sends nothing when analytics are off.
- The daemon's common properties are untouched (coordinated with the install_source/first_open worker).
- New copy is translated into all 8 shipped locales. `docs/telemetry.md` has a new "Desktop onboarding" section.

### Telemetry events and properties
| Event | Change | Properties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ao.onboarding.attribution_answered` | **new**, once per install | `skipped` (bool), plus `channel` (enum above) only when answered |
| `ao.onboarding.step_skipped` | **new** | `step` |
| `ao.onboarding.step_viewed` / `_completed` / `_abandoned` | `step` now allows `welcome` (now actually fired from Home), **`attribution`**, `github_auth` | `step` |

All properties go through the renderer allowlist (`sanitizeRendererProperties`). Anything outside the enum is dropped, and the event carries no PII.

## Screenshots
First-run home with the question (dark / light), and the same page after answering:

| Dark | Light | After answering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/60fa42656b870bf6123a1bfc892d3fef71111ed7/home-dark.png) | ![light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/60fa42656b870bf6123a1bfc892d3fef71111ed7/home-light.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/60fa42656b870bf6123a1bfc892d3fef71111ed7/home-after-answer.png) |

These were captured with the Playwright renderer harness (`dev:web` + fake bridge, with `getAcquisitionChannel` returning `pending`). The same run clicked "Hacker News" and asserted that `recordAcquisitionChannel("hacker_news")` was called and the card disappeared.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- `npm test` (frontend): 597 files, 9,960 tests pass. New tests:
  - `app-state.test.ts`: pending only on marker creation, never for pre-existing markers, one answer per install, kept across updates and migration writes, enum enforced.
  - `AttributionQuestion.test.tsx`: options, no textbox, hidden for null/answered/skipped, answer, skip, no event when already recorded.
  - `onboarding-telemetry.test.tsx`: skipped-phase rules.
  - `telemetry.test.ts`: allowlist for `step_skipped`, the new steps and `attribution_answered`.
  - `_shell-index-home.test.tsx`: welcome reporting and completion; question placed after the welcome actions and before GitHub sign-in; hidden once projects exist.
- `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 132 passed and 1 failed (`chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts` "visibly selected with a pointer drag"). That spec fails the same way locally on unmodified `origin/main`, so it's a local environment issue unrelated to this change. Relying on CI for that job.

## Measuring impact in PostHog (project 475752)
- **Answer rate**: count `ao.onboarding.attribution_answered` where `skipped = false`, divided by `ao.onboarding.step_viewed` where `step = attribution`. Expect 40–70%.
- **Channel mix**: a trends insight on `ao.onboarding.attribution_answered` (filter `skipped = false`), broken down by `channel`, weekly. Compare spikes with X/YouTube/HN posting dates.
- **Onboarding funnel**: a funnel per install (`distinct_id`) of `step_viewed{welcome}` → `step_completed{welcome}` → `step_viewed{attribution}` → `attribution_answered` → `step_viewed{github_auth}` / `step_completed{github_auth}`. `welcome` should go from 0 to roughly one per new install.
- **Channel → activation**: a cohort per `channel` value of `attribution_answered`, joined to the activation proxy (≥3 `ao.session.spawned` in 7 days) and D7 retention. This feeds the planned `install_attribution` HogQL view (`self_reported_channel`).
- Only installs on this release or later are asked, so read rates from the release date forward.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Running an older build after this one rewrites the marker and drops the field. That install then won't be asked (the safe direction).
- Attaching `acq_channel_self_reported` to other events (e.g. via the daemon's common properties) is intentionally left to the install_source worker / a follow-up.

title: feat: pre-flight checks before agent spawns, with in-app fixes and spawn-failure codes
body: ## Why Growth research found that 8.1% of new installs never get a single successful session (Windows 9.6%). The top blocking causes in `ao.session.spawn_failed` are `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` (~1.1k installs), `AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND` (~1.0k) and `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` (~0.7k). `ao.renderer.orchestrator_spawn_failed` (~3.9k installs) carried no error code at all. Today these show up as a failed spawn with a raw daemon message and no next step. **Success metric:** % of new installs hard-blocked (no successful session in week 1), currently **8.1%**, target **under 4%**. ## What changed **Daemon: `POST /api/v1/sessions/preflight`** (new `internal/service/spawnpreflight`). It checks a prospective spawn without creating any session, worktree or runtime. Each check reuses the detection the spawn path itself uses: - **Agent installed and signed in:** the launch-purpose agent readiness check (`EnsureAgentReadiness`). A re-check invalidates the cached install and auth observations first, so it never answers from before the fix. - **Runtime prerequisite:** the session manager's tmux check, refactored into `sessionmanager.RuntimePrerequisiteError(goos, …)` so the spawn and the pre-flight cannot disagree. Only TUI launches on macOS need tmux. The pre-flight mirrors the spawn's Chat→TUI fallback to decide. - **Default branch:** the same `ResolveDefaultBranch` call the spawn's branch refresh makes, for the root repo and each workspace child repo. Only an authoritative "unresolved" counts. A timed-out probe is unknown and never blocks. - **Harness resolution:** the same role-override resolution as `Spawn`. A project with no orchestrator agent reports `agent_required`, exactly as the spawn would fail with `AGENT_REQUIRED`. Each blocker carries an OS-specific, copyable fix command: - Agent install commands come from a new `systeminstall.AgentInstallCommand`. It uses the same planner as the installer catalog and skips downloaded-script installers, whose display form names the script rather than a runnable line. Those harnesses get only the setup guide. - Sign-in commands come from the existing agent auth plans. - The tmux command comes from `systeminstall.Resolve(goos, …)`. Each check also reports `canInstall` and `canStartLogin`, from the same viability the installer and auth plans use. A signed-out probe blocks only Codex, mirroring the spawn, which itself refuses only a signed-out Codex. For other harnesses it is a soft check with **Start anyway**. **Renderer:** `ensureSpawnPreflight` runs before every local orchestrator spawn (`spawnOrchestrator` and the project-add auto-spawn in `_shell.tsx`) and before project worker tasks (`TaskComposer`). Remote hosts spawn unchecked. A pre-flight that cannot run, or that answers malformed, never blocks. When blocked, one shared **SpawnPreflightDialog** opens with: - the exact install, sign-in or tmux command for this OS, with **Copy command** and a setup-guide link; - **Use another installed agent**: a picker of agents that are ready on this machine. For an orchestrator the choice is saved to the project config (`orchestrator.agent`). For a worker it applies only to this task; - a **Default branch** field that saves `defaultBranch` to the project config; - **Install**, when AO can run the installer itself. It uses the existing install job (`POST /agents/{agent}/install` with the recommended method, or `POST /system/install/tmux`) and re-checks automatically when the job succeeds. On failure, the job's error is shown and the copyable command remains; - **Sign in**, when the harness has a reviewed terminal login. It opens that login (the same `POST /agents/{agent}/auth` terminal Settings uses, reusing `HarnessAuthTerminalPanel`) embedded in the dialog. When the terminal exits it closes and the pre-flight re-checks on its own. A login terminal still open when the dialog is dismissed is closed; - **Check again**, which re-checks against the daemon without restarting the app, and starts the spawn as soon as the check passes. Dismissing the dialog cancels the start. No spawn runs, so no `*_spawn_failed` event or replacement-error dialog follows. New UI copy is translated into all eight shipped locales (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, zh-CN). ## Telemetry All new values are fixed enums. No commands, paths, branch names or messages are sent. Both events respect the existing opt-out and per-event allowlists (daemon `remotePayloadAllowlist`, renderer `sanitizeRendererProperties`). Documented in `docs/telemetry.md` ("Session start checks"), and listed as low-volume in `docs/posthog-cost-controls.md`. | Event | Properties | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `ao.session.preflight_checked` (new, daemon) | `result` (`pass`/`blocked`), `blockers` (sorted, comma-joined enum list), `blocker_count`, `harness`, `kind` | One per check and re-check | | `ao.session.preflight_resolved` (new, daemon) | `blocker`, `method` (`install`/`login`/`switch_agent`/`set_default_branch`/`recheck`), `harness`, `kind` | One per blocker a re-check no longer reports | | `ao.renderer.orchestrator_spawn_failed` (changed) | adds `error_code` (daemon code, or `REQUEST_FAILED`), `harness`, `kind` | `error_code` must match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$`. `harness` must be a known agent id | Blocker codes: `agent_not_installed`, `agent_unauthorized`, `runtime_prerequisite_missing`, `default_branch_unresolved`, `agent_required`. Telemetry values must be scalars, hence the comma-joined `blockers`. ## Measuring impact in PostHog (project 475752) After release, compare cohorts of installs first seen after the release with the Aug 1–Oct 20 baseline (8.1%), using the same bot-filtered cohort definition as the growth report. 1. **Hard-blocked installs (primary metric):** new installs with no `ao.session.spawned` within 7 days of first seen, among installs with at least one `ao.renderer.orchestrator_spawn_requested` or `ao.session.preflight_checked`. Break down by renderer `platform` (join on `install_id`; daemon events have no `$os`). Target is under 4%, and Windows under 5%. 2. **Pre-flight funnel:** `preflight_checked` with `result = 'blocked'` → `preflight_resolved` → `ao.session.spawned` for the same `install_id` within 1 day. ```sql SELECT properties.blockers AS blockers, count(DISTINCT properties.install_id) AS installs FROM events WHERE event = 'ao.session.preflight_checked' AND properties.result = 'blocked' AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY GROUP BY blockers ORDER BY installs DESC ``` 3. **What fixes work:** `ao.session.preflight_resolved` broken down by `blocker` × `method`. A high `switch_agent` share means people prefer an agent they already have over installing one. 4. **Residual spawn failures:** `ao.renderer.orchestrator_spawn_failed` broken down by `error_code` and `harness`. `AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND`, `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` and `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` should fall sharply. Remaining codes are the next targets. 5. **Guardrail:** `ao.session.spawned` per install should not drop. A drop would mean the pre-flight is blocking spawns that would have worked. ## Screenshots These come from this branch's renderer (`dev:web`) driving this branch's daemon against scratch data. The project's remote cannot resolve and its orchestrator agent (Auggie) is not installed. After saving `main` as the default branch, the re-check clears that blocker: The agent picker lists only agents that are ready on this machine: ## How I verified it - **Go:** new tests in `spawnpreflight` (each blocker; Windows, macOS and Linux runtime gating; per-OS tmux command; stale or failed probes never block; branch-probe timeout is unknown; resolution events emitted only for cleared, known blockers; re-check invalidates readiness), `session_manager` (`RuntimePrerequisiteError` per OS; `PreflightSpawn` harness, mode and branch facts), `systeminstall` (`AgentInstallCommand` on darwin, linux and windows; never a script placeholder), controller route tests, and the PostHog allowlist test. `go test` passes for `./internal/httpd/...`, `spawnpreflight`, `systeminstall`, `daemon`, `adapters/telemetry`, and the new `session_manager` tests. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 reports 0 issues on the touched packages. `npm run api` regenerated `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`. - **Renderer:** new `SpawnPreflightDialog.test.tsx` (Windows, macOS and Linux fix commands with copy; re-check reports the copied fix as `method`; still-blocked re-check; orchestrator vs worker agent switch; default-branch save and save failure; Start anyway only for soft checks; Escape cancels), `spawn-preflight.test.ts` (gate, remote skip, unavailable or malformed pre-flight proceeds, cancellation, config writes), and `spawnOrchestrator` and sanitizer tests for the new failure properties. `npm run typecheck` passes, and `npm test` passes in full (598 files). - **End to end:** this branch's daemon on scratch data. `POST /orchestrators` on a project without an orchestrator agent fails with `AGENT_REQUIRED`, and the pre-flight reports `agent_required` for the same project. In the UI, the dialog appeared, saving the branch cleared that blocker, and dismissing the dialog made no `POST /orchestrators`. ## Known risks and follow-ups - **Extra request per start:** each start adds one pre-flight request. The default-branch probe may contact the remote (bounded at 15s, and a timeout never blocks). The spawn already performs the same resolution. - **Host-dependent test failures:** a few existing `session_manager`/`systemcheck`/`tmux` tests fail on a macOS host with a live AO session. They fail identically on `origin/main` there, so they are unrelated to this change. - **`dev:web` against a real daemon:** loading credential routes such as `/agents/readiness` through `dev:web` needed a local shim that stamps the allowed `Origin`. That is a dev-tooling limitation, not changed here. - **Not in this PR:** a branch picker (there is no project-level branch-list route yet), so the dialog has a branch field. GitHub sign-in is not part of the pre-flight, so an authenticated `gh` is never prompted for. Missing git is already handled by the existing startup requirements gate, which has install actions. - **Screenshots predate Install and Sign in:** they show the copy-command version of the dialog. The new buttons sit above the command. The Install and Sign in flows are covered by renderer tests, not by a new live run. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Fixes #3944.

title: feat(telemetry): segment by OS, arch and install source; add first_open and durable firsts
body:
Code changes: +870 -34  
Tests: +798 -0  
Others: +26 -1

## Summary

Growth can't currently be segmented by OS or acquisition source. Per the telemetry audit (§1.5), daemon/CLI events (~60% of volume) carry no `$os` or arch, and the `installSource` recorded in `~/.ao/app-state.json` is never sent. `ao.app.installed` undercounts: it only fires when the install id file is under 24h old at daemon start and no tenure file exists, which gave 771 events against ~1,800 first-seen ids in one week. `ao.onboarding.first_session_spawned` fires again whenever the sessions table is empty.

This PR adds the missing segmentation, a reliable first-run event, and durable "first" flags.

### What changed

**Daemon common properties** (`backend/internal/adapters/telemetry/environment.go`, stamped in `PostHogSink.properties`). These go on every exported daemon/CLI event:
- `$os` / `$os_version`: names and values match posthog-js (`Mac OS X` / `Windows` / `Linux`). The version is the real product version (macOS `kern.osproductversion`, Windows `RtlGetVersion`, Linux kernel release), restricted to a version-shaped pattern.
- `platform` / `arch`: Node's values (`darwin|win32|linux`, `arm64|x64`), the same as the renderer.
- `release_channel`: read from `~/.ao/update-settings.json`, mapped the same way as the renderer's `releaseChannelFrom` (`stable|nightly|feature|unknown`).
- `install_source` and `installed_at`: read from `~/.ao/app-state.json`. `installed_at` is coarsened to the UTC day.
- `is_ci` (bool) plus `ci_signal` (`ci_env|container`): detected from `CI` (honouring `CI=false`), common CI provider env vars, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, `container`, `/.dockerenv` and `/run/.containerenv`. `ci_signal` lets a dashboard drop CI runs while deciding separately about dev containers, which can be real people.
- The file-backed values are cached for 5 minutes, so a channel switch shows up without a daemon restart.

**Desktop**
- `frontend/src/shared/install-environment.ts` defines the `install_source` enum: `npm-bootstrap | dmg | brew-cask | exe | appimage | deb | rpm | dev | unknown`, and anything off-list is sent as `other`. The Go side has the same list.
  - Detection works from the running bundle: a Caskroom receipt means `brew-cask`, otherwise macOS is `dmg`; NSIS means `exe`; the `APPIMAGE` env var means `appimage`; a dpkg record means `deb`; `/usr/...` without a dpkg record means `rpm`; unpackaged builds are `dev`.
  - `--installed-via` still wins on first creation, and recorded values stay sticky. The one exception: a recorded `unknown` is refined by a detected format, because builds before this change recorded every non-npm install as `unknown`.
- `app-state.ts` now carries through keys it doesn't own on every launch write. That keeps it compatible with agent-orchestrator-165's `acq_channel_self_reported`, which the old writer would have dropped on the next launch. The exception is `updateRestartProtocol`: it's still not inherited from a newer build.
- The renderer gets the same `arch`, `install_source`, `installed_at`, `is_ci`, `ci_signal`, plus the real `$os_version` (Chromium freezes macOS at 10.15.7 in its UA). These come through the telemetry bootstrap.

**`ao.app.first_open`** (new). The daemon emits it once per install id on any build. The marker `~/.ao/data/telemetry_first_open_emitted` holds the install id, so installs that predate `ao.app.installed` are covered too.
- An opted-out install reserves nothing, so the event goes out after the user opts back in.
- It is only reserved when a PostHog remote is actually configured, so a local-only run doesn't use up the single send.

**`first_for_install`** on `ao.session.spawned` and `ao.projects.created`:
- Based on O_EXCL markers `telemetry_first_session_spawned` / `telemetry_first_project_added` (new `ports.InstallMilestones`).
- True only when the marker is newly claimed **and** there were no prior rows. That way an install upgraded from a build without markers never reports its next session as its first.
- `ao.onboarding.first_session_spawned` / `first_project_added` are unchanged and documented as deprecated.

**`launcher`** (`desktop|cli`, from `AO_OWNER`) is on `ao.app.installed` and `ao.app.first_open`. The common `client` stays `cli` for every daemon event, so existing dashboards don't shift.

### Telemetry events and properties

| Event | Change |
|---|---|
| all daemon/CLI events | + `$os`, `$os_version`, `platform`, `arch`, `release_channel`, `install_source`, `installed_at`, `is_ci`, `ci_signal` |
| all desktop renderer events | + `arch`, `install_source`, `installed_at`, `is_ci`, `ci_signal`; `$os_version` corrected |
| `ao.app.first_open` | **new**: once per install id; `launcher` + common props |
| `ao.app.installed` | + `launcher` (common props now include `install_source`, `$os`, `arch`) |
| `ao.session.spawned` | + `first_for_install` |
| `ao.projects.created` | + `first_for_install` |
| `ao.onboarding.first_session_spawned`, `ao.onboarding.first_project_added` | deprecated (unchanged, kept for continuity) |

Privacy:
- The common props are set by the sink and appear in no per-event payload allowlist, so a payload can't override them. A test enforces this.
- New payload keys (`launcher`, `first_for_install`) were added to the allowlists of exactly the events above.
- No free text, paths, emails or usernames: `install_source` is an enum, `installed_at` is a day, the OS version is pattern-checked, and CI detection sends only a bool and a category.
- Opt-out is honoured as before: the sink is suppressed, and `first_open` is not reserved while opted out.
- `docs/telemetry.md` is updated.

Coordination: this doesn't implement the onboarding attribution question (agent-orchestrator-165). The only touchpoint is that app-state launch writes now preserve their `acq_channel_self_reported` key.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Daemon events lacked OS, architecture, and install source; first milestones could repeat after rows were removed. | Events carry bounded install context and durable first flags; a first open is reserved per install ID. |

## Handoff verification (2026-10-30)

Exact head b96b60a0b83f994a56812f63baf8fc461bc54c2f. All reported GitHub checks succeeded. Focused local telemetry adapter and project service Go tests passed. Full local suite could not be certified in this sandbox. The CI and container classification is deferred to #7471.

## Verification

- **New tests**
  - Go: CI/container detection, OS/arch naming parity, OS-version and install-source sanitising, install-context file reads and TTL refresh, release-channel mapping, segmentation on sink properties, the "allowlists can't carry common props" check, milestone claims, and `MarkFirstOpenEvent` (once per id, opt-out, replaced id).
  - Daemon lifecycle wiring: first start, then restart, then a local-only run.
  - Session and project `first_for_install`: durable vs table-empty, an upgraded install with prior rows, and the nil case.
  - Frontend: installer detection on every platform, `resolveInstallSource` stickiness and refinement, key preservation in app-state, the bootstrap install reader, and the renderer context.
- **Local suite results**
  - `go build`, `go vet` (darwin/linux/windows) and `golangci-lint` all pass with 0 issues.
  - `go test ./...` passes except three tests that fail the same way on clean `origin/main` on this machine: `integration/TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch`, `commandcode/TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders`, `opencodev2/TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects`. They depend on the local git config and the installed OpenCode version. This needs `AO_*` session env vars unset.
  - `tsgo --noEmit` is clean.
  - vitest: 596/597 files pass. The one failing file is `browser-profile-import.test.ts`, because better-sqlite3's native binding wasn't built locally (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`).
- **End to end**
  - Setup: I ran the built `ao daemon` with an isolated data dir and pointed PostHog at a local capture server, seeding `app-state.json` (`dmg`, plus an extra `acq_channel_self_reported` key) and `update-settings.json` (`nightly`).
  - Every event arrived with `$os: Mac OS X`, `$os_version: 26.5`, `platform: darwin`, `arch: arm64`, `release_channel: nightly`, `install_source: dmg`, `installed_at: 2026-10-27`, `is_ci: false`, and the app-state extra key was not exported.
  - The first start sent `ao.app.installed` and `ao.app.first_open` (`launcher: desktop`). Adding a project sent `ao.projects.created` with `first_for_install: true`. After a restart, only `ao.daemon.started` was sent.

## Measuring impact in PostHog (project 475752)

After release, filter to `app_version >= <this release>`.

1. **OS coverage of daemon events**: Trends on `ao.v2.app.active` (or all events) where `client = cli`, broken down by `$os`. The share of `$os is not set` should drop from ~100% to ~0% on new versions. Break down by `arch` for the Apple Silicon/x64 split.
2. **Acquisition source**: Trends of unique `install_id` on `ao.app.first_open`, broken down by `install_source`, weekly. `npm-bootstrap` vs `dmg` vs `brew-cask` vs `exe`/`appimage`/`deb`/`rpm` is the channel mix. `unknown` should shrink as desktops relaunch and refine it.
3. **First-run undercount fixed**: Compare weekly unique `install_id` of `ao.app.first_open` against `ao.app.installed`. `first_open` should be ≥ installed and track first-seen ids (~1,800/week rather than ~771). During the first weeks it also includes upgraded old installs firing once, so judge from week 3 on, or restrict to `installed_at` within the week.
4. **Exclude CI fleets**: add a global filter `is_ci != true` to the DAU/WAU dashboard. Compare DAU with and without it, and check the size of `ci_signal = ci_env` vs `container`.
5. **Activation funnel on durable firsts**: funnel `ao.app.first_open` → `ao.projects.created` (`first_for_install = true`) → `ao.session.spawned` (`first_for_install = true`), broken down by `install_source` and `$os`. This replaces funnels built on the deprecated `ao.onboarding.first_*` events. Expect a lower (truer) first-session count than `first_session_spawned`.
6. Desktop/CLI split of new installs: break down `ao.app.first_open` by `launcher`.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Container detection also flags dev containers; dashboards should key on `ci_signal = ci_env` if those users should be kept.
- deb/rpm detection is heuristic: `rpm` is "under `/usr` without a dpkg record". If neither signal is present, the install records `unknown`.
- Upgraded installs that deleted all their sessions/projects before upgrading will report one false `first_for_install = true`.

title: fix(desktop): give the macOS dmg a real install window layout
body: ## Summary The macOS DMG now opens as a compact, on-brand drag-to-Applications window instead of a large blank one: - 660x400 window with 128pt icons, the app on the left and Applications on the right - the agent harnesses Orchestrator runs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, opencode, Goose, Aider, Grok), floating as small tilted tiles in the margins - one tapered ink arrow as the drag cue, with an italic "drag to Applications" on the labels' baseline - the app icon as the volume icon, and the volume named **"Orchestrator"** A build/CI gate fails if a DMG ever loses that layout again. The `.app` keeps its "Agent Orchestrator" name in this PR (see "Rename" below). The published DMG only changes once the conductor follow-up, **OrchestratorInc/ao-releases#49**, merges after this PR (see "Rollout"). | | Before (published v0.14.7) | After | |---|---|---| | Dark appearance | | | | Light appearance | | | Real Finder windows captured on macOS 26.5. The image is mounted read-only, and only that window is captured, then closed and detached. "After" is this branch's builder run on the app from a local unsigned `electron-forge make`. ## Root cause The published DMG is **not built by `MakerDMG`** at all. - `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml`, the public unsigned build the conductor dispatches, uploads only the `.zip` for darwin. The `MakerDMG` output never leaves the runner. - The private conductor (`OrchestratorInc/ao-releases` `_pipeline.yml`, stable only) signs, notarizes and staples the app, then wraps it with `ditto` + `ln -s /Applications` + `hdiutil create -srcfolder`. That copies the folder verbatim: nothing writes a `.DS_Store` (window size, icon positions, background) or a background image, so Finder uses its defaults. The wrap has to happen there because the DMG must enclose the *stapled* app, and a read-only image can't be re-signed. - It isn't the buildForge bridge, the dmg options, headless CI or `sealDmg`. electron-builder 26's dmg target (bundled `dmgbuild`) writes `.DS_Store` headlessly, with no Finder or AppleScript. A local `MakerDMG` image already had one, just with electron-builder's generic template, 80pt icons and a `" -"` volume name. The new check, run on the published v0.14.7 image: ``` agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg has no usable install window layout: - missing .VolumeIcon.icns - expected one background image, found 0 - missing .DS_Store (Finder will show the default window) ``` ## Changes - **`frontend/scripts/build-mac-dmg.mjs`**: one layout definition and two entry points: - `--app --arch --output ` wraps an existing app via app-builder-lib's `buildForge`, with the same settings as `MakerDMG`: `mac.identity: null` (never re-signs the app), `dmg.sign: false`, `writeUpdateInfo: false`, `publish: null`. It then runs the check. The conductor calls this (ao-releases#49). - `--check ` mounts `hdiutil attach -readonly -nobrowse -noautoopen` under a private mount root and asserts: - `.DS_Store` holds Iloc positions for both items, a picture background and 128pt icons (icvp), and 660x400 window bounds (bwsp). - Exactly one background image, a HiDPI TIFF with the 1320x800 Retina representation. - `.VolumeIcon.icns`, the `.app`, and an `Applications → /Applications` symlink. It always detaches. dmgbuild stores the background as a hidden `.background.tiff` at the volume root, so the check accepts that or `.background/`. - **`makers/maker-dmg.ts`**: spreads `macDmgLayout()` into the dmg config. Signing options, the blockmap filter, artifact names and the `MakerDMGConfig.dmg` override order are unchanged. The volume name is "Orchestrator". - **`forge.config.ts` postMake** runs `checkMacDmgLayout` on every DMG before `sealDmg`/`verifyDmg`, so `npm run make` on macOS (including `build-artifacts.yml`) fails on a layout regression. `sealDmg`, `verifyDmg` and the zip verification are untouched. - **Background art** (`assets/dmg/background.svg` → `background.png` 660x400 + `background@2x.png` 1320x800, regenerated by `scripts/render-dmg-background.mjs` on macOS): - Near-white paper (`#fbfbfc`), so Finder draws the labels black and they stay legible. - Nine harness tiles in the margins. They reference the renderer's own logo files in `src/renderer/assets/agents/`, so the art tracks the product's logo set. - One tapered ink arrow between the icons, plus "drag to Applications" in italic New York on the labels' baseline. - The image sets the window **frame**, so the title bar hides the bottom ~32pt. Icons sit at y=184, centred in the visible area, and a test keeps all art inside it. - **Volume name** is now "Orchestrator" (`VOLUME_NAME`). Nothing looks the volume up by name; the relocation logic is path-generic. - **App icon regenerated** (`assets/icon.icns`, also the volume icon): - The old file stored its 16x16/32x32 sizes as PNG in the legacy `icp4`/`icp5` slots, which Finder decodes as noise. That showed up in the DMG's title bar, and likely wherever macOS draws the app at 16px. - It's rebuilt with `iconutil` from the PNGs already embedded in it, so every size keeps its exact artwork while 16/32px move to `ic04`/`ic05`. - Verified in a real Finder title bar. A test fails if `icp4`/`icp5` come back or a size goes missing; it fails on the old file and passes on the new one. - **Label legibility (measured, not assumed)**: Finder draws icon labels **black over this light background in both Light and Dark appearance** (see the captures). It picks label colour from the background, not the system appearance, so no label treatment is needed. - **CI**: new `mac-dmg-layout` job (macos-latest, in the `test` gate). It builds a real DMG around a fixture app with the script, then checks that a bare `hdiutil create -srcfolder` image is **rejected** and that nothing stays mounted. - **Tests**: - `makers/maker-dmg.test.ts`: layout options, and that the signing options survive the merge. - `forge.config.test.ts`: the layout check runs before sealing and stops the build when it fails. - `scripts/build-mac-dmg.test.mjs` (app icon): `icon.icns` is the volume icon and carries every size, with 16/32px in `ic04`/`ic05`. - `scripts/build-mac-dmg.test.mjs`: - the arrow starts past the app icon and lands before the folder - every harness tile stays clear of both icons and labels, inside the visible area, and points at a logo file that exists - all art stays inside the visible area - exact 1x/2x PNG sizes - `.DS_Store` record parsing - rejection of the bare-image shape - builder argument validation and options ## Verification - `npm run typecheck`: passes. - `vitest` for `makers/`, `forge.config.test.ts` and `scripts/build-mac-dmg.test.mjs`: 96/96 pass. - CI on the previous head was fully green, including `mac-dmg-layout` on the GitHub macOS runner. - **Real unsigned local build** (`electron-forge make --arch arm64`, Node 24): produced `out/make/Agent Orchestrator-0.13.0-arm64.dmg` and the `.zip` with unchanged names and no blockmap. postMake printed `[dmg] layout ok`, then `sealDmg` took its unsigned no-op path. - **The seal survives the builder**: I wrapped a copy of an installed, Developer ID–signed, notarized, stapled build (0.14.8-nightly). Inside the mounted image the app passes: - `codesign --verify --deep --strict`: valid - `xcrun stapler validate`: worked - `spctl -a -vv -t exec`: `source=Notarized Developer ID` - `diff -r` against the source: identical, with framework symlinks preserved The image is 245 MB vs 296 MB for v0.14.7 (UDZO level 9). - Not verified here: signing and notarizing the new container. That needs the conductor's credentials, and its existing `codesign` → `notarytool` → `stapler` → `verify-mac-artifact.sh` steps apply unchanged. ## Rollout **OrchestratorInc/ao-releases#49** replaces the conductor's stage + `hdiutil create` with `node public/frontend/scripts/build-mac-dmg.mjs --app "$app" --arch "$arch" --output "$dmg_path"`. Merge it only after this PR is on the public `stable` branch. The conductor runs the script from the release ref, so a ref without it fails the stable sign job loudly rather than shipping a bare DMG. ## Windows NSIS installer report (no changes in this PR) `makers/maker-nsis.ts` builds an **assisted** (`oneClick: false`), per-user-default installer with shortcuts. It is functionally sensible but **unbranded**: - **Flow**: install-mode page ("Only for me" / "Anyone who uses this computer", since `perMachine: false`) → choose directory → progress → Finish with a "Run" checkbox. There is no welcome or license page. Desktop and Start-menu shortcuts are created. - **Imagery**: no `installerSidebar`, `installerHeader` or `installerHeaderIcon`, and no `build/` resources dir. The Finish page and the uninstaller's welcome/finish pages fall back to NSIS's stock `nsis3-metro.bmp` sidebar, and the other pages have no header image. Only the icon is branded (`assets/icon.ico`). - **Naming**: the wizard, shortcuts and Apps list say **"Orchestrator.inc"** (`productName`), while the file is `Agent Orchestrator Setup .exe` and macOS ships "Agent Orchestrator". - **Suggested follow-up**: - A 164x314 `installerSidebar.bmp` and `uninstallerSidebar.bmp` and a 150x57 `installerHeader.bmp`, in the same restrained style. - Optionally a short welcome page. - I couldn't produce Windows screenshots: there's no Windows host or VM on this machine. ## Rename to "Orchestrator" Agreed to do this as a separate PR. The label under the icon is the `.app` filename, and `Agent Orchestrator.app` is looked up by name in several places: - `ao start` (`backend/internal/cli/start.go`) - stale-copy cleanup - the updater's relocation logic - the repair installer's guard - docs and e2e Auto-updates also install over the existing path, so current users keep the old name. The follow-up renames the bundle and teaches those lookups to accept both names. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(telemetry): extend #7304's usage counts and add session outcomes (telemetry v2)
body:
Code changes: +1284 -57  
Tests: +1527 -26  
Others: +186 -10

## What

Extend #7304's durable usage telemetry with human send surfaces, worker PR outcomes, session outcome facts, and a stable experiment cohort. This existing PR now targets `main` directly. Its net diff contains #7420 work only; #7417 was squash merged separately.

- Add `steer_count`, `send_count`, `desktop_count`, `mobile_count`, `cli_count`, `kind`, and `harness` to `ao.usage.messages_sent`. `count` keeps its original direct human Chat meaning. Standalone messages remain excluded by #7304's project usage query.
- Add `created_by` (`user`, `orchestrator`, `scheduled`, `automation`) and request `surface` to `ao.session.spawned`. `created_by` is the sole reason started property and is persisted for session outcomes.
- Emit `ao.sessions.ended` once for a real session end with bounded `outcome`, `duration_ms`, `had_pr`, `waiting_input_count`, and known creator. It joins project message batches through the existing privacy safe grouping IDs. A durable SQLite claim only succeeds after the session row is terminal, preventing duplicate outcomes across concurrent end paths and restarts. Clean orchestrator replacement also reports the old session, including a cleanup failure after termination.
- Extend worker PR associations and merges with bounded kind, harness, provider, timing, review, and first for install facts. Emit `ao.prs.closed` for a PR closed without merging. New outcomes are one event per PR; historical backfill stays grouped. Durable reservation and opt out behavior remain in place.
- Record `merged_via` from the actual AO merge surface as `desktop`, `mobile`, or `cli`; externally observed GitHub merges use `github`. Unknown external surfaces omit the property.
- Use one shared `telemetrymeta.SessionKind(kind, projectID)` helper across session and usage events. It reports `standalone` when `rec.IsStandalone()` and otherwise the stored kind. #7471 can reuse this helper after #7420 lands.
- Persist one 0 to 99 `experiment_cohort` value per installation for daemon and desktop events.
- Update the event allowlists, denylist coverage, queue handling, rate limits, and telemetry docs for the new names and properties.

## Why

The durable counts in #7304 answer how often AO is used. These additions show where human activity occurs and whether worker sessions and PRs deliver, without exporting message text, PR text, repository names, or unverified outcome facts.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Human messages and PRs had coarse durable totals. | The same durable rows carry source and outcome detail with bounded values. |
| Session endings had no bounded product event. | `ao.sessions.ended` reports real termination facts and a millisecond duration. |
| A CLI merge was labeled `other`; phone merges were labeled `mobile_swipe`. | Merge sources use `desktop`, `mobile`, `cli`, or `github` when known. |
| A standalone worker could appear with kind `worker`. | Session events use `standalone` for records without a project. |

## How

The daemon derives request surfaces and stores counts at the existing insertion and PR observation boundaries. The flusher reserves each usage fact before export. It discards pending usage on opt out, keeps historical facts grouped, and omits unknown properties rather than inventing values. The remote sink admits only per event allowed fields and validates grouping IDs and `merged_via` values.

## Testing

- Exact local head: `48f6ba7824b3ee590f95245d738934f580687be5`; base main: `be4259d4fa281c6194f3acf24f8b12323aa750e7`.
- Passed after main integration: `go test` for telemetrymeta, deliverytelemetry, daemon, session service, telemetry adapter, SQLite store, PR service, and lifecycle; `go build ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `npm run frontend:typecheck`; `git diff --check`.
- `npm run sqlc` regenerated the session telemetry model from the final migration; SQLite, store, recorder tests and `go build ./...` pass after the generated field fix.
- Durable claim tests cover live row rejection, concurrent callers, and persistence across database reopen. Replacement tests cover success, cleanup failure after termination, and failure before termination.
- A canceled request regression test confirms all post termination fact reads use a bounded, cancellation independent context and still emit the complete outcome. The delivery telemetry, session service, lifecycle, and daemon suites passed after this fix.
- The broad `go test ./...` run could not pass in this local host. Its e2e and HTTP tests could not bind loopback ports in the sandbox; live OpenCode discovery could not write its log; an OpenCode v2 test found the installed 1.x binary; persistent ACP process tests failed to start their host. It was stopped after these unrelated environment failures. Remote exact head CI is the remaining full suite evidence.
- Previous revision verification included focused frontend telemetry tests and the cohort restart capture check. Those were not rerun after this Go only follow up.

## Checklist

- [x] Existing PR and history preserved; no replacement PR or force push.
- [x] #7417 implementation absent from the net diff against main.
- [x] Consent, opt out, privacy allowlists, stable install identity, and #7304 durable dedup preserved.
- [x] New event names, enum values, duration unit, and standalone behavior covered by tests.
- [ ] Required exact head CI and an independent human approval before a normal squash merge.

## Known limits

Cue invocations and side Chat questions are not included in human message counts. Local API calls without a browser origin use `cli`. Sessions created before this release omit `created_by`; their waiting input count starts at upgrade. The broader old style event rename is separate work and is not included here.

title: feat: remote What's new card and a notifications onboarding step
body:
Code changes: +1092 -15  
Tests: +744 -4  
Others: +247 -10 (generated OpenAPI/schema, 9 locale catalogs, docs, feed.json)

## What

Two "come back" surfaces for the desktop app, plus the missing "agent finished" notification they rely on.

**1. Notifications step in onboarding** (`NotificationsStep`, shown after the GitHub step on Home and the board welcome)
- Explains that Orchestrator notifies you when an agent finishes, opens a PR, or needs input.
- **Turn on notifications** sends a real test toast through a new `notifications:test` IPC. On macOS the first toast also raises the system permission prompt. Electron has no permission query, so the main process reads the toast's `show` / `failed` events and returns `granted` / `denied` / `unsupported` / `unknown`.
- When notifications are blocked, it says so and offers **Open System Settings**, which opens the app's Notifications pane on macOS or `ms-settings:notifications` on Windows. Both URLs are added to the exact-match external-URL allowlist.
- **Send test notification**, **Done** and **Skip** buttons. Only installs that saw the step during first-run onboarding get it. If such a user leaves by adding a project, the step returns on Home until they finish or skip it. Existing installs never see it.

**2. Remote What's new card + version-targeted nudges**
- The main process (`src/main/whats-new.ts`) fetches `https://docs.orchestrator.inc/whats-new/feed.json` at most once per launch and at most once per day, about 5 seconds after startup. The request carries no cookies, identifiers, or app version (`credentials: "omit"`, only an `Accept` header, no redirects). It caches the feed in `~/.ao/whats-new.json`. Any failure (offline, HTTP error, bad JSON) keeps the cache and stays silent.
- Feed schema (`src/shared/whats-new.ts`, strict parser): `id`, `kind` (`announcement` | `nudge`), `title`, `body`, `publishedAt`, optional `expiresAt` (defaults to 30 days after publishing), `imageUrl`/`videoUrl` (must be https on `docs.orchestrator.inc`, so no third party is contacted), `cta` (`{label, url}` or `{label, action: "update"}`), `minVersion` (inclusive) and `maxVersion` (exclusive). A nudge such as "Update to fix X" sets `maxVersion`, and its `update` action opens Settings → Updates.
- While the app stays open, the renderer re-asks main for live items every 15 minutes (a local read, no network), so items go live at `publishedAt` and disappear at `expiresAt` without a restart.
- A sidebar card above the footer shows the newest unseen item. Dismissing it marks all unseen items seen. **See all**, Settings → Updates → **What's new**, and a Cmd+K search entry reopen the full list.
- **Kill switches:** remote `"enabled": false` in the feed, and local `AO_WHATS_NEW=0`. `AO_WHATS_NEW_URL` (https or 127.0.0.1 only) points a test build at another feed.
- **Hosting:** the docs site in this repo. `frontend/src/docs/public/whats-new/feed.json` deploys to GitHub Pages via `deploy-docs.yml` on merge to main, so no ao-landing change is needed. The seed item has `publishedAt: 2026-11-03` and stays hidden until then; edit or re-date it before merge as needed. CSP `media-src` gains `https://docs.orchestrator.inc` for feed videos (`img-src` already allows https).

**3. "Agent finished" desktop notification (new `agent_completed` type)**
"Needs input" (`needs_input`) and "PR ready" (`ready_to_merge`) already existed. "Agent finished" did not, so it is added:
- Lifecycle emits `agent_completed` when a non-orchestrator session's agent completes a working turn (`active → idle`, not terminated). Turns that end without a result do not notify: provider failures (`stop-failure`), interrupts (`interrupt`, `chat.interrupt.reconciled`) and a lost process or controller. Chat now reports `chat.turn.failed` / `chat.turn.interrupted` instead of labelling every turn end `chat.turn.completed`. Each turn is keyed by `SourceKey`, so it notifies once per finished turn, and hook retries don't duplicate it.
- Adds a migration that widens the `notifications.type` CHECK (table rebuild, mirroring 0170), plus enrich copy ("<session> finished"), the DTO enum, regenerated OpenAPI and `schema.ts`, the main-process type union, and the mobile notification view (label "Finished"; tapping opens the session).
- All three types are on by default. Every backend notification type already gets an OS toast when the window isn't focused, and there is no per-type off switch, so nothing else needed turning on.

## Why

Users who came back on days 1–6 were far more likely to be back in week 2 (40.5% vs 3.5%). We have no channel to reach users: no email and no in-app messaging. These are items 3 and 4 of the competitor findings (Orca's remote changelog + nudge JSON, and its notifications onboarding step with a test ping and macOS diagnosis), part of growth-plan A3 / §8b.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Home with no notifications step and no What's new card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/ba7da8d2a3ecbe1c43462cb0e873f92ec23973ea/home-before.png) | ![After: What's new card in the sidebar and notifications step on Home](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/ba7da8d2a3ecbe1c43462cb0e873f92ec23973ea/home-card-and-step.png) |
| No way to request or test notification permission | ![Granted: Notifications are on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/ba7da8d2a3ecbe1c43462cb0e873f92ec23973ea/step-granted.png) |
| Blocked macOS notifications fail silently | ![Denied: macOS is blocking notifications, Open System Settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/ba7da8d2a3ecbe1c43462cb0e873f92ec23973ea/step-denied.png) |

title: feat: offer follow-up tasks after the first worker, and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to start the next
body:
Code changes: +944 -24\
Tests: +662 -3\
Others: +391 -9 (generated OpenAPI spec and TS types, 9 locale catalogs, telemetry docs)

## What

The "Run 2 more" moment: help users who run one worker run several in parallel.

1. **Suggestions card on the board.** Once an install's first worker exists, the project board shows *"Your orchestrator can run more at once"* with three follow-up tasks AO found for that project:
   - open tracker issues (GitHub/GitLab via the existing tracker port) that no session in the project is already working on,
   - `FIXME`/`TODO` notes in tracked files (`git grep`, FIXMEs first, at most two per file, vendored/generated/fixture paths skipped),
   - built-in starter tasks (fix a small bug, bring the README up to date, add missing tests) to fill the list.

   Each row has a one-click **Start**, an **Edit prompt** inline editor, and the card has **Start all** and **Dismiss**. It is never shown again after Dismiss, or once the install has run 3+ workers (that is remembered, so archiving workers does not bring it back).
2. **Cmd/Ctrl+Enter on the new-task page** starts the task and keeps the page open on a fresh draft (with a newly prepared worktree) instead of opening the session. A toast confirms the start. Steering (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter during a running turn) is unchanged. A hint under the composer and a row in Keyboard shortcuts make it discoverable.
3. **New daemon route** `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/task-suggestions` returns structured facts only (issue number/title/url, or path/line/note text). The renderer writes the prompt in the user's language.
4. **Telemetry** (see below) plus a `spawnSource` field on `POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate` and `POST /api/v1/sessions` that only labels `ao.session.spawned`.

## Why

From the growth plan (sections 3, 4, 8b): 36% of activated users run only one worker on day 1, and only 6% of them start a worker again in week 2, vs 18% at 4–9 workers and 32% at 10+ (Sep 21 – Oct 14 cohorts; the gradient holds for every harness and OS). Orca shows a contextual "Start another task in parallel" tour step, and T3 Code has Cmd+Enter-to-next-draft. Here AO proposes the actual tasks, so the user doesn't have to come up with them.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the board with one worker and no prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c62d36b96a0632c1d7c064d28d26e5de217ba7e4/board-before.png) | ![After: the board offers two FIXME/TODO notes from the repository and a starter task](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c62d36b96a0632c1d7c064d28d26e5de217ba7e4/board-card.png) |
| No way to adjust a suggested task | ![Edit prompt opens the generated prompt inline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c62d36b96a0632c1d7c064d28d26e5de217ba7e4/board-card-edit.png) |
| Cmd/Ctrl+Enter on the new-task page sends like Enter and opens the new session | ![Cmd/Ctrl+Enter starts the task and opens the next draft, with a hint under the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c62d36b96a0632c1d7c064d28d26e5de217ba7e4/new-task-hint.png) |
| `ao.session.spawned` has no marker for where a task was started | carries `spawn_source: parallel_prompt` or `composer_next` |

Captured with the browser preview (`npm run dev:web`, the preview's sample board) against a daemon built from this branch with scratch data under `/tmp`, so the suggestion rows are real `task-suggestions` responses for a throwaway repo with one FIXME and one TODO. The "before" board is the same preview without the card.

## How

- **Single experiment gate:** `parallelPromptEnabled()` in `frontend/src/renderer/lib/parallel-prompt.ts` reads one key, `localStorage["ao.experiment.parallelPrompt"]` (`"off"` disables it, anything else including unset enables it). Every surface of the card goes through it, so a first-run cohort assigner (telemetry v2's cohort or later feature-flag plumbing, plan B10) can switch it per install with one write. It is on by default, so the release can be measured right away. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter is a power-user keyboard path and is not gated.
- **When it shows:** local projects only (not cloud, Scratchpad/standalone, remote hosts or missing folders), with at least one worker in the project, and an install-wide worker count (archived workers included) from 1 to 2. Dismissal and graduation are stored under `ao.parallelPrompt` in renderer storage, which already lives under `~/.ao/electron`.
- **Safe parallelism and limits:** each start goes through the same `POST /orchestrators/delegate` path as the composer: its own worktree, the project's worker-agent default, and the existing readiness, auth and plan checks. **Start all** starts tasks one at a time and stops at the first refusal, showing the daemon's reason (for example a missing sign-in or a limit) in the card. No retries.
- **Suggestion sources are best effort:** the tracker lookup has a 5s timeout and the `git grep` a 3s timeout. Any failure just yields fewer rows and the starter tasks fill in. A suggestions call never fails because a source failed. PRs are already filtered out by the GitHub tracker adapter, and issues are matched against existing sessions by issue number in any id form.
- **Retries and revisits:** a start whose answer is lost (or that fails after the daemon may have created the worker) keeps its request id and brief, persisted per project, and a retry resends them so the daemon replays the first result. Its prompt editor stays locked until then. Starting an issue records it on the worker (delegate accepts an optional `issueId`), so the daemon stops suggesting it. The card also remembers started suggestions per project, so revisiting the board never re-offers a running task.
- **Rebased onto `main`:** `ao.session.spawned` now carries both `main`'s `first_for_install` and this PR's `spawn_source` (allowlisted side by side), and the `ru` locale that landed on `main` has this PR's copy.
- **Idempotency:** `spawnSource` is excluded from the client-request fingerprint, so a retry of a lost response from another surface is still the same request.
- **Not done here (left for follow-ups):** failing-test suggestions (would mean running the suite) and LLM "split the current goal" suggestions. The card only appears on the board, not in the worker's session view where users land after their first start. Exposure is measurable via `parallel_prompt_shown`, so placement can be tuned with data.

### Telemetry (respects existing consent/opt-out, enums and counts only)

| Event | Properties |
| --- | --- |
| `ao.onboarding.parallel_prompt_shown` (once per project per launch) | `suggestion_count` (number), `source` ∈ `issue`, `todo`, `starter`, `mixed` |
| `ao.onboarding.parallel_prompt_action` | `action` ∈ `spawn_one`, `spawn_all`, `edit`, `dismiss`, `count` (tasks started, or rows dismissed) |
| `ao.session.spawned` (daemon, existing) | new `spawn_source` ∈ `parallel_prompt`, `composer_next`, absent for ordinary starts; allowlisted in the PostHog sink |

Renderer sanitizers drop everything else (titles, paths, prompts) and coerce unknown values to `other`/`0`, with tests. Both renderer events go through `captureRendererEvent`, so the opt-out, denylist and rate limits apply. `docs/telemetry.md` gains a section.

**`created_by`:** owned by telemetry v2 (agent-orchestrator-169), now on `main` (`domain.SessionCreator`, values `user | orchestrator | scheduled | automation`). This PR adds no `created_by` of its own. Starts from the suggestions card and from Cmd/Ctrl+Enter go through the desktop delegate path with no parent, so they are labelled `user`. `spawn_source` sits next to it on `ao.session.spawned`, as does `main`'s `surface` (which client made the request: desktop, CLI or mobile), and they don't overlap.

### Measuring impact in PostHog (project 475752)

1. **Funnel (exposure → action → worker):** `ao.onboarding.parallel_prompt_shown` → `ao.onboarding.parallel_prompt_action` where `action in (spawn_one, spawn_all)` → `ao.session.spawned` where `spawn_source = parallel_prompt`, per install, within 1 day. Break down the first step by `source` to see which suggestion source converts.
2. **Primary outcome:** among installs whose first worker (`ao.session.spawned`, `kind = worker`) lands after this release, the share with **2+ workers in the first 24h**. Baseline: 64% (36% stop at one).
3. **Retention:** the plan's headline W1 metric (another worker in days 7–13) for the one-worker bucket vs installs that saw the prompt. Baseline 5.9% for 1 worker on day 1, 15.3% overall.
4. **Keyboard path adoption:** unique installs with `ao.session.spawned` where `spawn_source = composer_next`, and those starts per install.
5. **A/B once cohorts exist:** set `ao.experiment.parallelPrompt = "off"` for the control cohort at first run, compare (2) and (3) by cohort, and keep `dismiss` rate and `ao.renderer.task_create_failed` as guardrails.

Example HogQL for (1):
```sql
select properties.source as source, count(distinct properties.install_id) as installs
from events
where event = 'ao.onboarding.parallel_prompt_shown' and timestamp > now() - interval 14 day
group by source
```

### Overlap

- **#7415 (onboarding attribution):** both add `ao.onboarding.*` renderer events and touch `telemetry.ts`/`telemetry.test.ts` and the locale catalogs. The changes are additive in separate `case`s and keys, so at most a textual merge conflict.
- **#7416 (pre-flight checks):** touches `TaskComposer.tsx` and spawn paths. This PR only adds an optional `spawnSource` and a `prepareNext()` to `useTaskLaunch`; Start/Start all go through the normal delegate route, so pre-flight failures surface in the card the same way any refusal does.
- **Telemetry v2 (agent-orchestrator-169, merged):** after rebasing, `emitSpawned` takes the spawn config in addition to v2's `createdBy`, and v2's attribution test passes the config. `created_by`, `first_for_install`, `surface` and `spawn_source` are all allowlisted on `ao.session.spawned`.

## Testing

- Backend: new tests for the suggestions service (open issues minus already-started ones, FIXME before TODO, per-file cap, skipped paths, quiet degradation), the HTTP route and DTOs, `spawnSource` validation/forwarding on delegate and sessions, and `spawn_source` on `ao.session.spawned`.
  - `go test ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/adapters/telemetry/ ./internal/observe/trackerintake/ ./internal/domain/` all pass. Spec drift and route/spec parity pass after `npm run api` (with `openapi-typescript@7.4.4`).
  - `golangci-lint v2.13.2 run`: 0 issues.
  - Full `go test ./...` locally: these packages fail **identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree** on this machine (environment: tmux/agent binaries): `adapters/agent/commandcode`, `adapters/agent/opencodev2`, `adapters/runtime/tmux`, `cli`, `integration`, `service/systemcheck`, `session_manager`. `adapters/agent/codex` and one `service/session` content-search test hit their timeouts only while the full frontend suite ran in parallel, and pass when re-run alone. Relying on CI for these.
- Frontend: new tests for the gating/ranking/telemetry module, the card (start one, edited prompt, start all stopping at a refusal, starter fallback, dismiss), board placement (shows at 1 worker, never at 3+ even after archiving, off with the flag), the new-task page (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter starts with `composer_next`, stays on a fresh draft, and the next plain send navigates), the composer (modifier send reported only when not steering), and sanitizers.
  - `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` are clean. Full `vitest run`: all pass except `browser-profile-import` (my local `npm ci --ignore-scripts` skipped the `better-sqlite3` build; passes after `npm rebuild better-sqlite3`) and one `TopbarOpenEditorButton` case that passes when re-run alone.
  - The i18n coverage gate passes. New copy is translated into all 9 shipped locales (de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-CN).
- CI follow-up: `SessionsBoard.remote.test.tsx` now settles its query clients after each test. Its archive/restore case left a batched query notify that could fire after jsdom teardown and fail shard 3 with an unhandled `window is not defined` while every assertion passed.
- Manual: as described under the screenshots, a scratch daemon from this branch returned real suggestions for a throwaway repo, and the card, editor and new-task hint rendered as shown.

title: fix(chat): stop the question dock clipping its rows' focus ring
body:
Code changes: +6 -2\
Tests: +72 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Clicking into a Claude question's **Other…** field drew its focus ring with no bottom edge, so the footer's **Skip** row looked like it was laid over the field's border. The same clipping hit any answer row that keyboard focus scrolled to the edge of a long list. Focused answer rows now always show their whole ring.

## Why

The answer rows sit inside the dock's scroll body, which has `overflow-y-auto`. Their focus ring is `ring-2`, a box-shadow drawn 2px *outside* the row, so the scroll body clips whatever reaches past its edge:

- **At either end of the list**, the first choice and the Other row sat flush against the scroll body's top and bottom edges. Other is always clipped when focused (a text field shows its ring on click). The first choice is clipped when reached by keyboard.
- **Mid-list, once the list scrolls**, moving focus with the arrow keys or Tab scrolls the focused field only until it touches the edge. The ring past it is clipped again. For Other it's worse: the field sits 4px inside the row that draws the ring.

Measured in the dock: the Other row ended exactly at the scroll body's bottom (697px), and its ring reached 699px.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Other focused: its ring has no bottom edge, and Skip appears to sit on it | Other focused: the whole ring shows above Skip |
| First choice focused with Tab: the ring's top edge is cut off under the question | The whole ring shows |
| Long list, arrowing down: each choice scrolled in at the bottom loses its ring's bottom edge | The whole ring shows at every step, down to Other and back up |

Screenshots of the Other state, before and after, to follow.

## How

All on `elicitation-scroll-body`, so it covers every layout inside it, not just the Claude question rows:

- `py-1` keeps the ring clear at either end of the list.
- `scroll-py-2` keeps it clear wherever focus scrolls a row in, including the Other field's 4px inset inside its row.
- Both leave a little room to spare. Scroll offsets round to whole pixels (in the e2e layout the body is 310.52px tall), so padding exactly the ring's width came up 0.61px short on the Other row at the bottom of a long list.
- The generic form layout drops its own `pb-1`, which the scroll body now provides, so its bottom spacing is unchanged.
- The ring itself is unchanged (DESIGN.md: focus rings are never removed); it just gets room.
- The URL-request layout has its own scroll body, but it holds only text and no focusable rows, so it is unchanged.

## Testing

- The e2e test in `chat-question-dock-overflow.spec.ts` now uses a question with 12 choices plus Other, long enough to scroll at 960×640. It Tabs in and arrows down through every choice, Tabs to Other, then Shift+Tabs back and arrows up to the first. At each step it checks that the focused row's whole box-shadow ring fits inside the scroll body.
  - It passes with this change (also 3/3 with `--repeat-each=3`).
  - It fails on a mid-list choice with the PR's first fix (padding on the question rows only) and with no fix.
- `chat-question-dock-overflow.spec.ts` and `chat-question-history.spec.ts` (local Chrome channel): 4 passed.
- `ElicitationDock.test.tsx` and `ElicitationHistory.test.tsx`: 29 passed. On the first revision, `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat` gave 1507 of 1508 passed. The one failure, a `ChatMarkdown` test under full-folder load, passes when its file is re-run alone.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- Visual check: the real `ElicitationDock` mounted in `dev:web` with a four-choice Claude question and with a 12-choice one, using Other focused and keyboard focus moved through the list.

**Not run locally:**

- The full renderer smoke (`@T0|@P0`) and the full `npx vitest run`. `src/main` needs better-sqlite3 built for system Node, and this machine has it built for Electron's ABI.
- The Go jobs; this PR has no backend changes.
- Local Node is 23.6.1, while CI pins 24.
