The full error still goes to the main-process log. ## Why When a check failed with an HTTP error (for example GitHub returning 504 on `/releases/latest`), Settings rendered the updater's message verbatim: the HTML response body, the header block (including `set-cookie`), and stack frames with local `app.asar` paths. The GitHub provider wraps the inner `HttpError`'s `stack` inside `Cannot parse releases feed: …`, so the whole dump arrives as one `Error.message`, and `errorMessage()` passed it straight through. Fixes #5755 ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `Cannot parse releases feed: Error: Unable to find latest version on GitHub (https://github.com/…/releases/latest), please ensure a production release exists: HttpError: 504 Gateway Time-out "method: GET url: … …" Headers: { "set-cookie": "…" } at createHttpError (C:\…\resources\app.asar\…\httpExecutor.js:53:12) … XML: …` | Couldn't check for updates — the update server timed out. Try again in a few minutes. | | Same dump in the check-error notice beside a staged build (automatic checks) | Same one-line sentence | | Restart to update dialog: heading plus up to 1000 chars of the dump | Heading plus `Couldn't install the update — the update server timed out. Try again in a few minutes.` | | Settings while a Windows/Linux restart re-downloads its build and that fails: the same dump | `Couldn't install the update — …`, the same sentence as the Restart dialog | | Offline: `net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED` in the check-error notice, after a failed download and in the Restart dialog | ` — the update server couldn't be reached. Check your connection and try again.` The status line keeps its localized restart guidance. | | macOS: the native updater fails after a requested restart (for example `The request timed out.`): the progress helper and Settings show Squirrel's text as-is | `Couldn't install the update — the update server timed out. Try again in a few minutes.` | | Windows: a build that fails the publisher check, with the whole Authenticode result appended as JSON | `Download failed — the update's signature couldn't be verified, so it was not installed. Download the latest build manually and install it over this one.` | | Return to Stable/Nightly from a PR build fails its check: the dump | `Couldn't return to your update channel — …` | Other failures it now explains, each prefixed by the operation (`Couldn't check for updates` / `Download failed` / `Couldn't install the update` / `Couldn't return to your update channel`): | Failure | Sentence after the prefix | | --- | --- | | HTTP 408 / 504 | the update server timed out. Try again in a few minutes. | | Other HTTP 5xx | the update server isn't available right now. Try again in a few minutes. | | HTTP 429, or 403 with "rate limit" | the update server is limiting requests. Try again later. | | HTTP 404, missing manifest, no published release | the update information / update file was not found on the server. (same wording as the existing manifest-404 copy) | | Any other HTTP status | the update server returned an error (HTTP 403). Try again later. | | Socket timeout (`Request timed out`, `ETIMEDOUT`, macOS `The request timed out.`), even under the releases-feed code | the update server timed out. Try again in a few minutes. | | `net::ERR_*`, bare or wrapped inside a provider error; Node socket errors (`ENOTFOUND`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, …); macOS NSURLError sentences (`Could not connect to the server.`, `The Internet connection appears to be offline.`, …) | the update server couldn't be reached. Check your connection and try again. | | Signature rejection (`ERR_UPDATER_INVALID_SIGNATURE`, "is not signed by the application owner") | the update's signature couldn't be verified, so it was not installed. Download the latest build manually and install it over this one. | | Unreadable feed (`ERR_UPDATER_INVALID_RELEASE_FEED` / `INVALID_UPDATE_INFO`) | the update information from the server couldn't be read. Try again in a few minutes. | | Anything else that still looks like a dump, when its first line is short (≤ 300 chars) and clean | that first line, for example `Download failed — Something odd` | | Anything else that still looks like a dump | (generic) `. Try again in a few minutes.` | AO's own messages (disk space, install-location blockers, "no longer available", macOS staging copy, the "Update check timed out" deadline) pass through unchanged. A `net::ERR_*` failure still sets `netError`, so the Settings status line keeps showing its localized restart guidance (#3526). The check-error notice, downloads and the Restart dialog have no such flag, so they show the connection sentence instead of the raw code. Each sentence is shown in the app's language. In Japanese, for example, the timed-out check reads `アップデートを確認できませんでした — アップデートサーバーの応答がタイムアウトしました。数分後にもう一度お試しください。` ## How - **`shared/update-error-message.ts` (new).** `describeUpdateFailure(err, phase)` maps a failure to `{ message, info }`: the English sentence and an `UpdateErrorInfo` saying what it means (`kind`: timeout, unavailable, rate-limited, not-found, http-error, unreachable, unreadable-feed, invalid-signature, detail, generic; `phase`: check, download, install, return; plus `httpStatus` or `detail` where they apply). AO's own messages pass through with no `info`. `userFacingUpdateError` returns the sentence alone. It reads the HTTP status from `HttpError.statusCode` or from the `HttpError: NNN` text the providers keep when they wrap it. It checks that status before electron-updater's error code, because the 504 above carries the outer code `ERR_UPDATER_INVALID_RELEASE_FEED`. `looksLikeRawUpdateError` detects dumps (HTML tags, `Headers: `, `set-cookie`, stack frames, `.asar` paths, `HttpError`, `ERR_UPDATER_*`, or more than 1000 chars, the bound the restart dialog used to truncate to). Failures below HTTP (Chromium `net::` codes, a socket timeout, Node socket errors) are also matched before the error code, because a timeout on `/releases/latest` arrives under the same releases-feed code as an unreadable feed. Matching is case-insensitive and covers the NSURLError sentences Squirrel reports on macOS. A signature rejection gets its own sentence, because a retry fetches the same build. A dump nothing else explains keeps its first line when that line is short and clean, so a failure a retry won't fix still names its cause; otherwise it gets the generic line. The `"return"` phase gives a failed return-home check its own lead. `isManifest404Error` moved here unchanged apart from tolerating a null error, and `updateErrorText` is exported so the main process has one error-to-text conversion. - **`main/update-settings.ts`.** `UpdateStatus` gains `errorInfo` (what an error status's `message` says) and `checkErrorInfo` (what `checkError` says). `message` and `checkError` stay as the English fallback. - **`main/auto-updater.ts`.** Every place that broadcasts or rethrows updater text now goes through `describeUpdateFailure`, and every broadcast carries the matching `errorInfo` / `checkErrorInfo`: the error-event fallback, `checkError` for automatic checks and for a manifest 404 beside a staged build, manual check, automatic download, `returnToHome`, `downloadUpdateNow`, and both restart paths. On macOS the restart progress helper and broadcast get the sentence, including when the native updater's own `error` event ends a requested restart; on Windows/Linux the remembered-build re-download was rethrowing the raw error with no catch at all. `broadcast()` rewrites any error status that still looks like a dump, so a path that builds its own message can't reach Settings raw. Each path that now drops the raw text logs it with `console.error` once: a manual operation's own catch logs it, and the error event logs only for a failure nobody awaits. `failedUpdatePhase()` picks the lead: while a restart is fetching its build the failure says `Couldn't install the update`, so Settings and the dialog describe one failure the same way, and a failed return-home check says `Couldn't return to your update channel`. The manifest-404 branches call `userFacingUpdateError` instead of repeating its copy. `isStagedInstallRejection` still matches on the raw message. Telemetry is unchanged: `emitUpdateFailure` still buckets the raw text into a category and never forwards it. - **Renderer.** `lib/update-error-copy.ts` (new) `localizedUpdateError(text, info, fallback, t)` rebuilds the sentence from 15 new `settings.updates.error.*` keys (a lead per phase, a reason per kind, and `{{lead}} — {{reason}}` / generic templates), added to all 8 locale catalogs. The English keys match the main process's sentences exactly. Without `info` (AO's own messages, or a status from an older main process) it shows the text through `displayableUpdateError`, the second line of defense for an error shape the main process doesn't know yet. `UpdatesSection` uses it for the status line and the check-error notice. `RestartToUpdateDialog` receives the rejected install as English text over IPC; when the broadcast status describes the same failure it shows that status's localized sentence, and a dump (overlong text included) still shows the heading alone. The manual-check override in Settings clears `errorInfo` so it never pairs with another message. `requestUpdateDownload`'s IPC-rejection fallback also runs through `displayableUpdateError`. - The macOS native restart progress helper still shows the English sentence; it is a separate native window outside the renderer's i18n. ## Testing All runs from `frontend/` on Node 23.6.1 (CI pins 24): - `npx vitest run src/shared src/main/auto-updater.test.ts src/main/update-*.test.ts src/main/mac-update-progress.test.ts src/renderer/components/settings src/renderer/hooks src/renderer/components/RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/lib src/renderer/i18n`: 276 files, 3721 tests pass (locale coverage and interpolation-parity tests included). - With the four source files reverted to `main` and the new tests kept, all 10 new or updated updater, Settings and dialog tests fail, so they cover the bug. - Against this PR's first commit, the 13 tests added or updated in the second commit fail (bare and wrapped connection failures, the check-error notice, a failed download, a failed Windows/Linux restart, overlong dialog detail). All pass now. - Against the second commit, the 9 tests added in the third commit for the review fixes fail (native macOS restart failure, signature rejection, first-line fallback, macOS network sentences, return-home lead). All pass now. A further test pins that a manual failure is logged once. - Localization (fourth commit): `update-error-copy.test.ts` checks that the English catalog reproduces the main process's sentence for every kind × phase, and that each other locale has a complete sentence. Settings renders Japanese and German, and the Restart dialog renders Japanese. Those three renderer tests fail against the components before this commit. Nine existing updater tests that compared error statuses exactly now also assert `errorInfo`. The non-English copy follows each catalog's existing update wording and formality; a native-speaker check is welcome. - `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) is clean. - Two existing tests pinned the raw text on purpose: the manifest-404 `checkError` test and "still surfaces non-manifest 404 errors". They now expect the rewritten sentence; both still assert that the failure is surfaced. Three more pinned a bare `net::` message (the two "flags net errors" tests and "stops showing checking when an error event fires…"); they now expect the connection sentence and still assert `netError: true`. "renders bounded recovery details as plain text" became a plain-text test under the bound plus a test that overlong text shows the heading alone. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (text-only change; before/after strings above) - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) After

title: fix: keep AO's ao first after login-shell startup files
body:
Code changes: +429 -8\
Tests: +699 -0\
Others: +16 -2

## What

Agents, reviewers, Codex Chat and AO terminals now run the app's own `ao` even when a shell startup file puts another one first on `PATH`: a legacy npm or Homebrew install, an nvm global, or the `scripts/daemon-build.sh` link. On an AppImage, sessions that outlive an app restart still reach the running app. A packaged `ao version` now names its build instead of printing `dev`.

## Why

Fixes #3562.

AO pins its `ao` first on each session's `PATH` (`agentlaunch.PinnedPATH`), but a login shell runs the user's startup files after that. Codex runs every agent command through `zsh -lc` or `bash -lc`, and every AO terminal is a login shell (`shellterm/loginshell.go`), so `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` in `~/.zprofile` hands agents whatever `ao` lives there. On an AppImage, the pin and Codex/Auggie hooks name `/tmp/.mount_*/resources/daemon/ao`, which is gone after the next launch.

## Before / After

`~/.zprofile` and `~/.bash_profile` prepend `~/.local/bin`, whose `ao` links to a June 27 dev build. The shells start with exactly the env a session gets, using the built daemon at `…/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Codex `zsh -lc 'command -v ao; ao version'` → `~/.local/bin/ao`, `dev-local commit 5fa53ad9 built 2026-06-27T13:57:21Z` | `…/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`, `0.13.0 built 2026-10-30T18:52:55Z` |
| `bash -lc` → the same stale build | the app's `ao` |
| AO terminal (`zsh --login -i`) → the same stale build | the app's `ao` |
| AppImage session after an app restart: `PATH` and hooks name the old `/tmp/.mount_*/…/ao`, which no longer exists | they name `<data dir>/runtime/ao-current/ao`, which the new daemon points at its own mount |
| packaged `ao version` → `dev` | `0.13.0 commit <sha> built <date>` (`-dev` suffix for dev builds) |

## How

`agentlaunch.LoginShellEnv` writes wrappers under `<data dir>/runtime/login-shell` and returns the variables that load them. `ZDOTDIR` points zsh at files that source the user's own `.zshenv`, `.zprofile`, `.zshrc`, `.zlogin` and `.zlogout` and then put the pin back first. `BASH_ENV` does the same after a non-interactive bash reads its profile, and a one-shot `PROMPT_COMMAND` does it before an interactive bash's first prompt. The user's own `ZDOTDIR` (including one set in `~/.zshenv`), `BASH_ENV` and `PROMPT_COMMAND` still run. `/etc/zshrc`'s `HISTFILE` stays in their home, and an interactive zsh ends on their `ZDOTDIR`, so tools like `p10k configure` still write there. It is applied in `Manager.runtimeEnvChecked` (agent and Codex Chat sessions), the reviewer launcher and shell terminals. `ao doctor`'s `ao-login-shell` check starts the shell with the same env.

`agentlaunch.UseStableExecutable` runs at daemon start. When `AO_APPIMAGE` is set, it moves `<data dir>/runtime/ao-current/ao` to this mount and makes `agentlaunch.Executable` return that link. Durable installs keep their own path.

The earlier revision's automatic repoint of `~/.local/bin/ao` is removed, along with its exception to the `~/.ao` hard rule: the wrappers fix that link and every other copy without touching user files. Doctor still names the link and gives the `rm`.

Rejected: repointing the link (fixes one copy, writes outside `~/.ao`); telling agents an absolute path (they still type bare `ao`); turning off login shells for Codex (Codex's choice, and the thread says not to).

Intentional omissions: sh, dash, ksh and fish have no hook after their startup files, so doctor still warns there. Windows has no reorder of this kind.

## Testing

- `agentlaunch/loginshell_unix_test.go` runs real `zsh -lc`, `bash -lc`, `zsh -c`, `zsh --login -i` and `bash --login -i` against an isolated `HOME`. Each case first asserts the stale `ao` wins without the wrappers (the reproduction), then that the pinned one wins after every user file ran. It also covers the user's own `ZDOTDIR`/`BASH_ENV`/`PROMPT_COMMAND`, a daemon started from an AO shell, `HISTFILE`, and the interactive `ZDOTDIR` hand-back.
- Call-site tests for sessions (spawn and restore), terminals and reviewers. A Codex hook test and two stable-executable tests cover the AppImage link. Doctor tests cover real zsh and bash shells passing and `sh` still warning.
- Revert check: with the wiring reverted, the session, terminal and reviewer tests fail; with Codex hooks back on `os.Executable`, the AppImage hook test fails. Removing the `HISTFILE` line fails its test.
- `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, golangci-lint v2.13.2 (0 issues), and full `go test ./...`. `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders` in `commandcode` fails on this Mac on the unchanged PR head too. Five adapter tests timed out only while lint ran alongside and pass on their own. `-race` on all touched packages. `build-daemon.mjs` built both packaged and `--dev`.
- Not run locally: an AppImage on Linux and Windows (Go tests and CI only), and the real desktop app.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(cloud): list Cloud's model catalog in a Cloud project's New Task
body:
## Summary

New Task in a Cloud project now lists AO Cloud's model catalog for the selected agent, not this computer's. Fixes #6673 together with the control-plane change in the private control-plane repo.

Before:

- The picker read the local daemon's catalog, so an expired local Claude login emptied it for a Cloud task.
- It offered models the Cloud worker could not run. Codex showed GPT-6-Luna and GPT-6.1-Sol, and the worker refused GPT-6-Luna (#6673).

After:

- The picker reads `GET /api/cloud/v1/orgs/{orgId}/providers/{agent}/models`, which answers without a live worker.
  - `source: release` is the models the control plane's pinned CLI supports for every account. The footer reads "Models for Codex 0.165.0".
  - `source: worker` is the list a Cloud worker reported for the user's current credential. The footer reads "Verified on your Cloud workers".
- **Default** sends no model, so the project's or the agent's own default applies. Nothing is picked for the user.
- A configured, remembered or typed model the catalog does not list stays selectable, with a warning that it may not run in Cloud. Any model ID can still be entered.
- A listed model takes only the effort levels it reports, so picking Low on Sonnet and switching to Haiku starts with no effort. Claude refuses a turn whose effort its model does not offer.
- Choosing the default drops an effort chosen for another model, and a Cloud task waits for the catalog before it can start.
- When the control plane has no catalog:
  - OpenCode's 409 keeps its credential-scoped discovery.
  - A code-less 404 or 501, from an older control plane, shows this computer's models as unverified suggestions, never selected automatically.
  - Any other failure keeps the default, manual entry and choices already made.
- Local projects and Scratchpad are unchanged, including when the composer moves between them and a Cloud project.

## Changes

- `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`:
  - adds `listUserAgentModels`;
  - adds optional `source`, `cliVersion` and `accountListed` to `ChatModelsResponse`;
  - `packages/cloud-client` is regenerated.
- `TaskComposer.tsx` (`useTaskLaunch`), `TaskModelControls.tsx`, `AgentModelCombobox.tsx`: the Cloud catalog query, picker footers, unlisted-model warning, effort rule.
  - The query key covers the control plane, user, org, agent and credential connection, so switching any of them asks again.
- `lib/cloud-cp`: client method and types.
- Strings in all eight locales.
- `docs/harnesses/model-catalogs.md`: the Cloud tasks section.
- An e2e spec (`frontend/e2e/cloud-model-catalog.spec.ts`).

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- TaskComposer: 135 tests. With the related suites (notice, combobox, i18n, cloud client, New Chat page): 239 tests. cloud-client: 31 tests.
- The `cloud-model-catalog` e2e spec: 6/6.
- Full vitest on the final commit: 10,015 pass. Four fail on this machine, none in files this PR touches:
  - ContextMeter and ChatWorkspace context usage expect `258,400`, but this machine's locale writes `2,58,400`;
  - a remote-proxy HTTP/2 test times out;
  - ReadOnlyFileView failed once in the full run and passes 3 of 3 on its own.
- oasdiff against main: no breaking changes.
- Staging (control plane at the private PR's head), with this build pointed at it and local model discovery forced to fail:
  - the route served Cloud's Claude Code 2.1.287, Codex 0.165.0 and Cursor lists, and the picker showed Claude Code's and Codex's (this account has no Cursor connection);
  - it made no local catalog calls;
  - a Haiku task picked from the list ran and replied;
  - Sonnet plus Low, then Haiku, started with no effort and the turn succeeded;
  - the Claude picker showed the account's models with "Verified on your Cloud workers";
  - the Codex picker showed GPT-6-Luna, GPT-5.6-Terra and GPT-5.6-Luna with "Models for Codex 0.165.0";
  - after a Codex worker signed in to ChatGPT reported the account's list, the Codex picker showed the same three with "Verified on your Cloud workers", and a GPT-5.6-Terra task created from it ran and replied;
  - a Claude session on a Coder workspace behaved the same as on Freestyle.
- Scratchpad in the running app still shows this computer's models, with no Cloud footer and no calls to the new route.

## Credit

This builds on #6706 by @codebanditssss, who reported and reproduced #6673 with the worker's exact rejection and designed the Cloud catalog picker this keeps. #6706's control-plane half moved to the private control-plane repo with the repo split, where it is rebuilt as a catalog that needs no live worker and covers Cursor.

title: fix(chat): keep a remote chat's box open while its host is away and drop the raw transport error
body:
## Summary

On a remote host, a short tunnel drop during a send has three problems on main:
- A raw red "remote daemon unreachable" sits under the box, and stays after the tunnel is back.
- The box is locked while the host is away, so nothing can be typed.
- The message waits in **Not sent**.

This PR keeps the manual resend: the message stays in **Not sent** and Retry sends it again with the same delivery ID. It removes the raw error and keeps the box open for typing while the host is away. Send, Enter and Retry wait until the host connects. There is no automatic resend. #7789 already keeps the chat on screen.

**Cause**

1. The tunnel drops while a send is in flight. The send fails with no error code, or with one of the proxy's own 502s (`UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, `HOST_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED`).
2. The composer parks it in the #7751 **Not sent** row, as intended.
3. The chat hook also shows that transport error as a red command error under the box.
4. While the host is away, `SessionChatSurface` locks the whole box (`composerLockedPlaceholder`), not only sending.

**Changes**

- `useConversationCommands`: a send error that no daemon answered (no error code, or one in `HOST_UNREACHABLE_CODES`) is not shown under the box. The **Not sent** row already says the message did not go. Refused sends and Stop, approval and settings errors still show.
- `useConversationConfigOptions` keeps the loaded options when a poll fails, so a blip does not show the error under the model row.
- `sendBlockedReason` (`SessionChatSurface` → `ChatWorkspace` → `ChatComposer`):
  - It is set while the host is unreachable and nothing else blocks new work.
  - The box stays open for typing.
  - Send, Enter and Retry do nothing until the host connects.
  - The placeholder and the Send tooltip read "Host is offline. You can send when it connects."
  - Rollback, queue edits, settings, attachments, steer and compact stay off while away, as on main.
  - The reviewer chat is unchanged.
- `remote.sendWhenConnected` is in all 9 locales.

## Before / after

Same scenario in both:
1. The tunnel stalls and Enter sends "status here".
2. The tunnel drops.
3. "next thought, typed offline" is typed during the outage, and Enter is pressed.
4. The tunnel comes back. In the AFTER take, Retry is pressed, then Send.

Some waits are shown 4× faster.

**Before (main edfee50dfe)**

![Before: the box locks, a raw red "remote daemon unreachable" stays under it after the tunnel is back, and the message waits in Not sent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/276b0ee9d8dccd820c6134f70ad5f044146b6f16/8ccd444/before.gif)

**After (this PR)**

![After: the box stays open with a plain offline placeholder, Send and Retry wait, no red error, then Retry and Send deliver both messages in order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/276b0ee9d8dccd820c6134f70ad5f044146b6f16/8ccd444/after.gif)

Higher-quality MP4s of the same takes: [before.mp4](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/276b0ee9d8dccd820c6134f70ad5f044146b6f16/8ccd444/before.mp4) · [after.mp4](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/276b0ee9d8dccd820c6134f70ad5f044146b6f16/8ccd444/after.mp4)

| | Before (main, 2 runs) | After (8ccd444384, 2 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| Box during the outage | Locked in 147 of 148 and 294 of 449 samples. The offline message could not be typed | Typeable in 145 of 145 and 148 of 148 samples |
| Send during the outage | Locked with the box | Disabled in 145 of 145 and 148 of 148 samples. Enter sent nothing to the host |
| Placeholder | "Showing the last saved copy until the host connects." | "Host is offline. You can send when it connects." in 143 of 145 and 147 of 148 samples |
| Raw transport error | "remote daemon unreachable" in 173 and 746 samples, still there after the tunnel returned | None |
| Retry during the outage | Disabled | Disabled in 143 of 145 and 147 of 148 samples |
| After the tunnel returns | Still "Not sent" 20 s later; the host got nothing | Retry enabled after 0.85 s and 14 s. Retry and Send delivered "status here", then "next thought, typed offline", each once, in both runs |

The probe sampled the live DOM every 100 ms during the outage. Its red-text check (`[role=alert]`, `.text-destructive`, `.text-status-needs-you`, `.text-error`) also matches the "Not sent" label and the usage meter, which are not errors. The host order was read from the host's conversation API after each take.

## How it was reproduced

The lab ran the real dev desktop app against a second AO daemon with a real Claude chat session:
- Traffic went through the second daemon's loopback-only remote listener and a fault proxy that can pass, stall or drop connections.
- A loopback stand-in control plane provided the sign-in that remote hosts require.
- No public tunnel was used.
- The BEFORE take swapped main's renderer files into the same checkout.

## Tests

- `SessionView.remote`:
  - While the host is away, the box takes typing, Send stays disabled, Enter posts nothing, and the message sends after reconnect.
  - A send whose response is lost, and a send answered with a 502 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, both stay in **Not sent** without the raw error. Retry is disabled while the host is away, and after reconnect it reuses the delivery ID.
  - With the `useConversation` filter and the `sendBlockedReason` wiring removed, all three tests fail.
- `useConversation`: loaded config options stay usable when a later poll fails.
- Local runs:
  - `SessionView.remote`: 30 of 30 passed.
  - `ChatComposer`, `ChatComposer.optimistic`, `ChatWorkspace`, `useConversation`, `chat-drafts` and `SharedSessionChat`: 632 of 632 passed.
- CI is green on b2fcfdb7a6 (main merged in after #8248).

## Risks and follow-ups

- A message lost in a blip needs one Retry click once the host is back. There is no automatic resend.
- Retry and Send wait until the desktop sees the host again. That took 0.85 s and 14 s in the two runs.
- Text typed while the host is away lives in the local chat draft until it is sent.
- The reviewer chat still locks its box while the host is away.

title: feat(mobile): draw the turn plan as the desktop panel does
body:
Code changes: +461 -42\ Tests: +184 -3\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The mobile turn plan now uses the desktop plan panel's design (#6884): - A long plan scrolls inside a short window (about six steps) that follows the step in progress. The edge with more steps behind it fades out. - Steps are set at subheadline size (15pt, up from 12pt). Each step's mark shows its state: a turning arc while in progress, a dashed ring when not started, a ticked ring when done. The arc turns only while the turn runs: a stopped or failed turn, or a plan the agent keeps across turns, leaves a step in progress, and its mark holds still instead of spinning after the agent has stopped. The uppercase `COMPLETED` / `IN PROGRESS` label on every row and the orange `STILL CHANGING` tag are gone. Screen readers still hear each step's state, and the header reads e.g. "Plan, 17 of 19 steps done. Now: Building for the Pixel". - A plan opens only while its turn runs and has steps left; otherwise it starts folded to its header. A stopped or failed turn keeps a step in progress, so past turns would otherwise each show an open panel. A finished plan shows a filled tick, and a folded plan with work left names its current step in the header. - A list the agent keeps across turns (`spansTurns`, Claude's task list) shows only on the latest turn that carries it, as on the desktop; earlier turns hold stale copies. - A plan that fits does not catch drags, so the transcript scrolls past it; only an overflowing plan scrolls its own window. Step text follows the reader's text size up to the body cap, with the marks and window growing to match. - The whole header row is the toggle (48pt). Plan activities whose turn has no turn-level plan (for example one AO could not match to a turn) use the same panel when they carry steps, drawn as the desktop draws that row: the default "Plan" title and no live state. ## Why On a phone, a 19-step plan filled the whole screen in small type with a status word on every row, so it was hard to see where the agent had got to. The desktop already solved this with a scrolling window that follows the live step; mobile now matches it. ## Before / After Same 19-step plan on both sides. The "before" card is `TurnPlan` from `main`, copied verbatim into a temporary screen and rendered in the same build. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Every step was always shown, so there was nothing to scroll | Scrolled mid-list, fading at both edges:
| | Folded, the header showed only `Plan`, `STILL CHANGING` and the count | Folded, the header names the current step:
| ## How - `packages/mobile/lib/chat/TurnPlan.tsx` is the panel; the pure parts (which step to follow, where to scroll, which edges to fade, the accessibility label) are in `planModel.ts` with unit tests. - The window is a nested `ScrollView` (`nestedScrollEnabled` for Android) with a `maxHeight` that grows with the text size, and scrolling enabled only when the steps overflow (no bounce). It centres the active step using each row's measured layout, lands instantly the first time and animates after that, and never scrolls the transcript. - Step marks are `react-native-svg`. The spinner uses the existing `Spinning` wrapper, so it holds still under Reduce Motion. - Edge fades are SVG gradients over the card surface colour. Both run top to bottom and the bottom edge swaps the stop opacities, because react-native-svg on Android drew nothing for a reversed (`y1="1" y2="0"`) gradient. - `TurnPlan` is memoised with a by-value plan comparator (`samePlanProps`), since every step draws its own SVG and the timeline re-renders while text streams. - `groupConversationByTurn` attaches each turn's plan to its group and drops stale copies of a spanning list, mirroring `ChatWorkspace.tsx`. - Adds the `list-checks` glyph to the mobile icon map (the desktop header uses `ListChecks`). ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `packages/mobile`: 254 files, 2664 tests pass after rebasing onto `main`. `planModel.test.ts` covers follow, centring and clamping, edge fades, overflow, the memo comparator and the accessibility label; `timelineModel.test.ts` covers the spanning-list filter; two source tests were updated for the move to `TurnPlan.tsx`. - iOS simulator (Release build with this branch's JS embedded) and Android emulator (debug build on Metro), each in dark and light: the window opens on the live step, dragging inside it scrolls only the plan (not the page), both fades show mid-list, tapping the header folds and reopens it, and a finished plan starts folded. - Review fixes on the iOS simulator: a stopped turn with a step in progress starts folded while running ones open; a drag starting on a 3-step plan scrolls the page while a drag on a 14-step plan scrolls only its window; at accessibility XXXL text the marks stay level with the first line and the window centres the live step. - Spinner stops with the turn: on the iOS simulator, a running and a stopped plan, each with a step in progress, compared pixel for pixel across five frames. The running mark changed in every frame and the stopped one never did. - Inside the chat transcript: the production `ChatTimeline` (inverted list on iOS, upright on Android), fed a six-turn conversation shaped like a long Claude chat with a task list kept across turns. Only the newest turn shows the list, folded and still when settled, open on the live step when running. A drag inside the plan scrolls only the plan on both platforms. Results and screenshots are in [this comment](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7432#issuecomment-6525594683). The before/after captures above render the component on a temporary screen; neither lab screen is part of this PR. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Bug]: stuck worker reports make AO press Ctrl-C in terminal orchestrators, which cancels their turns in a loop
body:
### What went wrong?

When a worker report is stuck, the report coordinator interrupts the project's orchestrator before it submits the batch. For a terminal (TUI) orchestrator that interrupt is a Ctrl-C into the PTY:

- `backend/internal/service/report/coordinator.go` `deliverProject`: `batch.hasState(domain.ReportStuck)` → `c.delivery.Interrupt(ctx, target.ID)`
- `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go` `reportSemanticDelivery.Interrupt`: a non-chat session goes to `InterruptTUI`
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/runtime.go` `Runtime.Interrupt`: "sends Ctrl-C to the PTY"

In Claude Code or Codex running in a terminal, Ctrl-C cancels the running turn, or a prompt that was submitted a moment earlier. The submit that follows is then refused. Inside the 3-minute `ReportInterruptWindow` the batch is deferred ("repeated stuck report coalesced inside interrupt window"), and when the window ends the next attempt presses Ctrl-C again. The loop only ends when someone acknowledges the report by hand.

Seen on 2026-10-28 with 15 terminal-mode orchestrators (Claude Code and Codex), on a local build based on `main` 44d71b5c with no changes to the report code. From the orchestrator transcripts and the database:

- Running turns were cut ("[Request interrupted by user]") 6 times across two orchestrators.
- A session message submitted 0.3 s before a Ctrl-C was cancelled, and its text went back into the input box.
- A normal report batch typed 5 s before a Ctrl-C was marked acknowledged, but its turn was cancelled, so the orchestrator never read it.
- The stuck report itself was never delivered. It reached 26 to 30 `delivery_attempts` until an operator acknowledged it by hand.
- In the same minutes, normal reports to the same orchestrators were acknowledged on the first attempt.

Expected: terminal orchestrators already queue typed input while a turn runs, so a stuck report can be submitted like any other report, without Ctrl-C. Chat-mode orchestrators can keep the rate-limited interrupt.

The code is the same on `main` de4a47da today.

A fix with tests is ready (PR to follow): skip the interrupt for terminal orchestrators, and defer a refused submission behind reports that are already due, so one orchestrator that keeps refusing cannot hold the front of the delivery queue for every other project.

title: fix(report): never press Ctrl-C in terminal orchestrators for stuck reports
body:
Code changes: +16 -2\
Tests: +120 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Stuck worker reports no longer press Ctrl-C in terminal (TUI) orchestrators. They are submitted like any other report. A submission the orchestrator refuses is now deferred behind reports that are already due, instead of keeping its place at the front of the delivery queue.

## Why

Fixes #7434

For a stuck report, `deliverProject` calls `Delivery.Interrupt` on the orchestrator first. For a terminal orchestrator that becomes `InterruptTUI`, which writes Ctrl-C to the PTY. In Claude Code or Codex, Ctrl-C cancels the running turn or a prompt that was just submitted, the next submit is refused, and the batch comes back 3 minutes later (`ReportInterruptWindow`) with another Ctrl-C. On 2026-10-28 this cut 6 running turns across two orchestrators, cancelled a session message submitted 0.3 s earlier, and cancelled the turn holding a report batch AO had already marked acknowledged, so that orchestrator never read it. The stuck report itself reached 26 to 30 delivery attempts until an operator acknowledged it by hand.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A stuck report sends Ctrl-C to a terminal orchestrator, then submits | A stuck report is submitted to a terminal orchestrator with no Ctrl-C and no interrupt reservation |
| A refused submit releases the batch with its original availability; schedule selection takes the earliest pending report across projects, so the same batch is picked again and again, and one refusing orchestrator blocks report delivery for every other project | A refused submit is deferred by the retry delay with its refusal reason in `last_error`; reports already due in other projects go first |
| Chat-mode orchestrators: rate-limited interrupt | Unchanged |

Measured on one machine with 15 terminal-mode orchestrators, which has run this change in a local build since 2026-10-28 04:19 UTC. Counted at 2026-10-29 14:03 UTC: 0 interrupts recorded since the change (`report_worker_interrupts`; the last row is from 02:52 UTC that day, before the change), and 135 reports created, all 135 acknowledged, including 2 stuck reports. The first stuck report after the change was acknowledged 6 s after it was created, on its second attempt. The second was acknowledged on its first attempt.

## How

- `deliverProject` takes the interrupt path only when the target orchestrator's mode normalises to `chat`. Terminal orchestrators already queue typed input while a turn runs, so the normal submit is enough there.
- The interrupt-window deferral used to be the only thing that moved a refusing stuck batch out of the way. With it gone for terminal targets, a non-busy refusal (for example "prompt submission was not observed") would have been released at its original availability and selected again first. `retryLater` defers it with `DeferReportBatch` by the coordinator's retry delay, keeping the batch identity and the refusal reason. The existing busy-composer path (`OrchestratorBusyRetry`) is unchanged.
- Intentional omission: no change for chat-mode orchestrators; their interrupt goes through the chat service, not a PTY.

## Testing

- `cd backend && gofmt -l .` (empty), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./...` on macOS arm64, Go 1.27.1: 209 packages pass, 3 fail. None of the 3 imports `service/report`, and none is caused by this change:
  - `adapters/agent/commandcode` `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders` and `adapters/runtime/tmux` `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` fail the same way on unmodified `main` de4a47da on this Mac, and both packages pass in the Linux CI run for de4a47da (Go workflow run 40857145552). They look specific to macOS git and tmux.
  - `terminal` `TestAttachmentExitsOnDestroyUnderDetachOnDestroyOff` timed out once ("condition not met within 5s") during the full parallel run, and passed on a rerun on both this branch and de4a47da.
- `go test -tags e2e -count=1 -v ./internal/cli/...` (the native `cli-e2e` job), run with an empty `HOME` and a minimal `PATH`: pass, 0 failures.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- New tests: `TestCoordinatorNeverInterruptsTerminalOrchestrator`, `TestCoordinatorRetriesTerminalStuckReportWithoutInterrupt`, `TestCoordinatorRefusedSubmitDoesNotBlockOtherProjects`, `TestReportStoreDeferredBatchYieldsScheduleToOtherProjects` (pins the existing store ordering this relies on).
- Checked that the tests catch the bug: restoring the interrupt for terminal targets fails the first three tests; restoring the plain release fails `TestCoordinatorRefusedSubmitDoesNotBlockOtherProjects`.

title: fix(persistenthost): let Windows chat host shutdown delete its descriptor
body:
Code changes: +47 -2\
Tests: +63 -0\
Others: +1 -1 (CI workflow)

## What

On Windows, chat host shutdown no longer collides with its own descriptor file. AO now reads `chat-hosts/<session>/host.json` with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, so a reader no longer stops the exiting host from deleting it. The `Shutdown` wait also treats a briefly busy descriptor as "not gone yet" instead of failing.

## Why

`TestPersistentClaudeACPHibernateAndNativeResume` fails intermittently on the `windows-workspace` job, with two different errors:

- `Hibernate: wait for chat host shutdown: context deadline exceeded` ([run 40888462620](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40888462620/job/123498429740), 2026-10-29)
- `Hibernate: open …\chat-hosts\restart-test\host.json: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.` ([run 40704946402](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40704946402), 2026-10-28)

Both come from one race. `Shutdown` polls `host.json` every 20 ms with `os.ReadFile`, while the exiting host deletes it in `defer func() { _ = os.Remove(path) }()`. Go opens files on Windows with `FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE` only (`syscall.Open`), never `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, so:

1. **The host deletes while a poll has the file open.** `DeleteFile` fails with a sharing violation, the error is dropped, and `host.json` outlives its host. `Shutdown` then polls a descriptor that will never go away until its 10 s deadline, which is the first error. A longer wait can't fix this case.
2. **A poll opens while the host's delete holds the file.** The open fails with a sharing violation, and `Shutdown` returns it as fatal. That's the second error.

Unix doesn't have this, because unlinking an open file is always allowed.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A `host.json` reader opened like `os.Open` makes the host's `os.Remove` fail with `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`, so the descriptor outlives the host | Removal succeeds while a `readDescriptor` reader has the file open |
| While a delete handle holds `host.json`, `readDescriptor` fails with `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` | `readDescriptor` reads it; a `Shutdown` poll that still sees a busy file keeps waiting |

No user-visible change on macOS or Linux. On Windows, Hibernate, provider switch and host reaping stop failing intermittently on this race.

## How

- `openHostFile` (`child_windows.go`) opens with `CreateFile(GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE|FILE_SHARE_DELETE)`. On Unix it's `os.Open`. `readDescriptor` uses it, so every descriptor reader benefits: `Start`, `Connect`, `Reconcile` and `Shutdown`.
- `hostFileBusy` classifies `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` and `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (a delete pending until another handle closes). Only the `Shutdown` wait loop uses it, to keep polling; on Unix it's always false.
- Not changed: the host still ignores a failed `os.Remove`. With our own reader fixed, the remaining risk is a third-party handle (antivirus, indexer) that denies deletion; I left that out rather than add a retry loop.

## Testing

- New `TestWindowsHostDescriptorReadAndRemovalDoNotBlockEachOther` (`//go:build windows`) holds each conflicting handle on purpose, so it's deterministic instead of timing-based:
  - A plain `os.Open` reader makes `os.Remove` fail with a sharing violation (this documents the cause), while an `openHostFile` reader doesn't.
  - While a `DELETE` handle is open, `os.Open` fails with a sharing violation that `hostFileBusy` recognises, while `readDescriptor` succeeds.
  - Added to the `windows-workspace` job's "Windows Chat provider process cleanup" step, which only runs the tests it names.
- Windows can't run locally here, so the Windows test is verified in this PR's `windows-workspace` job, where it passes ([run 40911019479](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/40911019479)). Its `os.Open` assertions passing on the runner confirms the sharing violation described above. `TestPersistentClaudeACPHibernateAndNativeResume` passes in the same job. Locally: `GOOS=windows go vet` and `GOOS=windows go test -c` for the package.
- `GOOS=windows` golangci-lint v2.13.2 on `persistenthost` reports the same 4 findings as unchanged `main` (none in this change).
- Locally (macOS, Go 1.27.1): `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/` passes.
  - gofmt, `go build ./...` (also `GOOS=windows`), `go vet ./...` (plus `GOOS=windows` on `chatdriver/...`) and golangci-lint (0 issues) pass.
  - Full `go test -race -count=1 ./...`: 204 packages pass. 6 fail the same way on unchanged `main` on this machine, because the tests read the developer's environment (`opencode`, `opencodev2`, `opencodev2acp`, `crush`, `commandcode`, `runtime/tmux`).
  - 2 more failed once under full-suite load and pass in isolation: `service/chat` `TestSendSurvivesCancelledViewWake` (15 of 15; its test file doesn't use `persistenthost`) and `service/session` `TestSearchWorkspaceContentCommonTermReachesLaterFiles` (3 of 3; doesn't depend on `persistenthost`).

title: Turn on Electron Sentry and telemetry for consented users
body:
Code changes: +56 -135\
Tests: +202 -249\
Others: +14 -40

## What

Turn on Electron Sentry in packaged stable and nightly releases. Share error events and Share usage analytics are on by default for fresh installs and existing users unless the user explicitly turned the corresponding choice off or an environment opt-out applies. Both remain toggleable in Settings > General > Privacy. Remove the error-sharing renewal dialog and gate. Support durable error-sharing choices on Windows.

| Fixes | Result |
| --- | --- |
| SEN-1 | Opens the Electron Sentry production gate for the default-on error-sharing choice. |
| SEN-2 | Removes renewal gating and preserves prior choices, including recorded opt-outs. |

Tracker: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1V-JA-zuMh-_xUxMYkTyYoo8ZweXv-pKG521lvkzLF58/edit

IDP-14 is handled separately by HSB. The privacy policy must state that error sharing and usage analytics are on by default. This PR does not edit or publish that policy.

## Why

The previous PR revision required existing users to renew an error-sharing choice and left both Windows senders off. The current product decision makes both choices default on while preserving explicit opt-outs on every desktop platform.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Packaged Electron Sentry stayed off behind a release constant. | Packaged Electron Sentry starts when error sharing is on, including on a fresh install. |
| An existing opt-in produced a renewal dialog and blocked both Sentry senders. | Existing opt-ins send without a dialog; recorded opt-outs remain off. |
| A missing policy file blocked daemon Sentry in the previous PR revision. | A missing file permits the packaged daemon to send, matching main; the live check still stops an explicit opt-out. |
| Windows could not save the error-sharing policy and kept Sentry off. | Windows writes a flushed temporary record and retries a locked rename. Both senders and the Settings toggle use the saved choice. |

The visible change removes the renewal dialog. A real-app screenshot was unavailable because the local package build could not download tmux in this environment; the renderer tests and policy tests cover the removed flow and replacement behavior.

## How

Original base: `dbeaf19c8a9decc2330fc1fac8c36f22b417dabd`. Current PR base: `8f4ecd5f9da7392ffe0d5c7f11c091f45229c068` from origin/main, including #7386 and #7304. The rebase preserved #7304 usage telemetry wiring and documentation.

### Gate audit and rollout

| Path and gate | Evidence and action |
| --- | --- |
| Packaged Electron main | `main.ts` loads the desktop policy, then `DesktopTelemetryController` starts the Sentry transport when the release constant, environment, acknowledged choice, and completed purge permit it. The production constant is true. Fresh packaged installs write an enabled record. |
| Existing error-sharing choices | Version 1 and legacy version 2 records remain readable. `events_enabled` alone records the choice; the old production-consent field is accepted only to read legacy records. The renewal popup, its strings, and its state field are removed. An explicit `events_enabled: false` remains off. |
| Windows desktop authority | Windows now loads and writes the policy. The temporary file is flushed before rename, and `EPERM` or `EBUSY` replacement locks are retried. The daemon reader skips the Unix permission-bit check on Windows while still rejecting symlinks, malformed records, and nonfiles. |
| Electron transport and renderer IPC | Renderer exceptions still forward through main with generation checking and sanitization; there is no renderer Sentry transport. A blank DSN, environment veto, dev default, or incomplete purge prevents sending. Opt-out drains and purges the offline queue. |
| Daemon Sentry | The packaged app supplies `AO_SENTRY_DSN` and `AO_TELEMETRY_EVENTS=on` unless explicitly overridden. The reader matches main's missing-file default-on rule. One check per capture reads the current policy, so a recorded off choice or environment veto stops subsequent captures without a restart. Unsafe or unreadable records fail closed. |
| Daemon PostHog | Packaged remote export defaults to PostHog. The separate Share usage analytics marker and explicit environment controls can stop it. Error sharing does not change this choice. |
| Renderer PostHog | Packaged renderer telemetry defaults on. The Share usage analytics marker and `AO_TELEMETRY_RENDERER=off` stop it independently of error sharing. |
| Restart and purge | The controller serializes changes, drains and purges Electron queues on opt-out, purges at startup while off, and blocks sender restart until cleanup finishes. These gates remain in place. |

Development builds retain their remote-off defaults. Explicit DSN overrides remain available. This change does not send synthetic test events to production or access real user settings.

## Testing

Passed locally: 126 focused frontend tests across six files, frontend typecheck and e2e typecheck, Go policy and Sentry race tests, daemon suite with local listener access, Go build and vet, Windows Go reader cross compilation, gofmt, and `git diff --check`. Tests use local fixtures and synthetic transports. Windows replacement tests simulate `EPERM` and `EBUSY`; a native Windows test run remains a CI validation gap.

The complete frontend suite was run locally and hit an unrelated `ReadOnlyFileView` failure, then was stopped. The package build reached the tmux download and failed because this environment could not fetch the tarball. Neither is marked as a local pass. The full Go suite has known unrelated local environment failures; the affected daemon, reader, and Sentry suites passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Continued the existing PR branch based on main
- [x] One focused change with tracker links
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After documents observable behavior
- [x] Regression tests cover default-on, prior choices, Windows writes, and opt-out
- [ ] Complete remote CI suites pass

title: fix(sidebar): offer no rename for a Cloud session or the orchestrator
body:
Code changes: +27 -13\
Tests: +52 -3\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The app no longer starts a rename that can't be saved. A Cloud session, and the project orchestrator, no longer go into rename on F2, double-click, double-tap or the context menu. This covers the sidebar row and the session's own tab in the main pane.

## Why

Refs #6519: Rename looked broken for Cloud sessions and orchestrators. The issue also asks that the UI not offer Rename where it isn't supported.

- **Cloud session.** #7372 hid Rename from a Cloud session's context menu. But the sidebar row still started an inline rename on F2, double-click and double-tap. So did the session's tab in the main pane, for a Cloud session in terminal mode. On commit, `useSessionRename` sent the name to the local daemon's `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/{id}`. The daemon doesn't know the session, so the name snapped back, and the error only reached the console. AO Cloud has no rename route: `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` has only `GET` and `DELETE` on `/orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}`.
- **Orchestrator.** The orchestrator can't be renamed. The daemon refuses it with `ORCHESTRATOR_RENAME_UNSUPPORTED`, and its own agent can't rename it by naming its thread. The session tab already never offered it (`CenterPane`). The sidebar row and its context menu didn't check for it. Today the sidebar lists an orchestrator row only in a project shared from another organization, and those are Cloud sessions, so the Cloud rule happened to hide Rename there. This PR makes the app check the orchestrator rule itself, so it doesn't depend on that.

This PR does not make Cloud sessions renamable. That needs a control-plane route, and renaming in Cloud is on hold until a product decision is made (see the hold on #6983). So the issue stays open for that half.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| F2, double-click or double-tap on a Cloud session's sidebar row opens an inline rename. Enter snaps the name back, and `Failed to rename session` is logged to the console. | Nothing starts a rename. The row has no `aria-keyshortcuts="F2"`. |
| Double-tap on a Cloud session's name eats the next tap, so the session doesn't open. | The next tap opens the session. |
| On a Cloud session in terminal mode, F2, double-click or right-click → **Rename** on its tab in the main pane opens an inline rename that snaps back the same way. | The tab offers no rename and has no F2 hint. |

| Local worker sessions: rename from F2, double-click, double-tap, context menu, session tab and board. | Unchanged. |

No screenshots: the change only removes an affordance. The Sidebar and CenterPane tests below check each surface.

## How

- `canRenameSession(session)` in `types/workspace.ts` returns false for `session.cloud` and for `isOrchestratorSession(session)`. Both rules already apply elsewhere; this puts them in one place.

It also skips the F2 `preventDefault`, the `aria-keyshortcuts` hint and the double-tap's suppression of the next click. The double-click handler keeps its `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation`, so nothing changes for parent handlers.

- `SessionPaneTab` in `CenterPane` uses `canRenameSession` instead of only `isOrchestratorSession`. The chat view's session tab is the same component, so it follows too.
- No change to `useSessionRename`, `renameSession`, the daemon or the contract.

F2 and double-click open no editor, the context menu has no Rename, and the daemon is never called. The orchestrator case has no `cloud`, so it checks the orchestrator rule on its own.

title: fix(session): idempotent cleanup, session delete and retention
body:
Code changes: +1385 -146\
Tests: +1410 -35\
Others: +580 -21 (generated OpenAPI, schema.ts and sqlc code; docs; locale strings)

## What

`ao session cleanup` no longer revisits worktrees it already released, and every cleanup result is now recorded for every session. Skipped workspaces report a stable `code` (`dirty`, `locked_worktree`, `permission_error`, …), and a locked worktree says how to unlock it. Terminated sessions can be deleted from a trash action on archived cards, with `ao session delete [--cleanup]`, or with `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}`. An opt-in setting deletes archived sessions after 7, 30 or 90 days.

## Why

Fixes #3402. Cleanup facts were written only for sessions that already had a row, so every run and dry-run revisited every terminated session forever. Failures carried only free text, `ListTerminalCleanupCandidates` was never called, and session records could never be removed.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A second `ao session cleanup` reports `Already gone: <id>` for every session the first run cleaned | `No sessions to clean up.` once nothing is pending |
| Locked worktree: `Skipped: <id> (workspace teardown failed)` | ``Skipped: <id> (worktree is locked by git; run `git worktree unlock` on it, then retry cleanup) [locked_worktree]`` |
| A cleanup interrupted by a daemon crash stays pending forever; one refused because the worktree was busy is recorded as failed | The 10-minute background pass finishes both |
| Archived cards offer only Restore | A quiet trash icon opens a destructive confirm. A worktree still on disk is cleaned up first, never forced; a refusal shows in the dialog and the session is kept |
| No way to drop old archived sessions | Settings → Sessions → "Delete archived sessions": Never (default), 7, 30 or 90 days |

## How

- Results are recorded per cleanup generation, so a restored session's new worktree is never hidden. Results found by the sweep or `ao session cleanup` for sessions the app did not archive are stored `report_only` and do not raise the topbar banner. Temporary refusals (worktree busy, shared with a live session, shell open, cleanup running) stay `pending` for the background pass.
- The background pass never removes a worktree on its own. It finishes cleanups that were already accepted, and prunes git's registration for folders that are already gone.
- Delete holds the session operation guard and requires a released workspace; with `cleanup` it runs the normal cleanup first. It refuses sessions in a shared orchestrator conversation. Spend moves into `deleted_session_account_usage`, `session_num_floors` stops a deleted id being reused, and an `AFTER DELETE` trigger emits the project-level `session_updated` event.
- Retention reads a trigger-maintained `sessions.terminated_at` (older rows fall back to `updated_at`) and deletes only sessions whose worktree is already released.
- A stale `initializing` lock from a crashed `git worktree add` is lifted; any other lock is reported. `git worktree` and `git status` run with English messages (message language only), so this works in any locale.
- Omitted: cloud sessions get no delete button, and `ao session delete` is not taught to agents.

## Testing

- `go test ./...` in `backend/` passes except `commandcode`, which also fails on a clean `main` on this machine. gofmt, vet and golangci-lint v2.13.2 report 0 issues; `npm run api` and `npm run sqlc` output is in sync.
- `npm run typecheck`, lint and vitest for the touched areas pass.
- New tests cover repeat cleanup, report-only recording, retryable refusals, the background pass, delete gating and cleanup-first delete, usage preservation and id floors against real SQLite, lock handling against real git (including a German locale), retention expiry, and the board and settings controls. Reverting the banner filter fails its test.
- Ran the desktop app on isolated data: delete succeeds, a refused cleanup keeps the session, retention saves, and a sweep failure is recorded without a banner.
- Not run locally: Docker-based jobs, Windows and Linux.

title: feat(session-import): import Pi harness chats
body:
Stacked on #6364 (base: `codex/session-import-build`). Retarget to `main` once #6364 merges.

Extends the local chat import (Claude Code + Codex) to the **Pi** harness (agent id `pi`, driver `piacp`). Only Pi is added; Pi-specific logic lives in new files and shared files only register the harness, so sibling harness PRs stay mergeable.

## Verified Pi facts (re-checked read-only on a real `~/.pi/agent`)

- **State root / env:** `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, default `~/.pi/agent`.
- **Files:** one JSONL per conversation at `sessions/--<cwd-dashed>--/<ISO-time>_<uuid>.jsonl`. Each file is its own conversation.
- **Native ID:** the UUID (v7) in the file name, confirmed equal to the `id` in the file's `session` header record. The parser derives the native ID from the name and rejects a header `id` that disagrees (`native identity mismatch`).
- **cwd:** taken from the `session` header (absolute), never the lossy dashed folder name.
- **Transcript:** records are `type:"session"` (header) and `type:"message"` with `message.role` (`user`/`assistant`/`toolResult`) and `content` blocks (`text`/`thinking`/`toolCall`). Only user/assistant `text` is imported; thinking, tool calls, `toolResult` messages, `model_change`/`thinking_level_change` records are dropped. Oversize/torn records reuse the shared `readOne`/`eachRecord`/`recordSkim` skimming; title and last-activity derive as for the other harnesses. **Pi files are id/parentId trees** (rewinding/branching appends records under an earlier parent), so the reader collects records as tree nodes and walks parent links back from the last appended record, emitting only the active branch in order — modeled on the Claude reader. A dangling parent stops the walk without hiding the reachable branch; held text is bounded during read (`maxClaudeHeld`) and the final visible-budget trim is unchanged.

## Resume path (hard gate) — PASSED

Confirmed against the installed `@victor-software-house/pi-acp` 0.17.1 (the driver's tested minimum):

1. It advertises `loadSession: true`, so AO resumes via `session/load`.
2. `loadSession` resolves the session file by id via a global `SessionManager.listAll()` scan (`resolveSessionFile`), which is **cwd-independent** and includes sessions created by the Pi CLI/TUI, then opens it with the **caller's cwd** (the AO worktree).
3. It keeps `params.sessionId` as the session id and continues appending to the same resolved file, so the native id is **not forked** — the resumed conversation reports the original ID, satisfying `chat_spawn`'s same-ID check.

## Touchpoints

- `sessionimport/service.go`: register the `pi` root, scan list, discover dir (`sessions`) + `.jsonl` filter, and `nativeID()`.
- `sessionimport/transcript.go`: dispatch Pi to `readPiTranscript`.
- `sessionimport/pi.go` (new): Pi discover helper + transcript parser.
- `session_manager/session_import.go`: resume config env key (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`); open-elsewhere writer detection for Pi (see below).
- `adapters/agent/pi/continuation.go` (new): `NativeSessionConfigDir`, `ProbeNativeSession`, `LocateTranscript` (resolves by id across cwd folders, mirroring pi-acp).
- Frontend: add `pi` to `IMPORTABLE_AGENTS` (generic copy; no harness-specific strings needed).

## Open-elsewhere (writer) detection

**Pi has no open-elsewhere protection, by design here.** It keeps no writer lock or live-session registry, and — unlike Claude/Codex — it does not hold its session file open: the pi CLI/TUI and pi-acp persist with `appendFileSync`/`writeFileSync`, so `lsof` would only catch a Pi writer during the instant of a write. pi-acp's `session/load` also does not refuse a second writer. The only candidate positive signals are unreliable (argv `--session <id>` appears only on a *resumed* TUI, missing the original still-open session; cwd equality is ambiguous across sibling sessions in one `--cwd-dashed--` folder), so rather than ship a check that looks protective but never fires, none is added. `importOwnedElsewhere` falls through to the shared `writableTranscriptOwner`, which matches only Claude/Codex, so Pi is always treated as not-owned; both functions document this. Consequence: importing a Pi conversation that is still open in the Pi CLI/TUI can interleave turns with the other writer — the documented posture for lock-less providers (same as OpenCode in the rollout plan). Claude/Codex detection is unchanged.

## Tests

- `sessionimport/pi_test.go`: keep only user/assistant text (drop thinking/toolCall/toolResult), cwd/title/native-ID from header, native-ID mismatch rejection, tool-only conversation rejection, discovery grouping one file per conversation keyed by UUID. Active-branch tests: linear chat unchanged, a rewind shows only the replacement, a session branched at its root shows only the active branch, and a missing parent is tolerated.
- `agent/pi/continuation_test.go`: config-dir env/default resolution, locate-by-id across cwd folders, probe availability tri-state, invalid-ID rejection.
- Frontend: `IMPORTABLE_AGENTS` gate includes `pi`.

## Not verified end-to-end

- No live end-to-end import+resume was run (CI-only validation per repo rules).
- The chat's last model is intentionally not stored for Pi; `session/load` restores the session's own model state.

title: feat(sessionimport): import OpenCode chats
body:
Stacked on #6364 (Import Claude Code and Codex chats); base is `codex/session-import-build`, not `main`. Retarget to `main` when #6364 merges.

Adds session import for the **OpenCode** harness (agent id `opencode`), the ninth row of the per-harness rollout.

## What's different about OpenCode
OpenCode keeps every conversation as rows in **one global SQLite database** (`opencode.db`) instead of a file per chat. So discovery and parsing read the database **read-only** (`mode=ro`, never written or checkpointed, `busy_timeout` to ride out OpenCode's own writes) rather than walking a `projects` tree. Session content lives in `message` (role) + `part` (type=`text`) tables; `session_message`/`session_input` are unused in current OpenCode.

## Touchpoints (per the plan)
Logic is in **new files**; shared files only register the harness.

- **New `backend/internal/service/sessionimport/opencode.go`** — root resolution (`OPENCODE_DATA_DIR` → `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode` → `~/.local/share/opencode`), `discoverOpenCode` (top-level, non-archived sessions, newest first; child sub-agent and archived rows excluded), and `readOpenCodeTranscript` (user/assistant **text** parts only — tool/reasoning/step parts are provider internals; placeholder `New session - <ISO>` titles fall back to the opening prompt; cwd from the session row; per-message and overall visible-byte budget via the shared `trimVisible`).
- **New `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/continuation.go`** — `NativeSessionConfigDir` and `ProbeNativeSession` (a read-only row lookup) for the resume/adopt path.
- `service.go` — add the `roots` entry, a `discover` dispatch to `discoverOpenCode`, and `opencode` to the scan list.
- `transcript.go` — dispatch `readTranscript` to `readOpenCodeTranscript`.
- `session_manager/session_import.go` — resume config-env key `OPENCODE_DATA_DIR`; open-elsewhere returns **not-owned** for OpenCode (no per-session lock, live-session registry, or writable transcript file — documented). The `writableTranscriptOwner` process-name list is intentionally **not** extended: OpenCode short-circuits before that fallback, which only runs on a real transcript file path.
- Frontend `IMPORTABLE_AGENTS` gains `opencode`.
- Tests: synthetic SQLite fixtures for discovery/parsing, child + archived exclusion, text-only filtering, title fallback, non-conversation rejection; `ProbeNativeSession`/`NativeSessionConfigDir`; open-elsewhere not-owned; frontend gate.

## Verified facts
- **Format**: OpenCode 1.19.3, `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (SQLite, WAL). `session` rows (`id` = `ses_…`, `directory` = cwd, `title`, `time_updated`, `parent_id`, `time_archived`); content in `message` + `part`.
- **Native ID**: the `ses_…` session id, stored verbatim as `ProviderConversationID`; `opencodeidentity.Decode` returns a bare id unchanged for the v1 harness.
- **Resume route (hard gate) — verified empirically against the real `opencode acp` (1.19.3):** `initialize` advertises `loadSession: true`; `session/load` of a **CLI/TUI-created** session with a **mismatched cwd** (a non-original directory) replayed the full history (user + assistant chunks) by native id and did **not** fork it into a new id. The shared ACP driver uses `session/load` when `loadSession` is advertised, so an imported chat opens by native id from the AO worktree cwd.

## Not verified end-to-end
- No local `go build/test/vet`, `npm ci`, lint or typecheck were run (per the rollout rules); relying on PR CI.
- Full open-of-an-imported-chat through the AO UI was not exercised end-to-end; the resume protocol behavior it depends on was verified directly against `opencode acp` as above.

title: feat(sessionimport): import Droid (Factory) chat sessions
body:
Stacked on #6364 (base branch `codex/session-import-build`). Retarget to `main` when #6364 merges.

Adds session import for the **Droid** (Factory) harness (agent id `droid`), the fourth importable Chat harness after Claude Code and Codex.

## What Droid stores
`~/.factory/sessions/-<cwd-dashed>/<uuid>.jsonl`, beside a `<uuid>.settings.json` sidecar (and `.bak`) that import ignores. Records: a single `session_start` (`id`, `title`, `cwd`, `owner`) then `message` records (`role`, `content` blocks). Other record types (`todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`) are skipped.

The file name is the native session id and matches `session_start.id`; a mismatch rejects the file. Verified read-only against real local histories (droid 0.251.0); fixtures are synthetic.

## Parsing
- Keeps user/assistant **text** only; drops `thinking`, `tool_use`, `tool_result` blocks.
- Drops injected context: user-role records whose id carries a `context-` prefix (system reminders / tool catalogs), so titles and the first prompt are real.
- Placeholder titles (`New Session`, `Start new chat`) fall back to the first prompt.

## Resume path (hard gate) — PASSES
Opening an imported chat calls droidacp's `Resume` with `ProviderConversationID = NativeID`. Verified from the droid 0.251.0 binary:
1. The ACP daemon (`droid exec --output-format acp-daemon`) advertises `loadSession: true`.
2. Droid's session resolver locates `<id>.jsonl` by **scanning every `-<cwd-dashed>` folder** (plus flat and `btw` fallbacks), independent of cwd — so `session/load` with cwd set to the **AO worktree** finds a CLI/TUI-created session.
3. The native id is preserved: droidacp leaves `Encode/DecodeProviderConversationID` nil, so the raw UUID flows through `session/load` and is reported back unchanged, satisfying the chat_spawn "did the provider resume the original conversation" check.

## Touchpoints
- **State root + env override:** `FACTORY_HOME_OVERRIDE` (a *home* override — Droid appends `.factory`), default `~/.factory`. Both the import roots map and `applyImportedConfigEnv` account for the home-vs-dir distinction (the override is pointed at the parent of the config dir).
- **New files:** `service/sessionimport/droid.go` (root + record parsing), `adapters/agent/droid/continuation.go` (`ContinuationCapabilities`, `NativeSessionConfigDir`, `ProbeNativeSession`, `LocateTranscript`).
- **Shared files — registration only:** discover dir/filter + `nativeID` + scan list (`service.go`), native-id + parse dispatch (`transcript.go`), config-env key + `droid` writer name in the lsof fallback (`session_import.go`), `IMPORTABLE_AGENTS` (`SessionImportPanel.tsx`). Expect only trivial conflicts with sibling harness PRs on these lines.
- **Open elsewhere:** Droid has no per-session lock or live-session registry, so detection relies on the shared lsof writer-owner fallback (now matching the `droid` process name). `adoptedOwnedElsewhere` returns not-owned for Droid — documented limitation.

## Not wired
Model is not imported into session metadata: Droid uses custom per-org model ids that need not map to AO's catalog, so resume uses the user's default model.

## Tests (synthetic fixtures)
- Discovery grouping + sidecar skipping; `FACTORY_HOME_OVERRIDE` root resolution.
- Transcript parsing: injected-context / thinking / tool noise stripping, placeholder-title fallback, native-id mismatch and missing-`session_start` rejection, context-only rejection.
- Continuation: `NativeSessionConfigDir` (override + HOME), `LocateTranscript` across folders / flat / absent / non-uuid, `ProbeNativeSession`.
- `applyImportedConfigEnv` home-override behavior; frontend `IMPORTABLE_AGENTS` gate.

Not run locally per repo policy (CI verifies).

title: feat(chat): import local Kimi sessions
body:
Stacked on #6364 (Claude Code + Codex chat import). Base this on `codex/session-import-build`; retarget to `main` once #6364 merges.

## What

Adds session import for the **Kimi** harness (agent id `kimi`): a user's local Kimi Code chats import into AO as Chat sessions and resume over ACP.

## Verified facts (read-only inspection)

- **Root:** `KIMI_CODE_HOME`, default `~/.kimi-code` (confirmed in `dist/main.mjs`: `getDataDir()` = `KIMI_CODE_HOME` env, else `~/.kimi-code`).
- **Layout:** one conversation per `sessions/wd_<name>_<hash>/session_<uuid>/`; the resumable transcript is the main agent's `agents/main/wire.jsonl`, with title/cwd in a sibling `state.json`.
- **Native id:** the `session_<uuid>` directory name — what `kimi --session` and ACP `session/load` both accept.
- **Transcript format:** `wire.jsonl` is JSONL. Typed prompts are `context.append_message` with `role=user` and `origin.kind=user`; injected context (`injection`, `skill_activation`) is dropped so titles are real prompts. Assistant text is `context.append_loop_event` → `content.part` of type `text`, grouped on the user-prompt (turn) boundary; `think` (reasoning), tool calls and tool results are dropped. `turnId` is deliberately not parsed (its JSON type varies string/number across versions).
- **Retractions:** context.clear resets the collected history; context.undo retracts the last N undo anchors, matching Kimi 2.3.3 applyUndo/isUndoAnchor (origin-less and origin.kind==user non-inTurn prompts plus user-slash skill/plugin activations are anchors; injected context is skipped; undo stops at a context.apply_compaction).

## Resume & auth — what was and was not verified

**Verified by executing `kimi acp` 2.3.3 (read-only session/load probe, since removed):**
- `kimi acp` advertises `loadSession`.
- `session/load` of a **CLI-created** session (`kimi -p`) from a **different cwd** (an AO-worktree-like path) succeeds, replays the stored history, and reports the **same** `session_<uuid>` — it does **not** fork the id. This is the import's hard gate (chat_spawn requires the resumed id to equal the imported NativeID).

**Verified by read-only source/code inspection (not executed):**
- Opening an imported Kimi chat must run with `KIMI_CODE_HOME` = the source home, because Kimi reads sessions only from its home. `KIMI_SHARE_DIR` is **only** the legacy kimi-cli migration source (`resolveLegacySourceHome`), and there is no sessions-dir or session-path launch arg — so keeping AO's managed home and redirecting only the session lookup (preferred option 1) is not possible.
- That override is **equivalent to a managed Kimi chat**: AO's managed home only mirrors the same login (`ShareCredentials` symlinks its credentials to the user home and seeds its config from it), so auth resolves to the exact credentials AO's own Kimi auth check reads; standing instructions reach the ACP session via the workspace `.kimi-code/AGENTS.md` + first-prompt preamble (home-independent); and the `config.toml` lifecycle hooks are TUI-only and unused by the ACP chat driver. Documented on `applyImportedConfigEnv` and covered by a regression test.

**NOT verified (could not, and did not re-run kimi):**
- A fully authenticated live import → open → resume through the AO UI. The probe's `session/load` returned `Authentication required` on this machine because its `managed:kimi-code` OAuth token is empty (the only working provider here is `zai`, whose login was used to confirm `session/new`/`session/load` mechanics). AO only offers the import when the user's Kimi login is authorized, and the launch uses that same login — but an end-to-end authenticated resume was not demonstrated.

## Scope

Kimi logic is in new files — `backend/internal/service/sessionimport/kimi.go` and `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/continuation.go`. Shared files gain only registration entries (roots map, `discover`/`readTranscript` dispatch, scan list, config env key, open-elsewhere check (Kimi per-session lock), `IMPORTABLE_AGENTS`), so sibling harness PRs stay mergeable.

## Tests

- `sessionimport`: synthetic discovery + parsing, native-id grouping (subagent/stray files ignored), injected-context stripping, title fallback without `state.json`, `state.json` id mismatch, non-conversation rejection; undo-anchor parity (origin-less prompt, in-turn steer, user-slash skill, undo across compaction, over-count undo).
- `agent/kimi`: `NativeSessionConfigDir`, `LocateTranscript`/`ProbeNativeSession` (found/missing/bad-id).
- `session_manager`: imported-chat `KIMI_CODE_HOME` points at the source home; `kimiSessionLocked` open-elsewhere matching (missing/malformed lock, dead pid, another host, live pid).
- frontend: `IMPORTABLE_AGENTS` gate.

All fixtures are synthetic; no real user content is included.
