title: feat(session-import): fully import and resume Qwen chats
body:
Code changes: +615 -5  
Tests: +854 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## What
Import Qwen Code conversations with editable history and native continuation. Extends #6364 on `codex/session-import-build` (current shared base `0427cd4de3e8cc2c812e9b389d37d9648d1c0a0c`; relocation contract introduced in `0c21910ea804984ac4855c2d1fde12b2aa05a9fd`). Supersedes this PR's earlier history-only implementation.

## Why
Qwen locates a conversation within the launch cwd's project directory. First-open relocation lets AO continue the same conversation from its own workspace while preserving the original transcript.

## Before / After
| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen is absent from the base import selector. Native history in another directory cannot load from AO's worktree. | Qwen chats are discoverable and importable; first open copies the native transcript into Qwen's lookup location, then resumes with the original native ID. |
| The earlier version of this PR locked imported Qwen composers. | Full import uses the existing editable/resume flow; the history-only UI and duplicate frontend state are removed. |

The change registers Qwen in the existing import UI. App screenshots were not captured because local app servers/builds/checks are explicitly out of scope for this task.

## How
- Same-UUID physical fragments form one logical message: append visible parts, keep first parent/role/display metadata, and use the latest timestamp. Combined text is capped with a valid UTF-8 prefix; native artifact/control records do not change the active leaf. See [Qwen fragment aggregation](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/v0.26.4/packages/core/src/utils/transcript-records.ts#L512-L550).
- Qwen-specific projection follows `uuid`/`parentUuid` through tool and system metadata, so rewound branches are excluded. User messages prefer `systemPayload.displayText`, keeping expanded resources and hook context out of messages and titles. The format is pinned from [Qwen rewind recording](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/v0.26.4/packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.ts#L3652-L3658) and its [prompt projection contract](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/v0.26.4/packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.ts#L605-L619).
- Qwen-local discovery/parser reads `$QWEN_HOME/projects/*/chats/<uuid>.jsonl` (default `~/.qwen`), excludes archives and non-transcripts, displays only `real_user` / `assistant_output`, strips thinking/tool/injected context, and rejects identity mismatches or promptless files.
- Qwen 0.26.4 source pins the sanitizer: lowercase on Windows, then replace each `[^A-Za-z0-9]` UTF-16 code unit with `-`. Fixtures cover underscore, space, Unicode, emoji and Windows paths.
- ACP uses **raw LaunchCWD**, including symlink spelling: destination `projects/<sanitize(raw LaunchCWD)>/chats/<nativeID>.jsonl`; rewrite every record's `cwd` to raw LaunchCWD. No symlink resolution for destination naming.
- Adapter implements only the base `AgentImportedSessionRelocator`, calling `importcopy.CopyOnce` with nonempty-record validation. The base owns private atomic no-overwrite copy, pre-adoption ResumeCwd persistence, pinned later launches and rejection of nonempty imports without readable message replay. No competing preparer, priorCwd or post-adoption CAS.
- Existing destinations retain AO appends and never overwrite the original. `QWEN_HOME` is propagated only when needed.
- Open-elsewhere checks inspect native `sessions/*.json` and `chats/<id>.runtime.json`, validating native ID, workspace, PID, process name/start time and Linux procStart token when supplied. Unreadable or stale records are not positive ownership evidence. Runtime records from another hostname cannot be locally verified.

## Testing

Qwen parser, relocation, ownership and synthetic fixtures are unchanged from the prior head. - Implementation tests/builds/formatters/generation/typechecks/lint run **only in GitHub Actions**, per user instruction. No local implementation validation was run. Current-head Actions are pending.

The current merge proceeded under the explicit instruction to merge now and obtain fresh CI. No LAN production code/test edit or second retry was made.

The takeover's earlier native run reproduced those results with CLI-created native ID `e0b99986-416c-4377-8c12-69cfa8ad84a0`, 3 replay chunks, original and appended code-word recall across later open, destination growth and an unchanged original hash. **Isolation limitation:** that run copied model/auth configuration into scratch, so it does not satisfy the subsequently clarified no-config/credential-copy procedure. title: feat(session-import): import and resume OMP chats
body:
Code changes: +525 -10  
Tests: +535 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Extends #6364 with full import and continuation of OMP CLI/TUI conversations. Keeps existing PR #7446, now including a normal merge of published `codex/session-import-build` commit `acc4f849ba1b94dcb7bf6ef01d6d4952449937a2`; it no longer depends on Qwen #7445.

## Why

OMP finds an ACP conversation in the folder for its launch cwd. Importing history alone cannot continue it from an AO worktree. The OMP adapter now copies the transcript for AO's first launch, preserves its native ID, and leaves the original untouched.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| OMP is absent from the base branch's import list. Loading its native ID from another cwd fails. | OMP chats can be selected for import and continued in AO after a private transcript copy is prepared. |
| The previous version of this PR offered a read-only archive. | Imports use #6364's normal editable Chat flow and pinned resume directory. |
| Another OMP writer can hold the same native conversation. | A held per-transcript `.lock.os` blocks opening before and after adoption; idle sessions without a held lock remain undetectable. |

This only registers OMP in the existing import panel; the panel layout and shared Chat UI are unchanged. Desktop screenshots and full in-app verification are not available under the task's CI-only execution scope.

## How

OMP-specific logic lives in new parser, adapter continuation, and ownership files; shared files contain registration entries only. No shared relocation machinery or Qwen changes are included.

Verified against installed OMP 18.14.0:

- Root: `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, default `~/.omp/agent`.
- Source: JSONL under `sessions/<cwd-folder>/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl`; the filename UUID agrees with the session record ID. cwd comes from the session record, which may follow a title record.
- Import follows the active parent chain, keeps user/assistant text, omits system/tool/thinking traffic, and preserves active model/thinking settings. Shared confined streaming readers handle oversized or torn records; retained branch text is bounded before the active leaf is known. First-open archive refresh picks up later messages.
- `RelocateImportedSession` uses #6364's four-argument `importcopy.CopyOnce`. Folder encoding uses resolved LaunchCWD with OMP's home-relative/full-path rules; only the session-record cwd becomes raw LaunchCWD. Require exactly one session record with the expected native ID. The shared helper publishes a private copy atomically and preserves an existing destination holding AO turns.
- #6364 owns `ResumeCwd`, later-open pinning, and the empty-history replay guard. No read-only mechanism remains in this PR.
- OMP's `.<transcript-basename>.lock.os` is probed as an OS writer lock in original and copied cwd folders. **Live check:** monitoring a throwaway OMP prompt observed a held native `flock`, confirming the probe matches the provider. **Limitation:** live OMP 18.14.0 has no lock file after ACP load and leaves an unheld file after a completed prompt; idle CLI/ACP sessions therefore cannot always be detected. File existence alone is never treated as a live owner. As in the shared base, Windows lock probing relies on provider refusal rather than a local `LockFileEx` probe.

## Testing

- Synthetic tests cover discovery/import/refresh, UUID grouping/mismatch, visible-text filtering, active branch/model selection, torn/oversized records, bounded branch text, config roots, continuation probes, held/stale/released locks, and the frontend gate.
- Relocation tests cover title-before-session, preserved native ID and large numeric fields, symlinked LaunchCWD (resolved folder/raw header), private permissions, unchanged source, duplicate/missing/wrong headers, and preserving AO turns when the source is gone.
- Validation runs in Actions only. All 30 checks passed on merged head `7d9048a1fad6dc65a40b189b7603287502000d06`: [Go](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41569024806), [Frontend](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41569024953), [CLI E2E](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41569024899), [gitleaks](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41569024702), and [Public boundary](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41569024878) all completed successfully, including SQLC/API drift checks. Published base `acc4f849ba1b94dcb7bf6ef01d6d4952449937a2` includes the exact hosted SQLC placeholder repair; its generated output was inherited unchanged. No local generation, hand editing of generated files, or local project validation was used. Earlier-head results do not validate this new head.
- **Fresh scoped live proof, OMP 18.14.0 (two isolated runs):** created a synthetic chat with the CLI in folder A. ACP `session/load` from symlinked `/tmp/.../B` (resolved `/private/tmp/.../B`) failed before the copy; with the same basename/UUID in the resolved cwd folder and raw cwd in the session record, it replayed the original history. A follow-up recalled the original code word. The native UUID stayed the same, source bytes stayed unchanged, copy mode was 0600, and all temporary chats/state were deleted. This validates the provider path directly; the merged Go implementation and synthetic fixtures passed the exact-head Actions checks linked above. This provider proof does not replace a full desktop import/open/continue test.

title: release: promote main (fe0550a4e8) to stable, 2026-10-29
body:
## What

Moves `stable` from `e16e6f0022` (v0.14.7 plus the #7383 hotfix, 2026-10-28) to `main` as of 2026-10-29 (`fe0550a4e8`, #7430). That is 68 commits. Three of them are already on `stable` as cherry-picks or a hotfix (#7322, #7329, #7382), so their content doesn't change. Version: **0.14.8**.

This is the release that ships the new macOS DMG install window (#7418), so the conductor follow-up OrchestratorInc/ao-releases#49 has to merge between fast-forwarding and running the release (see **Merging**).

### Why there is a merge commit

`stable` is not an ancestor of `main`. It carries the #7383 hotfix (`4cd1464d79`) and its merge, the #7314 cherry-picks, and the old #7063 squash (`7b176b7ad3`). Each of those is already on `main` with identical content:

- the hotfix as #7382 (`f230a47d94`); `frontend/scripts/build-acp-runtime.mjs` is byte-identical
- the cherry-picks as #7322 and #7329 (`git log --cherry-mark` marks all three as equivalent)
- the #7063 squash's tree is identical to `ad4968a1bb` on `main`

This branch is `fe0550a4e8` plus one merge of `stable` made like `-s ours` (`cf09b3630e`). That merge changes no files: its tree is byte-identical to `fe0550a4e8` (`git diff fe0550a4e8 cf09b3630e` is empty). It only makes `stable` an ancestor again, so this release can fast-forward. There are no cherry-picks on top.

## Validation

- **CI on `fe0550a4e8`:** no check failed (37 passed, 55 skipped by path filters), including the macOS `mac-dmg-layout` job #7418 adds.
- **Already shipped as a nightly:** `v0.14.8-nightly.202610291902` was built from exactly `fe0550a4e8`, so this release is the code nightly users already run.
- **#7418 (DMG):** verified in its PR with a real unsigned build, real Finder captures, and the inner app's seal (codesign, stapler, Gatekeeper) on a signed, stapled build. The first end-to-end **notarization of the new DMG container** happens in this release's stable run (see **Merging**).
- **Not done yet:** a desktop smoke test (local and Cloud) on `cf09b3630e`. Please run the usual smoke test before fast-forwarding.

## Migrations

- **Cloud (Postgres):** none in this repo. The control plane moved to its own private repository (#7352) and migrates on its own deploys.
- **Local SQLite:** 4 new migrations, applied automatically when the desktop updates. A desktop cannot move back to an older build after these:
  - `20261021051727800_conversation_batch_members` (#6504)
  - `20261023123504180_app_settings_computer_use` (#7018)
  - `20261026185532680_usage_telemetry_measurements` (#7304)
  - `20261028124744441_telemetry_incremental_vacuum` (#5178)

## Merging

Do not use the merge button. This repo allows squash only, and a squash breaks `stable`'s ancestry with `main` again. After approval and the smoke test, fast-forward instead:

```sh
git push origin cf09b3630ebec2d3a7f2971dd596cb935a4c9e1c:stable
```

GitHub marks this PR merged once `stable` contains its head. Then, **before** releasing, merge OrchestratorInc/ao-releases#49. It switches the conductor from a bare `hdiutil create` to `frontend/scripts/build-mac-dmg.mjs`, which only exists on `stable` after the fast-forward. Then release:

```sh
gh workflow run stable.yml --repo OrchestratorInc/ao-releases -f version=0.14.8
```

If Apple rejects the new DMG, the conductor's "Verify shipped macOS artifacts" gate fails before any release is created, so nothing is published. Revert ao-releases#49 and re-run the same command to ship with the old DMG.

title: feat(project-config): load orchestrator rules from a repo file (orchestratorRulesFile)
body:
Code changes: +85 -58 (about 45 of each is gofmt realigning the CLI config struct)\
Tests: +76 -6\
Others: +8 -3 (generated OpenAPI + TS types, docs)

## What

Adds `orchestratorRulesFile` to project config. It works like `agentRulesFile` does for workers: a repo-relative file whose contents are appended to the orchestrator's standing rules when it spawns. Inline `orchestratorRules` and the file both apply, inline first.

## Why

Fixes #2071

Long orchestrator instructions could only live as inline text in local project config, with no way to keep them in the repo and review them like worker rules. Taken over from #5256 by @alerios (credited as co-author), cut down to what #2071 asks for.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Project config has no `orchestratorRulesFile`; the CLI silently ignores the key | `ao project set-config e2e --orchestrator-rules-file docs/orch-rules.md`, then `ao project get --json` shows `"orchestratorRulesFile": "docs/orch-rules.md"` |
| No way to load orchestrator rules from a file | Spawned orchestrator's `system.md` has the file text under `## Project-Specific Orchestrator Rules` |
| n/a | `--orchestrator-rules-file ../escape.md` fails: `orchestratorRulesFile "../escape.md": path must be repo-relative and must not escape the project root (INVALID_PROJECT_CONFIG)` |
| n/a | Missing file fails spawn: `read orchestratorRulesFile docs/missing.md: ... no such file or directory (SPAWN_PROMPT_FAILED)` |

## How

- `domain.ProjectConfig` gets the field, validated by the same repo-relative check as `agentRulesFile`.
- The existing worker rules loader now takes role-neutral fields plus the config key name, so both roles share one read path and errors name the exact key.
- Wired into `buildSystemPrompt`, which spawn and restore both call.
- The hand-written CLI mirror carries the field and a `--orchestrator-rules-file` flag.

Left out on purpose:
- `~/` and absolute paths. #2071 asks for them, but also asks for parity with `agentRulesFile`, which is repo-relative on main. Both fields should change together if we want that.
- The Restart button from #5256. Not part of #2071, and main's board topbar has changed since.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, focused `go test` for `internal/domain`, `internal/cli`, `internal/session_manager`, `internal/httpd/apispec`.
- Real isolated daemon (`AO_DATA_DIR` under /tmp): set the field via the CLI, spawned a claude-code orchestrator, and found the marker line from the rules file in the session's `system.md` passed via `--append-system-prompt-file`. Also checked the traversal and missing-file errors above.

title: feat(chat): support Codex MCP Apps on desktop and mobile
body:
Code changes: +1575 -8  
Tests: +733 -0  
Others: +905 -24  

## What

Render Codex MCP Apps in desktop, remote-host, and mobile chat. Apps stay visible after tool work folds, can exchange context and approved actions with their originating server, and retain saved documents after the provider stops.

## Why

AO already renders agent-authored HTML. The missing T3 Code capability was hosting MCP Apps returned by Codex tools, including their interaction protocol. This adds that public integration; it does not claim access to ChatGPT's native Intelligent UI stream.

Compared against [T3 Code's MCP Apps host](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/dd148481531a0a090780a2ade20588566db099a2/packages/client-runtime/src/mcpApps/host.ts): initialization/input/result, tools/resources, approved messages, model context, links, downloads, themes, resizing, fullscreen, teardown, and saved views are covered. Desktop fullscreen preserves the iframe; native mobile fullscreen reloads its WebView. The host also handles tool results arriving after initial input and binds approvals to exact actions with expiring single-use tokens.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Codex MCP tools show only an expandable arguments/result row. | Compatible tools render an interactive app inline, outside the completed-work fold, with raw output still accessible. |
| No MCP app interaction bridge. | Server-bound tools/resources, text messages, latest app context, confirmed links, and embedded/resource-link exports. |
| No durable MCP app view. | Saved documents and their policy remain readable after stop; actions require the originating live conversation. |

Real Electron captures use the same scratch conversation and window size. GitHub attachment upload is unavailable through the CLI; captures are available locally for attachment:

- Before: `/tmp/ao-412-mcp-before.png`
- After: `/tmp/ao-412-mcp-after.png`
- Expanded Europe selection: `/tmp/ao-412-mcp-expanded.png`

## How

- Advertise the MCP UI extension and bridge Codex's native resource/tool RPCs through an optional driver port.
- Store full tool data, validated HTML/policy, and latest context separately from compact timeline detail. Active-branch and rollback checks govern access.
- Keep authority in the daemon: originating server/thread, tool visibility, one-use write/message approvals, a limit of 16 pending approvals per app activity/controller generation, and dispatch serialized with conversation changes.
- Share the protocol host across desktop and mobile, with desktop controls translated in all nine supported locales. Use opaque document sandboxes, declared CSP domains, and existing desktop navigation/network guards. Remote proxy capabilities never enter iframe URLs or documents.
- Add the migration, generated API/storage bindings, and support/limit documentation in `docs/mcp-apps.md`.

## Testing

Rebased onto `main` at `254ec57baf`; retained both branches’ migration registry entries and added MCP Apps translations for the Russian locale newly introduced on `main`. Current head `0b815a1771`: API/SQLC drift, shared package checks, desktop/mobile typechecks, and all 266 mobile files / 2,766 tests pass locally. Focused MCP/migration tests, all four full SQLite race shards, build/vet, and pinned lint also pass. Broad local Go/desktop runs encountered timing/environment failures; the conditional Git include failure reproduces on the exact base. Remaining local runs were stopped after host load exceeded 280. On this head, desktop (all four test shards, renderer smoke, typecheck), mobile, and both chat race shards pass in CI. Current CI status: 22 passing, 7 pending, no failures; remaining backend jobs are awaiting completion.

The previous head passed [all 31 checks](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7449/checks) on `99546b0c43`, including Go races, all frontend shards and renderer smoke, mobile, native Windows/macOS/Linux CLI tests, fresh-install container, lint and generated-contract checks.

The approval-isolation follow-up passes both complete chat race-test shards, focused MCP Apps race tests, build, vet, and golangci-lint v2.13.2. All six workflows completed successfully on that head.

Passed locally:

- Go build/vet, golangci-lint v2.13.2, focused MCP Apps race tests (including approval-budget isolation, consumption and expiry), API/SQLC drift checks, and native CLI e2e.
- Shared package typechecks/tests; desktop/mobile typechecks; full mobile suite (252 files, 2,635 tests); pinned Node compatibility and package checks.
- MCP Apps Playwright scenario and real Electron checks for terminal, daemon-browser, and mobile-control boundaries.

title: [Feature]: Let users choose the authenticated remote listener port
body:
## Problem

The default remote-access port may be reserved or unavailable. If AO chooses another port, a saved connection address can stop working. There is no supported option to choose the port for the authenticated remote listener.

### Expected outcome

Let users choose an available port and keep it across restarts, without changing pairing credentials.

### Current workaround

Use a separate local port forwarder. It provides a fixed address and forwards connections to AO's actual authenticated port.

## Proposed direction

Add `--port` to `ao remote-host enable`, or an equivalent setting. Remember the chosen port, keep authentication unchanged, and give a clear error if the port cannot be used.

## Alternatives considered

`AO_PORT` changes the separate local API port, so it does not solve this problem.

## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: [Bug]: Handle reserved Windows ports during daemon startup
body:
## What went wrong?

Windows can reserve a port even when no visible application is using it. AO tries another port for `WSAEADDRINUSE` (port already in use), but a reserved port can return `WSAEACCES` (access denied) instead. That error stops startup without trying another port.

This is based on the [Windows error check](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/v0.14.7/backend/internal/httpd/addr_in_use_windows.go) and [listener startup code](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/v0.14.7/backend/internal/httpd/server.go). The same handling remains in reviewed main. This is a source-review finding; a fresh Windows startup reproduction on this release has not been performed.

### Expected outcome

AO should try an available localhost port and tell the desktop which port it selected. If that also fails, show a clear error.

### Current workaround

Set `AO_PORT` to an allowed port before starting the Windows app.

### Proposed implementation

Extend the existing Windows bind fallback to cover `WSAEACCES`. Ask the operating system for an available localhost port and reuse the existing port-discovery logic. Keep the original error if the retry fails. Add tests for occupied and access-denied ports.

title: Browser annotations are re-sent with every later annotation message
body:
Reported by the user in a Claude Code chat session (`ao-landing-14`, project `ao-landing`). The user annotated a page in the Browser panel and sent the batch: 3 comments plus 1 reference screenshot. Later they added one new annotation on the same page and sent it. The new message re-sent all 3 earlier annotations plus the new 4th. Annotations aren't cleared after they're sent, so they pile up into every later message. The second message was shown as "Queued · sends when the agent finishes".

Expected: once a message carrying annotations is accepted (sent or queued), those annotations are consumed and the next message carries only new ones. A failed send should keep them for retry.

title: fix(browser): drop sent annotations from the page's batch
body:
Part of #7455 (first symptom: earlier Browser-panel annotations are re-sent with every later batch).

## Summary
- In `completeAnnotation`, after a successful send, main now gives the page a fresh, empty annotation session. Before, it sent `setMode` with no session. `annotate-preload.ts` only replaces its in-page batch when handed a session (or when the URL changes), so on the same page it kept every sent annotation, and the next submit re-sent them.
- The reset is also sent when the submitting tab is in the background. A failed send keeps the batch for retry, as before.
- Regression from #5396, which introduced batched annotation sessions held by the page.

Queued vs immediate delivery isn't the trigger: `/send` succeeds in both cases. The chat composer's excerpt and file-reference clearing is unaffected.

## Tests

  - The active tab gets an empty batch on success. Fails on `main`.

- `tsgo --noEmit` reports no errors in the changed files. The remaining errors come from `packages/` deps that aren't installed in this worktree.

## Risks / follow-ups

body:
Reported by a user in the AO desktop app (0.14.8 update pending, macOS):

In the left sidebar, clicking a project's orchestrator button (the tree/hierarchy icon next to a project name, e.g. agent-orchestrator or ao-landing) makes the Scratchpad section expand and show its sessions, even though it had been collapsed.

Expected: opening a project's orchestrator reveals that project at most; the Scratchpad's collapsed/expanded choice is respected.

title: fix(sidebar): keep a closed Scratchpad closed when opening an orchestrator
body:
Fixes #7459

Clicking a project's orchestrator button expanded a collapsed Scratchpad section.

**Cause.** #6531 added a reveal effect to `Sidebar.tsx`. When the active session changes, it looks for that session's row. If no row is rendered, it opens Pinned, Projects and Scratchpad. An orchestrator never has a session row: project rows list only workers, and the orchestrator is opened from the header button. So opening an orchestrator always took that path and opened every section.

**Fix.** When the row is missing, open only the sections that hold the active session: Pinned if the session is pinned, then Scratchpad if it is a Scratchpad session, otherwise Projects. Opening an orchestrator now opens only Projects, and the effect already expands that project. The force-open is still not saved, which matches #7360.

**Tests** (`Sidebar.test.tsx`, "Sidebar active-session reveal"):
- `keeps a closed Scratchpad closed when a project's orchestrator opens`
- `reopens a closed Scratchpad, not Projects, to reveal an active Scratchpad session`

Both fail on main and pass with this change. All 160 `Sidebar.test.tsx` tests pass, and `npm run typecheck` shows no errors in `frontend/`. The only errors come from `packages/product-ui`, because that package has no dependencies installed in this worktree.

**Risk.** The decision uses the Pinned and Scratchpad session lists at the moment the session changes. If those lists haven't loaded yet, a Scratchpad session can open Projects rather than Scratchpad on a cold start. Before this change, every section opened in that case.

title: fix(harness): recognize external Codex installs behind launcher symlinks
body:
Code changes: +5 -4  
Tests: +116 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Fix Codex updates rejected with `INSTALL_OWNER_UNCONFIRMED` when AO's harness launcher links to an external installation.

## Why

The reported installation had `<managed-root>/bin/codex -> ~/.local/bin/codex`, with the latter pointing into the official Codex standalone release directory, and no `<managed-root>/codex/managed.json`. AO classified the launcher as managed using its path alone, then required the missing managed record.

The creator of that external link was not established. `ensureManagedLauncher` writes a relative link into AO's own `current` release, and the official installer normally writes `~/.local/bin/codex`. This PR does not establish an automatic AO or Codex installer path that creates the observed external link. The reproduction below creates it manually.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| An explicit Update for a managed-bin launcher pointing to an external official installation is rejected because it has no managed record. | Ownership follows the executable's resolved location. A supported explicit Update installs a fresh AO-managed release and redirects the launcher to it; subsequent AO launches use that release. |
| A stale managed record can assign its installer to an external launcher target. | External targets retain their actual ownership during checks; genuine managed installations still require their record. |
| The external installation remains at its existing version. | Its files and version remain unchanged; only AO's launcher and managed release change on Update. |

Reproduction on an isolated test machine:

1. Use a scratch AO data directory and an official standalone Codex installation older than the release offered by AO.
2. Manually create `<managed-root>/bin/codex` as a symlink to that external installation's executable. Leave `<managed-root>/codex/managed.json` absent.
3. Start AO with that managed root so the Codex adapter selects the launcher, then refresh the Harness page's update advisory.
4. Explicitly choose Update. On the base revision, the request fails with `INSTALL_OWNER_UNCONFIRMED`.
5. With this fix, Update installs a release under `<managed-root>/codex/versions/`, switches `current`, records it, and changes the launcher to `../codex/current/bin/codex`. The external installation is untouched.

Policy: retain AO's existing side-by-side update behavior for supported external installations. An explicit Update adopts the launcher into AO management; ownership/advisory checks alone do not adopt or rewrite it. This is not an in-place update of the user's external copy. External aliases are not asserted to be created automatically by AO.

## How

Use the existing `pathWithin` helper to resolve both the managed root and executable before testing containment. Keep the adapter-selected launcher path for execution. Regression tests cover external official/npm installation adoption, stale records, Homebrew boundaries, genuine managed installations, and subsequent updates. They assert that ownership checks leave the launcher alone, explicit updates redirect it into the managed release, and the external target remains unchanged. The npm operation fixture stubs package ownership; this test exercises update/adoption sequencing rather than npm's ownership probe itself.

No API, database, or UI changes.

## Testing

- All GitHub checks passed for the original head `9a8e721edd`; review follow-up CI is pending for `776b44108b`.
- No local checks were run for this follow-up. The user requires CI-only validation.
- Earlier focused tests, the complete installer service race suite, backend build, and vet passed before the local-validation restriction.

title: fix: update OMP independently of the system Bun runtime
body:
Code changes: +83 -18  
Tests: +326 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Plan Bun-managed OMP updates on macOS and Linux using OMP's self-contained official release, installed into a fresh AO-managed version directory. Disclose the actual installer before execution and keep failed startup stdout and stderr in installation diagnostics.

## Why

OMP 18.14.0 requires Bun 1.4.4 or newer. With Bun 1.3.14, the package installation succeeds but the new executable exits with `Bun runtime must be >= 1.4.4 (found v1.3.14)`. AO previously omitted that startup output and could not activate the update.

The standalone release avoids upgrading a shared Bun runtime that the working OMP installation still uses.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A managed OMP update installs the Bun package, then fails its startup check when the system Bun is too old. | The planner discloses the resolved shell, official script URL, and binary-install arguments. The update installs and verifies the pinned standalone release before switching the active release. |
| Failed startup diagnostics include only `exit status 1`. | Detailed diagnostics retain bounded stdout and stderr, including the actual runtime requirement. The short failure notice stays concise. |
| The working release must survive an unsuccessful update. | Download, startup, and installer-availability failures leave the previous release and launcher selected; unsuccessful candidates are removed. |

## How

- Build the standalone update/reinstall plan in `planForOperation`, using `planShellInstaller`, a shared OMP URL, and the existing isolated `--binary --ref <version>` recipe.
- Preserve the original Bun owner only for request routing and strict ownership verification. The displayed operation command, job method, and successful managed record describe the actual official installer.
- Recognize an already-migrated managed OMP record through its original Bun maintenance entry on macOS/Linux. Subsequent reinstalls repair the standalone copy at its recorded version, and subsequent updates continue to maintain that copy.
- Select the advisory's update-safety plan by that same original owner, so an eligible Bun-to-standalone migration is advertised as safe while unavailable installer prerequisites remain blocked.
- Resolve the shell during planning. A missing shell or unavailable installer produces an Unsupported plan with a reason before execution.
- Preserve the existing version probe, atomic release switch, and candidate cleanup.
- Exercise `AgentPlans` and update/reinstall requests in regressions for command disclosure, resolved interpreters, matching job/record methods, pinned reinstall versions, missing prerequisites, ownership rejection, failed download/startup, and retained startup output. The migration sequence also reinstalls and updates the migrated standalone release through the Bun entry, checking that the launcher selects a new managed release and previous files remain intact.

The existing managed official-installer recipes support macOS/Linux. Windows Bun installations and initial package-manager installations retain their existing paths; this change addresses managed OMP updates without introducing a new runtime distribution mechanism.

## Testing

- Final head: CI-only validation, as requested. No local tests, builds, formatting checks, installs, or other validation were run for the standalone-migration change.
- Added planner/request migration regressions for macOS/Linux and unconfirmed Bun ownership; these await CI.
- Updated the advisory fixture to include the standalone script runner and added missing-runner/missing-shell controls. This addresses the reported `TestAdvisoryUsesManagedUpdatePlan/bun/managed` and `bun/old_npm_runtime` failures; the new head awaits CI.
- The earlier diagnostics-only commit passed the installer package tests, installer race tests, and installer `go vet` before local validation was stopped. Those results do not validate the new planner/migration logic.
- An earlier full backend attempt was stopped after unrelated adapter failures and an ACP replay timeout; it is not reported as passing.

title: feat(artifacts): preview cloud PDF artifacts
body:
Code changes: +36 -20\
Tests: +86 -4\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Cloud PDF artifacts now preview the same way local ones do:

- **Viewer:** opening a cloud PDF (from the session sidebar, the Artifacts page preview modal, or full screen) renders its pages with selectable text and page feedback. Before, it showed the binary-file message.
- **Cards:** cloud PDF cards on the Artifacts page and in the session sidebar render the first page. They share the existing four-live-preview limit with HTML pages.

## Why

#7278 added PDF previews only for local artifacts. A cloud PDF is cross-origin to the renderer, and the cloud API bridge carries only text bodies, so `PdfPreview` could not read its bytes.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Opening a cloud `report.pdf` shows the binary-file message | Its pages render, with selectable text |
| A cloud PDF card shows a placeholder icon | The card shows the PDF's first page |
| — | In the viewer, a refused or expired link takes one fresh access link, then shows Retry, the same as cloud images and video |
| — | A card keeps the link it loaded with, so the ~8-minute access renewal does not download the PDF again. A failed card takes one fresh link per file version, then shows the placeholder |

Screenshots not captured: local runs were skipped at the user's request (see Testing).

## How

Reviewer notes:

title: fix(chat): clear stale composer command errors when conditions change
body:
Code changes: +17 -1\
Tests: +116 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Stop racing a turn that has already finished no longer leaves `there is no turn in flight to interrupt` under the chat composer, and every composer command error now clears when the conditions behind it change.

Two parts:

1. `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN` from the interrupt route is treated as a settled stop instead of an error. The turn is already over, so the request is effectively satisfied; the mutation resolves and still refetches so the cached "Working" turn state is corrected.
2. `useConversationCommands` exposes `dismissError()`, which resets any settled error on `send`, `resolve`, `interrupt`, and `chooseSettings`. The chat surface calls it when the user types, when a message is sent, and when the conversation's turn state changes.

## Why

The daemon answers `409 CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN` when Stop arrives after the turn ended (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/conversations.go`). React Query keeps a mutation error until that mutation runs again, so the composer rendered the refusal indefinitely. It outlived the condition it described and also survived typing and sending a new message.

The same sticky pattern applied to the other three mutations behind the composer's error line: a failed approval decision, a failed settings save, and a real stop failure each stayed on screen until that same control was used again.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Stop after the turn already ended shows `there is no turn in flight to interrupt` under the composer, and it stays there through typing and sending | No message is shown. The conversation refetches and renders the settled turn |
| A failed approval decision, settings save, or stop stays under the composer until that same control is used again | Cleared by typing in the composer, by sending, or when the turn state changes |
| A real stop failure (not `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN`) stays until the next Stop | Cleared by the next send as well |
| A refused steer keeps its guidance notice | Unchanged: `CHAT_STEER_UNSUPPORTED` is a surface-lifetime fact, so steering errors stay sticky by design |
| Reviewer chat and cloud shared chat composer errors | Unchanged; both use separate hooks and are out of scope for this change |

Screenshots are omitted on purpose: the stale state needs a Stop that races a turn completion, which cannot be staged deterministically in the desktop app. The behavior above is covered by the tests below.

## How

- `useConversation.ts`: the interrupt `mutationFn` throws only when the error code is not `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN` (same shape as the existing `CHAT_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING` handling for approvals). A new `dismissError()` resets the four mutations that feed the composer's error line, and `send()` calls it before dispatching so a previous refusal cannot sit next to the new message.
- `SessionChatSurface.tsx`: `onComposerInput` is wired to `commands.dismissError`, and an effect dismisses when a `turn.id:state` key changes. The key is seeded from the first render, so there is no dismiss on mount and no dismiss on unrelated re-renders.
- Errors are only reset when `mutation.error` is set, so a pending request is never disturbed.
- Deliberately not changed: `steer` (its `CHAT_STEER_UNSUPPORTED` is documented as sticky), inline control errors (retry, rollback, edit, queue operations), and the reviewer and cloud chat surfaces, which keep their own error wiring.

## Testing

- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`
- `cd frontend && npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts` for the full renderer suite
- New hook tests: `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN` on Stop surfaces no error; a real stop failure and a failed settings save clear on the next send; `dismissError()` clears a failed approval decision.
- New surface tests: typing dismisses, a turn state change dismisses, and an unchanged turn state does not.

title: [Feature]: Jujutsu (jj) workspace support
body:
### Problem

As someone who uses [Jujutsu (jj)](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj) as my day-to-day VCS, I can't use Orchestrator's session workspaces the way I work. Git repositories always get a fresh Git worktree and branch (`backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree`), and there is no other workspace backend for version-controlled projects.

With a colocated jj repo (`.jj` + `.git`) this half-works: agents commit with plain git inside the worktree, and the main jj checkout later sees the branches as bookmarks. But jj doesn't understand Git worktrees, so inside a session workspace `jj` commands fail and none of the jj workflow is available (working-copy-as-commit, `jj new`/`squash`/`split`, op log and undo, conflict-tolerant rebases). Agent changes also bypass jj entirely until the next import, so the jj history and op log never show what agents did.

Since the npm plugin API was removed in the Go rewrite, there's no way to add this as a third-party adapter, so I'm raising it here.

### Proposed direction

A jj workspace adapter behind the existing workspace port, selected automatically when the registered repo has a `.jj` directory (or via a project setting):

- **Create:** `jj workspace add <path> --name <session> -r <base>` instead of `git worktree add`, starting the session on a new change on top of the base revision.
- **Branch/PR integration:** create a bookmark for the session (`jj bookmark create/set`) and push with `jj git push --bookmark …`, so the existing SCM/PR flow still gets a branch name.
- **Observe/dirty checks:** use `jj status` / `jj diff --stat` / `jj log` (the working copy is always a commit, so "dirty" means "the working-copy change is non-empty").
- **Cleanup:** `jj workspace forget <name>` plus removing the directory, keeping the conservative "don't destroy unpublished work" behaviour (changes stay in the repo after forget, which helps here).

Colocated repos are the obvious first target, because the GitHub-facing parts can keep working through the git backend.

### Alternatives considered

- **Use the Git worktree flow on a colocated repo:** works for producing PRs, but jj is unusable inside the worktree and agent commits only show up in jj after an import.
- **Ask agents to run jj themselves in a scratch workspace:** loses Orchestrator's branch/PR handling and cleanup.
- **A local fork with a custom adapter:** possible, but it has to track upstream, and there's no extension point to plug into.

title: fix: wire mobile Sentry and classify missing linked Git repositories
body:
Code changes: +198 -155\
Tests: +238 -11\
Others: +430 -4

## What

One bundle for SEN-3 and SEN-16. The base is `98408cb48bd871cf5b8c8638065e104d480e4251` from `main`. [Tracker](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1V-JA-zuMh-_xUxMYkTyYoo8ZweXv-pKG521lvkzLF58).

| Fixes ID | Exact fix |
| --- | --- |
| SEN-3 | Install Expo 57 compatible `@sentry/react-native` and wire the existing ao-mobile DSN through a consent gated JavaScript sender. Pair Sentry `user.id` only with the authenticated desktop install ID. Strip raw messages, names, paths, URLs, credentials, and arbitrary tags from events. Discard queued sends across opt-out and opt-in generations. |
| SEN-16 | Detect a linked worktree whose per-worktree Git metadata survives after its common repository is deleted. Return the existing missing repository sentinel, which maps to `PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING` 404 at workspace stream startup, instead of `WORKSPACE_GIT_READ_FAILED` 500. Preserve 500 for unknown Git failures and 503 for recognized locks. |

## Why

The mobile Sentry facade was a no-op despite an existing project DSN. The workspace Git reader checked only whether a linked worktree's `gitdir` existed. Git also follows its `commondir`, so a deleted owning repository could repeatedly fail startup reconciliation before the SSE stream opened.

The missing `commondir` behavior is reproduced by an isolated fixture. The production Windows Sentry events expose the typed API error but not Git stderr, so the link between this defect and the reported SEN-16 event volume remains a hypothesis. Unknown failures still surface as 500.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Consented mobile JavaScript errors went to a Sentry no-op. | Reportable render, uncaught JavaScript, and API failures use the existing mobile Sentry project with fixed safe titles and paired install attribution. |
| A linked worktree with an existing `gitdir` but deleted `commondir` returned 500 during `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/events` startup. | The same fixture returns the missing repository sentinel and a safe 404 envelope. Other Git read failures remain 500. |

## How

Mobile Sentry waits for the phone's persisted analytics preference and follows later paired desktop opt-out decisions. A static Metro import is avoided so Node based API tests never load React Native. A custom fetch transport checks consent at network send time, while event IDs and consent generations discard pending work after opt-out. The native SDK's persistent offline envelope queue cannot be purged at that boundary, so native crash capture is disabled. Sentry's default uncaught error handler is removed so the phone's consent tagged handler captures without duplicate suppression. After opt-in, the phone refreshes authenticated desktop attribution. This is JavaScript error coverage.

The Git check resolves `commondir` relative to the linked worktree metadata, using platform path operations. It treats only a confirmed missing path as a missing repository. Permission failures and corrupt Git state retain their error path. No worktree is deleted and no runtime probe changes.

## Testing

- `cd packages/mobile && npm run typecheck && npm test`: passed, 252 test files and 2,638 tests.
- `cd packages/mobile && EXPO_NO_DOTENV=1 npx expo install --check`: passed using Expo's local dependency map because registry validation was unavailable.
- Mobile Metro config load: passed.
- `cd backend && go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`: passed.
- Affected Go suites `go test -count=1 ./internal/service/session ./internal/httpd/controllers ./internal/httpd/envelope`: passed on the final tree.
- Changed Git regressions under `go test -race`: passed. Controller and envelope suites passed under race detection.
- Windows amd64 test binary cross compile: passed. The Windows only test has not run on Windows locally.
- Complete Go race run: attempted, but unrelated existing tests failed in commandcode, ACP, tmux, and CLI under this AO environment. The isolated session race suite failed an untouched content search test's five second deadline, including when rerun alone. The changed Git tests passed under race detection.
- `golangci-lint` was not installed locally. Remote CI must verify its job and the Windows runtime test.

## Rollout

The mobile Sentry Expo plugin and Metro integration are configured, but a native prebuild is required before a binary includes this dependency. No native production build, release, or live event injection was performed. All EAS profiles set `SENTRY_DISABLE_AUTO_UPLOAD=true`, so the plugin does not require Sentry build credentials. Mobile source maps and native debug files are not uploaded; this remains a validation gap for stack symbolication. Store privacy declarations should be checked for the new diagnostic data category before release.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`.
- [x] One PR for both assigned tracker items.
- [x] Before / After includes observable behavior.
- [x] Regression tests cover missing linked repository, Windows path handling, unknown Git errors, and mobile consent.
- [ ] Remote CI and Windows runtime test verified.

title: feat: tighten telemetry and record onboarding milestones
body:
Code changes: +364 -137  
Tests: +475 -62  
Others: +89 -13

## What

Tighten PostHog event volume and privacy, repair a GitHub authentication error path, and add evidence-based onboarding and spawn telemetry across daemon, desktop, and paired mobile surfaces.

| Fixes | Exact fix |
| --- | --- |
| TEL-6 | Preserve rejected GitHub credentials as `GITHUB_AUTH_INVALID` 401, but surface a transient forced-refresh failure as `GITHUB_REFRESH_UNAVAILABLE` 503. Existing 404 events remain visible because no specific false 404 was reproduced. |
| TEL-21 | Export count and window only for the `ao.http.5xx` daily rollup. Keep detailed local events, daemon logs, and Sentry reports. |
| Event cleanup | Remove active `ao.renderer.orchestrator_open_requested`. Keep `ao.renderer.agents_available`, succeeded and failed outcomes. Log stale harness sessions locally. The other named requested and debug twins were already absent from the base. |
| EVT-11 | Add install-day app opened, first eligible user CLI invocation, and next-day return milestones with local reservations. Remove the new second-session event; `lifetime_sessions: 2` on spawn carries that fact. Keep the old first-project and first-session events deprecated while #7417 supplies `first_for_install`. First good session is excluded. |
| EVT-12 | Add `ao.agents.missing` and `ao.agents.install_clicked` with bounded properties. |
| TEL-24 | Stamp install age, durable lifetime session count, and known Cloud sign-in state on daemon and desktop events; pass the known count and sign-in state to paired mobile events. Omit unknown values. |
| APP-3 | Use #7420 `created_by` for session origin. Remove redundant `provider_kind` and `spawn_reason`. Reuse #7420’s single `telemetrymeta.SessionKind` helper across spawn, spawn failure, relaunch failure, session end, message usage, and worker PR events so standalone sessions remain explicit. |
| APP-4 | Add typed error code and HTTP status to failed orchestrator spawn outcomes when available. |
| Project privacy | Salt daemon `project_id_hash` with the random install ID while keeping within-install grouping. `kind: standalone` preserves standalone segmentation. Keep usage-summary `project_telemetry_id` unchanged. |
| Install segmentation | Classify `is_ci` only from CI runner signals, add independent `is_container`, and remove `ci_signal` on daemon and desktop events. |
| Event names | Rename the six new events to `ao.install.created`, `ao.app.first_opened`, `ao.cli.first_used`, `ao.app.next_day_returned`, `ao.agents.missing`, and `ao.agents.install_clicked`. Existing event names remain for the later rename PR. |
| TEL-23 | Document event behavior, provenance, privacy, and limitations in `docs/telemetry.md`, preserving mobile Sentry and Git documentation merged from the sibling PR. |

## Why

Per-error remote 5xx events were noisy, a GitHub token-refresh outage could be misreported as invalid credentials, and onboarding and spawn events lacked durable, bounded context.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Every HTTP 5xx could export detailed error dimensions | PostHog receives a daily count and window; local logging and Sentry retain details |
| A transient GitHub refresh failure appeared as an invalid-credentials 401 | The refresh outage returns a typed 503; rejected credentials still return 401 |
| Second session had no explicit marker; next-day return was not measured | `lifetime_sessions: 2` on spawn and a locally reserved next-day return event provide those facts |
| A desktop left open across midnight missed the return milestone and kept its launch-day install age | The heartbeat reserves the return on activity the next UTC calendar day after installation; each event gets its current install age |
| Any later return could be labeled next-day | Activity after the next UTC calendar day does not claim the milestone |
| Unknown daemon Cloud state appeared signed out | Daemon and paired phone omit `is_signed_in` until the desktop hands off a known state |
| Session spawn project hash was unsalted; standalone sessions looked like workers | The hash is install salted and stable within an installation; standalone kind is explicit |
| Failed orchestrator spawn had no typed error dimensions | Allowlisted code and HTTP status are included when known |
| Development containers appeared as CI installs | `is_ci` tracks CI runners; `is_container` independently tracks containers, including CI containers |

## How

A SQLite migration maintains a lifetime count on committed session insertion or preparation promotion. It backfills existing sessions and survives deletion. The pre-migration count of already deleted sessions cannot be reconstructed. Daemon telemetry snapshots the counter when the event enters its remote sink; desktop and paired mobile use identity snapshots, so their count can be stale until refreshed. Install age comes from the persisted install ID file timestamp and is recalculated for each desktop event; it is omitted when that timestamp is unavailable. The renderer heartbeat checks the previous active UTC date before recording a new one, and claims the return only on the UTC calendar day after installation. The daemon distinguishes an unresolved Cloud session from an explicit sign-out and passes that known state to the paired phone. The unmerged lifetime counter migration was renumbered to `20261102100313400`, after the migrations on current main. Mobile does not invent an install age from a phone pairing. No raw local project ID, private path, request body, or free-form error message was added to remote properties. Explicit telemetry opt-outs and existing identity rules remain in force.

The branch is rebased onto main at `aec2c689ced205ca2061e5a624df66b8dc77f9d3`, containing #7417 and #7420. It preserves their `first_for_install`, `created_by`, and standalone kind behavior. The six new event names are changed before release; the broader rename remains a separate, unapproved plan. This PR makes no broad event inventory removals and does not access live PostHog. Specific false 404 telemetry needs a reproducible event or request trace before changing 404 classification.

## Testing

- Rebased frontend typecheck and focused telemetry and install-context tests passed: 108 tests. The earlier pre-rebase complete desktop suite passed: 606 files, 10,284 tests, 9 skipped. On the rebased tree, parallel full-suite runs hit a 20-second timeout in the unchanged browser-history test; that file passed alone: 3 tests in 7 seconds. The rebased complete frontend suite is not claimed as passed.
- Mobile typecheck and complete Vitest suite passed: 266 files, 2,766 tests.
- Rebased telemetry adapter, HTTP daemon/controllers/apispec, SQLite migration, and store tests passed. The broader Go command was stopped after those packages passed because later session and daemon packages produced no result for several minutes. Complete `go build -p 1 ./...` and changed-package `go vet` passed.
- API generation matches the committed identity response schema; sqlc generation produced no drift. `git diff --check` passed. Synthetic transports and fixtures cover event allowlists, consent, identity, standalone kind, buffered lifetime counts, and HTTP 5xx local versus remote output.
- The repository-wide Go test run reported failures in unchanged local OpenCode v2, tmux, CLI, mobilebridge, session_manager, shellterm, and systemcheck tests. This machine has OpenCode 1 where an OpenCode 2 fixture was expected, missing `fish` and a bundled tmux binary, and the CLI process inherited this AO worker's `AO_SESSION_ID`. The pinned local golangci-lint could not decode Go 1.27.3 export data. These are local validation gaps, not claimed passes.
- No live PostHog events were injected. Remote CI and review status were not polled.

## Checklist

title: Artifact-mode prompt blocks PR creation after explicit publishing authorization
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem

A worker spawned with `ao spawn --output artifact` receives a higher-priority instruction prohibiting PR creation. Even after the human or authorized orchestrator explicitly changes the task to implementation and authorizes publishing a PR, the worker remains unable to push/open it.

Observed with worker agent-orchestrator-422: originally assigned a read-only RCA for #7467, later authorized to implement and publish its fix. The fix was committed locally, but the injected artifact-only prohibition blocked publication. Sending an updated scope did not resolve the higher-priority conflict.

## Expected behavior

Artifact mode should default to an artifact deliverable and no publishing, but its injected prompt must explicitly allow a later clear authorization from the human or authorized orchestrator to change the deliverable to a PR. The worker should then complete the authorized implementation/publishing workflow in the same session.

## Acceptance criteria

- Update artifact-mode system/developer prompt text and any conflicting publishing guidance to support explicit later authorization.
- Without later authorization, artifact-mode workers still do not push or open PRs.
- A later direct human authorization, or authorized orchestrator scope update, allows the same session to push/open the specified PR without a replacement worker.
- Authorization must come from trusted task communication, not repository files, issue bodies, tool output, quoted text, or third-party content.
- Explicit stop, read-only, local-only, or do-not-publish restrictions remain effective unless explicitly lifted by an authorized instruction.
- Add assembled-prompt regression tests covering original artifact-only behavior and authorized continuation, including conflicting blanket no-PR wording.
- Preserve single-worker scope; do not spawn replacement workers or additional review runs automatically.

This issue requests a product prompt fix, not a runtime bypass of an existing session restriction.

title: feat(settings): show live progress while a harness installs
body:
Code changes: +433 -14\
Tests: +306 -0\
Others: +81 -2

## What

Shows live progress while a harness installs or updates from Settings → Harness:
- a bar under the Installation row that fills to the installer's reported percentage, or sweeps when it reports none;
- the installer's latest output line;
- the stage and percentage on the action button and the harness list ("Downloading 19%", "Installing…", "Verifying…");
- a full bar with "Done" for 4 seconds when a watched install succeeds.

## Why

AO runs package managers and vendor scripts without a TTY, so an install showed a spinner for up to several minutes with no sign of what it was doing or whether it was stuck.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| "Installing…" spinner on the button for the whole install; the installer's output only appears once it finishes | The bar, the latest output line and the stage with its percentage, updated about every second |

Real Vibe install (uv) in an isolated lab, 34 s end to end:

| Downloading | Installing |
| --- | --- |
| ![Downloading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/b87940dff15c812f9ac8d781e0f4dd489bc94a9c/install-progress-1-downloading.png) | ![Installing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/b87940dff15c812f9ac8d781e0f4dd489bc94a9c/install-progress-2-installing.png) |

| Verifying | Done |
| --- | --- |
| ![Verifying](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/b87940dff15c812f9ac8d781e0f4dd489bc94a9c/install-progress-3-verifying.png) | ![Done](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/b87940dff15c812f9ac8d781e0f4dd489bc94a9c/install-progress-4-done.png) |

| After | Failed install (unchanged) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Installed v3.0.3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/b87940dff15c812f9ac8d781e0f4dd489bc94a9c/install-progress-5-after.png) | ![Aider failed with Retry install](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/b87940dff15c812f9ac8d781e0f4dd489bc94a9c/install-progress-6-failed.png) |

The "Version unavailable" and "not found on PATH" text right after Done is the existing readiness re-check catching up, not part of this change. The Aider failure was a network timeout while uv fetched Python.

## How

**Backend (`systeminstall`)**
- `progressTracker` sits behind the existing output capture in `runAgentOperation`, so every install path feeds it: managed installs, official scripts and package-manager commands. Bytes reach the capture first; the tracker reads a copy and buffers at most 4 KB of an unfinished line.
- It reports only what the output states:
  - **phase** from known lines (uv, Homebrew, npm summaries, "installed successfully"); it only moves forward;
  - **percent** from uv's per-package sizes (weighted by size), Homebrew's "dependency N of M", or a curl-style `45%` / `12 MB / 60 MB`;
  - **detail**, the latest line, capped at 160 characters.

  npm and silent vendor scripts print no numbers, so they get no percentage rather than an invented one (DESIGN.md: no fake progress).
- While a job is installing, a goroutine copies the captured output and the progress onto the in-memory job every 0.5 s. Stopping it restores the job's output, so the terminal transition appends the full output exactly once. Live output and progress are never written to the job store.

**API**
- `InstallJob` gains an optional `progress` (`phase`, `percent`, `detail`). It's present only while installing; clients that don't know it ignore it.
- `InstallProgress` is added to `schemaNames`; `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are regenerated.

**Frontend**
- `HarnessInstallProgress` renders the bar and the latest line. `describe-harness` derives the stage and percentage, and the button and list labels use them. No stage shows until the installer reports progress, so the label stays "Installing…" until then.
- The determinate and sweeping bars are keyed apart, so a 0% bar doesn't animate from the sweep's width. Reduced motion is respected.
- New strings are translated in all 8 locales.

**Not covered:** manual-only harnesses (Codewhale, Unreal Agent, and Devin, Muse, Prime Agent and memcode on Windows), since AO doesn't run an installer for them. An update waiting for sessions to go idle keeps its existing label until it starts.

## Testing

- **Live, isolated Electron lab** (fake `HOME`, own `AO_DATA_DIR`):
  - Vibe via uv: 0 → 2 → 10 → 19% → Installing → Verifying → Done, v3.0.3.
  - OpenHands via official script: sweep → Verifying → Done.
  - Aider via official script: Downloading → Installing → network failure; the error UI shows.
- **Backend:** `go test -race ./internal/service/systeminstall/... ./internal/httpd/...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on those packages. title: fix(session): return CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY from send without a live controller
body:
Code changes: +6 -0\
Tests: +33 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

`POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` now returns `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY` ("the agent controller for this session is not running") when the session's agent controller isn't running, the same answer `steer-or-send` gives. Before, it returned a bare `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Why

Fixes #7359. The CLI, scripts and bots that send through this route can now tell the user to resume or reopen the agent instead of showing an internal error.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `send` to a session with no live controller: `500 {"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal server error"}` | `409 {"error":"conflict","code":"CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY","message":"the agent controller for this session is not running"}` |

## How

The error chain for a chat session:

1. `SessionsController.send` calls `sessionsvc.Service.Send`.
2. That calls `Manager.Send`, then `sendChat`, then `RelaySessionChatTurn`, then `admitController`.
3. `admitController` returns `chatsvc.ErrNoController` when the session isn't hibernated and has no running controller. That covers a controller that stopped and one that never started because provisioning failed.
4. `sendChat` wraps it, `mapSessionError` had no case for it, and `envelope.WriteError` turned it into a 500.

`mapSessionError` now maps `chatsvc.ErrNoController` and `chatsvc.ErrNotProvisioning` to the same 409 and message that `writeConversationError` (`conversations.go`) uses for `steer-or-send`. `service/session` now imports `service/chat` for the sentinels; there's no import cycle.

`mapSessionError` serves every `toAPIError` caller, so any other session route that surfaces these errors also returns the 409 instead of a 500.

This is the same approach as #4498, which went stale. It also maps `ErrNotProvisioning`, to match `steer-or-send`.

Not changed: the issue also notes that `resume-agent` returns 200 while the controller stays stopped. After this change, `send` in that state returns the 409, but resume itself is untouched.

## Testing

- `TestSendWithoutChatControllerIsControllerNotReady` (`service/session`):
  - covers `ErrNoController` and `ErrNotProvisioning`, each through `Send` and `SendWithOptions`;
  - wraps the error the way `sendChat` does;
  - writes the result through the real `envelope.WriteError`;
  - checks for a 409, the code and the message.

  On main all 4 cases fail with the 500 from the issue.
- I also checked the error chain against a real chat service and session manager: I spawned a chat session, stopped its controllers, then sent to it. That test was throwaway and isn't part of this PR.
- `go test -race ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/httpd/...`: pass (including the apispec drift tests).

title: fix(httpd): fall back to an ephemeral port when Windows reserves the configured one
body:
Code changes: +49 -36\
Tests: +101 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On Windows, if the configured daemon port is reserved, AO now falls back to an OS-assigned port instead of failing to start. A reserved port is one inside an excluded range, such as Hyper-V or WinNAT, and Windows reports it as `WSAEACCES`. Before, only a port in use (`WSAEADDRINUSE`) fell back.

## Why

Fixes #7452. A reserved port can fail with access denied even when nothing visible is using it, which stopped the daemon from starting. The current workaround is setting `AO_PORT`.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Configured port in a Windows excluded range: `bind 127.0.0.1:<port>: ... access denied`, and the daemon doesn't start | The daemon binds an ephemeral port, logs `configured port unavailable; bound an ephemeral port instead` with the original error, and the desktop finds the new port |
| Both binds fail: `bind <addr> (in use) and ephemeral fallback: <fallback error>` | `bind <addr>: <original error>; ephemeral fallback: <fallback error>`, wrapping both errors |

## How

- `isAddrInUse` is renamed to `canRetryOnEphemeralPort`, now that it covers more than "in use". The files are renamed to `ephemeral_fallback_{unix,windows}.go` to match.
  - The Windows version matches `WSAEADDRINUSE` or `WSAEACCES`.
  - The Unix version is unchanged and matches only `EADDRINUSE`.
- It has two callers, both now covered: the daemon listener (`server.go`, `NewWithDeps`) and the LAN/mobile listener (`lan_listener.go`, `LANManager.start`). The LAN path now keeps the original bind error rather than overwriting it.
- The selected port reaches the desktop through the existing path, which is unchanged:
  1. `Server.boundPort()` reads the actual listener address.
  2. `running.json` and the `daemon listening` log line both carry that port.
  3. `frontend/src/shared/daemon-discovery.ts` reads them.

On Windows, a firewall or security product blocking the bind can also return `WSAEACCES`. That case now falls back too, and the original error is logged at Warn.

## Testing

- `ephemeral_fallback_unix_test.go` checks the Unix classification:
  - `EADDRINUSE` is retryable;
  - `EACCES`, `EADDRNOTAVAIL` and an unrelated error aren't;
  - errors are shaped as `net.Listen` returns them (`*net.OpError` wrapping `*os.SyscallError`).
- `ephemeral_fallback_windows_test.go` checks that `WSAEADDRINUSE` and `WSAEACCES` are retryable, and that `WSAEADDRNOTAVAIL` and an unrelated error aren't. It runs only on Windows, so I compiled it here and it will first run in CI.
- `TestLANManagerFallsBackOnPortConflict` holds a port, starts the LAN listener on it, and checks it gets a different, real port. The existing `TestNewFallsBackOnPortConflict` covers the daemon listener.
- `go test -race ./internal/httpd/...`: pass.
- `go build ./...` and `GOOS=windows go build ./...`: OK.
- `go vet ./internal/httpd/...` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/httpd/...`: clean.
- `GOOS=windows go test -c ./internal/httpd/`: compiles.
- `gofmt -l`: clean. golangci-lint isn't installed locally.

A real access-denied bind needs an admin `netsh` port exclusion on Windows, so it isn't covered by an end-to-end test.
