title: Cline shared hub credits hooks to the session that started it
body:
Reported by @Meraj-08 in [this review of PR #2904](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/2904#discussion_r4421004265).

With two Cline TUI sessions sharing one hub, `cl-4` started the hub, but `cl-5`'s `session-start`, `permission-resolved`, and `stop` hooks ran in `cl-5`'s worktree with `AO_SESSION_ID=cl-4` and `cl-4`'s launch ID. The interactive hook payloads included `sessionContext.rootSessionId`. AO stored `cl-5`'s root ID (`1793340719019_wylge`) on `cl-4`, while `cl-5` received no native ID; hook activity was also credited to the wrong AO session.

Expected: each session's hooks update that session's activity and native identity.

The reviewer noted that this behavior already exists on `main`. PR #2904 can recover the correct restore ID from worktree-scoped history, but live hook activity remains misattributed. This issue tracks that separately from restore recovery. These observations are relayed from the review; no additional local reproduction was run.

title: feat: local share links — contract (random IDs, active-only slots, direct uploads, public details) and desktop share flow
body:
Code changes: +1216 -97\
Tests: +576 -3\
Others: +472 -50 (generated `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts`, strings in all 9 locales)

## What

Local share links, contract and desktop together (the desktop half came from #7482, squash-merged into this branch). Every signed-in AO user can share a file from a local session as a public link. The free plan has a limit of 3 active links; paid and contract organizations have no limit. There is no file size limit.

**Public Cloud contract (`contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, generated `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts`)**
- **Link IDs:** a new link gets a random 26-character ID (`a-z`, `2-7`) instead of `<project>-<feature>-<email>`.
- **Slots:** only active links count toward the limit. Unpublishing frees a slot; restoring needs a free one. `ArtifactShareList.used` counts active links, and the optional `unlimited` is true for paid or contract organizations.
- **`ArtifactShare`:** adds `contentUrl` and an optional `viewerUrl` (`url` is kept).
- **Uploads straight to storage:** new `createArtifactShareUpload`, `presignArtifactShareParts`, `finalizeArtifactShare` and `abortArtifactShareUpload`. Each part URL signs its part's length and SHA-256. A video, or a new document over the link limit, is refused before anything is stored. There is no file size limit.
- **Body-upload routes removed:** `POST /me/artifact-shares` and `PUT /me/artifact-shares/{shareId}`, plus their `ArtifactShareName`/`ArtifactShareSHA256` parameters and `ArtifactShareEnvelope`. They only ever ran behind the development-only `AO_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_SHARES` flag, never in staging or production.
- **Unpublish:** deletes the stored file at once. Publishing the same document again restores the link under a **new URL**, so the revoked URL never serves again (ao-control-plane #20).
- **New public route:** `GET /api/cloud/v1/artifact-shares/{linkId}` (no sign-in) returns what a viewer page shows: name, type, size, owner display name (never the email) and `contentUrl`.

**Desktop (`frontend/src`, `backend/internal/sessionartifacts`)**
- **Offered only where it works:** the main process checks once per control plane whether it serves share links (`GET /me/artifact-shares`: 404 means the share flag is off). Share is hidden until the check answers, and stays hidden where sharing is off. No sign-in is needed.
- **Share button:** beside Edit in an open local artifact's header and in the artifact preview, like Claude's artifacts. It's hidden while the file is being edited, and disabled for video.
- **Share popover (`ShareArtifactPopover`), anchored to the button, 296px wide.** Every state is a title, an optional status line, and one action row whose primary action sits at the right.
    - **Ready:** title "Share {name}", with Publish at the right. The left of the row shows "{left} of {limit} free links left" (nothing on a paid plan). A credential warning appears under the title. The file size isn't shown.
    - **Publishing:** a progress bar, with "N% uploaded" at the left and Cancel plus a disabled "Publishing…" at the right. Preparing the snapshot is the first half and uploading the second. Closing the popover keeps the publish going; reopening shows its progress.
    - **Published:** a green globe with "Public · anyone with the link can view", the link in a plain mono field, quiet red Unpublish at the left, and Copy link at the right, which turns into "Copied" with a check.
    - **Confirm unpublish:** "Unpublish this link?" with Cancel and a filled red Unpublish.
    - **Also:** sign in ("Sharing a file needs a signed-in account."), limit (only **Upgrade**, never unpublishing; a server limit refusal shows it at once), changed file and error.
    - **Sizes:** 13px title, 11px secondary text, 12px and 28px-high buttons. App buttons and inputs inherit their font (`styles.css`), so the action row and the link field set their sizes on the container.
- **Share button state:** muted like the header's other actions; brighter on hover; pressed while its popover is open.
- **Main-process publish (`main/cloud-share.ts`, `main/cloud-share-ipc.ts`).** The renderer never sees file bytes or the sign-in token.
    1. Resolves the file strictly inside `<data>/artifacts/<session>`, refusing `..`, absolute paths, symlinks pointing out, `.versions/` and non-files. Opening it checks device and inode, so a parent folder swapped for a symlink is refused too.
    2. `inspect` scans the file and returns a **fingerprint**: the hash of the scanned first 32 MiB, plus the size and mtime.
    3. `publish` copies the file once into a private `0600` snapshot under `~/.ao` (free space checked first; it can be cancelled), hashing and scanning it. If the snapshot's fingerprint isn't the one the popover showed, it returns `{ status: "changed", inspection }` and uploads nothing, so the person sees the new state and publishes again.
    4. Uploads the snapshot in presigned parts (at most two in memory) and finalizes. A failed part stops the other worker; a failure or cancel aborts the upload.
- **No second, native confirmation:** Publish in the popover is the person's decision. Only the app window's main frame can call `cloudShare`. The preload bridge isn't in the frames artifacts render in, and the handlers refuse a subframe. Code running in the app's own renderer could publish without a click; that's the accepted trade-off of dropping the native dialog. `shared/cloud-share.ts` records it.
- **Proxy block:** `cloud-cp-proxy` refuses every non-GET request under `/api/cloud/v1/me/artifact-shares`, so share links change only through the main-process flow, which is confined to the artifacts folder and bound to what was inspected.
- **No agent path:** `TestNoBackendPathPublishesShareLinks` fails if any daemon, `ao` CLI or MCP code names the share API.

## Why

The share-links design: only a person publishes, from the desktop's trusted process, with the file confined to the session's artifacts folder and exactly the bytes they were shown. Agents read untrusted content, so a hidden "publish `.env`" must have no route to a public link. The old link name put the owner's email in a public URL. Counting revoked links meant unpublishing never made room for another file.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `http://<project>-<feature>-<email>.<share host>/` | `https://<26 random chars>.<share host>/` |
| Revoked links count toward the limit | Only active links count; unpublishing frees a slot |
| File sent through the API in one body, 10 MiB cap | Presigned multipart upload straight to storage, no size limit |
| No way to share a local artifact from the app | Share → popover → Publish → progress → Copy link |
| The renderer could change share links through the CP proxy | Proxy refuses share writes; only the main-process flow publishes |

## How

- **Compatibility:** additive except the two removed dev-only routes, which no released client used. oasdiff reports them as `api-removed-without-deprecation`, so this PR needs the `contract-breaking-change` label.
- **Control plane:** OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#20 and #22 implement the contract and vendor this branch.
- **Document key:** the project, plus the session and the file's folder, plus the file name. Republishing a file updates its link.
- **Secret scan:** an independent list of well-known credential formats and file names, covering the first 32 MiB. It warns and never blocks; what's published is what was scanned.
- **No file size limit, by product decision:** the free plan's limit is 3 active links. Abuse handling (size or storage quotas, takedown) is deliberately deferred.
- **Existing gap, not changed here:** the CP proxy trusts a renderer-supplied `baseUrl` (any https host); `cloudShare` uses the same check.
- **Not in this PR:** the Shared links list (which will use `shareId` to update a link), the version-history "Shared" badge and post-restore prompt, and upgrade-and-return. Cloud session files are in #7555; the viewer page is OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#22.

## Testing

- `oasdiff breaking` (v1.34.1) against `main`: only the two intended route removals.
- `packages/cloud-client`: typecheck and tests (31 passed). `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- `frontend`: `tsgo --noEmit` shows no errors in `src/`. The `src/main` tests, the share, artifact-view and locale tests pass, except `browser-profile-import` and a timeout in `browser-history-store`, which fail the same way without this change.
- Tests:
    - **Path guard, secret scan, fingerprint:** same for scan and snapshot, new after a write.
    - **Snapshot:** hash, `0600`, a final symlink swap and a parent folder swap refused, progress and cancel.
    - **Upload client:** part hashing, token only to the control plane, abort on failure, no part sent after the abort.
    - **IPC:**
        - publishes with no second confirmation;
        - a file changed after inspect uploads nothing;
        - a second publish refused at once;
        - only the main frame;
        - empty project refused;
        - refusals mapped.
    - **Proxy block:** including dot-segment tricks.
    - **Popover:**
        - sign-in, warnings, publish, copy and Copied;
        - publish carries the fingerprint;
        - changed file;
        - server limit;
        - a publish survives closing;
        - Upgrade-only at the limit;
        - a paid plan shows no count;
        - no public status before publishing;
        - progress as "N% uploaded";
        - Unpublish before Copy link;
        - video.
- **Manual check in the running desktop app:** an isolated dev app (its own data directory, light mode), driven over CDP and pointed at a local ao-control-plane compose stack with shares on, from a local session's artifact header.
    - **Ready to publish:** title and Publish only. The local stack has no plan limit, so no free-links count.
    - **Published, after a real publish:** green globe status, the viewer link in the mono field, Unpublish at the left and Copy link at the right.
    - **Copy link:** turns into "Copied" with a check.
    - **Unpublish:** opens the inline confirmation with Cancel and a filled red Unpublish. Cancelled, so the link stays published.
    - **Share button:** pressed while the popover is open.
    - **Sizes measured in the app:** popover 296px wide; title 13px; status and link 11px; Unpublish and Copy link 12px and 28px high. This caught that app buttons were inheriting 14px and 11px before the container sizes were set.
    - **Not seen on screen:** the "Publishing…" progress (a local publish finishes too fast), the free-links count, and dark mode. Unit tests cover the first two.
- `go test ./internal/sessionartifacts/` passes; `golangci-lint` on that package: 0 issues.
- All #7482 CI checks passed before it was merged here, including gitleaks `scan`.

title: feat(desktop): share a local artifact as a public link
body:
Code changes: +928 -5\

Others: +208 -0 (strings in all 8 locales)

Stacked on #7479 (contract). The control plane side is in the private control-plane repo.

## What

Local users can share a session artifact as a public link. The new pieces:

- **Menu item.** The artifact menu (full menu only, not the card menu) gets a **Share** item for local sessions. It reads "Sign in to share" when signed out and "Share · Coming soon" for video.
- **Share dialog** (`ShareArtifactDialog`, built on the shared `ConfirmDialog`):
    - shows the public-link warning, "Free plan: n of 3 active links", the file size, and a warning when the file looks like it holds a credential;
    - shows upload progress with Cancel;
    - shows the finished link with **Copy link**;
    - at the free plan's link limit, offers only **Upgrade**, never unpublishing. There is no file size limit.
- **Main-process publish** (`main/cloud-share.ts`, `main/cloud-share-ipc.ts`). The renderer never sees file bytes or the sign-in token. Main:
    1. resolves the file strictly inside `<data>/artifacts/<session>`, refusing `..`, absolute paths, symlinks that point out, the `.versions/` history and non-files;
    2. copies it once into a private snapshot under `~/.ao` (`0600`, opened `O_NOFOLLOW`) while hashing it and scanning for common credential formats;
    3. asks the person in a **native dialog**, defaulting to Cancel when a credential was found;
    4. uploads the snapshot straight to storage in presigned parts (hashed by streaming, at most two parts in memory), then finalizes. A failure or cancel aborts the upload.
- **Proxy block.** `cloud-cp-proxy` now refuses every non-GET request under `/api/cloud/v1/me/artifact-shares`, checked after URL normalization. Injected UI script can't publish around the native confirmation.
- **No agent path.** `TestNoBackendPathPublishesShareLinks` fails if any daemon, `ao` CLI or MCP code names the share API.

## Why

The share-links design: only a person publishes, from the desktop's trusted process, with the file confined to the session's artifacts folder. Agents read untrusted content, so a hidden "publish `.env`" must have no route to a public link.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| No way to share a local artifact | Share → dialog (warning, `n of 3`, secret warning) → native confirm → upload progress → Copy link |
| The renderer could send any request to the share API through the CP proxy | Proxy refuses share writes; only the main-process flow publishes |

Screenshots of each dialog state still need to be added from a local run against the compose control plane. Not done yet.

## How

- **Document key:** a link's document is the project, plus the session and the file's folder, plus the file name. Republishing a file therefore updates its link, and same-named files in different folders get separate links.
- **Snapshot cleanup:** snapshots go under the desktop data dir (`~/.ao/.../tmp/share-uploads`, per the `~/.ao`-only rule), are deleted after each publish, and leftovers are cleared at startup.
- **Secret scan:** an independent list of well-known credential formats (AWS, GitHub, Slack, Anthropic, OpenAI, Stripe, Google keys, private keys, `*_PASSWORD=` style assignments) and file names (`.env`, `id_rsa`, `*.pem`, …). It covers the first 32 MiB, and it warns rather than blocks.
- **Not in this PR:** the Shared links list, the version-history "Shared" badge and post-restore prompt, upgrade-and-return to the same file, cloud session files, and the viewer page come next.
- **Existing gap, not changed here:** the CP proxy trusts the renderer-supplied `baseUrl`, which may be any https host. `cloudShare` uses the same check.

title: fix(workspace): move orphaned worktree folders aside before add
body:
Code changes: +139 -6\
Tests: +293 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

If git has forgotten a worktree but its folder is still on disk, AO now moves that folder aside before creating the new worktree, instead of failing on every attempt. A folder that isn't a forgotten worktree of the project's repo is never touched; creation fails with a 409 `WORKSPACE_PATH_OCCUPIED` that names the path.

## Why

Fixes #7358. A project's orchestrator always uses the same worktree path. When a folder is left there that git no longer tracks (its `.git/worktrees/<name>` admin entry was pruned), `git worktree add` refuses with `fatal: '<path>' already exists`. That blocks every orchestrator for the project until someone finds and removes the folder by hand.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Folder at the orchestrator path whose worktree registration was pruned: `provisionState=failed`, `git worktree add ... fatal: '<path>' already exists`, every time | The folder is renamed to `<name>.orphaned-<UTC timestamp>` beside it, with every file kept, a Warn log names both paths, and the orchestrator starts |
| Any other non-empty folder, a full clone, a worktree of another repo, or a file at the path: the same opaque `exit status 128` error, reported as a 500 | 409 `WORKSPACE_PATH_OCCUPIED`: `"<path>" already exists and is not a git worktree of "<repo>"; move or delete it and retry`. The path is left untouched |

## How

- `addWorktree` calls a new `clearOrphanedWorktreePath` before either `git worktree add` form, so Create, Restore and workspace-project repos all go through it. Paths git still registers (live or stale) are left to the existing `existingWorktree` / `staleRegistrationForPath` handling, and an empty directory is left in place because git adds into it.
- A folder counts as an orphaned worktree of this repo only when all of these hold:
  - `<path>/.git` is a file containing `gitdir: <dir>`, with relative paths resolved the way git does;
  - `<dir>` no longer exists;
  - `<dir>` sits directly under `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`/`worktrees`, with paths compared after resolving symlinks.
- The folder is never deleted. The existing `moveStrayPathAside` now wraps a generic `movePathAside(path, suffix)`, which picks `-2`, `-3`, ... if the name is taken.
- There's a new sentinel, `ports.ErrWorkspacePathOccupied`, mapped to `apierr.Conflict("WORKSPACE_PATH_OCCUPIED", ...)` next to `WORKSPACE_LOCKED`.
- In `Create`, a FreshBranch add that fails with `ErrPathOccupied` skips `rollbackPreparedAdd`. Nothing was created before the refusal, and the rollback would have reported the untouched folder as a dirty partial worktree.
- `destroy` isn't changed, so this doesn't overlap #7440.

## Testing

All in the new `workspace_orphan_test.go`, using real git repos:
- `TestWorkspaceIntegrationCreateOrchestratorMovesOrphanedWorktreeAside` reproduces the issue. It creates the orchestrator worktree with an uncommitted file, deletes its admin entry, runs `git worktree prune`, and creates the worktree again. The new worktree must be registered and clean, and exactly one `.orphaned-*` folder must remain, still holding the file. On `main` it fails with the issue's error: `fatal: '.../todo-app-orchestrator' already exists`.
- `TestWorkspaceIntegrationCreateMovesOrphanWithRelativeGitdirAside` covers the same case with a relative `gitdir`.
- `TestWorkspaceIntegrationCreateRefusesOccupiedPathAndLeavesItUntouched` covers an unrelated folder (also with FreshBranch), a full clone, an orphaned worktree of another repo, and a regular file. Each returns `ErrWorkspacePathOccupied` (not `ErrWorkspaceDirty`), and the path is left unchanged, with nothing moved or registered.
- `TestWorkspaceIntegrationCreateAddsIntoEmptyDirectoryInPlace` and `TestMovePathAsideSkipsTakenDestinations` cover the empty-directory and name-collision cases.
- The `mapSessionError` table test has a new row for `WORKSPACE_PATH_OCCUPIED`.

Commands run:
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/... ./internal/ports/... ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/session_manager/...`: pass.
- `GOOS=windows go vet` and `GOOS=windows go test -c` on `gitworktree`: clean.
- `gofmt -l`: clean.
- golangci-lint v2.15.0 with `backend/.golangci.yml` on the touched packages: 0 issues. The pinned v2.13.2 doesn't run with my local Go toolchain.

Not covered:
- The `.orphaned-*` folders are kept until someone removes them, since they may hold work, and nothing in AO cleans them up.
- On Windows, the rename fails if a process still holds a file open inside the folder. The add then fails with a clear "move path aside" error, and nothing is lost.
- The frontend's error-code table has no entry for `WORKSPACE_PATH_OCCUPIED`, so it falls back to the generic conflict handling.

title: bug(activity): nothing demotes a stale active state for harnesses without a TerminalActivityDetector
body:
## What went wrong?

For most harnesses, nothing demotes a stale `active` activity state. If a turn ends without the hook that reports it, the session reads **Working** forever. This is the general form of #3387 (Layers 1 and 3), which #7433 fixes only for Kimi's provider-error path.

Two pieces are missing:

1. **Status derivation has no staleness check.** `contract.DeriveStatus` (`backend/pkg/contract/status.go`, called from `service/session/status.go`) maps `ActivityActive` to `StatusWorking` however old `LastActivityAt` is.
2. **The stale-activity observer covers only harnesses that implement `ports.TerminalActivityDetector`.** Today that's aider, claude-code, cline, codex, continue, crush, hermes, kiro, memcode and muse. The observer skips every other terminal harness, including opencode, opencode-v2, grok, droid, amp, agy, cursor, qwen, gemini, copilot, goose, auggie, devin, kimi, kilocode, vibe, pi, kimchi, prime-agent, autohand, omp, codewhale, mimo-code, openhands and command-code. Some of these may only run in Chat, where the controller reports turn ends; that needs checking per harness.

The same family shows up per harness: #3387 (kimi), #5050 (agy, Esc interrupt), #6131 (orchestrator on claude-code), #4142 and #3115 (closed, fixed per harness with a detector).

## Why a simple time-based decay isn't enough

#3387's Option B (decaying `active` after N minutes) would wrongly flag long turns that only run tools, for harnesses that report nothing mid-turn: Kimi until #7399, and any adapter without tool hooks. A general fix has to tell "the turn ended silently" apart from "the turn is long and quiet".

## Possible directions

- **Per-harness detectors**, the way #4142 and #4048 were fixed: authoritative idle from each TUI's idle composer. This is accurate, but each one also changes message-delivery readiness for that harness, so it needs real frames.
- **Process-level evidence:** a session whose agent process is alive and idle (no CPU, no output) for a long time while it reads `active` could move to a distinct "possibly stuck" status rather than idle. That surfaces the problem without claiming the turn ended.
- **A "stale" status in `deriveStatus()`** that only applies when no detector exists and the adapter reports mid-turn activity, so long quiet turns stay `working`.

## Done when

A turn that ends without its end hook no longer leaves the session on "Working" indefinitely, on any harness. Either a detector or some other signal moves it to idle or to a visible "stuck" state, and long tool-only turns aren't misreported.

Related: #3387, #7433, #6131, #5050, #4145.

title: [Feature]: Permanently delete archived sessions from the desktop app, plus an optional retention policy
body:
### Problem

Terminated sessions stay in the database forever. Archiving in the desktop app is reversible by design: it moves the session to the board's Archive section (and optionally deletes its artifacts), so every session ever spawned keeps piling up there and in SQLite.

#7440 (for #3402) adds a safe permanent delete, but only on the CLI and API:

- `ao session delete <id>` and `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}`
- refused until the session is terminated and its worktree is cleaned up (`WORKSPACE_NOT_RELEASED`), while another operation holds the session, or when its turns belong to a shared orchestrator conversation (`SESSION_HISTORY_SHARED`)
- removes the session's AO history (conversation, PR facts, attachments, artifacts), keeps its spend in the agent account usage totals, and never reuses its id

Desktop users have no way to reach it, and nothing ever removes old sessions on its own. These are the two parts of #3402 Finding 3 that #7440 leaves out on purpose.

### Proposed direction

**1. A desktop delete action for archived sessions.** It would sit on archived session cards (board Archive section and the standalone archive view) and call the existing endpoint. Design decisions, per `DESIGN.md`:

- where the action lives (card menu vs. a bulk action in the Archive section)
- the confirmation, which must say the delete is permanent and what goes with it
- what to show when the worktree is not cleaned up yet: offer "Clean up and delete", or explain and link to cleanup
- how the 409 refusals (`WORKSPACE_NOT_RELEASED`, `SESSION_HISTORY_SHARED`, `SESSION_OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`) read in the UI

The board already refetches on the project-level `session_updated` event the delete emits, so the card disappears without extra wiring.

**2. An optional retention policy** (needs a product call):

- opt-in vs. on by default, and the age threshold (e.g. archived for N days)
- whether it deletes only sessions whose worktree is already released, or also runs cleanup first (dirty worktrees must never be forced)
- whether a project or a session can be exempted
- where it runs: the daemon's existing 10-minute workspace cleanup pass from #7440 is a natural home

### Alternatives considered

- Keep CLI-only delete. It works, but desktop users never see it.
- Add this to #7440. Left out to keep that PR to the backend fix, since the UI needs a design review and retention needs a product decision first.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(windows): start batch shims' targets directly so argv reaches agents byte for byte
body:
Code changes: +404 -74
Tests: +533 -15
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #7212

## Problem

On Windows, `codex` installed via npm resolves to the `codex.cmd` shim. AO cannot start a batch file directly, so the whole command line went through `cmd.exe`, which re-parses it and has no way to carry a double quote inside an argument. The Codex hook overrides contain quotes followed by `&`:

```
-c hooks.SessionStart=[{hooks=[{type="command",command="& \"C:\...\ao.exe\" hooks codex session-start",timeout=5}]}]
```

cmd.exe splits that value at the `&`, Codex exits 255, and `ao doctor` reports `codex-launch-flags` failing.

## Why no quoting can fix it

Verified empirically on Windows 11 with a real `%*`-forwarding shim and a child that echoes argv: no escaping round-trips an argument containing `"` through a batch shim.

- `""` doubling and `\"` escaping both split the value at `&` (the issue's exact symptom).
- Caret-escaping `^&` leaks into the child argv when the value stays quoted, and is consumed before the shim's `%*` re-expands the line when it does not — either way the line still splits.
- Go's own `os/exec` `.cmd` handling splits this argument too, and it also fails to quote a shim path containing spaces.

So the durable fix is to remove `cmd.exe` from the path entirely rather than search for a magic escaping.

## Fix

`process.Command`/`CommandContext` now resolve a `.cmd`/`.bat` shim to the target its own launch line starts (npm/pnpm/yarn shapes: bundled `node.exe` or PATH `node`, entry script, fixed flags) and start that directly, so argv reaches the harness byte for byte. `process.ResolveBatchShim` exposes the same rewrite for callers that already resolved the program.

The rewrite is conservative: a shim is unwrapped only when it matches a shape this package understands and every check passes. Otherwise `Command`/`CommandContext` run it through `cmd.exe /d /s /c` with every token quoted (`quoteWindowsBatchArg` doubling, as on `main`), so an unfamiliar shim like Node's bundled `C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.cmd` behaves exactly as before. The shell is `ComSpec`, or `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe` (then `exec.LookPath`) when `ComSpec` is unset, so the launch never depends on `cmd.Dir`. A shim is declined, and keeps that launch, when:

- its launch line does not forward `%*` last, or a path it names is missing;
- `%_prog%` resolves to an interpreter other than Node in the shim's `ELSE` branch (cmd-shim writes the entry point's shebang there: `bun`, `sh`, `deno`), so the entry keeps its own runtime;
- it `SET`s anything beyond `dp0`/`_prog`/`PATHEXT` — pnpm's `NODE_PATH` would be lost by a direct start;
- the launcher it names is itself a batch file (yarn v1 global chains, version-manager `node.cmd`), which would hand the line back to cmd.exe.

## Relationship to #6239 / #6468

Those PRs rewrite shims at agent-launch sites and re-point the doctor canary. This change is independent and complementary: it fixes the shared child-process layer every caller uses — including `ao doctor`'s probes, harness installs, and preview commands — on `main` as it stands today. If both land, `agentlaunch.ResolveWindowsShimArgv` becomes redundant at spawn sites that go through `process.CommandContext` and can be simplified later. The `_prog` handling here mirrors `deepseekharness`'s parser (same `ELSE`-branch read, same node/nodejs check); sharing one parser is a possible follow-up but touches those PRs, so it stays out of scope here.

## Testing

- New Windows tests in `process`: npm and yarn shim shapes unwrap to the expected target; rejected shapes include bun-shebang (`_prog=bun`), pnpm (`@SET "NODE_PATH=..."`), Node's bundled `npm.cmd` (`NODE_EXE`/`NPM_CLI_JS`), a launcher that is itself a `.cmd`, and `LookPath("node")` answering with a `node.cmd`; and an end-to-end regression runs a real shim from a spaced directory, asserting the `hooks.SessionStart` value with its embedded quote, `&` and spaces arrives byte for byte.
- `systemexec` and `previewserver` tests: npm-shaped shims unwrap (shim directory with a space); plain batch files with spaced shim paths still run through the `cmd.exe /d /s /c` path that `process` now owns.
- The review's P1 repro was verified against the real install on this machine: `commandContext(ctx, "C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\npm.cmd", "--version", "--userconfig=C:/no such dir/npmrc")` prints `11.4.2` (on the previous head it failed with `'C:\Program' is not recognized`).
- `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean; `go test` green for `process`, `previewserver`, and `systemexec` (except suites failing identically on pristine `main`: `systemexec` `sh`-dependent install tests, re-verified at the merge-base `144c32f`).

## Review updates (dff3ea64)

Addressing the review round:

- **P1, ComSpec fallback**: `systemexec` and `previewserver` take the direct-target path only when `ResolveBatchShim` actually unwrapped the shim; shims it declines keep their previous `ComSpec /d /s /c` launch, which also keeps the `/d` AutoRun guard (the fallback moved into `process` in 09ddc407). The test fixtures are back to spaced shim names (`agent tool.cmd`, `preview helper.cmd`), and both unwrap tests now run from shim directories containing a space.
- **P2, interpreter**: `%_prog%` is followed only when the shim's `ELSE` branch assigns `node`/`nodejs`.
- **P2, environment**: shims that `SET` variables the rewrite does not carry into the child are declined rather than losing them; pnpm fixture added.
- **Chaining**: launchers that resolve to another `.cmd`/`.bat` are declined at all three resolution sites.
- **Perf**: `Command`/`CommandContext` build the `exec.Cmd` first and rewrite `cmd.Path`/`cmd.Args` from the path `exec.Command` already resolved — no extra PATH scan per launch; `ResolveBatchShim` takes the caller-resolved path.
- **Nit**: the unfamiliar-shim test comment now describes the actual fallback (Go's default batch launch, `cmd.Path` still the shim) and points at the ComSpec fallback for the quoted-path case.

## Review updates (5358016)

- **ComSpec-empty fallback**: the `cmd.exe /d /s /c` fallback this commit moved into `process` now names the shell as `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe` (falling back to `exec.LookPath`) when `ComSpec` is unset. `Cmd.Start` resolves a bare `cmd.exe` against `cmd.Dir`, which callers set to a workspace after construction, so a `cmd.exe` checked into a clone could run; with no such file the launch failed as ``fork/exec .\cmd.exe: The system cannot find the file specified``. New test clears `ComSpec`, points `cmd.Dir` at another directory and runs a declined shim; verified the batch launches again through `process`, `systemexec` and `previewserver` with `ComSpec` cleared.
- **Nit**: `Command`'s doc comment now points at `rewriteBatchShim` and says a declined batch file runs through `cmd.exe /d /s /c`, instead of sending readers to `ResolveBatchShim`.

title: feat(contract): a machine's host key, so a device with its account token cannot act as it
body:
Code changes: +0 -0
Tests: +0 -0
Others: +32 -5 (contract, generated client types)

## What this changes

| Where | New |
|---|---|
| `PUT /api/cloud/v1/me/hosts/{hostId}` | Optional `hostKey`: the machine's Ed25519 public key, unpadded base64url. It is stored on the listing. A registration without it keeps the listing's key, and removing the machine clears it. |
| `GET /api/cloud/v1/me/hosts` | `hostKeys`: whether the deployment takes `hostKey`; absent means false. A deployment without it refuses a registration that carries one, because its decoder rejects unknown fields, so a client sends the key only where `hostKeys` is true. |
| `POST /api/cloud/v1/remote-hosts/{hostId}/address` and `/tunnel` | A new `hostSignature` scheme, the `X-AO-Host-Signature` header, required with `hostDigest` on a listing that has a host key. `401` covers a missing, invalid or expired signature. |

The header is `<t>.<signature>`:
- `t` is the Unix time in seconds.
- `signature` is the Ed25519 signature, in unpadded base64url, of `ao-host-v1`, the method, the path, `t` and the hex SHA-256 of the body, each followed by a newline.
- It is accepted within 5 minutes of `t`.

`packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated with the pinned `openapi-typescript` 7.4.4.

## Why

Every signed-in device of an account can read the machine's account token from `GET /me/hosts`, and `hostDigest` is only its SHA-256. So any device that ever held that token can fetch the machine's tunnel run token and serve its fixed address, or publish another address for it. That remains true after the device is signed out.

A host key closes this: only the machine holds the private key, and its own requests are signed with it.

What it does not change:
- A device that is still signed in can still remove the machine and add it again. Signing that device out of the account is what ends it.

## Compatibility

Additive only:
- the new field is optional;
- the new security requirement is an alternative next to the existing `hostDigest`.

An older desktop sends no `hostKey`, so its listings keep working with the digest alone. A newer desktop sends one only where the list says `hostKeys`, so it keeps linking against an older deployment. An older machine on a listing that has a key gets `401` until it updates, or until it is removed and added again.

## Testing

- The `breaking-changes` gate (`oasdiff` against `main`) runs in CI.
- `npm run cloud:check` verifies the regenerated client types in CI.
- Redocly reports the same 119 errors and 113 warnings on this file as on `main`.

## Merge order

1. This PR.
2. The control-plane PR that implements it, after `npm run contracts:sync` there.
3. The daemon and desktop change that sends the key and signs the machine's requests.

title: feat(remote): sign the machine's own AO Cloud requests with a host key
body:
Code changes: +156 -24
Tests: +137 -6
Others: +5 -1 (generated API spec and types, docs)

Stacked on #7294. It implements the daemon and desktop side of #7495 and #7498.

## What this changes

- **Host key:** the daemon keeps an Ed25519 key in `<data>/mobile/host.key`, mode 0600. It is made on first use, and nothing else ever reads it.
- **Signed requests:** the fixed-tunnel request and the address publish carry `X-AO-Host-Signature`. That is the key's signature over `ao-host-v1`, the method, the path, the time and the body's SHA-256, as #7495 describes.
- **Linking:** `POST /api/v1/remote-host/account-token` also returns `hostKey`, the public half. Every path that lists a machine sends it, only where `GET /me/hosts` says `hostKeys`:
  - Connect Mobile and **Allow access**;
  - Remote hosts' **Add host**, for another machine;
  - the phone's claim of a paired machine.
- **Clock:** a signature carries AO Cloud's time, from the `Date` of its last answer, so a machine with a wrong clock is not refused.
- **Path:** the signed path starts at `/api/cloud/`, as AO Cloud receives it behind a proxy that strips a prefix.
- **No key:** when the key file cannot be read, the requests go unsigned and the token answer has no key. That still works wherever the listing has no key. The key file is made only after the password checks.

## Why

Every signed-in device of an account can read the machine's account token, and AO Cloud accepted the token's SHA-256 alone on the machine routes. So any device that ever held the token could take the machine's tunnel run token and serve its fixed address, or move the listing to an address of its own, even after it was signed out.

A device that is still signed in can still remove the machine and add it again; signing it out of the account ends that. The docs say so, and that listings made before this version have no key yet.

## Compatibility

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| A new daemon and desktop against an AO Cloud without host keys | It does not list `hostKeys`, so the desktop sends no key and linking works as before. Its strict decoder would refuse the field. The signatures are ignored there. |
| A new daemon and desktop against an AO Cloud with host keys | The listing gets the key; the machine's requests are signed |
| An older desktop, new daemon | No key is sent; the digest alone keeps working |
| A listing with a key, an older daemon | Its requests are unsigned, so AO Cloud refuses them until it updates, or until the machine is removed and added again |

## Testing

CI is the gate. New and changed tests:
- `TestTheHostKeyIsMadeOnceAndKeptPrivate`: one key across reads, file mode 0600.
- `TestTheMachineSignsItsTunnelRequestWithItsHostKey`: a test server rebuilds the signed message and checks the signature and its time.
- `TestTheHostSignatureMatchesAFixedVector` pins the message with a fixed seed, time, body and a prefixed URL. A signature from the same code was checked against AO Cloud's own verifier.
- `TestASignatureCarriesAOCloudsTime` and `TestAMachineWithoutAHostKeySendsTheDigestAlone`.
- `TestPublishRemoteHostAddressUsesScopedDigestWithoutRedirects`: the publish is signed.
- `TestIssueAccountTokenRequiresPairingPasswordAndPersistsHash`: the answer carries the public key.
- `link-this-computer.test.ts`: the listing carries `hostKey`, and does not where the list lacks `hostKeys`.
- `ThisComputerAccess.test.tsx`: its AO Cloud lists no `hostKeys` and refuses the field, while its daemon returns a key. So every Allow access test now also covers an older AO Cloud.

`backend/internal/httpd/apispec/openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated.

## Merge order

1. #7495 (merged) and #7498, the contract.
2. The control-plane change that accepts and checks the key.
3. #7294.
4. This PR, retargeted to `main`. Its order against the control plane does not matter, because of `hostKeys`.

title: fix: consolidate AO side-chat commands to /btw
body:
Code changes: +9 -28  
Tests: +294 -32  
Others: +8 -8 (locale assets)  

## What

Use `/btw` as the only AO side-chat command in the main and side composers. Typing `/side` still finds `/btw` through its description; choosing the suggestion inserts `/btw ` so the user can write the prompt before anything is created or sent. Literal `/side {prompt}` submissions go to the agent normally, and provider-owned `/side` commands remain available.

## Why

Two AO aliases exposed the same action. Side-composer completion also created a destination immediately instead of letting users finish the question. Keep routing simple: an old saved main-composer `/side` retry now sends its original text to the agent, just like a new literal `/side` message.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `/si` lists both AO `/side` and `/btw` | Only AO `/btw` appears; its description still matches “side” |
| Choosing a side-composer command immediately opens a new destination | Enter, Tab or click inserts `/btw`; the eventual submitted prompt creates the destination |
| Literal `/side question` is intercepted by AO when side chats are enabled | New literal `/side question` messages reach the current agent |
| Old main-composer `/side` retries opened AO side chats | Retrying sends `/side …` as ordinary agent text with the original delivery key |
| Settings hints advertise both aliases | All eight existing localized hints advertise `/btw` only |

title: fix(chat): hand the previous orchestrator's context to its replacement
body:
## Problem

When a project orchestrator is replaced (a clean replacement, or a new orchestrator after the old one was killed), the new orchestrator rebinds the same project conversation. The UI keeps the full history, but the new agent starts a fresh provider session with only its system prompt. An "Agent context reset." marker is the only trace. So the user sees the whole history while the agent knows none of it: "continue with what we planned" has nothing to continue from.

## Change

- `service/chat`: when an orchestrator starts a fresh provider over a branch another orchestrator left, `startLocked` builds a handoff note from that orchestrator with the provider-switch builder (`domain.BuildHandoffNote`: original task, turns, artifacts, changed files). The previous owner is the inherited active branch's session. Turns are read from the project conversation itself, so a retry after the rebind still gets them.
- **Unanswered request.** If the previous orchestrator was replaced mid-turn, its last human request had no answer and was dropped. The note now carries it under "Unanswered request": not done, or only partly, and the agent waits for the user before acting on it. It is not replayed and not reported as completed.
- **Bound to the provider branch.** The note is stored as `HandoffNote` on the replacement's own provider boundary, the same field provider switches use. Every restart of that branch re-applies it. A later provider switch creates a branch with its own note, so a cold resume after a switch uses the switch's note, not the older replacement note. A fresh restart on the session's own lineage carries the note to its new boundary.
- The note reaches the agent through `withHandoffNote` on the provider system prompt. It does not appear as a user message and does not start a turn. The UI history and the context-reset marker are unchanged.
- Never fails a spawn: if the note cannot be built, a Warn is logged and the start continues without it.

## Not changed

A project's first orchestrator, a session restarting itself, provider switches, and native provider handoffs.

## Notes

- B's chat opening empty although it owns A's conversation (seen in review) is a separate issue.
- The old orchestrator's provider process can stay alive after a replacement (#4317). Separate fix.

## Validation

No local builds or tests were run, per the user's instruction; CI runs them.

New tests (`backend/internal/service/chat/replacement_handoff_note_test.go`):
- a replacement gets a note with the previous orchestrator's real chat turn (request and answer), and no unanswered section after an idle replacement;

title: fix(kanban): make card statuses match what is actually happening
body:
Code changes: +372 -175  
Tests: +705 -43  
Others: +195 -65 (generated sqlc and OpenAPI, i18n)

## What

The status text on Kanban cards now matches what is actually happening. Every state of AO's own review stays in Validating, In review only holds PRs waiting on a person, Ready only holds PRs that can merge, a working agent says "Working", the spinner only shows for work in progress, and the session dot describes the same PR as the card.

## Why

Several card statuses were misleading or false:

- "Review scheduled" on a draft PR, which auto review never reviews.
- "Review pending" with a spinner after a cancelled review, which auto review never retries on the same commit.
- "Review failed" on a pass auto review was still going to retry.
- "Needs review" after AO's own review had already asked for changes.
- "Approved" in Ready on a PR with merge conflicts or failing CI.
- A red dot next to "Mergeable" on a session with two PRs, because the dot read the worst PR and the label read the best one.
- "Awaiting PR" on every idle session with no PR, including chat and research sessions.

## Before / After

Same scenarios on the base commit (`0a43ac09dd`) and this branch. Each card's column, phrase and status come from running that commit's own `DeriveKanbanPresentation`/`DeriveStatus` on the same facts, rendered by that commit's frontend (`dev:web` with the e2e fake agent).

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Board before](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dab5684ed1/docs/screenshots/pr-7503/kanban-before-brick.png?raw=true) | ![Board after](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dab5684ed1/docs/screenshots/pr-7503/kanban-after-brick.png?raw=true) |
| Validating card whose AO review asked for changes: "Needs review" | "Changes requested" with the attention pulse |
| Idle no-PR card: "Awaiting PR" | "Idle" |

Full behavior table:

| # | Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Draft PR, auto review on | Validating · Review scheduled | Validating · Draft |
| 2 | Auto review on, agent working, no review yet | Validating · Review scheduled + spinner | Validating · Working + spinner |
| 3 | AO's review was cancelled, auto review on | Validating · Review pending + spinner | Validating · Review cancelled |
| 3b | AO's review was cancelled, auto review off | In review · Needs human review | In review · Review cancelled |
| 3c | AO's review cancelled on a mergeable head another harness approved, auto review on | Ready · Mergeable | Validating · Review cancelled |
| 4 | AO's review failed, retries left | Validating · Review failed | Validating · Retrying review + spinner |
| 5 | AO's review failed 3 times | Validating · Review failed | Validating · Review failed (unchanged) |
| 6 | AO asked for changes, auto-fix off | Validating · Needs review | Validating · Changes requested |
| 7 | AO asked for changes, auto-fix on, agent idle (feedback delivered or not) | Validating · Needs review | Validating · Changes requested |
| 7b | AO asked for changes, auto-fix on, agent working | Validating · Needs review | Validating · Addressing comments + spinner |
| 8 | AO asked for changes, no auto review, no auto-fix | In review · Needs human review | Validating · Changes requested |
| 9 | Waiting on a person's review | In review · Needs human review | In review · Awaiting review |
| 10 | Waiting on review, merge conflicts | In review · Needs human review | In review · Merge conflicts |
| 11 | Approved, merge conflicts | Ready · Approved | In review · Merge conflicts |
| 12 | Approved, CI failing | Ready · CI failing | In review · CI failing |
| 13 | Approved or mergeable, agent working | Ready · Mergeable + spinner | Ready · Working + spinner |
| 14 | Agent working in In review | In review · Needs human review | In review · Working + spinner |
| 15 | Two PRs: one mergeable, one CI failing, legacy sidebar design | Mergeable with a red dot | Mergeable with a green dot |
| 16 | Only AO posted the changes request | Dot says changes requested, label "Needs human review" | Both say changes requested |
| 17 | No PR, agent idle | Building · Awaiting PR | Building · Idle |
| 18 | Agent asked a question | Blocked | Needs input |
| 19 | Mergeable or approved PR, worker exited or silent | Ready · Mergeable or Approved | Ready · Exited or No signal |

## How

- `backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go` holds all column and phrase rules. Worker states that need a person (Blocked, Needs input, Exited, No signal) are shared by every live column, and an active worker wins the phrase except on merged or closed PRs.
- Validating holds every state of AO's own review on the head: scheduled, running, failed (including retries used up), cancelled while auto review is on, and any AO changes request, with or without auto-fix. In review is only for a person's review on the provider. With auto review off, a cancelled or failed AO pass moves the PR to In review, since nothing will run it again.
- "Addressing comments" and "Fixing CI" only show while the worker is active. An idle worker with an AO changes request shows "Changes requested", even after AO delivered the inline comments, because nothing is being addressed until the worker picks them up.
- The current-head review run query now also counts failed auto passes on that head (`failed_auto_runs`). The retry limit moved to `domain.AutoReviewFailedRetryLimit`, which both existing copies now use. It also reports `auto_retry_blocked` for a cancelled or decided pass on that head and harness, so "Retrying review" only appears when auto review will really retry.
- `displayStatus` is an enum in the API, so the OpenAPI spec and `schema.ts` are regenerated. Removed values: "Awaiting PR", "Needs review", "Needs human review", "Review pending". Added: "Needs input", "Idle", "Retrying review", "Awaiting review", "Review cancelled", "Merge conflicts".
- Product UI: the loader follows the phrase only; the attention pulse adds "Needs input" and "Merge conflicts".
- The sidebar dot in the current design follows the card's lane, from main, and now treats "Needs input" and "Merge conflicts" as needing attention, matching the card. The legacy Developer-mode dot takes its colour from the PR phrase when there is one and falls back to the SCM status for worker phrases.
- Mobile treats "Needs input" like "Blocked" for "Needs you".

Intentionally not changed: drafts and output-file sessions stay in Validating.

title: perf(chat): keep splitting streamed replies when only code looks like a link definition
body:
Code changes: +13 -5\
Tests: +7 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Streamed chat replies keep rendering block by block when code in them only looks like a link definition.

## Why

While a reply streams, `ChatMarkdown` re-renders only its last few blocks. Link reference definitions and footnotes apply to the whole reply, so a reply that has them renders as one document. That check was the regex `/\]\s*:|\[\^/` on the raw text. It also matches common code:

- `def load(rows: list[int]) -> dict[str, int]:`
- `if rows[0]:`
- `for k in items[1:]:`
- `{ [key]: 1 }`

Once a reply contained any of these, every later update re-parsed and re-rendered the whole reply. A long reply with Python in it got slower with each update.

## Before / After

A 50 KB reply streamed as 500 whole-text updates through the real `ChatMarkdown` (vitest + jsdom on `main`, median of 3 runs, text fade on):

| Reply | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Has Python with type hints | 34.8 s total, 64.7 ms per update (median), 220 ms worst; 1 block | 2.0 s total, 3.6 ms per update (median), 15 ms worst; 472 blocks |
| TypeScript only (control) | 2.1 s total, 3.7 ms per update (median) | 2.1 s total, 3.6 ms per update (median) |

The final HTML is identical before and after for both replies.

## How

- The parse tree decides, not the text. `splitStreamingMarkdown` already parses the unsettled tail with the renderer's own parser. The reply now stays whole only when that tree has a `definition` or `footnoteDefinition` node. Text inside code blocks never produces one.
- The tree also finds definitions the old regex was never meant to cover: definitions nested in lists or block quotes, and computed object keys on their own line no longer trigger a false match.
- Committed blocks are safe. Each one was in the parsed tail when it was cut, so if it had held a definition, the reply would already have gone whole.
- Trade-off: a reply that really contains a definition or footnote is now parsed once more per update than before, because the regex skipped parsing. Agents rarely write these, so I kept the check simple.
- The numbers above were measured with an earlier version of this fix that anchored the regex to line starts. For the replies benchmarked, both versions take the same block-splitting path. I did not re-measure the final version.

## Testing

- Added two examples to the "matches a full GFM parse at every character" test: a definition nested in a list and quote, and a Python fence with `dict[str, int]:`.
- Added a test that a reply whose only `]:` is inside code still splits into blocks.
- Tests and checks were not run locally. CI covers them.

title: feat(settings): turn on swipe back/forward by default
body:
Code changes: +1 -1\
Tests: +14 -15\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Turns the "Navigation gestures" setting (two-finger horizontal swipe for back/forward) on by default.

## Why

#6858 shipped the swipe navigation but defaulted it to off, so nobody finds it unless they open Settings. It should work out of the box.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A user who never touched the toggle has gestures off | A user who never touched the toggle has gestures on |
| A user who turned it on keeps it on | Unchanged |
| A user who turned it off keeps it off | Unchanged |

No screenshots. The only visible change is the toggle's initial state in Settings > General.

## How

One line in `ui-store.ts`: the stored value was read with `=== "true"`, now `!== "false"`, the same way `terminalCopyOnSelect` is read. The toggle always writes the string `"true"` or `"false"` to `localStorage["ao.navigationGestures"]`, so a missing key means the user never touched it. An explicit `"false"` is an opt-out and stays off. No migration is needed, because nothing else writes the key and the default was never persisted.

Known unverified risks from the review of #6858, now exposed to everyone by default:

- A mouse with horizontal wheel notches (tilt or thumb wheel) may navigate on Windows and Linux, and possibly on Mac. Chromium reports about 100px per notch and gives phase-less wheel events synthetic begin/end phases, so the scroll-phase relay cannot tell a mouse from a trackpad. Two notches inside 120ms pass the 110px arm threshold. Not reproduced on real Windows or Linux hardware.
- The momentum decay rule can navigate before the fingers lift, once an armed fast swipe decays for four events in a row.

## Testing

Not run locally. Relies on CI: `ui-store.test.ts` (default is on, an explicit off survives a restart) and the `navigation-gestures` e2e spec (on by default, turn it off, survives a reload).

title: feat(mobile): start Connect Mobile from the sidebar, a switch to turn it off, and no note while remote access starts
body:
Code changes: +38 -48
Tests: +33 -31
Others: +0 -32 (locale strings)

Stacked on #7294.

## What this changes

Clicking **Connect mobile** in the sidebar now turns Connect Mobile on as its page opens, so preparing the pairing code starts at once instead of after a second click on **Generate**. While the code's internet address starts, nothing is said under the code anymore.

| Way to the page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar **Connect mobile**, Connect Mobile off | Shows **Generate** | Turns on and prepares the code |
| Settings → Connect Mobile, Connect Mobile off | Shows **Generate** | Same |
| Turned off on the page while it is open | Stays off | Same: it starts once per opening |
| Under the code while the internet address starts | "Enabling remote access / Until then, works on this network only" (or "…only over Tailscale") | Nothing. The code already works on this network and gains the address by itself. |
| Under the code once it has the address | "Remote access on" | Same |
| Remote access failed | "Works on this network only — remote access couldn't start…" | Same |
| Turning it off | A ghost text button, "Turn off mobile connection", at the bottom of the details | A **Connect mobile** switch row under the code, like the Keep awake row below it. **Generate** stays on the code while it is off. |

## Why

The sidebar button is the user asking to pair a phone, so it is the consent that **Generate** asked for. The **Generate** click only added a step before the 20–30 seconds remote access takes to start.

## How

- `openGlobalSettings("mobile", { startPairing: true })` from the sidebar. `stores/ui-store.ts` keeps `startPairing` on the settings modal only for the `mobile` section.
- `ConnectMobileContent` calls the same `startBridge` that **Generate** calls, once per opening, when the status says Connect Mobile is off. Signed in, that is the existing path that links the computer before the tunnel starts.
- The starting note and its three labels are removed from the panel and all 8 locale files.
- The switch row reuses the sidebar's **Connect mobile** label; the unused "Turn off mobile connection" label is removed from all 8 locale files.

CI is the gate. In `ConnectMobileModal.test.tsx`:

Making it a focusable link would add a dead tab stop. The keyboard path to the session is the link itself (Enter).

title: fix(desktop): align macOS titlebar with the framed center panel
body:
Code changes: +44 -32\
Tests: +14 -14\
Others: +0 -0

## What

macOS window chrome polish:

- The traffic lights, sidebar brand, and in-panel page title (e.g. "Automations") now share one centreline.
- The red traffic light lines up with the sidebar's row icons (Search, Automations).
- Collapsing the sidebar no longer expands the center panel. It keeps its inset, border, and radius, and nothing in its padding animates. Its border drops to 50% strength while the sidebar is collapsed.
- The sidebar brand reads "Orchestrator" instead of "Orchestrator.inc". The app name, window title, and About dialog are unchanged.

## Why

The sidebar's top row and the native traffic lights were centred on a 36px row (y = 18). With the sidebar open, the center panel sits 6px inset plus a 1px border below the window top, so its 36px header centres at y = 25. The brand sat 7px above the page title next to it. The lights also started 4px left of the sidebar icons below them.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Brand and traffic lights ~7px above the "Automations" title; red light left of the Search icon; collapsing the sidebar animates the panel to flush | Brand, lights, and title on one line; red light aligned with Search; panel keeps its frame when the sidebar collapses, border at half strength |

_Screenshots to be added._

## How

- `shared/window-chrome.ts`: the new `MAC_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_ROW_HEIGHT` = 36 + 2 × (6px inset + 1px border) = 50. Main centres the native buttons on it, zoom-aware via `syncMacWindowButtons`. `MAC_WINDOW_BUTTON_X` changes from 14 to 18 (8px rail padding + 10px row inset).
- `tokens.css`: `--size-traffic-light-clearance` uses the same formula, so the sidebar offset, the `TitlebarNav` row, and the drag strip all follow it. `--size-titlebar-cluster-left` moves from 80 to 84 to keep the toggle's gap after the lights. Fullscreen keeps the flush 36px row, because it has no frame and no native buttons.
- `styles.css`: on macOS (windowed), the panel has the same 6px inset on all four sides whether or not the sidebar is open, so collapsing never resizes or snaps the frame. Shell padding no longer transitions. With the sidebar collapsed, the surface border fades to 50% (the existing 280ms border-color transition). Native fullscreen stays flush.
- The title clearance for a collapsed sidebar is now measured from the framed panel's inner edge (`--size-titlebar-content-offset-mac-panel`). The traffic-light drag strip stops at the panel header's bottom (`--size-mac-panel-header-bottom`), so it never covers panel content.
- Linux keeps its 36px titlebar row. The artifact viewer's fullscreen overlay header sits on the traffic-light row.
- `_shell.tsx`: the panel no longer goes flush, so I removed the closed-sidebar band that painted the topbar colour behind the traffic lights. Otherwise it would cover the panel's top-left corner. The strip stays as a drag region.
- I tried moving the native lights with the sidebar state and rejected it. AppKit can't animate them, so they jumped 7px on every toggle.

| --- | --- |
| ![Before: selection across lines 2-4 with the Add to chat button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef7c7ce1-ce21-4e0b-874e-b0c044c013a9) | ![After: selection and button gone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aef1b1e2-03ed-45f5-b532-15c5fdf13669) |

**2. Shift+click extension is broken, and clicking "Add to chat" afterwards hangs the renderer.**

Shift+clicking a later line extends the native selection (the highlight visually covers the new range and the button stays visible), but the feature does not work past that point:

- Clicking **Add to chat** (or pressing Cmd/Ctrl+L) adds **nothing** to the composer — no chat message is sent and no rejection message is shown.
- After that click, the renderer's main thread blocks: the page stops painting and stops executing JavaScript (a scripted frame counter over 2s returns nothing; `page.evaluate` never resolves). The window stays unresponsive.

Video 1 (rebuild, 8s) — the selection and the Add to chat button disappear the moment the rows are replaced.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/628ceca0-f0d9-41e1-927a-9929e5213dc9

Video 2 (shift+click) — the highlight extends and the button stays, but clicking "Add to chat" sends nothing and freezes the page.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62d896dd-caf3-4957-8b0e-8d9620c8af3c

## Expected behavior

- A redraw that replaces the selected rows for fresh copies of the same content should keep the selection (and any in-progress drag/shift+click anchor) alive, placing it back on the rebuilt rows at the same characters. Deliberate clears — Escape, clicking elsewhere — should still clear it.
- Shift+click on a later line should extend the selection, and **Add to chat** should quote the extended range.

## Repro steps

1. Open a session in chat mode with workspace changes, and open the session view's **Files** tab so the diff renders in the review pane.
2. Drag-select a few lines of code (e.g. lines 2–4). The floating **Add to chat** button appears next to the selection.
3. Trigger a row rebuild: let the workspace refresh (a snapshot landing mid-stream does it), or observe the redraw when the highlighter finishes loading right after the tab opens. → The selection and the button vanish.
4. For the shift+click hang: reload, select lines 2–4 again, then shift+click on a later line (e.g. line 6). The highlight extends and the button stays. Click **Add to chat**. → Nothing is added to the composer and the window becomes unresponsive.

The recorded evidence above was produced with the repo's Playwright harness (`e2e/files-ask-in-chat.spec.ts` infrastructure, route-mocked session with `src/retry.ts` changed), rebuilding the rows exactly the way the viewer does — replacing every row with a fresh clone — and asserting the outcomes above. The relevant existing spec pins the destructive behavior as expected: "the button hides on Escape, when scrolled away (returning when back), and when the rows redraw" expects `askButton` to be **hidden** after a row rebuild.

## Relevant code (main)

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/diffs/useCodeSelection.ts` — `update()` publishes `null` as soon as `readCodeSelection` returns `null`; once a rebuild disconnects the selected rows, `root.contains(anchor)` fails and the selection (plus the drag/shift+click anchor) is dropped. The `MutationObserver` only re-reads; it never restores a selection onto rebuilt rows.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/diffs/SelectionAskButton.tsx` — the button/`Cmd+L` → `onAsk` path that silently no-ops (and wedges the main thread) when the selection was extended with shift+click.
- `frontend/e2e/files-ask-in-chat.spec.ts` — "the button hides on Escape, when scrolled away (returning when back), and when the rows redraw" encodes today's destructive behavior.

Happy to take a run at fixing this if the maintainers agree with the direction: snapshot the live selection's ends in row-relative coordinates (row index + character offset), and when a rebuild disconnects them, restore onto the rebuilt rows; treat shift+click as a first-class extension.

title: feat(desktop): share sessions and projects with teams
body:
**Draft for review. Please don't merge.** The control plane side is OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#31, and the desktop needs it.

## What this adds

Share a session or a whole project with a team once, and everyone in it gets the access you picked.

## Share dialog (`ShareSessionDialog`)

It keeps the same props and exports, and the existing test still passes.
- **One field** for people and teams. Type to search the workspace's teams and the people it knows, or type any full email.
- **Staged summary.** Picks become tokens, and the dialog spells out who gets what before you share. For example: "Dana Kim and Omar Haddad get Watch. Ben Ortiz already has this or more. Farah Nasser already has full access as a workspace member."
- **Access list:**
  - the owner;
  - teams, which expand to show each member's effective access and where it comes from;
  - people, marked "from a link" or "shared directly";
  - pending emails;
  - shares that come from the whole project (changed at project level, with a link to switch scope).
- **Edits:** access changes happen in place and optimistically. Stopping a share shows a toast with Undo.
- **Links:** the old link UI is kept under "Anyone with the link".
- **"New team…"** opens straight from the field, with whoever is picked so far.

## Settings › Teams

- Your workspace's teams, plus teams you're in elsewhere.
- A page per team: rename, leave, delete, people with role menus, and what's shared with the team.
- Removing someone, leaving or deleting first asks the server what is lost and says it plainly, including what the person keeps another way.

## For the person shared with

- **Sidebar:** a quiet people mark on shared projects. Its tooltip says who shared and through which teams.
- **Session header:** a tag such as "Watch · via Platform", in the same place the owner sees Share.
- **Toast:** "Asha Rao shared Add Apple Pay with Platform", with Open. The first list after sign-in is remembered silently, so nothing old is announced.

## Details

- **Suggestions list:** it floats above the dialog, so a short dialog never clips it. It closes after each pick so the summary stays in view. It scrolls with the wheel inside the dialog's scroll lock, using the same approach as `SearchablePicker`, and follows the keyboard.
- **i18n:** about 140 strings, in every locale (es, fr and pt-BR include `_many`).
- **Copy:** no new jargon. The access levels and limits are the ones links already use.

## Testing

- **New unit and component tests (32):**
  - the share dialog (owner, team rows, expansion, staged summary, share payload, change in place, stop with Undo, project scope);
  - the people field (ordering, keyboard, unavailable rows, emails, New team, workspace members, close after pick);
  - Teams settings (empty state, both lists, roles and the last owner, owner eligibility, remove, delete and leave confirms);
  - the share toast (silent first load, a new share via a team, the 3-toast cap);
  - the session tag and the sidebar tooltip;
  - the access labels.
- **Typecheck:** clean.
- **Full vitest:** the same 42 failures as untouched main (browser-profile-import, remote-proxy, ChatWorkspace, ContextMeter), plus `ReadOnlyFileView` once under full-suite load. It passes on its own and this branch does not touch it.
- **Driven end to end in the dev app** (Electron with CDP) against a local control plane seeded with a workspace, 16 teams, a guest and a second workspace:
  - sharing with a team and an email (67 ms round trip);
  - editing access;
  - Settings › Teams;
  - the guest's sidebar, session tags and a live toast that opens the session.

  The polish commit fixes what that run found.
- **Against staging** (td 362, control plane #31), signed in as a real account that gets access only through a team:
  - the shared project mark and its tooltip;
  - Teams you're in, and the team page with both shares at their levels;
  - the live toast "Pritom shared pricing-page-… with Design reviews", 12 s after the share.
- **CI:** all 12 checks pass (typecheck and every vitest shard).

## Found along the way (not changed here)

Reloading the window leaks its cloud streams in the main process (`cloud-cp-proxy.ts`): a reload doesn't destroy the WebContents. After a few reloads the 8-stream cap answers `429 This window already has 8 open cloud streams`, and live state (viewers, composer) stops loading until restart. That's worth its own small fix: tear streams down when the main frame navigates.
