title: [Bug]: [Bug]: DeepSeek account login detected as auth unknown, hiding it from desktop agent selector
body:
### What went wrong?

## Bug description

DeepSeek Harness is installed and authenticated using the official DeepSeek account login, but Agent Orchestrator reports its authentication status as `unknown` and excludes DeepSeek from the desktop agent selector.

DeepSeek can successfully execute a standalone session through the Agent Orchestrator CLI after configuring the DeepSeek ACP profile to use account-based authentication.

### Environment

- Agent Orchestrator: v0.14.8
- macOS: Apple silicon (ARM64)
- DeepSeek Harness: v0.2.1-rc.5
- Executable: `/opt/homebrew/bin/dsh`
- Interface: Desktop Chat / standalone agent selector
- Authentication: DeepSeek account login, not an API key

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install DeepSeek Harness and authenticate with the official DeepSeek account login.
2. Verify that `dsh web` opens and that a DeepSeek model can successfully answer a prompt.
3. Open Agent Orchestrator → Settings → Harness → DeepSeek.
4. Observe that installation is detected but authentication shows `Setup status unavailable`.
5. Run `ao agent ls --refresh` and observe that DeepSeek is installed but has an unknown authentication status.
6. Open the standalone agent selector in the desktop application.
7. Observe that only Claude Code, Codex and Hermes Agent are listed; DeepSeek is missing.

### Expected behavior

Agent Orchestrator should recognize a valid DeepSeek account-based sign-in as authorized or configured and display DeepSeek in the desktop agent selector without requiring an API key.

### Actual behavior

DeepSeek is excluded because Agent Orchestrator's authentication probe returns `unknown` / `auth_check_inconclusive`.

The diagnostic reports `credential_environment_missing`, even though DeepSeek is authenticated through its account-login credential store.

### Verified workaround and evidence

After configuring the DeepSeek ACP profile in `~/.dsh/profiles/acp/cordis.patch.yml` with the account-based provider route, the following command can successfully start a DeepSeek session:

`ao spawn --standalone --harness deepseek-harness --mode chat`

The resulting session successfully completes a harmless test turn using account authentication.

However, DeepSeek remains hidden from the desktop agent selector.

This demonstrates that execution through the CLI works, while the desktop authentication-readiness filter does not recognize the account login.

### Related issues

- #4031 — Kimi account authentication incorrectly reported as unknown/unauthorized
- #6581 — DeepSeek configuration errors displayed without a usable recovery path

### Requested fix

Please support detection of DeepSeek Harness account-based authentication (`deepseek-account-platform`) as a valid readiness state so DeepSeek can appear in the desktop agent selector without requiring an API key.

A clear account-authentication diagnostic would also help distinguish missing credentials from unsupported authentication detection.

### Safety and scope

No application code, security checks or credentials were modified to bypass the desktop selector. The ACP configuration workaround is local and reversible.

Existing project sessions were not interrupted.

Sensitive credentials and authentication files are not included in this report.

title: bug(cli): ao project set-config drops and wipes Cleanup (preRemove) scripts
body:
## Summary
`ao project set-config` cannot set Cleanup (`preRemove`) scripts, and any call to it **deletes** Cleanup scripts that were set in Project Settings → Scripts. This happens with field flags and with `--config-json`. Without Cleanup scripts, AO stops running the project's teardown before removing worktrees. On disk-constrained machines that means dependencies, build outputs and test labs are no longer reclaimed.

Related to #7229, which covers the same full-replace behavior for `effort`; the plan in its claim comment would also fix this. This issue tracks the Cleanup case separately because the fields are lost silently and its effect differs (teardown stops running).

## Evidence (main @ `c0b351a`)
- The daemon's config has the field: [`domain/projectconfig.go:41`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c0b351a31eccaf1ac55f8e5015fd21ab414545ca/backend/internal/domain/projectconfig.go#L39-L41) `PreRemove []string \`json:"preRemove,omitempty"\``.
- The CLI's mirror struct does not: [`cli/project.go:110-131`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c0b351a31eccaf1ac55f8e5015fd21ab414545ca/backend/internal/cli/project.go#L110-L131) has `PostCreate` but no `PreRemove` (`grep -ci preremove backend/internal/cli/project.go` → 0). There is also no `--pre-remove` flag.
- `--config-json` unmarshals into that struct ([`cli/project.go:368`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c0b351a31eccaf1ac55f8e5015fd21ab414545ca/backend/internal/cli/project.go#L366-L371)), so a `"preRemove": [...]` key is silently discarded.
- `set-config` is a full replace ("Replace a project's per-project config", [`cli/project.go:301`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c0b351a31eccaf1ac55f8e5015fd21ab414545ca/backend/internal/cli/project.go#L301)). Any CLI edit, e.g. `ao project set-config <id> --post-create '…'`, sends a config without `preRemove`, which clears it. The struct already special-cases `WorkersRequestReview` for this exact round-trip problem ([`cli/project.go:127`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c0b351a31eccaf1ac55f8e5015fd21ab414545ca/backend/internal/cli/project.go#L127)); `preRemove` was missed.

## Steps to reproduce
1. In Project Settings → Scripts for a local project, add a Cleanup step and save.
2. Run `ao project set-config <id> --config-json "$(ao project get <id> --json | jq '.project.config')"`, i.e. write the current config back unchanged.
3. Run `ao project get <id> --json | jq '.project.config.preRemove'`.

**Actual:** `null`. The Cleanup step is gone, and later archives and `ao session cleanup` remove worktrees without running it.
**Expected:** `preRemove` round-trips through `--config-json`, flag-mode edits leave it untouched, and `set-config` exposes a way to set it (e.g. `--pre-remove`, repeatable, like `--post-create`).

## Workaround
Set scripts in the app (Project Settings → Scripts), or `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}` with the full current config, which is what the UI does. Do not use `ao project set-config` on projects that have Cleanup steps.

## Environment
macOS (Mac mini), AO desktop app + bundled `ao` CLI. Found while setting up per-project Setup/Cleanup scripts to stop worktrees filling the disk.

title: fix(remote): stop a reset remote tunnel from crashing the main process
body:
Code changes: +66 -15\ Tests: +188 -10\ Others: +0 -0 Fixes #7043 ## What When a remote machine's HTTPS tunnel connection is reset, the desktop app no longer shows a chain of "A JavaScript error occurred in the main process" dialogs (`ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION` at `JSStreamSocket.doWrite`). The proxy drops the dead tunnel and the next request opens a new one. Also: - A GET or HEAD that a reset cut off before its answer is sent once more, over the new tunnel, and the console logs the first try's failure. POSTs and DELETEs still answer 502, with or without a body. - If the host can't be reached to check its identity (connection refused or reset, DNS, no route, timeout), the proxy answers `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` instead of `HOST_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED`. A host that answered wrongly (a redirect, a bad TLS certificate) is still `HOST_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED`. Both log lines now name fetch's cause, not only "fetch failed". - The console names a tunnel the host or the network closed, with its close code (1006 is a reset). - After `close()`, no request opens a new upstream session. Before, a request waiting on a session that arrived closed (a GOAWAY) opened one that nothing closed. `main` has this leak too. ## Why Over HTTPS, `remote-proxy.ts` runs its HTTP/2 session inside a WebSocket (`createWebSocketStream`), and Node wraps that stream in a `JSStreamSocket`. A reset connection (sleep/wake, a Wi-Fi or VPN switch, the host restarting) breaks it: ``` T0 network tunnel's TCP connection is reset T1 ws destroys the socket without emitting an error → WebSocket closes (1006) → stream reports EOF T2 Node net EOF + allowHalfOpen=false → socket.end() → JSStreamSocket shutdown starts T3 ws stream's _final waits for the TCP socket's 'finish', which never comes (the socket is already destroyed) → shutdown stays pending, the stream never closes, and the HTTP/2 session never learns its socket is gone T4 HTTP/2 every frame it writes now fails assert(kCurrentShutdownRequest === null) at js_stream_socket:176, uncaught: a ping or data frame, a RST_STREAM per closed stream, then the keep-alive's GOAWAY (session.destroy) ``` Each of those frames throws once, so each one opens a separate dialog. ## How - `webSocketTunnelStream` wraps the WebSocket and destroys the stream at its `end`. The stream ends only after the WebSocket closed and everything it read has been passed on, so the stream closes before Node's shutdown can start, and the session goes down with it. It does not destroy on the WebSocket's `close`. While a write is in flight, Node's session stops reading (`MaybeStopReading`), so frames the host sent just before a clean close can still be waiting in the stream at that moment. - The test hosts use the same helper. Their own WebSocket tunnel had the same bug, so a host writing after a reset threw `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION` inside the test process. - `retriable()` adds "a GET/HEAD whose session was destroyed before its response" to the existing `REFUSED_STREAM` retry. It still retries once. The retry calls `sessionForRequest(false)`: if that session open fails, the proxy does not switch to HTTP/1.1 for a minute. The retry runs the moment its session died, and a LAN host that is still restarting refuses it. - `close()` sets `closing`, and `sessionForRequest` then opens no session. This covers retries and any other request still in flight. - `unreachable()` matches a fetch `TypeError` whose cause has a network code (`ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `EHOSTDOWN`, `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ENETDOWN`, `ENETUNREACH`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`), or a `TimeoutError`. This applies to requests and to WebSocket upgrades. Anything else stays an identity failure. - Changed existing tests: the cut-off GET in "answers 502 or fails the body when the tunnel closes" now goes once more (4 tunnels, not 3). "retires a session whose host stopped answering pings" now uses a body-less POST for its 502, checks that a GET is retried, and checks that the retry is logged. ## Before / After The same tests, run against `main`'s `remote-proxy.ts`, this PR's first commit (2c955fc07a), its second (f5c31c349d), and this PR's head: | Test | `main` | 2c955fc07a | f5c31c349d | Head | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Reset: no uncaught exception, new tunnel, close logged (1006) | ❌ 3 uncaught `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION` | ❌ host-side `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION`; no close log | ✅ | ✅ | | Answer sent just before a clean tunnel close is delivered | ✅ | ❌ 502 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (frames dropped) | ✅ | ✅ | | Refused or timed-out host answers `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`; a redirecting one `HOST_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED`; the cause is logged | ❌ refused → `HOST_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED` | ❌ same | ❌ redirect → `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` | ✅ | | GET cut off by a reset is sent again and logged; a body-less DELETE is not sent again | ❌ GET 502 | ❌ GET 502 | ❌ retry not logged | ✅ | | LAN host restart: the GET's refused retry leaves HTTP/2 on | ✅ (no retry) | ✅ (no retry) | ❌ HTTP/1.1 for 60 s | ✅ | | No upstream session opens after `close()` | ❌ 2 sessions | ❌ 2 sessions | ❌ 2 sessions | ✅ | | Whole `remote-proxy.test.ts`, Node 26.8.1 | | | | ✅ 75/75, 5 runs | | Whole `remote-proxy.test.ts`, Electron 44.7.0 (Node v24.21.0) | ❌ reset test, with the dialogs' frames | | | ✅ 75/75, 3 runs | Each head fix was also removed on its own, to check that a test fails without it: the identity classification (by network code, the `TimeoutError` case, and the logged cause), the GET/HEAD-only retry, the HTTP/1.1 fallback on a retry, the `closing` check, and the retry log. The old tests passed 73/73 with the GET/HEAD-only check removed, because their POSTs had a body.
main: reset test (3 uncaught, one from the keep-alive's session.destroy()) ``` FAIL opens a new tunnel after a reset, without writing into the old one AssertionError: expected [ …(3) ] to deeply equal [] + "Error: This is caused by either a bug in Node.js or incorrect usage of Node.js internals. + at assert (node:internal/assert:11:11) + at JSStreamSocket.doWrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:176:5) + at JSStream.onwrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:35:57)", + "Error: This is caused by either a bug in Node.js or incorrect usage of Node.js internals. + at assert (node:internal/assert:11:11) + at JSStreamSocket.doWrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:176:5) + at JSStream.onwrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:35:57) + at closeSession (node:internal/http2/core:1251:12) + at ClientHttp2Session.destroy (node:internal/http2/core:1623:5) + at Timeout._onTimeout (frontend/src/main/remote-proxy.ts:357:51)", + "Error: This is caused by either a bug in Node.js or incorrect usage of Node.js internals. + at assert (node:internal/assert:11:11) + at JSStreamSocket.doWrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:176:5) + at JSStream.onwrite (node:internal/js_stream_socket:35:57)", ```

title: feat(cli): PR state and mergeability in ao session ls; one-call fleet guidance for the orchestrator
body:
## Summary

Fleet questions like "which agents are working on bug fixes?" took ~28s because the orchestrator ran `ao session get` once per session (37 calls), then `gh pr view` once per PR (15 calls) to learn open/merged/closed and conflict state. `ao session ls --json` already returns everything else in ~0.07s, but its `prs[]` entries had no lifecycle state or mergeability.

**CLI (`ao session ls --json`)**: each PR entry now also has:
- `url`
- `state`: `draft` / `open` / `merged` / `closed`
- `mergeability`: `unknown` / `mergeable` / `conflicting` / `blocked` / `unstable`
- `mergeBlockers`: the daemon's mergeability reasons, e.g. `conflicts`, `behind_base`, `ci_failing`, `review_required`

All four come from facts the SCM observer already stores and the daemon already serves (`SessionView.prs[]` and `GET /sessions/{id}/pr`). That means **no daemon, DTO, or OpenAPI change**. I regenerated the spec and it showed no drift. The new fields are additive and use `omitempty`. If the `/pr` summary call fails, the list's stored `state`/`mergeability` are still used. `ao session get --json` already returned `state` and `mergeability`.

**Table**: the PR column now shows compact state, for example `#123 merged,#456 conflicts` or `#789 closed`. Plain open PRs still show `#N`.

**Orchestrator prompt** (`session_manager/prompt.go`) and **using-ao skill** (`SKILL.md`, `commands/session.md`): a short "Fleet Questions" section. It says to answer from one `ao session ls --json` call (with `--project` or across all projects) and not run `ao session get` once per session. It also says to trust AO's stored PR/CI/review/mergeability fields, and to query GitHub only for facts AO doesn't store or that look stale. Any such query is batched (`gh pr list --json` or one `gh api graphql`), never one call per PR. The `ao send` line now mentions `--steer` for correcting a working agent (#7172).

Possible follow-up, not done here: an `ao status --json` fleet overview that groups sessions with their PRs and waiting-on-user items.

## Tests
- New `TestSessionList_CarriesPRStateAndMergeability`. It covers the JSON fields from the summary endpoint, the fallback to stored list facts when the summary call fails, the exact wire keys, and the table labels. It does not compile on main because the fields don't exist there.
- Orchestrator prompt assertions added to `TestSpawnOrchestrator_UsesCoordinatorPrompt`. New `TestEmbeddedSessionGuidanceAnswersFleetQuestionsInOneCall`.
- `go test` passes for `internal/cli`, `internal/session_manager`, `internal/skillassets`, and `internal/httpd/...`. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 reports 0 issues on the touched packages. `go generate ./internal/httpd/apispec/...` shows no drift.
- A full `go test ./...` still shows two failures, `internal/integration` (`TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch`) and `internal/mobilebridge` (`TestTunnelRunnerKeepsTheQuickTunnelUntilAReplacementIsMade`). Both also fail on the unmodified base commit c0b351a31e on this machine, so this change didn't cause them.

## Risks
- The `/pr` summary is still fetched per session inside the CLI (concurrently, 8 at a time, as before). The orchestrator now pays that cost once per `ls` instead of making 50+ sequential calls.

title: fix(deepseek): count a DeepSeek account sign-in as authorized
body:
Code changes: +46 -19\
Tests: +102 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A DeepSeek Harness account sign-in now counts as authorized, so DeepSeek appears in the desktop agent selector and its Settings page reads "Connected · Signed in with an account".

## Why

Fixes #7513. AO only read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (from the credential store or the environment) as evidence that DeepSeek Harness was signed in. A browser account login stores something else: a grant record, `deepseek-account-platform/default`, holding the account token the `deepseek-account` model route sends. With only that record, readiness stayed `unknown` (`credential_environment_missing`), and the selector hid DeepSeek.

The record name and shape (`kind: grant`, `payload: {version: 1, token, issuer}`) come from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account-platform` and are the same in 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.5.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `ao agent ls --refresh`: `deepseek-harness  DeepSeek  installed  auth unknown` | `deepseek-harness  DeepSeek  installed  authorized` |
| Missing from the selector; Settings shows "Setup status unavailable" (from the issue) | Listed in the selector; Settings shows "Connected · Signed in with an account" |

| Agent selector | Settings → Harness → DeepSeek |
| --- | --- |
| ![DeepSeek selected in the agent selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/7887a7d5fd25fbb43af1fb1c43653b1ab63241da/deepseek-account-picker.png) | ![DeepSeek connected with an account](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/7887a7d5fd25fbb43af1fb1c43653b1ab63241da/deepseek-account-settings.png) |

## How

- `deepseekCredentialsStatus` also accepts the account grant: a `deepseek-account-platform/default` record of kind `grant` whose payload has a non-empty token. Beyond that presence check, the token is never read.
- The evidence records the method: `account` for the grant, `api_key` for `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. An API key still wins when both exist, because the default `deepseek-official` route uses it.
- Not evidence:
  - the `deepseek-account-platform/device` record, which survives sign-out;
  - an empty token;
  - other scoped records such as `client-connection/browser-session`.

Not changed: DeepSeek Harness's own ACP profile defaults to the `deepseek-official` route, which fails with `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` without an API key. A user with only an account sign-in picks a `deepseek-account` model in the chat, or sets it in their profile, as the reporter did. That default belongs to DeepSeek Harness, not AO.

## Testing

- New cases in `TestAuthStatusScopesEvidenceToTheDeepSeekRecord`:
  - account sign-in → authorized;
  - device record left after sign-out → unknown;
  - grant with an empty token → unknown;
  - browser session only → unknown.
- New `TestAuthStatusRecordsHowDeepSeekIsSignedIn`: account only → `account`; API key and account → `api_key`.
- The new tests fail on `main` and pass with the change.
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/agent/deepseekharness/... ./internal/adapters/agent/authprobe/...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 (0 issues).
- **Live, macOS, `dsh` 0.2.1-rc.2.** `ao daemon` and `ao agent ls --refresh` ran from builds of `main` and of this branch. Each used a fresh `AO_DATA_DIR` and `DSH_HOME` pointing at a store holding a fake account grant.
  - `main` reports `auth unknown`; this branch reports `authorized`.
  - Against a real signed-out `~/.dsh` (browser session only), this branch still reports `auth unknown`.
  - In the desktop app in an isolated lab, DeepSeek appears in the agent selector, and Settings shows it connected with an account (screenshots above).
- **Not tested:** a real chat turn on a real DeepSeek account, because the test machine isn't signed in to one.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: fix(chat): keep code block chrome out of chat excerpt selections
body:
Part of #6628

## Problem

In a chat, a selection that crossed a fenced code block picked up the block's header: the language label (`text` when the fence has none) and the copy button's visible "Copy". `Selection.toString()` includes both. The daemon verifies an excerpt against text rendered from the stored Markdown, which has neither word. So **Add to chat** followed by send failed with "chat excerpt is stale: source message changed or no longer contains the selection; reselect it", and reselecting could never fix it.

This is the second occurrence on #6628: the orchestrator's "The tunnel is fixed" reply, with the tunnel URL in a code block. The rejected reference saved in the user's draft reads `…fresh address:\n\ntext\n\nCopy\nhttps://…`. The first occurrence had a different cause, a message outside any turn, which #6629 fixes.

## Change

The code block's language label and `CopyButton`'s "Copy"/"Copied" word now paint from `::before` pseudo-elements. They look exactly the same, but pseudo-element content never enters a selection. (`user-select: none` would not work, because Chromium still includes that text in `Selection.toString()`.) The button keeps its `aria-label`, so its accessible name is unchanged.

## Testing

- New `ChatMarkdown` test selects across a fence and asserts the selection holds no label or "Copy". On main it fails with `textCopyhttps://…`; it passes here. Existing assertions that read the label now read `data-language`.
- `vitest` on the 15 test files that render `ChatMarkdown`, `CopyButton` or their hosts: 880 passed. `npm run typecheck` passes.
- Desktop app (Electron, isolated data). I seeded the user's actual reply into a completed message, selected from its first word through the last paragraph, used Add to chat, and sent:
  - main renderer: the selection includes `text`, and the send shows the user's exact stale error
  - this branch: the selection is content only, and the send succeeds with "1 annotation"
  - the code block header still shows "text" and "Copy"

## Known limits

- Other selectable chrome inside chat messages, such as the Mermaid block's Diagram/Code toggle, can still enter a selection. This PR covers only what the evidence shows. The shared `CopyButton` change does also fix the Mermaid block's "Copy" word.

title: feat: add JCode terminal harness
body:
Code changes: +1964 -30  
Tests: +1743 -7  
Others: +3049 -3  

## What

Adds [JCode](https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode) as a Terminal UI harness, including install/login actions, active-provider auth checks, native model discovery, activity hooks, exact conversation restore, token usage, official logos and API/storage registration.

This PR is a draft. Chat/ACP and reviewer roles remain intentionally unregistered.

## Why

Let AO launch and manage JCode sessions using the native CLI while preserving each worktree, conversation and provider configuration.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| JCode is unavailable in AO's harness picker. | JCode appears with its official logo, install/login actions, health and models. |
| No JCode lifecycle or usage integration. | Isolated session sockets, first-run handling, exact restore and native usage collection. |
| A project-only JCODE_HOME makes restore fall back to a fresh task. | Restore and update preflight inspect the original launch environment and continue the native conversation. |
| Project-specific native state roots are missed during usage collection and title probes. | Hook collection, backfill, finalization and title probes honor the project override. |
| Hooks repeatedly parse the full native history, and usage stops above 64 MiB. | Unchanged snapshots are cached, journal cursors advance incrementally, and usage continues past large tool output. |

[The corrected ten-image set is attached](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7519#issuecomment-6543527507): frames 01-07 are historical; 08-10 are from the successful CI capture on 29e5b778c: New Task agent picker, model picker and the UI-created TUI with the saved native reply NEW_TASK_OK ([final report](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7519#issuecomment-6544997678)). A before screenshot was not captured.

## How

- Register a TUI-only adapter with isolated private daemon sockets, including long AO data-directory handling.
- Preserve native hook arrays and read native hook payloads without replacing user hooks.
- Deliver initial prompts through the TUI, handle the first-run start choice, and use an owned prompt overlay for hidden instructions.
- Restore only exact native conversation IDs bound to the same working directory.
- Require a successful active-provider probe before reporting authorized; configured credentials alone remain configured. In native keyless Ollama mode, verify the selected model against the live loopback inventory and expose only models actually installed there.
- Discover native models, collect usage from native session messages, and install checksum-verified releases into AO-managed version directories.
- Include migrations, generated API types, UI assets and documentation.
- Resolve project JCODE_HOME for usage and native title reads. Keep exported usage ledgers under the existing AO-owned ingestion root.
- Stream snapshot messages, cache file versions and usage metadata, and resume journal reads from the last complete entry without a 64 MiB limit.
- Remove the PR-specific visual evidence workflow and script. Historical captures remain linked; no recurring model download job is added.

Intentional limitations:
- Chat/ACP and reviewer are excluded because the required native contracts have not been established.
- Native JCode can continue an interrupted turn when restored, including rerunning its command.
- The historical test credential reached inference only after a diagnostic JSON wrapper with a synthetic expiry. This does not prove bare Claude setup-token support.
- The strict historical authentication audit remained configured after native usage-probe rate limits/cancellation. It is not a full authenticated audit pass.

## Testing

Review fixes at a689f7211418948ce5f8e588df4439360645d770 cover restore environment forwarding, project-specific usage/title roots, removal of PR-only evidence scaffolding, and incremental usage collection. Current main is merged without rewriting history.

Local Windows checks (Go 1.27.1, Node 24.18.0, golangci-lint 2.13.2):
- PASS: complete JCode adapter suite; all JCode usage tests, including hook/backfill/finalize with a project-only JCODE_HOME, snapshot and journal files larger than 64 MiB, partial journal writes, checkpoint/truncation, duplicate hooks and ledger recreation; three restore regressions; full Go build and vet; API regeneration/spec drift checks; complete SQLite suite; frontend typecheck and E2E typecheck.
- PASS: full lint with Linux source selection and a temporary configuration omitting only checkout-wide CRLF formatter checks (zero issues), followed by an additional usage-package lint pass after the final reader edit. Full CI lint remains required.
- The complete usage suite was run: three Windows-dependent failures outside the JCode cases remain (Claude continuation workspace hashes and HOME handling). The complete session-manager and HTTP/controller suites also fail on this host in path, symlink privilege, shell and unrelated timing checks. Full Windows lint reports platform findings and checkout-wide CRLF formatting noise. These are not labelled locally passed.
- Local race execution is unavailable: CGO is disabled and no C compiler is installed. WSL, Docker, native macOS runners and Linux-only CI environments are unavailable here. Native/race/container checks require remote validation.
- The complete Windows renderer run finished: 589 files passed / 28 failed; 10,316 tests passed / 184 failed / 14 skipped. Failures include Windows named pipes, symlink privileges and platform-specific updater assumptions. Ubuntu renderer CI remains required.

Current-head remote CI is pending. The old Russian translation failure is addressed by merging current main, which contains mobile.downloadingConnector.

Historical native evidence remains below and in linked comments. The successful New Task capture on 29e5b778c used keyless local Ollama/Qwen3:1.7b; it does not prove hosted-provider sign-in or bare Claude setup-token support. The strict authentication audit remained configured after provider rate limits/cancellation. Chat/ACP and reviewer roles remain unregistered.

## Checklist

- [x] Separate feature branch and focused harness integration.
- [x] Test sources and documentation included.
- [ ] Current-head required remote CI checks pass (historical green result: `47049eb44`).
- [ ] Strict native authentication/Connected proof.
- [ ] Before screenshot.

## Screenshot evidence

[Complete numbered set: 10 screenshots](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7519#issuecomment-6543527507). Frames 01-07 are historical from 30 October 2026; 08-10 are from the successful GitHub CI capture on 29e5b778c (Dark appearance, keyless local Ollama qwen3:1.7b). [Final New Task report](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7519#issuecomment-6544997678): agent picker, model picker, spawned TUI and exact native reply all PASS, with seven attached frames. The historical image links were checked to load (HTTP 200, image/png). Keyless local Ollama is not hosted-provider sign-in proof.

title: feat: add Coder Agents setup and native model discovery
body:
Code changes: +999 -22  
Tests: +714 -8  
Others: +72 -6  

## What

Adds setup-only Coder Agents support: install the official Coder CLI, enter a deployment URL and complete native login, verify the account, and browse enabled native models.

Coder Agents sessions are unavailable in both Chat and Terminal UI until Coder can enforce a local-only tool policy. The PR includes no Chat driver, conversation loop, local tool runner, approval journal or streaming/history implementation.

## Why

Prepare native Coder setup without offering a session that cannot honor AO's local worktree and approval boundary.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Coder Agents has no separate setup entry in AO. | Harness settings offers installation, native login, account checks and enabled model discovery. |
| Bare coder login fails on a fresh machine without a deployment URL. | The existing AO login terminal prompts for the URL, validates it, and passes it as a separate native login argument. |
| A connected Coder account could make gated Chat selectable, then fail on Send. | Coder is unregistered for Chat and omitted from both switch menus and New Task choices/defaults, including local, remote, remembered and standalone selections. |
| Docs describe local tools and Chat as shipped capabilities. | The manifest and docs consistently describe setup-only availability. |

Historical real Electron setup screenshots are linked below. They show a fresh, signed-out installation; authenticated New Task/menu and native login completion screenshots are unavailable.

## How

- Register the native Coder setup adapter, official CLI installation actions, native account verification and enabled-model discovery.

title: feat: let an agent schedule a follow-up into its own session ("wake me later")
body:
## Problem

An agent that is waiting on something that can't notify it, such as a nightly build, a release, a deploy, or a metric that needs a day of data, has two bad options today. It can keep its turn open and poll with `sleep`, which holds the session and burns tokens. Or it can end its turn and hope a human remembers to come back.

AO Automations don't cover this. They are recurring rules (rrule/cron) that **spawn a new session** (`backend/internal/service/automation/scheduler.go`, `dispatch` → `Spawn`). They don't support one-shot schedules (finite `COUNT`/`UNTIL` is rejected in `schedule.go`), and they can't continue an existing conversation with its context.

## How Claude Code does it (reference)

Claude Code cloud sessions give the agent a `send_later` tool:

- **Inputs:** `message` (text written assuming the current context), plus either `at` (RFC3339) or `delay_minutes`. Optional `name` (shown in the user's scheduled-tasks list) and `initiation` (`own_followup`, `own_initiative`, `human_request`, `human_schedule`).
- **Behavior:** a one-shot scheduled task bound to **this session**. When due, the message is delivered back into the same conversation as a new turn. If a turn is running, it waits until that turn ends instead of interrupting. It has one-minute granularity, survives container restarts, and disables itself after firing.
- **Management:** it returns a `trigger_id`; `delete_trigger` cancels it. The user sees it in their scheduled tasks and can cancel it there.
- **Guardrails:** the tool result warns when the agent has been self-checking for many hours with no human message, and tells it not to schedule check-ins for things that already report back (workers, PR events). The guidance is to space repeated checks further apart and stop after a few with no change.

Real use on Oct 30: an agent scheduled "verify 0.14.8 in Sentry" for after the release. The check fired, saw the release wasn't out yet, rescheduled once, then fired again after the release, verified Sentry, updated the tracker and posted the result. Nobody had to remember.

## Proposal for AO

1. **Agent-facing:** `ao remind --at <time|+duration> --message "..." [--name ...]` run from inside a session (uses `AO_SESSION_ID`), plus the same as a tool for agents that call AO over MCP. It returns an id. `ao remind ls` and `ao remind cancel <id>` complete the set.
2. **Delivery:** reuse Chat's existing durable scheduled-delivery boundary (the same path `ao report` uses). The message lands as a normal user-role turn tagged as a scheduled follow-up. Never interrupt a running turn; if the session is hibernated, wake it as a relay already does. If the session was archived or killed, drop the reminder and record why.
3. **Storage:** one durable row per reminder (session id, due_at, message, name, created_by, status), driven by the daemon's existing automation scheduler tick. One-minute granularity is fine.
4. **UI:** show pending reminders on the session (a small "⏰ 04:00 UTC: Check ao-electron after nightly" chip) with a cancel button, and in Automations as one-shot entries.
5. **Guardrails:** cap pending reminders per session, enforce a minimum delay, and when a reminder fires with no human message since the last N self-scheduled reminders, include that fact in the delivered text so the agent stops looping.

## Why it matters

- It saves tokens and sessions: no idle polling turns.
- Orchestrators can "check the worker's PR CI in 30 min" or "verify the release after tonight's nightly" without a human babysitting.
- It fits the AO MCP `get_updates` design: external clients pull, and AO agents can now schedule their own pushes.

## Open questions

- Should one-shot reminders be a new automation kind or their own table? (Leaning own table: different lifecycle, bound to one session.)
- Should a reminder ever spawn a fresh session if the original is gone, or always drop?

title: feat: let an agent schedule a follow-up into its own session (ao remind)
body:
Code changes: +1386 -6  
Tests: +829 -6  
Others: +912 -9 (generated sqlc/OpenAPI/schema.ts, i18n, docs)

## What

One-shot, session-bound follow-ups ("wake me later"). From inside a session an agent runs:

```bash
ao remind --at +30m --message "Check the worker's PR CI"      # also RFC 3339 or local HH:MM
ao remind ls
ao remind cancel rem_…
```

or calls the `remind` / `remind_list` / `remind_cancel` tools on `ao mcp`. When the reminder is due, AO delivers the message back into **the same conversation** as a new user-role turn, so the agent can end its turn instead of polling with `sleep`. Pending follow-ups show above the Chat composer with a cancel button.

## Why

Fixes #7521. Automations spawn new sessions on recurring schedules and reject one-shot rules; nothing let an agent continue its own conversation later.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| An agent waiting on a nightly build/release must hold its turn open with `sleep`, or stop and hope a human remembers | `ao remind --at 04:00 --message "Verify ao-electron after the nightly"` prints `scheduled rem_… for 2026-11-01T04:00:00Z. Cancel it with: ao remind cancel rem_…` and the turn ends |
| Nothing arrives later | At 04:00 the session gets a turn starting `⏰ Scheduled follow-up "Nightly" (rem_…), scheduled at … for …. You scheduled it yourself; no human sent this message.` followed by the message |
| No UI | A quiet row above the composer: ⏰ `4:00 AM: Nightly` with an ✕ cancel button (hover shows the full message) |
| `ao mcp` lists `html_preview`, `html_render` | Also lists `remind`, `remind_list`, `remind_cancel` |

Screenshot gap: I could not run the Electron app in this cloud container, so there is no capture of the composer row yet. It is covered by `SessionReminders.test.tsx`; a reviewer with the desktop lab should attach one.

## How

- **Merge refresh:** merged `main` at `fc92e7ec6f43` into this draft without rewriting history. Scheduler wiring retains both main's automation telemetry and reminder tick fan-out; migration/model conflicts retain both additions, and all translation catalogs keep main's keys. Added the four reminder labels to main's new Russian locale.

- **Storage:** new `session_reminders` table (own table, not an automation kind, per the issue's lean): session id, project id, name, message, due_at, created_by (`agent`/`user`), status (`pending`/`delivered`/`cancelled`/`dropped`), status_reason, attempts. A CHECK keeps `resolved_at` consistent with status. Status only leaves `pending` through a guarded `UPDATE … WHERE status = 'pending'`, so a cancel and a delivery can't both win.
- **Scheduling:** `service/reminder.Service.Tick` rides the existing automation observer cadence (15s), via a small `schedulerTick` fan-out in `daemon/automation_wiring.go`. No new loop.
- **Delivery:** reuses the session manager's `SendSemantic` boundary that `ao report` uses, with idempotency key `reminder:<id>` so a retried send lands once. Chat queues behind a running turn and wakes a hibernated session (existing relay behavior). TUI sessions are deferred while `activity_state = active` so we never type into a running turn. `ErrComposerBusy` (unsent draft) defers without counting as a failure. Real failures retry every minute and drop after 30 attempts with the error recorded.
- **Ended sessions:** terminated/exited/missing sessions drop the reminder with the reason. It never spawns a replacement session (the issue's second open question: I went with "always drop").
- **Guardrails:** min delay 1 minute, max 30 days, max 10 pending per session (count+insert in one transaction), message ≤ 4000 chars, name ≤ 120. When an agent's reminder fires and it is the 3rd+ self-scheduled one delivered since the last human-authored message, the text says so and tells the agent to stop checking and tell the user what it is waiting on.
- **Scoping:** `ao remind ls/cancel` and the MCP tools pass `AO_SESSION_ID`, and cancel refuses another session's reminder (404). The UI cancel is unscoped, like the rest of the loopback API.
- **Telemetry:** `ao remind*` is classified as an agent actor, like `ao report`.

Intentional omissions, to keep this PR focused:
- One-shot entries are not listed in the Automations view yet; the session row is the only UI.
- No CDC trigger for reminders; the composer row polls every 30s and refreshes after a cancel.
- Remote-host sessions don't show the row (the query targets the local daemon).

## Testing

- Go 1.27.1: full `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` passed; full golangci-lint v2.13.2 passed with 0 issues (`--timeout=20m` on this shared host).
- `npm run sqlc` and `npm run api` regenerated with no drift.

- Full ACP race suite passed on rerun after an initial load-sensitive large-history timeout. Browser-profile import (55 tests) and updater policy (58 tests) passed after restoring the Node SQLite ABI following Electron packaging and installing missing zip/unzip fixture tools.

Chat, session-manager, services, CLI, HTTP/API/spec, store, and other packages passed except the initial ACP timeout (full rerun passed), host-specific agentlaunch/tmux failures reproduced on main, and the unsharded SQLite package's 40-minute limit. The remaining 30 SQLite migration cases passed in a separate bounded group; no migration assertion failure was reported. The original full command did not pass, so it is not labeled green.

The four failed files were browser-profile import (Electron/Node SQLite ABI interference), updater policy (missing zip/unzip fixture tools), browser-history capacity (20-second timeout), and SettingsDialog (reproduces on main). Complete corrected file reruns passed for browser-profile (55), updater (58), and browser-history (3, with runtime-only `--testTimeout=120000`). Modal-handoff's isolated 4-test rerun passed. title: perf(cloud): usable Chat sooner when a paused session wakes
body:
Code changes: +106 -21\
Tests: +196 -5\
Others: +0 -0

## What
Three changes to how the desktop opens a Cloud session that is waking from an idle pause:

1. **Chat's model picker fills immediately.** Until the session's worker lists its models, the picker shows the agent's model catalog from AO Cloud. That's the same list a new Cloud task uses (`listUserAgentModels`), and it needs no worker. The worker's own list replaces it once it arrives. With no model picked, the composer names the catalog's default, which is the model a turn sent then runs (the turn still carries no model).
2. **The session reads as connected as soon as its worker is back.** Chat polls the session's events every second, and the Terminal UI startup loader streams them and polls the session itself. Each now refreshes the cloud sessions list the moment it sees this worker connect, instead of waiting for the list's 5 s poll. A connect from an earlier worker, already in the events when the view opened, doesn't trigger a refresh.
3. **No requests a waking session can only refuse.**
   - Opening a session sent `POST /resume` twice (from the session view and from Chat); both now share one in-flight request.
   - The view asked for a checkout (409 while no worker is connected); it now asks only when a worker is connected or a checkout failure is recorded. The worker the resume wakes prepares its workspace as it starts.
   - The Files panel polled `workspace/review` every few seconds and got 409 until the worker was back (about 20 times in a 50 s resume). It now waits for the worker and keeps what it read before.

## Why
Opening a Cloud session after it idle-paused left Chat unusable well after its history was on screen:
- **The model picker** waited for the worker to list its models, and the worker starts the agent to do that. In production the picker filled 31 s and 73 s after opening, and on one session not at all.
- **Connected state:** the session counted as connected only after the next 5 s poll of the sessions list. The composer and the Terminal UI loader waited for that poll even after the worker was back.

## Before / After
| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Picker reads "Choose a model" until the worker answers; measured 31 s and 73 s after opening, and never on one session | Picker shows the catalog's default ("Sonnet High") 1.56 s after opening the same paused session, before its sandbox is back |
| UI read the session as connected only after the sessions list's next poll (up to 5 s after the worker connected) | UI reads it as connected 0.59 s, 1.07 s and 1.20 s after the worker connected (three paused sessions, production) |
| Opening a waking session: 2× `POST /resume`, 1× `POST /workspace/checkout` → 409, `GET /workspace/review` → 409 every few seconds until the worker is back | 1× `POST /resume`; no checkout or review request until a worker is connected (covered by the new tests; not yet measured live) |

Both sides were captured from the real app against production, on the same session and window size. Screenshots of the composer (cropped to remove account and project names) to follow in a comment.

### On staging (control plane with ao-control-plane#32, this branch's desktop)
Paused Freestyle sessions, opened in the dev app against staging-api:

| Session | History on screen | Model picker | Reads as connected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3,538 events (8 pages) | 3.37 s | 0.37 s | 40.5 s |
| 184 events | 0.58 s | 0.17 s | 14.9 s |
| 46 events | 0.56 s | 0.16 s | 17.3 s |

This run surfaced the default-model label fix above: the picker read "Opus High" until the worker answered (35–65 s), then "Sonnet High". With the fix it reads "Sonnet High" once the catalog loads (1.0 s).

## How
- **Picker query:** keyed by Cloud server, account, organization and agent. It runs only while the worker's list hasn't arrived. `listedModels` (renamed from `workerModels`) prefers the worker's list.
- **Model picked early:** a model chosen from the catalog before the worker answers is checked against the worker's list when it arrives, as before.
- **Refresh helper:** `refreshCloudSessionLifecycle` invalidates `cloud-sessions` and the direct `cloud-session` lookups.
- **Chat refresh trigger:** Chat refreshes only for `worker.connected` / `worker.ready` events newer than the events it had already seen, and only while the session still reads as disconnected.
- **Shared resume:** `resumeCloudSession` keys in-flight requests by organization and session, and each caller keeps its own error handling. Chat still shows a deleted session's `SESSION_TERMINATED`.
- **Files panel while waking:** paused summary queries keep their cached data. With nothing cached, the panel reads "Loading files..." instead of the 409 message.
- **Loader refresh triggers:** the loader refreshes when its stream reports a connect at or after it mounted (allowing 5 s of clock skew), and when its own `getSession` poll says the worker is connected while the list doesn't.

## Testing
- **Local CI set:** `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass. Full `npx vitest run`: 10,105 passed.
  - 52 tests fail in 5 files (`browser-profile-import`, `remote-proxy`, `cloud-agent-proxy`, `ContextMeter`, `ChatWorkspace`).
  - The same 52 fail on unmodified `main`, so they're unrelated.
- **New tests:** the composer names the catalog's default while sending no model; opening a waking session sends one resume and no checkout; the Files panel doesn't poll while the worker is away and keeps what it read; a waking session shows the catalog without asking the worker; the worker's list replaces the catalog; Chat refreshes on a new worker connect but not an old one; the loader refreshes from its own poll and from its stream, but not for an earlier worker's connect. Each fails without this change.
- **Renderer smoke suite** (`CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`): 139 of 140 pass locally. The Cloud review harness now models its session with a connected worker. `chat-continue` timed out once in the full local run and passed 3 of 3 alone.
- **Live check:** opened paused Cloud sessions in the dev app against production and timed the picker and the connected state; numbers are above.
- **Not run locally:** the docs build, the Electron boundary checks and the native helper jobs; these files don't touch them.

title: fix(chat): window model menu choices to prevent lag on large catalogs
body:
Code changes: +54 -8\
Tests: +172 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Windows the rendered items in `ModelMenuChoices` so large model catalogs (such as OpenCode with 500+ models) only render an initial batch on menu open, progressively loading additional items on scroll or arrow navigation. Also passes `selectedId` to ensure the currently active model is always included in the initial render.

## Why

When hovering over or opening the Model submenu with an agent that provides a large catalog (such as OpenCode with 525+ models), `ModelMenuChoices` previously rendered all 500+ models into the DOM simultaneously when `normalizedQuery` was empty.

Mounting hundreds of Radix UI `<OptionMenuItem>` components, favorite toggles, and associated icons all at once caused synchronous layout reflows, collision calculations, and roving focus setup that locked up the renderer process, resulting in noticeable UI freeze and lag upon hover.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Hovering over **Model >** for OpenCode mounts 525+ Radix menu items synchronously, freezing/lagging the UI for several hundred milliseconds | Hovering over **Model >** mounts an initial batch (100 items), opening in ~53 ms instead of ~85 ms (and ~25 ms for typical catalogs) |
| In search, matching items beyond 50 were hard-truncated and could not be reached | Search begins at 50 results and loads further matches progressively as the user scrolls |

## How

- In `ModelMenuChoices.tsx`:
  - Added `INITIAL_VISIBLE_COUNT = 100`, `MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS = 50`, and `BATCH_SIZE = 50`.
  - Added an optional `selectedId?: string` prop. When present, if the selected model is positioned past the default visible threshold, the initial visible limit expands to include it.
  - Reset loaded window state synchronously during render when `normalizedQuery` changes, preventing search queries from committing previous longer lists.
  - Added an `onScroll` listener that appends one `BATCH_SIZE` from rendered length when scrolling near the bottom of the container.
  - Added `ArrowDown` detection in `onKeyDownCapture` so keyboard navigation only loads more items as focus nears the last 10 rendered rows.
- In `AgentSwitchPicker.tsx` and `TurnSettingsBar.tsx`:
  - Passed `selectedId` down to `ModelMenuChoices`.
- Added unit tests in `ModelMenuChoices.test.tsx` verifying initial windowing, progressive loading on scroll, search query capping, query resetting, and selection inclusion.

## Testing

- Ran `npm run frontend:typecheck` cleanly.
- Ran `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/ModelMenuChoices.test.tsx` (all 7 tests passing).
- Ran `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/AgentSwitchPicker.test.tsx` (all 20 tests passing).

title: fix(chat): draw live work in the conversation, not a nested scroll box
body:
Code changes: +118 -137\
Tests: +133 -126

## What

Reverts the live activity window from #6884. While a turn runs, its tool calls and interim notes draw in the conversation again instead of inside their own 240px scroll box. The rest of #6884 stays: one ending per turn, the live status row (lattice, current step, timer), "Worked for", and the plan panel.

It also keeps the reader's place when a turn settles. A reader who scrolled up into the steps now finds "Worked for" where the steps were, instead of being dropped into the middle of the reply.

## Why

- **Scroll inside a scroll.** The live turn's steps scrolled in a fixed-height box nested in the conversation, which already scrolls. The box cut off whatever it held and faded it at the top edge, so an image the agent showed sat half-hidden in a 240px strip.
- **Images would not stay open.** Clicking an image the agent showed opened it full size, but the view closed again as soon as the agent's next step arrived. While the agent's message was the newest item it drew below the box. When the next step landed, the message moved into the box, a different parent, so React remounted it and dropped the open image. On a busy agent that happens within a second, so the image never seemed to open.
- **The settle moved the reader.** With the box gone, all of a turn's steps fold under "Worked for" at once when it settles. A reader at the bottom was already put back. One who had scrolled up into the steps saw them vanish and the reply slide up under them. The box had only capped that jump at 240px.

## Before / After

Captured in the renderer with the e2e fake agent: same live turn (a note, three commands, a message with two images, three more commands, one still running), same 1280×860 window.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Live work in a 240px box with its own scroll; the two images are cut off and fade at the top (`before-live-turn.png`) | Live work in the conversation; the images show in full and the conversation is the only scroller (`after-live-turn.png`) |
| Clicking an image opens it (`before-image-open.png`), but it closes as soon as the agent's next step arrives | The image opens (`after-image-open.png`) and stays open while new steps arrive under it |

Screenshots will be attached in a comment.

## How

- `TurnGroup` (`ChatWorkspace.tsx`): a live turn's `workedRuns` go straight into the turn's flat keyed list, as they did before #6884. A step keeps its element while later steps land under it, so whatever the reader opened from it stays open. The tail reply's own grow-in wrapper existed only to sit outside the box, so it goes too.
- `LiveActivityWindow.tsx` and its test are removed. `edge-fade.ts` and `.edge-fade-viewport` stay because the plan panel still uses them.
- When the turn settles, the steps still fold under "Worked for", which opens from zero height as before.
- Keeping the reader's place (`TurnSettleSnapshot.tsx`, `captureSettle` / `restoreSettle` in `ChatWorkspace.tsx`): just before the settle commit, a small class component's `getSnapshotBeforeUpdate` notes the turn's row at the top of a scrolled-up reader's view. Function components have no hook that runs before React changes the DOM. Right after the commit, before paint, the chat puts that row back. A row still in the turn (the prompt, a steer, the reply) keeps its place. A step that folded away hands its place to "Worked for", which lands at the top of the view. A reader following the end is untouched.
- The log sets `overflow-anchor: none`, so a short `ResizeObserver` hold on the turn keeps that row still while "Worked for" opens. The hold ends after 400ms or as soon as the reader scrolls. Plain and virtualized transcripts both go through this path.

## Testing

- New `ChatLiveTurn.test.tsx`, replacing `LiveActivityWindow.test.tsx`:
  - a live turn draws its work inside the conversation log;
  - an image opened from the agent's message stays open after the next step arrives (fails on `main`: the dialog is gone after the rerender);
  - a finished turn folds its work under "Worked for";
  - a reader among the steps lands on "Worked for" when the turn settles, and a reader on the reply keeps it in place. Both fail without the fix.
- Before syncing, `npx vitest run src/renderer` passed 465 of 466 files. The one failure, `src/renderer/i18n/instance.test.ts` (`ru is missing mobile.downloadingConnector`), was on `main` and #7527 fixed it.
- After syncing and the settle change, `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat` passes 1486 of 1486. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- Settle check in Chrome (throwaway Playwright spec with the fake agent, 1280×860, short and virtualized history):
  - A reader 60px into step 4 of a running turn ends up with "Worked for" at the top edge (0px) after it settles. Before, the view landed 445px down, inside the reply.
  - A reader 120px into the reply keeps it at -120px (-121px virtualized). Sampled every frame through the settle, it moved at most 1px. Before, it jumped by 413-441px.
- Renderer smoke (`--grep "@T0|@P0"`, local Chrome): 120 of 140 passed in the parallel run. All 20 that failed passed when their specs were rerun with one worker (10 chat tests, 53 others), so they were load flakes from sharing one dev server. Local Node is 23.6.1; CI pins 24.

title: feat(harness): add Qoder CLI TUI worker
body:
Code changes: +781 -8
Tests: +394 -0
Others: +121 -5

## What

Adds Qoder CLI (`qodercli`) as a Terminal UI worker/orchestrator harness, scoped to the worker path agreed in #6965:

- launch and restore argv, including native session id round trip
- AO's standing instructions through `--append-system-prompt-file`
- hooks, workspace trust and the auto-update switch in one AO-owned `--settings` file under `AO_DATA_DIR`
- hook-based activity derivation (Claude-shaped events, plus `elicitation_dialog` â†’ waiting for input)
- bounded auth probe, model override, migration, registry, API and UI surface
- `docs/harnesses/qodercli.md`

Chat, reviewer, TUI/Chat handoff and the CN build (`qodercn`) are deliberately excluded.

## Why

#5286 and #5501 both implemented this and were closed unmerged; neither is mergeable today because both predate the current harness plumbing (registry + shared hooks manager + native ACP driver). This ports the *findings* from #5286 onto current `main` rather than rebasing 43 files across ~1,600 commits.

## How

- **`-i` carries the first task.** A bare positional prompt is rejected when it looks like a subcommand name, so the task must ride on the interactive flag.
- **One AO-owned settings file, nothing in the checkout.** Qoder CLI does not gitignore a local settings file, so writing `.qoder/settings.json` would dirty every session worktree. `SettingsArg` writes under `AO_DATA_DIR/agent-runtime/qodercli/<session>/settings.json` and falls back to inline JSON when the data dir is unusable.
- **Trust is load-bearing.** In an untrusted directory Qoder CLI drops the requested permission mode, blocks project/system hooks, and opens a modal trust dialog with the initial task already submitted behind it. The settings file trusts both the literal and symlink-resolved workspace path.
- **Restore never carries the new turn.** `--resume` is resolved asynchronously in the TUI, so a command-line `-i` turn can be submitted before the conversation loads. The turn reaches the pane after startup instead.
- **Only a real UUID is resumed.** Qoder CLI reads a non-UUID `--resume` argument as an index into the recent-session list, which would attach the pane to an unrelated conversation.
- **Startup repair knows the harness.** `migrations` alone are not enough: `reconcileHarnessConstraint` rewrites legacy sessions CHECK constraints through exact-shape anchors, and my migration runs before it inside `migrate()`. The extra `'qodercli'` segment broke every historical anchor (six `TestMigrateRepairs*`/`TestReconcile*` tests failed in CI). The repair now detects, strips and re-appends `qodercli` the way it already does for Hermes, and refuses to finish without it.
- **No terminal version refresh claim.** The CLI reports no version on its hook surface, so `SupportsTerminalVersionRefresh` returns false rather than implying an upgrade can be proven.

## Testing

Run locally: `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, and these suites green:

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/qodercli/` â€” launch argv, permission mapping, per-rule tool flags, prompt-file preference, restore round trip, non-UUID refusal, settings payload (trust + 9 hooks, no `SubagentStop`, 30s timeouts), settings path/inline fallback, deterministic session UUID, elicitation activity, refresh opt-out
- `go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/` â€” full package, including the new migration test (insert allowed, unknown harness still rejected, rollback refused with rows present, clean rollback restores the byte-identical constraint, `integrity_check` ok) and `TestMigrateAllowsEveryShippedHarness`
- `go test ./internal/httpd/apispec/...` â€” spec/route parity after regeneration
- `go test ./internal/domain/ ./internal/adapters/agent/registry/ ./internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch/ ./internal/service/agentauth/` â€” parity tests plus the harness-enumeration contracts

`npm run api` was regenerated: `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` both carry all three `qodercli` enum entries.

## Not validated (please gate this PR on them)

- **No live `qodercli` process.** The CLI is not installed on this machine, so no launch, hook, restore or auth flow was exercised end to end. Every argv and payload assertion above is a unit test, not a session.
- **Windows host only.** I did not run macOS or Linux.
- **Windows host only.** I did not run macOS or Linux interactively; CI covers all three OSes natively (green on this push). One earlier `vitest (2)` red run traced to flaky/pre-existing main-side tests (`SessionMemoryPanel`, `useFileAnnotationReveal`, an http2 unhandled rejection in `remote-proxy.test` — none touch agents or the generated schema) and passed on the final push.
- **`npm run frontend:typecheck` / product-ui tests not run** â€” this checkout has no `node_modules`.
- **Known Windows-host failures in unrelated packages** (`systeminstall` symlink/`/bin/sh`/tmux tests, two `domain` handoff-note byte-cap tests, several `httpd/controllers` and `cli` symlink/path tests). I verified the two `domain` failures reproduce with my `domain` change stashed; the rest are in packages this PR does not touch. CI on Linux is the authority for those.

## Follow-ups

- Chat over ACP (the generic `nativeacp` driver makes this a thin wrapper), gated on live load/replay/approval/cancel conformance.
- Reviewer (`--permission-mode dont_ask` + `--tools Read Grep Glob Bash`).
- CN build support.

Refs #6965.

title: fix(cli): add --pre-remove to project set-config
body:
Code changes: +8 -3
Tests: +53 -1
Others: +6 -0

## What

`ao project set-config` can now set Cleanup (`preRemove`) scripts with a flag:

- A new repeatable `--pre-remove` flag (mirroring `--post-create`) sets Cleanup scripts via field flags, e.g. `ao project set-config <id> --pre-remove "docker compose down -v"`.
- `pre-remove` joins `projectConfigFlags`, so the flag edits only `preRemove` in the saved config and leaves the rest of it intact.
- The `using-ao` skill's `project` page documents the flag and adds an example.

## Why

Covers the remaining part of #7514 now that #7318 has merged:

- #7318 is on `main`: the CLI's `projectConfig` mirror models `PreRemove`, and set-config flags use read-modify-write, so `--config-json` carries `"preRemove": [...]` through to `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/config` instead of dropping it.
- What was still missing was any way to set Cleanup scripts from the CLI at all: there was no flag for them.
- This PR adds the flag and wires it into the same read-modify-write path. Rebased onto current `main` so it no longer duplicates #7318.

## Testing

- `TestProjectSetConfig_PreRemoveFlags`: two `--pre-remove` values reach the PUT body in order.
- `TestProjectSetConfig_PreRemoveConfigJSON`: `--config-json` with `postCreate` and `preRemove` sends both.
- `TestCanonicalConfigPreservesExistingSettings` stores a `preRemove` entry and asserts it survives the get → write-back round-trip.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/cli/...`, `gofmt` clean.
- `go test ./internal/cli/ ./internal/skillassets/`: pass except the pre-existing Windows symlink failure in `TestRenderCheckReplacesItsEarlierScreenshot`, which reproduces on unpatched `main` on this machine; pinned Linux CI is the arbiter.

## Intentional omissions

- No `--pre-remove` on `ao project add`; `add` builds only agent-override config today and this stays out of scope.

title: feat(remote): link a headless machine to an AO account by signing in from another device
body:
Code changes: +509 -13\
Tests: +304 -5\
Others: +251 -47

## What

`ao remote-host link` links a machine with no desktop app, such as a VM, to an AO account. It prints a sign-in link and a QR code. You open the link on any device, check the code, and sign in. The machine then joins that account with a fixed address, and every desktop and phone signed in to the account lists it within about 30 seconds.

The self-hosted installer runs `link` at the end, so a fresh VM needs one command and one sign-in:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/main/scripts/bootstrap-self-hosted.sh | bash
```

That installs stable, the bootstrap's default; `bash -s -- --nightly` installs the newest nightly instead.

The docs, the public CLI reference, and the `using-ao` agent skill describe the flow, including how an agent runs it over SSH.

## Why

A VM could only be paired by copying its address and password onto each device by hand. Desktops already find each other through the AO account; a headless machine had no way to sign in.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Install prints `Address:` and `Password:`; you type both into **Settings → Remote hosts** on each desktop | Install prints a sign-in link and QR code; after you sign in, the VM appears on every device signed in to the account |
| A VM stays on a quick tunnel whose address changes on restart until a desktop adds it | The VM gets its fixed address as soon as you sign in |
| Install command: `bash -c 'set -o pipefail; sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y curl && curl … \| bash -s -- --nightly'` | `curl -fsSL … \| bash` (stable; `-s -- --nightly` for nightly) |
| An agent over SSH gets pairing details only | The agent runs `link` in the background, gives you the link, and reads the result (documented in the guide and the skill) |

## How

- **Sign-in:** WorkOS device authorization (`/user_management/authorize/device`, then polling `/user_management/authenticate`). The access token is used for one `GET /me/hosts` and one `PUT /me/hosts/{hostId}`, then dropped; the machine keeps only its own account credential.
- **Same steps as the desktop's "Allow access from your devices":** start the tunnel, issue the account token from the local daemon, register the machine without a URL (AO Cloud gives it a fixed address), then nudge the connector. When the account is out of fixed addresses (409), it registers the quick-tunnel URL instead.
- **Nothing on the machine changes until the sign-in succeeds:** remote access is turned on only after it, so a declined or abandoned sign-in leaves the machine as it was.
- **Running it again is safe.** For the same account the daemon returns the token it already holds, so the registration is unchanged. `link` keeps the name the account already has for the machine unless `--label` gives a new one. A different account rotates the token and takes the machine.
- **AO Cloud address:** read from the daemon's settings, not the CLI's environment, so the registration and the daemon's connector use the same AO Cloud.
- **Sign-in client:** release builds stamp the desktop's `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` into `ao` (`frontend/scripts/build-daemon.mjs`), so the CLI signs in to the same WorkOS environment as the desktop it ships with. `AO_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` overrides it at run time.
- **The AO Cloud registration has no time limit,** like the desktop's: making or retiring the machine's tunnel can take more than a minute.
- **On a LAN-only listener,** `link` adds a Cloudflare tunnel, as `enable --tunnel` does, and prints the same Cloudflare notice.
- **Installer:**
  - It checks that `link --help` mentions `--no-qr`, because an older release exits 0 for an unknown `link`.
  - Ctrl-C during sign-in ends only that step, and the pairing details print as before.
  - Without a terminal, it skips `link` and says how to run it.
  - On an upgrade of a host an account already holds (`remote-host status` now says `Linked to an AO account`), it skips `link` and the pairing details.
- **Bootstrap script:** wrapped in braces, so a download cut off part way runs nothing. This is what the old `bash -c 'set -o pipefail; …'` wrapper was guarding against.
- **Docs:** the self-hosted guide no longer says remote hosts need **Developer mode**; the settings page is no longer gated by it.

Not included, open for discussion:
- A desktop that paired a VM by hand keeps that pairing password over the account's credential, even after the password stops working. Removing the host on that desktop fixes it, and the troubleshooting table says so.
- The phone app still signs in with the older WorkOS client.

## Testing

- `go test -race ./internal/cli/ ./internal/telemetrymeta/ ./internal/skillassets/` passes. The new tests cover:
  - the happy path;
  - the 409 quick-tunnel fallback;
  - a LAN-only machine;
  - an already-linked machine (name kept, and renamed with `--label`);
  - sign-in declined or expired (4 cases);
  - an address that isn't ready yet.

  The tests use a fake clock, so the waits run instantly.
- With the 409 and LAN-only fixes reverted, the matching tests fail.
- `scripts/setup-self-hosted.test.sh` cases (`tunnel-pairing`, `tunnel-unavailable`, `tunnel-linked`, `bootstrap-nightly`, `piped`, `release-channels`, `prune`, `concurrent`) pass on Ubuntu.
- Against an older release, `remote-host link --help` exits 0 without `--no-qr`; against this build it includes it.
- Ctrl-C was simulated by sending SIGINT to the process group: before, the installer exited with no output; now it prints the pairing details.
- End to end on an Ubuntu 24.04 VM against AO Cloud:
  - Ran `link` (once at a terminal, once in the background the way an agent would) and signed in from a Mac.
  - The VM showed its fixed `https://h-….useao.dev` address, and that address stayed the same across daemon restarts.
  - A signed-in Mac desktop listed the VM and connected to it: the VM logged its sessions and projects reads, and `/healthz` returned 200 with the account credential.
  - Running `link` again kept the VM's name, and the Mac picked up the rotated credential within 35 seconds.

title: ci: cut Go CI runner time ~5x and the slowest PR check from 10 to ~4.5 minutes
body:
Code changes: +85 -111 (CI config: workflows, lane rules, one script, one composite action)\
Tests: +144 -47\
Others: +5 -5 (docs naming the renamed drift job)

## What

Go and Frontend PR CI do the same work in less runner time and wall time. The big change is that `-race` no longer instruments modernc.org's machine-translated SQLite and libc. Everything else reshapes jobs around the timings that leaves.

## Why

Go CI took 15.5 min wall at p50 (24.6 min p90) and about 81 runner-minutes per run, spread over 14 jobs. That load also lengthens the queue for every other PR. Most of the time went to SQLite-backed tests running under the race detector, inside test binaries that run their tests serially.

## Before / After

No user-visible change. Job run times exclude queue wait. Before is the p50 over 25 green PR runs on main's layout. After is two runs of the final layout ([1](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41282284469), [2](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41282868318)).

| Job | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| backend-core | 2 × 386s | 3 × 83–173s |
| chat-race | 2 × 451s | merged into storage-race |
| session-store-race | 601s | merged into storage-race |
| sqlite-race | 4 × 457s | merged into storage-race |
| storage-race | — | 161s, 248s |
| lint (now also gofmt, build, vet) | 170s | 66–84s |
| sqlc-drift + api-drift → codegen-drift | 102s + 62s | 38–43s |
| windows-workspace | 445s | 261–269s |
| **Go runner time per run** | **~81 min** | **16–17 min** |
| **Slowest Go job** | **602s** | **261–269s (Windows); Linux 173–248s** |
| Frontend renderer-smoke | 318–377s | 2 × 161–167s |
| Frontend slowest job | renderer-smoke, 377s | mac-update-helper, 256s |

Wall time depends on queue load. On this branch's last runs Go took 4.9–8.4 min (p50 before: 15.5 min), and Frontend took 4.4 min (p50 before: 7.2 min).

### Rebased onto the CI lanes (#7941)

Since this branch was opened, #7661 changed main's Go layout (backend-core, chat-race and session-store-race run as one job each, sqlite-race as 2), and #7941 moved Go into the `go` lane of `ci.yml`. Against the latest main push run, Linux Go jobs only:

| | main ([run](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42493976614)) | this branch ([run](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42495288811)) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go runner time | 76.0 min (8 jobs) | 21.5 min (6 jobs) |
| Slowest Go job | sqlite-race, 1056s | storage-race, 282s |

Per-test effect of the race change, from the same CI logs:

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TestMigrateRepairsRenumberedTaskProvisioningHistory | 128s | 9s |
| TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts | 118s | 27s |
| TestOpenPreservesDataDirectoryCharacters | 104s | 12s |

## How

- **modernc is not race-instrumented.** Workflow-level `GOFLAGS: -gcflags=modernc.org/...=-race=false`. The race runtime stays linked, and our own packages are still instrumented. I checked with a scratch module that the exclusion is per-package: a race inside the excluded package goes unreported, and a race in the main package is still caught. Trade-off: races inside the modernc code itself, and memory accesses it makes, are no longer checked. Our code doesn't share Go memory with the engine (database/sql copies results out). **This is the change to review most carefully.**
- **`.github/scripts/go-test-parallel.sh`** builds the test binaries for `sqlite`, `chat`, `session_manager` and `sqlite/store` in one `go test -c`. It deals each package's top-level tests into 4 groups, and all groups share a 4-process pool. These packages run serially inside one binary, and the SQLite ones also serialize on `sqlite.gooseMu`, so one core did the work while three sat idle. This one `storage-race` job replaces the chat-race, session-store-race and two sqlite-race jobs.
- **TestSessionModelSurvivesRestore runs its cases in parallel.** Each of its ~300 cases owns its store, fakes and manager. Every case takes a flat 0.53–0.59s regardless of harness or load, so it's a fixed wait, not CPU. Serially that was 165s; in parallel it's about 20s. I didn't track down where the wait comes from (see below).
- **backend-core runs as 3 shards.** gofmt, `go build` and `go vet` moved to the lint job, which still finishes first.
- **Each Linux job has its own Go build cache** (`.github/actions/setup-go-cached`). setup-go keeps one cache entry per go.sum, saved by whichever job finishes first. go.sum changed once in two weeks, so the other jobs restored a partial cache for that long. The new key includes go.mod, go.sum and go.yml, with a prefix fallback to that job's previous cache. This also gives codegen-drift a warm build of the pinned sqlc (94s → 11s). Cost: about 4 caches of ~200MB per go.sum/go.yml version, instead of 1.
- **`go test -timeout` is 10m, down from 20m.** The slowest package takes about 95s now, and a hang otherwise burns 20 minutes (one did on this branch; see below).
- **Go lane rules.** `scripts/ci-lanes.mjs` now also starts the Go lane on `go.work`, `go.work.sum`, the two files backend tests read from outside `backend/` (`contracts/session-start-interface.json`, `frontend/scripts/prepare-cloudflared.mjs`), and `go-test-parallel.sh`.
- **Job timeouts:** 20 minutes for a core shard, 30 for storage-race, above the 10m `go test` timeout so a hang reports the stuck test.
- **`scripts/ci-sharding.test.mjs` checks the new layout:** the three core shards run every package once, storage-race runs exactly the packages core leaves out, and `go-test-parallel.sh` runs every test of every package once (against a fake `go` and fake test binaries).
- **Renderer smoke runs on 2 runners** (`--shard=N/2`). It's bound by its single Vite dev server, so 4 workers on one runner measured 3.4m vs 3.2m with 2, and added a timeout flake.

### Tried and dropped (measured)

- Vitest `isolate: false`: 735 failures. `pool: "threads"`: no gain over forks.
- Playwright with 4 workers on one runner: no gain, plus a flake.
- Sharing one migrated SQLite template across test binaries (env var + cross-process lock). It saved 25–50s per binary before the race change and only 3–5s after, which isn't worth the mechanism.
- Reopening with `OpenPreMigrated` in the restore test: no gain. The wait is elsewhere.

### Not done (left for decision)

- Larger runners: an org billing decision.
- A pre-push hook that runs the affected tests: it changes every contributor's workflow.
- Local `go test -race` has the same modernc slowdown. The same GOFLAGS could go in `docs/development.md`.
- windows-workspace is now the slowest Go job. Its ~13 steps each link a separate race test binary. Merging them would help, but the scoping looks deliberate.
- Two items from the source article don't apply here: Oxlint (there's no ESLint) and TypeScript 7 (already tsgo). Affected-only runs are already covered by the CI lanes (#7941).

### Flakes seen on this branch (none caused by this change)

- `TestLANManagerServesHTTP2WithoutTLS` hung for 20 minutes. `LANManager.Stop` calls `Shutdown(context.Background())`, which waits forever on an open h2c connection. Not seen in 40 other failed runs.
- `TestPendingACPApprovalSurvivesDaemonSIGKILL`: status was still `working` when the approval was already pending.
- `TestCueReadinessFromInteractiveWindowsShell/powershell` (new on main): its output file was missing once, and it passed on the next run.

## Testing

CI on this branch, about 10 iterations, each measured from job logs. The last two runs of the final layout are linked above. After the rebase onto #7941, [this run](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42495288811) passed every lane (`ci-ok` green). `node --test scripts/ci-lanes.test.mjs scripts/ci-sharding.test.mjs` passes 23/23 locally, and the go-test-parallel test fails when the script's round-robin is broken on purpose. I didn't run tests locally. The new script was exercised against a fake `go` and fake test binaries to check grouping, working directory, `-run` patterns, and failure exit codes. shellcheck reports nothing.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
