title: feat(chat): move a usage-limited Chat session to another account and retry once
body:
Refs #7385

## Summary
When a Claude Code or Codex Chat turn is refused for a usage limit, an opt-in setting moves the session to another signed-in account of the same harness that has verified room, then retries the refused prompt once.

- **Setting:** "Move to another account at a usage limit" in the agent accounts panel. One daemon-owned switch for Claude Code and Codex, shown in both harness tabs; off by default (`PATCH /settings/account-handoff`).
- **Choosing an account:** fresh native limit readings (Claude `get_usage`, Codex `account/rateLimits/read`), counting only the meters the conversation's model uses: Claude's 5-hour/weekly plus the Opus/Sonnet/model meter; Codex's overall bucket plus a model bucket. When the conversation has no explicit model (a provider default), every meter counts. A bucket Codex reports as reached counts as full. The account with the most room in those meters wins, however little: a 95%-used account is still picked when it is the only one with room.
- **Move:** the existing Session Manager account transition (drain policy), so it commits or rolls back. If the session's account changes while the limits are read, the handoff stops.
- **Retry once:** a scheduler tick claims the refused turn in an in-memory map, so it is handled once per daemon run. The retry goes through the existing retry path, which rechecks lineage under the send lock, so a person's own retry or newer message withdraws it. Lineage (`retry_of_turn_id`) and history are kept.
- **Thread note:** `account.limit_handoff` names the destination account after a successful move. Once the retry is attempted, a second line says "Prompt sent again." or "Prompt not sent again. Resend it if needed." It never promises a retry that might not happen.
- **Stay on this account:** per-session pin in the session account summary (`PUT /agents/accounts/sessions/{id}/stay`; 404 for an unknown session).
- **No candidate, pinned, or failed move:** the session keeps its account, and auto-resume at reset is armed when the reset is known; unknown reset leaves recovery to the user. A cancelled move does nothing else.
- **No ping-pong:** a refused retry stays put. An account at its limit reads full, so it is never picked back.

There is deliberately no durable handoff record. A manual switch needs none because the person resends the prompt; this keeps the automatic version close to that.

## Demo
Desktop app against a lab daemon with a fake Codex provider: work@example.com refuses for a usage limit, personal@example.com answers. The setting is turned on, the prompt is refused, Orchestrator moves the Chat to personal@example.com, notes it in the thread, and retries the prompt once.

![Account handoff demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/ao/agent-orchestrator-1-326/pr-7534-evidence/account-handoff.gif)

The recording predates the shorter note: its second line shows the earlier wording.

[Full-resolution MP4](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/ao/agent-orchestrator-1-326/pr-7534-evidence/account-handoff.mp4)

## Tests
- Chat service under `-race`: handoff on both providers with one retry under 8 concurrent ticks and the note recording it; no candidate (known and unknown reset); failed and cancelled moves; pin; setting off; old failures; ping-pong; turning the setting off during selection; superseding prompt (note says the prompt was not sent again); session leaving the target; pending retry across hibernation and a failed wake; restart leaving the prompt alone.
- Domain bucket selection, `HandoffTarget` picker (a 95%-used account is picked when it is the only one with room; a 100%-used one never), Stay on an unknown session, migration ledger, API spec drift.
- Frontend: setting switch, Stay switch, thread note for each retry outcome, no recovery offered once Orchestrator retried.
- Real daemon with a fake Codex provider, over HTTP: refused prompt moved from `device-codex` to `personal-codex` with one retry and one note; a pinned session stayed and armed auto-resume; a refusal from before a daemon restart got no move and no retry.

## Risks and follow-ups
- A daemon restart between the refusal and the retry drops the handoff. The session stays on whichever account it reached, the prompt is not retried, and the thread note may be missing; the person resends it.
- Two daemons on one database are not supported by this guard.
- Turning the setting off does not stop a move already underway.
- No test drives the handoff through the full daemon wiring; that was checked by hand on the lab daemon above.
- No dedicated docs, CLI flag, or mobile UI.

title: fix: preserve mixed chat excerpts without UI control text
body:
Code changes: +1066 -305  
Tests: +1942 -7  
Others: +62 -0 (generated API contracts)

## What

Preserve one annotation containing ordered prose, code, commands and plain-text output from a completed chat turn. Exclude UI controls by DOM identity, validate every source in the daemon, and deliver the reference to main chat, an existing side chat or a new side chat.

## Why

Mixed command/reply selections previously had no usable attachment action. This also addresses Ronish's review: copy-only selections no longer raise sticky alerts, creation uses main's merged #7560 recovery flow, and the daemon no longer duplicates browser JSON or terminal formatting. Related to #6628.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Selecting a command, plain-text output and reply cannot attach the whole range. | One annotation preserves source order and provenance; Ctrl/Cmd+L forwards all segments once. |
| Unsupported copy selections raise a persistent red alert. | Disabled attachment actions explain the restriction in the active locale; collapse or a changed selection clears the toolbar. |
| Two mixed selections with identical text can collide in side-chat deduplication/recovery. | Segment-aware identities distinguish sources, order and revisions; nested references are cloned for drafts and receipts. |
| Side creation opens the inspector before a usable destination exists. | The inspector opens after eligible activation; clearing a pending selection saves its annotation without opening an empty inspector or stealing focus. |
| Go copies renderer serialization/terminal rendering and rewrites activity details. | Only verifiable plain-text command fields are attachable; raw activity details retain key representation and 64-bit integer precision. |
| The HTTP/2 LAN test can leave its client connection open while waiting indefinitely for listener shutdown; CI timed out after 40 minutes. | The test closes idle client connections before shutdown and bounds requests; HTTP/2 and authentication assertions remain intact. |

Paired before/after PNGs below use base main and the updated native Electron renderer with matching synthetic bridge/API fixtures and window dimensions. Media stays outside Git; all images are uploaded GitHub attachments.

## How

- Rebased onto upstream main `f7907457e`, including merged #7560 and main's ACP readiness correction. Preserved the shared Button/Pressable components, newer translations and side-chat naming. Retained its creation receipts, lost-response recovery and draft merging; extended identities, request serialization and cloning for ordered segments.
- Added typed unsupported-selection reasons and localized disabled-toolbar explanations across all nine renderer catalogs. Explicit attachment failures remain retryable. Restored the reference-limit translation and retained the eight-annotation, 24 KiB and 32-segment limits.

- Removed Go JSON/ANSI/caret formatting replicas and the side-snapshot detail rewrite. Validate plain-text fields using nonempty whitespace-normalized containment while preserving source ownership/revision/completed-turn checks. Structured output and control-character transformations are intentionally unsupported, including through direct daemon requests.
- Preserved legacy wire representation and hashing, propagated provenance through drafts/echoes/navigation, separated excerpt/navigation DOM markers, added layout-neutral wrappers, moved ChatWorkspace file docs before imports, formatted E2E tests, and aligned unavailable segmented anchors with legacy errors.

No database migration or new endpoint. The optional ordered-segment API remains compatible with legacy message references. This PR deliberately does not support attaching rendered Mermaid labels, structured JSON output or transformed terminal fields; users can select Mermaid Code view or supported text instead.

Current head `647294884` is rebased onto upstream main `f7907457e`. The latest completed CI failure on the old head was `backend-core (0)`: `TestLANManagerServesHTTP2WithoutTLS` waited in `LANManager.Stop` / `http.Server.Shutdown` for 40 minutes. These use mocked bridge/API responses; SQLite/fake-provider Go workflow tests cover daemon delivery separately. Matching base captures pass 2/2.

title: fix(mobile): Android sign-in Unmatched Route and production WorkOS client
body: Code changes: +131 -14\ Tests: +108 -10\ Others: +0 -0 ## What On Android, signing in to Orchestrator Cloud from Settings succeeds but leaves an **Unmatched Route** screen showing `aomobile://callback?code=…&state=…` on top of the app. Tapping "Go back" reveals the signed-in account. This adds an Expo Router `+native-intent` that keeps the sign-in redirect out of navigation. It also switches mobile to the production WorkOS client. Mobile was still on the old default client, so sign-in went to `studious-horse-78-staging.authkit.app` instead of `auth.orchestrator.inc`, where the desktop signs in. ## Why The sign-in returns through `https://api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return` to `ao-app://callback`. On iOS, `ASWebAuthenticationSession` captures that URL privately. On Android, the Custom Tab hands it to `MainActivity` as an ordinary `VIEW` intent (both `ao-app` and `aomobile` resolve there), so two listeners receive it: 1. `expo-web-browser`'s `openAuthSessionAsync` (`lib/account.ts`), which completes the sign-in, and 2. Expo Router, which navigates to `/callback`, a route that doesn't exist. Router prints the URL with the first scheme, hence `aomobile://` in the screen. **WorkOS client.** `lib/account.ts` hardcoded `client_01KZ3VRKC374HS91XGRDPT3671`, the default baked into the desktop and CLI source. Desktop release builds override it with the `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` repository variable (`client_01KZ3VRKTDKBZ3JA8AMKTF6W2X`, set 2026-10-07), and the CLI gets the same value at build time. Mobile never picked that up. The control plane still accepts the old environment's tokens as legacy, so sign-in worked. But a user who exists only in the production environment would get a different account on mobile and not see their desktop's machines. Mobile sign-in would also break once legacy tokens are no longer accepted. | Client | WorkOS authorize redirects to | | --- | --- | | `client_01KZ3VRKC374HS91XGRDPT3671` (mobile before) | `studious-horse-78-staging.authkit.app` | | `client_01KZ3VRKTDKBZ3JA8AMKTF6W2X` (desktop release, mobile after) | `auth.orchestrator.inc` | ## Before / After Android emulator (API 35, debug build). `ao-app://callback` was delivered while the AuthKit Custom Tab was open, with a fake `code`/`state`, so the "could not be verified" alert is expected in both runs. It shows the sign-in code still receives the callback. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Router also opens the link: Unmatched Route behind the alert | Settings stays put; only the sign-in code handles the callback | App killed during sign-in, then cold-started by the callback: it opens on home. ## How - `lib/auth-callback-intent.ts` exports `redirectSystemPath`. It matches only `ao-app://callback` / `aomobile://callback`, and leaves every other path unchanged. - **Warm link:** returns `null`, so Router ignores it. `openAuthSessionAsync` listens on `Linking` itself and still gets the URL. - **Cold start** (the OS reclaimed the app mid sign-in): returns `/`. The pending sign-in promise is gone by then, so opening the app normally is the best outcome. - `app/+native-intent.ts` only re-exports it, because a test file under `app/` would become a route. - `RouteErrorBoundary.test.ts` lists every file under `app/` as a route. It now skips `+native-intent`, which expo-router does not treat as a route; the test's own comment already named it. - `lib/account.ts` now uses `client_01KZ3VRKTDKBZ3JA8AMKTF6W2X`. That client already allows the `https://api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return` redirect, which the desktop release also uses. The token exchange is unchanged: public client, PKCE, no secret, the same as the desktop's `authenticateWithCode`. `account.test.ts` now asserts the client ID in both the authorize URL and the token request. - **Existing sessions:** WorkOS user IDs are per environment, so anyone signed in today gets a new user ID from the production client. - Each session now stores the client ID that issued it. A session from another client, including every existing one, is retired when read, with no WorkOS call. The phone shows signed out, and the old user ID and email are kept as the previous account. - At the next sign-in with the same email, account sync (`adoptPreviousAccount`) runs before the stale-ID cleanup. It retags machines the listing still contains in place, keeping their phone-local name, icon and endpoints, so no unpair is queued. It also moves the hidden-machine set to the new ID. - A different email adopts nothing. - JS only, with no native or config change, so both fixes ship over the air. ## Testing - `npm test` in `packages/mobile` (2765 tests) and `npm run typecheck`. - New unit tests cover the warm callback, cold callback and unrelated links. - Account migration tests: machines tagged with the old ID and still listed keep their name and icon with no unpair, the hidden set moves to the new ID, and a different email adopts nothing. These fail without the adoption step. - Session tests: an old-client session is retired without a network call, and its account is recorded when a new sign-in replaces it. - Emulator: reproduced the bug with the file removed, then verified the warm-callback and cold-start cases with it. See Before / After. - Pixel 10a and iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 27.2): release builds with the callback fix installed side by side. A real Orchestrator Cloud login completed on both with no Unmatched Route, so iOS is unaffected. These device runs predate the client switch. - Upgrade on the Pixel 10a: installed a build with the old client, signed in, renamed a machine and forgot another, then installed this PR's build over it, keeping the app's data. The old session was retired, so the app showed signed out. Sign-in went through `auth.orchestrator.inc`, the renamed machine kept its name and icon, the forgotten one stayed hidden, and nothing was duplicated. The renamed machine was a manual pairing, so relabelling account machines was covered only by unit tests. - WorkOS client: requested the authorize URL for both client IDs with mobile's redirect URI (table above). The production client accepts the redirect and lands on `auth.orchestrator.inc`. - Production client on devices: rebuilt both side-by-side apps from this branch. On the Pixel 10a and iPhone 17 Pro Max, sign-in opened `auth.orchestrator.inc`, and a real login landed back on Settings signed in, with no Unmatched Route. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(cloud): bring Cloud chat and sessions to parity with local
body:
Code changes: +3067 -345\
Tests: +647 -54\
Others: +1282 -92 (generated cloud-client `schema.ts`, translations)

## What

Brings Cloud sessions to parity with local ones in the desktop app, makes Cloud chat stream smoothly, and fixes a tab-strip contrast glitch.

**Streaming**
- Cloud chat reads new events from the session's event stream (`GET …/sessions/{id}/events`, resumed after the newest event it holds) instead of polling `chat-events` once a second. Events are batched once per frame; the poll stays as a 10 s safety net, or 1 s while the stream is down.
- The text reveal now paces itself to how far apart bursts arrive (140–700 ms settle, adaptive), and a finished reply's short remainder plays out quickly instead of snapping in.

**Cloud chat matches local chat**
- Agent and model picker with the agent's mark (the unified `AgentModelPicker`, offering only the session's own agent).
- Plan checklist, context meter, changed-files card, command exit codes, subagent nesting, "stopped" on interrupted steps, and file-vs-command wording on approvals, all read from new worker events (shapes in the control-plane PR).
- Quoting a selection and file captures: inlined for the agent the way the local daemon does it, and recorded as content blocks so the transcript shows the typed message with chips. Against an older control plane the message falls back to text only.
- `@` file mentions (searching the Cloud workspace), file tabs and the new-shell button in the tab strip, suggested prompts, reviewer chat, and palette chat hits scrolling to the message.

**Cloud sessions and projects**
- Rename (context menu, sidebar double-click/F2, tab, chat header) and per-user pins.
- Full-page new chat for Cloud projects, with the approval-mode control; model picking applies the Settings → Models filter, the last-used model and the Opus default.
- Inspector: activity-timeline commits, linked PRs with the external-repository check, artifact editing, version history, "Show in Finder" (copied under `~/.ao/cloud-artifacts/<session>`), and copy for any UTF-8 file up to 256 KiB.
- Command palette: file-content search and chat search over Cloud sessions.
- Terminal: the agent-ended screen for Cloud sessions, with restart.
- Project settings: Environment, Cues, Issue intake, the workers-request-review toggle, editable agents with the required-agents check, and the local default-reviewer mapping.

**Glitch fix:** inactive tab names in the session tab strip used passive text, which disappears over the translucent window; they now use muted text.

Contract (`contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`) and `@aoagents/cloud-client` gain the matching additive routes and fields.

## Why

Cloud chat polled once a second while its reveal was tuned for ~150 ms updates, so replies arrived in bursts with pauses between them. Many local features were missing for Cloud sessions and projects. AO is GUI-first, and Cloud should feel the same as local.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud chat fetched `chat-events` every second for as long as it was open | Production control-plane logs for a Cloud session opened in this build: 5 `chat-events` fetches in the first 5 s, then none, with the session's event stream open for the full ~75 s visit |
| A reply's text revealed in ~0.4 s, then sat still for ~0.6 s until the next poll | The reveal is spread over most of the gap between bursts (unit-tested), and the end plays out instead of snapping |
| Cloud composer: plain model menu, no agent mark | Agent mark plus model, the same picker as local chat |
| Cloud chat has no file tabs or new-shell button | An opened file and new shells appear as tabs beside the chat |
| Rename and pin hidden for Cloud sessions | Rename and pin work for Cloud sessions |
| Inactive tab label invisible over a translucent window | Readable (muted contrast) |

Dev-desktop screenshots of the After states will be attached in a comment.

## How

- `CloudSessionChatSurface`: the event stream (`useCloudChatEventStream`), `mergeCloudEvents` (a union by sequence, so the poll and the stream never drop each other's events), the new snapshot fields, and the annotation and `@`-file wiring.
- `ChatTimelineItems.useSmoothStreamingText`: adaptive settle time from an EMA of burst gaps (each gap capped at 1.5 s, so a tool-call pause doesn't slow the next reply), plus a finishing drain capped at 2,000 characters.
- `ChatComposer`, with text delivery, now also passes the captures and the typed text, so the surface can record them for display. The agent text is unchanged.
- `useSessionRename` reads the query client from context, so a tab rendered outside a query provider still works.
- All Cloud API use is additive. New routes return 404 against an older control plane, and the desktop hides the feature or falls back.

## Testing

- `npx tsgo --noEmit` (frontend): clean.
- Full frontend vitest suite: every failure also fails on `main` on this machine:
  - `browser-profile-import`: the native module is built for Electron.
  - `remote-proxy` / `cloud-agent-proxy`: websocket timeouts.
  - `ContextMeter` and one `ChatWorkspace` test: the en-IN locale formats 258,400 as `2,58,400`.
- `packages/cloud-client`: generate, typecheck and its 31 tests pass. `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- Dev desktop against the production control plane:
  - The Cloud event stream stays open, and polling stops after the first page.
  - The agent mark shows in the Cloud composer.
  - The Cloud shell tab and file tab open from Cloud chat.
  - The inactive tab label is readable.
  - A full streamed reply could not be measured live: the test accounts were out of Claude quota and the local Codex model was unavailable.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [ ] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable (combined on purpose: one PR per repo for the Cloud parity work)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (to be attached in a comment)
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: fix(chat): clear the expired-login banner once the login works again
body:
## Summary

A Claude Code (or Codex) chat whose provider refused its login shows "Your Claude Code login has expired. Log in again to keep using this chat." That notice cleared only when a **later turn completed**. Signing in again, through AO or with the CLI outside it, changed nothing on screen. A turn sent after the sign-in kept the banner for its whole run. On the reporting machine, the banner stayed through a 19-minute turn that was working the whole time.

## Cause

`ReconcileConversationAuthentication` is the only path that clears a conversation's credential demand. It needs a completed turn that started after the demand. No login path updates the conversation, and the account catalog's readings (the Harness page, the session summary) never reach it.

## Fix

- **Account readings confirm the login.** When `agentaccounts` reads an account and finds it signed in, and its limits come back from the provider under that login, it reports the account and the time the reading began (`SetLoginConfirmed`). Those limits are an authenticated API call, so this is provider evidence, not a liveness guess. `claude auth status` alone is not enough, because it only reads local credentials.
- **The daemon clears matching chats.** It lists session conversations with a pending demand (`SelectConversationsAwaitingLogin`) and resolves each session's account with `SessionAccountID`. On a match it calls `ConfirmConversationLogin`, which clears only a demand recorded before the reading began. A newer refusal keeps its banner. The existing `account_json` CDC trigger refreshes an open chat.
- **A turn after a refusal rechecks the account.** When a root turn starts while a demand is pending, the controller calls a separate `RecheckAccount` hook, which the daemon wires to `RecheckSessionAccount`. The banner then clears within seconds of the agent starting work, not when the turn ends. The hook does not go through `onAccountChanged`, because that path is for refusals and also runs `InvalidateCodexAccountAuthentication`, which marks the active Codex account and Codex readiness stale for every session.

The timeline row "The provider needs you to sign in again" stays as history.

## End-to-end evidence

This used the real dev desktop app built from this branch, with isolated lab data and a real Claude Code chat (Haiku 5.5) on this machine's Claude login. Both daemons ran the same scenario:

1. The chat records a credential demand. The lab writes the `account_json` AO stores when Claude answers "Not logged in · Please run /login", because a working login cannot be made to fail on cue. The banner appears ([still](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7e1a129ab49f9377526e7df3ea34bbb15f6b5987/after-banner-shown.png)).
2. The login works again, as after a CLI sign-in outside AO. The user sends a message that keeps the agent busy for about 40 s.

| | main `b691ffc74b` | this PR `52e3a0fb3e` |
|---|---|---|
| Banner once the turn starts | stays for the whole 46.6 s turn | gone 2.2 s into a 45.8 s turn |
| 15 s into the turn | ![main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7e1a129ab49f9377526e7df3ea34bbb15f6b5987/before-mid-turn.png) | ![this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/7e1a129ab49f9377526e7df3ea34bbb15f6b5987/after-mid-turn.png) |

Videos, 49 s each with the wait at 2× speed: [main](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7e1a129ab49f9377526e7df3ea34bbb15f6b5987/before-main.mp4) · [this PR](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/7e1a129ab49f9377526e7df3ea34bbb15f6b5987/after-pr7544.mp4)

### Codex: the turn-start recheck leaves Codex readiness alone

This used a real daemon with isolated AO data and a real Codex chat on this machine's Codex login. Codex readiness (`GET /api/v1/agents/readiness`) and the chat's `account_json` were sampled every 250 ms, and the Codex account stream (`/agents/codex/accounts/events`) was recorded. The lab records a refused-login demand, then sends a message that runs a 30 s shell loop.

| | PR head before this change `422ff9d434` | this PR `aba9489f8d` |
|---|---|---|
| Codex readiness once the turn starts | stale 0.26 s in, and for the rest of the turn (175 of 176 samples) | fresh the whole time (0 of 200 samples) |
| Codex account stream | 5 of 6 events mark the active account stale | 0 of 3 |
| Banner | cleared 5.26 s into a 41.8 s turn | cleared 4.71 s into a 48.0 s turn |
| Turn with no pending demand | readiness stays fresh | readiness stays fresh |

Readiness then stays stale until something checks it again. On the old build, the next launch-purpose Codex readiness check took 2.62 s to re-probe sign-in; the same check takes 0.01 s once readiness is fresh.

[Timeline](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/18787955546bcab221c4b2cee2cc05682272f8d2/codex-readiness/timeline.txt) · raw samples: [before](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/18787955546bcab221c4b2cee2cc05682272f8d2/codex-readiness/before-demand-long.json), [after](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/18787955546bcab221c4b2cee2cc05682272f8d2/codex-readiness/after-demand-long.json) · [lab script](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/18787955546bcab221c4b2cee2cc05682272f8d2/codex-readiness/lab.py)

## Tests

- `store`: `TestConfirmedLoginClearsOnlyAnOlderDemand` checks that readings that began before or at the demand leave it, a later one clears it, and the failure history and plan survive.
- `agentaccounts`: `TestAReadingThatReachesTheProviderConfirmsTheLogin` checks that signed-out and failed checks do not confirm, and that a CLI login made outside AO does, with the reading's start time.
- `chat`: `TestATurnAfterARefusedLoginReadsTheAccountAgain` checks that a turn after a refusal calls `RecheckAccount` and not `OnAccountChanged`, and that a turn with no demand calls neither.
- Locally: `go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages, and the full `agentaccounts`, `store`, `chat` and `daemon` suites pass.
- Headless A/B against the real Claude CLI login, using a lab daemon holding a copy of the stuck conversation. After `GET /api/v1/agents/accounts?refresh=true`, main stays `required` and this branch moves to `authenticated` and emits `session_updated`.

## Risks

- A turn that starts while a demand is pending now runs one account check in the background: `claude auth status` plus a limits read, or the Codex equivalent. It does not touch agent readiness.
- `SelectConversationsAwaitingLogin` scans `conversations.account_json` after each confirmed reading. Readings are cached for 5 minutes per account.

title: [Bug]: Orchestrator can't resume: SelectConversationTurns exceeds 30s on large forked conversations (missing turn_id index)
body:
### What went wrong?

## Summary
On v0.14.8 (macOS arm64), a long-lived Chat orchestrator can't be resumed. `ao session resume-agent` fails at almost exactly 30s, every attempt, with "The agent controller stopped" in the UI. The error names the browser capability verifier, but the time is spent in `SelectConversationTurns`.

## Error
    reconcile <session>: relaunch failed and commit state became uncertain: restore <session>: resume chat: chat driver unavailable: persistent ACP host: prepare chat controller environment: persist browser capability verifier: update browser capability verifier for <session>: context deadline exceeded
    get session <session>: context deadline exceeded (CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE)

## Root cause
The resume path calls `service/chat.(*Service).Start` -> `branchUnanswered` -> `LoadConversationSnapshot` -> `SelectConversationTurns`. All 553 stacks sampled on that path during a failed resume were in this query.

On forked conversations, the lineage `EXISTS` runs per turn. It filters on `turn_id`, `conversation_id` and `sequence`, but no index covers `turn_id`, so SQLite range-scans `(conversation_id, sequence)` for each turn, roughly turns x messages. #6846 added the `conversation_id` bound, which helps smaller histories, but large ones still exceed the deadline. The deadline then surfaces on the next unrelated DB call.

## Reproduction data
Conversation: 16,856 turns, 39,907 messages, 45,690 activities, 15 branches (14 forks).

Timings use the exact 0.14.8 query on an APFS clone of the DB, with the sqlite3 CLI 3.51:

| Indexes | Time |
|---|---|
| Existing | > 150s (stopped at cap) |
| Added `(turn_id)` | > 100s (stopped at cap; planner ignored it) |
| Added `(turn_id, conversation_id, sequence)` | 0.14s |

## Workaround
Applied to the live DB, after which resume succeeded:

    CREATE INDEX local_idx_conversation_messages_turn_lineage
      ON conversation_messages(turn_id, conversation_id, sequence);
    CREATE INDEX local_idx_conversation_activities_turn_lineage
      ON conversation_activities(turn_id, conversation_id, sequence);

They took 6s to build on a 20 GB DB. One attempt straight after indexing returned SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE at 30s; the next succeeded, cause unknown.

## Suggested fixes
1. Add these indexes in a migration.
2. Don't load the full snapshot inside the 30s resume deadline; `branchUnanswered` shouldn't need the entire history.
3. Report the operation that used the deadline, not the next call to fail.
4. Don't show a session as `working` when it has no chat host.

## Related: startup VACUUM blocks the daemon with no feedback
On first start after upgrading, `20261028124744441_telemetry_incremental_vacuum.sql` (#5178) took about 18 minutes on a 20.8 GB DB:
- The app showed an empty window, and `ao status` reported `stopped` while the migration ran.
- Nothing was logged, so it looked like a hang. Killing the daemon appears to discard the work and restarted it.
- Disk use peaked at about 40 GB extra, close to twice the DB size. A low-disk machine could fail here.

Suggest moving it to a background task, or at least showing migration state in the app and `ao status`, with a free-space check first.

## Environment
AO 0.14.8, macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5), arm64, Claude Code harness.
ao.db 20.6 GB; `conversation_provider_events` 8.6M rows, about 11.7 GB of payload.

title: fix(windows): apply env prefixes to supervised agents
body:
Code changes: +76 -43  
Tests: +198 -46  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Handle AO launch argv in the form `env NAME=VALUE ... command` when `agent-process supervise` starts an agent on Windows.

The change moves the existing ConPTY env-prefix parser into `internal/agentlaunch`, reuses it from the Windows supervised-process path, and adds a Windows integration regression test plus focused edge-case coverage.

## Why

Windows does not provide a Unix `env` executable. The supervised-process path currently passes `argv[0]` directly to `exec.CommandContext`, so an adapter-generated env prefix fails before the actual agent starts:

```text
ao: start managed agent: exec: "env": executable file not found in %PATH%
```

Fixes #7546

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A supervised Windows launch beginning with `env NAME=VALUE` fails with `exec: "env": executable file not found in %PATH%`. | AO applies the assignments to the child environment and starts the real executable. |

## How

- Share the existing `env NAME=VALUE ... command` split logic between ConPTY and supervised process launch.
- Translate the prefix in `agent-process supervise` only on Windows; Linux and macOS retain direct `env` execution.
- Append launch assignments after the inherited environment. Go's Windows env de-duplication makes later values override inherited values case-insensitively.
- Return fixed errors for empty or assignment-only argv without printing assignment values.

The parser intentionally does not emulate general `env` flags such as `-i` or `-u`; AO's generated launch argv uses assignment prefixes only.

The currently unwired `AO_LAUNCH_SPEC` foreground path remains unchanged; it should use the shared helper if that path becomes active.

## Testing

Passed on Windows with Go 1.27.3:


title: [Feature]: Chat rollback should also restore the worktree files
body:
### Problem

In a Chat session, "Roll back to here" makes the agent forget the turn and everything after it. The files in the worktree stay exactly as they were, and the confirmation dialog says so.

So undo only covers half of a bad turn. Example: I ask a worker to refactor the auth module. It edits 14 files and breaks the build. I roll back to the turn before. The agent no longer remembers the refactor, but the 14 edited files are still on disk, and the next turn starts from code the agent doesn't know it wrote. I have to clean the worktree by hand with git, or kill the session and start over.

This affects anyone who uses Chat sessions. It costs more with many parallel workers, because every bad turn needs its own manual cleanup.

Current behavior on `main` (`a7d8bcfca`):

- `backend/internal/ports/chat.go`: `ChatRollbacker` "discards history back to a turn, provider-side".
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspaceRollback.test.tsx` asserts that the dialog tells the user the files are "left exactly as they are".

### Proposed direction

Snapshot the worktree after each settled Chat turn, and let rollback restore the files and the conversation together.

t3code (`pingdotgg/t3code`) already does this. After every turn it saves a git checkpoint as a hidden ref, so the user's branch gets no extra commits. Reverting a turn restores the files and rolls the provider conversation back together. If the provider can't roll back its conversation, t3code refuses before it touches any file. See `apps/server/src/checkpointing/CheckpointStore.ts` and the "Turn completion and checkpoints" section of `docs/internals/overview.md`.

A rough shape for AO:

1. When a Chat turn settles, snapshot the worktree, including uncommitted and untracked (not ignored) files, into a hidden ref such as `refs/ao/snapshots/<session>/<turn>`. Leave the branch, index and stash alone.
2. "Roll back to here" first checks that the provider can roll back. Then it restores the files to that turn's snapshot and calls `ChatRollbacker`. If either step fails, nothing changes and the dialog says why.
3. Before the user confirms, the dialog lists the files that will change.
4. Snapshot refs are deleted when the session ends.

Open questions:

- Turns that committed or pushed. Restoring files is easy, but moving the branch back rewrites history. One option is to refuse rollback past a push. Another is to restore files only and leave commits alone.
- Edits the user made in the same worktree after that turn would be lost. AO's rules say never force-delete dirty worktrees, so this needs a clear warning or a refusal.
- The refs live in the repo's `.git`, not under `~/.ao`. Worktree git objects already live there, but this should be checked against the "all AO state under `~/.ao`" rule.
- AO already uses "checkpoint" for native chat history (`native_checkpoint.go`). A different word, such as "file snapshot", would avoid confusion.
- Start with Chat. TUI sessions could follow for harnesses whose hooks report when a turn ends.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep the current behavior and let users clean up with git. It works, but it's manual, and you have to know which files the turn changed.
- Ask the agent to undo its own changes. It's unreliable, and it costs a turn.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix: make Sentry failures diagnosable without leaking context
body:
Code changes: +256 -58  
Tests: +276 -32  
Others: +29 -9

## What

Audit daemon, Electron main, renderer, mobile, and CLI Sentry paths. Preserve useful error identity while keeping request text, local paths, credentials, and account details out of outbound events.

## Why

Several reportable failures reached Sentry as broad server or renderer errors. The sender also treated a controller frame as a Go throw stack. Renderer frame sanitization could collapse distinct sites, and typed daemon 503 responses could become reportable renderer issues.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /sessions/{sessionId}/conversation/messages` could return `INTERNAL_ERROR` for an unclassified delivery failure. | It returns `CHAT_DELIVERY_FAILED` with the same HTTP status and envelope shape. The wrapped cause remains available to local diagnostics. |
| A daemon issue could read `HTTP server error` with a controller frame presented as a throw stack. | It has a fixed title such as `Database operation failed (sqlite)` or a stable code, a route template and bounded cause type, and no invented stack for an ordinary Go error. Recovered panics still retain their interrupted frame. |
| A renderer event could read `Renderer error` with an unknown code and no asset location. | A synthetic `TypeError` in the real `ChatWorkspace` function reads `Renderer TypeError in ChatWorkspace (render_crash)` and retains `assets/app-A1B2C3D4.js:42`. A minified frame in `_shell` reads `Renderer TypeError in assets/_shell:42:7 (unknown)`. Different columns on the same chunk line form separate issues. A dev frame without an asset name uses a bounded line such as `renderer:3`, so distinct sites do not merge. Local paths and arbitrary function names are removed. |
| No user-visible change to renderer handler registration. | Source inspection confirms the existing app boundary already binds handlers independently of PostHog. Synthetic transport tests verify Electron main checks the durable Share error events policy. |
| Every consented desktop error could be sent. | Regular Electron main and renderer errors are sampled at 25% once at the main sender. Unhandled renderer window errors and rejections are nonfatal and sampled at 25%. Fatal main, child process, and React boundary crashes are retained at full rate. |

## Audit findings and fixes

| Surface | Evidence and finding | Fix or remaining gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Daemon | Source: packaged DSN handoff, policy check, release, environment and installation ID are wired. HTTP errors enter through `envelope` and `requestLogger`; safe route templates reach `sentryobs`. Generic codes and synthetic frames hid the cause. | Stable operation codes and wrapped causes for send, review, orchestrator spawn, report, and conversation read failures. Fixed type tags and titles, no invented Go error stack, and a five per minute and 200 per day cap per fingerprint. |
| Electron main | Source and synthetic transport tests: `DesktopTelemetryController` starts the offline sender only under acknowledged consent, and opt out drains and purges its queue. Release, environment, and installation ID are set. No live ingestion was tested. | Fixed vocabulary titles, code and category grouping, and validated renderer frame metadata. Unknown error text cannot become a title, tag, or frame function. Regular desktop errors have a 25% client sampling rate; fatal crashes bypass it. |
| Renderer | Source: the bridge is transport free, and `captureRendererException` reaches the main owned gate. The app boundary already binds global handlers independently of PostHog. | Only validated app relative asset names, fixed function names, standard exception types, and bounded lines and columns reach main. Typed daemon 503 envelopes remain breadcrumbs; untyped 503 failures remain reportable. Existing expected 409 probe skips remain unchanged. |
| Mobile | Source and synthetic tests: consent, paired installation ID, release and environment, fetch transport guard, and no persisted failed send are wired. Native capture remains disabled. | No mobile code change. A native prebuild and a built binary are required to verify mobile delivery. EAS automatic source map upload remains disabled. |
| CLI | Source: the CLI consumes daemon API envelopes and has no separate Sentry sender. | No CLI code change. New codes retain the existing envelope fields and status mapping. |

| SEN ID and sanitized issue | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| SEN-8, daemon grouping | Route template, stable code or fixed cause type, and honest stack representation. |
| SEN-9, affected installation identity | Verified existing installation ID assignment in daemon and desktop source and synthetic tests. |
| SEN-10, expected noise | Keep canceled requests and typed daemon 503 envelopes quiet; preserve existing expected 409 probe skips and narrow desktop noise matching. Untyped 503s remain visible. |
| SEN-15, quota pressure | Bound daemon event volume locally and sample regular Electron errors at 25%. Fatal desktop crashes remain at full rate. Provider quota and spike protection still need read only verification before stable release. |
| SEN-1 and SEN-2, desktop intake | Verify existing renderer handler binding and the consent owned Electron sender through source inspection and synthetic tests. |
| SEN-3, mobile delivery | Verified source and synthetic privacy tests; native prebuild and live ingestion remain unproven. |

## How

The event boundary accepts fixed codes and types only. Renderer frames retain an app relative hashed asset filename, line, and column, while unapproved function names become a fixed placeholder. Fingerprints use a bounded chunk, line, and column for minified renderer frames, or numeric line and column for minified main frames. Dev renderer frames without a packaged asset name use bounded line and column numbers when available. Error strings, local paths, URLs, stack context, and account fields do not enter the final event. Go error causes are wrapped for local diagnosis and classified by type; ordinary Go errors are not assigned synthetic throw stacks. The daemon cap is in process and resets after restart. Electron main applies the shared 25% rate once in `beforeSend` to ordinary errors, including forwarded renderer errors. The SDK rate stays at 100% because it samples after `beforeSend` and would otherwise drop fatal crashes.

## Testing

Passed locally: `go test ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/observe/sentryobs ./internal/telemetrymeta`; `go build ./...`; `go vet ./...`; frontend typecheck and 78 focused Sentry, consent, and observability tests; mobile typecheck and 56 focused consent and Sentry tests; `git diff --check`.

Attempted full suites: `go test ./...` failed in unrelated command setup, tmux, CLI, and session manager tests under this AO session environment. The full frontend suite encountered an Electron binary download failure and network bound test timeouts, then was stopped. These are local validation gaps. The pinned local golangci-lint could not typecheck with installed Go 1.27.3 because of an export data version mismatch; CI uses Go 1.27.1. Its two reported lint findings were corrected in this PR. Review follow-up: Go build and vet, affected Go suites, frontend typecheck, and 98 focused desktop tests passed. A later dev frame regression test also passed with frontend typecheck and 42 focused tests. Sampling follow-up: frontend typecheck and 43 focused tests passed, followed by 22 main sender tests after the final assertion. The full suite was not rerun for this change, as requested. Column follow-up: frontend typecheck and 25 focused main and renderer Sentry tests passed, including two failures on one minified line and invalid column rejection. Sampling policy clarification: frontend typecheck and 26 focused tests passed; the added test confirms unhandled renderer errors are nonfatal and React boundary crashes are fatal. A local Vite production bundle build passed. The build produced 619 JavaScript assets; all 619 match the bounded asset filename rule, including `_shell` and dotted route chunks. No production event, account setting change, release upload, native prebuild, or live Sentry ingestion was used as a test. Source inspection and synthetic test proof do not establish live ingestion or provider quota health. Existing Sentry issues will regroup once when the new daemon code or cause type fingerprints take effect. PostHog fingerprints are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` at `a7d8bcfcaaf6898a232ebfeaab2c208923e20e37`
- [x] One Sentry audit PR
- [x] Before / After and focused tests included

title: fix: stabilize five desktop recovery paths
body:
Code changes: +383 -91\
Tests: +544 -14\
Others: +191 -9

## What

Bundle five recovery fixes for missing workspaces, automatic update checks, state conflicts, task setup, and link previews.

## Why

These paths could keep requesting a known missing resource, repeat failed background work, send calls during an unavailable state, or leave a user without a safe next step.

## Impact (last 7 days, PostHog)

| Reported baseline |
| --- |
| Files/manifest/history polling a deleted workspace: 1,233 installs (41% of 3,005 active) |
| Auto-update failing repeatedly: 912 installs, 40k events |
| Link preview 502 retries: 542 installs |
| Resume 409: 369 · Skills 409: 309 · Diffs 409: 305 · Prompt-suggestion 409: 363 |
| Spawn setup failures: stale model ~83, stale effort ~57, default branch unresolved ~81, agent not installed ~57, branch checked out elsewhere ~39, no agent picked ~9 |
| Total: ~1,750 distinct installs (58% of weekly active) |

These are user supplied baseline figures, not independently verified counts or measured improvements after release.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Files continued requesting a confirmed missing project folder. | The Files pane explains the missing workspace and stops that session's polling. Retry is available immediately; the bounded cache expires after one minute for later user or event driven reads. |
| Failed automatic update checks returned to the normal cadence and could repeat a failing operation. | Consecutive failures use exponential delays from the base interval, capped at four hours; a completed successful operation restores the normal cadence. |
| Controller catalogs could load during resume, and a refused resume lacked a clear recovery path. | Catalogs wait for a ready controller; typed resume conflicts show actionable messages and refresh session state. Stale diff snapshots refresh their manifest. |
| A task could lack a ready default agent, keep a stale model or effort, or fail on a branch conflict without recovery. | The composer selects a ready agent, preserves typed refusals, offers a reviewed agent default after stale saved tuning, guides installation or base branch setup, and requires confirmation of a new branch name. Existing local or remote names are rejected before spawn and at workspace creation. |
| Repeated hovers retried the same failing link preview. | A failed URL falls back to its plain link and is cached negatively for two minutes, with a bounded per URL cache. |

UI screenshots were not captured in an isolated desktop lab. The changed states are covered by component tests.

## How

| Item | Actual fix | Expected metric drop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Exact `PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING` plus HTTP 404 detection is scoped by session and host, with an explicit recovery epoch and a bounded one minute cache. | Repeated missing workspace 404s per affected session. |
| 2 | One automatic check queue retains its existing watchdog, cancellation, and manual paths while failures back off from the base interval. | Repeated automatic updater failure events during an outage. |
| 3 | Controller readiness gates catalog and prompt suggestion reads, 409 suggestion responses remain retryable after recovery, resume errors use typed causes, and stale diff conflicts refresh the manifest once per version. | Wrong state 409 requests from stale client state. |
| 4 | Existing readiness policy picks only an installed authenticated supported default; rejected saved tuning requires a reviewed retry. The daemon and workspace adapter reject existing explicit branch names. Automatic default branch resolution still requires authoritative metadata or project configuration. | Setup and spawn validation failures for the covered cases. |
| 5 | Only HTTP 502 preview responses enter a two minute, 256 URL negative cache. | Repeated preview 502 requests for the same URL. |

The daemon remains authoritative for validation and idempotency. No automatic installation, permission change, agent retry, branch takeover, or update installation is added. These are expected directions, not measured post release results.

## Testing

Passed locally on this branch:

- Backend build, Git default resolver tests, and complete `internal/service/project` and `internal/httpd/controllers` package suites after CI test corrections.
- Git workspace adapter suite before the final child collision test; targeted local, remote, and child branch collision tests passed after it.
- Session delegation and API error mapping tests passed, including explicit branch conflicts.
- Frontend typecheck; 692 focused composer, New Chat, SessionView, workspace cache, updater, and locale tests after merging latest main.
- Product UI typecheck and test suite.

Local gaps: the full session service suite is blocked by an unrelated macOS `xcrun_db` file appearing in a test that expects an empty temporary directory. The default sandbox denies loopback listeners; the complete controller package passed with test scoped access. The full frontend run encountered unrelated listener dependent tests and was stopped after those failures. Earlier renderer smoke testing passed 139 of 140 tests; the remaining New Task focus failure did not reproduce in the focused model shortcut test. Desktop screenshots were not captured in an isolated lab. API regeneration after the merge produced no drift. Remote CI must be verified on the final pushed head.

title: feat(desktop): ask Local or Cloud before listing project sources
body:
Code changes: +167 -79\
Tests: +151 -80\
Others: +155 -91 (locale catalogs, DESIGN.md)

## What

When Cloud is enabled, the New project modal now asks where agents should work before it lists any sources. It opens on two tiles, **On this computer** and **Cloud**. The local sources (Clone a repo, Open a local folder, Open a workspace, Start a standalone agent) come after the first tile, as a 2×2 grid of the same tiles. Without Cloud, or with a remote machine selected, the modal opens straight on that grid.

The PR also rewrites the modal copy in all nine locales and renames "AO Cloud" to "Cloud" in this flow.

## Why

The modal put "Clone to the cloud" in the same list as "Open a local folder" and "Clone a repo". That mixed two separate decisions, where agents run and where the code comes from, into one list. `DESIGN.md` asks this flow to "present one decision at a time".

## Before / After

Captured from the desktop app on the same window size and scratch data. Before is `main`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before, Cloud on: one list with Clone to the cloud above the local sources](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/1e725406060add6388a072fecc81f092/raw/before-cloud-on.png) | ![After, Cloud on: step one asks where agents should work, with On this computer and Cloud tiles](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/1e725406060add6388a072fecc81f092/raw/after-cloud-step1-v3.png) |
| Cloud on, after picking a local source: no separate step | ![After, Cloud on, On this computer: back arrow, How do you want to start?, and a 2×2 grid of sources](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/1e725406060add6388a072fecc81f092/raw/after-cloud-step2-v6.png) |
| ![Before, Cloud off: four tall rows under Add a project](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/1e725406060add6388a072fecc81f092/raw/before-cloud-off.png) | ![After, Cloud off: New project, How do you want to start?, and the 2×2 grid](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/1e725406060add6388a072fecc81f092/raw/after-cloud-off-v6.png) |
| Back from a local sub-step (for example Clone a repo) returned to the source list | Still returns to the source grid, not the Local/Cloud tiles |
| On a fresh launch the picker could show the local list, then switch once settings loaded | Waits for the cloud gate (up to 500ms) and shows the right step first |
| With remote machines connected, they were picked from a Machine select above the list | The local tile reads **On your machines** ("This computer or a connected machine"), and the Machine select sits above the grid behind it |

## How

- **Who owns the choice:** `ImportSourcePicker` renders the tiles when `cloudEnabled && !hostId && !localChosen`. `localChosen` lives in `CreateProjectFlow`, so it survives the clone and folder sub-dialogs. It resets when the modal opens, is dismissed, or finishes a cloud create. The Cloud card never opens while a remote host is selected.
- **One tile for both steps:** a single `tile()` renders the Local/Cloud tiles and the source grid. Each tile has a borderless `bg-interactive-hover` fill that steps up to `bg-interactive-active` on hover, a bare 24px muted icon aligned with the title, and a `text-wrap: pretty` description. Hover is instant and there's no press scale.
- **Motion:** the steps cross-fade in place (`AnimatePresence mode="popLayout"`, opacity, 120ms). The body measures itself with a `ResizeObserver` and springs to the new height (250ms, `bounce: 0`). Reduced motion makes both instant.
  - The outgoing step gets `pointer-events: none`, so a quick double-click can't land on the next step.
  - The tile containers use padding, not margin, because popLayout's absolute positioning would apply the margin twice.
- **Focus:** when the step changes, focus moves to the new step's first control, so keyboard users aren't dropped to the top of the dialog.
- **Cloud gate:** `useCloudGate` now exposes `loading`. The picker renders no step until the gate settles, and stops waiting after 500ms because the settings query retries while the daemon boots.
- **Copy:**
  - The source labels (Clone a repo, and so on) are unchanged because `HomePage` shares them. Their descriptions now say why you'd pick each: "Start from any GitHub or Git repo", "Pick up a project you already have here", "Work across several repos at once", "Explore or prototype without a project".
  - The subtitle is "How do you want to start?" because one tile is an agent with no code. With a remote host it's "How do you want to start on {{label}}?".
  - `remote.addProjectOn` and `remote.projectPathHint` have no catalog entries, so their inline fallbacks changed.
  - New keys: `createProject.placementQuestion`, `placementLocal`, `placementLocalDesc`, `placementMachines`, `placementMachinesDesc`, `placementCloud`, `placementCloudDesc`, `backToPlacement`. The unused `createProject.kindCloudHint` is removed.
- **DESIGN.md:** the Add Project rule now describes this tile-based flow, and the decisions log records it.
- **Intentional omission:** the home page's "Clone to the cloud" card is unchanged.

## Testing

- **Manual:** checked in the desktop lab app (scratch `AO_DATA_DIR`, Cloud toggled in Settings):
  - both steps, Back in both directions, and backing out of Clone a repo
  - the cross-fade and height change
  - opening the modal right after a reload, which no longer flashes the local list
- **Automated:** the tests are updated for the new step and copy. New tests cover:
  - the Local/Cloud step
  - waiting for the cloud gate
  - focus moving between steps
  - the "On your machines" label
- **Not run locally:** an earlier version passed the `CreateProjectFlow`, `Sidebar` and i18n suites (274 tests) locally. The later changes were not re-run locally, at the author's request, so this PR relies on CI.

title: feat(desktop): share cloud session artifacts from the Share button
body:
Stacked on #7479. Adds Share to cloud sessions' artifacts and to the cloud artifact preview. It opens the same popover as a local file.

**Flow**
- **Inspect:** the main process finds the file in `GET /orgs/{org}/sessions/{session}/artifacts`. It scans the first 32 MiB for credentials, read through the session's short-lived file access link.
- **Publish:** calls the new `POST /orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}/artifacts/share`, with the `sha256` the popover showed (the inspection's fingerprint, as for local files in #7479). If the session committed another version since, the control plane refuses and the popover shows the file again (`status: "changed"`). The control plane copies the committed version inside its bucket, so nothing is uploaded from the desktop.
- **Same rules as local files:**
  - 3 active links on the free plan; no limit for a paid organization.
  - Videos refused.
  - Sharing the same file again keeps its link.
  - Unpublish deletes the link's copy only.
- **Records:** links are remembered per organization, session and path, so Share on a published cloud file opens straight to its link.
- **Guests:** a guest of a shared project (`cloud.shared`) gets no Share.

**Contract (additive):** `shareSessionArtifact`, with input `SessionArtifactShareInput { path, sha256, shareId? }`, returns `ArtifactSharePublishResult`. `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated.

**Control plane:** OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane, stacked on #22.

**Popover:** cloud files use the same popover as local ones (#7479's new layout). The server copies the file in one request with no progress events, so while it copies the row shows a disabled "Publishing…" with "0% uploaded" at the left. It's usually under a second.

**Tests**
- `cloud-share-ipc.test.ts`: cloud inspect (range read and scan), publish (no upload, record key, `shareId`), and refusals (limit, source changed, video, signed out, malformed org).
- `SessionArtifactsView` and `ArtifactsView`: Share is shown for cloud files and hidden for shared-project guests.
- `tsgo --noEmit` passes.

Others: +0 -0

## What

Reconcile an in-process macOS staged update with ShipIt's remaining plist and extracted bundle. If those files disappear, AO clears the stale staged offer, disables install on quit, and starts a fresh automatic check. Renderer tests preserve the restart recovery action for a stalled stage.

## Why

Issue 6911 showed a staged record surviving after ShipIt's cache and extracted bundle were deleted. The installed main process remained alive, so its in-memory native readiness could also outlive those files. This change addresses that confirmed stale-state failure. The original point where the install click stalled remains unconfirmed.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A deleted native stage can leave Restart to update visible and let the install path trust old in-memory readiness. | At the next periodic check or install attempt, AO discards the lost stage, removes the restart action, and checks for another update. |
| A retained install promise can intercept later clicks before the missing-file check. | The install preflight and periodic check release a pending install, clear retained restart state, and start fresh discovery. |
| A Finder-renamed running app makes its valid extracted bundle look missing. | The probe accepts an extracted `.app` with `Contents/Info.plist` under `update.*`, so staging remains ready. |

No screenshots are attached because this task does not authorize launching a real AO app. The UI behavior is covered by renderer tests using the same status shape.

## How

The native ready event remains the source of readiness. Squirrel.Mac prepares the extracted bundle and writes ShipItState.plist before it reports the update ready ([SQRLUpdater source](https://github.com/Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac/blob/main/Squirrel/SQRLUpdater.m)), so AO checks both files immediately after native readiness. Native readiness requires both files; a stalled stage retains its restart recovery action until AO discards it. The extracted bundle name comes from the downloaded zip, so the probe does not assume it matches the running app name. The periodic probe runs before queue admission and the in-flight check guard, allowing a later timer tick to release a blocked install. Synthetic ShipIt directory tests cover a Finder-renamed installation, missing files, a pending helper handshake, a queued automatic check, and file loss after a quit request leaves the main process alive. The check does not parse the plist, validate bundle signatures, cancel an existing ShipIt process, or claim to solve the original uninstrumented click stall.

## Testing

- Sidebar and Updates settings Vitest after the renderer correction: 176 tests passed. Updater Vitest after the main merge: 242 tests passed. The earlier three-file updater and renderer run passed 411 tests before this follow-up.
- The PDF preview test mock was missing the PDF.js text layer methods used during cleanup. CI exposed the timing. The mock now implements them and the test explicitly unmounts after both pages render. The merged main introduced a PeopleField blur timer that survived unmount; this PR clears it and tests that cleanup.
- CI Vitest shard 2/2 passed locally on the new main merge: 329 files, 5,646 tests passed, 3 skipped, with two workers and no unhandled error. The focused PeopleField and share dialog tests passed: 35 tests.
- Renderer smoke: 140 tests passed locally on an earlier head. The `@P0 live update flow` test passed on the preceding PR head. On the rebased head, CI passed 152 of 153 smoke tests; the model scroll test intermittently selected from a menu with two search fields. Its locators now target the Model submenu and move the pointer into its search field before keyboard selection. The focused test passed five repeats with installed Chromium. The CI headless browser binary was unavailable locally.
- Frontend TypeScript and end to end TypeScript checks passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The full frontend Vitest suite could not complete in this sandbox. An unrelated `remotes-main.test.ts` test failed alone because binding `127.0.0.1` returned `EPERM`. The full run was stopped after those timeouts. CI must verify the complete suite and macOS jobs.
- No installed AO app, real AO state, ShipIt process, or updater cache was used or changed.

title: fix(acp): allow nested workspace directories without extra scope
body:
Code changes: +39 -6  
Tests: +234 -0

## What

Fixes #5663: allow OpenCode to start workspace chats when the extra directories are already inside `cwd`.

## Why

OpenCode does not advertise ACP `additionalDirectories`. Registered child worktrees are nested beneath the workspace root, so rejecting that redundant scope prevents startup. Related earlier attempts: #5684 and #5875.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Actual OpenCode 1.19.5 rejects Start and cold Resume with nested child worktrees: `ACP agent does not support additional workspace directories`. | Both succeed; the real OpenCode read tool reads files in both children before and after cold resume. |

## How

Normalize and deduplicate first. Preserve forwarding for capable providers. For unsupported providers without an implicit-workspace binding, require directory existence and both containment checks before using cwd alone. Preserve main’s explicit `ImplicitWorkspaceDirectories` behavior for Hermes. Cover new/resume/load/fork RPCs and symlink boundaries. title: fix: recover unanswered side-chat creation requests
body:
Code changes: +181 -44  
Tests: +479 -2  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Recover unanswered side-chat creation requests without creating another destination after the parent advances. Split from #7327 as requested in review; this PR is independently based on main.

## Why

A lost creation response must retain its request identity. Each new Add click should still follow the current side chat, and deliberate New side chat actions must remain independent.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Retrying a lost creation reply after the main chat advances can create a duplicate | Retain the creation key and original payload; reuse the first destination |
| Anchor reuse forgets the requesting alias | Remember alias keys within the current daemon launch |
| Late creation completion can focus a previously active chat or overwrite queued edits | Validate ownership, merge the latest draft, and preserve the current focus |
| Closing a destination and retrying its primary /btw request | Preserve existing behavior: create a fresh destination and send with the retained client message ID |

## How

- Keep processing locks separate from unanswered receipts. Read the active side for each new activation; no automatic retry.
- Store only alias keys in the daemon map. Closed aliases fail definitively; primary keys retain the existing retry-after-close behavior.
- Share reference deduplication and the eight-reference limit between recovery and ordinary Add.
- Scope receipts to the mounted session surface and aliases to the daemon launch. No API, database, recovery-export or saved-draft format changes.
