title: fix(scm): hide worker-reported PRs tracked under a renamed repository
body: ## Summary The session inspector showed some PRs twice: once as the tracked PR card, and again as a "Reported by worker" link. **Cause.** The repository was renamed: GitHub's current name is `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`, while the project origin still uses the old name `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`. A worker that builds its PR link from the origin reports the old-name URL. The tracked PR row carries the current name. **Why #7206 missed it.** #7206 wrote a per-PR alias, but only when discovery inserted the PR from the old-name listing. A checkout with git remotes for both names lists the repository twice, in random map order. When the current-name listing ran first, no alias was ever written. - 29 of the 37 tracked `OrchestratorInc` PRs on the affected machine had no alias. - 9 sessions showed the duplicate card, including #7534. - Merged PRs could never get an alias, because discovery only lists open PRs. **Fix.** The rename is now recorded once, at the repository level: - **Discovery** (`recordRename` in `observe/scm`): when a PR listing for one name returns PRs whose base repository has another name (GitHub `base.repo.full_name`), the observer stores `old name → current name` in the new `repository_renames` table. Each rename is written at most once per daemon run. - **Read** (`ListPRListing`): old repository names are mapped to their current names before comparing the existing normalized PR key (`ChangeRequestReference.Key()`, which already ignores case, `www.`, `http` and trailing slashes). Every PR of a renamed repository dedupes, merged ones included. - **Removed:** #7206's per-PR discovery alias (`listedRepoAlias`) and the `resolveReportedPRURL` "try as typed, then normalized" lookup. `report_store.go` is back to its pre-#7206 form. ## Tests - Unit tests: - Observer: a listing under the old name records the rename exactly once across two polls. - Store: a rename round-trips, and the latest name wins. - `ListPRListing`: reports under the old name in odd spellings are hidden, while a same-numbered PR in an unrelated repository stays visible. - Passing locally: `go test` for `internal/domain`, `internal/observe/scm`, `internal/service/session`, the store tests touched here, and the `internal/storage/sqlite` migration tests (without `-race`). `go build ./...` and `go vet` also pass. - Real-data check (throwaway harness, not committed): - The real GitHub listing of `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` (400 open PRs), run through the real `recordRename`, stored `untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator → orchestratorinc/agent-orchestrator`. - The 9 affected sessions' rows were copied from a real `ao.db` into a lab DB and run through the real store and `ListPRListing`. Every session went from 2 cards to 1, including #7534 and the 6 merged PRs in terminated sessions. - The full desktop run is under **Before / After** below. ## Before / After The dev desktop app ran against an isolated lab daemon: `main` (`24e2d7eb80`) before, and this PR (`bbbba051c0`) after. The lab data is two sessions copied read-only from a real `ao.db`. They are terminated in the lab, which is why the "agent controller stopped" banner appears. The after daemon learned `untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator → orchestratorinc/agent-orchestrator` from its own live GitHub listing. The session API's `linkedPrs` went from the old-name URL to empty for both sessions. | | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | #7534 (open) | | | | #7152 (merged) | | | "Pull requests (2)" with a "Reported by worker" duplicate becomes a single "Pull request" card. ## Risks - New migration `20261101145613011_repository_renames.sql` adds one small table. - A recorded rename is never removed. If someone later creates a new repository at the exact old name, a same-numbered PR there would be hidden behind the tracked one. GitHub breaks the old-name redirect in that case, so the edge is left unhandled. - Only GitHub listings report a base repository name that can differ from the listed one, so GitLab renames are not learned. That matches today's behaviour. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(opencode): approving a permission leaves the session stuck in Needs You until the turn ends
body:
### Bug

OpenCode 1 sessions stay in **blocked / "Needs You"** after the user answers a permission prompt (approve **or** reject). The state only clears when the whole turn ends (`stop`). Anything AO tries to deliver to the session during that window — messages, nudges, handoff prompts — is refused with `ErrAwaitingDecision`.

OpenCode 2 (`opencode-v2`) is unaffected: it already emits `permission-resolved`, which the lifecycle reducer treats as a turn boundary.

### Expected

After `permission.replied` / `question.replied` / `question.rejected`, the session returns to `active` while the agent resumes work, and `idle` when the turn ends.

### Actual

The plugin reports the reply as generic `active`. The lifecycle tool-flight precedence rule suppresses generic `active` while the session is blocked (by design — it must not let sibling tool traffic clear a live dialog), and OpenCode's payload carries no tool identity, so the correlated-post clear can never fire either. The block lifts only at the next turn boundary.

### Reproduction

1. Start an AO worker using the OpenCode 1 harness with permissions set to ask.
2. Prompt it to run an operation that triggers `permission.asked`. The card shows Needs You ✅.
3. Approve (or reject) the prompt in the TUI.
4. Observe the card **stays** on Needs You for the rest of the turn; try to send the session a message from AO → send fails with `ErrAwaitingDecision` until the turn finishes.

### Root cause (source evidence, commit `72e80ae0`)

| Step | Location | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Ask → `permission-blocked` | `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/assets/ao-activity.ts:178-184` | payload: `{session_id, model}` — no `tool_name`/`tool_use_id` |
| `permission-blocked` → blocked | `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/activity.go:20-21` | `ActivityBlocked` (sticky) |
| Reply → generic `active` | `ao-activity.ts:186-193` (`permission.replied` / `question.replied` / `question.rejected`) | generic `active`, no tool identity |
| Generic `active` suppressed while blocked | `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:1427-1461` (`applyToolPrecedenceLocked`) | only `isTurnBoundaryEvent` or the correlated post may apply |
| `permission-resolved` **is** a turn boundary | `manager.go:1324-1328` (`isTurnBoundaryEvent`) | already first-class in the reducer |
| No correlated-post fallback possible | `manager.go:1393-1424` | candidate needs `ToolUseID`/`ToolName`; OpenCode payload has neither → fail-closed |
| v1 deriver doesn't know `permission-resolved` | `activity.go:10-24` | unmapped events degrade to metadata-only signals, and precedence only runs `if s.Valid` (`manager.go:968-970`) |
| Delivery refused while blocked | `backend/internal/sessionguard/guard.go:130-138`, `:212-228`, `:339-351`; `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:5023-5024` | `SuppressedAwaitingUser` → `ErrAwaitingDecision` |

The reducer side was built for this exact fix and already has a passing test for the cure: `TestToolPrecedence_DefinitivePermissionResolutionClearsBlocked` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/toolflight_test.go:284-293`) drives `permission-blocked` → `permission-resolved` → active. The OpenCode 1 adapter is the only producer that never sends it.

### Proof (runtime reproduction against the real Manager)

A temporary test in the `lifecycle` package (scratch file, removed after the run; no source changes) drove `Manager.ApplyActivitySignal` with the exact events the plugin emits at commit `72e80ae0` (Windows verification host; none of the cited files modified in the tree). Results — all assertions passed:

| Sequence applied | Observed state |
|---|---|
| seed active → `blocked`/"permission-blocked" | `blocked` ✅ |
| `active`/"active" (the approval report) | **still `blocked`** — bug reproduced |
| further `active`/"active" (tool traffic) | still `blocked` |
| `active`/"permission-resolved" | `active` ✅ |
| `idle`/"stop" | `idle` ✅ |
| metadata-only signal (`Valid=false`, event `permission-resolved`, i.e. plugin fixed but deriver not) | **still `blocked`** — proves the deriver change is mandatory |
| rejection path: blocked → `permission-resolved` → `active` → `stop` | `active` → `idle` ✅ |
| question flow (same normalized pair) | identical stuck window ✅ |
| 2× `pre-tool-use` + uncorrelated `post-tool-use` while blocked | stays `blocked`; `permission-resolved` clears ✅ |
| duplicate `permission-resolved` after unblock | harmless no-op ✅ |

Not verified live: an end-to-end OpenCode 1 TUI session (no OpenCode binary in the verification environment). The inputs used are byte-for-byte what `ao hooks opencode` produces from the plugin's documented payloads.

### Why #4087's fix doesn't hold

#4087 mapped asks → `permission-blocked` (correct) and replies → `active`, on the assumption that "active … clears the sticky blocked state immediately". The tool-flight precedence rule added to prevent sibling/subagent traffic from clearing live dialogs intentionally suppresses non-boundary actives while blocked. So #4087 fixed "stays Working during the prompt" but left "stays Needs You after answering".

### Proposed minimal fix

1. `ao-activity.ts:186-193` — emit `permission-resolved` instead of `active` for `permission.replied` / `question.replied` / `question.rejected` (mirrors the shipped v2 plugin, `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/assets/ao-activity.ts:76-79`, and the Cline precedent, `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/hooks.go:86`).
2. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/activity.go` — add `case "permission-resolved": return domain.ActivityActive, true` (required; see proof above).
3. Tests: deriver row in `opencode/activity_test.go`; assert the installed plugin wires `permission-resolved` in `opencode/opencode_test.go`; add a lifecycle sequence test pinning `permission-blocked` → `active`(suppressed) → `permission-resolved` → active.

Additive only; no lifecycle contract changes; plugin + deriver ship in the same binary.

### Related

- #4087 — introduced the current mapping (its reply→`active` assumption is the defect)
- #3306 — Cursor: identical "sticky needs-input for the whole turn" shape, fixed via correlated clearing

title: fix(browser): make the first profile the default
body:
Code changes: +50 -12  
Tests: +173 -15  
Others: +18 -18  

## What

Make the first browser profile the default, visibly, instead of silently falling back to the oldest saved profile.

- The first profile you import or create becomes the default and shows the Default badge.
- Deleting the default promotes the oldest remaining profile. With no profiles left, sessions use Temporary.
- Users who already have profiles but no default get their oldest profile as the default once, on the first start after this update.
- Sessions with no choice of their own use session choice → default → Temporary, so "Unset as default" is a real way back to Temporary.

## Why

#6345 made unbound sessions use the first saved profile. #5453 replaced that with an explicit default. During review, the reason given was that a hidden fallback can expose cookies or a signed-in identity to unrelated sessions. That left users who imported Chrome but never starred a default on Temporary.

This keeps the default visible and reversible while fixing that case. Earlier revisions of this PR restored the hidden `profiles[0]` fallback, and this revision replaces that approach. With the hidden fallback, unsetting the default on the first profile did nothing, Settings showed no badge for the profile actually in use, and deleting a profile moved closed sessions onto another signed-in profile.

## Before / After

| Situation | Before (main) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First import, no default set | Sessions open in Temporary | The imported profile is the default; sessions use it |
| Existing profiles, no default (upgrade) | Temporary | Oldest profile becomes the default once |
| User unsets the default | Temporary | Temporary, and it stays unset across restarts |
| Default profile deleted, others remain | Temporary | Oldest remaining profile becomes the default |
| Last profile deleted | Temporary | Temporary |
| Open browser on a deleted profile | Switches to Temporary | Unchanged: switches to Temporary |
| Session explicitly set to Temporary | Stays Temporary | Unchanged |

## How

- `browser-profile-store.ts`:
  - `createProfile` sets the default when it creates the only profile. Imports pass `claimDefault: false` and call `claimDefaultIfFirst` only after every imported profile has committed, so an unbound worker never opens a half-imported profile that a failed or cancelled import then deletes.
  - `deleteProfile` promotes `profiles[0]` when the deleted profile was the default.
  - `parseRegistry` seeds the oldest profile as the default when the registry has no `defaultProfileSeeded` marker. Every write records the marker, so a later unset sticks. The registry version is unchanged, so older app builds can still read the file.
- `browser-view-host.ts`: the `profiles[0]` fallback is removed. The store guarantees a default whenever one should exist.
- `BrowserProfilesSection.tsx`: mirrors both store rules after create and delete, so the badge stays accurate without a reload.
- Copy (all locales): `settings.browserProfiles.description` drops "shared only by workers you explicitly bind", and `settings.browserImport.description` drops "isolated". Both now say the first profile becomes the default that every worker without its own choice uses.

title: bug(opencode): subagent sessions overwrite parent identity and corrupt session restoration
body:
### Bug

OpenCode reports subagents as child sessions on the same plugin event bus AO's activity plugins subscribe to. Neither the OpenCode 1 nor the OpenCode 2 plugin filters child sessions, so child `session.created`, prompt, tool, and completion events are forwarded to AO as if they belonged to the parent. The lifecycle manager then overwrites the parent's persisted native session id with the child's id.

### Expected behavior

A parent AO session keeps its own native OpenCode session id, its conversation checkpoint, and its own active/idle lifecycle regardless of child-session (subagent) activity. Restoration must always resume the parent conversation.

### Actual behavior

- The child's native id overwrites `Metadata.AgentSessionID` (the restore handle) whenever a child event is the latest signal — and flips back and forth as parent and child interleave.
- Each identity change resets the conversation checkpoint.
- Child completion (`session.status` idle on v1, `session.execution.*` on v2) marks the parent AO session idle while the parent is still working; the state then flaps.
- If a child emits the last event of the turn (a guaranteed ordering risk with v2 background subagents), the durable restore handle is the child's id and AO later resumes the **wrong native session**.

### Reproduction

1. Spawn an AO worker on the OpenCode 1 (or 2) harness and let it invoke a subagent (task tool).
2. Observe the session's `agentSessionId` metadata while the subagent runs: it flips between the parent and child native ids.
3. Let the subagent finish after the parent's last event.
4. Restart/restore the AO session: it resumes with `opencode --session <child id>` (v2: `--standalone --session <child id>`), i.e. the wrong conversation.

Runtime proof against the real lifecycle manager (commit `72e80ae0`) — inputs are the exact events `ao hooks opencode[-v2]` produces from the plugin payloads:

| Sequence | Observed |
|---|---|
| parent registered (`ses_parent`), checkpoint set | baseline stable |
| child `session-start` (`ses_child`) | handle → `ses_child`; checkpoint cleared |
| child `stop` | parent AO session → idle mid-turn |
| parent `active` | state active, handle back to `ses_parent` |
| parent `stop`, then delayed child `stop` | **durable handle → `ses_child`** |
| grandchild `session-start` | handle → `ses_grandchild` (nested hijack) |
| two concurrent children | each hijacks in turn; last reporter owns the handle |

### Root cause

OpenCode marks subagents with `parentID` on `session.created`, but the AO plugins never read it:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/assets/ao-activity.ts:97-104,125-138` — `switchedSession` adopts any session id and emits `session-start` for it.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/assets/ao-activity.ts:44-48` — `ensureSession` reports `session-start` for any new session id.
- `backend/internal/cli/hooks.go:636-639` — `hookAgentSessionID` lifts `session_id` from every payload (both harnesses are `SupportsHarness`).
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:2060-2067` (`applyActivityMetadata`) overwrites `AgentSessionID` with any non-empty id; `manager.go:748-767` resets the checkpoint on identity change. The only guard is timestamp ordering (`manager.go:742-747`), which newer child events pass. The launch fence does not help: children share the parent's `AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID`.
- Restoration consumes the corrupted handle: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/opencode.go:149-170` (`--session`), `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/opencodev2.go:64-78,119-121`.

Upstream evidence that `parentID` is available on `session.created`:

- v1: `Session.Info.parentID` and `Event.Created` schema `{sessionID, info: Info}` — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.4.9/packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts
- v1 task tool creates children with `parentID` — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.4.9/packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts
- v2: `parentID` on `SessionSchema.Info` — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/session/info.ts
- v2 subagent tool creates children with `parentID: context.sessionID`, supports nesting (depth walk over `parentID`) and background children — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts
- `session.status` deliberately does not carry `parentID` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/30043, closed as "fetch the session and check the parent yourself"), so the plugin must track `session.created` itself.

### Proof

- Lifecycle-level runtime reproduction results in the table above (scratch test against the real `Manager.ApplyActivitySignal`; inputs byte-identical to what `ao hooks opencode[-v2]` posts).
- No live OpenCode TUI end-to-end run was performed; child-event emission is verified from the upstream sources linked above, not asserted.
- Duplicate check: no AO issue or PR reports OpenCode child-session identity hijack; commit search for `parentID` returns 0 results (see Related for the partial overlaps).

### Proposed fix

Plugin-side filtering in both managed plugins (no lifecycle changes):

1. Track child session ids from `session.created` where `parentID` is non-empty (v1: `properties.info.parentID`; v2: `data.parentID`). Treat the first `session.created` without `parentID` as the root; any other session id is a child.
2. Never report identity-bearing signals (`session-start`, prompt, stop) for children.
3. Optionally re-attribute child tool/execution activity to the root id as plain `active` (child id never forwarded) so subagent work still reads as activity.

Filtering must happen in the plugins: parent and child arrive at the daemon identically (same `AO_SESSION_ID`, same launch id, no lineage in the payload), and a Go-side identity heuristic would break deliberately supported new-native-session flows. Known non-goal: with v2 background subagents the parent may report `stop` while a child still runs — AO then shows idle until the next parent event. That is a display limitation, not corruption; root-attributed child activity (3) is the follow-up that addresses it.

### Regression tests

- Plugin behavioral harness (pattern: `opencodev2/hooks_test.go` `TestManagedV2PluginReportsLifecycleInOrder…`): parent + child (`parentID`) + grandchild events → no captured `ao hooks` call ever carries a child id; child tool activity carries the root id.
- Concurrent children and out-of-order child completion → only parent events reported.
- Static assertions that the installed plugins reference `parentID` filtering.
- Lifecycle pin: with parent-ids-only input, interleaved same-launch events preserve `AgentSessionID`.
- Existing identity tests (e.g. `TestActivity_NewNativeConversationClearsPriorConversationCheckpoint`) stay green.

### Related

- #6201 — Claude/Codex-only subagent idle handling; OpenCode was left unfiltered, and identity was out of its scope.
- #4125 (fixed), #6585 (open) — same symptom family (session identity rebound to the wrong native conversation) for Claude, via process-env inheritance; different mechanism.
- #7564 — separate OpenCode lifecycle bug in the same plugins (permission resolution), filed separately to keep root causes distinct.

title: bug(opencode): tool executions are never tracked - generic active events discard identity and starve the step timeline
body:
### Bug

AO's OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 plugins report every tool execution as a generic `active` activity event. The lifecycle manager's tool-flight tracking and execution-step timeline are driven by the specific events `pre-tool-use` / `post-tool-use` / `post-tool-use-failure`, so OpenCode sessions never register a tool start, completion, failure, or duration — even though OpenCode's plugin API hands the adapter the tool name and a stable call id on both versions.

### Expected behavior

OpenCode sessions should populate the same tool telemetry every other hooked harness provides: a current running tool, recent completed tools with start/end times, a failure flag on errored tools, and in-flight tool correlation (which also enables correlated permission-dialog clearing).

### Actual behavior

- **OpenCode 1** discards the tool identity entirely: `tool.execute.before/after` receive `{tool, sessionID, callID}` upstream, but the plugin forwards only `{session_id, model}` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/assets/ao-activity.ts:202-209`).
- **OpenCode 2** forwards `tool_name`/`tool_use_id` but still labels the event `active` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/assets/ao-activity.ts:92-99`). The lifecycle only performs flight/step tracking for events literally named `pre-tool-use`/`post-tool-use*` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:1354-1367`; `backend/internal/lifecycle/steps.go:18-46`), so the fields are dead weight.
- `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/activity` (`current`/`recent` tool steps) is built solely from the step ring (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/usage.go:158-187`), so it stays empty for OpenCode sessions: no current tool, no recent tools, no durations, no failure flags.
- Neither OpenCode deriver recognizes the tool events (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/activity.go:10-24`; `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/activity.go:7-17`), so even a plugin-only change would degrade to metadata-only signals that skip tracking (`backend/internal/cli/hooks.go:657`; `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:968-970`).

### Reproduction

1. Run an OpenCode 1 or 2 worker session and let it execute several tools (including a failing one).
2. Query `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/activity`.
3. Observe `current` and `recent` are empty/absent, and stay empty for the whole session. Compare with a Claude Code session, which shows the running tool and the last completed tools with durations.

Runtime proof against the real lifecycle manager (commit `72e80ae0`), driving `Manager.ApplyActivitySignal` with the exact signals `ao hooks opencode[-v2]` produces today:

| Sequence applied | Observed |
|---|---|
| `active` event with no tool identity (v1 shape) | 0 steps, 0 in-flight entries |
| `active` event **with** `ToolName`/`ToolUseID` (v2 shape) | **still 0 steps, 0 in-flight** — the event name gates tracking |
| `pre-tool-use` Bash/call_1 → `post-tool-use` Bash/call_1 | in-flight registered then cleared; step opened and closed |
| two concurrent `pre-tool-use` (call_1, call_2) | both tracked independently; each post closes only its own step |
| `post-tool-use` with unknown call id | clears nothing; other tools untouched |
| `pre-tool-use` → `post-tool-use-failure` | step closed with `Failed=true`, in-flight cleared |
| duplicate `post-tool-use` | no-op |
| tool events while `blocked` (uncorrelated dialog) | suppressed — tool traffic never clears an OpenCode permission dialog; only the turn boundary does |

### Root cause

OpenCode's plugin API provides everything needed, verified from upstream source:

- v1 `tool.execute.before` input: `{tool, sessionID, callID}`; `tool.execute.after`: same identity (+ `args` and the tool result). Both fire with the **same `callID`** — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.4.9/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts (trigger sites ~lines 414-433). Note: the after trigger follows the successful `execute`, so **v1 emits no failure signal for a failed tool**.
- v2 hook events (`@opencode/plugin`): `execute.before` = `{tool, sessionID, agent, messageID, id: Tool.CallID, input}`; `execute.after` = same identity plus a discriminated `{status: "completed", result} | {status: "error", error}` — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/effect/tool.ts. Same `id` on both events; `status: "error"` identifies failures.
- Tool arguments (`args`/`input`) are present in these payloads and must **not** be forwarded to AO activity events.

### Proposed fix

1. `opencode/assets/ao-activity.ts` — `tool.execute.before` → `ao hooks opencode pre-tool-use` with `{tool_name: input.tool, tool_use_id: input.callID}`; `tool.execute.after` → `post-tool-use` likewise. Never serialize `args`.
2. `opencodev2/assets/ao-activity.ts` — `execute.before` → `pre-tool-use`; `execute.after` → `post-tool-use`, or `post-tool-use-failure` when `status === "error"` (identity fields already forwarded).
3. Derivers: add `pre-tool-use`/`post-tool-use`/`post-tool-use-failure` → active to `opencode.DeriveActivityState` (also add `permission-resolved` per #7564) and to `opencodev2.DeriveActivityState`. Both deriver and plugin changes must land together — unmapped events become metadata-only and skip tracking.
4. Coordinate with #7567: only emit tool events for the root session, so subagent tool traffic neither hijacks identity nor pollutes the parent's timeline with child ids.
5. Known limitation (v1 only): upstream fires no failure hook, so a failed tool's step stays open until later steps rotate it out of the 20-entry ring; the in-flight map is cleared at the turn boundary (`manager.go:1469-1472`) — same best-effort behavior as other harnesses without failure hooks.

No lifecycle changes required: the existing machinery handled every proposed event correctly in the runtime proof above.

### Regression tests

- Deriver table tests in `opencode/activity_test.go` and `opencodev2/activity_test.go` for the three tool events.
- Static plugin assertions (`opencode/opencode_test.go`, `opencodev2/hooks_test.go`): installed plugins wire `pre-tool-use`/`post-tool-use(-failure)` and forward `tool_name`/`tool_use_id`; assert tool arguments (`args`/`input`) never appear in hook payloads.
- CLI seam: `ao hooks opencode pre-tool-use` with `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_use_id":"call_1"}` populates the signal fields (`cli/hooks_test.go`).
- Plugin behavioral harness: tool before/after sequence produces stable call ids across the pair.
- Existing `toolflight_test.go` / `steps_test.go` already pin the machinery; keep green.

### Related

- #4083 — merged PR that introduced the OpenCode plugin with the generic-`active` tool mapping (origin of this behavior).
- #7564 — same plugins: permission resolution leaves sessions blocked (fixed independently; the two fixes compose — tool posts stay suppressed against uncorrelated dialogs).
- #7567 — same plugins: child-session identity hijack; the tool fix must skip/re-attribute child tool events.
- #2814 / #7399 / #2873 — Kimi: same problem class (missing mid-turn tool signals), fixed by adding tool hooks.
- #6054 / #6618 — Chat-timeline tool-call display for chat/ACP drivers (different surface, different root cause).

title: feat: add first run project prompt
body:
Code changes: +932 -331\
Tests: +514 -138\
Others: +0 -0 (1 binary asset)

## What

The prompt half of eligible fresh desktop installs opens a compact Start a project modal with repository URL, a native clone destination picker, and Clone and continue. Open a local folder and Start a standalone agent reuse the existing functional flows.

[Design reference / online HTML preview](https://claude.ai/artifact/GmdSsxTrjpS4C9o9kHSyVt). This is the supplied reference mock, not implementation evidence.

## Why

Give new users a direct first project path while preserving the home experience for returning users, including users who have deleted all projects.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A fresh install opens the existing four Get Started cards. | Half of eligible installs open Start a project; the control half retain the four cards. |
| No durable first project prompt decision. | Existing app markers are treated as seen; fresh markers stay pending until dismissal, an accepted alternate action, or successful clone registration. |
| Opening the local folder picker from the new prompt initially dismissed the modal. | The modal stays behind the native picker and validation; cancelling the picker retains the prompt. |

Real Electron captures were taken at base `d23a10a630` and head `915dd90a81` with the same window and isolated scratch data. Screenshots are retained as `first-run-before.png` and `first-run-after.png` in AO session 433 artifacts. Both current experiment arms were also captured in isolated Electron profiles as `first-run-experiment-prompt.png` and `first-run-experiment-control.png`, with telemetry bootstrap null. GitHub attachment upload is unavailable through the current tools, so the screenshots still need attaching here.

## How

- Read the existing install cohort through app-state IPC independently of telemetry bootstrap. Reserve exposure with an atomic file next to the app state so concurrent windows and restarts cannot duplicate it. Renderer events still honor the existing telemetry consent policy.
- Persist `firstRunProjectPrompt` in the existing Electron app marker through typed preload IPC. Existing markers default to seen, independently of project count. Existing projects and the legacy migration offer suppress the prompt.
- Wait for daemon, workspace, requirements, and migration readiness before offering it. Keep the pending marker through clone validation or registration failures.
- Reuse CreateProjectFlow and CloneRepositoryDialog for native directory selection, backend preparation, validation, agent setup, registration, navigation, cancellation, and retry. First run does not invent a destination path.
- Retain existing Radix focus and keyboard behavior, theme tokens, responsive layout, and localized strings. No replay button, shortcut, or settings action is added.

## Experiment

Eligible fresh installs use their existing fixed `experiment_cohort`: 0 through 49 receive `prompt`, 50 through 99 receive `control`. A missing or unreadable cohort uses control. The UI reads the cohort independently of telemetry consent. Change `FIRST_RUN_PROMPT_COHORT_MAX` from 49 to 99 for full rollout; PostHog feature flags remain disabled.

- `ao.onboarding.first_run_experiment_exposed` sends `{ variant: prompt | control }` at the eligibility decision. An atomic install marker reserves exposure once across renderer remounts, restarts, and concurrent requests.
- `ao.onboarding.first_run_prompt_action` sends `{ action: clone | local_folder | standalone | dismissed }` for the prompt arm. Clone reports after successful preparation; successful registration does not double count it. Cancelling the native local folder picker does not count as choosing a folder.
- Main metric: percentage of exposed installs with at least one `ao.projects.created` within 7 days, split by variant. Target: reduce installs that never add a project from roughly 40% to below 30%. Existing project creation events already carry `experiment_cohort` and `first_for_install`.
- Secondary metric: at least two projects within 7 days. Guardrail: first session spawned within 7 days must not decline. Inspect the prompt action breakdown.
- Harshit will configure the PostHog dashboard after merge and run the experiment for two full weeks from the 0.14.9+ stable release.

## Testing

- CI repair: updated the retired automatic GitHub notice integration tests to exercise `GitHubSetupPanel` through explicit user actions, preserving daemon terminal adoption, reconciliation failure, retry, cleanup failure, and skip/remount coverage. Supplied explicit GitHub readiness in project import fixtures. Production behavior is unchanged by these test fixes.
- The reported shard command `npx vitest run --shard=3/4` passed locally: 157 files, 2,872 tests passed, 3 skipped.
- Full frontend candidate suite passed: 627 files, 10,816 tests passed, 9 skipped. The concurrent commit `0dcd4f5fdf` then removed the overlapping home case instead of retaining the replacement guard; its production code is identical to the passing candidate. The final home suite passed all 26 tests.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: passed.
- Renderer Vite build: passed.
- Renderer smoke: the first attempt could not launch because the pinned Playwright browser was missing. Installed Chromium in a temporary cache and started the full command again on an isolated port; completion has not been inspected.
- Real isolated Electron: prompt rendering, Escape dismissal, durable seen marker, and no prompt after reload verified. Native picker cancellation and delayed validation transitions covered by regression tests.
- Experiment verification: boundary cohorts, control/prompt eligibility, exposure deduplication across remounts and concurrent claims, action routing and deduplication, and rejection of unknown telemetry values. Both arms verified in real isolated Electron with telemetry bootstrap null.
- Three existing import tests now hold validation responses pending explicitly rather than depending on transient timing.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Remaining CI coverage: Linux runner and pinned container behavior, docs and shared package jobs, Electron origin boundary jobs, OS packaging, and release checks were not reproduced locally. Remote checks after these test fixes have not been polled. No review run was started. Screenshot attachments and the earlier renderer smoke completion remain unverified. No review run was started.

- [x] One focused change

title: bug(opencode-v2): no user prompt reporting - every stop marks the conversation checkpoint unsettled and blocks handoff/replay
body:
### Bug

The OpenCode 2 activity plugin reports session creation, execution, status, and permission events — but never a user prompt. AO's conversation checkpoints advance only on a `user-prompt-submit` boundary (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:804-855`), so every OpenCode 2 turn ends as a "scoped Stop without its prompt boundary": the checkpoint is durably marked unsettled (`manager.go:888-906`) and the TUI→Chat handoff / conversation-replay trust gate fails closed for the session's lifetime.

OpenCode 2 exposes the needed event — `session.inbox.enqueued` with `item.type == "user"` and the prompt text at `item.payload.text` — and AO's own cloud worker plugin already uses exactly this (`cloud/internal/workerexec/assets/ao-activity.ts:100-108`, verified live against opencode 2.0.19 per its header). The local v2 adapter (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/assets/ao-activity.ts:50-80`) handles no prompt event at all.

### Expected behavior

An OpenCode 2 turn that starts with a user prompt and ends with `stop` produces a trusted conversation checkpoint (`prompt` → `complete`, not `unsettled`), so interface switching and replay work like OpenCode 1 and Claude Code sessions.

### Actual behavior

Runtime proof against the real lifecycle manager (commit `72e80ae0`, `HarnessOpenCodeV2`), driving `Manager.ApplyActivitySignal` with the exact signals `ao hooks opencode-v2` produces today:

| Sequence | Observed |
|---|---|
| `session-start` → `stop` (today's v2 stream: no prompt event exists) | checkpoint state `empty`, **`ConversationCheckpointUnsettled = true`** — first stop of the first turn poisons the session |
| `session-start` → `user-prompt-submit` → `stop` (with the fix) | checkpoint `complete`, clean |
| two prompts → `stop` | latest prompt retained; checkpoint `complete` |
| duplicate prompt (same timestamp+text) | cleanly fenced by the manager (`manager.go:818-828`) |

Two additional manager behaviors the fix must respect (also runtime-confirmed):

1. **Double stop unsettles a completed checkpoint**: a second `stop` without an intervening prompt marks `unsettled` again (`manager.go:888-906`). The current v2 plugin maps BOTH `session.execution.{succeeded,failed,interrupted}` AND `session.status(idle)` to `stop`, so one turn can emit two stops (the adapter's own fixture models this sequence, `opencodev2/hooks_test.go:191`). The plugin must dedupe stops to one per turn.
2. **A replayed older-timestamp prompt is fenced but does not clear an existing unsettled flag** — later stops keep it unsettled until a genuinely newer prompt arrives. Prompt dedup must therefore happen in the plugin (once per inbox item id), not be left to AO.

### Root cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/assets/ao-activity.ts` — event switch handles `session.created`, `session.execution.*`, `session.status`, `permission.*`; no prompt source.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/activity.go:7-17` — deriver has no `user-prompt-submit` case either (unlike v1, `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/activity.go:14-15`), so plugin and deriver must both change.
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:899-906` — promptless scoped stop ⇒ `ConversationCheckpointUnsettled = true` and assistant text dropped.
- Upstream event schema (verified in source): `SessionEvent.InboxEnqueued` payload is `{inboxID, sessionID, item}` with `item ∈ user | synthetic | compaction | move`; the user payload is `UserPayload{text, files, agents, skills, metadata}`; delivery ∈ `steer | queue` — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/session/inbox.ts (`admit` publishes the event; `Item`/`UserPayload` from `@opencode/schema/session-inbox`). Filtering `item.type == "user"` excludes synthetic/system, compaction, and move items.

### Reproduction

1. Spawn an OpenCode 2 worker, send a prompt, let the turn complete.
2. Attempt TUI→Chat interface switch (or any native replay/handoff that requires a trusted checkpoint): it fails closed because the session's checkpoint is unsettled since its first turn.
3. Cross-check the session's durable metadata: `conversationCheckpointState` never advances past empty and `conversationCheckpointUnsettled` is set.

### Proof

- Lifecycle-level runtime table above (scratch test against the real Manager; inputs byte-identical to `ao hooks opencode-v2` output).
- No live OpenCode 2 TUI session was run. The cloud plugin's live verification of `session.inbox.enqueued` on 2.0.19 covers API-driven sessions; TUI-mode coverage of the same event is [verify live] — the inbox is the session's pending-input table that all input promotes through, but the plugin fix should keep the existing v1-style fallback behavior in mind.

### Proposed fix

1. `opencodev2/assets/ao-activity.ts`: handle `session.inbox.enqueued`; when `data.item.type === "user"`, emit `user-prompt-submit` with `prompt: data.item.payload.text` (truncation/sanitization already applied downstream by AO: `cli/hooks.go` caps and sanitizes; forward no files/metadata).
2. Dedupe per inbox item id (an item can be re-delivered/reconciled — upstream `admit()` skips the event only when a row already exists, and `promotedFromMessage` can synthesize one).
3. Dedupe stops: emit `stop` once per turn (prefer `session.status(idle)`; suppress a stop that immediately follows another without an intervening `user-prompt-submit`), so execution events + status don't unsettle the completed checkpoint.
4. `opencodev2/activity.go`: add `case "user-prompt-submit": return domain.ActivityActive, true`.
5. No lifecycle changes — the manager already fences duplicates and advances checkpoints correctly once the boundary arrives (proven above).

### Regression tests

- Extend the v2 behavioral harness (`opencodev2/hooks_test.go` `TestManagedV2PluginReportsLifecycleInOrder…`) with: inbox.enqueued(user) → `user-prompt-submit` with the prompt text; inbox.enqueued(synthetic/compaction/move) → ignored; duplicate inbox id → single emission; execution.succeeded + session.status(idle) in one turn → single `stop`.
- Deriver row in `opencodev2/activity_test.go` for `user-prompt-submit`.
- Lifecycle pin (optional): prompt + single stop completes the checkpoint for `HarnessOpenCodeV2`; double stop leaves unsettled (documents the dedup requirement).

### Related

- #7564, #7567, #7568 — the other OpenCode lifecycle defects in the same plugins; fixes compose (this one adds the prompt boundary the other fixes assume exists).
- #7111 — Codex TUI→Chat handoff failing on an untrusted checkpoint: same failure surface, different harness/cause.
- #6216 — checkpoint settling machinery (Claude/Codex-oriented).

title: feat(session-import): support Kimchi native copy and resume
body:
Code changes: +760 -6  
Tests: +803 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Add full Kimchi session import with native copy-and-resume. Stacked on #6364 (`codex/session-import-build` at `0427cd4de3e8cc2c812e9b389d37d9648d1c0a0c`); this diff contains only Kimchi parsing/discovery, relocation, continuation/root admission, import environment wiring, and import eligibility.

## Why

Kimchi finds a conversation in a cwd-keyed folder. Resuming the same ID from AO's workspace without a correctly placed copy silently opens an empty chat.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Kimchi chats are absent from import eligibility | Native conversations can be scanned and imported with their identity, title, model, effort, and active history |
| Same native ID from another cwd can return an empty chat | First open prepares the exact raw-LaunchCWD lookup path, rewrites the single session record cwd, and requires native history replay |
| A config-root override could appear usable although Kimchi ignores it | Discovery uses the default native home root; incompatible source roots and effective child-home roots fail clearly before native launch |
| Rewound or retracted messages could appear in displayed history | Parsing follows the active parent chain and applies active context edits/retractions |

The frontend change only extends the existing eligibility set; no layout/composer redesign. No desktop screenshots were captured under the restricted local-validation scope.

## How

- Kimchi 1.24.3 bundled `src/modes/acp/server.ts` pins `encodeCwdDir`, `resolveSessionPathById`, and strict header ID/cwd equality. Folder and header use RAW `LaunchCWD`, including symlink paths.
- Implement `AgentImportedSessionRelocator` using the base's four-argument `importcopy.CopyOnce`. Keep the source basename, require exactly one session record and native identity, preserve all other records, and validate existing destinations without overwriting AO additions. Reject ambiguous matches, symlinks, malformed/incomplete files, and empty copies.
- The shared base owns atomic 0600 publication, first-open orchestration, `ResumeCwd`, and the empty-native-replay guard. No duplicate shared machinery or sibling harness changes.
- Kimchi 1.24.3 bundled `src/entry.ts` unconditionally resets both `KIMCHI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` to `homedir/.config/kimchi/harness`. Custom config-root overrides are **unsupported**. The Kimchi resolver and ACP admission model the actual effective child home; directory aliases of the same root are allowed. Imported source-root metadata is carried as a launch assertion. This code never changes HOME or copies credentials.
- Kimchi has no reliable live-writer lock; import uses its own relocated transcript rather than writing the original.

## Testing

Fresh exact-head Actions checks for `8b71b35abf128b7a90221fa7f4a464ac263e9a4a` are pending after normally merging base `0427cd4de3e8cc2c812e9b389d37d9648d1c0a0c`. The two eligibility-list conflicts retain OMP and Kimchi while preserving the base's Droid deferral alongside OpenCode and Kimi. Both OMP/Kimchi eligibility assertions, all deferral regressions, and the base's admission guard are preserved. Kimchi's parser and adapter are unchanged; generated files match the base.

Current-head AO review is requested and its verdict is pending. Earlier CI and review results do not validate this merged head. **Needs independent human GitHub approval.**

All builds, tests, lint, formatting, and generation run **only in GitHub Actions**. No local checks, installs, new live-proof sessions, or credential/config copying were performed.

Added regressions cover raw symlink cwd lookup, source immutability/private permissions, preservation of AO-added turns, invalid/duplicate/missing headers, identity mismatch, incomplete copies, existing invalid/ambiguous destinations, active-branch edits/retractions, scan/import continuation metadata, ignored custom roots, effective child-home mismatch, and equivalent-root aliases. The base already has `TestImportedResumeRejectsEmptyNativeReplay`.

Authorized provider-level live proof used the installed Kimchi **1.24.3** binary, with throwaway chats in an isolated child HOME's default `.config/kimchi/harness` root. It did not execute the Go adapter or the production AO launch path:

- Without relocation: the same native ID loaded with **0** replayed user/assistant chunks.
- With a private copy under the **raw symlink LaunchCWD** folder and matching header cwd: **2** history chunks replayed.
- Follow-up recalled `cobalt-tamarind-515`; the source stayed byte-for-byte unchanged and the relocated file gained the follow-up turn.
- Temporary home/config/auth/chats and child processes were cleaned. Two earlier environment-only isolation attempts created new proof IDs in the native default store because the runtime ignored the override; only those newly-created transcript files were removed.

This proof establishes provider copy/replay behavior within the isolated HOME. Production default-root routing is supported by the source trace plus the new admission regressions; it has not been exercised end-to-end locally. It does **not** establish support for custom config roots. No further live runs or credential/config copying are planned.

## Checklist

- [x] Stacked on the explicitly requested feature base #6364
- [x] One harness; preserves sibling registrations and shared copy contract
- [x] Before / After describes changed behavior
- [x] Meaningful regression tests added
- [ ] Current exact-head Actions checks pass (pending)
- [ ] AO review approves current head `8b71b35abf12` (pending)
- [x] No reviewer pings, approval, merge, or shared-base push

title: fix(workspace): stop labeling killed branch probes INVALID_BRANCH
body:
Code changes: +10 -3  
Tests: +54 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Fixes #5043.

`validateBranch` filed every `git check-ref-format` failure under `ErrWorkspaceBranchInvalid`, so a probe that died to SIGKILL surfaced as `INVALID_BRANCH` for a valid `ao/<session>/root` name. It now treats a probe that never finished (`ExitError` with exit code -1, i.e. signal-terminated, or the caller's context done) as an unfinished check and returns the real cause. Spawn then reports `WORKSPACE_CREATE_FAILED` (or `SPAWN_CANCELLED`/`SPAWN_TIMEOUT` via the joined context error). Genuine git rejections (exit 128) still map to `INVALID_BRANCH`.

All `validateBranch` callers (create, restore, recreate, multi-repo, task-branch rename) go through this one function. `gitdefault.Resolver.validateBranch` does not use the sentinel and is unchanged. Skipped: the retry and the `workspace: workspace:` prefix cleanup suggested in the issue.

| | before (base) | after (head) |
|---|---|---|
| probe SIGKILLed, valid name | `INVALID_BRANCH` | `WORKSPACE_CREATE_FAILED`, cause `signal: killed` |
| `--branch 'bad branch!!'` | `INVALID_BRANCH` | `INVALID_BRANCH` |

## Evidence: real daemon + `ao spawn`, same boundary before and after

- base: `e8e3342d3fff2112ca64764a7254000f2d637f68` (origin/main)
- head: `dea27ac54f52631abc977f874aa8ebae6d8ba74a`

Each binary is `go build ./cmd/ao` at that commit, run as `ao daemon` with isolated `HOME`, `AO_DATA_DIR`, `AO_RUN_FILE`, `AO_PORT` and a throwaway repo. A wrapper `git` first on the daemon's PATH sends itself SIGKILL only for `check-ref-format --branch ao/...` and execs `/usr/bin/git` for everything else:

```sh
case " $* " in
  *" check-ref-format --branch ao/"*) kill -KILL $$ ;;
esac
exec /usr/bin/git "$@"
```

Commands per binary: `ao project add --path <repo> --id lab --worker-agent claude-code`, then `ao spawn --project lab --name probe --harness claude-code --skip-agent-check --prompt hi`, then the control with `--branch 'bad branch!!'`.

**This is controlled signal injection.** It proves the classification boundary: a killed probe is no longer labeled a bad name. It does not reproduce or identify what killed git in the original report (jetsam, a client abort, or something else); that external kill is still unproven.

Before (base):
```
== base: dev
== real git verdict on the generated shape:
ao/lab-1/root
exit=0
== spawn (default branch ao/<session>/root, probe SIGKILLed by injection):
spawn lab-1: workspace: workspace: invalid branch name: "ao/lab-1/root" (git -C /private/tmp/ao5043/base/repo check-ref-format --branch ao/lab-1/root: signal: killed) (INVALID_BRANCH) [request <host>/upiu1mzyJw-000006]
exit=1
== control spawn (--branch 'bad branch!!', real git rejects the name):
spawn lab-1: workspace: workspace: invalid branch name: "bad branch!!" (git -C /private/tmp/ao5043/base/repo check-ref-format --branch bad branch!!: exit status 128: fatal: 'bad branch!!' is not a valid branch name) (INVALID_BRANCH) [request <host>/upiu1mzyJw-000009]
exit=1
== injection log:
2026-11-01T20:28:29Z injected SIGKILL pid=46822 args: -C /private/tmp/ao5043/base/repo check-ref-format --branch ao/lab-1/root
```

After (head):
```
== head: dev
== real git verdict on the generated shape:
ao/lab-1/root
exit=0
== spawn (default branch ao/<session>/root, probe SIGKILLed by injection):
spawn lab-1: workspace: gitworktree: branch name check for "ao/lab-1/root" did not finish: git -C /private/tmp/ao5043/head/repo check-ref-format --branch ao/lab-1/root: signal: killed (WORKSPACE_CREATE_FAILED) [request <host>/p7C22m9EoR-000006]
exit=1
== control spawn (--branch 'bad branch!!', real git rejects the name):
spawn lab-1: workspace: workspace: invalid branch name: "bad branch!!" (git -C /private/tmp/ao5043/head/repo check-ref-format --branch bad branch!!: exit status 128: fatal: 'bad branch!!' is not a valid branch name) (INVALID_BRANCH) [request <host>/p7C22m9EoR-000009]
exit=1
== injection log:
2026-11-01T20:34:51Z injected SIGKILL pid=75969 args: -C /private/tmp/ao5043/head/repo check-ref-format --branch ao/lab-1/root
```

## Tests

- New `TestCreateDoesNotCallKilledBranchProbeInvalid`: real signal-killed `*exec.ExitError` (POSIX; skipped on Windows) and a cancelled context. Fails on base with `invalid branch name`, passes on head. `TestCreateRejectsInvalidBranchName` still passes.
- Local, Go 1.27.1: `go build ./...` ok; `go vet ./internal/adapters/workspace/... ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/session_manager/...` ok; `go test ./internal/adapters/workspace/... ./internal/service/session/...` ok.
- Local gap: `./internal/session_manager` fails 4 tests (`TestSpawn_RejectsMissingAgentBinary`, `TestSpawn_MissingBinaryPreservesNonEmptyScratchWorkspaceForRetry`, `TestSpawn_ValidatesBinaryAfterEnvPrefix`, `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingBinaryAfterEnvPrefix`) with `tmux required on macOS ... not found`. This machine has no tmux, and the same 4 fail on untouched main. CI is the clean-runner check.

## Risks

On Windows a killed process exits with a code rather than a signal, so only the context-done branch applies there.

It is gated on Diagnostics and a local board, as before, and its tooltip now opens below it. `useHasAppMemory` and the archive view's `trailing` light are gone. - The branch merges current main, which replaced `ShellTopbar` with the shared top bar frame (#7397); the light needed no per-platform copy after that. - Strings: `shell.cpuGraphMachine`, `shell.cpuGraphAO` and `shell.memoryColumnShare` are new in all nine catalogs; `shell.cpuLegendMachine` is removed. `shell.memoryProcessCount` drops its trailing "›", and `shell.memoryPanelTitle` uses each locale's `settings.diagnostics` wording. - `SessionsBoard.remote.test.tsx` now unmounts, empties its query clients and waits one timer tick after each test. title: fix(codex): use the session executable for account login
body:
Code changes: +13 -2  
Tests: +139 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Make Codex account add and reauthentication use the same adapter-resolved executable as sessions, including AO's managed installation when available.

## Why

Account login starts `ao codex-login` without an explicit executable. The menu then searches `PATH`, which can select a broken, independently installed npm launcher even when the session resolver selects a working managed Codex.

Related: #6371 fixes finding Node for npm launchers. This change fixes the separate executable-selection boundary. The reported `spawn .../codex ENOENT` screenshot prompted this investigation, but its underlying installation failure has not been confirmed on the reporter's machine.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| With a managed Codex fixture and a broken npm launcher on `PATH`, account login opens `ao codex-login`; the launcher hits a real Node `spawn` failure (`ENOENT`, exit 1). | Account login opens `ao codex-login --executable <session-resolved path>`; the same CLI smoke selects the managed fixture and exits 0. |
| An unresolved/blank session executable still allows an account-login terminal to open. | Returns `CODEX_LOGIN_TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE`, removes pending files and the login reservation, and allows a subsequent retry. |

The smoke uses a Node launcher that spawns a deliberately nonexistent native executable. The successful fixture performs no real authentication.

## How

- Inject the existing agent service resolver into the account manager; pass its result through the menu's existing `--executable` option.
- Preserve the private pending `CODEX_HOME` and file credential store.
- Cover both add-account and reauthentication, failure cleanup, and retry. Update the existing terminal-command expectation.

This does not repair a missing native payload, infer a Codex version from its path, or change the general harness-login flow, which already receives a resolved executable.

## Testing

title: docs: clean Markdown exports, add compare links and FAQPage data
body:
Code changes: +347 -19\
Tests: +126 -0\
Others: +32 -12

## What

Docs SEO and GEO wrap-up for docs.orchestrator.inc:

- **Clean Markdown exports.** `llms-full.txt` and all 47 `.md` pages used to contain raw JSX (`<Cards>`, `<Card …/>`, `<Steps>`, `<Accordion …>`, `<Callout …>`, `<InstallDownloads />`, `<PlatformSupport …/>`) and raw HTML (`<span id>` heading anchors, the legacy CLI `<details>/<summary>/<span>/<code>` block). Every element is now written as plain Markdown: cards become `- [title](absolute url): description` lines, steps a numbered list, callouts quotes, accordions a bold question and its answer, the downloads a table of links, `<code>` a code span; layout wrappers and anchors are unwrapped or dropped. Site links (`/quickstart`, `#section`) become absolute `https://docs.orchestrator.inc/…` URLs (files such as `/llms.txt` keep no trailing slash).
- **Guard test.** `src/lib/markdown-export.test.ts` runs every English article through the export options the build uses and fails if the Markdown has a JSX-looking tag (`/<[A-Z][A-Za-z]*[\s/>]/`), an HTML tag, or a site-relative link outside code.
- **Compare links.** `llms.txt` gets an "Orchestrator.inc comparisons" section with `https://orchestrator.inc/compare/` and six comparison pages (each checked to return 200). The intro, installation and FAQ pages link to `/compare/` and `/download/` (5 new inline links, mirrored in the ja and zh-CN translations, whose `translatedFrom` is updated).
- **FAQPage JSON-LD** on `/faq/`, built from the page's own `<Accordion>` questions and answers and rendered in the page's existing JSON-LD graph.

## Why

AI crawlers and answer engines read `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and the `.md` twins. Raw component tags and relative links made those copies hard to use outside the site, and the FAQ had no structured data.

## Before / After

Local build of `main` at the merge base (fc330a79b7) vs this branch, `npm run build` in `frontend/src/docs`, checked by script over every exported file and by hand in the browser:

| Check | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.md` pages exported | 47 | 47 |
| `.md` pages with JSX, HTML or site-relative links (outside code) | 39 | 0 |
| `llms-full.txt` JSX tags outside code | 141 | 0 |
| `llms-full.txt` lines with HTML tags outside code | 54 | 0 |
| `llms-full.txt` site-relative links (`](/…` or `](#…`) | 97 | 0 |
| `grep -c '<[A-Z]' llms-full.txt` | 142 | 1 (`` `# ao-timeout: <N>m` ``, inside inline code) |
| `llms.txt` "Orchestrator.inc comparisons" section | no | yes, 7 compare URLs (all return 200) |
| `/faq/` JSON-LD | TechArticle, WebSite, BreadcrumbList | + FAQPage with 13 questions |
| Links to `orchestrator.inc/compare/` / `/download/` on intro, installation, FAQ | 0 / 1 | 3 / 3 (plus ja and zh-CN intro and installation) |

title: feat(github): sign in to GitHub from AO instead of the gh CLI
body:
Code changes: +1062 -811\
Tests: +533 -587\
Others: +581 -273

## What

AO now signs users in to GitHub itself, with GitHub's device flow, instead of depending on the `gh` CLI.

- On launch, a sign-in window that can't be dismissed blocks the app until GitHub is connected. It shows a code, opens github.com, and ends on a "You're all set" step with the user's avatar.
- Settings → General → GitHub shows the account (avatar or GitHub icon) and a **Disconnect** button. Disconnecting brings the sign-in window back right away when nothing else connects GitHub.
- Agent sessions get the token as `GH_TOKEN` plus a git credential helper for HTTPS pushes, so `gh pr create` and `git push` work without the user setting up git credentials.
- PR tracking, issue reads, `ao doctor`, and "create a GitHub repo" for a local folder all use the same credential.

## Why

Installing and signing in to `gh` was the least reliable onboarding step. When it failed, users could get stuck. Device-flow sign-in needs only a browser: no install, no terminal, no client secret.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Inline "Connect GitHub" card that opened a `gh auth login` terminal, or sent users to install `gh` | Full-screen GitHub sign-in that can't be closed (logo, code, success step with avatar) |
| "Recommended: install gh" in the startup dependency dialog | Removed |
| Creating a GitHub repo for a local folder needed a signed-in `gh` | Daemon creates it through the GitHub API with the AO sign-in |
| No way to see or remove the GitHub account in the app | Settings → General → GitHub, with Disconnect |

Screenshots to add before review: sign-in, code, success, Settings row.

## How

- **Daemon:** `githubpat/device.go` runs the device flow and saves the token in the existing `~/.ao/github-pat.json` (0600).
  - New routes: `POST/GET/DELETE /api/v1/github/login`, `GET /api/v1/github/owners`, `GET /api/v1/github/repository-availability`.
- **Credential order:** one order everywhere: `AO_GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, then AO's sign-in, then `gh auth token`. Existing `gh` users keep working and are never blocked. The sign-in window only offers the AO sign-in.
- **OAuth App:** "Agent Orchestrator", client ID `Ov23lieqORSXeDaVaJ7D`, device flow on, non-expiring tokens.
  - It's an OAuth App, not a GitHub App, so one sign-in covers every repo the user can access, with no per-org install.
  - It's currently owned by @ronishrohan. An org owner should transfer it to the org; the client ID stays the same.
- **Session env:** sessions get `GH_TOKEN`, and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` adds a github.com credential helper after the user's own helpers. A token the user already sets wins, and a `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` the user already sets is left alone.
- **Removed:**
  - the `gh` system requirement and install target
  - `POST /system/github-auth/terminal`
  - `PUT /github/pat`
  - the unused browser OAuth flow that needed a client secret (`provider-auth-flow.ts`)
  - the `gh api` calls in `main.ts`
  - `gh repo create` in the importer
- **Not changed:** the Cloud GitHub App install and the Cloud token field.

**Known gaps (follow-ups):**
- **Remote hosts:** they still need `gh auth login` on the VM. The plan is a device sign-in from the desktop that saves the token on the remote daemon.
- **Disconnect:** it only deletes the local token. The app stays authorized on GitHub until revoked there.
- **Running sessions:** they keep `GH_TOKEN` until restarted.
- **Docs:** the ja/zh-CN install docs and `docs/self-hosted-remote.md` still describe `gh`.
- **Shared avatar sizing:** the product-ui `cn` doesn't know the `size-icon-*` tokens, so callers can't override `UserAvatar`'s size. The Settings row works around it.
- **Branch:** 79 commits behind `main`. It needs a rebase before review.

## Testing

- Desktop lab with an empty `gh` config and scratch data:
  - the sign-in window appears
  - device sign-in completes, with the code approved on github.com
  - the success step and Settings row render
  - the token is stored in the scratch data dir only
- The device-code endpoint returns codes for the client ID.
- Not run yet: Go and frontend unit tests, typecheck, lint. Tests were added or updated for:
  - device login
  - session GitHub env
  - systemcheck
  - importer repo creation
  - the sign-in gate
  - the Settings row

title: feat(chat): restore worktree files when rolling back a turn
body:
Code changes: +1108 -57\
Tests: +1090 -16\
Others: +203 -4 (generated openapi.yaml and schema.ts)

## What

"Roll back to here" in a Chat session now restores the worktree files along with the conversation. Before you confirm, the dialog lists every file that will change (put back, reverted or deleted). When AO can't restore the files, the dialog says why, and the rollback changes only the conversation, as it does today.

## Why

Fixes #7549

`chat.Controller.Rollback` only called the provider's `ChatRollbacker` (Codex `thread/rollback`) and hid AO's turn rows. Nothing ever captured the worktree, so the agent forgot a bad turn while its edits stayed on disk, and the next turn started from code the agent didn't know it wrote.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Confirmation: "The agent will forget this exchange and everything after it … Files it already changed in the worktree are left exactly as they are; only the conversation is rolled back." | Confirmation: "… and the worktree goes back to how it was before it. 2 files will change.", listing `src/farewell.ts` Deleted and `src/greet.ts` Reverted |
| Agent edits `src/greet.ts` and adds `src/farewell.ts` in a turn; rolling that turn back leaves both on disk (`git status`: ` M src/greet.ts`, `?? src/farewell.ts`) | The same rollback leaves `git status` clean: `src/greet.ts` is back to its earlier contents and `src/farewell.ts` is gone |
| `GET …/turns/{turnId}/rollback` → 405 | Returns `{"filesRestorable":true,"files":[{"path":"src/farewell.ts","change":"removed"},{"path":"src/greet.ts","change":"reverted"}],"totalFiles":2,"commitsSince":0,"planId":"…"}` |

## How

**Snapshot before each turn is sent.** `Controller.dispatch` calls `snapshotFiles` just before `SendTurn`. The new `internal/filesnapshot` package records the worktree under `refs/ao/snapshots/<session>/<turn>`, including tracked, staged and untracked files but not ignored ones. It writes a commit shaped like git stash's: the tree is the worktree, parent 1 is HEAD, and parent 2's tree is the index. It works through a temp copy of the index (mtime kept, so git's stat cache and racy-file check still apply), so the branch, the real index and the stash are never touched. Snapshotting at dispatch rather than at settle means "roll back to here" lands on the exact state that turn started from, including edits the user made between turns. Only drivers that implement `ChatRollbacker` pay for it, and only for session-owned conversations. A turn whose untracked files pass 5,000 files, 50 MiB for one file or 200 MiB in total isn't snapshotted, so large generated output never holds up the turn or piles up in the object store. A failure, a skipped snapshot or a run past the 10s budget never blocks the turn; that turn just can't restore files.

**Rollback order: files, then provider, then rows.** With `{"restoreFiles": true, "planId": "<from the preview>"}`, the controller plans the restore again and refuses with 409 `CHAT_ROLLBACK_FILES_CHANGED` if the plan no longer matches the preview (`planId` hashes the snapshot, HEAD and the current worktree and index), so nothing the user wasn't shown is overwritten. It then saves the current worktree and index under `refs/ao/snapshots/<session>/before-rollback/<turn>` (shaped like a stash, so `git stash apply <ref>` brings them back), writes the files and index entries for the changed paths only, and then calls the provider. If the provider refuses, `Restore.Undo` puts the files back, so nothing changes. That's the only order that can be undone, since a provider rollback can't be reversed. Commits made after the turn stay on the branch, as the issue's "restore files only and leave commits alone" option and t3code both do. Their changes come back as uncommitted edits, and the dialog says how many commits that covers.

**Honest refusals.** `filesnapshot` refuses, with a reason the dialog shows, when the workspace isn't the root of its own git repo (so a scratch dir under a git-tracked home is never snapshotted as that repo), when there's no snapshot for the turn (turns sent before this change), and when the worktree or the snapshot holds another repository (workspace-project child repos, submodules, or a repo the turn cloned in), whether or not it changed. Git records such a repository only as its checked-out commit, so a restore would silently skip edits inside it.

**Compatibility.** The POST body is optional and `restoreFiles` defaults to false. Mobile and older desktops keep the conversation-only rollback their copy already promises. A new desktop talking to an older daemon gets an error from the preview route and falls back to that same copy and behaviour. Snapshot refs are deleted when the session's worktree is destroyed (`gitworktree.DestroyReclaim`), and kept when teardown is refused for a dirty worktree. Each snapshot commit records the worktree it was taken in, so creating or destroying any worktree also deletes the snapshots of sessions whose worktree is no longer registered, however those sessions ended.

Rejected: snapshotting after a turn settles (needs a separate baseline, and misses edits made between turns); `git clean -fd` + `git restore .` like t3code (touches every path and resets the whole index); moving the branch back past commits (rewrites history the user may have pushed).

Intentional omissions: mobile keeps its conversation-only rollback for now (it sends no body, so its "Files stay changed" copy stays true). Snapshot refs of turns discarded by a rollback, and the before-rollback refs, stay until the session's worktree is gone.

## Testing

Reproduced on `main` first: a Chat rollback left the turn's edits in the worktree.

- `internal/filesnapshot`: real-git tests for restoring worktree plus index (staged and untracked files, ignored output left alone, empty directories pruned), Undo, file↔directory swaps, capture leaving HEAD/index/stash untouched, commits made after the snapshot left on the branch, nested and child repositories refused (including an uncommitted edit inside a committed submodule), the before-rollback save restorable with `git stash apply`, a plan id that changes when files are edited or staged, oversized untracked files skipped (ignored output not counted), per-session ref deletion across linked worktrees, and orphaned sessions' refs deleted while others are kept.
- `service/chat`: a two-turn rollback restores to the start of the rolled-back turn; a provider refusal puts files back and keeps the turn; no snapshot means a refusal before the provider is called; a conversation-only rollback leaves files; a file edited after the preview refuses the rollback before the provider is called; the overwritten files are kept under the before-rollback ref; agents that can't roll back get no snapshot refs.
- `httpd/controllers`: preview route (cap at 200, kinds, reason), optional body, `planId` required with `restoreFiles`, `CHAT_ROLLBACK_FILES_UNAVAILABLE`, `CHAT_ROLLBACK_FILES_CHANGED`. `gitworktree`: destroy deletes only that session's refs and keeps them on a refused teardown; creating a worktree deletes the refs of a session whose worktree was removed outside AO.
- Vitest: the dialog lists files and stays disabled until the preview answers, explains why files can't be restored, falls back when the preview fails, sends the preview's `planId` only when files were listed, and reopens with a fresh list when the daemon answers `CHAT_ROLLBACK_FILES_CHANGED`. The hook sends the body and reads the preview.
- Revert check: removing the snapshot call, the undo-on-refusal, the index restore, the nested-repo guard, the root-of-repo guard, directory pruning, the destroy cleanup, the submodule refusal, the plan check, the before-rollback save, the size limit, the orphan sweep on create, or the dialog's reopen each fails its test; the new dialog tests fail against `main`'s `ChatWorkspace.tsx`.
- Real app: an isolated dev instance of this branch (own `AO_PORT`, run file, Electron profile and data dir) with a real Codex chat session. Codex edited `src/greet.ts` and created `src/farewell.ts`. The preview listed both, and "Roll back to here" in the native window showed them. After confirming, the timeline said "1 turn was rolled back" and `git status` in the worktree was clean. The "before" dialog was captured in the same window with `main`'s `ChatWorkspace.tsx`. This run predates the review fixes and was not repeated for them.
- Cost: on a 5,584-file checkout of this repo, a snapshot took about 150 ms and a preview about 160 ms, measured while other test suites were running.

Commands: `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, golangci-lint v2.13.2 (0 issues), `go test -race ./internal/service/chat` (CI's chat-race job), the backend-core package set with `-race`, the CI Destroy/Kill race job, `npm run api` (no drift), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, vitest on `src/renderer` and `src/shared` (497 files, 8363 tests), and the renderer smoke suite (`@T0|@P0`) on installed Chrome: 142 of 143 passed. The one failure, `cloud-model-catalog.spec.ts` "failed keeps safe choices", passes on its own on both this branch and `main` (6/6), so it was flaky under load.

For the review fixes: `gofmt`, `go vet ./internal/...`, golangci-lint v2.13.2 on the touched packages (0 issues), `go test` for `filesnapshot`, `gitworktree` and `httpd/controllers`, the chat rollback tests with `-race`, `npm run api` (only the two `planId` fields changed), `npm run typecheck`, and vitest on the three touched test files (102 tests). The full `-race` chat suite and the renderer smoke suite were not rerun.

Not green locally, and not caused by this change: `internal/service/shellterm` `TestCueCommandCanBeRecalledFromInteractiveHistory` and `TestCueCommandPreservesDataInInteractiveShell` fail identically on a clean `upstream/main` export on this Mac (local shell setup). Not run locally: Docker-based cli-e2e and gitleaks, Windows/Linux runners, and Node 24 (local Node is 22.23).

title: fix(chat): prevent vertical jumps during sidebar animations
body:
Code changes: +59 -7  
Tests: +56 -5  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keep the chat's scroll position stable while the project sidebar or inspector animates open and closed. Preserve the latest-message position when following, or the visible turn's offset when reading older messages.

## Why

Sidebar width changes rewrap transcript rows. Virtualizer scroll compensation can run before the resized rows reach the DOM, and chat can then treat that reflow as incoming-message growth and animate back to the end. During diagnosis, a 40-turn renderer fixture moved vertically by 69px while opening the inspector.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Opening or closing either sidebar can make chat move vertically and then return during the animation. | Capture the scroll anchor before remeasurement and restore it after the updated row positions reach the DOM. The requester confirmed the isolated desktop build resolved the visible glitch. |
| Reading older messages relies on virtualizer compensation that can precede the updated row positions. | Restore the captured turn offset after layout instead of writing against stale positions. |

No new before/after recording was captured: the requester asked to stop local tests and checks. Animation evidence is therefore incomplete. An earlier desktop screenshot is available locally at `/tmp/ao-chat-sidebar-before.png`; it is not committed or attached.

## How

- Detect viewport geometry changes before virtual row remeasurement.
- Save anchors by stable turn key so history prepends cannot redirect the resize correction to another turn.
- Hold virtualizer scroll writes until resized rows are committed, then restore the viewport in a dedicated layout effect. Keep initial rendering and ordinary content layout in their existing passive effect.
- Settle resize corrections immediately; retain smooth following for conversation growth. Resizing can settle an active smooth scroll immediately, and text still rewraps naturally.
- Add renderer-CI-tagged browser regression cases for the latest prompt and an older visible turn during all four sidebar toggles, using a virtualized 40-turn conversation. Capture the baseline before dispatching the toggle and assert that the viewport width actually changes.

## Testing

- The requester manually confirmed the fix in the isolated Electron dev app on this branch.
