title: perf: open session terminals instantly; remove /terminals page
body:
Code changes: +336 -317\
Tests: +285 -119\
Others: +15 -66 (generated OpenAPI/schema/route tree, i18n key removals, Windows CI step)

## What

- Removes the standalone `/terminals` page. Terminals only live in a session's tab strip; ⌘T outside a session does nothing.
- Starts the shell as soon as the terminal is created instead of after the tab attaches, so a new terminal shows its prompt sooner. This is the main user-facing change.
- Removes CSS `:has()` rules that restyled the whole app on every terminal repaint. This was the cause of 100–300 ms freezes per ⌘T in the dev app; the packaged app on `main` does not show noticeable lag, so in production this is headroom for heavy pages rather than a visible fix.

## Why

A new terminal's prompt took noticeably longer to appear than in a native terminal: the shell only started after the tab mounted xterm, attached, and reported its size. Opening several terminals in a session was also visibly laggy in the dev app.

Profiling the dev app showed the freezes were full-document style recalcs: every xterm DOM-renderer row update (xterm uses the DOM renderer when window translucency is on) restyled ~2,000 elements at ~15 ms each, 10–20 times per press. The cause was CSS `:has()` rules anchored on big containers (`body`, `#root`, `.session-split`, `.center-panel-shell`) plus two Tailwind `group-has-*` variants with attribute arguments: any DOM change under those containers made Chromium invalidate their whole subtree.

## Before / After

Measured in the dev Electron app, same session and window, 5 presses per run. The style/freeze rows are dev-mode numbers: a packaged build of `main` was checked by hand and did not feel laggy, but was not profiled. The PR's packaged build measured 13–27 ms per ⌘T.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘T → tab painted: 100–300+ ms | 20–52 ms |
| Style + layout work per press: ~294 ms (14+ full-document recalcs) | ~23 ms |
| Main-thread long tasks per press: 2–5, of 60–400 ms | 0–1, of ~55 ms |
| ⌘T → first prompt bytes: 300–385 ms | 257–287 ms (native `zsh -il` startup is ~160 ms on the same machine) |
| `/terminals` page reachable from ⌘T on the board and the + button | Page removed; terminals open only inside a session |
| A shell left open on the old page is restored on every launch | Session-less shells are reaped on the next launch (nothing can show them); session shells are preserved as before |

## How

- **`:has()` → attributes.** New `useDocumentFlag` / `useAncestorFlag` (`hooks/useElementFlag.ts`) publish state that CSS used to detect with `:has()`: live native browser page, browser popout open, shell platform, inspector expanded (on `.session-split`), startup screen (on `.app-shell-root`). An attribute toggles one restyle per state change instead of one per DOM mutation.
- **Tailwind `group-has-*`** in `TerminalTabFrame` and `ui/sidebar.tsx` rewritten as arbitrary variants with child combinators; two settings-page rules (`keyboard-shortcuts.css`, harness) rewritten without a `div:has(...) > *` subject.
- **Hidden chat panel**: `HoldWhileHidden` skips parent re-renders of the conversation panel while a terminal/reviewer tab covers it; it renders with fresh props when shown again.
- **Forced layout**: xterm's fit stabilizer proposes grids from the ResizeObserver box instead of `FitAddon.proposeDimensions()` on every repaint; tab-strip `scrollIntoView` moves to the next frame.
- **Session-less shells**: `ReapShellTerminalsFromPreviousAppRuns` destroys durable shells with no session from previous launches, even when alive, since no client can show or close them. Session shells keep the preserve-while-alive-or-uncertain rule.
- **Early shell start**: `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` accepts `cols`/`rows`. When both are set the pty-host spawns immediately at that grid (`--size=COLSxROWS`), taking precedence over `startOnAttach`. The renderer sends the grid the session pane last showed (`lib/terminal-grid-hint.ts`), saved in localStorage so the first terminals after a relaunch start early too; a stale grid is corrected when the tab attaches. With no hint yet (first terminal ever), or against an older daemon, it falls back to start-on-attach.

Review focus: the CSS rewrites in `styles.css` should match the same elements as before, now scoped by attributes on `<html>` rather than by containment.

## Testing

- Measured in the real desktop app (`npm run dev`, isolated data) with CDP traces: style-recalc counts and element counts per press, click → paint latency, websocket timing for attach and first output.
- Confirmed the early-started shell spawns at the pane's width (`--size=146x35` vs attach at 146×37) and the first prompt renders without zsh's stray `%`.
- Added tests: grid hint persistence across launches (including corrupt and blocked storage), `--size` pty-host argument round trip, client-grid start and out-of-range grid in the shell service, and the document/ancestor flag hooks.
- **CSS equivalence in the live app:** each replaced `:has()` selector was evaluated next to its replacement with `querySelectorAll`, and matched the same elements in every state: inspector open; live browser page docked, maximized, and restored; simulated Windows and Linux platform with the popout open; session tab menu open (the tab icon hides); Settings › Harness, with sibling probes; and Settings › Shortcuts. The in-shell startup loader was shown for real by holding the `/system/requirements` probe: old and new selectors matched the same `.app-shell-root`, which computed to `visibility: hidden` with the loader `visible`, and both reverted once the probe answered.
- **Relaunch reaping:** created one session-less shell and one session shell, hard-killed Electron and the daemon so the detached pty-hosts survived, then relaunched. The log showed `reaped shell terminals from previous app runs count=1`; only the session shell's pty-host remained, and it was still listed.
- **Behavior:** the terminal grid fills its pane within one cell after resizes made while visible and while hidden behind chat. The chat panel catches up after being covered and its composer accepts input. `#/terminals` renders the router's Not Found, and navigating back works. No console errors throughout.
- **Windows `--size`:** the `conpty` package never ran on Windows CI, so `windows-workspace` gains a step running `TestConPTYStartsAtRequestedGrid` (a real ConPTY started through `hostStartGrid` at 146x37 reports exactly that in `mode con`) plus the start-grid and argument tests. It passes.
- **Production CSS:** built the renderer with `vite build --mode production` (the config Forge packages). Its compiled CSS contains none of the nine replaced `:has()` forms and all ten replacements. With the dev stylesheets disabled and only that CSS applied in the running app, a DOM change costs 0.46 ms (0.42 ms with every `:has()` rule removed), and a real ⌘T press ran 187 style recalcs, none touching more than half of the 2,540 elements, for 15 ms in total. The selector comparison and the startup-loader check repeated with that CSS give the same results.
- **Packaged app (`npm run package`):** the renderer CSS inside `app.asar` is byte-identical to the production build tested above, apart from asset URL base paths (`./` instead of `/assets/`). The packaged daemon binary (built from this branch's head), run headless in an isolated HOME and data dir: `cols`/`rows` reach `pty-host --size=146x37`, a request with an unknown field is accepted, and after a SIGKILL crash and a restart as a new app run it logs `reaped shell terminals from previous app runs count=1`, with the session-less shell's pty-host gone. The packaged app was then launched from a scratch `Applications` folder, so relocation chose "stay". It ran with a scratch HOME, `--use-mock-keychain`, and isolated data, and the system `ao-app://` handler was restored afterwards. In the launched app (production bundle, `app://` renderer, real preload), ⌘T paints in 13–27 ms, a press does 5 ms of style work with no full-document recalc, and terminals fit after visible and hidden resizes. The selector comparison matches in the default, inspector, live-browser, maximized, restored, tab-menu and real in-shell-loader states, and `#/terminals` renders Not Found. After force-killing the app and daemon and relaunching, the session-less shell's pty-host was reaped and the session shell survived and stayed listed. This PR changes no main-process, preload, shared or Forge files.
- **Production JS:** the production renderer bundle was loaded into the real Electron window (preload bridge present, no Vite client), and the checks were re-run against it. ⌘T paints in 17–24 ms, a press does no full-document recalc (16 ms of style work), the terminal fits its pane after visible and hidden resizes, the chat panel and composer work, the tab icon hides with its menu open, and the selector comparison matches in the inspector, live-browser, maximized and restored states. The only console error is a pre-existing `index.html` font preload 404 that this PR does not touch.
- **Windows, repeated:** the `windows-workspace` step runs with `-v -count=3`; every listed test, including `TestConPTYStartsAtRequestedGrid` and all four `TestHostStartGrid` cases, shows `--- PASS` three times.
- **Older daemons:** a create request with an unknown field returns 201, so a remote daemon that predates `cols`/`rows` ignores them and keeps start-on-attach.
- **Packaged PR build vs installed nightly, by hand:** the PR build opens terminals and shows the prompt noticeably faster. The nightly showed no ⌘T lag either, consistent with the freezes being dev-mode amplified.
- Tests and typecheck were not run locally; CI is green (30/30, including Windows and Linux jobs).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat: import local GitHub Copilot chats
body:
Code changes: +421 -5\
Tests: +589 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Import local GitHub Copilot CLI conversations as AO chats that continue through Copilot's existing ACP `session/load` path. Stacked on #6364 (`codex/session-import-build`), pinned initially to `37d504450bab2bb37ef01773c11526da37135e9a`.

## Why

Copilot's CLI and ACP server share the same UUID-addressed native event store. Its verified cross-directory resume path lets AO continue those conversations without relocating the native history.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Copilot histories are absent from the session-import scan and Copilot has no Import tab. | Scan reads top-level `session-state/<uuid>/events.jsonl` under `COPILOT_HOME` or `~/.copilot`; the existing import controls are enabled for Copilot. |
| A local Copilot conversation cannot be adopted as a continuing AO chat. | Import stores its original UUID and provider home, refreshes the archive before first open, and resumes through the existing ACP driver from the AO workspace. |
| Native event files contain tool traffic, model snapshots and injected context alongside chat text. | Imported history shows typed user and assistant text, applies explicit clears/rewinds, and keeps the opening/newest text when the display budget is exceeded. |

The existing UI layout and strings are reused. Real-app before/after capture and full desktop import/open/continue verification remain unperformed under this session's CI-only implementation-validation scope.

## How

- Discover only immediate UUID session directories; read the bounded optional `workspace.yaml` name/cwd metadata and validate its identity when present. Confine native reads to the selected provider home.
- Parse visible timeline events and ignore transformed model inputs, streamed deltas, system/tool/model events, reasoning, injected source messages and subagent responses. Retain original native IDs and timestamps; deduplicate repeated events.
- Add native-home resolution, native-session availability probing and transcript location using existing ports. Reuse the protected imported-config environment path for `COPILOT_HOME`; do not change `HOME`, copy credentials or relocate native event logs.
- Treat a positively identified writable Copilot transcript descriptor as open-elsewhere evidence. Idle clients are not reliably detectable; no exclusive-ownership guarantee is claimed.
- Keep Agy and OpenCode v2 deferred; no shared relocation contract, storage schema or dependency changes.

## Testing

- Added synthetic backend regressions for discovery, identity validation, transcript/sidecar confinement, visible-event filtering, clear/rewind behavior, bounds, custom/default roots, archive refresh, native UUID preservation, duplicate imports, cancellation, source-home routing and positive writable-descriptor detection.
- Added frontend regressions for signed-in Copilot import offers, harness filtering and selected import requests.
- Source/diff inspection and `git diff --cached --check` completed. No local project builds, tests, formatters, generators, installs or hooks were run; Actions validation is pending for this PR head.
- Prior installed-runtime evidence (Copilot CLI 1.0.105): created a throwaway CLI conversation in folder A using isolated `COPILOT_HOME`, loaded the same UUID from folder B over ACP without copying, replayed two message chunks, recalled a marker, appended another turn, reopened and recalled both markers. The native event log grew; scratch and child processes were removed. `HOME` and existing credentials/configuration were not copied or changed. This verifies the provider resume path, not this new Go/UI implementation or a full desktop import flow. No new live runtime launches were performed for this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing the explicitly requested #6364 stack on a separate branch
- [x] One focused Copilot import change
- [x] Before / After behavior documented; real-app capture gap disclosed
- [x] Regression coverage added
- [ ] Exact-head Actions checks pass
- [ ] Full desktop import/open/continue verification (outside current validation scope)


## Live tool-folder check (user-authorized, 2026-11-03)
Copilot CLI 1.0.105 ships as a compiled binary, so its source can't show where a resumed chat's tools run. I ran one live check instead, using the same launch AO uses (`copilot --acp --no-auto-update`):
1. `session/new` with `cwd` = throwaway folder A, which contains `MARKER_A.txt`.
2. In a new process, `session/load` of that exact session id with `cwd` = folder B, which contains `MARKER_B.txt`. `loadSession: true`; the same id was resumed.
3. I asked it to run `pwd && ls`. The shell tool returned `/private/tmp/…/B` and `MARKER_B.txt`.

**Result: the resumed chat's tools run in the folder AO passes in (the worktree), not the folder the chat was created in.** Afterwards I deleted the throwaway session's state and both folders. No references to it remain in `session-store.db`. No other sessions or settings were touched.

title: fix(chat): keep a crashed turn's failure when resume replays it as interrupted
body:
Code changes: +6 -0\
Tests: +22 -0\
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #5289

## Summary

When a chat host dies mid-turn, AO marks the turn `failed` with the reason `controller ended before the turn completed`. On resume, Codex replays that turn from history as `interrupted` with no error. That replay overwrote the failure, so the timeline said **"The agent was interrupted by you"** about a turn nobody stopped, and the reason and Retry were gone.

`SettleTurnWithFailureCode` now ignores an empty `interrupted` replay when the turn is already `failed` with a reason. A real Stop is unaffected, because that turn is still running when it settles.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| State after resume | `interrupted` | `failed` |
| Stored reason | empty | `controller ended before the turn completed` |
| Timeline | "The agent was interrupted by you" | "The agent ran into a problem" with the reason and Retry |
| Real user Stop | "The agent was interrupted by you" | unchanged |

## Evidence

Both runs used the real `codex` 0.164.0 binary and the real desktop app, with no fake provider. Each build had its own disposable data directory, and "before" is main with the store fix removed.

1. Point Codex's API at a closed local port, so the turn stays in progress retrying. Nothing reached a provider.
2. Send a message and wait for the turn to run.
3. `kill -9` the session's chat host.
4. Let the desktop app reconnect the session, which replays the thread.

The explicit `resume-agent` call in the transcripts returns 409 because the app had already reconnected.

**Before (main):**

```
== after crash
DB    conversation_turns: (..., 'failed', "'controller ended before the turn completed'")

== after resume
DB    conversation_turns: (..., 'interrupted', "''")
EVENT turn.completed|interrupted|...codex-history...
UI    turn outcome: ["interrupted: The agent was interrupted by you | Worked for | 9s"]
```

![before: the crashed turn says it was interrupted by you](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c1daf446d644040e639ff8060829716c706e0d1d/pr-5289/before-resumed.png)

**After (this PR):** the same replay event arrives, and the failure stays.

```
== after resume
DB    conversation_turns: (..., 'failed', "'controller ended before the turn completed'")
EVENT turn.completed|interrupted|...codex-history...
UI    turn outcome: ["failed: The agent ran into a problem | controller ended before the turn completed | Retry | Worked for | 9s"]
```

![after: the crashed turn shows the reason and Retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c1daf446d644040e639ff8060829716c706e0d1d/pr-5289/after-resumed.png)

**Regression check (this PR):** a second turn stopped through the app's interrupt endpoint still reads as interrupted, and the crashed turn above it keeps its reason.

![after: a real Stop still says interrupted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/c1daf446d644040e639ff8060829716c706e0d1d/pr-5289/after-user-stop.png)

Full transcripts: [before.txt](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c1daf446d644040e639ff8060829716c706e0d1d/pr-5289/before.txt), [after.txt](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/c1daf446d644040e639ff8060829716c706e0d1d/pr-5289/after.txt).

## Tests

`TestSettleTurnInterruptedReplayKeepsStoredFailure` covers the store fix. CI is the test gate; I did not run the Go suite locally.

## Scope changes

- Removed the earlier Codex change. Codex 0.164 attaches the error to every live failed completion, so that change handled a sequence it does not send. It was only ever exercised by a simulated provider, and that evidence is gone from this PR.
- Moved the ACP stop-reason gap to #7775, because it has not been reproduced with a real agent.

## Risks

- The fix is in the shared store, so it applies to every provider, not just Codex. Only Codex was tested end to end.
- A user Stop that races a host crash now shows the crash reason rather than "interrupted", because AO records the crash first.
- `controller ended before the turn completed` is technical wording. This PR does not change it.

title: fix: open artifact files with ao preview and add Open in AO Browser for HTML
body:
## Summary

Agents must save deliverables in the session artifact directory (`~/.ao/data/artifacts/<session>/`), outside the workspace, and the prompt tells them to open the main one with `ao preview`. The daemon resolved absolute paths only inside the workspace, so each of those calls failed with `403 PREVIEW_FILE_OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE` and the Browser panel stayed empty. A user reported this as "opening HTML and Markdown files in the side panel got much worse in a recent release". The two rules have conflicted since #4805, and #7162 made the artifact rule stricter.

The same user also wanted to open a page from the thread in the Browser panel without asking the agent. This PR adds one **Open in AO Browser** action wherever AO shows HTML. Other files keep opening in Files.

## Change

### `ao preview` accepts artifact files (daemon)
- An absolute path or `file://` URL that resolves inside the session artifact directory now opens on the existing artifact preview origin (`ao-preview-artifact.<id>.localhost`), which serves from `ArtifactDir`. Artifact cards already use this origin for HTML artifacts.
- Workspace files keep the workspace origin; the workspace is checked first.
- Symlinks are still resolved before the containment check, so a link that escapes the artifact directory is still rejected with 403.
- The `preview.md` guide and `ao preview --help` describe artifact paths, and the 403 message names both roots.

### Open in AO Browser for HTML (desktop)
The same globe button and label (**Open in AO Browser**) appear in each place AO shows HTML:

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Files viewer, workspace `.html` | source only | button in the toolbar, where Markdown has Rich preview |
| Artifacts tab, HTML artifact | Rich preview, View source | + button; opens the same URL `ao preview <artifact path>` stores |
| Inline `ao render` page in chat | Wrap, Expand | + button on hover and in the expanded dialog; opens a new Browser tab with the render's `sandbox` CSP |

- Chat link clicks keep main's rule: a workspace `.html` link opens in the Browser panel, every other file opens in Files (#5119). Right-click still offers both.
- The Files button is shown only for the live workspace file, not for a commit or a deleted file. The Artifacts button is hidden for cloud sessions and old versions. All three are hidden for remote hosts and inactive sessions.

## Evidence

### `ao preview` of an artifact file
One isolated desktop lab: same data dir, same Claude Code chat session, same artifact files. Only the daemon binary was swapped. The agent was asked to run `ao preview ~/.ao/dev/preview-artifacts-lab/data/artifacts/standalone-2/release-summary.html`.

| | main (`2aeaaa3ee9`) | this branch (`bcb860aa52`) |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /sessions/standalone-2/preview` | 403 `PREVIEW_FILE_OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE` | 200 |
| Browser panel | empty | renders `release-summary.html` |

**After:** the same request in the same thread opens the page in the Browser panel.

![After: the HTML artifact renders in the Browser panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/931b68f5927c93b688e5bc4d0519973e97b1cd27/after-fix-html.png)

**After, Markdown:** `ao preview .../notes.md` renders the Markdown artifact.

![After: the Markdown artifact renders in the Browser panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/931b68f5927c93b688e5bc4d0519973e97b1cd27/after-fix-markdown.png)

### Open in AO Browser
Same lab and session, daemon from this branch. "Before" swaps only the changed frontend files back to the PR base; "after" is `1d55fcd798`.

**Files viewer, before:** a workspace `reports/index.html` shows its source and no way to see the page.

**Artifacts tab, before:** Rich preview and View source only.

**Artifacts tab, after:** the same button sits next to them…

…and opens the artifact on its preview origin in the Browser panel.

| 04 | Click `assets/diagram.svg` | Files | [04](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/acc196d73178317f57a0a458dcee9e1074585885/scenarios/04-svg-link-files.png) |

title: feat(chat): name senders from outside AO instead of drawing an automation card
body: ## Problem A message sent with `ao send` from a terminal, or by a tool calling `POST /sessions/{id}/send`, was stored like AO's own nudges: origin `automation`, no sender. The timeline could not tell the two apart. So any text it did not recognize, such as a lab driver's `ao send standalone-1 --message "Run exactly this one shell command…"`, drew as the generic "automation" card. #7337 handled only senders that put a `[via NAME]` prefix in their text. ## Change - **Send API:** `SendSessionMessageRequest` takes an optional `senderName`. It is kept as one line of at most 60 characters, and it is ignored when `senderSessionId` is set, because an AO session's own name wins. - **Relay:** the name travels in `MessageDeliveryOptions.SenderName` and is stored in the message's existing `sender_display_name` column, on both the live and the queued (hibernated) paths. No migration. - **CLI:** `ao send` run outside a session sends `senderName: "ao send"`. Inside a session, nothing changes. - **Timeline:** a message with a sender name and no AO session draws the way #7337 draws a `[via …]` message: a bot mark, the name and time, then the text. The `[via …]` prefix still names senders that don't pass the field. AO's own messages are unchanged: - The app's buttons (file feedback, diff selection, git actions, browser notes) send no `senderName`. - Lifecycle nudges never pass through this endpoint. ## Screenshots The desktop app built from this branch, run against a sandboxed copy of real data. Each message was sent with `ao send --session --message …` from a terminal outside any session: - **Before:** the installed nightly's CLI, 0.14.9-nightly.202611011830. - **After:** this branch's CLI. The stored rows show the difference: `sender_display_name` is empty for the first and `ao send` for the second. | Before (nightly CLI) | After (this branch) | |---|---| | | | ## Tests - `sessions_test.go`: the name is flattened to one line, and dropped when an AO session is the sender. - `hibernate_test.go`: a queued relay keeps the outside sender's name. - `send_test.go`: `ao send` names itself only outside a session. - `ChatWorkspaceWorkerUpdates.test.tsx`: a named message draws as the sender's row, not the card. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat: import Terminal sessions with Gemini pilot
body:
Code changes: +1592 -110  
Tests: +1767 -31  
Others: +9 -0  

## What

Extend #6364 with native Terminal session import, the Gemini pilot, and append-only per-harness registration and preparation seams. Current head: `28cb5a7da562b1c355a299e3fc485c0562dbef03`. This branch retains the original base `37d504450bab2bb37ef01773c11526da37135e9a` and normally merges the completed Chat roll-up and repair base `22605049426b939c712885cd2754e4badc836208`.

## Why

Imports previously selected Chat unconditionally. Terminal-only harnesses need their native conversation restored in the AO worktree, with exact identity, provider-root and launch-generation checks. A failed first open must retry its prepared native context without replacing the visible archive with newer turns from the original.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Every import selected Chat. | Driver capability and optional per-importer override select Terminal when appropriate. |
| Terminal-only histories could not be offered or opened. | Gemini is eligible; pending imports show a readable archive and require native restore to open. |
| Native preparation assumed one immutable provider ID. | First open checkpoints the prepared native ID/root/cwd/transcript separately from immutable source provenance; proven forks can adopt a new ID atomically. |
| A failed launch could refresh its archive from an original that had advanced beyond the private copy. | A checkpointed import retains the archive paired with its prepared native history. |
| Source removal after native-copy publication but before checkpoint persistence blocked recovery. | Fingerprinted S2 preparers can verify their durable private-copy proof before original-source refresh and recover the exact target. |
| Preparation and runtime could resolve different launch overrides. | Pending imports resolve account/project launch env once, pass a clone to preparation, and reuse the result at launch. |
| Repo-local and CLI-listed native histories lacked discovery inputs. | Registered project roots and bounded read-only list commands are available to separate harness consumers. |

The archive is a pending history surface, not a transcript fallback or read-only harness mode. No screenshots or app runtime proof were captured: local execution is prohibited by task scope.

## How

- Inject Chat capability from the driver registry; keep per-harness discovery/parser/native-ID/config/ownership registrations immutable after initialization. Sibling harness PRs stack on these seams; this PR registers Gemini only.
- **S1:** supply explicitly registered project/repository paths, exclude HOME/AO data roots and their unsafe ancestors, and confine reads to each source root. Global stores can use this inventory for legacy metadata resolution; no home scan.
- **S2:** optional native preparation returns an exact ID/root/transcript ref. Persist resume facts before launch, preserve source dedup provenance, reuse checkpoints on retry, and atomically bind observed fork identities to the exact runtime generation. Locate the adopted transcript and clear stale prepared-path bindings.
- Persist optional exact source fingerprints from scan. Validate before/after the import-time source read; pass the fingerprint through existing native preparation/relocation. Provider consumers must compare exact content, including sidecars, before snapshot/publication. Unset consumers retain existing behavior.
- **Recovery ordering:** only fingerprinted `AgentImportedSessionPreparer` consumers defer common original refresh until after S2. An original availability probe is deferred only for an already prepared AO workspace that exists on disk and has no resume checkpoint. The adapter must verify private provenance against the selection fingerprint or validate the selected source before copying. Errors refuse launch. Successful preparation checkpoints before refresh; both manager and service then retain the pinned archive. Non-S2 and unfingerprinted source validation remains in its existing order. No new validator/recovery interface or blanket source-validation bypass.
- Pass optional `ImportedSessionRelocation.Env` as a read-only clone of once-resolved launch overrides. Preserve present-empty clears and absent-key inheritance. Reuse the result at launch, reapply a returned native root, and bind the retained Chat capability verifier under the controller gate without issuing/resolving again. Never persist/log the map; redact adapter preparation errors. Non-import ordering and fields remain unchanged.
- Carry existing source/resume/config metadata keys into strict preflight and ordinary/interactive restore for matching pending/adopted imports. Optional workspace-hook native ID/mode/import-root fields identify exact restore context; fresh launches leave them empty. Imported non-reconnect Chat restores run those hooks after relocation and before ACP startup.
- **S3:** CLI-listed discovery has a 10-second deadline, 8 MiB stdout/64 KiB stderr bounds and process-tree cancellation. Metadata-only native Terminal records contain no fabricated messages; Chat retains its readable-history requirement.
- **S4:** use current rendered-terminal evidence and exact-launch fences, rechecking readiness and unchanged input before answering. Empty initialization input sends no user task. Fork takeover requires explicit adapter opt-in and exact source/target proof; ordinary restore identity remains fixed.
- Admit only unadopted, never-launched idle Terminal imports through the first-open guard. Ordinary/adopted idle sessions and imports with runtime bindings retain normal exited-session checks. Prepared interactive retries preserve exact identity binding; strict native history and no-fresh-fallback behavior remain.
- Keep Chat writes mode-gated. Pending Terminal archives permit read-only snapshot calls without a Chat composer; Terminal adoption does not create a Chat controller or read a Chat replay boundary. Locale catalogs include the Terminal archive notice.
- Gemini legacy hash directories resolve only against registered project paths when modern metadata is absent. Windows registry/marker comparisons use provider path normalization and preserve existing slugs.

- Gemini: `GEMINI_CLI_HOME/.gemini`, default `~/.gemini`; `tmp/<project>/chats/session-*.json{,l}`. Read legacy JSON and current JSONL messages/patches/rewinds; resolve cwd from `.project_root` or `projects.json`. The native ID is the full `sessionId`, not the abbreviated filename suffix. Restore argv remains `gemini --skip-trust [permission/model flags] --resume <id>`. Gemini looks up the session within the launch project, so first open copies only that file, preserves its basename and native ID, rewrites project hashes, and uses a destination ownership marker. The source file and provider registry are never changed by the copy. Copy uses private temporary file + rename and preserves an existing copy on retries. Symlinked Terminal launch cwd is resolved, matching CLI `getcwd`.
- Ownership limitation: Gemini has no reliable per-conversation lock/registry in the inspected source. Writable-transcript process evidence is best-effort and cannot catch append/open/close writers reliably. No provider takeover or termination is attempted.

Primary provider source: [Gemini recording](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.ts), [Gemini selector](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/cli/src/utils/sessionUtils.ts), [Gemini project registry](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/config/projectRegistry.ts), [Goose paths](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/main/crates/goose/src/config/paths.rs), [Goose session storage](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/main/crates/goose/src/session/session_manager.rs), [Goose resume/cwd handling](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/main/crates/goose-cli/src/session/builder.rs).

## Deferred

Droid, OpenCode v1 and Kimi remain excluded by the authoritative #6364 source-safety deferrals. Continue is dropped: its only exact-ID route forks again on every reopen, outside first-open S2; no unsafe newest-session resume is enabled. Memcode/Aider are separate Phase 3 S1 consumers.

Goose is dropped by the Phase 3 agent/tools worktree gate, even with the precisely recognized no-answer prompt route. At provider `cfb67d72f6129ba3c9f68d4c225d8dfcaba18a87`, [builder.rs:499](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/cfb67d72f6129ba3c9f68d4c225d8dfcaba18a87/crates/goose-cli/src/session/builder.rs#L499) only changes process cwd on yes, and resume at line 723 leaves the saved working_dir intact. [extension_manager/mod.rs:809](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/cfb67d72f6129ba3c9f68d4c225d8dfcaba18a87/crates/goose/src/agents/extension_manager/mod.rs#L809) reloads that saved session and line 867 binds the extension set to its working_dir. [lease.rs:703](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/cfb67d72f6129ba3c9f68d4c225d8dfcaba18a87/crates/goose/src/agents/extension_manager/lease.rs#L703) passes it into ToolCallContext; [developer/mod.rs:211](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/cfb67d72f6129ba3c9f68d4c225d8dfcaba18a87/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/developer/mod.rs#L211) forwards it to shell/file tools, and [shell.rs:569](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/cfb67d72f6129ba3c9f68d4c225d8dfcaba18a87/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/developer/shell.rs#L569) explicitly uses it for command.current_dir. No Goose registration, DB mutation/copy, or unsafe prompt answer ships here. S4 remains available and synthetically covered for qualifying providers.

Prime Agent is a separate approved native-fork import workstream; the --extension compatibility fix is already inherited from main #6588.

Aider/Memcode provider-only recovery follow-up is owned by worker 523 on the existing `e4086568` seam, following the owner’s revised decision. Their consumer PRs track the implementation and validation; no additional shared interface or production change is required here. The checkpointed archive fix is retained.

## Testing

All validation runs in CI only. No local builds/tests/vet/lint/typecheck/formatters/generators/provider commands/installations/repository binaries ran. **Live proof not run.** Synthetic fixtures only; real provider history is read-only and never copied into fixtures.

Coverage includes registration/mode selection, root confinement, bounded CLI discovery, metadata-only eligibility, import-time fingerprints and cwd drift, native checkpoint/adoption/retry, strict fallback refusal, terminal prompt/generation fences, Gemini legacy/Windows paths, and ordinary idle-session admission. Env regressions cover one resolution/issuance, account precedence, empty clears, clone isolation, returned-root replacement, secret redaction/non-persistence, failure before native effects, and full non-import Terminal/Chat map equivalence.

Prepared-archive regressions cover ID/cwd/both checkpoints with/without fingerprints, source append/removal, and unchanged private bytes. Generic normal-Resume recovery tests publish a proven copy, fail the checkpoint, remove/change the original, recreate the adapter, and recover the same target; absent/unproven copies, invalid sources and missing/unprepared workspaces refuse. The unchanged no-preparer fingerprint guard and unfingerprinted refresh ordering remain covered. The real Cursor adapter/service crash-recovery regression is coordinated in #7634; real Aider/Memcode launch-failure/archive regressions live in their harness PRs.

Current exact-head AO review `c816790c-8743-450d-9fd3-ff19d5f120df` APPROVED `28cb5a7da562b1c355a299e3fc485c0562dbef03`; six visible hosted checks are queued. No prior approval or check is attributed to this head. No Ready claim. The final Chat roll-up remains inherited from `22605049426b939c712885cd2754e4badc836208`; no Qwen-only follow-up merge. Generated artifacts remain unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Links #6364 and targets `codex/session-import-build`; original base preserved.
- [x] Explicit URL pushes, normal history-preserving merges; no remotes/config edits, force-pushes, reviewer pings or PR merges.
- [x] Synthetic success/refusal regressions; native identity/worktree gates and source evidence documented.
- [ ] Latest exact-head CI green.
- [x] Latest exact-head AO review approved; all required threads resolved.
- [ ] Needs independent human GitHub approval. App screenshots and live proof were not run under task constraints.


Earlier compiler repair `f44ae55f4bf6b69d66a5ec3fd4e99bbe97cab6b9`: Hermes Windows job `125727595067` exposed two typed `ProjectID` map indices and the relocation struct comparison invalidated by the `Env` map. The test-only repair uses `string(record.ProjectID)` and `reflect.DeepEqual`, retaining all fields and assertions. Production code/seams unchanged. Exact-head AO review `05df8f7d-5c57-4b47-87e5-889a46e9cdcb` approved the repair; fresh CI pending. Earlier e408 checks do not cover this head. No local checks ran.

Earlier CI repair `a092982872d4b743ed42eb2a6c6c8ffbcddcf8a3` addresses three shared `nilerr` findings from [Aider exact-head lint](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41585098375/job/125749197508). Three scoped annotations explain intentional per-item batch collection and test-fake unavailable-state classification. Error/result semantics and assertions remain unchanged. Fresh AO review and CI are required; no local checks ran.

Actual CI fixture repair `28cb5a7da562b1c355a299e3fc485c0562dbef03`: [session-store-race job](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41601871470/job/125809519544) failed two assertions without a data-race report. The interactive publication fake incorrectly rejected rollback process-exited signals as well as identity publication; it now fails only session-start. title: fix(chat): honor supported permission modes for Kimi launches
body:
Code changes: +98 -26  
Tests: +343 -4  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Honor the selected Chat driver's supported permission modes in new standalone and project launches. Kimi launches with its native default permission behavior instead of requesting unsupported `auto` mode.

## Why

The launch composer offered generic Auto-approve and inherited AO's `auto` default even though Kimi ACP supports only `default`. The existing supported-mode endpoint already knew this, but new launches did not use it. Backend preflight checked transport approval capabilities without checking provider-specific mode support, so failure happened late during controller startup.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Kimi New Chat offered Auto-approve and failed with an unsupported `auto` mode error. | Kimi offers only Use agent permissions and sends `default`. |
| Unreal with the Chat default received an invented `auto` policy and failed admission. | Unselected policies stay omitted in direct launches and replay snapshots, preserving the harness default. |
| Saved ACP menus could reintroduce unsupported permissions. | Saved choices are filtered against the daemon's supported-mode catalog. |
| A permission choice could be unsupported after changing agents. | Kimi uses its native default while the chosen policy is preserved for switching back. |
| Unsupported explicit modes could pass preflight and fail during startup. | Preflight and startup share admission checks; unsupported requests return typed `CHAT_PERMISSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` validation errors. |
| A fast caret move followed by a padding click could restore an older Lexical selection. | Background focus adopts the native caret before the browser changes selection; subsequent typing stays at the intended offset. |

Real-app before/after captures remain outstanding. Visual evidence and remaining validation gaps are tracked below.

## How

- Preserve omitted approval policies outside the default-only correction. Direct launch and New Chat replay snapshots share the same payload policy, so Unreal retains its daemon-owned harness default while explicit user choices remain explicit.

- Renderer CI caret fix: handle composer padding focus on primary mousedown, preserve the native selection, and synchronize it into Lexical before refocusing. Interactive controls and editor text keep their own pointer behavior.

- Permission discovery blocks new launches only while initially loading. Omitted-agent or failed-request responses still reach authoritative daemon admission and its existing fallback/error recovery.

- Reuse the daemon permission-mode catalog in the shared launch hook and filter both generic and cached provider menus.
- Substitute a native default only for providers whose sole supported mode is `default`. Never implicitly choose bypass permissions or substitute defaults for providers with multiple choices.
- Preserve explicit backend request/project permission semantics: unsupported choices remain errors. Only unset spawn defaults receive the default-only-provider correction.
- Keep the chosen frontend policy intact across agent changes so returning to another provider restores it.
- Add fake ACP, catalog/admission, HTTP error, spawn, switch, menu, and asynchronous capability regressions. No paid agent launch or live user settings mutation is needed.

## Testing

Passed locally:

- Rebased onto `main` (`80556c340d`), new head `df2f073aa5`. Resolved settings-bar conflicts while retaining Cloud approval controls and configured-default model labels alongside local permission filtering. All 196 launch, New Chat, and permission-query tests and both typechecks pass. The complete fake renderer smoke suite also passes on this rebased head.

- Unreal default regression (`7192fd2f4e`): both project and standalone cases reproduced the invented `auto` before the fix. Real-query fixtures use Unreal's bypass-only catalog and verify direct launch omission, replay omission, and explicit bypass selection. All 169 composer, New Chat, and permission-query tests pass; frontend and e2e typechecks pass. title: [Bug]: Chat to Terminal switch during the setup step fails with "WorkspacePath is required" (accepted while provisioning, but does not wait)
body:
### What went wrong?

A new Orchestrator session is switched from Chat to Terminal while it is still in its `setup` provisioning step. The switch fails, and the rollback fails the same way:

```
switch interface <id>: install hooks: claude-code.GetAgentHooks: WorkspacePath is required; source restore: switch interface <id>: resume chat: workspace path must be absolute, got ""
```

The transition ends in phase `recovery_required` with code `RECOVERY_REQUIRED`, and the "Interface switch needs attention" banner appears.

This is the error chain that @axisrow reported on nightly 0.14.3 in [#6267](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6267#issuecomment-6257845701). There, @21lakshh could not reproduce it on v0.14.2 and asked whether the project has setup commands. Ours does, and the timeline below shows that the switch arrived during that step. It also happens on a stable build.

Collected with Claude Code from a read-only look at `ao.db` and the tagged source.

**Environment:** AO desktop v0.14.6 (stable AppImage, Linux), Claude Code orchestrator, started in Chat by the Orchestrator button. The code path is unchanged in v0.14.8.

### Steps

1. Use a project with a `postCreate` setup command. Ours runs `composer install` and `npm ci`; with warm caches that takes about 6 s.
2. Click the Orchestrator button. The session starts in Chat.
3. Within a few seconds, before setup finishes, switch the interface to Terminal.

### Timeline (UTC, from `sessions.provision_steps` and `session_interface_transitions`)

```
07:58:49.44  session created (Chat)
07:58:50.65  fetch done
07:58:50.65  worktree done (the existing orchestrator worktree was reused)
07:58:50.65  setup started
07:58:54.19  interface transition requested (chat -> tui, policy drain, history strict)
07:58:55.00  transition finished: recovery_required / RECOVERY_REQUIRED
07:58:56.68  setup done
07:58:59.22  agent done, session idle in Chat
```

Answers to the questions in #6267, read after the fact for this session: `provision_state=ready`, `provision_error=""`, `workspace_path` set. Afterwards `GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/interface-transition` returned `supported: true`, and the session kept working in Chat. So, unlike #6741, the session did not get stuck. Only the switch failed.

### Cause (code reading, v0.14.8 `403a8c8`)

- [`interfaceWorkspaceUnavailable`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go#L148-L153) lets a switch through on purpose while the session is provisioning: "A session still provisioning is not refused: its workspace is on the way."
- Nothing on the transition path waits for provisioning to finish. [`startTransitionTarget`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go#L1257-L1284) reads the record and passes [`workspaceInfo(rec)`](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L7245-L7254) to the relaunch. That copies `rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath`, which the error shows is still empty during setup.
- The rollback uses the same record, so it fails in the same way.

### Expected

Either refuse the switch until provisioning is done (as `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE` does for a failed start), or wait for provisioning to finish before the target starts.

title: fix(opencode): resolve permission blocks on reply in OpenCode 1
body:
Code changes: +10 -5  
Tests: +7 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

On OpenCode 1, answering a permission or question prompt (approve **or** reject) left the AO session blocked in **Needs You** until the whole turn ended. Everything delivered to the session in that window was refused.

The plugin forwarded the reply as generic `active`, but the lifecycle tool-flight precedence deliberately suppresses generic `active` while a dialog is open (it must not let sibling tool traffic clear a live dialog), and the OpenCode payload carries no tool identity, so no correlated tool post could clear it either. Only a turn-boundary event lifts the block.

## Fix

- The plugin now reports `permission.replied`, `question.replied`, and `question.rejected` as `permission-resolved` — the same turn-boundary event the OpenCode 2 plugin already emits — instead of generic `active`.
- The OpenCode 1 deriver maps `permission-resolved` to active. The lifecycle reducer already treats that event as definitive, so the block clears as soon as the user answers, and the session returns to idle at the turn end.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/...`
- Deriver table test covers the new mapping; the installed-plugin test asserts the reply handler emits `permission-resolved` and that the event is wired through `ao hooks opencode`.
- The manager-side sequence (blocked → suppressed `active` → `permission-resolved` → active) is already pinned by `TestToolPrecedence_DefinitivePermissionResolutionClearsBlocked`.

Fixes #7564

title: fix(opencode): keep subagent sessions out of parent identity
body:
Code changes: +111 -18  
Tests: +157 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

OpenCode reports subagents as **child sessions** on the same event bus the activity plugins subscribe to. Neither the OpenCode 1 nor the OpenCode 2 plugin filtered them, so child `session.created`, prompt, tool, and completion events were forwarded as if they belonged to the parent:

- the latest child event overwrote `Metadata.AgentSessionID`, the persisted native restore handle, and it flipped back and forth as parent and child interleaved
- every identity change reset the conversation checkpoint
- a child finishing (v1 `session.status` idle, v2 `session.execution.*`) marked the parent idle while it was still working, so the state flapped
- if a child emitted the last event of the turn, restore resumed the subagent conversation

## Fix

Both plugins now track child sessions from `session.created` (`info.parentID` on v1, `data.parentID` on v2) and never forward a child id as the session identity:

- child `session-start`, prompt, and turn-boundary (stop) events are dropped, so a child can never move the parent's identity, checkpoint, or turn state
- child tool and permission traffic is folded onto the parent id: `active` for tool work, `permission-blocked` / `permission-resolved` for dialogs, so subagent work still reads as activity and a child dialog still surfaces on Needs You
- v2 child tool activity carries no tool identity, so a child's tool cannot enter the parent's in-flight tool bookkeeping
- a child's own `session.status` is ignored entirely rather than folded, so its idle never stops the parent

V1 `Session.fork` does not set `parentID`, so deliberate new and forked native sessions keep adopting normally. Child ids are globally unique, so tracking them for the life of the plugin is safe.

## Tests

- New OpenCode 2 Node harness mode drives a parent, child, and grandchild: asserts no captured hook call ever carries a child id, child completion emits no `stop`, child tool activity carries no tool identity, and the parent's tool identity is preserved.
- Static source assertions pin the same `parentID` filtering in both managed plugins (the OpenCode 1 plugin runs only under Bun, which CI does not install, so it has no executable harness).
- New lifecycle test pins that parent-only OpenCode traffic leaves `AgentSessionID` and the conversation checkpoint untouched for both harness versions.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/... ./internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/... ./internal/lifecycle/...`
- The v2 harness test skips on Windows like the existing ones. I ran the identical harness against a compiled fake `ao` and confirmed the exact sequence: `session-start, active, active, permission-blocked, permission-resolved, active, active, stop`, all on the parent id. The OpenCode 1 plugin was exercised the same way under Bun with a parent + child + grandchild stream.

Note: `cloud/internal/workerexec/assets/ao-activity.ts` forwards the same two shapes for the cloud worker; that is outside these adapters and left as a follow-up.

Fixes #7567

Code changes: +532 -2

## What
Import Grok terminal sessions with first-open workspace relocation. Stacked on #7592 (`ao/terminal-import/shared`); extends #6364.

## Why
Grok has readable local transcripts but ordinary resume restores the original folder. A private copy allows AO to continue the native ID inside its own worktree.

## Before / After
| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Grok conversations do not appear in import scans | Local history can be selected and continued in the Terminal view |
| `grok -r <id>` restores the original cwd | First open prepares a worktree-local bucket with the same ID; later opens preserve its new turns |

## How
- Root: `GROK_HOME`, default `~/.grok`. Layout: `sessions/<URL-encoded-cwd>/<UUID>/summary.json` and `updates.jsonl`.
- Reads the authoritative ACP update stream using the shared confined reader, groups visible user/assistant chunks into turns, applies native prompt-boundary rewind markers, drops tool/thought/hook noise and tolerates torn tails. Timestamps use native Unix seconds, with file-time fallback for legacy records. Duplicate native IDs group as one conversation.
- Existing restore argv: `grok --no-auto-update -r <UUID>`. First open copies native state to the resolved worktree's percent-encoded bucket and rewrites only the copy's `summary.info.cwd`. Private staging directory + atomic rename, files 0600; source untouched; existing copies preserved. Long encoded bucket names fail clearly rather than guessing Grok's slug/hash format. Compaction checkpoints are copied recursively; nested subagent metadata is intentionally not copied.
- Continuation probes and transcript locator use confined reads. `active_sessions.json` provides best-effort live-ID/PID ownership checks before and after adoption; missing registry/PID reuse are limitations.
- Provider source/docs: https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/17-sessions.md

Provider revision `xai-org/grok-build@2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8`: [`session/persistence.rs:435`](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8/crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/session/persistence.rs#L435) resolves native IDs in the current cwd bucket. AO prepares the current-worktree bucket and rewrites only the copy's summary cwd, so the native ID/history continue with tools in the worktree. No generic fix is duplicated here.

## Before / After

The following compares source behavior; live proof not run. Screenshots and recordings were not captured because the task prohibits local runtime launches and verification.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cline is absent from the import gate and discovery registry. | Cline history is offered as Terminal import candidates. |
| An existing native conversation cannot be opened through import. | First open rereads its archive and uses `cline --cwd <AO worktree> --id <exact native id>` with the resolved source data root. |
| Imported Cline ownership has no harness-specific signal. | Manifest identity/status/live-pid evidence is consulted before and after adoption. |

## How

- Root: `CLINE_DATA_DIR`, else `<CLINE_DIR>/data`, default `~/.cline/data`. Group `sessions/<id>/<id>.json` and `<id>.messages.json`; retain the complete native id accepted by `--id`.
- Source gate pinned to `59cce11bc2fe2aaf250f8b97ccdf75af195c09c2`: [`resume.ts:4-12`](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/59cce11bc2fe2aaf250f8b97ccdf75af195c09c2/apps/cli/src/utils/resume.ts#L4-L12) reads messages globally by selected id; [`session-runtime.ts:272-290`](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/59cce11bc2fe2aaf250f8b97ccdf75af195c09c2/apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.ts#L272-L290) starts that same id, using [`session-config.ts:25-26`](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/59cce11bc2fe2aaf250f8b97ccdf75af195c09c2/apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-config.ts#L25-L26) for current cwd/workspace root. Explicit `--cwd` pins tools to AO's worktree; history does not restore its saved cwd.
- Stream the JSON message array using shared `recordSkim` per message. Keep readable text around oversized tool payloads and torn final writes. Parse user/assistant text, cwd, title, activity and count; skip injected environment/system context. Confine reads with `os.Root`; refresh both documents before first open.
- Add continuation probes and source `CLINE_DATA_DIR` propagation only when different. Use manifest id/status/live pid/start time, with writable-descriptor fallback. Detection is best effort and does not make the provider scan/launch race atomic.
- Two narrow dispatches in the existing strict verifier and restore-command method select new-file helpers only when the shared import-source metadata key is present. They require the exact resume id (or source id), resolved import config root, matching explicit `CLINE_DATA_DIR`/`CLINE_DIR`, valid native history and an absolute AO tool cwd. body:
Code changes: +884 -2

**Dropped under the credential-copy restriction; retained as a draft.** Pinned MiMo stores account credentials in the selected database: [account/account.sql.ts:5-31](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/account/account.sql.ts#L5) defines `control_account` and `account` with `access_token` and `refresh_token`; [account.ts:211-268](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/account/account.ts#L211) resolves/refreshes those stored tokens. Model-provider keys also exist separately in `auth.json`, but copying DB/WAL/SHM would still copy account credentials. The user requires dropping a harness with database-backed auth rather than copying credentials. Direct native export also mutates its source ([storage/db.ts:93-117](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/storage/db.ts#L93)). Export is refused before binary resolution; backend admission and the frontend offer remain disabled. Parser/remap code and synthetic tests are retained for a future provider design. No snapshots, provider runs, source writes, credential copies or HOME overlays. Live proof not run.

## What
Draft MiMo Code Terminal import work with a new native identity graph and strict S2 takeover, on shared #7592 / foundation #6364. The private remap/import confirmation pipeline and synthetic tests are retained behind a fail-closed source-export guard. The Phase 3 remap route remains blocked by native bootstrap side effects; no DB copy or new environment seam is implemented.

## Why
MiMo rejects execution when the saved directory/workspace differs from the current instance. Importing unchanged IDs would preserve that wrong location or conflict with the original row. An independent native graph bound to the AO worktree preserves the original conversation.

## Before / After
| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| MiMo's original native ID cannot execute in a different directory | An independent graph remap is implemented, but opening is held at the source-export gate |
| Arbitrary tool payload IDs can resemble graph references | Only schema-defined native references are rewritten; tool input/results and provider metadata remain unchanged |
| Native export bootstrap mutates the source store | Export is refused before binary resolution, Scan/UI admission is disabled, and the PR stays draft |

## Retained prototype (disabled)
- Discovery and native confirmation read SQLite with `mode=ro`. AO does not copy or rewrite the native database. The provider's own export reads the original conversation; its own import creates the new rows.
- Export JSON is kept in AO's private temporary area (0700 directory, 0600 files) and deleted after success or failure. Commands have deadlines, output caps and process-tree cancellation. Stderr contents are not exposed.
- The remap allocates the complete native identity graph before rewriting only schema-defined parent/session/message/part links, revert references, compression boundaries/projections, context watermarks, deferred inputs and agent sender-session provenance. Arbitrary tool state, structured results, providerMetadata/providerOutput and metadata remain unchanged, including unrelated prefixed IDs or values equal to graph IDs. External graph references, duplicate IDs, entropy failures and collisions refuse opening.
- The optional queue snapshot is omitted. The native importer then materializes settled history itself, instead of transferring live process ownership or pending receipts. Native messages/parts remain intact; this is native import, not transcript handoff.
- The prepared session must exist with exactly the AO directory, empty workspace identity and all imported native rows. S2 checkpoints its actual ID before runtime launch and reuses it on retries; no fresh-chat fallback.
- Existing shared `MIMOCODE_DB` binding selects the same store. The adapter accepts absolute paths with the supported `mimocode.db` filename and rejects unrelated filenames. The imported-only workspace hook checks effective project/daemon environment on first and later restores.
- Ownership is best effort: a process holding a global database does not identify which conversation it owns, so no such inference is made.

## Saved-workspace validation audit
Pinned provider [3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/tree/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a):

Without a queue snapshot it calls `materializeHistory`. Lines 235-242 retain the exported directory/workspace, so the private JSON must set them before import.
- [execution-ownership.ts:20-36](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/session/execution-ownership.ts#L20) requires the saved directory to equal the current instance when no workspace ID is set. AO sets and confirms that directory, and rejects the [MIMOCODE_WORKSPACE_ID override (flag.ts:424)](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/flag/flag.ts#L424).
- [session-cwd.ts:17-18](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/tool/session-cwd.ts#L17) returns `Instance.directory`; [bash.ts:911-914](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/tool/bash.ts#L911) uses it as the default tool cwd. The launch instance is the AO worktree.
- [id/id.ts:23-92](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/id/id.ts#L23) uses 64 timestamp/counter bits: sessions have sixteen descending hex digits plus ten base62 characters; messages/parts use the ascending `g` marker, sixteen hex digits and nine base62 characters. AO mirrors the provider algorithm with cryptographic entropy.
- [message-v2.ts:283-346](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/session/message-v2.ts#L283) defines checkpoint/compaction references; [session.ts:150-157](https://github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code/blob/3de989f477acfe9b2ce6aa0f1ac7db4d0f5b194a/packages/cli/src/session/session.ts#L150) defines context identity/watermark fields.

title: [Bug]: Report delivery to a Claude Code Terminal orchestrator loops forever when Claude Code wraps the paste in <pasted_content>
body:
### What went wrong?

A Claude Code orchestrator in **Terminal** mode received the same report batch again and again, about every 17 seconds, for 1.5 hours. One batch was delivered 51 times and another 41 times. Every delivery started a new orchestrator turn.

The cause: Claude Code now wraps a pasted prompt in a `<pasted_content id="xxxx">` tag. AO recognizes a report delivery only when the prompt **starts** with `<ao-report-delivery id="`. So AO never sees the delivery accepted, and it redelivers forever.

Collected with Claude Code from a read-only look at `ao.db`, the session transcript and the tagged source.

**Environment:** AO desktop v0.14.8 (stable AppImage, Linux). Claude Code 2.1.316 for the orchestrator, in Terminal mode.

### What we saw

- The orchestrator transcript shows the prompt that Claude Code recorded for each delivery:
  ```
  <pasted_content id="bca5">
  <ao-report-delivery id="report-batch:rpt_…">
  …
  </ao-report-delivery>
  </pasted_content id="bca5">
  ```
- Deliveries before 09:58 UTC that day were not wrapped and were acknowledged normally. From 09:58 on, every delivery was wrapped. The Claude Code version (2.1.316) did not change and the session was not restarted, so the wrapping seems to be switched on from the server side. Claude Code's own SDK schema text says the CLI "may wrap it in `<pasted_content>` tags".
- The `reports` rows stayed `pending`/`claimed`, with `delivery_attempts` rising to 51 and these errors:
  ```
  session: semantic message acceptance unsupported: prompt submission was not observed
  orchestrator cannot take reports right now: send <id>: session: composer has an unsent draft
  ```

### Cause (code reading, v0.14.8 `403a8c8`)

- `SendSemantic` pastes the wrapped report into the pane and waits 10 s until the UserPromptSubmit hook records that coordination id ([manager.go L4953-L5005](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L4953-L5005)). If it does not see it, the batch is released and delivered again.
- The hook gets the id from the prompt with `CoordinationDeliveryID` ([hooks.go L826-L840](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/cli/hooks.go#L826-L840), also [L459](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/cli/hooks.go#L459)).
- `deliveryID` requires the trimmed prompt to start with the marker (`strings.HasPrefix`, [report.go L26-L30](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/domain/report.go#L26-L30)). With the `<pasted_content …>` line in front, it returns `false`, so the acceptance never arrives.
- The same check covers `<ao-session-delivery` ([report.go L214-L219](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/403a8c8385ed43bbf9e9289e3f3bbaa6517dc437/backend/internal/domain/report.go#L214-L219)). So `ao send` messages to Terminal sessions are probably no longer recorded as coordination either. We did not verify that part.

### Workaround that worked

We pointed the orchestrator's UserPromptSubmit hook (in the worktree's `.claude/settings.local.json`) at a small wrapper. The wrapper removes one leading `<pasted_content id="[0-9a-f]{4}">` line from the payload's `prompt`, then pipes the payload to `ao hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit`. Claude Code picked up the changed hook without a restart. All stuck batches were acknowledged within 10 seconds, and the loop stopped. AO reinstalls its hooks when a session starts, so the workaround does not survive a relaunch.

### Expected

AO recognizes its own delivery marker when Claude Code wraps the paste. For example, `deliveryID` could accept the marker after one leading `<pasted_content id="…">` wrapper; that keeps the "must start with" protection against user-typed markup. Another option is to write the delivery to the pane in a way that Claude Code does not treat as pasted text.

A related gap: a batch that is never accepted is redelivered forever, every ~17 s. A cap, or a back-off with a visible warning, would limit the cost when the next format change breaks acceptance.

title: feat(kanban): fill an empty card summary from the done report
body:
Code changes: +80 -13\
Tests: +72 -0\
Others: +21 -0 (generated sqlc)

> **Stacked on #5861.** The counts above are this branch's own change on top of #5861's head (`7dcb1de153`). GitHub shows #5861's commits in this diff until it merges; I'll rebase onto `main` then.

## What

When a worker finishes with `ao report --done` and its kanban card has no summary, the report's note becomes the card summary.

## Why

A tester ran five identical Claude Code workers with card summaries on. All five got the same "Card Summary" prompt section, but only one ran `ao summary`, so four cards stayed blank. Every one of them ran `ao report --done --note "..."`. Using that note fills the card without relying on agents remembering a second command.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A worker that finishes with `ao report --done --note "Listed every API route in a markdown summary"` but never runs `ao summary` has a blank card | The card shows "Listed every API route in a markdown summary" |
| A done note longer than 200 characters could not be a summary | It is cut at a word boundary and ends with "…" |
| A worker that did set `ao summary --done "..."` keeps it | Unchanged: the note never replaces a summary the agent set |

Screenshots to follow once #5861 lands; this is a daemon change and the card UI is unchanged.

## How

- `FillSessionCardSummary` is one SQL update guarded by `card_summary = ''` (and `is_terminated = 0`), so it can never overwrite an agent's own summary, even if both arrive at once.
- The report service calls it synchronously after storing a done report, like it already does for reported artifacts. It is best effort and never fails the report. It uses the note, or the free-form message when there is no note.
- `domain.CardSummaryFromNote` cleans the text the same way as `ao summary`, but cuts long notes instead of refusing them.
- Intentionally left out: a card that has only a stale start summary ("Reading the code…") is not replaced by the done note. That needs knowing whether the existing summary was final, which nothing stores today.

## Testing

- `go test` for `service/report`, `domain`, `storage/sqlite/store` and `daemon` pass; build, vet and gofmt are clean.
- New tests: a done report fills an empty card and a later one does not replace it, a checkpoint report fills nothing; the store fills only an empty summary; long notes are cut at a word boundary.

title: feat(chat): dictate into the composer with native macOS speech recognition
body:
Code changes: +778 -10\
Tests: +43 -1\
Others: +56 -1 (localized strings, helper Info.plist, CI workflow, package.json, .gitignore)

## What

Dictation in the chat composer on macOS, shown only when **Developer mode** is on (Settings → General) while it's in preview. A mic button sits left of send, and **⌘D** toggles it. While you speak, the button stretches into a pill with a live level meter, and your words fade into the composer letter by letter.

## Why

The mobile app has had push-to-talk dictation since #3400. The desktop composer had none: macOS's own dictation works there, but only through Fn-Fn or Edit → Start Dictation, with the system's popup and mic UI. This keeps the system's speech recognition and moves the controls into the app's own UI.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Composer has attach, model and send only. No way to dictate except macOS's own Fn-Fn popup. | Mic button left of send (⌘D). It stretches into an inverted pill with a centre-weighted bar meter. Text streams into the composer and fades in letter by letter. |

Recording: ⌘D starts dictation, the mic stretches into the pill, words stream in and fade, ⌘D finishes.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43f9c495-855a-43b6-b604-42d0d1539f9b




## How

- **Native recognition, app UI.** A small Swift helper (`native/dictation-helper/main.swift`) records with `AVAudioEngine` and transcribes with `SFSpeechRecognizer`, on-device when the language supports it. It streams JSON lines over stdout: mic levels, transcript, end, error. `src/main/dictation.ts` runs one helper at a time and forwards events to the shell renderer only, dropping events from a helper that was replaced while it shut down. In the renderer one composer owns the dictation and listens for events only while it does; starting in another (a side chat, say) finishes the first and keeps its words.
- **Helper is its own app bundle, `Orchestrator.app`**, with the app icon and its own usage strings, so the Microphone and Speech Recognition prompts read "Orchestrator". It disclaims responsibility on launch (`responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim`), so macOS asks for the helper's permissions instead of the launching process's. Without this, macOS kills the helper when it was started from a terminal with no speech usage string.
- **Utterances after a pause.** Since macOS 15 the recognizer starts a new utterance after a pause and reports only its words, and on stop it can re-send an ended utterance revised. The helper keeps finished utterances and uses the audio timestamps of ended results to tell a revision (starts inside an earlier utterance's audio, so it replaces it) from new speech (appended). Earlier word-matching rules duplicated or dropped text.
- **Responsive meter.** The recognition tap delivers ~100 ms buffers, which made the meter lag. An `AVAudioSinkNode` reports a level every render cycle (~10.7 ms at 48 kHz). The renderer smooths it (30 ms rise, 140 ms fall) and draws straight to the bars each frame, outside React.
- **Live text in the editor.** `ComposerEditor` gets `dictate()` / `endDictation()`. Each dictated letter is a `DictationLetterNode` that fades in once with the existing `stream-char` animation, staggered 14 ms per letter. Revisions change letters in place, so nothing flashes. The run becomes plain text after the last fade. The whole dictation is one undo step. While dictating, the caret and prompt suggestion are hidden, and the empty composer's placeholder crossfades to "Start speaking".
- **Stopping.** ⌘D, clicking the pill, or Esc finishes and keeps the text after the recognizer's final wording. Sending, or typing a key, stops at once and keeps the text. Leaving the app (switching apps, hiding or minimizing the window) finishes dictation and keeps the text, and quitting kills the helper. Errors keep what was heard and show for 6 s.


- **Shortcut.** New `dictate` app shortcut: ⌘D on macOS, Ctrl+Alt+D elsewhere (plain Ctrl+D is end-of-input in terminals). It acts through the mic button, so it does nothing while Developer mode is off, and it is listed in Keyboard Shortcuts only in Developer mode (labels in all 9 locales). It is left out of the command palette, and pages in the in-app browser panel keep ⌘D.

- **Shipping.** `prePackage` builds the helper for the target arch and `extraResource` bundles it on macOS. `postPackage` fails if it is missing. osx-sign signs the nested bundle with `com.apple.security.device.audio-input`, since the hardened runtime blocks the helper's microphone otherwise. The frontend CI job compiles it for x64 and arm64 and lipo-verifies both.
- **Private API.** `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim` is undocumented but stable. Chromium uses it for the same reason. AO ships outside the App Store, so it is fine here.

Intentional omissions:
- macOS only, and only in Developer mode. The button and helper are absent on Windows and Linux.
- No auto-stop on silence, since people pause to think.

## Testing

- Manually tested in the desktop lab (`electron-forge start` on its own daemon and profile): start/finish via ⌘D, click and Esc, sending mid-dictation, pauses between sentences, permission prompts, pill and meter animation, letter fade.
- Replayed a `say`-generated clip with two 3.5 s pauses through the helper and confirmed the transcript joins all three utterances with no repeats.
- Added `forge.config.test.ts` cases for bundling the helper on macOS only and for its signing entitlement, a browser-panel case that leaves ⌘D to the page, a default-chord row for ⌘D, and a Keyboard Shortcuts dialog check that Dictate stays hidden outside Developer mode.
- Not done locally: CI suites, typecheck and lint (relying on CI), and a signed, notarized package build. The first signed release should confirm the helper prompts for and records the microphone.
