title: fix(opencode): report tool executions as tool-use events
body:
Code changes: +281 -70
Tests: +598 -7
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Both OpenCode plugins reported every tool execution as a generic `active` activity event. The lifecycle manager's in-flight tool tracking and execution-step timeline are driven by `pre-tool-use` / `post-tool-use` / `post-tool-use-failure`, so OpenCode sessions never registered a tool start, completion, failure, or duration, and permission-dialog clearing that correlates on the in-flight tool never fired either.

- OpenCode 1 receives `{tool, sessionID, callID}` on `tool.execute.before/after` but forwarded only `{session_id, model}`.
- OpenCode 2 forwarded `tool_name`/`tool_use_id` but labelled both events `active`.

## Fix

- v1 plugin emits `pre-tool-use` and `post-tool-use` with `tool_name` plus `tool_use_id` (the upstream `callID`).
- v2 plugin emits `pre-tool-use`, and maps a failed `execute.after` result to `post-tool-use-failure`.
- Child/subagent tool calls stay folded onto the root session as plain `active` (inherited from #7597), so a child call id never enters the parent's bookkeeping or identity.
- Tool arguments and results are never forwarded; only the correlation identity is.
- The v1 managed-event list and both derivers map the new events to `active`, so the existing flight/step machinery applies unchanged.

## Second CodeRabbit round + re-review

**Cross-harness semantics of `blockedCandidates` (blocking, re-review inline).** Accumulating candidates was right for OpenCode, whose asks really are open at the same time, but it changed behaviour for every other harness reaching the path: with a replace-per-ask rule, a fresh ask retired a stale candidate, so a dialog whose tool never posts (a denial that emits no post, a lost post) could not strand the session blocked past the next dialog. Fixed as suggested: accumulation is limited to `permission-blocked` — the OpenCode ask event, where concurrent dialogs are real and the plugin's `permission-resolved` report on the last reply preserves liveness. Every other ask keeps the single-candidate snapshot semantics exactly as on `main` (id-carrying Kimchi notifications and name-matched `permission-request` both replace). Two further properties are pinned by tests: `TestToolPrecedence_NonOpenCodeAsksKeepReplaceSemantics` (the unique-first-dialog-never-posts case the re-review asked for) and `TestToolPrecedence_OpenCodeAsksStayBlockedAfterADeniedDialog` (OpenCode stays blocked through the stale candidate until `permission-resolved`).

**An ask that matches nothing tracked now fails closed again (major).** While translating the accumulate rule, the uncorrelated case had drifted: an ask carrying an id or name that matches nothing in flight — a child session's dialog, whose tool start is folded away — used to erase the candidate entirely on `main` and must not let any post release the block. That wipe is restored: identity present but uncorrelated clears the set, so only a turn boundary or a permission resolution lifts the block. An identity-less notification duplicate (Claude) still touches nothing. Covered by `TestToolPrecedence_UncorrelatedAskFailsClosedUntilResolution`.

**A suppressed tool post still closes its step (minor).** The early return for a state-suppressed signal ran before `recordStepLocked`, so a swept failure arriving while the session was blocked would leave the step open — the exact "running forever" symptom this PR fixes, resurfacing behind a dialog. Tool-use events now land in the step ring even when the state write is suppressed; fence rejections are untouched, so `TestStepsOnlyLandForAcceptedSignals` still holds. Covered by `TestStepsRecordSuppressedToolEventsWhileBlocked` and `TestStepsSweptFailureClosesStepWhileBlocked`.

**v1 thrown subtask reported as a success (minor).** OpenCode 1's subtask path fires `tool.execute.after` even when the subtask throws, with no output. The handler now reads `output` and, when it is `undefined`, keeps the call in flight and reports nothing, so the turn-boundary sweep closes it as a failure instead of the old premature success post. Verified by hand through Bun: a thrown subtask produces no success post and is swept as `post-tool-use-failure`, while a real output still posts normally.

**v2 nested Code Mode executions on one lifecycle (minor).** Nested executions reuse the outer call's id and session, so parallel nested tools used to overwrite the entry, the first completion would delete it and close another running tool's step (the step ring matches by id), and a turn boundary after a nested completion would find nothing to sweep. The plugin now keeps one lifecycle per id: the first start opens it and reports `pre-tool-use`, deeper starts only nest, and the completion that empties the nesting reports the outcome. Verified by hand: three starts and two completions produce exactly one pre and one post, and an interruption after a nested completion still sweeps the outer call. Covered by `TestManagedV2PluginKeepsNestedExecutionsOnOneLifecycle`.

## Review follow-ups

**Rebase (blocking comment).** Dropped the pre-merge copy of #7597 (`fc2f659af5`) and rebased the remaining commit onto `main`, so the branch is now a single commit and the GitHub diff contains only this PR's changes. The conflict resolution keeps `main`'s v1 dialog work intact: `openAsks` tracking, the `permission-resolved` report on the last reply, its entry in `opencodeManagedEvents`, and the `permission-resolved` case in v1 `DeriveActivityState`. The stacked `manager_test.go` hunk is gone — that coverage already landed with #7597.

**A failed tool stayed "running" after the turn ended (P2).** Fixed in the plugin, as suggested. Both plugins now track root call ids that have not seen their `after` hook and close the leftovers as `post-tool-use-failure`:

- v1 sweeps on `session.status(idle)` before `stop`, and in `switchedSession` so a replaced identity's steps close under the id they were reported with.
- v2 sweeps on every root execution boundary (`succeeded`/`failed`/`interrupted`) and on `session.status(idle)`, which also covers interrupted turns; the sweep is keyed to the outgoing root when a new root is adopted.

One deliberate deviation from the suggested `Set`: the tracker is a `Map<callID, toolName>`, because `recordStepLocked` returns early when a signal carries no `ToolName`, so a nameless post would close nothing. The lifecycle is unchanged by this particular fix; the CodeRabbit round below does change `toolFlight` in `manager.go`, and that change applies to every harness — see its semantics note there.

**Permission prompts were not matched to their tool (P2).** v1 `permission-blocked` now forwards `tool_use_id` from `properties.tool.callID`. That field is the whole `tool` object on the ask — upstream `permission.Request` declares it as `Schema.Struct({ messageID, callID })` — so there is no `tool_name` to send with it, and the lifecycle's id-based correlation (`f.inflight[ToolUseID]`) is the precise path anyway. Replay through the branch: `pre-tool-use(call_1)` → `permission-blocked(call_1)` → `post-tool-use(call_1)` clears the block as soon as that tool finishes, without waiting for the turn boundary. With two dialogs open, the second ask re-snapshots the candidate to `call_2`, so `call_a` finishing no longer clears a dialog that is still on screen — the same fail-closed behaviour `#7596` wanted, without its single-candidate gap. `permission-resolved` on the last reply still clears the block; the correlated post covers a reply event that never arrives.

**Is `input.status === "error"` the real OpenCode 2 shape?** Yes. The upstream plugin reference for `tool.hook("execute.after")` documents exactly this branch — `if (event.status === "error") … event.error.message` — so `status` is the documented discriminator and `error` is the failure detail. The check is now `input.status === "error" || input.error != null` so a future payload that drops `status` cannot silently downgrade a failure to a success.

**Test nit.** The v1 leak assertion no longer greps the bare substring `"args"`; it now asserts the plugin contains no `input.args`, `output.args`, or `output.output`, matching how the v2 test checks `input.input`.

## CodeRabbit follow-ups

**Multi-dialog permission gap (major).** CodeRabbit was right, and the gap was introduced by forwarding the id: the lifecycle held a single `blockedCandidate`, so a second ask replaced the first and that tool's post set the session active while the older dialog was still on screen. `toolFlight.blockedCandidate` is now `blockedCandidates map[string]struct{}`, mirroring the existing `cursorPending` multi-dialog pattern: every ask adds its id, and the block lifts only when the last tracked tool's post arrives, at a turn boundary, or on a permission resolution. The ambiguity rule is unchanged — a name-only ask with two same-name tools in flight still contributes no candidate and fails closed — and an identity-less notification duplicate still adds nothing and erases nothing. Covered by new `TestToolPrecedence_TwoOpenDialogsStayBlockedUntilBothToolsFinish` and `TestToolPrecedence_IdCorrelatedAskStillClearsOnItsOwnPost`; the existing `AmbiguousSameNameBlockFailsClosed`, `SequentialDialogsResetAmbiguity`, `IdentitylessBlockedDuplicatePreservesCandidate`, and `UniqueSameNameToolClears` tests pass unchanged.

**Sweep ignored session ownership (minor).** Both plugins now store the owning session with each tracked call, and `failOpenTools` closes and drops only that session's entries. A stale idle from a replaced root can no longer drain another session's calls or report them under the wrong id. Verified by hand: root A switching to root B, B starting a tool, then a late idle for A leaves B's call untouched, and B's own boundary closes it under `ses_B`.

**v2 adoption swept another root's calls (major).** `adoptRoot` no longer sweeps at all. Sessions run concurrently in OpenCode 2, so the previous root's open calls still belong to it and are closed by its own boundary — never by a hook or boundary belonging to another session. Verified by hand: root B appearing while root A has an open call no longer produces a spurious failure for A, and A's late `execute.after` reports normally. One deliberate non-change: a tool hook from a non-current session still re-adopts that session as the root, because that identity behaviour is what #7597 established and child folding depends on it.

**A new turn's call can be swept by an older boundary (major — documented, not fixed).** The suggested fix — associate calls and boundaries with a turn — is not implementable: the `execute.before` input carries `sessionID`, `tool`, and `id` but no turn id, so the plugin cannot tell which turn a call belongs to. Reordering the sources cannot help either, because the hook genuinely fires before the boundary is processed; any ordering discipline would still close the call. The window is narrow (a turn must end in interruption or failure while the next turn's first hook lands before the boundary event is delivered) and the blast radius is one mislabelled step in the execution timeline — the turn itself still ends correctly, and nothing sticks. The trade-off is recorded in the `failOpenTools` comment: the alternative is leaving genuinely failed and interrupted tools open forever, which is the P2 this PR fixes.

**Nitpick: orphaned parent post in the fixture.** The subagents harness now invokes the parent's `execute.before` before `execute.after` and asserts the matched pair, so the expectation can no longer pass on an orphaned post.

## Verification

- v1/v2 deriver table tests for the three tool events.
- Lifecycle: the multi-candidate tests, the cross-harness replace-vs-accumulate pin, the uncorrelated-ask fail-closed test, the suppressed-step tests, and every existing tool-precedence/step test unchanged.
- v1 install test asserts the plugin wires `pre-tool-use`/`post-tool-use`, forwards `callID`, forwards the blocked `tool.callID` on `permission-blocked`, carries the `failOpenTools` sweep, keeps thrown subtasks in flight, and serializes no tool payload fields.
- v2 static wiring test plus Node harness runs: a stable call id across each before/after pair, `post-tool-use-failure` for an errored tool, an interrupted execution closing its still-open step, the subagents fixture pairing the parent tool callbacks, and nested Code Mode executions producing exactly one pre/post per outer call.
- CLI seam tests: `ao hooks opencode pre-tool-use` lifts `ToolName`/`ToolUseID` and reports `active`; `ao hooks opencode permission-blocked` reports `blocked` and carries the tool id.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages, `gofmt` clean, `golangci-lint` 2.13.2 clean on the touched packages, `go test -race` clean for `lifecycle` and `opencodev2`.
- `go test ./...` for the touched areas — `lifecycle`, `opencode`, `opencodev2`, `cli`, `storage`, `httpd` — passes. Both plugins were also driven by hand on Windows (v1 through Bun, v2 against a compiled fake `ao.exe`) for the failed-tool sweep, permission identity, child folding, identity-switch sweep, session ownership, nested Code Mode lifecycles, and thrown subtasks.

Not run locally: Linux/macOS. This Windows machine fails a set of tests identically on unmodified `main`, all unrelated to this change: the `TestOpenCodeNativeSessionConfigDir`/`TestPrepareImportedOpenCodeSession*` path-separator expectations, `TestPrepareV2DataHomeFailsWhenWholeLegacyStoreVanishes`, `TestRenderCheckReplacesItsEarlierScreenshot` (symlink privilege), four `internal/httpd/controllers` tests, and ten adapter packages (agy, aider, claudecode, codex, commandcode, copilot, crush, cursorstore, fake, goose) whose failures are symlink/path/HOME shaped — six of those were re-run on clean `main` and fail the same way. CI on Linux covers them.

## Fixes

Fixes #7568.

  * Permission-blocked status is more accurately tied to pending tool approvals, and remains active while relevant approvals are unresolved.

title: fix(opencode-v2): report user prompts and dedupe stop
body:
Code changes: +107 -13 (includes #7613)
Tests: +417 -2 (includes #7613)
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

The OpenCode 2 plugin reported session creation, execution, status, and permission events, but never a user prompt. AO advances conversation checkpoints only on a `user-prompt-submit` boundary, so every OpenCode 2 turn ended as a scoped stop without its prompt boundary: the checkpoint was durably marked unsettled and the conversation-replay trust gate failed closed for the session's lifetime.

The same turn can also end with both `session.execution.*` and `session.status(idle)`, producing two stops; the second one unsettles an already completed checkpoint.

## Fix

- `session.inbox.enqueued` with `item.type === "user"` now emits `user-prompt-submit` with `item.payload.text`. Only the prompt text is forwarded; files and metadata stay native.
- Prompts are deduped per inbox item id (`inboxID`, falling back to the item id), so re-delivered or replayed items do not re-open the turn.
- Synthetic, compaction, and move items are not prompt boundaries.
- The turn boundary is the durable execution terminal. OpenCode 2 publishes one `session.execution.started` → `succeeded/failed/interrupted` pair per busy period, plus an ephemeral `session.status` that can report `idle` between the steps of a still-running execution (observed ~4s into a turn on real 2.2.5). Once a session reports execution events, a status idle can no longer end the turn: the early stop can neither complete the checkpoint before the agent finishes nor be re-cleared into a second, unsettled stop. A session that never reports executions keeps its status-idle boundary.
- The stop dedup reopens only on the next user prompt. `execution.started`/`status busy` reopen it only until the plugin has seen a prompt for that session, keeping the mid-turn-subscribe fallback without letting a segment boundary inside a turn unsettle a completed checkpoint.
- The OpenCode 2 deriver maps `user-prompt-submit` to active.
- Child-session prompts and stops stay dropped by the #7597 filtering.

## What the checkpoint gates for OpenCode 2

`user-prompt-submit` + `stop` give AO a trusted `prompt` → `complete` checkpoint bound to the launch owner and the native session id. That checkpoint is the trust input to AO's native-history replay gate: when a chat controller attaches to the session's native thread (for example a chat session resumed after a daemon restart), a settled checkpoint lets strict-history replay proceed, and an unsettled one fails closed. Terminal→Chat switching for `opencode-v2` is still refused up front with `INTERFACE_HANDOFF_UNSUPPORTED`, so a settled checkpoint does not unblock that switch yet.

## Verification

- v2 deriver table test for `user-prompt-submit`.
- Static plugin tests for inbox handling, user-only filtering, stop dedup, and the execution-terminal turn boundary.
- Node harness `prompts` mode: a duplicate inbox item, synthetic/compaction/move items, and the execution/status double-stop sequence produce exactly one prompt per item and one stop per turn; prompt payloads carry the text and no files/metadata.
- New node harness `dedupe` mode: `idle → busy → idle` inside one running execution, a trailing idle, and a second execution segment in one turn yield a single stop per turn, and a status-only session still stops on its idle boundaries.
- The lifecycle harness now includes a user prompt before each turn and still asserts the single ordered event sequence.
- `go test` for `opencodev2`, `opencode`, `lifecycle`, `cli`; `gofmt` and `go vet` clean. The node-executed harness tests skip on Windows (this machine); the same harness source was run locally against an `ao` stub to verify the expected event sequences, and CI's Linux run executes them.

## Stacking

This PR is stacked on #7613 (#7597 merged; rebased onto `main`, resolving with the `permission-resolved` deriver entry that landed since). While #7613 is open, the GitHub diff and the counts above include its commit. After it merges I'll rebase so the diff and header shrink to this PR's own changes.

Fixes #7572.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * OpenCode session activity now more accurately reflects user prompts and tool execution, including starts, completions, and failures where reported.
  * Activity and stop notifications are better aligned with session turns, with duplicate prompts and stops filtered out.
  * Parent-session tool activity includes the tool’s identity, while command arguments are not forwarded. Child-session tool activity continues to be reported without tool details.

title: feat(cloud): cloud on for everyone, faster Settings, share gate, file attachments
body:
Code changes: +574 -242\
Tests: +175 -134\
Others: +73 -161 (generated API spec and SDK schema, sqlc, locale strings)

## What

Four desktop changes for AO Cloud, paired with OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane PR (branch `fix(cloud)/further-bugs`):

1. **Cloud is on for everyone.** The Developer Mode "Cloud" toggle, its confirm dialog, `PATCH /api/v1/settings/cloud-offering` and the settings response's `cloudOffering` field are removed. The daemon's cloud gate is on whenever a control plane is configured (the desktop ships one). `AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=0` stays as the dev/CI off switch.
2. **Settings (and every daemon request) no longer queue behind event streams.** EventSources connect to `ao-events.localhost`, which Chromium resolves to loopback as a separate host. Settings warms Codex accounts with the cached read first and starts the slow forced reconciliation 1.5 s later. The settings read is bounded at 10 s.
3. **Share only where the organization may share.** The session header offers Share only when the session's organization has the `share` feature in `/me` `offering.features` (WorkOS organization metadata `feature=share`).
4. **File attachments in cloud Chat and terminals.** Cloud sessions now take images, PDFs and any other file:
   - **Chat:** attach, paste or drop a file in the composer and it uploads to the session right away. The message carries it as `attachmentIds`. Sent messages show images inline, PDFs as their first page (opening the whole document), and other files as a chip that saves them.
   - **Terminal:** a file dropped on a cloud terminal is uploaded, placed in the sandbox, and its sandbox path typed at the prompt.

## Why

- Cloud should be available to everyone, without Developer Mode. The RCA for the "Cloud switch disabled" report traced the stuck switch to the renderer's settings query never settling. Its prerequisite, the toggle, is gone.
- Settings was slow to open. Measured on a cold open in the dev app:
  - The renderer holds 3 to 5 lifelong EventSources on the daemon's single HTTP/1.1 host, which allows 6 connections, so ordinary requests shared 2 or 3 connections. They waited up to 950 ms before they were even sent.
  - Settings forced a Codex account reconciliation on every open, which took 4–9 s and held one of those connections.
  - A daemon request that never completes would hold a connection, and with it the settings query, until restart. That matches the reporter's "only quitting fixed it".
- Session sharing is limited to organizations WorkOS flags with `feature=share`.
- Cloud chat was text only. A file dropped on a cloud terminal pasted a path on the Mac that the sandbox cannot open.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud appears only after Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode → Cloud → confirm | Cloud is on; no toggle |
| Cold Settings open: daemon requests wait up to 950 ms before being sent (`/import` 951 ms, `/mobile/devices` 900 ms, `/settings` 175–280 ms); forced Codex reconcile 4.0–9.3 s at open | Every request sent within 5 ms (`/settings` 3 ms, `/mobile/devices` 2 ms, `/import` 2 ms); the forced reconcile starts ~1.5 s later, after the page's reads |
| Share button on every cloud session the user's org owns | Share only when the org has `feature=share` |
| Cloud chat: no attach control; dropping a file on a cloud terminal pastes a Mac path the sandbox can't read | Cloud chat attaches any file up to 25 MiB; terminal drop types the file's sandbox path |

Measurements: Chrome DevTools Protocol network timings from the dev desktop app, comparing a cold reload and Settings open before and after (`send_after` is the time from request creation to request sent). Screenshots of the attachment UI will be added once the control plane change is on staging; the attachment routes do not exist on production yet.

## How

- **Cloud default:** `Offering.CloudEnabled()` is `CloudOffering && control-plane URL`. `config.CloudOffering` now defaults to true. The stored toggle, its store method and its sqlc query are removed. The old `app_settings.cloud_offering` column is left in place and is no longer read, so no migration is needed.
- **Connection pool:** `eventStreamBaseUrl()` maps only the loopback daemon base (`127.0.0.1`) to `ao-events.localhost` on the same port. Remote hosts are untouched. CSP already allows `http://*.localhost:*`, and the daemon's CORS check keys on Origin, not Host.
- **Attachments:**
  - A new main-process `cloudCp:requestBinary` channel carries bytes in both directions, with the same token handling and `/api/cloud/v1` path checks as `cloudCp:request` and a 32 MiB cap.
  - The composer's existing staging hook uploads each file and returns an `ao-cloud-attachment:` reference. The cloud send turns those references into `attachmentIds`, so the composer UI (paste, drop, chips, drafts) is reused unchanged.
  - The composer now passes each file's name to staging. Local staging strips it, so the daemon receives exactly the bytes it did before.
  - Images render as data URLs, because the renderer CSP does not allow `blob:`. `PdfPreview` takes an optional byte loader.
  - The draft store accepts `ao-cloud-attachment:` references as attachment paths, so a sent message's acceptance is recorded and the composer clears. A cloud chip never builds a daemon URL from its reference. Each PDF viewer gets its own copy of the bytes, because pdf.js takes ownership of what it is given.
- **Contract (additive, `oasdiff breaking` clean):**
  - `ChatMessageInput.attachmentIds`. `text` may be empty when files are attached.
  - `UserMessageEvent.payload.attachments`, using a new `MessageAttachment` schema.
  - The `cloud-client` schema is regenerated.
- **Removed:** `e2e/settings-cloud-confirm-stacking.spec.ts`. The Cloud toggle's confirm dialog was the vehicle for that stacking regression test.

## Testing

- `npm run frontend:typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, `packages/cloud-client` typecheck + tests (31 passed).
- `npx vitest run` (frontend): 10,500+ passed. The remaining failures are in `browser-profile-import`, `remote-proxy`, `cloud-agent-proxy`, `ChatWorkspace` and `ContextMeter`; all five files fail identically on `main` on this machine.
- New tests:
  - `cloud-cp-proxy.test.ts`: the binary channel's token, limits and signed-out 401.
  - `cloud-attachments.test.ts`: reference round-trip, upload SHA-256, error message, placement path.
  - `api-client.test.ts`: the event-stream host.
  - Updated settings, composer, event-transport and notification tests.
- Backend: `go test ./...` for the touched packages passes. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 reports 0 issues. Ten packages fail identically on `main` on this machine (agent CLI probes, `daemon`, `session_manager`, `shellterm`).
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok. `oasdiff breaking` against `main`: no breaking changes.
- Settings performance was re-measured in the dev desktop app after the change (table above).
- **Staging, end to end** (control plane `e312e64`, this branch's dev desktop):
  - Chat: an image, a PDF and a text file attached in the composer upload (`201`), render under the message (image inline, PDF first page, opening the full document; text chip), and the agent replied with the secret word from each file.
  - Terminal: a file dropped on a Coder worker's terminal was uploaded, placed (`/home/ubuntu/repository/.ao/attachments/…`) and read by the agent. `git status` stays clean (`/.ao/attachments/` is in `info/exclude`).
  - Staging found two bugs, fixed in this PR. After a send with cloud files, the composer kept the files and showed "Message acceptance couldn't be recorded locally". A second preview of the same PDF fell back to a file chip.
- Not run locally: the renderer Playwright e2e suite and the Electron boundary jobs; these will run in CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [ ] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable. This PR combines four related cloud fixes, as requested.
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording. Measurements are included; attachment screenshots will follow once staging has the control plane change.
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.). Local runs are described above; CI pending.

title: fix(updater): stop Restart & install from waiting forever behind a stuck update step
body:
Part of #6911.

## Problem

On macOS, clicking **Restart & install** can leave the dialog on a disabled **Preparing update…** button indefinitely. One reporter's AO stayed in this state for two weeks and never offered a newer build.

`quitAndInstallUpdate` runs on `updaterOperationQueue`, the same queue that background checks and downloads use. Neither the queue, the install's wait for its turn, nor the install's own steps had a time limit. The pending request is also cached in `macRestartPreparation`. So if anything ahead of it, or inside it, never settles, every later click gets the same pending request back. Automatic checks also queue behind it, so no newer build is ever downloaded.

One step that can fail to settle is electron-updater's hand-off of a finished download to Squirrel (`MacUpdater.doDownloadUpdate`). That promise only resolves when Squirrel finishes reading the zip from the local proxy, and it ignores the cancellation token. Inside the install, the progress helper's file writes (mkdir, copy, `active.json` rename) sit outside the helper's 10 s READY timer.

## Fix

- **Each phase gets 60 s:** first waiting for a turn on the queue, then the install's own steps. Two kinds of time don't count: native preparation, which has its own watchdog, and a download that has reported progress within the last minute. That keeps a slow but healthy download of a newer build from failing a staged install.
- **Past that, the request fails and the dialog offers Relaunch AO.** The message is "Another update step didn't finish, so the install couldn't start…" in the queue, or "The install got stuck before AO could close…" inside the install. The dialog shows its existing **Relaunch AO** action, and Settings shows the error.
- **A result that arrives late can't restart AO.** Every step checks `installAbandoned`. The helper start is aborted through an `AbortSignal`, so a start that finishes late removes its attempt instead of writing `active.json`, and a late helper is told the install failed. `macRestartRequested` is set only just before `quitAndInstall`, so an abandoned request never leaves AO marked as restarting. A cleared deadline stays cleared.
- **The timeout is logged.** `install-queue-timeout` (with `phase: queue|install`) is written to `logs/updater.jsonl`.

title: fix(updater): make Relaunch AO exit even when quit cleanup hangs
body:
Part of #6911. Companion to #7617.

## Problem

When the macOS update dialog fails, its action becomes **Relaunch AO**, which called `app.relaunch()` and then `quitCompletely()`. That is an ordinary full quit:

- **The quit could hang forever.** `before-quit` waits on `disposeAllBrowserViewHosts`, `remoteRegistry.closeAll`, `cloudAgentProxy.close`, telemetry and the usage flush, and none of these has a deadline. Only an update restart (`isUpdateRestartRequested()`) armed the 15 s `finishUpdateQuit` exit, so one cleanup step that never settles kept the process alive.
- **The dialog could stay disabled for good.** The renderer only reset its pending state when the relaunch IPC call *rejected*. A quit that stalled, or was cancelled at the unsent-draft prompt, left the button on a disabled **Preparing update…** with Cancel disabled too.
- **A cancelled relaunch came back later.** `app.relaunch()` was armed before the quit, and Electron can't take it back. Someone who chose Stay at the draft prompt got AO relaunched on their next full quit, and every click armed it again.

## Fix

- **Relaunch AO gets the update-exit deadline.** `updates:relaunch` marks the quit as an update exit, so `before-quit` arms the same 15 s `finishUpdateQuit` deadline it uses for update restarts. Cancelling at the draft prompt clears the mark.
- **The relaunch is armed only once the quit goes ahead.** `app.relaunch()` is armed once, in `before-quit`, after the draft prompt has let the quit through.
- **The handler reports whether the quit went ahead.** `before-quit` runs inside `quitCompletely()`, so the handler already knows. The dialog gives its buttons back immediately when the quit was cancelled, and after 20 s if AO is still running (5 s past the main-process deadline).

## Not in this PR

- The Restart & install wait itself is bounded in #7617, and the helper that made ShipIt cancel is #7620.
- Ordinary tray **Quit completely** still has no cleanup deadline. That is the same cleanup path, but it is not part of the update flow.

## Testing

All in the dev app from this branch, run against isolated data and driven over CDP:

- **Relaunch AO with nothing pending:** a relauncher was armed, AO exited, and a new instance started. `relaunch()` resolved `true`.
- **Relaunch AO with a pending-attachment draft:** the native prompt appeared. I clicked **Stay** through System Events: `relaunch()` resolved `false`, AO stayed open, and no `--type=relauncher` process existed.
- **Relaunch AO with a quit cleanup that never settles** (a temporary local-only hang, not committed): AO exited at exactly 15 s, logging `Update shutdown cleanup exceeded 15 seconds…`, and relaunched.

New `RestartToUpdateDialog` tests cover the 20 s release and the immediate release on `false`. I didn't run them locally; CI runs them.

title: fix(updater): keep the macOS update helper from cancelling the install
body:
Part of #6911. Found by reproducing the reporter's update with the published builds.

## Problem

On macOS, **Restart & install** quits AO, and then Squirrel refuses to install:

```
ShipIt  Beginning installation
ShipIt  Aborting update attempt because there are 1 running instances of the target app
ShipIt  Installation cancelled: SQRLInstallerErrorDomain Code=-9 "App Still Running Error"
```

The "running instance" is AO's own progress helper (`ao-update-progress`, #5002). AO starts it right before quitting, and it started `NSApplication` immediately. LaunchServices files an AppKit process under the app that is its parent, so the helper was registered as AO:

```
"agent-orchestrator"  bundleID="dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop"
  executable path = …/update-restart/attempt-…/ao-update-progress
  originalPid     = <AO main>   (AO's own record shows "exited-with-subordinates")
```

None of these change that registration: an embedded Info.plist with its own `CFBundleIdentifier`, the `__CFBundleIdentifier` env var, or `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim`. I tested each. An orphaned process (parent launchd) gets no bundle identity.

ShipIt cancels while any app with that identifier is running, so the helper cancelled the install it was meant to report on. A plain quit (install-on-quit, and the update e2e) doesn't start the helper, which is why it still works. That is also why the reporter's `kill -TERM` workaround in #6911 installed fine.

## Fix

- **The helper stays a plain process.** It prints `READY`, then polls its state every 0.5 s. It never starts AppKit on the normal path. If the relaunched AO acknowledges, it cleans up and exits.
- **A window needed while AO is still its parent comes from an orphan.** That happens when AO's quit stalls for three minutes. The helper starts a copy of itself and exits, so the copy is orphaned before it starts AppKit. The copy keeps the original's stall clock. If the copy can't be spawned, the helper stays headless until launchd adopts it.
- **A failure while AO is still open doesn't leave a window behind.** The helper stays hidden for 20 s, longer than AO's 15 s forced update exit. If AO exits in that time (Squirrel can fail after `quitAndInstall`), the orphaned helper shows recovery. If AO is still open, it keeps its own error dialog and the helper ends (new `.abandoned` stage). Before this, a lingering failure window made AO's next quit cancel the staged install.

## Reproduction (real signed builds, isolated `HOME` under `~/.ao`)

| AO build | Helper | Scenario | ShipIt result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.14.3-nightly.202610161732 (reporter's) | shipped | Restart & install (shell or `open` launch) | App Still Running, cancelled |
| 0.14.9-nightly.202610311751 | shipped | Restart & install | App Still Running, cancelled |
| 0.14.9-nightly.202610311751 | shipped, killed when AO exits | Restart & install | Installed |
| 0.14.9-nightly.202611011830 → 202611022329 | shipped + embedded Info.plist | Restart & install | App Still Running, cancelled (helper still `dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`) |
| 0.14.9-nightly.202611011830 → 202611022329 | first version of this PR (headless only) | AO paused 3+ min after `quit-and-install`, then resumed | App Still Running, cancelled (window started as AO's child) |
| 0.14.9-nightly.202611011830 → 202611022329 | **this PR** | Restart & install | **Installed** |
| 0.14.9-nightly.202611011830 → 202611022329 | **this PR** | AO paused 3+ min after `quit-and-install`, then resumed | **Installed**. The window came from an orphan (ppid 1, bundleID NULL) |

The last commit (5ab5097, failure grace and spawn-failure fallback) was checked standalone with a fake AO process: a failure while AO stays open, a failure followed by AO exiting, and a stall with AO alive.

## Not in this PR

- #7617 (Restart & install waits forever behind a stuck update step) and #7618 (Relaunch AO exits even when cleanup hangs) cover the dialog that never leaves "Preparing update…".
- The stale `staged-update.json` from the report is #7557.
- The update e2e only covers plain quit. A dialog-driven hop would have caught this; that's a follow-up.

## Testing

- The reproduction above.
- `StateTests.swift` covers the failure grace and `.abandoned`. I ran it locally because the helper is native and CI only builds it.

fix(httpd): answer a reassigned LAN address with 421 before auth
body:
Code changes: +19 -2\
Tests: +12 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The mobile LAN listener now checks which machine a phone expects before it checks the phone's password. If the phone expected a different machine, it answers `421 HOST_ID_MISMATCH` instead of `401`, and the attempt doesn't count toward the lockout.

## Why

A phone saves each machine's LAN address. When that address is reassigned, for example by DHCP or by a second AO daemon taking the port, the phone reaches a different AO install. That install checked the password first, so the phone got a `401`, read it as a rotated password, and told the user to re-pair. Each try also counted toward the wrong machine's lockout.

The mobile app already treats `421` as "this address is another machine now" and looks for its own host again (`connectRuntime.ts`), so no app change is needed.

Split out of #7419 at review's request (it changes request handling ahead of auth, so it deserves a focused review).

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Phone expecting host A reaches host B at A's old address: `401 Unauthorized`, app says the password was rotated | `421 HOST_ID_MISMATCH`, app looks for host A again |
| Each of those requests counts toward host B's lockout | No lockout attempt is spent |
| Phone expecting host B, right password: `202` | Unchanged |
| Phone expecting host B, wrong password: `401` | Unchanged |
| Client that sends no expected host (older apps) | Unchanged: auth applies as before |

## How

`NewMobileLAN` used to wrap the expected-host guard inside auth. It now passes the guard as a `preAuth` wrapper, so the order is control block → host guard → auth → handler. The guard's own logic is unchanged.

**Please review the ordering.** The guard now answers unauthenticated requests. Its only reply is `421` with the code, which says nothing the unauthenticated identity probe doesn't already disclose, and it serves no content. Blocked control paths are still blocked first.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/httpd/...` and `go vet ./internal/httpd/` pass.
- `TestMobileLANRejectsReassignedAddressWithSamePassword` now covers six stale requests with the other host's password: each gets `421`, and none locks out host B's correct password. It fails on the old code.
- From the #7419 review: Prasad checked `421 HOST_ID_MISMATCH` against a daemon built from this change. Mismatched hosts got 421 without touching the lockout, the right host and password got 200, and blocked control paths still returned 404.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(usage): track Gemini CLI token usage
body:
## What
Adds Gemini CLI to the Usage page's per-harness token and cost tracking. Stacked on #7649 (open usage source kinds).

- New `gemini_session` source kind (registered in `domain.AllUsageSourceKinds`) and `gemini` usage harness. No migration: #7649 removed the schema's harness/kind CHECK lists.
- Parser for Gemini's chat log. Each `gemini` message's `tokens` (`input`, `cached`, `output`, `thoughts`, `tool`) becomes one native-reported event:
  - input = prompt + tool-use prompt, and cached is a subset of input;
  - output = candidates + thoughts.
  - Gemini reports no cost, so pricing comes from the catalog.
- Collector:
  - reads the transcript path from Gemini's hooks;
  - falls back to discovery under `<GEMINI_CLI_HOME or ~>/.gemini/tmp/*/chats/`;
  - binds the file by the `sessionId` in its metadata line;
  - rejects other sessions' logs and subagent logs.

## Why
- **Format:** Gemini CLI ≥ 0.60, AO's minimum version, writes an append-only JSONL chat log. Checked against upstream `chatRecordingService.ts` at v0.60.0 and v0.66.0. That fits the existing byte-offset tailing, so this PR needs no whole-file snapshot mode.
- **Repeated messages:** Gemini re-appends a whole message whenever it changes: once without tokens, then with tokens, then after each tool-call update. A bounded list of counted message IDs in parser state emits each message once, even when a restatement lands in a later chunk. Otherwise the replay would conflict with a stored event whose billing provider the legacy repairer had since inferred.
- **Session binding:** AO already pins Gemini's native ID (`--session-id`, `--resume`), so the binding never relies on workspace path.

Known limit: subagent chat logs (`chats/<parent-id>/<subagent-id>.jsonl`) are not counted yet.

## Testing
New parser, collector, hook, and store round-trip tests use small inline fixtures. No checks were run locally; CI verifies it.

title: feat(usage): track Cline token usage (snapshot sources)
body:
## What
Adds Cline CLI to the Usage page. Stacked on #7629 (Gemini).

- **Generic snapshot source mode** for session documents an agent rewrites whole each turn:
  - re-reads the document when its digest changes;
  - emits every billed message under a stable per-message key, and the store's per-binding uniqueness keeps only new ones;
  - leaves cursor and events alone on a torn mid-write read.
  - Snapshot sources keep `byte_offset` at 0, so a rewrite that shrinks the file isn't treated as a replaced file.
  - With no offset and no checkpoint, the legacy repairer leaves them alone, so an inferred attribution can't make a replay conflict.
- **Cline parser** for `<sessions>/<id>/<id>.messages.json`. Each assistant message's `metrics` becomes one event:
  - `inputTokens` is the whole prompt (AI SDK total), with cache reads and writes inside it.
  - Anthropic routes use Anthropic vocabulary, so cache writes are priced apart.
  - `modelInfo.provider` is the observed billing route; the catalog prices it.
  - Cline's own `cost` is kept as reported in the stored usage object.
  - Message IDs dedupe copies a resume or fork makes into another session's document.
- **Binding:**
  - by the hook-reported native session ID;
  - the session manifest's `cwd`/`workspace_root` must also be the AO session's own worktree. That rejects the misattribution in #7478, where a shared hub reports another session's ID under this AO session.
- The sessions dir follows Cline's own resolution: `CLINE_SESSION_DATA_DIR` → `CLINE_DATA_DIR/sessions` → `<CLINE_DIR or ~/.cline>/data/sessions`.
- New `cline_session` kind (registered in `domain.AllUsageSourceKinds`) and `cline` harness. No migration is needed on #7649's open schema.

## Why
Cline CLI 3.x (verified against the installed `@cline/core`) persists messages with an in-place `writeFileSync` of the whole JSON. Byte-offset tailing would either recount history or miss messages after a shrinking rewrite. The snapshot mode lives here rather than in #7629 because Gemini CLI ≥ 0.60 writes append-only JSONL. Continue reuses this mode next.

title: feat(usage): track Hermes token usage from cumulative counters
body:
## What
- Reads Hermes's `session_model_usage` rows from `state.db`. There is one row per session × model × billing route × task. Rows are read for the native session AO titled and resolved, plus the compression and delegation child sessions that descend from it via `parent_session_id`.
- Hermes keeps no per-message usage rows, and it only ever adds each call's delta to these rows. So the parser keeps a per-row baseline in its parser state and emits only the growth since the last read, the same way the Codex parser handles cumulative totals.
  - A row that shrinks becomes the new baseline. It records a `non_monotonic_cumulative_usage` anomaly and never emits negative usage.
  - Event keys include the cumulative values, so replays dedupe.
  - The baseline carries into a replaced source generation, in both the ingestor and the collector.
- Generalizes the SQLite reader from #7630 so each kind returns its own chunk and cursor: row ID for Goose, total usage volume for Hermes.
- A provider-returned cost (Hermes's `actual` status or `actual_cost_usd`) is stored as the event cost. Hermes's own estimates are replaced by catalog pricing.
- `state.db` is found through the Hermes home AO records per session (`agents/hermes/<id>/native-home`). Watch roots refresh for those homes.
- Registers `hermes_state` in `domain.AllUsageSourceKinds`. The schema no longer enumerates harnesses or source kinds (#7649), so no migration is needed.

## Why
Hermes stores usage in SQLite as running totals rather than per-call rows.

Crush is intentionally not included. Its `crush.db` has only per-session totals, which would be workable, but AO never learns Crush's native session id: there are no hooks, no `ResolveNativeSessionID`, and the restore path reads an `AgentSessionID` that nothing sets. Binding would mean guessing by workspace. Adding Crush first needs a separate change: a hook, native-id resolution, or a pinned data dir.

**Source gate: PASS for the inspected installed Cursor Agent version `2026.10.22-27dcf5f`.** Readable bundled provider source is installed under `~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/2026.10.22-27dcf5f/`; these are physical file:line references (the chunks are minified on one line):

title: test(conpty): check the closed listener directly in TestKillReq
body:
## What
`TestKillReq` now checks that the host's listener is closed by calling `Accept` on it and expecting `net.ErrClosed`. Before, it dialed the old port and expected the connection to be refused.

## Why
`shutdown()` closes the listener before `Accept` unblocks (`host.go`, `shutdown` and `runAcceptLoop`), so the listener is always closed by the time `waitDone` returns. The old check dialed `127.0.0.1:<freed ephemeral port>`. CI runs many packages at once, and each opens `127.0.0.1:0` listeners, so another process can be given that freed port and accept the dial. Less often, a localhost TCP self-connect on the ephemeral port does the same. Either way, the test failed with "Dial succeeded" even though shutdown worked:
- Crush #7608, job 125316828557 (`host_test.go:837`)
- Grok #7603 at `ca104860` (same assertion)

Neither PR touches `conpty`.

## Before / After
| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Asserts the freed port refuses connections, which races with port reuse | Asserts the listener itself is closed, which is deterministic |

## Testing
Not run locally; CI runs it. The kill path, the PTY-close check and the Serve-return timing are unchanged.

## Risks
Test-only change.

Transferred history is pinned to the import-time snapshot, and durable private proof recovers publication followed by a lost resume checkpoint.

## Why

Aider persists its native conversation in `.aider.chat.history.md` per repository. AO previously could not discover and resume that history in its worktree.

## Before / After

Source-based behavior comparison; live proof not run. Runtime screenshots/recordings were not captured because local launches and proofs are prohibited by the task.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Aider history is absent from the import list. | S1 discovers the exact history file at explicitly registered project roots, without a home or recursive repository scan. |
| AO cannot reopen that native conversation in its worktree. | First open prepares the selected Markdown, checkpoints its worktree location, and launches Aider with `--restore-chat-history --chat-history-file <AO worktree>/.aider.chat.history.md`. |
| Existing worktree history has no import protection. | Only a confined regular non-symlink file matching the imported size and SHA256 is admitted; differing, unpinned or symlinked history is refused without overwrite. |
| A private copy can be stranded if its resume checkpoint fails and the original disappears or changes. | Retry first verifies durable selection/workspace proof and the private bytes, then resumes that exact snapshot without original-source reads. |

## How

- Native resume and saved-workspace audit: Aider 0.86.2 [`base_coder.py:519-523`](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/v0.86.2/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L519-L523) loads the native Markdown into `done_messages`. Its tool/edit root comes from the current Git repository at [`base_coder.py:434-447`](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/v0.86.2/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L434-L447); the history loader does not restore a saved cwd. AO launches in its worktree and explicitly pins the history filename, overriding history-file config.
- Aider has no conversation UUID. A stable file handle derived from the original canonical history filename identifies this repository's native conversation. A private marker preserves that identity after copying; no transcript is injected as a replacement prompt.
- S1 receives registered project/repository paths only. The reader follows Aider's native Markdown role rules, hides tool output, and bounds regular-file reads to 16 MiB. Discovery fingerprints the raw bytes with size + SHA256; the shared service pins that selection through import, and this preparer validates it at first open. A changed source requires a new scan. No parent traversal, home scan, provider execution, or auth changes occur during discovery.
- S2's `AgentImportedSessionPreparer` checkpoints the prepared file's native handle, config root and transcript path separately from immutable source provenance. Missing history is installed privately and atomically without replacement. An unproven pre-existing file is admitted only when both it and the source still match the import-time fingerprint, using confined bounded reads that reject symlinks and changed file identities. Identity/proof records are added without rewriting native bytes; wrong markers, mismatches and missing fingerprints retain refusal. Source history stays read-only. No shared transfer exclusion is added.
- Before returning for checkpointing, preparation atomically installs a bounded private `.aider.chat.history.md.ao-import.json` record binding native id, selected source filename, physical AO worktree and size/SHA256 fingerprint. Retry verifies that record, the identity marker and exact private native bytes before any original-source access. A fresh adapter can recover when the original file or directory is gone or its history has changed. Missing proof requires exact source validation; invalid proof or changed private history refuses without overwrite or fresh fallback.
- Native restore validates the private history and marker before constructing argv, so missing/mismatched history cannot become a fresh launch. Import mode is explicitly Terminal even if a Chat driver is registered.
- Writer detection uses the shared best-effort writable-descriptor fallback. Aider opens/appends/closes its log and exposes no per-session writer registry here, so detection is limited to an observed write.
- Only Aider-specific new files and registration entries differ from the shared base. Generic seams are consumed unchanged.

title: fix(remote): connect to account hosts with the account token, not a typed password
body:
## Problem

A remote host added by hand in Settings → Remote hosts kept its typed connection password forever. That held even after AO Cloud listed the same host with an account token: `remotes:importAccountHost` deliberately kept a typed password over the token.

When the host's password later changed, the saved entry was rejected for good. A password changes when a new phone pairs through Connect Mobile, when someone clicks Regenerate, or when access is turned off and back on. The sidebar showed "Password rejected" next to a Retry action, and retrying sends the same rejected password again. We hit this between a MacBook and a Mac mini: the mini rotated its password, and the MacBook could not reconnect until its entry was removed by hand.

## Design

One rule: **if your AO account lists a host, connect with the account token; otherwise use the password you typed.**

The host keeps its account token current, because it links itself again whenever its password changes (#7294). A typed password goes stale on the first rotation. The old rule kept the typed password so this client could link the host again later, but linking again is now the host's own job, so clients don't need to keep another machine's password.

## Changes

- **Account sync** (`remotes-main.ts`): for every host the account lists, the account's token replaces a typed password **once the client has seen that token work** (an identity-checked probe returns `online`). If the host rejects the token, for example because it was linked to another account and this account's listing is stale, or the host can't be reached, the client keeps the typed password, takes the listing's label and address, and tries again on the next sync. The client disconnects a proxy left on an old address. This installation's own row is never written.
- **Manual add or edit while signed in** (`RemoteHostsSettings.tsx`): once the host is linked, the client keeps the issued token. The 8-character password is used once to get the token and isn't stored afterwards.
- **Rejected credential** (`RemoteHostsSection.tsx`): the sidebar row reads **Update password** and opens that host's edit form through a new `editRemoteHost` settings option. It no longer retries the same credential.
- **Remove dialog**: removing a linked host has always deleted its AO account record too, but the dialog said it only "forgets the connection on this computer". It now says the host is removed from the account and from every signed-in device.

## Security

This is a net improvement. Clients no longer store the short connection password, which is valid over the public tunnel, for hosts the account lists. They keep only the 256-bit account token. Removing a host from the account now also removes it from every device, which is what revoking should mean.

## Tests

- `remotes-main.test.ts`:
  - a stale typed password is replaced by the token
  - the proxy on the old address is closed
  - the entry is pruned once the account drops the host
  - replacing at the same address invalidates the old proxy
  - this machine's own row stays untouched
  - a typed password that still works is kept when the token is rejected or the host is unreachable
- `RemoteHostsSettings.test.tsx`:
  - manual add while signed in imports the issued token
  - an `editRemoteHost` request opens the right host's form
  - the Remove dialog explains the account removal
- `RemoteHostsSection.test.tsx`: a rejected host shows **Update password** and calls `onUpdatePassword`; an offline host still retries.
- Ran locally: `vitest run` on those three files plus `src/renderer/i18n` and `src/renderer/stores`, 145 tests passing. `tsgo --noEmit` reports no errors in `frontend/src`. The remaining errors are in `packages/product-ui`, because this worktree has no root install.

## Not verified

I haven't run this in the desktop app yet. The UI changes are a sidebar label plus an edit form that opens itself, and they're covered by component tests.

## Risks and trade-offs

A host typed in by hand that's also in the account now follows the account. Removing it from the account removes it on this computer too.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)

- Stop printing the connection password in `ao remote-host status` by default.
- Restrict the short password on the public tunnel once a host is linked.
- Rate-limit failed logins by IPv6 range, and restart dead quick-tunnel connectors.
- Per-device tokens.

title: fix(cli): hide the connection password in ao remote-host status by default
body:
## Problem

`ao remote-host status` printed the connection password every time. Status is the command people run to check on a host, and they paste its output into chats, bug reports and agent transcripts. The password is accepted over the public tunnel, so every pasted status leaks a working credential. It happened in a support session this week. The agent skill told agents to `grep -v '^Password'`, which only works when everyone remembers to do it.

## Change

- `ao remote-host status` prints `Password hidden: run ao remote-host status --show-password to show it.` in place of the password.
- `ao remote-host status --show-password` prints it as before.
- `ao remote-host enable` still prints the password. That's the moment it's issued, and `scripts/setup-self-hosted.sh` reads it from `enable` output. That script may also run against an older release binary, which wouldn't know a new flag.
- Docs, the `using-ao` and bug-triage skills, the grok-bot setup skill, and the Settings → Remote hosts hint (en, ru) that pointed at `status` for the password now pass `--show-password`. The using-ao skill tells agents never to pass the flag.

- `go test ./internal/cli/ ./internal/skillassets/...`: passing.

Scripts that parse `status` for the password need `--show-password`. I found none in this repo: the installer reads `enable`, and its `status` polling only reads addresses.

title: fix(remote): restart dead quick tunnels; keep LAN IPv6 out of /64 lockouts
body:
## Problem

**Dead quick tunnels.** #7294 restarts a fixed tunnel's connector after 3 minutes with no live connection, but a quick tunnel had no such watch. When the machine slept, Cloudflare deleted the quick tunnel. cloudflared kept retrying (473 refused registrations in one night, measured) and AO kept advertising a `trycloudflare.com` hostname that returned NXDOMAIN, until someone killed cloudflared by hand. This still hits signed-out desktops, headless hosts, accounts without a free fixed address, and any machine that falls back to a quick tunnel.

**LAN devices sharing a lockout.** #8038 now counts failed logins per IPv6 /64. Link-local (`fe80::/64`) and private ULA prefixes are shared by every device on a LAN, so one phone mistyping the password locks every other LAN client out for a minute.

## Change

- `mobilebridge/tunnel_runner.go`: every connector gets the `connectorHealth` watch, so a quick tunnel with no live connection for 3 minutes, or one refused 4 times in a row, is stopped. The runner then starts a new one with a new address, and the address publisher sends it to the account. Replacement bookkeeping (`repair`, `unhelped`) stays fixed-tunnel only.
- `httpd/auth.go`: `lockoutKey` keeps #8038's /64 grouping for global IPv6 and leaves link-local and private addresses per-address.

## Tests

- `TestTunnelRunnerRestartsAQuickTunnelThatLostEveryConnection`: a quick connector that registers and then drops is stopped well before the fake connector's 30-second idle, with no repair requested and nothing advertised.
- `TestTunnelClientCannotDodgeTheLockoutAcrossItsIPv6Prefix` covers the tunnel path (`CF-Connecting-IP`), alongside #8038's direct-address test. `TestLockoutKeyGroupsOnlyGlobalIPv6` covers which addresses get grouped.
- `go test ./internal/mobilebridge/ ./internal/httpd/`: passing. `golangci-lint run` on both packages: 0 issues.

## Risks

A quick tunnel that's slow to register (over 3 minutes) now restarts, which costs one connector start. Quick tunnels register in seconds.

Rebased onto #8038, which landed the /64 lockout this PR originally added.

title: fix(auth): artifact URL fan-out can exhaust files and delete Cloud login
body:
## What went wrong?

On Windows desktop v0.14.8 connected to a remote host, switching between a terminal worker and a Chat orchestrator progressively slows down, then remote session loading fails. The desktop may still display the account name although its AO Cloud credential file has been deleted.

A controlled diagnostic reproduction captured the first failure as `EMFILE` while reading `cloud-auth.bin`, followed by `readAuthStore` requesting deletion of that file. There was no concurrent credential write and no captured token-refresh failure in this recurrence.

## Outcome

Remote session/artifact browsing should remain usable with thousands of artifacts, and a transient local I/O failure must not destroy a valid saved Cloud login.

## Affected code

Both paths remain present in v0.14.8 and in main at `25bc9b148f76438a117b930608a4a19d60e32fab`:

- [Remote session artifact conversion](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/25bc9b148f76438a117b930608a4a19d60e32fab/frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useWorkspaceQuery.ts#L328): nested `Promise.all` resolves every artifact's `rawUrl` through `aoBridge.remotes.previewUrl` across the entire remote session list, without a concurrency bound.
- Each `remotes:previewUrl` call performs remote account validation, which reads the encrypted login store.
- [Authentication-store read handler](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/25bc9b148f76438a117b930608a4a19d60e32fab/frontend/src/main/cloud-auth.ts#L194): its broad catch unconditionally removes the login file for read failures as well as decode failures. `EMFILE` therefore becomes a destructive sign-out.

## Reproduction

1. Use Windows AO v0.14.8 (Electron 44.7.0) with an authenticated remote host.
2. Have approximately 3,500 artifact URLs spread across the remote session list, including inactive/older sessions. File contents and names do not appear relevant; the count is the significant input.
3. Alternate between an existing terminal session and a Chat orchestrator. Observe repeated remote session-list refreshes and eager artifact URL conversion.
4. Instrument only aggregate request/read concurrency and sanitized error codes. Eventually a login-file read fails with `EMFILE`; the handler removes the saved credential file and remote session loading fails.

The occurrence is intermittent. One diagnostic run failed on switch 4; a fresh sign-in survived 12 switches before a later run failed on switch 5. The underlying workload uses normal sessions and artifacts, not malformed credentials.

## Evidence and controlled comparison

The installed main bundle was inspected and its auth-store functions separately exercised against disposable synthetic files. A separate diagnostic replica retained the original read/deletion behavior while adding argument-free counters and bounded error-stack capture.

- A baseline inventory contained 3,470 raw artifact URLs across 18 sessions.
- Six session refreshes generated 20,820 artifact conversions, plus two session-preview calls.
- Peak simultaneous login-file reads: **3,470**.
- The first captured error was `EMFILE` in `readAuthStore`, with **zero active credential writes**. Later reads failed with `ENOENT` after deletion.
- Renderer breakpoint samples identify the nested artifact mapping in `useWorkspaceQuery` as the bulk caller, rather than thousands of independent user actions.
- Limiting execution of the diagnostic `remotes:previewUrl` handler to **16 concurrent calls** preserved the original auth handler and returned values/errors. A clean comparison completed **60 switches and 246,876 preview calls**, with **no credential loss, session-load errors, or auth-read errors**. Peak auth-read concurrency fell to **26**. The queue fully drained.

The capped run processed a slightly larger artifact inventory than the baseline. It supports a resource-exhaustion mechanism; it is one bounded comparison, not a universal stability guarantee. Debugger/instrumentation can affect timing, and historical original-install failures do not all have equivalent internal traces.

A separate disposable regression check injected a single `EMFILE` at the file-read boundary of the unchanged installed auth-store functions: a valid synthetic store was deleted and signed-out state returned, with no writer. A preservation assertion failed against that behavior. An EMFILE-only test guard preserved the file and allowed the following successful read to recover the session. This guard was not applied during the live concurrency comparison.

## Scope

- Bound, deduplicate, or defer eager remote artifact URL conversion so a session-list refresh cannot launch thousands of parallel authentication reads.
- Preserve saved credentials on transient read/resource errors and propagate a retryable failure rather than treating it as corrupt/revoked credentials.
- Consider coalescing concurrent auth-store reads as an additional way to reduce repeated filesystem work.

## Acceptance criteria

- Refreshing a remote list with several thousand artifact URLs has bounded conversion/read concurrency and completes without `EMFILE` or credential loss.
- Injected `EMFILE`/similar transient read failure preserves the existing credential file; a subsequent successful read can recover the session.
- Preview URL values and real account/host authorization checks remain intact.
- Regression coverage distinguishes temporary read failures, absent stores, invalid encrypted data, explicit sign-out, and terminal token-refresh failure.

## Out of scope

A separate in-place credential-write/read race may also exist, but it is not the first failure captured in this reproduction. That is not needed to explain the EMFILE path reported here. This also differs from #4778's terminal refresh-failure UI handling and #4476's workspace watcher descriptor issue.

Only sanitized aggregate measurements and public source references are included. No raw traces, screenshots, credentials, callback URLs, local paths, account identity, host/session names, or application/workflow data are attached.

title: feat(usage): stop enumerating usage harnesses in the schema
body:
## What

Usage harnesses no longer need a database migration. Stacked on #7626 (Qwen).

- Rebuilds `usage_bindings` / `usage_sources` once more, with only non-empty checks on `harness` and `kind`. `model_usage_events` is untouched.
- The store is now the guard:
  - `UpsertUsageBinding` requires a known `AgentHarness`.
  - `InsertUsageSource` / `ReplaceUsageSource` require a certified `UsageSourceKind`, from the new `domain.AllUsageSourceKinds`.
  - The collector still binds only `usage.SupportedHarness` harnesses.
- Drops the outer `ub.harness IN (...)` allow-lists in `HasPendingUsageDiscovery` and `ListUsageDiscoveryBindings`. They only duplicated the CHECK; the per-harness discovery rules stay.
- Rollback restores the Qwen constraints and removes only usage outside them.

## Why

Each usage harness used to widen both CHECK lists with its own table rebuild. Harness PRs built in parallel would each drop the others' kinds:
- chat-reported #7631
- Goose #7630 → Hermes #7633
- Gemini #7629 → Cline #7632

The only alternative was forcing them to merge in one fixed order. After this, a new usage harness adds its kind to `AllUsageSourceKinds` and `SupportedHarness`, with no migration.

The trade-off: the database no longer rejects an unknown harness or kind on its own. The store does, and so do the collector and the parser's `default` branch.

## Testing

No checks were run locally. CI on this PR verifies it.
- `TestMigrationOpenUsageSourceKinds` checks that a later harness is accepted, that blank values are rejected, and that rollback keeps Kimi/Qwen usage and drops the rest.
- `TestUsageStoreRejectsUnknownHarnessAndKind` covers the store guard.

title: feat(usage): track Grok token usage
body:
## What
- Tracks Grok token usage and cost from `$GROK_HOME/sessions/<workspace>/<session id>/usage.json`. Grok rewrites that file in place with each model's running totals.
- Adds a whole-file snapshot mode to the polled SQLite source path. Snapshot readers return rows plus a growing cursor, so polling, finalization and source replacement work the same way as for Hermes.
- The parser diffs each model's totals against a baseline kept in parser state, the same way Hermes does. If a total goes down, it becomes the new baseline, an anomaly is recorded, and nothing negative is billed. The baseline carries over when the file is replaced.
- Forked or restored sessions include their parent's history in their totals. On the first read, the parent's totals (found via `parent_session_id` in `summary.json`) seed the baseline, capped at the fork's own totals.
- Cost: `costUsdTicks` is kept as the provider-reported cost. Grok's docs say 10¹⁰ ticks per USD, and local sessions match xAI list prices exactly at that scale. Rows with no cost are priced by the catalog.
- Binding uses the native session ID from Grok's hooks, never the workspace path. The file must sit in that session's own directory, and its `sessionId` must match.
- Adds the `grok_session` kind and the `grok` harness. No migration is needed, because #7649 stopped enumerating kinds in the schema.

## Why
Grok sessions showed no usage on the Usage page.

## Testing
- Parser tests with inline fixtures cover counter growth, cost scaling, replays, shrinking totals, fork inheritance, and rejecting another session's file.
- An ingestor test covers in-place rewrites.
- Collector tests cover binding by native ID and path attribution.
- No checks were run locally; CI verifies it.

title: fix(session): refuse interface switches while the session is still starting
body: Code changes: +33 -7\ Tests: +78 -20\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Refuse a Chat ↔ Terminal switch (and an account move) while the session is still starting, instead of accepting it and failing into `recovery_required`. ## Why Fixes #7594 A switch that arrived during the `setup` provisioning step was let through on purpose ("its workspace is on the way"), but nothing on the transition path waited for it. `rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath` is still empty during provisioning, so the target launched without a workspace (`install hooks: claude-code.GetAgentHooks: WorkspacePath is required`), the rollback failed the same way (`resume chat: workspace path must be absolute, got ""`), and the switch ended in `recovery_required`. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Mid-setup the status reported `supported: true`. The switch was accepted, Chat was stopped, and the target failed with `WorkspacePath is required`, so the switch ended in `recovery_required` | Mid-setup the status reports `supported: false`, `WORKSPACE_PROVISIONING`, "This session is still starting. Switch interfaces once setup finishes." A forced `POST …/interface-transition` returns 409 `WORKSPACE_PROVISIONING`, and nothing is stopped | After, in the desktop app during a 40 s setup step: **Switch to terminal UI** is disabled, and its tooltip gives the reason. ## How - `InterfaceTransitionStatus` reports `WORKSPACE_PROVISIONING` while `ProvisionState` is `provisioning`, ahead of the existing `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE` check from #6743. - `StartInterfaceTransition` and `StartAccountTransition` share a new `interfaceWorkspaceNotReady` guard: `ErrInterfaceWorkspaceProvisioning` while provisioning, and `ErrInterfaceWorkspaceUnavailable` for a failed start, as before. The service maps the new error to 409 `WORKSPACE_PROVISIONING`. - The renderer rechecks the status for `WORKSPACE_PROVISIONING`, as it already does for `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE`, so the control enables once setup finishes. - I chose to refuse rather than wait because the start itself launches the Chat controller when setup ends. A switch waiting for provisioning would race that launch. - The refusal can't stick: only the async Chat start sets `provisioning`, every exit path sets `ready` or `failed`, and boot reconciliation fails a start that AO restarted in the middle of. ## Testing - Reproduced on unmodified `main` with a session in `provisioning` and an empty workspace: the switch was accepted, the controller log showed `stop:chat`, and the transition failed with `WorkspacePath is required`. - `TestInterfaceTransitionRefusesSessionWithoutWorkspace` now expects a refusal for "still provisioning", where it used to assert the switch was allowed. It also covers setup running in an already-recorded workspace. - New: `TestInterfaceTransitionAllowedOnceProvisioningFinishes` and `TestAccountTransitionRefusedWhileProvisioning`. - All of these fail without the fix. - `go test -race ./internal/session_manager ./internal/service/session ./internal/httpd/...`: two failures, neither from this change. - `TestSpawn_AfterStartPromptReservesCallerDeadlineForFallbackDelivery` is a load flake; it passes 3/3 alone. - `TestSearchWorkspaceContentCommonTermReachesLaterFiles` also fails on `main` under `-race`. - `vitest`: `useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx` 29/29, including the new `WORKSPACE_PROVISIONING` poll case. - Live in the desktop app with an isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`: a Claude Code Chat orchestrator in a project with a `sleep 40` setup step. During setup the status API, the 409 on a forced switch, and the disabled menu item with its reason were all confirmed, both on first start and on **Retry start**. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(scm): track PRs a session opens in repositories outside its project
body:
Fixes #7653. Related: #5986 (open design for cross-repository PR associations), #6297, #2629, #3252.

## Problem
A worker's PR in a repository that isn't an AO project never showed up properly on its session. This happened with ao-landing-14 and OrchestratorInc/ao-releases#50. The evidence is on #7653:
- `ao session claim-pr <session> <url>` rejected any PR outside the project origin, canonical repo, or workspace children (`PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`).
- `ao report --pr-created <url>` stored cross-repo URLs only as reference-only `linkedPrs` with no state, and nothing polled them. ao-landing-14 only mentioned #50 in a report note, so AO had no record of it at all.
- No `gh` wrapper exists in the Go daemon, so the report is the only signal at creation time.

## Change
- **Claim** (`claim_pr.go`): a full PR/MR URL in any repository the provider can fetch is claimed as an external-repository PR. The PR must still exist, be open, and be fetchable with the user's credentials. Number refs still resolve only against the project.
- **Report** (`reported_pr.go`, `report/service.go`, `daemon/report_pr_tracker.go`): a `pr_created` output in a repository outside the project (rename-aware) that the session doesn't already track is claimed with no takeover. This runs off the request with a 45s timeout. If the claim fails, the PR stays a "Reported by worker" reference.
- **Observer** (`observer.go`): an external repo has no PR-list guard or sync cursor, so without a change these PRs would be refetched every tick. Now they refresh only when their commit checks change, on a forced review refresh, or every `DefaultPRMaxAge` (5m), which also catches merges and closes. Terminal reconciliation skips them.
- **Inspector**: tracked PR cards in another repository show the repository name and the existing "External repository" badge.
- How project-repo PRs are discovered and claimed is unchanged.

## Tests
New tests, each confirmed failing without the change:
- `TestPoll_ExternalRepoPRRefreshesAtMaxAgeCadence`: an external PR is polled, its merge persists, and it is not refetched within max age, even when the project repo's listing changes.
- `TestTrackReportedPRClaimsOnlyUntrackedPRsOutsideTheProject`: external GitHub and GitLab PRs are claimed. Project, renamed-project, and already-tracked PRs are not.
- `TestCreateTracksEachCreatedPRAfterTheReportIsStored`
- `marks a tracked PR in a repository outside the project as external`, plus the negative case.

Existing claim tables that asserted `ErrProjectMismatch` now assert an external claim against the PR's own host and repo, with no collapse onto the project.

Ran:
- `go test ./...`: passes except `adapters/agent/{codex,commandcode,opencodev2}`, which depend on this machine's tools (local OpenCode 1, codex auth timeout, git include setup). This PR doesn't touch those packages.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2 on the changed packages: 0 issues.
- `tsgo --noEmit` for frontend and product-ui: pass.
- vitest `SessionInspector` and `SessionLinkPreviewCard`: 204 passed.

## Risks / follow-ups
- This intentionally loosens the claim trust boundary for full URLs. A claimed external PR gets the normal CI and review injection.
- A reported PR that is already merged or closed can't be claimed and stays a reference.
- ao-releases#50 itself still needs a `claim-pr` (or a fresh `--pr-created` report) from that session. This PR does not touch ao-landing-14.
- The sidebar hover card still shows only `PR #N` without the repository.
