title: feat(desktop): sign in through orchestrator.inc and link the website visit
body:
Release builds now sign in through a page on the website, `https://orchestrator.inc/app/auth/return/`, instead of `https://api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return`. The page forwards to `ao-app://callback` as before. For website visitors who accepted analytics, it also adds `web_distinct_id`, and the app uses it to link that website visit to the signed-in account in PostHog.

**Do not merge before the website page is live** (OrchestratorInc/ao-landing#112). Release builds with this change can't sign in until that page is deployed.

### What changes
**Return address** (`resolveCloudAuthRedirect` in `cloud-auth.ts`):

| Build | `redirect_uri` |
|---|---|
| Packaged on the production WorkOS client (stable, nightly, preview) | `https://orchestrator.inc/app/auth/return/` |
| Packaged on any other client | `https://api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return`, unchanged |
| Dev | loopback `http://127.0.0.1:3000/callback`, unchanged |
| `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT` set | that value, unchanged |

Both production addresses are registered in WorkOS. The old one stays the default, so released desktops keep working.

**Linking a website visit:**
- `web_distinct_id` is read only after a real code exchange.
- It is validated: `^[A-Za-z0-9._$:-]{1,200}$`, and PostHog placeholder ids are refused.
- Main holds it in memory until the renderer takes it, once (on the session notification, or on mounting when the sign-in link started the app). It is never stored or logged.
- It never affects sign-in.
- The renderer calls `posthog.alias(webId, userId)` right after `identify`, and captures `ao.renderer.cloud_web_visitor_link_requested` (PostHog can still refuse the merge).
- It does neither when analytics is opted out, when the remote denylist covers either event, or on a refresh, a restart or another account.

**Docs:** `docs/telemetry.md` describes the link.

### Testing
- `npm run typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass.
- 208 tests in the 8 related files pass: cloud-auth, cloud-auth-local, telemetry (3 files), TelemetryIdentityRuntime, cloud-session, cloud-telemetry.
- New tests cover:
  - the same sign-in result with a valid, invalid or missing id;
  - a replayed link handing the id over once;
  - error and state-mismatch links unchanged;
  - the id absent from the auth store, data dir, console and storage;
  - the address per build flavour;
  - every alias and event case.
- Gitleaks finds nothing.
- **Not run yet:** the full vitest suite (left to CI), and a live sign-in through the new page, which needs the website page deployed.

### Rollout
1. Merge and deploy the website page.
2. Sign in with a current packaged build started with `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT=https://orchestrator.inc/app/auth/return/`.
3. Merge this.
4. Keep `api.aoagents.dev/app/auth/return` registered in WorkOS until old desktops are gone.

**Notes:**
- `packages/mobile` still uses the old address on purpose: it has its own release, and the old address stays registered.
- #7384 touches the same redirect code and will need a rebase if this lands first.

title: feat(onboarding): guided first-run onboarding
body:
## What

A guided first-run onboarding for the desktop app. It shows once, on a fresh install with no projects, as a full-window takeover: copy on the left, a live preview of the app on the right, and a bottom bar with progress and the page's actions.

Four pages:

1. **Welcome.** What Orchestrator does, in one line. The preview plays the three parts on a loop: you describe the work in the orchestrator chat, workers start on the board, and the board sorts them by what they need from you (most land ready to merge).
2. **Create an account** (optional). Cloud sandboxes and the mobile app as the two reasons. An iPhone showing the mobile Workers tab slides in beside the window, with the same sessions. Skipped when already logged in.
3. **Your tools.** One checklist: GitHub CLI (install, `gh auth login`) and the coding agents (install, sign in). Continue needs one ready agent. Skipped when everything is ready.
4. **Your first project.** Open a folder or clone a repo. The agent questions are skipped: the best ready agent (Claude Code, then Codex, then the default priority order) runs both workers and the orchestrator. Once the project exists, the page becomes a first-task box; sending it posts the message to the orchestrator and opens its chat.

Skip setup is offered only on the last page, behind a confirmation.

## How

- `components/onboarding/FirstRunOnboarding.tsx`: the flow, mounted in `_shell.tsx`. Shown while the app-state marker `firstRunProjectPrompt` is `pending` (written by main, from #7569's plumbing) and there are no projects. Step persists in `localStorage` (`ao.firstRun.step`).
- `components/onboarding/OnboardingPreviews.tsx`: one persistent app window built from the real `product-ui` board and card views plus copies of the shell, sidebar, topbar, chat and agent picker markup. Only what changes animates (cards glide between lanes, rows unfold, pages swap in place).
- `components/onboarding/OnboardingPhone.tsx` + `lib/mobile-theme.ts`: the mobile Workers tab in HTML, coloured from the desktop's selected theme through the mobile app's own derivation (mirrored from `packages/mobile/lib/themeDerive.ts`, which the renderer can't import).
- `CreateProjectFlow` gains an optional `autoAgent` prop (only the onboarding passes it). The agent sheet still opens when the folder needs repository setup or creating fails.
- `styles.css`: the preview window's translucent material over a wallpaper, and the onboarding's chrome treatment in a translucent window (it's a `role="dialog"`, which the floating-surface rule would otherwise make solid).
- Copy in all 9 locales.

## Testing

Not run locally (typecheck and tests left to CI). Checked by hand in an isolated dev app: each page, the welcome loop, Create an account → Maybe later → project and Back, the stage collapse, auto-skips, and the skip confirmation.

Not yet checked: light theme, reduced motion, and a full first project + first message end to end.

title: [Bug] `question` tool from opencode-v2 sessions never renders a card, turn hangs in "Working" (0.14.9-nightly)
body:
### What happened

With `harness: opencode-v2`, when an agent calls the **`question`** tool the UI never renders an answerable card. The transcript stops right after the assistant's text, the session keeps showing `Working for Nm`, the composer shows *"Next message you send will be queued"*, and there is no way to answer. The message turn stays `running` and the session stays `activity_state = waiting_input` indefinitely.

### Environment

- AO `0.14.9-nightly.202611022329` (commit `25bc9b148f76`)
- macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)
- harness `opencode-v2`
- model served through a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- project kind `single_repo` on a self-managed GitLab instance

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a worker or orchestrator session with harness `opencode-v2`.
2. Give it a task that needs a decision, so the agent calls `question`.
3. Observed tool input shape:

```json
{
  "questions": [
    {
      "header": "short header",
      "question": "Which option should I take?",
      "options": [
        { "label": "Option A", "description": "..." },
        { "label": "Option B", "description": "..." }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

4. Nothing renders for this call: no card, no options, no plain-text fallback.

### Evidence

- provider transcript: last assistant message contains `tool: question` with `state.status = running`, and it never leaves `running`
- AO session row: `activity_state = waiting_input`
- conversation turn row: `state = running`
- UI: the assistant text renders, then nothing; only the spinner and "Next message you send will be queued" remain

### Expected

- Render the question together with its options so it can be answered (similar to the structured-question work in #6184), **or**
- if a harness path cannot render it, do not expose `question` to `opencode-v2` sessions, or fail fast instead of leaving the turn hanging.

### Related

- #6184 covers Codex blocking questions and MCP form/URL elicitation; the `opencode-v2` path looks uncovered.
- Similar symptoms reported earlier: #7610 (stale Working), #6726 (sticky waiting_input).

### Workaround

Project/global agent rules now forbid the `question` tool; agents list numbered options in plain text and the user replies with the number.

title: ci: reduce queue pressure with guarded PR and native jobs
body:
Code changes: +0 -0  
Tests: +118 -0  
Others: +129 -30 (workflow configuration and contributor docs)

## What

Reduce CI queue pressure in ten workflows through guarded execution and fewer race/vitest shards, with selector regression coverage and contributor guidance.

## Why

Avoid running expensive suites on draft and stacked PRs, and coalesce superseded main pushes. Historical queue-delay and capacity estimates are not new measurements or proven savings. Org plan, concurrency cap and spending limit remain unknown.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Go, Frontend and CLI E2E run heavy jobs on drafts and stacked bases | Existing jobs report skipped unless the PR is ready and targets main; ready, base-edit and draft-conversion events refresh the verdict |
| Native OS jobs run on every relevant PR | `ci:macos` enables frontend macOS; `ci:full` enables frontend macOS, Go Windows and the full CLI matrix. Apply labels before the next push; label changes alone do not restart CI |
| Every main push has its own heavy-workflow concurrency group | Pending main runs coalesce; active Go, Frontend and CLI E2E runs finish, preserving a completed main signal |
| Frontend gate requires macOS even when intentionally skipped | Policy and Linux dependencies must succeed; both macOS jobs must succeed when requested. Only unrequested native jobs may skip |
| Many jobs have no explicit runner timeout | Every job in the ten touched workflows has a timeout |
| Go core/chat/SQLite use 2/2/4 shards; frontend vitest uses 4 | Go uses 1/1/2; vitest uses 2. Full expanded Go matrices go from 14 to 10 jobs; Frontend including policy goes from 12 to 10. Six fewer runner jobs per qualifying full run |

## How

- Keep existing workflow names, job IDs, PR path triggers and main push coverage. Main-target policy is job-level rather than a workflow branch filter, so stacked checks still report skipped instead of disappearing.
- Keep the broad Frontend workflow-edit path trigger to preserve validation of workflow changes.
- Keep gitleaks and public-boundary on draft, stacked and docs-only PRs. No docs exclusions.
- Deliberately retain per-SHA main gitleaks runs: each push scans a distinct introduced-commit range, so canceling one could lose secret coverage. PR cancellation remains enabled.
- Add missing public-boundary and cloud-contract concurrency groups. Other schedules and release/build workflows are untouched.
- Heavy workflows cancel active PR runs only. The ref-scoped main group lets an active run finish while newer pushes replace its single pending run, avoiding cancellation starvation. Smaller applicable workflows still cancel superseded main work.
- Drop `labeled`/`unlabeled` from all three heavy workflows, avoiding unrelated triage-label restarts and avoiding newer skipped gates hiding failures. Keep `edited` so retargeting to main runs validation; title/body edits still rerun the full applicable suite and may restart active PR work. Today's metadata-event frequency was not measured, and the source audit's aggregate run counts cannot establish it. After this change, label/unlabel events generate zero Go/Frontend/CLI E2E runs; the remaining `edited` cost is explicitly unquantified.
- Created repository labels `ci:macos` and `ci:full`; documented use for native helpers/updater/packaging and Windows/cross-platform changes in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Apply before the next push. Old-run reruns can retain the original event payload, so they are not promised to refresh labels.
- Keep the full CLI OS matrix and gate checkout, setup and test steps, not matrix expansion. Unrequested native legs still briefly acquire OS runners and report successful no-op checks with the same names. This saves test work, not job count, and avoids relying on inaccessible required-check configuration.
- One small Frontend `policy` job computes native selection once. Both macOS jobs and the gate consume its output; the gate now includes `mac-update-helper`. Policy failure, cancellation, missing output or unexpected native skip fails the active gate. This adds one lightweight Linux job to applicable ready/main runs, not to draft/stacked heavy runs.
- This is partial Phase 2: native selection is label-only, not automatic path detection. Main retains the full OS matrix; no new nightly or manual trigger is introduced.
- Readable active rules on main require linear history only; the integration branch rule endpoint returned no rules. Classic protection endpoints returned 404, so inaccessible policy is not assumed absent. No check names were renamed.
- Public release documentation and build workflow use an explicit pinned ref/SHA and independent unsigned artifacts. Those workflows are unchanged. External exact-SHA CI consumers were not verified; coalesced pending main CI cannot promise green status on every historical SHA. Active heavy main runs are no longer canceled by later pushes.
- Shard merging is now explicitly authorized: core and chat retain singleton `[0]` matrices to preserve their first shard names, SQLite uses two alternating test-name partitions, and vitest uses `1/2` plus `2/2`. Core and chat execute their complete original package selections. Keep `-race` and `-count=1`; no test exclusions were added.

Retired internal shard legs no longer report; any inaccessible policy requiring those specific shard names would need migration to the stable gates. Readable main rules contain no required checks. Static-check consolidation is intentionally deferred to avoid removing more check IDs.
- Increase merged core/chat/SQLite jobs to 50 minutes with 40-minute package timeouts, and vitest jobs to 30 minutes. These are bounded safety margins for larger shards, not measured runtime claims.
- Add five dependency-free selector regression tests to the existing Frontend checks job, with a matching source-path trigger. The tests execute the actual Go workflow commands against a fake tool to prove package/test selection, race/cache flags and empty-selection failure, and assert frontend matrix/denominator agreement.

title: feat(artifacts): live-refresh an open local artifact when its file changes
body:
Code changes: +323 -11\
Tests: +625 -3\
Others: +106 -0 (generated `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`)

## What

An artifact that is open locally now updates by itself when the agent (or anything else) rewrites its file. Before, the preview kept the content it opened with until you closed and reopened it.

## Why

Cloud previews already pick up new versions, because a cloud file's URL carries its `updatedAt`. Local previews didn't:
- The open file's content query is keyed without the file's version, so nothing ever refetched it.
- The 15s workspace poll and the 30s artifact observer only refresh the file list, not an open file.
- The Artifacts gallery preview held a snapshot of the row it opened from, so it never saw a newer `updatedAt` (this affected cloud rows too).

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Agent edits `plan.md` while it's open in the Artifacts tab or the gallery preview: the preview stays on the old content until it is closed and reopened. | The preview shows the new content about 150ms after the write. An open HTML page reloads when its `updatedAt` changes. |

No screenshots: the change is visible only over time. See Testing.

## How

- **Daemon:** new stream `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/artifact-events`. It watches the session's artifact directory with the existing `workspacewatch` package (the watcher behind `workspace/events`) and sends only invalidation edges: `ready`, `artifacts_changed`, and a 15s `heartbeat`. It is mounted with the other long-lived streams (outside the REST timeout middleware), and refuses a missing artifact directory with 404 `ARTIFACT_DIR_NOT_FOUND`. The path is outside `artifact-files/` so it cannot shadow an artifact named `events`.
- **Renderer:** `lib/artifact-file-events.ts` keeps one ref-counted `EventSource` per session, with the same backoff and base-URL rebinding as the other SSE consumers. On each event it rereads that session's `session-artifact-file` queries within 150ms (a bounded window, so continuous writes still show progress), and the workspace list at most once a second, since that list carries the `updatedAt` that reloads an open HTML page.
- **Subscribers:** `useArtifactFileChanges` runs only while an artifact is open, in the session's Artifacts tab (not for remote-host sessions) and in the gallery preview. Local sessions use the daemon stream, and cloud sessions use their shared event stream. The gallery preview now follows its live row (looked up by `artifactKey`, falling back to the clicked row).

Why a stream rather than polling: an open artifact can sit idle for hours. Polling would reread it every tick, while the watch costs nothing until a file actually changes.

Known trade-offs:
- The watch leaves out what the artifact list leaves out (`.versions`, `node_modules`, `.git`, `__pycache__` and OS metadata), through `workspacewatch.WatchSkipping` and `sessionartifacts.Skips`. On macOS kqueue holds a descriptor for every file in a watched directory, so a tree of generated files must not be watched at all. A large tree of ordinary artifact files is still watched.
- If you are editing an artifact when the agent writes to it, your draft is kept, and saving is refused with the existing fingerprint conflict.

Cloud sessions get the same behaviour: #7663 was merged into this branch, and OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#44 has merged. An open cloud artifact listens on the session's existing cloud event stream for `artifact.changed` and rereads its file list, so no new cloud stream is added.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/httpd/...`: pass, including 3 new stream tests that write real files (rewrite in a subdirectory, new directory plus file, missing directory → 404).
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on `./internal/httpd/...`: 0 issues.
- `npm run api`: no drift after rebasing on current `main`.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`: clean.
- Vitest: 182 tests pass across the artifact files (`artifact-file-events`, `useArtifactFileChanges`, `useCloudArtifacts`, `ArtifactsView`, `SessionArtifactsView`, `ArtifactFileView`, `ArtifactHistory`), including:
  - stream sharing and teardown, per-session invalidation, throttling under continuous writes, backoff after a refused stream, rebinding to a new daemon port;
  - the gallery preview reloading a local page when its row's `updatedAt` changes (this test fails without the fix);
  - subscription only for an open local file, and never for cloud or remote-host sessions.
- Not yet exercised in the packaged desktop app.

title: feat(artifacts): live-refresh an open cloud artifact on artifact.changed
body:
Code changes: +50 -13\
Tests: +110 -9\
Others: +0 -0

Stacked on #7662 (local artifacts). Needs OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#44 for the event to arrive; without it nothing changes and the 5 s poll still applies.

## What

An open **cloud** artifact now updates as soon as the control plane commits a new version, rather than on the desktop's next 5 s poll of the cloud session list. Local artifacts behave as in #7662.

## Why

#7662 made local artifacts live through a daemon stream. Cloud artifacts already reload when their file list carries a new `updatedAt` (the file URL carries `?v=`), but the desktop reread that list only on its 5 s session poll. Combined with the worker's 30 s mid-turn rescan (fixed in ao-control-plane#44), a mid-turn edit could take ~35 s to show.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A cloud agent rewrites `plan.md` while it's open; the view updates after the next worker rescan plus the next 5 s poll. | With ao-control-plane#44, the view updates a few seconds after the write: the worker's sync, then this listener rereading the list. |

## How

- **Same hook for both cases:** `useArtifactFileChanges(session, enabled)` now takes the session.
  - Local sessions keep the daemon's `artifact-events` stream from #7662.
  - Cloud sessions listen with `useCloudSessionEventListener` on the session's one shared event stream (`session-events-hub`), the same way the cloud Files view follows `workspace.changed`. That listener adds no viewer presence, and no new stream is opened.
- **On `artifact.changed`:** it invalidates `["cloud-artifact-files", baseUrl, orgId, sessionId]` (a new `cloudArtifactSessionFilesQueryKey` prefix, so whichever version is current is reread). The new `updatedAt` changes the open file's versioned URL, which reloads it.
- **Bursts:** a listener that joins first gets the session's history replayed, and several commits can land together, so events are folded into one reread within 250 ms.
- **Where:** the session's Artifacts tab (any open artifact, not on remote hosts) and the gallery preview (local or cloud).

## Testing

- `npm run frontend:typecheck`: clean.
- Vitest: 166 tests pass across the artifact files (`useArtifactFileChanges`, `artifact-file-events`, `ArtifactsView`, `SessionArtifactsView`, `ArtifactFileView`, `ArtifactHistory`, `useCloudArtifacts`). New `useArtifactFileChanges.test.tsx` covers:
  - the local path subscribing only while enabled and unsubscribing on unmount;
  - a cloud session using its event stream instead of the daemon;
  - five `artifact.changed` events folding into one invalidation of the session's list key;
  - other event types being ignored.
- Not exercised against a staging control plane.

title: feat(desktop): another member's cloud session files are view only
body:
Code changes: +56 -25\
Tests: +62 -3\
Others: +24 -6 (contract, generated cloud-client schema, 9 locale strings)

## What

A cloud session's artifact files belong to the person who started it. Every other member of the organization can still open and read them, but the desktop no longer offers them anything that changes or copies the files:

- Edit, both the card's pencil and editing in the viewer
- Restore this version (they can still look at old versions)
- Delete
- Download
- Copy contents / Copy as Markdown
- Show in Finder / Open in Finder, since that copies the files to this machine

The file's menu says why: *"View only. Only the person who started this session can change, download or copy its files."*

The contract already carries `Session.createdByUserId` (from #7479). This PR extends its description and documents the `403 artifact_not_owner` that `saveSessionArtifact` and `restoreSessionArtifactVersion` now return to anyone else.

## Why

This is R1 in the share-links ownership review: another member's session files are read-only. Only the owner of a file may publish it, and the same rule now covers changing, removing and exporting it. The server half, which refuses deletes, edits and restores from non-creators, is OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#43.

## Before / After

File menu on a cloud session's file:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Your own session | Version history · Show in Finder · Copy as Markdown · Download · Delete artifact | unchanged |
| Another member's session | same as your own | Version history, then the "View only…" note |
| Card actions on another member's session | Edit · Delete · More actions | More actions only |
| Version preview on another member's session | Back to current · Restore this version | Back to current |
| Viewer on another member's session | editable | read-only (no save) |

I didn't capture screenshots. Showing this needs a second account in a team org on a deployed control plane. The behavior is covered by the tests below.

## How

- `canChangeSessionArtifacts(cloud, cloudUserId)` in `lib/artifacts.ts` is the one rule. Local sessions are always yours. A cloud session's files are yours only when `createdByUserId` is your control-plane user ID. `ArtifactActionsMenu`, which every artifact surface uses, and `SessionArtifactsView` both read it.
- **Which ID:** `cloudUserId` comes from `useCloudMeUserId` (`GET /me`), not `useCloudCp().userId`, which is the identity provider's ID and never matches `createdByUserId`. Until `/me` answers, the files stay view only, the same as the Share button.
- **Older control planes:** if a control plane doesn't send `createdByUserId`, the desktop shows the actions and the server decides. That keeps a newer desktop working against an older control plane. The cost: on a new control plane, a session with no creator on record (deleted account) still shows the actions and gets a 403 if you use them.
- `ArtifactVersionPreview`'s `onRestore` is now optional; with no handler, the Restore button isn't shown.
- **Not covered:** a non-creator can still read the file in the viewer (select and copy text, screenshot) and can still chat with the agent or open the terminal in a team session. The review records this as an accepted gap.

## Testing

- New in `SessionArtifactsView.test.tsx`:
  - On another member's session: the cards have no Edit, Delete or Open in Finder; the viewer opens read-only with no save; the menu shows only Version history and the note.
  - On your own session: every action is offered. The test's desktop account ID differs from its `/me` ID, so it fails if the wrong ID is compared (checked).
  - I checked that the view-only test fails when the rule always allows.
- New in `ArtifactHistory.test.tsx`: no Restore button without `onRestore`.
- New in `lib/artifacts.test.ts`: the rule's three cases (creator, other member or signed-out, local or older control plane).
- `npm run typecheck` in `frontend` is clean.
- `cloud:check` steps all pass: generate is stable, typecheck is clean, 31/31 cloud-client tests pass. `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh` reports ok.
- Full renderer suite: 10,808 passed, 50 failed across 4 files, none of which this PR touches:
  - `browser-profile-import` (47) and `browser-history-store` (1) need native modules I didn't build (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`). `browser-history-store` passes on its own.
  - `useSessionBrowserLink` (1) passes on its own.
  - `useSessionWorkspaceFiles.network` "stops missing workspace requests…" times out here and also on a clean `origin/main` checkout.

title: feat(mobile): send with Return on an iPad hardware keyboard
body:
Code changes: +330 -44\
Tests: +219 -4\
Others: +22 -0 (Expo module config and podspec)

## What

On an iPad with a hardware keyboard, Return now sends from the mobile chat composer and the reviewer composer, matching the desktop composer:

- **Return** and **Option+Return** send.
- **Cmd+Return** and **Ctrl+Return** steer the running turn when the draft can steer (text only, steer capability, turn running), and send otherwise.
- **Shift+Return** and the on-screen keyboard's Return still insert a newline.
- After a keyboard send the field keeps focus, so the next message can be typed straight away. The send button still dismisses the keyboard as before.
- In the reviewer chat every modifier sends (there is no steer). While the reviewer is working, Return is taken and does nothing, since that state has only Stop and no Send.

## Why

On an iPad keyboard case, none of Return, Ctrl+Return, Option+Return or Cmd+Return sent a message; Return only inserted a newline. Reaching for the screen to tap Send breaks typing flow, and the desktop composer already sends on Return.

## Before / After

Observed on an iPad Pro 11-inch simulator (iOS 26.5), Release build, keys sent as hardware keyboard HID events (`axe key` / `axe key-combo`) into the real `ChatComposer`:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Return inserts a newline | Return sends; the field stays focused and the next keystrokes land in it |
| Option+Return inserts a newline | Option+Return sends |
| Cmd+Return does nothing | Cmd+Return steers the running turn; with no turn running it sends |
| Ctrl+Return opens the Select / Select All edit menu, which then swallows the next keystrokes | Ctrl+Return steers the running turn (sends when idle); no menu, typing continues |
| Shift+Return inserts a newline | Unchanged |
| On-screen keyboard Return inserts a newline | Unchanged |

No recording attached: the change is keyboard-only, and the simulator build was torn down after testing. I can add one if a reviewer wants it.

## How

- A multiline RN `TextInput` reports only `"Enter"` from `onKeyPress`, with no modifiers and no way to tell a hardware Return from the on-screen one, so this needs native code. A local Expo module, `packages/mobile/modules/hardware-return`, provides a wrapper view that registers `UIKeyCommand`s for Return with no modifier, Option, Control and Command. Key commands only come from hardware keyboards, so the on-screen keyboard is untouched. Shift+Return is deliberately not registered, so it falls through to the field.
- `canPerformAction` declines while an input method is composing (`markedTextRange`), so Return commits a Japanese/Chinese/Korean composition instead of sending a half-typed message.
- **Ctrl+Return is also iPadOS's keyboard "click".** In any `UITextView` it opens the edit menu, and the open menu then takes all hardware keystrokes, so the next message silently went nowhere. An lldb trace showed the text view's `com.apple.UIKit.keyPressClickDriverPrimary` press recognizer starts presenting the menu on key-down, before any key command runs, so cancelling it from the handler is too late. The wrapper therefore keeps recognizers named `keyPressClickDriver*` disabled on its own field for as long as it is on screen, independent of whether Return is currently taken, and restores them when it leaves the window. Tap and long-press menus use other recognizers and still work; plain text fields elsewhere are unaffected (verified). The lookup by name uses public API only; if a future iPadOS renames it, Ctrl+Return still sends and the menu just reappears.
- JS: `HardwareReturn.ios.tsx` wraps the field only when the native module exists (`requireOptionalNativeModule`), so an older binary renders the field exactly as before. `HardwareReturn.tsx` (Android and other platforms) renders the children directly, with no wrapper in the row.
- Return is taken only while the composer can send (the Send button's own `sendBlocked` condition). While it is pending, disabled or loading its draft, Return stays the field's and inserts a newline instead of being caught and dropped; the keyboard click stays off regardless, so Ctrl+Return still opens no menu then.
- `useKeyboardSendRefocus`: a keyboard send makes the field read-only, which takes its focus. The hook holds the composer open from the send until the field reports focus again (the pill opens on focus, so otherwise it closed and reopened after each send), refocuses once per send, and leaves focus alone if the user moved to another input while the send was in flight. A 500 ms settle timer releases the hold if no focus event arrives.
- `hardwareReturnIntent` maps modifiers to the existing send/steer intents, and `composerDeliveryRoute` still decides whether a steer is eligible, so Return follows the same rules as the Send and Steer buttons.
- **Release impact:** this adds native code, so it changes the fingerprint runtime version and ships with the next store build, not as an OTA.

Not in scope: Android hardware keyboards (Chromebooks, tablets) keep inserting a newline. That would be a separate `dispatchKeyEvent` wrapper.

## Testing

- Mobile CI job run locally on Node 20 (`npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`): 347 files, 3420 tests pass (on top of the native overhaul, #7839).
- New unit tests: modifier → intent mapping; Return sends without dismissing the keyboard and refocuses the field once the send lands (confirmed the test fails without the refocus); Cmd/Ctrl+Return steers an eligible draft and sends an ineligible one; the wrapper is off while the agent is stopped and while the composer is pending or disabled; the composer stays open across a keyboard send whose field blurs (fails without the hold). `useKeyboardSendRefocus`: refocus after the send, no refocus when another input took focus or the field kept it, one refocus per send, settle timeout. `ReviewerComposer`: Return sends and refocuses when idle; while the reviewer is busy the wrapper stays on (so Ctrl+Return can't reopen the edit menu) and Return does nothing (confirmed this test fails on the earlier `&& !busy` version); off when stopped.
- iPad Pro 11-inch simulator (iOS 26.5), Release build from this branch, temporary lab route rendering the real `ChatComposer` (not committed). Hardware keys via `axe`: every row of the table above, including Ctrl+Return twice in a row followed by typing, a multi-line Shift+Return draft sent with Option+Return, and queue vs steer while a turn runs. Also checked that an unwrapped `TextInput` still opens its menu on Ctrl+Return and that tapping the focused composer still opens the edit menu.
- Re-run after the rebase onto #7839, on a fresh Release build with the lab route logging every `onExpandedChange`. A/B with one binary and two Hermes bundles: without the hold, each keyboard send logged `EXPANDED false` then `true` (the composer closed and reopened); with it, none. Pending and disabled: Return inserts a newline, Ctrl+Return opens no menu, typing continues; with both off, Return sends the multi-line draft. Running turn: Ctrl+Return twice and Cmd+Return steer, Shift+Return newline, Option+Return and Return send, no menu at any point, typing continues without a tap. The plain field still opens its menu on Ctrl+Return; tapping the focused composer still opens the edit menu.
- **Not yet tested on a physical iPad keyboard case.** CI has no native iOS build for the mobile app; the Release `xcodebuild` above was local.

title: fix(artifacts): show a poster frame for video artifact cards
body:
Fixes #7670

## Summary
Video artifact cards (`.mp4`, `.webm`, `.mov`, `.m4v`, `.ogv`) in the Artifacts gallery and the session rail showed a grey placeholder with a generic file icon. `ArtifactThumbnail` never had a video branch, so these paths fell through to `unavailable`. This isn't a regression: the gallery (#7098) shipped without video previews, and viewer playback (#6880) was never affected.

This PR renders local video artifacts as a muted `<video preload="metadata">`. The card stays inert and the video has no controls and no autoplay. It uses the same streamed artifact URL and `crossOrigin` handling as the viewer's `FileMediaPreview`:
- **No whole-file load.** The daemon route uses `http.ServeContent` (206/Range, `video/mp4`). With a metadata preload, Chromium fetches the header and the first frame. The reporter's files are faststart, and the 42 MB release video's `moov` is 126 KB.
- **Same lazy loading as image cards:** the video mounts only near the viewport.
- **Fallback:** a decode or load error shows the existing placeholder, which now uses a video file icon.
- **No server-side thumbnails and no cache,** so nothing new is written to disk.

Cloud video cards stay placeholders. That would need the signed-link refresh flow the image and PDF cards use, so it's left as a follow-up.

## Tests
- New `ArtifactThumbnail.test.tsx` cases (`local video artifact thumbnails`): a metadata-only `<video>` renders with the streamed URL for mp4/webm/mov, and a decode error falls back to the placeholder. All 4 fail on `main` and pass here.
- `vitest`: ArtifactThumbnail, ArtifactsView, SessionArtifactsView, ArtifactFileView: 161 passed.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`: passed.

## Risks / not verified
- I did not run the app in the Electron lab because disk space is tight. Painting the first frame from `preload="metadata"` is standard Chromium behaviour and is the same element the viewer already uses, but the change hasn't been checked visually in the real app.
- Many video cards in view each open a media element. They are lazy, metadata-only and muted, but they aren't capped the way HTML/PDF live previews are.

title: fix(accounts): show the CLI login and a saved account with the same login once
body:
## Summary

Settings → Claude Code → Account listed the same login twice: once as the CLI's own login (`~/.claude`) and once as the account added in AO. AO's duplicate check ran only when an account was added; a CLI login signed in outside AO afterwards was never compared again.

- **Backend** (`agentaccounts.List`): the CLI login gets `sameLoginAs` = the saved account signed in as the same login (same provider, case-insensitive email, both signed in). Exposed on `GET /agents/accounts`.
- **Same login = same email and same organization**: one email can belong to several Claude organizations (e.g. personal and Team), which are separate subscriptions. The Claude CLI's `orgId` from `claude auth status` is now read, and two logins match only when their organizations match too. When either side reports none, email alone decides, as before. For a saved account that is signed out, AO uses the last organization it saw it signed in to (kept in memory).
- **Add account** (`VerifyLogin`): re-reads the CLI login before the duplicate check (a cached "signed out" let a terminal sign-in from moments ago through), and refuses the login of a saved account that is signed out or holds another login. You sign that account in again instead of creating a second folder.
- **Settings**: the CLI row folds into the saved account's row, with AO usage summed across both. While the CLI login is itself the default it stays its own row, so the saved account can still be made the default.
- **Usage page** (added on main since): its Limits view lists a login once too, merged and labelled the same way as Settings.
- **Sign-in messages** (found by QA, also on main): a sign-in that ends with an API key now says so (`not_subscription`) instead of "Not signed in yet" forever, and a signed-out CLI login is named "Claude Code CLI login", not "OAuth token".
- **Session account picker**: one choice per login. A session on the CLI login also keeps its saved twin listed, so it can move to that folder.
- **Same email, several organizations**: `orgId` and `orgName` are returned by `GET /agents/accounts`. When two listed accounts share an email, each is labelled with its organization, or as the CLI login when the organization doesn't tell them apart.

## Before / after (real logins, real renderer)

Before = base `23840aa541`, after = this PR. Both read the same Mac's real Claude Code CLI login and one AO-added account that hold the same login. The email is shown as `user@example.com`. Method, raw files and full test logs: [evidence comment](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7674#issuecomment-6605932055).

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d038ef52e24a09cf416252d45f209e5103819ec5/before-settings.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/71512704a3924945c67cb67f228c31b27d2317ac/after-settings.png) |
| Same login listed twice (38.8M + 1.1B tokens) | One row, 1.2B tokens (the sum) |

`GET /api/v1/agents/accounts`, CLI login entry: before has no `sameLoginAs`; after has `"sameLoginAs": "d5ed0d17-35be-4f78-8197-d154f76809b0"` (the saved account).

New tests on the base code: 9 Go bug scenarios and 2 panel tests fail. On this PR, all pass.

## Scenarios covered (fail before, pass after)

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Account added, then the terminal signs in to it (also: switching from another login, email case differs) | two rows | one row |
| Terminal signed in, same login added in AO within the 5-minute cache | duplicate saved | refused |
| Saved `a@` signed out, `a@` added again | second folder | refused |
| Same email in another Claude organization (CLI, signed-in or signed-out saved account) | merged / refused | separate rows / added |

These must stay separate rows, and are tested: the CLI on another login or signed out; the saved account signed out or holding another login; the same email on Codex and Claude. A failed identity check that was signed in last time still counts as the same login, so the row doesn't flicker.

## Tests

- `go test -race ./internal/service/agentaccounts/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/`; `go test ./internal/httpd/...` (spec drift); golangci-lint v2.13.2: 0 issues; `go build ./...`; `go vet ./internal/...`
- Vitest: `useAgentAccounts.test.ts`, `AgentAccountsSection.test.tsx`, i18n suites: 34 passed. The new panel tests fail on the old component.
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in `frontend/src`. `packages/product-ui` errors come from deps that aren't installed locally.
- Read-only check against a real `~/.claude` login and a real AO account with the same email: the CLI view got `sameLoginAs` set to the saved account.

## Risks / follow-ups

- No visual check in the real Electron app (it can't build on the dev Mac). The UI is covered by component tests.
- The merged row doesn't carry the CLI login's **Log out** button. If the terminal signs out, its own row returns with its controls.
- **Codex** reports no workspace ID through AO's client, so Codex logins still match on email alone.
- A saved account's organization isn't stored. After a daemon restart, a signed-out account's organization is unknown until it's next seen signed in, so the add check falls back to email for it.

title: fix: name sidechat tabs from the first accepted message
body:
Code changes: +10 -1  
Tests: +213 -2  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Automatically name a sidechat tab from its first accepted message. For example, sending `Explain this code` changes the tab from `Side Chat` to `Explain this code` without waiting for an agent response.

## Why

Numbered default labels make separate sidechat conversations difficult to identify. The first question provides a useful title while preserving the existing manual rename behavior.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Sending `Explain this code` leaves the tab named `Side Chat`. | The tab becomes `Explain this code` as soon as the message is accepted and the list refreshes. |
| Sidechats retain numbered default labels unless renamed manually. | Each new sidechat takes a normalized, one-line title of up to 80 Unicode characters from its first accepted question. Manual names remain authoritative. |

Desktop screenshots are unavailable: the isolated Windows Electron launch cannot rebuild `better-sqlite3` because there is no supported Python installation for node-gyp and no matching Electron 44.7.0 prebuilt binary. Native visual verification remains outstanding; the Before / After table describes the behavior covered by automated tests.

## How

- Assign the automatic label under the store mutex when reserving the first turn, after validation and duplicate detection. Reuse `NormalizeTitle` and retain the default if it produces an empty title.
- Preserve manual labels, later-message stability, idempotent delivery, queued-message edits/cancellations, and existing in-memory recovery.
- Refresh the tab list after a successful send without treating a refresh transport failure as a failed delivery.
- No API, storage schema, or generated contract changes. Existing conversations are not backfilled; attachment/excerpt-only messages use the existing fallback question text.

title: fix(chat): re-sign the bundled Node when it crashes on Intel Macs (#6621)
body:
Release builds sign the x64 acp-runtime Node without
com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory, so V8 aborts
(exit 133) at JIT tier-up and every Claude Code Chat session fails with
"ACP initialize: peer disconnected before response".

On darwin/amd64 the daemon now smoke-tests the bundled Node once. If it
shows that crash, it copies the binary under the AO data dir, ad-hoc
re-signs the copy with allow-jit and allow-unsigned-executable-memory,
and launches the adapter with it. The app bundle is never modified. If
the repair fails, the error names the cause and suggests Terminal mode.

The release signer still needs to keep the entitlement; this keeps
users working when a build ships without it.

title: release: promote main (25bc9b148f) to stable, 2026-11-03
body:
## What

Moves `stable` from `403a8c8385` (v0.14.8, #7447) to `main` at `25bc9b148f` (#7551), the commit nightly `v0.14.9-nightly.202611022329` was built from. That is 103 commits. Version: **0.14.9**.

### Why there is a merge commit

`stable` is not an ancestor of `main`: it carries #7447's merge commit and the earlier hotfix and cherry-pick merges. Its tree is byte-identical to `fe0550a4e8` (`git diff fe0550a4e8 403a8c8385` is empty), and `fe0550a4e8` is an ancestor of `25bc9b148f`, so everything on `stable` is already in this release.

This branch is `25bc9b148f` plus one `-s ours` merge of `stable` (`f6f15e02fb`). That merge changes no files (`git diff 25bc9b148f f6f15e02fb` is empty). It only makes `stable` an ancestor again, so this release can fast-forward. There are no cherry-picks.

## Validation

- **Already shipped as a nightly:** `v0.14.9-nightly.202611022329` was built from exactly `25bc9b148f`, so this release is code nightly users already run.
- **CI on `25bc9b148f`:** no check failed. 43 passed and 15 were skipped. 12 `owners`/`sync` runs were cancelled (superseded), not failed.

title: feat(mobile): swipe and filmstrip for artifacts in the viewer
body: Code changes: +352 -34\ Tests: +62 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Opening an artifact from the mobile Artifacts gallery now opens a swipeable viewer over the session's artifacts, in gallery order. Two ways to move between them: - **Swipe** left or right to step through the artifacts. - **Filmstrip** under the page: a row of small tiles for every artifact, like a photo app's strip. The page on screen is outlined and the row keeps it in the middle as you swipe. Tap any tile to go straight to that artifact. The header shows the file's name and its position (e.g. "2 of 4"), and its version-history and ⋯ actions act on the page on screen. ## Why Going through several artifacts, such as a set of screenshots, meant going back to the grid and tapping the next card each time. Swiping fixes the stepping; the filmstrip shows how many there are, where you are, and reaches any one of them in a tap. ## Before / After Android emulator (API 35, Release build), rebased onto `main` after the native overhaul (#7837–#7839). The same scratch daemon and nine artifacts are used on both sides; "Before" is `main` with this PR's mobile files reverted. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | No strip: back to the grid to reach another artifact | | | | | ## How - `app/artifact/[sessionId].tsx`: - `ArtifactPager` exposes `scrollToPage` through a ref. A swipe and a strip tap both leave it on the same page index, so the effects that follow the page index do not scroll a second time. - `ArtifactFilmstrip` is a horizontal `FlatList` with fixed-size tiles (`getItemLayout`), so it can jump to any tile. It scrolls to the current page, centred, and animates after the first placement. - The review tray lifts above the strip, and the strip is hidden while a comment composer is open, so comments always attach to the file on screen. - Page order is the list's order when the viewer opened (`stableArtifactOrder` in `lib/artifacts.ts`). The list is newest first, so without this a file the agent rewrites would jump to the front, remount its page and lose its scroll. New files go at the end; removed ones drop out, and the pager follows a removal in a layout effect, before paint. - Sideways scrolling inside a page: on Android the pager would otherwise take every sideways drag. `ChatMarkdown` takes an opt-in `nestedScroll` prop that only the viewer page passes; it sets `nestedScrollEnabled` on the table and on unwrapped code (left off in chat and in filmstrip previews, where a nested-scroll view under the finger would stop the strip from scrolling). The viewer's WebView sets `nestedScrollEnabled` too, so it, which keeps its own drags (panning a wide or zoomed page, a pinch). **On Android an HTML page is therefore left through the strip, not a swipe.** iOS hands the gesture over natively. - A tile whose image fails to load, or whose preview fails, falls back to the kind's glyph. The strip has no `initialScrollIndex`: when the tiles fit without scrolling, the list rendered from the current tile on and never drew the earlier ones. - `lib/artifactVisual.ts`: the per-kind glyphs and tints move out of the gallery screen so the strip and the grid share them. - Tile images use the same authenticated image source as the gallery cards, so each image artifact downloads once more for its tile. - Text, markdown and HTML tiles show the same live peek as their gallery card (`ArtifactThumbnail`), and load only while on screen. A preview that fails falls back to the kind's glyph. Other kinds show their glyph. title: fix: close Sentry blind spots in the daemon and desktop app
body:
Code changes: +1264 -297  
Tests: +886 -29  
Others: +33 -12  

## What

Closes the places where real failures never reached Sentry, in both the daemon (`ao-daemon`) and the desktop app (`ao-electron`).

## Why

Sentry only saw a fraction of real failures. The daemon captured HTTP 5xx, panics and relaunch failures, and nothing else. Electron main captured only crashes, and kept a random 25% of everything else. Example: the Claude Code model picker error in #7672 ("no credential could be resolved for this provider") has zero events in Sentry, because discovery failures answer 200 with the error inside the catalog.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Async chat spawn failures (after the 201) only log | Captured as `Async chat spawn failed` |
| Spawn/resume/project-git faults answered 409/400 skip Sentry | Registered fault codes captured with `category=http_fault`; status codes unchanged |
| 503 from a hung git/exec call (`context.DeadlineExceeded`) dropped | Captured with `category=http_timeout`; lock contention 503s still dropped |
| Model discovery failures (200 + warning) invisible | Unclassified failures captured per agent; signed-out/expired/rejected stay out |
| Chat turn, projection, provider error, wake/drain failures only log | Captured under `chat` with the agent tag |
| Boot restore, reconcile, interface transitions, quarantine only log | Captured under `session_manager` |
| Reaper mass-death breaker only logs | Captured as `Reaper mass-death breaker tripped` |
| Daemon won't start / exits: PostHog only | `Electron main daemon failure (spawn_failed / exited / …)` with signal or exit code |
| Auto-update failures: `console.error` only | Captured per phase; offline, timeouts, rate limits, 404s and server outages stay out |
| IPC handler throws swallowed | Captured per channel (`channel:app:chooseDirectory`) |
| 75% of non-fatal Electron errors randomly dropped | All consented errors kept |
| Renderer errors before the consent policy loads are dropped | Up to 20 held in preload and forwarded once the policy is known |
| One noisy `TypeError` exhausts the renderer budget for every `TypeError` | Budget per error type and call site |
| Remote-host and GitHub daemon API errors bypass reporting | Same reporting as the local API client |
| Router boundaries swallow session-route errors | Global router catch and session error components report once without changing the visible fallback |
| Non-API query and mutation failures stay inside React Query | Cache hooks report unexpected client errors, excluding transport-owned failures |
| Side-chat recovery and snapshot errors only warn locally | Consent-gated, deduplicated and budgeted main-process reports |
| Entry-module failures happen before renderer handlers bind | Main-world preload handlers capture before imports, read policy independently, then hand off without duplicate listeners |

## How

Aggregate CI gates skip whole-workflow cancellation while retaining their failure assertions for genuine failed dependencies.

**Daemon**
- `sentryobs.CaptureBackground(ctx, err, component, operation, extra)` is the one path for failures off the request path. It admits at most four concurrent sends without a retry queue, so controller locks and storage transactions never wait on the network. Admission pins the existing consent gate; opt-out drains admitted sends. Concurrent events use isolated Sentry scopes. Components, operations and reasons are allowlisted; agent identifiers are shape-checked; unregistered extra fields are dropped before fingerprinting and the scrubber drops unsafe tags, so no raw error text, project/session IDs or paths are sent.
- `sentryobs.IsFaultCode` lists codes that are daemon faults even though they answer 4xx/503. `WORKSPACE_PROVISION_FAILED` and `WORKSPACE_CLEANUP_FAILED` (the user's own scripts), clone/network codes and auth codes are deliberately not on it.
- Each package filters its own expected state before capturing: `ErrChatAuthRequired`, `ErrAgentModelDiscoverySignInRequired`, `SetupStepError`, canceled contexts.
- Held main-process captures cannot interrupt startup if the telemetry sink throws.
- Fingerprint-budget overflow now uses one bucket per operation instead of one shared `unknown` bucket, so a noisy day can't hide a new failure elsewhere.

**Electron**
- `main/main-error-capture.ts`: `captureMainError({ category, reason, error?, detail? })` with fixed categories and reasons; `detail` only accepts `signal:SIG…`, `code:N`, `channel:…`, `kind:…`. Captures before consent loads are held (max 20), and the sink applies consent.
- `installIpcErrorCapture` wraps `ipcMain.handle` once; errors still reject back to the renderer unchanged. Typed expected remote connectivity, sign-out and validation errors stay out; genuine unexpected throws are captured. `telemetry:*` channels are skipped.
- Daemon failures are reported from `setDaemonStatus`, once per transition into a failure. `not_ready`, `not_configured` and `daemon_unreachable` are transitional and not reported.

**Additional desktop capture boundaries**
- Router and React Query cache boundaries share object-identity deduplication. Local, remote-host and GitHub daemon failures retain API ownership; typed control-plane failures remain owned by their service. Existing API message wrappers preserve that ownership without changing their UI text. Unknown client failures and successful responses with missing data remain reportable.
- Preload installs a self-contained main-world handler before renderer imports and reads the existing consent policy itself. Startup reports use fixed text, a standard type and validated asset positions. Runtime handlers take over the same listeners; opted-out captures are discarded without replay, and a late initial policy response cannot replace a newer broadcast.
- Side-chat restore/snapshot failures use fixed main-process labels, error-identity deduplication and a five-per-minute/200-per-UTC-day budget. Expected connection, authentication, cancellation and stale-attachment states stay out. Recovery retry and rejection behavior is preserved.

**Intentional omissions**
- Migration diagnostics and detailed cause classification are out of scope.
- Native crash dumps (minidump / `crashReporter`): they capture process memory and need a privacy-policy decision first. Separate PR.
- The renderer does not report daemon fault codes or catalog warnings itself: the daemon now owns those, so reporting from both would double-count.
- Cloud control-plane client errors: that service's errors belong to its own monitoring.

## Testing

- Latest final rebased tree: Test Files  673 passed (673);       Tests  11542 passed | 9 skipped (11551). Both typechecks, chat capture race regression, full Sentry race suite and CI-pinned backend lint pass (zero issues).

- Latest conflict resolution: rebased all 14 existing commits onto main `2cc4111357bdbcfaf735726da94a7f80991e7add`. Preserved upstream PDF rendered-content coverage and existing cleanup assertions, plus the new Chrome setup flow and API ownership. All 54 focused PDF, Chrome, sign-in, preload and capture regressions pass. No extra native review was started.

- November 5 final rebased head: complete frontend suite **667 files passed, 11,438 tests passed, 9 skipped**. Both typechecks, chat capture race regression, full Sentry race suite and CI-pinned backend lint pass (zero lint issues).

- November 5 conflict resolution: rebased onto main `1afe0b89a10583efa180e84d977f72f96fb81c74`, preserving all 13 existing commits. Preserved the new native sign-in flow and carried API error ownership through its IPC response and display wrappers. All 37 focused sign-in, main IPC, preload and capture regressions pass. No native-review rerun was started.

- Final native-review fix head: complete frontend suite **646 files passed, 11,199 tests passed, 9 skipped**; both typechecks pass. Complete chat package passes; focused chat capture and Codex normalization race tests, full Sentry race suite, and backend lint pass.

- Native-review follow-up: known provider usage limits stay out of chat faults; Electron invocation rejections retain main-process ownership and disconnected hosts remain expected API state. In-memory transport regressions, Codex normalization race tests, full chat suite, Sentry race suite, and 63 focused IPC/cache capture tests pass. Backend lint reports zero issues.

- Final import-only rebase validation: 92/92 artifact-version, capture-gap, preload, side-chat and Settings regressions pass; both TypeScript checks pass. The complete frontend suite was not repeated after this import-only rebase.

- Complete frontend suite before the final import-only rebase passed: Test Files  645 passed (645);       Tests  11184 passed | 9 skipped (11193) (four test processes, unchanged timeouts). The earlier full run exposed the corrected Settings timer fixture and two load-sensitive failures; all pass in this complete rerun.

- Rebased onto main `cf321a61ebe82df869cccdfd5ca10e75d9cd3bc0`, preserving all existing commits. Main advanced during the complete frontend run, requiring a second import-only artifact conflict resolution. Added API ownership propagation for main's new avatar query and isolated Settings test reconciliation timers. Both typechecks and 145 Settings/project-creation tests pass. CI-pinned backend lint reports zero issues; Sentry and all HTTP/API-spec race packages pass.

- Latest complete frontend suite after closing the four non-native capture gaps: **637 files passed, 10,982 tests passed, 9 skipped**. Both frontend and E2E typechecks pass.
- Regression coverage includes real router loader failures and StrictMode, query/mutation errors, raw/wrapped/non-JSON API deduplication, missing data and unknown client failures, preload serialization and runtime handoff, read-only policy bootstrap, opt-out without replay, stale policy responses, side-chat restore/snapshot capture and expected-state exclusions, SDK scrubbing, and minute/day retry budgets.

- Native-review fixes: 142/142 passed across main-error capture, real remote IPC handlers, telemetry initialization, telemetry sanitizers and renderer Sentry. Covers offline, unauthorized, both sign-out paths and unexpected throws; also exhausts one real exception location before reporting another for window errors, rejected promises and React boundaries.
- CI fixture correction: the cloud-PDF preview test now supplies the PDF.js text-layer render/cancel contract and explicitly verifies cleanup on unmount. The full media-preview file passes 16/16 tests, and both frontend typechecks pass after this change.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: passed after the review fixes (Node 24.22.2).
- Full backend lint passed with CI-pinned Go 1.27.1 and golangci-lint 2.13.2 after correcting transition context propagation and import grouping. The interface-transition race suite, Go build and vet passed after the context fix.

Representative Git conditional-include (`commandcode`) and tmux test failures reproduce against a temporary export of `main`. The HTTP IPv6-loopback test also hit a graceful-shutdown deadline. Failed packages were `adapters/agent/commandcode`, `adapters/agent/opencodev2`, `adapters/chatdriver/acp`, `adapters/runtime/tmux`, `cli`, `httpd`, `service/session`, `service/shellterm`, `service/systemcheck` and `session_manager`. Only the representative commandcode and tmux failures were reproduced on main; other baseline equivalence is unverified.

title: fix(desktop): open a terminal with Cmd+T on remote sessions
body:
## Summary
Cmd+T (new terminal) did nothing on a remote machine's session. The shell layout (`routes/_shell.tsx`) skipped the shortcut whenever the route had a `hostId`, and opened shells through `useOpenShellTerminal()` with no host, which only reaches the local daemon. That gate dates from multi-host support (#5921), when the shortcut could only open local shells.

Remote session terminals are already supported: the tab strip's "+" button calls `useOpenShellTerminal(hostId)`. The shortcut now does the same:
- `useOpenShellTerminal(routeParams.hostId)` opens the shell on the host that owns the session on screen.
- Both `hostId` gates are removed; the shortcut still needs a session on screen.
- Remote routes pass the route's `projectId`, because the local workspace lookup does not cover them.

## Tests
- Added a regression test to `shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx`: on a remote session route, Cmd+T opens the shell on that route's host for that session.
- Not run locally; CI is the gate. Not yet tested against a real remote host.

## Risks
None known beyond the above. Local and cloud session behavior is unchanged.

title: feat: add full-history find in chat
body:
Code changes: +1747 -16 Tests: +1264 -25 Others: +525 -10 ## What Add **Find in chat** to locate case-insensitive literal substrings in the active chat’s retained user and agent messages, including history outside the viewport. Open it with **Ctrl+F** on Windows/Linux or **Cmd+F** on macOS. The binding is editable in **Settings → Shortcuts**, with live reassignment, alternatives, conflict handling, and reset to default. The bar shows an exact occurrence counter such as `2/5`, highlights matches, and navigates with previous/next or Enter/Shift+Enter while preserving the composer draft. The 320px bar floats at the top-right of main and side chats without resizing the message viewport or shifting messages. It uses the app's 10px corner-radius token, a 40%-opacity container focus ring, and shared compact quiet icon buttons. Clickable inline file references remain included in search highlighting. The bar stays visible when focus leaves it, but search requests, timers, navigation work, and highlight observers stop. Interacting with the bar or using its shortcut refreshes against the latest history. Existing highlights remain until their DOM nodes change or search closes. Initial searches use an accessible loader; refreshes retain the completed count until replacement. There is no standalone launch button or native input clear button. ## Why Finding a specific instruction, code fragment, or explanation requires complete occurrence navigation within a chat. The existing Ctrl+K Command Palette is designed to discover relevant messages across chats and cannot provide the same substring-search contract. Ctrl+K, session search, and file search remain unchanged. ## Before / After Updated screenshots supplied by the author show the current floating Find in chat bar. The comparison below uses the same conversation with search closed and open; the closed state is a current-build comparison, not a capture from the base branch. | Before / without search | After | | --- | --- | | Scrolling an active match out of the mounted timeline could snap the reader back. | Each navigation consumes its reveal once; manual scrolling stays independent of the active match. | | Markdown hard breaks counted the `
` and following newline separately, shifting offsets and preventing exact highlight/reveal. | Both hard-break forms count as one break, with exact DOM ranges in settled and streaming text. | | **4. Without searching** — the find bar is closed and text has no search highlights. ![Without searching](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec76c57d-8e1c-4f65-a78d-ea1b012b7a2d) | **2. When i press ctrl+f** — the floating Find in chat input opens. ![When i press ctrl+f](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fe166e3-7a7b-4d3d-b8b3-1fac75839c74) | | The conversation has no active search query or occurrence navigation. | **1. Search** — `ts` reports `2/6`; highlights include the inline `example.ts` reference and `tsc` / `example.ts` inside the fenced PowerShell command block. ![Search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/649769f5-640f-4e2c-8df2-a05044bdcf06) | | With search closed, no result status is shown. | **3. Search (but no result)** — `asdasd` displays `No results`. ![Search (but no result)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c3fe3db-df12-41e8-b011-4bb7fe5735e8) | | Opening search previously consumed layout space and reduced the message viewport. | The 320px bar overlays the conversation at a 12px top/right inset. | | The bar previously had pill corners, a full-brightness focus ring, and custom circular controls. | Uses the app's 10px radius, a 40%-opacity container focus ring, and standard compact quiet buttons. | | Clickable inline filenames were counted but could fail to highlight/reveal because button text was skipped. | Inline file-reference text participates in highlighting and offset mapping; toolbar controls remain excluded. | The Search screenshot demonstrates matching in code-related text and a fenced command block. The TypeScript code block is also visible, but that screenshot does not show a selected match inside its body. Tool execution output remains outside the search scope. [Earlier feature walkthrough and historical screenshots](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7684#issuecomment-6609285613). ## How 1. **Separate matching, shared foundations.** Ctrl+F uses standard Go substring matching after Unicode case folding, canonical normalization, and whitespace normalization. It reuses the shortcut and transcript-navigation infrastructure. Ctrl+K keeps its existing SQLite FTS5 word-based search, stemming, and final-word prefix matching. 2. **Every occurrence versus ranked messages.** Ctrl+F searches the active chat and returns exact totals with pages of up to 200 occurrence references in transcript order. Ctrl+K searches across chats and returns up to eight relevant message results, falling back to recency for very common queries. Its limited, ranked results cannot power complete next/previous navigation. 3. **Displayed text and precise highlights.** Ctrl+F projects Markdown into displayed text, so `hello **world**` can match `hello world`. Punctuation is literal, accents are preserved, and offset maps keep highlights correct after normalization. Ctrl+K indexes stored message text and treats punctuation as word separators. Tool output, reasoning, attachments, inactive branches, queued drafts, and embedded artifacts are excluded from Find in chat. 4. **Different efficiency tradeoffs.** Ctrl+K’s persistent index suits discovery across many chats. Ctrl+F scans one chat for complete substring counts, supports active streaming refreshes, and adds no persistent index. It uses a bounded transient snapshot cache and bounded responses; paging can still repeat scanning and text preparation. Read-only find/history-window routes, revision-bound cursors, cancellation, and focus-based suspension limit unnecessary work. Transports without complete history explicitly report that limitation. ## Testing Latest merge follow-up (`bef3a26ddf`): merged `main` at `01612ebf5e` and resolved both test conflicts. No additional production changes beyond the upstream merge. Preserved both the hard-break find regressions and upstream link-handler regressions. The occlusion test retains upstream settled-capture retries and failure artifacts, plus decoded-pixel tolerance, the deliberate bleed-through control, and visibility cleanup. Local Node 24 / macOS validation so far: **423 tests passed** across the four complete find/Markdown/workspace suites; all **4 occlusion Playwright cases passed**, including the negative control; frontend/E2E typechecks, Go build/vet, focused Go find/API tests, API/SQL generation without drift, and the public-boundary check passed. The renderer run also had a windowed turn-settle assertion fail before it was stopped. These broad local results are incomplete and are not evidence of a clean full-suite run. The exact failed Linux CI merge reproduced the original screenshot failure in three of four cases. Captured images had identical geometry and only icon/edge rasterization differences of up to 5/255 per channel. The test now compares decoded RGBA pixels with that sub-2% channel tolerance, requiring zero pixels outside it. A negative control removes the production clip and requires real underlying-card paint to be detected; cleanup restores both clipping and visibility. No snapshots, dependencies, production source, or math changes. E2E typechecking passes. Repeated targeted checks: 11/12 passed, with one page-startup timeout before screenshot assertions. Focused frontend suite: **406 passed, 1 baseline locale assertion failed**. - Full local Windows frontend suite: **11,930 passed, 193 failed, 19 pending**; baseline reproduces 192 assertion failures and the same three module-loading failures. The remaining sharing-dialog test passes on recheck. Renderer smoke on a separate port: **150 passed, 3 failed**; two reproduce on baseline and the /btw recheck passes. title: fix: make Stay Awake responsive and recover after charging
body:
Code changes: +139 -35\
Tests: +288 -27\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Make the Stay Awake coffee control respond immediately and remain clickable while native wake registration finishes. Keep the sidebar-sized coffee cup in every state, with a small red hazard triangle at its top right when an enabled request is inactive.

Shorten the tooltips, align the Mobile settings info button, and automatically recover existing wake requests after a low-battery pause clears.

## Why

The control previously dimmed and rejected clicks for several seconds, making a working action look unresponsive. Low-battery requests could remain latched after charging, and the replacement warning icon and long tooltip obscured the feature's meaning.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Clicking waits for native acknowledgement and disables the coffee button. | Selection updates immediately; the pointer stays clickable and rapid clicks settle to the latest intent. |
| A warning triangle replaces the coffee cup when an enabled request is inactive. | The normal 14px coffee cup remains, with a 10px red hazard triangle at its top right. |
| Long battery explanation asks users to toggle off and on. | At the default limit: “Paused: battery below 10%.” / “Resumes after charging.” Custom limits retain their configured percentage. |
| Low-battery safety stop stays latched after the battery recovers. | Fresh, complete safe readings restore existing owners after charging or connecting AC; expired requests and explicit off actions stay off. |
| The Mobile info button sits below the text baseline. | The info button aligns with the sentence. |

Final Electron captures are available for manual attachment (GitHub CLI cannot upload PR-body image attachments):
- `/Users/vaibhaav/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-221/stay-awake-active.png`
- `/Users/vaibhaav/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-221/stay-awake-paused.png`

The paused capture uses a controlled lab-only 10% appearance preview; it is not included in this branch. A matching base capture could not be completed because the background native window stopped rendering.

## How

- Share optimistic intent through React Query; serialize writes and coalesce queued changes so the latest click wins across controls. Read current cached ownership before starting or stopping.
- Keep battery observations running during a low-battery stop. Require fresh safe battery and thermal readings before restoring wake ownership; persist recovery before reacquiring the hold.
- Preserve the existing native assertion implementation, default 10% protection, and explicit-off behavior. Previously paused rules remain paused; after a daemon restart, persisted rules stay paused conservatively rather than guessing their prior intent.
- Add concise localized tooltips across all nine locales. The custom-data-directory warning already existed; regression tests verify it does not appear for normal app data.

## Testing

CI follow-up: fixed the board integration test’s retry-delay race without changing sign-in behavior. The test now uses an immediate retry and asserts both failed reconciliation attempts plus no terminal spawn. The complete 36-test board file passes. Full failed Vitest shard validation passed under Node 24: **318 files / 5,452 tests**; frontend typecheck also passed.

- Passed: 66 `AwakeControl` tests; focused Mobile/i18n regression suite from implementation (164 passed, 6 skipped).
- Passed: complete awake/mobilebridge package race suites, full backend build and vet, Go formatting, and `git diff --check`.
- Passed: frontend `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` under CI’s Node 24 runtime.

- The earlier full frontend run completed with 635 files passing and two timing failures in unchanged Settings and side-chat files; both failing files passed separate reruns. A fresh Node 24 full run and the 148-test renderer smoke run hit extensive timeouts in unchanged files under local contention and were stopped; these runs are not claimed as passes.
- The full backend race rerun was stopped during the same contention. The prior non-race full backend run had failures in unchanged harness/provider, shell, browser-runtime, and systemcheck fixtures; focused affected packages pass.
- Linux and Windows runner behavior requires remote CI. Local validation is macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.1 and Node 24.22.2. Remote checks remain pending.

Manual native Electron validation used an isolated checkout and scratch AO data: immediate coffee feedback, rapid toggles, paused badge/tooltip, and real low-battery stop/recovery through a temporary configured threshold.
