title: [Bug]: Android chat paints its first message for a frame when opened
body: ### What went wrong? On Android, opening a chat draws the top of its transcript (the first message) for one frame, then jumps to the latest message. In a long chat the incoming screen shows "1. The apple…" during the push animation, and the next frame is at the end. Seen on an Android emulator (API 35, Release build of `main` + the resume fix), 30 fps screen recording of a board → chat push. ### Why it happens The chat timeline is not inverted on Android (`lib/chat/timelineModel.ts`, `conversationTimelineRenderPlan`), because Android's text-selection toolbar breaks under FlatList's inverted transform (#6441). Without inversion, a freshly mounted `FlatList` renders from offset 0 (`initialNumToRender={4}` draws the oldest groups), and `ChatTimeline` reaches the end only afterwards, from `onContentSizeChange` → `requestAnimationFrame(scrollToEnd)`. Every mount therefore paints the top first. iOS uses the inverted list and mounts at the end. This was the visible "jumps to the first message" half of the resume flicker. The resume half is fixed separately (the chat no longer remounts on an app switch), so what remains is this one frame on a fresh open, mostly hidden by the slide-in. ### Proposed fix Give the Android timeline a list that starts at the end natively instead of scrolling there after the first paint, without the inverted transform so text selection keeps working. Candidates, both JS-only (no native build): - `@legendapp/list` (3.7.1): `initialScrollAtEnd`, `maintainScrollAtEnd`, `alignItemsAtEnd` - `@shopify/flash-list` (2.3.3): `maintainVisibleContentPosition: { startRenderingFromBottom: true }` Hiding the list until it has scrolled would only mask this, so it isn't proposed. ### To check when doing it - Partial text selection in agent replies (#6441) still works on Android - Jump to a message (`jumpToSequence`), "Load earlier messages", the "Latest" button and following the tail while a reply streams - iOS keeps its current behaviour, or moves to the same list with no regression - A frame-by-frame recording of a fresh open shows no top-of-chat frame

title: fix(mobile): keep the open chat mounted across an app switch
body:
Code changes: +420 -213\
Tests: +513 -22\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The mobile chat no longer drops to a loader and back when you leave the app and return. On Android the chat used to go blank, show its first message, then jump to the latest; on iOS it went blank with a spinner. Now the open chat stays on screen and refreshes in place once the connection is back.

## Why

Reported from a user's recording: every return to the app flashed a loader and "flicked" the chat.

Backgrounding drops the store's verified connection (`config`) on purpose, so a LAN address that belongs to another machine after the phone wakes never receives the bearer. But the same value also told screens *which machine* they were showing. With it gone, `sessionRouteView` swapped the chat for its loader and `ChatSessionScreen` unmounted, then mounted again when the endpoint race finished. Android's timeline isn't inverted (#6441), so the fresh mount painted from offset 0 before `scrollToEnd`. The conversation cache, pending-send banners, composer key, draft and attachment keys, and the PR review card were all keyed on `config` too, so each reset on every app switch. #6783 fixed this for the board only (`heldMachine`).

Not an Expo issue: the behaviour dates from #5921, and the app has been on SDK 57 since long before.

## Before / After

Release builds, the same native binary with only the JS bundle swapped, a long chat on a scratch daemon. The app goes home for 3 s and returns; each frame is 33 ms apart (30 fps screen recording).

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Android before: the chat fades to a spinner, shows its first message, then jumps back](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/fcb6b5eec077ebb5e28825bf871a84c7137f9dfb/android-before.jpg) | ![Android after: the chat stays put](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/fcb6b5eec077ebb5e28825bf871a84c7137f9dfb/android-after.jpg) |
| ![iOS before: the chat fades to a blank spinner for about 150 ms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/fcb6b5eec077ebb5e28825bf871a84c7137f9dfb/ios-before.jpg) | ![iOS after: the chat stays put](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/fcb6b5eec077ebb5e28825bf871a84c7137f9dfb/ios-after.jpg) |
| Android, 3 runs: settles 267–300 ms after the window appears; 5 blank and 4 top-of-chat frames | Settles 133–167 ms (the window animation alone); 0 blank, 0 top-of-chat |
| iOS, 3 runs: a blank spinner frame in 2 of 3 | 0 blank frames |

## How

- The store publishes `machine` and `paired` next to `config` (`lib/viewMachine.ts`). They come from the selected machine, which an app switch or endpoint race does not change, and replace the board-only `heldMachine`. `config` keeps its meaning and its safety property: requests still wait for a verified connection.
- `sessionRouteView` takes `paired` instead of a config-derived `configured`; the session route reads `machine` and `paired` from the store, which also stops a found lookup for an unlisted orchestrator from resetting on every background.
- `useMobileConversation(verified, machine, sessionId)` keys its page cache and pending sends on `machine`. Restoring from cache and refreshing are now separate effects, so losing the connection pauses requests without emptying the transcript. A connection for a different machine (mid-switch) is ignored.
- The composer key, draft key and attachment key use `machine`, so an app switch (or an Android picker activity) no longer remounts the composer.
- The PR review card reads the summary cache through the last verified config for the same machine (`useLastVerifiedConfig`); fetching still uses only the live one.
- Because the screen now stays up while the connection is re-established, chat actions can be tried in that window. They fail before anything is reserved (a pending-send record that never reached `pendingSends` would block the next send), and say "Still reconnecting to your machine" (`RECONNECTING_ACTION_COPY`) instead of "This phone isn't paired". The same applies to Resume and the Chat/Terminal switch.
- Terminal sessions stay mounted too, so the terminal now reattaches itself when a new socket connects under an xterm that is already up (`useTerminalMux`): it resets the xterm (RIS, since the daemon repaints every fresh attach with its scrollback) and opens the PTY on the new socket. Before, the route's remount hid that the config-change path never reopened the PTY. The phone's grid now travels in the open frame (`MuxClient` keeps it per terminal and replays it on `onopen`), because a resize sent while a socket is still connecting is dropped and the daemon sizes a fresh attach from the open.

Review focus: `reloadConfig` now compares the newly read selection with the last committed `selectedHostId` (instead of the held host id) to decide whether to clear rows.

Out of scope, filed as #7687: on Android a *fresh* chat open still paints the first message for one frame under the push animation, because the non-inverted list mounts at offset 0. That needs a bottom-anchored list.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) and `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npx vitest run`: 350 files, 3425 tests pass (after rebasing onto the native overhaul, #7838 and #7839)
- New tests, each confirmed to fail against the old behaviour:
  - `lib/viewMachine.test.ts`: every connection state a paired machine passes through keeps an open chat on its screen, through the store's own row filter and `sessionRouteView`; a different machine never shows the previous one's session
  - `lib/store.resume.test.tsx`: the real store, background → active → race lands on another endpoint → first poll, never leaves the chat screen or changes `machine`
  - `lib/chat/useConversation.resume.test.tsx`: the transcript survives the connection going and coming back, and is never requested through another machine's connection; while reconnecting, send/steer/interrupt reject with the reconnecting copy and store no pending send, and a send after reconnecting goes through
  - `lib/session/useTerminalMux.test.tsx` (real `MuxClient`, a fake socket that refuses sends until open): config LAN → null → tunnel under a mounted xterm; once the still-connecting socket opens, its open frame carries the phone's grid (also one reported while connecting); the xterm is reset before the repaint, output is not left buffered, and nothing opens twice
  - `lib/mux.test.ts`: an open asked for while connecting carries its grid, a resize while connecting is kept, and the client's own reconnect re-attaches at the latest grid
- On device: Android emulator (API 35) and iOS 26.5 simulator, Release builds paired with a scratch daemon. An automated script recorded each return at 30 fps and classified every frame against the settled chat, the top of the chat and a blank screen; 3 runs per build per platform.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): escalate the ACP history settle attempt budget
body:
Code changes: +107 -28
Tests: +197 -13
Others: +0 -0

Ported from wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator branch `plus/hermes-adapter`, commit ef7934621b ("fix(chat): escalate the ACP history settle attempt budget", fork issue wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator#39). The cherry-pick onto current `main` is content-identical to the fork commit; only hunk line offsets moved.

## User-visible failure

A harness/interface switch that needs the provider transcript replay (ACP `session/load`) failed on slow machines — observed in the field on Windows with Defender scanning the agent process: the first replay legitimately takes longer than the fixed 45s settle budget / 30s per-attempt bound, the load deadline was classified as `ErrChatHistoryLoadFailed` (a terminal provider verdict), and the switch failed even though a longer attempt would have succeeded.

## What changes

- The settle attempt budget escalates: the first provider re-observation keeps `nativeHistoryLoadAttemptLimit` (30s) so a hung load still yields quickly; every later attempt gets the whole remaining settle budget, so the last attempt ends only when the settle budget itself ends. Every attempt stays cancellable by the parent.
- Provider JSON-RPC -32602 answers whose text carries a context deadline are classified as the new retryable `ports.ErrChatHistoryLoadDeadline` instead of a terminal load failure; genuine provider verdicts (-32603, auth) stay `ErrChatHistoryLoadFailed`. The field-observed shape is `{"code":-32602,"message":"Internal error","data":{"error":"context deadline exceeded"}}`.
- `nativeHistorySettleLimit` is raised 45s → 120s to absorb a full first replay on slow machines.
- `ChatHistoryUnsettledError` and the settle-wait error shape are unchanged, so the interface transition and its Retry path keep working; a budget exhausted on a stalled load reports the typed unsettled failure with the original checkpoint reason.

## Provenance and scope

This is one of four fork-only hermes interface-switch fixes ported upstream:

- The other three (native identity read from the chat conversation `dbcde4e690`, TUI→Chat fresh-start degrade `a66294da97`, Chat→TUI native-restore-or-fresh-TUI degrade `5faf9cb6d3`) are already on `main`: they landed as part of #6635 (verified: `interface_transition_identity_degrade_test.go`, `terminal_resume.go`, and the `hermesNativeConversationID` helper are byte-identical with the fork versions at those commits). This PR carries the only missing fix.
- One commit, one concern; the fork's `Fixes #39` trailer was re-pointed to the fork repo (`wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator#39`) so it cannot close an unrelated upstream issue.

## Tests

- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/service/chat/ ./internal/ports/` all pass (identical to the pristine `main` baseline measured before the port), including the ported tests: `TestACPDriverHistoryRefreshMapsProviderDeadlineErrorToRetryable`, `TestNormalizeACPLoadErrorKeepsOtherCodes`, `TestInterfaceHandoffExhaustsSettleBudgetWhenHistoryLoadStalls`, `TestInterfaceHandoffRetriesDeadlineLoadWithEscalatingAttemptBudget`.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2 (repo-pinned): 0 issues.

Note for maintainers: this repository's first-time-contributor workflow-approval gate applies to each push — CI runs will wait for your approval.

title: fix(session): bind hermes native identity on native restore + high-water replay dump
body:
Code changes: +55 -1
Tests: +43 -0
Others: +0 -0

## What

Bind the hermes native identity to a native resume's launch immediately, like Codex and Claude Code already are, and dump the failing high-water reconciliation to `/tmp/ao-history-replay-dump.json` on the error path.

`session_manager/manager.go`: `bindNativeIdentity` on `RestoreModeNative` excluded hermes. Hermes's fallback proof (the `/proc` lease chain in `readSessionInfo`) is Linux-only, so on darwin a hermes TUI relaunched outside a transition (daemon restart + resume) could never re-confirm its identity, and every later TUI→Chat handoff failed `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED`. The restore path already proves the identity (recorded native home + native conversation lookup) before the launch exists.

`service/chat/controller.go`: `debugDumpHistoryReplay` writes the failing high-water reconciliation (boundaries, mapped turns, replay events) to `/tmp/ao-history-replay-dump.json` when the `ao_high_water` boundary check refuses a replay — the instrument that localized a transcript-collapse bug to missing ACP chunk messageIds.

## Why

A hermes TUI session resumed after a daemon restart could never hand off back to Chat on macOS: without the immediate `AgentSessionIDLaunchID` bind, the later TUI→Chat handoff always failed `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED`. Ported from fork commit `1013d2546b` (wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator branch `plus/hermes-adapter`), adapted to the post-#6635 upstream code (the bind list gained `HarnessAgy` and the terminal-version-refresh clause; the restore command moved to the title-based `sessionCommand`).

Dependency note: on the fork, this commit was written alongside dbcde4e690 ("read the hermes native identity from the chat conversation", `hermes_rollback.go`), which is not on upstream main. This PR adds only the manager bind; the identity-read change is being ported separately. The bind is a no-op for plain chat sessions (which carry no `AgentSessionID`) until that lands; for TUI sessions the identity comes from the existing native resolution and the bind fixes the darwin resume path immediately.

## Before / After

Non-visual change; regression test on upstream main without the fix (RED):

```
$ go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run TestResumeAgent_HermesNativeResumeBindsIdentity -v
=== RUN   TestResumeAgent_HermesNativeResumeBindsIdentity
    native_restore_hermes_test.go:38: native hermes resume identity launch = "", want launch-new
--- FAIL: TestResumeAgent_HermesNativeResumeBindsIdentity (0.05s)
```

With the fix (GREEN):

```
=== RUN   TestResumeAgent_HermesNativeResumeBindsIdentity
--- PASS: TestResumeAgent_HermesNativeResumeBindsIdentity (0.00s)
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/session_manager
```

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Hermes native resume leaves `AgentSessionIDLaunchID` empty; TUI→Chat handoff fails `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` on darwin | Hermes joins the immediate bind: the resumed launch owns the recorded identity, handoff proceeds |
| An unresolved `ao_high_water` refusal is only a dimension name in the mismatch | The failing reconciliation (boundaries, mapped turns, replay events) is dumped to `/tmp/ao-history-replay-dump.json` |

## How

- Add `domain.HarnessHermes` to the `bindNativeIdentity` harness list in `relaunchSessionWithPolicyAndGeneration`, with the rationale comment (restore already proves identity; `/proc` fallback is Linux-only).
- Port `debugDumpHistoryReplay` verbatim in structure from the fork, hooked at the `len(boundaries) > 0` refusal site of `nativeHistoryCheckpoint.mismatches`, adapted to the upstream struct shapes (unchanged field names). Error-path only, best-effort write, matching the fork.

## Testing

- RED receipt above: new `TestResumeAgent_HermesNativeResumeBindsIdentity` (test-only commit `8250a8ff8`) fails on upstream main `a1fe965e7` with exactly the missing bind.
- GREEN: the same test passes with the fix.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/service/chat/...` all pass (92s / 80s local).

## Checklist

- Fork provenance: `1013d2546b` (branch `plus/hermes-adapter`).
- Note: pushes from this first-time-contributor account re-arm the workflow-approval gate; a maintainer may need to approve CI runs for this branch.

### Report

Tried to switch a Hermes chat session to the Terminal UI. The switch fails with:

> TARGET_PREFLIGHT_FAILED: hermes: current terminal identity was not observed

Happens on every attempt. Reporter: @wesleymatosdev (2026-11-03, Hermes chat session viewed from the mobile client, session lives on the Mac daemon).

### Agent-collected evidence

- Read-only query against the production SQLite DB (`session_interface_transitions`, collected 2026-11-03 ~23:50 UTC): session `agent-orchestrator-137` (harness hermes, chat mode) recorded 5 failed `chat -> tui` transitions on 2026-11-03 between 14:03 and 16:03 UTC, all with error code `TARGET_PREFLIGHT_FAILED`, detail `hermes: current terminal identity was not observed`. A `chat -> tui` transition for a claude-code session on the same daemon completed normally minutes later, so the failure is hermes-specific, not a general switch outage.
- Affected build: serving daemon is an upstream `main` snapshot from 2026-11-03 (commit approx `a1fe965e70`); the daemon self-reports version `dev`, so the build identity is approximate.
- The preflight requires the hermes terminal identity to be observed before the handoff; if no native terminal identity exists, the whole switch fails instead of degrading. A candidate fix (degrade the hermes Chat→TUI handoff to native restore or a fresh TUI) exists on the public fork branch `plus/hermes-adapter` (wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator commit `5faf9cb6d3`).

### Duplicate check

Searched OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator issues+PRs for "terminal identity was not observed" and "interface switch hermes" (2026-11-03). Closest matches #7111 and #6211 are Codex-specific switch failures; no hermes equivalent found.

title: bug(chat): hover card stays open after chat auto-scrolls and blocks content (no scroll dismissal)
body:
### Report

An open hover card in the chat timeline can end up stuck covering content: while the chat auto-scrolls (e.g. during streaming), the card's trigger row moves out from under it but the card stays open, and it blocks what's underneath until you click elsewhere. Observed on the Windows client; made a session timeline hard to read. Reporter: @wesleymatosdev (reported 2026-11-01).

### Agent-collected evidence

- Root cause (code-level, fork-side analysis 2026-11-01): Radix hover cards have no scroll dismissal. In the chat timeline, streaming/auto-scroll re-anchors the trigger row under an already-open card, so the card never receives a leave event and stays open.
- Supporting telemetry from the reporter's Windows client: ~14k pointer-events calls in 30s in `hover-card-*.js` while the card was stuck (pointer-churn hot loop).
- A candidate fix exists in the shared wrapper `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/hover-card.tsx`: a capture-phase window scroll listener that dismisses open cards except for in-card scrolls (commit `8099a06daa` on a fork work branch, not yet pushed/PR'd).
- Duplicate check: searched OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator issues+PRs for "hover card scroll" (2026-11-03) — no match.

title: bug(chat): interface switch fails on slow machines — fixed ACP history settle budget times out with context deadline exceeded
body:
### Report

Switching a session from Terminal to Chat fails on a busy/slow machine with:

> switch interface bela-portfolio1-20: resume chat: wait for settled native conversation history: chat conversation history is not settled: checkpoint mismatches [ao_high_water]: refresh ACP session history: context deadline exceeded: {"code":-32602,"message":"Internal error","data":{"error":"context deadline exceeded"}}

Retrying hits the same wall. The fixed total settle window is too short when the provider's history load is slow. Reporter: @wesleymatosdev (observed on a real Windows-client machine; sessions for this project run on the macOS daemon).

### Agent-collected evidence

- Production DB (`session_interface_transitions`, read-only query, collected 2026-11-03): multiple failed `tui -> chat` transitions for `bela-portfolio1-20` with `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` and the error above.
- This is a recurrence of the settle-deadline class previously closed for Claude/Codex (#5292, #6870, #6700); it now also affects ACP providers (e.g. hermes) where the underlying `session/load` itself needs longer than the fixed budget, and the per-attempt ACP refresh bound plus a fixed total (45s) leave no room. When the provider answers with a JSON-RPC deadline error (`-32602`/context deadline exceeded), the current classification does not distinguish retryable-slow from fatal.
- A candidate fix exists on the public fork branch `plus/hermes-adapter` (wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator commit `ef7934621b`, "fix(chat): escalate the ACP history settle attempt budget"): escalating per-attempt budget, retryable classification for provider deadline errors, larger total window, same typed failure shape so the Retry path keeps working.
- Duplicate check: searched OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator issues+PRs for "history is not settled" (2026-11-03); listed closed Claude/Codex issues above are prior instances of the class, no open ACP/hermes equivalent.

title: feat(session): auto-attach PRs opened by a worker session — PR/CI tracking stays empty until a manual claim-pr
body:
### Report When a spawned worker session opens a GitHub PR itself, the PR is not attached to that session: the session's PR/CI/REVIEW columns in `ao session ls` stay empty, and `ao status` views never show it. Today the orchestrator has to know out-of-band and run `ao session claim-pr ` (or the worker must remember to send `ao report --pr-created `), or the PR is invisible to AO's native tracking. Observed 2026-11-03/04: three active worker sessions with open PRs showed no PR column until a claim was made manually; one claimed PR then tracked CI/review fine (`passing / review_required`), proving the tracking layer works once attached. Reporter: @wesleymatosdev. ### Agent-collected evidence - `ao session ls --project

` on 2026-11-04: sessions with worker-opened PRs showed `-` in the PR column while an explicitly claimed PR on another session showed live CI state. - Expected behavior (hypothesis, not verified in code): the daemon already detects worker PR heads for review triggers (`ao review trigger` works on worker PR heads), so auto-attaching on PR creation from the session's harness — or accepting the session's own `ao report --pr-created` as attach — looks like a small gap in the existing pipeline. ### Duplicate check Searched OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator issues+PRs for "claim-pr" / "session PR attach" style terms (2026-11-04); no matching open issue found.

title: feat(ci): notify/report when a tracked PR check transitions to FAILURE — tracking is pull-only today
body:
### Report

AO tracks CI and review state natively for session-attached PRs (PR/CI/REVIEW columns), but the tracking is pull-only: nothing reports or notifies when a check transitions to FAILURE. A red CI job sits invisible until someone happens to open the board or run `ao session ls`. On 2026-11-04 a PR had a failing `lint` job and an older orphaned PR (owner session long exited) sat with three failing checks — both unnoticed until an external watcher flagged them. Reporter: @wesleymatosdev.

### Agent-collected evidence

- Attached-PR tracking verified live (`passing` / `review_required` rendered in `ao session ls`), so the poll layer exists; the missing piece is the transition event reaching a report/notification surface (e.g. an `ao report` into the owning session's thread, or the orchestrator chat) when CI flips.
- Orphaned PRs (owning session exited) drop out of native view entirely.
- Workaround in use meanwhile: a recurring worker automation that polls `gh pr checks` for open PRs and routes fixes — happy to retire it if this lands natively.
- Related nit: `ao automation create --cron` rejects step syntax (`*/15 * * * *` → "minute must be an integer from 0 to 59"); `--rrule "FREQ=MINUTELY;INTERVAL=15"` works.

### Duplicate check

Searched OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator issues+PRs for CI status notification/report terms (2026-11-04); no matching open issue found.

title: feat(chat): steer running turns on Qwen Code, Kimchi, and OMP
body:
Code changes: +723 -54\
Tests: +1244 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Steering, which means adding guidance to a turn while it is still running, now works on three more harnesses: Qwen Code, Kimchi, and OMP. Claude Code and Codex already had it.

- **Qwen Code 0.18+:** AO holds the guidance until Qwen collects it between tool calls.
- **Kimchi:** AO calls Kimchi's own steering method.
- **OMP:** steering already worked. When OMP replies `failed`, AO now treats it as a refusal.
- **Reply order:** text the agent streams after a steer starts a new message, so it appears below the "↳ Steered" bubble.
- **Dock errors:** when a steer from a queued card is refused, the dock shows the daemon's reason instead of "That action failed."

## Why

The ACP driver only knew ACP's `_session/steering` request, which neither Qwen Code nor Kimchi implements. On those harnesses, a message sent mid-turn waited in the queue until the turn ended.

## Before / After

The Before column describes the old behavior. These screenshots come from the live test of this branch.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| **Qwen Code, Steer on a queued card.** Qwen didn't advertise steering, so the message waited for the turn to end. | ![Qwen: message queued with a Steer button while a command runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a317dad257ef3e0b21c1ea5bea58c93207ab994e/qwen-1-queued.png) ![Qwen: the queued message joins the running turn as a Steered bubble, and the reply continues below it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a317dad257ef3e0b21c1ea5bea58c93207ab994e/qwen-2-steered.png) |
| **Qwen Code, busy in a 40 s command.** Not possible before. | Qwen can't collect guidance during a long tool call. After 5 s AO withdraws the steer and returns `409 CHAT_TURN_NOT_STEERABLE` with the reason. The card stays queued and runs as the next turn. ![Qwen: the card is still queued after the refused steer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a317dad257ef3e0b21c1ea5bea58c93207ab994e/qwen-3-not-collected.png) ![Qwen: the queued message runs as the next turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a317dad257ef3e0b21c1ea5bea58c93207ab994e/qwen-4-ran-next.png) |
| **Kimchi, ⌘↩ during a turn.** Kimchi has its own steering method, not `_session/steering`, so Steer wasn't offered. | The plan changes mid-turn: the agent edits `staging.yaml` and leaves `prod.yaml` alone. ![Kimchi: change of plan steered into the running turn; only staging.yaml changed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a317dad257ef3e0b21c1ea5bea58c93207ab994e/kimchi-steered.png) |
| **OMP 18.16, ⌘↩ during a turn.** Steering already worked, but OMP's `failed` reply and invalid-params errors left the steer's delivery status unknown. | Same steering, and those replies now settle as refused. ![OMP: change of plan steered into the running turn; only staging.yaml changed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a317dad257ef3e0b21c1ea5bea58c93207ab994e/omp-steered.png) |
| **Refused steer from a queued card.** The dock said "That action failed." | The dock shows the daemon's reason, e.g. "the agent did not collect the guidance within 5s; it collects between tool calls". This is covered by a unit test; there is no screenshot of it. |

## How

- **Steering per harness.** `acp.Config` takes one of two optional settings, and a harness with neither keeps `_session/steering`.
  - `SteerRequest`: one client-to-agent request, with handshake detection, params and outcome mapping. Kimchi uses `_kimchi.dev/steering`, advertised at `agentCapabilities._meta["kimchi.dev"].steering`.
    - Its optional `TakesImages` reads from the handshake whether the request carries images. Kimchi before 1.2.0 drops `attachments` from a steer and still answers `injected`, so Kimchi's reads `agentInfo.version`, and an image steer to an older build is refused before anything is sent.
  - `SteerDrain`: the agent asks AO for waiting guidance at its own step boundaries. Qwen Code uses `craft/drainMidTurnQueue`, plus a best-effort `craft/midTurnSendNow` nudge. It is enabled only when `agentInfo.version` is 0.18.0 or newer.
- **Steering on Qwen.**
  - `Steer` returns `injected` only after Qwen has taken the text. If the turn ends first, it returns `ErrChatNoSteerableTurn`, so the message is sent as a new turn.
  - After 5 s it withdraws the guidance and returns `ErrChatTurnNotSteerable`, which keeps the card queued.
  - The wait is short because the Chat controller holds its dispatch lock during a steer, so Stop and new sends wait too.
  - Qwen's own wait for AO's reply is 2 s, and it stops asking after three misses. AO answers from memory under the conversation lock, so it never comes close to that limit.
  - The `craft/midTurnSendNow` nudge runs off `Steer`'s path, so a write that stalls can't hold `Steer` past its wait. Only one nudge is in flight at a time.
- **Stop.** Stop withdraws waiting guidance before it takes the dispatch lock, and marks the turn as stopping. Any later steer for that turn, including one that already held the lock, is refused at once with `ErrChatTurnNotSteerable`, so it can't join the turn or hold Stop up. A later turn steers as usual. If Stop doesn't stop the turn (the interrupt fails, or Stop can't read the running turns), it gives steering back through the restore that `WithdrawPendingSteers` returns. That restore is bound to the turn it withdrew, so a late one never lifts a later turn's Stop.
- **Legacy method names.** `craft/*` methods have no ACP underscore prefix, so the SDK can't send them. The nudge goes through the existing legacy transport, which now has a generic `call`. The drain method is aliased, the same way `ClientExtensionAliases` already handles legacy names.
- **Steered message segments.** Qwen sends its message chunks without ids, so each turn got one `assistant-<turn>` id. The text after a steer was then folded into the bubble above it. Each accepted steer now bumps a per-turn segment, and id-less chunks become `assistant-<turn>-N`. Chunks that carry their own id are unchanged. Kimchi and OMP send one on every streamed message (Kimchi a fresh `messageId` per content block, OMP a UUID per live message, since AO's minimum 15.0.0), so a reply that is streaming when they queue a steer stays in its bubble.
- **Not changed.**
  - The OMP minimum version stays at 15.0.0. Raising it would block chat for older OMP installs, and steering is detected from the handshake anyway.
  - The Chat service's error classification already handled these errors.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/kimchiacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/qwenacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/nativeacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/ompacp/` passes. They cover:
  - Qwen: injected only after collection; withdrawal after the wait (a later drain returns `{"messages":[]}`); the turn ending first; images refused; the legacy method alias; a stalled nudge can't hold `Steer`, and only one nudge is in flight. The drain fixtures report the identity the binding supports and check that Steer is offered, and the collection test holds the agent back to prove `Steer` returns only after it collects.
  - Stop: a steer that arrives after Stop began is refused at once and never parked; the next turn steers as usual; a Stop that fails gives steering back (driver and controller).
  - Kimchi: params, attachments and status mapping; image steers below 1.2.0 refused before sending, and the image reaches the request on newer versions.
  - OMP: `failed` and invalid-params count as refusals.
  - Message order: text after a steer becomes a new message; a reply that carries its own id stays one message across a steer.
  - Each new check was confirmed by reverting it: the test fails without it.
- **Dock test:** `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/QueuedMessageDock.test.tsx` passes. The new test fails on the old code.
- **Lint:** `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on the changed packages reports 0 issues.
- **Full CI suites, run locally the way CI runs them:**
  - Go: `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean.
  - The full race suite fails in 5 packages that also fail on a clean `main` checkout here, because they depend on tools installed on this Mac: `commandcode`, `crush`, `opencodev2`, `opencodev2acp` and `shellterm`. This PR touches none of them.
  - `runtime/tmux` and `daemon` failed once under parallel load and passed when rerun on their own.
  - The separate race jobs pass: `service/chat`, `storage/sqlite` and `storage/sqlite/store`. `session_manager` failed once under parallel load and passed when rerun on its own.
  - Frontend: `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass. `vitest run` passes 11,058 of 11,073 tests. Of the 6 failures, 4 pass when rerun alone. The other 2 are context-meter tests that fail under this machine's `en-IN` locale (`2,58,400`) and pass with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`.
- **Live, in the desktop app** (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` and `HOME`, real agents):
  - **Qwen Code 0.25.1:**
    - ⌘↩ steer: 202.
    - Queued-card Steer: 202 after 2.3 s, and `notes.txt` got the steered line.
    - Steer during `sleep 40`: 409 with the reason; the card was kept and ran next.
  - **OMP 18.16.0:** ⌘↩ steer works; `staging.yaml` set to 45 and `prod.yaml` left at 30.
  - **Kimchi 1.26.0:** ⌘↩ steer works with the same result, and the plan updated.
  - **Not tested live:** queued-card Steer on OMP and Kimchi (the free model quota ran out). It goes through the same driver call as their ⌘↩ steer.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)




<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Mid-turn message steering is supported for compatible ACP agents, including Kimchi and Qwen. Supported agents can receive text guidance and, where available, images. Guidance is delivered when collected; uncollected guidance is withdrawn when a turn ends or is interrupted.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Interrupting a turn no longer has to wait for pending steering guidance to time out.
  * Steering and reorder failures show specific error messages when available instead of a generic notice.
  * Steering refusal messages are punctuated consistently before retry guidance.

title: Manual reconnect loses the legacy machine id
body:
Machines migrated from older versions have an empty string as their id. When you reconnect one of them with the manual option, the connect sheet opens like a brand new connection instead of editing the machine you picked.

The cause is in packages/mobile/lib/sheetResult.ts: the route drops hostId when it's "", so the form never learns which machine was selected. A route test shows it.

The fix keeps the empty id and only treats a missing id as a new connection. PR: #7705. This is the manual-entry follow-up mentioned in the #7627 review, which covers the QR reconnect for these machines.

title: feat(topbar): simplify the session top bar and float it above the center panel (Developer Mode)
body:
Simplifies the top bar and floats it above the center panel on macOS, **as a Developer Mode preview**. Turn it on in Settings > General > Developer Mode > "Simplified top bar" (on by default once Developer Mode is on). Without Developer Mode, everyone keeps the previous top bar.

## Who sees what
- **Developer Mode off:** the previous top bar, unchanged. The old session cluster is kept verbatim (`LegacySessionTopbarActions`, diffed identical to `main`), along with the old board buttons, New terminal beside the actions, and none of the floating shell. The PR removes no existing CSS. The only added rule not scoped to the new layout is a hidden drag-strip element. The new telemetry event and the cue menu's focus handling are silent/off too.
- **Developer Mode on, switch on:** the new bar below.
- When the new bar graduates, delete the legacy copies and the `useSimplifiedTopbar` switch.

## Controls
| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Worker | editor▾ · ▶ · Archive · **[Orchestrator]** (solid) | Orchestrator · editor▾ · ▶ · *divider* · inspector |
| Orchestrator | **[+ Task]** · Open Kanban · editor▾ · ▶ | editor▾ · ▶ · Board · **[+ Task]** · *divider* · inspector |
| Board | + Task · **[Orchestrator]** (solid) | Orchestrator · **[+ Task]** |

- Orchestrator looks the same everywhere: quiet, labeled, and first. + Task is the only solid button.
- Archive left the top bar. It's still in the inspector Summary, the sidebar row menu, and ⌘⇧A (`SessionArchiveShortcut`, no visible button).
- The editor control is just the editor icon and its dropdown caret. Run is icon only.
- New terminal (+) sits right after the last tab, not with the actions.
- A half-strength divider separates the session's actions from the inspector tabs. It shows only while the inspector is open and lines up with the inspector's left border. The resize handle's hover line meets it instead of floating 1px off.
- The cue button keeps the normal hover fill when its hover menu opens, and the highlight no longer sticks after hover-off.
- Opening or closing the right sidebar no longer shifts the action buttons: their end padding and the divider ride the rail's own spring (only for the new bar, only for a toggle inside the current session).

## Floating top bar (macOS, windowed)
- The bar sits on the window chrome, and the panel's rounded frame starts below it. It's drawn with CSS rather than restructured: the surface paints the panel fill (`::before`) and frame (`::after`) from the bar's bottom edge, and a mask clips content to the rounded corners. No page components moved.
- Session tabs are rounded pills that match the inspector tabs. All gaps are the 4px tab gap. Windows, Linux and native fullscreen keep the previous panel layout.
- **Pages with no top bar** (home, new chat, the welcome panel) let the panel claim the band above it, so it's taller. The new chat page keeps its top edge draggable with a thin invisible strip. With the sidebar closed the band stays, so the traffic lights keep clear of the panel.
- Moving from a session to a page that reclaims the band no longer flashes the panel border bright.

## Telemetry
New event `ao.renderer.topbar_action_clicked` with allowlisted enum properties, sent **only from the new bar**:
- `action`: `new_task`, `open_board`, `open_orchestrator`, `open_editor`, `editor_menu`, `run_cue`, `inspector`, `notifications`
- `view`: `worker`, `orchestrator`, `board`

Existing events carried no source, so top bar clicks couldn't be separated from sidebar or shortcut use.

## Risk and verification
- Tests were added or updated for the gate, the legacy path, the shell classes, the route wiring, the telemetry gate, the drag strip and the new settings switch. **I did not run them locally; CI is the check.**
- Not yet checked: light themes and window translucency, the popped-out browser and Files panels, and the new bar on Windows and Linux (the layout is macOS-focused; those platforms get the new controls but not the floating shell).
- The drag strip's behavior (dragging the window from the top of the new chat page) is verified by code, not by hand.

## Test
1. Developer Mode **off**: open a session, the board and the new chat page. They look and behave as they do today.
2. Settings > General > turn Developer Mode on. "Simplified top bar" appears, on.
3. Open a worker session on macOS. The bar floats above the panel and reads Orchestrator, editor▾, ▶, then the panel toggle and bell, with no Archive button. Press ⌘⇧A: the archive confirm opens.
4. Open the inspector. A short divider appears on the inspector's left border. Toggle the right sidebar a few times: the buttons glide rather than jump.
5. Open the home page and the new chat page: the panel is taller, and the top edge still drags the window. Switch the sidebar closed: the band returns.
6. Turn the "Simplified top bar" switch off: the previous bar returns without leaving Developer Mode.

title: feat: a session owns its agent, projects no longer pin one
body:
## What this changes for users

Switching an agent on an orchestrator or a worker now sticks. Before, the project's pinned agent could pull a switched orchestrator back. The board offered "restart needed", saving project settings replaced the orchestrator, and spawning with no agent failed unless the project had one.

New sessions with no explicit agent now start on the first ready agent in the order claude-code, codex, cursor, opencode.

This is PR 1 of 3 and only changes the local app. Cloud projects and the mobile app are unchanged; they move later in their own PRs. The create-project form and project settings still show the agent pickers here. PR 2 removes them and the CLI flags. PR 3 steadies the new-project handoff.

## How it works

- The session's own harness is the source of truth. A new session resolves its agent in this order. First an explicit choice. Then the spawning session's agent, so workers follow a switched orchestrator. Then `domain.ChooseDefaultHarness` over `DefaultHarnessPriority`, using agent readiness.
- An orchestrator replacement or restart keeps the project's latest orchestrator agent in any state.
- Project `model`, `effort` and `mode` now apply only when the launch agent is the one `role.agent` names. A switched or default-picked agent starts from its own defaults, so a Claude alias is never sent to Codex. Permissions still inherit.
- The role `agent` field stays in the config for now and only scopes those settings.

## What was removed

- Frontend: `orchestratorNeedsRestart`, `hasConfiguredOrchestratorAgent`, the restart-needed board state, the settings redirects, orchestrator replacement on settings save, and the "agents required" Save check for local projects.
- Backend: the project-pin fallback in spawn, the harness check in orchestrator replacement verification, and the CLI's project-config agent lookup.

## Cloud stays as it is

The cloud control plane still requires a role agent on every role it stores and defaults orchestrator-spawned workers to claude-code when none is set. So cloud project settings keep their "agents are required" check. It is now an opt-in `requiredAgents` capability that only the cloud form turns on.

## Review notes

- The CI run is the first run of the Go and frontend tests. About 100 existing spawn call sites now pass an explicit harness, and nothing was run locally.
- Provider-native history does not carry across a switch. The target agent starts a fresh thread seeded with the AO transcript, as it already did.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode 2 session fails to start — lstat ENOENT copying legacy data store (persistent ACP host)
body:
### Observed behavior

Tried starting an OpenCode 2 session in Agent Orchestrator under the "zod-compiler" project. It fails to start every time (always has, for this project).

Error shown in the UI:

```
Session setup failed
✓ Workspace created
✗ Getting OpenCode 2 ready
spawn zod-compiler-2: chat controller: chat driver unavailable: persistent ACP host: opencode-v2 ACP: prepare data home: opencode: copy legacy data store: lstat /Users/s/.local/share/opencode/shell/9b29c8a3ea477dcfbde51766b401cd337ce370e8/sh_1a52baa1f003KIBVsLJgZKK1oa.out: no such file or directory
Your messages are saved here and will be sent if you retry.
```

### Frequency

Every time. Always failed for this project (not a recent regression).

### Expected behavior

OpenCode 2 should start the session, or the legacy data-store migration should tolerate a missing/stale shell-output file instead of failing the whole spawn.

---

**Agent-collected evidence** (collected on the affected machine, 2026-11-04)

- Agent Orchestrator 0.14.8 (`Agent Orchestrator.app` `CFBundleShortVersionString`), macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64). OpenCode CLI on PATH reports `opencode v2.2.5`. No `ao` CLI was present on PATH, so the native CLI's own `--version`/`status --json` could not be cross-checked.
- Read-only check of `~/.local/share/opencode/shell/`: the directory named in the error, `9b29c8a3ea477dcfbde51766b401cd337ce370e8`, does not exist at all under that path (not just the `.out` file inside it). This confirms the error is a literal ENOENT on a legacy OpenCode-1 shell-session entry that AO's v2 data-home migration ("copy legacy data store") expects to be present.
- Hypothesis, unconfirmed: the migration enumerates OpenCode 1's shell-session entries (likely from its own store/db) and then copies each by path, without tolerating an entry whose directory/output file was already pruned or rotated by OpenCode itself between enumeration and copy. That would make the migration abort hard on a stale reference instead of skipping it.
- No daemon error log persisted for this failure; `~/.ao/logs/` only contains `updater.jsonl` (unrelated), consistent with daemon stderr output not persisting outside keep-alive launches.

**Duplicate search**

Searched `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator` issues and PRs (open + closed) for: "legacy data store", "prepare data home", "opencode-v2 ACP", "persistent ACP host", "chat driver unavailable", "lstat shell", "no such file or directory opencode".

Closest related issue: #7125 ("OpenCode 2 model discovery times out while copying legacy data store on macOS"), fixed by open PR #7138. That issue hits the same migration step (`PrepareV2DataHome` / "copy legacy data store") but through model-catalog discovery and with a `context deadline exceeded` timeout, not an ENOENT on a specific file during ACP-host session spawn — PR #7138's fix is a timeout-budget change and does not appear to touch the missing-file case here. No exact match for this ENOENT/lstat symptom was found, so filing as a new issue rather than a duplicate.

title: fix(opencode-v2): keep migrating when a legacy entry vanishes mid-copy
body:
Code changes: +46 -3\
Tests: +222 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The OpenCode 2 data-home migration now skips a legacy entry that disappears after it was listed, logs it, and carries on. It used to abort the whole migration.

## Why

Refs #7714. A new OpenCode 2 session failed with:

```text
opencode-v2 ACP: prepare data home: opencode: copy legacy data store: lstat .../shell/<project>/sh_<id>.out: no such file or directory
```

`copyTree` walks `~/.local/share/opencode` while that store is live. `filepath.Walk` lists a directory and then `lstat`s each name, so anything removed in between ended the migration. The session could not start until a migration finally completed.

Real OpenCode 2.2.5 does this: on startup, `opencode acp` deleted every `sh_*.out` older than 7 days within about 0.2 seconds, starting about 0.4 seconds after launch. A live OpenCode's `opencode.db-journal` hit the same failure.

This uses `Refs`, not `Fixes`, because what deletes the file on the reporter's machine is not established. #7714 should close once they confirm the fix.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A file or directory removed mid-copy fails the session with `copy legacy data store: lstat ...: no such file or directory` | The entry is skipped, the rest of the store migrates, one summary warning reports it, and the session can continue |
| A file removed between `lstat` and open fails with `openat ...: no such file or directory` | Same skip, counted in the same summary |
| Real `opencode acp` racing the migration, 24 trials: **24 failed** (23 `lstat`, 1 `open`) | Same trials: **24 succeeded**, with the deletion overlapping the copy in all 24 |
| A dangling symlink fails with `unsupported legacy data entry` | Unchanged: still fails |
| The whole store deleted mid-copy fails with `lstat ...: no such file or directory` | Still fails, with `legacy data store vanished during migration`, and nothing is activated |

## How

- Only "does not exist" is tolerated, at the two places it can surface: the walk callback and `sourceRoot.Open`. Other errors still abort.
- The source root going missing still fails, including after the walk: children of a store deleted mid-copy are skipped as vanished, so the root is re-checked before the copy is activated. Without that, a near-empty copy would become the permanent store.
- Skips produce one warn-level summary with the count and the first 5 paths relative to the store, because OpenCode can prune thousands of files during one copy.

**Trade-off for review:** the migration runs once, so a skipped entry never reaches the new store. That is harmless for a deleted file. An entry that was *moved* mid-copy, rather than deleted, would be missing from the snapshot under its old path and its new path may or may not be picked up. I kept tolerance across the whole store, not just `shell/`, because the real-binary run also failed on `opencode.db-journal`, and blocking every OpenCode 2 start is the worse failure.

**Omitted:** leaving `shell/` out of the copy entirely. I have not established that OpenCode 2 never needs old shell output.

This touches `copyTree` and `v2home.go`, which open PR #7138 also edits. #7138 changes the timeout and error text, not the walk, so any conflict should be small.

## Testing

**Against real OpenCode 2.2.5** (the reporter's version, release zip SHA-256 verified), with `HOME` and all XDG paths isolated in a scratch directory. No deletion was injected.

Each trial seeded 3,000 expired and 500 recent 64 KB `sh_*.out` files, started `opencode acp` on that store, and ran `PrepareV2DataHome` at a delay swept across the window before the deletion burst. The old side used `v2home.go` from `main`.

| | Old code | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trials succeeding | 0 of 24 | 24 of 24 |
| `lstat` ENOENT | 23 (including at least one on `opencode.db-journal`) | 0 |
| `open` ENOENT | 1 | 0 |
| Other errors | 0 | 0 |
| Recent files migrated | n/a | All 500, in all 24 trials |
| Real `opencode acp` on the migrated home creates a session | n/a | 4 of 4 checked |

**Unit and static checks:**
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/`: pass.
- `go test -race -run 'V2DataHome|CopyTree|SnapshotSQLite' ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/`: pass.
- `go vet` on the package, and `go build` of the agent adapters and the OpenCode 2 ACP driver: pass.
- New tests against the old `v2home.go`: fail with the reported `copy legacy data store: lstat ...` error.
- Removing each new branch on its own makes the new tests fail, at `openat` and at `lstat`.

The new test deletes at every `ctx.Err()` check in turn, so it needs no timing. It cannot delete between a directory's `lstat` and its listing, because no check runs there. That case goes through the same walk-callback branch.

The real-binary trials above ran before the root re-check and the summary warning were added. The re-check only adds a failure when the store root is gone, which did not happen in those trials, and the summary only changes logging.

**Not established or not run:**
- The fix has not been confirmed on the reporter's machine, and their trigger is unknown. AO's OpenCode 2 ACP runs against the isolated home, so that launch can't delete from the legacy store. Another `opencode` on the default data home could.
- Real cleanup leaves the directory in place even when all its files expire, so it does not explain the reporter's missing `shell/<project>` directory. It also deletes each expired file once, so it does not by itself explain failure on every attempt.
- These runs called `PrepareV2DataHome` directly. A full AO daemon and desktop session spawn was not exercised.
- The full backend suite and other CI jobs were not run locally, because the maintainer asked me not to run full suites on this low-disk machine. `golangci-lint` was not run locally: the installed v2.0.2 cannot load this repo's Go 1.27.1 config. These need to pass in CI.

ID                LABEL           INSTALL        AUTH

The hover on that row was uneven. The duration carried its own color, keyed off the row header with no transition, so "8s" snapped bright on hover. title: bug(hermes): Chat→Terminal switch fails with SESSION_CHANGED when the conversation can't be resumed
body:
### Report

Switching a Hermes Chat session to the Terminal UI fails when the Chat has messages and AO can't resume its native conversation. The session stays in Chat, and every retry fails the same way until the conversation can be resumed:

> SESSION_CHANGED: release untouched Chat provider for lab-1: empty root proof changed

AO is meant to fall back to a fresh terminal here (`degradedTerminalFreshMarkerText`: "Terminal started fresh — the Chat conversation stays archived in Chat."), but that fallback only works for a Chat with no messages.

For a user this looks like #7691 (Chat → Terminal is stuck), but it's a different error and it reproduces on current `main`.

### Reproduction

On `main` at `f7907457e8` with real Hermes (v0.22.5 Homebrew) and a fake model:

1. Start a Hermes Chat session and send one message.
2. Make the conversation unresumable. I tested two ways, both by editing lab data: clear its `title` in Hermes `state.db`, or delete `<data>/agents/hermes/<session>/native-home`.
3. Switch to Terminal: `POST /api/v1/sessions/<id>/interface-transition` with `{"targetMode":"tui","policy":"drain"}`.

Result: both cases fail with `SESSION_CHANGED`, including on a second attempt with the title cleared. A normal session with a resumable conversation switches fine.

I forced these states, so I haven't shown how often this happens without editing data. From the code, `PrepareNativeTerminalResume` also reports nothing resumable when the title is missing or ambiguous, or the conversation's `cwd` isn't the session workspace.

### Cause

`hermesNativeTerminalResumeID` returns no native id, so the switch is admitted as `identity-reset` with an empty `native_conversation_id`. `CommitSessionControllerEpoch` then treats an empty native id on Chat → TUI as a fresh start and requires an untouched Chat (`session_interface_transition_store.go`). A Chat with messages fails `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider`, which returns `empty root proof changed`.

Stable `v0.14.9` is not affected because it has no Hermes Chat. Nightlies built after #6635 are.

title: fix(session): open a fresh terminal when a Hermes Chat can't be resumed
body:
Code changes: +54 -3\
Tests: +134 -3\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A Hermes Chat → Terminal switch now opens a fresh terminal when the Chat has messages and its native conversation can't be resumed. It used to fail with `SESSION_CHANGED`. The Chat stays archived, and the fresh terminal doesn't run the session's prompt again.

## Why

Fixes #7724. The degraded switch promises a fresh terminal in this case, but the epoch commit only allowed one for a Chat with no messages, so the session stayed stuck in Chat.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Conversation has no title: `failed SESSION_CHANGED … empty root proof changed`, on every attempt | `completed`, terminal opens with `--create-if-missing`, Chat history kept |
| `native-home` missing: same failure | `completed`, fresh terminal, Chat history kept |
| A resumable conversation resumes | Unchanged |

No visual change beyond the switch succeeding.

## How

- **Store:** `CommitSessionControllerEpoch` accepts a touched conversation only when the active transition is Chat → TUI, `identity-reset`, with no native conversation. The empty-Chat guard stays for everything else, including `TestCommitSessionControllerEpochFreshTerminalRefusesTouchedConversation`. Reading the transition row inside the transaction avoids changing the epoch signature and its callers.
- **Prompt:** the first version of this fix re-sent the session's prompt to the fresh terminal, so the agent started the task again. `startTransitionTarget` now passes an empty prompt override when the Chat has accepted work (`LatestSequence != 0`). A Chat that never ran its prompt still hands it over, and the session keeps its saved prompt. If that read fails, the terminal opens without the prompt, because a blank terminal is recoverable and a repeated task isn't.
- **Rollback:** if the fresh terminal fails after the epoch commits, the existing restore path returns the session to Chat. I read this path but didn't exercise it live.

Please look closely at whether keeping the Chat's provider binding is right here. Unlike the empty-Chat path, it isn't released. Round trips back to Chat and to Terminal again worked live.

Until #7701 merges, the "Terminal started fresh" notice still reaches the model as a prompt (#7700). In the lab it showed up in Chat after switching back. That isn't changed here.

title: fix(browser): pass Cloudflare in the panel, hide the idle agent debugger, solidify Chrome mode
body:
Code changes: +466 -40\
Tests: +875 -20\
Others: +54 -9

## What

Follow-up to #6876, fixing reviewer feedback on the Browser panel and Chrome mode:

1. **Cloudflare and Google sign-in in the Browser panel.** The process-wide user agent now matches the panel's identity, and the `Electron/` token is back.
2. **Agent debugger visibility.** `Runtime` is off whenever no agent command is running.
3. **Chrome mode.** Agents get their own window and no longer take a tab from the user. Pages open faster, the extension reconnects by itself, setup takes fewer steps, and the extension shows Orchestrator's logo.
4. **Profile import.** Anti-bot cookies such as `cf_clearance` are no longer copied, and profiles already imported are repaired once when AO updates, with no re-import needed.

## Why

**Cloudflare.** After #6876, signing in at `dash.cloudflare.com` failed with "There was a problem with verification", even by hand on a fresh profile. #6876 set the user agent with `session.setUserAgent`, which left `app.userAgentFallback` on Electron's default, so the panel reported two user agents. Turnstile rejects that.

**Google.** #6876 also removed the `Electron/` token. Claiming to be plain Chrome made Google answer "This browser or app may not be secure" after the email step. Keeping the token passes.

**Agent debugger.** The first agent command on a tab left `Runtime` enabled until the session closed. Pages can measure that: a console-timing probe read about 230 ms against about 0 ms on a clean view.

**Chrome mode.** Agent tabs lived in the user's focused window, and every trusted click, keypress or screenshot switched to the agent's tab. In the agent's own window, those actions still pulled the user back from another tab. `open` waited for the full `load` event, which took 17–19 s on YouTube. The reconnect timer died with the suspended service worker.

**Import.** Bot managers bind these cookies to the browser that earned them, so replaying one from another browser can cause repeat challenges. Sites issue new ones on the next visit. Imports before #6075 also widened host-only cookies to domain cookies. Once a site sets its real cookie, the browser sends two with different values, and Google answers with "We've detected a problem with your cookie settings". Nightly updates reach existing users, so the repair ships here.

## Before / After

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare login, full identity | "There was a problem with verification" | Passes; hand sign-in succeeded |
| Google sign-in in the panel | "This browser or app may not be secure" | Reaches the password or passkey step |
| Pixelscan Browser card | Red "a Chromium-based browser on Mac OS" | **Still red.** Reported by hand on the final build |
| Console-timing probe while the agent is idle | ~230 ms | 0 ms |
| Agent action while the user is on another tab in the agent's window | Switches the user back | The tab stays; input is synthetic; screenshots and drags return a clear error |
| `open` on YouTube | 17–19 s | Returns at most 1.5 s after `DOMContentLoaded` (expected; the time was not re-measured) |
| AO restarts | Could stay disconnected until another extension event | Reconnected unaided in about 25 s |
| Chrome mode setup | Copy a path and follow one paragraph | One click registers, copies the path and opens `chrome://extensions`; three short steps remain |
| Google sign-in on a profile with duplicate cookies | Cookie settings error | Normal sign-in page after the startup repair |
| New session in Chrome | Consent window every time | Same by default, with an optional "allow every AO session" |

**Pixelscan is still red, and that is a trade-off.** A build that hid the `Electron/` token showed a green "Chrome 152" Browser card, but Google blocked sign-in on it. Sign-in on real sites was chosen over the Pixelscan card. Its headline also said "inconsistent" and listed "Automated behavior detected" even on that green build.

## How

**User agent (`browser-identity.ts`, `main.ts`).** `applyUserAgentFallback(app)` applies the same rewrite to the fallback first thing in `app.whenReady`. A test guards the call. The rest of the #6876 identity is unchanged.

Evidence from the real panel on wiped profiles. Turnstile's verdict appears on page load, without submitting anything:

| Identity | Turnstile |
| --- | --- |
| Electron defaults (twice; the second as a control after the failures) | Pass |
| `Sec-CH-UA` headers only | Pass |
| Reduced Chrome version only | Fail |
| App name removed only | Fail |
| All parts, `Electron/` token kept | Fail |
| App name removed + matching fallback | Pass |
| Full identity + fallback (twice) | Pass |

Which context Turnstile reads the old string from was not identified; the fix is established by behaviour.

`browserUserAgent` now keeps the `Electron/` token. Testing showed Google blocked the variants that hid both the token and the app name, and passed every variant that kept the token. The final combination was then checked by hand, below.

**CDP bridge (`agent-browser-cdp-bridge.ts`, `agent-browser-runtime.ts`).** `run()` brackets each command with `beginCommand`/`endCommand`. The bridge disables `Runtime` when none is running and re-enables it for the next one, after a synthetic `executionContextsCleared`. Client traffic between commands, such as a popup attaching, goes quiet again after 250 ms. `Emulation.set/clearDeviceMetricsOverride` from clients are swallowed, mainly so an agent can't clear AO's live viewport. `ensureDebugger` no longer enables `Runtime`.

**Chrome mode (`browser-extension`).**
- Each session gets its own unfocused window. A minimized one is restored without focus. When a session ends, its window closes if everything in it was the session's; if it holds a tab the user opened or handed over, the window stays and pages are ungrouped.
- If the agent's window shows a tab no agent owns, it is left alone.
- `open` waits for its own navigation to commit, then returns on `load` or 1.5 s after `DOMContentLoaded`, with `isLoading` set. A fragment-only `open` finishes at once.
- A 30-second alarm and `onStartup`/`onInstalled` reconnect the bridge.
- "Allow every AO session" is off by default. A session ending keeps it; revoking from the popup or the kill switch ends it.

**Setup (`BrowserChromeSection`, `chrome-extensions-page.ts`).** `chrome://` has no OS handler, so a new IPC launches Chrome with the URL. If that fails, the row says so and offers a retry. Strings are in all 9 locales. Chrome only lets a person load an unpacked extension, so Developer mode and Load unpacked remain until a Web Store listing, which is a separate PR.

**Import and repair (`browser-profile-import.ts`, `browser-cookie-repair.ts`).** Named anti-bot cookies are skipped and counted as skipped, with no warning, since nothing is lost. On the first launch of this version, the existing profiles are recorded, and only those are ever repaired, once each: anti-bot cookies are removed, and so is a domain cookie that a bulk import created when the site's real host-only copy arrived later. Old imports left no record, so `Cookies` is read directly: a burst of at least 20 cookies less than 100 ms apart marks an import (a real imported profile had 407 in 21 ms). A pair the site set itself is kept. If the store can't be read, duplicates stay. Each is deleted by setting it expired, which targets exactly one name, domain and path and leaves valid cookies untouched, so a failure or crash can't sign anyone out. `cookies.remove` is avoided because it takes every cookie the URL can see with that name. The jar is read back, and only cookies really gone count. Profiles created later earned their own cookies and are never touched. `browser-cookie-repair.json` under `~/.ao` tracks what is still pending. Each profile gets one attempt: failures are logged and not retried, because repeating this every launch would wipe freshly earned anti-bot cookies. An unreadable or unwritable state file repairs nothing. The repair runs in the background, so it never holds up the window. A page opened during that first run could briefly see the old cookies. A same-named cookie on a parent domain is kept, since it can't be told apart from a legitimate one, so a site that rejects that pair stays affected. Partitioned anti-bot cookies may not be deletable this way (untested), and with no retry they would stay until they expire. An import of fewer than 20 cookies isn't recognised, so its duplicates stay.

**Review focus and trade-offs:**
- **Reload required:** this adds the `alarms` permission, so existing installs must reload the unpacked extension.
- **Console capture:** `ao browser console` and `errors` may miss messages logged between commands, on every page including local previews.
- **`Runtime` during commands:** it is still on while a command runs, so a page checking at that moment can see it. Agent-driven Cloudflare passed anyway, but other sites may differ.
- **Synthetic input:** used only while the user is on another tab in the agent's window. Sites can detect it more easily, and some may ignore it.
- **Blanket consent:** "allow every session" removes the per-session prompt for anyone who ticks it. Please check you're comfortable with that.
- **Alarm cost:** while AO isn't running, the alarm launches the native host every 30 s.
- **macOS occlusion:** a fully covered window counts as hidden, so trusted input and screenshots need the agent's window visible somewhere.

**Known gaps, not fixed here:**
- A hidden panel still reports an outer size of 0x0 and a parked 1280x720 viewport. The earlier claim that agent-browser forced 1280x720 was wrong: that is AO's `OFFSCREEN_BOUNDS`. The only fix found, parking under another view inside the window, makes every hidden tab report itself visible and keep running. Agent-driven Cloudflare passed with the panel hidden.

## Testing

Run on this branch before the final identity commit, which changes only `browser-identity.ts` and its test; after it, the project typecheck and identity tests were rerun:
- `npm test`: 643 of 644 files passed; 11,170 tests passed, 1 failed, 9 skipped. The failure is `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`, a file this PR doesn't change; it passed 3 of 3 when rerun alone.
- `npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 147 of 148 passed. The failure is `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts`, which fails the same way locally on clean `main`, and renderer smoke passed in CI on this PR's previous head.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: 0 errors.
- `npm run build:browser-extension`: passes.
- `npm run test:browser-postcondition-integration`: passes, through the real `agent-browser` and the changed bridge.
- `go test ./internal/browserchrome ./internal/browserruntime`: passes.
- `TestChromeE2E` in Chrome for Testing 157 passes: the existing flow plus new checks for keeping the user's tab, restoring a minimized window, separate windows per session, closing a finished session's window, ticking "allow every session", and recovering after the window is closed. It ran with `--no-sandbox` and occlusion-detection flags in the test environment; the test documents them. `--use-mock-keychain` is now documented in the test: without it, macOS asks for the login password on every launch, which appeared to stall pages.

Real Electron, against real Google: a clean profile reached sign-in; adding the duplicates produced `CookieMismatch`; the expired-cookie repair restored sign-in and kept the real and unrelated cookies. Real Electron also confirmed a parent-domain cookie and another path survive deleting one exact cookie. On a real Chromium cookie store, with the browser holding it open, burst detection found the imported cookies, removed the import-damaged copy and kept a site-set pair. In the real dev app, the first launch repaired the existing test profile once, and a profile added afterwards was left alone on the next launch.

Manual, on the dev build:
- On the final identity, by hand in the panel: Google, Cloudflare and ElevenLabs passed. Pixelscan's Browser card is red.
- Agent-driven `open` of the Cloudflare login, with the panel hidden, showed no verification error. No credentials were submitted.
- The debugger probe read 0 ms at the end of a 90-second idle after agent commands, with one 2 ms blip in the 18 seconds of history it keeps.
- The extension reconnected in about 25 s after a dev app restart, with nothing touched in Chrome.
- In real Chrome, a Fireship video run felt much better and faster after the tab and `open` changes. That was before the last two commits.

Bot-protected sites in the real panel, loaded by an agent with the panel hidden, page text read after 12 s. No credentials submitted. A page loading without a challenge does not prove that a login would pass.

| Site | Result |
| --- | --- |
| reCAPTCHA v3 score demo | Score 0.9 |
| ElevenLabs, ChatGPT, Discord, LinkedIn, X sign-in pages | Load, no challenge |
| Nike (Akamai expected, not confirmed) | Loads, no block |
| nowsecure.nl | Loads, no challenge |
| Google sign-in | Agent could not get past the email step; passed by hand on the final identity |
| DataDome test page | Not a real test: it showed the site's homepage text |

**Not tested:**
- A packaged build; its profile path is fixed to the installed app's. To be checked on the first nightly.
- The new setup flow by hand: Set up opening Chrome, the three steps, and the failure message have unit tests only. The rendered Settings UI has not been checked against `DESIGN.md`, so there are no screenshots yet.
- A real profile from before #6075 going through the startup repair: the real-Electron run used recreated duplicates.
- A fully covered agent window, and sites that reject synthetic input.
- A freshly imported profile against Cloudflare: the skip has a unit test only.
- Windows and Linux, beyond CI and unit tests.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [ ] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable (related fixes from one round of #6876 feedback; no issue)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (Before / After is filled in; Settings screenshots are still missing)
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) (pending for this push)

title: [Feature]: Support GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (*.ghe.com)
body:
### Problem

As a developer whose company hosts code on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (`<company>.ghe.com`), I can't use the PR, CI and review lanes, because every repository on a `*.ghe.com` host is treated as GitLab. I found this by reading the code and haven't run AO against a GHE repository yet.

Three places in the code cause it (at `2ac80eb`):

- `RepositoryProvider` in `backend/internal/domain/repository_identity.go:29` only recognizes `github.com`, `*.github.com` and `*.ghe.io` as GitHub. Any other host goes to the GitLab adapter, including `*.ghe.com`. The same allowlist appears in `parsePRURL` (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/provider.go:657`) and in `observer_provider.go:847`.
- `backend/internal/daemon/scm_wiring.go:55` builds the GitHub SCM provider without `RESTBase` or `GraphQLURL`, so all calls go to `https://api.github.com`, whatever the repository's host.
- The GitHub tracker (`backend/internal/adapters/tracker/github/tracker.go:23`) defaults to `https://api.github.com` in the same way, and `tracker_wiring.go:22` doesn't set `BaseURL`.

As far as I can tell, a `*.ghe.com` repository goes to the GitLab adapter, so AO never sees its PRs, checks or reviews. Sessions would then stay out of In review and Ready to merge, and CI failures would never reach the worker.

### Proposed direction

1. Add `*.ghe.com` to the GitHub host check, keeping the check in one shared place so the three copies can't drift.
2. Derive the API base from the repository host instead of the hardcoded default:
   - `github.com`: `https://api.github.com` and `https://api.github.com/graphql`
   - `<sub>.ghe.com`: `https://api.<sub>.ghe.com` and `https://api.<sub>.ghe.com/graphql`. These are the hosts `gh api --hostname <sub>.ghe.com` calls. See [Network details for GHE.com](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/data-residency/network-details-for-ghecom).
3. Pick the provider per repository host in the SCM and tracker wiring, so one daemon can serve both github.com and GHE projects.
4. Resolve the token per host (the equivalent of `gh auth token --hostname <host>`).

Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server (`https://<host>/api/v3`) would fit the same per-host shape, but it needs an explicit host setting because it can't be recognized by hostname. I'd leave that out of this issue unless you want both at once.

### Alternatives considered

- Using the board without the SCM lanes. That leaves out the CI and review feedback loop, which is the main reason I want AO.
- Keeping a patched fork. I'd rather fix it here so other GHE.com users get it too.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

I'd like to open the PR for this. Can I work on this?

title: fix(editor): skip the Cursor Agent shim and toast launch failures
body:
## Problem

Clicking the editor button showed "Could not open Cursor. Check that it is installed and try again." as truncated red text in the top bar, on a machine without the Cursor IDE.

The Cursor Agent CLI installer puts a `cursor` shim in `~/.local/bin`. Without the IDE it only runs `cursor agent`; anything else prints "No Cursor IDE installation found" and exits 1. AO found `cursor` on PATH, listed Cursor as an editor, and every open failed.

## Fix

- `editor-handoff.ts`: when the `cursor` found on PATH is the agent shim (detected by its error text, reading only the first 4 KB), it does not count as Cursor. A `Cursor.app` bundle is still detected.
- `TopbarOpenEditorButton.tsx`: launch failures show as an error toast. The inline top-bar error is removed.

## Testing

Verified in the dev desktop app with the real shim on PATH:
1. Editor list from the main process had no Cursor; the Open-in menu matched.
2. Put a fake `zed` that exits 1 on PATH, chose Zed from the menu: error toast appeared bottom-right, nothing inline in the top bar.

Unit tests added for the shim case and updated for the toast; CI runs them.

title: feat(review): persist provider-neutral receipts
body:
Code changes: +399 -52  
Tests: +917 -3  
Others: +119 -10

## What

Store an optional, target-bound publication receipt with each review result, including provider, status, reviewed head, and typed references.

## Why

Distinguish the local verdict from reported publication while preserving legacy GitHub compatibility.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Results expose a verdict and optional GitHub review ID. | Results also support published, blocked, or unconfirmed receipts. |
| Publication evidence is not persisted with the result. | Receipt, result, and first-submit policy snapshot are stored atomically and included in trigger-owned change events. |

## How

Validate receipt identity and cross-field consistency. An explicit GitLab receipt with `githubReviewId` is rejected before persistence. Valid retries are idempotent; receipt-free legacy behavior is unchanged. HTTP/CLI and generated storage/API contracts carry the optional receipt.

Provider publishing, publication routes, native approvals, feedback delivery, UI, and tracing follow separately, including GitLab legacy-ID restrictions without a receipt. A receipt does not independently prove publication or delivery.

## Testing

Relevant local receipt, migration, storage, wire, and race checks passed. CI will run on the upstream pull request. Independent review of the synchronized revision found no required changes.
