title: fix(dictation): add speech usage string to the app's Info.plist
body:
## What

In packaged builds, dictation fails immediately with "Dictation stopped unexpectedly." This adds `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`, and a dictation-specific `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, to the main app's Info.plist.

## Why

The first signed nightly with dictation (`0.14.9-nightly.202611040702`) crashes the helper every time you press the mic. Each crash report says:

> This app has crashed because it attempted to access privacy-sensitive data without a usage description. The app's Info.plist must contain an NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription key…

The helper's own Info.plist has the key. When the helper is signed and nested inside `Agent Orchestrator.app`, macOS checks the request against the enclosing app's Info.plist, and that plist only had Electron's default strings. I narrowed it down by running the shipped helper in different setups:

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| Signed helper inside the app, launched from a terminal (disclaim path) | Crash |
| Same, launched on its own by LaunchServices (`open`, parent is launchd) | Crash |
| The same signed helper copied out of the app bundle | Works |
| Locally built ad-hoc helper (dev) | Works |

#7611 was only tested in the dev lab, where the helper is ad-hoc signed, so this never showed up.

## Notes

- The permission prompts say **Orchestrator**, the app's display name.
- The microphone string replaces Electron's generic "This app needs access to the microphone". It's worded for dictation and for tools run inside AO, since macOS also attributes terminals and agents to the app.
- Only a signed build can confirm the fix. A dev build doesn't reproduce the crash. Check the nightly built from this change: press the mic, macOS should prompt for Speech Recognition, and the text should stream in.

## Testing

- Added a `forge.config.test.ts` case that checks both keys are in `extendInfo`.
- Local tests and typecheck weren't run; leaving those to CI.

title: fix(session): let a degraded fresh TUI keep its messaged Chat archived
body:
Code changes: +84 -30
Tests: +226 -0
Others: +0 -0

## What

A degraded hermes Chat→TUI switch whose native conversation cannot be resolved
now starts a fresh terminal even when the Chat has messages, and the messaged
Chat conversation stays archived exactly as it was. Previously the switch
failed with `SESSION_CHANGED` on every attempt.

Fixes #7724 · Related #7691 (same user-visible symptom, different error; its
fix family is in flight on other branches and is not touched here)

## Why

The fresh-terminal degrade path (`degradedTerminalFreshMarkerText`) only fired
for an empty Chat. The controller-epoch commit for a Chat→TUI switch with an
empty native id unconditionally required the untouched-Chat release proof
(`ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider`), so any Chat with real history failed
the commit with `SESSION_CHANGED: release untouched Chat provider ...: empty
root proof changed`, and every retry failed the same way until the native
conversation became resumable again.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Chat with messages + unresumable native conversation → `POST /interface-transition {"targetMode":"tui"}` fails `SESSION_CHANGED`; session stuck in Chat, retries fail identically | Same switch completes through the degraded fresh-terminal path (`degraded_kind=identity-reset`); the messaged Chat conversation stays archived with its provider binding and turn history intact |
| Strict Chat→TUI handoff with an empty native id still proves the Chat untouched | Unchanged: the strict commit keeps requiring the untouched proof (pinned by the existing `TestFreshInterfaceEpochReleasesOnlyUntouchedRootProvider`) |

No user-visible UI change; the observable behavior change is the transition
outcome recorded on the durable transition row (phase/error code above).

## How

Adapted from the fork commit `5faf9cb6d3` (`plus/hermes-adapter`, "degrade
hermes Chat→TUI handoff to native restore or fresh TUI"). Upstream already
landed that commit's admission + marker logic via #6635 — including the
fresh-TUI fallback this bug breaks — so nothing from the fork was duplicated;
the fork's store has the same untouched-proof gap and needed no port. The fix
is new and minimal:

- `CommitSessionControllerEpochArchivedChat` (SQLite store): same CAS epoch
  commit, but the Chat→TUI empty-native-id commit skips the untouched-release
  requirement and keeps the source Chat conversation archived as-is, provider
  binding included.
- `lifecycle.Manager.CommitControllerEpochArchivedChat` threads the flag to
  the store (`controllerEpochStore` gains the method).
- The session-manager transition runner uses the archived-chat commit only
  when `transition.DegradedKind != ""` (degraded identity-reset). Non-degraded
  paths are unchanged. Rollback (`RestoreControllerEpoch`) swaps the modes and
  never reaches the release block, so it is untouched.

## TDD receipts

RED (test-only commit `bf6e6e2c5a`, pushed before any production code; test
run against unmodified upstream `main` @ `2ac80ebc4e`):

```
--- FAIL: TestInterfaceTransitionHermesChatWithMessagesToTUIDegradesToFreshTUI (0.40s)
    interface_transition_identity_degrade_test.go:371: phase = failed, code = SESSION_CHANGED, error = release untouched Chat provider for proj-1: empty root proof changed
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/session_manager	0.711s
```

GREEN (fix commit `6f486e10b7`):

```
--- PASS: TestInterfaceTransitionHermesChatWithMessagesToTUIDegradesToFreshTUI (0.42s)
```

Plus a store-level boundary test added with the fix:
`TestArchivedChatInterfaceEpochKeepsMessagedChatArchived` — the strict commit
still refuses a messaged Chat; the archived-chat commit succeeds and preserves
the archive.

## Testing

- `go build ./...` ✅
- `go vet ./...` ✅
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/lifecycle/...` ✅
- `go test ./internal/service/...` — all packages pass except a pre-existing,
  environment-specific failure in `internal/service/shellterm`
  (`TestCueCommandPreservesNativeEvalEOFAndOptionBehavior`: local
  bash/sh EOF-backslash behavior + missing `fish` binary). Verified failing
  identically on pristine `main` @ `2ac80ebc4e` before my commits.
- `golangci-lint v2.13.2 run --path-mode=abs` (whole backend) ✅ `0 issues.`

## Coordination note

In-flight branches `fix/hermes-restore-identity` (#7690),
`fix/acp-history-settle-attempt-budget` (#7689), `fix/hermes-resume-no-model-override`,
and `fix/hermes-title-children-restore` carry adjacent hermes
identity-read/degrade code. This PR touches the same degrade family
(`interface_transition.go`, its degrade tests) but only the epoch-commit
path; expect a trivial rebase order with those branches, no semantic overlap.

Note for maintainers: as a first-time contributor to this repo, my CI runs
likely need maintainer approval before they execute (GitHub first-time
contributor gate). Please approve the workflow run so the lint job can go
green on this head.

title: fix(desktop): stop the window jolt when opening menus with no browser page
body:
Code changes: +17 -3\
Tests: +41 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On macOS, opening any dropdown or dialog no longer shrinks the window by 1px for a frame. Opening the model or permission picker made the composer (and everything else pinned to the bottom) jump up a pixel and back, which looked like a shake.

## Why

When an overlay opens, the main process raises the shell view above the embedded Browser page. On macOS a raised shell can show a stale surface that hides the page under it, so `window-composition.ts` shrinks the shell by 1px and restores it on the next tick to force a rebuild (#4136). That runs on every menu or dialog open, even when no Browser page is on screen, because the overlay observer is mounted for every session view. With no page underneath there is nothing to hide, so the nudge is a visible resize and nothing else.

Measured in the dev app over CDP, clicking the model picker in a chat:
- before: `innerHeight` 860 → 859 at ~145ms → 860 at ~157ms
- after: 860 the whole time; no element moved

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Opening the model or permission picker jolts the whole window by 1px (composer visibly shakes). | Picker opens with nothing moving. With the Browser panel showing a page, the repaint still runs as before. |

Screenshots: see local files.

## How

- `createWindowComposition` takes `hasLivePageBelow`. `setOverlayOpen(true)` only runs the 1px repaint when that returns true. It defaults to true, so callers that don't pass it keep the old behavior.
- `main.ts` wires it to a new `browserViewHost.hasVisiblePanel()`: any Browser panel that is on screen with at least one tab. This is the same condition `refreshLastFocusedPanelSurface` already uses before it refreshes the page.
- `restackShell` (a browser view added while an overlay is open) still always repaints. The new view may not report itself as visible yet at that moment, so skipping there could bring back the blank-page bug.

title: feat(scm): support GHE.com tenant hosts
body:
Code changes: +425 -121\
Tests: +445 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Support GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (`<tenant>.ghe.com`) next to github.com in one daemon. Tenant repositories are now treated as GitHub, and their SCM and tracker calls go to the tenant API with that host's own gh login.

## Why

Closes #7729. Core-team scope approval on that issue is still pending, so this PR is open for scope feedback, and I'm happy to narrow or split it. Every `*.ghe.com` repository was classified as GitLab, and even as GitHub every call went to `api.github.com`. So PR, CI, review and issue-intake lanes never worked for these projects.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Origin `https://acme.ghe.com/team/app.git` is classified as `gitlab` | Classified as `github`, host `acme.ghe.com`, repo `team/app` |
| PR URL `https://acme.ghe.com/team/app/pull/7` is rejected as "not a PR/MR URL" | Parses as GitHub PR 7 of `team/app` on `acme.ghe.com` |
| SCM and tracker requests for a tenant repo go to `api.github.com` with the github.com token | They go to `api.acme.ghe.com` (REST) and `api.acme.ghe.com/graphql`, with `gh auth token --hostname acme.ghe.com` |
| A tenant issue URL or `team/app#5` in a tenant project resolves against github.com | It resolves against the tenant tracker, and the tracker ID carries host `acme.ghe.com` |

No UI change.

## How

- One shared `domain.IsGitHubHost` replaces seven copied host allowlists. A tenant is exactly one DNS label before `.ghe.com`, so `ghe.com`, `api.acme.ghe.com` and `acme.ghe.com.evil.example` are not GitHub.
- The GitHub SCM provider keeps one lazily built client per tenant (`clientFor`), following the GitLab adapter's `clientForHost`. github.com and `*.ghe.io` keep the existing client, so their behaviour is unchanged.
- Credentials: a tenant only uses its own gh login. The github.com chain (`AO_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, default gh login) is never sent to a tenant. gh applies `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` to every `*.ghe.com` host, so the tenant lookup strips both. A missing tenant login fails closed with `ErrNoToken`, and no request is sent.
- A mixed github.com and tenant batch is split per host. A failing tenant only marks its own PRs as not fetched.
- The SCM observer keys identity and rate-limit cooldown per tenant. A tenant login (for example an EMU account) and the tenant's API quota stay separate from github.com.
- The daemon registers a `githubHostTracker` under `"github"`: host `""` goes to the existing tracker, and each tenant gets its own lazy tracker.

Intentional omissions:
- Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server (`<host>/api/v3`). It can't be recognized by hostname and needs explicit config.
- Env-var tokens for tenants. Only the stored gh login is used.
- Tenant login in the status/telemetry views and `ao doctor`.
- The SCM credential probe still runs plain `gh auth token`. On a machine logged in only to a tenant, it depends on gh's default-host fallback.

## Testing

- New tests cover tenant classification and look-alike hosts, tenant API routing, per-host identity, the github.com token never reaching a tenant, fail-closed without a login (including a fake `gh` on `PATH`), mixed-host batches, tracker host stamping and routing, and tenant issue references.
- `go test` for the touched packages (`domain`, `cli`, `adapters/scm/...`, `adapters/tracker/...`, `daemon`, `observe/scm`, `observe/trackerintake`, `service/session`) passes at every commit. golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports 0 issues.
- Full `go test ./...`: 110 tests fail locally, and the same 110 fail on the base commit. They are environment-specific (missing `fish` shell, agent CLIs and account state on my machine), so CI is the reference for the full suite.
- Not run against a live GHE.com tenant. The tenant API shape (`api.<tenant>.ghe.com`) follows GitHub's "Network details for GHE.com" docs.

title: fix(chat): never lock the composer on a send with no answer
body:
## Problem

When a send gets no answer (a dropped tunnel to a remote Mac, or the app restarting mid-send), the composer keeps the message as a `dispatching` delivery and goes read-only until that exact message is retried. Plain sends had no way to discard it. A user on a remote session couldn't type at all: an old 4,482-character paste was stuck in the box, and the only way out was a send arrow that wasn't clearly a retry.

## Fix

- **The box never locks.** An unanswered send moves to a "Not sent" strip above the composer. The box stays editable, and new messages send beside it with their own delivery IDs.
- **Retry** resends exactly that message with the **same delivery ID**, so the daemon dedups it and it can't arrive twice. The chevron shows the full text, plus Copy.
- **Discard**, with a 5 s Undo.
- If the chat already holds the message (the answer was lost, not the message), the strip clears itself.
- The send POST times out after 60 s (except with attachments, whose upload can take longer) and logs `[chat] send got no answer`, so a hung send leaves evidence instead of waiting forever.

Storage: one optional `unsent` slot on the session draft (`chat-drafts.ts`), validated on load and kept by every other draft write.

## Evidence (real desktop app, isolated lab, real Claude session)

Repro: the send POST is aborted at the network layer (`route.abort("failed")`), so the daemon never sees it. Then the window reloads.

| Before (main) | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/0aaa73e9748560d5cfbcf9652204bd8fab4445cb/before-3.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/0aaa73e9748560d5cfbcf9652204bd8fab4445cb/after-3.png) |
| Box is read-only, and typing "yo" does nothing | Box is editable and "yo" is typed beside the strip |

| "yo" sent while the old message waits | Full text | Retry delivered the old message (agent replied "ok") | Discard + Undo |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/0aaa73e9748560d5cfbcf9652204bd8fab4445cb/after-4.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/0aaa73e9748560d5cfbcf9652204bd8fab4445cb/after-5.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/0aaa73e9748560d5cfbcf9652204bd8fab4445cb/after-6.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/0aaa73e9748560d5cfbcf9652204bd8fab4445cb/after-7.png) |

## Tests

- New: `chat-drafts.test.ts` covers park, retry, discard, restore, survival across writes, validation, and the refused cases. `ChatComposer.test.tsx` "unsent message strip" covers a restored send, an in-session lost answer, Retry with the old ID, Discard/Undo, and observed acceptance.
- Updated to the new behavior: the optimistic-send retry tests and the `ChatWorkspace` rejected-send test. Legacy locked-path tests pin `parkUnsentSends={false}`.
- Local: 4255/4255 renderer tests in lib, chat, NewChatPage, i18n and hooks; `tsgo` reports no errors under `src/`.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Excerpt and file-reference sends keep the old locked retry, as they already do for optimistic sends (the strip can't show those chips yet).
- One unsent slot per session: a second unanswered send while one is parked stays in the old locked state until the first is resolved.
- After parking, an image's bytes leave memory with the next draft, so Retry re-reads the staged file (the same path a restart retry already uses).
- `NewChatPage` opts out (`parkUnsentSends={false}`): its pending launch tracks its own unanswered send.
- The underlying reason the original send never reached the remote Mac is still unknown. The new timeout and log line are there to catch it next time.

title: fix(opencode-v2): skip pruned legacy entries when copying the data store
body:
Code changes: +24 -2
Tests: +53 -0
Others: +0 -0

## Why

An OpenCode 2 session fails to start whenever AO's one-time legacy data migration hits a shell-session output file that OpenCode has already pruned:

```
chat driver unavailable: persistent ACP host: opencode-v2 ACP: prepare data home:
opencode: copy legacy data store: lstat .../shell/9b29.../sh_1a52....out:
no such file or directory
```

`copyTree` walks the legacy store with `filepath.Walk`, which reads a directory's entries and then `lstat`s each one by path. OpenCode prunes its own shell-session directories concurrently, so a directory can disappear between those two steps. The walker then reports `ENOENT` for a child that is no longer reachable, and the migration aborts. Because a failed migration removes its staging directory and leaves no isolated store behind, every retry re-runs the copy and can fail at the same stale reference — which reads as "always fails for this project".

## What

Treat a vanished legacy entry as already migrated and skip it, at each point the copy can notice it: opening the source root, the walk callback's error, the directory `Mkdir`, and opening the source file. Every other copy error (permissions, unsupported entry types, I/O failures) stays fatal, and an interrupted or partial migration still cannot overwrite an existing isolated store.

## Reproducing

`TestCopyTreeToleratesEntryVanishedBeforeCopy` rebuilds the reporter's store shape (`shell/<session>/sh_*.out`) and prunes the session directory from inside the walk, after its entries have been read but before they are stat'ed — the exact sequence that produces the reported error. A small `walkLegacyData` seam (same pattern as `claudeNow` / `renameCodexFileForRemoval`) makes that ordering deterministic instead of a timing race. Without the fix the test fails with the reported `lstat`/`GetFileAttributesEx` ENOENT; with it, the pruned entry is skipped and the surviving `auth.json` still lands in the isolated store.

`TestCopyTreeToleratesVanishedLegacyStore` covers the other ordering: the store disappears between `PrepareV2DataHome`'s existence check and the walk, which must also be a no-op rather than a hard failure.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/...` (Windows, and `-race`)
- `go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/...`
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/...` — 0 issues
- `gofmt -l` clean

Known local gaps, none introduced here:

- `TestPrepareV2DataHomeSkipsToolCache` skips/fails on unprivileged Windows because it needs symlink privileges; it fails identically on `main` without this change.
- `internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog` and `internal/service/agentauth` have pre-existing Windows-environment failures that reproduce on an unmodified checkout.

Fixes #7714

title: fix(release): point macOS download links at the published dmg names
body:
Code changes: +29 -10\
Tests: +3 -3\
Others: +27 -20

## What

The macOS download links return 404. Stable v0.14.9 publishes `Orchestrator-darwin-{arm64,x64}.dmg`, but the README, its 7 translations, the docs install table and the Grok setup skill still link `agent-orchestrator-darwin-{arm64,x64}.dmg`. This PR moves those links to the published names, and the hourly release guard now fails when a linked asset is missing.

No release asset changes here. This PR changes no asset name and does not touch the auto-updater.

## Why

Refs #7726

Supersedes #7457, the companion link PR named in ao-releases#50's rollout plan. This PR has all of its changes, plus the Grok manifest regen it was missing.

The release process renamed the DMG on purpose. OrchestratorInc/ao-releases#50 made the stable name `Orchestrator-darwin-<arch>.dmg`, and the conductor now rejects the old `agent-orchestrator-darwin-<arch>.dmg`. The links in this repo did not move with it. That repo is private and I can't read it, so this comes from somewherelostt's review of this PR. `build-mac-dmg.mjs` writes whatever `--output` the conductor passes, so this repo does not set the name.

fc330a79b (#7438) is not the cause. It leaves `maker-dmg.ts`, `build-mac-dmg.mjs` and `build-artifacts.yml` unchanged. Its `productName` edit also doesn't explain the old name: 27 stable releases shipped `agent-orchestrator-darwin-*.dmg` while `productName` was `Agent Orchestrator`.

v0.14.9 is the first release with the new name. Nightlies ship no DMG, so nothing showed it earlier.

This PR does not cover the website's Download link or the file name the release process produces. Both live outside this repo, so #7726 stays open until those are settled.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| README and docs macOS links: 404 | 206 for both architectures |
| Grok setup skill on a Mac: `DOWNLOAD_FAILED` | Downloads `Orchestrator-darwin-$a.dmg`, which returns 206 |
| A linked asset missing from the latest stable: guard passes | Guard fails and names the asset |

## How

Links moved because this repo cannot change asset names, and v0.14.9 is already out. Merging fixes the README at once and the docs site after its deploy, with no new release. The next stable is expected to use the same names, so these links should keep working.

Old `agent-orchestrator-darwin-{arm64,x64}.dmg` URLs are outside this PR. They include saved links and a hardcoded link on orchestrator.inc/download. That site left this repo in #5824, so this PR cannot change it. Copies of the DMGs under the old names were added to v0.14.9, the way the zip, exe and AppImage already ship two names with one digest. Both old URLs now return 200 and the downloads match the original SHA-256, but only for v0.14.9. `latest/download` moves with each stable and the conductor will not ship the old names, so those URLs return 404 again from the next stable. orchestrator.inc/download needs to move to the new name before then.

The Grok skill edit comes with a regenerated `integrations/grok-bot/manifest.json` (version 2026.11.04.1), because `ao-update` compares and verifies skills against it.

`InstallDownloads` now takes full filenames, because a fixed `agent-orchestrator-` prefix could not express the DMG name. Its release host is now `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`, like the other links; it had been relying on GitHub's redirect from `Untrivial-ai`.

The guard reads asset names from the README, translations and `mdx.tsx`, so there is no second list to keep in sync. It reports after publish, so it cannot block a bad release.

## Testing

- Ran the guard step's script against the real v0.14.9 release: exit 1 on main (`missing asset 'agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg'`), exit 0 on this branch.
- Ran it in a checkout using the workflow's sparse patterns: exit 0. A missing source file and empty sources both exit 1 with an `::error::` line.
- Requested all 14 download URLs on this branch, following redirects: all 206.
- Checked all 7 Grok skills against the regenerated manifest: bytes and SHA-256 match.
- Full suites run in CI.

## Manual E2E

Every check was by hand on Windows 11, 2026-11-04. Downloads were full files fetched with `curl -L` from `releases/latest/download/…`, then `sha256sum`, size, and the `koly` trailer in the last 512 bytes (the UDIF DMG footer).

| Link | Clicked from | File | Size / SHA-256 | OK |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg` (new) | README on this branch, in the Claude browser pane: download started, page stayed (a bad name lands on GitHub's 404 page) | `Orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg` | 245971768 / `da804ce0…0a12ca`, `koly` | ✅ |
| `Orchestrator-darwin-x64.dmg` (new) | href on this branch's README, the translations and the built docs page (not clicked in the browser) | `Orchestrator-darwin-x64.dmg` | 259832751 / `6bcae40c…31b87b`, `koly` | ✅ |
| `agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg` (old) | README on main, in the browser pane: download started | `agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg` | 245971768 / `da804ce0…0a12ca` (same as new), `koly` | ✅ (v0.14.9 only) |
| `agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.dmg` (old) | README on main, in the browser pane: download started | `agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.dmg` | 259832751 / `6bcae40c…31b87b` (same as new), `koly` | ✅ (v0.14.9 only) |
| Docs `InstallDownloads` (static `next build` of this branch) | `out/installation/index.html` | 8 hrefs: both new DMGs, both zips, exe, AppImage, deb, rpm, all on `OrchestratorInc` | each 206 | ✅ |
| Grok `ao-setup` (`SKILL.md:55`, `$a` = arm64 / x64) | same URL as the new DMGs above | `Orchestrator-darwin-$a.dmg` | as above | ✅ |
| zip ×2, exe, AppImage, deb, rpm, `latest.yml`, `latest-mac.yml`, `latest-linux.yml` | `curl -sIL` | unchanged names | all 206; `latest-mac.yml` still lists `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-*-0.14.9.zip` | ✅ |

Not done in the browser: the x64 click on this branch's README, and clicks on the translated READMEs and the served docs page. The browser pane stopped responding after the first DMG downloads. For those links I read the hrefs from the source files and the built docs HTML. They are the same URLs that were downloaded and hashed above.

## Regression risk

Risk tier: NORMAL
Could break: README and docs download links, the Grok setup install, the `latest-release` guard job.
Checked: every link and the guard step, as listed under Testing. Updater feed: `latest-mac.yml` references only the versioned zips, so it does not use these names. Homebrew: the cask uses the zip, which returns 206.
Changed test expectations: the DMG layout test and the `frontend.yml` fixture now use `Orchestrator-darwin-arm64.dmg`, including the expected `artifactName`.
Regression from: OrchestratorInc/ao-releases#50 in the release process (see Why). Nothing in this repo.

Not verified: the workflow running in GitHub Actions (it runs on a schedule, not on PRs), the docs table in a deployed site beyond CI's build, and the renamed `frontend.yml` fixture (`mac-dmg-layout` is skipped on this PR). The guard covers the README and docs names. The Grok skill builds its URL from a shell variable, so the guard cannot see it.

The hourly guard run is already red for a separate reason: its `package-version` job fails because `frontend/package.json` on main says 0.14.8. This PR does not touch that, and until it is fixed that red run can hide a new asset failure.

title: feat(desktop): offer Republish for a published file that changed
body:
Code changes: +49 -19\
Tests: +66 -0\
Others: +9 -0 (locale strings)

## What

When a published artifact has changed since it was published, the share popover now offers **Republish** beside **Unpublish**. Republish updates the same link: same URL, same link slot. A published file that has not changed keeps today's popover, with only Copy link and Unpublish.

## Why

The popover already told people "The link still shows the earlier version", but gave them no way to fix it short of unpublishing, which breaks the link for everyone who has it.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Changed file: a message, then only Unpublish and Copy link | Changed file: the same message, then Unpublish, Copy link and Republish |
| Published view shows no credential warning | Changed file with a credential: the warning shows above the actions, naming what the new version holds |

Screenshots to be attached by hand (`gh` cannot upload images). They come from the real `ShareArtifactButton` and app stylesheet in Chromium, with a stubbed bridge and sign-in, not the full desktop app.

## How

- **No backend or contract change.** Publish already accepts `shareId`, for local uploads and for cloud session files, and treats it as an update of the active link. The popover now sends it from the published view.
- `outdated` on the published phase was a boolean and now carries the inspection and links, because Republish needs the fingerprint it was shown. The fingerprint check still refuses a file that changed since.
- A republish in progress keeps its link in `PendingShare`, so closing and reopening the popover resolves it the same way.
- The action row now wraps, with actions kept right-aligned. Three actions do not fit on one line in German, Spanish, Portuguese or Russian. The Russian label is "Обновить" ("Update"), because the literal wording overflowed the popover even when wrapped.
- The progress state reuses "Publishing…" rather than adding a new string.

Intentional omissions:

- The replaced version stays in S3 for up to 1 hour (`ArtifactReplacedGrace`), so reads in progress can finish, and is no longer served immediately. Unpublish deletes at once; republish deliberately does not.
- A local file's fingerprint includes its modified time, so re-saving identical content offers Republish. Republishing then re-uploads the same bytes, which is harmless.
- Records from before fingerprints were kept have nothing to compare, so they offer no Republish until the link is next published.

## Testing

- Added popover tests for offering Republish and updating the same link, the credential warning, a file changing during a republish, cancelling, and an unpublished link. Added an IPC test that a republish sends `shareId` and clears the change.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e` and the CI-sharding test pass, on Node 24.
- Full frontend vitest: 11102 passed, 53 failed in 5 files, none caused by this change. 47 were `browser-profile-import.test.ts`, which failed identically on clean `main` because dependencies were installed with `--ignore-scripts`; all 55 pass once `better-sqlite3` is built. The other 6 passed when their files were rerun alone, and looked like load in the parallel run. The full suite was not rerun after that.
- Rendered the popover in Chromium and measured the action row in all nine languages: nothing overflows.

Share store tests ran against a temporary Postgres 17: `go test ./internal/postgres/ -run 'TestArtifactShare|TestRepublishingTheServedVersionQueuesNothing'` in `ao-control-plane` passes, including the assertion that an update keeps the link's slug. No control-plane code changed.

Republish itself has not been exercised end to end against a real control plane. Remote CI covers what could not run locally: the `checks` job (real-Electron boundaries, docs) and `renderer-smoke` passed on `179c19ed`.

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
