```
11:43:34.406 WARN  resume agent: relaunch failed sessionID=…-159 step="chat start"
  error="resume agent …: resume chat: chat conversation resume failed: configure ACP session:
  set ACP session mode \"dont_ask\": {\"code\":-32603,\"message\":\"Mode changes apply when
  the session is idle; try again after this turn.\"}"
→ POST /api/v1/sessions/…-159/resume-agent → 409 (repeated at 11:43:37 and 11:59:36, same error)
```

Meanwhile the underlying agent process **kept working and committed its result 30 minutes later** — the session was healthy mid-turn; only resume was broken.

### Root cause

The chat resume path unconditionally applies the session mode (`dont_ask`) as part of "configure ACP session" during resume. ACP forbids mode changes while a turn is in flight (`Mode changes apply when the session is idle; try again after this turn.`), so resume during an active turn can never succeed, and retry just hammers the same failure.

### Expected

Resume during an active turn should succeed: bind/reconnect to the running conversation and **defer the session-mode set until the session goes idle** (or apply it best-effort with a retry after the turn completes). A mode-set rejection must not fail the whole resume.

### Actual

Every resume attempt while a turn is active fails with 409 and the same `-32603` error; the user is told the conversation could not resume even though the agent is mid-turn and producing output.

### Environment

- Desktop app 0.14.9 (macOS 26.4.1), daemon `v0.14.9-nightly` build 202611040702
- Session kind: worker (chat mode, hermes harness / ACP)

title: fix(chat): render worker reports live in the orchestrator thread
body:
## Root cause

Worker report rows in an orchestrator chat thread were not materialized anywhere at `ao report` ingestion time. The `reports` table row (pending, `available_at` up to 1h away for checkpoint/informational reports) only became visible chat rows when the batch was later *delivered*:

1. Coordinator `RunDue` fires at `available_at` → `Submit` → `SendSemantic` → an automation message in the orchestrator conversation, which the renderer parses back into rows (`workerUpdatesOf` → `parseReports`), stamped with the delivery time. While the orchestrator is busy the batch is deferred (`OrchestratorBusyRetry`), and Chat can only accept it between turns.
2. The user sends the next message → `PreparePiggyback` claims ALL pending reports regardless of `available_at` → envelope folded into the human message → renderer `piggybackedUpdates` parses rows stamped with the user message time.

So an open thread stays frozen until the next user message (or until the coordinator gets a between-turns slot), and every row carries the flush time instead of the report's creation time. The renderer side (CDC → snapshot → `WorkerUpdateRows`) was already live and healthy; the daemon just never emitted a report-kind conversation row at ingestion.

## Fix

**Emission at the root, no polling.** New `ThreadRecorder` (`backend/internal/service/report/thread.go`), wired in `daemon.go` with the sqlite store. At report ingestion (`report.Service.Create`, synchronous like Artifacts) it:

1. finds the project's active **chat** orchestrator (same selection as the coordinator, plus chat mode),
2. resolves the worker's display name,
3. writes one `ao_action` activity row (action `worker.report`, operationId = report id, providerItemID `ao-action:worker.report:<id>`) into the orchestrator conversation via `ConversationForSession` + `UpsertActivity`.

The INSERT goes through the existing `conversation_activities` CDC trigger, so an open thread refetches and renders the row within ~1s. Recorder failures never fail the report itself, and ingestion is skipped cleanly when there is no active chat orchestrator or no conversation.

**Renderer parse + dedupe** (`WorkerUpdates.tsx`, `ChatWorkspace.tsx`):

- `worker.report` ao_action activities parse into `WorkerUpdate`s with `createdAt` = ingestion time = the report's true creation time. Body text is built exactly as `PreparedBatch.Render` does, so each text-parsed row (batch message or piggyback envelope) can be identified.
- Dedupe: `indexWorkerUpdates` collects identities (session + state + body) of ingestion rows; render sites drop text-parsed rows that already have a live row, and skip a delivery message whose entries are all threaded (its rows already exist above). Partial batches keep their unthreaded entries. Old transcripts without ingestion rows render exactly as before.
- Batches and piggybacked envelopes still inject into the agent's next turn unchanged — agent-turn injection (piggyback envelope, coordinator "Reports since your previous turn" `Submit`) is untouched.
- `runsOf` treats report activities as run boundaries so consecutive reports each render as their own quiet row instead of collapsing into an "N actions" summary.

## Tests

- `service/report`: recorder receives each created report; skips without chat orchestrator / without conversation; failure never fails the report.
- sqlite store: report thread row lands in the conversation projection and emits a `change_log` event.
- `WorkerUpdates`: parse + identity + dedupe. `ChatWorkspace`: live row renders, threaded envelope rows suppressed.

## Gates run locally

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./internal/service/report/... ./internal/storage/sqlite/...`
- `golangci-lint v2.13.2` on the touched packages (0 issues)
- frontend `typecheck` + vitest for `WorkerUpdates.test.ts` and `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` (248 tests passed)

BEFORE evidence: see the screenshot already attached to #7753. AFTER evidence (screencast + screenshots of a report landing live in an open orchestrator thread): https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7761#issuecomment-6636797794 AFTER evidence (live delivery in an open orchestrator thread) will follow in a comment on this PR.

Fixes #7753

title: fix(cli): find the Windows app where the installer puts it
body:
Code changes: +82 -28\
Tests: +87 -5\
Others: +0 -0

## What

`ao start` on Windows now finds the installed app in the folder the installer actually uses.

## Why

Follow-up from #7726. `ao start` looked for `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Agent Orchestrator\agent-orchestrator.exe`. The NSIS installer puts the app in `Programs\agent-orchestrator\`, so that lookup never matched.

- electron-builder names the folder after `win.executableName` when it is set (`AppInfo.productFilename`; `getWindowsInstallationDirName` in app-builder-lib 26.15.3). `forge.config.ts` has passed `EXECUTABLE_NAME = "agent-orchestrator"` since #2467 (2026-07-08). The lookup came from #2204 (2026-06-26) and was never updated. #7438 and #7578 changed display names only, not the folder.
- Both Windows assets on v0.14.9 (`agent-orchestrator-win32-x64.exe`, `Agent.Orchestrator.Setup.0.14.9.exe`) are the same file (same sha256), so they install to the same folder.
- On a real Windows 11 install (0.14.9 nightly), the registry `HKCU\Software\d06535a3-…\InstallLocation` is `…\Programs\agent-orchestrator`.

Who it hits: anyone with no `~/.ao/app-state.json` marker. That means a website install that was never opened, or a deleted or stale marker. They fall through to the scan, the scan misses, and `ao start` downloads the ~190 MB installer and runs it with `/S` over the existing install. It then checks the same wrong path and fails with `installed app not found`. A brand-new Windows user running `ao start` always gets that error after a successful install. Users whose app has written the marker are not affected, because the marker is checked first.

## Before / After

Same isolated run against the real installed app. `AO_DATA_DIR` and `AO_RUN_FILE` point at empty temp dirs, so there is no marker. `releaseRepo` is stamped to a repo that does not exist, so a fetch fails at download and nothing is reinstalled.

| Before (`main` at cf321a61eb) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- |
| `download https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/ao-start-probe-does-not-exist/releases/latest/download/agent-orchestrator-win32-x64.exe: unexpected status 404 Not Found` (exit 1): the scan missed the installed app and went to fetch | `{"resolved": true, "fetched": false, "opened": true, "appPath": "C:\Users\…\AppData\Local\Programs\agent-orchestrator\agent-orchestrator.exe"}` (exit 0) |

With the real release repo, "before" downloads and silently reinstalls, then errors with `ao start: installed app not found at …\Programs\Agent Orchestrator\agent-orchestrator.exe`.

## How

- `windowsAppLocations` lists the candidate folders in this order:
  1. The NSIS `InstallLocation` from the registry, HKCU then HKLM. The installer allows a custom folder, and this is the only way to find one.
  2. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\agent-orchestrator`.
  3. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Agent Orchestrator`: the folder from #403 to #2467, which the installer keeps on upgrade.
  4. The same two names under `%ProgramFiles%`. The old per-machine fallback also used the wrong name.
- `fetchAppWindows` looks for the exe after the silent install the same way, instead of checking one hardcoded path. The error lists every path it checked.
- The registry read is in `start_windows.go` (`golang.org/x/sys/windows/registry`, already a dependency), with a no-op `start_other.go`.
- Go can't import the TS constants, so `TestWindowsInstallNamesMatchForgeConfig` reads `frontend/forge.config.ts` and checks three things:
  - `windowsExeName` is `EXECUTABLE_NAME` plus `.exe`.
  - The first folder name is `EXECUTABLE_NAME`.
  - The registry key is `Software\` plus electron-builder's UUIDv5 of the NSIS `appId`.
  
  If someone renames either value in `forge.config.ts`, this test fails.
- macOS and Linux are unchanged. The macOS bundle stays `Agent Orchestrator.app` (PACKAGER_NAME / `build-mac-dmg.mjs` APP_NAME), and the DMG rename only changed the outer file name.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/cli -count=1`: ok (Windows 11).
- New tests:
  - `TestWindowsAppLocations` checks the order and that empty inputs are skipped.
  - `TestWindowsInstallNamesMatchForgeConfig` is the drift guard; it computes `d06535a3-65f7-5495-a483-b4bc9f28c80a` from `dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`, matching the real registry key.
  - `TestResolveApp_FindsWindowsInstallFolder` resolves with no marker. It is skipped on macOS, where a bundle is a directory.
- `go vet ./internal/cli` with GOOS=windows, linux, and darwin.
- Manual run before and after, as in the table above, against the real install.
- Not run locally: golangci-lint. The pinned v2.13.2 is built with go1.26 and refuses this go1.27 module, so CI is the check.
- Not tested: the real silent-reinstall path, so the user's installed app was not modified.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): resume succeeds while the agent turn is still active — defer the mid-turn ACP session-mode set
body:
## Root cause

Auto-resume of a chat-mode session whose agent turn is still running failed permanently. The ACP driver's resume path applies the session's turn settings as part of `configure ACP session`, which unconditionally issues `session/set_mode`. ACP forbids mode changes while a turn is in flight, so the harness answered:

```
set ACP session mode "dont_ask": {"code":-32603,"message":"Mode changes apply when the session is idle; try again after this turn."}
```

That error propagated as `ports.ErrChatResumeFailed` → resume-agent 409 on every retry (`resumeSession` in `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/driver.go`, `applyTurnSettings` in `conversation.go`), while the underlying agent process stayed alive and kept committing work.

## Fix

The driver now recognizes that specific busy rejection (`isACPModeBusyRejection`: JSON-RPC -32603 whose message reports mode changes need an idle session). Instead of failing the settings application:

- the desired mode (and the approval it maps to) is recorded as `pendingMode` on the conversation;
- the resume succeeds and binds/reconnects to the running conversation;
- when the session goes idle — the active turn releases in `finishPrompt` — a retry applies the pending mode; a repeated busy answer stays pending for the next idle transition, and any other failure is dropped there so the next turn's settings application reports it in context.

Permission bookkeeping follows the mode: while deferred, `permissionMode` keeps the value the agent is actually in, and is updated only when the deferred set lands.

## Test

`TestACPDriverResumeDuringActiveTurnDefersModeSet` (RED before the fix — it reproduced the exact incident error): a fake ACP agent rejects `session/set_mode` while a prompt is in flight; a second controller resumes the same provider session mid-turn, the resume succeeds, and the deferred mode lands on the agent once the session goes idle.

## Validation

- `go build ./...`
- `go vet ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp` and `go test -race` (full package, including the new test)
- `golangci-lint v2.13.2` on the package: 0 issues

Fixes #7760

title: fix(chat): render worker reports live in the orchestrator thread
body: ## Summary Worker report rows in an **orchestrator chat thread** only rendered when a batch was *delivered* — at the coordinator's `available_at` (deferred while the orchestrator was busy) or folded into the user's next message — so an open thread stayed frozen and every row carried the flush time instead of its true creation time (#7753). The root cause is emission, not rendering: nothing was written to the orchestrator conversation at `ao report` ingestion time. This PR: - **Daemon** — writes one `ao_action` timeline row per report at ingestion (`service/report/thread.go`) into the project's active Chat orchestrator conversation via `ConversationForSession` + `UpsertActivity`, through the same trigger-covered CDC path every other live timeline row uses, so an open thread renders the report within ~1s. Best effort by contract; the audience matches `PreparePiggyback` (terminated ends a thread, an exited agent does not). - **Renderer** — `workerUpdatesOf` parses `worker.report` ao_action rows into the same quiet worker rows a delivered batch draws, with the report's true creation time. Later delivered copies of an already-threaded report are dropped (batch message fully threaded ⇒ suppressed; partial batches keep their unthreaded entries; old transcripts without ingestion rows render exactly as before). Report activities break activity runs so consecutive reports stay one quiet row each instead of collapsing into an "N actions" summary. - **Unchanged** — the `Reports since your previous turn` agent-turn injection (piggyback envelope + coordinator `Submit`) is untouched; the agent still receives the same batch text at its next turn. Fixes #7753 ## Before / After Both sides run the real daemon + real Chat renderer against throwaway rigs (see "Evidence provenance"): the orchestrator chat is open and idle while two worker sessions finish and run `ao report`. | Behavior | Before (base `9d3cdf07e9`) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | --- | | Reports ingested while the thread is open and idle | | | | Row timestamps | Rows appear only after the next user message, all stamped with the flush time | Each row carries its true report time, as it lands | Screencasts and full stills: [evidence comment](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7765#issuecomment-6636602002) (hosted on the fork release [`demo-7753`](https://github.com/wesleymatosdev/agent-orchestrator/releases/tag/demo-7753)). ## Tests - `service/report`: recorder contract (row shape, note/message and information-state labeling, orchestrator audience incl. exited-but-open threads, best-effort failures never fail the report). - `storage/sqlite/store`: end-to-end — report ingestion lands the thread row in the conversation projection **and** fires the CDC `change_log` event the open thread invalidates on. - `WorkerUpdates.test.ts`: thread-row parsing, delivered-copy identity, dedupe. - `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: live row renders; threaded delivered batch is suppressed; unthreaded batches still draw. - Gates: `go build`, `go vet ./...`, `go test` on touched packages plus the service/sqlite/daemon/httpd/session_manager suites, `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 (0 issues), frontend `tsgo --noEmit` + full vitest. Local failures in unrelated packages (`shellterm` bash/fish, adapter auth/probe suites) were verified to reproduce on a clean `upstream/main` checkout. ## Evidence provenance The packaged desktop window is TCC-restricted for headless automation on this machine, so the captures use the app's real Chat renderer (`ChatWorkspace` and its WorkerUpdates rendering, unmodified) served by the branch's own Vite config against a real daemon built from this branch, with the rig creating the project, an orchestrator chat session (claude-code), and a worker that runs `ao report`. The `Reports since your previous turn` injection was separately exercised end-to-end in the base-run capture (a real orchestrator turn received the folded batch), and delivery injection is covered by the existing provisioning/coordinator suites. ## Risks / follow-ups - The thread row is display-only; report delivery scheduling, claiming, and acknowledgment are untouched. - Workers whose project has no Chat orchestrator (TUI orchestrator) get no thread row — unchanged behavior, delivery still injects at the next turn.

title: ci: native (macos-latest) job cancelled mid-run on first-time-contributor PRs — red ❌ with no failing step and admin-only rerun
body:
### What happened?

On external (first-time-contributor) PRs, the `native (macos-latest)` CI job gets **cancelled mid-run by the runner** — no failing step, no error output — while `native (ubuntu-latest)` and `native (windows-latest)` pass on the same commits. The job then shows as a red ❌ on the PR, and rerunning requires admin rights, which the PR author doesn't have.

### Occurrences today (2026-11-04, all `wesleymatosdev` PRs)

| PR | Job | Conclusion | Runtime | Failed steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #6634 (earlier head) | native (macos-latest) | cancelled by runner | — | none |
| #6634 (9d3cdf07e9 head) | [native (macos-latest)](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41856673408/job/126667072752) | cancelled | 17m04s | none |
| #7761 (4dadee42d7 head) | [native (macos-latest)](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/41865980318/job/126700157491) | cancelled | 21m01s | none |

In every case `gh api .../jobs/<id>` reports `conclusion: "cancelled"` with zero failed/cancelled steps, the job log is not retained, and `gh run rerun --failed` answers `Must have admin rights to Repository`.

### Impact

First-time contributors cannot green their macOS job: they can't rerun it, can't see why it died, and the PR shows failing CI through no fault of the change. Both PRs above are fully green otherwise (all ~20 other checks pass, including the ubuntu and windows native jobs).

### Expected

Either the macOS job completes (or cleanly fails with retained logs) on external PRs, or — if macOS runners are intentionally restricted/unavailable for first-time contributors — the job should be skipped with a visible reason instead of being cancelled into a red ❌, and/or the cancellation pattern documented in contributing docs.

### Environment

GitHub Actions, `native (macos-latest)` job of the repo's PR workflow, observed 2026-11-04.

title: fix(shell): keep the macOS titlebar strip as wide as the sidebar
body: Code changes: +22 -15\ Tests: +0 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What On macOS, the sidebar-colored drag strip behind the traffic lights is now exactly as wide as the sidebar. It no longer paints over the center panel's top-left corner and border. ## Why The strip measured the sidebar once, on the first animation frame after `ShellLayout` mounted. During startup the shell renders `DaemonStartupLoader` instead of the sidebar, so that query found no `[data-slot="sidebar-container"]`, returned, and never ran again (its only dependency, `sidebarHasLayout`, does not change). The strip then fell back to `w-(--ao-sidebar-w, var(--size-sidebar-default))`. `--ao-sidebar-w` never reaches the strip either: `useResizable` writes it in the sidebar's layout effect, before React attaches the later-sibling strip's ref. So the strip and its fill were 240px beside a narrower saved sidebar. Native fullscreen collapses the strip to `h-0`. The overhang therefore became visible when the window left fullscreen and the strip grew back to 50px, which is how it was reported. ## Before / After Measured in the real Electron dev window (CSS px, zoom 1.095, saved sidebar width 234px), after a cold renderer reload and after leaving native fullscreen: | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Sidebar right edge | 233.99 | 233.99 | | Drag strip right edge | 240 | 233.99 | | Strip fill (`bg-sidebar`) right edge | 240 | 233.99 | | Center panel surface left edge | 233.99 | 233.99 | | Hit test at (238, 30) | drag strip | center panel surface | Before: a sidebar-colored notch covers the top-left corner of the center panel down to the bottom of the traffic-light band. After: the panel's rounded corner and left border run unbroken up to the top inset. The dev window is translucent, and CDP captures of it come out flat gray, so the table above stands in for screenshots. ## How - Moved the measuring effect below `isStartupLoading` and added it to the gate and the dependencies. It now re-arms when the loader gives way to the shell, and again after any later reconnect that remounts the sidebar. - The strip's inner fill gets the same measured width as an inline style. The fill is absolutely positioned and overflows the strip, so a var fallback wider than the sidebar would still cover the panel even with the outer strip measured correctly. It keeps the last measured width while the sidebar is collapsed, so the fill still slides out at full width. - Not changed: `useResizable` still writes `--ao-sidebar-w` before the strip's ref exists. With the measured width on both elements, the strip no longer depends on that var. ## Testing - Real Electron dev app (isolated `~/.ao/dev` data), driven over CDP and the main-process inspector: cold renderer reload, then `setFullScreen(true)` and `setFullScreen(false)`, measuring the strip, fill, sidebar and panel each time (table above). - `vitest run src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/renderer/hooks/useSidebarChromeGeometry.test.tsx src/renderer/components/TitlebarNav* src/renderer/test/shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx src/renderer/__tests__/_shell-create-project-config.test.tsx`: 269 passed. - `tsgo --noEmit`: clean. - No regression test: jsdom computes no layout, so a unit test would only re-state the ResizeObserver mock. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(chat): offer a login when a turn fails on a refused login
body: Code changes: +565 -50\ Tests: +591 -0\ Others: +184 -1 (generated OpenAPI spec and TS types, 9 locale catalogs, CSS for the band) ## What When a chat message fails because the agent's login was refused, the chat no longer shows the CLI's own advice ("Not logged in · Please run /login"). The login moves onto the chat box. A band slides up from behind the composer and sits on top of it: "Claude Code is signed out · your message sends once you're in" and a **Log in** button. The composer keeps its exact place and look. Typing is locked, because the agent would refuse anything new the same way, but nothing on the box changes: it still reads "Message the agent", and its tools and the agent and model picker stay usable. Under the refused message's bubble its own row reads "⌛ Queued", then its time and copy button, on one line. **Log in** opens the Harness page on that agent's login, on the session's own host. The band then follows the login through: 1. If you come back without logging in, it says "Finish logging in on the Harness page · your message is waiting", with **Open again** and **Send again** (for a login finished somewhere else). 2. When the login takes there, settings closes and the band says "Logged in to Claude Code · sending your message". 3. The queued message runs. The band goes away, the composer unlocks, and the message shows once: the retry's copy is that message, so the refused original is not drawn beside it. If sending it again fails, the band says why, with **Send again**. Switching the chat to another agent also ends the refusal and unlocks the composer. So does a login fixed outside the app (a terminal, a refreshed token): once the daemon confirms it, the band says "Logged in to Claude Code · send your message again" with **Send again**. The message is only sent again by itself when it ran no tool and changed nothing. Otherwise the band and the line ask you to send it again. ## Why `/login` is a command for the Claude Code terminal UI. In Chat there is nowhere to type it, so a signed-out user saw a red "The agent ran into a problem" with a mono block telling them to run a command they can't run. The fix already existed one click away (the Harness page can start the login), but nothing on the failed turn led there. The daemon already knew what happened: claude-agent-acp reports this case as a typed `auth_required` session failure with a `login` action, and `claudePromptResponseFailure` maps it to `ErrChatAuthRequired`. The turn just didn't carry that fact to the renderer. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Red "The agent ran into a problem", the raw `Not logged in · Please run /login` in a mono block, Retry / undo under it, and a separate "Log in again" banner at the top | The message's row under its bubble reads "⌛ Queued", its time and copy, on one line. The login is a band that slides up onto the composer: Claude Code's mark, "Claude Code is signed out · your message sends once you're in", **Log in**. Typing is locked until the login takes or the chat switches agent, and the composer looks just as before. No CLI text, no failure card, no banner | | Logging in meant finding Settings → Harness yourself, then coming back and pressing Retry | **Log in** opens the Harness page with the login already started. A login that takes closes settings, and the band shows it signing in and sending the message again | | A message that ran commands before failing | Same band, worded "send your message again once you're in". It is never sent again automatically | ## How - **One failure code for every agent.** `ChatEventTurnCompleted` with `ErrChatAuthRequired` (and no driver-specific code) now settles the turn with `failureCode: "auth_required"` in the chat controller. Every driver already reports a refused login with that sentinel (Claude via the typed session failure, Codex, Pi, AGY, native ACP), so this is the one place to set it. No new text matching on provider messages. - **Band on the chat box.** `ChatComposer` gets a `trayBand` slot, drawn in `.chat-composer-band-tray` above the composer: the mirror of the New Chat tray hung under it. It is narrower than the composer and stops at its edge instead of going under it, so the composer keeps its place and its own fill (a see-through window's composer is itself a wash, so anything behind it would show). Dark gets a 9% wash, because its composer is only a little lighter than the canvas; light keeps 5%. `ChatLoginBand` draws five states (signed out, waiting, sending, logged in, send failed) with the agent's `AgentAvatar`, one sentence, and its action (waiting has two: **Open again** and **Send again**). On a narrow chat the actions move under the sentence instead of squeezing it. - **The band slides; nothing else moves.** `ComposerBand` (in `ChatComposer`) wraps the slot in `AnimatePresence`. The band slides up out from behind the composer (150 ms, `--duration-normal`, ease-out) and back down behind it (150 ms, ease-in) by transform alone: its space is taken at once and clipped at the composer's edge, so nothing else is laid out again while it moves. Reduced motion makes it instant. - **Typing locked while signed out.** While the band says signed out or waiting, `ChatComposer` gets `typingLocked`: the editor is `readOnly` (no input, no submit, no history recall), but nothing is restyled. The placeholder, opacity, attachments and mic stay as they are; disabling the box instead dimmed and re-worded it, which read as a blink. The turn settings bar (agent, model, effort, approvals) has its own enabled state, so it stays usable. A `provider_switch` after the refused message ends the refusal, so switching agent unlocks the chat. It also unlocks once the daemon confirms the session's login after the refusal (`account.authenticationState` back to `authenticated`, verified after the refused turn), however the login came back. The lock only holds while the message can be sent again, and the waiting band offers **Send again**, so it always has a way out. - **Status on the message.** A refused message whose turn did nothing else gets a `status` on `HumanMessage`. `LoginStatusNote` then leads the message's own row under the bubble, and the time and actions follow it in view on the same line: "⌛ Queued", "Waiting for login", "Sending…" or "Not sent". The row stays in the flow, so nothing floats over it. The hourglass stays still, and the turn draws no "Worked for" row. A turn that did work ends on "Stopped · send it again once you're in" as its outcome instead. The provider's text is not rendered: it is CLI advice and means nothing in Chat (it is still stored on the turn). The DeepSeek missing-key card is unchanged. - **One place that follows the login.** `useChatLogin` in `ChatWorkspace` picks the latest refused message that hasn't been retried yet. It feeds the band and every refused message's line, and it sends the message again. - A `loginReturn` entry in `ui-store`, keyed by session, remembers the login while the Harness page is open. - Log in records the account the session runs on: it reads `GET /api/v1/agents/accounts/sessions/{sessionId}` once, as the Harness page opens, and stores it on the waiting login (`setLoginReturnAccount`). It is not a query hook, so the chat still renders without a query client. A login brings the chat back only when it is that account: `AgentAccountsPanel` passes the account a saved-account sign-in completed, and `LocalHarnessContent` passes the computer's own account when a CLI login terminal, or main's inline `HarnessLoginPanel` sign-in (#7163), is verified. A remote host's accounts are not readable from here, so there it matches agent and host. A match closes global settings. - The chat then sends the message again through the existing retry, but only when all of these hold: the turn is still retryable, nothing else is running, the login took within the last minute, and the turn has no `command` / `file_change` / `mcp_tool` / `ao_action` activity and no diff. - The login stays marked done until the message's copy appears. From the moment the chat sends the message again, the band says it is sending (a local flag until the retry reports pending), so it never offers **Send again** for a message on its way. If the retry is refused (`retryControl.error`), the band shows the reason with **Send again**, instead of falling back to "signed out". - Otherwise `settleLoginReturn` keeps "Logged in" on the band until a new message is sent. - **One message, not two.** `hiddenTimelineTurnIds` now also skips an `auth_required` failure once a turn retries it (and that retry isn't rolled back). The retry's copy is that message, so the timeline and the up-arrow history show it once. - **Only the latest refused message is offered.** Earlier refused ones read "Not sent". A refusal the conversation has moved past (a later turn, or a switch to another agent) drops the wait, and nothing is sent. - **Banner dedupe and return.** `ReauthBanner` hides while the band shows. When it does show (a login that lapsed without a refused message), its **Log in again** now starts the same login as the band, so a login that takes brings the user back to the chat; with nothing refused, nothing is sent. The wait is dropped once the login takes, or when settings close without one, so a later refusal starts signed out. - **Copy** is in all nine catalogs. The Harness page is named from the app's own `settings.harness` label. **Intentional omission:** cloud sessions get the band and open the cloud view of the Harness page, but nothing sends the message again automatically: `CloudHarnessContent` reports no login completion today. The band says "send your message again once you're in" there. ## Testing After merging main (`8bf3684709`), with the second review's fixes: - **Type-check:** frontend `tsgo --noEmit` is clean. - **vitest** (`--maxWorkers=2`): the 11 chat files around the login (`ChatWorkspace*`, `ChatComposer`, `ChatTimelineItems`, `ChatStatusBanners`) plus `HarnessSettingsSection` and `AgentAccountsSection`: 794 passed. - **Go:** `go build ./...` passes; `go vet` and `go test` pass for `service/chat` (incl. `TestRefusedLoginTurnCarriesAuthRequiredCode`) and `authprobe`. - **New tests in `ChatWorkspaceLogin.test.tsx`:** - the chat opens once the daemon confirms the login after the refusal (a confirmation from before it doesn't count), and the band offers **Send again**; - the waiting band offers **Send again**; - typing stays open when nothing could send the message again; - the band stays on sending, with no **Send again**, while the retry hasn't reported pending; - a banner-started wait is dropped when settings close without a login; - no "Worked for" row under the refused message. Undoing any one of these six fixes fails exactly one test. - **Screenshots** (renderer in Chrome, stubbed snapshot) of signed out, waiting and daemon-confirmed, dark and light, 1100 and 430 px wide. At 430 px the waiting band's two buttons first squeezed the sentence into a narrow column. Its actions now move under the sentence; signed out stays on one line. Earlier runs, on the branch after merging main (`6ecafb3150`), with the first review's fixes: - **Go** (unchanged since the first commit): - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass. - `golangci-lint run` (v2.13.2) reports 0 issues. - The new `TestRefusedLoginTurnCarriesAuthRequiredCode` checks that the adapter's exact title gets the code and an ordinary failure gets none. - **`npm run api`:** the spec and `schema.ts` each gained only the new enum value. - **Type-check:** frontend `tsgo --noEmit` and `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.e2e.json` are clean. - **`vitest run src/renderer`** (the whole renderer): 8716 passed, 6 skipped. 9 tests in 7 files timed out while the machine's load average was ~17; all 7 files pass alone (471 tests). - **Go:** `go build ./...` passes; `go test` for `service/chat` and `chatdriver/claudeacp` passes (`TestPublishRenderStopsWaitingForAMeasureAtTheTimeout` timed out once under load and passes 3/3 alone). - **New `ChatWorkspaceLogin.test.tsx`** covers: - the band and the queued status replace the CLI advice, the failure card, the retry row and the banner; - the status leads the message's own row, with its time and copy button; - Log in opens the Harness page with `startLogin`, and coming back shows the waiting band and status; - a login that takes closes settings and sends the message again, once; - a turn that ran commands is not sent again, and the band says the user is in; - the remote-host variant only completes on that host's login for that agent; - only the latest refused message is offered, and earlier ones read "Not sent"; - once the message is sent again, the band goes and the message shows once (the copy's); - typing is locked while signed out, without restyling the box (same placeholder, not dimmed), and opens again once the login takes; - a switch to another agent ends the refusal and unlocks the composer, also while the band is showing (it slides away); - a refused re-send shows the reason and **Send again**; - only the session's own account's login brings it back; - a conversation that moved on drops the wait and sends nothing; - the banner's **Log in again** brings the user back too, sending nothing. Removing the re-send fails 2 of these tests, and so does dropping the latest-only rule. Drawing the original again, moving the status out of the message, dropping the lock, or ignoring an agent switch fails 1 each. - **Settings tests:** - `HarnessSettingsSection` covers both the terminal login and main's inline sign-in signalling the waiting chat. The inline test fails without the hook. - Both also cover a login for another account leaving the chat waiting. - `AgentAccountsSection` covers the saved-account sign-in, for the session's account and for another one. - **Renderer smoke** (`--grep "@T0|@P0"` over `e2e/chat-*`, Chrome, before the merge): 42/44. - `chat-continue.spec.ts:87` hit its 5 s first-load wait on a cold dev server, and passes 2/2 alone. - `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts:139` fails on this machine without this change too. - **Spacing:** with main merged, the gap under a sent message before the next row is main's 48px again (it was 10px on the old base, where the hover time and copy covered the next card). - **Composer stays put:** the composer's position, size, fill and edge are identical with and without the band, in dark and light at 1100, 700 and 430 px wide. With the composer locked, the agent picker still opens. - **Animation, frame by frame** (rAF log while the band comes and goes): the composer's rect, its field's opacity and its fill never change. The band slid over 15 frames in and 12 out at the earlier 0.26 s / 0.2 s timing (now 150 ms both ways), and its clip height stays fixed throughout, so there is no layout work per frame. - **Screenshots** come from the renderer in Chrome with a stubbed conversation snapshot (no daemon). The log-in-and-send-again flow was tried once in the desktop app before this revision: the message re-ran after the login. That run is how the duplicate message and the covered status line were found. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Chat displays sign-in prompts and message-delivery status, with relevant login and resend actions. * Eligible local messages that did no work can retry automatically after a matching sign-in; other messages can be resent manually. Cloud chats require manual resend. * Completing a matching sign-in returns you to the chat. * Login guidance and message statuses are available in all supported languages. * Typing and message retries are locked while sign-in is pending; other composer tools remain available. * **Bug Fixes** * Authentication failures are distinguished from other provider errors and display clearer status in chat.

title: [Feature]: All-projects board across hosts (desktop and mobile)
body:
### Problem

I run AO on one always-on Linux host with several projects registered, and I check on it from the desktop app on another machine and from the phone. To see what needs me, I have to open each project's board one at a time. There's no single view of all workers across projects in the board lanes (Working / Needs you / In review / Ready to merge).

- Desktop: the board routes are `/projects/$projectId` and `/host/$hostId/project/$projectId`, both project-scoped. `SessionsBoard` already has a `projectId ?? "all"` branch, but no route reaches it, and it only covers the local host.
- Mobile: the Fleet tab already merges sessions across hosts and projects with an "all projects" filter, but it's a list, not the lane board.

### Proposed direction

An "All projects" board:

- Desktop: a sidebar entry and route (e.g. `/board`) that renders the board for every project on every connected host, local and remote.
- Each card shows its project (and host, when more than one is connected).
- Same lanes, ordering, and card actions as the per-project board. Project-only controls (orchestrator, spawn) either ask for a project or are hidden.
- Mobile: a board layout for the Fleet tab, or an "all projects" option on the board, reusing the same lane derivation.

### Alternatives considered

- Registering a parent folder with `--as-workspace` to get one board. Only works when the repos share a parent folder, and it changes how the projects are set up.
- Living with per-project boards plus "Needs you" push notifications. Workable, but slow to scan once there are more than two or three projects.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(windows): pin ao from the data-directory shim so sandboxes can run it
body:
Code changes: +139 -18
Tests: +361 -17
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Fixes #7171. On Windows, an AO-spawned Codex session could not run `ao`: `ao status` reported `CommandNotFoundException`, `Test-Path` on the installed `ao.exe` reported `ItemExistsUnauthorizedAccessError`, and the session had no way to spawn workers or report back.

Root cause is an ACL mismatch, not PATH injection and not a missing CLI. Codex's Windows sandbox runs agent shell commands as a separate provisioned local identity. That identity inherits read/execute on the user profile, but `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` carries an explicit owner-only DACL, and the AO desktop installer is per-user (`perMachine: false`), so it installs exactly there. `pinDirectory` pinned that install directory — which holds only `ao.exe`, so the shim branch never ran — and `ao` therefore resolved to a path the sandbox could not read.

Reproduced inside `codex sandbox powershell` with AO's own `PinnedDir` value on PATH (Codex CLI 0.166.0, Windows 11 26200):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `ao status` | `CommandNotFoundException` |
| `Test-Path ...\resources\daemon\ao.exe` | `UnauthorizedAccessException: Access is denied` |
| `& "...\resources\daemon\ao.exe" --version` | `CommandNotFoundException` |
| same binary copied to `%TEMP%` | `ao version dev` |

ACL chain behind it:

| Path | ACE for the Codex sandbox group |
| --- | --- |
| `%USERPROFILE%`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `%TEMP%`, `~/.ao` | present (inherited) |
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` | absent — inheritance blocked here |
| `...\Programs\<product>\resources\daemon` | only `SYSTEM`, `Administrators`, the installing user |

macOS and Linux sandboxes permit those reads, which is why this is Windows-only. AO's own hook delivery was unaffected: Codex spawns hooks itself, not through the sandbox.

## Before / After

Screenshots of an actual Windows console window running `codex sandbox powershell`, captured from that window with `PrintWindow`. Both sides are builds of this repository — `main` at `6eb2469b0d` and this branch at `3bc412d49c` — and `whoami` shows the sandbox identity `yash\codexsandboxoffline` on both sides, so the only variable is which directory `ao` is pinned from.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: ao is not recognized and the install path is denied](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/290c24d49a97a279795e82591a60eff1e6370eb7/docs/screenshots/pr-7771/before.png) | ![After: where.exe ao finds the shim and ao status runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/290c24d49a97a279795e82591a60eff1e6370eb7/docs/screenshots/pr-7771/after.png) |

The `icacls` line in the first shot is the root cause: the sandbox identity gets `Access is denied` on the install directory, so `ao` is not on PATH and `Test-Path` fails the same way. In the second shot the shim inherits `YASH\CodexSandboxUsers:(M)`, `where.exe ao` resolves to it, and `ao --version` and `ao status` both run.

The per-user install DACL is reproduced with a fixture directory (inheritance removed; only `Administrators`, `SYSTEM`, and the installing user allowed), matching `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`.

The capture scripts, harness, and unedited transcript are not committed — `.agents/skills/pr-description/SKILL.md` says never to commit screenshots or recordings — but remain readable in the branch history at [`290c24d49a`](https://github.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/tree/290c24d49a97a279795e82591a60eff1e6370eb7/docs/screenshots/pr-7771). No daemon was started for the capture, so `ao status` reports `stopped`; that still requires the CLI to execute and resolve its data directory, which the "before" side cannot do at all.

## Change

- `pinDirectory` now prefers the data-directory shim on Windows even when the install directory holds no sibling executables, so the pinned directory inherits the profile's ACLs. Validated inside the same sandbox: the shim's `ao.exe` answers `ao --version` and `ao status`.
- The shim's `ao.exe` is copied instead of hard-linked. A hard link shares its target's security descriptor, so linking would have kept the install directory's ACLs and reproduced the identical denial (verified: a hard link created in `%USERPROFILE%` still showed the install file's DACL).
- `ao.cmd` lets cmd resolve the shim directory itself — `%~dp0`, falling back to `%~dp$PATH:0` when a quoted `"ao.cmd"` is resolved from PATH — for callers that resolve the batch sibling (Git Bash, `call ao`). cmd parses a batch file in the console's OEM code page, so the earlier embedded UTF-8 path broke under a non-ASCII data directory; resolving the directory from the file's own location at run time avoids the encoding entirely.
- If no shim can be produced (relative/empty data directory, unreadable executable), the pin falls back to the install directory rather than disappearing, because losing the pin breaks `ao hooks` callbacks. The fallback logs a warning so the regression is diagnosable. Shared installs keep the hard failure: pinning them directly would promote `node`/`git` ahead of the agent's runtime.
- Refreshing the shim replaces its `ao.exe` in place first, so the common app-update path never leaves a moment where the shim directory has no `ao.exe`. Windows denies replacing a running image (an in-session `ao mcp`, for example), so that case renames the old copy aside and renames the fresh one in; renamed-aside copies are removed best-effort on later passes once their process exits. Both moves retry briefly on sharing violations, which covers an antivirus scanner holding the freshly written copy, instead of dropping the pin back to the unreadable install directory.
- A leftover shim from an older build can be a hard link with byte-identical metadata; the freshness check now also rules out `os.SameFile`, so it is copied through and stops carrying the install directory's ACLs.

## Tests

- `TestWindowsPerUserInstallPinsShimDirectory` (new): a single-executable install directory pins below `<data>/runtime/ao-path`, the shim runs standalone, and `ao.cmd` does not reference the install directory.
- `TestWindowsAOPathShimCopiesExecutable` (rewritten from the cross-volume link test): asserts the shim is a copy rather than a hard link, that it preserves the source modtime so repeat launches reuse it, and that Git Bash resolves `ao` to the shim.
- `TestSharedWindowsInstallSelectsOnlyCanonicalAO`: identity is now compared by content instead of `os.SameFile`, since the pinned binary is a copy.
- `TestWindowsAOCmdRunsWhenInvokedQuoted` (new, review follow-up): executes `ao.cmd` bare and as `cmd /d /s /c ""ao.cmd" ...`, with the shim on PATH and a foreign working directory, from both an ASCII and a non-ASCII (`José dätä`) data directory. Against the `%~dp0` revision the quoted leg fails with the reported `<cwd>\ao.exe is not recognized`; against the embedded UTF-8 path the non-ASCII leg fails on a CP437 console.
- `TestWindowsShimRefreshesWhileRunning` (new, review follow-up): holds a shim `ao.exe` running across an install update, asserts the refresh succeeds and the renamed-aside copy disappears after exit; fails against remove-in-place with `Access is denied`. It waits for the child with a timeout and kills it from `t.Cleanup`, so an early failure no longer leaves it blocked on stdin or blocks the temp-directory cleanup.
- `TestWindowsShimRefreshesIdleCopy` (new, review follow-up): updates the install executable with nothing holding the shim, asserts the copy is replaced byte-for-byte, and that no renamed-aside file is left behind.
- `TestWindowsShimReplacesHardLinkedCopy` (new, review follow-up): a hard-linked shim with identical metadata is replaced by a real copy.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint v2.13.2 run ./internal/agentlaunch/...` (0 issues), `gofmt` clean, and `GOOS=linux`/`GOOS=darwin go vet ./internal/agentlaunch/` for the new build-tagged sharing-violation check.
- `go test ./internal/agentlaunch/` at `b88f0f280f`: the Windows shim tests pass, including `ao.cmd` run from a CP437 console with a non-ASCII data directory. The two tests that shell out to `bash` fail on this machine only because `bash` resolves to the WSL launcher with no distribution installed; `windows-workspace` covers them.
- Full `go test ./...` at `290c24d49a` compared against pristine `canonical/main` (`f7c1092a3c`): 274 vs 273 failing tests, and none of the difference reproduces — the three head-only names (`TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination`, `TestLastInputAtReadsWithoutBlockingInput`, `TestOpenCodeDiscoveryRunsAgainstRealBinary`) pass 3/3 in isolation, and two other tests failed only at base. The failures present on both sides are pre-existing Windows/environment gaps in this checkout (POSIX `/tmp` fixtures, POSIX permission-mode assertions, missing `kimi`/Git Bash/WSL setups), not related to this change.
- All 29 CI checks passed on `290c24d49a` (this branch merged with `main` at `32fd8d243f`), including `windows-workspace` (the Windows job that exercises `./internal/agentlaunch/`), which is gated behind the `ci:full` label that this PR carries. One `frontend / renderer-smoke (2)` shard hit an unrelated pixel-equality flake in `window-transparency-overlap.spec.ts` and passed on rerun; `internal/agentlaunch` passed in both runs.
- End-to-end sandbox check described above, using Codex's own `codex sandbox` runner with the exact PATH AO now produces.

Not verified locally: a full AO→Codex spawn (no Codex credentials on this machine: `codex exec` → 401, `codex doctor` → no credentials). CI and a credentialed run should confirm the session-level behavior.

title: fix(desktop): match the startup loader to the shell background
body:
With window transparency on, the startup loader showed the bare vibrancy blur and skipped the shell's 70% sidebar tint, so in dark mode it looked lighter than the app once the shell rendered. The loader now paints the same background as the shell, so the handoff from loader to app has no visible shift.

- **Transparency on:** the loader paints the same tint as the shell plate. Both use one shared `--ao-shell-tint` variable.
- **Transparency off:** the loader paints `bg-sidebar` (the shell plate and native window colour) instead of the center-panel colour, so the window frame no longer shifts at handoff.
- **Theme before first paint:** `apply-initial-theme.ts` sends the theme preference to main before first paint. The vibrancy material follows `nativeTheme`, and the shell only sent it after the loader. Before this, a light app on a dark Mac showed its loader over a dark material.

Main-process code is unchanged, so the Dock-reopen vibrancy fix from #6729 is untouched.

## Screenshots

Cold start of the desktop app, dark theme, window transparency on, same isolated profile. Captured from the native window so the vibrancy shows.

Added `apply-initial-theme.test.ts` to cover the early theme handoff.

title: [Bug]: Project setup fails at "Create remote repository" when gh and git use different GitHub accounts
body:
### What went wrong?

## What happens
When I add a local folder as a project and choose to create a new GitHub repository, AO creates the repository but can't push the initial commit if `gh` and `git` are logged in as different GitHub accounts. Setup stops with this banner:

> ~/ao-repro-push failed while running Create remote repository. Review the step below, then retry or go back.

The step itself only says "Needs attention".

This leaves setup half finished:
- The private repository exists on GitHub, but it's empty.
- `origin` is set locally, and the initial commit exists only on my machine.
- Sending the same request as Retry fails with the same error.
- Creating the repository by hand fails with "already exists", because AO has already created it.

## Expected behaviour
Setup should push the initial commit to the repository it just created. If the push can't succeed, AO should show the reason.

## Error
The UI doesn't show this message. I got it by sending the same request as Retry to `POST /api/v1/imports/prepare-git`:

```text
push initial commit: git -C ~/ao-repro-push push -u origin HEAD:
exit status 128: remote: Repository not found.
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/<gh-account>/ao-repro-push.git/' not found
```

## Steps to reproduce
You need two GitHub accounts: `gh` active on one, and a keychain credential for `github.com` belonging to the other.

1. Check that the two logins differ:
   ```bash
   gh api user --jq .login
   printf 'protocol=https\nhost=github.com\n\n' | git credential fill | grep '^username='
   ```
   If you've run `gh auth setup-git`, both will match. Add `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` before `git credential fill` to check the keychain login instead, and use it in step 3 too.

2. Create a test folder:
   ```bash
   mkdir ~/ao-repro-push && echo "repro" > ~/ao-repro-push/README.md
   ```

3. Start AO from `frontend/`:
   ```bash
   env -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_RUN_FILE -u AO_PORT GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null npm run dev
   ```

4. Add `~/ao-repro-push` as a project and create a new private GitHub repository, with the `gh` account as owner.

5. Setup fails at "Create remote repository".

6. Check the result:
   ```bash
   gh repo view <gh-account>/ao-repro-push --json nameWithOwner,visibility,isEmpty
   ```
   The repository exists, is private, and `isEmpty` is `true`.

## What I found
A dry-run push from the same folder to the same repository gave different results depending only on the login:

| `git` login | Result of `git push --dry-run -u origin HEAD` |
| --- | --- |
| Keychain account (not the repository owner) | `Repository not found`, exit 128 |
| `gh` account (through `gh auth git-credential`) | Would create `main`, exit 0 |

Control: with `git` using the `gh` account, the same `prepare-git` request on the same folder succeeded with no code changes, and the commit reached GitHub. I sent this request directly to the API, because the form blocked me from continuing (see Related problems).

So I think the cause is that `runGitPreparationAction` in `backend/internal/service/importer/importer.go` creates the repository with `gh repo create`, then runs a plain `git push`, which uses whatever login `git` has configured. GitHub normally reports a private repository as "not found" to an account without access, which makes the error misleading.

Workaround: running `gh auth setup-git` made the push work, but it changes how `git` logs in to GitHub for every repository, and nothing in AO points users to it.

## Possible fix
Draft PR #7582 looks like it would fix this for new repositories, because it creates the repository and pushes with AO's own GitHub sign-in. I haven't tested that branch. I'm filing this so the failure is on record until that PR lands. Is there anything here you'd like me to help with, such as testing the scenario on that branch?

## Related problems
I can file these separately if you'd like:
- **The real error is hidden:** the daemon returns it in `event.error`, but `CreateProjectFlow.tsx` only shows "Needs attention", even though the banner says to review the step.
- **Retry can't recover a missing repository:** if the repository is deleted after `origin` is set, Retry skips `gh repo create` and the push keeps failing.
- **Setup can't be resumed after reopening:** if AO is closed after this failure, adding the folder again requires the create-remote step, but the form reports the repository name as unavailable and disables Continue. The repository only exists because AO's failed attempt created it.

## Environment
- AO: run from source, `agent-orchestrator@0.14.8`, `main` at `a1fe965e70`
- OS: macOS 27.0 (Apple silicon)
- Git credentials: `osxkeychain` by default, with `gh` logged in to three accounts

title: fix(claude): discover models with the default saved account
body:
Code changes: +60 -11  
Tests: +260 -8  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Discover Claude models with the saved account that AO would use for a new task, including that account's scoped macOS Keychain credentials.

## Why

Claude can report a saved account as signed in while the model picker fails with `no credential could be resolved for this provider`. Model discovery used the computer's login instead of the saved account, and the Keychain resolver only checked unscoped service names. A valid computer login could hide the bug until that login or the model-cache fingerprint changed.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: New Task cannot resolve Claude credentials](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ca559bb-5bb9-494b-89f6-d1ef6138a8f1) | ![After: isolated app loads Claude Opus 5.5 without the credential warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3b7c462-529f-438c-a2e1-a595356aa556) |
| Saved Claude accounts are signed in, but an absent computer login leaves the model catalog unavailable. | Model discovery uses the account selected by the new-task account selector. |
| A scoped account lookup checks the computer's unscoped Keychain service. | It reads the service derived from the exact account config path and keeps credentials isolated between accounts. |
| Startup warms model catalogs before saved-account callbacks are wired. | Account callbacks are available before model warmup starts. |

Screenshots: **Before** is the original user capture from the installed app. **After** is the isolated development app with the original discovery fix. The captures use different window sizes and data.

## How

- Reuse the existing new-task account selection and fallback rules through `DefaultLaunchEnv`, without binding a session.
- Carry the saved account environment into both model discovery and credential fingerprinting; cloud credential scopes keep their own context.
- Resolve Claude's Keychain service suffix from the exact secure-storage/config path, including explicit config overrides.
- Start model warmup after wiring account callbacks.
- Treat unavailable saved accounts as a sign-in state: preserve cached models or manual entry, store an idle auth warning, and keep unexpected lookup errors visible.

## Testing

Passed locally:

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and formatting checks.
- Full `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 run: zero issues.
- Full race suites for `internal/service/agent`, `internal/service/agentaccounts`, `pkg/agentcreds`, `internal/adapters/agent/claudecode`, and `internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog`, with an isolated test HOME/PATH.
- Regression cases failed before the review fix and passed afterward: queued saved catalog, uncached revalidation, and first picker read. They assert retained models/manual entry, the persisted auth-required warning, idle refresh state, and no retry budget; unrelated account lookup errors still propagate.

Isolated validation of the original discovery fix:

- Red case: the device login was signed out while saved Team and Max accounts were valid; the baseline picker reported that no credential could be resolved.
- Fixed case: saved Team and Max model discovery returned 13 and 14 models respectively, and the native New Task picker loaded without that warning. A disposable ACP fixture chat also completed. The existing-session dropdown was not automated because the native driver refused to raise its background popup.
- The installed app's later recovery coincided with its device Max sign-in becoming available; it retained its original daemon and did not run this patch.

Full Linux race, CLI E2E, fresh-install, generated-file drift, boundary, and secret checks are tracked in [PR CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7774/checks). Docker is unavailable locally. Earlier broad native runs did not complete cleanly because of inherited AO context and a disappearing Go toolchain; the current affected suites passed after isolating the environment and restoring the toolchain.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (rebased onto current `main`)
- [x] One focused change; related issue is the user report in AO
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After compares observable backend behavior
- [x] Regression tests cover default-account changes, scoped credential lookup, missing credentials, cloud isolation, and model fingerprints
- [x] Local validation results and remaining CI coverage are documented

title: bug(chat): ACP turns that end on a failing stop reason store no error message
body:
## Bug

When an ACP agent ends a turn on `max_tokens`, `max_turn_requests`, `refusal` or an unknown stop reason, AO settles the turn as `failed` with an empty `error_message`. The timeline then shows a bare "The agent ran into a problem" with no cause.

**Status:** found by reading the code. It has not been seen with a real agent yet.

## Cause

In `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go`:

- `turnState` maps every stop reason other than `end_turn` and `cancelled` to `failed`.
- `finishPrompt` only attaches an error when a provider binding's prompt-failure hook returns one. With no binding error, the failed completion has none.
- The turn-completed event is the only event that sets `conversation_turns.error_message`, so the turn is stored with no reason.

## Fix

Give the failed completion a reason derived from the stop reason, for example "The agent reached its output token limit", with `Stop reason: <reason>` as the detail. Leave the detail out when the reason is empty.

## Before fixing

Reproduce it first with a real agent ending on one of these stop reasons. This gap was split out of #5289 and PR #7589, which could not show it happening for real.
