title: feat(chat): flush pending messages without extra steer text
body:
## What to build

Let a Chat session flush every pending message through the existing steering delivery path without requiring a newly typed message. An optional extra message joins the batch after the pending messages. This extends the batching behavior delivered by #6500 and gives both Chat and ao send a usable operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An active Chat turn with queued messages accepts a steer request with no extra text and delivers the pending messages in enqueue order as one provider input.
- [ ] If extra text is supplied, it follows the queued messages and retains its own identity. Every queued message keeps its text, attachments, origin, sender metadata, and separate transcript row.
- [ ] With no pending messages and no extra text, return a clear no-op result without contacting the provider. With an extra message and no active turn, preserve the existing normal send behavior.
- [ ] The Chat action and ao send --steer can invoke this behavior without adding a placeholder message. Preserve client message id recovery and do not resend an uncertain provider delivery.
- [ ] Tests cover empty and mixed batches, attachments, concurrent enqueue, provider refusal, retry, and recovery. The response distinguishes queued, provider accepted, and no-op outcomes.

## Blocked by

None. Can start immediately.

## Related work

#6500 added queued batch delivery. #6360 tracks a race when steer falls back to a new turn. This issue must preserve that race as an explicit regression case.

title: feat(chat): interrupt and restart explicit Steer with pending batch
body:
## What to build

Make an explicit Steer action in a Chat session stop the active provider turn, preserve all pending messages, and start one new turn containing the pending batch plus optional new text. When the session is idle, send the batch as a normal turn. The operation must not use the existing Stop behavior that cancels queued messages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For an active Chat turn, Steer requests interruption and waits for the named turn to reach a committed terminal outcome before starting the replacement turn.
- [ ] The replacement input contains every message pending at the claim boundary in enqueue order, followed by optional new text. Each source retains its own durable identity, attachments, origin, sender, and timeline attribution.
- [ ] A Steer with queued messages and no new text works. With no queued messages and no new text it returns a clear no-op. An idle session with content starts one normal turn.
- [ ] Chat UI steering and ao send --steer use the same stop, claim, and dispatch semantics. Ordinary Stop keeps its existing cancellation behavior.
- [ ] A new message arriving during interruption is either included in the claimed batch or remains queued for the next delivery. No message is lost or delivered twice.
- [ ] If interruption is refused or its outcome is uncertain, AO does not start a replacement turn on an unconfirmed state. The pending batch and stable delivery handle remain recoverable.
- [ ] Tests cover late completion events, failed prior turns, provider refusal, concurrent sends, daemon recovery, and the fallback race described in #6360. TUI behavior remains unchanged.

## Blocked by

- Blocked by #7777.

## Related work

#6360 documents an existing steer fallback race. This change must satisfy its acceptance conditions without dispatching before the previous result is committed and acknowledged.

title: feat(chat): deliver ordinary messages at active turn provider boundaries
body:
## What to build

When ordinary messages arrive during an active Chat turn, durably queue them and ask a provider with native active turn steering support to deliver the pending batch into that turn. The agent should see the messages at the provider's next model request boundary instead of waiting for the turn to finish. This applies to human sends, inter-agent sends, and eligible lifecycle notifications. Explicit Steer keeps the interrupt and restart behavior from #7778.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A normal message to a busy Chat session is persisted before provider I/O. For a provider advertising active turn steering, AO claims eligible queued messages in order and submits them to the current named turn without waiting for completion.
- [ ] A burst of concurrent messages can form one batch. Only one flush may claim a given row; arrivals after a claim remain queued and trigger a later flush.
- [ ] AO records which queued rows the provider accepted, preserves individual transcript attribution and attachments, and does not describe mere enqueue as delivery.
- [ ] A provider that lacks native steering keeps the existing durable queue and completion drain. The same fallback applies when the running turn is not steerable.
- [ ] Definite provider refusal releases the batch for normal delivery. An uncertain outcome does not cause blind replay or duplicate execution; recovery uses durable receipts.
- [ ] Provider turn completion, a manual Steer, Stop, hibernation, and concurrent sends do not lose, reorder, or duplicate messages.
- [ ] Tests cover Codex and negotiated ACP steering, unsupported providers, long tool calls, mixed message sources, concurrent arrivals, completion races, and recovery. No claim is made that AO can inject into arbitrary tool response contents or interrupt a blocked tool call at an exact instant.

## Blocked by

- Blocked by #7777.
- Blocked by #7778.

## Related work

#3634 records delayed delivery for a TUI worker. This issue covers Chat sessions; TUI delivery remains tracked there.

title: CI-failure nudges fire on a green PR: stale failed check run on the same head SHA is treated as current (no latest-run-per-check-name)
body:
**Summary**
scmChecksFromGraphQL / failedSCMChecks (backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go) treat every node in statusCheckRollup.contexts as a current check. When a workflow run is superseded by concurrency cancellation, GitHub keeps the old run's check runs on the same head SHA. A gate job in that run (e.g. a job that needs: a cancelled job and fails with "Require X to pass") reports conclusion FAILURE while the run itself is cancelled. The newer run's same-named check is SUCCESS, but AO still sees a failed node, so it sets CI=failing and injects "CI is failing on your PR" into the worker every poll.

**Repro (observed 2026-11-03, ao desktop 0.14.4 daemon, main still has the same code)**
PR with a workflow using concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true and a gate job (Worker startup check) that fails when its dependency is cancelled.
Push twice quickly. Run A (old) is cancelled; its gate job concludes FAILURE. Run B (new, same head SHA) passes.
gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup lists three Worker startup check entries: FAILURE (run A), FAILURE (run B-attempt), SUCCESS (latest). GitHub UI shows green.
AO sends the worker "CI is failing ... Failed: Worker startup check (failed)" every ~5 minutes (we saw 4 sends in 17 min for one PR, many PRs at once), citing run A's job URL, while the PR head is green.
Expected
Only the newest run of each check name on the head SHA is considered. A PR whose newest run of every check is passing/skipped is not CI-failing, and no nudge is sent.

**Actual**
All nodes are considered; any failed node => CIFailing + nudge with a log tail. Dedupe signature includes URL/LogTail so it re-fires whenever the observation rebuilds.

**Proposed fix**
In scmChecksFromGraphQL output, keep one check per name: highest CheckRun databaseId wins (StatusContext: last wins).
If the rollup summary is failing but no failed checks remain after step 1, recompute summary from the deduped checks (passing, or pending if any queued/in_progress). Patch + unit test attached (not compiled locally; Go 1.27.1 not installed on our side).
Impact
Each nudge makes the worker fetch CI logs. With ~10 workers on stacked PRs this exhausted the shared GitHub REST rate limit (2026-10-30), blocking all gh calls for every session for the rest of the window. Also wastes worker tokens and trains workers to ignore real CI alerts.

**Related**
#1409 (stale CI-failure injection, closed), #1122, #4850 item 3 (misclassified failure).

title: feat(desktop): ao-app://new-task deep link that opens a prefilled New task composer
body:
## Problem

Docs and marketing sites now commonly have buttons like **Open in ChatGPT**, **Open in Claude**, **Open in Cursor** and **Open in v0**. One click takes the reader from a page into a tool with a prompt already filled in. We want the same for Orchestrator: an **Open in Orchestrator** item in the "Copy page" menu on pages like `/migrate/conductor/`. It would open the desktop app on a New task with a prompt such as "Set up Orchestrator" or "Migrate my Conductor setup".

The desktop app has no deep link for this today. `ao-app://` is registered (`frontend/forge.config.ts` `AUTH_PROTOCOL`, `frontend/src/main/cloud-auth.ts` `setAsDefaultProtocolClient`), and every URL goes through `handleCloudDeepLinkAndFocus` in `frontend/src/main.ts`, which only handles:

- `ao-app://share/...` (a shared cloud session)
- `ao-app://billing` (the Stripe return)
- everything else → `handleCloudDeepLink` (the WorkOS auth callback)

This means any other `ao-app://` URL is treated as a sign-in callback and can show the **sign-in failure dialog**. That is a bug in its own right: a stray or malformed link should not look like a failed sign-in.

## Proposed direction

Add `ao-app://new-task?prompt=<urlencoded>`, with optional `&project=<id>` and `&agent=<harness>`.

**Behavior**
- It opens or focuses the window and shows the **New task composer with the prompt prefilled**.
- It **never starts an agent by itself**. The user reviews the text and presses send, because a link on any web page must not be able to run anything.
- Without `project`, the composer's normal project picker applies. A standalone agent is fine for the "Set up Orchestrator" case.
- Unknown `project` or `agent` values fall back to the defaults instead of failing.

**Input safety**
- Cap the prompt length (for example 8 KB after decoding).
- Reject control characters (except `\n` and `\t`).
- Ignore unknown query params.

**Routing** (in `handleCloudDeepLinkAndFocus`, before the auth fallback)
- Cover all three entry paths: warm `open-url` (macOS), `second-instance` argv (Windows/Linux), and cold-start `process.argv`.
- On a cold start, queue the link like `pendingShareLink` (a `pendingNewTaskLink` plus a `take…` IPC that the renderer calls once it has mounted), since the shell WebContents may not be ready yet.
- Send only real auth callbacks (the `callback` host) to `handleCloudDeepLink`. **Log and ignore unknown hosts**, with no sign-in failure dialog.

**Website side (follow-up, not in this issue)**
- Link to an https page such as `orchestrator.inc/open?prompt=...` rather than straight to `ao-app://`. That page tries the deep link and offers the download if the app is not installed, since a bare custom-scheme link does nothing silently when no app handles it. It also gives us a place to count clicks.

**Also**
- Unit tests for URL parsing (encoding, the length cap, control characters, unknown params, unknown hosts) and for routing.
- A docs mention under `frontend/src/docs/content`.
- A changelog line, if the release process wants one.

## Acceptance

- `open 'ao-app://new-task?prompt=hello'` on macOS opens the New task composer showing `hello`, both with the app running and with it closed, and nothing starts until the user presses send.
- `open 'ao-app://whatever'` logs and does nothing (no sign-in failure dialog).
- The same works on Windows and Linux through argv.

Once a release ships this, the website's Copy page menu can link to `ao-app://new-task?prompt=...` for the install and Conductor-migration prompts.

title: feat(desktop): warn when another ao on PATH shadows the app's CLI
body:
Code changes: +597 -13  
Tests: +619 -1  
Others: +189 -0

## What

Detect when a terminal resolves a different `ao` than the desktop app's bundled CLI. Passive detection never executes the other binary. Details offers **Run ao version**, with an explanation that this executes it; permission applies only to the displayed file identity. After that explicit check, equal versions clear the notice, newer versions stay in Settings, and older or unreadable versions keep the notice.

**Use this app's ao** replaces a writable unmanaged executable with a symlink after confirmation. Replacement checks both paths and file identity/metadata before staging and immediately before rename. Homebrew installs, npm paths, read-only directories and unsupported builds receive manual guidance instead. Dismissal identifies the executable, so another file appearing at the same path warns again.

## Why

Fixes #7310.

A stale `ao` first on `PATH` makes current commands fail with errors that look like AO bugs (`unknown command "remote-host" for "ao"`), and it cannot warn about itself. `ao doctor` only runs on request, and typing it runs the stale binary.

**Scope changed since the issue was filed:** #7429 (merged Nov 1) already makes AO terminals and agents using zsh or bash run the app's `ao`. This PR covers what is left: terminals AO does not start, such as Terminal.app and VS Code, and AO terminals using fish.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: home screen with no warning](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rhithesh/067e47c6728bfee256d71a5b41cea3c0/raw/f9cdcfde47c0ca4b61c7cdaaa4e6c87808e8cc53/before-home.png) | ![After: short notice with a fix button](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rhithesh/067e47c6728bfee256d71a5b41cea3c0/raw/f9cdcfde47c0ca4b61c7cdaaa4e6c87808e8cc53/fix-popup.png) |
| No way to see which `ao` runs | ![After: details with both paths in monospace](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rhithesh/067e47c6728bfee256d71a5b41cea3c0/raw/f9cdcfde47c0ca4b61c7cdaaa4e6c87808e8cc53/fix-popup-details.png) |
| No fix offered | ![After: confirm dialog before replacing](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rhithesh/067e47c6728bfee256d71a5b41cea3c0/raw/f9cdcfde47c0ca4b61c7cdaaa4e6c87808e8cc53/fix-confirm.png) |
| No fix offered | ![After: Homebrew install gets Show in Finder and a copyable command](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rhithesh/067e47c6728bfee256d71a5b41cea3c0/raw/f9cdcfde47c0ca4b61c7cdaaa4e6c87808e8cc53/fix-popup-brew.png) |
| No Settings row | ![After: Settings row aligned with the other rows](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rhithesh/067e47c6728bfee256d71a5b41cea3c0/raw/f9cdcfde47c0ca4b61c7cdaaa4e6c87808e8cc53/fix-settings.png) |

The screenshots show the original UI before the explicit **Run ao version** control was added to Details. No updated screenshot of that control is attached. The paths in the screenshots are from a dev build, with a scratch `ao` under `ao-repro/fake`. The Before capture is from an earlier `main`, which is why one home card differs. The screenshots with the fix button used a temporary, uncommitted patch: see Testing.

The version-based rows below apply after the user explicitly chooses **Run ao version**. Before that action, a different executable has an unknown version and raises the generic notice.

| The other `ao` | Notice | Settings row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Older | Yes, says "older" | Yes |
| Version can't be read or ordered, such as `dev` | Yes, says "different" | Yes |
| Newer | No | Yes |
| Same version | No | No |
| None, a symlink to the app's `ao`, or the login shell failed | No | No |

## How

- **Detection (`shared/cli-shadow.ts`):** takes the first executable file named `ao` in `PATH` order, as a shell would, and compares realpaths. A failed login-shell probe reports `unknown` and stays silent. There is no fallback to `process.env.PATH`.
- **Versions:** runs the other executable only after the explicit Details action, bound to its file identity. Takes the first valid semver token from `ao version`, and compares with `semver`, which the app already uses. A `dev` build can't be ordered, so it is never called older.
- **Which fix is offered:** a replace, unless one of these applies, in which case the user gets a command to run themselves:
  - The real path is under `/Cellar/`, `/Caskroom/` or `/node_modules/`: `brew uninstall ...` for Homebrew, or a quoted removal command for the discovered npm shim. A `node_modules` path alone cannot establish a global npm install, so no global uninstall command is suggested.
  - The directory isn't writable: `sudo rm ...`.
  - This build fails `cliLinkSupport` (not installed, AppImage, translocated, on a mounted volume): `rm ...`.
- **Replace (`replaceCliShadow`):** stages a symlink, runs `ao version` through it, re-checks, compares the confirmed file identity (device, inode, size and modification/change times for the entry and target), then renames over the path. This detects edits and replacements at the same pathname. The final comparison and rename are separate filesystem operations, so this is not an atomic compare-and-swap. Replacing a symlink leaves the file it pointed to. Replacing a regular file deletes it, and the confirm says that can't be undone. Shell rc files are never touched, and AO never runs `sudo` or the removal commands.
- **IPC safety:** the renderer sends the path, real target and file identity the user confirmed, and the main process re-inspects and refuses unless they are still the current first `ao`. Reveal takes no path at all.
- **Paths:** each path segment is kept whole, so lines only break at a slash.
- **60s probe:** moved from `main.ts` to `main/cli-shadow-shell-path.ts`, with tests that only a successful answer is cached.

**Please check these:**

1. **`cliLink:link` is not reused.** The review pointed to it, but it refuses any `ao` AO didn't create (`foreign`), its confirm only covers AO's own stale links, and it needs Developer Mode and a set list of directories. Its header also says it never replaces a command AO did not create. So `replaceCliShadow` copies its stage, verify and rename steps as a separate function, and its `cliLinkSupport` check is reused.
2. **"Not writable" alone would not catch npm or Homebrew,** since those directories are usually writable by the user. That is why the real path is checked too.
3. **Choices the review left open:** a newer `ao` only appears in Settings. An unreadable version raises the notice, because it may be just as old.
4. **The button is hidden in dev builds,** following `cliLinkSupport`, because a link into a checkout goes stale. A dev app shows the fallback, so reviewing the button needs an installed build or the patch under Testing.
5. **Running the discovered executable now requires an explicit action.** Passive inspection, reveal and replacement never run it. Verification of the trusted bundled binary and staged link still uses `readCliVersion`.

**Intentional omissions:**
- Windows reports `unknown`.
- Aliases and shell functions are not detected, because this reads `PATH`. `ao doctor`'s `ao-login-shell` check still covers them.
- A replace writes no `cli-link.json` marker, because the path may not be one the Developer Mode link manages. That row may call such a link "not an Orchestrator link".

**Known rough edges:**
- The confirm dialog shows paths in running text, so they can still wrap at a hyphen there.
- An npm shim that needs `node` may not answer `ao version` under the minimal env, so it would read as "different".
- The non-English translations are mine and have not been reviewed by native speakers.

## Testing

### Maintainer follow-up (`36aaf7799c`, `7972e09876`, `557efbbcad`)

- Discards superseded inspection results, so a slow version check cannot resurrect the warning after a successful replacement. Covered by a deferred-probe regression test.
- Uses current `primary` / `secondary` button variants, fixing the CI typecheck failure against current `main`.
- Focused tests: **68 passed across 3 files** (`cli-shadow.test.ts`, `cli-shadow-shell-path.test.ts`, `CliShadowBanner.test.tsx`). Includes passive inspection, consent for a changed executable, actual edits after inspection and during staged-link verification, local npm guidance, and changed-file dismissal.
- Startup in the real isolated dev desktop left the disposable shadow executable's execution marker absent. Native UI automation did not reliably exercise the new action; no packaged-build verification is claimed.
- Broader local validation was stopped at the maintainer's request. Only focused tests were run after that instruction. Full validation is left to CI; no complete local frontend-suite pass is claimed.

### Original author verification (before the maintainer follow-up)


On macOS arm64, against the real Electron app in dev mode, with `AO_DATA_DIR` pointing at scratch data and `SHELL` pointing at a wrapper that sets `PATH` (rc files untouched, and my real `~/.local/bin/ao` unchanged).

**The replace was tested with a temporary, uncommitted one-line patch** forcing `isPackaged: true` in `cli-shadow-ipc.ts`, since dev builds hide the button. **I did not launch a packaged build:** from outside `/Applications`, startup relocation hands off to the installed app or replaces it.

- **Replace, clicked through the real button and IPC:**
  - Cancel changes nothing.
  - A symlink is replaced, and the old file is kept. The status becomes `match`, the notice clears, and the path now runs the app's `ao`.
  - A regular file is replaced.
  - A file changed while the dialog was open is refused with a message and left alone.
- **Versions in the real app:** older, same, newer and `dev` all behave as in the table above.
- **Fallback:** a writable symlink into a `Cellar` gets `brew uninstall ao` and is left unchanged, and Copy command fills the clipboard. Without the patch, the dev app shows Show in Finder and Copy command. I did not click Show in Finder.
- **Settings row:** its label lines up with the other General rows.
- **New tests:** `cli-shadow.test.ts` uses real temp dirs and symlinks, including failure and race cases. `CliShadowBanner.test.tsx` covers the notice, confirm and Settings row. `cli-shadow-shell-path.test.ts` covers caching.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- **`npm test`:** 11,331 passed, 49 failed, 9 skipped.
  - 47 are in `browser-profile-import.test.ts`, which fails the same way on `main` here (`better-sqlite3` ABI mismatch, running Node 26).
  - 2 in `import-folder-scan.test.ts` timed out under full-suite load. That file passes alone (10/10).

**Not run locally:** Playwright e2e, the Electron boundary checks, docs and packaging jobs, the Linux and Windows suites, and a packaged build. Please rely on CI for these.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording

title: feat(chat): fold long user messages behind Show more
body:
Code changes: +258 -32\
Tests: +84 -8\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Long user messages in chat fold to about 10 lines with a soft fade and a **Show more** / **Show less** button. Turns that go straight to an answer keep an empty row under the prompt, the same height as **Worked for**, so the prompt's hover actions (time, edit, copy) no longer sit on the reply.

## Why

A pasted log or long brief filled the whole chat with one bubble. And when a turn had no "Worked for" row, the floating hover actions overlapped the first line of the reply.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the prompt's time, edit and copy buttons sit on the reply's first line](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/fc176893156e3ec33a26e8052dec4217/raw/before-actions-overlap-reply.png) | ![After: long prompt folded with a fade and Show more; an empty row keeps the actions off a direct reply; a Worked for turn has the same spacing](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/fc176893156e3ec33a26e8052dec4217/raw/after-folded-and-reserved-row.png) |
| A long message renders at full length | Folds at ~10 lines with a fade and "Show more"; short messages are unchanged and have no button |
| — | Opening/closing animates height and fade (220ms); reduced motion switches instantly |

## How

- `CollapsibleHumanBody` wraps the bubble contents. It measures the rendered content height before paint, so text, code blocks and attachments all count. It only folds when that hides at least 2 more lines.
- Folded and animating states use `overflow: clip` (not `hidden`), so focus or find-in-page reaching folded text cannot scroll it. The height animates with a CSS transition between px values (open → `auto` after the transition). The fade is a mask with a registered `--chat-human-fade` length, the same pattern as `edge-fade-viewport`.
- Scroll: the toggle carries `aria-expanded`, so the timeline's existing pointerdown rule releases auto-follow like other disclosures. While collapsing, the text is set to `overflow-anchor: none`, so the browser anchors on the toggle and "Show less" stays under the pointer. Virtualized chats already compensate through TanStack.
- The fold state and fold height are remembered by the message's visible text. The first message remounts twice at session handoff (new chat page → session, then local echo → stored copy with a new id). Keyed by id, it flashed full length and an opened message snapped shut.
- The reserved row is in the "Worked for" slot with the same height and transition. When "Worked for" arrives as a turn settles, the gap shrinks while the summary grows and gives back its 10px flex gap, so the reply does not move. It is skipped when a branch navigator already reserves the row and for orchestrator one-line replies.
- Uses `Button` (`quiet`, `xs`) as requested, rather than `Pressable` for this disclosure.

## Testing

- Verified in the desktop dev app (isolated data): long first message stays folded through the session handoff (checked per frame with a MutationObserver), Show more/less, reserved row measured at 28px next to a 28px "Worked for".
- Updated `ChatLiveTurn.test.tsx` settle-anchoring layout to count the reserved row, and three `HumanMessage` tests to find the body by `data-chat-message-body`. `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` asserts the reserved row appears without "Worked for" and not with it. New `CollapsibleHumanBody.test.tsx`: no toggle for short content, no fold for 1–2 hidden lines, fold/open/close, remount starts folded, opened state survives remount.
- Local typecheck/tests not run; CI green on f90e79bbaf.

Manual steps:
1. Send a short message: unchanged, no button.
2. Paste ~40 lines and send: folds at ~10 lines with a fade and "Show more".
3. Click "Show more", then scroll to its end and click "Show less": smooth, button stays under the pointer.
4. Send a first message from New chat and wait for setup: it stays folded, with no full-length flash.
5. Hover a prompt whose reply came with no tool work: actions sit in the empty row above the reply.
6. Turn on Reduce motion: open/close switch instantly.

title: A failed telemetry-consent save stays latched after a policy event, so Settings shows "Telemetry cleanup failed" for a view that was just applied
body: **Project:** OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator **Affected snapshot:** fd855e49280bc80493a525c8c3340411b9e1feba ## Summary `useTelemetryPolicyStore` keeps save failures in a single `saveError` boolean. Both failure paths set it — the `getPolicy` catch and the `setEventsEnabled` catch — and the only place that clears it is the start of the next `setEnabled` attempt. The store's `onPolicy` subscription, which delivers every policy the daemon republishes, commits the incoming view with `set({ view, loaded: true, saving: false })` and never touches `saveError`. `GeneralSettingsSection`'s telemetry row then gives `saveError` precedence over every status derived from the view. Once any save attempt has failed, each later policy event replaces the view but not the error flag, so the row keeps rendering the failure alert — including over an `applied` view whose switch is on. The failure is never re-evaluated against the view it now describes; only a new switch toggle clears it. ## Expected behavior A policy event carries the authoritative view from the daemon, so the rendered status should describe that view: when the incoming view is `state: "applied"` with `eventsEnabled: true`, the row must present the enabled consent and must not keep the "Telemetry cleanup failed. Reporting remains disabled while cleanup retries." message from an earlier rejected write. A failure belongs to the attempt (and consent generation) that produced it; a newer view from the daemon supersedes that attempt, so either the flag is cleared when the view is committed or the flag is compared against the current `consentGeneration` before it is allowed to set the status. The switch and the row's description must agree. Today the switch is driven by `view.eventsEnabled` while the description is driven by `saveError`, so the two can describe opposite states of the same consent. ## Actual behavior Driving the real store and the real `GeneralSettingsSection` through a failed save followed by a policy event produced: ```text after failed setEnabled(true) saveError=true view=generation-1 after onPolicy(generation-2) saveError=true saving=false view=generation-2 view.eventsEnabled=true rendered row one role="alert" span with text "settings.telemetryEvents.failed" control (same view, no failed save) no alert ``` `settings.telemetryEvents.failed` is the localized string at `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/en.json:1285`: "Telemetry cleanup failed. Reporting remains disabled while cleanup retries." It is rendered next to a `Switch` that `checked={view?.eventsEnabled ?? false}` evaluates to on, because the replacement view has `eventsEnabled: true` and `state: "applied"`. The row is therefore simultaneously showing an enabled consent and a message saying reporting remains disabled after a failed cleanup. The same latch is reachable from the load path: `load()`'s catch sets `saveError: true` when `getPolicy()` rejects (`telemetry-policy-store.ts:31`), and the subscription registered a few lines above (`:28`) will then keep committing later views without ever clearing it. In that case the user never attempted a save at all, yet the row reports a save/cleanup failure for the rest of the session. ## Root cause The reducer for an authoritative policy view omits the failure flag: ```ts // frontend/src/renderer/stores/telemetry-policy-store.ts:28 aoBridge.telemetry.onPolicy((view) => set({ view, loaded: true, saving: false })); ``` while the flag is set by both catches: ```ts // frontend/src/renderer/stores/telemetry-policy-store.ts:31 catch { set({ loaded: true, saveError: true }); } // frontend/src/renderer/stores/telemetry-policy-store.ts:39 catch { set({ saving: false, saveError: true }); } ``` and is only cleared at `:37` (`set({ saving: true, saveError: false })`), i.e. by starting another save. Nothing in the store compares the failure with the view it belongs to, and no other subscriber resets it. The presentation layer turns that latched boolean into the row's primary status: ```tsx // frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/GeneralSettingsSection.tsx:270-277 const status = saveError ? "failed" : !view ? null : !view.durabilitySupported ? "unsupported" : view.state === "cleanup_failed" ? "failed" : view.state === "cleanup_pending" ? "pending" : view.reason === "environment_veto" ? "veto" : view.reason === "release_blocked" ? "releaseBlocked" : null; ``` and renders it as an alert: ```tsx // frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/GeneralSettingsSection.tsx:282-284 {t(status ? `settings.telemetryEvents.${status}` : "settings.telemetryEvents.description")} ``` Because `saveError` is checked first, it overrides every view-derived status for as long as it stays true. ## Impact A single transient failure — a rejected `setEventsEnabled` write, or a `getPolicy` read that failed once during `load()` — poisons the renderer's view of the telemetry consent until the user toggles the switch again. Every policy event the daemon publishes (the subscription exists because main republishes the policy while a change is still pending) replaces the view and leaves the stale error in place, so the Settings row keeps asserting that cleanup failed and that reporting remains disabled while the switch shows the consent enabled. The user sees a permanent, contradictory failure state for a policy the daemon has already applied, and the UI offers no way to reconcile it other than toggling a consent they may not want to change. The store also cannot distinguish "the last write failed" from "the daemon's view is a failure state", because both are collapsed into the same first-precedence flag. ## Suggested fix Clear the flag when an authoritative view is committed, since the view supersedes the attempt: ```ts aoBridge.telemetry.onPolicy((view) => set({ view, loaded: true, saving: false, saveError: false })); ``` If a failure should survive until the same generation is confirmed, keep the failure with its generation instead of a bare boolean — e.g. store `saveErrorGeneration` set from `view?.consentGeneration` in the catch and render `failed` only while it matches the current `view.consentGeneration` — so a newer view drops it. The load-path catch needs the same treatment; it is not a save failure at all and could live in a separate field so the row does not render "cleanup failed" for a failed read. Add coverage for the sequence above: fail `setEventsEnabled`, then deliver an `applied`/`eventsEnabled: true` view through `onPolicy`, and assert that the row has no `role="alert"` and that the switch and description agree; keep the existing control (same view, no failed save) as the baseline.

title: feat(terminal): show the agent running in a shell tab, with live status
body:
Code changes: +1207 -19  
Tests: +691 -5  
Others: +27 -0  

## What

With Developer Mode on, when you start a coding agent by hand in a local terminal tab (`claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `pi` and the other harnesses AO supports), the tab now shows the agent:

- **Logo:** the terminal icon becomes the agent's logo almost immediately.
- **Name:** a default-named tab reads as the agent ("Codex"). If two tabs in the strip run the same agent, both keep their numbers ("Claude Code 5", "Claude Code 6"). Tabs the user renamed keep their name.
- **Status:** a spinner while the agent works, a red alert when it is waiting on you (a question or permission prompt), and a dot when it finished while you were on another tab. The dot clears when you open the tab.

When the agent exits, the tab goes back to the terminal icon and its "Terminal N" name.

## Why

With several agents running in terminal tabs, every tab looked the same ("Terminal 1", "Terminal 2", ...). There was no way to tell which agent was in which tab, or which one was done or needed you, without opening each one.

## Before / After

Same session and the same four tabs in both: Claude working, Claude waiting on a question, Codex idle, and a plain shell.

| Before (`main`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: four shell tabs named Terminal 1 to 4, all with the plain terminal icon, although Claude and Codex are running in three of them](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/f41c9285ffd9a9107509f6691c3beccf4015427e/terminal-agent-status/before-strip.png) | ![After: Claude tabs with the Claude logo, one with a working spinner and one with a red waiting alert, a Codex tab with its logo, and a plain Terminal 8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/f41c9285ffd9a9107509f6691c3beccf4015427e/terminal-agent-status/after-strip.png) |

After the first Claude finishes its turn while its tab is in the background, its spinner turns into a done dot:

![After: the first Claude tab shows a grey done dot in place of the spinner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/f41c9285ffd9a9107509f6691c3beccf4015427e/terminal-agent-status/after-strip-done.png)

The captures above show the agent names cut to "Claude Co…". With Developer Mode on, agent tabs use a 192px width cap so full names with their numbers fit. Other tabs keep their 140px cap:

![After: tabs read Claude Code 5 and Claude Code 6 in full, next to a short demo tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/dc003de286fb8a73d382861ccbbb0624fc4b2bc4/terminal-agent-status/after-strip-fit.png)

## How

- **Detection is in the pty-host and event-driven.** After output, at most once per 100 ms, the host reads the terminal's foreground process group (`tcgetpgrp` on the master, as tmux does) and that group leader's argv. An agent is recognised as soon as it draws.
- **"Working" means the program is drawing.** Agent TUIs animate while they work and go quiet when they stop. Echo of typed input, redraws after a resize, and a program's first screen (2.5 s grace) don't count.
- **Waiting comes from the screen.** When the agent goes quiet, the daemon reads its screen with the per-harness screen checks AO already uses for its own sessions, falling back to common approval wording.
- **Developer Mode scope.** Ordinary users keep the existing terminal icon, title and tab width. Agent watchers start only while the Developer Mode tab preview has a mux subscriber, and PTY foreground checks run only while a watcher is attached. Switching Developer Mode off closes the preview socket and returns to plain tabs.
- **pty-host protocol v3** adds a watcher message (`MsgWatchForegroundReq` / `MsgForegroundState`). Hosts from an older AO answer v2 and are skipped, so terminals opened before the upgrade keep the plain icon until reopened.
- **Status travels over `/mux`, not a new stream.** The daemon's `shellagent` manager pushes snapshots on a new `shell-agents` channel of the terminal mux WebSocket: the client sends `{"ch":"shell-agents","type":"subscribe"}` and gets `snapshot` frames. A separate SSE stream would hold one of the 6 connections Chromium allows per host, which the app's other live feeds already crowd, and SSE stalls over the mobile quick tunnel. Mobile and remote clients can subscribe the same way later.
- **Renderer:** a small zustand store holds one mux socket while a local shell tab is mounted with Developer Mode on. `ShellTerminalTab` swaps the icon, renames default-named tabs and adds a status glyph through a new `trailing` slot on `TerminalTabFrame`, reusing the sidebar's status icons. Only visible agent tabs use a 192px cap so "GitHub Copilot 12" fits.

**Platform scope:** logo/status detection is enabled for native macOS and Linux PTYs. Windows ConPTY and the tmux backend keep ordinary terminal tabs. Mobile, remote and cloud terminals retain their existing terminal I/O; their status UI is outside this PR. `npx <agent>` launches are not detected. `fx` and Command Code's `cmd` are left out because those names clash with common tools.

## Testing

Local validation after the regression audit and Developer Mode gate:
- Affected PTY, runtime-router and shell-agent packages pass `go test -race`. The tracker and real Unix PTY `exec` regressions pass 10 repetitions; the manager test covers a quiet permission prompt without an intervening busy state.
- The final focused terminal, store and CenterPane run passed 75 tests; frontend typecheck passed. The shell-agent and PTY targeted race tests passed three repetitions. The manager tests also passed ten repetitions after fixing cleanup of shells closed before subscription. Go build and targeted vet passed. A production renderer build contains the agent tab width utility.
- Earlier validation: all 187 focused frontend terminal/store tests pass. Frontend and E2E typechecks, `go build ./...`, and `go vet ./...` pass.
- The mobile audit passed all 2,768 tests. Linux and Windows PTY test binaries cross-compile; local Docker is unavailable, so native Linux execution is verified in CI.
- Full local suites are not a clean pass. The audit reproduced native-shell/tmux failures on the PR base and found inherited AO environment effects. The full frontend rerun still encounters the existing native SQLite addon ABI mismatch and unrelated Settings timing failures. On this head, the local shellterm suite still fails its existing EOF-backslash fixture; the relevant backend packages pass under the race detector. Full native CI is enabled with `ci:full` for this update. The pushed head is being checked in GitHub Actions.

The follow-up fixes cover four reproduced cases: fast permission output suppressed as echo now gets one settled-screen recheck; `exec agent` refreshes argv on output; daemon-address changes clear old status and reject obsolete socket callbacks; interpreter classification stops at the script instead of matching its arguments, while preserving Bun/Deno config flags. Stdin and ambiguous interpreter options retain the plain terminal icon. Unknown/malformed status frames preserve the last valid snapshot. Regression tests failed before these fixes and pass afterward.

Manual checks in a dev build on macOS:
- All 14 harnesses installed on the test machine were started in terminals and then closed. claude, codex, aider, opencode, grok, droid, amp, gemini, muse, pi and prime-agent were detected and killed on close. opencode's background `serve` helper exits about 10 s after close, the same delay as after a normal Ctrl+C. cursor-agent, dsh and hermes failed to start on that machine for local install reasons.
- States were checked on the live stream: working while drawing, waiting on Claude's question prompt, idle, done dot when finished in the background, and back to the plain terminal on exit.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(remote): open remote chats instantly and keep them readable offline
body:
Code changes: +630 -129\
Tests: +519 -30\
Others: +35 -0 (generated openapi.yaml, schema.ts)

## What

Remote chats open in under a second on a slow link, stop re-downloading while idle, and stay readable while the host is away.

- **Open:** the click navigates first and refreshes behind it. The first page is 30 messages with tool output capped at 512 B (head and tail), and "Show the whole output" reads one row.
- **Idle:** the 2 s poll is gone. A change event triggers a tail read after the last sequence.
- **Offline:** the newest page of up to 50 chats and each host's project and session lists are kept in IndexedDB and shown until a read replaces them. While the host is unreachable the chat is read-only, with a notice in the composer.

## Why

Opening a chat on a remote host took 15-20 s over a tunnel. Measured on a real host:

- The click awaited a refetch of the sidebar lists before navigating: 1.3-1.5 s.
- The chat polled its live page every 2 s with no in-flight guard. The page was 3.24 MB, 2.0 MB of it tool output, so the first page took 14.6 s to arrive.

With the host unreachable, a chat you had already read showed nothing at all.

## Before / After

Real desktop app against a second real daemon, over a shaped link (4 Mbit/s, 250 ms RTT). Before is `main` at the base of this PR, for both the renderer and the host.

The chat is a real 191-message conversation with about 2,300 tool activities, and every word is replaced by filler of the same length because this repo is public. It gzips to 110% of the original, so the wire numbers lean high on both sides.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: cold open takes 3.6 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80cb629a-eb80-4afc-8525-830da659a2e9) | ![After: cold open takes 0.6 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa821404-59d7-4643-a94f-491b532f8c1b) |
| ![Before: host unreachable, reload shows only an error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d97e49a-cd35-4350-b604-a19d1410ee64) | ![After: host unreachable, reload shows the saved chat, read-only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a890fb8-4d00-4b6d-914e-8a208fec89f0) |
| ![Before: tool output sent whole in every page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/351a5b66-d2ef-4db1-953a-7c7fd7792718) | ![After: tool output head and tail, with Show the whole output](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd1bd8d7-4052-4d0d-a9e0-f1208f7ba459) |
| Cold open: 3,389 ms, 3,468 KB down | 620 ms, 62 KB |
| Reopen: 257 ms, then a 2,311 KB refetch | 195 ms, 55 KB |
| Reload on the chat: 7,351 ms | 1,347 ms |
| Idle chat for 20 s: 10.4 MB down, 9 full chat reads | 2 KB down, 0 chat reads |
| Remote edit appears: 4,927 ms, 4,623 KB down | 636 ms, 53 KB |
| Whole tool output: sent in every page | Read on demand in 303 ms |
| Reload with the host unreachable: "Host is offline", nothing else | History shown, read-only |
| | Host drops with the chat open, then returns: 0 of 1,944 samples lost the chat, and an edit made during the outage appeared on reconnect |

Offline reload timing: 0.9-1.4 s on this branch before its last rebase. One run after it took 4.0 s with the machine at load ~15, and I could not get a clean repeat, so read this as about 1 s, not a measured figure for this exact commit.

Both clips have the same grey cast from the capture method. The window is white in the app.

## How

- **Backend:** `afterSequence` tail reads and an opt-in `outputLimit`, so clients that don't ask get what they got before. "Show the whole output" is a one-row range read, not a new route.
- **Stale-while-revalidate:** what a host showed last stays until a read replaces it, also across a failed read or a reconnect. Only a host refusing this device (`BAD_PASSWORD`, `HOST_API_INCOMPATIBLE`) takes it away.
- **`savedCopy`:** hides the controller banner on a saved copy, because that state is stale and neither action works. It is not keyed on the composer lock because Cloud read-only sets that lock too, and there the banner is true.
- **Pickers:** New Task, New Chat and notifications stay connected-only, so they list only hosts that can take work.
- **Stream reconnect:** a host's event stream that drops while the host stays connected now reopens with the shared SSE backoff (`computeSseRetryDelayMs`, about 5 s first). Before, nothing reopened it, so one dropped link left that host on the 2 s fallback poll, which re-reads the project and session lists and the open chat.

Worth a close look: the delta merge in `useConversation.ts` and the `hostUnreachable` / `hostRefused` rule in `SessionView.tsx`.

Known limits:

- Only the newest page of each chat is on disk. Older pages and "Show the whole output" need the host.
- Reviewer chats are not saved.
- A turn that was running when saved still looks running.
- After sign-out, saved chats stay on disk, hidden, until the saved host list changes.

Not included: capping `artifactFiles` in `/sessions`, which is still large on hosts with many artifacts.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, plus `go vet` and `go test` on the chat, httpd, store and daemon packages. `golangci-lint` found 0 issues on the changed code, and the regenerated spec and schema match.
- `tsgo` clean. 4,269 renderer tests in 224 files pass across remote, chat, session, sidebar, shell and i18n.
- After the last merge of main at `8bf3684709` (one conflict in `event-transport.ts`: main removed the Codex account stream beside the remote disk cache line), `go build ./...`, `tsgo` and 102 tests in 5 files were re-run locally: transport, `SessionView.remote`, `useWorkspaceQuery.remote`, the remote cache and the tail merge. The regenerated `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` match the merged ones.
- The review fix re-ran `tsgo` and 201 tests in 9 files: transport, every `useConversation` suite, `SessionView.remote` and `ChatStatusBanners`.
- The stream reconnect re-ran `tsgo` and the transport and backoff suites, 59 tests. The new transport test failed before the change because no second stream opened.

**Gaps:** I did not run every CI job locally, so CI is the check for the rest. The full build, before the stale-list fix below, was also measured on a second Mac over a Cloudflare quick tunnel, from a real click to the newest message: cold 0.69 s, reopen 0.43 s, reload 1.5 s (3 runs, dev renderer, real-sized session list, no live agents on that host, so treat it as a best case).

The lab found two bugs the unit tests missed, both fixed and now covered by tests:

- The chat vanished for about 700 ms on reconnect, in 28 of 945 samples, because a stale query error dropped the session.
- A red "agent controller stopped" banner sat over the saved copy, with buttons that could not work.

Review found a third: a chat opened while the host was offline kept a red "Could not load this remote conversation." alert after the host returned. The lab showed it in 2 of 2 runs, until each run ended 28 s and 37 s later. After the fix it did not show in 4 runs (2 opened offline, 1 link drop, 1 host kill), sampled every 25 ms. The lab host leaves `connectedHosts` before the 2 s poll ticks, so a poll read failing during a drop ran only in a unit test.

Review also found that an undone or cancelled last turn left the tail floor above the newest visible turn, so a second undo from another client stayed on screen. A unit test covers that; a two-client undo did not run in the lab.

The lab also found a stale to-do list, with real Claude on a remote chat. If every item was done when a turn started, nothing replayed the list, so the first write came mid-turn. That write superseded the older copy, which sits below the tail floor, so the old list stayed on screen for the rest of the turn: 39.0 s and 38.5 s in 2 of 2 runs, none with an item still open. A new copy of a list that spans turns now forces a whole-page read. With the fix, 2 of 2 runs showed no stale list, at the cost of one more whole-page read in those turns. `tsgo` and the 11 tail tests were re-run locally for this change.

The lab also found that one dropped link left a host on the 2 s poll for good; `main` has the same code. The lab cut every live connection while the link kept listening, so the host never went offline. Before the reconnect, the stream did not reopen in 90 s, and the renderer read the session list and the project list 21 times each per 20 s (5 each before the cut) and the open chat 10 times. On the real host the session list is 994 KB per read. After it, the stream reopened 3.9 s and 4.3 s after the cut in 2 of 2 runs, then list reads went back to 2-8 per 20 s and chat reads to 0.

The lab also found a hole in history: a cached chat reopened after more than a page of new messages lost the rows between the two pages. On the old code the saved page jumped from sequence 2585 to 2596, and "Load earlier messages" ran out without showing them. Now the new page replaces the cached one, and one click showed the first new message.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording

title: fix(chat): clear stale model labels when switching providers
body:
Code changes: +5 -0\
Tests: +55 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Clear the previous provider's model-resolution override when a Chat provider switch commits. Switching from Claude Code to Codex now lets the composer show Codex's selected or default model.

## Why

After Claude resolves `opus` to `claude-opus-5-5`, AO stores that resolution on the conversation. Switching to Codex replaces the provider and its settings but previously retained the Claude resolution. Clients prioritize that record when naming the answering model, so Codex could be working while the composer still showed Opus.

## Before / After

Backend conversation snapshot after switching Claude Code to Codex, without an explicit target model:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `harness: "codex"`, with `modelReroute.toModel: "claude-opus-5-5"`; the composer displays the stale Claude model. | `harness: "codex"`, with no model reroute; the composer uses Codex's own model. |
| A failed switch preserves the source provider's settings and model resolution. | The same source state is preserved on failure. |
| The earlier Claude resolution remains in chat history. | The same historical activity remains visible. |

Evidence is covered by the service regression test against real SQLite storage. This changes the backend snapshot; no renderer code or layout changes.

## How

Use the existing generated model-reroute update query to write SQL NULL inside `CommitProviderSwitch`, in the same transaction that publishes the target branch, provider settings, and switch marker. Failure rolls the change back with the rest of the switch.

No migration or generated API changes are needed. This applies to subsequent successful provider switches; it does not rewrite already-switched conversations during upgrade.

## Testing

- Added a Claude-to-Codex service regression that asserts the stale model override disappears while its historical activity remains.
- Strengthened the failed-switch test to assert the source model resolution is preserved.
- Before the request to stop local checks, the regression reproduced on the base and passed with the fix. API regeneration completed without drift.
- Broader local checks were stopped at the user's request. Remaining validation is delegated to GitHub Actions; no complete local suite pass is claimed.
- Manual diff review found no additional actionable issues.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions
- [x] Before / After includes observable backend behavior
- [x] Regression tests cover the changed behavior

title: Split panes
body:
Code changes: +1810 -95  
Tests: +299 -5  
Others: +63 -0

## What

Drag center tabs into resizable split panes, with a drop preview and grouped tabs. Terminals, the session chat, reviewer chat, and local files retain their views as the layout changes.

## Why

Keep a terminal beside the agent conversation or a file without repeatedly switching tabs.

## Before / After

Captured from isolated native apps at the same window size and dark theme.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: separate chat and terminal tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5de23c07-8eaa-464c-be86-fd8250cdd94e) | ![After: chat and terminal side by side](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98dcd108-1626-4996-9719-6d3df5464902) |
| Each terminal/file has a separate strip tab | A group tab names the focused pane and shows the other members as icons |
| No pane split shortcuts | Command-D opens a terminal on the right; Command-Shift-D opens one below; Command-W closes the focused pane |

![After: chat beside stacked terminals](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a827ecb-6a80-45cd-9d03-a962ba73a5b4)

## How

- Model pane groups as split trees; resize by updating CSS variables and move the drag ghost by transform.
- Allow several cached terminals on screen and move their live containers between pane slots.
- Keep file and reviewer-chat containers mounted while their placement changes.
- Provide group context-menu ungrouping, hover close controls, click-to-focus, and collapse to a single tab when a split has one member left.
- Keep the main session chat undimmed. Other inactive panes dim to show keyboard focus.
- On macOS, diff moves to Command-Shift-G and dictation to Control-Command-D. Other platforms use Ctrl-Alt-Shift-D to split right and Ctrl-Alt-Shift-minus to split below.

Cloud files still use the existing single-file view and are excluded from groups. Layout groups last for the renderer session; they are not persisted across app restarts.

## Testing

The native app was started against isolated scratch data for screenshot capture. Observed Command-D opening a terminal on the right and Command-Shift-D opening one below. Drag, resize, and close flows were not exercised manually.

title: [Feature]: Beads (bd) tracker for issue intake
body:
### Problem

I plan agent work in [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) (`bd`), a local, git-backed issue tracker built for coding agents. It needs no server and no API credentials. I would like AO to pick up ready Beads issues through the same opt-in intake it offers for GitHub and GitLab. Today I run an external bridge that polls `bd ready`, starts AO sessions through the daemon API and syncs state back. It works, but it duplicates intake logic AO already has.

### Proposed direction

A Beads adapter at `backend/internal/adapters/tracker/beads` implementing `ports.Tracker`, registered as a `trackermulti.NamedTracker` in `backend/internal/daemon/tracker_wiring.go`, with a Beads `domain.TrackerProvider`, provider validation in `TrackerIntakeConfig.Validate` and `ao spawn --tracker-provider`.

The adapter shells out to the `bd` CLI and parses its JSON output:

| Port method | `bd` call | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `List` | `bd ready --json` (with `--assignee`, `--label`, `--limit` from `ListFilter`) | `bd ready` already excludes blocked and deferred issues, so dependency order comes for free |
| `Get` | `bd show <id> --json` | `description` → `Body`, `labels` → `Labels`, `assignee` → `Assignees`, `status` → `NormalizedIssueState` |
| `Preflight` | `bd --version` plus a read in the configured store | Fails fast if `bd` is missing or the store is unreadable |

Store scope: the Beads store is a directory, not a repo URL, so each AO project needs an explicit store path (default: the project repo's own `.beads/`). `domain.Issue.URL` has no natural value; I'd leave it empty or use a `beads://<prefix>/<id>` form, whichever you prefer.

Scope and safeguards for v1:
- Same project opt-in, daemon-wide gate and required assignee rule as today. Label-based eligibility would follow from #5700 once it lands.
- Read-only: no status changes, comments or sync back into the store.
- No credentials: the adapter runs a fixed binary (`bd`, path configurable) with argument arrays, never a shell, and only against the configured store path. Issue content never selects a command, flag or path.
- Issue title and description handled as untrusted input, the same as GitHub intake.
- Any spawn limits from #2344 apply.

Happy to build this if the shape is welcome.

### Alternatives considered

- **Keep the external bridge** (what I run now): it works, but it reimplements intake, polling and prompt building outside AO and talks to the daemon's HTTP API, which is more fragile than an in-process adapter.
- **Mirror Beads issues into GitHub Issues**: adds a second source of truth and loses Beads' dependency-aware `ready` queue.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: Claude usage windows go blank: usage reads ignore 429/Retry-After, and the per-session rate_limit_event is dropped
body:
**Clean-hour test.**
- No account-list reads were made from about 18:05Z to 19:05Z. One read at 19:05Z followed.
- The two AO-managed accounts recovered: one showed weekly 97%; the other showed 5h, weekly and Fable all at 0%.
- The computer's own login, the most-read one, still showed no windows.
- Reducing reads helps, but AO still blanks the reading and ignores the back-off.

**Environment.**
- Agent Orchestrator 0.14.9 (commit f9dc4727, built 2026-11-04T07:46Z), on macOS.
- Claude Code 2.1.316.
- Three Claude subscription accounts: the computer's own login, plus two AO-managed accounts (Max).
- One Codex account.

## Symptom

- Settings › Harness › Claude Code shows no usage windows for any Claude account, including a brand-new one.
- `GET /api/v1/agents/accounts` returns `limits.windows: []` with a current `fetchedAt` and `problem: null`.
- Codex usage is unaffected.

## Mechanism

**How a read works.** Whenever a client lists the accounts and the last reading is more than about 60 s old, AO does this for each Claude account:
1. It starts a new `claude --print --input-format stream-json` process (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to the account's folder).
2. It sends `{"type":"control_request","request_id":"ao-usage","request":{"subtype":"get_usage","skip_behaviors":true}}`.
3. Claude Code calls `GET /api/oauth/usage` with that account's login.

**What goes wrong.** Anthropic answers HTTP 429. With `--debug-file`, Claude Code logs:
- `fetchUtilization: 429 remembered for this bearer; not asking again for 723s` at 17:11Z;
- `... for 3316s` at 18:01Z (on a near-idle account);
- `Failed to load usage data: Request failed with status code 429`.

Claude Code then answers `get_usage` with `rate_limits: null`, still reporting success, and AO replaces the last good reading with empty windows.

**Why it never recovers.** The 429 hold lives only inside that short-lived process. The next AO read is a new process, so it asks the endpoint again while the penalty is still running.

**What makes it worse.**
- The app's Settings › Harness and Subscriptions views and a session's Summary › Account view each poll the account list every 60 s.
- Each poll costs one usage request per Claude account, so adding accounts multiplies the rate.

## Requests

1. **Honour 429 / Retry-After per account in the daemon** across reads: persist the hold and do not start a reading process before it expires.
2. **Keep and show the last good reading** with its age, instead of replacing it with empty windows after a failed read.
3. **Read usage at most every few minutes per account**, whatever the client polling rate; serve list requests from the daemon's cache.
4. **Surface the failure.** Show a "usage temporarily unavailable (rate limited until …)" problem or stale marker rather than silent emptiness.

**Evidence** (local, sanitised): debug lines from single replays of AO's `get_usage` request at 17:11Z and 18:01Z on 4 Nov 2026. No credentials were read or printed.

## Update, 5 Nov 2026 07:05Z: the per-login budget is tiny, and sessions spend it too

**One deliberate replay per account at 07:04Z.** All three logins answered HTTP 429, each with its own Retry-After:

| Login | Live sessions | Retry-After | Implied lockout start |
|---|---|---|---|
| Device login | 15 (5 active) | 2777 s | 06:50:50Z |
| Managed A | 3 (1 active) | 878 s | 06:19:12Z |
| Managed B | 0 | 3600 s | 07:04:35Z, this request |

All three are Max 20x (`organizationRateLimitTier: default_claude_max_20x`).

**What the replays show:**
- **The lockout is per login and fixed at about 1 h.** A rejected request does not extend it: Managed A's hold kept counting down through the replay.
- **The budget is tiny.** Managed B has no sessions, read successfully at 06:19Z, and was locked by a read at 07:04Z, with at most one other Claude process start (06:38Z) in between. So the allowance is a few reads per hour per login.
- **Busy logins lock out first.** The device login's lockout began at 06:50:50Z, when neither our tools nor our sweep read it.

**Session-side reads in Claude Code 2.1.316:**
- A busy login's own sessions call the same endpoint: Claude Code's extra-usage and overage checks do it on events.
- Interactive-only offer and reset reads are excluded for SDK sessions (entrypoint `sdk-ts`).
- The 429 memory is an in-memory map per process.
- The shared snapshot (`cachedUsageUtilization`) is answered only while under 60 s old, and is written only after a success.

**The usage numbers are already free inside every session.**
- Every inference response carries the unified rate-limit headers. Claude Code applies them to its in-process limit state (`applyWindowReadings`) and emits SDK `rate_limit_event` messages.
- The ACP adapter (`claude-agent-acp`) has no rate-limit handling, and the daemon records none.
- So each session's own traffic, the one reliable per-login source, is dropped.

## Requests, revised (most valuable first)

1. **Forward `rate_limit_event` through the ACP adapter, and record it per bound account.** That gives live weekly and 5-hour utilization for every login with zero extra requests. It removes the need to poll `/api/oauth/usage`.
2. **Never start a usage read because a client polled.** Read each login at most every 30–60 min from the daemon, and serve every client from the daemon's cache.
3. **Honour Retry-After, and the 1-hour lockout, per login across processes.** Persist it.
4. **Keep and show the last good reading with its age.** Show the lockout ("usage unavailable until …") instead of empty windows.

title: fix(mobile): keep an account machine's routes across Cloud syncs
body:
Code changes: +4 -1\
Tests: +35 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On a phone signed in to Orchestrator Cloud, a machine imported from the account no longer reconnects every 30 seconds. Before, any such machine that advertises more than one route had its live events stream dropped and restarted twice per 30 s sync. On Android that also made an idle open chat on that machine flash a loader and rebuild.

## Why

The account host sync in `store.tsx` runs every 30 s. For an account-owned machine, `performSync` (`lib/accountHosts.ts`) counted it as current only when its saved routes were exactly the one address the Cloud listing gives. Otherwise it saved `[address]`. After every race, `connect.ts` saves the machine's advertised routes back with `mergeEndpoints`. So a machine with LAN plus Tailscale or a tunnel changed routes on every sync, and changed back on the next connect.

`useOtherHosts` restarts a machine's runner whenever its saved routes change. The restart sets `connection: "connecting"`, which unmounts that machine's `HostConversationTransport`. The sync also reloads the config when the selected machine's routes changed, and that reload reads the restored routes into state, restarting the runner a second time about 1 s later.

Not affected: signed-out phones, and machines the phone paired itself. A machine the phone paired itself stays a manual pairing, even after the phone links it to the account. The check dates from #6558.

#7688 keeps an open chat mounted through reconnects in general. This PR removes the reconnects that the sync caused.

## Before / After

No visual change. The difference is connection churn.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Saved routes across sync → connect → sync → connect: `tunnel` → `lan,tailscale,tunnel` → `tunnel` → `lan,tailscale,tunnel`. Every step rewrites the host, and each rewrite restarts the connection | `tunnel` → `lan,tailscale,tunnel`, then later syncs leave it alone |
| Pixel 10a, 3 min on screen: 9 `/events` streams ended (each 30 s: one ~29 s, then one ~1 s), 12 identity probes, 12 `/endpoints`, 21 `POST /push/devices` | Same 3 min: 0 streams ended, 0 identity probes, 0 `/endpoints`, 0 `POST /push/devices` |
| iPhone 17 Pro Max, 3 min on screen: 8 streams ended, 15 identity probes, 15 `/endpoints`, 18 `POST /push/devices` | Same 3 min: all 0 |

Device numbers come from the second machine's request log. Both phones run one Release binary built from this branch, signed in to the same account, with both machines imported from it. Only the JS bundle differs: unfixed (`accountHosts.ts` from `main`), then this branch installed over it, keeping sign-in and machines. With the fix, each phone kept 3 open connections and polled the machine normally (32 rounds each in the 4 min after relaunch); only the reconnects stopped.

## How

- One condition changes: an account machine is current while the listed address is one of its saved routes. The old check required `length === 1` and the first route to equal the address; the new one uses `.some(...)`.
- These still replace the routes with `[address]` as before, after which connecting learns the rest again:
  - a different token;
  - a different account;
  - a listed address that is no longer among the routes.
- Left as is: `useOtherHosts` still restarts a runner on any route change. Keeping a runner whose current route is still listed would be broader hardening, and this loop doesn't need it.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile` on Node 20, as in the Mobile workflow:
  - `npm ci`;
  - `npm run typecheck`: clean;
  - `npm test`: 266 files, 2770 tests pass.
- New tests in `lib/accountHosts.test.ts`:
  - *keeps the routes a connect added to an account machine across later syncs*: runs a sync, then the real `mergeEndpoints` with the machine's advertised routes, then two more syncs. The saved host must not be rewritten. Fails on `main`.
  - *replaces an account machine's routes when its listed address moves*: guards the reset that should stay.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- Not run locally: gitleaks (not installed here). CI runs its pinned build.
- On device: Pixel 10a and iPhone 17 Pro Max, an A/B with the same Release binary (see Before / After). Both phones were signed in fresh, so the second machine came from the account listing rather than being paired on the phone, which is the case this fixes.
- Diagnosis: a signed-in Pixel on a release build, paired with a Mac and a scratch daemon. The daemon's request log shows the cycle above. A signed-out emulator on the same daemons kept its streams open for minutes.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(sidebar): clean light surface for the session hover card
body:
## Problem

In light theme, the card that appears when you hover a sidebar session row looked dirty: a mid-gray fill, a dark hairline, and a heavy shadow over the light app.

The cause is a rule in `styles.css` added with the new sidebar (#7365). It mixes 14% foreground into the card fill and adds a 14% ring plus a 35% black shadow. That lifts the card in dark, but in light it turns the card gray.

## Fix

- Dark: the same rule, now scoped to `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`. Values are unchanged.
- Light: the card uses the same surface as menus and popovers: `--color-bg-elevated` fill and the faint `--color-border-overlay` edge. The hover card wrapper already adds `--shadow-popover`, so the card adds no shadow of its own.

`--color-bg-elevated` is solid in translucent windows, so the card looks the same with window transparency on or off.

## Before / after

Checked in the dev desktop app (isolated data) by hovering a sidebar session row.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Light, transparency on | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/bd5c347c58771a15728c7fc1fca51ca807deee69/before-light-tron.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/bd5c347c58771a15728c7fc1fca51ca807deee69/after-light-tron.png) |

| Dark (unchanged) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/bd5c347c58771a15728c7fc1fca51ca807deee69/before-dark.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/bd5c347c58771a15728c7fc1fca51ca807deee69/after-dark.png) |

Other light themes after the fix:

| Solarized (transparency off) | Flexoki (transparency on) |
|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/bd5c347c58771a15728c7fc1fca51ca807deee69/after-light-solarized.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/bd5c347c58771a15728c7fc1fca51ca807deee69/after-light-flexoki.png) |

Computed card fill: light went from `oklch(0.885)` gray to each theme's popover color (for example `oklch(1 0 0)` and `rgb(251 252 253)` for GitHub). Dark stays at `oklch(0.3508 0.002 250)`.

## Tests

No local tsc/vitest runs; this is a CSS-only change, so CI covers it.

To check by hand:
1. Settings → Appearance → Light.
2. Hover a session row in the left sidebar.
3. The card should be white with a barely visible edge and a soft shadow, like the row's three-dot menu.
4. Repeat with window transparency off, with another light theme, and in dark (dark should look the same as before).

## Risks

The light rule uses `!important` on the fill, like the dark rule it replaces. As before, it overrides the needs-attention tint on this preview card in both themes.
