title: fix(mobile): cap the request card so a long command can't push its answers off screen
body: Code changes: +100 -43\ Tests: +72 -2\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The mobile request card (the approval or question card that replaces the composer) now has a height cap. Its question scrolls inside the card, while the header with the close button, an approval's decision buttons and the typed-answer row stay pinned. ## Why When Claude asks to run a command without giving a reason, the approval card shows the raw command verbatim. With a long command (a heredoc plus a build loop), the card grew taller than the screen: - The composer dock keeps its full height, and the chat above it is the only part of the screen that shrinks. So the chat shrank to nothing. - Before the native overhaul (#7839), the dock ran off the bottom: Deny / Allow sat below the screen edge with nothing to scroll them into view. That's the report that started this. - On current `main` the dock is anchored to the bottom, so the card grows upward instead. The decisions are reachable, but the command draws over the header: the back button, the title and the card's own close button (at y = -86 pt on an iPhone 17 Pro) are buried or off screen. ## Before / After Same native build on both sides (current `main` plus this branch); only the JS bundle differs (before = `main`, after = this branch). The approval is a real Claude Code request from a scratch daemon. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | The command can't be scrolled within the card | | | Same on Android | | ## How - `requestCardMaxHeight(windowHeight, keyboardHeight)` in `requestDockModel.ts` caps the card at half of the space above the keyboard, with a 180 pt floor (the header, a couple of lines and one answer). The keyboard matters for free-text answers: without it the field you type in could be pushed behind the keyboard. - `RequestCard` is now a column: header, a `ScrollView` body (`flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 1`, so a short question still sizes to its text and only a long one gives way), then pinned answers. - **Approval:** the decisions are pinned. They are the way out of the card. - **Question:** the options are the content and scroll with the question; the typed-answer row and the Send / Next button of a several-answers question are pinned. - **Deferred request** (form, URL handshake): the message scrolls; "Open the full request" is pinned. - When the body is clipped, the first pinned row gets a hairline top border so the edge reads as "more above". - The body is keyed by the request's sequence, so a new request starts at the top rather than at the previous scroll offset. - Cards that already fit look exactly as before: no cap is reached, no divider is added. Reviewers: the change only touches the card. The dock and timeline layout in `ChatComposer` / `ChatSessionScreen` are unchanged, so the chat still gets whatever the card leaves. The cap now guarantees that is at least half the screen. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `packages/mobile` (346 files, 3412 tests). - New `RequestCard.test.tsx`: a long approval's command is inside the scroll body while Deny / Allow and the close button are outside it; the cap follows the window and the keyboard; a question's options scroll while the typed answer is pinned. All three fail against the component on `main`; the four tests that came with the overhaul still pass. - New `requestCardMaxHeight` unit tests. - Release builds on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5) and an Android 15 emulator, paired to a scratch daemon running a real Claude Code chat with `permissions.ask: ["Bash"]`. Run before the rebase, and again after it with fresh native builds of current `main`: - Long-command approval: reproduced the bug on `main` each time (both platforms); with the fix the card is capped, the command scrolls to its end, and tapping the pinned **Allow Once** resolved the approval on the daemon. - Before the rebase, a 2-question `AskUserQuestion` with long option descriptions: options scroll inside the card, the "Other" row stays pinned, and a horizontal fling still pages to "2 of 2" (both platforms). After the rebase, unit tests cover this path, including the new several-answers Send button staying pinned. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(desktop): stop a failed telemetry save outliving the view that replaced it
body:
Code changes: +25 -6\
Tests: +120 -6\
Others: +9 -0 (locale strings)

## What

The Settings row for "Share error events" no longer keeps showing "Telemetry cleanup failed" after a newer policy view has replaced the attempt that failed. A failed policy read is now reported as a load failure instead of a save failure.

## Why

`useTelemetryPolicyStore` kept failures in a single `saveError` boolean that only the next toggle could clear. Policy events replaced the view but left the flag, and the row gives `saveError` precedence over every view-derived status. One transient failure could leave the row saying reporting is disabled next to a switch showing the consent on.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Failed save, then an `applied` view with a new generation and `eventsEnabled: true`: switch on, `role="alert"` with "Telemetry cleanup failed. Reporting remains disabled while cleanup retries." | Switch on, default description, no alert |
| Failed save against `cleanup_pending`, then the same generation arrives as `applied`: failure alert stays | Default description, no alert |
| `getPolicy()` rejects during `load()`: "Telemetry cleanup failed...", and it stays after later views arrive | "Could not load the error sharing preference." until a view arrives, then the row describes that view |
| A policy event during an in-flight save set `saving: false`, re-enabling the switch before the write settled | The switch stays disabled until that write settles |

Screenshots not attached yet: the behavior above comes from rendering the real store and `GeneralSettingsSection` in tests, not from the desktop app.

## How

- The store records the view a save was rejected against (`saveErrorView`), read when the rejection arrives. An event clears the failure only when its `consentGeneration` or `state` differs from that view.
- A republish of the same generation and state keeps the failure. The retry loop in main republishes every retry while cleanup is pending, and that says nothing new about the attempt.
- The view is read at rejection, not at the start of the attempt, because main publishes before it rejects: `disable()` publishes `cleanup_failed`, and a failed enable rolls back through `disable()`, which publishes a new generation. Comparing against the starting view would let the attempt's own event erase its failure.
- This goes beyond the one-line fix suggested in the issue, which clears the flag on every event. That version also clears a fresh failure on the next retry republish, and its `saving: false` ends an attempt that is still in flight. A second toggle could then overlap the first, and the first one's rejection would be attributed to the second. Events now leave `saving` alone.
- `load()` failures move to a separate `loadError`, following `useAnalyticsOptOutStore`, with a new `settings.telemetryEvents.loadFailed` string in all nine locales. It is only set while there is no view, and any view clears it.

Intentional omission: a same-generation, same-state republish keeps the failure even when that state is `applied`. Main does not republish an unchanged `applied` view in normal operation, so this should not latch in practice. The "cleanup failed" wording for writes that were not cleanup failures is also left as is.

## Testing

Run from `frontend/`.

- Regression tests failing on the unmodified code: five store tests and two `GlobalSettingsForm` tests, including the issue's fail-then-`applied` sequence.
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/stores/telemetry-policy-store.test.ts src/renderer/i18n`: passing, 3 files.
- Reverting the store to the one-line fix fails three of the new store tests: same-view republish, in-flight attempt, and failure measured at rejection.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- Full `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts --testTimeout 120000`: 11211 passed, 85 failed, on a heavily loaded machine (load average above 50). None of the failures are in the telemetry store or i18n tests.
  - 16 of the 17 failing files, including `GlobalSettingsForm` and `SettingsDialog`, were rerun with `--maxWorkers=2 --retry=3`: 1669 passed. Retries were allowed, so individual flakes are not ruled out.
  - The remaining file, `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts` (47 failures), was not rerun. The 30 errors of this kind in the run are `Could not locate the bindings file`, consistent with installing with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. The other failures in that file were not inspected individually.
- Not run locally: the other CI jobs, including docs, browser runtime and native jobs. These need checking in CI.

title: fix(mobile): keep picked agent and model when the spawn sheet changes scope
body:
Code changes: +22 -4\
Tests: +211 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Choosing a different scope in the mobile spawn sheet, including **Standalone agent**, no longer discards the agent and model the user already picked.

## Why

The project picker called `changeProject`, which clears `agentTouched` and the model override. Clearing `agentTouched` re-runs the effect that resolves the default agent, so the picked agent was replaced by the project default or the first available agent. The task then started with an agent the user had not chosen, and the sheet gave no warning beyond the chip changing.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Pick Codex, choose Standalone agent: the agent becomes Claude Code (first available) | The agent stays Codex |
| Pick Codex and a model, choose Standalone agent: the agent resets and the model returns to Automatic | The agent and model stay, and the task is created with both |
| Pick Codex, choose a project that defaults to Cursor: the agent becomes Cursor | The agent stays Codex |
| Nothing picked, change scope: the agent follows each scope's default | Unchanged |
| The sheet's project is deleted and it re-seeds to another project: picks are cleared | Unchanged |

Behavior is compared through the rendered sheet in a component test. No simulator or device screenshots are attached.

## How

`changeProject` has two callers with different meanings, so they are now separate:

- The re-seed effect keeps `changeProject` and its resets. The sheet moved itself there, onto a project nothing was picked for. #5058 routed this path through the resets on purpose, so a touched agent is not posted to a project the user did not choose.
- The picker now calls a new `pickProject`, which keeps explicit picks. With nothing picked it resets as before, so the agent still follows each scope's default.

Decisions to review:

- **The model is kept as well as the agent.** The issue names the agent, but the same reset cleared the model, which would leave the same bug one chip over. Since #7049 model catalogs are per device and the API ignores a project id, so a picked model stays valid across scopes.
- **A picked model also holds its agent.** If only the model was picked, `pickProject` sets `agentTouched`. Otherwise the new scope's default agent could replace the agent while the model stayed, and the task would be posted with a model from a different agent.
- **The picker keeps the loaded model catalog** when picks survive, because the agent has not changed. The model request still re-runs for the new scope and `modelLoading` holds Start task until it settles.

Omitted: a first seed that lands after the user picked an agent still clears the pick, because it goes through the unchanged re-seed path.

The test renders the real `SpawnModal` with its controls mocked instead of extracting a helper, so it covers the interaction between the picker, the touched flags, and the default-agent effect.

## Testing

Run from `packages/mobile`, on Node 24 (CI uses Node 20):

- `npx vitest run lib/spawn-sheet-scope.test.tsx` on the unmodified `spawn.tsx`: 4 failed, 2 passed. The failures are the four picks-kept cases. The two that pass guard behavior that must not change (no picks, and re-seed after a delete).
- The same command with the fix: 6 passed.
- `npm run typecheck`: passes.
- `npx vitest run --testTimeout=60000`: 267 files, 2774 tests passed.

title: fix(sessions): report review run verdicts in session PR facts
body:
Code changes: +51 -6\
Tests: +249 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

`prs[].review` on `GET /api/v1/sessions` and `GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>`, and the REVIEW column of `ao session ls`, now include AO's review verdicts on the PR's current head. A PR whose latest run is complete and approved no longer reads as `none`.

## Why

`prs[].review` only ever held `pr.review_decision`, which the SCM observer fills from the provider's aggregate (GraphQL `reviewDecision` on GitHub). AO's verdicts live in `review_run` and are served by `GET /sessions/<id>/reviews`. Nothing connected the two, so the fact stayed `none` whenever the provider had no aggregate decision. GitHub leaves `reviewDecision` empty when the repo does not require reviews. That is the likely trigger for the report, but I did not confirm it on the reporter's repo.

`ao session ls` had a second gap: it takes the REVIEW value from `GET /sessions/<id>/pr` when that call succeeds, so a fix on the list route alone would not have reached the table.

## Before / After

Worker with one PR; the latest run on its head is `complete` / `approved`; the provider decision is `none`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /sessions?project=<id>`: `prs[0].review = "none"` | `prs[0].review = "approved"` |
| `ao session ls`: REVIEW `none` | REVIEW `approved` |
| New commit pushed after the approval: `none` | Still `none`; the approval was for the older head |

Verified with tests, not against a live daemon or the desktop app.

## How

`withReviewRunVerdicts` in `service/session/status.go` folds the runs into the reported facts at read time. Nothing new is stored. It uses the `ListCurrentHeadReviewRuns*` queries the Kanban reducer already reads: those match `target_sha = pr.head_sha` and keep the latest pass per harness, so stale runs and superseded retries never reach it, and running, failed and cancelled passes carry no verdict.

A pass can add to the provider's decision but not hide it:

| Provider | AO verdict on current head | Reported |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | approved | `approved` |
| any | changes requested (any reviewer) | `changes_requested` |
| `changes_requested` | approved | `changes_requested` |
| `review_required` | approved | `review_required` |

Keeping `review_required` is a deviation from a strict "same as the review runs" reading. The provider still requires a review, so reporting `approved` would tell a script the PR can merge when the provider will block it.

Reviewers should check these decisions:

- `status` and `scmStatus` still derive from the provider's decision alone, so the overlay is applied after them. `prPipelineStatus` reserves `changes_requested` for the provider's formal decision (#5765), and Kanban already reads runs separately. A session can therefore report `status: pr_open` with `review: approved`.
- `GET /sessions/<id>/pr` `review.decision` stays provider-only, as its contract type documents. The desktop and mobile merge gating reads it, and an AO `changes_requested` should not start disabling merge there. The daemon's own merge-readiness check reads a fresh provider observation and is not affected. `ao session ls` therefore prefers the list fact and falls back to the summary for a PR the list does not cover.
- The single-session read used to skip the runs query for terminated sessions while the list did not, so the two routes would have disagreed. The skip is removed, at the cost of one more query when reading a terminated session that has PRs.
- The claim response (`POST /sessions/<id>/pr/claim`) also uses `SessionPRFacts` but is unchanged, so it stays provider-only.

Client effects from `prs[].review` changing, read from the code and not exercised:

- `WorkerUpdates` shows "ready to merge" for an AO-approved PR with passing CI and no conflict.
- The inspector adds its `changes_requested` state for an AO verdict.
- `sessionPRFactToSummary` feeds the fact into merge gating only when the rich summary is missing, so an AO `changes_requested` can block merge in that fallback.

No field or struct tag changed, so `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` do not change.

## Testing

Regression tests were written first and failed on unmodified code:

- `TestSessionPRReviewReflectsCurrentHeadReviewRuns`: the precedence table above, on both the list and single read, plus `scmStatus` staying on the provider decision.
- `TestSessionPRReviewIgnoresRunsForAnEarlierHead`: against the real SQLite query, `approved` on `head1`, then `none` once the PR moves to `head2`.
- `TestSessionPRReviewReadsTheSameForATerminatedWorker`: list and single read agree.
- `TestSessionList_ReviewFollowsListFactsOverProviderSummary`: table and `--json`, including a PR only the summary covers.

`TestToSessionWithFactsAppliesAliasReviewVerdictToCanonicalPR` covers a run recorded under an older alias URL. It was added after the fix and fails when the overlay is removed. Restoring the terminated skip fails the terminated test on the single read.

Ran from `backend/`:

- `go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages, `gofmt -l`: clean.
- `go test ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/review/... ./internal/service/review/... ./pkg/contract/...`: all pass except `TestSearchWorkspaceContentCommonTermReachesLaterFiles`, which times out the same way on a clean export of the base commit on this Mac and does not touch this code.
- `go test -race` on the new and neighboring session tests and on `TestSessionList_*`: pass.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2 on `internal/service/session`, `internal/cli` and `internal/httpd/controllers` under Go 1.27.1 (the version in `go.mod`): 0 issues. The linter fails to typecheck under the Go 1.27.2 installed here, so I pinned `GOTOOLCHAIN`.

Not run locally: the full `go test ./...`, frontend and mobile checks (no frontend or mobile files changed), and the Windows/Linux runners.

title: fix(chat): stop offering retry for a sent message whose record was superseded
body:
Code changes: +39 -11\
Tests: +289 -0\
Others: +9 -0 (translation catalogs)

## What

When a message the daemon already accepted can't be recorded because its local delivery record was superseded, the composer now says the message was sent and no resend is needed, and it stops offering a retry. A real local storage failure keeps the existing retry wording and button.

## Why

`markChatComposerDeliveryAccepted` returned one generic failure for two different situations:

- **Storage failure:** the store can't be read or written. Retrying can work.
- **Superseded:** the session was reset elsewhere, another surface already cleared the delivery, or the record was corrupted. Retrying can't work.

Both showed "Message acceptance couldn't be recorded locally. Retry safely...". In the superseded case after a reset, the "Retry message safely" button then failed on every press with "Nothing was sent" until the surface re-keyed.

Every caller of this path already has proof the daemon holds the message: `onSend`/`onSteer` resolved, the journal says `accepted`, or the daemon reported the client message id. A resend gets a new client message id, which the backend can't dedupe, so the old advice could also deliver the message twice.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Session reset during delivery: red alert "Message acceptance couldn't be recorded locally. Retry safely to reconcile it with the same delivery ID." | Status notice: "Message was sent, but its local record had already been replaced or cleared, so it couldn't be updated. No resend is needed." |
| "Retry message safely" stays armed and the editor stays locked | No retry button; the editor is editable again |
| Sent steer text can stay in the editor, inviting a duplicate send | Sent text and attachments leave the editor |
| Leaving the chat prompts about an unsaved draft | No leave prompt, unless the user has unsaved text typed since |
| Storage read or write failure: retry wording and button | Unchanged |

The behavior comes from component tests. No screenshot is attached, because this state needs a session reset to land while a delivery is in flight, and that hasn't been captured in the real app.

## How

- `loadChatSessionDraft` failures now carry a `reason`: `superseded` when another incarnation owns the session, `storage` otherwise. A lease in `activating` for the same incarnation counts as `storage`, because that activation can still finish.
- `markChatComposerDeliveryAccepted` also returns `superseded` when the record loads but no longer holds the expected delivery, and `storage` when the write fails.
- `acceptAndClearDurableDelivery` handles `superseded` by applying the draft that is actually stored, through the existing `applyAcceptedDraftResult`. This releases the retry pin and shows any newer draft from another surface.
- If the surface has already re-keyed to the replacement incarnation, it leaves that draft and delivery alone and only shows the notice.
- The key `chat.draft.recordMessageSuperseded` is added to all 9 locale catalogs.

This builds on the review of the closed #6159, written from current `main`. Three differences from what that review suggested:

- **Wording:** the copy doesn't state the session was reset, because the same reason covers a delivery cleared elsewhere and a corrupted record.
- **Notice slot:** the message uses the `role="status"` notice slot, not `textDraftPersistenceError`. An error there would arm the `persistence-failed` leave prompt once `durableDelivery` is released, and nothing is left to save.
- **No `synchronouslyClearedDeliveryRevision`:** that ref only matters while `durableDelivery` is still set, and this path releases it.

Intentional omission: inline edits have the same collapsed failure (`markChatInlineEditDeliveryAccepted`, `chat.draft.recordEditFailed`). This PR leaves them unchanged to stay on the composer issue.

## Testing

Run from `frontend/`:

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/lib/chat-drafts.test.ts src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.test.tsx`: 263 passed. The new reason and composer tests failed on the unmodified code. The existing "preserves safe retry when recording acceptance fails" test still passes for both read and write failures.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts`: the touched suites and i18n tests passed, with 167 failures in 35 other files on a heavily loaded machine (load average about 120). Most were 20s timeouts.
  - Re-running 34 of those files with `--maxWorkers=3`: 1759 passed, 0 failed.
  - The 35th, `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`, needs native bindings that were missing because dependencies were installed with `--ignore-scripts`. It wasn't re-run and this change doesn't touch it.

Not run locally: the rest of the CI `checks` job (Electron boundary tests, docs, packages). This change doesn't touch those areas, so they rely on CI.

title: fix(chat): record why an ACP turn failed on its stop reason
body:
Code changes: +25 -0\
Tests: +57 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When an ACP turn ends on a failing stop reason, the turn now records why it failed.

## Why

`turnState()` marks a turn as failed when its stop reason is `max_tokens`, `max_turn_requests`, `refusal` or an unknown value. When no provider binding supplied an error, the turn was stored with an empty `error_message`. The timeline then showed only "The agent ran into a problem", with no cause.

#7589 moved this gap into its own issue. That PR changes the SQLite store and does not touch this code path.

Fixes #7775

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Turn ending on `max_tokens`: failed, `error_message` empty, timeline shows the generic "The agent ran into a problem" | Failed with title "The agent reached its output token limit" and detail "Stop reason: max_tokens" |

The same applies to `max_turn_requests` ("The agent reached its request limit for this turn"), `refusal` ("The agent refused to continue") and any other failing reason ("The agent stopped before finishing the turn").

## How

- In `finishPrompt`, if the turn is failed and `turnErr` is still nil, attach `stopReasonFailure(resp.StopReason)`, which is built with `ports.NewChatProviderFailure`. An error from a provider binding still takes precedence.
- The detail line is left out when the stop reason is empty.
- Stop reasons that settle the turn normally (`end_turn`, `cancelled`) carry no error.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/` passes. New tests: `TestFailingStopReasonRecordsWhyTheTurnFailed` and `TestSettledStopReasonsCarryNoError`.
- Not tested: a reproduction with a real agent. The only ACP agent on this machine (gemini) is not signed in, so the tests drive the stop reasons through the fake ACP agent used in `prompt_failure_test.go`.
- `TestACPReplayLoadLargeHistoryThroughSDK` is flaky on `main` locally too and is unrelated to this change.

title: feat(cloud): create cloud workspaces and upload local folders to them
body:
## Summary
Desktop half of cloud **workspaces**. It needs the control plane change in OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#49.

**Creating a workspace**
- Creating a cloud project can now make a workspace (`config.layout: "workspace"`): pick GitHub repositories and local folders, each checked out in its own folder of the workspace (`CloudWorkspaceCard`).
- The cloud project setup moves out of `CreateProjectFlow` into `CloudProjectSetup` (a move, behaviour unchanged for local import, GitHub repository and standalone projects).
- While a workspace is creating (uploads can take minutes), Escape and outside clicks don't close the dialog, and nothing runs for a card that has unmounted.

**Uploading a local folder** (`main/cloud-folder-push.ts`, `lib/cloud-folder-upload.ts`)
- The control plane creates (or connects) an empty private repository (`POST /orgs/{orgId}/github/repositories`). The main process then pushes the folder to the returned `pushPath` over git smart HTTP.
- The member's bearer token goes to git through environment config only (`http.<url>.extraHeader`). It never reaches the renderer, the command line or the folder's `.git/config`; any `extraHeader` from the user's own git config is cleared first, `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` and git tracing are dropped, and TLS verification is forced for the push URL.
- Only a folder picked in the app's folder dialog, requested from the app's own shell window, can be uploaded.
- A folder that's already a git repository uploads the commits of its checked-out branch, and the row names that branch (or "the checked-out commit" when detached; linked worktrees count). Any other folder is imported (its `.gitignore` applies), dated by its newest file, so retrying an unchanged folder after a lost reply finds it already uploaded.
- Refused before uploading, with a clear reason: nested git repositories or submodules, shallow clones, Git LFS, files over GitHub's 100 MB, imports over 1.5 GB, history over the control plane's 2 GB.
- Errors, translated per code (with git's or the main process's words as detail where they add something):

  | Error | What the user sees |
  |---|---|
  | `repository_owner_required` | owner picker |
  | missing or ineligible GitHub installation | Connect GitHub card |
  | push gets 401 (git: "could not read Username") | signed out, sign-in prompt |
  | push gets 403/404 | no access |
  | branch exists (control plane's "already exists", or git's "fetch first") | branch exists |
  | GitHub refuses `.github/workflows` changes | workflows explained |
  | other create errors | message, then retry |

**Settings**
- "Add a local folder" to an existing workspace, with a rename + Upload/Cancel step; a retry reuses a repository already created.
- The planned repository is checked against the workspace (limit, duplicates, the main repository, reserved folders) **before** it is created, and saved into the workspace as soon as it's uploaded, so leaving Settings never strands a filled repository. Settings stays open while an upload runs; a 401 asks to sign in.
- Settings writes never send `layout` (the control plane refuses any PATCH naming it), and `updateProjectSettings` strips it as a safeguard.

**Contract** (`contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, `schema.ts` regenerated): `createGitHubRepository` with its refusal codes, 502 `SCM_BROKER_FAILED`, the push limits of `pushPath`; `ProjectLayout`; description `maxLength: 350`.

## Merged main
`upstream/main` (up to 05436d27d4) is merged in. Conflicts in `preload.ts`, `bridge.ts` and `test/setup.ts` were both-sides additions (kept both). In `CreateProjectFlow.tsx`, main's edits to the cloud setup this PR moves into `CloudProjectSetup` were carried over there. The workspace code follows main's #7903 (icons from `components/app-icons`), #7999 (secondary instead of outline buttons) and #7685 ("Orchestrator" / "Orchestrator Cloud" instead of "AO" in app text, all nine catalogs).

## Known limitations
- A **changed** folder retried after a push whose reply was lost fails with `branch_exists`; the message tells the user to remove the folder and add its repository from GitHub instead. (A git folder's same commit, or an unchanged imported folder, retries fine.)
- Removing a folder after its repository was created leaves an empty private repository on GitHub.
- Uploads can't be cancelled mid-push; the dialog stays open until they finish.
- The control plane's own error messages from `createGitHubRepository` are shown as it sends them (English).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run cloud:check` steps (generate + no drift, typecheck, 31 tests); `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh` ok
- [x] Workspace suites: 14 files, 411 tests (folder push, folder upload, workspace card, layout settings, CreateProjectFlow incl. Escape mid-upload, useWorkspaceQuery, cloud-cp client, cloud project repos, i18n, SettingsDialog, CloudProjectSettingsForm)
- [x] `cloud-folder-push.test.ts` (34) runs real git: 401/403/404/fetch-first/GH001/workflow mapping, same-commit retry, shallow clone, submodules, LFS (repository and import), file size, token kept off unverified TLS and traces, IPC only from the shell for a picked folder, stale-only import cleanup
- [x] **End to end, locally:** this push code with real git against the control plane's routes (#49's handler harness over a real `git http-backend`): create 201, git folder push, same-commit retry, `branch_exists`, plain-folder import honouring `.gitignore`, `signed_out` for an invalid token, `push_forbidden` for a repository not created for the workspace, clone refused
- [x] Full renderer suite: 12343 passed, 16 failed in 4 files this PR doesn't touch or import: `remote-proxy` and `cloud-agent-proxy` (`server.shouldUpgradeCallback is not a function`, the local Node's HTTP API), `ContextMeter` and `ChatWorkspace` (this machine's `en_IN` number formatting / a timeout). Not rerun on `main`.
- [x] All new strings translated in the 9 locales
- [ ] Not yet tried against a deployed control plane

## Review fixes (re-review at 0938e5c364)
**Which files count as secrets** (`main/cloud-folder-push.ts` `secretPathKind`, `contentHoldsSecret`). Before this, any `.npmrc`, `*.pem` or `*.key` anywhere in a repository's history got the folder refused, and an import always left `.npmrc` out. The new rule:
- Still refused by name, whatever they contain: `.env*` (except `.example`/`.sample`/`.template`), `*.p12`/`*.pfx` (key stores hold private keys by design), SSH private keys, `.netrc`, `.pypirc`, `.git-credentials`, cloud credential JSON, and anything under `.ssh`/`.aws`/`.gnupg`.
- `.npmrc` counts as a secret only when it sets `_authToken`, `_auth` or `_password` (plain or `//registry/:`-scoped) to a real value. A value that only names an environment variable (`${NPM_TOKEN}`, the usual CI setup) is not a secret, and neither are comments or registry/engine settings.
- `*.pem`/`*.key` count as secrets when they hold a `PRIVATE` PEM block, or anything other than public PEM blocks (a binary or headerless key counts). So certificates, CA bundles and public keys go through. A private key is refused **wherever it sits, `test/fixtures` included**: its path doesn't tell us whether the key is real. I didn't add an override, because the escape hatch already exists: push the repository yourself and add it from GitHub.
- History checks read every version of such a file that was added or changed. An import checks the file on disk, then reads it again after `git add`, so a file that gained a credential in between is refused.

**Folder upload, main process**
- The history scan now streams (`spawn`) instead of buffering `git log` under 64 MB, and reads merges against each parent (`-m`), so a file added only in a merge commit is caught.
- When the upload runs right after its preview, it skips the history checks for a commit that passed them in the last 10 minutes. Those checks depend only on the commit, which can't change. A folder that moved to a new commit is checked again in full, and the shallow-clone check still runs every time. Import files are `lstat`ed 32 at a time.
- If git can't read a `.git` (dubious ownership, broken gitdir), the folder is refused with git's message. Before, it silently fell back to importing the working tree.
- The preview now returns the checked-out branch.
- If `getToken` throws, the result is `signed_out`. `http.followRedirects` is now scoped to the push URL, like the token header.

**Renderer**
- Whether a folder uploads its commits or its files, and which branch, now comes only from the main process's preview. The scan is only used for the origin, and the two run in parallel.
- Workspace card: Create stays disabled while a folder dialog is open. The dialog doesn't block the window, so before this a folder picked after Create was silently left out.
- Settings › Add a local folder: shows "Checking <folder>" while it checks and stays disabled while picking or checking. Before, repeat clicks started parallel full scans.
- Settings: the workspace page label now comes from the project itself (`getProject`, the same cached query the page uses) instead of the active org's first 100 projects.

**Not changed:** the folder dialog is still not attached to the app window. `main.ts` avoids that on purpose because of a white flash on Windows, and on macOS it would turn every folder picker in the app into a sheet. The renderer guards above close the race either way.

title: fix(chat): show Worked for on every turn and settle it without a jump
body:
Code changes: +221 -124\
Tests: +235 -37\
Others: +1 -0 (DESIGN.md decision log)

## What

Every finished chat turn now opens with **Worked for 12s**, including a quick answer that ran no tools. A turn with steps keeps the fold and its chevron. A turn without steps gets the same words as plain text: no chevron, no hover, nothing to click. The time no longer moves down to the answer's copy / undo row.

The handover when a turn finishes (the live row under the streaming reply goes away, "Worked for" appears above the reply) and opening or closing "Worked for" no longer jump. The prompt and the scroll position hold still. The reply slides up into the room its steps left, and the live row fades out where it was.

## Why

The time sat in two places: at the top of turns that had work to fold, and at the end of the action row of turns that didn't. Readers saw "Worked for 3m" on one reply and a bare "5s" next to copy on the next.

The settle handover glitched. Sampling every frame in a real browser on `main`:

- **The chat dipped and glided back.** The steps fold away in one commit, before the prompt spacer can grow back to absorb them. A reader following the end (the normal case while watching a turn) had no settle fix-up, only a reader who had scrolled up did. The browser clamped the scroll and the follow glided it back: the prompt and everything above it dropped 96 px for a frame in a short chat. In a windowed chat (over 20 turns) the virtualizer's end anchoring pulled it 102 px and it glided back over about 200 ms.
- **The live row teleported.** `AnimatePresence mode="popLayout"` absolutely positions the leaving row, but the turn column had no positioned ancestor inside the scroller, so the fading orb row landed about 230 px lower (the scroll offset) while it faded.
- **10 px bump.** The reserved row under the prompt shrank while "Worked for" grew from zero, but the turn's 10 px row gap applied to the new row at once, so the reply jumped down 10 px and crept back.
- **Windowed collapse drifted and snapped.** Collapsing a fold in the latest turn of a windowed chat clamped the view to the stale list height on every frame (the virtualizer learns the new height a frame before React draws it, and the spacer waits for the two to agree), then snapped 32 px when the animation ended.

## Before / After

| Before (`main`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| A turn with no tools: no "Worked for"; the time is a bare `5s` after copy and undo | "Worked for 5s" above the reply as plain text, no chevron; copy and undo only |
| Turn finishes, short chat: prompt jumps 96 px for a frame | Prompt and scroll position constant on every frame |
| Turn finishes, windowed chat: whole chat drops 102 px and glides back over ~200 ms; "Worked for" opens squished from zero height | Same: nothing above the reply moves; "Worked for" fades in at full height in the reserved row |
| Fading live row jumps ~230 px down | Fades where it was |
| Reply bumps 10 px down then creeps back | Reply slides up 102 px from where it was to its place, ease-out, 240 ms |
| Windowed chat, collapsing "Worked for": reply drifts the wrong way, then snaps 32 px | Reply eases up; scroll position constant |

## How

- **Label vs fold** (`TurnWorkSummary`). Without children it renders the same 28 px box and text edge as the trigger, but as plain text. `showsWorked` now holds for any settled turn with a duration, except the orchestrator's quiet worker replies and read-only worker turns, which already fold their work elsewhere. `durationMs` is gone from `TurnActions`, `TurnOutcome`, `AssistantMessage` and `TimelineItem`, along with the standalone `TurnDuration` variant.
- **Handover without a height dance.** The reserved row is a plain 28 px div, replaced in the same slot by "Worked for", which only fades in (240 ms). Only one is ever in the DOM, so the row gap counts once.
- **Settle snapshot for every reader** (`captureSettle` / `restoreSettle`, still inside the same commit via `TurnSettleSnapshot`). Before paint it:
  - leaves the popped live row out of layout (`display: none` for the measurement) so it can't prop up `scrollHeight`;
  - in a windowed chat, feeds the virtualizer the turn's new height (`resizeItem`) and writes the list height now;
  - sizes the spacer, then holds the view: a reader following the end keeps their `scrollTop`, clamped to the end only when the spacer can't absorb the shrink (a reply taller than the viewport). A reader who scrolled up keeps the existing anchor-and-hold logic.
  - FLIPs every row that still moved on screen (WAAPI `translateY`, 240 ms, the chat's existing ease-out). The live row gets a constant transform, so it stays put on screen while it fades.

  Reduced motion skips the slides and the fade.
- **Windowed fold resizes** (`scrollToFn`, `onChange`). While the spacer under the latest prompt is open and the reader follows the end, size changes in that turn are the spacer's to take, as they already are without windowing: the virtualizer's end-anchoring write is skipped for that measure only (flag set in `measureElement`, cleared in a microtask). When the virtualizer learns a new total, the list height is written in the same frame and the spacer re-synced: always while following the end, and while reading back only when the shrink would otherwise clamp the view.
- `TurnGroup`'s column is `relative`, so popLayout positions the leaving row inside the turn.

**Changed behavior to review:** `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` "preserves the spacer and bottom anchor during a disclosure resize" asserted the old windowed behavior: spacer untouched, virtualizer shifts `scrollTop` by the delta. That is the end-anchoring that produced the drift-then-snap above, so the test now asserts the spacer takes the change and only the remainder changes the scroll range (`lets the prompt spacer take a disclosure resize…`). It fails on `main`.

## Testing

- New `e2e/chat-turn-settle.spec.ts` (`@T0`, real renderer in Chrome, fake agent): samples every animation frame of the finish handover in a short and a windowed chat, a straight answer, and opening and closing "Worked for" in a windowed chat. It checks that the prompt and `scrollTop` never move, the reply only rises during the settle, and the live row fades in place. 4/4 pass. On an untouched export of `main` it fails where the recordings did: `scrollTop` 235 → 139 → 235 (short chat), 17254 → 17154 → … → 17254 over ~200 ms (windowed), and no "Worked for" on a straight answer.
- Also recorded by hand at the same level of detail: a reply taller than the viewport (no prompt spacer). The reply stays put on screen and the end holds.
- `vitest run src/renderer/components/chat`: 1685/1686 pass. The one failure, `IndependentSideCreation.test.tsx` "keeps native focus outside the side composer…", flakes under full-folder load and passes alone (14/14), as it did before this change.
- Updated: the Worked-for and action-row duration tests in `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` and `ChatTimelineItems.test.tsx`, the windowed disclosure-resize test (see How), and the `ChatLiveTurn.test.tsx` layout stub.
- `tsgo --noEmit` and `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.e2e.json` on the exported commit: clean.
- **Not completed locally:** the full `vitest run` was stopped partway. Failures up to that point were the machine-only `src/main` ones (`browser-profile-import` on the `better-sqlite3` ABI, `remote-proxy` "verifies the host once per upstream session"). The full renderer smoke (`@T0|@P0`) and the Go jobs were not run locally (no Go or backend files changed). CI covers them.
- Not checked in the Electron app against a live agent turn: all of the above ran the renderer in Chrome with a stubbed conversation.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

## Problem

The default light theme looked gray and flat next to apps like Devin, Claude and ChatGPT. The canvas was `oklch(0.97)`, the sidebar `0.95`, and the composer was a gray fill (`0.935`) with no edge, so it looked disabled instead of being the main action. Default light tokens (`styles/tokens.css`):

Not changed: dark, the catalog palettes themselves, the accent color, the sent-message bubble and the active sidebar row (they keep their gray fills, which now read as subtle on the lighter canvas).

title: fix(desktop): move the shared project tile into the session header
body:
## Problem

On a shared project's orchestrator, the "Shared project / N pull requests" tile floated over the top right of the conversation (and of the terminal, for a terminal-mode orchestrator). It covered the first right-aligned user message (a "hi" bubble sat under the tile's text) and anything that scrolled beneath it.

## Fix

The tile is now a header control beside Share, built from the existing primitives:
- `TopbarButton` with the people icon and the pull request summary as its label ("0 pull requests", "2 pull requests · 1 to approve"); its accessible name and tooltip are "Shared project: ...".
- It is a `data-priority="secondary"` control, so at narrow widths the label compacts to the icon, as Open Kanban does.
- The list (who opened each pull request, merge requests, approve and reject) is unchanged and opens in a portaled, end-aligned `Popover` with a "Shared project" header row; Escape and outside clicks close it.
- A merge request waiting on the owner keeps a dot on the icon, so it stays visible when the label is compacted. Guests get no dot.

- It shows only once the project has a pull request or a merge request. A shared project with none shows nothing in the header (no "0 pull requests"). If it hides while its list is open (the last pull request closed), it closes, so it does not pop open on its own later.

- Also fixes a test leak that can fail a vitest shard on any PR: the Teams people field's 120ms blur timer kept running after the field unmounted ("window is not defined" from `ShareSessionDialog.people.test`). It is now cleared on unmount, with a test.

Nothing renders over the conversation or terminal any more. Otherwise who sees the control is unchanged: a Cloud orchestrator of a project with participants.

## Screenshots

Dark theme, the dev app against staging, cropped to the session pane. The orchestrator's first message is "hi". The pull request is a stub written into the renderer's query cache so the populated state can be shown; nothing was opened on GitHub.

title: Artifacts list shows every file in the artifact dir (assets, bundle internals, variants) as a separate artifact
body:
## Summary

Every regular file a worker writes anywhere under its session artifact directory shows up as a separate artifact in the UI. A deliverable that ships with supporting files therefore floods the artifact list. In one real session the user saw **68 artifacts**, where the worker had reported only 5 as deliverables.

## What happened

A design worker (a brand board, then a Liquid Glass app-icon page) was told to put its deliverable plus an `/assets` folder into its artifact directory. The pages load images through relative links, so the worker kept those files next to them. It also kept export variants and a few test inputs. The artifact directory ended up holding:

- the deliverables: 2 HTML pages, 1 Markdown doc, 2 screenshots
- files the pages link to: 9 print images, icon PNGs, and smaller 512 px web copies of the renders
- export variants: 1024 px icon renders for each appearance and 64@2x Dock sizes
- `.icon` bundles, which are directories, so `icon.json` and the SVG inside each one count as separate artifacts
- a few test or placeholder files that should have gone to temp (worker error, see below)

Through `ao report --artifact` the worker reported only these 5 files: `brand.html`, `BRAND.md`, `brand-board.png`, `glass.html`, `glass-page.png`. The UI listed all 68 anyway.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/sessionartifacts/sessionartifacts.go` → `List()` walks the whole artifact directory recursively. It returns every regular file and skips only `.versions/`, symlinks and `ignored()` names. Nothing in the listing uses the artifacts a worker has reported. The prompt rule ("only finished deliverables and files a deliverable needs") also can't prevent this. A page's linked assets legitimately belong in the folder, yet each one still becomes a top-level artifact.

## Contributing factors

- **Worker error.** Some files were working material and should have gone to the system temp directory: unused placeholder renders, test `.icon` bundles, an unrequested mark PNG. Better prompts alone won't fix the flooding, because the legitimate assets also show up.
- **Contradicting requests.** Task requests often explicitly ask for an "/assets" folder or "export the PNGs". That works against "prefer one consolidated deliverable".
- **Invisible effect.** Nothing tells the worker that each file on disk becomes a user-visible artifact.

## Suggested direction (for discussion)

1. **Primary vs supporting.** Treat files reported via `ao report --artifact` (or files at the root of the artifact directory) as primary artifacts. Show nested files, such as `assets/**`, as attachments of the primary that links them, or behind a collapsed "supporting files" group.
2. **Bundles.** Treat directory bundles (`*.icon`, `*.app`, `*.bundle`, `*.xcassets`) as a single artifact.
3. **Worker guidance.** Tell the worker how its files will be listed: either state in the prompt that every file becomes an artifact, or say that only root and reported files are primary.
4. **Optional cap.** Warn the worker (`ao report` output) when its artifact directory grows past N files.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A session with one HTML deliverable plus 50 linked images in `assets/` shows one primary artifact, with the images grouped or collapsed.
- [ ] An `.icon` or other bundle directory is listed as one artifact.
- [ ] Reported artifacts (`ao report --artifact`) are what the artifacts list highlights.

Related: #4803, #4804 (Session Artifacts V1), #6573 (artifact versioning), #5895.

title: Windows: keep agents running in the background when the window closes (system tray)
body:
## Problem

On Windows, closing the AO window quits the app. You cannot close only the window and keep the orchestrator and workers running, as you can on macOS.

- The tray is enabled only on macOS: `isTrayEnabled` returns `platform === "darwin"` (`frontend/src/main/tray-lifecycle.ts:5`).
- When the last window closes, `window-all-closed` calls `app.quit()` on every platform except macOS (`frontend/src/main.ts:4057`).
- The "close the window, keep running" quit handling is also macOS-only (`frontend/src/main/desktop-quit.ts:18`).

Today this full quit stops the app-owned daemon, and the agent processes keep running without a daemon. When #7183 lands, a full desktop quit also stops every agent. On Windows, closing the window will then stop all agents.

## Expected behaviour (same as macOS)

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Close the window | The daemon, orchestrators and workers keep running. The tray icon stays. |
| Tray → Quit AO Completely | The daemon and all agents stop (#7183). Sessions stay resumable. |
| Daemon restart or app update | Agents keep running and the new daemon adopts them. |
| Open AO again (Start menu or tray click) | The window opens on the running daemon. |

## Notes

- Electron's `Tray` works in the Windows notification area. The macOS tray uses template images (`setTemplateImage`, `frontend/src/main/tray.ts:58`). Windows needs a full-colour `.ico`.
- Windows puts new tray icons in the overflow menu by default. Show a notice on the first close ("AO is still running in the background") so users do not think it quit.
- Replace the three macOS-only checks above with one shared platform check.

title: Linux: keep agents running in the background when the window closes
body:
## Problem

On Linux, closing the AO window quits the app. You cannot close only the window and keep the orchestrator and workers running, as you can on macOS.

- The tray is enabled only on macOS: `isTrayEnabled` returns `platform === "darwin"` (`frontend/src/main/tray-lifecycle.ts:5`).
- When the last window closes, `window-all-closed` calls `app.quit()` on every platform except macOS (`frontend/src/main.ts:4057`).
- The "close the window, keep running" quit handling is also macOS-only (`frontend/src/main/desktop-quit.ts:18`).

Today this full quit stops the app-owned daemon, and the agent processes keep running without a daemon. When #7183 lands, a full desktop quit also stops every agent. On Linux, closing the window will then stop all agents.

## Expected behaviour (same as macOS)

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Close the window | The daemon, orchestrators and workers keep running. |
| Quit AO Completely (tray or app menu) | The daemon and all agents stop (#7183). Sessions stay resumable. |
| Daemon restart or app update | Agents keep running and the new daemon adopts them. |
| Open AO again (launcher or tray click) | The window opens on the running daemon. |

## Notes

- Tray support on Linux depends on the desktop environment. Electron's `Tray` uses StatusNotifierItem/AppIndicator. KDE, XFCE, Cinnamon and Ubuntu's GNOME show it. Stock GNOME, as on Fedora, shows no tray without an extension.
- So background mode must work without a visible tray. Opening AO again must bring the window back, and Quit AO Completely must also be in the app menu.
- The macOS tray uses template images (`setTemplateImage`, `frontend/src/main/tray.ts:58`). Linux needs a full-colour PNG.
- AO ships AppImage, deb and rpm builds (`frontend/forge.config.ts`). Test at least on GNOME (with and without the AppIndicator extension) and KDE.

title: feat(artifacts): zoom and pan, a file menu for the viewer's actions, open in browser
body:
Code changes: +1220 -113\
Tests: +423 -10\
Others: +45 -0 (translations in 9 locales)

## What

Three changes to the artifact viewer (inspector and full screen), for local and cloud sessions:

1. **Zoom and pan.** Trackpad pinch zooms around the cursor. A floating `− 100% +` toolbar sits over the bottom of the preview (click the percentage to fit). Cmd+= / Cmd+- / Cmd+0 work too (Ctrl elsewhere). Range is 25%–500%. Two-finger scroll pans when zoomed, and images can also be dragged. The toolbar shows only when the file can zoom, and fades out after 1.5 s idle. It comes back on any zoom or when the pointer nears the bottom edge.
2. **A cleaner header.** The header keeps only back, the file's name menu, Share and full screen (plus Cancel/Save while editing). Everything else moved into the name menu:
   - page or source (HTML)
   - display mode (file or rendered)
   - Edit
   - Add feedback
   - Open in AO Browser
   - History
   - then the existing file actions: Show in Finder/Terminal, copy, download, delete
3. **Open in browser.** A new name-menu item opens the file in the system default browser. It shows for HTML, SVG, and every image, video, audio and PDF format the viewer previews.

## Why

Artifacts couldn't be zoomed, and pinching over them did nothing. The header had grown a row of icon buttons that duplicated or crowded the file menu. A file couldn't be opened in a real browser.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: image, no zoom](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/3010700bb01e4899e10d9e07c18a01b1/raw/before-image.png) | ![After: image pinched to 261%, floating toolbar](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/3010700bb01e4899e10d9e07c18a01b1/raw/after-image.png) |
| PDF had no zoom | ![After: PDF at 190%, redrawn sharp](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/3010700bb01e4899e10d9e07c18a01b1/raw/pdf-pinch.png) |
| HTML page had no zoom | ![After: full-screen page pinched to 190%](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/3010700bb01e4899e10d9e07c18a01b1/raw/after-html-fullscreen-pinch.png) |
| Markdown had no zoom | ![After: Markdown at 200% with horizontal pan](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/3010700bb01e4899e10d9e07c18a01b1/raw/md-zoom.png) |
| Header: rendered/source, Open in AO Browser, Edit, Add feedback as icon buttons | Header: back, name menu, Share, full screen; those actions are rows in the name menu |

The four zoom captures were taken before the header moved into the menu, so their headers still show the old icon buttons. The zoom behavior in them is current.

## How

**Zoom** (`lib/artifact-zoom.ts`): a per-view store kept outside React state, so a pinch tick doesn't re-render the view. Whichever renderer is showing registers as the target.
- Electron delivers a trackpad pinch as `wheel` with `ctrlKey`. The viewer calls `preventDefault` and zooms the artifact, never the app. `wheelZoomFactor` follows Chromium's pinch scale, with a Ctrl+mouse-wheel notch capped at about 1.28×.
- **Images:** transform anchored at the cursor. Pan is bounded by the image's fitted (object-contain) size × zoom, and an axis that still fits stays centered.
- **PDFs:** zoom multiplies pdf.js's fit scale, so text stays sharp and selectable. Pages redraw into an offscreen canvas 150 ms after zooming stops, so they never go blank. The anchor keeps its page and its position within that page; page heights scale, the 12 px gaps don't.
- **Local HTML pages:** the page is a cross-origin iframe. `render_bootstrap.js` gets an opt-in bridge: once the host sends `zoomable`, the page forwards Ctrl+wheel, Cmd+=/-/0, and "pointer near the bottom edge" as `ao/zoom` messages. It then applies the host's zoom as a root transform anchored at the pinch. Chat renders never opt in.
- **Cloud HTML pages:** the control plane serves them from an opaque origin with no bridge. The frame gets a viewport of pane size ÷ zoom and is scaled back up, so the page re-lays out like browser zoom and pans with its own scroll. A pinch inside a cloud page doesn't reach the viewer; the toolbar and shortcuts do.
- **Text documents** (Markdown, code, CSV, SVG, Mermaid): transform on the content, panned with the pane's scrollbars. Off while editing.
- **Shortcuts:** while a viewer that can zoom is under the pointer or holds focus (including inside a framed page), the main process claims Cmd+=/-/0 in `before-input-event`, ahead of the app menu's View zoom, and sends them to the viewer. This is the same path a focused terminal uses for its font size. Elsewhere the chords are the app's zoom as before.
- **Toolbar:** same surface as the dropdown menus, with a 150 ms fade that is skipped under reduced motion. It stays while hovered or focused. While hidden it still takes the pointer, so hovering its spot brings it back over any page.

**Header → menu:** `FileContentPane` takes an optional `menuActions` registry. With it, the pane publishes its display modes, Edit and Add feedback instead of portaling buttons, and keeps only Cancel/Save in the header. The name menu reads the registry each time it opens. Display modes, and page vs. source, are radio rows. Workspace Files views don't pass the registry and are unchanged.

**Open in browser:**
- **Local:** new `editorHandoff:openArtifactInBrowser` IPC, with the same shell-sender check as the others. It resolves the path through `artifactFilePath` (realpath-confined to the artifact dir).
- **Cloud:** extends `cloudArtifact:openFolder` with `open: "browser"`. It copies the session's files into a separate `<session>.browser` folder under `~/.ao/cloud-artifacts`, so a page's own files load, then opens the copied file. Only the page must copy (siblings are best effort), a failure names the file, and the item is disabled while it runs. Like the cloud Show in Finder, it's offered only to the session's owner.
- **Shared rule:** both paths use `isBrowserArtifactPath`, checked on the requested and the resolved path. The file opens with the default `https` handler (`open -a` on macOS, the browser exe on Windows), so a PNG goes to the browser, not Preview. Other platforms fall back to `shell.openExternal`.

## Testing

No local typecheck or test runs; CI verifies. Tests added or updated:
- `artifact-zoom` controls and fade (`SessionArtifactsView.test.tsx`), including reveal over a framed page
- image pan bounds (`ZoomableImage.test.tsx`)
- PDF anchoring on page 51 and inside a gap (`PdfPreview.test.ts`)
- the shared browser-format rule (`browser-artifact.test.ts`)
- local open-in-browser containment (`editor-handoff.test.ts`)
- cloud open-in-browser (`cloud-artifact-ipc.test.ts` and the view test)
- the menu moves: page/source radio rows, Add feedback, Open in AO Browser

Manual, in the dev desktop app (isolated data, an HTML/PDF/PNG/Markdown artifact):
- CDP Ctrl+wheel over a page zoomed the artifact, not the app.
- Image, PDF and Markdown zoom and pan.
- The floating toolbar shows and hides.
- Open in browser and Show in Finder open the file.

Not checked by hand: a physical trackpad pinch, the native-menu Cmd+= path, the final menu layout, and cloud sessions (no cloud account in the dev app).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in with screenshots
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (pending)

title: fix(desktop): every Cloud model picker uses Cloud's own model list
body:
## Problem

Cloud project settings listed this computer's models, not the ones the account can run in Cloud. A project could be saved with a model the Cloud account does not offer (seen in prod: `claude-opus-5-5`), and every task on it then failed. The New Task composer and its agent switch also mixed local and Cloud catalogs, and a model picked for a local project carried into a Cloud one.

## Fix (every harness, every provider)

- **One source for every Cloud model picker.** `useCloudModelCatalog` is the one query for Cloud's model list of an account and agent, used by the New Task composer, its agent switch, and Cloud project settings. It is keyed by the account's credential (a new sign-in asks again), re-read on focus, and every 15s while only the release list is known, so the account's own list shows as soon as the control plane learns it.
- **Same rule as the server.** `cloudModelVerdict` mirrors the control plane's `modelcatalog.Offers` (case, bracketed variants such as `sonnet[1m]`, dated releases). A model the account's own list lacks is never picked by default (project model, remembered pick, kept choices). The composer and settings say so plainly. The release list alone raises no warning, because the account may still run the model.
- **Local and Cloud picks stay apart.** A pick made for a local project is parked, not carried into a Cloud project, and comes back when you return.
- **No send on a model Cloud refuses.** With ao-control-plane#51, Cloud refuses an explicit model the account's own list lacks (422 `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`), so the composer keeps its warning and disables Start until another model is picked. The release list alone never disables it.
- **Fresh after a session lists models.** A session's own model list refreshes every open Cloud list for that account and agent.
- **Same alias rule as the server.** Claude Code lists its current models only as aliases (`opus`, described "Opus 5.5 · ..."). `cloudCatalogOffers` now also offers:
  - a dated release of a listed undated ID;
  - `opusplan` when `opus` is listed;
  - a full ID such as `claude-opus-5-5` through an alias, but only when the account's provider confirmed it: some entry's `providerId` is that model. An `opus` entry with no `providerId` (the prod case) does not offer it, so the composer warns and keeps Start disabled.

  A list without `providerId` (stored before ao-control-plane#51) keeps the description rule. It is tested on the same real staging lists as the server.
- **Contract.** `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` gains the optional fields the control plane now sends: `ChatModel.providerId` and `sessionOnly`, and `ChatModelsResponse.sessionOnlyMarked`. The Cloud client `schema.ts` is regenerated with its pinned generator. oasdiff reports no breaking change.
- **The Chat says when a session runs the default.** When a session starts on the agent's default because the account lacks the project's model, the control plane now serves `session.model_unavailable`. The Cloud Chat shows it once, outside any turn: "claude-opus-5-5 isn't available to your Claude Code account on Cloud, so this session uses the default model." It is translated in all 9 locales. Older desktops skip the event, since it has no text.
- From the live check: no Retry beside a "model isn't available" notice, since re-reading cannot fix it (Retry stays for a failed list read). In settings, the warning takes its own line under the agent and model pickers, which stay side by side.

- **CI flake fixed at the root.** The renderer smoke spec `model-menu-scroll` failed about 1 run in 5 on main (and failed this PR's first CI run). Cause: Radix starts a 100ms hover-open timer when the pointer moves onto a submenu trigger and does not cancel it when a click opens the submenu, so a choice made inside that window (click Model, search, Enter) closed the submenu and the stale timer reopened it. `OptionMenuSub` now reopens a submenu a selection closed only when its trigger is asked again (click, key, or a real pointer move). New unit test reproduces it with fake timers; the spec passes 40 of 40 runs (was 25 of 40).

Server side: OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#51 learns every user's list from their sessions and starts a session on the default when the project's model is not on the account's list. This PR works against the current control plane too (no contract change).

## Tests

- New: `lib/cloud-model-catalog.test.ts`, `hooks/useCloudModelCatalog.test.tsx`. New cases in `TaskComposer.test`, `CloudProjectSettingsForm.test`, `CloudSessionChatSurface.test`, `AgentSwitchPicker.test`, `NewChatPage.test`. Each new case was checked to fail without its change.
- Review round:
  - The real staging lists (`cloudCatalogOffers on the real staging lists`, 25 cases plus `claudeModelName`).
  - The provider-confirmed rule (`cloudCatalogOffers on a list carrying the provider's models`, 17 cases plus the verdict for the prod case).
  - The Chat notice (`CloudSessionChatSurface.test`).
  - Removing the alias rule fails 6 tests; ignoring `providerId` fails 4.
  - Cloud client: `npm run generate` leaves no drift; typecheck and 31 tests pass.
- Full desktop suite: the same 50 pre-existing failures as main, in the same 4 files (browser-profile-import, remote-proxy, ChatWorkspace, ContextMeter). `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` are clean.
- Live in the dev app against staging, on a Cloud project whose worker model is one the account cannot run:
  - Settings: the model picker lists Cloud's models for the account, with "claude-not-a-model-9 isn't available to your Claude Code account on Cloud, so tasks use the default. Pick another model." on its own line.
  - New Task: the composer picks the account's default (Opus 5.5), not the project's model, and shows "This project's model, ... isn't available ... Change it in Project settings." with no Retry.

## Review follow-up (60447d4ce4)

Each item from the review, what changed, and the test that proves it. Every new test failed on ef2edc9b57 first; each new rule was then mutation-checked (reverting it fails its test).

**Blockers (composer pick parking, `TaskComposer.tsx`)**
- **B1 (a local project ran another local project's model) and B2 (a Cloud project ran another Cloud project's model):** picks are parked per project instead of per local/Cloud kind, and only an explicit (touched) pick comes back, only to the project it was made in. An untouched value resets so that project's own defaults apply, and the default effects are held back only for the value actually brought back (it was all of them, including the commit where the new project's default arrived). Tests: `starts a local project's task on its own model after a Cloud project, not on the last local project's (B1)` (B visited first so its project is cached; asserts the delegate sends no model), `starts a Cloud project's task on its own model after a local project, not on the last Cloud project's (B2)` (asserts `createSession` sends `c2-model`), `never sends an explicit pick made in one local project for another after a Cloud project`, `does not bring back a project's old default when its model changed while the composer was away`.
- **B3 (a model restored under another agent):** a parked pick records the agent it was made with and is dropped if another agent is in effect; the agent itself carries as on main. Test: `does not send a model picked for one agent with the agent picked in a Cloud project (B3)` (asserts `agent: "claude-code"` and not `gpt-5.5`).
- The intent is kept: `brings an explicit pick back when the composer returns to the project it was made in`, plus the existing Scratchpad and local-to-Cloud tests.

**Non-blocking**
- **Settings with no Cloud list (5xx, or 409 for opencode without a credential type):** the model field now says "Couldn't load AO Cloud's model list for <Agent>." or "AO Cloud has no model list for <Agent>. Enter a model ID.", with a Retry that reads Cloud's list again (the field's refresh does too), and model IDs can still be entered. It never falls back to this computer's list. New strings in all 9 locales. Tests: `says when Cloud's model list could not be read, and reads it again on Retry`, `says when Cloud has no model list for an agent, without falling back to this computer's`.
- **422 `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`:** a Cloud create refused for the model re-reads the account's Cloud list for that agent, and Cloud's message is shown. Test: `reads Cloud's list again when Cloud refuses the model, and shows Cloud's reason`.
- **Polling:** the release list is read again on a doubling schedule, 15s, 30s, 60s, 120s, 240s, then every 5 minutes; a window focus reads it at once and starts again at 15s; no reads once the account's own list is in. Every picker of an agent (the composer, the three role fields) shares one query and one read per interval: React Query re-arms all observers' timers on each read and shares an in-flight read. Tests (fake timers): `reads the release list less often the longer it stays the release list`, `starts again at 15s when the window regains focus`, `reads once per interval for every picker of one agent, however many are open` (three pickers mounted 5s apart: 4 reads in 105s).
- **Scope:** a Cloud session's agent switch now passes `cloudOrgId`, so its catalog reads are Cloud's (test: `lists the session's agent's models from Cloud's list for the account, not this computer's`; the picker side is `AgentSwitchPicker.test.tsx`). Automations are not changed: the daemon only creates an automation for a local project (`PROJECT_NOT_FOUND` otherwise), so this computer's list is the right one there.
- **`default`:** `cloudModelVerdict` no longer treats the literal `default` as always offered; like the control plane's `Offers`, it is offered only by a list that names it (Claude Code's does, Codex's does not). The TS table now has the 3 Go cases it lacked (`GPT-5.6-Terra`, `gpt-5.6-terra/high`, `opencode-go/model-1`). Test: `treats the literal default as the control plane does`.

**Verification (60447d4ce4):** `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` clean; the touched test files pass (TaskComposer 180, CloudProjectSettingsForm 46, CloudSessionChatSurface 96, useCloudModelCatalog 4, cloud-model-catalog 70); the full vitest suite has 50 failures in 4 files (browser-profile-import, remote-proxy, ChatWorkspace, ContextMeter), all in main's known-failing set; locally `cloud-model-catalog`, `model-menu-scroll`, `new-chat-handoff` and `new-task-focus` e2e specs pass (17), and the renderer smoke suite passes 147 of 148 (the one failure, `chat-composer-text-selection` pointer drag, fails locally on main too and passes in CI).

## Live check in the desktop app (main + this PR + #7852, against staging td 428 = ao-control-plane#51 + #53)

Local projects A (`opus`) and B (`sonnet`), Cloud projects C1 (`sonnet`) and C2 (`opus`), driven in the real app:
- **B1:** A, then C1, then B: B shows `sonnet`, and Start sends `{projectId: B, agent: claude-code}` with no model (B's own model applies).
- **B2:** C1, then A, then C2: C2 shows Opus 5.5, and the session it created on staging runs `opus` (medium), not C1's `sonnet`.
- **Round trip:** an explicit Haiku 4.5 in A, then C1 (shows its own model), then A: Haiku 4.5 is back.
- **B3:** a Codex pick in A, then C1 with the agent switched to Claude Code, then A: no Codex model is sent with Claude Code.
- **Found live and fixed (66e68f3839):** after switching agents in A (which remembers a pick per agent), A, then C1, then B handed A's remembered Claude pick to B, which showed and sent it. Remembered agent picks were parked per kind (local, Cloud); they are now parked per project. New tests: `does not hand a pick remembered for an agent in one local project to another after a Cloud project` (failed before the fix) and `brings a project's remembered agent picks back with it after a Cloud project`. Re-checked live: B shows `sonnet` and sends no model; A gets its pick back. Picks still carry between two projects of the same kind, as on main.
- **Settings, no Cloud list:** C1's worker on OpenCode (Cloud answers 409): "AO Cloud has no model list for OpenCode. Enter a model ID." with Retry; Retry sends one Cloud read; nothing from this computer is listed. The worker model list on Claude Code is Cloud's (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 4.5).
- **Unavailable project model:** a custom `claude-not-a-model-9` in settings warns "isn't available to your Claude Code account on Cloud, so tasks use the default"; the composer shows the same notice and starts on a model the account runs; a session started without a model (an older desktop, an orchestrator's worker) falls back on the server, and its Chat shows "claude-not-a-model-9 isn't available to your Claude Code account on Cloud, so this session uses the default model." It replied.
- **Polling:** a release-only list (Cursor) read at +31 s, +61 s and +121 s after a focus, and not at all while the window was hidden; an account's own list (Claude Code, Codex) is never polled.
- **In-session picker:** a Cloud session's model menu lists Cloud's list for the account, and its agent switch offers only the agents Cloud has for it.
- Not reproducible from the UI: the 422 path (the composer never sends a model the account's list lacks); covered by `reads Cloud's list again when Cloud refuses the model, and shows Cloud's reason`.
- Full vitest after 66e68f3839: 50 failures in 4 files (browser-profile-import, remote-proxy, ChatWorkspace, ContextMeter), all in main's known-failing set; TaskComposer 182/182.
