title: Claude alias sessions always show a false "Answered by claude-opus-5-5 instead of opus" reroute banner
body:
## Summary

Every Claude chat started with a model **alias** (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`, `default`, `opus[1m]`) shows a "model rerouted" banner after its first completed turn, even when the alias resolved to exactly the expected model:

> 🔀 **Answered by claude-opus-5-5 instead of opus**
> The installed Claude Code resolves "opus" to claude-opus-5-5

No substitution happened — Claude Code 2.1.318 resolves `opus` to `claude-opus-5-5`, the newest Opus. The banner is a false positive, and its shuffle icon + "instead of" wording reads as a fallback/downgrade.

## Repro

1. Start a Claude chat with model `opus` (Claude Code 2.1.318, AO `0.14.8-dev` @ `c2a83c7b49`).
2. Send any prompt (e.g. "Reply with the single word ok").
3. Banner appears on the first completed turn.

## Root cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/driver.go` — `claudeServedModel` runs only for aliases, reads the answering model from Claude's transcript, and returns the generic reason `The installed Claude Code resolves %q to %s`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go` — `reportServedModel` emits `model.rerouted` whenever `served != selected`.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx` renders it as "Answered by X instead of Y".

`selected` is an alias (`"opus"`) and `served` is a concrete ID (`"claude-opus-5-5"`), so `served != selected` is **always true for aliases**. The only dedup is per (selected, served) pair within one conversation.

The doc comment on `reportServedModel` states the intent was narrower — *"an alias that the installed CLI resolves to an **older** concrete model"* — but nothing checks "older", only "different string". `ChatEventModelRerouted` (`ports/chat.go`) is documented as *"the provider answering with a model other than the one asked for"*, so normal alias resolution is being reported as a substitution.

Introduced in b39378b963 (#7136, "gate models the installed Claude Code is too old for"). The existing test (`acp/prompt_failure_test.go`) only checks which model is passed to `servedModel`, not that a correct resolution stays silent.

## Impact

- Low severity, nothing functionally wrong.
- Misleading on every alias-based chat (implies a fallback).
- Defeats the feature's purpose: an outdated CLI resolving `opus` to an older Opus looks identical to the normal case.

## Proposed fix

1. In `claudeServedModel`, compute the alias's expected resolution — the newest available model in that family from the version-gated catalog AO already builds — and return `""` when `served` matches. Only report when `served` is older, with an actionable reason, e.g. *"Claude Code 2.1.x resolves opus to claude-opus-5; run `claude update` to get claude-opus-5-5."*
2. Alternatively/additionally, don't reuse the shuffle "instead of" reroute UI for alias resolution; show it as a quiet `opus → claude-opus-5-5` hint on the model chip.
3. Add a test: `opus` resolving to the newest Opus emits no `model.rerouted` event.

title: fix(chat): keep reloaded steers on the turn they were sent in
body:
## Problem

After a Claude chat worker restarts or wakes from hibernation, a message you steered into a running turn can show up again below the answer, with "This turn was recovered from an earlier session" and no reply under it. Sometimes the turn's prompt comes back the same way.

ACP `session/load` starts a new replay turn at every user message, and Claude stores each steer as its own user message. If a steer lands while Claude is still waiting on the model, one AO turn replays as several turns: the prompt alone, each steer alone, then the answer. Only the last one holds an assistant item that `mapReplay` can match. AO's steer turns have no provider turn id, so nothing else matches the earlier turns either, and AO imports them again as new turns. Their outcome is unknown, so they show as `recovered`.

## Fix

`mapReplay` gets one more pass, `splitTurnOwners`. It handles a replay turn that holds only one user message. Such a turn attaches to the closest matched turn before or after it, when that turn's prompt or a steer it recorded has the same text. Messages replayed inside matched turns claim their text first, so each recorded prompt or steer absorbs at most one replayed message. A later message with the same text that AO never recorded, for example one typed in the terminal, still imports as a new turn. Claims stay local because the turn index is reused across replays.

## Evidence (real Claude Code, before and after)

Lab setup: an isolated `ao daemon` built from `main` (eb1d1ca646) and one built from this branch, each with its own `AO_DATA_DIR` and chat hibernation on. Each runs a Claude Code chat worker (`claude-opus-5-5`, effort `high`). The worker gets a no-tool reasoning prompt, then two `ao send --steer` calls 0.5 s apart while Claude is thinking. The worker then hibernates and is woken with a new message.

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Claude transcript for the turn | prompt, steer 1, steer 2 as three separate user messages, then the answer | same |
| `session_load` on wake | ok, 2.19 s | ok, 1.30 s |
| Turns imported from history | 2, both `recovered`: the prompt and "some more observation" | 0 |
| User messages in the chat | 5, including 2 duplicates | 3 |

The original report has the same shape. In that session, two queued messages were promoted into the running turn 0.5 s apart. After the next `session/load`, the first one came back as its own `acp-history-turn:` row in state `recovered`.

If both steers arrive during a tool call, Claude merges them into one user message at the tool boundary. On `main` that shape did not duplicate, and this change leaves it alone.

## Tests

- `TestReplayAttachesSplitTurnsToTheirAOTurn` covers both shapes: steers after tool work (as in the report), and steers before any output (as in the lab). Both fail on `main` with the duplicates above.
- `TestReplayKeepsUnrecordedRepeatOfSteerText` checks that an unrecorded repeat of a prompt's or a steer's text still imports.
- `go test ./internal/service/chat/` passes.

## Risks

- Chats that already contain a duplicate keep it. On the next reload the duplicate matches its own `acp-history-turn:` id, so nothing changes for it.
- The pass only touches replay turns that hold one user message and nothing else, and only binds them to an adjacent matched turn with an unclaimed prompt or steer of the same text.

title: fix(lifecycle): keep terminal sessions resumable after their host dies while AO is down
body:
## Problem

After a reboot, a crash, or a quit that stopped the agent processes, a terminal (TUI) orchestrator disappeared from its project. Chat workers in the same project came back stopped and resumable. Users reported this as "the orchestrator is gone after quitting AO or after an upgrade".

## Cause

At boot, the startup check (`checkSessionHealth`) finds the terminal session's runtime dead and records the agent as exited. The reaper then probes the same dead handle. The lifecycle manager reads that as a crash and terminates (archives) the session. This happens in two places:

1. In the runtime pass that runs right after startup reconciliation (`ReconcileRuntime`).
2. On a slow boot, even earlier: the periodic reaper starts with the lifecycle stack, before the startup check has run.

The reaper never probes Chat sessions, so only terminal sessions disappeared.

## Fix

- The startup check records the dead launch as released (`releaseTerminalRuntime`) before it records the exit. `ExitAgent` uses the same fence for a deliberate stop. The reaper then skips the session, and the session stays stopped and resumable.
- The periodic reaper waits until the post-startup runtime pass has run (`reaper.Config.StartAfter`). The boot goroutine releases the reaper when it exits, so a panic before that pass cannot leave the reaper off.
- The reaper skips stopped sessions whose launch was released (`SessionRecord.RuntimeReleased`, shared with the lifecycle guard). Such a session keeps its dead handle until it is resumed. Without the skip, enough stopped sessions trip the mass-death breaker on every pass, and a real crash is never ended.

## Evidence

- New regression test `TestStartupHealthKeepsDeadTerminalOrchestratorThroughTheReaper` runs the startup check and then a real reaper tick on a SQLite store. It fails on main (`terminated:true … released:""`) and passes with this change. `TestStart_WaitsForStartAfter` covers the reaper gate. `TestTick_SkipsReleasedLaunchSoStoppedSessionsDoNotTripBreaker` (5 stopped + 3 live, one crashed) fails without the skip and passes with it.
- Isolated lab with real Claude agents. A cold stop is a SIGKILL of the daemon, the hosts, and the agents, as in a reboot.

| After a restart | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TUI orchestrator, agent processes killed (cold stop) | archived | stopped, launch released |
| Resume of that orchestrator | not offered | `claude --resume <same session id>` (native); the conversation is kept |
| Agent processes still running (warm restart, upgrade) | all sessions come back | no change |

## Relation to #7183

#7183 stops agents on Quit AO Completely through `ExitAgent`, which already releases the launch. This PR covers the cases where agents stop without that path: a reboot, a crash, or a quit whose agent stop failed.

## Testing

- The new tests (red without the change, green with it), the reaper, lifecycle, domain and startup-health tests, and `go vet` on the touched packages.

## Risks

- If a startup reconcile step hangs, the periodic reaper waits for it. Before this change the reaper ran while boot was stuck. A panic no longer blocks the reaper.

title: fix(sidebar): show session status on Scratchpad rows instead of harness logos
body:
Code changes: +11 -44\
Tests: +25 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Scratchpad rows in the sidebar now look and behave like project and remote session rows. The harness logo is gone. Each row shows the same status icon (working spinner, needs-input alert, PR markers, unread/read dot), the same title shimmer while working, and the same time-ago column.

## Why

title: feat: remove the project agent and model setup
body:
## What this changes for users

Creating a local project no longer asks for a worker agent, an orchestrator agent or models. Pick a folder and the project is created, then you land in the orchestrator chat. Local project settings lose the agent and model pickers. An agent is chosen per session and can be switched at any time.

Defaults follow the same order as PR 1: the remembered ready agent, else the first ready one in claude-code, codex, cursor, opencode.

Stacked on #7711. Review that first. Only the local app changes; cloud projects and the mobile app keep their current agent setup.

## What was removed

- Frontend: the local "Set up project" agent step, the agent and model pickers in local project settings, `useProjectDefaultWorker`, and the `orchestratorAgent` field on workspace summaries.
- Backend: project `model`, `effort` and `mode` no longer reach a session. Project config contributes permissions only. `Summary.OrchestratorAgent` and `DefaultWorkerReviewer` are gone, and legacy import no longer maps agent or model.
- CLI: `--worker-agent` and `--orchestrator-agent` are hidden, deprecated no-ops.
- Docs: new "Choosing and switching agents" guide replaces the per-role agents page.

## Compatibility

- The API decodes projects with `DisallowUnknownFields`, so the legacy `agent`, `model`, `effort` and `mode` fields stay in the schema. They are ignored and stripped on create, update and set-config. Deleting them is a later breaking-API cleanup.
- Remote hosts on an older AO: those daemons still need a project agent to start the orchestrator. When adding a project on a remote host, the desktop sends the host's default agent (first authorized in the priority order) in the deprecated role fields. Current daemons strip it; older ones use it. If the agent list cannot be read, nothing extra is sent.
- Cloud: project creation and settings keep their worker and orchestrator agent pickers, and settings still require both.

## Review notes

- Existing local projects' saved model, effort and mode are now dropped for new sessions. Existing sessions keep their own saved model on restore.
- Many frontend and e2e tests were rewritten without a local run. CI is the first run.

title: feat(chat): fold agent actions into Worked for, collapse Agent Reports, drop harness logos
body:
## Summary

Three Chat thread changes:

1. **Agent actions fold into "Worked for".** The CLI now sends its session as `X-AO-Caller-Session`. When the session that runs the command is also the action's audience, and its conversation has exactly one running turn, `recordAction` files the `ao_action` row under that turn. Spawn, terminate, rename, restore and claim rows then fold with the turn's steps, and "Spawned N agents" moves inside the fold (or the quiet reply's work toggle) instead of sitting after the reply. Desktop clicks, another session's commands, and old rows stay standalone.
2. **Agent Reports collapse into one line.**
   - **The line:** "[logo][logo][logo]... N Agent Reports · K needs you ›". It shows up to three senders' agent logos in black and white (the only logos left in the thread, on purpose), then "..." when there are more. It isn't a pill: it highlights on hover, uses the 13px size, and is brighter than muted text.
   - **Under a human message:** reports sent with it sit under the bubble instead of above it.
   - **Report-only wakeup:** a turn opened only by reports gets the same line on its own.
   - **Expanded rows:** each row still links to its worker.
   - **Needs-you count:** it stays on the closed line and clears once that worker sends a newer update.
   - **Batched reports:** placement comes from recorded delivery data, never timestamps. Turns now expose `deliveredWithTurnId` (`promoted_to_turn_id`, batched rows only). A report a steer carried (listed in that steer's `providerInputSourceTurnIds`) goes under that steer. A report drained in a queued batch goes under that batch's last human message. A batch with no human message keeps its own line.
3. **No harness logos in Chat.** Worker rows, agent messages and handoff lines draw the neutral glyph or the model name. The chat tab gets `providerIcon={false}`, and the provider name stays in its `aria-label`. The composer model picker hides marks unless `terminal`. `AgentAvatar` and `ProviderMark` are unchanged, so the sidebar, inspector, terminal tabs and terminal agent picker keep their logos. `TerminalTabFrame` keeps the icon slot only while a hover action needs it.

4. **Replies to reports read like any other turn.** The indented one-line answer (`↳`, with its work behind a chevron) is gone. A turn opened by a report now shows "Worked for", then the normal reply with its copy and rollback row.

New strings are in all 8 locales with each locale's plural forms.

## Tests

- `e2e/chat-turn-settle.spec.ts` now waits for one sampled frame before settling the turn. This fixes a race where a busy CI runner settled the turn before the first sample (`settled` was 0).

- `go test` passes for `service/session` (new caller-turn binding test), `httpd/...`, `storage/sqlite/store` and `cli`. The `cli` tests pass only with this machine's `AO_*` session env unset; they read `AO_SESSION_ID` and `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY`.
- `vitest` passes for `components/chat`, `CenterPane`, `CenterPanelShell`, `SessionInterfaceSwitch`, `TerminalAgentControls` and the i18n gates: 71 files, 1,795 tests.
- New tests cover `placeBatchedReports` (drain, steer, no-human batch), the collapsed piggyback line with needs-you, and the logo-free chat tab.
- Typecheck is clean for the app.

## Not run

- `golangci-lint`: the local binary was built with Go 1.26 and the repo targets Go 1.27.1, so it refused to run. CI should run it.
- The real desktop app was not launched, so these layouts have not been seen on screen.

## Risks

- A background CLI process left over from an earlier turn that runs an action during a later turn would be filed under the later turn.
- The reports line under a human bubble is left-aligned and 28px tall so it shares the row with the hover actions on the right. Worth a visual check in the app.

title: CI-failure nudges fire on cancelled runs: CANCELLED counts as failing, and gate jobs in a cancelled run report FAILURE
body:
## Summary

AO counts a cancelled CI run as a failing one, so workers get "CI is failing on your PR" when nothing actually failed.

There are two ways this happens. Neither is covered by #7780, which only counts each check's newest run.

1. **A cancelled check counts as failing.** `isFailingCheckStatus` (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/provider.go`), the rollup in `ciSummaryFromGraphQL` (`case domain.PRCheckFailed, domain.PRCheckCancelled: return domain.CIFailing`) and `failedSCMChecks` (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go`) all treat `CANCELLED` like `FAILURE`. GitLab does the same (`isFailingCheckStatus` in `backend/internal/adapters/scm/gitlab/observer_provider.go` includes `canceled`). A run cancelled because a newer push or edit replaced it, or cancelled by hand, sends a CI-failure message citing a job with no failing step.
2. **A gate job inside a cancelled run reports `FAILURE`.** Jobs such as `build-test` check that their dependencies passed (`test 'cancelled' = success`), so they fail when those dependencies were cancelled. The check's result is `FAILURE`, but the workflow run's result is `cancelled`. Handling `CANCELLED` per job doesn't catch this. AO has to look at the workflow run's result (or check suite) the job belongs to.

## Repro (2026-11-05, PR #7822)

1. Push a commit, then edit the PR description while the `Go` workflow is running. The workflow uses concurrency cancel-in-progress.
2. Run 42027469065 on head `d158767081` is cancelled: `lint`, `api-drift`, `sqlc-drift`, `backend-core` and the race jobs all end as `cancelled`. Its `build-test` gate then fails with `test 'cancelled' = success` / exit 1.
3. A new run (42028174717) on the same commit is queued and has not finished.
4. AO sends the worker: "CI is failing ... Failed: build-test (failed)", with the gate's log tail.

Nothing in the code failed. The newer run had not reported yet, so #7780's newest-run-only rule would not have prevented the message: at that moment the cancelled run's gate was the newest finished `build-test`.

## Expected

- A `CANCELLED` / `canceled` check does not make CI failing on its own and does not trigger a CI-failure message. It is either neutral or pending a re-run.
- A failed job whose workflow run (or check suite) ended `cancelled` is treated as cancelled, not as a failure.
- CI counts as failing only when there is a real failure (`FAILURE`, `TIMED_OUT`, `STARTUP_FAILURE`, ...) in a run that was not cancelled.

## Proposed fix

- Drop `PRCheckCancelled` from `isFailingCheckStatus`, the rollup's failing case, and `failedSCMChecks` (GitHub and GitLab). A PR whose only non-passing checks are cancelled counts as pending, or unknown when nothing is queued.
- Request the job's `checkSuite { conclusion }` (or its `workflowRun` result) in the rollup query. When it is `CANCELLED`, record the job as `PRCheckCancelled` even if the job itself reported `FAILURE`.
- Tests: (a) a rollup with only cancelled jobs is not `CIFailing` and sends no message; (b) a `FAILURE` gate inside a `CANCELLED` check suite is not reported as failed; (c) a real `FAILURE` in a run that completed normally still sends the message.

## Related

- #7780: newest run per check name on the same commit (complementary; fix both)
- #4850 item 3: a job that never started is reported as failed

title: fix(sidebar): keep the session hover card open while the pointer heads for it
body:
Code changes: +167 -7\
Tests: +149 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The sidebar session hover card now stays open while the pointer moves from a row to the card, including diagonally across other rows. It uses a safe triangle ("menu aim").

## Why

Moving toward the card closed it, for two reasons:

1. Radix's `HoverCardTrigger` runs its own `pointerleave → onClose` timer. With `closeDelay={0}`, it reported a close the moment the pointer left the row, and the Sidebar's `onOpenChange` turned that into `preview.hide()`. Even a straight move across the 12 px gap lost the card.
2. On a diagonal path, the pointer crosses other rows, and each crossed row opened its own card in place of the one you were heading for.

## Before / After

Same data and window. The pointer leaves `hello repro one` heading for its card's lower-left corner, and is over the `Keyboard test` row at the moment of capture.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Keyboard test's card replaced the one being aimed at](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/41d5cd5aeebde350cc715e099c549f54/raw/before.png) | ![After: hello repro one's card stays open while the pointer crosses Keyboard test](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/41d5cd5aeebde350cc715e099c549f54/raw/after.png) |
| Diagonal from row to card: closes at the row edge, the crossed row's card flashes, and nothing is open on arrival | Card stays open the whole way and while the pointer is on it; closes once the pointer leaves the card |

## How

All changes are in `useSessionPreviewHover.ts`.

- **Claiming events from Radix:** the hook's row and card pointer enter/leave handlers call `preventDefault()`. Radix's `composeEventHandlers` then skips its own hover timers, so the hook alone owns pointer open/close. Escape and outside presses still close through Radix's dismissable layer.
- **Safe triangle:** when the pointer leaves the row while its card is open, the apex is the exit point, pushed back 4 px (Floating UI's `safePolygon` `buffer`), and the base is the two card corners on the edge facing the row. `safeTriangle()` picks the right, left, top or bottom edge, so it works wherever Radix places or flips the card.
- **Grace:** 300 ms, the value used by both Amazon's jQuery-menu-aim (`DELAY`) and Radix's submenu `pointerGraceTimer`. The timer restarts only when a move brings the pointer closer to the card, so stalling or drifting sideways lets it run out. Backing away more than 2 px, or leaving the triangle, ends the aim at once. When the aim ends, the row under the pointer takes over instantly, like a normal sweep. If no row is under the pointer, the card closes with the existing 60 ms leave delay.
- **Crossed rows** record themselves as hovered but don't open their cards while an aim belongs to another row.
- **No jank:** tracking runs on the existing passive window `pointermove` listener, using module state and plain geometry. Nothing triggers a React render per move.
- **Why not a library:** `@floating-ui/react` is only in the lockfile as a transitive dependency of `@lexical/react`, and its `safePolygon` only works inside Floating UI's own `useFloating`/`useHover` context, not with a Radix HoverCard. Radix's submenu grace polygon isn't exported. So the hook carries roughly 70 lines of geometry and state.
- The first-open delay, warm sweep, cool-down, keyboard focus/blur, Escape, scroll handling and touch exclusion are unchanged.

## Testing

- New `useSessionPreviewHover.test.tsx` covers triangle geometry for all four card placements, point containment, and, with fake timers, holding across a crossed row, handing over after a stall, switching rows on leaving the triangle, the normal close when leaving away from the card, and returning to the row. Per project practice I didn't run vitest/tsgo locally; CI covers them.
- Real Electron dev app (isolated data), driven with trusted CDP mouse moves:
  - Diagonals down and up across a neighbouring row, at 16 ms and 4 ms per step: the card stays open the whole way, stays while the pointer rests on it, and closes after the pointer leaves it. On base, the same script closes the card partway and opens the crossed row's card instead.
  - A vertical sweep down the list still switches cards row by row straight away.
  - Stalling in the triangle hands over to the row underneath at about 310 ms.
  - Moving out of the triangle switches to the row underneath immediately.
  - Keyboard focus opens the card, blur closes it, and Escape closes a hover-opened card.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: fix(sidebar): close the session preview when the archive confirm opens
body:
## Summary

Archiving a session from the sidebar floated the row's preview card over the "Are you sure you want to archive this session?" dialog, and the card stayed on screen after pressing No.

Both causes are in `useSessionPreviewHover`:

- **The card opened above the dialog.** The confirm is portaled to `<body>` but is still a React child of the row, so its focus and pointer events reach the row's preview handlers. Focusing the dialog opened the card after the dialog, and the later portal paints above the overlay at the same z-index.
- **The card stayed after No.** On close the confirm correctly hands focus back to the row. That focus requested a preview with no pointer on the row, so nothing ever closed it.

The row's handlers now ignore events from outside the row's DOM, and focus with no `relatedTarget` no longer requests a preview: focus handed back after a dialog arrives from nowhere, while Tab arrives from another control. Hovering a row or tabbing onto it still shows the preview.

**Escape took two presses to close the confirm.** It has the same cause, on the sidebar, topbar and board. The confirm sat inside `TooltipTrigger`, so its focus and pointer events opened the "Archive session" tooltip above the overlay. That tooltip was the newest dismissable layer, so it took the first Escape and the dialog stayed open. Each site now passes the tooltip as the dialog's `trigger`, so the confirm is no longer its child.

## Evidence

Real dev desktop app with isolated lab data and one real Claude chat session, rebased on `main` including #7828. The same script ran on both builds and checked which source Vite was serving. Route: right-click a row, then Archive session.

title: fix(scm): ignore superseded check runs when deriving GitHub CI state
body:
## Problem

PR #7774 showed **Checks failing** in AO while GitHub showed "All checks have passed (1 skipped, 15 successful)". The session also logged "CI Failed", which can trigger the CI auto-fix nudge.

The head commit ran each workflow three times. The first run was cancelled when the workflow ran again, and `build-test` failed in the second. `statusCheckRollup` keeps all 44 runs, and its `state` stays `FAILURE`. GitHub's checks list and `gh pr checks` show only the newest run per workflow, event and job. AO used the rollup `state` (observer) or failed on any failed node (legacy provider), so the stale runs decided the verdict.

The same panel said "The review requirement is satisfied, but failing checks still block this PR" while the review was still required: `mergeReadinessDetail` checked CI before review.

## Change

- `latestCheckRuns` keeps the newest CheckRun (highest `databaseId`) per workflow name, event and job name. The CI summary, the check list, `FailedChecks` (the auto-fix nudge input) and job-log lookup all use it.
- The observer still uses the rollup `state`, but re-derives a `FAILURE` from the newest runs when the full context list is fetched.
- The CheckRun selection now asks for `checkSuite{ workflowRun{ event workflow{ name } } }`. Tokens without Actions read access get errors on that field, so `doGraphQL` ignores errors whose path is on `workflowRun`. CheckRuns with no readable workflow are never merged with others, which is today's behavior.
- `mergeReadinessDetail` checks the review before failing checks, so the checks-failing message is only shown when the review requirement is met.

## Verification

Live `FetchPullRequests` against the real #7774 (head `f622415b51`), using a throwaway test that is not committed:

| | summary | checks | failed checks | merge blockers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `failing` | 44 | 7 cancelled + `build-test` | `ci_failing`, `review_required` |
| this PR | `passing` | 16 | none | `review_required` |

- `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/github/` passes. The new `TestCISummaryIgnoresSupersededCheckRuns` and `TestFetchPullRequestsToleratesWorkflowRunAccessErrors` fail on `main`.
- `vitest pr-display.test.ts` passes (52 tests).

## Risks

- I haven't seen the `workflowRun` permission error with a real limited token. The tolerance is tested against a synthetic GitHub error response.
- Two workflows with the same `name:`, event and job name are treated as one check. GitHub's checks list and `gh pr checks` do the same.
- The desktop panel wasn't driven end to end. The fix is in the adapter output that the panel renders.

title: Steer/message muse-harness TUI workers: paste-as-input via existing PTY path
body:
# Steering/nudging muse-harness TUI workers from the orchestrator is impossible

## Problem
An AO orchestrator cannot steer, nudge, or message into a running `muse`-harness worker session:
- `ao send --steer` fails at the daemon with `SESSION_MODE_MISMATCH` (TUI mode, no chat conversation).
- `ao spawn --mode chat --agent muse` is refused with `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` (muse has no chat driver).
- Plain `ao send` is accepted but its effect on the TUI agent is unobservable (no transcript for TUI sessions; `ao session get --transcript` exits 1).
- Native `muse session-message` is closed (`external_agent_ingress_closed`).

Net effect: orchestrators command muse fleets through spawn/kill/lifecycle plus file artifacts only. A stuck-at-prompt worker is indistinguishable from a busy one until its output lands or never does.

## Evidence (ao 0.14.9, Muse Code 1.4.14, Arch Linux)
- Full `ao`/`ao session`/`muse`/`serve`/`session-message` help surveyed: no CLI verb writes bytes into a TUI session.
- Daemon binary contains a complete steer bookkeeping family (`decode steer input`, `steer queued turn`, idempotent `--client-message-id`) — all gated on a chat controller — plus a shell-terminal/PTY route (`/api/v1/shell-terminals`, `SHELL_TERMINAL_*` errors, `pty-host`) with an origin gate and no CLI verb.
- Offline MSP schema export (70 methods) confirms `turn/start` with `{queue, steer, replace}`, `turn/steer` with `expectedTurnId`, `turn/interrupt` — but no `serve` host sits behind a TUI session, so MSP is unreachable for exactly the sessions that need steering.
- `ao hooks` flows worker→daemon (activity reports), never daemon→worker. Wrong direction, not a steering channel.

## Minimal proposal
One branch in the daemon's send/steer handler where it returns `SESSION_MODE_MISMATCH` for `mode == tui`: instead of refusing, deliver through the existing pty-host/shell-terminal input path (the same write path the origin-gated attach uses) — paste the message into the session's PTY as terminal input, i.e. plain-send semantics, never mid-turn interruption. Keep `--client-message-id` idempotency/`--recover-only` semantics; keep refusing unknown/terminated sessions and empty messages; surface a busy state instead of silently dropping input. No new route, no CLI auth-model change, no chat driver for muse, no muse-side or hook/MSP changes.

## Acceptance
- Orchestrator sends a message to an idle muse TUI worker; the worker receives and acts on it.
- Orchestrator sends a message to a busy muse TUI worker; it is queued as the next input, never lost, never duplicated, never leaked into the wrong turn.
- Failures (unknown session, busy PTY) report clear errors, never silent drops.

title: fix(chat): replace the edit replay notice with one branch line
body:
Code changes: +11 -35\
Tests: +12 -13\
Others: +9 -9 (translations)

## What

The chat edit box now shows one line on every edit: "Starts a new conversation branch. Files stay as they are." It sits in the button row. An error or the "Stop the current turn" message takes its place.

This replaces the two-sentence "Reconstructed context" notice, which appeared only on some edits.

## Why

The old notice described replay internals (tool calls, approvals, workspace history) that a reader cannot act on. It also made the box taller, and it appeared only on edits that take the replay path, so the same action looked different depending on the agent.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: replayed edit with the two-sentence notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a224005-9e76-449b-8ec7-82c974df4c2c) | ![After: replayed edit with one line in the button row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68f01402-3ab3-4efa-9b7c-9ed92a6888a5) |
| ![Before: first-prompt edit with no note](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d5a0001-6362-4eba-8e06-40655fa75e18) | ![After: first-prompt edit with the same line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/452caa88-9271-4267-a4bb-6b8a1a1e4c0f) |
| ![Before: busy state with the notice and the stop message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86877bd8-4545-4762-9ae9-a88b730ea92c) | ![After: busy state with only the stop message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7925b567-b9e3-4f32-954a-70af1f864715) |
| Error: the notice stays above the error | Error: the error replaces the line (covered in `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`) |

The box is 38 px shorter on a replayed edit (160 to 122 px, measured in the app).

## How

- **Wording:** an edit keeps the old messages on a conversation branch, reachable from the branch navigator on the message, so the line does not say they are removed. It says "conversation branch" so it does not read as a git branch. Neither edit path touches the worktree.
- **One slot:** the line shares the left side of the button row with the error and busy messages, and only the most important one shows. `aria-describedby` follows it.
- **Removed:** `reconstructedContext` and `reconstructedTurns` no longer affect anything, so they are gone from `ChatWorkspace`, `ChatTimelineItems`, `HumanMessageEditor` and `chat-drafts`. Saved drafts that still carry the field remain valid, because `isInlineEdit` ignores it. Which messages can be edited is unchanged.
- **Key:** `chat.edit.reconstructedContext` is now `chat.edit.branchNote` in all 9 locales, reusing each locale's existing term from `chat.branch.position`.
- **Intentional omission:** the UI no longer says that a replayed agent loses its tool-call history. This was a deliberate product choice for a shorter note.
- **Left alone:** `packages/mobile/lib/chat/timelineModel.ts` computes its own `reconstructed` set, but it shows no note.

Reviewers: the translations have not been checked by native speakers.

## Testing

On this commit:

- `vitest run` for `HumanMessageEditor`, `ChatWorkspace`, `chat-drafts` and `i18n`: 5 targets, 314 tests passed.
- `tsgo --noEmit` in `frontend/`: 0 errors.
- Real desktop app on isolated data, in one chat with the real Claude Code binary, for each state above. The Before side ran main's renderer files in the same window. Note text and `aria-describedby` were read from the DOM for each state.

Not run locally, to be verified in CI: the full frontend suite and the other CI jobs. No Go code changed.

## What

The native groundwork for the mobile overhaul: dependencies, native patches, Expo config plugins and the icon and font assets the later PRs draw with.

- **Dependencies:** every Expo SDK 57 package moves to its latest patch, and `expo-symbols` and `sf-symbols-typescript` are added for system glyphs. Android builds `expo-ui` from source so its patch applies. Vitest mocks `expo-symbols` once in a shared setup file.
- **Patches:**
  - `react-native-screens`: answers UIKit's `shouldSelectTab` on iOS 18+, so the tab iOS 26 sets apart honours `preventNativeSelection`.
  - `@expo/ui` (Android): lets the app set a Material theme per colour scheme, gives `Text` its slot's font family, and opens `DropdownMenu` against its anchor rather than under the status bar.
- **iOS scene life cycle:** `expo-build-properties`' `ios.enableSceneSupport` adopts it. Without it, iOS 27 traps at launch. This is Expo's own option, maintained across SDK patches, rather than a plugin of ours.
- **Config plugins:**
  - `withIosSoftScrollEdge` keeps the soft scroll edge under the glass bar, on iOS 27 only.
  - `withAndroidDialogTheme` gives `Alert` dialogs Material 3 shape and the app's palette.
  - `withHarnessMenuIcons` copies the harness menu image sets into the asset catalog.
- **Assets:** Material drawables, harness menu image sets, tab icons and DM Sans, with the scripts that regenerate them.
- **Config:** turns off Android predictive back. This fixes a bug on `main`: on Android 13–15, Back (gesture or key) from a pushed page, such as a project opened from Projects, left the app instead of going back.

## Why

#7419 is too large to review (858 files). This splits it into four PRs that each build and pass the full mobile suite on their own base. This one carries everything native, so it can be checked on devices by itself.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| iOS 27 traps at launch (no scene life cycle) | The app adopts the scene life cycle and launches |
| Android `Alert` dialogs: AppCompat's grey slab, square corners, upper-case teal buttons | Material 3 shape and the app's palette, sentence-case actions |
| Android `DropdownMenu` can open under the status bar | Opens against its anchor |
| Android 13–15: Back from a pushed page leaves the app | Back returns to the previous screen |

Screenshots of the `Alert` dialog and a menu on Android, and of iOS launch, will be added from a simulator run.

## How

- Each config plugin has a source test next to it (`iosSoftScrollEdge`, `harnessMenuIcons`).
- The plugins read assets added in this same PR, so they have to merge together.
- Scene support: `expo prebuild` writes the same `AppDelegate.swift` and `Info.plist` with `enableSceneSupport` as with the hand-written plugin it replaces (checked byte for byte).
- **Reviewer focus:** adopting the scene life cycle changes how the app starts on every iOS version, not just 27. Launch, opening from a notification, deep links and QR pairing are the paths to check.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`: passes.
- `npm test`: 268 files, 2,800 tests pass.
- `expo prebuild --platform ios`: succeeds with no warnings.
- Not done locally:

title: feat(chat): name each step by what it did, and show the running one beside the loader
body: Code changes: +1959 -269\ Tests: +871 -9\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Chat step rows now say what each step did, and what it did it to, with a small icon in front, instead of one "Ran command" for most things. - **Reads, lists, searches:** "Read README.md", "Read 2 files package.json, tsconfig.json", "Listed files", "Searched for TODO", "Found files *.test.ts" - **Git and GitHub:** "Checked git status", "Viewed recent commits", "Created branch feat/x", "Read PR #7804", "Listed pull requests" - **File operations run as commands:** "Created folder activity-demo", "Renamed hello.js → greet.js", "Moved notes.md → archive", "Deleted activity-demo", "Wrote notes.md" (`cat > file`, `tee`) - **Running things:** "Ran hello.js", "Ran tests", "Installed packages", "Built project", "Type-checked", "Ran lint", "Fetched nodejs.org", "Waited 6s" - **Web searches:** "Searched the web for latest stable Node.js version", from Codex and from Claude Code - **Claude Code's built-in tools:** "Read README.md", "Searched for TODO", "Found files **/*.test.ts", "Fetched versionlog.com", "Loaded tools WebSearch, TaskCreate". A run of known reads, searches and fetches names those actions in its summary - **Anything else:** "Ran docker", "Ran printf". The program's name replaces "Ran command". A step that is still running uses the present tense: "Running hello.js", "Reading README.md", "Editing notes.md". So does the live line under the turn, which only ever names a running step. The running step now shows once, on the live row beside the loader ("Waiting 6s · 2s ›"), instead of also as its own row above it. A muted dot keeps the step's own numbers apart from the turn's timer. The live row opens onto the step's command, output, patch or tool payload, and it opens by itself once a command starts printing, as the step's own row did. When the step finishes, its row joins the steps above as before. The live row sits right under the steps, and the plan card goes below it, not between them. The shimmer, the timer, the grouping and folding, the expanded command and output, and the file-edit rows' `+N −N` all behave as before. ## Why Most command rows said "Ran command". Creating a folder, running a script, renaming a file, deleting a folder, a test run and a web search all looked identical, so the collapsed turn told the reader nothing. Reads only said "Read file", and every `ls`, `rg` and `find` said "Search". Claude Code's built-in tools showed the provider's raw title instead. A web search was only its query in quotes (`"latest stable Node.js version"`), with nothing saying it was a web search. While a turn ran, its current step showed twice, as its own row with a spinner and again on the live row just under it. When the agent kept a plan, the plan card sat between the steps and the live row, so the loader was cut off from the work it belonged to. The live line under a running turn used the same label, so it said "Ran command", in the past tense, while the command was still running. ## Before / After The same stubbed Codex turn, which runs the 18 steps of a test prompt, is shown mid-run in both: the last step (`sleep 6`) is still running. | Before (`main`) | After | | --- | --- | | Conditional parent-folder `AGENTS.md` lookup → `Ran AGENTS.md; do if …` | `Looked for AGENTS.md` | | `ls -la` → "Search" | "Listed files" | | Grouped reads and searches → "Explored 4 tool calls"; inner groups → "Explored 2 tool calls" | "Searched for 2 patterns · Read 5 files"; inner groups name searches and reads | | `sed -n '1,40p' README.md` → "Read file" | "Read README.md" | | `rg -n "TODO" .` → "Search" | "Searched for TODO" | | `git log --oneline -3` → "Checked repository" | "Viewed recent commits" | | `gh pr view 7804` → "Checked repository" | "Read PR #7804" | | Codex web search → "Ran command" | "Searched the web latest stable Node.js version" | | `mkdir`, `node hello.js`, `mv`, `npm test`, `rm -rf` → "Ran command" ×5 | "Created folder activity-demo", "Ran hello.js", "Renamed hello.js → greet.js", "Ran tests", "Deleted activity-demo" | | Live line during `sleep 6`: "Ran command" | "Waiting 6s" | | Claude Code `WebSearch` → `"latest stable Node.js version"` | "Searched the web for latest stable Node.js version" | | Claude Code `WebFetch` → "Fetch https://versionlog.com/nodejs/" | "Fetched versionlog.com" | | Claude Code `Read` → "Read README.md (1 - 40)"; two reads → "Ran 2 tool calls" | "Read README.md"; "Read 2 files" | | `command -v gh && gh pr list …` → "Ran command" | "Listed pull requests" | | Running step: a "Waiting 6s ⟳ ›" row, then the live row "Waiting 6s 2s" | Only the live row, "Waiting 6s · 2s ›", which opens onto `sleep 6 && echo done` | | Live turn with a plan: steps, plan card, live row | Steps, live row, plan card | | `git add -A && git commit -m x && git push` → "Checked repository" | "Pushed changes" | | `rm -rf dist && npm run build` → "Ran command" | "Built project" | | `npm test \| tee log` → "Ran command" | "Ran tests" | | `cd frontend`, `export CI=1`, `source .env` → "Ran command" | "Changed folder frontend", "Set CI", "Loaded .env" | | A step with a provider title and no command line → "Ran command" | The provider's title | | Failed `git push` → "Checked repository `exit 1`" | "Pushing changes `exit 1`" | | A stopped turn and its "Continued" marker: 10px, 6px and 18px gaps | 4px and 2px inside the turn, and the marker sits closer to the turns on both sides | ## How - **`activity-step.ts` (new)** turns a command line into `{ done, live, target, icon }`. It reads the part of the line that does the work: past `cd dir &&`, env assignments, `sudo`/`timeout`/`env` wrappers and `bash -lc '…'`, the first stage of a pipeline, and heredoc bodies and stream redirects such as `2>/dev/null` and `2>&1`. A `> file` redirect from `cat`/`echo`/`printf` counts as a write. Chained plain reads (`sed -n … a.ts && sed -n … b.ts`) count as one read of both files, which is what the old file count did. - **Chains and multi-line commands.** A chain is named by its last segment that changes or runs something, so `git status` or `echo done` at the end does not take the name. Quotes spanning lines, heredoc bodies, comments, `&>` and unquoted `$(...)` are parsed rather than misread. Grouping reads the same segment, and a command named as a write (`cat > a`, `sed -i`) no longer counts as exploring. - **Failed steps.** A step that failed or stopped uses the present tense when its past tense would claim the result ("Deleting build `failed`"). "Ran tests `exit 1`" stays, because the tests did run. - **Claude Code's tools** (`activityToolStep`): Claude Code's Read, Grep, Glob, LS, WebSearch, WebFetch and ToolSearch reach AO over ACP as tool calls, which render in the MCP tool row. Each is now named from its `providerToolName` and raw input, like the command that does the same job, with the same verb, target and icon in the row and the live line. A call to an MCP server (one with a `server` or `namespace`) and an unknown tool keep their own title. Another ACP agent's read, search or fetch only gains the icon. Read, search and fetch calls count as exploring in the run header. - **The live row** (`ChatWorkspace`, `LiveResponseStatus`): while the turn runs, the step the live row names is left out of its run. That only happens for a command, file edit or tool call that is not part of a subagent's tree, so the subagent view keeps every row. `LiveResponseStatus` takes that step and, when it has details, becomes a button with a chevron that opens them. The details are the same bodies the step's own row opens onto, now shared as `GenericActivityBody` and `McpToolBody`. The open/closed choice is kept per step, and the default is open while a command is printing. The live row renders before the plan card, so in a settled turn, which has no live row, nothing moves. As the turn settles, the plan slides up into the live row's place with the other rows (the existing settle animation). - **No prose misread as a command.** When a provider sends only a title and no command line, a backticked title is read as a command and any other title is shown as written. "Ran command" remains only for a title that names nothing ("Terminal"). Codex's web search, which arrives as a command with only a "Searched the web for …" summary, gets its own label. - **Group headings** now summarize known reads, listings, searches, file matches, web searches and fetches using the row descriptions. Adjacent built-in tool calls are grouped by action icon so reads and searches get separate inner headings. Unknown calls retain the generic count. - **Row** (`GenericActivityRow`): command and file-edit rows get a `size-3` muted icon in front, as `AOActionRow` already has. The target uses the file-edit row's name style (`text-xs text-foreground/65`) with the same 4px gap, and gets a tooltip only when it is shortened (a basename of a longer path, or over 48 characters). A space that the flex row never draws keeps the accessible name "Read README.md" rather than "ReadREADME.md". - **Copy stays English.** "Ran command", "Read file" and the other labels this replaces were never translated, so the new ones are not added to the nine i18n catalogs either. - **Reasoning summaries stay hidden.** The live row names tool work, and the settled turn keeps its existing folded work without adding provider reasoning text. - **Subagent rows are not part of this.** The subagent view is in #7176. ## Testing - Conditional lookup follow-up: regression assertions added; no local tests or checks run, per request. Remote CI will validate the push. - Group-heading follow-up: no local tests or checks run, per request. Existing assertions were updated; remote CI will validate the push. - Takeover pass (merge with `main`, review fixes, spacing): tests were updated by reading the code and rely on CI. Nothing was run locally, and it still needs a manual test in the app. - New `activity-step.test.ts`, 18 cases: each step of the test prompt, the common dev commands, `cd`/env/wrapper/`bash -lc` prefixes, `command -v` checks, redirects and heredocs, a quoted `">"` pattern, the Codex web-search summary, prose summaries keeping "Ran command", and Claude Code's tools with the detail its ACP driver records (MCP server calls and unknown tools keep their title). - `ActivityRun.test.tsx`: a run of a Claude Code Read and WebSearch says "Read 1 file · Searched the web", and its rows read "Read README.md" and "Searched the web for latest stable Node.js version" with the globe icon. - Updated label assertions in `TurnChangedFiles.test.tsx` (now also checks the icon is a `size-3` mark and the bordered rows' terminal icon is absent) and `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`. - `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: a running step shows once, on the live row, and the live row comes after the finished steps and before the plan. It opens onto the step's command. A step that finished gets its own row back. Checked to fail with the old order. - `vitest run src/renderer/components/chat`: 1707/1707. - `e2e/chat-turn-settle.spec.ts` and `e2e/chat-continue.spec.ts` (installed Chrome): 6/6. - `npm run typecheck` (tsgo): clean. - `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean. - Full `npx vitest run`: 11402 passed, 51 failed, all in `src/main`, none in the renderer. 48 `browser-profile-import` and 2 `browser-cookie-repair` failures are this machine's `better-sqlite3` being built for Electron's Node ABI (`NODE_MODULE_VERSION 149`). 1 is the `remote-proxy` HTTP/2 hook timeout, which also fails on `main` here. - Renderer smoke (`CI=true`, `--grep "@T0|@P0"`, installed Chrome): 137/153 passed in the full run. 15 of the 16 failures pass when rerun alone with `--last-failed --workers=2` (load timeouts). The remaining one, `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts:139` (dark selection contrast), fails the same way on an untouched export of `main`. - Latest follow-up removes the reasoning-summary display and Codex override. No local tests or checks were run, per request; remote CI passed. - Rendered the stubbed turn above through the real renderer in Chrome (fake bridge, as in `chat-turn-settle.spec.ts`), light and dark, on `main` and on this branch. - Rendered a real Claude Code turn of the same test prompt, taken from the dev app's database, before and after the Claude Code fix. Every row in the table above reads as listed. - Rendered the stubbed turn mid-run with a five-step plan, closed and opened, before and after the live-row change. - Launched the Electron dev app from this branch against the isolated dev data; it starts and loads projects. A live agent turn in the desktop app has not been checked yet. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat: make Add to chat excerpts reliable across formatted content
body:
Code changes: +1218 -223  
Tests: +1483 -24  
Others: +144 -4 (generated API artifacts)

## What

Capture immutable chat excerpts across local, Cloud, and side chats. Simplify their previews, number mixed chat/file attachments consistently, and navigate diagram references to the captured source block. Preserve clickable workspace filenames in new captures and make the annotation preview body navigate to its source.

## Why

Rendered selections differ from their Markdown source. Source membership/revision checks can reject valid formatted selections or invalidate an attachment after edits, rollback, or deletion. References should preserve the context selected by the user and remain deliverable independently of later history changes.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Formatting, code, and transformed blocks can fail substring-based source validation. | Capture-time UTF-16 source mapping preserves readable text and frozen raw source; transformed content uses an explicit broader-block fallback. |
| Sending depends on finding the source and a supported completed paired turn. | Snapshots send without source rehydration. Available completed-turn background is frozen once and deduplicated. |
| Chat previews have no shared ordinal reference across mixed attachments. Diagram source can appear as selected text. | `1. Selected text:` headers match provider labels; compact plain-text previews expand with Show more / Show less. A top-right flowchart badge hides diagram labels/source while preserving raw context. |
| Diagram navigation can fail to locate the selected transformed block. | A revision-checked source-block anchor distinguishes repeated diagrams; uncertain anchors scroll to the message without guessed highlighting. |
| The initial PR reserved an extra action row beneath every human message. | Restore the existing floating actions and branch-navigation layout; add no blank row. |
| Cloud message budgeting counts UTF-16 characters, so multilingual context can exceed its byte limit. | Budget the complete prepared payload in UTF-8 bytes; omit optional turn context first and preserve frozen retries. |
| Main, side-chat, and Cloud display payloads repeat frozen background messages that the UI never displays. | Omit only snapshot.turn from returned/display copies; retain raw source, navigation metadata, saved input, and AI delivery context. |
| A shared Cloud-sized limit rejects a 70 KiB local message with references. | Cloud uses 64 KiB; local main and side chats use 128 KiB, preserving frozen retries. |
| A workspace filename rendered as a button disappears from new excerpts; a filename-only selection fails. | Include explicitly marked filename buttons in capture and navigation, retaining readable text, exact raw source, and file-opening behavior. Toolbar and hidden controls stay excluded. |
| Only the selected-text header navigates to the source. | Clicking the preview body also navigates. Text selection, dragging, Show more / Show less, removal, and disabled controls remain separate. The header keeps keyboard navigation. |
| Rendering serializes an offset for every character into DOM attributes. | Retain bounded source metadata and calculate each selected element’s mapping once per capture. |
| New excerpt validation errors are always English. | Return translation keys and translate at the display boundary in all supported locales. |
| ![Before review fixes: reserved action rows and excerpt preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38c234c8-d6ae-4a51-9d93-b56893114528) | ![After review fixes: existing floating actions and preserved excerpt preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70a4cd6e-a52a-4355-8998-7ee9e4f68c99) |

The native comparison above uses the same seeded scratch transcript and 1200 × 900 viewport in the real Electron app: the originally reviewed PR before the earlier visual fixes, and code commit c32cb7bde after them. The current response filtering and budget follow-ups do not change this layout. The controller is stopped; no live-provider send is claimed. The native-build workaround is confined to disposable review worktrees and excluded from this diff. Screenshots are uploaded as GitHub attachments, not committed.

## How

- Add version-1 snapshot metadata to daemon DTOs, durable content, transcript summaries, drafts, and Cloud's existing display-content envelope; regenerate OpenAPI and frontend types.
- Retain structural validation, access boundaries, eight-annotation and separate 24 KiB readable/raw limits. Optional per-role turn background is bounded and omitted first when required by transport budgets.
- Compare captured payloads for idempotency conflicts; keep queue/retry payloads frozen. Preserve already-prepared legacy deliveries and upgrade only unsent legacy references.
- Send one numbered reference instruction per newly prepared message. Keep file capture/delivery semantics unchanged; add only its visible index. Keep raw source and completed-turn inspection controls out of the normal UI.
- Preserve rendered-text anchors for ordinary selections. Diagrams use source ranges plus bounded resize following, canceled by user interaction.

The filename correction applies to new captures. Older saved excerpts are not rewritten; when their previous text or positions no longer match, existing navigation can fall back to the source message without guessed highlighting.

Intentional boundaries: one settled source message per selection; native selectable text only. Cross-message selection, streaming capture, pixel selection, new fork eligibility, `@` references, summarization, and private Cloud control-plane changes are excluded.

## Testing

### Latest follow-up: `b09ea4098`

Merged `main` through `d1143d57b` and resolved the annotation-summary conflict while retaining the new attachment tiles. The filename correction and preview navigation are in `e5510e746`; the final commit only renames an inherited retry-delay variable to satisfy the pinned linter, preserving its 500 ms value.

Validated in isolated Linux checkouts with Node **24.22.2**, Go **1.27.1**, and golangci-lint **v2.13.2**:

- **Complete frontend:** 724 files passed, **12,788 tests passed**, seven skipped. The clean full run passed after restoring the Node SQLite binding following Electron verification.
- **Complete renderer smoke:** **180 passed, no retries**, including filename-only and mixed-prose capture, preview-body navigation, selection guards, exact highlighting, and frozen provider input. Both new filename flows also passed with interaction recordings enabled.
- All **191 focused tests** across capture, Markdown, annotation summaries, file previews, and source navigation passed. Both frontend typechecks and the renderer production build passed.
- Complete backend core and chat/session/store/SQLite race suites passed, as did build, vet, formatting, whole-tree lint, CLI E2E, the fresh-install container smoke test, public boundary, and API/SQL generation checks. After the lint-only rename, full shell-agent/shell-terminal race suites, backend build/vet, and whole-tree lint passed again.
- CI script tests, shared-package generation/typechecks/tests/builds, package dry runs, Node 22 lockfile compatibility, and the pinned secret scan passed. Browser postcondition integration and all three real-Electron control-boundary suites passed.
- Native Electron verification used the same seeded transcript and 1200 × 900 viewport on base `d1143d57b` and updated frontend `e5510e746`. The preview retains `src/app.ts`, and clicking its body highlights the exact source sentence. Both apps used isolated data under the container user's `~/.ao/dev/` and were stopped. No live-provider send is claimed. New screenshots and browser interaction recordings are saved locally; their paths are supplied in the chat handoff for attachment. The screenshots already embedded above document the earlier visual fixes.

Hosted validation on `b09ea4098`: **passed** in [CI run 42819179471](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42819179471) (17 successful jobs including ci-ok; 8 jobs skipped by lane policy), [secret scan](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42819179450), and [public boundary](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42819179591). Native Windows/macOS jobs are skipped by lane policy and are not claimed as passed. No publishing or deployment command was run.

### Earlier validation

Validated the merged branch in an isolated Linux container with Node **24.22.2**, repository-pinned Go **1.27.1**, and golangci-lint **v2.13.2**. No real AO data was used.

- Complete backend core and chat/session/store/SQLite race suites passed, along with backend build, vet, formatting, whole-tree lint, CLI E2E, and the fresh-install container smoke test. The final duration-name correction also passed the complete shell-agent race suite, build, vet, and whole-tree lint.
- Complete frontend run on application head `28b4e5119`: **710 files passed; one browser-history capacity test timed out; 12,593 tests passed, one timed out, seven skipped (711 files total)**. The complete history-store file passed all three tests when rerun alone with unchanged default timeouts (12.3 seconds for the capacity test). All 896 tests across 11 complete chat/excerpt/find/Markdown/file-lookup suites passed without unhandled errors.
- Both frontend typechecks, the renderer production build, CI script tests, Cloud client generation/drift/typecheck/tests, product UI typecheck/tests, and both package dry runs passed.
- Public boundary, API/SQL generation drift, Node 22 lockfile compatibility, and the pinned secret scanner passed.
- Guarded browser-navigation integration and the terminal, browser, and mobile control boundary tests passed in real Electron under Xvfb.
- Complete renderer smoke on `28b4e5119`: **174 passed, no retries**. Browser postcondition integration and all three real-Electron boundary suites also passed again after the chat-find merge.
- The application tree merged at `b2b4eb23f` exactly matches CI checkout `0086c103f`, whose backend, lint, typecheck, unit-test, boundary, and other successful jobs are recorded in [run 42665854158](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42665854158). Its new held-session streaming test also failed on upstream main without this PR. Commit `94155f758` bounds the fixture to one pending CDP dispatch; all original assertions, 120 ms nominal interval, CPU throttling, and timeouts remain unchanged. The complete held-session spec passed **4/4**, and the complete affected renderer shard passed **87/87 with two workers and no retries**. E2E typechecking passed.
- **Hosted checks passed on final head `94155f758`**: [CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42700761188) (17 successful jobs including both renderer shards and `ci-ok`, eight jobs skipped by lane policy), [secret scan](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42700760973), and [public boundary](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42700760846).

Focused chat/excerpt suites cover display omission, unchanged captured input, provider delivery, duplicate-send/retry identity, preserved navigation/diagram metadata, and explicit **64 KiB Cloud / 128 KiB local** budgets. Eight-reference fixtures assert that the serialized reduction is exactly the omitted background-turn properties, including a Cloud fixture saving more than 48,000 bytes.

Main through `be49556dd` is merged in `b2b4eb23f`; the earlier chat-find integration is in `d13592b33`. title: fix(desktop): title a Cloud session whose sandbox stopped responding
body:
## Review follow-up

- **"The card only shows briefly before the session goes back to the loader" (under ao-control-plane#53 as it stood):** fixed in #53 (d7e5396). A `sandbox_unresponsive` park now stays parked through the resume the app sends when a session is opened, messages, keystrokes and the daily re-check; only Retry (or a pause and a resume) starts it again. Verified live in this desktop app (main + this PR) against staging td 428 (main + #51 + #53):
  - opened the parked session: the card showed, and the app sent `POST /resume` (202) at the same second, exactly the path traced in the review;
  - three minutes later the card was still up, the VM still paused, and the control plane logged no restore or launch after the park;
  - after the VM was repaired, Retry on the card cleared it in about 5 s and the session answered a message sent from the composer.
- **Duplicate of #7833:** only one pair should land (#53 + this PR, or ao-control-plane#55 + #7833). #53 covers #55's cases; the choice is the maintainers'.
- **Minor, nested ternaries:** the title now comes from a code-to-title map (3b82226af1). A table test pins every title, and passes on the old ternaries too, so nothing changed.

## Problem

OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#53 stops repairing a Cloud session forever when its worker went silent and every repair failed (a Freestyle VM that stopped responding). It parks the session with the new startup error code `sandbox_unresponsive` instead of leaving it on the "Preparing your repository and agent" loader.

The desktop showed that as "This session couldn't start", which is wrong for a session that had been running.

## Fix

- `CloudSessionStartupError` titles `sandbox_unresponsive` "The sandbox stopped responding" (all 9 locales). The server's message ("The sandbox stopped responding: AO tried to restart the session's worker 4 times over 12 minutes and every attempt failed. The sandbox has been stopped. Retry to start it again.") and Retry are unchanged.
- `CloudCpSessionStartupError` documents the code.

Every other code renders as before, and an older control plane never sends this one. An older desktop shows the generic title with the same message and Retry.

## Screenshots

The real app (this branch) against staging, on a session the control plane parked after its worker repairs kept failing, dark theme:

| Parked | After Retry |
| --- | --- |
| ![parked card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/f7db8bcf8b7a1f8f7c4eb0a896b1557487fa782b/park-card.png?v=1) | ![recovered after Retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/f7db8bcf8b7a1f8f7c4eb0a896b1557487fa782b/park-recovered.png?v=1) |

Pressing Retry on the card restarted the sandbox; the worker was back in about 30 seconds and the message queued during the outage was answered.

## Tests

- `CloudSessionStartupError.test.tsx`: the new case shows the title (and not "This session couldn't start"), the message, and a Retry that calls `retrySessionStartup`. It fails without the change; the other 23 cases pass unchanged.

title: fix(claude): read the current login and finish the login terminal
body:
Code changes: +66 -5\
Tests: +249 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Fixes three defects in AO's Claude Code login check. Together they make a successful sign-in look like a failure:

1. AO's keychain lookup can read a stale item instead of the login Claude Code uses.
2. After a login, AO keeps using the `claude auth status` report from before it, for up to 5 minutes. A recheck reads as signed out and **new tasks are refused**.
3. The login terminal closes only on a verified login, so it stays open if AO can't verify online.

## Why

Fixes #7851

On the reporter's Mac, the login terminal says "Claude Code sign-in complete." but doesn't close, and the New Task screen keeps showing `no credential could be resolved for this provider`. The reporter also saw new tasks failing, then starting a few minutes later for no apparent reason. In the lab, a spawn was refused with `AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED` for 275s after a completed login, then worked once the cached report expired. Claude Code itself still works in a separate terminal, because it does its own auth.

The keychain there holds two `Claude Code-credentials` items. AO looks up by service only, while Claude Code 2.1.318 reads with `-a <user>`. Tested with the real `security` tool on a scratch keychain, a lookup without `-a` returns the least recently written item, and `-a` returned the current item in each order tested. Claude Code rewrites its own item when it refreshes a token, so after a refresh any leftover item wins the account-less lookup.

## Before / After

Reproduced in the real desktop app using a fake `claude`, the real `security` tool and a scratch keychain, starting from a tokenless stale item under account `unknown`; the login adds the current item.

| Before (`6eb2469b0d`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal prints "Claude Code sign-in complete." and stays open on **"Signed out"**, at least 16s later | Terminal closes about 2.5s after the login starts; the account row shows "Signed in as lab@example.com · Max" |
| Readiness after login: `cli_signed_out`, `credential_missing` (`cli_signed_in`, `credential_missing` once the report cache expired) | Readiness after login: `cli_signed_in`, `provider_unreachable` (the lab's deliberately dead proxy) |
| Composer: `no credential could be resolved for this provider`, with Retry | Models API reachable: `authorized`, `provider_accepted`, model list loads, no error |
| New task right after login: refused with `AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED` ("the project credential was rejected"), retried every 30s until it worked at t+275s, right after the report cache expired | New task right after login: starts immediately |

Controls on the base build: removing only the stale item changes `credential_missing` to `provider_unreachable`. A stale item holding an expired token gives `token_renewal_pending` and a different error, so the reporter's message points to a stale item with no usable token (or a failed read of it).

Screenshots are from the lab; `gh` can't upload them, so they'll be attached in a comment.

## How

- **Keychain (`agentcreds/keychain.go`):** per service, look up under Claude Code's account first, using its rule: `$USER`, then the OS user, then `claude-code-user` if that fails or isn't a valid name. If `security` reports that account has no item (exit 44), the old lookup still runs, so an item filed under another account name keeps working. Otherwise the account's result decides: another account's token never stands in for it, and a failed read (a denied prompt, say) isn't repeated without the account.
- **Report cache:** `InvalidateAgentAuthentication` cleared AO's readiness state but couldn't reach the adapter's cache, despite `Probe` documenting that a post-login check can't get a pre-login answer. It now calls a new optional `ports.AgentAuthCacheInvalidator`, which the Claude adapter implements.
- **Terminal:** Claude Code now counts `configured` as a finished login, like the existing `mimo-code` case. `configured` means the CLI confirms the login but AO couldn't verify it online, for example offline or behind a proxy.

Worth reviewing:
- **Hidden failure message:** if a login fails while another credential still reads as `configured` or `authorized`, the terminal closes and its failure message goes with it. This already happened for `authorized`; it now also applies to `configured`.
- **Another account's item:** with no item under the user's account, AO can still read another account's item, as it did before.
- **Login made outside AO:** AO only drops its cached report when something invalidates it, and nothing does for a login in another terminal. If the online check is also inconclusive, new tasks can still be refused for up to 5 minutes. Seen in the lab when the keychain changed behind AO's back; with a reachable API the online check decides instead.
- **Related, not changed:** #7672 (a stale CLI using up the discovery deadline) and #7677 (a long-lived Chat process holding old credentials) have different causes.

## Testing

Confirmed to fail with their fix removed: `TestKeychainPrefersClaudeCodeAccountOverOlderItem`, `TestKeychainDoesNotReplaceAccountItemWithAnotherAccounts`, `TestKeychainDoesNotWidenLookupAfterAccountReadFails`, `TestProbeDropsTheAdaptersCachedAuthentication`, and the new frontend terminal test. The remaining new tests pin existing or supporting behaviour and weren't checked that way: `TestKeychainStillReadsItemFiledUnderAnotherAccount`, `TestKeychainAccountFollowsClaudeCodeRule`, `TestKeychainItemMissingRecognizesARealExitStatus`, `TestPluginInvalidationDropsThePreLoginCLIReport`.

Passed locally:
- `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`
- `go vet` on the changed backend packages
- `go test -race -count=1` on `pkg/agentcreds`, `adapters/agent/claudecode`, `service/agent`, `service/agentauth`, `service/agentaccounts`, `adapters/agentaccount`
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend), `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`
- The new frontend test and the MiMo login test

**Real-app lab rerun on the final commit (`042b3b6351`):**
- A signed-out spawn is refused, the login terminal closes at t+2.5s, and a spawn right after login succeeds.
- A denied read of the account's item (simulated exit 51) makes no lookups without `-a`.
- A real exit 44 still falls back and finds an item under another account.

**Not run to completion locally; relying on CI.** The dev machine ran out of disk, so these have no valid local result:
- the full backend race suite
- `golangci-lint`
- the full frontend suite, and the wider harness settings tests
- the other frontend CI jobs

**Not tested:** the real Anthropic API, and the reporter's Mac. The lab used a fake `claude` and fake tokens. First-party `authorized` wasn't reachable there, so that row used a local models server through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, which goes through the same keychain read.

## What

Telemetry cleanup for PostHog events: one naming convention, `{product}.{object}.{past_tense_verb}`, plus fixes for the identity, install, session-end, onboarding, request-failure and setup gaps found on 0.14.9. It also adds a launch-time metric, `spawn_duration_ms`.

## Why

- Signed-in desktop users still sent launch events under a throwaway `anon_` ID, and a restarted or CLI-started daemon forgot the Cloud user.
- `ao.install.created` fired for existing installs.
- `ao.onboarding.step_completed{step=github_auth}` almost never arrived.
- Some `ao.sessions.ended` events had no `session_telemetry_id`.
- Request-failure 404s were dominated by a client bug.
- There was no honest launch latency per harness: chat sessions start asynchronously, so the old `duration_ms` measured enqueue time.
