Events not in the table keep their names. These are listed so nobody expects a rename: `ao.renderer.artifact_create_*`, `ao.renderer.automation_create_succeeded/failed`, `ao.renderer.cloud_*`, `ao.renderer.settings_save_failed`, `ao.renderer.notification_mark_read_failed`, `ao.renderer.open_in_editor_failed`, `ao.renderer.update_unsupported`, `ao.renderer.update_check_succeeded`, `ao.renderer.update_channel_changed`, `ao.renderer.support_submitted`, `ao.renderer.topbar_action_clicked`, `ao.renderer.review_auto_review_toggled`, `ao.renderer.session_state_unknown`, `ao.renderer.project_clone_succeeded`, `ao.session.relaunch_failed`, `ao.review.comment_resolved`, `ao.review.rereview_requested`, `ao.harness.update_idle_wait`, `ao.harness.update_resume_failed`, `ao.daemon.panic`, `ao.automation.created`, `ao.onboarding.step_abandoned`, `ao.onboarding.first_run_*`.

## How

- **Renames (all producers)**: the daemon, CLI (exported by the daemon), renderer and mobile now capture under the new names. The `ao.v2.*` alias maps are gone; only `session_management_summary` keeps its shipped exported name. Allowlists and sanitizers are keyed by the new names. `ao.cli.active` and `mobile.app.active` keep the existing once-per-UTC-day reservations, so there is no new polling. The two renderer "logs" events go to the renderer console, because the desktop has no persistent renderer log (see gaps).
- **Identity**: the desktop already POSTs `/internal/telemetry/identity`. The gaps were launch-time and restart:
  - The daemon now restores the bound Cloud user from `telemetry_bound_user` on start, after validating the ID format. A restarted or CLI-started daemon therefore exports under the Cloud ID.
  - Main passes `cloudUserId` in the renderer bootstrap only when the stored WorkOS session's user equals the daemon-recorded binding. The renderer then boots identified, so `app.active`, `app.loaded` and `first_opened` are no longer anonymous.
  - Sign-out still resets the renderer and rotates the daemon's anonymous ID. Signed-out activity is never attributed to the account, and `install_id` never changes.
- **Install / first open**: `ao.install.created` is removed. `ao.app.installed` additionally requires an empty store (no projects, no sessions); otherwise it spends its marker silently. `ao.app.first_opened` is claimed in main with an exclusive `telemetry_first_open_emitted` marker, on install day 0 with no sessions. Every install that ran a build sending `ao.install.created` already holds that file, so upgrades never send it.
- **Session end**: every termination path (kill, replacement, PR merge, issue close, runtime death) already reports through one recorder, and project sessions always mint their grouping row (FKs are on, and projects are soft-archived). The missing IDs come from standalone sessions, which had no project to group by. They now get an install-salted opaque `session_telemetry_id`, using the same salting as `project_id_hash`.
- **github_auth**: #7569 removed the only producer of this step. Before that, completion only fired on an in-place mount transition. The shared `GitHubSetupPanel` now reports `viewed` while setup is actually needed. `completed` is recorded for a viewed step wherever sign-in is observed: the panel, the first-run GitHub state, or the renderer resolving the daemon's GitHub login on a later launch.
- **Common properties**: `days_since_install`, `lifetime_sessions` and `is_signed_in` are on every desktop and daemon event. `is_signed_in` is false instead of absent without a binding. The renderer re-reads `lifetime_sessions` (new IPC `telemetry:getLifetimeSessions`) when the daemon wasn't ready at bootstrap.
- **`ao.requests.failed`**: a read-only aggregate of 0.14.9+ request failures showed no 401s. Most 404s were session workspace reads (`files`, `manifest`, `history`) answering `SESSION_WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` before an async start published its worktree.
  - The inspector count, branch summary and activity history now wait for `sessionWorkspaceReady`.
  - The event now carries the daemon's stable `error_code` (validated `[A-Z0-9_]`). `GITHUB_AUTH_INVALID` still reports, with its code.
  - The operation normalizer also no longer leaks side-chat UUIDs or shell-terminal IDs for routes without a template.
- **Feature flags**: flags load by default. `advanced_disable_flags` is deliberately left out of the init config, because in posthog-js 1.390.2 an explicit init value overrides the runtime `set_config` used to switch flags off. `opt_out_capturing` does not stop `/flags`, and `reset()` reloads flags (it also clears `setReloadingPaused`), so an in-session opt-out calls `set_config({ advanced_disable_flags: true })` before `opt_out_capturing` and `reset`, and opt-in re-enables and reloads them. `save_campaign_params` and `save_referrer` are off, so `/flags` carries no stored first URL or referrer (that path skips `before_send`). An opted-out launch never creates the client, and dev builds still get no bootstrap. Real-SDK tests cover no `/flags` after opt-out and no route in the `/flags` body. Reviewer recommendation still open: keep flags off until an experiment reads one (nothing in the app reads a flag yet). They stay on per task section 9 unless the owner decides otherwise; the Share usage analytics copy now mentions them.
- **`ao.setup.checked`**: a shell hook reuses the startup requirements query and agent readiness. It reads the GitHub credential probe's cached answer only and never triggers that probe, since the probe can be slow or interactive. It sends booleans (`git`, `tmux`, `gh`, `gh_signed_in`), counts, and sorted registry agent IDs. It fires the first time these answer and again when the signature changes; the signature is stored only after a successful capture. Requirement `detail` text, which holds paths, is never read.
- **`spawn_duration_ms`** (on `ao.sessions.spawned` and `ao.sessions.spawn_failed`):
  - Boundary: milliseconds on Go's monotonic clock (the start reading is not converted to UTC) from the session service accepting the spawn (every surface, including schedules, intake, orchestrators and cue, funnels through `spawnWithTelemetry`) to the session being usable. It excludes the agent's first reply.
  - A synchronous start is usable when Spawn returns. An asynchronous Chat start answers first, so the single `ao.sessions.spawned` now waits for `mark_ready`. Background failures emit `ao.sessions.spawn_failed` with the same boundary; previously they emitted nothing after counting as spawned.
  - The manager calls one provision observer from `setProvisionState`. `provisioning` opens an attempt, and the first `ready`/`failed` closes it, so repeated writes are ignored. A retry of a failed start is a new attempt timed from the retry, with no `duration_ms`.
  - The `first_for_install` claim is taken only by a start that became usable. An attempt interrupted by a daemon restart reports nothing, because it is never opened in the new process.
  - `duration_ms` keeps its old meaning (time to answer the request). `lifetime_sessions` still counts accepted sessions, including failed async starts; this is documented.
- **Activation (#7437)**: already merged. Verified on main that there is no renewal check in `shared/telemetry-policy.ts` and that the Windows rename retry is present. Nothing duplicated.
- **Docs**: `docs/telemetry.md` covers every change above and includes the full rename table.

## Changes after review

- Sign-out retires the telemetry binding durably on the desktop (new anonymous ID, binding and CLI summary removed) before sign-out completes, and on any launch that finds a binding without a stored sign-in, so a CLI-started daemon never restores a departed account.
- Workspace reads are gated on a new `workspacePublished` session field (the daemon has a recorded workspace) instead of provision state; OpenAPI and TS types regenerated.
- `spawn_duration_ms`: no GitHub lookup on the async launch path; `duration_ms` recorded when `manager.Spawn` returns; cancelled starts (kill mid-start, shutdown) report nothing; timed-out starts still report `spawn_failed`.
- `ao.setup.checked` waits for agent probes to settle and ignores fields not yet known; `ao.app.first_opened` is claimed only when about to be sent and never on an unknown session count; renderer `lifetime_sessions` refreshes after the desktop creates a session; an `ao.app.active` kill-switch entry no longer silences `ao.cli.active`.
- `telemetry_schema_version` is 3 on daemon, desktop and mobile, to separate current `ao.cli.invoked` / `ao.app.active` from the legacy firehose that uses the same names without a version. `docs/posthog-cost-controls.md` is rewritten for the new names, with a release gate: the live PostHog transformation and any allowlist must change before this release ships.

## Testing

- Backend: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and pinned `golangci-lint v2.13.2` (0 issues; run with `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.1` because the local Go 1.27.3 export data is newer than the linter supports).
- `go test ./...`: all packages I touched pass. Eight packages fail locally (`tmux`, `systemcheck`, `session_manager`, `cli`, `shellterm`, `integration`, `commandcode`, `opencodev2`): the identical 78 tests fail on a clean `origin/main` checkout on this machine (no tmux), and no failure is new.
- Frontend: `npx vitest run` (673 files, 11,520 tests pass), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`.
- Mobile: `npx vitest run` (267 files, 2,769 tests pass), `npm run typecheck`.
- New tests, all at real producer/sink boundaries, sanitized:
  - Every renamed daemon event exports under its new name, with no old allowlist key.
  - Renderer: every renamed event captured under its new name and never an old one; log-only events; legacy kill-switch names in Go and TS.
  - Mobile name registry.
  - Daemon identity across sign-in, restart, sign-out, restart and sign-in; malformed binding ignored.
  - Renderer identified boot, sign-out reset, re-identify, and no identified boot after a seen sign-out.
  - `boundCloudUserId` (symlink, traversal, malformed).
  - Fresh vs upgrade install; `claimFirstOpen` once, fresh-only, upgrade marker.
  - Standalone `session_telemetry_id`.
  - `github_auth` producer (panel) and completion after abandon / next launch.
  - Common properties; lifetime refresh; flags pause and resume.
  - `ao.setup.checked` builder, allowlist and hook (first, same, change, retry when unsent).
  - `requests.failed` `error_code` plus normalizer; workspace readiness gating.
  - Spawn: sync duration; async ready, failure, retry, settle-before-answer, error-after-async and unopened attempt; manager observer states and causes on the request context.

## Known gaps and disagreements

- Renderer "logs" events go to the renderer console; the desktop has no persistent renderer log to write to.
- The remaining lower-volume 404s (`GET /sessions/:id/interface-transition` and `GET /projects/:id` on deleted or stale items, link preview, etc.) are not fixed here. They can now be attributed by `error_code`.
- `ao.onboarding.second_session_spawned` and `ao.onboarding.cli_detected` are in the migration table but never shipped on main. No emitter was invented: the second session is `lifetime_sessions: 2`, and CLI detection shipped as `ao.cli.first_used`. `ao.usage.worker_pr_closed` and `ao.usage.daily_summary` were never shipped; the real `ao.prs.closed` is unchanged.
- Daemon death during an async start reports neither outcome for that attempt.

## Follow-ups (PostHog-side, not done here; need explicit approval and a team login list)

- Internal filter (section 8 descoped to PostHog): set the person property `is_internal = true` on the team's PostHog persons, and filter on it in the project's existing test-account filter (for example, define that filter's cohort by `is_internal = true`). The app sends no new property.
- Move dashboards and insights to the new names using the table above.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change (telemetry cleanup, as scoped)
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions
- [x] Before / After: no user-visible UI change; telemetry names and properties only (table above)
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Relevant local checks pass for the area touched (environmental failures identical on main noted above)

title: feat(artifacts): list only the deliverables an agent registers
body:
Code changes: +1847 -123  
Tests: +1708 -26  
Others: +839 -10  

## What

Agents now register deliverables with a new `ao artifact add` command, and artifact lists show only those. The list API still returns every file, each with a `registered` flag.

## Why

Fixes #7811. Every file in a session's artifact directory appeared as an artifact, so a page with its assets flooded the list. One session in the issue showed 68 artifacts for 5 deliverables.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Every file in the artifact directory is listed as an artifact | Only registered files are listed |
| 1 HTML page and 50 images in `assets/` list as 51 artifacts | 1 artifact, and the page still loads its images |
| Each file inside an `.icon` bundle is its own artifact | The bundle is one entry |
| A file past the 1000-file walk cap is dropped, including `brand.html` behind 1000+ `assets/` files | Registered files are always listed |
| No way to say what is a deliverable, and no feedback on what the user sees | `ao artifact add brand.html` prints `5 other files stay in the folder but won't be listed as artifacts.` and names unregistered root files |

## Screenshots

From the real Electron app on sample sessions. The sidebar count is 10 across sessions holding 1,020 files.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Artifacts page, gallery** ![gallery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/2545fc07e11d70f26f6f34a30023ee16e85523c0/1-artifacts-gallery.png) | **Artifacts page, list** ![list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/2545fc07e11d70f26f6f34a30023ee16e85523c0/2-artifacts-list.png) |
| **Session with registered files:** 11 files, 3 entries, the bundle counted once ![registered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/2545fc07e11d70f26f6f34a30023ee16e85523c0/3-session-registered.png) | **Nothing registered:** falls back to root files ![fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/2545fc07e11d70f26f6f34a30023ee16e85523c0/4-session-unregistered-fallback.png) |
| **Large session:** registered files listed past 1000+ assets ![large](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/2545fc07e11d70f26f6f34a30023ee16e85523c0/5-session-large.png) | **Bundle:** opens as one artifact ![bundle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/2545fc07e11d70f26f6f34a30023ee16e85523c0/6-bundle-open.png) |

## How

- **Mark, don't filter.** `artifactFiles` stays complete because `ao://` links, chat images, the file and version routes, the delete count and output type all depend on it. `SessionArtifactsView` looks up the open file in the full list, so a link to an unlisted file still opens.
- **One rule.** `deliverableArtifacts` in `packages/shared` decides what is listed, for desktop and mobile: registered entries, else root entries, else everything. Sessions from before this change, and agents that never register, take that fallback. No backfill, by design.
- **One writer.** `ao artifact add` is the only writer. `ao report --artifact` and `ao render --artifact` keep their jobs and register nothing, so a deliverable needs both commands to be listed and reported. The prompts say so.
- **One row per artifact, with an ID that survives renames.** A new `session_artifacts` table has one row per tracked file or bundle directory: `id`, `session_id`, `path`, `registered_at` (NULL when not registered), the file's identity, and `previous_paths`. See "Renames keep the artifact" below. A row with no file is ignored, so an agent rewriting a file through delete and create keeps its registration. A session has no limit on deliverables; 100 only bounds one request. The session list reads these rows in one batched statement.
- **Edits need no command.** Registration is by path, and version capture is unchanged.

Mobile viewer: swipe and the filmstrip (#7681) page through the listed artifacts only. A hidden file opened by a link opens as a page of its own.

Bundles: a bundle row opens a real file inside it and has no row actions, because Delete would reach only that one file. Expanding a bundle into its files isn't in this PR.

Decisions taken from the plan's recommendations, for review:

1. Unregistered root files are hidden once any file is registered.
2. ~~Renames rely on the prompt rule.~~ Superseded: a rename keeps the artifact. See below.
3. `ao artifact add` always names unregistered root files, which covers resuming an old session, where a first registration hides its other root files.

This goes beyond the issue's "grouped or collapsed" wording: unlisted files aren't shown in any artifact list. The acceptance items should be updated to match.

## Renames keep the artifact

Added after the regression run above. The table and screenshots there predate it.

A renamed file used to be a new file, and its share link stayed published under the old name. The renamed file offered **Publish** instead of **Republish**, and publishing it made a second link. Now a rename, including a plain `mv`, keeps the artifact.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mv draft.html final/report.html` | New file: unregistered, no history, no link | Same artifact: same ID, still registered, history moved, no new version and no rename entry |
| Share on the renamed file | **Publish**, which makes a second link | **Republish** on the same link, under the new name |
| `ao://…/artifacts/draft.html` in an old chat message | "Unavailable" | Opens `final/report.html` |
| Renamed while open in the viewer | Closes | Stays open |
| Agent prompt and skill | "run `ao artifact add` again on the new path" | "renames or moves need no further command; a copy is a new file" |

**How a rename is recognised**
- Each row records the file's device, inode and birth time (`sessionartifacts/fileid_*.go`).
- A tracked path that disappears, while an untracked path shows the same file, is a rename. A copy or a newly written file never matches.
- Linux birth times come from a coarse clock: on ext4, a file written right after another was deleted can reuse its inode *and* birth time. So on Linux the identity also holds the inode generation (`FS_IOC_GETVERSION`, ext4/btrfs/XFS), or the modification time where there is none. The tests caught this.
- Windows has no identity, so a rename there is still a delete and a new file.

**Where it runs and what moves**
- Rename detection (`Observation.Changes`, a pure planner) runs in the version capturer's `Track` on every session read and every poll.
- A rename moves the row and its version rows to the new path in one transaction (`ApplySessionArtifactChanges`). Rows wait at a path no file can have, so files that swap paths never collide.
- A file moved over another keeps the destination's artifact. The same holds when the destination's file was deleted earlier but its artifact is registered or has version history: it keeps its ID, history and share link, and the moved file's own row goes as a gone file's does. So the outcome does not depend on whether a scan ran while the path was empty, as in `rm report.html`, then writing `report.tmp.html` and moving it onto `report.html`. Only a row with neither gives its path to the moved file.
- Version capture appends only while the file is still at its path, under the same lock, so a rename never strands a version at the old path.
- The migration makes every path with version history an artifact, so existing files keep their history.

**Links**
- The API returns `id` and `previousPaths` on each file.
- The desktop keys share records by `[baseUrl, session, "", artifactId]`. A record keyed by path from before this change moves to the ID key the first time the file is inspected.
- `artifactAtPath` (`packages/shared`) opens a link to an earlier path.

**Cloud**
- The contract adds optional `SessionArtifact.id`, `previousPaths` and `WorkerArtifactCommitInput.moved`, and lets a share update carry a new name.
- The control plane side is OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#74.

**Merge order:** this PR first. The cloud side stores registration on `ao_session_artifacts` instead of a new table, so `ao artifact add` waits there for the file to sync. The control plane PR vendors this contract change and must re-sync from `main` after this merges. Until that ships, a cloud agent has no `ao artifact add`, so cloud sessions use the root-folder fallback. Then OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#74, after `npm run contracts:sync`: it uses this PR's contract additions.

Until #74 deploys, republishing a renamed file is refused with 409 `artifact_share_name_changed`. Local renames already keep their ID, registration and history.

## Regression: `ao artifact add`

Run on a throwaway daemon and data directory with the built `ao` binary, then in the real Electron app against that data, on `ba425b0ff1`, before the later rebases onto `main`. Those brought in #7875, #7681 and others, so the run and screenshots predate them. **42 CLI and API cases passed, and all 7 UI checks passed.** Sessions were seeded rather than spawned, so no agent ran these commands.

| Area | Cases | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validation | 14 | No session, no paths, empty path, unknown session, missing file, plain directory, the folder itself, relative and absolute paths outside it, a symlink, `.versions/`, one bad path registers nothing, 0 and 101 paths in a request |
| Register | 8 | Relative and absolute paths, a bundle, a nested file, repeat, an uncleaned path, names with `$` and an apostrophe, several calls adding up |
| Summary | 4 | Counts and root names, singular wording, one line when nothing else exists, more than 5 root files truncated |
| Listing API | 2 | Every file returned whether or not any is registered |
| Lifecycle | 5 | An edit stays registered, a rename needs a new add and its old row is harmless (superseded, see below), delete and recreate stays registered |
| One writer | 1 | `ao report --artifact` writes `report_outputs` and registers nothing |
| Delete | 4 | User delete of a registered and an unregistered file, archive with delete artifacts, deleting an archived session |
| Limits | 2 | 320 deliverables in one session, and files past the 1000-file walk stay listed |
| Concurrency | 1 | 24 parallel adds lose nothing |
| Restart | 1 | Registrations survive a daemon restart |
| UI | 7 | Sidebar count, gallery, list, session panel, root fallback, no root files shows everything, a bundle opens as one entry |

Not covered: `ao render --artifact` live, because it needs a running agent controller (`TestRenderArtifactKeepsThePageOrWarns` and `TestSaveRenderAsArtifactWritesTheServedPage` cover it), opening an unlisted file by link in the real app (component test only), the mobile app, and cloud sessions, because #54 isn't deployed to staging.

## Testing

- See Regression above for the end-to-end run.
- `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint`, `npm test` (frontend), `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`, `npm run sqlc` and `npm run api`.
- New tests: walk cap, path validation, bundles, the store, service, controller and CLI, the shared rule, and the desktop lists including opening an unlisted file by link.
- Rename work, in this sandbox (Linux, ext4):
  - `go test ./...` passes except `integration` and `service/shellterm`. Both are already listed below and neither is touched.
  - New tests: the planner against real renames, copies, delete-and-write, swaps, moves over another file, moves onto a deleted registered or versioned file under every scan timing, renamed directories and bundles, and rename-then-edit (`identity_test.go`); a real `mv` keeping version history in the capturer; the store's moves, swaps, drops and stale plans; share URLs by artifact ID.
  - Desktop: a renamed file finds its link and republishes under the new name; a path record moves to the ID key; `artifactAtPath`; old-path links; a renamed file stays open.
  - `npm run typecheck` (frontend, cloud-client) passes, as do the touched vitest files.
  - Not run: `golangci-lint`, and the macOS-specific identity code, which is vetted with `GOOS=darwin` but not exercised. Please check the macOS rename path in the app.

Failures in those local runs, none in code this PR touches or caused by it:

- Reproduced on clean `main`: `TestBrowserRequiresSessionAndValidWait` and four `TestSpawn_*` tests that report tmux as missing.
- Not baselined, in packages this PR doesn't change: `adapters/agent/{claudecode,codex,commandcode,opencodev2}`, `adapters/runtime/tmux`, `integration`, `service/shellterm`, `service/systemcheck`.
- Frontend `src/main/browser-*` tests, and mobile `uitextview-selection-color`, after installing with `--ignore-scripts`, which skips native builds and dependency patches.
- `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` failed once in the full run and passed alone.

Not run or not verified locally, so check these in CI or by hand:

- The mobile app.
- Frontend `typecheck` output was filtered to the touched files, because `packages/product-ui` dependencies weren't installed. `packages/cloud-client` typecheck did not run (`tsgo` wasn't installed).
- `go test -race` on the backend, and `cloud-contract-compat`.

## Review fixes in 3d8a03ba6e

- Batched session reads now retain `has_versions`, so a replacement move keeps the destination's saved history and snapshot bytes.
- Registration records the file identity in the same transaction as registration, so a new file or bundle can be renamed immediately without waiting for a scan.
- A published filename change now offers Republish even when content and modification time are unchanged, updating the same public link.
- Added real service/store/capturer regressions and a popover regression. The focused `artifactversions`, `sessionartifacts`, `service/session` and SQLite store suites pass, as do all 29 ShareArtifactPopover tests.
- The requester manually tested the main artifact UI in the real Electron app with isolated sample data before these fixes and confirmed it works. The rename/history fixes were verified with the regression tests.
- Full backend race, frontend typecheck and full frontend test runs were interrupted at the requester's instruction to stop background tests. They are not claimed as passed; the new head must pass GitHub CI before merge.

## Checklist

title: fix(session): report spawn step failures on timeout
body:
## What

A spawn timeout now includes the best-effort step failures that preceded it. The collector records default branch resolution and base ref refresh failures, and `toSpawnAPIError` appends them to the `SPAWN_TIMEOUT` message.

## Why

The spawn pipeline logged why a step failed, then discarded that reason when the deadline expired. Users saw only `Session spawn timed out before the agent could start`, so an unreachable origin looked the same as a broken daemon.

Fixes #6683

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `Session spawn timed out before the agent could start` | `Session spawn timed out before the agent could start: default branch resolution: resolve repository default: context deadline exceeded; base ref refresh: git fetch origin main: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` |

## How

- `spawnDiagnostics` travels in the spawn context, so concurrent spawns for different projects never share notes.
- `Spawn` wraps a deadline error in `SpawnTimeoutError` only when notes exist. The wrapper still unwraps to `context.DeadlineExceeded` and the workspace stage sentinel.
- Notes pass through `agentlaunch.RedactValues` with the project env, and the list is capped at five entries.
- Error kind and code stay `Conflict` and `SPAWN_TIMEOUT`. Clients that switch on the code are unaffected.
- This covers the synchronous spawn path. Async chat spawns report through their own provisioning path and are unchanged.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go test ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/service/session/ -run 'TestSpawnTimeoutAggregatesBestEffortStepFailures|TestSpawnTimeoutReportsBestEffortStepFailures' -count=1` passes.
- The same tests pass with `-race`.
- `cd backend && go build ./...` passes.
- The full `session_manager` package has one environment failure, `TestSpawn_EarlyFailurePreservesNonEmptyScratchWorkspace`, because `tmux` is not installed on this machine. It is unrelated to this change.

title: fix(chat): edit a message in place so nothing moves
body:
Code changes: +329 -162\
Tests: +149 -8\
Others: +27 -0 (translations)

## What

Editing a chat message now happens inside its own bubble, and nothing on the page moves when the edit opens.

- The textarea holds only the text you wrote. Attachments stay where the bubble shows them, above the text, instead of AO's hidden "Attached files (read these files in the workspace): - .ao/attachments/…" suffix showing up as editable text.
- The bubble keeps its fill, padding, width, text size and author name, and draws no ring.
- Cancel and Send sit on the "Worked for" line under the message, right-aligned with the bubble. An info icon next to them explains that an edit starts a new branch.

## Why

Before this change, clicking Edit swapped the bubble for a full-width composer card. The card was at least two rows tall, had its own padding and a footer row, and hid the author name, so the reply and everything below it jumped. The edit box also put AO's internal suffix into the textarea, where people could accidentally edit or delete it, and listed the image twice: once as a path and once as a bare "image/png" chip.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Clicking Edit replaces the bubble with a full-width card, at least two rows tall | The bubble itself becomes the editor. In the real renderer, opening it moved the reply 0px and kept the bubble's width and height |
| The textarea holds the text plus the "Attached files…" suffix | The textarea holds only the text you wrote |
| A bare "image/png" chip with no preview sits under the text | Attachments render exactly as in the bubble, above the text, with no duplicate chip |
| The branch note and the ✕ and ↑ buttons take a footer row inside the card | An info icon (the branch note in its tooltip), Cancel and Send sit on the "Worked for" line |
| Send is enabled on an unchanged message | Send stays off until the text or attachments change, except when retrying an uncertain delivery |
| A non-image file is only reachable by editing its path line | A file chip's icon turns into a remove button on hover, so the chip keeps its size |

## How

- **In place:** `HumanMessage` renders `HumanMessageEditor` with the bubble's own classes, its excerpt summary and its cloud attachments, so the editor draws the same box. The author name stays visible while editing.
- **Sizing:** the textarea shares a grid cell with a hidden copy of the draft (`.chat-human-edit-field`), so the box fits its text the way the bubble did. A zero-width space, not a trailing space, gives a trailing newline its line without widening the box. Past the bubble's ten-line fold the textarea scrolls. Deleting text never narrows the box below its starting width.
- **Actions:** Cancel and Send float, like the hover actions, on the "Worked for" line the turn reserves one row gap (10px) under the bubble. With a branch navigator they take the navigator's in-flow row. The busy and error messages go in the same row. The branch note is the field's accessible description and the info icon's tooltip.
- **Attachments:** `StagedAttachmentItems` moves into its own file, so the bubble and the editor share one list. In both, attachments sit above the text. In an edit, a file chip's icon becomes a remove button on hover. Images have no remove, because the backend's `EditMessage` always resends the original image data.
- **Split and recombine (unchanged from the first commit):** the editor still takes and publishes the full prompt text. It splits off the staged block with `stagedAttachmentParts` and rebuilds it with `withAttachmentReferences`, and it skips re-splitting text it published itself, so a whitespace-only draft isn't wiped.
- **Strings:** adds `chat.edit.cancelAction` ("Cancel") and `chat.edit.sendAction` ("Send") in all 9 locales, plus `chat.attachment.remove` from the first commit. The buttons keep "Cancel edit" and "Send edited message" as accessible names.
- **Contrast spec:** the message-edit case measures the Send label's text, since the button no longer has an icon.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` in `frontend/`: 0 errors.
- `vitest run` on `HumanMessageEditor`, `ChatTimelineItems`, `ChatQueuedAttachments`, `ChatWorkspace` and `src/renderer/i18n`: all pass. New tests cover Send staying off until the text or attachments change, the branch note as the field's description, and attachments sitting above the text.
- Real renderer on a settled two-turn conversation with a file attached, dark and light themes: opening the edit moved the reply 0px, the bubble kept its width and height, and the info icon, Cancel and Send were centered on the "Worked for" line, with Send's right edge on the bubble's.
- Playwright `chat-contrast` (all four theme and transparency variants) and `chat-attachment-open` on Chrome, on the pushed head: pass. The pasted-image case in `chat-attachment-open` once timed out on "Orchestrator is starting" under load, then passed when run alone.

Not run locally, to be verified in CI: the full frontend vitest suite and the rest of the renderer smoke suite. No Go code changed.

title: feat(clone): stream git clone steps into the clone dialog
body:
Code changes: +390 -31\
Tests: +328 -24\
Others: +227 -9 (generated OpenAPI spec and TS types, translations)

## What

While a repository clones, the Clone a Git repository dialog shows the step git is on, one line at a time: `remote: Enumerating objects · 3s`, then `Receiving objects · 45% · 7s`, then `Resolving deltas · 80% · 12s`. Git's percent and the timer tick in place; each new step slides in from below as the last one slides up and fades. The duplicated "Large repositories can take…" hint is gone.

## Why

While cloning, the dialog said twice that large repositories take minutes: once in the destination line and again in a hint under the spinner. A long clone showed only a timer, so a slow download looked the same as a stuck one.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The long-clone sentence appears twice: "Cloning into … Large repositories can take a few minutes." and, under the spinner, "Large repositories can take several minutes. AO retries temporary connection failures automatically." (screenshot 1) | It appears once, and the line under it is the live clone status (screenshot 2) |
| `Cloning repository · Ns` for the whole clone | The step git is on, with git's percent when it prints one and the timer ticking in place: `remote: Enumerating objects · 13s`, `Receiving objects · 45% · 15s`, `Resolving deltas · 80% · 20s`, `Updating files · 100% · 21s`, then `Checking checkout` (screenshots 3 and 5, taken before the percent was added; dark theme in 6) |
| No transition | Each new step rises in from below while the previous one slides up and fades, clipped to one line: 240 ms in, 200 ms out, instant with reduced motion (screenshot 4, captured mid-handover) |
| The hint promised automatic retries | When a retry starts, the row says `Connection dropped, retrying` |
| `POST /api/v1/projects/clone/prepare` answers once, after git exits | New `POST /api/v1/projects/clone/prepare/stream` sends `data: {"progress":{"phase":"receiving_objects","attempt":1}}` for each step, then `data: {"result":{…}}` or `data: {"error":{…}}` with the usual API error envelope |

Screenshot 1 is from the base build. Screenshots 2–7 are from the desktop app on this branch, with the clone stream stubbed in the page. Cancel still works (screenshot 7). They are attached below.

## How

- **Daemon.** `prepareClone` takes an optional progress callback. When one is passed, git runs with `--progress`, and its stderr goes through `cloneStderr`, which splits on `\r` and `\n`. It maps git's progress titles (git runs with `LC_ALL=C`) to a fixed phase enum, reads the percent git prints on that line, and reports when the phase or the percent changes. No git text leaves the daemon, because git can print a URL that contains credentials.
- **Retry classification.** Lines that aren't progress still go into the existing 32 KiB buffer used to classify retries, and progress lines stay out of it. Without that, a long progress run could push git's final error out of the buffer and break retry detection.
- **Route.** `prepareCloneStream` writes SSE `data:` frames of `ClonePrepareStreamEvent`, each carrying exactly one of `progress`, `result` or `error`. Errors use the same envelope as the JSON route through the new `envelope.StreamError`, which is split out of `WriteError` without changing that function's output. A mutex stops a late progress event from following the final one. The route gets the same 30-minute clone budget as `/clone/prepare`.
- **Manager.** `Manager` gains `PrepareCloneWithProgress`. `PrepareClone` and `Clone` behave as before.
- **Renderer.** `usePreparedClone.prepare` reads the stream when it is given `onProgress`. On 404 or 405 it falls back to the JSON route, which covers older remote daemons. `CloneRepositoryDialog` renders one status row keyed by phase and attempt inside `AnimatePresence`, and reuses the chat's live-row `chat-working-shimmer`. Phase names and two shared formats (`step · time`, `step · % · time`) are in all nine catalogs, and `createProject.cloneSlowHint` is removed.
- **Intentional omissions.** Size and speed are not sent: the review follow-up asked for the percent, and the line stays one step at a time. `POST /projects/clone` and the CLI are unchanged.
- **Reviewer focus.** The `envelope.WriteError` split, and the phase labels, which keep git's `remote:` prefix for steps that run on the remote.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go vet ./... && gofmt -l .`: clean.
- `cd backend && go test -p 2 ./...`: 213 packages pass. Two packages that this change doesn't touch fail on this Mac:
  - `adapters/agent/commandcode`: `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders`, which depends on the local git `user.email` include.
  - `service/shellterm`: three `TestCue*` tests, which depend on the local shell setup.

  All four fail the same way on a clean `main` here.
- New Go tests:
  - `TestCloneStderrReportsPhasesAndKeepsErrorsClassifiable`: 2,000 progress redraws, then a transient error that is still classified.
  - `TestCloneWithProgressReportsGitPhasesAndRetries`: a fake git prints progress and fails once with `connection reset`.
  - `TestPrepareCloneStreamSendsProgressThenResult` and `TestPrepareCloneStreamEndsWithErrorEnvelope`.
  - `TestCloneRoutesUseExtendedTimeout`, extended to cover the stream route.
- `npm run api`: regenerated `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`.
- Percent follow-up (`80dafaad41`): the clone service, controller, `httpd`, `apispec` and CLI tests pass, as do `npm run typecheck` and the dialog, flow, hook and i18n vitest files (184 tests). New checks: redraws at the same percent report once, and a new percent ticks in place without a second line.
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`: passes.
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2` on `CloneRepositoryDialog`, `CreateProjectFlow`, `usePreparedClone`, `src/renderer/i18n`, `Sidebar` and `lib/api-client`: all 406 tests pass. New tests cover streamed steps, events split across reads, the stream's error envelope, and the 404/405 fallback.
- Renderer smoke, run locally on Chrome: `clone-recovery`, `clone-preparation-lifecycle` and `project-agent-management` (8 tests) pass. They now stub `/clone/prepare/stream` with server-sent events, and the specs that assert no clone starts count both clone routes.
- Real desktop app (isolated lab instance on :3014), with the clone routes answered by an in-page stub so nothing was cloned: pushed each phase, captured frames mid-handover and settled in light and dark, and checked that Cancel aborts the stream.
- Not run locally, so this relies on CI:
  - golangci-lint: not installed on this machine.
  - The full 520-file renderer vitest suite and the full renderer smoke run: too heavy for this 8 GB Mac.
  - The Docker-based cli-e2e and gitleaks jobs: Docker isn't installed.
  - Local Node is 22; CI pins 24.

## Checklist

title: fix(browser): stop Browser opening on session switch and cut toggle jank
body:
Code changes: +220 -28  
Tests: +180 -10  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Three Browser panel fixes in the desktop app:

1. Switching to a session no longer opens its Browser panel by itself.
2. Opening and closing the inspector (Browser included) no longer janks through the slide.
3. Switching to a session whose Browser shows a page no longer flashes black.
4. The live page tracks the inspector slide from the first frame instead of jumping in behind the panel.

## Why

**Browser opening on switch.** `SessionView` reveals Browser once per explicit agent `open` / `tab-new` command. It accepts either the `started` or the `finished` event, because a fast command's two events can land in one React render. The per-session dedup set resets on every switch. So a command that **started while the user was on another session** (that event was filtered out by view id) and **finished after they switched in** looked new, and opened Browser one or two seconds after arrival. Agents run `ao browser open` constantly and page loads take seconds, so this is the common case. Separately, an orchestrator session opened Browser on its first *passive* activity (snapshot, click, ...), which CLAUDE.md says should only badge.

**Toggle jank.** I profiled the real dev app with Chromium traces, long-animation-frame entries, and rAF frame deltas on a 120 Hz display. Three causes, largest first:

| Cause | Cost per toggle (traced) |
| --- | --- |
| On the translucent macOS window (the default), `publishBrowserHole` wrote `--browser-hole-*` to `:root`'s inline style on every frame of the slide. Custom properties on `:root` inherit everywhere, so each write restyled the whole document. | ~41 full recalcs × ~5.6 ms (~290 elements each) |
| The tab strip's ResizeObserver (`useTabScrollEdges`) read `scrollWidth` mid observer pass, right after the terminal refit dirtied layout, which forced a synchronous layout every frame. | ~140 ms forced layout |
| The terminal refit on every frame of the 0→900 px width animation: an xterm buffer reflow plus a PTY resize (a SIGWINCH redraw by the agent), ~36 times per toggle. DESIGN.md §10 says the inspector collapses "without reflowing the active terminal/chat into an unusable transient width". | ~45 ms `updateScrollbar` + reflow, plus agent redraw output |

Native `WebContentsView` bounds updates were **not** a cause: about one cheap IPC per frame.

**Black flash on switch.** The panel is transparent over a live native page. On switch, the old view was hidden by a post-paint effect cleanup (~40 ms), page state reset to empty, and the new view was shown only after the `ensure` IPC answered and another frame passed. That left 100–150 ms with no page under the transparent panel.

**Page lagging the slide.** The native page is not a DOM node, so it follows the panel only through `setBounds`. The hook drove that from ResizeObservers, which miss the panel's transform; on open the first update arrived ~110 ms into the 300 ms slide (the panel had already moved 470 px), so the page jumped in behind it and then stepped on most frames.

**Is the hidden browser still rendering?** I checked this directly. A probe page counts rAF callbacks and 10 ms timer ticks and runs a CSS animation:

| Probe page state | rAF/s | timer ticks/s | page CPU | GPU process CPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visible in Browser | 120 | 100 | 5.8% | 5.6% |
| Inspector closed | ~4.5 | 100 | 0.6% | 0.9% |
| User on another session | ~1 | 100 | 0.7% | 0.9% |

The hidden view is already `setVisible(false)` and parked offscreen, so it stops painting and compositing. Its JS timers do keep running at full rate, and it reports `visibilityState: "visible"`, because tabs are created with `backgroundThrottling: false`. I left that alone on purpose: #6127 added it so the mobile live stream can capture hidden pages, and agent automation drives hidden pages all the time. Throttling them would slow every background agent command. It is also not what made the toggle lag: hidden-page CPU is under 1%.

## Before / After

Mean of 5 open + 5 close toggles in the real dev app (isolated data, translucent window, 120 Hz, Browser showing a live page). Each window is 700 ms around the 300 ms slide.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Chat session, open: p95 frame **25.0 ms**, **6.4** frames over 20 ms | p95 **10.0 ms**, **1.0** frames over 20 ms |
| Chat session, close: p95 **25.6 ms**, **6.6** frames over 20 ms | p95 **10.8 ms**, **1.4** frames over 20 ms |
| Terminal session, open: p95 **46.6 ms**, **10.6** frames over 20 ms, 51 frames delivered | p95 **10.8–16.8 ms**, **2–3** frames over 20 ms, 78–80 frames delivered |
| Terminal session, close: p95 **37.4 ms**, **10.2** frames over 20 ms | p95 **9.0–13.8 ms**, **2.2–2.4** frames over 20 ms |
| Style recalc during a slide: ~5.6 ms each, ~290 elements | ~0.7 ms each, ~37 elements |
| Agent `ao browser open` starts while the user is on session A; they switch to B before it finishes → **B's Browser pops open** ~1.5 s later | B stays closed; the Browser tab gets the activity badge |
| Orchestrator's first passive browser command → Browser opens | Badge only |
| Open the inspector: no page bounds sent for the first ~110 ms of the slide, then one jump of ~470 px | Bounds sent on every frame from the first, matching that frame's DOM position (41 sends over the slide) |
| Switch from a session with the inspector closed to one showing Browser: page placed 36 px low and short (y=123, h=726) for ~100 ms, then jumps up | Page placed at its final rect (y=87, h=762) on the destination's first painted frame |
| Switch between two sessions with Browser open: old view hidden at ~40 ms, new one shown at 70–112 ms, panel empty/black in between | New view shown and old one hidden in the same tick at commit (~45 ms, before first paint); panel stays live throughout |

These are timing and behavior changes, so the table carries measurements, not screenshots. A `ao browser open` / `ao preview` issued while you are on the session still reveals Browser exactly as before.

The remaining one or two slow frames per terminal toggle are the single refit when the slide lands, which replaces the ~36 per-frame refits.

## How

- `useBrowserView`: the agent-activity listener records which command IDs it saw *start* for the current session. It clears that set on session switch and stamps each event with `startObserved`.
- `SessionView`: an `open` / `tab-new` reveal requires `startObserved`; otherwise it badges, like passive activity. The orchestrator path badges instead of calling `setInspectorOpen(true)`.
- `styles.css` + `useBrowserView`: `--browser-hole-*` are `@property` registered with `inherits: false`, written on `.app-shell-root`, and pulled into its `::before` with `inherit`. The mask was checked in the app and still tracks the page rect.
- `XtermTerminal`: while the inspector gap is `data-motion="animated"`, ResizeObserver deliveries schedule the existing stable fit instead of resizing the grid. A `transitionend` on that gap's `width` flushes the fit right when the slide lands. Drag-resizing is unchanged and still live.
- `useBrowserView` (switch): each session's last native view id, page state and tabs are cached. On the destination's first frame (not at React's commit, where the address bar still renders inline before moving into the top bar), the hook measures and shows the cached view, then hides the departing one. The guard render shows the cached page instead of an empty one. `ensure` still runs and refreshes everything. Nav and tab events for off-screen views update their cached state, so switching back never shows an address bar from before an agent navigated that page; the swap always hides the departing view, even when `ensure` answers first with a recreated view. The ensure effect's cleanup now hides only the view its own run owned, so it can't hide the view the swap just showed.
- `useBrowserView` (slide): a `transitionrun` on the inspector gap or container (width/transform) starts a per-frame `measureAndSend` loop that stops on `transitionend`/`transitioncancel`, with a 1 s backstop. It runs only while the browser slot is active, so a Summary or Files slide with Browser hidden sends nothing.
- `useTabScrollEdges`: ResizeObserver updates are coalesced into one `requestAnimationFrame`. Scroll updates stay synchronous.

## Testing

- New: a `transitionrun` on the inspector gap sends bounds every frame until `transitionend`, then stops; with Browser hidden it sends none.
- New: a page navigated while its session was off screen shows its new URL on switch-back; the departing view is hidden even when `ensure` returns a recreated view first.
- New: switching back shows the session's cached view (with its page) before `ensure` answers, and shows it before hiding the departing view.
- New: `useBrowserView` marks only commands whose start it saw, including after a switch away and back. `SessionView` does not reveal for an `open` that started before the switch; an orchestrator's first activity only badges.
- Existing reveal tests now pass `startObserved: true`, matching what the hook emits for commands seen starting.
- Verified in the real Electron app (`ao-desktop-dev`, isolated data). I reproduced the switch bug with a slow page and `ao browser open` before the fix and confirmed it after, plus the control (a command started on the session still reveals). The terminal refits to the right width after open and close. Measurements are above.
- Per request, I did not run tsc/vitest locally; CI is the check.

## Risks / follow-ups

- A command that started before you arrived now only badges. That is deliberate: you were not there when it was asked for.
- The preview poller re-publishes a workspace-file preview (bumping `previewRevision`) whenever the agent rewrites that file. That still reveals Browser while you are on the session. It is not a switch-time pop, so it is out of scope here, but it is another "opens by itself" source worth a follow-up.

title: fix(desktop): clean light transparency and instant theme switching
body:
Code changes: +147 -45\
Tests: +43 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

macOS window transparency, light mode and theme switching:

- **Light + transparency** now looks like a native light app: a bright frosted sidebar and top bar over a solid center panel. Before, the whole window was one flat gray plate with gray-on-gray cards.
- **Light mode (transparency on or off):** the selected top-bar tab matches the center panel with a visible hairline, and top-bar icons use the full foreground instead of muted gray.
- **Theme switching with transparency on** is an instant single-frame cut. Before, the page froze for ~250 ms and the old theme's tint showed through the new one.

Dark mode is visually unchanged. With transparency off, theme switching keeps its current behavior.

## Why

Light + transparency looked muddy, and switching light/dark with transparency on felt laggy, with the sidebar and top bar changing at a different moment than the rest of the window.

## Before / After

Light theme, transparency on, same window and data, over a light and a dark wallpaper (native on-screen captures of the dev window only).

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: light wallpaper, whole window one flat gray](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/62a86aaa4068d33612258fb8e373bf41e6238ad0/before-light-wallpaper.png) | ![After: light wallpaper, bright frosted sidebar, solid content](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/62a86aaa4068d33612258fb8e373bf41e6238ad0/after-light-wallpaper.png) |
| ![Before: dark wallpaper, wallpaper tint muddies the whole window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/62a86aaa4068d33612258fb8e373bf41e6238ad0/before-dark-wallpaper.png) | ![After: dark wallpaper, frosted sidebar picks up the wallpaper, content stays solid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/62a86aaa4068d33612258fb8e373bf41e6238ad0/after-dark-wallpaper.png) |
| Switch with transparency on: new theme painted at ~65 ms, page frozen until the transition finished at ~320–340 ms; old tint visible through the new one | New theme revealed in one frame at ~90 ms; transition over at ~105 ms; native material flips when that frame is shown |
| Main per switch: 3 × `setVibrancy` + 3 × `setBackgroundColor`, and `setVibrancy` on every resize event | Identical calls skipped; full re-apply kept on window creation, show/restore, reload, fullscreen and each translucency request |

Timings are from the renderer (View Transition `ready`/`finished` and long-animation-frame entries) in the dev app, median of several switches.

## How

- `styles.css`: light + transparency gets a lighter, whiter shell tint (frost still shows through), and `.center-panel-surface` restores the solid surface tokens the way floating surfaces already do. The center panel therefore behaves like the opaque window, including the existing native-browser hole rules. Dark keeps the single clear tint plate.
- `theme.ts`: in a translucent window the theme update runs inside a View Transition with every animation off (the root group's 250 ms animation was the freeze) and the old snapshot hidden (it showed through the translucent new one). The callback waits for React to flush so all consumers change in the revealed frame. `onReveal` (the `theme:set` IPC) fires on `transition.ready`, so the native vibrancy material flips with the revealed frame instead of ~45 ms earlier. Transparency off keeps the existing code path.
- `ui-store.ts` / `_shell.tsx`: `theme:set` moved from a post-commit effect to the switch itself. `apply-initial-theme.ts` already sends it at startup. The window-background effect is skipped while translucent: main ignores the color then, and its `getComputedStyle` read forced an extra whole-document style recalc mid-switch.
- `main.ts`: `syncNativeWindowBackground(force)` skips unchanged native calls per window, and forces them on lifecycle events and `theme:set-window-translucent`, so the Dock-reopen fix (#6729) and the loader handoff (#7772) keep re-applying.

## Testing

- Verified in the real desktop app (isolated dev data): light/dark × transparency on/off, over light and dark backdrops; home, board, chat session and an open menu; theme switching felt instant with no staggered parts after the final change.
- Updated `e2e/window-transparency-overlap.spec.ts`: in light + transparency the board archive (center panel) is now solid; the sidebar row and body stay clear.
- Added a `theme.test.ts` case for the translucent path (update inside the transition, `onReveal` only after `ready`). Typecheck and tests were not run locally; CI runs them.
- Not re-checked after the final change: a live native browser page in light + transparency (it uses the same rules as the opaque panel).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in with screenshots
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass

title: bug(opencode-v2): failed compaction shows "The conversation history was compacted"
body:
### Report

When OpenCode 2 fails to compact a conversation, AO tells the user it worked. The chat shows the same message as a successful compaction, and nothing mentions the failure.

### What happens

On `main` at `2efa5a7c47` with real OpenCode 2.2.5 and a scripted fake model, the failure was forced by having the model reply without OpenCode's summary template.

| Run | OpenCode's result | AO chat |
|---|---|---|
| Summary matches the template | Compaction worked | "The conversation history was compacted" |
| Summary doesn't match | `failed`: "Compaction summary did not match the required template" | "The conversation history was compacted" |

Both rows are from the real desktop app, 1 run each. OpenCode's database recorded the second run as failed.

The same failure through `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation/compact`:

1. The turn ended as `completed`, with no error.
2. AO saved a completed "Compacted the conversation history" activity with `tokensBefore: 1010` and `tokensAfter: 1010`.

Over raw ACP, OpenCode reports the failure in `session_info_update`, then ends the turn normally with `stopReason: end_turn`:

```json
{"opencode/compaction": {"status": "failed", "reason": "manual", "error": {"type": "compaction.failed", "message": "Compaction summary did not match the required template"}}}
```

### Cause

AO decides from the turn state alone. `conversation.go:959` calls `settleCompaction` for any completed compaction turn, which emits `ChatEventCompacted`. `controller.go:3586` then also sets `compactedAt`.

OpenCode's failed compaction is a completed turn, so that check passes. The result is only in `_meta["opencode/compaction"]`, and the `SessionInfoUpdate` case at `client.go:738` doesn't read it.

### Expected

AO should read the compaction status and show a failed compaction as failed, with OpenCode's error. It shouldn't add the compacted row or set `compactedAt`.

### Not run

- Other failure paths in OpenCode's `compaction.ts`, such as "Compaction produced no summary" and provider errors.
- Automatic compaction. Only manual compaction was tested.
- What the model receives on the next turn after a failure.
- Other ACP agents. This code is shared, but only OpenCode 2 was tested.
- A live run on the current `main`. Only `66dc8e0660` was checked by code: 3 commits ahead, with `conversation.go`, `client.go` and `controller.go` unchanged.

title: fix(pty-host): answer DA1 queries so fish starts without a 2 s stall
body:
## Problem

fish 4.1+ sends a Primary Device Attributes query (DA1, `ESC [ c`) at startup and waits up to 2 s for the reply. In AO terminals no reply ever arrived, so every new fish shell stalled for 2 s and printed:

```
warning: fish could not read response to Primary Device Attribute query after waiting for 2 seconds
```

Ghostty and iTerm answer it, so fish starts normally there.

Nobody answered in AO for two reasons:
- The desktop pane (`XtermTerminal.tsx`) forwards only OSC colour replies and cursor-position reports from xterm.js. On top of that, a new shell's first output goes through the replay gate, where replies are suppressed on purpose.
- The pty-host's rendered surface throws away its emulator's replies. With `--surface=lazy` it isn't even running live.

## Fix (Go only, pty-host)

- `pumpPTY` runs a small stateful scanner over PTY output. It matches `ESC [ c` and `ESC [ 0 c`, including a query split across reads. `ESC [ > c` and `ESC [ = c` don't match.
- On each match the host writes `ESC [ ? 1 ; 2 c` to the PTY, the same reply xterm.js sends. A separate goroutine does the write through a small queue, so a program that floods queries without reading its input can't deadlock the read loop.
- The host is now the only thing that answers DA1. The phone's WebView xterm forwards everything it generates, including replies to replayed scrollback, so client input made up only of DA1 replies is dropped. Without this, a program would get two answers whenever the phone was watching.
- On Windows the change does nothing (conhost answers DA1 inside ConPTY).

I checked whether any client attaches a real terminal to the pty-host (the case where a double reply would come from the attached terminal): nothing in `backend` puts a TTY in raw mode, so no such path exists today. If one is added later, the client-reply filter already covers it.

PR #7787 (already on `main`) doesn't conflict: this adds one scan call in `pumpPTY`, one guard in `MsgTerminalInput` and a new `deviceattrs.go`.

## Tests

- `deviceattrs_test.go`:
  - Scanner cases: DA2/DA3/RIS/replies don't match, and fish's `ESC[?u` followed by DA1 does.
  - Queries split across reads.
  - The reply-filter regex.
- Host test: a shell gets the reply with **no client attached**, with the query split across two reads.
- Host test: a client's DA1 reply is dropped, and typed input still reaches the PTY.

Per the project's workflow these weren't run locally. CI runs them.

## Manual verification

1. Start fish 4.1+ in an AO terminal tab (`fish --version` should show ≥ 4.1).
2. The prompt appears right away: no 2 s pause and no "Primary Device Attribute" warning.
3. Optional: open the same session on the phone while starting a new fish. Still no warning, and no stray `?1;2c` text at the prompt.

Once this ships, you can remove the `~/.local/bin/fish-ao` workaround (`fish --features=no-query-term`).

title: release: promote main (eed7877e2d) to stable, 2026-11-06
body:
Code changes: +23202 -4069\
Tests: +22573 -796\
Others: +5387 -698 (docs, generated files, lockfiles, config, translations); 9 binary files

## What

Moves `stable` from `f9dc472702` (v0.14.9, #7680) to `main` at `eed7877e2d` (#7682). That is 84 commits. Version: **0.14.10**.

### Why there is a merge commit

`stable` is not an ancestor of `main`: it carries #7680's merge commit and earlier merges. Its tree matches `25bc9b148f` (`git diff 25bc9b148f f9dc472702` is empty), and `25bc9b148f` is an ancestor of `eed7877e2d`, so everything on `stable` is already in this release.

This branch is one `-s ours` merge of `stable` onto `2efa5a7c47` (`0f1b24238b`), then a merge of `main` at `eed7877e2d` (`34900d03ed`). The result matches `main` exactly (`git diff eed7877e2d 34900d03ed` is empty). The `-s ours` merge only makes `stable` an ancestor again, so this release can fast-forward. There are no cherry-picks.

## Why

Requested to get fixes on `main` to stable users, including #7716, which stops an OpenCode 2 session failing when a file vanishes during the first-use data copy (#7714). `v0.14.9` does not contain that fix.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Stable is `v0.14.9`, without #7716 | Stable is `0.14.10`, with #7716 and the rest of the list below |

## How

Same shape as #7680. `stable.yml` stamps the version during the build, so this branch doesn't change `frontend/package.json`.

## Migrations

- **Cloud (Postgres):** none found in this repo's diff.
- **Local SQLite:** 4 new migrations, applied automatically when the desktop updates. A desktop cannot move back to an older build after these:
  - `20261031021251693_session_interface_transitions_degraded_kind`
  - `20261101192928401_add_shell_terminal_command_owner`
  - `20261102164353715_automation_template_metadata`
  - `20261103094403671_backfill_spanning_plan_copies`

## Testing

- **Nightly:** `v0.14.10-nightly.202611060909` was built from exactly `eed7877e2d`, so all 84 commits have shipped as a nightly. It is the first nightly with the last 7, including #7682.
- **CI on `2efa5a7c47`:** 74 passed, 18 were skipped, 6 failed. All 6 failures are the same scheduled `package-version` job from `Release latest guard`, and they aren't about this commit: `frontend/package.json` on `main` says `0.14.8` while the latest stable is `0.14.9`. That guard will keep failing until `main` is bumped, which is a separate change.
- **CI on `eed7877e2d`:** 36 passed, 1 was skipped, 4 failed. 2 are the `package-version` guard above. The other 2 are one intermittent failure: `backend-core (0)` and the `build-test` gate that reports it. `TestLinuxDefaultSpawnHostEndToEnd` has failed on 3 of the 4 finished Go runs on `main` since #7864, and passed on `e1c62f2493` and on #7864's own PR. When it fails, the host's new DA1 reply reaches the program's input ahead of `hello`. Backend jobs skip on a PR into `stable`, so this PR's own checks do not show it.
- **#7716 is included:** `959b41cf34` is an ancestor of `34900d03ed`.
- **Not done yet:**
  - Resolve `TestLinuxDefaultSpawnHostEndToEnd`, failing intermittently since #7864.
  - A desktop smoke test (local and Cloud) on `34900d03ed`.
  - Full local test suites. This relies on CI for `eed7877e2d`.
  - Triage of bugs filed since `v0.14.9`. I did not check whether recent reports such as #7844 to #7849 are regressions in this range.
  - Confirmation from the #7714 reporter that #7716 fixes their case.

## Merging

Do not squash. A squash breaks `stable`'s ancestry with `main` again. Fast-forward instead:

```sh
git push origin 34900d03ed0111d5289d1a3190c218c5f6b6b7aa:stable
```

GitHub marks this PR merged once `stable` contains its head. Then release, which is for the release conductor to run:

```sh
gh workflow run stable.yml --repo Untrivial-ai/ao-releases -f version=0.14.10 -f ref=34900d03ed0111d5289d1a3190c218c5f6b6b7aa
```

title: fix(opencode-v2): show a failed compaction as failed
body:
Code changes: +43 -0\
Tests: +167 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A failed OpenCode 2 compaction now shows as failed, with OpenCode's own error, instead of "The conversation history was compacted".

## Why

Fixes #7863

OpenCode ends a failed compaction with a normal `end_turn` and reports the failure only in `session_info_update`. AO judged the result from the turn state, so it showed success and set `compactedAt` when nothing had been compacted.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Failed compaction shows "The conversation history was compacted" | Shows "The agent ran into a problem" with "Compaction summary did not match the required template" |
| Failed compaction is saved as a `completed` turn and sets `compactedAt` | Saved as a `failed` turn with OpenCode's error; `compactedAt` stays empty |
| A compaction that fails with a prompt error is saved as `failed`, but its turn is left out of the timeline, so nothing appears | The error appears in the timeline |
| Successful compaction shows "The conversation history was compacted" | Unchanged |

## How

- `client.go` reads `_meta["opencode/compaction"]` during a compaction turn. The latest status wins. The same status on a normal turn is ignored, so a failed automatic compaction doesn't fail the user's turn.
- `conversation.go` fails the turn from that status instead of settling it as compacted.
- A compaction turn has no prompt or reply, and the timeline only includes turns with an item on the page. A failed one also emits `ChatEventError`, so it can be seen. The app already hides that row when it repeats the turn's error, so the message shows once.
- Retry stays hidden because there's no human prompt to resend. Running `/compact` again is the retry.

The status is read in the shared ACP driver, next to the existing JetBrains session-failure metadata. Only OpenCode sends this key.

## Testing

**Real desktop app** with OpenCode 2.2.5 and a scripted fake model. The failure was forced by having the model reply without OpenCode's summary template. OpenCode was placed at AO's private installer path by hand.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `/compact` fails | Error shown once, no Retry, `compactedAt` empty |
| Reload the failed session | Error still shown |
| Send a message after the failure | Agent replies normally |
| `/compact` succeeds | Compacted row shown, `compactedAt` set |

**New tests**, confirmed failing before the fix: reported failure with and without a message, a failure not carrying into the next compaction, a prompt error reaching the timeline, and a failed status on a normal turn.

**Local CI on macOS**
- `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 passes on the ACP driver package, not the whole repo.
- On the rebased commit, with `-race`: `chatdriver/acp`, `chatdriver/nativeacp`, `chatdriver/opencodeacp`, `service/chat` and `storage/sqlite/store` pass.
- The full `go test -race ./...` ran before the rebase, and 6 tests failed in packages this PR doesn't change. All 6 also fail on clean `main` on this Mac:
  - `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders`
  - `TestCrushLocalAuthStatusDoesNotUseProviderCatalog`
  - `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects`
  - `TestWrongOpenCodeMajorIsRejectedBeforeACPProcessLaunch`
  - `TestCueCommandPreservesNativeEvalEOFAndOptionBehavior`
  - `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` (intermittent: 7 of 8 runs failed on `main`, 6 of 8 on this branch)

**Not run:** the Linux and Windows jobs, a real provider failure, a real automatic compaction, and other ACP agents.

title: fix(awake): keep sidebar and Settings Stay Awake in sync
body:
## Summary
- **Sidebar ↔ Settings sync:** the sidebar Stay Awake button started idle-only wake, but the Settings → Mobile "Keep this Mac awake" switch only shows *closed-lid* wake, so turning wake on from the sidebar left Settings off (the reverse direction worked). On Macs that support closed-lid wake, the sidebar now requests the same mode as Settings. Macs without lid support keep idle-only wake.
- **Stuck "Starting closed-lid keep awake…":** the lid POST returns before the native helper acknowledges its lease (~2s scan), so the cached status said `lidReason: "starting"`. Mobile status has a 60s staleTime and no polling, so the line never cleared. `useStayAwake` now re-reads mobile status (up to 5s) until the helper settles, and `KeepAwakeRow` no longer renders the transient starting line. Real problems such as low battery, heat, or a missing helper still show, and so does "armed".
- Removed the now-unused `mobile.keepAwake.lidIdle` string from all locales.

## Behavior change
Turning Stay Awake on from the sidebar now keeps the Mac awake with the lid closed on supported Macs, which uses more battery. The existing safety stops still apply: below 10% battery or at critical heat.

## Tests
- `npx vitest run AwakeControl.test.tsx ConnectMobileModal.test.tsx ThisComputerAccess.test.tsx`: 161 passed, 6 skipped.
- Two new regression tests in `AwakeControl.test.tsx`. Both fail without the fix:
  - sidebar on → Settings switch on (and off again)
  - transient `starting` status stays hidden and is re-read until the helper confirms "armed"
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in changed files. Unrelated `packages/product-ui` errors come from deps not installed in this worktree.

## Not verified
Not exercised manually in the desktop app. Closed-lid wake only runs against the real `~/.ao/data`, which needs the installed app quit. Please check both toggles in a build.

title: feat(share): let a share link include the file's version history
body:
Code changes: +529 -27\
Tests: +417 -1\
Others: +497 -7

## What

Adds an **Include version history** toggle to the artifact Share popover, off by default.

- **Off:** the link shows only the published version, as it does today.
- **On:** anyone with the link can read the file's older versions too, up to 50.

The toggle also appears on a live link. Turning it on asks first. Turning it off removes the older versions at once and keeps the URL. A link that shows its history brings it up to date on Republish.

## Why

Someone sharing an artifact may want readers to see how it evolved, not just where it ended up. Until now a link could only ever show one version, and the choice has to stay with the person because old versions can hold things they would not publish today.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Share offers Publish only; a link shows one version | Share offers Publish plus an **Include version history** switch, off by default |
| A published link offers Copy link and Unpublish | The switch also appears on a published link, with a confirmation before older versions go public |
| Only the current file is checked for credentials | Turning the switch on checks every older version too, and warns before anything is published |

No screenshot: the popover has not been viewed in the real desktop app yet. See Testing.

## How

**Contract (additive).** New `PUT` and `DELETE /me/artifact-shares/{shareId}/history`, `POST .../artifacts/share/history`, and `historyVersion` and `historyRevision` on upload. `ArtifactShare.includeHistory`, `ArtifactShareList.versionHistory` and `PublicArtifactShare.versions` are new optional fields. `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated.

**Consent happens before publishing.** `cloudShare:inspectHistory` lists the older versions and scans each one, because a credential a later edit removed is still in the history. Publishing carries exactly the versions the popover showed. Local blobs are content-addressed, and the upload refuses a blob whose hash no longer matches.

**Failure shows viewers less, never more.** The current file publishes first, then older versions arrive one at a time, and the link shows them only when all are there. If one fails, the link is live with its latest version and the popover says so. `resolveShareFile` still refuses `.versions`; only `resolveShareVersion`, reached from the person's choice, reads it.

**A stale update is refused.** The first `PUT` returns a `revision`, which each upload and the finishing `PUT` carry. If the person turned history off meanwhile, the control plane answers 409 `artifact_share_history_changed` and the popover reports it, so nothing withdrawn can go public again.

**A changed file waits for Republish.** Otherwise versions newer than the link's latest would go public without ever being published.

**Compatibility.** Against a control plane without this, `versionHistory` is unset and the toggle is hidden. Local versions come from the daemon's existing `artifact-versions/sync` route, so there is no daemon change.

**Intentional limits**
- Cloud versions are scanned on the start of their text only, because that is what the version route returns. Local versions are scanned on the first 32 MiB.
- Republishing from an older desktop leaves the replaced version out of the link's history.

Focus review on `toggleLinkHistory` and `publish` in `ShareArtifactPopover.tsx`, and `shareLocalHistory` in `cloud-share.ts`.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` in `frontend`, after rebasing on `main`.
- `vitest`: `cloud-share-history.test.ts` (new), `cloud-share-ipc.test.ts`, `cloud-share.test.ts`, `ShareArtifactPopover.test.tsx` and `src/renderer/i18n`.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`, and `go test` for `sessionartifacts` and `artifactversions`.
- Full frontend suite before the rebase: 658 of 671 files passed. Ten of the 13 failed files pass alone. The other three (`browser-profile-import`, `browser-cookie-repair`, `agent-browser-runtime`) were not rerun; none touch share code, and the first two hit native modules skipped by an `--ignore-scripts` install.

**Not tested:** the popover in the real desktop app, or a publish end to end against a running control plane. Each side is covered by its own tests only. `eslint` was not run.
