title: Security: bump bundled ACP Node runtime from 22.23.2 to 22.23.4+
body:
The desktop app ships a bundled Node binary for the ACP runtime at:

`Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node`

On the current stable macOS build (**v0.14.9**, released 3 November 2026), that binary is still **v22.23.2**.

On 21 October 2026 Node.js published a security release for the 22.x line: **[22.23.4](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.4)**. That release (and later 22.x patches) addresses several high-severity issues, including TLS hostname checks for non-canonical IP addresses, DNS resolver handling of null bytes, and a Brotli decoder memory-corruption bug, plus an NSS root-store update. The matching bars on the other supported lines are 24.22.1+ and 26.12.1+.

I could not find a changelog note, release note, or existing issue saying AO plans to refresh this bundled runtime. Other security fixes since 21 October (for example refusing requests from untrusted localhost pages) are unrelated to the Node version inside `acp-runtime`.

**Request**

Please bump the bundled ACP Node to **22.23.4 or a later patched 22.x** (or move it to another currently patched line, such as 24.22.1+ / 26.12.1+), and mention the new version in the release notes so users can confirm it.

Happy to test a preview/stable build on macOS Apple Silicon once it ships.

title: Let agents split the desktop window's panes with `ao pane`
body:
Stacked on #7791 (split panes). Agents can now arrange their session's tabs in the AO window, for example "open a terminal below the chat" or "show this file next to the chat". Like split panes itself, this is a Developer Mode preview.

## What agents can do

```
ao pane                                   # tabs, their keys, and the current splits
ao pane split terminal --side bottom      # new shell terminal below the tab on screen
ao pane split file:src/app.ts --beside session --side right
ao pane focus <tab> | remove <tab> | ungroup [group]
```

Every command prints the layout after the change (`--json` for the same data). Refusals are final and explain themselves: `SPLIT_PANES_OFF`, `SESSION_NOT_ON_SCREEN`, `TAB_NOT_FOUND`, `NO_SPLIT`, `NO_DESKTOP_WINDOW`.

## How it works

- **Relay** (`backend/internal/service/panes`): in memory only. It keeps the last layout each window reported per session, and sends a request to every connected window. It waits up to 8 s for the window showing the session to answer with the new layout; a window that isn't showing the session says so, and only when none shows it does the agent hear that.
- **Window link**: a new `panes` channel on the existing terminal mux, the same pattern as `shell-agents` from #7787. The window subscribes, reports layouts as they change, and answers commands.
- **API**: `GET` and `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/panes`, in the OpenAPI spec, with `schema.ts` regenerated.
- **Desktop**: the session view on screen (local sessions, Developer Mode) applies requests through the split-panes store's shared actions from #7791, opening a terminal or file first when asked. A new terminal is answered with its real key once the daemon lists it.
- **Agent guide**: `using-ao/commands/pane.md`, listed in the skill index.

## Testing

Manual, end to end in the dev app (isolated data) against a real session, from the CLI built from this branch:
- `ao pane` listed the session's tabs and Split panes state.
- `ao pane split terminal --side bottom` opened a terminal below the chat in about 0.1–0.4 s and printed the new layout.
- `ao pane split file:README.md --beside session --side right` opened the file to the right of the chat.
- `ao pane ungroup` turned the split back into tabs. An unknown tab gave `TAB_NOT_FOUND`; ungroup with nothing split gave `NO_SPLIT`.
- With Split panes turned off, `split` was refused with `SPLIT_PANES_OFF` and nothing changed.

The manual run found two problems, both fixed here: `split terminal` answered with the temporary `pending-shell:` key, and long keys misaligned the `ao pane` columns.

New unit tests: relay, mux channel, controller, CLI, and the window-side relay (`pane-relay.test.ts`). `go vet` passes on the touched packages; the test suites were not run locally, so CI verifies them.

## Known limits

- Local sessions only. Cloud and remote-host sessions don't take pane requests yet.
- The window only links up while a session is open in it with Developer Mode on, so with no session on screen the agent gets `NO_DESKTOP_WINDOW`.

title: feat(settings): pick the default shell for new terminals
body:
## Summary

Settings → Sessions → **Terminal shell** is now a dropdown on every platform (it was Windows-only). It picks the shell for newly opened terminals.

- **System default** shows the shell it resolves to (`$SHELL`, or the Windows auto order).
- **Installed shells** are detected by the daemon (`GET /api/v1/terminal-shells`): `/etc/shells` plus zsh, bash, fish, nu, pwsh and others in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/bin`, `/usr/bin`. Symlinks to the same binary are listed once, under the link path (`/opt/homebrew/bin/fish`, not the Cellar path). On Windows: PowerShell, Windows PowerShell, Command Prompt, Git Bash and WSL when present (WSL is a new selector).
- **Custom…** shows a path row. The daemon validates it (`GET /api/v1/terminal-shells/check`): absolute or `~/` path, or a command on PATH, and it must be executable. Invalid paths show an error and are not saved.
- Each option shows its name and a muted mono path. The hint under the row says it applies to new terminals only; open terminals keep their shell.

**Stored value is unchanged.** It is still `{ kind, path? }` in `ui-settings.json`. A shell picked from the list is stored as `{ kind: "custom", path }`, so existing custom shells (for example `~/.local/bin/fish-ao`) keep working and show up under Custom….

**Launch is the same as the default.** On macOS/Linux the daemon used to ignore the setting. It now launches the picked path exactly like `$SHELL`: the bare executable on the PTY (interactive), with the same AO login-shell environment (ZDOTDIR/BASH_ENV wrappers, PATH pin). No extra flags are added. An unavailable shell returns the existing `SHELL_TERMINAL_SHELL_UNAVAILABLE` error and the renderer falls back to System default, as Windows already did. The renderer now sends the setting for local terminals on every platform; remote hosts are unchanged.

## Screenshots

Dropdown on macOS:

![Terminal shell menu](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/8f6eaa6cfb5878d4b5a551caaf0c01a2/raw/d07def61c279aa7705a172bf07df51bbf0edafd9/shell-menu.png)

Custom path:

![Custom shell path](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/8f6eaa6cfb5878d4b5a551caaf0c01a2/raw/d07def61c279aa7705a172bf07df51bbf0edafd9/shell-custom.png)

## Testing

Checked in the real desktop app (isolated dev data, daemon `$SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/fish`):

1. Open Settings → General → Sessions → Terminal shell. The menu lists System default (`/opt/homebrew/bin/fish`), bash, csh, dash, fish, ksh, sh, tcsh, zsh (`/bin/zsh` and `/opt/homebrew/bin/zsh`) and Custom….
2. Pick **bash**. `ui-settings.json` holds `{"kind":"custom","path":"/bin/bash"}`.
3. Open a session and click New terminal. The pty-host child is `/bin/bash` and the pane shows an interactive `bash-3.2$` prompt.
4. Pick **Custom…** and enter `/etc/hosts`. The row shows "No executable shell at this path." and the setting stays bash.
5. Enter `~/.local/bin/fish-ao`. It saves. New terminal 2 runs `/opt/homebrew/bin/fish --features=no-query-term` with the fish greeting; terminal 1 is still `/bin/bash`.

Unit tests added for detection (symlink dedupe, link path kept), path validation, and unix shell resolution; frontend tests updated for the all-platform request and the macOS menu. Not run locally; CI runs them.

## Risks

- The menu lists every shell in `/etc/shells`, including csh/tcsh/ksh on macOS.
- Windows detection is untested on a real Windows machine; it reuses the existing Windows resolvers.

title: fix(updates): full-width download track and single v in update versions
body:
## Summary

Two updater UI bugs:

1. **Short download track in Settings > Updates.** The settings row text column shrink-wrapped to its longest line, so the `w-full` progress track stopped under the build line instead of running to the actions. The column now takes the free row width (`flex-1` in `SettingsRowLabel`); only the green fill shows completion.
2. **`vv` in update versions.** Nightly discovery published the GitHub release tag (`v0.14.10-nightly...`) as the status version, and every label template adds its own `v`, rendering `vv0.14.10-nightly...` in Settings and the Sidebar (it also broke the Sidebar's nightly label parse). Discovery now publishes the bare semver (the raw tag is still used for release URLs), which also fixes the release notes match against `info.version`. The renderer strips a leading `v` when it receives an update status, so a prefixed version from any source still renders one `v`.

## Tests

- New `@P0` e2e cases in `e2e/updates-settings.spec.ts`:
  - track starts at the text column and ends just before the actions at 1400px and 900px, with a constant width across progress 0/10/57/100
  - `v`-prefixed nightly, `v`-prefixed stable and bare stable versions render one `v` in Settings and the Sidebar, with no `vv` anywhere on the page
- With the source fix reverted, the new tests fail on exactly these bugs (track 409px short at 1400px; `vv0.14.10-nightly...`, `vv2.0.0`).
- `auto-updater.test.ts`: two assertions that expected the prefixed discovered version now expect the bare one.
- Vitest (updater, settings, Sidebar, restart dialog, hooks): 1948/1948 passing. `npm run typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass.

## Notes

- The existing untagged e2e test "downloaded update keeps the full version readable and actions aligned" already fails on main because of stale copy ("Ready to install.", "Current version:"). It is unchanged here.
- At 900px the old layout happens to pass the width check (text wraps to fill the column); the 1400px case is the regression guard.

title: feat(desktop): right-click menu for center tab strip tabs
body:
Code changes: +319 -85  
Tests: +77 -5  
Others: +18 -9 (locale strings)

## What

Right-clicking any tab in the session tab strip (terminal and chat surfaces) opens a context menu. The rows change with the tab type, and every row is an action the app already had somewhere else (button, shortcut, sidebar menu, file viewer, artifacts menu).

| Tab | Its own rows |
| --- | --- |
| Session / chat | Open in ▸ (editors, Finder, terminals), Copy path, Rename (F2), Pin session, PR / branch rows when present, **Archive session** (⇧⌘A) last |
| Shell terminal | Rename (F2), New terminal (⌘T), working directory: Copy path, Reveal in Finder, Open with editor |
| File / diff | Copy path, Copy relative path, Reveal in Finder, Open with editor, Open in AO Browser (HTML only) |
| Artifact | Show in Finder, Show in Terminal, Copy relative path |
| Reviewer terminal / reviewer chat | none (Close tab only, disabled) |

Every tab ends with **Close tab** (⌘W shown on the active tab), disabled where the tab can't close.

- Rows that don't apply right now are disabled, not hidden. Examples: Close tab on the session tab, Rename on the orchestrator tab, native rows for remote or Cloud sessions.
- Shift+F10 or the menu key opens the menu from a focused tab. Arrow keys move through it, and Escape returns focus to the tab.
- Windows shell tabs used right-click to rename. They now rename by double-click like macOS and Linux, and right-click opens the menu, which has Rename.

## Why

Most tab actions were hidden behind hover buttons, shortcuts, or other surfaces, and only the session tab had a (Rename-only) menu.

## Before / After

The screenshots predate the last commit: they still show a **Close other tabs** row under Close tab, which is now removed.

Before: only the session tab had a right-click menu, with a single Rename row. Other tabs had none.

| Tab | After |

title: fix: bound Sentry volume and filter expected failures
body:
Code changes: +67 -50  
Tests: +375 -17  
Others: +5 -3  

## What

Follow-up to #7682 and [the requested corrections](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7682#issuecomment-6681148421). Bounds handled Electron main captures across every category, excludes additional expected states, and removes Sentry transport waiting from the HTTP response path.

## Why

Fixed fingerprints group events but do not limit their volume. Fresh IPC errors could therefore flood Sentry during a cloud outage. The daemon also misclassified agent sign-out and some tracker refusals, while request logging could wait for a synchronous Sentry send.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Only side-chat handled errors have a capture budget | Every main category is limited to five per minute and 200 per UTC day per sanitized category/reason/detail, with at most 1,024 budget keys per day |
| Agent sign-out and expected tracker conflicts can create fault events | Both auth sentinels and user setup states stay out; tracker intake reports only internal errors or registered fault codes |
| Remote proxy connectivity/identity 502s look like renderer server faults | `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` and `HOST_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED` remain expected states with response bodies preserved |
| HTTP completion can wait on Sentry transport | HTTP and background reporting share four nonblocking send slots; saturated diagnostics are dropped without a queue |
| Renderer exception operation labels disappear at the main scrubber | Fixed operation labels reach the final scrubbed Sentry event; arbitrary values are dropped |
| A new `Error(apiErrorMessage(...))` silently loses API ownership | A CI AST source guard rejects direct, aliased and namespace-import variants |

## How

- Preserve consent admission and opt-out draining across the shared asynchronous daemon path. Copy capture tags before starting its goroutine, retaining safe HTTP metadata without retaining the request or raw error.
- Apply handled-main budgets before the bounded startup queue; changing the sink does not reset them. Existing object-identity deduplication and privacy sanitization remain in place.
- Reuse existing domain error classification. No new cause taxonomy, native crash reporting or migration diagnostics.
- Add real tracker polling and HTTP middleware regressions with in-memory/blocking transports, plus auth, updater, daemon-transition, remote-fetch, operation-tag and budget coverage. Move daemon transition reporting into the existing main capture module so it is directly testable.
- Remove nine unused background reasons, the unused handled-renderer-process reason and the test-only fingerprint wrapper. Correct per-operation overflow documentation and the sampling/volume comment.

## Testing

- Complete frontend suite: **679 files passed, 11,741 tests passed, 9 skipped**. Both frontend and E2E typechecks pass. Final AST guard fixture/repository checks pass.
- Focused frontend telemetry suites: 105 passed. Updater outage/signature regression passes through its existing mock harness.
- Complete HTTP, tracker-intake and Sentry race suites pass. Final Sentry race rerun covers copied asynchronous HTTP tags. Focused chat auth/capture and session-manager expected-state tests pass.
- CI-pinned Go 1.27.1 / golangci-lint 2.13.2: complete backend lint passes with zero issues.
- Broader chat and session-manager race suites were attempted with a four-minute package timeout and did not complete. Four session-manager missing-binary assertions fail because their restricted PATH hides the macOS tmux prerequisite; all four reproduce on an unmodified export of exact base `eed7877e2d68980888613311c4ada91ee4c66318`. The ACP replay test also timed out in isolation on both the follow-up (120 seconds) and the exact unmodified base (90 seconds). No complete chat/session-manager race pass is claimed.
- No API shapes or generated artifacts changed. Full repository race coverage and platform packaging are unverified locally.
- **Requested packaged/live validation remains pending:** the existing no-live-telemetry restriction has not been lifted, and no test DSN was supplied. No packaged app, real telemetry injection or settings mutation was performed. A packaged daemon/main/preload event run still needs explicit authorization and an identified test DSN; fake transports do not substitute for it.
- No workers, additional reviews, merge, release or deployment were started. Remote CI is not claimed green and will be handled through completion events.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from current `main`
- [x] Links the merged PR and follow-up request
- [x] Before / After describes the nonvisual behavior changes
- [x] Regression tests cover capture volume, privacy, expected states and HTTP admission/draining

- [ ] Remote CI passes

title: feat: close the harness troubleshooting loop with helper findings
body:
Code changes: +195 -25\
Tests: +146 -3\
Others: +216 -9

> **Depends on #7133.** GitHub can't stack a fork PR on another fork branch, so this targets `main` and includes #7133's commits. Only the newest commit, `f66c2549a`, is new here. Review that commit, or review after #7133 merges.

## What

Builds on the harness troubleshooting flow from #7133 so that it can explain a problem, help fix it, and report a genuine AO bug:

- **Helper findings.** The helper agent writes `troubleshooting-findings.json` to its session artifact directory: likely cause (`setup` / `provider` / `suspected_ao_bug` / `unknown`), outcome, whether the native CLI works, evidence, repairs and remaining uncertainty. AO reads it live through the existing artifact stream and shows it as the helper's hypothesis. It is also added to the issue draft.
- **Genuine-issue flag.** A report is *recommended* only when the evidence points at AO: the helper suspects AO, the native CLI works while AO disagrees, or AO's checks still fail after a repair attempt. When checks pass it reads "usually not needed"; otherwise it's optional. A helper's "fixed" counts only once AO's own fresh checks agree.
- **Richer diagnostics.** The snapshot (format v2) now includes the harness version, install source, maintenance method and update status from the update advisory, but not its binary path. The helper is told to start with `ao doctor --json`.
- **Easier filing.** "Open GitHub issue" opens a prefilled new-issue page that the user reviews and submits. A draft too long for a URL is copied to the clipboard for pasting. AO never files anything itself.

## Why

#7133 only reported a coarse state (installed / signed in / unverified). What the helper found was lost before the report, and nothing separated an AO bug from a setup mistake. Users had to retype the helper's conclusions, and maintainers got reports with no root-cause signal.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Helper conclusions stay in its terminal; the report draft has blank "Repairs attempted" | A "Helper findings" card shows the likely cause, outcome, changes made and evidence; the draft includes them, labeled as a hypothesis |
| "Prepare issue draft" looks the same whether or not AO is at fault | A suspected AO bug shows "This looks like a problem in AO…" with a primary action; passing checks say a report is usually not needed |
| Copy the draft only | "Open GitHub issue" with title and body prefilled, plus a paste fallback for long drafts |
| Snapshot has no version or install method | `harnessVersion`, `source`, `maintenanceMethod`, `updateStatus` (paths excluded) |

Screenshots of the new findings card and report states are still to come (see Testing).

## How

- **No backend change.** Findings travel through the session artifact directory (`GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/artifact-files/...`), which persists after the helper stops; cleanup runs only on spawn failure. The query shares the `session-artifact-file` key prefix, so `subscribeArtifactFileChanges` refreshes it as the helper writes. Version and source come from the existing `update-advisory` endpoint and fail soft to `null`.
- **Untrusted text.** Findings are helper-written, so they are parsed defensively: unknown enum values fall back to safe defaults, lengths and list sizes are capped, and text goes through the existing `sanitizeReportText` (paths, tokens, bearer and key patterns) plus email redaction.
- **Sandbox.** The artifact directory sits outside the helper's workspace, so Codex or Claude Code may ask the user to approve that one write. The prompt says so.
- **Issue URL.** `githubNewIssueUrl` was pulled out of `report-problem.ts`, so both flows use the same builder and repository (`GITHUB_NEW_ISSUE_URL`, currently `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`, the same target as "Report a problem").
- All nine locale catalogs are updated.

## Testing

- Unit tests: advisory evidence without paths; findings parsing, redaction and bounding; malformed findings; missing, invalid and ready artifact reads; report-advice rules; findings in the draft and the AO-bug title; issue URL and long-draft fallback.
- Panel tests: the findings card's waiting → ready states, live artifact subscription, the recommended-report state, the draft containing findings, and opening a prefilled GitHub issue.
- Not run locally: tests, typecheck and the app aren't run on the author's Windows workstation by policy, so validation relies on CI (Linux/macOS).
- No live end-to-end run yet with a real helper writing findings against a broken install. That and screenshots are the follow-up before merge.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from the #7133 branch (continuing that work)
- [x] One focused change; links the related PR

- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (screenshots pending)

title: fix(topbar): open the worktree in the file manager when no editor is set
body:
Code changes: +30 -24\
Tests: +61 -12\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When no default editor is installed, the session top bar's open-in-editor split button now opens the session's worktree in the platform file manager instead of showing a dim, disabled `</>` placeholder.

- macOS: Finder, with Finder's real app icon
- Windows: File Explorer, with the icon read from `explorer.exe`
- Linux: the default file manager through xdg-open, with a folder icon (there is no single app to take an icon from)

The tooltip and label follow the editor pattern ("Open this session's workspace in Finder" / "Open in Finder"), and ⌘O does the same as the button. The dropdown still lists every editor; picking one replaces the fallback as before.

## Why

The saved preference defaults to Cursor. On a Mac without Cursor, the main button rendered a generic code glyph, disabled, so it looked broken. An editor that is saved but no longer installed hit the same state.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: disabled code glyph with "Choose an installed editor or use a native fallback"](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/f4b977475269e5984de9707fad0071cc/raw/989253900ece6ab13066847f6a18d152b980bca6/before-no-editor.png) | ![After: Finder icon with "Open this session's workspace in Finder"](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/f4b977475269e5984de9707fad0071cc/raw/989253900ece6ab13066847f6a18d152b980bca6/after-finder-fallback.png) |
| Main button disabled; ⌘O opened the first target in the list (an editor if any was installed) | Main button and ⌘O open the worktree in Finder until an editor is picked |

Both captures come from the same dev app, session and window. Cursor is not installed and Zed is, with no editor picked.

## How

- `TopbarOpenEditorButton`: the main target is the preferred installed editor, else the `file_manager` target. A preferred editor still launches without an explicit target id, so main resolves the saved preference as before.
- `OpenTargetIcon`: file managers use their native icon when main supplies one, falling back to the bundled Finder glyph or a folder icon if it is missing or fails to load. This also changes Finder's icon in the dropdown and the chat path menu, so they match the button.
- `editor-handoff` (main): Windows now reads the File Explorer icon from `%SystemRoot%\explorer.exe`. macOS already read Finder.app.
- The context menu's "Open in…" submenu trigger is unchanged. It's a labeled submenu, not the empty split button.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.

- Updated `TopbarOpenEditorButton.test.tsx`: Finder fallback for a saved-but-missing editor, the default Cursor missing with another editor installed (icon, tooltip, click, ⌘O, then picking VS Code), and Finder's native icon in the menu.

title: Pasting into the terminal "Find in terminal" box doesn't work
body:
Reported by a user, relayed through the orchestrator:

In the terminal's "Find in terminal" search box, typing works but pasting doesn't. The session in the screenshot was on a remote host ("Prateek's MacBook Air"); the search overlay showed `0/0` with the case and regex toggles, previous/next and close.

title: fix(terminal): keep paste in the search box out of the PTY
body:
Fixes #7881

## Problem

Pasting into the terminal's "Find in terminal" box did nothing visible. The text wasn't lost: it went to whatever was running in the terminal, with newlines turned into `\r`. Without bracketed paste mode, a multi-line clipboard is submitted to the foreground program.

## Cause

`TerminalSearch` renders inside the terminal's `shell` element, and the `shell` listeners treat every event in that subtree as terminal input. The capture-phase `paste` listener runs before the input, calls `preventDefault()` and writes the text to the PTY. This dates from #4473, which first put the overlay inside `shell`. It did not come from #6531 or #6465.

The same cause affected other input in the box:

| Action in the box | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paste (Cmd+V, Edit > Paste, and the Windows/Linux shortcuts) | Blocked, sent to the PTY | Goes into the box |
| IME commit | Into the box **and** the PTY | Box only |
| Right-click | Terminal menu, whose Paste writes to the PTY | No terminal menu |
| Copy, when the terminal has a selection | Copies the terminal's selection | Copies the box's selection |
| Cut, select-all | Unaffected | Unaffected |

## Fix

`isTerminalSearchEvent` returns early from those listeners when the event comes from the search overlay. Input aimed at the terminal is unchanged, including while the overlay is open.

## Testing

- `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`: 169 pass. Of the 5 new tests, 4 fail without the fix; the fifth is a control that a paste aimed at the terminal still reaches it.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- Real app, isolated Electron lab on macOS, driven over CDP, before and after the fix. PTY input was recorded with `cat > <file>` in a shell tab:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trusted paste on the input | `defaultPrevented: true`, box unchanged | `defaultPrevented: false`, a 24-character clipboard landed in the box (5 → 29) |
| Sentinel paste (synthetic event) | Reached the PTY | Did not reach the PTY |
| IME composition | In the box and the PTY | In the box only |
| Terminal menu on right-click | Opens | Does not open |

## Not tested

- **Remote session:** not run. All sessions share one renderer path, `mux.sendInput`, and the fix sits before it, so it should behave the same.
- **Windows and Linux:** not run. Their paste routes raise the same native `paste` event.
- **Real copy and cut in the lab:** skipped because they overwrite the system clipboard. Copy is covered by a unit test.

## Follow-up to consider

Right-clicking the box now shows no menu, the same as other AO text inputs, because the app has no native edit menu for inputs. Mouse users can paste with Edit > Paste. A right-click Paste for inputs would be a separate app-wide change.

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

Updates `baseline-browser-mapping` from 2.10.35 to 2.11.35
Release notes

Sourced from baseline-browser-mapping's releases.

v2.11.0

What's Changed in 2.11.0

  • feat: Adds a new getTimeline() method for getting the series of minimum browser changes, either grouped by date or by browser.
  • refactor: Substantial refactoring of the data compression process that replaces the full list of browsers from @mdn/browser-compat-data and downstream-browsers.json and features from web-features (in their very pared down form) with a change-list timeline that reflects which versions supported Baseline (newly available) on a given date. Thanks to @​swwind for the idea!
  • refactor: Some common functions have been moved to a util.ts module for use in other scripts.
  • fix: Removes process.exit() calls when unsupported option combinations are passed to getCompatibleVersions() and getAllVersions() in favour of throwing an Error. There is a small security risk with process.exit() calls that sites accepting unsanitised inputs could be the subject of attacks. Unsupported config options now throw and Error which should allow for more graceful handling. Thanks to @​bnbdr for flagging this as vulnerability CVE-2026-45819 .

Fixes #134

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6

title: test(conpty): let the DA1 reply arrive before the end-to-end input
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +8 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Fixes a flaky end-to-end test on Linux, `TestLinuxDefaultSpawnHostEndToEnd`, and makes the same fix in its Darwin twin, `TestDarwinDefaultSpawnHostEndToEnd`. No product code changes.

## Why

The Linux test has failed `backend-core` at random since #7864 merged, on `main` and on PRs that include it. In the last 120 Go runs, all 8 failed runs since #7864 were this test with identical output, against 15 passing runs, so about 1 run in 3. `build-test` then fails too, because it requires `backend-core`.

Those counts are per run, not per attempt, and earlier failed runs in that window came from other causes.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| With the DA1 reply ahead of the input, the test times out on `received:\x1b[?1;2chello` | With the reply in either order, the test passes |

No user-visible change: this only changes tests.

## How

Both tests run a script that sends a DA1 query (`\033[c`) and then reads a line. Since #7864 the host answers that query on the program's stdin, as a real terminal would. The reply and the test's `hello` come from independent writers, so their order is not fixed. The script never reads the reply separately, so when it arrives first the shell's line starts with it and the `received:hello` check never matches.

The check now removes `da1Reply` before matching. These tests cover the spawn path: the detached host, environment, input and output round trip, and kill. Input order is not part of that, so I kept the tests and the query. The reply behaviour itself is covered by `TestHostAnswersDA1WithNoClient`.

**Intentional omissions:** #7864's product behaviour is unchanged. `go.yml` has no macOS job, so CI does not run the Darwin test; it can only fail on a developer's Mac.

## Testing

To force the failing order, a temporary overlay delayed `hello` by 300 ms so the reply always landed first. Nothing from it is committed.

| Test, reply forced first (macOS) | Old check | New check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TestDarwinDefaultSpawnHostEndToEnd` | failed 5 of 5, with CI's exact output | passed 10 of 10 |
| Linux test body, run on macOS via overlay | failed 5 of 5, with CI's exact output | passed 10 of 10 |

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go test -race -count=3` on `internal/adapters/runtime/conpty` (macOS) | pass |
| `go vet` on that package, Darwin and `GOOS=linux` | pass |
| `gofmt -l` on that package | clean |

**Not verified:** the Linux test was not run on Linux locally. The race does not reproduce on macOS without forcing it, so the real check is repeated green `backend-core` runs in CI.

- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable (refs #7864; no issue exists)

title: fix(mobile): draw the composer's mic again on Android after a turn ends
body: Code changes: +8 -2\ Tests: +126 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What On Android, the chat composer's round button went blank every time an agent turn ended. The stop face turned back into the dictate face, but the mic glyph was never drawn: you got an empty white disc in dark mode and an empty black disc in light mode. The button still worked, and reopening the chat drew it again. The reviewer composer had the same bug with its send arrow after the reviewer stopped. - `ChatComposer`: the round button's disc no longer clips (`overflow: "hidden"` removed from `roundDisc`). - `ReviewerComposer`: the stop and send buttons each get a `key`, so each face mounts its own view. ## Why The two faces are the same elements in the same slot, so React keeps the native views and only swaps the disc's fill and the glyph. On Android, a view that clips (`overflow: "hidden"` with a radius) doesn't draw a child that changed size in the same update as the view's own background. The stop glyph (`iconSize.xs`) is smaller than the mic (`sm`) and the reviewer's arrow (`md`), so every turn end hits exactly that case. I isolated this with a temporary lab route in a Release build on an API 35 emulator. Each row flipped between the two faces every 2.5 s: | Variant | Mic after the flip | | --- | --- | | Exact replica of the composer button | blank | | Same, without `overflow: "hidden"` | drawn | | Same, no border on the stop face | blank | | Same, same ripple on both faces | blank | | Same, disc remounted per face (`key`) | drawn | | Clipped disc, only the glyph changes (stop → mic, size changes, same fill) | drawn | | Clipped disc, only the fill changes (mic stays) | drawn | | Clipped disc, accent ↔ red with same-size mic ↔ stop (dictation toggle) | drawn | | Reviewer replica (clipped Pressable, stop → send) | blank | | Reviewer replica with keys | drawn | So it takes a clipping view, a fill change and a resized child, all in the same update. `react-native-svg` isn't at fault: keying the ` | | | | | | | | ## How - **Chat composer:** the disc only holds a centred glyph or a small spinner, and the press ripple sits on the outer `Pressable` (`roundTarget`), so the clip drew nothing. Removing it takes away the condition that triggers the bug. iOS draws a rounded background without clipping, so it should look the same there. - **Reviewer composer:** here the clipped view is the `Pressable` itself, and the clip keeps its bounded ripple round, so it stays. Separate keys give each face its own native view. - New Task and the terminal composer use the same clipped disc, but they only swap faces between same-size glyphs (dictate ↔ stop dictating), which the lab showed draws fine. Left unchanged. ## Testing - New `ChatComposer.roundButton.test.tsx` drives a running turn to a completed one and checks that the disc under the new dictate face doesn't clip. It failed before the fix (`overflow: "hidden"`). - New `ReviewerComposer.roundButton.test.tsx` checks that busy → idle mounts a new send button instead of reusing the stop button's view. It failed before the fix. - `npm run typecheck` passes, and `npx vitest run` passes: 348 files, 3,408 tests. - On the Android 15 emulator (Release APK), I watched a real Claude turn end (a slow `sleep 8` turn, so the stop face showed first) in dark and light mode. The mic is drawn after the turn in both. - The reviewer fix was checked with an exact replica in the lab route, not a live reviewer session. - iOS was not re-run on a simulator. The change there is only an unclipped disc with the same rounded background. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(cloud): share dialog in the Google Docs pattern, with General access and Copy link
body:
Code changes: +1337 -667\
Tests: +470 -366\
Others: +899 -364 (locale catalogs)

## What

Redesigns the cloud session Share dialog after Google Docs' share dialog, with Figma's broadest-to-most-specific access list:

- **People with access**, broadest first: the owner, then the workspace (Full access), then the project's shares (`from project`, locked), then teams, then people, then emails still waiting for sign-in.
- **General access**, one sentence that says who the link lets in:
  - *Only people with access*: "Only people in Northwind and people added above can open this session." In a personal workspace it reads "Only you and people added above…".
  - *Anyone with the link*: "Anyone signed in to Orchestrator.inc with the link can watch this session…". With several live links it describes the broadest and adds "and N more · Link settings".
- **Footer:** Copy link (`footer` variant) beside Done (`footer-primary`). While adding people the footer is Cancel / Share, and the line "They'll find it under Shared with you." sits where *Notify people* will go once sharing sends email.
- **Header:** `Share "<session>"`, with "Session in <project> · Share the whole project instead" underneath, which replaces the scope switcher. On the right are a gear (Link settings) and `CloseButton`.
- **Link settings (gear):** how long new links last (1 day, 7 days, 30 days or never), and every live link with when it was made, its expiry, how many people joined by it, and Revoke.
- **Header Share button:** now a split button whose menu has *Copy link* and *Share…*. The toast after copying names who the link lets in and offers *Manage*.
- **Stable builds** (no Teams) get the same dialog with links only. `ShareLinkDialog` and `ShareLinksSection` are deleted.

## Why

This implements the share-dialog research (Google Docs and Figma) and its review:

- **Write access by link is the real risk.** Links default to *Can watch*. *Can write* asks first, and the confirmation says the agent runs in your sandbox with your repository access and its secrets. A link never offers *Trusted*.
- **One sentence can't describe several links.** The sentence describes the broadest link and counts the rest. Turning link access off says how many links stop working.
- **Copying shouldn't make more credentials.** The URLs this device made are kept encrypted with `safeStorage` (`main/session-share-urls.ts`, under `~/.ao`, keyed by control plane and link id), so Copy link copies the same link after the dialog is reopened. *Copy new link* appears only on a device that never saw the URL.
- **Leaks should be reversible.** Turning off a link, or revoking one in Link settings, offers *Also remove the N people who joined by this link* when the control plane reports `joinedCount`.
- **Personal workspaces:** "people in Pritom's organization" reads oddly, so a personal workspace says "Only you and people added above".
- **Design system:** footer button variants instead of an outlined pill, neutral lock and globe icons, `CloseButton` and quiet icon buttons.
- **Share links on orchestrator.inc:** when the control plane names one, the dialog copies `https://orchestrator.inc/s/<code>` (`shortUrl`).

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Scope switcher, people list, then a Create link / Revoke list. The URL was shown once in an input with "Copy it now. The link can't be shown again." | `Share "<session>"` with the project line, the people list, then General access with one sentence, and Copy link + Done in the footer *(screenshot below)* |
| Links: Watch or Write to the agent, and Trusted allowed | Links: Can watch by default, Can write after a confirmation, never Trusted |
| Share button opens the dialog only | Share button's menu has Copy link (disabled with "Link access is off" when there is no link) and Share… |
| Share link `https://api.aoagents.dev/app/share#<org>/<token>` or `<cp>/s/<code>` | `https://orchestrator.inc/s/<code>` once the control plane sets `AO_CLOUD_SHARE_LINK_ORIGIN` (OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane PR), else `<cp>/s/<code>` as before |

Screenshots were taken from the real app against staging and are attached in a comment below. They show the restricted state, the General access menu, Link settings, and the Share menu. Not captured live: the Anyone-with-the-link state and its confirmations, because those make a real link. Component tests cover them.

## How

- **`share/linkAccess.ts`** derives General access from the live links:
  - *Live* means active, `anyone`, and not expired.
  - The broadest link is ranked by role, then cap, then expiry.
  - `useLinkAccess` handles turn on, turn off, replace, copy new and revoke, and keeps the device's stored URLs in step.
- **Changing a link's access makes a new link.** Access is fixed when a link is made, so the new link is created first (ending when the broadest did) and the old ones are revoked after. A failure leaves access as it was. The confirmation says the current link stops working.
- **`removeJoined`** is sent only when the control plane reports `joinedCount` in its list response. Without that, the confirmation says people who already opened the link keep their access.
- **Personal workspace check** (`isPersonalWorkspace`): an offering that isn't Coder/WorkOS, or a workspace named after the account (its email, its name, or "<name>'s organization").
- **Main-process store:** IPC calls are refused unless they come from the window's main frame. Without protected storage (no keychain, or Linux `basic_text`) URLs stay in memory and are never written as plain text.
- **Copy feedback:** the button changes to "Link copied", keeps a fixed width so the footer doesn't move, and is announced in a polite live region inside the dialog. The global toast is used only from the header menu, because it sits outside the modal's focus trap.
- **Esc** leaves Link settings first, then the add-people step, before it closes the dialog.
- **Copy:** the role names (Can watch / Can write / Can start sessions, Agent permissions, Remove access) are updated in all 9 locales. Sharing strings say "Orchestrator.inc". The rest of the app keeps "AO".

**Intentional omissions:**
- No help (?) icon, because there is no sharing docs page for it to link to.
- No persistent per-session link with *Reset link* (the research's Phase 2), which needs control-plane work.
- No email *Notify people*: the footer line is placed where it will go.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Share, teams and i18n suites: 15 files, 186 tests pass (`ShareSessionDialog*.test.tsx`, `SessionPeople.test.tsx`, `share/*`, `teams/*`, `settings/TeamsSection.test.tsx`, `lib/share-links.test.ts`, `main/session-share-urls.test.ts`, `i18n/*`). New tests cover:
  - the restricted state;
  - turning link access on (Can watch, 7 days, URL remembered, Copy link copies it);
  - Copy new link with the same access and remaining expiry;
  - the broadest of several links and "and 1 more";
  - no Trusted on links;
  - the write confirmation, with the new link made before the old one is revoked;
  - turning off with removeJoined, and without control-plane support;
  - Link settings revoke;
  - "Share the whole project instead";
  - links-only builds;
  - the clipboard-failure fallback;
  - the personal workspace check;
  - the Share menu's Copy link and its toast;
  - the encrypted store's IPC guards.
- Full `npm test`: in the local run, failures outside this change are in `ContextMeter`/`ChatWorkspace` number formatting and in network timeouts in `remote-proxy`, `cloud-agent-proxy` and `browser-cookie-repair`. None of them import changed code. CI is the check for them.
- Real app: a dev build against staging was driven over CDP to capture the screenshots.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (screenshots to attach; see above)
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review follow-up (10ae81aadb)
This supersedes anything above that differs:
- **Removing people who joined is opt-in everywhere.** Copy link replacing a Trusted link, narrowing a link, turning link access off and revoking in Link settings all start unticked. The confirmation says those people keep their access unless the box is ticked.
- **Copy new link** recognises the link it just made by server timestamps and keeps it in the cached list, so client/server clock skew can't mint a link per click. On a Can write link it asks first with the write warning; raising a link from Read only to Standard asks too.
- **Personal workspace** comes only from `/me` `kind: "personal"`. The name heuristic is gone; an unknown workspace (loading, failed) reads "Only people with access can open this session" and keeps the workspace row.
- **Header menu** re-reads links before copying and opens the dialog for a link that is no longer live. With only the project's link on it says "Only the whole project's link is on".
- **URL store** is owned by the signed-in user: another user's file is ignored and removed after a restart, and a file it can't decrypt is treated as empty and replaced.
- **Removal notice** uses the server's `removedGrants`.
- **Contract:** the project share-link endpoints (list, create, revoke with `removeJoined`, redeem) are in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`; `schema.ts` regenerated; `oasdiff breaking` reports none. Other share routes (grants, direct, access, teams) are still not in the contract.
- Tests: typecheck clean; share, teams, client and i18n suites 270/270.

title: fix(chat): open HTML artifacts outside the chat from their preview origin
body:
Code changes: +26 -11\
Tests: +33 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The chat artifact card's **Open in external browser** and **Open in AO Browser** now open an HTML artifact from its preview origin (`ao-preview-artifact.<session>.localhost`), without the chat frame's `#ao-theme` fragment. Before, both opened the daemon's `artifact-files` route. If the session lists no preview URL for the artifact, the card doesn't offer either action. Renders are unchanged.

## Why

Reported by a teammate. Opening a chat artifact in the system browser landed on:

```
http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/poc-14/artifact-files/permissions_framework.html#ao-theme=…
{"error":"forbidden","code":"ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN","message":"Origin is not allowed to access this daemon"}
```

Root cause: `RenderFrame`'s `standaloneUrl()` builds `getApiBaseUrl() + page.path + renderThemeFragment(…)` for both renders and artifacts. For an artifact, `page.path` is `artifact.url`, the `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/artifact-files/…` route that the chat frames. A top-level browser navigation sends no Origin, only `Sec-Fetch-Site: none`. `browserRequestAllowed` lets that through only for preview hosts, the `/preview/{files,artifacts}/` routes and `/renders/{id}`, so renders open fine and artifacts always 403. The daemon is right to refuse it; the client was opening the wrong URL.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Open in external browser on a chat artifact → `127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/{id}/artifact-files/<page>.html#ao-theme=…` → 403 `ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN` | Opens `http://ao-preview-artifact.<session>.localhost:3001/<page>.html`, the same URL the Artifacts tab's Open in AO Browser and `ao preview` use |
| Open in AO Browser on a chat artifact → same 403 URL | Same preview URL |
| Artifact with no listed preview URL: both actions shown, both fail | Both actions hidden |

## How

- **`standaloneUrl()`:** returns the artifact's `previewUrl` from `useChatArtifactLinks` for an artifact, and keeps the render route plus theme fragment for a render.
- **`opensStandalone`:** gates both actions, so an artifact with no preview URL never offers a link that can't load.
- **Daemon:** no changes; its origin checks are unchanged.

## Testing

No local test runs; CI verifies. `RenderFrame.test.tsx`:
- External browser and AO Browser open `previewUrl` with no fragment.
- An artifact without a listed preview has neither action.
- The existing render tests (render route plus `#ao-theme`) are unchanged.

Separate from #7814 so it can ship on its own; #7814 doesn't touch `RenderFrame`.

title: fix(chat): keep slash commands when the daemon reattaches to a live chat host
body:
Code changes: +45 -1  
Tests: +84 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Claude Code chats that survived a daemon restart showed only AO's `/compact` in the `/` menu. Claude Code's own commands and the user's skills and plugin commands were missing. The persistent chat host now keeps the latest command catalog, and a reattaching daemon picks it up from there.

## Why

The bug showed up in the orchestrator because it's the longest-lived chat, but it isn't specific to orchestrators. On a live daemon, every Claude chat created before the current daemon start returned `{"skills":[]}` from `GET /sessions/{id}/conversation/skills`: the orchestrator plus workers `-4` and `-7`. Every chat created after the start returned the full list (~340 entries).

Root cause:

1. ACP adapters (claude-agent-acp included) announce slash commands once, as an `available_commands_update` notification right after session setup. The ACP driver's `ListSkills` reads only what that notification left behind.
2. Chat providers run in a persistent `ao chat-host` process that outlives the daemon. The host's ACP relay forwards that notification to whichever daemon is attached at the time and keeps no copy.
3. After a daemon restart (for example an app update or relaunch), the new daemon reattaches to the running host. It rebuilds the conversation from the host's `ACPState` snapshot, which holds only the `initialize` and `session/new` results. No `session/load` is sent, so the adapter never re-announces its commands and the catalog stays empty until the host itself restarts.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Claude chat reattached after a daemon restart: `conversation/skills` → `{"skills":[]}`. The `/` menu shows only AO's `/compact`. | The same reattached chat keeps its full catalog (343 entries for the orchestrator and 338 for the worker in the dev run). The `/` menu lists Claude Code commands, user skills and plugin commands. |

## How

- `persistenthost`: the ACP relay records the latest `available_commands_update` catalog together with its session ID. The `ACPState` snapshot includes it (`availableCommands`) only when that session is still the host's session.
- `acp` driver: on the live-reattach path, the driver seeds the conversation with that catalog before `start`, so the skills and compaction capabilities are set as they are for a fresh session. A newer catalog replayed from the detached buffer still replaces it.

## Testing

- Unit tests:
  - `TestACPRelayRetainsAvailableCommandsForReconnect`: the latest catalog wins, and a catalog for another session is not handed over.
  - `TestPersistentACPResumeRestoresAvailableCommands`: a reattached conversation lists the commands and reports the skills and compaction capabilities.
- Real desktop app (`ao-desktop-dev`, isolated data dir):
  - Created a Claude Code chat orchestrator and a worker. Both listed their commands.
  - Stopped the daemon and later the whole app; the `chat-host` processes stayed alive. The new daemon reattached (initialize under 1 ms, no `session/load`). Both sessions still returned 343 and 338 commands.
  - Typing `/` in each composer showed the Claude Code commands and user skills.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet` ran locally. The test suites run in CI.

## Notes

- The ring next to `+` in the bug report is `ContextMeter` (the "Context window used" progress bar). It's a static fill that appears after a turn reports usage, not a loading indicator, and it isn't related to this bug.
- Hosts already running an older build don't have the catalog, so an existing reattached chat recovers once its host restarts (for example after restarting the session). New hosts keep it across daemon restarts.
- Not covered: a later `config_option_update` is lost across reattach in the same way. That's a separate change.

## Checklist

- [x] Root cause identified and fixed at the host/driver boundary
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Verified in the real desktop app

title: fix(desktop): mask-based scroll edge fades that work with window transparency
body:
## Summary

Edge fades were gradients painted into a solid surface color (`bg-sidebar`, `bg-primary`, `--bg`, `bg-settings-menu`). With window transparency on, that color is itself translucent or doesn't match the tint underneath, so the sidebar session lists, the center tab strip, and the Browser and side-chat tab strips showed hard cuts or tinted smears. The chat transcript also had no fade under the top bar.

Every scroll edge fade now goes through one shared utility:

- **`.edge-fade` / `.edge-fade-x`** (styles.css): a CSS `mask-image` on the scroller itself. It doesn't depend on the background, so it works with transparency on and off, in every theme, light and dark. Masks don't affect hit testing, so faded content stays clickable.
- **`hooks/useEdgeFade.ts`**: `syncEdgeFade` toggles `data-fade-start` / `data-fade-end`. `observeEdgeFade` runs it from a passive scroll listener, plus a frame-batched ResizeObserver (on the scroller and its first and last child) and a childList MutationObserver. Scrolling never re-renders React. `useEdgeFade(ref)` and `useEdgeFadeRef()` wrap it.
- Sizes are per site through `--edge-fade-size`, `--edge-fade-start-size` and `--edge-fade-end-size`. The default is 24px; the sidebar uses 16px.

Where it's used:

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar project and Scratchpad lists | Gradient into `bg-sidebar` | Mask, top and bottom, 16px |
| Center tab strip (terminal pane and chat session) | Gradient into `bg-sidebar` / `bg-primary` | Mask, left and right |
| Browser and side-chat tab strips (inspector) | Gradient into `--bg` | Mask, left and right |
| Chat transcript | No top fade; 10px gradient above the composer | Top fade 24px once scrolled (none at scrollTop 0), 12px bottom fade while there is more below |
| Settings, Artifacts, Archive and Home page bodies | Hard cut under the top bar | Top fade only |
| Model and option menus | Gradient into `bg-settings-menu` with React state | Mask, top and bottom |
| Chat plan window | Already a mask (chat-only helper) | Moved onto the shared helper |

Also fixed: a tab strip's glide to a new tab held its end fade off until the glide reached the end. If the glide was interrupted, the end fade stayed off. It now clears on `scrollend` and on the reader's wheel.

Audit notes. These stay as they are: the static `mask-image` clamps in HarnessUpdateNotice, SessionLinkPreviewCard and ArtifactThumbnail are already background-agnostic, and annotate-preload's adjustment panel is injected into web pages and paints its own solid `--bg`.

## Screenshots

These are native captures of the dev window (`screencapture -R` on the on-screen region, so vibrancy is real) over a busy test wallpaper. Each image shows the sidebar lists and the top bar with the transcript; before is on top, after is below.

**Light + transparency on** (the most visible breakage: the transcript under the bar, the last Scratchpad row, and the tab strip's right end are hard cuts)
![light translucent](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/de0c3a98a7785d5a514f7becce9f8542a374eb9e/compare-light-translucent.png?raw=true)

**Dark + transparency on**
![dark translucent](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/de0c3a98a7785d5a514f7becce9f8542a374eb9e/compare-dark-translucent.png?raw=true)

**Light + transparency off**
![light opaque](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/de0c3a98a7785d5a514f7becce9f8542a374eb9e/compare-light-opaque.png?raw=true)

**Dark + transparency off**
![dark opaque](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/de0c3a98a7785d5a514f7becce9f8542a374eb9e/compare-dark-opaque.png?raw=true)

## Testing

- Verified in the real Electron dev app (isolated data copy) with transparency on and off, in light and dark. Checked the tab strip at mid scroll (both edges fade), the transcript scrolled up (top fades under the bar; nothing fades at scrollTop 0), sidebar lists mid scroll, and the Settings page top fade. Inspected the computed masks and data attributes over CDP.
- Updated tests: Sidebar, CenterPane and TurnPlan now assert the fade attributes. Added `hooks/useEdgeFade.test.ts`. Per repo practice, typecheck and vitest weren't run locally; CI is the check.

## Risks / follow-ups

- `mask-image` on the large chat scroller adds a mask layer. It's static apart from 150ms transitions of registered lengths, and scroll stays composited.
- The Browser panel tab strip and the model menus share code paths with the verified surfaces, but I didn't screenshot them in the app.

title: fix(sidebar): show the session hover card again after a context-menu rename
body:
## Problem
After renaming a session from its right-click menu, hovering that row no longer showed the session hover card. Only the renamed row was affected, and it stayed broken until the app reloaded. Renaming by double-click, F2, or double-tap was fine.

## Root cause
`SessionRow` suppresses its preview while `contextMenuOpen` is true. That flag is set from the uncontrolled Radix `ContextMenu`'s `onOpenChange`.

Choosing **Rename** runs `onSelect` synchronously. That sets `rename.isEditing`, and the row renders the inline editor in place of the `ContextMenu`, unmounting the menu while it is still open. Radix (`use-controllable-state` 1.2.3) reports an uncontrolled close from an effect, and that effect never runs after unmount. As a result `onOpenChange(false)` never fires, and `contextMenuOpen` stays `true` for as long as the row is mounted.

## Fix
`beginRename` clears `contextMenuOpen` before it starts editing. The safe-triangle and hover logic from #7828 in `useSessionPreviewHover` is unchanged.

## Tests
- New `Sidebar.test.tsx` case: rename from the context menu, commit, hover the row, and expect the board card.
- I didn't run tests locally; CI covers them.
- Reproduced manually in the desktop app via the context menu. The double-click rename path was not affected.

title: fix(desktop): a Cloud worker defaults to its orchestrator's model
body:
## Problem
Starting a worker in a Cloud project never considered the model the project's orchestrator runs. With no worker model set for the project, New Task fell back to the last used or catalog default, so an orchestrator on Opus 5.5 got workers on another model.

## Fix
**New Task default model for a Cloud project, first match wins**
1. The model you pick.
2. A model you picked before for this project and agent.
3. The project's worker model for that agent.
4. The orchestrator's current model, when the agent matches, the account can run it, and the picker can select it.
5. Last used, then the catalog default, then the existing fallback.

The orchestrator's model shows a **"Same as orchestrator"** hint in the New Task picker and the new-chat agent picker (`newTask.sameAsOrchestrator`, all 9 locales). The hint shows whichever model is the default.

**Default effort**
- An effort you picked comes first.
- Otherwise, the effort that goes with the model shown: the project's with the project's model, or the orchestrator's with the orchestrator's model when Cloud's catalog lists that level for it.

**The orchestrator's model comes from the server.** `useCloudOrchestratorModel` takes the project's live orchestrator from the cached session list. It reads `currentModel` / `currentReasoningEffort`, which the control plane resolves with the same rule its spawns use (OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#61); `""` means the agent's default.
- While that orchestrator's Chat is open in this window, its live settings are newer and win. "default" means no model, and an effort stays with the model it was chosen for.
- A control plane that predates `currentModel` omits it, and the hook falls back to the session's created model.
- No new requests, polling or streams. The hook wakes only for the session list query.

**Only what you chose is remembered**
- Launching and switching agents used to save the model and effort on screen as if you had picked them, which froze the effort over the orchestrator's and the project's.
- Now only picks you made are kept, and a chosen effort is saved with `effortChosen: true`. An effort saved before this change, which may never have been chosen, applies only where neither the project nor the orchestrator names one.

**Session events hub:** when no stream is wanted any more, the hub now publishes its closed state. Before, it left `open: true` with no stream, and a remounted Chat polled slowly.

**Contract:**
- `Session` gains optional `currentModel` and `currentReasoningEffort`.
- `CreateWorkerChildInput` gains optional `model` (maxLength 500) and `reasoningEffort`.
- `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated, and oasdiff reports no breaking changes.

## Known limits
- Local (daemon) orchestrators are unchanged.
- A Chat model switch made on another device reaches this composer on the next session-list refresh, not instantly.

## Tests
- [x] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` clean.
- [x] TaskComposer "Cloud orchestrator model" block (15 cases). It covers:
  - the precedence;
  - the effort that goes with each default;
  - a launch with an untouched effort not freezing it;
  - a chosen effort being remembered;
  - a legacy saved effort;
  - a "default" orchestrator;
  - another agent, a terminated orchestrator, and another project being unaffected.
- [x] Hook tests:
  - the server fields;
  - live precedence;
  - "default" handling;
  - present-but-empty versus absent `currentModel`;
  - live model changes and effort.
- [x] A hub closed-state test, plus TurnSettingsBar, NewChatPage, AgentModelCombobox, settings and i18n suites. Affected suites: 56 files, 1067 tests pass, plus cloud-client typecheck and tests. CI green.
- [x] Dev app against staging (control plane with #61), all as intended:
  - With a project worker model set, New Task defaults to it, and the orchestrator's model is marked "Same as orchestrator", read from the server with its Chat never opened.
  - With none set, New Task defaults to the orchestrator's model and effort.
  - After a launch with the effort untouched, raising the orchestrator to High moves New Task to High.
  - An effort picked by hand is remembered over the orchestrator's.
  - An orchestrator on "default" marks nothing.
  - Leaving and reopening the orchestrator's Chat reconnects it.
  - Launched tasks ran the model and effort the composer showed.

title: fix(desktop): restore archived sessions from the chat view
body:
Code changes: +45 -13\
Tests: +131 -1\
Others: +18 -0 (locale strings)

## What

An archived (terminated) chat session now shows **Restore session** in the chat view. Clicking it restores the session: the worktree comes back, Setup runs, and the agent resumes on the same conversation.

## Why

The chat banner offered **Resume agent** on an archived session. That calls `/resume-agent`, which the daemon refuses for a terminated session, so the click only printed "Session is terminated" (409) and the session stayed stuck. The CLI (`ao session restore`) and mobile already restore here; the desktop chat view was the only client without a way back.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: archived chat shows a red "The agent controller stopped" alert with Resume agent and Open shell](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c199dd59-1c3b-403b-923a-d6b2dd91de2d) | ![After: archived chat shows "Session terminated" with Restore session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ac6b3f8-0b01-4003-8897-55c63c919d28) |
| ![Before: clicking Resume agent fails with "Session is terminated"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35fe2f21-a995-46fe-ad6e-e52c602b5f6f) | ![After: clicking Restore session shows "Restoring session" with the composer locked](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50cd150f-67e7-4b6e-a1d1-9baeea25fedb) |
| The composer says "The controller is not connected" and never unlocks | ![After: the restored agent answers the next message on the same conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5336786a-171f-4a9b-a89e-ebf869a9f236) |

## How

- `useConversationCommands` takes a `terminated` flag. When it is set, the resume mutation calls `useRestoreSession` (the same path as the session list's Restore, with remote-host, cloud and telemetry handling) instead of `/resume-agent`. The daemon still refuses `/resume-agent` for terminated sessions.
- The mutation stays pending until the session query is refetched. Without that, the cached snapshot still read "stopped" for about 100 ms after a successful restore and flashed the red crash alert.
- `ControllerBanner` on a terminated session: muted tone, archive icon, `role="status"`, "Session terminated" title, **Restore session** button. **Open shell** is hidden there, because with the worktree removed the shell silently opens in the project root, not "the same worktree".
- The composer stays locked while the session is terminated and says "Restore the session to continue", then "Restoring session" during the restore. The startup reconnect wait is skipped for terminated sessions.
- Two new strings, `chat.archived.body` and `chat.archived.placeholder`, in all 9 locales.

## Testing

- New tests, written to fail first: restore path, pending until the restored agent is read, refused restore reported through the resume error (`useConversation.test.tsx`); Restore instead of Resume, composer locked while restoring, no reconnect wait (`ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`); terminated flag passed for archived and live sessions (`SessionChatSurface.test.tsx`).
- Locally: the renderer `hooks`, `components/chat` and `i18n` suites passed (2926 tests); after the last change to the restore wait, the touched test files passed again. Rebasing onto current `main` left the commit unchanged (`git range-diff` reports `=`); CI covers the rebased tree.
- Real desktop app in an isolated lab (own data dir and port) with a real Codex chat session. Before: `POST /api/v1/sessions/repo-1/resume-agent` returned 409. After: `POST /api/v1/sessions/repo-1/restore` returned 200, the composer unlocked in 1.6 to 4.5 s, and Codex replied on the same conversation across five archive and restore cycles with every earlier turn kept.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
