title: fix(sessions): restore an archived worktree on its last branch
body:
Code changes: +44 -2\
Tests: +144 -17\
Others: +3 -0 (generated `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`)

## What

Restoring an archived session now brings its worktree back on the branch the agent last had checked out, such as its PR branch, instead of the session's `…/root` branch.

## Why

Archiving removes the worktree together with its git worktree registration, so restore no longer knew which branch the worktree had. It recreated the worktree on the session branch. An archived session whose agent had moved to a PR branch came back on its root branch, without its work and, in the case that found this, 60 commits behind `main`.

## Before / After

Real desktop app and a real Codex chat worker, same steps on both builds: the worker moves from its `…/root` branch to a new branch `…/pr-work` and commits `WORK.md` (not pushed). The branch prefix comes from the prompt, so it is `ao/branch-commit` in the Before run and `ao/pr-work` in the After run. The session is then archived and restored, and the restored agent is asked for `git branch --show-current` and `cat WORK.md`.

| Before (`main`) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: after restore the inspector shows ao/branch-commit/root and the agent replies "ao/branch-commit/root cat: WORK.md: No such file or directory"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3ff9f04-75a9-4ec9-b691-f84c9b08aa03) | ![After: after restore the inspector shows the session branch ao/pr-work/root with 1 commit not pushed, and the agent replies "ao/pr-work/pr-work agent work"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5d5c4b9-9ef9-4f42-b812-d66808874b39) |
| Worktree restored on `ao/branch-commit/root`; `WORK.md` and the agent's commit are missing | Worktree restored on `ao/pr-work/pr-work`, with `WORK.md` and commit `agent work` |
| Recorded `branch_state`: `{"commits":1,"unpushed":1}` | `{"branch":"ao/pr-work/pr-work","commits":1,"unpushed":1}` |
| Session branch after restore: `ao/branch-commit/root` | `ao/pr-work/root`, unchanged; the inspector's label shows it, as it does for a live session that switched branches |

<details><summary>Lab output (After)</summary>

```text
== before archive
worktree branch: ao/pr-work/pr-work
session branch: ao/pr-work/root | status: idle
db branch_state: {"branch":"ao/pr-work/pr-work","commits":1,"unpushed":1}
session repo-1 killed
== archived
worktree dir present: no
session branch: ao/pr-work/root | status: terminated
db branch_state: {"branch":"ao/pr-work/pr-work","commits":1,"unpushed":1}
<lab>/repo  7c12e06 [main]
local branches: ao/pr-work/pr-work ao/pr-work/root main 
== restored
worktree branch: ao/pr-work/pr-work
WORK.md: agent work
9c7c851 agent work
session branch: ao/pr-work/root | status: idle
db branch_state: {"branch":"ao/pr-work/pr-work","commits":1,"unpushed":1}
```

</details>

## How

- The branch-state reconcile records `branch`, the branch checked out in the worktree, in `SessionBranchState`. The branch is part of its change fingerprint, so switching to a new branch on the same commit is still recorded.
- Single-repo restores (manual restore and restore-all) pass it to the workspace as `WorkspaceConfig.LastBranch`. States recorded before this change have no `branch`; for those, the pushed `remoteBranch` (`origin/<name>`) names it, so already-archived sessions with a pushed PR branch also come back on it.
- `gitworktree.Restore` uses `LastBranch` only when no git registration survived (a surviving registration still wins, as before), the local branch still exists, and no other worktree has it checked out. Otherwise it restores the session branch, as before.
- Archiving records the worktree's branch itself, after the agent stops and before the row is terminated. The observer ticks every 30 s and skips terminated sessions, so without this a branch the agent switched to just before the archive was never recorded.
- Restore no longer rewrites the session branch to the branch the worktree came back on (single-repo projects, every restore path, including a worktree that survived the archive dirty). Before, after a restore onto `ao/x/pr-work`, PR auto-attribution narrowed from `ao/x/*` to that one branch, and a later restore after `ao/x/pr-work` was deleted created an empty branch with that name. The checkout stays in `branch_state`.
- Workspace projects are not changed. `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are regenerated for the new optional field.
- Separate from #7898 (the chat view's Restore button). #7381 and #7388 change `manager.go` near restore, but not which branch it uses.

## Testing

- New tests, written to fail first: real-git `TestWorkspaceIntegrationRestoreUsesLastCheckedOutBranch` (branch exists → PR branch; deleted or checked out elsewhere → session branch); reconcile tests now expect `branch`, including a same-commit branch switch; `TestRestorePassesTheLastCheckedOutBranch` (recorded branch, `remoteBranch` only, never observed).
- Ran locally: `go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages, the full `gitworktree` package, `session_manager` restore and reconcile tests, the `apispec` drift tests, and the `service/session` package. In that package, `TestSearchWorkspaceContentCommonTermReachesLaterFiles` (content search, not touched here) timed out once at a load average of about 98 and passed when run alone.
- `schema.ts` matches the frontend's `openapi-typescript` output byte for byte.
- Lab: a bare `ao daemon` per build with its own data dir and port, a local `origin`, and a real Codex chat worker, as in Before / After.
- `TestKill_RecordsTheWorktreeBranchBeforeTeardown`: the kill records the branch while the row is live and the worktree exists. `TestRestoreOnTheLastBranchKeepsTheSessionBranch`: a restore onto another branch leaves the session branch as it was.
- More lab cases on this branch: one daemon, a local `origin`, a real Codex chat worker per case. Git state was set by the agent (C1, C13) or by the same git commands in the worktree, then the session was archived and restored with the CLI.

| Case | Restored on | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 agent switches, commits and pushes a PR branch | the pushed branch; resumed agent reports it, tracking `origin`, with `WORK.md` | as expected |
| C2 row recorded before this change (`branch` removed, `remoteBranch` kept) | the pushed branch | as expected |
| C3 PR branch deleted while archived | `…/root`, no error | as expected |
| C4 PR branch checked out in the main checkout while archived | `…/root`, no error | as expected |
| C5 new branch on the same commit, no commits | the new branch | as expected |
| C6 detached HEAD at archive | `…/root` | as expected |

title: feat(chat): open images in rendered pages at full size
body:
## Summary

Images in a page an agent shows with `ao render` or `html_render` now open at full size when clicked, and the chat image viewer uses the whole window instead of half of it.

- **Render images.** A render runs in a sandboxed frame, so the app never saw clicks on its images. The render bootstrap now sends a click on an image that is not inside a link or button to the chat frame (`ao/open-image`). The frame opens it in the chat image viewer, with copy and save on right-click.
  - Only the chat frame opts in, through an `openImages` host-context field. The artifact viewer and pages opened on their own are unchanged.
  - A page that handles the click itself (`preventDefault`) keeps it: the listener is on `window`, after the page's handlers, including delegated ones on `document`.
  - Only `data:image/` sources are passed on, and only while the reader is using that frame (the same check link requests use). The viewer loads the URL in the app document, outside the page's sandbox, CSP and local-network guard, so a remote URL could leak data from an offline render or reach the local network. `ao render` inlines local images as `data:`.
- **Viewer width.** The viewer dialog was `w-auto` on a `left: 50%` fixed element, so shrink-to-fit only had the right half of the window and images stopped near 50vw. `w-max` sizes it to the image, still capped by the existing `max-w`/`max-h`. Chat markdown images get this too.

- **Copy and Save on `data:` images.** The viewer's right-click menu reads the image with `fetch`, and the packaged renderer CSP left `data:` out of `connect-src`, so both failed for `data:` images, which is every image `ao render` inlines. `connect-src` now allows `data:`. A `data:` fetch never reaches the network.

Stored renders get the bootstrap at serve time, so existing renders pick this up once the daemon updates.

## Before / after

Desktop dev app, window 1320×860, with a real Claude chat that published a render with `html_render` and then replied with a markdown image. Before is the same lab and chat with the three renderer files swapped back to `origin/main`. The driver checked the served source each time. The new bootstrap does nothing there, because main's renderer never sends `openImages` (in-frame image cursor: `auto`).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Click an image in a render | ![Clicking the wallpaper in the render opens nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef200d4a-d2ec-4807-9681-1f9f2c2bd832) | ![The wallpaper opens in the image viewer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc485a26-8f7b-459f-8c4f-5e52f42d6d65) |
| Click a markdown image | ![The viewer stops at half the window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a716e401-8dae-4af5-82e6-8c3e6f75cf93) | ![The viewer fills the window height](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/709b015d-3fa4-4abb-a627-c75da301aad1) |

| Measured | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Render image click (inline 378×246) | no dialog | viewer, 732×732 |
| Markdown image (natural 1320×860) | viewer, 642×418 | viewer, 1124×732 |

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/renderpage/`
- vitest `render-frame.test.ts`, `RenderFrame.test.tsx`, `ChatImage.test.tsx`, `vite.renderer.config.test.ts`: 63 pass. New cases: `readRenderImageRequest` accepts only `data:image/` sources (refusing `https:`, local-network, loopback and `blob:` URLs), and `RenderFrame` opens a posted image only from the focused frame. That test fails with the focus check removed.
- `tsgo --noEmit`: no errors under `src/`.
- CSP: in Electron 44.7.0 / Chromium 152, with the build `connect-src` from `contentSecurityPolicy("build")`, `loadChatImage`'s fetch of a PNG `data:` URL is refused on main and reads 67 bytes `image/png` on this branch. `vite.renderer.config.test.ts` pins `data:` in the build `connect-src`.
- Bootstrap: in Electron 44 with trusted mouse input on a framed page, a click on an image the page's delegated `document` lightbox claims opened both viewers before and only the page's after. A click on an `https:` image posted its URL before and posts nothing after.

## Risks

- A page that handles image clicks itself without calling `preventDefault` now also opens the viewer.
- Remote (`https:`) images in a render, and relative image URLs in HTML artifacts, do not open in the viewer.

title: Feature request: notify the orchestrator when a worker's turns fail repeatedly or it goes silent
body:
# Feature request: notify the orchestrator when a worker's turns fail repeatedly or it goes silent

## Context

Tested on daemon 0.14.10 (commit 033d597032e4). AO already has solid automatic detection:

- the runtime reaper (5s tick) marks sessions `exited`/`terminated` when the process dies,
- the turn-failure observer (2s tick) corrects failed/interrupted turns to a terminal state,
- `waiting_input` is the one event that auto-generates a user notification.

Report delivery itself is excellent — the coordinator delivers reports automatically, survives daemon restarts, and stuck/needs-input reports arrive within the same second in our data.

## The gap

The reaper and the turn-failure observer **only update the session state row**. They never generate a report, never notify the orchestrator, and never notify the user. So when a worker's process is alive but:

- every turn fails at startup (e.g. a JSON-RPC `-32600` harness/provider mismatch), or
- the worker goes silent for a long stretch,

…no one is alerted. The session can sit in `working` the whole time.

## Real case (from our local ao.db)

One worker failed turn startup 5 times in a row over ~27 minutes. During that
window: zero notifications, zero reports. When the user asked the orchestrator
"is everything on track?", the orchestrator answered "yes, normal" — because
`ao session ls` still showed the session as `working`. The failure was only
found ~10 minutes after the user challenged the answer, when the orchestrator
read the session transcript and saw 5 consecutive `failed` turns.

## Requests

1. **Turn-failure notification**: when a session accumulates N consecutive failed turns (say N=3), generate an orchestrator-visible notification — same channel as `waiting_input` — or synthesize a system report into the report queue.
2. **Silence watchdog (optional)**: alert when a running session has had no turn activity for X minutes, covering "alive but stuck".
3. **Surface failure counts in `ao session ls --json`**: expose a per-session recent-failed-turn count so orchestrators can detect this class without fetching every transcript.

## Evidence shape (local, ao.db)

- `conversation_turns`: 5 rows `state=failed` for that window;
- `notifications`: no rows for that worker in that window;
- the -32600 error text is a local gateway detail, redacted here.

Happy to provide more detail if useful — thanks for the great tool.

The desktop app's icons now come from [Myna UI](https://mynaui.com) (`@mynaui/icons-react` 0.4.11) instead of lucide.

Most of the 217 files are one-line import swaps. The files that need a real review are `app-icons.tsx`, product-ui `icons.tsx`, `components/icons.tsx` and `SessionInspector.tsx`.

title: fix(mobile): keep the keyboard up while typing in iOS Connect manually
body: Code changes: +13 -5\ Tests: +141 -3\ Others: +0 -0 ## What On iOS, typing a host in **Connect manually** closed the keyboard after the first character. The field showed `1` and the rest of `127.0.0.1` went nowhere. The same happened when you cleared the host, when the port switched between valid and invalid, and on the first edit after a failed connect. Edit machine had the same problem with the port and with a save failure. - `FormFooter` takes optional text and draws nothing when there's none. It always applies `foregroundStyle`: hierarchical secondary (what iOS uses for a footer by default) for a hint, red for an error, so switching between them changes only the style. - Connect manually's Connection section and both of Edit machine's sections keep their footer mounted; only its text changes. ## Why `@expo/ui`'s `SectionView.swift` builds `regularSection` with a `@ViewBuilder` `if`/`else`. It chooses a different SwiftUI `Section` depending on whether a footer slot is present. These sections passed a footer only while there was a hint or an error (`footer={error ? … : hint ? … : undefined}`). So whenever the footer appeared or disappeared, SwiftUI took the other branch, rebuilt the section's text fields, and the focused field lost focus along with the keyboard. In Connect manually, with the name and port filled, the first host character removes the "Add a host to connect." hint, and that is when the keyboard closed. Editing a field also clears a failed connect, so the first keystroke of a fix removed the error footer. I confirmed the cause on an iOS 26.5 simulator. With the footer held in place (an invalid port `0` keeps "Enter a port from 1 to 65535." showing), the whole `127.0.0.1` typed without losing focus. With the footer allowed to change, focus dropped on every change. The bug came in with the native Connect manually rebuild in #7838. ## Before / After iOS 26.5 simulator (iPhone 17 Pro), Release builds of `main` and of this branch, fresh install, same steps. Type the name, tap the host field once, type `127.0.0.1`. Then press backspace 9 times and type `10.0.0.5`, still without tapping the field again. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | Step (one tap on the host field) | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Type `127.0.0.1` | `1` | `127.0.0.1` | | 9 backspaces | `1` (focus already gone) | empty | | Type `10.0.0.5` | `1` | `10.0.0.5` | ## How - The fix stays in JS, with no native or `@expo/ui` patch, so the runtime fingerprint for the 2.3 build doesn't change. - **Trade-off:** an empty footer is still a footer, so with nothing to show, Connect manually has about 10 pt more space above "Connect with QR code" (see the After screenshots). A zero-height frame on the empty text doesn't remove it, because the gap is the footer's own inset. Removing it would need a patch to `@expo/ui`'s `SectionView` (always use the `footer:` initializer), and that is native. - Edit machine's name section keeps its footer only for an account-managed machine, the only case where it can show one. That doesn't change while you type, so it never toggles. - The other conditional footers (`MachineDetail`, `MachineNameForm`, `project-card`) sit on sections with no text fields, so they're left as they are. ## Testing - New `ManualConnectSheet` test: walks the form through the hint going and coming back, an invalid and a valid port, and a failed connect that then gets cleared. It checks the footer stays mounted at every step. It failed at "first host character" before the fix. - New `MachineEditorForm.test.tsx` (iOS): checks the Connection footer through a port error and a save failure, and the account machine's name footer. Both tests fail against `main`'s `MachineEditorForm.tsx`. - Updated the three existing assertions that expected the footer to disappear. - A further test renders the footer and checks that the hint and an error carry the same single `foregroundStyle` modifier, with only its style changing. On the simulator the hint's text is pixel-identical to `main` (same colour, same pixel count). - `npm run typecheck` passes. `npx vitest run`: 354 files and 3,448 tests pass. - iOS 26.5 simulator, Release build: the host typing check above, before and after. - The port and failed-connect paths were seen failing on `main` while pairing a simulator (a port that ended up `50`, and a password fix that needed a re-tap). For the fix they're covered by the unit tests, not re-run on the simulator. - Android is unaffected: `ManualConnectSheet.android.tsx` and `MachineEditorForm.android.tsx` don't use SwiftUI sections. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(mobile): keep a loader up through chat/terminal switches
body:
Code changes: +267 -98\
Tests: +106 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On mobile, switching a session between Chat and Terminal now shows one continuous loader from the tap until the other screen appears. It no longer flashes "Session terminated", and a newly opened terminal no longer shows an empty grid.

## Why

Switching Terminal → Chat first showed **"Session terminated"**, and the chat UI only appeared about 3s later. The switch stops the terminal's PTY on purpose. Its exit set the screen's dead state, and the "Session terminated" overlay drew on top of the "Switching to Chat" card. It stayed up until the board's next poll changed the session's mode and the route swapped to Chat.

Switching Chat → Terminal had two problems. It only showed a thin banner. Then it landed on an empty black terminal while the agent's TUI booted.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal → Chat: "Switching to Chat" card, then "Session terminated" + a "Terminal exited" notice for ~3s, then Chat | "Switching to Chat" card the whole way, ending on "Chat is ready. Opening it now." until Chat replaces the screen |
| Chat → Terminal: yellow "Switching to Terminal UI · …" banner, then the "stopped" banner, then an empty black terminal | Same card as the other direction ("Switching to Terminal", with Cancel/Retry), then a "Starting terminal…" loader until the agent draws |

Not yet checked against a live switch on a device or simulator, because a switch stops and restarts a real agent. Screenshots or a recording still need to be added.

## How

- **`useInterfaceHandoff`** / **`interfaceHandoffPending`**: there is a gap after the daemon reports the transition `completed` and before the board row's `mode` flips. During that gap, the source screen keeps its switch card. This only applies to a switch the screen saw while it was live, so an old completed transition never brings the card back on a later visit.
- **Terminal screen**: while the card is up, the PTY exit still marks the terminal dead, but the screen shows neither the "Session terminated" overlay nor the exit notice. A PTY that exits outside a switch is reported as before.
- **Chat screen**: the active-switch banner is replaced by the same card. Other banners are held back while the card is up, because a stopped controller at that point is the handoff itself, not something to act on.
- **`InterfaceSwitchCard`**: the terminal's existing overlay card, extracted so both screens share it. It has the same styles, the same Cancel/Retry behaviour, and the same blocked-recovery state.
- **First-paint loader**: `useTerminalMux` gains an optional `onOutput` event. `createPaintDetector` returns true at the first byte that draws something. It ignores escape sequences, control bytes and spaces, and keeps parser state across chunks. Looking for any output wasn't enough: the attach handshake and a blank repaint arrive at once, while the TUI is still empty. The loader gives up after 15s so a genuinely blank terminal (a cleared shell, an empty alternate screen) is not hidden for good.

## Testing

- `npx tsgo --noEmit`: clean
- `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 356 files, 3473 tests pass
- New tests:
  - `interfaceHandoff.test.ts`: when a completed switch counts as pending
  - `terminalPaint.test.ts`: escapes, OSC titles, sequences split across chunks
  - `TerminalSessionScreen.test.tsx`:
    - the loader stays until the first paint
    - the card stays and the screen never shows terminated during a switch
    - a terminal that exits on its own is still reported
    - no card for a transition that completed before the visit
- Built and ran on the iOS simulator (iPhone 18 Pro) from this branch. The app loads and connects to the Mac. The switch flow itself has not been run end to end yet.

title: fix(mobile): footers that change go through FormSection, enforced by a test
body:
Code changes: +34 -22\
Tests: +100 -41\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Follow-ups from @ronishrohan's review of #7911, which was merged before they were pushed ([style thread](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7911#discussion_r4500907466), [props thread](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7911#discussion_r4500907662), [test thread](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7911#discussion_r4500907796)).

- **`FormSection` takes `error` and `hint`.** It works out the footer's text (`error || hint`) and its colour (`Boolean(error)`) itself, so the two can't drift apart, and an empty error still shows the hint.
- **Every footer that changes goes through `FormSection`.** That now includes `MachineDetail`'s default-machine note and `MachineNameForm`'s icon hint, so no SwiftUI `Section` in the app has a footer that comes and goes.
- **A source test enforces it.** `formSection.source.test.ts` fails if any file importing SwiftUI's `Section` passes it a conditional `footer` (`?` or `&&`), so the next form can't bring the #7906 focus bug back. This is the lint rule the review suggested. `DESIGN.md` is the desktop design guide, so the rule lives in a test instead.
- **Shared style:** `secondaryForeground` (in `lib/swiftUIStyles.ts`) builds the hierarchical secondary style once. `FormFooter`, `NativePickerList`, the elicitation choice list and the review actions sheet share it.
- **Tests:** the `ManualConnectSheet` footer tests share one helper. They drop the element-type check that `FormSection` made impossible to fail and keep the modifier check.

## Why

#7911 left two expressions computing the footer's text and its colour separately. It also left two plain `Section`s with conditional footers. They're harmless today because neither section has a text field, but nothing would stop the next form from repeating the pattern next to one. The same style modifier was also rebuilt in four places.

## Before / After

No user-visible change. iOS 26.5 simulator, Release builds:

- **Machine page:** Lab Mac's page, whose default-machine note now goes through `FormSection`, is pixel-identical to before. All three footer notes have 0 differing pixels.
- **Other footers:** now that every non-error `FormFooter` draws in hierarchical secondary, the machine page footers are also pixel-identical to a build whose non-error footers had no modifier. In a section footer the style resolves to exactly what iOS draws by default.
- **Connect manually:** still keeps the keyboard. With one tap, `127.0.0.1` types through, and clearing it and typing `10.0.0.5` works without a re-tap.

## How

- An empty `FormSection` footer draws nothing (#7911), so moving `MachineDetail` and `MachineNameForm` onto it changes nothing on screen for a machine that isn't the default, or for a form with no icon hint.
- The source test only looks at files that import `Section` from `@expo/ui/swift-ui`, so React Native components with their own `footer` prop (such as `project-card`) aren't affected.

## Testing

- **New:** `formFields.test.tsx`, where `FormSection` shows an error in red and otherwise the hint, including for an empty error. Also `formSection.source.test.ts`, which flagged `MachineDetail`, `MachineNameForm` and `MachineEditorForm` before the change.

## What

Adds a guide, **Test parallel sessions together**, under Guides, and links it from the guides list and index. It shows how to use fanout, an open-source (MIT) Claude Code and Codex plugin, with Orchestrator sessions: it tests session branches merged together before merge and stops two sessions from doing the same task.

Each session's pull request is checked by CI on its own. title: fix(chat): reconnect after a question pending across a restart
body:
Code changes: +53 -0
Tests: +100 -0
Others: +73 -0 (generated sqlc)

Fixes #7944. Surfaced by #7658; that report's no-card symptom is not reproduced by this change (see the review discussion).

## What was wrong

The chat host survives a daemon restart and replays its pending requests. An elicited question reaches `UpsertActivity` with only its `RequestID` — it has no `ProviderItemID` — and `UpsertActivity` matched existing rows by provider item id alone. The replay therefore went to insert and hit the partial unique index on `conversation_activities (conversation_id, request_id)`. The controller treats a failed projection as fatal: it stops with the provider retained for replay, the turn stays `running`, resolving the question returns `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`, and every retry — including **Resume agent** — replays into the same wall (#7944).

## The fix

A replay now refreshes the row AO already stored for that request id, in `UpsertActivity`:

- match by `request_id` when the activity carries no provider item, and settle that row instead of inserting a duplicate;
- only an **in-flight** row (`pending` or `running`) is brought up to date;
- any **settled** row stays settled, so a late replay cannot reopen it: a `resolved` row (an answered question), and equally a `failed` one — `settleOrphanedWork` fails a stranded question together with its turn, and reviving it would park a pending question on a failed turn, one the dock never shows.

Approaches explored and dropped after review:

- *controller-side turn anchoring*: dropped — `ActivateLiveReconnect` installs the turn correlation before the replay gate opens, and the stored row is already linked to the running turn in every observed run.
- *frontend dock fallback for turn-less questions*: dropped — `main` already docks a turn-less pending question while a turn runs (the `: !turn` branch of the skip condition is false when a turn exists), and docking one while *nothing* runs would surface stale questions.

## Tests

`TestUpsertActivityReplayRefreshesTheStoredQuestionInsteadOfColliding` — a replayed `input.requested` lands on the stored row (fails on `main` with exactly `UNIQUE constraint failed: conversation_activities.conversation_id, conversation_activities.request_id`, verified on pristine `main`), stays pending, and a late replay after the user answered keeps the row resolved.

`TestUpsertActivityReplayDoesNotReopenAFailedQuestion` — after `FailPendingInputs` (the `settleOrphanedWork` path: row and turn fail in the same pass), a replay keeps the row failed instead of reviving it to a pending question on a failed turn.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/store/` green, including both new tests; focused `internal/service/chat` failures are pre-existing Windows-environment issues (drive-letter `mkdir` syntax, symlink privilege, POSIX file mode) and reproduce identically on pristine `main`.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2: `0 issues` for `./internal/storage/sqlite/...`.
- `npm run sqlc` regenerated; the committed `gen/` output matches (CI sqlc-drift validates).

title: fix(desktop): render check fails with UnknownVizError on Electron 44
body:
Code changes: +25 -9\ Tests: +67 -21\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The render check behind `html_preview` and `ao render --check` now takes its screenshot from the offscreen window's `paint` frame instead of `webContents.capturePage()`. It waits a frame at a time until a frame shows the whole page. ## Why Every `html_preview` call failed with `UnknownVizError (RENDER_CHECK_FAILED)`, even for `

test

`. Agents are told to preview before `html_render`, so in practice they couldn't show inline HTML in chat. Reported by worker agent-orchestrator-27 (requests `KN6nyum1Pf-003780`, `-003871`, `-003907`), and reproduced from another session on the installed nightly `0.14.11-nightly.202611071129` (`KN6nyum1Pf-004807`). **Root cause:** the Electron 33 → 44 upgrade (#6462, merged 2026-10-17). `capturePainted()` called `invalidate()`, waited for one `paint` event, then called `capturePage()`. On Electron 44, an offscreen window's `invalidate()` re-sends its *last* frame synchronously. So the "paint" it waited for was the stale frame from before the resize to the page's height. `capturePage()` then ran before the compositor had a frame at the new size and rejected with `UnknownVizError`. Electron 33 resolved there instead, and the code's existing "capture again if stale" path covered it. One frame (16 ms) later `capturePage()` succeeds, which is why this was deterministic, not flaky. Measured in plain Electron 44.7.0 with the real `render-check.ts` (bundled) against a trivial page: a loop of `invalidate()` + `paint` produced 257,842 synchronous paint events in one second, all at the old 720×800 size. Ruled out: nothing in the render path changed between the nightlies before and after the report (`202611061959..202611071129`), and `render-check.ts` hadn't changed since #6327. CSP/origin/`cors.go`, #7891's `previewUrl` change, edge fades (#7893), and theming don't matter here: a page with no CSP or bootstrap, served by a bare HTTP server, fails the same way. The GPU process was healthy (up since launch). Renders published after 2026-10-17 don't show the check working, because `html_render` doesn't require a passing check server-side. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `html_preview` with `

test

` → `UnknownVizError (RENDER_CHECK_FAILED)`, every call (installed nightly and an isolated dev app on `main`, 2/2) | Returns a 720×49 PNG, `contentHeight: 49`, and console messages (isolated dev app on this branch, 3/3 MCP calls + `ao render --check`) | | Bundled `checkRender` in plain Electron 44.7.0, 4 checks in a row against a trivial page: 4 × `UnknownVizError` | 4/4 pass on the trivial page, 4/4 on a real 425 px-tall daemon-served render page | The screenshot `ao render --check` returned on this branch shows "test" on the theme background (not blank). ## How - `nextPaint()` resolves with the `paint` event's image. Electron documents it as the whole frame, and without `useSharedTexture` it's a bitmap copy. - `capturePainted(window, width, height)` waits for the first frame that `showsWholePage`, sleeping one frame (`MEASURE_POLL_MS`) between tries. The sleep matters: without it, the synchronous re-sends spin the loop on stale frames without ever yielding to the compositor. The loop is capped at `MEASURE_RESIZE_LIMIT_MS` (1 s) and stays inside the existing 20 s check deadline. If no frame reaches the size, the existing "captured WxH, not the WxH page" / "empty image" errors report it. - `capturePage()` is no longer used by the render check. The measure path (`measureRender`) never captured, so it's unchanged. ## Testing - The test fake now models Electron 44 as measured: `invalidate()` re-sends the last frame synchronously, frames can lag the resize, the frame comes in the paint event, and `capturePage()` rejects with `UnknownVizError`. Every passing check in the suite therefore fails if the code goes back to `capturePage()`. - New regression test: a trivial page (18 px) passes without calling `capturePage()`. - New: waits frame by frame past 3 stale frames; fails with the frame's size within ~1 s when no frame reaches the page size; the empty-image test now runs on fake timers. - Manual: isolated dev app (`ao-desktop-dev`, own `AO_DATA_DIR`/profile/run file, port 3012) with a standalone Claude Code chat session, calling the `html_preview` MCP tool over `ao mcp` stdio. Before (main's `render-check.ts`): 2/2 `UnknownVizError`. After: 3/3 pass. - tsgo/vitest not run locally; CI covers them. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(ops): treat secondary install trains as channels of upstream — train-crossing silently wedges existing chats
body:
### Summary

A second AO install train (e.g. a fork packaging its own daemon + hermes build) currently behaves as a *separate install*, not as a *channel* of upstream releases. Both trains share `~/.ao/data`, and upstream's harness binary-identity gate rejects the other train's builds — so simply *updating across trains* wedges every existing chat, with errors that look like corruption but are a topology gap.

### Incident (2026-11-03 → 2026-11-08, macOS, hermes harness)

1. A machine ran the hermes fork's daemon (`setup-self-hosted.sh` rig under `~/.ao/host`, launchd-managed) with a source checkout of the hermes CLI on the `0.23.0+canary` line. Chats created under it pinned launch credentials per the fork adapter's resume protocol.
2. Updating to the upstream nightly (0.14.11, bundled daemon) silently crossed trains. Result A: older chats could not resume — `launch_credentials_unavailable` ("This chat can't use the API key it was started with any more"), because the fork adapter's resume re-supply behavior has no upstream equivalent. Result B (after the Nov 7 nightly): *all* hermes chats failed with `chat driver unavailable … version banner "… v0.23.0+…canary …" is not a Hermes release line AO has qualified; agent: binary identity unknown`, because `qualifiedReleaseLines = {0.21, 0.22}` rejects a 0.23 canary banner and `qualifiedSourceCheckout` demands a clean checkout at a release tag.
3. The only user-visible remedy suggested by the harness (`/new`) discards the affected chats' liveness; nothing indicates the root cause was train-crossing, nor which train a stored session belongs to.

### Root cause

- One data dir (`~/.ao/data`) is shared by trains with incompatible chat/resume protocols and binary-identity rules, while train identity is *implicit* (which binary happened to win port 3001).
- Session rows and chats carry no train/harness-build provenance, so a daemon cannot tell "this chat belongs to a train I can't resume" from "this chat is broken".
- The fork ecosystem (and any patched third-party train) is forced to be a full parallel installer rather than a release channel of upstream, guaranteeing the above on every crossing.

### Proposal

Make a second train a first-class **channel** of upstream instead of a parallel install. Any subset of:

1. **Per-chat train provenance**: stamp sessions/chats with the harness build/train that created them (build id + hermes banner), and surface it in the resume error: "this chat was created by train X; resume it from train X".
2. **Channel-aware qualification**: allow an operator-declared additional qualified train (a signed channel descriptor — repo + release feed + permitted hermes release lines) so a fork release becomes a channel of upstream rather than a divergent install.
3. **Per-train data dirs** (documented + supported, e.g. `AO_DATA_DIR` per install) so crossing trains cannot touch another train's chats, with an explicit one-time migration command between them.

Any one of these would have turned the incident above from a silent fleet-wide wedge into a actionable message.

### Environment

- AO nightly 0.14.11 (2026-11-07), macOS 26; previously fork daemon release train (Oct 26 build).
- hermes source checkout: rejected banner `v0.23.0+canary.20261107T064357Z-73-ga9ff9799e2` → resolved by repinning the checkout to the `v0.22.7` release tag (qualified line {0,22}) and archiving the fork daemon rig.

title: fix(agents): find node for npm Gemini/auth probes; show configured agent while orchestrator starts
body:
Fixes #7917

## Summary
**Gemini "installed" but "Installation check failed" / `auth_check_failed`.** Gemini's binary lookup finds npm/nvm/fnm/volta installs outside the daemon PATH, but `checkVersion` ran `gemini --version` with the daemon's own PATH. When a Dock-launched daemon falls back to the static PATH floor (for example, the 3s login-shell probe times out on a slow `.zshrc`), the `#!/usr/bin/env node` launcher can't find `node`. That failure also fails `AuthStatus`, so the version stays unknown and auth reports `auth_check_failed`.

- `gemini/version.go`: the `--version` probe now uses `agentlaunch.ProcessEnvForLaunchBinary`, as Codex already does (#6370).
- `authprobe/authprobe.go`: `CmdRunner` uses the same environment, which fixes auth probes for every harness using `CLIStatusWithDiagnostics` (Amp, Kilo Code, Command Code, MiMo, Devin, OpenCode). `agentlaunch` imports only the standard library, so there is no import cycle.

**Claude Code icon while the orchestrator starts.** `OrchestratorStartingChat` hardcoded `"claude-code"` in its pending snapshot. The shell and board now pass the project's configured orchestrator agent, falling back to the orchestrator session's provider, and Claude Code only when neither is known.

## Tests
- New: `TestVersionProbeFindsNodeOutsideDaemonPATH` (gemini) and `TestCmdRunnerFindsNodeOutsideDaemonPATH` (authprobe). Each uses a fake `#!/usr/bin/env node` launcher with an nvm-style `node` and an empty daemon PATH.
- Not run locally; relying on PR CI.

## Risks / follow-ups
- No render test for the starting-view icon; CI type-checks it.
- The configured orchestrator agent wins over an older session's provider, which is intended after an agent switch.
- Not covered here: OpenCode `--version` (`opencode/version.go`) and Pi/oh-my-pi hook setup, which have the same pattern according to the issue. Follow-up.
- The root cause is inferred from code and the reported health panel; not reproduced on the reporter's machine.

title: fix(accounts): keep the last Claude usage reading when a refresh is rate limited
body:
Code changes: +25 -3\ Tests: +133 -2\ Others: +0 -0 ## What When Claude's usage read is rate limited, AO keeps showing the last good usage reading and says it could not refresh it, instead of silently replacing it with an empty one. ## Why Partially addresses #7793. Claude Code answers `get_usage` with `subtype: success` and `rate_limits: null` when its own usage request fails (for example HTTP 429). AO treated that as an empty reading and replaced the last good one, so the usage bars disappeared with no explanation. Not covered here, and tracked in #7924: honouring `Retry-After` / the per-login lockout, a cap on how often usage is read and sharing concurrent reads, showing how old a kept reading is (and expiring a window after its reset time), and out-of-order publication of overlapping reads, which predates this change. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | A `rate_limits: null` reply is read as success with no windows and replaces the last good reading, with no error | The previous reading is returned with its original `fetchedAt`, plus `problem: "Claude usage is temporarily unavailable"` | | Session summary, renderer only, same API response (kept reading plus a `problem`):
| Same response:
| The session summary row is a browser build against simulated account responses, so it shows the renderer change only, not the real desktop session path. Both screenshots are in the table above. ## How - `adapters/agentaccount/claude.go`: a null `rate_limits` is returned as `domain.ErrUsageUnavailable` instead of an empty reading. The adapter cannot tell a 429 from an omitted field, so the error is named for what it knows: usage is unavailable. - `service/agentaccounts/service.go`: when a read fails with that error (and no other), the previous reading is carried over only for the same login (matched by email, case-insensitive). The original `fetchedAt` is kept. A different login, a mismatch, or a login with no email never inherits a reading, because it cannot be shown to be the same login. Other limits errors behave as before. - Login confirmation is unchanged in meaning: a login is confirmed only by a real usage reading. A kept reading or an unavailable usage read does not confirm. A confirmation only on a real reading is not new behaviour, but note one consequence: on unfixed `main` a null reply was read as success and did confirm the login; with this change it no longer does, so chats waiting on sign-in stay blocked until a real usage read succeeds. - `SessionAccountSummary.tsx`: renders `account.problem` beside the bars, matching Settings. - Known limit: overlapping reads for one account can still publish out of order (a slower older read can overwrite a newer one). That was already the case before this PR and is tracked in #7924. "A different login discards the old reading" therefore holds for sequential reads. ## Testing - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, gofmt clean. - `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on Go 1.27.1: no findings in the changed files; one existing finding in `service/shellagent/manager.go` (`watchRetryMin`), not touched here. - Backend: `service/agentaccounts`, `service/chat` (race), `adapters/agentaccount` and `httpd/controllers` pass on the final head. On an earlier head, the full main group had the same failures as the unfixed base on my macOS machine (opencode, shellterm, modelcatalog, commandcode, fake); `TestDarwinPTYCloseDoesNotWaitOutAShellThatIgnoresSIGTERM` in `conpty` failed once under full-suite load and passes in isolation and as a package. I have not established why it failed, so I treat it as unexplained. - Frontend: `npm run typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e` and the full vitest suite in 2 shards passed; the frontend code has not changed since. - Real Claude CLI against fake accounts and a local TLS-intercepting proxy that returns HTTP 429, through the real adapter, service and controller: usage kept with the original `fetchedAt` and the warning on 429; warning cleared on recovery; first-refresh 429 shows the warning with no reading; a different login discards the old reading; saved-account mismatch shows nothing stale; a token login without an email does not inherit a reading; a real reading confirms the login and a 429 does not. - New unit tests: null `rate_limits`; same-login keep and different-login discard; no keep after another limits failure; no carry-over without an email; only a real reading confirms the login; session summary warning. - Not run locally: docs, cloud-client and product-ui jobs, the real-Electron boundary jobs, macOS-native jobs, and Windows beyond compile/vet. CI on this head decides those; I will not call them passing until they have run. - Not tested: a real pending sign-in demand where local auth status reports signed in but the provider rejects the credentials, and a real Electron session with a real Claude account. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Feature]: Claude usage reads: per-login 429 backoff, read-rate cap, and age of a kept reading
body:
Follow-up to #7793. #7923 covers the first part: AO keeps the last good Claude usage reading and warns when a usage read is unavailable, instead of replacing it with an empty one. These parts are still open.

## Problem

When Claude's usage read is rate limited, AO can still make the lockout worse and gives little context about the numbers it shows:

1. **No per-login backoff.** AO keeps re-reading a login whose usage is unavailable on its normal 5-minute schedule, and forced refreshes bypass even that. It does not remember a lockout across restarts or processes.
2. **No read-rate cap or coalescing.** Several concurrent `GET /agents/accounts?refresh=true` callers each cause their own usage request for the same account. In a local test with a real Claude CLI and a local proxy, 8 concurrent refreshes made 8 usage requests.
3. **Age of a kept reading is not shown, and old windows are not expired.** `fetchedAt` is in the API, but the UI does not show it. A kept window also keeps showing "% left" after its reset time has passed.
4. **Claude's rate-limit event is only partly used.** The ACP client already reads `_claude/rateLimit` into an `account.rateLimits` event, using the top-level utilization and reset time. It does not preserve the per-window detail (`unifiedWindows`), and that event is not used to update the account usage that Settings shows.
5. **Logins without an email** (token logins) cannot be matched to an earlier reading, so they show the warning with no bars.
6. **Overlapping reads can publish out of order.** `read()` publishes its result unconditionally, so a slower older read for an account can overwrite a newer one (for example after a login change). This predates #7923.

## Proposed direction

Optional. I would split it:

- Item 2: share one read between overlapping callers, for example `singleflight` with `DoChan` so each waiter can cancel on its own. The shared read should run under its own bounded context, recheck freshness and any hold inside it, and reject a result from before a login change. It collapses overlapping work only; sequential forced refreshes still need a rate cap.
- Item 3: show "as of" time next to a kept reading, and hide or label a window as historical once its reset time has passed. Windows without a reset time need a bounded display age.
- Item 1 needs a maintainer decision: where a hold is stored and how long it lasts. Use `Retry-After` when the adapter can obtain it. With only a null reply, call it an "unavailable cooldown", not a confirmed 429 deadline. Apply it to forced refreshes too. In memory is a reasonable first step if restart behaviour is stated; persisting needs a migration.
- Items 4, 5 and 6 are left for later.

## Alternatives considered

Keep #7793 open for the remaining items instead of a separate issue. I opened this one so the finished part (#7923) and the remaining scope are tracked separately; happy to close this and continue in #7793 if that is preferred.

## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar (#7793 is the parent)
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(session): stop session deletes from stalling the daemon writer
body:
> **Explainer:** [One track, one token](https://orchestrator.inc/artifact/gkmkve6euvdfhz7fhag7342wy5) is an interactive walkthrough of this fix. It covers the write lock, cascades, indexes, RESTRICT, a before/after replay of the lock, the alternatives measured on real sessions, and a quiz.

## Problem

A hibernated chat showed "Message delivery wasn't confirmed", then "The agent controller stopped", then "Waking agent…". The cause was the 7-day retention sweep (#7440), which runs at boot and every 10 minutes. It deleted 263 archived sessions back to back. Each delete held the daemon's only writer connection (`writeMu`) for the whole `ON DELETE` cascade, which took 8–35 s per session on the 5.2 GB database. The wake and the message send waited behind that lock and timed out.

Three things made one delete slow or impossible:

1. **Unindexed cascade lookups.** For each deleted turn, SQLite sets `turn_id` to NULL in `conversation_activities` and `conversation_messages`. For each deleted review, it does the same to `review_id` in `conversation_provider_events`. None of those columns had an index, so each lookup was a full table scan. On a real 2 GB copy that was about 90 ms per turn and about 4 s per review.
2. **One huge transaction.** All of a session's provider events and activities (tens of thousands of rows) were deleted inside the transaction that held `writeMu`.
3. **`RESTRICT` self-links.** `conversation_branches.parent_branch_id`, `fork_after_turn_id`, `replaced_turn_id` and `conversation_turns.retry_of_turn_id` are `ON DELETE RESTRICT`. SQLite enforces these row by row, even inside a cascade. As a result, a chat with an edited or retried turn could never be deleted (`FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`). Retention then retried it every 10 minutes, paying the slow cascade each time before rolling back.

## Fix

- **Migration `20261107181854835_session_delete_child_indexes`.** Adds partial indexes on `conversation_activities(turn_id)`, `conversation_messages(turn_id)` and `conversation_provider_events(review_id)`.
- **`DeleteTerminatedSession`.**
  - Before the final transaction, it deletes the session's provider events and activities in batches of 1000. Each batch takes `writeMu` by itself, so writes that are waiting run between batches.
  - Each batch deletes only while the session is still terminated, so a restore that happens mid-delete stops the drain.
  - The final transaction still re-checks "terminated" and "not shared history" before deleting.
  - Inside that transaction it NULLs the branch and retry self-links, limited to the session's own conversations. A link from another conversation still refuses the delete.
- **`TestLineageTurnQueriesAreBoundByConversation`.** It now also accepts a seek on the new `turn_id` index. Production plans do pick that index (see "Query plans that change"). On a real 379-turn chat that plan is faster (16.5 → 1.3 ms). The assertion still rejects a scan.

## Evidence: before (main) vs after (this PR)

**Lab setup.**
- Daemons built from `main` and from this branch, each in a sandboxed data dir. The data is a copy of a real `ao.db` with 159 archived sessions, 921k provider events and 46k activities (2 GB).
- Retention set to 7 days, and every imported session set to expire just after the first sweep tick.
- A real Claude Haiku chat session (`--mode chat`, hibernation on) hibernates before the tick.
- When the sweep starts, the lab:
  - opens that chat, which wakes it;
  - sends "Reply with the single word pong.";
  - pins and unpins another session every 0.5 s as a write probe, measuring how long each write waits for the writer.

| Measurement during the sweep | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Open the hibernated chat (wake) | **43.1 s** | **3.9 s** |
| Send a message: accepted / answered | 10.3 s / 25.5 s | 0.1 s / 3.1 s |
| Probe write wait: median | 8 ms | 7 ms |
| Probe write wait: p90 | 1.85 s | 46 ms |
| Probe write wait: p99 | 13.6 s | 123 ms |
| Probe write wait: max | **23.1 s** | **0.19 s** |
| Probe writes waiting over 1 s / over 5 s | 29 / 7 of 203 | 0 / 0 of 192 |
| Sessions deleted in the pass | 113 | 146 |
| Sweep length | 184 s | 36 s |
| `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` in the pass | 33 | 0 |
| Archived sessions left | 46 | 13 |

The 13 sessions left after the fix share conversation history with another session. The sweep refuses those by design (`ErrSessionHistoryShared`).

The incident database was 5.2 GB, more than twice the lab copy. That is why the before wake here was slow but did not cross the timeout.

No review was deleted in this run. The lab seed sets `review_id` to NULL on the imported provider events, so these numbers don't cover the `review_id` index. The per-review cost without it (about 4 s, under Problem) comes from timing single-session deletes on the same copy.

## Query plans that change

The new indexes also change the plans of 14 of the 49 sqlc queries that read these tables. This happens without `ANALYZE` statistics, so it applies in production. Method: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the 2 GB lab copy, with and without the three indexes.

- 8 queries go from a full table scan to an index search: `AttachLegacyCompactionsToRollbackAnchor`, `FailOrphanedConversationActivities`, `SelectConversationProviderInputContent`, `SelectLatestAutoResumeConversationTurn`, `SelectNextQueuedConversationTurn`, `SelectQueuedConversationBatch`, `SelectReservedConversationTurnForPromotion`, `SelectRetryableConversationPrompt`.
- 6 queries switch from a `conversation_id` index to the `turn_id` index: `FinalizeConversationPlanActivity`, `SelectConversationEditAnchor`, `SelectQueuedConversationMessage`, `SettleRunningConversationActivitiesForTurn`, `SettleStreamingConversationMessagesForTurn`, `UpdateQueuedConversationMessageText`.

Timings on the same copy use the largest conversation (1,645 messages) and its busiest turn. Each is the median of 15–25 warm-cache runs, and writes are rolled back.

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `FailOrphanedConversationActivities` | 50.7 ms | 0.12 ms |
| `SelectNextQueuedConversationTurn` | 12.3 ms | 0.04 ms |
| `SelectConversationProviderInputContent` | 8.1 ms | 0.14 ms |
| `SelectQueuedConversationBatch` | 7.1 ms | 0.03 ms |
| `SettleRunningConversationActivitiesForTurn` | 6.7 ms | 0.39 ms |
| `SettleStreamingConversationMessagesForTurn` | 1.6 ms | 0.06 ms |
| `FinalizeConversationPlanActivity`, turn with 630 activities | 0.54 ms | 0.70 ms |
| `FinalizeConversationPlanActivity`, median turn with a plan (47 activities) | 0.46 ms | 0.43 ms |

The before scans read the whole table, so they grow with the database. `FinalizeConversationPlanActivity` is the one query that can read more rows after the change. It used `(conversation_id, kind)` and now reads all of the turn's activities, which costs 0.16 ms more on the largest real turn.

## Tests

- `TestDeleteTerminatedSessionWithEditedAndRetriedTurns` seeds a branch chain (parent, fork point, replaced turn) and a retried turn. It fails on `main` with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed (1811)` and passes here.
- `TestDeleteTerminatedSessionClearsHistoryInBatches` seeds more than two full batches of provider events and activities, for one archived session and one live session. It checks that the refused live delete leaves the live session's rows intact, and that the archived delete leaves none.

## Risks

- A delete is no longer one transaction. Provider events and activities go in batches first; messages, turns and the session row go in the final transaction. The delete can stop between the two: the request is cancelled, the daemon shuts down, or the final transaction fails. The session then stays archived without some of its provider events and activities. Deleting it again (the next retention pass) finishes the job. If the user restores it instead, the transcript keeps its messages but loses the drained tool activity.
- The migration builds three indexes on existing tables, once, at the first daemon start after upgrade. On the 2 GB lab copy, startup went from 0.5 s to 10.1 s for that one start; a larger database takes longer.

title: Support a per-project worker launch wrapper for Docker Sandboxes
body: In v0.14.10, `worker.agent` is validated as a built-in harness identifier, so it cannot point at an `sbx` wrapper. Please support a host-owned launch wrapper/runtime independently of the selected harness. It should receive structured argv and the session workspace, preserve the selected harness protocol for launch and resume, support explicit environment/credential handling without inheriting developer secrets, and participate in session cancellation and cleanup. This would allow each worker to run in its own Docker Sandbox while the host daemon remains outside it. Is there an existing supported integration point for this, or would you accept a feature proposal?

title: Talk to the Cloud API on api.orchestrator.inc by default
body:
## Why

The Orchestrator Cloud API is moving from `*.aoagents.dev` to `*.orchestrator.inc`, with both names serving the same control plane until released builds age out. The full cut-over plan is `docs/api-hostnames.md` in ao-control-plane. New builds should use the new names so `aoagents.dev` stops appearing anywhere users can see it.

> **Draft: do not merge until `api.orchestrator.inc` and `staging-api.orchestrator.inc` serve** (plan step 1) **and `https://api.orchestrator.inc/app/auth/return` is registered in the WorkOS Staging environment** (step 2). A build from this branch can't reach the cloud before then.

## What changes

- **Daemon** (`backend/internal/config/config.go`): the baked control plane is `https://api.orchestrator.inc`. `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` still overrides it. Nothing the app stores is keyed to the hostname, so no one is signed out.
- **Packaged CSP** (`frontend/vite.renderer.config.ts`): `connect-src` (`wss://`), `frame-src` and `media-src` list both names for production and staging. An override to either keeps cloud terminals and artifact frames working.
- **Sign-in redirect** (`frontend/src/main/cloud-auth.ts`): builds on a non-production WorkOS client return through `https://api.orchestrator.inc/app/auth/return`. Release builds already use `https://orchestrator.inc/app/auth/return/`.
- **Mobile** (`packages/mobile/lib/accountHosts.ts`, `account.ts`): defaults to `https://api.orchestrator.inc`, and signs in through the website's page `https://orchestrator.inc/app/auth/return/`, already registered in WorkOS Production for desktop. That page forwards `code`, `state`, `error` and `error_description` to `ao-app://callback` with `location.replace`, which is what `account.ts` checks.

One desktop release is enough. The control plane never hands clients an absolute API URL, so released builds stay on `api.aoagents.dev` within their own CSP.

## Testing

- `vitest`: `vite.renderer.config.test.ts`, `cloud-auth.test.ts`, `cloud-control-plane-url.test.ts`, mobile `account.test.ts` and `accountHosts.test.ts` pass. `go test ./backend/internal/config/` passes. On Windows, `cloud-auth.test.ts`'s two `resolveCloudAuthDir` path-separator tests fail as on `main`.
- The full mobile suite has 3 failures and 7 `tsc` errors. All are in untouched files (`formSection`, `conversationChrome`, `uitextview-selection-color`, `ChatMarkdown`, `HighlightedCodeText`, `TerminalSessionScreen`), and the same ones appear with this branch's mobile changes reverted.
- **Real desktop app** (`npm run dev`, Windows, scratch `AO_DATA_DIR`):
  - With no override, the daemon reports `cloudControlPlaneUrl: https://api.orchestrator.inc`. The app starts and runs normally while that name doesn't resolve yet.
  - Pointed at a local control plane (`AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18081`) and driven through `window.ao` over CDP: local sign-in works, and `/api/cloud/v1/me` through the main-process proxy returns 200. A renderer asking for `https://api.aoagents.dev` or `https://api.orchestrator.inc` as `baseUrl` is still refused by the pinning guard. Sign-out works.
  - The rendered CSP for both `build` and `serve` lists the four API origins.
- Not testable yet: a packaged sign-in against `api.orchestrator.inc` (no DNS). Sign in on a real iPhone and Android before the mobile store release.

## Companion changes

- OrchestratorInc/ao-landing#132: the website reads from the new names with a fallback. Safe now.
- ao-control-plane: deploy-script overrides, a `/healthz` guard, `host` in the access log, and the plan doc. The patch is waiting on push access.

title: Docs site: add 'Suggest a change', a top navbar, a landing-page logo link, and other reader improvements
body:
## Summary

The docs site (https://docs.orchestrator.inc, built from `frontend/src/docs`) already has search, a table of contents, "Copy Markdown", "Open in" for chat assistants, "View on GitHub", `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt`, a sitemap, code-block copy buttons, previous/next cards and a language picker. What it lacks is a way to report a problem with a page, links back to the rest of the product, and a few things that help readers find their way (screenshots, a real changelog page, a useful 404).

I went through all 48 English pages at desktop and narrow widths. This issue lists three must-have changes and a prioritized set of further improvements. No code has been changed yet.

---

## Must-have

### 1. "Suggest a change" on every page, opening a new GitHub issue

**Today:** each page has a "View on GitHub" button (`src/components/page-actions.tsx`) that opens the `.mdx` source. A reader who spots a wrong command or an outdated screen has no direct way to report it unless they know how to edit MDX and open a PR.

**Wanted:** a "Suggest a change" (or "Report an issue with this page") action on every page that opens a **new GitHub issue** prefilled with the page title and URL, for example:

```
https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/new?title=Docs:+<page title>&labels=documentation,comp/docs-site&body=Page:+<page url>%0A%0AWhat's+wrong+or+missing:%0A
```

- Keep "View on GitHub" (or rename it "Edit this page") for contributors who want to open a PR.
- Put the new action in the page actions row at the top **and** at the bottom of the article, after the content, where readers finish reading.
- Use the existing `documentation` and `comp/docs-site` labels. Optionally add a small `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/docs.yml` ("Docs problem": page URL, what's wrong, suggested fix) and link to it with `template=docs.yml` instead of a free-form body.
- Translated pages (`/ja/`, `/zh-CN/`) should send the URL of the page the reader was on, so we know which language is wrong.

**Files:** `frontend/src/docs/src/components/page-actions.tsx`, `src/components/article-route.tsx` (bottom-of-page placement), `src/lib/llms.ts` (next to `sourceUrl`), `src/lib/constants.ts` (issues URL), locale catalogs under `frontend/src/docs/locales/` for the new label. Optional: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/docs.yml`.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every docs page, in every language, shows "Suggest a change" near the top and at the end of the article.
- [ ] Clicking it opens `github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/new` in a new tab with the title `Docs: <page title>` and the page URL in the body, with the docs labels applied.
- [ ] Title and URL are URL-encoded correctly (test a page whose title contains `&`, `:` or non-Latin text).
- [ ] The label is translated in the locale catalogs.

### 2. A top navbar with Changelog, Download, Discord and GitHub

**Today:** there is no top bar on desktop. The only outbound links are "Main site" and "GitHub", tucked into the top of the left sidebar (`baseOptions().links` in `src/lib/layout.shared.tsx`). There is no way from the docs to download the app, read the product changelog, or join the community. The page footer is empty.

**Wanted:** a persistent top navbar on every docs page with:

| Label | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Changelog | https://orchestrator.inc/changelog |
| Download (primary button) | https://orchestrator.inc/download |
| Discord | https://discord.com/invite/UZv7JjxbwG |
| GitHub | https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator |

- Search stays reachable (keep `Ctrl/⌘ K`).
- At narrow widths the links move into the mobile menu; Download stays visible if space allows.
- Discord and GitHub can be icon buttons with accessible names (`aria-label="Discord"`, `aria-label="GitHub"`).
- Store the URLs in `COMPANY` in `src/lib/constants.ts` so they are defined once.

**Files:** `frontend/src/docs/src/lib/layout.shared.tsx`, `src/lib/constants.ts`, `src/components/docs-layout.tsx` (if the layout variant changes to one with a top bar), `src/styles/tokens.css` / `global.css` for spacing, locale catalogs for "Changelog" and "Download".

**Done when:**
- [ ] On desktop, every page shows a top bar with Changelog, Download, Discord and GitHub, using the URLs above.
- [ ] At 375 px wide, all four links are reachable from the mobile menu, with no horizontal scroll.
- [ ] External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- [ ] The links are no longer duplicated at the top of the sidebar (or the sidebar copy is removed on purpose).

### 3. Top-left logo links to the landing page

**Today:** the logo and "Docs" label in the top-left link to `/` (the docs home), because `nav.url` is set to `homeUrl` in `src/lib/layout.shared.tsx`.

**Wanted:** clicking the **logo** goes to https://orchestrator.inc. The docs home stays one click away, either through the "Docs" label next to the logo or as the first sidebar item ("Introduction", which already exists).

**Files:** `frontend/src/docs/src/lib/layout.shared.tsx` (split the logo and the "Docs" label into two links, or point `nav.url` at `COMPANY.MARKETING_URL` and keep the docs home in the sidebar).

**Done when:**
- [ ] Clicking the logo on any docs page, desktop or mobile header, opens https://orchestrator.inc.
- [ ] The docs home is still reachable in one click.
- [ ] The logo link has an accessible name such as "Orchestrator.inc home".

---

## Suggested improvements

### High

**H1. A site footer.** Every page ends with the previous/next cards and then nothing. Add a simple footer with Product (Download, Changelog, Docs), Community (GitHub, Discord, X), and Legal (Privacy, Terms) columns.
*Why:* readers who reach the end of a page have nowhere to go besides the sidebar; the footer is where people look for community and legal links.
*Done when:* every page shows the footer, links match the landing site, and it stacks into one column at mobile width.

**H2. Screenshots on key pages.** None of the 48 English pages contains an image. Pages like Quickstart, Dashboard, Installation, Guides → Review loop, and Configuration → Remote access describe screens the reader has never seen. The repo already has usable screenshots in `docs/assets/readme/` (dashboard, new task, review, browser preview, session terminal).
*Why:* readers can match what they read to what they see in the app, which matters most during first-time setup.
*Done when:* at least Introduction, Installation, Quickstart, Dashboard and the Review loop guide each have one or more current, light-weight screenshots with alt text, stored under `frontend/src/docs/public/docs/`.

**H3. A short demo video on the Introduction page.** A 30–60 second clip showing a task going from issue to worker to PR.
*Why:* explains the product faster than text, especially for people arriving from search.
*Done when:* the Introduction page embeds a video (poster image, no autoplay with sound, captions), and the page still loads quickly.

**H4. Make the Changelog page useful.** `/changelog/` is 85 words and only links out to GitHub releases. Either show the latest release notes in the docs (a feed or the last few entries), or turn the page into a clear pointer to https://orchestrator.inc/changelog with the latest version number and date.
*Why:* readers on the docs who want to know "what changed" end up at an almost empty page.
*Done when:* the page shows at least the latest release (version, date, highlights) or links prominently to the product changelog, and the top navbar "Changelog" link and this page agree on where release notes live.

**H5. A helpful 404 page.** `src/components/not-found.tsx` renders a plain message pinned to the top-left of an empty screen, with no sidebar, search or navbar.
*Why:* broken links from old blog posts and search results land here; today it's a dead end.
*Done when:* the 404 page uses the normal docs layout (navbar, sidebar), offers search, links to Introduction, Installation and Troubleshooting, and includes a "Report a broken link" action that opens a prefilled GitHub issue (same mechanism as must-have 1).

### Medium

**M1. "Was this page helpful?" feedback.** Yes/No buttons at the end of each article; "No" leads to the same prefilled issue as must-have 1 (or a short text box), "Yes" just says thanks. If we already send docs analytics, record the vote; otherwise the GitHub issue link alone is enough.
*Done when:* every page has the widget, it works without cookies, and it is translated.

**M2. Show "Last updated" on each page.** `src/lib/last-modified.ts` already computes each article's last commit date for the sitemap, but readers never see it. Show it at the end of the article (e.g. "Last updated 3 Nov 2026").
*Why:* tells readers whether a page is likely to match the current app.
*Done when:* every page shows a date that matches the latest git change to its `.mdx` file.

**M3. A Keyboard shortcuts page.** The app has a command palette and several shortcuts, but no docs page lists them. Add `content/keyboard-shortcuts.mdx` under Reference, with macOS and Windows/Linux keys side by side using `<kbd>`.
*Done when:* the page lists every shortcut the app currently registers, and the list is easy to keep in sync (ideally generated from, or checked against, the shortcut definitions).

**M4. An "Open in your editor" page.** The app can open a session's worktree in an external editor (topbar open-editor button), but the docs don't explain it: which editors are detected, how to pick a default, and how to tell several editor windows apart.
*Done when:* a page under Using Orchestrator covers opening a worktree in an editor, choosing the default, and common problems.

**M5. Task-focused recipes.** The Guides section is good but short (7 guides). Add short "do this one thing" recipes, each with a goal, steps, and the result, for example: run two agents on the same task and keep the better result; fix review comments in the background; split a large refactor across several workers; triage a batch of issues overnight; drive workers from the CLI.
*Done when:* at least four recipes exist, each linked from the Guides index.

**M6. Install page tabs per OS.** Installation lists all platforms in one table and then mixes macOS-only notes (package-manager install, "developer cannot be verified") with general steps. Use tabs (macOS / Windows / Linux) for the platform-specific steps and remember the reader's choice. A `docs-tabs` component already exists in `src/components/docs-tabs.tsx`.
*Done when:* Installation and Platforms use OS tabs for platform-specific steps, and the chosen tab persists across pages.

**M7. Light theme.** The theme switch is disabled (`themeSwitch.enabled: false`), so the docs are dark-only.
*Why:* many readers read docs in daylight or print them; dark-only is hard to read for some.
*Done when:* the site follows the OS setting by default, a toggle is available (navbar or sidebar footer), and code blocks, callouts and tables pass contrast in both themes.

**M8. Breadcrumbs on nested pages.** Pages like Built-in capabilities → Workspaces → Git worktrees show only a small section label above the title. Show a clickable breadcrumb trail (Built-in capabilities › Workspaces › Git worktrees).
*Done when:* every page deeper than one level shows clickable breadcrumbs.

### Low

**L1. Privacy & telemetry page.** One page that states what the app collects, how to opt out (the in-app opt-out already exists), and where data is stored (`~/.ao`).

**L2. A Community / Getting help page.** Where to ask questions (Discord, GitHub Discussions/Issues), how to report a bug, how to contribute docs.

**L3. Search result quality.** Searching "worktree" returns long paragraphs instead of short snippets, and some indexed text still says "AO". Trim result snippets to a sentence or two around the match and run the same "AO" → "Orchestrator" display cleanup on search content that the page body already uses.

**L4. Copy link to a heading.** Show a link icon on heading hover that copies the URL with the `#anchor`, so people can share a specific section.

**L5. Video or GIF clips for visual features.** Short muted loops for the browser preview, diff review and multi-session layout, where a still image doesn't show the interaction.

**L6. Settings reference.** One page listing every setting in the desktop app's Settings screen, what it does, and its default, so Configuration pages can link to it.

---

## Notes

- Docs source: `frontend/src/docs` (static export, deployed by `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml` on pushes to `main` that touch `frontend/src/docs/**`).
- Any new UI strings need entries in `frontend/src/docs/locales/*/messages.po` (`scripts/check-translations.mjs` checks this).
- Must-haves 1–3 are small and independent; they could ship as separate PRs.

title: fix(chat): open cloud chat links in the session's Browser tab
body:
Code changes: +12 -1\
Tests: +16 -4\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Links in a cloud session's chat now open in that session's Browser tab, the same way local chat links do. "Open in ao browser" in a link's right-click menu is no longer greyed out in cloud projects.

## Why

`CloudSessionChatSurface` never passed `onLinkOpen` to its chat, so its links fell back to the opener in `_shell.tsx`. That fallback is gated on `kind === "worker"`:

- **Cloud orchestrator chat:** the menu item was disabled, and a plain click opened the system browser.
- **Cloud worker chat:** the item was enabled, but it POSTed the cloud session id to the local daemon's `/sessions/{id}/preview`, which returns 404. The Browser tab opened empty.

## Before / After

Same chat (a cloud project's orchestrator), same link, right-click:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Open in ao browser is greyed out](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/369d303527e836733eed0c77978d959ebb55b03e/before-cloud-link-menu.png) | ![After: Open in ao browser is enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/369d303527e836733eed0c77978d959ebb55b03e/after-cloud-link-menu.png) |

After choosing "Open in ao browser", the issue loads in the session's Browser tab:

![After: the linked issue open in the session Browser tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/369d303527e836733eed0c77978d959ebb55b03e/after-cloud-link-browser.png)

## How

- `SessionView` passes `browserView.openLink` to `CloudSessionChatSurface`, which hands it to the chat through `useSessionBrowserLink`, as `SessionChatSurface` already does for local chats.
- `useSessionBrowserLink` never asks the local daemon about a cloud session. A cloud session's files live in its sandbox, so it opens web links only. Before, a workspace-file link in a cloud chat went to the local daemon and failed. Now it does nothing in the Browser tab. Previewing sandbox files in the Browser is out of scope.
- The `_shell.tsx` fallback is unchanged. Other cloud callers that use it without an opener, such as inspector PR links, now open nothing instead of an empty Browser tab. Wiring them is a separate change.

## Testing

- New `useSessionBrowserLink` test: a cloud session opens a web link through the Browser opener and makes no local daemon request for a workspace file link. It fails without the guard.
- `useSessionBrowserLink.test.tsx`, `AppLink.test.tsx` and `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx` pass (107 tests). `tsgo --noEmit` shows no errors in `frontend/src`.
- Live check in an isolated dev desktop from this branch, signed in to production AO Cloud, on a real cloud project's orchestrator chat. I swapped the three renderer files between this branch and `main` under Vite, and checked the served source before each run:
  - On `main`, the menu item has `aria-disabled="true"`.
  - On this branch, it is enabled. Choosing it opens the issue in the session's Browser tab, in a native view whose URL is the issue. A plain left-click on another issue link opens it as a second tab.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
