title: fix(inspector): hide Create PR once the session's PR is merged
body:
## Summary

After a session's PR is merged, the inspector still offered **Create PR**. Clicking it asks the agent to open a duplicate PR for work that already shipped.

1. `SessionInspector` sets `openPRNumber` only from open or draft PRs, so a merged PR leaves it `undefined`.
2. A squash merge lands as a new commit on `main`. The branch's own commits never become its ancestors, so `rev-list --count main..branch` keeps counting them (4 for #7899).
3. `gitActionPlan` then fell through to `commits > 0` and returned **Create PR**.

Fix: the daemon's branch state now carries `remoteHead`, the commit the remote-tracking branch points at. The inspector hides **Create PR** only when a merged PR's head is that commit. A commit pushed after the merge moves `remoteHead` off the PR head, so the button comes back. Uncommitted or unpushed work offers it as before.

## Before / after

Real dev desktop app built from this branch, with isolated lab data. The lab session is on #7899's actual head branch (`63ebc91189`: 4 commits, pushed, squash-merged as `8bf3684709`) and carries #7899's PR record, copied from the real session that showed the bug. Before serves `origin/main` renderer code in the same window; the capture script checked the source Vite served for each shot. The third shot adds one commit in the lab worktree and moves its `origin/...` tracking ref to it, which is what a push does locally (nothing was pushed to GitHub).

| Before (`main`) | After (this PR) | After, commit pushed after the merge |
|---|---|---|
| ![Before: merged PR #7899 with a Create PR button under 4 pushed commits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3db19b7-3aad-46bf-826f-c214b2bf8834) | ![After: merged PR #7899 with no Create PR button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3bd51bc-fc4a-426b-b219-028cb56ccf14) | ![After: a fifth commit pushed after the merge brings Create PR back](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f123089a-f699-4b57-9718-21504c6b036f) |

DOM and daemon facts for each shot:

| | Create PR buttons | Commits row | `remoteHead` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | `["Create PR"]` | `4 commits` | (not on `main`) |
| After | `[]` | `4 commits` | `63ebc91189` = PR head |
| Pushed after merge | `["Create PR"]` | `5 commits` | `e3b803c720` |

## Tests

- `branch_state_test.go`: branch state reports `RemoteHead` after a push and keeps it while a new commit is unpushed.
- `SessionInspector.test.tsx`: three merged-PR cases. "offers no Create PR once the merged PR has the pushed head" fails on `main`. "offers a new PR for commits pushed after the merge" fails on this PR's first version and passes now. "offers a new PR for work made after the merge" covers uncommitted work.
- Locally: the full `SessionInspector.test.tsx` (180/180) and the Go `session`, `store`, and `apispec` packages pass. `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are regenerated.

title: fix(cloud): reopen a Cloud chat instantly and load its history newest first
body:
## Problem

Reopening a Cloud orchestrator after a few minutes away showed the empty "What do you want to work on?" screen (the new-chat welcome) for several seconds, then the whole conversation popped in.

Measured on production (a teammate's recording plus control-plane logs, orchestrator session `0918f827`):
- The chat's last history poll was at 20:16:51 UTC; it was reopened at 20:25:18, **8.5 min later**.
- The reopen's history read (`chat-events`) took **13 ms** on the server and was a single page.
- The conversation appeared at ~20:25:23, **~4.5 s** later. The welcome screen was shown the whole time.

Two causes in the renderer:
1. **The history cache expired.** `cloud-chat-events` used React Query's default `gcTime` (5 min), so a chat closed for longer than that reopened with no history and read it all again.
2. **"Not loaded yet" looked like "empty".** `CloudSessionChatSurface` built its snapshot from `eventsQuery.data ?? []`, so `ChatWorkspace` greeted the chat as a new one until the read finished.

## Fix

- **Cache for an hour.** `cloud-chat-events` gets `gcTime: CHAT_EVENTS_CACHE_MS` (60 min). Reopened within that, the conversation renders from the first frame. The existing loader already reads only events after the newest cached sequence (`loadCloudChatEvents(..., existing)`), and the stream resumes from there.
- **Unknown history is not an empty chat.** New `historyPending` prop on `ChatWorkspace`, set by the Cloud surface until its first read. It uses the existing arrive-with-history path: composer docked, "Restoring your conversation" with the starting shimmer, and the transcript fades in. The composer stays typeable. A chat whose read comes back empty gets the welcome screen as before. Cloud sessions carry no `lastUserMessageAt`, so this can't be decided earlier.

No new strings.

## Testing

- New tests:
  - `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx`: unread history is pending, not empty; the cache outlives 5 min; a reopen renders the cached conversation on its first frame and reads only `after: <last sequence>`.
  - `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: `historyPending` shows no welcome, docks the composer, keeps it typeable, fades the history in; an empty read still shows the welcome.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean. All chat tests pass (1746) except the two number-formatting tests (context usage, ContextMeter), which fail identically on `main` on this machine.
- **Real app against staging** (dev build, orchestrator `06743eee`), sampled every animation frame:
  - **Cold open** (window reloaded, empty cache): no welcome frame at all. The composer was docked and "starting" from 167 ms, and the history appeared at 417 ms.
  - **Reopen after 5 min 41 s away** (past the old 5 min `gcTime`): the conversation was on screen in the chat's first frame. There was no welcome or loading state in the next 4 s.

## Latest-first loading

The history now loads newest first, so a long chat doesn't read every page from its first event before showing anything. This needs OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#63 for the server side.

- **First open:** the newest page (`before: newest, limit: 150`) renders as soon as it arrives. Then the 30 minutes before it (`before: nextBefore, since: oldest - 30 min`). Anything older loads only on demand, through ChatWorkspace's existing "Load earlier messages" control and scroll-to-top. No new strings.
- **Catch-up reads** (safety poll, invalidation, reopen from cache): `{ after: newest, before: newest, limit: 500 }`. With more than 500 new events, the list starts over at the newest page, as remote chats do (#7789).
- **Window state** lives in `["cloud-chat-history", orgId, sessionId]` (`gcTime: Infinity`), so a cached partial list is never mistaken for the whole history.
- **Partial windows:** `toSnapshot` gets `{ partial }`, so a turn first seen after its prompt reads as started, not queued. `useCloudScriptRuns` reads its own events when the chat list is partial.
- **Compatibility:** against a control plane without #63 (no `hasOlder` in the response), the loader falls back to today's forward paging. Either PR can merge first.
- **Tests:** 19 loader unit tests in `lib/cloud-chat-history.test.ts`, 4 surface tests, and client request-parameter tests.

Full suite on the combined branch: typecheck clean. 67 failures in 6 files (browser-profile-import, remote-proxy, cloud-agent-proxy, browser-cookie-repair, ContextMeter, the ChatWorkspace number-formatting test); the same files fail on `main` on this machine. One more, `telemetry.init.test.ts`, failed only under full-suite load and passes on its own (49/49).

title: feat(docs): docs issue form and "Was this page helpful?"
body:
Part of #7932. Stacked on #7936 (`ao/docs-reader-improvements`, rebased on its latest commit 5b1798af45); GitHub retargets this to `main` when #7936 merges.

## Why

The "Suggest a change" links from #7936 pass `labels=documentation,comp/docs-site` in the URL. GitHub applies that parameter only for people with triage access, so most readers' reports arrive unlabelled. Labels set in an issue form apply for everyone.

## What changed

- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/docs.yml`**: a "Docs problem" issue form with the `documentation` and `comp/docs-site` labels and three fields: **Page URL** (`id: page-url`, required), **What's wrong or missing?** (required) and **Suggested fix** (optional). It appears in the issue chooser next to Bug report and Feature request.
- **`docsIssueUrl()`** (`frontend/src/docs/src/lib/docs-issue.ts`) now opens `issues/new?template=docs.yml&title=Docs: <title>&page-url=<url>`. The `labels` and `body` parameters are gone (an issue form ignores `body`). The page URL still includes the locale, e.g. `/ja/quickstart/`. This covers "Suggest a change" at the end of every article, "No" in the new prompt, and "Report a broken link" on the 404 page.
- **"Was this page helpful?"** (M1 in #7932) at the end of each article, above the existing report and edit links. **No** is a link to the same prefilled issue (it works without JavaScript) and then says "Thanks. Tell us what to fix in the GitHub issue that just opened." **Yes** says "Thanks for letting us know." Nothing is stored or sent, so there are no cookies. The docs site has no analytics, so no votes are recorded.
- All 5 new strings are translated in the 15 non-English catalogs (16 locales in total).
- Tests: `docs-issue.test.tsx` checks the new URL, that `labels` and `body` are gone, encoding of `& : #`, and non-Latin titles. It also reads `docs.yml` and checks that its labels equal `DOCS_ISSUE_LABELS` and its field ids are `page-url, problem, suggestion`, so the form and the link can't drift apart. The new `page-helpful.test.tsx` checks the Yes and No behaviour and that no cookie is set.

title: feat(docs): site footer, "Last updated" dates and full breadcrumbs
body:
Code changes: +255 -1\
Tests: +111 -0\
Others: +459 -0 (locale catalogs, 17 languages)

## What

Three items from #7932:

1. **H1, site footer.** Every docs page, the 404 included, now ends with a footer with three columns, all links taken from orchestrator.inc's footer:
   - **Product:** Download, Changelog, Docs (Docs goes to the docs home in the page's language)
   - **Community:** GitHub, Discord, X
   - **Legal:** Privacy, Refunds & Cancellations, Support & Contact, Apache-2.0 License

   It also shows the logo, linking to orchestrator.inc, and the same © line as the landing site. At mobile width it's one column. External links open in a new tab.
2. **M2, "Last updated".** Each article ends with "Last updated Nov 2, 2026", taken from the git date that `src/lib/last-modified.ts` already gives the sitemap. The date is formatted in the reader's interface language ("Zuletzt aktualisiert am 2. Nov. 2026", "最終更新日: 2026年11月3日") inside a `<time datetime>`.
3. **M8, breadcrumbs.** Pages below the first level show a linked trail ending at the current page: Built-in capabilities › Workspaces › Git worktrees. Each section links to its overview page. Before, only the parent section was shown, styled like the current item. Top-level pages have no trail, and section overview pages show one level (Built-in capabilities › Workspaces). The trail is a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` with the page marked `aria-current="page"`.

The new labels are translated in all 16 interface languages.

## Why

Part of #7932. When readers reached the end of a page, the only things below the previous/next cards were the sidebar and the edge of the page. Readers also couldn't see how current an article was, and on nested pages they couldn't tell or jump to where they were in the tree.

## Before / After

All captures come from local static exports (`npm run build`) at the same widths. Before is this PR's base, `ao/docs-reader-improvements` at 5b1798af45 (#7936, where "Suggest a change" and "Edit this page" are only at the end of the article). After is this branch. The live site doesn't include #7936 yet. A live capture is in the last row.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Git worktrees at 1440 px, breadcrumb shows only Built-in capabilities › Workspaces](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/before-plugins-workspaces-worktree-top-1440.png?v=2) | ![After: Built-in capabilities › Workspaces › Git worktrees, sections linked](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/after-plugins-workspaces-worktree-top-1440.png?v=2) |
| ![Before: Git worktrees at 375 px](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/before-plugins-workspaces-worktree-top-375.png?v=2) | ![After: full trail at 375 px](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/after-plugins-workspaces-worktree-top-375.png?v=2) |
| ![Before: end of Git worktrees at 1440 px, nothing after the previous/next cards](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/before-plugins-workspaces-worktree-bottom-1440.png?v=2) | ![After: Last updated date, then the footer beside the sidebar](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/after-plugins-workspaces-worktree-bottom-1440.png?v=2) |
| ![Before: end of Git worktrees at 375 px](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/before-plugins-workspaces-worktree-bottom-375.png?v=2) | ![After: footer in one column at 375 px](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/after-plugins-workspaces-worktree-bottom-375.png?v=2) |
| ![Before: end of the Japanese intro at 375 px](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/before-ja-bottom-375.png?v=2) | ![After: Japanese footer at 375 px](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/after-ja-bottom-375.png?v=2) |
| ![Before: 404 page](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/before-does-not-exist-bottom-1440.png?v=2) | ![After: 404 page with the footer](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/after-does-not-exist-bottom-1440.png?v=2) |
| ![Before: Adapter development, a page the sidebar doesn't list, with a plain-text Plugins label](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/before-plugins-authoring-top-1440.png?v=2) | ![After: Built-in capabilities › Adapter development, linked and named like the sidebar](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/after-plugins-authoring-top-1440.png?v=2) |
| ![Live docs.orchestrator.inc today, end of Git worktrees](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/somewherelostt/8989c60ddf8d096ad3a5975d4b14d9a1/raw/live-plugins-workspaces-worktree-bottom-1440.png?v=2) | Live site before this PR, for reference |

## How

- **Footer:** `src/components/site-footer.tsx`, rendered by `LocalizedDocsLayout` after the page and by the 404. Its styles live in `global.css` rather than utility classes, because the docs have no PostCSS config and fumadocs' prebuilt CSS has no class for the grid it needs. In the notebook layout it fills the article and table-of-contents columns of a fourth grid row. The sticky sidebar stays beside it. A full-width footer would sit under the sidebar, and auto-placement would put the footer in the empty table-of-contents row above the article. New URLs are in `COMPANY` (`X_URL`, `PRIVACY_URL`, `REFUNDS_URL`, `SUPPORT_URL`, `LICENSE_URL`, `LEGAL_NAME`).
- **No Terms link:** orchestrator.inc has no Terms page (`/terms/` returns 404). Its Legal column is Privacy, Refunds & Cancellations, Support & Contact and the license, so the docs use the same links.
- **Last updated:** it sits between the article and the "Something wrong or missing on this page?" box, so the date is the last line of the article itself. A small client component (`LastUpdated` in `src/components/page-meta.tsx`) gets the ISO date from the server and formats it with Lingui's `i18n.date` in UTC. The prerendered HTML and the hydrated page show the same text, and English pages switch to the saved language like the rest of the interface. I didn't use fumadocs' `PageLastUpdate`: it fills in the date only after hydration, in the browser's locale rather than the interface language, and its "Last updated on" label isn't in our catalogs. The deploy already checks out full history (`fetch-depth: 0`), so dates are per file.
- **Breadcrumbs:** `PageBreadcrumbs` replaces fumadocs' breadcrumb (`breadcrumb={{ enabled: false }}`). It finds the sections from the page URL's parent folders in the sidebar tree, not from the page's position in the tree. Four pages aren't listed in any `meta.json` (`plugins/authoring`, `plugins/notifiers/desktop`, `plugins/notifiers/webhook`, `plugins/terminals/iterm2`). Fumadocs puts those in a fallback tree whose folders have no overview page, so a tree-based trail showed "Plugins › Notifiers" as plain text with names that don't match the sidebar. Folder names are the translated ones the sidebar uses.

## Testing

Run under Node 24 to match CI, from `frontend/src/docs`:

- `npm ci` ✅
- `npm run check:i18n`: re-extract, strict compile, translation check ✅ (0 missing in all 17 catalogs, no diff afterwards. The two `quickstart.*.mdx` "changed since translated" warnings are already on the base branch.)
- `npm test`: 6 files, 20 tests ✅. New `page-meta.test.tsx` covers the trail on a nested page and on a page the sidebar doesn't list, no trail on top-level pages, the localized date with `datetime`, the footer's link columns and new-tab links.
- `npm run build`: static export ✅
- `tsc --noEmit -p .` ✅

I verified it in three passes: the first build, a rebuild after the layout fixes, and a clean `npm ci` followed by the full chain.

- **Every page:** a script parsed all 54 article pages in the export (48 English, 3 `/ja/`, 3 `/zh-CN/`). Each has the footer with 3 / 3 / 4 links and a `<time datetime>` "Last updated" line. Every page two or more levels deep has a breadcrumb with linked sections and an `aria-current` page. **54/54 pass.** The same script against https://docs.orchestrator.inc today: **0/54**. Both 404 variants (`/404/`, `/_not-found/`) have the footer.
- **Dates:** spot-checked against `git log -1` for `index.mdx` (Nov 3), `quickstart.mdx` (Oct 26), `quickstart.zh-CN.mdx` (Oct 23), `plugins/workspaces/worktree.mdx` (Nov 2) and `changelog.mdx` (Oct 9). All match.
- **1440 px:** on `/`, `/quickstart/`, `/ja/`, `/zh-CN/quickstart/`, `/configuration/remote-access/`, `/plugins/workspaces/worktree/`, `/changelog/` and `/cli/` the footer starts at the sidebar's right edge (268 px), 48 px below the article, with 4 columns. `scrollWidth` is 1440.
- **375 px:** on those pages plus `/configuration/`, `/plugins/notifiers/desktop/` and the 404, `scrollWidth` is 375 (no horizontal scroll) and the footer is one column.
- **Breadcrumb click:** "Workspaces" on Git worktrees goes to `/plugins/workspaces/`, which shows Built-in capabilities › Workspaces.
- **Saved language:** with the saved language set to German, an English page shows "Zuletzt aktualisiert am 2. Nov. 2026", "Brotkrümelnavigation", and Produkt / Community / Rechtliches with translated links. No hydration warnings in the console.

Not yet verified: the live site after deploy. This PR is stacked on #7936 (base `ao/docs-reader-improvements`), and `deploy-docs.yml` publishes on merge to `main`. After that I'll re-run the same page script against https://docs.orchestrator.inc.

title: feat(docs): follow the OS theme and add a light theme
body:
Code changes: +121 -36\
Tests: +33 -0\
Others: +272 -0 (locale catalogs, 17 languages)

**Stacked on #7939** (Tailwind through PostCSS). The diff here is against that branch; merge #7939 first, then retarget this to `main`.

## What

M7 from #7932: the docs follow the reader's OS theme and have a light theme.

1. **Follows the OS by default.** `<html>` no longer hard-codes `dark` (docs pages and the 404). The theme provider (next-themes, via fumadocs' `RootProvider`) is on with `defaultTheme: "system"`. Its inline script sets the class before first paint, so there's no flash on load.
2. **Theme switch** in the sidebar footer (desktop) and in the mobile menu header: Light, Dark, Use system theme. The choice is saved in `localStorage` (`theme`). Picking "Use system theme" goes back to following the OS, live. Fumadocs' single-key shortcut (`d`) is off so typing never flips the page.
3. **Light tokens.** `:root` holds light values, and `.dark` keeps today's dark values unchanged. The light lightness steps (background, card, muted, muted text, accent, border, sidebar) follow the desktop app's light theme in `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css`, in the docs' warm hue. Links use the app's light Markdown link colour `#304c83`.
4. **Prose, code, callouts, tables:** the hard-coded `rgb(255 255 255 / …)` in `prose.css` and the code-block frame are now derived from `--foreground`, with new `--link`, `--code-surface` and `--code-border` tokens. Callouts, accordions, cards, steps and tables already use tokens after #7939. GitHub Light's keyword red (`#D73A49`, under 4.5:1 on the code surface) becomes GitHub's darker `#B31D28` in light mode only. Platform status dots use darker green/amber in light mode.
5. **Translations:** the switch's labels ("Light theme", "Dark theme", "Use system theme", "Toggle theme") are in all 16 interface languages, keyed the way fumadocs' switch looks them up.

## Why

Part of #7932 (M7). The docs were dark-only even for readers on a light OS, which is hard to read in bright environments and didn't match the light desktop app.

## Contrast

Measured in the browser, not assumed: a script composites each visible text element's real computed colour over its real background stack and computes the WCAG ratio. Run on Home, Quickstart, Installation, Platforms, FAQ, CLI, Connect Mobile and the 404, in both themes.

| | Lowest ratio found | Where | Failures (< 4.5:1, or < 3:1 for large text) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Light | 5.03:1 | code token (`--name`, GitHub Light blue on the code surface) | 0 |
| Dark | 5.69:1 | code token (`sw_vers`) | 0 |

Muted text (callouts, accordion answers, card descriptions, TOC, sidebar) is ≥ 5.8:1 in light and ≥ 6.7:1 in dark; table cells 6.98:1 / 8.6:1; links 6.4:1+ / 7.1:1+. Before the red fix, light mode had one failure (`<` in `ao send --session <session-id>`, 3.66:1).

## Before / After

Local static export of this branch, captured with macOS set to dark (left) and light (right), no saved choice, so both columns show the default "follow the OS". Dark mode matches #7939 within 0.1 % on every page except the new switch and a 5 px code-scrollbar capture jitter on three long pages.

</details>

## How

- `site-root.tsx`, `global-not-found.tsx`: drop the `dark` class; `suppressHydrationWarning` was already there for next-themes.
- `providers.tsx`: `theme={{ defaultTheme: "system", enableSystem: true, disableTransitionOnChange: true, hotKey: false }}` instead of `{ enabled: false }`.
- `layout.shared.tsx`: `themeSwitch: { enabled: true, mode: "light-dark-system" }`.
- `tokens.css`: light `:root`, dark `.dark`, plus `color-scheme` so form controls and scrollbars match. The brand colours stay theme-independent.
- `prose.css` / `global.css`: `color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) N%, transparent)` with the same percentages as the old whites. One unlayered rule lets the switch fill the sidebar footer row when there are no icon links in it. Without it, fumadocs leaves the switch at the end of an empty bordered box.
- `docs-tabs.tsx`: drop `prose-invert` (our `.prose` variables already decide the colours, and it would be wrong in light mode).
- Shiki already renders both themes (`--shiki-light` / `--shiki-dark`), and fumadocs switches them on `.dark`, so the code highlighting needed no new config.

## Testing

Node 24 (as in `deploy-docs.yml`), from `frontend/src/docs`:

- `npm ci` ✅
- `npm run check:i18n` ✅: 50 messages, 0 missing in all 16 languages (the two `quickstart.*.mdx` "changed since translated" warnings are already on `main`)
- `npm test`: 9 tests ✅. New: `theme-switch.test.tsx` checks the layout enables the 3-way switch, and renders fumadocs' real switch with our translations to assert the buttons are labelled "Light theme", "Dark theme", "Use system theme". Renaming one key makes it fail (checked).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` ✅
- `npm run build` (clean `.next`) ✅
- In the browser on the static export: with the OS set to light the page is light, with no saved value. **Dark theme** → dark, saved, still dark after reload with the OS still light. **Use system theme** → back to light. Switching the OS to dark while on "system" turns the page dark without a reload. The 404 page follows the saved choice too. The static HTML contains next-themes' blocking script and no `class="dark"`.
- Captured every page type twice in light mode: identical (0.00 %).

## Notes for merging

- #7936 (navbar, "Suggest a change") touches the same 17 `.po` catalogs and appends to `global.css`. Whichever PR lands second gets textual conflicts there: keep both sides' rules in `global.css`, take either side's catalogs, then run `npm run i18n:extract` and re-check that both PRs' strings are translated. #7936 also moves to fumadocs' notebook layout, where the theme switch renders in the top navbar; the footer rule here simply won't match there.
- The live site can only be checked after #7939 and this PR merge and `deploy-docs.yml` publishes. Today docs.orchestrator.inc is dark-only and pixel-identical to local `main`.

title: ci: run only the lanes a PR's files can affect, gated by ci-ok
body:
## Summary

One workflow, `ci.yml`, now starts all PR checks. Its `changes` job reads the PR's files, draft state, base and labels from the API and calls only the lanes those files can affect. `ci-ok` passes only when every started lane passes, so it can be the single required check.

| Lane | Starts on |
|---|---|
| `go` | `backend/`, `pricing/`, `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`, root `package*.json` |
| `cli-e2e` | `backend/`, `test/cli/` |
| `frontend` (typecheck, vitest, renderer-smoke, postcondition) | `frontend/` except docs and native, `packages/product-ui`, `packages/shared`, `packages/cloud-client` |
| `docs` | `frontend/src/docs/` |
| `boundary` (real-Electron origin tests) | everything `frontend` starts on, plus `backend/internal/httpd/` |
| `cloud` / `product-ui` / `mobile` | their packages (`mobile` also on `packages/shared`) |
| `mac-native` | `frontend/native/`, the helper build scripts, `frontend/assets/dmg/`, `ci:macos` or `ci:full` |
| `config` | `.github/`, `scripts/` |

A change to a workflow or to the lane rules starts every Linux lane. A push to `main` and `ci:full` run every lane in full, with Windows and macOS.

### What changes

- Go, Frontend, CLI E2E and Mobile become called workflows. Their path filters, draft/stacked guards and inner gates (`build-test`, `test`) move into the picker and `ci-ok`.
- **No more `edited` trigger.** A body edit cancelled the real run (212 of 461 edit repeats in 2 days did this) and left skipped rows that read as a pass. `ci-retarget.yml` re-runs the PR's CI run when a stacked PR moves to `main`.
- **`checks` is split** into `docs`, `boundary`, `postcondition`, `cloud` and `product-ui`, each on its own paths. `packages/shared` now starts frontend and mobile; httpd starts the Electron boundary; the macOS helpers start on their paths; `config` runs `create-migration.test.mjs`, which had no job.
- **CLI E2E** runs only the Linux matrix entry on PRs without `ci:full`, so no macOS or Windows runner starts to skip its steps (518 such jobs in 2 days). `AO_INSTALLER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` lets `TestE2E_SecondDaemonOnSameDataDir` shorten the installer drain it waits for (305 s to 22 s locally).
- **vitest on PRs** runs the tests related to the changed frontend files plus 25 tests that read files from disk (`frontend/scripts/ci-vitest-always-run.txt`). Global files (package files, vite/vitest/tsconfig, `src/renderer/test/`, `frontend/scripts/`, `packages/`) run all. In a replay of 144 real vitest failures, this missed 3, all fixed by the always-run list.
- Playwright retries a failed test once in CI and reports it as flaky; vitest hides the console output of passing tests (the #7829 vitest log was 9.5 MB).

### Measured before this PR (2026-11-04/05, every PR job)

- The repo is public on the free plan: the limit is 20 concurrent jobs (5 macOS), reached for ~8 h a day. Commit to all checks: p50 20.6 min, p90 58.2 min.
- 28% of runner time re-ran an already-seen commit because of `edited`.
- #7829 (8 renderer files) used 20 runner minutes; with lanes it starts only `frontend` with 8 related files.

## Proof

This PR's own run starts every lane, because it edits workflows: 23 jobs, 94.1 runner min, `ci-ok` green ([run](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42422636041)).

Scenario PRs ran in [illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pulls?q=is%3Apr), a copy of this branch's tree with `ci-ok` required on its `main`:

| Scenario | Lanes picked | Jobs | Runner min | `ci-ok` | Merge state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [#1](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pull/1) README only | none | 2 | 0.2 | pass | CLEAN |
| #1 + `ci:macos` label, re-run | mac-native | 4 | 6.1 | pass | |
| [#2](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pull/2) renderer hook | frontend; vitest ran 32 related files of 347 | 6 | 9.3 | pass | CLEAN |
| #2 body edited while CI ran | no CI run; the running run finished | | | | |
| [#3](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pull/3) planted failing test | frontend | 6 | 7.7 | **fail** | BLOCKED |
| [#4](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pull/4) `packages/shared` | frontend + mobile; vitest ran all 347 | 7 | 18.6 | pass | CLEAN |
| [#5](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pull/5) httpd | go, cli-e2e (Linux only), boundary | 13 | 68.5 | pass | CLEAN |
| #5 earlier push with an unformatted Go edit | same | 13 | 60.6 | **fail** (gofmt, lint) | |
| [#6](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pull/6) draft | none | 2 | 0.2 | pass | |
| #6 marked ready | frontend | 6 | 7.7 | pass | CLEAN |
| [#8](https://github.com/illegalcall/ao-ci-lanes-proof/pull/8) stacked on #7 | none | 2 | 0.1 | pass | |
| #8 retargeted to `main` | `CI retarget` re-ran it: frontend | 6 | 10.8 | pass | CLEAN |
| Push to `main` | every lane, with Windows and macOS | 28 | 105.0 | pass | |

Before and after, by the same sum of job durations:

| PR shape | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Renderer change (#7829, proof #2) | 7 jobs, 19.3 min; vitest 9.6 min | 8 jobs, ~11 min (6 jobs, 9.3 min in the proof run, plus boundary 0.8 and postcondition 0.9 added in review); vitest 2.4 min |
| Backend change (#7928, proof #5) | 13 jobs, 71.4 min, with a macOS and a Windows runner | 13 jobs, 68.5 min, no macOS or Windows runner |

The proof repo's `main` leaves out the release, deploy and other unrelated workflows so they cannot fire there. It keeps `build-artifacts.yml` (dispatch-only) because a vitest test reads it. Two runs failed before that file was restored: the first push run and the first #4 run. Those failures and the first #5 failure came from the proof setup and were fixed there. They are not lane bugs.

### Expected effect

Queue model: the 2,975 real runs of 2026-11-04/05 replayed through 20 runner slots. The model reads low against the observed wait times, so use the ratios.

| | Runner min/day | Wait for all checks, p50 / p90 / mean |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 15,154 | 17.1 / 35.3 / 27.7 min |
| This PR | 10,374 | 13.9 / 22.5 / 13.5 min |
| This PR + #7533 | 5,886 | 4.1 / 7.9 / 5.4 min |

Most of this PR's saving comes from the removed edit re-runs and the CLI fix, which free the queue. The path lanes only stop checks that the changed files cannot reach. A per-file check of every tracked path against the old filters finds no lost check that depends on the file.

## Not in this PR

- Making `ci-ok` the required check on `main` is a repository setting. Add it after this merges; before that the check does not exist on other PRs.
- #7533 (race-free modernc SQLite, Go 71 to 13 runner min per run) is separate. Whichever merges second rebases `go.yml`.

## Risks

- Related vitest selection can miss a test whose dependency is not an import. Pushes to `main` still run everything, and `ci:full` forces a full run on a PR.
- The `checks` split changes which install each step sees; this PR's own run (every lane, since it edits workflows) exercises all of them.

title: fix(mobile): stop Android crashing when a machine edit is saved
body: Code changes: +9 -2\ Tests: +8 -1\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Saving a machine's edit page on Android (**Settings → machine → Edit → Save**) no longer kills the app. Before, the save landed but the screen went black and stayed that way until the app was force-closed. This happened for any saved change, name or icon. ## Why Reported from 2.3.0 on Android: renaming a remote machine in Settings crashes the app to an unrecoverable black screen. The release code is unchanged on `main`, and it crashed in 4 of 5 saves on an emulator. ``` IllegalStateException: ScreenStackFragment added into a non-stack container at com.swmansion.rnscreens.ScreenStackFragment.canNavigateBack(ScreenStackFragment.kt:503) at com.swmansion.rnscreens.ScreenStackHeaderConfig.onUpdate(ScreenStackHeaderConfig.kt:282) ``` React then tears down its instance (`reactInstance is null. Dropping work.`), which is the black screen in release builds. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Save crashes the app (debug redbox shown; black screen in release) | Save lands and returns to the machine page, titled with the new name | ## How The edit page blocks leaving while there are unsaved changes (`usePreventRemove`). After a successful save it released that block (`holding = !saved && …`) and called `backOr()` in the same effect pass, so the release and the pop landed in **one commit**. expo-router's native stack derives a header prop from the block (`headerBackButtonMenuEnabled: !isRemovePrevented`). That commit therefore removed the edit screen from its stack **and** updated its header config. On Android, rn-screens' `ScreenStackHeaderConfig.onUpdate` calls `canNavigateBack()`, which fails its `container is ScreenStack` check on the detached screen. iOS has no such check, which is why only Android crashed. Discard never crashed, because it leaves *through* the block (`navigation.dispatch(data.action)` while still held). A landed save now does the same thing: `holding` no longer depends on `saved`, and the prevent-remove callback dispatches the blocked action straight away once `saved` is set, without asking. Nothing about the header changes in the commit that pops the page. JS-only, so it can ship to 2.3.0 as an OTA. ## Testing - Reproduced on an Android emulator (API 35, debug build of `main`) paired with a scratch daemon, renaming the machine and tapping Save: - before: 4 of 5 saves crashed with the error above - after: 0 of 8 crashed; each rename persisted and the app returned to the machine page - Back on a dirty form still asks "Discard changes?", and Discard leaves without a crash - Each A/B run checked that the device's downloaded dev bundle contained (or lacked) the change. - Added a native log in `ScreenStackHeaderConfig.onUpdate`, used for diagnosis only and not part of this PR. It showed the edit screen's header updating with `container=null` right before the throw. - `lib/machine-edit-screen.test.tsx` used to assert the hold was released after a save. It now asserts the hold stays on and the blocked removal goes through without the Discard prompt. It fails on the old code and passes with the fix. - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 360 files, 3489 tests pass. `npm run typecheck` is clean. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: bug(chat): a question pending across a daemon restart leaves the session stuck for good
body:
### Report

If the AO daemon restarts while an agent is waiting on a question, the session gets stuck for good. A crash, an update, or a plain `ao stop` and start all do it. The chat host survives the restart and replays the pending question. AO tries to store it a second time, the database refuses the duplicate, and the whole session projection stops.

The app then shows "The agent controller stopped". The question card is still visible, but it can't be answered, and the turn stays "Working". **Resume agent** doesn't recover it: the banner goes away and the card looks normal again, but the replay fails the same way, and the composer says "the agent controller for this session is not running".

### What happens

On `main` at `8bf3684709`, with real OpenCode 2.2.5 (`opencode-v2`) and a scripted model that calls the `question` tool with the input from #7658:

1. Start a Chat session and let the agent ask the question. The card renders and can be answered.
2. Restart the daemon while the question is pending.
3. Wait, then open the session.

| Restart | Controller after 60 s | Daemon log | Answer the question | Agent continues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Daemon killed (`SIGKILL`) | `stopped` | `persistent chat projection stopped; provider retained for replay … insert activity: constraint failed: UNIQUE constraint failed: conversation_activities.conversation_id, conversation_activities.request_id` | `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY` | No |
| `ao stop`, then start | `stopped` | Same error | `409` | No |
| Daemon killed, then **Resume agent** in the desktop app | `stopped` | The same error a second time | `409` | No |

The first two rows ran through the daemon API, the third in the real desktop app. The database still has exactly one row for the request (`user_input`, `pending`, linked to the running turn), so nothing is lost; the replay just can't be stored. The desktop app shows the same thing on the build from #7658 (`25bc9b148f76`).

To confirm the cause, I built `main` with one change: `UpsertActivity` skips the insert when the conversation already has a row with that `request_id`. With it, the same hard restart reconnects within 5 seconds, the answer returns `204`, the turn completes, and the agent replies.

I only tested `opencode-v2`. From the code, any chat host that survives a restart and replays a pending question would hit the same path.

### Cause

`UpsertActivity` in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/conversation_store.go` only recognises an existing row by `ProviderItemID`. An approval normally carries one, so its replay updates the row. A question (`input.requested`) carries only a `RequestID`, so its replay goes to `InsertConversationActivity` and hits the unique index on `conversation_activities (conversation_id, request_id)`.

The controller treats that insert error as fatal: it stops the projection and keeps the provider for a replay. Every reconnect, including Resume agent, replays the same request and fails again, so the session can't recover.

### Expected

A replayed question that AO has already stored should match the existing row, so the session reconnects and the question can be answered after a restart.

Possibly related: #7658 reports a `question` from `opencode-v2` that hangs in "Working". The reporter saw no card at all, which I couldn't reproduce, so I can't say it's the same bug. #7919 doesn't change this path.

title: fix: follow GitHub repo renames for project avatars
body:
## Problem

The agent-orchestrator project showed GitHub's grey placeholder Octocat in the sidebar. Its origin is still `https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git`, but the org was renamed to OrchestratorInc. The old login no longer exists, and `avatars.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai` answers with the placeholder and HTTP 200, so the sidebar cached it as a real avatar. The same stale owner also breaks `ao session claim-pr`; that fix is split into #7951, stacked on this PR.

While testing I found a second cause: the login-based avatar URL currently returns the placeholder for most **live** orgs too (vercel, microsoft, facebook, anthropics, cli). The id-based URL (`/u/<id>`) is correct for all of them.

## Fix

- **Daemon:** for `github.com` origins only, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` resolves the repository. It follows renames and transfers and uses AO's existing GitHub auth. `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}` now returns `canonicalRepo` (current owner/name) and `canonicalOwnerAvatarUrl` (GitHub's id-based owner avatar; only `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com` URLs pass).
  - Results are cached in memory: 12h on success, 10 min on failure. A failed refresh keeps the last good answer (only a 404 replaces it), so the avatar doesn't flip back to the placeholder when offline. Concurrent lookups for the same repo share one request.
  - A project read waits at most 2s. A slower lookup keeps running in the background and fills the cache.
  - The daemon warms the cache in the background at startup, so the first read is already resolved. Startup does not wait for it.
- **Renderer:** the sidebar and New Task avatars use the canonical owner and the id-based URL when present, and fall back to the remote's owner otherwise. The avatar cache is keyed by URL, so a new owner gets a new key and the cached placeholder is no longer used.
- **Not changed:** the user's git remote is never rewritten. Self-hosted, GitLab, Bitbucket and other non-`github.com` remotes are never sent to GitHub. GitHub Enterprise hosts are not looked up.

## Screenshots

Real desktop dev app, isolated data. Two lab projects: one with origin `https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git`, and a control with origin `https://github.com/vercel/next.js.git`.

| Before (main) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/68f9797650c8c646708de20a0e354773/raw/before-crop.png) | ![after](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/68f9797650c8c646708de20a0e354773/raw/after-crop.png) |

Full windows: [before](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/68f9797650c8c646708de20a0e354773/raw/before.png), [after](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/68f9797650c8c646708de20a0e354773/raw/after.png).

## How to test

1. `mkdir /tmp/lab && cd /tmp/lab && git init && git commit --allow-empty -m init && git remote add origin https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git`
2. Run the desktop dev app from this branch on isolated data, signed in to `gh`.
3. Add `/tmp/lab` as a project.
4. The sidebar shows the OrchestratorInc avatar. `curl localhost:<port>/api/v1/projects/lab` returns `canonicalRepo: OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`.
5. Add a project whose origin is on a self-hosted host. It gets no avatar and no GitHub request.

## Tests

- `repo_resolver_test.go`: rename via a 301 redirect, unchanged repo, API failure (cached briefly, then retried), 404, a caller deadline that doesn't cancel the shared lookup, last good answer kept on a transient failure, off-host avatar dropped.
- `canonical_repo_test.go`: `canonicalRepo` for renamed, SSH, unchanged, API failure (falls back to empty), and non-GitHub hosts (no lookup). The warm-up looks up only `github.com` origins.
- `repository-avatar.test.ts`: canonical owner, id-based URL, off-host URL rejected, non-github.com remotes ignore canonical data.

I didn't run the test suites locally; CI runs them. `go build`, `go vet` and the API regeneration ran clean.

## Risks / follow-ups

- On the very first launch after upgrading, if the warm-up hasn't finished, the sidebar can show the old cached placeholder for a moment. It switches once project details refetch.
- Workspace child repositories still use their own remote owner. Only the root origin is resolved.

title: fix(settings): size the QR canvas height as well as its width
body: Code changes: +4 -1\ Tests: +39 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The pairing QR in Settings › Mobile draws correctly at 125% display scaling. Before this change it was stretched twice as tall with its bottom half cut off, and phones couldn't scan it. ## Why A new `` starts out 300×150. `QrCanvas` resized its backing store only when `canvas.width !== Math.round(size * devicePixelRatio)`. The pairing code is 240 px, so at a device pixel ratio of 1.25 it needs exactly 300 device px. That meant the width already matched, the resize was skipped, and the height stayed at 150. The code was then drawn for a 300×300 square into a 300×150 canvas, which CSS displays as 240×240. 125% is the usual Windows laptop default, so this hit Windows users on 0.14.7 through current `main`. It came in with #6699. ## Before / After Settings › Mobile in the dev Electron app, launched with `--force-device-scale-factor=1.25`: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Backing store 300×150: stretched 2× tall, bottom-left finder and lower half missing, logo on the bottom edge. `BarcodeDetector` finds no code. | Backing store 300×300. `BarcodeDetector` decodes it to its exact `aomobile://` pairing value. | ## How The resize check now compares the height as well as the width. Other device pixel ratios already worked because a different width forced both sides to be set. The App Store codes (140 px) would only hit this at about 2.14×, but the same check covers them. ## Testing - New `QrCanvas.test.tsx` checks that the backing store is square at 1×, 1.25×, 1.5× and 2×. Before the fix the 1.25× case failed with `{ width: 300, height: 150 }`. - Ran `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, and the full `npx vitest run` (694 files pass) in `frontend/`. - Manual check: ran the dev Electron app on scratch data at `--force-device-scale-factor=1.25` with Connect mobile on. Before the fix both pairing canvases were 300×150; after it they were 300×300, and the live pairing canvas decoded to its `data-qr-value` with `BarcodeDetector`. The scratch daemon behind these screenshots has been stopped and its data deleted, so the pairing code shown no longer works. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(mobile): build the Android worker-row menu only while it is open
body:
Code changes: +31 -7\
Tests: +48 -6\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On Android, a worker row's long-press menu (the Compose `MenuView` with every action in it) is now built when the long press lands and torn down after it closes, instead of sitting under every row of the Workers board.

## Why

Feedback was that scrolling on Android should be a lot smoother. Profiling a release build on a Pixel 10a (`simpleperf`, scrolling a long chat) found this:

- On Android, React Native pushes the ScrollView's offset into Fabric state on **every scroll frame**: 120 times a second on this panel (`ReactScrollViewHelper.updateStateOnScrollChanged`). Each push is a commit, and each commit runs Yoga layout plus pixel-grid rounding over **the whole mounted tree**. Yoga's `roundLayoutResultsToPixelGrid` walks every node unconditionally.
- These commits were **62% of the JS thread** while scrolling a chat. `layoutTree` was 48%, and `fmod` (the rounding) alone was 20%.
- The tree under an open chat was **1,607 Yoga nodes**. **1,141 (71%)** were the Workers board, which stays mounted underneath the chat. Each board row was 49 nodes, about 27 of them the always-mounted context menu and its items.

The chat itself was only 118 nodes. Nearly all of the per-frame work while scrolling *any* screen was the board's unopened menus. React Native has no way to switch off the per-frame state push, so the app has to keep the mounted tree small.

## Before / After

Release builds of `main` vs this branch, same scratch daemon data (31 workers, a 4-turn long-markdown chat), scripted flings. Pixel numbers are averaged over 5–6 runs per side; emulator (60Hz) over 3.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Yoga nodes mounted under an open chat: **1,607** | **986** (−39%) |
| Yoga nodes per board row: **49** | **22** |
| Pixel 10a (120Hz, 8.3ms budget), board scroll: p90 frame **11ms**, p99 **~20ms**, 0.85% janky | p90 **9ms**, p99 **~13ms**, 0.62% janky |
| Pixel 10a, chat scroll: JS thread **~5.0s** per run | **~4.2s** (−16%) |
| Emulator (60Hz), JS per run: board **253ms**, chat **517ms** | board **210ms**, chat **433ms** |

The menu itself looks and behaves the same: it opens under the finger, and its actions, dismiss and re-open all work.

## How

- `WorkerRowContextMenu` (Android) keeps the menu anchor as state that is `null` while closed, and renders `MenuView` only when it is set.
- A long press sets the anchor under the finger. An effect then calls `show()` on the next frame, once the menu has mounted at that point.
- `onCloseMenu` (Compose dismiss, or an action chosen) schedules teardown after 400ms, so Compose's exit animation isn't cut off. A long press during that window cancels the teardown and moves the anchor.
- Out of scope: iOS (SwiftUI menu) is untouched. `PRCard` and `MessageContextMenu` also keep a `MenuView` mounted per row, but they wrap the row *inside* the menu, so lazy mounting them changes how the row is hosted. They're worth a follow-up, since a visited Pull Requests tab adds to the same per-frame cost.
- The board's FlatList window (`windowSize: 7`) was already capped on `main`; the profile showed nothing else on the board worth changing.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 360 files, 3,492 tests pass.
- New/updated tests in `worker-rename-context-menu.android.test.tsx`:
  - no menu is mounted at rest;
  - a long press mounts it at the finger and shows it on the next frame;
  - it is removed after it closes;
  - a menu reopened while the previous one is closing survives.
- On the emulator (release build): long-press opens the menu at the finger, **Pin** moves the row into Pinned, and dismiss then a second long press opens a fresh menu.
- Profiling and A/B: release APKs installed side by side as `aoagents.dev.perf`, `dumpsys gfxinfo` frame stats, per-thread CPU from `/proc`, and `simpleperf` call graphs on the JS thread.

title: fix(claim-pr): accept PRs on a renamed or transferred GitHub origin
body:
Stacked on #7947 (uses its GitHub repo resolver). Split out of #7947 to keep the trust-boundary change reviewable on its own.

## Problem

A project whose origin still uses a renamed GitHub org (`https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git`) rejects `ao session claim-pr` for PRs on the renamed repo (`OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`) with `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`, unless the old URL is passed.

## Fix

When the PR's owner/name differs from a `github.com` origin, claim-pr asks GitHub (through #7947's cached resolver) to resolve both. It accepts the PR only if both resolve to the **same repository id**. Lookup failures, other hosts, GitHub Enterprise PR URLs, and different ids keep `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`. The existing rules in `repository_identity.go` are unchanged, and an exact origin match needs no lookup.

This grants no trust beyond the origin: git already reaches that same repository through GitHub's redirect from the origin URL. If someone later registers the old name, the origin resolves to their repository id, so PRs on the renamed repository stop matching.

## Tests

`claim_renamed_repo_test.go`: same id accepted (HTTPS and SSH origins). Rejected: different id under the same new owner, unknown PR repository, lookup failure. No lookup for an exact origin match, a non-GitHub origin, or a GHE PR. I didn't run them locally; CI runs them.

title: fix(chat): show the working state while Claude runs a cycle on its own
body:
Code changes: +137 -22\
Tests: +171 -5\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A sidebar row now shows the working spinner while a Claude Code chat agent works on its own after a turn, even when the session has a PR open. Before, the row showed only the green PR icon.

## Why

Reported by Aditi: an agent was visibly working (tool calls streaming, composer spinner) on a session with an open PR, but its sidebar row showed just the green PR icon.

The sidebar precedence was already right (working beats PR state). The working signal was wrong. Claude Code starts cycles without an ACP prompt, for example to answer a background task that finished after the agent said "I'll wait for it". AO had no turn for those cycles, so the session's `activity` stayed `idle` and its status fell through to the PR state (`Mergeable`). This affected every surface that reads activity: sidebar rows, the board card loader, and the tab label ("· Idle").

## Before / After

Same dev app, isolated data. Each session has an open, mergeable PR. The open session ran a background job, ended its turn, then Claude resumed on its own to run a foreground job.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: agent working on its own, row shows only the green PR icon](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/b8bd92b6a6e3e4f7fa03d9073c0b4d93/raw/before.png) | ![After: same situation, row shows the working spinner](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/b8bd92b6a6e3e4f7fa03d9073c0b4d93/raw/after-working.png) |
| Daemon reports `activity: idle`, `status: mergeable` for the whole 33 s cycle | Daemon reports `activity: active`, `status: working` from the moment the cycle starts |
| — | ![After: cycle finished, every row shows the green PR icon again](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/b8bd92b6a6e3e4f7fa03d9073c0b4d93/raw/after-idle.png) |

## How

- **Claude session meta** (`claudeacp/driver.go`): sessions ask claude-agent-acp for the SDK's `session_state_changed` messages through its existing `_meta.claudeCode.emitRawSDKMessages` filter. No bridge patch.
- **ACP driver** (`acp/client.go`): `_claude/sdkMessage` notifications with `running`/`idle` become a new `provider.state` chat event. `requires_action` is ignored because approval and input events already report it. Messages for other sessions or during history load are dropped. The host's persistent event id is kept so replays dedupe.
- **Chat controller**: `provider.state` reports `active`/`idle` only when AO has no turn in flight (pending, dispatching, or compacting). During AO's own turns the turn events stay the only source, because an SDK idle can lag behind the next turn's start. Idle is skipped while an approval or question is pending.
- Codex's `thread.state` stays out of activity, as before. This is a separate, Claude-only event.
- **Sidebar**: the precedence moves into `getSessionRowIndicator` in `lib/session-presentation.ts` (working, then needs-input/CI/review, then PR state). Project, Scratchpad, pinned and remote rows all go through `SessionRow`, so they share it. The hover card keeps the PR status and detail while the row spins, so no extra badge was added.

Known limit: a Claude chat already attached to a running persistent host keeps its old session meta until that host restarts (agent restart, app update), so the fix takes effect for new or restarted chats.

## Testing

- Reproduced the bug and verified the fix in the real desktop app (`ao-desktop-dev`, isolated data, fish shell) with Claude Code chats and an open PR row: the before/after captures above, plus API polling of `activity`/`status` through each cycle.
- New tests: `getSessionRowIndicator` (working + PR open shows working, idle + PR open shows the PR icon, needs-input and provisioning/terminated cases), controller tests for `provider.state` inside and outside AO turns, an ACP driver test for `_claude/sdkMessage` parsing, and a Claude session-meta test.
- Locally: `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the touched packages. Go and frontend test suites and typecheck run in CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording

title: feat(harness): show remote hosts' harness updates in the update notice
body:
## Summary

The startup harness update notice only asked this computer's daemon, so harness updates on a connected remote host never surfaced. A user who works mostly on a remote saw updates only for their laptop. Each remote's daemon already checks and installs its own harnesses (and **Settings → Agent Harnesses** can already update them with the remote selected); nothing told the user an update was waiting.

The notice now spans this computer and every connected remote:

- **One notice, all hosts.** Readiness, installers, auth plans, install jobs and advisories are fetched per host (`[local, ...useConnectedHosts()]`) with `useQueries`. All per-harness state (starting, settling, errors, finished jobs, "updated" cards) is keyed by host + harness, so the same harness on two hosts never shares state.
- **Host tags and grouping.** A remote card carries its host's name, using the sidebar's existing host badge. A collapsed stack spanning hosts reads "N machines"; expanded, its rows sit under a heading per host ("This computer", then each remote). A stack whose updates all come from one remote is tagged with that host. Local-only notices look exactly as before.
- **Actions run on the card's host.** Update, Update all, Login, View details and Show diagnostics target that host. The Settings buttons pass `hostId`, so the Harness page opens with that remote selected.
- **Per-host dismissal.** `harnessUpdateNoticeKey` already included the host; the notice now passes it.
- **Hosts are independent.** Each host joins once its own checks are in, so an offline, failing or slow remote never holds back (or reorders) this computer's updates. Disconnected and incompatible hosts aren't in the connected list, so they're skipped.

### Hook changes (additive; existing callers unchanged)

- `useAgentReadinessQuery.ts`: `agentReadinessQueryOptionsForHost()`, plus `useEnsuredReadinessHosts()`, a multi-host version of the ensure gate. It runs one check per host, so a remote connecting or leaving never reopens another host's gate.
- `useAgentAuth.ts`: `agentAuthPlansQueryOptions()`.
- `useHarnessUpdates.ts`: `useHarnessUpdatesOnHosts()` (`useHarnessUpdates` delegates to it) and `useStartHarnessUpdateOnHost()` (`useStartHarnessUpdate` delegates to it).

### Strings

New keys in all 9 locales: `settings.harness.agentOnHost` and `settings.harness.updateHostCount_*` (with `_many` for es/fr/pt-BR and `_few`/`_many` for ru).

## Tests

**Not run locally.** The author's workstation is Windows, where we don't run the suites, so CI is the first run (including type-check).

- `HarnessUpdateNotice.test.tsx`: a new "harness updates on remote hosts" suite, with a fake connected remote mocked via `lib/host-clients`:
  - a remote update shows tagged with its host;
  - Update installs on the remote, never locally;
  - a stack spanning hosts groups rows under host headings and says "2 machines";
  - dismissing on one host keeps the same release on the other;
  - a remote whose checks fail is left out while the local update shows;
  - Show diagnostics on a remote failure opens Settings with `hostId` set.
- `useAgentReadinessQuery.test.tsx`: `useEnsuredReadinessHosts`. It checks each host once, a joining host doesn't reopen another's gate, a host that leaves is dropped and re-checked when it returns, a failing remote doesn't block local, and a previous enabled period can't complete a newer check.
- Existing notice tests are untouched; local query keys and dismissal keys are unchanged.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Not yet exercised against a live remote; worth one manual check with a paired VM.
- The jobs-completion effect now runs after every render instead of on `jobs.data` changes. It's idempotent (a job is acted on once, when it stops running), but it's a behavioural detail worth a reviewer's eye.
- Out of scope: updating the AO daemon itself on a remote, and a remote-only (no local daemon) mode. Both are follow-ups.

title: feat(chat): show MCP tool calls in plain words
body:
Code changes: +517 -8\ Tests: +273 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What MCP tool calls in a chat thread now say what happened in plain words. **AO's own tools** (the `ao` server) get their own rows: | Call | Row | | --- | --- | | `html_preview`, clean | Previewed the page | | `html_preview`, page had errors | Previewed the page · 1 console error (expands to the errors) | | `html_preview`, failed | Couldn't preview the page (expands to why) | | `html_render`, shown | no row: the page itself is the next row | | `html_render`, failed | Couldn't show the page (expands to why) | | `launch_app` | Opened Calculator | | `list_windows` | Looked at Calculator windows | | `get_window_state` | Looked at a window | | `click` | Clicked, Right-clicked, Double-clicked, ⌘-clicked | | `type_text` | Typed "12" (expands to the full text when it was cut) | | `press_key` | Pressed ⌘S, Pressed Return | | `bring_to_front` | Brought an app to the front | | `run_steps` | Took 2 actions in Calculator (expands to each step; says where it stopped) | While a call runs, the row and the live line use the present tense ("Previewing the page", "Opening Calculator"). **Every other MCP tool** reads ` · ` whichever harness made the call, and Claude Code's arguments show again when the row is expanded. ## Why Every MCP call went through one generic row: - The title was the provider's internal name, and it differed by harness: `mcp__ao__html_preview` in Claude Code, `html_preview MCP · ao` in Codex. - Expanding showed text written for the agent: the page check's JSON (sizes, Electron's dev-only security warning, "your sandbox has none"), html_render's "Do not describe the page" note, or a computer-use accessibility tree. - Codex records a failed AO tool call as completed, so a failed `html_render` looked like it worked. - Claude Code sends arguments as `input`, but the row only read `arguments`, so Claude rows never showed them. Follow-up to #7920. #7840 does the same for shell commands and Claude Code's built-in tools, and skips MCP calls on purpose. This PR only touches the MCP row, so the two don't overlap. ## Before / After Same conversations in the dev app, before and after the change. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Claude Code: raw names, no arguments
| Same turn: errors named, the failed render explained, the shown render has no row
| | Codex: `MCP · ao` rows, the failed render looks like it worked
| Same turn in Codex
| | | A normal turn: one quiet row, then the page
| | | Computer use, with a real refused `type_text` and a `run_steps` batch
| ## How - **`lib/mcp-tool.ts` (new)** reads a call the same way for both harnesses: the tool and server from `mcp____`, `Called /` or Codex's `server`/`toolName`; arguments from `arguments` or `input`; result text from Codex's `result.content` or ACP's `content` items. It drops Claude Code's "[Image: source: …]" temp-file line and unwraps its fenced errors. - **`aoToolView`** turns an `ao` call into a label, an optional note, and what expanding shows. The tool answers are never shown as is. A failure keeps its message without the error code and the daemon's request id (`(RENDER_INVALID) [request host/…]`). - **Failure from the answer, not only the status.** Codex reports these calls as completed, so a preview that came back without its report, a render that did not say where it was shown (`(render )`), or a `run_steps` that answered `1/3 steps ok` counts as failed. - **The shown page.** `readableItems` in `ChatWorkspace` drops a completed `html_render` before runs are grouped, so a run never counts a row that is not drawn. A running or failed one stays. - **Computer-use rows** are built from the call's arguments only. The answers are accessibility trees and snapshot ids, and in a real run (Calculator) the elements had empty names, so the labels do not try to name the clicked element. Tools this build does not know (`zoom`, `scroll` as its own tool) fall back to the generic `tool · ao` row. - **Copy stays English**, like the generic row it replaces. - **Not in this PR:** a preview thumbnail. Claude Code's screenshot is stripped before storage (`acp/client.go`), so showing one needs a backend and storage-size decision. Codex already keeps small screenshots inline in `result`. ## Testing - New `lib/mcp-tool.test.ts`: name and argument parsing for both harnesses, every AO label, the failure cases Codex reports as completed, error cleanup, and `run_steps` lines. title: fix(spawn): show CLI-spawned workers as starting, not stopped
body:
Code changes: +105 -11\
Tests: +205 -1\
Others: +6 -0 (generated OpenAPI spec and TS types)

## What

Workers started with `ao spawn` now open the way New Task sessions do: the prompt is the first message, the setup checklist sits under it, and the sidebar row shows a spinner. The "agent controller stopped" banner no longer appears during startup.

A child session's termination also stops showing up in its spawn parent's chat unless the parent ran the kill.

## Why

`ao spawn` took the synchronous start. Its session row existed for the whole worktree, setup and agent launch (about 33 s in the reported case) as a ready session with no controller and no prompt, so the UI correctly read it as stopped.

The "Terminated an agent · Spawned an agent" summary was not a misclassified command. The "terminated" row was a real, unrelated worker being archived at that moment. The daemon wrote it into the orchestrator's chat because the orchestrator had spawned that worker, and it landed beside the running `ao spawn`.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: red controller stopped banner over an empty chat](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/b6c805b6174633e0ea047fdef2e5e55d/raw/87badb2565dcfc8ea3fcae30ba02c89923603566/spawnlab-before.png) | ![After: prompt as first message with the setup checklist](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/b6c805b6174633e0ea047fdef2e5e55d/raw/87badb2565dcfc8ea3fcae30ba02c89923603566/spawnlab-after.png) |
| 4 s in: `provisionState: ready`, controller `stopped`, no turns | 4 s in: `provisionState: provisioning`, controller `connecting`, first turn `queued` |
| Archiving a spawned worker adds "Terminated an agent" to the parent's chat | Only a kill the parent ran appears there; otherwise it stays in the worker's own chat |

Both captures come from this branch's dev app with the same project. The "before" is a `POST /api/v1/sessions` without `async`, which is the request the old CLI sent and still takes the unchanged synchronous path.

## How

- `POST /api/v1/sessions` gets an opt-in `async` field that routes a project-backed Chat spawn through the existing async start. No second implementation of the optimistic path, and no renderer change was needed.
- The async path now seeds the row as `provisioning` on first insert, so no read can see a ready session with no controller.
- `ao spawn` sends `async`, then polls until the start settles. It still exits non-zero with the daemon's reason, and `--claim-pr` still runs after the start.
- `ao session kill` sends `callerSessionId` from `AO_SESSION_ID`. The termination goes to the spawn parent only when the caller is the parent.

Worth reviewing:

- **A failed CLI spawn now keeps its session.** It stays visible as failed with its reason and Retry, as New Task does, where the sync path deleted the row. Orchestrators retrying a failed spawn will leave those behind.
- **The composer stays open during startup** and queues ("Queue a follow-up while Claude Code gets ready"), matching New Task, rather than being disabled.
- Standalone and TUI spawns stay synchronous.
- Existing "Terminated" rows in old chats are not rewritten.

## Testing

Run in the real desktop app, isolated data, fish shell, with a 20 s setup step to hold the window open:

- Ran this checkout's `ao spawn` with `AO_SESSION_ID` set and opened the worker from the sidebar during startup: no banner, prompt shown at once, spinner in the sidebar.
- `ao spawn` waited about 22 s and printed `(working)`. After the agent replied, the conversation held the prompt once.
- Killed one spawned child with no caller and another through the CLI from its parent: the rows landed in the child's and the parent's chats respectively.

New tests cover the first row being `provisioning`, the `async` opt-in, the CLI wait and failure report, kill routing, and the renderer's starting state. They were not run locally, by request; CI verifies them.

The background-failure path was exercised by tests only, not in the app.

title: fix(codex): read auth from a custom model provider's env_key
body:
When Codex's `config.toml` selects a non-OpenAI `model_provider` (here a LiteLLM proxy with `env_key = "LITELLM_API_KEY"`), Codex never uses its OpenAI login. AO still judged Codex by that login, so Settings showed Codex as not set up and new Codex tasks were refused. Reported on Discord in #report-bugs ("codex shows unauthenticated with litellm"); there is no GitHub issue. - `service/agent`: `authenticationWithAccount` skips the Codex account check when a custom provider is selected, so readiness falls through to the adapter. - `adapters/agent/codex`: `AuthStatus` reads the selected provider (top-level `model_provider`, or the one set by `profile`). It reports `configured` when the provider's `env_key` is set in the daemon env, and `unknown` otherwise. Providers with `requires_openai_auth = true` and the default OpenAI provider keep the existing checks. - `service/agentaccounts`: `newSessionAccount` keeps the default account for Codex when a custom provider is selected, instead of refusing with `AGENT_ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_UNUSABLE` because the Codex CLI login is signed out. ## Screenshots Desktop app from this checkout on scratch data, Codex 0.167.0, a real LiteLLM 1.83.9 proxy with a master key, `LITELLM_API_KEY` exported. Before is `main`, after is this branch. | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Settings > Harness > Codex | | | | New Codex task | | | Before: Codex has a red dot and the task is refused with "The default account is signed out or now holds another login, and no other account is signed in. Sign one in again in Settings." After: no red dot, and the task runs and replies through LiteLLM. "Codex CLI login: Signed out" stays, since there is no ChatGPT login. The composer's model picker lists only OpenAI model names and sends the selected one (`gpt-6.1-sol` here), so the lab LiteLLM also serves that name. A LiteLLM that serves only its own names rejects the request with "Invalid model name". That is a separate follow-up.
CLI and API output Lab: codex-cli 0.167.0, LiteLLM 1.83.9 proxy on 127.0.0.1:4011 with master key, stub upstream behind it, scratch AO_DATA_DIR, daemon built from this checkout. ## 1. Codex works through LiteLLM; `codex login status` says Not logged in ``` $ cat $CODEX_HOME/config.toml model = "lab-model" model_provider = "litellm" [model_providers.litellm] name = "LiteLLM" base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:4011/v1" env_key = "LITELLM_API_KEY" wire_api = "responses" $ codex --version codex-cli 0.167.0 $ codex login status Not logged in (exit 1) $ codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Reply with the word pong." -------- user Reply with the word pong. codex pong from the LiteLLM proxy tokens used 2 pong from the LiteLLM proxy (exit 0) ``` ## 2. Before (main): AO says Codex needs auth ``` $ ao agent ls --refresh | grep codex codex Codex installed needs auth $ curl -s localhost:3901/api/v1/agents/readiness # codex.authentication { "state": "unauthorized", "reasonCode": "unauthorized", "reason": "Sign in to Codex or add an account in Settings." } $ ao spawn --project lab --agent codex --mode tui --name litellm-repro --prompt "Reply with the word pong." warning: agent "codex" may need auth according to daemon readiness; continuing and letting spawn validate runtime readiness Add or sign in to a Codex account in Settings before starting a Codex session (CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED) (exit 1) ``` ## 3. After (this branch): configured from LITELLM_API_KEY, spawn works ``` $ ao agent ls --refresh | grep codex codex Codex installed configured (unverified) $ curl -s localhost:3901/api/v1/agents/readiness # codex.authentication { "state": "configured", "reasonCode": "auth_configured_unverified", "reason": "Codex has credentials configured, but AO could not verify them.", "account": { "method": "api_key", "sourceKind": "environment", "source": "LITELLM_API_KEY" } } $ ao spawn --project lab --agent codex --mode tui --name litellm-fixed --prompt "Reply with the word pong." warning: agent "codex" auth status is unknown; continuing and letting spawn validate runtime readiness spawned session lab-1 "litellm-fixed" (idle) [prompt 25 B, system 15349 B] (exit 0) $ ao session history lab-1 ## Turn 1 of 1 2026-11-08T07:39:08Z codex User: Reply with the word pong. Assistant: pong from the LiteLLM proxy ``` ## 4. After: signed-out OpenAI Codex still needs auth ``` $ cat $CODEX_HOME/config.toml # OpenAI provider, no auth.json model = "gpt-5" $ ao agent ls --refresh | grep codex codex Codex installed needs auth ```
## Tests - `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/... ./internal/service/... ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/httpd/...`: changed packages pass. Locally, `session_manager` (4 `TestSpawn_*MissingBinary*`), `systemcheck` and `shellterm` fail on missing tmux and fish on this machine; they are untouched here and fail the same way on `main`. - New: `TestAuthStatusUsesCustomModelProviderKey`, `TestCustomModelProviderSkipsCodexAccountCheck`, `TestCustomCodexModelProviderStartsOnSignedOutDefault`. All three fail on `main`. ## Risks - An `env_key` that is set only in the project env, not the daemon env, reads as `unknown` (not blocking) instead of `configured`. - `configured` is shown as unverified. body:

title: fix(chat): move a steered message out of the queue dock at the click
body:
## Problem

Steering the last queued message leaves an empty "0 Queued Messages" frame above the composer. It stays until the steer request and a conversation reload both finish, so it grows with latency and is worst on remote hosts.

## Cause

`QueuedMessageDock` hid a steered row in its own state, but `ChatWorkspace` mounted the dock from the daemon snapshot, which still listed the turn as `queued`. The dock is always header plus one row tall, so it drew an empty frame. The steered text was missing from the timeline too, because its steer row comes from the same reload.

## Fix

- `ChatWorkspace` owns the set of turns being steered. They leave the dock's list at the click, so steering the last one unmounts the dock.
- While the snapshot still has a steered turn queued, the timeline gets a steer row built from the queued message. The daemon retires the queue item and writes its steer row in one transaction (`CompleteQueuedTurnPromotion`), so the real row replaces it in one render.
- A refused steer puts the message back in the dock with the reason, through a new `steerErrors` prop.
- `QueuedMessageDock` drops its own optimistic set.

## Evidence

title: fix(scm): re-observe a session's PR when its agent changes it
body:
Code changes: +153 -19\
Tests: +208 -0\
Others: +6 -0 (generated OpenAPI spec and TS types)

## What

When an agent runs a command that probably changed its PR (`gh pr merge/close/ready/review/create/edit`, `git push`), AO re-reads that session's open PRs about 500 ms later instead of waiting for the next poll.

## Why

Root cause: the SCM observer learns about a merge only on its 30 s tick, and nothing told it the agent had just merged. The rest of the path is already fast: CDC relay polls every 100 ms, `pr_updated` is not throttled by the renderer, and DB to sidebar row measured about 0.1 s.

## Before / After

Time from GitHub's `mergedAt` (1 s resolution) to the sidebar row showing merged, real desktop app, isolated data, throwaway private repo.

| Before (merge with no local signal) | After (agent runs `gh pr merge`) |
| --- | --- |
| 13.6 s, 18.7 s, 25.8 s (bounded by the 30 s tick) | 4.8 s on this trimmed build; 4.6 s, 4.8 s, 5.4 s on the earlier longer version |

The remaining ~5 s is mostly `gh` returning and the hook firing (~2 s), the debounce, and the poll's API calls.

## How

- `domain.CommandMayChangePR` is a single regex. It is only a hint: a false positive costs one fetch, a miss waits for the next poll.
- Two sources: `post-tool-use` hooks (terminal agents) send `prMayHaveChanged` on the activity route; chat controllers check finished command activities.
- `Observer.RequestSessionRefresh` debounces with one shared 500 ms timer and wakes the existing triggered poll loop. Each request forces one fetch of that session's open PRs.
- A forced poll defers other sessions' commit-check guards to the next tick. They run serially at ~0.45 s each, which would otherwise grow with the board.
- The 30 s cadence, rate-limit cooldowns and terminal-PR handling are unchanged. A cooled-down provider is still skipped.

Intentional omissions:
- No follow-up polls. Every measured merge was visible on the first forced fetch. After `git push` or `gh pr create`, GitHub may lag, in which case the next regular poll picks it up as it does today (not measured).
- `ao session claim-pr` needs no trigger: it already fetches and writes the PR synchronously.
- Merges outside an agent (github.com, your own terminal) still wait for the poll.

## Testing

- Seven agent-driven and three no-signal merges in the desktop app against throwaway PRs; daemon logs show the hook POST followed by a poll 500 ms later.
- Added tests for the classifier, hook flag, activity route, coalescing, and session-scoped forcing. Not run locally by request; CI runs them.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
