title: [Feature]: Choose and remember the host terminal for Neovim
body:
### Problem

On macOS, opening Neovim from AO launches it in Terminal.app. Users who normally use iTerm2, Ghostty, or another terminal may have different font and display settings there, so Neovim plugin icons and glyphs can look different or render incorrectly.

AO can already open a workspace directory in installed terminal apps, but that choice does not configure the terminal used to launch Neovim.

### Proposed direction

Add a **Neovim → Host terminal** selector in the editor-related settings (suggested placement). Show supported installed terminals with their names/icons, remember the local preference, and use it consistently for existing Neovim workspace and file-opening actions.

Initial scope: macOS. Keep Terminal.app as the default for users who have not configured a preference.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Allow choosing installed Terminal, iTerm2, and Ghostty.
- [ ] Persist the choice across AO restarts.
- [ ] Launch Neovim in the selected terminal at the correct workspace or file, including paths containing spaces or non-ASCII characters.
- [ ] Use the selected terminal's existing font/display configuration; verify plugin icons and special glyphs.
- [ ] Identify the chosen terminal clearly in settings and launch hints.
- [ ] If the selected terminal is removed or fails to launch, show a useful error and allow reselection; explain any fallback.
- [ ] Preserve the existing default behavior and cover preference persistence, terminal selection, and failure handling with tests.

### Related history

- #4607 — original Neovim support request (closed).
- #4723 — merged Neovim editor handoff; macOS uses Terminal.app.
- #6730 — merged workspace terminal-app discovery/menu support.

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for Neovim, nvim, host terminal, and preferred terminal; no matching host-terminal preference request was found.

Feature proposal only; implementation is not being started.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar.

title: feat(artifacts): show published artifact links to agents

## Summary When you publish an artifact with **Share** in the desktop and then ask the agent to attach the link to a PR, the agent now finds the link. Before, it answered "I can't get the public link from here". **Cause.** Only the desktop is signed in to AO Cloud. The desktop records each published file in `share-links.json` in the data dir, but that record kept only the link's ID, not its URL. So the daemon, the `ao` CLI and agents had no way to get the link. **What this PR changes:** - **Desktop.** The record in `share-links.json` now keeps the public URL. Publish stores it. Each link list refreshes it, and it is dropped once the link is revoked or AO Cloud no longer lists it. Unpublish removes the whole record, as it did before. - **Daemon.** `sessionartifacts.ShareLinks` reads that file, using only the records of the configured AO Cloud. It re-reads the file only when its size or mtime changes, and accepts http(s) URLs only. It sets `shareUrl` on the session's `artifactFiles`, and the API spec and `schema.ts` are regenerated. - **CLI.** `ao session get` now ends with an `artifacts:` list, with `(public link: )` on each published file. `--json` also includes `shareUrl`. - **Agents.** The worker artifact prompt and the `using-ao` session guide say that only the user publishes, and that `ao session get` then shows the link. **Not in this PR:** agents still cannot publish. Publishing stays in the desktop, because the AO Cloud token never leaves it. ## Before / after Both runs follow the same steps: 1. A real Claude Code chat session (Haiku 5.5) writes `release-notes.html` as a session artifact. 2. I click **Share → Publish** in the desktop. 3. I send: _"ok cool, I have published the artifact. ` release-notes.html (public link: http://6f43lolpfdi3l4bg4aliyxypzb.share.localhost:8441/)` | `share-links.json` after publishing: | Before | After | |---|---| | `{"shareId":"404a4c28-…","fingerprint":"6749ac4b…"}` | `{"shareId":"bbe64e31-…","fingerprint":"623190f2…","url":"http://6f43lolpfdi3l4bg4aliyxypzb.share.localhost:8441/"}` | The link is a `share.localhost` address because the lab used a local AO Cloud. ## Testing **End to end, on this machine:** - **Setup.** - A local AO Cloud control plane, built from its main branch, with artifact sharing turned on. - The dev desktop app with an isolated data dir, signed in to that control plane. - The before run used main's daemon and frontend. The after run used this branch's. - **After run.** - The published link served the page (HTTP 200). - The agent ran `ao session get` and replied with the exact link. - **Unpublish** removed the link from `ao session get`. Publishing again showed the new link, in text and in `--json` (`"shareUrl"`). - **Before run.** The same steps left no URL in `share-links.json`, nothing in `ao session get`, and the agent asked for the link to be pasted. **Unit tests:** - `go test ./internal/sessionartifacts ./internal/service/session ./internal/httpd/controllers ./internal/cli ./internal/skillassets ./internal/session_manager` - `npx vitest run src/main/cloud-share-ipc.test.ts src/renderer/components/ShareArtifactPopover.test.tsx`: 44 passed. title: feat(daemon): record write lock holds over 1s in telemetry
body:
## Summary

Every DB write in the daemon goes through one write lock (`writeMu`). When a writer holds it for seconds, every other write queues behind it. Wakes then run past their 60 s deadline and show "The agent controller stopped". Account switches fail their 5 s transition step, and HTTP requests time out. Until now nothing recorded who held the lock or for how long. The last two stalls (sessions 371 and 374) had to be rebuilt from `change_log` gaps and process samples, on a single machine.

This PR makes the write lock time each hold. When a hold lasts 1 s or more, AO emits `ao.daemon.write_lock_held` after the lock is released:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `level` | `warn` |
| `caller` | holder's 4 innermost frames, e.g. `store.(*Store).UpsertProject:23 \| project.(*Service).Add:422 \| controllers.(*ProjectsController).add:197 \| http.HandlerFunc.ServeHTTP:2338` |
| `duration_ms` | hold time |

- **Where it goes.** The event is written to the local `telemetry_event` table. It is also sent to PostHog, so slow writers can be counted across installs and app versions.
- **What PostHog gets.** The remote allowlist keeps only `caller` (function names and line numbers, no paths) and `duration_ms`. Opt-out and rate limits apply as for every other event.
- **Docs.** `docs/telemetry.md` lists the event under "What Orchestrator.inc sends".
- **Volume.** Only holders report, not the writers waiting behind them. A 110 s stall is one event.
- **Cost.** A hold under 1 s costs one `time.Now()`. The stack walk and the emit run only for slow holds, after the token is released.
- **No deadlock.** The observer runs after release, so the local sink's own insert can take the lock.
- **Release site.** Each frame's line is where the lock was released inside the holder, for example the `return` that runs the deferred `Unlock`.

Local query:

```sql
select occurred_at, json_extract(payload_json,'$.duration_ms') ms, json_extract(payload_json,'$.caller') caller
from telemetry_event where name = 'ao.daemon.write_lock_held' order by occurred_at desc;
```

## Tests

- `TestContextMutexReportsSlowHolderAfterRelease` (`-race`) checks four things:
  - a fast hold is not reported;
  - a `defer` hold names its function;
  - a method-value release (the `conversationWriter` pattern) names the real caller;
  - the observer can take the lock again within 1 s, which proves it runs after release.
- `TestSanitizeRemotePayloadKeepsWriteLockHolder` checks that `caller` and `duration_ms` survive sanitizing and that other keys are dropped.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports 0 issues on `store`, `daemon`, and `adapters/telemetry`.
- Real daemon, isolated lab (own data dir, port, and a local fake PostHog endpoint):
  - An external `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on `ao.db` was held for 3 s while `ao project add` ran.
  - `telemetry_event` got `{"caller":"store.(*Store).UpsertProject:23 | project.(*Service).Add:422 | controllers.(*ProjectsController).add:197 | http.HandlerFunc.ServeHTTP:2338","duration_ms":1099}`.
  - The fake PostHog endpoint received the same event with `caller`, `duration_ms`, and the standard properties (`install_id`, OS, version).

## Risks

- During a long I/O stall, the sink's own slow insert can report itself. This is bounded by the stall and by the sink's 128-event buffer, which drops when full.
- `LockContext` callers that cancel while waiting record nothing, because they never held the lock.
- `caller` line numbers change between releases, so group by version in PostHog.

title: feat: remember the Neovim host terminal on macOS
body:
Code changes: +161 -20  
Tests: +161 -6  
Others: +27 -0

## What

Add a macOS **Neovim terminal** selector under Settings → General → Sessions, with installed Terminal, iTerm2 and Ghostty choices and native icons. Remember the choice across desktop restarts and use it for both session-workspace and chat-file Neovim launches.

## Why

Closes #7965. Neovim currently always launches in macOS Terminal, whose font, glyph and profile settings can differ from a user's preferred terminal.

**Draft: core-team feature scope approval is still pending on #7965.** This is an independently scoped implementation for discussion; it is not ready for upstream review or merge until that approval and the checks below are complete.

Related history: [original Neovim request #4607](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/4607), [Neovim support #4723](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/4723), [workspace terminal choices #6730](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6730). The terminal-shell setting discussed in [#7874](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/7874) chooses a shell rather than the Neovim host application.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| General settings has a default-editor choice but no Neovim terminal choice. | A Neovim terminal menu lists installed supported apps with their icons; the default remains Terminal. |
| Workspace and file actions launch Neovim in Terminal. | Both actions use the stored host and set the workspace/file-parent working directory. Editor labels indicate a nondefault host. |
| There is no saved host to diagnose when an app is removed. | A missing saved host remains selected with an actionable error; launches fail without silently falling back, and an installed replacement can be selected. |

Real Electron captures use the same 1280×1000 General screen and isolated AO data. **Screenshot attachment is pending:** the available GitHub connector/CLI has no issue-attachment upload operation. Captures for a maintainer/person with an authenticated GitHub browser to attach in this table:

- Before (exact main base): `/Users/will/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-2/neovim-terminal-before.png`
- After (saved iTerm2): `/Users/will/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-2/neovim-terminal-after.png`
- Installed-app menu: `/Users/will/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-2/neovim-terminal-menu.png`
- Missing Ghostty: `/Users/will/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-2/neovim-terminal-missing.png`

## How

- Extend the existing serialized, atomic editor-settings file with a validated terminal ID. Merge queued updates so editor and host saves preserve each other; older/invalid settings default to Terminal.
- Keep app paths and launch construction in Electron main, behind the existing shell-webContents IPC trust check. Reuse supported installed-terminal discovery and native icon caching; no daemon/API contract changes.
- Refresh supported-host discovery when Settings opens, and refresh on a selected-host cache miss before launch or save. This also supports registered apps outside the standard Applications folders on a fresh desktop process. Resolve the saved host again at launch. Terminal and iTerm2 use quoted AppleScript shell input; iTerm2 creates a window with its default profile. Ghostty uses its native app via Launch Services with working-directory and `-e` arguments.
- Intentional scope: macOS only, these three host apps, each app's default profile/configuration. No arbitrary executable/command input, per-session settings, terminal-profile management, font changes, or Linux/Windows host selector.

## Testing

Cold-discovery regressions cover registered iTerm2/Ghostty installations such as `/Volumes/Tools/iTerm.app`: Settings-first and fresh workspace/file/save actions work without an unrelated menu refresh. All four added cases fail before the fix and pass afterward; focused suites: **204 passed**.

Reproduced separately on this PR's exact clean main base `1c3022d6dac0226126aa86f7d3610bc51bfefc3e`; no unrelated contrast changes included. Initial resource-concurrent run had transient navigation/focus failures; the final whole-suite run above was isolated from Vitest/source changes.

title: feat(desktop): show unread orchestrator replies on its buttons
body:
Code changes: +195 -23\
Tests: +74 -0\
Others: +18 -0 (locale strings)

## What

The orchestrator buttons on the sidebar project row and in the top bar now show when the orchestrator has replied and the user hasn't seen it.

- A small accent dot appears on the icon when a reply finishes and the orchestrator isn't open.
- A quiet breathing dot shows while the orchestrator is working.
- Opening the orchestrator clears the dot. Seen state is per project and survives restarts.

## Why

There was no way to tell the orchestrator had replied unless you were looking at its chat.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Sidebar row before](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/sidebar-before.png) | Reply unread: ![Sidebar row with unread dot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/sidebar-unread.png) |
| ![Top bar before](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/topbar-before.png) | Reply unread: ![Top bar with unread dot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/topbar-unread.png) |
| ![Sidebar row before](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/sidebar-before.png) | Working: ![Sidebar row while working](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/sidebar-working.png) |
| ![Top bar before](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/topbar-before.png) | Working: ![Top bar while working](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/topbar-working.png) |
| No dot on the board's Orchestrator button | ![Board top bar with unread dot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/board-unread.png) |
| Unread state did not exist | After opening the orchestrator: ![Sidebar row cleared](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/sidebar-cleared.png) ![Top bar cleared](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/70dc3333c1acb7bf620a95dbf7b1053c/raw/topbar-cleared.png) |

## How

- **What counts as a reply:** the orchestrator's activity going from `active` to `idle` or `waiting_input`, seen live in the workspace data. Tool calls keep it `active`, and the user's own message starts a turn rather than ending one.
- **Why not compare timestamps:** restore, resume and provider switch all reset activity to idle with the current time, so comparing `lastActivityAt` would show false dots after a restart.
- **Storage:** `stores/orchestrator-reply-store.ts` keeps reply and seen times per project in localStorage, like the existing `session-read-store`.
- **Dot styling:** it matches the Browser button's unseen dot (`size-1.5 bg-primary ring-2`). `bg-primary` is the same colour as the filled Orchestrator button, so the dot uses the button's label colour there.
- **Row visibility:** the project-row button is already always visible, so no hover change was needed.
- **Top bar scope:** the dot is on every copy of the button: simplified top bar, previous top bar, and board header.

Known limits, for reviewers:

- A reply that finishes while the app is closed isn't flagged, because the renderer has to see the turn end. A reliable fix needs a daemon-side "last turn completed" field on the session.
- Stopping a turn by hand also goes `active` to `idle`, so it counts as a reply.
- The working dot shows for any orchestrator turn, not only ones started by the user. Activity state doesn't record who started it.

## Testing

In the real Electron app, with isolated data and a Claude Code orchestrator in chat mode:

- Sent the orchestrator a message and switched to a worker: both buttons showed the working dot, then the unread dot when the reply finished.
- Reloaded the renderer: the dot was still there. Electron itself was not restarted.
- Opened the orchestrator from the top bar: the dot cleared and stayed cleared after going back to the worker and reloading.
- Let a reply finish while the orchestrator was open, then left: no dot.
- Sent a message with `ao send` while on the board: working, then unread, on the sidebar and board buttons.

Added `orchestrator-reply-store.test.ts`. Per project convention, tests and typecheck run in CI, not locally.

title: fix(shell): align top bar and sidebar, add button press states
body:
Code changes: +24 -21\
Tests: +3 -3\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Aligns the macOS shell to one set of guides and gives buttons a press state.

- Buttons now deepen their fill while pressed. There is no scale or movement.
- Top-bar tabs and controls, the brand, the sidebar toggle and the traffic lights share one centerline.
- The traffic lights share the sidebar icons' left edge.
- Sidebar footer labels share the text column used by the other rows.

## Why

Apple's HIG says to "always include a press state for a custom button" and to align elements so they're easier to scan. `Button` had no pressed style, and the shell had small offsets between elements that should line up.

## Before / After

Measured in the Electron app at 100% zoom on macOS, with Developer Mode on.

| Element | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Button while pressed | Same as hover | Deeper fill |
| Top-bar controls, vertical center | 24.5px | 25px |
| Brand, vertical center | 24.3px | 25px |
| Traffic lights, left edge | 18px | 19px (sidebar icons are at 19px) |
| Footer row label, left edge | 43px | 41px (other rows are at 41px) |

## How

- `GHOST_PILL_CLASS` carries the pressed fill, so non-`Button` triggers that use it get it too. Text links and Settings/modal footer buttons are unchanged.
- `outline` needs `dark:active:` as well, because its `dark:` rules otherwise outrank `active:`.
- The traffic lights moved instead of the sidebar content. The sidebar's `pl-px` balances its transparent 1px right border, so removing it would make row highlights uneven.
- Merge and Approve override the primary fill with green, so they also get a green pressed fill.
- The brand keeps its natural width so it clips instead of truncating while the sidebar collapses.
- The project row's `translate-y-px` stays. It is an intentional optical offset covered by a test.

Not covered: the x position of the traffic lights doesn't scale with window zoom, and light themes and the collapsed sidebar weren't checked.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.

Positions were measured in the running Electron app through CDP. The traffic-light position was read from a native capture of the window. The pressed style was confirmed as a loaded CSS rule, not by clicking.

title: feat(desktop): add top bar commands to the macOS menu bar
body:
Code changes: +330 -14\
Tests: +113 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The important session top bar commands now also live in the macOS menu bar, each with its keyboard shortcut, as Apple's guidance asks: toolbar commands should also be in the menu bar. The app looks the same; only menu items are added.

- **File:** New Task (⌘N), New Terminal (⌘T), Open in Editor (⌘O), Open in Finder, Archive Session (⇧⌘A)
- **View:** Toggle Sidebar (⌘B), Toggle Inspector (⇧⌘B)
- **Go (new):** Back (⌘[), Forward (⌘]), Orchestrator (⇧⌘O), Notifications

## Why

Until now none of the top bar or tab strip controls had a menu item. Their keyboard shortcuts could only be found from tooltips or the shortcuts sheet.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| File menu: only Close Window | File: New Task, New Terminal, Open in Editor, Open in Finder, Archive Session, then Close Window |
| View menu: reload, DevTools, zoom, full screen | Toggle Sidebar and Toggle Inspector added at the top |
| No Go menu | Go: Back, Forward, Orchestrator, Notifications |
| — | Items that don't apply are greyed out (e.g. New Terminal on the board, session items under Settings) |

## How

- **One set of handlers.** A menu item sends the same IPC message its keyboard shortcut already sends (`appShortcutDelivery` in `app-shortcuts.ts`), so it runs the existing renderer handler. The two commands with no shortcut (Open in Finder, Notifications) use one new `app:menu-action` channel.
- **Shortcuts come from the registry.** Accelerators are built from `effectiveShortcutBindings`, so they follow the user's custom bindings. The menu is rebuilt when bindings are saved.
- **No double fire.** `before-input-event` already consumes these chords, so the menu normally never sees them. A chord that falls through to the menu is ignored in two cases: while a binding is being recorded, and when the Browser owns that chord.
- **Enabled state.** Each component that owns a control reports whether its command applies, through `useAppMenuAvailable` / `useSessionMenuAvailable`. Session items stand down under the full-page Settings, matching `useSessionShortcut`. Main accepts these reports only from the shell `WebContents`, coerces them to known ids and booleans, and clears them on reload.
- **Windows/Linux are unchanged.** Their templates are untouched, because plain Ctrl+B and similar keys must keep reaching terminals there.
- **Labels are English**, like the rest of the native menus, which don't use i18n today.

**Intentionally left out** (the menus are kept minimal):
- Close Tab (⌘W): letting ⌘W fall through to a menu item is a known hazard in this code.
- Board: orchestrator only.
- Run cue menu: its contents change per project.
- Other editors and Copy Path from the editor dropdown: rarely used.
- Split terminals: Developer Mode only.
- A separate Browser item: the inspector toggle is the Browser on orchestrators.
- Coder workspace link and owner tag: niche.

## Testing

- Tested by hand in the dev app (macOS): menu items, shortcuts and greyed-out states.
- New unit tests cover menu placement, accelerators, the enabled state, click routing, coercion of the IPC payload, Windows/Linux templates staying unchanged, accelerator naming, and the preload channel.
- Local `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass. Focused menu, preload, and shortcut tests: 130 passed. Full local Vitest had a Node ABI mismatch in `better-sqlite3`; after rebuilding it, three affected files passed and one unrelated workspace retry-count test still failed locally. Local renderer smoke: 152 passed, one selection-contrast failure. All required PR CI checks passed on the pinned runners.

title: Reduce desktop renderer lag without visual changes
body:
## Summary

The desktop app feels slow during session switching and several related interactions. A live **development-build** recording described in the reporter's 2026-11-08 conversation found repeated React work in the renderer, with short single-threaded blocks. The proposed work is to reduce avoidable renderer work **without changing the UI's visual design or interaction timing**.

This is **one tracking issue** for the complete investigation and grouped fixes. Begin with **A (chat render cost)** and **B (session switching)**, as requested in the conversation. Implementation can use focused PRs linked to this issue; the PR boundaries below are a planning proposal, not a request to open more issues.

### Evidence and limits

The original investigation reported:

- Up to **20,476 component renders and 90 React commits in one second** during a session switch, across SessionView, Sidebar, ProjectItem, and many tooltips.
- A switch blocked the UI for up to **274 ms**, with one **671 ms** outlier.
- Typical session visits were **149 ms first visit** and **123 ms revisit** in the benchmark described in the conversation.
- InlineCode accounted for **250 ms across 299 renders in one second**. Its file-link lookup reportedly normalized and searched the workspace path list up to three times per render.
- A first session-view code load took up to **269 ms**.
- While an agent ran, Timeline and TurnGroup rendered **15–23 times per second**; slow keystrokes were **96–104 ms**, versus **9 ms** in the comparison described by the prior investigator.
- A post-steer refresh caused **12,570 renders and a 254 ms freeze**.
- Real-use monitoring saw up to **71 frames over 50 ms per minute**.
- The backend, polling, GPU, and Electron main process were reported quiet during this capture. The evidence points toward renderer work, but the individual causes still need verification.

**These figures are from a dev build and from a prior agent's report in the attached conversation.** The raw capture and harness are not included here. Absolute timing may be lower in a production build. The heavier 8–10-session, many-browser-tab scenario was not tested. All earlier “after” figures were projections, not measurements or acceptance guarantees.

## Complete finding inventory

| # | Area | Reported observation | Proposed fix group |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Session switch | Whole app repeatedly rerenders; up to 20,476 renders, 90 commits, 274 ms freeze and one 671 ms outlier. | A, B, C, D |
| 2 | InlineCode | Workspace file-list normalization/search dominates chat cost: 299 renders, 250 ms in one second. | A |
| 3 | First session open | Session-view chunk loads on demand; up to 269 ms on first switch. | B |
| 4 | Session revisit | Revisit still rebuilds chat, around 123 ms versus 149 ms first visit. | B |
| 5 | Route change | Sidebar and closed CommandPalette rerender roughly 9 and 5 times per session open. | D |
| 6 | Loaders | Working-label shimmer visibly stops when the renderer blocks; spinner behavior was not confirmed. | E, secondary to reducing blocking |
| 7 | Streaming/typing | Timeline and TurnGroup rerender 15–23 times/s; some keystrokes take 96–104 ms. | A |
| 8 | After steer | Refresh burst rerenders chat/sidebar together: 12,570 renders, 254 ms freeze. | C, A, D |
| 9 | Hover generally | Hover arrives during frozen frames; up to 71 >50 ms frames/minute. | Cross-cutting |
| 10 | Hover styling | The 100 ms color fade contributes to perceived delay. **Reporter explicitly chose to preserve it.** | Excluded |
| 11 | Sidebar hover | One row hover causes about 10 React commits. | D |
| 12 | Sidebar scroll | Tooltips rerender about 67 times per scroll; a later summary cited 12 dropped frames. | D |
| 13 | Browser tab open | One recorded opening took 256 ms. One sample is insufficient to assign cause. | G |
| 14 | BrowserPanelView | Repeated renders cost about 1.9 ms each; it appeared in 45 separate seconds of the recording. | G |
| 15 | Inspector toggle | Opening/closing panel rerenders chat: Timeline 10–14 times and InlineCode around 191 times. | A |
| 16 | Inspector resize | Chat rerenders while dragging; 8 dropped frames, worst frame 48 ms. | A |
| 17 | Chat scroll | Timeline rerenders about 75 times; 19 dropped frames, worst frame 63 ms. | A |
| 18 | Sidebar collapse/expand | 4–6 dropped frames; worst frames 56–68 ms. | D |
| 19 | Project toggle | Toggling one project rerenders 20 ProjectItems. | D |
| 20 | Artifacts open | Each thumbnail mounts actions menu, confirm dialog, and tooltips; around 15,000 renders and a 186 ms freeze. | F |
| 21 | App reload | Around 614 ms to usable sidebar, with 17,000 renders. | **Excluded from this interaction-lag scope**; requires a separate startup investigation if desired |

The recording's “not the cause” statement is scoped to what was observed in that capture; it should not be treated as a blanket finding about every environment.

## Grouped work and rough size

The line counts below were planning estimates given **before implementation**. They are not work already done or a commitment to add that many lines. Prefer the smallest change that solves the measured problem.

### A. Chat render cost — first priority (findings 1, 2, 7, 15–17)

- Cache or precompute InlineCode's workspace path lookup so unchanged snippets do not repeatedly scan the full list.
- Trace why Timeline and TurnGroup rerender while streaming, typing, scrolling, and changing inspector geometry. Keep unchanged turns stable without hiding live updates.
- Prevent inspector toggle/resize and chat scroll from making the chat tree repeat expensive work.
- Preserve file links, path menus, inline-code rendering, text fade, selection, scrolling, and live message behavior.

**Estimate:** 200–300 app-code lines plus 80–120 test lines; medium risk. Prior projected results such as “250 ms to 20 ms” for InlineCode and “about 15 ms” typing are unmeasured hypotheses.

### B. Session switching — first priority (findings 1, 3, 4)

- Preload the session-view chunk while idle, without introducing a new visible loading state.
- Investigate keeping roughly four recent sessions mounted (the previous suggestion named React `<Activity>`). Verify compatibility with the project's React version and architecture before choosing that mechanism.
- Check duplicate DOM IDs, hidden-session subscriptions and background work, memory use, focus, scroll position, session state, open animation, and text fade. A revisit must look and behave like a fresh open.
- Measure first open and revisit separately.

**Estimate:** 150–250 app-code lines plus 60–100 test lines; medium to high risk. Prior projected 30–50 ms revisits and 40–60 ms overall switches are estimates only.

### C. Refreshes after send/steer (finding 8)

Trace the refresh burst and coalesce updates where correctness allows. Preserve visible status/content order and timely delivery.

**Estimate:** 40–80 app-code lines plus 30–50 test lines; medium risk.

### D. Left sidebar (findings 5, 11, 12, 18, 19)

Reduce unrelated ProjectItem, Sidebar, closed CommandPalette, and tooltip rerenders. Trace the preview-card hover state so one hover does only necessary work. Improve collapse/expand frame pacing without changing the animation, tooltip/preview delay, row appearance, or hover fade.

**Estimate:** 150–250 app-code lines plus 60–100 test lines; medium risk.

### E. Working-label shimmer (finding 6)

The shimmer was *not* identified as a material source of lag. A compositor-backed implementation may keep it moving during renderer blocks, but it does not make the freeze shorter. Only change it if appearance, sweep, and timing can be matched; otherwise leave it as is.

**Estimate:** 20–40 app-code lines plus 0–20 test lines; low risk if the visual constraint is met. Defer behind work that reduces actual blocking.

### F. Artifacts page (finding 20)

Avoid mounting every thumbnail's actions menu, confirm dialog, and tooltips at initial page open. Preserve their current appearance, availability, focus behavior, and interaction timing when invoked.

**Estimate:** 60–100 app-code lines plus 30–50 test lines; low risk.

### G. Browser inspector (findings 13, 14)

Investigate the 256 ms Browser-tab opening sample before attributing it to BrowserPanelView. Reduce rerenders caused by unrelated state while keeping browser tab behavior and look the same.

**Estimate:** 50–150 app-code lines plus 30–60 test lines; unknown risk until diagnosed.

The prior combined estimate for A–G was **670–1,170 app-code lines** and **290–500 test lines**. It also described a **626-line local measurement tool** already written in a separate dev checkout; locate and review it before assuming it is available or suitable.

## Non-negotiable constraint: no visual design changes

The reporter's rule applies to **all** groups: change how much work the app does, not what users see. Preserve layout, typography, colors, hover fade (including the 100 ms fade), loader appearance, animations, tooltip and preview-card delays, menu/dialog presentation, chat transitions, and the behavior of a fresh session open. If an optimization cannot meet this rule, leave that part out and document why. Screenshots alone are insufficient for motion or timing; compare recordings/interactions as well.

## Verification and completion criteria

1. Capture a comparable **production-build baseline and after run** for each affected interaction. Record median/typical and worst-case interaction times, long frames, React renders/commits, and the test conditions. Label dev-build numbers separately.
2. Verify first session open, repeated switching/revisit, active streaming while typing, send/steer refresh, sidebar hover/scroll/toggle/collapse, inspector toggle/resize/Browser tab, chat scroll, and Artifacts open.
3. Repeat key interactions with **8–10 sessions and multiple browser tabs**. Report new bottlenecks rather than assuming the current list is exhaustive.
4. Compare before/after screenshots **and motion/interaction recordings** for affected states. No intentional visual change, including hover fade or animation timing.
5. Add behavior-focused tests around any changed boundary, run focused checks followed by the CI commands required by AGENTS.md, and report any validation gaps.
6. Publish measured before/after evidence in implementation PR descriptions. Do not report projected numbers as achieved results.

### Out of scope and status

- Startup/reload optimization (finding 21) is intentionally outside this issue's interaction scope.
- Changing the 100 ms hover fade is intentionally excluded by the reporter.
- No app fix is claimed by this issue. Earlier analysis began tracing code paths for A/B, but the pasted transcript shows no completed change or verified after result.
- The source conversation is preserved in a separate comment below. It is context, including earlier agent proposals; it is not a confirmed technical specification.

title: ao remote-host link fails with 502 tunnel_unavailable and the machine is never listed; status still says devices list it
body:
Reported by Prateek (relayed from AO session standalone-39), while preparing the remote-machines launch video.

**What happened.** Linking a fresh self-hosted VM to an AO account fails at "add this machine to your AO account":

```
Signed in as <the user's account>.
add this machine to your AO account: AO Cloud answered 502 (tunnel_unavailable); run `ao remote-host link` again
```

Sign-in succeeds, but the machine never appears on the account's signed-in devices (phone machine list, desktop). Reproduced 2 of 2: once from the bootstrap installer, once from `ao remote-host link --label build-box`.

**Expected (per #7294).** When AO Cloud can't make the fixed tunnel (429/502), the machine keeps its quick tunnel. A registration with `url` still succeeds, so the machine is listed at its quick-tunnel address.

**Afterwards.** `ao remote-host status` says "Linked to an AO account: its signed-in devices list this machine." while no device lists it.

**Environment.** Azure VM Standard_D2s_v5, Central India, Ubuntu 24.04.5 x86_64. Installed with docs/self-hosted-remote.md's bootstrap (`bash -s -- --nightly`), which gave v0.14.11-nightly.202611071807 (commit 8bf36847091d). Phone: the new native mobile design (TestFlight). Desktop: nightly 0.14.11.

**Timeline (UTC 2026-11-08).** 11:11:19 quick tunnel up. 11:12:09 account token issued. About 11:12:24 the installer prints the sign-in, then the 502, then the manual pairing details. About 11:16, `ao remote-host link` shows the same sign-in success and the same 502.

**Impact.** The documented VM path ends with a machine that never shows up. It also blocks the "add a machine" part of the launch video.

The AO Cloud side (why the 502 happens) is tracked in OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane (linked in a comment below).

title: fix(remote): list a linked machine at its quick tunnel when AO Cloud cannot make its fixed address
body:
Part of #7976. The AO Cloud side, why the fixed address could not be made, is OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#66.

## What was wrong

**Linking failed instead of falling back.** On a fresh VM, `ao remote-host link` signed in, then failed with `AO Cloud answered 502 (tunnel_unavailable)`. The machine was never listed. The CLI retried with the quick-tunnel `url` only on `409 fixed_address_limit_reached`. AO Cloud's contract also answers `429 tunnel_rate_limited` and `502 tunnel_unavailable` when it cannot make the fixed address, and a registration with `url` still lists the machine. The desktop path from #7294 already falls back on any failed link.

**Status overclaimed.** `ao remote-host status` then said "Linked to an AO account: its signed-in devices list this machine." It shows that line whenever `accountLinked` is true, and `accountLinked` only means the machine holds an account token. The CLI issues that token before the AO Cloud PUT, so a failed PUT leaves it behind.

## What changes

- **`ao remote-host link`:** retries with the quick-tunnel `url` on 409, 429 or 502 (`noFixedAddressNow`). The daemon keeps asking AO Cloud for the fixed address afterwards, as before.
- **Daemon:** the address publisher records AO Cloud's 401 `unauthorized` refusal per account-token digest (`BridgeService.NoteAccountListing`). `GET /mobile/status` exposes it as `accountLinkRefused`. AO Cloud sends that same 401 for a missing listing and for a credential it doesn't accept, so the field claims only that AO Cloud refuses the link. An accepted publish clears it, and so does a new token.
- **Recheck after linking:** `POST /mobile/remote-access`, which the CLI and the desktop call right after linking, nudges the publisher to publish at once. A successful relink therefore clears the refusal without waiting out the backoff.
- **`ao remote-host status`:** with `accountLinkRefused`, it says AO Cloud refuses the machine's account link, so the account's devices may not list it, and suggests `ao remote-host link` again.
- Regenerated `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.

## Tests

AO review (codex `gpt-6-astra`, high) requested two changes, both addressed in 5a4c691324: report a refused link instead of an absent listing, and recheck right after linking.


- `TestRemoteHostLinkUsesTheQuickTunnelWhenAOCloudCannotMakeTheFixedAddress`: 409, 429 and 502 cases. With main's `remote_host_link.go`, the 429 and 502 cases fail and 409 passes.
- `TestRemoteHostCLISaysARefusedLinkMayNotBeListed`: fails on main, where status prints "devices list this machine".
- `TestStatusReportsAnAccountLinkAOCloudRefuses`: covers the refusal record. It needs the new API, so it does not compile on main.
- `TestAddressPublisherReportsARefusedLinkUntilALinkNudgesIt`: AO Cloud refuses, then accepts the same token and address after `StartRemoteAccess`. It fails if the nudge is removed. It also passes under `-race`.
- `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/daemon ./internal/httpd/...` passes, run with the `AO_*` session variables unset. Frontend `tsgo --noEmit` passes. golangci-lint is not installed locally, so CI runs it.

## Risks and follow-ups

- Until the publisher's first attempt (at most 30 s after a token appears), status still shows the old "Linked" line.
- A relink that skips remote access waits out the refusal backoff (1 min, doubling to 30 min). Both the CLI and the desktop call remote access after linking.
- The desktop's Connect Mobile UI still reads only `accountLinked`. Not changed here.
- Not tested live: the VM is set up for filming and was read only during triage.

## Why

An orchestrator's rail only had Browser, so its account could not be switched. When an orchestrator hit its 5-hour limit there was no way to move it to another account.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the orchestrator rail has only Browser](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/illegalcall/3d1124a49ae3b37efe00d99eb74df332/raw/orchestrator-rail-before.png) | ![After: the orchestrator rail opens on Summary with the account picker](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/illegalcall/3d1124a49ae3b37efe00d99eb74df332/raw/orchestrator-account-switch.gif) |

The recording opens the rail, picks another account, confirms "Stop and move", and ends on "Moved from work@example.com to personal@example.com".

Captured from the `dev:web` renderer with the e2e fake bridge and terminal mux. Accounts and the move are mocked with placeholder emails; the demo orchestrator fixture is shown as Claude Code. Before is from `main`.

title: Mobile New task fails with "model capabilities unavailable for model """ for a Standalone agent with the default model
body:
Reported by Prateek (relayed via the AO session standalone-39) on 2026-11-08 while filming the remote-machines launch video.

On the iPhone (new native mobile design, TestFlight): Workers → compose (New task) → machine **MacBook** → project **Standalone agent** → default model → send. A red error appeared: `Spawn: model capabilities unavailable for model "".` Picking **Opus 5.5** in the model menu didn't clear it. Switching the project to **agent-orchestrator** (same machine, same prompt) worked. Around 11:37:20 UTC.

Expected: a standalone task with the default model starts, as it does for a project.

Screenshot: `mobile-new-task-empty-model-error.png` (reporter's machine); recording `take4-work-across-part1.mov`, 0–35 s.

---

### Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-11-08 from main at 43599f1c88. The phone's build and the MacBook's AO version weren't checked; the MacBook was not accessible from this session, so its model catalog could not be read.

- The exact message (no `: catalog is stale` suffix) is produced only at `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:1778` (`%w for model %q`). Reaching it requires a non-empty effort, an empty model ID after `if modelID == "" { … item.IsDefault … }` (so the catalog had **no `IsDefault` entry**), and no listed model selected.
- The phone sends an effort even when no model is chosen. In `packages/mobile/app/spawn.tsx:184-196`, with no project detail (Standalone agent) and no catalog default, `effortModel` falls back to `defaultEffortModel()` (the first Opus with effort levels), `withFallbackEffort` checks Medium, and because that model names no `defaultEffort`, `chosenEffort` is sent while `model` stays `undefined` (`modelOverride(displayedModel, false)`).
- In a project the project config pins a worker model, so `displayedModel` is non-empty and a model is sent, which is consistent with agent-orchestrator working.
- For comparison, this Mac mini's (0.14.11-nightly.202611071807) Claude Code catalog (`GET /api/v1/agents/claude-code/models`) lists `opus` with `isDefault: true`, so the server resolves `""` → `opus` → Opus 5.5 and the same request would pass here. The failure needs a catalog with no default, as the MacBook's apparently had.
- Hypothesis, unconfirmed: why picking Opus 5.5 still failed. If the row picked was the default row (`__auto__`, `spawnModel.ts` `menuModels`), it sends no model either.

Related, not duplicates: #7024 (explicit models rejected by the Claude catalog check for custom providers), #5679 (Codex off-catalog model + effort), PR #7156 (lets the CLI validate a model when no effort is set; this case has an effort).

title: Remote access lockout refuses the correct password: requests with no password (any device on the same IP) count as failed attempts
body:
Reported by Prateek (relayed via the AO session standalone-39) on 2026-11-08 while filming the remote-machines launch video.

On the iPhone: Settings → connect manually to a Linux VM (`build-box`, v0.14.11-nightly.202611071807) through its quick tunnel (Host = the VM's trycloudflare address, Port 443, TLS on). The phone said: "Your machine locked this device out after too many failed attempts…", even though the password matched (checked on the VM). After waiting out the lockout, it connected with the bare hostname and Port 443. The error didn't make clear what had caused the lockout.

Expected: only real wrong-password attempts lock a device out, and the correct password isn't refused.

---

### Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-11-08 from main at 43599f1c88. Read-only: build-box itself was not contacted.

**Requests that carry no password at all count as failed attempts.** In `authMiddleware` (`backend/internal/httpd/auth.go:282-327`), every request except `GET /api/v1/identity` that doesn't present a valid token calls `lock.fail(src)`, including requests with no `Authorization` header. Five in a minute lock the source out for a minute, and each further failure extends the window. Through the tunnel, `src` is the visitor's `CF-Connecting-IP` (`clientSource`), so failures from **any device behind the same public IP** (other phones, desktops, or a browser) count against the phone too.

Reproduced with a throwaway test against `newAuthUnderTest("right", …)` (not committed): five tokenless GETs to `/`, `/favicon.ico`, `/apple-touch-icon.png`, `/apple-touch-icon-precomposed.png`, `/` from one `CF-Connecting-IP`, roughly what a browser makes when it opens the tunnel URL, each got 401. The next request from that IP **with the correct password** got **429**.

**Ruled out:** the host as typed (`https://<host>.trycloudflare.com:443`). `normalizeServerHost` strips the scheme but not `:443`, so the phone builds `https://<host>:443:443`, which fails before reaching the daemon and shows as unreachable, not as a lockout. That is filed separately. One manual Connect tap sends one authenticated request (`useManualConnect.ts` → `pingServer`), so a single correct-password tap cannot trip the lockout.

**Not determined:** which requests tripped it in this case (earlier mistyped attempts, a browser visit, or another device on the same network). There are no request logs for the tunnel listener; #6765 asks for that logging.

The phone's lockout copy (`packages/mobile/lib/connectionError.ts:209-219`) says "check the password, then try again", which points at the password even when it is right.

Related: draft PR #7285 (would count distinct wrong tokens, with a missing token counting once; it has no issue). PR #7645 (IPv6 /64 lockout keys). #6765 (log rejected LAN requests).

title: Mobile Connect manually: a Host with ":443" fails as unreachable, and Port cannot be left empty
body:
Reported by Prateek (relayed via the AO session standalone-39) on 2026-11-08.

In Settings → Connect manually on the iPhone, they entered the Host as `https://<host>.trycloudflare.com:443` (with Port 443, TLS on), and it didn't connect. It worked with the bare hostname. The form also wouldn't allow an empty Port, which was confusing when the address already said 443.

Expected: pasting a full address with its port works, or the form says what to change; Port can be left empty when the Host carries it or TLS implies 443.

---

### Agent-collected evidence

Main at 43599f1c88. `normalizeServerHost` (`packages/mobile/lib/endpoints.ts:18-23`) removes a scheme and trailing slashes but keeps `:443`, and `probeIdentity`/`pingServer` then build `https://<host>:443:443` (`connectRuntime.ts:100`), which fails client-side and is reported as unreachable against the Host field. `canConnect` requires `isValidPort(cfg.httpPort)` (`useManualConnect.ts:120-121`), so an empty Port blocks Connect.

Related: the lockout seen in the same session is filed separately (it is not caused by this; the malformed URL never reaches the daemon).

title: [Bug] AO Cloud Codex workers stuck at runtimeConnected: false — unable to start
body:
## Bug Description

I'm setting up an autonomous AI Software Factory using Orchestrator Cloud and Codex.

The Engineering Manager successfully creates worker sessions, but the workers never establish runtime connections and cannot execute assigned tasks.

This has happened in two consecutive attempts. Earlier Codex workers in the same project successfully completed planning and review tasks.

## Environment

- **Platform:** Orchestrator Cloud (AO Starter plan)
- **Project:** `outpick-leads-agent-lab`
- **Harness:** Codex
- **Worker model:** GPT-6.1-Sol Medium
- **Orchestrator model:** GPT-6.1-Sol High
- **Approval mode:** Session policy
- **Setup/Cleanup scripts:** Empty
- **Codex Cloud authentication:** Connected

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Orchestrator Cloud project.
2. Start an Engineering Manager session using Codex.
3. Ask the Engineering Manager to spawn one Codex worker with a simple read-only task.
4. Observe that `ao spawn` successfully creates the worker session.
5. Monitor the worker's runtime connection status.
6. The worker remains `status: working` and `runtimeConnected: false`, without executing the task.

## Expected Behavior

The worker should provision its cloud sandbox, start Codex, establish a runtime connection, receive its task instructions and return a response.

## Actual Behavior

- Worker session and branch are allocated successfully.
- Worker status remains `working`.
- `runtimeConnected` remains `false`.
- Worker never responds.
- Messages remain queued.
- No startup error is exposed.
- Worker must be manually terminated.

## Affected Sessions

**Attempt 1 — Worker Policy Verification**

Session ID: `4a0d4918-634b-482b-9844-44ebf85f0675`

- Worker created successfully.
- Runtime connection never established.
- Follow-up returned: `message queued (delivered when the child agent is ready)`.
- Manually terminated.

**Attempt 2 — Minimal Connectivity Test**

Session ID: `b239faa7-2c53-4bb9-9911-b78171ef5c72`

- Created November 8, 2026, approximately 11:55:40 UTC.
- Monitored until approximately 11:57:48 UTC.
- Runtime remained disconnected.
- Manually terminated after the two-minute monitoring window.

Both sessions subsequently reported `status: terminated` and `isTerminated: true`.

## Troubleshooting Already Performed

- Verified Codex is connected in Cloud Harness settings.
- Verified Worker and Orchestrator model configurations.
- Confirmed Setup and Cleanup scripts are empty.
- Confirmed the Engineering Manager can run successfully.
- Confirmed previous worker sessions completed planning and independent review tasks.
- Retried once with a minimal read-only task.
- No explicit authentication, provisioning or quota errors were available.

## Requested Investigation

Could you please inspect the backend logs for both session IDs and identify where initialization failed?

Specifically:

1. Did cloud sandbox provisioning complete successfully?
2. Did the Codex process start and authenticate?
3. Were worker instructions delivered?
4. Did the runtime connection handshake fail?
5. Were there any quota, resource, timeout or infrastructure errors?

Please identify the earliest failing stage and recommend the corrective action.

If possible, please also clarify why the sessions remained in `working` status despite never establishing runtime connections.

Please exclude credentials and tokens from any shared logs.

## Impact

This blocks autonomous worker delegation in the Software Factory. Planning and orchestration are functional, but coding and review workers cannot reliably start.

Thank you!

title: fix(chat): reduce repeated file lookups and historical turn rendering
body:
Code changes: +64 -7  
Tests: +195 -5  
Others: +3 -1

## What

Reduce repeated workspace-file lookup and historical-turn rendering during chat updates. Refs #7975, group A only. This PR leaves the tracking issue open for the remaining groups.

## Why

Parent updates repeatedly invalidate chat-link context. Inline code then rescans the workspace catalog, and freshly decoded but unchanged branch points also invalidate every turn's memo boundary.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Median synchronous stream-refresh work **153.75 ms**, trial medians 144.65 to 173.25 ms | **4.05 ms**, trial medians 3.75 to 5.20 ms |
| Chat and file-menu appearance | Pixel-identical captures with the live timer/working row masked equally; identical compiled CSS and message geometry |

Five alternating trials per revision, 20 stream updates per trial, production renderer fixture with 18 mounted turns, 108 inline references and 6,000 catalog paths. Driver Node 24.22.2; frozen bundles built with Node 25.9.0 under the same production configuration. Chromium 148.0.7778.96, macOS arm64, Apple M5, 1440×1000. This was a heavily loaded host, initially load average 50.75 on 10 logical cores. These are fixture timings, not installed-desktop/session-switch latency. Every run preserved final text and the latest file-opening callback, with zero page/request failures. Render counts, frame gaps, typing samples and raw trials are in the evidence bundle.

Local evidence, available from [the AO worker session](ao://sessions/agent-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator-47):

- Report: `/Users/ronish/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-47/chat-render-cost.html`
- Captures: `before-chat.png`, `after-chat.png`, `before-menu.png`, `after-menu.png` in that directory.
- Recordings: `before.webm` and `after.webm` in that directory, covering streaming, width changes, scrolling, the file menu and draft editing.

These files are local artifacts; screenshots/recordings are not uploaded to GitHub.

## How

- Cache InlineCode/FileReference lookup hits and misses per immutable file catalog, capped at 1,024 references. Keep the existing matching and ambiguity rules; replace the cache when the catalog changes.
- Index the catalog by exact path and basename on the first file reference, so opening a session with a large workspace no longer scans every path per reference. Matching and ambiguity rules are unchanged.
- Reuse link-context callback identities through the existing latest-callback hook, while updating handlers and capability availability correctly.
- Reuse structurally unchanged branch-point data so historical TurnGroups retain their memo boundary. Necessary geometry and live-content updates continue.
- Add an opt-in production renderer benchmark. Correct the existing history assertion for windowed rendering. Cover catalog replacement, current handlers, capability removal, branch updates, and question resolution using independent snapshots.

No CSS, animation, hover fade, preview delay, scroll scheduling, preload or session-retention change.

## Testing

- Full Node 24 frontend suite: **12,169 passed, 39 skipped**; one unchanged startup import hook timed out. Rerunning its complete file passed **83/83**.
- Frontend and E2E TypeScript checks passed.
- Renderer smoke at the expected port: **144/153 passed** initially; **8/9** failed cases passed in an isolated rerun. The remaining selection-contrast check reproduces on the original `43599f1c88` sources with the identical ratio **1.077189186501969**, below its 1.5 threshold. Selection succeeds. No color or threshold workaround was made.
- Production benchmark and 250-turn history checks passed; separate five-pair timing, render-count and typing trials completed.
- Native build-script checks: **19 passed**; CI sharding checks: **5 passed**.
- `npm run build` passed. The first attempt stopped at the ncurses mirror checksum mismatch; the GNU archive matched the existing pinned SHA-256 exactly and was cached before retry. No build script or checksum changed.
- Local all-workflow validation could not run: missing build variables and Docker daemon unavailable. Remote frontend checks, TypeScript checks, both full unit shards and renderer smoke passed. Full packaged-desktop timing and the 8–10-live-session/many-tab scenario are not measured by this PR.

Reproduce the production fixture:

```sh
cd frontend
AO_PERF_PRODUCTION=1 AO_PERF_BENCH=1 AO_E2E_PORT=5497 \
  npm run test:e2e -- chat-performance --grep chatRenderCost --repeat-each=5 --workers=1
```

title: fix: preserve orchestrator through settings saves and replacement recovery
body:
Code changes: +76 -25\
Tests: +174 -21\
Others: +33 -8 (generated sqlc)

## What

Keep a running orchestrator when saving worker settings, stop the old Chat controller before retiring it for a replacement, and allow an untouched replacement branch to recover when its provider never persisted the reserved conversation ID. No UI design changes.

## Why

In the reported incident, the running orchestrator was Codex while the project default still named Claude Code. Saving project settings compared those two values and started a clean replacement even though the orchestrator setting had not changed. The retired controller could continue projecting into the newly bound project conversation. After a restart, the replacement had inherited project history but no provider transcript; the recovery proof only accepted an empty root, so it returned `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED` instead of starting its untouched branch fresh.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A worker-only settings save can retire a running orchestrator whose provider differs from the saved project default. | Only an explicit orchestrator default change or a retry of a failed replacement starts a replacement. |
| The old Chat controller can write after project history is rebound to its replacement. | Retirement waits for the old Chat controller to stop; a stop failure leaves the old session and workspace intact. |
| An untouched replacement with inherited project history and a missing provider transcript fails to resume. | Its unused child branch can start a fresh provider conversation; the session and branch IDs change atomically while earlier history stays intact. |
| A branch with recorded provider work must not discard that work. | Fresh recovery still fails closed when the active branch has turns, messages, activities, or raw provider events. |

## How

- Remove the saved-default-versus-running-provider mismatch trigger from project settings saves.
- Drain Chat before `RetireForReplacement` terminates the old session or releases its workspace.
- Check activity on the active replacement branch, rather than the project conversation's global sequence, and enforce the same proof in the SQLite provider-ID swap.
- Regenerate sqlc output from the query source.

## Testing

- Passed: focused replacement, retirement, and resume Go regressions; `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./internal/session_manager ./internal/storage/sqlite/store`; `go build ./...`; `go vet ./...`; scoped pinned golangci-lint; `npm run sqlc`; frontend typecheck; all 56 `ProjectSettingsForm` tests; `git diff --check`.
- Full local Go suite: changed packages and `service/chat` passed. The run failed in unrelated Git-config, locally installed OpenCode, tmux, CLI/observer, shell terminal, and terminal tests.
- Full local frontend suite: 12,184 passed, three failed outside this change. The two `GlobalSettingsForm` failures passed on direct rerun; `useSessionWorkspaceFiles.network` still observed 14 requests where its test expects 13.
- Desktop packaging stopped before packaging: the ncurses 6.5 archive from `invisible-mirror.net` failed its expected SHA-256 check. `agent-ci --all` could not run because the Docker socket is unavailable here.
- Remote PR checks: all required jobs passed, including backend core, chat and SQLite race suites, frontend typecheck, renderer smoke, both Vitest shards, lint, and generated-code drift checks.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from current `main`; one focused incident fix
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After describes observable behavior; no visual change
- [x] Regression tests cover the failure and fail-closed cases
- [x] Remote CI checks pass

title: fix(mobile): follow account machine renames without a re-sign-in
body:
Code changes: +17 -6\ Tests: +51 -4\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The phone now picks up machine renames made on the account (for example on the desktop) on its next account sync, without signing out and back in. A name set on the phone still sticks. ## Why Fixes #7983. Account sync kept the stored name over the account's label for every machine the phone already had (`name: existing?.name ?? item.label`), so the first label a phone saw stuck forever. A label-only change also hit the "routes are current" early return and never reached the save. Signing out cleared account machines, so the next sync seeded the current labels, which was the only workaround. ## Before / After Same lab on both platforms: a signed-in phone with two account machines, first listed as `mac-mini` and `MacBook`, then renamed on the account. | Before (main) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | |
Account renamed to "Prateek's Mac mini" / "Prateek's MacBook Air". After a sync and a cold start, iOS and Android still show `mac-mini` / `MacBook` |
Same phones updated to this build: the first sync adopts the account's names, with no sign-out | | A rename on the account while the app is open never shows |
Renamed to "Studio Mac mini" / "MacBook Air (work)" with the app open: updates on the next 30 s sync, with no relaunch | | A name chosen on the phone is kept |
Still kept: the MacBook renamed on the phone ("Desk laptop" on iOS, "Travel laptop" on Android) survives the account renaming it to "Prateek's MacBook Pro", while the Mac mini follows the account to "Office Mac mini" | ## How - `Host` gains `accountLabel`: the account's label at the last sync. While `name` still equals it, the name follows the account. A rename on the phone makes them differ, and the phone's name is kept. Renaming it back to the account's name hands it back to the account. - The early return for unchanged routes now also requires the name and `accountLabel` to be current. A label-only change keeps the saved endpoints (the routes a connect merged in), so it doesn't reintroduce the route reset the early return exists to prevent. - An empty or whitespace label never replaces a name. - **Migration trade-off for reviewers:** machines saved before this change have no `accountLabel`, so a stale copied name can't be told apart from a name chosen on the phone. They adopt the account's label once. This fixes phones that are already stuck, like the one in the report. The cost is that a rename made on the phone for an *account* machine before this update is reset once; after that, phone renames stick. ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 360 files, 3493 tests pass. New cases in `accountHosts.test.ts`: a label-only rename updates and keeps connected routes and the icon; a phone rename survives later renames on the account; a legacy machine adopts the label once; an empty label keeps the name. Existing tests are adjusted for the tracked label. - `npm run typecheck` (tsgo) and `tsc --noEmit` pass. - Tested on an iOS 26.5 simulator (Debug build) and an Android 15 emulator (debug APK), both running this branch's JS from one Metro, against: - a fake AO Cloud `/me/hosts` and token endpoint on loopback; - a scratch daemon listed as one real, connected account machine, plus one offline machine. "Before" ran `main`'s `accountHosts.ts`/`hosts.ts`, and I checked the device bundles for a marker before trusting each run. A temporary lab route seeded the signed-in session; it isn't in this PR. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): recognize Claude's current usage-limit refusals and their reset time
body:
## Summary

Usage-limit auto-resume stopped working for Claude chats because Claude Code changed the wording of its quota refusal. It now says:

```
You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 6:20pm (Asia/Calcutta)
```

The usage-limit regex only accepted `session`, `weekly`, `daily`, `usage` or `individual spend` before `limit`. So these refusals were stored as ordinary failures: the generic "The agent ran into a problem" block, no usage-limit notice, no auto-resume, and the refusals were reported to Sentry as faults. In a real `ao.db`, every Claude limit since 2026-10-29 (17 turns) missed. So did 16 `You've hit your org's monthly spend limit` refusals.

## Approach

Detection now follows the upstream components rather than AO's own pattern list.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Is this a usage limit? | AO's hand-written regex | `USAGE_LIMIT_ERROR_PREFIXES` from `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.232, the same list `claude-agent-acp` 0.70 uses to mark a refusal as a usage limit |
| Reset time | Clock parsed from the refusal text (minute precision; cannot read `resets Nov 14, 5am`) | The SDK's structured `rate_limit_info.resetsAt`, forwarded by `claude-agent-acp` as `usage_update._meta["_claude/rateLimit"]`. The text parse remains a fallback. |

Rules for the structured reset:
- A window counts only while its `status` is `rejected` and overage is not allowed (`overageStatus` allowed/allowed_warning, `isUsingOverage` or `overageInUse` cancel it).
- `allowed` and `allowed_warning` clear a window.
- Expired windows drop out, and resets beyond 31 days count as unknown.
- The turn resumes at the latest reset, and only when every rejected window has one.

Why the text fallback stays: `claude-agent-acp` forwards `rate_limit_event` only after a usage update in the same prompt, and the CLI throttles unchanged frames. 5 of the 17 real limited turns had no structured frame at all, but all 17 carry the reset in their text.

The structured reset travels on the turn-completed event (`ChatEvent.UsageLimitResetsAt`), and the turn settle writes it to `conversation_turns.usage_limit_resets_at`. That column already takes precedence over the reset read from the text. Codex does the same with its rate-limit notification, so neither driver adds text to the provider's message any more: no `Resets at <ISO>` line for Claude, no `Usage limit exceeded; resets <ISO>` line for Codex. Old rows that contain those lines still parse.

## What the chat shows

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Timeline row | "Usage limit reached" + provider text + our reset line | "Usage limit reached" marker + the provider's sentence, word for word |
| Above the composer | Gauge, title, countdown, "Resets …" sentence, buttons | Controls only, on one line: `Auto-resume at reset`, or `Auto-resume is scheduled.` + `Cancel auto-resume`, or `Resume` |

The eight `chat.usageLimit.*` strings this leaves unused are removed from every locale.

## Evidence

- **Real data:** I ran the new classifier over all 162 failed turns in a real `ao.db`. All 17 `5-hour limit` refusals and 16 org spend-limit refusals are now usage limits, with resets matching the text (`6:20pm` → `12:50Z`, `5am` → `23:30Z`). No other failure is newly matched, and the Codex refusals are unchanged.
- **Real daemon (`backend/e2e`):** the fake Claude now sends `claude-agent-acp` 0.70's wire format: a rejected `_claude/rateLimit` usage update, then `You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets <clock> (Asia/Calcutta)`.
  - On main: `native quota did not become durable failure … State:failed … UsageLimit:<nil>`.
  - On this branch: `claude-code: … exactly one native retry at 13:00:06.95Z (reset 13:00:06Z)`. The reset has second precision, so it came from the structured value.
- **Real desktop app (final head `0b30a88230`):** a real Claude CLI on the device login, through a local proxy that answers with HTTP 429 and the unified rate-limit headers.
  - 5-hour limit: the stored `error_message` is exactly `You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 4:44pm (Asia/Calcutta)`. `usage_limit_resets_at` is `11:14:00Z`, and auto-resume finished 4.3 s after the reset with "pong".
  - Weekly limit three days out: Claude wrote `resets Nov 12 at 4:46pm (Asia/Calcutta)`, which the text parser cannot read. Before any click, the row already had `usage_limit_resets_at = 2026-11-12 11:16:00Z` and `auto_resume = 0`, and the composer offered `Auto-resume at reset`.
- **Mutation checks:** emptying the prefix list fails the domain cases, and removing the structured-reset hook fails the new `structured reset` wire case, and dropping the column write fails the Codex case of `TestUsageLimitRecoveryAcrossProviders`.

## Tests

`go test` passes for `internal/domain`, `internal/ports`, `adapters/chatdriver/{acp,claudeacp,codexappserver}`, `service/chat`, `storage/sqlite/store`, and `e2e -run UsageLimit`. Frontend: `UsageLimitNotice.test.tsx`, the i18n tests, and `e2e/chat-usage-limit.spec.ts` (8/8, both providers, including the 390 px cases) pass.

## Risks / follow-ups

- The prefix list is a copy of the SDK constant, so it needs updating when the SDK adds prefixes.
- A weekly limit whose turn received no structured frame (a chat refused on its very first turn) still has an unknown reset, because its dated text is not parsed. It shows `Resume` only.
- The Codex frame is covered by driver and service tests, not by a recorded run.

title: fix(chat): keep typing during an account move
body:
## Summary

Switching a chat's Claude account made the composer inert for the whole move, and the controller refused sends, so whatever you typed was lost and had to be typed again afterwards.

- Once the old agent has stopped, a send is stored as a queued turn. This is the same path a starting or hibernated chat uses (`queueWithoutController`). The store accepts it only while an account move is between `source_stopped` and `activating`.
- Before `source_stopped` (preflight, draining, stopping) nothing changes: the composer stays locked and the backend refuses a send at once, so nothing reaches the old account. A drain-policy move can sit in `draining` for minutes while the running turn finishes.
- The new agent's `Start` keeps that queued turn instead of settling it as orphaned work, the same way a wake does. This covers a rollback restart of the old agent too.
- The queue is drained when the move completes or rolls back.
- From `source_stopped` on, the composer is editable and hides Stop, since no agent is running.
- The inspector times "Switching account" from when the move started, not from the session's last activity (it showed "3h ago").

## Evidence

Real desktop app, real Claude Code on two accounts (team → personal), isolated lab data. The script types a message and presses Enter about 2 s into the move.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Composer during the move | inert, aria-disabled; typing lost | editable; Enter shows "1 Queued Message" |
| Message typed mid-move | never sent; retyped after the move | queued at `target_starting`, ran on the new account 4 ms after the move committed |
| Click → answer | 10.3 s (with retyping) | 7.6 s |

The move itself is unchanged (3.5–4.4 s in the lab).

## Tests

- `TestSendDuringAccountMoveQueuesForTheNewAgent`: a send after the old agent stopped is queued, and starting the new agent keeps it.
- `TestSendWhileAccountMoveDrainsIsRefusedWithoutQueueing`: a send during `draining` is refused at once and queues nothing.
- `useSessionInterfaceSwitch` test: the composer opens for `source_stopped` and `target_starting`, not for `draining` or `source_stopping`.
- `go vet` on the touched packages is clean. The test suite runs in CI.

## Risks

- A move that ends in `recovery_required` does not deliver the queued message: the next ordinary start settles it as failed, with its text kept in the timeline.

title: fix(chat): ask for a sign-in when a resume is refused, and sign in the session's own account
body:
## Summary

Three problems hit when a Claude login expired on an older session:

1. **Raw error instead of a sign-in prompt.** Opening the chat ran a resume. The persistent ACP host wraps the refused login, so the error chain was `ErrChatDriverUnavailable` → `ErrAgentAuthRequired`. `mapSessionError` checked the driver/recovery sentinels first, so the user saw `CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE` with "chat driver unavailable: persistent ACP host: agent requires authentication". A refused launch also has no chat controller, so nothing recorded the chat's login demand and the "Log in again" bar never appeared.
   - For a resume (`RelaunchError`), the auth sentinels now map before the driver/recovery ones, so it returns `AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED`. A refused chat spawn keeps `CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE` and its terminal fallback.
   - A chat start refused for its login calls the new `Store.RequireSessionLogin`, which sets the same demand a refused turn sets (`ConversationAccount.RequireLogin`, shared with the controller) and records which refusal it was. A pending demand is left untouched. No demand is raised while an account move launches on its target account. The existing `ConfirmConversationLogin` clears the demand once a reading shows the account is signed in.
   - The bar has no close button. For a local Claude Code or Codex session, the stopped-agent banner (Resume agent, Open shell) is hidden while the bar shows: neither action can fix a login, and an account reading clears the request once the login works, after which Resume agent returns. While the agent is stopped for it, the composer says "Log in to continue" instead of "The controller is not connected". Other harnesses, remote hosts and cloud sessions keep that banner, since resuming is how they find out the login works. Open shell stays on the session's terminal button.
   - `RedactError` keeps `errors.Is` matching, so a refusal whose text contains a project env value still maps to a sign-in.
   - Reading a chat that waits for a sign-in no longer takes the writer lock unless a verified turn can clear the demand.
2. **"Log in again" signed in the wrong login.** The bar always started this computer's CLI login. It now sends the session's bound account: a saved account starts its sign-in in its own folder (`POST /agents/accounts/{id}/login`), and this computer's login starts the CLI sign-in from its row once that row can. The button waits until it knows the session's account. Sessions on a remote host or in the cloud keep the existing flow. The request travels as `accountLogin` in the ui-store, and `AgentAccountsPanel` takes it once the row has loaded; closing settings drops it.
3. **Removing an account looked stuck.** Removal stops the account's agents first, one at a time, and the dialog locks while it runs. `ExitAgentsOnAccount` now stops them concurrently, and the confirm button reads "Removing…" while the request runs (all 9 locales).

## Screenshots

Desktop app in a lab, real Claude Code, same steps on main (`8912917478`) and on this PR. The email of this computer's own login is replaced with you@example.com.

| | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Opening an older chat whose account's login expired | ![Before: raw driver error, no sign-in bar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca60687a-e766-4a8d-8ccf-52f1aac8e325) | ![After: only the Log in again bar, and the composer says Log in to continue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1fb6bc7-00ac-40c7-b940-0fd09c2c3666) |
| "Log in again" on a chat that runs on the saved account lab-expired | ![Before: the CLI's own sign-in method picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31403989-10ca-4bf8-a452-8c46de7441da) | ![After: lab-expired's sign-in terminal in the accounts list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bd3a787-83ee-4aba-abf6-4b3696d96275) |
| Removing an account that runs 2 busy chats, 1.2 s after confirming | ![Before: Remove account greyed out, no progress](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2cb52d4-d3c2-4b43-adf0-b52387c24152) | ![After: Removing…](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2efab4dc-b76c-4dd7-9a17-930698219960) |

- Resume: main shows the raw `chat driver unavailable: persistent ACP host: agent requires authentication` and no bar. This PR shows only the sign-in bar, and the composer says "Log in to continue"; the daemon itself records the demand from the refused resume. This shot is from `bc3cccdb81`; the other two are from `00d60ee700`.
- Log in again: main shows no bar for a refused resume, so that shot records the demand by hand. Its click opens the CLI's own sign-in and sends no request for the session's account. This PR sends `POST /api/v1/agents/accounts/lab-expired/login` (202 in the daemon log), and the sign-in opens in that account's folder.
- Remove: main keeps "Remove account" greyed out for 5.2 s. This PR says "Removing…" and finishes in 3.2 s.

## Evidence (daemon-only lab, real Claude, before/after binaries)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Resume of a chat whose login is refused | 409 `CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE`, raw driver message, no demand recorded | 409 `AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED`, `account_json.authenticationState = "required"` with `reauthRequiredAt` |
| After signing in again + account refresh | n/a | demand cleared, resume → 200 |
| Remove an account running 4 busy chats | 9.15 s | 5.55 s |

## Tests

- Go: `mapSessionError` cases for a resume refused for its login (`AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED`) and a spawn refused for its login (`CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE`); `TestResumeChatRefusedLoginAsksForSignIn` (refused login records a demand with its own reason, a Codex-style refusal records the chat reason, an account move and provider down record none); `TestLaunchRefusalRaisesTheChatLoginDemand` (demand set, plan kept, a repeat refusal keeps the same failure ID, reading the chat while the writer is held returns, login check clears it, a later refusal raises a new demand, unknown session is a no-op); `RedactError` hides the value and keeps the sentinel.
- Frontend: `ReauthBanner` passes the bound account (saved or this computer's), waits for it, and has only Log in again; `ChatWorkspace` hides Resume agent and says "Log in to continue" in the composer while a Codex login is refused, keeps Resume for opencode, and shows it again once the login works; `AgentAccountsPanel` starts a requested sign-in exactly once, signs this computer's login in through the CLI once it can, and clears the request; closing settings drops it; the remove dialog shows "Removing…" until the DELETE resolves.

## Risks / follow-ups

- #7769 reworks the refused-login band and touches `ChatStatusBanners`, `AgentAccountsSection`, `ui-store` and the i18n files, so whichever lands second will need a rebase.
