title: fix(mobile): accept host:port and an empty Port in Connect manually (#7981)
body:
Code changes: +87 -17\
Tests: +97 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Mobile **Connect manually** now accepts a Host that carries its own port (`example.com:443`, `https://example.com:443/`, `[::1]:8080`), and the Port field can be left empty. The Port falls back to the port in the Host, or to 443 when Use TLS is on. If the Host and Port disagree, the form says so instead of failing as "unreachable".

## Why

Fixes #7981

**Root cause:** `normalizeServerHost` (`lib/endpoints.ts`) removes the scheme and trailing slashes but keeps `:443`. The probe and ping then append the Port, so they build `https://host:443:443`. That URL fails on the phone before any request is sent, and the form reported it as an unreachable host. Separately, `canConnect` required a valid Port, so an empty Port blocked Connect even when the Host already said 443.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Host `https://x.trycloudflare.com:443`, Port `443`, TLS on → "unreachable" (URL `https://x…:443:443`) | Connects to `https://x.trycloudflare.com:443` |
| Host `x.trycloudflare.com:443`, Port empty → Connect disabled | Connects on 443 |
| Host `x.trycloudflare.com`, Port empty, TLS on → Connect disabled | Connects on 443 |
| Host `x:443`, Port `3011` → `x:443:3011`, "unreachable" | Error: "The host says port 443 but Port is 3011. Make them match, or clear one." |
| Host `https://x`, TLS off → silently connected over plain `http://` | Error: "The host starts with https://. Turn on Use TLS, or remove https://." |
| Host `192.168.1.42`, Port empty, TLS off → Connect disabled | Still disabled; the hint now asks for "a port (or turn on Use TLS for 443)" |

No screenshots: I did not run this on a device or simulator (see Testing).

## How

- New pure helper `resolveManualAddress(host, port, secure)` in `lib/connectionFields.ts`. It removes the scheme and trailing slashes and splits `host:port` and `[ipv6]:port`. A bare IPv6 address with no port is left as typed, as before. The port comes from the Port field, else the port in the Host, else 443 if TLS is on. It returns either the resolved address, an "incomplete" state (blocks Connect without an error), or an error message.
- `manualAddressError` turns that result into the form's error. Forms keep their existing `portError` prop, so the iOS and Android form components are unchanged.
- The same helper is used by `useManualConnect` (Connect and its hint), `useMachineEditor` / `canSaveDraft` (machine editor), and `persistManualHostEdit` (the save path), so all of them agree.

**Behaviour changes for reviewers:**
1. **`https://` with Use TLS off now shows an error** instead of silently using http (and `http://` with TLS on errors the same way). I chose an error over flipping the toggle automatically, so what's on screen matches what gets saved.
2. **Edit connection and the machine editor now follow the same rules**, including allowing an empty Port when the Host has a port or TLS is on, and the host/port conflict error.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` in `packages/mobile`: passes.
- `npm test` in `packages/mobile` (full suite): 364 files, 3523 tests, all pass.
- New `lib/connectionFields.test.ts` covers a plain host and port, `host:443` with an empty Port, `scheme://host:port` with and without a trailing slash, IPv6 with and without a port, an empty Port with no port in the Host (TLS on and off), conflicting ports, invalid ports, and a scheme that contradicts TLS.
- `lib/manualConnect.test.ts` adds save-path cases (a pasted `https://host:443` is saved as host + 443; conflicting ports are refused before probing). `lib/environmentEditor.test.ts` adds `canSaveDraft` cases.
- The mobile package has no lint script, and mobile CI (`.github/workflows/mobile.yml`) runs only typecheck and tests.
- **Not tested on a device or simulator.**

title: fix(mobile): send no stand-in effort for a default-model new task (#7979)
body:
Code changes: +21 -5\
Tests: +43 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Stop the mobile New task composer from sending a stand-in model's fallback effort when no model is picked.

## Why

Fixes #7979

With **Standalone agent** + **Default model**, and a model catalog that marks no model as the default, New task failed with `model capabilities unavailable for model ""`.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Request sent `model: undefined, effort: "medium"`; the daemon rejected it with `model capabilities unavailable for model ""` | Request sends neither `model` nor `effort`; the provider's default model and effort apply and the task starts |

No screenshot: the visible composer is unchanged; only the request payload differs.

## How

- When nothing is picked and the catalog names no default, `spawn.tsx` borrows a stand-in model (`defaultEffortModel()`) so the effort gauge has levels to show, and checks a fallback level (Medium). The `chosenEffort` check counted that fallback as a real choice because the stand-in has no `defaultEffort`, so an effort went out without a model.
- The "which effort to send" rule is now a pure helper, `spawnEffortToSend` in `packages/mobile/lib/modelEffort.ts`, which never sends the stand-in's fallback.
- Unchanged: a level the user taps still pins the stand-in as the model (`selectEffort`) and is sent; the fallback is still sent for a real model with no default; a model's own default is still left to the model.
- No daemon change: `resolveAgentConfig` correctly rejects an effort it has no model to validate against.

## Testing

- New `modelEffort.test.ts` cases: untouched gauge on the stand-in (no effort), tapped level on the stand-in (sent), fallback on a real model with no default (sent), model's own default (not sent), model with no effort levels (none).

title: fix(mobile): keep the chat's clear glass bar to iOS 27, the stack's bar elsewhere
body:
Code changes: +9 -6\
Tests: +10 -0\

## What

The chat screen's clear glass header is now limited to iOS 27 and later. Every other iOS version, iOS 26 included, gets the stack's own header, the same one terminal sessions already use on iOS 26. The conversation starts below that header instead of scrolling under it.

## Why

On iOS 26 the system's soft scroll-edge blur under the clear bar reached only the status bar over the conversation. The title and subtitle sat over sharp message text, which looked clipped and masked. iOS 27's edge blur covers the whole bar, so it keeps the glass header.

| iOS 26: messages scroll under a clear bar, blurred only under the status bar; title and subtitle overlap sharp text | iOS 26: the stack's own header, page-coloured, as on terminal sessions; the conversation starts below it |

Screenshots still needed: the iOS 26 "before" from the reported device, and an iOS 26 "after" from a device or simulator running this branch. I could not capture either here (no iOS Simulator in this environment).

- `CLEAR_HEADER` in `lib/chat/ChatSessionScreen.tsx` now requires iOS 27 or later on iOS (`SYSTEM_GLASS_HEADER && Platform.Version >= 27`); Android is unchanged.
- With `CLEAR_HEADER` off, the screen takes the existing solid-bar path that iOS 18 and earlier already used: no transparent header, no header overlap or inset, banners inline.

title: fix(scm): stop reporting cancelled checks as CI failing
body:
Code changes: +72 -17\
Tests: +195 -3\
Others: +26 -3 (doc comments, locale strings)

## What

A cancelled CI check no longer counts as a failure, on GitHub or GitLab. A PR whose runs were cancelled by a new push or a PR body edit shows "Checks pending" while the replacements run. A run cancelled by hand with nothing replacing it settles as "Checks cancelled" instead of spinning or reading as failing.

## Why

GitHub's status rollup counts a cancelled check run as `FAILURE`, and `ciSummaryFromGraphQL` mapped `PRCheckCancelled` to `CIFailing` alongside `PRCheckFailed`. On #7964, head `4b9668bf59` showed "CI failing" while the replacement runs were still in progress and no check had failed. GitLab's `pipelineStatusToCI` had the same `canceled -> failing` mapping.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Runs cancelled by a PR body edit or new push, replacements still running: "CI failing" | "Checks pending" |
| Run cancelled by hand, nothing replaced it: "CI failing" | "Checks cancelled", settled, no loading animation; PR is not merge-ready |
| Run cancelled, every other check passed: "CI failing" | "Checks cancelled"; not reported as passing |
| One job failed, another cancelled: "CI failing", `failingChecks` lists both | "CI failing", `failingChecks` lists only the failed job |
| GitLab pipeline `canceled`, no failed jobs: `failing` | `unknown`, shown as "Checks cancelled" |
| GitLab pipeline `canceled`, a required job already `failed`: `failing` | Still `failing` |

The board's "CI failing" status and the `ci_failing` merge blocker follow the CI state, so they disappear for cancelled-only PRs too.

## How

- `ciSummaryFromGraphQL`: cancelled no longer short-circuits to failing. Pending wins if anything is still running. With nothing running, a cancelled check resolves to `CIUnknown` even beside passing checks, because it proved nothing and `unknown` already blocks merge readiness. Documented in `github/doc.go`.
- `scmCISummary` falls back to GitHub's rollup state, which stays `FAILURE` for cancelled runs. Fixing the mapping alone still showed failing, so the fallback now trusts the per-check verdict when a cancelled check explains the rollup's `FAILURE`.
- Cancelled checks are dropped from `FailedChecks`, failure fingerprints, log-tail fetches, and stored-tail reuse (`isFailingCheckStatus` in both providers, `observer.go`).
- `summarizeCI` lists cancelled checks under `failingChecks` only when the CI state is `unknown`, so the renderer can tell "cancelled, settled" apart from "still loading". No API shape change: `failingChecks[].status` already allows `cancelled`.
- `pr-display.ts` adds a "Checks cancelled" row and readiness label for that case. Two new i18n keys, in English in every locale, matching how `pr.card.checksUnavailable` was added.
- GitLab: `canceled` pipeline maps to `unknown`, except when a required job already failed, which stays `failing`.
- Agent CI-failure messages already skipped cancelled checks (`failedPRChecks` in `lifecycle/reactions.go`), so no false notification was sent; the user-visible symptom was the board and card status.

Known limit: a PR with more than 100 checks still shows failing when the rollup says `FAILURE`, because AO cannot see every check to rule out a real failure.

## Testing

Unit tests added, written from the neighbouring tests. Not run locally; CI verifies.

- `github/provider_test.go`: `TestCISummaryCancelledChecksAreNotFailures` (replacement running, other check running, cancelled by hand, cancelled beside passing, cancelled plus real failure), and the `TestObserve_CIStates` case updated to `unknown`.
- `gitlab/provider_test.go`: `TestFetchPullRequests_CanceledPipeline`, and `TestPipelineStatusToCI` updated.
- `service/session/service_test.go`: `TestListPRSummariesListsCancelledChecksOnlyWhenCIUnknown`.
- `pr-display.test.ts`: cancelled-with-no-replacement shows as settled.

Manual steps on a throwaway PR: edit the PR body while CI runs and expect pending, not failing; cancel all runs by hand and expect "Checks cancelled" with no spinner; re-run and expect pending then passing; fail one job and cancel another and expect only the failed job listed.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; related to #7964 but separate from it
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; the UI change is a status label, no screenshot captured
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (pending)

title: fix(desktop): make link hover cards settle and compact
body:
Code changes: +576 -196\
Tests: +779 -45\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Link hover cards now always settle, and they are much smaller. Every hover ends in content or a one-line fallback showing where the link goes, within about 3 seconds. Favicons follow the app theme. GitHub PR links and text artifact links that stay on screen load their card data ahead of the hover, so those cards open with content.

Link navigation is unchanged.

## Why

Hover previews showed skeletons that never resolved, took up to 8 seconds, or showed nothing at all. Causes found:

- A failed preview rendered no card. A hung page showed a skeleton for 8.3 s and then vanished.
- The shared daemon fetch ran under the first hover's request, so leaving a link cached a 502 on a healthy page for 2 minutes and failed anyone waiting on it.
- The daemon read up to 2 MiB of each page instead of stopping after the head.
- Hovers were never cancelled, so 8 outstanding previews held the renderer's daemon connections and pushed an unrelated read from 10 ms to 7.9 s.
- `ao://` links from a remote host with no running query, or from a signed-out Cloud source, stayed loading forever.
- Focus returning to a clicked link could open a card.
- Dark favicons disappeared on dark cards.
- A cold PR card waited on the daemon's GitHub fetch (1.7 to 4.8 s observed), and an artifact card read its file only after the hover began.

## Before / After

Crops are from the real desktop app, with the original frontend and this branch run against the same chat.

**Dark**

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub PR card | ![Before: rich](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-dark-rich.png) | ![After: rich](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-dark-rich.png) |

| Title-only card, favicon from a host without CORS | ![Before: plate](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-dark-plate.png) | ![After: plate](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-dark-plate.png) |
| Loading, 1 s in | ![Before: loading](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-dark-loading.png) | ![After: loading](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-dark-loading.png) |
| Hung page, 4.3 s in (before: still a skeleton; after: fallback) | ![Before: fallback](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-dark-fallback.png) | ![After: fallback](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-dark-fallback.png) |
| `ao://` session link | ![Before: session](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-dark-session.png) | ![After: session](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-dark-session.png) |

**Light**

| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub PR card | ![Before: rich](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-light-rich.png) | ![After: rich](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-light-rich.png) |
| Docs page with image | ![Before: image](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-light-image.png) | ![After: image](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-light-image.png) |
| Title-only card, favicon from a host without CORS | ![Before: plate](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-light-plate.png) | ![After: plate](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-light-plate.png) |
| Loading, 1 s in | ![Before: loading](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-light-loading.png) | ![After: loading](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-light-loading.png) |
| Hung page, 4.3 s in (before: still a skeleton; after: fallback) | ![Before: fallback](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-light-fallback.png) | ![After: fallback](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-light-fallback.png) |
| `ao://` session link | ![Before: session](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/before-light-session.png) | ![After: session](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/6d8191be786c0b57958f92a7374bff5d/raw/after-light-session.png) |

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hung page | Skeleton, gone at 8.3 s | Fallback at 3.3 s |
| Slow page, content at 6 s | Skeleton until 6.3 s | Fallback at 3.3 s, upgrades in place |
| Page with instant head, 5 s body | 5.3 s | 332 ms |
| Upstream 403 or 500 | No card | Fallback at about 335 ms |
| Abandoned hover on a healthy URL | 502 for 2 minutes | 200 on the next hover |
| Recovery after a failed fetch | 2 minutes | 30 seconds |
| Unrelated daemon read during 8 stuck hovers | 7,889 ms | 3 ms |
| First hover on a PR link already on screen | Skeleton, then content after the GitHub fetch | Content when the card opens (323 ms, the 300 ms hover delay), no request on hover |

## How

- **Daemon:** the shared fetch is detached from callers and bounded by its own 8 s timeout, so a hover ending only cancels that hover's wait and the fetch still warms the cache. It stops reading at `</head`. URL fragments share one cache entry. Because the fetch now runs outside the HTTP server's recover, a panic is reported and returned as an ordinary fetch failure.
- **`useLinkPreview`:** uses a `QueryObserver` on the shared client, so the last hover leaving aborts the request. A 3 s settle timer flips to the fallback, and a late response upgrades the card. The client-side 502 cache is gone because the daemon owns the failure window.
- **Cards:** `LinkPreviewHoverCard` is the one 256px web-link overlay for `AppLink` and the terminal. Session cards are compacted to match. Artifact cards are unchanged because their page scale is computed for their current width.
- **Favicons:** icons are loaded with CORS and measured on a canvas. One-colour glyphs invert to suit the theme, and icons with their own colours are left alone. Hosts without CORS are reloaded plainly and get a light plate in dark themes.
- **Preload:** `lib/link-preload.ts` keeps one `IntersectionObserver` for the page. A link that stays on screen for 250 ms is queued, at most two load at once, and a queued link that leaves the screen is dropped. Only `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>` with no query string and local `ao://` text artifacts qualify. Any other web link stays hover-only, because preloading it would make the daemon contact whatever URL an agent wrote, with no hover. A URL is tried once per 5 minutes, so a failed preview is not requested again on every scroll.

Coverage, from source: `AppLink` web links (chat markdown, markdown file view, notifications, session inspector, intake fields, project creation, product links), terminal web links, and `ao://` session and artifact links in chat.

Intentionally unchanged: the raw link in `IndependentSideChats.tsx`, fragment and `mailto:` links, workspace file links, `ao:` links in the terminal, remote-host local links, and buttons that just open a browser.

Known limits: sites that reject the preview bot show the fallback, and a hung page still costs the daemon 8 s in the background after the UI has moved on. Preload does not cover terminal links, image or HTML artifacts (read from the local daemon, so there is little to gain), or GitHub issue links.

## Testing

**Local checks not run on the final head; GitHub Actions handles validation.** Regression tests were added for each root cause above.

Manual verification in an isolated Electron app, using real hover events and native window captures, before the last review fixes (panic recovery and resetting icon state between links, neither of which changes the rendered cards):

- Light and dark themes, in chat, terminal and `ao://` links
- Cold and warm cache, repeated hover (warm hover made no requests)
- Rapid switching across 8 hung links (all aborted)
- Stale response, slow and failed responses, recovery
- Keyboard focus opens a card and blur closes it

Preload, in the same isolated app with a copy of real data: an on-screen PR link was fetched once, without a hover, and its card then opened with content, no skeleton and no preview request, with images from disk cache. Preloading of text artifacts was not exercised in the real app, because the chats tried had no usable text artifact link; it is covered by new tests only.

CI results are recorded on this PR as checks.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [ ] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: [Bug]: New Task preselects the first listed OpenCode 2 model, not the model OpenCode runs by default
body:
### What went wrong?

I wanted to check that AO's "auto" model selection for OpenCode 2 works, meaning the task starts on whatever model OpenCode itself would run when no model is chosen.

When I open New Task with OpenCode 2, a model is already selected: `beam-free`. That is only the first model in the list (the list is alphabetical). When I start an OpenCode 2 worker without choosing a model, OpenCode runs `iceman-free` instead. So the model New Task shows is not the one OpenCode would use, and the model list has no "Auto" or "Default" entry to pick.

### What I did

1. OpenCode 2 (v2.2.6) installed and signed in to the `opencode-go` and `openai` providers, plus a local `ollama`.
2. Built AO from current `main` (`d022509b3c`) with an empty profile, added a small git repository as a project, and used OpenCode 2 as its worker agent.
3. Spawned a worker with no model: `ao spawn --project auto-clean --harness opencode-v2 --name auto-clean-worker --prompt "Create auto.py that prints auto from AO, commit it on your branch, do not open a PR, then stop."`. It finished the task, and its composer showed **Iceman Free**.
4. Opened New Task for the same project. The model chip reads **beam-free**. Opening the model list shows `beam-free`, `big-pickle`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-opus-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-6`, and so on, with no Auto or Default entry.

### What I expected

New Task to preselect the model OpenCode would run (`iceman-free` here), or to offer an explicit automatic choice, instead of an arbitrary first model in the list.

### Environment and frequency

AO built from `main` at `d022509b3c`, Linux (X11), OpenCode v2.2.6. It happened every time I looked, in a fresh profile. I did not submit a task from New Task, so I don't know which model that task would actually have used.

title: fix(opencode-v2): mark the model OpenCode 2 runs by default in its catalog
body:
Code changes: +77 -1  
Tests: +185 -0  
Others: +9 -0 (docs)

## What

When AO discovers OpenCode 2's models, it now asks OpenCode itself for its default model (`opencode api --standalone GET /api/model/default`) and marks that model `isDefault` in the catalog, so New Task preselects it instead of the first listed model.

## Why

Fixes #8006

For OpenCode 2, no model was ever marked as the default, so New Task fell back to the first row of the list (`beam-free`, alphabetical). An OpenCode 2 worker started without a model runs `iceman-free`. The resolver added in #6063 reads config files and deliberately gives up for OpenCode 2, because OpenCode 2 also reads config from directories above a launch worktree's git root that discovery cannot see. #5834 sets the rule that an unknown default should not be made up; asking OpenCode removes the need to guess.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/agents/opencode-v2/models`: 174 models, none with `isDefault`. New Task model chip: `beam-free`. | Same endpoint: `opencode/iceman-free` has `isDefault: true` (what `opencode api GET /api/model/default` returns). New Task model chip: `iceman-free`. |
| An OpenCode 2 worker spawned without `--model` ran `iceman-free` while New Task showed `beam-free`. | New Task shows the model OpenCode would run. |

Screenshots of the New Task chip before and after will be attached in a comment.

## How

- `opencode_v2_default.go`: `openCodeV2ResolvedDefault` runs the lookup in the discovery directory with the same command runner and environment as the `models` call, and `parseOpenCodeV2DefaultModel` reads `data.providerID` / `data.modelID`. Any failure, empty output, or `"data": null` leaves the default unmarked; the model list is unaffected.
- `catalog.go`: for `opencode-v2` the CLI's answer outranks the file-based resolver. `applyConfiguredDefault` is unchanged, so a catalog that already marks a default keeps it.
- `CatalogFingerprint` gains a `:resolved-default-v1` suffix for `opencode-v2`, so catalogs cached without a default are replaced by the normal background refresh (the same pattern as the existing `shared-providers-v1` suffixes).
- OpenCode 1 is untouched, and a test asserts it never calls the v2 endpoint.

Intentional omissions and limits:

- **Transient 503 at startup.** If the lookup runs while OpenCode's plugins are still activating, OpenCode answers `ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating`. That leaves the default unmarked, which is today's behavior, until the next refresh (catalogs are trusted for 6 hours). I reproduced this on a machine whose OpenCode config starts MCP servers through `npx`/`uvx`, and it does not happen once those have started. A retry did not help (both attempts hit the same wait), so there is none. A follow-up could treat this case as a retryable discovery result.
- **Device-wide directory.** The catalog is computed from AO's own discovery directory, so a `model` set only in one project's OpenCode config is not reflected.
- **Cost.** The lookup starts a private OpenCode server, adding roughly 5-10 seconds to a discovery run.
- **Endpoint stability.** OpenCode describes this API surface as experimental. A change on their side degrades to "no default", not an error.
- It adds a background probe of the OpenCode binary through the existing `modelCommand` path, like `opencode models`; relevant to #7134 only if that guard is applied per command.

## Testing

Run locally on Linux with the CI commands (`-race -count=1`, `GOFLAGS` as in `go.yml`):

- New tests pass: 6 test functions in `opencode_v2_default_test.go` (a parser table of 8 cases, success, lookup failure, null default, OpenCode 1 not queried, fingerprint) and 1 live check in `opencode_integration_test.go` against a real OpenCode 2.2.6 (skips if absent), which marked `opencode/iceman-free`.
- `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 (the release binary built with Go 1.27) over `./...`: clean, 0 issues.
- `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...` passes, and the CLI container fresh-install check passes.
- `storage-race` job (`go-test-parallel.sh 4 ...`): passes.
- `backend-core` (226 packages, all but the four storage packages): 201 pass, 11 fail. I re-ran those 11 packages on a pristine `upstream/main` checkout: 120 of the 123 failing tests fail there too, so they come from this machine (Codex account tests, Cue shell tests with no `zsh`/`fish` installed, the `opencode` and `opencodev2` suites, and similar). The other 3 (`TestACPReplayLoadLargeHistoryThroughSDK`, `TestCLIStatusDiagnosticsPreserveFailureWithoutRawOutput` and its subtest) failed only in the full run and pass in isolation on this branch, which looks like load.

Not run locally: the Windows-only jobs in `go.yml` (no Windows runner) and the `codegen-drift` job (no SQL or query changes). Remote checks are not verified yet.

- [x] Branched from `main` (`d022509b3c`)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue (#8006)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: ci(release): bump the Homebrew cask after stable releases when BrewTestBot does not
body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/homebrew-cask-bump.yml`, which bumps the `agent-orchestrator` Homebrew cask after a stable desktop release. It also records the release rules the cask depends on.

### Important finding: Homebrew already autobumps this cask

The plan assumed the cask was not on Homebrew's autobump list. It is. `autobump.txt` was removed from homebrew-cask in July 2025, and the list now comes from Homebrew's API: https://formulae.brew.sh/api/cask/agent-orchestrator.json reports `"autobump": true`. BrewTestBot uses the cask's `livecheck` (`:github_latest`) to open the version-bump PR within about 3 hours of a stable release. `brew bump-cask-pr` refuses autobumped casks. Locally, `brew bump-cask-pr --dry-run --version 0.14.10 agent-orchestrator` fails with "Whoops, the agent-orchestrator cask has its version update pull requests automatically opened by BrewTestBot every ~3 hours!"

So the workflow first checks the API. While `autobump` is true it skips with a notice and does nothing. It opens the PR itself only if the cask later gets `no_autobump!` or a livecheck `skip`. Today, the release rules below are the part that matters.

## Before / after

**Before:** no Homebrew step. The cask version moves only when someone opens a PR on Homebrew/homebrew-cask by hand, or when BrewTestBot does it.

**After:** on `release: released` (a stable release is published, or a pre-release is promoted), plus `workflow_dispatch` with a `version` input for manual retries, one `macos-latest` job:
1. Resolves the tag and requires `^vX.Y.Z$`, `isPrerelease == false`, `isDraft == false`, and both assets `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-{arm64,x64}-<version>.zip` on the release. Nightlies (`v*-nightly.*`) never trigger `released`, and the tag regex rejects them again.
2. Skips with a notice if Homebrew's API says BrewTestBot autobumps the cask. **This is the path today.**
3. Skips with a notice if the `HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN` secret is missing.
4. Otherwise runs `brew tap --force homebrew/cask` and `brew bump-cask-pr --no-browse --version <version> agent-orchestrator`. This step has `continue-on-error: true`.

The workflow runs separately from release publishing, because releases are published outside this repo by the release conductor. Combined with `continue-on-error`, a Homebrew failure can never fail a release.

## Secret to add (only needed if the cask ever leaves autobump)

- **Name:** `HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN` (repository secret on OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator)
- **Type:** classic personal access token. A fine-grained token cannot open PRs on a repo its owner does not own.
- **Scopes:** `public_repo` and `workflow`. Homebrew needs `workflow` to push to a fork of a repo that contains workflow files.
- **Owner:** the account whose fork of Homebrew/homebrew-cask the PRs come from. The job commits as that account's noreply identity.

Without the secret the job only logs a notice.

## Release rules the cask depends on (also in the workflow header)

1. Keep the versioned zip asset names `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-{arm64,x64}-<version>.zip` under tag `v<version>`, and upload them before publishing.
2. Keep nightlies and every other pre-release marked pre-release. The livecheck reads `/releases/latest`.
3. Never re-upload or replace assets on a published release. The cask pins the sha256, so ship a new version instead.

## Validation

- `actionlint .github/workflows/homebrew-cask-bump.yml`: clean (with shellcheck installed).
- Ran the resolve step's script locally against real releases: `v0.14.10` → `version=0.14.10 skip=false`; `v0.14.11-nightly.202611081824` → skipped as not stable; `v0.14.9` → `version=0.14.9 skip=false`.
- The bump step itself has not run end to end. It cannot while the cask is autobumped.

title: fix(inspector): show a worker's Artifacts tab whenever artifacts are listed
body:
Code changes: +3 -2\
Tests: +8 -5\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A worker session's inspector now shows the **Artifacts** tab whenever the session lists artifact files. Summary stays the default tab. Before this change, the tab appeared only after an artifact was opened and disappeared once the user switched to another tab.

## Why

Artifacts were only reachable by clicking a file in Summary or following an artifact link. Once you left the tab, the only way back was another click in Summary. Keeping the tab visible whenever artifacts are listed makes them always one click away. This matches the orchestrator behavior proposed in #7973.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Worker with two artifacts: tabs show Summary (and Files/Browser…), no Artifacts tab until a file is opened from Summary. | Same worker: an **Artifacts** tab is always present after the other tabs; Summary is still selected by default. |
| Open Artifacts, then click Summary: the Artifacts tab disappears. | Open Artifacts, then click Summary: the Artifacts tab stays. |
| Worker with no artifacts: no Artifacts tab. | Unchanged: no Artifacts tab. |

**Screenshots pending.** I ran the dev app from this checkout with isolated scratch data and a worker listing `q3-report.html` and `release-notes.md`. The agent session that made this PR doesn't have macOS Screen Recording permission, so it couldn't capture the window. Before/after captures will be added in a comment.

## How

- `SessionInspector.tsx`: the worker tab filter no longer requires `requestedView === "artifacts"`. The tab shows when `session.artifactFiles` is non-empty, or while an artifact link is pending (`artifactRequestPending`). That pending case keeps the tab available for a link that arrives before the session list refreshes. The existing fallback to Summary still applies when there are no artifacts.
- The Artifacts tab is still last in `VIEW_DEFS`. Nothing else changes: no new tab order, and the default view stays Summary.
- Orchestrators aren't touched here. On `main` they show only Summary and Browser (#7978). #7973 proposes adding Artifacts for orchestrators.

## Testing

Updated tests in `SessionInspector.test.tsx`:
- `shows the Artifacts tab whenever the session lists artifacts`: Summary is selected and the Artifacts tab is present.
- `keeps the Artifacts tab after leaving it`: open Artifacts, return to Summary, and the tab is still there.
- Both fail against `main`'s `SessionInspector.tsx` and pass with this change. The existing tests still pass: pending link, no artifacts, and still loading.

Local runs (macOS, Node 24.12, Go 1.27.1):
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- `npx vitest run --shard=1/2` and `--shard=2/2` (full suite, CI's default config): 12,232 passed, 1 failed. The failure is a timeout in `src/main/browser-history-store.test.ts` ("caps entry count…", 20 s under full-suite load); that file passes 3/3 when run alone.
- `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer` (both shards):
  - 151 passed and 1 flaky (passed on retry).
  - 1 failure: `chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts:139` ("pointer drag"). It fails identically with `main`'s code on this Mac, so it's a pre-existing local failure. CI runs this suite in the Linux Playwright container.
- `npm run test:browser-postcondition-integration`: one flaky failure in the "native tab gap restart" scenario, then passed on 2 of 2 reruns.
- Boundary lane (`TestMuxOriginElectron`, `TestBrowserBoundaryElectron`, `TestMobileControlOriginElectron`): pass. I ran them natively on macOS, not under `xvfb`.
- Not run locally: mac-native, docs, cloud and product-ui lanes. This change doesn't trigger them.

- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(shell): render session switches without blocking the sidebar
body:
Part of #7975 (group B, session switching). Follows #7988 (merged).

## Summary
- Each switch rendered the whole destination in one blocking pass, because route state reaches React as a synchronous store update. This froze main-thread animations, including the sidebar's working shimmer.
- `LocalSessionHost` now defers the session id. The sidebar responds immediately, and the destination renders in interruptible slices with the previous session left on screen until it's ready.
- `useSessionSwitchSnap` keeps chrome transitions off until the deferred session commits, so switches look the same as before.
- While the switch is held, the previous session's workspace is `inert` and loses focus, so keystrokes after a keyboard switch (⌘], ⌘1–9) cannot reach the old composer. No visual change.
- The topbar actions take their session from `SessionView`, not the URL, so they always match the session on screen.
- Only a session that is already on screen is kept. Returning from the board before the deferred value caught up renders the destination directly.
- Markdown links in chat use the indexed file lookup from #7988, like inline code already did.

## Measurements
Production Electron build, an inert copy of real local chats and 147 sessions, clicking the real sidebar. Three alternating runs per revision; sessions over 150 activity rows. Before = this branch without the deferral. Samples where no chat rendered are excluded from frame and settle numbers.

| | Longest frame, median / p90 | Blocking tasks per switch | Longest task | Content settled, median |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revisit before | 61 / 92 ms | 0.94 | 106 ms | 82 ms |
| Revisit after | 41 / 75 ms | 0.27 | 80 ms | 110 ms |
| First open before | 54 / 109 ms | 0.52 | 115 ms | 364 ms |
| First open after | 50 / 77 ms | 0.48 | 87 ms | 546 ms |

## Trade-offs and limits
- The destination appears slightly later, about 28 ms on revisits, in exchange for fewer freezes. The first-open settle time includes network and file-list arrival and varied widely between runs.
- The DOM commit is still synchronous, so frames of 40–80 ms remain.
- No live agents were streaming during measurement.
- Keeping recent sessions mounted was not attempted here.

## Tests
- `useHeldSession` (the switch logic, moved out of `LocalSessionHost`): the held render keeps the old session and its project; focus leaves the held workspace; `inert` is set then removed; the snap hold is released; entering from another route renders directly; rapid switches settle on the last one; unmount releases the hold.
- `SessionTopbarActions`: actions follow their `route` prop over the URL and fall back to the URL without one.
- `useSessionSwitchSnap`: transitions stay off until a held destination commits.

Manual check in the dev app is pending.

title: fix(artifacts): name binary file types and offer a download
body:
Code changes: +50 -3
Tests: +87 -3
Others: +27 -0 (i18n message catalogs, nine locales)

Closes #7845

## The bug

`fileMediaKind()` only recognizes image/video/audio, so a `.zip` artifact fell through to `ReadOnlyFileView` and got the generic "Binary file preview is not available." with no action — a dead end.

## Visual proof

Captured in the desktop app against a seeded session with a real zip artifact (~374 B) and a markdown artifact:

| Artifacts list | The zip artifact, after the fix |
|---|---|
| ![Artifacts list showing the seeded zip and markdown artifacts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/proof/7845-artifact-preview/proof/7845/shot-1-artifacts-list.png) | ![Zip artifact shows "Preview isn't available for .zip files." plus a Download button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/proof/7845-artifact-preview/proof/7845/shot-2-zip-fixed.png) |

Clicking **Download** in that build opened Electron's native save dialog and wrote `classroom_persona_suite.zip` — 374 bytes, byte-for-byte the seeded file.

The shared viewer path is intact — the same session's markdown artifact still renders:

![Markdown artifact rendering normally in the same session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/proof/7845-artifact-preview/proof/7845/shot-3-md-contrast.png)

## What changed

**`ReadOnlyFileView.tsx`**
- The binary branch names the file type when the path has an extension: "Preview isn't available for `.zip` files." Extensionless paths keep the generic string.
- New optional `binaryAction` slot renders under that message.

**`FileContentPane.tsx`**
- Binary artifacts (`source.kind === "artifact"`) pass a `DownloadArtifactButton` through `binaryAction`, saving the artifact from the same content URL its preview would have streamed.
- The bytes are fetched to a blob and handed to an anchor, because a cross-origin link's `download` attribute is ignored and would navigate the viewer away from AO. The saved file keeps the artifact's name; failures toast `files.downloadFailed`; the button disables while the save is in flight.

**i18n** — `files.previewUnavailableType`, `files.download`, `files.downloadFailed` in all nine locales.

## Testing

- `ReadOnlyFileView.test.tsx`: type-aware message, extensionless fallback, action slot renders.
- `ArtifactFileView.test.tsx`: download offered for a zip artifact (edit and read-only variants), blob save flow uses the artifact name and revokes the object URL, failed save toasts and re-enables the button.
- Manual: the desktop-app walkthrough in the screenshots above, including a real save to disk through Electron's dialog.

## Intentional omissions

- Workspace binary files in the Files panel get the type-aware message but no download action yet; this PR keeps the action scoped to artifacts, per the issue. The new `binaryAction` prop is generic and can be reused for the workspace blob route in a follow-up.
- The compact diff-review rows (`WorkspaceReviewPane`, `CloudWorkspaceReviewPane`, `WorkspaceDiffView`) still use the generic string; they are summaries, not the artifact viewer.

title: fix(chat): stop the plain Worked label being selectable
body:
## Summary

A turn with no steps to fold shows "Worked for 7s" as plain text. That `div` inherited `select-text` from the transcript viewport, so a pointer drag could highlight it. The fold trigger and the live status row already set `select-none`. This adds the same class to the plain label.

Message prose, code and command output are unchanged.

## Verification

I mounted the real `TurnWorkSummary`, `LiveResponseStatus` and `AssistantMessage` with the app's CSS, inside the transcript's `select-text` classes, and ran real pointer drags in headless Chrome.

| Drag target | Selected text |
| --- | --- |
| Control row with the old label classes | `Control unfixed 7s` |
| Plain "Worked for 7s" | none |
| Fold "Worked for 12s" | none |
| Live status row | none |
| Assistant prose | full sentence |
| Code block | `const codeSample = 42;` |

A drag from the control row through the labels into the prose selected the text on either side and skipped the labels. Select-all skipped them too.

The label's text content is still "Worked for 7s", the fold button keeps its name and still toggles, and the live label keeps `role="status"`.

The page also rendered in the AO Browser panel, but `ao browser drag` hung there, so the drags ran in headless Chrome. Tests and typecheck were not run locally and are left to CI.

## To test

title: feat(chat): steer Antigravity through agy acp
body:
Code changes: +925 -93\
Tests: +1684 -7\
Others: +0 -0

> **Depends on #7702.** This branch is stacked on it and reuses its steering framework (`SteerRequest`/`SteerDrain`, steer segments). Until #7702 merges, the diff here also shows its two commits; review the last commit, `975956d757`.

## What

Antigravity now steers: a message sent while a turn is running joins that turn.

- **agy 1.5.4+:** AO launches the ACP server built into the agy CLI, `agy acp`, instead of the separate `agy_acp_server`. The separate server is no longer needed for agy 1.5.4 and newer. Before 1.5.4, `agy acp` can hang a turn when a tool call needs a second approval and drops a resumed session to the default mode (1.5.4 changelog), so older CLIs keep the separate server.
- **Steering:** ⌘↩ and the queued card's Steer both work. Steer is offered only on `agy acp` 1.5.4+.
- **Older agy CLIs**, or an explicit `AO_AGY_ACP_SERVER_PATH`, keep the separate server, unchanged.

## Why

`agy_acp_server` has no steering. `agy acp` steers when a second `session/prompt` arrives mid-turn (its 1.5.0 changelog: "steering a running turn by sending another prompt"). I checked this live before writing any AO code: 3 runs out of 3 against agy 1.5.3 with a real model, raw ACP.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| **⌘↩ during a turn.** Antigravity had no Steer, so the message waited for the turn to end. | The change of plan joins the running turn (↳ Steered). The agent replies "I will edit staging.yaml next for the STAGING environment" in the same turn. ![agy acp: change of plan steered into the running turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a327fab881baf8b06505ec168e5f98ceb2155835/agy-1-steered.png) |
| **Queued card.** No Steer button. | The card offers Steer while the command runs, and the message joins the turn. In this run Antigravity acknowledged it and ended the turn while the command ran in the background (see Known limitations). ![agy acp: queued change of plan with a Steer button while sleep 20 runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a327fab881baf8b06505ec168e5f98ceb2155835/agy-2-queued.png) ![agy acp: the queued message steered into the running turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a327fab881baf8b06505ec168e5f98ceb2155835/agy-3-card-steered.png) |
| **Stop after a steer.** Not possible before. | The turn ends once, interrupted, and the next message runs normally. ![agy acp: Stop after a steer, then a normal next turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/a327fab881baf8b06505ec168e5f98ceb2155835/agy-4-stop-after-steer.png) |

## How

- **How `agy acp` steers.** When a second `session/prompt` arrives mid-turn, agy answers the earlier prompt with `end_turn` at once and carries the same work on under the new prompt. The new prompt returns the final answer.
- **`acp.SteerPrompt`**, a third binding next to `SteerRequest` and `SteerDrain`.
  - A steer sends another `session/prompt` under the running turn's context, so Stop cancels it with the turn.
  - The turn's prompts are tracked as a set, and the turn settles once every one has returned. Behind the persistent host, its result is the answer carrying the host's receipt, whichever order the SDK wakes the prompt callers in.
  - `Steer` reports `injected` only on evidence: an earlier prompt hands off, or the steer prompt itself completes inside the turn. With neither within 5 s, or if the caller gives up, it reports the delivery uncertain rather than delivered.
  - If the new prompt fails while the earlier one still owns the turn, the agent refused it. `Steer` returns a provider refusal and the earlier prompt keeps the turn.
  - If the turn ends before the steer prompt reaches the host, the host refuses it and `Steer` returns `ErrChatNoSteerableTurn`, so the message can go as a new turn.
  - A turn adopted after a daemon restart can be steered, unless the host is compacting it. Its first prompt belongs to the host, which passes that prompt's handoff on as `_ao/persistent_prompt_handoff`, and the adopted turn ends on the host's result.
  - A handoff settles only the next steer prompt, the one the work went to. A cancelled answer is no handoff, and a steer prompt answered as cancelled is uncertain.
  - Stop releases a steer prompt still waiting, as uncertain, so it doesn't wait out the 5 s. A steer prompt that Stop overtakes before it is written is never sent, and its `Steer` is refused.
  - A steer prompt answered "Session not found" is a refusal that stops the provider, as `_session/steering` is on main.
  - A steer that takes starts the reply's next segment at once.
  - A late answer from a handed-off prompt never completes the turn a second time.
- **Persistent host.** The relay allowed one prompt per turn and journaled the first answer as the turn's result.
  - It now admits a `session/prompt` marked `_meta["ao.steerPrompt"]` into the active turn, and only while the turn is active and unacknowledged.
  - The turn's journal is kept, and the answer of the last prompt to return is journaled as the turn's result.
  - A refused steer prompt hands the turn back to the earlier prompt.
  - A steer prompt that arrives after the turn ended is refused with a marked error (`ao.steerTurnEnded`), also once the result is acknowledged, so it never starts a turn of its own.
  - The stall watchdog keeps main's cancel-first steps. Only the answer to the turn's last prompt becomes the stall failure. If the adapter ignores the cancel, every prompt still waiting fails in one pass, oldest first.
  - Once a `session/cancel` for the turn has passed through, from Stop or the watchdog, a steer prompt is refused.
  - Unmarked second prompts are refused as before.
- **`acp.Config.SessionModeForAgent`** picks the approval-mode mapping from the handshake, because the two Antigravity servers name their modes differently.
- **Antigravity driver.**
  - **Launch:** `agy acp --app-data-dir antigravity-acp` when `agy --version` is 1.5.4 or newer. The result is cached per binary path, size and mtime.
    - `antigravity-acp` keeps Chat data where the separate server put it. So AO's history checks and the Chat/terminal handoff still find it, and a Chat started on the old server resumes.
    - `agy acp` ignores the `GEMINI_HOME` variable, so a session's or the daemon's `GEMINI_HOME` is passed as `--gemini-dir`. Without this, Chat wrote to `~/.gemini`; I found it in the lab and fixed it.
  - **Handshake:** accepts `agentInfo.name` "Antigravity ACP Server" at 1.5.4 or newer.
  - **Approvals:** `agy acp`'s modes are `default`, `accept-edits` and `plan`; nothing runs every tool without asking. AO's auto and bypass map to `accept-edits`, and a `PermissionPolicy` answers the remaining requests with `allow_once`, never `allow_always`. That matches what the old server's `yolo` did. Default and accept-edits still ask the user. 1.5.4 adds an `auto` mode, but it still asks before a command leaves the terminal sandbox, and AO's Auto means "run without asking", so it keeps this mapping.
  - **Sign-in:** `agy acp` reuses the CLI's login, so the separate server's authenticate bootstrap is skipped. Its `authenticate` could start a browser sign-in.
  - **Steer:** offered only for `agy acp` 1.5.4+.
- **Not changed.** Picking a Gemini variant ID such as `gemini-3.8-flash-high` on a server that splits model and thinking level is handled by #7719. The default model and full IDs such as `claude-opus-4-6-thinking` work without it.

## Known limitations

- **Antigravity sometimes ends the turn early.** When its command has gone to the background (`run_command` waits 10 s, then backgrounds it), Antigravity sometimes answers the steer, says it will wait for the command, and ends the turn. Nothing follows until the next prompt. This happened in 1 of 3 raw ACP runs with no AO involved, and twice in the app. AO shows what the agent sends.
- **The live test `TestLiveAntigravityACPAndCLIShareConversationAcrossCopiedDatabases` fails on agy 1.5.3, independent of this PR.**
  - The terminal step runs `agy --conversation … --print` with `GEMINI_HOME` set, and the 1.5.3 CLI ignores the variable. It reports "conversation not found" and reads and writes `~/.gemini`.
  - That is AO's terminal restore path, which this PR doesn't touch. It needs its own issue.
- **Sign-in comes from the agy CLI on 1.5.4+.** AO launches `agy acp`, which uses the CLI's login and skips the separate server's sign-in bootstrap. Someone who signed in only through `agy_acp_server` would need to sign in to the agy CLI. The lab runs used one login for both.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/agyacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/` passes. The new `SteerPrompt` tests also passed 30 times in a row with `-race`. They cover:
  - **Conversation:** one turn across the handoff; two steers in order; a refusal leaves the first prompt in charge; Stop ends the whole turn once; no steer without a running turn; binding precedence.
  - **Relay:** only a marked prompt is admitted; the turn settles on the steer prompt, or on the last prompt to return; a refused steer hands the turn back; a steer after the turn ends is refused as too late, before and after the ack; a reattached controller hears of the earlier attachment's handoff; a stalled steered turn ends once with the stall marker when the adapter answers the cancel, and every prompt fails without it when the cancel is ignored; a steer is refused once the turn is being cancelled.
  - **Conversation over a scripted host,** with the order the prompt callers are woken in pinned both ways: the turn ending before the steer arrives keeps the host's result and refuses the steer as too late; the host's result settles the turn in either order; steering a turn adopted after a restart; an unanswered steer is uncertain after the wait or when the caller gives up, and a late refusal leaves the first prompt in charge; a stall failure ends the turn once; no steer prompt is sent once Stop has begun; a handoff reaches only the next of two steers; a cancelled answer is uncertain; Stop releases a waiting steer; a steer prompt Stop overtakes before it is written is never sent, in both orders; a lost session on a steer prompt stops the provider; an adopted compaction takes no steer; a steer that takes starts the next reply segment at once; a handoff skips a steer prompt not yet written; a cancelled adopted answer is no handoff; a lost session after the wait still stops the provider.
  - Each of these fails with its fix reverted.
  - **Antigravity:** launch target by CLI version and override; launch arguments including an inherited `GEMINI_HOME`; handshake gate; mode mapping; approve-once policy; skipped bootstrap; `agy acp` and Steer only on 1.5.4+; the live test's approval filter.
- **Live through AO's driver and persistent host** (`AO_LIVE_AGY=1`, Gemini 3.8 Flash, private `GEMINI_HOME`):
  - **Re-run on agy 1.5.6 after the review fixes:** `TestLiveAgyACPSteersARunningTurn` passed 4 of 6 at `beb793a2b2`. The steer now asks for `NEXT-FILE-STAGING` or `NEXT-FILE-PROD`. The test requires the first, and requires that the reply names `staging.yaml`. It reads events for its whole quiet window, approves the slow command only as written, and approves read-only requests inside its temporary folders. In both failures agy tried to check on the backgrounded command with a command outside those folders (`ps aux | grep …`, `find / …`), the test refused it, and agy ended the turn with no reply. Earlier, 4 of 9 runs ended the same way after the test rejected `ls -la`, a read of agy's own task log, or a `find` (agy's choice; AO saw one turn each time).
  - **Earlier, on agy 1.5.3:**
  - **New `TestLiveAgyACPSteersARunningTurn`:** passed 3 of 3. It uses default approvals, approves only the `sleep 20` command, steers during it, and expects one turn whose reply names STAGING. Two earlier runs, before the test created `prod.yaml` and `staging.yaml`, failed because the model went looking for `staging.yaml`.
  - **`TestLiveAntigravityACPConformance` on `agy acp`:** passed twice, covering standing instructions, reject, auto, downgrade, interrupt and resume. Its first prompt now says "Do not use any tools", because `agy acp` inspects the folder first and the test rejects that.
- **Live in the desktop app** (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`, Electron profile and `GEMINI_HOME`, real agy login, default approvals):
  - ⌘↩ steer, queued-card Steer, and Stop after a steer all behave as in the screenshots.
  - The launched process was `agy acp --app-data-dir antigravity-acp --gemini-dir <lab>`.
  - `~/.gemini/antigravity-acp/conversations` was unchanged afterwards.
- **Lint:** `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on the whole backend reports 0 issues.
- **Not re-run after the review fixes:** `TestLiveAntigravityACPConformance` and the desktop checks above. The fixes change how AO settles steers and turns, not what it sends to agy.
- **Full CI suites, run locally the way CI runs them:**
  - Go: `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean.
  - The race suite passes except in 6 packages that fail the same way on the base branch on this Mac, because they depend on tools installed here: `commandcode`, `crush`, `opencodev2`, `opencodev2acp`, `runtime/tmux` and `shellterm`. This PR touches none of them.
  - The `service/chat` race job passes.
  - No frontend changes.

title: Support external Codex cloud review completion signals and human acceptance notifications
body:
**Problem**

Orchestrator successfully forwards GitHub Codex review comments to Workers, enabling an automated review-and-repair loop.

However, AO does not detect when Codex cloud review has completed successfully for the current PR HEAD.

The existing `ready_to_merge` notification can fire before Codex finishes reviewing the latest commit.

**Requested behavior**

1. Recognize GitHub Codex cloud review completion from its machine-readable PR summary.
2. Verify the reviewed commit SHA matches the current PR HEAD.
3. Confirm no unresolved blocking review findings remain.
4. Generate a durable, deduplicated notification: `Awaiting human acceptance`.
5. Invalidate the previous completion state whenever the PR HEAD changes.
6. Preserve human-controlled merging and independent CI requirements.

**Environment**

- AO v0.14.9, Windows 11
- GitHub Codex cloud review, automatically triggered on new commits
- GitHub Actions CI
- AO native Reviewer disabled

**Reproduction evidence**

In one test, CI succeeded at 07:22:18 UTC. AO emitted `ready_to_merge` at 07:22:32 UTC. Codex cloud review completed at 07:23:23 UTC — approximately 51 seconds after AO's notification.

The cloud review result was successful, but AO did not produce a SHA-bound completion notification.

**Expected result**

AO should notify the user only after the current PR HEAD has completed the required external AI review and no blocking findings remain. It must not auto-merge.

title: feat(terminal): label terminals with the title their program sets
body:
Code changes: +984 -126\
Tests: +1 -0\
Others: +193 -52 (generated sqlc and API contract, docs)

## What

Terminal-backed sessions and shell tabs now show the title their program sets. Claude Code and Codex emit OSC 0/2 titles as they work; AO captures them and keeps the latest one even when no terminal is open.

The label order is: explicit name, then meaningful program title, then the existing fallback.

## Why

Terminal tabs read `Terminal N` whatever is running in them, while the running program already reports what it is doing.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Shell tab running Claude reads `Terminal 2` | Tab reads the task topic, such as `Login redirect` |
| A title change while the panel is closed is lost | The latest title is there when the panel reopens |
| Renaming a tab changes the stored name | Same, and later program titles cannot override it |
| Starting a rename nudges the tab text and resizes the tab | The text and tab stay in place |

## How

- **Capture:** a read-only scanner on the pty-host's PTY pump handles chunk-split sequences, BEL and ST terminators, and bounded payloads. Forwarded bytes do not change. Leading status glyphs are removed, so spinner frames are not title changes. Title watching is pty-host protocol v4.
- **Retention:** `service/terminaltitle` reconciles live TUI sessions and shell terminals from storage and writes only changes, at most once per 2 seconds per terminal. A replaced host reports its own title, which clears the previous one.
- **Storage:** session titles use the `session_terminal_titles` sidecar because every `sessions` update bumps the revision that fences observer writes. `display_name_explicit` and `title_explicit` record intentional names.
- **Display:** the daemon resolves precedence and sends `terminalTitle` only when it should be shown. Bare directories, `user@host`, `<command> <path>` (fish), shell names and agent product names do not count.

**Please review this decision:** a program title outranks AO's generated and prompt-derived names on new sessions. Sessions named before this migration keep their names, because old names cannot be told apart.

**Not covered:** chat and cloud sessions, legacy tmux handles, and pty-hosts started before this build until they restart. A program killed without resetting its title keeps it until something replaces it. An explicit name cannot be cleared back to automatic titles.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.

Tried by hand in an isolated dev app. No new automated tests were added, at the author's request.

title: chore(claude): move the bundled claude-agent-acp from 0.70.0 to 0.101.0
body:
### Report

AO bundles `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` **0.70.0** (`frontend/acp-runtime/package.json`, released 2026-08-18). The latest is **0.101.0** (2026-11-05), 31 releases later. At packaging time, `frontend/scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.mjs` patches the compiled 0.70 adapter in six places. Each patch matches exact 0.70 source text and fails the build if that text changes, so a version bump can't be a one-line change.

The steer patch's own comment says to drop it at 0.86; its upstream fix actually first shipped in 0.82.0. Three of the six patches are now upstream. The other three have to be re-ported, because 0.101 restructured the code: `acp-agent.js` is now split into modules such as `background-work.js`, `session-model.js` and `session-failure-extension.js`.

I'd like the team to agree on the plan before anyone picks this up.

### What changes

From reading both published packages (`npm pack` of 0.70.0 and 0.101.0). **Nothing has been run against 0.101 yet.**

| AO patch (`build-acp-runtime-helpers.mjs`) | Why AO added it | In 0.101 | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `patchClaudeSteerSettlement` | Steered turns stuck "Working" (port of upstream #1166) | Upstream: #1166 merged 2026-09-23; its code (`steeredAwaitingResult`) first appears in the 0.82.0 package | Drop. Check AO's one extra rule: a result that names a steer answers it even in a task-notification cycle. |
| `patchClaudeFoldedPromptSettlement` | A prompt folded into a task-notification cycle never settled (port of #1233 for #1145) | Upstream: #1233 merged 2026-10-07, in the 0.87.0 release notes | Drop |
| `patchClaudeStaleIdleDebt` | Leftover idle debt swallowed a steered turn's idle (port of the 0.79 sweep) | Upstream since 0.79, according to AO's patch comment (not checked separately) | Drop |
| `patchClaudeRetryDetails` | Pass `retry_delay_ms` through so the UI can show the backoff (#4611) | Still missing. `api_retry` now posts a warning, "Retrying Claude, attempt N of M", but no delay | Re-port onto `session-failure-extension.js`, or drop it if the team accepts no backoff time |
| `patchClaudeContextUsage` | Report the SDK's `getContextUsage` estimate instead of the last message's usage | Still reports `lastAssistantTotalUsage` | Re-port |
| `patchClaudeHibernationCheck` | AO's own `_ao/session/can_hibernate`, built on the adapter's background-task registry | AO-only, not upstream; the registry moved to `background-work.js` | Re-port |

Other changes that come with the bump:

- **ACP SDK** goes from 1.3.0 to 2.4.0, and the **Claude agent SDK** from 0.3.232 to 0.3.318.
- **Protocol:** 0.101 serves ACP v1 and v2 (`CLAUDE_AGENT_ACP_PROTOCOL=auto`). AO negotiates v1, and steering is v1-only upstream for now, so AO can stay on v1.
- **Node:** the adapter's `engines` now says `>=22`. AO already requires Node 22 (`minimumNodeMajor` in `claudeacp/driver.go`).
- **Claude Code CLI:** AO runs the user's installed `claude` through `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE`, so the newer agent SDK will talk to whatever CLI each user has. The adapter's minimum CLI needs checking.
- **Native steering:** unchanged. 0.101 still advertises `_meta.steering` and handles `_session/steering`.

### Cause

AO pinned 0.70 and fixed bugs by patching the compiled adapter while the upstream fixes were pending. Those fixes have since shipped, but the pin never moved. Each patch is a tripwire on the 0.70 text, so later releases can't be picked up without reworking the patches.

### Expected

AO moves to a current adapter, with these steps:

1. Bump `frontend/acp-runtime` to 0.101.x and regenerate its lock file.
2. Delete the three patches that are now upstream, with their tests.
3. Re-port the retry, context-usage and hibernation patches onto the 0.101 modules, keeping the "fail the build if the source changed" tripwire.
4. Live-test Claude Code Chat in the desktop app. Cover streaming, tools and approvals, steering (⌘↩ and the queued card, including during a background task), Stop, resume after a daemon restart, hibernation with a background task, retry and backoff display, the context meter, and usage-limit refusals.

**Questions for the team:**

- Go straight to 0.101, or move in steps, for example to 0.87 first? 0.87 is the first version where both settlement patches can go.
- Re-port the retry backoff patch, or upstream it first? It's a small change to `api_retry`.
- Several open PRs touch Claude Chat (#7991, #7993, #7253). Should this wait for them, or go first?

title: Refactor sidebar update UI into dedicated component
body:
Code changes: +427 -340\
Tests: +85 -60\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Extracted the sidebar update status display logic into a new `SidebarUpdate.tsx` component, replacing the previous inline implementation in `Sidebar.tsx`. The new component provides both expanded (`SidebarUpdateRow`) and collapsed (`SidebarUpdateRail`) variants with improved UX:

- Download available state now shows version with optional dotted underline linking to release notes
- Download progress displays as a visual bar instead of percentage text
- Failed downloads/installs show with error state and retry action
- Removed the 24-hour dismissal feature for available updates
- Removed the "retry check" action for failing update checks (only download/install failures now show)

## Why

Consolidates update UI logic into a single, testable module and improves the update notification UX by:
1. Making release notes discoverable via hover card on the version number
2. Providing clearer visual feedback during downloads
3. Simplifying the update state machine by removing dismissal complexity
4. Focusing sidebar actions on user-actionable failures (download/install) rather than check failures

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Update available row with dismiss button; download progress as "Downloading… 42%"; retry button for check failures | Update available row with version as dotted link to release notes; download progress as visual bar; no dismiss; only download/install failures show retry |

## How

**New `SidebarUpdate.tsx` exports:**
- `SidebarUpdateAction` type: discriminated union of update states (downloading, download available, install ready, failed)
- `sidebarUpdateAction()`: derives the action from `UpdateStatus` and failure phase
- `updateFailurePhase()`: determines if an error was a download or install failure
- `SidebarUpdateRow`: expanded footer variant with full text and pill button
- `SidebarUpdateRail`: collapsed icon-rail variant with tooltip
- `FOOTER_RAIL_BUTTON_CLASS`: shared styling constant moved from `Sidebar.tsx`

**Key implementation details:**
- `useSidebarUpdateAction()` hook tracks state transitions to attribute errors to the operation that was in flight, preventing the failed row from blinking when status cycles through checking/available/not-available
- `displayVersion()` strips nightly build stamps for cleaner display
- `nightlyCaption()` formats nightly build dates for hover card
- `AvailableTitle` component renders version with optional dotted underline and hover card showing release notes
- `ProgressRing` SVG component visualizes download progress in the rail variant

**Removed:**
- `useSidebarUpdateDismissal` hook and its 24-hour dismissal logic
- `UpdateStatusRow`, `UpdateInstallSlide`, `UpdateStatusRail` components from `Sidebar.tsx`
- Dismissal-related i18n keys across all language files
- "Retry update check" action and related i18n

**Sidebar.tsx changes:**
- Imports `SidebarUpdateRow`, `SidebarUpdateRail`, `FOOTER_RAIL_BUTTON_CLASS` from new component
- Removes dismissal state management
- Simplifies footer layout: Connect Mobile button moved to icon-rail with tooltip
- Removes `UpdateInstallSlide` component (install action now in `SidebarUpdateRow`)

## Testing

- Added `SidebarUpdate.test.tsx` with unit tests for `sidebarUpdateAction()` and `updateFailurePhase()` logic
- Updated `Sidebar.test.tsx` tests to match new behavior:
  - Download action now via pill button, not row click
  - Release notes shown via hover card on version
  - No dismiss button
  - Download progress shows as bar with progressbar role
  - Failing checks don't render in sidebar
  - Failed downloads/installs show with retry button
- Existing e2e tests updated to reflect new UI structure

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change: consolidates update UI into dedicated component with improved UX
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions
- [x] Before/After comparison provided
- [x
