title: bug(updater): macOS update blocked with "/Applications isn't writable" when the app bundle is owned by another user; message blames the wrong folder
body:
## Summary

On macOS, when the installed `Agent Orchestrator.app` is owned by a **different user account** than the person running it, the "Restart to update" dialog blocks the update and blames the **wrong folder**:

> AO could not prepare the update. Please try again.
> The update can't be installed because Agent Orchestrator's location isn't writable: /Applications. Fix that folder's permissions, or move Agent Orchestrator.app somewhere you can write to, reopen it, and then restart to update.

`/Applications` is writable. The **bundle** is not. The user is told to fix a folder that has nothing wrong with it, so they can't get past this on their own.

There are three problems here:

1. **Wrong diagnosis in the message (confirmed).** `getMacInstallBlocker()` checks the bundle and its parent in one `try`. Whichever check fails, the message names the parent.
2. **The preflight blocks an install Squirrel.Mac can do (needs testing).** Squirrel.Mac already handles a bundle the user can't write to: it runs ShipIt with admin rights after a macOS password prompt. Our preflight stops before Squirrel gets the chance.
3. **"AO" in user-facing text (confirmed).** `update.restart.prepareFailed` says "AO" in all 9 locales. It should say "Orchestrator".

## Who can hit this

Anyone whose app bundle is owned by another user ID:

- Macs set up with **Migration Assistant** from a machine where the account had a different UID. This is the most likely cause on the machine below.
- **Shared or family Macs**, where another account installed the app.
- **Managed or work Macs**, where IT or MDM installed the app as root or an admin account.
- Installs done with `sudo`, or copied with tools that keep the original owner (`ditto`, `tar`, `cp -p` run as root).

People who download the DMG and drag the app in themselves aren't affected, because they own the copy.

## Environment

- Installed app: **v0.13.3** (`dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`), notarized Developer ID build (team `X9LNSP8MC2`), downloaded with Safari on Oct 2.
- Update offered: **v0.14.10**.
- macOS 27.2 (26B123), Apple silicon. SIP enabled.
- Not installed through Homebrew. The only cask in the Caskroom is unrelated.
- The same logic is on `main` at `fd1b11aec6`, so current builds behave the same way. Only the product name in the message has changed since.

## Evidence (usernames, home paths and download IDs redacted)

**The running user is UID 501 and in `admin`. UID 502 doesn't exist on this Mac:**

```
$ id
uid=501(<user>) gid=20(staff) groups=20(staff),...,80(admin),...

$ dscl . -list /Users UniqueID | awk '$2>=500'
<user>                   501
```

**`/Applications` is writable. The bundle is owned by the missing UID 502 and is not:**

```
$ stat -f '%Su(%u):%Sg %Sp %N' /Applications "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app"
root(0):admin drwxrwxr-x /Applications
(502)(502):admin drwxr-xr-x /Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app

$ python3 -I -c 'import os;b="/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app";print("bundle W_OK",os.access(b,os.W_OK));print("parent W_OK",os.access(os.path.dirname(b),os.W_OK))'
bundle W_OK False
parent W_OK True

$ find "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app" ! -user <user> | wc -l
    7085
$ find "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app" -user <user> | wc -l
       0

$ ls -ln "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents" | head -4
-rw-r--r--@  1 502  80  2073 Oct  2 05:00 CodeResources
drwxr-xr-x@ 10 502  80   320 Oct  2 04:51 Frameworks
-rw-r--r--@  1 502  80  2935 Oct  2 04:51 Info.plist
```

All the other apps in `/Applications` are owned by the current user or by root, so this is the only one affected.

**The bundle is genuine and was downloaded normally:**

```
$ spctl -a -vv "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app"
source=Notarized Developer ID
origin=Developer ID Application: <team name> (X9LNSP8MC2)

$ xattr -p com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app"
01c3;6ac0f4e5;Safari;<redacted-uuid>
```

**Probable origin of UID 502:** the bundle's ctime is `Nov 1 15:35:09`. `/Users/Shared` and `/Applications/Utilities` have the same ctime, which fits a migration or restore that day. This hasn't been proven, and the fix below doesn't depend on it.

**The installed v0.13.3 `app.asar` contains the same check:**

```js
if((0,o.existsSync)(e))try{(0,o.accessSync)(e,o.constants.W_OK),(0,o.accessSync)(r.default.dirname(e),o.constants.W_OK)}catch{return`The update can't be installed because Agent Orchestrator's location isn't writable: ${r.default.dirname(e)}. ...`}
```

## Code

**`frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`, `getMacInstallBlocker()`** (added in #3623):

https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/fd1b11aec6fcaa898ba95e696acba68ff6833e93/frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts#L2988-L3001

```ts
  try {
    accessSync(bundle, fsConstants.W_OK);
    // ShipIt writes into the enclosing directory, not just the bundle.
    accessSync(path.dirname(bundle), fsConstants.W_OK);
  } catch {
    return (
      "The update can't be installed because Orchestrator's location isn't " +
      `writable: ${path.dirname(bundle)}. Fix that folder's permissions, or move ` +
      "Orchestrator somewhere you can write to, reopen it, and then " +
      "restart to update."
    );
  }
```

Both checks share one `catch`, so a failure on `bundle` is reported as a failure on `path.dirname(bundle)`.

**Squirrel.Mac already handles this case.** `Squirrel/SQRLUpdater.m`, lines 417–424:

```objc
BOOL targetWritable = [self canWriteToURL:targetURL];
BOOL parentWritable = [self canWriteToURL:targetURL.URLByDeletingLastPathComponent];
BOOL launchPrivileged = !targetWritable || !parentWritable;
...
return [[SQRLShipItLauncher launchPrivileged:launchPrivileged] ...
```

`SQRLShipItLauncher.m` then calls `AuthorizationCreate(... kAuthorizationFlagInteractionAllowed ...)` with the prompt "An update is ready to install.", and submits ShipIt to `kSMDomainSystemLaunchd`. For an admin user, Squirrel would show a password prompt and install the update. Our preflight returns a blocker first, and it also turns off `autoInstallOnAppQuit`, so that path never runs.

**User-facing "AO" string**, `update.restart.prepareFailed`:

- `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/en.json:1954`: `"AO could not prepare the update. Please try again."`
- The same "AO" appears in `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `ru` and `zh-CN`.
- `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx` asserts the old text at lines 288, 390 and 404.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, install the app into `/Applications`. Then give the bundle to another UID:
   ```bash
   sudo chown -R 502 "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app"
   ```
   You can also install it from a second account on the same Mac.
2. Open the app as your normal admin user.
3. Wait for an update to download, then click **Restart to update**.
4. **Expected:** either the update installs after a macOS admin password prompt, or the message correctly says the app is owned by another user and explains how to fix it.
   **Actual:** the update is blocked, and the message says `/Applications` isn't writable, which is false.

## Workaround for affected users

This needs an admin password:

```bash
sudo chown -R "$(whoami)":admin "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app"
```

After running it, quit and reopen Orchestrator, then click **Restart to update**. Dragging a fresh DMG copy into `/Applications` and replacing the old app also works, though Finder may ask for the password.

## Proposed fix

1. **Report the real cause.** Check the bundle and its parent separately and return a different message for each case:
   - **Bundle not writable:** for example, "Orchestrator.app belongs to another user account on this Mac, so it can't be updated. Run `sudo chown -R $(whoami) "<bundle>"` or reinstall it from the DMG." Including the owner UID would help support.
   - **Parent not writable:** keep the current message.
   - Add unit tests for both cases. Mocking `accessSync` per path is enough.
2. **Let Squirrel's admin prompt run.** When the bundle or its parent isn't writable but the user is in the `admin` group, don't block the update. Let `quitAndInstall()` reach Squirrel's privileged ShipIt path, and change the dialog to warn that macOS will ask for a password. Keep the hard block for App Translocation and for users who aren't admins.
   - Before shipping, test this on the current macOS. `SMJobSubmit` with an `AuthorizationRef` is deprecated, so confirm the prompt appears and the swap completes. Check the resulting bundle ownership too, so the next update doesn't hit the same problem.
3. **Fix the wording.** Change `update.restart.prepareFailed` to "Orchestrator could not prepare the update. Please try again." in all 9 locales, and update the 3 test assertions.

## Acceptance criteria

- If the bundle is owned by another UID and `/Applications` is writable, the dialog names the bundle and its owner, not `/Applications`.
- If item 2 lands: an admin user sees the macOS password prompt, and the update installs and relaunches.
- No locale shows "AO" in `update.restart.prepareFailed`.
- Existing behaviour is unchanged for App Translocation and for a parent folder that really isn't writable.

title: feat(chat): steer Hermes with its /steer command
body:
Code changes: +443 -50\
Tests: +1440 -3\
Others: +0 -0

> **Depends on #8016**, which depends on #7702. This branch builds on #8016's `SteerPrompt` binding and generalises it. Until those merge, the diff also shows their commits; review the last commit, `5303be5caf`.

## What

Hermes now steers. A message sent while a turn runs joins that turn and reaches the model at its next step.

- **⌘↩ and the queued card's Steer** both work. The turn stays one turn, with "↳ Steered" on the message.
- **The steer arrives after the current tool call.** It doesn't cut off the model's reply.
- **Versions:** offered on Hermes 0.22.4 and newer, and on builds that report no version, such as Homebrew's 0.22.4, which reports "0.0.0".

## Why

Hermes has two ways to take a message mid-turn over ACP:

- **A plain second `session/prompt`** calls `agent.redirect()`. That cancels the model request in flight and retries with the correction, so the reply in progress is lost.
- **`/steer <text>`** calls `agent.steer()`. Hermes answers the command at once with a note and delivers the text to the running turn after its current tool batch (`acp_adapter/commands.py`, `_cmd_steer`). This is what AO means by Steer.

AO's Hermes driver used neither, so a message sent mid-turn waited in the queue.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| **⌘↩ during a turn.** Hermes had no Steer, so the message was queued and ran as the next turn. | The message joins the running turn. The model gets it on its next request, right after the tool result, and replies in the same turn. ![Hermes: change of plan steered into the running turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/4082b05c3a21d6b61e413a246c70e69bd7fd9d3f/hermes-1-steered.png) |
| **Queued card.** No Steer button. | The card offers Steer while the command runs, and the message joins the turn. ![Hermes: queued change of plan with a Steer button while the command runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/4082b05c3a21d6b61e413a246c70e69bd7fd9d3f/hermes-2-queued.png) ![Hermes: the queued message steered into the running turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/4082b05c3a21d6b61e413a246c70e69bd7fd9d3f/hermes-3-card-steered.png) |
| **Stop after a steer.** Not possible before. | The turn ends once, interrupted, and the next message runs normally. ![Hermes: Stop after a steer, then a normal next turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/4082b05c3a21d6b61e413a246c70e69bd7fd9d3f/hermes-4-stop-after-steer.png) |

## How

- **Builds on #8016's `acp.SteerPrompt`.** A turn's prompts overlap and the turn settles once all of them have returned, with the host's receipt-bearing answer as its result.
- **The `/steer` prompt is a command.** Hermes answers it at once and the running prompt keeps the work. It is marked `_meta["ao.steerKeepsTurn"]`, and the persistent host never takes its answer as the turn's result: the running prompt's answer is, success or failure, in either order. So a failed turn isn't reported completed because the command answered last. If the turn's own prompt answers while a `/steer` command still runs, the host holds that answer until the command answers, so the turn stays open; the watchdog settles a held answer too. Once the client has the host's result, it waits at most 10 s for a command's answer.
  - A steer prompt that fails while another prompt still runs is a refusal, as before.
  - If the turn ends just as a `/steer` is sent, Hermes answers "No active turn" and runs the text inside that request. When it is already idle, it runs the text as a plain prompt instead. The host keeps the turn open until that request answers, so the run belongs to the turn and nothing runs outside it.
  - A steer prompt's late answer for a turn that is over is dropped, so it can't complete that turn twice.
- **Two optional hooks on `SteerPrompt`:**
  - `Prompt` reshapes the guidance. Hermes uses `/steer <text>`, text only; other blocks are refused, not dropped.
  - `Ack` recognises the agent's acknowledgement message. A recognised acknowledgement is kept out of the reply; "↳ Steered" already says it.
  - For an agent with `Ack`, only the acknowledgement says whether a steer took. It settles the steer as soon as it arrives, taken or declined with Hermes' reason, and other prompts' answers say nothing about it. A steer prompt that answers with no acknowledgement within 300 ms is a refusal. So an older or changed Hermes fails safe: the message stays queued instead of being reported as steered.
- **Hermes binding (`hermesacp/steer.go`):**
  - `agentInfo.name` "hermes-agent", version 0.22.4 or newer, or no version ("0.0.0" or non-numeric).
  - Recognises "⏩ Steer queued for the active turn", "No active turn — queued for the next turn" and "⚠️ Steer failed: …"; the last one is a refusal carrying Hermes' reason.
- **`nativeacp`** passes `SteerPrompt` through.
- **Antigravity is unaffected.** Its tests from #8016 pass unchanged: one turn across the handoff, two steers, refusal, and Stop.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/agyacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/hermesacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/nativeacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/` passes. The steering tests also passed 5 times in a row with `-race`. New tests cover:
  - **Acknowledgement first:** one turn, settled by the running prompt, with the acknowledgement kept out of the reply.
  - **Refusals:** a declined acknowledgement is a refusal carrying the agent's reason; an answer with no acknowledgement is a refusal.
  - **No false positives:** acknowledgement-like text in a turn that sent no steer stays visible.
  - **Hermes binding:** version gate, `/steer` shaping, and recognising only Hermes' replies.
  - **Over a scripted host,** with the order the prompt callers are woken in pinned both ways: an acknowledged steer settles with the host's result; a declined acknowledgement stays a refusal before or after the turn's own prompt answers; a turn adopted after a restart can be steered; the running prompt's failure fails the turn; a command answer that never comes doesn't hold the turn; a "No active turn" run stays in the turn until its answers arrive; a late steer answer after a later steered turn is dropped; an accepted acknowledgement starts the next reply segment at once; a straggler's late answer is dropped even after later steered turns. Each fails with its rule reverted.
  - **Relay:** a steer command's answer never settles the turn, whether the running prompt succeeds or fails; a turn's own answer is held while a `/steer` command runs, and settles the turn when the command answers; the watchdog settles a held answer with the stall marker after an answered cancel, and fails the turn without the marker after the grace.
- **Hermes over raw ACP** (`~/.local/bin/hermes` 0.22.5, a scripted OpenAI-compatible model, a scratch `HERMES_HOME` holding only `config.yaml`):
  - **`/steer` during a tool call (2 of 2):** answered at once with the "⏩" note. The first prompt kept the turn, and the model saw the steer right after the tool result.
  - **During plain text (2 of 2):** delivered after the text, as a second request in the same turn.
  - **When idle:** Hermes ran it as an ordinary prompt in that request.
- **Live through AO's driver and host** (`AO_LIVE_HERMES=1`, Hermes 0.22.4, scripted model): steering during a tool call passed 3 of 3; steers sent as the turn ends stayed inside their turns in 3 runs of 8 turns.
- **Live in the desktop app** (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`, Electron profile and `HERMES_HOME`, Homebrew Hermes 0.22.4, which AO picked, plus the scripted model):
  - ⌘↩ during the command, Steer on the queued card, and Stop after a steer all behave as in the screenshots.
  - The model log shows the steer reached the model as Hermes' out-of-band user message, after the tool result, in the same turn.
  - The first run in the app found that Homebrew reports version "0.0.0", which turned Steer off. That's fixed here.
- **Lint:** `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on the whole backend reports one issue, in `internal/service/shellagent/manager.go` (`watchRetryMin`). It comes from `main` (#7787), not this PR.
- **Not run locally:** the full backend race suite. The touched packages pass, and #8016's full suite run covered the rest of this stack. No frontend changes.
- **Not re-run after the review fixes:** the raw-ACP and desktop runs above. The fixes change how AO settles steers and turns, not what it sends to Hermes.

## Known limitations

- **No live test against Hermes 0.23.0.** Its `/steer` and `_claim_turn_or_queue` code is the same as 0.22.5's (read from the v0.23.0 tag).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Send guidance to supported agents while a conversation is running, with delivery status handled across different steering methods.
  * Added steering support for additional ACP-based agents, including newer versions of the agy CLI.
  * The app can use the built-in agy ACP server when available, with fallback to the separate server.
  * Interrupting a conversation withdraws guidance the agent has not yet received.

title: bug(desktop): the main pane can shift 44 px left, hiding the session tab under the sidebar
body:
### Report

The app's main pane can end up shifted 44 px to the left. When that happens, the session tab's left edge, with the agent icon and the first letters of the session name, slides under the sidebar. Every button on the right moves left too, and a blank strip appears along the right edge of the window. It stays that way until the window reloads.

### What happens

On `main` at `c147beb01c`, in the desktop app (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`, macOS):

1. Open any session or project page.
2. Something inside the centre pane is scrolled into view by code. In my case it was test automation clicking a button near the right edge; any `scrollIntoView` or `focus()` that reaches the pane does the same.
3. The pane scrolls sideways by exactly 44 px and stays there.

| | Centre pane `scrollLeft` | Session tab |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh page | 0 | Fully visible |
| After `scrollIntoView()` on the hidden forward swipe arrow | **44** (on `div.relative.min-h-0.flex-1.overflow-x-hidden`) | Left edge hidden under the sidebar ("Orchestrator ‸gy-steer"), blank strip on the right |
| Same call, with that container switched to `overflow-x: clip` | 0 | Fully visible |

I first noticed it in screenshots taken for #8016. From the step it appeared at, it was Playwright scrolling a right-side element into view before clicking it. I couldn't trigger it with ordinary actions: a two-finger sideways swipe and drag-selecting text to the right edge both left the pane alone. So I can't say how often users hit it, but any code path that scrolls an element into view inside the pane can cause it.

### Cause

`SwipeNavigation` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SwipeNavigation.tsx`) parks its two arrows invisible (`opacity-0`), just past the pane's edges: `translate3d(±44px, -50%, 0)` (`PUCK_HIDDEN_PX = -44`). The forward arrow therefore overhangs the right edge by 44 px.

The pane that hosts it, `routes/_shell.tsx:1570` (`relative min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-x-hidden`), hides the overhang with `overflow-x: hidden`. `hidden` blocks user scrolling but still lets code scroll the box, so any `scrollIntoView`, focus scroll or `scrollLeft` change can move it up to that 44 px.

The project-settings dialog mounts the same arrows (`SettingsDialog.tsx:585`).

### Expected

The parked arrows shouldn't make any pane scrollable. Clipping them in a box that can't scroll (`overflow: clip`) keeps them hidden while parked, and leaves them fully visible during a swipe.

title: fix(desktop): keep the parked swipe arrows from scrolling the pane sideways
body:
Code changes: +6 -2\
Tests: +18 -0\
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #8023.

## What

The app's centre pane can no longer be pushed 44 px to the left. That shift hid the session tab's left edge under the sidebar and left a blank strip on the right.

## Why

`SwipeNavigation` parks its two swipe arrows invisible, 44 px past the pane's edges (`PUCK_HIDDEN_PX = -44`). The pane hides the overhang with `overflow-x: hidden` (`routes/_shell.tsx:1570`). `hidden` blocks user scrolling, but code can still scroll the box, so any `scrollIntoView`, focus scroll or `scrollLeft` change could move it by the arrow's overhang, and it stayed there. Details and the live reproduction are in #8023.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `scrollIntoView()` on the hidden forward arrow scrolls the centre pane by 44 px. The tab reads "Orchestrator ‸gy-steer" and a blank strip appears on the right. ![The centre pane shifted 44 px left](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/08074b2d3b30ef59de7b19b791ffef5ec96aa9e5/before-shifted.png) | The same call on both arrows scrolls nothing. ![The layout unchanged after scrollIntoView on both arrows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/08074b2d3b30ef59de7b19b791ffef5ec96aa9e5/after-no-shift.png) |
| — | Mid-swipe, both arrows still show in full inside the pane, set to the position and armed state a swipe gives them. ![Both swipe arrows fully visible](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/08074b2d3b30ef59de7b19b791ffef5ec96aa9e5/after-arrows-visible.png) |

## How

- `SwipeNavigation` renders both arrows inside `<div class="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 overflow-clip">`. `overflow: clip` hides the parked overhang like `hidden` does, but the box can't be scrolled, by code or otherwise.
- The fix sits in the component, so both places that mount the arrows are covered: the shell's centre pane and the project-settings dialog (`SettingsDialog.tsx:585`).
- **Not changed:**
  - The swipe logic.
  - The arrow positions. The box fills the same positioned container the arrows used before, so the arrows land where they did.
  - The arrows' `z-chrome` layering. The box adds no stacking context.

## Testing

- **Unit test:** `SwipeNavigation.test.tsx` gains "clips the parked pucks in a box that cannot be scrolled". It fails on the old component and passes with the fix. `SwipeNavigation.test.tsx` and `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` pass, 68 tests.
- **Live in the desktop app** (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` and Electron profile, built from this branch):
  - `scrollIntoView()` on both arrows, in the centre pane and in the project-settings dialog, leaves every element at `scrollLeft` 0. Both boxes report `overflow-x: clip`.
  - On the old code, the same call in the centre pane gave `scrollLeft` 44 on `div.relative.min-h-0.flex-1.overflow-x-hidden`.
  - With both arrows set to the visible swipe state (`translate3d(±18px)`, opacity 1, armed), they render fully inside the pane, as in the screenshot.
  - Not tested live: a real trackpad swipe. In Electron the handler only follows wheel events while macOS reports fingers down, so synthetic wheel events from automation are ignored, on `main` too. The swipe logic is unchanged, and its unit tests pass.
- **Typecheck:** `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass.
- **Full renderer suite** (`vitest run`): 12,217 passed and 53 failed, in 5 files. None are caused by this change:
  - `IndependentSideChatDelivery`, `GlobalSettingsForm` and `shell-new-session-shortcut` pass when run alone (35, 60 and 83 tests).
  - `browser-cookie-repair` (2 failures) and `browser-profile-import` (49 failures) fail the same way with `main`'s component, because they depend on this Mac's browser profiles.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: docs: match the marketing site's design and compile Tailwind
body:
Code changes: +701 -90\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +7 -0 (PostCSS config)

**Companion PR:** OrchestratorInc/ao-landing#138 restyles the changelog in the same design. Its Cloudflare preview is at https://claude-stoic-pascal-f3rud4.ao-landing.pages.dev/changelog/. The docs site deploys only from `main`, so this PR has no preview deploy. To see it, run `npm run dev` in `frontend/src/docs`.

## What

Redesigns the docs site (docs.orchestrator.inc) in the marketing site's (orchestrator.inc) visual language, and fixes the docs build so Tailwind actually compiles.

- **Colors:** `tokens.css` takes the marketing site's blue-slate neutrals (hue 257) in place of the olive-green ones (hue 107).
- **Texture:** the marketing home page's binary-matrix background runs behind every page.
- **Sidebar:** section labels styled like the site's feature tags, quieter rows, and one sky marker on the current page, top level or nested.
- **Articles:** light page titles; h2 sections ruled off by hairlines; links white with a sky underline.
- **Code and tables:** code blocks and tables on the site's panel color in hairline frames; tables drop the doubled and vertical rules.
- **Callouts:** an icon and a tone per type (sky note, amber warning, red error), without the stray paragraph margins.
- **Components:** cards and plugin cards on panels with a hover state and an arrow; numbered steps on a guide line; accordions with a chevron.
- **Installation:** the download table becomes one card per platform with a button per package. Asset file names are unchanged, so `release-latest-guard` still finds them.
- **Page actions:** use the site's quiet secondary button.

## Why

The docs looked like a separate, older site: an olive-green tint, default fumadocs chrome, and custom components that rendered broken.

The broken components came from a bug. `frontend/src/docs` had **no PostCSS config**, so Tailwind never ran. `global.css` shipped its `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@tailwind utilities` unprocessed. The only utilities on the page were the ones fumadocs' precompiled CSS happened to include. As a result, classes used only by our own components were missing: `<Cards>` stacked full width instead of a grid, card links kept their underline, and platform status dots had no size (`size-1.5` was absent from the built CSS). Adding the `@tailwindcss/postcss` plugin, already a dev dependency, fixes both `next dev` and the static export.

## Before / After

I couldn't upload images from the session that made this PR, so the screenshots are not attached yet (see below).

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Olive-tinted neutrals (hue 107), default fumadocs sidebar | Marketing site's blue-slate neutrals, binary-matrix texture, sidebar section labels and a sky current-page marker |
| `<Cards>` stacked full width, card text underlined | Two-column card grid, no underline, hover state and arrow |

| Installation: plain download table | One card per platform with a download button per package |
| Built CSS contains a raw `@tailwind utilities` line, and `.size-1\.5` is missing | No raw directive left; the docs' own utilities are generated |

Screenshots (1440px wide, local dev server, same pages before and after) are in the Claude Code session that produced this PR, as `docs-redesign.png`. They need attaching here by hand.

## How

- **Tokens:** `tokens.css` and `prose.css` stay copies of the marketing site's files. Only the color values in `tokens.css` changed, copied exactly from ao-landing's `styles/tokens.css`. All docs-specific overrides live unlayered at the end of `global.css`, so they win over the unlayered `prose.css` and fumadocs' layered utilities.
- **Plain CSS for new pieces:** the page title (`.docs-title`), the matrix (`.docs-matrix`), steps and callout bodies use plain CSS classes rather than utilities, so they don't depend on utility generation.
- **Binary matrix:** `binary-matrix.tsx` is a copy of ao-landing's `BinaryMatrix`. It sits fixed at `z-index: -1` behind the layout, with `pointer-events: none`, pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs, and skips the ambient twinkle for reduced-motion users.
- **Review focus:**

  - `DESIGN.md` rules out decorative textures in the working UI. This is the public docs site, styled to match the marketing site on request, not the desktop app.

title: fix(chat): let compacted Claude sessions switch from Terminal to Chat
body:
Code changes: +239 -8\
Tests: +393 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Claude Code sessions that have compacted, either automatically or with `/compact`, can now switch from Terminal to Chat. The native checkpoint reader now reads a compacted transcript the way Chat's replay does, instead of rejecting it.

## Why

Switching such a session to Chat failed every time, on desktop and mobile, with:

> switch interface …: resume chat: wait for native checkpoint: claude native checkpoint: compacted native ancestry requires reconciliation: chat conversation history is not settled: checkpoint mismatches [unsettled_turn_boundary]: context deadline exceeded

`verifyCheckpointTranscript` returned "unsettled" as soon as it read a `compact_boundary` record. `verifyNativeCheckpoint` treats "unsettled" as "Claude has not flushed yet" and retried this permanent answer for 3 s before failing. The TUI had already been stopped for the handoff, so the user was left on "Session terminated". Long sessions are the ones that compact, so this hit exactly the sessions people most want to keep.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal → Chat on a compacted Claude session fails after 3 s with `compacted native ancestry requires reconciliation … context deadline exceeded` | The switch settles on the latest prompt after the compaction, as for an uncompacted session |
| Same failure after a manual `/compact` | Settles: the `/compact` command and output records are skipped, as replay skips them |
| Transcripts over 64 MiB fail with a misleading `incomplete native record` | The bound applies to the history since the latest compaction; a 110 MiB compacted transcript settles |
| — | Switching before any prompt since the compaction still fails, now with `no native user prompt since compaction` |

## How

All changes are in `claudeacp/checkpoint.go`. The checkpoint must name a turn that Chat's `session/load` replay will show. Replay comes from the Agent SDK's `getSessionMessages`, so the reader follows that function's rules:

- **Kept messages.** A `compact_boundary` has no parent, and the summary after it starts the visible history. Claude Code keeps the newest messages from before the boundary (`compactMetadata.preservedMessages`, or the older `preservedSegment`). The SDK hangs them after the summary at load time; the append-only log never rewrites them. `relinkCompactedTranscript` applies the same re-parenting, so the walk from the leaf crosses the summary and the kept messages and ends at the latest boundary.
- **Evidence from before the compaction.** Hook observations accumulate for the whole native session, so they include prompts the compaction hid. An observation whose prompt or submission correlation was flushed before the latest boundary is settled by that boundary, because replay cannot show it. A turn that ran on through the compaction keeps its prompt ID on the summary record (true in every real transcript I checked). It is marked `carried`. Compacting between turns puts the summary right under the boundary. Compacting mid-turn (Claude Code 2.1.306 to 2.1.318) first writes `instructions`, `session_context` and `date` attachments, so `followsCompaction` walks up through attachments to find the boundary. If Claude answered in it after the boundary (`resumed`), it is checked as before: it must complete and match its Stop text.
- **`/compact` records.** The command, its arguments and its stdout are user records under the summary's prompt ID. `claude-agent-acp` strips local-command markers on replay and skips messages that end up empty. `claudeLocalCommandMetadata` ports that rule so these records are notes, not a second turn with the same prompt ID.
- **Size bound.** At each boundary, earlier records are folded into the compacted sets and dropped, except the kept messages. The existing 64 MiB bound now covers only the records retained since the latest compaction. A separate 1 GiB cap bounds the total read. A set of UUIDs is kept so duplicates are still detected across dropped records.

What reviewers should check:

- Settling evidence by "flushed before the latest boundary" is the trust decision here. The boundary is written after those records in an append-only log, and replay cannot show them, so Chat has nothing to lose. A Stop for a turn that ended before the compaction no longer has its text compared, because no replayed turn exists to compare it with.
- One case still fails, deliberately: switching before any human prompt since the compaction. Replay starts at the summary, which Chat skips, so it has no user turn for `nativeBoundary` to match.
- Possible follow-up, not changed here: `nativeHistoryCheckpoint`'s AO high-water gate checks AO's latest durable turns against replay. If a session's latest Chat turn is older than a compaction, that gate would still report `ao_high_water`. In the usual case, the latest turn comes after the compaction.
- The SDK reads files over 5 MB from the last boundary only. If it then cannot find every `preservedMessages` UUID, it skips the re-parenting. This reader always reads the whole file, so it always re-parents. The two can differ only in which turn the kept messages attach to. That decides the boundary only when no prompt follows the compaction, which already fails.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/` and `-race`. New `checkpoint_compaction_test.go` covers:
  - Settling after a compaction, with `preservedMessages`, with `preservedSegment`, and with nothing kept.
  - Repeated compactions.
  - A turn that runs through the compaction, with the summary under the boundary and under the real mid-turn context attachments, including a pending tail and a wrong Stop text.
  - Manual `/compact` records.
  - Unknown prompts and submissions still failing closed.
  - No prompt since the compaction, and a boundary not yet followed by its summary.
  - SDK-equivalent re-parenting.
  - The size bound counting only the history since the compaction.
- Ran the reader on all 19 compacted Claude transcripts on my machine (0.4 to 110 MiB), with a Stop observation for each file's last prompt. 14 settle. The other 5 have no human prompt after their last compaction, which I confirmed separately. Before this change, all 19 failed.
- `go vet` and `golangci-lint v2.13.2` (0 issues) on the touched package. `go test -race ./internal/service/chat/` passes.
- `go test ./...` on my machine: everything I changed passes. It also reports failures I didn't cause, all present on `main` too:
  - `runtime/tmux`, `agent/commandcode`, `agent/opencodev2`, `service/shellterm` and `service/systemcheck` don't import `claudeacp`.
  - The failing tests in `cli`, `integration` (`TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch`) and `session_manager` fail the same way with `main`'s `checkpoint.go` swapped in and `AO_*` cleared.

title: fix(remote): don't count requests without a password toward the lockout
body:
Code changes: +11 -7\
Tests: +52 -1\
Others: +4 -3

## What

- The daemon no longer counts a request that carries no password toward the remote access lockout. It still gets 401.
- The phone's lockout message no longer tells you to check your password. It says the machine is pausing connections from this network after too many wrong passwords, possibly from another device on the same network.

## Why

Fixes #7980.

Opening the tunnel URL in a browser requests `/`, `/favicon.ico` and the touch icons without a password. Through the tunnel, every device behind the visitor's public IP shares one lockout (`CF-Connecting-IP`). Five of those requests locked the phone out, and the correct password then got 429. The phone's message said to check the password even when it was right.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| 5 tokenless requests from one tunnel visitor, then the correct password: **429** | Same sequence: **200** |
| 5 wrong passwords, then the correct password: 429 | Unchanged: 429 |
| "Your machine locked this device out after too many failed attempts. It clears on its own in about a minute — check the password, then try again." | "Your machine is pausing connections from this network after too many wrong passwords, possibly from another device on the same network. It clears on its own in about a minute." |

No screenshot: the change is one string in an existing error state.

## How

- `authMiddleware` skips `lock.fail` when `connectionToken` returns `""`. That covers no `Authorization` header, an empty `Bearer `, and a preview file request without the cookie. A request with no password reveals nothing about it, so brute-force protection is unchanged: every wrong password still counts, and 5 still block the source for a minute.
- Password-less requests neither add to nor clear an existing count.
- The 429 line in `userFacingError` got the same wording change.
- ADR 0001 and the mobile README now say "5 wrong passwords" instead of "5 failed attempts".

Related: draft #7285 by @ronishrohan counts each distinct wrong password once and a missing password once. The two changes are complementary and touch the same `lock.fail` call. If #7285 lands after this, its "missing password counts once / counts as a guess" test cases need to expect no count. Not addressed here: #7981 (`:443` in the Host field), #6765 (logging rejected LAN requests).

## Testing

- New `TestTokenlessRequestsDoNotCountTowardLockout` (browser-style tunnel requests, then the correct password → 200; wrong passwords interleaved with password-less requests still → 429). It failed with 429 before the fix.
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/httpd/`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l`: pass.
- `cd packages/mobile && npx vitest run` (3536 tests) and `npx tsc --noEmit`: pass. The rate-limited copy test now requires "same network" and forbids "check the password".
- Not tried on a device or against a real quick tunnel.

title: bug(ci): the archive occlusion check in window-transparency-overlap fails intermittently in renderer-smoke
body:
### Report

`frontend / renderer-smoke (2)` fails intermittently on `e2e/window-transparency-overlap.spec.ts` › "@P0 sticky project and archive occlude sessions". It happens on PRs that don't touch the code it checks, and a re-run picks a different variant to fail. CI keeps no screenshots of the failure, so it can only be re-run, not inspected.

### What happens

The failing assertion is in `expectOccludes`, on the board's archive panel:

```
Error: content underneath must not affect the surface's pixels
> 34 | 	expect(before.equals(after), "content underneath must not affect the surface's pixels").toBe(true);
```

Seen on 2026-11-09:

| Run | PR | Failed variants |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [42596130756](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42596130756), attempt 1 | #8024 (swipe arrows) | dark + transparency on (failed, and failed its retry); light + transparency off (failed, then passed on retry) |
| Same run, attempt 2 | #8024 | dark + transparency off (failed, and failed its retry); the other three passed |

At the same time, `main` at `c147beb01c` passed this job, and so did #8016 and #8022. (An earlier version of this table listed #8020's run [42595697362](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/42595697362). That run failed in `updates-settings.spec.ts`, not this spec.)

On `main` since #8024 merged (`6f4f9415ae`), from `renderer-smoke (2)` logs:

| | Runs | Runs where this spec failed | First-attempt variant failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before #8024 (`d022509b3c` … `aebf2029c4`) | 22 | 0 | 0 |
| From #8024 (`6f4f9415ae` … `d25418c4a2`) | 8 | 8 (5 red, 3 green on retry) | 14 of 32 |

Every failure is the archive call (line 72), never the sticky project row. The opaque variants fail too.

Locally on macOS (Chromium headless shell 148), it passes every time:
- 40 runs with 2 workers: all 80 comparisons pixel-identical.
- 32 runs under 4× CPU throttling (CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`): all 64 comparisons identical.

I couldn't run CI's Linux image (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble`) here, so the exact pixel difference on CI hasn't been seen yet.

### Cause

It started with #8024, as pointed out in the #8031 review. The opaque variants fail too, where the archive is `z-20` with alpha 255, so cards can't paint through it. The archive's own pixels change between the two captures. The `ResizeObserver` timing suggested here first doesn't explain that.

#8024 moved the two swipe arrows (`z-chrome`, `opacity-0`, `translate3d(±44px, -50%, 0)`) out of the centre pane, where its `overflow-x: hidden` clipped them, into `<div class="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 overflow-clip">` in `SwipeNavigation.tsx`, which covers the pane above the board.

How that changes the archive's pixels isn't known yet. It doesn't reproduce on macOS, even with Chromium on SwiftShader. A CI run with only the wrapper reverted, with the before and after images, will show:
- whether the wrapper is the trigger;
- whether the change is visible to users (a product bug in `SwipeNavigation`) or only a compositing difference between captures.

The `renderer-smoke` job has no artifact upload, so the actual before and after images from CI are lost.

### Expected

- The occlusion check compares screenshots taken once the surface has settled. It should still fail when content really shows through.
- A failure keeps its images, so the next one can be diagnosed from CI instead of being re-run.

title: test(e2e): compare settled screenshots in the occlusion check, keep failures
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +27 -2\
Others: +11 -0

Refs #8029. (It will close #8029 only once the CI run with #8024's wrapper reverted is in.)

## What

`window-transparency-overlap.spec.ts`'s occlusion check no longer fails because of timing on slow runners. When it does fail, its screenshots are kept, so the failure can be inspected instead of only re-run.

## Why

The check takes one screenshot of a surface (the board archive, or a sticky project row), hides the content underneath, takes a second one, and requires them to be identical.

It started failing with #8024. In `renderer-smoke (2)` on `main`, none of the 22 runs before #8024 merged (`6f4f9415ae`) failed this spec, and all 8 runs since did: 14 of 32 variant attempts failed first time, 5 runs went red, and the other 3 passed only on retry. Every failure is the archive check, never the sticky project row, and the opaque variants fail too. Cards can't paint through an opaque archive, so the archive's own pixels change between the two captures. Details are in #8029.

#8024 moved the two swipe arrows (`z-chrome`, `opacity-0`, `translate3d(±44px, -50%, 0)`) out of the centre pane, where its `overflow-x: hidden` clipped them, into `<div class="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 overflow-clip">`, which covers the whole pane above the board. Why that changes the archive's pixels isn't known yet. It doesn't reproduce on macOS, even with Chromium on SwiftShader. A CI run with only that wrapper reverted, with images, will show whether the wrapper is the trigger, and whether the change is visible to users (a product bug to fix in `SwipeNavigation`) or only a compositing difference between captures (what this test change handles).

The `renderer-smoke` job uploads nothing on failure, so CI's actual images were lost.

## How

- **Bracketed captures.** `expectOccludes` takes three captures: content shown, content hidden, content shown again.
  - If the two "shown" captures differ, the surface changed on its own, so the attempt says nothing about what's underneath. It's retried, up to 5 times, 100 ms apart, and each one is recorded as a "surface changed on its own" annotation.
  - If they match and the hidden capture differs, the content underneath shows through and the test fails.
  - If all 5 attempts change on their own, the test fails with its own message.
- **The comparison is still strict:** pixel-identical, no threshold.
- **On a failure,** the captures are written to the test's output folder (`surface-with-content-underneath.png`, `surface-with-content-hidden.png`, and `surface-with-content-underneath-again.png` when the surface kept changing) and attached to the report.
- **`frontend.yml`:** the `renderer-smoke` job uploads `frontend/test-results/` when it fails, as `renderer-smoke-results-<shard>-attempt-<n>`, one per run attempt, kept for 7 days. It uses `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, like `build-artifacts.yml`. This is a separate part of the change; reviewers can drop it if CI artifacts aren't wanted.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Since #8024, failed in about 4 of 9 attempts in `renderer-smoke (2)`, with no artifacts to inspect. | A capture pair is only judged when the surface didn't change on its own around it. On a real failure, the images land in `test-results/` and CI uploads them. |

There are no UI changes.

## Testing

- **The spec, locally** (macOS, Chromium headless shell 148, `CI=1`, no retries): 40 runs of the 4 variants with 2 workers, all passing. Main's single-capture version also passes here every time, including under 4× CPU throttling and with Chromium on SwiftShader, so the CI-only failure isn't reproducible on this Mac. See #8029.
- **It still catches show-through.** In a scratch copy, with the archive made transparent and the clip on the lanes behind it removed, the test fails with "content underneath must not affect the surface's pixels", and both PNGs are written to `test-results/<test>/`.
- **It retries a surface that changes on its own.** With the archive's background changed once, the moment the cards are hidden, attempt 1 is recorded as changed and attempt 2 passes.
- **A surface that keeps changing** (background flipped every 16 ms): one run failed after 3 changed attempts, with the message saying so. Another passed, because one attempt's three captures matched by chance. Nothing showed through in that case, so a pass is still correct about occlusion.
- **`npm run typecheck:e2e`** passes.
- **`frontend.yml`** parses (Ruby `YAML.load_file`).
- **Not verified:** the upload step itself. It only runs on a failing `renderer-smoke` job.

title: fix(inspector): list Summary artifacts newest first with their update time
body:
3 files changed (1 source, 1 component, 1 test)

## What
The session inspector's Summary panel now lists artifacts newest first, and each row shows when the file was last updated (compact relative time, with the full time in a tooltip).

## Why
Users could not find new artifacts in a session. The control plane and daemon return artifacts ordered by path, and `sessionArtifacts()` passed that order straight through, so the Summary list was alphabetical and showed no timestamps. title: fix(mobile): show failed tool servers the way the desktop does
body: Code changes: +159 -20\ Tests: +211 -16\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The mobile chat screen now reports MCP servers that failed to start the way the desktop does (`McpServerBanner` in `ChatStatusBanners.tsx`). Instead of a yellow banner across the top of the conversation, a one-line note appears just above the composer, for example "Aws-mcp, Posthog, Canva, Notion didn’t start. Continuing without them." It fades after 3 s. ## Why The yellow banner, with the provider's failure reason (`reauthenticationRequired`), Reload and a close button, took a lot of space at the top of every conversation with a broken tool server. There is nothing to do about it from the conversation, so the desktop just says it once, quietly, and moves on. Mobile now matches that. ## Before / After Same session (`agent-orchestrator-mo-132`, four failed servers), same iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5, dark). | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Banner stays until closed, and comes back on the next visit | Shown once per run of the session, then fades. Reopening the session does not show it again | The GIF is a screenshot burst at its real timing (about 0.6 s per frame). ## How - New `McpServerNotice` (`packages/mobile/lib/chat/McpServerNotice.tsx`) ports the desktop component. It uses the same copy (`chat.mcpNotice.unavailable`, names capitalised), 3 s show plus 200 ms fade, and once-per-incarnation memory. It is keyed on host, session id and the session's `createdAt`, the way the desktop keys on `session.createdAt`. An in-memory set covers remounts, and AsyncStorage (`ao:mcp-notice-shown:`) keeps a relaunch from replaying it. It is announced to screen readers once. - It waits until the chat screen is focused and the app is in the foreground, like the desktop's `active` prop. The chat stays mounted under pushed routes (Changes, a file, Preview, another session) and under chat sheets. Those are bottom sheets over the composer, right where the note sits, so the screen passes plain `useIsFocused()` rather than the view lease's "focused or under chat sheets" test. The note counts as read only after its full 3 s on screen. If it is covered sooner, by a route or a sheet, it goes back to waiting and shows again when the chat is back in front. - It sits inside the composer's `KeyboardFollower` as a zero-height strip, so it floats over the bottom of the timeline, rides the keyboard with the composer, and never changes the composer's measured height. It ignores touches, and it is held back while the Terminal switch card is up, like the other banners. - The glyph is the registry's `disconnected` symbol (SF `powerplug` / Material `power_off`), standing in for the desktop's lucide `Plug`. - **Intentional omission:** the banner's **Reload** button is removed. It was mobile's only MCP reload control, and the desktop has none. If reload is worth keeping on mobile, it should go in the conversation menu rather than back in a banner. - Like the desktop, the note is a single truncated line. With four servers on a 402 pt-wide phone it ends at "Continuing w…". ## Testing - `cd packages/mobile && npm run typecheck`: clean. - `npx vitest run`: 3545 passed. `McpServerNotice.test.tsx` covers what the desktop's `McpServerBanner` tests do: the copy, 3 s on screen then a 200 ms fade, waiting while no server has failed, once per run across remounts (in-memory record) and relaunches (AsyncStorage), a restarted session (new `createdAt`) showing it again, a failed storage read still showing it, and waiting while the chat is covered. title: fix(remote): harden remote host credential storage and lockout
body:
Five small fixes to how remote host credentials are stored, shown and rate limited. No protocol change.

- **Renderer never sees account host tokens.** Main syncs and links account hosts (`remotes:syncAccountHosts`, `remotes:linkAccountHost`). The Cloud proxy strips `token` from `/me/hosts` responses to the renderer and refuses that path on the binary and stream channels. Replaces `remotes:importAccountHost`, `remotes:pruneAccountHosts` and `remotes:issueAccountToken`.
- **`remotes.json` passwords encrypted with `safeStorage`.** An existing file is rewritten on launch. A password that can't be decrypted is kept, not wiped. On Linux `basic_text` they stay plaintext (0600) as before, so hand-paired hosts survive restarts.
- **`ao remote-host status` hides the password** unless `--show-password` is passed. `enable` still prints it; `setup-self-hosted.sh` parses that output.
- **Lockout counts failures per IPv6 /64** instead of per address.
- **Retired password hashes capped at 8.**

Tests:
- `go test ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/cli/...` passes. Three `cli` tests fail only inside an AO session, where they read `AO_SESSION_ID`; they pass with the `AO_*` variables unset.
- vitest: `remotes-store`, `remotes-main`, `remotes-ipc`, `cloud-cp-proxy`, `useRemoteHosts*`, `RemoteHostsSettings`, `ThisComputerAccess`, `link-this-computer`, `preload` pass.

Not covered: the mobile app still reads host tokens from AO Cloud directly.

title: fix(desktop): replace the CLI shadow toast with a quiet Settings entry
body:
Code changes: +28 -84\
Tests: +149 -123\
Others: +0 -9

## What

Removes the `CliShadowBanner` toast, so the app no longer pops up a warning about another `ao` on `PATH` in any build. Detection and **Use this app's ao** stay in Settings, which now stays empty in dev and isolated-profile builds.

## Why

Follows #7783. The toast caused more noise than help:

- **Noisy "different" warnings:** passive detection never runs the other binary, so its version is unknown and the relation is always `different` until the user clicks **Run ao version**.
- **Reset on every nightly or profile:** dismissal lived in `localStorage` under `ao.cli-shadow-dismissed-identity.v2`, keyed on the file's identity, so a replaced binary or a new profile warned again.
- **Permanent in dev:** a dev build's `ao` comes from its checkout, so any `ao` on `PATH` differs by design. `dev` versions can't be ordered either, so even **Run ao version** left it `different`.

## Before / After

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Launch, another `ao` first on `PATH` | Toast bottom right | Nothing pops up |
| Settings > General, installed build | Row with Details and fix | Same row |
| Settings > General, dev build | Row, permanently | No row |
| Settings > General, packaged with `AO_DATA_DIR` or `AO_RUN_FILE` | Row | No row |
| Login-shell probe on launch | Every launch | Only when Settings > General opens, installed builds only |

No screenshots: the only visual change is that something no longer appears, and the local build was skipped on purpose (see Testing).

## How

- **Gate (`cliShadowEnabled`):** true only when `app.isPackaged` and neither `AO_DATA_DIR` nor `AO_RUN_FILE` is set. A blank value counts as unset.
- **Where it applies:** the three `cliShadow:*` IPC handlers check it first. When off, `inspect` answers `unknown` before the login-shell probe, `replace` refuses, and `reveal` does nothing. So dev builds can't reach the replace flow either.
- **Unchanged:** `inspectCliShadow`, `replaceCliShadow`, and their identity checks and staged swap. `cliLinkSupport` still handles AppImage and translocated installs.
- **Removed with the toast:** `cliShadow.dismiss` in all 9 locales, the dismissal key, and the `surface` prop on `CliShadowActions`, which only existed to style the toast variant.

**`ao doctor`: no new check in this PR.** The passive check already exists: `ao-binary` uses `LookPath` and `os.Stat`, never runs the other binary, and warns "ao in PATH is X, which shadows the running daemon's binary Y" (`TestDoctorChecksAOBinaryIdentity`). `ao-login-shell` covers aliases and startup files using `command -v`.

The remaining gap is `ao doctor` run from an AO zsh or bash terminal, where `PATH` is pinned to the app's `ao`, so a stale copy that only a plain terminal would hit isn't reported. Closing it needs decisions I didn't want to guess:

1. Whether doctor should warn in dev builds. The Go side has no `isPackaged`, and a permanent warning there repeats the problem this PR removes.
2. A passive check can only say "different", not "older", which is the wording this PR moves away from.
3. It needs the user's unpinned login-shell `PATH`, including fish, whose output format differs.

## Testing

Not run locally, per the maintainer's preference: no tests, typecheck, build or app launch. CI verifies. The dev-build behaviour above comes from reading the code path, not from running a dev app.

- New: `cli-shadow-ipc.test.ts` (disabled means no shell probe, replace refused, nothing revealed; enabled still probes), and `cliShadowEnabled` cases in `cli-shadow.test.ts`.
- `CliShadowBanner.test.tsx` moved to `settings/CliShadowSettingsRow.test.tsx`, with the version-probe consent, replace, failure and manual-fix cases now targeting the row. Deleted the two dismissal cases, the "no notice for same/newer" case and the toast-plus-row case.

To check by hand:

1. Install a build of this branch and put a different executable named `ao` first on your login shell's `PATH`.
2. Launch the app. Confirm no toast appears.
3. Open Settings > General. Confirm the "Your terminal runs a different ao" row appears, then use **Use this app's ao** and confirm the row clears.
4. Run `npm run dev` in `frontend` with the same `PATH`. Open Settings > General and confirm the row is absent.

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable

- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording

title: feat: add ZCode TUI-only harness support
body:
Code changes: +433 -3
Tests: +498 -0
Others: +86 -0 (docs)

## What

Register the official OSS ZCode CLI ([zai-org/ZCode](https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode), CLI source at `apps/zcode-cli`) as a **Terminal-UI-only** agent harness, branched fresh from `main`:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/zcode/` — a self-contained adapter modeled on the existing TUI-only templates (`crush`, `memcode`): manifest, PATH-first binary resolution (plus Homebrew and Node version-manager locations), launch, restore, prompt delivery, auth probe, and supervisor exit detection.
- `zcode --cwd <worktree> [--mode <mode>] [--disallowed-tools <names>]` launches the interactive TUI; worker task prompts are delivered after startup. Only flags documented in the CLI's own reference (`apps/zcode-cli/docs/usage/02-cli-reference.md`) are ever passed. Launches that request a model/effort override or a tool allowlist fail rather than run with the override silently dropped — the CLI documents no `--model`/`--allowed-tools` flags.
- Permission mapping: default → no flag, accept-edits → `--mode edit`, auto → `--mode build`, bypass → `--mode yolo`. A project's agent config may set `mode` directly (`plan|build|edit|yolo|guarded`); a per-spawn permissions override wins.
- **No Chat driver is registered** for the harness. Per the chatdriver registry's contract, chat-mode spawns fail with `ErrChatUnsupported` — TUI sessions only. That is the point of this PR.
- Restore emits `--resume <id>` when a native session id is known and otherwise falls back to the documented `--continue` (latest session for the same working directory; AO worktrees are one-session-per-directory). No hooks are installed in this PR.
- `domain.AllHarnesses` gains `zcode`; the shared `AgentConfig` mode vocabulary (validated on write) gains ZCode's modes alongside Amp's existing ones.

## Why

ZCode's OSS release removed the old objections to a TUI integration: the CLI documents `--cwd`, `--mode plan|build|edit|yolo|guarded`, and `--resume <sessionId>` / `--continue` as top-level args, so an interactive-only adapter needs none of the previously-missing surfaces. This provides the minimal main-based shape; a richer Chat/protocol integration exists separately in #6003 and is intentionally left untouched.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `ao spawn --agent zcode` rejects the harness (`zcode` is unknown) | Spawns an interactive ZCode TUI session in the worktree; `ao agent ls` lists ZCode |
| Chat-mode spawn | Still fails with `ErrChatUnsupported` — deliberate: ZCode ships no chat driver |
| Project agent config rejects `mode: plan` | Accepts `plan|build|edit|yolo|guarded` for ZCode sessions |

## Desktop evidence (isolated lab, fresh data dir)

Captured from isolated desktop labs (AGENTS.md recipe: fresh clone per side, `npm ci`, `--dev` daemon, scratch `AO_DATA_DIR`, real Electron app over CDP). **Before** = `upstream/main` (`be49556dd1`); **After** = this branch's head (`5988075494`).

| Surface | Before (upstream/main) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Task agent picker — no ZCode | ![BEFORE upstream main: New Task agent picker without ZCode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac1c043b-aa12-46e5-9e13-9918fbbec48c) | ![AFTER this branch: ZCode listed in the New Task agent picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d4e9ada-46ea-4fd8-8463-b6d837683922) |
| Searching "zcode" in the picker | ![BEFORE: searching zcode matches nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/362df1ca-28f7-4685-b71d-90cb8bfa8709) | — matches, as above |
| ZCode selected as the agent | — impossible on main | ![AFTER: ZCode selected as the agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea1db966-99a4-454c-9dcd-9b3cd8bdbc67) |
| Prompt typed, session spawned | — | ![AFTER: prompt typed for the ZCode session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/381d1623-321e-4703-86fe-c867e81eeb84) |
| ZCode TUI boots in the terminal panel | — | ![AFTER: ZCode TUI live in the terminal panel with the delivered prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c356ffe6-5333-4489-812d-574c539c0c16) |
| ZCode answers (tool approval → reply) | — | ![AFTER: ZCode answers in the TUI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6ca0e69-afa9-4411-a253-ccd609348f6e) |

Screencast of the full interaction (open picker → select ZCode → TUI boots → prompt delivered → tool approved → response):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52ee599b-1503-494a-b6ff-9f8a6f3a9565

Lab notes: the spawned session runs ZCode's own TUI (v3.11.2-22, the machine's official `zcode` install) inside AO's terminal panel in an AO-managed worktree; the tool permission gate and the answer are ZCode's native UI, not AO chat rendering.

## CI status

CI runs for the latest commits are **pending maintainer approval** of workflow runs (fork first-time-contributor gate): the runs sit in `action_required` until a maintainer approves them; no check runs have started for head `5988075494` yet.

Backend-only change: no frontend surfaces were modified (the agent pickers are registry-driven, so ZCode appears automatically; it has no avatar asset or reviewer entry by design — it is not in `AllReviewerHarnesses`).

## How

- `GetLaunchCommand` / `GetRestoreCommand` build argv from documented flags only; `--prompt` is never passed (prompt delivery happens after the TUI starts, with a bounded settle delay and no asserted terminal marker).
- `ExitDetectionMode` opts into AO's process supervisor (the TUI exposes no exit hook).
- `SupportsTerminalVersionRefresh` is deliberately `false`: the `--continue` restore fallback cannot guarantee exact-conversation reselection for idle restarts.
- `AuthStatus` reads the documented personal provider config (`~/.zcode/v2/provider_config.json`, honoring `ZCODE_PERSONAL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE` / `ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR`) and reports authorized only when a provider rule carries an access entry; `zcode login` credential-store sessions report unknown rather than a guess. No credential values are read into results.

## Relation to #6003

Not stacked on #6003 (ACP/protocol Chat integration); that PR stays as-is on its own branch. Known overlapping paths if both land: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/zcode/` (different package contents), `backend/internal/domain/harness.go`, `backend/internal/adapters/agent/registry/registry.go`, and `docs/harnesses/zcode.md`. This PR is the minimal main-based TUI-only shape; resolving the overlap in favor of whichever lands second is mechanical.

title: fix(chat): show a Claude model's real context window during its first turn
body: Code changes: +131 -0\ Tests: +231 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Adds a packaging-time patch for the pinned `claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0 adapter: `patchClaudeContextWindowProbe`, next to the other `patchClaude*` patches. When a top-level assistant message starts and the session's window is still the adapter's unconfirmed 200k default, the patch asks the SDK's `getContextUsage` for `rawMaxTokens` without holding the stream. When the SDK answers, the patch stores that window and publishes a context-only `usage_update`, so AO shows the real window even if the turn is waiting on a long tool. ## Why Fixes #8005 Related: [#6453](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6453) reports the same 200k window for `claude-opus-5-5`. Its open PR, [#7045](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7045), covers a new adapter host resuming a pinned model. This PR covers a fresh session's first turn. The adapter starts a fresh session at `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 200000` unless the model's id, label or description has a `1m` token, or this adapter process has already cached the window from an earlier result. It learns the real window only from the turn's `result.modelUsage`. A worker spawned with `--prompt` usually does its whole task in one turn, so every mid-turn `usage_update` says `size: 200000`. AO passes that through unchanged. A `claude-fable-5-1` session (1M window) then reads `206k/200k` and full while it keeps working. `claude-opus-5-5` showed the same during investigation. The cache lives only for the adapter process, so fresh sessions in a new process start from 200k again. A session that resumes successfully reads its window during `session/load` and isn't affected. ## Before / After **In the desktop app.** These are the dev desktop app of each commit: base a19069ef40 and this branch at 8db765e178. The later commits only add a test case and reword a comment outside the patched code. - **Setup:** isolated dev data, Claude Code 2.1.319, Windows 11, the same 1320×860 window. Each side ran a fresh `claude-fable-5-1` session on the same scratch project, with the same prompt: "Without using any tools, write about 800 words on why the sky is blue." - **Timing:** both captures were taken about 37 s after Send, while the answer streams (Stop is showing), with the context meter's tooltip open. | Before (`main`) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | | | | | Every frame during the turn's 28 s showed a 200,000 window (`42,797`, then `44,421 / 200,000`). Only the result changed it, to `42,793 / 1,000,000` | Every frame showed a 1,000,000 window, starting with the first at 27.6 s: `42,795 / 1,000,000 tokens (4%)` through the turn, then `44,462` and `42,793 / 1,000,000` once it ended | The model picker showed effort Low on base and High on this branch. Base's composer kept Low from a first attempt whose workspace setup failed before any turn ran. The window depends on the model, not the effort, and both turns used about 42.8K tokens. **The adapter's own output.** These are single `claude-fable-5-1` turns through the real 0.70.0 adapter, recorded with a minimal ACP client. - Before has `main`'s packaging patches. That run comes from the earlier review rounds; `main`'s patches haven't changed since. - After is a fresh run with this branch's patches at 95c1a10b4e. Its Claude Code transcript confirms the model was `claude-fable-5-1`. - The client derives the "mid-turn" and "result" labels from whether the update carries `cost`; they aren't ACP fields. | Before (`main`) | After (this branch, 95c1a10b4e) | | --- | --- | | `+6714ms { used: 47147, size: 200000 }` mid-turn | `+6522ms { used: 47175, size: 200000 }` mid-turn, first message, probe sent | | — | `+7154ms { used: 47175, size: 1000000 }` mid-turn, published by the probe | | `+14810ms { used: 47656, size: 200000 }` mid-turn | `+14296ms { used: 47704, size: 1000000 }` mid-turn, printed twice 2 ms apart (see below) | | `+17095ms { used: 47139, size: 1000000 }` result | `+15948ms { used: 47167, size: 1000000 }` result | With this branch the window became 1M about 0.6 s after the turn's first message, instead of only at the end of the turn. The probe publishes once. The second copy at +14298ms is the adapter's own `rate_limit_event` republish of the current usage, which has no `cost`; the client prints only `used` and `size`. ## How - AO already patches this compiled adapter during packaging. It also already treats `getContextUsage().rawMaxTokens` as authoritative in `patchClaudeContextUsage`. This patch follows the same pattern. - **Tripwire.** The patch compares the whole top-level stream branch with the pinned code: the top-level-message check, the authority and default-window guards, the heuristic, the `message_delta` accounting, and the guarded `usage_update` publish whose counter, sender and session id the probe reuses. The comparison ignores only whitespace and whole-line `//` comments, which is all the pinned branch has. The branch's first line may carry only indentation before it, no block comment may be open there, and the nearest enclosing case must be `stream_event`. A statement on an earlier line that skips the branch, such as a brace-less `if` or a `break`, is not detected. The probe goes right after the heuristic's closing brace, and only whitespace may separate the two. - Packaging fails without touching the file on any of these: a changed guard, a block comment inside the branch or opened before it, a `//` in front of the branch's first line, a comment between the heuristic and its brace, the branch outside the `stream_event` case, or the anchor appearing twice. - The check is a text scan, not a parse. A `/*` inside an earlier string would also fail packaging, and a string literal wrapped around the branch would go unseen. The pinned file has neither. - **When it probes.** Upstream deliberately avoids `getContextUsage` at `session/new` and on a model switch: a fresh session doesn't service it before its first turn (~15 s stall, upstream #886/#880). - The probe runs only at a top-level `message_start`, after the turn has started. It runs only when the `1m` heuristic found nothing and the window is still the non-authoritative default. - While a probe is pending, no other is sent for the same model selection, in this turn or a later one. - A failed or unusable answer is retried when `session.activeTurn` changes. That's once per turn, or twice when the turn's replayed echo lands after its first message: the first probe then runs before the turn is active. A broken SDK isn't asked on every message, and a turn cancelled before its result doesn't leave the session at 200k. - Every model switch, including a switch back to the same model, starts a new selection and probes again. That includes a switch back while the earlier probe is still pending: a new request is sent, and the old answer is discarded because it may describe the other model. AO sets the model only when the user changes it (`Service.SetConfigOption`); nothing re-applies it per prompt. - **No timeout.** The pinned SDK's public `getContextUsage()` takes no abort signal, so it can't be cancelled, and a timer wouldn't cancel it either. It would only throw away a late but correct answer. A late answer is accepted unless a `result` (or AO's result-time context snapshot) has set the window meanwhile, or the model was switched, even back to the same model: an answer that spans a switch may describe the other model. A failed probe is logged, and the window is corrected at the result as before. - **Unproven risk.** The SDK doesn't queue control requests: its `request()` writes each one straight to the transport with its own id. So `interrupt` and `set_model` aren't held behind a pending probe on the SDK side. Whether the Claude subprocess delays handling them is not measured. In the live runs the probe answered in about 0.5–0.6 s. Switching models while a probe is pending can leave more than one `getContextUsage` request in flight, one per switch at most; how the subprocess handles concurrent requests is also unmeasured. - The SDK exposes no window before a turn: `ModelInfo` and the `system/init` message have no window field. - Intentional omissions: - No change to the provider-neutral Go usage path or to `ContextMeter`: showing "unknown" when usage exceeds the window would hide real over-limit readings. - No change to the mobile app. Its context meter, session menu and "Context & usage" sheet read the same conversation usage from the paired daemon (`GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation`), so they get the corrected window too. Its meter, which appears from 70% full, now waits until about 700K tokens on a 1M model instead of about 140K. Not checked on a device. - No hard-coded model-window table in `claudeacp`: it would need upkeep and can't know per-account entitlement. - No reliance on the user's `autoCompactWindow` setting: the 1M comes from the SDK. - The real fix belongs upstream in `claude-agent-acp`. Drop this patch when AO moves to an adapter that learns the window before the first result. #8019, the planned move to 0.101.0, will need to port or drop this patch along with the other `patchClaude*` patches. ## Testing - `npx vitest run scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.test.mjs`: 37 passed. The 6 tests for this patch run the patched pinned branch inside its `stream_event` case, in one consumer per session. Its usage counters persist across messages as in the adapter, and a new turn replaces `session.activeTurn` as `activateTurn` does. They cover: - an answer after 10 s and two more messages is still used and published with the latest usage, and only one probe is sent - a known or `1m`-named window is left alone - nothing more is published on failure, on an answer whose `rawMaxTokens` is missing or 0, on a 200k confirmation, when a result or model switch wins the race, or after a new turn resets the counter - switching A→B→A probes A again whether A's first probe was answered while on B, failed, or is still pending; the still-pending answer is then discarded - a failed or unusable probe is retried once the active turn changes, including after a cancelled turn. It isn't retried while the active turn stays the same, and never while a probe is pending. - the patch ignores indentation. It fails packaging without changing the file when: - a guard or the top-level check is removed, or the top-level check sits behind a `//` - the publish is disabled with `&& false` or wrapped in `/* */` - a `// }` comment follows the heuristic - the branch is wrapped in a block comment opened on an earlier line - the branch leaves the `stream_event` case - the block appears twice - Each of these 15 mutations of the patch makes at least one test fail: - no publish - publishing the first message's usage instead of the latest - no null-counter check - no result-wins guard - a re-added 2 s timeout - no retry on a later turn - retrying while a probe is pending - never settling a failed probe - keying the pending check on the model id instead of the selection - keying the race guard on the model id instead of the selection - the old comment-blind brace search - dropping the block-comment check - dropping the line-prefix check - dropping the `stream_event` case check - dropping the finite check on `rawMaxTokens` - Applied every `patchClaude*` patch, in `build-acp-runtime.mjs` order, to the real 0.70.0 `dist/acp-agent.js`. I did this once with the base's helpers (a19069ef40) and once with this branch's. All applied, and `node --check` passes on both results. - On the real file, the tripwire rejects each of these and leaves the file unchanged: - a `// }` comment after the heuristic - the branch and its notification loop wrapped in `/* */`, with the opener on its own line or on the branch's line - the top-level check moved behind a `//` - the branch moved out of the `stream_event` case - the publish wrapped in `/* */` - a removed authority guard - The real patched branch, run with the adapter's own turn bookkeeping (`activateTurn` and `resetTurnScratch`, `activeTurn = null` at a cancel): - A probe rejected in one turn, then a cancel and a new turn: a second request is sent and `210000/1000000` is published. At a018ef0f78 the second turn stayed at `210000/200000` with one request. - A→B[1m]→A in one turn after a rejected probe: the same. - 100 message starts with a probe pending, then a new turn: still one request. - Live adapter turns: the second table above. After is a fresh paid turn at 95c1a10b4e: every `patchClaude*` patch, in build order, on the pristine 0.70.0 file. The later commits change no emitted code: 8db765e178 rewords a comment inside the probe, and the last two add a test case and reword a helper comment. An earlier After run at 492ad95c2a showed the same sequence: `200000` at the first message, then `1000000` from the probe about 0.5 s later. - **Desktop captures.** Before / After comes from each commit's dev app (`npm run dev` in its own worktree), each with its own isolated `~/.ao/dev` profile, run file and data dir. - I drove the real window over the remote debugging protocol. The project was added through the daemon's `POST /api/v1/projects`, because the UI's add-project flow opens a native folder dialog; the session itself was created and prompted in the UI. - The packaged ACP runtime came from each checkout's own `build:acp-runtime`: base's adapter has no probe, this branch's has it. - Forge's `better-sqlite3` rebuild needs a Visual Studio that the pinned `@electron/node-gyp` recognizes, and this machine only has VS 2026 Build Tools (version 18). So both worktrees used the `better_sqlite3.node` that ships in the AO 0.14.10 release. That release has the same `better-sqlite3` 12.11.1 and Electron 44.7.0 (ABI 149). - **CI lanes.** `scripts/ci-lanes.mjs` picks `frontend` + `boundary` with `vitest=all` for these files. I ran each job's own commands at 8db765e178 in Linux containers on this machine, using the workflows' pinned runtimes.
