title: fix(chat): open a link to a listed artifact as that artifact
body:
Code changes: +21 -1\
Tests: +26 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

In chat, a Markdown link to the file a session artifact was written to now opens that artifact (the session's Artifacts view) instead of a workspace file tab.

## Why

A Cloud agent links the artifact it just made by the file it wrote, under the worker's artifact directory, e.g. `[guide](/workspace/.ao/worker/artifacts/<session>/conductor-migration-guide.md)`. Clicking it opened a workspace file tab. That view reads the file through the session's checkout, and the artifact lives outside it, so the request was refused (HTTP 422) and the tab stayed blank. Opening the same artifact from the Artifacts list worked.

Inline code naming the same path (`` `…/artifacts/<session>/<path>` ``) already became an artifact link through `artifactLinkForPath`; Markdown links skipped that step.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Clicking an artifact link in a Cloud chat opens a file tab named after the file; it requests the file from the workspace, gets 422 and stays blank | The link is an `ao://sessions/<project>/<session>/artifacts/<path>` link and opens the artifact in the session's Artifacts view, which loads the stored artifact |
| A link to a path under `/artifacts/` that the session does not list | Unchanged: still a file link |

No screenshots: the after state needs a live Cloud session with a fresh artifact. The before state was reproduced in the desktop app from `main` against production, and the 422s match the requests the app made when the bug was reported. The new test checks the after behaviour.

## How

- `MarkdownLink` hands a link whose target contains `/artifacts/` (and is neither a web link nor an `ao://` link) to a small `ArtifactFileLink` wrapper. That wrapper maps it with `artifactLinkForPath` against the chat's session-link source, as `ArtifactPathCode` does for inline code; every other link renders exactly as before through `MarkdownLinkTarget`.
- The lookup lives in its own component on purpose: calling the session-link hook from every `MarkdownLink` subscribed each link to the session list and required a `QueryClient` wherever chat Markdown renders (it broke `ChatPathMenu`, `AutomationMessage` and `ActivityRun` tests in a first attempt).
- A link only becomes an artifact link when the session lists that file; an unlisted path keeps today's file-link behaviour.

## Testing

- New in `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx`:
  - a Markdown link to a listed artifact's file gets the artifact `href` and opens through the session-link handler, never `onFileOpen`;
  - a link to an unlisted artifact path stays a file link.
- Mutation check: with `ChatMarkdown.tsx` from `main`, the first test fails; with the change, `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx` passes 120/120.
- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- `vitest run src/renderer/components/chat src/renderer/components/ChatPathMenu.test.tsx src/renderer/lib/session-links.test.ts src/renderer/components/SessionLinkPreviewCard.test.tsx`: 1900/1902. The 2 failures (`ContextMeter`, `ChatWorkspace` context usage) come from this machine's `en_IN` number formatting (`2,58,400`). Both files pass under `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` (269/269).

title: feat(desktop): open sessions from ao-app://sessions deep links
body:
External tools (e.g. the ao-bridge dashboard) render `ao-app://sessions/{projectId}/{sessionId}` links so a click can open the desktop app directly on that session. Today any `ao-app://` URL other than `callback`/`billing` only focuses the window and silently drops the URL. This adds a `sessions` host case: the app focuses and navigates to that session.

The renderer resolves deep links through the same `session-links` path as in-app `ao://` links, so the two schemes share one parser and behave alike (including artifact routes and the terminated-session refusal).

## Accepted URL formats (for tooling)

```
ao-app://sessions/{projectId}/{sessionId}
ao-app://sessions/{projectId}/{sessionId}/artifacts/{path}
```

- Both ids are percent-decoded; reserved characters (e.g. space) must be encoded (`%20`). An id containing an encoded slash (`%2F`) is rejected, exactly as for in-app `ao://` links.
- A trailing slash is tolerated. Any other host (`callback`, `billing`, unknown), wrong protocol, or a link without a target path is not claimed by this handler — `callback` and `billing` keep their existing handlers untouched.

## Behavior

| Behavior | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Valid session, app running | Window focuses, renderer navigates to the session |
| Valid session, cold start (argv) | Link is queued until the shell mounts, then navigates — `open-url` (macOS) and the Windows/Linux second-instance argv path behave identically |
| Link arrives before the first workspace page is confirmed (startup loader, daemon not ready, cached empty page) | Held until the confirmed startup fetch lands, then navigates — never a false "not found" against empty lists |
| Link targets a remote host whose data is still loading (remote hosts enabled) | Held until the host list is read and each enabled host's project query loads or fails (an offline host counts as settled) |
| Unknown session | Window focuses, quiet "Session not found" toast; never navigates to a wrong session |
| Terminated session | Window focuses, quiet "Session {id} is terminated" toast — the same refusal as in-app `ao://` links |
| Artifact route | Opens the file in the destination session, like in-app `ao://` artifact links |

Screen recordings and before/after screenshots are in the first comment.

## Implementation

- `frontend/src/shared/deep-links.ts` — `isSessionDeepLink()` routing predicate + the dedicated `app:open-session-deep-link` IPC channel (no overloading of the settings channel).
- `frontend/src/main.ts` — `sessions` case in `handleCloudDeepLinkAndFocus` forwards the **raw URL**; a link arriving while the shell is still mounting queues like the existing cold-start folder-drop path and flushes on the `TRAY_RENDERER_READY` handshake.
- `frontend/src/preload.ts` — `onOpenSessionDeepLink` with the same buffer-and-forward dispatcher as `onOpenFolderPath` (the readiness ping fires from a child effect before ShellLayout subscribes).
- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx` — swaps `ao-app://` for `ao://` and reuses `parseSessionLink`/`parseArtifactLink`/`resolveSessionLink` (`renderer/lib/session-links.ts`), keeping the remote-workspace fallback; navigates via the existing `sessionNavigateTarget()` helper, quiet toast when nothing matches or the session is terminated.

## Testing

- `frontend/src/renderer/test/shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx` — deep-link suite written red-first against the previous implementation: hold-then-flush across a daemon-not-ready query, terminated refusal, artifact open, remote fallback, not-found toast, live navigation.
- `frontend/src/shared/deep-links.test.ts` — routing-predicate cases (valid, artifact route, trailing slash, billing/callback/unknown-host/non-`ao-app` rejection, malformed URLs, no-target-path links).
- `frontend/src/preload.test.ts` — delivery after subscription, cold-start buffering race, malformed-payload rejection, buffer semantics across dispose/resubscribe.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; i18n coverage suite green (`deepLink.sessionTerminated` added to all locales).
- Verified in the running app from a scratch data dir (screenshots in the first comment).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Open sessions directly from `ao-app://` links, including sessions in remote workspaces.
  * Artifact links can open the requested artifact in the linked session.
  * Links received before the app or workspace is ready are handled once it becomes available.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Missing sessions, unavailable hosts, and terminated sessions display appropriate messages instead of navigating to an unavailable session.
  * Session links can resolve sessions in later workspaces that share the same project.
* **Localization**
  * Deep-link error messages are available in English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, and Simplified Chinese.

title: fix(artifacts): let a cloud file's menu Edit open the editor
body:
Code changes: +6 -7\
Tests: +10 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Choosing **Edit file** from an open cloud artifact's name menu now opens the editor. Before this, it did nothing for cloud `.md`, `.txt` and other text files. The pencil on the file's card already worked, and local artifacts were not affected.

## Why

`usePinnedArtifactUrl` returned new `repin` and `refresh` functions on every render. `SessionArtifactsView` passes `repin` (through `accessRefused`) as the cloud file source's `onAccessRefused`, so the source object changed on every render too. `FileContentPane` resets its edit state whenever its `source` changes. Starting an edit re-renders the panel (it hides Share while editing), and that re-render closed the editor straight away. The card's pencil avoided this because it opens the file with `initialEditing`, which the reset keeps.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud artifact → name menu → **Edit file**: the editor flashes open and closes, so the file stays in view mode | The editor opens with Save/Cancel, as for a local artifact |

## How

`repin` and `refresh` are now wrapped in `useCallback`. They only call the stable `setPinned`, so they need no dependencies. I left `FileContentPane`'s reset effect alone: it is shared by every file view, and reworking which `source` changes should reset it is a wider change than this bug needs.

## Testing

- Reproduced the bug with a throwaway `SessionArtifactsView` test using the real `ArtifactFileView`/`FileContentPane`: an owned cloud `.md` file, opened, then **Edit file** from the name menu. The editor never opened before the fix and opens after it.
- Added a regression test in `useCloudArtifacts.test.ts` that checks `repin` and `refresh` stay the same across renders. It fails without the fix.
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/hooks/useCloudArtifacts.test.ts src/renderer/components/SessionArtifactsView.test.tsx src/renderer/components/ArtifactFileView.test.tsx`: 121 passed.

title: fix(chat): give the queued message dock a solid fill on translucent windows
body:
Code changes: +6 -0\
Tests: +14 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On a translucent window, the transcript no longer shows through the open queued-message dock. The dock still floats over the transcript's last rows, as before, but now with a solid fill.

## Why

The dock is meant to float. The composer reserves room for the folded dock, and the open dock grows upward over the transcript (#4684). Its fill is `bg-surface`, which on a translucent window resolves to a 5% foreground tint. So transcript lines like "Waiting a few minutes for CI to start…" and "Checking CI · 1h 9m" showed straight through the "3 Queued Messages" header and rows. On an opaque window the same fill is solid, and the dock already looks right there.

An earlier revision of this PR moved the dock into the composer column's flow instead. That stopped the overlap, but it resized the transcript every time the queue opened or closed, so it's reverted here.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Dark translucent window: the transcript's last two lines read through the open dock's header and first row | Same window: the dock is a solid surface and the transcript stops at its edge, as on an opaque window |

Captured from a throwaway harness that renders the real `ChatComposer` and `QueuedMessageDock` with transcript lines above it, `data-window-translucent="true"`, and a dark backdrop standing in for the window's vibrancy.

## How

- One rule: on a translucent window, the dock, its header and its body (the three layers that paint `bg-surface`) use `--solid-bg-secondary` as their background, the value the same fill has on an opaque window.
- No surface tokens change, so everything else inside the dock (hover fills, buttons, text colors) is exactly as on `main`.
- The layout is the same as `main`: the slot still reserves the folded height, and the dock is still absolutely positioned inside it.
- Trade-off: on a dark translucent window the folded dock is now solid too, instead of the 5% tint the composer uses. Limiting the solid fill to the open state would let the transcript show through again during the 420ms close animation.
- On a light translucent window the center panel already uses solid surfaces, so nothing changes there.
- The 1rem strips beside the open dock still show the edge of the transcript, as they already do on an opaque window. Painting them over put a square slab behind the rounded dock on a translucent window, so they're left as they are.

## Testing

- `e2e/shared-composer-layout.spec.ts` gains "open queue keeps a solid fill over a translucent window". It fails with `main`'s CSS (alpha 0.05) and passes on this branch. The existing 960px and 390px layout tests pass (3/3 on Chrome, branch export).
- vitest: `QueuedMessageDock`, `QueuedMessageDock.keyboard`, `ChatSteer`, and the tests that read `styles.css` (`native-composition-cascade`, `WindowTitlebar`, `CenterPane`): 105/105 passed.
- Not run locally: the Electron window with live vibrancy, the full vitest shards, the full renderer smoke suite, and `npm run typecheck` (no TypeScript source changed). Left to CI.

title: feat(chat): keep tool calls collapsed until the reader opens them
body:
## Summary

Tool calls in the chat timeline now stay collapsed until you click them, in the running turn and in finished turns. Labels and naming are unchanged.

| Surface | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Run summary ("Ran 2 tool calls") | Open for the turn's latest run, or when a command printed | Collapsed |
| Subgroup inside a run | Same | Collapsed |
| Subagent steps | Open while the subagent worked | Collapsed |
| Single command row | Open while printing | Collapsed |
| Live row step | Open while printing | One line |

MCP and AO tool rows and resolved "Worked for" folds already started closed.

## How a running step presents

One compact line: the live row's loader, the step in the present tense ("Running tests"), the timer and a chevron. It never opens a body on its own, even while printing. Click opens the command and output, and that choice carries over when the step moves up into the list. A second call running at the same time shows as a one-line row, or as the spinner on its run's summary line.

## What stays visible

- **Failed calls.** A folded run, subgroup or subagent shows its failed calls as rows under the summary line. In a finished turn, a run with a failed call stays out of "Worked for", as errors and warnings already do. Calls count as failed when `status` is `failed`, or when an MCP tool reports `success: false` or `error`, since some providers mark those completed.
- **Permission requests and questions.** Unchanged. They were never in runs: pending ones own the composer or dock, and answered ones have their own rows.

Manual toggles, `aria-expanded`, Enter/Space (native buttons) and text selection are unchanged.

## Decision to check

An ordinary non-zero exit is not treated as a failed call, matching the existing split between red "failed" and muted "exited". A `grep` with no match would otherwise pin a row on most turns. Those stay folded and are counted as "N exited" on the run's summary line. In a finished turn they sit under "Worked for". To pin them too, change `isFailedCall` in `activity-command.ts`.

## Coordination with #7840

#7840 merged on 2026-11-09 before this branch was cut, so this is built on top of it and needed no rebase. I read its diff first. This PR only changes when disclosures open. It does not touch `activity-step.ts`, step labels or the live row's markup.

## Scope

The project setup script panel (`ScriptRunPanel`) keeps its behaviour. It is not a tool call, and it stays open while running or failed.

## Testing

Per the requester's instruction, no tests, typecheck, build or app launch were run locally, so CI is the only verification and this has not been checked in the app. Tests were updated by reading them, including new cases for streaming output, keyboard toggle, failed calls in a run, subagent and settled turn, and non-zero exits.

To try it in the app:

1. Send a prompt that makes the agent run several commands, such as "run `sleep 5; echo done` three times, one after another".
2. While it runs, check the steps above the live row show as one summary line or single collapsed rows, and the live row shows one line with a timer.
3. Click the live row. The command and output open. Click again to close.
4. Click a "Ran N tool calls" line. The calls appear. Click again to fold.
5. Send "call a tool that fails, such as reading a file through an MCP server that errors". The failed row shows under its folded summary while running, and stays visible under "Worked for" once the turn ends.
6. Tab to a summary line and press Enter. It toggles.

title: fix(desktop): stop showing kept worktrees as a top bar error
body:
## Problem

The desktop top bar shows red text next to the open-in-editor button: `Worktree has uncommitted chang…`. It stays there, it is cut off mid-sentence, and nothing on the page explains which session it means.

## Root cause

`useProjectTerminateSessionStates` turned every session in the project with a `preserved_dirty` or `failed` cleanup into an entry for `ProjectTerminationFeedback`, which the orchestrator top bar and the project board render at `max-w-48 truncate`.

Both states are terminal. The daemon stops retrying and keeps them until someone retries by hand (`backend/internal/domain/cleanup.go`). So one archive of a dirty session put a permanent red label on that project, and each further one added another. The `workspaceCleanupReportOnly` filter only excludes cleanups started by a sweep, so archive-started ones stayed forever.

## Decision

The message has two different uses, and they get different answers:

- **As standing top bar text, it should not exist.** A kept worktree is the app protecting uncommitted work, not a page-level error, and DESIGN.md limits the top bar to orientation and high-value actions. Settled cleanup outcomes no longer reach the top bar. In-progress `Cleanup pending` and `Archiving` stay, since those are live.
- **As feedback on an archive the user just ran, it should exist.** Otherwise a worktree is silently left on disk. It now appears once as a toast when that archive's cleanup settles, with the full sentence wrapped, the session named, and a **Retry cleanup** button.

Details:

- `preserved_dirty` uses the neutral info tone. `failed` uses the error tone, since that is a failed operation.
- Retry calls the existing `POST /api/v1/sessions/cleanup` for that project, the same call as Retry cleanup in project Scripts settings, on the session's own host. If the session is still skipped, the toast comes back with the reason from that retry.
- Standalone sessions get the notice without Retry, because they have no project for the sweep to target.
- Remote archives are followed through the host's always-polled session list, so they report even when no page for that host is open.
- Archives from earlier runs and sweep-recorded cleanups raise nothing. Project Scripts settings remains the durable place to retry them.
- `useTerminateSessionState` also drops the durable message. The daemon only returns cleanup facts for archived sessions, while its consumers only render for active ones, so the branch could only ever show stale cache.

No backend change and no new strings: this reuses the existing copy.

## Testing

Per the task instructions I did not run tests, typecheck, builds or the app locally. CI is the first run of this code, and the toast has not been seen in the real app.

`useTerminateSession.test.tsx` is updated by reading: settled states stay out of page state, the toast fires exactly once per archive and in the right tone, success and sweep results stay silent, and Retry repeats while dirty, then reports the result or the failure.

## Known limits

- Retry sweeps the whole project, matching the Settings button. The endpoint has no per-session option, and dirty worktrees are never forced.
- The `failed` copy still says "Retry cleanup in project Scripts settings", which reads slightly oddly beside a Retry button. I left it to avoid touching every locale.
- Kill-request errors (the daemon rejecting the archive) still use the red truncated top bar text. They are transient and a different message, so they are out of scope here.

title: fix(chat): show sent attachments above the bubble, never folded
body: Code changes: +551 -199\ Tests: +138 -3\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Everything attached to a sent message now renders as one 64px-tall tile on a single row above the bubble: images, files, PDFs and "Add to chat" text. Attachments are never folded, and the bubble holds only text. ## Why A sent screenshot rendered as a cropped image with a "Show more" under it, inset with its own border inside a large padded card. On manual review, moving attachments out of the bubble fixed that, but they were still too big and each kind was a different size, so a mixed row looked uneven. The cropping cause: a single image rendered up to 320px tall (`max-h-80`), and `CollapsibleHumanBody` folds anything taller than about 264px, counting attachments as content. So nearly any normal screenshot got clipped at 220px. ## Before / After No screenshots yet. The reported screenshot exists only in the original chat, so it could not be attached here. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | An image over about 264px tall is cut off at the fold, with "Show more" under it | Attachments are outside the fold and always fully visible; only text folds | | Image inside the padded bubble, so its border sits inside the bubble's edge | Image on the canvas with one hairline border and `rounded-md` | | Images up to 320px tall | Images in a 64px-tall tile, cropped to fill: one square wide at minimum, two at most; click to open full size | | Image, file chip, PDF card (176×~160px) and annotation chip are all different sizes | All 64px tall, on one row that scrolls sideways and fades out at an edge with more past it | | "Add to chat" text is a 28px chip inside the bubble | A card in the row: two lines of the text, with the count in a small tag | | Attachment-only message draws a padded card | No bubble; timestamp, copy and edit still appear on hover | | File chip shows the name only (cloud: name and size) | A 128×64 card: name on top, then a small type tag (`rounded-xs`, not a pill) and the size when known; text isn't selectable | | Files show only a name, whatever they are | Videos show their first frame and PDFs their first page filling the tile (`PdfPreview` `cover` mode), with the type as a tag; both open full size. Text and code show their first lines. HTML keeps its name card, and audio has no preview | | Composer images are static thumbnails | Click or Enter opens the full image; file chips show type and size; `rounded-md` everywhere | | Image previews have no visible keyboard focus | `focus-visible` ring | ## How - **Direction:** attachments outside the bubble, in `AttachmentStrip`. It removes the fold, the padding and the double edge in one move. - **One size:** `ATTACHMENT_TILE_CLASS` is shared by every non-image tile. An image in an attachment row carries its border on the ``, so the border counts inside the 64px and it lines up exactly with the others. `ChatImageAttachmentRow` scopes this, so images in agent replies keep their existing sizes. - `HumanMessage`, the non-automation steered message and `HumanMessageEditor` use the same row, so starting an edit still moves nothing. Lists inside it use `display: contents`, so different kinds share one row. The row is capped to the bubble's width and scrolls sideways with the shared `edge-fade` mask (`useEdgeFade`), so a long row never wraps or pushes the bubble. - The composer strip stays at its compact 28px; its chips and the annotation chip were already that height. Worth checking in review: - **Staged files show no size.** A staged message stores only the path, so the size isn't known without a new request per file. Cloud and composer chips show it. **Original names are a local display hint.** Staging renames a file to `attachment-.ext` and the message keeps only that path, so the composer remembers the original name per path in `localStorage` (newest 500). A file attached before this change, from another machine, or on a new chat before its workspace is ready shows the generated name. The agent still sees the generated path. Attachment storage and upload are unchanged. - **Type labels are uppercase file extensions** (`PDF`, `TXT`). They read as abbreviations rather than styled labels, and stay useful when a name truncates. - **Previews load only near the viewport** (`IntersectionObserver`), and the name card sits under each one as its loading and failure state. Rendering attached HTML would need an isolated origin, so it stays a name card. Cloud videos and text stay name cards because their bytes would have to be downloaded whole. - Automation-framed steered messages use the same tiles, but keep their own layout. ## Testing Tests were updated by reading them. No tests, typecheck or builds were run locally, by instruction. This differs from the AGENTS.md rule to run CI jobs locally. To check it in the app, in dark and light themes: 1. Send a screenshot with one line of text. A 64px-tall image shows above the bubble, with no "Show more". Click it: the full image opens. 2. Send a screenshot, a `.pdf` and a `.txt` together. All three are the same height in one row. Attach enough to overflow it: the row scrolls sideways and fades at the edge with more past it. 3. Select text in a file or chat, choose Add to chat, and send with a screenshot. The annotation is a same-height tile in that row. Click it: its list opens. 4. Send a screenshot with no text. There is no card around it. Hover it: the timestamp and copy icon appear below. 5. Send 30 lines of text with a screenshot. The text folds and the image doesn't. 6. Tab to an image and press Enter: a focus ring shows and the dialog opens. 7. Attach an image and click its composer thumbnail. The full image opens. 8. Hover a sent message with an attachment and click the pencil. Nothing moves. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable (no issue exists) - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene, except local CI, skipped by instruction - [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (behavior table only; screenshots owed) - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: docs: add a Move from Conductor guide for the Cloud shutdown
body:
## Summary

Conductor joined Meta. Conductor Cloud goes read-only on 13 November 2026 and starts deleting Cloud data on 20 November; the local Mac app keeps working until early 2027. This adds a **Move from Conductor** guide under Guides so people can act before the deadline.

- **Save your Conductor Cloud work before 13 November:** push every branch, **Transfer to local**, **Settings → Account → Export data**, and write down Cloud settings. These steps happen in Conductor; Orchestrator cannot read Conductor Cloud.
- **Move a repository:** add the root repository, copy `.conductor/settings.toml` / `settings.local.toml` / `conductor.json` settings into Project settings by hand, and rename `CONDUCTOR_*` variables to the `AO_*` names Setup and Cleanup get today.
- **Move Conductor Cloud work:** create a Cloud project and set up its scripts and environment.
- **Teams and your phone:** where sharing, takeover, mobile and routines live.

The guide describes only what ships on `main`. The Conductor settings and chat import (stacked on #6364) will replace the manual steps when it lands.

## Verification

- Every UI label named in the guide exists in `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/en.json` on `main`.
- Local Setup steps run in the worktree with `AO_SOURCE_TREE_PATH` and `AO_WORKTREE_PATH` (`runPostCreate`), and Cleanup gets both (`workspace_cleanup.go`). Cloud Setup and Cleanup get both, per `ProjectScriptCommands` in `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts`.
- No local build; CI builds the docs.

## Risks

- Conductor's own steps (**Transfer to local**, **Export data**) come from Conductor's announcement and press coverage, not a live Conductor Cloud account.
- `deploy-docs.yml` publishes on merge to `main`, so this goes live without an app release.

title: feat(import): import Conductor chats; agent sets up Conductor settings
body:
Builds on the session import from #6364 (merged).

## Summary

Conductor joined Meta; Conductor Cloud goes read-only on 13 November and starts deleting data on 20 November, and the local app winds down in early 2027. This brings Conductor chats over in code and leaves Conductor's settings to the user's agent, so nothing changes for people who never used Conductor.

**Chats** (`sessionimport/conductor.go`)
- New `conductor` source reads `conductor.db` with SQLite `mode=ro`, adding `immutable=1` when Conductor is closed and no `-wal` file exists (a plain read-only open would create `-wal`/`-shm` files in Conductor's folder). It needs the tables and columns of Conductor 0.94; `testdata/conductor-0.94.sql` is the schema of a real 0.94.0 install, and any other layout stops with "unknown layout". Only macOS has a Conductor folder; elsewhere the source finds nothing.
- Offers every Claude Code and Codex chat, archived workspaces included, with no age or per-folder limit. Skips deleted (hidden) chats and Cursor/ACP chats. Reads the legacy `session_messages` rows and 0.94's `session_events`, whose `agent` events hold the Claude Agent SDK message or the Codex thread event.
- A chat reads from its agent's own history when this Mac has it (`~/.claude/projects/*/<id>.jsonl`, or the Codex rollout found by thread id) and keeps Conductor's title. A Claude chat without one is rebuilt from `conductor.db` as a new Claude Code transcript (exclusive create), so `claude --resume` continues it. A Codex chat without a rollout is not offered.
- A chat shows once: the Conductor candidate takes the Claude/Codex candidate's ID and replaces it.
- A chat whose workspace folder is gone (archived) is placed in the repository checkout (`root_path`, plus `.main` for `storage_version` 1).
- `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` record the read exception for `conductor.db`.

**Settings, set up by the agent** (`skillassets/using-ao/commands/conductor.md`)
- No settings import, endpoint or UI, and no `CONDUCTOR_*` variables in terminals, Cues, Setup or Cleanup.
- The using-ao skill gets a guide, linked from `SKILL.md` and `references.md`, that tells an agent where Conductor keeps settings (`~/.conductor/settings.toml`, `conductor.json`, `.conductor/settings.toml`, `.conductor/settings.local.toml`, and the repository's row in `conductor.db`, read-only), how each key maps to `ao project set-config` (Setup, Cleanup, env, agent rules) and `ao cue create`, how to copy `.worktreeinclude` / `file_include_globs` / `.env*` files in a Setup step, how to rewrite each `CONDUCTOR_*` name, and to confirm the plan with the user before applying it. It warns that the repeatable flags replace whole lists.

**Guide**: `guides/migrate-from-conductor.mdx` tells users to send their agent "Set up this project's Conductor settings in Orchestrator." The chat section now matches the code (no age limit for Conductor chats, archived workspaces included). The docs-only version for `main` is #8057.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/service/sessionimport/` against the real 0.94 schema; on macOS the same 5 `/private/var` path tests fail as on `main`. CI is the gate.
- `TestConductorChatsPlaceWorkspacesLikeConductor` (storage v1/v2/v3/NULL, checkouts, Cursor and hidden chats left out), `TestConductorReadsAClosedWALDatabase` (no `-wal`/`-shm` created), `TestConductorImportsEveryChat` (90-day-old legacy chat, archived folder rebuilt and placed by checkout, native Claude chat deduped with the Conductor title, Codex with and without a rollout, hidden chat, rescan shows all imported).
- Chats end to end with this branch's daemon and desktop on lab data, real Claude Code and Codex logins, and a `conductor.db` in the real 0.94 schema filled from real Claude and Codex runs: 3 repositories and 9 chats imported with Conductor's titles and dates; a native Claude chat, a Codex chat, and an archived Claude chat rebuilt from `conductor.db` each continued with its earlier context; uncommitted edits in a Conductor workspace came along into the new worktree.
- Settings end to end, after this change: this branch's daemon on the same lab, Claude Code (Sonnet) in a `conductor.json` repository with only the usual skill pointer and the guide's prompt. Turn 1 proposed, without changing anything, a `.env*` copy step, the setup script, the archive script as Cleanup, and a `Run` Cue with `$CONDUCTOR_PORT` rewritten to a path-derived port. After "go" it applied exactly that, and the saved Setup steps ran in a fresh worktree and copied `.env`.

## Risks and follow-ups

- Conductor no longer takes new sign-ins, so the lab data was written into the real schema by hand, following the installed runtime's code, not created by the Conductor UI. The assistant JSON in legacy `session_messages` rows is assumed to be Agent SDK JSON; no real row confirmed it.
- Codex chats without a rollout on this Mac (for example from Conductor Cloud) are not offered; writing a rollout from `session_events` is a follow-up. Cursor chats are not imported.
- The settings setup depends on the agent following the guide; only Claude Code (Sonnet) and a `conductor.json` repository were tried.
- Seen in the lab, not import code: the folder picker leaves folders with fewer than 3 chats unticked under "Other folders", a message sent in the first seconds after opening an imported chat, while it resumes, fails with "the agent controller for this session is not running", and the **Run a cue** menu stays open after choosing a Cue.
- Not done: committing and pushing each Conductor branch before import, workspace notes and diff comments, and Conductor Cloud settings for Cloud projects.

title: fix(e2e): stop fake streams from outrunning the browser
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +7 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keep the streaming session-switch test from queuing overlapping browser updates.

## Why

The test advanced its chunk counter while earlier `page.evaluate` calls were still pending. Diagnostics measured up to 32 pending calls on a slow browser. Fetched updates could appear after the existing 10-second assertion deadline.

First affected commit: c9b7237eb8 (#8013), which introduced this fixture. Its first main CI run failed before passing on retry.

## Before / After

No user-visible change. This changes only the test fixture.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| 4x CPU: 10/10 passed | 4x CPU: 10/10 passed |
| 6x CPU: 7/10 passed, 3 failed | 6x CPU: 10/10 passed |

The baseline used main at `5da2663b8e`. The 6x result also improved to 10/10 on that same base before moving the fix. The after counts above are fresh checks from `7b550c6d96`.

## How

Allow one fake notification in flight and wait for it to settle before advancing another chunk. The assertions, timeouts, chunk format, and 120 ms timer interval stay unchanged.

## Testing

title: [Bug]: Agy TUI workers ignore 'auto' / 'accept-edits' permissions (only bypass-permissions is mapped)
body:
### What went wrong?

An Agy worker never gets auto-approval, even though the project's worker permissions show **auto** and the session is stored with `session_permissions = auto`. Agy prompts for every tool permission, so an orchestrator-spawned Agy worker stalls until a human approves each step.

**Repro (AO 0.14.10, Windows 11, Agy is TUI-only here: no `agy_acp_server` installed)**
1. Project settings: Worker = Agy, permissions = auto.
2. Have the orchestrator spawn a worker (or `ao spawn --harness agy ...`).
3. Look at the launched process command line:

```
agy.exe --add-dir <worktree> --model gemini-3.8-flash-high --prompt-interactive "<task>"
```

No approval flag is passed. The `sessions` row has `harness=agy`, `session_mode=tui`, `session_permissions=auto`. Three Agy workers across two projects behave the same way.

**Cause:** `backend/internal/adapters/agent/agy/agy.go` (main @ 49bc06b) maps only one mode, in both launch and restore:

```go
if cfg.Permissions == ports.PermissionModeBypassPermissions {   // :120 and :156
    cmd = append(cmd, "--dangerously-skip-permissions")
}
```

`auto` and `accept-edits` are dropped silently, so they behave like `default`.

**Expected:** map the modes to Agy's native flags (from `agy --help`):

| AO mode | Agy flag |
|---|---|
| `default` | (none) |
| `accept-edits` | `--mode accept-edits` |
| `auto` | `--mode auto` |
| `bypass-permissions` | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` |

`gemini/gemini.go` already uses this kind of switch (`auto` → `--approval-mode auto_edit`, `bypass-permissions` → `yolo`). If a mode can't be mapped, the settings UI should say it has no effect for Agy rather than showing "auto".

Agent-assisted investigation; the cause was confirmed against the source on main, and the fix was not tested.

title: feat(chat): mark sent skills and files as colored text in user messages
body:
## Summary

In the composer, `/review` and `@file` show as chips. Once sent, the user message showed them as plain text (`/review the pr…`). Sent messages now show those tokens as their own text in the accent color (`text-logo-accent`, theme-aware in light and dark). Per review feedback there is no pill and no icon in the bubble. The composer keeps its chips unchanged.

**What gets sent and stored:** the composer's Lexical `ComposerTokenNode` sends only its wire text: `/name` for a skill, and the path (quoted if it has spaces, no `@`) for a file. The stored message is plain text with no structured mention data. `fileReferences` and excerpts are a separate annotation feature, shown as tiles.

**How tokens are found:**
- **Recorded at send.** `ComposerEditor` gets a `getTokens()` handle. `ChatComposer` records the chips when it sends, in a small capped localStorage store (`sentComposerTokens.tsx`) under `~/.ao/electron`. Records are kept per session. A send with no session yet (the `/new` page) is recorded under a hash of its text.
- **Derived safely.** Text is colored only when it exactly matches a recorded chip, or a skill listed for the session's agent (`ChatTokenSkills` context, provided in `ChatWorkspace`). The match must be a whole word: at the start or after whitespace, and followed by the end, whitespace or closing punctuation. So `/reviewer`, `a/review`, `@word` and `/Users/me` stay plain. Text inside fenced and inline backtick code is never colored.
- **Text unchanged.** The colored span holds exactly the sent text, so selection, copy and find in chat behave as before. The long-message fold is unchanged.

**Covered:** sent messages, history and replay (records persist), queued bubbles in the timeline, edited and re-sent messages (same session record), the user's own steer bubble (not steers from other sessions), and cloud sessions on desktop (they share `ChatWorkspace` and `HumanMessage`).

## Composing with #8064 (user-message markdown)

`useComposerTokenRenderer(sessionId, body)` returns a stable `(text, renderPlain?) => ReactNode`. It returns `undefined` when the message can have no tokens, which keeps `UserMarkdown`'s memo. Whichever PR lands second wires it into #8064's `renderText` hook. That hook runs on each plain string in paragraphs, list items, `em` and `strong`, and skips code, so colored tokens work inside lists and emphasis:

```tsx
const renderTokens = useComposerTokenRenderer(sessionId, body);
const renderImages = inlineImageRenderer(attachments, sessionId, apiBaseUrl);
<UserMarkdown text={body} renderText={renderTokens ? (text) => renderTokens(text, renderImages) : renderImages} />
```

The inner callback should be wrapped in `useMemo` if `UserMarkdown`'s memo matters there. Worker 74's optimistic attachment tiles live in the strip above the bubble, so there's no overlap beyond nearby lines.

## Not covered

- **Mobile app** (`packages/mobile`): a separate React Native timeline.
- **Messages sent from another device or before this change.** Skills are still colored when the session lists them. Files are not, since nothing was recorded.
- **Queued message dock** (the one-line preview above the composer), **side chats** (their composer doesn't use `ChatComposer`), and the **message editor** (a textarea): all stay plain.
- **Recorded files are per session.** If someone later types the exact same path as plain text in that session, it is colored too.

## Testing

None. Per standing instructions, no tests, typecheck, lint or build were run. The dev app was launched for the user to test by hand; I didn't exercise the flow myself. No existing tests reference the changed markup.

title: fix(chat): show sent attachments and steered messages immediately
body:
Follow-up to #8056. Right after a send, the tiles above the user's bubble were empty or still loading, even though the composer already had the files. Steered messages didn't show at all until the daemon answered.

## Why it happened

- A sent message refers to its files by their staged workspace path. Each tile read its file back from the daemon (`attachmentURL(...)`) after the bubble was drawn. The composer had the bytes but didn't pass them on.
- Steers had no local echo. `optimistic: !shouldSteer` kept the steer's text and files locked in the composer. They showed up in the turn only after the daemon accepted and a refetch arrived.

## What changed, by flow

| Flow | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Normal send** (images, video, PDF, text, other files) | Bubble appears at once, tiles empty until each daemon read finishes | Tiles appear with the bubble, drawn from the composer's in-memory copy |
| **Inline image chips** in the bubble text | Load from the daemon | Use the same local copy |
| **Steer** (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter while a turn runs) | Nothing in the turn until accepted and refetched; text stays visible in the locked composer | Steer row appears in the turn at once, with its files. It sits where it was sent, so later output stays below it. The daemon's row (matched on `clientMessageId`) replaces it with no duplicate and no reordering. A refusal or a failed request removes it, and the draft stays in the composer as before. While it's in flight the composer hides the text and files, the same way it hides a send, with the same 3 s timeout that brings a stalled draft back. |
| **Queued send** | The queue panel shows a one-line label (no tiles); the bubble's tiles load from the daemon when it runs | Unchanged label. If the turn runs within 5 minutes, its bubble uses the local copy |
| **Message editor** (editing a sent message) | Tiles load from the daemon | Uses the local copy while one is available (it shares the tile component) |
| **Cloud sessions**: image and PDF tiles | Fetched from the control plane after the server message arrives | Use the local copy, looked up by the same cloud reference the composer staged |
| **`/new` first message**, worktree already prepared | Echo tiles load from the daemon | Local copy, in both the opening echo and the session's first message |

### Why steering is still not optimistic in the draft store

A steer can be refused ("send it as a new message instead"), and the draft must still be in the composer when that happens. A steer that gets no answer is never retried automatically (`clearUncertainChatComposerDelivery`). Making the draft store optimistic for steers would mean reworking that recovery logic. So the stored draft stays as it is: the timeline shows the echo, and the composer hides the draft while the steer is in flight. The echo looks the same as a send's echo, which also has no special pending style.

## How the local copies are kept (`lib/sent-attachment-previews.ts`)

- On submit, the composer saves an object URL for each staged file, before the echo renders. It uses the picked `File` directly when it still has one (no copy). After a remount it decodes the base64 instead, and skips files over about 18 MB.
- New tiles can get a copy for 5 minutes. A copy stays alive while any mounted tile shows it, and is revoked after that. Each tile keeps the URL it mounted with, so the image source never changes under a drawn tile (no reload, flicker or re-layout). Total kept is capped at 256 MB, oldest first.
- Text previews read a `blob:` URL directly, since a `blob:` URL can't take the `?raw=true` query or a Range header.
- If object URLs aren't available (jsdom), nothing is saved and tiles read from the daemon as before.

## Tests

- New `lib/sent-attachment-previews.test.ts` covers: handing out a URL, decoding when the file is gone, ignoring a repeat send of the same file, expiry and revocation, and keeping a copy alive while a tile is mounted.
- I read the existing composer, steer, queue and file-attachment tests. None should need changes: composer-only steer tests take the non-durable path, which this PR doesn't change. No local test run, typecheck, lint, build or app launch, per the standing instruction. CI will verify.

## Not verified

- Nothing was run or tried in the app. In particular, not checked:
  - that the swap from echo to daemon message really shows no flicker
  - large video and PDF tiles
  - that the steer row lands in the right place against live streaming output
  - the cloud image and PDF lookup (it depends on the server event's `fileName` matching what was uploaded; if it doesn't, the tile just reads from the server as before)

## Not fixed here (follow-ups)

- **Cloud plain sends have no local echo at all.** Only the opening brief does. The message appears when the server event arrives, though its image and PDF tiles are now instant at that point. Adding a cloud send echo is a separate change.
- **Cloud steers with files** send the cloud reference lines as plain text (the cloud steer drops attachments). This was already the case; the echo just mirrors it.
- **`/new` and spawn files held until the worktree exists** (`holdAttachments`). They have no staged path before launch, so the echo can't show them, and the first message still shows the staged name. Fixing this needs the launch response to return the staged paths.
- The queue panel stays a one-line label without thumbnails, as designed.

title: feat(chat): light markdown in your own messages, list keys in the composer
body:
## Summary

Your own chat messages now show light markdown, and the composer helps you type lists. The composer is still plain text.

### Decision 1: how user messages render

Sent and steered bubbles go through a new `UserMarkdown` in `ChatMarkdown.tsx`. It uses the same react-markdown pipeline and components as replies, cut down to a safe subset.

- **Renders:** bullet and numbered lists (nested too), task boxes (read-only), bold and italic, inline code, fenced code, links, `<url>` and bare-URL autolinks, block quotes, and `ao://` session links.
- **Stays literal text:** headings (ATX and setext), `---` rules, 4-space indented code, raw HTML (`<Component>` stays visible), tables, images (`![a](b)` shows as `!` plus a link), footnotes, link definitions and `~strikethrough~`. These are turned off in micromark's parser, not hidden after rendering. Pasted logs and notes keep their look, and no characters disappear.
- **Whitespace:** a single newline is still a line break, so a plain multi-line message looks the same as before. Paragraphs split by a blank line keep a full line of space between them. One change: runs of spaces inside a line now collapse.
- **Nothing runs or opens by itself:** every fence renders as code, ` ```mermaid ` and ` ```math ` included. There is no math plugin, so `$` signs stay text. A link opens only when you click it, the same way reply links do.
- **Kept as before:** the long-message fold (it measures what's rendered), text selection, the Copy button (raw text), and inline image chips. Chips go through a `renderText` hook that also reaches text inside list items and emphasis.
- **Copying a selection:** if your selection covers the whole message, the clipboard gets the raw text you typed. A partial selection copies what you see, as it does for replies.
- **Sending and storage are untouched.** Markdown only changes the display. The stored text and the text sent to the agent are the raw source.

### Chat find (daemon)

The daemon used to index a user message as one plain block. Find highlights map daemon blocks onto the rendered DOM, so a rendered list would have broken them. `FindUserBlocks` now splits user messages with a goldmark parser that has only the same subset: lists, fenced code, quotes, paragraphs, code spans, links, autolinks, emphasis and task lists. Cached blocks are now keyed by role as well as text.

### Decision 2: the composer

The composer stays a plain-text Lexical editor, so the draft is still plain markdown text. Live bullets or bold styling inside the editor would mean a rich-text node model, and that puts chips, paste, undo, IME and drafts at risk. What it does instead (new `composerLists.ts`):

- **Shift+Enter** (or Enter when Enter doesn't send) on `- foo`, `* foo`, `1. foo` or `- [ ] foo` starts the next item: `- `, `2. `, `- [ ] `.
- The same key on an **empty item** removes its marker and ends the list.
- **Tab** nests the item under the one above it and restarts the numbering. **Shift+Tab** moves it out a level, and out of the list from the top level.
- **Backspace** right after a marker removes the marker.

These handlers run at LOW priority, after the existing send and completion handlers turn the key down. They only ever replace a plain newline, a Tab focus move or a Backspace. Enter-to-send, slash and @ completion, prompt suggestions, IME, undo (each list edit is its own step), drafts and paste behave as before. Nothing styled shows in the composer, so nothing in it is misleading.

## Since review

- **Rebased onto #8062.** Both bubbles pass one memoized `renderText` (`useUserTextRenderer`) to `UserMarkdown`. It marks known `/skill` and `@file` wires in the accent color and draws inline image chips, inside list items and emphasis too. Code stays plain.
- **Composer fixes:**
  - A lone `1. ` followed by Shift+Enter is kept; an empty item only ends a list that's already going.
  - Tab and Shift+Tab keep an item's own `[x]` box.
  - Tab stops at the parent item instead of lining up with an earlier list's child.
  - List keys do nothing inside an open ```` ``` ```` or `~~~` fence.
  - Backspace only reads the draft when a space or tab is before the caret.
- **Bubble:** a list, quote or code block at either end of a message no longer adds its outer margin inside the bubble.
- **Find:**
  - Indented lines in a user message are searchable again; the daemon parses them as paragraphs, the way the bubble shows them.
  - Staged image paths are removed per block, after parsing, and only where the bubble draws image chips. A path inside a code span or link label stays searchable.

Known gaps where find can still land a highlight in the wrong place, left as is:
- An image whose alt text contains a link (`![a [b](u)](v)`).
- An entity written without a semicolon (`&copy`).
- The space after a task-list checkbox in a loose list.

The last two behave the same way for agent replies today.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Live styling in the composer (bullets, bold/italic preview).
- Mapping a partial selection back to raw markdown when copying.
- Go/TS shared fixtures for the user subset in `test/chat-find.json`. The fixture test now skips the message-level check for any plain fixture the subset reshapes.

## Testing

Per the standing instruction, nothing was run here: no tests, typecheck, lint, build, app launch or manual check. CI will verify. By reading only, I updated three `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` cases that asserted the old plain rendering, and the Go shared-fixture test.

Not verified:

- How lists, code blocks and quotes look inside the bubble, in light and dark themes.
- The `[p+&]:mt-[1lh]` paragraph gap.
- List keys in the real composer, including IME and undo.
- Whether goldmark's restricted parser splits blocks exactly as micromark does in edge cases.

title: feat(board): open the archive as a searchable modal of compact rows
body:
## Summary

**Before:** the board ended in an inline "Archive 63" section. Opening it showed a grid of heavy bordered cards (title, restore and trash icons, branch pill with a copy button, PR number, a footer with "Terminated", the time and "1 of 1 PR merged"). You couldn't search it.

**After:** a quiet **Archive 63** ghost button sits under the lanes, where the section header used to be. It opens the archive in the Cmd+K surface (one backdrop, the shared glass surface, solid in translucent windows):

- A search field at the top, focused when the modal opens, with the dialog's close ✕ at its right end. It filters as you type across title, branch, PR number (`#123` or `123`), project and agent. Every word has to match. Filtering runs in the client over the sessions the board already has.
- Below it, the archived sessions as live board cards: the same component, hover, cursor, focus and right-click menu as the lanes, without the redundant "Terminated" status or the "1 of 1 PR merged" line. The modal is wider than the palette (up to 1200px) and taller, and the grid never drops below three columns. Newest first. (A compact-row version was tried first and rejected in review.)
- Keyboard: ↑/↓ to move between cards, Enter opens the session, ⌘↵ (Ctrl+Enter elsewhere) restores, Esc closes. Delete has no shortcut (⌘⌫ keeps clearing the search line); it is the trash button on each card. The footer shows these hints. Pointer hover is the card's own CSS; the list's selection is only drawn (as that same hover) while the arrow keys move it, so it never trails the pointer or stays lit after it leaves.
- A card's own controls (restore, delete, copy branch, PR links) act alone and never open the session. Delete still asks for confirmation. That confirm is now owned by the modal, outside the list, so the list's Enter handling can't swallow its keys (`ArchivedSessionCardAdapter` gained an optional `onDelete`; the Scratchpad page keeps the card's built-in confirm, now `DeleteArchivedSessionDialog`). Cloud sessions still have no delete.
- Empty state ("No archived sessions") and no-results state ("No results.").
- A click on a card opens the session once (the card opens itself; the list only handles Enter). Keys from a card's menus and dialogs never reach the list.
- The first 24 cards render with the modal (it never opens empty). The rest mount six at a time while the app is idle, up to 120, so scrolling never waits on a mount; past 120, scrolling near the end or arrowing onto the last cards mounts the next 24.
- Cmd+K → **Open archive** (current project, shown when it has archived sessions, with the count) goes to that project's board and opens this modal. It works from any page in the project, including a remote host's board. The palette asks through a one-shot ui-store request that the board consumes; an unconsumed request expires after 5 s.
- Cards whose session ended without a PR used to keep the board's red "terminated" tint; in the archive every card has the plain surface (also on the Scratchpad archive page).

**Behavior notes**
- Opening a session: archived board cards used to have no click action. Enter or a click now opens the session page, the same way Cmd+K already opens archived sessions. Nothing is restored.
- Restore works as before: it navigates on success, shows the restore-unavailable dialog when the session can't be resumed, and shows the error on the card otherwise. It's ignored if you've moved to another board, and other restores are disabled while one runs.
- No backend or archive-semantics changes.

**Removed:** `SessionsArchiveView` and the `ARCHIVE_TOGGLE_HEIGHT_PX` / `archiveToggle*ClassName` exports from `@aoagents/product-ui` (only the desktop board used them), `BoardArchivePanel`, and the board's overlay clip-path / bottom reservation. product-ui README updated. DESIGN.md lists the archive with the other glass surfaces and records the decision.

**New i18n keys** (all 9 locales): `archiveModal.searchPlaceholder`, `archiveModal.empty`, `archiveModal.restore`, `command.openArchive`, `command.archivedCount_*`. Everything else reuses existing keys.

## Tests

No tests, typecheck, lint or build were run locally; CI verifies. Tests edited or added:
- `SessionsBoard.test.tsx`: the archive tests now go through the modal (search filters, focus, Esc, cards in the modal, card controls don't open the session, open without restore, ⌘↵ restore, delete confirms). Removed the collapse/remount and grid-layout tests.
- `product-ui/SessionsBoardView.test.tsx`: removed the tests for the deleted `SessionsArchiveView`.
- `lib/command-palette.test.ts`: Open archive appears only with archived worker sessions, with the right count and action.
- `e2e/window-transparency-overlap.spec.ts`: the archive no longer overlays the lanes, so the overlay/clip-path occlusion half of that test now just opens and closes the archive modal.

## Not verified / risks

- Checked in the dev app (dark theme, a copy of real data, CDP): cards on the first frame, ✕ closes (Enter on it opens nothing), the delete confirm opens on top and Esc closes only it, Cmd+K Open archive from a session page lands on the board with the modal open. Scroll p99 frame time went from 25–42 ms to 9.3 ms with idle mounting. Light theme not checked.
- The restore-unavailable dialog over the modal wasn't exercised by hand (the delete confirm, which uses the same placement, was).
- PR titles aren't searchable: session facts only carry PR number, state and URL. Each card still loads its own SCM summary, as the board's cards did, so only 24 mount at a time.

## Follow-ups

- #7265 (archived sessions on demand): once the workspace list stops carrying ended sessions, this modal is where paging (`active=false&limit=&cursor=`) and a loading state should go. Today every archived session is already in memory, so there's nothing to page.
- The Scratchpad archive page (sidebar → Archived sessions, `StandaloneArchiveView`) still uses the old cards. It could open this same modal scoped to Scratchpad.
- Mobile has its own paged archive section of rows with no search.
- The archive confirm copy ("restore it from the Archive section later") still says "section".

title: fix: honor Agy worker permission modes
body:
Code changes: +14 -4  
Tests: +75 -45  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Honor Agy worker permissions when launching and restoring terminal sessions.

## Why

Fixes #8061. `auto` and `accept-edits` were stored but silently omitted from the Agy command.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `accept-edits` launches/restores without an approval flag | Adds `--mode accept-edits` |
| `auto` launches/restores without an approval flag | Adds `--mode auto` |
| Default has no flag; bypass uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Both behaviors preserved |

## How

Use the existing Gemini-style normalized permission switch in both Agy command paths. Verified against installed Agy 1.5.4 `agy --help`: all requested flags match. Table-driven tests compare complete launch and restore argv for all four modes, including model, workspace, prompt/conversation arguments.

Chat intentionally unchanged: `agyacp.sessionMode` already maps default to `default`, accept-edits to `auto_edit`, and both auto and bypass to `yolo`. Thus Chat auto currently selects the standalone server's approve-all mode, unlike TUI's native `--mode auto`. Any permission request the server still emits is presented to the user; AO does not auto-select `allow_always`.

Chat availability is a separate gap: AO requires the standalone `agy_acp_server.exe` (override `AO_AGY_ACP_SERVER_PATH`, beside agy, or on PATH) and companion `localharness_external.exe`. The installed CLI now exposes `agy acp`, also documented by Google, but AO does not discover/invoke that subcommand. This PR does not change discovery or install software.

## Testing

- PASS: `go test -count=1 -run 'TestGet(Launch|Restore)Command' ./internal/adapters/agent/agy`.
- Regression proof: same tests with original `agy.go` via Go overlay fail exactly the four accept-edits/auto cases.

- `gofmt` and `git diff --check` pass. Required ripwire checks attempted: edit-check/quality-delta cannot obtain a Git baseline in this linked worktree; test-gate reports broad tests/untested entrypoints, not a clean gate.

title: fix(chat): stop entrance animations and edge fades replaying on session switch
body:
## Summary

Switching chats replayed animations for content that was already on screen: tool-call rows and "Ran N tool calls" groups faded in again, and the top edge fade of the chat eased in again. Entrance motion now plays only for content that arrives while the chat is open: a new tool call, a new group, a new live label, a new dock. It no longer plays when a chat is opened, switched back to, loads an older page or scrolls a row back into view.

## Root causes and fixes

**1. Tool rows and groups fading in again.** `ChatWorkspace` is keyed per session, so every switch remounts the timeline. `ActivityRun`'s group wrapper and `ActivityTransition` (which wraps every tool row and every run/subgroup summary label) both had an unconditional `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}`, so everything faded in on each mount.
- New `components/chat/chat-entrance.ts`: a per-timeline gate provided by `Timeline`. `floor` is the newest sequence the chat opened with, taken from the first render that has items. Sequences are conversation-scoped and never reused, so a row above the floor arrived while the chat was open. Older pages loaded with "Load older" sit below it. A `played` set stops a row that windowing remounts from playing again. The gate is a stable mutable object that rows read once at mount, so it adds no re-renders and nothing on the switch path.
- `ActivityRow`, `ActivityRun` and `ActivitySubgroup` pass the gate's answer to `ActivityTransition` through a new `enter` prop (default `true`, so behaviour outside a chat timeline is unchanged). Reduced motion is handled as before.

**2. Top edge fade easing in again.** `useEdgeFade` attached in a passive effect, and its first `syncEdgeFade` ran a frame after mount. A freshly mounted scroller therefore painted unmasked, and `data-fade-start` then animated `--edge-fade-start` from 0 to 24px over 150ms. Separately, `Timeline` returns `null` while the chat is empty, so the effect ran with no scroller and never attached once one existed. A chat that started empty had no edge fades until a remount, and then it animated in.
- `observeEdgeFade` now syncs right away and sets `data-fade-instant` (CSS `transition: none`). The attribute stays until the content has held for two frames after it first overflows, or 1s if it never overflows. That window covers the chat's scroll-to-end snap. After it, scroll-driven changes ease as before.
- `useEdgeFade` attaches in a layout effect. The chat scroller uses a stable callback ref (`useEdgeFadeRef`), so the fade attaches whenever the scroller mounts.
- `useTabScrollEdges` (the chat header's tab strip, which also remounts per session) gets the same instant first state, only on the first attach of each strip element.

**3. The live row's label fading in again.** The `.chat-live-label` span is keyed by label kind, so a working session's "Searching…" label replayed its entrance on every switch. The label a live row mounts with alongside its chat is now drawn in place. Any later change of kind fades in as before. `TurnGroup` passes `entranceKey={\`live:${group.key}\`}` so a remount by windowing doesn't replay it.

**4. Composer docks sliding in again.** The queued-message, question and unsent-message docks used `queue-dock-enter` on mount, and `ElicitationDock` added its own `animate-in`. A dock already up when the composer mounts is now drawn in place, including the question's inner animation via `[data-dock-quiet]`. A dock that comes up later slides in as before.

Already correct, left unchanged: human message and attachment-tile entrance (`newHumanMessageIds`), streamed-prose fade (`ChatOpeningRef`), header slide-in (`headerSlidSessions`), sidebar marker pop, startup step stagger, minimap reveal, and every disclosure under `AnimatePresence initial={false}`.

## Known gaps (not fixed)

- **Cloud paused badge** (`SessionView.tsx`, `CloudLifecycleBadge`): fades and slides in on every switch to a paused cloud session. It needs a "seen" marker per session; I left it out because it is cloud-only.
- **Brand-new chat, first batch:** the floor is taken from the first render with items, so activities that arrive in the same server batch as a new chat's first item don't fade in. Later ones do.
- **Catch-up rows:** if a cached snapshot is stale and a refetch right after the switch brings rows that arrived while you were away, those rows fade in as arrivals.
- **Folded group gaining a live call:** a single history row in a live turn that becomes a group when a new call joins now appears without the group fade.
- **Opening a fold:** new rows still fade inside the accordion's own fade on first open, a double fade that predates this PR.
- **Not audited:** skeleton and loading flashes in the inspector Summary and Activity panes; I only checked them for mount animations.

## Testing

Per the standing instruction, I ran no tests, typecheck, lint, builds or app launches, and did no manual verification. CI is the first check. None of the existing tests I read assert on the classes or initial opacity changed here. Rows rendered without the gate keep `enter = true`. The Sidebar edge-fade test drives scroll events, which still sync immediately.

Not verified in the app: that switching no longer replays, that genuinely new tool calls and the live label still fade in, that the edge fade doesn't pop, and that scroll restore is unaffected.
