title: feat(brand): trace Ruto from the desktop icon and generate every icon from it, with a Liquid Glass app icon
body: ## Summary The app icon, phone icon, sidebar mascot, landing logo and README logo were separate rasters that had drifted apart. Ruto is now traced from the current desktop app icon into vector form, and every icon and logo is generated from that one source. The macOS 26 app icon uses Liquid Glass. | Before (desktop `icon.png` on main) | After (desktop `icon.png`) | After (README / Liquid Glass) | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | | **Sources**, documented in `assets/brand/README.md`: - **Ruto geometry:** the `Ruto` section of `scripts/generate-brand-assets.swift`, traced from the pre-glass desktop icon onto its 1024 grid. It holds the outline, eye holes and baton, the face gradient, and the colors of the rims and eye walls. - **Rims:** built from the outline as mitered chamfers, shaded by which way each edge faces. - **Output:** the script writes `assets/brand/ruto.svg`. Rendered next to the original desktop icon, the mascot differs by about 5/255 per pixel on average. - **`AO.icon/icon.json`:** the Icon Composer document. It has a dark gradient tile, with Ruto and the baton as separate glass groups (specular highlights; a layer-color shadow on Ruto, a neutral one on the baton). The color-space override is gone, so Icon Composer reads the SVG colors as sRGB. Before, the blue rendered as saturated cyan. **Generator:** `swift scripts/generate-brand-assets.swift` (macOS 26+, Xcode 26+; uses Icon Composer's `ictool`, `actool` and `iconutil`). It runs in about 8 s and writes the same bytes on every run. `Assets.car` is only recompiled when the bundle changes, because actool output is not byte-stable (tracked by `Assets.car.sha256`). **Desktop** - macOS 26+: the precompiled `frontend/assets/Assets.car` ships as an extra resource, and `CFBundleIconName: AppIcon` points at it. The system then draws the Liquid Glass icon in light, dark, tinted and clear. - Older macOS: `icon.icns` stays as `CFBundleIconFile` (16 to 1024 px including @2x, with the mask and shadow baked in). - Packager's built-in `.icon` support isn't used, because it throws on hosts older than macOS 26 and the Intel release runner is `macos-15-intel`. `postPackage` now fails the build if `Assets.car` is missing from the bundle. - `main.ts`: packaged apps no longer call `app.dock.setIcon(icon.png)`, which would flatten the glass icon. Only unpackaged runs set the DEV icon. - Regenerated: - `icon.png`, `icon.ico` and `icon-dev.png` - tray template icons (the tray script now takes the silhouette as an argument) - browser extension icons and the QR logo - `ao-logo.svg` (docs OG image and the site copy) - The sidebar, startup loader and first run now use `frontend/assets/ao-mascot.svg`, with dark pupils and the same optical size. It replaces a 256 px PNG plus an SVG eye overlay and its CSS, and both `ao-mascot.png` copies are deleted. **Mobile** - `AO.icon` uses the same glass layers as desktop. - Regenerated: - a full-bleed `icon.png` - Android adaptive background, foreground and monochrome layers - splash, favicon and `mascot.png` - a new `notification-icon.png`, wired into `expo-notifications` - The adaptive layers are scaled from the artwork's farthest pixel, so Ruto stays inside the 66 dp safe zone (31.6 and 32 dp). - Removed `packages/mobile/scripts/generate-icons.sh` and `icon-build/from-desktop.py`. That older generator would overwrite the bundle with PNG layers cut from the desktop render. **README:** same path. `logo.png` is now an Icon Composer render at 192 px for its 96 pt slot. ### Still showing the old artwork outside this repo - orchestrator.inc `/ao-logo.svg` and `/favicon.svg` (the docs header and favicon load these from the site). Copy them from `assets/ao-logo.svg`. - The X and GitHub org avatars. `assets/social/ruto-twitter-avatar.png` is a separate hand-made asset and was left alone. - App Store and Play listings, which update with the next mobile build. ## Validation Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation. What I did locally: - **Generator:** ran it twice; all 32 checked outputs were byte-identical. `Assets.car` was excluded from that check (its stamp was confirmed to match the bundle). - **Renders:** - Icon Composer `ictool` renders of every appearance (Default, Dark, Clear and Tinted). - A macOS icon-services render (`NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:)`) of a stub `.app` carrying the compiled `Assets.car`, in light and dark. - CoreSVG and Chromium rasterize `ruto.svg` the same way. - **Tests:** added forge config tests for the `Assets.car` resource, `CFBundleIconName` and the `postPackage` check. ## Not verified / please check manually - **The real macOS 26+ Dock with a packaged, signed build.** The previews are icon-services renders of a stub bundle, not the app. Check that the Dock, Finder, Launchpad and the dmg volume icon show the glass icon, and that tinted and clear modes work (System Settings → Appearance → Icon & widget style). - A release build on the `macos-15-intel` runner. `Assets.car` is copied as-is, so this should be unaffected. - Expo/EAS iOS and Android builds: the iOS icon from `AO.icon`, Android adaptive and themed icons in a real launcher, the notification icon, and the splash. - The sidebar mascot in the app at 1x and 2x, light and dark, and the docs OG image route with the new SVG.

title: feat(artifacts): cache gallery previews as WebP snapshots rendered offscreen
body: ## What Artifact previews were live-rendered on every view (iframes for HTML, React for markdown/tables/mermaid, pdf.js for PDFs). Now each preview is rendered **once** in a hidden offscreen window, encoded as a **640x360 WebP** (about 2-12 KB), and kept on disk. Gallery cards load that image as a plain `` straight from disk, so nothing is rendered again until the file or theme changes, and it survives restarts. A card with no cached image yet draws live exactly as it did before, so a first visit is no slower than without the cache. ## How - `main/artifact-snapshot-window.ts`: hidden offscreen `BrowserWindow` (kept open for 30 s of idle, then closed) loads a new `artifact-snapshot.html` page that draws the same `ArtifactThumbnail` a card draws (every kind looks identical cached vs live), waits for it to settle, takes the painted frame, and has the page encode WebP (Electron images only encode PNG/JPEG). - `main/artifact-snapshots.ts`: disk cache under `/artifact-previews/`, keyed by cloud org, session, path, `updatedAt`, theme and colour theme (URLs excluded, they change per launch). Bounded to 150 MB / 4,000 files, oldest-read pruned. Renders one at a time in a single warm, low-frame-rate window (every job shares it, so concurrent jobs would unmount each other), newest request first, deduplicated per artifact, 150 ms pause between renders, failures not retried for 60 s, queue capped at 64 (the oldest request is dropped). - Main serves cached images on a `ao-artifact-preview://` scheme (`registerArtifactSnapshotProtocol`; a miss is a 404, another host's artifact is refused). Renderer: `ArtifactSnapshotThumbnail` renders an `` of that URL; on a 404 it draws the live `ArtifactThumbnail`, and once that has stayed on screen 1.5 s with its preview drawn (`data-preview-state`) it asks main to render the snapshot (`artifactSnapshot:request`) in the background. A card that only scrolls past is never rendered. - Second Vite HTML entry (`artifact-snapshot.html`) so the hidden window loads a minimal page, not the whole app (it does load the app's preload, so renderer error handlers and the telemetry policy fetch still run; nothing else of the app does). ## Scope - **Cached:** gallery cards on the Artifacts page and a session's Artifacts tab. - **Still live:** inspector Summary tiles (the newest artifacts). - **Live fallback:** another host's artifacts and any render that fails or has no preview. Remote hosts are decided by `hostId` (carried on the row, rejected again in main and part of the cache key), not by URL shape, since the remote proxy hands out `*.localhost` URLs. - **While no snapshot exists** the card is the live preview, as before; a card past the page's live-preview limit shows its kind icon until its snapshot is ready. - The hidden window shares the app's session (it needs the daemon and cloud access), sets no session-wide handlers, and is closed with the shell window and on quit so it never counts as an app window. - A file with nothing to draw is not retried until restart. Cloud snapshots are kept in their own `cloud/` cache folder, which records the account that owns it. A sign-out, a session lost for good, or another account signing in (also across restarts) deletes it, after any write already under way has finished; Cloud snapshots are served only once that has worked, and a failed delete is logged and retried at the next sign-in or launch. - Board hover card unchanged (cheap text excerpt). ## Verification - Ran in the desktop dev app on a copy of the Artifacts demo data: all 8 files (html, md, png, svg, json, csv, log) rendered correctly to valid WebP, and leaving and returning to the page showed every card instantly. - Unit tests added for the store (cache hit/miss, dedupe, concurrency, retry delay, pruning, IPC validation) and the card component (cached, request, fallback, remote host). **Not run locally**; relying on CI. - Not verified: Cloud artifacts and PDFs (supported, untested). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Artifact galleries can display cached preview images, with live previews shown when snapshots are unavailable. * Snapshots are generated for eligible local and Cloud artifacts; remotely hosted artifacts continue to use live previews. * Previews reflect the selected theme and style. Snapshots are requested after a live preview is ready and has remained visible. * Cloud previews are kept separate between accounts and cleared when you sign out.

title: feat(cloud): show a workspace's own ready check on the startup screen
body:
Code changes: +215 -27\
Tests: +131 -3\
Others: +24 -2 (generated cloud-client schema)

## What

While AO Cloud waits for a bring-your-own Coder workspace's own **ready check** (the connection's "Workspace ready check" command), the cloud session's startup screen now says so, with live progress:

- the workspace step reads **Waiting for your workspace's own setup** instead of "Creating the workspace";
- under the steps: time since Coder reported the workspace ready, out of the check's timeout, and the checks so far (for example `20:12 of 1:00:00 since Coder reported the workspace ready, 31 checks so far`);
- the check's latest output and exit status when the check printed something (bounded and redacted by the control plane). A check that prints nothing, like a bare `grep -q '^Ready' ~/.bootstrap-status`, shows no output block.

It moves on as soon as the check passes, and covers worker and orchestrator sessions in both Terminal and Chat (they share the startup screen).

Contract (additive): `SessionStartupError` gains an optional `readyCheck` (`SessionReadyCheck`: `since`, `timeoutSeconds`, `attempts`, `exitCode`, `output`, `checkedAt`), sent with the new startup error code `workspace_setup_pending` while AO waits, on bring-your-own compute only. The Coder settings hint for the ready check now says the session shows what the check prints while it waits.

Control plane counterpart: OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#78 (private repository).

## Why

A bring-your-own Coder template kept setting up for about 21 minutes after Coder reported the workspace ready. AO correctly waited on the connection's ready check, but the desktop only showed "Creating the workspace" with no explanation while Coder showed the workspace as running, so the session looked stuck and AO looked slow.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Startup screen: "Creating the workspace" for the whole wait, nothing else | Step: "Waiting for your workspace's own setup"; below: "20:12 of 1:00:00 since Coder reported the workspace ready, 31 checks so far", ticking every second |
| A check that prints progress: nothing shown | "Latest output of the ready check (exit 1)" with the tail of what it printed |
| Check passes: loader moves on | Unchanged: the wait is taken down before the worker is installed and the steps continue |

Screenshots from the real app still to be attached: the wait needs a control plane that serves `readyCheck` (the private PR), so the states above are covered by component tests for now.

## How

- `cloudStartupProblem` passes `startupError.readyCheck` through on the existing "retrying" phase, so this extends the startup-error path the loader already uses for its note; no new request or channel. The sessions list (5 s poll) carries it.
- `CloudSessionStartupLoader` renders the wait in place of the plain startup note and relabels the active workspace step. Elapsed time is computed from `since` against the control plane's clock (`desktopClockLeadMs`) and formatted like script step timers (`formatScriptDuration`). The output block reuses the Setup log's output treatment.
- Compatibility: everything is optional. Against an older control plane (no `readyCheck`) the server's message stays the startup note as before; an older desktop against a newer control plane shows the server's `workspace_setup_pending` message as its note. Providers without a ready check never send it.
- Strings added for every locale, including the CLDR plural forms.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts` on `CloudSessionStartupLoader.test.tsx`, `SessionView.test.tsx`, `cloud-lifecycle.test.ts`, `i18n/*`, `CloudSessionStartupError.test.tsx`, `chat/CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx`, `useWorkspaceQuery.test.ts`, `CloudWorkspaceExplorer.test.tsx`: 605 passed.
- New tests fail on `main`'s sources (9 failed: loader, lifecycle, SessionView worker/orchestrator x Terminal/Chat), pass with the change. Cases: empty output (no output block), printed output, no timeout, check passed, wait without progress stays a note.
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend): clean.
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` leaves `schema.ts` unchanged, `typecheck` and `test` (31) pass.
- `oasdiff breaking` against `main` with `.github/cloud-contract-severity-levels.txt`: no breaking changes.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.

Redesigns the Artifacts page header and adds bulk delete in the new layout.

**Supersedes the bulk delete in #8033.** That PR's selection logic, delete path, confirmation dialog, strings and tests are ported here onto the new header, so #8033 can be closed once this lands.

### Header and filters
- The **Artifacts** title moves into the topbar beside notifications, using the same `Package` icon as the inspector (the left sidebar now uses it too).
- Below the title, a filter row has location pills on the left: **All · On this machine · Cloud**. **Cloud** only shows when the control plane keeps artifacts.
- On the right are icons for **search**, **filter**, **list view**, **select** and **new**.
- The **Filter** menu filters by **project** and by **type**: All images, All videos or All documents. Documents are everything that isn't an image or video, including HTML, Markdown and PDF. Each active filter shows as a removable chip.
- Search sits behind an icon. It stays open while it holds a query, and Escape clears it.
- The gallery shows **three artifacts a row**, dropping to two, then one, on narrow panels.

### Bulk delete (ported from #8033)
- The **Select** icon (Myna `SelectMultiple`) turns on checkboxes on every gallery card and list row.
- While selecting, the toolbar shows **N selected · Select all / Deselect all · Delete · Cancel**. **Search and the Filter menu stay usable** (a change from #8033), so you can narrow the list and use Select all on what's showing. Escape in search clears the query without leaving selection mode.
- The delete path, partial-failure handling, unpinning and view-only cloud files behave as in #8033.

### Session inspector
- A session's **Artifacts** tab shows cards **two to a row** at every width. It used to be one column until the panel reached 30rem.
- The cards no longer repeat the **session name**, since every card belongs to that session; each shows only its time.

### File type icons
- One helper, `artifactFileIcon`, gives every artifact a Myna object icon for its type. The Summary list, the Artifacts list view, gallery card labels and thumbnail placeholders all use it.
- The mapping is Globe for HTML, FileText for Markdown, Image, Video, Music for audio, ChartBar for Mermaid, Table for CSV and spreadsheets, Presentation, Archive, Database for JSON, YAML and config, and Code for source. PDFs and unknown files use File.

title: fix(cloud): show and apply project instructions changed while a session runs
body:
Code changes: +160 -10\
Tests: +105 -0\
Others: +105 -3

Control-plane PR: OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#79

## What

AO Cloud: project instructions (orchestrator and worker instructions in Project settings) that change while a session runs now reach that session without anyone retyping them or losing the conversation.

- Contract (`contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, additive): `Session.outdatedInstructions` (`restart` | `next_start`), set while the project's instructions for the session's role changed after its agent started and the agent does not run with them yet; and an optional `restartSessionAgent` body `{ "applyInstructions": true }` that restarts even a running agent so it starts with the current instructions, keeping its conversation. `@aoagents/cloud-client` regenerated, `restartSessionAgent` takes `applyInstructions`.
- Desktop:
  - Cloud project settings > Instructions now say when changes apply: new sessions start with them; running sessions pick them up with their next Chat message, or when their terminal agent restarts.
  - Project board: a Cloud orchestrator with outdated instructions gets a banner ("Orchestrator instructions changed after this agent started. Restart the agent to apply them. The conversation is kept.") with a **Restart agent** button. This restart resumes the conversation in place; it is not the existing `restart_needed` Restart, which replaces the orchestrator with a new session.
  - Agent terminal (orchestrator or worker, terminal interface): the same notice as a strip above the terminal.
  - The button is disabled while the agent is working (restarting would end its turn) and says so; for a session whose worker can only apply them at its next start (`next_start`), the notice says that and offers no button.

## Why

A customer saved orchestrator instructions a few minutes after the project's orchestrator started. The running orchestrator never got them and the instructions had to be retyped into the chat. The same applied to worker instructions.

Root cause (in the control plane): a session's instructions were handed to it once, when it started, so a change after that never reached it until it was restarted, and nothing recorded which instructions a session ran with, so the app could not tell the user either.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Instructions saved after a session started are silently ignored by it until its worker restarts; the user retypes them into the chat. | Chat sessions run their next message with the saved instructions automatically. Terminal sessions show "instructions changed after this agent started" with Restart agent, which applies them and keeps the conversation. |
| Settings hint: "Added to every worker's prompt." | Adds: "New sessions start with these instructions. Running sessions pick up changes with their next Chat message, or when their terminal agent restarts." |

Screenshots of the board banner and the terminal strip to follow (draft).

## How

- The control plane decides and reports the state (`outdatedInstructions`); the desktop only renders it and calls the existing restart route with `applyInstructions`. No new route.
- Chat needs no UI: every Chat turn already resumes the conversation in a new agent process, and the control plane now hands the worker the instructions current when the turn is claimed.
- What the model actually receives was checked with the real CLIs against a local stub model API: Claude Code keeps the system prompt it recorded when a conversation started unless it is launched with `--system-prompt-snapshot off`, and Codex does not resend developer instructions on `thread/resume`. The control-plane PR handles both, so the Restart agent action and Chat's next message deliver the new instructions to the model, not only to the CLI.
- A terminal agent is not restarted automatically: a draft typed in the agent's own input box cannot be detected reliably and would be lost, so the restart is the user's explicit action.
- Compatibility: every addition is optional. An older desktop ignores the field and sends no body; a newer desktop against an older control plane never sees the field (no button), and an older control plane ignores the body. `oasdiff breaking` against `main`: no breaking changes.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/OutdatedInstructionsNotice.test.tsx src/renderer/components/CloudProjectLayoutSettings.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n src/renderer/types src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.test.tsx src/renderer/components/SessionView.test.tsx src/renderer/hooks src/renderer/lib/cloud-cp`: pass.
- Fail without the fix: with the fix's sources stashed (tests kept), the new notice tests (6), the settings copy test and the cloud-client restart test fail; they pass with it.
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend), `npm --prefix packages/cloud-client run typecheck && npm --prefix packages/cloud-client test`, `schema.ts` regenerated with `npm --prefix packages/cloud-client run generate`, `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: pass.

The only gate was `isSimplifiedTopbar` (`developerMode && ao.simplifiedTopbar !== "false"`). The tab strip, the dividers (#7918/#7945) and the tab menus (#7877/#7955) had no gate of their own.

### Ungated (now the only behavior)
- `CenterPanelShell`: the top bar floats on macOS whenever the window is not in native fullscreen (`center-panel-shell--floating-topbar` / `--bare`).
- `SessionTabsTopbar`: the New terminal `+` sits right after the last tab, not with the actions. The tab list no longer stretches (`flex-1` dropped in `CenterPane` and `ChatWorkspace`).
- `SessionTopbarActions`: the new cluster for everyone. Workers get a quiet Orchestrator link first. Orchestrators get Board, then New task as the one filled action. Archive is reachable through ⌘⇧A only, as before in the new bar.
- `ProjectBoardActions` board header: Orchestrator is quiet and first, New task is filled.
- `CueRunMenu` hover/focus handling from the new bar.
- `topbar_action_clicked` telemetry now reports for everyone, not just Developer Mode.

### Deleted (dead code)
- `lib/simplified-topbar.ts` (+ test), `hooks/useSimplifiedTopbar.ts`.
- `LegacySessionTopbarActions` and `LegacyTopbarArchiveButton`, which were a verbatim copy marked "delete when the simplified bar graduates".
- The `simplifiedTopbar` store field, its setter, the `ao.simplifiedTopbar` storage key, the Developer Mode "Simplified top bar" switch and its palette entry.
- i18n in all 9 locales: `settings.simplifiedTopbar`, `settings.simplifiedTopbarHint`, `shell.openKanban`, `shell.archiving` (the last two were used only by the old cluster).
- Tests for the old layout, and the `developerMode: true` setup that only existed to show the new bar.

### Deliberately left gated (not part of this change)
- **Split panes (#7791)**: `splitPanesEnabled` = `developerMode && splitPanes`. It is separate from the tab strip; the drag ghost only copies the floating class.
- **Terminal agent status (#7787) and terminal titles (#8018)**: `ShellTerminalTab`, `SessionView`, `useWorkspaceQuery`.
- **Left sidebar (#7365)**: already on for everyone. Developer Mode only allows opting out. Not tied to the top bar.
- Side chats, dictation, diagnostics, Chrome agents, CLI link, the feature update channel and the Developer Mode switch itself are unchanged.

### Stored settings
- Nothing reads `ao.simplifiedTopbar` anymore. Users with Developer Mode on or off, or with the switch off, all get the new bar on next launch.
- Tab order, active tab and inspector state use their own keys, which are untouched, so no tabs or layout are lost.
- The stale `ao.simplifiedTopbar` value stays in localStorage and has no effect.
- The main process never read this flag, so there is no startup change.

## Tests
Per the standing instruction, I did not run anything locally (no tests, typecheck, lint, build or app launch). I updated tests by reading them:
- Unit: `CenterPanelShell` (the legacy case now checks that native fullscreen does not float), `CenterPane`, `ProjectBoardActions`, `SessionTopbarActions`, `GeneralSettingsSection`, `topbar-telemetry`, `board-empty-states`.
- e2e: `titlebar-brand` now expects `Board` instead of `Open Kanban`. `topbar-controls` and `files-narrow-inspector` no longer turn on Developer Mode.

## Risks / not verified
- Not checked in the real app on macOS (floating/transparent, light and dark), Windows/Linux title bars, remote sessions or window drag regions. The non-mac paths did not change: they never got the floating class. The `+` placement and cluster changes do apply on every platform.
- CI is the first typecheck and test run of this change.

title: feat(cloud): show and update Cloud's harness versions beside local ones
body:
Code changes: +523 -32\
Tests: +491 -0\
Others: +689 -0 (contract and generated `schema.ts`, i18n catalogs)

## Review fixes

From the control-plane review (OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#82):
- A release an organization chose that AO's tested release has since caught up with no longer runs. The control plane reports it as `supersededVersion` (no `selectedVersion`, `advisory.currentVersion` is the AO-tested release), so the Harness page shows the AO-tested version. The field is added to the contract (`additionalProperties: false`) and to `CloudCpHarnessVersion`, with a `describeCloudHarness` test.
- `UNVERIFIABLE_HARNESS_VERSION` (a release whose install AO Cloud cannot check against its publisher) is added to the install route's 422 codes. The desktop shows the control plane's message, as for the other codes.
- Checked: `tsgo --noEmit`, the four Cloud harness test files (52 tests), and `packages/cloud-client` typecheck and tests (31) with `schema.ts` regenerated.

## What

AO Cloud joins the Harness settings page and the startup update notice as one more place a harness runs. For Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, each harness's installation row gets a compact second line for Cloud: the release new Cloud sessions run, the newest release, and (for organization owners and admins) one Update that covers this computer and Cloud together. The cloud contract gains three routes for it: `GET /orgs/{orgId}/harness-versions`, `POST /orgs/{orgId}/harness-versions/{agent}/install` and `DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/harness-versions/{agent}`.

Control-plane side: OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#82 (org setting, publisher lookups, worker installs with integrity checks, model catalog that follows the org's release).

## Why

"Claude Fable 5.2 isn't visible on cloud projects." Locally a user updates Claude Code from Settings, and the newer CLI lists Fable 5.2. Cloud sessions ran the CLI release pinned in the control plane (Claude Code 2.1.287, whose `fable` alias still describes Fable 5.1), and the only way to move it was a control-plane release plus an image bake. This PR gives Cloud the same GUI the local harnesses have, built from the local code: the same rows, Update action, progress and failure states.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Harness page: no Cloud information on a harness's page; the Cloud tab's rows say "API version not reported". | One installation row per harness with a quiet Cloud line: `Cloud v2.1.287`. The Cloud tab's rows show the same version. |
| No way to change the Claude Code, Codex or Cursor release Cloud sessions run. | An admin sees `v2.1.322 available` on the Cloud line and one **Update** (hover: "Updates this computer and Cloud"); a member sees the version read-only. |
| Startup notice: only this computer's updates. | The same harness entry says "This computer and Cloud" and its one Update covers both; a member never sees a Cloud update. |
| A Cloud model list for a new task always came from the pinned CLI. | After an update, the list a session on the new release reports (with Fable 5.2) is the one new tasks offer. |

Screenshots (rendered from the real components and CSS in a component fixture, dark theme; I cannot upload from this environment, so they need attaching by hand): `~/.ao/dev/cloud-harness-versions/screenshots/` on the author's machine: `both.png`, `both-hover.png`, `cloud-only.png`, `member.png`, `none.png`, `failed.png`.

## UX

The cloud data never adds a row, a card, a modal or a focus change.

- **One row per harness.** Cloud is a second, compact line inside the harness's existing installation row (`HarnessDetailRow`'s new `secondary` slot), not a row or card of its own. The harness list keeps one entry per harness; its single status mark covers both places (one update icon, one spinner, one error dot).
- **Quiet by default.** With no Cloud update, the line is the Cloud label and the version only: no badge, no button.
- **Both places need an update (admin).** One Update button in the row; it starts this computer's update as before and saves Cloud's newer release. Which places it covers shows on hover. Progress shows on the same button and on the Cloud line; a failure shows in the same row.
- **Only Cloud needs an update (admin).** The same Update button, hover "Updates Cloud". When the harness is not installed here (the row's action is Install), the Cloud line carries its own small Update instead.
- **Member.** The Cloud line shows the version read-only; no update is offered anywhere, and the details say only owners and admins can change it.
- **Details on demand.** The Cloud label is a disclosure: it opens the AO-tested release, Claude's Chat adapter release (read-only: it always runs the release AO tested, also after a Claude Code update), a failed install's error and output, and **Use AO-tested version** (admins, when Cloud runs a newer release).
- **No layout shift.** While Cloud's versions load, the line is already in place ("Checking…") at the same height; the startup notice waits for Cloud's answer with its first batch, so an entry never gains a Cloud target after it shows.
- **Startup notice.** No separate Cloud cards: Cloud is one more target of the same harness entry ("This computer and Cloud", per-place versions on hover; "Cloud" when it is the only target). Dismissing the entry dismisses both. Someone who cannot change Cloud's version never sees a Cloud update.

## How

- **Contract** (`contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, generated `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts`, type aliases): additive routes and schemas. Each harness entry carries the local daemon's `AgentInstallPlan`, `AgentUpdateAdvisory` and `InstallJob` shapes, so the renderer reads Cloud with `hasConfirmedHarnessUpdate`, `maintenanceMethodId`, `isFailedInstallJob` and `versionLabel` like a computer's harness. `plan.methods[0].updateAvailable` is false for a member, so the read-only state is the existing "cannot update" state.
- **`useCloudHarnessVersions`** reads the versions (refreshing on the advisories' 15-minute schedule) and treats a 404 or 405 from an older control plane as "nothing to show". Its `startUpdate` re-checks at click time (`refresh=true`) and installs the newest release it finds, as the local update re-checks its advisory.
- **`HarnessCloudLine`** renders the line; `HarnessAccountTab` folds Cloud into its single installation action; `LocalHarnessContent` runs the combined update (Cloud's save, then the local update exactly as before, including the sessions-in-use dialog).
- **`HarnessUpdateNotice`**: each entry is now `{ local?, cloud? }` per harness; Update all also saves Cloud's releases.
- **Copy** says "Cloud", the term the app already uses (the Cloud tab, "Cloud project"); new strings are in all nine locales.
- **Relation to #7954** (remote hosts in the notice): this PR does not depend on it. Both change the notice; whichever merges second needs a small rebase in `HarnessUpdateNotice.tsx`, where Cloud stays one more target of a harness entry (under #7954's per-host model, Cloud counts as one more host in the same stack).

## Testing

- `npx tsgo --noEmit` (frontend typecheck): passes.
- `npm test` (full frontend vitest suite): 12,587 passed; 54 failed in 6 files unrelated to this change (`browser-profile-import`, `browser-cookie-repair`, `annotate-preload`, `remote-proxy`, `ContextMeter`, `ChatWorkspace`), which fail the same way on this machine without it: `better-sqlite3` built for Electron and Vite's file allow-list under a shared `node_modules`, locale number formatting, an HTTP/2 timeout. CI is the check for those.
- New tests, all failing with the UI wiring reverted (11 of 12 fail; the 12th asserts that a member sees nothing, which also holds before):
  - `HarnessSettingsSection.cloud.test.tsx`: both places need an update (one row, one Update, no extra card, both updates start, hover text); Cloud-only update for an admin; member read-only line with no update; no update anywhere (quiet line); line held in place while loading; failed install in the same row with Use AO-tested version; own Update when not installed here.
  - `HarnessUpdateNotice.cloud.test.tsx`: Cloud folded into the harness entry with one Update; Cloud-only entry for an admin; nothing for a member; waits for Cloud's answer; dismissing dismisses both.
  - `useCloudHarnessVersions.test.tsx` (older control plane, click-time re-check, member click does nothing, refused update); `lib/cloud-cp/client.test.ts` (routes and bodies).
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` is clean against the contract, `npm run typecheck` and its tests pass.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- Not run locally: the Electron app itself (screenshots come from a component fixture), and the Go and docs CI jobs (no Go or docs changes).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; screenshots need attaching from the paths above
- [x] Tests added for the user-visible behavior
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (to verify on the PR)

title: feat(tabs): ⋮ always on the session tab, ghost close button over the icon on others
body:
Builds on the new tab UI from #8077 (merged), rebased onto `main` after #7822.

## What changes in the session tab strip

- **Only the session tab has a ⋮ menu, and it's always visible.** It sits after the title on the right, at rest as well as on hover, and never covers the agent logo. It's the same menu as right-click: rename, copy, archive with its confirmation, split rows, and the agent picker and interface switch where they apply. It shows in every state, including Cloud, orchestrator and agents that can't switch. Before, it was there in some states and replaced by a switch icon, or nothing, in others. While an interface switch is being requested or running, its status (cancel on hover) takes the ⋮'s place.
- **The session tab is wider.** It can grow to 260px (new `--size-session-tab-max`) so its title and ⋮ fit. Other tabs keep main's sizes and fit their content: a 64px minimum, a 140px maximum, and 192px for agent shells.
- **Every other tab keeps its close button (X) in the icon's place on hover**, as on main. That covers shell, file, diff, artifact and the focused member of a split group. Their menus stay on right-click, in the original row order. The reviewer tab can't close, so it shows no button.
- **The X and ⋮ are pure ghost buttons.** No background on hover, focus or while the menu is open; only the glyph brightens.
- **Cloud's interface switch moved into the session ⋮ menu**, as the "Switch to chat/terminal UI" row local sessions already have. Cloud still gets no agent picker (new `picksAgent` flag).
- **Middle-click closes** shell and file tabs, and a split member's pane, exactly as their X does. A middle or right press no longer starts a reorder drag.
- **The chat session tab keeps its agent logo.** #7822 dropped it, which left the chat tab as the one session tab without an icon. `providerIcon` is removed.
- **A shell agent's state is a badge on its logo.** It used to be a spinner, red alert or dot after the title, which shifted the title as it came and went. It's now a 6px dot on the logo's corner: pulsing while the agent works, red while it waits on you, muted for a finished turn not yet seen. Split group members show the same badge. The screen-reader text is unchanged. `ShellAgentIcon` replaces `ShellAgentStatus`, and the frame's `trailing` prop is gone.

`TerminalTabFrame` gains `actionPosition` (`"icon"`, the default, or `"end"`) and `wide="session"`.

Unchanged: ⌘W, F2 and double-click rename, Shift+F10 and the context-menu key, every right-click menu's rows and order, the archive confirmation, drag-reorder and drag-out to split, active and hover fills, light/dark themes, the macOS floating bar, and every aria-label ("Close terminal …", "Close …", "Session actions").

## Why ⋮ on the session tab and X on the others

The session tab can't be closed. Its actions are switching the interface, picking the agent, renaming and archiving, so an X there would promise a close that doesn't exist. Every other tab's main action is closing. Showing the session's ⋮ all the time marks that tab as the session's own.

Rejected along the way: ⋮ on every tab, with Close tab first in the menu (closing takes two clicks); every tab reserving a control slot after the title (it left empty space on the right of short tabs).

## Tests

Nothing was run, per the standing instruction. I updated these by reading the code only:
- `ShellTerminalTab.test.tsx`: middle-click closes.
- `CenterPane.test.tsx`: session ⋮ after the title, `max-w-session-tab-max`.
- `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: chat tab logo back.
- `TabMenuParity.test.tsx`: `picksAgent` fixtures.

## Not verified / risks

- Not seen in the app, including the Cloud ⋮, the agent badge (Developer Mode only) and middle-click on Linux.
- Middle-click closes a shell running an agent without a confirm, the same as X and ⌘W.

title: feat(remote): per-device tokens and one-time pairing codes
body:
Every hand-paired device shared one pairing password that never expired, so one device could not be revoked without re-pairing all of them.

- **Pairing codes.** `POST /api/v1/mobile/pairing-code` (loopback only) makes a code that works once, within 10 minutes.
- **Device tokens.** A device exchanges a code, or the pairing password it already holds, at `POST /api/v1/remote-host/devices` for its own token. The registry (`~/.ao/mobile/access-devices.json`, 0600) stores only token hashes.
- **Listener.** Accepts device tokens. A removed device gets `DEVICE_REVOKED`. `require-device-credentials` refuses the pairing password; device tokens and the account token still work.
- **Device list.** `GET /api/v1/mobile/devices` merges devices with push registrations and shows the linked account's shared token as one row. `DELETE /api/v1/mobile/devices/{id}` revokes the token, closes its connections and removes its push registration. Regenerate also removes every device token and push registration.
- **Account linking.** `/api/v1/remote-host/account-token` accepts a device token as proof.
- **CLI.** `ao remote-host pair`, `devices`, `devices revoke <ID>|--all`, `require-device-credentials on|off`. `enable` and the installer print a pairing code instead of the password.

The device list UI changes here because the route and response shape change.

Devices signed in through the account keep sharing one token. A device removed while the host still accepts the password can be paired again by hand with that password.

Tests:
- `go test ./...`: the changed packages pass, also with `-race`. Tests in `commandcode`, `integration`, `sessionimport` and `shellterm` fail on my machine with and without this change.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2: 0 issues on the changed packages.
- `npm run api` leaves `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` unchanged.
- Frontend `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e` and the settings, i18n and remotes vitest suites pass on this branch.
- `scripts/setup-self-hosted.test.sh`: `tunnel-pairing`, `tunnel-pairing-code`, `tunnel-linked`, `tunnel-unavailable`.

title: feat(desktop): pair with one-time codes and per-device tokens
body:
The desktop side of per-device tokens, both as a client of other hosts and as a host.

- **Add host and edit.** The typed pairing code or password is exchanged for this desktop's own token before the host is saved.
- **Saved hosts.** A saved pairing password is swapped for a token on the next connect, never under a live connection. The password is kept, encrypted, as a fallback for a host that goes back to a release without device tokens. A host that answers `DEVICE_REVOKED` is not retried with it.
- **Connect Mobile.** The QR and the code beside it carry a one-time pairing code. It is prefetched with the mobile status, and replaced when a device pairs, when the password changes, and every 9 minutes. The password is hidden until asked for, and not shown once the host refuses it.
- **Settings.** Regenerate becomes Revoke all devices. Turning the password off stays a host command, `ao remote-host require-device-credentials on`, not a desktop switch.
- New and changed strings in all nine locales; `remote-access.mdx` updated.

Tests:
- Frontend vitest: 12,682 pass. `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` clean.
- Docs `check:i18n`, `test` and `build` pass.

Not checked by eye: the Connect Mobile panel in the desktop app. The web preview cannot load it.

title: feat(mobile): pair with one-time codes and per-device tokens
body:
The phone side of per-device tokens.

- **Scan, manual connect and machine edit.** The code's secret, or what was typed, is exchanged for this phone's own token after the identity check and before anything is saved. A used or expired code is reported as a rejected credential.
- **Saved machines.** A saved pairing password is swapped for a token on the next connect. The password is kept in the keystore as a fallback for a machine that goes back to a release without device tokens. A machine that answers `DEVICE_REVOKED` is not retried with it.
- Account-synced machines keep the account token.
- Copy: a rejected credential says to get a new code.

A desktop without device tokens answers 404 to the exchange, and the phone keeps the token it has. A phone app from before this change cannot use a QR from an updated desktop; it pairs with the password.

Tests: vitest 3,587 pass, `typecheck` clean. Not run on a device.

body:

## What

Orchestrator Cloud on the phone. AO Cloud joins the app as an environment beside paired machines, not as a separate tab:

- **Sign in and settings.** Settings → Machines → AO Cloud signs in to Orchestrator Cloud, picks the organization, connects coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) and GitHub.
- **Board, projects, New task.** Cloud sessions sit on the Workers board and Cloud projects in Projects. New task offers AO Cloud in the machine picker, with approval mode and effort. Standalone and GitHub projects can be created. Sessions can be started, renamed, pinned, stopped and deleted.
- **Session screen.** Chat runs on the shared ChatComposer: live event stream, attachments, plans, approvals, usage, and the opening brief while the sandbox starts. Chats open newest first, and "Load earlier messages" pages back. The agent's terminal and the sandbox shell are both there, and a session switches between Chat and Terminal UI.
- **PRs, Files, Artifacts.** The same screens as for machine sessions, through backends picked per host:
  - PR cards and the PR tab.
  - The review page with Cloud reviews and the reviewer's chat, Send to worker, and merge.
  - Changed files and their diffs.
  - The artifact gallery, viewer and history. A file its creator published shows its public link, with Share link and Copy link.
- **Notifications.** Cloud notifications appear in the inbox. They also arrive as pushes once the control plane sends them (the control-plane change: OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#87).
- **Plan.** Settings → AO Cloud shows the organization's plan and its usage: the two session-hour windows as native progress bars, with when each resets, and running and total sessions. New task on AO Cloud says up front when the plan can't start a task. Any request the plan refuses opens one sheet with Cloud's reason, when it lifts, and the usage. On Free, which runs no cloud agents, coding agents, GitHub and New cloud project are hidden.
- **Contract.** Adds `PUT` and `DELETE /me/push-devices/{installId}` and a read-only `GET /orgs/{orgId}/billing`, all additive, and regenerates the cloud-client schema.

## Why

Cloud sessions could only be run from the desktop. This lets the phone start, follow, review and merge Cloud work the way it already does for paired machines.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The phone lists paired machines only; Cloud sessions and projects don't appear | AO Cloud is listed with the machines. Its sessions are on the Workers board, its projects in Projects, and it is a choice in New task's machine picker |
| No way to sign in to Orchestrator Cloud from the phone | Settings → Machines → AO Cloud: sign in, pick the organization, connect Claude Code / Codex and GitHub |
| A Cloud session can't be opened | Chat with live events, attachments, approvals and plans, newest messages first. Agent terminal and sandbox shell. Chat ↔ Terminal UI switch with the same card machines show |
| PRs, Files and Artifacts work for machine sessions only | They work for Cloud sessions too: review, reviewer chat, Send to worker, merge, diffs, the artifact viewer and history, public links |
| No Cloud notifications on the phone | Cloud notifications in the inbox, and as pushes once the control plane enables them |
| No plan or usage on the phone | Settings → AO Cloud shows the plan and its usage. New task says up front when the plan can't start a task, and any refusal opens a sheet with the reason and when it lifts |

Device screenshots from the iPhone and Pixel test runs will follow in a comment.

## How

- **No native change.** `@expo/fingerprint` gives this branch the same runtime as `main` on iOS and Android (same checkout, same install).
  - `main` itself left the runtime 2.3.0 was built at with #8069: the new app, splash and notification icons are native. So no EAS update published from `main` reaches 2.3.0 any more, with or without this PR.
  - This PR's commits up to 9be76d0918, before `main` was merged in, keep the earlier runtime. The plan work after them is JS as well. Merged onto `main` as it was just before #8069 (30cd5ff3da~1), they give the same iOS and Android runtime as that commit. Cloud can still go to 2.3.0 as an update, published from such a branch.
- **Coding-agent sign-in without the native piece.** Claude connects with its paste-back code and ChatGPT with a device code. One-tap browser sign-in needs a native loopback listener, which is in #8086 and goes out in the next store build. `lib/cloud/browserSignIn.ts` checks for that module when it runs, so the same JS uses the browser once a build has it, with no flag. GitHub connect needs no native code: it opens the signed-in browser (expo-web-browser).
- **One set of screens, two hosts.** The screens stay shared: `lib/reviewBackend.ts`, `lib/files/backend.ts` with `files/cloudBackend.ts`, and `lib/artifactsBackend.ts` with `lib/cloud/artifacts.ts` pick a machine's daemon or Cloud. AO Cloud is host `orchestrator-cloud` in the store. Every account-scoped cache is cleared together when the provider resets (`lib/cloud/accountCaches.ts`).
- **Newest-first chat** (`lib/cloud/chatHistory.ts`). It loads the newest 150 events and the 30 minutes before them, then older pages via `before`/`nextBefore`. A closed chat stays cached for an hour, at most 8 chats.
- **Chat ↔ Terminal UI for Cloud.**
  - Upstream's hook became `useInterfaceTransitionWith(backend)`, and `lib/cloud/interfaceTransition.ts` is the Cloud backend.
  - Cloud drops a finished transition from the session status. So `useCloudSwitchHandoff` reads the session again and holds the card until the new interface shows; without it, "Agent terminal ended" flashed.
  - The card covers the screen from the tap. The banner is kept only for "Finish, then switch" on a busy agent.
  - From an idle terminal the switch back to Chat uses `interrupt`, because Cloud's `drain` never finishes there (SOURCE_DRAIN_FAILED).
  - Machines keep upstream's behavior.
- **Artifact public links.** Read from `GET /me/artifact-shares`. Cloud doesn't record which file a link came from (the desktop keeps its own record), so a link belongs to a file when it names the file's name and the sha256 of the version on screen.
  - A file committed again since it was published shows no link, because the link still serves the old version.
  - Only the session's creator can publish, so only their list asks for links. If the links can't be read, the files list as before.
- **Errors.** Errors are shown in Cloud's own words (`lib/cloud/errors.ts`), including plan limits with their reset time. That holds on the screens shared with machines too (`userFacingError`): a Cloud 429 usage limit used to read as a paired machine's password lockout.
- **Plans** (`lib/cloud/plan.ts`, `planStore.ts`, `planRefusal.ts`, `CloudPlanSheet.tsx`).
  - Read from `GET /orgs/{orgId}/billing`, which the desktop's Plans page already reads. One read serves every screen and stays fresh for 30 seconds. It is cleared on an account change and read again after a refusal.
  - The client reports every plan refusal to its owner (`onPlanRefused`), as the desktop's does, and the sheet opens at most once a minute.
  - The phone shows no prices, checkout or upgrade links, so it stays a companion app under App Store guidelines 3.1.1 and 3.1.3(f). That's also why Free hides what it can't use: the desktop lets a Free user try and sends the refusal to its Upgrade page, and the phone has no such page.
  - The control plane lists `GET /api/cloud/v1/orgs/{}/billing` in `routes-outside-contract.txt`. Its next contract sync after this merges must drop that line.
- **New task's machine and project rows** no longer rise over a notice or button above them while the keyboard is up. Their SwiftUI host keeps out of the safe area, as the composer's controls host already does.

Intentionally not in this PR:
- Project settings and environment variables, cues, an orchestrator's children, and Teams (composer lease, shares, merge requests, org credentials).
- Publishing or unpublishing artifacts from the phone.
- Showing which Claude account is connected. Cloud stores no account identity, so that needs a contract and control-plane change.

Known Cloud-side issue, the same on the desktop: a reviewer's chat turn can stay "running" after its verdict. Closing the review chat cancels the worker mid-turn, so the turn's completion is never recorded.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile` with Node 20, as in CI (`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`), after merging `main`: typecheck passes and all 3867 tests pass with `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`.
  - Under this Mac's en-IN locale, `conversationChrome.test.ts` fails because 1,000,000 formats as "10,00,000". It fails the same way on `main`.
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` leaves `src/schema.ts` unchanged; typecheck, tests and `npm pack --dry-run` pass.
- Contract: `oasdiff breaking` (v1.34.1, as in CI) against `main` reports no breaking changes. `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh` passes.
- `scripts/*.test.mjs`: 26 of 27 pass. The one failure is `go-test-parallel.sh`, which needs bash 4 (`mapfile`); macOS ships bash 3.2, so CI covers it. gitleaks wasn't run locally.
- On device: iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS dev build) and Pixel 10a, against production Orchestrator Cloud.
  - Sign-in, projects, sessions, chat, terminal, and the Chat ↔ Terminal UI switch both ways, on fresh sessions.
  - On a test repository, Cloud workers opened PRs; the phone ran their reviews and merged them.
  - Files and diffs, and the artifact gallery, viewer and history.
- Plan screens: checked on the iOS simulator with sample plan data (a paid plan, near and at its limits, Free, and a refusal).
- Not yet checked on device:
  - The code-based coding-agent connect on a build without the listener, which is what 2.3.0 users get. Worth a pass on a preview build before the production update.
  - Artifact public links, which need a Cloud file published from the desktop.
  - The plan screens against a real plan, and on Android.

## Checklist

- [ ] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable (one feature, but large: it ships Cloud on mobile as one OTA)

title: feat(mobile): sign in to Cloud coding agents through the browser
body:
Code changes: +411 -0\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +61 -0 (podspec, Gradle, manifest, package manifests, lockfile)

> **Goes out with the next store build (2.4.0).** This is a native change, so it moves the app's runtime fingerprint. `main` already left 2.3.0's runtime with #8069 (new app icons), so merging this no longer changes what an update from `main` can reach. It's a draft for now.

## What

A native loopback listener (`packages/mobile/native/oauth-loopback`, iOS and Android) that lets the phone connect Claude and ChatGPT to Orchestrator Cloud through the browser.

## Why

Without it, connecting a coding agent on the phone means copying a code: Claude's paste-back code, or entering ChatGPT's device code. With it, sign-in runs on the provider's own page, in the browser that already holds the person's sessions, saved passwords and passkeys, and returns to the app when done.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Connect Claude: sign in on claude.com, copy the code it shows, paste it into the app | Connect Claude: the provider's page opens in Safari's sign-in sheet (iOS) or a Chrome Custom Tab (Android) and closes by itself once authorized |
| Connect ChatGPT: open the device-code page and enter the code | Connect ChatGPT: the same one-step browser sign-in |

## How

- **Listener.** The module listens on localhost for the provider's OAuth redirect and answers it with a URL back into the app:
  - iOS: `ao-app://agent-login`, the callback of the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, so the sheet closes by itself.
  - Android: an `intent://` URL naming the app's package, so Chrome returns to the app without a chooser.
- **No JS here.** The JS that uses it is `lib/cloud/browserSignIn.ts`, in #8085. It looks for `NativeModules.AOOAuthLoopback` when it runs. Builds without the module, and listeners that can't take their port, fall back to the code-based sign-in. So this PR changes nothing until #8085 is in, and #8085 needs nothing from it.
- **No other native changes.** No config plugin, Info.plist or permission changes: the `ao-app` scheme is already registered, and the listener binds to localhost only.

## Testing

- CI picks no lanes for a draft, so `mobile / check` runs on GitHub when this is marked ready for review.
- `packages/mobile` with Node 20, as in CI (`npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`): 3556 of 3557 pass. The one failure is `conversationChrome.test.ts` under this Mac's en-IN locale. It passes with `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` and fails the same way on `main`.
- `@expo/fingerprint`: with this change the runtime differs from `main` on iOS and Android, as a native change should. Without it (#8085 alone) the runtime equals `main`'s.
- iOS request reading (`AOReadRequestLine`): tested in a socket-pair harness built from the committed function. It covers a request line split across reads, one byte per read, the 8 KiB cap, a client trickling bytes (gives up at 3.0 s), a client that closes early, and invalid UTF-8. The whole file passes `clang -fsyntax-only` against the React Native headers, with no warnings.
- The iPhone and Pixel test builds for the Cloud work included this module. Browser sign-in for Claude and ChatGPT should get one more check on a build of `main` with both PRs merged, before the store submission.

title: fix(sentry): bound desktop error volume and give renderer errors real titles
body:
0.14.10 used up the Sentry quota in two days. Since #7682 desktop errors send at 100%, the renderer cap was keyed on the raw first stack line and lived in memory (one install sent 2.5k errors in about two days), and scrubbing turned almost every renderer error into "Renderer Error in unknown (unknown)" (AO-ELECTRON-1: 38k events on 0.14.10). Budget: about 5.5k errors per day across all apps.

## What changes

**Install sampling (desktop main, renderer, daemon).** An install sends non-fatal errors only when `sha256(install_id)` (big-endian uint32) `% 10 == 0`. Electron main and the daemon use the same hash, pinned by tests on both sides. Electron main uncaught exceptions, process crashes (`process_exit`) and daemon panics always send. Every event is tagged `sample_rate`: `0.1` for sampled events, `1` for the always-sent fatal ones (tagging those 0.1 would make the "multiply by 10" math wrong).

**Caps in Electron main, after scrubbing.** `beforeSend` scrubs, samples, then budgets on the final Sentry fingerprint: 3 per fingerprint and 25 total per install per UTC day, persisted to `~/.ao/data/telemetry_sentry_budget.json`, so a reload, a new window or a restart keeps the counters. The renderer's in-memory exception budget is removed (`reserveCapture` stays for PostHog events). The daemon gains a 25/day per-install total on top of its per-fingerprint budget.

**Real renderer titles.** `safeRendererFrames` keeps anonymous frames (`at app://renderer/assets/x.js:L:C`) and named frames whose function is not allowlisted, as `renderer_frame` with the validated location. Titles now read like `Renderer TypeError in assets/useSessionWorkspaceFiles:123:45 (unknown)`. Error messages stay blank.

**Source maps (debug IDs).** With `AO_PUBLISHED_BUILD=1`, `@sentry/vite-plugin` emits hidden source maps for the main and renderer bundles and stamps debug IDs. Forge leaves every `.map` out of the package. Renderer chunk debug IDs go to main as `debug_meta` images (the SDK overwrites frame debug IDs with main's own lookup), and main bundle frames and images are rewritten to `app:///.vite/build/...`, so install paths never leave.

**Expected states dropped.** Daemon "Model discovery failed" (all variants, including `exec_exit`) is no longer captured, and `CODEX_ACCOUNT_SETUP_INCOMPLETE` is out of the fault codes and also skipped when a deadline caused it (that path would otherwise still be captured as `http_timeout`).

**Published builds only.** Sentry initializes only for a release-stamped `X.Y.Z` or `X.Y.Z-nightly.<12 digits>` version and a build carrying `AO_PUBLISHED_BUILD=1`, which only `build-artifacts.yml` sets. The marker is needed because self-built copies also show bare versions (`0.4.1`, `0.14.99` both reached ao-electron), next to `0.13.0-ragcorp.7`, `0.14.10+ptbr.1`, `0.14.9-nightly....local`. The daemon applies the same version pattern. An explicit `AO_ELECTRON_SENTRY_DSN` / `AO_SENTRY_DSN` still overrides.

`docs/telemetry.md` documents the sampling, caps and published-only rule. PostHog events are unchanged.

## Needs the release conductor

`build-artifacts.yml` is test-enforced to reference no secrets, so it does not upload to Sentry itself. It now publishes `sentry-sourcemaps-<platform>` run artifacts (main and renderer `.js` + `.js.map`, 1 day retention). The conductor has to run `sentry-cli sourcemaps upload --org untrivial-x0 --project ao-electron <dir>` on all four of them (debug IDs come from bundle contents, so a platform whose bundle differs needs its own maps). A build step also fails if the `AO_PUBLISHED_BUILD` define did not reach `.vite/build/main.js`. Until it does, events carry debug IDs but frames stay minified. A build with `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` set uploads directly from the plugin.

## Tests

- Go: install sampling (hash pinned, unsampled and unknown installs send only panics), 25/day total cap, model discovery not reported, Codex setup-incomplete skipped including the deadline variant (mutation checked), published-version gate.
- Electron main: sampling by install with `sample_rate`, fingerprint cap, total cap, cap persisted across a re-init (mutation checked), anonymous-frame title plus debug image, main bundle path normalization, unpublished versions never init.
- Renderer: anonymous frames and chunk debug IDs, no private function text or paths.
- Build: `AO_PUBLISHED_BUILD=1 vite build` of the renderer emits hidden maps with `debug_id` and `//# debugId=` bundles; forge ignore drops `.map`; workflow test pins the marker and artifact.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; full `npm test`: 12688 passed, 1 failure in `browser-history-store` that passes on rerun (untouched file). `go test ./...`: 93 failures in 9 packages (tmux, cli, session_manager, ...), identical test names on untouched `origin/main` locally, so environment-specific. Local golangci-lint is too old for go1.27; CI will lint.

## Risks

- If the conductor ever builds outside `build-artifacts.yml`, that build sends nothing to Sentry (by design, but silent).
- Renderer window errors are sampled like other non-fatal errors; only main-process uncaught exceptions and crashes bypass sampling.
- Daemon total cap is in memory and resets on daemon restart (persistence was only asked for desktop).

title: feat(automations): redesign the page with starters up front, a list toolbar, and plain-language schedules
body:
Code changes: +393 -152\
Tests: +149 -32\
Others: +297 -72

## What

Redesigns the Automations page in the same style as the recent Artifacts page (#8073).

- **Starters stay where they were:** "Start with a template" and the three starter tiles lead the page in every state, as before.
- **No automations yet:** "No automations yet" sits below the starters with a single **New automation** button. There's no toolbar, because there's nothing to search or filter yet.
- **With automations:** below the starters, the list gets a toolbar. **All / Enabled / Paused** pills with counts sit on the left, the same pattern as Artifacts' location pills and the old page's status buttons, so the total is always visible. On the right are search (behind an icon), a **Filter** menu for project (shown only when automations span more than one project), **Sort** (next run with paused ones last, name, or recently created) and a **New automation ▾** menu (Start from scratch or any starter). A project filter shows as a removable chip.
- **List:** one shared list with hover highlights replaces the bordered table with column headers. Each row shows its schedule in plain words ("Weekdays at 9:00 AM", "Every Friday at 4:00 PM", "Monthly on day 1 at 10:00 AM") with the project, then the next run, the last run's status, edit/delete on hover and the on/off switch. Expanding a row still shows the prompt and run history.
- **Starter tiles:** they now use AO's own tile from Add Project and Home: a faint fill that gets stronger on hover, a bare muted icon above a 14px title, three to a row on wide panels.

## Why

The page had a busy header (title, description and button all in the topbar), always-visible starter cards above the list, an always-visible search field and filter pills, and schedules written as fragments ("Mon–Fri · 9:00 AM"). This brings it in line with the Artifacts page, keeps the starters where people already find them, and makes each schedule readable at a glance.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: empty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/before-empty.png) | ![After: empty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/after-empty.png) |
| ![Before: list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/before-list.png) | ![After: list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/after-list.png) |

**After: a single automation (status pills fill the left; no Filter button with one project)**

![After: single automation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/after-single.png)

**After: Filter menu, with a project filter applied**

![After: filter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/after-filter.png)

**After: New automation menu**

![After: New automation menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/after-new-menu.png)

**After: expanded row with run history**

![After: expanded row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d335c296964af0db4a780de6c91ce67c960c0d3d/automations-revamp/after-expanded.png)

Screenshots were taken from the real renderer under the e2e fake bridge (`dev:web` + Playwright) with mocked automations, at 1280×800, dark theme.

## How

- `describeSchedule()` in `lib/automation-schedule.ts` reduces a daemon RRULE (including a DTSTART line) to `daily` / `weekdays` / `weekly` (ordered days) / `monthly` / `other`. Rules with an interval, or day lists AO doesn't author (such as `1MO` or `BYMONTHDAY=-1`), fall back to "Repeats <frequency>" or "Custom schedule", so the list never claims a cadence the scheduler won't follow. Times are formatted as wall-clock values in the automation's timezone, as before.
- `ToolbarSearch` and `FilterChip` move from `ArtifactsView.tsx` into a shared `PageToolbar.tsx`, and both pages use them. Artifacts behaves exactly as before.
- Adds an `ArrowDownUp` (lucide) icon for Sort.
- The create/edit dialog, schedule form, API and telemetry are unchanged.
- New strings are in all nine locales. Retired the page description, the empty-filter message, the old `Monthly · day N` label and `latestState`. The search placeholder drops its trailing ellipsis, per DESIGN.md. The non-English strings were written for this PR and could use a native-speaker pass.
- Intentionally not included: bulk select/delete (unlike Artifacts) and a separate templates view. The starters keep their place at the top of the page and are also offered in the New automation menu.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/AutomationsView.test.tsx`: 62 pass. Updated for the new layout, with new cases for the empty-state order, the starters staying above the list, the toolbar appearing only with a list, the status pills, the project filter showing only with more than one project, the New automation menu, sort order, and plain-language schedules.
- `src/renderer/lib/automation-schedule.test.ts` adds `describeSchedule` cases, including DTSTART rules, interval rules, unauthored BYDAY values and negative month days.
- The ArtifactsView, SessionArtifactsView, i18n catalog/coverage, automation-templates and AutomationMessage tests pass.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean for `frontend/src`. Locally, the only errors were in `packages/product-ui`, whose dependencies weren't installed in this worktree.

title: feat(sidebar): open a project's archive from its row menu
body:
## Summary

Adds **Archive** to a sidebar project row's ⋮ menu and right-click menu. It opens the board's archive modal (#8065) for that project.

- **Placement:** after New task, Open orchestrator and Open dashboard, and before the copy-path and pin/settings/remove groups.
- **Icon and label:** uses the `Archive` icon and the existing `shell.archive` label, the same as the board's Archive button.
- **Count:** the archived count appears muted in the menu's hint column. Its spoken label is the board button's existing `shell.archiveSessionsAria` ("Archive, 3 sessions"). The item is hidden while the archive is empty, as the board's Archive button and Cmd+K's Open archive are.
- **How it opens:** it uses the same one-shot `requestArchiveOpen(projectId, hostId)` as Cmd+K, then goes to the project's board, so the modal opens already scoped to that project. This covers local, remote-host (through `onOpenRemoteProject`) and cloud projects; the board renders the modal for all three. The modal has no "all projects" mode, so there is nothing to widen to.
- **Archive modal height:** the modal's list is now always full height instead of fitting its cards, so the modal keeps one size with only a few archived sessions and while a search narrows them.
- **One shared menu list:** the two menus were separate hand-written lists that had drifted apart. They now render one `MenuEntry[]` through `MenuEntries`, the same model `useTabMenuItems` uses since #7955. As a result, ⋮ now also shows Open orchestrator, Open dashboard and Copy path, which only right-click had before.
- **Performance:** the list is built only when a menu opens, so the count adds no work to a closed row. There are no new queries, polling or subscriptions, and `ProjectItem` takes no new props (#7975 group D).
- **`menu-model`:** `MenuEntry` items gain an optional `count` for the trailing number.
- **DESIGN.md:** the archive rule now lists this entry point and the full-height modal.

### Other rows

- **Scratchpad:** its right-click menu already has Archived sessions (to its own `/sessions` archive page), and it has no ⋮ menu. Unchanged.
- **Standalone rows inside `ProjectItem`** (a remote host's Scratchpad): they have no board, so the entry is hidden there.
- **Orchestrators:** they have no row of their own. They live on the project row's button, so this project-row entry covers them.

### i18n

No new keys. Both strings already exist in all nine locales.

## Testing

Not run, by request: no tests, typecheck, lint, build or app launch. I read the existing `Sidebar.test.tsx` and e2e menu assertions, and every label they query is unchanged.

## Not verified

- Visuals in light/dark and in the collapsed sidebar. The collapsed rail has no ⋮, so right-click on the project icon is the path there.
- Keyboard: arrow navigation, Enter opening the modal, and Esc returning focus to the ⋮ trigger. I expect Radix's focus restore to handle this but did not check it.
- A remote host that is offline: the entry still shows and goes to the board, which shows whatever cached data it has.
- That the trailing count reads well in the shortcut column's micro/tracked type.

title: feat(artifacts): one-click Publish and Republish, and artifact names in the UI font
body:
Code changes: +139 -39\ Tests: +131 -63\ Others: +9 -27 ## What - **Share → Publish, in one click.** The artifact header button (and the preview modal's icon and the "…" menu item) is now **Publish**. Clicking it publishes the file right away and opens the popover on the public link. There is no second Publish click inside the popover. - **Republish when the file changed.** If a published file has changed since its link was made, the header button reads **Republish**. One click puts the newer version on the same link and shows it, and the button goes back to **Publish** once the link is up to date. - **Same popover content.** Copy link, Unpublish, the "Public · anyone with the link can view" line, and the change/credential/error messages are all still there. - **Bare file name as the title.** The popover is titled with the file name alone, without its extension (`launch-plan.html` → `launch-plan`), instead of "Share launch-plan.html". - **Links-left count moved.** The count ("1 of 3 free links left") now shows under the link once the file is published, and refreshes after a publish. - **More breathing room.** The popover padding goes from 12px to 16px, the popover gets slightly wider, and there's more space between lines, all within the DESIGN.md 4–18px rhythm. - **Artifact names in the brand UI font everywhere.** These used the monospace face before: - worker-report `artifact:` lines in chat - inline-code paths that resolve to a listed artifact - code inside `ao://…/artifacts/…` links - the share link field ## Why Sharing took two clicks (Share, then Publish), and republishing a changed file took two as well (Share, then Republish). The popover also repeated "Share" in its title. Artifact names showed in a code font in some places while the buttons beside them used the UI font. ## Before / After Same component and data in both columns, dark theme. Light theme is in the collapsed section below. **New file** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | **1. Click Share:** a panel asks for Publish
| **Click Publish:** the file is published, and the link is ready to copy
| | **2. Click Publish again:** the link
| *(no second step)* | **Published file that has changed since** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | **1. The button says Share** (no sign the file changed) | **The button says Republish**
| | **2. Click Share:** a note and a Republish button, needing another click
| **Click Republish:** the newer version is on the same link, and the button is back to Publish
|
Light theme **New file** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | **Published file that has changed since** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | |
These were captured from the real `ShareArtifactButton`, with the app's CSS, in a throwaway Vite harness. The cloud-share bridge was stubbed (a fake link and fake fingerprints), so no real account or upload was involved. They were not captured from the packaged Electron app. ## How - **Opening the panel publishes.** `SharePanel.load({ publishNow })` publishes directly when the panel opens and the file has no active link. It still stops at a **Publish** button in these cases: - **Credential detected:** the file looks like it holds a secret, so it waits for an explicit click under the warning. - **After Cancel or Unpublish:** it doesn't immediately publish again, so there's no loop. - **File changed mid-publish:** it shows what the file now holds and asks again. - **At the free-plan limit:** Upgrade is unchanged. - **Republish label.** `usePublishedOutdated` decides whether the button says Republish: - **Cheap check first:** it inspects the local file fingerprint, and asks the control plane for the link list only when that differs from the published fingerprint. That confirms the link is still active, so a link unpublished elsewhere keeps the label at Publish. - **When it checks again:** when the file's `updatedAt` changes (passed as `revision` from `SessionArtifactsView` and `ArtifactPreviewModal`), when a publish finishes, and when the popover closes. - **One-click Republish.** The panel receives `republishOnOpen`, fixed at the moment it opens, so a check that lands while it's open can't start a second publish. It republishes to the same `shareId`, except under a credential warning. - **Menu item.** The "…" menu's Publish item still opens to the link with the in-panel Republish button, as before. - **Removed note:** a file whose earlier link was unpublished now gets a new link straight away, so the "This file's link was unpublished…" note no longer appears. - **i18n:** - The trigger uses the existing `artifacts.share.publish` and `artifacts.share.republish` strings. - `artifacts.share.menu` and `artifacts.share.title` are removed. - `artifacts.share.changed` no longer mentions "Share". It is reworded in all 9 locales; the non-English ones were machine-written and are worth a native check. - **Chat:** `ArtifactPathCode` takes an `unlisted` fallback, so a listed artifact renders as a plain link while other paths keep the code chip. A new `InsideArtifactLink` context drops the code styling inside artifact links. **Left alone:** the global unlayered `button { font: inherit }` in `styles.css` overrides Tailwind text-size utilities on every `Button`. Changing it would resize buttons app-wide, so it's out of scope here. ## Testing - `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts` on `ShareArtifactPopover` (31 tests, 3 consecutive green runs), `SessionArtifactsView`, `ArtifactsView`, `ChatMarkdown`, and `i18n`: all pass. - **Publish tests cover:** - one-click publish, with publish called exactly once - the credential case waiting for Publish - no re-publish after Cancel - the extension-less title - the links-left count after publishing - **Republish tests cover:** - the button saying Republish only for a changed file with an active link - the link list not being fetched for an unchanged file - one-click Republish to the same `shareId`, with the label returning to Publish afterwards - the credential warning blocking the auto-republish - no re-republish after Cancel - **Chat test covers:** artifact links rendering without ``. - `npm run typecheck`: no errors in touched files.
