title: fix(sidebar): unpin sessions from offline or unlinked remote hosts
body:
Code changes: +212 -11  
Tests: +44 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Unpinning a session that belongs to another host (the host badge in **Pinned**) now always works, including when that host is asleep, offline, or no longer linked. The row leaves Pinned at once and stays unpinned after a restart; the owning host is told whenever it next answers.

## Why

Pinned lists a remote host's sessions from the copy this computer saved (IndexedDB `ao-remote-chats`) while the host is not connected. Unpin sent `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}/pin` through `clientForHost`, which throws `Host … is not connected` for such a host. The mutation only `console.error`ed it, so clicking unpin (hover icon or context menu) did nothing and the row stayed. The same happens for a host whose saved entry never reconnects (for example, re-linked under a new host id): its pinned sessions were stuck for good.

A row with no visible controls is not a separate bug. The pin/archive buttons only show on `:hover` (styles.css `.group/session-row:hover [data-session-action-buttons]`); a hovered row also reserves room for them, which is why its host badge truncates sooner.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Unpin on a pinned session from an unreachable host: nothing happens, console logs `Failed to unpin session: Host … is not connected` | Row leaves Pinned immediately and stays out after restart; the host gets the DELETE when it next connects |
| Unpin on a reachable remote host while the request fails: row stays, no feedback | Row leaves Pinned; the request is retried (at most once a minute) on later list loads until the host agrees |
| A pinned session's hover unpin button is a crossed-out pin in brighter text | The same plain pin as a pinned project's unpin button |

No screenshots: per the requester's instructions this was not run in the app.

## How

- `stores/remote-unpin-store.ts`: pins removed here for remote sessions, `{hostId, sessionId, at}` keyed by `sessionUiKey`, persisted in `localStorage["ao.sidebar.remote-unpins"]`. `withRemoteUnpins` shows those sessions as unpinned. A pin set later on the other computer (`pinnedAt > at`) wins.
- `useRemoteWorkspaces` and `useRemoteProjectQuery` apply it, so the Pinned section, the row's hover icon, the context menu label, and the board agree.
- `useUnpinSession`: a remote session records the unpin locally and returns; it never throws for an unreachable host. `usePinSession` clears a kept unpin first.
- `lib/remote-session-unpins.ts`: sends the DELETE right away if the host is connected, and otherwise whenever that host's session list loads. A list read after the unpin settles it when the host no longer pins or lists the session (404 counts as done). Unpins for hosts no longer saved are pruned in `_shell` next to `syncRemoteCache`.
- The session row's hover pin button uses the plain `Pin` icon, like pinned project rows (menus already matched).
- "A later pin wins" compares the host's `pinnedAt` with the `pinnedAt` that was removed (both the host's clock), so a host clock running ahead cannot hide an unpin.
- Local and Cloud pins are unchanged. No session is archived or deleted.

## Testing

- Added `stores/remote-unpin-store.test.ts` (override, other-host isolation, later-pin-wins, host pruning).
- Not run locally (tests, typecheck, lint, build, or app). Relying on CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Scoped to session pins for remote hosts
- [ ] Manually verified in the desktop app (not done)

title: fix(usage): keep last limits on refresh failure; drop unused endpoint and pricing generator
body:
Follow-ups to #7148, in three commits.

## Keep the last limits reading when a refresh fails
A failed limits refresh used to blank the bars. Now the last good windows stay on screen next to the error, with their age ("Showing numbers from 12 minutes ago"). If the account's email changes, the old numbers are dropped, so one account's limits never show under another. Session-start limit checks still treat a failed read as a failure.

## Delete `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions/{sessionId}`
Nothing in the app calls it. The Usage page and session cards read the compact list. This removes the route, its DTOs and spec entries, the per-model grouping in the summary reader, the domain summary types, the `GetUsageSessionIncomplete` query, and the `useSessionUsage` hook. `openapi.yaml`, `schema.ts` and sqlc output are regenerated.

## Remove the pricing catalog generator
The daemon already builds its catalog from LiteLLM's live table and caches it under the data dir. This removes:
- `backend/cmd/pricingcatalog`
- the repo-writing half of `catalogsync` (`Sync`, `Validate`, manifest and blob checks)

`build()` now takes only the table. The `catalogsync` tests build in memory and also run the result through the runtime decoder. Tests that read the shipped catalog (`report_test.go`, `codex_write_rate_test.go`) now use small inline tables. The report table keeps the shapes those tests assert: a 2x priority tier, an above-272k row, and Anthropic 1-hour writes.

The pricing workflow keeps one job: download the live table from the same URL the daemon uses, then run it through the fetcher and a throwaway cache.

**Kept for released builds:** `pricing/catalog/v1/` (data only) stays. Stable v0.14.10 fetches its manifest from `main`, and a fresh install has no cache to fall back on. With the generator gone the data stays frozen at the Oct 16 refresh. A follow-up deletes it once a stable release includes #7148.

## Tests
CI is the test gate. Locally: `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `gofmt`, sqlc and spec regeneration.

title: feat(mobile): preview artifacts in the formats the desktop previews
body:
Code changes: +1738 -194\ Tests: +965 -9\ Others: +1332 -76 (package-lock.json +1307 -76) ## What The mobile artifact viewer now previews the formats the desktop previews, and says "Preview not available" for the rest, as the desktop does. - **Video and audio** (mp4, mov, m4v, webm, ogv; mp3, m4a, wav, aac, flac, ogg, opus) play in the platform's own player (`expo-video`). Audio gets its own play/pause, seekable progress bar and times. - **PDFs on Android** render with the platform's `PdfRenderer` (`react-native-pdf-renderer`) after an authenticated download to the cache. iOS keeps its WKWebView. - **CSV / TSV** render as a table with sortable headers and right-aligned numeric columns, behind a **Table / Source** switch. - **Mermaid files** (`.mmd`, `.mermaid`) render as the diagram behind a **Diagram / Source** switch, in the app's light or dark theme; a file Mermaid cannot draw shows its source with "Couldn't draw this diagram." - **Binary files** (known binary extensions, and files over 1 MiB whose first 64 KiB are not text) show "Preview not available · ZIP file · 2.4 MB" instead of opening a blank page. That screen, and a format the phone cannot play, also says where to open the file: "Open it on Studio Mac with “Show in Finder” in the desktop app." It is named as the desktop's artifact menu names it on the machine's platform (Finder, File Explorer, File Manager), or points to the artifact's ⋯ menu when the platform is not known. - `.ico` previews as an image; gallery and filmstrip use the desktop's file-type glyphs. The format lists, the CSV parser and table sorting move to `packages/shared/files/file-formats.ts`; the desktop's `file-media`, `image-files`, `delimited-text`, `TableFileView` and `mermaid-diagram` now re-export or use them, so the two apps can't drift. Desktop behavior is unchanged. ## Why MP4 and audio artifacts never played on either platform. The viewer loaded them in a WebView, which sends the `Authorization` header only with the page load. The video element then re-fetches the file in byte ranges, and since #7077 put `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` on preview files, the page has an opaque origin, so the `SameSite=Lax` `ao_conn` cookie is withheld too. Every range request got a **401** (reproduced in headless Chromium against the same headers; with the sandbox removed the same flow plays). Android PDFs, CSV tables, Mermaid diagrams and a clear "no preview" state were also missing compared with desktop. ## Before / After Same scratch daemon, same artifacts, one native binary; "before" is `main`'s JS on it. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | **iOS · video**: the WebView never loads it
| Native player
| | **Android · video**: broken media placeholder
| Native player with controls
| | **Android · audio**: broken media placeholder
| Play/pause, seekable progress, times
| | **Android · PDF**: "PDFs can't be shown on Android yet"
| Pages rendered natively
| | **iOS · CSV**: raw text
| Sortable table, Table / Source switch
| | **iOS · Mermaid file**: raw source
| Diagram, Diagram / Source switch
| | **Android · 3 MB binary**: blank page, starts a download
| "Preview not available" with type and size
| | **iOS · 3 MB binary**: the WebView spins forever
| "Preview not available", type and size, and where to open it
| Daemon log for the same MP4, before → after: `GET …/demo-recording.mp4 Range: bytes=0-` **401** → **206** for every range request. ## How - **Media:** `artifactStreamSource` builds the existing preview-files URL (`?raw=true`, streams any size, answers ranges) with the Bearer header; `expo-video` sends that header with every request, so the cookie and the sandbox no longer matter. Off-screen pages in the pager pause. iOS cannot play WebM/OGV; that shows "This video can't play on the phone · WEBM file · 80 KB". - **Android PDF:** `downloadArtifact` writes to `cache/artifacts/.part` and moves it into place once complete, keyed by paired machine, session, path and modified time, so an unchanged file opens from cache and a rewritten one downloads again. Once a version is in place, that file's other copies (and stale partial downloads) are deleted, and the folder is capped at 200 MiB, least recently written first, so the cache keeps one copy per file. Names are a 128-bit hash of machine, session and path, plus 64 bits of the version, and a copy the PDF renderer cannot read is deleted so **Try again** downloads it again. - **Mermaid:** the engine (`mermaid@11.17.2`, the desktop's version) runs in an isolated WebView loaded from memory: no origin, CSP `default-src 'none'` with only inline script and style, `securityLevel: "strict"`, link taps open in the system browser. The 3.5 MB engine ships as an **asset**, not in the JS bundle: `metro.config.js` copies it from `node_modules` to a gitignored `assets/generated/mermaid.webjs` on every bundle, and it is read only when a diagram opens. - **Large files:** over 1 MiB, the viewer reads the first 64 KiB with a Range request (`getArtifactHead`) and decides text vs binary before loading anything into a page. - **Daemon and Orchestrator Cloud:** after #8085, the viewers read through `ArtifactsBackend`. `streamSource` is where a native player or download reads a file: the daemon's preview-files URL with the Bearer header, or Cloud's signed address with none. The size probe, binary probe and bounded text read (`size`, `head`, `textWithin`) are optional and only the daemon has them for now, so on Cloud an unlisted table opens as a page, a large text file opens without the binary check, and a PDF's size is checked on the download itself. The daemon backend's `key` is now the machine's host id (`machineIdentity`), which keys the PDF cache by paired machine. - **Native change:** adds `expo-video`, `expo-asset` and `react-native-pdf-renderer`. This moves the runtime fingerprint, so it needs a store build, not an OTA. - Unlisted files a worker report links to (media, PDF, image, binary) now open in the same viewers instead of the WebView. An unlisted table or diagram first gets its real size with a one-byte range request (`Content-Range` gives the total), so a large one still takes the large-file path. ## Testing - `packages/mobile`: `npm run typecheck`; `npx vitest run`: 368 files, 3575 tests pass (new: format classification, format label, cache names, Mermaid page escaping/CSP/messages, media time). - `frontend`: `npm run frontend:typecheck`; `TableFileView`, `FileMediaPreview`, `artifact-file-icon`, `delimited-text`, `mermaid-diagram` tests: 142 pass. - Debug builds on an **iOS 26.5 simulator** and an **Android 35 emulator** against a scratch daemon (isolated data dir) with one artifact per format: played MP4 (both), WebM (Android plays, iOS shows the can't-play state), MP3 (both), Android PDF, CSV sort, Mermaid valid/broken, ZIP, 3 MB binary, 3 MB log, ICO, dark mode. - Mermaid page rendered with the real engine in headless Chrome under its CSP: flowchart and sequence diagrams draw, a parse error reports `failed`, no CSP violations. - `expo-doctor`: only the seven patch-version notices already on `main`. **Includes #8099:** Mermaid fences in chat replies and markdown artifacts were reviewed in #8099 and squash-merged into this branch, so this PR now carries them too. See #8099 for their description and screenshots. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Mobile artifact previews now support audio and video playback, PDFs, sortable CSV/TSV tables, Mermaid diagrams, and expanded image and file-type handling. * Switch between rendered and source views for tables and diagrams. Mermaid diagrams can also render in chat, with a code view available. * Audio playback includes play, pause, and seeking controls; video playback uses native controls. * Tables and diagrams can appear in artifact thumbnails. Large or unsupported files show clearer preview states, and downloaded artifacts can be reused from a local cache.

title: feat(mobile): draw Mermaid fences in chat replies and markdown artifacts
body:
Code changes: +320 -33\ Tests: +242 -1\ Others: +0 -0 ## What A ```mermaid fence now draws as its diagram on mobile, wherever `ChatMarkdown` renders: chat replies, markdown artifacts, version history, reviews and file previews. The desktop draws them in chat and in markdown files; on the phone they were a block of `flowchart TD …` source. ## Before / After Same scratch daemon, same markdown artifact and the same real agent reply; "before" is #8098. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | **iOS · markdown artifact**: fence as code

title: perf(artifacts): mount a card's actions menu when the card is first visited
body:
Part of #7975 (group F, finding 20). Does not close the issue.

## What changes

The Artifacts page mounted every card's actions menu when it opened: two Radix tooltips, the dropdown menu, the share popover anchor, the delete `ConfirmDialog` and three mutation observers, per card. They also re-rendered on every card re-render.

`DeferredArtifactActionsMenu` (in `ArtifactActionsMenu.tsx`) is used for the two Artifacts page call sites, gallery cards and list rows:

- Until the pointer moves over the card (`pointermove` on its `li`) or focus enters it (`focusin`), it draws the closed trigger buttons (pin, open in session, more actions) with the same element types, classes, ARIA attributes and `data-state`/`data-slot` the closed menu gives them.
- It still starts the same queries as the menu (`useShareAvailable`, `useCloudMeUserId`, `useCloudArtifactAccess`). The menu therefore offers the same items (Share, Download, owner-only actions) the first time it opens.
- On first visit it mounts the real `ArtifactActionsMenu` in place and keeps it.
- If focus was on a stand-in, it moves to the matching real button in a layout effect, before paint. The tooltip-on-focus and `:focus-visible` work as before.
- A press that starts on a Pin or Open in session stand-in (a first tap, or a pointer that pressed without moving) keeps that stand-in in place until its click lands, because a browser sends the click only to the pressed button while it is still in the page. The click is then replayed on the real button. A press on the more-actions stand-in mounts the menu right away and replays its `pointerdown`, which is what opens a Radix menu. Scripted `.click()` and `userEvent` presses are replayed the same way.

`pointermove` is used rather than `pointerover` so that wheel-scrolling with the pointer resting over the grid doesn't mount menus for cards that only scroll past.

Other `ArtifactActionsMenu` users (session file tabs, preview modal, session artifacts view) are unchanged.

## Expected effect (reasoning, not measured)

This PR reports no measurements; performance is left for manual measurement. From the code: opening the page no longer mounts, per card, two tooltips, the dropdown menu, the share popover anchor, the delete `ConfirmDialog` and three mutation observers. A card pays for its own menu the first time the pointer moves over it or focus enters it.

## What to check by hand

- **Profile:** open Artifacts with many artifacts (100+) in the React profiler and Performance panel, compared with `main`. Then hover one card, sweep the pointer over a row of cards, and wheel-scroll with the pointer resting over the grid. Scrolling alone should not mount menus.
- **Looks:** at rest, on hover, with a tooltip, with the menu open and with keyboard focus, cards should look identical to `main`.
- **Tooltip timing:** the pin and open-in-session tooltips should appear after the same delay as on `main`, including on the very first hover of a card.
- **Mouse:** the menu lists the same items (Share, Download, owner-only actions for cloud artifacts). Escape returns focus to the trigger.
- **Keyboard:** Tab or Shift+Tab into a card that the pointer hasn't visited. Focus should land on the same button with a focus ring, and the tooltip should appear on focus. Enter opens the menu, and Escape returns focus.
- **First press without hover:** on a card that the pointer hasn't moved over, press Pin, Open in session and More actions. Use a touch screen if one is available; otherwise rest the pointer on the button by scrolling it under the cursor, then click without moving. Each should act on the first press. Also press and drag off the button before releasing: nothing should fire, as on `main`.
- **Delete:** the confirm dialog opens and deletes as before.
- **Other views:** session file tabs, the preview modal and the session artifacts view still use the eager menu and should be unchanged.

## How this composes with the artifact preview cache work

Session agent-orchestrator-77's offscreen WebP snapshot cache (pushed to `ao/artifact-worktree/root`, not merged) for gallery previews, which changes `ArtifactGalleryCard.tsx` and `ArtifactThumbnail.tsx`. This PR does not touch either file; it only changes what goes into the card's `actions` slot. The two changes are independent: the cache cuts thumbnail work, this cuts per-card menu mount work, and they should merge cleanly in either order.

## Audit (code reading, no runs)

Each risk was checked against the code. Two defects turned up, both from review, and both are fixed.

| Risk | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Keyboard: Tab or Shift+Tab to a card, then Enter or Space on the first press | Safe. `focusin` mounts the menu with discrete priority, so the commit lands before the next keydown. Focus moves to the real button in the same layout effect, before paint. |
| Escape and focus restore | Safe. The real Radix menu handles them; the stand-ins never open anything. |
| First press without hover (touch, or a pointer that pressed without moving) | **Fixed** (c23c3ae664, 02b721a070). Pin and Open in session lost the click: the button was swapped before the click arrived. The stand-in now stays until its click lands, then the whole tap (pointerdown, focus, pointerup, click) is replayed on the real button. |
| Tooltip on first hover, same delay | **Fixed** (02b721a070). The move that mounted the menu reached the stand-in, so the tooltip timer never started until the next move. That move is now forwarded to the real trigger, unless the pointer has already left. |
| No tooltip after a tap | **Fixed** (02b721a070). The real trigger now sees the replayed pointerdown before focus lands on it, as it does on `main`. |
| Keyboard focus tooltip | Safe. It opens on focus, as on `main`. |
| Right-click | Safe. These buttons have no context menu. A right press mounts the menu, and its replayed pointerdown (button 2) is ignored by Radix, as on `main`. |
| Delete confirm on first use | Safe. The dialog lives in the real menu, which is mounted by the time a menu item can be chosen. The existing cloud test goes from an untouched card's More actions to Delete, confirm and the delete call. |
| Flash or layout shift | Safe. The stand-ins use the same element types, classes, ARIA and `data-*` attributes. The real menu adds no wrapper DOM (Tooltip and TooltipTrigger `asChild`, DropdownMenu, the share popover anchor), and a closed `ConfirmDialog` renders nothing. |
| Screen-reader labels | Safe. The names, `aria-pressed`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded` are the same. |
| Bulk select and delete (on `main`) | Safe. Cards render no actions while selecting, so the stand-ins never meet the checkbox. Leaving selection mounts fresh stand-ins. |

## Tests

Added in `ArtifactsView.test.tsx`:
- Enter and Space each open an untouched card's menu on the first press, and Escape returns focus to More actions.
- One `pointerMove` onto Pin, with nothing after it, shows the tooltip after the delay.
- A first tap (pointerdown, render, pointerup, click on the still-connected button) pins the artifact and opens no tooltip.

The existing tests press stand-ins through `userEvent`. No assertions changed. Nothing has been run locally; CI is the first run.

## Not verified

- Nothing in this PR has been tested or measured: no app run, no profiling, and no screen-reader or real touch check. The hand checks above are what's needed.
- The replayed pointerdown and pointerup are synthetic events that bubble up to `window`, so window-level listeners see a second copy of a press that already happened. Nothing on this page reacts to them, but this is unconfirmed in the real app.
- Whether Chromium sends its own `pointermove` to the new button under a resting pointer is unknown. If it does, Radix ignores the second move, so the tooltip timer doesn't start twice.

title: perf(chat): wake hibernated chats less often, and faster
body:
Code changes: +32 -16\
Tests: +27 -3\
Others: +15 -10 (generated sqlc)

## What

Three changes that make a hibernated chat wake less often, and wake faster when it has to:

1. **Wake replay lookups use their indexes.** 15 queries in `conversations.sql` that look up a row by provider item, client message, or provider turn id now add `AND <col> <> ''`, so SQLite can use the existing partial unique indexes instead of walking every row of the conversation.
2. **A hidden window no longer re-wakes its chat.** While the window is hidden, `SessionView` skips a chat-view renewal that arrives after the 30 s lease has lapsed, and renews on `visibilitychange` when the window comes back.
3. **Idle timer from 90 s to 10 minutes.** `IdleBeforeHibernate` keeps a quiet provider parked for 10 minutes before idle hibernation may stop it.

## Why

Measured on a real Orchestrator database (204 Claude wakes over 1.9 days, 24 sessions): a wake takes 6.5 s median, 15.3 s p90 from wake start to ready, and people come back to a chat a median 37 minutes after its last activity.

1. The replayed tail is written one event per transaction, and each event first looks up its row. `WHERE conversation_id = ? AND provider_item_id = ?` cannot use the partial index `WHERE provider_item_id <> ''`, so on a big chat every lookup walked the whole conversation while holding the writer.
2. 52 of 256 wakes were the same chat hibernating and waking again within seconds, overnight, with no user turn. Chromium throttles a hidden window's 10 s renewal to exactly 60 s, which equals the 30 s lease plus the 30 s grace: the sweep hibernated the chat, then the late renewal counted as a new view and woke it.
3. With a 90 s timer, any follow-up a few minutes later, from you or from the orchestrator, paid a full cold start.

## Before / After

No user-visible change apart from speed.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Activity lookup, session with 4,475 activities (warm, best of 5) | 12 ms | 0.01 ms |
| Message lookup, same session | 0.87 ms | 0.008 ms |
| Turn lookup, same session | 0.04 ms | 0.008 ms |
| Desktop lab, window hidden 15 min | 3 hibernations, 3 wakes | 1 hibernation, 0 wakes; 1 wake on return |
| Real Claude, follow-up 4 min after leaving the chat (3 runs) | woke every time, first token 4.85-5.63 s | never slept, first token 1.80-1.91 s |
| Wakes a day, replayed against the 10-minute timer | 109 | 86 (21% fewer, 4.3 min less waiting a day) |

Replaying the same wakes against other timers, for the choice of 10 minutes:

| Timer | Wakes avoided | Waiting saved a day | Avg extra awake chats | Peak |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 min | 10% | 2.0 min | 0.11 | 4 |
| **10 min** | **21%** | **4.3 min** | **0.27** | **6** |
| 15 min | 26% | 5.6 min | 0.43 | 7 |
| 30 min | 45% | 8.2 min | 0.81 | 7 |
| 60 min | 61% | 10.5 min | 1.38 | 7 |

Each extra chat kept awake saves 14-18 minutes of waiting a day on the steps up to 10 minutes, and 8 on the step to 15. An awake Claude chat measured 147-678 MB (about 190 MB typical), so 10 minutes costs about 50-90 MB on average and up to ~1.9 GB at the busiest moment.

## How

- **Lookups:** only the SQL strings change; sqlc v1.31.1 regenerated `conversations.sql.go`. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the real database moves all 15 queries to the unique partial index. Every caller was audited for empty ids: each one either guards `''` already, or an empty id used to match an unrelated row (user messages, old promoted turns), so returning no row is the safer result.
- **Hidden window:** a renderer-only change. A visible window renews exactly as before. A hidden window keeps renewing while its lease is live, and stops once a renewal would arrive after the lease lapsed, so a throttled timer can no longer register a "new" view. The chat may then hibernate while hidden, and wakes once on return.
- **Timer:** hibernation still looks only at idle time, not at free memory. On 16 GB machines the timer is the only limit on idle chats, which is why it is 10 minutes and not 30.

## Testing

- New `SessionView` test: a hidden window's on-time renewal still goes out, a renewal after the lease lapses is skipped, and the return renews.
- The hibernation test that back-dated activity by a fixed 6 minutes now back-dates past `IdleBeforeHibernate` itself.
- The version-refresh tests' quiet window (`refreshIdle`) now sits 10 minutes past `IdleBeforeHibernate`: their harness starts sessions idle for exactly that long, so with a 10-minute timer the "not yet quiet" checks would otherwise start already quiet.
- Unit tests run in CI.
- Labs: real-DB query plans and timings (lookups); a dev desktop with an isolated daemon, a 1 s sweep and the same throttling delay applied to before and after (hidden window); before and after daemons running in parallel with real Claude haiku (timer, run on a 30-minute build, and 4 minutes is inside 10 as well).
- Not yet measured: the end-to-end wake time with the lookup change.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: perf(sidebar): stop unrelated sidebar re-renders on route, toggle and scroll
body:
Part of #7975 (group D, left sidebar: findings 5, 11, 12, 18, 19). Does not close it.

## Summary
The shell re-renders several times per route change. Each time it gave the sidebar new inline callbacks, new remote-workspace arrays and a new `SidebarProvider` `onOpenChange`. In `ui/sidebar.tsx`, `setOpen` depends on that handler, `toggleSidebar` on `setOpen`, and the context value on both, so every shell render created a new sidebar context. Every `useSidebar` reader then re-rendered: the app `Sidebar`, the shadcn root, and each `SidebarMenuButton` with its Tooltip, Popper and trigger, including buttons inside memoized `ProjectItem`s.

- `_shell.tsx`: `onOpenChange` is a `useCallback` keyed on the open flag. The sidebar's remote-project handlers are stable (`useCallback`, or `useLatestCallback` for handlers that read route state when they run).
- `Sidebar` and `CommandPalette` are wrapped in `memo`. `CommandPalette` takes no props, so the shell's re-renders no longer reach the closed palette (finding 5).
- `useRemoteWorkspaces` returns the same `data` and host-id lists until something its mapping reads changes: a host's query data, a pending unpin, Developer Mode, the UI language, or an in-flight kill. It used to build new arrays on every render, even with no remote hosts, which would have defeated the `Sidebar` memo.
- `toggleProjectDisclosure` used to depend on the expanded-id state, so each toggle gave all project rows a new `onToggle` and re-rendered all of them. It now keeps its identity and reads the state when called (finding 19). The pinned-row kill handler and `openExistingProject` changed the same way, so route changes no longer re-render pinned rows.
- `SidebarMenuButton` no longer calls `useSidebar`; a small `SidebarMenuButtonTooltipContent` reads it. It renders `TooltipContent` with the same props in the same order, so the DOM is unchanged. Collapse and expand now re-render only that content, not each button and trigger (findings 12 and 18).

Visuals and behavior are unchanged by design. There are no CSS, class, animation, hover-fade, tooltip or preview-card delay changes. The `ProjectItem` comparator and the held session switch from #8013 are untouched.

## Freeze audit (code reading only)
`memo` and stable references can only freeze the UI where a render reads state outside React (`getState()`, module variables, `localStorage`, `Date.now`, the i18n global) that used to be refreshed by the parent's incidental re-renders. A component's own subscriptions (zustand selectors, React Query, router hooks, context, `useTranslation`) still re-render it under `memo`.

**Checked, no change needed**
- `Sidebar.tsx`, every component it renders, and `CommandPalette.tsx`: all `getState()`, `localStorage` and `Date.now` reads are in effects, handlers or `useState` initializers. This covers `requestArchiveOpen` in the project menu (#8092) and in Cmd+K, the sidebar order and pin store, and expanded/section state.
- Dialogs the two components mount (`CreateProjectFlow`, `SessionArchiveDialog`, `ConfirmDialog`), `RemoteHostsSection`, `AwakeControl` and `BuildInfoTooltip`: same result. The preview card's `appI18n` label is under `SessionRow`, which was memoized before this PR.
- Sidebar props from the shell (`workspaces`, `remoteHosts`, remote lists) are immutable: new arrays on change, never mutated in place.
- The handlers converted to `useLatestCallback` (project toggle, pinned-row kill, `openExistingProject`, remote orchestrator and remove) are only called from user events or async completions, never during render or from a child's layout effect. They see the latest state.
- Collapse/expand and ⌘B: the shell's `handleSidebarOpenChange` has the same logic and inputs as the inline handler it replaces. The provider's `keyboardShortcut` is still off, so the shell still owns ⌘B.
- Command palette open/close and its shortcuts: driven by its own `useUiStore` subscription, unaffected by `memo`.
- Remote unpins (#8094): `useRemoteUnpinStore` is subscribed in `useRemoteWorkspaces` and is a memo input.

**Found and fixed** (all in the `useRemoteWorkspaces` memo, which reads three values outside React)
- Developer Mode (terminal titles): fixed earlier in review.
- In-flight kills: `applyOptimisticSessionKills` reads a module `Set`, and a remote kill does not touch the sidebar's remote queries. An archived remote row would have stayed visible until the next poll. The set now notifies subscribers, and the hook subscribes through `useSyncExternalStore`.
- UI language: the remote Scratchpad's name comes from `appI18n.t`. It would have kept the old language until host data changed. The language is now a memo input.

**Nothing was split out or dropped.**

## Regression tests (written, not run; CI runs them)
- `Sidebar.test.tsx`, "Memoized Sidebar with unchanged props": rendered once with props that keep their identity, then only the real store changes.
  - project pin and unpin through `useSidebarOrderStore`;
  - project expansion from `useSessionImportStore`;
  - consecutive disclosure toggles that each see the previous state;
  - the archive entry's count following new `workspaces`, and it writing `archiveOpenRequest` to the real ui store;
  - a remote pinned row going through the real `useRemoteWorkspaces`, which disappears on an offline unpin, comes back when the unpin clears, and disappears while a kill is in flight.
- `useWorkspaceQuery.remote.test.tsx`: with unchanged cached host data, the lists follow a remote unpin, an in-flight kill and a language change. Developer Mode and identity-stability tests were already there.
- Route changes are tested through the mocked router hooks, which now subscribe like the real ones. No test drives the real TanStack router; check that by hand (item 1).

## Measurement
Earlier in this task, under the original brief, I measured render counts and timing on a headless production build. At the user's request, those numbers are not part of this PR; the user will measure by hand. Nothing in this description is a measured result.

## What to check by hand
Use a production build with many projects (about 20), a few pinned sessions and several expanded projects. React DevTools Profiler with "Highlight updates" makes the changes visible.
1. **Route change:** click sessions in different projects, and use back/forward. The sidebar's active row and the open project must follow every time. Only the old and new active project rows and the `Sidebar` itself should re-render, and the closed Command palette should not re-render from the shell. Switching should look and feel as before.
2. **Project toggle:** open and close several projects in a row. Only the toggled `ProjectItem` should re-render. The expand animation is unchanged, and the open set survives a restart.
3. **Sidebar scroll:** scroll the project list with the pointer over it. Row tooltips should no longer re-render while scrolling.
4. **Collapse and expand (⌘B or the titlebar toggle):** the slide and its timing should be unchanged, and the commit at the start of the slide should be smaller. Row tooltips should still be hidden while expanded and behave as before when collapsed.
5. **Row hover:** the 100 ms fade, the preview-card delay and the safe-triangle aim to the card should all be unchanged.
6. **Pins:** pin and unpin a project from its menu, and pin and unpin sessions. The sidebar should update at once. Archive the active pinned session: navigation should still go to the next session or to the project.
7. **Project menu Archive (#8092):** archive a session, then open the project's ⋮ or right-click menu. "Archive" shows the new count and opens that project's archive.
8. **Remote hosts:** with a host offline, unpin one of its pinned sessions; the row leaves Pinned at once. With the host online, archive a remote session; the row should leave at once, not at the next poll. Retry, remove, configure and open orchestrator should behave as before.
9. **Settings changes while the sidebar stays put:** switch the app language with a remote Scratchpad listed (its name changes), and toggle Developer Mode (remote session titles and the Usage row change).
10. **Cloud and Scratchpad rows:** they should update as sessions start, finish and are archived.

## Not done
- **Row hover (finding 11):** a hover with no card triggers no React state change. The commits around showing a card are one row render that passes `open` to the HoverCard, plus Radix HoverCard internals. Cutting more would mean restructuring the row and HoverCard boundary, so I left it.
- **Remote-host projects** still get a fresh scoped selection and handlers on each `Sidebar` render. I left this unchanged.
- Collapse still re-renders the `Sidebar` body once. This is required, because tab order and labels depend on collapsed state.
- No tests, typecheck, lint or builds were run locally; CI runs them.

title: perf(chat): redraw only the turns a send or steer changes
body:
Part of #7975 (group C, finding 8: refresh burst after send/steer). Does not close the issue.

## What changed

The work is cut per commit; the number of commits stays the same, so nothing on screen changes and nothing arrives later.

- **Timeline turns** (`ChatWorkspace.tsx`): every `TurnGroup` got the timeline-wide `busy`, `editBusy` and `newHumanMessageIds`. Those values change on send/steer, so every memoized turn re-rendered on each commit. Each turn now gets a value only where it reads it, and a fixed value otherwise:
  - `newHumanMessageIds`: only a turn that holds one of the new ids. It is read only as `.has(itemKey(item))` for a human message's entrance.
  - `editBusy`: only the turn holding the message being edited. It is read only in `HumanMessage`'s editing branch.
  - `busy`: only a turn with an approval card. `ApprovalCard` is its only reader inside a turn.
- **Inline artifact paths** (`ChatMarkdown.tsx`): `ArtifactPathCode` reads the workspace list, so every workspace refetch (any session's status) re-rendered each path's `ChatPathMenu` / context-menu tree. It now returns the same element unless `href`, `path` or `children` change.

## Expected effect (reasoning, not measured)

This PR reports no measurements; performance is left for manual measurement. From the code: on a send or steer, only the turns that read the changed values re-render. Those are the turn with the new human message, the turn being edited and turns with an approval card, plus every rollbackable turn while `rollbackDisabled` flips (see below). All other memoized turns keep their render. Inline file paths in messages no longer re-render their context-menu tree on every workspace refresh.

## Why commits were not merged

Reading the send/steer path:
- The `onMutate` and `onSuccess` cache writes already land in single commits.
- Repeat conversation fetches after a send return structurally shared data, so they render nothing new.
- The remaining commits are spaced by network/SSE latency (the user message echo, the status flip, the first agent frame). Merging them would mean holding back content the user is waiting for.

So this PR makes each commit cheaper instead. The steer echo from #8063 is untouched.

## Left out on purpose

- **`rollbackDisabled`** flips on send and re-renders every rollbackable turn. The flip is visible (the rollback control disables), so each of those turns does need the new value. Narrowing it further means restructuring how that state reaches turns; that belongs in a separate change.
- **SessionView cascade.** SessionChatSurface reports its work state up, and SessionView re-renders and passes 11 new callback/element props back down, which renders the chat a second time. Fixing it needs all 11 stabilised, and `interfaceSwitch` legitimately changes on that update anyway. Worth a follow-up; not done here, to keep the instant session switch from #7988/#8013 untouched.
- **Sidebar re-render** on workspace refetch is group D (#8102).

## Audit (code reading, no runs)

**Narrowing is exact, not approximate.** For every item a turn draws, the narrowed value equals the full one:
- `newHumanMessageIds` is read only as `.has(itemKey(item))` by `TimelineItem`, for items taken from `group.items`. The narrowed set is the full set whenever any item in the turn has a key in it. Otherwise none of the turn's items is in the full set, so the empty set gives the same answer.
- `editBusy` is read only by `HumanMessage` inside its `editing` branch. `editing` is `item.turnId === messageEdit.turnId`, and `turnEditing` checks the same thing on `group.items`.
- `busy` is read only by `ApprovalCard`, for approval activities in `group.items`.
- Batched reports carried under a turn render as `WorkerUpdateRows`, which read none of the three. The standalone edit bubble (an edit whose message isn't in the timeline) still gets the full flags.

**The listed scenarios** all reduce to that per-render equality, because the helpers are pure functions of the turn and the flags and keep no state:
- concurrent turns, turn id reuse and reconnect catch-up;
- steer reconcile by `clientMessageId` (#8063): `itemKey` uses `clientMessageId` on both sides;
- cloud, remote and side chats, history replay, and the held-session switch (#8013).

**Other timeline content doesn't read these props.** Streamed assistant text, tool rows, the live status row, queued state, rollback, retry, failure and outcome cards, and compaction markers redraw from their own props (`group.items`, `queued`, `rollbackDisabled`, `outcome`). This PR doesn't change any of those.

**`ArtifactPathCode`:** the memo's deps (`href`, `path`, `children`) cover every input of the returned element. Context reads inside `MarkdownLink` and `ChatPathMenu` still update through a memoized element.

No defect found; no code change from the audit.

**Tests added** (not run; CI is the first run):
- `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: the entrance moves to the newest human message send after send, and the previous turn drops it.
- `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: an open edit of an earlier turn disables Send and shows "Stop the current turn before branching" when `newWorkDisabled` flips, then re-enables.
- `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx`: an inline artifact path, given the same children, links when a refresh lists the artifact and unlinks when it goes.

## What to check by hand

- **Profile:** in a long conversation, record a send and a steer in the React profiler compared with `main`. Older turns should no longer show as rendered, except rollbackable turns while the rollback control toggles.
- **Send:** the new message appears with its usual entrance animation, at the same moment as on `main`. Agent output streams in as before.
- **Steer:** the steer message appears straight away, as with #8063.
- **Approvals:** while a request is in flight, the approve/deny buttons disable and re-enable as before.
- **Inline edit:** edit an earlier message while the agent is working. The edit's send button is disabled exactly as before, and other turns are unaffected.
- **File paths in messages:** artifact paths still open as links. Right-clicking a path still shows the path menu, including after other sessions change status.
- **Rollback:** the rollback control disables during a send as before.
- Also check remote-host and cloud chats.

## Not verified

- Nothing in this PR has been tested or measured: no app run, no profiling, and no unit tests, typecheck or lint locally. CI is the first run.
- By reading only, the existing `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx` `ArtifactPathCode` test is unaffected.
- No visual or timing change is intended: same DOM, and the same entrance-animation trigger (the new message's turn still gets the ids).

title: perf(browser): skip Browser panel renders from unrelated state
body:
Part of #7975 (group G: Browser inspector, findings 13 and 14). Does not close it.

## What this PR is worth
**This PR only reduces Browser panel re-renders.** It does not touch the Browser-tab open (finding 13). Reading the code, the open's cost is mostly not `BrowserPanelView` (see the diagnosis below). Expect fewer panel re-renders while switching sessions and on other `SessionView` updates with Browser open, not a faster open. Whether that is worth merging is for your profile to decide. The change is small and has no visual effect.

## What changed
- `useBrowserView` now returns the same object until one of its fields changes. Before, it built a new object with new inline callbacks (`goBack`, `goForward`, `reload`, `stop`, the devtools actions) on every render. Those callbacks are now `useCallback`s that read the live view id through `viewIdRef`, the same as before.
- `useBrowserAnnotationQueue` does the same.
- `SessionInspector`'s `BrowserView` passes a stable `onTogglePopOut` that still calls the latest prop.
- `BrowserPanelView` is wrapped in `memo`.

Nothing the panel renders, and no effect or IPC call, was changed.

## Measurement status
**Numbers in this PR are not measured results.** At the user's instruction, this PR carries no measured numbers, and the user will measure everything by hand. An early dev-build profiling pass was done in this session before that instruction arrived. Its figures are deliberately left out and should not be cited. The diagnosis below is a hypothesis to confirm with your own profile.

## Diagnosis (hypothesis from reading the code)
**Finding 14, re-renders.** Before this PR, every `SessionView` or `SessionInspector` render handed the panel a fresh model object and a fresh `onTogglePopOut`. The panel wasn't memoized, so it re-rendered its whole toolbar (every tooltip) and every sortable tab each time. After this PR it should render only when browser state, the session object, `active`/`poppedOut` or the topbar host changes. During a switch, real state changes still render it several times: the switch itself, the main process's tabs and devtools pushes, and the lookups after `ensure`.

**Finding 13, the 256 ms open.** It is probably not `BrowserPanelView`. Opening Browser:
1. Switches the rail to the wider Browser width profile (`useResizable` reads `split.clientWidth` and writes the width variable in a layout effect), so the chat column reflows. The wider rail is intended design.
2. Mounts the whole toolbar: Radix tooltips, menus and the sortable tab strip. `useTabScrollEdges` then reads `scrollWidth`, forcing another layout.
3. Starts `useBrowserView`'s per-frame bounds loop. TanStack Router's scroll-restoration listener reads `scrollTop` on scroll events.
4. Re-renders `SessionView`, so the chat `Timeline` re-renders (group A).

Fixing the open would mean reordering layout reads and writes in shared rail and tab-strip code. That needs a profile first to stay pixel-identical, so it is not in this PR.

## Audit: stale state and stale closures (code reading)
Checked, with no defect found:
- **Values that should be live:**
  - No effect or memo anywhere depends on the whole `browserView` or `annotationQueue` object.
  - No panel effect depends on the callbacks that used to be inline.
  - Every panel effect has a dependency array. So do the panel's own hooks (`useDocumentFlag`, `useTabScrollEdges`).
  - During render the panel reads only props, self-subscribing hooks (`useUiStore`, `useBrowserRuntimeState` via `useSyncExternalStore`, `useBrowserDownloads`, i18n, reduced motion) and the constant `window.ao?.browser`. Refs are read only in effects and handlers.
- **Model fields:**
  - Every field gets the same value as before, including the cached view's state during the intervening switch render.
  - The memo depends on every field.
  - The `nativeViewBySession` cache read stays outside the memo, so a cache change is picked up on the next render as before.
- **Callbacks:**
  - The new `useCallback`s read the current view through `viewIdRef`, so none captures an old view id.
  - Queue callbacks were already `useCallback`s over refs.
  - `togglePopOut` depends on `onTogglePopOut`.
- **Pop-out and pop-in:** the inspector's placeholder is outside the panel. The maximized overlay in `SessionView` passes the same stable objects plus `handleToggleBrowserPopOut` (a `useCallback`). A `topbarHost` change is a prop change, so the address bar still moves to the top bar on the next render (#7861's 36 px jump fix).
- **Native view bounds, occlusion, overlay and the #7861 flash/jump fixes:** all of these run in `useBrowserView` (slot callback ref, layout effects keyed on the session, bounds loop), not in panel renders. `slotRef` identity is unchanged.
- **Auto-open rules:** `SessionView`'s effects read the same `agentBrowserActive`/`agentBrowserActivity`/`viewId` values as before. No auto-open is driven by panel renders.
- **Theme, light/dark and translucency:** handled by CSS. Annotation reads theme colors at call time.
- **Remote and cloud:** `origin`/`cloudAgentBrowser` change `navigate`/`openLink` etc., which changes the model. `session.hostId` arrives through the `session` prop.
- **Tests that mutate shared mock state:** `BrowserPanel.test.tsx`'s mocked hook returns a fresh object per call, so those tests still re-render the panel.

## Tests (written, not run; CI runs them)
- `BrowserPanel.live-state.test.tsx` drives the real hook, the real annotation queue and the real memoized panel. Between steps, the parent also re-renders for an unrelated reason. It proves the panel still shows:
  - pushed URL, loading (Stop/Reload) and back state;
  - tab list changes, active tab, title and favicon;
  - a session switch, while pushes from the departed view are ignored;
  - the latest `onTogglePopOut` on Maximize;
  - annotation mode and queue status (Annotate → Cancel annotation) and pushed annotation counts.
- `useBrowserView.test.tsx` checks that the model is the same object across a parent render with no state change, changes on a session switch, and keeps stable callbacks.

## What to check by hand
1. **Look and behavior:**
   - Open Browser on a session with several tabs.
   - Switch sessions with Browser open; there should be no flash, jump or blank page.
   - Maximize and return to the panel.
   - Add, close, reopen and drag-reorder tabs.
   - Watch tab titles, favicons and loading while pages load.
   - Use back/forward/reload, find-in-page, devtools, annotate (pick, send), and the profile picker.
   - Try light and dark themes and the translucent window.
   - Confirm Browser never auto-opens from reply text.
2. **Profile (React DevTools Profiler, "record why each component rendered"),** with 8–10 sessions and several Browser tabs each, against `main`:
   - Switch sessions with Browser visible. `BrowserPanelView` should render only when its props change.
   - Idle with Browser open; there should be no panel renders.
   - Summary → Browser in the Performance panel: check whether the long task is layout (rail width, tab-strip measure, router `onScroll`) or tooltip mounting. That confirms or refutes the finding 13 hypothesis.

## Not verified
Remote-host and cloud sessions with a live agent browser, a streaming agent with Browser open, Windows, and production builds.

title: perf(windows): replace per-ConPTY-terminal wait goroutine with a shared monitor
body:
## Summary

Every Windows ConPTY terminal spawns one dedicated goroutine whose sole job is to block on `cmd.Wait()` until the process exits, then close `doneC`. With many open terminals, that's one idle goroutine per terminal doing nothing but waiting. On Windows this is a meaningful tax: higher syscall/scheduler overhead than Linux, more process-handle tracking, and no sharing across terminals.

## The exact code path

1. **`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/host_conpty_windows.go:newConPTY()`** creates a ConPTY session and unconditionally spawns a waiter goroutine (line 67):

```go
go c.wait()
```

2. **`host_conpty_windows.go:wait()`** (lines 71–88) does nothing but block:

```go
func (c *conptyConn) wait() {
	_ = c.cmd.Wait()          // blocks until the Windows process exits
	code := 0
	if c.cmd.ProcessState != nil {
		code = c.cmd.ProcessState.ExitCode()
	}
	c.exitMu.Lock()
	c.exitCode = code
	c.exited = true
	c.exitMu.Unlock()
	c.doneOnce.Do(func() { close(c.doneC) })
	c.closeConsole()
}
```

3. **`host.go:pumpPTY()`** (line 272) is the consumer:

```go
<-h.cfg.PTY.Done()  // waits for the process to exit before broadcasting status
```

So the goroutine's entire purpose is to signal process exit via `doneC`. It is spawned per terminal and lives for the lifetime of that terminal.

## Scope

This pattern exists on all three platforms:
- Windows: `host_conpty_windows.go:67` ← **priority target**
- macOS: `host_conpty_darwin.go:52`
- Linux: `host_conpty_linux.go:73`

Windows is the priority because process creation, teardown, and syscall overhead are higher than on Linux, and developers running many concurrent Windows terminals feel the baseline overhead most acutely.

## What has already been done (and why it's not enough)

Prior ConPTY/terminal work addressed read-loop blocking and surface rendering, not goroutine count:

| Commit | PR | What it fixed | What remains |
|--------|-----|---------------|--------------|
| `aa94885e2a` | — | Stopped the pty-host from throttling programs on heavy output | Per-terminal `go c.wait()` still spawns |
| `ca9a083036` | #6232 | Added `asyncSurface` with its own goroutine per host process | One goroutine per terminal still waits on `cmd.Wait()` |

No shared process-wait monitor exists. No `WaitForMultipleObjects` usage. No integration with the existing 5s reaper loop (`internal/observe/reaper`) for ConPTY PID tracking.

## The fix

Replace `go c.wait()` with a **shared process-wait monitor**:

**Option A (Windows-native, recommended):** One goroutine per daemon using `WaitForMultipleObjects` via `golang.org/x/sys/windows` on all tracked process handles. When a handle is signaled, close that terminal's `doneC`. Most efficient on Windows.

**Option B (simpler, cross-platform):** Register each ConPTY PID with the existing 5s reaper loop (`internal/observe/reaper`). When the reaper detects the process is dead, signal `doneC`. Adds ~5s detection latency but reuses existing infrastructure.

`Done()`, `ExitCode()`, `PID()`, `Close()` all keep identical signatures. Callers in `host.go` (`pumpPTY`, `shutdown`, status handling in `handleClientMsg`) need no changes.

**Files to touch:**
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/host_conpty_windows.go` — remove `go c.wait()`, register PID with shared monitor
- New or existing shared monitor in `conpty` package or `processalive`

## Why this matters (the argument)

- **User-visible:** Each idle `wait()` goroutine holds a stack (2 KB initial), a process handle, and scheduler entries. With 10–20 terminals open that's 10–20 goroutines doing nothing. On Windows, baseline memory and scheduling overhead is higher than Linux, so session startup and teardown feel heavier than they should.
- **Scaling:** The cost is linear in terminal count. A developer with many sessions across projects pays the tax continuously, even when terminals are idle.
- **Correctness risk (mitigated):** The existing code uses `sync.Once` for `doneC` closure (`doneOnce`), so a shared monitor must preserve the "close exactly once" guarantee. `Close()` already calls `disposeOnce` and best-effort `cmd.Process.Kill()`, so the transition is safe.

## Estimated impact

Fewer goroutines, lower baseline memory and scheduler overhead on Windows with many sessions. Faster session teardown. No change to correctness or API surface.

---

**Definition of done:**
- [ ] `go c.wait()` removed from `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/host_conpty_windows.go`
- [ ] Shared process-wait monitor added (Windows-native via `WaitForMultipleObjects` or reaper integration)
- [ ] `conptyConn.Done()` still signals exactly once via `sync.Once`
- [ ] `go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/...` passes
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/...` passes
- [ ] Manual verification: spawn multiple Windows terminals, confirm `doneC` fires on exit and no goroutine leak

title: perf(terminal): pool base64 encode buffers to reduce GC churn under heavy PTY output
body:
## Summary

Streaming a heavy command (`npm install`, `cargo build`, `go test -v`, `seq 1 100000`) makes the daemon allocate and copy every PTY output byte several times before it reaches the renderer. Previous work reduced the *number* of frames; the per-frame allocation and copying cost is still there. This issue tracks removing it, with the wire format unchanged.

## Current code path (verified on `main`)

1. **`backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go:195-208`** — `copyOut` reuses one 32 KiB read buffer but allocates a fresh chunk per read:
   ```go
   buf := make([]byte, 32*1024)
   n, err := p.Read(buf)
   chunk := make([]byte, n)
   copy(chunk, buf[:n])   // copy #1: caller now owns chunk
   a.onData(chunk)
   ```
2. **`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:565-590`** — `outQueue.push` merges consecutive output for the same terminal into one frame, bounded by `maxMergedData = 256 << 10`; on the non-merge path it copies again:
   ```go
   msg.raw = append([]byte(nil), msg.raw...)   // copy #2 of the same bytes
   ```
3. **`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:604-620`** — `outQueue.drain` base64-encodes each drained frame:
   ```go
   frames[i].Data = base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(frames[i].raw)
   ```
4. **`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:637-681`** — `writeLoop` calls `c.conn.WriteJSON(ctx, msg)`, implemented as `wsjson.Write` in `backend/internal/httpd/terminal_mux.go:55`.

## Allocation cost per data frame

Measured against Go 1.27.1 and `github.com/coder/websocket v1.8.14`:

| Step | Allocation |
| --- | --- |
| `copyOut` chunk | `n` bytes |
| `push` copy | `n` bytes — **redundant on this path**, the chunk is already owned |
| merge `append` | amortized growth, up to 256 KiB |
| `EncodeToString` | `make([]byte, encodedLen)` **plus** a `string` copy of `encodedLen`, where `encodedLen = 4*ceil(n/3)` |
| `wsjson.Write` | **not** a full `json.Marshal`: it streams through `json.Encoder` straight into `c.Write(ctx, MessageText, p)`, and `encoding/json` pools its `encodeState` |

Correction to an earlier draft of this issue: the JSON step is *not* a third large allocation. The avoidable cost is the double copy of the payload plus the two base64 allocations.

## Fix

Three independent, additive changes; each is safe on its own.

1. **Drop the redundant copy in `push`** for callers that already own their bytes (`copyOut` does). Either document that `serverMsg.raw` transfers ownership and remove the copy, or let `copyOut` hand over its chunk. Saves one full payload copy per read.
2. **Pool the base64 scratch buffer** — borrow a `[]byte`, `base64.AppendEncode` into it, build the string, return it. Removes the `make([]byte, encodedLen)`; the `string` copy remains.
3. **Optional larger win:** build the whole data frame in one pooled buffer with `base64.AppendEncode` and write it with a new `WriteMessage(ctx, []byte)` method on the `wsConn` seam (`manager.go:27-32`, implemented as `a.c.Write(ctx, websocket.MessageText, p)` in `terminal_mux.go:52`). That skips both the base64 `string` and the encoder copy. Keep `WriteJSON` for every other frame type.

The wire format is identical in all three cases: same JSON object, same base64 `Data`. No client, protocol, or migration change.

**Files:** `backend/internal/terminal/manager.go`; for option 3 also `backend/internal/httpd/terminal_mux.go` and the `wsConn` fake in the tests.

## Prior work (complementary, not this fix)

| Commit | What it changed | What remains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `65748f32b5` | Merged consecutive PTY chunks so base64 runs once per merged frame | Each merged frame still encodes and copies |
| `b06a3a4058` | 4 ms burst pacing: ~2,900 messages to ~23 for `seq 1 100000` | Each of those frames still pays the cost above |
| `ca9a083036` (#6232) | Moved VT emulation off the PTY read loop (`asyncSurface`) | Unrelated to encoding |
| `7a142e5658` (#6465) | WebGL context pool, batched frames, faster terminal open | Renderer side only |

There is exactly one `sync.Pool` in the backend today (`previewGzipWriters`, `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:604`), so pooling here is consistent with existing practice rather than new machinery.

## Why it matters

Allocation and copy cost scales with output volume times open panes. It lands as GC work in the daemon and as decode work in the renderer, and it is the part that remains after the frame-count work: fewer, larger frames still carry every byte through two copies and two base64 allocations. Option 1 alone removes a full copy of every PTY byte.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `push` no longer copies payload bytes it already owns (ownership documented)
- [ ] base64 encoding reuses a pooled buffer
- [ ] optionally, data frames are written from a pooled buffer via `WriteMessage`
- [ ] `go test ./internal/terminal/...` passes, including `outqueue_test.go`'s base64 assertions
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/terminal/...` passes
- [ ] `go test ./internal/httpd/...` passes
- [ ] a benchmark (`BenchmarkOutQueueDrain` or similar) records allocations/op before and after

title: fix(chat): load just-sent attachment tiles in packaged builds
body: ## Problem On the packaged nightly (0.14.11-nightly.202611101246), a just-sent image tile shows only its alt text ("Image 1") and never loads. This is a regression from #8063. ## Root cause (confirmed by reading the code) #8063 draws just-sent tiles from an object URL (`blob:`). The renderer CSP in `frontend/vite.renderer.config.ts` had no `blob:` in `img-src`, `media-src` or `connect-src`, so the packaged app blocked: - **Images and inline chips:** the `` errors and `ChatImage` falls back to its alt text, which matches the screenshot. - **Video first frames:** blocked by `media-src`. - **PDF first pages and text previews:** their `fetch(blob:)` is blocked by `connect-src`. - **Cloud image and PDF tiles:** blocked the same way. The dev app doesn't apply any CSP. `injectCspMeta` is `apply: "build"`, so the comment claiming the dev and packaged policies match was wrong. That's why the earlier dev-app check passed. A key mismatch would have fallen back to the daemon URL, which works, so the alt-text tile shows the `blob:` URL was used and refused. ## Fix 1. **CSP:** add `blob:` to `img-src`, `media-src` and `connect-src`, with a comment saying why. No other directive changes and no new network origins: only the renderer's own scripts can create a `blob:` URL. This also fixes copying a non-PNG chat image, which re-encodes it through an object URL. The dev-parity comment now says dev runs without a CSP. 2. **Fallback:** `useSentAttachmentPreview` now returns `{ url, onError }`. If the local copy fails to load, the tile switches to the daemon's copy (or, for cloud tiles, the control plane's) once. The switch is keyed on the failed URL, so it can't loop. `ChatImage` sets its own failed state and calls the caller in the same event, so React applies both in one render and the alt text doesn't flash. `AttachmentFilePreview` now keys its failed state on the URL, so the replacement gets its own attempt. The cloud PDF `load` reads the control plane's copy if fetching the local copy throws. 3. **Revoke race:** if a URL is revoked after a tile's render reads it but before its effect holds it (retired with no other holder, or StrictMode's re-run of the effect), the hold now fails and the tile falls back instead of keeping a dead URL. A tile that gave up its local copy also releases its hold, so the URL can be revoked. Tiles look the same as before: the fallback only changes which URL they load. ## Tests (written, not run locally) - `vite.renderer.config.test.ts`: `blob:` in `img-src`, `media-src` and `connect-src`; exact `img-src` and `media-src` strings. - `sent-attachment-previews.test.ts`: failure hands the tile over once; a failed tile releases its hold; a URL revoked between render and hold is dropped. - `ChatImage.test.tsx`: the replacement source draws with no alt text in between; alt text shows only when the replacement also fails, and the local-failure callback runs once. - `StagedAttachmentItems.test.tsx` (new): an image tile falls back to the daemon URL; a text preview reads `?raw=true` from the daemon when the `blob:` fetch fails. - `CloudMessageAttachments.test.tsx`: a cloud image reads the control plane after the local copy fails; a cloud PDF `load` falls back when `fetch(blob:)` throws. ## Manual check (packaged build only; dev never applies the CSP) Send each of these and check the tile shows right away and stays: an image (tile, plus the inline chip in the text), a video (first frame), a PDF (first page), a text file (first lines), a steered message with an image, a queued message with an image, the first message from /new with an image, and a cloud session image and PDF. Also: Copy image on a JPEG in chat now works. ## Risks - `blob:` is now allowed for images, media and fetches. Only the renderer's own scripts can create those URLs, so this adds no network access. - Dev still runs without a CSP. Applying it in dev is a separate change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(onboarding): import earlier chats as a first-run step, not on Home
body:
## Summary

The "Bring your earlier chats into Orchestrator" card (#6364) sat on Home under the Get started actions and looked out of place. As agreed with Dhruv in chat, importing is a one-time step for a new user, so it is now a step in first-run onboarding.

- **Onboarding:** a new optional **Import earlier chats** step sits between the welcome screen and "Let's set up your first project".
  - It opens as a short summary, not the full list. The header says the step is optional and can be done later in Settings, and a small card shows the agent logos and "Found N chats from Claude Code, Codex… on this computer."
  - **Skip** goes on to project setup. **Choose folders** expands the step into the folder list (the same picker as the folder import dialog, suggested folders checked), and Back collapses it again. Nothing opens on top of onboarding.
  - Back from project setup returns to the import step.
  - A finished import ends the first-run prompt, since each imported folder is now a project.
  - The step only shows when an agent with importable chats is installed and the scan of this computer found chats. Otherwise Get started goes straight to project setup. The scan starts on the welcome screen. If it is still running when Get started is clicked, the step shows "Reading local histories…". If the scan then finds nothing or fails, the step moves on to project setup by itself.
- **Home:** the offer card is removed. So is the `sessionImportOfferClosed` flag (`ao.sessionImport.offerClosed`), which only that card read.
- **Still available elsewhere:** Settings → Agents → import, and the per-project offer on the project board (unchanged).
- **Code:** the folder picker in `SessionImportDialog` is now an exported `FolderImport` (header, cancel label and callbacks passed in). The dialog's own folder view wraps it with no change.
- **Telemetry:**
  - The prompt action gains `import`.
  - Imports from the step report source `onboarding`.
  - `ao.session_imports.offer_shown` reports surface `onboarding` instead of `home`.
- **Copy:**
  - New `firstRun.skip`, `firstRun.importDescription`, `firstRun.importFound` (plural) and `firstRun.importChoose` in all 9 locales.
  - The step reuses `sessionImport.offerTitle` ("Import earlier chats") and `foldersDescription`.
  - The now-unused `offerDescription`, `offerDismiss` and `offerChooseFolders` strings are removed.

Earlier versions of this PR (a corner notice, then a tile on the project step) were replaced in this branch.

## Tests

No tests, typecheck or builds were run locally; changes are tested by hand. Updated by reading:
- `CloneRepositoryDialog.test`:
  - The import step shows after Get started when an agent is installed and chats were found. It opens as a summary, and Choose folders expands the list while Back collapses it.
  - Skip and Back move between it and project setup.
  - The step is skipped with no installed agent, and skipped when the scan found nothing.
- `CreateProjectFlow.test`: a finished import reports the `import` action and closes the first-run prompt.
- `telemetry.test`: the new action and surface.
- `ProjectImportOffer.test` and `SessionImportPanel.test`: dropped assertions on the removed flag.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Only users in the first-run experiment's `prompt` variant see onboarding. Users in the control variant now find import only in Settings → Agents and on the project board.
- If the agent check (not the scan) is still loading when Get started is clicked, the import step is skipped for that run.

title: fix(updater): show notes for the selected stable release
body:
Code changes: +60 -11  
Tests: +153 -11  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Stable updates now show release notes from the exact release being downloaded. If those notes cannot be verified, AO omits them while keeping the update available.

## Why

GitHub's Atom feed contains only ten releases. When ten nightlies displace the stable release, electron-updater still selects the correct stable download but silently uses the newest nightly's notes. The reported screenshot matches that situation. No existing open fix was found; #8020 changes the sidebar presentation rather than release-note selection.

## Before / After

The regression fixture exercises the real GitHub provider against a simulated feed containing ten nightlies and no stable entry.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Stable `v0.14.10` download carries `Changes in this nightly` from the newest feed entry. | The same stable download carries the body fetched from `/releases/tags/v0.14.10`. |
| Missing stable notes can display another build's changelog. | API failures, rate limits, malformed responses, and mismatched tags produce no notes. |

## How

Use electron-updater's custom-provider extension to subclass its GitHub provider for Stable. Keep its existing version selection, manifest parsing, file URLs, and download behavior. Replace only `releaseNotes` using an exact-tag lookup, validating the tag and stable, published release flags. The optional request has a five-second timeout.

Configure the provider synchronously to preserve background-check event ordering. Switching to Nightly or a pinned preview restores the standard provider and existing prerelease discovery.

## Testing

Review found and fixed a stale cross-channel cache: selecting unpinned Stable now clears prior direct-feed notes and offers. Regression coverage switches from an unstaged Nightly offer to Stable with no verified notes, then checks the background no-update path. GitHub CI passed on corrected head `71f1843fb1`: typecheck, both unit-test shards, both renderer smoke shards, boundary checks, browser integration, secret scan, and `ci-ok`. No additional local checks ran.

- Before the review correction: 265 focused updater/provider tests passed under Node 24, including a control that reproduces the dependency bug and the same fixture passing with the fix.
- Passed: simulated macOS, Linux, and Windows providers preserve all download metadata and resolved URLs.
- Passed: manual/background Stable configuration, switches to Nightly and preview, failed lookups, and stale-note rejection.
- Passed: frontend and E2E type checks, renderer production build, main-process bundle, real Electron browser integration, 19 native build-script tests, and public-boundary check.
- Broader frontend/backend runs were stopped at the user's request to avoid further local checks. Before stopping, runs encountered an artifact-search focus failure and tmux integration failures outside the changed files. Those failures were not fully diagnosed.
- Full local workflow validation was unavailable: Docker is not running and `agent-ci run --all` requires `VITE_AO_TEAMS` and `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`. Linux/container and remaining CI validation must run on GitHub. No publishing or deployment was performed.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After includes observable provider output
- [x] Regression tests cover the reported scenario and failure paths
- [x] All relevant CI checks pass

title: feat(session): fork a session into a new session at any turn
body:
## Summary

Session forks: copy a session, as one of its turns left it, into a new session that can try a different direction while the original carries on untouched.

**Stacked on #7585** (per-turn file snapshots). This PR targets that branch so the diff shows only the fork work. Once #7585 merges, GitHub will retarget this PR to `main`.

### What a fork gets
- Its own worktree and branch, starting at the original's commit for that turn, with the files as that turn left them (uncommitted and new files included).
- The conversation up to that turn and the agent's own memory of it:
  - Claude Code (copy cut at the turn) and Codex (native fork at the turn) can fork from **any finished turn**.
  - Other Chat agents with a native fork, from their latest turn.
  - Terminal agents with a fork command (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Grok, Droid, Continue).
  - **Every other agent**: a fresh agent is given the original's conversation as text (AO's record of the turns, changed files, artifacts, and the end of a terminal screen). These forks are labelled "Conversation copied as text".
- Copies of attachments and artifacts (as of the forked turn); `ao://` links point at the fork's copies.
- `node_modules` / `.venv` cloned copy-on-write where the disk supports it; setup runs with `AO_FORK=1`.
- The original's agent, model, effort, permissions and account.

### Around it
- The inspector's Forks section says it in plain sentences with links: "This session was forked from **X**" in a fork, and "N sessions were forked from this one:" with each fork linked in the original.
- Fork button on a turn's action row (desktop and mobile), "Fork session" in the session menu (greyed out with the reason when forking isn't possible), `ao session fork <id> [--check]`.
- Naming "Fork of X" / "Fork N of X" against the root; inspector Forks section with Forked from (live title), forks list, and the original's PRs as read-only links.
- PR protections: a fork never owns the original's PRs; `ao review trigger` refuses them; `ao session claim-pr` moves a PR and tells the other session (starting a Chat agent if it isn't running).
- Cleanup: archiving/deleting a fork removes its worktree, copies, starting-files ref and agent session file, and drops changes it only inherited; the original is never touched.
- Refusals with reasons: orchestrator, multi-repo project, not git, terminated, busy, still setting up, no finished turn, turn files not saved.
- Docs: `guides/session-forks.mdx`, CLI reference.

### Cost per turn
- To fork from an older turn, AO needs the files and artifacts as that turn started, so turns of agents whose forks can start from an older turn (Claude Code and Codex) take a snapshot as each turn starts. Codex already did for rollback; other agents fork only their latest turn and take none.
- The file and artifact snapshots run side by side. Measured on this repo (6,729 tracked files): about 0.23 s per turn; 1 to 2 s with 4,500 untracked files; above 5,000 untracked files the snapshot gives up in about 0.1 s (that turn can still be rolled back in the conversation, just not forked from).

### What runs if you never fork
Most of the feature runs only once a session is a fork: copying files and artifacts, the fork's instructions, its restore and cleanup rules, and the text copy of a conversation all check for fork lineage first. These parts run for everyone:
- **A file snapshot before each turn**, for Claude Code and Codex Chat sessions only, so a later fork can start from that turn. It stores one git ref per turn in the repo. It took about 0.23 s on this repo, is capped at 10 s, and a failure never holds the turn.
- **An artifact list and copies at each turn start**, alongside the file snapshot and capped at 3 s. Only a session's last 50 turns keep their list, and copies no remaining list names are removed. Unchanged content is hard-linked to the version store's copy, so it takes no extra space.
- **A "PR moved" notice on any PR takeover.** When `claim-pr` moves a PR from one session to another, the previous owner is now told, whether or not forks are involved.
- **A new `session_forks` table**, which stays empty without forks.
- **A cleanup pass at daemon start** that deletes only fork snapshot refs older than an hour.
- **A fork-options check per chat view**, so the Fork button shows as enabled or greyed out. It's a cheap read plus a quick git check.

## Testing
- Unit/integration tests added across domain, chat service, session manager, fork service, store, daemon wiring, API, desktop components and mobile.
- Ran: `go build ./...`, `go vet` on touched packages, `go test` for domain, chat, sessionfork, session_manager, daemon, store and httpd; frontend `typecheck` and fork/sidebar/menu vitest suites; mobile `tsc` and chat vitest suites.
- Known pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (also fail on the base commit): four `TestSpawn_*MissingBinary*` tests that depend on the local PATH.
- Manually verified in a dev build: forking at the latest and older turns, files/artifacts per turn, fork of a fork, naming and lineage after a rename, independence both ways, Copilot terminal fork via text, PR protections against a real PR, mobile fork from the simulator.

## Known limits / follow-ups
- A text-copy Chat fork starts with an empty timeline (its agent has the conversation as text).
- Text-copy forks can start only from the latest turn.
- The mobile app doesn't show the "copied as text" label yet.

* **New Features**
  * Fork sessions from the desktop app, mobile app, or CLI, choosing an eligible conversation turn where supported.
  * Forks carry over relevant conversation context, workspace files, artifacts, and attachments. When an agent cannot copy a conversation directly, the fork can start with a text handoff.
  * View fork relationships, availability details, and related pull requests. Forks receive distinct names and can be created from existing forks.
  * Receive a notification when a pull request is claimed by another session.

* **Documentation**
