title: fix(desktop): bound interface-transition polling like mobile
body:
Code changes: +165 -47  
Tests: +233 -2  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Bound desktop readiness polling and failure retries using mobile's existing schedule, while refreshing spent readiness on session lifecycle events.

## Why

The desktop interface-transition status poll (`useSessionInterfaceTransition.ts`) had no budget and no backoff:

- The native-session readiness recheck (`NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`, `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED`, `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE`) re-polled every 1s forever. A `--resume` relaunch can stay UNVERIFIED indefinitely (#4122), so an open session view sent one request per second for as long as it stayed open.
- A failed request re-armed on the last good status, so errors kept polling at 250ms (live handoff) or 1s (readiness) with no backoff and no stop, including for a session the daemon says is gone.
- The query's own `retry: 1` doubled every attempt.

Mobile already bounds all of this (`packages/mobile/lib/session/interfaceTransition.ts`).

Note on scope: mobile does not cap a live transition. It polls a live handoff until it settles, by design (a drain lasts as long as the agent's turn, and a capped live retry stranded the banner, #4852 review). This PR matches that: the 10-try cap is the readiness recheck, and failures back off.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Readiness retries could poll indefinitely | Mount read plus ten readiness rechecks, then no interval polling |
| Failed requests retried on a flat cadence | Shared mobile failure backoff and retry limits |
| A cached live Cloud handoff could keep polling after authentication was refused | Authentication errors stop the timer immediately; successful explicit refresh can recover after sign-in |
| A spent readiness budget could leave a slow-starting terminal session unable to switch | Session-row CDC events recheck the named switch status after provisioning or native identity changes; id-only usage events do not reopen polling |

## How

- Desktop Cloud authentication refusals (`CloudCpAuthError`, including HTTP 401 or missing credentials) stop the interval even when a live transition remains cached and the query stays enabled. Ordinary Cloud failures retain their existing backoff. A later successful explicit refresh clears the error and allows normal scheduling.

- New `packages/shared/session/interface-transition-poll.ts`: mobile's schedule as one pure function plus its constants (10 readiness answers, 1/2/4/8s failure backoff, stop after 5 failures when no handoff is live, stop on a deleted session, never poll a recovery-fenced handoff). Mobile's `interfaceTransitionNextPoll` now delegates to it; its outputs are unchanged and its existing tests pass untouched.
- Desktop `refetchInterval` uses the same function. Budgets are kept per react-query `Query`, so every observer of one key shares one count. Any data that lands (poll, manual recheck, accepted start) clears the failure count, and a new phase or reason opens a fresh readiness window, so a new transition never inherits a spent budget.
- Desktop session-row CDC events now invalidate the named interface-transition status when the row payload carries activity. This includes native identity and provisioning updates even when activity itself has not changed. Id-only usage updates do not trigger these reads, and unchanged readiness does not refill the polling budget.
- Desktop query `retry` is now `false`; the shared backoff owns retries.
- End state after the budget is spent: polling stops, no spinner (`isLoading` is false), and the switch shows the status reason or `statusError` as its disabled reason. This mirrors mobile, where polling stops and the next user action re-asks.

## Testing

- Latest auth review fix: all 93 tests in the transition-hook and event-transport suites passed; frontend `npm run typecheck` passed. New regressions cover live/readiness authentication refusal, a cached error on the first scheduler check, both Cloud read paths, no retries over 60 seconds after 401, successful explicit refresh after sign-in, and unchanged 503 backoff.

- Lifecycle review fix: all 87 tests in `event-transport.test.ts` and `useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx` passed, and frontend `npm run typecheck` passed. The new real QueryObserver regression exhausts the readiness budget, ignores id-only usage CDC, rechecks once on an unchanged session-row event without restarting interval polling, and becomes supported after the native hook's row event.

- New unit tests in `useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx`: stops after 10 readiness answers, backoff 1/2/4/8s then stop at 5 failures when idle, live handoff keeps retrying at 8s, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` stops, success on try N stops when the handoff completes, budgets reset when a new transition starts.
- Fake-timer tests through real react-query: exactly 11 requests (mount + 10 rechecks) for a readiness wait, and exact request counts at 1s/3s/7s/15s for a failing poll, then no more requests over the next 60s.
- `npx vitest run` in `frontend/`: 723 files pass. The 2 failing files (`browser-cookie-repair`, `browser-profile-import`) fail with "Could not locate the bindings file" because this worktree installed deps with `--ignore-scripts`; unrelated.
- Mobile: `lib/session`, `ChatSessionScreen.switch`, `chatModeApi` suites pass (311 tests). Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from pre-existing `packages/product-ui` module resolution.

## Risks

- Desktop now retries a failed first read (cold start) up to 5 times with backoff, like mobile. Before, a failed first read with no data never re-polled.
- Lifecycle events can cause explicit readiness reads after the interval budget is spent. They do not reset the budget or add a new interval timer.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused regressions and affected suites passed.
- [x] Frontend typecheck passed.
- [ ] Latest GitHub CI checks verified.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Interface-transition status now refreshes on a controlled schedule: live handoffs are checked frequently, while readiness checks and repeated failures use limited polling with increasing delays.
  * Polling stops when a session is missing, sign-in is required, a handoff completes, or the applicable check limit is reached.
  * After a sign-in-required error, an explicit refresh can resume status checks.
  * Session activity updates can trigger a refresh of the related interface-transition status.
  * Updates that do not change transition status no longer restart its polling budget.

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

Updates `baseline-browser-mapping` from 2.10.35 to 2.11.35
Release notes

Sourced from baseline-browser-mapping's releases.

v2.11.0

What's Changed in 2.11.0

  • feat: Adds a new getTimeline() method for getting the series of minimum browser changes, either grouped by date or by browser.
  • refactor: Substantial refactoring of the data compression process that replaces the full list of browsers from @mdn/browser-compat-data and downstream-browsers.json and features from web-features (in their very pared down form) with a change-list timeline that reflects which versions supported Baseline (newly available) on a given date. Thanks to @​swwind for the idea!
  • refactor: Some common functions have been moved to a util.ts module for use in other scripts.
  • fix: Removes process.exit() calls when unsupported option combinations are passed to getCompatibleVersions() and getAllVersions() in favour of throwing an Error. There is a small security risk with process.exit() calls that sites accepting unsanitised inputs could be the subject of attacks. Unsupported config options now throw and Error which should allow for more graceful handling. Thanks to @​bnbdr for flagging this as vulnerability CVE-2026-45819 .

Fixes #134

Full Changelog: https://github.com/web-platform-dx/baseline-browser-mapping/compare/v2.10.44...v2.11.0

title: fix(sentry): bound desktop and daemon error volume (stable hotfix)
body:
## What

Backports two Sentry volume fixes from `main` onto `stable` (`v0.14.10`, `033d597032`), so they can ship as a stable patch without promoting the rest of `main`:

- `f4d0ae6be2` fix: bound Sentry capture and exclude expected provider states (#7878), cherry-picked from `c7f0f45677`
- `ef67238ebf` fix(sentry): bound desktop error volume and give renderer errors real titles (#8087), cherry-picked from `6554304e6f`

#7878 comes first because #8087 builds on it. On its own, #8087 conflicts on `stable` in the daemon `sentryobs` package and in `sentry-main.ts`. With #7878 applied first, both commits apply without conflicts.

## Why

0.14.10 used up the Sentry quota in two days (details in #8087), so Sentry is dropping errors. Every 0.14.10 install sends every desktop and daemon error.

## Before / After

| Before (0.14.10) | After |
| --- | --- |
| Every install sends every non-fatal desktop and daemon error | One install in ten sends them; Electron main crashes and daemon panics still send from every install |
| Renderer budget in memory, keyed on the raw first stack line | 3 per fingerprint and 25 per install per UTC day, saved in `telemetry_sentry_budget.json` in the data directory |
| Most renderer errors are titled `Renderer Error in unknown (unknown)` | Titles name the bundle file and line, and events carry debug IDs for uploaded source maps |
| Self-built copies with release-like versions report to Sentry | Only builds from `build-artifacts.yml` (`AO_PUBLISHED_BUILD=1`) with a stable or nightly version report |

## Testing

A PR into `stable` skips the Go and frontend test jobs: `go.yml` and `frontend.yml` run them only when `base_ref == 'main'`. So I ran them locally on `ef67238ebf`:

- `go build ./...`: clean. `go vet` on the 7 touched packages: clean.
- `go test -count=1` on `daemon`, `httpd`, `observe/sentryobs`, `observe/trackerintake`, `service/agent`, `service/chat` and `session_manager`: all pass.
- `npm ci` in `frontend/` succeeds with the backported lockfile. `npm run typecheck` passes, with `packages/product-ui` installed the way CI installs it.
- `vitest` on the 11 touched test files: 462 passed.
- The added and removed lines of each cherry-pick match its `main` commit exactly. For #8087 only the surrounding context lines differ.

Not done: the full vitest and Go suites, a packaged `AO_PUBLISHED_BUILD=1` build, and a desktop smoke test.

## Migrations

None in either commit.

## Merging and release

Merge with a merge commit, as with #7383. Then the release conductor cuts the patch from the new `stable` head:

```sh
gh workflow run stable.yml --repo OrchestratorInc/ao-releases -f version=0.14.11 -f ref=<stable head after merge>
```

The `build-artifacts.yml` run publishes `sentry-sourcemaps-<platform>` artifacts, kept for 1 day. Upload all four to `ao-electron` with `sentry-cli sourcemaps upload --org untrivial-x0 --project ao-electron <dir>`. Until then, frames stay minified.

#8070 (promotion of `main`) also uses `0.14.11` and fast-forwards `stable` to `7e807beb01`. After this merges, that push is no longer a fast-forward, so #8070 needs its `-s ours` merge of `stable` redone and its version changed to `0.14.12`. #8070 already contains #7878 but not #8087.

## Risks

- Installs on 0.14.10 keep sending at full volume until they update. A rate limit on the Sentry client keys covers them in the meantime.
- The daemon's per-install daily cap is in memory and resets when the daemon restarts.
- A build made outside `build-artifacts.yml` sends nothing to Sentry. This is intended.

title: fix(artifacts): list orchestrator artifacts on the Artifacts page
body: ## Summary Files an orchestrator session wrote never showed on the Artifacts page or in the sidebar's artifact count. Files from worker sessions did. **Root cause:** `groupArtifactsByProject` in `frontend/src/renderer/lib/artifacts.ts` runs every project's sessions through `workerSessions(...)`. That has dropped orchestrators since the page was added in #6567, and a test pinned it ("skips orchestrators"). Both the Artifacts page and the sidebar badge use this function. The rest of the path treats both kinds the same. I checked each step: - An orchestrator is spawned through `Manager.Spawn`, so it gets `artifacts//` like a worker. - Its system prompt gets the same "Session Artifacts" section, with its own directory and `ao artifact add`. - `ao artifact add` and the registration service have no worker-only check. - The session list, the `outputType` reconcile and `deliverableArtifacts` don't check the session kind. So the orchestrator's own inspector Artifacts tab already listed its files. Only the project-wide list left them out. ## Changes - `groupArtifactsByProject` lists orchestrator sessions too. They follow the same rules as workers: registered deliverables only (#7855), bundles collapsed into one entry (#7811), archived or terminated sessions hidden. - An orchestrator's row shows "Orchestrator" instead of its bare session ID. The rest of the app labels orchestrators the same way. - No prompt change. ## Existing artifacts Files that past orchestrators wrote show up after this ships, with no backfill. The list is read live from each session's artifact directory. A replaced or killed orchestrator stays hidden, the same as a killed worker. Its files are still on disk under its old session ID. ## Tests (written, not run locally) - `lib/artifacts.test.ts`: an orchestrator's rows are listed next to its workers' and titled "Orchestrator". Only its registered files are listed, and a bundle is one entry. A terminated orchestrator stays hidden. The old "skips orchestrators" case now covers only remote hosts and PR-only output. - `ArtifactsView.test.tsx`: the page lists an orchestrator's artifact, shows "agent-orchestrator · Orchestrator" in Recent, and "Open in session" goes to the orchestrator session. - `manager_test.go`: an orchestrator's prompt, terminal and chat, names its own artifact directory and `ao artifact add`. ## Risks / follow-ups - Cloud orchestrators go through the same function. Whether they show also depends on the control plane reporting their `outputType` and artifact count. That isn't checked here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(spawn): 120s setup budget, timeout labels, no live model lookup, auto-start breaker, spawn telemetry, Sentry cap
body:
Code changes: +1291 -90  
Tests: +1336 -74  
Others: +77 -6  

## What

Spawn reliability: a longer setup budget, correct timeout labels, no live model lookups during a spawn, a stop for automatic retry loops, spawn step telemetry, and a cap on Sentry noise.

## Why

Spawn setup could exhaust its request budget, automatic retries could repeat failures, and stale saved tuning could block launches. Failures also lacked bounded, useful telemetry.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Spawn setup routes started with a 60-second request limit | Setup routes start with at least 120 seconds, with the existing Setup-step extension |
| Mixed project and worker tuning could hide an inherited invalid model or effort | Model and effort resolve independently; a confirmed reset clears their owning slots |
| Saved effort survived on concrete Claude models that support no effort levels | Unsupported effort can be reset with explicit confirmation, including omitted empty lists; family aliases resolve through the newest effort-capable family model |
| Automatic starts could retry repeatedly after failures | Three identical configuration/auth failures pause automatic starts; one probe is allowed after a 30-minute cooldown, while transient failures break the streak |

## How

**1. Spawn request limit: 60s to 120s.** `httpd/api.go`: setup routes (spawn, orchestrator start, restore, resume-agent) start from `max(timeout, 120s)` instead of `timeout`. The Setup-step extension (`ports.ExtendSpawnRequestBudget`) still applies on top. Every other route keeps the 60s REST timeout.

**2. Desktop Chat starts in the background.** Most of this was already in place, so only a small change was needed:
- Desktop project tasks go through `POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`, not `POST /api/v1/sessions`. Delegate already spawns with `Async: true` (`service/session/delegation.go`).
- Orchestrator starts were already forced async in `Service.Spawn`. The desktop already shows the returned session as starting, keeps the start's checklist, and shows a failed start with Retry inside the session.
- `TaskComposer`'s `POST /api/v1/sessions` call is only for standalone sessions, and the daemon ignores `async` for standalone and terminal starts. I left that body unchanged.
- What changed: `_shell.tsx` now sends `async: true` for the orchestrator start explicitly, as the CLI does, and the test asserts it. Starting and failed rendering stays covered by `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` ("starting session's checklist", "failed start's checklist with ... Retry").

**3. No live model lookup during a spawn.** `resolveAgentConfig` validates against the saved catalog only and never calls `Models(..., true)` inline. When the saved catalog cannot answer (the read failed, or it is stale, updating, or does not list the model or effort), a coalesced refresh starts on the manager's background context and the launch goes ahead, leaving the final say to the agent CLI, as Codex already did. Two hard rejections stay: a model the saved catalog marks `RequiresVersion`, and an effort the saved catalog lists as unsupported for the model. A cancelled spawn still stops. (If no catalog has ever been saved, the read still waits up to the existing 500ms first-load bound.)

**4. Model picker catches bad settings before the spawn.**
- Models that need a newer Claude Code were already disabled in the picker with their reason. They now also offer an "Update Claude Code" item, which opens Settings > Harness for Claude Code on the catalog host with its usual update flow.
- `useResetStaleProjectTuning` offers a dismissible Reset saved settings action for a stale model or unsupported effort. Opening the composer performs no project GET or PUT. Only the explicit action re-reads the project, validates current catalog capabilities and per-field ownership again, and saves. The proposal remains available until dismissed, and failed saves offer Retry. Dismissing keeps saved settings. Models marked `RequiresVersion` and their effort are preserved so the picker's Update Claude Code action remains useful.
- A stale or loading catalog (MODEL_CAPABILITIES_UNAVAILABLE) never resets anything. Unlisted dynamic/configured models stay available for agent-side validation. Removed-model resets are limited to complete official static catalogs. Effort-only settings are checked against the catalog default without changing the saved model.

**5. Stop automatic retry loops.** In `service/session/auto_spawn_breaker.go`, automatic starts for one project, role, harness and effective model/effort pair pause after 3 identical configuration or authentication failures. Further automatic starts answer `AUTO_SPAWN_PAUSED` during a 30-minute cooldown. The first later occurrence reserves one probe atomically; concurrent automatic starts remain blocked until that probe settles. Success clears the pause, while an identical failure starts another cooldown.
- A successful start resets only its own launch configuration. Admission captures a generation token; stale or duplicate asynchronous outcomes cannot modify a repaired configuration. Settlement is entirely in memory with no project lookup. Automation-attributed asynchronous starts settle even without an automation run ID. So does a change to the project's default agent config or its worker/orchestrator agent settings (detected by a fingerprint, so there is no cross-service wiring).
- Manual starts are never paused. Timeouts, internal errors, controller failures, workspace-operation failures, cancellation, and other transient codes do not count and break any prior configuration streak.
- Local and remote pause notices stay visible until acknowledgement; acknowledgements survive denied storage writes in memory. Host and launch-configuration identities distinguish notices.
- Active pauses are listed on `GET /api/v1/projects` as `autoSpawnPauses`. Expired cooldowns are not listed and listing does not consume a probe. The API error and desktop notice explain cooldown recovery, so headless schedules can recover on a later occurrence without a settings change.
- The scheduler still marks a paused occurrence failed rather than replaying missed work. Cooldown recovery permits a later scheduled/intake occurrence; it does not replay previously failed occurrences.
- Automatic spawn callers (every `SpawnConfig` built without a person behind it):
  - `observe/trackerintake/observer.go` (tracker auto-spawn / intake): `CreatedBy: automation`, sync start.
  - `service/automation/scheduler.go` `dispatch` (schedules): `AutomationRunID` set. A worker start is sync; an orchestrator start is async and counted when it settles (`settleAsyncSpawn`).
- Not automatic, so never paused: `service/cue/invoke.go` (user-invoked cue), `review/review.go` (reviewer launch, its own launcher), `service/session/delegation.go` (desktop delegate), agents running `ao spawn` (`ParentSessionID`), desktop, CLI and mobile.

**6. Correct timeout labels.**
- New `sessionmanager.RelabelSpawnTimeout`. `Manager.Spawn` checks both the request context and the Setup-extended budget context, which expires about 1s before the request, so a stage killed by it returns while the request is still live. `spawnWithTelemetry` and `failAsyncChatSpawn` (with its own 10 minute budget context) do the same.
- Whatever a stage returned, an expired deadline makes it a `SpawnTimeoutError`, and `toSpawnAPIError` maps that to SPAWN_TIMEOUT first.
- `chatdriver/acp/driver.go`: when the startup retry wait is cut short, it returns `errors.Join(ctx.Err(), err)`.

**7. Cancels are not failures.** A spawn that ends in SPAWN_CANCELLED sends `ao.sessions.spawn_cancelled` with the same props instead of `ao.sessions.spawn_failed`. This covers both the sync path and an async start cancelled in the background, which previously reported nothing.

**8. Spawn telemetry.**
- A `SpawnTrace` rides the spawn context, including into the async background start, and records:
  - `model_check_ms`, `branch_fetch_ms`, `worktree_ms`, `setup_ms` and `agent_start_ms` for the steps that ran.
  - The first failing step.
  - The model bucket (only fixed Claude family aliases, optionally `[1m]`, or `custom`; every concrete or discovered ID is bucketed even when listed in a gateway catalog), `mode` (`chat` / `terminal`, omitted before selection) and `async` (true only after background admission).
- `spawned`, `spawn_failed` and `spawn_cancelled` all carry these. `spawn_failed` and `spawn_cancelled` now also carry `surface` and `created_by`.
- Failures add `failed_step` (`model_check`, `branch_fetch`, `worktree`, `setup`, `agent_start`, `prompt`, `other`) and `cause`:
  - Git and worktree causes come from the git stderr already held in `commandError` (`gitworktree/failure_cause.go`).
  - Agent and Chat start causes are `exited`, `no_response`, `not_logged_in`, `killed` and `other`.
  - `timeout` applies whenever item 6 does.
- No paths, branch names, repo names, prompts or error text are sent.
- `$os`, `platform` and `arch` were already stamped on every daemon event regardless of launcher (`adapters/telemetry/environment.go`), CLI-launched daemons included.
- Allowlist (`adapters/telemetry/posthog.go`) and `docs/telemetry.md` / `docs/posthog-cost-controls.md` are updated.

**9. Sentry noise cap.**
- Per-fingerprint daily cap: 200 down to 10 events per install per day, which is one daemon.
- Refused events are counted per fingerprint, and the next event sent carries `dropped_since_last`, across the day boundary too.
- `failed_step` and `cause` are Sentry tags on spawn errors, attached through a `SentryTags()` error hook that passes the same safe-tag filter.
- `WORKSPACE_GIT_READ_FAILED` (AO-DAEMON-9): the desktop polls workspace git reads (file list, diff, content search), so a repository stuck in one broken state sent one event per poll. Each workspace root and Git operation reports once per failure state (exit code plus first stderr line, kept in memory). Only recovery of that operation re-arms it, including grep success or no-match and capped-output reads. Clients still get the same 500. Separate operations and workspaces cannot re-arm one another.

## How to verify

PostHog:
- `ao.sessions.spawn_failed`, grouped by `failed_step` and `cause`. A slow spawn should now show `error_code: SPAWN_TIMEOUT` with `cause: timeout`, not `SPAWN_INTERNAL` or `CHAT_CONTROLLER_FAILED` with "signal: killed".
- `ao.sessions.spawned`: `model_check_ms`, `branch_fetch_ms`, `worktree_ms`, `setup_ms`, `agent_start_ms`, `mode`, `async`, `model`. `model_check_ms` should stay small, because there is no live discovery.
- `ao.sessions.spawn_cancelled` replaces the cancelled share of `spawn_failed`. `spawn_failed` also gains `surface` and `created_by`.
- Automatic loops: `spawn_failed` with `created_by` = `automation` or `scheduled` should stop at 3 per launch configuration per error code.

Sentry:
- Tags `failed_step` and `cause` on spawn errors (`chat_spawn` background captures and `http_request` captures on the spawn routes).
- `dropped_since_last` on the first event after a fingerprint hit its 10/day cap.
- AO-DAEMON-9 volume should drop to about one event per workspace operation per failure state.

## Testing

- Backend:
  - 120s budget on setup routes only (`api_timeout_test.go`).
  - A killed git process and a peer-disconnected ACP error under an expired context both map to SPAWN_TIMEOUT (`spawn_telemetry_test.go`).
  - Git `cause` classifier, one case per value, plus a real killed process (`failure_cause_test.go`).
  - Retry stop rule: trip at 3, different codes, manual failures, manual success reset, settings change reset, async schedule failures, cancels (`auto_spawn_breaker_test.go`).
  - Sentry per-install cap and `dropped_since_last` (`sentryobs_test.go`).
  - Git-read once-per-state (`service_test.go`).
  - The model check not waiting on live discovery: the refresh is held open and the spawn still resolves (`provision_test.go`).
  - Spawn props and the `spawn_cancelled` event.
- Updated model-check tests that asserted the old inline rediscovery or rejection.
- Frontend:
  - Orchestrator start sends `async: true`.
  - Picker disables a newer-CLI model and offers Update Claude Code.
  - Stale-tuning rules, and the reset hook (requires confirmation, preserves upgrade-only selections, rechecks sources/capabilities, and keeps unrelated config).
  - Pause notices persist until acknowledgement, distinguish remote hosts/configurations, and tolerate storage failures.
- Suites: see the results comment below.

### Review regression validation

- Mixed project/worker inheritance is validated per field, with source-aware config re-read guards after explicit reset confirmation.
- Claude models with empty or omitted effort lists offer a confirmed reset of saved unsupported effort. Empty family aliases use the newest effort-capable family model, matching daemon validation.
- Earlier focused run: 91 tests passed across stale tuning, the reset hook, model choices, and the model picker. Frontend typecheck passed.
- Full repository suites and remote CI verification remain with GitHub CI; these focused passes do not imply all checks are green.

### Latest review validation

- All 68 tests in the reset hook, pause notice, stale-tuning utility, and model picker suites passed. Frontend typecheck passed.
- Focused breaker and model-resolution telemetry regressions passed. Breaker tests also passed with the race detector, including concurrent probe admission and an in-flight probe lasting beyond another cooldown.
- Linux-target golangci-lint v2.13.2 with Go 1.27.1 passed for both affected Go packages (zero issues).
- The full affected session-service suite had one content-search timeout under load. That same test failed in the earlier clean-base log and passed when rerun alone. This is not a full-suite pass.
- Desktop visual verification was not run; confirmation, dismissal, stale-action guards, and save failures were exercised in hook tests.
- Full repository suites and latest remote CI verification remain with GitHub CI.

### Backend CI recovery (79dacfec05)

- CI backend-core shard 0 failed in `TestCaptureBackgroundDoesNotBlockAndOptOutDrainsAdmittedSends`: an expected admitted send did not reach the transport.
- Background test fixtures now close capture intake and drain admitted sends before disabling Sentry. Receiving an event alone does not guarantee its goroutine has released a shared admission slot, so the next fixture must not reinitialize global state before draining. Production admission and telemetry behavior are unchanged.
- The failure did not reproduce in 20 initial local race-enabled runs. After the cleanup fix, the affected Sentry package passed 30 shuffled race-enabled iterations at each of one and four CPUs (60 runs total), and Linux-target affected-package lint passed with zero issues using Go 1.27.1 and golangci-lint v2.13.2.
- The full backend shard and latest remote CI remain to be verified by GitHub CI.

### Storage-race CI recovery (8584db4df4)

- The storage-race job failed in chat `TestCompactionSettlementWithoutStartDrainsQueue/turn.completed`, where the test observed a running turn before the provider had received its message. The extracted job diagnostics contained no data-race report.
- Queued dispatch deliberately claims a turn as running before calling the provider, preventing duplicate replay. The test now waits on the existing fake provider send callback before asserting exact delivered text, while keeping the durable running-state assertion. Production code is unchanged.
- The final test passed 30 race-enabled iterations at each of one and four CPUs (60 iterations total, covering both settlement event types). The related compaction test group passed with the race detector. Linux-target chat-package lint passed with zero issues using Go 1.27.1 and golangci-lint v2.13.2.
- The full storage-race shard and latest remote CI remain to be verified by GitHub CI.

### Review follow-up validation (7c4be63e14)

- 94 tests passed across saved-tuning/reset, persistent toast/pause, model picker, and remote workspace suites. Frontend typecheck passed.
- Focused race-enabled regressions passed in session service, session manager and Git worktree packages, covering configuration isolation, stale async outcomes, automation attribution, cooldown probes, telemetry admission, operation-specific Git/grep recovery, and nonblocking catalog resolution.
- Full affected Git worktree and project-service suites and API spec drift tests passed. Pinned OpenAPI TypeScript generation passed.
- Linux-target golangci-lint v2.13.2 with Go 1.27.1 reported zero issues in the three affected Go packages.
- POSIX signal tests now skip Windows; Windows execution remains CI-only. Full repository suites, latest remote checks and real desktop visual verification were not run for this follow-up.

### Final review follow-up

- Manual starts do not retain new breaker configurations (8868a72a0a); focused breaker race tests and session-package lint passed.
- Remote pause titles include the host ID, distinguishing same-name projects (a81291b1b6). All three notice-hook tests and frontend typecheck passed.

## Risks and follow-ups

- A model the saved catalog does not list now launches and fails in the CLI, if it fails at all, instead of being refused up front. The picker and the optional confirmed reset let the user correct saved choices before launching.
- The breaker and the Sentry budget live in memory, so a daemon restart allows three more automatic attempts and refills the Sentry budget. Both are marked `ponytail:` with the upgrade path.
- An effort the saved catalog lists as unsupported is refused even when that catalog is stale, and the background refresh fixes the next attempt.



## Checklist

- [x] Focused regression tests passed.
- [x] Frontend typecheck passed.
- [ ] Latest GitHub CI checks verified.

title: feat(chat): show a turn's artifacts as preview cards
body: Code changes: +113 -8\ Tests: +160 -2\ Others: +0 -0 ## What When a turn creates or edits a session artifact, the chat now shows it as a preview card under the reply, like the Summary's Artifacts row, instead of listing it under "Files Changed". Each card shows the thumbnail, the file name, and whether that turn **Created** or **Edited** it, so you can tell which turn made or changed each artifact. Clicking a card opens it in the inspector's Artifacts tab. Workspace files keep the "Files Changed" card. If a turn only touched artifacts, that card is not drawn. ## Why An artifact written to the session's artifact directory showed up as a plain diff row (`pocket-guide-to-tea.md +26`) next to code changes, with a Review button that opens the workspace diff, which doesn't include it. It looked like a code change, and from the chat you couldn't tell which turn produced which artifact. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before: artifacts listed as changed files](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/e068f8eb2058078d3eb4e96fa9da9488c4213277/turn-artifact-cards/before-full.png?raw=true) | ![After: artifacts shown as preview cards](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/e068f8eb2058078d3eb4e96fa9da9488c4213277/turn-artifact-cards/after-full.png?raw=true) | A turn that made two artifacts and edited one workspace file. The artifacts become cards, and only `format.ts` stays in "1 File Changed": ## How - `lib/turn-artifacts.ts` splits a turn diff into deliverables and other files. The renderer isn't told where the artifact directory is, so an absolute diff path is matched on the daemon's `/artifacts//` suffix. Bare names are resolved through the turn's own absolute paths first, using the same `turnPathHints` the Files Changed tooltips use. - Only files the session lists as **deliverables** (`deliverableArtifacts`, the same rule the Summary and Artifacts views use) become cards. A deleted artifact, a supporting file, or a file written after the last session refresh stays a plain changed file, so nothing the turn changed is hidden. Renames resolve through `previousPaths`, and files inside a bundle collapse into one card. - `TurnResults` replaces `TurnChangedFiles` at the end of a completed turn and renders `TurnArtifacts` (cards built on the existing `ArtifactThumbnail`) followed by `TurnChangedFiles` with the remaining files. - The session's artifact list already reaches the chat through `ChatImageSourceProvider`. It now also carries `cloud` so thumbnails resolve for cloud sessions. A card opens through the existing `onOpenFile` path, which the daemon already routes to the Artifacts tab for an artifact path. Known limitation: a card shows the artifact as it is now, not as it was at that turn, so an earlier turn's card shows a later edit. Per-turn snapshots would need artifact versions in the turn record. ## Testing - `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/lib/turn-artifacts.test.ts src/renderer/components/chat/ src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx src/renderer/components/ArtifactThumbnail.test.tsx`: 2104 passed. Two side-chat tests (`IndependentSideChatDelivery`, `IndependentSideCreation`) timed out under full-suite load and passed 52/52 when rerun on their own. They don't touch this code. - New unit tests cover path matching (POSIX, `~`, Windows, other sessions, relative paths), the deliverable-only rule, deleted artifacts, bare-name resolution, renames, and the card/Files-card split, including clicking a card. - `npm run typecheck`: no errors in `frontend/`. - Screenshots come from the real renderer (`dev:web` + the e2e fake-agent bridge, Playwright Chromium, dark theme) with stubbed conversation and artifact responses: markdown, SVG, and HTML thumbnails. The before shot is the same fixture on the parent commit. The Electron app against a live daemon was not exercised. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(spawn): start terminal sessions in the background
body:
Code changes: +417 -229  
Tests: +687 -3  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Start Terminal worker and orchestrator sessions in the background when `async: true` is requested. Return the seeded starting session before workspace creation, Setup, agent startup, and opening prompt delivery. Keep synchronous callers and automation Terminal launches synchronous.

#8119 merged on November 11, 2026 (squash commit `59a0179c8f0d67c5e0285ad3a339378fb36217ba`). This PR now targets `main`; its own commits were rebased onto `10f14253b179dc5f9f41ae91efaec407c06e18d0` to exclude the merged dependency from the diff.

## Why

Terminal session creation currently blocks the desktop request during slow repository preparation. The existing Chat background startup machinery already provides the bounded lifecycle and durable progress needed for Terminal starts.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal creation waits for workspace, Setup, runtime, and prompt delivery. | Async creation returns a starting row before those operations. A synthetic blocked-workspace test verifies acceptance before any runtime or prompt operation. |
| Terminal availability can precede a usable agent. | The read model exposes the Terminal only after runtime creation and opening prompt delivery succeed. |
| A failed Terminal start can remain a spinner. | The desktop shows the stored failure reason and Retry. |
| Terminal starts do not use the async outcome timing path. | Final success or failure retains Terminal mode, async attribution, step timings, and total time to settlement, exactly once. |

Real Electron before/after captures and an actual large-repository launch were not performed. Component tests verify starting, failure, retry, and attachment gating with synthetic data. No paid/live agents, real telemetry, or user application data were used.

## How

Reuse the existing async Chat workspace/provisioning path, selecting the real Terminal runtime launch at the agent boundary. Extract the synchronous Terminal launch into one helper shared by both paths. Preserve the ten-minute background budget, cancellation and rollback behavior, durable restart reconciliation, saved retry prompt, and retained handles when cleanup is uncertain.

Carry PR1's service-owned spawn trace into the detached context. Record the resolved launch mode and actual async eligibility, and time Terminal runtime creation inside the helper. Preserve catalog-validated model attribution, background timeout classification, auto-spawn settlement, and separate cancellation events.

## Testing

Latest rebase preserves main's `LaunchConfig.Env` in the extracted Terminal helper. Added a regression test for synchronous and background starts receiving the project environment.

- Focused race checks across session manager, session service, and HTTP/SQLite integration pass on Go 1.27.3, including immediate acceptance, failure paths, restart recovery, delegate behavior, and final outcome timing. The same focused checks also pass on pinned Go 1.27.1.
- Affected frontend suites: 87 tests pass. Refreshed lockfile dependencies for the PR1 base; frontend typecheck and e2e typecheck pass, and the affected suites pass again.
- Rebased onto current main after #8119 merged. Focused race checks pass on main's required Go 1.27.4 toolchain across manager, service, and HTTP/SQLite integration. Pinned golangci-lint 2.14.0 reports zero issues on the PR delta with Go 1.27.4.
- Backend build and vet pass.

title: fix(cursor): explain rejected-login update failures and stop calling them Connected
body:
Fixes #8126.

## Summary

When Cursor's service rejects the CLI's saved login, `cursor-agent status` still exits 0 with `Logged in (unable to fetch user details)`. `cursor-agent update` then fails with `Error: Update failed: [unauthenticated] Error`. AO showed the account as **Connected** next to a bare `exit status 1`, with no way forward. Both the 2026.04.16 and current 2026.11.10 Cursor builds behave this way (reproduction in #8126).

- **Update failure explains itself.** A Cursor update whose output contains `[unauthenticated]` now fails with "Cursor's update service rejected the CLI's saved login. Log out of Cursor, update, then log in again. (exit status 1)". The full CLI output stays in diagnostics. Other failures and other harnesses are unchanged. This follows the existing Autohand-specific message in the same branch.
- **Unconfirmed login is no longer plain "Connected".** The Cursor auth check adds an `account_unconfirmed` diagnostic when `status` says it couldn't fetch user details. The verdict stays `authorized`, because Cursor prints the same text when its service is unreachable, so this must not log out offline users. Settings shows **Login not confirmed**, with a muted hint to log out and log in again if updates or sessions fail. Strings are added in all nine locales.

- **Sign-in tone (after rebase onto #8379).** main's shared `authTone` is green only for a fresh, successful sign-in check. An unconfirmed login now gets the neutral tone instead of green; a confirmed one stays green. Both are covered in `describe-harness.test.ts`.

Log out → Update → Log in was verified as a recovery path in the #8126 reproduction: with no saved login, Cursor's update succeeds.

## Tests

- `go test` for `./internal/adapters/agent/cursor/ ./internal/domain/ ./internal/service/agent/ ./internal/service/systeminstall/` (Cursor/Autohand/diagnostic tests), run with `AO_*` vars stripped. `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.
  - New: `TestCursorRejectedLoginUpdateExplainsRecovery`, which covers the hint, an unrelated Cursor failure, and another harness with the same output.
  - New: `TestCursorUnconfirmedLoginStaysAuthorizedWithCaveat`, which uses the exact CLI output from both builds.
- `vitest`: `describe-harness.test.ts`, `i18n/instance.test.ts`, `HarnessSettingsSection.test.tsx` (169 passed). `npm run typecheck` is clean.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Not visually verified in the desktop app. The UI change is a label swap plus one muted helper line that reuses the existing `-mt-3 text-xs text-settings-muted` pattern.
- An offline Cursor check also shows "Login not confirmed". That's intentional: it's a caveat, not a sign-out.
- Matching relies on Cursor's CLI wording (`[unauthenticated]`, `unable to fetch user details`). If Cursor changes it, AO falls back to the previous behaviour.
- Not included: an automatic fallback to Cursor's installer, which can't be pinned to the approved version.

title: Harness logos missing from chat tab and composer model picker since nightly 0.14.11-nightly.202611101246 (#7822)
body:
## Bug
After updating the desktop app to nightly `0.14.11-nightly.202611102030`, harness/agent logos are gone from the chat surfaces. The composer's model control shows only `Opus 5.5 High` with no Claude mark, and the orchestrator's chat tab shows `Orchestrator` with no agent icon.

**Source:** AO orchestrator chat (desktop) | **Reported by:** the AO user (desktop app owner) | **Analyzed against:** `f9b90ef6ce` (origin/main), tags `v0.14.11-nightly.202611100625` / `…1246` / `…2030`
**Confidence:** High

| Composer model control | Chat tab |
|---|---|
| ![composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-harness-logos-dropped-7822/.issue-assets/harness-logos-dropped-7822/composer.png) | ![chat tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-harness-logos-dropped-7822/.issue-assets/harness-logos-dropped-7822/chat-tab.png) |

## Reproduction
1. Install nightly `0.14.11-nightly.202611101246` or later (the user went straight from `…100625` to `…102030`).
2. Open any chat-mode session (e.g. the orchestrator).
3. The chat tab has no agent icon, and the composer's model picker (button and menu rows) has no harness marks.

## Root Cause
Intentional removal in [PR #7822](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7822) (`b0fabec156`, *feat(chat): fold agent actions into Worked for, collapse Agent Reports, drop harness logos*, merged 2026-11-10 09:44 UTC). Its first commit says: "The chat tab shows its title only, and the composer picker lists models without marks. The terminal picker, sidebar and inspector keep their logos."

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx:2621,2632` passes `providerIcon={false}` to `SessionPaneTab`, and `CenterPane.tsx:756` now renders the `AgentAvatar` only when `providerIcon` is set.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/AgentSwitchPicker.tsx:407,443,457,491` renders `ProviderMark` only when `terminal`, so chat-mode pickers show none.

It is not a packaging or asset failure. In the installed `app.asar` the `AgentAvatar` chunk and every logo asset are present, the CSP allows `'self' data: blob:` for images, and `.size-icon-*` utilities are in the CSS. The daemon still reports `harness: "claude-code"`.

**Why the user saw it only now:** `~/.ao/logs/updater.jsonl` shows `…1246` was downloaded but never installed. The user installed `…100625` (09:52 UTC), then `…102030` (2026-11-11 00:39 UTC). #7822 is in `…1246` and `…2030` but not in `…0625`.

## Fix
Restore the agent mark on the chat tab and in the composer model picker (button, favorites, provider rows, search rows) for chat sessions. Leave #7822's other changes alone (Worked-for folding, Agent Reports line).

## Impact
- In chat mode you can no longer tell which harness a session or model belongs to from the tab or the picker. This affects the orchestrator and every chat worker.

## Related
- [PR #7822](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7822): introduced the removal
- [PR #8042](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/8042): agent logos in color on the Agent Reports line (same surface, open)
- [PR #7819](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7819): Scratchpad sidebar rows show status instead of harness logos (related trend)

title: feat(workflow): add P0 startup step guidance and harden plan creation
body:
Code changes: +228 -20\
Tests: +177 -1\
Others: +180 -9 (i18n catalogs)

## What

Adds P0 startup guidance to the Workflow workbench and hardens the plan-creation form.

- **Startup step strip.** One derived step is shown at a time: create planning task → activate → wait for Planner → extract output → confirm task graph → resume scheduling. Nothing executes automatically; each step keeps its own user-triggered action.
- **Planner polling and status.** The planner attempt is polled while it is in flight or unclaimed, and polling stops on every terminal state. Status is classified as not scheduled / planning / succeeded / failed / unknown. Extraction is enabled only for `succeeded`; `UNKNOWN` is classified separately from success and can never enable extraction. A button opens the planner session (navigation only).
- **Create form.** `targetRef` is derived from the project detail `defaultBranch`. `baseSha` is entered by hand with a full 40/64-char commit-id check and `git rev-parse` guidance. Model and effort stay optional and prefill from the existing agent model catalog. Field-level blockers explain why submit is disabled.

## Why

The startup flow had no visible current step: activation, extraction, confirmation and resuming scheduling were all reachable at once, so the required order was only documented in prose. The planner attempt state was not polled, so a finished planner needed a manual reload, and only `unknown` was guarded — a `failed` attempt could still be extracted. The create form hard-coded `refs/heads/main` as the target branch, ignoring the project's actual default branch, and accepted any `baseSha` string.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `before-plan.png` — no step indicator, no planner status line, extract button ungated | `after-plan.png` — step chip `2 / 6 · Activate workflow`, status `Planning in progress`, extract disabled with its reason |
| `before-create.png` — `targetRef` hard-coded to `refs/heads/main` | `after-create.png` — `targetRef` derived from project `defaultBranch` (`refs/heads/develop`), submit disabled with blockers |

Captured from the real renderer (`dev:web` + fake bridge) at 1280x720 with identical fixture data; the before images come from base `87b2bc15`.

Image files for upload (not committed to the repo): `C:/Users/11459/.ao/data/artifacts/agent-orchestrator-15/workflow-p0-ux/{before,after}-plan.png` and `{before,after}-create.png`.

## How

- `lib/workflow-startup.ts` holds the pure projections: `startupStep`, `plannerStatus`, `canExtractPlan`, `plannerPollInterval`, `isFullCommitSha`, `createBlockers`. Ordering is decided from durable facts only (workflow state, latest planner attempt, candidate `confirmedRevision`, the separate scheduler `paused` flag).
- `useWorkflowTask` gained a `refetchInterval` callback so the caller decides polling from the parsed response; terminal states return `false`.
- `targetRef` is resolved at submit time from the project-detail query, so a draft started before the detail arrives cannot submit a stale branch. When the default branch cannot be read the field renders as unavailable and submit stays disabled — there is no `main` fallback.
- The model/effort inputs reuse `agentModelsQueryOptions("codex", "")`. They are text inputs plus suggestion buttons rather than a `<datalist>`/combobox, because changing the input's ARIA role would break the existing provider-select contract.
- 20 i18n keys per locale, added to all nine catalogs.

Intentional omissions: no new API, no schema/DTO/OpenAPI change, and no SHA lookup — the UI states how to obtain the SHA instead of fetching one.

## Testing

Local checks (Windows, Node 22.20.0; CI pins Node 24):

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` — clean.
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/workflow src/renderer/i18n` — 6 files, 44 tests passed.
- `npx playwright test e2e/workflow-navigation.spec.ts` (CI renderer-smoke `@T0` spec) — 1 passed.
- Full `npm test` — 634/644 files, 10496 passed, 7 failed, 47 skipped. Every failure was re-run in isolation and 4 pass there; the remaining `shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx` fails identically at base `87b2bc15` with this change stashed (`beforeAll` hook timeout on a lazy `import`), so it is pre-existing. `GlobalSettingsForm` passes 59/59 in isolation.

Not run locally: the macOS-only CI jobs (`mac-update-helper`, `mac-dmg-layout`) and the three `xvfb-run` Electron boundary tests in `checks`. `build-artifacts.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only, requires `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`, and is not a PR gate. These are the exact local gaps; nothing above is claimed as CI-passed.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change

- [x] Before / After filled in with real captures
- [x] Tests added for the new behavior

title: fix(archive): open the archive modal in place, never via the board
body:
## Summary

**Before:** Archive in a sidebar project's ⋮ / right-click menu (and Cmd+K → Open archive) went to that project's board, then opened the archive modal there. You lost the page you were on.

**After:** the archive opens over whatever page you're on (a session chat, Artifacts, settings, the board) and closing it leaves you exactly where you were. Nothing navigates unless you open or restore a session from inside it, which closes it.

- **One modal, mounted once in the shell.** `ArchiveModalHost` (in `_shell.tsx`, next to `NewTaskNavigator`) renders `SessionArchiveModal`. `useUiStore().openArchive({ projectId, hostId, query? })` / `closeArchive()` drive it. The board's Archive button, the sidebar project menu and Cmd+K's Open archive all call `openArchive`; none of them navigates.
- **Same modal, same look.** The archive looks and works exactly as before (same scope: the project you opened it for). Only where it opens changed.
- **Optional initial query.** A request can prefill the search. Nothing passes one yet.
- **Focus.** Radix returns focus to a dialog's trigger, and the archive has none, so every opener says where focus goes when it closes: the board's Archive button, the sidebar menu's ⋮ trigger or right-clicked row (`menuFocusReturnTarget()` in `ui/menu-focus.ts`), or wherever Cmd+K was opened from. It's handed back two frames after close, only if nothing else took focus, so a session page the modal opened keeps its composer.
- **Leaving the page closes it.** If the user moves to another page while it's open (a shortcut, history, a notification), it closes. A restore still running then doesn't navigate when it finishes; neither does one whose modal was closed or replaced by a new request. Search-param-only changes keep it open.
- **Session shortcuts stand down** (Cmd+Shift+A and the rest of `useSessionShortcut`) while the archive covers the page, as they already do under Settings, so they can't act on the hidden session.
- **Data.** The host reads the workspace list (`useWorkspaceQuery`, or the new `useRemoteHostWorkspacesQuery` for a remote host), enabled and subscribed only while open. It stays mounted after the first open, so an enabled observer would have kept the cloud lists' own 5 s / 15 s poll timers running. Closing keeps the last list on screen for the exit animation.
- **Perf (#7975 group D).** `ProjectItem` takes no new props. The menu callback is a store action read only when the menu list is built on open, so sidebar rows are unaffected.

**Removed:** `archiveOpenRequest`, `requestArchiveOpen` / `clearArchiveOpenRequest`, the 5 s request expiry, the board's archive open state and its own `SessionArchiveModal`, and the Cmd+K / sidebar navigation to the board.

**Unchanged:** the modal's look and size, search, windowed list, restore, delete confirm, keyboard (↑/↓, Enter opens, ⌘↵ restores, Esc closes), light/dark, cloud sessions having no delete, the Scratchpad and standalone rows not showing the entry, and remote and offline hosts (restore disabled while offline).

**i18n:** none. **DESIGN.md:** the archive rule now says it opens in place instead of going to the board first.

## Tests

Not run, by request: no tests, typecheck, lint, build or app launch. Edited by reading:
- `SessionsBoard.test.tsx`: the board renders with `ArchiveModalHost` beside it, as the shell does. A new test opens it from a bare request with no board (prefilled query, Esc closes, focus returns to the opener, no navigation). The two "restore finishes after leaving the board" tests now close the modal instead.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx`: the menu's Archive sets `archiveModal` for the project and doesn't navigate.
- `CommandPalette.test.tsx`: new test that Open archive opens the modal, closes the palette and doesn't navigate.
- `SessionsBoard.remote.test.tsx`: its store mock is now a small real store with `openArchive`, and the shell's host renders beside the board, so the remote restore test goes through the shared modal.
- New: closing on a page change drops a running restore (search-only changes don't close it); focus returns to the opener; `useAppShortcut.test.tsx` covers session shortcuts standing down under the archive.
- `e2e/window-transparency-overlap.spec.ts` opens the archive from the board button inside the real shell, so it needs no change.

## Please check by hand

1. On a session chat, open the sidebar ⋮ on a project with archived sessions → Archive. The modal opens over the chat with the URL unchanged. Esc returns you to the same scroll position with focus on the ⋮ button.
2. Same from right-click on the row, and from the collapsed icon rail (right-click the project icon). Focus should return to the row.
3. From Artifacts and Settings: the modal opens over them, and closing leaves the page as it was.
4. Cmd+K → Open archive from a session: the palette closes, the archive opens, and Esc puts the caret back in the composer.
5. Enter or a click on a card opens that session and closes the modal. ⌘↵ restores and opens it. Delete still asks for confirmation.
6. A remote-host project's menu → Archive, with the host online and offline.

## Risks

- Focus return from the sidebar menu and Cmd+K wasn't checked by hand; the test covers the hand-back itself.

title: fix(artifacts): size section headers as section headings, not page titles
body:
Code changes: +3 -1  
Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Artifacts page section headers (Recent, Pinned, each project, Scratchpad) now use the same type as a Settings section heading instead of the page title's type.

## Why

Team feedback (Aditi): the type sizes on the Artifacts page looked inconsistent. The scope tabs (All | On this machine | Cloud) were small, the section headers were much larger and bolder, and the page title was a third size.

In the code, `ArtifactSection` copied `topbarTitleClass` almost exactly (`text-brand font-semibold tracking-tight leading-none`, 16px/600). So every section header was as large as the page title and well above the 12px tabs next to it. No other page uses `text-brand` outside the topbar. The rest of the app keeps 16px/600 for the route title only:

| Element | Where | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page title | `PageTopbarTitle` (all pages) | 16px / 600 / tight |
| Section heading | Settings `SettingsSection` | 14px / 500 / 20px leading |
| Project rows | Sidebar | 14px / 500, 14px icons |
| Section heading | Automations "Templates" | 13px / 500 |
| Scope tabs | `Button size="sm"` (Artifacts, Usage, Automations) | 14px / 400 as rendered (see note below) |
| Card title | `ArtifactGalleryCard`, list rows | 13px / 500 |

DESIGN.md: "500 medium for controls and small hierarchy; 600 only for headings, selected values, and genuinely primary emphasis", and 21–22px is reserved for "route-level title only". A collapsible group label is small hierarchy, not a page heading.

## Before / After

title: fix(styles): let text and font utilities apply to buttons and inputs
body:
Code changes: +4 -6  
Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Removes the unlayered `button, input, textarea, select { font: inherit; }` rule from `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`. Font-size, weight and line-height classes on buttons, inputs, textareas and selects now apply.

## Why

Found while checking #8135 (Artifacts type scale) in the dev app. The Artifacts scope tabs are `Button size="sm"`, which asks for `text-xs` (12px), but they rendered at 14px/400. CDP matched styles on the "All" tab showed three rules:

| Rule | Layer | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tailwind preflight `button, input, select, optgroup, textarea, ::file-selector-button { font: inherit }` | `base` | overridden by utilities (intended) |
| `.text-xs { font-size: var(--font-size-sm) }` | `utilities` | should win |
| `button, input, textarea, select { font: inherit }` in `styles.css` (since #3518) | none | **wins**, because unlayered CSS beats every layer |

So every Button, Input, Select and raw form control has silently ignored its `text-*`, `font-*` and `leading-*` classes, and the `font` shorthand reset size, weight and line height to the parent's values. Preflight already provides the same inherit default inside `@layer base`, so this copy is redundant except for blocking utilities. Elements with no type classes keep inheriting exactly as before.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `Button size="sm"` / `size="xs"` render at the parent's size (14px in most pages) | 12px (`text-xs`), as the Button primitive defines |
| Default `Button` inherits the parent's size and weight (e.g. 12px inside a `text-xs` container, 500 inside `font-medium`) | 14px / 400 (`text-sm font-normal`), as the primitive defines |
| Per-call `className` type classes on Button, Pressable, Input, Select and raw controls (`text-control`, `font-medium`, `text-caption` …) are ignored | They apply |
| Elements without type classes inherit the parent's font | Unchanged |

No screenshots: not run locally. Please capture before and after by hand (see Testing).

## How

One rule deleted, with a comment saying why it must not come back. Scope by grep (single-line JSX only, so a floor): about 151 `size="sm"`/`"xs"` Buttons in 62 files, plus a few dozen per-call type classes on Button/Pressable and raw controls.

## Risk

This is an app-wide visual change: every compact button gets smaller, and some controls whose authors set a size or weight that never applied will now look as written. Some of those classes may have been tuned against the wrong rendered size and could look off. Those are follow-up fixes at each call site. Re-adding the global override would hide them again.

## Testing

No tests, typecheck, lint or builds run locally (author's standing rule); CI will run them. No test asserts this rule. Please check by hand in dark and light:

1. Artifacts, Usage, Automations: the scope/filter tab rows (All, On this machine, Cloud …) are now 12px, still vertically centered in their 28px pills, and the selected pill looks right.

5. Sidebar, top bar, session tabs and the tab ⋮ menu: no label, icon or badge shifts or truncates.
6. Board cards, archive modal and Cmd+K: buttons and the search input.
7. Anywhere a compact button now looks too small for its row: note it as a call-site follow-up.

title: feat(mobile): start New task in the project last worked in
body:
Code changes: +64 -7\
Tests: +99 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The mobile New task screen now opens with the project you last worked in on that machine already picked.

## Why

New task only fell back to the board's project filter. With the board on "All projects" (the usual state), it showed "Choose project" every time, unless the machine had exactly one project.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Board on All projects → New task shows "Choose project" | New task shows the project last used on that machine |

## How

- New `lib/lastProject.ts` keeps one project id per machine in AsyncStorage, with an in-memory cache. `useLastProject(hostId)` reports `loaded: false` until the stored value has been read.
- A project counts as used when you start a task in it, open its project page, open one of its sessions, or pick it in the PR list's project filter. The Workers board's own filter is already passed to New task as the routed project, so it still wins.
- `resolveSpawnProject` takes the last project as a new fallback. Order: routed project (project page or filtered Workers board) → last project used → saved project filter → sole project.
- A remembered project the daemon no longer lists is skipped. Before the list arrives it's trusted the same way the saved filter is, then checked once the list lands.
- Sessions whose project was removed don't overwrite the remembered project.
- The spawn screen waits for the stored value before seeding. Otherwise the board filter could be picked first and stick.
- Standalone sessions carry no project, so they never overwrite the stored one.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation (`mobile.yml` typecheck + vitest).

- `lib/projectFilter.test.ts`: order of the fallbacks, skipping a deleted last project, and the last project winning before the project list is known.
- `lib/lastProject.test.tsx`: not loaded before the read, separate per machine, live update, a remember during the initial read wins.

Not tried on a device yet. To check it: with the board on All projects, open a session in project X, go back, tap New task, and X should be selected.

title: fix(terminal): send clicks to programs that track the mouse
body:
## Summary

AO's terminal never lets a click or drag reach the program running inside it, even when that program has asked for the mouse (DECSET 1000/1002/1003). One visible symptom: the close (×) on Claude Code's right-hand panel does nothing in AO.

**Culprit:** https://github.com/aoagents/ReverbCode/pull/372 ("fix: add terminal controls and restore copy/scroll", merged 2026-06-21). It reached this repo through #2166, as commit `7ba860741c`. It replaced xterm's `shouldForceSelection` with `() => true` and removed `enable-mouse-events`, so every press became a text selection. At the time, every session ran under zellij (later tmux) with mouse mode on. That override is the most likely way that PR got drag-to-copy back, but neither the PR nor the code says so. New macOS/Linux sessions now run on the native PTY host, and agent TUIs use the mouse. Claude Code has enabled mouse tracking since 2.1.150.

## What changes

- **Clicks and drags go to a program that tracks the mouse**, the way iTerm2, Ghostty, VS Code, Orca and Paradev handle it (Paradev made the same change for Codex in its PR #8361).
  - Mouse reports are forwarded only when they are a complete SGR or 7-bit X10 report produced while a real DOM mouse event is being dispatched. The rule against forwarding raw `onData` stays in place for everything else.
  - Wheel reports from xterm are dropped. AO keeps synthesizing its own, and the wheel handler is unchanged.
- **Option-drag (macOS) or Shift-drag (Windows/Linux) always selects text.** These are `macOptionClickForcesSelection` and xterm's built-in rule. Alt stays column selection off macOS.
- **Some presses always stay with AO:**
  - Right and middle presses, so the context menu is unchanged and tmux's own right-click menu can't appear.
  - Presses on a hovered link (web, OSC 8 or `ao:`), so links open exactly as today.
- **New setting, Settings → General → "Terminal clicks": Send to app (default) / Always select text.** "Always select text" installs the old override unchanged. The setting is also in the command palette and translated into all 9 locales.
- **A one-time hint the first time a drag goes to a program:** "Hold ⌥ Option and drag to select text" ("Hold Shift…" off macOS). It uses the existing in-terminal notice style plus `CloseButton`, is dismissible, and the flag is stored in localStorage.
- **tmux:** a plain drag goes to tmux, which routes it itself. It goes to the inner program if that program wants the mouse; otherwise tmux enters copy-mode. When the copy-mode selection ends, tmux emits OSC 52.
  - AO honours **OSC 52 writes only**, only within 1.5 s of a gesture this terminal sent to the program, only when "Copy on select" is on, and never during replay.
  - Clipboard reads are never answered.
  - Option-drag in tmux uses today's xterm selection path.
- **Copy on select** no longer re-copies a stale selection when the gesture went to the program.

## Testing

- New `lib/terminal-mouse.test.ts`. The new "mouse routing" block in `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` covers:
  - which modifiers, buttons and links stay local;
  - that "Always select text" installs the old override;
  - a live setting switch;
  - report forwarding and its gating;
  - OSC 52 write/query/gesture/copy-on-select gating;
  - no stale re-copy;
  - the one-time hint.
- Three existing copy-on-select tests now set `mouseTrackingMode = "none"`, because they model a shell selection drag.
- After rebasing on `main`: the XtermTerminal, terminal-mouse, i18n (including renderer coverage), settings, stores and useTerminalSession suites ran; 64 files and 1,014 tests passed. `tsc` reports no errors in `frontend/src`.
- **Real Electron app**, isolated data and profile, driven with real CDP mouse events. A mouse-tracking fixture TUI stood in for Claude Code, which was not run because it would use live credentials. Each case below was checked against the fixture's log of mouse reports, xterm's state, the clipboard, or tmux's buffer and mode:
  - plain click on the fixture's close control → it closed;
  - plain drag → reports reached the app, no selection, hint shown once;
  - Option-drag → selected and copied, app got nothing;
  - right-click → AO menu, app got nothing;
  - wheel → AO's synthesized 64/65 reports, no duplicates;
  - plain drag in a shell → selects and copies as before;
  - "Always select text" → today's behaviour;
  - tmux plain drag → copy-mode → OSC 52 → system clipboard;
  - tmux Option-drag → xterm selection, tmux untouched;
  - tmux with the fixture inside → the click was forwarded and the panel closed.
- Wheel in the lab used page-dispatched `WheelEvent`s; it matched the parent commit's behaviour A/B.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Habit change:** a plain drag over an agent TUI now drives the agent's own selection. The hint and setting soften this.
- **Still relies on a private xterm API:** `_selectionService.shouldForceSelection`, the same seam as before.
- **X10 reports beyond column/row 95 are dropped**, because AO's input path is text-only. tmux and current agent TUIs use SGR.
- **Not verified in the lab:** real trackpad wheel, real Claude Code, Windows/Linux, and AO-runtime-created legacy tmux sessions (approximated by tmux inside a shell tab).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* **New Features**
  * Choose whether terminal clicks are sent to the active application or select text by default.
  * When an application handles mouse input, hold Option on macOS or Shift on other platforms to select text. A dismissible hint appears after a program-directed drag.
  * Terminal links remain clickable without routing their clicks to the application. Eligible clipboard writes from terminal applications can be copied after a program-directed gesture when copy-on-select is enabled.
