title: perf(terminal): drop redundant output copy and reuse encode buffer
body:
Code changes: +29 -5 Tests: +47 -0 Others: +70 -0 (docs asset) ## What this changes Two allocation costs in the terminal output path (`internal/terminal`), both paid once per queued output frame per attached client. **1. Every PTY byte was copied twice.** `outQueue.push` ran `append([]byte(nil), msg.raw...)` before queueing. The only producer of `raw` is the attachment read loop, which allocates a fresh chunk per read and never reuses it, so that copy bought nothing. The queue now takes ownership of the slice, and the contract is documented on `serverMsg.raw` and `push`. **2. The base64 scratch buffer was reallocated per frame.** `drain` called `base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString`, which allocates the encoded buffer for every frame, for every attached client. It now encodes into a pooled buffer and allocates only the returned string. The pool is bounded at 512 KiB, so a one-off oversized frame cannot pin memory. Net effect on a 32 KiB frame: **5 allocations / ~164 KB → 3 allocations / ~83 KB.** Behaviour is unchanged: same frames, same merge limits, same error paths. Only the allocation strategy moved. ## Proof ![Terminal output frame cost before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ApexYash11/agent-orchestrator/7d519f93b643aa27cf7deb7cc51c7d36cf1cf66e/docs/assets/pr-8142-terminal-frame-cost.svg) ### Result | Benchmark | Time (ns/op) | Allocated (B/op) | Allocs/op | |---|---|---|---| | 4 KiB frame | 23,315 → 16,693 (**−28.4%**) | 20,625 → 10,424 (**−49.5%**) | 5 → 3 | | 32 KiB frame | 160,186 → 128,096 (**−20.0%**) | 163,987 → 82,701 (**−49.6%**) | 5 → 3 | | 256 KiB frame | 1,129,626 → 926,637 (**−18.0%**) | 1,228,966 → 632,530 (**−48.5%**) | 5 → 3 | | Burst: 32 × 1 KiB, merged into one frame | 214,485 → 194,551 (**−9.3%**) | 277,145 → 228,534 (**−17.5%**) | 45 → 43 | Medians of 5 runs. Windows amd64, i5-1240P. Both halves measured on the same machine against the same base commit (`4511197a11`), switching only the two source files. ### What is being measured - `BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame` walks one frame end to end: producer chunk → `push` → `drain` (base64 encode). Sizes 4 KiB, 32 KiB and 256 KiB cover a keypress-sized write, a typical read, and the merge ceiling. - `BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst` reproduces the real flood shape: 32 × 1 KiB chunks queued behind a single writer wake, which merge into one frame — the case where a chatty agent streams a lot of small reads. ```bash go test ./internal/terminal/ -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkOutQueue -benchmem ``` ### Where the bytes went A 32 KiB frame used to allocate: the producer chunk (32 KiB), the `push` copy (32 KiB), the `EncodeToString` buffer (~43 KiB) and the returned string (~43 KiB). Now it allocates the producer chunk and the returned string only — the encode buffer comes from the pool. The 256 KiB row shows the same shape at the merge ceiling, where per-frame cost matters most: half a megabyte of garbage removed per frame. ### Raw output
before — canonical/main ```text BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 166495 7273 ns/op 563.16 MB/s 20624 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 168469 22128 ns/op 185.11 MB/s 20625 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 54074 23598 ns/op 173.57 MB/s 20624 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 49701 23315 ns/op 175.68 MB/s 20625 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 59593 24237 ns/op 169.00 MB/s 20625 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 7428 162439 ns/op 201.72 MB/s 163987 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 8600 156881 ns/op 208.87 MB/s 163987 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 7760 162569 ns/op 201.56 MB/s 163987 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 7018 153103 ns/op 214.03 MB/s 163987 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 7195 160186 ns/op 204.56 MB/s 163987 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 998 1074325 ns/op 244.01 MB/s 1228962 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 970 1173932 ns/op 223.30 MB/s 1228992 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 937 1129626 ns/op 232.06 MB/s 1228956 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 1213 1173487 ns/op 223.39 MB/s 1228993 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 1164 1108445 ns/op 236.50 MB/s 1228966 B/op 5 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 6294 228484 ns/op 143.42 MB/s 277145 B/op 45 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 5144 212845 ns/op 153.95 MB/s 277144 B/op 45 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 5269 214485 ns/op 152.78 MB/s 277143 B/op 45 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 4899 213031 ns/op 153.82 MB/s 277145 B/op 45 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 5044 215667 ns/op 151.94 MB/s 277146 B/op 45 allocs/op ```
after — this branch ```text BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 214959 6169 ns/op 663.97 MB/s 10428 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 130504 16640 ns/op 246.16 MB/s 10422 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 68539 16571 ns/op 247.18 MB/s 10428 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 69891 16693 ns/op 245.38 MB/s 10423 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/4KiB-16 66109 16978 ns/op 241.25 MB/s 10424 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 10000 129440 ns/op 253.15 MB/s 82747 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 10000 129223 ns/op 253.58 MB/s 82814 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 10000 125889 ns/op 260.29 MB/s 82663 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 10000 128096 ns/op 255.81 MB/s 82701 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/32KiB-16 10000 124097 ns/op 264.05 MB/s 82643 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 1221 932060 ns/op 281.25 MB/s 637868 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 1280 991960 ns/op 264.27 MB/s 643291 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 1201 925788 ns/op 283.16 MB/s 632530 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 1262 924856 ns/op 283.44 MB/s 631429 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueDataFrame/256KiB-16 1332 926637 ns/op 282.90 MB/s 630713 B/op 3 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 7029 190476 ns/op 172.03 MB/s 228676 B/op 43 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 6034 205899 ns/op 159.15 MB/s 228648 B/op 43 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 5964 194551 ns/op 168.43 MB/s 228975 B/op 43 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 6447 183469 ns/op 178.60 MB/s 228310 B/op 43 allocs/op BenchmarkOutQueueMergedBurst-16 5881 195717 ns/op 167.43 MB/s 228534 B/op 43 allocs/op ```
### Why it matters here Base64 encoding runs once per merged frame per attached client, on the daemon's hottest path. Halving the bytes allocated per frame halves the GC pressure that a streaming terminal session generates, and the saving scales with output volume. Small reads are common on Windows ConPTY, so the per-frame cost is paid more often there. ### Verification - `go build ./internal/terminal/` — clean - `go vet ./internal/terminal/` — clean - `go test ./internal/terminal/ -count=1` — pass - `go test -race ./internal/terminal/ -count=1` — pass - `gofmt -l internal/terminal/` — clean The existing queue tests (merge limits, drop/room behaviour, ordering) are unchanged and still pass, which is the check that this is an allocation change and not a behaviour change. Addresses #8106. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Terminal output is processed more efficiently, particularly during bursts of activity. Reduced copying and temporary memory use can help keep terminal sessions responsive. * **Tests** * Added benchmarks for processing individual terminal frames and bursts of output to track performance across different workloads.

title: test: keep the enclosing AO session's environment out of backend tests
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +121 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Backend tests now ignore the environment of the AO worker session they run in. A new `internal/testenv` package unsets the session variables, and a three-line `TestMain` in five packages calls it.

## Why

AO starts every worker with `AO_SESSION_ID`, `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME`, `AO_TMUX_BINARY` and similar variables, and Claude Code adds `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`. Product code reads them, so `go test ./...` run from a worker used the worker's own tmux socket, session id and Claude process kind, and failed 67 tests that pass in CI. `AGENTS.md` asks agents to run the full suite before a PR, so every agent working on this repo from AO saw failures it did not cause.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `go test ./...` from an AO worker: 67 failures in `runtime/tmux` (54), `systemcheck` (5), `session_manager` (4), `cli` (3), `integration` (1) | 0 failures in those packages |
| `tmux_test.go:379: call[0] = "-L", want new-session` | pass |

No user-visible change: test-only.

title: fix(commandcode): resolve symlinks when rebasing gitdir conditional includes
body:
Code changes: +16 -6\
Tests: +46 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

In a Command Code session, `[includeIf "gitdir:./"]` and `[includeIf "gitdir:~/..."]` keep matching when the git config file or `$HOME` is behind a symlink.

## Why

A Command Code session runs with its own `HOME`, so AO copies the user's git config and rewrites these conditions to absolute paths. Git resolves symlinks before it expands `./` and `~/`; AO used the paths as written. With a `~/.gitconfig` symlinked into a dotfiles repository, or a home directory behind a symlink, the rewritten condition never matched, and the agent committed without the included `user.email` or signing settings.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `HOME` behind a symlink, `user.email` set through `[includeIf "gitdir:./"]`: `git config user.email` in a session repo prints nothing | Prints the included email, as git does outside the session |
| `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders` fails on macOS, where temp dirs are under the `/var` symlink | Passes |

## How

- `anchorCondition` resolves the config file's path and the real `HOME` with `filepath.EvalSymlinks`, falling back to the path unchanged.
- Include paths (`path = ...`) still expand from the unresolved directory, which is what git does.
- One assertion in the existing test now expects the resolved home path in the rewritten condition.

## Testing

- New `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludesBehindSymlinkedHome` puts `HOME` behind a symlink. Without the fix it fails both on macOS and with a symlink-free temp directory (as on Linux CI); with the fix it passes.
- Same setup with plain git outside AO: git matches both includes through the symlink.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/commandcode/`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 (darwin, linux): pass.

## What

Revamps the Artifacts page:

- **One list, newest first.** No Recent, per-project or Scratchpad sections, so nothing is listed twice. Pinned artifacts stay on top of the same list with a small pin mark.
- **Every row says project · session**, so an orchestrator's artifact reads `ao · Orchestrator` instead of only `Orchestrator`.
- **Published artifacts are marked**: a green globe before the time, in list and gallery (tooltip "Published").
- **The ⋯ menu follows the publish state**: Publish (share icon) for an unshared artifact; Copy public link and Unpublish once it is published.
- **Filters take several values at once** and the menu stays open while picking; a new **Sharing** filter (Public, Not shared, All). One chip per filter.
- **Hover**: a clearly visible row surface, the time reads "Updated 14h ago", and Pin / Open in session / ⋯ sit after the time in space that is kept for them, so nothing moves.
- **Narrow panels keep the time visible**; names and context truncate instead.
- HTML files get a file-code icon instead of the globe, and the publish panel's Unpublish button is no longer clipped.

## Why

- Published artifacts were indistinguishable from unshared ones, and the ⋯ menu offered Publish on files that were already published. The cause: `toSessionArtifact` in `useWorkspaceQuery` dropped the `shareUrl` the daemon already sends (#7966).
- The sectioned page listed the newest artifacts twice and split the rest by project, which the Project filter already does.

title: fix(scm): treat a gate job that failed in a cancelled run as cancelled
body:
Code changes: +23 -3\
Tests: +130 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A gate job (such as `build-test`) that failed only because its workflow run was cancelled is now reported as cancelled, not failed. AO no longer tells the worker "CI is failing" for it.

## Why

Fixes #7823 (part 2; part 1, cancelled checks counting as failing, was fixed in #8000).

Gate jobs use `needs:` + `if: always()` and fail when the jobs they need were cancelled (`test 'cancelled' = success`). When a newer push or a PR edit cancels a run with cancel-in-progress, the gate's check run ends `FAILURE`, but its check suite ends `CANCELLED`. Until the replacement run's gate reports, that stale gate is the newest `build-test` on the commit, so `latestCheckRuns` (#7831) keeps it and AO sends a CI-failure nudge for a failure that never happened.

## Before / After

Live data for the #7823 repro (head `d158767081` of #7822). The Go replacement run (42028174717) is left out to recreate the moment the nudge fired. Both sides run AO's own `scmObservationFromGraphQL` on the real `statusCheckRollup`, fetched with each branch's query, in a throwaway test that is not committed.

| Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| `build-test`: conclusion `FAILURE`, suite not requested → `failed` | `build-test`: conclusion `FAILURE`, suite `CANCELLED` → `cancelled` |
| CI summary `failing`, failed checks `[build-test]` → CI-failure nudge | CI summary `unknown` (`pending` while the replacement is queued), failed checks `[]` → no nudge |

## How

- `checkRunFields` also asks for `checkSuite{ conclusion }`. It sits next to the existing `workflowRun` selection and only needs checks read access, not Actions access.
- `checkStatusFromGraphQL` maps a `FAILURE` whose check suite concluded `CANCELLED` to `PRCheckCancelled`. Everything downstream (`ciSummaryFromGraphQL`, the observer's `scmCISummary`, `FailedChecks`, the failed fingerprint) already handles cancelled checks after #8000, so nothing else changes.
- Kept narrow on purpose:
  - Only `FAILURE` is reinterpreted. `TIMED_OUT`, `STARTUP_FAILURE` and `ACTION_REQUIRED` in a cancelled run still count as failures.
  - A failure in a suite that is still running (conclusion `null`) or that ended `FAILURE` still counts.
  - A check run without a readable suite keeps today's behavior.
- Trade-off: if a job really failed and someone then cancelled the run by hand, the suite ends `CANCELLED` and the failure is no longer nudged. That matches the issue's expected behavior: a cancelled run is replaced or settled on purpose, and a real failure comes back in the next run.
- The check's raw `conclusion` (`failure`) is still passed through unchanged for display. Only the derived status changes.
- GitLab is not affected. Its part-1 behavior was fixed in #8000, and GitLab has no failing-gate pattern for cancelled pipelines.

## Testing

- New `TestCISummaryGateFailureInCancelledSuiteIsNotAFailure` (6 cases: replacement still running → `pending`; no replacement → `unknown`; real failure in a failed suite; failure while the suite is still running; no readable suite; `TIMED_OUT` in a cancelled suite). The two bug cases fail on `main` and pass here.

title: fix(chat): copy and save images from remote-host chats
body: ## Summary **Copy image** and **Save image** fail in chats on a remote host. Both show `Error invoking remote method 'chatImage:fetch': Error: Image request failed (403)`. **Cause:** copy and save fetched every http(s) chat image in the main process with `session.fetch`. That request sends `Sec-Fetch-Site` but no `Origin`, so the remote-host proxy's `validControlOrigin` (`frontend/src/main/remote-proxy.ts`) answers 403. The `` itself loads fine because `ChatImage` loads loopback URLs with `crossOrigin="anonymous"`, which sends `Origin: app://renderer`. **Fix:** `loadChatImage` now reads loopback images (`127.0.0.1`, `*.localhost`: the local daemon and remote-host proxies) with the renderer's own `fetch`. This is the same CORS request the `` already makes, and `connect-src` already allows those origins. It uses the existing `mediaCrossOrigin` helper to decide. Other http(s) images still go through `chatImage:fetch` in the main process. ## Evidence Real two-daemon lab: desktop A (this branch, `electron-forge start`) is paired with remote host B through the remote-host proxy. A synthetic PNG was sent in B's chat. The thumbnail is served from `http://127.0.0.1://api/v1/sessions/repo-1/preview/files/.ao/attachments/….png`. Both takes use the same window, chat and image. The driver checked which `chat-image-actions.ts` Vite was serving before each take: `origin/main` was swapped in for Before. Copy was checked on the real macOS clipboard (`osascript -e 'clipboard info'`). The save dialog was stubbed to a temp path. | | Copy image | Save image | |---|---|---| | Before (`origin/main`) | 403 toast, clipboard empty | 403 toast, no file | | After (this PR) | no toast, PNG on clipboard (69,585 bytes) | 140,644-byte 480×270 PNG written | ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/1ee8a73c25856453a17b4788fd72c68ffbd5417e/f4003698/before.png) ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/1ee8a73c25856453a17b4788fd72c68ffbd5417e/f4003698/after.png) ## Tests - `ChatImage.test.tsx`: the loopback copy and save cases now assert that the renderer `fetch` is used and `chatImage:fetch` is not. A new case covers an external `https:` image still going through the main process. - Not run locally; CI is the gate. ## Risks - The renderer path skips the main process's 64 MB size cap. This only affects loopback images, which come from our own daemon or a paired host. `data:`/`blob:` images already skipped the cap. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved handling of chat images from loopback addresses, including rejecting responses that aren’t identified as images or exceed the 64 MiB limit. * Copy and save actions use the appropriate access method for loopback and external HTTP(S) images, as well as `data:` and `blob:` images. * Image content types are normalized before use.

title: fix(prompt): tell agents the user's local time zone
body:
## Summary

Agents repeated UTC timestamps from GitHub word for word ("merged at 07:52 UTC") because nothing in their context named the user's time zone. Claude Code's system prompt gives only the date, and AO's prompt gave nothing.

Every agent prompt (worker, orchestrator, standalone) now ends with a short **Time Zone** section, placed before the confidentiality guard. It names the user's zone, asks for times in that zone, and notes that API timestamps are UTC and need converting.

### Where the zone comes from

1. **The desktop app reports it.** The renderer sends `X-AO-Client-Time-Zone` (from `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`) on write requests to the local daemon and to remote hosts. Only writes carry it: spawns are POSTs, and a custom header on polling GETs would add a CORS preflight per URL. The daemon (`internal/clienttz`) keeps the latest valid report in `<dataDir>/client-time-zone`, so CLI/orchestrator spawns and daemon restarts still use it. This is what makes remote hosts correct.
2. **Fallback, when no client has reported a zone** (CLI-only use): the machine's zone, from `TZ` (name or `…/zoneinfo/…` path), the `/etc/localtime` link, or `/etc/timezone`. UTC aliases (`UTC`, `Etc/*`, `GMT`…) are treated as unknown here, because servers, cloud sandboxes and CI default to them.
3. If neither gives a zone, the section is left out and the prompt is unchanged from today.

## Testing

- Go: `clienttz` (persisting, invalid/traversal names ignored, restart keeps the value), httpd middleware, zone fallback (TZ name/path, macOS/Linux links, `/etc/timezone`, UTC aliases), client report beating the machine zone, and the section in worker and orchestrator prompts.
- Frontend: writes to local and remote daemons carry the header; GETs don't.
- Live lookup on macOS gives `Asia/Kolkata`, and 12 other `TZ` values resolve correctly.
- Headless `claude -p` with the section, 9 zones (Kolkata, LA, New York, St John's, Kathmandu, Chatham, Kiritimati, London, Sydney) × 2 timestamps, one on a US DST change day: 18/18 matched Python zoneinfo. Without the section, the same question gets UTC answers.

## Known limits

- Several desktops in different zones sharing one remote host: the last one to report wins.
- Mobile doesn't send the header yet, so sessions spawned only from the phone use the last desktop report or the host zone.
- Only sessions spawned after this ships get the section.

title: fix(chat): stop showing Orchestrator's CLI in agent narration and step rows
body:
Code changes: +233 -32\
Tests: +94 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Agents in chat stop putting Orchestrator's own CLI in front of the user.

- **Prompt:** agents still narrate each step in a short, friendly sentence. When a step uses an `ao` command, they describe what it does ("Opening the page in the Browser panel", "Saving the page as a deliverable") instead of naming the command, its flags or output. Reading the `ao` guides and `--help` gets no narration.
- **Chat rows:** `ao` commands are named for what they do, the way `gh` commands already are, instead of "Ran ao". For example: "Previewed hello.html", "Interacted with the page", "Checked the browser console for Button clicked", "Saved deliverable hello.html", "Shared progress".
- **Plumbing hidden:** reads of Orchestrator's own guide files and `ao … --help` lookups no longer appear in the timeline.
- **Repeats folded:** back-to-back command rows with the same label that all finished collapse into one row. Opening it still shows every call's command and output.

## Why

The CLI is internal plumbing. Users saw narration like "ao preview exits 0 but prints nothing, so I'll wait…", rows reading "Ran ao", three "Read SKILL.md / browser.md / preview.md" rows with the guide text inside, and the same row twice in a row.

## Before / After

Same task in an isolated dev app, both runs on Sonnet 5.5: make `hello.html`, open it in the Browser panel, click its button, check the console, save it as a deliverable.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Read 3 files: `SKILL.md`, `browser.md`, `preview.md` | *(hidden)* |
| "I'll write the page straight into the artifacts directory, since it's the deliverable, and open it from there." | "Writing hello.html straight into the artifacts directory, since it's the deliverable." |
| Ran ao | Interacted with the page |
| Ran ao | Checked the browser console for Button clicked |
| Ran ao · Ran ao (two console reads in a row) | Checked the browser console (one row, opens onto both calls) |
| Ran ao | Saved deliverable hello.html |
| Earlier run: "ao preview exits 0 but prints nothing, so I'll wait a moment and check what the browser is showing." | No `ao` commands, flags or output named in narration |

## How

- `backend/internal/session_manager/prompt.go`: `userOrientationPrompt` keeps the sentence-per-step rule (#6996) and adds the plain-terms rule for `ao` steps. It applies to worker, standalone worker and orchestrator prompts.
- `activity-step.ts`: `aoStep` maps `ao` subcommands to plain steps. Read-only `ao` calls (console, errors, snapshot, wait, `ls`/`get`) count as observers, so a chain like `ao preview … && ao browser wait && ao browser act …` is named by the step that acts. A `grep`/`rg` stage fed straight by `ao browser console`/`errors` becomes the row's target. `isOrchestratorPlumbing` spots guide reads (Read tool, `cat`/`sed`/…) and `ao --help`.
- `ChatWorkspace.tsx`: `readableItems` drops plumbing next to the existing usage/reasoning filters, so group counts leave it out too.
- `ActivityRun.tsx` / `ChatTimelineItems.tsx`: `renderActivityRows` folds back-to-back completed command rows with identical labels. Failed or running calls, and rows with nested agent steps, are never folded. The folded row opens onto every call's body.

Not covered here: `ao_action` rows (daemon-side outcomes) are unchanged. A read that mixes a guide with a user file still shows.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.

Manual: ran the flow above in an isolated dev app (separate data dir and port) on a daemon built from the old prompt and one built from the new prompt, then reloaded the renderer to check each row change on the recorded run.

New tests: `ActivityRun.fold.test.tsx` (folding, plus failed and in-between rows staying separate), `activity-step.test.ts` (`ao` labels, chain naming, grep target, `tab new` URL, plumbing detection), `prompt_test.go` (prompt wording).

title: fix(mobile): reconcile dictation revisions and await recognition locale
body:
Code changes: +279 -47\
Tests: +650 -13\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Replace overlapping iOS dictation revisions without duplicating phrases, preserve distinct timed utterances, and resolve the recognition locale before starting the native recognizer.

## Why

Fixes #8159. Transcript-prefix comparisons mistake revised opening words for new speech. Starting before locale initialization finishes can recognize the first phrase in en-US instead of the resolved device language.

## Before / After

| Before (mocked native events) | After (same events) |
| --- | --- |
| Revised openings such as `How the` → `How's the` → `How is the` accumulate into duplicated phrases | The current utterance is replaced |
| Distinct utterances or cumulative revisions can be confused by transcript similarity | Native audio spans distinguish closed utterances from overlapping revisions; intentional repeated speech remains |
| Native recognition starts before a deferred locale lookup completes | Native start waits for locale resolution; cancellation prevents late starts |

These are automated provider-level reproductions, not recordings from the reporter's iPhone. No visual layout changed. Actual iPhone microphone/UI validation remains outstanding.

## How

- Use native word timing spans with final-like boundary evidence on iOS; never deduplicate transcript text.
- Replace covered native word spans while preserving uncovered speech and verified original formatting.
- Keep a replacement session's locale lookup valid when an older canceled start times out; restore the later closed utterance after an earlier timed revision.
- Preserve Android segmentation and microphone permission behavior.
- Share locale initialization, bound failed/hung lookup waiting to two seconds, and prevent stale lookup answers or canceled sessions from starting recognition.

Follow-up `c3326baf036364c899fbf0023d0b9747438f6f2a` corrects all three reproduced automatic upstream review findings, with dedicated regressions and independent Codex verification.

Intentional limitation: when native timing metadata is absent/zero, there is no trustworthy new-utterance boundary. The provider does not guess one from words. If native word text cannot be mapped into its formatted transcript, a partially covered phrase is retained conservatively; duplicate-free partial reconciliation cannot be guaranteed for that ambiguous metadata. Long dictation with pauses on actual iOS versions still needs device validation. Locale lookup failure/timeout retains the existing en-US fallback and permits a later retry.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`: **passed**.

- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

title: fix(notifications): withdraw resolved approvals without hiding pending requests
body:
Code changes: +388 -21\
Tests: +539 -6\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Move resolved approval notifications out of mobile Needs attention while keeping history, and withdraw matching Electron notifications after authoritative resolution. Reconcile missed resolutions after reconnect, including rows on later history pages.

## Why

Fixes #8158. Unread history is not the same as an unresolved request. A successful resolution previously left the mobile row in active attention and had no path to close its desktop OS notification.

This is separate from the activity-hook work in #6280/#6427. Provider-first resolution, pending-conversation-request checks, and backend lifecycle/authorization code are unchanged.

## Before / After

| Before (automated event/cache/registry reproductions) | After |
| --- | --- |
| A resolved unread approval remains under Needs attention | It moves to history without changing its read state |
| A read but unresolved approval can leave active attention | It remains in Needs attention on daemons supporting resolution metadata |
| Electron notification objects are not retained for dismissal | An authoritative resolved event closes exactly the matching notification |
| Missed resolution, late created replay, or an older row outside the first history page can leave/reopen stale attention | Reconciliation uses resolved records and host-qualified identity; failed/missing data never proves resolution |

These are mocked provider/event tests, not an exact-device reproduction. Native macOS banner and iPhone captures remain outstanding; no modified application was installed or launched. Existing layouts are unchanged.

## How

- Preserve independent read and resolution axes, with compatibility for older mobile-connected daemons.
- Keep live Electron references until close/click/resolution; do not evict live references by count.
- Forward exact-ID dismissal through the existing preload bridge; remote IDs remain host-qualified.
- Preserve known read/resolved state against stale creates, and reconcile still-live IDs through paged authoritative history after missed events.
- Keep unknown/failed resolutions visible. No permission decisions are synthesized and no timer clears approval requests.

## Testing

- Full mobile suite: **367 files / 3,576 tests passed**.
- Mobile, frontend and E2E type checks: **passed**.
- Full frontend run with local fixture permissions: **735 files passed; 13,035 tests passed; 39 skipped; one unchanged startup suite hit its 10-second import-hook timeout**. No test assertion failed in that run.

- Focused acceptance covers resolution/failure, concurrent requests, replay, exact host/ID dismissal, >256 retained live notifications, paginated reconnect recovery, missing/failed history, and initial empty reconciliation.
- Independent Codex review: **approved for PR**, with the CI/device limitations below.

Initial broad verification exposed missing SQLite test bindings, a host-timezone-sensitive assertion, and an import timeout under high concurrency. Existing test dependency setup was corrected; final verification uses TZ=UTC and conservative workers. No unrelated production source changes were made.

body:

## What

Private artifact sharing in the desktop app, following the private-artifact-sharing plan and mockups:

- **Publish publishes, privately.** A cloud session's file (already on S3) publishes on the toolbar click as a private link ("Only you"), and the popover opens on the live link. A file on this computer opens on a setup step first (invite by email with **Add**, people show "Gets access when you publish", choose general access), and the popover's **Publish** uploads it with those settings.
- **Published popover:** email invite chips + **Invite** (gives access at once), **People with access** (owner + invited, plain **Can view**, × to remove, scrolls), **General access** menu (*Only people invited*, read as *Only you* with nobody invited / *Anyone with the link*), an inline note when a public link is made private, and only **Unpublish** and **Copy link** (copies the viewer URL). No link box, no Republish.
- **Toolbar:** *Publish* → *Publishing…* (spinner, no percentage) → *Published* with a lock or globe. When the file changed since publishing it splits into **Republish** (amber dot, hover hint) and a lock/globe ▾ that opens the popover without republishing.
- **Unpublish:** in-popover confirm naming the invitee count, *Unpublishing…* spinner, a short *Unpublished* state with **Publish**, and "Unpublishing failed: … The link still works."
- **Contract (additive):** `ArtifactShare.access`/`grantCount`, `ArtifactShareList.privateLinks`, `PATCH /me/artifact-shares/{id}`, grant list/add/remove routes, `POST /artifact-shares/{linkId}/view`, optional `access`/`emails` on finalize and session share. cloud-client regenerated.
- Contract: `PublicArtifactShare.you {owner, shareId, grantCount}`, returned by `viewArtifactShare` to the owner only, so the viewer page can offer Unpublish (ao-landing#145).
- IPC: `cloudShare:setAccess`, `cloudShare:grants`, `cloudShare:invite`, `cloudShare:removeGrant` (mutations main-frame only).

Related: control plane OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#91, viewer OrchestratorInc/ao-landing#145.

## Why

Every share link was public. People need to share an artifact with specific people, signed in, without the slug alone exposing the file.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Share opened a popover with a read-only public link box, "Public · anyone with the link can view" | Published popover: invite field, people with access, general access menu, Unpublish / Copy link |
| A file on this computer was uploaded on the toolbar click | It opens on a setup step; the popover's Publish uploads it with the chosen people and access |
| Toolbar said Publish or Republish | Publish → Publishing… → Published (lock/globe); split Republish ▾ when the file changed |

Screenshots of every popover state (rendered from this branch in a harness with a fake bridge) are attached to the AO session as `publish-popover-states.png`; I could not upload images from the sandbox, so please attach them here. No before captures were taken.

- **Compatibility, no feature flag:** access and emails are sent only when the control plane lists `privateLinks: true`. An older control plane (it rejects unknown fields) or one whose viewer has no sign-in keeps public links: no invite field, static "Anyone with the link".
- Republishing a credential to a **public** link still waits under its warning, with a Republish button there only. This is the one place the popover shows Republish, kept as a safety exception.

title: perf(desktop): stop launch waiting on the version floor fetch
body:
Code changes: +52 -25\
Tests: +39 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The desktop app no longer waits for the version floor check before it opens the window and starts the daemon. The check runs in the background.

## Why

Every packaged launch awaited a fetch of `desktop-version-floor.json` from GitHub (10 s timeout) at the top of `whenReady`, before the window or the daemon. The commit that added the check (#5206) says "The fetch is fire-and-forget ... so it never blocks startup on network issues", but the call was awaited. Both `min` and `latest` in the floor file are empty today, so every launch waits for a file that changes nothing.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Launch waits for the fetch: median 571 ms (551 to 861 ms, 5 fresh Node processes on one Mac), up to 10 s on a slow or offline network | No wait |
| With `latest` set, launch also waits until the user answers the "Update Available" dialog | The dialog appears while the app starts |

## How

- The check runs in the background once the main window exists, instead of awaiting it before anything starts; errors still log.
- Both dialogs attach to the main window (a sheet on macOS, modal on Windows), so they block the window behind them.
- A version below `min` still gets the blocking "Update Required" dialog, then quits through `desktopQuit.quitCompletely`: plain `app.quit()` leaves the app running in the macOS tray. Like `updates:relaunch`, this quit keeps running agents. The unsaved-draft guard still runs; if the user stays to keep a draft, the dialog shows again after 60 s.
- Trade-off: with `min` set, the window is usable for the length of the fetch (median 571 ms here) before the required-update dialog covers it. Blocking during the fetch would bring back the wait this PR removes; `min` is an emergency lever and is empty today.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`: pass.
- `desktop-version-floor.test.ts`: 13 pass, including new tests that the required-update dialog attaches to the window and quits through the given quit, that it asks again after a cancelled quit, and that the nudge falls back to no parent once the window is gone.
- The fetch time above was measured with Node's `fetch` against the same URL. Not run here: a packaged launch before and after, which needs a signed build.

title: perf(review): release reviewer agents that sit idle after a review
body:
Code changes: +91 -0\
Tests: +85 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The daemon releases a terminal reviewer's agent process once the reviewer has been idle for 30 minutes with no review running. The next review resumes the same conversation.

## Decision needed

The review found that a released terminal reviewer can't be reopened from the session view until the next review runs, and that an open session view isn't told the reviewer was released. Fixing both needs a "Reopen reviewer" action in the session view and a migration that adds a change trigger on `review`. Hold this PR until that scope is agreed.

## Why

A terminal reviewer keeps its agent process until its worker ends. On one Mac, two reviewers whose reviews finished 1 and 2 days earlier (`complete`, `approved`) held 433 MB and about 1% CPU each, measured with `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions/memory` (`app.reviewers`) and `ps` CPU time over 60 s.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Idle reviewer agents stay alive until the worker ends: 2 here, 433 MB, idle 1 and 2 days | A 5-minute sweep releases a reviewer idle for 30 minutes; both reviewers on that Mac qualify (`tui`, `idle`, no running pass) |

## How

- `Engine.ReleaseIdleReviewers` lists live reviewer handles (`ListLiveReviewerHandles`) and, under the worker's lock, releases one only if it is a terminal reviewer, its activity is `idle` or `exited`, `review.updated_at` is at least 30 minutes old, and none of its passes is running.
- Release is the same as `TeardownReviewerTerminal` for that harness: destroy the pane and clear the handle. The review row and native agent session id stay, so `Trigger` spawns and resumes the conversation on the next review. Until then the Reviewer tab is gone: the session view has no restore action for terminal reviewers (see Decision needed).
- Chat reviewers are skipped: `RecoverChatReviewers` would restart them at boot, and chat hibernation covers them.
- Left for review: the 30-minute limit, and whether to skip a reviewer whose terminal is open in the UI. The trade-off is a few seconds of agent start-up on the next review.

## Testing

- New `TestReleaseIdleReviewers` (7 cases: idle and exited past the limit, under the limit, active, waiting on a prompt, running pass, chat reviewer). It fails when the release step is disabled.
- `go test` for `internal/review`, `internal/service/review`, `internal/daemon`, `internal/httpd/controllers`, `internal/session_manager`: pass.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2, darwin and linux: 0 issues.

title: build(desktop): cut about 78 MB from the macOS app
body:
Code changes: +43 -2\
Tests: +63 -3\
Others: +0 -0

## On hold

Removing the 46 Chromium language packs changes behaviour for users whose Mac is in one of those languages. Checked with Electron 44.7.0 and `-AppleLanguages "(it)"`: `app.getLocale()` goes from `it` to `en-US`, the Browser panel's `Accept-Language` from `it` to `en-US,it`, and built-in text such as form validation switches to English. Parked until we decide which languages the app supports. The runtime and daemon parts (36 MB) do not depend on that decision.

## What

The macOS app drops about 78 MB of files it never uses at runtime: Chromium locales for languages the app has no UI for, type declarations, source maps and markdown in the bundled agent runtime, and the release daemon's debug symbols.

## Why

The installed app is 618 MB (0.14.11 nightly), up from 489 MB measured in October. Every update downloads the full zip on macOS (differential updates are disabled), so each MB is paid on every update.

## Before / After

Measured on the files themselves: the installed app for Before, this branch's build scripts (or the new prune run on a copy of the installed folders) for After.

| Part | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chromium `*.lproj` in Electron Framework | 220 folders, 73.6 MB | 36 folders (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt_BR, ru, zh_CN and their gendered variants), 31.4 MB |
| App bundle `Contents/Resources/*.lproj` | 55 folders | the same 9 languages |
| `acp-runtime/node_modules` | 50 MB | 28 MB |
| `daemon/ao` | 52.3 MB | 37.0 MB |

## How

- `pruneLocales` runs in `afterCopyExtraResources` before `labelMacBundle`, so before signing. It prunes the framework and the app bundle's own `Contents/Resources/*.lproj`: macOS picks the app's language from the bundle, and Chromium then loads that language's `locale.pak` with no fallback, so pruning only the framework would leave a Mac set to an unkept language with no strings. The kept set comes from `APP_LOCALES`. `Bundle.preferredLocalizations(from:forPreferences:)` with the pruned list resolves `it-IT` and `zh-Hant-TW` to `en`, `pt-PT` to `pt_BR`, and keeps `ja` and `fr`.
- `pruneRuntimePackages` deletes `*.d.ts`, `*.d.mts`, `*.d.cts`, `*.map` and `*.md` under `acp-runtime/node_modules` after `npm ci`, except `LICENSE*`, `LICENCE*`, `NOTICE*` and `COPYING*`: seven packages ship their license only as markdown. Nothing launches the adapter with `--enable-source-maps`. The helper is part of the runtime build signature, so cached runtimes rebuild.
- `build-daemon.mjs` adds `-trimpath` and `-s -w` for release builds only. Go panics and pprof still name functions; macOS `sample` and Instruments can't symbolize a stripped binary, which is why `--dev` builds keep the symbols.
- Windows and Linux locale `.pak` files are not touched here.

## Testing

- New tests: `pruneLocales` (keeps the app's languages and their variants in both folders, removes others) and `pruneRuntimePackages` (removes declarations, maps and docs; keeps code, a file named `map.js`, and license files).
- `forge.config.test.ts`, `build-acp-runtime-helpers.test.mjs`, `daemon-launch.test.ts`, `release-workflows.test.ts`: 87 pass. `node --test scripts/*.node-test.mjs`: 19 pass. `npm run typecheck`: pass.
- Built the runtime with `node scripts/build-acp-runtime.mjs`: the main packages import, and the Claude adapter answers an ACP `initialize` request.
- Built the release daemon with `node scripts/build-daemon.mjs`: `ao version` and `ao --help` run.
- Rebuilt the runtime after the license fix: still 28 MB; `LICENSE.md`/`license.md` of `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, `qs`, `jose`, `json-schema-typed`, `ms` and `express-rate-limit` are present.
- Not run here: a full signed `npm run make` and launching the packaged app with `-AppleLanguages "(it)"`.

title: perf(chat): hibernate idle chats for everyone, not only in Developer Mode
body:
Code changes: +4 -3\
Tests: +2 -2\
Others: +2 -2 (docs/architecture.md)

## What

The desktop turns chat hibernation on for every user, not only in Developer Mode.

## Decision needed

Hibernation is still being worked on (#8101 landed on 11 Nov). Merge this when its owners consider it ready for everyone; until then this draft records the change and the measured gain.

## Why

An idle Chat session keeps its agent, ACP runtime and chat host running: 4 processes, about 250 MB footprint for one Claude Code chat in the lab below. Hibernation stops them once the chat has been idle for 10 minutes with no open view, and wakes the conversation when the user opens the chat or sends work. Today that only happens in Developer Mode.

## Before / After

Dev app on one Mac (macOS, Apple Silicon), isolated data dir, Developer Mode off. One Claude Code chat per build, each asked "Reply with the single word ok.", then left with no view open. Memory is the macOS `footprint` of the session's processes from `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions/memory`; RSS is not used because it swung between 53 and 242 MB for the same idle processes under memory pressure. Before is `main` at `eb18768699`; after is the same commit plus this PR's change. One run each.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat hibernation with Developer Mode off | off | on |

title: perf(storage): drop payloads of provider events older than 7 days
body:
Code changes: +73 -0\
Tests: +67 -0\
Others: +63 -0 (generated sqlc)

## What

The daemon empties the payload of raw provider events older than 7 days. Every row stays.

## Decision needed

The code calls this archive "the only way to answer 'what did the provider actually say' once a projection turns out to be wrong". This PR trades that record for disk after 7 days. Owners decide whether that is acceptable, and the retention period (`providerEventPayloadRetention`).

## Why

`conversation_provider_events` is never cleaned up while its session exists. On one Mac it held 220 MB of a 316 MB database after 5 days (112,362 rows since 7 November), growing 6 to 56 MB of payload a day. By method: `activity.started` 78.5 MB, `activity.completed` 29.6 MB, `message.delta` 11.3 MB, `command.output.delta` 8.5 MB.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Payloads kept forever | Payloads older than 7 days become `{}`; `turn.completed` keeps its payload |
| A backup copy of that database: 315 MB | The same copy with events older than 2 days compacted and `VACUUM`ed: 198 MB. With 7 days nothing on that Mac qualifies yet, so the gain there is a cap on growth. |

## How

- Rows are kept on purpose: `ProjectProviderEvent` projects an event only when its insert adds a row, so the archive is also what stops a replayed event (for example on `session/load`) from being projected twice. Deleting rows would duplicate messages on replay.
- Readers checked on `main`: `SelectVerifiedAuthenticationTurn` reads `turn.completed` payloads (kept). `ProviderEventsSince` reads all payloads but has no production caller, only tests.
- Runs in the existing 10-minute cleanup loop. `received_at` has no index, so each step reads at most 500 `(id, received_at)` rows after a remembered `id` cursor on the read connection, stops at the first row newer than the cutoff, and updates that `id` range under the writer lock. Both are primary-key range searches (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`); one 500-row read takes 7 ms on the 316 MB database. The cursor resets on daemon restart, so the first pass after a restart walks the old rows once, in bounded steps.
- SQLite reuses the freed pages; the file shrinks only after a `VACUUM`, which this does not run.

## Testing

- New `TestCompactProviderEventPayloadsKeepsRowsForReplay`: walking one row per step, only the old non-`turn.completed` payload is emptied, the walk stops before the recent event and makes no progress on a second pass, and replaying the old event is still recognized as already seen.
- `go test` for `internal/storage/sqlite/...`, `internal/daemon`, `internal/service/chat`: pass.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2, darwin and linux: 0 issues. `npm run sqlc` output is committed.

title: fix(chat): settle a running turn when its controller stops
body:
Code changes: +86 -14\
Tests: +63 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When the agent controller is really stopped, a turn the daemon still marks `running` stops rendering as live. The "Working for…" spinner ends and the turn closes on a new **unknown** outcome: "The agent stopped before this turn finished". The reviewer chat pane also gets the Open shell lever that its stopped banner already promises.

## Why

Fixes #6064. A reviewer whose controller died mid-turn (harness crash, daemon restart, kill) became a zombie pane. The stopped banner showed, but the turn kept spinning forever, the composer was locked, and there was no Stop. Still reproducible on current `main`: `activeTurn()` and `groupByTurn()` never consulted controller state.

This also supersedes the frontend part of the closed #6073 with a narrower change.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Stopped banner **and** a "Working for Xm" spinner that never ends, over a dead controller | Stopped banner; the turn closes with "The agent stopped before this turn finished" (`data-turn-outcome="unknown"`), and the spinner is gone |
| Reviewer pane banner says "open a shell" but shows only Resume | Reviewer pane banner offers **Resume agent** and **Open shell** (a shell in the worker's worktree) |

No screenshots: I verified this with component tests. I haven't captured it in the Electron app yet.

## How

- **One "really stopped" signal.** `ChatWorkspace` now computes `controllerStopped` once. It is the exact condition that already gated `VersionSwitchBanner`'s `agentStopped`: `controller.state === "stopped"` and not `controllerTransitioning`, `agentResuming`, hibernate wake, `resumingAgent`, or `startupReconnecting`. So a handoff or wake, which briefly passes through `stopped`, never flashes a turn as dead. #6073 gated on raw `controller.state`, and its review raised exactly this asymmetry.
- `activeTurn(snapshot, { controllerStopped })` skips running turns under that flag. Queued turns still count, because Resume dispatches them. Both call sites (the workspace and the timeline) pass it.
- `groupByTurn(snapshot, { controllerStopped })` marks such a turn not live, clears the live provider-failure row, and sets `outcome: { state: "unknown" }`. It sets no `rollbackable`, because the daemon still holds the turn open and would refuse a rollback.
- `TurnOutcome` gains an `unknown` entry (muted, `CircleHelp`), so the turn doesn't wrongly read "interrupted by you".
- `canContinue` keeps using the raw active turn, so its behavior is unchanged.
- `ReviewerChatSurface` accepts `onOpenShell` / `openingShell` / `shellError`. `SessionView` passes the worker's `addShellTerminal`, the same lever the worker chat uses. It is dropped when the host is unreachable.

**Intentional omissions:** this is a presentation-layer settle. The daemon's turn row stays open until a resumed controller reconciles it. A durable server-side settle and a cancel for a still-alive reviewer harness are #3745 territory. The kill-under-auto-review and orphaned-pane backend changes from #6073 are out of scope here.

## Testing

- New: `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` checks that a running turn with a stopped controller shows no Working row or spinner, gets the unknown outcome, and offers no Stop turn or undo, while Resume and Open shell both work. A second test checks that the same snapshot with `controllerTransitioning` stays live.
- New: `ReviewerChatSurface.test.tsx` checks that the Open shell callback, busy state, and error are forwarded and that the lever is hidden when the host is unreachable.
- I confirmed the new settle test fails with the `groupByTurn` change reverted.
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat src/renderer/types src/renderer/components/SessionView`: 2364 passed, 3 failed. The 3 failures are scroll and focus tests in `ChatWorkspace` (find navigation) and the `IndependentSide*` files. They fail only in the parallel run; all 313 tests in those three files pass when run on their own.
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend): clean.

title: fix(browser): keep the Browser page visible while a menu is open
body:
## Summary

Opening the model and effort picker (or any menu or dialog) made the Browser panel go blank until the menu closed. It happened every time in an opaque window (window translucency off) and in a light translucent window. The user saw it on a remote session.

## Cause

When a menu opens, the transparent shell view is raised above the native Browser page. While a page is live, a CSS rule clears the session panel backgrounds so the page shows through. The floating top bar (#7708) moved the center panel fill onto `.center-panel-surface::before`, and that rule never covered the pseudo-element. In dark translucent windows `--color-bg-primary` is transparent, so the gap only showed with an opaque fill.

## Fix

Add `.center-panel-shell--session > .center-panel-surface::before` to the existing `[data-browser-native-live]` clearing rule. The chat column keeps its colour because the chat surface paints its own background.

## Evidence

Real desktop app from this branch, remote session (second daemon linked as a remote host), dark theme, window translucency off, Browser tab showing a public artifact. Native window captures.

| | Picker closed | Picker open |
|---|---|---|
| Before (main) | ![before closed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/83f8ea565cd3e08473e6239962e747ce2b88eea2/before-closed.png) | ![before open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/83f8ea565cd3e08473e6239962e747ce2b88eea2/before-open.png) |
| After (this PR) | ![after closed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/83f8ea565cd3e08473e6239962e747ce2b88eea2/after-closed.png) | ![after open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/83f8ea565cd3e08473e6239962e747ce2b88eea2/after-open.png) |

The closed state matches pixel for pixel in the chat column, so nothing changes when no menu is open.

## Tests

CSS-only change; CI is the gate. Verified by hand in the desktop app as above.

## Notes

- Not changed here: `shell:focus` calls `forgetLastFocusedPanel()` before a click-opened menu, so `refreshLastFocusedPanelSurface` in the `browser:overlay` handler always returns early. It does not cause this bug.
- Also seen in the lab, not changed: if the shell renderer reloads while a menu is open, the main process keeps the shell raised until the next menu opens and closes.

title: fix: render artifacts in the Artifacts tab instead of ao preview
body:
Code changes: +26 -1\
Tests: +45 -6\
Others: +21 -31

## What

Artifacts now render in the session's Artifacts tab, not the Browser panel. Agents stop running `ao preview` on deliverables, and the desktop opens the Artifacts tab with a newly registered artifact, whatever its file type.

## Why

The worker prompt and the `using-ao` preview guide told agents to run `ao preview` on every "browser-displayable" artifact (Markdown, HTML, PDF, SVG, images) right after creating it. So a Markdown or HTML deliverable took over the Browser panel, and files outside that list got no handoff at all. The Artifacts tab already renders every type the file pane supports, so it's the one place artifacts should show.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The agent writes `report.md`, runs `ao artifact add report.md`, then `ao preview report.md`. The Browser panel opens on the rendered Markdown. | The agent writes `report.md` and runs `ao artifact add report.md`. The inspector opens on the Artifacts tab with `report.md` selected and rendered. Browser is untouched. |
| A `.csv`, `.parquet`, or other non-"browser-displayable" artifact isn't revealed anywhere. | Any newly registered artifact opens in the Artifacts tab. |

## How

- **Prompt** (`session_manager/manager.go`): replaced the "automatically open the primary requested browser-displayable artifact" sentence with a short pointer: never open an artifact with `ao preview`, whatever its file type, because `ao artifact add` shows it in the Artifacts tab. It stays short because the always-on pointer is capped at 260 words; the detail, including using `ao preview` when the user explicitly asks, is in `preview.md`.
- **Skill and docs**: rewrote the "Automatic artifact handoff" section of `using-ao/commands/preview.md` to match, and updated `references.md`, `SKILL.md`, and `docs/cli/README.md`. Previewing an artifact by absolute path is still documented, for explicit requests only.
- **Desktop** (`SessionView.tsx`): follows the same baseline pattern Browser uses for new previews. Artifacts already registered when the session is entered form the baseline. Each later registration reveals the newest new one via the existing `handleOpenArtifact`, which opens the inspector on Artifacts with that path selected. Unregistered files in the folder never trigger it. A renamed artifact doesn't either, because it keeps its `id` or matches an earlier path in `previousPaths`. Terminated sessions don't auto-reveal. If the user is watching a live page in Browser or reviewing Files, docked or popped out, the registration doesn't move the view. It puts an unseen dot on the Artifacts tab (a new `artifactsUnseen` flag mirroring `browserUnseen`, cleared when Artifacts is shown) and shows a global toast, "New artifact: <name>", with an Open button. The toast stays above a maximized Browser and is a polite status region for screen readers. A cloud session's baseline also waits for its artifact list (`artifactFilesPending`). A remote host's session takes its baseline from fresh data only: stale cached data is refetched on mount first.

Out of scope: `ao preview <artifact-path>` itself still works; I left it in place for explicit user requests rather than rejecting it.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/skillassets/ ./internal/sessionartifacts/` passes, as does `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run SystemPrompt`. The prompt and skill assertions were updated to require the Artifacts-tab guidance and to reject the old "browser-displayable artifact" sentence.
- `vitest run SessionView.test.tsx SessionView.remote.test.tsx` passes 335/335. Two new tests cover this: a newly registered `.parquet` opens in Artifacts, while artifacts already registered on entry and unregistered files don't.
- `npm run typecheck` reports no errors in the changed files.

title: fix(chat): keep a waking chat's settings usable and quiet
body:
## Summary

Reopening a chat whose agent had gone to sleep could show a red "the agent controller for this session is not running" under the model picker. The settings bar also greyed out until the agent woke. The page still held the chat's pre-sleep "ready" state, so the 5 s model-list poll hit the sleeping agent and got 409 `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`. On a large chat, the reload that would correct that state is slow, so the error stays up for most of the wake.

- A 409 `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY` from the model list reloads the chat's state and is not shown as an error. Other model-list errors still show.
- A chat that already ran keeps its settings bar usable while its agent wakes. A pick goes through the normal write, which wakes the agent and waits for it.
- "/" offers the agent's saved skills until the live list arrives.
- A send waits for any settings write still in flight, so the message runs with the setting just picked.

Real Claude Code (Opus 5.5) in an isolated desktop lab. Each take leaves the chat, waits for the daemon's own idle hibernation, then reopens it. title: fix(remote): stop polling a remote host whose workspace stream fails
body:
## Summary

A remote host could look connected while messages never arrived and new sessions never showed up. The cause was the desktop's fallback for a failed workspace stream:

- The host answered `GET /sessions/{id}/workspace/events` with an error (seen on a real host: 404 `PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING` for every git-backed session).
- The remote branch of `workspace-file-events.ts` then polled every 2 s and never stopped or reopened the stream.
- Each tick called `invalidateQueries` with the default `cancelRefetch: true`. The query functions ignore the abort signal, so the old `workspace/files` request kept running while a new one started.
- On a host where `workspace/files` is slow (21–40 s on the real host), requests piled up in Chromium's 6 connections to the host's loopback proxy. Sends, session lists and every other request for that host queued behind them.

## Changes

- When the remote stream fails, stop the poll and reopen with the shared `computeSseRetryDelayMs` backoff (5 s doubling to a 60 s cap, with jitter), as local streams already do.
- Remote invalidations use `cancelRefetch: false` and join a read already in flight. A change that arrives during that read queues one more refresh afterwards, so no update is lost.
- The healthy path is unchanged: poll until the stream delivers its first frame, then rely on `workspace_changed` events.

Trade-off: while a host's stream keeps failing, the workspace queries refresh on each reconnect attempt (at most once a minute) instead of every 2 s.

## Testing

- `workspace-file-events.test.ts` has 2 new tests: a failed remote stream stops polling and reopens after the backoff; a slow remote read is never restarted while polling. Together with `remote-sse-probe.test.ts`, 22/22 pass. On `main`, the 2 new tests and 2 tests whose call shape changed fail.
- End to end in the real desktop app against a second local daemon. That daemon was patched to return 404 `PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING` from `workspace/events` and to take 20 s to answer `workspace/files`. Each run kept the chat and Files panel open for 120 s, fetched a small test request every 2 s, and sent a message at 70 s:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `workspace/files` requests | 5 every 10 s, never finishing | 1 at a time, only on reconnect attempts |
| Requests queued at 120 s | 242 | 1–3 |
| Test request latency | ~50 s by 60 s, then never answered | 5–17 ms, all 60 answered |
| Message sent at 70 s | Never reached the host; shown as "Not sent" | Reached the host in 0.3 s; the agent replied |

- Recovery: after the host restarted without the fault, the stream reopened within about 5 s, and a file created on the host appeared in the Files panel within 2 s.

## Follow-ups

- Why the real host's `workspace/events` returns `PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING` is being investigated separately.
- `useWorkspaceFilePaths` still refetches remote file paths every 30 s without an abort signal.

title: feat: encrypt phone traffic end to end to the machine's host key
body:
The phone now encrypts everything it sends to a machine paired by QR, so Cloudflare and the LAN see only ciphertext.

- Daemon: `/api/v1/e2ee` runs an X25519 handshake signed with the existing Ed25519 host key, then carries HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and WebSockets in ChaCha20-Poly1305 records. Every request inside is authorized by the LAN chain, as in `/api/v1/tunnel`. The mobile status reports `hostKey`.
- Desktop: the pairing QR carries `hostKey`.
- Phone: a QR with a key pins it. API requests, the mux and live browser sockets, the chat event stream, pairing, endpoint refresh, account linking, images and chat renders then go through the channel, and a pinned machine never falls back to plain HTTP. Adds @noble/curves, @noble/ciphers and @noble/hashes (pure JS).

Both sides use fresh keys per connection, so a host key stolen later cannot decrypt recorded traffic.

Not covered:
- The app preview of a page on the machine needs the token in a native WebView, so an encrypted machine offers only the live browser view.
- Desktop to remote host traffic, and phones that add a machine only by account sign-in, stay unencrypted.
- Rolling the daemon back after pairing makes the phone refuse the machine until it is paired again.

An old phone ignores `hostKey`, and a QR from an old desktop has none; both keep working unencrypted.

Tests:
- `go test ./internal/httpd/`: handshake, wrong key, tampered record, low-order key, WebSocket inside the tunnel, test vector
- mobile `vitest run` (3624 tests), including the same test vector
- frontend pairing payload tests
- A live run against a daemon from this branch: pairing with a one-time code, endpoint refresh and the terminal mux went over the channel, and no code, token or path appeared in plaintext on the wire.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Mobile pairing codes include the machine’s host key, which is saved with the connection.
  * Mobile connections with a host key use an encrypted channel for requests, live updates, and media, with the machine’s identity verified during setup.
* **Improvements**
  * Images, artifacts, and browser content load through the host-aware connection.
  * If the machine’s host key cannot be read, the desktop shows a notice instead of a pairing code.
  * Connections with an unreadable saved host key do not fall back to unencrypted requests.

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.2 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

Updates `undici` from 6.27.0 to 6.29.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v6.29.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 · GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

title: feat(cloud): project setting to name Orchestrator a commit co-author
body:
Code changes: +17 -3\
Tests: +15 -0\
Others: +33 -1

## What

Adds a Cloud project setting, `coAuthorCommits`, to the public Cloud API contract and to the typed client. A Cloud project's **Pull requests** settings get a new **Add Orchestrator as a commit co-author** switch. The setting is on unless a project turns it off.

While the setting is on, commits that a session's agents make carry this trailer:

`Co-authored-by: <slug>[bot] <<bot id>+<slug>[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`

The trailer names the Orchestrator GitHub App's bot account, so GitHub shows the App as a co-author next to the person the commit is authored as. The Cloud guide also notes that cloud reviews are now posted as the person and end with a "Generated by Orchestrator" line.

## Why

Cloud commits and reviews should be attributed to the user, with Orchestrator credited visibly. Projects need a way to opt out of the co-author trailer.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud project Pull requests settings show "Automatic review" and "Workers request a built-in review". | A third switch, "Add Orchestrator as a commit co-author", is on by default. Turning it off sends `PATCH …/settings {"config":{"coAuthorCommits":false}}`. |

## How

- **Contract:** `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` adds `ProjectCoAuthorCommits` (boolean, default on) to the project config and to the settings patch. `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` is regenerated from it.
- **Draft and patch:** `cloud-project-settings.ts` reads `config.coAuthorCommits ?? true` and sends the field only when it changes, like the other settings.
- **Display:** the switch is Cloud-only (`capabilities.coAuthorCommits`). It is hidden for standalone projects, which have no Pull requests section. Local projects do not show it.
- **Translations:** the strings are added to every locale. They are English except `ru`, which follows how the neighbouring `workersRequestReview` keys are translated.
- **Rollout:** the control plane side is OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane `feat/cloud-reviews-user-token`, which validates the field and adds the trailer. Against an older control plane, only toggling the switch fails, and the error is visible. Nothing else changes.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` (frontend) passes.
- `npm run cloud:check` and `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh` pass.
- `npx vitest run` passed 788 tests across 54 files: the settings components, CloudProjectSettingsForm, i18n, and cloud-project-settings. New tests cover the default being on, sending only a change, and the switch sending `coAuthorCommits: false`.

title: fix(updates): open release-note links in the system browser
body:
Code changes: +42 -8\
Tests: +91 -3\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Every link in the release notes now opens in the user's default browser, never in the Orchestrator Browser panel. This covers the **Restart to update** dialog (PR numbers, "full comparison", the build-details commit link) and the same notes in **Settings > Updates**.

## Why

User report: clicking `#8141`, `full comparison`, or `Commit: 4d7c9cf` in the Restart to update dialog opened the page in AO's Browser panel. These links are for reading on GitHub in the user's own browser.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Plain click opened the link in the Orchestrator Browser. Right-click offered "Open in Orchestrator Browser". | Click, Cmd/Ctrl-click, Enter, and middle-click all call `openExternal`. Right-click shows only "Open in external browser" and "Copy link". |

No visual change: same classes, same underline, same hover card.

## How

- `DesktopReleaseNotes` is the one renderer for release notes. It used `ProductExternalLink` → `AppLink`, and `AppLink` sends plain clicks to the session Browser from `AppBrowserLinkContext`.
- `AppLink` gets a `systemBrowser` prop. With it:
  - Clicks of any kind call `preventDefault` and then `openLinkInSystemBrowser` (the `app.openExternal` bridge). Enter on a focused link fires the same click.
  - Middle-click (`auxclick`, button 1) is handled the same way, with `preventDefault` so the shell's window-open handler doesn't open it a second time.
  - Only `http:`, `https:`, and `mailto:` get through (new `isSystemBrowserLink`). Any other scheme opens nothing. The main process still enforces its own allowlist, and the notes' `urlTransform` still only allows AO GitHub PR, commit, and compare URLs.
  - The context menu leaves out "Open in Orchestrator Browser".
  - The #8001 hover card stays, but gets no `onBrowserOpen`, so links inside the card also open externally.
- `DesktopReleaseNotes` now renders `AppLink systemBrowser` directly. `ProductExternalLink` and every other `AppLink` caller (chat, PR summaries, inspector) are unchanged.
- Other notices: `HarnessUpdateNotice` already calls `openExternal` directly. The sidebar Update row and the channel help text contain no links.

## Testing

Per the requester, I did not run tests, typecheck, lint, or builds locally. CI will run them.

- `AppLink.test.tsx`: a `systemBrowser` link under an AO Browser provider sends click, Cmd-click, Ctrl-click, and middle-click to `openExternal` and never to the AO Browser. The menu lists only external and copy. `file:` and `app:` links open nothing, and `mailto:` opens externally.
- `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx`: under an AO Browser provider, clicking "full comparison", Cmd-clicking the commit link, and middle-clicking all go to `openExternal` with the right URLs.

To check by hand: open Restart to update (or Settings > Updates when an update is staged). Then click, Cmd-click, middle-click, and Tab+Enter on a PR number, "full comparison", and the commit link. Each one should open in your default browser, and the Browser panel should stay as it was. Right-click a link: the menu should show only "Open in external browser" and "Copy link". Hover a link, then click the domain or title in the card: it should also open externally. Chat links should still open in the Orchestrator Browser.
