title: fix(chat): draw queued turns a steer carried at that steer
body:
## Summary

A steered message looked like it vanished when the steer also carried queued turns into the running turn. The steer was delivered and drawn, but above a block of carried turns that stayed pinned over the composer, so it was out of view.

## Cause

A steer can deliver queued turns into the running turn with it (batched delivery, #6504). #7822 places the ones Orchestrator relays as **worker reports** under that steer. Every other carried turn, such as CodeRabbit review comments injected while the agent worked, stayed a turn of its own.

The timeline places a turn where its first row is. The carried turns' rows were recorded right after the running turn began, so they sorted after the **whole** running turn:

```
running turn (anchor 1914): work, steer 1941, steer 1944, reply 1945, ... every later row lands here
9 carried CodeRabbit turns (anchors 1915-1923)  <- always last, right above the composer
```

Every later steer and reply in that turn was drawn above the carried block, out of view. Neither the dock's temporary "steering" row nor the composer's steer echo was ever visible.

## Fix

Before grouping, `atCarryingSteer` places the rows of each turn a loaded steer delivered (and that is not already placed as a report) right after that steer, inside the running turn's block:

- Order follows what the agent was sent (the steer's `providerInputSourceTurnIds`), so a queue reordered before the steer draws in sent order.
- Each steer's carried rows are spread across the gap up to the next item after it, durable or a pending steer echo, so they never sort past it.
- Carried rows keep their own `turnId`; `groupByTurn` reads the carrier through a side map. Editing and edit state stay on the row's own turn.

Row identity is cached the same way as `outlivingAction`'s, so unchanged turns keep their memoized render.

## Evidence

Before (main, cropped from the reporter's recording of a remote host): the message is queued, **Steer** is clicked, the row leaves the dock, and nothing appears. The CodeRabbit block stays last.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/4a2385c98d3d33abc9ed6a9bf6af679ac296d5a0/ce30804d4b/steer-vanishes-before.gif)

[Full-speed MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/4a2385c98d3d33abc9ed6a9bf6af679ac296d5a0/ce30804d4b/steer-vanishes-before.mp4)

The remote host recorded all four steers, the agent answered them, and the desktop's cached page held every row. Rendering that real cached page (77 rows) through `ChatWorkspace`, DOM position of each marker:

| Build | Last carried CodeRabbit comment | Agent reply after the steer | Later agent reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 1464 (bottom) | 490 (above it, hidden) | 571 (above it, hidden) |
| this PR | 1306 | 1477 (below) | 1558 (below) |

The same real cached page rendered by the real `ChatWorkspace` and app CSS in a browser, scrolled to the bottom (a renderer harness, not the packaged app):

| main | this PR |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/3843a08e4e3b864b899ad9d44e0faa67392b2f3a/602daf15b5/steer-carried-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/3843a08e4e3b864b899ad9d44e0faa67392b2f3a/602daf15b5/steer-carried-after.png) |
| CodeRabbit comments pinned above the composer; no steer in view. | The steers and the agent's replies sit at the bottom, where they were sent. |

## Tests

New `ChatSteer.test.tsx` cases, each failing on the code before its fix:

- a carried automation turn draws at its steer, before the agent's reply;
- carried turns draw in sent order, not queue-creation order;
- two steers carrying 1,001 rows keep each block before the next row;
- a carried row stays above a steer sent right after the carrying steer;
- a carried human message keeps its own turn for editing after the carrier completes.

## Risks

- A carried turn whose steer is outside the loaded page keeps today's behaviour until that steer loads.
- The agent receives carried messages before the steer text; the timeline draws them under the steer, matching worker reports (#7822).

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed chat timeline ordering for queued turns carried into a running turn. Carried turns now appear at the steer activity that brought them forward, in source-turn order, before the corresponding assistant reply. Turns carried by separate steers remain grouped with the correct reply, even when many turns are carried forward. Carried messages also retain their own turn context for editing after the carrying turn completes.

title: fix(import): let the project import dialog scroll its chat list
body:
## Summary

In Project settings › Import chats…, the chat list can't be scrolled once a project has more chats than fit in the dialog. The mouse wheel does nothing, and rows past the first eight or so can't be reached.

The list's bordered box is a direct child of the dialog's scrolling body, which is a flex column. Because the box has `overflow-hidden`, its minimum height is 0, so it shrank to fit the body and cut off its own rows. The body then had nothing to scroll. Adding `shrink-0` keeps the box at its full height, so the body scrolls.

Once the list scrolls, an import error rendered at the end of the body ends up below the fold: after a failed import the button goes back to idle and the dialog looks like nothing happened. The error now sits between the scrolling body and the footer, next to the Import button, in both import dialogs. It is capped at 30% of the viewport height and scrolls beyond that, so a short or zoomed-in window can't push the footer out of the dialog.

## Before / after: scrolling

Both shots are taken after scrolling the mouse wheel over the list. The project has 29 synthetic chats.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d94461f8c575e638e21544ba14be159104243b65/import-dialog-scroll/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d94461f8c575e638e21544ba14be159104243b65/import-dialog-scroll/after.png) |
| List stays on the first rows | Scrolls to the last row (task 24) |

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| List box height | 477 px, cutting off 1,652 px of rows | 1,652 px |
| Dialog body | 527 px of content in 527 px | 1,702 px of content in 527 px |
| Mouse wheel | Doesn't move | Reaches the last row |

## Before / after: failed import

The import request is answered with "failed" for all 29 chats while the list is at the top. "Before" is this PR's first commit (list scrolls, error still inside the body).

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![error before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/43be1d8f6e1958912776e5ad8f26443f277cd2b1/import-dialog-scroll/error-before.png) | ![error after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/43be1d8f6e1958912776e5ad8f26443f277cd2b1/import-dialog-scroll/error-after.png) |
| Error at y = 1,855 px, dialog ends at 770 px: not visible | Error above the footer, visible; list still scrolls (363 of 1,702 px shown) |

## Before / after: failed import in a short window

Same failed import in a 330 px tall viewport, like a zoomed-in window. "Before" is the previous commit (error below the list, uncapped).

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![short before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/eb159e6d24cbb8b2eb236ae75c85dd5acb6fc8e6/import-dialog-scroll/error-short-before.png) | ![short after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/eb159e6d24cbb8b2eb236ae75c85dd5acb6fc8e6/import-dialog-scroll/error-short-after.png) |
| Import button at y = 324 px, dialog ends at 314 px: not visible | Import button visible; error box 99 px tall, scrolls its 164 px |

At normal height the error still shows in full (164 of 164 px).

## Testing

- Ran the desktop app from this branch against a fake home with 29 Claude Code and Codex chats in one project. A script opened the dialog, scrolled with the wheel, and measured the list and body heights, first with the fix and then with the class reverted.
- A second script failed the import request in the page, clicked Import, and checked with `elementFromPoint` whether the error is actually on screen, before and after the move.
- A third run repeated the failed import in a 330 px viewport (CDP device metrics override) and checked that the Import button is still on screen.
- The folder import dialog got the same error move but wasn't run in the lab.

Low. Layout only, in the two import dialogs.

title: feat(cloud): start standalone agents in Cloud from the Scratchpad
body:
Code changes: +310 -75\
Tests: +324 -5\
Others: +236 -0 (contract, generated cloud-client schema, 9 locales)

## What

Cloud standalone agents: the cloud counterpart of a local standalone session. A standalone agent is one worker session with no repository and no orchestrator, and it belongs to the person who started it.

- **New chat:** the project picker offers **Cloud scratchpad** beside the local Scratchpad, but only when the control plane lists the `standalone_agents` feature. Sending starts the agent and opens it on its own route.
- **Scratchpad:** the person's own agents join the Scratchpad section with a **Cloud** badge. They follow its order for keyboard navigation and appear in its archive, where they can be restored.
- **Not a project:** agents don't appear as projects in the sidebar, pickers, Home, the command palette or the board.
- **No orchestrator:** an agent has no orchestrator action. A new task started next to an agent starts another agent.
- **Share:** shares the agent on its own. There is no "Share the whole project instead" switch, and people from your own workspace can be added like anyone else, because nobody but the owner can see the agent until it is shared.

Control plane: OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#96. It adds `POST /orgs/{orgId}/standalone-agents`, `Project.standaloneAgent`, `GET /projects?standaloneAgents=exclude|only` and the access rules. This PR adds those to the public contract (additive; oasdiff reports no breaking change).

## Why

Locally you can start an agent without a project; on Cloud, every session needed a project. The closest thing was a repo-less "standalone project", but that came with its own orchestrator and board, appeared as a project for the whole organization, and offered project-wide sharing.

## Before / After

The same signed-in account, data and window, against the same local control plane. "Before" is `main`; "After" is this branch. Screenshots are attached below.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| New chat offers only the local Scratchpad (`before-picker-and-sidebar.png`) | New chat offers **Cloud scratchpad** too (`after-picker.png`) |
| An older desktop shows each agent as a Cloud *project* with an orchestrator button, and lists it under recent projects (`before-picker-and-sidebar.png`, `before-home.png`) | Each agent is a **Cloud**-badged row in the Scratchpad; there is no project row and no Orchestrator button (`after-scratchpad-agent.png`) |
| No standalone agent to share | Share reads **Standalone agent**, with no whole-project switch: "Only you and people added above can open this session." (`after-share-dialog.png`) |

## How

- **One project per agent:** each agent is backed by its own hidden standalone project. The desktop keeps it as a cloud workspace flagged `standaloneAgent`, so every existing lookup by project id keeps working: the session route, share URLs, restore and terminal. Grouping happens only in the UI, through `isScratchpadWorkspace` and `ownScratchpadWorkspaces` in `types/workspace.ts`.
- **Separate list reads:** `useCloudProjectsQuery` reads `standaloneAgents=exclude` and `standaloneAgents=only` in parallel and dedupes by id. Many agents can no longer push projects off the first page. A control plane without agents ignores the parameter and returns every project in both reads, so the dedupe keeps each once.
- **Composer:** `TaskComposer` treats `__cloud_standalone__` as a Cloud task with no project config and calls `createStandaloneAgent`. It seeds the new project into the cache and remembers which project the session belongs to, so NewChatPage can open the right route.
- **Shared agents:** an agent shared with you stays in the shared projects list, not in your Scratchpad. You can't share it further.
- **Old desktops:** they see their own agents as standalone cloud projects (the "Before" captures). That's acceptable, and other people's agents stay hidden from them, because the control plane filters them out.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- The `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh` check passes.
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` (schema is committed), `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass (31 tests).
- oasdiff against `main`: no breaking changes.
- New and updated vitest coverage:
  - `lib/cloud-standalone-agents.test.ts`: Scratchpad membership, navigation order and routing, archive, command palette.
  - `useWorkspaceQuery`: separate reads, flagging, dedupe and scope.
  - `TaskComposer`: calls `createStandaloneAgent`, never `createSession`.
  - `NewChatPage`: picker gating, and opening the agent's project route.
  - `NewTaskNavigator`, `Sidebar`, `ShareSessionDialog` and `SessionTopbarActions`.
- Full `npx vitest run`: 13,286 passed and 17 failed.
  - 2 were load flakes: `SessionView.remote` and `useCloudModelCatalog` both pass when run alone.
  - The other 15 fail the same way on a clean `main` checkout on this machine: `remote-proxy` (12), `cloud-agent-proxy` (2) and `ContextMeter` (1). None of them are in areas this PR touches.
- Real app: the dev desktop ran against a local control plane built from the companion PR. Through the UI I signed in, started two agents from Cloud scratchpad, checked the Scratchpad, topbar and Share dialog, and compared with `main` on the same profile.
  - Bug found and fixed this way: the workspace scope dropped `standaloneAgent`, so the topbar still offered Orchestrator. There is now a regression test for it.
- Review follow-up (b953db9037): an agent's project route now goes to Home (archiving it from Pinned had opened a board), and Share's team summary no longer says workspace members already have access to an agent.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(mobile): stop the sign-in listener when a browser sign-in fails early
body:
Follow-up to #8085. This commit was pushed to #8085's branch after #8085 had already merged, so it never reached `main`.

## Problem
On a coding agent's Settings screen (`[agent].tsx`), only `run()` stopped the loopback listener. If a browser sign-in failed before the browser opened, for example when starting the Claude or Codex login hit a network error, the listener kept running. Nothing stopped it later, even after leaving the page.

On iOS, a retry then collided with that stale listener on Codex's fixed port and fell back to codes. #8086 fixed that collision in the native module; this PR stops the leak itself.

## Fix
The sign-in's error path now stops the listener. It does so only while this sign-in is still the current one, because a newer sign-in owns the listener.

This path runs only in builds with #8086's native listener, which is now on `main`.

## Testing
- Mobile typecheck passes.
- `browserSignIn` and `agentLogin` tests pass.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

title: fix(mobile): size menu rows before their first frame
body: Code changes: +27 -10\ Tests: +48 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Worker rows on the iOS Workers board now get their width before their first frame is drawn. Switching the machine filter (Cloud → All machines in particular) no longer shows rows at the wrong width for a few frames before they snap into place. ## Why On a phone, switching from Cloud back to All machines showed every row drawn too wide for about 80 ms. Titles were not truncated, content was centred and ran off both edges, and then the rows snapped into place one by one. - Each row sits inside the long-press `MenuView`, which iOS hosts in SwiftUI. SwiftUI sizes the row to its content, so `useMenuRowWidth` measures the slot around it and gives the row that width. - The width came only from `onLayout`, which arrives after the row has been drawn. Every new row therefore painted once at its intrinsic width first. - The board is keyed by `machine|project` (`app/(tabs)/(workers)/index.tsx`), so each filter switch mounts every row again and repeats this for the whole list. - It is a race with the JS thread. It shows when the thread is still busy right after the remount, for example while the list renders further batches of a long board. ## Before / After First frame with rows after switching from an empty machine to All machines: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | Wrong frames on 16 of 16 switches: 1–6 frames, 42–100 ms | Wrong frames on 0 of 12 switches | The GIFs play the switch at ¼ speed. ## How - `useMenuRowWidth` also returns a `ref` for the slot and reads `getBoundingClientRect().width` in a `useLayoutEffect` on mount. On Fabric that read is synchronous against the committed layout, and a state update made in a layout effect renders before the frame is shown. - `onLayout` stays, so later resizes (rotation, split view) still update the width. A zero width (slot not laid out yet) is ignored and the row waits for `onLayout` as before. - The ref is attached in all three places that use the hook: the worker row (`worker-row-interaction.tsx`), `PRCard`, and the chat user row in `ChatTimeline`. The last two had the same first-frame problem. Only the worker row was exercised on the simulator. - Not changed: the board still remounts on every filter switch. That remount is deliberate (see the `identityKey` comment in `worker-board-list.tsx`), and it is no longer visible once rows are sized up front. ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 416 files, 4006 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. - New `lib/useMenuRowWidth.test.tsx`. Its "gives the row the slot's width on mount, before any onLayout" case fails on the old hook. - Simulator A/B on an iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator (iOS 26.5). One Release build of this branch, with the base and fixed Hermes bundles swapped into the same binary. Two lab machines sat behind a read-only proxy in front of a local daemon, one with 64 live workers and one with none. - An empty machine stands in for Cloud. The Cloud chip needs a real Cloud sign-in, and both show the same empty board followed by the same remount to All machines. - Each run recorded 4 × (empty machine → All machines). Every captured frame after a switch was compared with the settled board. Builds were alternated: before 4 runs, after 3 runs. - Settled layouts are identical between the builds (≤ 0.04 % of pixels differ: live timestamps and the Working spinner). - With only 9 workers (inside the list's first render batch of 12), the base build did not glitch either, which matches the race above. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: test(chat): cover OpenCode 2 steering from OpenCode 2.2.7
body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +568 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

OpenCode 2 Chat sessions can steer from OpenCode **2.2.7**, with no AO code change. This PR adds tests that pin it.

- **OpenCode 2.2.7** (released 2026-11-10) ships `anomalyco/opencode#54394`. Its ACP handshake now advertises `_meta.steering.supported`, and it answers `_session/steering` with `injected`, or `promptRequired` when no turn is running.
- **AO's ACP driver already turns Steer on for any agent that advertises it.** On 2.2.7 the conversation's capabilities include `steer`, and ⌘↩ and the queued card's Steer both work.
- **On 2.2.6 and earlier nothing is advertised,** so Steer stays hidden and messages queue as before.

## Why

OpenCode 2 was waiting on that upstream release. Nothing in AO's tests checked that steering works end to end through the OpenCode 2 binding and AO's persistent chat host, or that it stays off on older OpenCode builds.

## Before / After

No user-visible change from this PR: it only adds tests. Whether Steer shows depends on the installed OpenCode version. For review, this is what the tests pin: the desktop app from `main`, with OpenCode 2.2.7 and a scripted model.

| Before (OpenCode 2.2.6 or earlier) | After (OpenCode 2.2.7) |
| --- | --- |
| **⌘↩ during a command.** No Steer, so the message waits and runs as the next turn. | The message joins the running turn. The model gets it right after the command's result and replies in the same turn. ![OpenCode 2: change of plan steered while the command runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/ee527495dbdd08f2c80f7a7560447e88a16a55f3/oc2-1-steered-running.png) ![OpenCode 2: one turn, replying to the steer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/ee527495dbdd08f2c80f7a7560447e88a16a55f3/oc2-2-steered-done.png) |
| **Queued card.** No Steer button. | The card offers Steer while the command runs, and the message joins the turn. ![OpenCode 2: queued change of plan with a Steer button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/ee527495dbdd08f2c80f7a7560447e88a16a55f3/oc2-3-queued.png) ![OpenCode 2: the queued message steered into the running turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/ee527495dbdd08f2c80f7a7560447e88a16a55f3/oc2-4-card-steered.png) |
| **Steer during a text-only reply.** Not possible. | OpenCode finishes the reply it is writing, then answers the steer in the same turn. ![OpenCode 2: steer during a text reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/ee527495dbdd08f2c80f7a7560447e88a16a55f3/oc2-5-text-reply.png) |
| **Image in a steer.** Not possible. | The image reaches the model with the steer. ![OpenCode 2: steer with an attached screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/ee527495dbdd08f2c80f7a7560447e88a16a55f3/oc2-6-image-steered.png) |
| **Stop after a steer.** Not possible. | The turn ends once, interrupted, and nothing starts by itself. ![OpenCode 2: Stop after a steer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Meraj-08/agent-orchestrator/ee527495dbdd08f2c80f7a7560447e88a16a55f3/oc2-7-stop-after-steer.png) |

## How

Tests only, both in `chatdriver/opencodev2acp`:

- **`TestOpenCodeV2SteeringFollowsTheHandshake`.** The existing fake OpenCode 2 can now advertise steering and hold a prompt open. It runs through `opencodev2acp.New` and AO's persistent chat host:
  - With a 2.2.7 handshake, Steer is offered. `_session/steering` arrives with AO's `idleBehavior: promptRequired`. `promptRequired` maps to `ErrChatNoSteerableTurn`, and `injected` lands in the running turn, which then completes.
  - With a 2.2.6 handshake, Steer is not offered.
- **`TestLiveOpenCodeV2ACPSteering`**, opt-in like the Antigravity live test: `AO_LIVE_OPENCODE_V2=1`, and optionally `AO_LIVE_OPENCODE_V2_BIN` to pick a binary.
  - It runs the real `opencode acp` against a scripted OpenAI-compatible model, with a temporary HOME and XDG folders. It needs no account and never touches real OpenCode data.
  - A steer during a command joins that turn and reaches the model right after the tool result. The turn makes exactly two model calls, so nothing is left to start by itself.
  - An image in the steer reaches the model.
  - A steer after the turn ended is refused with `ErrChatNoSteerableTurn` and starts nothing.
  - It skips on Windows (the fixture is POSIX-only) and when the binary doesn't advertise steering (below 2.2.7).
- **Retries are safe.** `_session/steering` takes no delivery id, so the same call sent twice would inject twice. AO never resends a steer whose delivery is uncertain (the delivery receipts in `service/chat/steer.go`), so this can't happen from AO.

**Known behaviour (OpenCode)**

- **Stop after a steer that OpenCode hadn't picked up yet:** OpenCode keeps the steer queued, and it reaches the model at the start of the next turn, before the new message. The order matches AO's transcript, so nothing is lost, but it lands one turn late. Pi does the same (#8036).

## Testing

- **Unit:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/opencodev2acp/` passes, skipping `TestWrongOpenCodeMajorIsRejectedBeforeACPProcessLaunch`. That test fails on this Mac on `main` too, because it finds a real OpenCode 1 in `/opt/homebrew/bin`; it passes in CI.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/nativeacp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/opencodeacp/` passes.
- **Lint:** `golangci-lint` v2.14.0 on the package reports 0 issues.
- **Mutation check:** with AO's handshake detection disabled, the driver test fails (`steer capability = false, want true`).
- **Live test:** `AO_LIVE_OPENCODE_V2=1 go test -run TestLiveOpenCodeV2ACPSteering` passes 3/3 on OpenCode 2.2.7, installed by AO's own installer, and skips on 2.2.5.
- **Raw ACP against 2.2.7, outside AO, scripted model:**
  - steer during a command 3/3, one turn each;
  - idle 3/3 `promptRequired`, with nothing started;
  - text-only reply 2/2;
  - two steers in a row, both delivered;
  - a steer racing the end of the turn 6/6 `promptRequired`;
  - image 1/1.

  2.2.5 advertises nothing.
- **Desktop app from `main`,** with OpenCode 2.2.7 installed through `POST /api/v1/agents/opencode-v2/install` in an isolated HOME:
  - ⌘↩, the queued card, a text-only reply, an image, Stop, and ⌘↩ when idle (a normal send) all behave as described above.
  - After killing the chat host and calling `resume-agent`, a steer still lands in the running turn.
  - After a reload, 6 steers show 6 "Steered" markers, with no duplicates.
- **Not run locally:** the full `go test ./...`, which has unrelated local-only failures on this Mac. CI covers it.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: feat(desktop): persist lifecycle and respawn records for app and daemon
body:
Code changes: +853 -22\
Tests: +618 -2\
Others: +31 -0 (docs)

## What

Persistent, crash-survivable lifecycle records for Electron main and the daemon, a recorded reason for every daemon respawn, and an experimental Linux option to run the daemon (and so tmux and every agent) outside the desktop app's systemd scope.

- **`~/.ao/logs/desktop-lifecycle.jsonl`** (Electron main), which records:
  - start, with the Linux cgroup and OOM score
  - the quit sequence and process exit code
  - uncaught exceptions, and unhandled rejections (observed without changing Node's handling)
  - `render-process-gone` and `child-process-gone`
  - `previous_run_unclean` when the last run never reached a clean exit
  - every daemon spawn (with its trigger), exit (code, signal, uptime), restart decision and cancellation
- **`~/.ao/logs/daemon-lifecycle.jsonl`** (daemon): start, supervisor-link loss, shutdown cause (signal name, request, or server error) and `Run`'s error.
- **`~/.ao/logs/daemon-crash.log`**: Go fatal crash output (panics, runtime faults such as SIGBUS) via `debug.SetCrashOutput`.
- **Experimental `AO_DAEMON_SCOPE=systemd` (Linux only):** starts the daemon in its own transient user scope in `app-ao.slice`, with optional `AO_DAEMON_MEMORY_HIGH` / `AO_DAEMON_MEMORY_MAX`. Without a reachable systemd user manager it raises the daemon's `oom_score_adj` to 300 instead. The probe uses the launch's slice and memory properties; if a scoped daemon still exits with a code before it is ready, the scope is dropped for that run and the start is retried once with the fallback, keeping an automatic restart's intent and the failed launch's keep-alive choice. Off by default; macOS and Windows unchanged.

## Why

No GitHub issue: a user reported this privately. On Linux (AppImage, Electron 44.7, Hyprland/Wayland, ~18 sessions, heavy swap), the desktop window vanished seconds after an agent's headless Chromium (Vitest) crashed inside the app's systemd scope. There was no main-process or daemon log, no core dump, nothing in Crashpad, no Sentry event and no OOM record. Earlier the same day the app respawned its own daemon mid-turn, again with nothing recorded.

Why nothing was recorded (verified in code):
- **No native dumps:** Crashpad is never started. `sentry-main.ts` passes `defaultIntegrations: []`, and only Sentry's minidump integrations call `crashReporter.start`.
- **No daemon log:** in normal mode the daemon's stdout/stderr are pipes into Electron, and `newLogger()` writes only to stderr. That output dies with the app.
- **No Go crash trace:** a Go fatal panic exits 2 with its trace on the same lost pipe and no core dump. That fits the unexplained respawn.
- **No respawn reason:** `scheduleDaemonAutoRestart` and the replacement paths persisted nothing.
- **Shared scope:** the daemon, tmux and all agents share the app's systemd scope, and so its memory and OOM domain.

The root cause of the exit is **not established**. The records added here are what's needed to establish it next time. Inferred from code and the AppImage runtime source: the old instance's NetworkService SIGBUS came from the FUSE mount teardown after the main process had already ended, so it was a consequence, not the cause.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A daemon crash, respawn or app exit on Linux leaves only `~/.ao/logs/updater.jsonl` | `desktop-lifecycle.jsonl` gets `{"event":"daemon_exit","code":2,"signal":null,"uptimeMs":…}` then `{"event":"daemon_restart_decision","cause":"ungraceful_exit","decision":"restart","attempt":1,"delayMs":1000,…}` then `{"event":"daemon_spawn","trigger":"auto_restart","crashedPid":…}`, all written before the respawn |
| A Go panic's trace goes only to the app's stderr pipe | The trace is also in `~/.ao/logs/daemon-crash.log` under a `=== daemon pid … started …` header |
| A daemon stop leaves no cause | `daemon-lifecycle.jsonl`: `supervisor_link_lost`, `daemon_shutdown_begin` with `cause: "signal"` (and the signal name), `"requested"` or `"server_error"`, then `daemon_exit` |
| An app exit leaves no record | `main_window_closed` / `window_all_closed` / `before_quit` / `process_exit {code}`, or on next start `previous_run_unclean {previousPid, previousPidAlive}`; crashed Chromium children appear as `child_process_gone {type, reason, exitCode}` |
| On Linux, agents always run in the app's systemd scope | With `AO_DAEMON_SCOPE=systemd`: the daemon tree runs in `app-ao.slice/ao-daemon-<pid>-<t>.scope`, optionally memory-limited; default behaviour is unchanged |

No UI change.

## How

**Placement and durability**
- Both logs sit in `<run-file dir>/logs`, normally `~/.ao/logs` beside `updater.jsonl`, where users already look. They follow `AO_RUN_FILE`, and nothing is written outside `~/.ao`.
- Each record is one synchronous open/append/close, so it is in the kernel before the call returns and survives an immediate crash. There is no fsync, so a power loss can drop the last records.
- JSONL files rotate at 2 MiB and keep 2 older generations; the crash log rotates at 1 MiB. Files are mode 0600, and symlinked log files are refused.

**Privacy**
- Records hold fixed event names and scalar fields only.
- Free text (error messages, stack frames) is scrubbed of URLs, credentials, opaque tokens of 32+ characters and quoted strings of 40+ characters; a credential assignment's quoted value is redacted through its closing quote, spaces included, and the home directory is folded to `~`.
- Prompts and terminal output are never passed in. Nothing is uploaded.

**Behaviour neutrality**
- Unhandled rejections are observed by wrapping `process.emit` and returning its result unchanged. Adding an `unhandledRejection` listener would have changed Node's handling.
- Exceptions are observed through `uncaughtExceptionMonitor`.
- The log is installed only after the single-instance lock is won, so a losing second launch writes nothing.

**Respawn records**
- `startDaemon` takes a `trigger` (`startup`, `renderer_status`, `manual_start`, `manual_restart`, `browser_runtime_recovery`, `auto_restart`).
- `daemon_restart_decision` is written before the backoff timer is armed.
- Replacement and unresponsive-holder kills are recorded before they happen.

**Daemon**
- `Run` has a named return so a deferred record captures its error, or a panic that is then re-raised.
- The signal name comes from `context.Cause` on the `signal.NotifyContext` context.

**Scope prototype**
- `systemd-run --scope` adds its own PID to the scope and then calls `execvpe` in place, so the spawned child keeps its PID, pipes, process group, exit code and signal, and existing supervision is unchanged. This is from systemd's `run.c`; it hasn't been run on a live system yet.
- It's off by default until tested on real launchers (GNOME, KDE, Hyprland with uwsm or plain exec).
- Memory values are validated against systemd's syntax, so nothing else can be injected into the property list.

Reviewer focus:
- `startDaemonInner` and the exit handler in `main.ts`.
- `scheduleDaemonAutoRestart`.
- `daemon.Run`'s new deferred exit record.

Intentional omissions:
- Crashpad stays off; minidump contents need a privacy decision first.
- The daemon's general slog output is not copied to disk; only lifecycle facts are, to keep prompts and secrets out.
- Per-session agent scopes and making the scope the default are follow-ups.
- The bundled daemon still executes from the AppImage mount.
- Chat, ACP and persistenthost code is untouched; a separate change covers chat reattach.

## Testing

- `go test -count=1 ./internal/lifecyclelog ./internal/daemon ./internal/daemon/supervisor`, with `AO_*` env stripped: ok. Includes scrubbing, scalar-only fields, rotation caps, symlink refusal, nil safety, and a re-exec'd child that panics whose trace must land in `daemon-crash.log`.
- `GOOS=linux go vet ./internal/lifecyclelog ./internal/daemon` and a Linux test-binary build: ok.
- Vitest (Node 24): `lifecycle-log`, `linux-daemon-scope`, `daemon-auto-restart`, `daemon-auto-restart.integration`, `main-error-capture`, `update-diagnostics`, `daemon-owner`: 7 files, 152 tests passed.
  - The integration suite runs the real `main.ts` daemon functions in a VM.
  - New cases assert `daemon_restart_decision` and the `auto_restart` spawn record are logged before the respawn's `spawn` call.
  - They also cover the graceful no-restart path, give-up after the window is exhausted, the scope and OOM-score spawn paths, and no keep-alive log descriptor being opened when a stop lands during isolation planning, no respawn when a successor writes `running.json` during planning, no spawn from a normal start once quit is under way, a single fallback retry when a scoped launch exits before readiness (keeping an automatic restart's intent and the launch's keep-alive choice), and a distinct `nonzero_exit_without_run_file` cause (each fails without its fix).
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in frontend sources. The local run showed errors only in `packages/product-ui` because the workspace root wasn't installed in that checkout.

Not run locally:
- Any Linux runtime: a real systemd user manager, an AppImage mount, Wayland.
- golangci-lint v2.14.0; the local binary is too old for Go 1.27.
- The full repo suites. CI is the check for those.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

Suggested reviewers: Harshit Singh Bhandari (`main.ts` startDaemon, main-error-capture) and Yash Maheshwari (daemon-auto-restart).

* **New Features**
  * Added local lifecycle logs for desktop and daemon activity, including startup, shutdown, errors, and restart decisions.
  * Logs rotate automatically, use restrictive file permissions, and scrub sensitive text. Prompts, terminal output, and uploads are excluded.
  * Daemon crash output is saved locally and rotated.

title: fix(chat): stop a provider that lost its ACP session so the chat can resume
body:
Code changes: +107 -5\
Tests: +190 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When the Claude ACP adapter reports that it no longer holds a Chat's session, AO now stops that provider and marks the chat **exited**, so `resume-agent` can reload the conversation. Before this change, the chat stayed attached to a session that no longer existed.

## Why

From a user report. After a daemon restart, a Chat that was mid-turn failed every new message with:

```
set ACP session option "model": {"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"Session not found"}}
```

`ao session resume-agent` refused with `AGENT_NOT_EXITED`, and `ao send --steer` returned `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The user's workaround was `exit-agent`, then `resume-agent`, then resending the message.

Root cause, from reading the bundled `claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0 (`dist/acp-agent.js`, query-stream catch, ~L3460–3495): when the Claude Code process under the adapter dies, the adapter fails the active turn and **deletes the session from its in-memory map**, but the adapter keeps running. The persistent chat host's cached ACP state still names the session. So a restarted daemon reattaches live (`Resume`'s `live != nil` path, no `session/load`), and every session-scoped handler then throws `Error("Session not found")`. The SDK delivers that as `-32603` with `data.details`. Nothing in AO treated the error as a dead provider. The host stayed alive, so the controller stayed "live", and `resume-agent` kept refusing.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Every send to the chat fails with `-32603 … Session not found`; the provider stays attached | The first failing send stops the provider; the API returns `CHAT_PROVIDER_SESSION_LOST` ("resume the agent to continue") |
| `resume-agent` → `AGENT_NOT_EXITED` (host still alive) | The session reads as exited; `resume-agent` starts a fresh adapter and reloads the transcript with `session/load` |
| A prompt that hits the lost session announces Ready, so queued messages drain into the dead provider one by one | The turn fails with the cause and the provider stops instead of announcing Ready |
| `--steer` → `INTERNAL_ERROR`, an uncertain delivery handle | A definitive refusal, so the handle settles as rejected |

## How

- `isACPSessionMissing` (`acp/driver.go`) matches only `-32603` whose `data.details` (or the host-wrapped `data.providerData.details`) is "Session not found". A generic `-32603` is not treated as a lost session.
- `conversation.providerSessionLost` stops the provider with `closeProvider(true, false)`, the same no-`session/close` stop hibernation uses, so Claude's saved transcript survives for resume. It is wired into `SendTurn` (model switch and settings, where the reported `set_config_option "model"` failure came from) and into `Steer`.
- Prompt path (`finishPrompt`): it *marks* the session lost, emits the failed `TurnCompleted`, and then stops the provider instead of emitting Ready. Stopping first would close the event stream and drop the failed turn.
- `AcknowledgeProviderEvent` is a no-op once the session is lost. The host and its prompt journal are gone. A failing ACK would make `projectUnit` set `preserveProviderOnStop`, which skips the exited report and brings the bug back.
- New `ports.ErrChatProviderSessionLost`, mapped to `CHAT_PROVIDER_SESSION_LOST` in both the conversations controller and the session service error mapper.

Intentionally not in this PR:
- No automatic resume. The chat becomes exited and needs one `resume-agent`.
- No liveness probe at reattach time. The lost session is found on the next session-scoped call.
- The report also mentioned an accepted message delivered about an hour late while the session showed as working. This PR does not establish the cause of that.

## Testing

- `acp/session_lost_test.go`, with a fake persistent host answering every request with the adapter's exact error:
  - classifier shapes, including the plain and host-wrapped forms; generic `-32603` and other codes are rejected
  - `SendTurn` (`set_config_option`) → `ErrChatProviderSessionLost`, the host is terminated once, no Ready, no inconclusive stop, and the ACK is a no-op
  - prompt → turn failed with the cause, the turn is released, the host is terminated
  - steer → a `ChatRefusal()` error wrapping the sentinel, the host is terminated
- All three behavior tests fail when the stop is disabled. They pass with `-count=20 -race`.
- `go test` passes for `chatdriver/acp`, `chatdriver/claudeacp`, `chatdriver/persistenthost`, `service/chat`, `httpd/controllers` and `ports`. `go vet` is clean.
- `service/session`: `TestReconcileBranchStatesRunsGitOnlyWhenTipsMove` and `TestWorkspacePathsCancellationDoesNotCancelSharedInventory` fail locally on this machine, and they fail the same way on unmodified `main` in a separate worktree. This change only adds an error-mapping case in that package.
- `golangci-lint` was not run locally (the installed v2.0.2 predates Go 1.27.4). CI will run it.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

title: fix(desktop): bump bundled ACP Node runtime to 22.23.5
body:
Fixes #7872

## Summary

Bundled ACP Node runtime: **22.23.2 → 22.23.5**

22.23.2 predates the [22.23.4 security release](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.4) (TLS hostname checks for non-canonical IPs, DNS resolver null-byte handling, Brotli decoder memory corruption, NSS root-store update). 22.23.5 (2026-11-11) is the latest patched 22.x and includes those fixes. Staying on 22.x keeps this a patch-level change.

All three pins move together:
- `frontend/scripts/build-acp-runtime.mjs`: `NODE_VERSION`, the Node shipped at `Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node`. The version is part of the runtime build signature, so cached runtimes rebuild automatically.
- `scripts/bootstrap-self-hosted.sh`: the self-hosted source-build toolchain download and `PATH`.
- `.github/workflows/frontend.yml`: the typecheck lane's lockfile-compatibility check, which mirrors the self-hosted runtime.

**Release notes:** please mention "Bundled ACP Node runtime updated to 22.23.5" so users can confirm the fix.

## Testing

- Confirmed nodejs.org `v22.23.5/SHASUMS256.txt` lists every archive the builds fetch (darwin arm64/x64, linux arm64/x64 `.tar.gz`, linux-x64 `.tar.xz`, win arm64/x64 `.zip`).
- Not built locally. CI's frontend typecheck lane runs `npm ci --dry-run` on 22.23.5, and the packaging build checks the download against those checksums.
- After a build: `".../Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node" --version` should print `v22.23.5`.

## Risks

Low: a patch bump within the same LTS line.

title: feat: add Coder Agents setup and native model discovery
body:
Code changes: +999 -22  
Tests: +714 -8  
Others: +72 -6  

> Account migration from @nikhilachale to @milesatao-svg. This draft continues [original PR #7520](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7520) at original head `7de7e42e36b611f21d58f7f01914693e2525350c`. Original commits and commit authorship are preserved. Descriptions and evidence below include historical results with their original sources.

## What

Adds setup-only Coder Agents support: install the official Coder CLI, enter a deployment URL and complete native login, verify the account, and browse enabled native models.

Coder Agents sessions are unavailable in both Chat and Terminal UI until Coder can enforce a local-only tool policy. The PR includes no Chat driver, conversation loop, local tool runner, approval journal or streaming/history implementation.

## Why

Prepare native Coder setup without offering a session that cannot honor AO's local worktree and approval boundary.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Coder Agents has no separate setup entry in AO. | Harness settings offers installation, native login, account checks and enabled model discovery. |
| Bare coder login fails on a fresh machine without a deployment URL. | The existing AO login terminal prompts for the URL, validates it, and passes it as a separate native login argument. |
| A connected Coder account could make gated Chat selectable, then fail on Send. | Coder is unregistered for Chat and omitted from both switch menus, New Task, the project sheet, Project Settings, Automations and the artifact-session and new-project defaults, including local, remote, remembered and standalone selections. |
| Docs describe local tools and Chat as shipped capabilities. | The manifest and docs consistently describe setup-only availability. |

Historical real Electron setup screenshots are linked below. They show a fresh, signed-out installation; authenticated New Task/menu and native login completion screenshots are unavailable.

## How

- Register the native Coder setup adapter, official CLI installation actions, native account verification and enabled-model discovery.
- Resolve native credentials from environment or the CLI configuration/keyring. The setup API client sends only read-only account, organization and model requests and refuses cross-origin redirects.
- Use AO's existing trusted login-terminal launcher to collect the deployment URL and invoke the resolved Coder CLI. Preserve the terminal's stdin for Coder's browser/token flow and credential storage.
- Keep Coder out of advertised Chat capabilities and out of every picker or default that starts a session (shared `offersSessions` rule). Preserve native model IDs and reasoning-effort metadata for setup.
- Include the required harness registration/migration, generated API types, official assets with attribution, docs and focused tests.

Intentional omissions:
- No Coder session interface or driver ships. Built-in server-side tools cannot currently be disabled by a local-only policy.
- PR-specific visual workflow/script and the unrelated Go workflow drift-check change are excluded.
- Native sign-in has not been completed against a live Coder deployment here; deployment and model access remain administrator-configured.

## Testing

Current head: `f5cc8f58116c983d2c3a73904c58294e7e434f38`. Current main at `adf9f6a303` was merged in (no rebase, no force-push) on top of the original head `7de7e42e`, followed by two fixes:

- `2edcf68c44` merge: 7 conflicts resolved (CLI exemptions and spawn help, task DTO enum with main's `baseBranch` and 100 KiB brief, Orchestrator wording in auth plans, migration ledger, TaskComposer account picks and stale-tuning reset). Two breaks that git merged silently were fixed: `coder login` now passes main's new working-directory argument to `RunInteractiveCommand`, and `coder-agents` gets a neutral tone in main's new `agent-tone.ts`.
- `eb32b27c95`: the Coder migration moves from `20261031044911564` (below 22 newer main migrations) to `20261114172907961`, above main's latest. It edits the CHECK text in place, and no later main migration rebuilds `sessions`.
- `f5cc8f5811`: Coder no longer appears in the project creation sheet, Project Settings worker/orchestrator, Automations, or the artifact-session and new-project defaults. Each of these offered any signed-in agent, so a connected Coder account could become a project default whose sessions always fail. Regression tests added. Each fails without the fix.

Passed locally on this head (Windows, Go 1.27.4, Node 24.18.0, CGO off so no `-race`):
- `go build ./...`, and `go vet` of the touched packages.
- Coder adapter/API, Chat registry, CLI, agentauth, systeminstall: all tests pass.
- Model catalog: both Coder tests pass. `TestQwenSharedCatalogMarksConfiguredProviders` fails identically on clean main.
- SQLite: Coder migration up/down/refusal, legacy repair, ledger and interleaved-version tests pass. Full package run sharded as CI does.
- SQLite store, chat and session manager, sharded 8 ways: everything passes or fails identically on clean main. That includes 303 first-prompt, restore and resume tests (755 with subtests). 19 Windows-host failures (paths, git, file locks, time zone) are the same set on main.
- `internal/httpd/...` (7 packages) in 40 s, including `TestBuild_MatchesEmbedded`. 3 controller tests (`file://` clone URL, rename race, file-vs-directory status) fail identically on main.
- `go generate` for the API spec and `npm run api:ts`: no drift in `openapi.yaml` or `schema.ts`.
- Frontend `npm run typecheck` passes. 10 focused suites pass (561 tests): TaskComposer, AgentSwitchPicker, AgentAvatar, useAgentReadinessQuery, CreateProjectAgentSheet, CreateProjectFlow, ProjectSettingsForm, AutomationsView, useCreateArtifactSession, agent-select-options.

Earlier SQLite/HTTP timeouts: the SQLite-backed packages serialize on the process-wide goose lock (`gooseMu`), so run as one `go test` process on Windows they overrun the default timeout. Sharded the way CI's `go-test-parallel.sh` does it, SQLite finishes in minutes, and the HTTP suites finish in 40 s. Running 8 shards next to the TypeScript typecheck also produced SQLite `out of memory (7)`, and all of those passed when rerun by name.

Validation gaps:
- Full renderer suite, `-race`, and native macOS/Linux runs were not done here. Current-head GitHub CI is still required (standard jobs are skipped while this is a draft).
- There is no Coder CLI or deployment on this host, so install, native login, Connected state and live model discovery are unverified.
- A Terminal-mode Coder request fails when the launch command is built (same as Unreal Agent), with no typed 4xx before that. Chat requests get `409 SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`. Making Terminal refusals typed is a shared session-service change, left as a follow-up.

This draft continues [original PR #7519](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7519) at original head `a689f7211418948ce5f8e588df4439360645d770`. Original commits and commit authorship are preserved. Descriptions and evidence below include historical results with their original sources.

## What

Adds [JCode](https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode) as a Terminal UI harness, including install/login actions, active-provider auth checks, native model discovery, activity hooks, exact conversation restore, token usage, official logos and API/storage registration.

This PR is a draft. Chat/ACP and reviewer roles remain intentionally unregistered.

## Why

Let AO launch and manage JCode sessions using the native CLI while preserving each worktree, conversation and provider configuration.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| JCode is unavailable in AO's harness picker. | JCode appears with its official logo, install/login actions, health and models. |
| No JCode lifecycle or usage integration. | Isolated session sockets, first-run handling, exact restore and native usage collection. |
| A project-only JCODE_HOME makes restore fall back to a fresh task. | Restore and update preflight inspect the original launch environment and continue the native conversation. |
| Project-specific native state roots are missed during usage collection and title probes. | Hook collection, backfill, finalization and title probes honor the project override. |
| One usage export covering turns on two models (missed hook, backfill, recreated ledger) attributes every turn to the session's latest model; non-Claude jcode usage is rejected by the store. | Each journaled message keeps its own entry's model and provider; the store accepts jcode's Anthropic- and OpenAI-normalized events. |
| Hooks repeatedly parse the full native history, and usage stops above 64 MiB. | Unchanged snapshots are cached, journal cursors advance incrementally, and usage continues past large tool output. |

[The corrected ten-image set is attached](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7519#issuecomment-6543527507): frames 01-07 are historical; 08-10 are from the successful CI capture on 29e5b778c: New Task agent picker, model picker and the UI-created TUI with the saved native reply NEW_TASK_OK ([final report](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7519#issuecomment-6544997678)). A before screenshot was not captured.

## How

- Register a TUI-only adapter with isolated private daemon sockets, including long AO data-directory handling.
- Preserve native hook arrays and read native hook payloads without replacing user hooks.
- Deliver initial prompts through the TUI, handle the first-run start choice, and use an owned prompt overlay for hidden instructions.
- Restore only exact native conversation IDs bound to the same working directory.
- Require a successful active-provider probe before reporting authorized; configured credentials alone remain configured. In native keyless Ollama mode, verify the selected model against the live loopback inventory and expose only models actually installed there.
- Discover native models, collect usage from native session messages, and install checksum-verified releases into AO-managed version directories.
- Include migrations, generated API types, UI assets and documentation.
- Resolve project JCODE_HOME for usage and native title reads. Keep exported usage ledgers under the existing AO-owned ingestion root.
- Attribute each journaled message to the model and provider in its own journal entry's `meta` (jcode stores no model on a message); snapshot messages take the snapshot's. Accept OpenAI- and Anthropic-normalized jcode events in the usage store.
- Offer jcode's documented `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment sources as Account setup methods (main's per-harness invariant). A published key reports configured, not authorized.
- Merge current main: drop the unshipped `allow_jcode_usage` migration (main's `open_usage_source_kinds` already accepts any usage harness/kind, and the old guard failed on installs that applied main first); renumber `allow_jcode_harness` above main's latest migration; use main's `RestoreConfig.Env` and `launchRuntimeEnvForHarness` while keeping the env-aware restore preflight.
- Stream snapshot messages, cache file versions and usage metadata, and resume journal reads from the last complete entry without a 64 MiB limit.
- Remove the PR-specific visual evidence workflow and script. Historical captures remain linked; no recurring model download job is added.

Intentional limitations:
- Chat/ACP and reviewer are excluded because the required native contracts have not been established.
- Native JCode can continue an interrupted turn when restored, including rerunning its command.
- The historical test credential reached inference only after a diagnostic JSON wrapper with a synthetic expiry. This does not prove bare Claude setup-token support.
- The strict historical authentication audit remained configured after native usage-probe rate limits/cancellation. It is not a full authenticated audit pass.

- Usage attribution is per journal entry, not per message: a `/model` switch inside one turn goes to the model of the next save, and messages read only from the snapshot take the snapshot's model (jcode rewrites the snapshot on a provider switch).

## Testing

Current head: `d75d6bc955c80fa982900ab87532d2b1f0bdbd27`. It merges main `adf9f6a303a6` without rewriting history, plus fixes for per-journal-entry attribution (a journal copy outranks the snapshot copy of the same message), jcode provider acceptance in the usage store, the migration renumber, and provider-key Account setup methods.

Local Windows checks (Go 1.27.4, Node 24.18.0) at `cfdbdeb`, the previous head:
- PASS: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/...`; OpenAPI regeneration shows no drift, and `schema.ts` adds `jcode` in the same three enums as the spec.
- PASS: every JCode test in `adapters/agent/jcode`, `service/usage`, `observe/usage` and `storage/sqlite`, including the two new two-model regressions (both fail when the fix is reverted) and the renumbered migration tests. The jcode adapter, agent registry and activity dispatch packages pass in the full run.
- Full `go test ./...` on this host: 162 packages ok, 65 failed. In a PR-vs-main comparison over 11 touched packages, the only real PR-only failure was main's new `TestEverySupportedHarnessHasAccountSetupMethod`, fixed in `c9fcbf5`. The other PR-only failures are symlink privilege, SQLite OOM under parallel suites, or timing flakes outside jcode code.
- Not run locally on `c9fcbf5` or `d75d6bc` (no further local runs authorized). Remote CI must confirm it.
- Not valid on this host: golangci-lint 2.13.2 (built with go1.27.1) cannot read go1.27.4 export data. Frontend typecheck and vitest were not run (no `node_modules`). No race or container runs (no CGO).

Remote CI for this head awaits maintainer approval of the fork runs (CI, gitleaks, Public boundary, Harness release feeds).

The successful New Task capture on 29e5b778c used keyless local Ollama/Qwen3:1.7b; it does not prove hosted-provider sign-in or bare Claude setup-token support. The strict authentication audit remained configured after provider rate limits/cancellation. Chat/ACP and reviewer roles remain unregistered.

body:
Code changes: +1347 -9  
Tests: +821 -3

> Account migration from @nikhilachale to @milesatao-svg. This draft continues [original PR #7093](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7093) at original head `290a39bc8201b3eeab8fa1ce5d80b62f443c670a`. Original commits and commit authorship are preserved. Descriptions and evidence below include historical results with their original sources.

## What

feat: add Stakpak Agent TUI harness

<details>
<summary>Original PR description, preserved</summary>

## What

Adds [Stakpak Agent](https://github.com/stakpak/agent) (qualified on 0.3.88) as a **Terminal UI** harness. This is a new integration; it replaces the closed #6550.

| Area | How |
|---|---|
| Launch | `stakpak --system-prompt-file <file> [--model <m>]`. The TUI ignores a positional prompt, so AO types the first task once the composer footer (`$ shell \| / commands`) is drawn. Keys typed during Stakpak's ~3 s startup are lost, Enter included. |
| Status | No external hooks exist, so status comes from the rendered screen. A footer with `esc cancel` means active, the idle footer means idle, and an `Approval Required` box means blocked. |
| Session ID | Read from `stakpak sessions list --json`, matched by worktree (symlink-resolved) and launch time. |
| Restore | `--session <id>` after `stakpak sessions show` confirms the conversation still exists; otherwise a fresh launch. Instructions the conversation already stores are not re-sent, because Stakpak re-inserts `--system-prompt-file` on every resume. |
| Permissions | `.stakpak/session/auto_approve.json`, with a `.gitignore` and an AO marker. accept-edits approves `create`/`str_replace`/`remove`; auto and bypass approve every non-shell tool. A manual launch removes AO's file, and a policy file the user wrote is left alone. |
| Auth | Verified with a provider round-trip. A Stakpak key is checked by `stakpak auth status`'s API check. Bring-your-own-key profiles are checked by asking each provider of the active profile whether it accepts its key, without spending tokens: `GET /models` for OpenAI-compatible and custom endpoints, an empty Messages request for Anthropic-compatible ones. |
| Install / update / login | Homebrew tap `stakpak/stakpak/stakpak` or the official `install.sh` on macOS/Linux; manual release zip on Windows. Update with `stakpak update`, log in with `stakpak auth login`. |
| Models | Free text, forwarded as `--model`. |
| Wiring | Domain constant, registry, migration `20261108105252617_allow_stakpak_harness` plus schema repair, DTO/OpenAPI/schema enums, doctor probe, spawn help, avatar (Apache-2.0 mark), docs. |

### Not supported, with proof

- **Chat.** Stakpak's ACP `session/load` only records the session id; it never reloads or replays the stored messages (`cli/src/commands/acp/server.rs`, `load_session`), so a restored Chat would continue without its history. The ACP model list also omits custom providers, and a profile model without an `anthropic/`, `openai/` or `google/` prefix is routed to the Stakpak API.
- **Unattended shell commands.** Stakpak always prompts before `run_command`: it forces the base rule back to `Prompt` when loading the policy, and scoped rules match only by command name. In every AO mode shell commands wait for a human, and AO reports the session as blocked.
- **Unattended version refresh.** Off, because the session id is inferred rather than reported by a hook.

## Live audit (ao-agent-harness skill, #7081)

Run against this branch, using Z.ai GLM through Z.ai's Anthropic-compatible endpoint:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| cli_installed, cli_version, cli_login | PASS |
| ao_registered, ao_installed | PASS |
| ao_authenticated | PASS (authorized, not just configured) |
| ao_models | PASS (free-form) |
| tui_spawn | PASS |
| role_worker, role_orchestrator | PASS (AO's system prompt reaches Stakpak) |
| tui_prompt | FAIL: the task was delivered and the agent started, then stopped at Stakpak's approval for `pwd`. AO showed the session as `blocked`. This is the upstream shell-approval behaviour above. |
| tui_worktree … tui_restore_history | SKIP (depend on tui_prompt) |

Done by hand in tmux, not through AO: resume by id keeps history and follows the instructions; Esc cancels a running command; frames captured for idle, draft, working, approval and side panel (used in the unit tests).

Found by the audit and fixed here: the first task was typed before the TUI was ready. `waitForPromptReadiness` sends immediately when an adapter gives no text pattern, despite what the port comment says.

Known upstream behaviour: Stakpak redacts token-like strings in prompts, and by default appends `.stakpak/session*` to the worktree `.gitignore` (`auto_append_gitignore`).

## Verification

No local test run; CI verifies. New tests: `adapters/agent/stakpak` (terminal frames, launch/restore argv, session matching, auth probes against `httptest`, permission file), the migration, the install plan, auth plan and registry/wiring entries.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)








</details>

## Why

The contributor is moving this harness submission to @milesatao-svg. The linked source preserves the implementation and review history.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Submission in [PR #7093](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/7093) from @nikhilachale at `290a39bc8201b3eeab8fa1ce5d80b62f443c670a` | Submission from @milesatao-svg at the same commit `290a39bc8201b3eeab8fa1ce5d80b62f443c670a` |

Original product behavior and existing UI evidence are included in the preserved description and copied evidence comments.

## How

## Testing

Freebuff has no qualified private channel, so spawn and restore of any session carrying them (every worker/orchestrator) fail before writing Freebuff state, with `STANDING_INSTRUCTIONS_UNSUPPORTED`. Freebuff sessions therefore cannot start until a private channel is qualified with live evidence. Statements below about standing instructions in the first turn, and the historical runtime results, describe earlier heads. Receipt: see the latest PR comment.

Code changes: +2093 -94

Original commits and commit authorship are preserved. Descriptions and evidence below include historical results with their original sources.

## What

feat: add Freebuff TUI harness with login, auth check and model picker

<details>
<summary>Original PR description, preserved</summary>

Registers [Freebuff](https://freebuff.com) as a Terminal UI harness. The compiled catalog was qualified against the public 0.2.30 source; local native validation used the installed 0.2.32 binary. This replaces the earlier guarded, unregistered qualification hold.

## What works

| Area | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Install | Settings → Harnesses offers npm install, update and uninstall (`freebuff`). `ao doctor` probes `freebuff --version`. |
| Auth check | Local credentials are **configured**, not provider-verified, when the default profile contains a token/keychain pointer or `CODEBUFF_API_KEY` is set. Missing credentials are **unauthorized**. Effective `$FREEBUFF_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the default `~/.config/manicode`. |
| Login | **Log in to Freebuff** runs `freebuff login` (browser flow; the URL is also printed) in the harness auth terminal. |
| Models | Freebuff's 12-row `/model` picker, with MiMo v2.6 Flash Fast as the default. Each row carries its own reasoning ladder (DeepSeek low/high/max, GPT-6 Luna low…xhigh, and so on). |
| Applying model/effort | AO serializes startup per effective config directory, seeds the canonical model and migration stamp, then confirms the process-local model and effort through the running native picker. The guard remains held through first-turn acceptance. Settings preflight is side-effect free and `null` settings are handled safely. |
| Messages | First turns, follow-ups and lifecycle notifications use one native bracketed paste at the final guarded terminal write. Semantic prompt history is kept free of terminal frames; embedded escape sequences are rejected. Empty Enter-only nudges and other harnesses retain their protocol. |
| Launch | `freebuff --cwd <worktree>`. After confirming the current empty native composer, AO uses one native bracketed paste for the complete first turn. It reports successful delivery only after Freebuff saves the complete recent user turn, including its native pasted-text wrapper. |
| Standing instructions | Freebuff has no system-prompt input, so AO sends them with the task as one first turn, the same approach as fx. |
| Activity | Derived conservatively from the complete current native composer/footer and anchored running status. Transcript quotations, drafts and historical empty composers do not establish activity; styled cursor evidence is required for empty-input confirmation. |
| Restore | `freebuff --cwd <worktree> --continue <chat-id>`. Restore lookup and update-when-idle preflight use the effective session environment, including project `FREEBUFF_CONFIG_DIR`. The chat is matched by the `projectRoot` recorded in its `run-state.json`, because worktrees sharing a basename share a chats dir. With no match AO starts fresh rather than letting `--continue` pick an unrelated chat. |
| Registration | Domain enum, registry, sqlite CHECK migration plus schema repair, API enums (`openapi.yaml`, `schema.ts`), avatar (official Freebuff mark), product-ui label, docs (`docs/harnesses/freebuff.md`, agents table, spawn skill). |

## Not supported

Chat (ACP) mode, reviewer sessions, per-session tool allow/deny lists (Freebuff has no such input), logout from Settings (Freebuff only has an in-TUI `/logout`), and unattended terminal refresh on a new release.

## Verification

**Rebased head `cecef0feb` onto `main` at `a95139bb` (22 October 2026): merge conflicts are resolved; all 24 checks passed at this head.** [PR checks](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6553/checks). Both generated API files were regenerated together. Two stale CI assertions now check the combined harness set.

Local Go 1.27.1 build/vet, complete Freebuff/Hermes/terminal-guard/domain/launch-helper/installer race suites, all 31 cases in SQLite race shard 3, and five Freebuff/Cursor task-form regressions passed. The complete run is not counted as a pass.

title: fix(review): use a new session id when the Claude reviewer's derived id is taken
body:
Code changes: +30 -4\
Tests: +35 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A fresh Claude Code reviewer launch uses a new session id when the id derived from the reviewer already has a conversation.

## Why

`ReviewCommand` always passed `--session-id` with the id derived from the reviewer (`SessionUUID(inv.ReviewerID)`), which is the same for every fresh launch of a worker's reviewer. Once that conversation exists, Claude Code refuses to start. A trigger with a config override clears the saved id (`review.go`, `launchAgentSessionID = ""`), so `ao review trigger --effort high` takes the fresh path on every pass after the first.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Second `ao review trigger --effort high` for a worker: the reviewer pane prints `Error: Session ID 2ce4cddf-b554-5a08-88dd-8f0d19a95466 is already in use.`, only a placeholder `cat` runs in the pane, and the run stays `running`. Seen on nightly 0.14.11-nightly.202611111839 for 2 h 27 min and 7 h 43 min until cancelled. | The reviewer starts with a new id, and that id is saved as the reviewer's conversation id. |

## How

- `freshSessionID` probes `NativeConversationExists` for the derived id and asks the agent for a new id when it is taken. The id returned in `ReviewCommandSpec.AgentSessionID` is the one launched with, so later restores resume the right conversation.
- A reviewer with no conversation yet keeps the derived id, as before.
- `Preflight` builds a command with no reviewer id, so the probe is skipped there.
- Not covered: a reviewer agent that exits for another reason still leaves its run `running`, because the pane stays alive and `Alive` checks the pane.

## Testing

- Claude Code 2.1.322: `claude -p ... --session-id 2ce4cddf-b554-5a08-88dd-8f0d19a95466` in the worker checkout prints `Error: Session ID 2ce4cddf-b554-5a08-88dd-8f0d19a95466 is already in use.`, the failure this PR avoids.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/... ./internal/review/...`: pass. Two new tests: a taken derived id yields a new id that is both launched and returned; a free derived id is kept.
- Locally, as in `go.yml`: `gofmt -l .` empty, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, golangci-lint v2.14.0 on the package (0 issues). `go test -race ./...`: 211 packages pass. Four OpenCode packages (`modelcatalog`, `agent/opencodev2`, `opencodev2acp`, `reviewer/opencodev2`) fail on this Mac on `main` as well; `runtime/tmux` fails only because this branch predates #8143. CI passes.
- Not run end to end in the app.

body:
Code changes: +0 -0\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +110 -1 (docs content)

## What

A new guide, **Use Vercel AI Gateway** (`/guides/vercel-ai-gateway/`). It shows how to route Claude Code and Codex sessions through Vercel AI Gateway using a project's **Environment** variables, how to check that it works, how to split spend per project with one key each, and the caveats.

## Why

Step 25 of the backlinks plan. Vercel's AI Gateway docs have a "coding agents" section with dofollow pages for desktop agent tools. Our own tested guide comes first; then we pitch Vercel to add an Orchestrator page that copies it.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| No docs on using a model gateway with Orchestrator | Guide with the Claude Code and Codex setups, a check step, per-project keys, and caveats. Listed in Guides and its nav. |

## How

Every Orchestrator claim was checked against the code on `main`:
- **Project Environment reaches every agent:** `ProjectConfig.Env` (`backend/internal/domain/projectconfig.go`) is merged by `agentlaunch.MergeEnv` (`backend/internal/agentlaunch/env.go`). That covers worker and orchestrator spawns, restore and relaunch, Chat/ACP, interface switches, reviewers, shell terminals and `postCreate`.
- **Empty values survive both launch paths:** tmux writes `export KEY=''`, and ACP lays the project values over `os.Environ()`. That's what makes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` work.
- **The UI wording matches the app:** Project settings → **Environment** (`settings.project.environment*` strings). Values are stored unencrypted, and running processes keep their old values.
- **CLI:** `ao project set-config <id> --env KEY=VALUE`. `--env` replaces the whole map (`backend/internal/cli/project.go`), which the page warns about.
- **Shell variables:** the desktop app loads the login shell's environment at start (`frontend/src/shared/shell-env.ts`).
- **Separate agent accounts:** a non-device Claude account blanks `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` when they're in the daemon's environment, and a Codex account sets its own `CODEX_HOME` (`backend/internal/adapters/agentaccount/{claude,codex}.go`). The page tells those users to use the project's Environment, and notes the Codex config caveat.

## Testing

**The gateway settings, tested for real against a stand-in gateway.** There's no AI Gateway key to use, so I ran a local HTTP server that records each request's path and auth header (key values truncated), then pointed the real CLIs at it with exactly the settings the page gives. Throwaway `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME` dirs kept them away from real logins.

| Agent and settings | Request the agent sent |
|---|---|
| Claude Code 2.1.319: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=…/coding-agent`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=test-gateway-key`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` | `POST /coding-agent/v1/messages?beta=true`, `Authorization: Bearer test-g…`, **no** `x-api-key` |
| Same, but `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-fake…` | Same path and Bearer token, **plus** `x-api-key: sk-ant…`, so the direct key leaks to the gateway. This is why the page says to keep it empty. |
| Codex CLI 0.154.0: a fresh `CODEX_HOME` holding only `config.toml` with the `vercel` provider block, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=test-gateway-key` (the page's "One project only" setup) | `POST /codex/v1/responses`, `Authorization: Bearer test-g…`, model `openai/gpt-6-astra` |

**Not tested:** a live request through Vercel's own gateway (needs a real key), and a run inside the Orchestrator desktop app (not installed on this machine). How the app passes these variables on is from the code cited above, not from a run.

**Pass 1 — local build** (`frontend/src/docs`, on 12 Nov `main`): `npm ci && npm run build` passes; vitest: 7 tests pass. `out/guides/vercel-ai-gateway/index.html` exists and the Guides index links it. The four Vercel URLs on the page return 200.
