title: feat(mobile): show pull requests as an inset-grouped list
body: Code changes: +236 -129\ Tests: +179 -62\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The mobile Pull Requests page is now an inset-grouped list. Each section ("Ready to merge", "Needs attention", "In review", "Merged") is one rounded card, and its heading shows the count. - **Title first.** A conventional-commit prefix (`fix(mobile):`) comes off the title, which gets two lines instead of one. - **One status, only when it matters.** The line under the title shows `#number` and a single status: merge conflicts, the failing check by name ("android-build failed"), changes requested, unresolved comments, checks running, or ready to merge. Otherwise it shows the scope, or the repo when the list spans more than one. - **Age and disclosure.** The last-updated age sits at the trailing edge, with the iOS chevron. - **Per platform.** iOS draws one card with hairline separators inset to the text (26pt corners). Android draws Material 3's connected list, the shape `composeGroupedList` already uses: 20dp ends, 4dp joins, 2dp gaps, no chevron. ## Why The old rows spent two of their four lines on the repo name and branch, the same on every row, and cut the title to one line. "review required" was printed in amber on every open PR. It is every open PR's normal state and its section already says it, so amber stopped meaning anything and a real problem didn't stand out. Status was split across the icon colour, the top-right text and the amber line. ## Before / After Same screen and data on both sides, captured from the real app with a temporary preview route (removed). Before is `main`. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ## How - `prView.ts`: `prRowTitle` splits the conventional-commit prefix off; `prRowStatus` picks the one status a row shows, or none. They replace `prSummaryLine` and `prBlockerLine`, which only the card used. The status and the row's glyph read the board facts the section is chosen from (`prRowLifecycle`): the board re-polls every few seconds while the summary is fetched once per visit, so a summary fact would contradict the row's section. The summary adds only the failing checks' names, while the board still says failing, and facts a board row lacks entirely; the board's "unknown" merge state counts as an answer, and "Ready to merge" reads the same `mergeable` flag the section does. - `groupedRow.ts`: a row's position in its section → its corners, from a new `groupedCorner` platform token. Android's Compose grouped lists (`composeGroupedList`: machine detail, new project form, conversation actions) now take their positions, corners and gap from it too, replacing their private copies with the same values, so the shape is defined once per platform. - `PRCard.tsx`: the row layout above, plus `PRSectionHeader`. The long-press menu (SwiftUI context menu on iOS, Material dropdown on Android), accessibility actions and navigation are unchanged. - Inside the iOS context menu's SwiftUI host, a bare `flex: 1` on the row content kept the text's intrinsic width and the title ran off the card on one line. The content takes explicit `flexGrow`/`flexShrink`/`flexBasis: 0` and `minWidth: 0`. - `app/prs/index.tsx` passes each row its position, one per-minute `useNow` clock for ages, and whether to name the repo. - The branch name and diff size are off the row; the PR page shows both. ## Testing - `npm run typecheck` (packages/mobile) - `npx vitest run`: 417 files, 4030 tests pass. New tests cover `prRowTitle`, `prRowStatus`, `groupedRow` and the card's title, status and accessibility label. - iOS 26.5 simulator (Debug build from this branch): dark, light, Open / Merged / All, scrolling under the glass bar, long-press menu. - Android 15 emulator (debug build of the same base): dark, light, long-press dropdown. The ripple on the rounded rows was not captured. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Pull request lists now use grouped rows with section headings and platform-specific styling. * Rows show repository context when needed, relative update age, and status details such as failing checks and conflicts. * Pull request titles omit conventional commit prefixes, and accessibility labels include row context and update age. * **Changes** * Branch, diff, and blocker details are no longer shown in pull request rows. * **Bug Fixes** * Plain review-waiting statuses are no longer displayed in pull request rows.

title: [Bug]: Copilot authentication readiness reports unknown despite successful OAuth login and ACP execution
body:
### What went wrong?

# Bug: Copilot authentication readiness reports unknown despite successful OAuth login and ACP execution

## Environment

- Orchestrator: `v0.14.10` (`033d597032e4`)
- GitHub Copilot CLI: `1.0.109`
- OS: Windows 11
- Installation: Official npm Copilot CLI
- Authentication: Official GitHub OAuth device flow

## Actual behavior

Orchestrator displays `Login status unavailable` under **Settings → Harness → GitHub Copilot → Account**.

The backend readiness endpoint returns:

```text
installation.state = installed
authentication.state = unknown
reasonCode = auth_check_inconclusive
diagnostic = check_inconclusive
cached = false
```

However, the existing Copilot credentials are functional:

- Official OAuth sign-in completed successfully.
- Copilot ACP Chat starts and produces real model responses.
- A synthetic coding task completed successfully (2/2 tests).
- Native ACP session resume preserved the provider session ID and conversation context.

## Root cause

In `backend/internal/adapters/agent/copilot/auth.go`:

1. `copilotConfigAuthStatus` parses `~/.copilot/config.json` using strict `encoding/json`, but Copilot CLI 1.0.109 produces a configuration containing JSONC-style comments.
2. `copilotStoredAuthStatus` ignores the parsing error and falls through to other authentication sources.
3. `copilotLoggedInUser` expects `loggedInUsers` to be a map, while the observed configuration uses an array of account objects.
4. The normal OAuth credential is stored in the operating system's credential store, so the configuration does not contain a plaintext authentication token.
5. On a machine without an additional GitHub CLI authentication fallback, readiness remains `unknown`.

The frontend correctly renders the backend state. The issue is in the authentication readiness probe, not the UI mapping.

## Sanitized configuration structure

The observed configuration uses JSONC comments and an array of login metadata:

```jsonc
{
  // Copilot configuration comment
  "loggedInUsers": [
    {
      "host": "github.com",
      "login": "example-user",
      "kind": "..."
    }
  ]
}
```

This is illustrative only; no credentials or actual account identifiers are included.

## Expected behavior

The readiness probe should recognize supported Copilot CLI configuration formats and provide a more accurate account status without exposing, copying, or modifying credentials.

Account metadata should be distinguished from verified credential validity. A stale account entry alone should not be sufficient proof of current authorization.

## Suggested fix

- Support the actual Copilot JSONC configuration format, preserving strings and URLs correctly.
- Support both legacy map-based and current array-based `loggedInUsers` structures.
- Preserve existing token environment variable precedence, GitHub CLI fallback, and BYOK behavior.
- Avoid accessing or exposing operating-system credential secrets.
- Distinguish account configuration evidence from positively verified authentication.
- Add regression tests for JSONC parsing, array/map compatibility, malformed configuration, empty/stale accounts, and existing authentication sources.

## Impact

This is a non-blocking readiness/reporting defect.

Copilot execution works, but the Harness Account UI incorrectly suggests that login status is unavailable, reducing the reliability of multi-harness operational monitoring.

No changes to Copilot credentials or the installed Orchestrator are required to reproduce the issue.

title: fix: Files Changed dead links outside the workspace, and +0 counts for new files
body:
## Summary

Two user-reported issues in the chat's Files Changed card and the Files explorer.

**1. Clicking a file the agent wrote outside the worktree opened a dead tab.**
Claude Code keeps project memory under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. Those writes appear in the turn's diff, so the Files Changed card listed them as links. Clicking one opened a tab that could only say "This file is outside the session's workspace, so it can't be opened here."

- The daemon now marks a turn-diff file `outsideWorkspace` when it records the diff: an absolute path in neither the session worktree nor its artifact dir. Symlinked spellings of the worktree still count as inside. The flag is stored in the existing JSON column, so there is no migration.
- The card still lists those files (the turn did write them), with a passive "Outside workspace" label and the full path on hover. It no longer offers them as links.
- Turns recorded before this change carry no flag. For those, a click the daemon resolves as `outside` now shows a toast instead of opening a dead tab. Markdown links to outside paths get the same treatment.
- No Sentry event is added. That screen is a deliberate guard, not an exception, so the fix is to stop offering the link.

**2. New files showed `+0 −0` in the Files explorer.**
In a non-git (scratch) workspace, the Files list hard-coded `Additions: 0` for every file. Opening the same file showed its real count (e.g. `+11`). The list now counts lines the same way `GetWorkspaceFile` does. The existing 8 KB binary sniff already holds small files whole, so only larger text files are reread.

title: fix(cli): start the desktop app with open stdio instead of closed fds
body:
Code changes: +9 -2\
Tests: +95 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

`ao start` on Linux and Windows now starts the desktop app with stdout and stderr on `/dev/null` (or `NUL`) instead of closed.

This revives #6317 by priyanshujaiz, which closed as stale with one change request open. The fix is theirs. This PR adds the regression test that the review asked for.

## Why

Fixes #6261

`openApp` leaves `Stdout` and `Stderr` unset in `processStartConfig`. `startProcess` copied those nil `*os.File` values into `exec.Cmd`'s `io.Writer` fields, which makes a non-nil interface holding a nil pointer. `os/exec` then passes that as "no file", so the child starts with fds 1 and 2 closed.

The AppImage runtime opens its keepalive pipe on those free fds. The FUSE side redirects 0-2 to `/dev/null` when it daemonizes, which replaces the pipe. The keepalive thread then writes to `/dev/null` forever and holds one CPU core at 100% while the app runs (#6261 has the full trace).

## Before / After

| Before (main) | After |
| --- | --- |
| Child started by `startProcess` with no streams: `0=open 1=closed 2=closed` | `0=open 1=open 2=open` |

No UI change. On Linux AppImage installs, the AppImage runtime should stop using a full core. I could not measure that here (no Linux machine), so it is not claimed as tested.

## How

- `startProcess` assigns `cmd.Stdout` and `cmd.Stderr` only when the file is non-nil, so `os/exec` uses its `/dev/null` default. The fix sits in `startProcess` rather than `openApp`, so future callers are covered too.
- `TestStartProcessGivesChildOpenStdioWhenNoStreams` starts a `/bin/sh` child that checks `/dev/fd/0..2` and writes the result to a file. It must be a shell: a Go child reopens closed fds 0-2 on `/dev/null` at startup and would hide the bug (Vaibhaav-Tiwari's point on #6317).
- Both tests poll for their output file instead of sleeping 500 ms (axisrow's and Vaibhaav-Tiwari's point).
- The tests are Unix-only (`process_unix_test.go`). The fix also applies on Windows, but Windows CI runs only selected tests, and `cmd` cannot check its handles this way.

## Testing

On macOS arm64, Go 1.27.4:

- New test against main's `process.go`: fails with `child stdio = "0=open 1=closed 2=closed"`, using both `/bin/sh` (bash 3.2) and `/bin/dash` (Ubuntu CI's `/bin/sh`). It passes with the fix under both shells.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli/...`: pass.
- `go test -tags e2e -count=1 ./internal/cli/...`: pass.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint v2.14.0 run ./...`: clean.
- Not run locally: Linux and Windows. CI's ubuntu `backend-core` job runs the new test.

title: feat(mobile): choose the branch and changes Files compares
body: Code changes: +1434 -100\ Tests: +649 -6\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The mobile Files screen can now choose what it compares, as the desktop Files review does: - **Branch:** the checked-out branch, any other local or remote branch, or the session's pull request. The list is searchable, with the newest branches first. When another branch or PR is picked, the Changes list, All files, search and the file viewer all read from it, read-only. - **Changes:** *All since * (the existing view, still the default), *Uncommitted*, *Staged*, *Unstaged*, *All commits*, or one commit. Each row shows its file and line counts. A file opened from the list keeps the pick: its diff, previous/next, before/after images, and a line under the title naming what it compares (for example `Unstaged` or `untrivial/main · a2fb990`). A file opened from chat keeps the default view. Both platforms use their native picker sheets: a SwiftUI Form with checkmarks on iOS, Material radio rows on Android. ## Why Before this, mobile always compared the worktree with its base. You couldn't look at only the uncommitted work, a single commit, or what another branch or the session's PR changes, all of which desktop already offers. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | No way to pick which changes to show | | | No way to pick another branch or the PR | | | Only the worktree's changes | | | Only the combined uncommitted list | | | A file always opened on base → worktree | | Captured from the real app (iOS 26 simulator Debug build, Android emulator debug build) against a real daemon session, through a read-only proxy. "Before" is the same build running `main`'s JS. The bottom edge of some captures is cropped to remove the dev build's warning toast. ## How - **No daemon behaviour change** (one daemon test added, below). `workspace/branches`, `workspace/history`, `workspace/history/selection` and the snapshot reads of `workspace/file`, `/tree` and `/file/blob` already exist; the desktop uses them. - **A view is a backend.** `FilesBackend.git.at(view)` returns the same daemon backend with its file/tree/search/image reads pinned to a branch or PR (`snapshot=true`, plus `branch` or `prNumber`/`sourceUrl`). That way `FolderList`, search and the file viewer follow the pick unchanged. A view has no search route, so search uses the snapshot tree's `filter`. - **The pick travels as route params** (`branch`, `pr`, `prUrl`, `changes`, `commit`), parsed in `lib/files/selection.ts`. The default carries none, so links into Files from chat behave exactly as before. Each listed file is read with its own diff: a worktree section (untracked files in Unstaged read `section=untracked`), `commitSha`, or the view's whole range. - **Comments say what they were made on.** Each target carries the pick as `source` and `scope`, in desktop's wording (`Workspace` / `Branch ` / `PR #n (url)`; `combined`, `staged`, `commit `, …). The shared formatter sends them as `Source:` and `Comparison scope:`. Inline comments and row counts show only in the pick they were made in. - **A worktree scope reads its own sides.** The file route's `section` only scopes its git diff, so Staged, Unstaged, Uncommitted, Untracked and All commits read like desktop's review instead: `workspace/diffs` for the scope's patch (status and counts parsed from it) and `workspace/file/revision` for its after side (the index, HEAD or the worktree) as the content, fenced to the patch's `workspaceVersion` and re-read as a pair if the worktree moves in between. Commits and other branches use the snapshot file route. - **Gated by capability.** The pickers appear only when the backend has `git` (not Orchestrator Cloud), the manifest lists `sections.uncommitted` (not an older daemon), and `workspace/branches` reports `supported` (not a scratch session). Otherwise the screen is unchanged. The first two are settled once per machine, so a degraded manifest poll keeps the pick. A branch list that failed to load is retried on pull to refresh. - **Keyed on `backend.key`, not the backend object.** The app rebuilds the backend when its connection state refreshes. On a large worktree (a 2.4 MB manifest plus 1 MB of history) a read keyed on the object kept restarting and never finished. The changes sheet also reuses the manifest the Files screen just polled instead of downloading it again. - `NativePickerList` gains optional section titles (consecutive options sharing `section`), used to split *Working tree* from *Commits*. Reviewers: `lib/files/selection.ts` (what each pick lists and reads), `lib/files/useChangeList.ts` (loading and polling), and `app/files/[sessionId]/index.tsx`. **Intentional omissions** - One commit at a time. Desktop can tick several commits and combine them, which brings in conflict handling (`combinable` / `not_combinable`). That's left out on phones for now. - Another branch or PR is re-read every 30 s while shown, as desktop does. Nothing pushes its moves. - The picked pull request row wasn't exercised live because the lab session has no PR. It's covered by unit tests (params, `viewOf`, labels) and uses the same snapshot path as a branch. - Image previews for a worktree scope (Staged, Unstaged, Uncommitted, and All commits on the checked-out branch) show "No image preview for ". The blob route only reads base → worktree or a snapshot, and the scoped revision route drops binary content, so no daemon route serves those sides yet. All changes, single commits, other branches/PRs, and untracked files keep their image comparison. Turning the rest on needs a daemon follow-up. - JS only: no native modules and no `package.json` change, so this can ship as an over-the-air update. ## Testing - `packages/mobile`, as the Mobile workflow runs it, on Node 20: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` → 4072 tests pass. `scripts/ci-lanes.mjs` selects only the `mobile` lane for this diff. - \`go test ./internal/service/session/\` passes, including the new `TestScopedReadsKeepToTheirScopeWhenBaseHeadIndexAndWorktreeDiffer`: base, HEAD, the index and the worktree all differ, All commits stops at HEAD, Staged shows an edit the combined diff can't, and Staged numbers lines by the index. Also checked against a live daemon: the old `section=committed` read included an uncommitted edit; the scoped read doesn't. - `npx expo export --platform ios` and `--platform android` both bundle. - New tests: `selection.test.ts` (param round-trips, per-file reads, grouping for each pick), `compareOptions.test.ts` (sheet rows, counts, search), `api.test.ts` (URLs for views, commits and range selection), `NativePickerList.test.tsx` (sections on both platforms). - Manual, on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator against a real session with 199 branches, 250 commits and dirty/untracked files: the default view; Unstaged (an untracked file opens via `section=untracked`); one commit (list, diff, previous/next within the commit); another branch's commits (range selection, file diff, All files tree from the snapshot); branch search; switching back to the checked-out branch resets to the default. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Browse files by branch or pull request, and compare changes across commits or working-tree scopes. * Choose a branch and change range with dedicated pickers; file lists, details, search results, and folder navigation reflect your selection. * View change summaries in comparison controls, with picker options organized into labeled sections. * See loading, error, and empty states for branches, commits, and working-tree changes. * Branch views refresh periodically while the Files screen is active.

title: fix: Files Changed dead links outside the workspace, and +0 counts for new files
body:
## Summary

Two user-reported issues in the chat's Files Changed card and the Files explorer.

**1. Clicking a file the agent wrote outside the worktree opened a dead tab.**
Claude Code keeps project memory under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. Those writes appear in the turn's diff, so the Files Changed card listed them as links. Clicking one opened a tab that could only say "This file is outside the session's workspace, so it can't be opened here."

- The daemon now marks a turn-diff file `outsideWorkspace` when it records the diff: an absolute path in neither the session worktree nor its artifact dir. Symlinked spellings of the worktree still count as inside. The flag is stored in the existing JSON column, so there is no migration.
- The card still lists those files (the turn did write them), with a passive "Outside workspace" label and the full path on hover. It no longer offers them as links.
- Turns recorded before this change carry no flag. For those, a click the daemon resolves as `outside` now shows a toast instead of opening a dead tab. Markdown links to outside paths get the same treatment.
- No Sentry event is added. That screen is a deliberate guard, not an exception, so the fix is to stop offering the link.

**2. New files showed `+0 −0` in the Files explorer.**
In a non-git (scratch) workspace, the Files list hard-coded `Additions: 0` for every file. Opening the same file showed its real count (e.g. `+11`). The list now counts lines the same way `GetWorkspaceFile` does. The existing 8 KB binary sniff already holds small files whole, so only larger text files are reread.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/service/chat/ ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/domain/`: pass
- New: `TestPathOutsideSession` (relative, inside, symlinked worktree, artifact dir, outside, shared-prefix sibling, unknown worktree) and `TestTurnDiffMarksFilesOutsideTheWorkspace` (end-to-end through the controller and store)
- Updated: `TestListWorkspaceFilesScratchUsesFilesystem` now expects real counts, including a file larger than the sniff
- `golangci-lint v2.14.0` on the changed packages: 0 issues; `go vet` clean
- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- vitest: `TurnChangedFiles` (new outside-row test), `SessionView` and `SessionView.remote` (outside → toast), plus the chat, FileContentPane and SessionFileExplorer suites. `ChatWorkspace` "scroll away from a find result" failed once under full-suite load and passes on its own; it is unrelated code.
- `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` regenerated (one field)

## Risks / follow-ups

- Outside files are listed but not viewable in AO. Showing them read-only would mean letting the daemon serve a path outside the session, which loosens a security boundary on purpose. Left as a separate decision.
- The scratch list now reads text files over 8 KB up to 256 KB to count lines. Untracked files in git workspaces already do this.

title: feat(sessions): show PRs a session reviews or contributes to without owning them
body:
Code changes: +1125 -4\
Tests: +719 -0\
Others: +674 -0 (generated OpenAPI/TS schema/sqlc, i18n catalogs, docs)

## What

A session can now show a PR it **reviews** or **contributes to** without owning it. The board card, sidebar hover card, inspector Pull request section, and `ao session get` show "Reviewing #8020" or "Contributing to #8020", with the PR's title, state, author, and a link out. This works for branches outside the session namespace and for pushes from side worktrees.

A related PR is display-only. It never takes ownership, never sends review comments or CI results to the session, never changes the session's status, PR progress, or lifecycle, and never conflicts with another session's claim.

Refs #5986, #6864

## Why

When a session reviews or rebuilds someone else's PR, its card shows nothing about it. For example, a session reviewed #8020 (another contributor's branch), then merged main into it, redesigned it, and pushed two commits from a side worktree. Its card showed only its own branch and its own PR. Work on someone else's PR should count as that session's work on that PR.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A session that reviewed or pushed to another contributor's PR showed only its own branch/PRs | Board card, hover card and inspector show "Reviewing #N" / "Contributing to #N" with title, state, author and a link |
| `ao session get` listed only owned PRs | Adds a `related prs (not owned):` block |
| No way to record the relation | `ao session link-pr [<id>] <pr> --as reviewing\|contributing` and `ao session unlink-pr [<id>] <pr>`; `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/pr/link` / `pr/unlink`; `prLinks` on the session view |
| `ao review trigger --pr <url>` from session A against session B's PR left no trace on A | A shows "Reviewing #N" |

Screenshots not attached: this change was written without running the app (see Testing). A reviewer should capture the board card, hover card, and inspector after linking a PR.

## How

**Storage.** A new `session_pr_links` table, separate from `pr`, with one row per session and canonical PR URL. That keeps it out of everything that reads owned PRs: status, observer, CI/review routing, merge, and lifecycle. Title, state, and author are copied from the provider when the link is made. Its CDC triggers emit `session_updated` on insert, update, and delete. The cap is 20 links per session.

**Signals.**
- `reviewing` is set automatically when `ao review trigger` runs from session A against another session's PR. It uses the caller-session header the CLI already sends. The trigger adds a link only if none exists, so it never overwrites a link someone set. A session reviewing its own PR records nothing, since the existing refresh already attaches that PR as owned.
- Both relations can be set explicitly with `ao session link-pr <pr> --as reviewing|contributing`. The worker prompt and the using-ao skill tell agents to run it after pushing to a PR outside their namespace, or when starting a review. The orchestrator prompt lists it too. Relinking sets the relation and refreshes title, state, and author. `unlink-pr` deletes the link.
- Pushes are not detected automatically. A push from a side worktree AO does not track (exactly the #8020 case) leaves no deterministic signal. Terminal and command parsing is excluded by #5986. A global git hook would override repo hooks such as husky.

**Safeguards.** Validation matches `claim-pr`: `normalizePRRef`, then `requireProjectPRRepository` (project origin, canonical repo, or workspace child allowlist), then a provider fetch with the user's credentials. A PR the session already owns returns `409 PR_ALREADY_TRACKED` and is filtered out at read time. Orchestrators and scratch projects get `422 SESSION_NOT_LINKABLE`. Links are idempotent, survive restarts, and cost one extra statement per session list.

**Remote and cloud.** A remote host's sessions show related PRs once that daemon runs this version. Older daemons omit `prLinks`, which reads as none. Cloud sessions have no related PRs, since the control plane does not carry them.

**Overlap with #7655 (open).** This PR shares only `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx` (edits away from #7655's hunks) and `docs/cli/README.md` (rows near line 93; #7655 edits near line 328). No conflicts are expected.

## Not covered

- Title, state, and author are not kept fresh: they show what the provider said when the link was made, so a merged PR keeps showing its old state until someone relinks it. The previous revision of this PR had a background refresher; it was cut to keep the change small.
- Pushes are not detected automatically; agents rely on `link-pr --as contributing`, which the prompt asks them to run.
- `ao report --pr-reviewed` does not create a link.
- The inspector card has no Unlink button (use `ao session unlink-pr`) and no External repository badge.
- The sidebar row itself has no marker, since row markers mean status; the hover card carries the label. Cloud sessions and mobile do not show related PRs.

## Testing

Per the task's rules, **no tests, typecheck, lint, builds, or app runs were done locally**. I ran `gofmt` on the changed Go files and regenerated `openapi.yaml` (`go generate`), `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` (`openapi-typescript@7.4.4`), and the sqlc output (`npm run sqlc`). Early on I ran `go vet` once on three packages by mistake; it reported nothing.

Regression tests written, not run locally:
- `store/session_pr_link_store_test.go`: survives restart; an explicit save replaces and an automatic one never does; delete is idempotent; the cap applies, and relinking at the cap still works.
- `service/session/pr_links_test.go`:
  - Linking takes no ownership and leaves the session's status and PRs alone.
  - Relinking replaces the relation; unlinking by number removes it.
  - Rejects an invalid relation, an orchestrator, a foreign repo, an unfetchable PR, and an owned PR.
  - The review signal skips owned PRs and orchestrators, saves even when the fetch fails, and never overwrites an existing link.
  - `matchPRLink` refuses an ambiguous number.
- `service/review/review_test.go`: the caller is linked as reviewing (from `--pr` or the planned runs); no caller, self-review, or a failed trigger links nothing.
- `controllers/sessions_test.go`: link/unlink shape, error mapping, `prLinks` on the session view apart from `prs`.
- `cli/session_pr_link_test.go`: request sequence, `--as` required before any request, `AO_SESSION_ID` shorthand, `--json`, unlink, `ao session get` block.
- `product-ui/SessionsBoardView.test.tsx` and `renderer/lib/related-prs.test.ts`: the related row shows its label, state text, and link, and is not counted in PR progress.

Manual checks for a reviewer:
1. From a worker, run `ao session link-pr <someone else's PR URL> --as reviewing`. Its board card, sidebar hover card, and inspector show "Reviewing #N" with title, state, and author.
2. Run `--as contributing` on the same PR: the label changes. Then `ao session unlink-pr <n>` removes it.
3. From session A, run `ao review trigger <session B> --pr <B's PR>`. A shows "Reviewing", and B is unchanged and still owns the PR.
4. `link-pr` on a PR the session already owns returns `PR_ALREADY_TRACKED`; a PR from another repo returns `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`.
5. A linked PR does not change the session's status, PR progress, or review/CI delivery.

title: feat(mobile): show account quota as a composer chip instead of a banner
body: Code changes: +135 -65\ Tests: +107 -26\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Mobile shows the account's usage limit as a chip in the composer's chip row instead of a banner over the conversation. From 75% the chip reads `⚠ 76% quota · 23h` in amber; from 90% it turns red. Tapping it opens Context & usage, which now lists every limit the provider reported, each with its own bar and reset time. There is no quota banner at any level. Desktop: the chat composer now passes the conversation's `rateLimits` to `ContextMeter`, so its existing quota pill can appear at all. ## Why The mobile quota banner was a two-line bar pinned under the header that covered the transcript for a warning nobody can act on, came back on every visit to the conversation, and hid the context meter while it was up. At 90% it repeated exactly what a red chip says. Its Details sheet read only the primary window, so it could disagree with the banner (which warned on the fuller window), and showed "Primary limit · 0% used" when the provider reported only the secondary window. On desktop, `ContextMeter` already had a quota pill, but neither call site in `ChatWorkspace` passed `rateLimits`, so it never rendered. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | **Details** opened Context & usage with only the primary window: "Primary limit · 0% used" when only the secondary was reported | | | 90%+: red banner "92% of quota used", context meter hidden | | | Desktop: quota pill never shown, whatever the quota | Desktop: `⚠ 82% quota` pill beside the context ring from 75% (covered by a new `ChatWorkspace` test) | The quota numbers in the After shots are staged: a read-only lab proxy injected `rateLimits` into a real conversation response. The Before is a real device screenshot from the current release. ## How - `conversationChrome.quotaWindows` turns `ConversationRateLimits` into one readout per reported window and drops unreported ones (negative). `quotaWarning` picks the fullest, and `contextMeter.quotaChipModel` turns it into the chip's label and VoiceOver text ("Long-term limit, 76% used, resets in 23h"). - Window labels: the phone is not told a window's duration, so it cannot say "weekly". With two windows they are "Short-term limit" / "Long-term limit" (the provider's primary and secondary). With one, `planLabel` names it when present, since Claude sends the window type there ("five_hour" → "Five hour limit"); Codex sends the plan tier, which is why it is not used when both windows exist. Real names would need the daemon to send window durations; left out of this PR. - `contextMeterModel` no longer takes `quotaActive`: the context meter and the quota chip run out on different clocks and both show. - `ChatComposer` takes `onOpenUsage` instead of `quotaActive` and renders the chip as a `ComposerChip`, first in the chip row: the row scrolls sideways with no indicator, so behind a PR chip and a changes chip it would start off screen, and it is the only quota warning. The `composer chips` source test pins that order. - `quotaBanner` and its render in `ChatSessionScreen` are removed. - JS only; no native changes, so this can ship over the air. ## Testing - `packages/mobile`: `npx vitest run` (415 files, 4,013 tests) and `npx tsc --noEmit`. - `frontend`: `npx vitest run` on `ChatWorkspace`, `ContextMeter` and `ChatWorkspaceProviderState` tests (307 tests) and `npm run typecheck`. The new `ChatWorkspace` quota test fails against `main`'s `ChatWorkspace.tsx` and passes with the change. - iOS 26.5 simulator, Debug build of this branch, paired through a read-only loopback proxy that stubs every non-GET and injects `rateLimits`: chip absent at 60%, amber at 76%, red at 92%; tapping the chip opens the sheet with both windows; no banner at any level. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * The chat composer shows a quota chip when account usage reaches the warning threshold. It displays the usage level and reset time when available, and opens context and usage details when tapped. * The usage sheet displays each reported quota limit, including short-term and long-term limits, with its usage level and optional reset time. * **Updates** * Quota warnings appear in the composer rather than as conversation banners. * Quota indicators in desktop chat reflect reported usage limits.

title: [Bug]: OMP effort selection likely rejected with "The selected effort is unavailable"
body:
### What went wrong?

Likely the same bug as #8163, for the **OMP** (Oh My Pi) agent. Found in review of #8155 by reading the code; not yet reproduced with a real OMP install.

When an OMP reasoning model shows thinking levels in the effort picker, choosing one probably fails with:

> The selected effort is unavailable. Choose another level before starting.

**Why it likely happens**
- OMP's launcher passes the effort as `--thinking <level>` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/omp/omp.go:81`, `:113`), just like Pi.
- OMP's catalog (`models.db`, read by `ompProviderCatalog`) uses the same parser as Pi, which attaches thinking levels to each model (`piThinkingLevels`, `provider_catalog.go:191`).
- But `resolveAgentConfig` in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` only accepts effort for its listed harnesses. #8155 adds Pi and Prime Agent, not OMP, so an explicitly chosen OMP level is rejected with `UNSUPPORTED_EFFORT`.

**Expected:** a thinking level the selected OMP model offers should start the task. An unsupported level should still be rejected.

**To confirm first:** whether real OMP `models.db` records carry the reasoning fields `piThinkingLevels` reads, so the picker actually offers levels.

**Likely fix:** the same pattern as #8155. Add `HarnessOMP` to the effort list, the inherited-effort handling, and the terminal-launch check, with tests.

title: fix(chat): stop replaying arrivals when returning to a chat
body:
## Problem

Come back to a chat you left alone for a while (orchestrator or worker) and it glides from the middle down to the end while its rows fade in, as if it were a new chat arriving.

## Root cause

The Timeline treats any content that lands after the first second as a live arrival the reader is watching: `followEnd` smooth-scrolls any gap over 48px, and the #8067 entrance gate lets every row above the opening floor play its entrance. There are two ways content lands without the reader watching:

1. **Window hidden** (minimized, other Space, fully covered; Electron reports occlusion as hidden). The chat stays mounted and rows keep committing (worker reports, a working agent). `followEnd` starts a native smooth scroll and new rows start motion/WAAPI/CSS entrances. A hidden page draws no frames, so none of it runs. When the window is seen again the queued smooth scroll plays from the old position (now mid-log) to the end, and the entrances, the stream fade of text that streamed meanwhile, the "Worked for" fade and the settle slides all play at once. While hidden, the chat-view lease isn't renewed, so after 10 idle minutes the orchestrator hibernates. That is why it looked like a hibernation bug, but hibernation isn't what replays.
2. **Stale copy catching up**. Reopening a chat shows its cached copy at once. The refetch (events only invalidate a closed chat; a hibernated chat refetches only after its wake returns, seconds later) brings rows written while the reader was away. They sit above the floor taken from the cached copy, so they enter, and if they land after the 1s opening snap window the view glides down to them.

Hibernation doesn't renumber or rewrite rows: sequences are allocated on insert and kept on update, and ACP `session/load` replay is normalized.

## Fix

- `chat-entrance.ts`: `admitArrivals` runs during the Timeline render, before new rows mount. A batch is a catch-up if the window is hidden or any new row's `createdAt` is before the reader started watching (`watchingSince` = chat opened, or the window was seen again; 5s allowance for a remote clock running behind). A catch-up raises the floor past the batch and asks the view to snap. The floor is never reset by a snapshot replacement. `useChatEntrance` never enters a row that mounts while hidden. Human-message `animateIn` honours the same floor.
- Scroll: `useScrollFollow` lands instantly (`followEnd`, `glideToEnd`, `reaim`) while hidden. The Timeline's opening snap window also opens for a catch-up batch and when the window or the chat panel (after a shell/reviewer tab) is seen again; a send or Jump to latest glide in flight keeps going through it. On return, a glide that couldn't play is dropped and a reader at the end stays there. A reader who scrolled up is never moved.
- Hidden-window animations: streamed text shows whole and counts as settled for the fade. The "Worked for" fade, settle slides and the activity settle dip are skipped.

Unchanged: streaming auto-follow at the end, glide on send and on Jump to latest, the scroll-to-bottom button, scroll restore, reduced motion, and #8013 instant switching (no new renders or state on the switch path; the gate's per-render check exits early unless a new sequence arrives). Visuals are unchanged for content that arrives while you watch.

Covers orchestrator, worker, side, cloud/remote and reviewer chats, and the terminal→chat handoff (all render this Timeline).

## Tests (written, not run locally; CI verifies)

- `chat-entrance.test.tsx`: `admitArrivals` (first transcript, watched rows, rows from while away, remote clock allowance, hidden window, older page) and `useChatEntrance` while hidden.
- `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: no human-message entrance for a catch-up row or for a row landing while hidden. Rows arriving after return still enter. The existing "newest human message" test now stamps its live prompts with the current time.
- `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx`: text that streamed while hidden doesn't fade on return; text after return does.

Scroll glides can't be asserted in jsdom (test mode always snaps), so the glide side needs the manual check below.

## Manual check

1. Open a worker chat with an agent that will keep working for a few minutes, scroll to the end, then minimize AO (or switch Space) for 1–2 minutes. Come back: the chat is already at the end, with no glide and no rows fading in.
2. Same with the orchestrator chat, left minimized for over 10 minutes (it hibernates). Come back: no glide or fades while it wakes.
3. Open chat A, switch to chat B, have A's agent produce output (or send to A from mobile), switch back to A: new rows are in place with no glide or fade.
4. While watching a chat, send a message: the send still glides, and the reply still streams with the fade and follow.
5. Scroll up mid-stream, minimize, return: your position is kept.

## Risks

- A remote host whose clock is more than 5s behind: live rows there count as catch-up, so they don't animate and the view snaps instead of gliding. It never animates something that shouldn't.
- For about 1s after a return or a catch-up, automatic follow snaps instead of gliding. A send or Jump to latest still glides.

title: fix(archive): navigate the archive as a grid and make its cards compact
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #8065 / #8133. Feedback on the archive modal: keyboard navigation was wrong for a multi-column grid, a card behaved like one big button, hover and keyboard highlights could both be lit, and cards were twice as tall as their content.

**Keyboard and selection**
- Up/Down used cmdk's flat list, so they stepped one card sideways. The modal now runs its own selection over the grid (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/grid-navigation.ts`):
  - Left/Right move one card. Up/Down move one row in the same column and stop at the first and last rows. Down into a short last row lands on its last card.
  - Home/End go to the first and last card. PageUp/PageDown move by the complete rows that fit in the viewport from the current row, measured from the rows' actual positions.
  - The column count comes from the live grid's resolved `grid-template-columns`, so it follows the responsive layout instead of a hardcoded 4.
  - Windowing is unchanged (24 cards, idle growth to 120, a page more on scroll). A move past the mounted end mounts up to its target and one page more, in the same render, capped at 96 new cards per key press.
- The search field keeps focus. It is a `combobox` whose `aria-activedescendant` points at the selected `gridcell` in a `grid`. The grid fits because each card holds its own buttons and links; each card is a `row` with one cell, so a column change never regroups or remounts cards. Arrows work from the field. Typing filters and resets the selection to the first result. Modified arrows and Home/End stay text editing. IME composition is ignored.
- There is one selection, drawn on one card: the hover fill plus a `border-strong` edge, switched instantly. The pointer takes the selection only when it actually moves, so a card scrolling under a still pointer does not take it back.
- The selection is stored by session id and looked up across all results. A poll that adds a newly archived session does not move it to another card, even if that pushes the selected card past the loaded cards (it gets loaded). After a delete, the selection stays in the same place.
- Enter opens the session. ⌘/Ctrl+Enter restores. ⌘/Ctrl+Backspace opens the existing delete confirm. From the search box it only does this when there is no text before the caret, so text editing keeps working; it also needs a card that can be deleted.
- Tab goes from the search into the selected card's controls (restore, delete, copy branch, PR links), then the close ✕, then back to the search. Shift+Tab goes the other way. Once the archive moves focus, the Tab keydown stops there, so the dialog's focus trap can't wrap focus away from the last card's last control. An arrow or typing from a card's control returns focus to the search.
- The footer shows one "Navigate" hint (←↑↓→) and adds the Delete hint when it applies.

**Compact cards**
- `SessionCardView` (product-ui) gains `compact`: branch, PRs and time share one line and only wrap when they don't fit, with no status footer strip and tighter padding. The grid no longer uses `auto-rows-fr` or `h-full`/`mt-auto`, so each card is only as tall as its content.
- `SessionCardView` also gains `selected`: a list that owns the selection replaces the card's own hover/focus-within fill and drops the full-card overlay `<button>`. That overlay was the "one big pill" focus target. The board card is unchanged.

**Other**
- `CommandDialog` gains `plain` (the same surface without cmdk). cmdk's root handler calls preventDefault on Enter/arrows/Home/End, and its input overwrites `aria-activedescendant`.
- DESIGN.md's archive paragraph now describes this behavior.

No archive semantics or backend changes.

## Tests
- New `grid-navigation.test.ts`: the move math (row and column clamping, short last row, Home/End, paging) and column/row measurement.
- `SessionsBoard.test.tsx`:
  - Moving through a measured 3-column grid while the search keeps focus, plus Enter to open.
  - Pointer selection only on real movement.
  - The Tab cycle, arrow from a control, and ⌘⌫ opening the confirm.
  - IME composition ignored.
  - Existing archive tests moved from cmdk attributes to `gridcell`/`aria-selected`.
- `SessionsBoardView.test.tsx`: the compact layout and the selected fill.
- Not run locally (per the local rules); CI verifies.

## Risks / follow-ups
- ⌘/Ctrl+Backspace in the search box asks to delete the selected card only when there is no text before the caret; with text there, it still edits the text.
- One key press mounts at most 96 cards past those already mounted. In a very large archive, End stops on the furthest card within that, and pressing End again continues. There is still no true virtualization: cards above the selection stay mounted.

title: fix(cloud): start a Cloud chat with images; edit a queued Cloud message
body:
**Changes:** 17 files, 2 commits. The Cloud contract gains one route, one event and one offering feature, all additive (no migration here, no change for local chats).

## What

Two Cloud chat fixes:

1. **Start a Cloud chat with images.** A Cloud project's new chat had no attach control, and a Cloud task with files threw "File attachments are not supported for cloud tasks yet." Now an image (or any file) can start a Chat task on a Cloud project.
2. **Edit a queued message in a Cloud chat.** A Cloud chat's queue dock had no Edit button: the Cloud surface never wired `onEditQueuedTurn`, and the control plane had no way to change a queued message. Now a queued message can be edited before the agent starts on it, as in a local chat.

The control plane side of (2) is OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#101.

## Why

- (1) `NewChatPage` passed `holdAttachments={!task.isCloudProject}` ("A Cloud task cannot carry files yet"), and `TaskComposer.createCloudTask` threw on `input.attachments`. Cloud files can only be uploaded to an existing session, and a session created with its prompt queues that prompt as its first turn at once, so the files could not ride the first message.
- (2) Editing needs the worker to run the edited text. The worker reads a turn's text, files and settings from its `chat.user_message` event when it claims the turn, so the edit has to change that event while the turn is still queued, atomically with the claim. Only the control plane can do that.

## Before / After

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| New chat on a Cloud project | no attach control | attach control when the control plane takes files (offering `attachments`), up to its per-file limit |
| Cloud task with files, Chat | "File attachments are not supported for cloud tasks yet." | session starts; the brief is its first message with the files |
| Cloud task with files, Terminal | same error | "Files can start a Cloud task in Chat only. Start it in Chat, or remove the files." |
| Upload or brief fails | n/a | session deleted, error shown, task kept in the composer to retry |
| Cloud queue dock | no Edit | Edit on your own queued messages (control plane lists `queued-edit`) |
| Edit a message the agent already took | n/a | "The agent already started on this message, so it can no longer be edited." The edit stays in the composer |
| Teammate's message, or one with quotes/captures | no Edit | no Edit (only the author may edit; an edit cannot rebuild inlined captures) |
| Local chat queue | Edit | unchanged |

## How

**Images (commit 1)**
- `lib/cloud-session-create.ts`: `createCloudChatSessionWithFiles` creates the session with `prompt: ""` (no first turn), uploads each file, then sends the brief with `attachmentIds`, model, effort and approval mode. A session that did not start in Chat (an older control plane falls back to the terminal), or that the files or brief did not reach, is deleted. Each attempt creates under `<requestId>:files:<nonce>`, since replaying the same create would return the deleted session.
- `TaskComposer.createCloudTask` uses it when the task has files; without files nothing changes.
- `NewChatPage` holds files for a Cloud project whose offering lists `attachments`, with the Cloud per-file limit.

**Queued edit (commit 2)**
- Contract: `POST /orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}/turns/{turnId}/edit` (`editQueuedMessage`, body `{ text, attachmentIds? }`), `UserMessageEditedEvent` (`chat.user_message_edited`, added to `ClientEvent`), and `queued-edit` in `offering.features`. `packages/cloud-client` regenerated and gains `editQueuedMessage`.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface`:
  - passes `onEditQueuedTurn` when the offering lists `queued-edit`, and `canEditQueuedMessage` for the viewer's own messages without `content`;
  - splits the composer's Cloud references into `attachmentIds` (`cloudMessageAttachments`);
  - maps 409 `TURN_NOT_QUEUED` to `CHAT_TURN_NOT_QUEUED` so the editor releases the message as for a local turn.
- `toSnapshot` applies `chat.user_message_edited` to the message it already holds (text, files, no `content`, `revision + 1`) before turn bookkeeping, so the event never opens a turn, even on a partial page.
- `ChatWorkspace.beginQueuedEdit` keeps a Cloud message's files as retained attachments by their `ao-cloud-attachment:` reference, so saving lists them as a send lists staged Cloud files. A new optional `canEditQueuedMessage` prop reaches the dock row; local chats never pass it.

**Compatibility**
- An older desktop ignores `chat.user_message_edited`: no client validates events at runtime. The message's own event is rewritten too, so a reopened chat shows the edit.
- A newer desktop on an older control plane gets no `queued-edit` feature, so it shows no Edit.

## Testing

- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` (no further drift), typecheck, 32 tests passed (1 new).
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck` passes. Full renderer suite: 13,352 passed, 15 failed. The 15 failures (`remote-proxy`, `cloud-agent-proxy`, `ContextMeter`) fail the same way on `upstream/main` on this machine. New tests:
  - `cloud-session-create.test.ts` (4 new);
  - `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx` (edited projection, own turns);
  - `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` (Cloud files kept on edit, predicate hides Edit).
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- **Live, dev desktop against a local control plane** (the companion branch, with S3 faked), driven over CDP:
  - **New chat on a Cloud project, image + brief:** the attach control shows; one Chat session is created with an empty prompt and one turn, and its first `chat.user_message` carries `red.png`, the model and the effort. One session in the database, no duplicates.
  - **Two follow-ups queued:** the dock shows both with Edit. Editing one updates the dock in place; the control plane logged `POST …/turns/{turnId}/edit` 200; the message event holds the new text; a `chat.user_message_edited` event points at it; the queue order is unchanged. The edit survives a reload.
  - **Turn marked running mid-edit:** the composer shows "The agent already started on this message, so it can no longer be edited." and keeps the edit.

Not included: the mobile app. It has its own Cloud start (`packages/mobile/lib/cloud/actions.ts`, same refusal) and does not apply the new event yet. It can use the same API in a follow-up.

title: Agent accounts on self-hosted remote hosts: manage, switch the orchestrator's account, and switch from mobile
body:
**Setup**
- Self-hosted remote host (Ubuntu, `bootstrap-self-hosted.sh`, stable v0.14.10, linked to my AO account), macOS desktop and the mobile app as clients.
- Two Claude Code Max subscriptions and one Codex account on the host.

**What works**
The daemon on the host supports this well. `POST /api/v1/agents/accounts/login` added the second Claude account, and `PUT /api/v1/agents/accounts/sessions/{id}` moved a running session between accounts with the conversation intact (native resume). That includes an orchestrator session.

**What is missing in the clients**
1. **Settings → Harness → Account on a remote host** shows only the device login. `HarnessAccountTab` renders `AgentAccountsPanel` only when `!hostId`, so there is no way to add, list, sign out or set the default account of a remote host from the desktop. I had to drive the login API by hand.
2. **Orchestrator sessions cannot switch accounts from the UI.** `SessionView` sets `browserOnly` for orchestrator sessions, so the inspector has no Summary tab and `SessionAccountSummary` never renders. The backend accepts the switch for orchestrators.
3. **Mobile has no account controls at all.** `packages/mobile` never calls `/api/v1/agents/accounts*`. On a phone I cannot see which account a session uses, switch it when a plan hits its limit, or pick the account for a new session.

**Request**
- Show the accounts panel for remote hosts (add / sign out / set default), scoped to the selected host.
- Expose the session account switch for orchestrator sessions (Summary or the composer's agent/model picker).
- On mobile: show the session's account, allow switching it, and choose the account for a new session.
- Nice to have: account in the composer picker next to Agent / Model / Effort, so it is chosen at creation.

Happy to test nightly builds against a remote host.

title: perf(daemon): revive #7286's idle fixes for transcript lookup, preview polling and the pty ring
body:
Code changes: +199 -22 (46 of them sqlc-generated)\
Tests: +163 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

This revives three daemon fixes from ronish's #7286, which closed on 26 Oct only so it could be split up ("splitting out the stream-fade fix into its own PR"). The stream-fade fix landed later. These three did not come back:

1. **Claude transcript lookup** no longer globs every project directory on each reconcile pass.
2. **The 250 ms preview poll** reads 5 columns of live workers instead of every column of every session.
3. **The pty ring** grows the partial line by append and trims it at the latest full-screen clear, so full-screen agents no longer copy output quadratically or replay unbounded history.

Each commit keeps ronish as its author and can be reverted on its own.

## Why

These are the daemon's idle costs. In ronish's profile (a copy of a real 72-session database), Claude transcript discovery was 43% of idle daemon CPU, and daemon CPU on an idle board fell from 7.8% to 2.9% with the full set of fixes.

## Before / After

Re-measured on today's main with Go benchmarks (Apple M-series, `-count` 3–5, medians):

| | Before (main) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude transcript lookup, 1,800 project dirs | 65.8 ms, 28,841 allocs | 5.8 ms, 10,819 allocs |
| Preview poll query, 72 sessions (20 live) | 850 µs, 6,290 allocs, 439 KB | 50 µs, 242 allocs, 34 KB |
| Pty ring, 3,000 full-screen repaints (`BenchmarkRingTUIRepaint`) | 2.5 s, 26.9 GB allocated | 0.16 s, 24 MB |
| Replay sent on attach after those repaints | 17.9 MB | 3.2 MB |

The lookup runs once per live Claude session per reconcile pass. The poll query runs 4 times a second, so the new query also removes about 1.7 MB of garbage per second at 72 sessions.

## How

- **Transcript lookup** (`collector.go`): `discoverClaudePath` reads the projects root once and stats `<project>/<id>.jsonl` for each project. The result is the same: newest match, 128-match cap, and dot entries included as with `filepath.Glob`. Since #7286, main has added Grok and Agy discovery through the same generic glob loop. That loop is kept for them, and only the Claude case changes. This adaptation is the one change to ronish's diff.
- **Preview poll** (`poller.go`, `sessions.sql`, `session_store.go`): a new `ListPreviewPollSessions` query returns `id, kind, workspace_path, preview_url, preview_revision` for `is_terminated = 0 AND kind = 'worker'`. I checked every field `Poll` and `shouldRefresh` read on today's main: all five are covered. Pruning `p.seen` against workers only is equivalent, because `p.seen` only ever holds workers. The sqlc output was regenerated with the pinned v1.31.1.
- **Pty ring** (`ring.go`, unchanged from #7286): the partial line becomes a `[]byte` that grows by append. Past 64 KB it is cut back to the newest `ESC[2J` or `ESC c`. A 4 MB hard cap keeps the newest half, cut at an escape byte. Modes negotiated in the dropped bytes are re-sent on attach by `modeTracker.Restore`, which `host.go` calls on every replay.
- Not included: #7286's frontend switch-readiness backoff (`useSessionInterfaceTransition`). It conflicts with changes on main and belongs to the frontend, so it is left for a separate PR.

## Testing

- New `TestDiscoverClaudePathPicksNewestProjectMatch`: the newest of two matching projects wins. Non-matching projects, a plain file and a directory named like the transcript are skipped, and a missing root returns empty.
- New `TestListPreviewPollSessionsReadsLiveWorkersOnly`: an orchestrator and a terminated worker are excluded, and the live worker's kind, workspace, preview URL and bumped revision are returned.
- ronish's ring tests and `BenchmarkRingTUIRepaint` come with the ring commit.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `golangci-lint v2.14.0 run ./...`: clean. `npm run sqlc` (pinned v1.31.1) leaves no drift.
- `go test -race -count=1` on `internal/preview`, `internal/service/usage`, `internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/...` and `internal/storage/sqlite/store`: pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Terminal replay now handles screen-clear sequences split across output chunks and keeps recent content when large, newline-free updates arrive.
  * Claude usage discovery selects the newest matching transcript, improving which session data is reflected.
  * Preview polling returns data for active worker sessions, excluding terminated sessions and other session types.

title: fix(desktop): open links in the Orchestrator Browser on remote sessions
body:
## Summary

On a remote machine's session, the link menu's **Open in Orchestrator Browser** item was always greyed out.

`_shell.tsx` looked up the session for link handling only among local sessions, and returned nothing whenever the route had a `hostId`. That guard came from multi-host support (#5921): a remote session ID could match a local session with the same ID. With no session, `AppLink` gets no open handler and disables the item.

The lookup now searches that host's sessions and matches `hostId` as well as session ID, so a local or other-host session with the same ID is never picked. Only remote sessions carry a `hostId`, so the local lookup is unchanged.

`useSessionBrowserLink` already handles remote sessions by POSTing the link to that host's `/preview`, the same path a remote agent's `ao preview` uses:
- Web links load in a local Browser tab with the local Orchestrator Browser profile.
- The host's `localhost` URLs go through the tunnel.

## Testing

- CI.
- Not yet tried in the desktop app against a live remote host.

## Follow-ups

The agent's own browser on the remote host still has its own logins, separate from the local profile. That is a separate discussion.

title: fix: make side chat closing and recovery reliable
body:
Code changes: +1560 -534 Tests: +1304 -81 Others: +45 -36 (localized copy) ## What Keep the Delete confirmation busy until side-chat shutdown is confirmed, show a circular spinner in the affected tab header, and retain the loaded transcript. Unknown or partially completed shutdowns retain a read-only warning tab. A definitively rejected deletion restores interaction only after fresh evidence confirms the chat remains open. Confirmed shutdown removes the tab even if notification or other bookkeeping fails. Also preserve loaded older messages, drafts, selection, recovered titles and New availability across close/create/refresh races. After the final confirmed removal, a successfully loaded empty inventory shows only “No side chat opened.” A failed inventory read keeps its genuine availability error. ## Why Deletion was split between renderer HTTP requests and Electron cleanup tracking. View loss, late responses and incomplete launch recovery could lose shutdown evidence or restore interaction too early. Separate renderer flags also allowed stale list, pagination and mutation results to overwrite newer state. The main process now owns each close operation and the renderer projects its versioned result. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Closing title suffix, explanatory panel and Retry close appear during deletion
![before-deleting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/814d15a0-031a-4996-88ca-d7c36e44cea0) | Busy confirmation and target-tab spinner; transcript retained without the closing panel
![after-deleting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/870065bf-6cfb-415f-a266-da0cb75ddcab) | | Lost DELETE response leaves the closing panel and Retry close
![before-failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/643d65ce-6c56-4673-9fe8-45f6fd86987f) | Persistent warning inside the retained, read-only side chat
![after-failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9904d10-3183-4e74-8183-9b541f1d740d) Definitive rejection restores interaction; cleanup-pending remains read-only. | | Empty text says "No side chat opened yet" and late closed-side errors can appear below it
![before-empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2ce626e-42b4-41ac-8092-4423f6ebe1be) | Only "No side chat opened." after the last confirmed removal
![after-empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcee1341-1614-43cf-8dba-dc6898da885c) Genuine list/create failures remain visible. | | A refresh can miss cleanup pending and retain a read-only tab after its agent has stopped. | Electron remembers confirmed shutdown; the tab is removed even if no intermediate state was observed. | | A late close/list completion can overwrite a new tab or selection. | Updates use current state, ordered refreshes and lifecycle/attachment fencing; the new tab and unrelated selection survive. | | Closing another tab or resuming a rejected delete clears already loaded older messages. ![Previous PR commit: older history lost](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22c243c8-ab5a-4158-ac2d-3ff0a6a351ea) | Loaded older messages remain visible, with the warning and usable composer after confirmed rejection. ![Updated PR: older history retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e25bd38-e708-4985-99df-6a70e5557d16) | | List failures prevent applying positive shutdown evidence. | Apply authoritative close state before requesting the list; keep genuine list errors visible and preserve other tabs. | | Cancellation succeeds but its later snapshot fails, leaving an open chat incorrectly locked. | Remember the definitive rejection before cancellation; unlock only after fresh close state confirms no remaining intent. | The original paired UI captures use the base and PR checkouts, a real daemon/Codex provider and the same isolated scratch profile at 1280×800. The history comparison uses fdf280b and 91fc72d at 1653×1078; a controlled older-page response supplies pagination data. These earlier visual comparisons are retained below with their original recordings. Original closing/failure/success flow (3× playback): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99d4e3c3-f748-4084-90db-c8c184213f1d Loaded history through rejected deletion: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/627df0d6-afcf-4bec-a119-18dd2d3c52b7 Current native regression evidence was captured at 5936750 from a clean isolated checkout, real Electron/preload/daemon/Codex and scratch data under ~/.ao/dev/side-close-evidence. The subsequent 6837c00 commit only removes an unused Go helper. Main-process HTTP and notification faults are controlled; these captures do not claim a naturally occurring provider-stop failure. | Current state | Native capture | | --- | --- | | Busy dialog, target-header spinner and retained transcript | ![Busy native deletion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/874fe699-93a3-4b9a-9216-6682bd6cdd71) | | Rejected deletion: loaded history and interactive draft retained | ![Rejected deletion remains usable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9352c218-ebb9-4ecf-bcc0-c2e9df4b5092) | | Unknown shutdown: cached transcript retained, composer disabled | ![Unknown shutdown remains read-only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46e1fba3-5236-4631-ae1a-9c893c281350) | | Renderer reload plus failed list: recovered title and read-only warning retained | ![Recovered warning tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a62b013-e2b0-4101-8f70-1c4254dd756b) | | Confirmed shutdown plus failed notification/list: tab removed; inventory error remains accurate | ![Confirmed removal during list outage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/177a0d6d-97d6-4ccc-99c2-dc1c315f4e77) | | Inventory recovers empty: one empty-state message and enabled New | ![Final empty state](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50d4d5fd-2687-44aa-b8aa-a622dd120290) | Edited 30-second native recording: rejected deletion, unknown shutdown, reload, confirmed removal despite notification/list faults, creation after closing, and ordinary busy deletion. Idle QA pauses are omitted. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b82fa686-94b8-4f24-a411-32fc83a4a28b ## How - Merge compatibility with current main: retain its shared TerminalTabFrame and inline annotations while preserving the target-only spinner, stable read-only tabs, per-dialog close identity and focus restoration. Cancel a pending composer-focus request when opening Delete. Add regressions for the shared frame/spinner and blocked middle-click during cleanup; explicitly await hydration/readiness before existing UI assertions and rename gestures. - Resolve the missing Cloud-project description key introduced on main in CommandPalette by reusing its existing localized deletion explanation. This one-line compatibility fix restores typechecking. - Electron registers and deduplicates a versioned close operation before awaiting preparation or HTTP. It binds requests to an immutable daemon attachment and bounded deadlines, records HTTP 204 proof before fallible bookkeeping, and retains uncertainty across lost replies. A later rejection cannot erase an earlier dispatched-but-unconfirmed attempt. - Already-closed responses require fresh same-attachment recovery evidence. Rejected-open requires a matching open snapshot and list, cancelable local intent and no unresolved earlier dispatch or offered cleanup restore. Ordinary list absence and timeouts do not prove shutdown. - Separate launch claim from full restore readiness. Generic receipt/draft captures and close captures share the claim-only serialized snapshot queue. Coverage is stamped when the read starts; partial snapshots preserve missing private originals, including across a second crash. Initial close hydration remains read-only until authoritative readiness is established. - Extend the existing daemon DELETE to recover exact journal ownership when RAM is missing. Validate run/session/parent/host/fork/harness identity and retire the journal before close effects. Serialize metadata and cleanup ownership without holding locks during provider I/O; fence late fork callbacks, stale opening work and restore replays. Existing cleanup intervals and ownership remain intact. - Use one renderer close projection plus temporary invocation guards. Scope all reads, mutations, saves, staging and handoff continuations by side, operation, lifecycle and daemon attachment. Preserve loaded pages and cached transcripts; retain idempotent delivery receipts; suppress confirmed-closed identities and normalize selection against the latest rows. - Scope errors, editors, answers and busy tokens to their side. A failed preflight explains that deletion could not start without manufacturing close intent. Retained placeholders learn nonempty recovery titles without overwriting HTTP/create titles. - Keep the dialog non-dismissible while busy, announce status inside the modal and preserve tab keyboard focus when drafts hydrate. Existing Composer setText callers retain their behavior; only side-draft hydration opts out of DOM focus reconciliation. - Require the explicit browser-preview transport. Missing desktop preload or failed desktop IPC cannot silently switch to renderer HTTP deletion. Internal summaries exclude provider identities, launch configuration and credentials. Opening UI, deferred controller startup and broader creation/startup capability changes remain deferred. No new HTTP endpoints, database changes, migrations, polling loops or automatic DELETE retry service. ## Testing - Current conflict-resolution head: e1a8f74e1643f42e3a96bcb831889f3ab7293d7f, integrating main at a8451c437c. All 19 applicable PR checks passed. [Verified CI run](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/43640886337). - Complete CI frontend unit suites passed: 792 files, 14,603 tests, 7 skipped. Both complete renderer smoke shards, backend core/race suites, storage race coverage, pinned lint/build/vet, code generation, frontend/E2E typechecks, Electron boundaries, guarded navigation, both CLI E2E jobs, public-boundary and secret checks passed. - Local post-merge focused validation passed 340 tests across 13 suites. title: [Bug]: Grok Build sessions quit ~8 s after launch (TUI): Grok logs the exit as a keypress
body:
### What went wrong?

Every Grok Build session AO launches quits by itself about 8 seconds after start, before doing any work. Grok's own log records the quit as a **keypress**, but nobody touched the terminal. The same Grok binary with the same flags stays running in a normal terminal. Because AO has no Chat driver for Grok (`--mode chat` returns `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`), there is currently no way to run Grok in AO.

**Environment:** AO desktop 0.14.10 (AppImage) on Arch-based Linux (kernel 7.2, Hyprland), Grok Build CLI 1.0.77 (stable), session runtime `ptyhost-v1`. `ao agent ls` shows grok as installed and authorized.

**Steps to reproduce**

```bash
ao spawn --standalone --agent grok --name grok-repro --prompt "Run ao status and paste the output."
```

Output: `spawned session standalone-N "grok-repro" (exited)`. The session has 0 turns. Reproduced 2 of 2 times (once as a project worker, once standalone).

**Grok's log** (`~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl`, AO launch, times UTC):

```text
21:08:41.974  shell       connect finished        outcome=ok, connect_target=embedded
21:08:41.974  grok-pager  pager started
21:08:42.007  shell       startup interactive     interactive_ms=716
21:08:49.975  grok-pager  quit.started            trigger=key
21:08:49.990  grok-pager  teardown.pop_fence      decision=skip_da1_not_known
21:08:50.244  grok-pager  pager.exited            trigger=key
```

The other AO launch looks the same (`connect finished`, then `quit.started trigger=key` 9 seconds later). Across this machine's whole Grok log, the only two `trigger=key` quits are exactly the two AO launches; every other session ended by `hangup`, `enter` or `signal`.

**Control:** `grok --no-auto-update --permission-mode auto --rules 'test rules' 'say hi'` run under `script` (a real PTY) stayed up until the test timeout ended it (`trigger=signal`), with identical auth and startup.

**AO's launch command** (from `ps`):

```text
ao pty-host <session> <workspace> ao agent-process supervise --session <session> --launch <id> -- \
  grok --no-auto-update --permission-mode auto --rules "<~7 KB of AO rules>" ...
```

**Possible causes (unconfirmed)**

- The quit is a keypress at a fixed delay (8 to 9 s after startup both times), which suggests bytes AO writes into the PTY on a timer (prompt delivery, a readiness probe, or a key such as Esc, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D or `q`) that Grok 1.0.77's inline pager treats as quit.
- `teardown.pop_fence decision=skip_da1_not_known` shows the terminal never answered Grok's DA1 query. A late or partial terminal response could be read as a keypress.
- Grok 1.0.77 starts in an inline pager by default; it has a `--fullscreen` flag that AO does not pass.

**Suggestions:** check what AO writes to the Grok PTY in the first ~10 s; consider launching with `--fullscreen` or passing the prompt only as an argument; longer term, a Chat (ACP) driver for Grok (Grok already performs an ACP handshake at startup).

title: fix(chat): stop an ACP provider that lost its session so the agent can be resumed
body:
Code changes: +66 -2\
Tests: +143 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

When an ACP agent answers "Session not found" for its own session, AO now stops that provider so the agent reads as exited, and returns a definitive refusal instead of a raw internal error.

## Why

Reported by a paid Linux user (0.14.10). After a daemon restart, Chat sessions that were mid-turn stayed bound to a Claude ACP session the provider no longer held:

- every send failed with `set ACP session option "model": {"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"Session not found"}}`
- `ao session resume-agent` refused with `AGENT_NOT_EXITED`, because the chat host process survived
- `ao send --steer` returned `INTERNAL_ERROR`, and a message accepted at ~09:05 was delivered at 10:16 while the session showed working/active

Root cause: on reattach the driver trusts the session id cached in the surviving host (`acp/driver.go`, `live.SessionID`) and never notices the provider has dropped it. The host stays alive, so nothing marks the agent exited.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Send after daemon restart: raw `-32603 Session not found`, agent stays "working" | Send is refused as a provider refusal ("the agent lost this chat session; AO stopped it so it can be resumed"), the provider is terminated, agent shows exited |
| `ao session resume-agent` → `AGENT_NOT_EXITED` | Resume works (agent is exited) |
| `ao send --steer` → `INTERNAL_ERROR`, recovery says accepted, never delivered | Steer settles as rejected, not uncertain |

User's current workaround (`exit-agent` → `resume-agent` → resend) becomes: resume → resend.

## How

- `isACPSessionNotFound`: matches only the provider's own words, `-32603`/`-32002` with "session not found" in the message or `data.details` (TS SDK) / `data.error` (Go SDK). Transport failures (peer disconnected etc.) do not match, per the "unknown probe is not proof of death" rule.
- `abandonLostSession`: on a match from `SendTurn` (turn settings), `runTurn` (prompt) or `Steer`, terminates the provider asynchronously. Termination closes the event stream with a plain `ControllerStopped` (not recovery-inconclusive), which the controller already records as `ActivityExited`.
- Returned error is a `providerRefusal`, so the chat service classifies it as `ErrProviderRefused` instead of a 500.

Not in this PR: why the provider dropped the session in the first place (the adapter's stderr is discarded by the host). Daemon/main crash logging is a separate PR.

## Testing

- New `session_lost_test.go`: classifier table, lost session on send stops the provider and closes the event stream without the recovery-inconclusive marker, unrelated setting errors leave the provider running.
- `gofmt` clean. **Not run locally:** `go test` / golangci-lint. The repo needs Go 1.27.4 and the toolchain download was not reachable from my environment, so this relies on CI for build, tests and lint.
