title: fix(desktop): persist daemon output and app/daemon lifecycle records
body:
Code changes: +137 -11\
Tests: +62 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The desktop app now keeps a local record of why it or its daemon stopped:

- `<state>/logs/daemon.log`: the app-owned daemon's stdout/stderr, plus `--- <time> AO: daemon spawned/exited ...` markers. Bounded at 4 MB with one previous file kept, URLs and authorization values redacted.
- `<state>/logs/lifecycle.jsonl` (same writer as `updater.jsonl`): `app-started`, `app-exit` (code), `daemon-spawned`, `daemon-exited` (code, signal, requested), `daemon-exit-classified` (ungraceful, run-file state), `daemon-auto-restart` (attempt/delay or give_up), `child-process-gone`, `render-process-gone`, `main-uncaught-exception`, `app-window-all-closed`.
- The daemon runs with `GOTRACEBACK=all` unless the user set it.

`<state>` is the directory holding `running.json` (`~/.ao` in production), the same place `updater.jsonl` already lives.

## Why

Reported by a paid Linux user (0.14.10, AppImage): in one day the app respawned its daemon (08:59) and then exited outright (10:21), dropping all 18 sessions. He found nothing: no daemon or main log (only `logs/updater.jsonl`), no core dump, no Crashpad dump, no Sentry event, no OOM entry.

Root cause of the missing evidence: an app-owned daemon's output only went to an in-memory buffer (`daemonOutput`, last 12k chars) and the console. A Go panic or fatal error (unrecoverable, so not in Sentry, and no core dump by default) printed its stack into that pipe and was lost. The exit code/signal and the auto-restart decision only reached in-memory status. Only `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` wrote `~/.ao/daemon.log`.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Daemon dies, app respawns it: no trace on disk | `daemon.log` has the daemon's last output (including a Go fatal stack) and an `exited code=… signal=…` marker; `lifecycle.jsonl` has the exit, its ungraceful classification and the restart attempt |
| App main dies: nothing on disk | A clean exit writes `app-exit`; a SIGKILL or native crash leaves `app-started` with no `app-exit`, which pins it as an external kill or crash. Utility/GPU process deaths are logged with reason and exit code |

## How

- Reuses the `updater.jsonl` writer (synchronous, bounded, fail-open, 0600) via a new `createJsonlDiagnostics(stateDir, version, fileName)`; `createUpdateDiagnostics` is unchanged in behavior.
- `uncaughtExceptionMonitor` is used, not `uncaughtException`, so Electron's handling does not change. No `unhandledRejection` or signal handlers are added, for the same reason: adding them would change default process behavior.
- `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` keeps its existing `~/.ao/daemon.log` redirect; the new file is only for the piped, app-owned daemon.
- Local only. Nothing here is sent to telemetry.

Not in this PR: running agent children outside the app's systemd scope or under a memory limit (the user's third ask). That is a Linux process-placement change and needs its own design.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/daemon-output-log.test.ts src/main/update-diagnostics.test.ts src/main/daemon-auto-restart.integration.test.ts`: 45 passed. The integration test now asserts the exit/classification/restart/spawn records and that daemon stderr reaches the log.
- Also ran `sentry-main`, `browser-identity`, `daemon-auto-restart` and `auto-updater` tests: passing. `remote-proxy.test.ts` has 1 timeout that fails the same way on `main` in my environment (network).
- **Not run locally:** the full `npm run typecheck` (tsgo was OOM-killed on my 7 GB box). I type-checked `main.ts` and the new files with a scoped tsconfig: no new errors. Relying on CI for the full typecheck and suite.

title: fix(chat): send messages entered in quick succession instead of dropping them
body:
## Problem

Sending several chat messages quickly while the agent works ("spamming") lost them. Sending clears the box before the daemon answers, so people type the next message right away. Pressing Enter on it during that round trip did nothing: no send, no error, and the text just sat in the box.

## Root cause

All of this is in `ChatComposer`. The daemon queue was fine: it has no size limit, dedupes only by `clientMessageId`, and drains in enqueue order.

1. `submit()` returned the in-flight promise for **any** Enter during a send. This was meant to merge a double Enter on the same message, but because optimistic sends clear the box first, it also swallowed the *next* message.
2. Just after the send landed, `beginChatComposerMutation` refused new work until the acceptance receipt was applied on the next commit, and `performSubmit` returned without a word.
3. In the same window, a stale `busy` prop showed "Still sending the previous message", and a stale `durableDelivery` could make the Enter a "retry". That retry resent the old id (the daemon answered `duplicate`) and then cleared the new text.

## Fix

- An Enter on a new draft during a send is held and sent as soon as that send is accepted. Messages reach the daemon one at a time, in order, each with its own id, and each lands in the queue dock as usual.
- A repeat Enter on the message being sent, or on the empty box, still merges with it. Nothing is sent twice.
- A held message is sent only if the box still holds exactly the text that was entered. An edit made since waits for its own Enter.
- If the previous send is refused or gets no answer, the held message stays in the box and doesn't jump ahead of it (the first one goes to the unsent strip as before).
- If the saved draft no longer holds a delivery, it is no longer treated as a retry.
- Delivery is unchanged: when a turn ends, the daemon sends everything queued as one batch, and each message keeps its own row. Documented in `docs/architecture.md` next to the existing queue section.

Steer (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter), editing and removing queued messages, attachments, and the unsent strip keep their current behavior. The code is shared, so cloud, remote and orchestrator chats get the fix too.

## Queue dock

Follow-up from manual testing. The dock felt laggy, its Steer button blinked in and out, and a queued message sometimes got steered:

- **Accidental steer:** a bare Enter in the empty box steers the next queued message (the "↵ Steer" shortcut). A send clears the box at once and lands in milliseconds, so a double-tapped Enter steered the message it had just queued. That Enter is now ignored for 1 s after a send and when it is a held-key repeat. A deliberate Enter later still steers.
- **Steer button blinking:** the next row's Steer button showed only while the box was empty and nothing was sending, so it toggled on every first keystroke and every send. It now stays while a turn can be steered; only its ↵ hint fades, in a fixed slot so the row doesn't shift.
- **Lag:** every new queued row restarted a 420 ms height animation (and 300 ms on the header chevron). Both now use the design system's 150 ms (`--duration-normal`), with no animation under reduced motion.

## Tests

- `ChatComposer.optimistic.test.tsx`: next message entered mid-send goes out after the first, in order, with a new id; Enter on the cleared box mid-send sends nothing extra; a message entered during a send that got no answer stays in the box.
- `ChatSteer.test.tsx`: a second Enter right after sending does not steer; a held Enter key does not steer; the next row's Steer button stays while typing and only its Enter hint hides.
- `ChatComposer.test.tsx`: the old "Still sending the previous message" test now checks the message is held and sent once `busy` clears; a held message edited before then is not sent.

Not run locally (repo rule); CI is the check.

## Check by hand

1. Start a long turn. Type `one` and press Enter, then immediately type `two` and Enter, then `three` and Enter. All three appear in the queue dock in order, once each, and the box is empty.
2. On an idle chat, send a first message and type and send a second one before the agent starts. Both are delivered in order.
3. Press Enter several times on one message. It's sent once.
4. Cmd+Enter steer, editing/removing a queued message, and sending with an image still work, in light and dark.
5. With a queued message, type a message and double-tap Enter: it queues and is **not** steered. Wait a second, then press Enter in the empty box: the next queued message is steered.
6. Type in the box while messages are queued: the next row's Steer button stays put (only its ↵ hint fades). The dock grows and shrinks quickly as messages are added and removed.

title: feat(diagnostics): show how much disk each session's worktree uses
body:
Code changes: +529 -1\
Tests: +443 -1\
Others: +150 -0 (generated `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`)

## What

- `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions/disk`, next to `/usage/sessions/memory`: each live session's worktree size, when it was measured, the total, and how many worktrees are still being measured.
- Diagnostics (settings page and window) gets a Disk section under the memory table: every session with a worktree, largest first, sortable by size or last active, with the total in the heading.
- No delete or clean-up action.

## Why

Nothing in the app shows how much disk Orchestrator holds. On one Mac `~/.ao/data/worktrees` was 22 GB of a 24 GB `~/.ao`, and five sessions idle for 2 to 4 days held 7.7 GB between them.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Diagnostics shows memory and CPU only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illegalcall/agent-orchestrator/80b8d4bd6561f0a35314cdb8191e0eb2aeacecab/diagnostics-before.png) | ![After: Disk section under the memory table with four worktree sizes and a 1.6 GB total](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illegalcall/agent-orchestrator/80b8d4bd6561f0a35314cdb8191e0eb2aeacecab/diagnostics-disk-after.png) |
| `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions/disk` returns 404 | First call answers in 2 ms with `{"sessions":[],"totalBytes":0,"measuring":4}`. 3 s later it returns all four sizes |

Captured from an isolated dev app with four sessions, two of them with dependencies installed. The sizes equal `du -sk` for each worktree: 1183012, 252036, 105528 and 105528 KB.

A session whose agent has exited has no row in the memory table and keeps its Disk row:

![After: the session with an exited agent is listed under Disk at 1.1 GB but not under Sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illegalcall/agent-orchestrator/80b8d4bd6561f0a35314cdb8191e0eb2aeacecab/diagnostics-disk-exited-agent.png)

Light theme:

![After, light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illegalcall/agent-orchestrator/80b8d4bd6561f0a35314cdb8191e0eb2aeacecab/diagnostics-disk-after-light.png)

## How

- `DiskReader` in `backend/internal/service/usage/disk.go` caches each size by worktree path with the time it was measured. `Run` is one goroutine that walks one worktree at a time. `ListDisk` reads the cache and wakes `Run` when a size is missing or older than 5 minutes. It does not touch the file system.
- Nothing is walked unless the endpoint is called, and the UI calls it only while Diagnostics is open (every 2 s while `measuring` is above zero, otherwise every 60 s).
- Only paths under `<data dir>/worktrees` are measured, so a session that runs in the user's own checkout is not walked. Terminated sessions and hidden task preparations are skipped.
- Size is allocated blocks with hard links counted once, as `du` does. On Windows it is file length.
- The section is separate from the memory table because that table lists only sessions with a live process.
- Shown under the same gate as the memory figures: Developer mode with Diagnostics on.

Not in this PR: `ao session top`, the copied diagnostics report and the board card chip do not show disk. Worktrees kept for terminated sessions and prepared task worktrees are not counted.

### Open questions

- Should idle sessions get a "remove installed dependencies" action? `frontend/node_modules` alone is 1.3 GB per worktree.
- Should worktrees share dependencies instead of each installing its own?

## Testing

- `go test -race ./...` on macOS. Six tests in five packages fail, and fail the same way on the base commit on this machine: four OpenCode version-probe packages and `TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch` in `internal/integration`. `internal/httpd` and `internal/storage/sqlite` timed out in the full run on a loaded machine and pass when run alone.
- `gofmt`, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...` for darwin, linux and windows, and golangci-lint v2.14.0 are clean. `npm run api` leaves no diff.
- Frontend `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass. vitest: 741 of 743 files pass. The two that fail are `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts` and `src/main/browser-cookie-repair.test.ts`, which cannot load `better-sqlite3` under the local Node 26; CI uses Node 24.
- Not run anywhere yet: the Linux and Windows jobs and the Playwright renderer smoke suite. CI runs no test lanes on a draft (`scripts/ci-lanes.mjs`), so they run when this PR is marked ready.
- Real app: isolated dev app on its own port and data dir. Checked the first request, the 5 minute refresh, the measuring state, an exited agent, and that ended sessions drop out.

title: feat(projects): start new projects on the most preferred agent (Developer Mode)
body:
Replaces #7711, #7820 and #7821. Rather than removing project agent settings, a new project picks its agents for you, and you can still change them in project settings.

**For now the automatic flow is behind Developer Mode.** With Developer Mode off, creating a project works as on main: the setup sheet asks for the worker and orchestrator agents (preselected from recent use), and nothing is created until you press Create. The handoff, placeholder and sample-request fixes below apply to everyone.

## What changes

### Developer Mode on
- **Ranked agent list.** `preferredAgentList` ranks agents from the readiness snapshot the renderer already caches. Installed, signed-in agents come first (a `configured` credential counts as signed in), then agents AO hasn't checked yet. Within each group, AO's integration priority decides: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenCode v2, Aider, then the rest. Missing or signed-out agents are left out.
- **Defaults on create.** The worker and orchestrator start on the top agent. Only unattended-safe reviewers (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Muse, Kimchi) review by default, so the reviewer is the highest-ranked of those the machine has (the top agent itself when it's one), and Claude Code when it has none. With no usable agent, everything falls back to Claude Code, the daemon's default.
- **No agent step.** The setup sheet doesn't ask for agents. It opens only for tracker intake, the git setup notice, or a failed create (with retry). Otherwise the project is created as soon as its folder is chosen. Agent checks refresh while the create flow is open, so the ranking uses current state.

### Developer Mode off (default)
- Same as main: Worker and Orchestrator pickers in the setup sheet, preselected by the last 48 hours of use, and no reviewer is set at create.

### Everyone
- **Steadier handoff.** Creating a project lands straight in the orchestrator chat. The starting screen stays up until the chat route has loaded, so the Board doesn't flash in between.
- **Steady placeholder.** The composer reads "Starting your orchestrator" for the whole start.
- **Sample requests.** The starter chips show while the orchestrator starts and are disabled until it's ready.
- **Top bar.** Disabled editor and cue placeholders are shown where the session will have them (none on remote hosts, no editor on cloud projects), so the bar doesn't widen when the session lands.
- **Unchanged:** the project settings agent and model controls, cloud projects, mobile, and the daemon.

## Test steps

1. Check out `ao/agent-orchestrator-36/default-agents` and start the dev app.

**Developer Mode off (default)**

2. Sidebar → New project → Open a local folder → pick a git repo that isn't added yet.
   - Expected: the setup sheet opens with Worker agent and Orchestrator agent pickers, preselected as on main.
   - Pick agents and press Create and start. Expected: the project opens on the orchestrator chat with no Board flash, and the placeholder reads "Starting your orchestrator" throughout.

**Developer Mode on**

3. Settings → General → turn on Developer Mode.
4. Settings → Agent Harnesses: note which agents show as installed and signed in.
5. Sidebar → New project → Open a local folder → pick another git repo that isn't added yet.
   - Expected: no agent sheet. The project opens on the orchestrator chat in one step.
   - Expected: the orchestrator runs on the top installed agent (Claude Code if it's installed and signed in, otherwise Codex, and so on).
6. Open that project's settings → Agents.
   - Expected: worker, orchestrator and reviewer all show that same agent.
7. Sign out of or uninstall the top agent, wait for Agent Harnesses to show it as not ready, then add another new project.
   - Expected: the new project uses the next agent in the list.
8. Turn on tracker intake in Settings, then add a new project.
   - Expected: the sheet opens with only the intake fields (no agent pickers); Create and start works.
9. Add a folder that isn't a git repo yet.
   - Expected: the sheet opens with the git setup notice, and creating sets up the repo and starts the project.
10. Clone a repo (New project → Clone).
    - Expected: no agent sheet, and the cloned project starts on the top agent.

## Tests

Not run locally; CI covers them.
- With Developer Mode off, main's tests are restored: the sheet's picker tests, the Sidebar picker tests, the e2e specs (including `project-agent-management.spec.ts`), and the SettingsDialog integration test.
- The new flow is covered under Developer Mode: `CreateProjectFlow.test.tsx` and `Sidebar.test.tsx` Developer Mode cases, the no-picker block in `CreateProjectAgentSheet.test.tsx`, and the ranking and defaults in `agent-select-options.test.ts`.

## Risks

- **Developer Mode on.** If agent checks haven't finished when you create, the ranking waits for them. On failure it uses what is cached, then falls back to Claude Code.
- **Developer Mode on, remote host with no ready agent.** The project is still created and the orchestrator startup error shows, instead of the "no agents ready" message in the sheet.
- **Developer Mode off.** Create now waits for settings to load (to know whether intake applies). This is usually instant.

title: feat(accounts): agent accounts on remote hosts, per-session pick, and mobile switch
body:
Closes #8237

## Summary

Subscription accounts (Claude Code, Codex) now work on self-hosted remote hosts and from the phone.

**Daemon**
- The `/api/v1/agents/accounts` routes are no longer loopback-only. Remote desktops and paired phones can list accounts, add one, sign one out, set the default, and move a session to another account.
- CORS lets a paired phone, with the `Origin` React Native sets plus a LAN bearer, reach only these routes. Codex account management and the CLI credential routes stay renderer-only.
- `SpawnSessionRequest` and `DelegateTaskRequest` take `accountId`. The value is passed to `SpawnConfig.AgentAccountID`, which spawn already binds.

**Desktop**
- The account hooks take a host. The Harness › Account tab lists a remote host's accounts. Sign-in streams that host's login terminal through the host's own mux.
- Summary shows the account on remote sessions, orchestrators included.
- The composer's agent picker has an **Account** row (with Agent, Model and Effort):
  - in a running chat, orchestrators included, it moves the session;
  - in New chat / New task, it picks the account the task starts on.

**Mobile**
- The conversation's ⋯ sheet has an **Account** row that shows the current account. It opens the machine's accounts and moves the session. If a turn is running, it asks before stopping it.
- The switch card and the failure notice name an account move as one (they used to say "Switching to Terminal").
- Spawn shows an account row when the machine has more than one signed-in account for the agent.

## Evidence

Recorded on head 70b0899 in the real desktop app (desktop A) paired with a second daemon (host "Lab MacBook") through its password-protected bridge. Host B has two real signed-in Claude logins. Emails are masked in the page (personal@ / work@example.com). Each caption quotes host B's own API and the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` of the session's `claude` process, read at that moment. Waits for agent replies are sped up.

**1. A remote host's accounts in Settings › Harness** ([MP4](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/panel.mp4)): lists Lab MacBook's accounts, then Make default moves the default there and back. Host B's API reported `borrowed-untrivial`, then `device-claude`.

![remote accounts panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/panel.gif)

**2. Pick the account when starting a chat on the remote host** ([MP4](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/spawn.mp4)): the agent picker's Account row lists the host's signed-in accounts. A chat started on work@ (not the default) is bound to it, and its `claude` runs from that account's folder.

![pick at spawn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/spawn.gif)

**3. Switch from the agent picker, idle and mid-turn** ([MP4](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/switch.mp4)): idle move in 6.8 s. Mid-turn, the "Stop the turn and move?" confirm, then Stop and move in 17.7 s. The agent then quotes the stopped command, so the conversation carried over.

![picker switch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/switch.gif)

**4. Orchestrator session on the remote host** ([MP4](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/orch.mp4)): Summary › Account moves it in 8.8 s, and it still answers "OK" about its turn from before the move.

![orchestrator switch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/orch.gif)

**5. Phone path** ([full transcript](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/d1523be3a3d359426aff0343e5417da044bd1b2b/70b0899/phone-requests.txt)). There is no iOS simulator here, so this replays the mobile app's requests through the bridge with `Origin: http://localhost`:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| list accounts, no password | 401 `BAD_PASSWORD` |
| list accounts / a chat's account | 200, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost` |
| move a chat to another account | 202, rebound in 4.0 s |
| start a session with `accountId` | 201, bound to that account |
| start with an unknown / signed-out account | 404 `AGENT_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` / 409 `AGENT_ACCOUNT_SIGNED_OUT`, no session row left |
| move to a signed-out account | 409, binding unchanged |

Not exercised: Add (sign-in), Sign out and Remove. Cancelling a sign-in and removing an account both run `claude auth logout` on that folder. In an earlier lab run on this machine, that preceded the machine's own default Claude login being revoked, so the lab avoids them.

## Risk

The remote/LAN listener now serves the account routes. This adds little new power: a client past tunnel auth can already start agents that run code on the host, and can already run the CLI's own login and logout (`/agents/{agent}/auth/operations`, `/agents/{agent}/logout`). Previews still cannot reach any credential route.

## Tests
- Go: LAN listener reachability for the account routes; CORS matrix (paired-phone origin allowed only on account routes, not with a hostile origin or without a bearer); spawn and delegate pass `accountId` through.
- Desktop: remote orchestrator inspector shows the account; `SessionAccountSummary` asks the session's own host.
- Mobile: menu-model account row; account API calls; `accountId` on spawn/delegate.
- Not run locally; CI is the gate.

## Known gaps
- The Terminal UI agent picker has no account row: its menu unmounts on close, so it can't host the stop-and-move confirm. TUI sessions switch from Summary.
- Mobile cannot add or sign out accounts yet, because sign-in needs the login terminal. It lists, picks and moves.
- `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` was edited by hand to match `openapi.yaml`, because `openapi-typescript` isn't installed here. The CI codegen-drift check will confirm it.

title: perf(desktop): log launch timestamps in one line
body:
Code changes: +42 -0\
Tests: +47 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Main records when the app is ready, when the window is shown and when the daemon reports ready. The shell reports the first frame that shows the workspace list. Main then logs one line, in ms since the process started:

`launch timing: appReady=207ms windowShown=704ms daemonReady=711ms sessionsShown=949ms`

## Why

Launch has no timing instrumentation, so the cached start work (DL-1 and SU-6 in `docs/plans/2026-10-13-desktop-performance-overhaul.md`) has no number to compare against.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A launch prints no timing | One `launch timing:` line per launch on the main process stdout |

No user-visible change: the line goes to stdout only.

Baseline from this branch at `de719c54f5`, 5 cold launches, ms since the process started:

| Launch | appReady | windowShown | daemonReady | sessionsShown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 204 | 649 | 651 | 913 |
| 2 | 207 | 770 | 711 | 997 |
| 3 | 188 | 646 | 534 | 851 |
| 4 | 257 | 788 | 1350 | 1489 |
| 5 | 242 | 704 | 801 | 949 |
| Median | 207 | 704 | 711 | 949 |

The startup loader was on screen for a median of 245 ms (`sessionsShown` minus `windowShown`, range 205 to 701). The first launch after several idle hours logged `appReady=2018ms windowShown=2773ms daemonReady=3605ms sessionsShown=3775ms`, about 1.0 s of loader.

Method: this checkout run unpackaged (`electron .` on production Vite bundles, not the dev server) on an Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, with its own `AO_DEV_ELECTRON_DIR`, `AO_RUN_FILE`, `AO_DATA_DIR` and `AO_PORT`. Lab data: 1 project, 8 sessions (4 archived). The app and its daemon were fully stopped before each launch. One warm-up launch after the build is not counted.

## How

- `main/launch-timing.ts` keeps the first time each mark is set, measured from `process.getCreationTime()`.
- `windowShown` is the window's `show` event, so it covers the load path and the fallback timer.
- The shell reports from the second animation frame after the workspace renders, when that frame is on screen. It reports nothing while the startup loader is up or on the daemon failure screen.
- The line is logged once per process. A reload reports the frame again and main ignores it.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- `npx vitest run` at `de719c54f5`: 748 of 749 files pass. `useCloudModelCatalog.test.tsx` failed once in the full run and passes when run alone; this change does not touch it.
- After merging `main` and the review fix (`faf9444346`): both typechecks pass, and the shell, launch timing, preload and share dialog tests pass. The new shell case fails against the old predicate.

title: perf(browser): load a preview when the Browser panel is first shown
body:
Code changes: +35 -8\
Tests: +79 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A session's preview no longer loads until its Browser panel is shown, when the session has no browser tab yet.

## Why

Entering a session that has a preview URL loaded the preview into a new tab even with the Browser panel closed (`SessionView` passes `previewUrl` to `useBrowserView` without checking the slot). Every viewed session with a preview kept one renderer process for a page nobody was looking at. This is option E in the hidden browser tab memory design; option D (cap on hidden live tabs) follows in a second PR.

## Before / After

Dev build on one Mac, isolated data dir. 8 sessions with the same local preview page, each entered once with the Browser panel closed, then a ninth session with no preview. Sampled 60 s after arriving there. 3 fresh launches each, median (range). Before is `main` at `ae3c44f07a`.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser tab renderers | 8 (8 to 8) | 0 (0 to 0) |
| Their memory footprint | 332 MB (331 to 333) | 0 MB |
| Their RSS | 600 MB (599 to 637) | 0 MB |
| Then open the Browser panel on one session: tab renderers | 8 | 1 (1 to 1), preview loaded |
| Same step: footprint | 346 MB (334 to 348) | 72 MB (72 to 76) |
| Enter one session with a preview, panel closed: tab renderers, preview loads | 1, 1 load | 0, 0 loads |
| Then open the Browser panel: Browser tab click to loaded tab | 53 ms (tab already live) | 189 ms (tab created, then loaded) |
| An agent's first command in that session (`ao browser get url`) | the preview URL | `about:blank`, and the preview is loaded in that tab within 4 s |

Footprint is the macOS `footprint` figure (resident plus compressed and swapped), read per tab process found through `webContents.getOSProcessId()`. RSS is from `ps`. RSS is unstable on this machine: under memory pressure an idle tab's RSS fell from about 70 MB to under 3 MB within a minute while its footprint stayed at about 40 MB.

Screenshots of the dev app's real window, same lab data, window size and preview page on both builds. The sessions use a stub agent, so the session pane shows "Agent exited".

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: session 1 entered with the Browser panel closed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a3da3f7-335f-4f95-8bb9-c4b95588de79) | ![After: session 1 entered with the Browser panel closed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d34b0698-9c1f-4077-91f2-fa75291334d3) |
| Window looks the same. Process list: 2 renderer rows (the shell and one Browser tab), 1 preview load | Process list: 1 renderer row (the shell only), 0 preview loads |
| ![Before: Browser panel opened](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/221b52da-a16f-4ac9-a8a3-16e954317c14) | ![After: Browser panel opened](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69450eac-390e-4db6-83a8-4f64ddf68d50) |
| The page was already loaded: 53 ms from the Browser tab click to a loaded tab | The tab is created when the panel opens: 189 ms to a loaded tab |
| ![Before: panel closed, switched to another session and back, panel opened again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f54040f-920b-4577-b926-cefa6dbeac70) | ![After: panel closed, switched to another session and back, panel opened again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/241f0eb8-5573-4227-84b6-d1bf27de7630) |
| Same page, 1 preview load in total, no blank tab | Same page, 1 preview load in total, no blank tab |

## How

- `useBrowserView`: with the slot hidden and no tab of the person's in the session, the preview trigger is held instead of consumed. It is consumed when the slot is shown or a tab appears.
- A session that already has a tab loads the preview on entry as before: the renderer process exists either way.
- A held preview waits for a running agent command to end, then loads only if the active tab is still blank. An agent's `ao browser open` that arrived first keeps its page.
- The pending-load cancel moved from the effect cleanup to a request counter, because the effect now also re-runs on slot, tab and agent-activity changes. A session change bumps the counter.
- Not changed: a new `ao preview` on the viewed session still reveals the panel and loads at once. Agent commands still create their tab on demand. A phone still gets its first page through `openLivePreview`.

Agent-visible difference: a session entered with the panel closed has no tab yet, so an agent's first `ao browser` command there creates a blank tab and sees `about:blank`. The held preview loads into that tab as soon as the command ends (loaded 4 s later in the end-to-end check). Before, the preview was already live when the agent arrived.

Not changed here: when an agent opens a page in a session before the person has ever entered it, entering the session loads the preview over the agent's page. `main` does the same (scenario 6b below).

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- `npx vitest related --run` on the two changed files plus `scripts/ci-vitest-always-run.txt`: 35 files, 1478 tests pass.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- 4 new tests in `useBrowserView.test.tsx`; the 3 behaviour tests fail on `main`.
- Not run: CI. The lane picker runs nothing for draft PRs.

End-to-end check in the dev app (isolated data dir, window 1320x860, same preview page and daemon binary on both builds). Before is `ae3c44f07a`, the merge base; after is `fa0b5ad7f3`, this PR's head. One launch each. The Mac's screen was locked during this run, so times are to a loaded tab, not to painted pixels.

1. Enter a session with a preview, Browser panel closed: before 1 tab renderer and 1 preview load; after 0 and 0. Pass.
2. Open the Browser panel: both load the page and it renders (title "Lab page", 2000 table rows, 20000 objects kept). Click to loaded tab: 53 ms before (already live), 189 ms after (tab created). Pass.
3. Close the panel, switch to another session and back, open it again: both show the same page, one preview load in total, one tab, no blank tab. Pass.
4. A session that already has a tab (made by `ao browser tabs`), entered with the panel closed: both load the preview into it on entry. Pass.
5. `ao preview index.html` while viewing the session: both open the panel and load the page. 305 ms before (the live tab loads again, second load), 390 ms after (first load). Pass.
6a. Person enters with the panel closed, agent runs `ao browser open <url>`, person opens the panel: both end on the agent's page. Before, the preview loaded first and was replaced (1 load); after, it never loaded (0 loads). Pass.
6b. Agent opens a page before the person has ever entered the session: on both builds, entering loads the preview over the agent's page. The same on `main`, so not a regression, but the agent's page is not kept here.
7. Agent in a session entered with the panel closed: before, `ao browser get url` returns the preview URL; after, the first command returns `about:blank` and the preview is loaded 4 s later (`get url` and `get title` then return the preview URL and "Lab page"). A full `ao browser snapshot` of the 2000-row lab page exceeds the agent-browser output limit on both builds.

title: fix(chat): inset the composer's text and toolbar the same from both sides
body:
## Summary

The chat composer had more space on the left than on the right, both in the text and in the toolbar under it.

**Cause**
- **Text:** the editor had `pl-[7px] pr-0` inside the form's `px-3`. Text started 19px from the card's left edge, but on the right it could run to 12px.
- **Toolbar:** the leading **+** is a 28px ghost button. Its glyph's ink starts about 9.7px inside the button: 7px of centring, plus the Myna plus starting 2.7px into its 14px box. That put the ink about 22px from the left edge. The filled send circle *is* its own edge, so it sat 12px from the right.

**Fix (outer size, radius, colours and behaviour unchanged)**

| | Left before | Right before | Left after | Right after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft text and placeholder | 19px | 12px | 19px | 19px |
| Toolbar (+ ink / send circle) | ~22px | 12px | ~22px | 22px |

- **Editor padding:** `ComposerEditor` uses `px-[7px]` on the field, the placeholder and the prompt-suggestion ghost text.
- **Scrollbar gutter:** the field reserves `scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges`. So does whichever element scrolls (the field, or the wrapper in suggestion mode), and so does the placeholder (now `overflow-hidden`). With overlay scrollbars nothing is reserved. With classic scrollbars the gutter is the same on both sides, so text stays centred and does not reflow when the scrollbar appears or when the first character replaces the placeholder. The gutter lives only on the editor elements, not the shared `.chat-composer-scrollbar` class (ElicitationDock and sent-message folds also use that class).
- **Send controls:** inset by `me-2.5` (10px, a logical property). `COMPOSER_SEND_INSET` is exported once and used by `ChatComposer` and the side-chat `SideComposer`.

All composer variants go through these two components: session chat, the /new page, the orchestrator, terminal handoff (via `ChatWorkspace`), and side chats.

## Tests

The unit tests now check the symmetric classes on the field, the placeholder, the suggestion ghost and wrapper, and the send group/button (`ChatComposer.test.tsx`, `ChatPromptSuggestion.test.tsx`, `IndependentSideChats.test.tsx`). Per the local rule, nothing was run locally; CI is the check.

## Known trade-off

On systems with **classic** scrollbars (Windows/Linux, or macOS set to always show scrollbars), the reserved gutter now sits on both sides. The text is symmetric there, but it starts about one thin-scrollbar width further in than the + glyph. With macOS overlay scrollbars (the default with a trackpad) nothing changes on the left.

## Manual check

1. Open a chat. In an empty composer, the placeholder's left inset matches its right; the + glyph and the send circle sit the same distance from their edges.
2. Type a line long enough to wrap. Its wrap edge sits as far from the right as the text start does from the left. Typing the first character does not move the text.
3. Paste 10+ lines so the editor scrolls. No reflow when the scrollbar appears; try it with System Settings → Appearance → Show scroll bars → Always.
4. Repeat in light and dark, at a narrow window, with attachments staged, with queued messages (queue dock), on the /new page, in a side chat (`/btw`), and with a next-message suggestion showing.

title: fix(chat): reopen a chat where the reader left it
body:
## Problem
Leave a chat while scrolled up in its history and come back, and it reopens at the bottom. The scroll position was never remembered: a chat always starts pinned to the end and snaps there on first layout.

## Change
`ChatWorkspace.tsx` only.
- While a chat is scrolled away from the end, `onScroll` records the turn at the top of the view and the offset into it, per session, in a small in-memory map (capped at 64 sessions). Following the end clears the entry.
- A chat with a saved position opens unpinned. On its first layout it scrolls to that turn instead of snapping to the end. If the turn no longer exists, it falls back to following the end.
- Position is stored by turn key, not pixels, so it survives rows re-measuring. It is not persisted across app reloads.

## Validation
Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation. Behavior was checked by hand in the desktop app against a snapshot of real data.

title: perf(browser): cap hidden live browser tabs at 3
body:
Code changes: +279 -10\
Tests: +170 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

At most 3 browser tabs stay live in sessions whose Browser panel is not on screen. Past that, the least recently used hidden session that has been idle for 5 minutes has its views closed. Its tabs are rebuilt from their saved URLs when its panel is shown or an agent runs a browser command.

## Why

Each tab of a hidden session keeps a renderer process until the session ends or the app quits. This is option D in the hidden browser tab memory design, and the second half of TB-2 in `docs/plans/2026-10-13-desktop-performance-overhaul.md`. Option E is #8256.

## Before / After

Dev build on one Mac, isolated data dir. 8 sessions, each with one tab on the same local page and its panel not on screen, then a ninth session. 3 fresh launches each, median (range). Before is `main` at `6c02356681`. After is this branch, based on `ae3c44f07a`. The branch was rebased onto `adf9f6a303` afterwards. #8400 (Chromium throttles a hidden, idle session) landed in between and is not in these numbers.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hidden tab renderers at 1 minute | 8 | 8 |
| Their footprint at 1 minute | 333 MB (316 to 335) | 325 MB (324 to 335) |
| Hidden tab renderers at 7 minutes | 8 (8 to 8) | 3 (3 to 3) |
| Their footprint at 7 minutes | 320 MB (312 to 320) | 119 MB (118 to 120) |
| Their RSS at 7 minutes | 501 MB (471 to 594) | 225 MB (225 to 225) |
| Show the panel of the least recently used session: click to page loaded | 1.2 s (1.2 to 1.2), tab was live | 2.3 s (2.2 to 2.9), tab rebuilt |
| Tab renderers after that | 8 | 4 |

Footprint is the macOS `footprint` figure for each tab process (found through `webContents.getOSProcessId()`); RSS is from `ps` and is unstable on this machine under memory pressure. The 1.2 s on `main` is the harness's own delay, so a rebuild cost about 1.1 s here for one tab on a local page. The app's own log line reported 75 MB working set for each closed tab.

## How

- `discardSession` and `restoreSession` in `browser-view-host.ts` reuse the profile-switch path: `savedTabsForSession`, `agentBrowserRuntime.closeSession`, `disposeSessionTabs`, `rebuildSessionTabs`. Tab IDs, the active tab and the partition are kept; a Temporary partition is not cleared.
- Counted: tabs of sessions whose panel is not on screen. Background tabs of the session on screen are not counted and not closed.
- A session keeps its tabs while: its panel is on screen; it was used in the last 5 minutes; a command is in flight; its agent is working; a phone is watching; DevTools is open; a tab has a network capture, annotation mode or an unsent batch, a pending load, or audio; it has an agent tab.
- "Agent is working" is asked of the daemon (`GET /api/v1/sessions/:id`, `activity.state == "active"`). No answer counts as working, so remote host and cloud sessions are never closed. Without `isAgentWorking` wired, nothing is ever closed.
- While closed, `browser:getTabs` and `browser:ensure` answer from the saved state, so the tab strip and address bar do not change. Entering the session does not rebuild it; showing the panel does.
- Together with #8400: a hidden idle session is throttled first, and closed once the cap and the 5 idle minutes apply. A rebuild runs as a browser operation, so its pages load unthrottled; when it ends the session is throttled again.
- One log line per close and rebuild (`AO: closed N hidden browser tab(s) of <session>, X MB working set, panel was|never shown`).

Known gaps:
- Scroll position, unsent form input, script state and Back/Forward history are lost: the rebuild is a plain `loadURL`.
- For about 100 ms during the rebuild the panel shows its empty "New tab" state before the page appears (sampled once in the dev app). A profile switch does the same today.
- An agent command on a closed session waits for all its tabs to reload, active tab first.
- Not checked: a download in progress in a hidden tab.

## Decisions needed

Defaults taken, as instructed:

1. Reload on return: accepted. No notice in the panel in this version.
2. Cap and idle time: 3 tabs and 5 minutes, as constants (`MAX_HIDDEN_LIVE_TABS`, `HIDDEN_DISCARD_IDLE_MS`). No setting.
3. Agent's browser: never closed while the session's agent is working, in addition to the checks above.
4. `ao browser` results: unchanged. The agent is not told the page was reloaded.
5. Unsent form input: its loss is accepted in this version.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- `npx vitest related --run` on the three changed files plus `scripts/ci-vitest-always-run.txt`: 26 files, 1064 tests pass.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.
- 13 new tests in `browser-view-host.test.ts`: close order, what the panel is told while closed, rebuild from the panel and from an agent command, pages stay unthrottled during a rebuild, each exemption, session end, profile switch on a closed session.
- Not run: CI. The lane picker runs nothing for draft PRs.

title: [Bug]: HTTP/2 remote-proxy test teardown can time out on macOS
body:
### What went wrong?

A local macOS Vitest run of `frontend/src/main/remote-proxy.test.ts` reproduced a teardown timeout in `verifies the host once per upstream session, before the credential`. The focused run timed out in the HTTP/2 fixture's `afterEach` while waiting for the upstream server to close. The other 80 cases in that file passed.

The affected test file at upstream commit `78e66b41576462cf50ccb1a6c24655a57efec5a7` matches the reproduced version. This is a test failure. No application behavior was tested by the reproduction.

### Agent-assisted analysis

The nested fixture waits for HTTP/2 server shutdown before the outer hook closes the proxy and its persistent upstream session. Closing the proxy first made all 81 cases in the file pass on the same Mac. The four-line test-only patch is prepared on a branch based on upstream main.

title: fix(chat): start the live row's dots on the step icons' left edge
body:
Code changes: +30 -20\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The live row's activity dots (Thinking, Working, Running…, Starting/setup labels) now start on the same left edge as the step rows' icons and text, and the label starts where the step labels start. The setup checklist's marks use the same column.

## Why

In the chat timeline the live "Thinking · 20s" row's dots sat to the right of the row above. In the reported screenshot "Searched for 1 pattern" started at x≈20 and the dots at x≈27 (device pixels, 2x), so the loader and its label didn't line up with the step rows, their icons or the message text.

**Root cause.** `LiveWorkingMark` and the live row's slot around it were both `size-5` (20px) with `justify-center`. The lattice is 13px across (4 × 2.5px dots + 3 × 1px gaps), so centring it left (20 − 13) / 2 = **3.5 CSS px** (7 device px at 2x) before the first dot. With the 8px row gap, the label started at 28px. The step rows (`ACTIVITY_SUMMARY_BUTTON_CLASS`) put a 12px icon at the turn's edge and the label at 12 + 6 = 18px. The setup checklist used the same centred 20px slot, so its marks sat 3.5–4px in too. This came from the original live-row layout, not from #8245. #8245 (still open) shrinks the slot to 12px but keeps it centred. That leaves the 13px lattice half a pixel *outside* the column, where the live row's `overflow-hidden` wrapper clips it.

## Before / After

Offsets from the turn's left edge, in CSS px (device px at 2x in brackets):

| Row | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live row dots (Thinking / Working / Running… / Starting) | 3.5 (7) | **0**, the step icons' left edge |
| Live row label | 28 | **18**, the step labels' left edge |
| Live row failed ✕ | 4 | 0 |
| Reconnect detail line | 28 | 18 |
| Setup checklist marks (✓, ✕, pending ring, running dots) | 4 / 3.5 | 0 |
| Setup checklist labels and failed-setup notes | 28 | 18 |
| Step rows, "Worked for" | 0 icon / 18 label, "Worked for" 0 | unchanged |

Screenshots aren't attached: per the repo owner's workflow nothing was run locally, and they're checking it by hand.

## How

- New `STEP_MARK_SLOT_CLASS` (`flex size-3 shrink-0 items-center justify-start`) in `ChatTimelineItems.tsx` gives the step rows' icon column a name. The live row's slot, `LiveWorkingMark`, `ResponseSpinner` and the setup checklist's slot all use it, so the live mark and the settled row's icon are the same box: 12px wide on the same left edge. Nothing moves when a step leaves the live row for its own row, or when the live row hands over to "Worked for".
- The lattice is left-aligned (`justify-start`), not centred, so its first column of dots starts exactly on the edge and the extra pixel overhangs into the 6px gap. It still lands on whole device pixels at 2x.
- The live row's gap goes from 8px to 6px (`gap-1.5`, the step rows' gap). Indents under the label go from `pl-7` to `pl-4.5` (18px).
- `LiveWorkingMark` now renders `ResponseSpinner`, since the two were the same mark in different boxes.
- Not changed: the dots animation, copy, colours, type sizes, row heights and the shimmer. The orchestrator startup alert sits under the composer, not in the timeline, and has no loader, so it's left alone. Side chats, orchestrator chats and cloud chats all draw their live row through this one `LiveResponseStatus`, and no CSS shifts step rows or the live row in any of them, so the fix covers every surface and width.
- **Overlap with #8245:** both PRs touch the live row's slot, gap and indents. Whichever merges second needs a small conflict fix. The result should keep #8245's type scale and this PR's left-aligned `STEP_MARK_SLOT_CLASS`, not #8245's centred lattice.

## Testing

Not run locally, per the repo owner's workflow; CI covers it. I read the tests that touch this row: none assert the slot, gap or indent classes. They locate the mark as the label's previous sibling holding `response-spinner`, and that structure is unchanged.

Check by hand, in light and dark:
- Run a turn: "Thinking · Ns" dots start on the same x as the icons of the step rows above, and "Thinking" starts on the same x as their labels.
- A running command: "Running command · Ns" lines up the same way. When the step finishes and moves up into its own row, its icon and label don't move sideways.
- When the turn settles, the live row fades and "Worked for" takes over with no jump.
- A new session's setup checklist: the ✓ / pending / running marks sit on the same edge as the live row's dots, and the labels start together.
- Repeat in a side chat, an orchestrator chat, a cloud session and a narrow window.

body:
### Proposal

Would a short operator recipe for checking Git worktree conflict recovery fit the contributor documentation? The example creates two synthetic commits that modify the same file, attempts the merge in a detached review worktree, aborts the conflict and verifies that both branch refs and file contents survive.

The [44-line candidate](https://github.com/marikbrest/agent-orchestrator/blob/marik/upstream-worktree-conflict-recipe/test/contributions/worktree-conflict.sh) passed on macOS and in an Ubuntu VM. It requires Git and a POSIX shell and uses a disposable temporary repository.

This checks Git recovery in an isolated worktree. It would serve as a recipe. Coverage of AO credential or publishing boundaries would be a separate change using AO fixtures. I would appreciate guidance on whether the recipe belongs in the docs or should stay an external example.

title: feat(sessions): review someone else's PR with automatic fixing turned off
body:
Reviewing someone else's PR is now a normal claim with one flag: `ao session claim-pr --review` turns off the session's automatic CI and review-comment fixing and native auto-review, then claims. The PR stays attached, so you can try the branch and ask the agent about the changes, but none of its feedback is sent to the agent. `--review=false` turns fixing back on to take the PR over. An earlier version of this PR also used `--review`, but stored a new `review_only` mode (column, migration and "Reviewing" label). That was dropped: this `--review` stores nothing and only sets the switches each session already has. Refs #5986, #6864 ## What changed | Area | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Reviewing a PR | Agents were told never to claim someone else's PR | `ao session claim-pr --no-takeover --review` turns off automatic CI and review-comment fixing and native auto-review, then claims. If the claim is refused, the switches go back to what they were | | Spawning a reviewer | No way to start with the switches off, so a CI failure could arrive before the agent turned them off | `ao spawn --claim-pr --no-takeover --review` turns all three off before the claim | | Taking the PR over | Not possible without the inspector | `ao session claim-pr --review=false` turns CI and review-comment fixing back on | | Merge-conflict messages | Always sent, with no switch | Covered by the CI switch. If the switch can't be read, the message is skipped and the error surfaces, the same as the parent-stack check | | Agent instructions and skill docs | "Never claim a PR for review-only work" | Claim it with both switches off and use one session per review. The PR is not the user's, so leave it unchanged unless the user asks. To take it over, turn the switches back on | | `claim-pr` output | Checkout hints only | A `--review` or `--review=false` claim says which it was; a plain claim prints nothing new | | Claiming a PR left by a finished session | The PR kept the old owner's CI switch, so a reviewer with it off could still get CI failures and conflicts | The PR takes the new owner's CI switch | | CI switch description (9 locales and mobile) | "Sends CI failures…" | "Sends CI failures and merge conflicts…" | No database, API or UI behaviour changes beyond the switch description. Roughly +173 lines of code, +194 of tests, +85 of docs, and about 16 changed lines of prompts and strings. ## How to test 1. Run `ao spawn --project

--name review-test --claim-pr --no-takeover --review`. 2. Open the session inspector. Both "Automatically fix" switches and auto-review show off, and the agent gets no CI failure message. 3. In that session, run `ao session claim-pr --review=false`. Both switches turn on, and the next poll sends the CI failure. 4. On a conflicting PR claimed by a session with the CI switch off, no "merge conflicts" message arrives. It arrives after the switch is turned on. Use a PR you own for this. Claiming a real contributor PR with the switches on sends its review comments to the agent. ## Tests Written, not run locally: - CLI: `TestSessionClaimPRReview_TurnsEverySwitchOffBeforeTheClaim`, `TestSessionClaimPRReviewFalse_TurnsFixingBackOnToTakeOver`, `TestSessionClaimPRReview_RestoresSwitchesWhenTheClaimIsRefused`, `TestSpawnReviewTurnsSwitchesOffBeforeClaim`, `TestSpawnReviewRequiresClaimPR` - store: `TestClaimPRTakeoverAppliesNewOwnerAutoInjectCI` - lifecycle: `TestPRObservation_CISwitchOffSilencesMergeConflict` - prompt and skill-doc tests updated, with checks that the old "never claim" wording is gone ## Release note Turning off "Automatically fix CI failures" now also stops merge-conflict messages for that session's PRs. ## Risks - **The switches are per session.** A session that also owns its own PR loses that PR's messages too. The instructions say to use one session per review. - **Review comments that arrive while the switch is off are never sent**, even after it is turned back on. That matches the inspector toggle today. The takeover instructions tell the agent to read existing comments on the PR. - **Nothing blocks pushing.** "Leave the PR unchanged" is only an instruction to the agent. - **A plain `ao session claim-pr` (without `--review`) still sends feedback.** The agent instructions cover this; nothing enforces it. - **Native auto-review stays off after `--review=false`.** Start a review with `ao review trigger` or the inspector if wanted. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added controls to enable or disable automatic CI-failure, merge-conflict, and review-comment fixing for a session. * Added an option to disable automatic fixing when starting a session that claims a pull request. * Review-only sessions can claim another person’s pull request with automatic fixing off, without making other changes unless asked. * **Documentation** * Updated CLI help and guides with the new controls and review workflow. Clarified that automatic CI handling includes merge conflicts.

title: feat(usage): show consumed usage % in usage indicators
body:
## Summary
Usage indicators now show the **percentage of usage consumed** instead of the percentage remaining, and progress bars **fill as usage grows** (18% used = 18% filled).

Port of nikhilachale/agent-orchestrator#25 onto upstream `main`. The Codex-only settings components that PR touched were replaced here by `AgentAccountsSection` and the Usage page (#7899), so the change is re-applied to those surfaces.

### Surfaces
- **Usage page → Limits** (`UsageLimits` `LimitWindowRow`): shows `NN% used`, bar fills with usage. The pace marker and caption now show projected usage at reset ("about NN% used by the reset") instead of what is left.
- **Settings → Agents limit rows** (`AgentAccountsSection` `LimitRow`): `NN% used` with a filling meter; aria label `{window}, NN% used`.
- **Chat header `ContextMeter`** quota chip: names the window, e.g. `Session 78% used` / `Weekly 93% used` instead of `78% quota`. Non-finite or negative (not reported) values stay hidden.

Every provider already reports `usedPercent`, so values are drawn as-is (no double inversion). `remainingPercent()` in `lib/usage-limits` is replaced by a clamping `usedPercent()`.

### Other changes
- Warning tones flipped to match: amber at ≥75% used, red at 100% used.
- i18n keys renamed (`usedForLimit`, `percentUsed`, `usage.limits.used`, `usage.limits.paceUsed`; `barLabel` reworded) in all 9 locales, including `ru`.
- No changes to usage fetching or API integrations.

## Screenshot
Screenshot from the original PR (the pre-#7899 Codex settings layout). The same consumed-percentage presentation applies to the new surfaces:

![Usage indicator showing consumed percentages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nikhilachale/agent-orchestrator/ao/6410b74b-screenshots/usage-indicator.png)

## Testing
- Updated `ContextMeter.test.tsx` and `usage-limits.test.ts` for the new wording and values.
- Not run locally on this port; relying on CI.

title: fix(sidebar): remove projects optimistically instead of showing "Removing…"
body:
## Problem

Removing a project left its row in the sidebar showing "Removing <name>…" (grey, muted) for as long as the daemon took to tear it down, and that can take a long time. Removing any project also sent you home, even when you were looking at a different one.

## Change

Removal is now optimistic. When you confirm, the project disappears right away and a toast says **Removed \<name\>**. The teardown request runs in the background. There is no pending row, disabled menu item or spinner.

- **Every surface at once.** The project leaves the local list, the host's list (remote) or the raw cloud project list (cloud), plus the merged list. The sidebar and its pins, the board, Artifacts, the archive modal, Cmd+K, New Task/New chat pickers and notifications all read those lists.
- **No resurrection mid-teardown.** `optimistic-project-removals.ts` keeps a removed-ids set, modeled on `optimistic-session-kills.ts`. The local and remote fetchers and the cloud project fetcher drop those ids. The merged list and the sidebar's remote-host memo rebuild when the set changes. A poll or event refetch during teardown can't bring the row back.
- **Leaving the page first.** If you're viewing the project, its settings or one of its sessions, the app goes home (`replace`, so Back doesn't return to it) **before** the row is dropped. That way no page renders a project that's gone. Removing a project you aren't viewing no longer navigates at all.
- **Rollback.** If the request fails, the lists are read again. If the server no longer lists the project (for example, the teardown finished after the request gave up, the #7256 case), it stays removed. Otherwise it comes back in its old position: from the re-read, or from the snapshot if the read fails too. An error toast then shows the server's reason and a **Retry** action. Pins are only cleared after success, so a project that comes back keeps its pinned place.
- **When the tombstone clears.** For local and remote projects, it clears once a re-read confirms the server dropped the project. Adding the same folder again also clears it, because ids come from the folder name. Cloud tombstones stay for the rest of the session: the control plane archives after it answers, and cloud ids are never reused.
- **Remote and cloud.** Both follow the same path. Remote calls the host's `DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}`. Cloud calls the control plane's `deleteProject`. If the control plane isn't ready, cloud shows the error toast and removes nothing.
- **Code layout.** The flow lives in `useRemoveProject`. The shell passes stable callbacks into the memoized Sidebar.
- **Removed:** the Sidebar's `isRemoving` and `removeError` state, the in-row status and error lines, and the `shell.removingNamed` key in all 9 locales. Added `shell.projectRemoved`, `shell.couldNotRemoveProjectNamed` and `shell.removeProjectRetry`.

Backend behavior is unchanged: same endpoints, same teardown, nothing extra deleted.

### Not covered: "kept" notices

`DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}` returns only `{projectId, removedStorageDir}`, and `removedStorageDir` is always `false`. It doesn't report dirty worktrees it kept, and the "archive after teardown outlives the budget" fix (#7256) isn't merged. So there's no signal to show a "kept something" toast without inventing one. A late success after a failed request is handled by the re-read described under Rollback.

## Tests

Written, not run locally; CI runs them.
- `useRemoveProject.test.tsx`
  - The project drops before the daemon answers, and a mid-teardown refetch doesn't restore it.
  - The page is left before the row is dropped.
  - Failure restores the project in place, with the reason and a Retry that removes it again.
  - If the re-read fails, the snapshot is restored.
  - If the request fails but the teardown finished, the project stays removed.
  - Remote removal leaves the local project with the same id alone.
  - Cloud removal filters the raw list and keeps its tombstone; cloud rollback restores the raw list; nothing is removed while the control plane isn't ready.
- `useWorkspaceQuery.remote.test.tsx`
  - A remote row stays hidden through a poll and comes back on rollback.
  - The local fetch drops a removed project.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx`
  - Confirming hands off to the shell, with no Removing… status or alert and no navigation from the Sidebar.

## Check by hand

1. Remove a project you aren't viewing. The row and its sessions vanish instantly, "Removed \<name\>" appears, and the page doesn't change.
2. Open a project's board (or one of its sessions) and remove it. You land on home with no flash of a "not found" page, and Back doesn't return to it.
3. Remove a project with several live sessions. It stays gone the whole time, including after the next poll.
4. Pinned project: remove it and it's gone from the pinned group. Add the same folder again and it isn't pinned.
5. Failure: stop the daemon (or a remote host) and remove a project. It comes back in place, the error toast shows the reason, and Retry works once the daemon is back.
6. A remote-host project and a cloud project behave the same way.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Local, remote, and cloud projects disappear from project lists as soon as removal begins.
  - Removing the project you’re currently viewing navigates you away.
  - Successful removals show a confirmation; failed removals offer a retry.
- **Bug Fixes**
  - Projects stay hidden during workspace refreshes while removal is pending.
  - If removal fails, the project is restored when it’s still present.
  - Local, remote, and cloud projects with the same ID are handled independently.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(terminal): ship shell-tab agent status and program titles to everyone
body:
Ships two features that were Developer Mode only: the agent running in a shell tab, with live status (#7787), and terminal tabs and sessions labeled with the title their program sets (#8018). The known follow-ups are fixed first (separate commits), then the gates come out.

## Follow-ups fixed

**#7787 (shell-tab agent status), the three P2 review threads**
- `exec claude` showed "working" on its first draw: `exec` keeps the process group, so the start grace never reset. The tracker now also resets it when argv[0] changes.
- Typing at an idle agent's prompt read up to 60 screen lines on every pause. The host now marks a settled-screen update whose only output was typing echo (`echoOnly`, omitted by older hosts). The manager keeps its idle reading for those. A *waiting* agent is still re-read, since the keys may have answered its question.
- A dead host was re-dialed every 30 s forever. A watch now stops after six failed connections in a row.

**#8018 (program titles)**
- Fish: `MeaningfulTerminalTitle` only hid fish's `<command> <dir>` title when the command was one word, so `git status ~/x` labeled the tab. It now recognizes fish's default title shape (optional `[host]`, up to 20 chars of command line, then `prompt_pwd`, including dirs with spaces). Fish's own prompt and command titles never label a tab, the same as bash/zsh, which set no command titles by default. This also avoids every `ls` flashing on the tab. Programs that set their own title (vim, htop, Claude, Codex) still label it.
- 3 s full scan: `terminaltitle.Manager` no longer reads every session and shell on a timer. It reads live sessions once at start, then one session per CDC event (spawn, restore, terminate and delete all emit one) and skips events caused by its own title writes. The shell terminal service tells it when user shells open and close (shellterm now takes a list of trackers). Watches are keyed on handle + launch id, because a restored session keeps its handle but gets a new host. A watch ends when the runtime can't report titles (gone, tmux, old host) or the host refuses six connections, instead of retrying every 30 s forever.
- Also checked: writes stay debounced (≤1 per terminal per 2 s, changed-only); an explicit user name still wins (daemon read path, unchanged); Claude's `·` spinner frame is now trimmed like its other glyphs; titles are capped at 100 runes with control/bidi chars stripped; titles are keyed per session/handle; titles aren't logged and nothing sends them to telemetry.

## Gates removed
- `ShellTerminalTab.tsx`: `developerMode &&` on agent tracking, and `developerMode ?` on `terminalTitle`.
- `SessionView.tsx`: `developerMode &&` on grouped-tab agent tracking, plus the unused `developerMode` selector and memo dep.
- `useWorkspaceQuery.ts`: `developerTerminalTitle()` (both session mappers) and `developerMode` in the remote-workspaces memo inputs.
- Tests for the gates removed. New tests pin the ungated behavior.
- No daemon toggle existed for these. The `_shell.tsx` `{enabled: developerMode}` sync is chat hibernation and limit history, so it's untouched. No settings rows, palette entries or i18n strings named these features. The Developer Mode toggle stays for other previews.

Scope is unchanged: agent status covers local shells only. Remote-host and cloud shells stay plain because only the local daemon's mux carries `shell-agents`. Program titles show for local and remote-host sessions and shells, as they did in Developer Mode.

## Risk notes
- **Idle cost:** nothing polls now. Agent watches exist only while a shell tab is subscribed, and title watches are one host connection per live terminal. Per-event cost is one primary-key session read.
- **Windows:** ConPTY has no process groups, and its host held foreground watches open without ever answering. The conpty runtime now reports foreground as unavailable on Windows at once, so Windows shell tabs stay plain with no idle connection. Titles work on Windows.
- **Process inspection:** `tcgetpgrp` + `kern.procargs2` (macOS) or `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (Linux), on the user's own processes. A failure returns no argv, so the tab stays plain. No permission prompts.
- **Protocol:** `echoOnly` is an omitempty field. Old hosts with a new daemon keep the old behavior, and new hosts with an old daemon are ignored.

## Tests (written, not run locally; CI runs them)
- `conpty/foreground_tracker_test.go`: exec restarts the grace; echo-only flag for typing vs resize vs late output.
- `shellagent/manager_test.go`: no screen reads while typing at an idle prompt; a waiting agent is re-read; unreachable host stops after six dials.
- `domain/terminal_title_test.go` (new): normalization (spinners incl. `·`, controls, bidi, length cap) and the fish shapes.
- `terminaltitle/manager_test.go` (new): boot load, event-driven start/move/stop/delete, own-write events ignored, debounced changed-only writes, shells tracked, no redial of an unavailable terminal, restart after restore with a new launch.
- Frontend: agent shows and title labels without Developer Mode; remote/cloud shells stay plain and unsubscribed; remote session title without Developer Mode.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Local shell tabs show detected agent names and terminal titles regardless of Developer Mode. Remote and cloud shells remain plain tabs.
  * Changed-file annotations in session chat can open the referenced files.
* **Improvements**
  * Terminal activity tracking distinguishes typed-input echoes from other screen changes, reducing unnecessary updates while the shell is idle.
  * Terminal titles are recognized and cleaned up more consistently, including titles with spinner characters.
  * Session titles use available terminal titles without depending on Developer Mode.
  * Terminal title and agent tracking respond to session and shell-tab changes, with retries for temporary connection failures.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(grok): pre-trust the workspace so the first prompt cannot quit Grok
body:
Fixes #8244

## Problem
Grok Build 1.0.77 opens a full-screen **"Do you trust the contents of this directory?"** dialog (`y` = proceed, `n` = **No, quit**) in every new AO workspace. AO typed the after-start prompt into that dialog, so the first `n` in the task quit Grok, and Grok logged `quit.started trigger=key`.

The 8 s delay came from readiness. Grok draws on the alternate screen, so its `Grok Build` marker never appears in the raw output ring. Every launch waited out the 8 s timeout and then typed the prompt anyway.

Reproduced in an isolated dev daemon on Grok 1.0.77: a first key `n` (or `Run`) quit Grok, while `hi`, `R`, `u` and `Ru` did not. A rendered-viewport capture showed the trust dialog. `--fullscreen` fails the same way, so it is not a fix.

## Changes
- **Grok workspace trust (`grok/trust.go`)**: `PreLaunch` records the session workspace in `$GROK_HOME/trusted_folders.toml` (default `~/.grok`, resolved from the launch env via `NativeSessionConfigDir`). It works like the Kimi / Claude Code trust seeding:
  - Appends a `[folders.'<path>']` table in Grok's own layout (`trusted = true`, `decided_at = <unix s>`), so Grok's existing entries keep their formatting.
  - Leaves any recorded decision for the folder alone, including a user's "no".
  - Never writes a file it cannot parse, or one whose result would not parse.
  - Also records the symlink-resolved path when it differs (macOS `/private`).
- **Rendered-screen readiness (`ports.PromptReadinessHints`)**:
  - `RenderedScreen` makes `waitForPromptReadiness` match against `StyledTerminalOutputReader` (the rendered viewport). It falls back to raw output when the host reports `ErrStyledTerminalOutputUnavailable`.
  - `BlockingPatterns` hold readiness while a startup dialog is visible. If one is still visible at timeout, spawn fails with a delivery error instead of typing the task into the dialog.
- Grok opts in to both: `RenderedScreen: true`, plus the trust heading as a blocking pattern (the dialog also shows the `Grok Build` footer).

## Tests
- `grok/trust_test.go`:
  - seeds the trust table
  - keeps existing entries byte-for-byte and is idempotent
  - leaves a recorded `trusted = false` alone
  - leaves invalid TOML and a non-table `folders` key untouched
  - quotes a path containing `'`
  - is a no-op without a workspace
- `grok_test.go`: hints include `RenderedScreen` and the trust-dialog blocking pattern.
- `session_manager/prompt_readiness_rendered_test.go`:
