title: fix(mobile): size later-batch menu rows on their first render
body: Code changes: +79 -17\ Tests: +80 -3\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Follow-up to #8191. Menu rows that a list mounts in a **later render batch** now have their width on their first render, so they no longer draw at their intrinsic width for a frame or two after the list remounts. ## Why #8191 read each row's slot in a layout effect. That covered the rows a list mounts together with itself, but not the rows it adds in later batches. After switching the Workers board's machine filter on an iPad, where those rows are on screen, they drew centred at their SwiftUI intrinsic width before snapping into place. The gap was found while rebasing #8218. - An instrumented build showed the layout effect *does* read the correct width for later-batch rows (68 of 68 rows logged a real width). - The problem is ordering: such a row's first commit can reach the screen before the render that applies the width. - Measuring sooner therefore can't fix it. The row has to be sized on its first render. ## Before / After iPad Pro 13" simulator, Workers board, switching from an empty machine to All machines. These are the bottom rows: the first three come from the list's first batch, and the rest from its second batch. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | Second-batch rows misdrawn on 10 of 16 switches: 1–2 frames, 7–43 ms | 0 of 16 switches | The GIFs play the switch at ¼ speed. ## How - `MenuRowWidthScope` holds the width the rows of one list last measured. `useMenuRowWidth` starts its state from that shared value, so a row mounted later is sized on its first render without waiting for any measurement. - The layout-effect read and `onLayout` stay. They size a list's very first rows, follow resizes such as rotation or split view, and update the shared value. Only a positive width updates it, so a slot laid out at zero for a moment doesn't start later rows at zero. - Where the scopes are: - `WorkerBoardList`, the PR list (`app/prs/index.tsx`) and `ChatTimeline` each provide one scope. They do it through a thin wrapper component, so the existing bodies are not re-indented. - The Workers screen keeps the width above the board's `machine|project` key with `useMenuRowWidths()` and passes it as `rowWidths`, so a board rebuilt for a new filter starts its first batch sized as well. - A scope's rows are assumed to share one slot width. That holds for each of these lists, whose rows are all full width or all inset by the same gutter. A wrong seed would be corrected by the row's own measurement in the same way it is today. - Android is unaffected. Its row is a plain `Pressable` laid out by Yoga at the slot width, and the native menu there is only an anchor mounted on long-press. Nothing sizes an Android row to its content, so the seeded width matches what Yoga already gives it. ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 429 files, 4167 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. - `lib/useMenuRowWidth.test.tsx` has new cases. They fail on the #8191 hook (with a do-nothing scope) and pass here: - a later row whose slot reports no width yet renders at the list's width on its first render; - rows mounted again under the same scope keep the width; - a width measured later seeds the rows after it; - a list remounted under held widths is seeded; - a zero-width measurement keeps the last real width as the seed; - rows outside any scope still measure themselves. - Simulator A/B on iOS 26.5: one Release build of this branch, with the `main` and fixed Hermes bundles swapped into the same binary. Two lab machines sat behind a read-only proxy in front of a local daemon, one with 64–169 live workers and one with none. Every captured frame after a switch was compared with the settled list in 8 horizontal bands, and each differing band was classed as *blank* (not rendered yet) or *misdrawn*. - **iPad Workers board:** before, 10 of 16 switches were misdrawn, only in the second-batch bands. After, 0 of 16. - **iPhone Workers board** (only first-batch rows on screen): 0 misdrawn in both builds, so nothing regressed from #8191. - **Settled layouts** are identical between the builds (0.0–0.06 % of pixels differ; one pair differed by 1.3 % because a live session changed between runs). - **Not reproduced:** the PR list. On `main` with up to 118 PRs on the iPad (Open → Merged), I saw no misdrawn second-batch frames in either build, only blank frames while rows render. Those frames are unchanged here. The PR list gets the same scope, and the unit tests cover the mechanism. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Menu rows in worker, PR, and chat lists now maintain consistent widths when lists update or remount, including when switching worker board filters. * Rows retain their last valid measured width when a layout reports zero width. * **Style** * Onboarding buttons are centered, use the full available width, and are capped at 400 pixels wide.

title: Mobile shows "You're offline" and "Phone offline" while the phone is connected
body:
## What happens

The mobile app says the phone is offline while it is connected and working:

- The Workers board, Projects and Pull Requests show the banner **"You're offline. Check this phone's Wi-Fi or mobile data."**
- Settings → Machines marks a paired machine **"Phone offline"**.
- At the same time, **Orchestrator Cloud shows "Connected · 2 coding agents"**, and the machine's sessions update live on the board, in chat and in Files.

## When

Seen on a Pixel 10a (Android 17) running a Release build of `main` at `bd4d0d4540`. Android never validated the phone's network: `adb shell dumpsys wifi` reports `isConnected=true isValidated=false`, on the home Wi-Fi and on an iPhone hotspot. In that state there is no default network, so NetInfo reports the phone as not connected, while the app's own requests still succeed. Captive-portal checks can fail like this on some routers, corporate networks and hotspots, so real users can hit it too.

## Why

`isPhoneOffline` in `packages/mobile/lib/linkHealth.ts` returns `phone.connected === false` and trusts NetInfo alone. `classifyLink` then reports `"phone-offline"` before looking at whether requests actually get answered. This dates from #7336 and is in the 2.3.0 store build.

## Expected

Show the phone as offline only when it really can't reach anything: for example, when NetInfo says disconnected **and** no recent request to a machine or to Cloud succeeded. A phone whose requests are being answered should not see the offline banner or "Phone offline".

## Steps

1. On Android, join a network that Android doesn't validate (or one whose connectivity check is blocked) while the internet still works.
2. Open the app: the offline banner and "Phone offline" appear, while Cloud and the machine keep working.

title: fix: restore and customize the Add to chat selection shortcut
body:
Code changes: +47 -17  
Tests: +242 -8  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Restore the Add to chat shortcut for highlighted text in file and diff views, and expose one editable **Add selection to chat** command in the shortcuts window. Its default is Ctrl+L on Windows/Linux and Cmd+L on macOS; the configured binding applies to chat, file, and diff selections.

## Why

File tabs focus their outer scrolling region, while the shortcut checked the inner code surface. A live file preview can also have a separate inner clipping viewport. Both focus states could reject the shortcut even though clicking **Add to chat** worked. The shortcut was also hardcoded separately in the chat and code toolbars, so it was absent from the shortcuts editor and could not be changed.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Full-file selection: the focused outer viewport rejects Ctrl+L. ![Before: file selection shortcut](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8daee549-588b-4752-b00f-a34bb3a95a72) | Adds exactly one annotation, preserves its rows, and focuses Chat. ![After: file selection shortcut](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bec3350-c4c6-4c3a-8d98-2b49a18f45e2) |
| Diff selection: the same focus state rejects Ctrl+L. ![Before: diff selection shortcut](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2b0b679-b818-4437-b127-e82a9ff8e0fb) | Adds the selected diff rows with the correct side. ![After: diff selection shortcut](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04bc24df-cbd6-481d-990f-e2004f06ee07) |
| The live preview rejects the outer viewport while metadata loads. | Recognizes the explicit owning keyboard region even with a nested clipping wrapper. |
| Add selection to chat is absent from the shortcuts editor; toolbar hints always show the hardcoded default. | The command can be edited, unassigned, reset, and reassigned through conflict handling. Both toolbars show the current binding immediately. |

The file/diff keyboard recordings above are attached. Shortcut-settings desktop capture was stopped at the user's request to leave the dev window alone; the editor, remapping, reset, and persistence flows are covered by automated checks.

## How

- Mark the file's focusable region as the selection keyboard scope and accept events on that exact region or the captured viewport. Keep live-range, visibility, repeat, dialog, and unrelated-input guards.
- Register the selection command in the shared shortcut catalog and localized label maps. Reuse the existing editor and persisted overrides without adding a new settings format.
- Read the effective binding in both selection handlers and render their hints from the same catalog. Electron leaves this contextual action to the renderer; browser and terminal input retain their existing ownership.

## Testing

- Project and E2E TypeScript checks pass on Linux with Node 24. The pinned Node 22.23.5 lockfile compatibility dry run passes.
- Focused validation: 11 suites pass, covering defaults and remapping on Windows/Linux/macOS, live hints, unassignment/reset, editor conflicts, and saved settings loaded from disk.
- Native Electron validation: seven checks pass for remapped chat/file/diff shortcuts and default file/diff, review-list, and pending-metadata shortcuts.
- Full local Vitest workflow shards pass: 4,648 and 4,987 tests (9,635 passed, six skipped), including the mandatory workflow suites. The previously failing `ChatWorkspace` suite passes all 272 tests.

Public-boundary, gitleaks, and CodeRabbit checks also pass.
- Local browser integration and all three real Electron boundary checks pass. The browser integration uses a child subreaper because this Docker container's `sleep` PID 1 otherwise retains the fixture's killed native daemon as a zombie and its restart check times out.
- Complete local renderer smoke: **189 passed** in the serial run, with no failures or retries. Earlier parallel runs hit five-second startup/reload deadlines under container contention. Prior-run screenshot ownership was also corrected to match CI's unprivileged user. Both complete renderer shards pass remotely (97 and 92 tests).
- Public-boundary validation passes locally and in CI. The pinned gitleaks 7.4.0 scan passes locally on all three PR commits and in CI.
- Rebased onto current main (`304995a514`), which already fixes the stale quota-label assertion responsible for the previous Vitest failure. No duplicate quota change is included.
- Independent P0/P1/P2 review caught a platform-specific E2E hint expectation; fixed it and received LGTM on `9d8c8855b1` with no remaining actionable findings.

## Checklist

title: fix(mobile): clear the chat header title when the route swaps to Terminal
body: Code changes: +5 -0 Tests: +18 -0 Others: +0 -0 ## What After **Switch to Terminal UI**, the session header no longer keeps the chat's title and state. It shows the session name, as a terminal session opened directly does. Fixes #8283 ## Why `ChatSessionScreen` sets a `headerTitle` component (`ConversationTitle` with the chat controller's state) on the `session/[id]` route. When the switch completes, the route swaps the chat screen for `TerminalSessionScreen` on the same route, and the route keeps its options. The terminal screen sets only `title`, and `headerTitle` outranks `title`, so the bar kept the chat's last render. The switch stops the Chat controller before the terminal starts (`source_stopping`), so on the Pixel the frozen header read **Stopped** while the daemon and the board said Idle. Nothing updates that component once the chat screen is gone, which is why it never corrected itself. ## Before / After Same session, same emulator, Release builds of this branch with and without the fix. The chat header before the switch reads Ready: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Terminal UI keeps the chat's title and its last state (Ready here; Stopped on the Pixel in #8283, where the chat had already rendered the stopped controller) | Terminal UI shows the session name, as a directly opened terminal session does | ## How An unmount-only layout effect in `ChatSessionScreen` clears `headerTitle` when the screen leaves the route, the same way the screen already restores `headerTransparent`/`headerStyle` for the terminal. It is separate from the effect that sets the title, so the title is not reset on every state change. Cloud sessions are not affected: `CloudSessionScreen` stays mounted for both modes and owns its header throughout. ## Testing - New test in `ChatSessionScreen.switch.test.tsx`: folds every `setOptions` call into the route's options as the stack does, drives the switch to a stopped controller, unmounts the chat as the route does, and checks no `headerTitle` is left. Without the fix the header kept the chat's title and state; with it the header shows the session name and stays that way (checked after 20 s+). title: fix(desktop): make the Cloud Chat approval menu change the mode
body:
## Why

In a Cloud Chat session, the approval policy menu does nothing. Picking any mode (mouse or keyboard) closes the menu and keeps "Bypass permissions". Nothing is saved to `cloud-chat-settings:*`, and the next turn's `user_message` goes out with no `approvalMode`, so commands run with no approval prompt.

Seen in the A-Z runs on 11-12 (A11) and 11-13 (P4.12, still present on b58f4c408b).

Cause: the unified settings bar's approval rows (`TurnSettingsBar.tsx`, `PermissionRow` in the `showApprovalMode` menu) called `onChange({ ...settings, approvalMode })` without the `"approvalMode"` pick marker. The plain rows in the same menu pass it. `CloudSessionChatSurface`'s `onChooseSettings` keeps the current approval mode unless `picked === "approvalMode"`, because the bar sends the shown settings back with every change. So every pick from the unified bar was ignored. This came in with #6588 (unified bar) and #6901 (pick marker), both 10-21.

Local Chat is not affected: `useConversation.chooseSettings`, `useReviewerConversation` and the New Task page's `chooseTurnSettings` ignore the marker and save the full settings. Only Cloud reads it.

## Change

- `TurnSettingsBar.tsx`: one `pickApprovalMode(mode)` helper sends `onChange({ ...settings, approvalMode: mode }, "approvalMode")`. Both the unified `PermissionRow` and the plain `OptionMenuItem` rows use it, so the two kinds of row can't drift apart again.
- No visual change.

## Tests

- `TurnSettingsBar.test.tsx`: new test. Picking a mode in the unified bar's approval menu, by mouse and by keyboard, reports `(settings, "approvalMode")`.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx`: new test. It renders a trusted Cloud Claude chat and the real settings bar drawn from the chat's props, the way `ChatWorkspace` draws it. Picking "Accept edits" changes the shown mode, saves it, and the next `sendSessionMessage` carries `approvalMode: "accept-edits"`.
- With the fix reverted, both new tests fail (the shown mode stays `bypass-permissions`; `onChange` is called without the marker).
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/chat src/renderer/components/NewChatPage.test.tsx src/renderer/components/TaskComposer.test.tsx`: 2197 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures (`ContextMeter` "reports exact accessible values", `ChatWorkspace` "quota passes 75%") also fail on clean `origin/main` 541f3cb54e and are unrelated.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.

## Risk and rollout

Desktop only. No API or Control Plane change. Cloud Chat turns now carry the approval mode the user picks, which the worker already honors (A12 in the 11-12 run exercised approval prompts through turns that carried `approvalMode`).

title: fix(desktop): list Cloud's own models in a Cloud New Task's picker
body:
## Why

On a machine whose local Claude Code defaults to Fable, the New Task page for a Cloud project leaves Fable 5.2 out of the model picker (search "fable": Showing 0 of 15). The Control Plane catalog (`GET /providers/claude-code/models`) and the in-session Cloud Chat picker both list it. Seen in the 11-13 A-Z run (P4.5).

Cause: `NewChatPage` drew a Cloud task's bar from this computer's saved Claude Code bar (`ao.chat.settingsTemplate.v1`, key `local:claude-code`). That bar's "Default (recommended)" row is described as Fable 5.2.
- `draftProviderOptions` ran `partitionConfigOptions`, whose `resolveImplicitChoice` folds the Fable 5.2 row into the Default row.

This came in with #6733 and #5849. The same double fold also hid Fable from a local New Task on such a machine.

- `NewChatPage.tsx`: a Cloud project no longer reads the local settings template. Its bar lists Cloud's catalog (`task.chatModels`), as the Cloud session's own bar does. This follows #7815 ("every Cloud model picker uses Cloud's own model list"), and it matches how the page already skips this computer's `/` skills for a Cloud task.

- `NewChatPage.test.tsx`, new "New Chat model menu" tests:

title: fix(cloud): ask the worker for a live Cursor session's chat models
body:
Code changes: +1 -1\
Tests: +22 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Enables `modelsQuery` (`client.listChatModels`) for live Cursor sessions in `CloudSessionChatSurface`.

## Why

Fixes https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane/issues/68.

In `CloudSessionChatSurface`, `modelsQuery` was gated on:
```ts
enabled: Boolean(... && (session.provider === "codex" || session.provider === "claude-code"))
```
Because `"cursor"` was omitted, opening or running a live Cursor session never queried the worker for `chat.models` (`listChatModels`). The UI fell back exclusively to `catalogQuery` (`client.listUserAgentModels`), which only returned the release catalog containing `Auto` (from `internal/modelcatalog/release/cursor.json`). Furthermore, because `modelsQuery` never succeeded, `invalidateCloudModelCatalogs` was never triggered to invalidate New Task and settings pickers upon discovery.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Live Cursor sessions never called `chat.models` on the worker; model picker remained stuck on `Auto` only, and the account catalog was never refreshed. | Live Cursor sessions query `client.listChatModels` on the worker; the account's models (e.g. `grok-4.7-medium`, `claude-4.5-sonnet`) are loaded into the picker, and `invalidateCloudModelCatalogs` is invoked to update New Task and other Cloud model pickers. |

## How

- Added `|| session.provider === "cursor"` to `modelsQuery.enabled` in `CloudSessionChatSurface.tsx`.
- Matches the control plane worker's `chatModelListers` mapping in `ao-control-plane` (`internal/workertransport/chat_models.go`), which supports `claude-code`, `codex`, and `cursor`.

## Testing

- Ran vitest test in `frontend`:
  `npm --prefix frontend test -- CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx -t "asks the worker for a Cursor session"` (PASS: 1 passed)
- Ran TypeScript typecheck:
  `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` (`tsgo --noEmit`, PASS: 0 errors)

## Checklist

title: fix(cloud): approving a cloud Chat plan turns Plan mode off
body:
## Why

Bug 4 from the A-Z runs (2026-11-12 A20, 2026-11-13 P4.13): cloud Chat Plan mode has no approval step, and Plan mode stays on for later turns.

- The matching control plane change makes Claude's ExitPlanMode reach the cloud Chat as an approval card instead of being aborted.
- The cloud composer keeps Plan mode in its own settings (`executionMode`) and sends every turn as `read-only` while it is on. In local Chat, approving the plan moves the agent out of plan mode into the mode picked, and the composer follows. Cloud Chat had no such path, so after an approved plan the next turn would go straight back into plan mode.

## Change

- When the user approves a plan approval (ACP tool kind `switch_mode`) with one of Claude's modes, and the control plane accepts the decision, the composer turns Plan mode off and selects the approval mode the plan was approved with. For example, "Yes, and auto-accept edits" selects Accept edits, as local Chat does.
- "No, keep planning", or a decision the control plane refuses (the turn already ended), leaves Plan mode on.
- The card itself is the existing approval card, the same one local Chat shows for ExitPlanMode.
- No contract or cloud-client change: the approval event already carries `toolKind`.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/chat/CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.test.tsx src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.test.tsx`: 297 passed in 3 files (CloudSessionChatSurface 113, ChatTimelineItems 57, TurnSettingsBar 127). In the first run, the untouched ChatTimelineItems test "smooths received bursts up to 4,000 characters" hit its 20 s timeout while the machine was under heavy load; it passed on the rerun.
- New tests in `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx`:
  - "leaves Plan mode for the mode the user approved the plan with, as local Chat does" fails without the fix (Plan mode stays on and the next turn goes out read-only).
  - "keeps planning when the user rejects the plan, or the approval is refused".

## Risk and rollout

- Deploy the control plane PR first. This change only acts on plan approvals, which an older control plane never sends, so it is inert until then.
- An older desktop with the new control plane still shows and answers the card; it just keeps Plan mode on afterwards.
- In a shared session, only the owner's settings change (a guest's composer follows the owner's settings, as for every other setting).

title: fix(desktop): bring the reader to the end on a Cloud Chat send
body:
## Why

In a Cloud Chat, sending while scrolled up leaves the view where it was. The new prompt and the reply stream off-screen, and only "Jump to latest" brings them back.

Seen in the 11-13 A-Z run (P4.11): `scrollTop` stayed at 104 of 3003 after the send and after the reply. Earlier in the run, stop, steer, queue and attachment turns all streamed off-screen too.

Cause: `ChatWorkspace`'s timeline glides to the end on a send only when a new local echo appears ("The reader just sent: bring them to their prompt"). Local chats make a local echo for every send. A Cloud chat shows a send only once the Control Plane has it, and `CloudSessionChatSurface` passes only the opening brief's echo as `localEchos`. So a Cloud send never triggered the glide. It has been like this since Cloud Chat got the shared workspace (80556c340d2, #7543, 11-02).

## Change

`ChatWorkspace.tsx`:
- Counts the reader's sends from the chat's composer that the main transcript took: a message, one that queues behind a running turn, and a steer the running turn accepted.
  - A message counts only once the surface's `onSend` resolves. A refused send throws past the count, so the reader keeps their place.
  - A send that went somewhere else does not count. A surface says so by resolving `onSend` to the new `SENT_OUTSIDE_TRANSCRIPT`. The local surface (`SessionChatSurface.tsx`) returns it for `/btw`, which opens a side chat so the reader can ask aside without losing their place.
  - A steer counts once the turn accepts it, not when its echo is placed. A refused steer drops its echo and does not move the reader.
- Hands that count to the timeline. The timeline glides to the end when the count goes up or a new local echo appears.
- Local chats behave as before: their echo already glides at once. The local steer also glides now, once accepted.
- A queued-message edit is not counted, since it changes the dock, not the transcript.
- No visual change.

## Tests

- `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`, "in a chat that shows no local echo of a send". Each test reads back through the history (wheel up, "Jump to latest" shows), then sends from the composer with no `localEchos`.
  - The view ends at the bottom and "Jump to latest" goes away for: a message, a message that queues behind the running turn, and an accepted steer (Ctrl+Enter).
  - The view stays where the reader was (scrollTop 1000, "Jump to latest" stays) for: a question the surface sent to a side chat (`SENT_OUTSIDE_TRANSCRIPT`), a message the chat refused (`COMPOSER_LOCKED`), and a steer the turn refused (`not-accepted`). These 3 fail on the previous head bef109ef8f, which counted before the send was handled.
- `SessionChatSurface.test.tsx`: `/btw` resolves to `SENT_OUTSIDE_TRANSCRIPT` for every submission, and a literal `/side` sent to the agent does not.
- `npx vitest run` on `ChatWorkspace`, `SessionChatSurface`, `CloudSessionChatSurface` and `ChatComposer` tests: 707 passed (4 files).
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- Rebased on main c8b22b94fc (includes #8236).

## Risk and rollout

Desktop only. No API or Control Plane change. The change is in the shared transcript, so local chats also glide on a composer send the main transcript took. They already did through their echo, except for steer, which now glides once accepted. A `/btw` question keeps the reader's place, as it did before this PR.

title: fix(desktop): say who the workspace row in Share means, never an email
body:
## Why

In the Share dialog and in Project settings > Sharing, "People with access" listed the workspace as "People in <workspace name> · Workspace members · Full access", and General access said "Only people in <workspace name> and people added above can open this session."

Some team workspaces are named after a person's email: a workspace set up for one person takes its name from the identity provider's organization, and those were created with the email as the name. The dialog then read "People in asha@example.com", as if an address were a group, and nothing said what the row grants. Seen in the 2026-11-12 A-Z run on staging (P4.21, P4.31) and reported by a user on prod.

The app also had its own path to an email-named workspace: when `/me` lists no organization it creates one named from the account, and the control plane gives someone without a profile name their email as `displayName`, so the new team workspace was named after the email.

## Change

- **Workspace row:** titled "Everyone in your workspace". The subtitle is the workspace's name, only when it is a name (never an email, or a name containing one), plus the member count: "Acme · 4 members". The count comes from `GET /orgs/{orgId}/members`, an existing control plane route any member can read (new `listOrgMembers` client method, `useWorkspaceMemberCount` hook). No new route.
- **Full access** has a tooltip: "Everyone in your workspace can open and work in every session in this project. Workspace admins manage who is a member."
- **Nobody but you:** a team workspace with one member grants nothing, so it gets no row, as a personal workspace already did. On the project's sharing, where there is no session owner, you are listed instead ("Asha Rao (you) · Full access"), so the list is never empty.
- **General access** no longer names the workspace: "Only members of your workspace and people added above can open this session/project.", or "Only you and people added above ..." when nobody else is in it. While the workspace or its count is unknown it never says "only you".
- The list waits for the member count with its skeleton, so a solo workspace's row never flashes in.
- All nine locales updated (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-CN) with the plural forms each needs; the unused `share.workspacePeople`, `share.workspacePeopleUnnamed` and `share.workspaceMembers` keys are removed.
- **Auto-created workspace name** (second commit): "<first name>'s workspace", falling back to the email's local part, never the email.

Same logic on both surfaces: the dialog and Project settings > Sharing share `SharePanel`.

## Tests

- New `ShareSessionDialog.workspace.test.tsx` (14): row title, subtitle (name and count, count only for an email-named workspace, nothing when neither is known), the tooltip, hiding the row for a solo workspace, the "you" row on the project's sharing, a personal workspace makes no members request, and the General access copy for each case. On `origin/main` 13 of the 14 fail (the row reads "People in asha.k77@example.com").
- New `useCloudOrg.test.ts` (6): fails on `origin/main` (the email fallback case returns the email).
- Updated `ShareSessionDialog.test.tsx`, `ShareSessionDialog.people.test.tsx`, `CloudProjectSharingSettings.test.tsx` for the new copy; `client.test.ts` covers the members route.
- `npm run typecheck`: pass. `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/i18n src/renderer/lib/cloud-cp src/renderer/components/Share src/renderer/components/share src/renderer/components/CloudProjectSharingSettings src/renderer/components/SessionPeople src/renderer/components/teams src/renderer/components/settings/TeamsSection src/renderer/hooks`: 128 files, 1337 tests, all pass (includes the i18n catalog, plural and interpolation checks).
- Full renderer suite (`npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts`): 749 of 763 files pass. The 14 failing files are outside this change (browser profile import, cookie repair, remote proxy, chat timing tests); run alone on this branch and on `origin/main`, the same 54 tests fail in both (49 of them in browser-profile-import), and the rest were timeouts under the full run's load.
- Checked live in the dev app against staging, on a team workspace named after an email with 2 members: the Sharing page shows "Everyone in your workspace · 2 members · Full access" and "Only members of your workspace and people added above can open this project."

## Risk and rollout

- Desktop only. Uses an existing control plane route; no contract change. If the members list can't be read (older control plane, error), the row shows without a count and never hides, and General access keeps the workspace sentence.
- The email names themselves live in the identity provider's organization names, which the control plane copies on every sign-in; renaming those organizations is an ops step outside this PR.

title: fix(archive): label the archive's entry points Archived sessions
body:
Code changes: +10 -9\
Tests: +13 -12\
Others: +35 -43

## What

Every way into the archive modal now says **Archived sessions** instead of **Archive**:

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar project ⋮ and right-click menu (one shared list) | Archive 369 | Archived sessions 369 |
| Board button under the lanes | Archive 369 | Archived sessions 369 |
| Cmd+K, current project | Open archive | Archived sessions |
| Screen-reader label (board button, project menu, Scratchpad archived row) | Archive, 369 sessions | Archived sessions, 369 |

The count and hide-when-empty behaviour are unchanged. The Scratchpad's ⋮/right-click entry, its hover action and its archived row already said "Archived sessions"; only the screen-reader label on that row changes.

## Why

Team decision (Nov 13): on a project row, "Archive 369" reads as the verb, as in archiving the whole project. A noun names the place. The same mix-up showed up in the translations: es ("Archivar"), fr ("Archiver") and ru ("Архивировать") had translated the old label and its aria-label as the verb.

## Before / After

Text-only change. The labels are in the table above; the layout is the same.

## How

- Cmd+K follows "verbs for actions, nouns for places". The modal is a place, so the command is the noun "Archived sessions". It sits next to "Project settings", which is also a noun. The subtitle still gives the count ("2 archived sessions").
- `shell.archive` is no longer used, so it is removed from all 9 locales. The board and the project menu reuse the existing, already-translated `shell.archivedSessions`.
- `command.openArchive` is renamed to `command.archivedSessions`, using each locale's existing "Archived sessions" string.
- `shell.archiveSessionsAria_*` is renamed to `shell.archivedSessionsAria_*` and translated in every locale. Each locale keeps its existing plural forms.
- DESIGN.md: the archive rule now uses the new labels, says the archive is never called a bare "Archive", and gets a decision-log row. The Cloud guide now points at the project's **Archived sessions**.

**Left as is, on purpose:**
- "Archive session" (⇧⌘A), the inspector's Archive row, and "Archive reviewer" are verbs on one session.
- `column.archive` ("Archive") is a status/column name in `product-ui`, not this entry point.

title: fix(chat): keep the provider adapter's stderr in the chat host's directory
body:
## Why

A Claude chat turn can go silent: the adapter never writes anything to the host, and after 15 minutes the stall watchdog fails the turn with `provider stopped responding: no ACP output for 15m0s`. The host discarded the adapter's stderr (`child.Stderr = io.Discard`), so there was nothing to inspect afterwards. In the case I traced, Claude itself finished the turn in about 18 seconds, so the lost step is between the adapter and the host.

## What

- The host now writes the adapter's stderr to `chat-hosts/<session>/adapter.log`, next to the host descriptor.
- Owner-only (0600), rotates once at 1 MiB (`adapter.log.1`), so a long-lived host keeps at most 2 MiB.
- A restarted host appends to the earlier run's log.
- `Write` never returns an error. An error from the stderr writer would surface from the provider's process wait and look like a provider failure.

Hosts that are already running keep discarding stderr until they restart.

## Verification

- `go vet` on the package (type-checks the new tests).
- New tests cover rotation, append across hosts, and the never-fail behavior. I did not run them locally; CI will.

## Follow-up

The queue is held after a watchdog-failed turn (queued messages waited 37 minutes), tracked in a separate PR.

title: feat(desktop): Browser and side chat tabs use the session strip's tab frame
body:
## What

The Browser panel's page tabs and the side chat tabs now use the same tab frame as the session top bar's tabs (`TerminalTabFrame`). There is one component for all three strips, so they can't drift apart again.

| Height / type | 28px, 12px/550 | the frame's: `--size-topbar-control`, same size/weight as session tabs |
| Active | flat `--interactive-active` fill | secondary pill with the control inset; light theme fill from `--color-bg-primary`, no hover darkening |
| Hover / focus | own fill, accent outline | ghost hover pill, ring on the pill; no press scale |
| Close | always-visible 26px button with tooltip (hidden on inactive tabs past 8) | always-visible ghost X at the tab's right end, in the frame's end slot (where the session tab's ⋮ sits); still hidden on inactive tabs past 8; middle-click also closes |
| Dividers | none | always visible and centered, none beside the active pill or after the last tab |
| New (+) | 28px pressable pinned to the strip's far end | the session strip's quiet `icon-sm` button, 4px after the last tab |
| Overflow | edge fade | unchanged: `.edge-fade` + `useTabScrollEdges`, same as the session strip |

## Screenshots

title: fix(chat): release queued messages after the host fails a stalled prompt
body:
## Why

When the chat host's watchdog fails a prompt after 15 minutes of silence, the controller treated it like a provider outage and held the queue (`controller.go`, #4861). In the case I traced, the user's next two messages sat `queued` for 37 minutes after the failure and only ran when they typed again.

A watchdog stall is not an outage: the provider never answered, so it says nothing about whether the next prompt would fail.

## What

- **Relay:** the stall watchdog now works in two steps. It sends the adapter `session/cancel` and keeps the prompt active; when the adapter answers, the answer becomes the stall failure, so the next queued prompt starts on a quiet adapter and the cancelled turn's late output stays on the stalled prompt. If the adapter has not answered after 30 s it is wedged: the relay settles the prompt without it, **without** the stall marker, so the controller holds its queue as it did before this PR (the wedged adapter may still emit from the old turn; its late answer is dropped, as before). The stall error carries `data["ao.promptStalled"] = true` (the relay wraps it under `providerData` when it adds its event id).
- **ACP driver:** `normalizeACPError` maps that marker to `ports.ErrChatPromptStalled`. The error text is unchanged, so the failure card reads the same.
- **Controller:** a settled turn releases the queue if it completed *or* failed with `ErrChatPromptStalled`. Every other failure or recovery still holds the queue.
- `promptErrorFailure` no longer replaces a stall error, so the marker survives.

Hosts started before this build don't send the marker, so they keep the old behavior until they restart.

## Verification

- `go vet` on the four touched packages (type-checks the new tests).
- New tests: the relay cancels first and settles on the adapter's answer (late output stays on the stalled prompt), still settles after the grace for a wedged adapter, the relay puts the marker on the wire, the driver maps it (wrapped and top-level, and ignores unrelated -32603 data or other codes), and the controller releases the queue after a stall but still holds it after a provider error. I did not run them locally; CI will.

Companion to #8295 (keeps the adapter's stderr so the cause of the silence can be found).

body:
Code changes: +123 -7\

## What

Add native ACP Chat support for the installed Grok Build harness, including model/reasoning effort controls, standing instructions, permission handling, and native session continuation.

## Why

`ao spawn --agent grok --mode chat` currently fails with `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` because Grok has no registered Chat driver. This is a standalone request with no existing issue. The separate Grok TUI trust work in #8278 is unchanged.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Grok Chat spawn returns `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` | A standalone Grok Chat session starts using the installed `grok agent stdio` and cached login |
| Grok Chat has no model or effort controls | Its live ACP catalog supplies `model` and `reasoning_effort`; tested effort selection from high to low |
| An explicit Grok Chat `--effort high` is rejected before launch | Chat preserves the requested effort for ACP validation; Grok TUI behavior stays unchanged |
| Grok sessions cannot be reopened in Chat | Native reopen retains the conversation, settings, and existing transcript |
| The initial Chat implementation used `--always-approve` for Auto | Auto retains Grok command review through `_meta.autoMode`; bypass alone disables approvals |
| Standing instructions appeared in the initial user-message preamble | `_meta.rules` supplies native system instructions |
| Project-wide or role effort could make Grok Chat fail at startup | Only explicit spawn effort is forwarded; other launches keep the active model's native default |
| Grok task naming requested unsupported `accept-edits` | Grok uses compatible Default permissions, then safely refuses unsupported tool-disabled launches; naming keeps the prompt-derived fallback |

- Use modern `session/set_config_option` when the provider advertises a model option alongside legacy models, matching the existing direct config-option controller.
- Pass AO standing instructions as Grok ACP `_meta.rules`, placing them in the system prompt rather than a user-message preamble. Forward provider session metadata through the native ACP binding on new/load/resume.
- Default permissions use generic ACP tool approvals. Auto sends `_meta.autoMode: true` to preserve Grok's native command review; only explicit bypass launches `grok agent --always-approve stdio`. Accept-edits and live permission changes are rejected. Restart existing Grok Chat providers after updating to apply the new launch/session settings.
- Advertise history and reuse native session-id persistence and load/resume. Do not claim plan support.
- Register Grok and update the harness catalog and spawn guidance.
- Forward only explicit Grok Chat effort (`EffortOverride`), preserving strict ACP validation for user-selected values without inheriting tuning intended for another harness/model.
- Use compatible Default permissions for Grok background requests. The binding rejects `DisableTools` launches before starting Grok because no native mechanism to remove every tool has been verified. Automatic naming intentionally keeps the prompt-derived fallback; tool-free background suggestions remain unsupported. A temporary workspace or instructions alone are not treated as enforcement.

title: fix(usage): stop showing a login no account holds as open in Windows
body:
## Summary

Usage → Windows showed a weekly allowance for a login that the Limits view no longer listed, with "not read since …" under it.

**Cause:** `LimitHistoryReader` groups 14 days of limit readings by email and showed every login in them, marking a window `open` whenever its reset was still ahead. After "This computer's" Claude login switched to another login, the old login's weekly window (reset two days out) stayed `open`, so "This week's allowance" kept listing it. A removed saved account leaves its readings behind the same way.

**Fix:** the Windows view shows only logins that an existing account holds now. A login no account holds is left out entirely. Its readings stay stored (14-day retention), so when an account holds it again the view shows it with the windows recorded before.

The held login comes from the accounts service's last successful identity check (`ConfirmedLogins`): a failed check keeps the previous identity, and a sign-out or a folder signed in as another login holds nothing. For accounts not checked yet (right after a restart), it falls back to the account's newest limit reading. Device accounts always exist; saved accounts come from `ListAgentAccounts`.

No API or frontend change; the daemon passes the accounts service to the history reader.

## Evidence (real readings)

Ran `History` against the real `agent_limit_readings` and `agent_accounts` rows of a Mac where the CLI login switched away on Nov 12 and back on Nov 14 (emails replaced):

| When (IST) | Login | Weekly windows shown |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 13 12:00, on main | old@ (switched away) | seven_day 78% open, model:Fable 39% open (the stale cards) |
| Nov 13 12:00, this PR | old@ (switched away) | none |
| Nov 14 14:17, this PR | old@ (signed in again) | seven_day 94% open, model:Fable 39% open, including the readings from before the switch |
| both times, this PR | new@, codex@ (current) | unchanged |

## Tests

- `TestLimitHistoryShowsOnlyLoginsAnAccountHolds`: a login switched away and a removed saved account are left out; the current login and a still-saved account show. Fails on main, passes here.
- `TestLimitHistoryHidesASignedOutLoginUntilItIsBack`: logins signed out (identity changed with no new limit reading, or signed out) are left out; once the identity is that login again, it shows with last week's window and this week's.
- `TestConfirmedLoginsFollowTheIdentityWithoutALimitReading`: a switch whose limits call fails, two failed checks in a row (identity kept), sign-out, and a folder on another login.
- `TestAnOlderReadDoesNotReplaceANewerOne`: two overlapping reads of one account; the one that started first but finished last no longer replaces the newer identity.
- `TestAFailedNewerReadDoesNotHideANewerIdentity`: a newer read whose identity check fails does not hide an older read that found the new login. Stored readings are ordered by their last successful identity check, not by attempt.
- Mutation checks: dropping the held-login filter, dropping the existing-account check, ignoring confirmed logins, or not carrying the identity across a failed check each fails a test.
- `go test ./internal/service/usage/ ./internal/service/agentaccounts/ ./internal/daemon/` and `go vet` on those pass.

## Risks

- A login that is still signed in but read by no account (for example, signed out of Orchestrator and still used elsewhere) is not shown. That matches the Limits view.
- Not checked in the desktop app; the view renders whatever logins the API returns.

Related: #7674 (shows the same login once in the Limits view; no overlapping files).

  * Usage limit history now includes saved accounts alongside device-based and removed-account entries. Logins are grouped by provider and normalized email when available, with account ID as a fallback.
  * Entries are marked open only when a login is confirmed or inferred as held and the reset time is in the future. Other future-reset entries retain their existing final or partial status.
  * Account results now reflect the latest reading when checks finish out of order, and failed checks no longer replace or hide a previously confirmed login identity.

title: fix(chat): pause provider catalogs while remote host is offline
body:
Code changes: +1 -1

## What

Pause provider catalog queries while a remote chat's host is unreachable, keeping the saved conversation readable without a red disconnected-host error.

## Why

A cached conversation can retain controller state `ready` after a connection disruption. The catalog gate trusted that saved state, so settings polling continued and `clientForHost` raised `Host … is not connected` beneath the offline composer.

title: feat(share): drop the workspace row, share the project from the orchestrator and board cards; remove the Cloud GitHub PAT UI
body:
Code changes: +104 -292\
Tests: +245 -82\
Others: +18 -171 (i18n catalogs, 9 locales)

## What

Four changes to the desktop renderer's sharing and Cloud settings:

1. **No "Workspace members" row.** The share dialog's "People with access" list no longer shows "People in <workspace> · Workspace members · Full access". This also applies to Project settings › Sharing, which uses the same panel. General access now says "Only people added above can open this session/project." instead of "Only people in <workspace> and people added above…".
2. **Sharing from the orchestrator shares the project.** Share in an orchestrator session's header opens the dialog for the whole project only. The title uses the project name ("Share project “acme/web”"), and there is no "Session in X · Share the whole project instead" switch and no way back to a session. Worker sessions keep both options.
3. **Share from board cards.** Each kanban card for a cloud session this person can share gets a Share icon button next to Archive, shown on hover or focus. When a card already shows people circles (an already shared session), clicking them opens the same dialog. Neither the button nor the circles opens the session.
4. **No Cloud GitHub personal access token UI.** Settings › Harness › Cloud no longer shows the "GitHub private repositories · Not connected" row or the "GitHub token" field (`github_pat_…` input, Save token). The desktop's Cloud client no longer calls `PUT`/`DELETE /me/github-pat` or `POST /me/github-pat/validate-saved-repository`. **The control-plane endpoints are intentionally kept for now**; this is a frontend-only removal.

## Why

AO has no workspaces for now, so the workspace row and sentence described access that doesn't exist. The orchestrator is the project's own session and should never be shared as a single session. Sharing also needed an entry point on the board, not only inside a session. Cloud now reaches private repositories through the GitHub App, so a personal access token for Cloud workers is no longer needed. The PAT removal is in this PR, not a separate one, because the maintainer asked for it here: it's another small cleanup of the same renderer settings and sharing surfaces, in its own commit (`6ef529f`) so it can be reviewed separately.

## Before / After

I couldn't capture the live desktop app from the cloud sandbox: there's no Cloud sign-in or Go toolchain there. I also couldn't attach images here: the sandbox's GitHub access is a bot token, and GitHub only accepts image uploads from a signed-in person, so the table lists file names and a person will drag the images into a PR comment. The captures come from a test page that renders the real components (`ShareSessionDialog`, `SessionPeopleControl`, `BoardSessionCardAdapter`, `CloudHarnessContent`) with the app's styles, against made-up data (Alex Example and others at example.com), with the same page, data and 1280×800 size on both sides. Before for states 1–3 is `main`'s code. Before for state 4 is this PR's first commit, whose Cloud harness tab is unchanged from `main`. They are attached to the AO session as artifacts, with a paste-ready comment (`pr-8307-before-after-comment.md`) that also lists how the test page differs from the real app.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `before-share-dialog-session.png`: list has "People in Northwind · Workspace members · Full access"; sentence "Only people in Northwind and people added above can open this session." | `after-share-dialog-session.png`: owner, then the people and teams added; sentence "Only people added above can open this session." |
| `before-share-from-orchestrator.png`: Share on the orchestrator opens "Share “Orchestrator”" with "Session in acme/web · Share the whole project instead" | `after-share-from-orchestrator.png`: opens "Share project “acme/web”", "Includes every session, also ones started later.", with no session switch |
| `before-board-card.png`: a cloud card shows only Archive on hover/focus, and its people circles are not clickable | `after-board-card-share.png`: Share icon button (tooltip "Share") before Archive; `after-board-bubbles-open-share.png`: clicking the circles opens that session's share dialog |
| `before-cloud-harness-settings.png`: Cloud agents, then "GitHub private repositories · Not connected" and a "GitHub token" field with Save token | `after-cloud-harness-settings.png`: only the Cloud agents |

## How

- **Workspace row:** removed the row from `AccessList`. Also removed the plumbing that only fed it and the sentence: `useCloudOrg` in the share controller, `workspaceName`/`personal`, and `isPersonalWorkspace`. `restrictedSentence` now takes only `scope` and `people`. `membersHaveAccess` (StagedSummary) and `workspaceHasAccess` (PeopleField) stay: they describe how the control plane weighs workspace members in the confirm summary, not the removed row. Removed the now-unused keys and rewrote the restricted sentences in all 9 locales.
- **Empty list:** with no workspace row, a project nobody has been added to would show an empty "People with access" box. The panel now hides the list (and the section in Project settings) when there is no owner row and no entries.
- **Orchestrator:** `SessionPeopleControl` takes `shareProject`. `SessionView` sets it for orchestrator sessions (not standalone agents), and the dialog then gets no `sessionId`/`sessionName`, which is its existing project-only mode. One fix was needed: `SessionView` stays mounted across session switches, and the dialog's `scope` was `useState` seeded once. A dialog first used for a worker could then reopen on the orchestrator still in session scope. `scope` is now derived (`projectOnly ? "project" : chosenScope`). The new test fails without that fix.
- **Board:** `SessionsBoard` decides `canShare` per card the same way the session header does: a cloud session, not terminated, in the active org, with the org's offering including `share`, and not a standalone agent shared with this person. It holds one `ShareSessionDialog` for the card being shared and passes `onShare` to `BoardSessionCardAdapter`. The card's Share button is a `quiet` `icon-sm` `Button` with a tooltip and an accessible name (`Share “<title>”`). It uses the same hover/focus reveal as Archive, so it is keyboard reachable, and its click stops propagation. A card can now show circles, Share and Archive together; Share stays hidden until hover/focus so the title doesn't move.
- **Cloud PAT:**
  - Deleted `onboarding/GitHubTokenField.tsx` and the `CloudGitHubPatRow` in `CloudHarnessContent`.
  - Removed `putGitHubPAT`, `deleteGitHubPAT` and `validateSavedRepositoryAccess` from the Cloud client, with their request/response types.
  - Removed the PAT strings (`settings.cloudAgents.github.*`, and the already-unused `settings.githubPat.*`) from every locale, along with the stale `github_pat_…`/`ghp_...`/`GitHub PAT` allow-list literals in the i18n coverage test.
  - `CreateProjectFlow` had no token inputs left, only a stale comment, which is gone.
  - **Intentionally kept:**
    - the control-plane endpoints and the generated `api/schema.ts` / `packages/cloud-client` schema;
    - the local daemon's GitHub connection (`lib/github-daemon.ts`, `main/provider-auth-flow.ts`) and the Local harness tab's GitHub sign-in;
    - generic `github_pat_` redaction (`lib/telemetry.ts`, `lib/report-problem.ts`, `shared/observability.ts`, `main/cloud-share.ts`);
    - `hasValidAgentConnection`'s filter, which still ignores any GitHub connection the control plane returns.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- Frontend lint: the repo has no JS linter; the root `npm run lint` is the Go backend only and nothing in `backend/` changed. CI's frontend lane is typecheck + vitest.
- Full `npx vitest run`: 13762 passed. The one failure, `src/main/remote-proxy.test.ts` (HTTP/2, 10s timeout), also fails on `main` in this sandbox and passed in this PR's CI.
- Grep for `github-pat`, `githubPAT`, `GitHubPAT`, `GitHubToken`, `personal_access_token` and `github_pat` finds only:
  - the generated schemas;
  - the local daemon PAT;
  - generic redaction and its tests;
  - the local GitHub sign-in error text.
- New tests:
  - Share dialog: it names no workspace and shows the new sentence; an empty project list renders nothing; it switches to project-only when reopened without a session.
  - Session header: the orchestrator shares the project from both the button and the circles; a worker still shares the session.
  - Board cards: Share and the circles open the dialog without opening the session; Share is hidden where sharing isn't possible.
  - Board: the dialog gets the right session and project; Share is not offered for local sessions, other orgs, orgs without sharing, or terminated sessions.
  - Cloud harness tab: no GitHub token row, field or Save token. This test fails against the previous code.
- Not run locally: the macOS-only and Electron boundary jobs (no native runner/Electron binary here).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (as session artifacts; see above)
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(mobile): don't call the phone offline while its requests are answered
body:
Code changes: +150 -9\ Tests: +176 -1\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The mobile app no longer says "You're offline" or "Phone offline" while its requests to the machine or to Cloud are being answered. A real disconnect still shows "You're offline". ## Why Fixes #8282. On a Wi-Fi network Android can't validate, there is no default network, so expo-network reports the phone as disconnected while the app's requests still succeed. `classifyLink` returned `"phone-offline"` from that report alone (since #7336). ## Before / After Pixel 10a, Release builds, on an iPhone hotspot Android never validates (`dumpsys wifi`: `isConnected=true isValidated=false`). Before is `main` at `bd4d0d4540`. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | Airplane mode: "You're offline" at once |
On this network: "Reconnecting to MacBook…" at about 20 s, then "You're offline" at about 43 s | ## How - `lib/answeredRequests.ts` records when the newest answered request was **sent**. Any HTTP status counts. It is fed by `api.ts` (machine), `cloud/client.ts`, `accountHosts.ts` (Cloud machine sync) and the endpoint probe in `connectRuntime.ts`. - `trustedPhoneNetwork` in `lib/linkHealth.ts` turns the OS's "no network"/"no internet" into "not known" when a request sent after the OS's latest change was answered within the last `ANSWER_TRUSTED_FOR_MS` (45 s). The OS's "yes" always stands. - **Real offline:** when the OS's report changes, earlier answers stop counting, so a normal phone shows "You're offline" at once. Counting from send time means a request already in flight at the drop can't hide it. - **Why 45 s:** on the Pixel, airplane mode didn't change the report (it already said disconnected), so an answer also has to expire. 45 s is longer than Cloud's 30 s machine sync, so a machine that stops answering while Cloud still does reads as unreachable, not "Phone offline". The store schedules a re-check for when the answer expires. - **Reconnect probe:** the 15-second reconnect for a machine with no working connection is skipped only when the OS says there is no network at all (type `NONE`/`UNKNOWN`) and nothing has answered since it said so. On a network the OS wrongly calls offline, its report never changes, so after the answers expire this probe is the only way to find the machine again (`worthProbingForRecovery`). - The store publishes the trusted view as `phoneNetwork`/`phoneOffline`, and uses it for `linkHealth` and the reconnect, re-race and upgrade-race checks. On such a network, those checks no longer stay off forever. Racing after a network change still uses the raw OS report. **Trade-off:** on a network the OS already calls offline, a real drop takes up to about 45 s to read as "You're offline" (it shows "Reconnecting…"/"Can't reach…" first). ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 4177 passed. `npm run typecheck`: clean. - New tests: `answeredRequests.test.ts`, `trustedPhoneNetwork` cases in `linkHealth.test.ts`, `worthProbingForRecovery` cases, and four store tests in `store.refresh.test.tsx`: - the Pixel case, then a real drop; - airplane mode with an unchanged OS report; - a machine going down while Cloud answers; - the machine sleeping until the config is cleared and the answers expire, then waking: the app reconnects. The store tests fail without the fix (the airplane one fails without the 45 s limit). - On the Pixel 10a: side-by-side Release build (separate package id, OTA updates off). Results are in the table. - **Not yet checked on the device:** the banner clearing after airplane mode is turned off. The Pixel didn't rejoin the hotspot because it had stopped broadcasting. The store test "blames the phone's network, then races and polls as soon as it returns" covers that path. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved mobile connection status when the device’s network report is outdated. Recent successful requests can prevent the app from incorrectly showing the phone as offline. * Connection status updates as requests succeed or stop, and temporary adjustments expire automatically. * Improved offline detection when the phone can reach the network but the connected machine cannot.

title: feat(cloud): contract and shared handoff note for switching a Cloud session's agent
body:
Code changes: +395 -263\
Tests: +236 -192\
Others: +121 -4 (contract, generated client schema)

## What

Two pieces AO Cloud needs before a running Cloud session can switch its coding agent:

1. **Shared handoff note.** The desktop's provider-switch handoff note builder moves unchanged into the public `backend/pkg/handoffnote`. The private control plane can then hand an agent the same record of the conversation as the desktop does. `domain.BuildHandoffNote` becomes a thin adapter over it.
2. **Cloud contract for agent switching** (all additive):
   - `StartSessionInterfaceTransitionInput.targetHarness`: an interface transition that also moves the session to another agent. `targetMode` may then be the current mode, and `model` and `reasoningEffort` name the new agent's.
   - `SessionInterfaceTransition` gains `sourceHarness`, `targetHarness`, `sourceModel`, `targetModel` and `targetReasoningEffort`.
   - `CurrentAccount.agentSwitchHarnesses` lists the agents a session can switch to. A control plane without agent switching leaves it out and refuses `targetHarness`.
   - `chat.agent_switched` (`AgentSwitchedEvent`) marks the switch in the transcript.

## Why

Cloud sessions keep the agent they started with. The desktop disables the picker with "another agent is a new task". The agent-switch design reuses the interface transition's drain, held messages, rollback, recovery and notices, so the contract extends that endpoint instead of adding a parallel one. The note format is shared so an agent taking over a Cloud session reads the same structure as one taking over a local session.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `BuildHandoffNote` lives in `backend/internal/domain`, so nothing outside this module can import it | It lives in `backend/pkg/handoffnote`; the local note is byte-identical on 19 recorded inputs (see Testing) |
| A Cloud session's agent cannot change through the API | `POST .../interface-transition` with `targetHarness` switches it (on a control plane that lists `agentSwitchHarnesses`) |
| `/me` has no way to say a session can switch agents | `/me.agentSwitchHarnesses` |

No user-visible change in this PR by itself: the desktop UI comes in the follow-up PR.

## How

- `handoffnote.Input` has its own types (`Turn`, `Artifact`, `HistoryFile`). It also adds two fields:
  - `FullHistory`: the sentence pointing at the whole conversation. The desktop passes its `ao session history` line, so its output is unchanged.
  - `MaxChars`: the desktop passes its OS-dependent cap.
  - A note that has no `FullHistory` only counts the turns it left out.
- The builder's tests move with it. The Windows cap test, plus a test of the adapter's fields and pointer, stay in `domain`.
- Old desktops ignore `chat.agent_switched`: the Cloud chat projection skips event types it does not know (`CloudSessionChatSurface.tsx`).
- `oasdiff breaking` reports one warning and no errors: `response-property-one-of-added` for the new `ClientEvent` member.

## Testing

- Byte-identical notes: a temporary golden test recorded `BuildHandoffNote` output for 19 inputs before the move, then compared it after the move. The inputs cover 0–60 turns, artifacts, history files, injected headings and tags, the chat and terminal endings, and an oversized multi-byte case. All 19 were identical, and the temporary test was removed.
- `go test ./pkg/handoffnote/ ./internal/domain/ ./internal/service/chat/ ./internal/cli/` pass.
- `golangci-lint v2.14.0 run` on the changed packages reports 0 issues.
- `npm run cloud:check` passes: client regenerated, typecheck, tests and build.
- `oasdiff breaking` against `main` (the CI check) exits 0.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/`: 5 `TestInterfaceTransition*` tests fail. They fail identically on a clean checkout of `main` on this machine, so they are not caused by this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense

  * Sessions can report available agent-switch targets and show the source and destination harnesses, models, and reasoning effort in transition details.

title: release: promote main (bd4d0d4540) to stable, 2026-11-13
body:
Code changes: +117764 -30779\
Tests: +84913 -10700\
Others: +18780 -5229 (docs, config, i18n, lockfiles, generated sqlc; plus 117 binary files)

## What

Moves `stable` from `fb3a5c12ea` (v0.14.10, #7866, plus stable hotfix #8117) to `main` at `bd4d0d4540` (#8218), the commit nightly `v0.14.11-nightly.202611122237` was built from. That is 245 commits after the v0.14.10 source `eed7877e2d`. Version: **0.15.0**.

Source cutoff: `bd4d0d4540` (2026-11-13 02:56 IST). The 14 later `main` commits, up to `34c77c20cc` (#8194), are not in this release because no nightly has shipped them yet.

Supersedes #8070 (the 0.14.11 candidate at `5c65e8046e`, now conflicting with `stable` after #8117). That PR is left open for a person to close.

### Why there is a merge commit

`stable` is not an ancestor of `main`: it carries #7866's merge commit and #8117's two hotfix commits. Everything on it is already in this release:

- `stable`'s tree before #8117 matches `eed7877e2d` (`git diff eed7877e2d 033d597032` is empty), and `eed7877e2d` is an ancestor of `bd4d0d4540`.
- #8117's `f4d0ae6be2` (#7878) has the same patch-id as `c7f0f45677` on `main`.
- #8117's `ef67238ebf` (#8087) adds and removes exactly the same lines as `6554304e6f` on `main`; only the diff context differs.

This branch is `bd4d0d4540` plus one `-s ours` merge of `stable` (`f64d800adc`). That merge changes no files: `git diff bd4d0d4540 f64d800adc` is empty and both trees are `7a9b6919d6`. It only makes `stable` an ancestor again, so this release can fast-forward. There are no cherry-picks.

## Before / After

| --- | --- |
| `stable` at `fb3a5c12ea`, released as v0.14.10 | `stable` at `f64d800adc` (tree of `main` `bd4d0d4540`), to be released as v0.15.0 |

Same shape as #7680, #7866 and #8070. `stable.yml` stamps the version during the build, so this branch doesn't change `frontend/package.json`.

- **Local SQLite:** 13 new migrations, applied automatically when the desktop updates. A desktop cannot move back to an older build after these:

  - `20261028233910979_agent_limit_readings`
  - `20261030234657125_app_settings_limit_history`

## Testing

- **Nightly:** ao-releases run 43321445758 resolved `ref=bd4d0d45407bbe607898c176889327fb8588a6f4`, built `0.14.11-nightly.202611122237`, and succeeded.
- **CI on `bd4d0d4540`:** 57 passed, 10 skipped, 6 failed:
  - `package-version` (3) and the `ci-ok` rollup: the `Release latest guard` check, `frontend/package.json` on `main` is `0.14.8`, the same guard noted in #7866 and #8070; `stable.yml` stamps the version.
  - `frontend / vitest (2)`: `ChatWorkspace` "warns beside the composer once the account's quota passes 75%". Test-only collision: #8272 changed the badge to "Weekly 82% used", then #8231 merged a test still expecting "82% quota". Fails the same way locally. `main` fixed the test in `08cb91441c` (after the cutoff). `main`'s test file run against this tree: `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` + `ContextMeter.test.tsx` 283/283 passed, so the shipped behavior is correct.
  - `go / windows-workspace`: `TestTaskNamingWaitsForGateBeforeDeadline` (a timed gate wait) on Windows only. Locally (macOS): `-count=10` passed 10/10 and the full `internal/session_manager` package passed.
- **Not done yet:** a desktop smoke test (local and Cloud) on `f64d800adc`. Full platform matrices, race and packaging were left to CI.

## Merging

Do not squash. A squash breaks `stable`'s ancestry with `main` again. Fast-forward instead:

```sh
git push origin f64d800adc1596c23058f20fe97c03db68c053b0his PR merged once `stable` contains its head. Then release, which is for the release conductor to run:

```sh
gh workflow run stable.yml --repo OrchestratorInc/ao-releases -f version=0.15.0 -f ref=f64d800adc1596c23058f20fe97c03db68c053b0
```

title: fix(chat): compact the composer's / and @ suggestion menus
body:
Code changes: +36 -96\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Makes the chat composer's `/` (skills) and `@` (files) suggestion menus compact and quieter. Both menus, and the side-chat `/` menu, render through `ComposerSuggestMenu`, so this is a single-component change.

## Why

The menus used two-line rows (about 44px each), so only about five skills fit. Descriptions were large, the `user` / `repo` source labels competed with the names, the selected row's 8px corners were oversized inside the 10px panel, and the last row looked smeared because the scroll fades were painted in the card color over the overlay surface.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Two-line rows, about 44px, about 5 visible | One-line 32px rows, 8 visible within the same 256px cap |
| Description on its own line below the name | Description (skills) or parent folder (files) inline after the name at 11px, truncating with an ellipsis; the name keeps at least 3/5 of the row when a description is present |
| `user` / `repo` / `Orchestrator` label in muted text | Same label at 10px in passive text, like menu section labels |
| Selected row 8px radius | 6px, concentric with the 10px panel and its 4px padding |
| File icon aligned to the top of the text | File icon centered on the row |
| Gradient overlays in `--card` color over the `bg-overlay` panel | The shared `.edge-fade` mask via `useEdgeFade` (16px), fading only edges that have more content; `scroll-py-4` keeps a keyboard-highlighted row clear of the fade |

## How

- Rows follow the composer's existing add-menu row (`ComposerMenuRow`): icon, name, then a truncating description on one line.
- The hand-rolled scroll-indicator state, scroll handler and `ResizeObserver` are replaced by `useEdgeFade`, which every other scroll fade in the app uses.
- Unchanged: item set, ranking, filtering, keyboard navigation, Tab/Enter/Escape, click to pick, `listbox` / `option` roles, `aria-selected`, `aria-activedescendant` ids, the Enter hint label, and all file-type icons.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation. Checked by hand in the dev desktop app (`/` skills menu and `@` file menu).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
