title: fix(mobile): put the chat composer back down after the app resumes on Android
body: Code changes: +34 -0\ Tests: +67 -0\ Others: +0 -0 ## What On Android, the chat composer now goes back to the bottom of the screen when the app resumes. Before, it could stay stuck about a keyboard's height up, with the conversation showing underneath it. ## Why If the keyboard closes while the app's activity is paused, the whole close animation runs in the background. Two everyday ways to hit it: - Tap send, then press Home straight away, then come back. - Tap the composer's mic while the keyboard is open, the first time Android asks for microphone permission. The permission dialog pauses the activity, and any answer triggers it. On resume, every Reanimated transform driven by keyboard-controller snaps back to its keyboard-open frame. This affects `KeyboardFollower` and the inner card offset in `ChatComposer`. The composer then stays up until the keyboard opens again. Logging on an emulator showed every value was already correct: - keyboard-controller and React Native both reported the hide. - `useChatKeyboard` ended hidden with `composerLift` 0. - The shared `height` ran down to 0. Only the native views were stale, and since nothing in JS changed on resume, no style re-ran to correct them. Pulling down the notification shade or opening a SystemUI panel doesn't trigger it; the activity has to actually pause. ## Before / After Android emulator (API 35, 3-button navigation), same chat and same steps on both sides. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Send, then Home, then return: the composer is stuck mid-screen | The composer is back at the bottom | | | | | Mic tap with the keyboard open, then the permission dialog: the composer is stuck mid-screen | The composer is back at the bottom | ## How - New `KeyboardResumeResync` component, mounted once inside `KeyboardProvider` in `app/_layout.tsx`. On Android, when `AppState` becomes `active`, it calls `height.modify()` and `progress.modify()` on keyboard-controller's shared values. Every animated style that reads them then re-runs and redraws from the closed values. This one place covers `KeyboardFollower`, `ChatComposer`, `ReviewerComposer` and the New task composer. - It has to be `modify()` with no modifier, which forces the update. Writing the same value back (`v.value = v.value`) does nothing, because Reanimated's `valueSetter` drops a write when the value hasn't changed. I tried that first and the composer stayed stuck. - Only the follower's style re-running isn't enough. In that experiment the inner card in `ChatComposer` was left 40 dp low, which is why the fix goes through the shared values rather than any single view. - The root cause is below our code, in how Reanimated and Fabric re-apply views on resume after a paused animation. I didn't chase it further upstream; this restores the right frame from the values we already trust. - JavaScript only, so it can ship as an OTA update. iOS is unaffected (the component does nothing there). - `root-stack.test.tsx` and `settings-sheet.test.tsx` render the root layout with a minimal keyboard-controller mock, so they now stub the new component. ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 430 files, 4165 tests pass. The new `KeyboardResumeResync.test.tsx` checks that resume forces both values through, that iOS does nothing, and that the listener is removed on unmount. - `npm run typecheck` in `packages/mobile` is clean. - Android emulator with a debug build of this branch's JS, paired with a scratch daemon: - Send, then Home, then return: stuck before, at the bottom after. - Mic tap with the keyboard open, then the permission dialog, with both "Only this time" and "Don't allow": stuck before, at the bottom after. - Ordinary keyboard open and close, close with Back, system animations off, notification shade over an open keyboard: unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved keyboard behavior on Android when returning to the app from the background.

title: feat(cloud): switch a Cloud session's agent from the chat and terminal pickers
body:
Code changes: +303 -40\
Tests: +318 -1\
Others: +4 -0 (docs)

> **Depends on #8309** (the contract for Cloud agent switching) and on the control plane's OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#113. This branch is stacked on #8309, so its first two commits are #8309's. Review only the last seven. Until the control plane runs #113 with `AO_CLOUD_AGENT_SWITCH=1`, `/me` lists no switchable agents and every Cloud picker below behaves exactly as it does today.

## What

Part 2 of 2 on the desktop: a Cloud session can switch its coding agent from the same pickers a local session uses, in Chat and in the terminal.

- **Chat:** the composer's Agent menu lists the agents the control plane can switch to.
  - When an agent is picked, the next message starts the switch, then is sent to the new agent (held by the control plane until it is ready).
  - The transcript shows the local "Switching" line while it runs and "Switched from Codex to Claude Code" once it is done, above the message the switch held.
  - The composer shows the new agent's models (the model catalog is keyed by agent).
  - A failure appears as a composer notice with the control plane's reason.
- **Terminal:** the tab menu's agent row (the local terminal's picker) switches a Cloud terminal.
  - Like the switch from a Cloud terminal to Chat, it reads the agent's latest activity and stops an idle terminal directly (`interrupt`). A terminal cannot prove it is idle for a drain.
  - Switch is disabled while the agent works, and refused if the agent turns out to be working.
  - The open terminal shows the new agent when the switch completes.
- **Session view:** the interface-switch loader names the agent being switched to.
- No new UI component. Local and Cloud share `AgentModelPicker`, `TerminalAgentPickerRow`, the activity rows and the switch loader. Cloud only supplies the agent list and the start call (`useCloudAgentSwitch`).

## Why

The project settings and pickers already offer other agents, but a Cloud session could not switch: the picker was locked to its agent ("another agent is a new task"). OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#113 adds the switch to the control plane as an interface transition with a target harness; this PR wires the desktop to it.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud chat's Agent menu: only the session's own agent | Every agent the control plane can switch to (`/me.agentSwitchHarnesses`), e.g. Codex and Claude Code |
| Cloud terminal tab menu: no agent switch | The local terminal's agent row; Switch starts the Cloud switch |
| — | While switching: the local "Switching" line in the transcript and the agent's name in the loader; after: "Switched from Codex to Claude Code" |
| — | A refused or failed switch shows the control plane's reason (for example "Open the session so it wakes, then switch") |

Screenshots from the dev desktop against a local control plane running #113 with a Docker sandbox: <!-- attach after-chat-picker.png, after-chat-picked.png, after-chat-switching.png, e2e-picked.png (terminal agent row), t5-after.png (terminal after the switch) -->

## How

- `useCloudAgentSwitch(session)` returns the switchable agents and `start(pick)`, which calls the transition's start with `targetHarness` and the picked model and effort. It is the only Cloud-specific piece; the pickers take it through their existing `agentSwitch` prop.
  - Chat drains its agent first.
  - A terminal re-reads the session and switches with `interrupt` when the agent is idle, or throws "The agent is working" when it is not.
- The chat sends the held message without the old agent's model or effort (`afterSwitch`), so they cannot leak to the new agent.
- The "Switching" line is drawn from the running transition and replaced by the control plane's `chat.agent_switched` event, mapped to the same `provider_switch` activity a local switch writes.
- `StartInterfaceTransitionRequest.targetHarness` is sent only to Cloud. The local daemon still switches agents through its provider switch; nothing on the local path changed.
- `useProviderConnections(enabled)` lets the picker skip the local provider query for Cloud.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass. The public boundary check passes.
- New tests:
  - `useCloudAgentSwitch`: the agents offered; Chat drains; an idle terminal is stopped directly; a working one is refused.
  - The Cloud chat's switch, held send and failure notice; the Switched line above a held message (fails on the previous code).
  - The terminal row's Cloud switch.
  - The loader's agent copy, and that the Cloud loader is not shown for a chat agent switch.
- Full `vitest`: 13757 pass, 16 fail. The failures are remote-proxy (12), cloud-agent-proxy (2) and ContextMeter (1), which fail the same way on `main` on this machine, plus browser-history-store, which passes when run alone.
- **Real end to end:** the dev desktop against a local control plane running #113 (with production's terminal stream and relay flags), its Docker sandbox provider, the real worker, Codex and Claude Code with working logins.
  - **Chat:** Codex → Claude Code → Codex from the composer; each agent answered questions only the handoff note could answer, and the composer showed each agent's own model. A switch on a stopped sandbox shows the control plane's reason.

title: fix(chat): clear Claude model labels left on chats switched before #7790
body:
Code changes: +30 -0\
Tests: +72 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A data migration that clears the previous provider's model reroute on chats that switched providers before #7790. After upgrading, a chat switched from Claude Code to Codex shows Codex's model in its composer instead of `claude-sonnet-5-5`.

## Why

Fixes #8311.

#7790 clears the reroute when a switch commits, but only for switches made after it ships. Chats switched earlier still store Claude's reroute. The composer shows a reroute's model whenever no model is picked, so those chats keep naming the Claude model.

## Before / After

Composer of a chat switched from Claude Code to Codex before #7790, after upgrading:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5 High` (stored `modelReroute: sonnet → claude-sonnet-5-5`, harness `codex`) | Codex's own default model label (no stored reroute) |

## How

A conversation's reroute is cleared when its latest `provider_switch` timeline marker comes after its latest `model.rerouted` marker. That is the state a switch now leaves behind. Comparing timeline sequence numbers avoids comparing timestamps stored in different formats.

Left alone:
- a reroute recorded after the switch (the current provider's own)
- chats that never switched
- a reroute with no timeline row to place it

Timeline rows are not touched, so the chat history still shows "Provider answered with … instead of …".

The marker matching follows `20261103094403671_backfill_spanning_plan_copies.sql`.

## Testing

- New migration test covers four chats: switched after its reroute (cleared), rerouted after its switch (kept), never switched (kept), and a switch with no reroute row (kept). It also checks that the timeline rows are kept.

title: fix(computer-use): show, request and name Orchestrator's own macOS permissions
body:
Code changes: +442 -74\
Tests: +392 -20\
Others: +90 -18 (translations, 9 locales)

## What

Inside AO, macOS checks **Orchestrator's** Accessibility and Screen Recording for everything a session runs, including Claude Code's built-in computer use. AO never asked for these permissions or showed them, and Claude sent users to grant "the Claude desktop app". This PR makes AO show and request its own permissions, and points both the user and Claude at Orchestrator:

1. **Settings → Computer use agents → Native computer use → Grant macOS permissions to Orchestrator** (macOS only; the page is now split into a **Cua Driver** section and a **Native computer use** section): shows whether Orchestrator holds Accessibility and Screen Recording. Its gear asks macOS for what's missing and docks the existing System Settings strip with **Orchestrator** to drag in.
2. **Hook notice**: when Claude Code's computer use comes back with macOS's own Accessibility / Screen Recording refusal ("permission(s) are still not granted"), AO's existing Claude hook tells the user where to grant Orchestrator's permissions and tells Claude to name Orchestrator, not the Claude desktop app.
3. **Standing instruction**: terminal sessions on macOS learn that macOS checks Orchestrator, so Claude points users there for any refused permission.

Items 2 and 3 apply only to sessions whose daemon the desktop app started (`AO_DESKTOP_APP=1`). Under `ao start` from a terminal or a service manager, macOS checks that launcher instead, so AO says nothing.
4. **Crash fix** (bug already on `main`): closing the System Settings strip threw `TypeError: Object has been destroyed` in the main process.

## Why

Fixes #7241

Reproduced on current `main` (details in the issue): every session process is charged to `Agent Orchestrator.app`, AO wasn't listed under either permission until added by hand, and Claude's refusal named the wrong app.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Settings → Computer use agents only shows **CuaDriver's** permissions; nothing shows or requests Orchestrator's own | A macOS-only **Native computer use** section with a **Grant macOS permissions to Orchestrator** row shows both grants (`Accessibility: Missing · Screen Recording: Granted`) and its gear asks macOS, then docks the strip with Orchestrator to drag |
| In a terminal session, computer use fails and Claude says: *"macOS hasn't given the Claude desktop app Accessibility and Screen Recording… switch on **Claude**"* | After the refusal the session shows *"Computer use needs Orchestrator to have Accessibility and Screen Recording: macOS checks Orchestrator for everything this session runs, not Claude. Grant them in Orchestrator under Settings > Computer use agents > Native computer use > Grant macOS permissions to Orchestrator…"*, and Claude replies *"This session runs inside Orchestrator, so macOS checks Orchestrator's permissions, not the Claude desktop app's"* |
| Granting the right app meant finding Orchestrator in System Settings and adding it with **+** | The gear lists Orchestrator via macOS's own prompts; after granting, *"try again"* in the same session took the screenshot |
| Closing the strip (its ✕, or quitting System Settings) raised `Uncaught Exception: TypeError: Object has been destroyed` | Closes cleanly |

Screenshots of the terminal flow are available on request; the before/after above is from a packaged build of this branch on macOS 26.6 with Claude Code 2.1.323.

## How

**Reading and requesting Orchestrator's grants** (`frontend/src/main/app-privacy.ts`)
- The status is read in a fresh `/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript` process (`AXIsProcessTrusted()` + `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()`). A long-running process keeps the first Screen Recording answer it got until it restarts, so the main process can't ask itself; `osascript` is AO's child, so macOS answers for Orchestrator (~60 ms). Any failure reads as unknown, never as a guess.
- Requests use Electron's own APIs for whatever is missing: `systemPreferences.isTrustedAccessibilityClient(true)` and a zero-size `desktopCapturer.getSources({types:["screen"]})`, which lists the app under Screen Recording.
- Two IPC handlers (`app:getAppPrivacy`, `app:requestAppPrivacy`) accept only the main window and return nothing off macOS.

**The System Settings strip** (`frontend/src/main/privacy-guide.ts`) now takes a `target` (`cuaDriver` | `orchestrator`) instead of being hard-wired to CuaDriver.app. The tile name, icon cache and dragged file follow the target; with no app bundle to drag (an unpackaged run), it refuses before opening System Settings.

**Settings row** (`ComputerUseSection.tsx`) reuses `SettingsRow` and the existing gear. Only one strip is up at a time, so `guiding` became the strip's target, and only that app's grants are polled. Grant updates carry that target, and the strip ignores grants for an app it isn't showing, so a Cua Driver poll that lands while the strip switches to Orchestrator can't close it early. The new gear has its own accessible label.

**Hook** (`backend/internal/cli/hooks.go`): `emitComputerUsePermissionNotice` follows the existing Artifact nudge pattern. It runs only for Claude Code, on `post-tool-use` / `post-tool-use-failure`, for `mcp__computer-use__*` tools whose result or error says "not granted", and writes `systemMessage` (for the user) plus `additionalContext` (for the model). Every other tool, harness and event is untouched.

**Standing instruction** (`computer_use_prompt.go`): a "macOS privacy permissions" section for terminal sessions on macOS. Chat sessions are excluded: their computer use goes through Cua Driver, which has its own guidance.

### Changes after review

- Grant updates carry the guide's target, so a Cua Driver poll can't close Orchestrator's strip mid-switch (0423b9bc3).
- Desktop-only gate, a narrower refusal match, a 5 s `osascript` timeout, and failed reads still reaching the guide (d1a3f62d22). Settings split into Cua Driver and Native computer use sections (154592a056).
- The page records the grants it gives the guide before the guide opens, so a read that fails while it opens doesn't leave the poll running (380f077c86).

### Limitations we could not fix here

- **Claude Code's own permission box can't be changed.** "Computer Use needs macOS permissions" is drawn by Claude Code and names no app. I tried a `PreToolUse` check that warns before `request_access`, but Claude Code only renders hook messages after the call finishes, so it showed up after the box closed as a duplicate of the post-tool notice; I dropped it. The Orchestrator guidance therefore appears after the user presses Esc or **Try again**.
- **Chat sessions still get no built-in computer use.** They run Claude in SDK/stream-json mode, where Claude Code doesn't load `computer-use`; blocked upstream on anthropics/claude-code#106877.
- **A session running before the grant may still say "not granted"** until its agent restarts (the issue's finding 3). In testing it was sometimes needed and sometimes not; the notice says to restart only if it still fails. A one-click restart is a follow-up.
- **macOS shows each permission prompt once per app.** After a Deny, the gear can only list Orchestrator; the user turns the switch on, or drags the app in from the strip.
- **The standing instruction only reaches agents AO launches.** A `claude` typed into a shell tab gets the hook notice but not the instruction.
- **The settings path in the hook and prompt text is English only**, while the UI is localized.
- **In dev builds the strip says "Orchestrator" but drags `Electron.app`**, which is the app macOS actually checks there.
- **Intentional omission:** a clickable **[Grant]** in AO's notification bell. It needs a new notification type, a daemon route and API changes, so the notice names the Settings path instead.

## Testing

Automated:
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- `npx vitest run` (full suite): pass except 51 tests in `browser-profile-import.test.ts` and `browser-cookie-repair.test.ts`, which this PR doesn't touch; they fail locally because the installed `better-sqlite3` is built for a different Node ABI than the test runner.
- `cd backend && go test ./...`: `internal/cli` and `internal/session_manager` pass. Four OpenCode 2 adapter tests fail identically on a clean `main` checkout on this machine, and three Claude Code / Codex adapter tests hit 3 s timeouts under full-suite load and pass when re-run alone. None are in changed packages.
- Review follow-ups: each new regression test fails without its fix.
- New tests: `app-privacy.test.ts`, `privacy-guide.test.ts` (target, escaping, drag source, refusal), `ComputerUseSection.test.tsx` (row hidden off macOS; granted / missing / unknown text; gear requests then docks the strip; strip follows grants), `hooks_test.go` (both events, result and error field, silent cases), `computer_use_prompt_test.go` (macOS terminal sessions only).

Manual, on a packaged build of this branch before the review commits (macOS 26.6 arm64, Claude Code 2.1.323, Pro account). The review commits renamed the row and gated the notice to desktop-owned daemons. They're covered by unit tests but haven't been re-run by hand:
- Settings row and strip: granted both through the row; the row updated without restarting AO.
- Closing the strip no longer crashes the app.
- In a terminal session: computer use refused, AO's notice appeared, and Claude named Orchestrator. After granting, "try again" in the same session took the screenshot.

Not verified locally:
- `golangci-lint` isn't installed here; relying on CI.
- The macOS prompt text in a signed release build. Local builds are ad-hoc signed, so macOS treats them as a separate app; for testing I gave the build its own bundle ID.
- The standing-instruction section in a session AO launched itself (covered by unit tests).

- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(chat): keep a new chat's first message still when the session opens
body:
Code changes: +17 -3\
Tests: +27 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On macOS, the first message of a new chat no longer jumps down when the session opens. It appears where the session will show it, and the session's tabs slide into the top bar without moving anything.

## Why

On macOS the new chat page has no top bar, so its panel claims the band above it. When the session opened, the session's top bar arrived and pushed the whole panel, including the message just sent, down by a bar's height.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Send on New chat: message appears near the top, then jumps down when the session opens and its top bar appears | Send on New chat: the empty top-bar strip and the message appear together in their final place; at handoff only the tabs slide in |
| A refused send returns to the bar-less centered page | Same |

Screenshots not attached.

## How

- `NewChatPage` sets a new `newChatSending` ui-store flag while its first message is pending. It uses a layout effect so the flag is set before that message paints, and clears it on refusal, when the page moves to another project, or on unmount.
- `ShellCenter` treats a sending new chat page as a page with a top bar, so `CenterPanelShell` leaves bare mode. The page's existing empty `SessionTabsTopbar` placeholder takes the band. The session's `ChatHeader` already slides into that strip on arrival from New chat (`chat-header-slide-in`).
- Nothing changes before the send, or outside macOS's floating top bar (Windows, Linux and native fullscreen never used bare mode).

## Testing

title: [Feature]: Show and stop background tasks in Terminal UI sessions and the ao CLI
body:
## Context

Background tasks are coming to Chat sessions:

- PR #7550 adds a tab above the chat composer. It shows running shells with their elapsed time, and Claude Code tasks can be stopped from it.
- A follow-up PR will open a task in a Background tab beside Subagents, with its live output.
- #8322 (stop for other harnesses), #8326 (elapsed time after a restart) and #8327 (command and output data) cover the gaps found along the way.

All of that is Chat mode only. Someone working in a Terminal UI session, or from the `ao` CLI, still can't see or stop background work.

## What's missing

**1. Terminal UI sessions.** When a session runs the agent's own CLI in Orchestrator's terminal, background work is invisible. The daemon reports a Terminal UI session as `unavailable`, and the renderer only asks for chat sessions (`supportsLocalBackgroundTasks`). Switching a session from Chat to Terminal also hides tasks that are still running.

**2. The `ao` CLI.** There is no command to list or stop a session's background tasks. Orchestrator agents and scripts can't check for a dev server that's still running before they `ao session kill` a session, and someone working in a terminal has to open the app to see one.

## Proposal

- **Terminal UI sessions:** report background tasks with the same reading the chat tab uses, and show them in the session's UI. One lead for Claude Code: its `Stop` hook input carries `background_tasks`, the in-flight background work of the session, and Orchestrator already runs `ao hooks` for Claude Code. Other CLIs need their own source, or stay unavailable.
- **`ao` CLI**, on the existing endpoints:
  - `ao session tasks <session-id>` lists running and recently failed tasks with their state and elapsed time, plus a `--json` output for agents.
  - `ao session tasks stop <session-id> <task-id>` stops a task where the harness supports it, and says so plainly where it doesn't.
  - Optionally, `ao session ls` shows a running-task count per session.

## Open questions

- Which part matters first: Terminal UI sessions, or the `ao` commands?
- Should actions that end running background work warn first? For example terminating the session, exiting the agent, or switching between Chat and Terminal.
- Is a Terminal UI session's reading allowed to be partial, as Codex's is in Chat?

## Done when

- A Terminal UI session with a running background shell shows it, at least for Claude Code.
- `ao session tasks` lists the same tasks the chat tab shows, and `ao session tasks stop` stops a Claude Code task.

title: feat(mobile): switch a chat's agent from the model menu, as desktop does
body: Code changes: +624 -41\ Tests: +344 -5\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Mobile Chat can switch a session's agent the way desktop does: - The composer's model menu gets an **Other agents** section, built like the New task menu: every Chat-capable agent on the machine (installed and signed in), each opening onto its models with the default first. - Picking another agent's model only records the pick. The capsule shows the picked agent's mark and model, and the next message goes through `POST /sessions/{id}/provider-switch`, which switches and sends in one request. Choosing the running agent's model again drops the pick. - The transcript draws desktop's switch divider (`ProviderSwitchMarker`): "Switched", then each agent's mark and model with an arrow, the new side bright with its effort. A breathing "Switching" line sits above the composer while the switch's send is in flight. ## Why Agent switching existed only on desktop; on mobile a chat was stuck on the agent it started with, and the daemon's switch marker rendered as raw text ("Switched provider from claude-code to codex"). ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | No way to pick another agent from mobile | | | Sending always goes to the running agent | | | | | Same iPhone simulator, same scratch daemon session; before shots from `upstream/main` (8c038d42aa), after shots from this branch. ## How - **Matches desktop's pending-switch model** (`AgentSwitchPicker` / `SessionChatSurface`): a pick is local state, cleared when the chat reports the picked harness, when the session changes, or by re-choosing the running agent's model. Switching is disabled while the agent is busy, and the pick prewarms the agent's chat (`/agents/{agent}/chat/prewarm`) as desktop does. - **Rides the existing pending-send journal.** A send carries `providerSwitch` on its `PendingSend` record; `deliver` posts to `/provider-switch` with the message and uses the send's id as the switch's `idempotencyKey`. A retry after the chat already runs the target agent is an ordinary send (desktop does the same), so Retry/Discard keep working and a retry cannot switch twice. A new send of the same text to a different agent or model won't reuse an uncertain attempt; it must be retried or discarded first. - **Catalogs follow the harness:** when `snapshot.harness` changes, the shown catalog is cleared at once (even if the new agent's first load fails), loads still in flight for the outgoing agent are dropped, turn options reload uncached, and the remembered last catalog (the fallback for an empty load) is scoped by agent, so the outgoing agent's models and options never stay in the menu. - **Targets** load per agent (one agent still discovering its catalog doesn't hold the others back; polling stops when the chat closes) and are the daemon's `chatHarnesses` intersected with usable agents (same rule as New task), which is desktop's `CHAT_SWITCH_TARGETS`. Orchestrators and terminated sessions get no Other agents, as on desktop. - **Divider** names models from each agent's catalog (fetched once per machine and agent) with the menu's naming; an agent with no recorded model shows the agent's name; a marker without harness names shows plain "Switched". - Both platforms: SwiftUI `Menu` on iOS, Compose `DropdownMenu` submenus on Android. JS only, no native changes. Intentionally left out (desktop has them): carrying effort / permission mode with the switch (the new agent starts on its defaults), the divider's width-reveal animation, and switching Terminal UI sessions. ## Testing - `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 436 files, 4215 tests pass. New tests cover switch targets, the pending pick, the `/provider-switch` request body, the Android menu (pick, keep-current, busy), the iOS menu source, and the divider model. - iOS simulator against a scratch daemon built from this base: Claude Code → Codex ("banana" answered by Codex), Codex → Claude Code ("cherry"), and Claude Code → Codex again; each produced its divider, the header and capsule followed the new agent, and the menu reloaded the new agent's models. - Not run on an Android device or emulator. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added the option to switch agents from the chat settings menu and choose an automatic or specific model for the next message. * The menu shows available models for other agents, including current and older model options. * Shows when an agent switch is in progress and displays completed switches, including the agents involved, in the conversation timeline. * Prepares the selected agent before the next message is sent. * Remembers model and turn-option choices separately for each agent.

title: feat(chat): show site favicons before web links in chat
body:
Code changes: +349 -41\
Tests: +17 -2\
Others: +3 -0 (generated OpenAPI spec and TS types)

## What

Web links in chat show their site's favicon before the link text, with a neutral globe as the loading state and fallback.

## Why

A pasted link (for example `https://audio.raphaelsalaja.com/`) showed its favicon only inside the hover card. The inline link had no mark, so a message full of links was hard to scan.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Chat web links are plain underlined text | A 14px favicon sits before each chat web link's text |
| No icon until you hover the link | Each link asks for its site icon as soon as it renders; links typed or pasted in the composer start loading before they are sent |
| — | While the icon loads, the globe shimmers (a brighter band sweeping across a dimmed glyph) |
| — | With no icon (local/IP links, lookup failure, image failure, or 4 s with no icon) a still globe stays in the same slot, so the text never moves |
| Returning to a session reloads the hover card favicon | Icons already loaded this run show on the first frame |
| The daemon used the first `<link rel=icon>`, even one scoped to `prefers-color-scheme: dark` | Scheme-scoped icons are kept apart; the daemon returns `faviconDarkUrl`, shown in dark themes |

No screenshots attached.

## How

- **One favicon renderer.** `LinkFavicon` in `LinkPreviewCard.tsx` now backs both the inline mark and the hover card's domain row. It keeps the existing CORS tone measurement, plain-load retry and theme inversion. The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`, `alt=""`, `select-none`), so link text, focus, click, context menu and hover preview are unchanged.
- **Where the mark appears.** Only `http(s)` links rendered by chat markdown (agent replies and user bubbles). No mark on code, prose, `ao://` session/artifact links, file links, image links, or non-chat UI.
- **What gets fetched.** Only the link's **site root**, always over HTTPS (`https://host/`, including for `http` links without an explicit port), through the existing `/api/v1/link-preview` endpoint and its caches; never the link's own path, query or credentials. Loopback, IP literals, single-label and `.local`-style hosts are skipped. One request per site, at most three at a time, on a queue separate from hover-card warming. If a hover already loaded the link's own preview, that one is reused.
- **Composer.** `ComposerEditor` warms the site icons of URLs in the draft about 0.4 s after typing pauses. Erasing a URL drops it from the queue if its request hasn't started; requests already running finish, because the daemon caches the result either way.
- **Remount.** A module-level record (capped at 500) remembers each icon's measured tone or failure, so remounted links draw their final state at once.
- **Daemon.** `applyLink` sorts `media="(prefers-color-scheme: …)"` icons into separate light and dark slots. `FaviconURL` prefers an unscoped icon, then light, then dark; `FaviconDarkURL` is new and optional. `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are updated to match the generator's output.

**Trade-off for reviewers:** agent-written links now cause the daemon to fetch their site root without a hover. Path and query never leave, but the host name the agent chose does. This was requested so icons appear immediately.

## Testing

**Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.**

- Added `TestParseHeadKeepsColorSchemeIconsApart` (daemon head parser).
- `LinkPreviewCard.test.tsx` now resets the settled-icon record between favicon cases.
- Earlier iterations were tried by hand in a dev build, which led to loading on render, composer warming, the shimmer/timeout and the remount fix. The final head has not been hand-tested.

CI results: pending at the time of writing.

title: fix(inspector): keep PR chips from covering the earlier menu, and trim the PR card
body:
## What Small fixes to the PR view's sidebar card, from team feedback. - **PR chips no longer cover the "+N earlier" menu.** When a session's PRs are in different repos, each chip showed the full `owner/repo` in a part that couldn't shrink, so a long name overflowed and sat on top of the menu that holds the merged and closed PRs. With four merged PRs it looked like three had vanished. The chip now shows the repo's short name (`landing-site #42`), truncates the name and never the number, and keeps the full name in the tooltip. A fork and its upstream that share a short name keep their owner. - **The card's title line uses the short repo name too**, which leaves room for the PR title. - **The description preview no longer says "1 table".** Images keep their count, since it opens the gallery. - **The readiness rows drop the coloured dot, and review and conflicts read like the checks row.** They were one line of coloured text ("Review required", "No conflicts") next to a checks row that read as a label, an icon and a count. Now all three have the same shape: "Review · Required", "Conflicts · None", "Checks · 2 passed", with the colour on the icon. The classic card keeps its dots and wording. ## Why Reported on nightly: with multiple PRs the card looked broken, "Pull requests (4)" showed one PR with no visible way to the rest, "1 table" didn't mean anything to the reader, and the dots added nothing. ## Before / After The app running on a test repository, with the session's PR list patched on screen to four merged PRs across two made-up repos. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | The long repo name spills out of the chip and covers "+3 earlier"; the title line repeats it; "1 table"
| Short name, "+3 earlier" visible, room for the title, no table count
| | A dot before each readiness row, and review and conflicts as one line of coloured text
| No dots, and review and conflicts read like the checks row: a label, then an icon and the state
| ## Testing - New tests: the short-name helper (including the fork case), the chip for a PR in another repo with the earlier menu still present, a readiness row with no dot, and the review and conflicts rows split into label and state. Updated the description test. - 396 tests pass across the touched frontend test files; no type errors in the app. - In an isolated app, with the session's PR list patched to span repos, the pressed chip's right edge no longer reaches the "+N earlier" button and the menu opens with every earlier PR. ## Not covered - Five short new strings ("Review", "Required", "Conflicts", "None", "Unknown") are translated into the nine languages without a native review. - `packages/product-ui` tests were not run locally (no dependencies installed in this worktree); CI runs them. - The section still says "Pull requests (4)" with one card showing; a clearer "1 of 4" is not in this PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_011wvVxV4teMzKNLhbRp7M7y ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Pull request cards now show review and conflict details with clear status indicators. * Pull request pills and focused titles use shorter repository names, while tooltips retain the full repository path. Names remain unambiguous when repositories share a short name. * Status labels are available across supported languages. * **Updates** * Description previews count images as media; tables are no longer included in the media count.

title: perf(artifacts): fast Artifacts page and tab with many artifacts
body: Code changes: +382 -89\ Tests: +144 -5\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Makes the Artifacts page (left sidebar) and a session's Artifacts tab (right inspector) fast with many artifacts: 1. **One cloud session read for all cards.** Every card read the AO Cloud sign-in state on its own: about 4 IPC calls per card, 1,200–1,500 per click with 300 artifacts. Readers now share one store: one bridge listener, one read for mounts close together, and no re-render when the answer is unchanged. A local artifact's card also keeps no cloud settings poll. 2. **Only the cards near the screen are built.** Both grids build the rows on screen plus four rows either side. A spacer stands for the rest, so the scrollbar keeps its place. Columns and card size still come from the grid's CSS. The grid updates only when the built rows need to move, and the page's cards are memoized. 3. **A card is cheap to build again as it scrolls back.** - Local images show a 640-pixel copy, decoded and scaled once off the main thread, and kept per file version (an overwritten image gets a new copy). - Cached and fallback images load with `decoding="async"` and `loading="lazy"`. - The "can this HTML page be framed" check is kept per file version in React Query, not re-fetched on every mount. - A live card asks for its snapshot after 0.5 s on screen (was 1.5 s), so a card you scroll back to shows the cached picture. - A card's preview no longer measures itself when it mounts, which forced a whole-page layout for each card. ## Why Users with many artifacts reported the page and the tab were slow to open and to scroll. With 1,000 artifacts and no cached previews, the page took 4.3 s to show its first card and scrolled at 18 fps. Memory grew to 680 MB, because every card stayed built, live preview included. ## Before / After Measured with the production renderer build in headless Chromium, using mocked sessions and artifact files served locally. The mix is 40% HTML, 25% Markdown, 20% PNG (1600×1000), 10% PDF and 5% text. "Before" is `main` plus commit 1, so the comparison isolates the grid and preview changes; commit 1 alone took `cloud.getSession` from ~1,500 to 1 per click. "Empty cache" means no saved preview snapshots yet, so cards draw live; "full cache" means every card has a saved snapshot. **Clicking Artifacts, 300 artifacts, signed in (median of 3 runs)** | Click | Cache | First card | Visible cards drawn | Biggest freeze | Cards built | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Left sidebar | empty | 1,056 → **275 ms** | 1,827 → **467 ms** | 737 → **219 ms** | 300 → 24 | | Left sidebar | full | 1,111 → **309 ms** | 1,235 → **354 ms** | 717 → **90 ms** | 300 → 24 | | Right inspector | empty | 1,444 → **240 ms** | 1,745 → **307 ms** | 973 → **156 ms** | 300 → 18 | | Right inspector | full | 1,252 → **259 ms** | 1,372 → **284 ms** | 945 → **154 ms** | 300 → 18 | **Scrolling top to bottom and back twice, at 120 px per frame (a fast flick)** | Case | First card | Freeze on open | First pass | Later passes | Peak memory | Elements at end | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Page, 300, empty (3 runs) | 1.8 → **0.8 s** | 670 → **258 ms** | 42 → 43 fps | 49–60 → 45–47 fps | 123 → 105 MB | 18,700 → 2,511 | | Page, 300, full (3 runs) | 1.7 → **0.9 s** | 704 → **260 ms** | 58 → **49 fps** ⚠️ | 54–60 → **45–50 fps** ⚠️ | 76 → 61 MB | 9,184 → 1,375 | | Page, 1,000, empty | 4.3 → **0.8 s** | 1,980 → **260 ms** | 18 → **42 fps** | 36–39 → **50–51 fps** | 682 → **110 MB** | 59,619 → 2,511 | | Page, 1,000, full | 3.4 → **0.9 s** | 2,084 → **294 ms** | 52 → 48 fps | 52–55 → 45–52 fps | 180 → 61 MB | 29,904 → 1,375 | | Tab, 300, empty | 1.9 → **0.7 s** | 876 → **314 ms** | 33 → 35 fps | 48–60 → 42–45 fps | 155 → 122 MB | 17,999 → 1,489 | | Tab, 300, full | 1.9 → **0.6 s** | 901 → **294 ms** | 55 → 49 fps | 54–60 → 50–51 fps | 172 → 57 MB | 8,366 → 940 | Known gaps: - ⚠️ **Short lists with every preview cached scroll a little slower: 58 → 49 fps.** "Before" builds every card once and then only scrolls; "after" builds and removes cards while scrolling. The remaining cost is mostly the page layout each new row needs. At normal scroll speeds that's far less than this 120 px-per-frame stress test. - **A rare long freeze remains.** One run in six showed a single 1–1.7 s synchronous layout. The "before" build shows the same layout at a smaller size, about 450 ms, in every empty-cache run, so it predates this PR. The cause is not yet found and is worth its own issue. ## How - `lib/cloud-session.ts`: a module-level store read with `useSyncExternalStore`. - Mounts within 5 s share one `getSession`. A later mount still reads again, because the main process refreshes a stale token on a read. - Answers that serialize equal keep the same snapshot, so they re-render nothing. - One behavior change: a failed read now marks the app signed out everywhere until the next read, rather than only in the component that failed. - `hooks/useVirtualGridRows.tsx` (new): - Measures columns, row pitch and offset from the grid's layout through a `ResizeObserver`. - Listens to scroll, at most once per animation frame, and returns the slice to build plus spacer heights. - The first render builds 24 cards and measures before paint. With no layout to measure (jsdom), it builds every card. - Every card must be as tall as the first, which holds for both grids today. - I dropped `@tanstack/react-virtual` here because it re-renders its host on every scroll event. - `lib/downscaled-image.ts` (new): the image pipeline is fetch → `createImageBitmap({ resizeWidth: 640 })` → WebP blob URL, deduped per URL and kept in a 200-entry LRU. When it fails, the card shows the original image. SVGs and Cloud images keep a plain ``; the control plane has no CORS. - Intentional omissions: - Snapshots are not warmed ahead of the scroll position. - Snapshots are not warmed at app start. - A card does not swap to its snapshot while still on screen. ## Testing - New unit tests: - `useVirtualGridRows.test.tsx`: the spacer arithmetic, and building every card when there's no layout. - `cloud-session.test.ts`: 50 readers make 1 `getSession` and 1 listener. This test fails on `main` with 50 calls. - `downscaled-image.test.ts`: one decode per image, the fallback, and an overwritten image at the same URL getting a new copy. - Existing tests updated: - The snapshot dwell timings in `ArtifactSnapshotThumbnail.test.tsx`. - The image card test waits for the original image once the small copy can't be made. - `npm run typecheck` (with `packages/product-ui` dependencies installed, as CI does) and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass. - Earlier during this work, every renderer test file touching artifacts, the inspector, chat and cloud session passed (2,446 tests). The full suite and the production build are re-running now, so rely on CI for those results. - The before/after numbers come from a Playwright harness kept outside the repo. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (no visual change; measured numbers instead) - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Large artifact galleries now render visible cards first while preserving the full list and existing preview and selection behavior. * Local raster image previews are displayed in a downscaled format when available. * **Improvements** * Snapshot requests happen sooner after a card remains visible with its live preview drawn. * Preview images decode asynchronously and load only when needed. * Cloud session updates are shared across views, helping keep sign-in status consistent.

title: feat(chat): comment on selected text inline, with numbered annotation badges
body:
## Summary

Selecting text in a chat now works like the ChatGPT desktop app:

- **Inline comment box** above the selection. Typing goes straight into it; Enter adds the annotation, Escape dismisses, Cmd/Ctrl+L adds without a comment.
- **Numbered badges and highlights** stay on each annotated selection. Clicking a badge edits its comment or removes the annotation.
- **Composer chip** ("3 annotations") lists each selection with its comment; so does the sent message.
- **Comments reach the agent in place**: `comment` is a new optional field on the excerpt reference (conversations, side chats, cloud). The daemon writes "User's comment on annotation N" right after that annotation's text, capped at 4 KB.
- **No more "Wait for the pending message before adding an excerpt."** Annotation-only writes during an in-flight annotated send keep the delivery revision, and accepting the send keeps annotations added since, without resending the sent text.

## Screenshots (real desktop app, isolated lab data, real Claude)

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck` (tsgo): clean.
- Vitest, 32 focused files (chat drafts, selection actions, annotation summary, ChatWorkspace, side-chat delivery, shared): 859 passed. New test covers adding an annotation during an in-flight annotated send.

title: feat(cloud): UI-only Cloud parity quick wins (archive, restore, shells, file tabs, automations, notifications, PR conflicts, i18n, delete wording)
body:
Code changes: +284 -121\
Tests: +347 -11\
Others: +675 -18 (locale catalogs: 70 new Cloud keys + 4 new delete-project strings, one now-unused string removed, in all 9 locales)

## What

The UI-only quick wins from the Cloud vs local parity audit, one commit per item. Each commit typechecks and passes its related tests on its own.

| # | Commit | Gap closed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `feat(cloud): archive Cloud sessions from the shortcut, tab menu, and standalone-agent inspector` | Archive for Cloud sessions from ⌘⇧A, the session tab's context menu, and a Cloud standalone agent's inspector |
| 2 | `feat(cloud): offer terminal Restore for archived Cloud sessions` | Terminal "Restore" hidden for Cloud |
| 3 | `feat(cloud): remember Cloud shell tabs across a restart` | Cloud shell tabs forgotten on restart (cwd part skipped, see below) |
| 4 | `feat(cloud): keep every open Cloud file tab's view mounted, as local does` | Cloud file tabs: only one file view mounted |
| 5 | `fix(automations): stop offering Cloud projects in the automation project picker` | Picker offered Cloud projects that fail with "Unknown project" |
| 6a | `feat(cloud): raise OS notifications and count the dock badge for Cloud events` | No OS notification or dock badge for Cloud events |
| 6b | `feat(cloud): offer Resolve conflicts on a conflicting Cloud PR card` | No git step on the Cloud PR card (Resolve conflicts only, see below) |
| 6c | `feat(i18n): translate the Cloud project setup and settings copy` | 70 English-only Cloud setup/settings strings |
| 6d | `fix(cloud): word Cloud project removal as the permanent delete it is` | Cloud "Remove project" reads like local's, but deletes permanently |

Also included: one test-only commit, `test(share): wait for the staged chip instead of racing it`. It fixes a pre-existing flake in `ShareSessionDialog.people.test.tsx` that failed this PR's vitest shard twice. It has also failed CI on `main` and five other branches.

## Why

The parity audit found these Cloud gaps were renderer-only: the control plane already supports the action (archive, restore, message the agent, PR mergeability, notification inbox), or the fix is pure presentation. I checked each item against current `main` before changing it.

## Before / After

I couldn't run the real desktop app against AO Cloud in this sandbox. There are no Cloud credentials or control plane, and no display for Electron. So there are no screenshots. Each row describes behavior, and each one is pinned by the test named under Testing.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| **1.** On a live Cloud worker, ⌘⇧A does nothing and the session tab's menu has no "Archive session". A Cloud standalone agent with no PR has no Archive row in its inspector. | ⌘⇧A opens the archive confirmation. The tab menu lists "Archive session". A standalone agent's inspector shows Session controls → Archive, and confirming returns home. A session shared from another organization still can't be archived (it belongs to the sharer). |
| **2.** An archived Cloud session's terminal shows no ended strip and no Restore. | It shows "Session terminated" with a "Restore session" button, which restores through the control plane. A pause, handoff or reviewer socket still shows no strip. |
| **3.** After a restart, a Cloud session's shell tabs are gone. | Open, renamed and closed Cloud shell tabs are remembered and come back after a restart. They're stored under `~/.ao/electron` and reconnect to the session's workspace terminal. |
| **4.** With two Cloud file tabs open, switching tabs swaps one view's path, which resets its mode and unsaved edit. A Cloud file split into a pane renders nothing. | Each open Cloud file keeps its own retained view (the local loop), hidden behind the others or placed in its split pane. |
| **5.** Create automation → Project lists Cloud projects. Choosing one fails with "Unknown project". | Only projects the local daemon knows are listed. |
| **6a.** A new Cloud notification raises no OS notification, and the dock badge leaves out Cloud unread (the bell counts it). | A new Cloud row raises an OS notification (no replay of the loaded inbox, or on an account/org switch). Clicking it opens the session. The badge adds Cloud unread, matching the bell. |
| **6b.** A conflicting open Cloud PR's card (PR view) has no action. | It offers "Resolve conflicts", which sends the agent the same instructions through `sendSessionMessage` and shows "Resolving conflicts…". Guests don't see it. |
| **6c.** In de/es/fr/ja/ko/pt-BR/ru/zh-CN, the Cloud project layout/instructions settings, additional repositories, Coder template picker, the Cloud steps of Add Project, and the Cloud project's Repositories/Instructions/per-step repository labels show English. | They're translated. English is unchanged. |
| **6d.** A Cloud project's menu and dialog say "Remove project" / "This will remove X from Orchestrator" / "Remove", the same as local. | They say "Delete project" / "This will permanently delete X" / "Delete permanently", with no grey explainer under the lead (the lead already says it), and the toast says "Deleted X". Local wording is unchanged. |

## How

- **1.** One predicate, `canArchiveWorkerSession` (`types/workspace.ts`), now gates the ⌘⇧A confirmation and both tab menus (`CenterPane`, `SessionView` split panes). It lets Cloud through and excludes `cloud.shared`, matching the sidebar. `useTerminateSession` already deleted Cloud sessions through the control plane. The inspector gets a `standaloneAgent` prop from `SessionView`, so a Cloud standalone agent gets the archive-only Session controls row, as a local Scratchpad session does.
- **2.** In `TerminalPane`, the Cloud ended strip also shows once the row is terminated, and `canRestore` no longer excludes Cloud. `useRestoreSession` already restores a Cloud session through the control plane.
- **3.** `useShellTerminals` persists Cloud shell tab metadata to `localStorage` (Electron `userData` is pinned to `~/.ao/electron`). Entries are validated on read.
- **4.** `SessionView` renders Cloud file tabs through the same retained per-tab loop as local ones. It picks `CloudFileContentPane` for Cloud and `SessionFileWorkspace` otherwise. Nothing new was built.
- **5.** `AutomationsView` filters `kind === "cloud"` (which also covers Cloud standalone agents).
- **6a.** `NotificationRuntime` (inside the router) reads the Cloud inbox that `CloudNotificationRuntime` already keeps live (`live: false`, no second stream). It follows the remote-host pattern: seed on first load, show new unread rows, and handle clicks with a `cloud-notification:` prefix.
- **6b.** `useAgentGitAction` sends through the control plane for a Cloud session. `useOtherPRConflictStep` no longer excludes Cloud. For Cloud it applies to the focused PR, the branch PR included, because Cloud has no local branch rows. The card renders a standalone `CloudPRGitStepButton`, because `PRActionButton` merges, closes and stacks through the local daemon.
- **6c.** Seventy `t(key, { defaultValue })` calls had keys in no catalog. I added the keys to `en.json` with the same English, and translated them in every locale with interpolation variables aligned. `cloudRepos.problemLimit` is a plain key, because its count is a constant maximum.
- **6d.** New `shell.deleteCloudProject*` and `shell.cloudProjectDeleted` keys in all locales. The Cloud dialog drops the grey body line, so `shell.removeCloudProjectBody` is removed as unused.

### Skipped, and why (needs control-plane changes)

- **3, Cloud shell working directory.** The client doesn't choose a Cloud shell's cwd; the control plane opens the workspace terminal where it decides. `CloudCpSession` reports no working directory. The hard-coded `/workspace/repository` is only shown in the tab's rename tooltip. Showing the real path needs the control plane to report it.
- **6b, Commit / Push / Open PR on the Cloud PR card.** Locally these are planned from the worktree manifest: uncommitted vs committed files and branch ahead/behind. The Cloud API doesn't expose those facts (its workspace review has only a combined scope), so the card can't decide which step applies without a control-plane change. Only Resolve conflicts shipped, because it needs nothing but the PR's mergeability.
- **4, true parity.** Cloud file views now stay mounted and work in split panes, as local ones do. Cloud still has no "uncommitted" review scope (it maps to combined, as before). That is a control-plane limit.

Out of scope here: the other 37 English-only `defaultValue` keys in non-Cloud surfaces, and 6 Cloud New Task composer strings, which aren't setup/settings.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` passed at every commit (each commit was checked out and run on its own, with `vitest related` on that commit's files, all passing).
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` passed.
- Full renderer suite: `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts`, 14,069 passed, 10 skipped, 1 failed. The one failure is `src/main/remote-proxy.test.ts` › "verifies the host once per upstream session, before the credential" (10 s timeout). It fails the same way on unmodified `origin/main` in this sandbox, and this PR touches no `src/main` file, so it looks environmental. CI will confirm.
- New or updated tests per item:
  - **1:** `types/workspace.test.ts`, `CenterPane.test.tsx`, `SessionTopbarActions.test.tsx`, `SessionInspector.test.tsx`
  - **2:** `TerminalPane.test.tsx` (Cloud restore goes to the control plane, not the daemon)
  - **3:** `useShellTerminals.test.tsx` (restart round trip, invalid entries ignored)
  - **4:** `SessionView.test.tsx` (both Cloud views mounted, the hidden one retained)
  - **5:** `AutomationsView.test.tsx`
  - **6a:** `NotificationRuntime.test.tsx` (badge, no replay, org switch, click opens session)
  - **6b:** `SessionInspector.test.tsx` (owner sends through the control plane; guest gets no button)
  - **6c:** `i18n/instance.test.ts` (translated in de/ja/ru, including `count`), plus the existing catalog coverage and placeholder tests
  - **6d:** `Sidebar.test.tsx`, `useRemoveProject.test.tsx`
- Not run locally: the Playwright renderer e2e and the real-Electron boundary jobs (no browsers or display in this sandbox). Those are left to CI. No backend or Go changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording (behavior rows only: the real app couldn't be run against AO Cloud here)
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.): frontend typecheck, both vitest shards, renderer-smoke, boundary and postcondition all pass

No related PR in ao-control-plane; that repository is untouched.

title: fix(cloud): steer queued messages into the running turn, durably
body:
Code changes: +609 -25
Tests: +468 -1
Others: +168 -7 (generated `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts`)

## What
Cloud queued messages can now be steered into the running turn for real, and that state is stored on the server. Contract and desktop half of a two-repo fix. Control-plane half: OrchestratorInc/ao-control-plane#116 (private; it vendors this branch's contract).

- **Contract (additive):**
  - New `POST /orgs/{orgId}/sessions/{sessionId}/turns/{turnId}/steer-queued` (`steerQueuedMessage`).
  - New `TurnSteerRequestedEvent` and `TurnSteerFailedEvent`.
  - Optional `queuedTurnId`, `origin`, `senderLabel`, `authorUserId` and `authorName` on steer events.
  - `chat.turn_interrupted` reason `steered`.
  - Offering feature `queued-steer`.
- **`@aoagents/cloud-client`:** `steerQueuedMessage`, plus the regenerated schema.
- **Desktop:**
  - `ChatWorkspace` offers the queue's Steer only when the host can promote a queued turn, and shows host-recorded steer failures on the row.
  - The Cloud chat wires Steer to `steerQueuedMessage` (only when the server offers `queued-steer`) and rebuilds steering, steered and failed states from the events.
  - An orchestrator's steer renders as `[from Orchestrator]`.

## Why
**RCA, short version** (full RCA is a session artifact, `cloud-steer-queue-rca.md`):
- `ChatWorkspace` always gave the dock its own `promoteQueuedTurn` and decided whether to show Steer from `onSteer` alone.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface` passed `onSteer` but never `onPromoteQueuedTurn`. The Cloud dock's Steer therefore ran `useStableCallback(undefined)` → `undefined?.()`, which resolved successfully and did nothing.
- The local `steerStartedAt` map still hid the row and drew a synthetic "steering" row, but **nothing reached the control plane**.
- A remount (switching tab or screen) reset that state, so the message reappeared in the queue, and it later ran as its own turn.
- Not caught because every dock test passed `onPromoteQueuedTurn`, and `useStableCallback` turns a missing handler into a successful no-op.

The same server path also fixes **Bug 1**: an orchestrator's `ao send` to a busy Cloud worker was only queued, so a status request waited for an hours-long turn to end. The control plane now steers it into the running turn when the provider can steer, and records it with these events.

## Failed steers are always visible
Required for this change. A steer that fails never fails silently. The message goes back to the queue in its original place and its row shows an inline error: **"Couldn't steer: <reason>. It's back in the queue; select Steer to try again."** The row's Steer button retries. The state comes from the control plane's events, so after a remount or tab switch the message shows as steered if it was delivered, and as queued with the error if not.

| Failure | Row shows |
| --- | --- |
| Agent or harness rejects the steer (`chat.turn_steer_failed`) | "Couldn't steer: <harness reason>" |
| 45 s timeout (`chat.turn_steer_failed` from the expiry), or a steer left unanswered for 90 s (`QUEUED_STEER_STALE_MS`, for a worker that went silent) | "Couldn't steer: the agent did not take the steer in time" / "…did not answer in time" |
| Turn ended before delivery (the control plane fails the steer when the turn finishes) | "Couldn't steer: The agent finished its turn before it took the steer" |
| Harness can't steer (409 `TURN_NOT_STEERABLE`; Steer isn't offered then, so this only happens in a race) | "Couldn't steer: the agent's running turn can't take guidance" |
| Server or network error on the request | "Couldn't steer: AO Cloud could not be reached" or the server's message |

Tests:
- `ChatSteer.test.tsx`: the row is back in its place with the reason, and Steer retries.
- `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx`:
  - Failed and delivered steers render identically across remounts.
  - A steer left unanswered past the deadline turns into a failure.
  - Refused and unreachable requests become the row's reason.

## Delete on queued Cloud messages
Commits: `f847ae612d`, `6cb1e3c400`.

**1. "Delete doesn't work" (cause confirmed).** Before #8236 (merged 2026-11-13), the Cloud chat called `cancelTurn` only for the active turn (~line 1550) and never passed `onCancelQueuedTurn`. The dock's Delete therefore ran a missing handler: a no-op with no request, the same pattern as Steer. #8236 wired it to `deleteQueuedMessage`, and this branch includes it. The human's build predates it.
- **Pending:** the row shows "Deleting…" and its buttons are disabled while the delete is in flight.
- **Server truth:** a deleted message (`chat.turn_interrupted{reason: deleted}`) stays gone after a remount.
- **Failure:** a refused delete keeps the row with the reason (network, a turn the agent took, …).

**2. Delete while a steer is in flight.** A message being steered now stays in its place in the queue, marked "Steering into the running turn…", with Delete available and no second Steer.
- **(a) Deleting the message being steered:**
  - If the worker hasn't taken the steer, it's withdrawn and the message is gone.
  - If the worker is taking it, `deleteQueuedMessage` answers `{ok, pending: true}` and the steer decides. If the agent didn't take it, the message is deleted. If it did, the message was delivered: the steer row reads "Steered: the agent took it before your delete could stop it" and the chat says "Not deleted: … it was delivered."
  - A delete after the agent took it (409 `ALREADY_STEERED`) shows the same notice.
- **(b) Deleting a different queued message** works at once; the steer and the queue order are unchanged.

**Contract (additive; oasdiff 0 errors):** `deleteQueuedMessage` 202 gains optional `pending`, plus 409 `ALREADY_STEERED`; steer events gain optional `deleteRequested`.

**Tests:** `CloudQueuedDelete.test.tsx` renders the real `ChatWorkspace` and dock, with 9 cases:
- Delete reaches the server, shows a pending state, and the message is gone after a remount.
- Refused deletes (network, steer in flight, turn taken) keep the row with the reason.
- In-flight steer cases: steering row state, delete of the steered message withdrawn and gone after a remount, delivered-before-delete, already steered, and deleting another row mid-steer.

The 4 base cases fail with the pre-#8236 wiring, and the 5 in-flight cases fail on the previous dock, ChatWorkspace and Cloud chat code.

## Before / After
| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud queue: Steer hides the message and shows "Steered" with no request sent; after a tab or screen switch it is back in the queue and later runs as its own turn. | Steer calls `steerQueuedMessage`. The message shows as steering until the agent answers, then as the steer in the running turn. It stays that way after a remount, because it is rebuilt from `chat.turn_steer_requested` / `chat.turn_steered` / `chat.turn_interrupted{reason: steered}`. |
| A steer the agent did not take (the turn ended, a refusal, a 45 s timeout) was silent. | The message is visibly back in the queue, in its place, with "Not steered: <reason>. It stays in the queue." on its row (also after a remount). |
| (new) A queued message with files | Refused with 409 `STEER_CONTENT_UNSUPPORTED`, because a steer carries text alone. It stays queued with that reason on its row and runs as its own turn, so its files still reach the sandbox. |
| A control plane without the feature still showed a Steer that did nothing. | No queued Steer unless the server offers `queued-steer` and the running turn can steer. |
| An orchestrator's message to a busy worker sat in the worker's queue. | It appears in the running turn as `[from Orchestrator]` (with the matching control plane). |

Screenshots: not captured. The sandbox has no AO Cloud control plane or display to drive the real desktop against, so reproducing the flow needs a live Cloud session. The behaviour is covered by the vitest cases below. A reviewer with a Cloud session can verify it: queue a message behind a running Claude Code or Codex turn, press Steer, switch tabs and come back.

## How
- `toSnapshot` tracks the newest `chat.turn_steer_requested` per `queuedTurnId`:
  - While it has no outcome: the queued message is withdrawn from the queue and a steer row is placed in the running turn.
  - `chat.turn_steered`: the steer row, attributed to the sender.
  - `chat.turn_interrupted` with reason `steered`: drops the queued message, like `deleted`.
  - `chat.turn_steer_failed`: puts it back. `cloudQueuedSteerErrors` turns it into the row's reason.
- The promote mutation waits for the outcome event, as the composer steer does, and rejects with the reason on failure.
- **Version skew:**
  - An older control plane has no `queued-steer`, so no Steer is shown.
  - An older desktop against a newer control plane keeps an unknown interrupt reason as an interrupted bubble and shows the steer row, so nothing is lost.
- **Contract compatibility:** oasdiff with `.github/cloud-contract-severity-levels.txt` reports 0 errors and 2 warnings (an enum value added, oneOf members added).

## Testing
- `ChatSteer.test.tsx`: no queued Steer without a promote handler, and a recorded failure shows on its row. **Fails before the fix.**
- `CloudSessionChatSurface.test.tsx`: steering, steered and failed states are rebuilt identically from events (the remount case), including a page holding only the outcome, and Steer is wired only under `queued-steer`, with a failure rejecting with the reason.
- `packages/cloud-client`:
  - `npm run generate` (schema committed).
  - `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (34 passed).
- `frontend`:
  - `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
  - Full `vitest run`: 768 files passed; 3 files fail, all in `src/main` (`browser-profile-import`, `browser-cookie-repair`, `remote-proxy`). Those failures come from the sandbox (`Could not locate the bindings file` for the native SQLite module after `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, plus an HTTP/2 hook timeout). They are untouched by this PR; left for CI to confirm.
- `scripts/check-public-boundary.sh`: ok.

title: fix(remote): reconnect offline hosts sooner and show them as offline in the chat
body:
## Summary

When a remote host drops, Orchestrator retried it every 15 seconds no matter what. A short tunnel blip often left the chat waiting more than 10 seconds after the host was already back, and the chat showed nothing about the host while it was away. This PR reconnects sooner, shows the host as offline above the chat with a Retry, and folds the duplicated connection paths in `useRemoteHosts` into one.

**Cause**

1. `useRemoteHosts` retried an offline host on a fixed 15 s interval, with no retry when the window came back or the network returned.
2. A failed read through a host's proxy started a full refresh (cloud host sync plus a probe of every saved host) from two places: `recheckRemoteHost` and an effect in `_shell`. One drop fired both, and the second canceled the first.
3. The refresh path and the retry path each had their own copy of the connect-and-adopt logic. The retry copy dropped `failureReason`, so a retry that came back unauthorized left a plain "offline" host that never retried again.
4. While its host was away, the chat hid the controller banner and showed no host status at all.
5. The reviewer chat still read its model catalog while the host was away (the session chat half was fixed in #8304).

**Changes**

- `useRemoteHosts`: one `attempt()` connects a saved host and records the outcome. It is used by the full refresh, the retry schedule and the per-host check.
- An offline host is retried with backoff: 1, 2, 4, 8, then every 10 s, each jittered into its upper half. While the window is hidden the wait is 30 s.
- An offline host is retried at once when the window gets focus or becomes visible, or the network comes back (`online`). The Retry button resets the backoff and runs a full refresh.
- A failed read now checks only that host (`requestRemoteHostCheck`), and only when it is still marked connected; an offline host is left to its backoff. The `_shell` effect that refreshed everything on any failed read is removed. The per-host throttle drops from 15 s to 2 s, since a check is now one host's probe, not a full refresh.
- A retry that is refused now shows why (password rejected, incompatible version) and stops retrying.
- `HostOfflineStatus` (Offline, the reason in its tooltip, and Retry) moves out of `SessionsBoard` into its own file. The chat shows it in the controller banner's place while its host is away, for both the session chat and the reviewer chat.
- `ReviewerChatSurface` stops reading reviewer models while the host is away.

## Before / after

Lab: desktop A connects to host B through a fault proxy; the proxy refuses connections for 5 s or 20 s, then lets them through again. "Detected" is when the chat stops allowing sends; "Reconnected" is when sending works again after the host is back.

| Outage | main: detected | main: reconnected | this PR: detected | this PR: reconnected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 s | 0.3 s, 0.3 s | 11.1 s, 2.8 s | 0.3 s, 0.4 s | 1.0 s, 2.3 s |
| 20 s | 0.3 s, 1.4 s | 7.1 s, 6.9 s | 0.2 s, 0.3 s | 7.1 s, 2.8 s |

The worst case after a long outage goes from 15 s plus the probe to 10 s plus the probe; short drops come back within about a second.

While the host is away (this PR):

![Host away](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/f662260f28f812702c041ad81fffa3bd5580ff9e/b4a83ff/host-away.png)

## Tests

- `useRemoteHosts.test.tsx`: the backoff curve, the first retry within about a second, retries at once on focus and on `online`, a refused retry shows why and stops, a failed read checks only that host and leaves an offline host alone, the saved-list event still rereads.
- `useWorkspaceQuery.remote.test.tsx`: failed reads send a per-host check, coalesced within 2 s.
- `SessionView.remote.test.tsx`: the chat shows Offline and Retry while the host is away, Retry calls the shell, the row goes away on reconnect; the reviewer chat does not read models while away.
- `shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx`: removed "rechecks a connected host when its session queries fail", which asserted the removed `_shell` full refresh; the per-host check replaces it and is covered above.
- Ran locally: the touched test files plus SessionView, SessionsBoard, Sidebar, the shell route and ChatWorkspace suites (17 files, 773 tests), and `tsgo --noEmit` with no errors in `src/`.

## Risks

- Faster retries mean more probes to a dead host while the window is visible: two small requests about every 5 to 10 s, against every 15 s before. Probes still run through the main process's single ordered queue, so a host that times out instead of refusing holds that queue a little more often.
- The 30 s account sync still re-probes every saved host, as before.

title: fix(chat): fail a turn at once when its chat host dies, and keep Claude running on a full disk
body:
## Problem

A full disk made the persistent chat host's replay-journal append fail. The host then killed Claude and exited. The daemon read that disconnect as inconclusive, so the chat showed **Working…** until someone resumed it. The turn then failed with `controller ended before the turn completed`, which doesn't say what went wrong.

## Change

- **The host keeps the agent alive.** When the journal can't be written, the host keeps forwarding. It holds the replay frames in memory, up to the existing detached-output cap.
- **The turn fails at once when the host is really gone.** If the host process has exited, the daemon fails the active turn right away with `the agent's process exited before this turn finished`, instead of leaving it running. A prompt result that already arrived settles first, and a compaction turn also gets its error row.
- **A chat whose own store write failed can be resumed.** When a store error stops the daemon's projection, the controller now reports the session `exited`, retrying until the store accepts the write. Before this, the session stayed `active` with no Resume control. Opening the chat now resumes it and replays the output the host kept.

## Evidence: real Claude (Haiku), isolated lab daemons, data dir on a 160 MB APFS disk image

Each run sends a turn that makes Claude run a 20 s Bash command, then acts during that call.

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Disk filled to 0 during the call | Host killed Claude at +26 s. Turn stayed `running` for 77 s, and on Resume failed with `controller ended before the turn completed`. | Claude kept running (same host pid). Session became `exited` at +28 s. On Resume the turn **completed with Claude's reply**. |
| Host SIGKILLed with ~100 MB free | Turn stayed `running` for 80 s, then failed on Resume with `controller ended before the turn completed`. | Turn failed **0.5 s** after the host died. |

The lab build also tagged the SIGKILL case with a `disk_full` code. That code has since been removed, so the same failure now carries the generic message above.

## Tests

- New: `TestACPRelayKeepsPromptFramesWhenTheJournalCannotBeWritten`, `TestHostExitedTellsAnEndedHostFromALiveOne`, `TestPersistentACPPromptFailsWhenTheHostExited` (turn / compaction), `TestPersistentACPHostExitKeepsAResultAlreadyReceived`, and an `exited`-report assertion in `TestPersistentProjectionNeverAcknowledgesPastFailedOutput`. The Go tests were mutation-checked and fail without their change.
- Ran locally: `persistenthost`, `acp`, the full `service/chat` package, and `httpd/...`.
- No frontend change.

## Limits

- If the disk is at exactly 0 bytes when the host dies, the daemon can't write the failure either. The chat becomes resumable once space returns, and that turn then fails.
- Only the ACP persistent host (Claude) is covered. Codex's host path is unchanged.
- Naming the cause, such as a full disk, is left to a follow-up: a generic turn-failure shape plus an app-wide system-condition banner, instead of one failure code per cause.

  * Active chat turns now report a clear failure when the persistent host exits before they finish, including during compaction.
  * Completed turns are preserved when their result arrives just before the host disconnects.
  * Controller stop notifications are reported more reliably, including after temporary reporting failures.
  * Prompt updates remain available for replay when normal journal storage is unavailable.

title: feat(cli): ao account commands and spawn --account
body:
Follow-up to #8253 (stacked on its branch; retarget to `main` after #8253 merges). Part of #8237.

## Summary

Coding agents can now do the account work from #8253 through the `ao` CLI:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ao account ls [--agent claude-code\|codex] [--refresh] [--json]` | List this machine's subscription accounts, with sign-in state and default |
| `ao account default <account-id>` | Make an account the default for new sessions of its agent |
| `ao account show [session-id]` | The account a session runs on (default: this session) |
| `ao account switch <session-id> <account-id> [--stop-turn] [--wait]` | Move a session to another account; it keeps the same conversation |
| `ao spawn --account <account-id>` | Start a worker on a chosen account |

The commands use the daemon the CLI runs against, so on a remote host they act on that host's accounts. Adding, signing in, signing out and removing accounts stay in the desktop app, because signing in needs a person in a browser.

`switch` returns once the move starts. `--wait` polls the interface transition until it completes or fails. An agent that moves its own session without `--stop-turn` moves only after its turn ends, so the guide tells it not to pass `--wait` then.

The `using-ao` skill gets `commands/account.md`, a SKILL.md row, a references entry and the `--account` flag in `spawn.md`; `docs/cli/README.md` lists the routes.

## Tests
