title: [Feature]: Font choice in mobile Appearance settings (Android first)
body:
### Problem

I use the Android app every day and read long agent output on it for hours. All text is drawn in DM Sans and there's no way to change it.

This hurts most on Android. Many Android phones let you set a system font, but that choice doesn't reach the app because the text face is bundled, so the app is the one place on the phone where I can't choose what I read in. I can already pick a colour theme here, and on a small screen the typeface matters at least as much for reading comfort.

I'd really like to read in Geist, and I expect other people will want the system font so the app matches the rest of their phone.

### Proposed direction

Add a Font row next to Theme in Appearance with three choices: DM Sans (default, so nothing changes for existing users), Geist, and System.

Geist adds four font files, about 0.36 MB in total. System adds nothing. The code font stays Geist Mono.

The choice is stored on the phone like the theme preference and read before the first frame, so there's no flash of the old font. Screens keep using the existing font tokens and only the files behind them change, which keeps the diff small.

Android first: I'm on Android and can build and test there, so I'd scope the first PR to Android and leave iOS on DM Sans. If you'd rather have both platforms in one PR, I can do that too.

### Alternatives considered

Loading fonts from the paired host. It costs no app size, but it needs a new backend route, font discovery on three operating systems, and it can't work before the phone connects.

Letting the user pick a font file from the phone is flexible and could come later if there's interest.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: feat(accounts): say why an account check failed instead of showing the CLI's error
body:
Code changes: +161 -27\
Tests: +198 -1\
Others: +83 -0

## What

A failed account check (Claude Code or Codex identity or limits) now explains what happened in plain words. Before, it showed the CLI's raw error, such as `context deadline exceeded`, in warning colour on the account row.

- The daemon sorts each failed check into a **`problemKind`**: `slow`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`, `cli_missing`, `other_login` or `other_org`. It sends the kind with the raw error, which is still sent in `problem`.
- The app gives each kind its own sentence, in all 9 locales.
  - **Clears on its own** (slow, rate limited, unavailable): muted text. When older numbers are on screen, it also shows how old they are.
  - **Needs the user** (CLI missing, different login, different organization): warning colour with an icon.
- The raw error stays available under a **Details** tooltip.

## Why

On a busy Mac, Claude Code can take more than 30s to answer the `get_usage` probe. The account row then showed `context deadline exceeded` in warning colour, even though the login was fine and the numbers below it were valid. That reads like something is broken and needs fixing, which led to an unneeded "Sign in again".

I compared against CodexBar, which also reads Claude limits through the CLI. It sorts failures by type rather than message text, and keeps the last good numbers with their age through temporary failures. It backs off retries while a fetch keeps failing, and keeps the original error copyable. This PR follows the same approach.

## Before / After

The same account and the same slow CLI (a stand-in `claude` that never answers `get_usage`). Settings → Harness → Claude Code → Account. Before is `main`; after is this branch.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: raw "context deadline exceeded" in warning color](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/001394dd1883d064ec7cebf91119bd352bff25c1/0e2e8fe/before-slow-check.png) | ![After: muted note with the numbers' age](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/001394dd1883d064ec7cebf91119bd352bff25c1/0e2e8fe/after-slow-check.png) |

The raw error is still available on hover:

![After: Details tooltip with the raw error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/001394dd1883d064ec7cebf91119bd352bff25c1/0e2e8fe/after-slow-check-details.png)

## How

- `domain.AgentAccountProblemKind` is set by `problemKind(err)` in the account service:
  - `errors.Is` for `context.DeadlineExceeded`, `ports.ErrAgentBinaryNotFound` and `exec.ErrNotFound`;
  - a text fallback for timeouts and rate limits, because some CLI clients pass these on as text only;
  - mismatch checks set `other_login` / `other_org` directly.
- `Claude.run` returns the context error when its deadline kills the CLI. Otherwise a slow `claude auth status` reports `signal: killed`.
- A check that failed on its own (`slow`, `unavailable`) used to be reused for the full 5-minute cache window. It's now re-read after 1 minute, doubling while it keeps failing, up to 5 minutes. A rate limit keeps the 5 minutes. In a preview against a CLI that kept hanging, a flat 1-minute retry restarted a 30s probe every minute, hence the backoff.
- `describeAccountProblem` in `useAgentAccounts.ts` is shared by `AccountProblemNote` (Settings) and `UsageLimits` (Usage page).
- An older daemon sends only `problem` with no kind; that reads as "Couldn't check limits right now".
- Colour follows DESIGN.md: warning colour only for problems the user must act on, always paired with an icon.

Not in this PR: other screens that may still show raw errors, and the cause of the slow probe itself. I tried CodexBar's start-up flags for the probe (`--strict-mcp-config` and turning hooks off via `--settings`); they made no measurable difference here, so I left them out.

## Testing

- `go test` for `service/agentaccounts`, `adapters/agentaccount`, `httpd/...` (spec drift included) and `domain`; `go vet`; golangci-lint v2.14.0 on the touched packages: 0 issues.
  - New tests cover: the classification table; a slow check retried after a minute while a rate limit isn't; the 1/2/4/5-minute backoff; the kind on the HTTP list; and `other_org` on `main`'s organization-mismatch test.
  - The new adapter test, where a killed CLI reports the deadline, fails on the old code.
- vitest: 113 files, 1,094 tests, covering settings, usage, hooks and i18n. That includes new Settings tests for the slow / old-daemon / different-login / missing-CLI cases and the per-locale completeness checks.
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in `frontend/`. The remaining errors are all in `packages/product-ui`, whose dependencies weren't installed locally.
- Manual check of the real renderer against an isolated daemon built from `main` and from this branch, both in a scratch HOME with a stand-in `claude` (screenshots above).

title: Mobile: secure-pairing (Tailscale Serve) address is never advertised, so the iOS app reverts to 100.x:51205 after LAN rediscovery
body:
## Summary

With **Settings â†’ Mobile â†’ Secure pairing** on and active, the daemon reports the MagicDNS HTTPS address (`<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:443`) in `securePairing`, but the `endpoints` list the phone refreshes from (and `tailscaleHost`) only contains the raw Tailscale IP on the plain-HTTP bridge port. When the iPhone joins the same LAN as the desktop, the app replaces its saved MagicDNS:443 address with `100.x.x.x:51205`. iOS blocks that plain-HTTP address, so once the phone leaves the LAN the app can't connect until the user retypes the MagicDNS address and port 443 by hand.

## Environment

- AO desktop `0.15.0` (commit `d3cdaca1b3ce`, built 2026-11-13), Windows 11 Pro
- AO iOS app, iPhone on the same tailnet
- Tailscale with MagicDNS + HTTPS certificates enabled
- Remote access: normal mode (not tunnel-only), account **not** linked, no Cloudflare tunnel

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Connect Mobile and turn on **Secure pairing**. `tailscale serve status` shows
   `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net (tailnet only) |-- / proxy http://127.0.0.1:51205`.
2. Pair the iPhone (re-paired after enabling secure pairing).
3. Put the phone on the same LAN as the desktop and open the app.
4. Move the phone to another network (cellular / other Wi-Fi) with Tailscale on.

**Expected:** the app keeps using `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:443`.
**Actual:** the saved address has been changed to `100.82.75.125:51205`. The connection fails off-LAN (iOS blocks the plain-HTTP port). Each time, the user has to set MagicDNS + 443 again by hand.

## Evidence

`GET /api/v1/mobile/status` with secure pairing active (password removed):

```json
{
  "endpoints": [
    {"kind":"lan","host":"192.168.124.1","port":51205,"secure":false},
    {"kind":"lan","host":"192.168.0.1","port":51205,"secure":false},
    {"kind":"lan","host":"192.168.0.20","port":51205,"secure":false},
    {"kind":"lan","host":"172.28.48.1","port":51205,"secure":false},
    {"kind":"lan","host":"172.23.0.1","port":51205,"secure":false},
    {"kind":"tailscale","host":"100.82.75.125","port":51205,"secure":false}
  ],
  "tailscaleHost": "100.82.75.125",
  "port": 51205,
  "securePairing": {
    "enabled": true, "available": true, "active": true,
    "host": "desktop-xxxx.tailxxxx.ts.net", "port": 443, "reason": ""
  }
}
```

`ao remote-host status` lists the same addresses, all on `:51205`, with no `ts.net` entry.

## Root cause (source at `d7470e2`)

- `backend/internal/mobilebridge/endpoints.go:54` `Endpoints()` adds only `LANHosts`, `TailscaleHosts` (raw `100.64.0.0/10` IPs from `TailscaleIPv4Candidates`) on the bridge port, plus the Cloudflare tunnel when it's ready. It has no input for the secure-pairing Serve host.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/mobile.go:556` `BridgeService.AdvertisedEndpoints()` (the phone's refresh route) and `Status()` (`mobile.go:502`, `TailscaleHost: first(ts)`) both build from those inputs. So even when `securePairingStatus()` (`mobile.go:699`) reports `active: true`, the advertised list never contains `host.ts.net:443, secure:true`.
- Result: the app's refresh/rediscovery only has `100.x:51205` for the Tailscale route and overwrites the user's working address with it.

## Suggested fix

1. When secure pairing is active, add `Endpoint{Kind: KindTailscale, Host: <serve host>, Port: 443, Secure: true}` to `EndpointInputs`/`Endpoints()`. Place it ahead of the raw `100.x` entry, or replace that entry (on iOS the plain-HTTP entry is unusable anyway). Also use it for `tailscaleHost`.
2. App side: don't let an endpoint refresh replace a user-entered address with one that isn't `secure`, or keep the manual address as a pinned candidate.
3. Add a test: secure pairing active â†’ `AdvertisedEndpoints()` contains the `ts.net:443` secure endpoint.

title: fix(mobile): advertise the secure-pairing MagicDNS endpoint

title: feat(usage): refresh usage in the background instead of a refresh button
body:
Code changes: +86 -38\
Tests: +160 -4\
Others: +9 -27 (locale strings)

## What

Removes the refresh button from the Usage page and refreshes its data in the background instead.

- **Limits** reads past the daemon's five-minute limit cache (`?refresh=true`) when the Usage page opens, when the view changes, and when the window regains focus. Reads are throttled to at most one every two minutes, shared across mounts.
- **Spend / Windows** already poll every 60s; window focus now also refetches the visible view, so returning to the app doesn't wait for the next tick.
- The provider header on Limits reads **"Updated X ago"** (was "Checked X ago") in all 9 locales.
- Removes the now-unused `usage.refresh` and `usage.limits.refreshFailed` strings.

## Why

The button was the only way to get current limit numbers: the Limits poll is answered from the daemon's cache (`freshFor = 5m`), so without the button limits could be ~6 minutes stale. Reading fresh when the user actually looks at the page keeps the same freshness without a manual control.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Usage toolbar has a refresh icon button on every view | No refresh button |
| Limits stay on the daemon's cached reading (up to 5 min) unless the button is clicked | Limits are read fresh on page open, view switch, and window focus (≤ 1 read / 2 minutes) |
| Returning to the window waits for the next 60s poll on Spend / Windows | Focus refetches the visible view immediately |
| Limits header: "Checked 2 minutes ago" | "Updated 2 minutes ago" |
| A failed manual refresh showed a "Couldn't refresh limits" toast | A failed fresh read shows its error inline on Limits, and the next open, view switch, or focus retries it at once |

> **Screenshots pending.** This change was written on a Windows workstation where we don't run the app, so no before/after captures are attached yet.
>
> **Reviewer, please verify the Limits tab on macOS** before approving:
> - The Usage toolbar has no refresh button on Spend, Limits, or Windows.
> - Opening Usage and switching to **Limits** shows cached numbers right away, then fresh ones within a few seconds, with the provider header reading **"Updated … ago"**.
> - Switching to another app and back refreshes Limits (at most once every two minutes).
> - With the daemon stopped, a fresh read shows an inline error on Limits, and it clears after the daemon is back and a fresh read succeeds.
>
> Screenshots of the toolbar and the Limits tab, before and after, are welcome in a PR comment.

## How

- `useFreshAgentAccountsRead` (in `useAgentAccounts.ts`) wraps `fetchAgentAccounts(true)` with a module-level two-minute throttle and writes the result into the `agent-accounts` query cache. The throttle timestamp is taken before the request, so concurrent triggers don't stack up CLI reads. Each fresh read starts the provider CLIs for every account (two short `claude` processes, or two `codex app-server` runs, per account), so two minutes halves the worst case from frequent window switching while staying well under the daemon's own five-minute cache.
- Before writing the fresh result it cancels the in-flight `agent-accounts` poll (`exact: true`, `revert: false`), so a poll that started earlier can't land afterwards with the daemon's older cached reading.
- `UsageView` calls it from an effect keyed on the Limits view (fires on mount and on view changes) and from a `window` `focus` listener, matching the focus pattern used elsewhere in the renderer (`useDaemonStatus`, etc.).
- The page-open read runs even when the page lands on Spend, so Limits is already fresh when the user switches to it; the throttle bounds the cost.
- A failed fresh read is returned as `error` (with `failedAt`) and shown inline on Limits until a fresh read succeeds (a regular poll only carries the cached reading, so it does not clear it; a poll that lands after the failure triggers one retry); it also resets the throttle so the next trigger retries immediately. Only the latest fresh read may write or report, so one that outlives the throttle cannot overwrite a newer result.
- Account mutations (remove, make default, sign-in verify, reset credit, Settings refresh) bump a write counter. A fresh read that started before one is not written; the accounts query is invalidated instead, so a slow read can't restore the older list.
- Settings → agent accounts keeps its own refresh button; `useAgentAccountActions().refresh` is unchanged.

## Testing

- Updated `UsageView.test.tsx`: no refresh button on any view; fresh limits read on open, view switch, and window focus; a failed fresh read shows on Limits and is retried once a later poll lands; focus refetches Spend.
- Added `useAgentAccounts.test.tsx`: the read goes out with `refresh: true`, fills the accounts cache, is throttled to one every two minutes, wins over an older poll that lands after it, keeps an account change made while it was out, and reports a failure then retries on the next call.
- **Not run locally**: this change was authored on a Windows workstation where we don't execute project tests/builds, so the frontend CI jobs (typecheck, lint, vitest) have not been run locally and are being verified in CI only.

title: fix(settings): close harness login automatically once connected
body:
Code changes: +72 -20\
Tests: +155 -17\
Others: +0 -9

## What

Removes the extra **Done** step at the end of the harness login panel. A verified sign-in now ends the login operation and closes the panel by itself. The Account tab then announces "Connected", moves focus to the row's login action, and shows the sign-in with the same green status dot the Health tab uses.

## Why

After a successful login, the user had to click a primary **Done** button just to dismiss a panel that only said "Connected". While that panel stayed open, the harness was also treated as "login in progress", which kept **Log out** / **Log in again** disabled.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Sign-in verified → panel shows "Connected" with a primary **Done** button; user must click it | Sign-in verified → panel closes on its own; the Account row reads ● **Connected** · Signed in as …, a screen reader hears "Connected", and focus lands on **Log in again** |

The panel deliberately stays open, with a **Close** button, when it still has something to say:
- **Configured** (a saved key the provider has not accepted): keeps its KeyRound confirmation, since the row may still read "Login required".
- **Key withdrawal failed**: keeps the "apps outside AO can still see this key" warning.
- **Cancel failed** (e.g. the remote host dropped): keeps the error; Close retries the cancel.

UI screenshots are not attached; the change was not run locally (see Testing).

## How

- `HarnessLoginPanel.tsx`: the close happens in the verification handler (and in `checkNativeSignIn` for native sign-ins), not in an effect, so it runs once and the connected state never paints first. It goes through `exit()`, which cancels the finished operation **before** `onClose(true)`. That leaves nothing for the unmount cleanup to dispose, so the account row is never held in the pending set. `leave()` is now a thin wrapper that respects `verifying`. `onClose` takes `signedIn?: boolean`.
- `LocalHarnessContent.tsx`: tracks `signedInAgent`, set only when a verified sign-in closes the panel. It is cleared on any other close, harness or tab switch, and any new login or logout. It passes `authCheckFailed` into `describeHarness`.
- `HarnessAccountTab.tsx`: an always-mounted `aria-live="polite"` region announces the sign-in. It is deliberately not `role="status"`, so the tab's own progress statuses stay unique. Focus moves to `[data-terminal-focus-handoff]` only when it was lost to `<body>`. The row label renders `HarnessStatusDot` from the shared tone.
- `describe-harness.ts`: returns one `authTone` (green only for a fresh check that did not fail). `HarnessHealthTab` reads it instead of computing its own, so the Account and Health tabs cannot disagree. `HarnessDetailRow`'s `label` is widened to `ReactNode`.
- Removed the now-unused `settings.harness.loginUi.done` string from all locales.
- Out of scope: the local Claude Code / Codex accounts list (`AgentAccountsPanel`) is unchanged. It already lists the signed-in account, and the announcement and focus handoff apply there too.

## Testing

- `HarnessLoginPanel.test.tsx`: the panel is unmounted on close through a parent, as Settings does. The test asserts it stays open while verifying, cancels exactly once before closing, calls `onClose(true)` once, and leaves nothing pending. Further tests cover the failed-cancel path, a configured result staying open until Close, and the withdrawal warning. The verified sign-in tests assert `onClose(true)` instead of the no-longer-visible "Connected".
- `HarnessLoginPanel.lifecycle.test.tsx`: the recovered operation is ended before the close.
- `HarnessAccountTab.test.tsx` (new): green dot for a fresh check, none when stale, plus the announcement and focus handoff.
- `describe-harness.test.ts`: the `authTone` matrix.
- Not run locally (Windows dev box); validated through CI.

title: feat(grok-bot): live events from the daemon, edit-keeping updates and more bot skills
body:
## Summary

The Orchestrator Bot (Grok skill pack in `integrations/grok-bot`) now hears about events the moment they happen and does much more from chat.

**Daemon: outbound webhooks** (`backend/internal/webhook`, `ao webhook`)
- `ao webhook add|list|set|remove|test` makes the daemon POST one JSON event per question (`needs_input`, then `input_resolved`), finished orchestrator turn (with the end of the reply), `failed` turn (with `usageLimit.resetsAt` for plan limits), agent exit, and PR or review change.
- Each webhook filters by project and event kind, so a project can have its own bot. Questions, failures and exits go first; bursts, and events held while a webhook is down or rate limited (429), fold into one `summary`. `--quiet-at-desk` skips events while the Orchestrator app is frontmost and in use.
- Secrets: URL and headers are typed into a Terminal window and kept in `<data>/webhooks.json` (0600). The API returns only the URL's host and header names. The routes are loopback-only (the LAN listener refuses them). Event text is redacted (keys, home paths).

**Bot skills**
- `ao-live` sets up the "AO events to chat" routine; `ao-event` handles one event (questions, approvals, failed turns with auto-resume or retry, exits).
- `ao-update` keeps skills the user edited: a three-way merge against the installed copy, with notify, auto and off modes and a weekly run.
- New skills: watch, templates, usage, report, tracker, learnings, checkup, cleanup, sync, dev-update and handoff. `ao-actions` gains rename, pin, model, retry, usage limit, search and diff.
- Hosts: account addresses (`useao.dev`) work for remote hosts, host names are unique, and a password-free check (`/api/v1/identity`) tells an offline Grok Bot app apart from a stopped Orchestrator, a stopped tunnel (Cloudflare 530) or a released address. The bot never reads `~/.ao/remotes.json`.
- `manifest.json` regenerated. It has been stale on `main` since #8081, so every bot update currently stops with `HASH_MISMATCH`.

## Testing

- `go test -race ./internal/webhook`; `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/telemetrymeta ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/daemon`; build, vet, gofmt. OpenAPI spec and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated after the rebase and identical.
- Lab daemon with a real Claude agent: test event, auth header, restart, finished orchestrator turn with its reply, question then `input_resolved` then finished, and a usage-limit `failed` event through a proxy that returns Claude's 5-hour limit (`resetsAt` matched Claude's own reset time). Auto-resume toggle (204) and retry (202, then completed) on that turn. `worker_finished` arrives only when named.
- Update fetcher: unedited, edited, both-sides-merge and conflict cases, new skills, a bot from the template with nothing on record, and the installed version's copies found in the real GitHub history.
- Host check against five real saved hosts: online (200 and its host id), stopped tunnel (530, `error code: 1033`), released address (does not resolve), gone LAN host (refused). The setup probe prints the account address and nothing else from `mobile/status`.

## Risks and follow-ups

- Bots still on the old update script overwrite edited skills once, on their first upgrade. Later updates keep edits.
- A send rejected at once (for example an unknown model) never starts a turn, so no `failed` event; the sender gets the error.
- Quiet-at-desk: both macOS probes (frontmost app, input idle time) were checked on a real Mac, but the skip itself was not exercised live. Other platforms never count as at the desk.
- After merge, republish the Grok Bot template so new bots start from these skills.

The session account picker listed the Claude CLI login as `d3v…@gmail.com · d3v…@gmail.com's Organization`, next to a greyed-out `d3v…@gmail.com`.

title: fix(workspace): keep workspace watches inside the descriptor limit
body:
Follow-up to #4476 (fixed by #4510, which only skipped folders the watcher could not open). Backend half of the remote "connected but not working" report; the desktop half was #8176.

## Problem

On macOS, fsnotify's kqueue backend opens one descriptor per watched directory and one per entry in it. An Orchestrator worktree costs about 7,400 descriptors per `workspace/events` stream. On a Mac with `kern.maxfilesperproc=10240`, one stream fits and a second one takes every free descriptor:

1. The second watcher skips directories with `too many open files`.
2. The manifest reconcile runs `git`, which fails with EMFILE.
3. `workspaceRepoUnavailable` cannot read the worktree's `.git` file. `Stat` shows a file, so it returns true.
4. The stream answers **404 `PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING`** for a repository that exists.

## Change

- **Descriptor budget** (`workspacewatch`): all watches in the process share one pool, sized as the soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` minus a reserve of `max(limit/4, 1024)`. Each directory costs its entry count, plus one when its parent is not watched (this matches what kqueue opens). Directories over budget stay unwatched, shallowest first. Linux and Windows cost 0, so they behave as before.
- **Partial coverage**: `Watch` and `WatchSkipping` also return `partial()`. Every 30 s, a partial `workspace/events` stream reconciles the manifest and branch state, then sends `version` if the version changed or `dirty` otherwise (the version ignores content, and the desktop refetches contents on any event). A partial artifact stream sends `artifacts_changed` on the same tick. Fully watched streams do no extra work.
- **Budget accounting**: a renamed directory stays charged until the watcher closes, because kqueue leaves its children open. A failed `Add` removes any partial registration before its refund.
- **`workspaceRepoUnavailable`**: an unreadable `.git` file is no longer "repository missing". Only a path that does not exist is.
- **`classifyWorkspaceGitError`**: `too many open files`, EMFILE and ENFILE map to the retryable `WORKSPACE_GIT_BUSY` 503.

## Evidence

Isolated lab daemon with `ulimit -Hn 10240`, a repo of 6,820 tracked files in 641 dirs, two sessions, and both `workspace/events` streams open at once:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Stream 1 | 200, 7,489 descriptors | 200, 7,490 |
| Stream 2 | **404 `PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING`** | **200** (partial watch) |
| Peak daemon descriptors | exhausted (`too many open files`) | 7,740 / 10,240 |
| `workspace/files` + `history` with both open | 200 | 200 |
| Edit in a dir stream 1 watches | 0.3 s | 1.3 s |
| Edit in a dir stream 2 does not watch | never | 24.1 s |
| Descriptors after both close | baseline | baseline |

Daemon log on this PR: `workspace watch skipped directories ... last_error="workspace watch descriptor budget exhausted"`, and no `too many open files`.

## Tests

- `TestWatchStaysWithinTheDescriptorBudget`: a 200-descriptor pool over a 2,000-file tree reports partial, stays within budget, and returns the whole budget on cancel.
- `TestWorkspaceGitDescriptorExhaustionIsBusy`: EMFILE in stderr or from exec maps to `WORKSPACE_GIT_BUSY`.
- `TestUnreadableGitFileIsNotAMissingRepository`.
- `TestWatchKeepsARenamedDirectoryChargedUntilClose`, `TestWatchSkippingReportsAnExhaustedPool`.
- `TestSessionsAPI_PartialWorkspaceStreamRefreshesContentWithoutAVersionChange`, `TestArtifactEventsRecheckAPartialWatch`.
- Lab rerun after review fixes: both streams 200, and a same-size overwrite in an unwatched folder got a `dirty` refresh 28 s later.
- `internal/workspacewatch` and `TestSessionsAPI_StreamWorkspaceChanges` pass locally. `go vet` is clean on darwin, linux and windows.

## Known limits

- A stream that starts partial stays partial until it reconnects, even after other streams free budget. Its unwatched dirs refresh within 30 s, not instantly, and while partial it refetches open contents every 30 s.
- Files created later inside a watched directory open descriptors outside the budget. The reserve absorbs that drift.

title: fix(chat): draw turns a queue drain carried right after the leader's message
body:
## Summary

In an orchestrator chat, a message sent while the orchestrator was busy could stay stuck in one place while every later reply landed above it. This is the queue-drain form of the steer bug fixed in #8184.

## Cause

When an orchestrator's turn ends, the queue drains as one input. The earliest queued turn runs as the leader. The rest join it as followers that keep their own turn ids (`controller.go`, `dispatch(batch[0], followers)`).

The timeline draws each turn as one block placed by its first row. A follower's first row comes after the leader's, so it sorted after the leader's whole turn:

```
22:27  worker report queued            <- orchestrator busy
22:28  "also check this bug" queued
       turn ends -> drain: leader = report turn, follower = human message
draw:  [report, reply, reply, ...]  then  [also check this bug]   <- every new reply lands above it
```

#8184 only handles turns a steer carried, and #7822 only places report turns, so a human (or any non-report) follower kept its own block.

## Fix

`atCarryingSteer` becomes `atCarrier`. A delivery with no steer resolves its carrier as the leader turn's first user message, and the follower is placed in the gap after that row, using the same placement, grouping side map, and row cache as steer-carried turns. Report turns that #7822 places under a human message are left alone.

## Evidence

A real drain from a local worker chat (fixing PR #8383): review comment #1 was queued while the agent worked and led the drain, and comments #2 to #8 followed it. The page is the daemon's real `/conversation?limit=200` response, converted with `toSnapshot` and drawn by the real `ChatWorkspace` with the app's CSS in a browser. The page is trimmed after row 1157, the leader's reply, so the drain sits at the bottom of the view.

```
1066       leader     review comment #1
1067-1077  followers  review comments #2-#8 (drained with it)
1150-1157  leader     work, then "I fixed all 8 review comments on PR #8383"
```

| main | this PR |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/57548d8bdb489a216e015579cf44b40c3d790e81/61f171f384/drain-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/57548d8bdb489a216e015579cf44b40c3d790e81/61f171f384/drain-after.png) |
| The drained comments are drawn after the reply, which is out of view above them, so they look unanswered. | All 8 comments come before "Worked for 9m" and the reply. |

## Tests

- New `ChatSteer.test.tsx` case: a worker report leads a drain, a human message follows, then two agent replies. On `main` the message is drawn after both replies (`expected +0 to be truthy`); with the fix it is drawn before them.
- `ChatSteer.test.tsx` and `ChatWorkspaceWorkerUpdates.test.tsx`: 78 passed.

## Risks

- Checked against a real worker-chat drain (Evidence above), not an orchestrator chat: the orchestrators on this machine run in the terminal. The drain path is the same for both.
- A follower whose leader message is outside the loaded page keeps today's behaviour until that page loads.

title: [Feature]: Stagger parallel sessions so they don't all burn through the usage limit at once
body:
### Problem

Relayed community report from **NNTin** (their words, lightly trimmed; their original post included a usage chart that is not attached here):

> I updated my agent orchestrator and let it work on a feature. However I get usage limited so fast and the feature I implement should definitely be possible within the weekly usage limit (I guess < ~50%). But instead I've now used 150%+ of the weekly usage limit and it is still going...
>
> I have a suspicion it is because I told let a "master" orchestrator talk to the orchestrator of 2 separate git repos and therefore have too many parallel sessions.
>
> You can see that previously my usage was gradually approaching the limit but now it just jumps towards the limit. Previously my work flow was to work on 1 session at the time and there I could use my tokens much more efficiently.
>
> Because I get usage limited so fast the "thinking" gets lost as well. So it will start the thinking again, may make mistakes because it didn't know what it did before and in general waste thinking tokens.

We are seeing the same thing: running several AO sessions in parallel uses up the usage limit far faster than working in one session at a time.

### Proposed direction

From the reporter:

> Is it possible to "stagger" the ao sessions so we don't have multiple rate limited usage session at the same time? Once a session is done another session can be continued. This way we can ensure that only 1 session gets usage limited and not e.g. 5 parallel sessions.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: feat(review): choose reviewer effort from the session inspector picker
body:
## Summary

The session inspector's Review controls could choose the reviewer agent and model, but not effort, although `ao review trigger --effort` and Project Settings → Reviewer already could, and the daemon already merges `effort` field by field (`mergeReviewerAgentConfig`).

Review controls now pick the reviewer **the way the chat box picks a session's agent**: one **Reviewer** row with a pill (the agent's mark, model, and effort, e.g. `Opus 5.5 · High`). It opens one menu laid out like the chat model menu: model search, then **Agent ›**, **Model ›** (**Mode ›** for mode-catalog agents) and **Effort ›**, each opening to the side.

- **New `ReviewerPicker.tsx`:** built from the same primitives and chat menu styles as `AgentModelPicker` (which exports its three style constants for this). It's not a mode inside the shared chat component, so chat and terminal sessions are untouched.
- **Different from the chat menu on purpose:**
  - A pick applies at once (no Switch/Cancel). The save locks the reviewer controls, so the menu closes after a pick and can't start a second change; the lock also shuts an open menu when a review starts or auto-review turns on.
  - The Agent list is the reviewer agents, ranked like Project Settings, with the project default first and marked "Default".
  - Chat-only rows are left out: recent, favourites, fast, thinking, auto-compact.
- **Saving picks:**
  - A picked model or mode is saved by name, the catalog default included, so it holds over a project-level choice. "Use agent model/mode" clears it.
  - The kept effort is checked against the picked model or mode.
  - Picking the agent that's already saved does nothing (it used to drop the model, effort, and hidden settings).
  - Unavailable catalog models are disabled, with their reason shown, as in the chat menu.
  - "Use agent model" checks the effort against the project's model; if a new model can't use the inherited project effort, its own default effort is saved.
- **Project inheritance:** `inheritedReviewerConfig` (SessionInspector) mirrors the daemon's `projectReviewerSelection` / `DefaultWorkerReviewer`. The menu shows the same-agent project reviewer's model and effort, and lists efforts for that model. When the project sets an effort, every level is saved as picked, and "Clear effort" returns to the project's.
- **Saving the reviewer:** effort is saved via `/reviews/switch` and sent with `/reviews/trigger`, and an explicit agent stays in the `harness` field. `useWorkspaceQuery` now maps `reviewerConfig.effort` (previously dropped, so a desktop save wiped an effort set elsewhere).
- **Active reviewers heading:** the live-reviewer rows get an "Active reviewers" heading (new `inspector.review.activeReviewers` string in all 9 locales).
- **Project Settings is unchanged:** `ReviewerSelect` only exports its agent ranking; `AgentModelField` is untouched.
- **Locking:** the pill keeps the old lock while a review runs or auto-review is on.

## Behaviour changes

- Picking a model for a session with an explicit reviewer keeps that agent explicit, instead of resetting the session to "project default".
- Picking the catalog's default model or mode saves it by name, rather than as "no override".

## Tests

`SessionInspector.test.tsx`, through the new menu (`openReviewerMenu` / `closeReviewerMenu` helpers):
- **Saving and running:** pill content; effort save plus trigger body; keep/drop effort on a model switch (one save); mode-catalog keep and drop.
- **Clearing and hiding:** clear effort without a reported default; Effort row hidden for models without levels.
- **Project inheritance:** explicit default level over a project effort; efforts of the inherited model; default mode saved by name over a project mode; clear back to the project's.
- **Agent picks:** re-picking the saved agent (project default and explicit) posts nothing; returning an explicit default-matching reviewer to project default; picking agents and suggested models; the Active reviewers heading.
- **Moved tests:** the agent/model-picking tests were moved to the new menu, and `ReviewerSelect.test.tsx` is back to main.

⚠️ Written on a Windows machine where tests and builds aren't run locally. CI is the check.

## Known limitation / follow-up

If the panel's default reviewer agent differs from the daemon's (project has no reviewer, and its default worker agent differs from this session's), the menu can't see the inherited config. Follow-up: the daemon reports its resolved default reviewer (agent + model) and the panel uses it. A separate follow-up allows switching while a review runs without cancelling it.

title: fix(chat): widen the gap between activity row icons and labels
body:
Code changes: +6 -6\
Tests: +1 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Widens the gap between a chat activity row's icon and its label from 6px to 8px. The rows affected are the live "Running command · 51s" row, the step rows (Thinking/Thought, tool calls, commands, and grouped "Ran N commands" headers) and the setup checklist shown while a session starts.

## Why

The live row's dotted loader sat right against "Running command". The loader is 13px wide in a 12px icon slot, so it spills 1px into the 6px gap and only about 5px showed.

## Before / After

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Icon-to-label gap (step rows, live row, setup checklist) | `gap-1.5` (6px; 5px visible next to the loader) | `gap-2` (8px; 7px visible next to the loader) |
| Reconnect detail line and setup-failure block, which line up with the label | `pl-4.5` (18px) | `pl-5` (20px) |

## How

- The step rows get their icon gap from `ACTIVITY_SUMMARY_BUTTON_CLASS`, so changing that one class changes all of them. The live row and the setup checklist get the same step, so every label still starts on one edge.
- `gap-2` is the next spacing step up. It is already the gap between the live label and its "· 51s" timer.
- Unchanged: the 12px icon slot, the loader's size and position, the "·" timer separator, typography, truncation, collapse behaviour and animations.
- Side effect: the shared class also spaces the items after the label. On grouped command headers, the gaps to the counts ("2 failed"), the +/− totals and the chevron also grow from 6px to 8px.

title: fix(chat): stop the error flash under the model picker when opening a session
body:
Code changes: +52 -11\ Tests: +157 -1\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Opening a session sometimes flashed a red error line under the composer's model picker, which then went away. This stops that flash. It also moves any real settings error into the picker row, so the composer no longer grows and shrinks when an error appears or clears. ## Why Reported in use: "when I open a session, there is an error line that shows up below model selector on composer, and goes away, this shouldn't happen at all." The line was the provider config-options read failing. Opening a chat enables that read from the cached snapshot's controller state. The snapshot can still say "ready" after the agent went to sleep or its controller went away: - a local chat's cached page (kept 30 min) shows while it refetches; - a remote chat shows its cached page before its open refresh; - the catalog cache itself is often already gone (default 5 min). The daemon then answers `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`, "the agent controller for this session is not running" (`readingController` in `backend/internal/service/chat/hibernate.go`). The composer printed that verbatim until the snapshot caught up. The skills catalog already treats this exact answer as "not ready yet" (#5374); config options did not. This cause was traced from source. It has not been reproduced at runtime. ## Before / After No screenshots attached: the reporter tests by hand, and the app was not launched for this PR. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Opening a session whose agent went to sleep flashes "the agent controller for this session is not running" under the model picker | No error. The bar shows the saved settings, disabled, until the agent reports its own | | A real settings error (refused pick, failed catalog read) adds a line under the picker row, so the composer gets taller, then shorter when it clears | The error sits in the picker row's free space: a warning icon and one truncated line, full text in a tooltip on hover or keyboard focus, announced as an alert. Row height and picker positions don't change | | A "not running" answer leaves the out-of-date "ready" snapshot in place until something else refreshes it | The hook reloads the chat snapshot once per episode, so the chat shows the agent's real state | ## How - `useConversationConfigOptions` (`hooks/useConversation.ts`): a read refused with `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY` is not reported as `error`, and the catalog stays unloaded. Every refused pick and every other read failure is still reported. On the first such refusal it reloads the conversation snapshot: `invalidateQueries` locally, `refreshRemoteConversationOnce` for remote hosts. A ref keeps the 5 s poll from repeating that reload; it resets on success or when the read turns off. - `TurnSettingsBar`: the two `

` lines under the row are replaced by one `role="alert"` item at the end of the left picker group. It is `flex-1 min-w-3.5 overflow-hidden`: it only takes space the pickers leave free, but the warning icon always keeps its 14px. The line is focusable and its full text is in a `Tooltip` that opens on hover or keyboard focus. - Ruled out while tracing: cross-session error leaks (`SessionChatSurface` is keyed per session) and the remember-permissions error (click-only, scoped to the project). - Known limit: if a freshly read snapshot keeps saying "ready" while the daemon keeps refusing, the picker stays disabled with saved settings rather than showing the refusal. The poll keeps retrying. ## Testing Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation. Tests added (results come from CI): - `useConversation.test.tsx`: a "not running" read shows no error, reloads the snapshot once (not on every poll), then loads; a new conflict after the read turns off reloads again, including when a read from before the turn-off answers late; other read failures are still shown; a refused pick is still shown. - `TurnSettingsBar.test.tsx`: the error renders inside the picker row, nothing is stacked under it, the icon keeps its room, and keyboard focus opens the full text. Manual checks for a reviewer: 1. Leave a session idle until its agent hibernates (or more than 5 minutes), then reopen it. There should be no red line under the model picker. 2. Trigger a real settings error. The warning should appear in the picker row and the composer should not change height. 3. Narrow the window. The error text should truncate and the icon should stay visible. Hovering or tabbing to it shows the full message. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [ ] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Settings errors now appear together in the settings row, with both messages available in a tooltip when the alert is hovered or focused. * Conversation settings recover more reliably when the chat controller is temporarily unavailable, without showing that temporary issue as a catalog error. Other catalog errors and option-setting errors remain visible.

title: fix(browser): let Chrome mode agents act while their window is covered
body:
Code changes: +64 -14\
Tests: +173 -38\
Others: +6 -3

## What

In Chrome mode, agents now act in their Chrome tab while its window is covered by other apps, minimized, or behind the user's own tab. Clicks, typing, key presses, drags and screenshots no longer need the agent's tab on screen, so agents stop asking the user to "bring the Chrome window onto the screen".

## Why

Reported by Prateek: "the agent seems to depend on the chrome window being in the foreground. Why is this a requirement? I don't face this issue when using Claude's Chrome extension."

Before every trusted action and every screenshot, the extension activated the agent's tab, un-minimized its window, and waited up to 2 s for the page's `document.visibilityState` to stop being `hidden`. Otherwise it failed with `BROWSER_TAB_HIDDEN`. On macOS, Chrome reports a window as hidden whenever other windows cover it. The agent's window is deliberately opened unfocused, so it usually sits behind Orchestrator or the user's editor.

The assumption behind that wait ("Chrome drops trusted input to hidden pages") is false. Measured on Chrome 157 (macOS), CDP `Input.*` and `Page.captureScreenshot`:

| Agent's tab | Trusted click / typing | Debugger screenshot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Window in front | lands | works |
| Window covered by another window (`hidden`) | lands | works |
| Background tab in a window the user is using (`hidden`) | lands | works |
| Window minimized (`hidden`) | lands | Chrome stops drawing minimized windows, so no frame |

Only `chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab` needs the tab on screen.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Covered or minimized agent window: `BROWSER_TAB_HIDDEN` after 2 s, and the agent asks the user to bring Chrome forward | Input and screenshots work in place |
| User switches to their own tab in the agent's window: input falls back to synthetic, screenshots fail with `BROWSER_TAB_BUSY` | Trusted input and screenshots reach the agent's tab; the user's tab stays in front |
| Every trusted action un-minimizes the agent's window (which on macOS also focuses it) | The window is never restored or focused |
| Screenshot of a minimized window | Returns `SCREENSHOT_UNAVAILABLE` within 4 s, telling the agent to use `ao browser snapshot`; it never hangs |

## How

- `trusted-input.ts`: while the debugger is attached, `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled` makes pages that check focus see the agent's tab as focused; it is turned off before detaching. A new `screenshot()` uses `Page.captureScreenshot`, which can only ever contain the agent's own tab. It is bounded by a 4 s timeout, and detaching cancels a request Chrome will never answer.
- `executor.ts`: trusted input no longer calls `showTab()` and no longer drops to synthetic input when the user is on another tab. Screenshots use the debugger wherever trusted input is allowed. Sites the user limited to synthetic input keep the old `captureVisibleTab` path, whose hidden-window error now tells the agent to use a snapshot.
- Minimized windows are left alone on purpose. Restoring one to get a frame focused it in 7 of 8 tries on macOS, even with `focused: false`, which would take focus from the user.
- Skill doc (`using-ao/commands/browser.md`): agents are told input and screenshots work in the background and never to ask the user to bring Chrome forward.
- `chrome_e2e_test.go`:
  - The run instructions no longer turn off Chrome's occlusion tracking. Those flags are what hid this bug from the test.
  - Fixed the tab-group title (`AO ·` → `Orchestrator ·`, stale since #7685).
  - Fixed a race where the consent click ran before `consent.js` attached its listener.

The separate window per session is unchanged here. Reusing the user's window comes in a follow-up, now possible because nothing needs the tab in front.

## Testing

- `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/browser-extension`: 100 passed. New and updated tests cover:
  - trusted input and screenshots behind the user's tab and in a minimized window, with no window updates
  - the focus-emulation on/off sequence
  - a screenshot that never gets a frame failing promptly without touching the window
  - the synthetic-site fallback
- `npm run typecheck`: clean. `go vet` / `go test ./internal/browserchrome/... ./internal/skillassets/... ./internal/cli/...`: pass.
- **Real Chrome end-to-end** (`TestChromeE2E`, Chrome for Testing 148, macOS): the real extension and native host, an isolated profile and data dir, occlusion tracking **on**. 5/5 runs pass in 8–14 s. The same test against `main`'s extension fails at `input tier behind the user's tab = synthetic`.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in (no UI change; behavior table above)
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (pending)

title: [Bug]: A follow-up task runs inside the full uncompacted history, re-sending ~460k tokens on every request
body:
### What went wrong?

Relayed from the token audit published by the #8385 reporter (NNTin): a worker was given a new follow-up task inside its existing conversation, which already held 359 messages and about 463k input tokens. Every request for the new task re-sent that whole history. Its first response wrote about 453k tokens to cache, and it used 5.2M raw tokens in 10 minutes. No compaction happened in any of the active sessions.

Source: https://gist.github.com/NNTin/bd11aed37feec8c74c805074810e69e0

---

### Evidence from the linked audit (collected by the reporter's agent, not reproduced here)

AO 0.14.10 (Docker, Linux amd64), Claude Code 2.1.311, `claude-opus-5-5`, 2026-11-14.

Within the 08:16:50–08:26:50 UTC window, during which account usage went from 34% to 81%:

| Conversation | Responses | Raw tokens | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Repo B worker | 11 | 5,212,291 | New follow-up work inside an existing 359-message / 463,550-input-token conversation |
| Repo A deployment worker | 26 | 2,349,119 | New scoped task; input grew from 39,257 to 128,936 tokens |

- The large worker's first resumed response wrote **452,997 tokens to cache**. Its later requests each re-read roughly 464k–483k input tokens.
- The audit states: *"No compaction-boundary records appeared in the active native transcripts. That supports investigating task-boundary history retention; it does not prove that every older item was unnecessary."*

**What this supports:** when a session takes on a new task, the cost of every request depends on the whole history carried over from earlier tasks. When that session is cold (cache expired), the first request pays to write the full history back to cache.

**Related:**
- #8385: staggering parallel sessions (scheduling)
- #7606: repeated report delivery

The audit treats this as a third, separate mechanism: staggering alone would not reduce the size of each request.

title: fix(browser): tidy Chrome mode setup and work in the user's Chrome window
body:
Code changes: +21 -13\
Tests: +83 -21\
Others: +31 -19 (translations, brand script, two icons) plus PR evidence images

Stacked on #8396 (base: `ao/agent-orchestrator-245/chrome-background-input`). Merge that first.

## What

Fixes Prateek's Chrome mode feedback ("This experience is very broken"):

- **Agent works in your Chrome window.** A session's tab group now opens in the background of the window you last used, instead of a new window. Your tab stays in front. A new unfocused window is used only when you have no normal window open (incognito windows are never used).
- **No extension ID** in setup.
- **Extension folder is copyable.** It is a read-only, selectable field (one click selects it all) next to the existing Copy path button.
- **No CLI command shown.** "Using it" now says what *you* do: "Ask an agent to use your Chrome. The first time, Chrome asks you to allow that session." (Updated in all 9 locales.)
- **Toolbar icon is readable.** The 16 and 32 px toolbar icons are the flat mark filling the square, instead of the app icon (dark tile and margin) shrunk to 16 px.

## Why

> Why are we showing extension id? Why are we showing extension path if I can't even copy it from there? Why are we showing the CLI command that the agent will run? … Orchestrator logo in chrome is tiny. It looks bad. … my agent created a new chrome window instead of reusing the existing one.

The separate window existed only because trusted input and screenshots needed the agent's tab in front of *some* window. #8396 removed that dependency, so the tab can live in your window, behind your tab.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Toolbar icon at 16 px (8× zoom): ![before](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/a6384941187e2e5ca446a96f89644c6a971f0d5e/docs/pr-evidence/chrome-mode-setup/toolbar-icon-16-before.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/a6384941187e2e5ca446a96f89644c6a971f0d5e/docs/pr-evidence/chrome-mode-setup/toolbar-icon-16-after.png?raw=true) |
| Toolbar icon at 32 px (4× zoom): ![before](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/a6384941187e2e5ca446a96f89644c6a971f0d5e/docs/pr-evidence/chrome-mode-setup/toolbar-icon-32-before.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/a6384941187e2e5ca446a96f89644c6a971f0d5e/docs/pr-evidence/chrome-mode-setup/toolbar-icon-32-after.png?raw=true) |
| Path as plain text that can't be selected, plus "Extension ID: eefgah…" and "an agent runs `ao browser target chrome`" | Path in a selectable field (shown selected), no ID, no command (screenshot below) |
| Each session opens its own Chrome window | Each session is a tab group in your window, behind your tab |

![Settings → Browser → Agents in your Chrome](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/a6384941187e2e5ca446a96f89644c6a971f0d5e/docs/pr-evidence/chrome-mode-setup/settings-after.png?raw=true)

## How

- `sessions.ts`: on a session's first tab, `chrome.windows.getLastFocused({ windowTypes: ["normal"] })`. If that window isn't incognito, the tab is created there with `active: false` and grouped. Otherwise the old unfocused window is created. Ending a session already closes a window only when it holds nothing but the session's tabs, so your window is never closed; the session's pages are ungrouped and blank tabs are closed.
- `executor.ts`: the `captureVisibleTab` path (sites limited to synthetic input) never un-minimizes a window. That now matters more, because the window can be the user's; the change itself landed in #8396 after review and is merged into this branch.
- Icons: changed the source script `scripts/generate-brand-assets.swift` (per `assets/brand/README.md`, outputs are never edited by hand) and committed only the two outputs it changes. 48 and 128 keep the tile. Running the script on this Mac also rewrote other assets because of local toolchain byte differences; those were left out.
- Settings: shared `Input` primitive, mono for the path as `DESIGN.md` prescribes. The `extensionId` label key is replaced by `extensionPath` (the field's accessible name).
- Not in this PR: publishing the extension to the Chrome Web Store. That is the real fix for "Load unpacked / paste a path" and needs the team's developer account.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/browser-extension`: 102 passed. New tests:
  - the tab group opens in your window, behind your active tab; trusted click and screenshot work there; ending the session leaves your window open
  - incognito windows are never used
  - with no window open, the session falls back to its own window
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/settings/BrowserChromeSection.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n`: 46 passed. The setup test checks:
  - the read-only folder field selects on focus
  - no extension ID and no `ao browser target` text
  - the new hint
- `npm run typecheck`: clean. `go vet ./internal/browserchrome`: clean.
- **Real Chrome end-to-end** (`TestChromeE2E`, Chrome for Testing 148, macOS, real extension and native host, isolated profile, occlusion tracking on): **15 consecutive passes**. The test now asserts:
  - only your window exists and your tab stays in front
  - a second session joins the same window in its own group
  - ending it leaves your window open and removes its group
  - closing the window with the group in it moves the session to your other window
- Also fixes two test-only races found while doing this: the visibility check now waits for macOS's minimize animation, and the consent click waits for `consent.js`.
- Settings screenshot: `npm run dev:web` with the preview status temporarily set to "set up" (not committed).

title: perf(browser): let Chromium throttle hidden, idle browser sessions
body:
Code changes: +45 -0\
Tests: +81 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A session whose Browser panel is hidden, and that nothing is using, now lets Chromium throttle its pages. Timers and animation frames drop to background rates, and after 5 hidden minutes Chromium's intensive throttling kicks in on its own. Its tabs go back to full speed when:

- its panel is shown
- an agent command or browser operation runs on it
- the phone streams it
- network capture or DevTools observes it
- a tab plays audio

## Why

User feedback: with many sessions open, the Browser tabs of sessions you aren't looking at keep consuming resources while you work in another session.

Every tab was created with `backgroundThrottling: false` (`browser-view-host.ts`), so a hidden session's pages kept running timers, polling, animations and dev-server reload loops at full speed for as long as the session stayed open. That is option A of the hidden browser tab work. #8256 (don't create a tab until the panel is shown) and #8262 (close hidden tabs past a cap) reduce the number of processes and their memory; this PR stops the processes that remain from burning CPU. They don't overlap and merge independently.

## Before / After

Electron 44.7.0 (the app's version) on macOS. Four `WebContentsView`s parked offscreen with `setVisible(false)` (as the host parks a hidden session), running a busy page: a 10 ms `setInterval` doing ~1 ms of work, plus a `requestAnimationFrame` canvas loop. 20 s samples via `app.getAppMetrics()`, 3 runs:

| 4 hidden busy tabs | Before (throttling off) | After (throttling on) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Renderer CPU, % of one core (median) | 20.7 / 20.4 / 21.2 | 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.2 |
| Timer callbacks per second, all tabs | 401 / 400 / 401 | 5 / 5 / 5 |
| Working set | 346 MB | 347 MB |

Memory is unchanged by design; #8256 and #8262 handle memory. No user-visible change while a panel is shown.

## How

- One `syncBackgroundThrottling(session)` decides for every tab of a session: throttle only when the panel is hidden, there is no live stream, DevTools is closed, `agentBrowserCommands` and `browserOperations` are both 0, no tab has active network capture, and the tab isn't audible. It calls `webContents.setBackgroundThrottling` only when a tab's state actually changes.
- Called at each transition:
  - `setBounds` show/hide
  - start and end of `setAgentBrowserActivity` (every agent command) and `withBrowserOperation`
  - live stream start, failure and detach
  - DevTools open and close (including a native close)
  - tab creation, so a popup that opens while hidden joins in
  - `audio-state-changed`
- Agent commands unthrottle the page *before* they run, so `wait`, `--dom-stable` and animations behave exactly as today while an agent works.
- Not included: freezing pages (`Page.setWebLifecycleState`) through the debugger that capture, the agent runtime and DevTools share. Chromium's intensive throttling after 5 hidden minutes gives most of that benefit with no new debugger traffic; freezing can follow if measurements still call for it.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts -t "hidden browser background throttling"`: 4 new tests.
  - a hidden session is throttled, a shown one never is, and repeated hides send nothing more to Chromium
  - a hidden page is unthrottled for the length of an agent command and throttled again after
  - an audible tab is never throttled until its audio stops
  - an open DevTools keeps the page unthrottled until it closes
- `npx vitest run src/main`: 104 files, 2,337 tests pass.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- The Electron measurement above, with a standalone script mirroring how the host parks hidden tabs.

## Review follow-up

`execute` returned pending `runNative` and network-capture work from inside its `try`, so its `finally` released the command before that work finished. That already ended the "agent active" indicator early, and with this change it would also have re-throttled the page mid-command. The command body now runs in an inner `async` function that `execute` awaits. Two regression tests cover it: an un-awaited `click`, and `network-start` staying unthrottled for the length of the capture. Both fail without the fix. `src/main`: 2,339 tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in (numbers; no UI change)
- [x] Tests added
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (pending)

title: perf(browser): reclaim leftover temporary browser profiles and stale caches
body:
Code changes: +89 -1\
Tests: +61 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The desktop app now reclaims the disk space its browser leaks:

- At startup, it deletes every leftover temporary browser profile folder (`~/.ao/electron/Partitions/ao-browser-temporary-<uuid>`). Named profiles, which hold your sign-ins, are never touched.
- When a worker's temporary profile is cleared at session end, its V8 code cache is now cleared too.
- Once per install, it clears the default session's HTTP and code caches, which only ever grew. Cookies and storage are untouched.

This is TB-7 in `docs/plans/2026-10-13-desktop-performance-overhaul.md`.

## Why

Every worker's Browser panel gets a temporary partition named with a fresh UUID, and nothing ever reuses one. Clearing it at session end (`clearStorageData` and `clearCache`) empties its storage but leaves the folder and its code and GPU caches behind. A quit or crash skips even that. On a long-lived install they pile up.

## Before / After

One developer Mac, read-only measurement of `~/.ao/electron`:

| | Before | After this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Temporary profile folders | 473 folders, 1.7 GB | 0 at each launch |
| Default-session `Cache` and `Code Cache` | 1.0 GB and 72 MB | cleared once, then normal growth |
| Total `~/.ao/electron` | 3.4 GB | about 0.6 GB |

Sweep check on real data: 40 real orphaned folders (148 MB) plus the 3 named profiles were copied to a temp dir and swept with this module. Result: `{"removed":40,"failed":0}` in 261 ms, and all 3 named profiles were kept.

## How

- `browser-storage-cleanup.ts`:
  - `sweepTemporaryBrowserPartitions(userData)` removes only real directories whose names exactly match `ao-browser-temporary-<uuid>`. Symlinks, files and look-alikes are skipped. It runs in the background from `app.whenReady` before any window exists. It's safe because the app holds the single-instance lock on this profile, and new partitions always get new UUIDs, so the sweep can never race one in use.
  - `purgeRootCachesOnce(session, userData)` clears `session.defaultSession` caches and then writes a versioned marker (`.ao-root-cache-purge-v1`). A failure writes no marker, so it retries next launch.
- `main.ts`: `clearElectronBrowserProfileData` also calls `clearCodeCaches({})`.
- Not included: a global `--disk-cache-size` cap. It would apply to named profiles too and could slow pages people use every day. The one-time purge plus the sweep reclaim the space without that tradeoff.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/browser-storage-cleanup.test.ts`: 4 tests, using real temp directories.
  - removes only temporary partition folders, keeping named profiles, a malformed name, a file and a symlink (whose target survives)
  - does nothing without a `Partitions` folder
  - purges once per version
  - retries after a failed purge
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- The real-data sweep above.

## Verified in the real desktop app

Isolated lab profile; a combined branch with #8408 and #8413:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| First launch with 30 real orphaned temporary profiles plus 1 named profile seeded (111 MB) | log `browser storage: removed 30 leftover temporary profiles`; only the named profile left (264 KB) |
| One-time root cache purge | `.ao-root-cache-purge-v1` written at first launch |
| Relaunch after using a Browser panel | log `removed 1 leftover temporary profiles` (the previous run's); marker timestamp unchanged, so **no second purge** |
| Combined branch suites | typecheck clean; `src/main` and `src/shared` 2,838 pass; renderer 14,364 pass |

Merge note: #8413 adds an import on the same `main.ts` line. Whichever merges second needs a trivial merge keeping both imports.

- [x] Follows AGENTS.md; all state stays under `~/.ao`
- [x] Before / After filled in (numbers; no UI change)

title: perf(browser): stop scrolling elsewhere from re-positioning the browser
body:
Code changes: +53 -12\
Tests: +63 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Scrolling chat, the terminal, a file list or anything else in the window no longer makes the Browser panel re-measure and re-send its position to the main process. A scroll that does move the browser (the document, or a container around the browser) still updates it at once.

This is TB-3 in `docs/plans/2026-10-13-desktop-performance-overhaul.md`.

## Why

`useBrowserView` listened to every `scroll` event in the window in capture phase. On each one it read layout (`getBoundingClientRect` up the slot's ancestors), claimed a new layout revision, and sent `browser:setBounds`. The main process then re-applied the native `WebContentsView` bounds and replied with `browser:boundsApplied`. That cost two IPC hops and a layout read per frame, for every frame of every scroll anywhere, while a Browser panel was open, even though nothing had moved.

## Before / After

| Scroll | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat or any element beside the browser (5 frames) | 5 `setBounds`, 5 main bounds updates, 5 replies | none |
| Container around the browser, browser didn't move | one per frame | none |
| Container around the browser, browser moved | one per frame | one per frame (unchanged) |
| Window resize, panel transition, slot change, fullscreen | always sends | always sends (unchanged) |

## How

- `scrollCanMoveSlot(target, slot)`: a scroll can only move the slot when its target is the document or an element that contains the slot. Anything else is ignored before any layout read.
- Scroll-driven measures pass `onlyIfChanged`. `measureAndSend` skips the IPC when the view, visibility and rect match what it last sent (`lastSentBoundsRef`, updated by both the visible and hidden paths).
- **Only scroll-driven measures deduplicate.** The main process can hide a view on its own (`clear()`, closing the last tab) without telling the renderer. So resize, ResizeObserver, settle, ref handoff, transition and fullscreen measures still send every time and keep correcting main.
- If a non-scroll measure is queued while a scroll measure is pending, the frame sends unconditionally (`scrollOnlyMeasureRef` is cleared by `scheduleMeasure`).
- No main-process change. With the renderer no longer sending redundant updates, main-side dedupe would only add a second source of truth.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.test.tsx`: 74 pass, including 4 new tests.
  - Chat scrolling sends nothing (fails on `main`: one `setBounds` per frame).
  - A scroll around the browser that moves nothing sends nothing (fails on `main`).
  - A scroll that moves the browser sends exactly one update with the new rect.
  - A window resize with the same rect still re-sends.
- Renderer browser, hook and lib suites: 284 files, 3,614 tests pass. `npm run typecheck`: clean.

## Measured in the real desktop app

An isolated lab app with a Browser panel open beside a long chat. 60 real mouse-wheel events (CDP `mouseWheel`) over the chat transcript; every run fired 30–60 actual `scroll` events. Main-process `browser:setBounds` messages were counted with lab-only instrumentation (not in this PR). The `main` and branch hooks were hot-swapped in the same app and session, so everything else was identical.

| 60 wheel events on the chat | `main` hook | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setBounds` IPC, run 1 / 2 / 3 | 30 / 60 / 60 (one per scroll event) | **0 / 0 / 0** |

Layout changes that move the browser still update it:

| Action | Slot change | `setBounds` IPC | Native view |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collapse / expand sidebar | none (inspector is right-anchored) | 0 / 0 | unchanged, aligned |
| Maximize browser | 614×745 → 1312×751 | 6 (across the animation) | fills the slot edge to edge |
| Return to panel | 1312×751 → 614×745 | 6 | back in the panel slot, aligned |

Combined branch with #8407 and #8413: typecheck clean; `src/main` and `src/shared` 2,838 pass; renderer 14,364 pass.

## Review follow-up

With the Browser panel closed, the slot is unmounted, so every scroll anywhere still re-sent identical **hidden** bounds. Scroll-driven hides are now deduplicated too, while hides from anything else (deactivation, slot removal, fullscreen) are always sent. New tests:
- 10 scrolls with the panel closed send at most one hidden update (fails on the previous commit).
- A non-scroll hide is still sent.

`src/renderer/{components,hooks,lib}`: 587 files, 10,554 tests pass; `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` clean.

- [x] Tests added

  * Repeated scrolling while a browser view is hidden no longer triggers redundant updates, and hiding a view after deactivation is still applied.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for browser view positioning and visibility during scrolling, window resizing, and deactivation.

title: feat(desktop): show skills by readable name in the / menu
body:
Code changes: +304 -16\
Tests: +217 -19\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The composer's `/` menu now shows each skill by a readable name instead of its invocation, and skill search ignores hyphens.

- Rows read `Better Interface`, `CE Plan`, `Remote Workflow`: a bright name, then a muted one-line description at the same size.
- A label the skill gives itself is used as written. The daemon reads it from the skill's `agents/openai.yaml` (`display_name`, `short_description`), the file Codex already uses, when an agent such as Claude lists only the folder name.
- Otherwise the slug reads as a title (`ce-plan` → `CE Plan`, `better-ui` → `Better UI`, `grill-me` → `Grill Me`). Words the author already cased are kept.
- Descriptions are cut to their first sentence, without Claude's `(user)`-style source tags; other parentheses such as `(PDF)` stay.
- `/runaofast`, `/run-ao-fast` and `/run_ao` find the same rows in the same order.

## Why

Pi-style agents list skills as `skill:<name>`, so the menu read `/skill:Better Interface`, while Claude's read `/ce-plan`. The orchestrator and session menus looked different for the same skills, and most rows were raw slugs followed by the model-facing trigger text. A skill named `run-ao-fast` was not found by typing `runaofast`.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `/skill:Better Interface  Cross-discipline interface review` (Pi-style agent) | `Better Interface  Cross-discipline interface review` |
| `/ce-ideate  Generate and evaluate grounded ideas. Use when the user as…` (Claude) | `CE Ideate  Generate and evaluate grounded ideas` |
| `/better-interface  Combines all of the better-* skills into a single review…` (Claude) | `Better Interface  Cross-discipline interface review` (from the skill's `openai.yaml`) |
| `/_gstack-command  Router for the gstack skill suite. (gstack) (user)` | `Gstack Command  Router for the gstack skill suite` |
| `/runaofast` shows no menu | `/runaofast` lists `Run AO Fast`, same as `/run-ao-fast` |
| Picked `skill:` chip reads `/skill:Better Interface` | Chip reads `/Better Interface`; the message still sends `/skill:Better Interface` |

## How

- **Display and invocation stay separate.** `Suggestion.value` (what a pick inserts), the chip's wire text, and the sent message are unchanged. Only `label`, `detail` and the chip's display text changed.
- **`composerSuggest.ts`**: `skillLabel` picks a provider label, else titles the slug after removing `skill:` and any plugin namespace. A namespace shows in the right-hand badge only when two rows would read the same (`ce-plan` vs `compound-engineering:ce-plan`). `looseScore` joins words for matching but remembers word starts, so `plan` still ranks `CE Plan` above a mid-word match; a native pre-check skips the per-character walk for non-matches.
- **`ComposerSuggestMenu.tsx`**: in the `/` menu the name is `text-foreground` and the description is muted at row size. `@` file rows are unchanged (folder stays `text-caption`). Row height, selection background and keyboard handling from #8313 are unchanged.
- **Daemon (`service/chat/skill_metadata.go`)**: when an agent gives no label, `Skills` finds the skill's folder in the session workspace's `.agents`, `.claude`, `.codex` skill folders, then the user's, then `~/.pi/agent/skills`, and reads `agents/openai.yaml` from that folder only. A project skill without the file keeps its listed name rather than borrowing a same-named user skill's. Names that are not a single path segment, including namespaced plugin skills, are skipped. Reads are capped at 64 KiB.

Trade-offs and omissions:

- The initialism list (`UI`, `PR`, `CE`, `QA`, `API`, `MCP`, …) is a fixed set; an unknown abbreviation reads as a capitalized word.
- For the skills that have an `openai.yaml`, the long description is replaced by its short one, as Codex already does, so description search for those skills covers the short text. Name search is unaffected.
- Plugin skills that live under Claude's plugin folders are not looked up; they get the titled slug.

## Testing

**Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.** The user tested the menu by hand in a dev build of this branch (Claude session).

Added or updated tests:
- `composerSuggest.test.ts`: `skill:` names vs. inserted value, titles from slugs, provider labels kept, plugin namespace badge on duplicates, first-sentence descriptions, hyphen-insensitive search with word-start ranking, empty-label fallback.
- `skill_metadata_test.go`: metadata lookup order, a project skill without metadata not borrowing a user skill's, `skill:` names, untouched names without metadata, rejected path-like and namespaced names.
- Composer, side-chat and `btw` e2e tests now find rows by their shown names.
