title: feat(palette): refresh Cmd+K with nested lists, menu parity and a shorter blank list
body:
Code changes: +1026 -220\
Tests: +365 -76\
Others: +74 -45

## What

Reworks Cmd+K so it's shorter when you open it, nests lists the way context menus do, and offers the same actions as the sidebar and tab menus.

**Blank list**
- On a project: that project's actions, under a heading with the project's icon and name. On a session: that session's main actions, under a heading with its sidebar status icon and title. Project actions, Copy branch and the rest of the session menu wait for a search.
- Needs attention follows the sidebar's alerts: first sessions that need you (input, failing CI, conflicts, changes requested), then review turns, newest first within each. Capped at 5.
- Projects, the full session list, PR numbers and Import chats only show when you search. **Go to project** and **Go to session** list them all.
- #7362's Recent sessions stays at the bottom. It skips the open session and anything Needs attention already shows.

**Nested lists**
- Theme, Color theme, Language, Terminal clicks and Chat send key open as lists with the current value checked. Arrowing through Color theme previews each theme.
- On/off settings (transparency, avatars, math, gestures, copy on select, sound, Developer mode, side chats, split panes, Stay Awake) are switch rows. They flip in place and the palette stays open.
- A session's actions are its right-click menu (`useSessionMenuEntries`), and Open in is a submenu. Rename happens in the input. Archive and Remove project ask first, as they do from the sidebar.
- A project's actions match its sidebar menu: new task, orchestrator, board, archived sessions, copy path, pin, settings, remove.
- → opens a row marked ›, and ← at the start of the input goes back.

**Search**
- Actions, general commands and settings come first, then sessions, projects and PRs. Past-session matches (#7362) come next, then files and chats. Enter runs the best match, wherever it sits.
- Matching is stricter. Keywords match at word starts only ("bug" no longer finds Developer mode via "debug"), and loose-letter matches must start at a word in the title.
- Chat hits are one row per chat, with its match count ("3 matches"), instead of one row per message.
- Text inside files is searched only from Go to file, not the main list.

**New rows:** chat ↔ terminal switch for the open session, Stay Awake, Notifications, Connect mobile, Automations, Artifacts, Usage, all archived sessions, Computer use settings.

**Removed:** stale settings rows that no longer match a settings page row, Toggle browser DevTools (only the main process can run it), and session-only shortcuts when no session is open. "Copy session path" now only shows for a local session.

## Why

The palette opened on a long mix of projects, sessions, PR numbers and settings. Enter often picked the first category, not the best match. Settings appeared as flat "Color Theme: Nord" rows. Several shortcut rows did nothing because main delivers those shortcuts on their own channels.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Blank Cmd+K lists projects, every session and PR numbers | Blank Cmd+K lists the open session's or project's actions and sessions that need attention; the rest wait for a search |
| "Color Theme: Nord", "Theme: Dark", ... as separate rows | Color theme › opens a list with the current theme checked and previews as you arrow |
| On/off settings jump to the settings page | Switch rows flip in place |
| ⌘N, previous/next session, previous/next tab, new/close terminal rows did nothing | They run, via `onDedicatedShortcut` |
| Each matching chat message is its own row | One row per chat with a match count |

No screenshots were requested. The user tested the flows by hand in the dev app against a copy of real data.

## How

- `lib/command-palette.ts`: a `session` group and `PaletteMenuView` (project actions, submenu, choices, rename, go-to). Also `menuEntryCommands`, `buildProjectActions`, `goToCommands`, `bestMatch`, the attention ranking from `getSessionRowMarker`, blank-list caps (`BLANK_GROUP_ROWS`), and the search group order.
- `lib/palette-registry.ts`: settings entries follow what the settings page shows (`when: "mac" | "developerMode"`), plus switch rows (`TOGGLES`) and choice lists (`CHOICES`). Shortcut rows marked `session` only show on a session page.
- `hooks/useAppShortcut.ts` `onDedicatedShortcut` and `hooks/useAppMenuCommand.ts` `runAppMenuAction`: shortcuts and menu actions that main delivers on their own channel also listen for the palette's in-renderer event. Before, running them from the palette did nothing.
- `stores/session-switch-store.ts`: `SessionView` publishes its chat ↔ terminal switch, so the palette offers it for the session on screen.
- Merged with main's #7362. Its Recent sessions and Past sessions groups are kept and placed as described above. `withoutChatHitsCoveredBySessionSearch` still drops chat rows for sessions that group already lists.

Areas worth a close look: the merge with #7362 in `CommandPalette.tsx` (`groups`), and the stricter `matchScore`.

title: feat(browser): offer to continue in Chrome when a site refuses the Browser panel
body:
Code changes: +505 -2\
Tests: +287 -1\
Others: +106 -0 (9 locales, agent skill doc) plus PR evidence images

Refs #7494

## What

When a site refuses AO's Browser panel, the panel says so in one line and offers **Continue in Chrome**, which opens that page in the person's own Chrome. Their sign-ins and passkeys live there, and Chrome mode agents work there too. The browser menu offers **Open in Chrome** for any page, so the way out exists even when detection misses.

![A site blocking the panel](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/8f3b95260a897885f3c48c708e7851fd24a1f0b8/docs/pr-evidence/continue-in-chrome/continue-datadome.png?raw=true)

## Why

Some sites reject embedded browsers: Cloudflare checks that never pass (#5945), bot walls (DataDome, Akamai), and Google refusing sign-in from embedded browsers. Today the person is simply stuck.

**Learning from #6919:** that PR handed a fixed list of sign-in and checkout sites to the system browser *before* they loaded. It was closed because Google sign-in already works in the panel, so pre-emptive handoff broke a working flow. This PR is **reactive**: it offers only after a site has actually refused this browser, and it never redirects by itself.

## How detection works (high precision by design)

The panel's existing main-frame `webRequest.onCompleted` listener (one per Electron session, already registered) classifies each finished top-level response (`shared/browser-site-block.ts`). Only signals sites send on purpose count; page text is never matched.

| Signal | Source | Offer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cf-mitigated: challenge` | Cloudflare's documented marker on every challenge page | only if the check **comes back** within 60 s, or is **still up after 10 s** |
| other `cf-mitigated` values | Cloudflare block | at once |
| 403/429 with `x-datadome` / `x-dd-b` | DataDome | at once |
| 403 from `server: AkamaiGHost` | Akamai Bot Manager | at once |
| `accounts.google.com` 403, `disallowed_useragent`, `/signin/rejected` | Google's embedded-browser policy | at once |

The grace period matters. Loading a real Cloudflare challenge page (`scrapingcourse.com/cloudflare-challenge`) in Electron 44 produced a `403 cf-mitigated: challenge` that **passed by itself** and loaded the real `200` page, so an immediate offer would have been a false alarm. Pages that are merely served by Cloudflare (`server: cloudflare`, e.g. `dash.cloudflare.com`, `example.com`) carry no `cf-mitigated` header and never trigger.

The offer clears as soon as the tab loads a page that works. It's per tab, shown only for the active tab, and only while the tab is still on the refusing host.

## UX

- **Placement:** one flat row under the tab strip, styled like the find row (DESIGN.md: no card, no shadow, sentence case). The page is pushed down, never covered. Icon, a one-line reason, one primary button, and a dismiss control.
- **Copy says why, in plain words:** "dash.example keeps asking to check you're human here.", "shop.example is blocking this browser.", "Google won't sign you in from this browser."
- **Names the real browser:** "Continue in Chrome" when Chrome is installed. Otherwise it uses the default browser's own name ("Continue in Firefox"), or "Continue in your browser".
- **After clicking:** the row says "Opened in Chrome" for 2.5 s, then folds away. On failure: "Couldn't open the page", with the button still there to retry.
- **Never nags:** dismissing hides the row for that site for the rest of the run; other sites still get it.
- **Menu:** "Open in Chrome" in Browser controls for any web page, with an app toast to confirm. It's disabled for blank pages and AO's own preview origins.
- **Agents:** `ao browser errors` reports `site-blocked: <host> refuses this browser (<reason>)` with source `browser-site`. The skill doc tells agents not to retry or work around it, but to tell the user, or use `ao browser target chrome` when Chrome mode is set up.

![Verification loop](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/8f3b95260a897885f3c48c708e7851fd24a1f0b8/docs/pr-evidence/continue-in-chrome/continue-verification.png?raw=true)
![Browser controls menu](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/8f3b95260a897885f3c48c708e7851fd24a1f0b8/docs/pr-evidence/continue-in-chrome/continue-menu.png?raw=true)

## How opening works

`main/user-browser.ts` opens the URL in Chrome, passing it as a process argument and never through a shell:
- macOS: `open -b com.google.Chrome <url>`
- Windows: `chrome.exe` from the registry's App Paths
- Linux: `google-chrome` / `google-chrome-stable`

If Chrome is missing or fails to start, it falls back to `shell.openExternal`. The main process reads the URL from the tab itself; the renderer only names the view. Only http(s) pages open, never `ao-preview-*.localhost`.

## Testing

**Automated (on this branch and on a combined branch with #8407 and #8408):**
- `shared/browser-site-block.test.ts` (6): each signal, case-insensitive headers, look-alikes that must not trigger (DataDome tag on a 200, AkamaiGHost 200, ordinary 403/429, `disallowed_useragent` on another host, non-web URLs), and `canOpenInUserBrowser`.
- `main/user-browser.test.ts` (6): macOS system and per-user Chrome, Windows App Paths, Linux, fallback naming, Chrome failing to start, and a URL with `&` and quotes passed intact.
- `main/browser-view-host.test.ts` (+5):
  - a check that passes is never offered
  - offered after the grace period, and at once on a loop
  - DataDome at once, plus the `browser-site` agent signal
  - cleared on a working page
  - opens the tab's own URL and refuses blank pages

title: SCM poll still waits on merged/closed PR reactions
body:
Follow-up to #7583 for #7057.

Merged/closed PR reactions are exempt from the shared 30s lifecycle budget. `dispatchObservations` still waits for them, and synchronous session termination can take Kill's detached 90s budget or longer for user cleanup. `StartTriggeredPollLoop` is serial, so the next provider poll cannot start during that wait. The 30–60s tick goal in #7057 is still unmet for terminal PRs.

title: fix(chat): stop the composer stealing focus from the field you clicked
body:
## Summary

Clicking the Browser address bar (or a terminal) while the Orchestrator window is in the background sent your typing into the chat composer instead of the field you clicked.

**Cause:** `ChatComposer` refocuses itself on every window `focus` / `visibilitychange`. When the click that activates the window has already focused another text field, the composer took focus straight back.

**Fix:** if an `input`, `textarea`, `select` or `contenteditable` element already has focus when the window regains focus, leave it there. The composer still refocuses when nothing (or only a button) has focus, so returning to the app still drops you into the composer.

## Evidence

Same dev build and data, before vs after. The Orchestrator window was in the background, I clicked the new-tab address bar once and typed `abc`. Renderer event log:

Before (`main`):
```
mousedown Browser URL → focusout Browser URL → focusin Message the agent → window-focus → keydown "Message the agent" a/b/c
```
Result: `abc` ended up in the chat composer.

After:
```
mousedown Browser URL → window-focus → focusin Browser URL → keydown "Browser URL" a/b/c
```
Result: `abc` in the address bar, composer empty.

## Tests

- New `ChatComposer.test.tsx` cases:
  - Focus stays in an address-bar input, a terminal textarea, or a contenteditable field when the window regains focus.
  - The composer still refocuses when a button held focus.
- The three new "leaves focus" cases fail without the fix and pass with it. `ChatComposer.test.tsx`: 230/230.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- Live-tested in a dev build as described above.

## Risk

Small. Only the window-focus refocus path changes. Opening or switching sessions still focuses the composer as before.

title: [Bug]: Codex chat never sends native image attachments — images downgrade to workspace files even though turn/start accepts input_image and the steer path already sends images
body:
# What went wrong?

In a **Codex chat session**, pasting/attaching an image does not put the image into the prompt. Because the Codex chat driver never declares an `images` capability, the composer downgrades every image to a **file written into the workspace** plus a text suffix — the agent receives *"Attached images (read these files in the workspace for visual context): - <path>"* and has to notice the pointer and open the file. The model never sees the image as part of the message.

By contrast, in a Claude Code chat session images that pass the ACP handshake go into the prompt as native image content.

The Codex app-server protocol itself accepts image input on `turn/start` (`input_image`), and AO's own Codex **steer** path already sends images natively — only the normal turn path doesn't. Additionally, the retry path hard-refuses native image blocks for Codex sessions ("image attachments are unsupported").

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Codex chat session.
2. Paste a screenshot (or attach an image) into the composer and send.
3. The delivered message ends with `Attached images (read these files in the workspace for visual context): - <path>` — the image is a workspace file the agent must open, not a native image part of the prompt.
4. Compare with a Claude Code chat session, where a handshake-negotiated image is embedded natively in the message.

## Expected

Codex chat should declare/negotiate image support and send pasted images as native image content — the protocol supports it, and the same driver already converts images on the steer path.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Verified against latest `main`: first reported on `3435361db9`, re-verified unchanged on `a8451c437c` (2026-11-15)

---

## Agent-collected evidence

Code audit of `canonical/main` @ `a8451c437c` (re-verified 2026-11-15), read-only `git show` / `git grep` against the remote branch. Code-level finding; not reproduced against a live Codex account.

1. The Codex driver's static capability map lists 21 capabilities and `ChatCapabilityImages` is not among them (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/driver.go:119-162`). Compare the Claude Code ACP driver, which negotiates images from the agent handshake (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/driver.go:1149`):
   ```go
   caps[ports.ChatCapabilityImages] = init.AgentCapabilities.PromptCapabilities.Image
   ```
2. The renderer keys the composer's native-image mode off exactly that capability (`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/SessionChatSurface.tsx:887`):
   ```tsx
   nativeImages={can(renderSnapshot, "images")}
   ```
3. Without it, the composer strips images into workspace files and appends the "Attached images (read these files in the workspace for visual context):" suffix (`ChatComposer.tsx:1673,1915`; the suffix is defined in `backend/internal/service/chat/find_message_text.go:12` and `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/messageAttachments.ts:8`).
4. The normal send path could not carry native images today even if the frontend sent them — `SendTurn` builds its `input` array from `msg.Text` only and never reads `msg.Content` (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go:347-361`, input built at line 360):
   ```go
   params := map[string]any{
       "threadId": c.threadID,
       "input":    []any{map[string]any{"type": "text", "text": msg.Text}},
   }
   ```
5. The protocol supports image input: `ContentItemTypeInputImage ContentItemType = "input_image"` (`codexappserver/codexproto/protocol.gen.go:1413`), `UserInputTypeImage` (`protocol.gen.go:5229-5231`), and the driver's own comment states *"Codex turn/steer accepts the same image URL input shape as turn/start"* (`codexappserver/steer.go:122-124`).
6. The steer path already converts image content natively (`codexappserver/steer.go:131-138`):
   ```go
   case "image":
       url := "data:" + item.MIMEType + ";base64," + item.Data
       input = append(input, codexproto.UserInput{Type: codexproto.UserInputTypeImage, URL: &url})
   ```
7. The retry path refuses native image blocks without the capability (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:1897-1899`):
   ```go
   if !capabilities.Has(ports.ChatCapabilityImages) {
       return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: image attachments are unsupported", ErrRetryUnsupported)
   }
   ```

### Duplicate check

Searched `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator` issues (open + closed) for "codex image" and "image paste chat". Nearest open issues are related but different: #6211 (Codex TUI→Chat **switch** blocked by draft misread / image-attachment checkpoint mismatch — a handoff problem) and #4427 (attachment UI hides delivery mode — related UI opaqueness, different gap). No existing issue covers the missing `images` capability itself.

### Possible direction (hypothesis, for maintainers to judge)

Mirror the bar the driver already used for steer ("advertised only after being driven against a live app-server"): verify a real `turn/start` carrying `input_image` against a live app-server, then declare `ChatCapabilityImages`, extend `SendTurn`'s input builder to convert image content the way `steerInput` already does, and keep the retry gate consistent.

title: fix(browser): read page text with a selector so --expect-text works
body:
## Summary

Every `ao browser act <target> --expect-text <text>` failed:

```
Missing arguments for: get text
Usage: agent-browser get text <selector>
```

Before dispatching, a text postcondition reads the page's text with `get` / `text` and no ref. `nativeArgumentsForAction` turned that into a bare `get text`, but agent-browser 0.38.1 (the version we package) requires a selector. With no ref, this now sends `get text body`. A plain `ao browser get text` with no ref is fixed by the same change.

```
$ agent-browser --json get text
{"error":"Missing arguments for: get text\nUsage: agent-browser get text <selector>","success":false,"type":"missing_arguments"}
$ agent-browser --json get text body
{"success":true,"data":{... "text":"Order placed\n\nThanks"}}
```

End to end in a dev build: an agent session ran

```
$ ao browser act "Ordinary 403 (needs sign-in)" --expect-text "You need to sign in"
Element matched; input dispatched: link [ref=e7]
Postcondition text: satisfied
```

title: [Feature]: Explainable live model and capability suggestions for delegation
body:
## Problem

An orchestrator choosing a worker has to judge which installed agent and model fit a task using information that changes over time: whether the CLI and model are usable on this account, the available context, task capabilities, and any spending constraints. A catalog entry alone does not prove that a model can be called or that a capability works through the selected harness. Picking by a model name also ages poorly.

## Proposed direction

Consider an opt-in, explainable suggestion before delegation. Reuse AO's existing model catalogs, readiness checks and context telemetry. Combine timestamped observations of CLI version, model availability and provider-reported context with user-supplied task requirements and model/cost preferences. Where supported and explicitly requested, a bounded live check could establish that a candidate answers or has a required tool capability. Present the suggested agent/model/effort, evidence sources and age, excluded alternatives and unknowns; let the operator choose or retain the existing settings.

Treat advertised context, effective session/compaction window, configured model, actually observed model and tested access as different facts. Treat a model's strengths as documented claims or measured results with a source, not facts established by listing it. A failed or unavailable probe should remain unknown. A refresh should not automatically send project content or incur a new provider charge without the user's choice.

This could start as a small read-only suggestion, with any automatic dispatch and provider-specific checks discussed separately.

## Alternatives and related work

Today users can choose harness/model/effort manually and inspect their own provider tools. AO already has provider model discovery, readiness checks and usage data; this proposal composes those rather than replacing them. The closed umbrella #3802 points to narrower issues, and #7056 covers a different decision: native subagents versus AO workers.

## Acceptance examples for discussion

- A candidate shown in a catalog but not probed is labelled as discovered, not verified usable.
- Unknown or stale context and capability data remain visible; an explicit choice is preserved.
- A task that requires a known capability does not silently treat an unknown capability as verified.
- Preview performs no model inference and sends no task content. Optional live probes disclose their target and cost context.
- Source, observation time and reasons are visible, with tests for stale data, no candidates and provider errors.

I searched existing issues and am willing to help implement a scoped version if maintainers agree.

title: [Feature]: Attach verification evidence to worker completion reports
body:
## Problem

A worker's completion report communicates a useful coordination claim, but an orchestrator may still need to find which checks were run, what they returned, and whether their results apply to the current commit. Existing PR/CI observations are useful for external checks, while local task-specific checks can be harder to associate with the report.

## Proposed direction

Consider an optional structured evidence reference on a worker report: check name, result, time, output reference, and the commit or artifact it applies to. Reuse existing CI and artifact information where possible. Preserve the existing semantics of `ao report --done`; missing evidence is unknown, and evidence for an earlier commit is stale.

Begin with reporting existing evidence. If command execution is proposed later, it should require explicitly trusted commands, bounded execution, and retrievable output; a worker-authored report must not cause arbitrary commands to execute automatically.

## Alternatives considered

Workers can put checks in a free-form report, and maintainers can inspect CI, but those records require manual correlation. This proposal does not replace CI or claim a successful command proves every requirement.

## Acceptance examples for discussion

- Pass, failure, timeout and not-run are distinct, with a retrievable output reference where available.
- A new commit does not present prior results as current.
- Existing reports, retries and delivery behavior remain compatible when no evidence is supplied.
- Restart and duplicate-delivery tests cover any durable evidence added.

I searched existing issues and am willing to help implement a scoped version if maintainers agree.

title: feat(browser): gate self-hosted remote browsers through the daemon; agents no longer hold the service token
body:
Stacked on #8426 (base: `ao/agent-orchestrator-248/approval-gate`). Closes the self-hosted remote-host bypass found in #8426: with `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL` set, `ao browser` went straight to the host's agent-browser service and never reached the approval gate.

## What changes

- **Agents' remote browser commands go through their own daemon.** New capability-checked route `POST /api/v1/browser/remote-commands`. The daemon describes the target through the browser service (snapshot refs for `@e` refs, a small read-only `eval` for the focused element or a CSS selector, page URL and title), runs the same classifier and gate as the desktop, and only then forwards the command with the service token.
- **Agents no longer hold the service token.** Sessions on a self-hosted host get `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL` but an empty `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_TOKEN`, so an agent can't skip the gate by calling the service directly. The daemon alone holds the token. Before this change the session manager put the token in every agent's environment.
- **Fail closed.** CLI with URL + capability but no token → daemon route only, with no fallback to the service; if the daemon isn't running, the command fails. A command that may need approval is refused (`BROWSER_APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE`) when the daemon has no gate. An unreachable service returns 503 `BROWSER_REMOTE_UNREACHABLE`.
- **The remote command set is wider than the desktop's**, so:
  - `click`/`dblclick <sel>`, `press`/`key Enter`, `keyboard … Enter`, `find … click` are described and classified like desktop actions.
  - `eval`/`js`, coordinate `mouse` commands, `batch`/`run`, and any command not on a read/navigate/fill allowlist **always ask** in Risky mode, as a new **Page script** category ("This runs JavaScript in the page, which can do anything the page can"). Always allow on this site covers it per site; Off mode skips it. A click whose element can't be identified also asks.
- **The app shows remote-host approvals with no steady load.** One verified SSE stream per connected host (`/api/v1/approvals/stream`, same probe as remote notifications); each event rereads that host's pending list. REST polling (15s) runs only while that host's stream is down. Decisions go through that host's client. A remote session's dock shows its own requests (keyed by host + session, so a local session with the same id is never confused with it). "Open session" goes to the remote session.
- **Config:** a session process (capability set, no token) loads config without the agent browser instead of failing on the missing token. The daemon's own check is unchanged.
- The agent guide `commands/browser-remote.md` says consequential commands and `eval` wait for the user. Nothing agent-facing used the token: it appears only in daemon config, the test env list and the historical PoC script (`experiments/remote-browser-poc`), and a person's own shell that holds the token still talks to the service directly.

AO Cloud's browser lives in the private control plane and stays a follow-up there.

## Tests (red → green)

- `service/browser/remote_test.go`: argument classifier (18 cases); deny never forwards; allow forwards exactly once; benign commands pass without asking; Enter in a card field asks with the payment reason; `eval` always asks; describe failure still asks; no gate means refused for gated commands while reads still work; capability checked; Off mode.
- `remote_http_test.go`: forwarder sends the token, files and args, and rejects a wrong token.
- `controllers/browser_test.go`: route OK / bad args / deny 403 / unreachable 503.
- `cli/browser_remote_test.go`: daemon mode forwards and writes returned files; a denial reaches the agent; no daemon means failure, with no direct call to the service.
- `config_test.go`: session-process config. `provision_test.go`: the token never reaches the agent, including a project-supplied one.
- Renderer: remote request in the global card decides on its host and opens the remote session; remote dock vs a local session with the same id; `connectRemoteApprovalStreams` opens one stream per host, refreshes only that host, and closes on disconnect.
- `go vet` + `go test` for approval, service/browser, httpd/..., cli, config, session_manager, daemon, skillassets: pass. `npm run typecheck`: only the pre-existing `CommandPalette.tsx:1468` error from main. Approvals, SessionView (+ remote), i18n and settings vitest: pass.

## Not verified live

No end-to-end run against a real self-hosted host. The coordinator owns the only dev instance on this laptop; I can send a script for a self-hosted host if one is available. The JSON shapes the daemon reads from the agent-browser service (`--json` output: `data.refs`, `data.url`, `data.title`, `data.result`) are tested with a fake. If a real service answers differently, describe falls back to asking (fail closed), so the risk is extra prompts, not missed ones.

title: fix(chat): show an annotation-only message as its annotation chip
body:
## Summary

A message sent with only a chat selection (Add to chat, no typed text) rendered badly:

1. **Filler text as the message.** The bubble read "Use the attached 1 chat excerpt(s) as context", the text the daemon writes for the agent when the message has no typed words.
2. **"excerpt" card.** When the queue carried the message into a running turn, the Steered row passed the excerpt to the generic attachment tile, which printed the block type "excerpt".
3. **No selected text.** That tile never read the excerpt's selection or comment.

#8340 made the steered case common: annotating while a send is in flight now works, so annotation-only messages get queued and carried into running turns more often.

## Changes

- Sent and steered messages draw annotations as the compact "N annotation" chip, right-aligned, matching the composer chip. Clicking it opens the existing popover with each selection and comment, and navigates to the source.
- Steered messages read the raw `excerpt` / `file_reference` blocks from the steer activity and no longer pass them to the generic tile.
- The filler text is hidden when annotations make up the whole message. The agent still receives it.
- Removed `ChatAnnotationSummary`'s large preview-tile mode; sent messages were its only user.

## Testing

- New test: a steer with the exact activity shape from the bug shows the chip, no filler text, no "excerpt" label, and the selected text in the popover.
- `vitest run src/renderer/components/chat`: 78 files, 2196 tests passing (before rebase); the three directly affected test files pass again after rebasing on current `main`.
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in renderer code. The only errors come from `packages/product-ui`, whose dependencies weren't installed in this worktree.
- Ran the desktop app from this branch against isolated data and sent annotation-only messages in a Chat session.

## Risks

- Placeholder detection matches the daemon's exact English filler strings. If the daemon changes that wording, the filler shows again (cosmetic only).

Tests: +55 -0\
Others: +9 -0

## What

Show a reviewer selector note when a saved model is absent from the fresh, provider-backed device catalog. Refs #6434; this is a limited warning and does not resolve the reported runtime-model identity problem.

## Why

A saved alias can remain visible even when the device catalog lists different model IDs. The note makes that mismatch visible without changing the saved configuration or claiming which model actually ran.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The saved `opus` alias appears without a catalog note. | `opus` appears with `(not in device catalog)` when a fresh provider catalog contains only `glm-5.3-flash`. |

Before and after screenshots were captured from the Electron app using an isolated fixture. Screenshot upload was interrupted; local capture paths are `outputs/reviewer-before.png` and `outputs/reviewer-after.png`. They are not committed to the repository.

## How

Only show the note for an explicit model in catalog selection mode with a nonempty, current, provider-sourced catalog and no warning or pending refresh. Suppress it for stale or uncertain catalogs and when a native mode is selected. Include an accessible description and localized strings.

The catalog is device-wide and can differ from a project-specific reviewer's provider. Absence from it is not proof of unavailability or of the model used at runtime. Reviewer-scoped discovery and alias resolution remain open. The issue author previously implemented a related warning in their fork: https://github.com/axisrow/agent-orchestrator/pull/66.

## Testing

- Focused reviewer and localization tests: 40 passed.

title: feat(review): run every configured reviewer and require all to approve
body:
Fixes the silent no-op described in Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#5465: `ao project set-config --reviewer` is repeatable and stores every reviewer, but the review engine only ever used `Reviewers[0]`.

## What changes
- **Selection list**: `projectReviewerSelections` returns every configured reviewer in order. Duplicate harnesses are collapsed, since a harness owns one review row per session. With no reviewer configured it returns the single inherited default, including main's fallback to the project's worker reviewer (`DefaultWorkerReviewer`).
- **Trigger loop**: `TriggerWithOptions` runs each configured reviewer one after another on the same PR heads. This happens when more than one reviewer is configured and there is no session-level or per-call reviewer choice. Each reviewer gets its own review row, terminal and runs, and these steps are scoped per reviewer:
  - starting one configured reviewer never releases another configured reviewer's pane, even an idle one
  - stale-run cleanup only cancels this reviewer's own runs when its pane is gone
  - planning and the same-commit checks only look at this reviewer's own passes, so one reviewer's approval or running pass never marks the head as done for another
- **Trigger options** fan out to every configured reviewer:
  - `Rerun`: each reviewer starts a fresh pass. A reviewer is still never started twice on one head at the same time.
  - `RejectReviewedHead`: a reviewer that already covers the head is skipped and is not reported as a failure. The trigger errors with `ErrHeadAlreadyReviewed` or `ErrReviewAlreadyRunning` only when every reviewer had nothing to start.
  - `PRURL`: every reviewer reviews only the targeted PR.
  - `InterfaceMode`: every reviewer launches in the requested surface.
- **Reviewer failures**: if a reviewer fails to start, its runs are recorded as failed and never count as approval. The other reviewers still start.
  - While another reviewer started a pass or is still running one, the trigger succeeds and lists the failure in `TriggerResult.ReviewerFailures`. The HTTP trigger response's `reviewerFailures` carries the same list.
  - A manual or agent trigger returns the failure as an error when no reviewer is reviewing.
  - Automatic sweeps keep the partial result, and the coordinator reports `reviewer_failed`.
  - The trigger always errors when no configured reviewer could be started or reused.
- **Legacy runs**: runs with no recorded harness belong to no reviewer when several are configured. They don't count toward any reviewer's plan, auto-review gating or same-commit checks. A reviewer's missing pane no longer cancels them as stale (`cancelStaleRunningRuns` takes an `includeLegacy` flag). Single-reviewer behaviour is unchanged.
- **Cancel**: main's Cancel already stops every running reviewer with a live pane, including a per-call override outside the configured set. On top of that, with several configured reviewers it also cancels the running passes of a configured reviewer whose pane is gone. Cancel still doesn't wait for the trigger lock. It records a per-worker cancel count first, and the trigger checks it around each reviewer. When a cancel lands mid-fan-out, the trigger interrupts the reviewer it just started and starts no further reviewer.
- **Combined verdict** (`PlanReviewers`), per PR head:
  - `changes_requested` if any reviewer requested changes
  - otherwise `running` while any reviewer is still running
  - otherwise `needs_review` while any reviewer has no approval for this head (none yet, failed, cancelled, or an approval of an older commit)
  - `up_to_date` only when every reviewer approved this exact head
- **API**: `PRReviewState.reviewers` lists each reviewer's harness, status and latest run. It is only set when more than one reviewer applies. List, Trigger and Cancel return the combined verdict, and the combined trigger result carries the first started reviewer's `reviewerSurface`. Both new fields (`reviewers`, `reviewerFailures`) are additive. Regenerated `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.
- **Auto-review**: the coordinator now checks every configured reviewer against its own runs and triggers all of them. Before, it passed `Reviewers[0]` as an explicit override, so auto-review could never reach the multi-reviewer path.

Single-reviewer projects and sessions with a reviewer preference behave as before.

## Not in this PR
- `SwitchReviewer`, `RestoreReviewer` and `TerminateReviewer` are unchanged and still act on one reviewer at a time.
- `SessionReviews.reviewerHandleId`/`reviewerHarness` and the legacy `TriggerResult.Run` field still report a single reviewer. The renderer does not show the per-reviewer breakdown or `reviewerFailures` yet.
- `domain.ResolveReviewerHarness` still returns `Reviewers[0]`, which is the right answer for single-reviewer callers.

## Tests
- `internal/review/multi_reviewer_test.go`
  - Selection and the basic fan-out:
    - building the selection list, and its fallback (`TestProjectReviewerSelections*`)
    - one reviewer behaves as before (`TestTriggerSingleConfiguredReviewerUnchanged`)
    - every reviewer runs on the same head (`TestTriggerRunsEveryConfiguredReviewerOnSameHead`)
    - a session preference keeps a single reviewer (`TestTriggerSessionReviewerPreferenceKeepsSingleReviewer`)
  - Verdicts and new commits:
    - one approval doesn't count for the other reviewer (`TestTriggerOneReviewerApprovalDoesNotSatisfyTheOther`)
    - only the reviewer that requested changes runs again (`TestTriggerReRunsOnlyReviewerThatRequestedChanges`)
    - a new commit sends every reviewer back to review, and one arriving mid-review replaces both stale passes (`TestTriggerNewHead*`)
  - Panes:
    - one reviewer's running pass isn't cancelled when another starts (`TestTriggerDoesNotCancelOtherReviewersRunningPass`)
    - another configured reviewer's idle pane is kept (`TestTriggerKeepsAnotherConfiguredReviewersIdlePane`)
  - Options:
    - `TestRerunFansOutToEveryConfiguredReviewer`
    - `TestRejectReviewedHeadStartsOnlyReviewerThatOwesReview`
    - `TestRejectReviewedHeadErrorsWhenEveryReviewerReviewed`
    - `TestTargetedPRFansOutToEveryConfiguredReviewer`
    - `TestInterfaceModeFansOutToEveryConfiguredReviewer`
  - Failures:
    - `TestTriggerReviewerFailureDoesNotBlockOthersOrApprove`
    - `TestTriggerErrorsWhenEveryReviewerFails`
    - `TestTriggerErrorsWhenOnlyOwingReviewerFails`
    - `TestTriggerReportsFailureWhenOtherReviewerStillRunning`
    - `TestAgentRerunReportsFailureWhileOtherReviewerStillRunning`
    - `TestAutoTriggerReportsFailingReviewerAloneOwingWork`
  - Cancel:
    - `TestCancelStopsEveryRunningConfiguredReviewer`
    - `TestCancelSingleReviewerUnchanged`
    - `TestCancelStopsPerCallReviewerOutsideConfiguredSet`
    - `TestCancelDuringFirstReviewerLaunchStopsFanOut`
    - `TestCancelBeforeNextReviewerLaunchStopsThatReviewer`
  - Legacy runs and surface:
    - `TestAutoTriggerIgnoresLegacyRunsWithSeveralReviewers`
    - `TestTriggerReportsReviewerSurfaceForConfiguredReviewers`
- `internal/review/combined_verdict_test.go`: table-driven combined-verdict rules, plus List and Trigger reporting the combined state.
- `internal/autoreview/coordinator_test.go`: auto-review gating with several reviewers, and `reviewer_failed` on a partial failure.
- `internal/httpd/controllers/reviews_test.go`: the trigger response carries `reviewerFailures` while another reviewer started.
- All Go CI jobs pass on the current head: lint, codegen-drift, the three `backend-core` shards and `storage-race`.

title: fix(reviews): show every PR comment and render CodeRabbit's HTML
body:
## What The session inspector's **Reviews** tab now lists every comment on the PR: inline comments from people and bots, plus top-level PR comments, next to each review's summary. CodeRabbit's reviews also render properly now instead of showing raw HTML. ## Why it was broken - **Bot inline comments were missing.** The backend PR summary (`summarizeReview` in `pr_summary.go`) skips `IsBot` comments, so `unresolvedBy`/`resolvedBy` never include CodeRabbit. A CodeRabbit review showed its summary with no comments under it. - **Top-level comments were never read.** The Reviews tab ignored `pr.conversation`, so CodeRabbit's walkthrough and people's PR notes didn't appear. - **HTML was printed as text.** The Reviews tab printed ``, `
` and `` literally. Inline comment rows showed raw source, and `PRMarkdown` flattened every `
` into one run of text. ## How - **Frontend only.** `unresolvedBy` also drives board counts, so the backend summary is unchanged. The new `lib/pr-review-comments.ts` builds the extra rows from the PR's stored `threads` and `conversation`: - Bot threads are grouped under that bot's review. A thread already listed in the summary is not repeated. - Bot rows never auto-inject review comments into the agent. - Top-level comments are listed as "commented" entries. - **HTML rendering.** The new `lib/github-html.ts` renders with `rehype-raw` plus `rehype-sanitize` using GitHub's own allowlist, minus `picture`/`source`. - Chat's existing config is shared from the same module. - Icon-sized images with no alt text are dropped, which removes CodeRabbit's decorative badges. - `
`, `
`, tables, `` and checkboxes get the matching styles. - **Inline comments.** A row previews as plain words via `commentTextLines` and expands to rendered markdown. Collapsed review bodies are height-capped so tables and `
` stay short. ## Before / after Tested in the real desktop app, running this checkout against isolated scratch data, on a real PR with CodeRabbit and github-actions reviews (#8395). That PR was used read-only: nothing was pushed or posted to it. **Before.** Raw HTML in the summary, no inline comments, no walkthrough. **After.** A clean summary, CodeRabbit's 4 open comments, and the github-actions table capped. **After, CodeRabbit's open comments.** Clean previews; an expanded comment renders as markdown. **After, top-level comments.** The CodeRabbit walkthrough shows with its collapsible sections. ## Tests - `frontend`: `PRMarkdown.test.tsx` (details, sanitize, icons), `SessionInspector.test.tsx` (bot inline and top-level comments listed), and the new `pr-review-comments.test.ts`. All pass. - `packages/product-ui`: `commentTextLines` and the expandable inline comment. 177/177 pass. The full frontend suite timed out locally on an overloaded machine, so I ran the affected files directly. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * GitHub review comments now display formatted Markdown, including expandable details sections and supported images. * The Reviews tab now includes bot-authored review threads and top-level conversation feedback, with resolved and unresolved threads grouped separately. * Expanded inline comments show formatted content, with clearer previews for longer comments. * **Bug Fixes** * Decorative icons in review comments no longer appear as openable images, and unsupported or unsafe markup is not displayed. * Blank top-level comments and comments from the pull request author are excluded from conversation feedback.

title: fix(lifecycle): serialize orchestrator restore admission with spawn
body:
Code changes: +36 -1  
Tests: +412 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Make project orchestrator restore use the same admission gate as orchestrator spawn/replacement. Reject restoring a different archived orchestrator while that project already has a live one, using the existing `ORCHESTRATOR_ALREADY_ACTIVE` conflict code.

This is a narrow, reproducible lifecycle defect relevant to #3921. It does **not** resolve that composite issue, add a global/per-project worker limit, or establish the cause of the original macOS incident. Historical #3987 and #5649 were closed without merging; this patch was written against current source rather than cherry-picking either branch. Related open #7387 handles the superseded native-chat owner at another layer; this change protects service admission across distinct archived session IDs and spawn/restore callers.

Tested base: `53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e`. Candidate: `3dcec6549cd56d2bd7943f6c18e904ef633058c2`. Main advanced to `2504f058e233abaddc56d4146fff5bd78556a244` during verification; the two subsequent commits touch neither changed file. No UI, API schema, storage schema, owner-specific settings, or packaging changes are included.

## Why

`Spawn`/`SpawnOrchestrator` protect the one-live-orchestrator-per-project invariant with a service-level project mutex. `Restore` previously called `Manager.RestoreWithMode` directly. The manager's per-session gate cannot serialize two different archived orchestrator IDs, or an archived restore competing with a new spawn in the same project.

The deterministic service regression harness reproduces the gap on the tested base. These are fake manager operations and in-memory session records, **not** real provider processes or a captured workstation crash.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| 64 concurrent restores of distinct archived orchestrator records in one project admit 64 and leave 64 active records in the deterministic harness. | Exactly 1 is admitted and 63 receive `ORCHESTRATOR_ALREADY_ACTIVE`; stages 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 40, and 64 obey the same invariant. |
| Restore can bypass a concurrent orchestrator spawn/replacement reservation. | Both paths hold the existing project gate through publication of the live record. |
| An archived coordinator can be restored beside a live successor. | Restore fails before invoking the manager for that archived coordinator. |
| Worker restores and restores in unrelated projects operate independently. | Those paths remain independent; missing and same-live-session errors retain manager behavior. |

## How

- Read the target record to identify project orchestrators; preserve the existing manager path for workers, missing records, and records without a project.
- Acquire the existing per-project gate, then check cancellation and enumerate active orchestrators.
- Reject a different active ID; otherwise call `RestoreWithMode` while holding the gate. Deferred unlock covers every error/success path.
- Fail closed if the session store cannot establish admission state. No workspace, terminal, or runtime is created on a rejected restore.

Tests cover both orchestrator modes, concurrent restore/spawn in both directions, replacement, unrelated projects, workers, a terminated successor, unchanged missing/same-live errors, store failure, failed restore, cancellation, and deadline expiration. Cancellation is checked after acquiring the existing mutex; this patch does not make the mutex wait itself interruptible.

## Testing

| Environment / command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Linux, Go 1.27.4: same new regression file applied to untouched base, `go test ./internal/service/session -run '^TestRestoreOrchestrator' -count=1` | Expected FAIL; reproduces the duplicate-admission defect. |
| Linux candidate: focused regressions | PASS. |
| Linux candidate: `go test -race ./internal/service/session -run '^TestRestoreOrchestrator' -count=20` | PASS, 7.673 s. |
| Linux candidate: full `./internal/service/session` suite | PASS, 22.371 s. |
| Linux candidate: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` | PASS. |
| Linux candidate: golangci-lint v2.14.0, bounded retry | PASS, exit 0, `0 issues.` |
| Windows 11 x64, Go 1.27.4: focused restore regressions, `-count=20` | PASS, 3.292 s. |
| Windows candidate: full service/session suite | FAIL in three existing tests; all three reproduce on untouched base: CRLF expectation in verified-SHA checkout, unreadable-workspace permission assumption, and unavailable symlink privilege. |
| Native Windows frontend `npm run typecheck` | PASS. No frontend files changed in this PR. |

Full validation is **not complete**. The Linux full-backend race attempt used the workflow's modernc compiler exclusion and encountered environment failures, then the runner was killed (exit -9). Representative failures in the three affected packages reproduce on untouched base: prohibited AF_UNIX sockets in `fx/herdr`, a missing fake hook `events.log` in the lifecycle package, and an inherited XDG config-path assumption in the OpenCode adapter. A supported CI runner must verify the full suite. Windows `-race` was not run because a supported CGO C compiler is unavailable; no privilege or security-policy changes were made to force tests through. Renderer/Electron end-to-end and other full-repository jobs are not claimed passed locally.

Reproduce the regression in an isolated checkout using the candidate test file against the base, then run the same command on the candidate:

```sh
git worktree add ../ao-3921-baseline 53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e
git show 3dcec6549cd56d2bd7943f6c18e904ef633058c2:backend/internal/service/session/orchestrator_restore_test.go > ../ao-3921-baseline/backend/internal/service/session/orchestrator_restore_test.go
cd ../ao-3921-baseline/backend
go test ./internal/service/session -run '^TestRestoreOrchestrator' -count=1
```

On the candidate, repeat with `-race -count=20`. All focused tests use fakes and consume zero model turns. There is no incident screenshot for this nonvisual regression; the numeric before/after comparison is synthetic test output.

Please review the invariant and coordination with #7387. Maintainer CI, including the Windows lane (`ci:full` if appropriate), is still required. This PR contains no data migration; rollback is an ordinary revert of the one commit, with the original admission gap returning. No production installation or upstream merge was performed.

## Checklist

- [x] One scoped lifecycle defect; conventional commit; existing error code reused.
- [x] Deterministic regression fails on the tested base and passes on the candidate.
- [x] Focused repeated race checks, full Linux service suite, build, vet, and lint pass.
- [x] Native Windows focused checks pass; baseline failures disclosed.
- [x] No API/storage contract changes requiring regeneration.
- [x] Public patch contains no host logs, credentials, private paths, or local safety defaults.
- [ ] Full remote CI green and maintainer review complete.
- [ ] Supported Windows race / broader native lifecycle coverage verified.

title: fix(docs): ignore language cookies for languages the docs do not serve
body:
## Problem

Clicking **Docs** on orchestrator.inc could open the docs with **Français** selected. The landing's footer language menu writes `ao_locale` for `domain=orchestrator.inc` (1 year). The docs' head script and switcher accepted any of the 17 interface catalogs in `SUPPORTED_LOCALES`, including `fr`. Articles exist only in en, ja and zh-CN. So one French pick on the landing left the docs picker on Français and `<html lang="fr">` on English pages.

Picking English in the docs didn't fix it either. The docs wrote a host-only `ao_locale=en` next to the landing's domain `fr`, the browser sent both, and the reader used the first one. After a reload the page was French again (reproduced, see captures).

## Fix

- **Served locales come from content.** The served list is `[DEFAULT_LOCALE, ...translatedLocales()]`, computed in `siteLayout`. That is English plus every language with translated articles, so today `en`, `ja`, `zh-CN`. It is passed to the inline head script, `Providers` and the 404 page. No new hard-coded list. `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` remains the interface-catalog list for Lingui and Fumadocs.
- **Anything else falls back to English** in the head script (`<html lang>` stays `en`, no redirect), in the switcher, and on the 404 page.
- **The switcher offers only served languages.** Otherwise picking Français would save a value the docs then ignore.
- **Reading duplicates is deterministic.** `findCookieValue` scans every `ao_locale` in header order and returns the first *served* value. Before, it stopped at the first `ao_locale` even when that value was unusable. An unserved landing value like `fr` can no longer hide a served one, and surrounding quotes (`"ja"`) are accepted. Empty, malformed or case-mismatched values are ignored.
- **A docs choice replaces the landing's value.** On `orchestrator.inc` and its subdomains, `localeCookieWrites` writes `domain=orchestrator.inc; path=/`. That is the same name, domain and path key as the landing's cookie, so it overwrites it instead of sitting beside it. It also expires the legacy host-only cookie that older docs builds wrote, and adds `secure` on https. On localhost, IPs and preview hosts a domain cookie would be rejected, so the docs keep a host-only cookie there. The shared domain is derived from `COMPANY.MARKETING_URL`.

### Why the shared domain scope
Only a cookie with the landing's own key (name + `domain=orchestrator.inc` + `path=/`) can replace the landing's value. A host-only docs cookie always coexists with it, and the browser sends both in an order that depends on creation time. Writing at the shared scope also means a docs choice of English, 日本語 or 简体中文 carries back to the landing. That is consistent with it being one shared preference.

## Effect on the landing and on ja / zh-CN
- The landing keeps reading and writing the same cookie. The docs only write the three languages they serve, which the landing presumably also supports. Assumption: the landing writes with `path=/`; if it uses another path, the docs' write would not replace it.
- `ja` and `zh-CN` behave as before: a saved choice redirects translated pages to `/ja/…` and `/zh-CN/…`, and untranslated pages show that interface around the English article.

## Intentional scope change
The docs language menu no longer lists the 14 interface-only languages (Français, Deutsch, 한국어, …). Those catalogs and the Lingui setup are untouched, so adding articles in a language (for example `page.fr.mdx`) brings it back automatically through `translatedLocales()`.

## Tests
- `src/i18n/locales.test.tsx` (new): served ja/zh-CN/en; unserved fr/de; near misses, wrong case, empty, no separator, lone quote, bad percent-encoding, longer cookie name; quoted values; duplicates in both orders, mixed with unserved; the parser still works when inlined; cookie writes for docs/apex/https vs localhost, IP, preview host and a lookalike domain.
- `src/i18n/saved-locale-script.test.tsx`: unserved languages leave `lang=en` with no redirect, zh-CN redirects, and a served duplicate wins over landing `fr`.
- `src/components/providers.test.tsx` (new): the switcher shows English with `<html lang=en>` for fr, de and garbage cookies, shows 日本語/简体中文 for served cookies, lists only en/ja/zh-CN, and picking a language saves it.
- `npx vitest run`: 5 files, 45 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean, `check:translations` passes, `npm run build` (Node 24) succeeds.

## Browser verification
Static export served locally. Headless Chromium maps `docs.orchestrator.inc` to it, so domain and host-only cookies behave as in production.

| Cookie | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| landing `fr` (domain), `/cli/` | Français, lang=fr | English, lang=en |
| landing `fr` (domain), `/` | Français, lang=fr | English, lang=en |
| host-only `fr`, `/cli/` | Français, lang=fr | English, lang=en |
| localhost `fr`, `/cli/` | Français, lang=fr | English, lang=en |
| landing `fr`, then host-only `ja` | Français, lang=fr | 日本語, lang=ja |
| `ja` (domain), `/` | → `/ja/` | → `/ja/` |
| `zh-CN` (domain), `/cli/` | 简体中文, lang=zh-CN | 简体中文, lang=zh-CN |
| host-only `ja` + domain `fr`, pick **English**, reload | jar `.orchestrator.inc=fr`, `docs…=en` → **Français** | jar `.orchestrator.inc=en` only → English |
| same start, pick **日本語**, reload | two cookies left | jar `.orchestrator.inc=ja` only → 日本語 |

Not deployed.

title: Session sidebar says commits are not pushed when a claimed PR's branch lives on a fork
body:
Reported by the user while a worker session was continuing a contributor's fork PR (#6138). The session inspector's right sidebar showed "6366 uncommitted files +868701 −222066" and "2 commits not pushed +435 −35", with a "Commit & push to #6138" button. The user didn't understand what the sidebar was showing: those commits were already on the PR.

Screenshot: available locally to the reporter.

title: fix(session): count commits on a fork PR's head as pushed
body:
## Summary

Part of #8460.

When a session continues a PR whose head lives on a contributor's fork (here #6138, claimed with `ao session claim-pr`), the local branch has no `origin/<same name>` ref. In that case `reconcileBranchTarget` set `Unpushed = Commits`, so the inspector showed "N commits not pushed" and kept offering "Push to #6138" for commits that were already the PR head on GitHub.

Now, when no same-named origin branch exists, branch state checks the session's open PRs. If one's recorded `HeadSHA` is the local tip, or one of its ancestors, that PR's head counts as the pushed point:
- `RemoteBranch` is `pr-<number>/<source branch>`. The frontend reads the part after the first `/` and matches it against the PR's `sourceBranch`.
- `RemoteHead` is the PR head.
- `Unpushed` counts only the commits after the PR head.

A PR at a commit the branch doesn't contain (another branch's PR) doesn't count. Branches that have a same-named origin branch keep the existing path. The PR head is part of the reconcile fingerprint, so a new push to the fork updates the state.

## Tests

- New test `TestReconcileSessionBranchStateCountsAForkPRHeadAsPushed` covers three cases: a fork PR at the local head (0 unpushed), one new local commit (1 unpushed), and an unrelated PR head on another branch (all commits unpushed). **It fails on `main`** with `Unpushed:2`, no `RemoteBranch`, which is the reported sidebar state, and passes with the fix.
- `go test ./internal/service/session/` passes; `go build ./...` and `go vet` are clean.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Branches with no origin ref now do one `ListPRsBySession` read per reconcile, plus a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` per open PR whose head isn't the local tip.
- The "6366 uncommitted files" row in the report was a merge that was staged but not yet committed when the screenshot was taken, so it isn't a bug.

title: fix(lifecycle): don't inject the PR author's own thread replies
body:
## What

A worker's own replies to review comments are no longer sent back to it as new review feedback.

## Why it happened

The worker runs `gh` with the PR author's account. So when it answers a review thread ("Fixed in abc123…"), GitHub stores that reply as one more comment in the thread, written by the PR author. The review-comment nudge in `lifecycle/reactions.go` filters comments only by resolved state and bot anchoring, never by author. Any poll that ran between the worker posting a reply and resolving the thread therefore saw "a new unresolved comment" and injected the worker's own words back into it.

This happened on #8454. Its stored comments show every `Fixed in …` reply from the PR author as the second comment in a reviewer's thread, and each one was sent back to the worker as "1 unresolved review comment".

## Fix

The new `withoutPRAuthorReplies` drops **replies** in review threads that are written by the PR's author (`pr.Author`, matched case-insensitively with a leading `@` ignored).

- **A thread the author starts is still delivered.** The worker shares the human's GitHub account, so an inline comment the human leaves on their own PR is still feedback for the worker.
- **`[bot]` stays part of the name**, so a `worker-account[bot]` app is not mistaken for `worker-account`.
- **If the PR's author isn't known yet**, nothing is filtered.
- **Comments arrive oldest first**, so a thread's root is the first comment seen for its `ThreadID`.

**Trade-off:** a reply the human types from the PR author's account inside someone else's thread is also skipped. The author can't be told apart from the worker on GitHub. A new thread, or a top-level review, still reaches the worker.

## Tests

- `TestPRObservation_PRAuthorRepliesAreNotInjected` covers four cases:
  - The author's reply is skipped.
  - A reviewer's root comment and another person's reply are still sent.
  - A thread the author starts is still sent.
  - A same-named `[bot]` app's comments are still sent.
- `TestWithoutPRAuthorRepliesKeepsEverythingWhenAuthorUnknown`.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/lifecycle/`, and `go test ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/observe/scm/... ./internal/service/pr/...` all pass.

title: [Feature]: search settings from the top of the Settings rail
body:
### Problem

The desktop app's Settings page has no search. To change a setting you have to know which page it lives on and click through the rail (General, Harness, Browser, Mobile, Updates…) until you find it. General alone holds 20+ rows, so even the right page needs scrolling. The only way to find a setting by name today is ⌘K, which leaves Settings and is not where people look while they are already in it.

### Proposed direction

A search field at the top of the Settings rail, above the section list:

- Typing replaces the section list with the settings that match, each with the page it is on ("Copy on select · General").
- Matching uses the same settings index and ranking as the ⌘K palette (`lib/palette-registry.ts`), so synonyms work ("dark mode" → Theme) and the two never drift apart. Pages the index does not name still match by their rail label.
- Picking a result (click, or ↑/↓ + Enter) opens its page, scrolls to the row and briefly highlights it, as palette deep links already do.
- Escape clears the query first, then closes Settings as before.
- Only pages currently shown in the rail are searched.
- With the sidebar collapsed, a search icon expands it and focuses the field.

### Alternatives considered

- Filtering rows in place on a single "all settings" page: hides rows by DOM text and fights React re-renders.
- A search field in the page topbar with a dropdown: duplicates the rail's job and needs its own popover.

title: fix(chat): open existing chats with the composer docked, not centered then dropped
body:
Code changes: +17 -2\
Tests: +21 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Opening the Orchestrator chat, or any session chat that already has history, now shows the composer docked at the bottom at full width on the first frame. Before, it first rendered centered and narrow, like a new chat, then slid down and widened once the history loaded.

## Why

While a session's conversation is read, `SessionChatSurface` shows a stand-in snapshot with no items (the Orchestrator on a cold open, and any chat arriving from the terminal). `ChatWorkspace` read that stand-in as an empty chat, so it centered the composer at `max-w-2xl`. When the real history landed, the docking motion (500 ms) and the `max-width` transition both played.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Open the Orchestrator after a relaunch: composer appears centered, then slides down and widens | Composer is at the bottom, full width, from the first frame; nothing moves when the history arrives |
| Switch a chat over from the terminal (session without a recorded user prompt): centered, then drops | Docked from the first frame |
| /new page: centered with the welcome heading | Unchanged |
| Orchestrator still being created: centered with sample prompts | Unchanged |

## How

- `SessionChatSurface` passes a new `historyUnread` prop while the stand-in is on screen for an existing session (not the shell fallback, and not a session still being created).
- `ChatWorkspace` reads it once at mount. For that mount the chat is never treated as empty, so the composer is docked and full width from the start, and the docking motion and width transition have nothing to animate.
- An empty transcript renders nothing above the composer, so the column is bottom-aligned whenever the chat opened docked, as a terminal arrival already did.
- `historyPending` (cloud) is unchanged. It also brings the "Restoring your conversation" arrival chrome, which a plain open should not show.

**Trade-off:** an existing session that turns out to have no messages, opened before its history is read, stays docked. It doesn't show the welcome heading or sample prompts, rather than jumping back to the center. The /new page and an Orchestrator still being created open centered as before.

## Testing

Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.

New `ChatWorkspace` test: a chat opened with `historyUnread` is docked and bottom-aligned with no arrival chrome, stays docked once read empty, and shows no docking motion once messages arrive.

Manual checks for a reviewer (quit and relaunch first so nothing is cached):
1. Open a project's Orchestrator chat that has history. The composer is at the bottom from the first frame, with no centered box sliding down or widening.
2. Open a worker chat with history, and switch a worker from Terminal to Chat. Same: no drop.
3. Open /new. Centered with the welcome text. Send a brief: one slide down on that page, nothing moves when the session opens.

title: feat(cloud-contract): let share links include a page's images
body: Code changes: +131 -2 (handwritten Cloud contract)\ Tests: +0 -0\ Others: +113 -2 (generated cloud-client types) ## What Adds the Cloud API contract for share links that also serve the files an HTML page refers to by relative path (images and other assets; video is refused with 415, as for a link's own file): - `POST /me/artifact-shares/uploads/files` (`createArtifactShareFileUpload`): starts the upload of one included file under the page's upload token, at a relative `path`. - `POST /me/artifact-shares/uploads/files/complete` (`completeArtifactShareFileUpload`): finishes it and returns a `fileToken`. - `finalizeArtifactShare` takes an optional `files: [{fileToken}]`, at most 200. If `files` is absent, an active link keeps its files; an empty list clears them. - `ArtifactShare.fileCount`. - Documents the `/~vt//` path: when a private page with files is opened at `contentUrl` with `?vt=`, it is redirected there, so relative URLs carry the token. ## Why A shared HTML page loses its photos today: only the `.html` file is uploaded, and the share host serves only `/` and `/raw`, so `` returns 404. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | A link serves one file; any other path on its host returns 404 | A link can also serve up to 200 included files at their relative paths, with range requests; video paths get 415 | | No way to upload a page's assets | `uploads/files` + `uploads/files/complete`, listed in `finalize.files` | | Private links carry the view token only in `?vt=`, which relative URLs drop | A private page with files is redirected to `/~vt//`; `contentUrl` itself is unchanged | ## How - Everything is additive. `oasdiff breaking` against `main` reports no breaking changes. Older desktops never send `files`, and a link they republish keeps its files. - `contentUrl` keeps its current shape, because the production viewer only accepts `https://./` or that URL plus `?vt=`. The share host handles the redirect. - There is no size cap on included files, matching the existing no-size-limit rule for share links. The count limit is 200. - The control-plane implementation is in a separate PR in the private repo. The desktop changes (scanning the HTML and uploading the referenced files) come in a later PR. ## Testing - `cd packages/cloud-client && npm run generate && npm run typecheck && npm test`: schema regenerated with the pinned openapi-typescript 7.4.4, typecheck clean, 34/34 tests pass. - `oasdiff breaking` (v1.34.1, as in `cloud-contract-compat.yml`) against `origin/main`: no breaking changes. - The control plane's route-parity test passes against this contract. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense (contract only; behavior tests are in the control-plane PR) - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Artifact shares now support uploading files referenced by an HTML page, with separate upload and completion steps. * Finalizing a share can include up to 200 uploaded files. title: perf(chat): scope ::highlight() rules to the elements their ranges are in
body:
Code changes: +17 -9\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Every `::highlight()` rule now applies only inside the element its highlight ranges are in, instead of to the whole page. There are six rules: chat annotations, chat find and the artifact text selection.

## Why

Scrolling a session's Artifacts tab (right inspector) with no saved previews got about 9% slower after #8339 sped it up. A bisect over the 46 renderer commits since #8339 found #8340 (`cd19f93e9b`), and splitting that commit showed the cause is the two global rules it added to `styles.css`: `::highlight(chat-annotations)` and `::highlight(chat-annotation-draft)`. #8340's JavaScript isn't involved.

A Chrome trace of the scroll shows why. The browser checks every global `::highlight()` rule against every element on each style recalc, even when no highlight is registered. With the two new rules, the same number of style recalcs took about 33% longer (6.4 s vs 4.8 s over the trace), and layout about 28% longer. Paint barely changed. Each rule on its own cost about half of the drop.

## Before / After

No user-visible change. The highlights look the same; the session page does less work.

Each of the six highlights was painted over the same text inside its real container, in both builds, in dark and light themes: all 12 crops are pixel-identical between `main` and this branch.

**Scrolling the session's Artifacts tab, 300 artifacts, no saved previews** (median of 5 runs; higher is better):

| | #8339 merge (`b9d60e0ad6`) | `main` (`e3a90f708e`) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First pass | 102 fps | 92 fps | **112 fps** |
| Later passes | 108 fps | 104 fps | **117 fps** |
| Slowest downward pass, any run | 98 fps | 87 fps | **109 fps** |
| JS heap after a forced GC | 41 MB | 42 MB | 42 MB |

This PR scrolls faster than #8339 did, because the four rules that predate #8340 (`chat-annotation`, `artifact-selection` and the two chat find rules) are scoped too.

Other cases changed by less than run-to-run noise (median of 3 runs):

| Case | #8339 merge | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Click the Artifacts tab, no saved previews: all visible cards drawn | 205 ms | 196 ms | 187 ms |
| Scroll the tab, every preview saved | 120 fps | 120 fps | 120 fps |
| Scroll the Artifacts page, no saved previews | 120 fps | 120 fps | 120 fps |
| `cloud.getSession` calls per click | 1 | 1 | 1 |

The scroll stress test moves 120 px per frame, and headless Chromium on this machine tops out near 120 fps, so cases at 120 are at the ceiling.

Peak JS heap during the tab scroll is higher on this branch (median 135 MB vs 110 MB on `main`). After a forced GC both are 42 MB. The difference is garbage not yet collected, because a faster scroll mounts cards sooner.

## How

- The four chat highlights and chat find apply only under `[data-chat-find-surface]`, the chat timeline wrapper that main and side chats already share through `Timeline`. Every chat highlight range comes from inside it:
  - `ChatAnnotationMarkers` and `highlightChatAnnotation` from the transcript;
  - `ChatSelectionActions` from the selection in its viewport;
  - `useChatFind` from its root, which is that element.
- `artifact-selection` applies only under a new `data-artifact-selection-scope` attribute on `ArtifactFileView`'s scroll box, the container `ArtifactSelectionAsk` reads its selection from.
- Each rule has one selector. The minifier (lightningcss) does not parse `::highlight`, so it would ship a selector list as separate rules, which is the cost this PR removes. Neither scope element holds text directly, so the descendant selector alone covers every range.
- Specificity rises from a bare pseudo-element to one attribute selector. No other rule styles these highlights.

## Testing

- Bisect, split experiments and before/after numbers come from a Playwright harness kept outside the repo. It uses:
  - the production renderer build with its real CSP;
  - the fake bridge, signed in;
  - artifact files from a local server, in #8339's mix: 40% HTML, 25% Markdown, 20% 1600×1000 PNG, 10% PDF, 5% text;
  - full headless Chromium at 1440×900.

  The three builds took turns on every run, and runs waited for a load average under 6.
- A pixel check paints each of the six highlights in both builds, in dark and light themes: identical.
- `vitest run` on the `ArtifactFileView`, `useChatFind`, `ChatAnnotationMarkers` and `ChatSelectionActions` tests: 77 passed.
- Not run locally: the full suite, typecheck and e2e. Rely on CI for those.

- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

- [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense (no behavior change; CSS scoping only)
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

## Why

Builds 0.14.10 and older have no Sentry event cap and used up the org's error quota (Sentry has accepted 0 events since Nov 8). 0.15.0+ has the cap, but shares the same DSNs, so old builds starve it. New DSNs let us switch the old keys off in Sentry and silence the uncapped builds.

## Change

`frontend/src/shared/sentry-config.ts` only:
- `DEFAULT_DAEMON_SENTRY_DSN` (ao-daemon, `/4512334276329472`): key `e21b875a...` replaced with `ce259857...`
- `DEFAULT_ELECTRON_SENTRY_DSN` (ao-electron, `/4512334283931648`): key `5fe434b5...` replaced with `6d68b5ec...`

Mobile DSN, cap, sampling and scrubbing are untouched. A repo grep found no other copies of the old keys (tests, fixtures, docs, CI env), and no test asserts on the DSN string.

## Verification

- `grep -rn "5fe434b5\|e21b875a"` returns nothing.
- Sentry tests (`sentry-config.test.ts`, `sentry-main.test.ts`, `renderer/lib/sentry.test.ts`): 49 passed.
- `tsgo --noEmit`: no errors outside `packages/product-ui`, which fails only because its deps are not installed in this worktree.

## Follow-up

Disable the old keys in Sentry once this ships.
